column3: As a former student, now a junior in college, I have to say this school has prepared me for college. I was one of the only people who knew how to organize notes and write a research paper in my first college English class. This skill is major for students going into college and the teachers at Palmer High do an excellent job teaching towards the future. The administration is not the greatest, the rules can be annoying and ridiculous, but I do have to say that I survived and am now doing very well in college, which is ultimately what matters after high school. I've been in palmer schools since kindergarten and I do believe it's the worst school in the district. The administration has no idea what they're doing, the rules are absolutely ridiculous and the male/athletics/popular students are favored. I've been in a class where a teacher will stop a whole lesson just to ask a student "if she can borrow her dress". Worst school compared to peers' schools from other towns. I think it's a great school! Wonderful principal , vice principal , guidance & teachers Very bad. Scheduling is very bad and some teachers do very little to help prepare students for state tests

column1: Going to South Miami Senior High School is depressing. The unpleasant aesthetics of the school (one of the buildings literally has no windows and is completely concrete), the prison like administration (with constant uniform sweeps, tardy tank that sends you to SCSI where one gets sentenced to a day of absolute silence in a tiny room with a barking babysitter, and of course the wonderful security gaurds that are constantly questioning you if you are spotted in the halls), and of course the education which is undoubtedly unsatisfactory. The regular course teachers are only there to prepare their students for the FCAT, so one has to take full AP courses to receive a decent education; there are a very limited selection of APs at that. The math department can be said to have only one good teacher, there are very few academies (the IT academy is deplorable, only very highly motivated students can succeed, as there is no real effort to do any sort of work), and there are even fewer elective choices for educational enrichment. I would not recommend South Miami Senior High School to anyone, even those who want to participate in a magnet program. I graduated a couple years back and really it's a great school. It made a MAJOR improvement from my freshman to junior year. I'm pretty sure it was able to go from a D school to a B school in one year. While there are some teachers who probably shouldnt be there (lack of competence, to be honest, and its a shame) there are several who are truly good at what they are doing. They care about the students and want to teach. They offer plenty of AP courses as well! I only wish their Arts program was better. Its also important to note that in my time there I never experienced or witnessed any really bad bullying. South Miami is a good school that I'm sure will keep on getting better! I think South Miami High has offered a better education than my previous private school. Like any school, there are great teachers, good teachers, and those that you wish you did not have to deal with. Overall, I have to say that this is a good school to attend. Ever since Bonce got there he made the place a prison. It is no longer a school, I dropped out in 2008 because I hated every minute of it. Specially the administration, faculty and staff. They are all very disrespectful to the students. I have been able to graduate college and I am currently working on a masters, no thanks to this horrible school and its pedantic administrators. Only way I see to fix this school is to do a complete overhaul and hire new staff, administrators and educators. And for the love of god will the get a decent architect/ engineer/contractor in there to put some windows in the main building. Seeing as how there hasn't been a recent review, I felt it was time for a current, relevant review of SMSH! Our child started this year in a magnet program as a 9th grader. After careful consideration, this was the school they chose out of the 5 they were accepted to. During the magnet process, SMSH did the best job connecting to students during a pandemic. While that was not the only deciding factor, connection was important.3 quarters into Freshman year, we have a happy teenager who is thriving at SMSH in all advanced classes. At the end of the day, a happy teenager that doesn't hate school is a blessing. The overall climate of the school is good. While there is the typical high school stuff that we hear about, it's not isolated to SMSH as every high school deals with these things. My child enjoys school, most of their classes, and their extracurricular activities and clubs. Further, they feel safe at school during and after school hours. Teachers: With the exception of 1 teacher, they have all been great. The classes have been engaging, the homework reasonable and meaningful, and communication on point. The teachers are knowledgeable and seem to really care about the student and their progress. Some are truly passionate about their subject areas. 1 is exceptional at developing critical thinking skills. I do wish this was the case in more classes. Magnet Program: So far, the program has been amazing. The content has been challenging enough to see improvement, while remaining developmentally appropriate with expectations and growth.Communication from the school's auto system is OVERKILL. Literally the same message days in a row via 3 methods: phone, text, and email. I appreciate being informed, but do not need to hear/read the same thing over an over again! I get that trying to get parents involved is important to overall student success, 9 of the same message is not the answer!AICE Program: This is a HUGE bonus! Students have the opportunity to take the AICE classes and exams and graduate with an AICE Diploma. For those going to college in Florida, this is guaranteed Bright Futures money for school. The classes are more rigorous and require the students to pass the exams for the classes taken in order to earn the AICE Diploma & their are plenty of options so that students can take classes that interest them. It's important to know the guidelines for completion of this program so there are no surprises.

column3: I graduated from GCHS in 2009 and am proud to say that. I understand people's frustrations with the district and will also admit that sports play a huge role in the school system, which isn't necessarily a good thing if it hinders the educational process. That being said, I recieved a quality education from k-12 with the exception of having a few teachers who were pathetic. You can find that anywhere though. I now attend St. Louis University, one of the most prestigous Jesuit institutions in the country...and I would add that I was fully prepared for it with the education I recieved from GCSD9. Yes, there are some bad politics in the district, but I blame mostly the students and parents for our lackluster academic standings. The best teachers in the world can't make a student learn if they don't want to or if their parents haven't instilled a sense of importance about education. Let's look at the where the real problems lie. This is one of the best schools in the area they take the time and put forth the effort to make sure our children become successful young men and women. The teacher and staff help our children to reach their full potential. They don't just fill our kids with book smarts they teach them how to be confident and ready for the world ahead. I love this school and the education my children are receiving. I am an involved parent and sadly most other parents are not. The teachers care and have engaging and comprehensive lesson plans. I have one child who graduated this school and three others enrolled. I could not be happier with the education they are receiving. This is a good school and the teachers really care. I am first in my class and I am taking all AP courses. The advanced curriculum here is not for the weak of heart! My only complaint would be the fact that my brother, sisters and I spend a lot of time fundraising for the school. It is not enough that we are in class 8 hours a day, plus the hours we spend in clubs, sports or band and the several hours of homework we have after our activities, we also have to spend extra hours selling things trying to raise money for the school. I love this school district. They take time to help our kids, they care and they make sure they are always safe. The kids learn to respect each other mo matter what differences they may have from financial to special needs. They grow up ready to face the next chapter in their lives. Thanks to all the students teachers and administrators for making this a great educational experience. I want to transfer them out. They are not learning anything and when I address this problem I get nothing but attitudes. Aren't you supposed to be professional and help the child instead of discarding them!!! We have had a mostly positive experience with this High School. Teachers and staff provide a good education. Extracurricular activities are available for all. The Band is top notch and sports are competitive. My oldest child graduated from GCHS. The teachers played a big role in preparing her for college which she has already graduated from with honors. Our son was the fourth generation in my family to graduate from this school district. We have teachers that care so much for our children and do so many extra projects and give of their time for our children. Our son graduated with all the tools he needed to be successful in his future. I love this school district! Three generations of our family has graduated from this school district and everyone's experience has been positive. Granite City High School supplies a quality education that prepares students for the real world. Many graduates leave GCHS and enter the work force. The college readiness rating is misleading, electricity, automotive, welding, building trades, machining, business technologies, are just a few of the career fields GC offers. Horrible because they don't do anything for students that need help. They focus on the more popular kids The population of this school district is steady declining and the tax base has taken a tremendous hit. Teacher and staff demand high salaries with large benifits. The past District Superintendent made some very bad choices when it came to closing some of the schools and forcing parents to send their children to schools outside their neighborhoods. The district will take no input from parents. The district continues to look for ways to raise taxes and has been shut down 2 times by tax payers in less than 5 years. The level of education is at best mediocure considering the pay for quality teachers.

column1: This school does NOT except new comers....if you are planning on bringing your child to this school DON'T!! the kids bully each other like crazy!! This is a follow up to my review on December 3, 2012 My child would not let me pursue the bullying endured at Caledonia High School and I wish I had but, nonetheless; it wasn't only the kids that made my child feel unwelcome but also the coaches specifically one of the sports coaches last year. My child sustained an injury and decided to go out for the only sport left to avoid any more injuries. He/she was told by a coach who prefaced it with how much he liked our child that the athletic ability displayed was "sub-par" therefore my child should not plan on coming to the rest of tryouts. That was the last of many rejections and my child whose life revolved around sports was crushed. Two weeks later I got to pace the halls of DeVos Children's Hospital after friends called the local sheriff because our child had shared plans to take his/her life. I hope you and your child never experience this!!! I also hope someone who "cares" takes the time to read this. Sincerely a concerned Mom. Caledonia School teachers do care about their students. So much so that they can retest on nearly everything until they get the grade they want! They do have a good sports program and are very competitive in the OK-Gold White despite regularly being up against two State powerhouses of East Grand Rapids and Lowell. The school does have some financial issues, primarily because of paying for the generous retirement benefits of prior administrations. They do have a poor Math program and they are real sensitive and vindictive about it. When a local University Professor was asked by them (on a unpaid basis) to review their Math program and pointed out its problems, the Administration & Teachers Union mailed dispute notices to everyone in the district and get the Professor fired. But as the Professor said, if your child is not going to college or not going to be majoring in the Sciences, their regular Math program is probably OK for you. However, if your Child is going into the sciences get them in the advance placement classes because the regular classes are too weak for your kid to survive College Math. Extremely Positive. I certainly don't have comparisons to match experiences other than my own, but chalk and an abacus don't qualify my experience as a comparison. I currently have 2 children attending Caledonia schools. The community as a whole is rude and bully newcomers relentlessly. If I had known, we never would have moved out here. The students bully new students until your child feels pushed out and alone. No child deserves to be treated as such. The school faculties do nothing about it. Staff refuse to punish accordingly, especially if a student is from a family that has been established in the community for a long time. A new child though will be suspended for being the recipient of bullying. But what else would you expect when you can't even grocery shop in Caledonia without receiving rude looks and disdain from the adults? The school system here is a joke. Test scores are inflated by allowing students to repeat tests as many times as they want. There are no real methods of teaching practiced. They will not work with a student who may not grasp as easily as another to further their knowledge. Students are not held accountable for their grades or their actions. We have decided to enroll in a neighboring, more welcoming, and well-performing district. I had a horrible experience at this school. People I knew were bullied and harassed tirelessly because we were different and the school did close to nothing about it. It got to the point where we were scared to even walk in the hallways in fear that something would happen to us. Im terrified for the youth that are entering this school. Something NEEDS to change. If you are enrolling your child in Caledonia make sure you are willing to fight and advocate for your kid til the end. This school destroyed my mental health.

column3: The school is impersonal and the individual students are just parts in a machine. Administration considers the 'machine' acceptable and will use the "1700 students" as a reason to ignore individual needs. Administration are also thick as thieves and are unwilling to take responsibility when they make mistakes. As far as teachers are concerned, I don't think they can get a fair rating because of the regime they report to. My oldest child, a graduate of CSHS and a Dean's list student in college says, "I'm ashamed to be an alum of that school.". The worst thing about this school and the district is that they are always grubbing for money, then they cut classroom budget, and spend, spend, spend on facilities and "image". They boast their "A" rating to the point of being sickening, especially when you know what day to day is really like.. The school and its administration is a joke. They spend thousands to put a helicopter in the air to take a video of the students on the field for their "year end video" but can't spend a dime to provide special education needs for its students who are struggling. Unbelievable!!!! DON'T send your kids here! Cactus Shadows is a very fine institution. I'm not going to lie and say that all of their teachers are the best in the state but they aren't the worst. I transferred to Horizon because I moved and anyone who thinks there is a drug or bullying problem should go to Horizon and see how lucky they are. No one pushes drugs on you and no one gets bullied at school. Online is another story. If you are getting bullied online just close your browser! Cactus Shadows has great events and really creative students. I am proud to say I attended Cactus Shadows and will be returning in the fall for my senior year. Honestly, this school is a perfect example of when they use the A grade rating to boost their reputation and all of the sudden when your invested in it, it's a huge lie. I've been a student at the school since freshmen year and I felt this school is a lifeless prison of a mediocre list of teachers and unreliable programs that struggles to prepare students for college. The students are horrible at this school specially the student body and stuco, they are disrespectful to their peers and new students from other schools. Overall, this school is horrible in education and everything, if you looking for a strong education that really preps your child for college, consider Pinnacle or Chaparral. The staff at this school are extremely rude and unaccommodating. The curriculum is basic for the classes my child is enrolled in and I honestly don't see how this school prepares students for college. One year is enough at this school and I'm glad my child will not be attending there next year. Cactus Shadows has a caring and dedicated staff whose number one priority is preparing students for higher education. My child is a highly academic student, and the school offers him the rigor he needs, along with a multitude of clubs, activities and events. They truly create a balanced environment for students. Thank you! Students and teachers treat one another with respect and thoughtfulness making the atmosphere pleasant. I hear a lot of laughter coming from both students and teachers. Cactus Shadows High School is an excellent high school. They offer academic programs to meet the needs of every student, including phenomenal college preparatory programs such as the International Baccalaureate Program and college classes. They achieve state and national recognition for many of their athletic teams, clubs and activities. Teachers, counselors and administrators have high expectations to ensure their graduates are college and career ready. The size of the school is perfect so that the students are not just a number. Their teachers know them and the students are friendly. There is no other school in the valley that I would want to send my child. Teachers are interested in your student's academic progress as well as personal development. Teachers, staff, and administration support and attend games and events, and are a huge part of the community. Concerns are addressed promptly and the teacher or administration make sure that all parties are satisfied with the result. We are thrilled with our child's experience at Cactus Shadows. Worse school my children have ever been enrolled in. There is no positive feedback provided to students who are struggling, it is all about punitive action, and poor teaching Cactus Shadows is a phenomenal high school. Teachers care about their students and make themselves available for extra help whenever needed. They are often seen attending sporting events cheering on the students. There is a tremendous sense of community at the school. The student council is very active and conducts events throughout the year which brings the entire campus together. There are too many clubs to name and between the clubs and the excellent athletic teams every student that attends Cactus Shadows can be involved in something. Our son transferred into CSHS for the IB program, and while he is only in his first year, we feel the school has lived up to it's promise of academic rigor. He is taking all AP/Honors as a pre-IB student and while some teachers are better than others, we have been satisfied so far. One area where CSHS excels is the counseling department. They are proactive, communicate well and provide a lot of opportunities for students/parents. The school also has good spirit and a sense of community. It feels smaller than it is. Only giving 4 stars right now since our student is not in full IB yet and that is why he is here - will update review then. The worst. I know many families who moved away so their kids could go to other schools. Being the only high scool in the area, kids drop out like crazy and home school. Terrible because i am looking to transfer elsewhere. Their are many kind people who have their hearts in the right place, but many of them are not properly educated. Not to mention, all events they hold are disorganized and chaotic. I have never been so happy to leave a school. I left halfway through my freshman year, as I struggled from depression and anxiety, mostly caused by that school. I would cry every morning before school, begging my parents to let me stay home. The stress kept me up all hours of the night, working on homework and studying. This school does not seem to understand that it isn't healthy for students to have this much on their plate. Every person I have talked to, at Cactus Shadows, has admitted to having at least one mental breakdown because of school. That shouldn't be normal! This school has a very poor learning atmosphere, and not very good academics. I've never been so unhappy. The worst school Ive ever went to in my life. If your low income student like I am, good luck making friends because they only care about if you have money, both teachers and students. If your poor like me and can only afford cheap clothes you will get bullied and the school will do nothing about it. Disappointing and embarrassing. They should be ashamed. If you’re looking for decent public schools, look at Pinnacle or Chapparal. Don’t waste your time with Cactus Shadows. I attended this school back in 2014 I believe. The staff at this school is disrespectful, biased, and very difficult to deal with as a student then, and continue to hear the same from current students now. No matter what your child will go through, no matter what kind of difficult encounters your child may come across, as unfortunate as it is to say, this school will only make it worse. I have heard lots of comments about many different school, and Cactus Shadows will always be voted in the most negative way. I could say so much about this school but it would only take me forever to write, so I would like to leave with this - it is very unfortunate to have only one high school near by Cave Creek. If I could give less than 1 star I would! Parents beware of the entire school district! The new superintendent has seemingly gone rogue slashing programs, jobs, and tools critical to successful learning. He was previously an assistant superintendent and likely is in over his head. His leadership skills are not at the level required for this position.The high school has a racism problem and he basically endorsed that by cutting a very successful language immersion program. I strongly caution anyone considering going to a school in this district. The district is going downhill rapidly. The mindset of the superintendent is literally high school graduation and nothing more. If that is your vision then this district is for you. This public school was ok when everything was ok and my kids did great in their classes.Once issues arose, NO ONE was helpful or even pretended they cared!!!A disgrace of a school.Aside from a few teachers, most teachers and admin are rude, judgmental, and the least concerned about the students! Great school and communication. I've appreciated the support from the teachers to help my kids. Love the sports and school spirit! Many recent changes for 2022/23. AP program expanded & IB full or partial certificates available now. New principal and counselors, many new teachers. Really like the new Football program, high expectations have been set with an emphasis on discipline and accountability/ responsibility. My child is on the AP/Honors track and is really enjoying the football program. They practice early in the A.M., allowing plenty of time after school for homework / family / and other activities. Constant communication via text, email, phone (INFO overload but can't complain there's a lack of it!). Been in this district 8 yrs, I see an improvement this year. Safe surroundings a plus. Con: sports/ activity fees are high due to lack of funding, as in most districts. I am being generous with two stars but only because Cactus Shadows provides a unique opportunity for students with disabilities. This is a big deal if your child has an IEP and plans to go to college. But this one positive does not outweigh the many negatives. The bullying situation at this high school is out of control. The teachers are not equipped to handle the physical and cyber bullying that hurts so many students. When engaged repeatedly to address the situation, the school leadership leaves victims and their families with the strong impression that they just want the problem to disappear. But, they do not solve the problem. Asking victims to switch classes to get away from bullies sends the wrong message to everyone involved. The new superintendent and principal must effectively deal with this situation ASAP for the safety and well being of those affected. CSHS offers the IB program and many other unique programs for students. We love it!

column1: Great high school. Teachers are very co-operative.. Small class ... My son hitanshu Soni grauate. Last year he love this school.. I have a daughter that graduated from this school and one who currently attends. They are both very different and therefore had different, but good, experiences. My graduate was in the Theater program and she loved it. It is a lot of work and dedication outside of the school day. I did feel the teacher put a lot of pressure on them and kept them later then needed at times. I get they are learning the business, but they are still children who rely on the parent for transportation, etc. She took standard classes and never had many complaints about the teachers and did satisfactory. My current student is in the Multi Media program and is an honors student. She also loves her shop and her teacher is great. She experienced some confusion about if she was in the right path or not so was able to briefly dabble in another shop. This is a time to figure things out so I was happy they allowed her the opportunity. She is in the honors program and she sometimes complains about the teachers but it is the math teacher who just seems awful. My daughter has always been pretty good at math and now seems lost and wants me to pay for tutoring which seems unfair given the numerous complaints about the teacher from not only my daughter but several other students/parents. Overall, a good school. I would recommend. Our daughter just graduated from MCVT and had a wonderful experience. She was in the digital film shop in the School of the Arts program and in honors classes. Her digital film teacher was excellent and truly inspired our daughter to develop her craft and challenge herself. This school is dedicated to their students and prepares them better than any other high school to either pursue college or become licensed in a trade, ready to work in a career they can be proud of. Recently they added an International Club and my daughter visited Paris, France! The small class sizes are an advantage, so students get more attention from their teachers and less likely to fall through the cracks. They have a supportive PTO in the School of the Arts program. The new principal is doing great and just added a music shop. This school is heading in the right direction for all learners. The school could use an update with bathrooms and a new sign in the front of the school, although they did get a digital sign on the corner. Overall I am very pleased with the education our daughter received here and I wish continued success to the faculty, administration, and students at MCVT! I highly recommend this school. If you are unsure I suggest you go to open house and see for yourself. Your child does need to be confident though to try something new and leave their friends. However, if they are truly their friends they will stay in touch and your child will make new friends. Take a leap and follow your heart; that's what our daughter did and never looked back. This school allows teachers to pick students for shop placement based on their level of enthusiasm, not testing, not grades, attendance, not even a review of your childs IEP needs but enthusiasm UNBELIEVABLE. Be sure to teacher your child how to "fake it till they make it" especially if they are more quiet and reserved. This school WILL place your child where they have ZERO interest.

column3: Great, Safe school! I would recommend it to anyone! It has some great teachers and some not so great but besides that it's a small school that makes it safe My two sons have graduated from CPHS, with my first son, I wanted him to go to El Camino HS, big mistake. CPHS is small, you get to know the teachers well, if you take your time for your kids and both graduated with honors. Be involved in your child's education and it will pay off. I attended this school and it offered all the tools I needed for success. Canoga park is not perfect. Unfortunately, like any other school it does have its bad crowds, so it really all comes down to who the students choose to be and how they choose to act. However, overall Canoga is a great school. It offers various challenging courses, and leadership positions the teachers are very attentive and tutoring is offered after school. Last but not least, the fact that it is a small school really does help kids get around and get to know each other like a family. The old administration loved the kids and were open to working with the parents and teachers. There were many good programs and teachers. Things have changed in the past two years. There is no longer a voice among the staff or parents. Many key people are gone and the programs are dwindling. Things are very sad at this campus. The new administration is terrible. Most of the programs are being cut and kids are suffering. They do not comply with LAUSD policies and trying to get any action is a losing battle. This school needs a complete overall - starting from the top. The Principal is horrible! !! He does not return parent phone calls, address any issues he simply passes the buck. The teacher's are not held to any LAUSD or ethical standard. They are pretty much given free range to do as they please. Student requests or concerns are discarded with the days garbage. My family was so excited about their Agricultural and Veterinarian Magnet it looked very promising and it has been nothing more than a disappointment. My child is a hard working student with good grades and has never been in any sort of trouble and this school doesn't help support any of these student's, they are all left on the back burner. This will definitely be the last year my child attends this school. Anyone who is considering sending their child to this magnet or school should seriously reconsider and look into North Hollywood Zoo Magnet or the new Animal Science Magent at Verdugo Hills High School. This was a good school but the principal (now gone) caused considerable harm. More concerned about his career than the students. Many programs were cut and the students suffered. Bullying is rampant and nothing is done to curtail it. Most of the good teachers have given up. Don't send your child here. I truly believe the unique extracurricular programs I was involved in made me a well-rounded individual, and helped me get accepted into all six of the UC and CSU schools I applied to. Where else in Los Angeles can you raise farm animals as your own and attend leadership conferences and competitions all over the state? Now I have come back to teach and enjoy it very much! The "best kept secret" in the San Fernando Valley that LAUSD has to offer anywhere! My son has had a great experience. The teachers and counselors care about the children they go over and beyond to keep the children on track . However the parents also need to be proactive and involved. I love this school. This is the best kept secret in the valley. My son and daughter attend Canoga Park High School. One is in the FFA program, being in this program tought him about farming and agriculture. He enjoys caring for the animals in the farm. He will be graduating this year with terrific grades.My youngest is in cross country and enjoys being part of team. They won city finals this year! The teachers are excellent, they care about the kids.

column1: Unfortunately due to things beyond our control my son enrolled At Columbia High 3 weeks before school was ending. my son is only in the 9th grade and is gifted. Columbia did not have an equivalent math for him to take(because they don't have a class that high) so they opted to not have him take a math class at all. So since he effectively did not finish the class at his previous school and Columbia doesn't have it. He will not receive credit. Also my son observes alot of fighting and other discipline issues , just far too many to list, on a daily basis. A school that decides not to enroll a student in a core academic class is not a decent scool. When you enter high school, all of the babying halts and the true character of your willingness and self motivation takes control. That is the virtue I presume Columbia High is promoting. They will not hold your hand, nor will they continue to ride you to get YOUR work done, or bring YOUR books to class. Trust me. At every school there are students who were forced in and don't care about the mischief they cause at school. Therefore, just like every other institution, Columbia offers excellence, and prosperity, but it is a personal decision whether or not you run with it. GO EAGLES!!! If you want a middle school then I would recommend you go to this school...if you want a high school then avoid this school. The students are hardly under control and the atmosphere filled with attitude. It feels like a jail. I've never been in trouble but I've seen the teachers and staff watch the students with caution. Most students don't know that they're missing out on a great education in other schools because they aren't properly informed but I've come from a school with great academics. The only reason I'm here is because it was the closest school to where we moved. The things I did in middle school are the things they're doing now in this "high school" if it's even worthy of that title. This is a very supportive school. Teachers and Administrators are always available to support the students and ensure the success of students that really want to succeed. It was a terrible experience good thing i left there are only a few good kids there Horrible. The staffs treat students like prisoners. Only about 5% of all students are actually good people. AP classes are overcrowded with broken chairs, yet filled with troublemakers and underachievers.

column3: The teachers at Mount Miguel High School care deeply for the students and offer many extra hours of tutorial assistance. The school offers a safe learning environment along with an academic program that fully prepares its students for college and careers. Mount Miguel High School is the best school in the Grossmont Union High School District. I really enjoyed my four years at Mount Miguel. I build very strong connections with many of the staff members. Teachers are great, caring, and loving. You definitely get plenty of leadership and community service opportunities, if and only if, you put yourself out there and get involved. #Shoutout to the Matador Business Academy. Great program. I would rate my school as a great school entirely because I have never been to a public high school and Mount Miguel was my first one and I am currently attending as a Junior. I love the teachers and the staff is very friendly, but people give us a bad rap and call us " Mount Mighetto" but if they actually went to Mount they would think differently about it. The classes aren't too crowded and every student gets the help they need whether its tutorial or Saturday scholars and there are so many things to do at Mount Miguel during break, lunch and after school from going in the choir room to going in the game room and after school going to the ice cream trucks. I attended the school and it was a great school for me. Led to my very successful career as a safety professional. Great athletic department and great coaches.Would definitely send my kids to the school but I moved out of the area as a younger adult.

column1: This school is known in the Northeast Kingdom for being a top-rated school. The staff are very pleasant and the facility is up to par with that of a much more populated area school. We previously were in a more surburban area and this school is just as good - if not better due to the closer community. Teachers are well-educated and caring. School has many extra curricular activities and events. People choose to live in Danville specifically to send their children to this school. Basically, your child will get a wonderful education in a safe, rural setting. Danville School is an outstanding Pre K- 12 grade school. My children will have had 15 years of a consistent schooling experience. This school keeps up with the changing times in education, and it is expected that every child will learn. The staff is engaging in coursework to keep current with technology, teaching strategies, and curriculum development. They are very fortunate to have a new principal who is leading the school in a forward direction. Danville School has the potential of being a great school as changes are currently taking place. There is a lack of discipline because teachers have not been supported by the current high school principal. A new administration has been put in place for next year and I see that as an excellent start. Holding teachers and students accountable is what this school needs. This school has excellent support by the community. As changes are made to the curriculum and method of teaching, I see Danville becoming a 5 in the next few years. I love the how Danville has opened so many doors for him and have welcomed him with open arms . Danville school is very organized has great community that are all was ready to help and work together for the better of the children and community! This past year at Danville has been a very difficult one for the community. A young, inexperienced HS principal, an older experienced elementary principal, and a last-year before retirement superintendent did not mesh together at all. It seemed as though there was a great deal of support for the elementary principal, who brought in many new ideas and gave the K-6 teachers a lot of help. At the same time, the HS principal and superintendent were charged by police with bad practices, and the school board allowed all sorts of administrative problems to occur. Lots of staff and teachers seem very upset with how things are going. We now have to start yet again (fourth time in 7 years I think) with two new principals and a new superintendent. I hope my children get the appropriate leadership at Danville that they deserve; they did have it with the prior elementary principal, but she resigned, I think because of all that happened this past year. Whatever school gets her will be very lucky.

column1: As a freshman of Cloudland High School, I love my school! I feel like I get a quality education I deserve! column3: No high school is going to be perfect for every kid, but Rye High does a great job overall. It tends to work more like a prep school than a typical average public school. It's clearly a competitive environment, where the expectation is that most students are not only going on to college, but to a selective college. A lot of kids graduate with more than six AP classes, some are essentially in a full college program by senior year. Every year, a few dozen kids go off to the Ivy League and the like. Sports and clubs are a big deal, and funded exceptionally well for a public school. It's an affluent community, and parents tend to pick up the slack where the school budget won't cover something. All that said, I don't think Rye High is the most inventive, creative environment. It's a bit old school in its approach, focusing on doing core education very well. There is good support for kids who struggle academically, but they could feel out of the mainstream. If diversity is important to you, you will hate this school. It's about as white bread as you'll find anywhere. My daughter has been here from 6-8th and entering 9th grade. We moved here for the education and safety factor. Teachers are outstanding (7 of 10 are) and the HS teachers are even better - told personally by parents with older kids. The major problem is there is no diversity here and it's not representative of the world that our children will have to perform in. Other major problem is, if your child has not been playing sports since/like 4th grade competitively to include sports camps, they will very likely never get on any of the teams, hence, they make half as many friends and are a second class citizen socially and to some degree confidence-wise. If these two issues have little value, I recommend this school 5 or 5 since the kids can also walk safely to a well monitored, town and learn independence much earlier...If your child is average or better excellent suggestion. If not, suggest they go somewhere else, since it seems like they actively try to dissuade low performers from attending to artificially elevate published performance stats. Rye High School is based in a nice, welcoming community. The teachers are all very helpful and engaging. The other students at the school involve themselves in many activies. The sports that Rye High School runs are great for character building as well as keeping students busy and interested. As a graduate of Rye High School, I would reccomend this school to anyone who is looking for a good education for their children. It is challenging, yet the teachers are willing to work with students in order to allow them to succeed. Academically, the experience has been very fulfilling. The level of courses offered is exactly what is needed to be competitive for the top colleges. Socially it has been a travesty! For a student who is shy, and not a member of the majority, this school can be brutal. The social aspect does ,of course, affect academic performance, so a kid that is a straight A student can become a B student; and a student who had great attendance, needs a mental health day at least twice monthly. Wondering if the academics is worth the trauma.

column1: I am a former student of St. Croix. I enjoyed many aspects of my time there, including the excellent music program and the care and diligence that many of my teachers showed for my fellow students and me. Unfortunately, my time there was negatively tainted by anti-gay bullying, even though I wasn't out of the closet at the time. School administration did nothing to stop this bullying, despite being made aware of it. I also was not the only student bullied for perceived or actual differences. Another student, who I will only describe as having some special needs, was also bullied, and worse than I was. Very little was done on his behalf by administrators and many teachers. Worse, the simple accomodations that I now know this condition required (we weren't educated about it at the time) would not have cost the school anything and would not have been more than a moment's trouble for the teachers and administration. Further, the school's science curricula is based on Young Earth Creationism and is decidedly anti-scientific. It is NOT suitable for students who wish earn college majors that require literacy of cosmological history or evolutionary biology or geologic sciences. Middle School children are allowed to try out for all High School sports. This could be a great recruiting tool for Middle School kids who would like to play High School level sports before reaching high school. Disappointing when your child doesn't make the High School team because of Middle School student can have a spot. St. Croix offers a unique combination of small class sizes (~20 students), highly qualified teaching staff (most have Masters Degrees) and integration of students from around the world (China, Korea, Africa, Europe) as well as the region (Rochester, Menomonie). Most students are involved in some type of extra-curricular activities. My sons are getting a caring, Christian education at St. Croix. St. Croix is not ashamed of The Bible and not afraid to teach it as truth. This has rubbed at least one reviewer here the wrong way. If you are being objective, it takes a lot more FAITH to believe in the THEORY of evolution. In fact, one can be an atheist, and still not believe in evolution! Darwin was concerned that the thousands of intermediate stages between creatures needed to prove his theory were not in evidence, but he expected they would eventually be found. Yet those thousands of missing transitional forms are still missing!I respect that St. Croix stands on the rock of scripture even if it isn't "popular". That is a valuable lesson for young minds.TH We have had a very positive experience at st. Croix! I am an alumni of this school and now send my kids there too. As an adult now I really appreciate the sacrifices that my mom made to give me and my siblings a great education. My kids love the school and have grown so much. The Learning Resource Center had been vital to the success and support that my son need to excel these past few years. My other son will utilizing the PSEO options this fall and we couldn't be more excited for him to get a head start on college. I will continue to recommend this school to anyone that will listen.

column3: I am currently enrolled as a sophomore at Arab High School, and I love it! Most people believe that Arab is a school full of rednecks and sluts, but i can truthfully tell you that it's not. Yes, the classes are hard, but doesn't that better prepare you for life ahead of you? Yes, it does. I am in Honors English 10 at the moment, and my teacher teaches this specific course as a college class. Yes, its hard, but I am glad she does it that way, because it prepares me. Extra ciricular activities are great! The sports teams this year have excelled so much. Like our football team takin us to the 2nd round of playoffs this year. Everything about this school is great, and i am glad to say, I'm part of this school district. :) I just sent a lengthy comment on your band that was in Chicago, Il. last weekent(l7March2012. I graduated from Arab High School, and having just completed my associate's degree on my way to my bachelor's, I can say with all confidence that I was better prepared in most cases than students from a lot of other schools in my area. I was blessed to have several great teachers who worked with me, and who heavily influenced my desire to teach one day. The school does have high expectations of its students, but those expectations require us to expect great things of ourselves. I'd love to come back in a few years as a teacher, and I would recommend the Arab school system to anyone who wants to be challenged to excel. I absolutely loved Arab High School. I went through the Arab City School systems and I believe it prepared me for everything after high school. The teachers were amazingly knowledgeable, the administration was helpful, and it offers every extracurricular imaginable. I am so thankful for Arab High School and the future it prepared me for. Arab High School provided an excellent educational foundation for our son, who is attending a leading Southern Engineering University. Prepared me for college & in turn, medical school. Great City, Great School! If you fail or get behind in any subject this school will try and find a way to get you out to protect their rating. They do it every year. You can ask the administration at any nearby high school and see for yourself. The staff would rather remove a student than try and help them learn. If you live out of district they may or may not let you attend, I guess they feel they can pick or choose, but I cannot wait until our title IX lawsuit is filed. Poor is the best answer to give, if this school was made to only allow students in it's district it would be much smaller. I’ve done fine but for any low income students your experience here probably won’t be good. But it’s better than other public schools in the area.

column1: my son graduated and daughter currently attends. new school and facilities, good parent involvement, great sports program, AP courses. definitely tops in the county. My son is a sophomore, we are having an excellent experience here. The administration and faculty are top notch and go above and beyond for the students. The sports and band are fantastic and truly enhance the high school experience. Kudos. love this school and everything about it. Truly is the best high school in the nation. I have a Sophomore at Cosby High School. He would never consider attending any other school. He is very challenged academically and participates in Cross Country and Track. The only negative about the school is that it is way overcrowded. They need to move the HSSC, but then if they do that the HSSC would lose the students who live in the Cosby school district. Can you say school run by spoiled rich kids? -Bullying is out of control. Bully never suffers any major punishment, student who was being bullied by two older class men receives 4 days of ISD and the bully receives only 2 and the student was still being harass. -ISD is a joke. Teacher allows children in detention to text,go on IPods, mess around in halls. -There is an administrator (not giving any names but she the thick one) never shows respect for her students, awful offensive sarcasm, and just upright rude -Over crowdedness is a problem -Dress code is a huge problem. The school goes on about dress code but you see the more higher up in the social ranks girls wearing skimpy dresses showing off there undergarments and not get caught. -there are some excellent teachers in this school but not enough to recommend kids here. I rather have people go to cloverhill than cosby I love this school, I have a son who graduated from Cosby, another son and daughter will also be graduating from Cosby. Parent involvement is Awesome, teachers that all my kids have had really seem to care about their students. The extra activities they offer are great, and my two younger kids have taken advantage of them, One in Show choir and the other is doing Fashion Design along with the courses offered off site. None of my kids have ever had a problem with bullying or fights at this school, Kids all seem to be very close to each other and protective of each other. When I go to the school events here at the school you don't hear them talk negative of other schools they are in competition with , you only hear them cheering the other schools on and saying positive things, I love that! Excellent school! My kids are involved in music (Orchestra) at Cosby and absolutely love it. They are challenged musically and academically. Cosby High School is the BEST school in Richmond Virginia. Dr. Brenda Mayo is a very professional, educated, diversed, poised and confident achiever in any task given her. Her leadership far exceeds the task as principal at Cosby. A principal's job is to secure the safety for all students in the course of every given day. Principal's job is not to walk the halls, but to make sure that the learning environment is condusive, the building is safely secured, no child is left behind in any respect, and her support staff, both administration and faculty, are accountable, contented and connected with the success of the student population. Kudos to Dr. Mayo for a continued success in a #1 school in Virginia! Kudos to your administration, staff and faculty! Keep up the Outstanding Performance ! The World is Watching! My husband and I have just purchased a home in the Cosby High School district. We are moving from out of state and when interviewing friends and family from Midlothian, they all recommended Cosby High and gave that school, their most confidence. Although, Midlothian has several great schools, we feel this district was the best decision we could make in where we should settle. We look forward to participating in all the community activities centered around Cosby. I cannot praise this school highly enough. We have never experienced such an incredible school and we have 2 older children that have already graduated. We were a little bit leery about enrolling our youngest daughter into as a junior. They have embraced her with open arms. Shortly after starting school, our daughter lost a very very dear friend, from her last high school, in a horrific, gruesome, fatal car accident and missed most of the week that followed the death. She has received nothing but support, love, concern, love and complete understand from the entire school, faculty and students alike. Cosby has given support to our whole family and have been there for/with us through the whole tragedy. I have nothing but total and complete praise and appreciation for this school! Has the potential to be a great school if it weren't for the queen that runs the school like a prison camp. The children are routinely bullied by the principal and she has no compassion for her students. She is disliked by the community and her staff. School is full of rich, snobby kids with a leader that does not care for her students. Dr. Mayo has zero genuine interest in the children, she only feigns interest when one of the students or sports teams have some type of accomplishment. She once made my daughter cry by asking her opinion/observation on a topic and then ripping her to shreds, embarrassing her in front of a committee. Academics here are a joke, the no-fail-policy prevents students from receiving a zero on any assignment, regardless of deadlines or merit of the work. Compared to other schools in the county, the workload is fairly easy. Students often play cards in class, yet the principal boasts that it is strictly academics in the classroom. Students may also buy their grades, bringing food items for extra points in an academic class. There were a few quality teachers but not enough to counteract the overall elitist atmosphere of the school. Both my kids attend Cosby HS one in the honors level program. I have no complaints about the school now that they have a new Principal (2016). Great teachers, very responsive to parents. Quality education and excellent sports programs. its a good school with caring teachers and staff. I attend in the specialty center and the work environment is good but you have to want to succeed if not you will preform poorly and find many things difficult in the school. Unacceptable, they sit 3 to a seat on the buses which conflicts with the safety guidelines set by the bus manufacture. Half the teachers don't want to put in the work to fix their mistakes. As in example, the teacher posts the wrong grade in their grade book. Upon the student asking for it to be corrected, the teacher will agree to fix it but will NOT follow through. Putting the GPA of the students below what they should be. On exam day, they made the students stand up during lunch as none of the seats were available. A pathetic display of leadership. The students are students, not your slaves to get your monthly paycheck. This school puts the risk of children everyday from and to school on the bus. This school treats the children as if they were serving jail. The people are more interested in themselves than the children around them. They post homework online even if the student doesn't have online access. They add fees on everything they want to even though they still call themselves public schooling. Which entitles free learning without fees or bills to attend the school. A RIGHT not a privilege for the children. This school may not fail your child, but will most truly treat your child second to their wallet and put them in harms way if it means they get more money. The admin of this school is beyond ridiculously rude. Good luck getting anything worth while to change with people who are so pathetic, they can't even refund a 15 dollar ticket for homecoming. As they should; due to wrongfully turning away people at the door. You should be fired and then put in a factory so that you can't destroy other people's nights due to your incompetent brain. New to the area. We just moved in and have been warmly welcomed. The kids are studious, and the area seems academically minded. High School homework load is about 1 hour to 2 a day. The only complaint I have heard is that the cafeteria food could use improvement... perhaps a sub sandwich bar could be added! :) The school allows online courses with permission, even foreign language if they do not offer a specific one, which is great. Its a good school.

column3: I am a current student at Nogales High School. I am a Junior, Class of 2015. I believe this school is a great school, its just the bad reputation that makes it seem bad.mit has a bad reputation because of all the gangs near the school. The teachers do care about the students' academic performance and do whatever they can to help them. This school is great! The Honors, AP and IB courses are excellent! Throughout the years, it has changed dramatically, in a positive way. Gotta love this school. Maybe the administration should stop worrying about who's shorts are "too short" and motivate students to care about their education. Teachers should also start doing their job instead of sitting around on Facebook during class and talking about their personal life that nobody cares about. Nogales High School is a great school. The teachers do care about their students, it's just many of the students are disrespectful and rude to anyone different or weak. My daughter was being bullied and the administration did nothing. The honors, IB/AP students are very friendly kids, so I would rather have my kid attend those classes instead of being harassed by others in regular classes. Another problem is the school officers around campus. They are always on their phones instead of doing their job. It makes me sick that the new principal is letting these administrators get away with this. How about instead of wasting your time trying to reconstruct the whole school and start reconstructing your whole administration. This school has its ups and downs, all schools do. Yes there are the student who do not care about the school, and will eventually drop out or move to another school, but it is also filled with students willing to make something of them self, the teachers here try there best to help you, want the best for you, administration, well you can't judge them much since every year we get new administration. I feel they need to get their stuff together, and find out ways to better the life the students who want to get their work done instead of focusing how to reward the miss behaving students, seriously I went here and recently graduated from here, I feel as they favor the misbehaving students and do not really reward the hard working ones. Administration get your stuff together really! What I do love about this school is the staff members who try to push you to do your best, the teachers, the counselors, the coaches, and advisers. Administration... I do not like you very much, or you security guards, stop being buddy buddy with the gang members and hating on the other students, we see that. This school is truly one of the best schools. From all the remodeling they have done that has left the school looking amazing and it isn't even completely done with remodeling. The Principal, teachers and staff members really make the children's academic success their number one priority. They have so many opportunities for their students. From Honors, AP and even the grigorous IB coarses to AVID, NATIONAL HONOR SOCIETY. To their career pathway coarses such as criminal justice, forensic science, medical field, law field you name it. Whatever your child wants as his major, whatever prestigious college/university he or she is considering. Their is a career pathway at Nogales that they can take to help prepare them, to give them exposure and experience. Their ROP coarses are just awesome. Their after school clubs such as robotics/science club and so many more all also help them in their career field of their choice. They have tutoring after school for those who choose to get the extra help. The summer school options are great to help get them ahead of the academic game. They really encourage their students to aim for success. To be the best not only academically but behavior and character wise. They care about the type of adults their students are becoming. They help support and inform the parents as well as the students about the opportunities and programs as well as all the requirements that are needed not only for their time being in high school but to their future in college. They involve the parents in every step of their child's high school chapter. You do have students that are careless about their future and have behavior issues as in every school with no exception of any. However that has nothing to do with the school as children are a direct reflection of their parents or parent. If the parents aren't giving their children structure, stability and discipline at home they do tend to carry that bad and disrespectful behavior to their school of attendance. But for most student here at Nogales and most parents of students here at Nogales as well as the Principal, teachers and staff they are simply amazing people doing an amazing job. My kids are very enjoying in the environment. Nice friends Nice teachers. I will recommend kids to go to this school for better future. Honestly, probably one of the worst I've seen. The kids aren't motivated to do anything. Teachers probably have to continuously baby sit them. It's an amazement that anything actually gets accomplished because the kids here feel as though they've given up on education and don't worry about the future/ don't think about consequences. Had many tough experiences that helped me develop and mature as a person; overall had a fun and fulfilling experience. the classrooms are actually very helpful. many teachers actually help me and my fellow classmates. some teachers, i admit are harder to handle than others but apart from that Nogales high is a really good school to go to. it doesn’t get the recognition it deserves, instead it is looked down upon. This school is great and I would definitely go here

column1: There are some teachers who don't really follow on the "great 5 star scale", but most of them do. I am currently a Freshman, and I have already gotten so much help from all the teachers, my counselor, AND the principle. As of right now, I have a 4.0 GPA, and I am on the top 10 GPA's of the freshman class. In Middle School, I struggled to get a 3.5. The teachers do understand sometimes you need some rest, but it's really when you respect them. SO you get respect back. The majority of the curriculum is good. AP classes are great too, the teachers have a lot more depth into the certain subject. Communication is a good way to befriend the teachers for both of your guys' advantage. Both of my older siblings went to Rochester High School (and Middle School), even though it was hard for them (like the dated reviews on this school) it has definitely made a 180 turn. I have excelled in school all thanks to the people who work there.

This is a really good school if you want to send your kid. I would reccommend it.

Even if the school hasn't had the best reputation, now it is a great school, where you will get a good education from great teachers. North is a great place to send you children to high school! Dedicated teachers, multiple opportunities for athletics and other after school activities. AP and honors classes and support for struggling students. Staff is wonderful at addressing both academic and social needs of students and make it a priority to offer support and encouragement to students. North is a great school that offers something for everyone! High. I have a graduate of North and a current sophomore and I truly could not be happier with the education and experience provided at North High School. My graduate is thriving at CU and my 15 year old is thriving in his studies and in athletics. We are the proud parents of a North High School student, and we would not have our daughter at any other school. Choices abound for families and their children's education, but I don't think you can go wrong at North. We absolutely love North and have told our friends and neighbors the same since our daughter started there almost three years ago. There are numerous afterschool programs for kids (and families!) including those in the arts and in athletics, and the kids take an immense pride in their school. The students, teachers, staff, and supportive community makes North a great place to send your child. Excellent. We have been happy with the courses offered, the teachers, the sports programs and the environment. We moved to North because of peer issues at another school. We have not had issues at this school to know whether or not the administration deals with bullying 'effectively.'I do feel as though North does not promote College Prep and concurrent enrollment nearly as well as our other high school did though. It has been quite disappointing.

column1: My daughter was a 2001 graduate of LAMP and I fully believe that she could not have been better prepared for college and life. LAMP is nationally recognized as one of the top 25 schools in the nation! My daughter is now a top executive at one of the largest advertising firms in the world. Thank you, LAMP! THE greatschools.org RANKING OF 6 IS INCORRECT PER THE greatschoools.org SUPPORT TEAM. IT HAS CONSISTENTLY BEEN A 10! I am a concerned parent who noticed that greatschools.org consistently ranked Loveless Magnet HS as a 10. After verifying that the test scores for grades 11 and 12 are literally 100% in all subjects, I immediately contacted the support department at greatschools.org on January 26, 2015. Below is their reply: (GreatSchools) Jan 27, 5:15 PM Hello, This is a bug in Alabama, about which we are aware. Thanks for your patience as we look to fix it over the coming months. Max - On January 28, 2015 I requested that a manual ranking be done of the school. Not only am I a mom and Civil Rights advocate, but I am also a real estate broker who has counseled clients for years, especially those with school aged children. Greatschools.org's ranking has such an iron-clad reputation, that many clients have used the site to assist the determination of where they would purchase a home. Hopefully, greatschools.org will correct this inaccurate ranking as soon as possible. Sincerely, MKW / Proud Mom This is an amazing school! Our oldest daughter transferred in as a junior and graduated with full scholarship offers from 7 different universities. The staff and learning environment are outstanding. Students leave LAMP truly prepared for college and our daughter still refers to LAMP as one of the best opportunities she was ever given. My son currently attends LAMP as a senior. It's an amazing school--the faculty sets high standards and holds students accountable--something that's missing at many public schools. The LAMP students excel in academics (corroborated by extraordinarily high scores on ACT and SAT), athletics, and citizenship. It would be nice if the local government leadership had a better appreciation for the fact that LAMP is the crown jewel in the public school system (one of the few bright spots). Last year, LAMP was forced to move from its dilapidated building in East Montgomery to the abandoned Houston Hills school building on Hall Street. Still, the faculty and students continue to shine despite being under-resourced. This place is awful!!!!! I hate the food and I’m not even a picky eater!! The gym sucks so do the bathrooms! I somehow managed to get into LAMP as it was actually REALLY hard to get into. At first, I was really happy since I was actually in the top 6 to get selected and literally thought that the difficulty of this school wouldn't be bothersome to me. I genuinely lost my emotions the second I started that school.Every day, go to Panera after school to study until 7pm. Come home, and study even more. If not, wake up as early as 5 am and continue studying. The worst part about this is that some of my friends had clubs in the morning as early as 4 am to 6.My grades started dropping one by one to Fs; which I never encountered any grade lower than A- or B+. My mental breakdowns stopped just 3 weeks later I started school as I normalized and named myself as the "idiot" one. In the reviews, the school is demonstrated as one of the BEST schools in the country, or that the school is amazing. It's not. Although I got along with people, the school itself destroyed me. Today I go to an ordinary school that I actually have a really good social life in and ranked top 5 in my grade. I think what matters is that you get to be WHO you are rather than some high school taking away your teenage life.

column1: The school is poorly run by the administration, but the biggest problem is the parenting of the kids in this school district. This is clearly evidenced by the number of misspelled words and poor grammar and sentence structure of most of the postings (from parents) on this website and the websites for the other schools in this district. Kids in Del Valle are the worst behaved students I have ever experienced. They cuss teachers out and even throw pens, pencils, paper, and desks at the teachers. They refuse to attempt to learn and have complete disrespect for authority, school property and each other. They are constantly babied by teachers and principals, because they won't do any work without hand holding and/or threats of punishment. All of this horrid behavior stems from poor parenting. A school's staff is there to educate the children academically, not be their babysitters. It is the parents' job to raise their children to act appropriately and this doesn't happen in Del Valle. This is the worst school that I've ever been to. I came from the RRISD and, I must admit, coming to DVISD, has really changed my opinon of school, because this school district only has one high school to go to. I am an A+ student, and all the students here,just talk through the period, distracting others, who really want to learn. It's just really sad. All children under the age of 18 are required to go to school, and the way I see it, is that, if we have to go to school, you might as well not waste your time and do what you're supposed to do, so you don't have to waste time and do it over again. I HATE this school, and no i'm not being basis, it's the truth and sometimeas the truth is ugly. Parents all I ask out there is that you do what's best for your kids and get them to a better school. I'm embarrassed to attend this school. I'm thinking about going to another one, but there's just one problem. There's only one school here.... This school is horrible. I am so sorry that I went here. It was a waste of a year. The Del Valle district is not for everyone. The DVISD is primarily minority, Hispanic/Latino. As a DVHS graduate, I am very proud my affiliation. Yes, DVHS does have opportunities to fix but which school district is perfect? DVHS does provide an array of organizations and teachers will bend over backwards to provide exponential classroom experiences. I do agree there the lack of strong administration is in result of the lack of parent involvement. But that's due to parents in the community having to work full time. Families in the district come from middle working class, so attending board meetings can be an inconvenience. Over all if you're moving to the area, DVHS is a great school. (Many board members are against adding another HS, due to retention: students drop out to help family financial needs - I myself agree) Every district does have it's flaws and for some reason, DVHS' flaws tend to stick out more. DVHS is ranked among the top 15 5A (2500+) schools in the STATE for the best educational institution for minorities. Del Valle has also met TAKS requirements 6 years in a row. My friends and I all graduated from a major university, so there is college readiness. I I am a freshman and I have a brother who attended here and I went to the orientation. I'd like to defend del Valle because it looked amazing, it was comforting and friendly. And the racial diversity is completely false. There is Hispanic, black and white race and we don't bully or harass each other. We blend in nicely, it's a great social environment and it's a great example to teach students about the real world. I am proud to be here! The AP classes here are lacking due tot he fact that most of the kids in the classes don't belong in them. Both of my sons are bored in the classes and teach themselves from the books most of the time. They have both easily passes the AP tests to receive college credit but only 5% of the other student pass them. The school is about 85% Hispanic,which we are not,and there are racial issues. There is also a huge lack of parenting in this district. My 3 kids have been in each level of school. Every school has major discipline issues,due to lack of parenting out of school. There are many kids doing drugs and having sex on campus. The dress code at the high school is rarely enforced;even the teachers dress poorly. The school lacks enormously in the communication department. I don't think the schools and the administration office works together on anything. Everybody has different information when you call or receive letters. My kids have to bring their own lunch because the food is so horrible. The brought home sandwiches that the meat was green! Yuck! My husband taught here 6 years...don't make that mistake. There is no backing by the school for teachers and no raises in 5 years. I'm a student at DVHS. I'm a senior this year and I'd just like to say that honestly, this school isn't as bad as people make it out to be. Yeah, the administration sucks, and the food sucks. But overall, majority of the teachers are FANTASTIC and have huge influences on students' lives. Sure, fights RARELY break out and people RARELY smoke on campus, but can you name a campus where that doesn't happen? Teenagers will be teenagers. They'll be rebellious if they want, not all kids are good. And quite frankly that's not the school's fault, that is solely the parents way of parenting their kids. Bullying is really non-existant at this school as well. People really aren't even mean, everyone's just loud. And when there's a new kid, the word usually quickly goes around and people are anxious to make friends with them. Del Valle is a fine school. teachers, atleast those that stay motivate and support our future as we are looked down upon, i have a great love for my school wouldnt trade it for the world There are many excellent involved teachers at Del Valle. The class options are great a and the support the students receive is amazing. Every person at this school is dedicated to my child behavior And education. They treat my son like he is part of the team. We always been welcome and accepted. Even with his disability the school always help my child fit in. I love my child high school The vast majority of teachers in this school go out of their way to ensure all students succeed. This school provides students with Chromebooks and all class materials so that students don't need to pay for them. Like any school Del Valle has its issues but by far and large this is a great school! Great athletics facilities and opportunities especially now. Modern building and good location.
