column3: Our two daughters, academically strong and from an affluent family did very well at AHS. Lots of AP options, talented teachers, good athletics and an outstanding art/music/drama program. Admin is so-so and has not been wholly stable. We were really very happy there. I just read many of the negative reviews. Many of these issues are true; a student who doesn't excel academically or in a club can get lost in the shuffle. We were at another outstanding school with the same problems. Parental involvement is crucial, and without it good schools are no substitute. The alternative might be to focus attention on the students who are not succeeding but that is fraught too. I suspect that a student who hates AHS, isn't doing well academically, and has parents who can't be bothered to interact with teachers would do no better at another school. The wide mix of AHS students might make this disparity more evident though. AHS will do better now that the SOL issue is diminishing, and it could use improvements in the physical plant. It could stop doing dumb things like buying iPads for (select) students too. I am a rising senior at Albemarle High School, and while I do agree that the school has some short comings, I would like to point out that no school is perfect. Hence the reasoning for my 4/5 star review as opposed to 5/5. There are a few incompetent teachers at the school, though if you bring it up with the higher ups things normally get straightened out one way or another, but overall I love all of my teachers, they're energetic but also informative, and yes, from what I have seen the extracurriculars at the school are great, and if you want to make a new club, then simply get a couple people together and get a teacher to represent you, then you're good to go, I set up a club for my robotics group this way. Yes, I am mostly an A student, so I can't speak all that much for the academic classes and it has surprised me that some years you either take academic or a college class of the subject, no honors, Also the comment about the drugs, that was only one incident, which was then dealt with swiftly, it is not the school's fault if its students decide to deal drugs on the premises, it is the school's fault if they let it continue. Which, they didn't, it was quickly dealt with. As a parent of a 9th grader there, I was of course concerned that the school be engaged with me and have a plan set up to make the transition an easy one. I have received neither. From summer assignments that were unclear or not even handed out to some children, to no regular access to teachers it was a shock. Since the first month though, things have gotten worse. They do not offer regular access to school extracurriculars, their school computer program is completely mismanaged, and much of the staff there have gone out of there way to demonstrate a culture of unaccountability. This school has firmed in our mind that we will be moving from the school district. Don't send your kids here. My rising 10th grader had a good transition to Albemarle this year. He is involved in sports and is in all AP and honors classes. He had a great year according to his grades and liked the kids and coaches involved with sports teams. We had no major bumps and hope for the same next year! I would love to move my family back to this area just so my son could go here. I loved this school. A+ I graduated from Albemarle High in 1989 and my husband graduated from Western Albemarle High. At the time and into my adulthood Albemarle County we're rated great, so naturally we wanted our children to go to the same great schools. Under the current and previous administration, these school have focused more on putting their time, effort and money into changing school names (which surveys show NOBODY agreed with) than getting the children to and from school. They completely changed grading so nobody fails (a child can basically give up trying and going to school and pass with flying colors). Bully's get high fives from the principal and rewarded when they behave but good, well behaved kids get nothing. Dress codes are non-existent as it seems to now be a trend to show as much skin as possible. There is absolutely no discipline from the teachers anymore so drugs and fighting has escalated. Also, they seem to dumb down the lesson plans every year. It's truly amazing how much the school board and superintendent has failed us in the past 6 years. I honestly regret moving back to this county.

column1: Bangor doesn't have a lot of money, and what little it does have is not spent wisely. column3: A wonderful school....no complaints. Love the principal. Awesome kids and staff. I love the way they make the kids read daily. <3 i dont know what everyone is talking about sayin serrano sucks. serrano is amazing with grades and sports especially football. we are number 3 in california and we have respectful teachers. this school by far is the best one in the inland empire and the high desert. I attended this school for 3 years, I graduated last year, and I am currently in college. The school is very good and the teachers do their best to educate the students. The only downside I noted was some students doing drugs, some graffiti, and one or two fights. Other than that, I loved the school and I miss being there with my friends. This school is a great school, depending on the student. If you try to succeed and work with the staff, they are amazing and will really go out of their way to help you. If you don't really care and just don't try because it's more fun to mess around, the staff just doesn't like to put more attention on you because there are students who actually want to learn. I am a student who wants to learn and succeed. I take a lot of advanced classes, but also a couple of regular classes. In both, the teachers are more than willing to help. HORRIBLE SCHOOL is all I can say.. Just horrible will never send my kids to this school after knowing what I know and seeing what i've seen beware of this school just warning all... The last comment I saw opened with. This is a great s hoop depending on the student. Don't agree with the great school part. I do agree that your experience depends on the student. If you don't fit into some stereo typical mold of kid. You are chastised, bullied, picked on and made to feel so low that you no longer enjoy school. The schools approach to our particular situation was to quickly sign the student out of the school and forget it happened. There are cameras and monitors. Nothing is picked up. And in a school where popularity seems to be key. As well as an immediate fear of being put down as well. Students witness and do nothing. Bullying is a major issue in American schools. In the adult world tripping someone and throwing things at them while taunting can be a jailable offense. People choose to ignore instead of getting involved. We r losing our kids. I for one am tired of it. Our kids deserve to go to school unafraid. They should embrace it. Not fear it. Harsher laws should implemented for bullies. It is no longer a matter of kids are kids. We all go through it. I love Serrano High School. I am currently attending as a sophomore/junior and I can honestly say that I am having the best time here. Although most of the rules and teachers could be modified or taken out, it is overall the best school in the high desert. Great school. I really loved the staff and teachers there. some of them still remain as some of my favorite people; words can't express how much they have shaped my life and inspired me to be a better person. However, there was heavy racism there at Serrano. From White to Mexican to Black, they would pick on Asian kids from time to time, throwing racial slurs and threatening them without thinking. Serrano is a great school and can offer a relatively good quality of education, but if you are an Asian American, expect a great deal of hostility and racism. I've reached at Serrano high school for years and every single day it was worse. The staff would pick on the students, yes the staff!! And n words were dropped on several occasions. Also students always complained about the learning and help they were receiving. Please do not send your child here. Anything is better than this atrocious district! Serrano is a great school, it's too bad the Attendence office staff is so terrible. These ladies are so rude to parents. Pinon Mesa office staff is much more proffessional. Serrano office staff is so unapproachable I hate even going in there. Good school. "The ladies " in the front office , the worst people skills I've seen in a school. Wow, can't believe they get paid for this type of behavior. What ever the case is, they really show how unhappy they are working at this school . I feel like an outsider most of the time. If you don't fit in or if you are different, it's like people ignore you. My education is good here. I just wish I didn't have to deal with the extra. Well Serrano used to be #3 in California 4 years ago now this year it''s down to #458. Honestly it's bad now I do not even want to be at this school anymore I'm half way through high school at Serrano and the only good thing it has is sports at this point. It really has gone down the drain go there for a day and ask about the new rules that the school lies about some of there rules being a state requirement when it really isn't. Kids are stressed like crazy so it's created more fights and lower scores. Sexual harassment goes on, drugs, and bullying, I know because so stuff has happened to me and I've witnessed it and the school police is a joke they literally don't really do anything except write up speeding tickets every day. Lots of students want to drop out plus I recently talked to a counselor about a university that I'm aiming for and they put me down telling me that I can only go to VVC or other schools in the high desert I was very discouraged and going to my dream University is the only thing keeping me in school and they still didn't accept it. The school sucks and has many problems and honestly need to do something about it because if you don't "fit in" your doomed. DO NOT send your children to Serrano if they don't do sports and aren't AP students or very social. Trust me they will have a really tough 4 years and will not enjoy there high school years. I taught students with special needs. The school would constantly refer to the kids as not our kids. They were rude and once told me to carry my wheelchair bound student up the stairs because the ADA accessible elevator was broken. Staff is very clicky. Campus police was ineffective and nonchalant about property theft and damage on campus. I now have 3 children attending this school, with so many programs available to the students, there is something to do for every child. this school has a strong sense of community, and there is no school I would rather send my children to. for that matter there is no district I would rather be in than Snowline Unified.

column1: I believe this school has an extremely effective approach on their students and encourages them to excel. At WAJ your child maybe the student, the entire family is part of the school. It’s a small school (under 300) which lends itself to a close knit community. The teachers are caring and wonderful - always willing to provide extra help. We came from a private school downstate and am so pleased with the academics and extracurriculars of WAJ. If your kid is special needs stay far away. They do not care about your child's safety and will call child protective services on you if you don't do what they want you to do which is not advocate for your child. They will do everything in their power to make you miserable. Lara McAnemy was a terrible cse and she's a even worse asst superintendent. Avoid enrolling your child in this school.

column3: Hoover is a great school. I very much enjoy coming in every morning. This is something I can honestly say I have never said about another school before. I have read some of the previous reviews and I do partially agree. Most students here are the typical suburaban Abercrombie and Fitch type. The others do fall through the cracks a little. Not "fitting in" is nonsense. The majority of the student population are friendly and outgoing. Teachers will always be there to help you. If a student is in need of extra help, many teachers are happilly willing to stay late to help a struggling student. Athleticly, you will not find a better school than Hoover. We have excellent sports teams here.But watch out, it is a big school and it is easy to get lost in when you first arrive. As far as being a freshman, I cannot recall a single instance of any sort of hazing. Hoover is a school mostly frree of bullys. No one likes a bully, and any Hoover student will help a peer.The surrounding neighborhoods are a great place to live. Hoover really is a great school. this school is the best school i have ever been too. they are really nice to their students. the faculty and staff are really nice. all the principals are really nice too. i think that when i have kids i want them to go to this school. I am a graduate from Hoover High School 2012. This was a very great school. I loved my teachers they tried there best to make sure I understood the material. Ms.Kruse was the best english teacher I ever had she taught me so many new things and I actually started to like english a lot more. At Hoover I did struggle with math but only because of my previous school system. There are alot of things to get involved with at Hoover like band sports and many clubs. I was involved in FCCLA TNT FTA. I would send my child to this school hands down I am currently a student at Hoover and I love it so much!! The teachers are awesome and you can tell that they love teaching, AND the staff is awesome! As a student taking all AP, I still have time to participate in extracurriculars, as they have a ton of sports and clubs to participate in. I would definitely send my future kids here!!

column3: Elko High School is a failure making machine with very few good teachers. Most teachers belittle students yell in class and give very little instruction. The only kids who do well, would do well no matter what the circumstances. I wish that someone would come and find out exactly how bad this school is. EHS has more diversity than the neighboring high school in Spring Creek. It is a school with solid teachers who have a lot of experience. EHS was established in 1895, so it's packed with tradition and beautifully remodeled old, brick buildings. The school also offers many AP, online, and college courses. As a discerning parent, I feel that my child is in good hands at EHS. 5 stars out of 5 stars - perfect Their lunch portions are small. They are very strict they make students put their phone away and take attendance by how many kids have phones in the holder on the wall. And if you’re caught with any type of Bluetooth device whether that be AirPods or any type of headphones or smartwatches. They are confiscated. And your parent will have to come pick them up. There are lots of issues at this school. May I mention they use this system called go guardian and it blocks everything and anything. Teachers may close down any tabs, set a tab limit example you’re only allowed to have 3 tabs open at all times. They even can lock down your computer. If you skip class you will get detention. If you have bad grades detention, too many absences detention. The key to how everything works at this school is giving you consequences in some way. Now don’t get me wrong the teachers at this school are so nice!! But the admin are not and I know it’s their job to be harsh and give consequences but it’s really bad. I wouldn’t recommend.

I have 2 kids that go to Poteet and I am not moving until the graduate because the school is good. It offers clinical and my child is taking this class and is also taking dual credit classes. column1: I am looking to send my son to a Christian School next year. I have been very happy with the info I have received and to see that ALL of their teachers are required to have a BA or a BS degree. Some schools do not require teachers to have a degree and allow them to teach our children by only having a teaching certificate. This school is tops on my list right now. Happy hunting... I have three kids who attend University Christian for the last four years. My daughter just graduated and received a full scholarship to college. My son just finished 10th grade and tested for the College Placement Test and will start his college courses this summer. He was told by the FSCJ instructor that his Math score was the highest that she had graded in Duval County. I also have an upcoming 6th grader. UCS has implemented the Bridge Academy for 5th & 6th graders. They are separate from Elementary and Middle School. This program is wonderful because it prepares him for Middle School. My husband is a graduate of the school and he wouldn't have our children anywhere else. The class sizes are small and the parent teacher communication is outstanding. Our son is looking forward to the Bridge Academy and all it has to offer. It is our goal to have them at UC until they graduate. The upper school has many dual enrolment classes and extra help in taking the SAT's. We have been very pleased so far. I feel as if the facility is being run like a business and not a Christian school for children. Public schools cannot throw children out, unless they perform seriously violent acts, but they have to take them back with behavior interventions. It is my understanding that Christians show patience like in Numbers 14:18, Peter 3:9, & Romans 2:3-4. Where were the behavior interventions? Suspending 4 y/o does not teach them how to change their behavior. My daughter is a 4 y/o and I feel like this school is teaching her that people will give up on her & turn their backs on her when she needs the most guidance & has the most need. This school is teaching her that teachers don't care enough about her to help her learn how to modify her behavior. Have you heard of the saying "It takes a village.."? I also feel like the school gave up too quickly when my daughter challenged their authority. I have been a parent at University Christian School since 1999 and this school has been so wonderful to me and my family. They have provided my kids (3 of them) with a very safe, structured family environment that I always feel welcomed in. My oldest son has since graduated and is doing great, my other son is a Junior this year and has had the opportunity to experience the Online Academy as well as in class instruction and has enjoyed having the diversity of curriculum instruction, and my daughter is a 6th grader who is absolutely loving the Bridge Academy! Thank You UCS for all that you are to our community! This school is not the place to send your children if you want them to get a good Christian education. Even though this school says it is a Christian school it does not support its claim. Horrible education and the faculty are not doing there job right. I go here and I am not satisfied with my education. As I read the reviews, I see that most have gone through the same things I did. My oldest began UC in k5 and graduated from UC. During that time, I loved this school. BUT, he was my perfect student. When it came to my other children, I found a complete lack of compassion for the students by the administration, a dictatorial and uncaring superintendent and seniors barely attaining combined SAT scores of 1000. In fact, the majority of graduates were not attending college at all or were only accepted by fscj. I could see no difference between uc and a lower tier public school, so my kids no longer attend there. I still have a special place in my heart for the school and many of its faculty, staff and students, but my kids deserve much better and are getting it elsewhere. As one parent said, uc is not college prep or Christian, so what's the point? It is funny that a parent would write that UC students primarily go to FSCJ, Not that I am knocking this college, but that is an UNTRUE statement. I recently inquired about the percentages and was given a completely different answer than that. Knowing many of the students that graduated in the class of 2012, I found that at least half of them were going to a state university such as UNF (primarily), UF, UCF, and FSU. There were a few of them continuing their education at FSCJ to obtain their AA, but what I find most incredible that everyone that I spoke with did not feel that not continuing their education was an option! They felt prepared and ready for the next chapter in their life and were excited. I think if we want to compare apples to apples here, UC has VERY high percentages of continued education over public schools. Their test scores were published and they are above the national average... I wish people would gain facts instead of gossip before posting things. I went to the source and asked a lot of questions and was given accurate information from the CollegeBoard. I am currently a student at University Christian School, and have attended for four years. University Christian provides a solid foundation and saving knowledge of Jesus Christ and a family setting. If you, as a student, are willing to develope a strong relationship with faculty, instead of dodging the rules, your experience at UC would be so much better. Unless you've experienced University Christians School for your self I ask that you not speak out negatively upon our school. There's been much succes within and will continue to be, as long as we're up and running. I've been going to this school since k-5 and I love it. I could never think of going to another school and having the same experiences I do there as I have here. The love and compassion shown by the administration and faculty makes it the best school ever! Hello I am a student at university christian school i am a 9th grader and ive been going to university christian school since kindergarten and ive loved everyday of it. i know everyone that goes here and i love all of the teachers. espcially now that im a high schooler and were all using the ipads its alot different but i like it everything is becoming electronic and its fun i definitely reccomend this school to anyone who wants their child to get a good christian education I've been a student at University Christian for four years and, I must say, I love it! As soon as I started at UC, I felt like I belonged. The staff here is always willing to serve, and us students have picked that up along the way as well. I am amazed at the level of concern that University Christian has put in my understanding of the bible and my faith. I love my school! I have been at UC for 3 years now and I love it! I grew up in a public school system and moved here my sophomore year and experienced more growth and community than I have in my entire life. The students are friendly and genuine, the teachers are loving and caring, and the faculty and other staff reflect the love of Christ in every aspect of their life. Not only are the academics excellent here, but also University Christian truly is showing kids the love of Christ through worship, academics, sports, and all other school activities. UC is also very mission oriented, having multiple service opportunities and mission opportunities theoughout the year. This school is worth your time and money and will show you what a true Christian education is all about. I have been at University Christian School for four years. I have loved every moment of my time here. The staff is so caring and passionate about not only your school work, but your spiritual life as well. That is something that makes this school so special. I have been at University Christian a total of nine years. I absolutely love the family atmosphere. I love the fact that in every class there is a Biblical lesson that is being taught. Our teachers really care about you, and they show it. The teachers are very understanding and are willing to work with you. The number one goal at University Christian is that every student will come to have a saving knowledge of Jesus Christ. You can sense that. We have chapel every Thursday. Chapel is amazing. We have a worship team and a speaker that brings a well delivered worship service. Many times you will see students on their knees, worshipping and surrendering to God. During these chapels you can definitely sense the Holy Spirit working. This is why I love this school so much, because the Christ-centered environment you are around with great mentors and spiritually sensitive students. I am a senior at UC and I was a new student last year. One of the truely remarkable things about UC that distinguishes it from any other private school I've been to is the family environment among the students and staff. From my very first day everyone made me feel as though I already belonged in the UC family. The techers are excellent and it's obvious that they care about the students, not just academically, but also personally and spiritually.The administration is also very helpful and supprtive in getting UC students to their next levels of education. I am currently applyingfor the US Air Force Academy, and because UC is much smaller than a regular public school, the administration has been readily available to help me with the numerous forms and documents. If parents want their kids to make great friends and receive a solid Christian education, I would definately encourage them to send their kids to UC! I second the dismal rating because of the (non) public response this allegedly CHRISTIAN school had to one of its students publishing political rants about his fellow citizens. Ignorant rants have repercussions in real life - but not at this "Christian" school? Ask why. I just wanted to add to this page that University Christian has proven to be the leading school in technology and the iPads have made a huge difference in the way learning is done! We are thankful for this and excited to see the advancement this will have on the kids education! Way to go UC!! My school maked me feel welcome when I came here last year ,I also love working with iPads . My school is great at making you feel welcome, they have an amazing 8th grade class!!!!!! My school is awesome because we have a great student council and the guidance counselor rocks. The iPads are a really cool advancement to our school. They are a great learning source. Their teachers are friendly and care about each students need. I'm a seventh grader and I have been here since first grade. I've learned a lot about Christ and I chose to follow Him here. This school is a great place for both school and sport lovers. It also has great staff and teachers, eager to help the student. We also use technology to our advantage as we use iPads to read, write, and just have fun. The school offers from pre-k to 12th grade with a variety of events and exciting fundraisers. University also offers a variety of sports such as football, soccer, cheer, baseball, and more along with excellent coaches. This is the best school I have ever gone to in my entire life. I'm new here, but the first day I walked in, I could feel the love. They welcomed me with open arms and taught me all about Christ. I'm a better person because of UC and its teachers. Words will never be able to describe the gift that UCS has given my son. The teachers, coaches and administration not only care for their students success academically but for the success of their social wellbeing. We will leave with a more confident, caring, healthy, and intelligent young man all because UCS refused to never give up on him! What a testament to their mission of truth, tradition and transformation. Submitted by a parent As a military family, we depend on Great Schools alot. It should be noted that this is an "urban" Christian school. It is a ministry for the church. Our child was exposed to much more than if he had been at a public school. We will not be returning next year. If you decide to enroll your child in this school, I HIGHLY recommend getting involved to see the school from the inside. Volunteer to substitute and you will see exactly what takes place in the classroom. UC is a Christ centered school that focuses on reaching kid's for Christ. It is academically sound, with teachers that care for the students, starting in Kindergarten and going through seniors! As with ANY school, people will always find areas in need of improvement. The administration is always listening and working to improve all aspects of the school. There are improvements each and every year, which shows how much the leadership cares about improving UCS! We love this school. As alumni, sending our children to this school has always been a priority. The teachers and staff at this school make our children feel loved and keep them looking forward to coming to school each day. The experience we have at UC is unmatched by any other in Jacksonville. The size, community, education, love and friendship that are provided by this school make the cost completely worth the investment! This is a terrible school! Absolutely nothing Christian about it. There is no communication between the school and parents. Some of the teachers are the most rude and uncaring Christians I have ever met. My sons 2 years there was a waste of money. The only thing they seem to care about are sports. In fact they will close the school down for a football game but will not call you it tell you the cops are at the school searching students for drugs. Glad my kid is out of that school! Much safer now! My children have just started their 5th year at University Christian School. The school is not perfect and neither are my children. However, it is the perfect fit for them. They have been nurtured, treated kindly and blessed by their teachers. Academics are strong and the teachers have high expectations for the students. Students have to work and are stretched to do their best. I love schoology because it gives parents so much more info than programs like ed-line and etc. I can check grades, assignments and completed work. There are comments on assignments helping me to know what my kids can do better in the future. Overall it is a wonderful school. I wouldn't send my kids anywhere else in Jacksonville. This is our families second year at University Christian School and with each passing year I love this place more and more! My child comes home excited to learn each day. He is being challenged and loved by his teacher. I am proud to have him at such a Christ-centered school where we work hand in hand with the teachers and staff. I am also encouraged that the administrators are easy to contact and don't just sit behind desks all day, they are in the halls with the students, investing in them! GREAT SCHOOL! University Christian is more than a school, it's a family. I have 2 sons at the school and they are interested in very different things. Academically they are both challenged daily. I love this school! I cannot say enough about how much we love University Christian School. From the teachers and administration to the quality of education, our experience has been more than we could ever have expected. We have watched our children improve academically and mature spiritually with such great staff/administration examples. All of our extended family live in other parts of the country and we've been so blessed to see how the UC community has loved on us and our kids and become truly family to ours. There is so much to be excited about at UC. It seems like they are always looking for ways to improve the atmosphere of the school whether it be through facility improvements or technology advancements as well as expanding the music/band department and other ways/programs that my kids will get to take part in. My children are constantly telling me every week about the exciting chapel services, the creative lessons the teachers are using, the new friends, extra-curricular activities, upcoming events..etc. UC has proven to be such a positive, and awesome experience for our family. We absolutely take pride in our school and are always privileged to be able to let others know that we are University Christians! I love, love, love this school. I graduated from UC years ago and now I am privileged to send my own kids there. I have been thoroughly impressed with all of positive changes that have happened since I was a student. UC is more than just a school, its a family. I couldn't imagine sending my kids anywhere else and knowing they are being loved and getting a Christ centered education. I look forward to watching my kids thrive at UC and for them to complete their school careers there. Go Christains!!! My children have been attending University Christian for many years. Those that have graduated have been prepared academically and socially to venture out into life and go after and achieve their goals. The faculty and staff really care about how the students are doing both in school and life. They take the time to mentor them and show them what their life can be like with care and prayer. Their relationships with Christ have become stronger and exciting. Over the last five years there have been tremendous changes in the facilities and curriculum, that have geared my students for life as they go to college. UCS has been part of our family for many years and the love and support that my children have received will be with the for the rest of their lives. The faculty and staff of University Christian have a genuine concern for your child as well as the entire family. The Spiritual and Academic achievements of the students are UCS are outstanding. This school is a huge blessing to our community. The teachers make sure that every student has come to knowledge of Jesus Christ and provide quality education in every class. The classes are excellent and they provide AP courses as well as extracurricular classes to get students prepared for College. Our son has been in UCS since K5. He is currently in the elementary level and we have enjoyed our experience. UCS is solid academically and he is being challenged and succeeding. He is growing socially and has developed great friendships. The school is a community and we like that it is not a bubble but a great representation of the Jacksonville community. Last, the school is a bargain tuition wise for what the education he is receiving. I don't feel that they accept outside students very well. If you don't attend their church you are ignored. Our experience was absolutely terrible. Our neighborhood is zoned for Terry Parker High and I believe she would have been better off there (for free). It is sad because we were very excited about this school to build her faith and protect her heart. We had the opposite happen. From day one, she was harassed and bullied to the point that her mental health was suffering. At the tour, every kid looked extremely respectful and sweet. When she got to the school, it was a complete bait and switch. The one thing positive I can say is that the instruction from the teachers is great and communication is timely. We went to the online academy because she cannot take the peer influences anymore and to my knowledge, nothing will be done to the kids who have harassed her this year. Huge mistake & I regret ever sending our 11 yr old to UCS. We transferred after one year as he was bullied & exposed to things I didn’t expect from a “Christian” school. This school’s main priority is athletics not academics. The teachers I dealt with were caring & loved to teach for the most part but they seem overwhelmed. Many of the students attend only because it’s safer than some of the public schools. University Christian School is a great place to have your children excel in their learning by incorporating traditional curriculum with a Biblical world view and how to prepare our young adults and children for real world situations. The classes are smaller size than the average public school which works well for teachers and students in developing a cohesive learning environment. Personally, I have witnessed a significant growth and improvement in both of my children while attending this school. I would encourage anyone looking to find a better educational community for their family to invest in UCS. UCS does accept scholarships, has an enormous amount of athletic programs as well as extracurricular activities to fit all interests and skill sets. Love God & Love People. Excellent school with great teachers, administrators, and coaches who really care about your son or daughter. We moved to the area from out of state and it's been nothing but a top notch experience for our son. You won't find a better school for the price. Great leadership from the top down. Highly recommend! Our son attended from 8th grade to 12th and excelled at UCS. The teachers and staff were wonderful and truly cared for my son's well-being and education. I grew up in the Jacksonville public school system and was in no way about to put our child through that. From day 1, the students were very friendly to our son and even invited him to play sports, join the Beta Club and even the National Honors Society - none of which we were even thinking about when we joined UCS. He also took several computer training and programming courses and was even awarded a STEM scholarship for college. UCS also issues students iPads that he was able to keep at graduation. Although being shy as first, he has made many lifelong friends which not only includes students but teachers, coaches and staff as well. We also love watching the various sports teams which usually make it to the playoffs. It's really exciting to attend these events. Our son even played in DOAK Campbell stadium for the State Championship. Starting our school search, we met with and physically toured "many" of the private schools in Jacksonville. We did a lot of research and a lot of praying before making the decision to attend University Christian. We have had a great experience are so thankful of the decision we made. Our son has been accepted to Stetson, University of West Florida, Jacksonville University and was awarded merit scholarships and a STEM scholarship which pays for most of his private college tuition. We are so grateful for our experience and relationships made at University Christian School.

column3: This is a best school, my kids have a lot of help, the teachers are really helpfull with the kids I definally recommended. Some teachers are great, especially the APE teachers. Some are not up to par...don't return emails or.phone calls, inflexible with student needs. Some of the office staff don't seem to care about trying to help students to succeed. Too many just collecting a paycheck. Ramona High School is amazing Students get out of school what they and their parents are willing to put into it. This is true in any school district. Both my daughters attended Ramona High School and it prepared them for entrance into two exceptional Colleges not only in academics but sports as well. The teachers were wonderful as was the entire High School experience. I have been in this area for 15 years. I know of so many kids that have moved on to wonderful things after graduating from RHS. Like ALL schools, there are students who are not a fit with the program - but Ramona has many alternatives available in their district for those that do not fit within the traditional school. When school first started there was no working air conditioning in my 6th period. It was 100 degrees outside after lunch and we have no air conditioning! my teacher emailed the principal several times, my mom called the principal 4 times and left several messages, and she called the district twice yet nobody got back to her. this went on for 2 weeks. Im a Sophmore attending Ramona high school and I can give you different insight besides the smiling faces that the super intentons get. teachers do not want to be there. There is only really only a handful of teachers that care if you graduate and want you to grow as a person in their classroom and outside of school. It is frustrating for the student when the teacher doesn't care. I'm a smart girl, I've always had good grades (A's and maybe a few B's) but since I have attended Ramona high school I've gotten D's, go to tutoring everyday after school because my teacher cannot teach me. Last year my math teacher was practically incapable, I got a D. this year my teacher does not care (and yes he's admitted it). How is that fair for me? We also have a drug problem, limited resources, This school is a joke to the community and the expectations of parents and students. They all seem to just be getting a pay check and not teaching at all. In fact I don't think they are capable of teaching especially the math teachers. Sending your child here is a total waste of time someone really needs to talk to the kids and get the real story on what is going on at Ramona High School. Am gay. Can not remember ever being less supported by any school I have ever attended, including my elementary school and the local junior college. Barely survived my high school experience- was suicidal for most of it. 0/10 would not recommend to any queer student. Not that you really have a choice as there is a limited number of high schools in the area. But really if you're queer and have a choice, go anywhere else. My kids went to Ramona High School before we moved to another area. Overall the school is o.k. Definite grade inflation compared to some other districts. Too many kids are getting AP credit for advanced classes and not passing the AP tests. Even a marginal student is guaranteed a B if they do their homework. The facilities are old and the campus is rundown. Teachers are hit and miss; some good and some not so good. Ramona High School seems to be on a steady decline as they lose good teachers and continue to lower expectations on students. I would rate this school 0 stars if possible. They are very understaffed and most classes have 40+ students in them. This is very dangerous as the teacher cannot keep up with the students. They also have no regard for students in need of help academically and personally. My nephew got kicked out of school just 2 months before graduation and they gave us no options otherwise. Unbelievable

column1: I'm really happy about this new principal at high school of natalia, she is making a difference for good there. High school has a excellent academic curriculum and a good athletic system. I will not move my boy from high school where he is already getting credit hours for college and he is only in 10 grade. After my first two weeks there, I saw minimal cleaning and have gotten sick from the school. They have one unproductive and inconsistent counselor, not to mention the messy admin. Instead of doing things right they tell how its, "nonnegotiable" to not only students but staff. They had put two different honors classes in the same period, leaving none for other periods so some students may have no better choices. They have lack of preparation leaving students and staff to do everything last minute like pep rallies and do a poor job of keeping students excited. Students are very obnoxious, no real discipline and school is not strict at all. No one pays attention, teachers aren't very engaged, and the curriculum choices aren't big. Breakfast is served in class, if you're lucky enough to get someone to take it to your classroom. Menu is lacking and boring, always one choice for lunch which lacks any flavor and generally is disgusting. A lot of funding was put into technology, with it being not that great and unused. Teachers rely on students having their phones at hand rather than going to a computer lab or teaching them in their notes, making learning a bit useless; some students may not have technology able for them. Instead of getting assigned lockers you have to sign up for them. Very small district, not worth living in or attending to. Lack of staff, instead of holding an event somewhere they would rather do it outside so they do not have to clean. Would not recommend.

column1: Great school and it has a lot of extra curricular's that really help the students to stay involved. teachers are committed and always ready to answer questions and be involved in the students academic progress. Any kid looking for a good high school that really pays attention to you should try this school out for sure I have been working with Essex Street Academy for the past year and think they are doing an amazing job. The principal, teachers, social workers and other staff members I have been in contact with are competent individuals and deeply committed to provide a safe school environment as they care for their students. The faculty and leadership of the school is exemplary and care about the students. My child is a freshman this year. The principal and vice-principal are dedicated to the students and the school. They encourage and facilitate opportunities for parent involvement. The teacher/advisors continue a high-level of communication with students and parents and are committed to the success of their students.

I graduated from Llano we never would have dreamed of treating kids the way the kids now do. Instead of fixing the problem and asking a child why they are acting out they want the kid to go get help. Stop the real problem the kids that are the bullies. Not the victims.

column1: I've gone to Delhi schools since Kindergarden. Now as a Senior approaching graduation quickly, I can truthfully say Delhi is a great school. The staff, Administration and especially the teachers are amazing. The English department is my favorite. I will miss Delhi, as I approach a new life, which Delhi has spread my wings and has prepared me for anything in my future Over the course of the past years up until this year, I can assure that Delhi High School has improved considerably. The years 2012 - 2013 introduced a new opportunity for Delhi, not just staff wise, but also curriculum wise. The music program restarted this year with a new energy, introducing a new program for students to be creative. Delhi now has a winter percussion ensemble, possibly for next year a new drum corp, and possibly a color guard. There's been new propositions, along with donations from the government, and new changes. However, as I graduated this year I won't be able to experience those changes for the next year. However, Delhi High School has the potential of becoming a great school. There are no cliques here, as mentioned before, but there are groups. Through my experience here there has been racism, but only on the behalf of the ignorant wannabe gangsters. Despite that, Delhi High School is a great school for your children to attend, but at the same time we're still in a closed box. The new principal Mr. Arista is trying to get his students out there, to be outside of the box. Delhi High School just earned a 6 year accreditation from WASC. The staff is amazing as are the students. The stereotype and negativity that precedes most conversations about the school are easily squashed. New Principal this year, but high expectations and endeavors remain. The science Academy is one of the best and only articulated academies in the valley, it send 90% of all students that complete the program to four year colleges. It name is DMAS, they work with colleges and have amazing leader of the program.

column3: Superior visual, media and performing arts course work. Great athletics. Awesome after school theatre program- both plays and musical offered. Jazz, concert and award winning marching band. Chorus, guitar, music theatre and performing arts management courses. Stagecraft, studio art, construction, technology classes, AP classes, lipdub, DPAC After Dark Concerts, and so many other exciting offerings for students that are interested in the only performing and visual and media arts high school of its kind in Berkshire county. New high school; state of the art facilities. Great, like minded student centered staff and administration. I really wouldn't rate this school very good, I've been to multiple schools but this was was probably my least favorite. I also recommend packing lunches because the lunch usually isn't good. I've heard they're trying to improve it recently though, wish they did that while I was there. This school is a joke, there are some good teachers but they're outweighed by the teachers that genuinely don't care about the students and are on power trips 24/7. I was forced into classes that I didn't want and was refused a change of classes when other students (well liked) had no problem changing classes at a later date. God forbid if you're a minority or have a 504/IEP because you won't be respected. The teachers don't take time to help students understand any work and then blame the student for not paying attention when they ask for help. We had a finance class once but it was really a math class with money word problems. Don't go here if you have issues with panic attacks or breakdowns, I had a teacher who would point and laugh at students having panic attacks. The lunch is just whatever they can find that hasn't got mold on it and everything smells terrible; you also have to pay for water and there is no lactose free milk available. A lot of girls had been sexually harassed by some boy and when they reported him the school did nothing. So many teachers verbally abuse students and then play victim and we don't have funding so we can't replace teachers. The only time we ever replaced a teacher during a school year was because they had thrown a heavy book at a student and it was caught on video, they were fired after a few days because the family could've sued. This isn't a school, it's a circus.

column1: My child is a senior at DHS and is excited about starting college this fall yet she often tells me that she will miss her high school teachers. She admires most of her teachers and has excelled particularly in those classes. I feel that she is ready for college and DHS has a big part in this.

column3: Absolutely wonderful so far. The JROTC program is great and students are very involved in helping out in the community. AP and Honors teachers are very engaged and care for their students. As with any High School, students must make an effort to learn and do their best. Regular classes may have students that are not as interested in learning but then again that is with all schools. Overall, a great school with a caring staff/faculty. Prepared me for not only a great military career but allowed me to succeed beyond my wildest imagination in college....GO COBRAS!!!! I believe the school will push students through just to get more funding for the next year, An 11th grade student should know how to do simple fractions, but as I was told, the teacher has NOT taught us that yet, but he got an A for the course. How does that happen? SAD WORLD WE LIVE IN WITH HHS We have 6 kids. 3 of them have already graduated from HHS and we have 3 more on their way. HHS is an outstanding school. They have many different opportunities for the students. Yes they ask for alot of family participation...but that's what makes them so great!! Any student that has the opportunity to spend their high school years here.... Should be honored!! The administration at this school is horrible! The administrators bully everyone: students, faculty and staff. They need to be fired and replaced. Horrible. Save your child the heartache and avoid this school. Even with medical issues and IEPs they do less than the bare minimum. I can honestly say the horrible administration at this school cares nothing about the kids. They bully the parents, staff, and students. If I could have rated them lower than one star I wouldn't have hesitated. Horrible school, principal thinks he’s a football coach and that’s ALL HE CARES ABOUT and has proven football comes FIRST!! Staff I highly unprofessional and refused to help with anything and told me that I was a trouble maker and a instigator and swept my problems under the carpet and wanted to blame me It was terrible and im glad I transfered out administration went out of there way to put me in advance courses even though I had a low G.P.A and wouldn't let me out which caused me to struggle in school and made me fail algebra 2.Not to mention the many times students are openly bullied or racial slurs are used and the staff does nothing. I am a gifted student, so I could pass by, but overall this school just isn't up to par. The administration was not focused on success as much as they should've been. If you are a prospective student, do NOT take AP classes here unless they are with Vachon or Wood! Dual enrollment is the way to go! Make the most of it, try to enjoy high school. Also - if you are looking into joining the marching band here... look somewhere else. The teachers and staff have Great parent teacher communication to give students every opportunity to graduate. If the student don't take advantage of their offerings it is not the blame of the school. So far my experience with Hudson high school is not a good one. Some of the teachers , not all seem to not care about whether these kids get an education. If a child ask questions, they are told it's not up for discussion. Very disappointed that they seem to have no interest in the kids. What is wroughly with Pasco county teachers? I am embarrassed for you. This school does not support students in a way for them to be successful. They use social media to communicate with the student body about events and things for students. While that may seem beneficial, some students don't have the privileges to check social media or see upcoming events. When I transferred from a school in a different state, which was very advanced, I came here expecting the bare minimum and received a below average performance. I missed out on opportunities such as the Cambridge Program which would help me get college credits and guarantee a Bright Futures Scholarship. I missed out on sports because I was not sure when tryouts started and waited until the next year. Some of the teachers are great but some prioritize being friends with the students instead of teaching, which cuts into other peoples time. Underlying problems still exists within the school even with law enforcement, such as drugs throughout students, a some what judgemental and unsupportive environment. I would not recommend taking your students to this school unless your students are interested in athletic pride. my child is one of the only black students in the whole school, he has been discriminated against and called slurs on multiple occasions. The staff does nothing, the teachers, and administration is complicit with bullying and racism. I urge anyone who doesn't want their kids hanging out with racists to choose a different school for thier children. now on another note, the school is filthy and many students here don't have good hygiene. I visted a few months ago for a parent teacher conference and i saw roaches scurrying around. Teens are left and right hitting vapes in class and using chewing tobacco some even spit it out into bottles and keep the bottles with them, teachers don't care and the students who are caught are not dealt with. This is not an environment fit for learning. Another topic id like to mention is this school has no security, the doors to most of the classrooms don't lock and there isn't a serious protocol for school shootings. my son told me when they had everyone rounded up in the gym for a drill that there was only do much they could do to secure the gym and the doors open from the outside had something actually occurred he didn't feel safe. column3: Camden Hills Regional High School is one of the better schools in Mid-Coast Maine and is a relatively new facility, thanks to the dollars that were once here when MBNA was in town. There are some outstanding teachers who are dedicated to education and make the extra effort to challenge their students, communicate with parents, and are available on a consistent basis for help. However, because of the relatively high number of students per teacher, the teachers are swamped and aren't always available for help. Many, many students have to use the local private tutoring services for help and even the school's guidance counselors recommend them. The administration is fair, at best, and are more of the " the crowd control and hall monitor" philosophy as opposed to "educators". There is no student ranking here which a lot of colleges prefer. Drug sniffing dogs were advocated at one point to help control the fairly prolific use of illegal substances, but were turned down. Unfortunately, admitting there is an issue outweighed the benefit of really trying to stem the problem. While, overall, a better school than most in the area due to higher median incomes, it's not perfect. This School stoops to the lowest levels when countered by [aretns and community members, leading many kids to feel that there expression, and speech is being stripped from them, piece by piece.

column1: I am a BCA freshman and I have to say that this school is great. I admit, that when I first joined the shcool I was mad that I had to follow strict rules and, that the building itself was so small. But now that I think about it, this school feels like a second home to me, it's small but that just proves how much more help you'll get here. Also, there are many great oppertunities at BCA that I know other schools wont give me, so I guess in simple words, BCA is the best! The teachers in this school are so kind and they make understand every thing. Also the staff are so friendly. THIS IS A GREAT SCHOOL AND I WANT MY DAUGHTER TO GO THERE NEXT YEAR I graduated from here in 2006, it's a good school for those who want an unconventional high school experience. The teachers were good, and some prepared you for college. I'm glad to see it kept up the good work all these years. I go to this school now and it is a great opportunity. It is fun with the people in it and its easy to make friends. By the time I enter college, I will be in my sophomore year. So that's less money to spend! For the most part, the teachers are fine. However, once the students get to campus, some of the "college classes " aren't taught by actual professors and most are entry level bc staff. The psychology professor, Amanda, my daughter told me is very good. And please have your kids be careful on social mediamedia, even private, because the school is small and worry about the personal aspects as well. This is a great school my son went here for one year but after coming from a larger school he did not like it so he moved with his dad and transfered. I think this is a great school for any student coming in as a freshmen as they won't feel lost and the smaller setting and student body is more welcoming. The school is very structured and the teachers and staff are familiar with each student since the school is small. Students also have the ability to gain College credits once they go to the Brooklyn College Campus in which i feel is a great opportunity. It was good I didn't have to much to complain about except the fact that we don't get respect from some of the teachers This school is an the best kept secret of Brooklyn. My daughter went there and graduated his year. She is offto Suny, Albany. BAC prepares their students for all parts of life. She was academically prepared.. She took all A.P. Courses thatchallenged her thinking and prepared her to do college level work. Outside of academics, her teachers were there for any questions,or things she needed to speak to an adult about. I'm so happy that she graduated BAC. The school is clean, beautiful, and looks new. Theyhave two campuses and by the time you get to 11th grade the second campus, she told me she felt like a college student. She loved it. I don'tthink BAC is for every child. They have to want to go to college because they should take advantage of BAC's college level courses. She graduated with over 20 college credits. This saves her time and money. BAC teachers expect a lot from their students and I like that. This school is not one of theschools you take the test to get into. But it should be, since it is not, this is why you should try to get your child into BAC!!!

column1: I graduated from South last May, and I don't think I really could have asked for much better! Teachers here really teach students how to think, and they care A LOT about students' well-being, in and out of the classroom. The variety of courses does have some to be desired, but in my observation, academics seem to be better here than at most other schools. In fact, I've found that many of my classes at South moved faster and covered the same material as college-level courses. The administration isn't always great, but the teachers make up for it with the work they do. Of course, South doesn't have all the fancy facilities that some bigger schools have, but I feel that students learn to work that much better because of it. Another perk to this school is that students can try out all the different activities they want. It's not at all unusual for the captain of the football team to also be captain of the academic team. Overall, it's a great school with great academics, great teaching, and a fantastic balance between school and the rest of life. My sons went to this school and it is a great school. Kids all have names and aren't just numbers like at the bigger schools. Teachers are all willing to help the students if they are having trouble or get behind. Small school with teachers who care about their students. Great learning environment for the kids, glad I went there and glad my kids had the opportunity to learn there as well.

column3: I attended Manhasset for my 9th grade and half of 10th grade years. Though the teachers and staff were phenomenal, and helped me leave, the environment in this school created by the kids was very exclusive. You were either in a group or out of it - and if you weren't able to be classified, you were bullied and picked on. I was bullied so badly that I had to leave the school in the middle of my sophomore year. I was shocked at some of the reviews I read regarding Manhasset schools. I attended the public schools in Manhasset from a young age, graduated, went to an Ivy League school and then a superb law school. I moved back to Manhasset so my children can obtain the same great education I did. One of my children is special needs and is thriving at Manhasset due to the superlative teachers and administration. The facilities are not falling apart. They are old, solid and well-built. Classic and well-maintained. The school is a safe place and vibrant place to learn. I don't even know where to begin. Teachers- a select few teachers are phenomenal while others deserve to be fired immediately. A good majority do nothing and just collect money. Others go above and beyond for students which is great. After-school activities- sports are everything. If you aren't playing one, expect to be lonely and picked on for all of middle and high school. Facilities- at least the school is quite nice looking. It was built in the late 1900's during as a Works Projects Adminstration and was tastefully decorated with eccentric moldings and tile details. Unlike earlier reviews, THE SCHOOL IS NOT FALLING APART. It was fixed recently. Overall- unless you or your kid aspires to be a lacrosse player, or a home designer looking for inspiration, STAY AWAY. SERIOUSLY. This school is far greater than it is described in many of the comments. Minority students used to be bullied, but now they get much help from teachers or other faculty members, and also from peer students. Teachers are great and the courses offered are excellent. However, some students tend not to welcome newcomers, especially when they are foreigners or English learners. If you are one of them, you may be hit by your shoulder, mocked, or excluded from your classmates for no reason. If anything happens, I recommend going to any ENL teachers, or the principal. Nowadays, the faculty members are highly aware of racism which is unfortunately still going on in the community, and they are willing to resolve the problem.

column3: I am a former student who graduated from PA. There are pros and cons to this school. Some teachers & their methods are indeed questionable. But I'll elaborate more on the good teachers I came across. Mr. Savoia, History ,Mr. Fraraccio, History teacher, Ms. Stepash, Art teacher, Mrs. Massopust, Art teacher (sometimey, but good) Mrs. Barrios excellent spanish teacher with great discipline. (She teaches you beyond the classroom walls) Mrs. Terell History teacher & there are so many more who at this time I can't remember their names...it's been a while since I've been there, the principle was my VP in Junior high. She's strong, firm but not cold, kind in fact. I'd say there are many things wrong with some of the staff but there are some amazing teachers involved hands on in the school--but I remember caring more about my friends' business back then. I think most teenagers are. Perth Amboy HS is not an "ideal" hs at all, but it has produced many successful students. I graduated 2 yrs ago and am attending one of the top colleges in NJ. The community in which the high school is in is an urban community, thus there are a lack of conventional resources (money, books, class size) available at the school. There are always questionable teachers, but the ones I have encountered have made significant use of the resources available to them. It's not an easy job, but success has been a product. The kids live in a poverty stricken neighborhood in which crime rates are higher in comparison with other communities. As teenagers, this influence can be overwhelming but with PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT & SUPPORT, this can be overcome. The failing test scores are the result of the lack of resources available (i.e. tutoring time) and the issue with standardized testing. The majority of PA is Hispanic with many being English language learners. These standardized tests are not altered for diff. cultures and languages! All in all, the students of PA face challenges but success is possible with effective use of resources and instruction, parental involvement, & dedication. We are so excited about all of the changes that have happened at the high school this school year. The school looks better than ever and the administration truly cares about the students and staff. Great place to be! I love and miss my high school Excellent!!!! Great school for your children to be at.

The school is very diverse, has a lot of clubs, the sports team are awesome and there is a lot of parent involvement. The teachers are very dedicated and sincerely care about the students. The principal is also very involved , hands on kind of guy. I am very proud to be a MMHS parent, my youngest just started her freshman year and i know she will have a great learning experience throughout the next 4 years! I couldn't wait until my girls moved from Challenger to MMHS. The teachers and admin are respectful and considerate of their individual needs. The amount of clubs, activities and sports teams is never-ending. I thank all personnel involved for the successes of my children. Their enthusiasm for adventures and learning would not be this great without your involvement and care. Thank you for a safe environment where our children can thrive. Mira Mesa High School is an awesome School with a caring and committed staff. The diversity our School offers is unmatched and adds to the overall growth of our kids. If that isn't example enough in choosing Mira Mesa over Scripps the spelling and grammar errors offered by the supposed Scripps parent shows the education expectations between the two schools. Having had 2 kids graduate from MMHS and a junior in the SchooI now, I know that that type of spelling and grammar is considered an embarrassment and wouldn't be tolerated at our School. The kid's and parent's that have been in and around MMHS know what we have and we are proud of all it has to offer. GO MARAUDERS!!!! Outstanding school. My Sr. and Fr. both have different learning styles and are on college prep path. I feel each are getting the appropriate levels of academic rigor to support their success in college. Top notch AP program- including Fine Arts. High pass rate for AP exams. My child will enter college with nearly a years worth of AP credit transferred. Extra-curricular activities are strongly encouraged and are supporting the development of the whole student. Both of my kids participate in sports and interest based activities. Overall very pleased with the school and what it is providing my family. his school is a horrible school. U should transfer them out immediately The teachers dont give the students any homework. Bad level of education and teachers give students 4.0 gpas end end up doing below basic education level resulting rejection from colleges. if you want your childeren to suceed take them to scripps ranch high school. the best highschoool in san diego. The best choice i ever made in my childs life. Its worth renting a place over there to get your children enrolled. Now one of them goes to harvard and the othere at UCLA. Marshall middle is a good school for middles school students. My son left in 10th grade just a week ago. Now he is saying that he is learning and his chemistry teacher is giving him so much to learn. He stays after school with UCSD profesers to learn about college as he is going to be the first one from our family to go. I really like Mira Mesa High School! There are so many great activities. Teachers are supportive. This is an amazing school! It offers a large number of diverse activities that make individuals well rounded. They have obtained the perfect balance of academics and extra curricular thus producing successful, educated, well rounded people who simultaneously have friends and lives. Although this school is roughly 40 API points lower than Scripps Ranch High School, it is much more school-like and way less life-less. Not to mention the fact that all of the staff are caring individuals who care about the students' success. This school offers a full variety of academic programs and resources including a long list of AP courses available beginning in 9th grade. Several languages are offered; my child is currently in Spanish 5-6. There are more than 16 sports and 53 clubs, plus band, ASB, theater, etc. The community is also very supportive of the school. My student is a sophmore and so far has been very successful both academically and socially. He plays sports, is in AP classes, does community service through the school and attends many of the additional activities they offer. This is a well rounded, diverse, high achieving, resource filled school. This school is just unorganized when it comes to office maintenance. I was being transferred into this school and I was not helped at all the first day of school. The office was in chaos and the staff was just rude. The attendance clerk is just rude and very sarcastic. The security staff just rides around in their golf carts not actually helping anyone. The system and campus is in chaos and possibly ruins. The biggest regret being transferred into this high school. The teachers are perfectly fine, the rest of school... Let's just say MMHS isn't the best. school is good..and teachers are very supportive to students..will give home works..my son is doing his 11th grade ..my son says his science teacher teaches excellent, maths teacher teaches good..but he use to always appreciate science teacher. I love this school! The people are so kinda. The teachers are actually really helpful. I transferred here from Torrey Pines High School where it a rich area and people assume the school is well funded. That's not the case. Mira Mesa is better funded definitely. Only one bad thing is the campus is closed for lunch. I would recommend this school. I switched from scripps recently and everyone is amazing at mira mesa. I feel more at home at mira mesa. Every teacher makes me laugh everyday and my grades have improved tremendously. I went from a 2.8 to a 4.0. It’s fine, teachers don’t really teach they like talking with students or going on their phones. Some science teachers are great not the biology. Math is great if your in advanced. English is bad, teachers just mess around and do not really grade besides advanced ones. History teachers are horrible, they put their opinions on the students and DO NOT teach at all.

column1: I loved CHPD the small school feel and support of MR Campbell was amazing I'm grateful I have the ability to strive for good grades but I'm just glad that life moves on. One big word I have to share. NOPE!! This was the worst times in my life, I've always pushed to make it better and for some reason, the I better pushed back. Life, friends, teachers, school rule I suppose, it just seemed like everything was over my head. It just sucked. I'd recommend this school if a student is only here to prove themself with homework and stay away from everyone from chs. Maybe this is why some friends of mine were home schooled. Who knows why. I kept to myself. Some teachers and students that were closest to me didn't like that. Maybe they were threatened.

column3: This school is horrible! I was enrolled at this school for one whole day to experience a disaster. Firstly the school is rather small. I didnt see any sort of bleachers on the football field. The track is dirt. There isn't even a cafeteria. Classes are limited. There is no diversity. One teacher had to explain the lesson in Spanish. In math, there wasnt enough chairs nor books. The teacher ended up giving me a CD! There's no nutrition & not enough time to get to class. The sports are bad. The students are faaaar below standards. I would NOT, at any circumstances, recommend Savanna High School. To be honest, Savanna High School brought me the worst 2 years of my high school career. I say 2 years because I left this school my senior year and because my freshman year was an exception. The biggest complaints I have with this school, are with the mostly the staff. some of the teachers at Savanna really care about their students and make sure everyone feels comfortable in their learning environment, while others really don't care about the student as much as they care about going on YouTube in the back of the classroom when they should be teaching. Savanna has only worsened over time and not to mention that the students aren't exactly the nicest people around if you can't behave in the obnoxious ways they do by clogging up the sinks in the bathroom, or taking every single drug under the sun. I would recomend attend this school, or any schools in the AUHSD. Fullerton schools are beleived to be better so I would personally recomend going there if you can. My experience at this school is wonderful they really do encourage you to join a club or any activity after school. And they have tutoring after school for ant student that needs it this school has brought me many memories when i came to this school toward my end of freshman year and playing football for savanna was very fun and being a senior here at savanna high school.

column1: The high school is a perfect place. Coming in as a freshman I was frightened of bullying seniors, confusing classes, and mean teachers. I was delightfully shocked to find that everyone seems to be nice to everyone, or at least respect them. The boys are gentlemen, which is surprising and wonderful considering social norms today. The teachers are kind and always make sure you understand everything. South Fremont is a wonderful place to go. You couldn't find a better one.
