column3: i recently moved ut of new jersey and my kids went to the high school and they want to coe back so bad. the school is amazing and how they prepare you for college is great. If you want to slack off then go somewhee else because this school is not for those people. the curriculum is the best and the teachers do care. where my kids go now they are two years behind and the kids at the new school think their work is hard, it's ashame now i have to put my kids in online school just to get the same education that they got a burlington township high school Very family oriented school district where everyone looks out for each other. All my kids are on the honor roll, or high honor roll. I have nothing but good to say about all schools in the district. Their theater prigram is the best in the area! Parental involvement is always encouraged, and communication is excellent from school to parents. Burlington Township High School prepared me for the rigors of college academics. I am now entering my senior year at a public NJ university, where I have received only A's and B's. The block scheduling that was provided by BTHS made the transition to a college schedule effortless, and the academics taught at the high school were a very strong foundation for my future college courses. The staff and faculty at BTHS always seemed warm and accommodating, and overall were very helpful. I am proud to be a graduate of BTHS, and only hope I can offer my future children an experience as great as the one I had in the BT schools. I moved to America 10 yrs ago. From Kenya with my 2 boys..my oldest sons were 5 and 8..ten yrs .I met with Dr Manno on his first week in township..he assured me that I was In good hands with him he told me he was taking over and everything township was ..awesome...10 yrs later my oldest son is in 2nd yr college..and my other son in 11 grade..awesome people ..awesome teachers..so glad I settled in township...Always looki g out for our kids.. Keep the good work I love this neighborhood and this school system. The curriculum has helped students become diligent and help prepare them for college life. The schools are safe and welcoming and I highly recommend this area to live in My daughter went from pre-k to 12th grade in the Burlington Twp School district. She worked hard and was challenged. She graduated from Twp .in the top 10% of class and went onto a college of her choice follow by grad school. She is now a successful professional in the medical field. Most of her friends from Twp. are also successful professionals. Outstanding experience. Teachers engaged. AP and honors offerings are extensive. Arts programs are highly valued. Nationally recognized theater and chorus programs.

column1: My children went to CBHS and all 3 of them have turned out fine with good grades and good community support they received! The kids were in lots of activities and have become well rounded young adults! I am from this area and we locals know our children do not get the advanced college courses that city and larger schools do! If you sek these things then please move to place that the school system provides what you want! If you want more 1 on 1 with teachers and students then stick to Basin! Current principal and vice principal are completely un-equipped to handle their job. They seem to have no clue how to lead. Two suicides in the last few months of the previous school year...both caused by bullying. This happened in a school with only 350 students. Both have been guilty of bullying, and did nothing to stop student bullying after being told about it on several occasions. Sports are their only interest. Drop-out rate is terrible, GPAs are pathetic, math and english proficiency-40%. The school board also needs shaking up. They have ignored complaints regarding current administration, even with lawsuits being filed. Something the taxpayers will have to cover. Really sad. This is a low income area, and the children are not being prepared for the future. They just continue with previous generation behavior--teenage pregnancies, drug/alcohol abuse. unemployment, one parent households...

column3: We just recently moved to the area and my daughter is in her first year at Shawnee. She really seems to like it. Maybe not the best, but certainly one of the better schools in the area based on the reseach I've done. Shawnee was one of the main reasons I succeeded in college, and now as a professional. Although I was not one of the best students in High School, Mediocre at best, Shawnee had prepared me for all that I was to encounter in life. I do agree that the honor students, and athletes are praised above the average students such as myself. However, there were those educators who went above and beyond for all of their students no matter what. Two of which Mrs. Lyras the German/Spanish teacher whom I had taken for 3 years. She was not only involved in every way possible, but she worked tirelessly to engage all students and to help them succeed in their goals. The other is Mrs. Serdynski. I had taken Mrs. Serdynski for Freshman Science, and throughout my four years at Shawnee, she was always the friendliest of faculty members. Even after not having me for three years, was still interested in me as a senior, and what I was doing. Thank you to both of you. You are inspirations to me in that I only want to be as passionate with my career as you two are about yours. They keep parents out and run the school like a boot camp. My daughter lovers her teachers, but the administration is rigid and detrimental to students that don't fit their version of ideal. While I have a few major differences with the school’s policy, like their inability to teach LGBTQ+ sex education, their stance on student feedback, and their attendance policy, it is a very privileged school in comparison to schools on lower income areas. In addition to these differences, we also have a rigid administration that separates itself from the students, often leading to decisions that create a stressful environment. We have a staff full of quality educators and a school filled with opportunities. The teachers here are wonderful. I only wish that they would make a few key changes to enhance the environment of Shawnee High School. Outstanding school that prepared our kids for college very effectively.

column1: I am a current student at I.C. Norcom and this school is horrible. The teachers are rude and they don't care if you know the material they teach or not. This school has some of the worst test scores for SOLs in the district. Also, this year they are making everyone wear uniforms on Mondays. You also have to join a club or you will fail (this I can understand, but the uniforms? No no no). I am a 1987 graduate of I.C. Norcom High School. It is well known that Norcom is the best school around with regard to pride, academics and respect from the other schools. The history of Norcom is long and the love and respect for the Maroon and Grey runs deep. It is worthy of your child's presence and then some! To many fights the kids don't listen the teachers can't teach our wont teach it's like a giant zoo they need to close the school down it so raggedy and infested with bugs horrible the schools are nasty students are disrespectful The leadership is weak. The leadership there has a terrible administrative record. There has been so much scandal attached to the leadership ... its amazing how it hasnt gotten any media attention considering how much scrutiny has been given to Portsmouth politics. I am not impressed with this school and frankly don't understand how they maintain their status. Unfortunately, the majority of us parents were either not aware that our houses were zoned for this school, or have been unable to sell our property due to the undesirable reputation that Portsmouth has. This school is full of gang members, homeless kids, and all sorts of other social issues. I think the teachers do the best they can with the resources they have, but it isn't nearly enough. I am contemplating giving my home away just to get out of this city and save my children from a life of crime, drugs, and gangs. This is what this school is turning out. Very sad. The 20% of kids that are actually motivated , have goals to become something other than a drug dealer, and will actually graduate don't get the attention much deserved. Quality education, with educators who pride themselves with integrity, skills, knowledge, and Greyhound Pride.

As a student of Putnam City High School, the teachers are not very caring exempting maybe 1 or 2 that I have had and the teaching blatantly is very dull and not very good. Bullying happens on the daily and foul language is used consistently among all the classes. No more funding for the extra curricular activities and all money goes to Sports. If you are a parent, I would not recommending sending your student to this school. If you are a student attending this school now, Feelings mutual. Teacher here: While there may be many negative comments about this school I can attest that it is getting better. Our new principal is very enthusiastic and genuinely wants to make this school better in all possible facets. Yes, the students here are constantly cursing and getting in fights but that happens in every school. This is a title I school where most students come from low income families. Education just isn't a priority for certain students and their parents. With that being said, things are getting better. The school's report card grade is the highest in the district & our community involvement is rising. It just takes time. We teachers do greatly care for our student's welfare and most of us do our very best to help our students succeed. My experience at the school is okay it is not bad and it is not good it is mutual Best school in nw okc. embrace minorities and cater to differences. This is easily the worst school I have ever been to in Oklahoma. I'm a senior at this school - or rather, I WAS. I was removed from the system for too many absences and now I'm being enrolled into online homeschooling. Neither me or my mother were made aware of this change. Not only is communication with parents and students horrible, but the school itself is an absolute joke. The bullying and fighting problems this school has is so extremely prominent with barely anything being done to combat them. The most that's been done is completely separating the freshman at lunch - which obviously hasn't worked because fights still happen regularly. Most of these fights even end with blood being shed and a teenager getting arrested. The majority of the teachers do nothing to help students and are often just outright rude to them. With a few exceptions, they barely do anything to actually teach or provide guidance. The school makes itself seem like a place accepting of all minorities, but homophobia, transphobia, and racism are all extremely common, even for the staff. Trying to navigate this school is an utter nightmare with a confusing layout and being extremely overcrowded. Students are disrespectful to teachers who've done nothing wrong. The school's idea of credit recovery for students falling behind is absolutely laughable for how ineffective and unnecessarily stressful it is. The school itself is VERY dirty - the bathrooms are covered in graffiti, the floors are coated in dirt and grime, dead bugs line the windows of some classrooms (there was a HUGE bug problem in one of the hallways at one point - there were insect corpses absolutely everywhere). Overall, this school is the definition of a last resort, and I would not recommend sending your kids here if you have the option to.

column1: Outstanding, devoted faculty who are teaching for the right reasons. The program includes terrific spiritual formation. Traditional college-prep environment that is motivated. Trinity's students achieve. It was the right choice for my son. Great college prep school. I have been impressed by the caring faculty and well-balanced students - encorporating religion, education, sports, and community service into the curriculum. The facility is in need of updating, but the school still graduates top-notch students. Smaller size is a plus - compared to the huge public schools nearby. Trinity High School is not your average high school comparable to ordinary government-funded schools. With the money Trinity does have from tuition (which, yes, is higher than most private schools), fundraisers, and donations, it cannot afford the technology to compete with area public schools - in that field. But what it does hold over other schools, public and private, is the quality of education it offers to its students. As a student, I feel that I am challenged to achieve to the best of my ability, not only in the classroom, but also on the field. The teachers are supportive, helpful, and tough (hey, it builds character). Sure, there are those few teachers who really don't teach or are just awful teachers, but you have that in every school. Expect it. If anything, I will be the first to admit that I don't come from a rich family; both of my parents work (Dad is a truck driver for ABF and Mom works in a cafeteria on the lunch line) and we live in a modest two-story house in the countryside of Boiling Springs. It's a struggle, but Trinity is worth it. Go Rocks! Great school, high standards in academics but most important family values and respect for everybody. Everybody is welcomed, love and respected regardless of your country of birth or religion. Students are always first. There is a shushed bias by an established history teacher who prefers females (in her classroom). She denies academically qualified and over-qualified males entrance into the advanced classes, and gets away with these and other bullying behaviors such as demeaning comments directly to the few male students. Emails/ phone calls from student or parent routinely ignored. The principal has his hands tied. Trinity did an outstanding job of preparing me for my college years and beyond. Despite being a B+ average student, I had no difficulty in getting accepted to the university of my choice. Due to their strong emphasis on core education, I was accepted into the honors track in both English and Math. I found myself referencing what I learned at Trinity throughout my undergrad and graduate school studies. In addition to what I learned in the classroom, I also had excellent opportunities to develop and refine my leadership skills. This has helped me to succeed in college, and throughout my career as a manager with both Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 companies. I am forever grateful to my parents for allowing me to attend Trinity, and to the faculty and staff of Trinity High School. They truly helped to shape me into the successful women I am today. The student's academic and religious education are the reason for the school. Trinity executes this mission extremely well. The teachers at Trinity work hard to provide a rigorous education for students. Class sizes are small and each child is known by name. There is a genuine concern for the well being and personal development of students, and graduates are very well prepared for college when they leave.

column3: We had to move to Blaine for family reasons. We worried about the high school before we moved here but hoped that we could just muddle through, since we didn't have many other public schooling options for 10th grade and homeschooling and virtual schooling didn't work for our family. BHS is run down and unsafe. The students have mostly just given up by now, and my daughter tells me that many of them are academically and emotionally crippled. Not sure whether the teachers are truly incompetent or whether they've just had to dumb everything down to push the herd through the system. And don't get me started about usability issues with the school/district web site.The last straw was my daughter telling me tonight that students aren't allowed to use computer keyboards to type out their homework. No typing allowed. They have to write out every single assignment. BY HAND. Even work they do at home. The school does have computers. But they're only used for standardized testing.In 10 years of K-12 schooling in various settings, we've had various weird experiences, but BHS knocks sanity right out of the ballpark.

column1: great school good teachers the kids learn alot! i was very impressed! the school system is great! The students here are not very good. They all think they are better than everyone else because they go here. All they care about are sports. We will recruit good players from nearby schools just for their sports abilities. Then when we win against a school 3x smaller we think it's a big achievement. Also another thing is we like to cheat at sports for some reason. At tournaments we will get officials that will help us win the tough games. If I was a parent I would not recommend Skyline High. When attending this school, I felt there weren't many academic opportunities for me. The main focus of the school is sports, sadly. The school has had grants taken away in the past because they were not being used for education, as intended, but instead were being used for sports fields and equipment, and such. I do not recommend this school to anyone that wishes to better themselves in life by receiving a proper education and wishes to have a delightful school experience surrounded by intelligent, kind peers, as nothing of the sort can be found at this school. Great school, better than Nevada by far!

column3: Go to a school board meeting or two. Quite often included in there are students that do not meet the typical criteria I have grown accustomed to elsewhere. I think it is easy to disparage a school and it's effort when I only see a school as reflective of the community it represents. I disagree with a whole laundry list of things, I could fill a page, but I almost understand when operational realities are juxtaposed against state politics, local and school board prejudice and bias, union demands, nepotism along with an unrealistic evaluation of educational success. Stay on top of your kids, assume responsibilty for their actions and results, but don't necessarily agree to all of the advanced class mandatory req to get into the AP classes. Get involved, ask questions and don't always believe the answers. The school needs to eliminate subjective teacher analysis, drug testing for "co-op" participation, and after middle school they need to do a better job supporting I.T. in an agricultural enviroment. There are not many private options but if you have the where-with-all...that is what I recommend. Horrible. An absolute waste of four years. I would've been better off taking my chances as a drop-out. In fact a high school diploma from solanco is the equivalent of dropping out in the real world. All the abuse solanco has left on me will affect my life forever. Do your kids the greatest favor and STAY AWAY FROM SOLANCO HIGH SCHOOL. I enjoyed my time at Solanco, but there were always good and bad things to deal with as I was never an outgoing, popular kid. Solanco isn't terrible and if students put effort into their work, they will get a good education. We had two valedictorians in a row go to MIT and lots of other good schools so you can get a good education at Solanco, but it isn't handed to you. Solanco has a hick school reputation due to its location, but we had a robust arts program during my time and students excelling in all disciplines so it is a misrepresentation to think Solanco=hicks or rednecks. As with everything, you can't make a blanket statement and think it truly applies to every aspect.

column1: My daughter is graduating from CHHS this year. We have nothing but positive things to say about the school and her experience there. Great teachers. Great staff. I am very impressed. The atmosphere of the school is great. This is our first graduating class and I can honestly say I am proud to work at CHHS. I wasn't sure what to expect when I came in, but have been overwhelmed with the caliber of people that I work with on a daily basis. Everyone pulls together and unlike my previous school, parents seem to know how to parent. Proud to be a pirate! We moved here from another state last year and have been thrilled with our experience!! Corinth Holders' principal, faculty, and staff are the epitome of what it means to be educators. They truly care that they are molding amazing teenagers into productive, thoughtful adults. I am so proud to call myself a pirate, and i know my girls are too. We moved here from overseas and my son is having a difficult time adjusting to this school. He is in his junior year. He is in the minority at this school. The kids are very very snobbish and they are not very welcoming to new students of different ethnicity. He's been at Corinth Holders for 4 months now and he truly HATE it!! There are some good teachers there! My son struggles everyday to get up, get ready and go to this school! My son is a freshman at Corinth Holders high school and we have been extremely displeased with his first year there. Administrators run the school like North Korea. They are dictatorial and inflexible. The smart lunch concept sounds great in theory, but results in more unnecessary disciplinary action against students than actual additional academic support. 100's of students regularly get after school detention due to a flawed system that is rigid and inflexible. For example, students were required to attend one tutorial for each class at the beginning of each semester, however in the first 3 weeks of this semester there were 8 snow days. Students were not given extra time to make up tutorials despite so much cancelled school. In some cases, it was impossible for students to meet the standard expected of them because of the tutorial schedule and cancelled school. Students were unfairly punished for not being able to achieve the impossible. 100's of students, including honor roll students were given after school detention. Just one of many examples of poor decision making by administrators. I go here now, and it's an alright school. I honestly wish I went to a better one, but for where I'm located, it's a very good school. They are still building things and we're nearly packed as it is. I'm a junior and I feel like we don't have a lot of student support for things like homecoming or senior trip (both got cancelled because of lack of interest). I don't know if that's just the way teenagers are now, but we do have a lot of facilities for a school in Wendell. My school is awesome! I think that Corinth Holders is by far the best school around. The school offers so many classes, and provide many opportunities for students to advance. There are also lots of activities for involvement, and the Principal and staff are also excellent. By Corinth Holders being the size it is, everyone seems to know that they are there to get an education. If I had more children, Corinth Holders is where I would desire them to attend! We moved from out of state last year and had high hopes for this school based upon reviews. Unfortunately in just one year our child has had several teachers and a guidance counselor who were either unhelpful, uncommunicative, apathetic, or burned out to the point of bitterness or simply not showing up. Though she had a couple of teachers who were caring and involved, they were definitely the exception. The beginning of last year was highly disorganized to the point of absurdity in terms of scheduling, and many things we thought would be offered were not. There's a heavy emphasis on team sports, but not much else is offered in terms of social activities or clubs. I have been at Corinth Holders High for almost a full year now. I have been very displeased with the disciplinary action taken by teachers, Assistant principles and principle. The lunch program "Smart Lunch" is an utter failure. It would be very helpful and convenient to just let kids have the full hour of lunch they should be given. High school is supposed to another step toward more freedoms, yet students are unable to hug their boyfriend/girlfriend for more than 3 seconds, much less kiss them. I can honestly say that I had much more freedom in middle school to do what I wanted than in this overly strict high school that I am sadly apart of. You may think I am saying these bad things just because I don't like being punished. I assure you I have looked at the injustice that is happening at this school from many an angle and have always arrived at the same conclusion. That this school is flawed and injustice in their distribution of freedoms and punishments to the students of Corinth Holders High School. The teachers that I have dealt with my two children have been wonderful. As for the "student" who left a review saying they weren't allowed to hug their boyfriends/ girlfriends for longer than 3 seconds or kiss them.....get over it! You have plenty of time for " freedom" in your future. I agree with the school. It's not a place for making out. it's for education. No one wants to see that type of behavior from " kids". The policies are helping teach kids good behavior when they aren't learning it from home!!! Corinth is a great school, that's why so many people are moving in this school district!And smart lunch. Great idea! I read a review from a student complaining that they shouldn't have to do smart lunch & should get their whole hour long lunch. What kids need a whole hour for lunch anyway? My elementary & middle school children don't even get a full hour! That student needs to wake up! The sports / athletics teams here are pretty cool. They are awesome! don't get fooled by those " student " reviews... You know kids don't like school anyway. I rate this school as a 5 ! This school has its issues but overall its great the smart lunch thing is fantastic and now works correctly the different principal is awesome.Its no long super strict (still is on some of its policies.Dress code is one of them).Phones are becoming an issue because no one seems to be able to not text or snapchat every three seconds.But i overall love this school. This school is great! Instead of starting the day with ‘Ugghhh, I have to go to school again’, it’s ‘Finally, I get to go to school again’. I really like Smart Lunch as it gives you a chance to make up tests, do homework, go to club meetings, or just talk to your friends. I’m proud to be a pirate! The staff is absolutely PATHETIC. I am typically one who wholeheartedly respects and gets along with adults and I have only had one teacher who I did not get along with before high school, but this school really did it. I’ve always been a straight A student and a good kid and while this school didn’t change THAT, necessarily, it's definitely made me change my outlook on adults and school in a very negative way. The staff forces their authority so much (which, again, I have never had a problem with authority EVER until coming here) even to the disadvantage of their students. The majority of the staff DOES NOT care about your student or their wellbeing. Be cautious, parents. The teachers here care more about the clothes on your children/if they fit the dress code than their problems in school, at home, or anywhere else. I extremely agree with what some others have said here, including this one excerpt that could NOT be more true, “unnecessary disciplinary action against students than actual additional academic support. 100's of students regularly get after school detention due to a flawed system that is rigid and inflexible.” Overall, education is GREAT, teachers are good at teaching yet terrible at everything else, staff is uncaring and awful, and the students are ignorant and unaccepting. However, I wouldn’t stop your kids from going here. I’m sure they’ll find their place somewhere, as terrible as this school is. Our children have thrived at this school. They have their issues, but not bad ones. A new principal this year will likely lead to great, new success! My son enjoyed his time at this high school, but received a below average education. I refuse to send my gifted daughter there because of the low quality of education and the refusal to improve. When I attempted to positively change the status quo I was met with excuses upon excuses. This school is one of the most racist school in Johnston County. They let caucasian students get away with bullying and making hateful comments to minorities. Administration does nothing to stop it and makes no effort to acknowledge it as a school. DO NOT send your kids here. The education is below average also. Overall just a horrible school. Our rising junior is enjoying her time at CHHS. She remained virtual for her sophomore year and received a great education while staying involved in clubs. We are actively involved in all our kids education. This school provides a balance of caring teachers and supportive administrative. The transition to high school was difficult due to a bad experience in middle school. CHHS Staff was supportive in listening to my request. They created a positive environment for her! Although the school is large there are opportunities for each student. She is excelling in many areas. Go Pirates!

column3: This school has a very unprofessional administration. The principal and vice principal are poorly qualified to run this school. Many things do not get done according to the regulations of the State and District. Teachers are constantly in violation and never get reprimanded for it. The principal is unable to listen and objectively deal with issues of when parents are justifiably criticizing the staff. The teachers will do as little as possible to individualize a student's education plan. Most are unwilling to just complete their job requirements, never mind going the "extra mile." As a parent, I have been left out of educational decisions regarding my child, which is illegal. There is no accountability on the part of the administration or staff for when intentional mistakes are made. The only ones that seem to have to follow the rules are the students. If you can, try a charter school or have your child sent to another school outside of this zoned one. The high school principal and one of the female vice principals are truly in the wrong positions.. Lead by example, right principals? The kids are essentially "thrown to the wolves" once they cross over the imaginary threshold. A LOT is expected of them starting in 9th grade, which is fine to an extent. But, when a student NEEDS to switch a class in order to balance out things or do better, it's near impossible, especially now considering the new, huge fines the district is imposing for over the limit class size. The student has to deal with what they were given or take the class on-line. Our children have been booted out of their classes weeks after the start of school only to have to catch up in their new class due to differences in what the teachers require. How does that promote learning? The principal favors certain sports teams and changed the contemporary homecoming traditions to please the school board, not the students. I don't feel she truly is in it for the right reasons. The school needs a couple of new leaders, starting with the principal. Please pay attention Pasco County School Board! Your teachers are too afraid to say anything for fear of losing their jobs!!!! Excellent school, great teachers and very modern. They have a wonderful computer center and lots of tools for parents and students. UNHAPPY- To Many social pressures for students from cliches to bullying on a daily basis . The schedules are changing and most unsuited for a Students needs which sets them up for failure . The guidance department at first glance or chance meeting you may think would help there are some underlying issues motives there. advantages: School offers many activities after school for student but, due to class schedule changes , social pressures to be in a cliche its just too much . as the other parents have said you are basically throwing you Child to the wolves . This year i am graduating from River Ridge as a senior, I have been at River Ridge since middle school. the teachers at river ridge Middle/High school give you any type of one on one you need as a student after school before and even in between, the problem is many students fail take advantage of this, it really depends on the students drive on how far they will go in river ridge that gos for any school in pasco county. Great programs/Positives At RR: AP Classes/Honors(A deff must), Engineering Program(Great Class), ROTC, Guidance(any types of problems),Sports. Also the key for me as a student here is to pick your friends wisely, as students of pasco we all know drugs, bullying, alcohol, its everywhere in pasco that is a fact it is only the student that can determine their fate in high school stay in school and stay driven. ADVANTAGES - Staff make sure the kids are safe by stationing themselves throughout the campus when students are arriving&leaving -The majority of the teachers care about the students education&learning progress -Safe (few fights&gang activity) - RR has work shops and tutoring for students who need help -Clinic department -AP classes are available DISADVANTAGES -The school could improve on the cleanliness of the bathrooms(no toilet paper, soap dispenser is always out) -Weird (Homecoming during football game, fire alarm system) -Needs to do something about bulling(Sometimes the main bullies are administrators/staffs/coaches own children or favorites so they turn a blind eye) -The guidance department is helpful but if you have a problem and you are "on track" to graduate they do not care and it will get pushed to the side -The school favors certain sports teams than others(big problem with money) a few sports in particular have to pay out of pocket for things other teams/schools do not -Most of the teachers are good and serviceable but there are some that are lazy &shouldn't be teaching -Principle is stubborn and does not have an open mind to parents opinions -Easy to skip class Proud to be a student here sense 6th grade . Great student section & proud supporters of all sports team . PURPLE POSSE RUNS PASCO. Go Knights ! As a student at this school, I believe it's an amazing school with an outstanding student body and staff. I've been able to learn and grow so much because of what I've learned attending River Ridge High School. Go Knights!!! I can't wait until my child graduates.The teachers are great,but many of the administration are incompetent . Really love RRHS and all the teachers and staff

column1: I am sorry for the previous message. I have never been to Eastern Hills High School and have no knowledge good or bad about this school. I should not make judgements about this school or its teachers or students when I have absolutely no knowledge of the campus. Once again I am sorry for the previous post. I honestly think that my school gets horrible reviews due to past experiences. I've been attending EHHS for the past 4 years and I will admit, the environment wasn't the best both my freshman and sophomore years. We went through principals like crazy and the students were unruly to say the least. But It seems to be that the classes before ours didn't really know how to act, because now there is hardly EVER any trouble throughout the school. Our new administration is doing very well and they all seem to be respected from all of the students and things seem to be looking up for us. We just had to get rid of those bad seeds! This school is really awful, the students and teachers there are so rude, and nasty. According to my son, there are always fights, and he says that even while walking down the hallway, other students seem to be rude and bulgar towards teachers and they do not get any type of punishment. This school needs to suspend or do something with all of those bad students and teachers... Thats why i had to move my son to a nearby school. Nolan Catholic. In conclusion , do not send your children to this school, the lack of education and discipline from teachers and students is shameful. The school overall is awsome.Its not the teachers is just some the students.2011 they really focus on education and scholarships for the students. Since Ms. Washington became the principle of Eastern Hills, things have taken a complete turn for the better. The attendance rates are higher and the want for education is as well. The teachers here really do everything they can possibly do for their students, even if they are rowdy, trying to make them open up and seeing what really is the problem and giving them someone to talk to. Many don't see us in the light we see ourselves because of all the past history at Hills but things have changed and it's not the school or the staff who have given it the bad reputation is holds, but the past bunch of students who made there bad actions stand out. Now a days people really enjoy the friends and times we've spent at Hills. Im a senior and I can honestly say that I'm going to miss Hills. Eastern Hills is a great school ! The teachers take care of us and try their verry hardest to make sure we have everything we need to learn. We may not be filthy rich like Northwest IDS, But we have something that they don't have and that's caring teachers and were all a family here. The gang activity has gone down alot since my freshman year at Hills.I honestly recommend this school for anyone looking for a transfer to a great school ! The school has a host of AP classes taught by top notch teachers, many with master's degrees or higher, out performed more affluent schools in the FWISD, such as Paschal HS, in such fundamental and important areas as Algebra in 2012 and 2013 and produced the fifth highest count of distinguished matriculants per Geometry STARR EOC results out of the district's 14 high schools. The school has excellent athletics, student driven after school programs, a high quality student program of choice for professional development, and the 2013 All-District EHHS Champion Chess Team. It is hardly a poor, impoverished, ghetto, or shameful school as some reviewers have posted. It is quite the opposite. The upswing of the school is so permanent, so meaningful and dramatic that some of the school's less burnished past is truly now, just a thing of the past. The schools old motto has been brandished once more: PRIDE OF THE EAST SIDE. It is a well deserved motto! I love EASTERN HILLS with a passion. There's no other school like it. Eastern hills as a whole is a very educated and highly motivated family.We might not have the best accommodations but anyone that comes to hills no that even though we're not a top notch school we still try to be the best.Im a freshman here and I love all the extra curricular activities and hands on teachers that love and support you and only want the best for you.i love the fact that the teachers teach you in a way that really makes spence. After school tutoring is basically one on one.that helps many students succeed and understand what they're struggling with. In conclusion I recommend any student to enroll here you won't regret it. this school is great!!!! wonderful teachers that stay for tutoring everyday if they have to, and they are willing to do anything for their students. Poor. Give your children a bright future and send them to a private school like Nolan that will encourage learning and giving them the tools they need to succeed in life. Or, transfer them to a better FWISD school such as Paschal or Arlington Heights.

column3: Alright so I just spent the past few minutes reading how Mott H.S. "sucks". I am currently a junior here at the high school ((2014 :D )) and I personally love it. Yes I took into accounts that those posts were years ago but Mott is a great school. Yes there is a lot more students, and you know what? That's stressing out the teachers. If you have a problem with the way they teach, talk to them about it, don't just ignore them and expect to 1. not get in trouble for not doing your work and 2. to automatically know everything and blame teachers when you fail a test. All I ever hear is how Mott is a horrible school and how we should all leave and go to other schools. Well if all these bad students changed and started acting more respectful, we wouldn't have problems at Mott. Sure it's not the perfect school with the perfect students and perfect teachers, but no school is. There are plenty of worse schools out there than Mott so stop dogging on it. Stop only looking at the bad things that have happened and look at all of the positives that occurred because of the school. I can honestly say that I love going here to Mott High School and I wouldn't want to go anywhere else. ~J.L.F. People may say that Waterford Mott H.S. sucks and that everyone there are druggies. I just became a sophomore at Mott (class of 2016!) and I honestly love it there. I do not see what is so bad about Mott. Not everyone there is bad, I have plenty of friends that I would trust with my life. You cannot judge a school by a few people that have had bad experiences. Take it from me, I am excited to be a Waterford Mott graduate in the next 2 years. I have had great teachers so far. Yes they yell, yes they get made, but that is only because some people don't listen, but that doesn't mean everyone won't listen. The teachers there just want their students to go far in life. People need to understand that. I am proud to be a Waterford Mott High School corsair :) I'm in my second year at Mott and I still don't so drugs & drink. People will never influence me. Most of the time they don't influence everyone else. We have minds of our own. We are not stupid & uneducated. I would love if all the hate towards Mott would end. Thank you :) ~ SMK I am a student at Waterford Mott I came from walled lake school district where all this kids are spoiled rotten coming to WMHS was the best choice I ever made its the real world with real people not spoiled little brats that get everything they want WMHS is a diverse school and I love it the teachers do the best they can offering help when needed so to all the people that downgrade Mott you need to take a better look LONG LIVE MOTT - LKU 2 of my kids attended Waterford Mott HS and I was very pleased with the quality of their education. It's always what you put into it and my kids worked very hard. One is in Grad school to be a Nurse Practitioner, works in the ER at St. Joseph's Pontiac, and the other is finishing up at U of M nursing school, also planning on Grad school. They participated in varsity sports, had many friends of all cultures and races. Was a great high school experience for both. Tired of all the negative comments. The racist comments here are making me sad. My kids attend Mott and it is clean and modern. The teachers and principal are involved, the grounds are kept clean, and the new sporting facilities are excellent. I have never seen anything even resembling a gang member and think some people are letting their imaginations run wild. Racist comments? Is that a joke? Test scores have dropped at Waterford Mott. There has been a substantial influx of Pontiac students. Where do you get racism in those observations? You want clean and modern? Go to Starbucks. We need to improve test scores at Mott. This school district is horrible. We moved to get out of there. Bullying is a HUGE problem. Gangs, drugs, just an awful excuse for a school district. Not just the high school.

column1: I am a junior at this high school and i was very disappointed when i read a review from a student in this school. This freshman said that our shcool was horrible but what can he/she know if they bearly started school here? Just fyi, our school offers English and History dual cradit classes, Spanish and Calculus AP courses and they are taught by excellent teachers. We also have a great band, marching band, dance team, cheerleading team, track and UIL teams just to name a few. I am also a student with a high grade point average and I think that this high school has grown alot. I would like to thank our principal, Mr. Martinez, for working so hard to make this possible. I am dissapointed in that freshman who talked so lowly of his/her own school. Where's your school pride? Here at Mountain View, the view is outstanding! Mountain View High School home of the Lobos, here in our school we students try hard to be recognized. Yes we are limited to extra carricular, but me as a freshmen have seen my class members and upper class men cope with it. We are hoping to get more activities at school. I'm proud to say that this school is great trying to improve everyday. As a student here its been great for me to atend this school. Although some may say this is a very strict school.believe me its not ..for sure ive seen worst.Teachers&Staff are excellent here at mvhs they do their best of whats in their hands to make us succeed. Here we have the opportunity to become someone in life,about dress code,ofcourse rules are applied.But its nothing out of normal NO UNIFORMS. Its certanly not a "horrible school" Our principal Mr. Martinez is one of the many people here that try to encourage us to look for a bright future.We are offered many activities such as band,art, dance,football,track,softball,tennis,golf,volleyball,basketball,baseball and some others,as well as AP classes.Im one of many that really enjoys being at Mountain View im also one of many who is searching a bright future.This school may not be one of the best highschools but its certanly a really good school.Based on our academic lev. we are the ones who decide how much we learn.Since the moment we are freshman to the point we are seniors we have loved being part of such a great school and even a family more than just another highschool I WOULD RECOMEND THIS SCHOOL.Welcoming anyone I am a senior at Mountain View high school, I have been here for 4 years. I love this school so much. I've seen old staff leave and new staff go. When I was a freshman Mr.Martinez was the principal, and now we have Mr.Harrington. I really appreciate what Mr.Harrington has done for us as students. At Mountain View high school, they do offer many activities, such as rifle team, color guard,cheer leading, track, softball,baseball, football, cadet challenge, etc. They do only have spanish as the foreign language but that will eventually expand. Mountain view high school is now offering child development, and a new nursing program! It is just excellent, and they offer an amazing cosmetology class. As for the administration, they are a great administration, and they are very strict about attendance. The school does offer tutoring, and to prevent from losing credit, you can go to tutoring and make up your hours. This year they have this new laptop thing. Every student receives a laptop in the beginning of the year, and each teacher has a google classroom where the teachers assign homework and classwork. My overall perspective towards the school and administration is excellent. Another thing I wanted to mention was the shaving, for the boys, the administration reminds them to be clean shaved everyday to look nice and prepare for the future. Every student needs to dress for success!

column3: Oxon Hill is a good school. Don't be afraid to attend.. As you see the school is going to be even better within the next 2 yrs.. They re-zoned neigborhoods and Oxon Hill is on itsway to greatness! One thing Oxon Hill need to do...Get rid of a certain history teacher..I'm not saying any names but his name starts with a "K" and ends with a "g" .. He is pulling down the student's moral.. Enough said! Go clippers I am an alumni at this school, class of 1996. This is one of the good schools to attend in PG County. It has a diverse program in Science, Foreign Language, Technology, and Art. Inlcuding a Science & Tech program which requires an exam to get into. I am a current Sophomore in the Science and Technology program at this school. This is probably one of the best schools you can go to. You may hear some bad reputation coming from this school, but, what school doesn't? Don't let those stray you away from going to the school. Since the new building was built this year, the school has made new zoning, so, the school population has downsized creating a less overpopulated school. Our choir IS the best in the country ( we have won the Stellar Award TWICE ). Well, the whole music department is great in general. We all have a great sense of family and we get close with one another. You could say ohana. Our ROTC unit is the largest in the country. That's a good thing, showing our students actually care about citizenship. I admit, some of these teachers aren't the nicest, but all schools have a mean teacher(s). You may be asking, " But what about all those fights and bad reputation?". Blahblahblah. Go to other high schools and you will see that they have the same problem, maybe even worse. This is a great school. A school with lots of history in it, I may add. Just don't let bad rumors your hear, because, not all of it is true. I am happy that this is my daughter's last year at this school. While I receive many calls alerting parents of the rules, regulations, and school codes, I have yet to witness the grand leadership of the principal, Dr. Cadet. He has missed 3 significant events, including tonight's Senior Inauguration. We were that today he is celebrating his birthday so he would not be in attendance. Wow! Inexcusable! Missing events, and there is sooooo many more inconsistencies. Be the leader that you project! It matters! As a senior parent, I am overjoyed with ALL my son has learned at Oxon Hill High School. The parent friendships & students I have added to my family are beyond the LOVE, I ever imagined. OHHS administration is DECIDATED to educating our students. The levels our students have reached due to our GREAT LEADER Dr. Jean Paul Cadet is a list too long to be written here. He was awarded the 2015 Washington Post Newspaper Distinguished Educational Leadership Award. Dr. Cadet has given his LIFE for our students, spending early days and late nights to be the difference our students, teachers, and community needs. I feel comfortable knowing that under this kind of leadership my son and others are safe to go out into the world and make us PROUD! I pray for OHHS to continue producing doctors, lawyers, actors, inventors, singers, musicians, and creative artists that have been home grown and raised, right here in Oxon Hill, Maryland. Our son completed the Science Technology Engineering & Mathematics Program in 2014 & was more than prepared for college. The AP classes taken were also instrumental in his college preparatory. Extracurricular activities abounded and every student receives attention needed to succeed, be they intensive SPED, ESOL, CRI, Stellar Award winning choir, Outstanding Band/Orchestra, Hall of Fame Air Force ROTC, Culinary Academy, Business/Finance Academy, Communication/Media Academy, outstanding Athletics Programs,etc. Brand new LEED state of the art facility built in 2013-14 Academic Year, 900 seat auditorium, dance studio, music wing, new instruments, Google Chrome Books for all students, hundreds of resources allowing EVERY student success. Active business & community support. Awesome Alumni & Parent Teacher Student Association. Excellent leadership under Dr. Jean-Paul Cadet who brought back excellence growing scholars who are college & career ready. A staff of truly dedicated individuals who go above & beyond for EVERY student's success & preparation. Much sought after even by those outside the school boundaries.

column1: West Seattle High School is a pretty good school and the teachers are great teachers too! The school is great and there are many courses for students to take! Sadly, I feel like there aren't as many clubs as other schools that I have seen. This is an awesome school and students get challenging assignments.Teachers are talented too.love this school. I'm a student here. This school is so much better that some of these reviews give them credit for. The teachers have been really nice and teach really well. The school is very technologically advanced for a public school, and there are a lot of fun extracurriculars to take there. They also make it really easy to catch up if you fall behind with after school study hall and Saturday school. Given the option between Chief Sealth and West Seattle, go to WSHS! You won't regret it. I think the comments on here speak volumes about the school. The student comments, though not completely without error, are better in a lot of ways than the negative posts by parents. One parent said "Know wander my son has difficulties focusing in class." It should say no wonder my son.... Another said seuccess instead of success. You can't blame a school for the behavior of students because in reality it is impossible to control the actions of other human beings. Learning begins at home and if they have a true thirst for knowledge that stems from natural curiosity, that as humans we are all born with, then disruptions in class would not stop them from learning because they'd be nothing but a minor nuisance. Also, it will be the same in college because professors aren't there to force people to learn, they're there to teach those who want to learn. Looking towards college, it's good to be able to ignore nuisances and be a self learner because that will be required in college. My child excels and I've never pushed him once to do so. This is a fantastic school. If your child is a good student they will excel anywhere and they give the tools needed to do so at WSHS. My daughter has been a student at West Seattle High School since 9th grade, she will start her junior year this Fall. The experience she has had at this school is all positive. She has taken AP classes and standard classes. It was a no-brainer to choose this school over Chief Sealth, number 1 was her safety. She skipped a grade in elementary and has never had a problem excelling. We can not say enough good about the quality of teachers at this school, yes she has plenty of homework but it is not too much.She has had no problem finding and keeping good friends, which was an issue at Dennys Middle School.Our daughter has joined several school clubs and is even starting a club this Fall, as well as being on link crew as a link leader.This is a great school, great teachers who really care that your student excells. My daughter is a student at West Seattle High School. Teachers and staff are very attentive and keep the communication open with the parents. Great honors and AP courses offered to help my student excel. Amazing music programs! All positive experiences for us! Great high school! My daughter was a student at WSHS and I pulled her out halfway through the year. The bullying problems at that school is out of control. I cannot recommend this school. Positive overall. The school is not great in every category, but I would say the school is great in many places that count, and with some effort can improve the areas that need it. It is important to say that the indicated rating the school has slightly lower than it should be based on a faulty state assessment reporting system. West Seattle High School has a program for students failing state assessments to retake them again the following year. The small fraction of students who do this do the testing at a different time of year than the general student population, and their test scores override and end up representing the overall pass rate for the entire school. As an example, the Biology Pass rate was actually closer to 80-85%, but because the students who failed the test the first time override the school’s score with their second-time test results, the report ends up indicate a 40-50% Pass rate. Complete lack of resources, communication with parents, leadership, and subpar teaching staff. Outstanding. My closest relative graduated four years ago, to gain acceptance to Mount Holyoke then Columbia University. Her teachers were exceedingly supportive of her every endeavor, and if it were not for the stellar education at West Seattle High School, she never would have made it to the Ivy League and excelled there as well. The campus is like a small private college. Excellent sports, and activities like you would not find at other schools across the country.

column3: I feel Lake Travis provides an excellent education opportunity for all students who wish to apply themselves. I believe the Lake Travis schools provide learning tools that compete somewhat to those offered in the private schools. If you write a honest review of the school this site deletes it. Lake Travis caters to the rich kids. If you have a cookie cutter kid then great. Normal people with normal kids go somewhere else. This school is going downhill fast...I plan on moving out of this district to get my daughter into a better school. Some parents I have spoken to are resorting to homeschooling. Coaches that teach need to be held accountable. They have more passion for coaching and put in less time on making the classroom lessons interesting...mostly students are given "busy work". I'm just so disappointed. I pay high taxes for my kids to go to these schools! As a freshman at Lake Travis High School, I love my school! Everyone is nice to you unless you are rude to them. There are many advanced courses that text your capabilities and broaden your horizons. Contrary to what someone else said we do not talk about drugs and alcohol often and we are not stuck up. Only one of my teachers receives criticism from the students, so considering the quality of teachers I have had before I would say the teachers here are pretty great! This school is so over rated and received itt' high marks from its' past history with the past administration. The school is so large and the teachers teach via "look on the webstie" teach yourself approach. Of course there are those few excpetions, but overall the school is all about athletics and not about the student. If you are the 4.5 student and can survive by teaching yourself, then you will do fine. If you are a good student, and need a teacher to teach and care, then this is a terrible fit for your child. There are DRUGS everywhere, and they all turn a blind eye to this. They care about bullying, not drugs, not do they educate the child to the dangers of all the internet. in their forums....just bullying. I think this school is a huge dissapointment from the middle school of Hudson Bend, which has a great prinicpal who is on top of things, cares about his students and the teachers are good as well. I would suggest getting your child out of the public system in LTISD by high school. Somebody needs to wake up to the real deal at Lake Travis. High School..aftter all isn't education at least equal to sports????? Not at this school. If you aren't rich or popular, don't come here. (I made this mistake :/) This is a very unaccepting, unwelcoming school. While the school is not perfect, and has its flaws, these flaws are present at all high schools, not EXCLUSIVELY Lake Travis. Of course, the school has a certain crowd that goes out and parties, but not every single student does so. The drugs/parties are not as big of an issue as people make them out to be, so if you don't want to get involved in any of that, you'll be fine. Classes are challenging without being completely impossible, and, yes, there are other activities besides football. I can't believe I did not read these other reviews before moving here. Wow, how accurate. "if you're not rich or very very very very social" you will not like it here. My child has never had issues with teachers until starting at this school. 2 of the teachers do not respond to their own email. And like another review all the teachers say the same thing: "just go to my website". My child goes in at "8am" to get help from the teacher and the teacher 50% plus of the time is not there. We have begged for help and are told, our child just needs to grow up. After we sell our home that we paid too much for, we will be moving. If there is a bright spot, it would be watching the football teams clobber their opponents. This school needs a serious leadership overhaul. The student code of conduct is not enforced campus wide and this affects the learning environment negatively. As with many high schools, this one's academic reputation is driven mostly by the area's high-income parent expectation, not the quality of instruction. Even so, it has dropped in national rank compared to some neighboring school districts. If your child needs help and qualifies for special education, they may not receive it. I have been going to Lake Travis High School since freshman year, and I am currently in my junior year. Although there are tons of sports and a love for football everywhere, most of the teachers care a lot about their students and want to help us. Yes, some teachers who are coaches may not be there in the morning or evening to help us with homework or questions we may have, but there are after school tutorials after school every tuesday and thursday and you can go and talk to another teacher if you want to. There are plenty of ways to get help if you need to. The AP classes are very challenging, and sometimes are impossible (AP Physics 1 &2) but the teachers are very well chosen for the AP curriculum. I personally am taking 4 AP classes this year and I feel like my teachers are very accomodating and helpful. The school is hospitable to every type of person, like music and fine arts and sports. Yes there are people who do drugs and drink, but that is not the majority of the population. Most kids are smart and work hard. This school district is not the 'destination district' for families of students with disabilities, and it is not a secret among disability advocates and attorneys in the Austin area. Texas is very low rated by OSEP, but this district is another couple of rungs down the ladder. Our daughter is a very strong student, but our experience at Lake Travis High School was highly disappointing. At every turn, we were tearing our hair out with frustration, and our daughter was very stressed out. The school is too large. The district needs another high school, or it needs to double the resources allocated to the high school. The high school simply does not have enough resources to respond to the needs of the district's students. Although we still live in the district, we will be sending our student to another high school next year. Very good school. It is large, so students have to be self-motivated and parents have to help with course and college planning. Healthy, competitive, with opportunities for all types of kids. Safe environment, no bullying. Every school has the same problems and it doesnt effect all the kids, just as it wouldnt at any other school. It takes a lot of effort and parent involvement to guide your kid the right way, whether he/she is a bully, wanting to try drugs, or needs a tutor or whatever else. Really great for a kid who is hard working and willing to give it their all in learning! If you have a slacker type kid who is more into impressing the other kids with the materialistic stuff they have rather than study, well, then you can't really blame the school can you? :) Well, you can I guess which is what a lot of the parents do when at the end of the year their prince/cess doesn't get into the college they want etc. Great school, fantastic sport program, kids are presented opportunities that colleges offer. Film program is great. I'm a Lake Travis High School alumni. I will start off by acknowledging my first two years as a freshman and sophomore. Times were great and I don't have any complaints. Come junior year I began to realize that this school lacks in the fair accountability of all students. The administration was always quick to judge and hardly forgiving. I feel as though their mission was to catch adolescents doing even the smallest substandard activity in order to place punishment on them in whatever way they possibly could. Now I know some decisions necessitate consequences; From previous experience I realized that they handled these consequences quite biased and unfairly by only allowing themselves to here one side of the story (usually from Lakeway mom complaints, and let's open our eyes to the fact that these mom's are complaining on behalf of their OWN child). Very sad. I strongly disagree that they effectively deal with bullying because, to a certain extent, I feel as though they partake in it. To add onto all of this, I want to point out that depending on WHO the kid is, consequences are dealt with differently; God forbid if it's a football player. By the end of my days as a high schooler I would have done just about anything to get out of that school as early as possible. They try hard to prepare you for college, but I was everything but prepared and my future was almost jeopardized by the administration allying with jealous kids doing just about anything to find dirt on me in order to bring me down.This school tries hard and are well known in their academics and football, but I think they have some things to work on on the topic of a student's personal experience. All three of my boys graduated from Lake Travis High School and I am a very proud Lake Travis Cavalier parent. My oldest son was not a strong student, but also not identified on any 504 program. It would have been very easy for him to slip through the cracks. The teachers were always offering extra help and encouragement in any subject that was ever a problem for him. The communication with me was superb and I always began the year getting to know the teachers so we could work together for my son. My other two boys excelled in advanced classes and while they aren't easy, they aren't meant to be...AP classes are college level classes so you can expect college level homework. The saddest thing is watching people come in from other places and complain about the amazing schools we have in Lake Travis ISD. Perhaps where they came from was not as demanding or as competitive. I will say that the top 10% in Lake Travis are only separated by .000....that means there is only 1/1000 of a point between #1 in the class and #2 in the class. A 93% average lands you in about the top 33% of your class. That being said, the great colleges in Texas all know Lake Travis and that is taken into consideration in a well rounded student BUT IT WON'T help with the auto admit policy of state schools in Texas and it can hurt your acceptances outside the state... MY ADVICE focus on the SATS and ACTS EARLY. Those matter even more than the class rank.....That all being said, the competitiveness of Lake Travis definitely prepared my kids well for college, but it is something to consider in a college bound student. Do you want them to be part of an amazing community, get a great education and be ready for college? Lake Travis is the place to be. Do you want them to be in a lesser school but be the big fish in a little pond but still be in the top 10%? That is a decision you will have to make. I would not change my experience for one single minute, and neither would my kids. They are proud to tell people they came from Lake Travis and the youngest two are juniors and seniors in college. That speaks volumes. GO CAVS! If I had to do it again, I would move to Westlake. The middle schools are great and the teachers and administrators were awesome. High school has been a real eye opener. For all the reasons above, I would say to anyone looking to move read the negative reviews and look for substance. Everything i'm writing is a FACT. Too many students, not enough diversity, and poor counseling. Our experience has been very mixed. My kids have received a good education, but some of the teachers have been bad. The administration is horrible and doesn't listen to parents. They promote the rich kids and football. Outside of that your child won't be encouraged. Not a well-rounded school at all. Westlake always seems one step ahead. Look at Vandegrift too. Several area schools ranked higher. If football is your things, go here. Otherwise, don't waste your time. Better, well-rounded schools in the Austin area. The experience is pretty good, mostly due to the teachers. The rest is eh. College preparedness is a plus though. Will see if this review stays up. Last week my review and 15 others were deleted on the same day within about 5 minutes. Apparently someone doesn't want the truth to be told. This school is a hot mess. The inmates are truly running the asylum. The school is too big and the administration cannot control it. There are a lot of drugs and the vaping problem sf huge. Athletes are given preferential treatment and often have disciplinary issues magically disappear as if they never happened. If you can swing rigor of AP and honors classes you can get a decent education here. If you are in on level classes and truly want to learn it will not be easy as lots of kids don't care about learning and are distractions in the classroom. The sad part is that several years ago this was a really great school that had a great reputation with Texas colleges and universities. Pretty soon, they will catch on that Lake Travis ain't what it used to be. I have had one to graduate but we pulled the second one out. Incredible how much this school has changed...and not for the better. not good. teachers don't care, the kids are mean, there's bugs in the bathrooms, athletes get special treatment, the girls here only talk to people that are skinny and if they're parents have money. Our children have attended LTISD schools since kindergarten and are now at LTHS and continue to have a good experience. Our daughters are both at LTHS and have attended LTISD since Elementary. What was a great academic school a few years ago is not mediocre at best. The passion and / or aptitude of the teachers is lacking and it is indeed a popularity contest. If your parents are wealthy or you're an exceptional athlete, you can get by with about anything. If not, well good luck and it's going to be a rough ride.Coaches can certainly be exceptional teachers, so long as they're proficient in their subject. However, subjects like calculus, physics and biology require a certain level of expertise to teach properly and many of these coaches are just warm bodies to fill classrooms. If you want to play State-level sports then this is the school for you.High school is intended to prepare you for college or life after school and LTHS fails in this regard. For example, if your student chooses not to prepare for an exam, no worries as you can re-take the exam multiple times until you get a satisfactory grade (even an A). How does this reinforce the good habits of students who are here to learn?Leadership at the Superintendent and board level are abysmal. One of our daughters had a horrible bullying incident (a boy was picking on her and getting physical). We reached out to teachers, the principal as well as the board and nobody did a thing. I actually had to teach my daughter to defend herself to make it stop. She did have to resort to physically stopping this abuse WHILE A TEACHER WAS WATCHING.If you're primary objective is a solid education, there are better options available in the area. honestly? lths kinda sucks. huge drug and vape epidemic and teachers and staff all turn a blind eye to it. with that said though, no other reviews mention the courses offered. there's courses for everyone, even if the school mainly prioritizes athletics. so, in summary: if you or your child is motivated and enjoys learning, and will take advantage of the courses, it's an alright school. The campus at LTHS is very big and there are alot of classes offered. The teachers are very nice too. My son was really looking forward to going here, he is an honors student at the middle school. But unfortunately, they don't let kids come from outside their district map and we can no longer afford to live in this area. Cost of living in Lake Travis and immediately surrounding is insane! I wish Lake Travis would allow other family's to go there that don't live in rich neighborhoods :( I am recommending the school, but just know that it is not very diverse. But with that being said, any child would be lucky to go to the district. The teachers are truly amazing and work hard to make sure the children succeed. I teach at Lake Travis High School. Yes, the school is older, and it is huge but what a great atmosphere to teach in! I love the administration and other teachers work to make sure the students achieve their goals. The students are so respectful and truly want to learn. It is like a bubble that I hope doesn't bust! My little girl will graduate here one day and I want her to have this atmosphere of striving to be the best she can be! Love it here! The programs offered and opportunities at this high school have been amazing for my daughter. I am writing this review after my child attended all four years at Lake Travis High School and is completing his first semester at a top 50 National University within Texas. LTHS is a school that will push your child to the next level in all aspects (Academics, Athletics & Social) due to the high standards they set from day one. The required in class and after school studies might seem over-the-top at first but through great mentorship and after class assistance by the senior year your child will have it down. LTHS best complement came from one on my son's professors this year. After writing a paper the professor had congratulated him on receiving the highest grade. He asked where did you go to HS. He stated LTHS, which the professor responded, ha makes sense! The only negative I have with LTHS is that if your child is not 110% on grades, and is participating in extracurricular activities or wants a social life, being in the top 10% is going to be a challenge. My son graduated with a 94.4 average. In most high schools that would have you in the top 25% easily. At LTHS he was barely in the top 60%. It is a very competitive school academically but the I have witnessed the educators go the extra mile if you child's goal is to graduate in the top 10%. Both of our sons went to Lake Travis High School and were well prepared for university. Our oldest went to University of Texas and graduated with a 3.85 GPA and then went on to accept a job with NASA after graduating. Our youngest also decided to go to UT and is a business major in McCombs. He was also accepted by numerous universities, including UC Berkley, as well as offered a full academic scholarship in Texas A&M's, Business Honors program. Overall, both of our boys had a great experience at Lake Travis High School and started university with around 30 hours of college credits from taking dual credit courses.
