column1: I love teaching at Madison. The community definitely could use the structure that is offered at Madison. Although we have some bad ratings and their are some schools that are better, we do the best with what we have. I graduated here in 2001, when times were a little different. The staff was caring and it felt like a community effort was put forth to ensure student success. If I could change one thing, it would be the level of community involvement at the school. I teach Algebra, one of the most challenging subject, yet each year I make use of technology, grouping, building repore, stations, and Interactive notebooking to employ to curriculum. I have shown academic growth each year. By the time freshman become juniors, they are at or above grade level for the most part. This is a good school. I mean we do averag 2300 students each year, and most are below grade level. I am not impressed with Madison nor their professionals. The kids seem to be out of control and there are HPD officers around the school, upon dismissal, to maintain peace. It's sad. As a former graduate i can tell you this is not a good school, and I do not feel like they prepared me for college. The students here are very disrespectful and are extremely disruptive most of the time the teachers can't control them, just wasting time for the kids who want to learn. In order to be able to graduate we have to apply to colleges and and scholarships which is a good thing, but if we don't do it then we can't walk on stage which i find ridiculous, and honestly i think they only makes us do it so the principal can look good. There are some very good programs like JROTC, and a couple of excellent teachers. I would not recommend anyone to send their kids here!!! This school is very bad they have nothing but crips and they stay jumping people in. The students are very disrespectful and the teachers not teaching you anything. column1: Hancock High School has an extremely inviting culture. The students, staff, parents and overall community are fantastic to work with in a school setting. Middle school was harder years for him making it harder to get him back on track since starting high school but that was a principal that had given up on his job & responsibility & was ready to retire. but in 12 years I have seen the district in a whole grow so much & make so much progress it definitely is a top notch educational facility & makes me proud to be apart of it. column3: High School has never been a cake walk for anyone but this school is horrible. We moved here out of state and my oldest son attended WP. He became severely depressed, developed anger issues and was physically assaulted on several occasions. In our home state he was one of the popular kids and had a lot of friends and always made honor roll. When I tried to get support from the staff of this school I found them cliquish and were only interested in continuing to be on their own egotistical agendas. It has been the worst experience of my parenting life and has cost my son his self esteem, his ambitions and his grades. I wish I had the money to send him to private school instead of leaving him victim to this "staff" of people. This school may very well have more opportunities and classes than other schools offer, but the environment and attitude of the students and staff and horrific! There is not one truly nice person in that entire school. Everyone fights all the time, people are rude, and so are the teachers. As a current student, I am appalled at the way the teachers favor the cute, skinny, popular kids who barely have a brain. I can say my own teachers have personally offended me many times. Also, the food given at the school is terrible. I have been given food poisoning from that food before. I certainly hope someone who is associated with this school will see it and realize that things need to be changed. It is my last year there and I cannot wait to get out of there. WPHS is an excellent school. As a former student, I have excelled in school. The school has an excellent learning environment. The teachers and staff members are willing to listen and help you in any way possible. The fine and performing arts department is one of the best in the tri-state area. Wheeling Park offers an abundance of extracurricular activities. The career and technical department offers a great curriculum and readies students for the workforce. I find the staff at WPHS to be callous and immature. It must be nice to have a teaching job where "students pay for the teachers mistakes" Now, as a student, and a current student, I would like to point out that this rating is not because of the lack of an education I am receiving. I have full confidence that this school is doing quite fine with giving children an appropriate amount of things to build off of for later life and / or college, and I am pleased to report that there are quite a few decent and even good-humored teachers among the staff here, not that there aren't one or two that can't tell when a certain individual needs help, when to put their foot down, or when to let their foot up. Other than that, the reason this 'grade' (heheh- I mean, the star rating) is so low is because new joiners of this school are not given any level of appropriate help from anyone to feel comfortable. The teachers do not care, the counselors are scarce and distracted as it is, and the majority of students are cruel, much crueler than the ones at my previous schools which were not only smaller (therefore less likely to have good people, you would think) but also had quite a good amount of violence going on. There is absolutely no opportunity for new kids whatsoever, it feels as if you had to grow up here to have any place, and this is not fair (it wasn't like I wanted to come here to begin with, now, was it?). I am entering the second nine weeks and have yet to feel comfortable, even as a remarkably intelligent student who had been very thrilled at the idea of meeting people that would share their interests (my prior school that was smaller had quite a few people that did, but now, apparently, even in this bigger place, there are none). But you can form your own opinion. My experience was ok but the crippling thing is that they allow students or encourage students to make false accusations on other students like me. A female student I was friends with made false stalking accusations on me and other false complaints on me. I don’t know how things exactly went down but I almost got expelled and in trouble with the law and this was just my freshman year. I do believe that it was all either faked or the female got false stalking reports of me stalking her by other teachers. Manipulation and fabrication was likely at play without my knowledge. This is the main reason I give this school such a low rating. What happened to me was likely plotted by the school. Anyone that understands this review this is just a warning before deciding to go to this school because the same thing can happen to anyone else. Be aware that there is no justice for anything like this that could happen to anyone other than me. Anyone that does go to this school have a bunch of support on your side because you will get false accusations on any of you most likely by females. Don’t be friendly with any females unless you know everything about them and vice versa because they will get you in trouble.

column1: I graduated from Central Catholic in 2007 and I can honestly say that my experience there has shaped my life in such a significant way. There were complaints about "sports rules" and "too much faith" but why did you enter a Catholic school in the first place? Faith education is a primary goal of Catholic education, if that isnt something that you hold as important than don't enroll in a Catholic school. If I had to do it all over again I wouldn't change anything. A lot of the drama over the role of faith obviously came from those who either felt threatened by it or who just werent ready to accept that in their life at that time. I personally did not find it over bearing but rather a very peaceful and welcoming environment. I would reccomend it. AMDG + Amazing experience so far. My daughter is a freshman this year and cannot say enough good things about her school. She says the kids are really friendly and the teachers treat the kids with respect. Mass at Central is awesome. It's hard to put into words, but there's a really special feeling at this school. Would not hesitate to recommend it to anyone. Students were great. Teachers were sub par. I had two great teachers and the others were very sub par. Class sizes are also large, just more kids shoved into less classes. I transfered from Public school and I'm planning on transferring back at the end of the semester. I was honestly disappointed with it all. The fact they call this school a "family" is the biggest joke. best college prep school in the region. No school is perfect, but ACCHS has great success with getting kids ready for college and teaching them responsibility and accountability. I teach in a pubic school and send my son to ACCH. It is a strong academic school. Yes you will have teachers that are boring in both schools. The school can't be "going down hill" when they have exceeded two years in a row with their enrollment. The teachers come from all walks of academic life from a business owners, scientist, and engineers. The students and parents share the same morals and values. If you want to float through school then this is not the school for you. Its challenging and the students are smart. And the administration has changed. Also, teachers make a point to come in early and stay late for students who need help in a respective subject. Love the school and my son loves it too. My daughter is a recent graduate of Central. While Central is not in the nicest part of town it delivers the best education in the Lehigh Valley. The faculty truly cares about the success of the students. It is not something you can put into words but there is just something about Central that is different. The students come from many different walks of life but somehow form a true family where everyone has a place. Graduated in 1961. Best education and prep for the future I could have imagined. Critical thinking skills within context and history; well-rounded social grounding; opportunities taken for leadership; instilled moral and ethical discipline; learning the importance of structure in life ... all led to a very successful and broad career based at CCHS, nurtured at Duquesne U, consistently growing thereafter and continuing today.

Not to mention the graphic design lab and the multiple computer labs! I've been to multiple other schools that only have chalkboards, not to mention that other schools in PA are cutting school lunches! Just think before you blindly complain. Bottom line is that it's a great school for the area. Some good some bad, but still above average. I would recommend this school because it is a friendly community and has a solid teaching staff.

column1: Outstanding high school. Very strong selection of AP courses; our children had especially good experiences in social studies. Great clubs, activities, supportive atmosphere. I agree with the previous parent about the misleading math MAP scores. (Site should fix this.) As a college educator, I was delighted to send my children to this school. Students are well prepared for college. Despite this website's rating of 7 out of 10, it is labelled second in the state elsewhere. Its ACT score compare favorably with John Burroughs, and the tuition is considerably less expensive, even if one is to pay out of pocket! As a former employee of the district, I am aware of the 24/7 mentality common to the faculty, and the predominance of professionals (doctors, lawyers, professors, business executives) among the parent populations whose expectations extremely high, even unrealistic at times. Our two children who are old enough to have graduated from Ladue Horton Watkins High School were admitted to the select Washington University of St. Louis, so called "Ivy League of the Midwest". We have had excellent experiences at Spoede Elementary, the middle school and the high school. No negatives. Moved in from Rockwood Schools in West County. They are also great, but from our experience, Ladue is far superior. Terrible principles. You have to fight to get your child extra help after showing disability diagnosis from general doctor and psychiatrist; they don't recognize disabilities- from 1-4 grades a specially difficult to get accommodations. They also, take in the students from other school districts that have been accused and/or prosecuted of sexual violence; and they don't let anyone know that these individuals are part of the school; they let them go to the 6 grade camps and other sleep over trips. I think the teachers are all great teachers that genuinely care about the students. There is a great learning environment and literally an extracurricular club for everything from debate to fashion club. The principals are always standing in front of the school or in front of the main office greeting each student in the morning. Personally, as a current student, I think Ladue is the best of the best in Missouri. We've lived in the Ladue district for seven years and feel both of our children are getting/have gotten a fabulous education. They both love school:) Excellent. It’s an environment that truly gets students ready, not only for college, but for the real world. The teachers are passionate and have a genuine interest in making sure that each student succeeds after graduation. The district's administration does not understand civil rights and special education law. Students with disabilities are discouraged from taking higher level courses. Administration has a blatant disregard towards students with learning differences/difficulties. Overall, Ladue High School has an excellent educational curriculum, teachers, fantastic new facilities. Problems in the Foreign language department with teaching. The school has a lot of sport and club activities, a unique music department! Saying all of that, it will work great if your child can advocate for him/herself. It almost feels that students left to solve their problems on their own—very little support from the administration. If a student falls behind, then this student pretty much left behind, unless parents interfere. School is oriented on independent, self-motivated, aggressive students. The school discourages students who need extra help from teachers to take advanced classes. They want to have an advanced class with no issues. Teachers with a few exceptions are not trained to recognize the problems in students, psychological or any others. Principals are not very supportive. Also, the environment among students is not the best and could be quite toxic due to high competition, and the way some students treat others. Once my child told me that I would not be able to handle her school. She refers to it as "very stressful." despite having good friends in the school. I am not sure if I would choose this school if I would know everything in advance—a harsh environment. All 3 kids, including their father dealt with learning or emotional issues and the grade, middle, and high schools were supportive and skilled.

column1: I have worked in traditional large high schools, private Catholic schools and now a New Tech public charter. I am constantly affirmed that students can and will step up to a challenge of learning how to think and find answers. It has been said before and is worth repeating, "Real life doesn't ask you to read and text and tell someone what it said, it asks you to know how to find information and then to apply it"; this is exactly what New Tech achieves. Anderson New Technology High School is small compared to most high schools, but it offers some of the best preparation for life after high school available in any school. The teachers were one of the best parts of New Tech. They help you strive to do your absolute best, and push you to do better. I thank them for that. The students are like the outcasts of traditional schools, looking for something new and different. You can't really lump them into cliques like other high schools, but there's social groups of diverse people with common interests. It's like one big Breakfast Club, so yes there's drama and fights, but then there's those moments where people open up and bond with each other. On a side note, the principal could have done a much better job with "conflict resolution" while I attended, but other than that I couldn't recommend the school any higher. As a Freshman at Anderson New Technology High School, I can say personally that New Tech, is not for everyone. New Tech consist of a lot of group and collaboration work. It is tough for those who are not focused on what they want, and it is tough for those who do not take their education seriously. I can truly say that there is no bullying at this school, nobody is going to judge you for what wear, or what kind of music you listen too. It's just a place where you can care about your education, and you can be yourself. I am thankful that my children were able to attend New Tech and i appreciate all of the teachers and staff that have made that school the place that it is today.

column1: We were very impressed with the leadership, teaching ability and overall involvement of the community for the high school. Our children had an opportunity to be involved in activities that they would have never been involved in in a larger district. Counselors, teachers and principals were very thorough in their reports and genuinely showed concern for students, wanting every student to succeed and were give every opportunity to succeed. This is a great local public H.S., a superb alternative to area private schools. The leadership is excellent, with high student expectations. Students are strongly encouraged to join extracurricular activities and clubs. I wish there was a school orchestra and greater number of club options, besides sports, but student involvement is high. Student teacher ratio is good, with very involved and knowledgeable educators. Teacher quality is very good. Most teachers are very caring and motivating. Of course there are always a handful that both kids and parents wish to avoid. College Prep track is available, but currently only one AP option. The commitment to education and smaller class size is worth that sacrifice. Basic education needs with alternate vocational training is also available-a good basic mix for all. I highly recommend over other larger school systems. My sophomore is not just a number in the classroom. People actually expect him to be there, to learn, and will contact parents, if necessary. I am able to access grades online, and contact teachers with direct e-mail, anytime. A++in my book! :) Parent/local private school & successful college grad. It's great and I learn so much! The teachers have a way of mixing fun into learning AR is a pain in my neck but I make up the misery with marching and concert band. It's the reason I'm smart, and the reason I come to this school in the first place. Wish I could drive though. Wish my bus didn't pick me up at four...:D

The population of students per class and students in average was greatly increased. I feel there was less student/teacher bond compared to the experience at Tully. I also found it hard not to have a great relationship with my student adviser. The curriculum was much easier than at Tully, so I felt like I was going back to elementary school. One perk about Liverpool was that I got to choose my classes to meet the career path I choose to follow with. I give them credit for the academic opportunities available. Although this school is very large my son and I fell in love with school. The teachers care about their students compared to previous schools such as staying after school to help the student that desire help.

column1: This school desrves more credit than it gets. There are some teachers that really have the students' best interest at heart, but others do not really pay much attention. Some of the programs that are offered now are challenging. Thw new World in Conflict class is a course that focuses on the wars and the events that changed different countries. This course has taught me so much already and the teachers that are involved are well educated in the areas of this course. I have to say that hiring Mr. Bueche as the new principal was a great idea. He is trying, against institutionalized apathy and laziness, to make the place into a good school. It is too bad that the teachers union is fighting him tooth and nail. He s doing some good things for kids. Miami is a nice small town friendly community with a proud history. I guess what I don't understand is why some would not fully support the current Principal who is resigning at the end of the year. I guess he is leaving. And he is a class act about it too. He only has positive things to say about the community and the school. He helped turn around Florence and Globe and he really cares about kids. It has been years since Miami had a dynamic principal who came from any kind of a background of results and proven success. He never got the support and resources he needed. I am concerned the school will spiral downward now that it is fully in the grips of some entrenched teachers with a union thug mentality. Too bad the superintendent sided with them and not our principal. This school has gone downhill in the last year or so. Not only does the superintendent play favorites, but the new high school principal and vice principal have shown that they are incompetent and also only care about themselves too. This used to be a great school, but I cannot say this anymore. Not with all that is going on. It is time for the school board to step in and do what is right here.

column3: This is our third child at this school, and while I think all public high schools are flawed in some ways (and experienced those flaws in another school for two years with one of our children), I am convinced that HHS does it's best to be the best, within the confines of what the LEA will let it do. I'm proud to have my children graduate from there. I am a student at heritage. Teachers are wonderful here and help you with school and outside of class are willing to help with anything you need. The administration doesn't just care about grades but about you individually. My peers are great and remember to get involved in sports or theater etc. because you will make a ton of friends and are almost guaranteed in freshman year. If you are between two schools (especially Heritage vs. Arapahoe) choose Heritage, you wont regret it. I am a teacher at Heritage ahd would like to respond to the February 4th posting about the harmlessness of TP'ing and pouring flour all over the floors of the school as senior pranks. With all due respect, I must say that while these pranks are indeed non-violent, they are disrespectful to people in other ways. Our neighbors do not appreciate their yards being littered with toilet paper, and our school custodians do not need to be cleaning up buckets of flour that has been strewn all over the floors. We need to teach our students to respect others in all ways - not just by refraining from violent activities. Wonderful school with a dedicated staff led by a strong, passionate Principal. The administration is helpful and caring. It has a very strong Post Grad department. My children are thriving at Heritage! I attended Heritage for two years and found it nearly impossible to adjust. The student body not only lacks diversity, but they are extremely clique - oriented. If you don't fit in with either the jocks, preps, geeks, or smokers, then you are doomed to be a loner at Heritage. I've had a handful of good teachers at Heritage. Unfortunately, many teachers will suffocate their classes with home work. I felt constantly overwhelmed at Heritage. If you are someone who loves white suburbia, fits into a clique easily, and have no trouble balancing large amounts of school & homework, then Heritage is the place for you. -Former student If your child is an athlete stay far away from this school. There is a definite parent problem at this school. There is an open door policy for parents to push their agenda with the inept Athletic Director. Since he does not want to be bothered he gives into the parents whining and complaining. I have never seen so many coaches fired because of parents. What a terrible example they have shown the students....complain until you get what you want. Not the way it works in the real world. Additionally, I have often wondered why an institution whose purpose is to mentor, teach and build children is so focused on finding things they have done wrong instead of encouraging and praising what they have done right. The lack of encouragement is so defeating to the students. Some teachers are great, however I would question some in the math department. One teacher, who claimed to be the department chair, was so inept at math that the students were constantly correcting her. The majority of the class had to hire a tutor to undo what she had taught in class. With the number of great schools in the metro area, stay far away from Heritage High School. This is an excellent, well-rounded, kid-oriented school. Teachers care, and they make themselves available to both parents and students. Student clubs and activities are abundant, and the course prospector offers an unbelievable amount of options. The principal is a fantastic leader who has earned the respect of the students and staff. I personally like that Heritage is tucked away in a quiet residential area. It feels safe and peaceful. No complaints from this mom--except for the non-stop standardized testing, which is a problem in all Colorado public schools, in my opinion. The amount of instructional time taken away through test preparation and testing itself is absolutely ridiculous. Being a first year student, I would say I enjoyed my time here so far, and hopefully, I would stay here till my graduation. For the reasons of generally amazing and inspiring people in the school, being both students and teachers alike. Plus the great events that take place in the school, being their dances and etc. I honestly don't regret going to do this school, and you shouldn't too :D We open enrolled our son at Heritage High School 3 years ago. Our older boy graduated from Jeffco schools and we actually reside in Jefferson county. We have been super pleased with everything about Heritage! The strong sense of community and tradition, the lack of turnover in teachers, the uniqueness from the open enrollment and the positive attitude toward the kids from day #1. Freshmen are welcomed and made to feel it is THEIR school-not that they are "bottom feeders" who don't belong. We've had all positive experiences with sports, the counseling department, most of the teachers and parents. The one drawback is that Heritage has allowed a couple of bad teachers to stay-but I suppose you will see that in any school. I'm appreciative of Heritage and the community of parents & kids and business people for the experiences we've had. Great if your parents are rich and you want to join a clique. Not so great for bullying, uncaring staff and entitled students I transferred my oldest daughter here as a junior when we moved from Evergreen to Littleton. Since then, two daughters have graduated with another entering her sophomore year in 2018. Heritage has been the most welcoming school for all three girls with very different interests and academic abilities. They have a school spirit that unites the entire student body, regardless of their interest or involvement in sports and in general I think this has created one of the best mannered and friendliest schools around. I considered other schools in the area before I moved, and Heritage stood out from the rest as a place that I felt safe sending my girls. We left Jeffco schools this year and decided to place our third kid at Heritage. The older siblings graduated from Jeffco high schools and we decided to try a different district for the third kid. So far, highly impressed with Heritage. The principal is visible and shows up at events. The teachers seem happy and do a good job. The athletics are amazing. There seems to be less drama with Littleton Public Schools compared to the drama with Jeffco. Our kiddo is very happy, is learning, has the appropriate amount of homework, etc.

column1: im a student at Holbrook Jr Sr High School and im a Sr. i have been at this school for 6 years and i hate it! not only is it bad education its a bad environment. Last year we had mold,ceilings falling down, no smartboards, i found hair in my lunch 3 times since i been here. If your looking for a good school Holbrook would be my last chose. Under budget or under funded take you choice! The one thing about Holbrook I love is our spirit! We will succeed, it would be great to have smart boards and updated classrooms but in the end we have each other and that can't be matched! Go Bull Dogs!!!!! Most of my positive experience is due to the excellent teachers and staff, they really make you feel welcome and give the sort of hospitality that you could only expect from family. The small school size allows for the teachers to help each student individually and ensure that they understand what is being taught and they have done a great job at inspiring me to do well. I have yet to have any trouble with the kids and they seem to treat each other with respect. I would recommend this school to anyone who would like a smaller, closer, community that has teachers who want you to succeed. My child has attended Holbrook public schools for about 2 years now and I've come to realize that there's a complete lack of care by many teachers, my childs grades went from getting mostly A's & B's in previous school to currently failing, my child was also put on an education plan after being evaluated and I found out after a months time that the education plan was never put into play, also was failing almost all of classes and acting out in class and none of the teachers reached out to me, a simple email was too difficult for them, I deeply regret sending my children to public school in Holbrook. Although a new school campus is in the near future that will not change the lack of care and effort by the majority of the teachers and administration in this school. Very disappointed! If this does not turn around within the next couple of months I will remove my children from Holbrook public school all together. It is a ok school. It has a lot of after school activities and clubs.

That being said, I'm not sure how the school is doing academically now, but I hope they continue to be one of the best in the area, and produce well-rounded and well-educated induviduals into the world. - Class of 2008 I don't know about their other schools, but I wouldn't send my kids to the high school. As a recent graduate of Springfield Township High School, I only have praises, for the school, staff and student body. Springfield gives an education equivalent to the best private schools, with small class sizes, excellent teachers who care about their students, more than enough clubs and sports to keep everyone involved, and an all around high school experience. I'm now enrolled at the University of Delaware and can whole-heartedly say that Springfield has made me more than prepared for all of the high level classes that I have encountered so far. Troubles that the school has encountered in the past, such as the hokey-pokey of Administrators and Principals, are far behind, making this small public school truly shine. My daughter attended Springfield Township High School, and I truly believe they did a very good job of preparing her for college level classes. She is starting her 3rd year, and has a 3.0 GPA. I will say that the school improved greatly with the new principal. This high school should only get better with the new leadership.

He keeps everyone thinking positive and is encouraging to listen to. Of course the renovations being made are great too. I am thankful to live in such a fine school district. I have a daughter at Willowbrook soon to have two there and yes this is a great school! all staff members,teachers are outstanding. wouldn't ask for a better and very positive principal! great school. Willowbrook high School is second to NONE! My youngest of three kids is a Senior this year. All of my children have nothing but positive things to say about their experiences at Willowbrook. My experience as a parent echos thiers. Mr Krause, along with the rest of the administrative staff, know all of the students by name as well as most of the parents. They really take a personal interest in the kids in and out of the school. The teachers are always accessable to the students and parents. The school really prepares the kids for college. I feel lucky to live in such a great district! Awesome school, fantastic teachers and principle. Kids have a lot of school pride and it shows. Wonderful program for special needs kids. My son has been there 2 years now and has nothing but positive things to say. He went from having no interest in school to having tonsnof interest in after school programs and extra curricular activity. They have tons of programs and clubs as well as college level course for early credit. Couldn't be happier with this h.s.. Great School and location. Very Friendly,helpful and polite students and teachers.Basketball team became a champion for 8th grade out of 25 teams. We have had an excellent experience at Willowbrook. I can not say enough good things! From the exemplary leadership, to the classroom attention, to the diversity of school clubs sports etc. There is something for every type of the student along with the support to make each one successful. Excellent overall experience, the school is extremely diverse and learning happens both in and out of class

column1: I went there this year and I think it was alright. There were a couple fights and there's not a lot of things to really do. Our sports are good but I don't fully like it here. My daughter went to this school last year, she missed over 40 days of school, was failing badly. I could not believe they basically gave her passing grades so she would pass. She is a senior this year and has not learned much in this system. I know she cannot pass a college entrance exam. Very sad school. In response to the parent below, all students in SC have to pass the HSAP in order to graduate. Also, you do realize that as a parent you can speak up and ask that your child be held back? The only way I know to pass with 40 absences is with medical notes and parental support. We have been very pleased with Cane Bay. Berkeley County has other school options if your child is very behind or truly advanced. I have met only caring teachers and a good support staff. They offer core classes on 3 levels - basic, college prep and advanced. Their electives are way beyond anything I was ever offered in high school. The school buildings are less than 8 years old and very clean. High school is not meant to entertain you, but to provide you with opportunity to educate yourself. Cane Bay is a rural school, with decent course offerings and a good amount of sports and after school organizations. If you want school to be like high school on TV, then either get very involved in extracurricular activities or move to a city where the average income is about 6 times higher. To the parent who's child (for unknown reasons) missed 40 days of school, Did you expect the school to teach your child through osmosis? If she wasn't there long enough to learn all of the material, how would she do anything more than just pass by the skin of her teeth? At what point do people stop playing the victim and own up to personal responsibility? Don't get me wrong.. There is definitely a uncalled for amount of poor performing schools all over SC, but your situation doesn't seem to reflect that. Whether it be Cane Bay, Berkeley or Sweet Valley High, parents need to realize that a good foundation for their child's education starts at home. My daughter is a straight A student. Has been since kindergarden. The only problem I have with this school is that there is no credit or encouragement given to the students. My daughter was use to hearing from her teachers that she does an amazing job and that she's an outstanding student. I find there are a lot of young teachers also that do not know how to professionally talk to a parent when they have a concern. One is particular but I'll keep the name to myself. We came from Florence school district where the teachers were into encouraging there students but here my daughter feels like just another student. I was happy recently that one teacher has stepped up to the plate and tells my daughter how proud she is of her. It makes her feel that all the hard work she is putting in means something. I am just glad that my daughter has two parents who encourage her other wise she wouldn't get that from 99 percent of her teachers. My son is a junior at Cane Bay High and has had nothing but great experiences. The arts teachers are second-to-none and the content teachers, in addition to being experts in their fields, are supportive and encouraging. The administration is heavily involved in making sure that all students are encouraged to excel. Although he had the opportunity to attend both a magnet school in the district and a school in the feeder pattern in which his father works, our family chose Cane Bay because of the excellent opportunities it affords. feel very blessed that my son has had the opportunity to get his education at Cane Bay High where the school is a community, pulling together for the success of all students. Canebay's academy s, AP, and honors class's are top notch. Beautiful safe school. Wonderful staff. The JROTC and Robotics programs are very enriching. Opportunity's for extra curricular are awesome! Extremely poor. The school seems to have an elegant infrastructure with a above average social class student base. Far from it, the kids wouldn't be acting better in a intercity school. The teachers are knowledgeable but poor communicators. The curriculum is far behind. Amazing High school, much better then others. It’s a the best school in the lowcountry Currently Enrolled at this School.CBH has been a great school, with awesome teachers and a plethora of advanced and special classes that most schools in my area don't offer. The teachers are all supportive, knowledgeable, and loving. Some teachers do give a ton of homework, and others may not be *as* nice as others, but that's to be expected with any school. Fights and other things do happen, but the SROs are some of the nicest and most professional officers out there. The school does live up to be "The best High School in the Lowcountry". From what I can observe, the Special Education program is also one of the best, with students participating to help and the teachers in the program being supportive. Most other things are a solid 9/10. Love this school.

column3: I'm very disappointed in the rating of this school. We have a child who has attended a top 50 HS in NY, as well as neighboring Olympus HS. Cottonwood is hands down higher quality. The mix of students from various socioeconomic status homes, some very poor, others very wealthy have created a school environment much more respectful of education, adults, and each other. I've always steered towards the "safest, richest" schools, but after a horrible experience at Olympus with excess partying by even the most religious children, sexual harassment by disrespectful entitled boys, and snotty girls (all who think they are wealthy, but have no concept of real money), we chose to trasfer to Cottonwood. The teachers in general seem to care, the new Principal is extremely hands on and my child is exposed to "real people" and real problems without it affecting her academic goals (she is in all AP and honors) OR her safety. Many of these children have to learn to work hard to get themselves out of poverty and I see their dreams and goals being set much higher than friends and family in neighboring "vanilla" East side high schools. Was worried about great school ratings but found this school to be far better than neighboring high schools with high ratings. Moved here from a top 50 nationally ranked hs and switched to cottonwood after two years at Olympus which was a very toxic environment with kids who think they have a lot of money and behave like spoiled brats above the law with no manners. Cottonwood has a ton of diversity, great honors and ap teachers, a phenomenal principal and counselors. Much more like the real world at this school which better trains our kids! i have had two kids go to this school and i do not like it at all! the lunch is so crowded they cannot eat at school, lunch is not long enough to feed that many kids in that amount of time! the teachers do not email me back, i have asked question after question and nothing for a whole year from some! i go to teacher nights and they say i never got that email, im sorry then still never answer emails! the office ladies are never in a good mood, the attendance office acts as if your child is in trouble for being sick or if you forget to call and excuse it...look out! Good luck on getting into the counseling center and once you do they tell you all kinds of great ideas and ahve no idea who your child is and never check in with them again. good luck in high school at cottonwood! The reviews on this site really need updated. Cottonwood HS is a great school. I almost sent my son to a different HS because the the rating here on GreatSchools! and I am so glad that I didn't. The teachers are all fantastic, the selection of electives is amazing & the school is updated and quite nice. We have had ZERO issues at this school & my 9th grader really enjoys being there. I am beyond impressed with Cottonwood High School! I had always heard negative things about Cottonwood and when my son said he wanted to go to Cottonwood I was a little hesitant. He is proud to be part of the football team which is growing and gaining new records. The basketball team has also been a great experience. AP classes, Acadamy of Finance, and a community of students that lean on one another where diversity is celebrated! My student has been thriving at Cottonwood and has more opportunities than I could have imagined. Even though overall test scores show low on this site. Keep in mind we have a LARGE population of refugees. Many students have English as their second language. These kids make our school a better place. I wouldn't trade that for anything! My daughter will be starting there next year as well. We are proud to be Colts! My family loves Cottonwood High School, we live just around the corner so it is our neighborhood school. I have a 9th grader, 6th, grader and 4th grader. My 9th grader is getting a 4.0 and on the varsity tennis team and golf team. All of these things are possible becasue of the great teachers, principal, and coaches. The support team here is amazing. She has met a handful of new, friendly, outgoing kids. We all want the best for our kids and for them to thrive especially in their high school years and at Cottonwood my student is doing that! I have a freshman at Cottonwood High (as well as kids at Bonneville Junior High and Woodstock Elementary), and he has had a great experience. The principals and teachers have been great and my son has thrived. He joined both the cross country and track teams--the coach is phenomenal and really takes an interest in these kids. And the school just got a new track which is awesome! Both my husband and I feel like the school has so much to offer and has a great community feel. If people think Cottonwood is interior based on some arbitrary test scores, they don't know the full story and haven't experienced Cottonwood like we have. Cottonwood High is a hidden gem. I have a sophomore that currently attends Cottonwood and two more that will be joining in the next few years. Cottonwood is a family school and has so much community support. My child is thriving in his AP classes and Cottonwood wood is home to two teachers of the year award recipients in the last four years. Cottonwood has amazing athletic and academic programs and is home to the Academy of Finance where students from all over the valley travel to Cottonwood to attend. There is an amazing network of parents and students. My child has been open to various perspectives that he would have never been able to experience at any other school in Utah. There is a wonderful refugee community at Cottonwood and has allowed my child to really open his eyes to the world outside of the Utah bubble. He has made great friends from all walks of life and is given an experience that is unmatched anywhere else in the state of Utah. This school is safe, strong and a community that I am proud of. My kids have loved their experience at Cottownood. There have been negative things said said this school, including it’s low test scores, etc. but diving in to understand what’s happening makes me respect and love this school more. The immigrant and refugee population (ESL students) being down the scores overall. But if you want your student to play on a sports team, star in a play, be in student government, then Cottownood is the right place. There are so many opportunities to students to shine at Cottownood. Think “big fish in a small pond” I would NOT hesitate to send my child to Cottonwood. If you’re a parent on the fence, please do more homework before you decide which school to send your kids to. Cottonwood is a gem!

column1: This school is currently on the list of the Georgia Department of Education's "Priority Schools" list. Composed of the worst performing schools through out the state. Out of the three warning levels, priority, focus, and alert, they're placed on the highest level, priority. I encourage you to check out the list at doe.k12.ga.us, the school's ID is 2552, and the district ID is 710 Every school has room for improvement and PCHS is no exception. Yes it has failed some of its testing but this is child/parent dependent. The teachers are very knowledgable and educated and are there to help. Two of my daughters graduated (2008 and 2011) from this High School and both entered very successful college careers. One is attending Nursing School and the other is attending a highly sought after college (only 500 out of 14,000 applicants get accepted each year to this college). If you are of an entitlement mentallity this school is not for you (they are not going to give you your grades, you have to earn them) but if you and your child are willing to put time and effort into helping your child succeed this is a great school and your kids will be very successful after graduation. The ROTC and Band programs are very active and very successful in keeping the kid motivated. Just for the record, behavior problems begin at home and to to school. Children should be taught respect and behavior at home. Don't expect teachers to be able to perform miracles with unruly children. I am concerned that the unruly children cause time wasted disruptions, that take away from instruction time. This school is one of the most lazy and uneducated school I have ever been to. I attended this school and can tell you first hand they do not care about their students success. The teacher do not your student and would much rather let them fail rather then spend a second helping them. I would like to clarify yes I have had some good teachers and made some friends they NEED to control their bullies and keep an eye on the teachers and staff. This a great school, the discipline good,the teachers are so dedicated,the principal works so hard and deserves a part in the back . The Academy of Research and science has even made it much better students work so hard ,hand in hand with their teachers considering that the school has a mix of all economic demographic. Bottom Line... Great School! The administrative staff and teachers work well with parents and students. My son's GPA is a steady 4.0! Very satisfied with this school. The academics are great, the teachers really care about the students, and the administration is involved. This school is amazing. I was in the magnet program for science and medicine, and I learned so much. The teachers are personable, and the faculty treat students with respect, and command respect. I was only able to go to this school for one year, because my dad's job was moved from Dobbins AFB to Robins AFB. I still regret not being to graduate from this school. Awesome school! The school is full of red necks and false claimers that wont be nothing in life. Never will my child go there again My daughter has been attending this school for 2 years now and we love it. They have a fantastic magnet program. if youre in the magnet program your secluded from "normal students' . you get better teachers and more privileges . if youre a normal student you are just seen as a student. magnet students are treated way better. safety at that school is horrible . a kid brought a unloaded gun to school and they knew about it and searched for the student but we never went on lock down. that has happened more than once . the school is not good for anybody. I am in the Academy for science medicine and research, and they offer great help and opportunities. They have helped every second of the way making sure that I learn everything required. The teachers offer help when needed, and the students in my classes are there to learn. I have run into problems with people in my school being harsh on each other, as well as some people will look down on other students as if they were lesser than them. I have also had problems with some teachers being unjust when operating a classroom. Overall, the school is a great place to learn and grow with your peers.

column3: This is the 2nd time I'v e been to fostoria high-school. Both trimester going they have messed up my credits and I've had to repeat a class when I was on track to graduate early. It seems as if the staff and teachers have nothing better to do than to pick on the students for the littleist flaws in there. Uniforms. The kids are horrible and the staff is no different. I would not send my future kids to this school. Period. I graduated from this school in 1993. I feel that I got a decent, even GOOD, education. I never had trouble with any of the teachers or staff. I do not remember any of them going out of there way to help me in my personal growth. Nor, do I remember any social groups offered, but academically, I learned a lot and did well. column1: Nothing has changed since that 2007 comment - grading is random and teaching quality is questionable across subjects. Phoning in academicly, lack luster in spirit, horriblely organized little district. If you want your child to be in a continuation of middle school environment, Steilacoom High is the place. Worldly or rigorous or even solid with the basics, no, no and sadly no. Would move out of the district completely if we had the opportunity. I think this is a great school district, one of the better ones in WA and certainly the best one within 50 miles of Ft. Lewis. The kids all seem to be well mannered. Every time I've visited the high-school (where my son attends) the kids I've encountered are polite even going as far as opening a door for me. The kids that attend the school makes a HUGE difference in the outcome of an education. If you have a school full of kids that are for the most part troublemakers then the schools environment will not be a good environment for learning; I truly think this is a healthy environment. The teachers, for the most part are, helpful and diligent about updating grades and sending emails when they see a problem. This is a great school, especially for military kids! Having three kids go through SHS, I can tell you with experience that this school is superior to most. The administrators are fair yet firm, holding kids accountable but in a common sense way. The majority of the starters on the sports teams are also academic superstars, and not because of easy grading as evidenced by SAT scores. My kids have participated in leadership, sports, honor society, etc. while their friends who needed extra help were tutored by they and other kids as peer mentors. Countless people will tell you that this population of kids is accepting, regardless of economics or disability or ethinicity, and beyond that, are purposely outgoing to help others feel included. I hosted an international exchange student who wept openly at the idea of leaving SHS to finish school in her home country. Like everything, education is what you make of the opportunities provided and dependent on the support given and accountability required not just at school but more importantly, at home. If I were rich, I would stil choose this school over private. These teachers care. The coaches care. And by example, these kids care. Steilacoom is a BAD school. the teachers & kids are friendly. there's only 2 teachers in the whole school that i actually like but they are horrible at grading our (students) work. the school sucks. im switching schools. if anyone asked me if they should go or there parent ask if it a good school. i'd say no to both questions. HORRIBLE school I attended Steilacoom High School for three full years and part of my Senior Year. I struggled a lot during my time at Steilacoom, largely because of certain teachers. I am an extremely shy person who was often subject to ridicule from my peers; in several cases I was "called out" in front of full classrooms in a manner that only worsened my shyness and feelings of inadequacy, and made me a target later (after class) for further teasing/bullying. In one case I had completed an English assignment in the "computer lab" and asked the teacher for permission to work on my creative writing piece, she gave me permission and I began working. About ten minutes after I approached her, she pulled up my writing on the projection screen in front of the entire class and yelled "WHO'S IS THIS?!" (drawing further attention to it, and allowed several students to make negative comments). This incident has stuck with me throughout the years and it took me a long time to find the courage to pursue my dream of being a professional novelist. That being said, there were also some incredible staff members who did help me; overall not a great experience, though my siblings have had more enjoyable ones. My son loved his new school and enjoyed being in the concert band. Awesome group and support! Terrible, principal's are horrible, teachers do NOT teach properly, then they expect all students to excel but never try to help them. As far as I see, Steilacoom High is full of pride but why, there is no point because it is not a unified school. They support H.I.B. but do not take action when kids are constantly bullied and threatened. Do NOT let your child attend this school. This is only my opinion. From all schools that my children have attended, this is the worst. I used to work in different schools as volunteer and I feel they are disorganize. The library seem small (not to much books). How do you expect teens to be reading if there is not many books of their interest. We ended up changing my son from school.There is bulling. My child dropped his grades. now in the new school, he is doing awesome. Steilacoom High School is a Spirited School and is full of PRIDE with an awesome ASB/ Leadership team. Great school, awesome teacher and good counselor. Many sports options with great coaches. I just hope Steilacoom school district or Dupont has swimming pool so kids do not have to travel to lakewood. This school and its staff are by far, the most rude, incompetent people I’ve ever come across. We had a problem with a teacher and tried for weeks to get a call back from the principal. Nothing. Same from the counselors. I’m disgusted. You want to send your children to a safe place where they they can be children, even as high schoolers. This is ironically that place most of the time, despite being located directly across the street from the Western State Mental Hospital! If you can look past the unfortunate location of the school, then do weigh what is most important to each of your children potentially attending. The staff is not going to get your child very far, and most interactions are disappointing to frankly disturbing at best. For the price of housing in this district, you could take the same money and easily buy in to a better high school catchment area. Please do your homework and look past the false first impression Steilacoom School District gives off. It is quickly replaced with the realization of the dysfunction, low achievement, and zero transparency. My experience with Steilacoom High School has been rewarding. I watched my son mature during these years and develop life long relationships not just with his classmates, but teachers and administrators as well. I know that a major part of his success was because of the compassion, guidance, and support the adults in that building provided to him and the student body. At Steilacoom, you do not just get, teachers or principals, you also get individuals that are fully invested in your students future, and gets just as excited as the student and parents, when students succeed. Thank you Steilacoom High School, continue to make the difference! If I could give more than 5 starts, I would. SHS Staff and Admin are AWESOME!!! We attended my daughters Graduation Ceremony last night and it was beautiful. The Staff obviously worked so hard to make this a memorable day for my daughter and all of her classmates. Even during this pandemic time they were so caring and wonderful. If you have an opportunity, go to SHS.

column3: the new building is nice, but the curb appeal doesn't bring excellence into the classrooms. I would say from watching my student, the English dept. is extremely lacking. There is little accountability to be held by the teachers and unless you have a very proactive teacher, students slip through the cracks. Thankfully our student has been blessed with 3 good teachers the past 2 years; teachers who try different teaching methods for different students and work with the parents for added success. Other than that, if it wasn't for additional home-schooling, my student wouldn't even know how to use punctuation, capitalization or proper grammer. It's hard to only blame the middle school, when the high schools giving him A's on such work. This school has so much potential, the facilities are fantastic but true to the entire district, appearances are more important than substance. Teachers here are generally uninvolved and uninterested, administrators are worse, a large number of students are miltary and fairly transient, only here for a few years so the staffs accountability level is pathetic. The english and math departments are rediculously lacking. Example of staff involvement.. the last teacher or staff post here was dated 2006. Our family is very happy with OHHS. A lot of schools are cutting important programs like AP and career and tech. Others are eliminating sports and activites. OHHS has maintained very strong programs in all these areas. Plus, the school facilities are amazing! We are impressed! I enjoyed this school. I just graduated last year, the first class to graduate from the completely renovated school. The hallways are slightly bigger and classrooms are too, but I think they could have better shaped classes and all indoor hallways. All of the teachers and administrators are interested in the well being of students and their success. I felt very close to each of my teachers. I think it helps that many teachers are in their 20's or 30's, and are coaches and club leaders, making them more relatable to students and more access-able. The perception that "drug use is on the rise" can be misleading as the students move through the grade levels and more people are exposed and start using. But no one knows how many people in each grade are using drugs except if they see them using. accusations and surveys cannot be an accurate representation because nothing is honest. I think that the career and tech classes and AP classes prepared me well for college and the school definitely works very hard to prepare students for a future that will be productive. Some rules seem unreasonable from a student stand point, but they are not up to the school, rather the district and state. One important note:the school was completely renovated in 2010 so all prior reviews on the facilities are not completely valid. This school is competent, and beautiful. Offers a wide variety of award winning career and technical training: auto shop,metal design,CAD,culinary and video production. The school website will reveal many AP courses (13). My child took 5 over the course of 2 years. He scored a 4 on AP-History and 2/1 on the AP physics, language, calc, and World History; so not stellar performance. Can't necessarily blame the educators,but want to note that he received A's in regular class room; possibly due to the RE-DO policy. I am not impressed with the English instruction - see parent Nov 2010 review, still holds true today. Only major complaint is the fact that my child will receive A's on work that I would evaluate as B- or below. There is hardly any homework, and the school implements a "RE-DO" policy that hardly encourages the kids to try hard the first time around. As with any school, there are great teachers and teachers that should have retired long ago,who have lost their zest for education. Staff parental communication is hit or miss. Oak Harbor HS is one of the best I have been to. The staff and the Administration care. There is a great level of parent involvement and school spirit. It has been a very easy transition for the kids Like most public schools, they push the kids through, collect the money and ask for more. No accountability for employees and blatant lies to parents. The whole district has this issue, to bad there is no other options for parents and children. We are very happy with this school. They have high expectations for students, excellent school communication, a wide variety of student programs and activities, and are very organized and on top of things. We'd definitely recommend this school to others! The School district is Amazing. I have 3 daughters that graduated and went on to graduate from college. They were very well prepared and having AP classes helped. 2 from University of Washington and 1 from Saint Mary's in California. They all had a great foundation academically as well as sports. Oak Harbor School District is known for their National award winning programs. We love this high school. They have more options for academics, arts and sports than any other school in the state. All of their teams and clubs are top tier and win awards and championships regularly. They have a huge selection of AP classes and regular classes. It's has been a great experience for all 3 of my very different teenagers horrible. My student has been overly disciplined for skipping one class. The Associate Principle tried to have my daughter enrolled in the alternative school instead of working with her schedule requests and attendance issues. If I hadn't been on top of the matter, even after telling him that the alternative school was NOT an option, he would have been successful. Even the teacher at the alt school didn't understand why we had to talk to him, he'd told the Ass. Princ. and the counselor that she could get the same services at the high school. The Deans have tried to have her put in juvenile detention even AFTER she made a complete turnaround with her attendance and grades. There is a psychologist on staff supposedly but when my daughter mentions she's having panic attacks, she's sent home with a list of counselors in the community. She has never been informed or had the services of the psychologist offered to her. I've been told that my daughter's teachers all say she is disruptive when she's in class but NONE of them have ever reached out to me to discuss this or try to correct the behavior, so I honestly doubt it's accurate. The attendance secretary is nice but I've had to repeatedly ask her to correct records that she has marked wrong.

column1: I didn’t realize how bad WCV was until I moved out of the valley. A handful of dedicated, talented teachers keep the school’s scores high but they are constantly considering quitting due to the low pay. It’s better than a lot of the other schools in the area but still smells of central New York. It’s okay, they don’t take bullying as seriously as they should

column3: River Valley has involved caring teachers who are tops in their fields and want students to succeed. Excellent administrators at all levels. I am currently a student at River Valley and the administration in our school is very poor, and only few sports are achieving any success. Most of the teachers at River Valley are good, but there are a few who do very poorly. River Valley has had a high number of student leaving to other schools, or dropping out. River Valley is a school that i personly dont hate going to but wish it was better. The students are respectful and have a lot love for their school. The teachers are good, some could be better. Great small school atmosphere.

column1: All this talk about intolerance is plain stupid. I am a 3 year student so far and I see no problems with the school. Its just the fact that we never had a great principle until now. With the Harding transition and all its not terrible. Some people just need to learn respect of others. The only thing tolerated is an act against the original Woodlan student. It seems to me that the Harding transfers get a lot more privileges than the rest of us. And people are saying all this stuff about because its a small town, but only about half of the students actually live in Woodburn. And only about 12 of the teachers are even from the Woodburn area. I use to go to that school and it was the worst experience ever. At that school no one knows how to welcome a new student. I felt judge and no one would bother to pick me as a partner for class. If you are new and going to go to this school don't expect to make a lot of friends. Students were stuck up. Teachers should really teach the students how to welcome someone new. Teachers also give out way to much homework and test. I was involved in the infamous attempt to fire a journalism teacher who approved an editorial by a student that advocated, wait for it, tolerance. Shameful. Because the teacher could not afford to lose her job, she had to agree to a disciplinary transfer to another school. Thankfully she landed a job elsewhere and then received an award for her courage in letting discussion be discussed in the student paper. Given the cast of characters I would assume. That this kind of thinking is still there. Stay away if you like tolerance. I feel Woodlan Jr./Sr. High School is a good school. I feel the staff needs to focus on the needs of the kids instead of what they are/aren't wearing, etc. The teachers seem to respect their students but I feel there isn't much leadership from our principal. We were very pleased with Woodlan in all aspects Love Woodlan k-12. The teachers and principals are fantastic, and very attentive to the children even in the middle of the pandemic. I get bullied at school because of my haircut The school focuses on its image and not academics. The staff are snobs and there is a ridiculous amount of bullying. I do not recommend this school. They do not make any effort to accommodate 504s or IEPe

column3: The teachers are great. The building is dilapidated. It's hot in the summer and cold in the winter. Very distracting. Lacks technology. Cutting elective courses to concentrate on the core subjects due to budget constraints. Not enough AP classes. But, a great sports school. Many sports scholarships generated here. On a yearly Basis Mansfield Scores In the 90th percentile in testing for Math , Sciences and English. Teachers are superb and communicate with parents promptly. This being said, the facility definitely needs upgrading.. no heat in the winter??

column1: I'm a student at RLPHS and the school is great the administrational staff are excellent. I am a senior this year so I am gonna miss friends, faculty and the great education. Timothy Davis is the best principal that I have ever had the pleasure of having. TOGETHER WE WILL WIN Great school! Safe too, great educators and administrative staff. The reviews (from 2008) about strict rules/guidelines for the students was accurate at that time but is definitely MUCH improved now! Since the (much needed!) change in leadership, this is a wonderful school! The administration is great & communicates well & the students really seem to enjoy the school! They really provide a super safe environment for the students & a HUGE emphasis is placed on academics....even the (new) football coach holds a mandatory 'Study Hall' prior to practices & has consequences for players that are not applying themselves acedemically. There is a multitude of opportunities to help prepare the students for college. I think RLPHS is a great school! The teachers care a lot about our educations and push us to do our best at all times. The band program in particular at Patton is great! I love going here! Patton is an OK High school - only average really. Almost all the teachers came from Freedom High (the sister school to Patton in Morganton). Those teachers were good at Freedom, and they continue to do a good job at Patton. There is a rumor that Patton is "a better school" than Freedom, but statistics don't bear that out. Example: US News and World Reports ranks Freedom higher than Patton (#32 to #43 in North Carolina) even though Freedom has a greater range of socio-economic indicators (more ethnic diversity; larger percentage of economically disadvantaged; etc.). Where I rate Patton High below average is it has a past history of racism (the first African American Football Coach was greeted with racial slurs and epithets spray painted on the buildings and football field; also several football players refused to play on the team - at least initially, they did not give any reasons, but the spray paint on the field spoke volumes). If you want a school with less diversity (and no more academic advantages than Freedom) then Patton is the place for you. The comment written below is making statements that are simply false. "the first African American Football Coach was greeted with racial slurs" is absolutely untrue. The student and parents at Patton welcomed this coach with open arms. Any negative reaction to his arrival at the school is due to the constant changing of football coaches over the years. There was no racism from the Patton community and they gave nothing but support. Patton and Freedom are both phenomenal schools, although the many community members view Patton as the academic high school and Freedom as the athletic high school. However, Patton has many successful sports team and Freedom test scores are excellent. The comment below is from a community member who feels that tearing Patton down will in turn build Freedom up. Patton provides students with exceptional educational opportunities, a positive and safe environment, and an amazing sense of school spirit and pride. I was extremely concerned about my son attending a public school in Burke county ( we came from the Chapel Hill school system). Patton is beautiful, clean and has a visually inspiring environment. The teachers in the advanced classes ( AP; Honors) have been outstanding. They show dedication, knowledge and compassion for the students. More than one teacher has offered to tutor/coach my child in order for him to excel in exams, interviews, etc. Our guidance counselor, Traci Riggsbee, has been a blessing. She coached us through each year and made excellent suggestions to insure college readiness. Of particular note, my son stated that there was not one single incident of bullying that he was aware of in the years he attended. Well done, Patton, well done. It is a good school yet the only problems I’ve noticed from students and staff alike is how truly degrading some students can be to others. The teachers like to make smart remarks to students, and the principal only seems to come up with more strict rules and guidelines every so often that only negatively affect my perception of this school. Instead of small things like cellular decides, why not focus on…hmm I don’t know, maybe how students like to damage and deface school property? Or how bullying isn’t effectively dealt with on campus? Or maybe how students will rarely but surely inappropriately interact/speak with one another that creates such an uncomfortable environment.

column3: Communication from Mr. Burleson is great. Parents are informed on a consistent basis of updates and activities at the school. The Principal and all of his staff take a genuine interest in the students. If I have any problem, I am able to speak to any of them directly and they follow up very quickly. My children feel respected and cared for by most everyone in the school. My granddaughter is a sophmore at NFHS and to say the school is bad is generous. Students are met with low expectations by instructors. Good instructors tend to leave. Nothing is enforced, no dress code. Security is extremely lacking. They bring drug sniffing drugs in on occasion and make a few arrests. My granddaughter's teacher and guidance counselor told me the curriculum is dumbed down and teachers are told not to give homework,as many students are from single parent households withmany children and the eldest are responsible for sibling care. This is a great injustice to each child in attendence at NF. How are these children going to thrive when they are held back by school administrators?? I can tell you they will not, except for outliers. As a former job corps counselor, I can see the damage prejudgement can do to adolescents ages 16-24. The school is running on low energy and expects the least. With that outlook, that's exactly what they get. The majority of children are being expected to lose. Shameful My experience here was a staff who does not care about students and motivating them to be successful attended here years back and would never send my kids . I never was a victim but they allow bullying and allow kids to do as they want . Avoid here at all cost do not set up your kid for failure

column1: This school was alright for the 2.5 years I went here. Recently things have gone down a bit, such as the emphasis on education and other problems. Although my years here have been rather down, I have made some friends that I miss so much and really wish I could be there to see them again, especially one friend who has made my days brighter than they ever were at the school. Overall, a decent school, but could use some upgrades. To be completely honest, moving here from a 5 star school system to this kind of environment was difficult. Not only is this school in DESPERATE need of COMMUNICATION between staff, students and parents, but it also lacks in the department of handling the Extracurricular activities so that it benefits the students as well. I do believe this school has some "less than worthy" staff or "volunteers" who have been making the years for certain students doing well, a living nightmare. My children go to school to earn an education, not be knocked down by staff telling them "THEY CAN'T" do something. If the staff grew up and acted their age, perhaps the level of maturity among the students might as well! TRY LISTENING TO THE CHILDREN, THEY ARE THE IMPORTANT ONES........DUH! Mohave High School, Bullhead City,Arizona This school is a good school but they need to recruit good teachers that are going to prepare the students for college. All high schools should be on college programs. We need to pay the teachers for what they teach in the class rooms. Arizona shools are far behind other schools in curriculum and it does not give the students a chance at good college because they are failing to meet the standards. We need to bring our education standards up. If we raise the bar on education you would be surprised that the kids will step up to what you are teaching. Most students are wanting to learn and be pushed beyond the limits. This is what seperates the students that want to learn and move on. Iam employed here at mohave high school, let me first say that I have worked at a lot of schools, and this is one of the worst! There is absolutely no supervision for these kids, there kids roaming the halls at all hours of the day, cell phones in every classroom, iPods, making out in the halls, the kids here are incredibly disrespectful! And that comes from THE PARENTS!!!! The staff, not all of the staff but a lot of the staff don't care, the cafeteria hardly ever has any adults to supervise all of these kids! No proctors walking around campus, so the kids just do whatever they want! They don't follow the rules, they eat in the halls, even though there are signs that say no eating, they throw there trash andfood on the floor , it's a compltet pack of respect, once in awhile you see the principle and both vice principles standing around outside the office, talking and laughing and totally ignoring what goes on, there is no support system for the staff here, that do care about the kids! And the parents are the biggest problem, it has to start at home, it's always easiest to blame the school, and they aren't blameless, but it needs to change! My god look at the day care center! 4/10The school has its ups and downs with some teachers being incompetent or incapable while some are just wonderfull and take their job and make interesting topic's for the students to lean from. This is NB class of 2021 submitting in 2019 We love the events they hold. The way they treat our children. Every parent teacher conference, the teachers are willing and ready to talk. Great core of teachers. Leadership is also on the upswing.
