column3: My kids have done well in Del Norte High School. The teachers there really care about the students. The new principal is doing a good job, and I think all kids feel valued. As with any high school, athletes are at the top of the food chain, but I dont' see that reflected in the ideals of most of the teachers. I think that attitude comes more from the community. My child was not an athlete and was treated very well by teachers.

column1: I graduated from this school, in 1981, as Edward W. Jackson. At the time, I thought it was the best high school ever. If it is not now. Then what happened? Your fail, not mine..... Stop wasting time with the children who don't want to be there and spend your money and efforts on those who do. It is 2013 people. I am a student at Reagan EARLY COLLEGE High and we are college bound students. Despite the earlier comments from people who obviously haven't stepped foot onto the campus, Reagan is a improving and better school then it used to be in the 90's and early 00's. College professors are on our campus everyday educating us, something that can't be found anywhere else. Our Athletics are improving with a new athletic director and our teachers work diligently to help us with our work. We constantly go year after year to playoffs and the staff and scholars reward us when doing so. I came from Kealing Magnet, and no one expected me to last very long at Reagan. If it was so bad as people said it is, I obviously would have left. You can't let the past be a barrier for your future. Reagan is a great learning environment and presents college bound opportunities like AVID, that assists us students to go on to a four year university. Under the new leadership of administration, students are well behaved and well mannered. A lot of the media tries to bring us Raiders down, but we all know at our campus, how great our school is, and know you know too. I am a teacher who works at Reagan Early College High School and lives in the East Austin community. There has been a stigma attached to Reagan stemming from the early to mid years in the 2000's when Reagan was not performing up to TEA's academic standards. The low performance combined with negative press and the No Child Left Behind Act allowed students to transfer out of the school further exacerbating the problem. However when Anabel Garza was hired during the 2008-2009 school year she began a campaign to save the school and to return Reagan to the standards that made it so special during the 1960s to 1990s. Since she took over in 2008 Reagan has met TEA academic standards every year. This consistency has stabilized the school and community.Reagan is now an Early College High School, which means that students can take ACC classes during their regular school day and graduate from Reagan with up to 60 college credit hours, enough for an Associates Degree.Reagan Athletics has made a comeback due to the stabilization of academics. The Football, Basketball, and Soccer teams have become annual playoff contenders and the athletes are equipped with brand new Nike uniforms.Reagan also boasts a wide variety of CTE (Career & Technology Education) pathways including Health Sciences, Business Management, Robotics, A/V Production, Criminal Justice, Automotive Repair, and more. Many of these pathways culminate with industry certifications and/or internships. In summation, before you decide to send your child to a charter school or transfer to a school with a better reputation, do your homework and research Reagan Early College High School. Reagan may be the perfect fit for your student, the school where they find their career passion, save thousands of dollars in college tuition, and meet lifelong friends in athletics and extracurriculars. I have volunteered at this school and seen the dedication and competency of the administration and faculty and the motivation and enthusiasm of the student body. These people are all working every day to make Reagan recapture its former glory. It is an inspiration to see students of all ethnicities working together to succeed. Austin Reagan High School was THE high school in Austin for many years. I graduated from Reagan when it was one the the best academic and athletic schools in Texas and the nation. Nationally ranked in almost every category. The school lost its sense of direction and purpose for a while but under leadership of the current principal and her staff Reagan has reclaimed its reputation for excellence and high achievement in its student body. I volunteer at the school and recommend Reagan to any student or parent who is seeking an outstanding high school experience and education. I'm a grad who has returned to help support Reagan, volunteering on campus and helping to raise awareness and scholarship money for students. Reagan Early College High School is a turn around story that is now being studied and replicated across the state of Texas. A combination of community members and faithful alumni have embraced the vision of principal Anabel Garza. The students and staff are all focused on getting the most out of their educational experience. Reagan is a far better school than it was five years ago. Reagan is a wonderful high school with teachers dedicated to helping the students have an opportunity to succeed academically and otherwise in life. Many of the students come from a background lacking in love, encouragement and family support but they receive all that and more from the faculty and staff at Reagan. The early college offers an opportunity for students to get as much as 2 years of college credit (and an Associates Degree) for free, while still in High School.GREAT GREAT SCHOOL - DEDICATED TEACHERS AND ADMINISTRATORS!! This is a great school. I love that it is small enough for the teachers and administrators to keep there eyes on everyone.

column3: Very uninvolved staff who do not care about the students, or shall i can "certain students" this school has their favorite pick of students who they give their time too and could careless about the rest of the staff. My children will not be at this school next year thank God! The school is absolutely wonderful, there are so many opportunities. The people who gave negative feedback more than likely did not get involved in all the options here. The academic department is fantastic; lots of help is giving to students who ask for. The athletic department is great; however money is unfairly distributed. The Fine Arts hardly gets any money compared to the athletic department, but they still pull through and put on phenomenal shows/concerts. I am very proud to say I attend Martin High School. I graduated from Martin HS class of 2012 and I had a BLAST!!!! I loved Martin High School with all my heart, it was the best 4 years of my life. The staff are very helpful and the amount of groups a student can get involved in are endless. The sporting events are awesome and I enjoyed going to each an every one. I am a freshman in college nd Martin prepared me so well especially for essays. The only bad affect of Martin is tha it is a HUGE "party" school but what high school isn't? I made some of the best friends I have ever could ask for and the students who talk bad about Martin are more than likely students who didn't get involved with the groups Martin had. Martin is a state wide recongnized school with a GREAT academic record. I hope I find a job in Arlington after I graduate s my kis can enjoy the same HS experience and get the same education I got I'm an alum from MHS, summa cum laude, and I currently attend Carnegie Mellon, pursuing an integrated master's and bachelor's degree in ECE. While I do appreciate all of the opportunities open to students at MHS, I find that even after taking 14 AP classes at this school, making A's in all of them except two, and all 3's-5's on the AP tests, the entire experience still didn't really academically and psychologically prepare me for the rigor of CMU. If your child is attending MHS and intends on pursing a difficult major at a highly competitive university, MHS might not be a perfect fit. Also, it was difficult for me to fit in to some sort of social niche at MHS, even though I involved myself in the UIL academic teams, the wind symphony, the marching band, the philharmonic orchestra. The school's huge in population, and it's easy to get lost, especially for students who have difficulty with friendships, or are learning how to develop meaningful relationships with peers. The social attitudes of the students of such a large school of adolescent youths revolve around a group mentality. Overall, though, it's an ok school. I was going to rate it 3.5 stars, but that's not an option. The students are focused on their education. A lot of them just really care about school spirit, some are lazy but there's not really a problem with them. As a substitute, it is a nice place to sub at. Martin manages its large population (approx 3,350) through a zero tolerance policy (consistent with the attitudes and policy of Arlington ISD) and constant competition. Students are expected to do what they are told, immediately and without question. A student should not expect or anticipate special treatment unless/until he (or she) makes an effort to bond with the teachers on his or her own time and at the convenience of the teacher. Teachers are responsible for approximately 120 students each semester and unless the student is somehow memorable or remarkable (either top or bottom of academics or behavior), then the student is just another customer/client who can expect satisfactory (not exemplary) service. Martin controls participation in sports, and fine arts (music, speech, drama and publications) by requiring enrollment as part of the students' academic schedule. Competition to get into the varsity team/squad in any activity is highly competitive and subject to the coaches/directors, consistent with the large student body. If a student wants academics, plus sports, plus music, plus drama, plus studio art; then find a different high school in Arlington ISD for guidance. This is a terrible school. I have watched my girls go from A-B students to failing. This school does not teach the kids. The teachers are only there to collect a paycheck. I took my girls out of this school and they are now actually learning and making better grades. They get the help they need to understand their courses and feel better about themselves. I cannot believe this school is still considered a good school on reviews when every parent I have talked to finds their child is struggling here and the whole school does not care. Drugs, violence and sex is what goes on in this school. I would highly recommend people finding other schools if possible to put their child in before enroll ing into Martin High School. I think overall Martin is a wonderful school. There are a lot of opportunities and the teachers and counselors are always willing to go above and beyond if a student is truly trying there best and ask for extra help. Most of the teachers will tutor as much as needed also. Martin also is great at preparing kids for college and helping them get started will enrolling in their first year of college. I was only at Martin briefly before transferring to Lamar. Now I'm a substitute teacher and I'm really beginning to wish I stayed at Martin. Unlike Lamar, Martin has better programs in both academics and athletics. And the students are really down to earth and honest. I can relate to them better. I graduated MHS class of 04, and absolutely loved it! I wasn't really part of a clique, I was friends with just about everyone. I always felt cared for and found my outlet, which was journalism/newspaper. I do think that Martin, along with other high schools, could better prepare the students for real life. For example, I never learned how to do taxes, what taxes are, how to vote, how important good credit is, how to buy a car or house. BUT high school went by so fast! I wasn't an AP student. I made A's-B's, sometimes C's. Math was hard for me, but most all my teachers had options for extra credit - I would just have to be on top of it. I think that Martin is an amazing school with AISD. When I went there, there were a lot of snobby kids there, but which high school isn't that way? The sports area was very competitive. The teachers and staff were there for you if you needed them. Juniors and seniors got to have off campus lunch, but there were many options for on campus lunch as well. I believe Martin is absolutely the best high school in the AISD. And that's not just me being biased. Martin HS is still the best high school in Arlington, and it's one of the main reasons for above average property values in this area. This school is the best HS in Arlington. It has the top rated music program in the state, It's a STEM School that brings in top students from all over the city, and it's academic focus is second to none. I would rate is a 10 out of 10 Hello i wanted to see if someone could do a report on the school. If I could give this school zero stars if i could. One strong reason for it is that they do not believe in having a policy for bulling through social media even though we have provided them with the proof an name of the bullies. I feel its highly unacceptable for this school to throw a situation that is so very delicate. A child should be able to go to school an not worry if someone is going to corner them or force them to fight to protect they self everyday when the school could simply put a stop to most of the doing by just taking the proper step to deescalate the situation we pay tax dollars for this school to just be a daycare hell no. this school has lost all hope if they feel that this is not an issue. i"m c/o 2020, and i've had such an amazing time growing at martin, and i would give anything to be back in class right now rather than being sheltered at home. this school welcomed me with open arms, and i was given encouragement, amazing learning opportunities, good life skills, and friendships that changed my life. this school is the best school by far i have a gpa of 4.0 all thanks to my teachers The STEMS program is getting all the best resources in school ,if your kids is not in the program what ever left … The school getting top students in Arlington and Grand Prairie dictrict so it is very competitive to get into top ten percent for college . I have 4 children, 2 have graduated. 1 is in his senior year and the last one I transferred out. Since COVID, no one really cares about the students. The admin has no sense of urgency to help out. Teachers really don’t care if your student is there or turns in work. I am thoroughly disappointed in this school. Schools are supposed to teach the children to think for themselves, not teach their political agendas. I have 2 daughters that have graduated from this school. One in 2020 and the other in 2018 they both went on to Universities with no problem. One was recruited for soccer at this school and the other graduated stem with basics to transfer to her university. Love this school. Lots of opportunities with their stem program.

column1: Penn Wood isn't the best school but it's certainly not the worst. There are many programs for students to take advantage of. The issue is that there is limited funding for resources ( parents must get involved write your state representative for more funding, etc) and a large amount of students coming from other areas that lack motivation. Test scores are a result of a lack of preparation which is on the the part of the school district and student's willingness to prepare themselves. What's happening is a lack of parent involvement as well. In most schools, if parents show lack of concern for their student, teachers will not bend over backwards and beg your student to be punctual, disciplined and willing to learn. Even in tuition paid college, instructors do not care if your student skips all classes. So really , if your student can't be responsible in high school, why pay college tuition? I believe that parents and teachers play a huge role in students' success. It can't be all on the teachers and administration. In addition, it can't all be on the parents. All my children attend the William Penn District. I pay mad taxes and for a system that isn't uplifting my children. My children attended private school and got a really good education. I can't afford to send my kids to a private school but the school taxes in Lansdowne are ridiculous.. My children tell me how the teachers aren't involved enough because of the size of these classes. I live in Lansdowne and I travel in Yeadon there is no way that many kids live in our district. They have to find a way to check if they are part of our district. Most but not all are children that have disipline issues and they bring it to our township. Please Pennwood step it up and save our kids. As a student, I am hurt by the insults here to our teachers. I've been a student in the district since first grade, and I've consistently had very talented and dedicated teachers. Even the students agree that the problems PW has don't stem from the staff or the educational offerings. PW has a reputation that is deserved to a degree, but things are definitely improving. Recent graduates are attending schools like Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Swarthmore, the once defunct marching band is competing again, the speech and debate team is a statewide contender, and our sports teams are doing very well. There are a lot of problems with this school; the curriculum is weak, standards are comparatively lower than at other schools, facilities are too small, and decaying, but there is a distinct renaissance taking place. Test scores go up each year, a new-ish principal is galvanizing the students, and things seem pointed in the right direction. Residents still smarting over the break-up of the old "Lansdowne-Aldan High School" may never get over it, but PW is presented as worse than it really is. No worse than BP, UD or even O'Hara. Bottom line is that students can and do achieve success here. just bad not a school to go to EPIC THIS SCHOOL IS COOL AND FUN TO BE AT I GIVE IT A 4 OUT OF 5

column3: The Army moved us to Wisconsin and we picked Waukesha North for our kids to attend. Academics and Band are extremely important to my kids. We contacted the band directors at North and West. West sent us back a small paragraph and then would not respond again. Doepke at North, responded with tons of info. He even sent gorgeous band programs and other things for us. That is where one of my children went for 4 years and graduated! My other child went to North for 2 years. The entire family loved the school, teachers, admin, EVERYTHING. I am also a teacher but did not teach at North. worst school ever!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! I hate this school so much WEST is so much better by a lot. I really really really hate this school! North is a great school to all kids. Especially their band program it has been excelling every year. I am sorry the prev comment by a student was not happy w/WNHS I was the 1st class to go all 4 yrs @ WNHS, and I have had 2 children, 10 years apart attend WNHS, and we have been very happy w/the school. Remember, its a building, the People, and what you do when you are there are what make it successful! The students, faculty, parents, and the community! While the teachers at North are wonderful, it is the teaching methods they use and the employees in the main offices that really bring the school down. The introduction of Flipped classrooms had made learning extremely difficult. Those who are placed in a Flipped classroom were not given the choice and have to be placed on a waiting list in order to be again placed in a traditional class. The introduction of the iPads to the school has created even more difficulties, as they are confusing to operate and most students, if not honestly all, merely use it as a tool to play games and waste time in class. Academic Options merely teaches 5th grade math, which does not help those truly struggling. Academic Excellence is really just a big waste of time, and the majority of students agree. So while the teachers at the school (save a choice few) are wonderful, the administration do not understand the needs of the student body and the school seems to want to push technology and new ideas rather than the needs of the individual students. The iPads really have only decreased the education quality of the school. If one wishes to leave class, they must use a disgusting communal bathroom pass. Ew. I am a 1992 graduate of North High School. I had an awesome experience! The teachers and staff were excellent. I graduated in 1984. Our son went there in 2014 and the ipads ruined his experience. Boys get sidetracked easily, and when the kids are allowed to play games in Algebra class they usually don't succeed. Colleges weren't pushed on the students. Our son left North after his Sophmore year with a 2.45 GPA. His first full semester at Catholic Memorial High in Waukesha he achieved a 3.72 GPA, one full point higher! There are no I-pads at CMH. North offers strong leadership to ensure academic readiness for the future. There is also a strong rec program matched with great coaches who really care. There is very little bullying, and being a smaller school helps maintain a strong feeling of community. Overall this is a great place to learn and grow! I'm a parent and this school is a big disappointment my son hates it and nothing is being done to fix the issues and the school district supervisor isn't any better im so upset and frustrated im moving from waukesha just so I can put my child into a different school Small town feel high school experience. Great class sizes and engaging activities for students, with most becoming involved in both the school activities and others around the wonderful surrounding community. The decision to move to this area was a no-brainer and we could not be happier with Waukesha North!

column1: My school is a safe and fun learning environment. I think that the teachers are providing fun activities while we learn. My grandson recently started high school and has some extordnary needs. Hes a real firecracker and gets into trouble alit for things. Mrs KB has been monumintel in helping him and me get throw this quarter. She really is a ‘kid wisperer’. I thank both her and EVERYONE at Cibola for all they do every day. It is the best school in town!

column3: I absolutely hated my first experience with this school! Absolutely hated it! The very mention of this school gives me a headache. I should have listened when my son begged me to enroll him in another school for his freshman year. Now to withdraw him I'm having the hardest time. Ugh! Really? To withdraw? Ugh! Thanks alot for a very unpleasant experience for my son AND for me! And you wonder why you have three star's? My sons are still friends with those he made at this school. Although the school is lacking in some ways, the overall goal is to educate. The IB program turns out kids that are competent and poised to interact as leaders in our community and nation. I think it is the best education that Leon County has to offer. The teachers are dedicated, talented, and offer more support to students than is required of teachers in more affluent schools in the county. The diversity at Rickards gave my sons the opportunity to have friends with similar academic goals and ability as they. These friends are of many cultures, including African-American, Indian, Chinese, Nigerian, Egyptian, Native American, Philipino, Korean, and more. What a wonderful opportunity to go to school with children that are different from him, rather than to go to a school with a homogeneous population. It provides a very global experience. I am very glad that my children went to Rickards. This is my children 1st year at Rickards. They were at Leon High where the staff did not give them a chance. People do change. The guidance council at Rickards Mr. King has been a life saver for my children. He took the time out to help my girls and now they are back on track for graduation. Sometimes if people would take the time to care instead of passing judgment, results like this would show. I am thankful that Richards High faculty had patience. Leon school is prejudice. They try to hide it but it shows greatly. Only if you walked a mile in my shoes with Leon High!!!!!!! Cudos Dr. King at Rickards. Because It can help me build my future Rickards is a good school. The students are typical teenagers and are good kids overall. The staff is down to earth and can relate to the students and understand the community. Richards HS is the most unorganized and unprofessional school I have ever experienced. I moved to Tallahassee and hoped this school would live up to what I thought was a school trying to improve itself. We gave it a chance and have been disappointed every single time. The staff is rude if you are anything less than impressed with them. They have lost our records 3 times and while they “require” parents do things by a certain time, they fail to show up. The “principal” is useless and when we had issue with 1 teacher, essentially we were unable to do anything about it for fear of retaliation which apparently is tolerated from teachers towards students. If you have a choice, if you have a possible way to avoid this mess of a school for your child’s well-being, DO NOT GO TO THIS SCHOOL! The ONLY thing this school cares about is sports and the students who play them. I’m so disappointed with this school I am relocating to avoid more permanent damage for my kids records. Rickards is the nastiest place I have ever been. They don't teach you much of anything and the teachers will let the kids do mainly what they want, there's probably a fight every day, and the school has 1400 kids inside of it with like 10 admin which barely give you suspension for the fights and I don't know how many times I heard of guns getting pulled out.

column1: Lana'i has wonderful, respectful students who don't give any trouble like in inner city schools. However, the academic rigor of the curriculum is not as high as it could be. What the school lacks, due to dwindling student enrollment and funds, the community is left to support. Despite the cutbacks and budgeting concerns, Lana'i is continuing with the construction to build more facilities for the campus. With the new ownership of our island and a new principal, Lana i is going through some positive changes right now. We still have a long ways to go to catch up to the rigor that the common core standards necessitate, but I do feel we are headed in the right direction. Teaching and working at Lana i school is exciting and rewarding. Negatively, we moved here with two mid-range students, and now both are behind but not for Hawaii!! As all the kids are behind unless they are super exceptional and self-motivated. I had a child that had two teachers (one for math and one for everything else), the main teacher expressed concern about my child's math (even though they weren't the teacher) when I spoke to the math teacher I was assured that my child was doing great in math. Well, I knew that was a lie as every afternoon, my child had no idea how to do the homework. So I had to try and teach it every day, and it ended in tears and anxiety and massive frustration. We found out that the entire class was failing, but my child was in the middle of that, which means it is all ok? Based on that and the constant bullying and general meanness, and I don't care attitude, I had to pull my child out of school and homeschool.

column1: The teachers are really great and encourage you to do your best. The work is really intense but you are encouraged to be the best you can be. The only negative there is are the students that go there. they are extremely materalistic and snobby. It's pretty much all about the money. There is a lot of stabbing in each others backs and fakeness among the students. Great staff. they are very attentive to their students. I had two children who recently graduated from Moreau. It was an excellent experience for both of them. The band program is amazing. There are after school sports activities for everyone. The cross country program is fantastic for all skill levels. The best part of the school is the morals that it imparts. It is a religious school but the students are taught to be open-minded. There have been a few sub-par teachers, but overall my children had a wonderful education and both are amazed at how ill-prepared many of their classmates in the university are. The school is expensive, but there are many students there on work scholarships and there is no stigma attached to that. I would highly recommend this school. I graduated from Moreau Catholic High back in 1985, my Son now attends and is a sophomore and we've been through the freshman year. Wow, it was tough, but I have seen him develop 10 times faster than most of his peers in other schools in the area. It truly is a college prep school and you certainly get what you pay for. Moreau is an Apple Distinguished School and the kids all use Macbook Pro's for their schoolwork. The academics are outstanding and the sports are top notch. I like the diversity of the school, in his class it's about 40% Asian, 30% White & 30% Hispanic & African American, it's a good mix just like the Silicon Valley as a whole. The music & drama departments are just phenomenal and are on par with college level performances. It may not be for every student, but if you wish for your kid to be trained to be a future leader in silicon valley business or his/her local community this is a great place to start. My daughter is in this school from Grade9. In her sophomore and junior years she took school s great program Mock Trial . During her time of participation, school became Champion in Alameda County Mock Trial competition in 2013 and 2014. During 2nd semester of her junior year, which just concluded yesterday, observed that her grade was going down and she was absent and tardy too many days. Brought this to school s attention and wrote emails to all her teaches requesting to update status of her test and homework assignments. Surprised to find out that in some difficult subjects she missed assignments and tests. Teachers replied everyday and updated me. From time stamped on the email I could see that some teachers even responded from their dinner table & very early in the morning from home. Within a month she was up to date with all her due tests & assignments. Her grade also went up. This was not possible without help from her dedicated teachers and school admin. My daughter is not their only student. But they gave special attention and save my daughter from complete train wreck. An example how teachers and school admin working with parent can make a difference in student s life. The teachers set you up for success. The administration gives lots of great opportunities for students to grow. My kids are very happy at Moreau! Really nice students, kind families. The school's leadership is Awesome and so dedicated. 90% of the teaching staff is Excellent (there are always a small few that you wonder about). Pretty, clean, safe campus. There is a program for students with learning differences, however it is limited. If this applies to your child, find out what accommodations they are actually willing to provide, and know that the support is limited and not guaranteed. Have a backup plan in place in case you are told to find another school, as we were. The teachers however are amazing. Kind and helpful. This school is a shadow of its former self. The majority of the problem stems from adminstration. You have a highly unqualified principle and it shows. For shame.

column3: I wouldn't recommend working in this school district to anyone. They fire teachers and administrators randomly for little to no reason and the schools are in the middle of nowhere. The district is bizarre. Go to Phoenix, Flagstaff, or any other place in the state - NOT HERE! I am one of those many teachers who quit in the 2012-2013 year. Before you spend your money moving to teach in this district, allow me to tell you what you should be joyful for. 1) Joyful to wear the teacher uniform so that you can look like you work at Lady Footlocker. 2) Joyful to give up two full weeks per quarter to nonstop testing 3) Joyful to give up your prep hour to substitute/babysit five or more classes (up to 80 students) daily 4) Joyful to never express concerns without fear of being put on admin leave 5) Joyful to give up Prop 301 money because the spur of the moment requirements were cumbersome and unrealistic 6) Joyful to work for principals who must support the superintendent instead of their teachers 7) Joyful to work for a district where the superintendent hates & fears teachers 8) Joyful to work in a district that threatens to withhold your pay for little to no reason 9) Joyful to work with teachers who get stellar reviews because of favoritism 10) Joyful to work in a district that hasn't given teachers a raise in 4 years yet administrators give themselves raises every year. Good luck!!!!!!!!!!!! As a retired teacher from this school the school is bleeding staff! I would advise anyone thinking of taking a job in the WRSD to think very carefully! I could see what has been happening in this district was going to happen a couple of years ago and this is why I retired! The State of Az needs to come in and take over the school because of the way money is being spent! Leaders take the blame when things go wrong the leaders of this school blame everyone but themselves! WRHS will be needing many new teachers in the 2013-14 yr. AZ is a right to work state that means low pay, weak unions, little to no protection, and double the above statements when on the Rez, an independent nation that goes unsupervised. Many Mid-westerners have come here sight unseen contract unread, having interviewed no one that has recently lived here-only to find that under the current superintendent, the best word to describe WRUSD is totalitarianism. If you think you can function without freedom of speech, evals based on faulty district- mandated tests- you will do fine. If you think democracy should rule in all corners of the US that you should have freedom of speech, not to be put on admin leave for questioning district policies, that district spys watching your email are unethical, having your computer blocked even for grading because you advocated for the students/yourself then prorate your move here for the amount of years you think you can take it. This is not a student- centered district, this is an administration centered district who tolerates no challenges from well educated critically thinking and questioning teachers. No union can help you here, not in Arizona. I can only offer one piece of advice for teachers considering employment in this district. Run! Run away! Run for your professional lives! My Sister-in-Law is a gifted "hands on" Biology Teacher who is wanting to move from Alaska to New Mexico or Arizona and would like to work specifically with the Navajo Nation. I visited the Nation with a group from my college back in 1991 and fell in l love with Window Rock and wanted to recommend this school district to have have her check out possible employment. I will not be doing that now. I would however like to appeal to the Leadership of the Nation to look into doing a house cleaning in the school district administration-just an uninformed outside observation. We have 612 students enrolled in our school. 9-12 grade with 98% Native American population. We offer CTE, advance and college dual enrollment classes What happened to the cooking teacher who put on the fashion shows? Where is the English teacher who did all the plays? What happened to the teacher who took all the pictures? What happened to the art teacher who won the award at the contest in Gallup? My oldest child graduated from WRHS 4 years ago and the teachers she had are all gone. My last son is there now and has 3 classes a day with long term subs. They don't teach them at all. How id he going to graduate? I can't afford a boarding school but I would not have him there is I could afford something else. The district has spend 43 million on a sport arena but they don't give raises to the teachers. The shows the priorities - sports and not the kids or the teachers who teach the kids. I would not recommend any teacher coming to this school. The district is in turmoil. They recalled the entire school board and it seems tribal issues and jealousys get in the way of doing what is right for kids. I had excellent evaluations and worked hard for kids and it didn't matter. They regularly put people out with no reason and no due process. Politics and petty issues trump what's right for kids and living there is a nightmare. Do NOT go there. They promise the world and deliver misery. Teachers can't access internet sites in order to make our students classroom experience one for the 21st century. Classrooms are not equipped for 21st century. Teachers do not get the supplies they need. Students enrolled in classes with only computers and/or long term subs because pay is stagnant and the work conditions keep teachers away or run them away. I have read the posted comments and feel they are misleading to a point. For a while there was really bad influences in the schools, namely gangs and drugs. The drugs are getting better and the gang presence has been 98% eliminated. The major problems in the discipline side are tardys and absences. There is a new set of administration throughout the district and they have done a tremendous job so far. The high school is a great place to work. The outdoor enthusiast will love the miles of space to hike and bike. The housing available is very nice and inexpensive to live in. The new district leadership is even looking at being able to provide high end stipends to recruit and retain teachers. Finding teachers is hard across the nation and especially in a rural area, but there are no better people to work with and for then the community of Window Rock.

column1: Anacoco is the ideal place to raise a family. The school cannot be topped, Im a former student and I will not let my children attend any other school around. The teachers genuinely care about their students, not only their grades but also the students themselves. I know that high school is supposed to be the best time of your life and for me it really was. I know that when I look back on my time there I cant help but wish I could go back. Anacoco High prepared me soo well for college that i actually got the chance to tutor other students my freshman year at Northwestern State University. I already had a lot of the basic knowledge in my core classes that a lot of the other students didnt have. I have soo much to thank my teachers for at Anacoco High School.You won't be sorry! I would like to take this opportunity to update a previous entry I made. We are a military family who spent two years commuting from Ft. Polk to Anacoco High and Elementary Schools. We knew we were providing our kids with the best education the area could provide, but were unsure as to whether or not our kids would measure up when we left Louisiana and moved to our next duty station in Pennsylvania. The schools in Pennsylvania are very challenging and the grading scale is higher than that in LA. Well, I am thrilled to report that my son and daughter both received straight A's. They were prepared for school here and I have the utmost respect for all those at Anacoco working hard to provide the kids with a quality education. Our deepest thanks to you! I graduated from this school and my kids will be going to this school because it is the best school in the area and one of the best schools in the state. I LOVE AHS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Anacoco is a tiny school in the rural south. As you can imagine, the school doesn't particularly care for outsiders (in ethnicity, culture, or religion). They don't really touch on topics like evolution. There are still regularly-held group prayers. And the amount of effort they put into enforcing insignificant rules (such as the boys and hair touching their eyebrows) is simply mind-boggling. While the teachers are certainly competent, it is worth noting that students that are particularly interested in science or especially mathematics may be suited elsewhere, as they run a good chance of stagnation. They only offer up to "Advanced Math" which is comparable to trigonometry and pre-calculus. As a former student, my peers and I were able to take algebra 1 through accelerated math in 8th grade. While my peers stagnated, I moved and was able to continue on. Upon graduation I'll be done with calc 2, they won t have even touched calculus (unless they insisted on taking college classes). They do have their act together on English though. And I can honestly say that I remember more from my history classes there than anywhere else (and the teachers are fairly open about any biases).

column3: In some cases, this is one of the best high schools in the area. It has a lot of AP classes and strong links to Hobart & William Smith. It has a large number of graduates that go on success in college and careers. On the other hand, the school is a very large reminder of the politics in the district. The school's former principal, who was a very strong and capable administrator as well as a devoted community member was denied tenure a couple of year ago for reasons that were mostly outside of his control. The faculty can be very cliquish here and show favoritism towards students or breaking appropriate teacher/student interaction guidelines. Discipline can also be a problem given the high poverty rate in the district, as well as freshmen coming in after being coddled in the middle school for three years. Administration almost has to run the school like a prison at times because of the discipline issues that sometimes arise. Is this a bad school? No. But it has the potential to be so much better than it currently is.

column1: This school was a horrific choice academically, Space Coast seems to have been nothing but few teachers actually willing to try and be compassionate with the student to better fund their academic progress. Most of the staff is incompetent and non-helpful entirely. I found the student population to be intimidating and lacking in social skills; as well, many students broke dress code on a consistent basis and no one thought the better of it. Facility are virtually fearful on students and respond to misbehavior by veering their eyes. This school, I believe, is a despicable representation of the public school system and its disciples. Space Coast is absolutely terrible. I Hate going there and if I could go to a different school, I would. The students lack care for each other and the teachers pretend we're all a big happy "family" but in reality we're enemies. We never get a break and if we miss a day of school, its like we're lost for eternity. I am a student at this high school, and I have read all of the reviews on this web site for the school. Many of this reviews are out of proportion. The dress code isn't strict in the frist place, but it is enforced. At this time I have had no problems with any teacher. The review with all the discription of smoking, profanity, and PDA on campass is neverly nonexistent. Truely my old middle school in a small town in Ohio was more of a problem. Many reviews have said that their student fail the courses at the school and if you do the work your grade will refect. At this time I have held a 4.0 GPA for a year and a half. Just remember with any high school kids will be kids. This school believes in honesty and integrity and I couldn't be happier about my sons going here! This school is a typical neighborhood school that does not hand pick its students such as Edgewood, but still offers a special program, called Viper Accelerated Program (VAP) for those that want more than just a basic education! I am very happy with this program and it keeps my daughter performing at a level as high as she wants to take it, the teachers are willing to accommodate different levels and assign work accordingly. All schools can be great, it's the teachers that make the difference!! And this school certainly has great teachers that truly care for the students' success and are willing to do what it takes to get the kids ready for their next stage in life!! Way to go VAP teachers!! Keep up the good work!!! 2016-17 brought a new principal with a new vision. She is working hard to establish Space Coast in a better direction. Parent Involvement is getting better, but still is very low. The majority of the teachers and staff are great. I see a much better future for kids at this school. More needs to be done for Orchestra programs and computer programming, but I hope this will be handled in the future (soon). My overall observation is that the school is more worried about their rating then about the children. If a child gets behind then they force them out. Kids just give up and quit because there is no help. Sadly, I live in West Port St. John and most of the kids on my street have turned out to be drop outs. It's pathetic that a school cares so little about the student body. Education is failing and crime is rising. Space Coast is a pretty good school. There are a few teachers/coaches that standout. Coach Kenny is amazing!!! What he does for his basketball players and the special needs students is awesome. I was the 2nd graduating class of this school and still since then I have seen nothing but well educated and excelling students coming out of that school. Administration disgusts me. Teachers are terrible. There is animal feces around the campus everyday. Food regularly has mold. Atmosphere is terrible for kids. Very bad baseball program, mentally unstable head coach

South San can be compared to any school in the city & even out with it. South San is NOT what it was 15 - 20 years ago. We have a Brand new school with state of the art equipment for use & great staff on board. We offer many paths for programs for college for students to enroll. All South San does is stress the importance of moving on into your next career field & helping you on the way. Do not always believe what Fox news puts on tv trying to represent us as still a "Ghetto school" because we are not. We have little to none Gang Violence & school fights because everybody just keeps to their group. The only real problem I can say is the National Honor Society is NOT taken seriously, but rather as a joke because anybody can get in & will probably graduate as one even if you had failing grades in the past year. South San is a great school that stresses college on the first day to freshmen & along with all students having the chance to choose their career. Now with the reviews in the past stating "Too much stress on students & not much help on teachers" is BS because us teenagers just like to wait last second to do things.

column3: I went to this school a few years back, grew up here. If you want to just get by or set a path for higher education it can be done here. You as a person set what kind of education you want to leave with. The teachers were there for the ones who wanted it and if you didn't well they weren't! I do have to say the education counciling could use a little help. They told me I would make a great flight attendant. I was an average student envolved in sports and was for sure headed to college. But not for a flight attendent! My best friend was told " no no you shouldn't got to school for grafic design you will never make it" Way to get the children thinking of bigger and better things out there for them. All in all I loved this school and only hope my children have the same type of teachers that care for them and their future as I did. Good school if you take advantage of the opportunities offered including pre-post secondary curriculum and trade classes including woods, welding, auto shop, drafting, restaurant program (Drift Inn) and early childhood education. Overall not a bad school, definitely tries hard to meet the needs of the students. No place to prepare oneself for college, maybe a trade school or homemaker will be better suited for these students. Okay. Like I said its about who you know and last names. Other than that amazing

column1: This school has repeatedly shown its ability to rebound from tough circumstances. The recent tornado is the latest example of many times when people have counted us out for the count, but we have come together as a community to overcome problems. Financial setbacks, tornadoes and tragic losses have only made us stronger, and we continue to show that ours is one one the best schools in northwest Ohio.

When openings arise, the district fills positions with under-qualified teachers. Administrators are aware of alarming test scores but just make excuses instead of changes. This school district is declining quickly.

column1: Great charter school. It's like a free private school. Some parents complain about how the school has too many rules ,yet those same parents will let there kids dye there hair and wear accessories that aren't allowed. If you are a parent and thinking about enrolling your child in this school, RUN don't walk away!! They claim to have a dress-code after the first week of school you see the boys pants sagging without their belts, the teachers have no control in the classroom or in the hallways, their security guards are hardly ever at a post in case of an emergency, on the junior high part at least its a few teachers that stand on the outside and to watch the children safely to their parents cars. But on the high school side the parking on the Outer Drive side is awful !! There is fights break-outs constantly, so if you're looking for a school with education as the first priority for your child Look Further!! As a former teacher, I say Run, Run, Run. Find a better school with a sound curriculum where the curriculum supports the student's future endeavors with regard to career goals! Overall I would have to rate my experience with the school as average I saw one comment about the parking on the high school side which is sad it's hard to get in and out there's not enough parking you have one entrance and exit and as far as seeing fights all the time out here I'm here every day to pick up my child and I have yet to see any fights out here I've picked up relatives at the other two schools across the street and seen more fights there than I ever have here at the Old Redford Academy so I think they do a good job at taking care of that but I have heard that some of the girls are being abused by so-called boyfriends getting slapped up but yet there's no security to stop this they have cameras in the school there should be somebody monitoring these cameras at all time there should be no abuse going on in that form as far as I'm concerned and as a father of a daughter I would have to step in to help the girl whether she's in the right or in the wrong it doesn't matter I'm young man or a man. Should not hit a woman or a girl at all just my opinion but God created us all equal and God expects more out of men we are supposed to be leaders The worst ever they should close it This school needs to be shut down. It does not have the students' interests in mind and is merely a funnel for government funding. Students do whatever they want as there are no consequences for behavior. They are passing classes without showing up the full year, and get pushed through online credit recovery if they don't. They are not doing the population any services; students are ill prepared for life and for future education opportunities. Most teachers and staff are amazing, but the nightmare administration prevents teachers from actually doing their jobs and educating. There are numerous gang related fights every week, misuse of funding for special education and intervention, horrible mandated curriculum, and a complete lack of respect and professionalism from those in charge. Do not work here or send your kids here.

column3: Norcross is one of the greatest HS in Georgia. Great administration, great teachers and a great student body not to mention its supported by a great community!!! Go Blue Devils! Another great Gwinnett County School! This school has the best teachers and administrators ever! It has everything a student needs to succeed. Diversity, clubs, sports, band and much, much more! Great experiences with all three of my children. All were not on the AP/IB track, but have received all of the devoted attention from their teachers and administrators that we could ask for. Facilities are terrific and improving even more, thanks to the Foundation. Don't think that being a Title 1 school is a bad thing, when the money is invested as wisely as these administrators have used their resources. Crowding and class size could use some help, but then everyone wants to be a Blue Devil! Caters to the children! Awesome school! Students walk in the school with a smile! My son attends this school and he loves it! The teachers are so caring and I believe the students are spoiled. The academics are also great (World School) and my son is an honor student. If you are a good parent and you stay connected with the teachers/school - this school may work for you. First, I would like to state that I am a student who attends Norcross. I am graduating this year with a 3.5 GPA and I'm also accepted to UGA. Almost all of these ratings refer to the IB and AP programs at Norcross, however they do not speak of the other academics. It is a terrible school from my point of view. The majority of students are very uneducated to be honest. There are constantly fights in the hall ways, gym or any other area of the school. My freshman class was nearly double my graduating class (little of 40% dropout). It's impossible to be in elective you would actually like. The counseling office is a joke, it is nearly impossible to get any schedule changes. Out of my 4 years here I can also say I have only had 3 or 4 good teachers out of roughly 28 that I have had. If you have the opportunity to send your kid anywhere else in the Alpharetta/Johns Creek area I would strongly recommend it. They may not have the "high AP and IB" scores but your child will receive a better education. I have attended Norcross High for the past two years and honestly this school is nothing how it used to be. All of the adminstrators are rude and dont even listen to the students .Futhermore the teachers are trash and dont care about the students . i have recently moved schools and now i will be attending Duluth High where things are a lot different and honestly im happy i left. I'm the parent of a special needs student at NHS. The school do not care about the needs and the support your kids need they only care about football. Norcross High School special education is horrible they are the worse I have ever experienced. If you have a child that attend this school and they are in special ed....Contact the state's Special Education director keep them involved in everything that is going on with your child at this. Tiffany rojas special edu. chair is the worse. They have failed my son in every worse way Great school they really care about you here. they also have some of the best teachers in: Coach Standard Coach Johnson Coach Jatko Mrs.Fish Mr.Pepitone this school should get awards for how great it is. I am looking into moving to the Norcross High School district and I have teenage daughters, but I am concerned with some of the reviews. Everyone that I have met in the surrounding the community looks nice and well kept in the areas that I have visited. I would love feedback before I move into this neighborhood. If any one has any input, please comment. I have to decided to move before mid to late September. Please help and be honest. Thanks! :) I am a freshman at Norcross high school. I have been in the school system since kindergarten and I absolutely love it. The classes at Norcross challenge me to my best ability while also being interesting and engaging. I like most of my teachers and my guidance counselor is amazing. There are many great electives, sports, and clubs that help students to act and feel like a part of the school community. I participate in cross country, theatre, blue crew, and all the advanced classes, and I love all of it. You will not find a school with more school spirit (from teachers and students). I love this school and strongly recommend moving here. Norcross has caring teachers who want what is best for each student. Graduating students attend most major universities in the south and other prestigious universities throughout the country. There are a ton of extra-curricular activities for students to participate in. 5 star school. Great academic program!!! Would definitely recommend this school. The school is all about sports, they even have a very large "arena style" score board in their baseball field. Many students get away with very vile acts and teachers tend to not bat an eye to these occurrences. The bathrooms are not maintained well at all and in general, GCPS school portions are very small. Also the school is over crowded with 3000+ students and 30+ outdoor trailers. My sons were both involved with the Band program and have gone on to study music in college - both receiving scholarships. Although there is too much focus on athletics at this school, having IB and such a strong music program was invaluable to their education. Not very good, freshmen year was great, however; I’ve had bad encounters with teachers, the school doesn’t have very clean bathrooms, and I wish the overcrowding proble could be fixed. The atmosphere of the school is timid and lacks equality in academics and athletics. Used to be a well sought out school but now, there are far too many other options out there. Norcross is an excellent school! My son has been there 2 years, and he has had an incredible experience! The teachers are amazing, and the classes are top notch! Trust me, I'm a teacher at a different school. Norcross treats all students equally, and gives them the freedom and respect high school students need. The administration is also amazing, and so is the PTSA. The Norcross Foundation for Excellence raises money for the school, and is a fabulous organization that is similar to galas in private schools. The sports programs at Norcross are top notch also. My son plays baseball and the coaches are excellent. He has friends who play tennis, football, soccer, softball, golf, etc... and each program is amazing. We are THRILLED with NHS! Great school offering diverse educational opportunities. Full spectrum of Advanced Placement classes, International Baccalaureate diploma and IB certificate opportunities. Norcross also has excellent drama program and band programs as well as a full array of competitive sports teams. The teachers and faculty really prepare their students for college and in life. There is a competitive culture both academically and athletically that really pushes students in ways that parents can't teach.

column1: I feel the school does not prepare the children well for college. As a former student, I struggled adjusting to the actual study time that was involved in college. I can only remember taking books home to study a few times. The school needs better teachers, that better prepare for the children's future. My daughter graduated from WBHS in 2009 and started in Montevallo. A friend of hers went to Samford. Both were straight A students in high school. Both dropped out of college because they weren't prepared and couldn't handle it. Now my youngest will be going to WBHS next year unless I can somehow manage to move over the summer. (I'm trying!!) As with all school systems, you have the "populars" and other cliques. Some of the teachers care and some don't. (Tenure should be outlawed.) Football is a huge deal, but they also have several other sports. Nothing really that isn't sports related, though. The area itself is very "good ol' boy" and outsiders will never fit in. Also, it's a very poor area and a lot of things are pretty run down. I've never seen it first-hand, but my doctor says drugs are highly prevalent. A lot of inbreeding and trailer trash. I can't wait to get out of here and give my second daughter a better chance than my first one had. Wish I'd realized it back then.

column3: We just moved to this area and my son hasn't even started at the school. Went to orientation day and was already bullied. I don't plan on keeping him at this school. I was a student at Roosevelt high school for 4 years, and I have to say the in ETA at least is friendly. The band program is fun, they don't care about competitions, but they have fun, and thats what its all about. The ETA Program has outstanding teachers, all of which are very dedicated to their students, in trying to help them succeed. However outside of ETA the quality of the School drops off the side of a cliff. Gangs, Bullying, Drugs just to name a few problems. However being in The ETA Program Limits interaction with General Population to a bare minimum. So if your in the ETA Program it's a good school, however if your in DATA or regular. Well get out while you can. Collage Dropout Rates - Roosevelt Regular 76% - Data 52% - ETA 3 % To the former student who asserts that Roosevelt has a 76% COLLEGE dropout rate: Where are you getting your statistics from? I haven't been able to find out any info on Roosevelt alumni college dropout rates. Are you referring instead to the percentage of Roosevelt students who drop out of Roosevelt? According to the Texas Education Agency (TEA) the overall percentage of kids who dropped out of Roosevelt was approximately 11.5% as of 2011 (the last year for which stats are available). They offer no stats on DATA or ETA because their numbers are folded in with Roosevelt's numbers. As someone who is considering sending two of my kids to either DATA or ETA I would love to know where you are getting your information from so that I can do my own follow up research. My child is getting ready to Graduate RHS and quite honestly I feel she was given a great education. She's been accepted into Texas A&M, UTSA, Texas State, etc etc. She ran track, played a couple of lead rolls in theater, and came out with a 4.2 GPA Whats not to like? Bullying ?? Drugs ?? Fights ?? Please, it's high school. I live North Central, I listen to my lawyers buddies tell me about what those children of theirs are doing. It's called "growing up" . Besides, if the reality is that kids on the wrong side of track are tougher, when do you want your kids to learn how to deal with that. Never? Cause our children will eventually will be dealing with these type people (if that's what you call them). Roosevelt is an amazing school with amazing teachers. Go Rough Riders !! My Son has great grades i cant complain about that but the Athletic program sucks the the coaches run the same plays every week they dont rotate players into the game half of the guys on the sideline are better than the starters but somehow Coach Carroll seems to keep his son in the game though my son will not be attending or playing football for this school next year I am a recent graduate of RHS. Though sometimes things were really bad (my first year there were plenty of issues) the school and the district did a lot to clean up the place. The real problem isn't the school itself, but rather the students. The majority of the students are quite disrepectful to each other and to the teachers. The people in charge don't do much about it. (Teachers weren't allowed to press charges when a girl pulled a knife on them) but the teachers really are caring and want to help their students. Most the teachers there do not want to leave because they don't want to give up on their students. Everyone KNOWS Roosevelt has a bad rep, but not many know how good it really can be. The good things that the school have accomplished is often overlooked. JROTC continuously gets awards as well as multiple sweepstakes achievements in the fine arts. The sports isn't always winning inside of district, because it is a competitive district, but it's not their fault. The real issue with this school is the lack of support, funding, and self-confidence.

column1: Mr. Guida (now principal) always has a smile on his face and is willing to help ALL students in anyway he possibly can. During my tenure at Holy Cross I passed the AP economics exam, the class he taught. My parents and I were ecstatic as this saved us thousands of dollars in college, how can you beat that? He is a wonderful teacher and I highly recommend him and the Holy Cross education. Currently I am employed full time in the economics field and a big thanks goes out to Mr. Guida! This is a midsize, excellent school. My son was academically successful and social kid until going to Lenape high school. As his parents we noticed that he lost his enthusiasm to school and realized that Lenape is not good for my son. My son hesitate to change his school at first. After talking with Admission director at Holly Cross we had a positive impression but a lot of what if in our mind. Admission director was great, transition of my son was smooth. Friendship was great. So many great teachers. Strong leadership of Principle. My son was able to catch up his academic success in many areas, made good friends. Furthermore, we are not christian we are an interfaith family, so we were not sure how to engage and be successful on all the religious classes. It was perfectly designed, my son enjoyed from the discussions, wonderful teachers. My son developped acceptance, understanding in religeous classes. He ended up top 1 in honor history class and had good amounth of scholarship. Now he is going in CUNY system for Political Sciences. It is a wonderful school, gave confidence, currage, faith to my son. Thank you Holy Cross I was a srudent here in the mid 1990s, when this was an overpriced alternative to Lenape High School. The year I graduated, Lenape placed far more students in top colleges than HC. I am shocked at how many of the Faculty from the 90s are still around. Very very poor education, wasn't always bad though. The last two years have just been awful though. If they tell you they have a "no tolerance" stance on bullying they're lying to you. They will not expel anyone. I think they'd rather keep the tuition coming in then expel a student who was caught red handed bullying and harrasing another student. You're child has better protection at the public school. Also, their academics are limited; very few AP courses. They promise the use of laptops and other technology but not all the teachers use the same system to assign/grade homework or don't use it at all so you're still stuck with lots of paper going back and forth. There are some really great teachers though. I'm sure if they had stronger leadership these issues wouldn't exist. A great school with experienced and caring teachers! Two of my children graduated from there and received numerous scholarship offers. My youngest is there now and is following in his siblings footsteps. Each day starts with a prayer. Catholic identity is an important part of the experience at Holy Cross! Extremely excited about the opportunities we have received as a result from graduating from this school. HC is succumbing to the same issues that closed the elementary schools: high tuition and fees, lack of support from the Diocese, declining facilities/enrollment, declining Catholic identity, high property taxes/cost of living in NJ, ineffective teachers, coaches and administrators (one who stole from the school) the priests scandals, competition from other schools, top heavy salaries, lack of air conditioning and too many fund raisers. A new school name and sign may not be enough. Terrible school experience. I atttended holy cross for all 4 years and I can tell you it was the worst 4 years of my life. Save the money and invest in a better education. Camden is better. I loved it. My mother went to Holy Cross and loved it too. I just wish the new people who r taking over would continue things lime alumni being able to see old teachers whenever they want. They have to many rules now and I cant even go visit my old teachers. it sucks. They need to fix this and bring old traditions back before they bring holy cross to the ground. Not good ,money goes out for everything they will contact u by e mail on everything to raise money and donate. Coaches are great and dedicated to the kids and will help in everyway ,even tutoring them. Wrestling was the best a real family sport that will be the memories we will have. As a parent of a current sophomore, I give Holy Cross Prep the highest possible honors. My son prefers sports to academics but they have helped balance his motivation and put him on a course to be well prepared for college. He is surrounded by motivation, guidance in faith, discipline and his studies. The school is worth every dollar and then some. I completely understand the overwhelming loyalty of the alumni and current student body. Holy Cross has been a great experience for me. The students, teachers, and classes have all been great at getting us ready for college. Excellent family feeling throughout the school. Inclusive environment among students, teachers and administrators. Some great teachers, however the school is very clique based. If you don’t fit into a clique you’ll be pretty much alone throughout your years here.

column3: I'd like to give this school a higher rating, but in the past 20-30 years, it has gone downhill. I have a daughter here now, and although she loves being with her friends, almost every day she's telling me things you'd expect from an inner city school. Ironically, inner city schools have really cleaned up, while those in the suburbs are becoming what they were in the 70s and 80s. A medal winning school, ranked top 50 in the state. Offers incredible extra-curricular activities and has top notch sports and music programs. The marching band has traveled to Dublin, Ireland to take part in their st. Patricks day parade...they're amazing. The school has continually improved over the past decade, and if it keeps going in this direction, it will soon be one of the very best in massachusetts. As a graduate of this school, I can attest to the phenomenal education received!

column1: White Cloud Schools provided my daughter with an excellent education that enabled her to be successful in her career. White Cloud was viewed by other schools in the county negatively due to a large amount of poor families and racial diversity. What they didn't realize was that students accepted differences in others and were guided by caring teachers and staff to do their best. I would not have chosen any other school I had four children graduate from White Cloud and have four grandchildren currently attending. It has been a great experience for all of them and definitely had them prepared for college. The staff was great and the students are and have always been so welcoming to new students coming in. I can't say enough good things about White Cloud public schools.

column3: Amazing high school. As an alumni, I can say that LWC prepared me to be a well-educated and well-rounded person even more than my college did. The only complaint is that it was not terribly diverse, but that's not a fault of the school's. Fantastic teachers, classes, extra-curriculars, and facilities. My son is a sophomore at LWC. The school is performing above state levels; however, they did not make adequate yearly progress. The curriculum program is well organized and they have a great sports program. Unfortunately, the school is behind with technology. Walk into a classroom and you will see a 20th century classroom. I have yet to look over their technology plan but I can imagine it is not a priority. Given that my son will be taking the PARCC Assessment, I am very worried that he will not be adequately prepared. The teachers and counselors really care about the kids at Central. They have gone out of their way to help my son succeed and realize his potential. He started to struggle a bit last quarter and his teachers were quick to offer extra help and also point the resources available at Central where he can go to get help. He is so proud to be a Knight. There are so many opportunities to get involved whether it is in sports or clubs.

column1: Seems like a good school, my kids are doing well and have a great attitude. What this school needs is to concentrate on is their marching band. It is really embarassing how other schools compare..this I do not blame on the band members or directors they are so strong to put up with what they are given and deserve better. The band IS important they represent the school. Times are tough..yes BUT what does it take to give a pat on the back? .Lacks support of the marching band and has little appreciation of the students that put in the hard work to represent this school. There are This school falls extremely short compared to other schools in the area. Also the alert phone messages you get on you home phone from the Prnicipal are not at all accurate and your calls are not returned you have questions regarding that message. The parents are mislead ..due to inaccurate messages. Low due to administration more than teachers. Lack of desire to actually help students with issues. Would rather punitive measures that hurt student in succeeding. The best thing about EYHS is the community. This is because of teachers who treat the students like family and will go above and beyond to help any student who is having difficulty who is also willing to do the work. Switching schools can be a horrifying thing but the easygoing an open nature of the students made this transition a breeze and made me glad for the change. Everyone in all of my classes are all just wonderful and friendly people, the culture that the students have built is that if you are in our class we are going to accept you and be your friend. What needs to change is the principle Timothy Mitzel, repeatedly he has talked a big game about how rules and new policies need to be followed, then he just doesn't follow through. Since I have never had disciplinary actions taken against me, these big announcements that he makes are the only times I have any interaction with his authority, and when he doesn't follow through on what he says, his authority just becomes a joke.

column3: Some teachers you can tell they are only there for the money not to help the students. They don't really take punishment seriously. If you are not a sports player u mean nothing to this school and if you are you get away with anything. Don't get me started on the bullying it's so bad and if u say something about it sometimes it seems to make it worse.

column1: I had to withdraw my daughter from this school due to her being constantly bullied by the same girls everyday. I went to the school several times to report it and nothing was ever done. It got to the point where my daughter cried every morning before going to school and begged me not to make her go. I am a HUGE fan of CCISD but this school needs to shape up. My daughter keeps a blog documenting the number of classes where students are openly sleeping in class (desks pulled together to make a bed) and kids are spending their classroom time taking "selfies" (pictures of themselves) She has told us many times how her math teacher has zero class management skills, so nothing is covered in class. She comes home and looks up the areas of study using Singapore math on You Tube and teaches herself. Great school! Good teachers, good environment, my daughter loves it. She is very happy there. Clear Falls is an incredible school. They have after school tutoring for every student. The teachers and counselors are not only caring but really interested in each and every child. When I had a serious concern, about student safety, I was able to speak with the V. Principal of my daughter's grade. Those concerns were quickly addressed . I do not which school the other two parents are writing about with such strange statements about CF's but never have I witnessed anything that was described below. This is a new school and they are doing a far better job of giving the students a TOP EDUCATION. The teachers at Clear Falls are informative and up to date on emailing and or texting parents. Enjoyed the open house last night. Probably happening in so many other high schools. We have great teachers at Falls and some terrible ones. Many times, my child would come home saying that all they did was watch movies or she and others were allowed to sleep in class. But the drama and bullying are the reasons why we are considering getting out of Falls. Brought this up to the counselors and they more or less said nothing could be done. This school is awesome. Definitely one of the best in Clear Creek ISD. The teachers are great for the most part, and the principal is amazing. I would highly recommend my school to anyone. I'm a senior and the first class of Falls to graduate being here all four years. Go knights! Was there for two years until I transferred to Lake. Education over at Falls is garbage compared to what I'm getting at Lake as far as taking AP classes. Lake is the school to go to if you want your kids to be more college ready. Don't waste time fiddling around at Falls and not getting the proper education you deserve. Starting senior year and can't wait to graduate in the blue robes rather than the green ones. I'll feel more accomplished!!!
