column3: Aweome school! I love this school! My brother went to this school, too. He loves it! Although this school consistently has high ratings there are issues. If you student is even upwind of any disciplinary problems by other students expect detention without even the chance to explain yourself. I find administration has zero tolerance and while this may work well for their high ratings it sends a message of injustice and unfairness to those wrongly accused. I also agree with the reviewer about dress code. Although my child has graduated from this school I don't have any warm fuzzy feelings about it. As a parent with 2 children in this school, I know that this is an "A" school! The teachers, staff and administration are a delight and pleasure on a daily basis. I have personally seen the swim coach tutor a student immediately after swim practice on the pool deck, that's dedication! My son is in Mrs. Dahn's ( teacher of the year '08) class and the dedication and time devoted to her differently-abled students is beyond compare! If any parent has any complaints about this school, they should move to 'The PSizzle' where they will fit right in! My children are districted for Martin County HS, but we chose Jensen Beach HS because we consider it a better school. Yes, the facilities are much nicer, but that's just the beginning. The administrators and teachers at JBHS expect, not just hope, that students will excel. The teachers are top notch and really push the students to succeed. My daughter struggled in middle school but now is exceeding our wildest dreams in high school. She has a 4.0 GPA with all honors and AP classes. She's passed two AP exams and did very well on her PSATs. Now she plans to go to an Ivy. Our son will be starting in the Fall. As for the rules, kids who follow them have few problems with them. They like the strictness of the school. It gives them order and prepares them for real life. JBHS is also the safest school in the county. This school is rated as an "A" school. The faculty must be doing something right. There will always be whiney parents who complains if their child is not doing well...or Mary wasn't elected to the cheerleading team. I would do away with your rating system. How do you know if some of the poor ratings are being submitted by teens who just don't make the grade because they don't want to put sufficient time into their studies? i'm pround to say that jensen beach high school was my best experience ever since starting a new school system. every of my teachers were devoted. im proud of graduating from an ever rating A school for several years now. Go falcons!! One of the best schools I have ever been to. You can tell that the teachers and staff really care about the students. :) We moved from another state and my child has never had a detention or suspension. One month after school starting 4 days Out of school suspension and 4 detentions later I question the school, not the child since there has never been any previous disciplinary issues!! I think 4 classes a day 100 min long is nonsense. I also think the main focus is on discipline not academics. The deans are quick to suspend and give suspensions and detentions for stupid reasons like not having your student ID on your person. They do not encourage a work program nor do they allow seniors to leave campus during study hall. If we were looking for a military school I would have sent my child to one. I can't give this school one star. (The site will not allow no stars) The administration treats staff and students like inmates. Their zero tolerations shows no compassion for students especially those with special needs. How many of us would still have jobs or a partner if everyone had zero toleration. Their special needs programs are a joke. No one can hope to benefit from this place. The community and parents need to let them know we are sick of their disrespect and do not approve of their policies or the administration. Jensen Beach High school is the Best! all 3 of of my children love it. I was concered at first, making a change from a small Christian School, but they are all making good grades and they are happy to be there. :) I am very thankful that we have such a great school in Martin County. this is school is one of the best schools in the united states. all the teachers are dedicated loyal want the best for each and every students, give 110 % of their time and money and devotion. the students outrank kids all over the united states. they all goes on to higher learning. all parents are involved and care and give. the best school ever. a neighbor. Jensen Beach High School exceeds any and all expectations I had as a parent. Yes, there are very strict dress codes and codes of conduct, a school this large wouldn't be rated in the top 2000 schools in the US if it didn't! My kids are excelling academically as well as socially! Can't praise this school enough! Jensen beach high school students are not bad, the problem are the teachers and deans. Teachers are meant to help you motivate you to do something not to bring you down and embarrass you in front of others when you have done something wrong. The school looks really well coming but that's the look to get students.Yes there are some good thing about these school, there welcoming and SOME teachers are willing to help out with what you need.The kids will welcome you and no one will be left alone as far as I know. Deans will not give a thought about suspending or expel you or give you detention, They never try to remember teachers are just human after all HUMAN'S ARE NOT ALWAYS RIGHT. The biggest problem with this school is that the school does not recognize a good student when it has one. my son has been in the school system since kindergarten, and has been on a path to graduate high school with a 2 year college degree since 6th grade. he did it! Only one in his class to do so.wants to go on to become a electrical engineer. He was not even invited to scholarship night? school ranking of 120? weighted GPA 5.8? this school system is really messed up! it only works if you take the easy classes so you can have a normal 4.0, do not study too hard or you will not get any scholarships! Administration is absurd - quick to issue punishment, slow to recognize and correct problems, even slower to recognize good behavior and achievement other than on EOCs. They make it quite clear to parents that they are NOT a partner in their kids' education. There's even a new campaign posted to Facebook to get parents to take action, so I know I'm not the only one who feels this way... Very frustrating to try to keep my kids motivated to do well when they're only told they don't. The administration is cruel and unfair to their students. The rules are too strict, especially the dress code. Their food is disgusting and unhealthy. And overall many of the kids look miserable in class. TERRIBLE!! My son has been harassed by Administration so much over the last month, that he has decided to quit school. I have had many conversations with the AP as well as the Dean and to no avail. His teachers adore and support him, but otherwise, he cannot be pushed to the very edge every time Administration gives out conflicting information. Excellent. Parent input and participation is encouraged. The leadership and teachers view parents as partners, not adversaries. Outstanding Academic program with caring teachers. A variety of electives and AP courses available to students, great sports and clubs for students to participate in. One of our kids is on their way to an Ivy League acceptance with the help of wonderful teachers. The only sad issue which needs to be addressed more closely is the bullying. It happens often and many times the target the of bullying has to pay the same consequence of the offender.

column3: I wish I could give NBHS 0 stars... I attended there for 4 years. I was at the top of my class (ranked 2nd out of 600 students who graduated). I played sports, was involved in many different clubs and activities, took all AP and Honors classes (with the exception of my language class, which was the only non-honors or non-AP class I ever took). The teachers were HORRIBLE. I had teachers specifically tell me that they didn't read our papers. I had a teacher who based her entire curriculum off of spark notes. Luckily, I was able to take several online classes (all AP's). I thought the most interesting thing about that was that I did four times as much work in the online classes as the SAME AP classes that my friends were taking at NBHS. I also passed AP tests that my friends didn't without even studying for the exams because I didn't take the classes at NBHS. I love it when I hear people talk about how great NBHS is and how you can get the same education as another school. That is entirely not true. I took classes online from non-NBHS teachers as well as at a boarding school. It is a TERRIBLE school. If I had a kid I would NEVER subject them so such LOW QUALITY of education. I attended NBHS from 04-08. It is not a bad school in my opinion and my time there was plenty enjoyable since the teachers I had were committed to helping their students. I had graduated on time and with a B average and hung around with the "good crowd". The overpopulation is a HUGE issue, since it is the only public high school in the city. (I wont count E.C Goodwin) Really, there does need to be more parent/teacher cooperation and involvement to keep the students motivated and more importantly TO STAY IN THE BUILDING. I was a student at NBHS class of "02" and now a parent. I was pushed by my guidance counselor to "withdraw" myself when i was of age to do so...some kind of guidance i was told to drop out just because of slipping grades? I was also told that i would never get into college! I was young and ignorant and at that time my parents where going through a divorce so i had no support so i decided to "withdraw" and completed my diploma through adult ED. This is when i met the best teacher i ever had! Mr. Bartlewski who is now retired. He was my english teacher and like my counselor! He gave so much encouragement. He told me not to give up and believed in the ones who had potential. I wish our school system could have more teachers like him! If every teacher could take something from Mr. Bartlewski and learn from it we could have more kids graduating!! My kids wont be attending high school in this town!! I have a brother and sister who also attended and had the same experience i had! There's no money in this town and they keep cutting budgets! Get out while you can and good luck! If you have a disabled child I do not recommend this school what so ever. New Britain high school fails on providing an Appropriate EDUCATION program to students. Really happy with this school choice for my kids. Would recommend to anybody looking for quality high school for their children

column1: Antelope has met every expectation.The staff is professional,cheerful; treats the students w respect. The rare times I have called w a need I got an immediate call back and the problem is fixed right the first time.Counselors are up to the minute w info about careers & colleges.Biomedical program is outstanding! Something for everyone here, excellent music and dance as well as sports. I recently transfered to this school for my senior year. The councelors were very happy to help me get into the classes that I wanted. they are freindly and all the admin staff is amazing. they enforce rules, but for good students that is not a bother. The teachers like to help students. the college and career tech does exeptional work with the students. Many come see her for advice and talk to her. She made me enjoy coming to this school and helped me get ready for college. This school has a great spirit. they have a Red Zone that comes to support games and it is amazing. So far my journey in this high school is great. Antelope High school is an amazing high school. The teachers and staff are very nice and warm towards you. The academic learning is phenomenal, the counselors will work very hard to make sure you're on a good path. Making new friends isn't all that hard. The school is very spirited and they have one of the BEST rallies! I'd recommend this school. My daughter has attended AHS for a year now. Her last school was full of drugs, teenage pregnancies and fights - Antelope High School is a refreshing COMPLETE change from that. The students have a lot of team spirit and teenage pregnancies/drugs/fights do not seem to be an issue at all. The teachers are definitely doing something right because she has a 4.0 grade average. I highly recommend this school to all. My son is entering his senior year and my daughter is an in coming freshman at AHS. This high school is right there with the best of them in the region. I went to a small town high school, AHS has that same feel. Amazing school spirt. Great programs from the 110 member marching band to the student government to Project Lead the Way for future engineers. Plenting of AP classes to take. The kids here don't care what car you drive or the brand of your jeans but care how you treat others. As the students put it "They are real at AHS". The sports teams have great coaches and have won several section titles considering its only 6 years old thats amazing. There is something for every child there. The staff at AHS is always helpful and friendly. Can't say enough about how greatful I'm that my kids are able to go to this school. I currently go to this school, and I absolutely despise this school. It is terrible. There are so many fights, drug use, bullying, pregnancies here is is absolutely ridiculous. The teachers seem to disregard our needs, and overload on school and home work. I really mean overload on work, it's really hard to keep up and I consider myself to be somewhat intelligent. The huge class size and terrible academic reach is the worst. This school needs to change. I really do hate it Unfortunately this school is mired in mediocrity. Drug use and poor attitudes abound. This doesn't mean there aren't some parents who make school a priority and guide their children appropriately; but there seem to be many more who don't Teachers do their best with what they have. There are much better schools within a short driving distance. Look elsewhere! I took my daughter out of this school due to bullying Terrible , they have the worst sports program and the child best interest is definitely not The schools priority Mediocre. It has support in town because it is newer than the other Antelope school. This school has an identity crisis on its hand. The staff are so over the top with their political correctness that the school mascot is a red dog and not a titan because the titan is too violent and a symbol of the patriarchy. (Their words not mine)The kids that are on the margin are not helped. Those that are in AP classes are the focus and they are WAY overloaded with unrealistic homework and busy tasks not really related to the business of living and being a responsible adult.The sports program has a rift with the music program (band) and the dance team and the cheerleading are all seperate enclaves. It is fractured because leadership is so worried about red and black rallies that they never get the groups to work together. We have had football games without the band there for years.Overall the campus is great, the tools are all there, they just need the leadership and vision and getting back to making the campus and environment safe for teachers and students. There is a lot of talk and not a lot of action. Not the worst school you can attend but if you are a student, watch out for the fights and the little clicks of wannabe gangsters. Antelope is a suburb and some kids think they are hard. Avoid those at all costs. My experience at this school is pretty good. All the teachers here are nice and in my opinion this is the best school in my area by far. I recommend it to other student because I never seen anything bad at this school. They keep it clean and are strict on rules and have good policys. Brian Hewitt is a “mandated reporter” who ignores emails of a student that endured certain harassment. Disgusting staff. My son had a really hard time in Middle school and Elementary but when he came to Antelope High School everything just clicked. His 9th grade year he got A's and B's. His 10th grade year he got honor roll. No one ever thought he was capable but he had a baseball coach that was a teacher help keep him motivated. A student goverment teacher that showed him the value of being involved with his school and a group of teachers that put 100 percent to help him. The principle stands at the front of the school saying Hi to all the students. As you enter the office the front desk people are the kindest making this school feel like a home to all there students. This school I owe so much to. They turned my son who didn't care to much about school to a kid that loves school and now talks about going to college. He never wants to be late and is always rushing me out the door so he can be early. So proud of this school.

I'm a current student at Esperanza Academy CHS. I have to say that I am proud to be here. So many bad ratings about my school disappoints me so much. The teachers are supportive. The only thing that probably needs improvement is our strictness on uniforms. Like I said, its not perfect, but its a wonderful school. There are good things as most of the students can feel like its home, but it is too much "home." There would be a sense of improvement if the students were disciplined better. From what is seen in my student after she began her last two years at nea, there is not a significant amount of work given as would need in college. The school could improve by giving less freedom, more work and also preventing the guys from inappropriately "feeling" on my daughter against her will I find the people very rude talking ill about Esperanza, if students fail and misbehave its because of parents children not the school's fault. I am an graduate of 2012 and I love this school very much the students need to behave more and dress proper. But overall it's a awesome school Roberto Clemente was the worst-est compare to Esperanza so go EA! Because my teachers taught me a lot unlike Roberto Clemente. I Love nueva & i am so sad that this is my last year. #ClassOf2013 I must agree with needing to be way more strict when it comes to the girl's uniforms. column3: This school truly is very diverse and has some really wonderful and caring teachers. I was a student here who took mostly AP Classes and a few regular classes for requirements that don't offer AP (Spanish, PE, etc.). ALL but 1 of my teachers were really caring about the student and their lives. HOWEVER, just because they cared about the student didn't mean they were good teachers. One math teacher I had for an AP class was very caring about the students and would help run after school math tutoring classes and led some clubs. But when I had her as a teacher, she taught on the 1st day of class and then maybe once a month later and then a couple of days the week before the AP test. Homework was assign about 2x and reading was never assigned. Our daily activities included us doing work for other classes, listening to music or sleeping while she chatted on the phone about her personal problems.Most of us got A's in the class but only 1 person passed the AP test. There are a few more teachers I can go on about (including 1 that changed the grades of a few of his favorite students who were also athletes in his sport, from D's/C's to A's when they didn't deserve it) but I'm out of space. I'm a senior in GHS, and this is the BEST high school I have been too! Diversity, great teachers, friendly people, what's there not to love?! Well, for my freshman year i went to Cerritos high, but then in the middle of my sophomore year we moved about 2min away from Gahr. I liked Cerritos HS so I was thinking of just staying there, but then i decided to stay at CHS for the rest of my sophomore year and transfer to Gahr for my junior year. I was so excited. and i've always wanted to go to GHS, and now I see why! There are great teachers, friendly people, and i made friends in a heartbeat. GO GLADIATORS! Gahr is the worst school. It has very cruel teachers an isn't very organized about showing kids around the campus's. I believe Gahr should be below 3 because it doesn't do what is best for the students like helping them meet new people or actually giving them a full tour of the campus's What is up with gahr cheer program and cheer coach? Went from 40 to 10 girls this year. Need a new and dedicated coach? We love Gahr. They have great caring teachers and administrative staff that promotes strong, intelligent and caring students. This year a new Principal joined the school. Ms. Wise an excellent choice, this Principal is hands on and visible on campus. She is a great supporter of students, parents and staff. I expect this school will rise to higher levels. Gahr is a fantastic school with great academic programs I would rate this school a 9 out of 10 because academically it help students prepare to excel in most community colleges and smaller public universities such as Cal States. Unfortunately, the school falls a tad bit short on academically preparing students to UCs and other prestigious universities. Despite this, Gahr does help students prepare great work ethics and an understanding of one’s ability to tackle on academic obstacles which easily helps out students with a slight academic disparity in high-end universities.Most teachers at Gahr were absolutely amazing because they provided students with the guidelines to think analytically versus memorizing information and regurgitating it back out. The teachers also have personal pointers to give students if they are in need of help with their college applications or finding a college right for them. I would rate this school a 7/10. I wish they prepared us more for college/SATs because I was an honors/AP student and didn’t know what UC and CAL States were and the differences until second semester of junior year. The school spirit could’ve been better as well. In terms of teachers most of them were good but the ones that weren’t are really frustrating because everyone wonders why they’re still here and make complaints but nothing happens. In conclusion, with a wide selection of courses (BTL/ESL/ROP/ATA/CP/Honors/PLTW/APs), friendly environment, mostly decent to great teachers or staffs, diverse student groups, moderate academic rigorousness, and innovative programs offered to assist students and prepare them for colleges. Why not Gahr? This school is terrible. They are disorganized and honestly, they do not care in any way about these kids. There is absolutely no one really doing their job in that school. The worst attitude I have ever seen towards parents and students. I have been witnessed to horrible accidents to students in campus and the school didn't do anything about it. The teachers do not care if your child understands anything in class. Those scores you see are average within the school and not the state. And if you even try to bring any of these issues up to the board of education, you are wasting your time because they will ignore you. The registration day was an absolute failure, kids and parents are still lost in what to do without anyone in that school to even bother to help you, they tell you everything is online, but their website and apps are an absolute failure without any intentions of upgrading them or solve the issues. Also be very careful with your kids, the school is not safe and like I said, they do not care about these kids if any accidents or anything happens to them or in campus.

column1: I went into Connolly as a sophomore (moved from MD to MA), and I was really impressed with the school. Environment: Connolly has a great student population. You really get to know basically everyone. There really aren't any trash students (I know this sounds demeaning, but I didn't know what else to say). The school is very old. I'd have to say it is outdated: the windows, floors, tables, desks, and walls are very old. This can be a negative for some, but it really doesn't bother me. Teachers: This is a tricky subject. There are some great teachers, and there are some not great teachers. Being such a small school, there aren't too many teachers per department. I didn't like how teachers were teaching subjects in which they had no education in (a math teacher majored in history, but is teaching math). However, there is no lack in education. One history teacher has three master's degrees, and one went to Columbia University and NYU. Administration: Overall good; never fails to discipline. Overall: I am impressed with Connolly, and I recommend it to anyone who wants their child to get a better education and smaller environment.

Anyone with negative comments most likely are not involved, do not know the facility and staff, and most likely hear the bad comments from their student who blame everyone else for their bad grades, etc. Terrible parent involvement. The Clear Creek High School Symphonic Choir has been invited to sing for TMEA convention 4 times and the ACDA National Convention 3 times (both HUGE deals). Their Chamber ensemble has taken first place for the past 3 times they have competed in the American Classic Madrigal and Chamber Choir Festival. They also hold the record for the most TMEA All-Staters from one school in the entire state, 13. The Clear Creek Choir program holds up a standard of excellence like no other. As a parent, I am very disappointed with the teacher quality at this school. I would estimate that 75% of the teachers spend class time talking about topics unrelated to the subject matter, are not capable of explaining the topics in depth, or unfairly favor certain student demographics over others. My son attended elementary and intermediate school in the same school district and the teachers there were much better than the teachers at this high school. The schoolis exceptional now. The Orchestra has a new and better teacher this year and hopefully will preform better now. The chariot and band are still the best fine arts in the school with band winning the UIL contest. The sports are very good with both girls and boys water polo teams going to state( only the girls won state). The 2012-2013 varsity football team is very good starting off with a 6-0 (2-0) record. The first time a CCHS football team has won 6 games in a row. There are very little problems as far as physical violence and the student body is very friendly to others. The school recently lost a lot of students due to te opening of two new high schools ( Clear Falls and Clear Springs ). So now in stead of the 4-5K students on the campus there are about 2,050 students attending Creek. This has led to smaller amounts of students. ( the smallest # of kids in my class is 20. Most of the teachers there are very good and the AP courses are of course very challenging. The engineering department has worked with NASA via the HUNCH program to build prototypes for the International Spaxe station for some time now. The school is a great place to be and I love it here Seniors 2014! My daughter attend Clear Creek now and I am not very happy with the staff or the way they treat parents of color here. I understand following rules but if you are a concern parent and try to talk to your childs teacher without a appointment the campus police will be called immediatly. Now I am not sure if this has happened to others but it happened to me which makes me very uneasy about my childs future here. The district is constantly leaving our school in the dust, just because our school is the oldest high school. They say they are still working on construction, but the thearte department still doesn't have a stage. While we also have the smallest high school, they zoned everyone to go to Falls or Lake. I have had two daughters graduate from Creek, and my son currently attends. Creek has a great culture and the teachers are very willing to help students who show they want to try. I think the administration is fair and kind. I know my daughters were well prepared for college and are very successful adults. I credit the Creek family with a great deal of their success. "Once a Wildcat, Always a Wildcat"! This school has 89% percent of its students perform at a proficient level for Biology and 96% perform proficiently in US History. Those are just the numbers I know off the top of my head. This website is horribly inaccurate. I loved being a Wildcat!! Class of 1989

column1: Meade County high school is outstanding. The teachers are mostly friendly and want to help us succeed. Our athletic department is fantastic with multiple teams going to championships this year. We take pride in our academics, athletics and students. We have a truly safe environment.

column1: East Duplin is a terrible high school. I have gone to it for a while and have lived in the area for years and it sucks. The education is subpar, there are few class choices, some teachers definitely need some refreshing on teaching and the whole school vibe sucks. The only classes that actually provide any challenge are honors or online unless you have a terrible teacher. The regular classes leave you learning little most of the times. The honor classes while better are just more work sometimes not necessarily more learning. The school looks run down as well. I would not send my child here if I had one, most of those who say they would have never been anywhere else or anywhere better. Another bad thing is the lack of extracurricular activities. If you have other options I would consider them for sure! East Duplin is the best school I've been to. I've been to other schools in the county and out of the county and East Duplin has been by far the most supportive of my children. The school looks great and the teachers actually act as if they love my kids. My kids are both involved in multiple clubs, both have played on different athletic teams that the school has, and both love the school. This is the happiest that I've seen my kids and they will both graduate as East Duplin Panthers! Well This Is a Great School. Teachers Are Great Lunch And Learn Is Awsome You Can Either Hang Out With Your Friends, Eat Lunch, Or Go To Tutorials To Improve And Review Your Classes That You Are Failing. It's Pretty Great I Highly Recomend It . And The Transportation Is Ok. I Mean It's A lido Overloaded On The Buses And Some People Have Bad Times To Get On Buses But You Can Drive There And Pay Money To Park Here Or They Can Bring You. It's Great I Love This School I love this school! I believe that if you really give it a chance by getting involved and getting to know people you will have a great time. Everything isn't perfect, but you can definitely tell that the administrators are working really hard to improve weaker areas. I'm a senior and each year I've been here it has gotten better. This year we are even competing for WITN's "How Cool is Your School" which means we are going to be on tv for 2 hours showcasing how great our school is. East Duplin is the BEST school around!

column3: MHS does a good job of managing the students and offering activities, and they offer a good education for those in the AP track. However, when my student chose some non-AP classes junior & senior year they were a disappointment. "A" level classes should challenge the students somewhat, they should have to read challenging material and get writing assignments that prepare them for college. He was assigned books he had read in middle school. I'd hate to see what they're doing in B and C level. Overall a good high school for a well-rounded education. Diverse student population sometimes dilutes the quality of 1-on-1 time and attention required for high achieving students. Focus and attention for exatracurricular activities is more towards athletics and little/none towards science,forensic/debate. MHS is a good school with lots to offer in terms or academics, electives extra-ciricular activities. There's a music program. They have a student art and design show. However, If your kid has ADHD non-attentive type he/she will likely slide under the radar and just get by...then look out. My son graduated in 2010 and failed in college and is doing not so much now. We are paying psychologists instead of college tuition or other post-high school education/training fees. The school system has psychologists on staff but no one picked up on the ADHD. I had him tested privately his just before his junior year....too late. This school is an extraordinary institution that strides to provide the best classroom experience. By far one of the most technology enhanced public institutions in the state, Morristown has the latest Apple computers, devices, and personal computers for each student. A near college experience is available for those students who truly care about learning, and most of the teachers have Masters degrees in their subject. It is sad to note that the large non native population in the school has lowered the average of test scores. It is shameful how people who have children who don't utilize this fantastic school and resources are aloud to review this school negatively. This is an extraordinary school, and has been since 1910. Morristown High School is a one- of- a kind phenomenal high school with a racially, and economically diverse student body, 35 Varsity spot, myriad AP classes which routinely places its graduates in the most elite universities in the United States. My son went to Princeton with three other graduates of the MHS class of 2007. My daughter (MHS 2011) is at the elite music school at Indiana University. My younger son (MHS 2017) is a freshman in the band, swim and lacrosse team and a student in the STEM Academy. Morristown High School has everything any private school in New Jersey can offer. I have a son who graduated from Morristown High School and is at highly selective college and extremely well prepared for the rigor is university is demanding of him. On an equally important level, he is open to meeting people of various backgrounds at his new "home" and accepting of difference, which is the BEST education he could have gotten in High School. We have been nothing but impressed with MHS since our son started last year. The school is large, diverse and truly offers something for everyone. My son takes honors courses and we find them rigorous and challenging. Most teachers appear to have Master's degrees in their subject area. This year they expanded the 1:1 Chromebook initiative to all students in grades 7-12 in the district. They are leading the way in integrating technology into public education. We also like and respect the principal, Mark Manning and his direct, hands-on approach. The number of sports, clubs, music, art and technology programs are astounding. The school is a microcosm of our society, and is doing a wonderful job preparing kids for 21st century learning. Great high school. They offer a very wide variety of classes and programs. If you are into sports, they have some very competitive teams and also have some no-cut teams. If your child is not interested in playing sports, they have a fantastic arts and humanities program. Their school plays are phenomenal. There are some very talented students and teachers at this school and the students get accepted to the best colleges in the country. The faculty offers numerous opportunities for college prep information and activities. My son is a freshman here and we are very happy with the school as are the other parents I know. I think a school like this really exposes your children to all the walks of life. Don’t let numbers fool you, the life lessons you’ll learn here are invaluable! Excellent. Morristown is the finest high school of it's type in the US. From an academic standpoint just your average school in NJ, most kids go to Rutgers and a lot go to 2 year schools. The bullying is the real problem here, not enough individual attention for students. I absolutely loved my time at MHS (class of 2015). I learned a lot and was able to take enough AP classes that I started college with 30 credits completed. This allowed me to skip introductory college courses in english, calculus, and biology, and I felt my education at MHS fully prepared me to jump up to the next level. The value of attending a diverse school is also something that is not easily measured or reflected in rankings, although I will say that honors and AP classes are unfortunately majority white. This is a great school. Don't listen to the 2/10 equity ranking or whatever. It's only like that because all the nearby schools are 100% white. If you look we are actually above average for New Jersey. We are always ranked number 1 in the county for math, science, etc. In fact, we often beat out the private schools nearby in these categories as well. The only subject we aren't the best at is Football.

column1: I'm pretty sure this school is fine if your kid is white and middle/upper-middle class. If not, I think you're going to have a hard time adjusting from experiences with earlier schools to the high school. Their communication is lousy, their orientation is useless, and their bureaucracy is a wall. The upside is that the teachers themselves seem great. Just hope you don't have to deal with anyone other than them. The community does not support the school system and the high school is not organized to handle that. Every extra curricular is pay to play and even after you scrap the money together, the Board of Education will have no record that you paid. The high school at Amherst is like a different planet when compared to the Junior High. Excellent school, great teachers, challenging classes, great kids Pretty great. The teachers are very willing to help their students succeed and provide courses to help them get ahead, such as college courses and vocational classes/school opportunities

As a parent with kids in the school and having hosted International visiting students, I am so impressed by this school and how many graduates go on to college and other great achievements. The HS is a hidden gem!!

column1: Ive got to say coming from a student RHS (roosevelt high school) that while the staff may be welcoming the school itself is terrible i HIGHLY dislike the people there and the school is set up TERRIBLEY i would rather do online school than spend another minute at rhs (coming from a very social person). Not to mention how the class system is set up and on an even less cared for but still mentionable note they dont even support workers permits there!!! overall i enjoy the staff as mentioned but besides the staff everything at rhs is TERRIBLE!!!!!! This school is great if you are into the sports side of education, but it is very sadly lacking when it comes to the arts. If you are not an athlete, this school has practically nothing to offer you. The quality of the Drama department, for example, is sad. The plays are never serious classics. They tend to be things like Zombeo and Juliet (a comical zombie adaptation of Shakespeare's classic tragedy "Romeo and Juliet"). The stage is not built right. I even question if it is tilted like a stage should be. The acoustics in the theater are also sadly nonexistent. Not to mention that the chairs are set up in a way that you can see right into the wings from the audience. It's built like a movie theater, not a theatrical stage. This is just one example of the quality of the arts at Roosevelt. If you believe a high school diploma is enough education for your child's future, then Roosevelt is a satisfactory choice. However, if your child wants to prepare to attend a four-year university, there are other schools in the area which are much more suitable. It was clear that Roosevelt prioritizes their sports programs over college preparatory and STEM classes, as well as overall academic vigor. Although both of our kids attend in-state four-year universities now, they both have required remedial training in math and science, at least. After discussing their high school experiences with their college peers, our kids were very surprised to hear just how many AP classes, STEM programs and related extracurricular activities other high schools offered. Do your research!

column3: Sadly, over the last two or three years two factors have forced this school to decline in status. #1 is how they are implementing the Common Core curriculum. The administration has chosen to severely limit class selection for middle and high school students making it difficult for advanced students to get challenging classes on their schedule. The school administration has demonstrated a disdain for students seeking transfer to MSMS or MSA so they purposely arrange for students to not get the classes they need to qualify. #2 is the current administration seems to be doing everything possible to push away students who want to achieve. Decisions seem to be arbitrary and in many situations they aren't aware of current laws or policy decisions that affect how they should be running the school. This is sad because the school does have good programs - strong football, an active choir program, a huge band program and a caring TAG teacher. However, these high points can't make up for all the head-butting one has to do just to get a decent education. The school could be nationally competitive but refuses to do what is needed to get there.

column1: I graduated in 2003. Englewood was a great school back then, but I am sad to say that since I've graduated the feedback I've gotten about the school suggests that it has gone downhill very fast in the last 8 years. What a shame. We used to have great professors and the student body was pretty good. The administration was very caring for the students, though I've heard from current students that is no longer the case. There are still a few teachers and administrators from my era, but most have moved on and it seems like the ones they have been replaced with are horrendous. This school was terrible. I attended it for ONE day before telling my parents I could not go there. I could see my education going down the toilet. The math teacher (for 11th grade-algebra 2) was teaching material I remember learning in middle school. They teach to the test, and the tests test to the dumbest. I remember one teacher sitting at his desk the entire class period reading the news paper. The environment was scary, I was scared for my safety. This school is a holding cell for kids before they turn 18 and can be thrown into jail. The staff is (mostly-there was one counselor I was very thankful for) unhelpful and uncaring. I was greatly disappointed, because I was very excited for the "oh-so diverse" atmosphere I had heard about. Although it IS diverse, it is not worth ruining your future to go here, though I know there are not other options for some people, and for that I am sorry. it is 2012 and i've been at this school sense 2010. this school is very laid back. there is not a lot of violence or whatever. as far as teachers and staff they are good people. they be so busy to the point where it take a while to get in touch with counselors etc. the only thing this school lack is motivational events to prep kids up to want to be involved in the school. i've been making descent grades sense i've been her though. I attended this school, didnt enjoy the majority of the students but my guidance counselor was amazing and she still helps me out with everything .It was difficult for me to imagine college with my financial situation but she helped me get scholarships to pay for my college and I am SO thankful. She went above and beyond to ensure I would have a good future. And I am so happy that there was an angel in that school and she chose to watch over me. So far so good for Englewood. The office staff was very professional when my daughter and I went the check into registering with them and it seemed like they had control over what the students were or were not doing. Just remember this was our first time there and she will be a freshman this year so we shall see what the rest of the school year brings. A very good school it has turned around a lot in the past few years and improved in academics and is trying to achieve a higher academic proceed. my school is fun and that mostly depends on who you know. like if you make the right friends and you know the right people you will have a good time. and surprising when first attended i thought the kids were going to be rude and mean and dump us in trash cans but I was wrong. Most of the time they are friendly and they are curious about you like you are curious about them. So far I am pleased with the staff, and as a parent faith in the staff is very important. Mrs. Edwards is a no nonsense lady, if you think the children are going to walk in her office and play games, think again. She works diligently to help the kids and parents. Mrs. Whitehouse is also very concerned with students education, and future. She took time for us, with a full schedule an testing. I had a couple of days in office to get everything needed for enrollment , while there I observed the staff and students, it wasn't only my child they gave 100% to, new enrollees , current students and parents had the staffs attention and time. I also am pleased to say the students are also very friendly, courteous, and respectful to students, parents and staff. I think it's important to show appreciation and acknowledgement to our children's ,teachers, counselors, aides, translators, and all the staff at the schools are all important and a part of their education and future..... so in closing, with staff and students I witnessed I'm confident in my child's education and well being while in school. Go Englewood Rams... A Parent backing up the staff as well as students. ********* The school is majority population low income, students are learning below average but the teachers are great. If you have a kid that is advanced this would not be the school for them. The girls dress way to sexy and boys love it. The kids they mix in to try to make the school diverse turn out being just like the kids on lower income. Not a good school academic wise. Terrible — I was accepted at UGA and struggled because I had no foundation— the teachers were awful. It's a very good school, i recommend it. I would most likely rate this school a 2 tops I dislike Duval County Public SchoolSystem PERIOD! honestly, don't send your kids to this school if you want them to learn anything. most of the things you learn, you already did in middle school. and some teachers give petty things for you to do. this one science teacher i have won't grade anything from my journal since it's not a gray journal. she even grades things when she feels like it instead of when the deadline hits. she even complains to the students about the class it yet tries nothing to fix it and says "i'm done teaching you." and leaves the kids confused and lost. she just gives piles of work to everyone without any explanation and is overall disrespectful. literally everything here you already learned and they won't teach you how to use cards, email, do taxes, buy land, look for a job, and sign up for a big business. just don't go here. I hated it they always had me in issp

column3: Having went there myself and enrolling in the I.B. diploma program, I can trust me children will do good in life if they go here. My daughter has received an excellent education here at Yonkers MIddle High School. She is being well-prepared for college. Her teachers show outstanding dedication. It is a fun school as well as a serious school. I am very happy with this school. Yonkers high school is one of the best high schools ever known . we have teachers who care and are with us till the end of school . The teachers work hard as well as the students. the school works together as one . with band,sports,art and more we are all proud to be bulldogs. My high school experience here was pretty good, coming from someone who just graduated two weeks ago. You will not find as much diversity in any other high school than you would in Yonkers Middle. It could be a lot better though. The school could be cleaner, the lunch could be edible, and the math department needs a lot of tweaking. Trigonometry and AP Calculus needs better teachers. The bilingual students need to learn and expand their English vocabulary more so the school's reputation can exceed where it is right now. The kids are so so. The IB program is good but there are a few who really don't care about their education so they think it's okay to fall back to community college. This school is amazing. It deserves a higher score. The teachers in the IB Programme are dedicated and knowledgeable and you come away being very prepared for college. As a recent college graduate I can say that a lot of the students in my class were ill prepared for college and complained constantly about tight deadlines and hard tests. I, however, was more than prepared for the rigors of college. It's one of the top schools in the country (according to US News). It's also one of the most diverse and has a tight knit feel despite the large amount of students (our class still gets together!). Great school! I'm in the IB Diploma Program and the only downsides I can think of is they give a lot of work but work that will help you for college. However it desperately needs more funding as a minority school the state does not give much aid and as a result we sometimes have to cut corners, yet we still managed to beat Scarsdale and Bronxville on rankings grade-wise. With the funding, it'd make a perfect five.

column1: MGHS wasn't a terrible school, but it is not really a good choice. I attended school there for three years and couldn't wait until the day I walked out. Teachers blow whistles and scream out of megaphones while students are switching classes, the ends of each hallway are guarded by administrators, and lets not forget the new assistant principal who brings "No Tolerance" to another level. This high school also lacks dedicated teachers that are willing to work with their students, except for select educators that actually do care. But the counselors, some of the assistant principals, and the new school principal are the only ones that give me hope for MGHS in the future. But as of right now, it seems like a jail with books that only concerns itself with discipline and undeserved recognition. I have to honestly say that I LOVE MILLER GROVE HIGH!!! Ive had a child to complete her education at MGHS and one that's in his Senior year. Our Principal is Personal & approachable and the students have a lot of respect for him, as he has a lot of respect for them. As with any school, there's challenges but it's nothing that can't be addressed...I Love the BAND and I am the Proud Parent of two WOLVERINES!!!! Ive had a child at MGHS since 9th grade now hes in 10th grade all the other subject teachers are nice and all but his math teacher is a waste for the school miller grove can do much better his math teacher waste time and her students are paying the price on the eoct all of her 10th grade class failed i think miller grove need to pay more attention to what the teachers are doing with there students. Terrible I hated it so much. That school made me hate everything about learning and people. The teachers are so disrespectful. The JROTC Teachers always tried to fight the students. Worst school experience ever. Made me want to kms. THESE ANTICS WOULD BE ONLY AT MILLER GROVE!!!!!! MILLER GROVE BE WILDIN!!! IS HE READING??? Super cool and super good school, all the good stuff happens at miller grove. -covets Only at Miller grove we be having the best Time . . . . . . . THESE ANTICS WOULD BE ONLY AT MILLER GROVE!!!!!! Only at Miller Grove! Go Wolverines! BRUH THIS A SCHOOL ONLY AT MILLER GROVE BRUUUUUHHH ONLY AT MILLER GROOOOOVEE

column3: I am a Senior at Canyon and have been attending this school for two years. We recently received a grant of over 1 million dollars for all new equipment and have also had the whole administration changed around. There are some new teachers, a new principal, and new assistants. There have been a great deal of changes to the rules around the school. The library is no longer open during lunch, 1 class period has been added to the schedule and no bathroom passes are to be passed out and a hall monitor must escort a student if they need to go. The education is great as long as you have the right teachers. There are some that do not teach very well and it is very difficult to succeed in their class. Though, with others, you simply HAVE to study otherwise you WILL fail. There are some GREAT teachers at Canyon and I believe they have a great magnet program (I've only heard from fellow classmates on this). Canyon has low test scores, yes, but that can easily change if the students actually cared. There are some students that do not care about their education and take it for granted. This school is more than a test score. My daughter got accepted into their law program her freshman year and so far she's had a wonderful time . She has always been very smart and driven and Canyons teachers and after school programs have been excellent Horrific. I was bruised by students. Afriad of my supervisor, and unsupported bybadmi . I have great experiences with teachers, administrators, and counselors. I honestly love Canyon Springs HS!

column1: Very unhappy with this school. Did not see any involement from the teachers or counselors to help my daughter who moved mid year. They knew she was struggling but I was not contacted to get her tutoring and couldnt get a response to my calls. A lot of drug issues too. Harrison is a great school and has improved a lot over the years and continues to get better. The education itself was very good, and the teachers and coaches were all involved and amazing. I attended and graduated with excellent grades, took honor's courses, excelled in athletics and extracurricular activities, and I was very prepared for college. I did attend another high school briefly, but it was terrible compared to Harrison. No books given to students or at least with special education. Very bad sign. Notes written by teacher/assistant inaccurate. Harrison HS has come a long way in the past few years. Its test scores, student conflict rates, and graduation rates have climbed. That said, there is an inherent problem when teachers are part of a pay-for-performance system. Due to the often transient nature of the student population, test scores are not necessarily representative of teacher effort. Because many parents do not speak English, parent-teacher communication is difficult. Students do not always have the resources they need in the classrooms. There is no PTA. And in general, the school seems to care a great deal more about teachers' salaries than in placing students where they can best achieve. Yesterday, August 7, 2015...I went to Harrison check in (registration) for my Freshman. My daughter and I were very excited and ready to meet some of the faculty and staff. Unfortunately, the staff was very rude, mean, short tempered and just came off like they didn't want to be there. With the exception of the nice older lady who was taking the forms for opting out of the military contact, the lady who gave you your final packet and the ladies who gave the schedules. They were pleasant. The heavy set, older lady who sat at the table for the athletic passes was so mean, bitter and rude! She yelled at another staff member in front of anout 15 to 20 parents, students and children because the other staff member was misinformed about a situation concerning photo IDs for the students. First impressions are the lasting impressions and I am extremely nervous about sending my daughter to this school. The bad part is that all of this was before 9 am. Sheesh! I hope this wasn't an indication to how this school year will be. I have been so impressed with this school on every level; academicly, athleticly, and morality. We have had an amazing experience. There is a need for leadership who truly care in this district and school. It’s very sad that many of these students are failing and falling through the cracks. Not a lot of parental involvement. The principal and some of the coaches behavior is extremely questionable. No one does anything to support parents and their concerns from the school to the district. If you are a concerned, involved and supportive parent...they don't support you at all. The counselors are garbage and allow your children to fail. Their counselor to student ratio is half of what the state average is which means they can do more but they don't. If your child is not exceptional or someone's favorite in the athletic department, they could care less about your child. This school and most of their educators are a Joke! The principals are HORRIBLE! When there is a problem with your child they could careless. When they act like they care they talk to you, promise they will get back with you and that's the last you hear from them. The people at the Administration building are the same way; left multiple messages with no return call at all. The Principal talks down to your child and puts them down, as of she (assistant principal) is superior to them, she is a Joke, sjr doesn't know how to communicate with an adult, as we tried to have a conversation and she kept hanging up on me, but apologized when I went in person. She did have the security lie to me, saying she was not there. DONT send your child here, it's worth it to drive out of district for your child!!!

column3: I am a proud parent of a freshman at the AI Dupont High school. My experience thus far has been great. I love the response time from the teachers and administrative staff. They have really made myself as well as my daughter feel welcome. Submitted by a pround parent, Brenda Banks I'm a sophomore at this school and I have never seen a more unorganized school. I rarely find out about events and etc. with the school because they sometimes don't even say anything about about them. They state that they are low on money, but that's probably because they are spending millions of dollars on needless repairs like a hallway to the annex building. Also they students there are not a smart bunch they are like this because most of the teachers are very bad at there job and don't really teach anything important. I have nothing good to say about the school and if I had kids I would never send them to A.I. DuPont highschool. My Daughter is a sophomore at AIHS and has had a wonderful experience so far. She is in their Early College Academy program, which has been great! Excellent staff! Principal is very involved and enthusiastic! Excellent communication from school; receive texts, social media alerts and emails. Could use more parent participation, but from what I hear, that is a common issue in High Schools. Great school, great staff. Teachers are involved. My children are happy with the school. Have not had any issues there. Diverse population that works well together

column1: I grew up in this school coming from other schools in the are and in comparison to (central valley and new Brighton) I find that Beaver Falls is a school district that thrives on passion. And being that most students are not well off, those who aren't are not as likely to get picked on. It is highly diverse community and the student body reflects that. Students treat one another with respect and occasionally there are disruptions but the teachers do well to keep the students on track and motivated. It is a rich atmosphere that does well to grow student achievement, scaffolding past learning to new and creating a great curriculum that students can enjoy. They work hard on PSSA scores and keep students in check with tools to help them thrive. They also have rich and highly successful sports teams. Their extracurricular programs are great and teachers are very involved.

column3: Beware Drugs are a major issue at this school. Councillors do not help and Principle and vice principles do nothing.....that's if you can actually get to speak to them. They do not return calls, they clearly are not that concerned or heard it all before. School police are fantastic but they have a hard task ahead of them with little support. Teachers- there are a number of Great teachers so if you can steer your kid in the right direction and keep them aware from the low life then you will be okay. Be realistic with yourself and dont be fooled in to thinking you can handle it. My advice would be to send them else where. Reading the comments about athletes. I have not found it to be true that your child can't make it if they didn't start as a freshman; parents don't volunteer; or that grades don't matter if you are an athlete. Maybe in other sports, but not girls volleyball. You try out every year and every year you can be replaced by someone better. Volleyball is very competitive at all schools, and it's this way everywhere. I do agree with the person complaining about how hard it is to get in touch with counselors. It's near impossible. After weeks of emailing and calling and leaving messages with everyone my husband finally took time out of his day to walk into the counseling office so we could get an appointment with our son's counselor. That appointment was supposed to be today, but our son was never called out of class. Very disappointing. There are some really exceptional teachers at PL. If you can excel you will do well here. It is impossible to get any communication from the school. The counselors don't return phone calls nor emails and are rarely in the office. The principal, vice principal and technical staff never respond to emails or calls and are never in the office to talk to. Our son had no Spanish teacher for the first 6 weeks and we couldn't get him moved into any other class. Very frustrating trying to deal with this school. I'm not happy with the quality of some of the teachers either. Not a good experience so far for a freshman student. I have to say, this school is one of the worst schools in the san diego unified school district. My son attended PLHS. He struggled at the beginning, but I always found that teachers, counselors and staff were responsive as long as we communicated what our needs were -- no one just steps in. He found that if he worked hard, was respectful to the teachers and looked for opportunities there were plenty of great things to be found there. The students that don't do well are not putting themselves out front, and their parents don't participate by volunteering and getting to know the teachers -- always a big mistake. PLHS is crowded and has a lot of budget issues, but if you work for them they will work for you and your child. A relatively new principal (2013) is helping things as well. A large number of students are bussed into this school and their parents either cannot, or will not, participate so if you have time and a few extra dollars you can make a huge impact here. We felt it gave our son a terrific foundation for college. Point Loma High School graduates many students that go on to the University of California System, Stanford and other great universities. There is an active parent program which provides support to the Administration. The campus continues to make improvements including recent approval of a master plan for new buildings and sports facility. The football field was recently renovated and a new workout facility was constructed.The PL Baseball field (actually at Dana) is being renovated for synthetic turf and will be ready for the next Season. Former PL Alum and MLB Perfect Game pitcher David Wells is now the head coach. There is great school spirit and a wonderful scholastic program. I am a former PLHS graduate. C/O 1997. I loved my peers and clubs that I belonged to. I had several stand out teachers that really pushed me as a student to think critically, problem solve and be proud of my work. Many of my HS graduate friends went on to UC colleges. I didn't have the money because I had to pay my way through college, perhaps there was ways around it. I ended up at a community college for a few yers, got accepted to CSU San Francisco and ended up going to the Art Institute of CA here in San Diego. I learned many valuable skills at PLHS and believe the curriculum prepared me for college. There are some teachers who care about students and students are friendly to each other. Unfortunately, this is the type of school where you have to do online research to get clear answers. There are no regular or intermittent email newsletters or onotifications to parents. My child's counselor is always frazzled, abrasive, and dismissve. She has been this way since his first day of school when we met her. After that meeting and on another ocassion when she met my husband it was apparent this is her method of surviving with her "caseload" of students. Anyway, if you are thinking about sending your child to this school, you really have to stay on your toes and communicate with everyone as frequently as possible or your student's college opportunities may dwindle. You must advocate for your child and they have to learn how to advocate for themselves beacuse once you get a taste of the culture of nonchalance and factory-type processing of students at PLHS, you realize not to count on a partnership between parents and school administrators, counselors, etc. They're too busy to even answer emails. Can anyone comment on the 4/10 rating and how valid that is from your experience? I see a 97% graduation rate which is phenomenal. Am I missing something about the measurable academic quality of the school? Outlier on last years English testing? PLHS is a special place with a great history, strong academics and fantastic students. The school has very good teachers and the advanced classes are actually challenging. My son and I have been happy with PLHS. Students are friendly - bullying is NOT an issue at all. Counselors, teachers and administrators are doing as well as can be expected as their workloads are heavy. Parents need to be proactive and take the lead with their child's education and college planning. Thankfully the internet allows parents and students to get information and resources - gone are the days of being dependent on school counselors. I can't say enough horrible things about this school. First of all, my son struggles in math. There are no good math teachers. When my son asks the teacher a question they say look in the book. The book gives 1 example and that's it. He has had some good English teachers. My son is a senior this year and first day of school he doesn't have 3 classes because 3 teachers left the school. Now 3rd week of school and he still doesn't have 2 periods. I've been in constant contact with his counselor and the principal and no response. My son finally talks to his counselor this morning and she tells him that I wrote an offensive, threatening e-mail. I'm livid!! First she should tell my child this and 2nd when she doesn't respond after 20 e-mails I might have been a little angry. I still haven't heard from her. To make matters worst the principal hasn't gotten back to me either. If my son doesn't graduate because of lack of school response that will be horrible. I'm so mad at this school!!! Another thing is drugs are everywhere. Kids have tried to sell drugs to my son. The kids post themselves on istagram, snap chat doing drugs and they think it's cool. I don't see the school doing anything about it. The bullying is awful. Last year a kid was bullying my son for the first few months of school. PLHS offers many options for students that want to learn and value academics. I am impressed with the number of AP: and College Level courses that are available, and is one of the main reasons we attend this school. The academic tract is strong and has a healthy level of competition amongst students. Sports programs are of high quality, and offers a well rounded high school experience for those who participate.

column1: We moved into this district, and after 1 1/2 yrs I m so happy for my children! Everyone is accepting and friendly. Nice small community with spirited involvement in music, sports and clubs. 75 is the passing grade, which sounded intimidating - I was a little worried, but my sons have thrived! Smaller class sizes than we were used to gave them more attention and helped them do much better. My sons are fairly conscientious, independent workers - they stay out of trouble and want to do well, so to be in this positive learning environment (with less clowning/bullying distraction than their old school) is wonderful for them. We have had little problem with fitting in, teasing or anything. B-G has teamed up with a local college & my older son has been taking online college classes during study-hall periods to get early college credit FOR FREE!! B-G also offers some college credit classes taught in school. My son was an average student - now he has blossomed! He's gained such confidence from doing well, so when he does have a bad grade, it doesn't deter him and the extra help offered is great too. I am so proud to be a B-G parent - the extra care and good teaching here is clearly evident! Don't send your children here they deserve better

column3: An Excellent School...Wickenburg High School has outstanding academic, athletic, and activities programs. Respectful and hard working students, a positive and safe environment. Caring, good teachers and administrators. I am fortunate to be able to have my children go to this school. One of the Nations Best Schools! By any measure; academics, activities, athletic, facilities, students, parents, community support, teachers, administrators, Wickenburg High is a terrific school. I am very fortunate to live in Wickenberg and have my two children go to Wickenburg High School. I attended this high school from 2008-2012. I strongly do NOT recommend it to you. Whether you want your child to excel in academics or athletics, WHS will be sure to crush that dream. It's been years since either the football or boys basketball teams even made the playoffs. There's a rifle club and w/ all this news about gun violence, is a gun club really a good thing? I had one good teacher my entire time here, the rest did not know how to do their job. My math teachers would fail me for using a different formula than them regardless of my getting the answers correct. My bio teacher would literally just give students the answers when they asked for help. How does that help us learn? This high school also has a larger drug problem than Lance Armstrong. If you send your kids to this school you can trust they'll be exposed. You don't even have to buy it, I was offered by almost complete strangers to go down to the wash and share their pot multiple times. Metal detectors are nonexistent at this school and their are only two cops on the whole of campus. In the 4 yrs I was here the school was evacuated twice, once b/c a kid brought in mercury & once b/c of a bomb threat. I dont go here. But I will be This coming year. My Dad told me were moving and this is the school me and my siblings are ggoing to. Im going to be a Sophmore My brother A Senior and my little Sister a 7th Grader. I was told this is a great school, but I noticed that it is such a big one at that. And I go to a Small School right now. Do tell if this is a great choice for my siblings and I. Thanks Sarah. My child just completed their Sophomore year. He is a smart student, but it has been a struggle with this school. The teachers have absolutely no control over their classrooms. I'm always seeing police cars in the parking lot. You'd think that seeing the police cars there would scare the students straight....not so. They still have a HUGE DRUG problem. I'm seriously considering home schooling my child. I was told by an inside source that the principal gets about 20-30 bullying/harassment complaints a day. If you are thinking about bringing your children to this school, you might want to think again. I know other parents who have tried to volunteer, but were turned away. Apparently they don't appreciate or need parent involvement.

column1: The homework transition from freshman year to sophomore year was overwhelming. It killed my grade point the first nine weeks and lead to many nervous break downs. The social scene, I recall, was very cliquey. I will praise the principal for stopping the bullying when it was reported very quickly and the bullies were dealt with accordingly. Also, the appreciation of diversity and religious tolerance are not very well promoted. The only chance students get to learn about other cultures is one semester of Global Regions Freshman year and an elective class of World Religions their Senior year. To me, I would think that it would be beneficial to the students if they studied different World Religions and how they are alike and different to the Catholic faith all four years rather than hear the same things they learned in Sunday School or at their Catholic elementary school. The teachers also need to be more creative and excited about what they are teaching if they expect their students to listen. Most are either monotonous or expect the students to learn the subject matter themselves. Its an excelt school, but it needs much improvement. We have had a terrible experience at the Mount. My daughter has been cruelly bullied and the administration does not care. I have her in therapy trying to undo the damage. Come to find out that the therapist has treated MANY mount girls for the same reason. This school damages young women. Stay away from Mount. I graduated from Mount in 2008. I didn't truly appreciate the education I received there until I was in college. I went to the University of Arkansas in Fayetteville, and each and everyone of my English teachers (Composition 1, & 2 and World Literature 1 & 2) asked me where I went to High School because of how well I could write a paper and analyze literature (and poetry, etc.). I never struggled in any class where a large portion of my grade was dependent upon writing. Especially once I started 3000 level classes and above, I became very aware that the writing skills I learned at Mount were a cut above the rest. I actually ended up teaching a lot of my friends who didn't go to Mount, how to write papers, do a bibliography, etc. Science for me was the same way! I didn't have to spend a lot of time studying for my Biology, and Biological Anthropology classes/labs because I already knew most of what we had to know! I give a lot of credit to Mount for the fact that I was able to graduate college in 4 years (even with changing majors once) because a lot of people these days take over 4. Also, I am and have always been Protestant; I had no problems with going to a Catholic High School. Overstaffed and over-exaggerated. Great choice for socially competitive families and young ladies who don't mind stigmata. I attended MSM and hated every moment of its extreme feminism and not-so-Catholic ways. As an oddly liberal school, it's English courses were phenomenal. Math and science-- not so much. Expensive calculators and computers provide these failing departments with tools to pass tests, not to truly learn the material. Administration blindly handled issues between students and amongst staff. If you want a normal, non-threatening high school experience I do not recommend Mount Saint Mary Academy So different from LRSD in the best possible way. Valuable education, but invaluable leadership training. At graduation one year, Father Fred described Mount as “an experience of love and mercy on Kavanaugh that will change you forever”—I could never quite find a string of words that put it any better than that. Of all the places I’ve been and people I’ve met, nothing has ever affected me as profoundly as Mount St. Mary Academy has. I trace 99% of my success back to Mount. This school teaches women to stand up for themselves and take on the world knowing that they are deserving of anything they're willing to work for. MSM gave me lifelong friendships with inspiring, brilliant women, the best educational experience of my life, and the confidence to pursue and achieve my dreams. I am forever grateful. Wonderful environment. Caring and helpful staff and students.
