column3: My son went to the counselor to try to "fix" his situation of retaliation through low grades, the counselor did not want to 'help him fix' the issue but he came in the middle of the year to the same counselor, impressing her with his more than capable grades. Her attitude toward him was more told in a tone of 'Why should I help you when I have so many others that try? You don't want to do the work.. He is a very brilliant boy capable and just refused to do work. NOW... they don't have books but they have a new school and the stadium - well.. money should not have gone to build a new school or other unnecessary luxuries when they don't bother to buy updated books for the kids to use. They share books with all of the other students for that class - not leaving those who take extra time to learn the work any kind of avenue to do so if they aren't afforded the internet at home. They care more about the football, basketball, and baseball programs than anything else and built the new school to keep up appearances that they are scaling the low sides in grades. Grades are not important to this school. I know that the school was old.. but books should come first in education! This School is Everything wrong with the American Education System...It's run more like a Prison and A NFL Simolator than an Actual School. Teachers here don't care about Students, A specially those learning Indifferent Ones, There just toss In a Special needs Classroom with an Uninspired Bad Teacher that doesn't care rather than giving Actual Resources that help them in Class. Bad Teachers and Bully Students run this School Unfortunately so my Advice look at Better Schools. I go to Zanesville High School and yes while it's a bigger school it allows for more options for student like myself and my peers if someone was just moving here I would recommend Zanesville High School every single time

column1: This school has a great number of outstanding activities for students. The music program is particularly outstanding. The jazz and marching band components are easily among the best in the entire state. My child was involved in music, drama and sports. Most of the treachers are very dedicated and appreciate the high quality of students they are priviliged to teach. As a relatively affluent district it does not have much economic diversity, but it does have quite a bit of ethnic diversity. Parental involvement and support for both the school and students is very high and is a significant reason for the success this school continues to experience. My child was accepted to a world class university after attending school in New Hartford. My child greatly enjoyed the social environment and has a wealth of very good friends from having attended school in New Hartford. The teachers at New Hartford have always done an impeccable job at fostering learning, mentoring their students, and providing experiences which help prepare students for college and life after high school. I had the best experience attending New Hartford schools. I graduated in 2007 and went on to earn my Bachelor's. I cannot put into words the impact that the teachers of NHHS (as well as Perry and Hughes) have had on my life and still continue to now! I learned beyond the walls of the classroom from the wonderful group of teachers who mentored me and pushed me to become my best self. The athletic programs and arts programs (basketball, track & field, and music, for me) are amazing and ranked among the best of the best. I still keep in contact with many of my teachers and friends from NHHS. I always enjoyed going to school and still enjoy visiting from time to time. I can't thank the community enough for my wonderful experiences as a student there, and I hope to someday move back to the area and enroll my future children in the New Hartford schools... simply put, they are the BEST!!! New Hartford Senior High School is a great school to attend. The advanced placement courses are outstanding, and the teachers are great. Graduating seniors are very well prepared for college.

column3: I currently go to Judson High School and personally I love it. I have had not major problems, a few things go wrong, but when in life is everything perfect? I think Judson prepares you for life and exposes you to diversity. I have good friends and am in honor classes, so I would like to think that i am on the right track. I would say that if you are the type of person that looks for trouble, you could find it at Judson. I am happy there and I couldnt imagine being anywhere else. I would recommend it. The best type of comment that could be on here is one form a student going there currently, so here mine is! GO Judson Rockets and Go Judson Rocket Band! Judson was the basis for my thriving career in the information technology field. They had numerous technology related courses teaching Microsoft, Cisco, programming, and more. Judson has many courses for students interested in a wide range of careers and it adequately prepared me for my college education. My only complaint is that it is easy to fall in with the "wrong crowd," but i'm sure this can be said of many schools. Barley get any homework or projects and the teacher done not all do not get back to you when you email them your questions and concerns. Great school!offering a lot of classes! Love the teacher. stay in this school district for my other children. Judson is a great school. When you look at its history in academics and athletics, it is a great school. Judson is back on the rise in academics. It used to be the worst school in the San Antonio area. It is starting to clean up. Judson offers a lot. They want to get you where YOU want to be. They have a lot classes to take to start your career. With over 3700 students, it is really not that bad. Judson used to be ranked 90/100 in the San Antonio area in the last 2 years. We are now at 71/100 in the San Antonio area. Teachers really care at Judson, daily homework and assignments are boosting Judson academically. Judson also hast great facilities. The best in the area. Judson is also very good in Athletics. Most people know for Judson for its Historic Football Program and recently, their Basketball program in both Boys and Girls. I would recommend your child to come here. It is a great school. Hi, I'm a current student at Judson. Don't bring your kid here. Someone once told me "Judson is for socializing, not learning", and they couldn't be more right. From what I've witnessed, the teachers are verbally abused daily by the students. I've never met such disrespectful children. The students never do their work, and in return, the teachers stop trying. This makes it very difficult for the very, very few students that actually enjoy learning. If you want help, don't go to the front office. They never know what's going on in the school. I've tried to receive help from them multiple times (regarding events going on in the school) and they didn't know what was going on. I thought it was very unprofessional. Students here constantly interrupt the kids, the teachers don't teach, etc. I know, you'd expect laziness from high schoolers, but these are next-level idiots. Like, my teacher whispered to me "I give up". Do you know how depressing that is? She was so excited at the beginning of the year, but now she can't wait to leave. I pray for all the teachers at Judson (who actually try) a strong mind so they may get through the rest of this year, and next year, peacefully. I had to remove my daughter for her safety and health. She was being harassed daily my male students, who felt they had the right to inappropriately touch and solicit her sexually. These male students harassing female students has got to stop. It is not o.k. and causing lasting damage. Thank God for Texas and public school choice.

I recommend asking anyone involved with this program their story and thoughts. Great school. My daughter attended New Paris Elementary School (part of the Fairfield district) for 6 years and loved it up until 4th grade. The bullying is horrible and the teachers are rude. The administration is not looking after the best interest of the students. Dissapointing degrading. One of the worst experiences I have been through with my child was at this school. Great!! Best school system I have seen in a while. Upstanding families, involved and caring community truly more than just a school. If you get involved you will experience the support and care from all.

column3: Peekskill HS has gone from a ghetto school, where few children did well to one that now includes AP courses and is educating all its students to go to good colleges. The Supt. of Schools, Judith Johnson, has made this happen over her 9 year tenure.. Peekskill high school is a diverse high school. The teachers are good and students should excel to take AP courses and challenge themselves. I have attended 3 high schools (A private catholic school in somers, PHS, and a public school in Florida). PHS was by far the best. The teachers provided quality and it was an overall wonderful experience. I wish I did not have to move for my senior year. Two of my children attends this school and I cant wait to get them out this school district There is a high administrative turnover. The students have little respect for the school and teachers. The athletic program is one of the worst in the state. I currently have two children in the Peekskill school district who are both high honor roll students,both involved in sports and clubs . The teachers are wonderful. We are very happy with the school district. Overall good experience with a diverse student body. Your kids will get out of it what they put into it. If they study, are respectful, and have a healthy curiosity for learning, they will find themselves in a good place. If they tune out or run amok, then they will wind up a poor statistic. Both of my daughters took advantage of Honors/AP classes, played sports, graduated, and went to excellent colleges. I personally know many previous grads that have gone on to NYU, RPI, St. Johns, Temple, Binghamton and Howard. There's always more to the stats than the superficial numbers. You may pick a different school that's rated a 9/10, but your kids wind up absolutely miserable with self-esteem issues, or feel they have to compete with superficial material items, or isolated by student cliques, unconscious biases. The diversity at Peekskill at least helps to offset the teenage angst, as well as parental angst. I had to send my children to a private school because of the lack of preparedness for college.There is no busing after 5th grade. I should have done my homework and moved to another town with a better school district. the teachers are very nice and teach well, very good environment overall

column3: In the Longview area this is pretty much the "safe" school and while there are some level of worldly kids thats pretty much to be expected in East Texas. However they tend to overemphasize social status so if you want your kid to be popular this is the best place. If you can't afford a lot of gimmicks and your child does well academically don't expect it to matter. Placement for college is spurious and there is a lot of grade inflation and extracurricular group projects to help people who aren't motivated but in the right clique get by but its not going to get people ready to go as college freshmen. Its really just a matter if you want your kids to be relatively safer and suffer a bit academically so long as you know there is a good group and a bad group. If your kid is in the bad group by high school the tell tale signs will start with encouragement to place them elsewhere and then discipline problems that never existed before will be invented. If you live in the right neighborhood this could be the best experience of your child's life before the real world catches up with them. School is noninclusive and harsh in it's policies. Staff doesn't respect students and is apathetic.

column1: This is a country bumpkin school. Don't let the Greatschools.org score fool you. If you are country bumpkin Iowa this school is probably mediocre but coming from the West Coast this school is a 3 out of 10. There are no Honors or upper level classes in English, everyone takes the same English level class even if you are an outstanding student. Like all of the Iowa high schools, most AP classes are not offered until junior year. There is a lack of choices in classes for students who are Honors level. The school is a God and sports school. The cliques are closed to outsiders in this school. If your child is academically focused, then take your child to Linn Marr or West High. The students at this school make fun of smart kids who have outstanding grades. It is uncool! The students are given laptops but only use to surf the internet at the school and teachers rarely give homework that involves the use of the laptop. Its a fancy gimmick but the school should have spent the money for higher level English and math classes. If this is college prep then what is the level of the Iowa colleges? Surely it is not on par with UC Davis and University of Washington. I love my school, my teachers, and all the great opportunities I have. It is the perfect place for a talented and gifted kid like myself. Prairie is an excellent choice for anyone. Like any school we have groups that like to hang out with each other but personally I could walk up to anyone of have a good conversation with them. The cliques aren't that strong anymore. This is an excellent school for academics and provide many college prep courses in partnership with Kirkwood and have been steadily expanding their AP opportunities for students. We have very strong music and speech/drama programs as well as very strong sports programs and have top notch facilities to accommodate those activities. This school district is bursting at the seams with the amount of students in our schools and we are constantly expanding and adding schools and it is in the next ten year plan to expand the high school to house the upcoming grades and continue to upgrade and expand to meet the needs of the explosive growth of the district. I believe we were recently ranked 9th in Iowa in academic/college prep. Prairie is a great choice but the schools are becoming over populated and the grade sizes are growing rapidly in the elementary schools especially, each grade being bigger than the one before. Is a Great School because when my Kids are not in school they call us to check on then they allways doing things for the kids thie school keep SAFE they send us (ALERT) Despite some of my concerns about conservative administration, our kids have benefited greatly from a good music program and some very good teachers. I also feel the Junior High does an exemplary job with not tolerating drug use/violence. The high school soccer coach was a real piece of work at the Valley invitational in Des Moines. Even the soccer players on his team were chiming in and yelling obscenities at the Valley staff, spectators and other teams. I hope they are not allowed back! Administration is terrible to staff. I do not recommend this school as a place to work.

column3: I am currently a student at FHS and I love it there. My courses and competitive and brisk, but well-taught. The teachers really get to know their students on a personal level and go out of there way to help their students achieve success. I especially appreciate their math, science, foregin languages, and English courses. The majority of the kids (and their parents) at FHS care deeply about their grades. Friendswood is a tight-knit community with old school values (family, community, volunteerism) and it really reflects in the school. Friendswood High School is very clickish like the community! Most teachers are great, and some just don't teach! If you have a problem the school's AP & P will handle it right away! Unfortuantely most students make it difficult for new students to feel welcomed! This is a school of exceptional students led by exceptional parents...no true leadership exists at FHS nor are the teachers above and beyond any other average school. There is a system set up so no one complains up to the superintendent and the principal does nothing but support his staff. Department heads do not support students nor do they investigate problems in a reasonable, common sense manner. Even students that are bullied at this school get tickets because the school does not investigate anything. They wash themselves of any responsiblility. My son has been taking engineering coursework, which is not considered toward AP work, with teachers who are not qualified nor suited for engineering or computer science. My advice to anyone would be to save your money and don't move to Friendswood for the schools. We did and we regret it. This school is full of teachers and administrators who graduated from FHS themselves who have each others back. It is all about money and promotion, not about the students. We are moving as soon as graduation is over. Overall even though you have your fair share of petty kids there, that doesn't put a damper on the other students who have both amazing minds and even more amazing hearts. Moving to Friendswood was the best move we ever did for our son. He was a newbie in 7th grade. He was bullied, but the principal at that time handled the issue effectively. Parents in this district are very involved. There is that "clickish" behavior present, but we just keep to ourselves and mingle with people who don't buy their 16 year old kid a brand new mustang ;) Not all of his teachers were effective - there was one whom I can't believe is still working, but overall, it is a top notch school run by a very stern administration. My son went on to college and excelled there due to his well-learned study habits. Great school for students who want to excel. My son has learned responsibility, accountability (something that’s missing in other districts), work ethic, and college readiness. Yes, there are cliques, but it has not hindered his learning and growth. Highly qualified teachers who are backed up by administration so they can do their jobs without much interference from parents. I’m glad we moved here in 2011. I feel like my son has a good foundation for lifelong learning.

column3: I went to many other shcools in the district. Hercules, DeAnza, and Richmond. I must say that this is the BEST school in the district thus far. For this poor district, El Cerrito has a lot to offer. It raises it's own money for clubs, and it uses the school funding wisely. For books and "the community project" which is basically a health care place and so much more. El Cerrito has open so many doors for me. I can actually see myself pursue my dreams now. I was a troubled kid, but El Cerrito representative offered me counseling, and I can't tell you how much that helped me. Not only my mood has changed, but also my mindset. I'm not saying this place is heaven on earth, nor saying it's the best school in the world. But to me, it's the best school I've went to so far in the district. Bottom line, education comes first here, teachers are dedicated, campus is safe. I love El Cerrito. El Cerrito is a good school. It has a diverse population of teachers and students. It has a history of alumni who help inspire a healthy shcool admiration for school spirit and academic education. It also has a community that supports all that the school reperesents. Kudos to El cerrito High School home of the Gauchos! The mission statement is as follows: "ECHS is a mutually supportive, academic community dedicated to helping students develop pride, perseverance, and purpose, in order to realize their potential." While this may be true for the majority of the student body, it is NOT true for students who have issues regarding motivation, resiliency, and anxiety. Students with ADHD, as well as other medical issues, including anxiety, suffer the most. Not only does the school REFUSE to support "teacher-student-match" when designing their schedule, but they will NOT allow a teacher change when the kids clearly cannot handle certain teaching styles. They will NOT consider anxiety level as a factor in preventing these students from learning, and hold fast to their "policy" of "no teacher changes." I feel so bad for these kids who have already given up in the 2nd week of the semester. They have NO motivation to persist in attending class or doing the work. Their anxiety level is HIGH. I cannot, in good conscience, speak well of this school. They are part of a problem and are not willing to become part of a solution. The lack of empathy on the part of the counselors and administrators is astounding. We have had a great experience at ECHS. Very happy there. Academics are strong, diverse student body, great new principal. El Cerrito is purgatory for children with special needs. In fact the whole West Contra Costa School District is. They cut therapy, incompetent teachers and teachers aids, a bureaucratic administration. If there are wonderful teachers and aids, they get solicited by higher paying districts, because this district would rather spend taxpayer's $ to upgrading schools. I'm fine with renovating school, they could use it, but many of the construction are ostentatious and wasteful. They would rather keep children with special needs in the dark ages. Out of sight, out of mind. terrible because i hate el cerrito and the other students are bullies This school offers the semesterized block schedule, so it's like college. Students take 3-4, 2-hour classes a semester. This allows them to focus on just a few subjects. In his junior year he has doubled up on sciences (AP Bio and AP Env Sci); next year he plans to double up on math (Math AB first semester, Math BC second semester). The ethnic and class diversity is great; I feel like my son has friends from all backgrounds. He and his buddies have not experienced any bullying, but he has seen some fights (usually between students of the same race). There are police officers on campus at all times, but the overall vibe seems very energetic and peaceful. My kid has been able to take lots of AP classes, and teachers are very dedicated. I think his first year was the hardest: he was in a lot of freshman-only classes (like PE, Art, & Geography). There were many disruptive students that made the learning environment uncomfortable. Once my son started his sophomore year, students matured, and he was in advanced classes with other motivated students. In addition to academics, ECHS has many strong elective programs, like debate, dance, and band, as well as two academic academies: IT and Media. This summer he will participate in Global Glimpse, a two week program in a latin country (students must apply, scholarships are available--some students only pay $500). My child came from a small private middle school, and I was concerned about the transition. However, I think he's getting an excellent education, he has lots of friends, and he will be ready for a competitive college! Go Gauchos!!! Being a student here is great. The teachers / faculty are very friendly, and the academia is just the right amount of challenging. I've seen numerous students from this school who excel in college! Student here! I'm not a big fan of El Cerrito for a majority of reasons, though there are some things that I can appreciate at this school. The student diversity is appreciated, and there are spaces for students to get on-campus counseling, however there are so many kids that actually need counseling that it's sometimes hard to get in contact with counselors, though I don't fault either of them. The school has gotten class schedules mixed up before ( adding / removing classes a week after the semester starts ) and some kids even have trouble talking with some of their teachers because of prior bad experiences with teachers, anxiety or lack of energy / willingness / ability to work due to a number of reasons. My daughter was in private schools until her freshman year and has matured immensely with the diverse and challenging atmosphere. She's learned to carry herself with confidence and is enjoying the academic challenges with her AP and Honors classes. She's plugged into sports and band and both communities are supportive and caring. The kids who are committed to academics soar at this school. NOTE: this site has old, outdated information, particularly with regard to test scores and student body racial makeup. My kid is applying to a multitude of colleges and she'll do fine at probably any one of them (she's hoping for a UC). She has challenged herself with AP courses and pulled in good grades. School is school... perhaps she would have excelled even better in a private or high end school or perhaps not. It's hard to know. Perhaps she would have felt like she was a failure due to the over the top competition. Overall, she's done great at ECHS and feels incredibly good about herself and her abilities. She has a bright future ahead for herself and ECHS has helped prepare her academically and socially for that future. Ms. Crespo has created an atmosphere that will drive away many families whom she perceives as privileged and entitled (mainly people that complain about things that are dysfunctional at the administration level). The school is ok. ADMIN is terrible and they don't allow kids to walk the stage for missing the 2 days of rehearsal. I know over 20 kids who won't walk the stage because they can't miss work or other required activities to go to both rehearsals but can make the graduation. This school is honestly a good school for the first year of school, but just because of the admin removing electives and not understanding this school is not recommended. Things have only gone downhill since the pandemic (not surprisingly). Aside from district wide teacher shortages, the Principal at ECHS cannot and does not lead. She was barely visible (except for online at her home, eating) once a semester. The vice principals are stronger (but one is leaving). My student has no homework, spent most academic classes just on their phone for half the class (with teachers permission) b/c little is being taught. Classes are long—it’s a block system of 3-4 classes a semester. We thought that would be great prep for college, but it’s been a bust as teachers mostly don’t know how to use that time fully. The music program used to be strong, but the pandemic also curtailed that (understandably). But rather than spend more time building a sense of community, the director has focused on a handful of students he likes and ignored the rest. We know at least 10 families that have dropped out of the band program the past two years—and these were kids who really loved playing prior to high school. It’s a toxic atmosphere. Academically, my student is doing very well grade-wise, but not convinced they have learned much. Will be a wake up call in college for those who have fallen behind as well as those who are seemingly doing “well”. Finally, there were two lockdowns last semester—for firearm possession on-campus. We learned of it first thru our student (they have phones after all). Admin was (sort of) forthcoming later and implemented a backpack check for a couple weeks. Not really a long term solution or adequate.

column1: Excellent academics, amazing staff , competitive athletics and great peers for my son. An all around fantastic school. Excellent teaching professionals, resources and learning environment. LOLHS is not as great as we had expected, especially as outsiders. We moved to the area as a military family, looking to settle down in a nice New England community with high quality schools. Naturally, we were attracted to Lyme-Old Lyme High School with its motto 'of private school experience in a public school setting.' The scores for the school likewise reflect great schools. However, our experience, and the experience of many other families that moved here from outside, has been similarly bad. Lyme - Old Lyme is very small. This leads to great class sizes and teacher to student ratios (and a surprising number of clubs and athletic options) but it has all of the worst attributes of a small town in SPADES. Surprisingly, despite a very well educated and well traveled populace, it is very much a small town, very closed attitudes towards outsiders. Most kids have friends they've had since elementary school, and no interest in involving new kids in their friend group. This experience has been the case with multiple kids in our family, an exchange student we had, other military families, and non-military families that are new to the area. Our kids have been profoundly sad and lonely. The administration chooses to see these as isolated cases of kids with mental health issues rather than a systemic problem. The feeling of the town as a whole is similar, LOL's adult community is similarly closed, withdrawn, and not particularly friendly to outsiders. We have been here four years and feel like we would still be outsiders if we stayed for 40 more. Not a friendly place, would not recommend moving here . If your kid is very outgoing, exceptional at a sport like basketball, soccer or rowing, then they might be able to break in to a group of kids involved in a sport. Otherwise, your kids will be happier in a bigger more worldly school. Agree with the previous review 100 percent. Some good teachers who care. You could live here for 30 years and be kept at the margins by the sharp-elbowed locals. Definitely a 'we were here first' ethos prevails. While it's disconcerting for adults, it's profoundly difficult for children in the schools/community. Happy to be nearing the end of our stretch here. The locals made it a slog for our kids, who gamely made the best of it. Onward! If at all possible, take a pass on this burgh. As a former student of this school with a good relationship with the teachers and administration I am disappointed and offended by the high standards they hold themselves to. After experiencing the real world I was shocked by the failure I was set up for by this school. Although the academics were good, I hold resentment in the lack of education on social issues as I had to learn the truth about them the hard way throughout college. This school is full of extreme hidden racism as I look back. The teachers are extremely discriminatory against students. The school has proven to handle mental health instances in an extremely inappropriate and offensive manor through enforcement, and continues to praise known sexual assaulters to this day. The administration overlooks the real issues of the school and targets specific students. To this day I am personally sickened by the persona this school puts on through PR, and their focus on gaining money through prioritizing out of town students who pay to attend. Things need to change, but the school will never recognize its extreme flaws. I feel the equity gap is too large. My son is the only Hispanic/black child at the school, and we feel as if he’s been pushed along. Smart kids succeed and the special need kids are slid along to graduate. I truly hope this is not the case and they truly care about the under privileged getting the same education and attention. We lived here for the schools, but can’t wait to move once our son is done with high school. No diversity and very exclusive. We’ve lived here for 5 years, participated in sports and activities, neither of us have established any friends. It is better to be here than where we were (Willimantic), granted, but he deserved better. I recommend trying for more diverse schools with mediocre ratings like in Hamden or East Rock New Haven for a more fair treatment of transfer/low income individual students. It’s hard to find housing these days so we are stuck for now. Get to together Old Lyme, it’s embarrassing sometimes.

column3: TC West has wonderful adult leadership in the principals, guidance counselors AND the secretaries of each area of the school. The athletics are phenomenal, and the music program is unmatched in the state. Having a high school the size of West take on a difficult just-released Broadway show like Phantom of the Opera with nine roles being doubled on alternating nights - and having sellout performances, one after another, speaks for itself. The leadership of this school is just outstanding. They set the bar high for their students and then lead them, encourage them and model for them how to reach their goals. Graduated here in 2010 after attending this school for a year. I had no issues with this school and I didn't meet one bad apple there (pun?). The staff were all helpful and I had no issues with the principals. The lunches were above average surprisingly, as the food they provided seemed to be great quality food (surprising, right?) I can't think of many negatives about this school really. This school has thousands of students, but the school has so many wide hallways and a second floor so you barely notice how many students are in this school. I never had problems in the hallways getting to class on time as there was never too many students in the hallways at one time. Overall, great school. I only wish I could have spent all my high school days here My son had a great experience at West Sr. High. They offer a large amount of AP classes and the staff is excellent. Even though it is a big school, it never felt big to him or us. The teachers and administration were very responsive to both his issues and our questions. He was very well prepared upon entering college.

column1: Mostly Positive. New principal this past year has been a great asset to the school climate and student/teacher support. Schools like this one, with a curriculum designed by local church leaders and old people, are what gives birth to young republicans that don't know better.

column3: Fantastic school. My son graduated in May of 2013 and my daughter is a freshman this year. Everyone really tries their best to help your students be successful. The communication between the school and parents is excellent. I always know what's going on in my students classes regardless of whether or not my kids tell me. When my son was preparing for college, all of his teachers and counselors were very helpful in helping him make the right decisions. They teachers and administrators helped the entire freshmen class transition easily from middle school to high school. If you are considering moving into the Chesterfield area, definitely move into the PCH attendance area. This school really isn't all that people are saying it is. The people aren't nice, a lot of them do drugs, they're are a lot of bullies, and it just isn't a place where I would want my kids to go. The teachers aren't great, some are some aren't. They all move too fast and if you need help during class there isn't enough teachers for them to come and work with you. I don't recommend anyone to go here, stay away from this school. I almost want to transfer to Fern Ridge, there's more hope for kids who suck at school. High quality school especially in Science and language arts. The science building is state of the art and the quality of the instructors is excellent. Two of my children graduated and went on to challenging colleges where they were well prepared and stood out among their college piers. I would highly recommend this school from the college counseling to the academic support. Also the students range from all interests and backgrounds. My two children entered in High School and made friends easily. Very positive, high values, diverse, and excellent academic standards

column1: Frankenmuth High School and the district in general used to be a great place. Now it is a good place. The school board and superintendent are a very clandestine operation and ruthless. The past four years has proven that athletics are a mere inconvenience to them. They would love for it to go away. They are also entertaining the idea of open enrollment which is not a good thing. The teachers union is very strong and they are in the pocket of the admin and vise versa. If I were moving to the area I would check out Freeland, Nouvel or Valley Lutheran. Freeland is closed enrollment and they really have it all going on over there. Frankenmuth has taken a hard turn to the left. A top notch school that has high test scores and sends nearly all students on to higher education. Academics are a top priority and several AP classes have been added in past years. They offer a wide variety of athletics and extra-curriculars where students also perform well. The school is not huge, your child will not get lost. Parents are actively involved and they expect top results. The staff is young, enthusiastic, and they make good use of new technology in the classroom. Frankenmuth High School has prepared our 3 children extremely well for College. We've been very pleased with all of the academic offerings and the addition of AP courses. Our sports programs have been a great compliment to the academics they've learned at FHS. I would strongly encourage anyone thinking of moving to the area to consider FHS. FHS has received a great deal of accolades due primarily to high performing test scores. The main reason for this is that the kids who attend come primarily from well educated homes where the parents are college educated, hard working and VERY involved in the entire education process. Additionally, the teachers are mostly very good. Keeping it real...the administration is poor. They are not at the front of education in a number of areas. The computer training is horrific. The counselors are overwhelmed and focus on paper shuffling. The principal seems to be resting on the laurels of a high performing school. Instead she should get moving on adding more AP classes, providing technology instruction that is current, and shore up her office - where the answer almost always is "no" - what's the question? The overriding issue is exactly as some others have described; arrogance and resting on laurels. Crucial social issues are unaddressed, even unacknowledged, while favoritism towards athletes apparently remains unchecked. Although there are some excellent teachers, the administration's bungling and subsequent denial of their mismanagement has ranged from unnerving to appalling. Academically, they may be superior to some, but they are not at the pinnacle, as they seem to imagine themselves. I recall school news letters rife with improper grammar and spelling. Come on! My children started school with perfect English and were reading aloud beautifully before kindergarten. Thankfully, they have excelled despite their experience at FHS, but others are not. Some concerned parents are transferring their children from Frankenmuth Public Schools and paying tuition at the local parochial school which has proven delightfully impressive, especially in the science curriculum. Unfortunately, our only option for high school is FHS, so one family has purchased a second home in a distant city with a great school, where they will live until their child graduates. I miss them, but I do understand! My experience at Frankenmuth High School and the Frankenmuth Public School District has been mediocre at best. Over the course of my seventh and eighth grade I was ridiculed by the teachers because of my forgetful tendency. I was called out in front of the class and put on a pedestal of shame as an example of how not to be. In the second semester of my sophomore year my mother and I found out (with great trouble) that I have ADHD and am on the autism spectrum. (although not visually noticeable) So throughout the years that I had been put down because of being "lazy" and "not trying" I was actually trying my heart out, only nobody would listen. The special education program is atrocious in this school district. Many laws regarding special education that were being broken by the school had been covered up in a glorious façade. This school district only focuses on the natural born athletes and the out-going "perfect students." They cover up the wretched special Ed program (that's nearly non existent) and lack of care for the arts. I'm currently a senior attending this high school and am happy to reveal the true Frankenmuth High School that most people don't know about.

column3: I am a parent of an IEP student. My child went to the Westfield MA public school system and I had so many issues with this school and some of the teachers there, and I am an alumni of the Westfield High School. I guess years do make a difference. I had to move out of state for my health and the Florida school which was one of the top schools in Florida I placed my child in. It was okay. My child had some nice and attentive teachers there. Unfortunately, we had to move back to Massachusetts due to a family emergency. This school is amazing! I have never had such an attentive IEP meeting with my child's teachers, and my child who has a learning disability went from bottom to top. My child is graduating this year in pro merito honor society. I am so proud and very happy with this school. The only thing I am upset about is they let one of the teachers go this year and this teacher did so well. So as a parent of an IEP child who attended this school I am very proud and I can not stop smiling. Not only that, my dad graduated at this school back in the 1960's and it makes me smile as my child was not able to meet her grandfather as he passed away before she was born. I give this school definitely an "A". Horrible. As the saying goes "the fish rots from the head down" A change in the administration, namely the Superintendent must go or this school will continue to go down. Look at the numbers over the last 4 years. We are accepting mediocrity. What a shame! This town needs to wake up I think that this school is different.

column1: Where do I start? Teachers. Curriculum. Building. Focus. Hmmm. To be honest I have multiple children enrolled in this school and babysit for multiple children in this school and the staff is deteriorating very quickly. Many times my children in various grade levels tell me that the teacher has told them " she doesn't have time to work on that" or maybe your parents should get you a tutor. There is no one on one time but there is plenty of time for them to stand in the hallway and gossip or have their own children come into the classroom during class times and disrupt my child's education. I have 2 gifted children and when I have requested additional work or to meet with the "gifted coordinator" you wait for 6-7 months before it happens. They don't do anything special with the gifted children they simply set them in a corner of the room with more advanced work and don't help them. It's okay for now but what about when they need something?

column3: Sidney High offers many after school programs in sports and music. It annually received more college scholarship funding than any near by school. Those students planning on college are offered many AP classes in Math, English, Physics and Chemistry. My college bound students all received academic honors and scholarship money thanks to the excellent teaching offered at Sidney High. Sidney High School has an amazing staff, great leadership, and outstanding students! I am proud to be a Sidney Yellow Jacket and know I would not have had the life experiences I have had if it weren't for the teachers that guided me along in my grade school years, always pushing me to excel. Sidney schools suck in general. Look at their state rating. Too many delinquents and unmotivated students and teachers.Way too many administrative personnel. I pulled my child and put her into county school. Sidney High School has amazing academic programs - more than 20 dual enrollment courses, 9 advanced placement courses, in addition to a number of college and career preparatory classes. Most impressive, the Academia team is ranked in the top 25 in the nation and top 5 in the state of Ohio! If your child is dedicated to learning, SHS staff will ensure they get the best education possible! I have had a very nice experience at sidney high school. I have always been a proud yellow jacket and a cheerleader. Despite my rating I think it was a pretty good school. Not everyone can say that about sidney though so I had to voice others opinion Great experience. Helped prepare me to go to The Ohio State University from which I recently graduated. Without the preparation from the dedicated teachers, coaches, and mentors, I would not have been ready to face the challenges college would bring. This school is probably one of the worst schools in the Northern Dayton area. For one, a good chunk of teachers are straight out of college and usually leave after 3 years; to get a better job at a better school. This leads to hit and miss teachers, on how effective they are. While I was there, there were literally 5 principles over a term of 4 years. Also, they don’t prep students to get accepted into college as they only have 4 AP classes, as they opted to go mostly with college credit plus classes. Bullying is literally a joke to them until something bad happens. Plus, the community doesn’t support the school district at all, they haven’t voted for a tax increase for over a decade, and the people who can have their kids attend other schools outside the district do instead. The school is essentially a feeder for the local factories, the school even has a program for it and they call it work force.

column1: I came from South Gallia High School and now im in college and i believe i got a better education here than i have at any other school in the state of Ohio that i went to.

column3: The director of special education, Carolyn Patton, created a lot of conflict and did not know how to implement special education services in Mount Diablo School District. She had to leave Vacaville, to go to Mount Diablo, and she only lasted there 2 years. Benicia High School is an average high school. Its not completely run-down like those in inner cities though not as great when compared to other towns. Most students are completely unmotivated towards the virtue of public education and unwilling to act mature for their age. The latter is not helped by the teachers' visible despondence. 'Let kids be kids.' is conventional term greatly endorsed by the school body. Maybe its that 'laid-back' ambiance this small town produces. I am speaking from a student's view when I write this statement; therefore, my words should provide insight yet are subjective. So take these comments with a grain of salt. The students are truly unmotivated to learn. They rather talk about gossip, sports & other topics in television, social media, and drug use which seems predominant in this high school community. All these aspects provide an hindrance towards education. Sadly of all, there is neither academic discipline nor 'segregation'. AP & Honor classes do not help. It is clear that intellectual integrity and distinction are not celebrated here. Only menial athletes are exalted. Benicia High School is a school where the adults are always right and the kids are always wrong. I had a teacher lie directly to my face without flenching. If your child is able to exist there without rocking any boats, then your child will do well there. But if your child asks questions or has an issue even as an "A" student, they will be trampled. As I was told "adults can do what every they want". I like Benicia High School. Yes they are going through changes all schools do. Do I agree with them all, no but I do have the opportunity to help with the change. As a parent of a junior at the school right now, I feel we all need to work as a team for the success our children. Great school, our son came as transfer student starting with Benicia Middle School.... our son also had also been Crohn's Disease and the administration, his teachers and the district were extremely helpful in making his experience a positive one. He also loves the school environment. This school gets high marks from me overall. Both of my two students that have gone here have been happy with the excellent band program. I think that the staff is good, and the students are prepared for collage at a high level. One of the issues has been a change of administration over the past few years, and my hope is that once the school settles on a policy with the administration and district that those policy changes will be complete. There is also a very good community support system here in Benicia. A lot of parents get involved. The teachers can be as diverse as the students and can take different styles like you will see in a collage setting. There has been an effort to make this teaching fair to everyone, and there are many electives to choose from. this school is great and stuff and Every time I think this school can't disappoint me any more it manages to surprise me. Teachers are generally ok but I've definitely had some who shocked me with how disrespectful they would act as well as their willingness to lie. Other school staff seem incredibly incompetent. Students are not treated equally. There's an organizational problem. This school's employees do not have the students' best interests in mind. Attending this school disadvantages students compared to the other schools in the area. With amazing resources to colleges, forums for the students to voice their opinions, multiple tutoring programs, and teachers that truly want to further your knowledge, I can say without a doubt that this is the school I would want to send my kids to when I am older.

column1: I transferred from Vista Del Lago to here, and wow is there a difference! The teachers are great. The only disadvantage of this school is its age. A lot of the door handles broken, but its cool with me. This school has teachers there that are so old they should not be teaching. Teachers refuse to try different ways to teach students. It is either the student gets it and if not lets keep going. The admin will not help students until it is too late to bring up grades even after parents have asked for help. My son was a freshman and I am transfering him to another school. Also the portfolio and senior project is just another area where teachers can degrade students who have trouble with writing. My son's first english teacher put him down enfront of all the students in his class. Wow that helps students learn. I would not choose this school for any child not an AP student. I am a Vally View graduate and now my son is a freshman. I am very excited to have him going to the same school I did. Valley View has always been a tough school on academics and discipline. There are always a few teachers and/ or staff that have lost their enthusiasm for doing their job but as a whole their are so excellent people at Valley View. Most want to see your child succeed. I believe the senior projects and portfolios are preparing students for college. Term papers are ususally a huge portion of their grade and they won't pass the class if not completed or their College Thesis. So hopefully your student rises to the challenge and graduates from Valley and goes on to College. Don't forget parents you are the biggest influence in your childs life and if you think it's too hard so will they! Science department refuses to update their curricullum. The new textbooks sit on the counter and are not used. This makes it impossible to help the student or hire a tutor, since there is no relevent reference material available. Test and intstruction cover a fraction of multiple chapters in order to match past textbooks and old lessons. Students are just confused and frustrated. Hopefully your student will go on to college and realize it was not them, but the poor instruction and assesment. Unfortunatly they will start behind their peers and may not have the grades required to get into a UC. Even worse, they may not believe that they have the ability to go on to a university. i went to valley laste year.this is a good school if your kids are willing to put in work and try hard if not the teachers will just give up on you and keep on moving on with no problem.the portfolio is just another way for the teachers to make sure your doing your work but at the same time if you didnt do that assignment that has to be in your portfolio you would fail english which happend to me.i believe if you cild is an AP student then that school will be a breeze to the.if not you cild will struggle but they might make it at the same time.the teachers are pretty decent they have alot of clubs and they support all of the sports to the fullest and all of the clubs to the fullest. Probably the best you're going to get in Moreno Valley. Great campus. We live just across the street and have had two students so far here with two more to attend here in the future. Valley View High School is a very unique high school. I enjoy attending it as well as others. For its small size, students have great spirit. Our football and basketball games have great support from the students. We also have a variety of clubs to join, which allows the students to interact with each other and make friendships. Academically we are strong in our district. We could be stronger if students work harder. We have great teachers, offer AP courses, and offer tutoring. However, with all the positives there are areas of improvement. Our school is small, so I feel it can expand to give the students more space on campus. The lunch is not the best and can improve if we get better food. I don't eat school lunch. Our technology is up to date, but we don't have any e readers or tablets like other schools do. If we can get them, we can improve our education. Also our football field need renovation as well as our cafeteria. It also won't hurt to fund our sports programs a little more, but we don't have the money. If our school is able to win this $5,000 it will only mean great achievements. It will improve the education of many students and can transform their lives. My child was straight 'A' and a good child. . VVHS is one of MVUSD best school. However, I pulled my child. She is in charter school now, and doing great! The overall experience at this school is okay, but the administration is really killing the spirit and effectiveness at the school. Parents and students feel detached, and teachers are leaving in droves. My experience at this school so far has been pretty bad. It's not the teacher, it's t=what the teachers have been giving. I've had a lot of homework and barely been able to keep up with it all. 0 zero 00 double zero. HORIBLE HORIBLE
