column3: I can't give LHS enough stars. I'm a proud alum and now a staff member as well. The teachers I had were top-notch - even with increasing class sizes, standardized testing, and NCLB, they made an effort to tailor their teaching to meet individual students' needs. I met several teachers who not only pushed me to excel academically, but also encouraged me to develop a strong sense of self. They inspired me to go to college, and made sure that I was prepared to succeed there, too. The music programs have historically been well-respected (I even got to go to London), and drama is a powerhouse that keeps putting on plays that matter (often regarding social issues and historical events). And yes, it's diverse and accepting, on top of all of that. Lincoln High has a strong sense of history and tradition, and with recent remodeling, Lincoln's historic "palace of learning" looks better than ever. As a student, and as a student of Lincoln High's chapter of the International Baccalaureate program, I couldn't be more proud of this school. The teachers here are involved with students, and really want to help us learn. It's a culturally diverse environment, and very convenient for Lincoln's High School Focus programs. The theatre, speech, and debate programs are excellent, and there are AP and IB classes available for students who excel academically. Lincoln High is top-notch. Amazing school. Diverse student body. Prepares students for the real world. AP/Diff programs had excellent teachers who collaborated thoroughly and provided unique and challenging experiences for students. The general experience of walking down halls filled with diversity, hearing 4-5 different languages, and playing sports with different nationalities gave an incredible character building experience. Lincoln High broke me out of the clique mentality that Middle School perpetuated. Great arts programs (theatre, band, etc). Great teachers who are involved and energized. Made life-long friends here. I’ve had my 2 youngest kids at LHS and my older ones went to Southwest and Southeast. I and my children are happy at LHS. They are exposed to all races, and socio economic classes, homeless children, single parents trying to finish high school and kids taking care of their families with their parents. We have a food bank in school and the kids can get help from a myriad of places. I am so proud to say this is where my kids go. We feel it’s the best in Lincoln! I had an amazing experience at this school. They offer a wide variety of class levels including differentiated, AP, and IB. This is the only school in Lincoln that offers the IB program and one of six in the state of Nebraska. The student body of this school is also amazing. It exposes the students to diversity and people from all around the world. 54 total languages were spoken when I attended and it makes the school only more tight knit. As an alum and parent of two LHS Alum I can’t express enough how wonderful this school is. This evaluation does not properly reflect the administration and teachers at this school. It is a very diverse school, that supports MANY learning differences including ELL, AP, IB, and Special needs students. It is a truly amazing school.

column1: First of all I'll be graduating this next school year from this school and honestly it's been one of the smartest things I've done in my life so far. For all those who are talking it up about how it only advertises itself and what not, well of course it is, it's a business? This school offers a lot, I already have a secured job after I graduate at a great workplace all Becaus of the opportunity I have here. The staff is amazing, I know every single one of them if not personally at least I can talk to them about how the days going. The education they offer is great, it's strict yes I know I'm going on my 4th year there but it's for our own good. Honestly there's nothing to bonplain about. I come from public schools and it wasn't anything I couldn't handle. And the fact that it targets Hispanics, why's wrong with that, were getting an opportunity to succeed. All those who complain about the school don't really appreciate what there being offered, I myself realize that by going to San Miguel I'm already more prepared than my friends at public schools! Not to say that at public schools there any less but here they actually push you to become the best you can. This school is worth it. Some believe that the harder a school is, the more successful students will be. This school proves that this is not true. Students are held up to unnecessarily high standards that only waste time and effort. This school relies too much on homework and not enough time is spent in class. Many teachers don't have teaching degrees or have enough experience. Students work to pay for an education they could get at a public school. Public schools might even be better. Students don't get spring or fall break. There is not enough extracurricular activities or AP classes. There are too many useless classes such as 4 years of religion, 3 years of Spanish when you only need 2, MSI, ASL, and much more. Most students just go to Pima or the U of A, which could also be done if a student goes to a public school. Too much time is wasted going to prayer services and mass. Classes don't prepare students for the ACT or SAT. The food is gross. Being a Catholic school , this school can be sexist and homophobic. Many teachers and students end up changing schools and doing better. Teachers are underpaid. This school is just terrible, it is not worth investing time, money, or energy. It'd be better to go to a different school. As a former student, I would not recommend San Miguel to anyone, in fact I talked my parents out of sending my siblings there. I'll start of by praising the work program it's unique, but this is about the only thing separating San Miguel from any other subpar charter school. This school has the potential to be one of the best in the state but they fail to invest in their students. As part of the "inclusive culture" they hire student teachers volunteers to teach classes including math and sciences classes. They are inexperienced and unprepared to lead a class of 20 students and the pupils are the ones that end up suffering. Over the years they have brought more and more of these volunteers, to not pay qualified, experienced instructors. I maintained a 4.0 through my 4 years there but that 4.0 would not match a 4.0 from a public high school or any other private one. This show's in the ACT and SAT, I doubt that any student has scored above an average. In college I staid away from the sciences because I knew that SMHS hadn't prepared me. San Miguel built a good reputation in it's first few years and has been living off that reputation since then, now they seem to be more focused on their profits than the quality of education they provide. San Miguel is an incredible place. Students graduate with 4 years of work experience, a college prep education and have support to and through college. 100% of San Miguel graduates have been accepted into college since the school opened in 2004. I had such a wonderful experience at San Miguel.

column3: I am a current student at Azusa High School and I am very bothered that all people think when they hear about us is our financial problems. We are a very spirited school that is bursting with pride for where we are from. I would not want to go anywhere else. Azusa has an amazingly successful band and pageantry, some highly successful students, and an all around Aztec pride! I know that everyone thinks we are terribly behaved poor kids we are so much more than that. We are a family at Azusa High and that's what makes us so great no matter the circumstances. -Once An Aztec Always An Aztec I am a student at Azusa High School and Azusa is the best out of the 2 high schools I've attended. The students are well behaved and are super polite and friendly, the teachers and administrators are amazing they'll do anything they need to do to help you get to where your goal is. Azusa High is well known for its outstanding and high award winning Performing Arts groups. My oldest received a diploma through a special needs homebound program at Azusa USD. The teacher who worked with my child was from Azusa High. He was exceptional. He understood my child's needs - not just academic but social and emotional. He also was not afraid to hold my child accountable and be challenging. My child graduated with a high GPA and is a college student. I do not believe this would have happened had my child not received so much support from this teacher. Some teachers in other schools didn't want to put in extra effort to work with someone who had special needs. I don't think they believed it mattered or that my child wouldn't notice - well, my child did and it had a heavy impact. This teacher was able to repair a lot of damage in that regard. To me, the teacher's dedication, loyalty, and innovation reflect the values Azusa High no doubt instills in its faculty. I'm proud of my child, but I am also immensely proud of and grateful for my child's teacher, who stepped up and became a role model and superhero when so many others failed at the same post. Love AZUSA high never forgot were I came from were I got my schooling I live in Ontario now but choose to send my kids to AZUSA high everymorning my wife makes the commute to AZUSA to take our kids in our eyes to the greatest high school Aztecs I don't care how much money you got or want to waste by sending your kid to one of those so called top notch high schools go for it ...I send mine to AZUSA and proud of it haven't forgot were I came from what about you!!!.... in my opinion and I can only speak from our experience the counselors need to be involved need to have a better connection especially if your child is a senior

column1: I retired from So Dak and moved to Co. Started driving school bus to Legend 2 years ago. All my contact with the principal, teachers, and security guards have been very positive. They are caring, kind, and professional. I am impressed with the Legend High students. They are great young adults giving me great confidence in the future. This school has earned the highest ratings. Teachers and administrative staff are sensational, knowledgable, and really work with individual students to achieve goals. Classes are fit for students to provide challenging curriculum for all levels. School environment is outstanding, with amazing respect among everyone. The activities, from athletics to the performing arts, are ideal and there is something for every student. Legend is an amazing school. Legend is the best thing that has ever happened to me. The leadership displayed by both the outstanding staff and upperclassmen inspires me everyday to be my best. Legend provides a variety of classes to fit the needs of individual students. I'm challenged to reach my potential in a postive manner. Legend is a wonderful school. I like that we are so united and supportive of one another and that really helps out in all areas. For the most part the teachers are great and helpful but there are a few that are no the best. There are high standards that keep the envoirnment really positive and happy. It is a really great school, I enjoy going to school there and would never want to change schools. This is such a great school! I moved to Legend last year after doing horrible in Kentucky and I noticed a big difference between the two. Legend has a huge caring family environment. The staff is always talking and communicating with students and if they see a student who feels left out, they go and talk to them and then hook them up with a couple of people. The students are so caring and they show a lot of pride. The staff come from all over Eastern Colorado and they can't stop talking about how great this school is. For only being 5 years old to this day, many schools in not only Douglas County, but in Colorado is looking up to us. They want to see what Legend High School is doing. The teachers are one of the best teaching staffs in the State of Colorado. If you are a music lover, this is the high school for you. We have theater, band, orchestra, choir, and unlike other schools, you can also create your own club that you can lead. The opportunities are endless when you walk into the doors of Legend. I've only been there for a year, but I can tell you this: this school will change your life, whether it be a teacher, a staff member, or another student. You will love Legend HS!!!! Don't believe all the great hype of this school! Too many over privileged kids with no adult supervision at home. Anything goes at legend from daily bullying, excessive drug/alcohol abuse, sexting cases, arrests, suicides and last years principal and assistant principals leaving. Teachers have been overheard saying how out of control all these rich kids are! Look elsewhere for an actual good school for the sake of your kids well being. Great leadership paves the way for this school's success! Legend prepares students for careers in so many different fields. They have awesome career readiness programs and the teachers are awesome! My student was in need of extra assistance and support to succeed, and we were greatly disappointed. There was zero follow through on the part of counselors and teachers and despite numerous emails and phone calls to counselors and teachers we got zero help in helping our child to be held accountable at school. One counselor vowed to do man things to help get our child on target, none of those things happened. We are at our wits end begging for help but getting no communication or support from the school. Legend's a great school for kids that are self motivated and do not require any special assistance or support, the celebrate success, if your child is struggling to be successful you can pretty much count on them to be ignored and left behind. Three failing years and only one teacher tried to work with us and remained in communication with us. I know our kid is challenging and we are frustrated and I know that our kid has to be accountable to themselves - but the complete lack of communication just makes it easier for them to think that it's okay to continue failing, because nobody cares and we are just the nagging parents. So disappointing so hopeless. if you have other options go somewhere else. This school is safe and fun to attend. The teachers are respectful to students and actually do their jobs, and students are kind to each other. Horrible glad my child left this school! Administration did nothing to help with bullies and bad teachers. All the good teachers have left and I would never recommend this school to anyone! his school sucks, the admin create an environment where only the athletes strive to be successful. The only teachers that like their job are the coaches(which is where our principal got his start!) and the only students that think this is a good school are the oblivious athletes. All other programs and activities are under funded and most don’t have teachers that stick around long enough to make a successful program when they are all quitting due to admin. Even departments such as English which is a core are suffering because the teachers are fed up with admin! On top of that students like me realize what’s going up and are also fed up! They are purposefully oblivious to bullying, drug abuse, and ect. In fact bullying comes from staff too! Not a good place for a students well-being. They are all cocky rich kids and the school lets them get away with anything. No leadership whatsoever! Both of my boys have gone to Legend High School (graduated 2019 and 2022) and have both loved it. They were only involved in sports for the first couple years and then found their passions in TSA, DECA, and FBLA. It's not true that Legend only cares about athletes as some of these reviews say. They encourage all students to be involved in a club and celebrate all students. My sons felt very well supported despite coming in as freshman from a charter school and literally not knowing a soul. They made friends very quickly and thrived. We open enrolled to this school because of the positive vibe my older son got on his tour and the extensive engineering and computer science class offerings. They never experienced or saw bullying. They never had a desire to be in the popular crowd - if there even is one, I never heard about it. They developed a tight group of like-minded, nice and supportive friends. Maybe they had a better experience because they took more honors and AP courses - I don't know. The staff and admin are very supportive and just fantastic, and Mr. Jacob (principal) really cares about every student. Don't hesitate to send your kids to Legend! There are many opportunities to get involved. The teachers care about their students. We had a concern when we first moved, and the leadership team handled it immediately. It's tough to move during HS, but Legend welcomed us and made it a positive experience. They helped us navigate time missed due to a longer illness and it truly made a difference in recovery. I look forward to my next student coming to Legend and experiencing the whole HS experience in one school with such a great community.

column1: I have two son's who attend this school. The teachers are concerned about the well being of the students; not only academically but in their activities as well. We, our entire family, loves California City High School. I am so proud about my relationship with all my teachers, they are like a bigger family to me. I was unwillingly pulled out of the high school by my parents due to family traveling amount. The teachers argued for my case so that I could stay, but it wasn't enough to convince them. I am very welcome and loved when I come to visit, and help out. I am always asked and told that I need to come back and am misses. Even as one of the higher educated ones at the school, everyone knows me and are all very friendly. It is nice to leave and come back after so long and everyone still knows my name. California City High Scool, being such a small school, does not have the same scholastic opportunities that big city schools have, but they do well with what they do have. My daughter graduated in 2012 with a high GPA and was easily accepted to numerous colleges. The curriculum that was available to her prepared her for University level instruction and she has been well capable of maintaining Honor Student status. Being from one of the first graduating classes the school had, the teachers did well with what they had and surviving with what they didn't have. The staff was great when communicating about my child's accomplishments and her needs. The Athletic department could be better managed but she survived well through the turmoil. A better Athletic program could of aided her in obtaining sport scholarship opportunities which was denied to her due to constant turnover of coaching staff and lack of knowledgeable coaches. Only complaint was in athletics, other than that Bravo CCHS for continuing to improve your academic program.

column3: i currently go to south cobb and i personally like the school. the one thing i dont like are the uniforms, we are in high school and shouldn't be treated like middle schoolers.otherwise this is a great school and the the magnet program is awesome. South Cobb High School has excellent teachers, A very strong principal and challenging academic programs. The Magnet Program is very rigorous and fun. Also the school environment is diverse and the campus is clean and beautiful. South Cobb is rising to the top and doing more for its students than many other schools in Cobb County. As a current student of SCHS and after watching my siblings graduate from the school, I can honestly say that South Cobb High School is a wonderful school. We've had our low moments but we're coming back on top & we will not stop. It is truly a school of excellence where the students are beginning to all become a family. I would not chose any other school to grow with. Eagle Nation. I attended South Cobb High School since 2009, and I must say that South Cobb HS has come a long way. The staff there is incredible, including Mr, Hosey. I am proud to be an Eagle. This is my daughter's second year at SCHS. I have heard many things about SCHS, most of them not true, and I am on an all out journey to change the perception of the school. Mr. Hosey, in his short time as Principal, has done great things. You get out of it what you put in it. Parents must be more involved - Schools like Wheeler, N Cobb, etc has the participation of their parents. Get involved to make a difference for the school, but more important for our children. I am a sophmore at SCHS and it is horrible I'm now in the magnet program and they barley teach us anything I went to pebblebrook and I don't understand why people want to come to this school its ghettoer and worse than pebblebrook. Pebblebrook has mor extracurricular activities and better staff here Im wanting to transfer back to pebblebrook My son has attended SCHS going on 4 years. He has always attended a private school. He went from a school of about 200 students to a school of almost 2000. Once we both started getting involved, we began to see the difference in not only the school, but in his behavior and attitude toward the school. SCHS is definitely moving in the right direction and the principal- Mr Hosey is right on target. He is determined to see that this school is one that stands amongst the greatest of schools. I strongly encourage those who are currently and are thinking about attending SCHS, to get involved and make a difference. The school is only as good as the administrators, parents, and students make it. Although my son will be graduating next year, i still plan to continue my involvement because I see the great things that the administrators want for the school and with the community, parents, and administrators involved, the sky is the limit as to the great school this will be. Although I ranked the teachers and parents at the level that I did, again, the school is definitely moving in the right direction as long as they keep Mr Hosey. Let start being apart of the solution. Lets get involved. I am parent with 6 students that attended south Cobbi now have 4 left. I see a big difference since my first child attended. I'm not from here and I don't see s lot of patent involvement in the schools in this area. I have seen students skipping, cursing disrespect teachers which is unacceptable. I like South Cobb it has potential to striving to bring successful but we as parents and a community need to come together and changing what's going on around us. Let's take our community back let's Build Our Schools, it can be done do let's do it.. My daughter is a Freshman at South Cobb High school. I have been monitoring ALL of the schools in Cobb County for some time now and SCHS is definitely improving. A school's success lies beyond test results and statistics. You must be involved to experience the positive changes and not rely on negative word of mouth or isolated incidents. EVERY school has issues. There are a lot of great/effective programs, students and educators at SCHS. Unfortunately, only certain schools receive accolades or recognition. We need to get the word out about the positive impact SCHS is making. South Cobb has teachers that truly want the students to do their best. Also, South Cobb High School has really great classes and teaching methods I graduated from SCHS in '89 and my children are now attending and I think for the most park the school is doing the best they can with the funds that they have. Kids who want to learn will learn and those who don't want to learn will make it harder for the teacher to do their job. Over populated classrooms, because noone can afford to pay for more teachers in each subject. It would be wonderful if we could get volunteers to assist with tutoring after school programs for children who are struggling in their studies. Facing these challenges I believe SCHS still has great things to offer, with a great group of kids, caring teachers and a good staff. South Cobb High School has the most dedicated teachers and principal. The students are motivated to achieve the highest standards and excel in their community. Go Eagles !!! im not gunna lie, this may be the best student oriented school, 4 out of 5 years i lived in this area have been the best of my life, the longer you stay the better it gets I am a Freshman at South Cobb, for middle school I went to a private school which in comparison was much better. In terms of public school South Cobb has a lot of opportunities such as the Magnet program and AP classes. If you take advantage of different activities at South Cobb you will have a better experience. However unlike the private school I went to they have a percentage of students who act negatively. I have had someone attempt to steal my phone, and seen a fight during class. This percentage can be found at just about any school. If you are friends with people who are not this percentage and you are not this percentage you will be fine. Over all in terms of public school South Cobb is a good school with great teachers, a good principle and some amazing students such as myself. If you are looking for a good Public High School, South Cobb might just be for you! You should try it and see if you'd like to stay After listening to so many so-so answers. Before my child attended SCHS, I found SCHS to be just as Excellent and Superior as all the other High Schools. This comment from a parent that is very particular about where my children education comes from. Also, both kids attended private schools. I think its all about the parent and the child studying, listening, respect, and wanting to be EDUCATED!!!! The mentality of the school has gone down tremendously. The children act and sound as if they live in the 'hood' and seem to impersonate gang-bangers. I have had two children graduate and my third child just finished freshman year there. We are moving to East Cobb. I remained an active parent and that is the ONLY way that I didn't lose my children there. Kudos to the principal and a few other teachers/administrators because they really have their hands full. Principal cares about the kids! He is a great mentor to young men. Parents need to step up to the plate and support their kid/ kids and their community! Greaux Dr. Hosey! this school has done some great things i am very satisfied and happy on how good my daughter has progressed Overall, the kids at South Cobb are great. It's just the few bad ones that give the school a bad reputation. This school is judged by any and every problem that occurs, but never recognized for the many accomplishments by its students and dedicated principal. I am a senior in the Magnet program here and must say that I could never imagine being anywhere else. Out of the multiple schools I've been to, I can honestly say that I've encountered some of the hardest- working, determined students while at South Cobb. I am proud to be a part of this family because as our principal reminds us everyday, "We are NOT what people may say, WE are NOT what people may think, We ARE better than they ever could imagine. Just come on down to South Cobb and see what we're truly capable of. i would rate this school a good school because it has a lot of cute boys !!!!! JK!!!! no but for real they have gangs behind the back of the school hey should get that checked out My experience at this school has been amazing. My mom never thought i would attend this school due to the bad rep people put out about it and now she loves it. Yes we fall short sometimes but what high school doesn't ? The environment is something you would want to be apart of... EAGLE NATION!!! This school is making a really bad 1st impression thus far. I really hope the teachers are better than all the registration staff and front office personnel. They have registration only 3 days a week and even if you make an appointment online, you may very well end up being SOL when you show up. They NEVER.. well, I can’t say never, because out of the 2 weeks I have been calling, leaving voicemails AND sending emails, I finally got through to someone yesterday. And even though they say Registrations are held Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday… sometimes they just decide they won’t have anything on a random Thursday it seems. (Oh, and after next week, no appointments for three weeks…. So, in case you were thinking of having your child enrolled soon because you’re moving or have some other circumstance… you kid(s) is going to be on a 3 week vacation. (The first of those weeks, is fall break though, so only 2 weeks of school work missed that they will need to make up along with what they already will need to get caught up with.) To top it off…Solely based off a conversation I overheard in the registration room... (No Privacy).. the counselors don’t seem to be rooting for the children to stay in school and graduate either. I only wish we had the option...well, schedule to petition to be able to enroll outside of our district. If you can drive and pick your child up from school every day, this is what I suggest you do and NOT enroll them in this school. Again though, I hope I am wrong and we love it here eventually.

column1: When I was in 8th grade and got accepted into Clark I was very excited because they showed us a high tech computer lab with awesome computers but when I got there it wasn't anything like they showed us. It is a technology school but the technology was outdated and they were down or not working 50% of the time. There is only a few good teachers. The rest are very strict. Even though I only 2 bad grades the whole year(a B- and a B) everyday I was pressured by the teachers. I can say that I would have been more healthy, mentally and physically, if I hadn't attended Clark. Every day I woke up I felt like I couldn't take another day of this but at the end of the day I had sports at GHS and that was the only thing I had to look forward to. I have a brother who goes to this school and I graduated from here two years ago and I can tell you that this school is terrible. I hated this school so much that I try to find as many as excuses to not to school that day. Not all the teachers were bad, during my 4 years I had two good teachers and the rest were absolutely terrible. Right now I'm enrolled in USC and Clark did nothing to get me here. I had to go to a community college and work my butt off to get here. If you are a parent and reading this just know that you are better off if you don't send your son/daughter here. Send your children to an actual high school where they can have a real high school experience. I love Clark!!!!! Ignore all these students that say that Clark is a horrible school, it is not... They only say that because they are horrible and dont care where they are going to get in life. The technology is amazing...yes, sometimes the internet might go down but that is for the whole district... If you are thinking to put your child in this high school it is probably because you live in Glendale, or La-Cresenta.... Or the fact that you know that Clark has no drugs, and discipline is a major part of Clark's mission. The dress code is great so what if you cant wear whatever you want to school, besides it will take forever to decide what to wear in the morning. THE TEACHERS ARE ALL GREAT.... THERE IS ONLY ONE HORRIBLE TEACHER AT CLARK AND HE IS LEAVING THIS YEAR SO THE TEACHERS ARE ALL GREAT. People say it lost its magnet but it got back in this year... PLEASE PUT YOUR CHILD IN CLARK ( ) It is a great school!!!!!!!! The teachers do not even teach, the suspension level is high, THE WHOLE SCHOOL IS SEXIST, and a horrible freshmen year Clark is a great high school. Mrs. Armineh Mikaelian is one of the best math teachers I have ever had and I am currently studying at UC Berkeley. Students often complain because they dislike the workload or their "inability to express themselves because of the dress code." The truth is, this school cares about your future and if students really were focused on their academics, then wearing polo shirts would not be as big of a deal as many students make it out to be. The only problems with this school are those that occur with every public school - not enough counselors, etc. You need to be able to find your own way. That being said, Clark has an amazing robotics program as well as very good technology (Apple TVs and flat screen TVs in all classrooms). I do not regret going to this school at all. It prepared me well for the rigor of Berkeley. Exceptional staff and teachers who care about kids and want them to succeed Horrible. This school sets up students to fail in life. They teach students horrible life skills and habits. Personally as someone who has attended clark as well as has had many family members and friends go to clark I must say there is a lot of exaggeration. I won’t lie there is a lot of work that comes with a lot of stress. Realistically freshman year is the hardest so you have to push through. It is a much better environment and people who transferred from ghs have even said they feel “safer” at clark. It pushes you, you have to put effort and be smart. The dress standard is okay, at first it’s a big deal but you get used to it, it’s not as bad as people make it out to be. People who are interested in stem and technology should definitely attend clark because the robotics is great. They have a decent variety of classes enough for people to choose different paths. A huge variety of clubs and they have a bunch of new ones each year. When people say you can’t take any sort of sports that isn’t necessarily true. Although clark does not have their own teams you can try out for the sports at your home school so that is still an option for you. Overall I would say send you kids there if they are hard working and willing to do what it takes. I’m finishing my freshman year here, and I’m gonna be transferring to a different school next year because it’s been too hard for me, and because the school is focused more on robotics and engineering and all that stuff, which isn’t really my cup of tea, but besides that my experience was mostly positive. The dress code can be a hassle only if you didn’t buy enough polos and wash them once a month because you don’t have an in-unit laundry, but if that doesn’t apply to you you’ll get used to it, especially since they still have free dress days, and a lot of the rules are ignored (ex. most girls wear really short skirts/skorts, and sometimes they aren’t even solid color, which is pretty much ignored but the staff). The teachers are mostly very nice and fair, the campus is clean, and at the same time small and cozy (the passing period is enough to get from one end of the school to another, if you know the shortcuts). I’ve mostly had a good and safe experience with the kids there, though classrooms can get really loud sometimes. Lastly, the work load can be a hassle, and you can’t be slacking off there if you wanna stay in the school. Anyone who comes to this school will leave the second they get the chance. There is a reason you sign a contract disallowing you to leave the first year (Note: People left anyway because of this school's mishandling of students.) First off, the amount of homework the teachers in this school give out is absolutely egregious. Seriously vile and disturbing, plum wild! This may seem like something many complain about, but this is not a normal amount of work to give to a developing child, seriously. Before you just disregard this and just chalk it down to students being lazy, that simply isn't true. Even if you were to do the work as early as possible, it leaves no time for you to be with friends, and family, or have any kind of personal time. From my experience, a good amount of the teachers simply don't care or don't have the qualifications to teach at all. As for social & emotional health, the counselors don't care about you or your problems and will most likely just pin problems on you. And, if the "advice" they gave was even remotely helpful then it might've been easier to get past the rudeness. Of course, there are exceptions such as Ms. Cerda who was my 9th-grade counselor. If safety refers to bullying then it is absolutely awful. If by any other metric such as safety from intruders the school has a basic drill that doesn't help with anything. Regarding familial engagement, well, there is none. The only connection a family would have with this school is their child complaining about it.

column3: Livonia is a great school! Although the principal is not very popular among the students, the teachers are fantastic! They truly care about their students, and each teacher is unique and creative. Our sports teams do very well in our area, winning multiple sectional titles. Our music program is the best around, kept alive despite the state budget cuts. There's no where else I'd rather be! This school does not offer enough creative resources to help students that are struggling. Superintendent was asked about results in particular subject that many students seem to struggle in and never got back to parent with information promised. Test results are indicative of students struggles throughout the year. Teachers and administrators seem to have no desire to brainstorm and come up with a plan to help students succeed in a very difficult class. I was a part of the class of 2015 and I have to say, it was a terrible four years at this school. Every single day was stressful and reprieves from a constant and ultimately unchallenging workload were few and far in-between. My main grievances with the school are as follows:- The classes are not tough, in fact even the AP classes were easy and tedious, but the workload is extremely high. I spent an entire day on a single project for one class on multiple occasions.- Kids who know 100% of the material can fail a class and kids who know 0% of the material can pass. - Following in line with the above, homework is daily for most classes and always graded.- Teachers LOVE putting kids in embarrassing situations under the guise of 'ice breakers' and 'getting-to-know-you' activities.- Teachers will grade on arbitrary projects/activities that aren't even related to the subject. A good example of this would be the infamous senior English project, in which students must create a video with music and talk over it explaining something they believe in. Those projects are not graded based on anything learned in the class, and from what I remember the following categories for grading were: * Pictures/slides used in the video * If there was music in the video * If there was a credit slide * If your voice was able to be heard clearly * The actual content itself (only thing relating to the class)This was a final project worth 20% of your actual grade and maybe 15% of the grading was based on actual class material.- My senior English class teacher threatened to fail me (and thus hold me back from graduating as it is a required class to pass) if I had another LEGAL, medical absence.

column3: There is a great lack of motivation in students. The school is a safe environment, but there are a lot of drugs around. The reason a kid may say they don't have a text book and it's all because of the lack of books it's because they were to lazy to sign one out. Now, I do agree that there is a bit of favoritism. There Administration and Counselors seem to care, which is most of the battle. The seasoned teachers are excellent but the amount of young inexperienced teachers is overwhelming. Great CAD and career tech classes as well as college prep courses. If you choose to send your child make sure they end up with Mrs. Dubay, Mrs. Moore, Mrs. Gazda, or Mrs. Iden for something. They are by far the three best educators that a young adult could ever hope to work with. The athletics facility is superb and the security is headed up by Mike Capra, one of the best people you could ever hope to meet. Overall, it's a great place. I'm proud to say this is where i'm from, and no other public school I know would be able to provide the resources to succeed in today's world like Hartland High School. What can I say about Hartland High School? The vast majority of the Teachers are very good, with some being absolutely outstanding. The teachers are always very friendly and truly care about the students, the material, and often have just casual conversations with students before/after class. The administration is also very involved in the school and in making sure they hear what the students have to say. Every other Friday, the Principal hosts "Pies with the principal" and meets with a randomly selected group of students for a pizza lunch, asking them for ideas on how to improve the school. The other administrators are also very involved, and can be seen at lots of after school events. Where Hartland really shines though is in their business/marketing department. They have four, full-time business teachers with real world experience. We have the largest DECA (Marketing Competition) Chapter in the Michigan, with over 400 kids. Last years alone we took over 200 to the State and 60 students to the International Completion. If you are considering sending your student here, make sure they get involved in something! There are tons of clubs are ways to get involved. I love Hartland. The kids have all the tools and help to succeed in everything. They care about the students they teach. I cannot disagree more with any negative reviews of Hartland High School. I was a student in the Hartland district from Kindergarten forward, and can't speak highly enough about the teachers and administrators. They genuinely care about their students and are experts in their subjects. I had teachers who, rather than give me a bad grade on an assignment and move on, would sit down with me during their own free time to discuss any trouble I was having in or out of the classroom. I never fully appreciated what a great high school education I received until I got to college and spoke to students from districts around the country. If there are parents who take issue with facilities or policies, I would suggest directing your comments to the administration, as they are constantly striving to improve. My suggestions to parents or students considering the school: get into a class taught by Paul Scheidler, Kent Wabel or Barb Gazda. Sign up for a marketing class and join DECA. Join a club that interests you--Hartland has such a vast selection, there is something for anyone. I have nothing but positive words to share about our experience in the Hartland schools as a whole. We went to Hartland as children and returned when our own children became of school age so they would have the best education. Reason, respect and responsibility has been part of our lives from the beginning and now that my own children are being taught the same wonderful, guiding principals, it makes us proud to call Hartland our home and school. The counselors are very involved and communicate often with the parents, the vocational tech offerings are excellent at preparing the children to become adults and for the real world!

It has a very high hispanic population which was not a problem but due to the fact I'm very fair and have blonde hair, I stood out like a sore thumb. After only two weeks of being there, people were spreading horrible rumors about me. And I mean HORRIBLE. The teachers I had, except for one, were very rude and inconsiderate. And the counselor I had was even worse. She believed that she knew everything and wouldn't listen to anything I had to say, which ended up really screwing me over. In the end, I only had 4 classes as a freshman and absolutely refused to put me into any other electives so that I wouldn't fall behind in credits (which she could've done without a problem.) All in all, rude students and faculty members destroyed the high hopes that I had for Valencia. Avoid this school at all costs. The staff and students are wonderful, my daughter had a great experience. The diversity of the campus makes this school a real-world experience. I recommend it all the time. In my four years as a parent of a student here, it surprises me that anyone had a bad experience. The staff are extremely devoted-- I have heard of counselors helping their students financially - I recall a fundraiser that helped a family recently (mother had cancer), I think they raised $1300 from just the staff and a few kids. Valencia is an incredibly underrated school. It is recognized nationally as one of the best in the country (Newsweek magazine). Valencia HS provides a lot of diversity, rigorous academics, and helpful teachers. I had a great experience in this school and still am. The sports I hear are great, the involvement is hands on, and the learning is fantastic. The people are really nice here and some teachers really care about the students future. You can get great advice from some of the counselors( AVID COUNSELOR was the best) and helpful tips for your future. The surroundings in the school are great, I really love that trees are around you and the campus is different. It has a little twist to your typical school campuses. The lunch food is not that great and I believe not healthy, but some teachers decide to bring food to school to sell to kids. For example: $1 noodle cup soups, chips, cookies, junk food, soda, and water. There are vending machines that sell junk food, Snapple, Gatorade, water, ice cream, and soda. Also the band room has an afterschool snack place that sells a ton of food, junk food, ice cream, beverages, and a lot more ALL FOR $1. It is the average teenagers dream, although I don't know if they will have the band afterschool snack bar this upcoming year 2014-2015. Pack own food to stay healthy. On my fourth year at VHS, I can say with certainty that this school is AMAZING Nowhere else will you find such great opportunities for your student, as well as true diversity and great academics. This school prepared me for a bright future. Thank you VHS :) Go tigers! There aren't too many high schools where you can experience a diverse student body combined with a strong academic program that allows access to ALL students. Amazing teachers, quality athletics, amazing clubs, and a strong instrumental music program. The drama program and school newspaper are the only things that suck. Overall good and sometimes bad for average and above-average students. But I am assuming it can get worse somewhere else.

column1: Tesoro High School at times can be overwhelming. If you are an AP student such as myself Tesoro will cater to your needs. The History department is by far the best in the school. Everyone tells you from day one to get involved at Tesoro, this is probably the best advice i ever received. However, if you are not a good math student good luck, because Tesoro's math department is really slacking. The department wide policy is 85% of your grade is weighted towards test taking making it very hard for those who struggle in math and on tests to get a good grade in the class. While I personally have had a great experience despite the overwhelming work load at times, i can see that non-AP students get neglected by not only the guidance counselors but the teacher's as well. This year I'll be a senior and while for the most part I've had a good experience I really can't wait to leave and explore something other then the bubble that Tesoro is in. P.S. have fun walking in the hallways during passing periods you won't be able to move. Overcrowding is a problem. Oh also, in addition to my previous comment below this comment.... For those who assume that the staff doesn't care, I would have to say they are wrong. They reach out to all students who are in need of help. They do help, as long as you respond to their help. Also, if you ask for help, they help! Tesoro High School is laughable. I am a sophomore excelling at an ivy league school no thanks to Tesoro though. Sure, some of the teachers are great but it's a gamble. Students that are not on the AP tract are neglected. The principles and vice principles are corrupt at best. Not to mention the athletics program is run completely by politics and largely is based off of parent reputation. In addition to all of this, students that do excel are only acknowledged if they are part of ASB, yet another laughable program. All in all this school does not deserve any of the quality reviews it is given. Clearly they are by naive parents who do not actually have to attend Tesoro. I am giving 4 stars to the teachers at Tesoro and some of the office staff but I marked some points off for the way the clubs/organizations and the athletic program are run on campus. I am satisfied with approximately 90% of the teachers my child has had at Tesoro and am particularly impressed with the math and science departments. However, I agree with the comment the reviewer made on May 7, 2014, that students are only recognized or given perks such being granted membership of the National Honor Society only if they are part of ASB. In addition, there is definitely some politicking when it comes to the athletics program. I was study in this school, and his school is fun Not the best. Not the worst. Really depends on the teachers you get. The staff is supportive and caring. Although at times Teachers are very demanding, the classes prepare them for College. Nice campus, respectful kids and approachable staff. PTSA is hardworking. Tesoro is a great and excellent public high school, despite some of it's rowdy, rude, conservative students, the teachers are excellent and I am glad I attended Tesoro! Go Titans! Both my kids have hated their high school experience at THS as well as 3 other kids from my extended family that have had a bad experience over the last 10 years. Send your kids elsewhere!! My kid has has a wonderful experience academically and athletically. Coaches appear to be fair and teachers do their best to communicate within 24 hours when I have a question. Both of my children have gone to this school . We started in the private catholic school education for elementary to middle school. I was apprehensive to go the public school route. But It proved to be the best thing we did for our children. My son is going to a 4 year college upon graduation. The academics are challenging for those who want to be challenged and they have modifications for children who need more help. I am a parent of two children who fit both of those. Academics and athletics come easy for one, and the other one struggles with academics. Both have had amazing experiences and the activities and opportunities for parents to be involved in makes it feel like a very small school. We have made friendships for life through Tesoro and the parents of students. Great high school great Academics, great AP courses and great athletic programs for all appetites football tennis baseball basketball. I know of numerous families that transferred from jaw dropping expensive local private schools to give their teenagers a better education at this school instead! Principle is caring and attentive… so are the teachers.

column3: Many of the teachers at Valley West don't seem to care if a student passes or fails. Tenure has taken away any incentive to become a good teacher. Wyoming Valley West is a great school. It's facility and staff truly care about the children's education and go out of their way to make the learning experience a positive and educational one. its okay i guess. i like it there I would say most of the teachers I met in this school are really nice.... but overall it’s not a wise choice to put your children in this school if you really care about your children’s education and want them to get into a decent college....cuz they don’t help at all.... Overall i’d say it’s an okay school, I found it easy to make friends because there’s a lot of students but it really depends on your own experience. The lunches are always bad and they only offer milk and food that contains dairy anything else you have to pay for, when most of us can’t afford that. The principal is really nice there’s thousands of us but he knows us by name he doesn’t yell at students in trouble instead he talks to out with us and helps us become better people and better spartans , i would say a lot of students don’t seem to care about their work in class and just sit on their phones and do nothing in certain classes but some teachers don’t allow that. if you want your kids to succeed here you have to communicate with their teachers email them and make sure your kids doing their homework. overall i’d say you can get away with not doing homework by just sitting there they don’t actively check. there are a lot of violent fights outside and inside of the school of course they break it up but the kids only get suspended for like 1-3 days and the same kids do it again. The punishment is”in school suspension” where you just kind of sit on your phone in a room which isn’t much of a punishment. They give chrome books and you can use them for work and if it breaks they do fix it for you. There’s sometimes school events but mostly can’t be afforded so we don’t have them. I’d say the most of the bullying is not in school but at football games it seems there is always trouble there and violent fights. Almost every single one of the kids smokes in the bathrooms or is chronically absent, most of the classes are always emptyand some kids just don’t come to school for months or weeks at a time

column1: Mitty's priorities are clear: Fundraising, and sports. We have two children that are in great colleges that went through public school, but we thought our third child could benefit from Mitty's so-called great teachers and smaller classes. Big mistake. Teachers are average and administration is unhelpful. Don't believe the brochure or open-house sales pitch. If your child has difficulty in a class, or needs accomodations of any kind, Mitty wants you out of there. Even with a 504 plan, Mitty will kick your child to the curb faster than you can say "holier than thou". It is all about their image, really no interest in helping kids. Not only a waste of money, it is damaging to kids. STAY AWAY! My expectations for choosing to commit $15k/yr + for my child's education at Mitty versus a public school were: Superior Academics, Deepening Religious Faith, and Acceptance to a Top University - via College Planning. The results were sub-par at best for the following reasons: 1. Academics was mediocre - many teachers were unavailable outside the classroom due to sports//coaching commitments. Good students had a difficult time excelling in the classrooms given lack of interest on the part of the teachers. My child had a 4.2 GPA and found most teachers disinterested and unresponsive for help. 2. Religious Education was watered down due to appeasing liberal, political correctness interests. In fact, it has damaged my child's desire to continue attending mass with us. 3. College (lack of) Planning Go online, use Naviance and find the colleges of choice. Where's the counselor's independent, honest assessment of where your child is best suited? My child wanted to go to an East Coast school, and even with high scores, the highest level achieved was being accepted into a UC school. AMHS just doesn't' have the gravitas or pull with college admissions directors. Avoid!!! Mitty is a joke. Presents itself as a college prep school, but its a joke. Unless your child is a sport superstar or would make it academically without teacher support your child will be just another number. Most students go to California State University (CSU) or University of California schools (UC). Entrance requirements are GPA's and SAT's. So why spend $15K for something you get at a public school? Teachers are iffy and many are coaches (ie. sports influence). I felt for many kids and their parents in Mitty. Many of freshmen struggled or dropped from honor / advanced classes all around my child. Many of them were depressed and acted out often. Of course, it puts parents in hell. I am very sure that teachers and school knew about that. Here is my assessment why many children are not doing well in Mitty: 1. overall, less instruction hours compare to public high schools 2. many of teachers are sports coaches 3. distraction from i-Pad, which school forced to children to use as a textbook. However, we (parents) all know, except the school administrators, how harmful i-Pad to our children. I strongly suggest you that do research before you choose Mitty to avoid hardship as many Mitty families went through. Hyper focuses on athletics and absolutely a school for extroverts. If you want your child to try something new, it's impossible because at Mitty you are expected to be great. That's the saddest thing. Academics seem good, and I think the pace will prepare them for college, BUT the off periods I think are too frequent and perhaps not appropriate for 14-16 year olds. 2 stars because of the price. I am a Junior at Archbishop Mitty so my opinion is a little biased, however, I have to say that going to Mitty has been one of my best decisions. I love my classes, my teachers, and my fellow classmates. Everyone is extremely respectful, my freshman year, a senior GAVE me lunch money when I was short a dollar for lunch. Our athletics program is simply amazing and in addition our school spirit is simply unmatched. We have tremendous turnouts to all of our events and even during spirit week. I read a review that said that our new Ipad program is harmful, however, being one of the last classes that remembers what it was like before Ipads, I can say that the Ipad program had definitely improved our academic program. We don't have to lug books from class to class and we have an unmatched note taking/homework doing device anywhere we go. We are definitely not "forced" to use the ipads as books, everyone is aware that if you prefer, you may order your own hard copy book and bring it to class. Overall, I love Mitty. I would not be the same focused, driven, and confident person I am today with out Mitty. Mitty's sports program has an exceptional reputation, however their programs are not any better or different than what one would find at a top tier public school or an average private school. The theater program is a bit above average, but if you're looking for a theater magnet school, Lincoln High School is a better option. Grades are grossly inflated to offset low test scores. The curriculum is far inferior to other high schools in the area, as most money and emphasis is allocated for the sports and theater programs. Most students end up at CSUs despite high GPAs due to poor test scores. If you want your child to go to a top university and do well, I would not recommend sending your child here. My son is a student at Mitty. He is not a sport kid and still loves the school. Mitty is so much more than its excellent athletics. It has amazing academics and an award winning theater program. The music department has incredible dedicated teachers with opportunities to perform and compete. My son is planning on applying to top tier and ivy league schools and scored amazing on SATs because of his teachers commitment to excellence. He has received so much from this school. They have helped him develop as a person with retreats and community service. Archbishop Mitty is an amazing experience for any kid. As a parent of the student, I'll hit the key points. 1. Administration can be inflexible. Especially to high achieving students (in terms of allowing external courses or attending events not sponsored by the school). They like students sticking to Mitty offering and not branch out. 2. Teaching quality can vary greatly from great to downright poor. Variation between the teaching quality and grading standards from one class (and hence, a teacher) to the next (all at the same level of course, APs or honors) can be shockingly high; Students frequently discuss how it's unquestionably harder to score higher grades with some teachers than others. 3. A positive surprise (in today's world). The values of the student pool is very good (generally speaking). And this is not a trivial one. 4. Too many free slots and little guidence from school on effective usage. 5. If your child's focus is academics, there are likely better private schools out there. If you're into sports, go for it! 6. Library is a joke. 7. Counselors have little time to spare (I thought this was a private school) In summary, you won't regret it. But will certainly question if 16k+ a year could have been better spent. Like many Catholic learning institutions, Mitty has fallen prey to apathy and a lackluster effort to develop faith formation programs and growth opportunities for the students. With one notable exception, the religion faculty is less than inspiring. The campus ministry program holds little priority on a campus where sports teams and athletic competition drive the culture of student life. Many of the enrichment opportunities at the school are available by lottery only, thereby offering some students multiple opportunities and other students none. The administration is too worried about stepping on toes to step up and address some of these participation limitations for students. I won't send another child to this school. I'm so happy with Mitty that it provides almost all necessary that my son needs. Academically, it has excellent teachers from English literature to social studies, with regular class or honor class, so both normal students and talented students are happy. Starting from 10th grade, it provides many AP classes with great teachers and enough spaces. Some AP courses and honor classes are very challenging, so students need to be prepared. Fortunately, their counselors are always available in time for recommendations. Mitty also provides a lot of great clubs. My son is very happy to be in two clubs. At Mitty, students are encouraged to manage their time wisely and recommended sleeping early to reduce pressure. Mitty students are very excited about their sports teams. Every day, I saw my child is so happy with great progress from academic, to social communication, to sports, to spirits, I told myself that my son and I made a right decision to choose this school, to have my son continue delivering excellences. I cannot say enough good things about Archbishop Mitty. Mitty allows for kids to be well rounded (which most colleges are looking for). They have phenomenal leadership opportunities, theater program, mock trial team, sports programs, and just about every club you can imagine. The teachers are wonderful and the kids are well prepared for college. While academics are important, Mitty goes above and beyond to make sure that there is more to your kids high school experience. The social and business skills that are taught at this school are assets and will be used for the rest of a graduates life. I highly recommend Archbishop Mitty! As a former student at Mitty High School, I was deeply disappointed with my experience. If I had to do it over again, I would have chosen another school. Furthermore, for the price I would never send my child there. The administration is solely focused on athletics and those athletes that can bring them titles. If you are not a stellar athlete, it is difficult to find your niche. Mitty does not foster an environment where students explore extracurricular activities such as dance, theater or student government. Students are expected to be GREAT by the time they enter the school freshman year or expect to get lost in the shuffle. There is little room for growth of ones talents or to even find what a student may be good at. I was deeply disappointed in my experience. Fortunately for me I was able to find my niche in college, student government, which has led to a very rewarding career in politics twelve years later. There is also much focus on money and whose rich parents donate to the school to get their name on a building. As a Catholic institution, I expected more emphasis on faith based initiatives. I did have some rewarding experiences and met some amazing people; however, if I could do it again - Presentation High School would've been my choice. Unfortunately the quality of teachers for most subjects is very poor. The counselors are just not helpful and I see that public school counselors are doing much better handling many more kids. Though the school claims to prepare students for college, i do not see any indication so far! I'm very disappointed and strongly encourage parents to stay away from this school. It is a complete waste of money. Archbishop Mitty High School has something for everyone in all subjects, whether it be sports, academics, or the arts, and the school just really allows for growth together as a community and as individuals. If your child is not into sports or religion this is not a good place to be. Most teachers are of low quality. If you bring this to the attention of administration, you become the bad guy. I've sent two children to this school, and I can't say enough wonderful things about it. There are so many opportunities for students to get involved, but it is up to the students to look for them; they can't be passive. With the appropriate documentation given to them, the school was helpful to my child with a learning difference, and she felt the workload prepared her for college. My second child is stronger academically, and there were enough challenging classes available to her. The school fosters a very safe, positive, and supportive environment. The tuition is very expensive, but if a family could make it work, the investment is worth it. Shadowing there was such an amazing experience. The teachers are very helpful and are very kind to the shadows. In terms of daily life, the students have a lot of time to catch up on work during the day, given that they have a considerable amount of homework. Also, I attended the Christmas rally. I got a sense of community, of family. The school gave gifts to deserving students during the rally and throughout the day. For example, a student and her sister used to play the ukulele with each other, but since the sister went off to college, the sister took the ukulele. The school and her friends chipped in to give her a ukulele so she will be reminded of her sister whenever she plays it. Overall, this is a great choice for incoming high schoolers. Sadly, I think this once-decent school has lost its way. Academics at the school are solid but the administration is mediocre. The Dean is like a failed police officer. Running the school like a prison is not a good representation of learning. There is a police presence at every event. Bringing drug dogs on campus and monitoring kids going to the bathroom is a sad way to run a school. Learning in a environment where fear is the culture is not a good way to teach and mentor. Sadly this school has lost it's way. If your child is the mature, well-rounded type, Mitty is probably going to be a really good school. Our Athletics programs are run pretty professionally, the Student Activities/Government is very passionate, performing arts are pretty strong and our teachers for math and science are pretty good for the honors/APs and at least acceptable for non-honors and religion. People here are outgoing and kind.With that being said the school is far from perfect. Almost everybody screws around on their iPads. People regularly go on their iPad to get homework done, watch youtube, and/or surf around on the internet in and out of class. I can't say that this is very conducive to a productive learning environment, or teaches kids to manage their time. I wasn't a very mature person in Freshman year, so I got a little addicted to youtube as a coping mechanism for high school stress and loneliness. iPad's weren't good for me, and if your child likes Video Games/Social Media it won't be good for him/her either. However, this system made transitioning to online education during the pandemic very easy, since it meant that most teachers/students were already very comfortable with doing their work online. If you do intend on doing well on STEM competitions like the AMC or F=MA Mitty is not the best place to do it. The Math club and Physics Club are not good places to either gain skills or find community. The Coding Club does have a fairly engaging environment but it is run pretty unprofessionally. If your child wants to do well in these competitions and/or find other like minded competition kids he'll have to go to a program outside of school.The three big clubs Mitty is known for are MAP (Mitty advocacy project), Speech and Debate, and Robotics. I didn't participate in any of these clubs, so I can't say much. What I can say for certain is this:- If your child is already very interested and passionate about advocacy, he/she will probably get a good position in MAP and do good work. If not, he probably won't do anything. -Speech and Debate generally seems pretty good. There were some people who just screwed around, but those who put in the work seem to learn a lot and probably got good training from the coaches. -If you get a good position in Robotics, you'll be able to learn and apply your skills at a high level, and gain a lot of leadership skills. If not, you won't do much. However it's the best and maybe the only way to properly connect with STEM kids in the school.

Latin club was rated best program in state. CHS offers French, German, Spanish, and Latin languages. Plenty of clubs, plenty of class choices and electives. Debate team always does well!The administration works miracles! Whatever classes you need, they will get you in them. I moved here from a different state and was missing a lot of required classes. I graduated alongside everyone else on time! The teachers are wonderful. He informed me I had no freedom of speech there and I was simply to blindly follow whatever I was told while I was attending there. I was then suspended for a week (first time ever getting in trouble and I had a 4.8 GPA, not a bad student) and then kicked me out of two of my classes that the suspension had made me go over allowed absences (this was just a show of power, they don't usually kick you out of classes for going over allowed absences) which dropped me down to a 4.2 GPA which I wasn't happy about. The staff there have zero respect for the students, there is a huge divide between the two and if you express your opinion and it's different from theirs they will come down on you as hard as possible in the hopes of getting you kicked out. I will never have my sons attend here.

column1: Woden is a very, very locally overrated district. There are some good teachers, but that's about it. There is poor balance between sports and other niches, the principal is a bit of a tyrant, and the school is chock full of typical small town ignorance. Politics and nepotism dominate the administration and there is a large amount of unhappiness amongst the teachers for unnecessary changes and amongst the students for the near-fascist state of control they are under. There is not much encouragement of critical thought and there is a lack of addressing many of the negative cultural elements common of the area (bullying, anti-intellectualism, machismo, etc). I would not recommend it. In the east Texas area Woden is often left out of the top schools category, while schools like Central Heights are included in it. When in actuality Woden almost always receives better test scores, and more awards than any other school on Nacogdoches county. I feel like if a student has a desire to learn they definitely will if they go to Woden. I believe that the teachers really care about the students, and want them to learn. Woden also has an excellent basketball & Cross Country program with coaches that know what they are doing. Horrible. The principal is an egomaniac with very little control over his staff. I have heard a teacher bragging about how they "look out for each other" if a parent voices concerns about the staff. Uncertified Special needs Teachers. My family member was treated cruel and I was cussed at by faculty.

column1: To be honest this school needs a lot more. clubs and organizational skills. There has been been many issues with my daughter's graduation. I'm quite disappointed with this school, I had always heard great things about this school but now I think otherwise. I feel like its gone downhill after Mrs. Miller left. There are issues with cords, lack of organization in graduation my daughter and her friends are not excited about it which saddens me because they should be excited about this time in their life. There is a lack of communication between the administration and staff, all I have heard throughout my daughter's senior year is that. The administration makes these new rules and neither the students nor the parents have any idea of what is going on! Sometimes even the teachers don't know. All I know is that I regret, sending my daughter to White Plains High School.

column3: As a parent not a former student I think Cyprus is a great school. I have a daughter who is struggling and they are bending over backwards to keep her in line for graduation. Most schools would have probably kicked her out by now (she's a Junior) due to poor grades and overall lack of interest. However, they really need air conditioning. I don't know how the kids can stand it. Cyprus High School at first glace is a little rough around the edges: but the compassion of teachers, community support, and pride in the students' hearts during games or on just a regular day is incredible. This school is wonderful and I recommend it for students desiring to attend. I am the mother of 2 Cyprus Pirates, 12th and 9th. I have found this school to have some great teachers. The staff from the new principal, counseling, front office and other support are happy to be working with the kids. Some of the kids think the grass would be greener at an other school, but generally there is a good school sprit here. Father & Mother of 2 great kids. I would rate it A+ + + + + or * * * * * :)

column1: Twiggs County High School is the worst school system that I have ever experienced. Compared to my experiences in college, the school failed to offer any sort of academic challenges. During my first semester of college, I struggled every week to get the same grades that I was getting in high school. Most of my peers had GPA's well over 4.0 out of high school because of the AP classes that their school offered. Twiggs county offered only a couple of those classes. I was able to earn a 3.3 GPA during my first semester at the University of Georgia, but it was one of the hardest times of my life. I finally was able to teach myself how to study based on mentors and fellow students who decided to help me. My friends had easier times. Of course, a good portion of students came from private schools. Did Twiggs County help me get to where I am? Yes, only because it was a high school. I am where I am today because of my motivation and my family. Please, get your kids out! If this angers or disappoints anyone associated with the school, I am sorry, but you need to accept the truth that Twiggs County belongs where it has been for years...dead last. Twiggs County High School has several problems: 1. Out-of-control student behavior 2. Total lack of parental interest 3. Very low test scores, but a strictly enforced dress code (for show, I guess) 4. Religious references in staff meetings as well as between teachers during school hours, as well as discrimination against those who speak out against it...very backward-thinking 5. Obvious racial discrimination toward those not African American (also ties into the religious issue) 6. Teachers/Administration not of high quality...I imagine the good ones leave very quickly.
