column1: Excellent teachers and the Principal is outstanding! The JROTC leaders are a credit to their school and the program! Went there, and LOVED it! GO pounders! YES, there were "bad eggs" in the school but they were disciplined and the teachers are very dedicated I feel this school needs to be more positive and supportive of students needs. They have no positive incentives, nothing for students to be excited about or look forward to. Maybe a jeans day on Fridays for good behavior, attendance etc. would help, anything positive would help! Some teachers are very unprofessional and portray the atmosphere of a high drama reality show. Inappropriate/negative remarks/comments made to students.I have seen some teachers who rise above the drama and give all they have to help a child succeed, they have to be mentioned here because they are the unspoken heroes. It is even more important in this type of environment. Overall this school needs some work on Positivity, Professionalism, Ethics, and Student Support (for all students, not just a selected few). Some teachers also need to be held accountable for their negative actions and uncaring attitudes. If they do not want to help students then why are they teaching. Is it only for a paycheck? Who is paying attention, anyone? This is such a negative school. My daughter struggles in school and the teachers don't notice or care. I know they have too many students but a bit of support would go a long way. Because my daughter struggles teachers say mean & negative things to her. She is harassed by many of her teachers who call her out and try to embarrass her in front of a whole classroom. Is this a teaching strategy or what? Her math teacher fails 97% of her class and nobody ever notices or does anything about it. Why? This teacher brags about her tenure to the students and tells them to go ahead and tell their parents because she has tenure and she isn't worried about it. When people come in to observe the classroom she "pretends" to be an involved teacher but stops as soon as the observer leaves. The students do notice these things so why doesn't anyone else? Some Personnel will work harder at trying to get out of doing something than in to trying to help. I will begin looking into other school options for my daughter very soon. This is the worst school I've ever seen. If I need to move to be in another zone that's what I will do. Central High School has improved a lot! School is what you make it while you are there. I'm involved in a lot of school activities, and the teachers have always been supportive of me. Our family chose Central over Ooltewah and have been more than pleased with the decision! The principal is outstanding. My child is having a wonderful high school experience at Central. No drama... just a good education and fun playing sports. What high school should be. I really can't believe a school could actually be this bad, they don't care, the teachers told me that I was faking my desease even though i had multiple doctors tell them what was wrong, then they acused me of lying about trying to get work so that i wouldnt fall behind. i really wish i could say something good about this school but the only thing i can say is "well the football team is good" I entered Central with mixed feelings, having heard not the best things about the school, and most of my friends were attending Ooltewah instead. However, looking back, I have no regrets. I absolutely loved my experience at Central. It is its own community, but you definitely get back what you put in. Take the time to learn about the school, its history, alumni, and the amount of people that truly love it. Love Purple, Live Gold.

column3: I once took pride in being associated w/ LHS. For years the school has had a bad stigma. I can tell you first hand LHS doesn't have any more fights, etc.. than any of the other HS's in Charles County. It's a normal HS. The teachers go over & above to make sure students receive a quality education. Sadly, however; the past 2 yrs were a major disappointment due to the change in leadership. That is the worst thing that could have ever happened to LHS. The fact that a local person was hired who is obviously GOOD friends w/a certain group and blatantly biased towards another. A couple of the "senior" Admin clearly need to retire. At this point they're simply taking up space. No help. LHS needs leadership who treats EVERYONE EQUALLY. Prime example is the fact that they hired a Varsity BBall coaching staff who are coincidentally GREAT friends with "leadership". WoW! It was devastating and unfair how they allowed excellent student players to be treated horribly but allowed students that could barely pass a class to play even after being arrested! The entire admin turned an eye on the situation. Tell me, what does that tell the good student? Bad kids get ahead? Shame on you all! Tragic! I wouldn't go anywhere else, the people who think lackey is a bad school are small minded on the opportunities presented to them. We have great teachers committed to teaching. My A.P. chemistry teacher was willing to not only stay after for 3 hours to help us study but drop a student off to their job afterwards. I've had teachers meet with the class on Saturdays, giving their own time and money to teaching. Our teachers are not just dedicated to the students but also to Lackey. There are many who will proudly say "I bleed blue and grey.". The administration is a joy. They recognize the good students and help them succeed while also pushing the students who need a little bit more guidance. Mr. Short, the principal, has bought the school to new heights, Like every school their are fights but don't let a few bad apples ruin the bunch. When you hear about 5 fights at Lackey in one day it's the same group of people who just can't seem to stay away from each other. We have strong clubs, developing powerful leaders. Culinary Club, Key Club, Invisible children, Modeling, Creative writing and one of the best Drama Clubs in C.C. Lackey's ROTC ranks #1 in the region, providing disapline. i lov ethis school if lackeys a bad school then so is every other school no school or teachers are perfect i n everything A dysfunctional school in a failing school district. For a more thorough review, see my at at gcrhoads.byethost4.com/lackey.html Bulling and fighting continues in the school if the child reports this nothing is done but if the bullying child defends himself even after the report they are suspended. The principle lacks leadership skills and common knowledge in basic conflict resolution. The teachers are more concerned with either becoming a child's friend or collecting a check. The few good teacher are not recognized because of the unruly classrooms. Ok so this school has the worst reputation in Charles county but none of it is true! Henry E Lackey is a very good school, and I am glad I attend it! This school is completely different from how it used to be, and I am proud to call myself a Charger! The principal dose keep the school running pretty smooth, like most schools there are several hiccups along the way. Yes we do have fights and we do have those bad kids here and there, but honestly who dose not. We, in my opinion, have very amazing teachers there have only been a few that have not been that good in my years at LHS. Lackey also has a lot of good clubs and organizations, I am a part of the Student Government Association, the theater/Drama department, I am in orchestra, choir, and part of the Bible club ! I love being at LHS, I would not want to go to any other school! Lackey may possibly be the most under radar school there is. Lackey has a reputation of being the "bad" high school of Charles county and for a time yes. Lackey however is now one of the best school's in not only the county but the state. I am a part of the very prestigious engineering program, which is no doubt the best public program in the state from our Mesa State championship and the senior course like no other offered in the state. No one else in the county has a better engineering program than Lackey, not even one close our program. So the whole reputation of Lackey being this horrible school is just a reflection of the past, not the present. Academically our school is average, there could be room for improvement with our test scores and performance, but this however falls back on the student body since Lackey has probably the most committed to success staff in the world, not one of them wouldn't go an extra mile to advance the knowledge of one. So a greater development of work ethic would be beneficial. Also our school has recently excelled in many areas from a 9-3 football team to our choir group winning a national competition. Lackey is definitely the place to be. My school is lackey highschool nothing has change if you read the self alleged good things that these lies that the reviewer and also teachers tell you about the school is false. What is really their is what the bad reviews said but worse their is students smoking in the bathrooms also teacher that don't give two cares if you pass or fail and as well their are people that will racial discriminate you if you don't act a certain way. i believe that not every teacher is bad but the majority. The intelligence in this school is sub par but their are times when you will question if they even been to middle school. I feel that the disrespect worsen along the school year and the generation after us isnt making it any better. If you can take my advice go to clubs and keep a low profile so you wont get notice by any one. After all this is H.E.L I use to attend this school. I was lucky to endure only two years. I was bothered by many of the annoying students who attended there. Teachers did not stand up for me. The students who would bother others for no reason usually got away with it. My guidance counselor favored those students/ She was no help at all. The principal could be better. I had an issue and he was no help at all. What a joke. The parents of some students are similar to their children and argue with he teacher even though their child is at fault. some teachers favored students too much. Especially male to female students. Letting some students skip another class or no reason. Some teachers were bullied by their students, calling the teacher stupid and how they knew nothing. some teachers are good and deserve to be treated better. I had a bad experience and know not everyone did. If you have the right teachers and are given resources to better your education; lucky you. I felt alone and had no one to talk to or direct me in any path. too much favoritism, bullying, and nonsense. Graduation was the best day. I'm putting this school in my book in a more detailed way. I hope is has changed or will change. This is my son's freshman year at Lackey. He is a student athlete and I feel that the support he has received this year is phenomenal. He made the honor roll for the first time in 2nd semester. I'm excited to see what the next 3 years will be like. I also like the fact that the coaches aren't just coaches they teach core subjects at the school and they offer study hall and are willing to assist my son. This school is like any other school, the more involved you are as a parent with your child's education the better the experience you will have. This is our second year at the school and have had no problems, if anything it is better than most of the "better schools" in the county. Best kept secret in Charles County. We transferred from La Plata High when me moved and heard terrible things about Lackey. Our experiences were the exact opposite! The teachers and staff are excellent, and the students are the same! My daughter loves that she can use the pool during lunch, or sit outside in the courtyard. She is a straight A student and looking at ivy-league schools. No complaints from us! Lackey had one of the worst reputations in the county and it always baffled me. The teaching staff are among the best I could've had (the ones who're still there, you know who you are!!! <3). If you're in the Pathways to Engineering Program (not listed in the STEM section on this site), you're in for a true learning experience because the teachers in that program were top notch. When I was there, we learned how to use CAD software, design circuits, etc. Stuff that I keep with me nearly a decade later. The after school options were ample. The AP offerings could be more, but hey - it's an underfunded high school. They do the best they can. The hour lunch program, if it's still there, provides a fantastic way to recharge. Students can eat, do their homework, take much-needed naps, exercise, read in the library, hang out with friends. Some even bond with teachers or work on extra projects. If your kid is the kind that buckles down and does the hard work, they will succeed here. If your kid is a slacker, you need to teach them the value of hard work so that they can get the most out of high school. Help them get solid study habits that they'll carry with them to college. Teach them that learning is a process and failure doesn't mean you're stupid; you just need to figure out where you went wrong and try again. Personal opinion, but if you're relying on the school for "college preparation" your kid won't do well in high school or at the university level - college is all about teaching yourself how to learn with the materials available to you. Lackey's offerings are ample and their teacher support for those with drive is great - exactly like in a university. Your kid's success just depends on whether they take advantage of it. All of that said - are there kids that smoke in the bathrooms? Yes. Teachers usually do care, but they're limited in what they can do. It's not like they can break the door down to catch the kid. Are there bad apples and sometimes fights? Absolutely. Do kids manage to sneak off to do things they shouldn't? Probably. But you have that literally everywhere. Better kids make mistakes in an environment with some supervision than them making mistakes without it. This school is great! Engaging teachers, coaches, and administrators. Lots of opportunities for kids in the area. Great for our son high school experience we moved from Montgomery county but the school system in charles county is truly so helpful to our kids

column1: Most of the classes just sit there and play on their cell phones. Some of the teachers set out to insult and embarrass the students then play it off like it was a friendly joke!!! I am left to make sure my kids are ready for college because these teachers do not care!!!

column3: We have two daughters within the greenfield school system and I must say I am very disappointed! The academics are on average but if you challenge the teachers about what they are teaching and/or how, you will get the cold shoulder. The real problem I have with the Greenfield School System is the blatant favoritism that infects the school system. The administration openly allows some students to do as they please with little to no consequences. Unfortunately, the children that are not on the "list" have a really hard time with the school environment. One of my daughters who is more outgoing had an easier time with teachers and the administration. My other daughter with ADD and a learning disability had a very hard time. We are looking into switching schools or moving away. Its very unfortunate because I know there are good students and teachers!! This school system is CLUELESS of what is going on when it comes to teaching, students being bullied and the massive drug use that takes place right in front of their face daily! The staff concentrate more on someone wearing a pair of jeans with a hole in the knee rather than helping any struggles that a student is facing. It is all about who knows who and who likes who that will determine the kind of experience students have. After having two children go thru Greenfield, I am disgusted with the people that make up this school system and the downright backward ways in which they operate. My three kids graduated from 2006-2012. They received an excellent education and have graduated and excelled at Purdue and Ball State. GCHS helped them build a terrific foundation, with a small-town feel, ethics and sensibility, but with a first-class academic resume. I have watch their friends graduate from Pharmacy Schools, enter Medical Schools, and all-around exceed as young adults. If you want to see what this school is made of, simply attend a parent-teacher night and watch the wonderful interaction of parents, kids and faculty in the halls. I love this school! GCHS is a terrific school! I put three kids through there and nothing but positive experiences. I have watched my peers struggle with the private school decision for high school, especially with their kids coming out of private elementary schools, but we had no such concern with GCHS. First class teachers, great administration that is smart and caring, and an excellent education. Small town values with big city resources! I hate this school. No one cares about the students and their futures. And when someone does apparently that's the one they fire. They fire them because it makes everyone else look bad. So done. To start off with my not saying the teachers are bad or anything thing to do with the academic part is bad it's the fact that, the so called "counselors" specifically Mrs. Kile, doesn't care about their students. My 8th grade year I told my counselor that I was going to do academic honors. She completely forgot I was going honors and now as a senior I had to drop to core 40 because I don't have the required classes that I should have taken in previous years. On top of that my senior wrestling season has basically ended. I was told I was ineligible until January and our sesason is done in February. The reason I'm ineligible is because my "counselor", Mrs. Kile, didn't know that you need 6 current classes in order to participate in a sport. I'm currently in 5. I'm getting punished because I tried hard through school to make my senior year easier on me but instead it turns out to be the worst year I've ever had at Greenfield Central. So if you are reading this I urge you to go to a different school because the administration does not care about their students and they only care about the high test scores so they look better on paper.

column1: This school is the definition of welfare. The school uses donated books and materials from the public schools. The walls and ceilings are lined with lung killing asbestos. I can't express my hate for the school through text. I am so happy I am now moving to another school. The school is old and outdated with non sense practices such as no cellphones or they will keep it until 3pm the next day. This school is not very structured and the staff try to act professional and fail at doing so. The school is a complete joke Small, involved and individual learning. We transferred in, have always had decent grades but now are being taught to analyze, examine and evaluate instead of teaching to the test. I am a graduate who watched in dismay as the image of the school shifted. Mr. Bucci is changing the image of the school in a positive way, and arts and academics are stellar. I transferred my teen and it was the best decision I've made. Very clean and state of the art equipment and facilities. Very warm and friendly teachers and staff. College and university enrollment outperforms many other schools. The principle Rich Bucci is doing a great job.

column3: If you are not in IB or an Athlete, avoid this school. Teachers, faculty, and administrators alike have no interest in you if you are not throwing a ball or (attempting) to get an IB diploma. As an AP student, I was insulted on at least 2 different occasions for "not being as smart" as IB students. The school is very segregated as well and, considering that GISD has a choice of school, I would suggest picking another school in the district if at all possible. I am a mother that has a daughter that attends Garland H.S the Owls. This school has very poor teaching skills, & the staff of the school does not know what they are doing. I have been having issues that the teachers keeps counting my daughter absent from class, but she will be there in the class room. I have called, been up to school, & my daughter letting the teacher know she is there but the same problem continues. I can see why alot of students drop out be of the frustration of school. I am having to withdraw my daughter from this unorganized school & place her in a better & caring school. My daughter is a Junior at GHS. She is actively involved in the IB program, choir and drill team. The extra curricular offerings at GHS are top notch. They have one of the best choral departments in GISD, placing 13 students in the Texas All-State Choir in 2013-14. Students and parents alike are encourage to be involved. The tradition is rich at GHS and the school spirit is fabulous. This is considered the best school in the district. That's not saying much. Some of the teachers involve religious beliefs in their classes. There is a church right beside the school for that; a church school. The English Pre Ap classes give a lot of tedious work, a lot of it being homework. The English teachers also constantly ask for books that they will never even use, which is a waste of the parents' money. Most of the core class teachers also make the kids carry separate books and binders; they usually want at least 2 inch binders along with their textbook, which can cause a lot of stress carrying all the required material from room to room. I am a student at Garland High School. I love this school. Sure there might be a little gang activity, but the spirit and tradition here is unmatched. But beware, if you arent in an IB class, you wont get bus transport. 5/5 Stars. Great School. Amazing kids. My kids will go here fr fr Great school for IB and higher education students! Students are wondering about the purpose of so many counselors. Most are unapproachable and unhelpful. Cant even be found! Students feel like absolutely there is no care within admin.

column1: I have a freshman at Whitney and so far, he has had an overall positive experience there. He has commented that he had more homework compared to the homework at the middle school he attended in Rocklin. It seems like it has been a breeze his freshman year getting all A's in his classes. My concern is if the teachers are preparing the students for what is to come at the college level especially after reading one of the comments from a previous student that Whitney did not prepare them for the challenging college courses. Also, why is Rocklin High still scoring 20 points higher than Whitney on API? As a student I loved going to Whitney. The teachers are great at their jobs and there is so much to get involved with. The school spirit is phenomenal. I just finished my first year of college and I feel that Whitney High prepared me for the rigors and challenges of college. Absolutely outstanding school! The kids are good, overachieving kids, there is very minimal drug use which seems to be a very big problem at Lincoln High School. The kids are very respectful and are college-bound. I recommend this school to anyone in the area. Having my third son now a Sophomore at WHS- I have to say that I couldn't be more pleased with the level of education, sports and school activities. Administration and teachers seem to do a great job with their respective duties. Whitney High School is an immature school with horrible, irresponsible teachers who do not teach and even fail you for no reason at all. The environment is full of drugs and alcohol, while the students here are mostly entitled, rich brats that think they are better than everyone else. Through many experiences I’ve had at this school I can clearly say that no student should ever be forced to try to “learn” in such horrible conditions. Excellent — a great deal of opportunity to challenge kids academically, athletically, and all around. I know that my daughter will absolutely be prepared for college upon graduation in 2021. Our girls loved their former school and are miserable at Whitney,the school caters to a small select group of students and fails others. This school is very unfair to students.Athletes can fight and even take out weapons during a game with no punishment,yet students that staff don't like are attacked and punished for everything they do that is less than perfect.Kids get "set up"all the time.Several special needs students have had restraining orders filed against them by other families at staff's suggestions for things they did not do. Bottom line,there are a couple bad apples in the staff barrel so watch your student and their files! I live in Rocklin and have loved the elementary school experience. Regarding Whitney High School, it seems there is an issue with violence, drugs and vapes. Freshman are so vulnerable and it is just too easy for the older kids to lure them in. I have heard enough (from people I know, as well as reviews I have read) about the administration at this school retaliating against those who complain or bring issues to their attention that I would not feel comfortable speaking to them about anything. That is not a good feeling. I really hope these reviews are taken seriously and these things are looking into. Our children need to feel safe. No parent or guardian wants to be at odds with school staff or administration.And they should never have to worry about their student being made to suffer because they have sought improvements.This campus has some work to do when it comes to responding to their students guardians effectively and without retaliating.Those placing students in this school must be able to trust staff working with them.Please put an end to the vindictive responses to parents voices who simply want their students kept safe!Whitney High school has always had a reputation for great teachers and lots of learning.Let's return to that sacred setting. The reports of extreme violence and prescription as well as illegal drugs being freely offered to our freshman are heart breaking.We bring our youth to this campus so they may be educated,and expect them to be protected in that process.We strongly recommend investing time in making wrongs right,rather than retaliating because errors by staff have been brought to your attention.This school belongs to the community and to the families of students attending,we take pride in the school and hate speaking words that are less than flattering.However our children must be safe,facts relating to their time there must be recorded honestly,and corruption on campus can not be tolerated,regardless of how high a position one holds at the school or with the district.Focusing on solutions and safety would go a very long way at Whitney. We feel very violated and disappointed.There is a disturbing lack of ethics among certain leaders at this school and absolutely no interest from the district in correcting or even addressing the issues.We do not feel our kids are safe at this school and aim to move this Summer so our teens are in an appropriate educational setting. Not happy campers.Very concerned about the weapons,drugs and violence on campus.Would like to see a much more solution oriented group running this site. I am fine with how the school year has been. I have kept my 4.0 last semester and I am trying to keep it again this semester. I am only in 9th grade but I can say Whitney High School is better than Rocklin High. I went to Rocklin High the first 3 days to see what the hype was about and was disappointed. The campus was small and rusty and did not feel like it met my needs. What annoyed me the most were most Rocklin High teachers. Most of them are much older and are more focused on their coming days of retirement than teaching the class. Whitney teachers are much newer which has some cons due to their inexperience. But they are more motivated to teach than Rocklin High teachers. 3/10 because, of the bullying and discrimination ive faced from this school . Whitney High School does not 1. cater to ones. 2. blames the victim for getting bullied . and 3. they dont punish anyone. *Also I will add the fact that kids here sell and use drugs non stop, And weapons have been brought to campus such as tasers,knifes,lighters, homemade shanks and much more which is scary if youre looking for a good school for your child WHITNEY HIGH SCHOOL IS NOT IT*~ A senior class of `21

column3: Mt. Whitney is a great school for my son to attend. The school has a positive culture and teachers are very friendly. Staff at the attendance office are very nice and are always willing to help me out everytime I go there. The discipline that my child has received from Mt. Whitney has been very fair and always based on VUSD expectations. If you are moving to Visalia, I encourage your child to attend Mt. Whitney, Home of the Pioneers. It has been a great school for over 50 years. As a student, I was satisfied. They're a openly creative school and offer a lot of artistic options, and their athletic program is great to be in too. One of the problems is the bullying. They recently put up a anti-bullying program that doesn't really work at all. Students don't take it seriously and, as a bully victim myself, nobody helped me. Also if you're involved in one or more after school activities, their scheduling conflicts with whatever you have and you would be forced to get kicked out of whatever club/sport you joined. Overall, I liked the some of the teachers and there are a lot of opportunities to get involved, but you would have to make sacrifices and pull your own weight in the school. I'm just saying this from a student's perspective. I have a son graduating in a few weeks and my daughter is wrapping up her sophmore year and we have loved it from the teachers to the coaching staff. The academies are great and offer students a different path through high school. They encourage student involvement and reward students with Pioneer GRIT. I am so please that when we moved back to California we choose Mt Whitney. they allow students to steal and theirs is no punishment.avoid mt whitney high school visalia

column1: The Attica schools have been a great experience for myself, my siblings and my family. The school district is very warm and caring for all of their students and offers kids a great opportunity to excel. With their good mix of academics, extracurricular activities, and sports, I found that throughout my entire time at the school I was offered all that I could have asked for. I would recommend this school to any young family trying to decide where their kids should go. They will not be disappointed. After having my children attend a private school for most of their schooling I was a bit hesitant in a public school education. column3: PHS has lots of training opportunities ahead of them in order to make the campus a safe and welcoming place. Great AP and honors classes, engaged teachers, some good options for electives. Academically it has been better than anticipated. The honors and AP classes are strong, most with excellent teachers who truly engage students and seem to love what they do. There are also some fantastic non-honors classes and teachers. But, I can also see how it could be very easy for a kid to sail under the radar without someone pushing them to challenge themselves. What has been the most disappointing is the lack of community and openness amongst the student body and even the parent community. There is not a ton of school spirit, and I think that reflects the student leadership...they almost treat it like a joke, and it's clear that they don't really care. And if the student leaders don't care, why should anyone else? There are pockets of community to be found in certain clubs, sports or groups, and maybe all high schools are like that, but it seems by the time you get to junior or senior year that stuff should start to melt away. Kids are pretty mean on a daily basis and thoroughly uninterested in extending themselves outside of their comfort zone. I wish the administration would address it somehow. Maybe it's just how teenagers are and my hopes are too high. The facility is also in dire need of investment, and not just the sports facilities! 10 out of 10! Mrs. Grainger is amazing. Daughter felt uncomfortable, as a person of color she was discriminated and made fun of.. she was not being supported throughout her high school journey

column1: Our oldest child is a freshman, and so far we love Notre Dame! The academic program has got to be one of the most innovative in the state of Illinois. The school runs on trimesters so that it can offer longer class periods. These longer class periods allow more time for writing and critical thinking development. Every student has a Mac book, and the teachers all receive regular training on how to use them in teaching. The school day is also staggered, meaning you might have math 1st period on Monday, but 2nd period on Tuesday. This means that students who need to travel for sports, service, or extracurriculars don't always miss the same class. Everytime we've stopped by the school we've been impressed by how polite and respectful the students are. The school is certainly very sports-oriented as well, but I don't see them sacrificing academics for it. If there is anything I'd change, it's the infrastructure - the school is old, the walls are thin, and it needs a new campus. It is the best high school in central Illinois, certainly in the Peoria area, though the IB program at Richwoods is a great alternative (minus the religious atmosphere that we highly value, of course). Peoria Notre Dame is definitely the best school in the area, the teachers are excellent.

column1: I grew up in a small town and when I became a teacher, I specifically looked for a position in a small district. I believe that the relationships we build with students have a direct impact on their success. Our students are engaged, active and positive leaders; our parents are supportive and generous. Our academic program is rigorous and offers a whole cadre of College in the Schools courses which allow students to graduate with college credit completed in Economics, History, Biology, Physics, English and Math. While small, our school is able to offer and support a full schedule of extracurriculars and activities. Each June it is delightful to sit in our graduation ceremony and know each student walking across the stage and to take honest pride in their accomplishments. Rockford's community stepped up and passed a referendum. There has been great renovations and additions to the three schools. Rockford is growing, yet still that small school environment that allows relationships with staff, extra-curricular opportunities, and a sense of belonging. I loved it so much I pulled my kid from a private school to attend. My youngest has a college resume full of accomplishments, awards.. that only a small school can provide. With the new cafeteria, grounds, stadium... our district is on the rise. Rockford High School is a great school. The facilities and academic standards are top-notch. It is a great public school that adequately prepares students for college. There are college level classes offered through CIS, Advanced Placement, and PSEO. Extracurricular activities include: 14 sports, cheerleading, debate, drama, band, choir, and others. The Rockford's size allows students to participate multiple activities concurrently without the need to specialize in just one or two per school year like larger metro schools. Love the opportunity to take college credits.The opportunities for students to participate in multiple activities has a huge impact on involvement. In larger schools the students usually have less chances to actually be on a team due to large turnout ( cuts are made plus the cost is high) Rockford High School recently was approved to be an International Baccalaureate (IB) school for the Diploma Program, as well as the Career Program. This programme will only add to the wonderful academic programs available to our kids. My son is currently a junior at RHS. When he graduates next year he will have enough college credits to be considered a mid-year sophomore in college. Rockford High School offers several College In the Schools (CIS) classes, as well as few AP and Honors classes. For our current 9th & 10th graders, they will have the opportunity to get CIS college credits as well as IB programme credits, which are earned after taking IB tests at the end of their senior year. What an awesome opportunity...not offered in many schools, if any. Rockford also has many opportunities for kids to be involved in several activities. Students can be involved in several extracurriculars in the academic area, arts and athletics. We have many students that are involved in three or more sports, as well as speech, band/choir and find time to participate in the fall musical. I would have to say the BEST part of RHS is the staff. The teachers CARE about their students. They teach the kids to advocate for themselves, work hard, study and become responsible citizens. I feel very blessed that my children have had the opportunity to attend school in Rockford.

My daughter is University of Maryland honors program with wonderful education from WLHS and great memories. WLHS has an exceptional principal and vice principles. Most of the teachers are exceptional, but a few of them need more training in dealing with diverse students/parents. However, any concerns are quickly addressed and resolved. If a parent is involved, the school offers an excellent academic and extra curriculum activities; that your child can participate in. The parents and teachers are the most generous and proactive group that I have been involved with. My child loves the school, and she has quickly formed many friends. She is involved in sports, band, and still maintains high grades. I am a parent of a student at Wilde Lake High School. I have been very happy with the schools efforts to provide the highest standards of education to my daughter these past few years. I am an advocate for higher education and would recommend this school to any parent who is intending on moving into this area. Wilde Lake High School is a great school. The teachers and administrators are talented and highly engaged. The extra curricular activities are diverse and welcoming of all skill levels. The students are challenged and supported academically to succeed. We are fortunate to have such a great school in our community. I am the parent of a recent graduate of WLHS. Mr. LeMon and the administration are excellent. There are many excellent teachers at WL who are engaged in the students' education while at WL and beyond. Another bonus of WL is that the student population is very diverse. My only complaint is that more parents need to be involved. Great school. Kids learned a lot and were very prepared for college. Definitely recommended for everyone. We have had two boys go through Wilde Lake, it is diverse, supportive, accepting, and academically challenging, all in one package. Most of the teachers are excellent, with the exception of a few weak links, but for the most part excellent. The administration is phenomenal. Period. LOVE the principals and vices, and even the arts are excellent. We had the experience of mostly honors, GT and AP classes, so I cannot speak to the quality of the on-grade classes. The diversity of Wilde Lake and Columbia is what brought us to Columbia 18 years ago, when we craved a diverse area to raise our family and Wilde Lake is truly a testament to what James Rouse had envisioned when he designed Columbia. We have neighbors whose children have gone to through Wilde Lake and ended up at Duke, Harvard, Columbia, you name it. My daughter graduated from Wilde Lake last year and had an excellent selection of colleges from which to choose. She was academically challenged, had the opportunity to play multiple sports, was well prepared for her college experience, and was involved in numerous extra-curricular activities. The administration, lead by an outstanding principal, is among the best in the county. The AP teachers are excellent (Wilde Lake AP scores are generally number 1 or 2 of all the county high schools). The diversity of the school was a great part of her school experience. I have heard kids from other Howard County schools say that they want to go to a college that is diverse because their high school was not. I say go to Wilde Lake High School where you can have it all! Both of my children graduated there, went on to get their degrees in four years and currently have great jobs and are out of the house. Excellent job Wilde Lake Staff! Counseling center has been very supportive of my child, who's been emotionally overwhelmed by the size and behavior of the student body. Teachers have been a mixed bag - some are truly caring and supportive, others just seem to be going through the motions, and a handful seem to have their hands full controlling the classrooms. A new principal took over in the fall of 2017, and he may be attempting to change the atmosphere, but I am concerned about the recent turnover with the faculty and the counseling center. Excellent school! Your child will receive an education within the Howard County School Distict (one of the top in the nation) while attending one of most diverse and spirited schools in the County. Students here are well-rounded and better prepared for life in the real world compared to some of less-diverse but more “highly regarded” county schools. Both of my children matriculated through Wilde Lake HS. Both went on to graduate from universities and are well adjusted successful young adults. All but one teacher were engaged and supportive. They were active members of the school community and socially connected. I have praise and no complaints about our family’s time at the Lake. The school is comprised of some great educators. My child feels supported and his needs are met. The facility is fine and is accessible. The worst school in the County! The teachers do NOT care if their students learn. The teachers have said as long as the barely pass is all they care about! The fights are almost every day! My daughter is traumatized when she walls out of her classroom to see another student covered in blood! The school always sweeping things under the rug and not addressing the problem! THERE ARE MAJOR PROBLEMS AT THIS SCHOOL

column1: My son graduated from Westfield and had a great experience. However, my daughter found it to be a very stressful academic environment. Both are top students. We moved out of state, and my daughter found her new school to be more relaxed and pleasant. Though she took honors and AP courses here too, she didn't have hours and hours of homework every night. She had time for other activities and work. Many of Westfield's teachers are good, particularly in English and the arts, but the science teachers are either not prepared or unable to impart their knowledge to the students. The math department has the attitude that top students should be able to teach themselves, so they test them on material they haven't even gone over in class. A meeting with concerned parents confirmed that yes, this is their policy. In my daughter's new school the teachers actually taught the class and asked if anyone had questions, etc., as it should be. Students from both schools are admitted to the nation's top colleges, including my two children. Part of the problem is the parents in the area Westfield serves, who naively believe a school must be that stressful for their children to succeed. Very impressed with this school especially Mr. Thomas won best principal in Fairfax County. He is a fantastic, engaging, communicative and honest administrator that does the right thing. I have never been disappointed about how he has handled the challenges during his tenure, many not of his making. The school has had some controversial & scary events associated with it but Mr. Thomas has stood tall and positive while acknowledging the issues. The guidance staff is outstanding & the process to bring the teachers, pupil & parents together to address issues is fantastic. The teaching staff is very solid although we have had some sub par teachers during our 5 years experience. Not terribly impressed with any Fairfax County school in how they manage poor teachers but we did see one completely out of touch teacher exit the year after we voiced our concerns to many administrators. Overall, very happy with the education, clearly communicated expectations of the students & their behavior as well as band/sports offered. Class size is improving but our first child had a class of close to 800 now it's down to 700 or so making it very competitive for extracurricular activities. Overall, we are quite satisfied with our child s experience at Westfield. Some great teachers, some good teachers and some mediocre teachers. The school building itself is obviously still relatively new and due to rezoning is no longer over capacity so overcrowding is not the issue that it was a few years ago. The athletic programs are second to none with the largest and most modern sports complex of the Fairfax County Public Schools. Westfield s Performing Arts departments are outstanding - led by their award winning Theatre and Band programs. Westfield has been recognized as a Virginia Honor Band 9 times in their 13 year history and their Marching Band was selected to march in the 2014 Tournament of Roses Parade. All four of my daughters have attended this school so I have experience with most of the teachers and the administration. I have found them to be caring, professional and truly exceptional. I have always been extremely pleased with the teachers and staff. Westfield is a large school but there is so much to do that it seems small for the kids. School spirit is tremendous, the facilities are without peer and they are award winning in each category! It was a wonderful experience for my children and they were well prepared for college. Communication was frequent and we always felt that our children's best interest were a priority. We are very happy with the education they received and delighted that they had the opportunity to attend this school.. I highly recommend Westfield High School. This is my first year in Virginia. I was worried that my 14 year old freshman would have set backs from moving so far away from Missouri. However, his experience was excellent. The counselor challenged him to take advanced classes and he excelled. His coaches challenged him academically also. The coaches talked to the players, keeping up with their grades and home life. My son did not want to take any days off from school to visit Missouri. He was excited about school. I was very impressed with the teachers, coaches and the staff. This was a great first year experience. Westfield made our move much easier than expected. I highly recommend Westfield High School. My son graduated this year and entered college with 27 AP credits! He scored a 5 in all but one of the tests - he received a 4. His teachers in the AP classes prepared him fully and thanks to them he exceeded expectations. I credit his teachers at Virginia Run Elementary for setting such a solid foundation. He was accepted to every college that he applied for. The school has SO much to offer. There are so many sports, clubs, and activities to join. He remained friends with many of his Virginia Run neighbors as well as developed a lot of new friends through all of the school sports and activities. Nice facilities, great staff, and numerous opportunities for students to push themselves academically. Our daughter enjoys attending this school and we are very pleased with the education she is receiving. While most of the teachers are ok, it is the administration that falls short in this school. For three years they let my child get bullied. Even though the school, school district and state have a strict no tolerance policy, they would dismiss the bullying as not punish the bullies. Until early this year my child was physically assaulted by one of her bullies. If you are a varsity athlete, they will take care of you, if you are anyone else... Good luck. We were new to the area and I was nervous to send my kids to such a large school but I am beyond pleased with their education, Academically, athletically, socially. They have thrived and have been challenged in a good way. Westfield and Fairfax county have so much to offer. This school has a very big drug problem. This is a great school considering it's size. I have 2 sons one who is in all AP and Honors and one who has learning disabilities. Both of my sons are treated with respect regardless of their abilities. Most of the teachers are great and care about their students. Both of my boys participate in sports which has helped them both. This school is horrible if I could give this school -5 stars I would there is a high drug problem and a lot of fights there is a whole week about it near the end of the year called fight week. In 2017 a girl got pepper spread by another girl. Very few teachers are helpful and actually care about the kids and not just their test scores. The sports teams are good I'll give them that. other than that just homeschool your kids. my family loves Westfield. it truly is a community. its a large school but doesn't feel like it. it's a hs of course there are issues that would find in any hs. I am very happy I still have younger kids and will be able to be a part of the Westfield community for years to come. Big drug problem, racism is prevalent, and unless a kid is a superstar they are just a number. It would be nice if ALL teachers used google classroom so it's consistent. The school is ok, probably no better or worse than other schools of its size. Westfield High School is a fantastic school with many opportunities for students outside of sports, and the school harbors intelligent, compassionate teachers. I have taught at the school for almost twenty years, and I am baffled by the reviews stating there is a "drug problem." You are responsible for your children, and if your child is hanging out with the "wrong" crowd anywhere and takes drugs -- that's your family problem and not a school problem. The majority of our students make wonderful life choices. Stop blaming schools and teachers for your child's choices. Westfield High School is top notch, and we truly care for our students and for the rigor of the academics. My children also attend the school.

column3: I love this school its great it has great students and teachers i would recommend this school. Going to Glenbrook South High School was definitely the best years of my life. Everyone is super kind and the school is actually diverse despite it's location. School spirit is definitely a big part of the school. When I first came, i wasn't big on school spirit but it gets contagious. The academics are outstanding, now that i'm in college, I feel like I got a head start by going to GBS. GBS prepared me well for my future. There's also SO many clubs and interesting elective classes to be a part of. I encourage new students to really try to get involved in the school, it really makes your experience 100x better! I promise. I would love my kids to attend this school in the future. Thank you GBS <3 Too much unneeded homework/tests with many test scores expecting a C as average from teachers, some teachers can be rude/yell shaming kids for not getting good grades, many girls are sent unwanted male genitalia pictures, kids are made fun of by others for sticking up for themselves as if that's a weakness, they get in trouble for things a student does OUTSIDE of school on weekends even, way too many rules-feels like a prison, must be rich or popular, this school expects you to be perfect and devote your child's life to them don't force them to go here the expenses they make you pay are not worth it My son had an IEP and has since graduated from college. He had a wonderful relationship with his case worker and together we brought him out of the lower level classes into the mainstream with the exception of areas he struggled with (math). Too many "good" schools like this one have emphasized accelerated classes that the average or student that learn differently from others out of the mainstream. I am so proud to say that Glenbrook South is my alma mater. My experiences at GBS helped shape me into the person that I am today. I love the community and family feel of the school. I love that GBS has a place for truly everyone. I know people have commented on this site stating that if you didn't have school spirit and did not attend games you were left out. I completely disagree. I felt like there was a place for everyone, no matter who you were. It is true that the school does have high school spirit and pep, but there are clubs of all sorts for a variety of interests/hobbies. If sports weren't your thing, then you could join yearbook/newspaper, drama club, gamers club, model UN, debate, anime club. You name it! The way I felt about GBS was that you got out of it what you put in. If you went to school wanting to be a part of the community in any way, there was an opportunity for you. I am now working for the school district and could not be happier that I am back with District 225. I hope that once my kids are of high school age, we can move to the area so they can have the amazing experience at Glenbrook South High School like I did. My experience was excellent. As a student and later as a staff member. I woudn't trade those years or experiences for anything! I love Glenbrook South my son spent 4 incredible years Both my kids loved their experience at GBS. The student body embraces all aspects of school spirit and the teachers are amazing. Glenbrook schools are wonderful for above average students. If you child has an IEP, be prepared to fight hard to get him/her services. For those above average students, homework is busy work that takes up most of your life. Sports and clubs will take up the rest of your life. My child wanted to do stage crew. The students work at the theater often until after 10 p.m. on school nights. Bullying is terrible (which the theater teacher participates in). The former head of the theater program is the father of the current head and his mother is head of the junior high theater. For all the taxes Glenview households pay, this school should be better and pick staff not out of favoritism but because they are talented.

column1: Best school in Johnstown. Hands down. Teachers care so much about the well-being of the students. I went there and had the best experience one could have in high school. Best that cambria county has to offer. Quality of students is superior, and the tuition keeps the trash very low.

column3: This is by far the best school in state. From the elementary school thru high school, this school system emphasizes character development along with education. I am a Homewood graduate that went to Shades Cahaba now my children are going thru the system. What I love the most about it is that any student can find what they truly love to do whether it is band, athletics , computer, drama etc.. There is really no "IN " crowd here. It is a fairly small and close knit school system with outstanding parental involvement. this school is garbage after the rapid decline of leadership in the past 3 years of Barnes' leadership. I love Homewood High. Teachers are amazing, students learn a lot, they offer many AP classes and extracurriculars. Such a great school. I couldn't imagine bein anywhere else. The leadership at the school and in the district lacks structure and any true concern for the students. The assistant administrator for the freshman is a bully and the principal hides in the office. I have had nothing but bad experiences with the teachers and adminsitrators there. I will say that the harassment is not based in color and gender. It's more about class and social status. For everything my kid loves about this school I can name 5 that I absolutely hate.

column1: This is an amazing school. I am graduating this year. This is a school of about 200. The selection for sports and other extra-curicular activities is not the best. The teachers seem to know just about every student which can get annoying at times but it gives a great experience. It's true that the teachers give preference to the students that actually try to do the work. Most of the teachers are top notch but there is not a great selection of classes. My only suggestion for classes: in SR year take Practical English, it gives you knowledge that is actually useful, such as how to write a resume and other things that are useful later in life. I love this school, the area is great and beautiful.

column3: This is a wonderful school. The students are for the most part well-behaved, and the teachers are well-prepared. Mr. Bush is an awesome principal. His hands on approach with the students is highly effective. The counselors in the Guidance Department are both knowledgeable and dedicated. Students are given pertinent educational planning information in a timely fashion. The teaching staff, like all public school teaching staff, are pulled in many directions. Harrison Central's teachers definitely put in the time. Harrison Central High School is a highly innovative school where student needs come first. This school is on the cusp of greatness. This school is one of the very worst I have seen. I have traveled the country and attended many different schools, due to my parents being in the military, and this school is the worst. The students are almost encouraged to act like little morons, just so the staff can get a laugh. And the teachers themselves are held accountable only for themselves and not the quality of education put out within the class room. The discipline of the staff and student body is ridiculous. I came to harrison central in my 9th grade year and was thrown into an education system that was on par with my 6th grade school. Advanced classes that are offered are a joke and the scholarship parternships with local colleges and universities are non existent. The board members are simply useless as there is never a change year in and year out to anything, look at the test scores (90% of students in 2010 were proficient in Algebra 1 compared to a ridiculous 68% in 2013), this by itself should be cause for teachers and board members to get the axe, but here we are with the same pathetic staff that we had last year. How did the school split in two and still have an above 20 student per teacher ratio? HCHS has a big problem. the teachers dont teach and when the parents ask "what can we do to help you teach our kids" all they get is we get all our lessons from the internet oh btw it's a closed site.. Counselors are a joke at least my son's was.So far we have begged for 3 years to get the information to help our son with hes school work and can't even get a basic lesson plan out of HC. I know it is a parent's job to help my wife and I are willing but without the teachers letting us know just What the lessons are about we have our hands tied. Average but could use some changes, security and safety...

column1: I moved to Seneca when i was in gradeschool, from the outside looking in SHS looks like a fantastic school. But it's all about who you know in that town. Teachers playing favorites there is an understatement. You could be one of the best athletes high school sports has ever seen but if the coach didn't personally care for you, expect to sit the bench. And if a teachers daughter/son also plays the same spot as you, you're FOR SURE sitting the bench. Teachers there gossip worse than the students, everyone knows your business whether it's true or not. During my senior year at Seneca High School i was being bullied by some girls in my grade that were "teachers pets" and started to feel like i was even getting bullied by teachers. This school treats you like a child and when i got to college i felt so lost, it did not prepare me for college what so ever. The only truly good thing i can say about this school is the art department. The 2 teachers in charge of it are fantastic! Not only do they have great knowledge of art but they were never judgmental, gossiped, played favorites, and you could talk to them about anything.

column3: I graduated from Theodore High School five years ago. All I can say, is I hope that they improved a great deal! I consider my self an average student. I struggled with most of my classes because the teachers there did not 'teach'. They baby sat. As you can tell, most of the current students who commented on this school can't even spell. I am not trying to offend any one or be rude. I am trying to be brutally honest. Unless there have been some major changes, I would not recommend this school! I sent my son to this school and for a child who did pretty well in missdle school he completely bottomed out at Theodore. I went to his school one day unannounced and baby sitting is just about the correct term for this school. Kids chewed gum in class, had their own conversations while the teachers where teaching, some even got up and left the class with out asking! The children cussed in ffront of teachers and when asked about it they said they could send them to the officce but tha the office would just send them back without punishment. I couldn't get my child out fast enough to try out Baker. I wont let Theodore ruin another child of mine. The first thing I can start talking about is the "staff." They aren't "staff..." they sit on the computer and don't care about the students...all they care about is being payed...about any school in Alabama has NO education...I'll NEVER live in Alabama due to terrible education. 2nd...NO homework...NO studying..how are you going to get INTO College? You simply CAN'T! I ask this girl daily..how much homework did you get..her responce "I dont get no homework." Hmm.....that's not good at all..such a school to get you "educated." 3. Kids can text on the phone, MAKE PHONE CALLS, etc WITHOUT the teacher caring.....hmm..this school REALLY has LOTS of issues...if you don't believe me go into the school for a day and the "teachers" will sit and do nothing. This school is a mockery of education. There is no teaching here. There is no punishment for misconduct. You diploma is a joke. It is embarrising to say i am graduating from Theodore High School. i graduated from there. the teachers and staff were friendly. Also, there is a high sense of pride among students. The sports and band are top-notch. I think it's a good school to go to. This school has been nothing but wonderful to me and my family.. My oldest son is ADHD going to 10th grade and the teachers have been so wonderful in keeping up with all the info and what I need to do to get him to graduate successfully.. thanks! All three of my kids graduated from here. I would give it a 7. Overall experience was good but too many teachers don’t help enough. They definitely need better Math Teachers. The Principal is great and the Band is a wonderful program!

column1: This is a horrible school! I attended this school for Freshman year, because I moved from King High in Riverside's territory to the Boulders, up the street from Citrus. The teachers are extremely lazy and rude. Students are out of control! All you hear is inappropriate language and all you see is inappropriate behavior! Not only are the students rude, but the parents are as well. And the teachers and staff do nothing about it! They'll also just give you a good grade because they don't want you to bother them. They also have this stupid rule about joining their Scholars Program. The principal doesn't even care about academics. If you ask me, this is a sports school. All he cares about is his football team, because they make him the most money. Most of their athletes don't even have a 2.0. Some of the staff can barely speak English! Considering most of the kids are from the rough part of town, my parents were worried that they would influence me badly. So they transferred me to Riverside Poly after Freshman year, because King was too full so I could have a better education. If you want your child to have a good education, stay away from this school. And if you can't, well good luck. The comment below from a freshman is sad. My daughter just graduated and has been in the school since freshman yr and she just loved her high school experience. Just because the majority of the students are below the poverty line does not make them bad people. As for foul language I am in the Orange Crest area all the time and the kids have potty mouths there to. That student must not have heard of the stabbing that occurred at King High. As for the teachers you will always have a few that are in the wrong line of work and that is in EVERY school! You will also have kids that have issues in EVERY school! You will always have alcohol and drug issues in EVERY school. Race and money doesn't make you any better or less. If you go into it with an I'm better than you attitude you will always suffer. This school does not put the jocks and cheerleaders first. You would be hard pressed to find a school where the band members are part of the royal courts. It is an amazing school the staff and councilors are always there for you. In her four yrs there she only had an issue with one teacher. Lesson- there are people in this world that you will never get along with - that's life! My son had a choice between CHHS and King. He made the decision to attend CHHS and we love it. I can not say enough good things about the school's administration staff, counselors, teachers, and coaching staff. They absolutely care about kids at this school. I'm an educator and I'm continually impressed by the level of commitment and dedication of CHHS teachers. I proud to say my son is a HAWK and he'll be graduating from CHHS this year. He's had an amazing experience. And just as an aside, I worked the snack bar at a football game once and the teenagers were very respectful...I could honestly count less than ten kids ( in a 4 hour time frame) who didn't say thank you. CHHS...they've got awesome teachers and kids!!! The teachers and staff are all so involved and caring, which contributes to the familiar and friendly environment of the school I am the same parent that posted about varsity volley ball coach I also wanted to say aside from the coach I have had 3 kids attend there and think teachers and principle Cabral is wonderful.Great choice for good education I love this school aside from the coach This school is absolutely sad. They have such low standards it's astonishing how a student wouldn't pass. Most of their 10th graders can barely pass their CAHSEE's. Doesn't shock me how they haven't even became a California Distinguished School. Citrus Hill is an amazing school! All the teachers are supportive and will help you succeed. Some students fail because they chose to talk and be disruptive therefore choosing to fail. Its funny how some parents make excuses for their child's mistakes when in reality Citrus Hill is great. Only two things ABSOLUTELY need to change, the restrooms and the lunch. The lunch isnt always fresh.. Great school, cares alot about students 10/10 Its been a great school for all 3 of my sons!! I am currently a Freshmen during Distance Learning and I love it... except the part of not going to school because of COVID-19. The courseload is good; you can choose from the IB program, AP classes, dual-enrollment, etc. We have ballet-folklorico, dance classes, yoga, etc, piano. The teachers are amazing-- a lot of them are really approachable, experienced, they know what they are doing, and they will help you if you need it. The administration is another story, though. Their attitude toward sexual assault and racism is lackluster; you can expect them to do very little if anything at all in response to such incidents. I've been called numerous slurs by numerous people and admin will do nothing about it. There used to be organizations like a BSU which helped students who were a part of oppressed groups get together and have a support group, but for some reason the BSU doesn't exist anymore.

column3: Best possible education for your child. The teachers are devoted and your child is in deserving hands thts all I would say for WHS. The students excell not only in academics but also athleticas and arts. 1 of my daughters graduated from here whem Mr Warren was principal. Schhol did OK. Now my other daughter is attending I like the new principal. They push studentd to excel and motivate them. No issues at all, except they should have a STRICTER dress code. Some of the girls dress like they are going to a night club. They've improved with the new principal. Teachers are there to help the students to achieve and strive. I've had no issues so far. BUT they should be more strict on the dress code. I really like the school and most importantly my child is very happy here. As a parent this is the first year at the school and the teachers and staff are always willing to help. The kids got new laptops that are used in the classrooms and at home. The students are friendly and the atmostphere is very positive. The principal is always visible outside in the morning and at the end of the day. There are a lot of classes to choose from and the teachers really seem to love what they do. Woodbridge High School has a lot of opportunities for students who are willing to work for them. Sorry that it has such a low score on this site. It is not indicative of the overall experience of this school.Wish it could measure all the positive things that the school is doing or what it has to offer the kids. My child will be graduating this year and I wanted to put in a review of the experience I had with the school for the last 3 years. The school has many classes available for kids of all levels. If your child wants to be challenged there are AP, Honors classes they can take and dual enrollment in some of the colleges. The principal and teachers are very caring and hardworking. You will see the principal around the school and in the mornings greeting the kids as they come in. All grades are updated on the parent portal , so you can see how your child is doing in their classes. The guidance dept puts in a lot of effort to get the kids ready for college and they always got back to me with any questions I had about classes needed and college applications. There are a lot of clubs and activities for the kids to get involved in during the year. They only thing I would like to see are some upgrades to the inside of the building. This is a very diverse population of students and if you are involved in your child's education this school has a lot to offer. I believe my child got a good education and positive experiences that will last a life time.

column1: Overall, excellent! We feel our son is prepared for the next step in life, which for him, will be college. We couldn't have done it without the support along the way of caring and hard-working teachers, staff, and administrators.

The administrative members are the most rude, inconsiderate kids that I have EVER meet in my entire life. Jeffrey Schultz does not know how to do his job correctly. He hates every student there. I had my son running to me in tears (sophomore) because of Schultz. We need to have him removed.

column1: Good School, Great Extracurricular Activities, Great Staff Members, Great Band, WCHS Is An Amazing School.

column3: My school is absolutely horrible. I'm currently a junior enrolled in Ardmore High (Not for long) and the entire school Is just plain horrible. The faculty is beyond poor, the students are ingrates and area is gang infested. The racial tension I think enough to get cut with a knife if you're the one handling said knife. The athletics are beyond rigged; the coaches pick favorites and new comers don't get a chance at all. Same for the band and "arts" teachers. To have a good teacher is one in a million. Same can be said for the fellow students. If you're new in the school, god luck making quality friends. Rumors are spread faster than fire on gasoline. This happened to me and a girl I went to school with. Overall this is a HORRIBLE school. I'm posting this on October 21st, 2013 and I am a student of this dreadful pit. The school is beyond repair. As with any thing, there is the good side and there is the bad side. Ardmore High School has some great teachers and administrators. A hierarchy does exist in the school, but, it is high school so I didn't expect any less. However, this hierarchy doesn't base on wealth necessarily but on how active you are in the school. It is always up to the student as to how he/she want to be perceived. If you want to be recognized then you need to be out there doing things with people who you don't like. If you can't be friend then at least be civil. That's how you get yourself ready for college and life or else you would be invisible. Sad but true. As for teachers taking favorites, that is because those people make the teachers feel respected. If you respect your teachers and act politely then your life would flow like a river. Save what left of your high school career and hopefully, you will improve your high school experience. Well, I started this year out as a sophomore and honestly I hated it. I came for a bigger school and I figured ardmore was going to be a good place. Forget it, the teachers are awful and do not care what so ever!! The students are so rude and non excepting. Me as a person can make friends easily but here they make it near to impossible. So rude and hateful. The sports is just all about who you are and who you know. Just favoritism. If you can send your child to ANY other place I reccomend you do that. Take it from me a former student. gangs, drugs, violence, poverty. please avoid at all costs unless you cant afford plainview or lone grove districts. Absolutely love this school. Other reviewers must have had revenge against some teacher or administrators! Teachers are some of the best around. School has had several National Merit Scholars. Facilities are being upgraded with a Fine Arts building that would rank high anywhere. Alumni are in some very high positions with some of the most respected companies in the world! (Disney, American Express etc.)

column1: As a recent graduate of Seneca East, I can say that I have really enjoyed my high school experience overall. The student body is very supportive and there is a strong sense of commitment to the community. Also, the school and its technical facilities are top notch! Very impressive appearance, size, competence, and cleanliness. The gymnasium and theatre are in a class of their own compared to other area schools. However when it came to academics, Seneca East's curriculum was far from challenging. Many of the departments (ie: Spanish, History, certain English courses) and their teachers are pretty lackluster. Because the administration has such little expectations, certain teachers put forth very little effort. Now, I can't talk smack about certain departments without giving credit to a very constructive science and music department- minus the choral division... Overall- a great high school experience. I wouldn't trade it for anything! This school has a well deserved reputation for tolerating bullying. In fact, some of the student bullies have parents who work at the school, who know what their kids are doing & do NOTHING about it. Do NOT send your kid here. I do not agree with the statement about bullying. I really see no bullying at this school. Obviously there is drama, like in every school, but in my 9 years at seneca east i've seen very little bullying. Though, with the small amount of bullying there is, I do agree that teachers aknowledge it and completely ignore it. They ARE trying to teach a lesson that the child needs to stand up for theirself or tell someone. If you put your child into this school they are likely to get great friends no matter their past. One thing I do NOT like about the school is it is built around a mold, provided by staff and students. In most grades, there are certain standards (or molds as i call it) that mostly everybody fits into, while the others that don't are ignored and feel outside. This school is very topsy-turvy (cheerleaders are losers, band is awesome) but thats what makes it unique. Though if you want to send your kid here for acedemic reasons, I suggest to choose a different school because there are virtually NO options here.
