column3: We moved away from here after only one year so our daughter wouldn't feel the embarrassment to have to call Oswego High School her Alma Mater. Many of the teachers would be classified as "ineffectiver" if they were teaching outside of Oswego. The social studies and math departments were a joke. One would think that phys ed teachers should set the example, but the two female phys ed teachers were very overweight and lazy. The stats show a poor performing school in a poor performing school district in an economically distressed town. Couldn't get out of there fast enough. I've been a community member for many years and have various neighbors with children who have successfully completed graduation requirements in this school district. I rarely hear negative comments from them. Of course there will be a few bad apples but many of the teachers, counselors, and administrators are working hard to make sure our younger citizens are well-taught individuals. I'm proud to call this area my home. There is not a single positive characteristic of the school. Compared to other schools, it is a joke. After being in this school I can attest that this school is incredibly mediocre, arguably unsafe, and (in my experience) pretty uncaring to individual students. All this being said, it is at least better than Fulton high school

column1: I went into Xavier expecting the most amazing school, how wrong I was. I am a 4.0 GPA student and I found the academics were nothing special, I actually believe I got stupider in some of my classes because of how uninteresting the teachers make it. These disinterested teachers kept their bored students occupied with mindless busy work. The teachers were probably the most cold and wicked people I have ever met. Yes, I said wicked, a number of the teachers would make students cry every day. The discipline was unfair and harsh. The faculty have no idea what it is like to to be a teenage girl and they feel the only way to deal with misbehavior is endless detentions. If you are not Catholic, get ready for it to be shoved down your throat. Unless you agree with every single thing that the Catholic Church says or does, keep your mouth shut. No First Amendment rights here. Xavier only relies on their reputation, which is long gone. Save your money and go anywhere else. If you say it's the worst school, then don't go there. You complain that they are harsh if you're not Catholic. The School is called a Roman Catholic High School for a reason. Almost everyone there is Catholic. If your not Catholic, then learn to read and don't go to a Catholic school. It's as simple as that. I have always believed that academics are most important. If you want a better social life or better athletics this would be a school for you. However, Xavier is not good at challenging students and making them thrive academically. Girls go here when they want to be popular or be recruited for sports, not because they want to go to a top name school and learn. If you want an easy A with no challenge; this is your school. If you want to learn and have to work hard; go somewhere else! This school weighs heavily the amount of money a parent can donate. Their children do have advantages over others. The principal has been there 50 years and while stability is a good thing, things are stuck in a rut. She doesn't even have an email address that parents can send emails to. Everything has to go through her secretary and often times things are "lost." Look at the reviews below, things are getting worse as the years go by. There are many disappointing reviews in the most recent years. If you are considering Xavier, I would ask to see their attendance records. I know that for my daughter's class, they started out with about 325 and maybe 250 graduated (i think the actual number was lower). That's over a 25% loss in enrollment. To me that signifies a big problem. If you have a child who is struggling do not assume that because you are at a religious school that anything will be done to help them. This includes severe bullying etc. Parent involvement is very high. Most of the families are wonderful, it is a shame that the school's leadership doesn't support these girls as they should. Brophy is a great example of positive leadership. This is an excellent school! We have one child there and one who graduated last year who is thriving in college due to what she learned at this school! I highly recommend this school! Some of the student reviews complain that this school does not provide a good education or that its too easy. However, I believe that a girl's experience of Xavier relies at least somewhat on their decisions and what they make of their time at school overall. I am currently a freshman and I was not disappointed at the difficulty of the classes. I think that this may be because a good portion of my classes are honors or advanced placement. At the middle school which I used to attend, I had a 4.0 GPA and I was bored in all of my classes. Now I am consistently engaged in class and I have a feeling of fulfillment after I complete the several hours worth of homework which I was assigned. I can say without hesitation that all of my teachers seem to care about the students and how they are doing both academically and socially. I have neither had any problems with bullying, nor do I know anyone who has been bullied. I just graduated from Xavier and I can tell you I disliked the school my entire 4 years there. If I could have left I would have. The school taught me nothing. Absolutely nothing yet I had 4-5 hours of homework a night. This school is made to cater to children with rich parents who can drop anything at a drop of a dime not kids with working parents. I am not catholic and though this is a catholic school, the way they taught religion was repulsive. The teachers were terrible. I have about 3 teachers I actually liked over the entire 4 years. The teachers were horrendous and made girls cry. 95 percent of the students were carbon copies. Caucasian, blonde, athletic and rich. Only now are they starting to add more minorities but when I was a freshman there were hardly any. Save yourself the money, your children their tears, and send your kids somewhere else. I have two daughters who went to XCP. If you are wealthy or poor, this is a great school and the staff will treat you kindly. The nuns go out of their way to talk to the wealthy parents. One of my daughter's friends was from a wealthy family. One of the nuns would approach her group to ask her how she was doing and ignore all of the other "middle class" girls. Wealthy parents can afford the school and can have friends donate to AZ Scholarship so their kids can go to the school for free. If you're poor, the tuition is free. Middle class? You get nothing. We spent about $3,000 a month sending two kids here at a time and did not qualify for financial assistance. That's fine, but stop asking me to donate when you never once gave us a discount. We were fortunate to be able to afford the tuition most of the time, but there were a few times when we were late on a payment. The harassing phone calls were horrible, but the way they humiliate the kids if their parents are a little behind is absolutely not Christian. Kind of ironic! Some teachers are great, but often my kids complained that the teachers just presented Powerpoints which were readily available online from Google. The level of classes available was not rigorous. If your kid ends up in a challenging college, they will find that their XCP education had lots of holes. If you want the more rigorous classes, you need to go next door to BCP. Sad that they save the rigorous curriculum for the boys next door. What century are we in? Sports are more important than academics. Empowers girls to be the best they can possibly be! Xavier pushes them to excel. My first daughter graduated from XCP in 2015. She received an excellent education and was accepted to all the colleges she applied to. She participated in many activities at XCP including being a student ambassador She feels that the honors college where she currently attends is easier then XCP. I was very impressed how XCP empowered her and empowers young women to be successful and future leaders.My second daughter is now attending XCP and is having a great experience. XCP has a lot to offer and I would highly recommend it. Send your daughters somewhere else! Phoenix country Day, Notre Dame Academy, definitely somewhere else. This school is not worth it; it’s all hype ! Xavier has lost it's purpose! They are so concerned about feminism that there is no focus on love of self, love of others or loving God....it's all about winning. Winning sports titles, getting scholarships and going to elite colleges. College preparatory should also be about LIFE Preparatory! These young women are only learning about how to get into college -- I want my daughter to learn about how to live in college and beyond! The stress Xavier puts on the girls is unreal! Busywork, rules, ridiculous and petty punishments....the joy is gone form the campus. 0/10. Send your kids somewhere else, please. I think the negative reviewers are not seeing the bigger picture. My sister graduated and went on to Pepperdine which she graduated with honors because it was easy compared to high school. She got her masters in teaching and then went to Georgetown Law. She learned how to deal with every type of person and she was on top of her studies because you have to be to make it at XCP. If you want your daughter to get the best education, learn to critically think, and do whatever she wants in life, this school is for you because they know how to teach the girls how to deal with LIFE. My daughter is a freshman this year and was overwhelmed at first. She went to a challenging catholic school who prepared her for the academics. What surprised her was how much punishment there is for small infractions. Every story she told me, whether it happened to her or someone else, I could see how it would help her deal with life’s challenges in the long run. Life isn’t fair! This school teaches you to follow the rules and use your brain. My daughter got detention the first month of school for a uniform violation and hasn’t had an issue since. We aren’t a rich family. My daughter is on financial aid and I don’t feel we are treated differently at all. It only covered the first semester, so now I’m 2 months behind and I haven’t received one harassing phone call. The administration has always been very kind to me when I need to go into the office. If you have high expectations for your daughter then this is the best school for her. If you don’t, and can’t see the bigger picture, then look elsewhere. I can’t think of another Az high school that I would want my daughter to attend. My brother went to NDP because it was closer to home and his experience was nothing like my sister. Drugs run rampant at NDP which is why they have to randomly drug test their students. My daughter said she hasn’t seen anything like that at XCP. Every school has positives and negatives that must be weighed when making a decision. The negatives of this school are the cost, strict Catholic ideology and some teacher quality. Yes this is a Catholic school, but if your student does not align with the ideology, they must be aware that they may have to keep their opposing beliefs quiet. There are certain known teachers, especially in the required religion classes, that will not allow discussion of ideas in opposition to the Catholic church and may even lower your grade for voicing said views. My daughter quickly learned which teachers were open to debate which weren't. To the ones opposed, she simply parroted back the Catholic mantra and did fine. Ironically, the two priests that were at the school during her 4 years were both welcoming, kind and listened to her opposing views and treated her with respect. Some teachers are not of the quality you would expect given the cost of this school. The administration needs to do a better job of hiring and retaining better teachers. Now the positive. The environment at the school is positive, with the girls and administrators championing the accomplishments of the students. At such a large school, it is easy to find a group of like minded peers, and those friendships become very strong. Especially without boys there on a daily basis. The friend groups really become a support community. The extra curricular and sports offerings at the school are top notch and there is definitely something for everyone. The academic rigor at Xavier is lacking. The feeder schools are sub-par, which feeds into pushing dual enrollment instead of AP because the students are not at that academic level. Xavier pushes dual enrollment to make more money and don’t put enough emphasis on AP classes. The entire school currently has 4 AP Biology students. In public school of the same size you will have 2 full classes of AP Bio students. If you are looking for academic rigor you are better off with a public school that has a strong AP or IB program.

Reactive because they are more concerned with its reputation than the students' welfare. your review here] I will be part of Alonzo and Tracy Mourning's first graduating class, and I can honestly say I would not trade it for any other school. My education here has been exceptional. There are not many students, the whole school adds up to just about 1,000 students, maybe less. This allows us to be able to get involved in many different activities. It is not hard to find a club or join a sport. The counselors and other staff are friendly and helpful. The teachers are not the most experienced out there, but they work hard to give us the best education they can, and I don't feel that I have missed out by having them teach me. Our principal is amazing! Ms. Alayon really cares about the school and its students and makes a point of appearing at all the important events, even the football games that we tend to lose often. But the biggest praise I have to give this school is how much they work to get us into college. All the english teachers make themselves available for help with our college essays and math teachers are there for SAT help. Our CAP advisor goes around talking to the students and brings speakers in to classes and the school has free SAT prep classes every friday. I am a current sophomore at ATM and it is the best school! Our principal is amazing and we have a lot of school spirit! This school is not good if you are good at football but we are getting there. It's a smaller environment which is very nice but the school is growing. I have learned so much! I would recommend ATM to anyone! THE TEACHERS ARE WRITING THESE REVIEWS! THIS IS A C RATED SCHOOL AND ITS GOING TO COME OUT VERY SOON HOW HORRIBLE THIS SCHOOL IS .... ITS WILL BE ON THE NEWS!!! MOTHER'S TALK TO YOUR LITTLE GIRLS ... PLEASE! What is your rating -- 7 out of 10 -- based on? ATM has the highest Florida School Grades rating: an A. The reviews are mostly very good, except for the one that says the teachers are writing the reviews. But that review is basically illiterate and shouldn't count. So...why the 7? I am a senior at this school right now & i am disgusted that this school is still up and running and no one from the county has come and done something. In this school when someone has a problem they don't handle it at all then when it gets physical they suspend everyone , they are literally as we speak trying to kick some of us seniors out for missing one credit, I've never seen such horrible administrators in my life. Please don't bring your kids here. I'm in the process of reporting them to the school board because they are telling me we need to talk about other "diploma options" 2 months before school ends ? This school is a joke!!! I will rate the school Excellent !

column1: SJM is well below average in a number of respects. First, teacher quality. The school has very little money to hire, train and retain quality teachers. Those who excel often leave for higher paying public school jobs. As a result expectations and policies around teaching quality are low and rarely enforced. Second, academic focus. While SJM likely makes one believe that its SAT scores and academics are top notch, they are no better than COMPARABLE public schools in Fresno. The school often touts its religion emphasis which makes sense as a Catholic institution. But this is not an excuse for mediocre academics. High school students need moral development but they also need teachers who can teach and teachers who believe their students can achieve at high levels. Low expectations limit the school's potential on a number of fronts. Finally, cronyism. If you are not plugged into the "elite", also known as a rich family who donates lots of money, then you won'e be taken care of as well. Simply put, the school needs money so they solicit wealthy parents and in return SJM takes "special care" of their students. It's not equitable and probably not Catholic... This is by far one of the biggest mistakes our family has ever made. This school is a hot bed for bullying. Many of the kids have horrible attitudes. It does not help that most of the administration is rude. The principal is by far one of the most pompous men that I have ever encountered. Well they say there academics are top notch they are pretty much the same as the classes offered at top fresno & clovis schools. This school is not worth the tuition at all. The parties are awesome! The girls are smart and rich! Defiantely a good school! I have been very pleased with this school and the experience my two kids are having. It is a safe environment where they can focus on learning. It is a college prep school where they are surrounded by other students that are also college minded and competing for grades. The faculty know all the kids by name and hold them accountable for grades and behavior. It is a close community with good parental involvement. No gangs. No fights. No police needed on campus. If you are serious about your child's future arrange a visit to the campus and see for yourself. The kids are extremely mean and stuck up. Overall a materialistic and superficial school. The staff only care about the students who have powerful parents. As a student at SJMHS I been treated equally and I was able to make friends very quickly. Many may make the excuse and say they leave out the ones with different beliefs. As a a student who has different religious belief, I have passed my classes and was treated the same if not slightly better. I would definitely recommend going no matter who you are. We love San Joaquin Memorial! We pulled our children out of public school after much dissatisfaction with the public school system. Our children love their new school. They really enjoy being at a smaller school. As a parent I’ve noticed they are much more involved at their new school. I also love they are getting a great faith filled education.

column3: I've had 3 children graduate from HHS and one more who is a junior this year. I've never had a single negative experience with any teachers or administration. We have had many issues arise with our kids and the school has handled them all with grace and worked hard to make sure my kids get the best possible education and genuine care. I'm so thankful we have such an amazing school system with awesome teachers! I would give it a 30 out of 100. Change the principle and maybe it would be better. Nobody cares about you in this school unless you’re an athlete. It’s a disgusting place. A nightmare for my student with a disability who was treated like a criminal for having autism and was trying to find connection and caring from a school that rejected him.

column1: Is it possible to give zero stars? Teachers spend more time talking about personal matters, or sitting on faecbook then actually doing there job. if your child is an honors student or star of a sport then the rules do not apply to them. The administration is lazy at that an hardly ever does anything besides scold students for having minor attendance issues. most parents in the community are involved but if your student isnt one of the best then the same attention is paid to the parents as their children,minimal! I felt so sorry for the child of the person who wrote the Aug. 18th review. The review had 3 punctuation mistakes, 8 spelling errors and 3 capitalization errors. This parent obviously had an issue with their childs attendance. As a parent, your job is to get your child to school, on time, every day. Don't blame the school because you did NOT do your job. They are preparing your child for real life. If you don't come to a job you are fired. The lesson learned is: If you don't follow the rules there are consequences. That is a good life lesson. You, as an adult, haven't learned that yet. I feel bad that your child has to suffer because of your ignorance. Try backing the school and teachers for a change and see how your childs world will open up. Perhaps you could set up a meeting and talk to parents of successful students and see what they do different from you. Ignorance is NOT bliss when an education is on the line. Linda I went to this school and found that the teachers cared about your personal learning more than they did about standardized tests and that may be why so many of us have gone on to have college degrees and careers that most people could only hope to have. This school is a little harder on its grading than most (at least when I was there 94% for an A-), but it teaches you to work hard, and to ask for help when you need it. Like all schools you get out of it what you put into it. I made sure to take advantage of teachers office if I needed it and I joined many clubs and sports teams. I would not have changed what I learned there or the experience for anything in the world. Parkview High School students receive a very strong education in a safe environment with great facilities. I strongly recommend Parkview HS. Parkview high school goes above and beyond to help all students excel.

column3: It is embarrassing to say I attended high school here. To designate even half of a star to this school district is generous. This school is such a disgrace to the community and taxpayers money! The principals lie straight to your face and abuse their powers. Teachers are complete utter garbage. Its sad to say but i think we kids are smarter than these failures. They have no respect for us and dont care about what we want. column1: Finally becoming a senior, I've seen that quality has drastically decreased. It used to be a good school with great administration, freedom for students, and amazing teachers. Though as years came by, the school became overcrowded with students, few classes did not have enough desks this senior year, and they have began to drop some majors, Welding was dropped 2011, and from the extent of my knowledge Web Design and Development and Video Productions was dropped. They didn't even bother to make an attempt to salvage these majors, or at least find substitutes that can teach the classes effectively. If you're planning to have open periods senior year, you will be forced to hold a job or have some training and receive credit, while the program is really good, I feel it shouldn't be forced upon students. The only thing I've seen improve is the food, everything is fresh in both the student store and actual lunch lines. Privacy is not a thing here in SECTA, if you have you're phone taken away, they will ask for you're password and inspect every spec of your phone, they will report you on anything they don't like. The school also does not promote open speaking, if you talk openly about how the school sucks they'll rather hopefully ignore it or send you to the office. Good teachers have become scarce, every teacher does want to make everyone succeed, though most aren't effective. It is important that you will only receive an ACTUAL DEGREE if you're in cosmetology, other majors are passed off as experience, If you're student requires special education or has a disability, chances are they'll be cleaning all day. Talk about outrageous rules is very common, and transportation to school is outrages, I've had to wait at my stop for more than 30 minutes before, several times. While this school has good intentions, they have poor methods of execution. This school highly suffers from Censorship, Invasion of Privacy, overcrowding, poorly trained teachers, and unreasonable rules. You are better heading to any other tech school like A-Tech or SWCTA because I feel like my high school years here were wasted because the only good things your child is getting is friendly teachers(bad at teaching), school lunch, and friendly students, nothing else. Students only have good grades because of their already placed problem solving skills, hence why the school is rated highly.

column3: It is my understanding that this school used to be better but im guessing budget cuts have ruined that for many schools- including this one. This school is way overcrowded. The Distinguished scholars program is no where near as challenging as they claim it will be and the all new adminstration abd counselors are so overwhelmed that you are lucky to get a call back after 5 or 6 attempts.In addition, if your child has any issues that need attendind to, dont expect ant compassion- they are rude and short with you and your kid... If you do not want your good student to end up "just a number" and lost in a crowd, find another school, i wished i had! We are out of there in January-semester change! Overall, Wilson is a great school. I have two children attending at this moment. One of my children is special needs; this is where Wilson needs to refine their skills. Granted parental involvement is vital with any student and especially when that child has special needs, but I have had to go beyond the norm to advocate for my child. Both my children are doing well at Wilson but be diligent if your child has any special needs. Wilson is a historic school with unsophisticated, completely disorganized and overly impacted programs. For the past four years we have experienced disengaged and unhelpful counselors and dishonest athletic booster clubs coupled with administrators who are more interested in the status quo rather than progress. Poly PACE or CIC seem to be much better programs in the same school district with overall better athletic performance. I am a parent of a Wilson student and a teacher at a different Long Beach High School. Wilson has a strong academic program, plenty of student support for both academics and personal issues and great parent support. My student is also an athelete and the coaches emphasize academics before athletics. The staff at this school has always returned my emails and phone calls either the same day or the next day. I even received an email from the counselor at 10pm. My student is very happy at Wilson and her academic program is both challenging and engaging. We have had only positive experiences at this school. This school is a really great school for learning, you got AP classes, accelerated classes, and even a special program for students that are falling behind (Below 1.4 GPA avg.) called Park Avenue. There are a wide variety of electives to choose from like Graphic Design, 3D art, Art and Animation, Ceramics, Architecture , Piano, and many others! There are also many other languages other than English to choose from! STAY AWAY!! This school is all about smoke and mirrors. While there are some hard working staff and teachers the administration is horrible. They allow the kids to run wild and are not supportive of their teachers there. It is severely overcrowded and they have lowered their standards in the past couple of years otherwise their "park avenue" would be overrun with kids below a 2.0 average. Stay away at all costs! Wilson is in a safe neighborhood close to some of the most beautiful parts of Long Beach. The teachers are very experienced and caring, college placement is high and the school excels in academics, athletics and student environment. Any student who is considering Wilson needs to get on campus during a normal school day to see what a great place Wilson really is. My three boys attended here and were challenged academically and athletically and were very well prepared for academics and athletics in college. One is still competing on the USA National Team. The administration for this school is horrible. It needs staff that cares about students education. The worst!!! As a father of 2 graduates from Wilson class 2010 and 2016, I can attest to the excellence of this school. Both of my daughters got into Stanford with very high GPA. And one of the Valedictorian with a 4.75 gpa. Do I need to say more? This is a great school. I like this school although it's overall score has dropped a bit since my daughter first started. Very poor experience leadership is interested in a few students AKA those from the Belmont Shore area There are a few teachers at this school who drive my kid crazy. They are poor teachers. But most of them are quite gifted considering how many non native English speakers go here. My kid is in the AP classes and she gets frustrated when she wants to learn and everyone else is messing around because the teacher won't or can't control the class room. But that is an exception and only one class a year for her seems to have that problem. nuetral in communication with teachers. school is too large I've only felt comfortable in one specific class, while the others were stressful or hard to understand. There is also an issue with smoking in the restrooms, it has gotten to the point where anyone hardly goes in there unless it's to smoke. Bullying is an issue swell. A classmate was being picked on in one of my past classes and the teacher did not bat an eye even though it was happening publicly. When students report things, it is hardly taken care of. With all that, I believe there is more to be done and I wish Wilson the best after. Long Beach School District: REMOVE THE MASK MANDATE NOW!You went from promising these kids "two weeks to slow the spread" to nearly TWO YEARS of these mandates.It is time to give our students back their FREEDOM!

column1: -a student I feel that Maquoketa Valley is a great place to go to school, I came from a 4A school with over 2,000 kids and coming to this school with 210 made me feel really welcome, the teachers are great teachers they're stern but really care for the students and they are all supportive of both sports and fine arts which to me as an advocate of both, that's important knowing that no matter what you decide to do you will be supported. Most of all, the students are great rarely ever are there problems with bullying and everyone gets along. I rate Maquoketa Valley a 10/10
column3: We moved to Geneva from Northern Virginia this summer and our daughter started her Senior year. It was a wonderful experience for her (and us.) The students welcomed her immediately and make her like she had been there always. The teachers and staff provided so much information to us about the school, the community and so much more. They confirmed our move was the perfect decision and the education they provide is outstanding! We are military and moved here from Italy and love it. It is a small country school with all the charm. The teachers are awesome and the kids are friendly. The community participates in all the activities of the school esp. football. It is nice to see such turn outs for the kids. The school is small but the children don't get lost in the crowd. We will be sad leave when it is time to move again.

column1: Class of 2013!!! I loved this school! I got to be honest when my mother told me she was putting me in an all girls catholic school I thought it was going to be the end of the world!! I went in there with a bad attitude! But I am SO happy my parents made me to SSA! The teachers are so helpful and caring! The girls are the best. One thing I did notice there was no cliques, everyone was nice to each other, I loved that we had mass every month, and the completions we used to do with our brother school Saint Paul. I loved every day of it. If I could I would go back! GO DOVES!!!!! This is a good school, not a great school. It is difficult on girls who transfer in from another school or out-of-state due to their 4x4 block schedule. I definitely would not recommend transferring in mid-year. And because of this scheduling, these girls are only taught Religion for 1 semester. I wish I had considered ahead of time. Some of the teachers are awesome. Some of the classroom buildings are very old though there are 2 newer buildings that are nice. There is little covered walkways for students on rainy days. Lunch is outside except for rainy days then the girls eat in the gym. For the amount of tuition, one would expect much nicer buildings and classrooms. Also laptops would be more efficient than the iPads which are difficult to take notes on. Fantastic learning and social environment! The girls are amazing. Would highly recommend! Can't wait for the new stem labs! SSA is the best option for girls in high school on the northshore. SSA offers a great academic program, champion athletics, and opportunities to make long lasting friends.

column3: As a student of Lumberton High school I have to say I am rather disappointed. I was new in February and I hardly learned anything while I was there. Some of the teachers are lazy and let the kids play on their phones instead of do actual work. I am a student of LHS, and very proud to be a student. I am very pleased of my school. We are a huge family. Even though we may not have the best coaches, we still support every athletic team. It should not matter if we win or lose. I have learned so much from all my teachers. Without being in an advanced class they still challenge us every single day. LHS might have a few fights, but you can not say that any other school has not had a fight. The point I'm trying to make is that, many students talk about how great it is at other schools. So they leave, and after a month there they complain how horrible their new school is. Every school will have its problems. But you have to deal with them. I love my school and everyone in it. Once a Raider always Raider! Terrible. The teachers themselves bully the children and it's the same school politics as usual where everyone covers for the other so nobody is held accountable. We are a military family. As army “ brats” my children have attended a lot of different schools. This is the worst. All of the programs my daughter was in before Lumberton don’t exist here. She had to give up DECA and debate and academic programs to be offered agricultural and Christian activities. Go to private school if you can. As a parent, LHS is an amazing school for your child to attend!! All the teachers are super amazing and are supportive of the children. They all care for the students as if they were there own child. After moving from Colorado my kids say that this school is so much better for them! Both my kids went from making B's and C's they both have all A's now! I definitely recommend this school to everyone!

column1: I am currently attending this school. The education system is excellent in my opinion. And there are plenty of friendly classmates, if you choose the right ones to hang out with. But be careful, some of them are backstabbers. The middle school counselor is the most unfriendly and unwelcoming person I have ever met. Don't expect your child to feel comfortable talking to her or being able to come to discuss anything The school is fine, and the people are great, but they could change many things. Including a teachers attitude

column3: My daughter will not be attending this High School the lazy,angry,Favortisim,nepatisim,(Yes most faculty are related to the students,to the staff to the aministration,etc.etc.)Very small town! Trust me the middle school gives a clear view of whats expected in the H.S. no thanks I'm moving my daughter out of this town! My daughter will not be attending this High School the lazy,angry,Favortisim,nepatisim,(Yes most faculty are related to the students,to the staff to the aministration,etc.etc.)Very small town! Trust me the middle school gives a clear view of whats expected in the H.S. no thanks I'm moving my daughter out of this town! This school is a parents worst nightmare. School is lax in checking residency so students are coming in from other districts and seriously overcrowding the school. Many of my daughters classes are packed with 30 students or more per class. Not enough books, overtaxed, disnterested teachers. The ones who are interested are seriously overworked and challenged with up to 150 students to oversee. Extreme lack of control of student behavior on all levels, the parents are equally unbehaved and lack simple manners; apple and the tree thing going on. . Sadly lack of parental involvement except for dances or cookie sales. If more parents paid attention to academics and raising funds for more books or extra teachers, rather than cookie dough, we might be able to help imrpove our childrens chances at a better education and future. IT IS A GOOD SCHOOL BUT THEY MUST HAVE UNIFORMS, THE GIRLS DRESS UP VERY INDECENT. My 15-year-old daughter attended Cliffside high school for one year because we moved. We have had great experiences with the elementary and middle school. The principle, Ms. Morrow from the middle school moved to the high school at the same time my daughter moved. Ms. Morrow is an excellent principal and had provided great support for my daughter who was having issues in middle school. Actually, the teachers and vice-president in the cliffside middle school were very helpful with helping me with my daughter. So even if the high school was having any issues I was confident with Ms. Morrow moving there that these issues would be straightened out immediately. Anyway, I immediately contacted all her teachers right away and met with her guidance counselor to ensure that I could help my daughter with her transition and they were very responsive. As far as I am concerned the experience was very positive and the staff were very good and concerned. I go to 8th grade in cliffside park and i am telling you right now not to move here. Bad enough stuff is happening in 8th grade(drugs, violence, sex) I know the people in the town and it is horrible i also know a lot of high schoolers and no one that i knew that graduated went to a good college. I know the teachers there and hear what my friends say they are disuntersted in their students. US news and world report rankings for high schools have given CPHS a bronze medal for effort over the past three years. This ranking of 3 is outdated. A few reviews talk about drugs but that is the case in many schools including the better private schools such as the Dwight Englewood school where drugs are rampant. As far as choices for college, teens choose to go wherever they want but gifted children go to Ivy League schools. My son is one of those. This high school really isn't that bad with its academic opportunities. I find that the only issues with the school are the students that attend it and the overcrowding. Many students in the school just don't have a passion to academically excel. Also, there are quite a bit of students that are disruptive and rude to teachers. Addressing the overcrowding part, there are a lot of students that attend this school, and the merge with the students residing in Fairview definitely adds to it. The school was built many years ago, back when the town had a much smaller population. So, this school really isn't meant 1,000+ students. Walking through the halls can be extremely frustrating. If you are, or will be, a student here just know that as long as you are mature in school, take your education seriously, and don't mind many of the annoying people around you, you will not have such a hard time. Yes, there are a few teachers that students would not be very lucky to have, but that is the same for every school. As long as you are respectful, many teachers are very helping. There are many excellent teachers I can name. This school offers a variety of advanced classes, such as AP Biology, AP Physics I, AP Calculus, AP English, and more. There are also honors classes for many of the core subjects. If you are able you get into these classes, you don't have to worry so much about bothersome students. Overall, this school is not bad, except for the fact that a good portion of the students are lacking in their ambition to excel. The efforts by administration and the teachers to help improve the school can definitely be noticed! Classes have been added to the curriculum and academic clubs/teams like DECA have been added as well. Hopefully the improvements will continue and more enriching and challenging courses will be added to the curriculum. Actually unsafe if you are not a white person. I had been one year in this school and i can say that its very difficult to be in these kind of space. most of the student in the school are spanish. its very hard to make a friends if you are not a spanish speaker. the counselor are not really good. the teachers having trouble teaching the students. if you are a spanish speaker i would recomend to go to this school. This high school is a great one. Many people like to put it down. If you have a hunger for success it starts with you. CPHS teacher’s, counselors are always committed to your own educational program. Study and be prepared, have a positive attitude about Your education. The school curriculum is state mandated. Therefore it offers from AP courses, honors, etc. I personally attended this school. It offered me what I needed for college.

column1: I am a 2012 graduate of Oak Park High School and I am PROUD to say it! I have been with the Oak Park School District for seven years and has seen the gradual downfall and rise of the district. This high school is under the wonder leadership of a wonder administration, being taught by excellent teachers that provide excellent academic courses that could at times become rigorous. With the NEW & IMPROVED Board of Education, this school and school district is DEFINITELY on the RISE to academic success and they care about each and everyone of their students. I would definitely recommend this school to anyone who is looking for a good school to enroll into. The security is terrible alway suspending pupils I would never ever recommend this school to no one. However testing scores are low too many pupils out of school steady learning Great and I’m glad that I came here instead of DPS I would rate my experience as a parent at this school a 7.5/10 just because of the environmental state it is in the effectiveness of helping others and cooperation is extraordinarily well.

column3: Ok school. There is a certain science teacher in 9th grade that brings it down. Certain teachers needs to go. It's is the worse school that my son attended. He received very little help from his teachers and the guidance councilor is rude and got annoyed when ask for advice or help. This school may be good for children that are advanced but not for any student that needs extra attention or below average! Don't be fooled by the "A+" school.... It's not, only on paper!!! I felt as though the school is more concern about the fcat scores than what the children are really processing and learning, I am a Freshman at Crestview High School and entering this school from the local middle school was a shock! The students at CHS are out of control and fights happen all the time, right in the middle of the halls! The school is unsanitary and old and many of the bathrooms are so repulsive I do not even want to use them. The school is definitely overcrowded and class sizes are very large. On a positive note, most of the teachers and staff are very helpful and informative, but some are clearly only at the school for their paycheck. The principal is helpful, the staff in the office try to help, but they often do not know the answers to your questions. Overall, Crestview is a great school from an academic standpoint, but something needs to be done about the fights, vandalized desks and lockers, corrupt students, and sanitation. My daughter went to Crestview High school and i can say its a great school. They have the CHOICE program and this year they just added cosmetology, they several other options too. There athletics are great. Academics are Amazing, all the teachers care and if they have a failing grade they will notify you if you let them know that you want them too. The principal is great too. The ESE program is wonderful. It does have crowded hallways but my Daughter could get from on end of the school to the other and be to class on time! Discipline is very high too. Fights, fights, fights daily, it is a great school however some of the kids here need to be sent off. It's quite unbearable here for me honestly because of just this. Most teachers here are great, they communicate with the students a lot with the exception of the few who just get up and teach until the day is finally over. Great school, so-so community (students). column1: Quality small town school district. Teachers and staff are caring and well qualified. Parents are friendly and care about their childrens education. Athens community has come together to pass a referendum a few years ago to help financially. Athens has been doing very well in a number of sports the last few year and should continue with a number of very good/caring coaches. School buildings are a little out dated but, overall, a very nice school and happy with my kids education so far. Rate this school it is low on the totem pole. I wouldn't send my dead dog here if it was the last school around. Staffing is poor coaching is poor and privacy is poor in school. Never again will I support this school and the decisions it wants to make. The can't keep track of the students they have and then go and harass parents after looking out for student safety. Takes a community to raise a child in the town then I guess it takes a community to keep that child's butt in the school too. Eat your own words and practice what you preach. Athens is a great place to be. I came here a few years ago and the community is so welcoming. The School District of Athens seems to be very innovative and creative. When I came here a few years ago, it seemed like Athens was the only rural School District around that was advocating for one-to-one devices in the classroom. Since then, every student has a one-to-one device and more and more classrooms are being updated to the newest technology available. The teachers are kind and caring as well. They will bend over backwards for parents and students. I came here because of the small town atmosphere. It's so refreshing! Even though Athens is smaller, they are consistently moving forward. The sports here aren't bad either. The volleyball team made it to state this year, while the track team made it to state two years ago. The football team made it deep into the playoffs a few years ago, and the cross country team has really been coming on the last few seasons by consistently sending more and more athletes to state as well. Wrestling continues to dominate the mat year in and year out as well. All in all, Athens is a great place to be and a great place to raise a family. I would highly recommend Athens to anyone.

column3: While I am a graduate of this school I recently had a child that attended Powers for four years. I am very disappointed in the quality of the educators, the curriculum and the general school environment. First, the educators do not show the level of professionalism one would expect in any school. The blatant nepotism and favoritism shown to those families of influence is astounding and not expected in a school that should be promoting Christian values, excellence and achievement! While the school does tout the fact that they have many young scholars that secure noteworthy college scholarships, I do not believe that the high school has much influence in this regard. I have since sent my other children to our public high school and have been very impressed. Bottom line...save the tuition for college. I have a child at this school and have already had one graduate. According to the one that graduated, they prepare you for life. But, we have noticed favoritism fort the students with important local celebs and if your child doesn't fit that category, you may be surprised to find that the limited-numbered things, sports or extra curricular, they may get left out and it;s obvious and hurtful. With all of that said, my current student wants to remain there. So, maybe decide if your local school is beneficial for a specific student and if not, try it. Just the christian part that makes me sad. No one should be judged at a Catholic school and no one should have power because of what your family does or is. Especially in the Flint area. hahaha My spouse and I are both products of public education and we live in a great school district. That being said, I have been very impressed with the quality of education my child has been receiving. My student is challenged everyday both academically and spiritually. I particularly LOVE that the student body is both socially and ethnically diverse. While no school is perfect, I have met very few students both past and present, who did not enjoy their time at Powers. With their new campus schedule to open in the fall of 2013, I honestly could not see why anyone would not take a hard look at sending their children there. Powers Catholic is the best school in Genesee county. My daughter is now in her senior year. When my family suffered a family emergency I knew that my daughter would be looked after and knew that this school is family. Everyone from the staff to the student support her. My daughter is thriving and is growing up to be a remarkable young women. I know that she is prepared for college and is very proud to be at Powers. Love the school. All students seem to get along. Atheletics are some of the best in the state. Teachers interact well with students. It's like one big family. Best school in the area. Way over priced $8,000. A. Year I paid $3,600. For 3 months Teachers failed to assign tutorial help as a needed Great reputation as a comic. Religion teacher failed to inspire or. Educate If your child is a self starter he will do well here. Parents do your homework don't rely on reputation I'm new to. Flint area. Schools Good luck Sports are important only if Daddy pays more than your tuition. The teams are not good because the spots are held for special kids. s The other's aren't even told about tryouts, etc. It's "pull kids that are athletes from outlying schools" and let them sit the bench while the super star money people get their training and spot on the team. Huge crowd from our area Fenton, not very nice young people. They are talking about each other most of the time. Sad for a "Catholic Based" school. Our grades have been calculated wrong several times and we have had to fight for grades. You don't want to do that in High School Cruel environment. None athletic students are pariahs. Students were made to feel ashamed or inferior if "nerdy". Bulling a very serious problem. Teachers were mostly coaches who treat no sports students as misfits. Counselors never gave good college or course advice. It was as though I had been written off. Teach catholic values but what is practiced will eventually cause students to leave the faith in later years. I believe that Powers is the best school in our area. My sister Logan attended the school for high school and has gotten her opportunities that she would've never had. Logan is now in the honors program and Ferris State University and fully believes Powers has gotten her where she is today. I am now in my freshman year at Powers and thought that I would completely hate it, but it turns out I was so wrong. I can finally say, for the first time in 4 years, that I love going to school again. Our son attended public schools until entering Powers as a Freshman. The new campus is beautiful. The teachers seem to truly care about your student as a whole person academically and otherwise. The academic program opportunities and advanced classes offered are excellent. As a freshman in his public school, there was only one advanced placement class offered. At Powers the academic ability is taken into consideration and the classes offered meet the students abilities/needs. Our son loves his school and looks forward to being there every day. The students are polite and show respect to each other and to adults. We are happy at Powers and feel a definite family and community connection there. I highly reccomend Powers Catholic. School success is based more on nepotism, family financial standing in the community and ability to donate to the school. Many "wannabe's", status seekers and socialites send their kids here so that they can have a chance at being a part of the "in-crowd". As for education, I was not impressed. Arts and music program...you had better be personal friends with the Director or you'll never get a main part. Many of the teachers teach several different subjects and do not have advanced degrees. The kids that attend the school are from families that value education, and in large measure have received good elementary and junior high educations. Powers will claim credit for the success some of their kids achieve but in reality, the kids that attend already have solid educational footings. The best description of the attitude of the parents and students that attend Powers is arrogance and privileged. I would not recommend Powers to anyone. Is it a Catholic School? In a superficial way it promotes and mouths Catholicism. The bullying, nepotism and low academic standards are not what I want for my children. Check out the Advanced Placement Courses and compare the results with a few other local schools. Powers AP classes are 1 semester long whereas other schools spend a year on the same class...no comparison in the results either. Note: I work with students from Powers and other area schools and have had my own children attend and graduate from Powers and other schools. We absolutely love Powers Catholic school. We live in the neighborhood near the school and are so happy with the rigorous academic program and athletics available to our children. We are not wealthy or privileged and are just down-to-earth people who want our children's education to be faith-based. The ability to take advanced courses and earn college credit has also been a wonderful thing. We don't know a lot of people or have connections and our students have still had great success. Thank you to all of the teachers and as a parent I highly recommend! Have sent my children here for the last 7 years and it was a great decision. Education is phenomenal, snobby girls are in a class of their own and give the movie mean girls a run for it's money I graduated from Powers Catholic in 2019 and I can honestly say that it was a traumatic experience for me. Not only did it not prepare me for college in any way, but it also turned me away from religion entirely. For parents looking to send their children to an environment that embodies Christ's example, Powers Catholic is not the place. Racism, homophobia, sexism, and classism are common in the student body and are not dealt with. Bullying is not dealt with efficiently and mental health support there is a joke. Just some examples, a student said he wished there was a Holocaust for gay people in front of the assistant principal and nothing was done about it. Said student served as an altar server for the school. Regardless of your views on homosexuality, race, and other religions, Jesus would clearly not tolerate hate such as this. Sexual harassment/nudes/etc are also an extreme issue within the student body, and victims do not feel comfortable coming forward as victim blaming is rampant. A friend of mine came forward about someone repetitively harassing her and asking her for nudes and she was blamed for it. My freshman year alone-I was 14-I had at least 7 different male students either ask for nudes or send unsolicited. While this is an issue at any high school, the school's response of "just don't send nudes" and abstinence is a joke. If you're a current future student there, do not bother going to guidance counselors for mental health help. I do recommend going to Father Jim though, he's a wonderful man who genuinely cares about the students and their overall wellbeing. Powers does have some great teachers, however, they are overshadowed by the school's main focus of money. As an overachieving student who took both dual enrollment classes and as many AP classes as I could, I still did not feel remotely prepared for college. It is common that material is spoonfed to students in order to raise overall grades regardless of mastery of material. I would have received a far more challenging education from my local public high school. The one good thing I can say about Powers is the requirement of public service. I really felt I gained a lot through completing this. Overall, I cannot in good faith recommend this school to anyone. According to current Powers students, the school has gone downhill since I graduated and it would not surprise me if it continues to do so. You are better off sending your child to public school.

Academically, the children are challenged with a variety of material. They offer many different diploma paths. However, they (school officials) are selective in who they help and how available they are. They greatly favor the more affluent portion of the student population. We have 2 NHS graduates and a couple that are close to graduation, in all that time the children and I can only count a handful of exceptional educators. Most fall woefully below that description. We had three sons graduate from NHS in the past and the waist of books and materials was shameful. Several workbooks they did not even use still new at the end of year what a waist of parents money on book rental. I was a student at Northridge up until last year. The teachers play favorites, the principals discipline people for no reason just to fill a quota of students punished. The bullying is horrible and the teachers just stand there and watch. The drug problem is way out of hand. My experience with the school was awful from Middle School and the High School. I find it odd some of the post on here. Clearly by people who wanted everything handed to them. I went to NHS and attended Middlebury Schools from 3rd grade on. I had a parent who worked for the school system. The teachers do their best for each and every student who wants to do something. If a child doesn't want to succeed then they aren't going to fight them on it. They will still make the effort and make themselves available, but it is up to the student to make the decision to succeed as it is in any school. Teachers don't play favorites they simply pay more attention to those actively seeking more attention. Yes of coarse there are drugs in the school, there are in every school in the United States, but they aren't visible unless you seek them out. Administration to single anyone out either; if you catch the attention of the Principal in a negative way it is because you were doing something wrong no other reason. If you had a bad experience as a student or parent it is because you wanted the bad experience because you like to complain. If you had a good experience it is because you sought out the things you needed to succeed like those who want to have success will. Northridge was great and I'm glad I went there and wish other schools were like NHS because we could use a school that from the top to the bottom tries as hard as the administration and staff do at NHS where I'm at now. Overall I would recommend NHS. All 3 of my children knew there were drugs in the school ( rampant in our local factories) they could easily avoid that crowd and choose a path to success. The sense of community and predominantly conservative values is everywhere. There is strong support for constant improvement in academics, trade skills and life skills. There are so many opportunities for involvement if the student/parent chooses to put forth some effort. There is a focus on excellence and achievement by working hard, many times taking average abilities and through hard work, achieving above average results. The school reflects the community: hard working, involved, civic minded, achievement oriented, predominantly middle class. Terrible, and I will be happy to remove my child from this school This school from the K all the way to highschool has major issues despite Covid. There are multiple parents who can’t control the drug issues in the area bit yes it’s a huge problem. They have a new superintendent so that’s promising?…but many parents wants consistency and change. We’re unsure what the future holds therefore considering relocating where levels are above 7 all around. Middlebury prides themselves with the test scores and the academics, but fails with bully prevention, bus system issues, and the expectations of the students are stressful and unrealistic given their ages. To their defense, the academics probably are better rated but only till you reach the high school level. Certain schools are better than others and same with the middle/intermediate. You can not transfer from school to school you must go within your zipcode even though the schools are literally less than 5 min apart. It’s been known in the area that kids at Orchard view thrive but other students at other elementary’s do not. Check out the ratings per school and the wide ranges will prove this. Heritage is also a school with several of the same issues. Teachers are hit or miss like any school, but there has been a lot of turnover and teachers leaving as of lately. If you want to solely focus on academics and do not care what else your child might encounter here then this school is for you, but if you feel your child might not thrive due to the issues mentioned here and reviews from below then steer a different way. If your child doesn’t “fit in” they are severely bullied. Several parents have been relocating their children since 2020 to schools that are either private, Goshen, Edwardsburg, or Concord. We wish this school would out as much emphasis on bigger issues than just academics. These issues DO affect academics and that’s why if this school doesn’t make serious changes these ratings will continue to fall. A successful school should try to focus on all these issues not just test scores. We wish we would have done our research before relocating.

column3: Wilson was named School Of The Year in 2012 by the Hispanic Scholarship Fund for sending so many students to prestigious Universities. Also in 2012, Wilson was accepted into the International Baccalaureate network of schools. In the years I ve been at Wilson, the school has totally turned around. Wilson s Law Magnet program continues to send its graduates to Ivy League universities like Harvard and Stanford. And Wilson s AVID program is so successful that it has become an AVID Demonstration School. Wilson has become such a great place. I started Wilson this year and honestly, the teachers here are great, but the classes aren't as challenging as I expected it to be. Wilson's campus is large and clean, but does need improvement in certain areas. This school could drastically improve if the students cared about test scores and grades. Not only that, but I feel as if there isn't much school spirit when there should be. When students care about their school, they will care about its reputation and will improve their scores, boost their sporting skills, and be involved in school activities and clubs. Now the worse things about Wilson High are its policies. For example, Wilson's attendance policy isn't strict enough. When I came to school late with a note, one of the attendants looked at me as if I were crazy and told me to just go straight to class; I couldn't believe it. I really do think this school could be one of the best, but these few, major flaws really bring Wilson down. Wilson USED to be a great school, before budget cuts that is. THE TEACHERS are not that great. Some are good, and some don't care what the students learn. There are probably only 4 for 5 good teachers out of 10. But it all depends on your SLC (Small Learning Community). Different SLC's have different types of teachers. THE STUDENTS are all different. There can be mean people and there can be really nice people. Depending on your SLC, you can become friends with people who are very intelligent and nice and are going to college, and then there students who are very ignorant and don't plan to go to college or do anything else with their lives. THE FOOD is horrible! Bring your own lunch unless you want to be eating microwaved food that tastes like cardboard. Because of budget cuts, i dont blame them. THE CAMPUS can be nice at times when it is clean. There is graffiti in some places and carved tagging on just about every desk. The school is very big and is filled with different buildings and massive stairs. THE BATHROOMS never have toilet paper nor soap. The soap smells horrible, so bring your hand sanitizer. There are few people who just hang out in the restrooms which is NASTY! My son attends and enrolled in the fire magnet program. Excellent Inovative ways to help children adjust to ability to absorb and learn valuable knowledge and life skills. School seems like it’s on a good growing path to be better by each year Woodrow Wilson High School is located on a hill that oversees the entirety of El Sereno. It provides students with great access to a variety of sports or opportunities to explore nature. However, since graduating, I have witnessed the school's lack of leadership and support for students become worse and worse. The school seems as though it is a built like a daycare and caters to the lowest common denominator. The administration is only concerned with statistics such as graduation rate and state test scores. There's little to no focus on college prep at all. As a college graduate who graduated from Wilson, I struggled in most of my college classes because Wilson teachers simply did not teach us nor prepare us for rigorous college courses. Wilson high school graduates who are entering college right now should be prepared to have the mentality that they need to go the extra mile just to be at the average of their college. I had a mixed experience at Wilson HS, mostly skewed toward the negative side. Although I had and am beyond grateful for the teachers who gave me support and guidance to pursue my goals, a majority of the teachers I had were incompetent and sometimes downright disrespectful. Some teachers did not follow the class curriculum and gave us useless assignments to avoid having to actually do their jobs educating us. When asked by one of my english teachers what I wanted to do after high school, I told her I wanted to pursue medicine. She didn't even try to cover up the look of doubt on her face when I said that to her. I felt insulted and that she had no faith in me to achieve anything with my life. This is just one example of the indifference I felt from most of the teachers and staff at Wilson. It felt like their passion to educate the next generation had died, and they were just showing up and going through the motions to collect a paycheck.

column1: An amazing school. My daughter attends now. She loves this school! My daughter loves this school so much and she lives her teachers. She is challenged while stlill keeping up her A grades. As a current student at foothills i am not prepared for anything regarding college. This school is horrible. The school counselor doesn't even give you the classes you ask for. There isn't enough teachers to make the class schedule consistent. Last year as a junior i didn't have a first period and then i had to TA (teachers assistant) another period which made my day longer and also made it so i had two periods of wasting my time. The whole dress code is based on favorites. Some girls can wear whatever they want while the same day another girl is wearing a similar thing and she gets into trouble. From freshmen year to now my senior year i have probably seen ten teachers not even knowing how to teach the class they were hired to teach. The school is out of date and depressing. Cock roaches and various other bugs creep through the halls. Kids deface school property on a regular basis. If you are looking for a safe drug free environment for your kid don't even bother, because the kids that get kicked out of other schools for drugs and fighting all get accepted here. I was once told by the Vice principal that i don't love jesus because i had four tardies. Foothills School for Failure. The first bad review from a student is farther from the truth . This school fully prepared my kids for college and really grounded then with integrity and responsibility. They are also very strong in their faith and love for God because of the bibilical teaching their. As a parent I would highly recommend this highschool. Great sports program too. I teach college science and have known some of the teachers at Foothills Christian High School for over 10 years When my sons were having academic struggles at public high school, I enrolled them in FCHS. I noticed immediately an improved attitude toward academics. My sons are also making better peer choices. Furthermore, I am noticing their public statement of faith. As a parent, I am able to see almost immediately when homework assignments are not completed through online grading that is easy to use. Betty Goodman is guidence councelor and a strong leader who challenges my sons. Chapel on Tuesday is good. It is hard to fully appreciate my older teens as they go through these difficult years. However, I notice they are developing critical thinking skills, synthetic abilities concerning world views, and interests that may lead them into careers. For improvement of my sons' attitude toward academics, I rate FCHS very high. My daughter has been a student at FCHS for three years. We are very pleased with the choice we made. The School is very welcoming and supportive to all . She has grown Spiritually and academically and knows she is cared for. We are confident that when she graduates next year she will be well prepared for college. FCHS is a wonderful school, great staff and students. my daughter was having issues with doing her work and had poor attitude.they worked with us and she is doing well.

column3: a broad range of academic levels to accomodate every student's needs. my daughter has since graduated from The Morgan School and gone onto a private college with high academic standards. within the college student body, she and other Morgan grads were better prepared for college work incl. writing than students who had come from expensive private Prep-schools. The students in the Clinton school system really are offered an excellent education. Morgan is a great school - my son is a senior there and got into his 1st choice (very competitive) school. I feel he is well-prepared for college (at least academically!). The school could do more for the students in the middle, but they are headed in the right direction under the current administration. Looking forward to a new Morgan School building in 2016. The School system in Clinton, to my family, is simply the best! When my two kids started Kindergarten they have had extraordinary teachers that have set the path for them to focus and be self motivators. Both kids are on the honor roll and continue to strive for their very best. I say thank you to all the teachers that have taught my children. I am a Morgan graduate and currently have one child at Morgan. Since attending Morgan, my child has felt extremely comfortable, and welcomed and inspired by the school's teachers. I am impressed with the number of young, passionate and energetic teachers at the high school, many of whom are local. I was also pleasantly surprised with how many clubs are offered at the school, to meet the varying interests of all students. "We are Morgan" is clearly a theme that has been warmly embraced by the student body, teachers and adminstration, bringing back "Morgan Husky Pride". I suspect that the new state of the art high school, opening in the fall of 2016, will only strengthen that pride and increase morale! My child's courses are extremely challenging and I have no doubt his academic experience at this school will prepare him well for college. Kudos to the administration for hiring additional guidance counselors and creating Grade 9/10 & 11/12 academies to focus on the transition in and out of high school to best prepare their students. The NEW Morgan School opened in Clinton in September of 2016. This new state of the art facility provides one of the nicest learning environments for our students in the state of CT. The rooms are set up in a way to foster collaboration amongst students and teachers. Floor to ceiling windows let welcome natural light into all of the classrooms. There is not a bad seat in the gorgeous auditorium. The school looks and feels like a true campus. All of our high school students are also provided with Chrome books, and technology has significantly improved. According to my son, overall morale has improved since they have moved into this new learning facility. My son is taking challenging courses, Honors and AP classes, as well as College Prep courses. His teachers and administration genuinely care about the students. Students often lead and assist with school orientations and open houses, etc. There are also clubs for just about every activity and hobby one can think of. Sports are also popular, and have increased school spirit. This is an alright school. Some of the teachers are cool but the assistant principal, Mr. webb is not. He used to search me almost every week and then when he would never find anything on my he stopped. I thought it was because he knew I wasn’t doinf anything bad but then he just started calling my mom and telling her that I’m vaping in the bathroom so he a bitch

column1: .I am a student at Rock Creek. Rock Creek Requires an Exit Project. This Project ruins the experience at the school for the last two years, as of which, i now find myself worrying more about a project, then what comes after the project, my friends, or my family. The school itself is possibly one of the best learning environments i as a student have been in. But the Exit Project ruins this almost great school. This is NOT a good school for your children, especially if they are special needs children. I have nothing good to say about this school. Students are often ignored and when a problem arises that makes the school look bad, the school covers it up to save its hide. Special needs kids are often mistreated and bullied with no consequences going towards the bullies. This district will also do anything to make itself look good, even at the expense of the students. Do not bring your children here. The teachers do not care about your children or their education. This school district puts education first! I graduated from Rock Creek in 2013 and could not have picked a better school to attend! I attended schooling in this district since Kindergarten. I loved the small atmosphere and we truly are a mustang family from K-12. I have a great deal of pride for my alma mater and I am extremely disappointed by the negative comments. My Exit Project has helped me so much in my college preparation and in life! It can truly be a wonderful experience if it is done correctly and honestly without trying to cut corners. The only reason the Exit Project keeps students from graduating is if they try to plagiarize or cut corners in some other way. Some students learn this lesson of life the hard way but they are not going to get away with cutting corners in the real world! Of course there are subjects that need to be improved on, as is there in every single school in America! All around, Rock Creek has a wonderful learning environment and is dedicated to providing a quality education for its students! I would HIGHLY recommend this district to anyone in the area without a doubt! This school is wonderful for students who enjoy school and for those who feel rewarded by receiving good grades. For those who dislike school it is terrible. It's easy to be a "good teacher" to those who want to learn; the challenge should be to help those who don't want to learn. Furthermore, the Senior Exit Project is set up the same way. For those who "care" about their grades it is fine. There is a small percentage of students who truly get lost in the system. Rock Creek is good at college preparation. However, we must recognize that not everyone wants to attend college and, guess what? This is okay! The school needs to have a secondary path so the students who aren't interested in furthering their education can learn real life skills. Also, there are some teachers who simply teach so they can coach (history) and others who are just rude (art). A specific English teacher (who has no children of her own) is one of the worst at realizing that not everyone has the same definition of success or the same goals in life. Unfortunately, this same teacher is highly involved with the Exit Project and will literally set a student up for failure if she dislikes him or her.Rock Creek would be a much better school if the faculty would teach individuals instead of trying to force their ways upon students. Not everyone learns the same!!
