column3: I am the mother of a special needs student. He attends some resource classes and some regular ed classes. The school is very willing to help choose the best types of classes for your student. They treat each special needs child as an individual. The school nurses are phenomenal and are so helpful. The special ed administrators are also great. All the teachers have worked so willingly with my child. I am very impressed. This has been a great choice for my special ed child. I am the parent of 2 children that have graduated from WHS and a third that is currently a junior in the Westside Engineering Geosciences Academy. The 2 older children were very well prepared for college, one having graduated with a degree in education and the other with a masters in finance. If a child is willing to work, an excellent and diverse education is available from WHS. Both of my sons attended 4 years and graduated from Westside and are now succesful in college. The dean system is excellent and really makes the difference. The new principal, Ms. Stewart, provides strong leadership and draws on her time at WHS as a dean and from her continued focus on the best developments in education. Students are expected to excell and there are plenty of academic opportunities. The list of colleges attended by WHS students is impressive. All students have an opportunity to find areas of interest to them through courses, clubs, fine arts and sports. The campus is modern and safety is a priority. School spirit is strong and the staff believe in Westside -- check it out for yourself! I have found excellent teachers and some really poor ones. In particular, one particular language department head displayed some pretty questionable ethics in the past. The school principal at the time (no longer there) whose name is actually mentioned in some of the reviews, circled the wagons and ran defense for her when she was clearly lying and covering up her poor judgment and behavior. The good teachers often don't stay and the bad ones hang on to their lifeboat/paycheck. Teacher accountability has always been a problem there. Having said that, this is probably one of the better high schools in the district. Love this school. Very well organized, keeps parents very well informed with weekly newsletters and phone calls. Many workshops to assist parents in helping their children plan their academic future. The Deans of every House are very hands off and accessible and the teachers are engaged and communicate and offer tutorials and take the time to contact parents know where they see the need for additional help. how do you switch schools that are assigned to your address or area?? hard to find greats schools w/o going outside the loop. He is not an athletic person but he has joined football. The player took him in like he has been there for year. Great group of kids as for the coaches they are also amazing. They talk to me and give me all the information I need and ask for. I had my doubts about this school but I was wrong. Dont always believe what you are told. Like over 200 wild styled wheels, in giant sizes. You couldn't buy such a thing, but the cars I designed needed that touch.. so, a 22" rim X 10" wide, and a 4" tire profile, was stock. The good students transfer out of there. And the bad students quit. The girls who's parent's are from Mexico are to busy watching there siblings rather than going to school. column3: The school is more of a prison than a school. There have been some incidents in the past 6 years, and now the school assumes that each student is like the one that caused the trouble. Too much security to feel like you're in a school. There are "random searches" where security officers will randomly pick students walking into school and make them walk through metal detectors, they'll wand them, and make them remove their backpacks so that they can pass them through the machine with the belt that scans/x-rays to see if there are any threats, just like at the airport. Also, students are not allowed to carry drinks with them because the school fears that they are carrying alcohol. If they carry coffee mugs to school the school directors will be waiting at the front of the school where they confiscate it and throw it out in the large trash bin next to them. There are some good teachers that care, but as you can see, there are some major trust issues between the directors and the students. Teachers and administrators are amazing! The students and staff take pride in their school and community. This school like every other school does have some flaws. I have 3 children in this school and could not be happier with the education they are receiving. My children are involved in sports and a few of the many after school activities they offer. I feel if your not happy with this school then maybe you need to experience everything they have to offer not just be there to hang out with friends because your missing some great opportunities. I am a parent and my daughter is now going in to 7th grade. She has had nothing but excellent experiences with her teachers since Kindergarten. Her teachers take a genuine interest in the children and foster exposure to many opportunities outside the classroom as well. Great school district that continues to keep current with changing technology providing a quality education in a safe and caring environment.

column1: Mr. Paul Anderson is the reason that I work at Ware Shoals High School. He is a teacher's principal and supports us in every way. He does a remarkable job with the limited resources that he is proved by the state. Congratulations Mr. Anderson for a job well done and thank you for your continued hard work. We appreciate you. You want to go to a good school......PLEASE don't come to Ware Shoals High School. I thought when I got to Ware shoals High, I was going to have a good time making friends and befriending teachers. I had the making friends parts down but this staff is something else. All they do is pick favorite students and then they pretty much ignore rest and don't even get me started on the principle Mr. Paul Anderson. He is a terrible principle and i not just saying that because I am a student and no student likes school. I'm saying it because he never punish the people he likes and he all has something smart to say to students even though we try and talk to him like a normal person. I have never seen a bad principle till I step through the doors Ware Shoals High School and seen Mr. Paul Anderson. he doesn't care about the safety of his students. just last year, two young males was about to fight out side in front of the school just as school was letting out and I sat there and told him they were and all he did was nothing. Then when they starting fighting, he just stood their for like 30 seconds. Then he walked over their so lazy like. So.. PLEASE don't bring your child here, they don't care I recently left this school in 2017 because of medical complications, however, I may speak from experience that this is a terrible school. Education quality aside, as the teachers can be a mixed bag between wonderful and insufferable, the building itself is likely dangerous to students and staff health. The building is nearing 100 years of age while lacking needed renovations to remove and replace rusted out pipes which taint the water with rust (if you entered the building on any day before the students arrive and run the water in any sink or toilet, it will come out opaque and dark orange with rust, and is always tinted orange after being run for a while), as well as exposed pipes that are within arms' reach,wrapped in something I can only hope is not asbestos insulation but may be due to the building's age. There is a hallway in which the ceiling is far lower than usual, where even I at 4'11'' can touch them above my head. These pipes are present throughout the entire building however. Regardless of poor funding or poor fund management, I am concerned for the health of the attendees of the school, students as well as staff, and am quite frankly baffled at how the school has not been shut down for various health and safety hazards. 0...worst experience ever. column1: i am currently a student at pioneer high school and i can't express how glad and grateful i am to attend phs. the school has a myriad of activities, a great and dedicated administration and great programs. i am involved in ASB, several AP courses and various clubs. ASB recently won the outstanding activites program award, making our asb one of the greatest in california. our school has undergone many changes, modernization of the campus, and there have been ZERO fights this school year. the school is great,despite the negative connotations, and it still has more to offer. our athletic teams are also improving and many have made CIF this year. what can i say, i would NOT move to another school in the district. besides, phs is a young and thriving school, and as we enter the 50th year anniversary,we can be sure that phs will have a long, lasting legacy. I attended here in the late 80s when this site wasn't around. What made this great was the friends I made and still keep. Some of the teachers are really good. However, some of them when I was there didn't know what they were doing, in particular the teacher who taught Math Analysis. I guess due to funding they couldn't get a proper teacher and had to use one who taught PE. I found out later that they also lacked faith in my ability to succeed, the Calculus teacher wrote in my yearbook my senior year that the faculty didn't think I could get better than a C. But the calculus teacher at that time was so awesome that I not only got an A in that class, I got a 5 on the AP exam! It just goes to show what students can do when they have excellent teachers. She believed in me even though other faculty still did not, and awarded the Math award at the end of the year to another student, although an excellent one, did not do as well as I did. I am a Sophomore here at Pioneer and I cannot express how Pioneer High School is an amazing school. People see it as "ghetto" school, but I don't see anything wrong with it. Teachers are phenomenal, counselors are so academically involved in what you do, and we have the administration who greets us everyday at the gate. I have been to to other schools and they don't do that at all. Being the smallest school in the Whittier Union High School District we are very family based, once you step foot in campus you feel that home feel. Pioneer shapes you to be better and work hard! We are striving for success everyday. We have one of the BEST math departments in the district where we challenge students to discover what their strengths are and use them to their advantage. If you are debating on sending your son/ daughter here don't stress about it, Pioneer will be the best choice you have ever made. After all the negative rumors I heard about Pioneer, I was hesitate to send my daughter to this school. However, I am so glad I did. The staff at Pioneer are friendly and the teachers care about the students. My daughter is a Junior now and has been very successful due to the after school tutoring and interventions this school has in place to help your child succeed. The student population is lower than the other schools in the district and I feel that it benefits the students. The teachers and staff know the students by name which helps most of them stay out of trouble. My daughter has made wonderful friends. It is a safe and wonderful learning environment and I could not be happier. Transferring from other schools Pioneer really is one of the best high schools. This is because the teachers are amazing by actual teaching the kids the subjects with excellent methods. As well as an excellent school safe environment for students. After all that if you’re a kid or have kids who want to make friends or have trouble making friends I guarantee if you/they join a sport they’ll have several.

My only concern now is the increasing number of students from the Memphis City Schools that come and distract those who come to school for an education, but outside of some of the "Distractors" I believe Horn Lake High School is still one of the most respectable schools in the area, and a place where your child will be prepared for college, or any other career path they pursue. column3: My school is one of the best public schools in Iowa to attend. We have an amazing teaching staff that cares about every student and want everyone to succeed. They go out of their way to do so. I like everything about my school! The staff, the sports, the programs, and the school itself! We have 1 to 1 laptops and they contribute greatly to learning here. There is really no way it could improve! This public school is awesome to go to! As a graduate of Pella Community High School, I felt challenged and supported during my high school experience. The transition to college (4-year state university, honors program) was an easy one: Many of my high school classes were more difficult than a majority of my college courses. There were many excellent extracurricular opportunities available in sports, music, art, drama, academia and more. It is easy to get involved, and the programs are very competitive with other schools (jazz and marching band, basketball, football, soccer and drill team are some of the best 3A in the state). The community is also extremely supportive of the schools, and a majority of teachers are very passionate about students and the subjects they teach. Responsibility and values are also strongly emphasized throughout the district, as is parental involvement. Classes are around 200, large enough to have choices in friends but small enough that you know your classmates. I'm not sure why Pella High has a less-than-stellar rating on this site, considering they are recognized around the state as being one of the best schools around. I've moved about ten times as a kid - I could tell that some communities were nicer than others. Interestingly enough, when returning to former communities, this one made previous places - even the nicer ones - look pretty trashy. The school mostly reflects the community atmosphere as a whole. The staff is pretty great at this school - I was very frequently pleased with my teachers, and the guidance office is very open to communicating with students. Course levels are pretty reasonable. Teachers are generally knowledgeable - I would say that the STEM classes are just a little lacking compared to a few schools in my experience, but students seem to succeed and grow well enough.This school has a pretty wide range of opportunities for its small size. There are plenty of classes that appeal to upperclassmen preparing for undergraduate or trade schools (from farming to engineering). The school made it pretty easy for me to take a lot of electives during each semester. Electives seem to be the school's specialty. Athletics seemed really successful. I mainly focused on music. The orchestra is a little small and not very competitive in comparison to the band and choir, but most kids will find challenge (without feeling like they're drowning). Teachers here really pushed me to my limits with my best interests in mind. They spend way more time to teach than what they get paid for. My band teacher pulled me out of a math class once just to talk to me in his office to make sure that I was doing okay.The school's more diverse than it might seem. Most kids were friendly - you get some weirdos and knuckleheads, but that's just life on earth. This is one of the best schools for kids who follow dress code, don't steal misplaced phones, welcome new students, etc. Most forms of bullying are pretty stinkin' rare. My main complaint is that the cliques are strong here - students are generally outgoing and respectful, but the small town life means that most kids knew each other since 1st grade, so it's hard to be new. I was mostly a nomad in the cafeteria, but I made friends here and there, and I knew just about everyone in the school as friendly. That tightly-knit feel can be weird, so your first impression to a small group will affect the rest of high school... But trouble won't really be part of your experience unless you look for it. This is as clean, safe, and opportunity-rich as it gets, and my only other complaint is that many of the students may not realize it.

column1: I went there for a year and a half. The school was a living hell. If you don't go there from Kindergarten up people isolate you and you become a freak. The people are like something out of Wrong Way by Stephen King. I go to Burnt Hills HS now and am much happier. Galway is a great school!! I have since graduated and I realize what a good place it is. Unlike the other reviews say, new students are not isolated. We have plenty of students who are always willing to help make other people comfortable, and we are not an all white, Christian school. The majority is caucasian, but we are accepting, and the school teaches tolerance and expects all students to treat each other the same. You cannot help your demographics!! Students from all walks of life make it to Galway, and every kind of student is accepted. The teachers are fantastic, and although some are tough, there is always available help. Don't listen to other people who say their kids only went for a year, they haven't experienced what Galway is about. I graduted from this school many moons ago. I hasn't grown at all since the 20+ years ago I was here. I actually has declined in enrollment. My kids now go here and I am really not happy with the future I see for the school. They offer the bare minium in acdemics and they only offer varisity sports. There is a booster club that tries to support the modified and JV programs. My daughter has lost over 20% of her classmates moving to other districts, private schools or home schooling. I understand with the economy times are tough but they need to stop patching a sinking ship and move on for the sake of the kids. They need more. We chose Galway and we would do it again. Our boys entered the district in the Middle School and immediately became involved in drama, sports, Odyssey of the Mind and other extracurricular activities that allowed them to develop a sense of pride, self confidence while being part of the community. In many rural areas, the school is a big part of the community and that is true for Galway. Our boys immediately became part of the community. Over the course of the years, we are thrilled that Galway has been able to balance the improvements with not just developing a solid budget that has allowed for increasing academic offerings and standards, but developing a culture of expecting more from our students, our teachers, our administrations, our parents and our community. Once again, we chose Galway and we would choose it again! Galway has many of the opportunities of a large school district and all the benefits of a small district. There have been many positive changes over the past few years. The buildings and grounds have been, and still are being, updated and improved. The community groups are amazingly supportive of the students.

column3: This school has a great engineering program allowing you to take college level courses and earn credit for upper level engineering courses through the PLTW program. They have an excellent athletics program and outstanding support from the parents and community. I appreciate that people value education and challenge students to think of a world outside their immediate surroundings. I love the increasing diversity at this school because we can learn so much from one another. It is such a benefit to the community to have this because it makes the area more desirable to live when the schools are strong. Thus, I am grateful for LHS. The teachers are nice and the test scores are good and all, but the kids are vicious (yes, more so than at other schools) and the administration does nothing to stop it. This school is so awful, my other child will not attend, even though it's our home school. We will either home school or she will attend a magnet school for her talents. My older child, who was taunted and excluded here, transferred to another high school. It's unfortunate because the building is attractive. Too bad that the people inside are anything but. awful in all aspects. admin have no clue what they’re doing, frederick county as a whole sucks.

column1: It teaches religious values besides academic skills. My son loved going to school every single day because he felt welcomed and loved by everyone.Excellent High School which I highly recommend.The academics are just as great as the sports.You get two for the price of one.The security is the best too.Home cooked meals for breakfast,lunch and dinner.I was so proud of my son on my way to his first basketball game it actually brought a tear to my eye because I knew this is where he was meant to be.We will always love and miss St.Benedict's Prep which was a High School I was so proud to say my son went to for two years.If he ever changes his mind and wants to go back we will go in a heartbeat.He just missed being away from his friends but now regrets he didin't stay.Now he realizes everyone at St.Ben's are his best friends forever. Thank you so much for giving my son such an excellent experience in High School which are really the best days of our lives. I can honestly say he had so much fun!!! One of the best schools and environments you could possibly hope to provide to your son. I had one who graduated in 2010 and a current student scheduled to grauduate in 2016. You can't beat the academc and overall spiritual value no matter your religion. St Benedict's prep is a great school excellent sport nice campus in the middle of the city. We'll known over the world and the country as far as sports number 1 school in the nation in overall soccer especially in wrestling basketball track and with out doubt soccer. Also the values of all races in one school working togther getting along and last year 99.8 percent of the senior class went To colleg. Also ephamsizes real world problems the boys will face one day a great school. And I swear to you guys number 1 school in the nation I cannot say enough good things about St. Benedict's. (My son is part of the class of 2016.) While their academic program is lacking in terms of technology, they more than make up for that in teaching young men to think for themselves. They take these boys from boyhood to manhood and teach them not only to respect others, but themselves. There is a real brotherhood at the school that is palpable and the boys take care of each other. I love that the students are all required to put in "sweat equity". Teenagers need an outlet for all their energy and they have that opportunity via sports. They also are able to express themselves via the drama guild and other creative outlets. This is a very well rounded education and the teachers give above and beyond to their students. The headmaster is a tough, no-nonsense man, but full of genuine love and caring for his students. This is an environment that fosters the growth of leadership, responsibility and compassion. My son was very shy and now is someone that speaks up for himself. Thank you, St. Benedict's! I'm a current senior and there is no place like St.Benedict's Prep. Just look at it's illustrious history and their will be no doubt that this is a very special place. For an inner city school St.Benedict's is an incredible institution besides the fact that it is located in one of America's most impoverished cities. The fact that it is in the center of Newark,NJ says a lot if you know anything about Newark's history. St.Benedict's really thought me to take advantage of all the opportunities and whether you take advantage freshman year or senior year every student learns to be a contributor for the betterment of society. It is one of the most diverse institutions in the world and it has been an amazing experience learning from people from around the world. This experience was great because this school has a great academic record an de has an awesome athletics team.

column3: As a parent of a second child attending charter tech, it is an all around good school for those who are interested in what charter tech is, for students that wanna attend for vocals, musical theatre instrumental etc, i disagree with charter tech offering basic academy, the basic academy is for those who do not wanna attend their district high school. And its not fair to the students that are serious about why they are attending.because they create distractions at showcases. I was just at the vocal showcase, my daughter majors in vocals, anyway a group of students that sat in the front row & second row were asked to behave professionally by one of the vocal teachers. They were anything but behaved, a poor elderly woman had to ask the bunch two times to please keep it down, they carried on as if no one asked anything. My daughter is a freshman my son graduated 2 years ago, this freshman year has been anythig but a great experience her first year, i hope next year sophomore year is better for her, shes already passed the test to move to intermediate, she was challenged to take theb test to move to the next level. I just hope for her sake, she ends up with better class mates next year. New AP Program is great! The Artistic Majors such as Instrumental, Vocal, Performing Arts, Film and animation are excellent and the opportunities to perform during the year through showcases is fantastic. There are many dedicated teachers and support staff that go well beyond the call of duty to help the students in academic, artisitc and personal growth. The students can not just leave the school or wander the halls. The staff keeps a close eye on the whereabouts of their students and the hallway is very quiet and clear during classes. Students go directly to their classes when the bell rings and must have a hall pass to go somewhere during class time. Besides AP classes they have honors and College Prep classes. Their are clubs and your student can participate in group sports in your sending districts high school. They have recording studios, 3 pianos, a film area, computers for all the students and a dance studio as well for the dance majors. They also have Art classes that are excellent. If your kids are interested in the Arts and want to have creativity plus academics- Ap classes and honors classes for those that aspire to college, then this school is a great choice. As a parent, my child and I had an absolutely, positively excellent experience. Five stars - My daughter loves this school. This year she was in all regular courses because of the transition to public school from homeschooling and I wish I had enrolled her in honors courses because of how well she has done, even with a considerable amount of home life stressors this year. This school offers 3 levels of academics - regular, honors, and AP. The performing arts aspect of the school is amazing. The kids are taught professionalism and the basics of what they will need for a career in their particular major, as well as given opportunities to explore different areas of that career with performances and displays of their work. This school has been nothing but positive, even when the teachers emailed me about possible failing grades they were positive that we could work together to bring those grades up. I like the upbeat positivity of the staff that translates to the students. I have found staff very easy to work with when necessary, and quick to find work arounds when we encountered roadblocks. I like this school quite a bit and would not hesitate to send any of our other children here if they were interested in performing arts. Do NOT, I repeat DO NOT send your child to this school. They do not handle harassment and bullying in a proper way and will blame the victim. I am going into sophmore year at this school and for the most part I love it. The teachers are so nice and if you you don’t go into to drama you mostly stay out of it. The fights aren’t handled the best but idk lol. I overall really like this school and as a film major loooove the film programs.

column3: This school is way to strict with it's dress code. I get it's for the safety of the students but they push it to much. It sucks going to a school everyday thinking your going to get in trouble for your jeans having a tiny hole in them or your hair a centimeter below your eyebrows little stuff like that. Overall tho the school safety is good, and a few teachers care about the students. Clovis East has beautifully kept grounds and is one of the only schools in Clovis with a complete agricultural farm on campus. Academics are priority and students are given the resources necessary to excel. Teachers are great with parent communication and availability. Student dress-code and campus rules are strictly enforced and (in my opinion) overly so. Safety issues are one thing and certainly encouraged, however I have received phone calls for such concerns as hugs. Strange, indeed. Not to my expectations. A couple of my kid's teachers don't teach. If you care about your child's education, this is not the school for your child. Counselors don't help you or the student. They're always out of their office when my kid goes to see them. Horrible...will not be continuing with my other kids. As a former student, I miss East so much. I was at Clovis East for 3 years and while it does have its ups and downs, it is a lot better than my current school. The dress code is strict but for the good of the students. 80% of my teachers were amazing. It is always up to the student to put in the work and if you don't do it, you will obviously fail. The teachers give you what you need and then it's all up to you. The campus is beautiful and you can find friends in all corners. While there are always bad parts like in any school, I believe that this was a great school to attend. I'm a student and let me tell you this school may look nice on the outside but it's pretty bad on the inside. Many teachers don't teach very well if at all. Teachers definitely play favorites. This school has many cliques so its VERY hard socially if you're a new kid like I was sophomore year. The reason I didn't give it one star is because it looks nice and they seems to keep it fairly clean. Clovis East and Reyburn are excellent schools. My son has had excellent experiences at both. The school experience there is what you make of it. My son has made wonderful friends and enjoys the many programs C.E. offers. The teachers there are VERY DEDICATED! They work hard building successful students. Mr. Sandoval and all of the administrators are caring and compassionate and truly want to do what is best for the the students there. I wouldn't have my son attend anywhere else. Both of my sons graduated from CEHS. Both also graduated from Portland State University and immediately got jobs. One recently started his PhD in Biomedicine. He was one of 15 students out of 800 to be selected for this program. The other pursued his interest in finances and has a job he loves. This should speak volumes for the preparation they had at Clovis East. While no school is perfect and there are many other factors that contribute to how the children will turn out, I am proud of them. CEHS is a solid school with dedicated teachers who make a difference in your children's lives. This school gives soo much homework that it takes 7 days to finish but the teachers five us 2 days which stresses me out. The bullying problem is very bad I see kids get bullied almost every day.

column1: I started going to this school in kindergarten and graduated in 2011. That place is my heart and soul. When I get finished with college and get ready to settle down, I want to raise my family there! It's a wonderful place to grow up. The teachers there are amazing and always do their best to help you. That school is the reason I have been able to succeed this far. I love that place and cherish my memories there. It might be a tiny school, but it makes up for it in heart! To fully understand, experience with all five senses. Hubbertville school is a great place for students who want to network with a lot of people. The close-knit community is known for coming together during the tuff times and celebrating in the good. I attended HUB from pre-K to 12th grade.There was opportunities available for everyone, all you have to do is ask.I had some great teachers and some not so great teachers, but the not so great teachers are only there for a short period of time, because the teachers are evaluated and must meet certain standards. The school does well in keeping up and staying ahead in Technology in the classroom. For students seeking challenging courses, I recommend taking ACCESS classes. For students needing extra help, I reccommend asking someone privately, or taking advantage of announced remedial opportunities. The school has a small student to faculty ratio. The school's leadership is dedicated to equality, fairness, and helping students achieve. Parents and Students who fail to show respect will miss out. I challenge you to enrich yourself in Hubbertville and experience it with all five senses! This school is wonderful and the dispite the other negative comments my review is from someone who loved being in highschool here. The Principal, Mr. Dunavant, is actually not the problem at all. He gives each child a choice of punishment. They get to choose the first two times. If they do not benefit then he decides the punishment. For children who were taught how to behave at home this is not a problem. Unfortunatly, there are some parents who have ruined what there children could have been. On the other note, If you went to school here and werent college and career ready it is probably your own fault. The classes now are strictly ACT or career classes . This school is great . I would want my children to be able to go here. I believe if we begin teahing our children when they are small how to be a moral person in society they will act that way the rest of their lives. That is where most parents mess up:in the home. I graduated from this school and my biggest mistake was sending my kids there. If i had it to do over I would NEVER have sent them there. The faculty places way too much emphasis on sports here. Ive even heard one coach here tell some of the atheletes that they are the leaders here at Hubbertville. Which I strongly disagree. I would bet my last dollar that every positive comment left on here was from a parent of a student that played some sort of sport here or a student that played a sport. If your not into sports your simply out!! Thats all that matters here. Bullying here is out of control and despite having talked with the Principal Tim Dunavant nothing has changed. Nothing will ever change here. Very few teachers here and I mean very few are truly interested in teaching your kids. Send your kids elswhere.. Im serious. This place is a JOKE!!! Way too many ignorant people around this area. We were apprehensive about sending our children to such a small school after moving to the area a few years ago. I must say all of those worries were unfounded. Hubbertville provides an exceptional program that is grounded in such a friendly family atmosphere. My children have had a far better educational and social experience than I myself relieved in a far larger suburban school. Our family will forever be Hubbertville Lions!! I got hate crimed here and nobody did anything about it. If you have a kid of color or a kid of the LGBTQ+ community I would not recommend bringing them to this school. The education isn’t really the problem but the students are, if you want your kid to be in a safe, non-bullying zone this is not the place. Even when confronted about the bullying nothing is done about it. Went to school here. More bullying than I thought possible. And yes sports are a big problem. If you play you get treated special, yes I played, and I know the principle. Went to school with him and at one time was best friends, untill they overhaul this school and the way it is I would never let my kids go here. Better to send them to fayette or winfield. Sad to say but I waited a long time to speak out on what goes on here. And I still got the test paper where the bonus question was if any one in my class would date me given by the coach Harris at the time

column3: Woods Cross is an excellent school! It has an amazing fine arts program, and it has a good supportive administration. This is a great school that excels in almost every single department that a high school could have. This includes music, math, science, english, history, athletics, and art. What an amazing place. I am a shopmore at woods cross and I love it I think that the teachers and students there are amazing! WXHS ruels!!!!! While my child is happy at this school, I am not impressed by it. Extracurricular activities are emphasized too much, even at the expense of academic progress. The amount of time required for many extracurricular activities is also too much. It undermines my child's focus on academic progress, does not allow adequate time for homework and leaves my child constantly sleep deprived. Further, teachers and counselors alike ignore, or don't enforce, academic or citizenship standards. Students are allowed to slip though the cracks. This school has not met the needs of my child. They do not take ADHD seriously and only go through the motions of meeting the district requirements. I have found most teachers are not interested in the success of their students and want to put in the minimal amount of effort possible. The faculty is even worse. They punish students severely for very minor issues - there focus is way off. Suspending a struggling student is crazy - put them in detention (but that would require more work for the school). I have two more children and there is no way they will attend this terrible school. This school allows students to slip through the cracks. If your child has any kind of learning issues DO NOT SEND THEM TO THIS SCHOOL. Most of the teachers and staff do not follow the district accomodation plans for students with disabilities. One of the teachers actually told me - "well who doesn't have learning disabilities"! If only I could go back in time and send my student to a school that cares. Sounds like some parents here aren't taking accountability for their students actions. My kids did fine. They worked hard, were pushed by me to succeed, and did well at this school. Don't blame the teachers and school for your kid failing, being unfocused, not having time for academics. Blame yourself, and your kid. I A very Great and fun school the band and choir is amazing and the sports are very fun to be a part of, also number 8 on the utah school list by ksl Although this is a great school for music, band, and orchestra, it falls short in many other areas. It does not have structure. We lived in Murray, Utah for 18 years before moving to North Salt Lake and having two of our kids attend Woods Cross. I suppose that if your student is a good student, they will excel anywhere. But, if they have a small amount of trouble and need help with anything, don't plan on getting help from the teachers at this school! Also, the discipline is WAY TOO STRICT for such small little things - i.e., like wearing a hat AFTER school hours! I think administration needs to concentrate on structure and making sure that the kids are understanding the subjects rather than bullying the students. That's right, teachers and administration BULLY the students! Also, I don't understand why the PTA doesn't have parents get more involved in the day to day association with teachers and students. As a student, I thoroughly enjoyed my time at Woods Cross. Well-known for their academic excellence, their other accolades are nothing to scoff at either. As always, the music program goes above and beyond expectations, usually sweeping the board in state competitions. WX claims a sizable agriculture department, something that nearby high schools can't boast of. Honors and AP enrollment has reached nearly 50% of the students. Athletics have really picked up in the last couple of years. Extracurricular activities, including service opportunities are stressed. What I personally loved the most about Woods Cross were the feelings of unity, school spirit, and inclusion. Despite the wide range of economic backgrounds, it felt as if we were all treated the same, as respectable students of WX High School. It is a very disciplinary school, but still more lax than some junior highs I attended. After having also attended Bountiful High for a semester, I can attest to the superior friendliness and acceptance that the student body of WX tended to show. My only complaint would be about the smaller size of the building and the outdated style, two things Bountiful holds over Woods Cross.

column1: The Music program is great at Bonneville. The advanced choir travels throughout the United States. The Sport teams are becoming better. The English department is incredible. The Pre-Cal and Calculus classes are amazing. Depending on the teacher, the History department will make learning history fun and worth every second. There are still a few subjects that are being taught by teachers that really don't know everything that they are teaching. As a student, I saw a struggle in the foreign language and science department. The Majority of the AP classes are worth taking. The majority of the teachers will help one prepare for the AP tests; though there are a few teachers that don't have this same goal. I graduated in 2012. the music program is amazing! Mr Dresen is exceptional in every way. also mr haroldson is the best history teacher you will ever have hands down. you will learn more in his class than in any college class you will ever take. unfortunately, the rest of the school is terrible. over the last several years they have become uncaring about students who work hard and want to achieve. they will only focus on your child if they are FAILING. the district gifted and talented program was canceled, (yes that is against the law.) terrible school, terrible education, treat their teachers terrible, treat the gifted kids terrible, we are so moving out of here. wish i had left 5 years ago. Some of the best years of my life.

column3: charlescity highschool is better than carrie lane because they have more socializing to help students with there social skills Charles City Middle High School provides opportunities that include two world languages, interdisciplinary classes, and unique co-curricular and extra-curricular activities. Excellent-had my two daughters graduate recently and both were well prepared for college and the real world. Please look at these statistics with a grain of salt-they don't tell the whole story. We are diverse which is wonderful-you get out what you put in-you want good-you will get it here! Our children attended a private grade school so we were a little nervous making this change. We have been more than pleased we the results we have seen the last 4 years as we have transitioned into CCCSD. The Charles City High School not only caters to individual students through multiple class availability, but you will also see students out in the community on a regular basis. There is a major shift from the traditional classroom setting to one pushes students in the direction they desire. Love me this school! Great place for kids! I loved it when I came here. They where very flexible with me. Charles City Schools is a great place for students to be involved. There are many different activities and clubs for students to get involved in. Gets students ready for college by offering classes through NIACC. A lack of college prep. A lack of caring from the teachers and staff. This school cares deeply about money but not so mych about education. I do not recommend this school.

column1: I graduated from this school in 2009 well prepared for life including college. Community college, I feel, is so much easier than UCA ever was. The teachers at UCA were always willing to work with me and I could tell God is who directed that school. I would definatly recommend UCA to everyone!!!!!!!! was very unsatisfied with the school. trying to get a straight answer out of anybody there was like pulling teeth. the financial aid is nonexistent and the tuition is through the roof. the public school system is the route to go. For our first year of boarding academy, we were pleasantly surprised with UCA. We found the tuition to be very competitive with other private boarding institutions and really like the incentive program that discounts a percentage off for each year you attend (TIP). The spiritual support from the staff was was wonderful. Our daughter was appropriately challenged in her classes and did very well. The music program is 2nd to none and the school provides so many activities to match the interests of so many children. There truly is something there for everyone. I highly recommend this school to anyone looking for a great Christian education. We heard so many great things about UCA that we went out of our way and past several local dorming academies to enrol our son. We are very happy and highly recommend UCA. They are academically challenging and have a spiritual school that is blessed. We have seen positive growth in our child as a result of the staff and their dedication! This school has way too many rules. I feel like i'm trapped and can't get out of this mess. I found UCA a great school to go to. I went there for 3 years and loved it They believe that what they can “get away with” is “what is right”. That is NOT what Jesus would do..... Unethical practices! Good for the most part and would recommend sending a student there.

My daughter graduated from, and my son is attending SFMHS. It is always a joy to deal with the administration and staff. Both my kids receive(d) great opportunities and experience at the school. I hate to think what they would have missed had they attended another school. The guidance counselors actually know who my kids are! It is a school with the widest educational opportunities available, and dedicated to the success of each student.The brand-new facilities add to the experience. I am suppose to go to this school. My mother thinks its the best chose. I want to become a Dentist in the future and South Fort Myers High will let that happen. column3: We were unhappy with the level of instruction and the attitude of the staff when trying to work out problems. I pulled my daughter out of the school, and enrolled her in online schooling which may not be perfect but is much better than having her attend Smoky Hill Outstanding school. Amazing school spirit and great traditions. IB and AP programs are exceptional. New renovation looks amazing. Smoky has some of the best teachers and security guards ever, every time i come to class, i want to learn because the teachers are so rad! And don't even get me started on the security guards! The security guards are the most interesting, trustworthy, AWESOME people you will meet, personally, they make Smoky Hill. but the deans are very strict and inconsistent on the dress code.Smoky, IF YOU CAN'T CATCH EVERYONE THAT IS VIOLATING THE DRESS CODE, DON'T CATCH THEM AT ALL PLEASE, its very unfair to those who do get caught.! how does the cleavage of my knees or shoulder effect the learning environment?? Other than that, Smoky is wonderful! My oldest child attended Smoky Hill for 2 years until we relocated. I was satisfied overall with the curriculum and the staff, but would have like to see more study skills presented to the students. The principal is amazing as are the majority of teachers and staff we encountered. The population is diverse, a plus for us, and there is lots of opportunity for student and parent involvement. My only issue with school activities is that everything met on Tuesdays after school, forcing kids to choose only one club or organization to participate in. We had a few issues with bullying but with the help of the deans they were addressed quickly and my child felt safe afterwards. Smoky Hill is full of all kinds of people. The great thing is, for the most part, they all get along. Being in drama doesn't make you exclusively a drama kid, just as being in IB doesn't really make you a nerd. People meet others and connect with others in all sorts of ways, and cliques really don't exist, at least not in the common sense of the word. Students respect each other for their talents and interests. There are those who aren't involved in anything, who fail their classes, and who are unknown. That is where the school has fault. Also, the school is sharply split by demographic. The African Americans and Hispanics are a large group of people that seem to be apart from the rest of the school, and they do badly. If they are not motivated to do well, Smoky Hill is probably not the best place for them. If your student has hobbies and is planning to join a sport, NHS, IB, AP, or band, drama, orchestra, or choir, they will succeed. Speaking from personal experience, the IB and performing arts environments are two of the best in the school. Both IB kids and performing arts kids support and love each other. I cannot speak as well for the other groups in the school. worst school ever. i wouldnt recommend this school for your child. all the teachers do is write students up and drown them with endless detentions and the teachers never have time for any of the students!! switching schools asap Highly dedicated and engaged teachers, strong school spirit, diverse student body, and opportunity for rigorous academic classes and extra curricula activities and a strong emphasis on athletics. I attended Smoky hill my freshman year and was bullied to the point I couldn't wait to leave. The school faculty did close to nothing to help me. Many of the teachers don't want to help you, or act annoyed when asking for help on school work. I would not recommend this school. I attended Smoky my freshman and sophomore years, before I had to move and switch schools. The best thing about Smoky is their school spirit- with over 40 clubs and sports, there's something for everyone. The pep assemblies are insane because everybody goes and participates in games and competitions between the different grades. Each class has a designated color, and go crazy with it during spirit week. The teachers try to help as much as possible, and if they can't they will point you to someone that can. I went from being a D average student in middle school to a B average, in hardened courses. Smoky is definitely the best you can get.

column1: As a former teacher, I was appalled at the way discipline and rules were so arbitrarily applied. Students who verbally assaulted teachers got away with it, yet others who commit relatively minor infractions were suspended. Parental involvement was dismal; some protected their little Johnny and Sally Troublemaker and blamed the teacher. Curriculum was an issue as well. We teachers were called on the carpet for not making it rigorous enough, but we were at the same time called on the carpet for failing too many students. Did they want us to make it challenging or dumb it down? Who knew! Morale was so low; it is as if people want this school to fail. If this school wants to succeed, teachers there need to be respected, and the students must not be allowed to run the school. this school is a really bad school i would not send my kids to this school!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

column1: I have never looked forward to coming to school. There have been cops waiting outside the lunchroom, and around the school because of suspected gang activity. I do not feel safe here and it's just a negative environment. The staff hides all of these problems from the parents! South is not a good school, if you're moving to the Plainfield area, look in the other attendance zones. I've been to many schools, especially in California. This school is so behind on learning and cares more about athletics (the athletic office has a flat screen television and a few other expensive things) while we have textbooks with covers falling off. Racial fights, plenty of drugs, and well some teachers are not great. Lots of homophobia, racism, and sexism. have fun! Despite all of the rumors about this school, I have to say it is the opposite of anything bad being said. My daughter loves it, the kids are great, teachers very pleasant and ready and armed with information. So far so good for us. I had 3 of my daughters attend PSHS and would always complain about the teachers not wanting to explain the material. Most of the teachers are young and inexperienced. Too many fights. Deans have have favoritism over certain students which interacts with them disciplining the troublemakers. Very bad school do not recommend The school has made great improvements and my student are really excelling. I think the principle has made a big difference and communication with the parents is wonderful. Keep up the good work and go Cougars!!! Plainfield south is a school that cares nothing about what the students say but will do anything to please the parents. If you would like your student to have a say without you holding their hand on any topic , do not send them to Plainfield south. I am in all of the top music programs and the school rarely supports anything we do! I am also in theater and the floors of the stage have not been replaced in 12 years and parts of wood come off while we are preforming. this school is way to focused on there football team. a TEACHER told my class a story of how 2 football players were not punished for fighting and they could play in a game still, there in also way too much fighting. the administration also lets the activity of classes in the past affect the things that the classes now can do, and that i feel is truly unfair I go to Plainfield South and I love it! I'm in honors classes and we are challenged everyday. We write lots of papers and are expected to read the textbook outside of the classroom. The sports are great too. I feel as a school we have great sportsmanship. I'm in two sports here at South and we have had other teams coaches talk to use about how great our sportsmanship was. PSHS has many different clubs and lots of opportunities to get involved. I do have some young teachers but not all my teachers were young. Even though they are young they still know a lot of information and are very helpful. I feel that the teachers are very caring and are helpful to go to if you have a problem. They listen to what we have to say. I'm also in choir and the music programs are fun and educational. We learn more than how to sing a piece of music; we learn about how to read music on our own, how to play the notes on piano, and important life lessons. The school has improved so much since our principal has changed. We keep getting better every year! I feel that people are generally nice to each other. I made many new friends this year. teachers are excellent, as well as communication. lots of opportunities, very few problems for a high school this size let me get started with a few things here, and lets be grand about it. first off the sanitation. there is a couple places i would like to talk about. place number one, the field house, there is a variety of things to say about it, the locker rooms, the track and its floors are so dirty, such as mysterious substances on floors , wrappers , food , and just miscellaneous stuff on the floor. i will be making several parts to this review. In the end, Plainfield South is a school that is clearly behind on learning and languishes in underfunding. I was so appalled at the facilities -- which were extremely dirty and old -- the disgusting food, and the administration's inability to enforce school policies.Many of my classmates were extremely inconsiderate and disrespectful, and many of my teachers were not passionate about their work and did poor jobs educating students. The environment is overall toxic, and the morale at Plainfield South is so bad that students -- and even teachers -- bemoan the school's lack of quality.Freshmen walking into this school are promised a sort of "college prep" experience that doesn't actually exist; the consolers end up being more problematic than useful, and the curriculum coddles students as opposed to exposing them to the real world. Students overall are given no guidance and -- to put it bluntly -- are put at a risk of having their futures permanently harmed due to the staff's incompetence.It's just all cringe-inducing. It's painfully obvious that the school doesn't actually provide "excellence" to its students. There's plenty of room for improvement at Plainfield South. I highly recommend freshmen to stay away from this school and go somewhere else. Their great, this school is good for students all age's from 9th grade to 12. We have been residence of Plainfield for 20 years. Plainfield South was an awesome experience for our 3 children and for us. All children had many great teachers and a few clunkers, but you show me in school and that will be true. All three of our children are in colleges and were more then well prepared. Each of our children were accepted to many colleges and had multiple scholarships for academics and music. Every school is what you make of it and who you decide you will hang around with. South fosters excellence in academics, athletics, and the arts. It’s up to each of us to take advantage of our opportunities. As a former student, this school is the worst. The only way you would actually learn something is by taking all AP classes, if you take any non AP you literally will learn nothing because they don’t care at all. The only teachers I’ve met that actually care were at WILCO which is a whole separate program from Plainfield South. “The School Effectively Deals With Bullying” I got bullied all 4 years, even cried during the bullying seminar next to teachers, no one cared. Spoke up multiple times they didn’t care, only when I voice I wanted to commit suicide they decided to do something and that was to expel me. There’s too many students they couldn’t possibly discipline all of them so to them they got rid of the problem, me to victim and not the bullies. Please don’t bring your children to this school. During the time here it has been a great experience. There is normal high-school drama every now and then . But , as far as learning goes the teachers definitely help me prepare for college. All together it is a great school . There are many dedicated teachers at PSHS. Our 5 kids had great experiences at the school.

He is currently attending Hofstra University in New York. He feels that he was sufficiently prepared for college. He played sports and developed a great relationship with his coaches. This school has offered programs to our daughter that a better rated school could not offer. It has also challenged her in every honors class versus adding the same but more work. We have found a positive and collaborative student body, an encouraging and intelligent staff, and many opportunities for growth. The sports programs and parents have also been supportive. We are looking forward to sending another daughter her next year. I'm even disgusted to say I let my two kids attend this school. I switched them to Shadow Ridge HS, it may be a longer drive but it's really worth it. This school lacks student safety, the campus isn't clean, and bullying isn't dealt with correctly. Communication in all aspects is terrible.2 messages to my daughters counselor never returned and I had to go into the office and basically wait for her to see me. I had to leave messages with no return call to find out about meet times and bus schedule for after school sports. My daughter arrived at her swim meet to never be acknowledged. When I arrived and approached the coach he contradicted himself several times saying she wasn't released to swim (all documents turned in the first day of school so she could participate) in the same sentence he said most of the swimmers in the pool had not been released yet. Academics is focused on one type of learning style. Treats parents and students like a number (funding I'm sure). Lacks resources for struggling students and they show no interest in the well being of the student. The public school system definitely lets most children down and we wonder why kids drop out or ditch.Terrible rating because they lack follow through, interest in the child's well being and individual attention is not genuine. The counselors and teachers really care about you and will go out of their way to help you at Willow Canyon. The campus is safe and there are plenty of opportunities for students to grow. Willow Canyon is an amazing school. My Son graduated 2 years ago and got a full ride to College. His teachers prepared him for college and he has done amazing there because of the great teachers at Willow that are seasoned teachers willing to go above and beyond to teach. We now have another child attending and we are excited that the same teachers are still there. We know without a doubt he is going to have a great education. Horrible. And the district's can't seem to figure out why they lose their funding to charter schools. Red for Ed remember. How about you earn you your pay like every other industry. My daughter went to school there for all four years of high school. Then went on to ASU. It not only taught her the school subjects but taught her leadership. Biased treatment of students, horrible administration staff . Worst school ever, this school is a perfect example of a broken education system and teachers that only work for their littler paychecks!.

It is honestly one of the worst schools ever. The rules, most of the teachers, and just their philosophy in general. This school is the best school I have never seen I give it a 10 over 10 Good School, the teachers seem to deal with problem students effectively and prove to care about their students' academic success. I have seen disciplinary measures implemented that show the level of professionalism one would expect from people who are mentoring their children. The student body shows "packer pride" and school sporting events always seem fun and successful. I went to school here and it was a good well rounded high school education.

column1: I recently moved to Haddonfield from Williamstown (both in New Jersey), I started my freshman year of high school in Haddonfield. I am an academically advanced student and was pleased to see that within a week of school I noticed that the school would provide me with a challenge. Since the district has such great teachers, most of the students were advanced and the average grade is around a 90. The school is very welcoming and I was integrated into the school within several days. Unlike Williamstown, the administration is very kind and interested in the students problems. I was able to walk right into the main office and speak to the principal about a problem I was having with getting my physical in for cheerleading. He helped me schedule an appointment and got me permission to cheer at the game. The school is awesome and I highly recomend it. HMHS is not worthy of its reputation. Haddonfield is made out to be some sort of paradise but it is no instead it perpetuates elitism. There is a tremendous difference between the way higher level classes are taught and the lower level classes. I took a mixture of both and everyone who does will complain about this. AP and accel classes are often rigourous yet interesting and taught by great teachers. While the cp (lower level) classes are boring and taught by teachers I cant believe were hired. Haddonfield focuses on there top students being ready for the ivy legues which is great but often leaves less achieving students to fall through the cracks. What bothered me the most about HMHS was the special ed program. I had an IEP for mild add. Rather than teaching special ed students to work around their learning disabilities the school work is watered down for them to a ridiculous point not typical accomodations made for special ed kids. The problem then becomes many of these students end up with all high A's in there classes because of the accomodations made get accepted to college and fail out because they were achieving those high grades doing the equivalent of 5th grade work at 17 years old. Haddonfield also pushes everyone into college even severly learning disabled students who would be better off in a trade school. Haddonfield is also a highly competitive cutthroat environment. Friend groups are established young and rarely change. Everyone wants to be the best. Playing a sport is essentialy a requirement if you want to have any friends. Only a handleful of students do not participate in any sports. Students almost exclusively hang out with their sports team. Crew kids are a friend group, cheer girls, Football guys, etc

column3: AHS was great. I just recently graduated, and can say that I had a great experience over the four years. I was engaged in sports, extracurricular activities, and an Honors student. Most of the teachers I had were good at what they did, and went above and beyond. However, like all schools, there are a few teachers that aren't so great. Also, AHS has steadily become one of the best schools in the state (test score wise), a commendable achievement, given the limited resources. The school has several fields of study, all of which are pretty rigorous. Lastly, a few suggestions and comments. Being outgoing and friendly is important in any environment, AHS included; that was one of the factors of my own success, in my opinion. On the same note, I believe that those who write scathing reviews and hate Attleboro are those who are the disruptive and uninvolved students and parents who do not engage themselves in the education process. Finally, the school could definitely do with a cosmetic do-over, AC, and to get rid of a few of the dead-weight teachers. But in all, it would be foolish to give less than 5 stars for the educational experience. Thank you. Blue PRIDE I hate the way it us set up, the guidance counselors don't care about their students. And all the school cares about is their athletics. Don't get me wrong they must care somewhere deep down but until it shows, it sucks. The school system is terrible because of the lack of staff, resources, and supplies. I've just heard recent news that over 20 elementary and 60 high school teachers will be laid-off in 2016. My family has always had quality experiences with the teachers and the administration at Attleboro High School. Great local public school. The city has expanded it so much it almost looks like a college campus. The administration uses punishment as it's go-to tactic to get students to "behave" and marginalized students are punished way more often than the majority students. The school fails to help all students to reach their full potential, and though the building is beautiful, it is understaffed with a lot of teacher "churn." The Titanic was also beautiful, and without competent leadership it still sunk,

column1: 4 kids graduated from Copper Hills and one more on the way. It is a great school. The Science department is a little weak as is the Foot ball team but, where they are weak in some ares they are strong in others Soccer, la cross baseball ect. They have a AP program and a fantastic concurrent enrollment program too. Hands down the best ASL (American Sign Language) program in the State ! LOVE LOVE LOVE the current principal. Very approachable and very involved with the students ! The football program at CopperHills High school is a joke!! If you son wants to play---SIGN THEM up at a different school. This year they moved half the varsity players to JV and are playing the sophomores. I guess they like being the laughting stock of football!! Also like the 09 season they have been having..... what a joke!! Worst. School. Ever. The principal is always bragging about "how great our school is" and "how Copper Hills is the best school there is". The school is always in very poor condition, and the style of teaching is just terrible. I have tried reporting things such as bullying, violence, abuse, and drug use to the school authority, and they do NOTHING about it! They say they will, but then they deny anything that happens! Terrible school, they have a terible staff. There is no accountability and they really dont want to talk to or work with parents in any way. This also goes for the hordan school district, I have talked to both the school and district about their failure to fix erroneous billing on my daughter's account and a year later I have gotten nowhere in resolving this issue. They told me principal quarnberg wont even talk to me about the issue. This school is the worst high school I have ever seen or heard of, dont move here if your child is in high school. You will regert it and so will your child. The AP, Debate and Sign Language departments and teachers are all great. My oldest was prepared for all of her AP tests. My second daughter in debate found a passion for school she has not had until now because the teacher encourages her free thought. Feel very comfortable sending my kids to this school knowing they will be safe and learn in an open environment.

column1: I enjoy Strawberry Crest High school but there are several things lacking. The AP's are very nice people, but the principle acts like the schools a jail and treats the students as such. Most of the teachers are excellent, with the exception of a few. I hear complaints a lot about lockouts and the immense pressure the principle puts on the students if they're late because they're stuck in traffic. Why can't students just call in like a work and say they will be 5 minutes late once and a while? Its ridiculous. At Strawberry Crest, I can mainly talk about the IB program. I find it to be great, the teachers (IB) amazing. Although there are quite a few lockouts, and the bathroom policy is very harsh, I still feel the charger pride! The IB program, teachers, and students are GREAT! Would like to see more encouragement from faculty for students to join clubs. Strawberry Crest has a wonderful administration and Great teachers at the school. Having 3 children that has attended high school in Hillsborough County, I would say this is the absolute best school that I've encountered. The school's administration has set a culture safety and student accountability that has student attention. Parent of students in attendance will appriciate staff's dedication. This school is one of the better schools in this area, but that said, Florida is ranked 48 out of 50 states for schools. Staff and administration are extremely unfriendly. They forget who is paying for their salary. The IB program offers an alternative for smarter students, but I don't really see the point of it. Honors programs in other states are much better than the IB program. As a parent, I feel very unwelcome at this school and do not feel that the administration or staff want parental involvement. School also does not encourage students to be active in more than one extracurricular activity. The school environment was really safe! Fights were unheard of and drugs were nowhere in sight. The principal does act like a dictator but in return you never have to worry about crime. The school itself is very clean and has updated technology. Everyone has so much school spirit and unlike many other high schools- you'll be questioned if you DON'T go all out for pep rallys! The reason for the missing star is that I didn't like most of my teachers because they assume you don't try if you don't understand something and fail a test. However they do push you to do good on standardized tests and for the most part, they succeed. Class size is also too large for my taste. Overall, I think you really get the high school experience without all the illegal stuff and I reccomend it. Florida's education system is No. 5 in the country, according to the latest annual "Quality Counts" report, released this morning by Education Week, the newspaper of record for American education news. The principal has been talked about here a few times as being a dictator. That sounds like kids who are used to getting away with being lazy, late and disrespectful. Mr Brown runs a tight ship however it's a safe environment and as a father of teenagers they all need discipline to help them be independent not co-dependent. Sounds like cry babies not getting their way when they misbehave to me. I say buck up and be more respectful of others. Life is not all about you and your imagined problems kid. Pay attnetion and maybe you will be able to hold a job and be a productive member of society one day. Strawberry crest along with the principal Mr Brown care more about status than they do students....just SAD!!!!! Pastor recommended, unbelievable school in great area!! Great, I am very happy about the opportunity of being part of this school. I believe Strawberry Crest is a great school. The teachers I have met have been very kind & understanding towards our children.The parents are informed quickly as possible of any misdoings. From Administration to the teaching staff, this school is top notch. You will see the principal at the sporting events and cheering on her students. The Guidance Counselors are kind and attentive. As a mother of two and a teacher myself in a feeder school, I'm very impressed with the overall experience .

column3: I am a parent of a special needs teenager. After struggling in every school he has ever attended, WEBO has been such a breath of fresh air. I feel I can finally trust that my son is being treated fairly and not being bullied. The Teachers, Special Ed staff, Principal, VP and Sports coaches have been helpful, encouraging and a delight to deal with. They truly put the needs of the student first and my son feels that this is the first school where he has felt the teachers actually cared. What a blessing WEBO has been in my son and my family's life. My family moved to the Western Boone community when I was in 2nd grade and my sister was in 7th grade. I still remember my family meeting with the administrators and feeling very welcome. We checked out two other school districts and Western Boone was the last one my parents looked at before they decided to settle here. I was never heavily involved in the many extracurricular activities Western Boone Schools offers, but I still stayed involved in the community and the school as a student. The administrators are great, teachers are fantastic and caring and they put in so much time and effort. The Western Boone community has become my second family. It's filled with great people, it's a fantastic place to live and the community and school corporation has offered me opportunities to be successful after high school. In fact, they've given me more opportunities than I can count! The best part about it is that the school corporation has gotten even better since I graduated. When I get married and have kids, they most certainly will be attending Western Boone Schools. As a student, I can say that Webo is not as great as it could be. There are the good students and athletes that everyone see's, but there is a seedy underground part as well. There is a lot of pills in circulation, a lot of rumors, and a lot of people who will get you drugs or cigarettes almost immediately after school lets out. Many students actually come to school high or on pills. Students don't really take the staff or discipline seriously and make jokes of it. And, personally, I have seen many teachers that lose their temper and go off on students. There are also drugs in the athletics department. Honestly, it's your average inter city school, and not to be mistaken for a rural, untouched and purely good school. I am, again, a student and will be a junior this year. Webo has a truly top notch art program that not only engages students, but pushes them to achieve their best work. The faculty cares about student success and makes them aware of opportunities they might be interested in, then helps out every step of the way to get them where they want to be.

column1: Bishop Miege is well worth the money spent. You come out of there well prepared and ready for college, and also come out with friends for life. The teachers there could go and teach in a public school and make more money, but they love teaching at MIege. Many of the teachers have been there for years. Miege also has some diversity compared to some of the other Catholic schools. It is not all "white bread America. It is like one big family. I loved it, and I know you will to iif you give it a chance. Bishop Miege is the most fabulous school imaginable. Excellent administration, teachers, office staff, EVERYTHING. A wonderful experience. The best school in the Kansas City area. Even if we weren't Catholic I would send any child I had there. Have had experience with 3 Catholic High Schools in the Kansas City area and Bishop Miege is by far, the best of all of them. None others are even closed.
