column3: The teaching seems to be pretty good but the problem is with the administration. My daughter has been bullied by some other girls and the principle and vice principal are not responsive to the attacks on my daughter. The complaints have fallen of deaf ears. The school needs to provide a safe and none bullying atmosphere for all the kids. We moved here a few years back and have had nothing but problems with the high school staff,including the teachers,coaches and principal. It's sad how much the school focus's on discipline and how little they focus on helping the students succeed. The amount of students who are always ineligible to play sports because of poor grades and the amount of students who have to take online courses or summer school to make up for the lack of help and education they received during the actual school year is astounding. We are never notified by the teachers if our children are in danger of failing and the teachers rarely keep edline up to date. How am I as a caring parent suppose to help my child succeed if the lines of communication are not open. I also think there are too many teachers that have inappropriate relationships with the students and are never reprimanded or have to face any consequences for their actions. This school's poor rating is a reflection of the poor education system and the way these students are not being properly cared for and educated for the future. It's sad when many of the seniors are not informed of the exact amount of credits they are lacking to graduate until a month or so into their last semester of their senior year. Many of these kids have poor family situations and they rely on the teacher's,coaches and counselors to guide them in the right direction. I hope for the sake of the kids that somewhere in the near future this school gets it together and figures out that their number one priority should be to help these kids pass every class and graduate. No child should be left behind. This school has a negative impact on almost every student that enters it. Kids are expected to act like adults but are treated like toddlers. Learning has gone out the door and almost every student has turned to cheating because they are not getting the resources they need. Teachers don't care about the students and they make it very obvious that they are only there to get paid. Students dropping out has become very normal and almost no administrators push to keep these kids still in school. Administrators look for any small reason to get a student in trouble and then question why all the students have such bad attendance and never want to come to school. When students are late to a class by even a second, they are sent to a room where they are not even allowed to work on their schoolwork. Students take this as an opportunity to skip class without getting in trouble and (bonus) they get to do nothing the entire hour! This concept just goes right over the administrators heads and they still believe sweep is a good idea.This school is flat out a joke. Sending your child to it would be like putting their education on pause because if they don't get one of the 4 amazing teachers that actually care about their students educations, they will be gaining nothing. Quite bad honestly. Sports seem to be a main focus of this school and nothing else. "Hey! We need 1,000 dollars for some stuff for our classroom" Answer; Sorry, no. "Hey we need more gear for football, only 5,000 dollars!" Answer; Yes! It's just, I don't know if learning is a main focus anymore of this school. Seems to promote intense anxiety and breakdowns. I have personally seen it, multiple times, where students have broken down in class because it gets too much. I would rate it as a positive experience.

column1: My child just transferred to Harlem, but it seems to be a great school. Very impressed so far. Moved to Fort Gordon with husband's PCS and chose Columbia Co. Schools over Richmond Co. because of test scores. Chose Harlem High school over other Columbia Co schools like Greenbriar & Lakeside because there is absolutely no diversity and as my children we raised on Fort Bragg, DOD schools, they wouldn't know what to do without any. People were friendly, this was prior to the creation of the HS in Grovetown, which worked both for and against Harlem High as it took some of the classes with it thus limiting the range but also making for smaller class sizes. Negatively, my youngest, an avid reader of Sci-Fi was somewhat perplexed when asked if she were reading a dictionary when clearly she was not. Perhaps, they were joking. They do seem to be a close knit community-- with the positives and negatives that go with it in every sense of it-- to include the school which would depend on your child, how they acclimate, and how adjustable they are as well. I went to this high school.. So discouraging. Hated it. The teachers didn't care at all. Lots of kids getting in trouble. I graduated from HHS in 2017. The only staff that had respect for the students were the ones with the lowest titles. Administration was awful, they did not give their students any respect. All issues that involved students were not investigated at all, they would blame the student if there wasn't any evidence. They also punish the victim in the case of bullying, even if the victim didn't fight back. I cannot stress enough how awful this school is. Made switch from private school to HHS, so glad I did! Love it! Best secret in Col Co.

column1: I am a senior here and I know that our school would be a lot better if they stopped dumbing down the exam test and had FEDERAL FUNDING. It is hard to be happy at a school that doesnt have cetain sports, and cannot afford to get new books or buy a printer that does not give teachers problem every week. It is also hard for a teacher when the education system itself is changing into something worse than it already was. And to make matters worse, the government is having budget cuts towards education again. I went here in from 9th grade in 2003 to graduation in 2007. Most of the staff, administration, and many teachers could not care less about you a human being. There none of them understood that life outside the school walls like family and work affected your performance in school. Guidance counselors included were of no support. Many a times when students in math class would have a question about the material, the teacher would respond "it's in the book." How funny, because I read the book, and now I have a question. The book is not getting paid a salary to teach. Thanks for nutritious honey buns for breakfast every morning, and the vitamin packed pizza and dry tater tots every lunch. Thank goodness the school is right next to McDonalds for an even healthier alternative. The staff must look at the student as a whole, speak with them one on one, guidance counselors and teachers alike. Teachers need to teach, not just relay info and mark whether it was regurgitated back properly. Guidance counselors should guide, actually help each grade instead of popping up just at the end of senior year. The one positive change was implementing the rotating schedule and activities period. I go to this school now. This school is just so bad. They always ask for money when you get your report card. They send the money on things they dont need like paper trays for food.... like really. Plus no one listens to you. Only the honor roll we give reward to only the honor roll. When other kids in the school do their best and try their hardest and only the honor roll people get stuff. They get to have a voice while us just one point and i could have gotten an honor roll are not good enough. Don't go to this school it is bad no one likes it. There is so much stress. People throw food at you when you get out of the lunch room, stick gum in your hair, laugh at you if you walk funny, and ugh this school is just so annoying. They expect so much from you. Some of the teachers aren't that bad. But everyone else are just a bunch of ughhh cant write this without a swear. The school is just bad dont go there no one cares about you in this school. I graduated Latin Academy in 2013 with high honors and got accepted into 8/11 colleges I applied to. Now that I'm an alum, I'm able to reflect back on my overall experience at BLA. Pros: A HUGE variety of AP course offerings - many of my fellow alums are ahead in college credits due to that. By far the biggest benefit of the school. There's a lot of support from your guidance counselors when applying for college as well. They walk you through the process including how to apply for financial aid. Oh, BLA also gives out a ton of scholarships to the graduating class for those who apply to them. The teachers that are actually good, are very supportive. Tons of support finding good after school/summer employment opportunities through BLA's partnership with PIC. The student body is also incredibly diverse and there's a variety of sports options. Cons: Bad administration. Although there's a lot of good teachers, there's still a good amount of bad ones. Lack of funding is significant as well. How can an exam school have such poor conditions? Outside of sports, there aren't that many clubs. If you take advantage of what the school has to offer and work hard, you will end up in a decent college. From what I've seen from my peers - including the ones that didn't do so well during their time at this school, we all collectively agree that BLA prepared us well for college in terms of getting used to the work load and the level of difficulty. While at certain points I felt rather miserable at the school, it wasn't until after graduating and going to college debt free that I realize how supported I was at BLA. Administration is horrible! The worst type of people to have to communicate with. They dont care about anyone but themselves.

column3: The teachers at Harbor are exceptional. They tutor- free whenever a student is willing to give up their lunch time and or after school. School funds limit the number of AP classes they offer, but I discovered its the number of state exams passed, not the # offered. Both my daughters received 4's and 5's on all exams taken. Also they limit the number of AP classes accepted towards college credit. They also consider the size of the school/ district the students come from and the and how they met all challenges leading to a college students success. It's hard to tell with a new principal how the school will respond.. The past 2 principals who gave a total of 10 years between them were real leaders. If your looking for a lot of direct help from a school, don't send them to collage. Harbor is now one of 48 high schools in the state to be recognized as a California Distinguished School! Poor Teachers, Poor Administrator, really bad experience. Send you kid somewhere else if you can My child has had a great experience at this school. The teachers are committed and supportive. Students are encouraged to achieve in all areas of interest. I went there in the early 00's. High school's usually not known for being some of the best years of your life, but I felt that way. Lucky to have had those years and loved Harbor!

column1: Cont from prior review-Forgot, the one thing ICHS lacks, and makes NO sense to me with the success of their teams (mainly football) is spirit!!! The concession stands at the football games is a complete JOKE. There is no program for the games (like other local high schools-all it takes is company sponsors) and the band was nonexistant until last year. We have the talent that no other schools have, now lets get behind these kids and show some spirit, like we care!!!! I do all I can do-like feed 150 boys each week during football season and get sponsors for new wrestling gear (along w/ our own donations and more importantly-our TIME) Cmon Gators, let's kick NFM High off in the spirit department!!! The School is convenient, the food is well and people are nice. I like it My daughter attends this school and I must say this is a GREAT one! When we moved to Cape Coral everyone told me to keep her out of this school and I was really worried about her attending but hoped for the best and it turned out even better! She is thriving academically and athletically there and has no problems! All of her teachers are wonderful! Don't let the rumors fool you, ICHS is absolutely awesome! My daughter was sick and feeling strange for a few days and I had no idea what was going on but do to the concern of her teachers, she was sent to the nurse who figured out my daughter was diabetic. It was day before springbreak and she was going out of town with her grandparents the next day. I don't know much about the teaching stuff but I do know they probably saved her life. Thanks to all involved. I find it funny how there are countless amounts of good reviews when I myself think negativity. Don't get me wrong, SOME of the teachers well-educate their students but most of them care what's on their pay check! Most of the students are rather accepting towards everyone but also half of the students,from my experience, are RUDE. Principle Bueno on the other hand is great while being heavy on the dress code for unecessary items. I'm actually accepted here. Before this place, I was bullied all the time. I was a misfit. From Caloosa Middle, to NFM Academy of the Arts. I was never accepted and people went over-the-top with me. But this school was different. I was in tears of how open minded the kids were. All you have to do is have a positive attitude. The school spirit here is astounding from admins. The students never bullied me, and I can openly say that I like they find weird, and a teacher or staff member will do all they can, literally, to stand up for me should any one say something, and by something, I mean it won't even go as far as something so little that it's not even a real insult to me. I never knew people could be so accepting of me, and fun! Especially Spanish 1's teacher. If you have this teacher at Island Coast, you will love this school, and that's a CERTAINCY. This school's kindness has me in tears, just thinking about it makes me think I'm truly at home. Keep shining Gators, just keep on shining. :') As a parent I am appalled. The school lost my daughters transfer papers not once, but twice. She ended up in the wrong classes because of this and was told in the middle of the school year that she had to take different classes. Now this year she has to take those classes again because she didn't take the whole class. We went to the guidance counselor to see what she needed to graduate and "thought" we had it all figured out, that is until yesterday when she got her class schedule and all the classes were wrong!Last year one of her teachers told her if she didn't go to a 4 year college she wouldn't amount to anything. Am I livid??? You bet. They are disorganized, no one knows what's going on and every teach and counselor has a different story. I'm very upset with this to say the least. Kids feel they own the school, berate others for expressing themselves, and very little discipline is enforced. Most teachers have an attitude without justification, and one teacher told a student she was "easy" as a slur! Guidance is completely oblivious to IEP's, they violated one student's IEP three or four times in a row, and no improvement since. Disgraceful, my year was truly upsetting. one of the best schools in Cape Coral,great stuff,very clean,good kids,very safe,high lever academics and sports. My daughter is going to be a senior this year. This is her second year. She has had a very positive experience except the French teacher is retiring and has taught her entire class nothing but how to watch movies. -10000 out of 10. Yes some teachers have good experience but the fact that bullying is a thing they don't care about is wrong. My friend got bullied to bad that she was sore for a week and no one cared. This needs to be fixed. Honestly, I cannot have a lower opinion of this school. It started with a leadership change in my oldest son's junior year, straight downhill. It is very difficult to say strongly agree when it does not even compare to wanting to say excellent! My son had to work for all of his grades! There was no fudging and I am grateful that he learned he was going to be held accountable for his actions if so. Those traits can only be learned early, especially for college preparedness. For those contemplating this school, I highly recommend it. The principle and teachers held strong to the expectations of my son regardless of what you read. BE an involved parent and there will be no surprises! It takes a team, not a sideline witness pointing fingers expecting everyone to do it, it is your child. You too must post haste your part! My son was assigned to this school when we moved to Cape Coral. They assigned him to a bunch of classes with no thought or reason. He was put in Honors marching band, he plays cello. He was put in ROTC without any discussion with us or him. They put him the girls chorus. They put him in remedial English but regular math and science. He was regular math, science and English back at home. When I called to get it fixed, they told us it would take 3 weeks before they could adjust his classes. We finally got them adjusted a month later. They put him a game design class. They then removed him from that class a month later and put him in a Spanish class that had been going for 2 months already and he's never had a language. While he were there multiple fights broke out and he was close to one in the lunch room. Also, they have no voice mail. I have no idea why, but you can't leave a message for any of the teachers, the staff, or anything. As an added bonus, just recently they made the news because one of their AP history teachers told his class that the N word didn't mean what everyone thought it meant, instead it just meant ignorant and that slave owners didn't mistreat their slaves. And they didn't fire the teacher, they suspended him with pay and were planning on re-assigning him elsewhere. If I could give 0 stars I would. Your child is better off running feral then going to this "school". This is by far the worst school I’ve ever been to, I understand there need to be strict rules in order to maintain order but it’s really getting out of hand. The principal wanted to talk to me and made fun of me stiffening when I couldn’t get my words out. I don’t have a math teacher and I’m forced to fail that class, we don’t get the right math classes work/zoom. Some classes have football teachers teaching and they admit to not knowing what they’re doing. Under all I would give this school a lesser rating if a could 10/10 don’t recommend this school. If I could I would give them no stars! The office lady is very rude and don't let kids through to see the counselor and if by luck you can go through he is too lazy to work, just to go sit around school telling kids his bored, but if you need him to do his job he just give excuses not to do it. And don't think you can talk to the principal, she is worst . . . making fun of kids when they stutter. She is supposed to be a role model for the kids, someone to look up to!!!

column3: The principal of Clackamas is a complete and utter control freak. He makes decisions about programs (such as the drama program) without adequate knowledge of the program and what it does. He is completely obsessed with the AP programs because they make him look good. The administrators of this school in general think they know more than parents and teachers combined even though all of them have only been there for a relatively short time. I have had kids at Clackamas for the past eight years, and this administration is the worst. I have to agree with the previous post. The current principal at Clackamas is very arrogant. Fortunately for the students, the teachers at Clackamas are very dedicated and caring. They are what makes Clackamas a great school. Too bad the administration is so bad. The students are stuck up snobs and CHS is all about their cliques so if you don't fit into a certain category I'd suggest a more open-minded school. If not in that high group, your are ignored. Would suggest to go to a different high school. This school is just o.k. There is barely any school spirit. There are no morning announcements or even a pledge of allegiance. Some teachers grade very oddly. No one knows about homecoming, clubs, or upcoming events. Therefore, it is very hard to get involved. Teachers don't care about students, grading mistakes are too frequent, classes are taught poorly, and boring curriculum I disagree with the comment that Clackamas High School doesn’t have dual enrollment. I had two kids that graduated from Clackamas and both ended up with college credits from Portland States and Clackamas Community College. Some of the classes at the time were also AP classes. Taking and passing the AP exams were important if they were going to go to a highly selective college but most colleges did accept the PSU and CCC credits with out the AP exams. They did graduate a few years ago but I did notice in other reviews that students were still receiving the college credits.

column3: Pros: Small community and has plenty of extra curricular activities to join. The school is very active in helping students get into college (even if it is just into a community college). Cons: This school has very few dedicated teachers (I can only recall 3 good teachers within my four years there). I don't know if it's funding but this school teaches for TAKS testing and nothing else. Most of the students can barely distinguish the difference between "there", "they're" and "their", and still use fragmented sentences in a paper. There are very few dual credit courses. Also adding on to previous post, the teachers DO favor the cheerleaders and football players considerably more than the other students (i.e. debate, band, orchestra, etc.) and, of course, most of the teachers had personal favorites. The school has offered several dual enrollment options through UTPA, TSTC, and STC. Classes have become much more challenging now in my senior year. I was only involved in academic competitions and am treated equally by my teachers so I can't agree with the football comments. My only complaint is that some discipline policies are too strict.

column1: My children have attended this school for five years. They have learned so much and are always prepared for the state test. The teacher's give adequate practice to ensure the skills are mastered. The campus is nice and clean also.

column3: This school does not protect children that are bullied. They talk a good game. My child was bullied for month's. They did a five minute investigation. The bullies Were not corrected. HBHS is an exceptional school with many dedicated educators that motivate students to work to their full potential. We are very pleased that our daughter is attending this great school! She has truly enjoyed all her teachers and looks forward to classes. Even though the AP classes can be overwhelming with homework, assignments, and reading, she continues to enjoy learning! The Campus atmosphere is also friendly and diverse. A gem of a high school! I love Huntington Beach High school. I think its better than many of the other schools in the HBUHSD. I had to do some research since my home school was Marina. (There was NO way I was going to go there!) And Huntington is definitely the right fit for me! I like APA, without it I don't think I would've made so many friends! I do think they need to hire some better math teachers. But they also offer some great electives, like guitar! This is a great school with an amazing nationally recognized arts program called APA. However I have been very disappointed with a couple of the academic teachers. My son struggled in pre-calculus and we made a huge effort to get him help, including spending hundreds of dollars on tutors and attempting to work with his teacher, but she was not willing to work with us or offer any additional help to my son. In spite of all our efforts and my son working extremely hard spending numerous hours of additional study time, he failed this class. His teacher could care less... no one should ever fail a class if they are giving 100 effort. Good school; APA is OK but not in the same league as OCSA. Sports programs are good. Teachers are demanding but fair. One comment posted that she doesn't understand about how working hard results in a failing grade. That's the sound of a participation award mentality that is warping this generation. Kids shouldn't be allowed to think that they will always be successful as long as they try hard. I've been completely happy with our choice of this high school. There are so many opportunities for students to be involved and parents to be included. This school is terrible. I am a former student. There are so many children of drugs here. I felt like a lot of them were from privilege and did not care about their futures so they turned to drugs. Bullying is rampant. It is especially hard here if you are a minority or from a low-income family. Huntington Beach is still unofficially segregated over sixty years after Brown versus Board of Education. Plus I think they need to do more in the way of preventing bullying especially for those targeted on the basis of their gender, religion, race, which I definitely was when I attended. Not sure yet it’s still our first year but so far my kid is happy Excellent! We have experienced 4 wonderful years at HBHS with active participation in the Model United Nations (MUN) program as well as the Academy of Performing Arts (APA). My child immersed themselves in the AP curriculum and graduated Summa Cum Laude with the California Seal of Bi-Literacy and Honors Distinction in the Arts. High school is whatever you make of it ... the more involved you are, the happier you can be! : ) The administration at this school is incompetent at best… The head of supervision is one of the rudest most unprofessional people I have ever encountered in my life! I have a child who has absolutely never been in any trouble at school however we needed the assistance from supervision for an unrelated issue… I was told to return to the school multiple times by different people then when returning was treated as if I had audacity to ask them to do their job! The police are on campus almost daily one of the most unsafe schools in our district! Givent all the resources, and a wonderful location that should draw the best staff and teachers, they do not do a good job of education student, especially college bound students. Very poor experience. I had two children go through this school, 10 years apart. Things got worse with the second child. Particularly the lack of teachers acting like authority figures, dress standards and the drug problem increased exponentially. My child is going into year 2. Last year was a good experience and they enjoyed the school, the activities and met new friends. The only thing I can say to those entering in as a freshman is the Honors English teachers vary considerably. Try not to get Anderson. His kids appear to score lower when compared to the other honors teacher. My child’s friend had Harshman and said she was great. It seems she is the better of the two teachers. Highly recommended (not just the best looking campus in California. . . so much more than meets the eye) The only good experience you are likely to have at this school is APA. The location of APA at this campus is the sole reason why this school has so many kids. If you are not in APA, and you are more academically inclined, this is not the best school for you. I feel like some of the good reviews I have seen on other sites are written by teachers or staff members. There are a couple of reviews here that are spot on. The school does everything for its staff but nothing for its students, and therefore as another reviewer said it, is not the best school for college bound students. Most teachers do little to nothing to prepare students for college or support their academic needs in any way, and the administration will not do anything about it. My son is in his senior year and has not had one good math teacher. And this is a subject that is very important to him. Haven't heard much better about the ones he didn't have either. Some of the Honors English and AP science teachers are Ok, but for the most part it's slim pickings. We had three kids go through this school and were very happy. All three were in AP/honors classes and two went through the awesome Model UN program. The school is a beautiful historical campus and in a great location. They all were accepted and attending top 50 schools out of HB so we are very pleased with our experience.

column1: All of my children have and still are attending South Jones Elementary plus High school, The children should be taught the times tables while in elementary and not promoted if they do not know them, The school breakfast and lunch program could do a lot better most children complain about how bad the food is and a lot do not eat it so it goes to waste. It would be much better to give them well presented tasty food that they will eat and I can see no reason for it not to be this way. The school could probably do with a lot more educational books so students do not have to share, Now the physical education side of this school is not good in my opinion as it only seems to cater to football, baseball and basketball, any child that does not participate in these sports do not get much in the way of exercise if any. It's a shame they do not have a gymnastics program in hardly any schools these days. But South Jones does have a very good music /band program. South Jones might be slightly better than the city school but the teachers and staff are not nice and I have contacted the school three time and they take message and never call you back. If you are not into sports or a kid of a certain race..they will not help your kid. They food is horrible and the kids don't eat lunch. Racism in the area is very strong and the teachers show their true beliefs toward the kids of color.

column3: I am not impressed by the JE School District. I have decided to home-school my daughter this year as I do not believe that this school puts the students first. I have had one child graduate and one still in the school, but I have nothing but communication problems with this school since 2004. They have all but depleted the sports programs (not enough qualified coaches), but are spending money on sports facilities. They do not offer a variety of electives that would allow our children to excel in the arts (if that is the desire). I never get a phone call back when I leave numerous messages about important issues. If you do not have a certain last name, you don't get picked for parts in plays, etc....I have had it up to my neck with this school. I cannot afford at the present moment to move out of this district, so I have had to resort to teaching my own child at home. She will get a far better education and will be allowed to also excel in her extracurricular interests. The drug problem is rampant in this district as there is absolutely nothing that is offered for these children to do in this town. A 6 in rating? Really? Maybe in test scores, but nothing else! Well rounded and readied to take on The world!

column1: Very little communication between parent/teacher/counselor. My child will not go return next year. While it may fit others, it was not a fit for our family. Our family is still trying to figure out what all the rave was about with this school. Our child has had the worst experience here in their entire life. We've found the teachers to not be caring and forget about having any of them ever respond to an email or call back. I'm in the same boat as the person who posted below - my child also will not return next school year. I am astounded by the last couple of comments. They sound like helicopter parents. This is hands down the best high school in the area--including privates. Always rated one of the top 10 public high schools in the nation by US News. Very diverse with a population of very intelligent kids with a wonderful South African principal. Our son has loved the IB program, but the AP track is also terrific. This school sets kids up for success by requiring much from them. Due to the quality of education, among other things, our son is being courted by 3 schools in the Ivy League. Getting in to Stanton is not easy. If you are foolish enough to leave when your kid has been admitted, I feel sorry for you. I am astonished by some of the poor reviews I read. Both my children have attended Stanton and I been extremely happy with the school. I am very pleased my children are around other children who desire to learn and are inspired by outstanding teachers. There are ample opportunities for students who are struggling. However, I do think the curriculum is challenging and not for every child. I teach at a private school in the area, but am very pleased to have my children attending Stanton! Several members of my family including myself graduated from SCPS and went to college. Students that did not suceed at SCPS were unable to maintain the high acedemic and mature expectations. The environment is a college prep atmosphere, teachers counselors should not have to respond to every trivial request. Before enrolling your child at Stanton, be sure to educate yourselves more about the success rate. We found out that less than 20% are successful at Stanton. Our straight A child whom attended Stanton for one year still feels that it was the worst year of her academic life, even though she still maintained her high standards. I also, like another parent who has previously commented, felt as though the teachers/staff were very lax with their communication. It's not particularly the curriculum that I complain about, its the staff uncaring attitudes. The peer group is excellent with nice students from all races and backgrounds. The administration staff are very nice but guidance counseling is average since most kids go to Florida colleges. The reason why they are ranked in the top 10 schools is because all of the students are required to take AP exams. Stanton has the worst AP exam pass rate (30%) in the district which is embarrassing since the students are much more capable than that. The teachers are terrible and there are few text books. i.e. Exams results are not returned for a month and the child never knows how they did while studying for finals. 2 chapters of a language were covered in 4 months and the last chapter is covered in one week before the final exam. The teachers are proud of the bad grades they dish out and the students struggle to chase the demands of disorganized teachers. The sports team suffer as many kids that were previous A students are quiting teams and not going out for teams because they stay up until midnight everynight studying when not playing on a team. Playing sports will really hurt your grades here. I'm not sure where the previous posters get their stats. Stanton is the highest rated school in the county, with a graduation rate of 98%. IB graduation rate is similar. We also have the highest AP pass rate in the county, and one of the highest in the country. I am the mother of a senior IB student and an incoming freshman. My son has had great teachers, and while he has worked very, very hard to be successful, has also played four years of a varsity sport, and been involved in all kinds of clubs and activities, both in and out of school, as have all of his friends -- all National Honor Society members. It's quite possible, it just takes work, commitment and good time management. As for counseling, it's far superior to what any of his friends have received in Duval/St. Johns schools, and although he has opted to stay in state - he has many friends going to excellent colleges all over the country. Get the facts before you make decisions. Stanton's a great school! This school is outstandiing! I really reccomend it! It may not fit some people, but this is a really great school and prepares you for your future! Stanton was definitely the best experience of my life. In response to some of the negative posts, I will say that not all teachers respond the minute you email them. However, it is a college prep school and I have found that my professors at FSU certainly don't always respond quicky, if at all. However, everything about the school is just wonderful. Some of the sports are excellent. The theatre department is amazing and always successful. What is more important is the environment. Every student at Stanton is there to learn, and to go to college. Having that sort of positive network of determined and driven students definitely had a positive effect on me. Also, I know many students who were inspired by the mix of various cultures at Stanton. The school spirit is always high, the lack of discipline issues is great, and the guidance department is absolutely phenomenal. Both my brother and myself attended Stanton (he was in IB, I was in honors), and it was the best decision possible. Go Blue Devils! This is a really good school and will prepare you for college. It may be overwhelming at first but you will be successful after high school. This is an amazing high school and I highly reccomend it! Hard working students and good enviroment! I am in my third year at Stanton and I can say without thinking twice that Stanton is by far the worst school I have attended. I moved to Stanton from a private school in Jacksonville and I can say that the teachers are not looking out for a student in the same way a teacher would at a school such as Episcopal or Bolles, and that the students found at Stanton cover a broad spectrum from the highly competitive to the druggies. I wish to leave Stanton but sadly as a result of the sky high tuitions at my former private school I am locked into one more year of this horrible school. i'm a senior at this school and the experience my vary, if your not a good student or one who cant keep up good work then the 4 years can be hard, im and ib student and at first i had a mixed experience first semester as freshmen, but if you find the correct path it will be a great experience, and the ib is so worth it, the college im going to, cause i did the Ib, I get to skip the first two years of my bachelor's degree, so only two years, but if you you the ib you are most likely skip 1-2 years of college I graduated from Stanton several years ago and realize the staff (and expectations due to technology) may have changed, but I believe Stanton is the BEST public school in FL (and surpasses many private schools) in education. It is inclined toward those who are self-motivated and appreciate an opportunity to be challenged, and don't require an extremely high level of communication with teachers. My peer group was very independent we truly learned to work together and support each other for success. Many students are given an opportunity for a challenging level of instruction (that they would not find in their neighborhood school ) without the need for constant parental involvement. Alright, I don't know why people complain about the hard work and the lack of connection between students and teachers. I am a Junior currently attending Stanton as an IB student. Honestly, as much as I hate to say it, Stanton is one of the best schools there is. I have a bitter-sweet relationship with this school. The work is overwhelming, and the facility may be a bit old, but besides that, this school is seriously awesome. It has challenged me mentally, and academically. Coming from a not-so-bright middle school did not really prepare me for this type of work. However, I had to force my way through it and now I am actually an OK student. I take pride in attending one of the top schools in the nation and you should too. If you do not want to be here, leave, there is other people willing to take your spot. Also, the teachers are amazing. I don't know what some of the people on here are talking about. Sure there's a few iffy teachers here and there, but a good majority of the teachers I've had have been amazing. If your child is failing, go to tutoring or instill in him a harder work ethic. Stanton College Prep is designed to challenge one's mind. It's simple; if you don't want to push yourself, do not attend. You have to be able to push yourself to get through all 4 years. They provide great teachers who motivate and encourage students, even though they seem like they hate you. It is a very hard school, but it teaches you things beyond the textbooks that you can rarely see in neighborhood schools. You meet several people that have complex cultural background, over half of our school is minority. This interaction provides you with an experience that you can not receive in a neighborhood school. Yes, it is stressful and there is a lot of work involved, but if you really want to succeed, or see your child succeed, send them here. I was a Varsity athlete 3 out of my 4 years (10-12) and I currently have a 3.56 GPA unweighted, I take all AP classes, I am a member of National Art Honor Society and National Honor Society, and I dedicate my weekends to volunteering and socializing. Time management is essential. But I suggest starting off in honors courses, and if you can handle that, move on to IB courses. I have to say, this school was one of the worst schools I have ever attended. I attended this school for one year but ended up leaving not because it was too rigorous but because I was bullied and not a single administrator took any action against it. Their only goal is to maintain their academic rating and do not care about injustice or bullying happening in the school. One of the faculty members even tried to buy me off with lunch. I spoke with multiple administrators and because the people who were bullying me were strong in their academics and played sports, they took no action against them whatsoever. Sure, they have great academics but when you have people trying to get rid of your complaints by buying you lunch, it's pathetic. Leaving this school was one of the best things I ever did. When I was here freshman year, everything was fine. I attended LaVilla and knew I didn't want to play an instrument for the rest of my life, so I chose Stanton over Douglas Anderson. I didn't do well in the AP I started out with because I had no choice in the AP I wanted. My worst subject is history. I'm just not good at it. So, I didn't do well, but I did well in all of my other classes. When sophomore year came, it all went downhill very quickly. I was given the worst teachers ever. Everyday, they would complain how the generation of students are getting dumber and dumber and would not help you at all. I have insomnia and I blacked out in one of my classes and when I went to my teacher to apologize for passing out in class, he told me he had no reason to help me. My grades went down as a result. So, many teachers here will put you down rather than try and help you. The education is great, I honestly loved the material I was learning, but I couldn't stand the teachers. They were all very unwelcoming and rude. I guess it was just a bad year, but it was bad enough to make me want to leave, and I left with lifelong anxiety I never had before coming here. Stanton is wonderful, although it is mentally challenging, they do it for a reason, and that reason is to prepare you for anything that may come. And the fact is that if you do IB, most people tend to skip the first year or two of college, which really saves you money and time in the long run. If you think about it now, the time you're spending on homework and essays and all of the academic work, you'll save that in college and you'll get to be the one doing fun things while others struggle through classes. And in college the classes are so large that you can't possibly get a one on one talk with the professor, but the staff at Stanton are always there to help you. There's so many safety nets instilled for everyone to do as well as they possibly can and the teachers are always there for you to ask questions and try to fully understand. The teachers may seem like they don't like you or they're rooting for you to fail, but they're really just teaching you about the real world and preparing you for that. All the staff is actually quite nice and respectful, especially our principal. She's the absolute best and she really wants us all to succeed. I'm proud to go to Stanton. it has been a great experience for my son and set him up for college and beyond. The only down side is the sports programs, poorly managed and very unprofessional. I was sorry to see him give up team sports after many years but if the choice is sports or academics I am glad for the academics. Very good communication by administration. High caliber of students that want to be at school and are active in their communities and Rob's of clubs and activities-though they are secondary to academics. Qualified Teachers very accessible before and after school for tutoring. It is a demanding curriculum with a tough magnet bus commute-truly college prep. These kids do well in college. Students need to be motivated and responsible to succeed. You cannot stay with Ds and Fs. Clear expectations-demanding, but tools provided. Guidance counsellors strong. Principal Majova is exceptional in taking personal interest in challenged students. School spirit and pride is high. High number of National Merit Scholars proves why this school is ranked high nationally. I am a parent of 11th grader who is in the AP curriculum. I am extremely pleased with my child’s experience at Stanton. Stanton is not for all kids, your child needs to be a high academic achiever willing to put in the work. But if they are willing to put in the work, the reward is going to a school where you are surrounded by kids that want to make an impact after high school. Stanton has tremendous school spirit, good athletics, lots of very active clubs, and teachers that are invested in the student’s success. Go to the Stanton website and take a look at the colleges that come onsite to recruit the Stanton kids, it is full of top national colleges. Jacksonville is fortunate to have a high school of this caliber, take it advantage of it if your child fits the academic profile. My daughter started off roughly, between the pressure of being in high school and not knowing many other kids and, of course, the intense educational curriculum. She wanted to transfer, but the options were limited and risks too great (Paxon was the only viable alternative for public high school, but she was not guaranteed to get in for sophomore year and could have lost her spot at Stanton, which would relegate her to our neighborhood high school). She stuck it out and, in my opinion, is much stronger, more mature and much more prepared for life as a result. Much of this is due to her rather than the school, but the school provided the challenge that is just not available most other places. I would honestly choose this school over all the other school in Duval. I am attending Stanton so this may be a little bias but this school, with its teachers and staff, provide such a great learning atmosphere where students excel both in life and in academics. Both students and teacher are helpful when you need help and the school offer a rigorous academic standard in which you will have to learn how to manage your time effectively and improve your academic potentials. I went there from 1987-1993. It was crucial we had a sense of family in order for kids to go to a magnet school. We encouraged each other to succeed. Learning was enjoyable and exciting. Choosing classes and a path to college was something we looked forward to. We looked to the future and were prepared. We went out into the world with that enthusiasm. I really believe we made and make a difference. I can directly attribute this to the teachers and leadership at Stanton. I love them to this very day. The students of this school are truly the best of the best, and they are what make Stanton as superb as it is. There is no public nor private school in a many-mile radius that even comes close to comparing to Stanton. However, at Stanton, there are truly some of the best and worst teachers in Florida there. The worst oftentimes comes from an issue of nepotism, which appears to be rampant among the staff at Stanton. Another gripe is that some members of the guidance department of Stanton are incredibly lackluster. Overall, your child, if they can do well at Stanton Prep, will truly be on a path of great success. Apparently, this used to be a good school, but over the years it has fallen from a top 25 school to now 75th. Even in Florida it is only the 7th best and given it gets the best of the best students in Duval County, there is something wrong with the direction of the administration. In the last 6 or 7 years the school has been spiraling downwards.

column3: Is West Branch Rose City Schools / Ogemaw County District schools rated a 501C3 ? I was traumatized and tried to take my own life for a few reasons and in the last year this school has gotten so much worse. My experience at Ogemaw Heights has been disappointing, I feel I have the potential to learn a great deal but it is hindered by the inadequacy of the teachers. As an advanced learner I was forced to use the online program to take the classes in order to learn at the level I desire. It is alright. Many of the aspects of teaching can be iffy depending on your learning style. Most of the students that occupy the school are rude and don't care to be in school. You can expect that in a county filled with farming, and low income families. Overall, if you need a school that provides the average everything. This is the school to choose. Anything other then that can be an issue. I was actually very contempt with the school during my first two years of school, other than just being upset with going to school. This slowly fell apart when my junior and senior years were starting. My ambition and motivation to do well in school went away when the school took away the fun and joy of itself. I cannot find interest in anything school related because of the school. I have learned to hate the school and its school board with a passion. I cannot find a reason to enjoy the school except for my friends and sports. My unpleasant time at school has been met with unpleasant people and teachers. the school should have a huge rework with a new school board and educational system.

column1: I graduated from Palos Verdes High School four years ago. I absolutely loved attending school there and could not imagine having a better high school experience. PVHS was able to provide students with the perfect balance between enjoying school and obtaining an excellent education. I grew so much intellectually and personally in my four years thanks to the wonderful staff. After high school I was accepted to a top 25 University. When I got to college I felt that PVHS had prepared me for college extremely well. I succeeded in the vigorous college level classes and I contribute my success to the preparation I received at PVHS. Although it is a public school, it is equivalent to a private school education. I HIGHLY recommend this school! My son started out at Peninsula High School which is also a very strong school in Palos Verdes and basically felt very out of the loop and unbalanced there. The homework load was very unreasonable. He had almost all honor classes and was getting good grades but did not have a balanced life. It was ALL about homework. He said that all of his honors teachers did very little lecturing but assigned an extraordinary amount of homework. He transferred to Palos Verdes High School after a month of attending Peninsula High School. He said that the teachers at Palos Verdes High school actually lectured and taught the students. Palos Verdes High school is on a block system and now he has time to do his homework without it completely consumming his whole life. He said he is learning a lot more and that the 2 hour classes go by much faster than the hour long ones at Peninsula because of how engaged the students become with the teachers being able to complete involved lesson material. If you want the bar to be set high and balance this is your school! PVHS is a good school. It is not as academically challenging as PVPHS, so it is a good fit for kids who want to socialize and have a lot of fun during high school. The test scores and AP results between the two schools show that Peninsula is stronger academically. However, the teachers at PVHS allow the students to complete homework during class, due to the block scheduling, so it's easier if you are an athlete. This school is amazing and challenging in every way. Those who say it is not are the same who choose to avoid the amazing array of AP and Honors classes. Most teachers are challenging and fill class periods with a learning experience. Also, they have recently been redeemed in light of academic competition with Peninsula High school by earning a 898 API score, equalling that of Pen's 898, despite PV's smaller population. Also, athletes are encouraged to better their academics while being champions in their sport. The arts at PV are also unmatched with their open opportunity and extensive programs of Drawing, Painting, Sculpture, Video Production, Dance, Music, Literature, Drama, and all kind of computer and media art imaginable. This school is like being at a country club. Grades are inflated and teachers are so far not prepare to teach subjects. Parent run the school not the administrators. Very did functional school. Kids go too college not prepared. Located in an amazingly beautiful neighborhood, Palos Verdes High School is one great school. The kids are hard workers, very determined to get into a great college and like to get involved in activities in school and in the community. The parents do an amazing job of supporting the school, from new buildings to new sports fields to the salaries of teachers and counselors. The only way the school could improve would be to add more parking places for the kids. You need to be Caucasian or rich for teacher to respect your kid. As an alum as well as parent of a current student, the standards of this school have remained constant. The development of each student as an individual is immense, and with the block schedule students are given the college-style experience well before the great change that is college ever happens. If your student is driven, goal-oriented, and capable of holding themselves in a kind and considerate manner, they will truly excel at this school. In comparison to Peninsula High, Palos Verdes High is average. If your student is not as academically inclined and motivated or is interested in things outside of academics, this might be a good fit. Both schools are great for different reasons. Many parents and students tout the block schedule and ability for students to do homework in class and participate in sports more. However, as a parent, homework is just that - to be done after class. In terms of preparing students for college, no college is going to allow your student to do their homework in class. Colleges will expect students to have the skills and motivation to work outside of class on papers, presentations, group work, and yes HOMEWORK especially in science, math, language and writing classes. There is no escaping homework. Unless you expect your child to get a sports scholarship, they will need to know how to focus on the academics and get work done. Both schools offer a wide array of clubs, sports, leadership, arts, and community service opportunities. So, it depends on your child and their goals.

column3: Since my child has attended this school, they have changed the grading system three times. Now they have credit by proficiency, which in my opinion, only teaches students to pass tests. The students don't learn from this. It is a big disservice to the students. Furthermore, this school does not prepare them for college. It also has a tracking systems - athletics vs. non-athletics. Athletes are given preferential treatment and allowed to miss lots more classes than non athletes and take more challenging courses. Their math and english departments are lacking good teachers. The principal, however, is actually trying to raise standards in the school but if Administration does not support him it is all for naught. I'm not impressed with this school at all. It is geared primarily for athletics not academics. My children have basically lost interest in school since they've been there. Parents need to be encourage to come in more than the twice yearly conferences. Parents, school board members and other guests were always accompanied by administrators during classroom sessions. It always felt like the administrators were watching to see we didn't share any personal views other than life in rose colored glasses. Again, I am hopeful for the district to recover from an employment nightmare. The superintendent, business manager, and two principals have changed. Only the Director of Special Education and Elementary Principal remains. The SPED director is now the acting superintendent. I don't know him, but I hope he understands why major changes are needed. An oppressive environment makes a poor educational atmosphere. The kids are good kids as a whole. Pacific Bridges, the alternative school, had a high success rate but is limited by being from small place to a smaller place which restricted numbers. Rules and operation were taken from the teacher who started it and micro-managed by the now former Principal. Hope for the new administration is high. I have heard good things about the new Principals. I give the school three stars based on hope of a positive setting. Very poor. I hope things have improved at this school.

column1: Although I only went there for about three months into my freshman year, I thought that school was amazing! Before I started highschool I lived in oregon all my life and hated school, I started skipping school and in 8th grade I only went to school for about 30 days out of the whole school year, then I moved to spanaway Washington and was having trouble processing the move and was scared about started school without knowing anyone. The first day I connected with many people and throughout those 3 months I became friends with many different students in many different grades. At many others school you would see different kinds of cliques and seperating and even bullying. But you will not find that at this school. When I went there i was actually editing to go to school, I came to school everyday with a smile on my face. And to find it weird I even went to bed early just to go to school. I went to stright Fs to a 3.5 and actually trying and paying attention to my grades,I became a whole different person. The teachers were amazing, for once In a lifetime I actually felt like someone cared about my future and were very helpful, I loved all of my teachers, I never dreaded going to math . This school is pretty great. My son seems really happy here and there are a ton of activities to engage all kids. My only complaint giving it 4 instead of 5 stars is the updating of family access. I don't know how many times I have checked it and it said my son had F's and missing assignments but he didn't (I double checked). It's quite heart stopping to see your A and B student have F's. Take it with a grain of salt or you will have a heart attack. I was worried that the school would be a little rough given the area but so far it's been a great experience. If your moving to the area rest assured that your kiddo could be very happy. 2 weeks into the school year my son fit right in and having a great experience. As a mom simply put; teachers are pretty great, there are a lot of kids, freshmen share lockers (could be a diaster), don't hear a lot about drugs or bullying or gangs, there is some though but it's one of the better area schools. All of the reviews of this school are outdated. My son is currently a senior and I have another daughter that is a freshmen. The school is very unsafe as it has had more than 25 fights in one year and a lot of them have been really bad fights to the point a policeman has threatened to tase students. I would not recommend this school to anyone. Also, the administrators don't do anything about bullying and are very incompetent. My daughter was being bullied and the schools VP advice was to "ignore them" when she was physically hurt by another student. Terrible terrible school. This school has been the most un uplifting public school I have attended. So many studentss are not passing and ther are fights everywhere. People do not value education and it is so boring that I had to leave. You are not motivated to do well and that is the reason why I had to leave. Some teachers are outstanding but others are horrible. If you want a competivitve and educational environment that pushes you, this is NOT the place. Sports aren't doing well either, basketball is starting to do better but if you have a child that wants to do sports get them into a better high school. I am currently enrolled at this school. Some teachers are amazing and care for the students and others seem like they are there just for the paycheck. There are often multiple fights in one day. I don’t always feel safe at the school but there are some awesome clubs to join and some teachers will work with you after school to help you if you are struggling. Also if you want to go to a school with good sports team this is not it. Three of my children graduated with honors from this School!! Great Opportunities available!! A great experience, no school is perfect but the end result proved hard work produced great students! The years are short but the days are long as each one of my students graduated I found myself in awe of their precious person and who they chose to be! This school helps those who seek it but without effort from the student or family you will receive the bare minimum.

column3: Trojan Nation! This school is amazing at creating school pride with everything it does. Yes, it is a melting pot of diversity but that's not what defines this school. You will feel a sense of pride, of community and the culture makes you feel like you belong. My 10th grader tells me this is the best school he has been to over the years. He states there really isn't any bullying and overall the kids really enjoy class. The football coaches are by far the most influential leaders in the school and run a solid program. Generally a good school. Teachers need to keep Infinite Campus up to date. We just had 4 weeks of grades in some subjects added 2 hours before the Thanksgiving break. To make corrective action possible where needed, we need to know where there are problems in a more timely manner. I graduated from here and done none of the school work and ditched school and teachers still passed me as if they were in cahoots to get me out of the school! They do not care about the students, they didn't even care that I walked several miles to school in the winter! The principals are just terrible too. I graduated from this school. I didn't choose this school. They simply just pass you! And the teachers get Personal with the students. They do not care about education in the least. I was in pre algebra for four years! Never went past that. They just kept me in the lowest math class over and over, not even caring that I never learned. I just had to take 4 years of math, they didn't care about preparing me for college. I passed and graduated with all D-'s. I didn't even deserve those! I was never in class, never done the work and yet they just passed me so they wouldn't have to see me again. The principal banned me from having friends and teachers would drive students around or ask students to pick up food for them at fast food places. I never learned anything here. They set up cameras in the halls, not enough places to sit in the cafeteria because there were so many students. I was not prepared for college because i didn't earn my diploma. I had to basically take high school classes in college. And besides math I was in honors and college level English, history and science and yet I still wasn't prepared for college! So I wouldn't go here! The teachers get personal and unprofessional with students and they just pass the kids and I remember a teacher told us that the ACT/SAT tests didn't matter so I intentionally failed them because they Said it didn't matter! I just graduated from this school. I've only been there for a year so I don't know what every teacher is like. I got lucky and got the gems of teaching though. The people who run the school are very kind. However, teachers do have favorites. If you have a coach as a teacher then expect to not be acknowledged if you aren't in that sport. But it's like that everywhere. Teachers pass athletes who truly don't deserve it. That's just life. The younger grades at this school are VERY bad kids. They are very disrespectful and I've witnessed girls stand on desks to flip their teachers off, vulgar language towards elders, drug use and more. That isn't my problem so I don't care, but if your young one is coming to this school, just be aware that they will be consumed into that. I can see how that kind of environment can change a kid for the worse. The people complaining about this school below really brought that on themselves because I've been to 5 high schools and I can say this is not a bad school. It's just the younger kids and lack of parenting that are bad. I feel like this school cared about giving us a send off that will prepare us for what college entails. I actually feel confident now. And I thank the teachers I had and the counselors for this. Teachers get too personal with students and would get involved with them outside of school. Homework load varies depending on class. Special needs kids are separated from the rest of the students. Unusual punishment by administration. Cameras in hallways, classrooms and around premises, not necessarily bad but made my child feel uneasy. They pass students even if the student didn't deserve to pass onto the next grade. My son and I are very disappointed with this school. Took him out In the middle of the school year. Cannot believe the lack of professionalism and compassion. Our experience has been great. Longmont High School is a well rounded school. Best high school in Longmont. Longmont is an excellent school where the majority of the teachers are very supportive and compassionate. The school has great diversity and a culture of kindness. There are opportunities for AP classes & medical career classes for students that are interested. All of the staff from Administration, safety team, office, counseling, athletics etc…seem to care about students. "It is what you make it"Life is what you make of it". Much is the same for Longmont High School. If you don't participate in out of school events, join the wrong crowd, or slack on academics then you won't like LHS. However, if you participate in sports, music, or student government you'll be accompanied by some of the best teachers and coaches in the state. These coaches care deeply for their students. I see other comments that imply inappropriate teacher relations with students, but I have not seen that to be true. The staff genuinely care for the kids. The programs at this school are outstanding. The sport programs are very strong and produce great athletes with real life skills. The music programs (very broad I know) are all strong. Most notably, the drum line that is literally GOATED. Drama program was good. There are AP classes that were honestly much harder than many of my college classes. However, a lot of general ed classes are low tier and have a lot of distractions. This is a good place to learn and prepare fo life. Students have the opportunities they need to succeed.

column1: I don't mind South Cameron High School. Some of the teachers are honest, but others show favoritism, are rude or harsh to the students. There is not a wide variety of school and club activities, and I personally think that they could have a better or more advanced learning system. It is not a very big school, because of the hurricanes, and I hope more people will visit. There should be a better dress code than there is right now. More interaction with the students. It would also be better for the students to have more hands on activities. the school is great! my girls love going to school and they work with the students often to make sure they get the lessons

column3: What a wonderful performance in the Halloween Parade last night in Toms River!! I am originally from Newark and was so pleased to see some of the good work being done by Newark students. The good news needs to get published too! So, my rating for this band's performance is a 4 STAR! I have graduated from this school in 1995 and I am ashamed that I had attended Weequahic. Most of their teachers were unprofessional, including a social studies teacher who had badmouthed me to the class behind my back, which I had confirmed with a classmate. I dont even remember her teaching social studies in the classroom, only the current events that had happened back then. The Newark school system was supposedly taken over by the state that year, but I don't feel that they had done a good job fixing the problems, because there are the same teachers that are still there although I believe that they should have been fired, and now, Im dealing with an incompetent staff member who deals with high school transcripts, who doesn't seem to understand the word "status" and doesn't return phone calls. The NJ state takeover of the schools did not work. what can we do to make our schools better? It's up to us to make a difference with our schools and city. Stop complaining about what's so bad about it and make a change.

column1: I would agree that there is a huge emphasis on sports, but what small/country school is not. What is concerning is the lack of interest in the students and education. I attended and graduated from Elmwood with honors. I was in the band, I played sports, and I was liked by all. Even with all that said, I would still advise all parents to send there children elsewhere. The teachers, principal, dean, and office staff, all play favorites. People who should be leading by example and giving all students an equal opportunity, label students and treat them accordingly. If your child gets labeled as a good student, then they will get more attention from an educational standpoint. If your child gets labeled as a bad student/trouble-maker (whether or not it is accurate), they will be singled out in class, and will be disciplined unfairly for every slip up. Please choose another school for your children. I have seen too many average students fall through the cracks, and too many students skate through with the "right last name" or the needed athletic ability. One of the best schools around. Yes, they love their sports, but all athletes are held accountable to academics no matter which sport they play. Most of the time when people write reviews it is because they have a complaint, therefore submitting negative reviews. The school is a good school. Lots of good teachers, coaches, and students. Send your kids there without hesitation!

column3: This school, in comparison to all of the other public schools in the area, is severely behind the times. Choices for electives are severely limited, and students with high potential are often restricted to simple classes that do not challenge them intellectually. The school's atmosphere is one of hostility toward all but the families that have been in Mancelona for decades, which is an extreme disappointment to newcomers. The school is rife with bullying issues and the attitude of both the students AND the staff is one that puts the entire state of Michigan to shame. The sports team is the only facet of the school that receives funding, putting both academic and elective classes to the wayside. If you're looking for a school that challenges and supports your child academically, with a relaxed friendly atmosphere and room for growth - seek another school. If you are looking to place your child in an infantile classroom with rude students, little challenge, no sense of community, and stunted growth - I suggest you reevaluate the needs of your child, or choose this school. Lots of offerings compared to surrounding schools...choir, into to woods, spanish 1, art 1, band, physics, art 2, marching band, art 2, color guard, advanced woods, spanish 2, Baker College Classes: english, speech, psycology, sociology and many on line classes as well. Also, one of the best after school programs in the area.

column1: Warren is a great school to go to if you want a good curriculam, life long friends, and an amazing high school experience!!! Warren is a very unique school. Lots of parental involvement. I am actually kind of surprised at the rating, I expected 8 or 9. The atmosphere is a little more like a private school just because of how involved everyone is. It's diverse in every way, with wealthy kids from Westover Hills and lower-income kids from other parts, yet everyone seems to be equal at Warren, with the same opportunities and you can tell how driven all of the kids are. We highly recommend Warren for their band, which is famous in the city: The Purple Pride of Northside, the Academic groups, of course sports, and the dance team. Love this school! I am a graduate that attended Warren and I am a little surprised by it's ranking. I have visited other high schools in our district and in comparison as the appearance, our school is defiantly one to contend with. As far as education, our teacher's are very engaging within their students academics. The thrive to push students to their absolute potential. We have a very cool construction career's program, in which they are actively doing things that are geared towards their purpose. The administration is strict but that is only to creat a non-disruptive harmony amongst trying to educate children. And I feel the best part of Warren are the clubs/extracurricular activities, they have something for every student, whether it be a gamer's club or something more along the lines of academics, such as Ac Dec or Speech & Debate. As a former student I feel as although Warren sets a good atmosphere for "the best four years of your (child's) life." I moved to Warren High School from a private school and I noticed that most teachers don't seem to care about the students. One teacher I had was the worst teacher ever. She didn't even know how to control the class. Some teachers are okay though. Most I had didn't seem to care. We hardly got any homework. THe students here are just plain mean, only had a few friends I've made...the rest seem very rude. This school needs more discipline. It's not the best, but it's just an O.K. school. Such a great school! Staff is great. Teachers are fun, but get things done, too. A very diverse school with students of many different backgrounds and cultures. Not ghetto in any way. Warren is actually a great school. Great parental involvement. Kids are exposed to so many good opportunities. If you want to succeed, you have every advantage here. Very diverse group of kiddos. Great band program. Lots of school spirit. Go Warriors! When coming to Warren I was scared because it was going to be my sophomore year and I wouldn't know anybody. Luckily everybody, students and teachers alike, are very friendly and encouraging. What surprised me the most was that instead of being more focused on academics most everybody had their eyes set on sports and clubs. Although I really love Warren I suggest that you take caution with the classes you take and who you have as a teacher. Unfortunately a couple of my teachers did not know both the content of which they were teaching us or how to simply help us finish our work. I suggest that if you are in the STEM strand to transfer to the magnet school due to the amount of depth and strength that you'll gather compared to the normal classes that Warren provides. Warren is a great school. The teachers push education & make themselves available to all their students for extra tutoring &/or questions. 11/10 I love this school, forever will be my favorite!
