column3: I graduated from Central in 2008 with a rounded education that allowed me to complete my bachelor of arts in English in only three years. I was able to opt out of math, science, and political science gen eds in college because Central provided classes that were sometimes even better than the college classes they could offer me. In addition to that Central has one of the most prestigious classical music programs in the state and gave me the opportunity to perform professionally with Mulberry Lane and at the College World Series. Central is the home of anyone who goes there. I often describe the feeling of family at Central as a mini Husker nation. The teachers of this school are some the best I've ever studied under, and as I complete my final semester of graduate school for my Master's degree, I can without a doubt say that Central is the reason I have the friends, world experience, and education I have today. Here at Omaha Central High School, you'll find dedicated teachers and thriving students. I've been here for almost two years and I plan on staying. The IB program here is amazing. Perhaps you've heard rumors about this school, but there nothing here that you wouldn't find at any other school. It's a matter of who is willing to put in the effort. I adore Central's diversity, opportunities, and overall appeal. Once an eagle, always an eagle. My school is very diverse which allows both staff and students to learn about others and their cultures, etc. With so many backgrounds, students learn a lot when others bring a mixing pot of information to class with them. Most teachers are focused on getting the most out of their teachings and see improvement in scores and personalities as well. I enjoy going to Central but the security staff should be rehired because they lack in there job, or at least one man does. He's useless. Other than that, the admin is great! The principal is having a hard time enforcing rules on a daily basis and needs to step up his expectations for daily behavior based on what I've seem and heard. Besides that, the school is a very well brought up educational school!!! I will rate a 4 not a 5 cause no school is perfect in my point of veiw Awesome. Loved it. Teachers were the BOMB school events were fun. There was a lot of homework help and cool clubs and I felt noticed and taken care of in a big school which was awesome. I rember my teachers and will my whole life. Also super diverse but not in a forced way. Felt like the melting pot america should be. I'm honestly not sure why Central High is rated so low on this site. This is widely know as one of the best if not the best in the city/surrounding area. I graduated from Central two years ago, and I have only good memories. I was an IB honors student, and all my teachers were wonderful and actually cared about my education. I still keep in contact with many of them. The students there obviously care about their school, and during sporting events almost the whole city comes out; the stands are packed. The school is extremely diverse, and all groups are accepted. I never saw anyone get bullied, and the few cases we had were quickly and effectively dealt with by administration. I would definitely recommend this school for anyone interested in the IB program, as it is the only IB high school in Omaha. Why is Central rated so low on this list

column1: This is an amazing school! I have been challenged and learned so much. I am glad I was accepted to this school. I am have been accepted to Harvard College on the east coast and Duke University (amongst others). I have chosen Duke University and is excited to attend in the fall. The teachers are great and they help you out if you need some extra help. I am going to miss Brooks College Prep. Let me say that brooks is a fundamental / AMAZiNG school. I dont go there but i am applying their they are my first choice the open house i attended was just wondeful. They have remodled and it's looking very good they have a pond outisde the school it's a beautiful site to see and there school is well organized and clean. There academics is excellent. They have 99% ready and prepared to graduate and go on to college is that cool or what. I hope i get accepcted well me and my twin. we both applied. if u are trying to find a good outstandnig high school brooks is the one. o and i LOVE their choir they all sound like angels ! GO BROOKS. :) the teachers there are awesome & cool. My school is fantastic. The clubs are amazing and useful to the community. The school is cultural, diverse, and welcoming. The people are amazing. The staff really cares about you and strives to help you be the best you can be. They want you to succeed. I really love this school. I would recommend this school to everyone. Small class sizes, excellent and involved principal, diverse student body, challenging courses (including AP), plenty of activities/ sports, 100% college placement and safe environment. There are NO fights or gangs at this school, only scholars! Parental involvement is strong at Brooks esp through Brooks Parents Club, which meets monthly. My child graduated from Skinner West Classical School (CPS)and is now a sophomore and is excelling. I feel comftable knowing he is safe when I drop him off everyday at Brooks. In the Spring, my son will travel overseas to Italy/Europe through Brooks travel abroad program. My son also participate in swimming and baseball. He has met a diverse group of friends from all over the city. I love that Brooks main focus us ACT preparation and getting every student into college with scholarships. I know we mafe the right decision by choosing Brooks. Attending Brooks College Prep is like attending a private school for free! My tenure at this school was emotionally trying because the students are so poorly behaved. Most of the teachers I had were excellent, but honestly, Brooks doesn't deserve a 10/10 simply because of the student body and poor leadership under Mr. Weaver. Luckily he is gone now, but the damage has been done. Personalized and individualized instruction makes this school unique....allows students to learn to their potential without the stress and pressure of having to be "perfect" all the time! Love this unique and modern..."healthy" learning approach. 9 out of 10. Very good school. I believe many of the teachers care and the principal is actively engaged with students and families. However, some of the teachers are very unprofessional and not held accountable for their actions. This impacts students in inequitable ways.

column3: Wonderful school with great academic and extra-curricular programs. The teachers and staff really care about the students!

column1: Military wife commenting below. I think you have hit the nail on the head. I have found that most parents and children who do not like their schools do not actively participate in anything at the school nor do they try to do anything to make change. They go with the flow and complain, complain, complain. Solutions, I feel for parents who do not particularly care for a certain school is to transfer the child(ren) to another school of their preference or to home school. In 20 years of Army service my children have changed schools 4 times. As you stated, several times, we too have called My husband's Branch requesting extensions and each time our requests were granted. 13 schools is a bit much but not unheard of even for officers. Since there are only 12 years of schooling, why 13 schools I wonder? I hope the other family didn't move every time her husband had to go to a special school for his career which sometimes only last 1 month or so. You never know. Well, this is our last assignment and I love RCHS. I am actively involved, the teachers and I exchange emails, we attend games, and volunteer whenever we can. We haven't joined the PTA yet but do intend on doing so. Let me address each of these issues. My kids participated in lacross, bowling , and band at schools in new york...all had free transportation to and from games and practice. All sports were free. Uniforms were provided free. RCHS wanted $500 a season for softball, and I was to provide transportation. With 3 students, its not affordable. Maybe your kids were born with a silver spoon in their mouth, mine weren't. My kids are healthy weights, not shy, and are adjusting VERY well in their 14th school, (our ONE deliberate move, to get OUT of RCHS). We did all we could to stay at our last station, but the ARMY thought it best for taxpayers to pay 20,000 to move our family so my husband can do the same job here he could have done there. Write your congressman. As for trying to resolve the issues,yes, I called assistant principles,guidence counselors,The principal, and even Mike Green superintendent. My conclusion is that they have all been educated at RCHS. This wasn't personal. I didnt bash you or your family. I gave an observation as a person with alot of experience in this area. Compared with the rest of the country...RCHS is pathetic. Look beyond your backyard and see for yourself. To the parent whose children were in NY. I have to say I agree with the other parents who have given feedback on your situation. My family and and a few other parents in my neighborhood came from NY/NJ area as well so we can understand the comparison. Guess I'm a bit different. When I've called ANYONE whether it's school or not in reference to my children and I don't get a return call within a certain amount of time, I make a face to face appearance. As far as money for different events at the school, along with the request for fees due, a letter has been sent home with my child for each sport for payment as well as a request for parents to help with fundraising so the fees can either be obsolete or lowered by more than 2/3s. Example, the track and soccer teams have been raising funds by working concession stands at college games, the bball sold t shirts and drink cups, the baseball team has done the same as well. My child so far this school year is participating in 2 sports (right now) and the only thing it has costs us is gas and time. By the way I have 4 children, 2 in high school and 2 in middle school. Have you been to the parent meetings posted on the website? Russell County High School isn't a terrible school, but it is FAR from being a great school. I have been a student there for four years, and in my experience, some of the teachers don't deserve the job, and the school needs people who actually understand how to run it. Some teachers give out little to no work, and do not teach at all. My advice: send your children to another school where they can actually get an education to prepare them for college and life. The entire school district is a joke! They do not care about educating our children. They have no interest in our childrens futures, nor do they care about them as individuals. They are quick to punish, yet won't protect a child being bullied. As a military family, our children have been in 5 different school districts in 4 different states and this is by FAR the WORST I have ever witnessed. My last year at Russell County High school was the best year of my high school career. The staff is extraordinary. I am a proud Warrior Graduate. GO WARRIORS! This school is all kinds of messed up! We got a new principal about a year ago and he has made things worse! Whenever I ask to speak to the counselor they always give me some excuse. 90% of the teachers don't care about helping you like they should. If I could move to another school, I definitely would but I can't because Russell County is the only school in my district. We need new principal.. one that actually cares! Hate this school. Don't have pep rallies, don't have money to do any extra curriculum activities, don't have enough people who care. The new principle is a follower - not a leader. This school is far far far back in the forest, so we need a "leader" who will go out of his/her way to make students, parents, and teachers, love this school. Most people want to but there is nothing to want, there's nothing here to need, there's nothing motivating us. The middle school, is definitely no better. Sure, the people here are nice country folks. That's what made me give this school and the middle school a try. They both hv failed. No one wants to volunteer, no one wants to go out of their way. People here are stuck, and content with doing what they have always been doing. Which is NOTHING. I am a parent, and I have 2 children (1 in middle, 1 in high), and they both make straight A's. Not on the account of these schools (because of me). They come from schools that give out homework, and expect assignments turned in. This schools does not. This is why this school fails. I have determined, that my children will not succumb to these low standards in education and will be going to new schools next school year. I'm seeing a pattern here and i will have to add to it. Another A student with many zero's for classwork and tests that have brought grades down to failing. Same stories I read here. The teachers have students open a book and read while the teachers sit at their desks. My daughter has one teacher that actually teaches in her class and guess what? She has a B and loves the class. Went to the guidance counselors today. We were told nope they dont teach like that. Your kid just isnt trying, thats all. Look at all the zeros. That explains the grades. Now, I know she isnt the absolute smartest kid around. None of our kids are, no matter what we want to believe. When the grades slip that drastically from a normally A to B student, you know something is up. Nobody gets zeros consistently on tests unless you arent there. We already home school our 15 year old that has a learning disability because the school was not providing the resources she was supposed to get from them. Of course, that wasnt their fault either. So I have 2 students who loved school that now wish they were anywhere else but russell county, or wish that the teachers would actually TEACH the subject. I am currently attending this school as a junior, and this is by far the worst school I've ever attended. The counselors say they will help you, but in the end, they actually make a larger mess of things. When a teacher is absent, they usually don't have a substitute to cover for them, and the students just do as they please. There are so many fights, and so much drug abuse. The kids that have drugs on them get the drugs confiscated, and then usually get suspended, but they don't get expelled. There is always dip spit in the water fountains, and graffiti inside of the stalls of the girls bathroom. I have never felt more disgust towards a school. I have watched RCHS dramatically change for the better in the last few years. As with any school there’s room for improvement, but they’re working on it Absolutely horrible, teachers don’t care, school is very dirty, and took the voice away from the students This is a good school with good people and students

column3: I love this school, I m so glad of the education I get from Albert Einstein High School ,The kids are just so excepting of each other but there are some kids you wonder about but don t all high school have them? The school is just great and beautiful and when I say beautiful I mean BEA-TI-FUL.The school is the location of the VAC (Visual Art Center) and the paintings the kids do in that program is so professional it will just blow your mind, but this is basically an arts school so the talent in the VAPA (Visual and Performing art academy) is just as great. The school has all 7th periods a day which is good especially if you re taking a foreign langue so you won t forget anything. The lunch is an hour so you have time to eat and visit a teacher. This is a fantastic choice if you re really into the arts ,we are a creative school consider the fact that we have the VAC and the VAPA but if your mostly in academics then this is also a great choice because we are an IB school so you can take really advance classes.It was the best choice I ever made. The school is wonderful, I love it so much; I can't wait to go back. I am a sophomore and when I arrive at Einstein my only attention was being in the VAC (Visual Art Center) I really didn't care about the school, in fact I thought it would be awful but the minute I step into Einstein I fell in love with it. It was not difficult at all to make new friends considering the Fact that the kids are creative, smart, artistic, and nice..... Well most of them. I m also getting a wonderful and rigorous education with the wide range of honors and AP courses at Einstein. The classes are 45 minutes (7 classes a day) NO BLOCK SCHEDULE! Which I prefer and so do most teachers. In the school you are require to choose an academy most of the student body choose VAPA (Visual and Performing arts Academy) but I'm in the VAC which is such a great place and program to be in if you re an artists. Kids from the whole county apply to this program but they only let in a small amount in each year. The school is beautiful and decorated with art and the community is very accepting and spirited. The IB program is so intense most students don't even make it by senior year. Sub par school, couldn't wait to get out of there. The students don't really care. Only a handful of good teachers. Einstein is absolutely WONDERFUL as a school! While I am moving because of personal reasons, I would recommend Einstein to any kid with a desire to be a part of theatre, art, music, sports, academics, or languages. The students are very accepting, and there is a blind student in our school with a guide dog, and he is included in everything, such as main roles in the school play. While there are a few teachers who are less than fantastic, many of the teachers are very helpful if you make the effort to see them during lunch (which is 50 minutes so students can spend half of it eating and half getting help from their teachers). Also, besides the general obnoxious attitude sophomores have, there is not a "class war." However, there are occasionally fights in school, but it is usually between the kids who aren't trying to participate in class anyways. Regardless, this school is amazing! My daughter is enjoying her time at Einstein. The principle is fantastic, and the teachers enthusiastic. They have a variety of programs that meet the needs all most/all of the kids. Very happy with our decision to go there. Please note, that most of the reviews below are VERY old and do not fully represent today's Einstein! This is my son's first year and he loves it. The school is very inclusive and activities are readily accessible. Great group of parents. Their participation is about average for a school this size. There are just enough folks to get quality programs going but more parent involvement would make Einstein a top tier school. Leadership is tried and true and have seen them in many after-school activities. The faculty and staff is visible and so far seemed proficient in their jobs. Word of caution: some teachers like handouts a little too much. This is usually a sign of lazy teachers who at the turn of a moment will direct you to what has been completed and what has not been turned in if your student is not doing well in class. Overall my son has found a home and I am glad. He is involved in Cross Country and they are a great and diverse group of kids. Small High School- great principal and the IB program is outstanding. Years ago it had a mixed reputation - but today it is considered fantastic. Don't believe what people "used to say" about the school... it's a whole story today! We currently have a sophomore attending Einstein, so far we've had an entirely positive experience with the school and staff. Our daughter is in the IB program and has taken some AP classes, the assigned work is challenging but her teachers regularly make themselves available during lunch or after school to help with assignments. In her two almost two years at the school, there have been a few fights at the school but these are normally among kids that are not interested in learning. Our daughter feels completely safe in the school. I am disappointed in the teachers and the administration. They clearly do not care about this demographic. One of the best in the DMV area. And I attended Whitman, and have worked at several private schools (including Sidwell Friends). Tremendous. Our experience was great. Our kid got into every college to which she applied. Great involved teachers. Polite and respectful student body. Involved parents. Wonderful place to learn and grow in a diverse setting. There is something for everyone here. And it’s such a warm, friendly place. I attended Einstein for my freshmen year of high school. My only good teachers were the ones I had in higher level classes. However any on-levels that I attended were bare-minimum effort and were physically painful to sit through. Furthermore I found the environment very depressing and dead inside. On top of that I never felt like admin cared or encouraged students in any way to rise above average standards. On my very first day of school the principals announcement to the class was that he was disappointed in our behavior from orientation, which may have been true-but needless to say was not encouraging. Overall, I just felt like morale was very low as well as expectations throughout my time at Einstein. AEHS has exceeded our expectations for a public high school in Montgomery County. Such a supportive learning environment with many opportunities for challenge. Lots of AP and IB courses and dedicated faculty teaching students coming from varying socio-economic backgrounds. Environment breeds free-thinking, respectful and compassionate individuals who recognize the importance and value of diversity in society and possess the skills to create change. Wonderful experience!

column1: In Central New York this may not be the best school, but having gone to other parts of NY I realize how amazing the education I got here was. I graduated with a complete understanding of all subjects and I can read, spell and think of more than three things at once, which I cannot accredit to many schools where I am now. I have just finished out my junoir year at this school, and am going to be a senoir and all I can say is that I couldn't have asked for a better school. I have been going to Cincy for my entire life, and it has been one of the greatest experiences. You may sometimes think that the teachers play favorites, but they truly dont. They grade you based on how hard you try, how much you time you put into something, and how much ability you use. I failed 2 years of math class because I chose not to do the work and I chose not to show my skills at it. The teachers only gave me the grades that I earned by doing the work, and even if they were having a bad day they would stay after school to give you any help you needed. They are truly amazing people, they show so much heart and character to the students that you wont get in a large city school. We had a teacher transfer back to Cincy after getting a better teaching job at a different school with better pay and hours because she missed her classroom family. At Cincy, you arent just another face in the crowd. You are part of a very large group of tightly knit friends and a very large family. You may think that your kid wont get as good an education at CIncinnatus Central School, but believe me when I say this: you walk out of that school knowing so much more than you would ever think. You get to have experiences that you will only possibly get once in a lifetime. In my opinion, you will get some of the best teachers possible in CNY, and Im honestly scared to graduate this year because I dont want to leave this school. It is and has been the greatest experience for me, and I wish I could do it all over again. If you want a good school with good teachers and a great staff that will treat you with respect and always be there when you need help, I couldnt reccomend Cincy any more than I already am. Excellent school with passionate teachers who really care for their students.

column3: My daughter had a bad experience with peer relationships before coming to Pine Creek as a sophomore. During her 3 years there, she felt it to be a much more friendly environment and as a result, became more involved in student activities. Also, her much loved sport of swimming was enhanced by the friendliness,inclusiveness, and support of the team and coaches. There were even rules around prom that if it weren't for the support of the principal (now retired) to make an exception, my daughter would not have been able to attend with her boyfriend. On education and teacher quality, it's one of the finest in the state. We have a gifted son who doesn't fit into the typical high school mold. He really likes Pine Creek High School because of the atmosphere (more college than high school) and mutual respect students give to one another. The variety of courses offered in the school's catalog, along with school sponsored sports teams and clubs, are also benefits to attending PCHS. Best school in the state. The teachers here care about the students. The staff wants to see them succeed, not only in the specific class, but in life in general. There will always be things to improve on at every school, but the base of Pine Creek is made of well meaning, inspiring staff members that push Pine Creek to its best every year. Pine Creek is an amazing school. The tech program is great (we have programming through APCS, and then there are classes like app dev and game programming), the sports program is amazing, we are working toward everyone having an iPad, the music is great, and there are so many classes it can be hard to choose. Many of the negative reviews were clearly written by students from rival schools, because the majority of Pine Creek students are very kind and accepting. As a person who has always had trouble making friends, I had no trouble making lots of them here. The teachers are generally very helpful. There are tons of clubs for people to join, making it easy to stay involved in the community. Lunches are great because we order in from restaurants, so we have Chinese, Subway, Burgers, Italian, Pizza, Chick-fil-a, Salad, and more. Campus is open for juniors and seniors, so people can go get lunch somewhere else. There is a big student parking lot, so driving to school is easy. Overall an amazing school. The school was great until they decided to change everything. The whole religious debate was a bit over the top. The class sizes gradually grew and grew which limited the attention each student received. The period of time called seminar was removed from the schedule. It was essentially a homeroom where students could get help from teachers, but now it has been replaced with an additional class. It is like going to school in a prison. They force the students into the cafeteria and refuse to let them leave. They also do not allow visitors unless the visitor is a parent....also not cool. So they took away the opportunity of seminar and lunch time as being help times for students needing to make up assignments or receive extra help, does that really make sense? If your child is a self motivated , self teaching and strong student this school will be fine as would any school. If you have an average student with any possibility of needing any help what so ever......DON'T go to Pine Creek HS. It also has an atmosphere of a Juvenile Hall....No respect. Rating for pine creek academics is at best C-/D I would not have gone to PCHS if I could do it over again. Terrible school. Non enthused with it. Academics are only if the student is self driven. Sports and coaches only recognize clicks and even parents have clicks in order to get their child on a team or given a title. Great school, athletics are top notch. All the staff care about the school and the legacy it holds. Your student will be challenged but they will be ready to go to college and supported by their teachers all of the way. The academics are amazing and the teachers really care about their students. The school is very safe and protected by multiple officers. Counseling staff is phenomenal and the college counselor is AMAZING and will help you to achieve your dreams and get to where you want to go. I wouldn’t have wanted to go to high school anywhere else in the springs!

column1: This school has been an extended family to us, we are on our last one of four to graduate and with each year the school has improved, encouraged, and grown to be a successful learning intuition. I am excited for their future.

column3: I would rate this school the worst I've ever seen in all aspects! From what I've seen they could care less about the students. I don't know how they can still operate. The worst school I have ever seen and the reason many families move from Galva is for their children to be treated with respect and fair

column1: Ambulances and fire trucks always at the school. This school is terrible, the absolute worst in the county. If this is what Baltimore County Schools are like, my child will not go to these schools. Teachers and students fighting often. Drugs, and hardly no rules being followed. Many of the administrators are unprofessional, show favortism, and too friendly with students. Many of them are not doing their jobs. There is no consistency with this school, fights all the time, poor education, kids always in the hallway. I took my daughter out of this school right away. I tried to be involved but sensed my involvement was not welcome. There was no respect for me, and all I was doing was being a concerned parent. My child was definitely not safe at this school and I do not want her safety compromised being there. This school should be shut down. My child's education suffered. This is my son's 3rd year at Woodlawn High School and he has seen much success in his years here. He has improved his grades from below average in standard classes to excellent grades in Honors, GT, and AP courses because of teacher's constant dedication to working with students in school and out of school on their spare time. He has matured exceptionally with being apart of the magnet engineering program, and the robotics and music program there. He was also able to be apart of an internship with the Maryland Transit Administration and the Baltimore Redline, college tours of HBCU's around the nation through the school, and perform at varies concerts with the music program at Woodlawn. Woodlawn in my opinion is a school with a tremendous amount of potential that is waiting to be seen though its students and I am glad the school is pushing students in the right direction when it comes to building character. Even though Woodlawn has just recently gone through restructuring, the school continues to work to push their student to become leaders of society. The school's motto is "Witness the Change", Well I believe I have witnessed this change within my son. I spent all four of my High School years at Woodlawn, graduating in 2007. I currently have a degree in Electrical Engineering from a top 20 University in Engineering. Woodlawn is about what you make of it. During long nights of studying in college, I would reminisce moments where my coach would say, "... how bad do you want it?" I remember teachers encouraging me to work-hard and focus because they recognized my potential before I could see it. Woodlawn taught me to be a leader and to never give up on my dreams! Woodlawn was a great experience for me. What I see is parents/guardians blaming adminstration and teachers for problems that students have. Woodlawn has always had a negative stereotype but was nothing like I've heard. The parents need to get more involved and build more positive relationships with staff to help all children succeed. I say stop complaining and help change. I have been successful since leaving Woodlawn and received a Maters degree. Woodlawn has some of the most caring and hardworking teachers in Baltimore County Pulic School system!!! I attended Woodlawn for 10th- 12th grade. I graduated in 2005. In my opinion Woodlawn was not a good school. I transferred from a private school and a lot of what was being taught in the 10th grade there were things I learned in middle school. A number of students, more than expected, could not even read at a high school grade level. I honestly tried to get something out of it but they were behind. Learning about prepositions in the 10th grade is just wild to me. I hear they have gotten rid of a lot of the teachers and changed a lot with the curriculum. They really needed to. It's much better now supposedly. I attended 10th-12th grade and graduated in 1996. All 3 years we were given the answers for the Maryland State tests. The test answers are multiple choice 1 finger was A, 2 fingers B and so on. I can't speak on what goes on there today however, now as a parent it's been a priority for my children not to attend Woodlawn Middle or high school based on my experiences. I wasn't prepared for college.

column3: Both my husband and I attended Lakeshore High School. After graduating from both undergraduate and graduates schools, we moved back to the area and bought a house in the Lakeshore school district again. We're looking forward to our children going to Lakeshore. It's an incredible school where the teachers truly care about each student and the staff works to know the students and their families. Great athletic and band programs, as well as the math & science center too. There was a very diverse group of students and there was never a lack of things to do. I went from a local private school for one year to Lakeshore and felt like I was a little behind everyone else. That being said, the teachers were great.

column1: I absolutely adore this school! I can not imagine being anywhere else because nothing can compare. To be honest I have gotten use to seeing teachers working at the bare minimum because they have just given up. Which is why when I came to this school, and I saw how motivated the teachers are, it just blew my mind. Not only that, before I came to this school I use to sleep during class and still get straight A's, not anymore. I don't mean to brag but they really have some top quality kids, everyone has something great to offer to the classroom and their community. The only con here is that I don't think they have enough funding. I attended Fenway in the late 80's, just a few years after it was created. I loved that school! The people I met - both students and teachers- were amazing. I had studied at Boston Latin School and Newton South before the Fenway, and it was absolutely my favorite. Miss Schirmer and the other teachers (educators, really) cared about us as individuals and nurtured our strengths. I was able to take AP classes at local colleges: B.U. & Simmons. Then I got a full scholarship to B.U.! I credit my experience at the Fenway (okay, and some fairly good study habits). I will never forget my experience at the Fenway. It's a fantastic charter school. Just ask Jordan & Jonathan Knight of NKOTB ;) I'd say they did pretty well for themselves too. my school is really good and their is a lot of support for student and i love my school

column3: I am highly disappointed in the school...my daughter has been enduring bullying and harassment since entering the high school as a freshman. We have been in numerous times to discuss this matter with the appropriate staff. Their response has been that she needs to learn to ignore it and that they cannot follow the harasser around all day. Are you serious? A child can only take so much bullying and harassment before they snap. I am now in the process of filing a complaint because they have allowed a harassing student to return as a student at the school after already 2 expulsions. Our children should have the right to a safe environment to receive an education, this is not the case here. I'm working on having my children withdrawn from the school district to have their education home-based where they will feel safe and be able to concentrate on their education. As a previous employee I can say that everything you will read in these reviews is sad, but true. J.M. Weatherwax High School Both of my children have graduated from this high school and have earned Master's Degrees. This high school offers more Advanced Placement courses than any other school in the county. It's students achieve higher college placement scores than any other high school in the area. The school has just implemented a one on one technology program where each student is issued an RT Surface tablet. The school is also home to a Skill Center where students from other schools in the county can attend. It has out standing activities as well as an extensive athletic program which students can join. It is an outstanding school. The school is just part of a system warehousing and babysitting our youth.

column1: My child had some fantastic teachers at this school. Teachers that really made a long term difference in his life. We moved out of district but I have to say, we are really sad we had to leave. This was a wonderful school. As a former SASA student and present PhD candidate, I would certainly recommend this school to all parent around the area (esp. those who fall on the lower-income side of the spectrum, like my family did). Now, I graduated ten years ago, so I'm sure things have changed (a beautiful new theater, for example), but I do have to say that I'm disappointed John Olvera is still around. He really did all students a disservice with his erratic, unhelpful, even harmful teaching methods. (As a college-level instructor, reflecting on his behavior has helped me from falling into any of those bad habits.) A stronger foreign language program would really help prepare students, as well. I attended this school for a short amount of time (as a student), however, while I was there I absolutely hated it. The building itself barely has any windows, there is no air conditioning, except for in the auditorium and the part that they added onto. At the beginning of the school year the classrooms were extremely hot and it felt like you couldn't breathe in there. Half the classrooms are so small that it could barely hold the amount of students in the class. Most of the classes did not have widows. If your son or daughter is claustrophobic, do not send them there. Parts of the walls in the cafeteria seemed to be kicked in or just missing.The school just seems so run down. Some of my teachers were decent, while I dreaded going to other teachers' classes. One of the classes I dreaded going to was my algebra class. The teacher was awful. Right away he gave us huge amounts of homework that was due the next day. It took me hours to get that homework done, and it got to the point where I wasn't able to do my homework from my other classes.The same teacher also yelled at a few students who forgot to bring their textbook to class (mind you it was only the second day we had them). All they focus on at the school is work, and you don't get a minute to breathe. The entire time I was there I was stressed and would go home having breakdowns. I do not recommend this school. This school is not as good as people say it is. My experience at this school was horrible would not recommend if you want your child to retain their soul. I've attended this school for about 4 coming onto 5 years and their treatment of the half-day students is less than acceptable. They treat us like second-rate students not even giving us the full experience saying "You have those opportunities at your homeschool" when in fact most other schools in the Saginaw area don't. Still, it seems counterintuitive as if one were to go to SASA in the morning and have it as your homeschool and go to some other school in the afternoon it would be quite difficult to attend student council meetings. Treat your half-day students with the same amount of respect and give them the same amount of opportunities is all I'm asking because all SASA students no matter half-day or full-day are still SASA students.

column3: Amazing school spirit, dedicated, passionate teachers and staff, friendly and kind students who do not discriminate in any way. Protective and safe environment with at least two police officers and many members of the staff walking around, chill enough to start a conversation but attentive enough to keep you safe. If you are planning to attend this school, ignore its old reputation and enter it with a fresh state of mind. Participate as much as you can and gorge yourself in school activities such as dances (always fun with or without a date), Spirit Week/F.A.N.T.A.S.T.I.C.S., sports, and clubs! It may seem somewhat intimidating, but exploring what's outside of your comfort zone will lead you an unforgettable high school experience. In that sense, you will get the most out of what the school has to offer. Most individuals who rate this school lower than it should be usually have an outside bias due to the past reputation (it has completely changed now, no gangs/fights at all), and are generally inactive in many of the activities offered. Simply incorporate yourself to the school, and your high school experience will be worthwhile. - J.S. I went to this school a month. Honestly I dislike this school. This school has a bad reputation of kids cutting school, foul language and poor education and teachers. well... lets talk about the teachers. I see kids in gangs and the teachers don`t care. The kids are not supposed to Join/attend gangs. and the teachers say foul language to the Kids that they are teaching.(I have some evidence on my phone.) well... In general this school is a bad reputation. Milpitas high school are caring and more supportive. It also has higher education than this school that I`m attending right now. (Yerba Buena). That is why we are moving out of San Jose because overall this school is a bad place. I graduated in 2011. All I could say is that I still regret my years in this high school after 5 years. Overall the school has some great teachers and some bad ones that falls through cracks. Honestly, the only negative thing about this school is the fact that the school's administration put the needs of community over the needs of the students. One giant example is the gym, the administration of the school would rather allow the community to have priority over the use of the gym then the students. Other than that the school is decent, in the sense that it has great teachers and a very smart and kind student body. This school is terrible and have a drug problem on campus. This school lacks diversity of students and the campus itself is super dirty. I strongly recommend you go to Silver Creek or Santa Teresa. I teach Industrial Engineering at YB. It is a CTE, 4 year program. The students have the opportunity to use industrial grade laser cutters, welders, CNC machines and 3D printers. They use Autodesk Fusion 360 to design prototypes and products that solve problems they are working on. 2nd year students focus on robotics preparing them to design, create and build autonomous vehicles. During the students senior year they do a capstone project. In past years, students would modify the go karts that were purchased for the seniors capstone projects. Stop by the engineering building and check the program!! This school is very poor. They are in debt and charge $1399 for a lost chromebook. Don’t recommend coming here!!!

column1: Parents are very supportive of school activities, and the work the teachers do. The board and administration are working to help teachers and students, by implemented new programs, such as dual enrollment in college algebra and Fresh comp. New labs and slide projectors help the students and teachers. Most of the students are hard-working, goal-oriented, and self disciplined. Because the number of students in each class ranges from 15-22, teachers help each student more and know each one well. After attending since kindergarten, my child completed Calculus and Spanish 3. My child will be attending college on full academic and athletic scholarships. He or she had excellent opportunities for leadership in the band, drama, and athletics. The faculty are well-qualified, caring, and hard-working role models. Daily, each class says the pledge, has a devotion, and prayer. The same Christian youth leaders meet monthly with the same class from 7th thru 12th grade. All of our international students are doing well in class and extracurricular activities. Graduates are published authors, recognized scientists, and graduates of Notre Dame law school. Pre-k-12th faculty work together. When making decisions about education, do not mistake great Websites and prestige for competence! Starkville Academy offers small classes and many opportunities for students to participate in extra-curricular activities. Don't mistake quantity for quality; many of those opportunities lack element of quality. Students may participate, but their experience is limited by lack of leadership from coaches, teachers, and administrators. There have been many instances of inequitable treatment in sports my daughter experienced. Also, I'm aware of different treatment in the classroom depending on who the child is from a social standpoint. Where do I start? Well, first of all SA lacks the time management skill and tries to cram seven classes into one day. The block system would be a godsend to all students attending. Teachers and coaches alike try to get as much done as possible, but with only fifty minutes per class, only so much can be accomplished. What's seems to be their biggest worry is a student on a cell phone. Administration is constantly walking by classrooms for the soul purpose of trying to catch students on their phones. What's more is the fact that the school is in need of repairs in many places, but instead invests more money into the football stadium and field. The school doesn't even financially support the art classes such as band (the roof inside the band hall has many holes in it) or art 1, 2, or 3. With the tuition they're making parents pay, a little money here and there shouldn't be so hard to use towards the art classes. I am a student there (obviously) and almost all of the other students can prove these problems. Most of my friends are either certainly or determining switching to starkville high as it provides the block system, more class options and so on. Certainly not worth the investment in terms of a higher quality education. The appeal of this school appears to be homogenous middle class environment. My children have received an excellent and well-rounded education in a safe environment where the teachers, administrators and staff truly care about their success. Recent additions such as an elementary STEM lab, iPad carts for all grades and Surface Pro 3's for Juniors and seniors have greatly enhanced technology and improved academic rigor. Class sizes average 18 students which is ideal in my opinion for optimal learning. I would highly recommend Starkville Academy to anyone that values an independent school education and is considering it as their school of choice. This school was created as a haven for white students to avoid integration. That's it's reason to exist, and it does it well. Both of my children attended this school and had a wonderful experience. They were prepared for college and beyond. SA has a great teaching staff and administration team. Everyone is welcoming and friendly. Great learning environment! Outstanding school! I would not want my children to be enrolled anywhere else. The teacher and other faculty are very friendly and welcoming. They also take time to make appointments with parents, in which they answer all questions and/or address any concerns. Christian values are taught, & Critical thinking skills and are in some form applied in each classroom. My children are thriving acedemically and socially. Some believe that private schooling does not leave your child prepared for the “real world,” and I could not disagree more. The newer state required common core teaching methods in the public school system do not prepare children for academically for college where every parent wants the next real world stop to be in their child’s life. I highly recommend this school! I love the way the students see a displayed Bible verse as they drive up. Its a great conversation starter for the children as they get out of the car to begin their day. The teachers are friendly and approachable. My grandson is learning so much at SA. I have loved my visits there!!

column1: Best high school in San Diego County. Everyone top to bottom cares deeply about boys education. There place for every boy who can handle a rigorous curriculum. They enter as boys and leave as well educated gentlemen. My son LOVED the "Saints" experience. This is the only private school to send a boy to in San Diego. the Students are a true family, the academics are top notch and the extra curricular activities are some of the best around. Also, the sports programs are some of the best. Having a son who is a senior this year and another as a freshman this year, I can not say ENOUGH about this school! Saints has been everything and so much more than we hoped for our sons. It truly takes your sons and shapes them into fine young gentlemen! Our boys are both so happy here and say they can't imagine going to school anywhere else. It is a true brotherhood! I'm very pleased with the education my son is getting at Saints. They really know how to help the boys bond and build responsibility and critical thinking. The academics keep his head in the books, and he is encouraged to aspire to college. The variety of extracurricular activities exposes him to many careers and vocations. The scheduling and pace of the curriculum is tailored for boys and manages them well. The traditions of the school also give the boys good reasons to achieve. I highly encourage parents with a high school son pursue admission to Saints. I graduated from SAINTS in 1955, that is 65 years ago. All of us held our teachers as Gods. They really cared about all of us and prepared us for life in many ways. To this day I still refer back to rules and formulas I learned at SAINTS. God has been very good to me and SAINTS was the BEST teacher for life there could be with any frame of reference. I loved SAINTS as a student and love it still as an alumnus. Thank you SAINTS for all you taught me. I've owned my own business since a student and still do and operate it every day. Thank you Father Glenn, I know your watching me from upstairs. Sanford E. Sanford, Class of "55".

column1: Last year I went to this school, but, unfortunatly I transfered this year to a new school. I find that I really do miss the staff and students from this excellent school. The small feeling of the school really helps you to feel a sense of belonging. Most of the teachers here have wonderful ways of teaching that helps kids to understand the material. Most discipline problems are resolved immediatly. The principal here is also very nice. I especially liked the band program at this school. This was a great school for a long time, but the current administration is not improving. Our testing scores are down, student, teacher and parent moral is down thanks to the principal and current school board. maybe we do need a change. The students of T.C. deserve to be at the top again, they deserve it!!! Tri-Central is a great small school with caring teachers and staff! All 3 of my children graduated from Tri-Central and were well prepared for college. My youngest took advantage of the AP classes and started out with 9 credits for college. The board does an awesome job now that some administration has been changed for the better. I would highly recommend this school. Also there are TONS on extra curricular activities that aren't athletic. Spellbowl, Ecology Club are just a sample. TC is a great school with a small, close knit family like atmosphere. They have done an excellent job with their AP classes. Tri-Central high school...their motto is "Small School, Big Results". I would change it to "Small School, Few Results". Many of their great teachers have left and been replaced with brand new teachers who lack experience. The guidance counselor is harsh, rude, and not encouraging to students at all. We have been very disappointed with this small school and wish we had chosen Eastern instead. I would say this school is below average, at best.

They have to wear blazers that were like $90 and didnt inforce the kids to wear them. I can not wait till the last months of school are over. My daughter will not be returning. But Pontiac is a Horriable school and I wouldnt advise anyone to attend!! I am a former student at the school. Some people say that parent involvement is needed, but parents can't do everything on their own. My parents were the most involved people in the school, my whole family was. But without help from the school, my family trying to help is pointless. So yes, parents need to be more involved, but the teachers and staff need to be more involved too. I've had teachers who didn't care about the students, even the ones who tried. I've also had teachers who didn't care what grade was on the report card, as long as enough students passed. i see everyday what goes on on the school bus , and at the school. the high school along with the middle school are terrible, its scary., and so sad. I currently have two kids in the Pontiac Schools ITA program. At first glance, I was very impressed. Then, I attended the parent/teacher conference. My impression then turned south. It was a cluster F^%$. I also understand that the teachers have taken a hit in salaries. I must live in Pontiac due to an impossible situation. My kids are really trying to do their best, but you can't get water out of a rock. These schools are a real mess. I think I will go up the road to Oxford Schools if things keep getting worse. I am a student at PHS, and, frankly, this school is very unsatisfactory. I don't blame the teachers or students entirely (although the students should have a bit more self-discipline and etc., and some of the teachers should actually try to control their classes), but a lot could change. Students don't really have a say in this school - every time I try to speak up about an issue, I get interrupted and quieted. Is this what a school is? I can't even walk into some of my classes without having some idiot goofing off to impress their "friends." It's ridiculous that I'm not allowed to express my concerns and suggestions. Personally, I think the school would be a lot better if it could accept criticism; the authority is way too arrogant and feel anything else other than what they dictate is incorrect, and they won't hesitate to make you feel as such. It's horrible. What I'm trying to say here is that this is a school that needs loads of improvement, but I still have a little hope for it. column1: The only thing I am concerned about, generally speaking is bullying. Not the obvious type. But the undertones that exist within different groups of the student body. While most would deny, It is not okay for teachers to let students make fun of others. And turn the other cheek. And it is not okay for teachers to say inappropriate things to the kids. This is still a learning environment and they learn what they see. Just because it is a small community school doesn't mean, it doesn't have its own issues. Best public school even comparable to those private schools without the high tuition costs. Look at the great test scores of the students of this school and it just proves that you do not have to pay such high tuition costs to achieve the same results. We made the mistake of sending our child to a high cost private school when one could have achieved the same or even better education at a fraction of the cost. El Segundo is a beautiful and quiet community and we are truly fortunate to have found such a wonderful hidden gem. Best kept secret in California. Perfect place for kids to grow and get top-notch education in a very family-friendly safe town. See even greater things coming for the future of el segundo. I loved the experience I had at this school. I graduated from here over 60 years ago, It was the very best .

column3: I am so blessed to go to this school! Unbelievable students and faculty! We are an awesome school! Our son is a sophmore in the Math and Science Academy and we, as well as our son, couldn't be happier with this school. Not only are we pleased with the Academy's course offerings, teachers, and leadership, but we are very impressed with the overall school. The staff, facilities, extracurricular offerings, and overall atmosphere of the school are excellent. We feel that OL does an excellent job at integrating the Academy students with the school and truly offers a positive and cohesive educational experience for all of it's Dolphins! My daughter is a freshman at OLHS in the Math and Science Academy. Having attended several events at the school (orientations, sports events, etc) I am very impressed with how organized the faculty is and how smoothly the school functions. The atmosphere is very professional. My daughter loves all the opportunities for extracurricular involvement as well. She has great things to say about her teachers. Everything about the school is first rate. I went to to OL from grades 9-12 and it is one of the most supportive communities I have ever witnessed. I recommend the Math and Science Academy, along with the school. Every teacher left a positive impact on me and has helped me grow in some form. We moved to the area 4+ years ago, before my daughter was in High School, but chose our area to live based on reviewing the HS's. We chose right! My daughter strongly disliked MIddle School, but is now a sophomore at OLHS and doesn't want to leave. There is something for everyone, interests and scholastic-wise. She started out at the math and science academy, which is wonderful, but we decided, with other commitments, the homework level and stress were not for her, so this year she is doing mainstream classes, and still loves the school. The band program is great, with lots of parental involvement. It's a great learning environment, and I've been around the school a lot (drop-offs in morning, football games, parent nights, volunteering, etc) and have never seen any person or behavior that would be cause for concern. For me, Ocean Lakes was perfect. I feel like it's amazing in every way possible. The school is incredibly diverse; and I feel like that was an huge plus in enriching the school's atmosphere. There is something for everyone. The Math and Science Academy, our theatre team, and our sports are all really great. Literally..Ocean Lakes is perfect in every way. Academically, we have some of the best scores. And Athletically, we have the best games and scores. And another plus, the teachers are fantastic. Most of them (or atleast the teachers I had), actually knew their stuff, and were willing to help you out any time you needed it. The best part, I feel, is that there are not that many "cliques", not really any of those 'rich, snobby' people. Everybody fits in. And we have plenty of clubs and activities, to make new friends and meet new people. I would definitely recommend Ocean Lakes...it's perfect, and I made many happy memories there. Two of my sons have already graduated from this school. I have one son who will graduate in 2018. I love the school. It's one of the best in the area. I love the diversity and the teachers' push to ensure the students are doing well academically. The only thing I don't care for is their bullying policy. I had two sons who were bullied. They both fought back and they both were suspended. I had to appeal the suspensions. My son has had an excellent experience in the academy program at this school!

column3: Although not aesthetically pleasing at first glance, you have to look deeper at the end results.....the school provides an outstanding education. The teachers and staff are dedicated and passionate about their profession. Eastern prepares and provides their students with the skills and knowledge needed across the spectrum of society. In other words, they will prepare your child for to compete in the highest scholastic environments for college and beyond, while also preparing students who choose to immediately enter the work force and be value added to society. Don't let the rough exterior fool you as it has so many others who pay college type tuition at a private school in the area for the same or lesser quality education. Maybe I am biased because i had to come here against my will because i was kicked out of Trinity High School (an all boys private school), but this school is really second rate. Some of the teaching staff even thought that the majority of students in the school were inherently bad. I am no perfect student, but i think that i at the very least deserve a benefit of the doubt. Some of the teachers even ganged up on a couple of me and my friends for being from a certain part of town, telling us that we were given the silver spoon our whole lives and did not have to work. Which i find troubling, even if that is true there is no reason to tell us that. The students for the most part are lazy and unmotivated besides the Advanced Placement students. The school is atrocious, it is dirty, with graffiti everywhere, and overall a terrible thing to look at. There are security guards roaming the halls, which makes students feel like they are in prison. Overall, i made some good friends here, and definitely saw a side of the world that i had not ever seen before. luckily i only had to stay there for a semester and a half so i could transfer to Collegiate Academy. Like the other poster, I was also expelled from Trinity High School, they have really tightened the belts on rules and no one gets away with anything. They hand Jugs out like free candy. I have been at Eastern for half a year so far, and let me just say, this school is a CAKE WALK compared to Trinity. I don't even have to study for tests and I get an A! Did I also mention I'm in their "Honors" program. The facilities are trash compared to Trinity. Next year I hope to move up to as many AP classes as possible, because the education is a joke and is way too easy. The students here are extremely lazy and rude. The teachers and students also pick on my because of what school I went to before, It's so unfair, because ever since I was expelled, I haven't exactly tried harder in school, I have just stopped goofing around. The family feeling I had at Trinity doesn't even exist here. The students are vicious and go out of their way to be mean. I really miss my old school. The school's renovations look great! And most of the teachers are really passionate about their jobs. They definitely want the best for the students. And I can tell that my counselor really cares about me and my well-being. Although the administration could use some work, the school and the staff is generally great! I would suggest this school to anyone. I am a Senior, and I feel completely prepared for college, and I can tell I've received a wonderful education! Eastern is a well known High School in the Middletown district. My husband and I thought it was supposed to be a good school. I'm not sure what standards people expect from Eastern,however they are not as high as ours. If you don't mind your child `s teacher talking on their cell phones, leaving for the class period, or your child not having ANY books then this is the school for you. If you expect your child to be prepared for college this is NOT the place for you! It speaks volumes when teachers and staff do not send their own children to the school where they teach. Very, very disappointed!! Worst school ever. Terrible teachers. The counselors and principle do not put students first. My oldest child went to Eastern, his siblings will not. All three of my children attended and graduated from Eastern High School and all applied to their dream schools and were accepted. My three students took a heavy load of AP courses, beginning in their sophomore year. Other classes were in the Advanced program which is a step above the Honors courses. This school isn't a "cake-walk" and you generally won't get easy As and if you do, then move up the ladder and into advanced classes. The teachers are as caring as the students, meaning if the class is apathetic, then so too can be the teachers. Test scores generally run high and teachers do have to deal with some very spoiled-rotten kids who can be a problem. All three of my students graduated in the top 2% of their class, one is now a chemist, another owns her own business and the last is a physician. Eastern High School and it's educators worked well for my family but then you only get out of a school what effort you put in. I am an alumni of Eastern HS. I would contend that it is the best community school in Louisville. The advanced academic classes I took helped me earn a great academic scholarship to college where I was well-prepared for success. I enjoyed being involved in extra-curricular activities and attending a school close to home. I couldn't be happier with my decision to send my daughter here! They have an incredible girls lacrosse team along with many other sports! They also have a club for everyone!! I will be sending my son with ADHD here to because I know they can handle him and he will not get bullied finally!! They are a school that I have finally found that doesn't tolerate it!! My daughter is a honor roll student and I am very pleased with her education here!! Go Eagles!! We made a decision to buy a home so our children could attend Eastern High School based on greatschools.org and it is one of the worst decisions we have ever made in their lives. Bullied at this school, they did nothing about it. 3 of my sons went to Eastern and graduated from 2010 to 2017. They all went to college and graduated and did very well. My youngest son just recently graduated from U of K at the top of his class 2021. He thanks Eastern High for his success.

column1: This school has fallen in its religious and moral values and is not the calibur it once was. The favoritism and clinques still exist very strongly and the AP classes do not teach the student how to learn the material and past the tests resulting in a lack of credits for college. The cost of tuition of the school does not in the academic results that a student could recive in a public school. The school is seemingly amazing when I first looked at it but almost everything the school shows is just a facade. The moral values of the students is low, the classes don't challenge enough, most "clubs" are nonexistent, and it is very questionable where the tuition money goes. Of the positives in this school though are the how caring some of the teachers are, some of the sports are great (girls soccer and basketball and boys baseball), and how much they prep students for the SAT. Overall though the school was very disappointing to me. We just finished our first year at MCC and I couldn't be happier. The academics and college preparation this school offers is wonderful and the staff is very involved and works hard to keep the kids on track. It is a smaller school than most public schools so it doesn't offer as many extra curriculars and fun after school activities but not so small that it feels like it is lacking. The education my son is receiving I believe is above average and he is very happy here. We could not be happier with the academics, teachers and staff. I shall definitely be sending the rest of my children through MCC. Excellent experience all 4years. My child felt comfortable going to faculty for assistance. I believe the retreats they have organized gave my child positive experiences, raising awareness of the career path to study, and is prepared for college and is extremely confident. My son's experience at the school was excellent. He received an excellent education, with the opportunity to take many advanced classes. He completed 12 AP classes while in High School, and got accepted into his dream school -- Notre Dame! He also had the opportunity to play a variety of sports. MCC continues to improve as a quality Catholic school as is evident with each graduating class. This school prides itself, and rightly so, on developing the spiritual growth of each student while preparing him/her for the rigors of life beyond MCC. They do this by working collectively as a faculty and with parents to meet the individual needs of each student. They truly believe it takes a village to raise a child to become a confident, upstanding young adult. Thank you, MCC! I am a parent of two Melbourne Central Catholic graduates. The education and life-lessons my children received from this school are priceless. The teachers and administration are caring and highly qualified I highly recommend this school to any family that is seeking a unique and special experience for their teenager. Go Hustlers! I transferred my sophomore year of high school into a private school where I had to wear a uniform, go to mass and do a lot of things that I wasn’t familiar with. Right now I am currently a senior at Melbourne Central Catholic and I am proud to say it. I think we can all agree that no school is perfect, but I don’t know where I would be right now if I didn’t go here. I believe that the friendships that I have made, the teachers that I have met, the coaches that have helped me along will always be in my heart. If you want to be a part of a family that cares about one another, helps one another, then you have come to the right place here at Melbourne Central Catholic High school.-Thank you As an alumna of MCC, I have been prepared spiritually and professionally. I experienced excellence in academics, athletics, and faith-based service opportunities. Teachers and staff were committed to helping me succeed, and I am incredibly thankful for my time at MCC. The past four years at Melbourne Central Catholic (MCC) have truly been a blessing to me. There is a common misconception that small schools do not offer the true high school experience, but I can attest to the opposite. The close, tight-knit community at MCC is academically competitive, spiritually nourishing, and mentally stimulating. The faculty and staff are clearly committed to the instruction and improvement of the student body, and are adaptable to the needs of their students, especially in this pandemic. Most importantly, the relationships I have cultivated with my teachers and counselors, as well as my academic progress and involvement in a myriad of extracurricular activities, helped to guide me in my college applications and now prepare me for the next level of education. Thank you MCC, and Go Hustlers! MCC has a wonderful community and wonderful educators. My children received a strong academic foundation and a strong faith formation from Melbourne Central Catholic. The educators are very caring and have a vested interest in every child. My children are thriving at their universities and I truly believe it is from the foundation of a well rounded education. Our first year at MCC has been a wonderful experience! The teachers provide the right amount of structure and guidance, and I am impressed by their feedback and overall communication. Most importantly, academics are held high and I know my daughter is receiving a quality education. MCC has provided me with a community filled with friendship, academics, and faith. MCC has a wide variety of leadership opportunities that I have been able to participate in such as Student Government/Council and Green and Gold School Ambassadors. Also, the teachers at MCC strive to ensure that each student receives an excellent education and always support the students in their endeavors.

column3: Two of our children graduated from West High. One was very motivated and excelled and the other had many learning challenges. Both were treated with respect and had teachers that were well loved by the students. Their AP courses are great for the gifted students but I'd also like to mention that the option the school district offers to challenged students was a godsend. The program allows for students to attend a class to prep for the GED but when a student achieves the GED, they are still awarded the high school diploma. That diploma aided my child to become a successful person in life.

column1: This is what a small town school is all about! The classes are small, teachers and administrators know every student and, more importantly, care about every student. They make a concerted effort to serve the needs of each student - across the spectrum of abilities. Student who struggle are given the attention they need; students that excel are provided with opportunities to reach their full potential. While the size of the school does limited the breadth of classes offered (e.g., only Spanish is offered as a foreign language), what is available is top notch. While other schools have nice physical structure and greater resources, I doubt the educational experience can match what is available at Delavan. As parents, we are thrilled with our decision to live in Delavan and have our child attend school here. This school is absolutely terrible. Delavan C.U.S.D. #703 has left me totally unprepared for life on all fronts. Academically this school is a joke. The books are pre colonial at best. The teachers, obviously not motivated by paycheck, couldn't care less about your education or well being. The administrative staff are paid far more than they should be and are commonly referred to as leeches. In regards to the IT department...words don't quite do justice to their incompetence and general computer illiteracy. The sports program is underfunded and substandard. The coaches know nothing about the activity or sport in which they coach. The programs could be aptly compared to a second rate nanny. All in all this apathy ridden school is, in the simplest term, bad. I love this school, it's one of the best. Great teachers and staff. You can definitely tell they care for the students The staff and administrators can be very rude and unhelpful at times. The dean doesn’t solve issues, and the janitors are just about the only cool people there. It’s sad that janitors are more helpful than teachers when a teachers job is to help a student grow and learn. Janitors have to take care of the school. The computer classes only reach you how to run certain programs, or code robots. All of the kids who aren’t interested in that and up failing, I think that coding should be an optional class so that the students who do join participate and make it easier for the tech teachers Outstanding experience with this school. The measures above do not accurately reflect the Dual Credit opportunities in which students can graduate with 30 credit hours, work-based learning opportunities, and CO-Op Learning. Positive through all facets of our experience. Exceptional, real-world experiences for students. Teachers KNOW the students and build relationships with them. The school is amazing, the teachers are supportive and hardworking. Additionally, they make the learning environments comfortable for students. The teachers truly want to get to know the students!
