column3: We love the faculty and staff at Monterey! I have not had any issues at all with anyone and all are willing to assist when I need it. My daughter (sophmore) loves her school and would be crushed if we took her somewhere else. My son will be a freshman next year and is looking forward to his high school years at MHS. I highly recommend this school to anyone looking for a great, quality education and a family atmosphere. I put a 2 star but teally i feel we had no help at all so I would really rate it a 1 star. Though Monterey High School as a whole is not without its issues (including discipline, drugs, etc.), overall, the staff and adminstration take the time to ensure that all students feel known and cared for and are willing to listen to and account for the desires, complaints, and opinions of its student body. The homework as an honors student can be excessive, but teachers are commonly understanding of students' situation and are willing to ensure each student's success. Many of the issues throughout tbe school earn quick and typically effective response, and commonly stem from a lack of funding and staff. If you choose to attend Monterey, be ready to get involved, especially in programs like its PLTW Pre-Engineering program (led by the amazing Scott Houy and Jessica Lara who will support students in every situation and motivate them for success), the Floyd Honey Chapter of the National Honor Society, MHS Leading Ladies, FCCLA, Chick-fil-A Leadership Academy, Student Council, and the many advanced-level courses offered at the school for the best experience. Students that fail to succeed often fail to become involved and keep in touch with athletic and other events happening throughout the school, including consistent conversation with counselors (like the amazing Kristen Lewis) and attendance clerks. It is important that as a student you get to know the administative staff, and your teachers - students are almost always safe to talk to faculty at Monterey, even if they are not involved in your activities or classes. I will acknowledge that there are issues within some organizations/activities regarding students' desire participate under the leadership, including Band, Tennis, Orchestra, Cheer, etc. I will also acknowlege that there have recently been staffing issues, especially in the Sciences (mainly Physics) and a few other areas. I know this has been somewhat of a run-on discussing various aspects of attending Monterey, but overall, it is a great school, with dedicated teachers and administration, a variety of programs, and the potential for success that make Monterey High School one of the best, if not the best, of all high schools in Lubbock. I would give the school a 7/10.

column1: If you are looking strickly into a Christian education this is the school for you. Academics are weak and students are not prepared for college. Not enough honor or advance classes are offered. More is put into school spirit and religion than education. BEWARE My daughter has been at Florida Christain since she started High School. Prior to that she had been at another Private Christan school in Dade since she was in pre-K. The best choice I have ever made was to place my daugher in FCS. This school let's the kids be themselves and not be in fear of every move that they make, yet are deciplined when need be and are treated with respect. The administration is ready to listen or to respond right away by email if need be. My daughter is now graduating with honors and going to Florida State all thanks to of course her hard work but with the leadership of Florida Christian. By the way this year the tuition did not go up because FCS understands the economic problem we are all facing. I truly believe in this school and when I have grandchildren I'm sure my daughter would choose to have them attend there as well. Both of my children started this school this year. We moved from another private school in the area. I was a bit hesitant at first, worried that the religious aspects of this school would hinder their academic needs. Quite the contrary-I am surprisingly impressed with this school. My child is learning in K5 what my older child was learning in second grade at his previous school. On the flip side-comming from another private school-my middle schooler had a hard time keeping up with FCS academics at first, but the staff has been so supportive and with hard work he has found his groove. I actually highly recommend this school-and I was a harsh skeptic in the beginning. My children have attended FCS since Prek3 and have to say that the academics and spiritual needs of my children have not only been met but exceeded any of my expectations. My children are working above grade level and are assuming all of their responsibilities very well. The school is wonderful in many ways.The staff and administration is also very supportive and loving towards the children. Both my children attend Florida Christian and I could not be happier. The academic expectations are set very high. My daughter is working at a grade level above and my son is beginning the reading process in Prek4. Once they reach 2nd grade they begin using Accelerated Reader, which is a great way for their comprehension skills to strengthen even further. The school is amazing and not only do they provide academic excellence but the Christian and spiritual growth I have seen in my children is wonderful! TOO MANY KIDS...My middle schooler has a 31 to 1 student to teacher ratio and my elementary schooler has a 25 to 1 student to teacher ratio. I can achieve that in public school. With tuition steadily rising and the class size gradually increasing, I would look to spend my money elsewhere where there are less kids in each classroom. My children will not return to FCS, I feel as though it is a waste of money. Pay just a bit more for other local private schools...at least your investment will be worth while...and for those who spout safety....please be aware that the middle school students run rampant after school and my child was assaulted with scissors in a classroom. way too many kids per class, per teacher! I was happy even with the 25 to 27 kids per teacher throughout elementary but not any more. There is now 32 kids in my child's class and the teachers just don't have the time to really assist every child. This is not what I expected; I am looking at other schools. The pre-school and early elementary grades at Florida Christian offer a very strong foundation. I have not been thrilled with the teacher student ratios, I feel that the class size is far from optimal. The upper elementary and middle school is where I feel there is much to be desired. Again the class sizes are way too large to offer individualized and differentiated instruction. There is absolutely no emphasis on creative writing. If your child is not the average learner they will not be challenged nor remediated in anyway. The middle school teachers have been there for years and are quite set in there ways. The only strategy they offer to assist academically is tutoring. Although, I wouldn't trade the early elementary foundation at Florida Christian, the middle school has been a very negative experience. I am not willing to give the high school a chance. I wish I would have known what I know now prior to putting 2 children through this. I will not go through this with my 3rd. My advice is do your research and know that things are not always what they seem. TERRIBLE. I could not get my children out of there fast enough. To be fair-the elementary is ACCEPTABLE at times. The middle school is the WORST experience I have ever encountered. We are not new to the private school circuit. We have been to 4 different private school spanning 2 different states so we are not unseasoned in our private school expectations. FCS is the WORST school we have ever encountered. They have a HUGE student to teacher ratio. When I found out there were OVER 30 children in each middle school class I was dumbfounded. The teaching techniques are antiquated with a "teach yourself" mentality going on. The teachers in the middle school are non-responsive and non caring. I would not be surprised if they did not even know my child by name. Terrible...from the top down simply terrible. We are MUCH happier at our new school (and we left mid-year b/c it was such a horrendous experience). Do your research before investing in this school. Definately NOT worth the investment. I hate the fact that many of the Middle School teachers don't grade the children's homework or classwork. They rely on the students to grade them. Some of the teachers do not adequately explain the subject and do not give appropriate time to all students to understand. I went to public school in Hialeah and all the teachers took the time to make sure all of the students understand and if they didn't have time during class, they made sure to take time out of their schedules to continue teaching after school or during their off period. The school is good at filling much of the extra-curricular needs of the children and the band program is top-notch with teachers that actually care about the children's progress. Computer class is lacking during Elementary and Middle School and only offers 1 elective. And the tuition is out of hand. One bright spot this year was the Middle School pronciple which was involved with the students and was quick to resolve issues with teachers and other students. By the way, my son will be getting straight A's this 6th grade school year but often came home with little idea of how to do homework because the teachers would not adequately explain the lesson. I am a student currently attending high school at Florida Christian, and have been attending this school since early elementary. Like many other reviews say, the elementary school provides a good foundation, but middle school and high school looking back now were lacking in quality teaching, not to mention the ridiculous increase in tuition. For every one good teacher per grade, the rest were mediocre in their methods. Most of the teachers seemed to have adopted this 'teach yourself' method, which is basically similar to throwing a student to the wolves. There is very little student/teacher interaction, making the experience seem much less personal. Some of the 'honors' classes are a joke, and the school also lacks in good elective classes (such as creative writing, etc.) and are very limited in their selection of honors and AP classes as well. Generally, there is a very reluctant and sort of bad vibe at the school. Personally, I don't think it's worth the amount of money that the school requires you to pay. Both of my sons graduated from Florida Christian School, and both have now graduated from college and are established in their careers. The school strives to offer a well-rounded program with great athletics, superior arts programs, and excellent academics. Best of all, my students loved going to Florida Christian and knew they were loved by all of the faculty. Terrible experience-glad it is over. We have been through many private schools large and small due to relocations associated with my husband's job. This school was by far the WORST experience we have ever had. I could not wait to get my children out of there. The elementary school was acceptable, I could have stomached a bit more time as it pertains to that aspect of the school. The middle school was a nightmare, unorganized and grossly overcrowded. If the teachers knew my child's first name that would have surprised me. The kids in middle/upper school run around that campus completely unsupervised. The academics are horrible considering you are paying for that education. My middle schooler was significantly behind when we moved to another school in another state. I still get angry when I think of the time and money wasted at this school. It was awful for us, worst school experience I have encountered hands down As with any school you will find that there are issues. I have 2 children that have been there since 4K and one is in college now. She is well prepared and received an above average education. To call this school the worst is a bit of an exaggeration. They have superior band, art, and choir programs. Their drama program has really flourished and they put on amazing plays every year. Their yearbook has also won many awards. So as far as electives go they put out the best. In elementary my children received an excellent foundation. Class size has never been an issue for my children. The student body as a whole is small and everyone knows my kids by name. Obviously the negative comments here are written by an angry parent who had a bad experience. Both of my children have had an overall good experience and a good education. My children have been at this school since preschool. One is now entering high school and the other is entering middle school. My older child was invited to take the SAT by Duke University because he tested in the top 10% of the nation on his 6th grade Stanford Achievement Test and will be entering high school with his Algebra I credit already completed. While the school is not perfect, I am very happy with my children's progress. The sports and fine arts programs are great. Aside from having an award winning band and choir department, there is also a musical theater production put on by the school approximately every other year and at least 1 play a year. For a "smallish" school, I think that is pretty impressive! On the down side, the class sizes should be smaller in middle and high school. I would also love to see more of a variety of elective course offerings. Like any school there are a few bad seeds on the faculty and I would love to see the administration be more proactive in getting rid of those few teachers that leave a bit to be desired. My kids have been students at FCS since K3. One is heading to the main campus next year and to tell you the truth.... I'm a bit concerned. I used to think my kids would graduate from this school but now I'm not so sure. In comparing FCS to another Christian school, FCS lacks a strong curriculum, choice of electives as well as sports. The classroom sizes are too large, the student ratio was 25 to 1,,, 30+ in some grades. Not to mention that the property needs major repairs. On the other hand, The teachers and staff my kids have had , have been both encouraging and nurturing and a real family bond forms with others parents. I think the administration needs to be more pro-active in pushing the school into the 21st century and adhering to the worldly problems are kids will no doubt face. I love this school and I hope good changes come before more students leave. This school could be better if only we had better staff and teachers. Also I should be getting paid more for putting up with student and their parents. You may be wondering why I am writing this, but I am just feed up. The board members don't want me to go. Why, I don't know. My son just graduated from FCS and my daughter graduated 4 years ago. I thank God for the excellent academics, teachers, and staff at FCS. Both of my kids got accepted to every school they applied for, both qualified for FULL Bright Futures Scholoarships, both had very high SAT scores and both got full ride scholarships. I cannot say enough good things about the school. This "school" lacks quality teachers, athletics are a joke, the academic courses are not challenging, assigns an overload of homework, and does not prepare well for SAT, ACT, or college. Does not teach you how to think on ones own. Focuses way to much on Christianity and I felt the books were opinionated to only one certain way of thinking instead of exploring the different religions and philosophies that exist in the world. Middle school did not prepare me for high school at all and I struggled immensely for awhile. While I was attending FCS I had a 3.7 gpa. I left to another school and I quickly found myself behind compared to my classmates and I finished the year with a 2.9 gpa. The tuition is overpriced and NOT worth the "education" you receive. My recommendation is to look elsewhere This is a great school and I highly recommend it to anyone who is looking for a school with a loving, safe and nurturing environment along with excellent teachers and curriculum. My son as been at FCS since the third grade. He is now in middle school and I have absolutely no complaint and nor does he. I attended this school for high school and seriously it was horrible. I recently graduated college and I must say this school did not prepare me at all for college. I'm not stupid or anything my GPA was high when I graduate but it wasnt because of the education, it was cause I was paying. I lost hope in private schools honestly I would send my child to a public school before sending them here. Honestly go somewhere else Florida Christian is a good school, but like any other in Miami-Dade County, it has much room for improvements. My expectations of a good Christian school begin with a Christian based foundation for the students, but it should also display great integrity in leadership, staffing and be an overall example of excellent curriculum and program opportunities for all. This Christian school in certain ways falls below that. Administration needs to review the way they handle staffing, curriculum and programs for the tuition they charge. My kids are there because it's convinient and a good safe environment. However, this year the Board and Mr. Andrews decided to increase tuition again! School is not improving, teachers have not changed for years, and nothing is included (no books, no uniform, no fees, nothing). Extremely expensive for middle-high for what they are offering to students. I can't stand hearing middle and high school kids continue saying that they did not learn anythign at these levels. Middle and High needs a huge revamp. academically. Kids are leaving to new charter schools in the area or other, even home school. I hope my I am able to convince my husband that I know keeping them there for the long run is not the necessarily the best. Did I say I am a teacher myself? Florida Christian is a great Elementary School. However at their middle and high school level they continue to decline. Nothing new has been added to the curriculum or academic program in years. Many teachers could do better in their teaching abilities and support of their students. Administration doesn't seem to understand the need to move up with the times. They also tend to favor students (of their own staff) over others. The Christian foundation is great, but that is not the only factor needed to be successful in life. I would not recommend this school at the middle or high school level. After investing several years at this Christian school, I have come to the sad realization that it does not live up to what I had hoped. At the middle and high school level, academics are not keeping up with competition from other schools. They emphasize the importance of a Christian based education and faith, however, I have seen many at the school behaving in contradiction to what they preach. Administration has consistently raised tuition for the same old program. Teachers seem to be on a life long contract at this school. Sports programs could be much better. If you are considering this school, my advice would be to talk to other parents and kids before making a decision to go there for middle or high school. Its just not worth the money in my view. My honest rating of this school is a 1 for middle and high school. The academic program at this school is awful. Teachers are below average and they never leave. Many teachers have kids going to this school free of charge because they work there. The tuition is very high for the quality. You will have to give extra money to some of the teachers for "tutoring" your kids after school, because during the day, apparently they are too busy to actually go over the lessons correctly. Many students seem unmotivated at this school. Go somewhere else before you spend your money here. I've had an excellent experience and recommend this school. Hope people realize the great opportunities that they are given at this school. Keep your high school student away from here! This is the worst Administration you could ask for. They are greedy and only concerned about tuition. Staff is mostly Alumni and/or Family members of Administration (so they can hide stuff under the rug). They will teach your kids about the Christian faith and to keep their bibles close, but nothing they preach is practice at this institution. Save your money! My children attended FCS from 3K through 12th grade, and it couldn’t have been a more delightful experience. In fact, it was life changing. FCS is family oriented and God-centered. They believe in a well-rounded education. In addition to a challenging curriculum, they embrace the arts, music, and sports. They manage their funds well and have grown at a healthy pace over the years. The faculty was always loving and gracious with my kids and extended an open door policy to me. I recall being shocked they gave out their home phone numbers!During my enrollment interview when my oldest was entering 3K, Dr. Andrews (Headmaster) said something I have not forgotten. He told me there are three elements at play when bringing up children – home, church and school. When all three are closely aligned philosophically, better results typically follow. At the time, we weren’t fully aligned in those three areas. However, exposure to the Bible and the people at FCS impacted my children and ultimately me. Alignment soon followed. When people tell me I did a good job raising my kids, I always tell them I had help. I tell them about FCS. The decision to attend FCS was life changing for my family. A decision that will last through eternity. “Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it”. Proverbs 22:6I think it’s important to note that while my experience as a parent was positive, the better barometer might be from the child’s perspective. Not too long ago I asked both my kids if they were glad they went to FCS. Their resounding “yes” put a smile on my heart. The sacrifice was worth it! Keep up the good work, FCS. There are more like us who need what you give. As a former student, please take my advice and do not enroll your child in this school! 90% of the teachers at this school act like a bunch of high schoolers themselves. They gossip about students and even bully students they do not like! It is a complete and total joke. The amount of times I heard teachers saying awful things about students is absolutely sad, especially for a school that claims to be based in a Christian values! Absolutely ridiculous. If you care about your child and their mental health, do not enroll them here. FCS is an excellent school that fosters spiritual and academic growth. My family has had a 5 star experience at Florida Christian. The Biblical foundation is excellent preparing my boys to be great Christian young men. The educational experience has been fantastic as well. The teachers are very involved and care for their students. Having an environment where my children can have a great educational experience as well as continued teaching in Biblical truths are an amazing combination that prepares them for college and for life. We have had the honor of being part of the FCS family for 3 years now. My older daughter is a senior and is so sad to leave. She absolutely loves her school! My younger daughter is in 7th grade. She also loves her school. They have both made incredible friendships, grown spiritually, and have been challenged academically throughout their time here. FCS is filled with caring teachers and a nurturing environment offering many opportunities. My girls have participated in both sports and the the fine arts, and have experienced trips of a lifetime with their friends and teachers. This place has truly become a second home. My child has been attending FCS for 4 years. This has been the best school experience she has ever had. Attending this school is the greatest blessing and privilege. I am beyond thankful for each staff member employee of FCS, even the housekeepers and maintenance crew are so kind and full of light. I highly recommend FCS to all families. Very poor. We have been with the school many years and have witnessed the decline in attention and care to parent concerns and overall student wellness and education. Lower Elementary, excellent. 5th Grade, (except an excellent 5th grade Math teacher) and Middle School, poor. My child has attended FCS for 5 years and he loves his school. The teachers are supportive, encouraging, and challenging. But above all, they share their faith with the kids to help them to grow as Christians and into well rounded and educated young adults. Lower elementary, some upper elementary, and some high school practices very good. Some upper elementary, most middle school practices, and some high school practices poor. Bullying is a huge problem in middle school. Even after it has been brought to the attention of teachers, counselors and administration. Nothing was done to correct the issue. Pulling my child out after only attending 1 year, for her mental health. I have been a parent with this school since 2007. Sadly, for the evangelical community in Miami , this school is failing in many aspects. The new administration has destroyed the school and the sense of a family in Christ that this place once had. It is with tears in my eyes that I am pulling my son out next year. I can not tolerate the academically and spiritual degradation in this institution right now. May the Lord have mercy upon this place that one day were my kids favorite place. Very sad to see this new reality !!!

column1: The only complaint about the school is they put some sports over quality teachers. They hire lesser teachers for coaching positions and fire quality teachers because of over zealous parents that don't like when the coach doesn't play their child as much as they think the coach should. The School Board says they do what's best for kids but its usually whats best for their own kid.

column3: My youngest daughter really enjoys attending NHS. Her attendance is AMAZING here after being a truant student in Los Angeles School District! My middle daughter Graduated from NHS in 2007. She really was always focused @ NHS and her talents supported! She won a Performing Arts Scholarship from NHS & went off to be a MLS & NBA Professional Dancer. She is a present Choreographer for NHS dance team! I hope my youngest graduates from NHS. The nurse Michelle is truly wonderful. I have always been an honor roll student, and that continued at NHS, however I wouldn't say the staff played a big roll in this. A lot of the time I had to teach myself material, and even more often I would have to teach my peers the material. There have been countless days I come home stressed out about the amount of unnecessary homework I have accumulated, and the students themselves have some of the lowest school spirit I have ever seen in a high school. There is also a very very VERY limited selection of classes to choose from. There is no culinary, no wood shop etc... when it comes time to choose your electives you basically have to choose between ceramics, drama, and AP Calculus/Stats/Trig. The technology is outdated, and the campus is starting to get old, but they are starting to renovate and get new supplies. On top of this, there is a group for everybody to fit into, there has only been one physical fight in my four year experience at NHS, and the office staff are very helpful.

column1: I graduated from RHS and believe me it is not a GOOD school at all. As I am reading the previous reviews I notice that a lot of the students are lacking in their grammar and spelling skills. Yes, RHS might have good sports programs and a good band, but what about Spelling and Grammar? Students will never survive at a University or College with poor communication skills. RHS needs to step it up and hire more qualified teachers. I just graduated from RHS and now at UTPA. As far as the education goes RHS is okay. Many of the teachers are certified and they have become more strict on who they hire. School violence is extremely rare. We would have like one at most (rare) two fights a semester. I thought that was a lot but after talking to other students in mcallen or other schools they would have monthly fights. The sports and music programs are all fun and good but i think what this school is really lacking is money and an open mind. Some of this faculty, (the principal) are dinosaurs. There are way to many restrictions and rules its not a good environment for kids to express their individuality and self confidence. They need to have classes that think outside the box. As far as money goes there's just not enough. More money means more classes, better teachers, more programs, and more spirit. Unfortunately money is one of those things you cant really fix since its based on taxes really. I think this school has gotten better and will continue to get better.
column3: I sent a comment a few minutes ago explaining that we are new to this school. My kid exceeded expectations in Santa Cruz high school the teachers are overruled by the kids if the town would actually help them we would would have better teachers blame it on the eloy council Ill be honest, besides the ratings, this school was pretty good. Its a poverty school so i wouldnt expect AP classes anyway. I get why everything is low, because most students who go there dont have much money. Thats the point of the school. They all teach the same things that other schools do. they just dont have the money for more stuff.

column1: My son is gradulaton this saturady .thank you to all his teachers and principles at brahear for a great four years witt out any problems Because there are people from all over the world with many languages, cultures, and ideologies, it's enjoyable and possibly will give you college experience.

column3: I have had 3 graduate from Herndon High school. The teachers and staff were always helpful and available if my kids needed extra help. Our boys both played lacrosse and our daughter played volleyball and was in choir. The choir department at HHS is one of the best in the county. The other parents are supportive and helpful with volunteering for sports events or choir events. Everyone works together well. Our children have all gone to VA colleges with 2 graduating this year. I highly recommend the school! I love this school i had two sons that when their they loved the teachers and loved how fun it was. When I met the teachers they were nice and very pulight. Great school, retired military and my kids wanted to come back to Herndon. Great small town in a big city. My daughter had a horrible experience at Herndon High. She was assaulted twice (the principal did NOTHING!), she was bullied, she had teachers who cared only about test scores and nothing about the kids and one who was actually emotionally and verbally abusive to both students and parents (several of us complained and NOTHING was done about it). The only highlight was the choir teacher...she was fantastic. I would never send a child to this school! My child left traumatized. Great high school, so much to offer for students in terms of honors program, classes and extra-curricular activities, preparing them for a good start for college! My son is a junior. He has had a great experience at HHS. He chose to go the Honors and then AP route so he is surrounded by other serious students. Most of the kids at HHS are good kids, regardless of the classes they are in. It's important who your kids choose to hang out with. Most of the teachers really care and go above and beyond to help the students. There is a lot of school pride here. English teachers are very rigorous, math teachers are excellent! Science teachers, not bad, but they could be better. My daughter graduated from Herndon High School in 2017 and my son is a Junior there now. She is now studying at Virginia Tech and excelling. I feel Herndon prepared her well for college. They both have developed strong friendships. The community at Herndon High is amazing. The teachers are excellent in most subjects. There is a good amount of diversity. Overall a great school and will be even better once the renovations are complete. This school left me scarred, traumatized, and self-conscious. Sure, I got a decent education, but I was a social outcast humiliated by my peers while the administrators turned a blind eye to my situation. If your child is, generally speaking, a "weirder" type, i.e. louder, more spontaneous, or socially awkward, he will likely experience bullying and isolation by other students with little to no help from the administrators. If your kid has a mental disadvantage or disability, for his/her sake, BE ASSERTIVE WITH ADMINISTRATORS ABOUT YOUR ACCOMMODATIONS AND HIS/HER SITUATION. If you are able, I recommend going to another school unless your child is, generally speaking, popular with other children and NOT mentally or physically handicapped at all. Excellent - very diverse group of students leads to well rounded graduates. The Robotics program is excellent. Great school assembled with very diverse group of students, deeply involved communities and dedicated staffs and teachers. No matter what kind of the paths your students wish to proceed, Herndon High always has something to offer, from the academic, art or sport, to community, social or language. Above all, kindness and respect are often found among the graduates.NASA funded Robotics program is absolutely a hidden gem. Class of 2022.

column1: My son graduated in 2011 from Central and he was very prepared for college. In fact, he was accepted to OSU Main Campus for his freshman year. He also was considered a sophomore after his first quarter at OSU due to all of the college credits he earned and classes he tested out of as a direct result from being a student at Central. Additionally, Central didn't have as many cliques as North did. Students are more accepted at Central. As the parent of a freshman at Central, I am very impressed with this school. The staff and principal are great--they have fun with the kids (even making a dance video of a popular song during spirit week). My child is in honors classes, and will be taking AP college level credit classes by his junior year. We not seen any problems (fights, lockdowns, etc.) since we have been there. The music program is outstanding, and the support for athletics is strong. Pickerington Schools have strong community support and parent involvement. All in all a great school in a school district that is Excellent With Disctinction! Pickerington is a great place to live and raise a family! My son absolutely loves his school! We are so impressed with how helpful the teachers and staff are. They really care about the kids education & work hard to make school a fun filled, learning environment. There are so many options for courses to choose from that my son is never bored. Many different races, cultures & backgrounds but none of that matters! Everyone is welcomed here!!!! My family absolutely loves this school! PHSC has a dynamic student body make-up. The school values and emphasized student achievement in all areas including academics, the arts, and athletics. The staff members truly care about the students. This is an excellent High School. Great for academics, sports, music and many more activities. Great teachers, provided a good education and were always willing to help out. Many after school programs. The school is located in a very safe area and good community. Great opportunities here that are not offered at many schools in Fairfield County Unfortunately, my overall experience at this school was negative. Many teachers I had, did not go above and beyond in several aspects. For example, when I was struggling in an algebra class and asked the teacher for assistance, she frequently had an excuse as to why she couldn’t give me a few minutes of her time. There was such a lack of communication and professionalism. For example, I did additional coursework to receive extra credit and when I submitted it, the teacher told me that she wouldn’t accept it because so already had an A in the class. I reviewed my notes from the first week of class and the syllabus and it made no mention of this rule. I asked the teacher if she could update the syllabus and she refused. Later, I actually heard her with my own ears talking negatively about me to another faculty member. Teachers and staff should refrain from gossiping about students, especially while school is in session.I also struggled with receiving disrespect and hurtful behavior from other classmates while many faculty tolerated such behavior. For instance, I was referred to as a racial slur, sometimes in the presence of a teacher and absolutely nothing was done about it.

Everyone I knew loved it at Cohoes High School. cohoes has become a laughing stock.....its district has the worst behavior toward the people of the city who pay for its keep....now they don't send the second half of the tax bill out.....i wonder if this is a way of trapping people who forget to pay into late fees....just another symptom of a horrific school The stress of common core broke my daughter in 9th grade. We got her into counseling while launching an initiative to homeschool her. The school threatened to hold her back all year only to push her through at the end of the year. Homeschool scholastic testing showed she was ready to enter 8th grade, not 10th. The school refused to release her records and went so far as to alter documents we submitted for the homeschooling. They finally did their job and released her records after we threatened legal/police action. The Leadership at Cohoes High is horrendous. Nobody holds anyone accountable, from administration to coaching staff. Mediocrity is acceptable here.

column1: My son attends vanguard high school. He really likes the school. The school offers many different types of programs. Vanguard is also involved in many colleges programs. It's tries to get all the childred ready for college. The only problem is more parents need to be involved . My son wanted a small school. And he very happy at vanguard. He is doing well. Vanguard high school is doing great, improving day by day, helping students in every subject they need help. I am very proud to said the my son is 90% honor roll student. I LIKE EVETHING THIS SCHOOL. ITS EXCELLENT SCHOOL. FOR ME IS THE BEST HIGH SCHOOL I took my son out of Catholic school and enrolled him in Vanguard and I could never have been more happy. The Principal, Vice Principal and Guidance Counselor are always there for the students and parents. They even have the best security guards that I have ever. encountered. They have a clear understanding on what it takes to have your children actually enjoy going to school. One of the worst high schools in Manhattan. The security is bad, education is way behind than - everything that my daughter has learned in middle school my son is learning in his second year. It's absolutely horrible. I'm in the process of transferring my son. The learning environment in this school is great. Every person is allowed to be who they are without being criticized or bullied. The principal (Bill), vice principal (Erica), and most of the staff's first interest is in our children's education and building on what they already know. When my daughter started here she was extremely antisocial. Now she has friends, good grades and is truly learning what she needs to know to be prepared for college. I'm hoping that my other daughter gets into this school for September 2015. Great learning environment for everyone. Every year or after each semester is over REQUEST your child's transcripts so that you know they are on track as well. I am currently a senior at Vanguard High School and I cannot wait to graduate from this exceptionally bad school. The teachers are incredibly lazy and behave atrociously in class. The students are some of the most disrespectful, badly behaved people I have ever encountered. This school does nothing to teach students how to behave respectfully. Academics and test scores are far below average and the school it’s self is run down, disgusting, and generally unsafe. There are fights and student “meltdowns” almost daily. The school is extremely underfunded resulting in lack of reasorces for the amount of students they have. You can forget about field trips. The principal, Bill, is the only thing keeping this school from completely collapsing. Worst experience of my life, do not go here. I just read my past review of this school from July 2015. To be honest after everything I have heard about the school now I came to the conclusion that students and some parents are placing the blame on the teachers because they do not want to admit to themselves their child is 90% of the problem. Yes, some (and when I say some I am only referring to maybe 2 or 3) teachers may need to stop lowering their level to the students when it comes to confrontation with students, but this school can still be a top school. Do not be deterred from sending your child here because of a few bad seeds who prefer to cut class and bad talk the teachers. What the school needs to do is do what they were doing when my daughters attended here and that is to start weeding out the bad seeds. I did realize when my second daughter started to attend here there were so many students from Harlem here and guess where those students are now because they didn’t do what they were suppose to do when they attended here? Half of the females my daughter was friends with are now mothers at the ages 21. Half of the guys are with low paying jobs, still living with their mothers, or are in jail! So what we should blame the teachers for that too? My now 23 year old daughter graduated from this high school a half of a year early and has learned a lot. I mean she had a rough last year here because of her attitude and 1 teacher she just could not get along with, but other then that I’d say her time at the school was a success. She is in a high paying career making more than 3 times the NYC 15 dollar minimum wage. My other daughter left in grade 11 because we moved and she was hanging with the wrong (Harlem) kids. Don’t get me wrong, I am not suggesting people from Harlem are the cause of this school going down a bit, but the majority of the Harlem students that came into this school the year my second daughter started to attend were no bueno. My second daughter is now 21. She graduated a semester early from college. She still needs a little guidance here and there, but she can financially support herself. With that said I still like the school. Right now my son is in a school that is rated 7/10, but if I ever had to move back to NYC I would consider putting him in this school.

Many students at this school are racist. It was as bad as we had heard, but we didn't believe it until we found out for ourselves. Transfer if you can to avoid sending your kids this school. Our neighbors had it right. They moved to the Concord High area when their kids were in middle school. This school is horrible. I would not recommend sending your child here. There are gangs, drug problems, and other things that are just horrible. The school is so easy, and has no challenge at all. I doubt any colleges would want you if you have a diploma from here. Really Great school. They have medicine academy, engineering academy, architecture academy, design academy and chef academy. All the students go to the college or university or army. This school has potential and could be better than what it is. The school is in Concord but serves the kids of Bay Point which is a far more ethnically diverse area than Concord. As a result of “white flight” , nearly 80% of the students who reside in concord and are supposed to feed into Mt. Diablo end up going to Clayton Valley or Concord high because the parents think they’re too good to be in classes with brown kids from Bay Point and feel they’ll get a better education by attending primarily white schools in areas they could never afford. If you are too good for the community you reside in than you wouldn’t be reside there. If the kids that are supposed to go there were required to than the average grades and test scores would go up which means more funding to make improvements. The teachers here are ok. Lots of unprofessional relations and interactions between students and teachers mainly within the music and arts academies (teachers should not be partying with their students even a year after they graduate) What this school really lacks is student participation and school spirit. The rally’s are boring and nobody is exited to be there and extracurricular activities like dances and other social events put on for students are very few and far between and not well attende. I love this school, just came there and Im an freshman. Rgeardless people are going to say this is a bad school. IT IS NOT. They are very welcoming and nice. They have JROCT, cooking, Public speaking or Debate team/class and more. MUptiple luages classes like French, Spanish and Mandorian chinnise. Tons of sports Football, basketball, tenniss and volleyball track too! The techers are pretty nice they tey to help out as much as they can just ask them. The food her is AWSOME. For kids who have food issues they let anyone and everyone get as much as they need/want they should know the limits. Bring your kid here its awsome!!!

column1: We just finished our first year at Prep and my son could not be happier. I am very pleased with the education,study skills, and friendships he has developed over the past year. Prep is an excellent school and I would highly recommend it to anyone and everyone. Prep is about academics not about letting the parents rule the school. I really like that! Often times, certain things seem to exist only to serve as a lesser or greater counterpart to something else. For example, cats, for many people, are a better alternative for household pets over dogs. Inversely, for many families, dogs are a better option over cats. The counterpart to this school is St. Andrew's Episcopal school. The only difference is that unlike the relationship between cats and dos where one is only sometimes better than the other, St. Andrew's will always be better than Prep. Prep is basically St. Andrew's with less academic excellence and more racial tension. It doesn't matter what anyone else from just Prep says, I have attended both schools and I've seen the difference. I am a Jackson Prep graduate and I am so thankful for the education I received at Prep. While at the time, I did not always enjoy the level of difficulty, Prep prepared me for college and my "big girl job". Being able to say "I am a graduate from Jackson Prep." also opens lots of doors in Mississippi. I would highly recommend Prep to any parents or students who are looking for a quality education for their child in the Jackson area. My daughter is currently a senior and will be graduating in a week. We have been at Prep for seven years - we started in sixth grade. This school is a wonderful place to send your children. We have grown to love the kids and their parents. The curriculum is tough and 4.0 + grade point averages are not achieved without a lot of hard work. The arts department is very strong and if your child is interested in drama or choir/vocal performance, Prep is the place to be! I can't say enough good things about Prep. Things weren't always perfect, but what institution is that is full of teenagers? I love Prep and will be sad to say goodbye. The school needs a true makeover! The school want a reputation for giving a lot of work. I am all for a rigorous program, but not to the extent where there is a lot of overload work unnecessarily especially when it's used to manipulate grades that effect "some students". Some of the teachers were not very approachable. It seemed that our concern led to retaliation. The school does not embrace diversity. Principle and some of the staff were unprofessional. Jackson Prep does absolutely nothing to stop bullying, this further ads to the adults these kids turn into. Is it ok to sexually harass? NO! Did the administration do anything? NO
