A great school for teens all from Houston A good school for all to learn. good. every one gets along well and great. Good school to learn at. 10/10 good. 10/10 for teach ing and teachers here these teachers dont help you AT ALLLLLL good school. opportunities are given to those who are willing to work hard.

column1: My two children have gone to Ripon High School and I think the teachers are very caring. I have three daughters. My highly academic athletic student graduated from Ripon High School. She played basketball, ran in track and Cross Country and participated in the talent show, choir and clubs. Yet the AP still said her name wrong in the talent show and called her by another person's name when announcing her group on stage. Her group worked really hard and no one, except her family, knew she was on stage. He got the popular kids names right and apparently that's whats important. Except for a few, Ripon High teachers and coaches were caring and hard working. Out of 30 something students in their classrooms they always took the time to respond to my emails and my concerns if there were any. My other daughters are in the 3.0 - 3.7 gpa range and didn't quite fit that highly academic/athletic highly spirited category that Ripon High seems to look for to highlight their school. Although my youngest did participate in Ripon's choir program and loved it. I ended up having to take my youngest out of Ripon's district because a teacher refused to accommodate an assignment and when I complained she changed the grade on an old assignment to a lower grade. Therefore, I transferred my youngest to another district where she was a lot happier. Both my oldest and my youngest have permanant medical conditions and Ripon High School wasn't a good fit for them. Again, most of the Ripon High teachers were pretty awesome, but my girls needed a larger school with more academic opportunities. They needed school and district policy that was going to guide them, reward them, give incentives and not make them feel less than because of their medical conditions. Larger schools have more clubs, more diversity, and less favoritism. Academics is important. College is important. Fitting in is also important. Not fitting in can cause depression, lower grades, and create a sometimes serious situation for some students. I am not so sure that Ripon High or our Ripon District understands this when they are only focusing on tests scores and winning games. Not everyone is a gifted athlete or is highly academic. Rumors and gossip run rampant in this little town and in our schools. Damaging and sometimes traumatizing rumors. This is a serious problem in our town and our schools. Ripon High school doesn't have hallway lockers and backpacks get very heavy. I recommend a lock for your backpack and password lock your phones because of classroom theft or retaliating students. this is a family school. the staff and students treat each other like family. they look out for each other. the education is top notch and the teachers and supporting staff are the best.

Literacy levels well below ( 2-4years) grade level and considered A OK! Guidance dept is miserable, Head of guidance never repsonds to calls or emails. 1. incompentent teachers far outweigh effective ones. And those effective ones are far too concerned with job security than doing what is right for the students. 2. Special education is sub par, S E teachers cannot write or manage legal, fair or effective IEP's. Due 3. females with abilities in math and science are not encouraged, because the tenured lazy teachers do nothing to excite or engage these kids. This middle income school cannot win until the leadership takes a forthright stand for the students education! Apalling, discouraging. Let your tax dollars work in another We recently made that switch from Private school to East and are very happy. I feel that my child is receiving an even better education in this public school. My children have had a great experience at East. The principal rules with a firm hand, is tough on drugs, alcohol and other issues and has the respect of parents & students. The teachers run the gamut, like anywhere - a good life lesson for my kids. The parents are really involved whether with sports boosters, band or general enrichment activities. I highly recommend East. I moved to East from a private school with much trepidation. I have found East to offer a wider variety of classes than I experienced before and the support for children with learning challenges or special interests (of which I have both) is great. Best of all, the parent community is involved and informative - trying hard to address the many questions we have. oh what a dilemma! we moved our daughters here after 8 years in Catholic school. They have been stagnant academically and turned off by about 1/3 of their teachers. There are a few young, and engaging teachersbut not enough. Those who have been at East too long ( principals and asst principals) are just biding their time, and the principal does nada- does not require any change in curriculum, or presentation. The guidance department is awful, disorganized and helpless. So, is this laissez faire or just LAZY FARE education? Time to return to "education" with value. Superintendent is tending less than super schools, but carefully minding the teachers union. NB 30% of parents are involved. Not the same kind of involvement that was at Catholic schools, or even neighboring public high schools- Rustin or Henderson. As an aunt of two girls who attend East, I have learned that there are more lazy teachers than good, that my nieces have one outstanding teacher for all their classes. WHY? Why are not all teachers excellent instructors? I have heard all about the drugs and sex that are prevalent in this school. I have heard about the rotten school spirit, the losing sports teams, the terrible teachers who are hired as 'coaches" And when I suggested they go to their counselors, they laughed and said how the counselors are useless. What is the principal doing? Friendly enough, but that is not working. He is leading Camp Runamuck! most distressing- If I had it to do again I would not move into this part of the WCASD. I agree with others that the Principal seems nice but if not effective in leading the administration or motivating teachers to do their jobs. I could write a book about the AD and sports program, avoid at all costs. Some good teachers, but too many who don't try and don't care. Parents do seem supportive and nice kids for the most part... too bad they're not getting a better education. I come from a family of teachers and have taught middle school in New Jersey, Virginia and Michigan, so I bring an experienced approach to evaluating WCASD and WC East in particular. Having moved here 15 years ago we have been thrilled with the education our two children have received especially at WC East High School. We have friends who moved their children to the exclusive private schools in the area for high school and, honestly, the education our children received at East surpassed the education in the area private schools. The course selections, number of AP classes and state of the art equipment and technology far surpass what is found in private schools. East teachers are engaged, knowledgeable and willing to stay after or come in early to support their students with extra help. The principal is dynamic and committed to excellence, and the staff matches these qualities. The student body is also enthusiastic, loyally attends school events and shows pride and spirit in East. Having experienced schools in different states and being familiar with both private and public schools in the area - East is truly a great school that will serve your children very well! We are extremely happy with the education our child has received at WC East High school. The teachers are engaged with the students and proactive with parents. The principal is truly commited to his school and to the students. The level of academic rigor is reflected in the number of seminar and AP classes offered. I could not be happier that 20 years ago we moved into the WCASD. I do not enjoy going here what so ever. The teachers and administrators make decisions out of impulse and do not think about students at all. After the fire alarm was pulled Administration made a rule where no student can leave the classroom for any reason. It is a basic right to go to the bathroom. They say we must go in-between periods but we only have 4 minutes between periods! I would love to see someone go to the bathroom and get to their next class on time in 4 minutes! The Fire alarm was pulled in between periods so all of these rules are irrelevant and really change nothing. What about kids with medical problems? Obviously this was not thought out at all. I don't feel like I'm at school anymore. Im locked in my classroom which now seems like a jail. Recently another rule has been put into place where if a kid misses a day of school without an excused absence, they will automatically get a 0 on any test or quiz they had that day. Administration is doing a great job of making school an even more dreadful place to go everyday. WC East is a school whether you love it or hate it. There are plenty of good teachers that actually want to be there and various classes. Attending this school I know that there are plenty of motivated students that are willing to put in the work to be successful in life which is about the majority of students. good, some kids are rude and some teachers are rude, but for the most part jazzy. Great school! Dedicated staff and administration. Excellent experience! Overall excellent experience - strong and caring administration and teaching staff. Lots of wonderful clubs, activities and teams allow every student to find their niche. Superb! Two years in and both parents and student are loving it. SO many opportunities to express yourself and grow as a student. Parents are given multiple opportunities to speak with administrators, teachers and staff. There are some older reviews on here that do not reflect the way things are now at East. We have an incredible principal and team of assistant principals. Caring and encouraging staff and teachers. No place is perfect, but this school really comes close. I have moved around the country and been in many different school districts. WCASD is by far the greatest. Students are the number one priority to them. At East High School, as well, students are the number one priority. I've had 3 very different kids go through the school and they have had an excellent experience! The administration and staff at West Chester East gave them an amazing foundation and I am truly grateful!

column1: My child went to Chapin High School their freshman year. Let me just say that I will not recommend this school to anyone. My child failed so many tests there because they were constantly pulling my child out of class. When I called the school about this, they said "We just wanted to talk to your child to make sure they were learning." Well my child was learning, until they pulled my child out of class every 5 minutes. If they really wanted my child to learn, they would've kept them in there so that they wouldn't be missing instruction. And another thing, whenever they gave my child a silent lunch, they told my child "You cant eat if we give you silent lunch." And my child was given silent lunches often. You know how long my child went without eating? You know how hard that is for a parent to witness? No, I will not recommend this school to anyone ever. The facilities are nice, the faculty are caring and the academics are good. The reason for my 2 stars is that the student body is well known for being unwelcoming to new students. The faculty acknowledge it and anyone from the surrounding communities will say that Chapin is known for being very cliquey. Even Chapin grads will say that new students have a very hard time. I wish that someone had warned me before I moved my family here. If I had known what I now know, I would NEVER have moved my family to Chapin. I hope this helps someone else from making the same mistake and putting their kids through what my kids are going through, my heart brakes for them. In my opinion, the previous post dated 4-21-2015 is accurate. Our family has moved 6 times, and have never before experienced this type of "clique-ishness" anywhere else. While other communities were welcoming and extremely hospitable, Chapin is not. We have lived here 5+ years and continue to experience this subtle bias. Thankfully, we have met many wonderful families in Chapin; however, it has occurred to us that 80% of those people are transplants, too. These great people have made living here worthwhile, and exude the true meaning of southern hospitality. Advice: Enroll your kids in as many youth groups, sports, and organizations outside of Chapin school system as possible. It's worth the drive. I moved here nine years ago and chose Chapin specifically for the schools. (We could have moved anywhere in the state.) While I wasn't thrilled with our experience in the elementary school, the middle school and high school experiences were excellent. Both schools have excellent music programs and promote excellence in education, music and athletics and the staff has been great to work with. As a substitute teacher and parent volunteer I was very pleased with the degree of respect the students showed to me and other parents and staff. I love Chapin and have never regretted our move here. Palmettos Finest! Need I say more. We moved to this community purely for CHS 6 yrs ago! For this school to have a rating of 7 out of 10 is a joke. It's a 10 all day long! Chapin High School has a staff which is excited about and loves teaching (or otherwise providing for the needs of) their students. The atmosphere for learning is great, and students are given respect and expected to respect staff as well as fellow students. The Athletics are impressive, with state champions in multiple sports (such as boys and girls soccer, Cheer leading, etc). The school spirit is prevalent and rightfully so, Chapin High School is truly the best school in the state of South Carolina My child has experienced biased consequences and sports are for the elite. It’s not a school to attend if you are culturally different or willing and able to donate donations of money to the school. My experience at this school is good Wonderful school that has far exceeded my expectations moving to Chapin! The kind caring staff go above and beyond what is expected. The amount of school pride is glowing. I would give six stars if I could.

column3: The school has strong support provided by the teachers to any student. Students are urged to pursue their own interests despite the strong science and mathematics emphasis already in place. And the house prices keep going up!! Thanks Lynbrook for doing such a great job. Interesting to read someone say "Sports not emphasized much, although they do excel in a few areas: tennis, water polo, track & field." I wonder how much that new stadium cost the taxpayers. I am very worry about what I heard from other students about how this school really is. Most of the students are very stuck up thinking they are from affluent families and behaving like they are the cream of the crops. LOLS LOLS LOLS. The affluent people do not live here in West San Jose. They are in Los Altos Hills, certain parts of Palo Alto, Atherton, Los Gatos, certain parts of San Francisco, etc. This school have way too many arrogant students which make them go several steps behind those students that are well rounded. Just remember this, there are other schools in California (the one in Cerritos, CA) and out of state that beat your score. I am afraid to say that this school will have plenty of students with lack of human skills. Please don't be fool to buy a house here. It is not the school that is good. It is the type of students that move here. The students along with their parents make the 80% effort and the teachers only 20%. It is just common sense that you cannot make an average to below average student smart. Don't let the API score fool you. Don't waste your money on buying these huts which they called homes in 95129 area code. 1.2 million for a dump of between 1300 to 1600 square feet of nightmare. Not all the steller students are steller naturally. I estimated about 30% of these students steller or not steller gets private tutoring. There are like 5% that are just born smart. Don't buy a house here. Many parents pay for private tutoring. It is the snobbish people that move here. Don't let the false information in suckering your hard earn dollar. If u have the money to waste, plus paying for private tutoring, etc, then go for it. The school is amazing! Most of the teachers are caring, the current principal is a fantastic role model and the parent involvement is outstanding. The support system is strong. I couldn't be happier with a school and its staff. To those who are reading the negative reviews submitted by "parents" and students please spend a day in this school. Most students enrolled are neither snobbish nor extremely wealthy. There are a myriad of students with different personalities in this school but most are very friendly. The parents and students complaining about "lack of human skills" or "students being smart due to private tutoring" are horribly mistaken. Indeed the AP classes are difficult but there are teachers and other students who are willing to tutor your child if the need arises. There are also tutorial periods for students to ask a teacher questions, do their homework or study for an upcoming quiz/test. The occurrences for bullying, theft, etc. at this school is EXTREMELY rare and are almost unheard of. The teachers at this school are also extremely friendly and bonds with students well (I know because I am a student myself). Overall this school is excellent and studying at this school could almost ensure you a spot into a Ivy League school or at the very least a UC. Keep up the good work Vikings! Some comment come from parent who just want to maintain their house value, do not fooled by some parent statement "studying at this school could almost ensure you a spot into a Ivy League school ", The parent and student do the 80% job and teacher only do 20% , a lot of parent are complaining this. Do some research before buy a million house there. Lynbrook offers a very inclusive learning experience. The teachers have a great track record for being progressive and involved in their students complete education. They are highly skilled and motivated, making Lynbrook a highly regarded school. I feel that students are well monitored, encouraged and motivated. Lynbrook prepares their student's not only for college, but to succeed in life. All aspects of learning is taken into consideration. The basic's such as math, science, liturature, & the arts, music, dance, & sports are all important. Lynbrook is considered be one of the "top high schools in the Bay Area", It had been raked one of the "top five public comprehensive secondary schools in California". There is such a high demand for parent's to have their children go to Lynbrook, that the housing market in the immediate area's have skyrocket, which increases the tax base, which again increases the funding for the school's. Additional families that move into the area are so involved with the best education for their children, many of the bond measures, for school funding, are continually supported. Lynbrook offers an outstanding curriculum & extra curriculum program to all. Obviously there are a lot of mixed reviews about how Lynbrook is, I think this is mostly based on how people respond to a high-pressure environment. For example parents reviews might be influenced by what their kids say about it. This school has a very large amount of very motivated people, but it's less the school and the teachers than the students themselves that push up LHS's test scores. Almost everything that is done at this school is done to look good on their college applications. The stress level that is experienced here makes cheating a huge problem because of the workloads and lack of time and sleep that everyone gets. Staff are trying to fix the problem this year but from what I can see it isn't working very well. One great thing about all of this is that the pressure that the students have on them to constantly excel in everything makes a great atmosphere of camaraderie, and the people at this school are some of the nicest that I have ever met. Some people may disagree with what I say here but this is how I see it after going here for two years. What I do know is that every day Lynbrook pushes me to learn as much as I can and to be the best I can be. Great environment for highly academic, self-motivated, over-achievers. A bit stressful for those who don't fit this profile. Not much cultural diversity, since the population is heavily Asian. Administration, teachers, and staff are very competent and caring. Highly intelligent, college educated parent population are actively involved. There is much emphasis on STEM and college prep, such that students may not get exposed to higher level humanities and ethics. In the highly competitive environment supported by parents' definition of success, cheating is an issue. Students with special needs and learning challenges may feel isolated and intimidated. This may not be a healthy environment for some students. I recently spent two weeks observing at Lynbrook as a prerequisite to applying to teacher's college and I was just amazed by he quality of teaching and their students. Yes, the students do tend to be competitive and resemble the characters of the Big Bang Theory but they are also very fun loving, hard working and teachable. There were always some activities in the quad to stir up school spirit and I always see a smile in everyone's face except when they come out of an AP Calculus quiz. As a teacher for over 12 years at Lynbrook and 4 years at Monta Vista, I can tell you Lynbrook is an exceptional high school. Don't be fooled by all the negativity, you will not find harder working teachers who not only take great pride in the work they do, but also love their students and connect with them regularly. As for the student body, I can tell you, having worked in 6 different high schools, this group is super inclusive. Bullying is almost non-existent. The camaraderie between students and spirit on the campus reflect the essence of the typical Lynbrook student. From Homecoming skits to the senior Spoons game, the students are ripe with creative outlets and bond with enthusiasm. Parents who are critical of the teachers "teaching only 20%", some nebulous and random percentage, should move. Sell your over-priced house and find something better. I wish you luck. The high ratings of Lynbrook are well deserved. Look at the Science Fair and the STEM program, ranked #7 in the United States. Look at all the Intel and Seimens winners, look at Model UN, DECA winners, a top notch Speech and Debate team, Viking Buddies and Link Crew, nationally rated Yearbook and Epic News magazine, those are just a few of the stellar opportunities for Students. Lynbrook is so much more than test scores and offers endless opportunities for learning both inside and outside the classroom. It a special place to work and I value every single day as much as I value each and every student. Best school you'll find. Lynbrook continues to be associated with the highest educational standards. Students graduate Lynbrook a formable amount knowledge that has prepared them for the next level of education. Additionally students have the opportunity to develop social skills, via arts & sports, school activities, dances, competition, plays, and so much more. Add the skill and support of the Teacher's and Staff, then there are no excuses for not succeeding. Thank you Lynbrook. This school is full of problems, it is easy to get carried away by the high ratings et al but the reality is that the school has declining enrollment, has bare minimum electives and course options, and availability is a question among the few electives. Plus there is no community support nor is there school spirit. Nepotism is highly prevalent in this school. Students and parents are desperately trying to please teachers blindly, for return favors. Students will not hesitate to backstab and lie about fellow students in order to get undue advantages and will never speak up truth against a teacher if questioned about things not going well with teachers. Competition is to such unhealthy levels that there is no soul to this school! The school administration is on the teacher's side and will never take any action unless one is involved in a drastic crime. The district office is also on the teacher's side and will never support a student's well being if it has anything to do with issues pertaining to teacher's irresponsibilities. The whole system is rigged from top to bottom. Sending kids to this school would be encouraging such negative culture. One should avoid this school if they can, there are many other public school options in the area that provide far superior all round development, many elective options, better teachers and definitely far superior school administrators, all while having great school spirit and community, while providing a nurturing school environment where a student can continue to have faith and trust in humanity at least until they grow into adults! This school is literally the most competitive school in the world and I believe also most competitive school in entire history. I am not placing this as a joke, but literally the school itself hit an all time record of reaching the highest number of valedictorians(4.0 gpa), highest number of APs/Honors taken by students, the highest number of extracurricular achievements(especially those related to STEM/academics) that any person could ever think of. I graduated in this school recently and from that valedictorian fact, literally 15% of my whole grade level earned their place as a valedictorian and almost everyone I knew had just an incredibly high gpa(like 80% of students earning a 3.96-3.98 gpa). I didn't knew a single person who wasn't top nor had some flaws within their academic record/grades/ as an individual person. I was literally the last student in my grade level and basically the dunce of the school itself, or in other words.. the number one donkey. It was just people were so enticed into being with their own friend circles and for the people who aren't that academically driven, you are going to have a hard time making friends. It is just the fact that many of these people you know just won't simply care about you in a strong way. I am the only one in the school who has literally failed to accomplish anything or be able to make friends. Every other person in my school was able to get something out of Lynbrook. I never felt this betrayed in my whole life. It is not what you see in the movies, where there are close group friends who are willing to side with another friend who is in need or support, but in Lynbrook, you have to be smart and have a superior quality to make people to engage with you. Lynbrook is a small community where most of the students are more superficially driven. The teachers do help a lot, but if a student is very low or is academically/socially inferior, nobody is going to simply help you. I was the only outcast in the lynbrook bubble who just had a hard time to gain something out of the school itself.If you are a person who wants to carry more of a meaning in life, THIS SCHOOL IS MOST LIKELY NOT FOR YOU!! I was a special education student and if you don't stand at Lynbrook, NOBODY IS GOING TO HELP YOU. Teachers think students are so brilliant that they are not willing to help the 1% of the students who are struggling. excellent in academic, extracurriculum and community service. This school is beyond horrible. I cant even bring to words how much pain this school has caused me. I can guarantee you a NORMAL child would not be able to survive here. This school is filled with cold, lifeless robots. You would only send your child here if you hate them. Absolutely no one deserves to deal with what this school brings to the table. The environment is absolutely disgusting. If you are thinking of coming here, DONT. As a senior at Lynbrook, I have mixed feelings about my experience. I'm ultimately sad to leave, but mostly because I'll miss some wonderful friends, incredible teachers who were there for me when I needed it, and the general "predictability" of high school- I liked the small classes and "small school" environment, and going to a huge public college is a big jump. On the other hand, this is a pressure-cooker environment, many peers can be quite rude, and it is definitely competitive- it was actually difficult for me to even form study groups at Lynbrook, no one ever wanted to work together. The pressure to be "perfect" is real, both academically and extracurricular-wise (plus, all the typical teenage pressures). The principal never seemed very involved directly with students, and the guidance department is mediocre and inflexible. In the end? I'm glad I went to Lynbrook because I did grow a lot here. My advice to incoming freshman? Relax, and don't take too much stress. College applications WILL work out. Find a good group of friends who truly care about you. Watch your mental health. Get to know your teachers and ask them questions- Lynbrook is lucky to have a few truly incredible teachers that I will never forget. Genuinely care about learning- it simply makes high school more fun, and your grades will work out if you just focus on learning and getting excited about the material. Take courses based on your interest (and sometimes, the teachers), and don't worry too much about grades- in every class at Lynbrook, you can do well if you are passionate about the subject, ask for help, and work hard. There is no class that is "too" difficult to the point where you cannot succeed. Wow, how much I love this school. I am in 9th grade, and I have less hoemwork than my elementary school. Yes, you read that right. I know APs/Honors might take longer than you think, my the school I want to as a elementary school was Faria. Faria gave too much homework. During COVID-19, I can't say which has more homework, (Faria probably changed as well) so I think Faria still has more. Way too much work causing way too much stress. Its ok nothing special some teachers were good but ultimately most were ineffective at teaching and unaware of their impact on students. There was construction ongoing constantly making it hard to learn and the campus was messy. During breaks, the lunch line and quad were chaotic to a harmful degree and the majority of the campus was unmoderated. this school is literally awful and you won't have a normal high school experience. there is too much pressure here and it will burn you out. you won't meet a dumb person at this school and everything here is about getting high grades. this is absolute hell and everyone here has no personality.

column1: The Principal, staff, and teachers are all so dedicated at Uplift. There are a large number of Programs that are offered to motivate students, and help increase their academic skills. There are also opportunities for students to tap into their creative talents such as tap dancing, choir, band, and the list goes on. I coordinate the GEAR UP Program at Uplift and we are working with the Senior Mentors to make sure that every senior at Uplift has applied to at least 5 colleges. We will make sure that students have sent transcripts to these schools, and we will assist them until they receive an acceptance letter from a college. We are aslo assiting them with ACT Prep, their Personal Statements, Applying for Financial Aid, and either writing letters of recommendations for them or helping them identify people who will write q letter for them. Uplift is a school that attempts to make sure that each student has as many opportunities, support, and personal one on one academic assistance as possible. Each teacher at Uplift has designated at least two days per week that they stay after school to help any student that needs that additional one on one time to understand anything that was not clear during class time. I can honestly say that in my 25 years of working with public schools Uplift is number one on my list. The outreach and support to parents and students is extraordinary at Uplift Community High School. As a parent of a Senior, I have to give Uplift 5 stars!. My son has been an on point since his Freshman year. The teachers are very dedicated to making sure all succeed. The one on one attention given if needed is so remarkable. There is a open door policy there , so any parent that says the cannot speak to the teachers or the principle has not tried. You are greeted with respect and the entire staff can tell you on any given day just what mood your child is in. The prep for college is remarkable and the push to have all succeed is not spoken on enough in my opinion. The excitement that the Juniors and Seniors project pertaining to the ACT and college completely blew my mind. And to make things better, the scholarships are flowing in! Kudos to uplift for doing such a remarkable job with not only my son, but all of their students. Parents, if your reading, get more involved...that's the only thing missing here. I went to UPLIFT when it first came about. Great school and so-so teachers at first. Now my cousins go there and there is a change...but for the better. Love UPLIFT.

column3: I've been (and currently still am) attending Monache High School. The school in general is a very good school. Unlike some of the other reviews failed to say is that Monache High has some of the highest API scores in the area. It doesn't have the cleanest, nor the nicest campus, but it is very big & the people are very well kept. (Well, most of them.) I love this school, & I cannot wait to graduate from here & have Monache High School on my diploma & college applications. I tried to work with counselor Scarlett Ceja to help my child graduate on time. Scarlett, Christina Sanchez and Tammy Keith refused to return any of my voicemails. Scarlett Ceja NEVER helped my child make healthy, independent decisions. NEVER created a plan of action toward obtaining goals. NEVER encouraged my student through making personal contacts and demonstrating a vested interest in her strengths, talents, challenges and triumphs. NEVER Facilitate relevant grade level specific discussions. NEVER Ensured fundamental college preparation activities at ANY grade level. This schools office staff lacked any effort to work with a concerned parent. Very frustrating!!

column1: We have four students at RRCS and have been all the way from Jr. High to a graduating senior. We like the uniforms, atmosphere and most of the teachers a lot, and think that Tom Hatch is great. My concerns are with the communications between the school and parents and the quality of academic guidance. Unless your children tell you everything and remember every deadline you will miss a lot of opportunities. This is not a large school but the guidance department takes very little interest in seeing that students maximize their time at Ross. This is very sad and I hope it changes - we thought that we were in a much better school until it really mattered and then just received excuses. This school has given my child faith in her education. The staff here is amazing! We love this school. The teachers are great and you can tell the new principal Mr. Parker loves being there. That's all my kids talk about. So glad we chose Reid Ross.

column3: I would never send another child of mine to this school. My daughter attended this high school and the school just promised a bunch of empty lies. When we met with the school in June to discuss the classes my daughter would be enrolled in, they told her she could take certain classes which never appeared on her schedule when school started. The Guidance Office has no idea what they're doing or what the other teachers are doing and were no help at all. I am very disappointed for sending my child here and I will not make the same mistake again. Having attended Northwest and graduated in 2009, I have to say that the reviews below are shocking and inaccurate. If your spelling is any indication, you clearly have no idea what a great education is. Northwest has small classes, amazing and engaging teachers, and an atmosphere where you will be thrust into leadership positions purely because of the small size of the student body. It is absolutely true that if a student doesn't put in the effort they won't do well, but generally the fault lies with them instead of the teachers. Like any school, some instructors are less than top-notch. On the whole, however, you will be hard-pressed to find a group of individuals more dedicated to assuring that their students are getting the most out of their education. At what other school can you make a sports team with no experience, practice daily for four years, and become the MVP during your senior season? Where else can you claim to know every student in your class upon graduation? The answer is nowhere. As I sit here at one of the top 35 colleges in the country, I have to say that Northwest prepared me to excel in college and in life, a combination that is far too rare these days. Plain awful. Northwest Catholic fails to provide an education that motivates and pushes the student to achieve more. It has a very limited course selection and the guidance and teacher quality is 20% really good and 80% awful. I feel like I wasted my money and my daughters time by sending her to this school. It looks great from the outside but its education, extra curricular activities and atheletics are terrible. I do not recommend this school for anybody. I graduated from the school a few years ago and it made a huge difference in my life. I was able to discover explore my talents and skills, which helped me determine the direction I wanted to go in college. I was challenged to learn more and apply what I learned - not just memorize facts and figures - and had the support of my teachers when things were challenging. This school was definitely a great fit for me. Northwest Catholic (NWC) offered an excellent education for me. Having tried public schools 2x growing up...NWC was always a full year ahead of the local high school, Hall High (which, by the way is considered one of the best in the US). Sure I could have stayed in the public school getting straight A's on easy street. But that wasn't what I was there for so I went back to NWC and trudged through their course load. And yes, it was difficult for me. But I was glad then and I m glad now. On top of the educational component I can unequivocally say that the values that they teach to you are impeccable. There is an atmosphere of community that you simply will never get in a public high school. I know this from my own experience and that of having my 4 children in public high schools. The bottom line is at NWC you get personal attention. The administration knows you and cares that you are successful. Trust me NWC does a great job. Believe you me. NWC is an excellent school for students who are able to rise to the challenge and can handle the sometimes heavy-handed control (e.g. uniform issues, schedule, discipline). Our teen is a moderate-achiever, self-starting individual. There is help - academic and otherwise - but students must seek it, and he doesn't by his own nature. We're about to embark on the college hunt, and it's here that I notice a big difference from our own experience with public and private high schools. Private high schools tend to incorporate SAT prep and college prep from day 1, whether it is meeting with counselors to ensure a balanced schedule (academics alone are not enough for good colleges), or incorporating SAT prep into math and English courses. That said, NWC seems to have a good college support system for juniors and seniors that includes parent participation. They have an excellent array of AP courses, particularly in STEM. Compared to public schools, their college prep program excels.Overall, STEM courses are strong, as are history, literature, and arts. Language options are too limited, but it is a small school and somewhat expected. The NWC community is very strong.For students who are strong academically and are interested in either sports, art, or music, this is a very good fit. Parents need to seek out information and push teachers and administration for answers and support. Students are expected to be self-sufficient and seek assistance themselves from Day 1 - and to be fair, NWC makes that very clear to parents. This is not a helicopter-parent school. Arts (including drama), music, and sports are very strong. If your student is a go-getter participant, they will fit in well. Pressure is very high, expectations are high, but students are stronger and succeed because of it. Be aware going in that your student will have to self-advocate, and that they will have to work much harder to achieve B's than they would to get easy A's at other schools - including nearby prep schools. I hope it pays off when we get to college applications and acceptances! My experience at NWC was fantastic. I was more than prepared to enter higher education. great school if only the vp and p and a lot of the staff actually cared about the students and not just their reputation. and your money isn’t going anywhere besides their pockets. Good: friends, sports, drama, teachers, staff. If your kid is an athlete, they’ll fit in well. Bad: lack of AP classes, few honors, old facilities, very old and limited labs, poor music program, overly dogmatic curriculum compared to other Catholic high schools. No computer science. Little choice in foreign language Few extracurricular activities (most listed in school handbook aren’t offered). And most of all, college prep and counseling.Our kids had pretty good experiences (except Religion teacher 9-11 grades). Teachers and staff are great. There’s a new principal so new families will have to see. Be forewarned - many AP classes listed aren’t available every year, and many except foreign language, can’t be taken before senior year because either there isn’t an available teacher or class (AP US History, AP English) are in very high demand so quite hard to get in. AP sciences are worse - no AP physics, and AP Chem and Bio alternate years. History department is great especially civics and AP Comp Gov.Unlike nearby private prep schools and public schools, there is hardly any college prep at NWC. Standard books in English classes which would help with SATs aren’t used. Math classes don’t teach many concepts needed, and don’t use SAT practice questions at all. No vocab even junior year! No coordination between history & English/lit to help with college essays and SAT reading comp.NWC had a fantastic, proactive, experienced college counseling team So helpful with getting us ready esp. junior year. O Summer 2021, without any communication, NWC eliminated the dept. and “merged” it in with advisory team AND no additional staff. 4 counselors for all grades, no one focused on college counseling or even related experience. Parents complained loudly once word got out through the rumor mill, and finally NWC confirmed it late October. One of the main reasons we chose NWC was college prep, and now there’s no college counseling team! 3 people’s full-time work dumped on the overtaxed advisors? We hired a private college admissions counselor, but it was late into the fall term because the school never let us know.NWC is a great school, but you need to know there are big gaps in college admissions and prep, honors classes, AP courses, sciences, building facilities, and family communication.

As children, my sister and I attended this school district (then known as Valley) and received a first class education that included college prep courses, team athletic opportunities and social experiences that served both of us well upon entering and graduating from the University of Nebraska - Lincoln. absolute garbage if you want your kid to be bullied this is the scjool for you

column3: Very helpful when it comes to being able to talk to the counselors bout the things that are bothering you. It is very hard at times though for students to feel comfortable to ask the teachers for their work. Some kids really aren't ready for it. Through one of the school's clubs, DECA (Distributive Education Clubs of America), I have learned more about the real world than I feel I have sitting in one of the classrooms there. As every student would, I would like to change their motivation to help minorities and also change their view on homework and it role in students lives. I would like to say my years at Lincoln were memorable but I can't, because of the lack of interest in the student body I would give Lincoln a 3/5 on a good day. two of five due to personal experiences with bullying and having a slower learning process My daughter transferred to this school from Washington High School in Sioux Falls because of medical discrimination at WHS (504 plan, diabetes). She had nothing but the best experiences at LHS. As a former teacher in the district, as well, I wish we had started her at LHS. I hate this school. the teachers are harsh, the principals are all rude and they pick favorites, and just the school's vibe is all off. I only come to school to see my friends honestly.

column1: As a Theater-Major sophomore of this school, this vibrant community of learners and teachers has helped me grow as a person abundantly. Freshman year I was new to the performing arts, and now I am in love with not only theater, but dance, music and visual arts as well. I went to a supposed "great" school for middle school, but this school has helped me to become the best academic student I can be. If it weren't for this school, I would most likely be reluctant about learning and going to college; now I love it! Exceptional arts education and academic approach that is rigorous and incorporates the arts into its curriculum. The teachers in the arts and academic areas that my son has had in this his first year have been outstanding. This is the first time my son has ever done well in math and science. Both of these classes are rigorous high school classes but he is flying along and bright eyed and learning so much. I have never seen a school with more teachers who are so passionate about teaching and warm and caring of their students. There is also an amazing cameraderie amongst these young student artists which makes for an amazing high school experience. All across the different arts academies friendships are made and collaborations are formed. Never have we felt so at home and connected to a school. My son goes to this school and all I can say is that it's the best school he's ever been to. He used to get Fs and Ds and I was really worried about his future but, after attending this school he managed to surprise me by getting a 4.0 GPA. He's really turned his life around and it's because of the excellent principal, staff, and students that helped him. Thank you VAPA! I really don't understand parents who gripe and moan about their precious babies having to go through a 'first come, first served' registration (it's not a lottery), for students living outside the school's boundary. That is the same process for every LAUSD neighborhood school, regardless of its focus, except for magnet campuses. And VAPA is, first and foremost, a neighborhood high school. Do they begrudge the neighborhood such an opportunity? And what a wonderful addition to the neighborhood and to LAUSD this is. There is a very caring, conscientious faculty and staff who, while they do live the Arts, never take their eye off of the core education being offered. It's only year 2, so there have been some growing pains, but overall I'm pleased with the Academic, as well as the Arts education that my daughter is receiving. Far from a 'fail,' I would classify VAPA as a huge LAUSD success in the making. I have two students at this school who have been there since the start. They are in different academies and both notice a decline in the focus on the arts, with a more prevalent militant atmosphere. The principal and administration are mostly self-serving and don't seem to have the best interest of the students in mind at all. They discourage parental involvement and communication is a real problem. The academics are weak. There are some extremely incompetent teachers who should be fired. However, there are some very capable and effective teachers who enhance the learning experience. There is too much turmoil and confusion and very little support. The architecture is lovely, but is an empty shell with very few supplies to really accomplish anything in the arts. The partnership with the arts in LA is weak and discouraged by the administration. Creative expression is not encouraged and there is a pervasive attitude that learning can only occur within a classroom setting; so assemblies and field trips are discouraged. This school is not even close to reaching its full potential! This is our first year at this school, having moved to the area from out of state. After careful consideration of several performing arts schools, we chose this school for several reasons, including commitment to academics and the fact that students don't have to audition to get in. Even though, my son could have been accepted at an school that required audition, the no-audition policy opens the school to all types of students, not just those who had the money for training prior to high school and, thus, gives a more authentic public-school experience. I have been impressed with the academics and the encouragement that my son gets to develop both academically and artistically. In the first semester he has been here, he has thrived and developed as a dancer, student and person. The teaching staff is passionate about teaching and treats the students with respect. There are very few of the problems of other high schools because students are encouraged to be themselves and be accepting of each other. I would recommend this school to anyone who desires to pursue a visual or performing art as a future endeavor, specially if the parents don't want to sacrifice academics in the process. "This school is the best I've ever been to," says my daughter. My daughter is a Junior now, and she says the teachers are understanding, respectful, and just great. She also says that this is the reason why she wakes up every morning. The students are really nice towards each other, and this school is very civilized. I am a senior at this school, and I have been here since its opening (9/9/2009). I came to this school completely untrained in visual art. Before, I was the "kind of interested in art because it looks cool and fun, but I'm not really good at it" student. Today, I can confidently tell any student, parent, administrator, or PERSON that this school shaped who I am today, in both character and lifestyle. My teachers are some of the most hard-working, dedicated, and passionate teachers I've ever had the privilege of working with, academically AND artistically. (Even our school librarian and janitors are awesome!) This is a community unlike any other school I've been to (3 elementary , 1 middle); here, you earn what you work for, and we accept and tolerate each other in a respectful manner. I entered this school (honestly) lacking artistic skill, and generally I was just another kid who didn't know what to do with my life--I didn't have a "passion" for anything, and I went to school living day-by-day. Now I look forward to school everyday, and I wish I had more time here (even though I am SO ready for college!!!). If I ever had a kid interested (or not) in the arts, I'd send them HERE! Ramon C. Cortines School for the Visual & Performing Arts This is the ony arts education HS on the west coast. The philosophy is thorugh the daily discipline of the arts the student will the corelate this to their daily critical studies. We are a no audition school but placement only which means students at 13 whom have never been exposed to the arts have front door acessiblity this campus. The scores are coming up everyday which means the mission is working which is to keep studetns engaged with their studies via the visual & performing arts. The first three valectdictorians attend Harvard, Columbia, and USC on full academic scholarships. The campus embraces and practices tolerance through arts integration by stating we all belong on the same canvas. Albert Einstein shared his wisdom & reality connection by stating "the world will not be saved by a scientist but instead by an artist", Scientists raise great riddles and artists solve them. My School is an amazing experience if you are talented whether it's music, art, dance or theater. Great school! My stars speak for me, but in the event that this does not suffice, I am more than welcome to provide a more detailed review: The school is COMPLETELY safe! In all my four years of attending this school I have never felt threatened by neither outside nor inside forces. The school and its faculty promote a nurturing, yet challenging atmosphere filled with interdisciplinary interaction. The kids aren't bad either. True, there are some that exude apathy for their school work and craft, but this is a prevalent characteristic everywhere. But if your child is motivated to learn and succeed, then he/she will naturally gravitate to the hard workers and the true artists. The students work very closely with the teachers, forging immensely strong bonds; if you are willing to stay active as a parent, you will surely become easily acquainted with the teachers as well. I still know a lot of fellow graduates who have stayed in close touch with our teachers; we love and respect them. This institution has sent students to ivy league schools, as well as premiere performing arts schools, a testament of its ability to cultivate intelligent artists. As artisans, we are taught to make change. I'm now an alumni at vapa, and I've been in that amazing school since it first opened. I'm happy to be pat of this school and its students and faculty. Students get along very well at vapa, and are quite helpful to each other or to anyone for that matter. 0 fights and 0 vandalisim inside and near the school. this school is full of diversity of characteristics,culture,and people, but we all put them either to good use or put them aside. Although VAPA can be a crazy school when its school year, its a "controlled chaos" type of crazy and both students ,teacher and parents help each other to have an acomplish year. as a musician to that school i was happy on what my 4 years of singing with the groups at vapa. Showing other school what we got and getting awards,partnerships, and prizes(if we get lucky) on our music tours. i guess te principal change and staff changes can decrease and have a permanent faculty.and all the miscommunication between teachers,office satff,students, and parents. but i guess its all part of the experience for this school. i had a good 4 years, but had to pay lot of trips because we dont get help from the district.... My son found an educational home at VAPA when he transferred there last year. He went from a school where his talent and unique personality were the focus of bullying (by teachers as well as other students!) to a place where he is accepted, celebrated, befriended and truly encouraged to work to hone his craft (percussion) achieve his dreams. My freshman year here was just great. At first, I was a bit skeptical about this school because I felt I had to fit in but I later realized you can be yourself at this school without being judged so harshly like other schools. Many people accept you as you are. The upperclassmen were really welcoming at times so I didn't feel so uncomfortable, which was a plus. The teachers I had were great! I felt like they actually cared to have a relationship with their students to help them grow academically and personally. This school is a grate school you get to have fun and learn new things every day will meeting new people in the same time. My daughter attends this school; she is a freshman in the Theater Academy and seems to be struggling a bit with the extremely high demands from some of the teachers and some disorganization from the school. The high turnover in Principals affects these kids one way or another and most likely the Teachers as well. The fact that these kids do not have any formal sports is very discouraging; they are missing out on the exercise benefit, HS games, and being able to cheer on their friends which is a huge factor in a teen's life. It is a great school and a lot of money was invested in bringing this school to the community, but I think the administration needs to be a little more open to these kids needs at this point in their lives and incorporate sports to their school. I know the majority of these kids are here because this is a career path for them, but they are missing out in the sports camaraderie which should be in every HS teen's life. The school is so lucky to have a new Principal. Kim Bruno is charismatic, smart and represents the school well. This is an excellent school for students who are interested in the arts AND a rigorous academic curriculum, with 16 AP courses offered. There are plenty of art classes and the academic teachers are wonderful, this is our son's fourth year at the school and all his teachers have been great. The lack of team sports is a plus, there is a great collaborative, non-competitive spirit among the students, who are kind and welcoming and just great kids. My Daughter has been there for 3 yrs and they do not have an emergency plan for handicap students in wheelchair. The elevator has broken down several times...and I mean SEVERAL times!!! Today my daughter called me at 2pm telling me she was stuck on the 2nd floor because the elevator broke down AGAIN. People on the office was informed but what happened? EVERY BODY left and it was 5pm and my daughter was still on the second floor. This is unacceptable. The staff and administrator do not care!! This school is not what it used to. For all the students going there now and calling it a great school, you should've been there when it first opened in 2009. I was a freshman in 2009 and that school was fantastic. The original staff and principal were amazing. But every year they made more and more cuts. Fired many wonderful teachers for standing up and voicing their opinions. Fired Ms. Gardea, who happened to be the best assistant principal the music academy had. The school went to hell after the class of 2013, the first class that attended all 4 years there, graduated. I'm so glad I don't go there anymore. Even my sister, former student, left the school her junior year and agrees that the school is horrible. It's glory year was 2009. This school will never be as amazing as it was before Incompetence with the administration. Not a safe school for students. Bullying and bad behavior ignored Grand Arts is an excellent choice when it comes to a strong academic and artistic education. We have no regrets about pulling our daughter out of our home district to send her to this LAUSD school. We plan on sending our other two children as well when the time comes. We are beyond grateful that this school exists! It's fun. Teachers work very hard to motivate others. You are free to be who you want to be. The academies are fun and they really teach you and go into depth especially music and theater. I'm sure it's a great school for the Arts, but the academics are not so good. I had to pull my daughter out of the school due to the academics. She attended private school up until middle school but wanted to go an Arts high school so she went to Grand Arts. It didn't take long for her to realize she was far ahead of most of the other students even in AP/Honors class. She loves Theater so she tried to stick it out for a few weeks but she just couldn't deal with having to review her entire middle school in Math, Science(Biology) and Lang Arts. So if you're not too concered about academics and your child being challenged, and they Love the Arts, then this school is for you My 10th grader loved this school so much, she always wanted to attend! Not a day went by that she did not want to go to school. Granted, this was for more social reasons, but still... They definitely focus on the arts, so if you prefer a more intense workload for core subjects, this is not the school for your child. but you prefer them to learn the arts and be happy, choose VAPA! They do offer AP and honors, tho. The teachers and admin are all so helpful, albeit busy at times. I always got an answer to inquires and they all cared to the next level to help in any way.They do fun activities at lunch. Lunch always has vegan ad veg options too.They have no sports so if you are looking for that, maybe not the best choice.There is very little bullying at this school as well, as the student population is not only diverse but celebrates those differences: culture, orientation, etc.The school building itself is also outstanding and has all the modern features.Their productions are top notch, all put on by the students, future starts!Can not recommend this school enough, especially for the arts. This school is rude, disorganized and for a performing arts school has no organization in informing what’s going on to parents or student. “Proud principle Lori Gambero” is a train wreck. Some arts teachers stand out and you have to commend them because the COVID times were a big monkey wrench - but over all just kinda meh. Facilities are great. Security is good but be prepared for general lacksidasical LAUSD mediocrity, bureaucracy and underwhelming academics.

column1: Very challenging, rigorous academics. I graduated from WA in 2010 and felt it had prepared me excellently for college. WA has a GREAT selection of AP courses and the teachers (..well, most of them) are qualified to teach AP. The courses are challenging - I averaged about 5-6 hours of sleep my junior and senior years. The guidance department tries their best to help out, but I wish they were more helpful during the College App process. The music department is great, the theater department is EXCELLENT, as is the Speech/Debate team. WA recently won the NCLB Blue Ribbon - well deserved. Great school all around! Westford has excellent elementary and middle schools, but falls short at the Westford Academy. Problems are swept under the rug and parents are left in the dark. I loved this school, the teachers are great they are really laid back, understanding, and flexiable with our needs. The guidance counselors and deans are top notch I loved them. They gave me more than I asked for in support academically and outside of it. Everyone in the school gets along with each other and are very respectful towards one another. There is also a great variety of classes and I had a great time! Westford Academy was a great place to go to highschool. For those students who graduated in the top 15% of my class (late 90's), we all had opportunities to attend either Ivy League or top tier private universities. Teachers were engaged, and AP and Honors classes were excellent. The class size was small (at or under 30 students for most classes) and we had various opportunities to study abroad as part of the foreign language curriculum, participate in various after school activiites and varsity and jv sports. There were also art, theater and music programs available, however these were not the most robust compared to other schools districts I attended as a child. These could be improved. There was a massive school renovation during my last year and I'd be interested to know how that impacted the experience for students graduating after me. Guidance counselers were helpful, but not as critical and constructive in helping select colleges appropriate for students' apptidue and personality - seemed like more of a check-the-box exercise. In general, an excellt school district. I greatly dislike this school. I'm a rising junior at Westford Academy and I have always loved going to school. So, when the first day of high school came, I was just as excited. But it was awful. Kids here are rude, mean, and judgmental. I myself am competitive, but never to the point that I would cheat. But the thing is, kids here do cheat. And worst of all, teachers virtually never realize it. The textbooks in most cases are horrible. I don't even understand how some of these science teachers even got their teaching degrees. The clubs that are student run are pointless- nothing ever gets done. There are a few great teachers here, but they're rare. Facilities are great, I absolutely love the library! But besides that, there are just SO many problems that need to be addressed. :'(. If you can, please do yourself and your kids a favor and send them to Acton Boxborough Regional High School instead! My parents almost moved us to Acton instead of Westford and not a day goes by without me wishing that we lived in Acton instead. This school has the worst guidance counselors. This blonde told my son he wasn't college material. He's finished Law school. She told my coworkers son , he wasn't college material and he flies for a major airlines, good grief... Coercive administration, shortest school day in MA. poor facilities with floating teachers, and students socially promoted to boost their graduation rates Westford Academy was just ranked #3 best school districts in Massachusetts in 2019... just behind Lexington and Newton, and #32 in the country by Niche. Some of the reviews from 4-5 years ago come across as fabricated especially about the preference of moving to Acton school systems. I’ve lived in this town for 14 years and have never known or heard of anyone sharing these sentiments. Do some homework and Westford Academy is always amongst the very top schools in Massachusetts This is truly a great school. All the credit goes to the teachers and the staff that work hard to make the kids experience as good as possible. They think outside the box. Just go to any open house. You will be impressed. My family moved to Westford this year and we have had a very negative experience at Westford Academy. My child's needs have been dismissed and ignored by certain teachers, the Dean and even the Superintendent. If your child is not completely typical and compliant, do not expect them to do well at WA. I moved to this town largely because of the wonderful reputation of the school system. I have been deeply disappointed.

column3: Overall: miserable. HOH high school is disappointing in every single department, has been for years and no change is visible in the future. Many high schools have fabulous newspapers, lively history classes, engaging math depth. science, foreign language, nice people, nice memories. Not here. Please avoid. Life is too short. There are many good public and private schools in the area where your kids will have wonderful experiences, learn a lot and make life-long friends.

column1: This is the best school I have ever been to. The teachers are amazing and they are willing to work with kids to help them out. The school has challenged me but I am able to excel. I am so glad I came to this school! This is an amazing school where students feel valued and are encouraged to succeed through problem solving and individualization. We waited years to get in, and are so thrilled to have our children here. The teachers are wonderful and caring, and each day my child can't wait to see what is next at school. His 3rd/4th grade teacher, Ms. B. is the best we've seen, and we are sad she won't be his teacher next year. I hope with the expansion the school retains its commitment to the children, rather than simply a test score. This school is wonderfully diverse, and has a student lead learning model rich with project based learning. I highly recommend it! My children do not fit into the bell curve, so to speak. They both have IEPs and learning and health challenges. My impression from 95% of the teachers in the middle and high schools was that they didn't have time to deal with my 2 children. After 4 years of fighting battles, dealing with prejudice teachers (even special education teachers), and inadequate leadership, I pulled my children from this school. Extremely disappointing. Child was bullied over and over and principle and teachers didn’t act on it. There was also racial bias-BIG TIME! Terrible for my kids! Lots of tension, inequality. This school needs a change with the two top administrators. Ok. Some good dome bad. New principal would help a lot. Why not everybody else has them at 5 Stars or at 1 star? If your kids go there, you know what’s right or wrong with all this? Even if you don’t go here you see what all this is about? Principles on the side teachers and not looking for the problem that exists!! The director if school’s not listening to paro, but will listen to staff without knowing what’s happening or what happened. But just ignore the parent by acknowledging that she isn’t listening to you or what you have to say, are you kidding me? But if you answer phones for her.....????........ But what can you do? Just leave and don’t say anything more, that’s what they want? They cannot say otherwise and she knows all of this without lying on HER new job?? I’m sure this is going to effect what and how my kids do, oh wait it’s already happening!!!!! This School has tons of bullying and no one does anything about it. Students make tons of racist, sexist, and homophobic jokes everyday. This school does not value a safe environment for their students. During COVID, they continue to host House Events which mix the entire school, K-12, together. They will not encourage masks for the students who chose masking as their COVID prevention option. Two months into school, they are still not enforcing weekly testing, as promised. The director does not communicate well with concerned parents. She avoids issues and pretends she does not know about COVID or the concerns of parents. The school does not value prevention and education when it comes to COVID protocol. They would rather pretend COVID is a cold and not a threat to our community. My family tested positive for COVID because of the school's lack of attention, concern, and action. Their hope is to get everyone sick so we can get past it. I would not look forward to dealing with any concerning situation with this school, as the director and board of governors DO NOT CARE about you more than money. I tried for two months to get someone to listen. Their response was to turn off their emails. Also, they did not focus on teaching my child at all so far this school year. No homework, no challenging assignments, little effort all around. As someone with an education background, this is a poor excuse for an educational facility. Besides sports, what are they teaching?

column1: For a public school, this school is decent, but it leaves a lot to be desired. College-bound students are given little help with the process as the administration focuses all of its resources on helping the lazy students who aren't on track to graduate. The soccer team is amazing and the band program is strong, but when it comes to getting into college, you have to be 100% self motivated. A lot of drugs too. My daughter graduates this year. She adores this school, but it must be said--she's a freak: Self-motivated, mature, tireless worker. The big surprise ffor us is the degree of school spirit she feels even though she could not care less for sports. What's worked? Fabulous teachers (she missed the duds), strong academics, award-winning lit/arts magazine, ultimate frisbee, coffee house, theater arts, and again . . . teachers-teachers-teachers. I cannnot speak for the experience of the less-academically inclined. This is a diverse student population with a fair percentage of low-income and immigrant children. For what I can see, they're doing the job. My son's experience as a freshman has been positive as well. He's a nerd, and has felt welcomed and connected. An awesome start, I'd say. As a student with ADHD, depression, and an anxiety disorder, I have trouble with most schools and their methods of teaching and assigning work. Schools are required to offer help and accommodations for mental illness, but at Shorecrest you have to fight tooth and nail to get it, and even after doing that I wasn't given any help. My brother had dropped out because of this, while I'm struggling to get through a second senior year. In all, I'm extremely disappointed with the administration. The only upside is the great performing arts program, but that doesn't seem to be a high priority with the administration. Teachers tend to be hit or miss, with some amazing teachers and some absolutely terrible excuses for educations. The Culinary Programs and Arts program are fantastic!!! The teachers and counselors care about students and make an outstanding effort to work with families, students, and staff so that ALL students can be successful in their pursuits for high school and higher education. The school definitely has a high drug and alcohol usage among students. The school security is awful since students bring E-cigarettes, cigars, and bottles of alcohol into school so easily. There is a lot of school pride, and lots of inclusiveness. There is problems with students AND teachers. Hallways and classrooms do get out of control frequently. Students are normally respectful towards one another. We have two kids who are at or have gone through Shorecrest in recent years and third chiled on the rise. At every level with the Shoreline School District, since elementary, but especially at SC, we have been thoroughly impressed with every facet of the District; and with Shorecrest, from Lisa Gonzales, the principal, through to every teacher, staff member, counselor, and office personnel, we have been so pleased. The facility itself, an $80mm ground up new construction on the original site c. 2015, is amazing. The AP course selection has been terrific for our kids, who have taken Calc AB/BC (a UW course) their junior/senior years, and AP courses in English, Physics, Chem, and History. The diversity of the student body, both racial and socioeconomic, has been incredible. Sports, music, and other extracurricular programs are abundant (and are a reason we've chosen SC over some excellent private school options nearby). Are there issues? Sure. But these issues aren't unique to SC and I think Principal Gonzales and the staff do an amazing job with each challenge with which they are presented. I would give this place six stars if I could. Without hesitation, and wholeheartely, we would recommend this to anyone looking for an excellent high school for their children. I was happy with my first child but unfortunately have been disappointed with how my second child has been treated. They will be losing a smart, enthusiastic STEM student because of their lack of action to address mistreatment by staff toward my child. I don’t recommend this school for all kids. Excellent. Really helped to prepare for college.
