column3: I am a teacher at palmetto. While I think we have an overall decent administration and many good teachers, it seems to me that there are some teachers out there who are too lenient and lax based just based on student behavior. Some do not enter enough grades and some put all their grades in at the last minute. It drags down morale, and referrals/conferences rarely help student motivation. Some classes are huge (approaching 40 students per class!) so this also does not help create an educational environment. Unfortunately, many students do not have a stable family structure at home and this also leads to a difficulties in the classroom, specifically with a teacher's expectations for achievement. There is a big, big drug/alcohol/absentee problem and many do not fear the repercussions. The school could improve with stricter guidelines for teachers, more guidance from administration, and a firmer, vocalized stance from the principal, specifically with using the intercom more. Overall, it's an average/okay school, but it could be so much better, because there is potential, but it is unrealized. I am a senior here at Palmetto high school +class of 2013) and I can ensure you that palmetto us great school with great opportunities. I have been a part of the Aice Program,Dual enrollment, and honors program for four years. These are all programs that will you stand out in the crowd to colleges 60% of my class are graduating high school with college classes already done. This school works to make sure everyone achieves their success. We have went from a D school to a b school in a year. Everything is getting stronger and the students here want to learn. The environment is so comfortable. We have had no fights or drama. If you ask someone who never went to palmetto what type of school it was they'd tell you many negatives. That us because outsiders voice their opinion in the past. The school has changed, there's new teachers and administration. They have everything going good. This school.. Some great teachers.. Some teachers give to many referrals.. Not a place for racist people.. Not really much bullying going on.. Drugs and smoking are a bog problem here. So if you worry about your child getting into that i'd be careful. . Soda machines only have diet . Some classes you do absolutely nothing others they pile work on work.. Big school, a lot of walking . Can get confusing sometimes.. Theres not much of a popularity problem.. Theres the boys( mostly) & girls who think they're better than everyone because they play football or cheer or what not.. Its an okay school. Some call it Palmghetto .. This came from a student. So ya I graduated from this school last year, and I have very mixed reviews. If your child is gifted, and would soar in AICE/Dual Enrollment courses, then they will enjoy PHS. The teachers that offer AICE/ DE classes are, for the most part, excellent teachers that are very helpful as well as fun. For the average/lower courses (i.e.; Intensive math/language arts), the teachers are usually very poorly educated, do not like to teach through the individual needs of a student, and lack at their job. If your child would be on those types of classes, do not go to PHS. They will struggle and the school will be a horrible place for them. AICE/DE students usually enjoy their time because they are treated like adults by the teachers of those courses and it is actually quite easy. Staff can be racist/play favorites, lots of fights and drugs (but hey, what HS does not have that?). Clubs are lacking, and guidance cons. are HORRIBLE, you will have to do everything yourself because they barely know anything going on (ex: I asked when our cap and gowns were coming in, she said she had no idea, they were not informed. I turn on the school news and I find my answer). Room for improvement. You get the feeling that some teachers have the attitude of "out to get you", don't really care for their students. Excellent PTSA. i love my school because i have great friends and teachers there. the environment of the school sometimes is a litter crazy , but you will find that in every school you go to. My daughter has had a great experience here. The teachers are phenomenal at Palmetto! She came in during her Junior year and made many new friends! She is also involved in many AP courses and after-school activities. The AICE, Dual Enrollment, and AP classes challenge the students, but the teachers make the course very exciting and encouraging. Regarding the extracurricular activities, my daughter loves them! My only complaint would be that they don't have many sports to offer. However, my daughter has made so many new friends and is getting good exercise while doing so. I cannot recommend this school enough! Horrible home school teachers, who gave up on me It’s a great school I am a freshman and I have learned a lot so far this year I love all of my teachers except for one which is Mr.Ling he is a butt face he is really rude like for real my best friend has him 7th period and she doesn’t like him For the past 4 years palmetto high school as showed me what its like to be a role model i would for sure recommend any incoming freshman students to come to palmetto high. I LOVE IT HERE!!!!!!!!!!! GO TIGERS!!!!!!!!!! My overall experience of this high school is great. The teachers and office staff are very nice and always seek out to help students. The honors classes can be difficult to most students, but there are plenty of people of campus that are willing to help you if you need it. The campus life is very fun whether its during school hours or before the football games when he have tailgates. Over the past four years, i have never regretted anything that I have done here at Palmetto High School, and i would recommend going here to anyone especially over Parrish Community High School. The palmetto high school AICE program has been one of the most helpful programs that i as a student have been in, it gives student responsibility to keep up with everything. This school helped me succeed in academics and maturity. The kind staff and teachers make sure to help you as much as possible and provide numerous resources. The school also provides many extracurricular activities that allow students to explore different hobbies and sports. The AICE program that Palmetto High School challenges students and gives them the opportunity to receive the AICE Diploma. Palmetto High is a great school for academics and sports. With the guide of teachers and staff I was able to finish high school early and receive my AICE diploma I have gone to this school for all 4 years and never had a problem. All my siblings go here too and its great. I've made so many friends and met some of my favorite staff members ever. I have been apart of the Palmetto High School AICE program for the past four years. The AICE program is an amazing opportunity to earn college credit while still in highschool. My experience at Palmetto High school was filled with ups and downs. But overall, Palmetto High is a great school for academics and athletics. I met new people and made some great friends. Palmetto High School has great academic courses, sports teams, and clubs. Each of the teachers and faculty members show us that they care and give us support when we need it. The AICE courses at Palmetto are great and the teachers for the courses make sure each students understands the concepts and they do their best to help us succeed. My experience at this school has been a wonderful ride through high school. Teachers teach to give students life skills to remember through their lives. The AICE program helps to get students prepared for the real work world by giving them important skills that help them in careers. Multiple academic rewards can be received through the school such as bright futures. These rewards are given fairly to all students and counselors are extremely helpful through the process. They respond to emails quickly and effectively and help you with any questions you need help with. All of the staff are very helpful, kind, and respectful. Palmetto High school is a really great school with qualified staff. If you ever encounter any issues, the school is ready to help you overcome them. All the teachers are very kind and wonderful. The atmosphere at the school is always great with laughing and happy students all around. All the staff members are all amazing and always looking to help students and protect them. At this school I've been able to make great friends and form connections with teachers and faculty alike. When it comes to public school I think Palmetto has a lot to offer. My experience at this school has been quite satisfactory. I would say that the academics and the AICE and AP courses provided by the school are amazing and are an awesome opportunity for students looking to go to college in the state of Florida. Palmetto High School is a very friendly and welcoming school. Many teachers go above and beyond to make sure that the students understand what they are learning and then some. Students at Palmetto love to make new friends and they are good at making you not feel left out. I moved from DC to Palmetto. I had previously attended very good schools, 2 in fact. When I came to Palmetto, I was in my senior year. I was in AP classes and immediately noticed a grift. I was reading books in AP English in 12th grade that I had read in 6th grade. They were very far behind my other schools. The standards were low. It's not a nice school, it's in a terrible part of town, drugs are RAMPANT. I know from firsthand experience. This was the worst school I ever attended. Words cannot express how happy I was to graduate. There is a massive racial divide here as well. Anyone that claims that the school is a good school their child is probably in the ace program. Otherwise this school is absolutely horrible . The teachers have no communication. The grades change daily so these kids are getting zero grades for things if they miss classes the system is just messed up it’s almost set up for these kids to fail. There are probably a handful of good teachers at the school at most otherwise most of them don’t care and they’re just going through the motions .Not to mention the violence their constant fights , The amount of videos that my daughter has shown me from the fights at the school are disturbing. Maybe if they put arm guards at the door you’d have less fighting and less chance of a gun being on campus like it just was at a football game.The bus is late every single day teachers don’t even know about the changes about the bus so kids are directed wrong directions nobody is on the same page at the school. The women at the front desk are rude. My daughter also was supposed to have an IEP that got lost in the shuffle never accommodated my daughter I feel like my daughter really lost a good chance of a decent education because of the school. I would never recommend anyone I know to send their kids to this school. they have no control over any of the students at the school.

column1: Parents and students seeking academic success...BEWARE. HCHS has great potential, but the root of its failure is the community. Teachers/superintendents have all been trained to do their job properly and do care at the core. The student body is however overwhelming the system through their choices and way of life constraining their motivations to reach their goals. It seems as education is not the first priority for many students, not saying all are like that, but its what is shown. On the plus side, the school has a good athletic program and most students show interest in participating. Faculty has shown great interest in pushing forth the dress code, but most students have failed to notice that it is the first step to provide the order and discipline required for a successful academic year and those more to come. Most students need to learn to follow the rules; their voices are heard but disciplinary cooperation is also needed back from them. - Former student

column3: Alumni/Parent. Great place for a tween/teen. It is a small town, so many parents and teachers have existing relationships. The "last name" advantage has been decried for 50 years but the names referenced change with each class, depending on which teachers have kids in school and which parents are involved. Because the town only has one elementary and one high school, relationships also carry over. The offerings are limited, but the ag and art programs are top notch, and both encourage parental involvement. In extra-curriculars, generally everybody who wants to play, perform or compete makes the team. You can expect everyone to all know your kid's name, and yours, to the extent that you are involved in extra-curriculars. Teachers are friendly and invest a lot of care into each student, and it shows. This school consistently graduates fine young people who are mature, polite, and assets to their colleges, workplaces and communities. I employ two of them myself. You have to stay on top of the guidance office, but there are high expectations for the new principal and vice-principal, both of whom were successful teachers at the school. Test scores are the best in the county and area. Dawn Eakins is a horrible Guidance Counselor. She misleads the students giving them the wrong information about important tests and online classes. She should be fired! Anna Delgoto is the Alg 1 teacher that is very hard to understand doesn't speak clearly or correctly. She's very rude to parents and students. Not professional at all. Dawn Eakins guidance counselor at the school should not be messing with the minds of children and trying to tear apart families. She should be making sure the kids graduate and not prey into personal life. (When there is nothing wrong with a child's home life). Very unprofessional and morally wrong. This school provides excellent success in students grades 6-12th grade.

column3: I left West Side after my freshman year and moved out of the state. Before this, I thought West Side was "the place to be", but now I just think its "the place to be, if you don't have anything better to do." Since leaving this school I have come so much farther in my academic endeavours, and I feel sorry for the people that are still there. I never knew there was so much to learn and so many opportunities for my future before I left this school. The only good thing that I can say about it is that I had some really great friends there, but, honestly, I didn't learn anything until I left. For all that posted positive comments about WS, thank you!!! For the negative posting, what are you doing to assist or correct the problems. If parents aren't involved, what can we do to assist the school with getting the deadbeat parents involved. A school is what parents make it. If no involvement is there, then the kids will act that way. Lets stop making it seem like the schools let down our kids, TAKE RESPONSIBLITIES FOR YOUR ACTIONS. (Gary Wirt High Grad, Proud supporter of the City of Gary) Lets get Gary on the Move! I am a parent of children who did not originally attend school within the Gary school system. However I grew up in the area and when my family fell on hard times we ended up back in the area. I knew when my children started the system that the schools educational system was substandard. I apologize if many of you in the community will not hear this but it is so true. I tried to leave several times but if you don't have the means, like many of the people in the city you are stuck. It is so easy to say the parent need to get involved but the truth is that most of the parents are those that have been their all of there lives and don't know anything different. It is not until you leave the city that you find out what you are truly missing in terms of educational advancements or opportunities. Also what is not understood is that because of the low economic standard of the community as a whole they are not afforded the amenities as other communities and this would include education. I am 46 yrs old and many of the books that are used today are the same books that were used when I was a student at West Side High and the same is with some teachers. Sorry if you are offended!! I am a parent of a westside student I moved here from a different school system.I attented Roosevelt High school .The Gary Cholo system is horrible. That is all That can be said about it.

column1: I am VERY thrilled with how the teachers teach the children and their vast knowledge in the specific studies. The children come first at Hiland which is appreciated. Their christian roots still hold strong today as they have prayer meetings. Sports program is loved by whole student body and famililes as they come together as a huge support to each other. Very impressed with the FFA/Ag chapter that Hiland holds. I feel that the teachers are very passionate with their job and respect the children as they teach. My only down fall with Hiland is they need to more open with the sophomores regarding future college planning. As a graduate of Hiland High School I can tell you that you won't find a better place anywhere in the state for your kids to go to school. My wife and I are looking to have kids but we are waiting until we can afford a house in the East Holmes school district. However, if you are ultra-liberal and want to raise your kids that way this probably isn't the school for you. Hiland very much promotes judeo-christian values in and out of the classroom. Although I was never forced to attend a religious function as someone on here claimed, it is very clear that most of the staff and students come from Christian homes. The real beauty of the system is that while judeo-christain values dominate school policy, I still received a very well-rounded education including exposure to other religions and ideas like evolution. As a graduate of an ultra-liberal state university I can attest that I was generally well-ahead of the class despite being taught in this environment. The only detraction from the school is the foreign language department which really misses the mark. If you want your kids to be safe, well-educated, and a part of an outstanding community this is the place for you!

column1: This school has some great teachers, and some horrible ones. I like 6 out of 7 of my teachers. On the contrary, the students are some of the most narcissistic and annoying people I have ever met. None of them seem to try to get to know you and most of them just do their makeup or yell at their friends during class (even when the teachers tell them to stop). The worst part of this school by far is the sweep program. Even if you are only a few seconds late to class (you get 5 minutes to try to get to class), you have to go to sweep. Sweep is a classroom where you sit and do nothing for 55 minutes. Most of the time there is no teacher in sweep, which means people play on their phone or hang out with their friends. The best part of this school is the teachers. My favorites are Mr. Beachy , Mr. Kuipers, and the Spanish 3-4 teacher (I forgot her name but I have her as my advisor). I haven't personally tried it, but I heard that the cafeteria food isn't that good and overpriced. They do have lots of food options though. The inside part of the cafeteria fills up very quickly; so many students have to sit outside. It would be nice in the winter, but in the record breaking, 115 degree heat, its too hot to enjoy the outside. It is a very crowed school with around 3000 students. They don't seem to care about dress code. There are a lot of clubs to join. They have chess club, creative writing club, anime club, gamer's club, beatboxing club, feminist club, band, various sports, etc. They do have a lot of electives. The school is very safe. They have security guards, closed campus, and all students have to wear ID's. Overall, there are good aspects and the bad aspects. If you want to mess around, you'll probably like this school. If you want a quality education, I'd recommend AAEC in Avondale. I sincerely hope you take my advice. I do not like this school for many reasons, for one the school is outdoors. the school has no lockers, they wouldn't take my credits because apparently in Arizona middle schools don't do high school credit courses in middle school, there goes all my hard work. We have to wear IDs all day and that's really dumb, you have this thing called sweep and that's also really dumb, it's like you want us to fail. They are not fair and consistent with the way the students are treated. They have a poor representation with the dean of discipline. This is a racist school that only focus is on race and color very unfortunate as the school is very diverse. Very unprofessional in speaking to Parents and more so to the students. Honestly believe she hates her job. Can not believe they have an administrator working with children like this. This is not a community high school this is a " If I like you, I will let you get away with anything with warnings, if I don't be prepared to be disciplined!" I am sure that other parents feel the same especially with the school ratings. Absolutely no school spirit, and no communication with parents until hours later by then you already know what is going on by students not administration. If you can pick another school for your child to attend do so. I have another son that attended Tolleson High School and nephews at Agua Fria and all have done amazing at those schools. The teachers and the administration are very involved in the education and the student welfare. I will never recommend this school to any other family. Until new administration come onboard. IDE rate it a 4/10...it’s not a bad school but it’s not that good either This school is very unique in goods but also bad ways. As a new junior I can say it was alright but I ended up moving because of how students treat each other and how fighting is common here it creates a not so good atmosphere as well with many teachers being lazy at their jobs not all but some. The good they offer many AP classes and many clubs to join and pretty decent at taking their sports seriously. I would say it’s okay but if your child is considering another school please take them out and send them somewhere else. The teachers in the school are nice but the people are not and they inflict dumb rules and certain color bathrooms for certain classes even if they are farther. d

column1: Alexander High School is an excellent school. I have been involved there for the past 8 years, first as a student and now at the professional level of a coach and professional Intern from nearby OU. Having observed other schools, I have yet to find one that displays the same amount of care and support for students from staff members. There may be some limitations due to it being a small school (the students say the lunch is inadequate this year due to budget cuts), but the environment is unlike any other. Students are very accepting of one another, and display respect to one another and to the staff. Their support and encouragement is something that will always be there for any student, former student, and staff member. went there in the past just graduated a few years ago overall its a good school , But there is a lot of favoritism and if you or your kids are not the picture perfect student/model or are not that interested in sports you might as well be ready to be treated like an outcast. many of the teachers are great there were only two or three that me and my friends disliked. DRESS CODE only applies to some students for example one rule is no yoga/leggings but if your ether a cheerleader or a volley ball player they wont reprimand you but if your a band member or a little "different" than everyone else you will get an after school. so this would be a great school for a student that is looking to play sports or something like that but nothing else many of the students and a few faculty members are very very judge mental! I felt compelled to write a review about this school after reading some of the reviews already published. I graduated from this highschool a few years ago feeling very lost. Everything about this school was discouraging. The classes are boring and repetitive. The number of sports and extracurricular activities are extremely limited. Socially, Alexander is a very repressive school. Sexism from students and teachers is commonplace and the poor are judged openly here. The drug problem at the highschool is well known and the schools way of dealing with the drug problem is even worse. They often punish the drug addicted students with school suspensions and turning them in to the police, which only makes the students feel even more isolated and alone. I cannot support a school that uses negative reinforcement with children. After I graduated from Alexander, I attended Ohio University. I saw my fellow classmates drop like flies during their freshmen year until only a few went on the graduate. I had a few wonderful teachers here but the memories of Alexander have made me want to homeschool my own children. Sexism, discrimination, controlling ways. No freedom in this school. No freedom to express what you believe, no freedom to be who you are, no freedom to learn anything of value to you. People are judged and unjustly treated. It often feels more like a prison or juvenile detention center than a school. Not to mention all the flaws in the administration of the school. If you are not the average high school student lets just say your time here will be torturous. If you are a person who has a fiery spirit against others trying to dictate over you and take away and ruin anything about you then this will be your own personal hell. I attended this school in the 80's and now have my children enrolled there. Things have changed so much over the years. Both my children attend college now and are doing very well and I am very thankful they learn quickly. The school seems to be so far behind what other schools are teaching. I realize some changes have been made to the curriculum recently but more changes are needed. Lets truly prepare them for college ex: take a test in one period for those in excellerated or honors classes, lay ground rules and stand firm. Dress code, that's another huge issue! I was embarrassed for some of the girls that attend prom and homecoming. Seriously, if the rules for the campus are in place then they should be carried out for every school function. Ex: length of dresses (don't tell me you can't find reasonable dresses, I found my girls appropriate dresses) Sports bras acceptable for sports practices... really! Come on Alexander we can be better than this!! Poor administration. Wanting to send kids to court more than do their jobs

column3: The school is beautiful and stunning. I had two girls who went to this school, one who graduated a couple of years ago and one who is close to graduating and from my experiences with my daughters, they love the school, the students, the atmosphere. The only downfall is that McKinley does have under-qualified teachers, however, I believe the school makes up for it in their strong robotics, band, and AP programs. Your child can really benefit from this school if they keep themselves well-rounded. I also approve of how strict the school is in maintaining their presence in public. McKinley rarely, if ever, gets into trouble for alcohol, violence, or drugs, at public outings, such as proms and sporting events. McKinley is in my opinion one of the best public school in the state of Hawaii. It has a few problems, like any other school but it also has a long list of pro to combat the con. Cons: -Many of the students are ESL and the teacher have to slow down in order to help them, which is awesome, but these same students tend to disobey and refuse to do their work and the language issue is hard for teachers and parents to contact each other. -A LOT of the teachers are under qualified and some are just stuck in the wrong position. -They have no really dress code. -Large class size Pros: -They focus on Academics, if you can't make grade you can't play your sport. -Great Robotics team and notable clubs/class (National Honor Society, AVID, AP, ETC.) -Friendly/helpful teachers and staff. -A wide variety of electives. -A great SPED program. -Plenty of financial aid help, which may be strange for a public school but they give out free bus passes and free/reduced lunch for those who qualify. -Great student body, the students though they have their issues with each other will have each others backs when they need it. -Central location I'm writing this review out of a severe concern. I am a friend of a single mom with one child who attends this school. The child is in her third year. She seems very bright and has a wonderful disposition. However... Recently, I had a conversation with this child and it turned out that she was virtually clueless about any kind of history. This poor girl had barely heard of George Washington. She knew absolutely NOTHING about how America was created via the revolution. She knew NOTHING about the Civil War nor could barely tell me who Abraham Lincoln was. On top of this, she had never heard of the Roman empire. Not a clue... Seriously? I learned about this stuff when I was in fifth grade. (Catholic School.) Sadly, the mother doesn't speak English very well as it is not her first language. Therefore she has difficulty in checking up on this child's homework and tests in general. However, this should NEVER be a reason for any child in being this clueless about the world. I cannot imagine that in one year, this child will be applying for college. Where are the standards and who is accountable? I feel like it has been an average experience. I haven’t been to other high schools so I don’t know how to compare but it has all sorts of people. 4.5 gpa students, students who don’t even come to class, teachers who really suck at teaching and teachers who you wish was your teacher for all subjects because they were so good.

column1: This schools teachers are the laziest ever, they dont care about you, most of them care for their paycheck, the principal is awesome Being a student here, and not knowing any other school other than the Heritage schools, it's hard to judge. I will tell you now, if you are a parent, you may not want to send your kid off here. The students are very spoiled, and the teachers will give you packets all the time. Some teachers will actually teach, but it seems as if the students here are pressured into getting good grades, and not getting a "Husky Help wristband". The teachers do not inspire, or seem to care. We are given busy work, and we usually use computers. Your tax money is not spent wisely at this school. I do have some good teachers, however. But students here are pampered, and we are also thought of as children. I want a teacher to be serious about their job, who won't be disappointing if I get a bad grade. They'd teach differently if we fail a test, and not point fingers at us. Other than teachers trying to explain things on a college level, they should simply explain it in a way we can all understand, inspire us, make it simple, and celebrate good grades. This school is trying, but a good school is not made up of "good" students, but good teachers. These teachers don't pass as "good". A great school! The principal is present and helps all students learn. The majority of my son's teachers are helpful and set high expectations for all students. I feel he is in a safe learning environment. The curriculum is rigorous. The school offers many elective classes so that he may express himself and have fun learning. Many parents who have time to spend helping at the school. As a senior at Heritage I must say that the experience has been amazing. The teachers are very helpful and go out of their way for each student, the activities are really enjoyable, the campus is gorgeous and the spirit is like no other. The teachers and the staff are genuine and they really want the students to achieve the highest level of education possible. The school offers many opportunities with career building such as the academies you can take to help decide what you will do with your future. I have been to other high schools before and none of them are as beautiful and clean as well as having friendly staff and students. The students are really like a big family, we all come together and if is such a great way to enjoy the four years spent here. Forever proud to call myself a Patriot! More than half of the teachers at this school barley know how to teach or could care less about the grades of the students. Heritage used to be a fun and spirited school, however each year it gets worse. The kids are stuck up and if you aren't in a 'clique' you're looked upon as a no body. Maybe if kids would learn to be kind to everyone no matter who they are we would't have a problem. However the parents and children think they're better than everyone not saying this goes to all because this deffinatley doesn't..however many are like this. If you want to send your child to a school where everyone is a part of the school and the experience is like a big family, don't choose HHS. Do not let the school's looks tempt you. This school has literally some of the worst teachers. Most teachers do not teach, they play on their phone while assigning busy work. The PE teachers make the students preform acts some would consider abusive. Teachers often set up students to fail. Even AP classes, like Human Geography, are set up to do repetitive busy work that causes students too "learn less more" and assign excessively large BS projects that will not help the student learn the material nor pass the AP test. While these may be common issues at other schools, they are pervading here. Heritage is a beautiful school that could pass for a JC. Unfortunately, the quality of the education is lacking. Many teachers are there just for a paycheck and are on their phones or Facebook while they handout busy work in class for students. They will tell the kids they don't care if they are on their phones and don't correct bad behavior and disruption I feel because of no support from the administration and the uninvolved parents. My child showed me a snap chat story that was done during school of kids doing vodka shots IN CLASS. A LARGE number of students show up stoned to class... Yes, these could be problems at any school but Liberty Union would have you believe their schools are fabulous. They are FAILING!! I moved my child to a private school in walnut creek and the 3.81 that was easily received at Heritage dropped to a 3.16!!! Spanish had to be dropped because of lack of knowledge, (received an A at Heritage) and was behind in every subject. If you want good preparation,for college, maturity, involved teachers, less politics, PLEASE move your child to a different school. I finally got smart after my child was missing 3 books after school had been in session 6 weeks!! And yes I went to her counselor (who is dressed worse than any inappropriate outfit a student could wear), the vice principal and the school district. Don't you know... "Common core" was to blame for the lack of preparedness the school had for their students. But don't worry, the athletic department has a LARGE budget to work with.... Special Ed students have to clean up trash in this heat and it makes me feel like it's unfair,I'm ashamed of having to attend this school this school. Though Heritage High has flaws, those flaws can easily be overlooked. The teachers are great, for the most part. Everyone complains of the lazy teachers only here for the paycheck, when that's a very small amount. And they also complain that they don't slow down, when you shouldn't have your hand held at this age, unless you have special needs. Get use to it. This is life, because once your time with high school is done, it's off to college. The principal is great, but the student leadership could use a little work. The school is VERY spirited. I'm in the band program, when I go to the Varsity Football games to play music, and many of the students have a blast, and respectful of those who get hurt. Speaking of, I'm yet to see a single bully in this school. Maybe I'm just doing a great job of blending in (which is what you should do), or the school deals with bullies greatly. The school resource officer is great at his job, and very friendly. And, the school is clean. Heck, even the bathrooms look nice. All vandalism is cleaned right away and trash is picked up daily. And students here are, yes, very spoiled. But, none are real jerks. I was welcomed here by many, I've made great new friends, and rekindled old friendships. I'm a freshman of this school, and this has been the best of year of school I've ever had. My son transferred from Freedom after some major bullying issues. He thrived at Heritage. His grades weren't the best as he had to learn due dates on assignments matter. However, he was engaged. He learned. If he had a problem his counselor was there for him. Not just for academic support, but emotional as well. over all a pretty good school. Bullying is a issue for me and teachers don't really do much about it. Unfortunately there is a lot of transphobia when it comes to students. Once again teachers turn a blind eye and ignore it. The teachers overall are great but its very hard to get your pronouns changed on your papers. There isn't a lot of wiggle room for students with different learning needs and teachers don't take kid's ADHD into account. a lot of, don't doodle in class, put that toy away its distracting etc. As with most schools the system is very outdated. Covid safety wise it'd say its decent. bathrooms as always still never have enough soap but hand sanitizer is easy to find around the campus. Bathrooms are fairly clean but not always. Teachers are nice and understanding and some are very LGBTQIA+ inclusive. There is a lot of action needed to be taken against bullying and students need to feel safe. Classes are fairly interesting and id say you definitely learn. There is a lot of insensitivity and teachers are pushing a lot of kids to their breaking points. Action needs to be taken. kids are not the ones failing, the school system is failing us and i wish something will be done. Students should not put their work before their mental and physical health. Students should not come home feeling useless and like a failure and cry everyday. I have nothing against this school and its decent but i think schools as a whole need to make changes Id also like to add that dress codes are extremely unfair, male students will wear tank tops with their nipples practically showing and be just fine while female and other students will show shoulders or a stomach and get their whole day disrupted. This needs to changeInclusivity towards students who are not on the spectrum of male and female needs to be added as well. Assumptions are harmful The school is in a very beautiful location and is an excellent school. I highly recommend to all parents who want their children to have a quality 4 year high school education. So far, the school has exceeded my expectations. My daughter is thriving both in class and through extra-curricular activities. We’ve found amazing teachers, coaches and mentors as well as as a community of school spirit. My only complaint is traffic !

column3: WLHS is a great, well rounded school. The academics are outstanding, the athletics are pretty good (for being a public school), the teachers and staff are very effective and helpful. The teachers actually care, and the staff take care of everything. Cliques exist. But they exist everywhere. The only thing is, there's a lot of racial tension towards some students, being that hispanics/ african americans/ orientals, ect. are a minority. However, all kids seem to find their way and be happy. The course loads can be challenging, which is great. Many classes are offered. The sports coaches are overall great. Just watch out for the girls basketball coach, he doesnt let you play multiple sports. (or at least he doesnt want you to)Theis school will prepare you very well for college! It is quite a textbook high school, which is great. However, it still stands out. Overall, this school is a circus. For the academically focused students there are a lot of opportunities and great teachers. The average student floats through with inflated grades (look at the number of "honor grads") while the administration pays lip service to helping the struggling students, but there are no programs to actually help them in any meaningful way or get them experience toward anything useful after they leave high school. There are few rules, no consequences and subsequently the student body as a whole has little respect for the building. Walk the halls after lunch and you'll get an idea. Students and staff that come from other schools as well as foreign exchange students are shocked at the things that are allowed to happen here on a daily basis. I and many other former staff members are glad to have left and work at a "real" school again where all students have opportunities, not just the college bound, and there is structure and discipline in place. The students have fun while they're here, but are they actually learning? The West Linn-Wilsonville School District has an 'open library' plan in which a library without walls sits at the center of every school. Study areas with lots of computers radiate off the library at WLHS and classrooms surround each of those study areas on three sides. It's a relaxing, sensible plan with no long scary halls to traverse. It seems like the openness of the building affects the staff here, as I find the teachers, students and administrators at WLHS to be very open, friendly, and enthusiastic. The principal, Lou Bailey, communicates with parents regularly via emailed newsletters and teachers respond promptly to emailed messages from parents. My kids go in early or stay late for help from teachers, whenever they feel the need, so I can tell that the teachers make themselves available. Bottom line: I like Wlhs, I've had my kids in a total of nine schools in four states over many years and I know a good school when I see one. As far as test scores, AP classes, etc. just check the web site. West Linn High has been a wonderful experience for my 9th grader. We relocated from Washington and chose this area for the schools and he is doing exceptional! Kudos to all involved at this school My son has grown so much at this school. He is excited to learn and has been encouraged to branch out and try learning in different ways, which I really appreciate, as that is a life skill. We love the sports and music programs. The kids are really supported here in all areas, not just academic. I appreciate all of the extra college prep offered too. We will miss the strong sense of community and overall feeling of everyone being treated as 'family' here. I highly recommend sending your children to West Linn High. AP course and math course teachers are great! However, it seems lower grade English teacher needs to practice teaching differentiation in the classroom to earn more respect from high achievement student. Every student is different. Teacher should spent some time to create positive relationship with different students instead of just email the parents they have "bad" children. We moved to West Linn specifically because of the West Linn/Wilsonville school district. We moved here from Washington state and relied on our realtor to point us to the area where the best schools would be found, our main home purchase priority. Our overall experience has been positive for our children within all 3 levels of education. We are now retiring and moving on but we will sincerely miss West Linn. It presented a sound, beautiful and safe environment for our children to mature. We made the right decison in moving here 20+ years ago. I am a former student with a disability. I agree with many others on their handling of students with disabilities. I too fell through the cracks of their system. After starting strong my freshman/sophomore year, I started to decline and dropped out within the first few months of my senior year. While not entirely the schools fault (I had illness, surgery and mental health issues) I don't feel like I received adequate support or that anyone in the school even truly cared if I graduated or not. That being said, I think there were positives to this school. Bottom line though; If you are rich, white and you plan on going to a four year university straight out of HS (which is probably over 85% of the population), you'll do fine at this school... Great high school in a great school district. Kids are challenged and get a great education. Many opportunities to join sports teams/clubs. Counselors are super helpful and knowledgeable about college planning. My daughter did great at WLHS! Interesting teachers, challenged academically and had great friends. We picked our home base on this school and really made the right choice. My daughter was very well prepared for college. I also love that my daughter got to participate in several HS sports and activities. WLHS was great at accepting all interested students in their programs.

column1: We don't have metal detectors. Everyone knows everyone else. Graduating class of less than 20. We are parents of an 8th grader. The facilities are bad, but temporary, as a beautiful new school is being built. The principal is great, some staff very good, some less (a bit busy minding their lunches, conversations, etc...). The counselors are very helpful. 7th grade teachers could use some discipline in assigning homework, giving feedback to students and parents, but overall our child had a good year and improved academically (tested independently to see if really an A student). Always felt safe and comfortable. Parents involvement and a good principal are making a huge difference for both students and teachers, and we look forward to the new year, with a new wave of great kids from local public school. For whatever reason, the cafeteria seems to consistently fail the students. Every Thursday for the past year, the cafeteria does not make enough food which leaves students without a meal and hungry. Despite the fact that the attendance department informs the cafeteria how many students need a lunch to avoid this exact problem. The whole point of the school providing a meal for students is to get them through the rest of the day and they can't even seem to do that. For many students, this could be the only reliable meal of the day. This is totally unacceptable and whatever underlying issue is causing this problem it needs to be resolved for the well-being of the students.

I am disgusted that it took me calling lawyers to get them to acknowledge what happened. I purchased my home because of the reviews of Maryvale and its diversity and I have not been disappointed.

column1: I believe this school as come a long way under the leadership of Mr. Daniel Hamada. He has changed the dynamics of the school for good. Student drop out rate has reached a all time low. Great job. The school faired much better under Gilmore Youn's leadership. Because of the new addition to admin, some great teachers left the school, which was very unfortunate. :( As a parent of a relatively recent graduate, I was surprised to come upon this rating while on a real estate website. One should wonder how an elementary school with such a poor rating (3) — and having taught there I don’t disagree — could possibly lead to a 96% HS grad rate. Unfortunately, the admin finds a way to graduate all kids at Kapa’a HS as long as they basically show up most of the time. The best thing about the high school is the division of freshmen students into different tracks based on their interests & ambitions following high school: auto mechanics, culinary, college prep, and so on. Which reminds me, the school ended its honors program after my child graduated because why would you want to put any resources into the brightest students when you’re too busy trying to figure out how to graduate all students and dealing with behavioral problems. Another reminder: those poor teachers. All the struggles with cell phones and dress codes. Some just give up trying to teach; they say do whatever you want during the next hour & here’s your homework due tomorrow. Underpaid teachers and counselors, overworked, working in Third World conditions. I just don’t know how you expect anyone to focus in a 90 degree classroom. That school begins end of July, during the hottest & most humid months in Hawai’i — it’s abuse. They close schools in NYC for much less. A broken air conditioner in a public building in California? The building will be closed when it reaches 80+ degrees. Yet here we are still in 2022. Buy your own fans. Thinking private schools in Hawai’i are much better? Think twice.

column3: Deep Creek is a good school but we need more funding for repairs and materials. In my math class last year we weren't even issued calculators because the school didn't have enough and this year the calcutlators we were given were falling apart and barely worked. The school is old and severely needs to be remodeled as well; bathrooms that are disgusting with broken toilets and desks that are basically rocking chairs. In addition the school is overcrowded it takes oil most all of my lunch time to even get my food. Overall the teachers are great and I learn a lot every day it's a small community and everyone knows everyone but things NEED to change. This school really helped my nephew! !! He was so far behind From his old school and they help get him caughtGod up. Now he will be grad with the rest of his class .. Thank God. .. This school is great. The faculty and staff are always willing to help with anything. I like how the small size allows all the teachers and students to feel like one large family. Our school's sports teams haven't been the best lately but, our school spirit is still here. I would recommend this school to anybody. Guidance counselors are awesome. There are a variety of after school clubs. The schools provide tutoring, SOL help. It's also smaller than some of the other Chesapeake high schools. I am hoping my daughter has a positive learning experience here. Drop Creek High School is a great school! We have 2 kids that graduated from here. Great experience for both! Our 3rd kid is a student currently at Deep Creek. We don’t have any issues with the school and call it a hidden gem. Get involved with the school & you find the teachers & Admin care.

column1: We have two children at Liberty North H.S . The teachers and staff did good for the 1st year of being open. Hoping next year to be even better. Excellent schools. Fair teachers who really care about ALL students. Students are more accepting than we have found at other schools. Very pleased. This is a school that strives for excellence and gives us all the tools to do nothing but excellence. I am the first freshman class to ever be at Liberty North and I could not be any more honored to go to North. It is definitely the place to be. Our son has attended Liberty North HS for a year now. We moved from out of State. What a wonderful school, students, teachers and Staff are all very welcoming. This is a beautiful school, wonderful facilities, they are having growing pains, with the addition of Freshman at the HS. But it seems like all are adjusting very well. 9 out of 10. Great school! Love it here

column3: Comstock Schools is a great district. Small enough that you can get to know the teachers and administrators on a first name basis, but large enought to offer kids a wide variety of AP courses and electives. Older well built school buildings that are in the process of being updated. Property taxes are the lowest in the county. I had two children graduate from Comstock. Both went to college after and are very successful, in part from the great experience we had in this school system. My oldest has moved back into the community and her oldest is now enrolled in Comstock, hoping to continue a great tradition. There are some teachers that attempt to do something to help the youth, but students are often forgotten by other teachers and not valued. There is little to know diversity that is appreciated, and students as well as teachers only look out for themselves. I have heard of horrible behavior issues that are never addressed appropriately, and apparently it is ok to condone cursing and immoral talk. Terrible place to send your kids! I wanna go home and it’s 29 degrees outside and it’s packed with snow ! That’s so unsafe ! The roads are Icey!!!

column1: My daughter is a Sophmore at AHS. We love it, the teachers are really great and are very concerned about their students academic welfare. Would highly recommend the school!! Our daughter transferred has a senior and her grades have never been better, we love the academic campus atmosphere and the college bound approach to her curriculum, having lunch outside also gives the students the freedom to take a break and accept responsibility with those privileges, great school we all love it! Staff has always shown accountability and genuine interest in them doing well! Our daughter is a sophomore at Arlington and we could not be happier. The teachers that we have encountered seemed genuinely interested in her studies. The teachers do an outstanding job of keeping her attention and she seems to truly enjoy learning from them. we would highly recommend Arlington High School to anyone who is considering. I recently transferred to AHS from a small religious school, here is my "new student" experience: The students are mostly white upper-middle class, there is a strong "preppy" social group, as well a good-size band group and a decent-size "church kid" group. AHS is very racially segregated: the African-American students sit in one corner of the lunch room and the white kids sit everywhere else. Racial slurs and inappropriate language are VERY common. A segment of the student population is heavily involved in the school, but a majority couldn't care less about AHS. Academically, I would highly recommend taking mostly honors and AP classes. Standard classes generally have the bad teachers and students who don't care. Because the school curves GPAs, taking honors/AP classes shouldn't hurt your GPA if you put in effort. My experience with the guidance department was a poor one. The counselor did not spend much time with me and I was placed in mostly standard classes even when I asked for honors (the promise to move me up if I did well in standard was never fulfilled). All in all, AHS is a good school, but make sure to take upper-level classes and get involved in a club/sport/etc! Guidance department is TERRIBLE! No personal concern or help for your students! Student committed suicide and Board will not consider exhaustion from early start time or overload from AP classes as factor affecting mental health of students! School administration dictates outcome for Spec. Ed and 504 evaluations. School routinely fails to follow proper procedures at expense of students. Awesome school!! Great academics outstanding teachers. I can't say anything negative

column3: Headed in the right direction. We thought about moving to another district or doing private school but changed our mind and we are glad we stayed. PV has made huge strides in the past few years with changes in administration and curriculum. Now with the laptop program for all HS students (the only one in PA) plus the new physical education center and gym there is no where to go but up. Numbers of those who move on to higher education are low but misleading. Our sd is located in a large agricultural area, so many students pursue other options or do mission work before college. I graduated from PV and know a current teacher and guidance counselor personally. They care about the students and really want kids to suceed. There are the usual disadvantages of going to a small school (weak sports programs at times, everybody knows everybody) but there are advantages as well (sense of community, everybody knows everybody!) My experience as a parent of 2 children who graduated from Pequea Valley school district after attending all 13 years was great. Many things have happened since the earlier reviews on here from years ago, and Pequea Valley school district has improved thanks to upgrades in technology, flexible learning and our one-to-one laptop program for all students in 5-12th grade. This levels the playing field for all kids, regardless of economic background. The administration is truly passionate about creating a great learning environment to prepare students for life after high school, whether it be at college or joining the workforce. Disgraceful at best, for parents and students who desire to learn and excel stay away. I’ve never seen such a lack of teachers who take their job seriously instead of just a paycheck. PV school district is all talk and appearance and fails the students in the classroom. Teachers use purchased online curriculum and "packets" rather than teaching, the coursework is routine busywork and not engaging, and the students are not prepared when they enter college. The administration is much more concerned with telling everyone about the laptops and the sports program than any actual education on the part of the students. The high school English, science, and math departments are pathetic. The ag program is excellent, as is the music program. The district receives almost twice the state funding for the students due to so many Amish, Mennonite, and homeschoolers in the area, and they still cannot do an adequate job. Their issues are not lack of funds or high poverty rates in the district, as they like to blame everything, but rather a lack of leadership and motivation on the part of the teachers. The district talks constantly about the high poverty rate in the student body, but then lowers the curriculum and expectations rather than giving those kids what they need to rise beyond their current circumstances. All staff pick favorites among the students and ignore the others, and the favorites are the athletes and the children of the school board. Trying to deal with this district has been many years of frustration and disappointment. Our children are thriving academically and vocationally despite the limitations of this district as we had to go around, above, and beyond to equip our children with the skills that they needed for college and life - even "teaching" English at home with book list and writing to correct what was lacking from the school. Bullying is very much alive in PV and is ignored by the administration even after bones are broken on the playground. I can't say enough about how disappointed and disgusted we have been with this district. I had quite a few issues with Pequea while I attended. The curriculum is ridiculously easy, and the teachers absolutely baby people. Didn’t turn in an assignment due a month ago? Turn it in now for full credit. Not to mention the classes were so mindless that I did not study once yet had an A- average. Bullying runs rampant at Pequea. The teachers will watch it happen. The popular students, who are typically the perpetrators, are praised by teachers and never punished, even when they are caught doing things. If you are not a straight, fit, attractive person, people will come for your neck. This is probably an issue in every highschool in America though. At my time in Pequea, it was not very cliquey considering the school was so small. You were either in, out, or trying to be in. I fell into the ladder. The biggest issue I have with this school is the terrible guidance department and college readiness. The guidance team does nothing to help you pick an area of study and almost act as if you are a nuisance to them by going to see them. I was never helped in choosing a college major. They make you do an online survey to see what jobs 15 year old you would fit in to and that’s about it. Extracurriculars are abysmal. You can choose from sports, yearbook, art club, FFA, FBLA and maybe a few niche ones they decide to try out for a year. All in all, if you plan on going into the work force after graduating, this school is for you. If you plan on getting a secondary education, AVOID.

column1: This is a descent school unless you have a disabled child. They are ill equipped to deal with any physical or emotional handicap. Of course some go out of their way to at least try to help. Overall though they are truly clueless. I just wanted to commend all the students, teachers and everyone....on an amazing job on the haunted trail. My entire family was extremely impressed with this project and very, very scared. One of our group lost her cell phone on the trail, and one of the supervisors there went out of her way and found it. What hard work !!! You should all be very proud!!! mark harriman

column3: Our daughter is a Sophmore at Belleville West and what I love most of all is the teachers. The teachers are reasonable with homework and their expectations of students is right on. The support offered to our daughter has been wonderful and communication is great. The online gradebook is a great way to see what is going on and the availablility for the teachers to upload video lessions for the students is great learning tool. Great school and great teachers! Academic classes offered and sports programs are great. bus service is good and on time, many lunch choices, and nice library. Four years at West and we highly recommend it! Belleville West, where do I start? The academics are simply amazing and even though these are high schoolers, the staff still cares and communicates with parents! (I’ve been to schools where they didn’t). The extra curricular activities they offer are in abundance and truly something for everyone ! They offer so many sports and activities and clubs to keep our young adults busy and help build their portfolio for college. This year they’re opening a vocational campus and working with employers to offer trades and skills training for those kids that prefer this option. I love how they support involvement and are communicative on social media as well. Counselors will work with them to ensure they have the best graduation plan. Not to mention the campus is absolutely BEAUTIFUL!!! We have two high schoolers her and another attending next year! We absolutely love B West and highly recommend !!!

column1: Take this as true advice from a current student. Jones should be an absolute fallback school. I turned down opportunities to attend extremely prestigious school for Jones. Coming to Jones was a complete mistake. I should have done more research on the school. The school environment is not ideal, and I feel completely out of place. The academics are a joke. The teachers are extremely lenient and do not push/challenge students whatsoever. Staff caters to the underachieving, and cannot discipline their classes. We are supposed to be one of the best high schools in the state, yet everyone attends mediocre colleges. Please considers all other options before Jones. I am a freshmen at Jones and I am in love with the school. The teachers and students are friendly, yet competetitive a bit. The Prinicipal is very encouraging and hands on. I am greatful to be part of this prestigious high school. This comment is in response to the student review of May 24, 2011. I am also a freshman at Jones and it is an incredible place which offers a wonderful high school experience. Based on my grades in elementary school and scores on the ISATS I could have definitely gotten into at least Whitney Young but choose Jones as #1 since I had shadowed here and looked at all aspects of their academics. It is difficult to hate its "easy academics" when they have the same math program as Northside Prep, so if you are really that bored of school then you should be in math3 which is plenty of a push/challenge for me. Teachers at Jones don't have any problem controlling their classes BECAUSE they are lenient and earn the respect of students. By the way, that's the first time I've seen someone complain about not being punished. However, you were correct in saying that teachers cater to confused students which is one of the best aspects of this school! No matter what your problem is the teachers will make themselves available at virtually any time to help you prepare. They never leave anyone behind because we don't have a six floor building to accompany the 10 people getting straight A's. Jones College Prep however does not really make students prepare to College. To me, it is like high school without any college prep method. Many students on other schools got accepted to top college and recieve scholarship when they take IB courses. For example, I heard that students @ (Curie Metro High School) has a high graduation percentage and got accepted to TOP universities when they take IB courses. So jones is not the only one that got accepted to good college however. review June 23 2011 - Do you go to or even have a child that attends Jones? parent of a junior at Jones - this school has been the perfect fit for us. The classes are challenging and the teachers go out of their way to help kids. The teachers, led by an excellent principal inspire excellence and genuinely care about all students. We are very hopeful about the next step, our college opportunities, and feel well prepared. Location - fabulous, downtown commute and proximity to lake, parks, library, museums and water tower all play into the student lifestyle. We were very fortunate to have this opportunity. I certainly hope the new building changes things. While going through the CPS process of getting into one of the top high schools during 8th grade, the whole family picked Jones as their first choice. However, I am a disappointed parent. Whether it is the lack of clubs and sports teams, or the urban setting, Jones is missing is the rah-rah attitude for the school. kids don't hang out. They go to class and leave. My son is a sophmore and there has been minimal "College Days", so I am not seeing my son getting prepared for college. The homework load seems to be very light. He has always been an honor roll student throughout grammar school but is getting B's, C's and now D's, and it is not due to the material being too difficult. It is lack of interest and no action by the school. I have engaged the counseling department at Jones but no plan has been put in place to help my son. He has a twin brother who attends a different college prep, who has school loyalty and many, many friends. The number of friends does not determine the quality of the school, but he seems to be having a normal high school experience compared to his brother at Jones. I am disappointed, to say the least. a nice high school with a multicultural environment.this building is state of the art.to sub and teach at jones is very hard because the kindness of the kids teachers never take off.very smart and advanced students at this school. Jones College Prep is the first CPS school to win the US Dept of Education's Blue Ribbon Award twice. The class of 2013 (200 students) were offered $33MM in college scholarships, and the most recent average ACT score was 26.5. The school is the most ethnically and economically diverse Selective Enrollment school in Chicago, and this year's freshman class hails from 169 different elementary schools and 63 zip codes. Located in the educational and culture corridor of the South Loop neighborhood, a new pre-law and pre-engineering CTE program is being offered this year. The new Perkins+Will LEED certified building will open to the students on Aug 26 after 10+ years in the planning, and its inspiring interior includes a gymnasium, auditorium/theatre, indoor pool, dance/wrestling studio, library, and giant atrium, all of which are available to the public on a rental basis. Dr. P Joseph Powers and his staff are phenomenal, and the teaching staff is unparalleled. Not only is the education experience superior, but the feeling of community among the students/faculty/parents is unique in a high school setting. Jones College Prep is truly a treasured jewel in the city of Chicago. In response to the Dec. 18th post, I say this: I am a freshman, class of 2017. Jones is great, I have adjusted well and have people I can consider my friends. The homework seems light, thanks to the Academic Lab at the end of the day. Jones has countless clubs and many sports teams, your son clearly isn't taking advantage of them. Jones is very laid back, and I feel very loyal to my school, Jones doesn't boast. The new building is clean and pristine, and there is loyalty and respect among all of the Classes. No complaints here, but your son clearly isn't trying, as there are six sport teams every season and countless clubs have flyers out. Don't like what you see in a club? Make your own with permission! Countless options are available. I am currently a freshman at Jones, class of 2017. I have to say that the school is not very rigorous and as competitive as other selective enrollment high schools. If you want to go to Jones, then it is really up to you whether you want to succeed and work with what you got when going to Jones. Yes, the school is welcoming and the teachers are willing to help. The teachers do give a load of homework based on the classes I am currently taking, so it takes me a good 3-4 hours completing my homework. The new building is great and the sport teams are all pretty good. For freshman year, I joined the Tennis team and got on varsity and we didn't do as well as we were capable of, but next year is going to be a big difference than freshman year! I am starting to really like the school, but I think the school needs to improve on rigor in academics even if most students do well based on their grades and exams. l am a parent who is aspiring to get my child admitted into Jones College Prep High School. From information gathered so far and little interaction with School Administration, this is a multicultural, accommodating,student-centered and an excellent academic performing School l would recommend to any parent. I am a parent of a senior graduating in June 2014. My son feels Jones College Prep gave him more than he expected. He played two sports all four years, maintained a high gpa, scored high in the ACT and actually enjoyed his high school experience. The teachers kept his interest and the counselors were very helpful. Mr. Powers was a hands on principal. The location was great and my son felt safe and secure at this school. I highly recommend Jones College Prep as it prepared my son to get into the college he chose. He also gained more diverse friends and a more well-rounded experience. I had two sons to attend Jones College Prep. One graduated in 2013 and the other in 2014. They both enjoyed the challenge the curriculum provided which prepared them for college. They are both on the Deans List and enjoying their college experience. Jones is an excellent multi-cultural school in a great safe location. I would definitely recommend the school to anyone. The principal and teachers are one of a kind. So far we have had a great experience with Jones College Prep. If your kid can get admitted to this school go for it. I am very satisfied with my experience at this school. This is an average public high school. The block schedule limits the number of electives severely. There are less STEM classes overall. The administration shares fundraising letters but precious little other info. Its been a disappointment. My daughter loves Jones and the great teachers and staff. The block schedule prepares students well for college life. Jones enjoys top tier college and university acceptances. We are thrilled with an educational experience that clearly rivals the top private schools. Jones also has an infinite number of clubs and activities. My daughter is thriving at Jones! I’ll admit, when she told me she wanted to go there when she was in 7th grade, I was highly skeptical. I wanted her to pursue admission at Walter Payton or Whitney Young because what I remembered about Jones was that it was more of a vocational school rather than college prep. My memory served correct, however, my daughter had done research to the contrary and was determined to go. She was accepted and is doing extremely well. She was mostly attracted to the school’s diversity and ultimately its top college/university acceptance rate. Although they are undergoing some issues with the administration, these students will overcome and go on to be leaders in their communities.

I wouldnt send my kid to this school if the school paid me 4 years of living h+++ I went to this fine school. I like it alot, becausethe teaches there are very kind. Hammonton high school is a school where students enjoy there last 4 years of high school. Outstanding ,very good teachers and outstanding facilities ! Both my children graduated from here , very satisfied! I'm 37 years old...I also went to Hammonton high school. Now, my daughters is in this school and my 8 year old is in the Elementary school. In all honesty, my kids love their schools and that says a lot coming from a 16 yr old. High school is a hard time for a kid and Hammonton has always been different in that sense. A great sense of community, and sure...pride. And that shows through in our children, parents, community and teachers. It has nothing to do with thinking we are the best but it does say something when people from other towns want their children coming here. And just because you have one bad experience with one person, it isn't a reflection on this school, its students or the faculty. Its even worse if no one says anything because the school faculty, ie principals, want to know about these things. I'm a parent and former student, current resident. I've had my moments with some teachers but problems don't get rectified unless you speak. And any issue I've ever had with my children or teachers, have always been heard and managed. Never pushed aside. -Christina D. Very good, the teachers are very knowledgable and helpful I loved my 4 years at Hammonton! Hopefully I will send my children there!! The administration in this school is flat out incompetent! We have been in this school system for many years and hind sight is 20/20. Should have run when we had the chance. They care more about sports above all. It is entirely who you know in this school district and if you have the right last name, you are golden. If we had it all to do over again, we would have never moved to Hammonton mainly because of the school system. You absolutely do not get what you pay for in taxes. I don't know how the administration sleeps at night! Students whose parents are employed by the school are given preferential treatment. They force testing down the kids throats! Most of the students in high school cannot read or write in cursive. They make a big production out of their anti-bullying program, yet when a child is actually bullied, nothing is done. This school district is a disgrace! It's a pity I couldn't give less than one star! Good technology with an often friendly student body with some really good teachers

column1: St. Paul's school offers good educational opportunities and good teachers; however, they have a long term problem with bullying that makes it hard for outsiders and newcomers to fit in.
