column3: First of all, the building is not an attractive space and both the exterior and interior need a major overhaul. The school seems to tend to the needs of two groups; the problematic student and the top 10% academic achievers. If you float in the middle, you will receive very little support to grow academically. Mediocrity seems to flourish here. It appears PVMHS s motto is, do your homework, behave, and graduate . I understand that PVMHS is a large institution but there has to be a way to encourage students to reach past their academic goals. PVMHS is not just just some high school. its historical and has amazing athletis and academics. GO TANNERS! amazing. no other school I recommend. teachers have changed. for the best I should say. best music program. outstanding academics as well. I am a current student and I can honestly say there is no where I would rather go than PHS! AMAZING!!! Best place! I love it here. PHS has everything a high schooler could need and want. a large diverse group here at PVMHS , makes everything so much more AMAZING! staff management is terrible with overly strict rules.

column1: As a student that just graduated from La Cueva, I am very glad that I was able to attend La Cueva for all four years, and then have the honor of placing in the top ten overall in my graduating class. I joined the band my freshman year, and I can say that you will make more friends from extracurriculars than from any other source. La Cueva may have its public relations problems, but as a whole, the student body does not participate in those nefarious activities. My experience with teachers varied, from having awful biology and chemistry teachers, but once you enter the AP-level classes, I never found a teacher that wasn't excellent. Also, it is worth taking summer P.E., Health, New Mexico History, Government, and Economics so that you may open up three more elective credits, which would aid you in gaining the foreign language experience many colleges now want. I feel that I am more than prepared for college, and that I may credit my teachers for helping to prepare me to attend a rigorous, out-of-state university. I am a graduate of LCHS and a very proud alumni. Having now worked in other schools within the state I see that La Cueva deserves the recognition for excellence that it has earned. While at La Cueva, I was treated with respect by teachers, given many opportunities academically and extra curriculum wise that I see no where else in the state. I see several comments regarding politics, elitism, and the like and that is in every school in every city. La Cueva deserves the title of best in the state. The test scores are far above 99% of the schools in NM and the graduation rate is the second highest in the state as well. The fine arts department is first rate as is the athletic department. La Cueva wins more awards for music, athletics, science, math, etc than any other school in NM. You will not find a better high school in NM. I attended La Cueva HS and actually had to transfer. Many of the kids are just rich inconsiderate jerks and the teachers are very disrespectful to the students. This is a school where sports come first and academics come second. I felt very unsafe at this school and have seen countless kids being taken out of the school on stretchers because they passed out from over dosing on drugs. A truly awful school. Send your kids to Sandia or El Dorado. I graduated a couple years ago from this school. Overall, it is an average school.There will always be good and bad teachers as well as good and bad students. The athletic departments always receive the bulk of funding, and I feel the fine arts should be better funded. I was in band and art classes. For band, we did our own funding, such as the craft fairs we held. I guess that helped develop humility in a sense. And our band program was stellar. We were outstanding during marching season, and state champs during concert season. Our art program wasn't too shabby either. Several students won awards for their work. I myself won $50 for a painting I did. Yet in my last years in painting classes, our teacher could barely afford paper towels (which believe me, we needed a lot of those). I'm not saying that atheletics shouldn't be funded, I'm just hoping that someday the fine arts department will get the share of the funding they deserve. La Cueva has some great teachers but the few that are bad are really bad and not much you can do about it except take a WF (withdrawal fail-even if student is passing) and have the student take it somewhere else. On another note, it seems like approximately 50% of the students at LC are transfer students. This school is very cheap. $30 for art class mandatory. Their agendas are like calenders not enough room to write anything. Have to buy p.e. clothes. All the teachers complain about the lack of money this school won't help teachers with. This school isn't as great as it seems. Just awful. Kids and parents are entitled. They berate teachers and call them names and administration does nothing to support teachers. Very impressed with the teachers overall and glad we made the switch this past year. The reviews that say LCHS is an elitist, unhealthy place overall are true. Kids are rude and feel they are better than staff and teachers and treat them and the building accordingly. Administration believes that LCHS is the best and has no behavior problems, unless it affects them directly, and so don't take care of things right away or ignore them. Teachers are blamed for problems, even though they have little control. Administration will make wide ranging decisions that make their lives easier but teaching harder. There is little money and lots of broken equipment and dirty floors. Kids sabotage the school, throwing trash in rafters, etc. Kids will thoughtlessly break and waste supplies in classrooms that were difficult for teachers to get or bought by the teachers. Kids are openly disrespectful swearing at teachers and other students in the hallways. Students rarely offer help to teachers. There are a few really good students who do their work, are helpful, and really try. They usually get ignored due to teachers having to deal with the obnoxious ones. Parents overall are horrible too. They are the ones who raised their kids to be these entitled little blighters. Bullying is rampant. Kids use the word "snitch" in their jargon too -I hear it daily - and know the school culture supports more bullying if they tell.On the safety side, COVID guidelines are not followed well and administration response has been weak. Even scarier is the security at the school: The school is large without many way to get out (everything is interior at this school), has a scary student climate, and very little security which is rarely visible. The school has several entrances and exits which are often open and not monitored. I feel something bad could happen here any time. This school is the worst school i have ever encountered, dont ever come to this school thinking the admin will help in any way. Bullying is such a big problem here and the bullies are protected. I did some job training at this school, & it was a cut-throat political culture in the dept I trained in. I didn’t correctly pick up on the temperaments of certain staff and ruffled feathers unbeknownst to me. Basically, morale is low there and it’s sad that this school is what’s considered the best ABQ had to offer.

column3: My freshman is enthusiastic about her French teacher and cross country coach. Overall, she has been made to feel welcome by her teachers and encouraged by the rigors of the curriculum. The counselors and teachers were very accomodating in helping to make any class changes. Great school, great envirement, and just great people at Valencia so it's really easy to fit in and meet new people. My child is having a very disappointing experience at VHS, after a great elementary and jr. high school. There have been a few good teachers, but some are mediocre and a few are downright bullies. Overall, they do not seem to care about the success of individual students. They do, however, care a great deal about the success of their sports teams. valencia high school is quite youngschool (open in 1994) it does not have 2nd level building. it's pretty decent the students are alright and kind. during my freshmen year, there are many kids trying to welcome me. I have treacher collins syndrome ;i have mild face deformities and overall the kids are pretty welcoming. the older kids are nice and if you smile at them they would give you butter melting smile. If you try to talk to the students they won't reject you just act confident even though you're not. don't look depress, they can sense it and they are happy people, they look forward to meet fellow happy people. there are no such thing as cool or not cool as long you talk and get involved they don't care if you're short, black, asian, skinny or ugly, they see your personality. Every school has their ups and downs. I am a black student who is in their third year at this school. People always like to comment on things they have no clue about. My shool is taking action by the law because what happened was not right, but just because the video went viral does not mean these boys should be punished anymore than other students that have been in this situation before but it did not go viral. I love my school. It use to be very racist now it is diverse and a good place to learn. I recommend people focus on the school as a whole and not by the ONE fight that really never happens at Valencia Great school. Some students have gone on to Princeton, Yale, UPenn, Georgetown and many of the UCs. This school has gone down hill over the past year or so as it is now way too crowded with all the Castaic area kids coming over, enrollment is way to high, classroom size is out of control. It is projected to only get worse next year. My kid is just a number, if your kid needs extra help in one of their classes good luck getting it! Valencia High School has so much potential to be a great school. As there's really no perfect school. Some schools have great leadership, amazing students, wonderful teachers, great programs...but unfortunately all 4 elements are never combined..either one or two points missed. This school is pretty nice. Sports are very well done at this school and highly recomended. Very safe and beautiful area. The teachers at this school are wonderful and so is the education. Although the students who attend this school are very closed to new people. If you are new and coming to this school friends are very hard to make. Other than that teachers are very caring, grading can be a little tough depending on teachers but this school is pretty nice. This school is all about the rich kids and the kids who are high achieving in either athletics or academics. If your child is middle of the road or an underachiever they're treated like they're nothing. No one cares about them. Lack of academic support for students. I have had 2 students in this school and have found that the career/academic counseling support for students is failing. There is no response or engagement from some of the counselors. Recently, I tried to contact my student's assigned counselor and have received no response. I have been waiting for 10 days. I emailed the counselor and waited 7 days with no response. Called the counselor, left a voicemail, and still waiting after 3 days for a response. I visited in person and was told the counselor is really busy ... doing what you ask?... Apparently she is focusing on working with the sports teams. You have the parent's attention who is trying to get assistance and you ignore the parent. There is no empathy, support, pro-active or re-active engagement for academic counseling assistance. This school is not student-focused or student-centered at all. Student success is not the number one priority here, instead the Principal seems to enable and turn a blind eye to outrageous bad behavior that does not serve students. They could benefit from learning more about the dangers of a fixed mindset.

column1: My son started attending this school last year. He came from a small private school so I was really nervous about him fitting in. He is so happy & has made so many friends. Teachers and staff are great! I am very thankful that he is here.

column3: Mount Vernon is an excellent school with excellent faculty. Very responsive to parents and truly dedicated to their students. My children had all been through elementary and middle school in private school, my oldest two through private high school. I am so much happier at Mount Vernon than I was with my oldest two boys private high school. Truly a team approach to education! Can't say enough about how truly pleased I am! Not a great school. I have two kids in this school, I have a freshman at this school and his teacher don't seem to care about him. His failing 2 classes, and he said Soar time doesn't seem to work because his teachers are failing half the class and all they do is busy work dong that time, and they don't even help him when he needs help. Graduation rates are low and not a good school. With the exception of one awful biology teacher, I have been happy with my daughter's teachers at Mount Vernon. She is being challenged in most classes, although some teachers have a hard time getting the classes under control from disrespectful students. This has made the learning environment difficult for my freshman. With the exception of 1 or 2 teachers over the course of our 4 years and 2 of 6 kids at Mount Vernon High School (and any issues with a teacher have been promptly and courteously handled appropriately) we could not be happier with the teachers and the counselors. As other reviewers have stated-there is a sincere interest in the individual student and and a genuine warm and caring staff from the front office on. We could not be more pleased!! Great principal, some great teachers, a lot of good teachers. Potential for friction with so much diversity but the administration handles it well. Let's try this again. We have only been at Mount Vernon for a year. My daughter came from a very small school and we were concerned about the size. My daughter also has a 504 education plan, another concern: would it be adhered to, would she fall through the cracks, would she fit it? I am THRILLED to report that we have had nothing but positive response and assistance in helping our child succeed through this transition, and she is thriving. We love the diverse population and the students and staff seem to be happy! Cannot say enough about this school (positive). Yes, there is a diverse student population, I enjoy that, as do my kids! Students, faculty and staff are very friendly and it's very cool to see the different students interacting. There is a top notch ROTC program, great sport programs, drama/other extra curricular activities, good parental involvement, and so far the teachers have been top notch!! I'm particularly impressed with the leadership and guidance departments, and how they truly support the teachers, students, and parents! For such a large student body, so many cultures and personalities (in the students and staff) it's certainly a fantastic school. mount vernon high is making a valliant effort to meet the needs of all students in the face of gross misconduct by several students. The principal is amenable and works to deal with situations to the best of his ability. So far this school has been very welcoming and helpful. We are military and new to the East Coast, so it was very important to us that the school be military firendly and understaning to transitioning students.We are looking forward to the new year! Mount Vernon continues to be a great school, having great athletic and extra curricular activities, but most of all GREAT teachers. We are thrilled to have our last of 5 entering this year! CRAZEH, 5 Stars Man. Very Diverse and stylish ways of teaching, Exellent IB program as well. My daughter is a freshman in High School. she never failed a class till she step foot in Mount Vernon High School. Her teacher is always giving her a hard time. the Principal leadership is failing. she needs to hire better teachers. As a military family with many years in DODEA schools where I served on the school board for many years, we are very disappointed in MTVHS. We thought MTVHS would be the right school for our child because of it's smaller size, other schools in F/FX County are huge. We were very wrong. This school is light years behind DODEA in every aspect. The sports program is bad, the arts program is poor...the musical program is a joke. Their IB Program is minimal in comparison to others. The admin seems to be clueless to the problems in the school, too. It is very diverse, which we like in a school, but the student social levels are very much a problem. The pep rallies and the basketball and football games are more like unto prison break outs with screaming out of control unattended rude students everywhere. School spirit does not mean vulgar rude behavior at such events. I have never seen a member of the admin try to control the students at these events and I attended every football game at MT After looking at all of the parent,s reviews I have seen many low ratings. Before you make up your mind that Mount Vernon is a bad school, consider what you are about to read. All if not most of the reviews are by parents. PARENTS AREN'T THE ONES GOING TO SCHOOL. I am a student , a real freshman student and Mount Vernon is the best school I have ever been to. I now go to a school with a 5 star rating because of parents liking the school, although students don't like it very much. Since I have left my confidence has dropped, significantly. MVHS is probably the worst school in Fairfax County. For one thing, most of the teachers either don't care if a student understands something or not, hate MVHS as much as the students do, or are just plain rude. Students get in trouble for silly reasons. The counselors are barely there. When they are, they are always busy. The dress code is ridiculous, the principal walks around every morning searching for people with something on that she doesn't like. Ex) ripped jeans. It could be the tiniest hole, and they send them to AIA. They don't allow leggings, but do allow yoga pants. They are basically the same thing, some yoga pants girls wear are even more inappropriate than leggings. These students have to miss a whole day because of something "distracting" even though the student will be sitting for 90% of the day, for no one to pay attention to. But they allow students to wear full on costumes to school for no reason which is way more distracting than leggings, ripped jeans, a skirt, or shorts. Most girls want uniforms, instead of being embarrassed by a lady shouting out "DRESS CODE!" in the middle of the cafeteria, and grabbing a ruler to measure your skirt in front of everyone. We have a freshman at Mt Vernon, were hesitant at first because of bad reviews, comments about the school. We are glad we decided to stay. Our child came from a Catholic middle school and feels very safe and happy in the new environment. The Principal seems to have the student's best interest on mind, has seniority, commands respect, and is very involved. Teachers, counselors, coaches and others have been very accessible and responsive. Students have a lot of extracurricular activities to choose from, including great athletics. All kids, no matter their race, ethnicity or socioeconomic status are encouraged to succeed. GREAT SCHOOL! I am about to graduate in June..... I can tell you that I never liked this school. Freshman year I had a bad biology who missed so many days, and end up failing me for the year.... Sophomore year I had a mediocre geometry teacher who wasn't a good teacher and ended up failing that class, and our sols scores are joke. Since Freshman year they might of replaced half the math teachers, and English teachers. none of my English teachers I had Freshman, Sophomore years, junior year are there anymore. Now the principal removed 0s cause too many people where failing so now the lowest grade we can is a 53% Just a struggle to get teachers involved, and with one child with an IEP a struggle to get the school to not label him disabled and tell him he was disabled so he could graduate with a standard diploma. This was not their agenda not their plan and it was a yearly fight for the school to keep him on track to graduate with his class. with my daughter she just needs lots of encouragement and she did not get that and it was the same fight to get the teachers on board to help her succeed. My daughter, unfortunately, only attended Mt. Vernon for her 9th grade year. We moved before her 10th grade year. We loved everything about Mt. Vernon. She was involved in sports and had wonderful experiences, especially with softball. Her teachers were great. Of course, like with any school she liked some teachers better than others but we were happy with all. The administrative staff was also wonderful. We really can't complain at all about the school. We all wish we could have stayed for her whole 4 years. I'm utterly shocked that MVHS is rated as a 1. I graduated from MVHS a few years ago and now I'm an engineer. I can attribute my success to the staff at MV and semi-dedicated parents. Although I didn't see the point of going full IB, I did take multiple advanced classes that helped me critically think, explore and improve my community, and effectively communicate with others.The academics were challenging, yet interesting. IB Anthropology, IB German (level 5), Anatomy (A&P) and Stats were my favorite classes. For freshman biology, I had to conduct a year long environmental scan of a local lake, do experiments, and write a 10 pg paper on my analysis. The teacher intended this to be 'hands off' so the student could learn how to problem solve, critically think and have long-term thinking. I hated that assignment but looking back, I see how beneficial it was. Excellent, My kids had a wonderful experience here. The students respects each other, and as for educations my kids were well prepared for college and were able to get into top notch schools . My daughter is in med school right now. Our child spent her K-through-8th grade years at catholic school. Initially, we were very hesitant to enroll our child at Mount Vernon High School. Thank goodness we took a chance on this school. The school's leadership is solid, the teachers are available to assist their students outside the classroom, and the students' behavior overall is of good character. We have found that the parents who have never had a child attend Mount Vernon, are the very individuals spreading negative and false information about the school. We, without hesitation, recommend considering this high school over private school; the education is equal if not better. Go Majors! Absolutely poor. If you are new to the area, leave Fairfax county. Excellent! We are so pleased with our daughter's experience that we purchased a home in this pyramid so her siblings can also benefit from this diverse and supportive school It seems like a normal school. everyone gets along. the kids do well. They have AP as an option. I cant say anything bad about it. My daughter liked the school, and she got into the college she wanted. she has a good handle on whats going on in the world. The school set her up for success. I like the school for my kid. some parents complain about too much school work and some complain that the teachers are upset when the kids don't do their work. I have to say the school hasn't given my kid anything they cant handle. It is a large school. There are a lot of different students with different backgrounds. I think it adds to the appeal. Our kids are mixed and they seem to do just fine. There are some kids who's parents come from different countries that have trouble with the work, because English isn't their first language. my kid liked to help them out. he also got to learn a language that wasn't common. I thought the opportunity to pick up another language was good. Also my kid helping out others was a bonus. Really diverse school that advocates for inclusion and for all students of all backgrounds. There is a club/activity for all students ranging from the arts to Championship winning teams.

column1: The staff and Administration are wonderful! They strive to help and lead the young people that attend Carolina. Carolina has one of the nicest facilities in the GCSD, it is clean and well cared for. The school has a bad reputation because of its location...what a shame! Carolina is indeed a hidden jewel! Things do happen, as they do at the wealthier schools in GCSD, but over all this is a great school with great students, teachers, and administration!

column3: I am so pleased with the growth that my child has achieved since he transfered to this school. This is a very chaotic school which the public knows little about. Students eat in class and take cell phone calls in class. The walkways each period find students walking during class and they are rarely questioned as to where they should be. Last year during Market Day, students put together a t-shirt with a pro-drug message, there were no consequences, and were allowed to take part in this event. Ask the school what percentage of those who enroll in an AP course actually sit for the AP exam. Last year there was a large fight during lunch which looked like a small riot. Another good question would be to ask the teachers which if any administrators do they think actually have leadership abilities. There is no discipline, students are very poorly behaved, class size is ltoo large for the school to be effective. This is a very, very poor school. If you are serious about your child getting a good education, do not send them to this school. We've been happy with the academic and overall life experiences at Arcadia. The school gives freshman the whole campus the first half-day of school. Faculty and staff return emails promptly. Students have a nice mix of backgrounds. Honors and AP classes are open to those wanting to try. Many extracurricular opportunities for each student to express and learn in their way. Good parental support, but it'd be nice if more came to parent-related meetings. Some, like a previous reviewer, would prefer more control. We think Arcadia prepares kids to succeed in the real world. As always, it's difficult to accurately compare with other schools because we haven't moved from school-to-school. Arcadia is for us. It's a better option than other Phoenix schools and coming from another state I am realizing how far behind even the "best" schools are. G&T here is average student in other states. There is a refusal to believe that Arizona is behind 95% of the nation in education and the PTO is run by stay at home moms who don't have a clue what the real world is like. They celebrate medicrity instead of encourage success. We have been very happy with Arcadia High School. My child attended a private school from K-8, so I was originally nervous about the transition. However, the transition couldn't have been more smooth and we have been impressed with the teachers and staff. Our child is challenged in honors classes and is very happy at Arcadia. We have zero complaints. I think it's a great school, I was more impressed with the curriculum they have for the students and the safe campus. My son really enjoys the school and the environment. I go to Arcadia and i found that it is very lacking in respect for the teachers as well as the students. Freshman are harassed by some of the teachers and students, but this is passed off as just messing around. Some teachers are just amazing and are able to create a classroom that is a home away from home, a place where the students feel safe. This school is a place for kids who are quite social and kind of lax on the idea of getting into a good college. I am not saying that about all of the students but most just talk about things that are not worth typing up in this review. If you want to truly challenge your kid in terms of science and math don't go to Arcadia, however if your kid is interested in filming and such they should got Arcadia. I am the mom of 3 children who attended Arcadia High School; 2 are now in college, one is still there. This is a school that embraces teaching the whole person, and offer students great academics with AP and dual enrollment classes in every academic subject, the opporutunity to participate in clubs and sports including 3 no-cut sports, and access to a wide variety of unique and high caliber CTE and fine arts offerings. My older children both were admitted to their top choice colleges early decision, one with a merit scholarship. All 3 of my children were able to play a varsity sport, take all college prep classes, and even create their own independent study curriculum in art. Every teacher goes beyond classroom teaching to support student growth, and there is an active, devoted parent organization that raises funds to support the classroom and coordinates volunteers all over campus. But you should decide for yourself. Arcadia offers weekly tours to prosepctive students and their parents, and to community members who want to see what a great school looks like. Just call the front office to make your appointment. 3 of my kids attend this school. My fourth will in two years. The new leadership by Mr. Slater has transformed the school over the past couple years. My three kids are excelling academically and socially. The assistant principals are very in tune to the students needs. Mr. Moony (the assistant principal) is extremely responsive to any issues that ever arise including bullying or substance abuse. There is a fantastic open communication policy at this school between parents and administration. The campus is very inviting with a large open lawn surrounded by classroom buildings. There are dozens of clubs and activities as well as excellent sport programs. Finally, the school is large enough to not have any cliques dominating the social scene. Kids are either from the immediate neighborhood or open enroll. Most of my kids friends open enroll and are appreciative of this policy as they recognize this as an exclellent educational venue. We live in Arcadia and had several options for high school including two top private schools. Arcadia turned out to be an excellent choice and exceeded my expectations. I haven't gone there yet, but both my aunt and uncle go there right now, they love it! They made friends that weren't from their previous school, and isn't complaining about anything, I am currently an 8th grader, and want to go to arcadia, but my parents kind of want me to go to Xavier, bleh, 7 hours of homework every single night!!! Moved here from Texas where my daughter was one of 283 nationwide students admitted to one of the top high schools in America. Culture shock on how far behind we are and how we are failing our children. She was issued books in 9th grade she had received in 5th grade. Arcadia was a clannish run high school with little interest in her well-being. Male students were acknowledged for achievements far less than hers (she received $80K in scholarship money for example). They pretended they were succeeding at bullying because they weren't looking for it and didn't see it. Meaningless signs and gestures don't cure the problem. Even worse? One of her teachers dressed like a professional streetwalker with half her body hanging out of her clothes and constantly bullied and belittled my child with no meaningful criticism. In all academic years she was National Honor Society and is so again in college but this teacher deliberately kept her out of NHS in high school with no academic reason ... it could be because my daughter was a published author in junior high school and this teacher still struggles with any sort of recognition for her work. She suffered from anxiety disorder and the school was well aware of that yet deliberatel chose to suddenly misspell her name on her diploma and mispronounce her name (the only student whose name was mispronounced) and could have cared less how it made her feel and claims they suddenly after years of spelling it right were going by the birth certificate which they were not. Their interpretation of the birth certificate was wrong. When we take egos and politics out of school maybe I will feel less that those who an do and those who can't ... but this school totally failed my child. It is scary how this school appears so perfect in writing but when you look at that great school ratings score of 5, it is so disappointing. If I were a parent moving here from out of state, the reviews vs the scores would make me confused. Veritas is rated a 10 and its is just a mile away, what could they be offering so different where their teachers make significantly less and the curriculum is of a liberal arts mind. Discipline and the art of actually thinking with content dive? Something is wrong in the Scottsdale school district and while parents are praising the almighty Titan, I think we should collectively figure out the eroding issue. The schools that have the best ratings within this district, are also schools that have active parent participation as well as a financial demographic that exceeds the median income in this state. But what about their schools where the majority is a minority or ESL children? With those variables in consideration this number looks different and this reflects Arcadia high school when one looks at the true scores. Why has this high school not been able to maintain its rating of 9 over the past decade? If a school cannot reach its most challenging demographic, there is something internally corrupting these variables. It is not challenging to educate my child, the upper class caucasian student whose parents are college educated; but what about the child that has no access to tutors, internet, additional support, and in some cases even transportation? So should we cease open enrollment to get the numbers where they should be? It might be warranted so that a true accurate picture could be displayed to the family that erroneously sees this school as an academic powerhouse, but we would not want to eliminate diversity in this school even though this population might be currently used as props. Whatever the opinion, there is something eroding with this great schools score and something that should be fixed sooner than later. Hopefully the new superintendent figures it out. This school is an A+ in my book. The Arcadia name is known by many colleges as a great school and one that prepares students for future academics and careers.

column1: I am a current student at notre dame, quality teachers are few and far between, the athletic program highlights football while it is our weakest sport, and belittles other more advanced sports teams we have, the administration is a sham, the worst part of this school is the slapped on "technology advancements" our buildings are falling apart AC is near non-existent, and we insist on forcing our students into paying 600 dollars on an iPad that is completely wasteful. while there are a few teachers that are stellar it is heavily outweighed by the poor teachings skills of others, if you are strapped for cash dont budget this school by its tuition, allow for massive fees such as "technology fees" (on top of ipads), mandatory fundraiser donations(dont even understand how its a fundraising at that point) and other such fees that will decimate your checkbook. you have been warned When I enrolled my child into this school the sky was the limit with the promises of a great education in a Catholic based school. We were so excited to have her attend. I am sad to say that every year this school has become more and more money driven. They focus on their image but do not focus on what's important , the kids. Bottom line, the kids run the school. The popular kids get away with being bully's, there is a scary level of drug use. The teachers are so busy trying to be cool or just don't care and the upper management are so busy fundraising that the kids are left to their own devises! My child got absolutely no help with college prep and the school does not communicate with the church so my son missed out on important events because they clashed with church obligations! This is a catholic based college prep school so they say, I would expect for those bases to be cover at least! I am very happy to be done with this school, my son has 2 more years of high school but we will not be wasting them here at ND. I rate this as an A++ school based on the experience from my family and siblings that have gone to this school. I have one more child to go to HS and will be going to ND. I had two children graduate from Notre Dame High School in Riverside, CA. Through all of their years at the school there was so much support given in both the religious and academic aspects that they were well prepared for college and life. Everyone at the school has always been so kind, caring and puts the needs of the students first. Needless to say both children have graduated college and have happy and successful lives. We have our two boys at Notre Dame high School ,one is about to graduate and we are so bless to be able to bring them in this school. Teachers are consistent on follow up or updates on how our kids are doing in school esp. when they are slacking off and as working parents that is very helpful for us. The school staff really prepares the students for college since it is a college prep which is a good foundation for them in future and most appealing for us is the catholic faith which the school greatly emphasizes to students. Having our kids in this school make us feel we are there guiding them in their future and molding them to be closer to GOD so they can be better person as they grow. We pray that this school will keep its excellent service to students and their Catholic values. Greatly appreciate you all Notre Dame Staff! The last 3 1/2 years have been great after they remove the principal without exclamation and created it and stable environment the school has definitely lost the Carrows him compassion and drive to move forward Ever since they change leadership at the top the school has gone by the wayside. Was a phenomenal school, now a mere skeleton of what was and could have continued to be. Use to be a school with high integrity and support.Now being run by the "mean girls" club! Unfortunately the SB Diocese has turned a blind eye to what is going on! Not a good scene for it to be a catholic school! For shame! I came here specifically to comment on the current situation at the school I find a lot of the recent comments highly misleading. The fact is there were 2 significant security situations last year that were not handled well and communication with parents was awful. There have been questionable decisions made with respect to funds spent. Why build half a football field? Additionally there were severe problems in the basketball program that were unaddressed for many years, despite multiple meetings with the principal, that caused more than a few students to leave the school. I find this campaign of trashing the school for making a change disgraceful. It seems to me the school has been in a bit of a rut and I think, at least so far this year, things are changing for the better I am a former student and a current parent. I, like the 8/24/19 parent, came here to address the recent smear campaign. I find it unfortunate that the so-called friends & family of ND are bashing the very school they purport to love. If they want to effect change, they are doing it the wrong way. Some of these parents currently have students attending. If things are so bad, then WHY keep them at the school? My son has received an excellent education, he was challenged, pushed outside of his "box" and learned things about himself that I don't believe he would have at any other school. His mentor was amazing (she retired this year) and he did things I never imagined he'd try. I look forward to seeing his continued success at ND. Notre Dame faculty & staff have done an outstanding job keeping the students learning & engaged during the Distant Learning program.

column3: I am a parent. My husband and I attended Murphy High School and our four sons have, as well. They were all AP students. We chose not to participate in the IB program because we wanted a better rounded high school experience. The oldest three received scholarships and have completed their college degrees and the third is on a full scholarship (32 on ACT). I must caution incoming students, however, about the lack of concern the counselors and AP teachers have for getting their students the college credits they are promised. Our youngest took English as dual enrollment. When he got to college he was told the school did not enroll him in the first semester of the course. So, the college did not give him credit for that until he was enrolled the second semester. Therefore, he was not given credit for the second semester (ENG 102) and we now have to pay the expense of that course. Instead of taking responsibility for errors, the counselor and teacher have passed the buck back and forth and even went so far as to blame the college where the students were to be enrolled. Disappointing. Now I can't get the teacher, counselor, principal, or board member for the school to respond. We took our son out of our district just to attend the IB program here. It was the worst thing we ever did to him. No need to bore you with details. Let me just summarize by saying this school is not a school but a big juvenile detention center, and the IB program is basically a pathetic attempt at beautification. The administration is so overwhelmed that they cannot be bothered with the needs of students who are NOT getting into trouble. There are a few good teachers, but not enough to make it worthwhile. Don't waste a single day of your child's youth, as we had. Avoid this school at all costs. Fantastic School, The panther pride and sense of family among the students and faculty are like no other school experience. My family has been a part of this school since the days of Barton Academy and now I am a teacher with 2 students who attend this school. As a parent, former student and now a teacher, I wouldn't send my children anywhere else!!!! I have been apart of the AP and IB experience, and I can say that the programs truly prepare your child for the real world and the college experience. The diversity of students...Asian, Russian, Indian, White/Black as well as income differences...its a small world with unique experiences which unite and bond everyone together. Murphy could be a great school with better leadership. The principal and counselors will not respond to calls or emails from parents. They have several great AP teachers that put alot of time in with their students. Unfortunately, the administration does not support them in disciplining the students and maintaining a good learning environment. There are way too many fights. The diversity of the students is an asset and will help students later in life. Murphy has a beautiful campas dispite the tornado repairs that are taking an extreme amount of time. If you are looking for scholarship money for college, you are on your own. The students get little or no guidance in this area. Outstanding! My grandchild just finished his Freshman year!!! The art and theater program are amazing. Musical chorus and band are the highest rated in the state! While this school offers some great opportunities such as Early College through the University of Alabama, IB programs, and AP programs it also has a lot of environmental factors to combat. The classes are overcrowded, the students who need special learning modifications aren’t receiving them, and the teachers are not sufficiently supported. This year there is a new principal who seems to be more active in implementing consequences for bad behavior. There are fights every week, it is situated in an area where most households are below poverty levels and there isn’t much support at home. The students enrolled in the advanced classes will graduate equipped to face adulthood, those in standard classes will not fail because the county superintendent doesn’t allow failures. Unfortunately this is turning out high school graduates who can’t function well in society.

column1: This school has achieved so much for being in such a small town! The school s performance score of 140.8 a nearly 20-point improvement over the prior year has it labeled an A+ school and ranked as the top nonselective public school in the state, according to Louisiana Department of Education rankings. It is awesome how truly dedicated the teachers of Erath High are in their work with their students! They don't give up until their students excel! Some of the programs implemented at Erath like mandatory tutoring either after school or during lunch for failing students and daily in-school tutoring, called intervention, that targets students who are falling behind in a course. Schools all over the state are getting ideas from Erath High School of how to help their students succeed! The parent and community involvement at this school is a main cause to the school's success! The administration knows how to make school fun and a place their students want to be. I only had one of my children attend this school. He didn't have a good experience. He witnessed teachers talking down to students (you're not going to do anything good with your life). He tried to help a teacher by saying that she was on the wrong page and he got fussed at saying, "don't correct an adult". He was suspended for 2 days for slamming his books on the desk. The previous day I got a letter saying that he was missing quality educational time by being tardy (but being suspending wouldn't affect that?) The front desk would never greet me when I approached the desk. I find as being a newcomer to Erath they treat you like an outsider. If you weren't born and raised here then you don't belong (I've been told this by others also.) I never meet friendly, helpful people. Please read this if you are considering enrolling at EHS. This school proudly boasts it is the number one high school in the state yet no google search can back up these claims. (I’m still looking into the validity of them myself). As of January 2020 the school’s majority of classrooms take place in old portal buildings that are falling apart and not kept up. I have had two classes (facs1 this year & ag1 last year) with mice in closets. The school does not pay their cafeteria employees enough to enjoy a fair lifestyle thus they quit early and students eat the bare minimum of food in brown bag lunches due to a short staff. Some students will not eat at all because of bad experiences of students with lunch debts getting to eat and others with debts who are turned away. The classes are often not what you believe they are when you sign up for them, for example I wanted to learn how to cook so I signed up for foods and nutrition but a week ago I had to have a parent sign a permission slip to take a 6 week course in business instead. And when I had raised my concerns to school faculty they would not make time to hear anything I had to say. This is not the first time this has happened. The faculty does not seem to care about students. There are only a small handful of teachers I’ve had since freshman year that I’m thankful to have met. The school itself is primarily white with few other races. The school focuses the majority of its attention on catering to the football team and severely limits the budgets for other sports which is a real shame. The faculty certainly picks favorites only caring about the best and brightest students and not considering anyone else’s claims to be valid or worth time to listen to. It takes bringing in a parent for the principal to take anything you say seriously. Growing up in Erath I’m very disappointed to see the decline of EHS. Please read this if you even think about sending your child to Erath. I'm currently going to this school, and as for someone who has had relatives who go there, and has asked them or their opinion on this too, this school is not worth it. The teachers, more often than not, don't care about what you (as a student) or what your child has to say. To be frank, there is only maybe about two or three teachers who actually treat their students with respect, and care about their opinion. I have often experienced the teacher's angry personalities, in which, most seem to have a superiority complex. They commonly yell to you, or your child if they need help, and a lot don't even try to assist if extra help is needed. Not to mention, that not specifically this school, but this whole parish has a problem of oversexualizing girls with the limited dress code that the girls have on the days they can wear free dress. Another problem, that still goes unnoticed by most is the bullying. Here at this school, it seems like if you move, and join this school late, you are an outcast. You can tell a teacher about any of the bullying, and if that teacher does not tell the principle, then the problem seems to go unnoticed. Along with the bad bullying problem, a lot of the boys, mostly found in football, are known to be EXTREMLY homophobic, transphobic, and racist. This is a major problem for the black community and the LGBT community. Lastly i would like to acknowledge the overall look, and schedule of the school. First, there is only a 30-minute lunch. With the number of kids that are in that school, and the short lunch time, most kids have to eat in their classes. This does not give them much of a break, like lunch time is supposed to do. This can cause a lot of stress for the kids attending the school. This, for a school, or any place, is not acceptable

column3: Coming to work here does not feel like work. The air here is full of friendliness and acceptance. Our school has something for everyone. Whether you are an academic, an athlete, a gamer, etc -- there is an organization waiting for you to join. In response to an earlier rating, there IS an organization that helps transfer students of all grades integrate into our school and that group is the Peer Facilitators. This group gives tours to new students, throws lunch parties for new students, and helps them become acquainted with the students and faculty. James River High is a nationally recognized Blue Ribbon School of Excellence and is highly recommended. This could be a great school, if your child is mainstream and learns "by the book" However, if your child has ADD or/and LD, they are very stingy with assistance. My daughter has ADD and math LD documented by professional psychologist. We were not granted an IEP, just the 504. The 504 makes the student accountable, which is great in theory but highly uncomfortable to the student. The IEP makes the SCHOOL accountable. And it appears, resources are saved for people who know how to work the system or bring in lawyers. On a positive note, my daughter did well in classes that were not math based. But she felt oppressed and judged and therefore did not embrace many opportunities or activities at James River. Very disappointed. She is very talented and I know will do great things in life, but no thanks to James River High School We have senior and sophomore sons at James River, both on college-bound tracks. We have found the teachers to be exceptional, striving within the constraints of SOLs and other regulations to provide creative, up-to-date and engaging educational opportunities. Our older son has a mental health condition that impacts his schoolwork and teachers have worked with him individually to help him learn. Our younger son is a self-starter and appreciates the organizational rigor of the curriculum and the just right mix of discipline and freedom afforded (the hour-long lunch for all especially). Both sons have played sports at JR and the coaches have been simply wonderful, committed and skilled. All that said, there are significant challenges. The guidance counselor has been entirely unhelpful in dealing with our older son's challenges, many of the students are from nearby high income households and behave like entitled snobs, and there is not much ethnic diversity. Like all Chesterfield high schools, classes start at 7:20 am, way too early for high school kids, in my book. Very impressive school. One of the area's Blue Ribbon Schools. A great advanced art program. Well organized athletics and a high level of parent participation. Highly recommend this school! Great student programs and academic offerings. Several events throughout the year to get community involved - sporting events, fun runs, plays, etc. Great curriculum and involved teachers. I always feel safe at the school and it's well run. Students seem happy. Great school with caring teachers, lots of extra curricular activities and a good sports program. James River is a fantastic high school. The quality of education is outstanding. It is an asset to the community. Well diversified and accommodates all levels are learning. Clubs, sports, music, something for everyone. My child is doing g very well with AP and honors classes. Jennifer Coleman is going to be a great principle. She is a caring administrator that cares deeply for James River HS and will be a great leader! This is a great school with a wide variety of offerings and a wonderful student population. It's a family-like community. The teachers and staff ho above and beyond for the kids James River High School is a wonderful school! We love to live near the school and attend the sporting events! Awesome staff and great education! Wonderful teachers and great school in a great community that is very involved in its students and schools Very bad school and incompetent administrators. Academics are subpar at best. Our experience has been so horrific we're not only moving from the district but the county entirely. I see it is currently 1 star over Richmond City Schools. That's pretty indicative of what's happening there. I'm not just one disgruntled parent. JRHS is a caring community of excellent teachers and staff . It's rating on this site does not do it justice. Did you know 2 summer 2012 Olympic athletes graduated from James River?! It houses an ESL center which contributes to its rich and diverse population. Unfortunately because The students are still learning English, their test scores are not very high and this affects the overall rating. Comparing the school to Midlothian high school based on this rating alone is like comparing apples to oranges . The population at James River is a refreshing slice of the real world. I taught at James River for seven years and loved it ! My daughter loved all her teachers and she excelled in all her classes. Has her PhD in Math now! My third child is now attending James River. I have two graduates - one at William and Mary and one at Virginia Tech. James River offers a strong curriculum with many AP courses. The teachers and administrators truly want the best for our kids. The community is wonderful. We bought our house in the James River district to attend this school. The JR Center for Leadership and International Relations attracts many students throughout the county. My two kids have gone to this school and had wonderful experiences with supportive and encouraging teachers. I have volunteered here on many occasions and the staff is a helpful and appreciative. Strong academic programs. James River provided a well-rounded social experience for our whole family. We found it to be a welcoming community after moving from out of state. My two older kids graduated and have excelled at college. My youngest is graduating in June. My kids took AP classes and honors everything. They were involved in sports, clubs, band and show choir. I was very involved within the school and on various boards and volunteered every year. I found the teachers very caring and strived to help students be successful. There is a something for everyone -as I told my kids, "You get out of school what you put into it! Work hard, play hard and strive to be your best! That is what is required for success!" I've worked with many volunteers for community service events from James River and every student I've encountered has been superior! Great enviorment and opportunities for students who want to take advantage of paths to a successful life Teachers are extremely dedicated! Incredibly lucky to have option to be part of a CREW team on the beautiful James River! JRHS was a great experience for all of my children. Great community of teachers, parents, staff, and students! Going into college after JRHS I was more prepared than many of my other school mates that attended other schools. The Staff have always been wonderful and welcoming! The location of the school to the James River has increased the number of families that want to move to this area. James River has dynamic, dedicated teachers who teach the curriculum with passion. The students get a diverse education especially when it comes to the sciences. It is a well run school with plenty of after school activities for the kids. I love the variety of educational experiences my student can have at JRHS! One teacher helped my student refine her passion for the future, another has recognized a talent that is not measured by academic testing and has given her the chance and the mentorship to foster and grow that talent. James River is an amazing school with devoted teachers and an incredible staff! We are lucky to have an education center located in the heart of the Robious Corridor that focuses on students and their community. Can't say enough great things about this school! All three of my children graduated from James River High School and I am proud to say they were well prepared for college and the working world. The teaching staff is caring and wonderful. My son loves his school. We had a foreign exchange student live with us for 6 months and he loved the school. They both felt safe and at home there. My son is academically challenged and is surrounded by other students who work just as hard. They create compassionate competition among themselves, driving each other to do better and celebrate each others successes. Top notch academic school, based on JRHS kids' experiences with grad years from 2005 thru 2019. Strong academics that successfully prepared my two children for college. Parent-teacher-student involvement is phenomenal. Athletic programs are competitive, are managed by committed teachers and prepare the students for college athletics. JR is a school of excellence and highly sought after by families from other counties seeking to be a part of the Leadership Program just to attend JR. Two of my children graduated from James River High School. It was a terrific experience and I felt they had an excellent education. It is a diverse school, with an ESL population which may be why test scores are lower. The rating is very unfair and does not reflect the quality of the school environment and culture . Excellent community school. They must have 50 different clubs kids can join and tons of sports activities. Academically they have a lot of AP classes and the Leadership specialty center is located here bringing some of the best students in the country. They have some lower overall test scores giving a rather poor greatschools rating because the school has some diversity. Not a bad thing either but the great schools rating is not an accurate reflection of this blue ribbon school (which also goes on the student diploma) Two children have graduated from this school, one in the leadership program and one in mostly all AP classes. This is a strong diverse school with great community involvement and even better teacher strength. Not to mention it is an esl school. My children are grown but my neighbors children have graduated from James River and loved it. Excellent teachers for the most part and willing to help when needed. Good variety of electives and opportunities for higher level classes. Sports programs and clubs are excellent. Blue ribbon high school. Great teachers. Great band. Prepared both my kids well for college. Prepped me well for college, great teachers and staff!! Fantastic facilities and beautiful location, Go Rapids!! I have found there to be an openness to dialogue, a willingness to include stakeholders in decision making, and high expectations for students, teachers, and parents. My son recently graduated and I have two other children there. My kids have thrived at JRHS. They have had teachers who have I spired and motivated. I have no reservations about my kids attending JRHS. There are tons of clubs and activities for all students to join. I have no doubts that my kids are well prepared for college and beyond. I am floored that this "non-profit" seems to have such a powerful effect on parent and homebuyer decisions when it fails to keep up with the latest information. The site seems to simply be a modern day version of redlining; maligning excellent schools with false and inaccurate data. So sad. We moved to a great neighborhood as we had heard James River High School was a great school. After 1 year here I can tell you it is the worst school we have ever attended. The teacher lack of care, time and involvement shows regardless of when they are "in person" or "virtual". I'm stunned that the student demographic doesn't match the neighborhood demographic, far from it. This is the worst experience we've ever had and it seems nobody cares, the Chesterfield School Board is the worst board we've ever experienced as well and have a total lack of representation of what the parents want. column1: This has been a really good school experience. The school has high expectations for its students. With any new program, it does have few kinks, but it has the right support to make the needed modifications for an excellent school. Positive parent involvement is the key to any successful school operation and Arabia Mountain has it. Students have many opportunities to display and fine tune their skills. talents and abilities. I highly recommend this school for a student and family that is serious about education. I attended AMHS for the 2 years that it has been open. I have had some very bad experiences there, I understand its a new school and I think that is one of the things that really bothered me about it. It was TOTALLY unorganized when it came activities for after school or something extra curricular. The teachers were good but you could tell they didnt enjoy working there because of the disorganization and the rude staff (administrators) I was in a carrer pathway class for healthcare without a teacher for a whole entire sememster! We learned nothing AT ALL! The staff was rude and didnt really want to be there either. The students did mainly WHATEVER they wanted and didnt really follow the rules. I think it would have been better if there was more involvment within the school (parents and others that sponsor the school are great) if there was more caring and me sincerity than it would be a great school...By the way I will not be attending that school next year. If your child is an average student this may not be the school for them as ALL classes are accelerated - whether past grades or test scores indicate they should be. Love the facility and uniform policy and the atmosphere that it created but the tons of homework, very late nights, and stress were not worth it. My child started there in 9th grade but we moved him to the home school after his first 10th grade semester - a semester too late. And we weren't the only one who withdrew. Looking at the eSis grades, it it obvious that a large percentage of the students (at least in my child's classes) were struggling. It's one thing to demand excellence from your students but that's hard to accomplish when you have a very high teacher turnover rate and a lot of the teachers are young and/or inexperienced. And they even admitted at a recent meeting that their tutorial sessions are not very effective. I'm sure Arabia will be a good school one day but we could not wait for that to happen. I love this school. I think that it opens up students for the real world and prepares them for college. The school offers all accelerated class but you have an option to take a general mathematics course. Also parental involvement is mandatory. I just graduated from this school this year and I must say that I had a great experience at this school. At first I didn't really like it because if the challenging work, but then as I got older I realized that the work was to prepare me for college and the workplace. If you want your child to be challenged then you should send them here. This school was excellent. I was a student there my 10th grade year and I played around. My grades slipped and I had to attend my home school. This school is not for the average and I plan on going back for my 12th grade year, ready to learn. Hi, Ms. Turner (Math teacher) This is my son's first year at AMHS and he is doing very well. There are some challenges within the school with organization and communication to the parents but things are getting better. The addition of a seasoned, no nonsense principal has improved student morale at the school. The academic program is challenging but I know my son will be prepared for college when he graduates from Arabia Mountain. My son had attended private Christian schools since 5th grade and I am glad he was able to get into Arabia as the requirements are high for admission to the school. Overall, my son and I are very happy with the school and its leadership as well as most of the teachers. this school is a very excellent, but there are a few problems. the administration talks down to you and acts as if we are criminals, all the classes are accelerated, teachers that teach accelerated classes are teaching AP instead, the work is very tedious and this school really has not been satisfactory for me. i recommend this school for kids who are magnet, gifted, or just a really hard worker. other than that i suggest you rethink where you want to send your children. There are so many safety nets for our students- late homework opportunities, retakes on tests, recovery tests, remediation plans with opportunities to make up zeros. But there are absolutely no incentives for teachers. Most of the teachers are worse than the students- they don't follow the rules and don't come to duty. Many teachers gave final exams early, teachers don't ever post grades, it just goes on and on. Administration is not supportive. There are teachers who do their job well and help the students succeed and they are completely overlooked by administration. There are no consequences either for those teachers who do nothing. There are even math teachers who aren't even certified teachers! No wonder the EOCT scores are horrible. Administrators need to crack down on the teachers and it would trickle down to the students. Get rid of the horrible teachers who don't do their job and the great teachers might stay. This is a great career preparation school that focuses on medicine, environmental and engineering. The involvement of the parents are amazing and the school is completely diverse with student from all over DeKalb county who are enrolled. There is always something for the students and parents to get involved in together building the family bond. I encourage anyone looking for a school to prepare their son or daughter for college and the real world to look at the benefits of attending Arabia Mountain High School. This is my daughter's 9th grade year and so far what I see is homework, homework and more homework with projects. My child is ending his 9th grade in a few weeks. My opinion about the school Is the accelerated courses are challenging. However, when you have teacher(s) practically abandon their responsibility to teach as a consequence your child's grades suffer. For ex. One paticular teacher went on leave and my child was given printed packets to complete daily and ovet 25 on line assessments to complete within 8 weeks plus several projects no feedback was given etc. Also, my child had to manage his other courses most with weekly projects. I am furious this happened administrators appear to be clueless when you If I feel like this a parent I think a parent center would provide better support. The priority of collaboration among teachet will allow them to bettet plan workload for studentd talk e them. On the othet hand the children are bright and have put on wonderful weekend events at the school ex: Ramboree carnaval and health fair. I'm not sure my child my be pushef out the school. Personally, being a student at Arabia Mountain High School, it is defiantly challenging especially since all classes are accelerated. It takes hard work and everyday we come home with Homework and Homework And More and Projects. It's very difficult but then that's when you have to set your mind straight because at the same time us students signed up for it meaning it's going to be challenging and we have to put an effort into it. Myself personally also struggled at the beginning of the first semester and it defiantly hard to bring grades up because extra credit isn't more then 5points or lower. So I would have to ask for pets say different worksheets, more homework. Some of the test are very hard to complete only if you study and I promise that's a 100% on your paper. Also just going to high school is very hard then having to go home and do your homework for all seven classes then study for test that's has to be taken the next day is honestly tiring and it's very hard. But then once again we signed up for it. So we must put in the effort and we have to put in the effort. So being a student personally at Arabia Mountain High School is tiring, all sweat and tears, but all Worth It. A majority of classes are accelerated, making it very difficult for an athlete to keep up. There are eight classes in a semester versus four classes at the area schools. Some of the teachers/staff are perceived to be professional and are very much the opposite. My daughter, an athlete would be finishing homework at 2-3am in order to keep up. The school will nickel and dime you for everything. My total cost for senior year, including, senior dues, senior trip, graduation stuff, senior pictures, sports fees & gear costs, prom fees, tests fees and college apps were approximately $2000+. I originally had two children who started at Arabia; however, my son was transferred back into the home school after his sophomore year. He is currently a straight A student and his self-esteem is no longer broken. Both of my children struggled with 9th grade Algebra of which no books were made available. The teacher was horrible. Lastly, my son has suggested that because of his light complexion, the male chemistry and biology teachers treated him and other male students differently. On a good note, parents care about their students education, the wardrobe is set and the students are focused. This is a public school which has a private school feel. The kids are always challenged to excel and they push each other. The administration and staff have a genuine concern for the kids an their future. I read a lot of the previous comments and it seems that those parents were looking for a mediocre school. Arabia Mountain is not that, they don't preach that and parents should not be expect mediocre. The school motto is RAMS.. Raising Academically Motivated Students. I have two daughters who attends, one is a junior and the other freshman. My Junior has a 4.1 GPA, and yes she does homework, but she is in bed by 11pm; rarely is it later than that. Plus she is involved with multiple clubs. I lived in South Dekalb County for 15 years and I know what little opportunties there are to find an academically challenging school so please don't trash the one or two we have. As a parent you know your child, you know if they are disciplined, academic students. If there are not than Arabia will probably not be the fit for him/her. So save yourself time and save your students GPA and enroll them into one of the lessor challenging high schools. You have plenty to choose from in South Dekalb so take your pick. But if they are academically motivated than I don't know a better school in the area and trust me I looked. But as a parent you have to be honest with your decision. Believe me, I have a son and he would not have enjoyed Arabia so he went to ......... and loved it, plus graduated on time. My son is graduating from Arabia Mountain next week and i could not be more proud than i am on his accomplishments. He is a student athlete and sometimes got a little lazy but we are a motivated family and worked through the challenges. My son has taken and passed 5 AP classes and will start college as a 2nd semester freshman. Arabia Mountain is as close as you can get to a private school without the high tuition. Parents, you know your child. If accelerated, challenging classes will create problems for your child, then do not consider this school. If, however, your child can handle the rigors of the coursework and wants to participate in extra curricular activities. I highly recommend Arabia Mountain. I have a senior who recently graduated with high honors and a soon to be 10th grader who finished the year with honors. Although the curriculum is rigorous the students take pride in their school. Teacher are hit or miss but the administration especially Dr. Swanson is awesome! If you're looking for a public school that gives you the private school vibe. Arabia Mountain High School is just that. Don't take it lightly being accepted into the school is a privilege, but is challenging yet rewarding! Extraordinary high school with excellent educators and the leadership is next to flawless. Arabia Mountain High is a school of excellence! My daughter has had a great experience at Arabia! She started in her freshman year & will graduate next year in 2019. My daughter is currently a freshman at Arabia Mountain High School. The course load is rigorous, and it took her about 2 months to really get acclimated to the amount of work she has on a daily basis. Using a daily planner has helped her tremendously in getting and staying organized, which is a MUST at Arabia Mountain. She has been able to maintain the A/B Honor Roll while being active in 2 sports, as well as the AFJROTC. The administration and teachers truly seem to care about the students' well-being, in and out of the classroom. And I have never seen a PTSA as active and involved as the one at AMHS. If you want your child to be successful in life, then Arabia Mountain High School is the place for him or her! My daughter overall is doing really well with her core classes. The work load is strenuous. I am pleased with the administration who genuinely seem to care about the students. The communication of the teachers is not the best. My daughter is taking an elective in which is required for her to take because it is the program she was accepted under. However, I have made several attempts to contact the teacher via text and email with no response. She is reading the messages and purposely not responding. It shows a lack of professionalism. Its a shame my daughter GPA has to suffer because I can not obtain any information from the teacher about her progress or what she needs to do to improve. If you are a parent with limited time to give to volunteer and evening activities this school may not be a good fit. They have no sympathy or understanding for single parents or parents who are working shift work. Weigh your options before applying This school is awesome and very welcoming. The staff is working everyday for the growth of the student inside and out.

I have had the most amazing experience at Lehi High School. Lehi has wonderful administration, students, and teachers. Lehi High School is an outstanding high school and I would highly recommend it.
