column3: We moved to Birdsboro three years ago and have had children in Birdsboro Elementary, D. B. Middle School, and D. B. High School. I never thought I could say this about any school, but the three schools my children have attended here have been a dream come true. The Daniel Boone School District is amazing. My elementary and high school age children both LOVE their schools. The teachers and staff are very caring, helpful, and enthusiastic. Even the office administrators are a joy to deal with. Parent-Teacher communication is wonderful. Education and special programs are excellent. The facilities are nice, clean, and mostly new. They have a great security program, including security locks on doors, and guards at the high school. The Daniel Boone schools have far exceeded our expectations, and we could not be happier. The school is just failing. There was a math class where 1/3 of the class had below a 2.0. What was being done about it? Nothing. The school claims somebody went into see the teacher "teach"...and the teacher was fine. Really? Grades are awful, kids are failing, nobody cares. Want a lot of study halls? This is the school to attend! Students have been known to have 6 study halls in 1 week! Really? You have choices...this should be low on the list. Great school? Not so much... I came from one of the most bad mouthed school district in Pennsylvania and it was a 100 times better than Boone. Some teachers are just way too harsh and don't bother to help. You're behind? That sucks. Find a way to catch up. Its not a good school at all. Can't wait to graduate to be honest. There are some good people in the staff, but not all of them are as great and perfect as they claim to be. And racism problems in 2013? You need to work on that...seriously. Boone does help out the community in a lot of stuff, but it needs to fix a lot of things. Sincerely, a senior of the class of 2014 DB is one of those schools that can go either way. If your child is a good student, who wants to do well, then they will thrive at DB. However, if your child doesn't care about school, or if they seem to get into a lot of trouble, that will only continue to be a problem. The school has tried to crack down, by instituting mesh or clear bookbags only, and having periodic searches, but the reality is that it really doesn't do much. During a search, the guards hardly even glanced inside of my bookbag before moving me along, and they did not even bother to check my sports bag. It would have been all too easy for me to sneak in banned substances or materials, something that is a problem at Boone. I see more and more people coming to school on drugs, and it disrupts the learning as we have to remain inside of our classrooms until the person is escorted out. The academics are alright, but a lot of self teaching is required. For me to get good grades, I often have to teach myself the subjects because the teachers don't really do their jobs very well. All in all, it's an alright school for the motivated student, but don't expect much. I have hope for the new superintendent to change things. I consider myself to be an intelligent person who has a desire for knowledge. I am taking three Honors classes, excluding Algebra II, of which I am at the Accelerated level (which I am "delighted" to tell you is to be eliminated, along with Conceptual and Honors classes that are available at the AP level). The Algebra II class I am enrolled in is a horror to me, and I am fully aware I am not the only one who feels this way. Until I discovered a tutor outside of school, I consistently received C's, D's, and even failed some quizzes and tests, all of that while going to after school tutoring with my teacher. Now, I have an A in the class. If that isn't proof of the inadequacy, I don't know what is. Now I will talk about the security guards (a reported $90,000 per year). These guards, although I was told there would be regular bag checks, do absolutely nothing to guard the security of this school. KIDS REGULARLY COME INTO SCHOOL HIGH, AND SOME GET HIGH WHILE IN THE BUILDING. Not to be derogatory, but a high percentage of them are old men. One even has a cane! How is that secure? This school needs to improve. I am not getting a quality education at Daniel Boone. The Daniel Boone Area High School isn't that different from other local schools. Overall, the education system in the United States is a joke in comparison to the rest of the world, however, this is a review of the Daniel Boone High School, not the excuse of an education system present in the United States. Teachers in Boone come as they do in any other school district. It is difficult to review teaching staff when they are held back (as are students) by the battery of standardized tests. Standardized tests include the Advanced Placement exams run by the College Board that follow a strict curriculum and fail to match college courses, the new Keystone benchmark testing (again, good intentions, but solves nothing), the SAT, ACT, and surely a few others taken by few students. There are multiple maintenence problems with the school, poor spending choices, outdated technologies, etc. Most of the problems faced in Daniel Boone are the same across the United States. COmpared to others, the school is average -- the school makes no attempts at freeing itself from the battery of nonsense and ancient, ineffective teaching, but yet shields itself from severe drug usage and crime. Gone to Daniel Boone since Kindergarten. Which used to be a great school all through Elementry school until middle school. Ever since 2011, the Daniel Boone school district has sucked. Terribly, in so many ways you wouldn't be able to talk about all of them. Starting off with the staff. You have some teachers who are amazing and go above and beyond the help you but the other 75% of their staff won't do a thing besides complain about you to other teachers. For example, Mrs. Derrick, Mrs. Reinhert, Mr. Jacobs, and a few others. The whole rest of the staff is just to be there to get paid. They don't care about the students grades, their future, and so forth. All they want to do is get through another year. To sum it up, the teachers do not reach the right standards that they should and do not teach the information that is students (and pass students) need. Administration, is a whole other topic. It's like they don't care about us anymore. Yes us students and parents might complain every once and awhile about something stupid but put up with it, u signed up for it. They tell us how important it is too pass out keystones but here they're not even teaching us students and from a parents side our kids the right things. It's said to see such a great school district just go into a ditch and each day it just goes down further. It's said when the school district can't afford cough drops or any medication becides Advil. Let alone tissues. Moral of the story, Daniel Boone School District is a very horrible place anymore. If I were moving in the area, I would direct you to Wyomissing School District. Great education you'll find there.Daniel Boone High School Student & Parent1/17/16 I think the negative reviews obviously haven't attended other high schools. Our family has recently attended and graduated two children from a "high ranked" Bucks county school to compare. Luckily our 3rd got to experience Daniel Boone for their last 2 years in school. It is hands down an amazing school with a super caring staff and friendly, high achieving students that participate in so many varied areas of interest from sports to making their own bio-fuel, and all do it with pride! The guidance counselor immediately guided my sports playing child towards Div I, II and III guidelines in picking classes, even though play in college wasn't a priority. Thank goodness she did as college sports are part of the equation. But besides that, you could tell she cared and did as needed throughout the college process in a timely manner. This NEVER happened for any of my 3 at the "top" rated Bucks County School district where we lived. Now, the greatness of DB didn't stop there or with this guidance counselor, just that was my first "wow" impression that comtinued for the next two years and DB's greatness and pride stick with me even after the youngest graduated. My child LOVED the much smaller school, friendly, know everyone atmosphere at DB so much that a very small college was this child's choice. This child had MANY educational gaps left from their old high school, ex: (and verified with other kids as I never just believe my own) Spanish I old school 50 verbs were taught (after 5 teachers in the year!) DB Spanish II students were to of gotten already 150-175 in Spanish I at DB, so a major gap. Major English gaps in fundamentals of the English language, as well as major math insufficiencies. My child didn't whine, got willing help where/when needed, struggled and was accepted at their first choice college, plays two sports in college, is now an RA as a soph, and ALL because of what they received at DB! As for other students, my child was a 3.0 kid, but paled in compartison to the other, mostly DB lifers (lucky kids!) and was ranked pretty low in the class ranking. As well, I've never seen so many kids going from one school to PSU main accepted into tough programs, as well as others going or accepted to many other top notch schools, multiple ivy leaguers, way more than much bigger, "high ranked" previous hs! Daniel Boone is great if you know the comparisons! My experience with faculty at Daniel Boone HS has been very well below what a parent should expect. I've called, emailed, left messages. Only to be ignored or dismissed by teachers and the assistant principal. My child is almost done with the DBSD. With zero assistance from the "district", my child is looking forward to attending the University of Delaware. I applaud my child for making the best of a bad situation. I've graduated from Boone, and I had an amazing time there, it's obvious that a majority of the teachers care deeply for their students.However, as much as I love it there, Boone did have a few problems. The principal of the high school, The Dark Knight, could really learn how to be more effective and put himself in the students' shoes. Secondly, many of the extracurricular events seemed to be put together a bit sloppily, although many were done very well.It is important to add, though, that the school also definitely has some sort of a heart to it- we're not the richest, nor do we get the best test grades, but Boone definitely taught me how to be a better person than any of the surrounding schools definitely could have. Anyone who gives DB a low rating has only seen the school at a glance, and doesn't know the beauty of it.Thanks for taking the time to read to this. This high school is not a great place for students of color. A good percentage of the student body use N word on a daily basis. Post racist views on their social media accounts and micro aggression is a constant issue. No help from the school staff. Absolutely no help from the head principal.

column1: If we're being honest, things could be better. There are a few teachers who legitimately care about the students' education, although they are rare. The students are very accepting, but as far as academics go, Community is very behind. With the right faculty, this school could be just as good as a 5A school. this school might be small and might not be very good in sports the best i have ever been to and ive been to six different schools in texas and this has been the best and every one here fun to be around OK, up until HS Community was 'passable' as a school system. HS is a whole different story. We have had no problems with the kids and the overall atmosphere of the school. Let me first say there are some teachers in the HS that truly do care and inspire. I know of one and I'll allow that there must be a few more. However, the majority of my personal experience with the faculty and staff has been horrible!! If you do happen to have an issue with a teacher don't expect support or even acknowledgement from the counselor, VP, or principal. They don't care. Period. The attitude of all but a handful of the adults at Community HS is not at all encouraging to the students. We even had one teacher when asked by a student how to bring his/her grade from an 88 to an A, reply 'this is an accelerated class, you're not expected to make an A so don't worry about it'. This is not the attitude of a teacher I want teaching my student. The school, in my opinion, actually discourages parent involvement. For the teachers that truly care and are trying, I commend you!! I wish I could call you by name here but I can't. The entire rest of the staff of the HS, forget it! They don't care. CISD has been a real challenge. Very racist school in a rural area. Teachers are the worst I've seen at any ISD we've had the kid's at. Almost switched districts to Wylie last year. But felt like we were showing the kids how you run from problems. So, we kept the kids there and with a new principal this year things had gotten better. Now it looks like some of the teachers are leaving next year. GOOD. Now let's work on the Superintendent. Stick it out, change what you can, and live true. I think for once school is headed in right direction. need more imphess on higher education, maybe getting better teachers or setting fire under them. Sports here is a joke no type of vision to play at next level. Ive been blessed to go community since kindergarten and all I can say is that I love it. I've grown up with most of the kids that were in kindergarten with me. We may be a small town school compared to most but you can never find a more caring and loving school. Some parents think that we aren't getting a good education well its not that our teachers aren't teaching us its the state of Texas requirements that they want us to know. Its hard. When it comes down to it. I wouldnt want to go to another school. We can all come together as a school but in reality were just a big family. People talk down about our athletic department but they work so hard and people don't realize it. Its always the people that talk just about what they hear not what they see or don't even go to Community. We are a hard working group of people and sometimes we just cant meet peoples to high expectations. We have put 3 kids through this school.. Great sports programs and really good teachers. Excellent school. All 3 of my children attended school here and all 3 graduated with honors and received scholarships. All schools have their bad and good apples, but I think it comes down to how engaged the student is, his/her willingness to learn and the parents involvement with their child's education at home. You cannot blame the entire school for a few bad teachers or if your child gets a bad grade. Over the years, we've only came across a few teachers who were not so great, but I believe they've all left or have been fired since the new superintendent has came along. I just hope this school stays the small community school we've known and not become one of these overcrowded schools like in other areas. My children were in small classes and got to know their teachers and fellow classmates so well that they are still friends with many of them even years after graduation. 10/10. The staff is very inclusive of new teachers, and each teaching subject is constantly searching for new ways to teach learning hindered students. This is a completely different campus than it was 5 years ago. The new superintendent has made some great, and needed changes, but the high school is in poor shape. My experience with all THREE of my daughters was horrible. There is not one good thing I can say about this school. They were bullied, the teachers, counselors and even the dean could care less. Its more political than what meets the eye. My children left this school damaged in more than one way. Its soo bad my last daughter went to live with her father so she could go to a new school. We looked at home schooling to paying to transfer as well.

column3: Woodside is amazing! It isn't just a school, its a place a grow and perform. There is so much diversity! I've never seen so many different children get along so well. And we had over 12% more than any other Newport News school in reaching our 3.0 G.P.A. quota. Woodside is the best school ever! I couldn't of ask for a better school! I have found it a struggle to get by at this school. I'm an army kid and I have been to a 3 other high schools and this one is the worst. I moved in the middle of the year and I felt alienated. My teachers did not get me up to date with what I needed to learn, leading to my failure in a class and low grades in others. And half the teachers are just not good at teaching. The student body I mainly made up of kids that really don't care. Some don't care about their grades, leading to classroom distraction, and others just do not care about their actions, leading to fights and conflict. I don't go a day were I am not nudged our of the way in the hall or given a dirty look by a random passerby. I was put into the drama program and the program is very good. The teachers are loving and supportive and most of the students in the drama department are great to be around. This is my third year at Woodside and I have to say it's been a interesting time here. I think coming in at the start of freshman year was very good because everyone was looking for new friends at the same time, so it was easy to find people to be friends with. I will say that this is the best school in the city, but if you are used to very good schools, the transition will be a little rough. I think the principal does a good job and it is possible to get a high quality education at this school if you will put in the effort, as with any school or college. It is a crowded school, but I've never had a class bigger than 30 students, and it is very uncommon to have a class that big. Overall it's a good school and I've been pleased with what I've seen so far. The school has zero parent involvement and the teachers do not care about the success of the student. My child is a junior here and has not had a teacher yet that has cared. And my child does not have any behavior issues and is an honor roll student. He is not challenged to be prepared for college or encouraged to. The teachers simply just want to score high on the SOLS and forget what is most important; the student. We just can't wait for his time at this school to be over because he his not happy there and neither are we. We can only hope that he gets into a decent college after graduation from the school. I really hate this school so far, I'm a freshman and I don't know a lot of people and a lot of things but I do know that this school is just crawling with bullies!!! A person can't even go a day without being picked on especially quiet people like me. Next year I'm hoping to be switching to another, I just can't deal with this anymore. This school is like the first school I've ever been bullied in my whole life time!!! Overall it's a good school, there were and still are so times when I get stressed over the work but it's ok because I can always count on my teachers for help. Also there are plenty of opportunities to get involved with the school.

column1: Exceptional -- Canton is basically a private school for public school children. Fabulous teachers and support for the kids. My children we well prepared for College and feel some of their college classes are more easily managed because of the learning in there courses at Canton High School. My children loved the inclusiveness of this school. Individual attention from teachers, and camaraderie among students! Both are excelling in college at private universities. Overall the school system is very good. It’s been my experience however that they fall short in taking care of special needs kids & the administration from the superintendent down through the principals & vice principals are very good at ignoring any emails or inquiries unless they need something from you.

column3: the so called "adult night high school" offers handouts to 17-19 year students as a way to pass time rather than actually give them a lesson! The night program also turns away many students upon arriving and sometimes does not mark them IN. Allowing absences to build until the motivated young adult goes away., nice program...guess it was a way for them to get $$. They once told a teen who was trying to enter the program that he was trespassing...yes TRESPASSING. Extremely disappointed parent... Yes you can apply even if you live in Jersey City. I live in Jersey City and my daughter was accepted there w/ a scholarship! If me and my son lives in Jersey City, New Jersey how does my son apply? Your child CANNOT go to school in Bayonne if you live in Jersey City. Since it's a public school and free, I also can't imagine what scholarship the prior poster is talking about. i like it. it is really great! i learn a lot in this school. this school help me a lot! I've been to so many different schools and this one truly is the best. Whoever is complaining about it will really know what I mean when they leave it. Currently a sophomore. I absolutely hate this school. Most of the teachers truly do care, but it's not enough. All the school cares about is the honors students. They offer no help to children who need it. Absolutely no money goes to their "special needs" program. I've had a friend with a very painful disease and they went through hell trying to kick her out and make life worse for her because they just didn't want to spend money. They also try to kick kids in resource for no reason to get money. I've been a straight A student until I moved to this city and went to this high school. It made me want to kill myself, the kids who go here are the rudest most ignorant people I've ever seen. And if you ever need any help, even an allergy, you will have to go through so much work just to SPEAK with someone. And then they "won't know how to help". Invest in a private school or your child's life will change for the worst. I don't even get to eat lunch. Even though I have health issues and medical support. Worst school ever. The staff and overall management of this school is alright. However, the culture of the general student population is egregious. (Good luck finding a student that could define that word in bayonne high school.) I'm a senior graduating with the class of 2016. I can offer a good perspective on this high school because my first and last year here is coming to an end. I transferred here in september. Something rather shocking I've noticed is the horrendous lack of respect between students and from students to teachers. Sex, drugs, and fighting are glorified by students. The students do not care about their education. The teachers are not flawless either and I don't blame them considering what they have to work with on a daily basis. Many teachers drop grades and pass students on. Also the passing grade here is a 65 which I find sub-par. I have also witnessed obnoxious and blatant disregard for simple rules in the school. For example, a teacher makes it clear that you cannot use your cellphone in class. This is an accepted rule across the majority of educational institutions in the country. However this rule is constantly broken. If a student were to be reading a book rather than have their face glued to a screen, they would be the odd one out of the bunch. Attendance and tardiness is also another large issue. Students are constantly late to class, absent, or cut and there are not many repercussions. I have also noticed a lack of professionalism by some teachers towards their students. Some teachers readily partake in gossip with students and do not discipline them when they should. Please do not send your children here and if you do, do everything in your power to stop them from confirming to the hideous culture of bayonne high school. You would think that this would spend like a fun place to be if you were 15,16,17,18 years old, however it is the epitome of how you wouldn't want your children to grow up. Look elsewhere for a high school education. Big class size.Wonderful athletics.Some teachers are wonderful - others seem indifferent.Great facilities for sports, theater.

column1: As its been stated before Nimitz is a school with a vast majority of students whom don't care about recieving an education. The teachers give you the basic knowledge you need to perform outstanding on Benchmark Exams. My suggestion is if you want to feel like your attending a good school try some AP courses which will change your outlook on things. Nimitz is HORRIBLE! Every day after breakfast there is trash everywhere. The teachers are horrible and hardly ever teach. The students dress like prostitutes and the administration say absolutely nothing at all. They don t care what you do especially if your parents come up to the school and get ghetto. There is a fight almost every day and it is just atrocious! I live in the Woodcreek neighborhood next to the school and from that you would think the school would be a nice school seeing as how the neighborhood is so nice and quiet a good suburban area then you go to the school and realize that it is the exact opposite. They have over 100 buses at the school because they bring students from all over and dump them at one school. I ve been told that Nimitz was amazing at one time until 2009 when it went downhill and unfortunately I am a part of that horrible class of 2013. A word of advice: DO NOT send your children there. Do not even take a second look at Aldine ISD because it will turn your sweet children into MONSTERS! It s sad but true. Find a new school, because the administration is just as bad if not worse than the students. I put one star but it should be none. I recently graduated from Nimitz High School as part of the Class of 2013. As a former student I have to say that the school shouldn't be blamed for its bad reputation. Though many parents might not want to here it, the fault lies with them and their out of control children. I was at the top of my class and had many of the faculty members help me through high school. I actually tried to do well and as a result, I start college at UT Austin in the fall. I can honestly say that without the encouragement from the teachers and counselors at Nimitz High School, I never would've made it through school. The school offers a lot of dual credit and there is a diverse campus of great teachers who work diligently, creatively, and compassionately at what they do. Students that take advantage of what is offered will go far in college and their career choices. The school needs to stop with the ridiculous collar shirt dress code; it's not a private school! It's a PUBLIC SCHOOL. The collar shirt dress code, does not put a stop to inappropriate attires of some girls. I see short dresses, crop tops, low cut tees on girls! WITHOUT COLLARS, but they still go a whole day without being put in "SAC". But honestly the whole dress code thing does not help improve grades, so why in force it to the school. Also, the staff who are "in charge" (I put quotation marks, because like I said I see many out of dress code students) need to be more focus on the outside of the school, during working school hours, because many students skip and go to LoneStar or outside in the forest; by the staff keeping the students in class instead of skipping to the outside, grades will most likeky improve. This campus has really turned around under the new direction and leadership of the administrative team over the past 4 years. The campus leadership is the reason that the school has gone from WORST to FIRST. Nimitz High School students and staff should be proud at the fact that Nimitz is the Highest ranking traditional high school in Aldine ISD. The students are learning more and more each year, receiving full-ride scholarships to the campuses of their choosing and are prepared to take their life and career to the next level. It is a campus rich in culture and there is no reason why the students should not feel like the best in the nation. Despite Nimitz always having a bad reputation, it actually helps a lot of students when it comes to their future goals. I graduated from Nimitz in 2019 as a cum laude student. If it wasn't for them and their dual credit program, I would have never gotten into Texas A&M. Throughout my time here, the school improved a lot. Academically, it could improve a little more, but when I was there, the students always achieved wonderful things. As a public school, you may think here are fights everyday, but I only heard of about two in the four years I was there. They also do not implement the collar shirts since the district decided to remove that policy. I did not LOVE this school, but I am forever grateful for the opportunities it gave me.

column3: East Stroudsburg North's reputation has been maipulated and twisted by those who have had bad experiences and bad attitudes. I am a recent graduate of ESN, so I can attest to the reputation that the school truly deserves. At ESN, the teachers provide a top-notch education to those who wish to learn and instill a will to learn in those who do not. The teachers are insightful and genreally jovial. Contrary to some comments that have been made, racial tensions, poor use of technology, and other erroneous claims about issues at North are not prevelant. Diversity at North is aparent and divisions are only found by those who want to find it. Many of North's classes are considered "classrooms of the future" and almost all of them utilize technology on a weekly basis. The reason East Stroudsburg North gets four stars rather than five is the community that surrounds it. To start, the district administration that runs both the North and South schools is more willing to kiss the butt of the South school and belittle the North school than it is to make "improvements" that the South school insists the North so desperately needs. Not to mention the uneven distribution of funds and resources... my child was going to north for two years and i took him out because the school is horrible my 2 year old is smarter the the teachers the kids are all from the city nyc or jersey and all out of control there is 3 cops in the school on a daily there is more drugs the a south bronx street corner i went to columbus high school in the bronx, north may not be as bad as that school but give it a few years and it will be so if anyone is going to move to the north high school area for a better life and better education DONT COME you are better off staying in the city This school is absolutely horrible. Most of the teachers here are as horrible as the students. This school has an unbelievable amount of bullying issues, "gang" problems, and is just a horrible school for your child to attend. Drugs are a huge problem with this school as well. I'm a 10th grade student at this school and a lot of these reviews do not do justice. I cannot exit my classroom without seeing a security guard and passes are color coded to each hallway so it is virtually impossible to cause mischief. I've never even heard of drugs ever being a problem and have gone to this district all of my life (like where do people get this stuff from???). Dress code is enforced, IDs must be worn, being tardy is not tolerated, and parents WILL be informed if there child skips or is failing. Classes offered go all the way to AP level. A multitude of great sports and activities are offered as well and the students are very diverse. Many of these teachers have made a profound influence on myself and others for the best. The school is entirely what the student makes of it, so please do not let some of these comments alter your opinion of this school. I have had 3 children in this school one who graduated the other two I took out and sent to the Charter school, because in this school some of the teachers don't care and are very racist. they make comments and they just don't know how to teach our children. the silliest little thing if you sneeze wrong they are on suspension. when do they find time to teach. I have had many friends also remove there children from them school High School South I hear is a much better school. This my second year of going to this school and I'm now currently a sophomore . My older brother graduated from this school last year. I do not recommend going to this school to get your high school diploma. I did not graduate yet, but I know some people who did. Most not all teachers are not respectful towards students in the school. Some are racist. Most of the teachers don't even teach and talk about random topics. The teachers here abuse there authority by writting students for little things. Only a handful of teachers here are respectful and want you to graduate. Please I highly recommend going to south even though it's an hour away from some people. This is my last year at this school since I am a senior. After that years being here, I would say it is a decent school. Basic education, sports, and activities are provided. Some teachers are very good but there may be a couple that not everyone really likes. Things may get out of control sometimes thanks to a couple of individuals. Picking an outfit to wear at this school used to be a problem sometimes, since the staff was so strict with clothes. You could get in trouble for having tiny holes in your pants and other miniscule matters. That's changed now because of the recent passing of this unnecessary dress code. Some of the students may not dress like how the staff wants them to, but punishing everyone else with a strict dress code isn't the way to handle it. The dress code really changed my attitude about this school. When I go back next Tuesday, I hope this year goes by quickly so I don't have to keep thinking about it. Isn't there other things to worry about like budget cuts and those type of problems then annoying most of the students and some parents that are against dress code? I believe attending this school was an absolute waste of time. The school's academic standards are incredibly low in my general. They do not teach elementary concepts which are necessary for college. Most teachers did not like teaching, very few were very capable/had the patience to teach, and these teachers clearly do not belong in a school environment Technology was outdated, and as a tech major I had NO opportunities to pursuit my career in this school. I felt as if I were the smartest student in this school when it came to my area of study, and there was nothing more to learn. Can you blame me for thinking like this? There was no one to challenge me. No (actual) technology teacher to challenge my way of thinking and I admittedly have fallen behind because of the lack of a "tech" teacher. Staff had called me to help them, when it SHOULD HAVE BEEN THE OTHER WAY AROUND! The entire district is lead by the rival South HS, and they are infamous among students of their corruption towards the North HS. As a result of this corruption the South HS has had more opportunities than the North HS in every aspect imaginable. This school...was a waste of four years The teachers are horrible they don't care. The guidance I have called for weeks now without a call back. I miss the where we used to live. At that school they actually cared about the students. Horrible . Teachers are worthless as well as administration I am struggling in college because i went here. North children are known as no good trash. There are more fights, and drug issues than anything else. I never had to study for any classes because even being in CP, everything was basic and so behind on curriculum. My highschool experience motivates me to get a job and out of this town, because i would never want my kids to go through what I went through. I went through the entire district and as an adult I moved just to not send my children to this school. The elementary is wonderful, past that just don't do it. I feel horrible for the teachers that are amazing at this school because they can't be as effective without the backing of the school district This school is diverse and helps its students feel involved & cared for. As a student here, I feel respected and appreciated & receive the education I desire. Amazing school with so many advanced students and this school is full of amazing teachers that help with everything my child needs. They are more than enough. THEY NEED A RAISE!! I totally recommend sending your child here because they are very well taken care of. Plus the students here work so hard and are scholars, they will make friends.

column1: Overall, this is not a good school. There is little respect for teacher and property. Students are mostly allowed to do whatever they want, especially athletes. I'd say about 90% of the students in the school will not do anything with their lives and not even attend college. There needs to be serious changes done or else its only going to get worse from here. I think Owen County High School does an excellent job for its students given it is a small, poor, rural school. The staff and faculty care a great deal for their students and the community and this pervades everything they do. My children have been students at this school for a few years with my oldest child getting ready to go off to college we of course have started looking into other curriculums. This is when I find out that most of the students who graduate from Owen county high School are not even college ready students! What are they teaching our children if they're not college ready by the time they graduate? Since covid has started my child has been slammed with work but 60% of it is nonsense work I tutor as well and high School child was sent the same school work that I was teaching a child that I tutor who is in the third grade! It is just ridiculous! Owen county is far from poor they need to spend the money on academics rather than other things!

column3: Our children do well and thrive at Middlesboro High School. The educators and the supportive community help the student exceed and train them to compete in the larger world. We try to focus our children on academics, however, the school's sports and arts programs are wonderful, too. The Middlesboro community is fortunate to have such an historical and proud instituion to educate its youth. MIddlesboro High School is a great school. They have a strong program for college bound students which successfully prepares them to compete for college admission nationwide. The school focuses on supporting and accademically challenging less fortunate students as well. Traditionally, MHS has been viewed as one of the best high schools in Eastern Kentucky. We think our daughter receives a great education at at MHS. The teachers are highly-skilled and the school has many resources and extracurricular activities. She has done very well on her college entrance exams and plans to go to a top college. I question this site's rating system if it does not give this wonderful school and community a great rating.

column1: This school has some acceptable qualities but overall they are focused on their athletics programs and are putting less attention to their academics.The administration is highly flawed and does not care about the student while they care more about the image that Xaverian portrays. The whole student body is extremely diverse which leads to racial tension and often the formation of racial groups that tend to keep to themselves.The tuition is highly overpriced and does not reflect in the amount of resources that are offered at this school.There are a large amount of public schools that will be exponentially better that Xaverian High school. I strongly recommend that you DO NOT send your son to that school. 4 Thumbs up to the staff of Xaverian. My son is in his second year here at Xaverian. He loves this school and it shows in his grades. Xaverian treat their students like adults, as if they are in college. They receive lots of work and are expected to know the lessons for the next class. I visited the school once for some information and was pleased to see that the kids act as adults not like animals I would see in many public schools. The students last year received Ipads to replace notebooks in class. I was hesitant about this program..but it did prove me wrong. Kudos to the administration! I believe many people think this school is not worth the money of its tuition, I believe it's worth every penny. My son has become a more responsible. organized, and matured individual. I know with the guidance of his school, my son will be well prepared for college. Thank you Xaverian! Xaverian HS is a second home to my son. He is having a great high school experience so far! He is currently a Sophmore playing 2sports while maintaining great grades! Xaverian teachers, guidance counselors, and the coaching staff really keep the boys on track and treat them with a level of respect which the boys mimic in return! They are at the most advanced High School with the Ipads which gives the students a well around academic challenge! I could go on and on my son and I love our new Xaverian family because that's what you become one big family!!! Just listen to the football team chant 1...2...3 Xmen 4...5...6...FAMILY!!! That speaks volumes about how our boys feel about their School community! So happy my son didn't go to Xavier in the city! Best choice he walked into the building a boy I know they are going to mold him into a fine young man for others! The good: Nice looking facility. I feel that the school leadership- principal, teachers, and guidance- care about the boys. When I had a question or when my son had issues, the staff was receptive and prompt in their response to my inquiries. The level of academics is appropriate, and there's enough for everyone- honors, advanced placement, general, and even special needs are available. Also, there is free tutoring available. The bad: This is a Boy's Club; my son chose this school, even though he is NOT 1 of The Boys: He is not white Italian and rich, which comprises the overwhelming majority of the student body. I feel that this may have been one reason he had a hard time adjusting, and missed a tremendous amount of time, especially in his sophomore year. Moreover, there are not merely as many after school activities as I expected, and what Xaverian leads you to believe. So, if you're not into sports then the options are limited. Lastly, this school is relatively expensive. Genesis is a separate middle school coed program within Xaverian, selling itself as Gifted and Talented. I spent the summer before my daughter started 6th grade debating as to wether she should go at Genesis or at Twain, where she had been accepted.... 3 years later, I can guarantee that Genesis is a well run catolic program that knows where it is going, with a strong focus on academics. They are stronger in writing than maths. They participate in the National History Day from competing at a school, city, state and finally national level. The school is not perfect but my daughter has worked extremely hard and learned a lot in a strict and lively atmosphere. The high school process seems to be mastered there and it looks like the girl do get accepted to elite schools in the city. Good luck, The school seems to be on the right track these days. Good administrators, good teachers, good athletics. I cannot say the same from when I attended there in the early 2000's. Good for them for making the right moves and changes. hopefully students today will have a better experience than I had. Our son is a senior at Xaverian High School. When we learned he wanted to go to Xaverian we were sceptical due to the tuition. But I have to say when I see the way he speaks and writes, we know we made the right choice and that he is is ready for college. When you hear your son say " I can't believe four years have gone by". You know he had a wonderful experience at Xaverian. He has been accepted to colleges with scholarships. Kudos to the administration and teachers for a job well done! Thank you for taking our in our son as a boy, and now will be leaving as a young man! My son is currently hospitalized because of the emotional harm that was done to him at this school. My son was in the Ryken program, which is for kids with special needs. The program basically violated my son's rights on multiple occasions. I will be filing a report with the state and possibly taking it further from there. This school loves to cover things up and make up lies to keep their "clean" image, even going as far as removing reviews that were made on their facebook page when they realized I made a post which brought their ratings down. Did they forget that people have the capabilities to screenshot? Yes, I did and will be posting that screenshot and submitting it to anyone who needs to review it. Removing the review is only going to prove that they like to cover things up. They didnt even care to check on my son when he was away from school for a while, and when the dept of ed informed them that my son was in the hospital, they still did not care to contact me to at least ask if he was ok and how he was doing. A real Catholic school would not lie and would care about their students. They can remove anything, but they CANNOT remove the screenshots that I have from when I first posted on facebook! I wonder what coverup/lie they will have when I submit my proof..... I should have known something was not right when I asked about the admissions criteria. I was told that it was "holistic." I took it to mean a social experiment that did not rely upon grades. I was correct. My child was accepted and did very well. I can not say the same for many classmates, who scored very low on exams and did not do any assignments. These students were abusive and bullied anyone that did well. It created three years of yell for my son. When the situation was discussed with the faculty it was brushed off. To prevent failing many students some teachers gave projects greater weight. Other teachers gave take home exams. My child would receive calls demanding answers to the exam. By the end of the year the failing students raised their grades to 70%.My child's experience was terrible because of the abuse. It is not a gifted and talented program if students are not interested in their grades. I would save your money and go public. till this day i am amazed at everything this school stands for,from the wonderful staff to the excellent programs and effective teachers. my grandson has been truly blessed. Excellent. I always brag about what a wonderful school this is. And how we Are cery prpud we sent our son here. Attending high school at Xaverian was a wonderful experience. Great teachers prepared me for life pe nis was the guy that jumped me in the bathroom

Enterprise is a great school its much better than the other school I went to it much more cleaner nicer I have met a lot of friend on my first week. this a great school. The only reason French was canceled was because Mrs. Bockman retired. Crestview is an amazing school!

column1: This school makes me feel safe and gives a great education. The staff is friendly, classes are fun, and it's overall a really great school. The iPad 1:1 program is a bonus, too, because every kid that goes to the Senior High School gets an ipad for their whole high school endeavor. Do not move your daughter to this school if she is into basketball. The coaches will not give her any play time no matter what. Do not be fooled by the "Positive coaching alliance" this is not actually practiced at this school, they only advertise that they follow these principles.

column3: The teachers are rude, and the classes are farther behind than the other schools i have attended The teachers are (with a few exceptions) apathetic. Many of then spend more time on the sport they coach than the class they teach. Fergus High School does a super job of preparing their students to be career and college ready, inspite of its size and the lack of local and state funding, . Past students have excelled at almost any institution of higher learning in the nation and graduates can be found leading and succeeding almost everywhere. Overall I really enjoyed growing up in Lewistown and attending Fergus. I got accepted into the engineering program at Montana State and have been working as an engineer for years. The teachers at Fergus prepared me as much as they could and I know many people who have excelled in life in very prestigious careers with the basics they learned at Fergus High.

column3: I graduated in 2009 in the top 5% and am now at UF. The school is filthy and dilapidated but the students are the brightest in Miami. Nearly all of the problems facing the school are due to the fact that it is part of MDCPS. Miami-Dade County is a desperately poor place and so is its huge school district. Most of the teachers are great but unfortunately many of the best are leaving. The school gets its good name from its students. The high test scores have very little to do with the teachers or the school. Put any school in a highly educated, affluent neighborhood and the students will find a way to excel. If you are highly motivated, this school can get you in to the college of your dreams. But, if you are still an immature kid try a daycare i.e. private school. No hand holding here. My sons school is a great school to attend and they keep you informed with pta meetings, activities, the class work and my sons love there school and respect there administrators... Why wasn't my original review posted? I did not have a favorable post for this school as I see most that have commented don't either. My son started two days ago as a freshman and I am so disgusted with the administration of that school. The pure arrogance of the couselors and principal My four kids graduated from Miami-Palmetto High School and I feel they got one of the best educations they could receive in public high school in Miami. Despite school appearances, the cream of the crop of Miami-Dade seems to find themselves at Palmetto. With a large selection of remarkably challenging AP classes such as Chemistry, Physics, Calculus BC, European History, Biology, etc, the elite students shine. The amount of frighteningly intelligent teenagers at this school is enough to make even your brightest son or daughter seem like any other average joe/jane. Unfortunately, Palmetto's strengths are not unchallenged. Competition in higher level classes is fierce creating demoralized students, the school's facilities, supplies and amazing teachers are in short supply, and the large amount of students who do not care for school bring the safety and quality of Palmetto down, while bringing the average class size up. Another flaw at MPSH is the counselor arrangement. There are FOUR counselors at Palmetto, one dedicated for 9th, and three for 10-12th grade. Do not expect one-on-one time very often. The idea to keep in mind for Palmetto is: if you want a personal experience with the staff, don't look for it here. Go to a private school instead. THIS SCHOOL IS AWfUL DO NOT I INSIST DO NOT GO HERE OR PUT YOUR KIDS HERE !!! This school is terrible, the faculty, staff, administrators don't pay attention to the students who need extra help. The office faculty have bad attitudes, they sit around acting like they're doing their jobs when they're reallly not.. The girls walk around and dress in clothes as if they were in a pool party. This school is overcrowded as well, don't put your children in this school, you'll regret it. Staff is rude. I'm a senior in this school. All my teachers are nice except one. She is really rude and disrespectful. I walked in the class putting my phone away and she saw me and demanded me to give it to her. I asked her, "Are you gonna give it back after class?" She said "No, I'm gonna give it to the principal and your parents have to come and pick it up." I was really angry when I heard that, because I don't live around the corner, we live really far from the school and my parents work. So the teacher wrote me up and I had to sit in CSI (indoor suspension) for 3 days and supposedly was gonna get my phone back the next day in the afternoon. when I went to pick it up, the receptionist in the front of the office who is also really rude and sarcastic said I am supposed to get it back after 5 days or before if my parents come pick it up. That is not with the admin told me, this school exaggerates with the phone policy. Give me a break. i think this school is bad and people are not doing there jobs right, and they are not polite towards the parents that walk in. iv'e witnessed i myself have been treated unproffessionally by the lady that sits in the front office. they have the students running the office while the staff runs there mouth off somebody needs to look in this school. The last three reviews are so over exaggerated. I have worked there for 10 years. We are the best comprehensive high school in Dade County and maybe the state. We don't choose our students. The reviewer who spoke of our girls dress is exaggerating. Our "easy" dress code is enforced and there are no pool party dressing. The phone policy is fantastic and yes some teachers are inconsistent, but it is better than the students constantly talking on the phone. Finally, our office staff is the very best. The person who spoke of the rudeness probably did not get what they wanted. Are we perfect...no, but we are very good at what we do. Miami Palmetto High School is consistently in the top 100 of "Forbes" best schools in the United States. Children can get the most or the least out of any school. As a 1962 graduate, let me remind you that dress codes back then were very restrictive -- and I'm sure today's standards would both shock and appall me. Go, Miami Palmetto - Go Panthers! The school has gone downhill. There is a uniform, although it is not enforced unless you are wearing shorts. Forget the boys who have their boxers hanging out and girls who show off their bras, but if you're wearing shorts you're in trouble. Some of the teachers don't know how to teach and get annoyed when students ask for help. The school is disgusting. I once had a roach climb out from my locker. All the money is spent on the tv program at school, and I do like to know what is going on in the school, but I would also like to have some toilet paper in the bathroom ("They can't afford any") and would not like to walk into the bathroom and see a soap dispenser in the toilet for a week, even after it's been reported. The office staff do not help parents unless you yell across the desk for them repeatedly. It's a terrible school and really needs to get itself together. I thought Palmetto was different, I thought it wasn't like southridge, but it is, your better off going to a private school, and if you can't afford it, try getting into Coral Reef, This school is nothing special. this school has a lot of hypocracy among girls. also the staff dosn't work like their suppose too. also the school is overcrowded. and the people are rude. I am an alumni, and I have two younger siblings who are alumni. If you are self motivated and have great support at home, you'll do well here, and rise above the filth. If you are from the Pinecrest or Palmetto Bay community, you'll find a culture shock from the disgusting Perrine and Cutler Ridge(Bay.. whatever they call it now) community which invades this school. There are bad students who are bused in, but the reality is the "gang" mentality comes form the administration at the school who are low class. Disgusting security guards and uneducated office staff ruin the school and hurt the student population. They smile and put on a nice face for parents and visitors, but they treat students disrespectfully and show a force of strength comparable to a prison yard. If your child is unprepared for the hard street mentality here, they might be damaged. On positive notes, majority of teachers are intelligent, well mannered and care about the students. Half of the students are also bright and come form good homes. 4/5 stars because sadly this school is better than most of the rest of Miami, but only because of the good families in the area. I am potential parent of this school. My son possible will go to this school soon he is studying in Shenzhen, China, but in the international class which is especially preparing the student to study in US at grade 12. For all the information I got from the internet, it is sure a very good school. As with any school, some things about Palmetto are less than perfect. It's not the cleanest place and there are a lot of students. However, I am currently in my third year at Palmetto and I absolutely love it. If you are a good student, or at least show effort/respect towards your teachers and peers here they will go out of their way to help you. Involved students get the most out of their high school experience - any kids who don't like Palmetto probably wouldn't be happy at almost any school in the area. I chose to go to Palmetto over any private school that was offered to me. I chose Palmetto for their reputation as a competitive school in regards to grades, sports (some more than others) and productions (TVP, Yearbook, and my personal favorite - Newspaper). My teachers love their jobs and want to see students show pride in everything they do. The uniform is casual - your choice of spirit shirt (most every club has one per year so there are tons to choose from) and jeans - it's no big deal/inconvenience. My only issue is that school starts too early, but that's not Palmetto's fault. Palmetto has great academics and a huge slate of clubs, sports and extracurriculars. The facilities will be updated under the new bond. It's great having my kid in my neighborhood school! My kids are very happy and I enjoyed being a volunteer and it has been a great experience, havent had any complains. This is the best comprehensive high school in the County (probably, the state too). With 27 APs, an iPrep Academy, the new Cambridge Magnet, a top-notch Jazz Band and other fine arts offerings, this school should be everyone's first choice. The Principal is dynamic, open-minded and energetic. Her administration is loyal and helpful. We are so fortunate to have Palmetto in our community! Interesting school. Fun band, fun kids. A little bit challenging. Go to this school if you're a easy learner. The school is decent. Not the best but not the worst:) So I suppose that's how I feel about this school. Fair warning, this is a big big school. If you or your child need individualized attention you will not get it here. My time at this school was one of the worst and darkest periods of my life. I'm by no means an idiot, but when I ran into roadblocks in the classroom I received very little help and that seriously tripped me up academically and I fell behind a lot. I fell through the cracks socially as well. I wasn't around healthy people and was the butt of many peoples jokes and remarks. If you need a healthy environment with more attention than a teacher with 150 students can give you don't go here. Size is not something the school can really help. Nor can they help the apathy of some instructors. I can say that my bumpy experience here truly prepared me for higher education. I learned what I liked, more about who I am. I learned to ask questions and that my education was worth getting those answers. I learned to choose better people to be in my life and I learned to love myself more cause no one else is going to do it for me. Thanks for the life-lessons Palmetto. This school is terrible. Please parents do not send your kids here. Everyone at that school is very rude and not welcoming and the school itself is terrible. They steal from their students and treat them like they are nothing. They even called my daughter, who is a very respectful person, a liar. This school is very rude and I do not recommend sending your kids here. TERRIBLE. this school is disgusting. Parents think just because its in a rich neighborhood that its a great school but really its so dirty, grimey, and the authorities are horrible and unhelpful. They used over 30,000 dollars or so to rebuild buildings in 2016 but they cant hire new janitors to clean the 3 week old milk on the seats in the caf. This school is one of the worst. The staff are so rude excepr dr. Harley and a few others. Mr hunter now enforces uniform after being a no uniform school since it started and if you dont wear it then you get a detention FOR UNIFORM. tje securities are so grimey and they do everything BUT secure. the ladies are rude and mean and the men just hang out and act buddy buddy with the students and let them skip. DON'T SEND YOUR KIDS HERE. The school is great so far. My son loves it, and is getting excellent grades. He is a freshman and he only has 8 students in his algebra class. He says it's basically like tutoring. I don't find it to be dirty, but, it is a large public school. Large is a relative term though when you consider other schools such as Ferguson have almost 5000 kids enrolled. This school is half the size. The school is great and the teachers are some of the teachers are awesome (shout out to mrs.dillon aka best English teacher ever) but the ladies who work in the office are the rudest people ever they complain and complain and u will literally sit in the office for like 10hrs waiting for something unless u speak up and then when u do speak up there extremely rude my mother hates going into the office just because of how rude and nasty they are they have so much sass and attitude especially mrs.mcdonald. MPHS is an all inclusive comprehensive high school that offers many opportunities for students with various learning abbilities. This is a fantastic school with academic rigor and top tier college placements that meet or exceed the elite private schools nearby. It is big, yes, but with size comes the ability to offer a huge selection of classes and extracurriculars. I had my kids at one of those snooty private schools, but they hated it and couldn't get the AP classes they needed. Here, there's 29 AP classes and they have the highest pass rate in the District. Unlike magnets schools, your kid can change his or her mind and explore tons of electives to suit their interests, whether it's arts, business, languages, science or whatever. And I think that's what high school is for - finding yourself. My freshman daughter is acedemically advanced and MPSH is the right place for her. She is challenged but supported. Her teachers are amazing! They truly care for their students. I am also pleased with the focus on community involvement in addition to the fun that is offered. She is experiencing a great balance of advanced academic rigor combined with traditional high school fun. We couldnt be happier. The school has a great selection to make up schedules. Therefore, every child can study for their passion. It is a great school with long history, the magnet programs have attracted pinecrest and palmetto bay students, which resulted in lower performance among the non-selective MPSH. Hopefully the new magnet programs, will help to attract more advanced students to the school.The principal Mrs Dobbs is a great and caring person. She resolves any problem that is referred to her.My children are taking the most advanced classes and doing well overall. MPSH has some of the best teacher in the county with best AP passing rates e.g. Ms Schlackman for AP enviro, Mr Garcia for AP calculus..etc. If your child is focused on what s/he wants, this school is for him. By the new magnet programs, you do not have to live in the catchment area to enjoy the MPSH panther's pride. The teachers all care about the students, the staff is incredibly helpful and the school offers a wide variety of ways to get involved, whether it be via clubs or sports. It's really a family. Our faculty care so much about students. We are really lucky to have phenomenal students who excel in the classroom, in sports, in theater, in competitions, in community service, year book, newspaper, and life! We found out exactly how great the school is when my son started college and found out he was as well prepared or more than any of his classmates for college level work. And he had a head start on college credits thanks to all the AP classes he took at Palmetto. I took advanced classes in high school here in Miami, but the classes Palmetto has are much more advanced than those I had over 35 years ago. Palmetto did a great job of preparing my older kids for college and is still doing a great job with my younger ones. Room for improvement. Some teachers and members of administration are excellent, some teachers don't show much care or respect for their students. While certain things made it great many instances made it bad during my time as a student there. Palmetto helped prepare my daughter for college. The teachers and curriculum prepared her academically and the atmosphere of diversity and acceptance prepared her socially. The school is a nice environment where we can learn and grow as human beings. Palmetto is a great place to work. Palmetto really fosters learning not only for their students, but for the faculty and staff. Palmetto's comprehensive programs, clubs and activities make it just the right fit for my daughter! Great School! Great Principal! Great Teachers!Our Principal and her Administration are doing a wonderful job supporting our teachers! Why would anyone go anywhere else!!!! BECAUSE ITS AN ORGANIZE SCHOOL AND GREAT educational school , love the sports team and shows they put on I'm new in school and don't really know how it is and work, but it is a thing of time I am so happy to have ms.jarrett as my Algebra 2 teacher. I can't wait to spend the rest of the year with her as my teacher ! I mean I just go to school to get good grades and do well. This school has provided that for me,I haven't had any problems with the staff or people. I just worry about myself and my friends and stay out of anything I shouldn't be involved in . its a good school it promotes learning, hard work and has staff that works well with the students. Good I enjoy school and everyone in it.my teachers are nice and everyone is chill This school has been great so far. Everybody is very welcoming. The staff is also great with students. It's great, everyone is really friendly, they're never fights, the food is amazing and the teachers are really chill The school has a lot of ups and downs and I believe they both average each other out. It is a great school with plenty of opportunities It's a nice school with many great sport teams

column3: First Colonial High is a wonderful school with loving and caring teachers! The teachers truly care about the student and his/her education. First Colonial offers a wide variety of clubs and athletic programs. She is a member of many clubs and is on the basketball team. She loves First Colonial! I came from a private school, and was a tad nervous about attending a public school. I was also worried that the education wouldn't be the same, but I was pleasantly surprised. Honestly, in some aspects First Colonial did a better job than private school. The teachers are welcoming, and the students made me feel right at home. This is a great school! First Colonial is a school that is second to none! I am a student leader at FC and I can say that I would not want to go anywhere else. As a member of the academy, I do live out of district and also had other options on the table for high school but I chose FC and love every minute. As SCA President, I get to know a lot of the student body and the majority of the faculty and staff and they are some of the greatest people ever. For a public high school, we have diversity but acceptance. Everyone has a place where they fit and with 53 clubs and dozens of sports teams, everyone can join something they are interested in. Every at FC feels welcome and part of the Patriot Family! It really is the best school at the beach. I really do enjoy attending the Legal Studies Academy, but some of their rules and regulations are stressing me out! I am very fearful about being late because of the tardy window. Even if you are late for lunch you have to go to the tardy window. That seems to be my only problem. I really enjoy the teachers even if it is the third day of school. They are really funny and fun to be around. I would recommend this school to anyone else out if they were interested in law. If the tardy window wasn't so intimidating, this would have gotten five stars! FC High is the best in Va Beach! The teachers communicate with the parents regularly. They keep the drug use under wraps and haress students who dont play along. The teaching is so-so and if any open up-they are punished-teachers included. Ask the ones in portables. Money talks and you get no where if you try stick up your child. I am glad we left, terrible place. The school is awful the kids or horrible the drug problems are so bad. The guidance and office don't care I have tried to get help multiple times. There are a few good teachers but most are horrible the school only cares about the unaccomplished and not the kids with true potential I switched schools because ti was so awesome Okay, this school is terrible. Most of the teachers are bullies (slight few aren't). I was told that I failed one of my sols and then I showed up to take it and they had gotten it wrong. I stressed for weeks over it and then didn't have to take it. There's no school spirit (at least in my class). Can't wait for june so I can finally be done with this school. Ok all y'all saying FC is a terrible school can go away and shutup. FC is an amazing school and I'm happy to go there!!! The teachers are nice and truste me I've meet terrible teachers so stop and the academy kids are ok my sis is in the academy and she loves it . If you pay attention and actually LISTEN TO YOUR KID you would see they are happy. I've went from Windsor woods elementary to plaza middle school to green run (for a month) then to first colonial and out of all the schools this is the only time I'm happy to go to school so yeah FCHS is an alright school. I graduated from here and only attended for my senior year due to my dad being in the military. It is a little cramped, as it used to be a middle school...lots of portables. When I was there the rules were pretty ridiculous (an ISS for checking the time on my phone...seriously?), but since then, the rules in VBCPS have become pretty lax. Of course there are annoying kids there, but that can be said about any school. Most of them are laid back and cool since most of the oceanfront goes there. I made some really good friends in the LSA (wasn't in it) and in just the normal zoning. Some of the teachers were hornery, but some of them were pretty awesome. Lots of artsy people here. I feel like I was able to be creative and develop myself more in the two art classes I took. Looking back, it was a pretty fun experience. The interaction and the communication the school has with both students and teachers. Eldest son was very successful and next son is having a great experience. First Colonial High School has great programs to advance your level of education prior to college. They always offer meet and greats in the beginning of the high school years to introduce children to different colleges, certified programs and other career options. They have several clubs and community programs to keep children involved. Excellent! My daughter is a senior in the Legal Studies Academy and is well prepared for college. FC is a really good school, but it should work a little more with bully and respect to other people from different races. I attended FC from my freshman year through my senior year and I really got a good experience, but I would say they are good and bad people and sometimes people treat other people like they are nothing and that's one thing that I hated so much from FC they really should work with bully and respect to others people, otherwise is a good school an de they offer a good education to the students. Great. Everyone there was nice and it was a great experience. 7/6/2020 - Parent here.... so far we have loved every bit of this school . My daughter is a rising senior. She participates in two activities within the school and has been since a freshman. She is not an AP student and I am a single mom . This school does have a pro dominantly white population but that has not affected her social or academic progress . She gets a long with all and has never come home with complaints about students or staff . She has attended school in VB since Kindergarten and this is the first school that we have had zero complaints . Wonderful atmosphere and the teachers are phenomenal. Very invested in their students. I would recommend you bring your children to First Colonial. This is a sorry excuse of a school. I don't understand how the administrator has kept her position, people say she is just biding time until retirement.It seems most of the positive reviews are being written by the Legal Studies students (LSA). The LSA is a school within the school. LSA has their own activities to keep them involved, challenged and bonded. They have their own Guidance, classes, and ways of disseminating information to parents, etc. If your student is LSA, they will be fine.If not, good luck. If you doubt it, just check the school website. What's listed under "Upcoming Activities"? Nothing. Who is the Student Activities coordinator? They do have one, but their staff list isn't even complete. Where can you find the clubs/sports/organizations w/the sponsor & contact information? You can't. Look under "news & important information", you'll find how to change a password. It has been this way for years, despite numerous complaints. Getting kids involved and interested in school is NOT a priority in the regular school, only in LSA. Communication is abysmal. Since the PA system does not work in some parts of the school and students miss morning announcements, they could record the morning announcements and put them on the website but they don't. Again, getting students involved and interested is not a priority. When PTSA does plan something i.e. "Fun Friday" it's not for ALL of the classes. Only the classes whose teachers participate gets to play & win gift cards and such. Teachers don't even know which days are spirit days, let alone students. When the overcrowded school went to "one lunch", kids ate in the halls on the floor or with their clique in a favorite teacher's room. There were supposed to be activities for students or other places for them to eat. Other district schools implemented great ideas. Again, student involvement or spirit, not a priority. Additionally, electives offered are extremely lacking because they can't retain staff. IT Fundamentals (beginning computer for 9th graders) isn't offered at FC, but is at other schools. The college process information doesn't begin at FC until Sept/Oct of the Senior year- some colleges are accepting applications already by that time. Yes, it's a rat and roach infested old building, but that is not what causes the lack of school spirit. It is the inequity, apathy and lack of leadership from the admin. It needs leadership that cares about getting students interested and involved. I am a recent graduate. I wish I had never gone to this school. To say that this place broke me and left me worse off is an understatement. I lost any passion I had for education, nor do I know what path I want to take at all. I wish I had been homeschooled or gone to a private school. I'd likely be better off. With that being said, when I have children, I would never bring them to a public school due to my experiences being at this one. Classrooms are a negative space when I think of one now.Most teachers often recycled material, therefore the lessons lacked any sort of passion. Some teachers couldn't even teach. Others rattled on about their home life during class. Then there were the coaches who got teaching or hall monitor jobs, and as you might guess, they had favorites in class if you played sports. I was forced to be in classes I didn't sign up for, even ending up in an all male class, with a football coach/teacher. I told him I was uncomfortable there and he treated me like I was lower because of it. No surprise, I had something horrible happen to me in front of him by one of the male peers and he did nothing to stop it. I lost my gym uniform near the end of the year since someone stole it. A gym teacher (male) offered no solution other than coming into the boys locker room everytime I had gym and digging through a bin for one. A biology teacher made me miss a whole lesson because she wanted me to change in the nurses office. Classrooms are a negative space when I think of one now.Most teachers often recycled material, therefore the lessons lacked any sort of passion. Some teachers couldn't even teach. I told him I was uncomfortable there and he treated me like I was lower because of it. Teachers were often the bullies here, they also allowed bullying if they also didn't like a student that was being bullied.I still have nightmares about this place and hate what it has done to me as a result.
