column3: I think Casa Grande is one of the best schools around. Although we have a limited budget, and our campus might not be as pretty as some would like, most teachers would give anything to see their students excel and succeed, and help figure out possibilities for the future as well as iron out the necessary details in order to achieve those. Casa is not individually oriented; the teachers continually push, even those who do not immerse themselves in academics, to try and be successful in their own way. Great school =] Casa Grande offers a challenging curriculum, for those students interested and capable. There are many opportunities for self-driven students to thrive and excel. Outstanding arts programs include band, drama, art and more. Very high functioning student body. Additional funding would go a long way toward building their tutoring programs, which would help those lagging behind. I honestly do not like Casa. I couldn't wait to go to high school, I wanted huge classes, a huge school, and to be extremely busy all the time with clubs and activities. But when i got to Casa, I was just so disappointed. I'm really unhappy at Casa right now. There are barely any clubs I want to join, classrooms are dirty and crammed, there's no ROTC (I wanted to be in that soo bad!), the school can't afford literally anything, and the leadership is terrible for planning events. Homecoming last year was just a dj in the gym with lights and a water station, there weren't any decorations or food except for backgrounds that were stolen off of the floats! And I had to pay 25$ for that ?!?!? I could go on and on about what a dump Casa is, and how there are BARELY any activities since our district can't afford it =_=. But I don't think anyone will listen, so goodbye. Casa has been amazing so far! I love it! I am a sophomore, and as the end of the year approaches, I couldn't be happier. I started freshman year at Rancho Cotate, which was horrid. The school and classes are easy and almost all kids are passed in all classes without doing anything. The students at Rancho were mean, unwelcoming and they all just wanted to get drunk, even freshman! Then I went to Petaluma High, and the teachers were less than enthusiastic. There is no discipline and no one cares. Then, at the beginning of the year I changed to Casa. It has been wonderful, the courses are challenging, I am currently taking AP World, Honors English, Honors Bio and Honors Algebra 2. It is challenging, fun and the teachers are amazing. They all are there to help and the communication is literally amazing. We have had some amazing speakers come including Mike Smith (look him up) and we even had a "Olympic games" for fun in February. The sports programs are awesome, the football team was undefeated and one game away from state, and the baseball is currently in the playoffs. There are art programs (Photography too!) and the AMAZING Hatchery program, as well as our award winning news paper. Most teachers are great. Academically, they pushed the students to the limit. Has many good AP and honor classes. Those students who wanted to excel academically went on to good colleges. Can improve at counseling and leadership. My son is a new student at Casa, I find that they are not welcoming at all. He has seeked out help from a few of his teachers. (Spanish especially and has been refused) we've been told to go to the jc college for help. They don't like new comers apprently. They push you off and hope you don't come back, we are from the east coast and were never turned away for help until now. I would never recommend this school. I even emailed the superintendent and never heard back. Advice to new comers don't choose this school. I had great experience at this school as a student. Terrible school, teachers are uneducated, all part of a terrible school system. My child is bullied and can purchase alchohol and drugs easily, I do not recommend this school. I will be transferring my child elsewhere shortly. Academics were great, all other areas epic failure! Even trying to volunteer your time and money the administration makes it hard! Teachers are disengaged and lack any kind of empathy. Workload during COVID was increased, even through distanced learning with unrealistic expectations. Some teachers marked zero for even one mistake while others wasted the entire zoom class talking about what they did over the weekend instead of preparing students for their homework; spoiler alert, the math homework didn't match the lesson. There was ZERO engagement from teachers with parents, even when their grades showed they were struggling to adapt to online learning. Some teachers didn't update grades for weeks, or even months leaving students and parents in the dark regarding the status of grades and class standing. Overall, some teachers are great and truly care while most others showed their true colors which is deeply troubling and an indictment of the entire school and administration. The school doesn't know anything about the students and everything they do that they think is the best for them is actually the worst case scenario. My child has been getting bullied and it's very clear and apparent to everyone even staff at the school but nothing has been done to help.

column1: It can be difficult for teachers to regain control of their classroom, especially in the classes that have more than 20 people. We don't feel ready for the real world at all and there is widespread intolerance among the students. Disciplinary problems come up all the time. The good things about this school are the counselor, (who is actually very helpful), the school band, and our various extracurriculars.

column3: I sent all three of my kids to this school and I can say that I have not regretted it for a second. Two of them have graduated with honors and are going on to university and the third one has recently finished this sophomore year. This school is great and the children are friendly and everything. My cousin's kids go to Cane Bay and they do not like it. It's like a twin of Stratford and everyone there hates it. Goose Creek High School is a dirty school. I hope this review helps other parents make a choice on which school to send their children because to me, Stratford High is the best. I am a parent of a Stratford graduate. Also, my youngest child attended Stratford until she went to the South Carolina Governor's School of Science and Mathematics. My children were under the old administration. Even back then the Band didn't have much money. The football team and the band have more expenses because they travel so much. The cost of travel has gone up a lot. With the country in such a mess financially no one has a lot of money. Academically Stratford has always been at or above the National average. My daughter was accepted at every school she applied to. She graduated from a private school up North who gave her a full ride scholarship. Her graduation class at Stratford had kids that went to Notre Dame, Harvard, Vanderbilt and several went to USC and Clemson. This was the class of children,who when they were in elementary school, they came in second at the World Competition of the Odyssey of the Mind. They missed first place by two points. At that time South Carolina was at or near the bottom of the list for education in the country. There are more schools now than there used to be for the county and state to support. We still follow the school. As a Stratford Alumni (1990)- I am proud to have been a student at this school. An 8 out of 10 rating aint bad. GO KNIGHTS! We moved from out of state and my ninth grade daughter was doing well especially during the pandemic and online learning. Within two months of online learning, she was called a racial slur. I immediately contacted the chain of command via email and then called and talked w/one of the asst principles for her grade. I was assured that this type of behavior was not tolerated. Needless to say, the situation was immediately addressed as the student was not online in class for several days. I was glad that a situation like this was not taken lightly and after overcoming this hurdle, my daughter has continued to excel in all classes. During the pandemic, homework is rarely given and in some classes, watching videos has become mundane. The teachers are pretty responsive considering the circumstances of teaching to online and traditional students at the same time. If we stay in this school district, we shall see how tenth grade goes.

column3: In two years Burrell has been reviewed 4 times, yet the two 5 star reviews are on the same day, which is suspect. If you look at the other two reviews they both talk about the sports at Burrell, and those are what ring most true to me. My son had an awful time at the school socially due to his lack of interest in sports, and the administration didn't seem to care about anyone but the athletes. It shouldn't be that hard for an A+ student to find a niche, and when serious allegations of cheating, favoritism and bullying arise, it would be nice for someone in power to actually look into the matter. We ended up doing cyber school for part of the year and then paying for admission into another district the next fall....no such problems since. Excellent teachers, wide variety of AP classes, partnership with Penn State New Kensington gives students a unique opportunity to get college courses throughout high school - we have been impressed. Graduates end up at top notch universities. As a local realtor with 2 children attending schools in the district I am continuously impressed with Burrell. Their new superintendent is very active and progressive; the kids are great and are provided with tons of opportunities. Because of its smaller size, every student has a chance to participate in athletics and extra-circular activities. I have heard this is not the case in huge quad A districts. I feel confident that my customers who buy homes in this school district will also be pleased with Burrell. Great school - good academics, tons of AP courses starting in 8th grade, opportunities to take college classes at Penn State New Kensington, tons of technology, & a well trained staff. The small community seems very supportive of the students and goes above and beyond to help them achieve. Recent grads went to M.I.T. & West Point. The opportunities are there for the students to get an amazing education and they are expected to be involved in their community in a positive way. Besides academics I beleive my kids are learning good values in this this community.

column1: This is a GREAT school because the teachers are very involved with their students and care that they recieve a GREAT education! The students and parents are known by name and not by number and treated with respect! Overall, I feel this school provides a quality education for my child in a safe and caring environment.

column3: I attended BA from 1981-1985 and the school was off the chain. The teachers back then were so serious about their kids, and their teaching us to learn. Maybe it's not the school; have you ever just sat back and thought...maybe it's the way the kids are being brought up at home in these times. If a child doesn't get that up bringing at home, you can't expect for the teachers to teach them & then have the kids being disrespectful. I've walked down these same halls and have noticed that there's a lot of disrespect; foul language; kids saggin' with the pants. And me being a parent it's like the kids could care less that there was any ADULTS around. My daughter graduated from DeSoto High this year (2012), but I still have a younger one who would love to attend my High School Alma Mata, but with what I've witnessed lately with the out of control students. She will also be attending the remaining of her schooling in the DeSoto area. I would loved for my girls to be like me: BA COUGAR 4 LIFE. PARENTS KEEP YOUR KIDS AWAY!!!! Administration lies to your face and teachers bicker among themselves. Look its not the school or the staff's fault for any of the problems going on or that are spread about B.A. As a alumni (Class of 2005) myself, as is most of my family... No one is to blame for each and every individuals actions and yes parents can be influential but they can not sit over there children 24/7 and know there every thought and every move. Take my experience for example I was in honors classes and had good grades freshman year well following year still in same classes and still managed to pass them all, but skipped more than half the year literally! Sad thing is my parents had no clue and when they found out what could they really do, but it gets better when i skipped i did not skip with class mates it was people i actually meet else where. If your child skips a lot use there smart phone to your advantage. technology is a great tool and as a parent its your right to know and be concerned about your child. But its not fair for anyone to point fingers, especially with the attitudes the younger generations have. At first my daughter disliked how everything was old and dirty and broken, that the building was in disrepair, how the teachers complained that there was no money for new things to make it nice, and how there were a lot of roughnecks attending. For about the first 6 weeks she was scared to go. Her last school was new and in a much, much better neighborhood. So understandably she'd need time to readjust. Most parents in our neighborhood send their kids to private schools because DISD has a reputation for poor schooling and bad financial choices. I am a sophomore and and cannot even put into words how much I love BA. Im in Avid and joined byran adams bell drill team. Seems like not everyone has been informed, but we are progressing. I believe we will achieve and progress more as long as we have Mr.Kastle running our school. If you are a parent of a student that attends BA, encourage your son or daughter to join Avid and take multiple AP courses. I believe that you cannot take control of where you came from, but you can control where you are going. When people go there they lose hope. It seems like the only way to get out is through an athletic scholarship or the army. That's if you aren't a parent by the time you graduate. At least they have pride. Bryan Adams has made great strides over the last few years. The teachers are some of the best in the district and the kids are a lovely, diverse group. BA has everything you want! It has sports, arts, clubs, advanced courses and now an Early College program. Please ignore the stupid low rating. BA has a large number of English language learners who have trouble passing standardized tests. That should not be the reason you don't check it out. If anything, they enhance the school with their textured experiences. Over all the school has been growing to the better since our principal Mr.Kastl has been in office he has made changes to the school system and the school has gotten better over the years .I am a junior now and ive seen the school grow over these years .All these other bad reviews arent very accurate because in the end this is a public school and realy you cant expect a whole lot from a public school, but Bryan Adams offers what your children need to succed I am an alumni. I received scholarship from several colleges, graduated from a private, nationally-ranked university with practically a 4.0 and two degrees, and have continued to succeed professionally. B.A. is a great place for students to decide that they want to win. Teachers and the community are great. Currently there is construction to make our school look better they have many different activities for you to be apart of. There are also many clubs you can join. Bryan Adams offers early college program were you can earn college credits. The environment is nice and very inclusive. This school, and the district overall, is still experiencing the results of forced desegregation that started in the mid 60's and resulted in mass exodus of whites to north suburbs such as Plano, as well as the rise of various private schools. For a significant percentage of home buyers in the area, they do not send their children here but include the cost of private schooling in their consideration.Problems cascaded afterwards which are not the fault of the families who cannot afford private education. 88% of the students are economically disadvantaged and are challenged by the educational disadvantages from an early age.Given the educational level when the students arrive, it's challenging to offer many advanced placement classes. Students graduating from here may have a difficult time competing against students who have had these opportunities.The facility itself has been kept up best it can. The east parking lot, no longer needed due to fewer students having cars, has been vacant and fenced off for many years.Those with wealth, who have been re-populating East Dallas, have yet to commit to making the school district (all of it, not just magnet schools) top notch. It would take several generations to do so. Failure to deliver accommodations on time (as required by law.) Coaches failing to inform parents about disturbing behavior of students (although they find time to gossip with other teachers.) I had to pull my student out. Stay far away from this school if your student is anything but way above average in all categories,..academic, extracurricular, social, mental health. They are not prepared to assist the majority of students.

column3: I came in as a substitute teacher not really having much experience in Public School. To my surprise the public schools were a lot better than I was lead to believe. I have seen many people complain about the staff at both the High School and the Middle School, but let's face it we are all imperfect people, so to demand perfection from teachers is not to fair in and of it's self. If a child doesn't turn out the way a parent expects them to, it isn't the fault of the school it is the fault of the parent. Teaching begins in the home not the classroom. So if our county parents would get behind the schools and teacher a bit more, maybe we would see more of the success that parents desire to see of their children.

column1: This school just needs to work on it's students more and more discipline for the students. Thank G-d I never went to Manual Arts Senior High School. I would hate to be associated with them. Irma Suarez Montes de Oca class of 1986 i am currently a freshman at mahs nd its is a good school the staff isnt topnotch but if you do fond a good teacher it will help you. i am in NAI (USC Neighborhood Academic Initiative) and i feel it is really helping me get through all dillemas at school because it helps me to achieve higher. Although I am not 100% on board with the structural changes taking place at Manual Arts, I have met the principal at a community function and he seems to be making a serious commitment to this school which I applaud. My son attended Manual for 2 years, and that was enough. The school is not terrible, but there is an attitude among the teachers that since this is a ghetto school they should be able to do whatever they want. There is no leadership from the administration and teachers run their classes however they see fit. Mr. Channel, who is mentioned elsewhere here, has a rule that if a student is absent even one day, with or without an excuse, they fail the course. My son was sick one day (with a doctors note!) and failed the class, even though he had all A's. Channel also designates certain pretty girls to be his "helper teachers", and these students get special privileges. Other teachers do much the same, favoring some students, enforcing bizarre rules, etc. We went as far as the school board to protest this, but the attitude seems to be "well , those teachers work in a tough school so we let them alone". At least we didn't have to worry about "teaching to the test". Nobody in this school seems worried about how their students do, long term or short term. I come from a family of educators and I have never experienced a school like this.

column3: Middleton is a great school that is improving every year. The amount of magnet students is rapidly increasing, and my experience there has been nothing short of fantastic. MHS has a culture promoting post secondary education for students of all skill levels with halls named for colleges and universities and a forward thinking administration and guidance staff. We boast national award winning US FIRST robotics team, and nationally recognized FBLA, FFA, and INTEL science students. Our magnet valedictorian in 2012 received a full ride scholarship to Columbia University and her immediate predecessor in 2011 earned a full scholarship to MIT. The teachers and staff at all levels are terrific to work with and communications with staff is excellent. In the past 3 years this school has elevated it's state rating from D to B status due to the culture of respect and learning at the admin level. There is a diversity of students and emphasis on STEM education. A variety of AP and dual enrollment courses are offered to students up for the challenge. MHS is a great school! My son is in the engineering magnet program and will graduate in 2014. He turned down IB to go to Middleton and it was definitely the right choice! The engineering curriculum is intensive and the faculty is awesome. He is also involved in the robotics program, which has been very successful over the past few years with teams earning a bid to the world championship for the past 3 years. (His team actually won the world championship in 2012, and were runners-up in 2013!) Middleton truly focuses on trying to ensure the every child has the opportunity to be successful, whether magnet or traditional. Middleton STEM Magnet High School was one of two black Tampa high schools before integration. Pride from alumni and the black community rallied to raise their alma mater to a school with high expectations. The 12-year old new Middleton facility is an award- winning campus design with a large grassy central courtyard. Hillsborough County School District (the 4th largest in the USA) has committed their STEM high school resources to Middleton. At Middleton, over 30% of the students are enrolled in a magnet major. My experience is that my child is strong in technology but low in reading. He thrives from the balance of Middleton s challenging STEM classes with a strong reading proficiency program geared to students with low performance. The rigor of taking 8 credits (two classes per year) of Computer Technology has kept him focused on academic classes. Over the last 12 years Middleton's priority has been on safety, high expectations, great leadership and STEM enrollment. Athletics was not a #1 priority in the school culture. This enables average athletes to participate on a sports team for fun, exercise and commitment to Middleton Pride. My school is Middleton high school,The land of the tigers,The one who never fall always rise up. Since I came to Middleton high school my dream start become real, A place where everyone is somebody, A school that show everyone future, A place that you feel real like a person not an animal, A place where everyone like not dislike, A place where you always see a better future above in the sky passing by. We will Improve our school in the disciplinary , respect way. We are the Tigers. The magnet program at this school is top notch. We are very happy that our son is attending this school. The faculty and staff do a great job. The principal is very committed to student success. My son was lost before he came to this school and now he has many good friends and has found his way. I don't know how much of that is the school and how much he just matured, but the school deserves at least some of the credit. Highly recommend 8th graders that have any interest spend 1 to 2 days shadowing at the school to see if it is right for you. The robotics program is world class, but FBLA and TSA clubs are also quickly becoming known for producing state and national champions. The best thing for my son is the acceptance of the geek culture. That is what I think is helping him grow and figure out what he wants to do with the rest of his life. Also, don't think the Game Design magnet is an easy magnet. Although not as challenging as the Engineering (offered at Middleton) and IB programs (offered at other schools), it does teach important skills. If your child is a real overachiever, consider joining 2 magnet programs and watch him or her accomplish things you never thought possible. Last week my son saved me $300 from buying a new LED TV. He used what he learned to repair my old TV (it had a bad board). I am in the Biomedical and Engineering magnets at Middleton High School and I have to say that both magnets are extraordinary. The magnet teachers often have experience in the field really know their stuff. There is a lot of project-based work involved in the magnet program, but it work that I consider fun. Magnet programs at Middleton give you experience in the field and give you an advantage in college. As of this year, Middleton is the only internationally STEM certified high school in the state of Florida. It also has 7 robotics teams (1 FRC, 3 FTC, and 3 VEX). Middleton also has many other STEM-related clubs, including TSA, FBLA, Mu Alpha Theta. Sports are pretty much open to everyone, but they aren't the school's strong point. Kids often push each other to do better in academics and also support each other. Most people seem to get along well and bring each other up, embracing the uniqueness and individuality of others. Middleton has a CNC mill, a plasma cutter, and multiple 3D printers. The curriculums for the Engineering and Biomedical magnets are created by PLTW and are very strong curriculums that are fun instead of just tedious. I highly recommend avoiding this school. The administration has no clue how to run a school or control its students. In my experiences, many of the teachers do not know what they are doing and if they do, they are clueless when it comes to teaching a class (looking at two magnet teachers in particular). The only reason that the grades are held at an average mark is because the magnet students are there to hold them up. The only thing that I have gotten from this school is a terrible GPA and even if I work extremely hard there is no way that I can recover from that and the severe mental damage that I have gotten from attending this school. Do not attend Middleton High School. I have wanted to pull my child out from this school since the first year, but my daughter insist that the STEM label will help her college application and she has made friends at the school. I do not know if the other high schools in the county are equally bad at assigning schedules and teacher retention, but I wish we had stayed in a charter school. I realize that there were budget cuts and some of that money has to be now spend on guards instead of counselors and teachers, but something like a schedule should be doable for all returning students. LEADERSHIP is a 2 star...When a student is failing, out of courtesy no one notifies you of this or any support afterwards. It seems Counselors are only worried about college information and higher classes(do not respond to emails). Some teachers will keep you informed (Edsby) while others do not respond at all. Otherwise this STEM school is good for the students which I give 4.5 stars. Love that the Parent/Teacher Conference dates/notifications have been sent out in advance.

column1: the school has so much to offer but they say they are a school of "no excuses'' I find the school makes an excuse for everything. from teachers not showing up on back to school night to guidence disregarding requests for appts., from students. It's a school that accepts mediocraty fom their administration and staff at the expense of their students. My daughter went to this school and I had to pull her out because they love to sweep problems under the carpet. There bullying policy is weak and they do nothing about it. I'm highly disapointed in neptune hs right down to their vice super intendent. You get no where with them. For a school of excellence they sure didn't prove it to me. The only good thing about this school is their JROTC program. This rating should really be updated. Neptune provides a good educational base and nice diverse culture. The teacher's are hardworking and invested in the students. As an alumni, college was never a problem. My biggest qualm is that the College prep courses are far too lackadaisical and not academically rigorous because of it. College prep houses smart students who don't like to study & since it teeters between regular & Honors courses they don't have to. A higher standard needs to be put in place there but the Honors & AP classes are great. All in all, a solid school. The inmates are running the asylum. Students are out of control. Fights prevail. The teachers collect a salary and hope to move on to a better school. I had a good experience at this school, though that was over 25 years ago. I was in mostly honors classes so I can not speak for the experiences of those in mid to lower level classes. I turned out fine, but can't say for sure whether or not I would've turned out better had I attended a "higher" ranked school. The negative reviews are inaccurate, ask any alumni. Neptune school board invests a lot of money in infrastructure, and the physical school is as nice as you'd find anywhere. Probably the nicest aquatic center in NJ. The money however would be better spent on student counselling programs, social work, job placement and vocational programs. It's disappointing that an expensive school system is not yielding better opportunities for the children and the community.

This is a school where doing well academically is the overall goal for everyone and make being "smart" cool! University High School Academy is one of the best schools in Michigan! My child applied her sophomore year because the school she was attending wasn't challenging enough. She decided to come to UHSA. This school is great. Her grades dropped a bit but I knew she was actually earning them and working hard. My son will attend the 8th grade prep academy in the fall. I am very pleased with the quality education provided. I know my kids will be prepared for college. They not only teach kids to write and do math, they are required to critically think, not memorize information. I love UHSA! Bates Academy. 2013-14 School Year off to a much better start. Jury is still out. University High School Academy is the best school in the area by far. My son has always been smart and at the top of his class until he transferred to this school. His grades did drop a bit, but at least I know he is finally learning! The staff and teachers are wonderful and really care about the kids and push them. If you have a child that needs to be challenged, then this is the school for them. The kids must take a test to get into this school, but it is well worth the time and effort. I love this school so much that I sent my daughter to their new 8th grade Preparatory Academy, and we've been just as pleased with that as well. This is one of the best schools in the state! I love the school and the administration. Dean Williams has a great team. I feel like my children are part of a village where failure is not an option. One star this school for sure. This school is absolutely ridiculous, the fact that you have to test to get in even though they just let in the students that failed that test is idiotic. The teachers hate the students and their own jobs making the school day worse for the students. They also go over the lesson plans too fast and expect us to comprehend immediately like we are robots, which we are not. They make it seem like we are all so smart when half of the students are failing. They also continue to lie to the students saying that they'll take us out of the school if we don't keep a 3.0 average but then keep students with a 2.0 and below. They force AP classes down your throat constantly even after you say you don't want it. A teacher dissapeared without anyone saying anything to the students causing a lot of confusion each day and unnecessary work that didn't even match the class they were taking. School by itself can cause a lot of anxiety and depression for students but this school makes it a whole lot worse, ultimately making the students excited to leave even during their second year of attending. First-year here, I've met many good teachers and friends, also feel as if I'm being taught well. I do feel the schol needs to show more emotional support for students and teachers.

A Christian environment with EXCELLENT teachers & staff, EXCELLENT academic program, and EXCELLENT nurturing and support! Thankful for a great four years! Our daughter loved it! Go, FLA!!! I love this school, including all the staff and students in it. The teacher to student ratio is great and allows the teachers to really help you one-on-one. They always make themselves available during lunch or even outside of school hours. The administration really knows the students and like to be involved as much as possible. I recommend this school to anyone who asks. Forest Lake Academy will quickly become your second family. This school does not care about anything but power, money, and rules. The principal and some of administration is extremely sexist, holding girls to a different standard than the boys, and completely different rules for the boys all together. Administration will pretend to listen to you what you have to say, but ultimately never listen to suggestions from parents or the students. Bullying is a huge problem on this campus, and when cases of bullying are brought to administration with several statements and concrete evidence, nothing gets done. Tuition continues to go up, and the money never goes to anything that will benefit the students, it all goes to promoting the school so that they can make even more money. This is the most hypocritical and toxic environment I have ever been in. Please do not waste your money by sending your kids here. FLA is a overpriced school. The first class if your late to it you wont have to pay $5. But it still counts against your 5 tardies for detention. That isn’t fair for parents and students. Parents cannot control how traffic drives. And most teachers are not very merciful about that. I wouldnt really recommend this school to someone. column3: As a former student, I can say that Daniel Boone is a poor school overall and I felt as if I spent years trying to catch up after attending this poorly run institution. Very few of the teachers actually challenge their students; mostly recycled dogma is taught. The school is run based on politics, so if you're not connected, your kids might not always be in the best position to succeed. Teachers will often decide that their personal religion is more important than anything else. Creationism was suggested to be fact when I was there. Overall, it's a relatively backwards place and stands in stark contrast to nearby high schools such as Science Hill (Johnson City), University High (Johnson City), and Dobyns-Bennett. If education is important to you and your child wants to enter college after HS, I would move into the Johnson City or Kingsport city limits and send your kids to either Science Hill or Dobyns-Bennett. Both will prepare your children for college much better than Daniel Boone. (That said, Boones Creek and Gray Elementary Schools are both good --- it all goes downhill once you hit Daniel Boone, unfortunately.) Daniel Boone High School is by far the worst school I have ever had the displeasure of attending. My family has moved all around the country and out of it because of military situations. The only thing i have to say that's good about this school is the ROTC and even that's not perfect. It's clear that this school does not care about any of their students unless you are a star athlete or valedictorian. Also, Northern state schools are stereotypically assumed to have better grade scores. Know why? Because they don't drown their students in homework and crowd tests and quizzes, they don't overcrowd schools and expect people to get along. Pile on responsibilities so high that they need antidepressants by their sophomore year. Do yourself a favour, GO TO A DIFFERENT SCHOOL. You'll thank me later. I go there. The school itself is pretty awful. Teachers didn't really care about teaching you, they just wanted to get TN Ready over with and get you out of their class. column1: This is the absolute worst school I have ever seen. While the teachers are well as doing their jobs, it's the students that are the problem. Some of the students are disruptive, and the teacher doesn't even send them out of the classroom. Sports are too high of a priority at that school. Everywhere you go, that's all anyone can think about. The girls here are extremely shallow and want a guy who plays sports. They don't even seem to care about his personality and I.Q. If you are a nerd who shuns sports and wants a non-disruptive place to learn, this school is NOT for you. Amazing! I am currently going to this school, and I have been all my life... I'm in middle school and being a kid myself I was very happy about how Ocosta handles threats and problems that occur. I feel like its important to feel safe at school, and I always have because they take things seriously. The lunches they serve are good quality, and not overpriced. I recommend this school. Ocosta is a great place to get a quality education. All three of my children graduated with honors and went on to four year universities, where they did very well. Ocosta has caring teachers that go out of their way to help students succeed. The only way not to succeed at this school is to not try or to not attend on a regular basis. This school has positive coaches in athletics and many teams regularly go to state. The knowledge bowl team is one of the most successful in the state with approximately 40% of the students participating. Ocosta School district currently has the worst administration ever at the high school level. The principal should have been fired several times over for misconduct but the school board and superintendent are intimidated by him. This school is in bad shape because of his awful leadership. My family & I are new to the Westport area, and our 13 yr. old son is currently enrolled in the Ocosta Jr./High School, and so far I have been very impressed and amazed with the teachers, and the district. We we're very skeptical at first, with reading some of the older reviews, but to date, as a father I am impressed. As a highschool freshman, I have seen worse schools, however it feels unwelcoming to people who didn't grow up in such a tiny area, much like myself. Only some of the staff care about students while the rest care about last night's game or coaching a sport. It isn't friendly to families that aren't focused on athletics and some both previous and current working staff promoted bad behavior from students.

column3: I do not love this school, in fact it has many fights and arrests. It is, in most classrooms, very unorganized and though we have five princples to oversee teachers, some of them don't teach much. There are almost no rewards for the students who exhibit good behavior at all times, but many rewards for undisciplinary students who show improvement every-so-often. We have broken sinks and weave on our toilets along with ants on the floor and an unbarable stench in the band hallway's bathroom. This school also has enough money to buy new things for our standium, but I have a classroom that isn't even seperated from another with a wall. On the bright side, it is an incredibly diverse school and I get along with mostly everyone. Books, no matter how tattered, go out to everyone with few exceptions of brand new classroom sets. The extracurricular activities offered are phenomenal and as a cheerleader and an active participant in many clubs, I enjoy them very well. They have an extracurricular for anyone with just about any interest, not to mention that they are always looking for new ideas. Academically, we need help, as seen even in our test scores, but extracurriculars are awesome. THIS SCHOOL IS A DISGRACE! If you want truly love your children this is NOT the school for you. One of our sons was beat up on a daily basis. And when our youngest was sent home with blood all over his shirt from being punched in the nose by a fellow student who was jealous he made a sports team, that was it. Of course as the other parents mentioned, the school did nothing to discipline the student who assaulted our sons. I heard the girls are even worse there. Our kids are in cyber school now and we love it! What a shame we had to do this. We never would have if the school even pretended to care. The school seems to has become GHETTO! Honestly the entire school district has become ghetto. Our neighbors have seen a dramatic change over the years. This school is not what it used to be -Which was a very respectable school with morals, values and a great education without bullying and distractions. Do not send your kids here if you LOVE them. Just do not. I didn't like this school. I am an honor student and was bullied constantly. My brothers and sisters and I all are all now in cyber school. This used to be a good school I heard. Now too many fights and it's not easy to concentrate in classes. Very noisy, tons of interruptions and outbursts. Rude obnoxious kids and ghetto mentality. Having look at all the comments, it truly concerns me about the direction the school district is heading towards. I was a student of Thomas Holtzman when he was a teacher. He always empathize respect for one another. This is what we have lost during the last few years since he left the school. We should always remember him and his ideas That means you kids, teenagers, adults, students, teachers,principles, school board members erverybody should help teach the way we were taught to respect one another. I TRULY LOVE THIS SUSQUEHANNA SCHOOL DISTRICT The High School offers application-only art, medical, and engineering schools within its school system. Great opportunity! My daughter is a freshman at the high school and she has excellent teachers who truly care about her and a terrific group of drama-free friends. I can't say enough good things about her gym teacher, Mr. Cook. He's a gem. She's fortunate to be able to take honors classes with students who actually want to learn, so she has not experienced any of the discipline issues that some parents complain about in the district. I honestly believe that most of the behavior issues stem from kids whose parents aren't involved in their lives. People want to blame all of the problems on the administration, but in my opinion, the problems start at home. My children know that my husband and I have high expectations for them and they behave accordingly. The best schools have involved parents who actually care about their children's education. End of story. I just graduated and honestly the faculty could care less. The teachers don't really seem to care whether a student learns or not. I didn't really learn anything the past four years. I had a horrible high school experience here. The teachers are engaged and supportive. It's like anything else. If the student puts forth the effort, they will gain it back in the return. I am a graduate of STHS. My time there was enjoyable and fulfilling. There are plenty of Athletic and Academic options to choose from as a student. I felt STHS did a good job in my overall preparation for college.

column1: I know this school as a grandparent and attend many of the events.There is tremendous community support and involvement. The school has wonderful spirit and involvement among the teachers, students and parents.My grandson just graduated and went into college and my grandaughter is a high honor student,hoping to go to Cornell. This school closely supports and cares about every student. I've been around this school for a while and it is the center of the community. We are very involved and watch closely over things. I hate to see how teh management is lettng it get worse and worse every year! And now they talk of consolidation with Ithaca district. Why do they want to throw out our school? The strengths of this school are its small size, involved community & parents, & staff/faculty that care. A new principal has raised the bar for the students academically, behaviorally, & increased pride & self respect. Weaknesses are that it being a small district somewhat limits some of the available elective courses. For example, no German, etc. The school district has, however, partnered with local colleges to get high school students college courses while in HS. Regarding the comment made by another about consolidation of districts. This is not an interest of the Newfield district but rather something the State Ed department is exploring for all its rural districts as a way of cutting costs. In my opinion, there's little chance of this happening unless there is significant change in the community's desire to remain independent. I would like to know more specifics regarding the comment that the management lets things get "worse and worse every year." By several measures, things are improving educationally. I do know of some grumblings because of recent changes encouraging the students to achieve their best -- sometimes changes take some time getting used to. Overall, I loved going here. I was there from second grade on, graduated 2014. Although changes have been made since my graduation.

column1: I graduated from Mayo. While there, I was involved in several extra-curricular activities both at Mayo and at my home school, and even worked part time my junior and senior years. All while maintaining a great life at home. I feel that Mayo was and is a great school, with amazing teachers and staff. Yes much is require of the students but it is not excessive. The school prepares the students for college life. I was able to attend a competitive college thanks to Mayo, and I was able to be successful and graduate on time, thanks to the 4 years I had at Mayo. It is an option to attend Mayo. It is not for everyone, but if your child can handle Mayo, they will be prepared for college and life. Very diverse and focused on discipline, studies and teamwork. The teachers work very closely with the students. My niece just graduated from Mayo and she became prepared for college receiving scholarship monies that has allowed her to attend Francis Marion College. She has express her wish to become a RN and Because of her knowledge, skill and guidance from Mayo, she will reach her goals. Go Mayo!

column3: Although people may think SRHS is nothing without Artquest, we have an outstanding amount of teachers who strive to bring many different types of knowledge to their students. Our teachers take pride in the school's rich history and maintain a museum in the main building that archives all of the amazing students that have graduated. The foundation raises thousands so students can have everything they need for a great education and the programs involve a lot of support from parents, the community, and teachers. SRHS has a record low amount of violence and a lot of diversity among students. The reason so many students come from outside of the district is they want to feel a part of a group, and not an outsider. We are bonded together by the pride we have for our school and anyone who is lucky enough to squeeze in on the transfer list will soon find out why. My son has been a student at SRHS since his freshman year. In the past 3 and ahalf years, he has had some of the best experiences in his young life. I transitioned him from private schools, and was worried about how well he would do in public school. With excellent teachers and sports programs he has truly excelled. In his senior year he joined choir and had a chance to experience a small part of the Art Quest program which is really impressive. From the teachers, staff,and coaches to the curriculum SRHS truly offers an experience to kids. I am a current student at Santa Rosa High School and this is my first year and I could not be happier. I am happy to go to school because of this school. For the first time in my life I'm not dreading Mondays or counting down the days to summer starting in august. To be honest, I can't say a bad thing about this school. Students are created equal from the staff and more importantly the other students. I have never witnessed an act of bullying and have not heard of any. There's no "popular kids" or "geeks." Everyone gets along. I think part of this reason is that the school is so diverse and has the ArtQuest program. Kids are literally taught to be themselves. Aside from artquest, we have the FFA program. I am not apart of either. A lot of people are scared to come here because "they aren't artsy." I am the least creative person you will ever meet and I fit in fine. This schools spirit and leadership amazes me. In my opinion, sending your kid to any other school like Carrillo or Newman is an awful decision. My son is an 8th grader who's decided to attend Santa Rosa High in the Artquest program in the fall. I've been spending a lot of time on campus lately, attending the school's 140th anniversary celebration, various Artquest showcases, school play, class selection night. My wife has joined the Student Teacher Parent group. So far our experiences have been extremely positive. Office staff have been courteous and helpful. The teachers seem intelligent, competent, helpful, and engaged. The campus is gorgeous. Obviously we' have a lot to learn about this school, but so far everything we've seen seems extremely positive. I am a parent with a student in the Art Quest program. We don't live in the district. So it was a big decision to go here. But I have been very pleased with this school. The rest of her classes have been very good. The teachers are good. I am happy with our decision to attend SRHS. I dunno, is mah first year here, last year I went to piner high ;-; (which was meh) Great school spirits, the kids who go here are super nice. I loved going to SRHS and the teachers were amazing there.

column1: I felt like it was a constant struggle to take courses that fit my academic need. I can't say enough about Munford High school. They care about the students every way and do everything they possibly can to help them succeed. Parents are highly involved and I feel that the communication makes that difference. The school is dirty and smells musty. It is run down and old. It really should be torn to the ground and rebuilt. You can also smell the farm animals inside the halls and classrooms. My daughter did not enjoy her time at the school the few months that she was enrolled. As a new student, she felt quite unwelcome by some of the teachers and the students. My younger daughter will not be attending here. The only thing this school has going for them is the band. Reconsider sending your child here.

High student to teacher ratio Increasing drug use on campus Poor preparation for college Student to teacher ratio is high Limited diversity and teacher access I am a student at RMHS and i love it! They have amazing teachers and students. They are lacking a bit though. They lack teacher assistance which is needed for many students. They will help you if you need help but you have to find the teachers, they don't find you. Overall, I highly recommend RMHS for you or your kids. Rocky is a great school. In our district this year 2 of the 4 seniors with perfect ACT scores were lobos. Honestly, I don't know what that parent was talking about, there is really not that much drug use at out school. I mean, it is a high school and some students try that stuff, but that happens at any high school. I think it is funny that people dislike having to find teachers to get help. I think it is really benificial, because out professors in college wont track us down. The thing I will warn of is that our schedule can be rigurious, but that is only if you don't pay attention to what classes you sign up for. Over all, I love my school. My mom has been thinking about moving nearer to Pouder High School, and I refuse to even consider moving. No way, once a Lobo, always a Lobo! The staff and students are the best individuals in Fort Collins, Northern Colorado, and maybe even all of Colorado. As of this moment I am a senior graduating in 2 days and am shocked to see the place I love receiving such a poor rating from those who know nothing about it. We have some of the best athletic, science, language, business, music, art, social studies, departments in the state. Never have I ever met more students who actually say, "I love Rocky". Never a stranger to progress, this school has the most diverse body of students, and a true atmosphere of inclusion. I am a Spanish speaker and a minority, yet I never felt like an outcast at Rocky. Something many of my friends attending other schools in town have had to face. From the bottom of my heart I can say that I love my school, I love my teachers. The memories Rocky made and fosters are innumerable and it is the best damn High School in Colorado... As a parent of a sophomore here I couldn’t be more impressed with the culture and education my child is receiving. She has grown and matured through the guidance and support of the staff and teachers. The teachers have always been honest, helpful and communicative about where my child is and how to support her. Very positive overall. Lots of support available from teachers, counselors, staff. Mike Ruffner and his sidekick Amy the registrar, are uncaring and clueless when it comes to helping a child in need at that school. As a student graduated from Rocky I could not compare the enrichment I experienced. Out of all surrounding poudre school district high schools rocky hands down the best school you can send your child. Rocky is top of school of choice for many parents/students outside of rockys neighborhoods. Students are only required the balance 4 classes a semester. Allowing your child to truly learn and immerse themselves into their studies. Many students requesting rocky as their school are turned away. So being within rocky’s “neighborhoods”Will not only guaranteed your child a seat within rockys walls as well as a great educational experience. Rockys accepting walls greet kids for all backgrounds, race, creed and religion are welcomed. Plus an amazing disabled student acceptances. I thought the rating for equity on this school was WAY off. Rocky has one of the best, most-inclusive cultures in the city. This school and it's principal go out of their way to establish a culture of fun school spirit, teamwork and a real sense of togetherness. The school is part of one of the best school districts in the state. Lots of support for well-being and mental health have been added over the pat few years. The teaching staff is friendly, supportive and really try to communicate and engage with parents on many levels.This high school is one of the smaller ones on town (2,000 students) but the school pride here is really strong, which starts with reaching out to the middle schools that feed into the high school with a field trip day to the high school in late spring. Mentors are paired with the 8th graders so they have an older peer to connect with and ask questions to so they can transition easier. Regular school assemblies, fun spirit weeks and a collective feeling of "we're in this together" approach really create a bond between the staff and students. My son missed his freshman year in-person due to the pandemic but the school still found ways to welcome all the 9th graders and keep them connected with drive-thru welcome trains, in-person support for students that just needed that format to learn best, learning cohorts and more. Lots of students in this town vie to go to this high school but often, there are not many spots available for opting into the school from other neighborhoods because all of the neighborhood kids don't stray to other schools often. Good high school , the best one in FOCO

Don't listen to all the horrible completely untrrue rumors. The teachers have the students’ best interest at heart, and with the smaller school population, a student can readily receive help if needed. The students at Warren work hard, want to learn, and show respect to the teachers and staff. Warren School is a great district for students to learn and grow up in.

column3: Tolman High School is just an average school. Some say they have their best years of their live at highschool, but I don't see how teens can do this at Tolman. The teachers aren't as good as they could be and the students don't really want to learn. Plus, Tolman is undergoing both a schedule change and a Portfolio, which completely kills the consept of highschool. Tolman is nothing like it used to be. As a student from Tolman High School, I can say from experience that if it wasn't for attending this high school I wouldn't be who I am today. Because of Tolman, I got to network and meet leaders in Rhode Island Criminal Justice System. Tolman gave me an internship in which I could of never imagined would make an ever lasting connection. Now I am in my Junior year of College studying law and proceeding to go to Law School after I graduate. Tolman is a very diverse school, and because of that I learned to communicate and work with other people of different races. Of course like many know, Tolman does have bad apples and people who don't care about their education. However, in my years at Tolman, every teacher motivated me and pushed me to my limits. The portfolio gave me a way to display my hardwork but also it prepared me for the workforce. I know that some students that graduated in 2010 with me can say the same. I have been asked to go back to Tolman and speak to the students about my experience and what doors it opened up for me. If any one does have any questions, email me. I'll tell you the truth.

column1: There are things in every school that need to be worked on and adjusted. Speaking from a student stand point. This school tries its best to work as a team. At some points it is not as successful as it could be, but it is a pretty decent school; the less you complain the quicker you will get over it. Franklin is a small school with a great approach to discipline. There are very strong leaders in this school's administration. The students are kept very involved with field trips and community involvement. Excellence is expected. Amazing School. Teachers are amazing and so nice. The students there are so kind and smart also.

column3: The school taught some disturbingly inaccurate information at times. For example, they tried to tell me that The Civil War had nothing to do with slavery (which, of course, isn't true). While I was there, I also had to endure an abstinence based sex education program that wasn't entirely accurate (example: they tried to say that if you slept with one person that had slept with someone that had slept with someone that had slept with someone with an STI that you all had that STI. That's not necessarily true, and it's reductive). My English teachers had ethnocentric viewpoints about the supposedly "One right way to write an essay" (which is NOT done in other cultures). My English teachers also had assignments with premises that didn't make sense. For example, they'd say something like, "Using this fictional novel, prove that love conquers evil." I wanted to write in my essay that I'd never use a fictional novel to prove anything about the world we live in other than that writers write books with the theme of love conquering evil, but I'm sure I would have failed my class if I actually demonstrated that kind of intelligence. They also did a poor job considering socio-economic considerations (example: praising a student that wore a suit to do a presentation and not really caring that not everyone had the funds to spend on a suit). I also came from a family that didn't own a TV, and I was sometimes assigned to watch things on the news despite the fact that I didn't have a TV. As someone that was raised an atheist, I sadly encountered a lot of religious intolerance there (the teachers said some REALLY INAPPROPRIATE things to me). Also, the general culture of that school was really terrible (a lot of people that weren't very progressive in their thinking, people not being considerate of the ways serious brain dysfunction can hinder your life opportunities, a lack of awareness of privilege). As someone with a Connective Tissue Disorder, I also feel that the gym teachers really didn't have training on such things, and I was asked to perform tasks that weren't healthy for my body. I also am an incredibly intelligent individual, but I have processing disorders, and I really could have used certain modifications...I think my general review of the school is that while a lot of schools have some of the problems I mention here, VVS most likely was just a little bit worse in some of these regards that other places.

column1: This school is horrible now. I am here for my ninth grade year. The students are rowdy. The administration treats everyone like inmates and never lets anyone do anything. The teachers act like they don't care about what happens to you or your future. The test scores are atrocious and it seems like many of the freshmen are failing i was at jd for ninth grade now finna be a sophomore but i only give this school a three because it wasnt so bad but not all that good either but hey we cant let the rotten apples spoil everything because this school was once a good school and it aint the only bad school either but we currently finna have a new principal so things proably get better or worse. #sophomore This school should be closed down. The teachers teach directly from the book and have no idea what they're doing. Worst school in the county. Teachers, asst principals, and the principal do not have the interest of the students at heart. Their main agenda is to suspend; for everything. If you can afford a private school or have the ability to homeschool please RUN, not walk from this place!!! I have to say, my time at JD was very interesting. I started in 2009 as a sophomore to 2012 as a senior. I've had some great classes, and I've had some terrible classes. Honestly, it really depends on what kind of teacher you have. I've had teachers that just gave us busy work and then I've had teachers who really want you to learn and prepare you for college and life. The administration constantly changed, which made the school unstable. I feel like the school could get a better reputation if it had a stable, long time principal and if the teachers there would collectively be proactive in the student's education. Yes, some of the students are unruly, but that honestly does not affect how you could learn at JD. As long as the student is diligent in their work, they should succeed just fine. The only thing I would want to see from JD is more resources for students like having career fairs and more tutoring offered for struggling students. What do you expect given the lack of quality of students and teachers?
