column3: If you have money and would not like to be in a diversity area, this school is for you. The school only cares if the parents have money - if you are a single parent, they wouldn't stand up for your kids. . Finsihing up the year with my daughter, a senior and delighted that we chose our neighborhood school over the variety of choices - prep schools, charter, private etc. The teachers are dedicated and energetic, and she learned critical thinking in science and english, history was awesome too. Could list her favorite teachers, but more important we didn't encounter any problems and communication was better than expected at this large school. Variety of activities so lots of opportunities to find a smaller niche. It helped that she was in Honors & AP classes, perhaps, but we saw tremendous parent involvement and teacher committment at all levels. Need more counselors and more money and focus in Arizona for public education, but we have no regrets. Great school, amazing neighborhood, especially if you get involved. I have one senior and one freshman this year. Corona is a fabulous school...from the faculty to the kids, I couldn't have asked for a better environment for my eldest. My freshman was identified as gifted and was registered at the Peggy Payne Academy but begged to go here because of his brother's experience, as difficult as a decision it was to make, we withdrew him and placed him in Corona w/ Honors classes. The music program is outstanding and I have no words for how much these teachers truly care about their students! The after hour time the faculty commits is astonishing and not common these days. If you're looking for a school that has a good balance between teaching independence and allowing for heavy parental involvement - Corona is the place for you. Just make sure your child is active in clubs or extra curricular activities....they will thrive! not good it has a loud libery it's quiet when someone inspects the school and they smoke in school everyday PRESCHOOL Review: This review is only for the preschool that is offered at this school, not the high school. This preschool is cheap! However, you get what you pay for. My daughter went to this school for a little over a year. The director told my child that if she did not follow directions "that Santa would not bring her any presents." I couldn't believe it! The assistant director (aka an adult) told me this was said. Not my child. Also, the directors give preferential treatment to students whose parents work at this school. Don't expect fair treatment here. I am a teacher and did not feel that my child was treated in a professional manner. I love that the children get to work with high schoolers, but couldn't be more disappointed in the leadership. Additionally, they serve so much sugary snacks to the children, it is ridiculous. Graham crackers covered in frosting are the norm. This school was the worst high school experience a student could ask for. Drugs are rampant in the school and the students are horrible, not just to each other but even to the teachers. I have not been very impressed with the majority of the teachers. Not to mention, the administration is not very organized or very helpful. In fact, they are rather rude and could care less about individuals. Also, it takes almost twenty minutes to get signed out of school because most of the time they just sit behind their desk doing nothing. Corona is AWFUL. I could be sitting in class and I'll just see smoke coming from the back of the room because there are kids smoking back there!! And the teacher doesn't even care! Some of the teachers are great but overall, it isn't worth it. Maybe you'll get a good teacher, bust mostly, you won't. Not to mention the cliques! You can't turn anywhere without seeing a group making fun of a kid by himself. If you're thinking of Corona, don't. You'll just be miserable the entire time. My son is just began his junior year at Corona Del Sol. Corona has been a terrific place for him to learn and grow. The academics have been tough and the music program has been excellent. There is something for everyone here. He has participated in after school clubs and feels a huge loyalty to Corona. The team sports after school have also given him a strong sense of self. High school years can be very rough on kids and although my son can be a bit of a loner, he continues to say he enjoys school and that Corona is the best. I couldn't ask for anything more. My son is a Freshman at Corona Del Sol and I couldn't be happier with his progress. He enjoys high school. The music program is outstanding. The teachers and faculty are excellent and keep you apprised of your child's progress. My son is actually learning and told me himself he likes that they treat him as an individual and not like he is being baby sat. He finds the curriculum challenging. There are a variety of after school clubs that corona offers which is great. I couldn't be happier with the quality and standards Corona Del Sol has to offer. Awesome school! My son is a Freshman at Corona Del Sol. We were lucky to go him in through open enrollment because our assigned Dobson High School is just awful, filled with gangs and troublemakers. So far, my son's year at Corona has been peaceful and enriching. The kids at the school really treat each other well and have a strong sense of school pride. The academics at the school are excellent. The music program is amazing-my son is taking the one of a kind steel drum class that they offer. There are many opportunities for clubs and sports. Most importantly, my son feels very safe. Sending him to Corona Del Sol is one of the best decisions I have made as a parent. I am a current Senior at CDS and I love my school. Corona Del Sol is one of the best schools there is. If you are considering any other schools choose Corona. You won't regret it. The teachers are cool and there are many clubs and activities students can get involved in. Yes this is another typical high school that has cliques, but each class gets along with each other. Our school has the best student sections and were one big family. The Tribe is what we call ourselves and the name says it all. We are proud and LOVE to show our school spirit so that everyone knows. There are many wonderful things about Corona Del Sol and I'm glad I've met all the people i have. Corona has given me the best high school experience ever. GO AZTECS! The school resources and facilities are good, and there are some good teachers. However, there are also many teachers who seem disinclined to teach at the slightest excuse, and some who simply use the classroom as a political indoctrination camp for the unfortunate students. I will refrain from posting detailed examples since none of it was ever captured in any syllabus or take-home material; suffice it to say I spent many, many hours over multiple years re-teaching my child what should have been taught in several classes, and un-teaching the radical environmentalism, radical feminism, loose morals, hatred of Christianity, and anti-Americanism taught as "facts" in those classes. Corona del Sol has fantastic academic programs and excellent music programs! Principal Brent Brown provides thoughtful leadership and is very supportive of academic and arts programs. The school offers students the opportunity to be well prepared for university work. My older son was a National Merit Scholar and received multiple academic scholarship offers. My younger son is involved in Marching Band, Steel Drum band, and arts programs. Ms. Reed and Mr. Wanta are excellent math teachers and their students do very well on AP exams. Ms. Blechacz, Mr. Doyle, and Mr. Morgan are outstanding teachers and their students get excellent AP test scores. Ms. Johnson and Ms. Gile are fantastic English teachers. Mr. Duplessis and Mr. Werner lead the Marching band, which is 190 students strong in 2015-2016. They are exceptionally talented leaders who know how to motivate and inspire teenagers. Mr. Werner also leads the Corona del Sol Steel Drum Band--the largest in Arizona.Corona del Sol is large enough to provide a wide variety of opportunities to students. However, the individual programs are excellent and provide a small community feel.I highly recommend, without any reservations, Corona del Sol high school! Given it's size (about 2500). You can expect the same level of teacher involvement as you would a small community college...that means the squeaky wheel gets the grease... I’m only a junior, but in my two completed years here, I always feel prepared and eager to learn. The friendships I’ve made will no doubt carry into adulthood and the bonds I’ve made with each of my teachers are unforgettable. Anyone who considers coming to Corona will always get the same response from me: Corona is an amazing place to experience all the high school glory, and I’m so glad I get to spend my days here. The key to experiencing these wonderful memories is putting yourself out there. Kids who sit in the back, hardly ever pay attention, and aren’t involved in any extracurriculars are obviously not going to share the same experiences. Also, part of feeling success in school is challenging yourself. Taking honors classes was the best choice of my life. The kids are more involved, push each other to do better, strive for success, and build on each other through common goals and constructive criticism. The school used to be good. Then from the district to the school level, the administration got a shake up. The results? Good teachers left in droves and it is very difficult for students to pursue extracurricular activities. The most ridiculous reason I heard was that some activities are too expensive for the low income kids, thus, no one should attend even if there is no low income kids on the team. My older one went through Kyrene from elementary to high school. We were happy till that point and I was planning to send my little one to the same schools. After than, no way. Now my little one is a happy kid at Brophy instead. as a student here, its an ok school. its big, almost 3000 students, and the hallways are busy. classes are challenging if you're in honors, teachers are good for the most part, clubs are cool, sports teams are good. if you're looking for a standard high school, this is a good school, but if your kid needs more one on one teacher attention, choose a different school.

column1: This is a Great School. Academically it puts you on track. My son graduated last year and is doing very well with the academic adjustment from high school to college. He is at a very good 4 yr college and did exceptional his first semester. That does not always happen.. 3.5... I have a daughter there now who is on track for college. the teachers I believe have a lot on them. This school has over 3000 students. However, parents .. reach out to them on e-mail and they bend over backwards to address anything your child needs or any concerns. Also, I have told my child to be active in her education. ... To ask the teacher if you need something. They have 100s of students. If you need something or even help.. just speak up and ask!!. ... Great extra curricular activities and school support of them. not just football either...lol I have two children at Grayson, a freshman and a senior. My daughter is an excellent student and is the top 5% of her class. The school has had 4 months since she was accepted to an internship, but still does not know where they are going place her. They are also dropping classes that focus on science (i.e. biotechnology and AP chemistry). Please don t get me started on the uniformed counselors who only seem interested in the path that requires the least amount of work. My son just started and all is not well. There are 35 students in his gifted math class! His teacher in his foreign language class has no classroom management skills so students play their ipods on deaf and sleep during class. A major irritant is that although he has no handicap tag, the principal always parks his huge truck in the handicapped spaces. I feel that Grayson has declined with each year. I would no longer recommend this school. We moved to Georgia last year. So far, I'm moderately impressed with Grayson HS. My child was lucky to find four very dedicated teachers last year, however, it seems like we've encountered either excellent or poor teachers with not a lot falling in the middle. The math dept. seems to have more than its fair share of teachers who are not well-trained in thier subject. One teacher in the foreign language dept. actually "helped" the students by hinting at answers while they were taking a final. Students might have scored well, but what did they learn? On the positive side, I am pleased that there is a zero tolerance for bullying and poor behavior. This is our first year at GHS...my daughter is a freshman. A few things that I dislike: the school is HUGE, very crowded halls, big classes, approximately 650 students in cafeteria during each lunch period, lots of trailers in back. My daughter's gifted classes have up to 35 kids in there, her AP class has what seems like 40! Things that I like: my daughter has some fabulous teachers (a couple are just average), the APs work really hard to keep all the kids in line, the school seems to be very clean or at least the areas I've seen. I'm not overly impressed with GHS so far, but to be a large metro public high school it's about what one would expect. I do feel from talking with other parents of older students the school has declined some in recent years. One of the best school and good. Teachers very help full teachers. With math physics language art ,Spanish and up keeping spirit. Is miss Balley. Thank you I have a son that is currently a freshman and we absolutely love this school! I am extremely pleased with the JROTC program and the path that they are working on with my son. He takes great pride in attending Grayson and has requested to finish his high school career @ Grayson High School. Starting off as a 9th grader, in marching band has made it a fantastic year. 10th grade will even be greater. Your strength is in your character.Aim High, you will Succeed. Strong leadership and hard working teachers. Great extra-curricular opportunities are available. Would highly recommend this school and this community. Excellent administration and many opportunities for students to be involved in their school outside of academics. Grayson is a great school and the extra curricular activities are great. The academics are also good. My son is a 10th grader, we transferred from South Gwinnett. I can honestly say that he was really behind when he arrived. The teachers and counselors at Grayson were excellent. He was provided all available resources to help him catch up and maintain a B grade. I cant thank Grayson enough. Academically doesn't compete with north Gwinnett schools. With 2 students currently at Grayson, we have had good experiences and look forward to more years of the same. Excellent Faculty and students are top notch. great and awesome it was a great experience. Don't let your child do football here. The head coach tells parents that he won't discuss playing time with your children. If you complain about anything your child is punished. They won't play at all. The Assistant Principal tells you he hired the Coach to win games. He doesn't care how not touching the field at all affects these boys as long as they win. They will use the same boys over and over again until they get hurt. Once they come back he doesn't use them again unless they were one of his star players. You can't meet with position coaches. They charge $1200 for program. And don't even let your child get safe equipment. All his Coaches left last year wonder why. They want yes sir folks. They don't develop players. He would be exposed if he didn't have great athletes already. He talks down to the boys. They're only one team when they have to do up and downs. He divides them up all the time. It's a lot of racial issues at this school. It won't never change. Run!! I always thought that high school would be difficult for my son, but I love this school, daily I ask my son and he is happy there

column1: I love Matoaca High! I move here at the end of my Sophomore year from Florida and all I can say is that this was a great experience! its nothing like I had back home. The students and faculty are very welcoming and the student population is greatly diverse. The courses set for each student is challenging based upon their needs and what they can handle, however the teachers do like to make it challenging at time to make sure that we are paying attention. all I can Say is that I LOVE IT Love this school has great opportunities and great programs to offer your children with lots of sporting activities to choose from. column3: I have recently moved because of this school they completely isolated my child just because he was asking to many questions. As a result he failed all of his tests. I would definetly not send my child here. I informed the principal but he did absolutely nothing. This school has a wide range of electives to choose from. They have a strong sports team, science olympiad and incredible musical program. The school is not overpopulated like some in the area, and the teachers stay in touch. The counselors help students with everything they may need and there are many opportunities for all types of clubs for every kind of kid. You can't get lost in the building, it's well staffed and classes are anywhere to 10-25 a class. They offer Chinese! They also offer an engineering program through RIT with credit (starting in 9th grade). My child enjoys the school, the friends they've made and the teachers. Parent involvement is incredible! Our principal had won awards with his leadership. This place is a nice little secret, and I call it our private school! Teachers and staff are deeply committed to students, and the curriculum includes great elective offerings. Jamesville DeWitt High School has offered me opportunities that I don't think many other area public schools offer. I have been involved in many of the schools well run clubs and have seen the vast majority of my teachers be professionals who both have a passion for their classes and a gift for educating. Furthermore, the counselers are incredibly committed to their students and have the time and patience to work with student schedules and the college application process. On a more practical note, I have really enjoyed the block scheduling system. I feel that it giveshould teachers more time to teach interesting material and allows for less of an emphasis on formulaic curriculum. Amazing the one of the only public schools that offer Chinese as a second language elective!

column1: Kinnelon High School does a great job of encouraging ALL students to be involved in extracurricular activities. I rate KHS as top notch! The ONLY thing that drives decisions by the administration at Kinnelon is how they will fall in the NJ Monthly High School Ranking. The prinicipal and superintendent are puppets to the parents, many of whom treat the teachers like their personal servants or dirt under their fingernails. It is very common to see administrators screaming at each other or at teachers in full view of the students. The day after back-to school-night is like D-day at this school because of the hundreds of phone calls that come in complaining about this or that. It is also very common for parents to call the teachers names like "idiot" or "moron" if they do not concede to allow their offspring to retake a failed test. Teachers are seen more as a hurdle to getting the A's that the student needs on his transcript than as any sort of respected figure who imparts knowledge. They allow almost anyone into AP courses to boost their rankings, and the grades are severely inflated because of the absolute pressure coming in from the community. As a result, the teachers are stifled and henpecked. They are constantly on the defensive, rather than being encouraged to be creative in the classroom. My brother had went to this school and he had a GREAT time! I could see, compared to his other school he had went to, he loved going to this school everyday, because the teachers would actually TEACH, the principle was nice and nice to everyone too, even me myself! He says he had lots of friends there and he had a PERFECT time, so I am writing this review for him. I have decided, all on my own that when I get out of middle school, I will go to this high school because my brother had went to this high school, and the teachers had taught him very well considering that now he goes to Harvard University. I am very amazed and impressed at this school, seeing how it has academics AND the arts and very good programs. I'm a big singer myself, I love singing, I am currently in this singing group at my current school, but Kinnelon seems so cool and I would really like to join the community! I hope they would let me sing also ^_^! Because I would be glad to attend every class, I can see myself from now and see my future self at Kinnelon. I'm a 1982 graduate now living in South Jersey. Loved the school! My sons now vs the Kinnelon Colts in Lacrosse! So cool!! Lol outstanding teachers who know every student by name, strong music : performing arts program (very popular), rigirous academics, heavy focus on preparing for post secondary education....lots of fat envelopes from top tier colleges and universities including Harvard, Yale, Princeton, NYU, Georgetown, Emory, Duke, UNC, etc..

column3: silverton high school is awesome!!! The school is not that big but i like it because we always have fun, and theres a lot of sports. The teachers are awesome, they always help you with your work and if you need help their always there for you... It was overall terrible. The food is filled with chems and is very low quality. The arts are shunned and ignored by the school, and has a racist core within. Sure the sports are great, but that is because more funding goes into that than education itself.

column1: The school's academics offered here is just too easy. Almost all the students here get all 90's and etc. If you are gifted and smart, please do not waste your time here, there are so many other schools, including public schools like NY LAB or Beacon HS that offer way better programs then this school. No diversity, all students are either African American or Latino. A good school needs to be challenging, diverse, and a safe environment. There are no connections at this school with universities and hospitals in the area. No Orchestra and few extra curriculum other than Step, and etc. I would only consider this school if you are a average student or have potential to become a good student to come here and become successful, but for smart and gifted students, don't bother applying. The curriculum is so easy. For students who want diversity, this isn't the school you want to go to. I have a sister who attended the University Program offered by the school for the incoming students and barely 3/4 of the students knew how to divide fractions or know their basic skills in order to succeed. Bad school for Gifted Students. Great school for averaged students who have potential. There was a parent's comment on the school lack of academic rigor. All NYC schools must follow NYS curriculum regardless if it is private. There are advanced classes just as a regular public school would have. If your child is up to speed they can be in those classes. It is a great learning environment. I am definitely not regretting sending my daughter to this school. This review is in response to the review dated on 8/2/12 - SJB has plenty of extra curricular activities/clubs to join. This school is a perfect school for girls to mold them into responsible, ambitious young women. I do not regret enrolling my child in this school. It is by far a school for slackers. It is challenging, a great school for school for gifted students and located in the UES (E. 77th St) - a safe area in my standards for my child. This school is great academically but in the sense of the students it is not that great. The school used to be very well known for its high grades but now it's known for its drama with other schools and with he other girls in the school. St. Jean Baptiste is a awesome academically challenging school. The girls are sophisticated and focused. The school has strong connections with internships ranging in the medical field , law, art, and engineering. The students help one another and support each other and the teachers are supportive and always there to help. Homely Environment ! Excellent. Teachers not only high quality academics, but also strong traditional values that will help you along your road through life. My daughter graduated in 2017. She was hesitant to attend an all girls school but in retrospect saw the value of an all girl Catholic school education. She was able to get SAT prep free of charge and was able to volunteer and make it to her first choice college and get a scholarship. She was able to play on the soccer team and Chutney dance. The schools location on the Upper East Side in proximity to Central Park is also an attribute. The school is wonderfully maintained and has nice bright rooms and a spacious cafeteria with a court yard.

column3: Run, run as fast as you can! I have two children currently attending this high school. The achadimics are substandered and the teachers abilities to teach are worse. I don't feel that my children's needs are being met. I know my children are not going to be able to advance to a continued education or trade school if they continue here. IEP's were not followed all year, we will have to take online programs to reclaim lost credits. Teachers are hired to be coaches but the athletics suck! We are seeking a variance to attend Mead. The commute will be worth it. Terrible, It is honestly horrible especially the lying bastard that is known as the "principal" I have no clue if everything I wrote out is going to go through but in conclusion everything I wrote can be translated to please don't put your kids in this school, try valley's Padeia school or heck even homeschool. As long as the secretary works at this school, DO NOT, I repeat do not put your children in this school. She discriminates, laughs in your face when you try to talk, and doesn’t have any customer service skills at all. Spoke to other parents around here and they tell me the same exact thing about her. It’s sad to see someone like that work in a school around children. None of my children will ever go to that school. They have had a better experience in Spokane than they ever have at one of these schools! Once my kids are done at Gess, they will immediately be home schooled or moved to a different school. I refuse to put my children in such a toxic and unhealthy school. I've been to 9 schools over the course of my life. I could name everyone and what I hated and what I loved them for. But this? This is by far the only school I've been to where I can't even say anything positive about it. As a rural school you shouldn't have high expectations, and trust me I didn't. But my god in heaven this was by far one of the worse experiences i've had since 3rd grade at Spokane Christian Academy. Immature students, disrespectful staff and a principal who could care less about you. I was severely bullied and I still am at this school. Last year it was pictures of my face being posted without my consent onto Instagram, this year, it's discrimination and degradation for who I am as a person. It is downright ridiculous that i'm being put through this and no one seems to even care. Honestly, this school ain’t bad for the rural experience. The other reviewers were calling out mr Anderson, who is a great principal that is really trying to do his best. As for the academics, they offer College in the Classroom and Running Start, so I am going to graduate high school with an AA degree. All in all, Jenkins really is a good small-town school with lots of wonderful people.Go Cougs!

column1: Santa Susana High is school is Incredible. The support from our teachers and staff is awesome! Majority of our teachers offer tutoring after school. I am an involved parent and have been welcomed in all departments. If you want to be involved log on to: http://www.santasusana.org/parents/organizations/ and make contact, we will show you the way. Our PTSA supports our school events, teachers/staff, and students. Boosters supports all the departments that focus in the Arts. Our Leadership Class supports all departments. All academies have their own committees and do a lot of fund raising on their own. Students at SSHS do not judge or stress about what you are wearing or who your friends are. Everyone is focused. They all know who they are and what they want out of life. My oldest son certified with honors in 2 Academies, Visual Arts with and Major in Animation and Computer Programming. My second son, a Junior; will certify in Music, Law, & Academics. The school has so much to offer, you just have to take advantage of it. I made a mistake in my last review and can't figure out how to edit it! The music teacher does not have a Masters Degree, she has a PHD in Conducting. This school started out really impressive but then turned out to be a disappointment. My son went to Santa Su for 4 years and had 3 different principals. I must say the first two were really good (especially the 2nd) but the the third and last principal was big mistake on the school districts part. She does not communicate with the parents well and is very defensive on most issues that you might have. The school really went down hill in the last year. There are a lot of really good teachers there but dealing with the administration is not only painful for the parents but the students as well. We could not get any help with our questions regarding college from the counselor and when I went to the principal for help she was very nasty and told me to stop bothering teachers and counselors. I am very grateful to the help of an outside college counselor that I had to hire for the proper guidance and that my son is finally done with that school. I have another child at Simi High. I can say enough good things about that school. My son just finished his first semester as a Freshman at Santa Susana Highschool. I would highly recommend NOT to send your child there. First of all the campus is completely open and with very little security. There is no supervision in the locker rooms or cameras in case something happens. My son was the victim of a bully who tried choking him to death over two dollars! Luckily my son got free and defended himself. The incident did not change a thing. We tried to move on from this but academically my son began to struggle. I tried to get support from the administrative staff which took a very long time for a response. This school is a regular public school with not much support for the teachers who seem overwhelmed and if a student is in need it is ignored. My son will be going to a charter school in January. I couldn't say it better than the parent who wrote the August 2014 review. Our experience would resemble theirs almost exactly. Any parent hearing the hype and clamor about Santa Susana High School should consider that the school really is going downhill and not administered in a competent or comprehensive way. A large High School (like Royal) with many resources and an experienced and responsive staff could easily council and direct a gifted or remedial learner to have an optimum education. My daughter is a sophomore at Santa Su. She is excelling academically and could not be happier with the opportunities afforded her at this great school. No other school in Simi Valley offers an extended school day so that she may fit in her love for theater, dance and choir into her required academic class schedule. She intends to add AP classes and participate in the school's award winning Mock Trial program next year. This school is shaping her into a very well rounded student and young lady. We are very pleased. Santa Susana HighSchool is a great school with caring teachers and staff. They focus on advanced academics, the arts and technology. Their students are are recognized outstanding academics (many AP classes to choose) and career education. They have French, German, & Spanish languages and have an internationally competing Mock Trial team. Their model programs are also in graphics, film, stagecraft, fine arts, robotics, theater, musical theater, vocal & instrumental music, & dance. Students often use mobile devices in their classes and teachers post their gradebooks online. SO DISAPPOINTED!!!! We heard so many great things about this school prior to coming here. Our kids just are not learning a thing. All of our kids agree the work they are being taught is what they learned in the 6th grade. Some of the teachers come from impressive backgrounds but simply lack teaching skills. Very not happy here. We would leave tomorrow if there was another school like this one which is supposed to focus on performing arts and technology. It need better teachers and better counselors. Also, remember this is not a school to go to if you like sports - not a sports school. This is a horrible school, and I would never send my child back..We pulled him out, and he went to a much better school..A couple of his teachers were worthless.. It's a great school. Though I was out for a while for health purposes, and I never caught up. I have a lot of pressure on me 24/7 to get things done. The teachers aren't the best either. I feel like none of them ever act like they want to be there. They always sound tired and it's really hard to focus in any of your classes when all of your teachers are so monotone. Not including that 1/2 of them have very strong accents and it's very hard to understand what they are saying. Make sure your also not a sports person, because they don't do that kind of stuff. I was here just for freshman year and I've already decided where I'm going next year, because I don't know if I can take another year in such an anxiety filled area. Though if your into arts and science it's a great school for those. I am a current student here, and I think this is the best high school I have gone to. I went to Royal for sometime, but the environment did not seem friendly, and it gave me bad vibes. But this review is about Santa Su! I will say that some teachers are not the best, but this school has alot of friendly students and I love how the school is directed towards Arts, Science, and Technology! Recent alum. Keep in mind that my experience may not be representative because you may not take all the classes I did and have different teachers, did different programs, joined different clubs etc. Overall thought the experience was probably better than average, and definitely a different experience than most high schools. Being a small school definitely has some of its disadvantages like not having the students/teachers/resources available to do some larger extracurricular activities or olympiads. However, Santa Su has found pretty unique ways to provide pretty special programs given the situation. While some AP classes might be missing, Santa Su makes up for it by providing special classes like entrepreneurship, honors engineering, and calculus c, which are hard to find elsewhere. Also, while I did not participate myself, our performing and digital arts programs are really cool, especially choir and photo. There's no sports, which can be a good thing or bad thing depending on how you think about sports. A lot of the teachers are also very supportive and fun to be around. Personal Rankings of Various Things:Academics: 8/10Sports: N/ATeachers: 9/10Arts: 10/10School Clubs: 6/10 (few good ones, missing a lot, usually not enough teachers or students to do things like competitive academic extracurriculars, but there's support for Mock Trial and Robotics)School Spirit: 3/10Friendly Vibes: 7/10In conclusion, Santa Susana High School is definitely unique and while may not have certain things, it makes up for it in various ways. If you're into the arts, I highly recommend. If you want academics, then there may be better academics in Conejo Valley, but there's special classes here that aren't offered elsewhere which you should consider. School life isn't very lively, usually students are in their small groups. Excellent school in many areas. Great academics, multiple options for interests such as performing arts, science and technology, visual arts, mock trial, robotics, etc. Staff and teachers really care about students.

column3: Great school, Excellent teachers, they always help students whow are new in school, i enjoy my days in Brook. I'm a senior in this school and I love this school. Hearing so many rumors about Clear Brook about how bad it is makes me angry because all they've heard is one thing about Clear Brook and they actually believed it. I've been at this school and I like the people, the teachers, and the administrators. The school gives a lot of cool classes such as, CBTV, Chinese, French, and many other classes, not a lot of school can offer what Clear Brook has. Clear Brook students are unique. In many schools you see the types of cliques, the goth, nerds, jocks, and etc. Everyone here in Brook are all together. It's like Mix It Up Day everyday. I have to say that when I graduate, I'm going to miss this school and teachers. Clear Brook High School is an awesome school....great kids, great teachers. It has strong, vibrant extracurricular programs that encourage parents to be very active in their student's activities. Teachers are very approachable and willing to work with each student's specific needs. I just wish I had more children to send to Clear Brook! I hated this school. My son was constantly bullied by his peers and also by school officials. And no one did anything about it when he asked for help. They let the boy who bullied my son go free and my son had to suffer the consequences. It was to the point where my son nearly took his own life. There is no discipline for school officials there. Clear Brook High School is sub-par, to say the least. There are plenty of classes available for students who simply need to graduate, but the school is lacking in opportunities for true enrichment. Some feeble attempts are made at offering enrichment to gifted students, but overall these are truly insufficient. Outlets such as the GT advisory and AP classes are not ways to help students grow intellectually, merely serving to make the school look better. The school is also constantly losing top students to schools like Clear Lake which offer more to higher achieving students and have a friendlier atmosphere. Many of the teachers there are not motivated to stimulate their students and openly admit to giving busy work regularly. A biology teacher of mine informed the class that humans under the age of 21 only use their brain stems to function, and do not use their cerebrum. Though there are several inspiring teachers at Clear Brook, they simply cannot make up for those who make life at Clear Brook a draining experience. Just about as good as most schools can get. Some things I don't agree with, but that's just a part of life. 2 main issues..Bullying and incompetent staff! My daughter has been bullied by the same group of girls for months, has made numerous reports officially and verbally to the staff and campus police, and absolutely NOTHING HAS BEEN DONE! They are not proactive at all with these type of situations. They don't bother to call the parents, they don't split the troubled students up..they even put off the problem for another day to the point the issue is never handled until it gets out of hand. My daughter is pretty much scared to go to class because the girls follow her from class to class, what kind of learning environment is that?? They staff was forced to deal with the situation because my daughter is finally fed up with it, and verbally defended herself..guess what the staff did..suspended my child for cursing even though the person bullying my child walks around trying to "jump" my child with other people and nothing is done about it!! Does this make sense to anyone, punish the victim and let the offender walk w/o even a phone call to their parents. This is becoming the worst school in the district. I went here in. The late 90's and it is like day/night now.. horrible staff! School stabbings, threats, fires, gas leaks. Safety of our children seems to not be a priority. This school has reached its downfall since the establishment of a new administration and principal. Initially, I had enjoyed the unique prospects of this school from a diverse array of students to special learning opportunities. But with administration focused on the wrong issues, there's been failure to provide attention to relevancy that our students need to prosper. For starters, the administration fails to provide support towards academic achievement, but rather to the band and sports. Students participating in academic competitions fail to receive the same recognition, which hinders their potential in such a distressed environment. Administration is more focused on handing out "core value popcorn" than providing time to their students. The administration doesn't provide time to their students upon request, and talk down on students as if they're in elementary. Not to mention the special education students who are treated as toddlers and locked away into one hallway in the school. The scheduling here is completely disorganized and thoughtless to the schedules of students, who are often misinformed. There are at least eight different schedules at this school that change on a daily basis without notice, leaving them clueless of what goes on (completely unsafe in emergencies). Students who have off periods are clueless on when to arrive, and schedules that push the school day back by a hour affect those with work schedules. Administration demands things from both staff and students at late notice. High school is a time for students to learn and grow into young adults, not feel baffled and terrified of the overly harsh environment to where they don't feel comfortable enough in striving for success. The school and district will take credit and boast upon achievements of students for statistics, but fail to acknowledge them as actual human beings otherwise. This school needs to work on the treatment of students, as this learning environment should MOTIVATE students to be their best rather than feel ignored and controlled by adults. I've never felt so control-less and ignored in my eighteen years of life, and its problem spindles off the administration's disorganization and unreasonable decisions. There are better solutions to being a safe and positive environment, and this school is not taking those steps.

column1: My two boys attended all four years at Hamilton and it was a wonderful experience. The school is small and the kids really become a family. They both played sports and we were impressed with the coaches and teachers. Many told us not to send our kids to this school. They were wrong! The small class sizes and small size of the school was perfect. I love this school. From the teachers to the sports staff to the administration,, this is a wonderful place for kids to attend high school.

column3: I believe attending Calloway county was very beneficial to me. I could not have recieved a better learning enviroment or overall atmosphere. Calloway is a great school. Teachers have high expectations for all students and the administration is very supportive. They were awarded a bronze star award by US News and World Reports.

column1: I can’t recommend anybody this school. Many other students are racist, homophobic, etc. I hear various slurs practically every day, and derogatory language directed towards minorities is incredibly common. The dress code, at first glance within the handbook, seems standard but some of the staff enforce it to a very high degree, often dress-coding girls for incredibly minor instances of a skirt slightly too short, shoulders showing, and even shirts that expose the stomach *only* when the arms are raised far above the head. It seems they do so on what they deem acceptable, not what the actual dress code says. The learning experience here is also not great. There are few advanced courses, and not that many electives outside of things like welding, agriculture, or wood shop (which teach good life skills and may interest many people, but there’s not a lot of variety) I don’t feel like I’m being properly prepared for college here. The one good thing I have to offer is that this school prides themselves a lot on their sports. Extracurriculars have high participation, and do not require tryouts. Anybody can join, and even if they aren’t great at the sport they can still learn and improve over time. All in all, I can’t really think of anything else good to say about this school. It can be a potential option since an actually good education is scarce in this area, but I highly advise against coming here.

column3: As a former student of Chico High I can read the review left on 6/19/2003 and say it's absolute rubbish and written by someone with a very limited understanding of education and educators and who perhaps like to defer their responsibilities to others. Chico High is the superior high school in Chico with a long and distinguished history of academic and athletic excellence. To add to the diversity there are a number of smaller learning communities within Chico High such as WEST and ACT that have unique and focused curriculum. In my four years there, all of my instructors were attentive, diligent and enthusiastic to work with the students in their respective subjects. Students were all treated and helped equally as well as individually given every opportunity for success and excellence. From the first-rate academia, to the stellar athletic program to the aesthetically beautiful campus with an incredibly history, Chico High stands out as a school that offers more possibilities for success and enrichment than any other high school in Chico. CHS is a Golden Bell Award winner this year for its outstanding CTE program in architect and construction design. They have a 3-d printer and can verify construction plans by actually building working models. The City of Chico expects applicants to RPF to submit it plans to the high class in order to verify that their plans will work in the real world! The lunch ladies are very kind and the teachers are very helpful ! The students get along with each other very well! I think this school is wonderful. It offers diversity as well as wonderful aesthetic and music programs. The two things I'm not too happy about our the art programs grading policiesand lack of a football field. Those are district issues though, I suppose. I have had my expectations exceeded as far as teachers, staff and athletic programs.specifically the football and wrestling program. I am a local business owner and have hired many students from Chico High over the summer. They have all been exemplary employees, polite, responsible, and trustworthy. Good job teachers, parents, and students. After coming out of the local continuation school (Fairview), I found Chico high to be a breath of fresh air both socially and academically. The atmosphere is friendly, the teachers work well with their students, and the career pathways are various and well designed. The academic environment is what I would deem a perfect mix between structure and freedom. With teachers who care, and a curriculum that is engaging, motivated students are set up for success. At the same time, individual autonomy is encouraged and no specific career path is highlighted more than others, a perfect balance in an overall wonderful school.

column1: My son and niece went to Lake Catholic High School. I agree with the previous poster, the school is average at best. The school is all about sports because athletes skate there. They are not challenged and are not held to the same accountability as other students. The culture is cold and clicky, its about who you know. My niece graduated from Lake with over a 3.0 gpa but couldn't score high enough on her ACT to get into state schools like Kent or BGSU. My son ended up transferring to VASJ after his sophomore year which has a much more challenging curriculum and a much more warm and welcoming environment. I would recommend parents look at VASJ first, followed by NDCL or St Ignatius before considering Lake. My wife and I both graduated from Lake back in the 80's and we are sending our child there and she loves the atmosphere as well as the teaching staff. She has plenty of work to keep her busy and does well in the school. A person's education doesn't just "happens" to them. Every experience and every grade is earned....NOTHING is given. I feel that Lake has a variety of different courses that meet the need of students of all academic needs. If someone is skating by and not being challenges, then that is a reflection of the student and them taking the easy course and the easy way out. Lake overall is a good school and works to tailor programs for all of their population. Lake is a great environment for a young adult to learn and grow up in. Lake teaches excellence, integrity, accountability and compassion. The school refuses to listen to the parents or even the students. The principal won’t return emails or even consider any facts given when making a decision. They have no admission standards, as they accept 100% of those that apply. In the end it’s all about the money. I have loved the experience at Lake Catholic. The community is what makes this program and school so unique.

column3: While small class sizes are a plus, there is very little offered at this school in terms of class choices . There is only one language offered . The is very little choice as far as optional curriculum . Having so few students means fewr teachers are employed .Ergo less class choices. Sports programs are practically nonexistant , if you want to join a team you have to join a Keansburg or Keyport team. Do your children's future a huge favor andeither send them to a private school or move to Middletown or Rumson. RFH is an amazing high school with wonderfully diverse choices and oppurtunity to actually prepare your child for the oppurtunities of the future. Henry Hudson is a forward thinking district that stays ahead of the curve on learning trends and educational techniques. I have been very impressed with their teaching staff and their administration. HHRS has a lot of offer to its students- there are many sports available for both middle and high school as well as clubs and extracurriculars. The music program is top notch and so is the broadcasting program! All in all a great school! Hudson is a pretty average school. The teachers are really good, and there are good opportunities in sports, but the administration is lacking in certain areas. This is a school that cares about the individual student and offers a lot of unique learning opportunities for students. Middle school and high school students work together to create a positive learning environment for all and with lots of club and athletic opportunities for all ages, this is a place where teachers and administrators know your son/daughter's name and who they really are as well as cares for them sincerely. The student to teacher ratio is a big asset. There are many great opportunities for students to grow and participate in clubs ,athletics, the arts, STEAM and Stem and mentor program. I like how all high school students (freshman to seniors) commingle in all areas. I would rate this school with 5 stars. I would not have sent my children anywhere else. As a graduate of HHRS, I've experienced the turn around by the current administration. The opportunities to excel in this school are above par. Small class sizes, the clubs, the athletics you will not find this at another area school. The staff is amazing and truly care! Everyone knows your child by name, as well as the parents! I can not say enough positives about our experience in this school. Coming to the school as a family that was new to the district, the school has made my child feel welcomed and included. She has been encouraged to reach her highest potential and has been given the skills and the opportunities to do it.

column1: I would give it a 4 out of 5, it is a pretty small school, but the students there are really nice to each another and the school work are hard at first, but will become like piece of pie after learning about it for 1 month.

column3: EPHS is a jungle. The staff will appear helpful when u go in to meet with them but they do not come through at all. I sent my child here and her grades plummeted right down, along with other issues. Which, btw did not get addressed as of yet and now it is summer time. Some children can survive the large, urban school but then some cannot. Mine cannot and I am working on finding another environment for her. ADVICE: If your child has a learning issue, find another small setting. Or get ready to be chasing down faculty there all year long! Avoid this school at all costs - My daughter has been going here for almost a year and her grades have done a nose dive do the teachers feel any respoinsibility for this (you know cause they are the ones teaching) nope they blame everyone but themselves for your childs bad grades it either the student not working hard enough or the parent is not doing enough but you will never hear them say its me I need more time with your child to get them to understand the subject at hand I attended East Providence High School and I can honestly say that the teachers, staff, nor the principal was at all helpful in ANY situation. If you are having trouble in your classes the teachers tell you to try harder when students can only try so hard. When a student asks for help it should be given. I failed English 9 due to issues with me, my parents, and the teacher. Instead of giving me a different teacher the next year they gave me the same one.. 3 TIMES. Each time failing while I was passing 10th and 11th grade English with no issues, I have a post high school reading level and found this to be ridiculous. If you are absent for a week or more due to personal reasons or being sick, instead of the staff showing compassion and caring, they threaten to suspend and even expel you. This school is utterly ridiculous and I DO NOT BY ANY MEANS RECOMMEND SENDING YOUR CHILD THERE. It is an unsafe, un-nurturing environment with hostile staff, students, and teachers. And the school buildings state? The School is falling apart at every corner no matter how many "renovations" they are doing. (Tiles containing asbestos still remain after 2 YEARS when they were told to remove it) The teachers in this school care about their students however that same level of caring about education isn't necessarily replicated within the student body. In fact the student body here is the most disgusting i have ever seen. They swear constantly, they enjoy bullying. The level of Homophobia is at unparalleled levels. Ok, can anyone tell me what is the purpose of the senior project. I can tell you that in my household it has just been just the stress and the expense. For Gods sake let the senior year be a year that these seniors can enjoy since the other 3 years have difficult ones East Providence High is not the greatest school to be in. Our son is getting a wonderful education at East Providence High School. The character they build in this school is beyond compare. Teachers are caring, competent, and go above-and-beyond to reach their students. The administration team in place is organized, approachable, and caring. The students who emerge from this school are well-rounded citizens: smart, centered, and committed to their community. East Providence High School has an epidemic of terrible leadership and often discourages students. Very few teachers are willing to teach as most just puts a power point for students to take notes and then give out homework oppose to something much more hands on and interesting. Being that it is my last year here, I can honestly say that EPHS is not a fair environment to both students and faculty members. The teachers that do teach and provide a helpful and interesting classroom do not have the resources that they need (broken SmartBoards, cold classrooms) and as for the students, the staff (administration) gives a special privilege to athletes. Some members of the staff are biased and even though the school's policy of discrimination is "re-enforced", it really isn't. How they deal with bullying and other important issues are not helpful. EPHS does have a social worker (who is great by the way!), but many students who are struggling with mental health issues (anxiety, depression, etcetra) are not really offered the opportunity to meet the social worker; many students actually don't know that we have this service. When it comes to a safe environment, East Providence High School would rank a 3.5/10 for me personally due to the lack of mental health help and the condition of the school overall. The school has much potential if it was under better leadership and provided teachers that actually cared about the students and are passionate about the subject, but I would say that only 50% (maybe less) of the teachers are actually passionate about what they teach. I enjoyed the (semi) diverse environment that an urban ring public school provides, but when it comes to racism, EPHS is pretty bad at dealing with it. Caucasian students are allowed to speak bigotry and xenophobic views with little to no consequences. The social probation rule that the school has also discourages students to join in school activities since after six tardies/unexcused absences, you're not allowed to go to (most) functions, including battle of classes. When it comes to spirit, if it wasn't for the students, there would absolutely be none.

column1: Nashville High School is arguably the best high school in Southwest Arkansas. Yes, we are proud of our sports traditions, but we are just as proud of our academics. We strive for excellence in everything we do. Our block schedule format allows students 90 minutes per class to really get into the lessons of the day, instead of just getting a cursory overview that is so prevalent in seven and eight period per day schools. It also readies our students for college coursework. I as a teacher have never felt that I lacked the tools to do my job. Yes, this community spends money on our sports programs, but we spend it on academics as well. I'm a graduate of Nashville High and only have good things to say about the school and the district. I've lived in several larger cities around the state and have found that the education I recieved is on par or better than what these larger districts are administering. I was more than prepared for college (both my undergrad and graduate degrees) and for adult life in general due to the education I recieved in my formative years. I am proud to have been a K-12 student of Nashville and look forward to raising my familiy in this area. Excellence in all fields. Academics and athletics. From band to cheer, from quiz bowl to Agri, every aspect of student development is fostered by an internal drive to succeed. Work hard, dream big. It takes both. From state championships.. to the Champions that arise after graduation; we all still have the heart of an underdog. No matter if you went K through 12 or just 1 year, if you sat under Scrapper teaching you know that "Once a Scrapper, Always a Scrapper!" #scrappernation

column1: At first the school may look ghetto, run down, and not a place you want to spend 4 years, but the teachers actually care. Students tell off teachers and they come back year after year and still continue teaching. The teachers are the ones that make the difference. Ganesha has the best math dept. in the district and has better AP scores than Diamond Ranch which gets all the money. The only reason it's not better is because it gets very little funding. Students are constantly fundraising for everything!!! I'm in college now and really appreciate where I came from. I can honestly say Ganesha is an exceptional school. I'm a freshman there and there are so many clubs like Anime club, The Green club, Math club, Bible club,The Latina club, French club and so on. They have wonderful programs like Avid(they claim to have the best Avid program California) the academic ellective that prepares them for college,Trio Upward Bound the program that gives tutoring to all students after school three times a week in their library, and other excellent acedmic programs. They also provide vocational classes for upper classmen, an Orchestra, Marching Band, Jazz band, And Quoir. They also have good leadership programs like ASB and JROTC. They also have very good teachers and more AP classes than some other schools. They also have a lot of fun school events and students will not feel out of place with the students here. People are friendly and the schools extensive programs and clubs will provide students to grow as an individualDid I also mention their 2012 validectorian graduated with a 4.9 and now attends Brown. And like many have said, if your student isn't suceeding in Ganesha, they problaly dont want to Ganesha High School serves over 1,000 on a daily basis, and is located in a low-income community. As my third year at Ganesha, I have taken the initiative to produce some change. Change in the areas were students seem to focus on which are the school meals and the restrooms. The school food, compared to other high schools, is rated negatively by the majority of the students. Many students would rather pass on lunch then eat the food being served, since the food is sometimes served cold, or is rather served poorly. Ganesha High School along with the rest of the local schools should not be underestimated due to the reputation the community obtains. Why not spark a change in the school meals, and see what are the POSITIVE consequences. I think GHS is one of the best schools in Pomona, it's the love, care, compassion, dedication and hard work of our teachers and staff that makes the difference. They do it because they truly care, as we all know the funds are not there, but some way, some how they make a difference in our children.

column3: Cloverleaf has a few dedicated and caring teachers, however most of them are too willing to fail a student rather than help them. The guidance counselors only care about the good students. They tell all of the 'problem kids' to transfer to the Medina County Career Center, so they don't have to deal with them. I graduated a few years ago, and although I'm doing much better in College, I have to say that my education at Cloverleaf did not prepare me for College at all. It's a lot of hard work making up for all of that lost time. Cloverleaf High School provided me with excellent teachers that motivated me and encouraged me to do my best. The principal and assistant principals all cared about the students and only wanted to see them succeed. Cloverleaf also provided challenging curriculum, it was just up to each individual student to do the work! Cloverleaf was a great place to be! I am both a parent and former graduate. The lower grades (1st - 3rd) are not that bad, but as you get older it gets worse. Many teachers that did care have been let go and most that are left are just there to get a check and wait for retirement. If you have any issues at all they try to ship you off to the Career Center. I have heard from Seniors that the Guidance Office does not help much with continuing with extra college credits thru Akron U. They actually will discourage. Not sure why. Maybe they lose money for each student. I got good grades but when I went to College I was behind and had to take about a year of classes to catch up. Cloverleaf is weak in Math and went I went for Engineering I was not ready. This is my experience and now I am seeing things being repeated again with my child. If anything it might be worse with the budget issues. I've had a son in the district from 2nd grade and he is now in 9th grade. If I were to stay here he would be woefully underprepared for college. The budget issues that the school has faced has cost them dearly in terms of quality teachers. They've been stuck with quite a bit of dead weight that they can't get rid of due to the union. It's a shame, really. The superintendent is absolutely the saving grace of the District. To blame anyone other than the voters of the District does the school an injustice. It took them over a decade to pass a levy, and this is what happens when schools are forced to cut back to nothing. The belief that the school spends wastefully is widespread and unsubstantiated. All one needs to do is attend a board meeting now and then to see that, though few bother. Overall poor. Poor leadership. Teachers are jaded and going thru the motions. Teachers don’t care about the students

column1: It was an adequate high school experience. By my SR year I was more than ready to leave. I didn't belong to the "in group" nor did I go to the same congregation as the leadership of the school/town so while I had some awesome teachers, the leadership from the assistant principal on up to the school board to also include the school counselor often made life very difficult and frustrating. I still managed to graduate in the top 10% of my class despite all this. I was also voted class favorite and most school spirit, so I'm not saying all this from a bitter stand point, just being honest with the school. It's good, but needs some serious improvement on the leadership side.

column3: I am a graduate at this school. I attended this school for 4 years and through those years, I saw many changes in the school, whether it is the cosmetic, academic, or staff changes. What I have to say is that this school is much better than the reputation it has, and this is because I've had friends that transfered from other schools to Fresno High to attend their senior year, and that is what they personally told me. I was also a student in the IB Program that this school offered, and I have to say that the IB Program really help guide my way through high school, and onto a University. Long story short for anyone who is looking to attend this school, or sending their child to this school, the Pro of this school would be the programs that this school offers. There are the rare IB Program, CAHSEE Prep Program, many different Afterschool programs, JROTC (Military) Program, Parent/School meeting programs for all different language, etc. The cons would be the very strict rules school enforces due to the school district. This school makes students feel like they are locked up in prison when they step on campus, which doesn't prep you for college in an open environment. I have two daughters that attend this Highschool and they say that the classes are challenging and the teachers are intellectual. They have a great afterschool program that assist with everything from homework assistance to SAT prep. I am satisfied with the education my children are receiving at Fresno Highschool. Beautiful Campus!... Mixture of old buildings and New. For the shear volume of students enrolled it runs rather smoothly. Teachers are willing to go the extra mile to help students that are unsteady. As well as clearing the way for students who are ready to excel! Security strives to be on top of each and Every incident!. There is a diverse group of people attending this campus. :) It is much safer than i had heard it was... The only thing i saw that was supposed to be a violation of the dress code was a little too much "Sagging!' students with droopy pants, Offending students are notified they comply the min. Staff gets out of view they revert to the same behavior. By allowing this to continue it sends a wrong message. Its Ok, Or going to be "Overlooked if i break the rules. :( Thank you, Dr. Forbes for the leadership which improves the education of students and the working conditions for teachers. It was great. I would love to see more diversity in the staff population. More classes that will beneficial to students. Make it an international experiences to student. Teach about the truth of American history. Support DACA students and have conversations on different privileges'. I moved here on Mc Kinley St. in 2009 with my husband directly West of Palm Ave. & lived here for 13 years..i like the Community even if it has changed since then.I was never a student at F.H.S., but remember the neighborhood well when attending F.C.C. back in the 70tys.Although many of my cousins graduated from F.H.S., & some still live in the neighborhood."3" became teacher's, one a " Assistant Director" at CSUF. & other younger cousins who moved " out of state" with " Successful high paying jobs". From what I have learned they all Loved F.H.S. with " Great Memories " & obviously a " Great Education" that was a " Stepping Stone" to their" Current Success" with their Careers.

column1: Very great place to learn & make friends. Teachers go above and beyond to help you graduate on time. Very hard to miss/skip class. The staff there knows what they're doing! Now, when she is trying to get her GED...they are dragging their feet getting her permission to use a calculatr for testing. It is always SOMEONE ELSES JOB! Any kid that needs extra help to graduate, they talk into quitting. That way it doesn't go against their State Report Card. PLEASE,PLEASE....IF YOU HAVE ANY CHOICE AT ALL DON'T SEND YOUR KIDS TO THIS SCHOOL. Hannibal School had my daughter graduate with an IEP diploma, when with a little extra work she could have gotten a general dipoma, but no.....they had to give her FIVE art courses a year, instead. When I tried to get involved and volunteer to help other special education kids, they wouldn't even listen. I guess they wanted puppets that would do what they wanted, instead of someone who would advocate for the kids. As a graduate of 2011 I am completely happy to never see Hannibal community again. They have nothing to offer here. It's a poor town with classes that are useless. Other school districts actually offer valuable classes. If you want your child well educated I do not recommend this school. They pull anyone off the street to teach at this school.
