column3: Grants Pass High School is one of the very best high schools in Southern Oregon. The faculty strives to offer all students the opportunity to grow and learn. The School Board and Administration have made this a safe and responsive school to the community needs. If you are moving to our area, it will be immediately evident to you as you enter this school that this is a great place for your children to attend. We have the top band program in the state and a wide array of sports programs and active clubs. There are an advanced courses for those who wish challenge themselves. The Theater Arts produces first rate performances in the Performing Arts Center which has no equal in the state. Two of the staff members at this school have Doctorates in their subject area and most of the faculty has their master s degrees. The Grants Pass High School Foundation gives out over 2 million dollars each year in scholarship awards on scholarship night. The school also boasts a multi- level alternative education schools for students who don t fit in to the regular school environment. No other school in the area has such opportunities. As a former student of GPHS I can honestly say that I wouldn't trade my experience there for anything. Not only did participation in their excellent Orchestra Program, Cheerleading, Golf team and student body aid in the procurement of a full scholarship to Columbia University - once there I was as prepared or more prepared for my courses than many students who had gone to expensive prep schools. Particularly Mr. Alves, Baldwin and many others not only equipped me for college, but taught me something invaluable - how to think. School officials care more about targeting and singling out 'perceived problem' students then education. NEVER have I seen a school so detention and suspension happy.

column3: My school is great....!!!! The teachers are kind and sympathetic with the students. Maybe we need more teachers of languages. On a yearly basis my son complains claiming that nearly 50% of his teachers lack group control skills. They grade students basically for minimum efforts in class such as buying things from the teachers or buying basic school supplies for them. Students can get average to good grades with VERY MINIMAL EFFORTS on their behalf. They are not challenged intellectually and sadly over 50% of the students are so far behind in the minimum skills required to be at they should be at, that they drag the other percent down. Many claim to use email as a communication tool but many answer way over 2 days and even a week so by the time you get a response... the issue is beyond repair. Impossible to get sit downs with ALL teachers at once, even when escalating things to the principal. Only office that is efficient is the Registration Office. Mederos is Top Notch quality and seems to be the only one who knows how to run her area as per high standards. Had it not been because its so near graduation year, I'd move to another country!! HIGHLY DISAPPOINTED! The professors are very dedicated . They work hard for our students. I want to say "Thanks ... for all your efforts . Assitants to Principal are very cooperative..... The school is very in organized. Some teachers are good at what they do and others are sloppy. My teacher smokes a vapor shark in class and is rude at times. The best teacher I have is Ms.Rahouly. She is the best math teacher you will probably ever meet. Other than her I don't know any other teacher who is dedicated to his/her work and I think that should be something to talk about in a faculty meeting. Some teachers are very lazy and they are sitting down most or maybe all of class time. They teach a little and then assign book work. Other than that the school is ok. The school is maintained but not all the time. I see rotten food in the stair ways and sometimes roaches. There are reasons why I'm leaving this school. I don't suggest this school to anyone. There are many teachers who genuinely care and teach well, but that does not go for all of them. The securities are absolute jerks. I tried going through a hallway where two students just went through. Despite a sign saying there was "gym testing", I figured I could go through. The security said "What? Can't you read? Get out". Extremely rude and unprofessional behavior. There are many teachers with a high preparation and very lovely. The school has organization. My son is leaving grade 9 and until now, I am very happy with all the staff. He has teachers with dedication and I think , they are working very hard. I am really happy for this reason.Some times many people , said me that Coral Park wasn't the best school for my son, I tried and my experience was amazing until now. Awesome I graduated in 1966 and I loved it. I was on the first cheerleading squad and I will never forget my high school years. Ehp The staff is mediocre, they lack accountability, problem solving, behavioral experience within different kid's personalities, they don't have idea how to deal with bullying, staff is not good at decision making. It's very sad to see this after so many years in business.Hopefully they get better and changed the Principal and administration. Too many wanna be gangsters and irresponsible staff, even the Principal won't take accountability. They let any kid go to this school even when they know the teenagers have behavior problems, too much bullying going on in this poorly develop school. I don't recommend it to any parent with good kids. A hidden gem, with great faculty and family atmosphere. This school gives the students many opportunities to get ahead their course work. With FIU real close students can also do dual enrollment courses. I am proud to say my three kids are CP alumni. My oldest was an Engineering Magnet student that went on to graduate as a Florida Gator majoring in Agricultural Engineering. My Middle child pursued a career in Teaching and recently earned her Master's Degree in Educational Leadership. My son recently graduated and is starting the Fire Academy. My children flourished at Coral Park. This school and the dedicated staff helped form the human beings they are today. Simply said, they were educated, cared for and guided. Are there pros and cons... Sure, but in life, pros and cons are everywhere! Coral Park offers a top notch education if you choose to embrace it. The wrong path is not a given, it is a choice.To all of those that submit bad reviews, I ask, what part did you or your child play while at Coral Park??? Miami Coral Park Sr. High School is a great school with an INCREDIBLE Engineering magnet. Not only did I and my husband graduate from CP back in 1983 but we sent our 3 children to CP and don't regret it for a minute. Our children were all in the Engineering magnet and was of great academic benefit to each who are now all professionals. CP is a school that employs various teachers that were once students. When a staff member returns to their own high school, that speaks volumes! I graduated from Miami Coral Park in 2008. I remember my time in CP very fondly. My teachers were kind and caring and they helped getting me through the toughest time in my life as I adapted to being in the country. When I graduated from college this was the first and only school I applied to. I am very proud to teach in this school that means so much to me and getting a peek behind the curtain. Our school is full of educators who deeply care about our students and their learning. I personally love teaching and my classroom is a place of experimentation and an open forum for the pursuit of scientific knowledge. My experience as a teacher at MCPSH is that Miami Coral Park is a highly functioning high school, producing students of character, integrity and academic preparation. This opinion is based on eight years of classroom experience at this school, and in comparison of other high schools in MDCPS. Both of my boys graduated from Miami Coral Park Sr. High. I feel that CP prepared them well for the next chapter in their lives.. college. Happy to say, both have since graduated from the university. My son transferred from a very small school to Miami Coral Park senior high school. He wanted to get used to bigger environment. though he was terrified in the beginning of school year. when he was graduating last year he said that was the best thing that has happened to him . I asked him what he loved the most about Coral Park. He said Coral Park has a Great communal environment. Teachers are amazing. As a parent II am so grateful to so many compassionate staff and teachers in Miami Coral Park senior high school For helping my son. Thank you a million times Coral Park is a neighborhood school with two strong magnets, The Engineering, Architecture and Construction Magnet and The Biomedical Magnet. It has a fabulous visual and performing arts program with amazing AP art results. The school has great potential and many opportunities for students to succeed at all levels. They are prepared for post graduate 2 year and 4 year colleges and universities as well as other certification and training opportunities. CP is a hidden gem that more families should consider. Coral Park Sr High is a hidden gem in Westchester. With a variety of magnet programs, DE, and AP classes offered, this is the place to get a one of a kind learning experience. Miami Coral park is truly a bright light of public education that has been kept in the dark. the bad reputation that has been give to this school is greatly undeserved. It is a school filled with programs to prepare their students for life after high school. No matter if they choose to continue their education or join the work force, MCPSH can prepare them to be successful in their future plans. With the amazing magnet programs that have found national recognition and success to the drafting and construction program, each student has an opportunity to prepare themselves for the rest of their lives. People need investigate and make an opinion for themselves about Miami Coral park. The problem in the area is that people are going of a 20 year old reputation with out finding out what new innovations and programs the school has now. Once people see the schools data comapaired to the other area schools they will see that Coral park is surpassing the area schools academically. Both of my kids attended Miami Coral Park Senior High School. One was part of the Engineering Magnet and went to off to super prepared based how easy his engineering coureses were from how prepared he left MCPSHS. As for my other child, she just graduated and even during the pandemic, was involved in her community through the leadership of her club teachers. She entered FIU early and also won an internship that was arvertised to her through On the Job Training (OTJT) representative at the CP. I am extremely appreciative to all the teachers and staff at the school. Definitely highly, recommend the school to parents looking for a great and caring staff that always goes above and beyond for the kids! Wonderful school with really talented and caring teachers and some really heartfull students! I have been teaching at CP for 25 years and it is my alma matter as well. It is the place where I met my husband and many friends who are still in my life. It is a second home to me. I love the feeling of family that CP provides. Teachers are passionate about seeing students succeed, creating an environment of kindness, acceptability and leadership. Our students are caring individuals who have the opportunity of being engaged in a multitude of courses, clubs and sports. Take advantage of all that Coral Park has to offer. Once a Ram, always a Ram! Coral Park Senior has so much to offer. The performing arts department is a wonderful outlet for students to show off their creative side. They offer performances, creative opportunities, stress relief outlet, field trips, shows and so much more. The dance team is award winning, along with our band, and drama program. Students have moved on from CP to go to New World College, Juilliard dance programs, Berkeley School of music, etc. I love this school!!!! The students are well behaved and my child has never had any bullying or negative issues there. The staff and administration are 100% student advocates. They have always made time to listen to parent concerns and followed up with us. I graduated from another Miami Dade County Public school. I wish I had attended Coral Park. If I had more children, they definitely would be attending Coral Park. One of the best schools in southwest Miami-Dade. I have been associated with Miami Coral Park High School since 1966. I am a graduate of the Class of 1981. I am presently beginning my 29th year of teaching here at CP. Miami Coral Park High School has always been the "BEST KEPT SECRET" in Miami-Dade. The students, teachers, staff, and administration that have graced the halls of this institution is up there with the BEST OF THE BEST in this county, state, and country. The Engineering Magnet Program since its inception in 1988 is undoubtedly one of the best magnet programs in this country and it happens to be the longest running magnet program for high schools in this county. The partnership with the Florida International University (FIU) Engineering Department since 1988 allows the senior students to take Dual Enrollment (DE) engineering courses such as Engineering Drawing, SOLIDWORKS, C Programming for Engineers, and JAVA Programming during school hours and allows the engineering students to acquire college credits as high school students. With the recent addition of the Biomedical Magnet Program along with the Architecture/Construction Magnet makes this school so unique as compared to other schools in the county. I would challenge anyone and everyone to come and visit and not rely on internet jibber jabber. Come here and witness it yourselves. RAMS (RIGHT ATTITUDE MEANS SUCCESS)RAMS (ROBOTS ARE MY SPECIALTY) This community is very safe for the students and the schools leadership is very effective I went to coral park all my four years and can say that the education is amazing. The teacher and administration care about all their student and always helps with everything you need. They have so much to offer and amazing opportunities. If you are looking to go to this school I recommend 100%.Sincerely,A Coral Park aluminum ! Amazing and well rounded experience! This school offered me the opportunity to complete AP classes, participate in multiple sports, and build lasting friendships. A solid foundation for my college years! ALWAYS A RAM! Miami Coral Park Senior is my home away from home! I am so grateful to have spent the majority of my career, educating Miami Dade's finest students in such a safe, challenging and positive environment. I would encourage anyone to enroll their children here! In fact, my own kids graduated from CP! We are a proud Ram Family! I have been teaching here at "The Park" for six years, and I have always found the school culture of the administrators, staff, students and their families to be incredibly friendly. Coming in to school or work every, it makes such a difference for everyone to be joining together to create a kind and caring community, and this school does that exceptionally well. I went to Coral Park all four years and I can truly say my life changed in this place, in middle school I hung out with the wrong people and when I started Coral Park I had no intention of actually caring for my education. However, many teachers like Mr. DeLaO, Mrs.Bown, Mr.Rodriguez and the amazing team of counselors quickly changed my mind and got me into the right path, not only educationally but personally. I had all support all around and I will forever be grateful to Coral Park for my experience. All 6 of my children attended Miami Coral Park. My 3 older children are University Graduates and successful individuals. My younger 3 children are attending University now and are well prepared and doing great. As a parent I am truly thankful to all of their teachers and the support and encouragement they gave my kids. They entered University prepared and confident individuals. My kids still talk about the experiences the had at Coral Park. Truly a hidden gem of a school. Miami Coral Park is definitely a school full staff members that is invested in making sure their students have a bright future. They’re dedication and devotion to teaching is truly rewarding and greatly appreciated. Once a Ram always a Ram!! I love CP, class of 2013!!! The best school ever!!! Wouldnt have gone to any other highschool. Love the teachers, staff, security and all the friends i made in the 4 years I called Coral Park my home. As a proud teacher in this school I know first hand that this is one of the best schools in our MDCPS District. In spite of the peculiar school year we had due to the pandemic, our school results in the last state wide tests were excellent. We offer a very safe environment for the well being and development of all our students. Amazing Robotics program. I am happy with the direction they take students As a proud teacher of 34 years I would say that Miami Coral Park Senior is a wonderful school and I would not trade it for another school. The Teachers are awesome and we have a very good Administrative staff that is always willing to assist. The custodial staff is friendly and always willing to assist. The food service employees are always willing to give a helping hand. The diverse student population makes it a great place. My family's history with MCP Sr HS goes back to 1963 when it was founded. My two cousins and I started H.S. then and attended Coral Park through our High School years and loved the school. It was and still is a great school with great programs. My daughter graduated in 1987, my grandson and granddaughter are both graduates of Coral Park as well. Our family still maintains the MCPSH connection and will continue to do so as my son-in-law is a very dedicated teacher at CP and has been for many years. The teachers give more than 100% of their time and dedication to their students and for the success of the school. They have a top engineering and cross-country programs for their students. My family and I strongly recommend and support Miami Coral Park Senior High school without a doubt !!!! The best school and great teams. Thank you teacher Angel Vazquez Administration and teachers are very dedicated! Great Engineering Magnet Program. During open house, met my sons Nutrition and Wellness teacher. Interesting class. They will actually learn how to cook healthy meals.

column1: Great school in one of the more suburban-like areas of Washington, DC. The teachers are great and many live in the area. Other than that, they are academically challenging and offer an amazing array of extras, like debate, a medical sci academy, all the sports, jrotc, on and on. And the full IB program! Unless you live a great distance from Capitol Hill, there's no reason to go elsewhere.

column1: I taught at Howard for a couple of years and would have willingly stayed a couple more. It wasn't that I particularly enjoyed teaching there, but I am a highly qualified teacher willing to do whatever it takes to help my kids succeed - something Howard needs. With that said, this school is a TERRIBLE environment for children who wish to learn. No parent that cares about their child should EVER allow him or her to attend this school. I loved Howard. I spent 2 years at the elementary school and 2 years at the high school. when I came into HS in 2005, the school had been completely remodeled, thank god. And yes the kids are rough around the edges, but where they came from was rough as well. You cant be weak minded going to or teaching at this school. You have to have a strong foundation. I had some doubts about going to HS here, but I met so many great people. The wonderful 2 years I spent here cant and will never compare to my last 2 years at Ooltewah High. We were pleased with the Howard and felt strongly that it is one of the better schools in Chattanooga. People like to think of this school as a low poverty school but the amount of income the kids parents have or don't have shouldn't take away from how smart the kids here are and how involved the parents are in the kids education. Don't believe everything you read and hear. Please don't go by all the reviews you see here look at the actual school records for graduation rate, kids going to college and test scores. Look to the numbers, they show all you need to know. Lousy school with multiple fights daily. No discipline and teachers are cussed out and have no backup from admin or SRO's. 3rd floor hasn't had working boys bathroom in over 2 months. I absolutely love being a part of the faculty at Howard. It’s a great school that steadily growing. Great experience to work in a place that truly cares about students. I’ve been an educator here for ten years. I’ve seen a lot of changes and the climate here has gotten better! I have enjoyed my first-year experience working at "The Howard School". This is an incredible school with hardworking teachers and brilliant, strong students. A great place to work and learn Outstanding, I wouldn't change a Thing, I love being at Howard; the Administration is top notch and my colleagues ,students really love being at the school. I Love it at Howard. How we work together, how we get along, the work ethic. It's a number of reasons, Dr. Ware it is wonderful working at The Howard High School! The leadership is awesome and goes beyond the call of duty to support the staff and students. I am a Retired Educator and served as an Interventionist for the Transition Academy at Bethlehem Center.

Yet, there are still many unenthusiastic and honestly, depressing teachers that teach here. I would say out of my 16 teachers that I have had, so far six have been very good, while at least five have not only been incompetent in their subject, but refused to teach and where blatantly disrespectful and used biased grading with the students because they hated their jobs. Green hope is known for excellent test scores, but what most don't know is that there is a percentage of students that does so well that it inflates the average and poor students scores. The school does not look to improve their lower scoring students scores very often. If a student wants to succed in the top half of the class, a tutor outside of school is positively mandatory.The pressure and competition here is insane, while the school lacks any positive reinforcement or incentives to students, or even any inspiration. The student body knows that we are more well off than some i'n economically challenged areas, but that's no excuse for the poor education I feel I am still receiving. I have been impressed with Green Hope High School since arriving in Cary, North Carolina almost 4 years ago. As I now have both a rising Senior and an incoming Freshman, I can attest to the school's overall professionalism, academic acheivements and excellent services. The faculty at Green Hope is "top notch" and clearly dedicated to the students. Mostly good teachers, but my daughter, who is a senior, has had some really bad ones, especially her chemistry teacher. Not too impressed with the principal. Hello I need help I am a student living in California right now and I am going to be a Freshman. Should I move to GHHS? Or not? And why? Help please! A good school is one with good teachers, good parents and good students. GHHS has all these three in place. So now it all depends on you (the student) how to make use of the available resources and in turn bring good name to GHHS. We are also planning to move to GHHS from CA. For those moving to the triangle area, Green Hope is arguably the best public high school in the state for both academics and athletics. They just won the statewide Wells Fargo Cup (4A) for athletic excellence - and you can see here their academic ratings (top in this area). I will have two graduates soon and both have had great experiences at Green Hope. We are looking to move from Texas to the area and are deciding on schools. Any updated information? My youngest child just graduated. Older children attended private high schools. Incoming parents, please note that although GH is a highly rated school, it is still a PUBLIC high school with 2200 students. Due to budgetary cuts, GH staff has been cut significantly since my child arrived in 9th grade. Take this into account when you interact with teachers and staff. My child had 2 lousy teachers, 2 outstanding teachers, and a bunch of pretty good ones. Counselors especially carry a huge workload. Your child may not get much attention until senior year when college applications are prepared. But they will get the help they need if you work with the staff politely and reasonably. Remember, if you want the same personal attention parents and students receive at Cary Academy, Cardinal Gibbons, and Ravenscroft, you'll have to pay for it. My son just graduated this weekend and he loved this school!! We are the minority in this area and he's never had a bad moment and never been bullied or picked on. He absolutely LOOVED Principal Summers!! He said out of his 13 years of school, she was the only principal that he felt cared about the students. She is very involved and talked to them not at them. I hope she stays that way. Green Hope is THE BEST SCHOOL in North Carolina! Nothing special. Grades are reflective of the student population (Asian), not the teaching. Outside of the high achieving kids, it is a typical HS filled with entitled kids, drinking and drugs. Families should not buy into the hype of GHHS being a top tier institution. There are a many good things about Green Hope, but the bad outweighs the good. Their athletic program is top notch, but past that the school is not so great. There are too many students to where individuals are not getting the attention needed to help students succeed. The worst thing about Green Hope is the competition. Healthy competition is good to help students to succeed, but it is toxic here. Students will be harassed to share grades and then put down if they didn't make a 95 or above by fellow students. This competition has caused cheating to run through the school since that's the only way student's feel they can succeed. This school may have been good 10 years ago, but now it is not somewhere I would want to attend again. Lots of extracurricular activities, but very competitive. If your child is smart but different in any way, they will emerge worse than when they started. Too large maybe... so many kids ignored. I’ve had 2 children attend, but I won’t send my 3rd here. As a teacher, GHHS always stands out to me because of the drive and motivation of the students. You can easily see the “bee hive” of energy by stopping by the media center during lunch time (filled to the brim with students working together and independently). To future GHHS students- yes, it’s a large school, but new students join daily . Whatever your interest is (theater set design, guitar, cyber security, etc,), there is a club/group/class that you can join and find your niche. Will some classes challenge you? Yes, but you will be well prepared for not only college but you’ll also have the necessary skills needed for today’s workplace. GHHS has fantastic teachers, counselors, coaches, administration, etc. who care deeply; they desire that all students not only succeed but thrive as individuals. It’s a fantastic school! As a parent, I have found that the new principal has zero interest, concern or love for this school or the students. She is systematically dismantling one of the best schools in the state. If you have choices -- make another one. I moved into this district specifically for the reputation of the school. Just as I moved in the old principal moved out and the new one has made one disappointing decision after another. The elimination of a very successful dance program that has been at the school more than a decade and the rude and dismissive tone to any parent that dares to speak up about the shortcoming of the Calculus program. Moral of the story is never move for a school. The biggest factor in your child’s success is you and your child. Overall, green hope isn’t an awful school. Unless you are gifted at math then it can be a struggle for lots of children. The culture at this school is very competitive and pushes you to take many APs and Honors classes. It’s also harder to get into college when coming from Green Hope. Most of the kids are pretty nice, but they can be a bit stuck up and self-absorbed. I have two students who attend here. One is sporty and another is artsy. They both have been able to find their niche & are getting a world class education. One is able to take honors courses, the other gets help with learning obstacles. The teachers are engaged & helpful. I don't know what is worse about this school. The academics, or the staff. The counselors who are supposed to be helping the students get ready for college, refuse to help the students who ask questions about college readiness and help them explore other programs outside of high school. The teachers assign more homework than in any other school that I have had experience with, forcing my student to quite their extracurriculars to maintain a high GPA. The teachers grade harshly and don't base their grading on how much the students learn, but rather on how well they listen to exact directions. Students are no longer focused on learning the material but rather doing exactly what the teachers want. This is harmful for their futures in college and this teaching system at this school is not setting up the kids for a successful future. The staff clearly does not truly care about students, as they often publicly humiliate students who may have broken a rule, such as dress code, rather than speaking with them in private or giving them a warning. The school is overcrowded to the point that half the students have classes in mods that are about 200 feet from the actual school, where they must walk there and back even in freezing temperatures or heavy rain. I was severely disappointed when I sent my child to this school. I expected teachers that help my children learn and staff that help my children be successful, but rather got immature staff and poor academics. I cannot begin to fully express my discontent with this school, but I hope this partly does it justice.

column1: Absolutely pathetic. The prep for the real world is missed - too many students now teaching, doesn't anyone actually get out of the city limits? There is zero prep for college. There is zero prep for the real world. The real world to people who live here is clouded with false ideas. The administration needs to get out of the 70's and stop worrying about dress codes, hair length and trying to win an athletic event and focus on preparing their young people for success. How about get a majority of the students off to college instead of trying to win a football or basketball game? In the end, you have ill prepared teachers - teachers who themselves have not had continuing education since they left college; and an administration who has no clue how to run a top performing educational institution. For you parents out there who think its so great - really? Your children are in the lower rankings of their peers.....oh but wait, most of you grew up there and now raising your children there. Now that's growth! There has been more emphasis on my son's appearance than his learning experience. The staff was quick to contact me with their concerns with my son but rarely, if at all, returned my calls about my concerns. To my chagrin, I am forced to make my son attend RISD for a second year due to work and financial complications. I have taken notice of the progeny of this educational system and city as a whole. It may be a great setting for those with an old line, stone age mentality, however, progressives need not apply!!!!

column1: Great school! I have been going to it since Kindergarten. Now, I am a Sophomore. Great facilities! Our 7 & 8th grade History Teacher, was named NATIONAL History Teacher of the Year, last year in 2010-2011 school year. The middle school has an annual history fair which is so much fun! The kids set up stands and talk about history from the Chinese Dynasties to Obama's Inauguration. Now about our athletic program, the coaches are absolutley AMAZING! I can honestly say I won't forget any of my coaches or teammates, they are practically a second family to me. Finally, our school band is AMAZING!! We have not only beaten schools in our district, but we have beaten Topeka HIgh's Band AND Orchestra along with other Topeka Schools. We also take a band trip every two years to a location decided by our conductor. While we are there, we will play at a competition, and we usually bring home a trophy I can't even start to tell your how many trophies we have in our band room! But all in all i believe that Royal Valley Elementary, Middle, ad High Schools are great and amazing schools! But the only weay to find out is to enroll your kid today! Check out the school's website: www.rv337.com If you have kids on either end of the spectrum this is not a good choice for school. They cannot handle either & then end up with disciplinary problems. The administration will not require any teacher to follow an IEP. Teachers are bigger bullies than the other kids. Especially against kids that need accomodations.

column3: Parent involvement is a key. I am new to the school with a 6th grader @ the middle school. I have attended the SAC meetings in the media center on the 2nd Tuesdays of the month @ 6pm. I am learning about all the exciting new programs the school is taking on for the students. The school is working hard to put students @ the top to be prepared for College or future careers. I want to be involved as much as I can for my 6th graders future. I hope ALL parents feel this way and start to Volunteer. I have two daughters who attend this school and they love it, but I think that they are too relaxed; there is not much for them to do when they are home. I would like to see them being challenged. There is not much motivation or anything that is pushing them to strive for the best. Marathon is a great school, but there is room for much improvement. After moving from Broward County at one of the "BEST" schools it had to offer that turned out to be a joke I am leary of public schools in Florida. Marathon has greatly changed my opinion. My daughter has excelled so far and has made such a huge turn around from the issues she had at her old school. Bullying is non-existant, teachers actually care and give the kids the attention they need. I'm so thrilled with this school and thankful this is the district we live in! Had a terrible experience here. Teachers spent more time "dealing" with troubled students than actually teaching. Which is probably why the average test scores are so low. This school also has its fair share of crime on and off campus. In the end it felt like this school only sees students as numbers and doesn't tend to care for them individually.To improve the overall experience here: The school's staff needs to further punish crime and trouble making students, care for each student as an individual, and get rid of the uncomfortable uniforms. The school itself needs a bigger cafeteria and cleaner restrooms. I went to this school for a little bit and ended up dropping out. Other schools were not and option for me. This school is by far the worst. There are teachers that physically harm students and principals who look the other way. Popularity among the staff and the students is based off how much money you have as well. Teachers will care much more for a student with wealthy parents and ignore ones who are lower then them. The whole school is a joke.

column1: It's not a good place if you want to actually learn This school is a monstrosity. My child has been bullied at this school since junior high and nothing has ever been done about it. The counselor is no help at all, the principle, Donna Kutac, has picked on my kid through the duration of their high school career. If you want to feel worthless, and learn nothing, go to this school. You're better off homeschooling you child or sending them to El Campo High School.

column3: A caring community supports this school. Opportunities abound in all areas of academics, music, and sports. The high school has been newly renovated and a new gym, sports facility and ag building have been added. A great place to send your high schoolers This school has a reputation of heavy bullying especially if you are non-hispanic. The principle believes he is the king of his own realm and refuses to work with parents. The education is extremely sub-par for the national average. Most emphasis is placed on sports (surprise). The only redeeming aspect of this school is the band program. This is a fantastic small school in a very welcoming community. Good balance between athletics arts and academics. I will never move my children to another school.

column1: I love Xavier High School. I know im only a Freshman but so far it's truly great. My sister is a senior. Everything is top notch! The BEST school I could ever hope to go to. Through my time at Xavier I have come to be a more complete person in every aspect of my life. Academically, Xavier ranks among the best in the state. The atmosphere there is incredible positive and supportive. The music and athletic programs are also among the elite anywhere. Catholicism permeates throughout the entire school and Christ's presence is felt everywhere. I could not imagine having gone anywhere else and I will certainly send my children to Xavier in the future. However, anyone should know that even though the high school is fantastic, sometimes the Xavier community (high school and middle school parents) is arrogant and full of themselves. They think they are more important then the school they support. But, don't let this dissuade you from sending your children there. The high school community is amazing and unique in the state. A character assination school which acheives mediocre academics given the amount of money poured into it. Not going to lie, I wasn't expecting to like Xavier. I actually wanted to go to a different, public, high school because a school like Xavier I thought was too uptown for my family. I was completely wrong lol! I have tons of friends here, everyone is nice, teachers are good (not the best but very nice), academics are a little harder but you'll manage if you study enough. It's pretty awesome here, not too big and not too small. The lunches are AMAZING here too. It's a race to get to lunch every day, that's how good the cooks are. My little brother is going here when he's old enough. No questions asked. This is a very expensive school to attend but they think it is reasonable to hand out $40 parking tickets. This school doesn’t even deserve one star. Save your money and go to public school for a positive experience and higher quality education. Great experience for my kids. They could express themselves and not be judged or told they cannot say something.

column3: As a student. This is my Senior year. I wish I had transferred to another school, this school was great Freshman, and Sophomore year, but now the school has turned around. There is hardly spirit week, no fun days outside like there used to be, and no school spirit at all. Everyday I wake up to a huge disappointment. I do not get respect from any of my teachers, I am not treated the way I should be especially when I ask a question, I am simply looked upon as a stupid person when I do. I never talk back or get in trouble. I just feel like my High School years have gone down the toilet, and I feel empty, and wish I could have moved. MHS is by far the best school I have ever had the pleasure of attending. The teachers have a good relationship with there students and the administration. The school it's self is run down but they stay up to date on the technology. It's not very gand like.. it's just not a fancy looking school... and the look makes parents worry that it's ghetto... but it's not... a earlier comment suggested that MHS gets medal detectors but I have never seen or heard of any violent weapons brought into the school... come to MHS

column1: My son and daughter have both been bullied repeatedly at this school. I brought it to the attention of the teachers and staff on 3 separate occasions and then I will see a front page article in the paper about how they have a handle on bullying. I can assure you that is not the case. If you are a basketball star you have it made. Other than that, forget it. I will say the special education teachers have gone above and beyond to help my student, but not so much the regular teachers. Special education is done in an "inclusion" setup in a regular classroom with regular students. I don't feel this has been a good mix as my student has not done well in this environment and the regular teachers are not equipped to handle his special needs. Surprised by some of these negative reviews I am reading. I attended this school and I most certainly didn't have a popular name associated within the community, and I was never a basketball star. I did however receive a good education and became very successful in life following graduation. South Ripley High School has made another leap forward in academic achievement. It has continued to improve from year to year and has added quite a bit of academic programing and technology since 2009. The completion of a $20 million dollar building program has given this small rural school corporation significant upgrades in science, fine arts, and computer access. The increase in dual credit courses, the availability of college courses in conjunction with IVY Tech Community College, and a college credit pre-engineering program they are definitely headed in the right direction. This corporation is an "A" rated school system in the state of Indiana with an Elementary rated as an "8" and a Jr. High a "10" by Great Schools so I find it hard to accept that they are only a "3" in your ratings. They have 1 Elementary, 1 Jr. High, and 1 High School building so I find it hard to believe they drop from a 10/10 to a 3/10 in quality from grade 8 to grade 9. They have a new principal and a 2nd year Superintendent that are working tirelessly with the staff to continue to improve . Above average and improving everyday. GO RAIDERS This school has come a long way in the last 5 years and my kids receive a quality education from South Ripley. The great schools ranking is way too low. At least a 6-7/10 on the low side. I have several children in this school since 1998 to present and have dealt with multiple instances of bullying. The staff and admins punish the victim as much if not more than the bully when they try to protect themselves, and offer NO solutions. They ignore the problems and brush everything under the rug, especially if your child is not an A-List child. They are very good at lip service and horrid at results. Real time grading is done as the instructors get around to it, and there's little to no communication when there are issues. They do like to call to say how well Little Johnny is doing on an assignment, but needing to know when there are issues tends to fall to the wayside until conferences, which they don't want you to attend unless your child is having issues. There are excellent teachers at SR but they're far outnumbered by the tenured staff that need to go. I agree with the poster who said there is preferential treatment depending on who you are. If your parent is a coach, a financial supporter of the school, if a family member is on the school board/staff, you can get away with anything, and you'll always be a starter. They fully deserve the 1-star rating. Bullying is an issue here. The parents of the bullies are lied to about the real reason their bully child was called into question. Rarely is the bully punished, or even reprimanded. The bully walks away thinking it was all a joke. Then rumors within the community start making it even harder for the one being bullied. The swinging door of leadership is enabling the issue. The one bullied teen walks away having not been helped, and self esteem even worse.

column3: Chaparral High School is one of the worst schools my daughter has ever been to. Not only based on her experiences and opinions but mine as a parent as well. They literally kick the students off school grounds during split class when lunch time is not available, at the end of the school year they demand to have the students belongings and hold them for two full days before returning them. That doesn't even make sense! As a parent I don't understand many of there practices. The teachers are horrible at mediating conflicts, as if they don't care about there students. My daughter was bothered many times throughout the year by other male students within her class while the teachers said nothing ,even when she reported this to the teacher, I can go on but I am running out of word count. I am currently filing many complaints concerning there school system. Please do not enroll your kids in this school. You may regret it as I have. ( Chaparral High School has transformed over the years into an excellent school. I'm proud to be a Cowboy and always will be. The teachers do their job and are helpful while the staff makes it exciting to go to school. Our school has been through its own trials and tribulations, but our Cowboy Pride has brightened up those dark moments. No one can knock us of our horse. Class of 2012. I am a [former] student of this school and I greatly enjoyed my time here. I made excellent friends and had some really great teachers that I actually learned from. I only gave the school four stars because I found the office staff to be quite...short and rude at times. Same with the counselors. I actually -hated- going to them sometimes. But I find that the teachers and other students made the school worthwhile. I haven't been to the school since the restructuring, but I have heard some great things. Couldnt want more from a school. The teachers have unique ways of teaching and you could fit into almost any classroom enviroment. Ive personally seen it change from a school labeled bad to a school that achieves what it wants. The extra-curricular programs are amazing and the camaraderie between the students and the teachers have made this school the most spirited that ive attended. I definitely recommend going to this school for the perfect high school experience. you know at first i did not wantto goto chap i wanted to goto vegas but then i got to know people and the students at chap and feel in love with the school everyone is so nice and they mind there own buisness im now a sophomore and proud my teachers took extra time out for me so i can pass and get all my credits so i would tell everyone to come to chap you can not judge a book by its cover an thats what people do well you cant judge unless you dont know that all i have to say I attended Chaparral Sophomore & Junior year and all I can say is...DON'T JUDGE A BOOK BY ITS COVER! This school is the absolute best in ccsd! Before I attended I thought it would be the worst years for highschool but I was wrong. The teachers are absolutely AMAZING! I never went to a school where the teachers actually understand where your coming from and they actually do everything in their power to make sure you walk across that stage. Shoutout to Mr. Coleman for making math actually enjoying! The students at Chaparral are great as well. Their nice, and will make you feel accepted to matter how different you are. 2011-before Chap was the most horrible school in Vegas but now, its one of the best. The ONLY bad thing I can say about this school is they are somewhat strict on dresscode. So watch out... All in all, I would attend this school Senior year if I wasn't moving. I already know my new school wont be as enjoyable. Enroll your child in Chap if you really want to see them with a diploma in their hand and have an awesome highschool experience for the next 4 years. LETS GO COWBOYS !! I went to Chaparral High school all my 4 years and teachers are helpful and supportive

column1: We were fortunate to have all our 3 children attend GK and continue on to higher education, their AP, Honor's and Band classes were commended by our children s. My son enjoyed his band trips as they were both enjoyable and dynamic. The school provided a way for them to prep and be challenged for their upcoming higher education and at the same time enjoy their time as a High School student as one should. One has graduated from University and his two other siblings are within 1 and 2 years behind him and they all say that GK was instrumental in there educations. Poor principal whose sole outlook is staff first student second. Such a shame. There are some great teachers, but a bad apple that has made our experience less than desirable. The counselors are wonderful, but they are limited by the principal. Who favors some staff. If you are looking for student first, this may not be the place for your child. Our first child tried this school also, but we found it to be the same so she changed schools where she flourished. I agree with the parent below that the principal only looks out for the staff and not the students. There was a problem with a teacher and just trying to get in touch with a principal is almost impossible. They also refuse to switch my child out of that class, even though I do not feel comfortable with my child being in her class. She is not professional at all and has no business teaching children. We have only been here for a year and already have had problems with two teachers that say something that is offensive. Awful, awful school. I am so happy my child will not be going there anymore. DONE. Lazy and rude office staff. Unprofessional teachers and disrespectful principals. I would recommend home schooling than ever sending another child to that school. This has been a wonderful tool for my child both educationally and socially. I only had one problem towards the end of this school year with an unprofessional teacher, but the issue was resolved. I was busy with day to day work but, I still made myself known and was physically present when needed for functions and for my son. I absolutely love the ROTC program here. Sgt. Sydney was awesome. We communicated almost weekly about what my son was and was not doing. He kept him on task there and I kept him on task at home. I almost hate to have to move just for this reason. I want my son challenged and with ROTC he was happy and challenged. My daughter is a sophomore at Graham Kapowsin High School. She started the school last year at the beginning of her freshman year. If your child is Hispanic or Black, this is a horrible school to attend. 95% of the staff are white and they target minorities, especially the administrators. They are a country school and have not done well with adjusting to minorities. The white students call the minority student racial slurs and administration does nothing to correct the behavior. I have filed a race discrimination complaint with the district and will transfer to another school in the district with more minorities. I attended as a junior at Graham-Kapowsin, I am a minority and majority of this school is white. It's very hard to fit in at this school if you aren't white. The culture of this school isn't welcoming at all, I only spent a semester at this school, in the very first couple days I experienced racial slurs and was picked on because of it. You'd think that a school of great expectations the teachers would know better not to be bias towards minority students. The culture at the school is unwelcoming. I understand the area this school is in and mainly white but the students need to be taught more about being friendly and welcoming towards other races. I was sick of the way I was being treated at this school. This school will let your kids fall behind Horrible! Like I said just because it’s a big new school doesn’t make it a better school than the rest.

column3: My son is having a great freshman school year and we are pleased with the academics at North Country. I do have concerns about safety and some disrespectful behavior of students to staff. Some solutions/programs to that end would be appreciated and needed I feel. I am currently a Freshman at North Country. And I tell it has only a few perks to it and that's it. This school has so much drama. And unless your a redneck or a Popular kid good luck fitting in. Im neither of these and its really hard. The only perk to the school is some of the staff is nice. A great principal! A great guidance dept. And a great couple of nurses we have. THATS IT. I dislike this school and am looking into other options for next year.

column1: The administration is not helpful. I do not know why I even bother going to them with an issue because I never get anywhere. It is very disappointing. Guidance is a joke, but the teachers seem to do well. Staff is caring and knowledgeable. Students are college or workforce ready.

column3: I wish my child had transferred to Creek sooner! Great school! Dedicated and involved staff, outstanding academic and athletic programs, welcoming environment from administration. We have never regretted the decision to transfer from parochial to public school for a minute. My child went through K-10 in parochial school and did very well, but has blossomed at Tates Creek. The perception of Creek is not very favorable, perhaps due to its location in the middle of a neighborhood that has in the past seen more than its fair share of crime. That perception does a grave disservice to the staff and administrators, and most of all, the students. Go Creek God awful teachers grade late and when grade reports come in it feels like all 8 classes start hitting you all at once. it sucks to go to this school A wonderful yet misunderstood school, which gives so much pride to those who attend. great loving environment people are way too harsh

column1: I am currently a Junior at Vista Ridge High School. I am also a Varsity Cheerleader, in Student Council, NHS, and AP/Honors student. I absolutely love Vista Ridge. Obviously it has its flaws but all schools do. Even though there are flaws most of the teachers are great teachers who really care. I am proud to be a Vista Ridge Wolf. When this school opened, my son was in the first graduating class..this was the best high school that my kids have been in. My other two kids hated leaving but when we were there we were really happy when they attended. The teachers are great and very helpful. Vista Ridge is a great school with so many enrichments, and academic quality. They really have quality teachers, and have after school study sessions for those who need it, a wonderful library, and a wonderful classroom enviorment. By going to this school, I have gained plenty scholarships from universities, and many opportunities to enhance my future. Through all the hard work I have put in to my education, and from the help of my outstanding teachers, I plan to graduate this year with a very successful future a head of me. I couldn't have done it without being a proud Vista Ridge Wolf! It's been good so far. It was nice to have the first day of school exclusively for 9th graders and to be greeted at the door with a "welcome to Vista Ridge" upon entering that first day! Honestly i started attending this school after moving from a dodds school in europe & i must say the adapting to the "public" school environment is tough. most of the teachers seem to be bored of their jobs so they teach very boringly. The best teachers who actually show excitement in teaching are Mr. Hites (spell check); Mr. Ockvirk; and Mr. Hill. Most of the teachers don't communicate with their students at all if they're confused about something. All they care about is their paycheck at the end of the day. The school has been nothing but drama hence the news & sometimes honestly i didn't want to go to school because it was just so boring. i mean seriously who just teaches by telling their students to write notes & then having a quiz the next day. it's stupid. anyways the positives. the students are pretty chill. some classes are fun & interesting. sports are alright. & the late starts on wednesdays. My children attend this school and they love it. Everything is brand new, and is up to date with technology. The teachers are absolutely wonderful. They care and want the kids to learn. This is an amazing school! I am so disappointed in Vista Ridge. I have contacted the 9th grade guidance counselor 15 times and still have unresolved issues. Currently they are only grading based upon test scores, so if your child is a great "tester" they will do GREAT at this school. However, if tests are hard for your child they will fall between all of the cracks. We are currently looking for a new school for my son. I cannot wait to get out of Vista! Can't get a hold of the guidance counselors Ever They don't return calls or emails. Can't contact counselling, can't contact attendance, the teachers are rude. I've only heard good things about a future teachers, namely Mr. Hill. My daughter's intelligence is wasted here. The school in new and beautiful inside but lacking in leadership. When my girls went here a few years ago they hated it! One of my daughters loves school so I know something was off. After the leadership issues many of the good teachers left. We ended up leaving the school as well. I'd rather drive my kids to a D20 school. I was happy with my choice to move them. I wish I would of done it sooner. One thing that shocked me is at parent info night we were required to pay additional fees based on the classes my daughters were in. One year it was close to $200! That's not counting the yearbooks and activity passes. The counseling department has helped my son and daughter so very much. Every time one of them goes into counseling they are friendly, very responsive and always willing to help in any way. My daughter has dealt with issues in the past and since we have moved schools she feels so comfortable in their environment. My daughter goes in and can speak with the secretary and does not feel judged or like she has to be embarrassed because she is there and she feels better after she leaves. I am very pleased with the way they handle the students. This district D49 & school pass kids onto the next grade regardless of if they pass their core courses. My son has graduated by the skin of his teeth yet he doesn't deserve to. The administration does not care. Since the 9th grade, I've been advocating for extra help, I got nothing. Finally, last year he began seeing a therapist and with a bipolar diagnosis, they made no mention that he was eligible for special needs accommodations. If I had it to do again he would have choices into D20. I am so disgusted with the principal and counselors. They are truly worthless to special needs kids and their parents. Vista Ridge High School was a waste of my tax dollars. I hope to change the district border so my neighborhood, which can go either way, definitely goes toward Academy School district 20! Meg Meadow should be released, principal Grose needs to be retrained. Horrible representation of educators. No wonder Coloradand are sooooo..... #dameshame!!!! Vista Ridge is the best high school in D49, however it is the best of the worst. The principal lacks leadership skills and common sense...has a view that kids should focus on what they can do well, and not be pushed at what they can't do. Frankly, I want my child to learn what he doesn't know well! Only a handful of teachers are great. The school policeman is pompous and is not kid friendly. He spends his time looking to handout as many traffic tickets as he can to parents on the street in front of the school. The school curriculum is horrible and doesn't come close to the many class choices other districts offer. The dance team coach did not care about her team last year and abruptly quit on the team before the last few games of the year, and the athletic director doesn't care about the dance team...and so, dance tryouts were held at the end of last year (for this year's team) by students and a parent, without the athletic director knowing. The parent/judge then brought her daughter in the last day of tryouts and she still made the team unfairly. It was brought to the attention of the athletic director and he let the team stay intact instead of making all the girls fairly tryout with a new staffed dance coach...many parents are upset. The counseling staff does not care about the kids or their schedules, and I could not get one of them to call me back until I threatened to call the administration building. This school is a waste of my tax dollars and is disappointing. I have moved my child to District 20 which also doesn't have nearly the fees that D49 has. This principal is clearly in the right line of work! He is enthusiastic about his job and deeply cares for the students. Also the guidance counselors are wonderful! Can't say enough great things about this wonderful school with a warm and caring staff. First of all, they took in 600 freshmen this year, through the choice in. This school cannot handle the volume. There are 80 kids in some classes, which are held in the common area's where there are too many distractions and the kids behavior is terrible and goes unchecked. The only thing the principle is concerned about here is the money he is getting, not the education of the students who are impacted. My son is in one of these classes and he is failing because he can't concentrate and can't get instruction due to the unruly behavior of the other kids. It is very clear that there are favorites by all staff, as some kids can do things and others can't. My children have been misplaced in classes that do not equal their skill level, nothing like setting kids up for failure. sports are a joke, again, if they like you, you play, if they don't, you don't, really has nothing to do with skill. My children will not be coming back next year. This is a fairly new school. They are working out kinks and adjusting where concerns are made. My son had attended this school for 3 years, 9-11, and will continue his senior year here. He has found great mentors in teachers, coaches, and admin. Mr. Gross is a beloved principle who listens to the students and respects their opinions. It has been a great experience and we love it. On my first day at a new school moving there from California, I sign up for ap european history, pre ap English 2, geomentry, chemistry, French 2, music theory and concert band. This school is so terriable! The counseling then put me in all regular classes. Can you believe this? Now I might be stuck in it for a whole year when I worked hard to be in ap at my old school and took all honors classes at my old school. The teachers are not welcoming and most can't even teach! The students are not nice to one another. Whatever you do don't send your kids here. Go to district 20 from my experience. Next year I'm going to the other school district. If you have a child who has any intentions of going to a high accedemic school spend the extra money and move to district 20. School doesn’t have an accedemic culture as a priority. It’s more for kids just hoping to graduate high school. My experience was okay not the best school . Really great school. Kind of like a charter school. Very strict but awesome teachers. I love it. My child is going to Berkley and my child who graduated last year went to Stanford. Really great for college readiness I think the school is great, especially the Afjrotc Team col Breedlove, and Msgt Tompson are awesome instructors I would definitely recommend Afjrotc.

column3: The one year that we were there, the leadership at that school leaves a lot to be desired. My daughter did not learn anything at that school, except how to fight. This school is a joke. I have no idea how high school age children are supposed to prepare for college and become productive adults when you have teachers allowing them to re-take tests as many times and they need to, just to get a passing grade. This will not happen in college (nor does it happen in any other school that I am aware of) and it teaches the child nothing about the need to study and come prepared to class. If they know they can just take the test over again until they pass it, what pushed them to study. By the third attempt they have already memorized the questions and should be able to pass without problems. This is a ridiculous way to teach and grade high school students. They have also just released new grading requirements. Teacher are unable to give a student a deduction in points if the assignment is late. How does this teach them to turn in homework on time if they know they won't lose points if its late?? I have never seen such an awful grading policy in my life. This school is teaching my step daughter nothing except that she can retake tests when she fails and not turn in homework until she is good and ready because she loses no points. Thanks Bryan Station, that is an excellent way to teach children! Very Good experiece for my son academic and sports related. I have had a great experience at this school. I understand that it had a questionable past, but they have worked hard and have been successful in turning it around. It’s unfortunate that most of the ratings on here do not reflect the change. It deserves another look. I attended for about 2 months, before my mental health declined. It was the worst. They didn't know how to handle the situation, I was getting made fun of by some girls, and etc.. My parents just ended up pulling me out and I've been doing online school since. It's the best choice I've ever made. great school it has been the best experience of my life I love it here, almost all of the teachers will listen and really care and talk to you about what is going on with you. I love the school and my classes with the inclusiveness of the school. I really like it here, but everyone has its ups and downs, and 3-star and below rankings for this school are kinda upsetting. I know our scores aren't the best, but you get so many opportunities to explore and adapt to what fits you the best. The students are amazing and friendly,, the teachers are chill for the most part it just depends on which one you have. I just finished my freshman year and it was a great welcome and beginning to my highschool years.

column1: Best school in the county. Lots of school spirit and very helpful teachers. Active in all levels of education and sports and the arts. Great teachers.
