column3: My son is a 10th grader at Chapel Hill. He transferred in from another high school. He has taken honors courses, etc and has found the rigor to be appropriate. He's now been recommended for AP courses next year. He got involved in FBLA, NJROTC and the golf team. I'm part of the parent support groups for two of these activities. I believe that is part of his success--parental involvement. I've come to know the teachers and principal and even the Sherriffs to be friendly, concerned and very engaged. We've traveled around the world in the military and can say CHHS is a great school. He's been to private schools too. Only one teacher I've dealt with has seemed indifferent. Over time she even came around. Overall- I think we've made a good choice in sending him to CHHS versus private school. i am curently a 9th grader at chapel hill high school and my expirience there has been good. the teachers are very supportive and want you to do and achieve your goals. if you want a good education come to chapel hills but if you are looking for a AMAZING sports programs you will not get that eventhough our softball, and cross country is good we are not as good in the other sports. This high school is a great school and i recomend it to anyone that is looking to go to this school. Overall, the teachers and staff do a good job. There are also various extra-curricular activities to take part in I am a student at chapel hill , my experience has been fine but could be a lot better. The dress code is very strict for it to be a public high school. Also the administrators do tend to go for the athletes more as well as the teaching staff, if your an athlete you have to have tough skin to go here. They look for every single thing you do wrong and even if you've done nothing they still try to find something. If your not an athlete the school is fine, the sports are okay, and the food is normal I am a current Freshman at Chapel Hill High School and I love it. The key to having a great experience at CHHS is to be involved. We offer a wonderful fine arts programs, a great drama department, and a lot of fun clubs. You are offered many different classes to choose from at CHHS. Our school has just been recognized as the AP school for the county. That gives a lot of students opportunities to take classes at our great school. We also have an amazing sports program. Volleyball made it to the state playoffs, football made it to playoffs, softball had one of the best years ever, XC did great, swimming has just started and they are doing amazing, basketball has started out with a win, and soccer had done great in the past. Chapel Hill is an over all great school, their is something for everyone to enjoy and have fun with. I would definitely recommend this school to anyone. I can honestly say that I have had a GREAT experience at Chapel Hill. Chapel Hill High has a great administration. CHHS has great clubs and sports. The classes aren't that hard. The schools lunch is not that bad. I think Chapel Hill is the best school in Douglas County. I am currently a freshmen at Chapel Hill High School, and my experience so far in the year has surely been an enjoyable one. The teachers are quite supportive and care about my education, which shocked me at first. If I do no understand a concept, they won't quit until I know what to do. I like the environment and the amount of extracurricular activities one can participate in. The only downside to attending this school is sports. From what I have seen and heard about, some of the sports teams here aren't so great. But overall, I would highly recommend this school for a student looking for a regular high school experience! Right now I am a freshman at CHHS. It's a great school with many great extra-curricular classes like Drafting and ROTC. You can sign for AP classes to get college credits, as well as honors classes. If you are struggling in a class, they also provide classes that take a slow approach to learning to make sure that you truly understand everything. You have many options for sports with Chapel Hill's great sports programs such as football, swimming and volleyball. I came to Chapel Hill from a small school called Brighten Academy which had trailers for classrooms and was probably a smaller school than the CHHS football field. I expected to be overwhelmed since I would be entering such a large school, but I wasn't. On the first day of school, Seniors and Staff told me where each of my classes were. It is a very friendly environment with great teachers and administrators. If anyone asks me where they should send their child, I would recommend Chapel Hill High School. I love this school. I knew from the very start that this was going to be a great academic school. There are no problems that I have encountered with this school. I already know that in the future when I am in college, I will look back to these days and realize that this school, is what helped me most in college. This school can prepare a student for college unlike any other school. They have teachers that make sure you understand exactly what you are learning. The administrators take care of everything they need to take care of. If there is any school I'd recommend to attend, it's Chapel Hill High School. Chapel Hill High School is definitely the best choice of all the high schools in Douglas County. I currently am a student here and I am a freshman. I originally thought that this school was going to have super easy classes. But truly our teachers try to challenge us as much as possible. CHHS offers AP classes and honors classes. Chapel Hill's athletic programs and clubs offer a variety of choices to find the activity perfect for you! I am currently on the swim team and involved in HOSA (Health Occupation Students of America). Our administration provides a safe and healthy learning environment as well. CHHS also has a AP Magnet Program which offers students from everywhere to come to Chapel Hill and participate in our AP classes. CHHS will for sure be the perfect choice for every student! CHHS is not the best school, but it's not the worst. Administration is really strict on dress code. Our football team is officially the worst team in Douglas County. However, it is a learning environment and has plenty of productive clubs an opportunities. It still feels like a prison. Lunch is basic, but edible; I recommend bringing your own lunch. Bus routes could be changed because from riding my own bus, I know they have routes that make them go in circles and waste time. I am currently a freshman and the school is ok simply because my friends go here. I personally do not like all the teachers because most of them sit around, eat, put a slide on the screen and tell you to copy it. Next day in class there is a test. No elaboration or explanation on the notes. I'm currently a freshmen here at Chapel Hill and so far it's been really enjoyable. Chapel Hill provides a variety of sports and clubs to choose from such as softball, volleyball, swimming, tennis and much more. The teaching staff here at Chapel Hill is very supportive and they're always here to make sure you understand what you're learning whether it's before or after school, because they care about you and your education. Here at Chapel Hill you have the opportunity to sign up for AP classes and earn college credit. Chapel hill not only provides you with an amazing high school experience it also prepares you for college. Chapel Hill is friendly and organized learning environment where I can strive to be the best that I can be. If you had to choose a school, I would definitely recommend Chapel Hill High School. I am a freshman here at Chapel Hill and in my short time at the school there have been several pros and cons I have seen. From a student's POV they would say the dress code is very strict because CHHS is the only school in DCSS that makes males tuck in their shirts, but to be honest it isn't that bad. Statistics show that many people are very complementary of kids behavior and appearance at CHHS. Next, the lunch quality was a huge jump from middle school. I was formerly a Yeager Mustang, and brought my lunch to school every day of the year. I haven't brought my lunch one time this school year because the food is fairly good. Go ahead and brag about how good ALX is but check the CCRPI please. Thank you and GO PANTHERS! I'm currently a freshman at Chapel Hill High School. This is actually my first year at a public school since I have attended private schools basically throughout my entire life. I'm a straight A student with good conduct and for that reason, I was scared that I'd be an outsider. I was prepared to see fights everywhere, but that wasn't the case, which was amazing to know. On the other hand when I first moved here, I was far too excited to stop wearing uniforms, however I didn't think that CHHS would have strict guidelines on their dress code, but I'm quite happy that they do. It definitely prevents many teenagers from dressing inappropriately since it is a school. I'm also thankful for being involved in many clubs such as HOSA, Key Club, and FBLA. I haven't played any sports for CHHS yet, but they definitely have good, competitive teams. As far the school staff, they're alright. That being said, I have extremely high standards, but for a public school, CHHS meets most of them. Overall CHHS is a good school, but it could honestly improve in food and making their classes more challenging. I am currently a freshman at Chapel Hill and I m enrolled in the AP Magnet program that is new to our school this year. The program allows freshman to take AP courses and later start dual enrollment to get college credit. If you ll be going to Chapel Hill anytime soon, I d recommend taking advantage of this program and what it offers. Overall the school is a great school; the teachers provide tutoring before and after school for students who might need a little extra help, and where academics is concerned, I d say our school is one of the best in the county. Our sports programs are decent. Our football team is not the greatest (we re probably the worst), but every other sports team is doing really well. There are clubs and activities that you can join and benefit from. Chapel Hill is a good school. Being a student at CHHS I know the atmosphere here is more like that of a middle school instead of a highschool. The dress code is rather strict for students that are 14-18, especially in comparison to the county's other schools. My middle school actually had the same dress code (no holes above the knee, no uncovered shoulders, three-inch skirt rule, etc.). The school is strict and i feel the student body would enjoy their time much more if the school toned down a bit. The teaching staff is a saving grace of CHHS. You can tell that they care about their students and our grades and futures. Other than dress code and the teachers, their is lunch which I don't particularly care for, they don't have halal, kosher, nor certified organic foods either (a downer). But they do serve salad as an alternative to non-carnivorous students. In the vending machines however; you will only find sugar-free, fat-free, extremely falsified-health-conscious snacks. Regarding parental involvement, I'm not sure about how active the PTA is, and clubs, there is a vary of clubs for different students. Overall, anyone should send their child here if you're looking for a focused on education for them. Chapel Hill High School is a true school of excellence. With its comprehensive curriculum and its constant drive to be the best, this is truly a school to be proud of. All of the teachers and staff work their hardest to ensure the best learning environment for our students. Chapel Hill exhibits a amazing level of concern and involvement in our lives. Chapel Hill takes pride in their fine arts and sports in a manner of respect and great support. And I am honored to call myself a Panther! Chapel Hill High School is a great academic school that is multicultural and has a great academic record. The teachers and students strive for excellence everyday in and out of the classroom. However i think some of the rules are a bit over the top, for instance no phones allowed until 3:40. None the less this is a school of the best getting better. chapel hill high school is pretty fantastic. Most of the teachers get very envovled with their teachings and make sure to interact with students. They care for your grade and try to benefit you in every way possible. Which means make up tests are a huge plus! School food honestly isn't all that bad and the salads are excellent. This school also provides many clubs and organization it kinda hard to not to fit in somewhere. You always feel a part of something. Not only is it fun but allows you great advantages when applying to colleges!! overall this school is perfect for my academic needs. I'm a freshman at Chapel Hill, and I think it's great. I'm in the AP magnet program. Not only is this school fun, but its involving. I've been in The !A Play, French Honor Society, sports, tutoring (due to absences), Gospel Choir,, and I'm planning on doing even more. I've moved around just about every year of my life, and this school, by far, has some of the best discipline I've ever seen in my entire life. We did a class activity where we rated our school and the average overall rating was an outstanding 8 (including those who rated like 1 just because). Anyone who doesn't like this school is probably basing it off one particular experience (meaning they messed themselves up). As long as you pull your weight, you'll do great and will love thus school just as much as I do. Though this school has a very struck dress code I still believe it is a very good school. In our math class we rated our school on a 1-10 number line and most people rated the school in the 6-10 range which is high. I feel that the school is very responsible. It focuses on the academic aspect of student learning and keep students safe. Chapel Hill also is great programs that people who can get involved in. We can get in to charities, sports, the arts, and etc. Even though this school is pretty good, it really doesn't make the social interaction an important part of the school. Eat even though everyone can get their group of people to hang out with, but it is not encouraged to go out there and meet new people. That is how I feel about you up with you high school. Im a junior at CHHS. I don't like majority of the people here but the school itself is not that bad. I think Chapel Hill High School is the best high school in Douglas County. Most of the teachers are great and try to be very involved with every student. I enjoy going gong to Chapel Hill, I've been there for 3 years and I've enjoyed each and every year. At, CHHS, my classmates averages sports to a 5.8 and lunch as a 4.7 out of 10. The deviation for both categories are high. Sport's range is a 7, lunch's range is a 6. 3 is the interquartile range both sports and lunch. Many students will say they don't like Chapel Hill. Most of that reason is because we do have a strict dress code and no technology. These strict rules have an advantage of having really high test scores. Our school is very intelligent. Having a dress code makes us look professional and sophisticated, and it gets us ready for the real world. We should be thankful our school cares about our appearance and future. I would say Chapel Hill is the only high school in the county that actually gets you ready for the real world. So Chapel Hill is a pretty decent school, most of the teachers are pretty chill and helpful, and the lessons are thoroughly delivered. I'll admit that we don't have the best football team, but where they lack, the education substitutes. There's a large variety of clubs and extra-curricular activities for us students to participate in, and to expand the learning experience. There are a few things that aren't so fantastic at CHHS, like the basic complaints we all have about the quality of our lunch meat and things of that nature, and of course there's quite a bit of unnecessary drama, but that is inevitable at really any high school. Its part of the experience. If I do say so myself though, I don't really regret coming here. I hear a lot of good talk about us, so, the administration must be doing something right. Chapel Hill High School is a school that is for students who are not good at everything, but want to challenge themselves in the subjects they are good at. CHHS is an A.P. Magnet school that has great teachers that are willing to help you if you need it. When it comes to sports CHHS has a great softball team that is ranked number 1 in the state, if you compete in cross country or track you are in luck Because they are good. If you are looking for a school with good food then you need to home school... For these reasons I'd give CHHS a 7.5/10 CHHS is actually a pretty nice cool. When comparing to English classes and teachers, on average student would give both topics and your seven. Saying that they are not that bad; that they are actually pretty good. My classmates and I recently analyzed what students Think about CHHS. The data I collected was based on 15 student opinions. I researched extra curricular activities and sports. Most students gave our extra curricular programs at 6.8 out of 10. Chapel Hill has many extra curricular options as well as many clubs you can join. For sports, The ranking was about 5.75 out of 10, mainly because students dislike how our football team ranks among other schools, but we are first in state in softball! Being a 9th grade student at CHHS isn't as bad as most people say it is. we may not have as much freedom as other schools, we may have to tuck our shirts in if we are guys, and we may not be able to use our cell phones, but all of these rules help us become smarter and more behaved students. here at chapel hill we have many amazing academic courses to choose from. for the most part, every teacher is very good. out of all of my teachers there is only one I have issues with. the teachers keep everyone on track and busy doing what they need to do to succeed. the disciplinary administrators are very strict people. I once was written up from my cell phone vibrating in class. I do think this might have been a little to ridiculous. If this happens more than once, you have to come to school Saturday and serve work detail. the athletic teams are outstanding and have amazing coaches. our softball team just won state this year ! in order to play you have to be passing at least 5 of your 8 classes. so coming from me, if you are planning on moving into the Douglas county school district, I defiantly recommend Chapel Hill High School as a good choice of a school. If a student wants to be heard for the mistreatment from the administration..... it will never happen. All five of the administrators do not listen to their students, unless you are the most liked from them. Besides that a student will not be heard no matter how hard they try. I don't care about the dress code, or no cell phones, you get used to it. Although, what I will not get used to is an administrator trying to give me ISS because of a lie ONE girl said I did. Never did I have the chance to express my side, neither did my friends. We all had witnesses over the issue to prove we did nothing wrong, but instead the administrator decided to listen to ONE girl whose side made absolutely no sense just because she is close with her parents. So many negative things I can say about this school BESIDES the dress code, no cell phones, and unequal treatment. Nine times out of ten, the "consequence" they give students never fits the act the student has done. Nine times out of ten, Chapel Hill will never dare to hear an issue a student is having with the administration. These administrators are so prideful and insolent. They will never listen to a students problem that they are having with the ADMINISTRATION. This is for the ADMINISTRATION, not the teachers, not other students, but the ADMINISTRATION. They say on the announcements every day "feeling untreated by a teacher, you can come to one of us about it" Well what if I'm having a problem with how unfair the administrators are being with the students? I would like to come talk to the administrators about it, without being sent to ISS for speaking up in a respectful manner. Unlike the administrators, they scream in your face for something so over the top like flipping a water bottle, or standing outside in the afternoon at the buses WHERE YOU ARE SUPPOSED TO BE. Let the students be heard. You know what could fix this issue? Start having student-parent meetings after school for those who are having issue with the administrators and/or teachers. Let us express our issues without belittling us. You want to make Chapel Hill a great school? Let the students be heard. This school has room for improvement. It has in the past accused me of doing something bad even though i did not do it. It has a rule that you have to tuck in your shirt and no hats. It will not allow to express your fashion and who you are. The teachers are good as a freshmen and really try to help you in the classroom. Overall the teachers are good, but the administrators and rules are pretty bad. The school is able to improve with just minor changes. Chapel Hill High School is a school that could use a little bit of improvement however it is not the worst school in the county. I feel that the teachers sometimes do not help students when they are struggling with certain material, and sometimes the teachers do not teach the material in a way students can learn it. The administrators are sometimes not very helpful with students. They are very picky on the dress code and are not always very friendly. The academics at Chapel Hill are very good. The majority of students pass their exams at the end of every school year. The sports teams are not the best, but they are not terrible. There are several clubs for students to participate in, but I feel like they are not very well organized. Some rules at Chapel Hill are a little too strict in my opinion including the rules about dress code and cell phone use. High school students should be able to have a little more freedom. The students at Chapel Hill are friendly overall. . Chapel Hill is a very diverse school in all aspects. It tries to give equal support to the fine arts, clubs, as well as sports programs. The school encourages academic excellence and student acceleration. It makes it a point to include everyone and provide many options for students to choose from. Options include things such as "Work based learning" , " Dual Enrollment", and all our various clubs. The administration can be very by-the-book and is not very lenient. There "wiggle room" is minimal and strict, however it does produce students who are college and real life ready. Students are prepared to take the next step. Academics is also very strongly emphasized at the school. Teachers are generally well prepared and willing to help out students, discuss, and teach according to plan. If your student is hard working, loves to be involved, and prepared for a school of excellence and rules, CHHS is for you! CHHS is one of the best high schools you could go to in Douglas County. I say this because even though the school is strict they are only this way to keep the students safe. The dress code is very limited but this is so all the students look presentable at school. If your child is into sports we have a wide variety of activities they could do but I encourage the school to have more. If your child likes clubs we have options but there is not a vast majority. If you are concerned about our academics we have the AP program and a great honor program so I encourage your child to join the panther family. Chapel Hill High School is a nice school with a variety of classes, programs, extra circulars, clubs, and sports to join. There are a large number of teachers and coaches to help you become successful throughout you high school career. There are a variety of classes to take throughout your 4 years in Language Arts, Math, Science, and Social Studies and also a variety of electives. Foreign languages offered here are Spanish and French ranging from I to AP. Chapel Hill also offers the capstone program. Plus, they have a variety of sports including, but not limited to, baseball, basketball, cross country, football, and swim. Games and meets are a great way to connect with your peers and have an enjoyable time. The school lunches aren't particularly great but they are feeding around 2,000 students a day. Luckily, every Thursday is nacho which is very popular among the student body. The school also has very kind administrators and a set of advisors to help students with their needs and questions about different programs. Last, but not least, CHHS has what some describe as "strict" rules which require no use of electronics during the school day, boys to tuck in their shirts, no mid drift is to show, no leggings, no holes above the knee without a sewn in patch, and a 3 inch rule pertaining to the wearing of shorts. This helps keep things black and white and keeps judgement off the table. In conclusion, I give Chapel Hill a 9 out of 10. Not impressed at all will never send my child back!! My kids have done well and developed strong academic skills. They have made strong bonds with the teaching staff and are always encouraged to work hard. the experience I've had with this school has been great with both of my grandsons. My eldest grandson is in his 2nd year of college and is doing well thanks to the training he had at Chapel Hill. The 9th grader is just starting high school and I think he is doing good. Thank you for the support that you are giving these students. This school is overall very good and works very well with its students. I have no problem with any of my teachers. They all provide everything they can for extra help and one on one works. Although there is a varying attitude among the students, I feel if you can tune out the bad you will be able to focus on yourself and your ambitions. The administration is amazingly close and understanding of the student body and their opinions. I’m glad I chose to go here and use their AP magnet program. There are many many options for student classes and they even provide a “pathways” system that helps students to take classes to get them closer to what they want to be and college opportunities. This school is very well developed and I continue to see growth here as a student. This school overall is a good school. Chapel Hill is one of the strictest high-schools in the county. Dress code is stricter and is enforce thoroughly. Students are expected to comply with the rules or strict measures are taken. Many students don't talk highly about this school because of admin rules but at the end of the day education at this school is effective. And is a number one priority in this school. There only about 2 pep rallies in the school and phones are not allowed in the building EVEN AT LUNCH. Overall, the school is good but the high school experience you get at this school is poor. Not much freedom is given to students making students very unhappy. Education shouldn't just be about desk work and homework. High school is a once in a lifetime experience and Chapel Hill limits the memories you can have. There are many pros and cons to Chapel Hill High School that can impact an individuals learning some more than others. This school is way too harsh on students. The dress code here is insane, along with cell phone policies. You cannot show a centimeter of your shoulder or else the administration throws a fit. One day, I came to school in a dress that was WITHIN regulations. it did not exceed three inches above my knee. THEY MADE ME CHANGE. meanwhile, a girl wearing the SAME EXACT DRESS the following day faced no repercussions. Now for the cell phone policy: this is by far the strictest school on cell phones. Not only can we not use them in the mornings BEFORE school starts, but we can’t use them during lunch and the teachers have to get PERMISSION to allow us to use them. Its insane. The only reason I am going to this school is because I would’ve had to go to New Manchester. If New Man didn’t have so many issues regarding student behavior, I would transfer there in a heartbeat. My rating was gracious, step it up, Chapel Hill!!! Terrible, honestly the worst school I've ever attended. I Left the school just before my senior year in order to be able to graduate without being bullied by the Administration staff. If you are a Christian Athlete at this school, you will be given special treatment and the staff will bend over backwards for you, but if you are neither of those things tough luck. Also, if you're wealthy you will get special treatment as well. Hopefully the county will fire the principal and the entire administration staff. Chapel Hill High School is a school were everybody has fun but still gets the education they need. As a student that goes to this school, i can guarantee that your child will gain the education they deserve and also have a great high school experience. They offer many after school activities; there is something for everybody at the school. 9 I;ve been here for a few months and i think its pretty neat, I can't complain. My experience at Chapel Hill has been fun. Other than unnecessary dess code and phone restrictions, I enjoy my time at school. The students are friendly and the extra curricular activies are a great way for students to meet new people. Some of my teachers were really good at their job and actually had me looking forward to school. I pllay a sport adn even if athletics aren't the best, students still come to support the school. Chapel Hill is a good school. There are areas where it does very well like are clubs. There is a club for any and everyone. Any hobby you can think of is represented and it helps students feel like they fit in with people who have the same interests as them. I also think the school does well in sports. We may not win every game, but the coaches do an amazing job on building not only skill, but character. Our athletes are very respectful and try to be good students even when they aren’t competing. The faculty and certain clubs do well in trying to make the school year fun with different activities like PowderPuff, the Lip Dub and other things. There are areas that could definitely use some improvement though. We have some great teachers, but there are some that don’t have the best attitude towards students. I understand that we don’t have to be friends, but just basic respect when they ask something of students could go a long way. Also, I feel like administration doesn’t prioritize as best as they should. They are very strict on dress code and their cellphone policy, but in situations where you would think it would be an uproar, they either aren’t aware of or they just don’t do more than a slap of the wrist (speaking metaphorically, Chapel Hill doesn’t hit their kids). Overall, I would recommend this school to others because it’s a good school. Just this year alone, I’ve seen changes and improvements, so I feel like Chapel Hill is on the right path to help push us and help us grow.

Grant may have a great curriculum but the way students are tested is horrible. It is about memorizing facts but in reality one needs to be able I analyze and think critically about different situations. This school doesn't do that. column3: Besides our lack of school spirit and lack of diversity, I think DHS is an amazing school. And it has a lot to do with the teachers. Yes there are some teachers that are strict and pile on the work, but most of them are really great. I can honestly say that I loved all my teachers including the ones this year that I barely know yet. I know I can go to them to talk about anything, and I think they do a terrific job at relating with the students and making classes fun and interesting. Our sports teams are unbelievable (except for maybe boys basketball- sorry guys). And we have so many different clubs that it's impossible for you not to fit in anywhere. And about the diversity thing, I know it looks really bad how 96% of our school is white, but I don't necessarily think that makes the students discriminate against other races. And in my core friend group (8 people), we have heights from 4"11' - 6"0', races from Black to Asian to Italian to German to Irish, and religions from Mormon to Catholic to Presbyterian to Atheist. My friends and I are very diverse and so I think I've personally been affected by the "Darien Bubble". I just know that I love it here :) This school was one of the worst experiences of my life. I got bullied and whenever I brought it to someones attention, they shrugged it off because my bulliers were doing extremely well in sports and they didn't want to affect their athletic careers. I played lacrosse here, and it was the only important thing to the school. My academics were put aside and were under appreciated. I went to dhs for freshman year, but then got out of here as soon as I could. The kids are rude, entitled, brats, and the teachers have no clue how to deal with them. The diversity in this town is so appalling, and I don't know why anyone would want to send there kid here. When we moved to Darien from New Jersey, we walked in blindly, without knowing what to expect from the school and community. I have two kids that are currently juniors in high school, and even though they were concerned about the new environment, they really liked how attentive school staff and classmates are. They participate in AP classes and were able to keep their grades up.I would definitely recommend the school to anyone who wants a quality education and a good environment for their children. For the right kid, this school is amazing. There is a wide variety of activities and courses, the facilities are outstanding, and the academic expectations are high. Excellent in every respect. Rich choice of activities and academics. Experienced counselors and teachers and positive atmosphere. Strong support for IEP and 509.

column1: My four children graduated from Washington County High School and they are all highly successful. Three out of the four graduated from college without any difficulty at all. They have also gone on to obtain additional degrees. The fourth is still an undergraduate in college. The teachers and administration at this school are very knowledgeable, caring and helpful. There are always teachers willing to stay after school to help students. Some teachers even come in on Saturdays to help students with their academics. This schools also has a challenging academic curriculum. If a student from this school isn't prepared for college, it's because they didn't put out any effort or take advantage of the services offered. Graduated from this school. Didn't prepare me at all for college. A few of the teachers are extremely rude and I even had one tell me I wouldn't go on to college. I made it to college and will soon graduate with two degrees. There are a few teachers I would thank deeply for believing in, the rest of my credit would go to my college professors who helped push me along.

column3: I detest this school. The entire educational system is horrible. I never learned anything in this school. Unfortunately, I am not struggling in college. I definitely regret the decisions my parents made, they ruined my high school experience. I would not recommend this school at all. I definitely detest this school. The teachers are absolutely horrible. To be quite honest, I learned nothing throughout high school. I had the worst expirience with the principal and staff at MAST. My child was suffering and being bullied daily at this school. We complained to the school and nothing was done. I would not recommend this school. My daughter just transferred from a private school and the academic standards are very high. When you walk around the school you get a sense of high energy and love of school from its students. The curriculum is tilted towards the science, my daughter has 3 science classes this year. So far, she likes it... so I like it. I'm a student here, and the environment is incredible, the teachers and staff are dedicated. Teachers and students are a lot closer than in normal schools offering a more personal learning experience which makes it easier for any student to do good in school. I'm enjoying my time in this school. My daughter is a student here and she is really happy about the school. Academic level is great. She is part of the swimming team. Next year two more sons will join the school. This is the year 6th grade opened. My child was unlucky to be amongst the 6th grade 'guinea pigs'. Unfortunately the school didn't live up to its reputation nor my expectations at all, I'm very disappointed. It is completely unequipped to guide kids coming out of elementary; 5 out of the the 7 teachers my child had, ranged from average to appalling, with the exception of wonderful Ms Ruppel and Mr Fahmie who are absolutely fantastic educators and role models. I'm actually considering switching my child to a different school in the future, depending on how 7th grade goes. I hope they have more than two good teachers in the 7th grade! My child adapted well, but isn't thrilled nor impressed with her school experience at Mast either. I'm a freshman/9th grader at this school for the 2021-2022 school year. I only came to Mast Academy this year and so far it has been pretty good. The school is a lot cleaner and spacious than I thought it would be. The teachers are younger so they can relate to you a bit more and the teachers I have are great at helping with academics/ extracurriculars, like Mr. Partagas for English, Ms. Gonzalez for History, and Mr. Lacayo for Art. With the homework, however, I think they give too much of it, I know that the school is supposed to be a stem school with rigorous academics, but I simply don't really have a lot of free time anymore. I mostly use my free time to study for quizzes and naps now. If you want to go to a stem school with a great environment and tons of great students and peers, I totally recommend it, but I don't think that you will have a lot of free time if you go here. Let me start by stating that this is one of the best schools in the country, it is ranked within the first 50. Teachers are amazing with very few exemptions. Students are challenged and made hard working individuals. The new principal has made a difference and her leadership skills create a wonderful atmosphere. Both my children have had amazing growth in academics. They have a strong and dedicated PTA Board that always has our children’s best interest at heart. The PTA is always allowing volunteering opportunities which makes it great for parents to come into the school. I absolutely love this school, I admire the leadership from the principal, I see the care that teachers have for the students, the administration is always kind and helpful. The PTA is welcoming and ready to advocate. The students are very nice and educated. This is a wonderful school and I am thrilled that my children had the opportunity to came here. They don’t teach well. Big problem with teachers, they focused more in giving homework than to teach and they don’t care about the well being of the students. Basically the system is designed for those kids who can studied by them selfs.

column1: I am a 10th grader at this school and on the topic of homework, it may take a while to get used to especially when compared to the amount given in middle school. The key to avoiding tension and the feeling of being overwhelmed is to aviod procrastation at all costs!! Take my advice, I've been there and done it all. Good Luck. ;)

column3: I had high hopes for this school, but now that I attend here as a freshmen I'm pretty dissapointed. The school is overcrowded and the people here are not always friendly, but that's only part of the problem. The big problem is that they put everybody into the MYP program for 9th and 10th graders, and that's not a good thing. Not every student wants to be challenged, and not every student deserves to be in a class where they distract other people who do want to learn. And worst of all, they put everybody into the IB program if they pass the HSPE. This is stupid because not every student who gets pushed into the IB program wants to be there, and not every student in IB deserves to have an IB diploma simply because they were pushed into it. From what I hear, this is also becoming a problem at Decatur for the AP program and at Federal Way High for the Cambridge program. If you can help it, avoid going to any school in this district whatsoever. This district has no idea what they are doing and are creating problems that shouldn't have to be dealt with in the first place. I know that TJ has been a great academic school in the past but it has gone down hill. There are average, terrible, and great teachers. All the teachers are treated the same: horribly and disrespected. This past year none of the teachers knew what was going on because of the new grading system. I just want to say, Don't do something you don't know how to do. All the students were taught differently and confused. Different curriculum throughout the three different teachers for the same exact class. Apart from the few amazing teachers I've had, most tell you hat you're doing that day, give it to you, then, expect you to do it on your own while they're on the computer or talking to other staff. Curriculum: I give it a 3.4, teachers, on average: 3, involvement in students: 2.9, and all around: 3.5. I had high hopes for this school but I've attended it for two years and I am somewhat dissapointed in my experience here. The problem isn't really a school problem, but more of a district problem and I believe it is starting to become a state problem. The FW district installed a new grading system that is very confusing and is difficult to understand exactly where you are standing. At least you used to be able to have a good idea of how well you were doing when they had percentages (70% = average, 80% = good and so on) but for some reason the district thought it would be a good idea to use standards instead of percentages that you either pass or fail. It wasn't because a great number of students failed last year and I imagine a good chunk will possibly fail this year as well. Now, this is the last year they are required to do this grading system so perhaps it will get better next year but I wouldn't bet on it. Try avoiding going to this district, and if you can help it try avoiding going to the neighboring districts (kent, auburn, sumner) as well. As for this school, education is good, some teachers are good. If you're competitive about sports, try another school. SO I HEAR FROM VALID SOURCE THE KIDS ARE ALLOWED TO WATCH TV ON THEIR PHONES ALL DAY INSTEAD OF LEARN, THEY STREAM NETFLIX AND VIMEO IN CLASS> OH BUT THEY GET A GRADES ? HOW IS THAT POSSIBLE >? MAYBE TEACHERS JUST THERE TO COLLECT A CHECK INSTEAD OF EDUCATE Im glad that my student goes here. She will have great advantages in preparing for college. The teachers were unprofessional, and the school itself was a huge downgrade from the terrible school in California we transferred from. I told my son when he gets into high school things will be different. Now I look like a liar. TJ is a joke. The staff are rude, unprofessional and jaded. They don't care and it shows. My son has come home telling me stories about what's going on in class. As the parent of a teenager I know sometimes things can be exaggerated. I was astonished when I attending his curriculum night and conferences. Everything I had been told, was very apparent. You'd think the teachers would turn on the charm while addressing the parents, even though they are the opposite in class. Nope. His English teacher flat out told me these kids "are a product of their environment so there's no point of investing one on one time with these students because they're going to do what they do." Uh, excuse me? My tax dollars are paying your paycheck. And you're going to sit here and flat out tell me to my face, in front of everyone that you don't give a hoot about him? I contacted the school, who referred me to the Vice Principle whom I was told is this teacher's superior. Not only did I inform her of the experience I had at the conference, but with the things she's been doing and saying to the children in class. I demanded they take my son out of this class and put him into another. The Vice Principle said she would speak with the teacher to come up with a solution. I got a call back saying the teacher denied what she said to myself and my son in front of the other students and parents waiting in line to see her. (Yes, wait in line. They give you a paper and have the teachers sitting around. You take the paper to each teacher to sign when they talk to you. Which is ridiculous because everything being discussed is heard by everyone around.) Only for the VP to tell me that they can't because they would have to switch another class because there were no other ELA classes that period. The class they'd have to switch is offered the other period w/ the same teacher. I told my son to video tape her actions with his cellphone when she is doing or saying something that isn't appropriate. I now have four recordings that I will be taking to the superintendent. The ELA teacher can say and deny whatever she wants. The video recording doesn't lie. My kids all are receiving a great education from very dedicated teachers who care about the kids and the material they learn. In my opinion, I think TJ is a good school. Most of the staff and teachers here are knowledgeable about their subjects and are helpful whenever you are stuck, Though there are a couple of less helpful teachers, I am sure this is the case for most schools. This school doesn't have a very strict rule about phones but it is up to you whether you want to learn the material or not. Overall, I recommend TJ. i love this school, the students and teachers are great but some of the teachers are weird in there own ways but i recommend this school 100% The TJ experience was great. Teachers (especially math) were professional and helpful but required assignment completions. They even offered our son after hours and weekend support with groups of students. Running Start was a great opportunity and well monitored. I'm am a student at this school and its big and nice but fights happen everyday and the bullying is out of control i had a anxiety attack on Tuesday and the staff didn't help me worse school ever

column1: I ask about sitting in on my child's classes I was told that the teacher had to give me permission first. Sounds like they don't want you to be a part of your child's education.Makes you wonder what they are trying to hide. I ask about having lunch with my child and was told they had to see if parents could still do this. I was allowed, but have you ever heard of not being able to have lunch with your child? Two teachers did not respond to my email addressing issues with my child even after a week went by. When ask about it I received an apology. They do not have a firewall on their computers so you not only have to be concerned about what they are doing online at home but you also have to worry about what they are doing at school. In the Honor's program A&P is an elective...what is up with this??She is not getting a proper education here.If I could get my child into any other school I would and have been seeking other avenues. What has happened to this school system??? I'm heading into 9th grade at Douglas Byrd High School. Only because I got redistricted from Jack Britt to now Douglas Byrd. But, as of now I don't find the school appealing to go to in any form. First, the so called "open house" was unorganized. There was only mentors there and no teachers! So I couldn't meet any of my teachers sadly. Also, they made the freshmen play games for the "open house" which I found ridiculous. Because I though I was going there to meet teachers. Second, a school is supposed to give you a good education with good grammar. But that seems not to be met,since their motto is " Got Swag?". "Swag" being a slang word,how is that teaching students good grammar? Also, I got a packet of paper work for my mom to fill out. I and her both found over 5 grammar mistakes. Also, the school isn't the cleanest and appealing. I walked around the school and it was dirty and each hallway I walked down had weird smells of ash or smoke. The school needs a lot of work, meaning the teachers are rude the school has at least a fight a day. For the person that wrote that the school is great maybe in your dreams. Wake up people the school is terrible and this is why the children have the biggest drop out rate out of any other school in Cumberland county. Frank Till I thought you were going to make schools safe and give our children a higher education isn't that true? The kids at Douglas Byrd learn nothing they are learning things that are for 6th graders. And what is the motto SWAG gosh sounds ghetto to me. Come on parents get involved and clean the school up its ridiculous that our children go to a school that the principal and the teachers can care less if our kids do well or not. Douglas Byrd doesn't even deserve one star. I agree with that parent, Douglas Byrd is terrible and why in the world do they keep a Principal that doesn't even meet with parents, or even put rules or regulations down in the school. The children fight and curse and this is why the teachers take off more then the kids. Wral News station why dont you pull the records of the teachers and you will see that the teachers are absent more the the children that attend the school. The news media news to get involved this is why I am going to start writing letters to are congressman/women because change needs to come to this school. I am a returning sophomore at DBHS. I have to say that although Douglas Byrd has it's faults (and I challenge you to name a school that dosen't) it's still a energetic learning environment. The teachers here (the ones I have encountered at least) are dedicated to the success of their students. And, for the most part they have succeeded. Sure, there are a few bad apples that try to spoil the bunch, but I believe that our administration is doing the best they possibly can to neutralize this problem. I am an honors student in this school and I feel as though my teachers really try to push the limits of my knowledge and I am and always will be ever so grateful for that. Overall, I feel DBHS is, maybe not the Best, but a great school to attend. This school is so behind in teaching things that 9-12 should be learning. I blame Douglas Byrd Middle School. Every 9th grader that comes to Douglas Byrd High School is giving not algebra 1,,my kids had algebra 1 in 8th grade at John Griffin, they had to do the same math again when they went into 9th grade AT Douglas Byrd High..what a waste of time. They are to lazy to check the children's records to see what they need to take and what they don't need to take. They don't have time to teach they are to busy telling the big mouth kids to shut up. A lot of negative things have been said about DBHS. But the main people complaining, are the parents!! You have to go to the school to understand how great of a school it really is. There's something for everybody. Clubs, arts, sports; you name it. Some people just don't apply themselves so the missout on the whole experience that DB has to offer. If and when you keep busy doing things you love at school with people who have the same interest, you won't notice all the "bad" things. So don't let these NEGATIVE reviews make you miss out on some experiences you won't find anywhere else! --Proud, Class of 2016 Douglas Byrd High Student A school can have a great administration and a wonderful teaching staff but it is all for nothing if PARENTS do not send their children to school ready to learn. Parents are the child's number one teacher and bears the BULK of responsibility for their child's educational experience and attainment. I raised my 2 girls to appreciate and respect education and the educational environment and they have both excelled despite the shortcomings of the schools they attended. I ask the parents complaining on here...What do YOU do, on a DAILY basis, to ensure that your child is academically ready to face the world? If you cannot positively answer that question then please don't throw stones at the schools. ---parent of a college graduate (3.95 GPA) and college freshman majoring in Nursing Overall, my experience at this school is bad. What little bit of self esteem was built up has quickly smashed against the apathy of this environment. I have maintained grades that place me on the honor roll every semester. Im in JROTC, involved in school sports, attend one of their specialty academies, but the environment is toxic. Other students are the problem. If school is part of the socialization process leading to adulthood than this place is a cesspool. As a parent I would never send my child to the school. Yes I am not there at the school but the bullying at the school that I have seen is the worst that I've seen I come from San Diego California and those are some pretty bad school's up there. This school my child has been bullied she has made complaints to staff teachers principal vice principal nothing has been done I have done the same I've called the school everyday never receive a call back. My daughter was beat up after school by one particular girl caught on video with a teacher just standing there watching the fight not calling for help not trying to split it up just standing there watching the fight as my daughter is getting beaten in the head. My child is a straight A sometimes B student never has been in trouble. In the videos that have been plastered all over social media this girl walks up to my daughter starts yelling at her cussing at her and starts choking her then repeadly hitting her inthe head pulling her hair out in chunks. My daughter trys to get her away from her and the other girl jumps on top of her hitting her in the head again. My daughter get suspended the other girl is at school the next school day. This school is a joke. My daughter is scared to be at this school and I'm scared for her.

column3: Lawrence High is a very good school, and it is getting better all the time. They have created academies: freshman and sophomore academies, and three career academies for juniors and seniors. The school is quite diverse and creates a welcoming environment for students. The teachers are encouraging and helpful to the students. A few years ago there was a significant renovation of the building. Some of the reviews below are out of date. As a parent of a Freshman, I have to say I am incredibly impressed by the school. The course work is challenging, the teachers are engaged and stimulating, the homework is not busy-work but rather thought-provoking and reinforcing of concepts learned in class. The teachers are supportive and make themselves available if the student needs extra help or claification on concepts. The school has an impressive amount of clubs available for every interest and the students are involved! Drama and music programs are stellar. The school has a diverse population so students get a varied mix of students from all walks of life (more like the real world). There are many AP and honors courses available. My daughter loves LHS and is pushed to excel. I am also the parent of a Freshman at Lawrence High School. I have been repeatedly impressed by the quality and quantity of opportunities available through our high school. Whether it's music, art, sports, model congress, debating, drama, community service--or much much more, there is a spot for every engaged student to shine. I am particularly wowed by the students' initiative. At any and all of the events I have attended, almost everything is student-run or student-managed, with faculty and administration stepping aside from the spotlight--so that their student-leaders can actually lead. We are new to Lawrence High School, transferring both a senior and sophomore from Notre Dame HS. From our first meeting w/guidance office in June, we have been greatly impressed by the school's administration and faculty, course offerings for AP and Honors students, and high academic standards. Our students both agree that they are being challenged academically like never before and feel welcomed by the student body. Wish we had started with Lawrence High School from the beginning! I am the parent of two LTPS students. One child is now in college, the other is at Lawrence High School. LHS is a school where all children can excel. The awards earned at the school speak volumes—AP Honor Roll, District of Character, Best Communities for Music Education. Situated between Princeton and Trenton, the Lawrence student body reflects a rich diversity both economically and culturally giving our kids a slice of the world they'll live in as adults. LHS has a commitment to character education and these compassionate students are accepting of their differently-abled peers. Each student is given a laptop computer and leaves high school with a mastery to compete in a technology-driven world. Team sports are offered to any student who meets minimum academic benchmarks, and co-curricular clubs offer before- and after-school opportunities to satisfy any interest. My kids wished there were more hours in the day to take advantage of all the possibilities. Lawrence High students are regularly making headlines in science, music, DECA, Model Congress and more. Every year LHS sees students accepted into the Ivies and other prestigious schools, but more than that, the students at all academic levels are well prepared and supported in whatever is the best path for their needs as young adults. I am a freshman just coming into LHS (only one academic quarter so far), and my experience has been great. I am a relatively high academic achiever, and my teachers are quick to recognize the varying potentials of the students in every classroom. I've noticed that the teachers really look out for you as a student. In addition to academics, I am involved with several extracurricular LHS activities, namely the Math League, the Model Congress, and International Alliance. All three clubs increase student cooperation, and International Alliance isn't even really run by the teacher who is present. The student officers take care of everything! Overall, LHS can accommodate students of all levels and backgrounds and transform them into ready young adults, as I've seen in some of my friends and neighbors from the upper classes. Thank you LHS! My 3 children received a very good education at LHS. Coming out of the 8th grade, there was much discussion about attending LHS vs going to one of the local independent schools. My wife and I are both products and supporters of public education. Good students will perform well in any good environment and LHS offered that. Our oldest daughter went to Princeton and is a VP at the College Board. The second, our son, went to Dartmouth and is a photographer and independent movie director. Our third, another daughter, went to Duke and is the development director at a large non-profit. All credit their LHS education as an important stepping stone to where they are now. Don and Pam Betterton Lawrence High School is an incredible diverse community that is accepting of all types of people. Its students are supportive of each other and most of them are hardworking and passionate about something, whether that's science and engineering or theatre or music. As a senior at Lawrence, I've grown up and deeply understand this community and what is has done for me. It has opened my eyes to many different kinds of people, given me access to a fantastic education, and allowed me to meet some great friends and peers. It's not about the rating of the school; it's about the ability for a students to take advantage of all the opportunities presented to them. LHS has given me so many great experiences just as any other school can. Anyone can be successful here. As a graduate, I can wholeheartedly say that I'm glad to have been a student at Lawrence High School. It prepared me for college with the dedicated teachers in each department & I was able to meet some fantastic people while I was there who helped me become the person that I am today. Lawrence High is truly an extraordinary school, although many may be quick to label it as "average" compared to neighboring blue ribbon districts. However, as a current junior I can honestly say Lawrence does not lack in providing any aspect of a strong education. This covers academics, athletics, arts, electives, clubs-you name it. Every imaginable opportunity is available, like most reviews have said. The teachers are incredibly skilled and become more of friends than apathetic mentors. Because of a diverse population, I am allowed to experience the real world and interact with people of all different kinds. I did consider moving or applying to a private school, but I realized it couldn't get any better than Lawrence. I personally know other graduates from here who now go to Ivy Leagues, so it is equally as possible to be accepted into a prestigious university from Lawrence as any other school! The AP and Honors courses challenge while also letting us demonstrate high potential, which is individually recognized. There is a safe environment and atmosphere of community, where excessive competition may cloud students' brains in other schools. The only thing discouraging Lawrence might be the preconceived notion that it is not viewed as good enough. But it is no less than Robbinsville, South Brunswick, West Windsor, etc. The kids can really take on leadership roles and try out or excel at anything they wish. My daughter is in her second year at LHS and I am very pleased with her experience thus far. Her teachers have been challenging and approachable. They seem to truly care about the students' academic careers. I love the diverse population of the school and the broad range of classes available. I was pleasantly surprised that my daughter, who is currently enrolled in honors classes, will be eligible for AP classes next year (as a junior). I've also loved seeing her get involved in a wide range of extra curricular activities. There are so many activities for the students: sports teams, drama club, Operation Smile, Students Helping Honduras, the Red Scare Marching Band, to name a few. LHS is a great place that truly reflects the real world. I'm glad my kids will go through LHS! As the director of undergraduate admission at Rider University (also in Lawrenceville!), we have an excellent relationship with Lawrence high school. We work closely with the school counseling staff to identify students who are well-prepared for college and for whom Rider is an excellent fit. While we have students on our campus from all over the country and from around the world, we consistently receive many applications from and grant many offers of admission and scholarships to Lawrence students each year. Those who enroll typically do very well and are among the most successful of our alumni. We have enjoyed a long and close relationship with the Lawrence counseling staff, and I can say confidently that they provide an outstanding, caring college advising experience to their students. There is no way to overestimate the value of this kind of preparation--to students and to parents--in today's college search process. We're proud to be their neighbors and colleagues!William LarrousseRider University We have lived in Lawrenceville Township since year 2003. My 2 children (ages 17 and 14) are receiving excellent education in this township, and we are very happy with the town and its education system. The house prices here are very reasonable as compared with the very high quality education and safety of the town. I will highly recommend anyone who is considering moving here. Our two children each received an excellent education that not only prepared them well for college (both now at Ivy League schools), but that helped them to discern their intellectual passions. They learned a great deal while also having time to relish rich extracurricular experiences and strong friendships that will continue well into later life. LHS gave them a strong academic foundation without the pressure-cooker environment that too often comes along with that. The dedicated faculty are genuinely interested in their students – you will often see them attending plays and sporting events, and I’ve watched many a gaggle of alumni go back to school on break to visit their former teachers. In a society in which we too often cloister ourselves with people just like us, the remarkable heterogeneity of their peer group at LHS prepares its students to be good citizens and to feel at home wherever their path in adulthood will lead. I'm delighted that our children were able to attend Lawrence High. My 3 children went through the Lawrence school district, from K-12. All 3 have gone on to successful college experiences and early success in their professional careers.Lawrence High gave them the motivation, guidance and specific subject learning to achieve in high school and after. My 2 daughters graduated from LHS and went on to attend very competitive colleges. Both my wife and I were happy with the quality of education and overall high school experience. In addition, both daughters received a bunch of college credits by taking AP exams – in fact the Physics AP pass rate is one the best. My younger daughter is a Junior Mechanical Engineering student, has close to a 4.0 GPA and is looking to graduate a semester early in large part due to the AP credits. I am so grateful for my four years at LHS, which I feel were of great benefit to me emotionally and personally. As a student I participated in many extracurriculars alongside enthusiastic students and dedicated faculty advisors; I also met some of my closest friends. I graduated in May from an Ivy League university where many of my peers went to private high schools, but I never felt disadvantaged by my public school education; in fact, given the extent to which I was taught to work independently and be responsible for myself, I often felt more prepared for college academic life than people around me. The experience of attending a rigorous and diverse public school has had such a positive impact on me, and I would recommend it to anyone else wholeheartedly. I am so happy that I went to LHS. Not only did I find that my teachers were great every year, but the music program is so great and the students like me who were/are involved in it are so dedicated. I made friends for life in that marching band and they were times that I will never forget. This school is excellent for kids who are going to "go for it." Whether it's art or sports, music or physics--there's a place to shine. There are so msny opportunities, that is is challenging for first-year students to narrow down their interests--not a bad problem to have. With the exception of a few rogue examples, the faculty is outstanding. You reap what you sow at LHS--so the students are very accustomed to self-direction as upperclassmen. The neighboring districts that are thought to have a more rigorous curriculum offer 19 or 20 AP classes. Lawrence High School offers 23 AP classes. The % of students completing an AP class with a 3 or better is 71.8% (state average). The % of students completing an AP class with a 3 or better is 83.2% at Lawrence High School. That is a significant difference. The faculty is committed and engaging, the variety of courses offered is exceptional, the environment is positive and the number of after school activities available is outstanding. Go Cardinals! The school shows tremendous support for all aspects of student life-academics, sports, music, theater, arts, clubs and extracurricular activities. Very well balanced approach so that each student can find something to be excited about and motivated by. Overall happy with the quality of education. Lawrence High School offers excellent AP courses. Staff is committed and encouraging. LHS provides a wide variety of after school activities. School is run by professionals. Teachers are excellent. School board is progressive. What else can you expect? I am very happy with the school. LHS really helps build kids build strong character in its students, like integrity, compassion and respect towards the society. Teachers really help students to got good work ethics. LHS has been a great school for my students. They have developed leadership skills and learned and grown during their time here. The school offers many AP classes, many arts and music opportunities and many extra-curricular groups. Exceptional public education that allows students to continue on to college, trade school or the workforce will interpersonal skills that serve them well in their future careers. Hopewell Valley, Princeton and WWP are all hybrid models, why is Lawrence still locking away its students? What am I paying taxes for in this district if the people running the show can't get their act together? Much is being lost in this process while the district is focused on other distractions. Every board meeting I attend there is a focus on the politics du jour of the day and little discussion about how the remote schedules are harming parents and students. Nov 30th for High School return are we serious Lawrence Twp? Ok, first, I went to and graduated from LHS, but now my children go there, so I know that many things have changed in 17 years, so I will focus on my own children’s current experience at LHS. I guest the best review is that my children attended LMS & LHS last year and this year (still virtually) and will be switching to a private school in the Fall (at least one that I can afford, not the $$$$$ Lawrenceville School), so we still making a relatively fair comparison. The bottom line is that in my own experience, suburban public schools in NJ are better than many other areas. LHS is a typical generic NJ suburban school, not on par with west Windsor or north Brunswick - both districts where my friends kids go. So the overall review is neutral. I’m moving my kids because the private school is in session and this virtual learning is not up to par. I’m luck that my two children are good students regardless, but they are not getting the education they could or should.

column1: Unfortunately for me, as a student I felt like this school was very sub-par in comparison to the surrounding education centers. While there are some staff that really do make the school a much better place to be in, a large portion of the teachers are lazy and repugnant. Refusal to change even when something does not work for students, is one of the biggest problems I had. NPHS has a rating of 6/10 based on standardized tests the school has taken, yet I will tell you they do not try to change in any way shape or form to make it better for the students. Not only this, but also I as well as many many others were bullied in our time at this school, and found the response to it very, very unsatisfactory. Literally nothing was done to them because they simply were part of extra-curricular activities. I left this school my senior year and went on to get my GED. I do not recommend this school, and I will never allow my children to attend it. This school is full of teachers not doing their jobs and students that bully multiple people and do not recieve any punishments. The principal is all about publicity and will do anything to get the punlicity that he wants. There are so many people bullied and even when it's brought to the administration multiple times, they say they'll handle it and do nothing. A school with an A grade, but should be a C or even a D. I am going to be a senior this coming fall and I’m honestly terrified. The administration has never been on my side and I have been the target for relentless racial profiling and extreme bullying since my freshman year. One time I went off on a kid for saying a homophobic slur and I got taken down to the office and told that I was “too aggressive” and that they would’ve handled this quietly. I have never seen a kid here get into trouble for saying literal slurs. It has gotten to the point where kids will brag about not getting into any trouble. Also as a trans student I am forced to use the staff bathrooms, which is fine, BUT people constantly stand in front of the door and wait for me to come out, bang on the door and yells slurs at me through the door. Not a single one of them has even gotten a stern talking to. They also don’t respect any cultural headwear, such as durags, hijabs, and other headwraps. My sophomore year they had 4 police cars surround my house because I forgot to sign in and do my online schoolwork. If you love and respect your child DO NOT put them in this school. Rampant bullying and a culture of torment for many students. Ignorance and drama and close mindedness abound. It’s like being in the 50s and early 60s In my time at this school I could not have asked for a better experience. The engagement of faculty, students, and community is unmatched. This school is a home away from home. The teachers care and take the extra step. I would never imagine sending my children to any other school. I am a recent graduate. My experience at New Prairie was excellent. The leadership from the Superintendent on down to the individual teachers was professional and you knew they cared for the students. Student-Athletes are extremely well taken care of, as the entire community is fully invested in the schools athletic programs. Other extracurricular activities are top notch as well, such as the choir, band and trades. School officials are constantly working to improve every aspect of the students educational environment. Sending your children to New Prairie is an excellent choice and you can have comfort in knowing they will receive and excellent education in an elite learning environment.

column3: Many of the teachers are genuinely caring and really want to help students succeed, but it is easy to get left behind. Some students struggle with work, and don't get the proper attention and guidance that they need. Classes also begin too early in the morning for adolescents, who have different circadian rhythms than adults, and it affects their ability to pay attention and learn.

column1: As a student here for two years, I could honestly tell you that this school barely deserves 2/5 stars. I don't even know where to start. The teachers have no passion; they are there to get paid and are very unreasonable. The staff is constantly being changed and re-arranged. GLD's can now be used (Global Learning Devices, which is a fancy name they give to our phones/tablets), which are used to basically keep us occupied at lunch so we don't get too rowdy (although there were more fights in the cafeteria this year than I can count on one hand). Sometimes we use them to do research in class, although most people just go on Youtube or whatever during that time. Another thing is that complaints/grievances are ignored. They have a "bullying" policy, but my bullying issues were never fixed. I got bullied all throughout middle school and got in trouble for standing up for myself and others. You will get suspended like I did for hitting someone back if they hit you first. This school is a joke. The pros about this school are that there are advanced classes you could take to get ahead, and there is free and reduced lunch offered to those needing it (although the lunch is cheap as it is). I am really impressed with the direction the BOE is going. With in the last 2 years they have made major changes to the curriculum and their passion of making all the schools the best. New members were voted in and have transitioned the district in the right direction. The new superintendent is a breath of fresh air. If you plan to move to Saddle Brook just know that the school system here is really really bad. I just transferred to Saddle Brook Mid/High school for about 2 months now, and it is literally the worse experience ever. This school could care less about your opinion and they literally expect you to immediately know everything they covered when you weren't in that school. They are totally unfair and not understandable at all. Literally all the girls wear jeggings or even jeans but they don't get detention or anything. I wore jeggings today and I got detention when basically all or most of the girls wear jeggings also. Some classes make you test on things you haven't even learned yet in your old school. Also, transferring near the end of a marking period can be hard too because you wouldn't have any grades in for that marking period. Especially when they make you test on things you haven't learned yet, most likely you would fail that test, and that would be your only grade in that specific marking period. This school is horrible and the worst school I've been to, and i've transferred to multiple schools before. This one is the worst one yet. This school doesn't even deserve one star. I will start by saying that as far as the Saddle Brook Middle School Guidance department, it has definitely approved since my other child was there. Thank God for that. The school is going thru some transitions, hoping that they are all for the best.
