column3: Great experience, lot of extracurricular opportunities in addition to Academic programs This school lacks communication skills. Teachers, councilors and administrators are unresponsive. I withdrew my youngest child and am teaching her with the assistance of a homeschool program. They recently notified me they will not allow my oldest child attend next semester due to inadequate progress. Apparently they don't want to help her excel. I requested assistance at the beginning of the school year when my child began to struggle. I was told we had to wait until the semester ended. The semester ended without any assistance. They recently notified me my child isn't welcome to finish the school year. Welcome to Bay City Central High School. Now leave. There wasn't any behavior issues. The only issue was learning. My child has a learning disability. I requested a meeting to make a 504 plan. I don't think they know what one is. I have been in education for 20 years. I graduated from the University of Michigan with a bachelors degree in education. I am deeply saddened by the integrity of this school system. The only thing more impressive than BCC's amazing architecture is it's staff! For generations, this high school has helped shape our community's youth into brilliant, productive adults! The success stories are endless- as a 1992 graduate, I realize so many accomplishments in my life have stemmed from the teachers and faculty who always went the extra mile to take care of us. As a local real estate agent, it is with great pride I recommend BCC to families moving in from out of town, or as a school of choice for our long time residents, as well! As a 2006 graduate I absolutely loved the opportunities I had and the diversity of my fellow students. Most of my teachers where great and very helpful. I graduated from here and love everything about this amazing school. We can't wait for our kids to attend. Bay City Central is a diverse and welcoming high school! It’s large enough to offer real world preparation and still feel welcoming. The principals and teachers are engaging and enabling of getting students to their best performance. Some highlights I find impressive: - Diverse community and cultures — child learns world does not just look like them- AP and college level classes or ability to take classes at local college if excel. - Numerous staff to help those who fall behind- Athletics/clubs! Central is in a large league with all major sports with role model coaches, others like bowling, golf, and every interest club the students desire!! Growing up here allowed me to attend this school which was amazing back then but now my children get to attend. The students, staff, and environment make this place the best!! I would not send my kids anywhere else! Staff is caring and there is great diversity. Something for everyone at BCC! Fantastic new education in an historic campus that looks like it is straight out of a movie. Provides an enriched learning environment for students from all ethnic and socioeconomic backgrounds. Offers a variety of advanced placement courses and does an excellent job of preparing students for college. Great school & a fantastic staff. Tons of awesome extra curricular opportunities. They also offer more honors and AP class options than any other school in the area. Central has a completely different atmosphere, from the teachers to the friday night football stadiums filled with the entire community. The entire faculty including Principal Marcinak, the teachers, custodians, lunch ladies, other facility members and more all truly care about the students. They do all they can to motivate them to be the best they can be and show endless amount of support. Great school with great staff!! Goes above and beyond for their students Central was the most inclusive school in Bay City Bay City Central is an incredible school with so much to offer! The staff goes above and beyond to give the students the best highschool experience possible! It is the most diverse school in our county in so many ways, which means, young people who come through Central are familiar with, and friends with, people from many different backgrounds, which best prepares them for the diversity of the real world. The football stadium is like no other…you’ll have to experience that for yourself to understand how special it is! There are many clubs, sports and activities to get involved with at Central, everyone can find something (or many things) of interest to them! Central has the oldest continuous marching band in the state of Michigan! Students who qualify for Advanced Placement classes are able to dual enroll at Delta College and earn college credit. The traditions that continue throughout the years at Central, such as the homecoming week festivities, make Central a place where many fond memories are made! These homecoming festivities include, a Wednesday night bonfire after the freshman football game, a Friday afternoon pep rally where classes compete for the spirit jug, a Friday evening parade down Columbus Ave. before the varsity football game, the marching band making their way around the block to the stadium with an unforgettable drum beat leading into the fight song that gets everyone pumped for game and so much more! I experienced memorable traditions as a student there, and now I get to relive them as my kids spend some of the best years of their lives there! I attended Bay City Central from 2015 - 2019. My entire experience was everything I wanted from high school. I had the opportunity to join sports, clubs, co-op, and BCC ultimately led me to my current career path. The teachers are willing to help out and make sure you succeed in and out of the classroom. I attended Bay city central from 2016-2020. I loved all 4 years! All of the teachers and staff as a whole really care about their job and make it their mission to improve every student they see! Very thankful to have attended BCC! I went to Bay City Central from 2013-2017. The teachers I had were incredibly supportive. My teachers were always willing to spend the time to answer questions I had or go over material I was struggling with. They would connect me to resources or let us know about opportunities we could apply for. I feel like the teachers and staff looked out for us and believed in our future. I’m lucky to have had the amazing teachers at Bay City Central. Bay City Central is a great school in a great community. The whole child is the focus. If you are looking for a wonderful high school BCC is the place to go. Mr. Marciniak and the staff have created a family-oriented school so every child can have advantages and support when needed. Great school to go to for your student

column1: Organized with a capital O! My son just registered for the 9th grade and this his first year at a public school and the staff were very welcoming and friendly during the process. The UHS school administrators are to be commended on how organized they run this school. My son comes from a small charter school and they are not organized and the staff members are not friendly. I am confident that my son will have a great education and valued experience at UHS school.

column1: The Reason i love New Mission is because they take the time to help the kids when they are in need. they comunicate with us the parents,and the most important part is the my child loves going to the school because of the teachers . my daughter has a learning problem and they help her out alot .she has improved alot thank you New Mission Parents do not be fooled! They are good with parent involvement, but at the end of the day students need to score well on standardized test like the SAT and MCAS, the students here score poorly, even the ones that have good grades. There is simply not enough resources and there made-up curriculum is simply not good enough!!! I attended Mission High, got excellent grades and struggled to get into the Universities of my choice (me and several other top scoring students) Do NOT send your kids here!!!! I think New Mission High Schoo is great. It is a small school and this is where the Teachers and Principal really takes time with the students. My son use to attend New Mission, he started off not really on a good note, but the staff and Principal realy worked with him. The Principal also was available for any reason. I recommend this school highly. Keep it up New Mission! Your the best. Enjoyed the learning process and the wonderful nuns.

column3: I love this school. And so do my boys. It has been a great experience and well worth the move As a student of 3 different High Schoolsfrom two different states, I can say confidently that this school DOES have a drug problem. There are great teachers here. No other school I've been to has teachers like Dacula. However, there is a strong drug influence. The test scores are generally high because there is a greater devide between students with higher and students with lower grades. There is a high drop out rate. Also, many students are transferred to dacula from other schools, because they were ejected for behavior from their previous school. This is done so that the school may remain 5A, for football region purposes. This does nothing but feed the drug problem. There have been new staff members hired this past year that may show signs of improvement. So there may be hope of fixing the drug problem, but it is going to take a few years. Bottom line this school has great teachers, a drug problem, and hope for improvement. Dacula does a great job working with all students! The "Big Board" celebrates their accomplishments in and out of the classroom. The faculty is strong in content and care for the kids. All high schools have some problems with teenager-type issues, but the staff and student body do a great job to be accepting and caring to everyone. Our student body is very involved with the community. The test scores of Dacula continue to rise and are comparable or better than all other surrounding schools! Go Falcons! My son is graduating from Dacula High this year. Overall I have been pleased with the quality of education that he has received. My only complaint is with the counseling staff, although I can only speak to the quality of the counselor assigned to him, I'm not a fan. I'd like to silence the false perception that Dacula isn't a top tier school. Dacula is a great school. The staff & admin are kind yet genuine people, that want every student to succeed past high school. The commons faculty members are very sweet people that encourage us to have big, big smiles in our faces everyday. The teachers here are helpful and drill us with the fact that we(the students) have the tools for success and only we can take the initiative to do so. Some students that may seem trouble some aren't judge as criminals like other schools might. No one is perfect. Here Dacula strives for everyone to have the chance for bright future. As for athletics, this school is a powerhouse from soccer to football. No short of talent here. This school is a great place to be. Glad to be a falcon. Hopefully, the administration can work against some of the negative streams flowing here. This school has a drug and violence problem. Fights and bullying are common. Racism is a stronghold at the school. I believe the administration team are doing the best that they can. I see police officers on site, often. On a positive note, they have a great sports program and they foster that strength. However, it has been our experience that you have to strongly advocate for your child, if they have any learning issues. There has been a new technology/digital program for the classrooms that the school is implementing that is amazing and leading other schools. The school's orchestra department is truly amazing, as well. If not for the violence, we would stay here. Hope it gets better. I haven’t seen a school this bad since Buford High with lack of respect by students and parents. Sporting events involving this school is awful. The kids are rude to other teams and refs, coaches. The parents say things smart comments to other teams parents almost trying to start a fight. Must be a rough area because the kids are hardened and the parents are just plain obnoxious. Avoid this area. Excelent staff! Great environment. Dual enrollment program has room to improve process and provide transportation options. I personally went to a Parkview Graduated in 1980. Gwinnett was great then. My older kids went to Brookwood great teachers great school. Schools were good paid attention worked with the parents. Now younger child goes to Dacula Hs HORRIBLE EXPERIENCE SINCE WEEK 2. No one cares or even returns your calls. I leave messages and no call back unless it is a message that has nothing to do with the call at hand. But if they want to talk to you man they bug the crap out of you to get what they want. Forget making your child accountable yet push to make your child accountable. HORRIBLE SCHOOL WITH LOW SCORES ALL AROUND. No wonder the graduating rate is low. Shame on Gwinnett County Schools. NOt like it use to be when schools really mattered. 1. The science teachers are great at this school. They teach the materials effectively and offer 1-on-1 help often. 2. Foreign language is not taught effectively. Teachers teach you in a way that requires you to memorize the material, rather than learn the skills and reason behind everything we do. Additionally, the textbooks are outdated and teach words that no one uses anymore. This explains why students don't remember their foreign languages after high school. The school needs to focus the first 2-3 years of foreign language on words that will help you in the real world. 3. Some of the clubs are boring. These clubs don't really offer anything new or interesting. It's the same activities you hear about every year. 4. Students don't really learn any character skills or life skills in advisement, even though the school strongly states that you do. 5. You can't eat in class, which is a dumb rule. If I have to starve until the end of the day, how will I be able to learn effectively? 6. School lunch sucks, but I'm not going to blame the school for that because it's the county's fault. 7. 9th grade language arts is the worst, but it gets better once you go to the other grade levels (except for AP Lit). 8. Teachers will talk about you behind your back or will throw shade at you. 9. The school offers lots of sports, but focuses most on football. school use be wonderful 15 years ago, has gone downhill and student behavior has gone crazy. personally do not feel like the administration is as strong as it was years ago. This school is a very good school even though many kids like drama but my gosh the teachers they are AMAZING. Shout out to Ms. Elder 9th LA she is the best teacher you could ask for. You can tell her anything and she will always check up on you to see how your doing. The admins are very good too they make life and school much easier and they are easy to talk to. And they give the kids 52 minuet lunches! The only school in Gwinnett that does that. If you are new to the area and looking for a good school for your kids send them to Dacula High School. I highly recommended to people to not go to this school. I went to this school for my freshman year and for my sophomore year, and I did some things that were wrong and unbearable in the past when I was there before the coronavirus outbreak. I will admit to that. But I will not admit to the fact that they do a horrible job of helping kids with special needs, because they only care about discipline. That is the only thing that they care about. They treated me like I was a prime suspect in a federal comic prison. I felt absolutely disrespected by the special Ed teachers that I had and my regular teachers did the exact same thing when I had them for my classes. Every student that has special needs, needs to be treated with respect by every single special Ed teacher because they do not know how to do that what so ever. They do not know how to do their actual job. During the outbreak when we were all in quarantine, I am pretty sure that they bragged so much that they worked so hard for every single student online. I beg a differ, like I am sorry to spill the beans for you guys but we are still in a pandemic. Anyways back to what I was saying about special Ed teachers. I am a male who suffers from autism because I am a autistic kid. And that is not a bad thing to have in you’re life. It is actually a great thing to have, a brilliant skill for instance. But I do not understand why it is such a mockery to make fun of someone that has autism. That is not even remotely funny at all. It is quiet a personal thing. I feel extremely offended by regular teachers and the special Ed teachers in the school. I never felt so disrespected in my life. Plus I never felt safe in that school because like I said before is that, I felt like I was being treated like a prime suspect in a federal comic prison. I never felt safe around people that were teachers and people that I started to become friends with that I do not know that person occasionally. It feels like you are walking into a school with a bunch of southern crazy rednecks. I mean I would sue them for harassment. Because I had enough of playing their stupid games because they were trying cause a sense of manipulation. They are very manipulative as well. They are also off task all the time of trying to teach a class to some students. Plus some of the teachers do videos of each lesson for each unit. I mean if I were in you’re shoes I would teach the lesson myself to the entire class and I would be more specific and helpful. I am parent of 4 children in the Dacula school cluster, and we are extremely pleased with the investment the staff has in this town's youth. They go above and beyond and can be seen at sporting events and town celebrations. In my opinion, Dacula is one of Gwinnett County's best kept secrets. "One Family, One Dacula". I was really surprised to see the rating of 6/10 for Dacula High School. My kids nor I have experienced any underserved areas. Principal Long is present and enormously invested in Dacula and every single one of its students. First class. He is very focused and supportive toward success of all the students and the school's programs. Exceptional staff all around invested in the success of the students. Excellent teacher / parent weekly correspondence regarding grades and progress. First class, successful athletics department. The school offers everything from an expanse of AP classes to weekly remediation and study hall sessions for students needing extra assistance. It provides an abundance of online resources to support the classroom instruction. Behavior issues that crop up among random students aren't tolerated and are handled accordingly. I think very highly of Dacula and love our diverse community. We are real, we are a strong community, and we lift eachother up. Gwinnett County is a national leader in education. I don't know what else you could ask for.

column1: Good area and great for a "basic education", but definitely lacking in science and technology. A very artsy school not for the future engineer or geologist, certainly great for any aspiring accountant or businessman. I have had two children graduate from this school and both had a fantastic education. Both, they each are now engineers, one is a mechanical engineer, the other is aeronautical engineer. This school provides many activities after school to keep the kids busy. I highly recommend. Great school with tons to offer the students to keep them engaged and busy. The magnet theater program is among the best in the state and the music ensembles consistently win competitions wherever they go.

This has to mean somebody's doing something right!

column3: My student entered this school from another school district, excelling and earning scholarship awards. With a good chance of fulfilling their dream of going to medical school to be a surgeon. My student found in their new school SHS that not all the classes, including Math and foreign language, had books for their students. The teachers here are not paid for any over time or coaching so the students suffer as teachers are forced to look elsewhere to supplement their pitiful income. My student doesn't want to leave friends for another school, but now my student who had ivy league paths now has to concede to a lower level state school. It is only the work from the previous school that my student even has the option of college. The school has tried to convince my student that a nursing assistant certificate is as good or better then getting a surgeon's education. Even the beauty that a reviewer stated is gone. The forest was ploughed down and a cement yard was put in it's place. For as someone recently at the school said 'SHS students aren't very smart, they might trip on tree roots'. I doubt the majority of students here had so little potential until they were taught so. I'm finishing off my sophomore year here. There are both pros and cons to this school. Good Things: Unlike what someone else said, there is little violence. Fights aren't as common as they are at the junior high. There are some ace teachers. The drainage system (which I'm surprised no one mentioned) got infinitely better after they took out the beautiful trees. They offer AP history courses and (I believe) an AP science class or two. The counselors are both very friendly and very helpful. Bad Things: The principal is awful. She's rude and is never around. Harassment is a big issue at this school. Most of the teachers will help you if you mention something, but otherwise they turn a blind eye. One of my teachers harasses me. There's nothing I can do about it. He's retiring this year. The campus is outdoors, so when it rains, you get wet. The tennis courts have major cracks in them and probably won't be repaired for another 20-40 years. As someone else mentioned, the communication issues between the junior high and the high school are bad. Schedules get messed up. A lot of people skip school. Even some of the teachers have the "it's just Shelton, you'll never get anywhere" attitude. Shelton High is in a very poor town and it is a very poor school. the facilities are falling apart. The school needs to be rebuilt. As a former student, I took the hardest classes offered. Honors classes were a joke. They handed out good grades and gave very easy assignments. The course catalog claims to offer AP classes, they never offered a single one while I was there. They claimed that there were not enough people to fill the class. They offer plenty of remedial and basic classes. Students get to their senior year and still have trouble reading (Because they were never taught right). Violence was common at Oakland Bay JR High, but was less common at the high school. There are several good teachers, but for the most part, they contribute to the poor achievement in the school. They are graduating people who cannot read, write, or do basic math. Many students have problems at home (single parent, homeless, very poor, violence, etc). These problems are brought into the classroom. I am a parent. I have two children that graduated from SHS and went on to do very well in college. I have two children, a senior and junior, who are currently enrolled there. It's not a perfect school. It's not a wealthy community, and many of the students come from tough backgrounds. But for the most part, the education my children received was good. Recently, the school remodeled its facilities and added new buildings. They are also implementing specialized programs providing pathways to prepare their students for future careers.When my oldest was struggling with a mental health challenge the counselors, administration, and teachers worked very hard to ensure that he had a supportive educational environment that accommodated him through a very tough time. They adjusted his coursework, his schedule, and communicated directly with his parents to ensure that he was successful. He recovered, graduated on time, and is currently pursuing a master's degree.Like any school, SHS has its share of problems, but it is definitely moving in the right direction.

column1: my son is a sophmore at Fairdale an my step son is a freshman.My youngest son will also attend as a freshman next year. They are both involoved ins sports at fairdale with grade point averages of a 4.0 an 4.2. The faculty and coachs are very wonderful at Fairdale. Did I mention that I also attended Fairdale? I graduated in 1994. Thanks to all the wonderful teachers at Fairdale. You are all doing a great job with our children. I go to Fairdale High School, in Louisville Ky, and I am a junior. Though Fairdale may not have a good rep because of past violence and bad test scores, our principal, Brad Weston, is changing everything about our school. No longer are there fights everyday, they are now far and few. No more are there bad test scores, because he has created a more strict curriculum based upon how the students learn. The teachers seem to care more and so does the faculty. I've heard many people put my school down, and it genuinely bothers me because they do not know the changes Mr. Weston has made, nor do they know how we all, as a school, strive to make Fairdale top again. My advice to new students is to not become lazy and to be prepared for some serious learning. Fairdale will no longer be a name that people scrunch their faces at. Fairdale will be a school the students will be proud to graduate from; how do I know this? Simple, because I'm both excited and proud to be graduating from Fairdale.

column3: [Enter your review here] My two children are currently at East, They enjoy the school life a lot. It is a wonderful high school from every aspects. We have had a student at East for 2 years and as parents have noticed: *Excellent, dedicated teachers who (besides knowing their subject matter): - Integrate real world facts with academic instruction - Provide cooperative group experience *and* individual projects - Use the internet creatively and professionally - Organize extracurricular field trips - Assess learning outcomes intelligently - Help students learn to take responsibility *Fellow students encourage one another to study but have fun together, too *International and multicultural student body *Students are comfortable conversing with adults as beings of the same species *Availability of challenging academics for those so inclined *Phenomenal drama dept. *Music program, student newspaper and numerous clubs *Sports ethos supporting young women athletes as much as its young men *Nurture and challenge as appropriate. East provides a good foundation for college where students must be self-directed to take initiative and ownership of their own lives. It is a big school built upon the hearts of many caring individuals. This is an excellent school. Teachers expect you to work very hard and by junior year you need to take about 5 AP's to maintain a competitive edge. However, I would say that while it is extremely stressful to maintain that course load and do a lot of extracurriculars, this is truly what real life is all about. There is a lot of competition and especially for people looking into ivy leagues, you ought to strive for academic excellence at all times. East isn't for everyone (especially not for those who like to slack off more often than not) but if you work very hard and strive for excellence you will find your niche. The teachers here aren't always understanding about the stress students are having but many do understand and are sympathetic to your concerns. East is misunderstood as a school that is "highly rigorous." I have two students there who are both excellent top of their class students, and both have been miserable and generally unsupported during their time at East. The problem is that the school is so large, with very little security or discipline, and tremendous pressure on the teachers by the administration to rank high on testing that everyone is stressed out. Teachers and administrators take ages to get back to parents, if they do at all. Concerns are met with hostility. Creativity and critical thinking are not valued. This school creates automatons who score highly on tests - not future leaders of America. In short, I do not credit my kids' success academically to the academic rigors of East CHHS. Mostly wonderful teachers, extremely challenging. My son has worked harder at East than I ever had to work during college or graduate school. For him it has been great - he needs the challenge. Stress levels can be high however - it depends on the personality of the student. East has many councilors, all of whom are great resources for the college application process. East Chapel Hill High School is nationally recognized in the highest designation as "Honor School of Excellence" with at least 90% of students at or above grade level. The majority of students take the SAT entrance exams and the schools average scores have been nationally recognized for high achievement for decades. Our family moved to so our then elementary age child go eventually go to high school here. He recently graduated And is now in college at the school of his choice. ECHHS is an excellent school with excellent teachers and Guidance Counselors who go the extra mile to get help your child. As a parent with a child who graduated in 2007 and a child who is a current senior, I can say this school has dropped significantly in quality. Test scores may be as good as ever but the principal and counselors are terrible. Getting the principal to return a call, let alone set up a face t o face meeting is nearly impossible. The athletic director plays favorites among teams. He let the high profile football (who quit after 2 years) devastate some of the other teams such as wrestling because the football coach bullied the kids into playing ONLY football. My son's counselor doesn't seem to care and gets very defensive when you ask questions. My older son a true relationship with his counselor. She checked in with him. Knew what he was involved in and was a great asset during junior in preparing for college. My current son's counselor will write him a college recommendation without even even knowing him. On a positive note - their are some outstanding dedicated teachers and my son has been lucky enough to have a few of these. The ones that not only share their knowledge but instill passion for curiosity. East is the most challenging public high school in the state. The stress level is unbelievable and most people say they put forth more effort here than they ever had to in college. If you don't take honors and AP classes, then you are looked down upon by peers, teachers and the administration. Very rarely do students take more then 1 standard class a year. It is very uncommon for a student to graduate with less then 5 AP credits. The rigor is unbelievable and most students are up all hours of the nigh doing work. Teachers are excellent and are reachable almost all hours of the day and night. If you aren't willing to put forth the effort of a rigorous college student, then this is not the school for you. As for the social aspect, Chapel Hill is a primarily wealthy town college town. So the preppy attitude is expected. With that the party atmosphere is not small. The school is very safe with 1 police officer, 3 security guards, and a key card system. If you want to put forth the effort, and used to the demanding social and educational atmosphere, then east is a great school for you. If you go to East you have to choose to either completely change your personality and not be able to live life normally again or fail and never be happy. Not so good. If they hire a teacher like that. It says alot all workers care deeply about progression and student's success, though theres an unfathomable amount of fights and social outcasts.

column1: It was a great school with great options but as a transplant moving there the locals don't let you forget you are not one of them. And that has an impact on your learning too. Once again School GREAT locals NOT. My son attended middle through high school. Teachers to a wonderful job of getting to know the students in meeting their individual needs. I am also a teacher and have subbed in that district for many years and believe that this district is as good as Lawrence Public schools where I taught for many years. The low teacher to student ratio allows teachers to really spend time with the students.

column3: I was going to give BHS 4 stars because the building is very old and can use a facelift, but I reconsidered since this review should be about education. One reviewer commented on the sports field, but since that post, the field and track have been updated and looks very nice. My son is a freshman and I've been pleasantly surprised with how challenging his courses have been. We had been contemplating a private school , but I'm very glad that he chose Butler. He's getting a very good education without the cost of tuition! I like every one of my child's teachers and feel that they are very caring and enjoy teaching. Honors courses are especially challenging. You get what you put into it. Good students and hard workers who take College Prep, Honors and AP courses will get an excellent education at BHS. My overall rating pertains to the general aesthetics of the school and education. The teachers are great and yearn to help if you're struggling and the principal and vice principal are like your pals, that is if you're a good student. But, the school is extremely old; approximately 90 years old, and the art building is about 48 years old. The school desperately needs money to update its appeal to the eye and technology. Although; the cafeteria, photo lab, auditorium(1980s?), physics and science labs have been renovated, the floors are rotting, some hallways are dark and uninviting, and the computers needs updating, along with televisions in each of the classrooms. There are only several communities and newer streets in Butler and Bloomingdale with larger, up-scale homes, otherwise we need grants because the tax money is not enough to keep the high school looking presentable. It should look modern and it needs a second gymnasium; the gym class sizes are too large. This school has it all, great staff that takes their time to help the students achieve their goals. The academy program really prepare our kids to be respectful. The football is one of the strongest programs around and the academic graduates some of the highest scoring in the state. I love the community feel of BHS. Faculty and staff are excellent. Plenty of opportunities for students in both academics and after school activities to succeed.

column1: Poor sportsmanship. The students are not managed by adults. They are allowed to yell inappropriate and foul language during games. As the parent of four children and a high school teacher,I believe that my child is receiving an outstanding education at GTCHS. Students have the opportunity to take college classes(for duel credit),and my daughter is on track to earn her Associates Degree while in high school.She is academically stimulated,engaged,and enamored with the courses she is taking.I'm stunned at how much money she is saving by taking transferable college credits towards her major.Small classes,uniforms,sports,and dedicated teachers make this one of the best public high schools in Greenville County. GTCH is a GREAT SCHOOL We have had four children attend this school. All have gone on to university. We are so thankful for the strong base that GTCH gave our children. The teacher and staff care about the children and support their development. We have had a lot of problems, especially with the special ed department needed for one of our kids, but we have more general complaints as well. Not every kid gets access to college classes, they now have a very tight rein on doling that out. They have had a new principal every year for the last four, and the current interim one is making sweeping changes without taking the time to assess what needs to be done. The discipline there is ridiculous, it is a very tense and unfriendly environment. If my kids weren't socially settled in there I would happily move them to a neighborhood school and let them do AP classes. GTCHS has been a great fit for my son, he is able to complete college classes giving him dual credit opportunities. When students grades fall below a certain grade the school offers academic assistance after school for each subject needed. Although they don't offer all sports, the students are exposed to sports they may have never been involved in in a larger school. I am very pleased with GTCHS for my son, but it may not be a perfect fit for every student. Every child is different and I feel blessed we have options for schools that fit each child's needs. Caring school community with great teachers and support team. DO NOT SEND YOUR CHILDREN HERE!!As an alumni, this school doesn't prepare you at all. Senior project doesn't help you at all and has nothing to do with any college prep whatsoever. Theven academics at Greenville were much more difficult than Charter's academics. Math and reading is what this school needs to improve on. I spent 6 years of college catching up because I wasn't prepared. The school should also have the military come at tell us how to pay for college like Greenville did in grades 9-10. I have a 10 grader and a freshman in college. My college freshman was prepared and knew what to expect from college professors because she has already taken college classes. My 10 grader will also take advantage of the college courses being offered. Our experience at GTCHS was and is great! Great experience with access to college level classes at GT Barton Campus. Dont send anyone here unless you wont to be unhappy. Athletics, admin, school events, and the principal are all terrible. 95% of the students dislike principal

As someone whos moved and been to a few different schools, this one is by far the worst. I have never felt so unwelcome, uncared for, and unsafe in a school environment before.

column1: This school, is the worst I have ever seen. The principal and the Board of Education does not care about the children that attend this school. They manage to take good kids who want to attend school and make good grades and dishearten them, when a child can make one mistake. I have a child who went from straight A's and honor classes to begging me not to go back to this school. I keep praying the state will step in and do something to help these kids and at the moment nothing is being done. If the state was watching then principal, the Superindent and the Board who decides these kids fates would not be the way it is. This school is terrible it has mold all over the walls and the janitors are pervs. If it weren't for two particular teachers I would rate my experience even worse--well, if there were an option to give 0 stars, that is. I switched schools after my Freshman year (although I have a sibling still currently enrolled) and was able to complete my last 3 years of schooling in 1 due to not being held back by lazy and/or judgemental teachers and staff and the problems with other students. The physical conditions of the school are also atrocious. There is mold, exposed wiring, very little heating/cooling (usually completely broken), and dismal lighting that interferes with learning, amongst other issues. Bullying is a serious issue, including from staff themselves. If any student tries to solve a bullying problem via teacher or staff (as they are supposed to do), nothing is done until it escalates into a physical altercation. At this point in time (even before COVID-19, to clarify), all classes are in-school online courses with very little teacher help. Most students are failing or leaving due to this. Applying for college with her guidance counselor fell short too in what we expected as they seem to lack a sense of urgency in sending out the documentation to schools and in using a proper student resume format. Great place to learn, BHS. not a good school was constantly bullied and ridiculed by students and teachers Not a good school My son is a sophomore and has had nothing but a great learning experience with very involved and competent teachers. column3: AG is really great! its so laid back as an environment but still structured so you get the skills you need. The other students are a bit rude but hey thats highschool. The teachers are very understanding also. After great experiences at Penn London Ele and AGIS, decent experiences at FS Engle, we are really disappointed in AGHS. Our kids have had some very good teachers but I have to say the administration and guidance department are not student focused. They seem more concerned with doing what they "have to" than doing as much as they can to help their students. I graduated from AGHS in 2013, and am currently on tract to become a doctor in college. I feel as if my four years at this high school from a students point of view were a complete waste of time. This school did not prepare myself at all for college and I feel that I could have worked a 9-5 job during this time and came out as a smarter individual. I am now a high honors student in college, and graduated from AGHS with a 3.0 GPA. I found that during my time here going to school felt like a jail, I did not get anything from the classes that made me feel like a smart individual. After 2 years of college I can feel myself getting more educated and wish that I could of had a chance during my teenage years to do so. If I were a parent looking for places to send my child, I would completely avoid this school. I graduated from Avon Grove in 2012. I am now about to enter my senior year of college, and honestly Avon Grove did not prepare me at all. I was an average student, but majority of the teachers didn't really seem to care. One of the biggest issues I had with the school is just the administration and the way things are run. I remember not being allowed to go to my locker after lunch to put my stuff away, even though the "hall monitor" would be able to see me go to my locker and then return to the lunch room. The last week of my senior year, after never once getting in trouble my entire school career, I got a detention for about 2 inches worth of my bra strap showing. It was my first "offense" ever and I was told I could either take the detention or take a week long suspension (sorry for having breasts I guess?) Someone needs to go in and fix this school. Become less focused on petty little things, treating your students like prisoners, and give them a real education. I attended AGHS the first year it moved into the current building around 1957. It was a very good school and I was not planning to attend college but the guidance counselor called me into his office when I was just a couple months away from graduating and wanted me to attend college. He was able to get me a Senatorial scholarship and I thus attended four years of college and was very employable upon graduation. I held three jobs before retiring in 2013 and they were all with major companies. AGHS gave me, a farmer's boy, a great start. Currently I am a Sophomore in Avon Grove High School, and i understand that i don't have much say about the school due to the fact that I still have two more years, but i can confidently say that this is the worst school i have ever attended. The administration has absolutely no care of the students mental health or education. All they care about is their precious image to the state. They are completely out of control and uptight with rules. For example, my friend was told that her shirt was too small, so she was walking to her locker to get a jacket. While walking to her locker another teacher comes around the corner and tells her to come to the office with her because of her shirt. So my friend told her, "Im heading to my locker right now to get my jacket". The teacher then responded with, "I dont care come to the office right now" My friend had received a detention for this Ive only been here for my freshman and partial sophomore year and i can honestly say, I am looking for a new school to attend. If you're a parent, please think twice before sending your child to Avon Grove School District.

column1: an ok school:/ but not as good as i though everything is bad.........wouldnt recommend it much Not a perfect school, but far better than Los Angeles High School. Teachers are well organized and are not only are they there to teach but also to keep their students enthusiastic, and counselors are very helpful. Coming from a student, Class of 2010. This school has the worst academic program. I know of two students who graduated with a GPA of 3.5 that don't know the multiplication chart from 1-10 and write a complete sentence. This school causes nonstop problems. It creates parking problems on the residential street behind it, especially during its overly noisy football games. The problems are so severe that they are actually creating a fire hazard. Cars are parked in emergency fire lanes and in front of all of the fire hydrants...all because the school refuses to open up their parking lot on game days. I would never allow my child to attend this school. If this school cannot even observe the most basic of fire codes, and student and resident safety, then i highly doubt that their curricular program is anything more than mediocre. I know a few friends who have been very successful at UCLA after attending this school. It's understandable that the test scores from many students aren't that high, but if the kid is willing to do the work, s/he will succeed regardless of the high school. 5 starts plus definitely my daughter will come in a year to West Adams

There is no money for coaches so sports have gone down hill. The racial division has grown with about 50% asian, so that seems to have caused less parental involvement. I don't see things changin anytime soon. I am a fairly regular substitute teacher at Cypress HS. Budget cuts have forced the cancellation of some programs, but, overall, this is a school with a dedicated core of teachers and the Administration is staunchly in favor of a high quality learning culture. I think this school is great, I'm in choir and we have lots of performances . One every 2 months! Most everyone is friendly and the teachers are great. I can't see the effects of budget cuts anywhere besides some supplies. Sports are not suffering either, they are great. Teachers are also really good, they challenge us and the ones I got this year are great. This high school was a great high school. They're also very friendly. The student's were just great. And the principle tried to be as fair as possible. I would be very happy to send my children to this school. Teachers there dont care about their students. The dress code rule was rediculous. I wasnt even allowed to wear shorts in 90 degree weather. The school doesnt have much creativty. They dont have events during school or lunch. Sadly i wasnt allowed to transfer to Los Alamitos either. I was in the sports program for song. Sadly i have to say that even though i was in their song it was very bad. Coach didnt care much about us and i have to say its like that for every sport at that school. Division 3 -divison 5 in all sports just made the school look terrible. School didnt prepare me for college. This school never does anything ! When my child was getting bullied. All they said I will transfer her to a different school. That's how they solve it for it to be easy for them. Amazing school and great environment. While my kids were attending there, they enjoyed every day. Cypress High School is the best school in Anaheim High School District. Mrs. Vaughn is my child's counselor and she is AWESOME!! She listens to the kids and REALLY cares about them succeeding in school and in life. I was a student here and I had a miserable time. The teachers and the administration were so unprofessional. The math system was awful. They only let math honors students take math courses based on the correct level. For example, I was supposed to take Pre-Calculus like normal with EVERY OTHER school, but they MADE me take Trigonometry, which put my math level a grade lower than. Even schools with lower school rating had students follow regular math levels but Cypress makes students one level lower by junior year.

column1: We moved here in Summer of 2010. Given the hype about how this school was up and coming and all the talk of "community", we are pretty let down. I doubt if my daughter could handle another school change or we would move to Edmond North. One small feather in this schools cap is they seem to have a good principal but the superintendent actually said he was "not into academics" at a presentation: he likes sports instead. The school and school district are in a bit of an ad-lib mode and function somewhat without a real strategy. Still they will get a multimillion dollar football stadium and Oklahoma will still lag far behind the nation in college graduates but lead in football. School board is a total joke with good ole boy system firmly entrenched and fraudulent dealings run rampant. If your son wants to play baseball you had better ante up some money for the head coach or no play. Teachers are all new with 1 out 10 being competent. Parents even have their own cliques and are shall we say way over the top. Disgusting As a sophomore student from Deer Creek High School myself, I am here to tell you that Deer Creek charges a fortune for every possible thing that they can and the teachers act like they really don't want to be there, thus not educating us very well. I don't think that the school district uses the money wisely and the cliques are so awful that outsiders can look at a student from this school and can tell that they go to Deer Creek. As soon as i get my drivers license, I will not be attending this school anymore. Staff worry more about making money than actually educating us. They hand us text books and basically thats the only way we learn. I definately don't feel as if Deer Creek is a family, and I won't go to any football games etc, because I don't want to opponent to see me as "one of those Deer Creek girls." I am really ashamed to be a Deer Creek student. As a student of this school myself, I can't say that I particularly hate this school... however, I do dislike it at times. The administration is all over the place; sometimes I wonder if they even know what they're doing. Consistency is a little problem also. For example, a teacher might be 2 weeks ahead in the curriculum compared to another teacher of the exact same subject. Also, the school makes it incredibly hard for someone to enroll in many advanced classes... most oftentimes, an administrator or a person of likewise standing will speak to you about your apparently "poor" decision. Seriously, if I want to challenge myself and think I can handle it and even went through the trouble of enrolling in all of these difficult classes, I'm pretty sure I would want to be in them. Sports are placed above academics at this school as can be seen in the abundance of sports award ceremonies and the scarceness of academic award ceremonies. All of these examples serve as irrefutable evidence in my observance of this school and its workings. Deer Creek is a good school. This is a school where you have to make it your own, and as soon as you do, you love it. There are many clubs to join, and friends are plentiful. I graduated in 2011. Deer creek is one of those schools where you need to imagine the stereotypical Hollywood high school. It's full of clicks with the wealthiest at top. Overall from a student body experience, I hated it at Deer Creek to the point I begged my parents to let me transfer out. Most of my problems came from being in band. I was out-casted by my peers for joining band. To make matters worse I was harassed from my freshman year to senior year by the band members and the band director. I was told by the principals that I deserved and earned the way I was talked to and treated. After being threatened by the band director and other incidents the school finally removed me from band because my safety became an issue of liability to the school. However not everything about Deer Creek is bad. There are new principals since I've graduated, and some of the teachers there cannot be replaced by any teacher. AP 4 English, the AP Chemistry teacher are amazing examples of the education a child can receive. However, there are only a few teachers like them in the entire district that I know of. When there are other schools like Piedmont around, I would honestly recommend them over DC. I graduated from Deer Creek, class of 2012. I had quite a few great teachers and many unforgettable memories. Deer Creek helped me prepare for College more then I wanted to believe while I was still in high school. The worst part is really the other students. They make it easy to change classes at the beginning of the year. I was a sophomore last year at DCHS. Deer Creek High School is a school with few fights and generally nice students. It seems that the school will change in the coming years, with many apartments being built nearby. Deer Creek High School is lacking a true arts program. There is a band and choir, but not much else. All plays are put on with cheap, reused sets that require a lot of imagination input from the audience. The band only exists to play for the football games. Although an arts building was (finally) built, the many efforts of students and parents to start an orchestra have all been denied. The NHS program is extremely disorganized, with all work hours recorded on slips of paper that get lost often by the students in charge. If they could, Deer Creek would become a sports academy. Academics are lacking, and discipline is practically non-existent, but public schools everywhere are going downhill. This small school is a good school to hide in as a shy person; you won't get beat up. (this may change with the new crowd drawn by apartments) If it was possible to give this place a negative number of stars I would. No school is perfect or without its issues, that being said I can honestly say that in my opinion the bad parent/student reviews given on your sight are coming from not knowing or having experienced a school district that has real deficiencies in quality facilities, staff, educators, safety, athletics, leadership... etc.... but most importantly in quality education and programs/support for student post graduation success and continued education. Trust me folks, this school is BLUE RIBBON TOP 10 PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOL IN THE STATE. DCHS has a student body with extremely high percentage of the students in above average intelligence range so the expectations are not average... and that is the best kind of problem for a school to have. I am extremely proud to have had my child graduate high school from Deer Creek High School, and I also have the highest standards. The staff was not my favorite many times, but overall there should be great pride in attending this school district IMO. I have been nothing but extremely impressed with Deer Creek High School. We have a daughter here and 2 more not far behind. The experience my daughter has had so far has been world class. Academics, Sports, Art, Music, Facilities and Staff are outstanding. The district is going quickly and I feel that the board has been very proactive in addressing the concerns felt by such a quickly growing district. I graduated Deer Creek High school with the class of 2014. Ever since kindergarten I have gone to Deer Creek schools. I can say nothing negative about Deer Creek. The level of education is very high and athletics are the very best. I took pride playing football, wrestling and track for this great school. Everyone is very friendly and the friendships I made will last forever. I looked forward to coming to school everyday knowing I would be making myself stronger, mentally and physically. And it most certainly did. I highly recommend sending your son or daughter to get a education at this school. Now, I'm a United States Marine. Looking back on my life before the one I have now, I thought to myself that I was so blessed to go to Deer Creek. Deer Creek HS, and the district as a whole is one of the best in the entire State. (There is no debating that.) When looking at overall ratings/rankings that are typically published at the /state, or national level.....the district never rates at the very top. However, it is for one reason..and one reason only. Those Ratings/Rankings use student "diversity" as a heavily weighted measure of the overall ranking. So, just because Deer Creek does not have a high percentage of minorities and or students of diverse ethnic backgrounds, they are punished in the ratings. So, you are welcome to interpret that however you so choose. Majority of the student make up, does include children of some of the wealthiest families in Oklahoma, so those who are not use to being around the "Country Club" type "rat race/mentality" see it as a bad thing...and have obviously complained about it on this site. So, as you can see...these have really been the only concerns......lack of diversity, and challenges of not being accepted by the uber wealthy. But strictly from an education standpoint...Deer Creek schools are the cream of the crop not only in Oklahoma City..but in the entire State. Period. I am really ashamed to be a deer creek student. i moved here 2 years ago and I came here hoping that my life would be so much better, but no I was fooled. Kids are not welcoming at all. They are plain materialistic. They don't even try to make friends with the new people. And if you ask to sit with them at lunch, they might even say no to your face. This is just from my experience and this school is only decent if you have been here since elementary. Your just another number here and the staff treats me badly. I do not look forward to coming to school everyday. It's plain miserable. I heard great stuff about deer creek before I moved here. Nothing exciting. Absolutely terrible. I had to move out of the district because I was bullied so often. The teachers saw this yet did nothing. Also once I moved I realized that the education at deer creek is terrible. I was three months behind in all of my classes when I moved We have 2 sons at Deer Creek. They have attended since elementary school. We have been very happy with the academic programs and opportunities here. Having 2 band students, we have been thrilled with the music faculty and their dedication to developing the students as musicians and also as persons of character. Deer creek high school is one of the worst in the state. WOKE District, TOP down. Not only WOKE with an agenda, but also with ZERO accountability. Not a safe environment for your highschool children, from administration, to administration staff to the janitor, flawed beginning to end. Too many lack of professional and Acute behavioral issues to comment on. If you choose to send your children here, you will encounter the upmost unprofessional, unaccountable school district you will ever have the displeasure to deal with. Teachers and Administration staff behaving in a manner that is nothing short of questionable and in many cases require a loss of license and accreditation.

column1: I transfered my daughter into Wells half way through her freshman year. I had MAJOR concerns regarding the reputation of the school, however after researching I found that they were cleaning house. My child has never been happier and I as a parent absolutely LOVE the staff at Wells. Principal Matias is doing an amazing job and has really given the school new vision. He greets parents and students with a warm, friendly hug and shows genuine interest in every single student. You just don't see that anymore within school administration. He and his staff are to be commended for their compassion and passion for their jobs. Regarding the things that ppl say about this school, don't believe it. Walk into the campus, take a tour, interact with staff and students. You'll quickly see that this school has gotten a bumm rap. I transfered my daughter from a school with a great reputation, which was my reason for putting her there to only have her belittled by the principal and staff. It was a horrible school, yet known for being "great". I put her in Wells, the reverse happened. A school that's looked badly upon, yet I found them to be amazing. Wells Academy has completely won me over. I attended Wells back in 1968 -71. I often check up to see how things are going there today. It was a wonderful school back then and I see it still is today! As I am 57 years old now I know all our old teachers have left or retired. Thanks to the Principals, staff and students who continue to make me proud! We also have a group on facebook., it's called...."Wells High School 1960 thru 1980" for those that attended back them. Good luck to all your current students! Sincerely, Diane Montague.CLASS OF 1972. Wells Loyalty Song........ Wells High, we raise our voice to thee. Wells High, you have our loyalty, fighting and always striving, to bring to you a victory. So we'll say Wells High, to you we pledge our hearts, to you we will be true. Fight on and keep our colors flying, silver and royal blue. wells academy is the most stupidest school in the city of Chicago with the worse staff who strive to provide the lowest quality education in Illinois! As a current student going to wells high, all I could say is that the teachers, staff, and principal of this school are a blessing. They have years of experience And they are doing 100% of their best to guide us to the right path and NEVER give up on a student if he\she felt if necessary. We may experience mindless fights here and there, but which school doesn't. The teachers, staffs, and principal does their best to steer that troubled teen back on track. This is my 3rd year attending wells high school, from what I've experienced, it'll always be with me. One of my teachers once told me that the story I wrote is talented and it mean alot to me because she is a hard teacher to persuade, but my story persuade her. Just then on, I know my passion is writing. Teachers can inspire you... Teachers can encourage you... Teachers can guide you... Teachers can create a life for you... And I got all that when I decided to come to wells high school. Next year, I'll graduate- but the spirit of wells he would never leave me, for it is the reason I have found the light instead of darkness.

column3: My son graduated from this high school. At the time, the school was split along racial lines; that is, around 65% Navajo and about 20% Hispanic. The remaining 15% was mainly white, with a few Asians. The Navajo kids were friendly. The Hispanics more or less bullied the Navajos. The whites and Asians kept to themselves. A lot of the Navajo kids would drop out, or go to school intermittently, by their junior year.Teachers were for the most part, average. The good ones would only stay a couple of years to get experience, and then move on. When questioned, a few of the teachers could not answer a simple question about what their degree was in. I do not if they were being evasive or smart alecks. I think the former.Counselors were a waste of time. Heck, I knew more than they did about college admissions and college visits.The sports programs were disjointed from a lack of leadership (i.e., real coaches).Anyway, I am glad we moved before our second child started high school.

column1: We moved into Northwest ISD just prior to my daughter beginning 9th grade. I must say, I have been nothing short of whole-heartedly impressed with the staff, parent/teacher communication, and education. Although Byron Nelson is much larger than any of the schools in our previous district, I feel that we have a much closer relationship with my daughter's teachers than we ever have before. They take a genuine and active interest in her success and went above and beyond to help her adjust. They also hold to extremely high technological and educational standards, so I feel confident that my daughter is receiving the best possible education to prepare her for life moving forward. We couldn't be more pleased with both her experiences as a student and our experiences as parents. This is overall a great school from the cafeteria to the teacher/staff involvement. I could not have asked for a better school! As a former student, I loved my time at Byron. With all the extra curricular activities that were offered, it was nearly impossible to not be included in something. The staff (for the most part) were great, as were (again, most of) the administration. There were some hiccups in dealing with discipline, but the school itself was overall a great experience that really helped to prepare me for what was to come. This school is very snobbish and stuck up. Don't go unless you want to be ridiculed and the teachers don't care. This school does not hold kids accountable.. They can turn in homework weeks late for a passing grade, they can RE take a test for higher score.. Nobody fails... This does not prepare kids for real life, or college. Need to change there grading policy. We RE changing districts. I am new to the School, and went to the registrar's office to enroll my girl for 14-2015 year. She had some athletic background but in general we needed advice and guidance on what to do to have her consider the Athletic program. Also, she is an international student, which makes our questions more 'rich' and complex. We were very well supported by the staff, and not a day has passed without them responding my emails or keeping me copied on important meetings even before the new year starts. They do a great job at including new parents and students, making you feel part of the team. Kudos to Byron Nelson! We are extremely pleased with the very high quality of educators, extra curricular programs, athletics, & support from the staff. Teachers and staff are quick to blame students and not listen to them. Dishing out lunch detentions is part of the norm here. I'm not impress with this school and another school in the ISD family. The ISD is all about the teachers and staff and not really about the students. Byron Nelson high school is a very good school I have 2 kids that attend Byron Nelson and they both love it... great job to all the teachers and workers at Byron Nelson Because it has great teachers and they have a great choices of extra curriculars! 2017 I can not stress enough how much this school simply does not care about the mental health or success of the students. They push students to take classes they are not qualified for, simply because it makes the school look good. Students mental health plummets and teachers do not bat an eye. They are too focused on making sure you did the 4 hours of homework they have assigned. I am so sick of this school and the mental health damage it has caused to many students. As a parent of 3 pupils there, I rate the experiences as terrific under Mrs. Parker, and mediocre to awful for our teenager under Dr. Myers. Poor. Pitiful. As in business (and don't think that getting federal tax dollars for your kid being there isn't business), the attitudes of those working the ranks is often driven from the top down. And the attitude at the top, you really don't want to find out for yourself. Terrible. Administration is more concerned with the school and it's reputation than with the students and improving them. They care more about preventing negative videos to surface than the physical safety of the student who was attacked all under the guise of "getting evidence on the attack" although there was a teacher right there - all the evidence needed. I am horrified at the number of violent incidents that are COVERED UP to preserve the reputation of the school. My time at Byron Nelson was the worst 3 years of my life. Innocent kids in my class were oftentimes pulled out of the classroom and questioned and searched by the SRO, and they were almost always expelled from the school even if they didn't have anything remotely suspicious with them. My twin brother and I were HARASSED by the police at the school and consequently dropped out. If you don't fit Trophy Club's rich white cookie-cutter image, Byron Nelson and the Trophy Club Student Resource Officers will bully you until you leave. This school is an absolute joke. I just transferred my daughter to this school. She said that the school is great and the teachers are very nice. She said the 45 minutes class is very productive. She loves learning at this school so much that 45 minutes for each class seems very short. She said it seems like a 20 minutes class. She likes all her teachers. She said that they are very nice and very helpful to her learning. She said the students are nice too. She met some weird kids, but she just ignored them. She is very happy that I transferred her to this school. She fits right in at Byron Nelson HS. I have a Sophomore and a Junior that are currently attending BNHS, as well as one child at the middle school. I can honestly say that they are getting an excellent education in a safe environment. Some of the sports teams are HIGHLY political, but I don't fault the school administration for that... some coaches are just that way. Dr. Myers does a marvelous job communicating with parents and I cannot imagine how difficult it must be to try and please the parents in this community. I'm a former teacher (different district) so I have something to compare BNHS to. Homework seems light to me, but my kids are definitely prepared for college and beyond since they're taking advantage of the AP, On-Ramp, and other supplementary programs that this school offers. This is a wonderful school. I had to switch districts, and Byron Nelson is the best school there is. Way better than my other school.
