column3: The reason for such a low rating is that this school is notorious for allowing bullying to take place. During my time at this school, I witnessed many children get bullied and nothing was done about it. This is especially apparent Junior High and High school where it's common for the victim to be accused of lying or labeled the bad person if you fight back. During my time at Dexter High school I witnessed several instances of students getting bullied. The ones that stick out the most are as follows. In gym class I was tripped several times by other students when asked to do laps around the gym. When I told the gym teacher about the incident, she said that she would watch them. The next day in gym class it happened again and she said didn't see me get tripped. Despite the fact that my friends and other people in the class saw it happen. I saw another student shout a homosexual slur a crossed the room, in front of the teacher every single day that semester and she did nothing. In the middle of a presentation when the class was quiet a student shouted out an insult, the teacher once again did nothing. We are currently juniors at DHS. We believe that DHS is a WONDERFUL school. I completely disagree with he bullying comment and the diversity comment. It's not DHS's fault that we are in a fairly "white" community. That doesn't make us "not diverse" Dexter is a great school in both athletics and education. Thank you everyone for putting up with me for 4 years. -Scott P.S If you're going to join the military, join the Air Force. I absolutely hate this school. Ever since I came here I've been depressed as hell. The teachers don't care about you and they assign so much homework, I feel like I'm drowning in it. I thought that this school would be great with all of the nice reviews, but students never go out of their way to say hello and the teachers are terrible. I hate this school and basically everybody in it. If you care about your child's well-being do not send them to this school. My daughter is a current student at DHS. They have appallingly bad support services for mental health issues, including bullying, depression and even suicidality. We have found the teachers to be lacking in compassion and the counseling office to be overworked and inattentive. Do not expect to hear from teachers, counselors, or administrators... you need to reach out multiple times to get a response. (Outside of Freshman year teachers who we found to be wonderful & empathetic). The changing of teachers mid year for upper level courses is chaotic and means teachers do not know their students and cannot be as supportive. In the current times of rising teen anxiety this is troubling. Despite informing teachers directly of my daughter's situation, which stemmed from in school bullying, the majority of her teachers were annoyed with her accommodation (extended hall pass to avoid bully) and reprimanded her in class daily threatening detention...making the situation worse until she felt she needed to skip that class altogether. At no point did any teacher or administrator become alarmed that a straight A student had begun failing their classes within a 2 month period of time. Even though they had been informed of the situation. When she went to the counseling office for support she was told she wasn't allowed to and to return to class. I find this extremely troubling and do not consider DHS to be a safe supportive environment. Unfortunately, I know of several other students struggling with their mental health issues at this school and none of them are being treated with compassion. The school is not looking out for your student, and sadly your student may not be safe in school. If you need help, you will need to advocate for it yourself and insist on accommodations. DHS is only equipped to handle a student with no special needs. If your student has anxiety or depression I consider this to be an unsafe place for them. I am currently overflown with homework and am becoming quite depressed as I can't keep up with anything anymore.

column1: Falcon High School cares about their students. My daughter was ill last Spring and when she returned this year every teacher that had her in their class took her aside to ask her how she was doing. I am giving it a 2 stars just because of the grading system before it was changed it was a 5 star.Falcon High has great teachers. My concerned for the last 2 years is that with the Standard Base Grading they will be burned out. With this new way of grading students can retake test to raise them " to master the topic". To do this teachers stay before and after school to reteach what was already taught in class. I don't see how this will help with getting them ready for college since the students are not motivated to do H.W. or stay on task since is not required, " study at tour own pase" I think that in the real world you do things on time correctlly or you get fired from your job. In college you have due dates and if you can't keep up with your class you fail. It is sad to overwork the teachers and have the students not being taught that responsability and time management is important. i love that school it help me though my rough teens years and i know that all of the other teacher that i know either retired from there they are a very good school i am the alumin for their i was graduate from there in 1992 and i learn alot from there so people need to learn alot from this school like i did I absolutely hate this school. The grading system makes your life a living hell. The teachers in the math department don't care about the kids. Some of the security officers are more of friends then security officers. Don't enroll your child here! Between Schoology and Infinite Campus, I am forced to spend many hours trying to find information on school work due, grades, attendance, quizzes, test results, etc. The information is never easy to find and both sites are extremely difficult to navigate. Getting information out of the teachers is nearly impossible, unless you are willing to meet them after school and don't be late or they will leave! This is a terrible school! The principle is incompetent and has poor judgment in hiring and retaining teachers and coaches. We have had the worst experience and this post is to prevent other parents from enrolling their children into this poor excuse for a high school! Not to big of a school and a lot of things to do. I give it 5 stars for the chance to get better. Many parents have to use expectation management. Smaller schools and districts don't have as much money. I hear complaints daily about things like sports uniforms and petty stuff. Then go live in a district that has outrageous taxes and HOA fees if you want materialistic things for your children. This area is growing and growing fast, give it time. Falcon is amazing. I didn’t go to falcon all 4 years so I had experience at another high school. Falcon has everything a potential new student or a freshman could need. From S2S (student to student) all the way to guidance counselors who actually care about their students and their success. 5 stars, students get out what they put in. Small town high school with a small town feel. The grading system is confusing at best and nothing like the rest of the high schools in the district. Extra curricular classes offered are sufficient except for foreign language, which is one choice, Spanish. Given that 2 years are a requirement you'd think there would be more options. As a parent, there's little to motivate my child to be interested in learning. First, off it should be mentioned that I have no hate for the school I just want to improve it. Second, For sake of privacy, I'm leaving out the teacher's name. Biology Honors, the style of teaching that this class uses is not good whatsoever. Our teacher has us take notes at home, then come into class expecting that we know everything, this is good for the next class, but you'll just end up forgetting the next 2 days or so, but for some students, this is a good style of teaching but for most, it's not. I love the teachers here but SOME classes do not teach the subject very well. As well, the system of grading here is really not the best, the tests are worth too many points, for context most of the coursework won't matter if you don't do well on a test. The only time it would help is if your grade is sitting right on the line of two letter grades. Even more, you can't switch classes after a certain period of time. But that wouldn't be a problem if it weren't for the fact that all the classes don't really get into work in the time frame in which you can switch classes. What I'm saying is the classes give you no real reason for you to switch until the deadline is up. To lunches, why is lunch 4 dollars? I know it's dominos's pizza and higher-quality food than the middle school nearby but 4 whole dollars? Why are half the appliances in the bathroom not working? Most sinks are not working, most blow dryers aren't working, and paper towel dispensers aren't stocked. I don't understand why they aren't working because you pay 4 dollars for lunch, 40 for an upcoming homecoming(not to mention all the other stuff your gonna get while you're there), and money to get into sports events, where's all of this going to(i suppose that isn't my business to know but, I'm just curious)?But, with all that mentioned there are a lot of good things about the school, The teachers themselves(not the classes) are amazing, the food is good(just a bit pricy), more freedom when it comes to phones, extracurricular activities, and the number of different classes to suit your future. A lot of the problems I mentioned above I believe could be fixed if mentioned by students, which, is my motive for writing this review. I have no hate towards the school but I just want it to improve.

When I asked her for advice on classes, she pointed me to the easy classes -- classes that required little to no effort to obtain an "A." In addition, many of the athletic activities required a large fee. Since many of the non-white students' family typically do not earn enough to pay the 200+ dollar fee, the team lacks diversity that could bring new perspectives.

column1: MCHS is a wonderful school with a family environment. Everyone knows eachother and feels relaxed in this safe enviornment. Help and support from teachers is always avalible to all students whenever requested. There isnt any sports but students are still active and have after school activities for example grade vs grade football games, running club, eco club, and some other stuff. It is truely a wonderful school with amazing opportunities like getting your AA degree before your high school diploma. My daughter got accepted to Middle College High School, and we are really excited about her opportunity however there are few concerns: 1) Office staff not helpful and barely polite 2) On end of year open house, I was expeciting to see remarkable student work, and I saw average or just below it. 3) They keep driving the point home that they don't have any athletics (obviously the reason that 60-70% of the students are obese), and almost no school activities. Can they offer at least a glimmer of hope for those of us hoping for happy, well-adjusted teens?,,, From the principal: To the parent who wrote this review - please come and see me to discuss your concerns. I am currently a sophomore here in middle college high and this school academically is great but the school has no school pride. I have tried to get other students involved in their school but they just give up. As freshmen you come in with a little spark of school pride and we could have school pride but due to the upperclassmen's lack of pride the new students learn that there is no school spirit and the little spark they had dies out. This school might not ever have school pride. I believe this is because our school does not have any sports thus noting to be proud of and no competition against us. Academically this school is great. The teachers in this school are always there if you are falling behind or having and trouble understanding some material. Our school has had a 100% passing rate in the 10th grade CAHSEE for the pass 6 years!!!! Most of the students have college classes and some finish with their AA. In the end i would not transfer to a different school. Our school is like a little family and and everyone knows everyone. All we need is a little school pride. This school is so great, the teachers really connect with you and it seems like everyone is a family. My daughter loves this school, shes become more outgoing and the privileges of being in college and high school at the same time is unbelievable! I am glad my son is at this school. He has been given tools to succeed in life and for his education. Dr. Apps and the staff really care about the kids and there future. My son is has a wide perspective of what requirements are necessary to succeed in higher education. I am so glad my child is able to form part of this school. The expectations are high but with the help and support from the educators I know my child will succeed. Thank you teachers and staff. well i really was looking forward for my daughter to attend this school.. but first she did not get an invitation which really surprised me...second when i called to get information the person who assist me was not helpfull at all ...it totally lowered my expectations toward her going here...

column3: This is a terrible school. Students can wear revealing and innappropriate clothing. Mp3 players are allowed in class. Students are not disciplined appropriately. The gang influence is extreme and the drug use is extravagant. This school allows kids to wear whatever they want, short shorts, low cut tops, flip flops, clothes you would expect to see at a beach or club, not school, this is very distracting. Orientation was very disorganized, many kids didn't get a class schedule, the office personnel are rude and unconcerned, kids drive way too fast in the stuent parking lot and the only good thing is the chorus teacher is amazingly interested in his students progress and the kids were selected to sing at Disney I would give the school 5 stars but dress code is not enforced & the administration is soft on discipline. My children go here & I substitute teach regularly (7 years) at this school. I don't know who the other reviewers were speaking about in the office personnel, but I have never had anyone be rude, disrespectful, or unconcern to me in any of the offices. The kids on the other hand, can be downright disrespectful & disgustingly undisciplined. Honestly, it reflects their parents disregard to the educators & not making their children take ownership of behavior & their education (blame the teachers not the child for the child's failure). As for the 105 teachers, 95-98% are wonderful & care deeply about all the children (even "bad seeds"). If the parents/students communicate with the teachers, the teachers will stick their necks out to help the students to succeed. This school has great trade classes, so the students aren't stuck to entirely general courses. It also has a good selection of music (orchestra, band, chorus, guitar, keyboard) & art (general, AP, ceramics, photography, industry) classes. In response: Yes students listen to their MP3s, not a problem if they are working. =) the school enviorment is very nice, teachers are so polite with student. The Staff The Teachers & The Principal are Amazing with making sure Our Kids Safety and Educations is their Priority. They have the Thunder College Program this year which is wonderful as well as the Elective Classes they have where the kids show motivation and are excited about belonging to this school. My Child Loves it and So do I. My Son also attended this school many years ago. Its all about The Students and Their Future.

column1: Needs much improvement ! I had a daughter there for 10th and 11th and she began cutting classes every day. I wasnt even notified until she was so far absent from a couple classes that she had little chance of passing the year at all. Between the drugs, guys grabbing her, and profanity, I almost understood why she would skip classes. Almost nothing was done to keep me informed of her attendance, except me calling and going by the school daily by popping in during school hours and making them call the teacher she was supposed to have at that time to see if she was actually in class before I would discover she wasn't there and was still continuing to miss. Nothing was done about cyber bulling or bullying on the bus which happened to my other daughter almost daily and was reported repeatedly. As for cell phone use, it is NEVER enforced. Don't know why anyone would want to send their child here. This school is honestly one of the worst of it's kind. I would rate it 0 stars if I could. There was a shocking amount of bullying going on. Most of the students were disrespectful and there is always profanity being used up and down the halls in between classes. Most teachers picked "favorites" and used that to judge your grade. There were only 2-3 good teachers that actually did their job the way it should be done. The Guidance Department is a joke and gives you no help in the college process whatsoever. One counselor will swear by one thing, while the other will tell you something completely different. I missed out on several scholarship opportunities due to being misinformed. Unless you're a cheerleader or a football player, you might as well give up on trying to get funding for any other program. This school mainly emphasizes on getting higher FCAT scores and less on preparing a student for the real world. I am a 2011 graduate of this school, and I couldn't be more happy. It's a shame that when others ask me where I graduated from, I have to say "West Nassau High School". All in all, you're better off going to another school if you value your education. -A Former Student. I enjoyed this school. For all the people who complain you need to be more in control of your education. It is a small time school with little bullying. If you think there are a lot of drugs and profanity go to a duval school. For the person who said it does not prepare you for the real world but the said students use too much profanity and bigger programs like cheerleading and football get all the funding...... Grow up that's pretty much how real life goes. You can't expect other people like counselors to get you in college, fill out your own applications. And for the parent with their kid skipping, get control of your kid. If you couldn't keep track at that at small time west nassau it would have been way worse at a duval county school. I graduated from west nassau with honors and continued to get a full ride academic scholarship to university of Florida. It's called hard work. If you are looking for a handout then yes this school isn't for you. But it has small town values, a place to build great friendships and actual communication and realionships with the teachers. I would never trade any of my memories made at this school. as a west nasty student, I can formally say that this school is pretty garbage most like all high schools though it just one big popularity contest that people look back on and laugh at how stupid we are so yeah its a garbage school but get over it.

column3: Silver Creek is my alma mater. I am now a teacher, elsewhere. I go back every now and then to visit old teachers and for sports events. I have also substitute taught at Silver Creek (elementary, middle and high), along with a broad range of other schools. I can say that, growing up in Silver Creek, my peers often spoke poorly of the school. At the time, I saw nothing wrong with the school, but teenagers have a way of bashing their school regardless of its quality. In my opinion, parenting has a lot more to do with a child's adolescent experience than anything. Your son or daughter will spend, on average, 13 percent of waking hours in school by age 18. That means 86 percent of children's time is spent out of school, mainly at home. Coming back to Silver Creek after experiencing many other schools has enlightened me on the following: the facilities are newer and better than most, the cafeteria is unbelievable, and the teachers are absolutely unmatched. Silver Creek, as a school district, is fantastic. Any weariness of sending a child to this school should be due to the community in which it is placed, which is very unfortunate. This school has all the potential in the world and I hope that it one day meets that potential. I succeeded in this school and my experience was more than enjoyable. I thank the school leaders and staff for their continued efforts.

column1: My daughter went there for three years and graduated from there. I also have a son that attends this school. It's clean,safe and has a good faculty. Both of my kids like the school. column3: We all know some people will complain about everything. But all I've seen is so far so good. I graduated from SHHS with a 3.8 GPA and honors and am currently attending Michigan State. I continue to do well in my studies. However, I can whole-heartedly and without a doubt say that none of my collegiate accomplishments can be attributed to the pathetic excuse for an education that I received here. I did well in my AP classes in order to bring as much knowledge with me to college as possible. The teachers failed to help me achieve this. I came to college confident of my ability, and for the last three years, it has become clearer and clearer of the simple things I find myself struggling with that all students around me gained from high school. Most notably, a proper history education and the ability to conduct formal research. AND the arithmetic sector of this high school--my AP calc class was basically a sham, with a teacher who had no right (moreso ability) to teach it. There are teachers, few and far between, who are knowledgable and generous with their time/ability to teach; but the lot is lazy and presumes "eh, most of the students are entering the workforce or Macomb Community anyhow, who cares." It is sad, and I should have transferred after freshman year. Absolutely terrible!!! I hated every single minute I was at this school. For starters, school starts way too early for teenagers to even learn anything. There are too many kids at this school and I just felt like a number in the crowd. I felt invisible. The kids already had their friend groups and I made no friends. I ate lunch alone every day and nobody ever came to sit with me or talk to me. The teachers are also terrible. My English teacher hated us and called us stupid. She made us do too much work. She made us write essays but we had to use her exact essay format which was a terrible way to write essays. My math teacher couldn’t teach worth anything and everyone that has had him agrees. The material on his test was not anything like what we had “learned” in class. I earned my first bad grade in his class because he couldn’t teach. My dance teacher called me and my dance partner “weighed down” and was discriminatory against bigger girls who didn’t have dancer bodies. Wcspa was terrible too. There are again too many kids and it focused heavily on dance. We maybe acted a handful of times throughout the whole year. Overall my experience was terrible.

column1: NDP is AWESOME end of story! We left SCA and couldn't be happier here, our son is thriving at NDP. And I don't have to deal with the inexperienced, inept administration at SCA any longer, that place is going down hill in a hurry. I am a student at Notre Dame Prep. Parents and staff may sell you on the "amazing" school where their child is "thriving" but they do not know what goes on inside of the school. Students enjoy ganging up on people to make them feel weak and no one stands up for them. For the most part, teachers hand out detentions to the same students because they simply think they're doing something wrong when in reality they are not. Over all this school's teachings of Reverence, Respect, and Responsibility, are not represented by the students in any way. We will withdraw our child from Notre Dame this year. Our child was sexually harassed and the boy was not permanently punished, although his behavior was ground for expulsion. Other girls were also harassed, and the administration has been aware, but the boy still attends Notre Dame. His behavior was was undeniably, "Behavior unbecoming of a Christian". Several members of the student body are mean and bully non-white students. In one situation a black teen had food thrown at them along with derogatory statements being screamed at them too. Although the school claims they do Good Works, most children do it only to fulfill a credit, not to truly exemplify Christian traits. With all the scandal in the Catholic church, I thought they would handle situations more carefully. The education is not better than the public high school either, yet you'll pay college tuition like fees to attend their school. I would not recommend this school to anyone. Notre Dame Preparatory is an excellent school. Teachers and staff are not only well prepared, but are truly committed to their students. Academics are challenging but most teachers tried their best to help students who need help. My oldest daughter graduated from NDP and is doing extremely well in college. She got a substantial scholarship to attend an out of state private university. Her graduating class received in excess of eight milion dollars in scholarships. I feel she was well prepared for college. The service oriented program allows students to realize the many opportunities how they can help and impact their community. I feel grateful for NDP's help in educating my child. Notre Dame Preparatory is an awful school. Not only do they worry about dress code over academics, they suck the fun out of high school. If your child is academically gifted, DONT send them here. NDP does not accommodate any one who cannot fit into their "cookie cutter" student. However, if you have money and parents willing to donate, than you're in luck because thats all they care about. NDP does not prepare high schoolers for the basics of life. They baby us and give anyone with money an 'A' or they let them stay in school after they broke their "zero tolerance" drug policy. The only thing this school is good at is prayer. If I had children of my own, I would NOT send them here. I LOVE THE MOMS AND THEIR $100 LULULEMON YOGA PANTS. I ALSO LOVE THEIR SARCASTIC STORIES OF HOW INCREDIBLE STUDENTS ARE Used to be a great school. New administration has all but ruined it. Most recently, a national event Project Graduation. Held on the night of graduation to keep our children safe, has been unilaterally decided upon to be two days after graduation night(a time when most accidents occur) It has always been the Night of graduation. Despite the class of 2015 and THE PARENTS objections, the principal has decided to have it two days later. Makes no sense!!!! Please have your children go elsewhere. I have had children there for ten years. Thrilled to be leaving This school is absolutely amazing. The teachers and administration are extremely caring about the students and the community. They expect nothing but the best from their students and work hard to show them how to achieve it. It is absolutely the best choice we could have made for our son. Many great teachers had left the school and more leaving. I feel bad that this school is already in decline given its short history. It looks great outside but if you dig a little deeper the school is poorly managed by the administrators. This school is not for a child who wants to succeed. I believe in religion and love for Christ. Just not at this school. It deprives your energy and it takes away a lot of things from you. The rules are ridiculous. I believe in strict not ridiculous. Do not let the new stadium fool you- Notre Dame is taking a rapid decline. Under current administration there has been very high teacher turn over, rapidly increasing tuition and a diminished sense of community. A very punitive culture has been created. There are a handful of great teachers (many however are brand new to teaching although higher tuition should suggest the opposite), and a wonderful Director of curriculum. The counseling department does not do very much in the college planning arena. The lack of Catholic values is alarming and the Diocese has been contacted over and over regarding the problem. So far-nothing has changed. There is great potential for NDP to be great again- new leadership is a must. We are in our 6th year at NDP and sadly are counting the days until we are done. I strongly advise doing homework and asking a lot of questions before committing to the school. NDP is an excellent school that prepares students for college, the challenges in life and helps them be well rounded contributing members of society. It is not an easy school and not for everyone, so maybe that's why there are disgruntled parents, you have to work hard at NDP, it is a private Catholic school so the rules may not be for everyone. I have put 3 kids through NDP and all have loved the school, its programs, athletics, faculty and it was worth every penny. Every school will have issues between parents and faculty about rules, education, etc. and while no school is perfect, your child will get an excellent education at NDP that will help them be a well rounded student and be prepared for college. Parents at this school are extremely poor examples for their children. Their belief that they are entitled to disrespect others and to treat them as less is shocking and reprehensible. So sad that the wonderful students at Notre Dame have parents that act they way they do. If you want your child to be successful in life and academically competitive enough to get them into a school other than Scottsdale Community College, do not send them to NDP. Kids are nearby charter schools are 5 years ahead in math of NDP kids. Meaning, your NDP high school senior is doing 7th and 8th grade math. May as well send them to a public school and save your money. Good school. Great kids come out of this great community in N. Scottsdale. It is a newer school. NDP really is a community and family for the students and parents. A great choice in education! Notre Dame is hit or miss. Some great teachers, some awful teachers. The bigger issue for us has been the students. The school is full of cliques, with some truly cruel students in leadership positions. If there are issues, the teachers and administration react by blaming and shaming the victims (telling them to try harder to be part of the cliques). Most parents, teachers and administration do not model caring, inclusive behavior. Also, how much money you donate directly impacts whether your student will get the classes they want and attention from the administration. Not a really bad school, but a disappointment for our family and our children. This use to be a great school. Developed students, made them grow. The new principal is terrible. He's chased away many of the good teachers. They try to catch the kids doing things wrong. So sad. Save your money. Hopefully, you'll see changes in leadership than can right the couse of this once great school! This is a case of great school gone very bad. New principal is beyond awful. Does not know the 1st thing about leadership. We chose NDP over Brophy, Chap, and Scottsdale Prep. After careful consideration, we chose the school best suited for our son. Students at NDP can challenge themselves academically by taking advanced honor-level academic courses. Plus, even though NDP has only 900 students, it plays up and competes in the second highest tier of AIA sports (now 5A, competing against South Mountain, Paradise Valley, and Sunnyslope). Our son loves it and is very happy! Drugs are rampant at this school. Their random drug tests are a joke. NDP is a public school you pay tuition for. I was really hoping it would be a great school. Very disappointed and no longer attend. No phone call from principal, VP, dean or priest. Save your money, and child, and stay far far away! The review from January is completely true. I'm a teacher at this school. I would never send a child of mine here. We are a month in a NDP and i feel the need to warn all prospective parents.... THIS IS NOT A CATHOLIC SCHOOL! This is a private school that caters to North Scottsdale wealthy families that don't want to continue their public education. I always wondered why friends who sent their kids to Brophy or Xavier smirked when I said mine was going to NDP, now I know. Bullying is rampant and if your kid is not a super jock, good luck. The culture caters to the athletically inclined and the drug testing is a JOKE. All of these kids are vaping, drinking, drugging. They just know how to buck the system. I'm BEYOND disappointed and will share it with the world. This school is NOT a Catholic centered school. It definitely is not diverse either. It is primarily a rich, white, population of spoiled kids. There is a big drug and alcohol problem, as well as a lot of bullying that goes on. It's out of control. My son has been able to come out of this tougher stronger and great human being. If he hadn't been helped by a few key teachers it could have been a disaster. CHOOSE NDP CAREFULLY; ITS NOT FOR EVERY KID. I DIDN'T CHOOSE THIS SCHOOL MY EX-WIFE DID AND WE (MY SON AND I) HAVE HAD TO DEAL WITH THE AFTER EFFECTS. We left NDP last year because of the bullying and lack of support for our student. I got the notice that the school was having its second annual run focused on teens helping teens with mental health issues such as suicide prevention, depression and anxiety. This is such a joke. NDP does NOT support students with mental health issues. The administration minimizes reports from doctors and specialists, teachers who are informed of them tell the students they don’t believe in the diagnoses and them them to stop pretending and making excuses. Other students pretend to be supportive at rallies and in front of their parents and teachers and then ridicule, bully and shun them socially and in front of other students. Do NOT send your child here if they have any learning issues, dyslexia, ADHD, depression or anxiety. You will regret it like we did. Public schools have the support your child will need. Not NDP. The message was sent to intimidate in fact the verbiage included a statement of “how much they had done for us … “ all in all we paid tuition just like everyone else, we left because of hazing, bullying without any oversight. It works for some families clearly, it’s an “elite mindset” not appropriate for education. Just when you’ve paid tuition save up for all the red carpet fundraising for heaven knows what… Not a safe place students fight and gang up on kids who are different and no one protects them There is NO Bully policy even if uou search their website for the word “bully” you’ll find nothing because they don’t care who is harmed in anyway there.. It’s made the lives of young male students living hell because they can’t be gay out loud. Suicide is talked about amongst these kids they are so fearful to be themselves .. it’s toxic i'm literally traumatized by this school. i lost so much confidence and gained many insecurities by the bratty girls judging me whenever i spoke and talked to them. keep in mind, i was only attending this school for a year. many people have left since i started because no one likes being surrounded by rich, materialistic teenagers. keeping up with your grades at this school is impossible too because the teachers are NOT GOOD. don't be fooled by the kids' fake smiles on their website and instagram. a majority of these kids dread going to school each day and getting referrals on their permanent records for not tucking in their shirt. the counselors are rude, and not there for the right purposes. do you really want your kids being told the pandemic is because of the asians? save your yourself and your mental state. On paper NDP is fantastic. It reality, it is awful. The staff turnover is incredibly high. Last year alone, we had the athletic director, varsity soccer coach, varsity pom coach, and dean of men leave mid-year. The student turnover is just as bad. The new principal, Mr. Sweeney, is a joke. Things were much better when Jill Platt was the Principal. NDP is an overpriced, average school that inflates grades to keep parents happy.

In short, Alexandria has a terrific public high school that prepares students for college success and for life. If you want to send your children to a high-quality public high school, TC is a great option. I am a junior at TC Williams High School. TC Williams is the worst high school in northern virginia. I can tell you many reasons to why it's bad. The bathroom smell extremely bad. One time I went in the bathroom you would not believe what I saw in there, apparently there was poop on the ceiling since November. The food there is extremely horrible. Sometimes when I get my food, it turns out that the food is barely cooked. Another reason is that some students in this school tend to have fights and others think it's interesting to watch people fight. TC Williams High School may have extracurricular activities and clubs but the students tend to have a very low academic record. Sometimes I sit and wonder, why couldn't I have gone to Annandale High School in 10th grade. Anyway, the only great thing about this school are the teachers because they are extremely helpful. The student population is exceptionally diverse and the volume of students is high. HOWEVER, the school does a laudable job at finding ways to meet the wide range of student needs it encounters there. Lots of opportunities for extracurriculars exist here, and the diversity was a great exposure for students to learn acceptance and tolerance in a constructive manner. I love the open-mindedness the experience instilled in both my sons, and I love that despite the size of the school, the administration has always seemed like one that will listen. I was a deployed reservist during my son's senior year, and he got incredible support from the school during that time. TC is a very good, community-oriented school that teaches students far more than just academics. I would love to see it grow its STEM program even more, and I hope that now the NSF is in the neighborhood, there will be additional involvement to help make that happen-- The well-regarded college prep curriculum and program at TC Williams is modern, comprehensive and personalized with excellent guidance resources. The staff and faculty are dedicated and skilled. With a diploma from TC Williams, a student can compete anywhere in the world and there is no limit to his or her growth potential. My son is enjoying the STEM program TC Williams is one of the best high schools around for students having potential and preferring a challenging environment. The school community, the educators, and the Alexandria community come together to support all students in this truly great high school. We highly recommend it to other families and encourage you to go visit the impressive campus. Large, diverse school with lots of options for kids who lean in TC Williams has high quality instructors, first-class facilities, skilled administrators, excellent college counseling, and a culture of success among the student body. While the many high-achievers receive attention for their successes, the school provides a truly great educational experience and extracurricular opportunities for all students. I cannot believe how misleading this website’s rating is for T.C. Williams High School. Alexandria’s diverse population with many non-native English speakers drives this error as the ratings formula is driven by mean scores which are naturally favor homogeneous communities. Go see the school and the Alexandria School System yourself. You will be impressed with the educators, the facilities and the resources. T.C.W.’s large cohort of college-bound students matriculate into top colleges around the county (and the world) each year. This is concrete evidence that T.C. is truly a great school and a great community. TC Williams consistently generates a pipeline of some of the most talented and accomplished student scientists in the United States. This year, a TC student won the prestigious and competitive Regeneron Science Talent Search. TC Williams has one of the nation’s premier high school rowing programs with hundreds of student athletes participating. The school’s boathouse on the Potomac in Old Town and the program’s community support are unique. People say TCW allows kids to choose “Yale or jail” and its true. You can find trouble here or take the AP courses and set yourself up for a great future - all less than 10 miles from DC. I was lucky enough to teach both the STAR program students and the AP students (and those classes in between). The difference in teaching and attitude is amazing. Most of the kids in the STAR program were low income kids, while the children in AP courses were middle /upper middle class children. There is bullying and fights that disrupt the learning process and the bullying keeps those kids, who would otherwise do well in class, not to excel. There is much much work to be done at TC Williams. I am a college student who attended TCW for four years, and I am quite surprised to see the negative comments below. The college prep track, including the Stem academy and health sciences academy, is superior to the local private schools and facilities are new and modern. The quality of the education, rich resources, and fantastic faculty provided me with a solid foundation to be accepted at a national university and to continue my studies. I made the massive mistake of sending my daughter to this school: poor teaching and counseling In unsafe environments. You can succeed if you want to. This school offers high-level courses and rigorous classes, although many students do not challenge themselves. Great facilitcies as well. Much better than other schools in the nearby area. column1: This is the first year of our child attending Heritage and my husband and I have been very pleased with the curriculum and experience our son has received. We will be back. This school was recommended to us by our neighbors. Their children have attended and loved it. We decided to send our child there this year and we have seen an increase in our child's productivity and grades. When my husband and I sat our daughter down to discuss how she was liking the school, she couldn't stop talking about how much she enjoyed it and how she felt like she got more one-on-one time with her teacher than at her previous school. We couldn't be happier with our experience! Heritage Academy has been a wonderful experience for our children thus far. My wife and I were recommended Heritage by a family friend because of their excellent standards. Our children both love the experience and we couldn't be more thrilled. I was hesitant to have my children switch schools, but I am so glad I did. They are in 7th, 8th and 10th grade. My two Jr. High Students absolutely LOVE it. They never had any trouble at the other school, they just were tired of the negative atmosphere and the poor choices that they saw going on around them all day. Although I didn't want to put my kids "in a bubble" one of my son's explained that he didn't want to be in a bubble, he just didn't want to have vulgarity and low standards around him while he was trying to learn. So, I told them we would give Heritage a try. It is wonderful to have them come home so happy and excited to share all about how different it was from their old school. My high school student is having a positive experience as well but does miss some of the freedom's of his old school like cell phones in class, hour long lunch breaks, and long hair. As a parent the lack of those things at Heritage is a plus, not a minus! I was concerned that I would see a drop in my kids grades because they never had a lot of home work at their old schools. They do have more work but I have not heard 1 complaint from them. I am so glad we made the switch. This school is EXCELLENT - great teachers, administration and a incredible education! Keep up the great work. My husband and I had to pull our kids out of this school after just a couple of months. Be aware that this is indeed a right-wing, L.D.S leaning school and they teach in this direction. If you are L.D.S. then this is probably a good choice for you because they teach directly into your wheelhouse. We are not and our children came home feeling frustrated and left out. I don't know if this teaching is a result of the school or the teachers but there is clearly a religious bend here and open-minded thinking is not an ideal they seem to encourage. I will start by saying we are not LDS, we are non-denominational Christians and are very glad we moved our daughter from the public high school she was in. Yes, this is a right wing school, one reason we like this school. They do put high value in education, another reason. They do have more rules and higher standards, yup another reason. We knew all of this going in and it has been the best decision for our daughter (10th grade). We also have a 6 & 3 yr old and both will attend from 7th -12th. Our only regret is that our 15 yr old did not start here in 7th grade. The staff actually cares about our child and is there as a teacher and protector. Our experience was horrid with public schools, from threats of violence to slander, etc. I now do not worry when the school calls that I am going to hear that my child is at the hospital, police station or worse. Heritage is a small community and we are blessed and thankful to be a part of this community. While our daughter needed time to adjust, going from a free for all environment to an environment that is respectful, honorable, trustworthy & dedicated to excellence takes time. She has adjusted and we all won't have it any other way!! We switched to Heritage a few years ago because our son was bored at the local public Jr High after going to an excelerated charter for elementary. He has an August birthday and we had not started him in kindergarten until he was 6.... so technically he should have been a grade ahead anyway. We approached the administration at the Pulic Jr High about him skipping a grade and they refused.....saying "Why would you take an excelling student and move him up a grade and make him mediocre?" What??!!!! So we took him to take the placement test at Heritage. He did extremely well on that test and was moved up a grade. After 1 WEEK at Heritage he tod us he never wanted to move back to the public school. He is now at the top of his class as a Sophmore and his sister is an 8th grader there. They feel safe and they love the small community. They love learning about the Founding Fathers and about the Constitution. Are younger 2 children will attend here as well! We love it! ndThis school is very exclusive. The teachers and students will talk about their beliefs nonstop. Now, if you are LDS, this may not be a huge deal. As someone who is not, however, it is interfering with my learning. It is also misleading in its advertisement. Listing it as a music/arts school when it is very much not. Think twice. This school has changed dramatically with the change in leadership. The experience is not what it used to be. Before this year, my kids loved Heritage. What is now left is not good. I will be pulling all three of my students, and I would advise those considering this school to weigh other options as well. It is no longer what it professes to be. Fabulous! I would recommend anyone to attend Heritage all 6 years. It is a great experience to launch a student into the real world of college and work. The dual enrollment program at Heritage Academy, combined with the exceptional faculty makes them soar above the other schools out there. My daughter is in her third year here and is on track to get her associate's degree at the same time she graduates from high school. I'm grateful for her hard work and dedication, paired with caring staff who are cheering her on and supporting her. Plus their arts programs are top notch!! There is a wonderful atmosphere at this school. It is truly one of a kind! This is a horrible school from top to bottom. The owner and principal have no business trying to be in education let alone any business trying to run a school. If the ADE went into this school and really investigated what really goes on here they would shut them down. Sped is a mess because the Sped director did not do her job and did not know how to do it. They are out of compliance with that entire department. Academics they have people in classrooms that have no business teaching and are not qualified. A theme that runs rampant in this school is that no one is qualified to be a teacher. There are those few who are, but only very few. Outstanding student scholars, faculty and administration are committed to having a positive and high-level learning environment. It wasn’t the best time. There was definitely a bias taught in the history class, specifically the seniors government class. The required textbook is obviously politically biased and it makes me unhappy to see it. It does have some great teachers and engaging classes, but it’s academically tough. Don’t go if you don’t want to struggle. Also there is little diversity (race, religion, or politics wise). Most students are nice, but I don’t know if it feels racist because I’m not a POC, but it might be lol. It doesn’t have many elective choices but it has some unique ones. Almost everyone there, the staff and students, are Mormon. As someone who isn’t Mormon but knows a lot about it, it is Christian based, subtly, in almost everything.

column3: I moved away from East Lansing, and oh do I miss the communication with the teachers, They are excellent at what they do, and the Principal Paula runs that school like it should be. Outstanding!!!!! Budget cuts have undermined what used to be an excellent school. Now it is merely "pretty good". There are over 30 kids in many English & Social Studies classes, making it difficult for teachers to review and return writing assignments on a timely basis. There are excellent teachers and sub-standard teachers - it's a roulette wheel each year regarding what quality level of teaching your student might get. Guidance support services are lacking in the area of curriculum preparation and application know-how for students who want to attend a selective college. Positives: The math and science programs are fairly strong for accelerated learners. What separates this school from the rest is it's accepting attitudes and inclusiveness of the student body. East Lansing High School is the worst school I ever put my daughter in. The local students are all spoiled brats and the bullying is outrages! If you are a transfer student be careful in selecting this school.The Principle Staff is a failure when it comes to addressing the bullying. The parents do not care what their kids or have no clue what they do at school. Look It's really not that special or different. There are basic busywork classes. I don't know how other schools do this, but the AP classes were IMPOSSIBLE. Most AP teachers wouldn't even talk about the material, but assign impossible tests, which studying for them left me with four hours of sleep per night. I didn't even want to go to college as a result!! There's social drama like everywhere else, and for four straight years, I was worried where I would "belong" in life, only to find that Michigan State, closer to the world, made way more sense, and was actually way different. I had a couple amazing teachers though, which I will remember for the rest of my life, one of whom will become principal next year. Nobody at this school has friends or dates, since they are trying not to fail their classes, and the people display liberal arrogance. Some teachers are good but a lot are too hard. It seems that it's the goal for everyone in this school to go to Harvard and MIT, which is pretty impractical IMO, especially since I'm going into electrical repair. It's not really different from most high schools otherwise. I am so glad that I can finish my high school education at LCC and get a diploma! I am removing my child from this school after this year. She had to repeat a math class that she got an A on last year. One teacher loses papers so they have to be redone; another teacher is mean, belittling, and intimidating and I've had to go to the principal about him; another teacher lets the kids go wild in class so the ones who want to work can't. My daughter is an advanced student and this is not the place for her. She gets blocked from her locker by a group of kids, who call themselves "gangstas," pick on her so she can no longer use it. She gets tired of all the talk of pot and sex (yes, I know this happens everywhere nowadays, but my daughter is actually there because she wants to learn). One of her friends is also being removed next year, and yet another already has been. Terrible. It's supposed to be the one of the best schools in Michigan. However, I guess a good education consists of 7 hours of fill in the blanks homework every day. The math department has declined since I was here and the teachers just read out of the book and can't answer simple questions. At the same time, the teachers grade really hard and make condescending comments towards the students. This school is supposed to be "tolerant and openminded", but I have never been bullied EVER to the extent when I was here, and only had a couple acquaintances for four years. One student even started a Facebook group against me and I couldn't sleep for days. This school doesn't educate the whole student body, it only caters to the top 10% and believes the other 90% are better off grilling burgers. I hated this school. They heavily discriminated against me because I'm a slightly overweight male. If you were a slightly overweight girl, there were no problems. Nobody should have to suffer so much for a few extra pounds!! Great school! My kids are very prepared for college and the sports programs are excellent.

column1: My school is union academy monroe nc. The students love their school and the teachers. Love to hear how well the students do their grades and getting into college. The teachers seem to have a closer relationship with the students and help the students learn so they can excel in their natural talents. My School is Union Academy. I have been attending this school since 2nd grade and I am now in 8th. This school is a good school because of what they teach. The only thing that they really need to improve on is the everyday bells because kids get locked out of the school :(. Otherwise this school is great with character, diversity. Plus if your child is struggling with academics they always have tutoring to help them. This is truly a great school I have several children at Union Academy. I am pleased with the education they are receiving, however in light of recent events, the school has proven that they do not have consequences for the children. Unfortunately, this school has proven that it CANNOT "do the right thing even when no one is looking". Good education but sadly lacking in discipline and good morals. It has changed so much and definitely not for the better. We will not be returning next year! Love love love this school!! The teachers really care about and love their students! I am daily amazed by all that my daughter is learning! This is our first year at this school and we find the teachers to be very caring, encouraging and quite proficient. My daughter's teachers genuinely love what they do. They incorporate creative ways to entice learning and solicit our input. They curriculum is appropriately challenging and we love their character development initiatives. Every staff member is so friendly and kind(Yes, they've seen me at my worst...) Every parent should feel welcome to the UA environment and experience. Even not-so-sociable parents like us are happy at UA. This school is top notch in ways that goes beyond just the great academics!! I had heard good things about this school, but we were very disappointed with all aspects. We found it to be poorly organized and lacking in all areas. The quality of the teachers and staff was subpar, especially in comparison to the teachers and staff we have encountered in the Union County Public Schools system. The teachers at the lower campus seemed like they had no training or knowledge pertaining to dealing with young children. We pulled our child out of this school, enrolled in our local public elementary school and we are so happy with our decision. We would never go back to UA after experiencing what it is like to attend a good public school. Great! They learn over there grade level. They need no improvement. If you move to Monroe, come here! What an unfortunate turn for the worst this school has taken. There has been a recent change in upper management, and it is obvious that this is causing serious issues. We will not be sending our child back to this now awful institution. The teachers aren't qualified, the staff isn't interested in improving, and I would be very surprised if this school still exist in 5years. We have just finished our third year at the Lower School at Union Academy. One of my children entered as a first grader after a disappointing kindergarten year in our zoned public elementary school . As a former teacher in both public and private schools, I can assure you that I have experienced only high quality instruction from dedicated and well-trained teachers at Union Academy. The expectations are high for both parents and students. Volunteer service is required of parents. Good character is emphasized along with academic excellence. I love the sense of community that I feel here at UA. I encourage you to visit the lower campus to see for yourself--it is a great place! We have been at this school for many years and I must say that while the lower campus is still true to the original charter, the middle and high schools have taken a serious nose dive. The administration all come from Monroe HS and thye dont have very high standards academically or in terms of character development. Money is spent on staff lounges, leadership trips while classes are now over crowded like the UC school system. Looking for other options for HS, which is sad as we have been hard core Cardinals for a long time. Wake up board and ask some questions! I have been a die-hard cardinal since kindergarten. I have fallen in love with this school and it is now my second home! The teachers and staff are my family and a great one they are. My academics are very important to lots of faculty here at UA and they hold very high standards for me. I am only a freshman this year but hearing what goes on at other local high schools, I can't imagine being anywhere else. People say that they hate our school when they first come in, but that is because they haven't experienced the family atmosphere for that long and it is a new and foreign concept to those coming from the UC public school system. I am excelling in all of my classes and my teachers are encouraging me to do better and be the best that I can be at this school. Although I am not a fan of the recent change of Administration or expansions, I am still in love with my school and wouldn't trade it for any other school. I would recommend this school for anyone who is new to the area because of its size and morals. I believe that all of the grade levels and campus' are great and I can tell you this first hand from experiencing all of them. This is our 2nd year at UA and the high school offers a rigorous curriculum for those students that choose to challenge themselves with AP courses. The staff and teachers go above and beyond to help their students learn and succeed. The students are a tight knit group that have a bond and loyalty to each other and to their school. We couldn't be happier with the opportunities and challenges our kids have had thus far at UA. This is our 2nd year and I couldn't be happier. The teachers are great and take the time to work with all kids not just those that excel. I like the small family environment that UA provides and I'm especially impressed with how they teach our kids to not only do well academically but they educate them on what it takes to be caring productive adult. This is something that the public schools don't have time for and I see the difference. I keep hearing about how unhappy some of the parents are with the recent changes and in the administration...all I can say is you haven't experienced a public school. Nothing is perfect but UA gets us a little closer. We are UA!!! Coming from the UCPS system, we are extremely happy with all aspects of UA - from rigorous academics and small class sized, to the family-friendly atmosphere. We are UA! The school has many opportunities for those that fit the mold. But for those that don't you should look elsewhere as the teachers are not into dealing with them. Biggest issue is with Integrity and High Character development. When these are part of who you are as a school you expect them to be valued in all aspects including sports. However if your parent works for the school or is connected in some way to the school you are automatically given a starting spot on whatever sports team you decide to join even if you have no business being there. When coaches from other schools identify integrity issues in your sports programs how hard do you think it is for the student athletes to do the same thing. With all that being said the educational opportunities that my children are receiving here are far better than the opportunities given to our other family members in UCPS. And I guess the old adage that School is for an education not sports is why we stay with UA. This was our first year at UA and we couldn't be happier! We were at two school previously (a public school for K and a charter for 1st) and we were NOT happy. UA has a close family feel, offers parents many opportunities to be on campus, and builds character in our children. We love it! The school used to be very good about 10 years ago. It's cheap budget and lack in ability to seriously handle real student concerns is sorely lacking. They sweep lots of problems under the rug to cover the title of School of Character. Our daughter have been attending this school for past three years and we love UA. The Admin at the school see you as dispensable the reason why its a "National School Of Character" is because the school admin never acknowledge non physical bullying. This school has gone down hill for the past 5 years. It is sad to see the lack of character at this school Unless you are in a really bad area, then I suggest that you stick with your local public school. In my opinion, your child will get a better education. All around good school i think where it messes up is its lack of caring about students and bias towards students who are kids of employees. The administration is another awful part of the school and events are constantly getting messed up because of it. This school needs a complete over haul of administration Had a high school transfer and an elementary student attend UA. The elementary program was great. Teachers were awesome and my child thrived. She is now thriving in the middle school which is under new leadership. My High schooler did well. It took a while for him to make good friends because many of the students at UA have grown up together so it was hard to fit in at first. The teachers were excellent and the guidance counselors were amazing. We have been pleased with all 3 levels of the school so far. Currently learning here and it is the best school. 100% recomend. Some other people will blame the school for what their children did wrong, not what the school did wrong. The staff is great and it just is a great school overall.

column1: Please rethink your child's school selection if you are headed in this direction. Although a small school for those children who do not do well in large surroundings, Leo does not administer the ACT for it's Junior class and does not offer extra help. Administration is not stern and lets the students walk over them. Fights, suspensions, good students, and bad students are everywhere so do not worry about that. A school is how your child perceives the experience, but academically Leo is not a great foundation to start your child for their future. It is not worth it for the money that you are spening!! Save your money for a 4 year university! My dad, Joe Prendergast, who was born in 1920, graduated from St. Leo's High School in the late 30's. He turned out to be a wonderful guy! Everyday he woke up he was thankful for the day! A very good worker and father of 12. He was proud and happy to have been a student there! Peace to All. Pat Prendergast Lytle my son is a freshman this year and loves it. He is 1 of 3 Hispanics there and gets along with all the young men there. I love it because its small compared to the public school he came from. The teachers and coaches care about my son, he gets tutoring when he needs it and the teachers keep us updated on his progress regularly. Overall I am pleased and look forward to the next couple years there. My son graduated from Leo in 2011 and continues to thrive well into his college years because of the great teachings from Leo H.S. The teachers are amazing. The males are great role models and are truly invested in the lives of these young men! My two sons attend Leo.The school has a computer lab with no computers. No access to computers to help with papers/assignments. Some of the staff & instructors are not giving 100% and last, my 17 wants to transfer out to a public school after attending 3yrs @ Leo for all of the above reasons.

column1: I love this school... I've been here since 6th grade and still haven't stopped loving it. Sure there are some teachers that are extremely hard when it comes to grading, and I as a band major am out from school a lot because of activities such as All-County and Jazz festivals. So for some teachers turning in makeup work is kinda hard. But the school is otherwise amazing! Getting an hour lunch is great for those who use it. Being in band is pretty tough because we're usually rehearsing for the first half of lunch... So the hour is GREAT! The school has a lot of fun activities like Color Wars (LOVE COLOR WARS!) and lunch time dancing (sometimes).. The enviroment is very homey and there are no cliques. Students here are very open and are who they are with no judgement attached. That's what I love most about this school! This school has really changed my life. Im actually excited to come everyday and everyone treats each other like equals because we all know we're different this school is great because it offers great oppurtunities for students and most students need those oppurtunities I absolutely loved going to this school. The teachers are/were understanding, versatile, and talented. This is a place of acceptance that fosters creativity. Since graduating, I moved to Boston and I am finishing up my Bachelor's Degree in History. The great thing is, I may have been a vocalist at Osceola County School for the Arts but the school did much more for me than train me in my field. I learned how to be well-rounded, explore different interests, and gained confidence. Although I am not planning to work completely in my field, I still have a passion for music and will continue to use the skills that I learned at this wonderful school. I definitely recommend it to any student with a love of the arts or even just an interest in them. Its just like any other school in osceola county.Nothing special about it.Does not provide enough activities for high school students. Ok lemme set y'all perspective applicants straight:If you're truly passionate about wanting to be at the school and love the arts, you'll thrive beautifully. Otherwise, steer clear if you're the opposite and if your parents are making you audition. OCSA has a fabulous relaxed educational environment. Being a 6-12 school eliminates the stress normally associated with moving to high school from middle school. Wonderful. Credit to these kids ultimately they are the reason OCSA is such a great place. We all love this school! Teachers have high expectations for the students, and the students have high standards for themselves, which is why OCSA is a 10 out of 10 school! Compare with other schools (I have been teaching in Osceola for years), I know my child is more than ready to be in college! Thank you OCSA!! I was very excited when my child was accepted to this school , the auditions and requirements to enter were strict and meticulous , which let our family to believe that it was a school in which they carefully choose the students academically and artistically . However, in our family’s experience the school needs to work on parent teacher communication , not even once during the school year I received information on how my child was performing . Also , the students have created accounts on social media in which the bully each other and make disrespectful comments about teachers and students . The band it’s amazing , the performances of students are beautiful, and the principal seems like a person who cares about the school . I am grateful for the teachers who worked hard and I have respect for all school staff who dedicate their life to help students. Just wish there was better communication from teachers to parents and that students had control on what they post on social media and wouldn’t be hurting other student’s feelings , which unfortunately is becoming a normal activity within our youth . MY SON IS VERY HAPPY IN THIS SCHOOL, BECAUSE THE TEACHERS ARE AMAZING.
