They have a unique way of teaching..from laptops to combining lessons between “2” different courses (ex: The Social Studies and English teachers coordinate their lesson plan) to the teacher sending parents “text messages” about upcoming tests. column3: This High School is poor. It is not diverse in its ethnicity or its approach towards it. The administration is rude and very unprofessional. The teachers are great, just don t let your child get into any kind of problem there big or small because your child will carry that label with them for the whole duration of their high school years. This school is bias and in my opinion the NY State Board of Education should take a better look at it. The school is over populated, they suspend students left and right. Their way of taking care of the population. Students have to be academically postive as well. That s not the case here with BSHS, Trust ME! If your child falls behind they will help at first, after that they want to swing the door open and try persuading ideas about GED and we will help you get into college courses, right in front of your child. Your child that already feels that they cant succeed now feels they wont! They don t want their scores to be low NO CHILD LEFT BEHIND ACT hitting two birds with one stone (over populated, test scores)! I am not the only parent that feel this way! My other children will not attend Ballston Spa HS. I'm not going to argue that this school doesn't have good (even excellent) programs and opportunities, because it does. I am however going to argue about the limited staff support for children that need it and I do have a serious issue with the amount of bullying that goes on. It is a VERY difficult school to acclimate a child into from a different district having little or NO assitance in doing so and credits do not transfer as they should. In addition, I think the limited parental support is obvious because it shows with the behavioral issues with many of the students. Blame the school? On a certain level yes I do. The dress code not being inforced simply digusts me every day that I drop my children off. If you don't want your children exposed to a strip club, then enroll them elsewhere because it is absolutley rediculous! We moved to this district based on specific criteria, test scores, awards, ect... I now know that there are hidden issues within every school, even the perfect ones. I am glad we opted NOT to purchase a home here and we will be looking into other districts (or private schools) very soon as a result. It is a shame that you can't go by everything you read. No school in a several county area offers more choice. The curricular options at BSHS are unparalleled: the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (BSpa is the only school in the suburban council with it), TEC-Smart (through which students come close to earning an associate's degree by the age of 18), both a biomedical strand and a technology strand through Project Lead the Way, more electives than most schools twice its size, ... Our children benefit greatly from the supportive teachers, counselors, and administrators. We chose this district and never have regretted the decision. -would move here again! This school is not perfect, no high school in America is. Well, not yet anyway. Sure, it does have great acedemic and technolgy programs that if offers, and it does also have the new International Bacchelorate which is the only one in the suburban council! But like i said, it's not perfect. It may not have the best sports teams, which could be improved, but what I'm more focused on is the attitude the students, like me also, have about this school. A lot of them are throwing away their education because of the management of this school. It is very overpopulated and that probelm needs to be fixed. It just needs "polishing up" they need to fix the dress code a little bit, seriously, it's like a strip club...especially the older kids. They also need to have a bit more of an eye on the "punks" as I call them, not only will this reduce potential future criminal rates, but it will give them a better view of the school. They also need a "Bully Box." Kids write down who's bully them and how on a paper and put it into a box in a secluded place like guidance or something. I may only be a freshman, but like I said, it's not bad, just has room for improvement. Notice...3 stars. I am..."The Z" BSHS is a great school. We have more programs than most area schools. We are the only IB World school in the Suburban Council. Most of the teachers here are really good. The administration and guidance department are excellent. I am proud to be a Scottie. I have been in this district for several years now. The school runs every Common Core pilot program that NYSED throws at it. Politicians & NYSED Commissioner John King walks the halls here too. The High school is running the pilot program for the Common Core English/Math in the Early College / H.S. Smart Tec program in the 11th/12th grades and intends to start the program in 9th grade in 2015. They have a robust technology dept by the means of RttT funding that this school district always seems to "win" from NYSED and the Governor. The High School environment is very rough with a wide range of kids that are bullied. The Demographics of this district is the high rate of kids that live in the poverty to others that live in relative wealth. Many of the kids that come from good families are "sucked in" by many bad influences that permeate the middle and high school. I will say that the high school principal is not warm and is not liked by parents, kids and the H.S. Staff. The teachers and counselors are great, but the leadership lacks and does not listen to the concerns of parents. Good academic programs, but hard to stay on a good path with tvery poor guidance. Most of the guidece counselors dont know how to do their job. Some years classes alternate and get dropped every other year. The counselors dont tell the students, they have to find out by themselves. The counselors are only put together students schedules, and some how some students schedules get messed up every year and they are forced to take classes they dont want. The administration is also very poor within this school. Their way of handling issues is with suspension. I dont have a problem with that, but if kids are getting suspended for playing games on computers, thats ridiculous. Colleges see the suspension and it looks bad, sometimes they dont look for the reason. They see it, and move on to their next applicant. They need to find other forms of discipline for small problems. Absolutely a horrible district, quick to judge and label, communication within as well external has to be the worst I have ever seen . If your child has an issue, you can be sure the district will label him/ or her for their entire high school career This district has major issues with bullying, labeling, as well as internal communication and support for your child. I had a guidance meeting concerning my childs behavior and grades, he was seeing a behavioral specialist at the school weekly, not one of his teachers knew that! LOL A complete joke, sadly that is what our tax dollars are paying for. I have had numerous phone calls and emails into the district with no return calls or email replies.... Not ideal.... My child also complained numerous times about a bullying incident that turned very serious. The district never contacted me. My child then reacted to this a month later and was disciplined for his reactions. There seam to be no communication between services teachers and leadership of the school. The school is to focused on trying to teach everyone to be kind in all grades the proper education. And there is to much school forced involvement with parents homes instead of proper work and teaching ethics in the classroom and at the school.

column1: This schools system is the worst school system I have been involved with. The administration is not held accountable by any one. They educate perhaps 10% of the students, with the right last name. Three generations is an outsider here. When questioned about a particular program the principals answer to me was the statics were askew. The program was at least three years old and suppose to help struggling students. As many parents we used school of choice after realizing there was minimal education available to bulk of the student poplualtion, now we are moving. The good reviews are from the 10% I assure you. I am a parent of two students at Martin Public Schools. Both have attended since kindergarten, and we considered several other neighboring districts as schools of choice options before enrolling our oldest child in Martin. Martin is a small Class D. There are some classes (foreign languages, choir, AP classes) that are not available. Some sports are not competitive. However, over all, as a parent with very high standards, I am so glad our children attend Martin. The small community environment is supportive of students no matter what gifts and challenges they bring. Students who might ordinarily be put in special education are regularly mainstreamed, and often the counselor or social worker will have students partnered with them to make sure they are welcomed and accepted. Any student can be in band and sports at a varsity level if they wish, so the ultra-competitive "making the team" dynamic does not exist. Because there are not as many classes, the district has aggressively pursued early college through AAESA, community and 4 year colleges. Students can earn up to 2 years credit virtually for free while still in high school, which is a huge leg up for college.

column3: Have you been to LHS lately? The new principal has done a great job in maintaining a safe and open learning environment. This is not the old LHS. My two daughters graduated from LHS and graduated from UT AUSTIN and U OF H. They were prepared very well for college. LHS has great teachers, facilities, and course selections. I would send my kids there again with no reservations. Please visit and talk to he new principal and see for yourself. Also, please note that most of the negative comments were prior to 2008. I graduated from LHS and I would never recommend it to anyone. My freshman class had 900 students. We graduated around 400. The students who didn't graduate, never were intending too, and good luck to the teachers trying to get a parent on the phone. The AP classes were great, the regular classes....how in the world could someone not pass them. RUN!! Longview High is the probably the best school all around and this includes the entire state of Texas. This school is ALWAYS competing in the top STATE and NATIONAL academic competitions and that speaks volumes about our staff in training these young students. I see parents on here that have either moved from L.I.S.D. when the atmosphere was rocky back in the early 90's and received the reputation that we deserved at THAT time, of course. GREAT SCHOOL! I am a parent who has had two children graduate from LHS. Both the AP and IB programs are excellent. Our daughter did the AP program and is a recent graduate of Baylor Law School. Other LHS friends are in Dental school and in Med school. They are all finding academic success. Our son just finished LHS through the IB program. What an impressive program! Where else can you take Latin and Baseball? I strongly recommend that you consider Longview. You won't be sorry! Super school! Only school in East Texas I am aware of to have won a National Championship in Robotics at the National Technical Students Associations Championships. LHS is World Class at everything. Education, Sports, Band, Orchestra, and diversity. Give your child a complete education and start in life. The best high school east of I-45. Longview High School has set transfer records into the school for 4 straight years. Why? Robotics (Tech Bowl) national champs 3 consecutive years; 64 consecutive 'superior' ratings for marching band; Established International Baccalaureate program; More dual credit offerings than any other district in the area; Multi-million dollar CTE expansion, including a culinary arts facility used by a local college; outstanding athletics program (just Google Longview Lobos); and the highest paid teachers in all of east Texas. Longview High School is a wonderful place to learn. There are programs for all types of learners, from those who plan to attend major colleges to those who wish to go directly into the workforce with a well-paying job. Longview ISD has the best educational offerings in East Texas. I choose to send my three children to the district, and there are many choices in the area. I recommend the school district to anyone moving to the area or looking for a challenging curriculum. My School is Longview High School which is known for its stellar IB program, STEM school within a school, CATE Program, and excellent teachers. Excellent college in high school offerings, community spirit, great sports programs.

column1: Great school, but....Why are there so few African American students? This school has the LOWEST percentage (1.7%) of African American students in NEISD. No other high school has numbers anywhere near this low. This is particularly problematic given that ISA is a top magnet school that draws from the entire district (and beyond). Diversity and excellence go hand and hand (something I think ISA & NEISD leadership would agree on) so I'm hoping that in the future there will be more serious efforts to recruit and retain African American students at ISA. In my opinion this will result in a student body that is even more prepared to deal with the realities of our city, our state, our country and (perhaps most importantly) the broader WORLD we live in. HorribleTerribleAtrociousDon’t come here I regret it Hate it here Get way too much homework. Administrators don't do anything to solve a problem they just let the problem go. This school erks me very much oof This is a unique school that really opens student's eyes to being responsible citizens and thoughtful humans. Academics are strong, and learning style is so original and unique! 7/10. It claims a little more than it actually puts into practice. These are upper middle class kids who were intelligent to begin with and are given a mediocre amount of tools to go to college with. Although it is drastically better in its staff and opportunities than other schools in the city, there are many ways ISA could improve. ISA encourages students to be critical thinkers and not just regurgitate memorized facts. Another reviewer here mentioned that these are all upper middle class kids… I’ve had three kids in this school and have not found this to be the case. There is a diverse student body and if your kid is open-minded, he or she will learn a lot about different segments of the larger population in San Antonio through this microcosm. As a preparation for college, ISA is outstanding. Development of writing skills required for college success is incredible. My child attended private school before being accepted into ISA. I have to say that the teachers and staff are so dedicated to our children. I'm a junior at ISA. The school has the atmosphere of a private school, despite being public. If there is one thing you absolutely have to know about this place, it's that the students are absolutely obsessed with sex—to a worrisome degree. I thought I was losing it when I went here at first because people would randomly tell me about hookups, etc. I do not recommend this place at all honestly. Schooling in San Antonio is subpar compared to Austin, and I assume it's like this for the rest of Texas, but you are better off just going to your zoned school than driving out to have your ears feel violated incessantly. I have 2 students that graduated from ISA. Both left very well rounded and prepared for college life and life outside the classroom. I couldn't have asked for a better experience. The travel experiences are amazing and the school strives to be inclusive in many ways.

column1: Terrible if you have a girl. A lot of cliques, and pressure to wear certain clothes. I really doubt those test scores, bc everyone in my daughter's sophomore class was under 40%. They are lying because they have that 80 million dollar school that's being built and they need as many students to attend so they get money from the government. My daughter will be transferring to Hardin Valley next year. Don't send your child based on these reviews that are coming from teachers and stafff!! They are bogus and there's a lot of bullying going on. So disappointed. This school used to be good! teachers are great I love coach Dunn and his way of thinking and explaining things. But I e been a student of Alcoa all my life and left my junior year to be homeschooled because of one teacher, Mrs. gorto she "teaches" marketing (my freshman year) and sports entertainment my sophomore year and I took hospitality my junior year so I could graduate with all marketing focus. Well.. I honestly don't know why I continued to take her classes she literally did nothing in that class she would sometimes show us a video and tell us to do a PowerPoint every single assignment was a power point. That gets boring after three years ! And she literally did not teach us a thing. We had a new "progect" everyday, and it was looking up on the internet what does this company do and why. What is that teaching us ..? I wasn't mad that we had to do work I was mad everyday that she let me and other students get picked on. When we had to present our PowerPoint for the class students had their phones out recording, posted online making fun of us with harassing comments. I told her about it and never did anything. This happened repeatedly and never did a single thing about it. And another thing that really bugged me, I had a doctors excuse for when I was out, and this teacher knew about my home situations cause I used to talk to her my first two years of high school about my health issues, I would miss assignments here and there but for the most part I did all my assignments, and she ever had this thing online where she would post the assignments so you could see what you missed and work on it on line (oh and we never did anything on paper all on computer, which half the class was on Facebook and YouTube ) well twords the end of the semester I was in the hospital, and I missed more than usual assignments and I was about to be homeschooled because it was too much to handle, I talk to her in private asking if I could make them up she said no! column3: Bowie High School is a very good school and the teachers try to reach everyone the best way they can.But, the classes are very overcrowded,and i feel the teachers can do better. Sometimes the teachers don't really like to teach and i am not very fond of that. The school is just very big and some of the students that attend the school do not live in the area. This is a very nice school but for me i don't think i would want send my kids here. This school is horrible. I've enrolled into the school 2 years ago. i am now a junior. The students there do not care what so ever. the teachers do not know how to control them. In my freshman year i was originally planning on going to Eleanor Roosevelt but didn't make the science and tech program. I decided not to go the regular school and instead went to bowie high school, and tried to take the test there. the guidance teacher soon told me the school wasn't in the program. Take my mistake as an advice I am a mom of a 2011 Graduate and have a freshman there now. Bowie High prepared by daughter to be very competitive for college and was accepted to her first choice school George Mason. The kids that were in the Honor Classes and involved in extra activities help make the school it's very best. In sports three (3) girls from the basketball team went on to Ivey League schools, and other athletics went on to D1 schools. Parents have to be involved with their kids and help the teachers help their kids. I can truly say Mrs. Spence set a great example and was Principle of the Year for Maryland. If we help with the problems and not be a part of them then we will have great schools across America. Mr. Trustee one of the gudiance counselors that was a very inportant part of the process from freshman - senior year, making sure the kids was on track for success. I love this school. But there is one problem it is in PG county. PG does not like Bowie because the students are not stupid like in the rest of the county. On the county website they made a 2 page article on on how they will make district heights elementary (the worst school in the county) better by painting it and buying toys rather than posting that whitehall elementary became a blue ribbon( only school in the county). I wish bowie could seperate from PG and merge with Anne Arundel This is seriously the most unprofessional school I have ever dealt with. The administrative staff that is there is extremely rude and honestly I will never send anyone to this school again. I'm a student and this school is awful. These teachers do not know how to teach, all my classes is basically like free time. There is nothing great about this school. Do not recommend . I am definatley not prepared for college next year. I was a former 2011 graduate, this school is beyond terrible, Even though I'm in college, I felt like I learned nothing. I feel like the teachers do not have discipline so of course the students Will not have any. I honestly feel like the majority of the teachers there are only there for the paychecks. Not the importance of teaching, not importance I students learning everyday. I felt like they didn't try hard enough to prepare students for the next level education. While in 11th grade, one of my worst years there, I discovered not only did the school care about teaching, they don't care about getting permanent teachers. For example, my English 11 never had a permanent teacher. The first week of school our teacher was a HSA coordinator. After a couple months she left, then we had a substitute for a couple months. Then about the February we finally received a certified teacher. In my 10th grade year, Spanish was the same runaround with the teachers. First there was a real teacher but our class was so bad that we ran her out of town, our second teacher was a substitute, but he left because he wasn't permanent, 3rd teacher was another sub. Don't go to this awful school! From the first day of registration, my experience with this school has been poor. The students are out of control. They don't listen to the teachers. The staff is unprofessional. Everything that the school secretary, Mrs. Lee told us was false. As far as their "No Bullying policy", that's a joke. There are fights there almost daily according to my child. I would definitely consider another school if you're able. I wish I had looked at the reviews before I enrolled my child, which took almost 2 weeks because they would not accept my proofs of residency. I've never had such a traumatic experience with a school. It's an awful school. This is my opinion, and I am very much into my child's education. I am sure some others may not agree, but this is my honest opinion from what I've experienced at Bowie High School. Also if you saw other reviews on this school, you would definitely see that there is definitely a cause for concern at this High School. This school is not up to par academically. I have met with counselors and administrators about disruptive behavior during my child's class. In September 2013 I repeatedly made them aware of my concerns because I am a parent who truly cares about my child's education. As of April 2014 nothing has improved. The teachers do not give students feedback. They fail to give tests or homework back to the students in order to allow them an opportunity to improve and enhance their performance. Teachers spend more of their time out of the classroom instead of teaching the class and insuring those students that want to learn actually can. Seriously the teachers need to stop getting paid to do nothing and get some teachers who really care about educating our children. its alright unorganized at times and underfunded but its still alright, could do better with the math teachers and their inability to speak fluent english; A lot of the other reviews are bad and bashing the teachers but its not completely their fault, We still have the highest test scores in the county so to call us stupid is asinine -current bowie high student class of 2015 The Honors and AP classes are great and most of those students work hard. I have heard that it is different in many of the regular classes. excellent teachers, cooperative administration, great resources for parents to participate and contributing to the school. If you are nervous about sending you r child to Bowie here's everything you need to know. Urge your child to try for the SUMMIT program, this is program gives your child higher classes from the very first day of 9th grade. Also there are at the max 65 kids in the program for your grade. These are the kids that your child will be around for the next 4 years. To get into the program you have to have at-least a 3.0 all throughout their 7th grade year and the 1st quarter of their 8th year, with no behavior problems. If they don't make SUMMIT then try to get them into honors classes.But make sure that they are involved in extracurricular activities, they definitely help seperate the people that you should steer away from and the people you should start getting close to and be around with. This will keep your child out of trouble AND have good high school years . ~CLASS OF 2015 WE OUT!!!!!!!!!! Summit Scholars program is amazing and very recommended. Overall a solid school with a lot to offer to all demographics. Good teachers and a great new principle moving the school forward. In all honestly i hate Bowie, little is done toward education( no homework or reviews) half of the students can barely pass in my class. The admins suspend children for no reason when there are bigger problems in the school . From jumping kids, lighting fires in the bathroom, and many teachers only teach from the book which many kids can not follow. Bowie is more concerned with looking good then helping students understanding the work. Please do not send your kids here unless you want them to sit around for 8 hours and learn nothing. Another thing teachers at Bowie do a terrible job at teaching so after school there is tutoring for upwards of $40 dollars a hour for learning that should be taught in class and free. My child has homework everyday. The new Principal is great. They are moving in the right direction. May God bless the students and staff! My experience as a student at Bowie High has been awful. The building is disgusting, full of roaches and rats, and crumbling in some places. There are never enough resources like soap, paper, tissues, etc. Security does little to nothing to control rowdy students and fights are a constant. The cafeteria is disgusting and not kids eat out of the vending machines. Administration spends all the funds on sports- like a brand new football field- and ignores academics entirely, despite the fact that the football team hasn’t won a homecoming game in over a decade. There are a few amazing teachers but most others have either given up or contribute to the chaos actively. The school is HUGELY overcrowded, despite there being an entire separate building for the freshmen, and there is never enough to go around. Attempts at school spirit are openly mocked and every student counts down until graduation, when they can get the hell out of here. Bowie High School is not the worst school in the area, that’s true. Doesn’t change the fact that it’s an overcrowded, underfunded mess. There are no resources, the heat doesn’t work, most teachers are downright awful and the students are out of control. (Remember, this review is from the perscpeitve of a Summit student, Bowie’s program for those who are generally considered their best students coming in)Overall my experience at Bowie so far (I’m going to be a senior in September) hasn’t been stellar. Setting aside personal stuff, it’s just not that great of a school. The Teachers in generally are pretty meh. There are some really good one (like the Summit English 10 teacher), but most of them are just ok. The bad teachers are REALLY bad. Even some of the AP teachers are pretty bad (AP World and AP Art History). From my experience, the French teacher, Algebra II teacher, and chemistry teachers are all quite bad. (If you’re thinking about going here, PLEASE get as many language credits as possible in Middle school). The Technology department is a complete joke, there whole weeks in Tech Design class where we did precisely nothing at all. The building isn’t great, and the bathrooms often lack basics like soap and paper towels. However, in my opinion the WORST part of Bowie is the students. Most of them are obnoxious jerks who don’t take the opportunity they were given seriously at all. Even the so called “smart” kid use their phones in class and regularly fail to do basic instructions. I’ve had so many classes with decent teachers made terrible by an awful class. They just do not care, and it unfortunately holds back the kids who really do. And the teachers usually just let it slide. They show up late to class with a chick fil a bag in hand and face no consequences. Or turn in assignments three months late and it’s still accepted. They can’t even get quiet at a freakin assembly for god sakes. Yet they still complain and whine about how they can’t to this and this teacher sucks (even though they don’t even try to listen during their class) and blah blah blah. Hey, maybe we don’t have open lunch because you guys clearly wouldn’t be able to handle it. The dumbest incident I’ve ever seen in school was when some geniuses decided to bring FIREWORKS and SMOKE BOMBS to our school and had the entire school sitting outside for over a hour, wasting time. Not to mention the fights. They honestly take what is an average, meh school and make it worse.So yeah, overall not a great school. (Also, the Summit program is essentially meaningless after 9th grade, just adds more graduation requirements It wasn't great when my daughter attended back 2012 and now have a middle child getting ready to enter this fall, totally considering moving out the county just because of the school system. The community is great, it's the kids at the school, surprised that it is even scoring a 5 out of 10. I can’t give more than 2 stars because my child’s academic advisor was absolutely awful. No words can express my level of disappoint in her apathy, unprofessionalism and rudeness. My child missed so many opportunities, especially scholarships, because this advisor refused to do her job. The school has not done anything about this person the last I checked. Thank goodness my child graduated and can move on with her life.

column1: still a small enough school, great teachers and administrators! very safe environment, new and clean. This is a great school! column3: WRHS has excellent teachers and meets the needs of most average students, especially sporty ones. I rated it low because of the administration. They do not treat parents as partners. The parents that care the most speak up the most ( I do not myself have the time, but I feel grateful for their time and energy) and they DO represent those that are too busy or trusting. In addition, the administration is way too defensive, and suffers from a lack of serving leaders. The comment posted on November 28th sounds like it came from an administrator: A WRSD administator is resistant to his constituents, paranoid, entrenched and self-congratulatory. The administration spends much energy and money on non-student/curriculum centered priorities (buildings, security systems, retro-fitting heating systems in old buildings, hiring more administrators rather than teaching staff, etc) With as much money as this district has, we should actually be AMAZING. Actually, I know the person who wrote the November 28 comment and she is not an administrator. She is a parent who has lived in the valley for over 20 years and knows the school and the community well. I would have to agree that the teachers are very good and most certainly have their priorities straight -- caring about their students. I am not going to argue about the administration as that, all to often, is really about politics, not education. I do have to agree, however, that the nosiest (and wealthiest) of the public seem to get their way and their way is to create a system which caters to the top 20% of the students, supporting the bottom 20% (special needs) and giving minimal consideration to the great majority (60%) of the students. As to the January 30 comment regarding the "sporty students": I have never been in a school district where being "sporty" meant LESS. I am a parent and do not presently have a student in the high school, but I do have two former students who received a very good education, have done very well in the post-high school education and careers and always speak highly of the school and several of their teachers. I rated this school unsatisfactory because it should be doing so much better given its level of per pupil funding (huge--around $25,000). Instead of being one of the best in the country, it is barely mediocre. Parents considering this school should look at graduation rates (mediocre), the abysmally small percentage of students that take the SAT, SAT scores that are lower than Idaho state average, etc. Then ask around. In other words, do your homework, don't just read the district public relations junk. Extremely poor district leadership (friends promote friends) is to blame. Good teachers struggle and are demoralized. Hopefully the school board (which is in transition) will ask teachers for their input. With great leadership, this district could be great. WRHS retains overpaid, mediocre teachers and staff, and a new principal with little experience making over 100k. Taxes provide 26k per pupil, but the result is low SAT scores. Support includes a top heavy district office who is being sued, with no accountability or ethics. This district is interested in buildings and grounds, not student achievement. A new school board that changes leadership will ultimately turn this negative climate, to one that is committed to education. Ego, politics and misrepresentation continue to plague this school and district. A rose with many prickles. More than a disappointment, an educational travesty. Wood river heigh is full of many tiles of students, but teacher is another thing I have never had a teacher in my years at wood river that actualy cared about the students.

column1: I don't know who that other teacher that gave tje school a bad review, but they must have had a chip embedded in their shoulder, not just on it. I have recently accepted a teaching position at ATCO high, and I can tell you it is the best school I have ever had the pleasure of teaching. The staff is supportive, they are equipping their classrooms for the 21st century, and the kids are the most well-behaved students I have ever encountered EVER. I have taught in other schools and felt like I was in cell block D. Atkinson County HIgh and MIddle is a great school and you would be hard pressed to find a better teaching environment and staff. I was formerly employed at Atkinson County High School as a teacher. The students are predominantly those whose parents could not afford or did not choose to send them to private school. They are generally well-behaved, but I do not believe that they are better or worse than children in most small community schools. The school administrators insist on paddling the students who misbehave. There are many other tales to tell, but I think that is enough to get the point across. Also, if you are an employee and can play politics and kiss the backsides of the right people and don't mind the fact that locals will always get preference over others, you will do well here. Do not be from the wrong family or place. Do not expect certain individuals would ever send their own children to this school. Do not expect people to do and say things that won't benefit them or theirs. Do not do these things and you will do well. The last and most important rule I can give you is never cross the wrong people or administrators. Look at how this school compares on the Georgia Public Policy Foundation website: ranked 304 out of 357 in the state, 100% poverty, 52% pass the EOCT, 72% graduate. You decide.

column1: HGP is the best place for my son. The teachers are there to develop those young men into Gentlemen of the World. HGP teachers and personal demonstrated that their care about him, today and in the future. He is a Freshman. Thanks! Having sent my children to public schools, boarding schools, and private day schools I can honestly say HGP has provided the best all around educational experiance. The all boys school is almost a throw back to earlier days with great academics, sports, and teachers that really care. What a great place! the right size. teachers who are knowledgeable, helpful, and caring. Lots of opportunities. Our son is a senior at HGP. His experience has been absolutely wonderful. The academic environment is unmatched. Not only would I say our son is well-prepared for college, but I would say that he essentially already is in college. The level at which these young men are taught and the expectations that are put on them by the school, their families, their peers and themselves result in students that are preforming at a college level while in high school. There are also countless opportunities outside of the classroom, be it in sports, interest clubs or service opportunities. The enviornment is very congenial and welcoming. I would whole-heartedly recommend HGP. What a great place! the President, Principal, the Deans and the teachers all know and care about the students. The teachers are scholars and they are available for the students. And Ghost has a great sports teams and they don't recruit! Holy Ghost Prep exceeded our expectations! The sense of comraderie among the boys and the teachers and staff is contagious. Our son felt right at home from the beginning and felt comfortable to join many activities. The single gender school is a plus, the boys are expected to grow as men, and the many alumni faculty is a true plus. The atmosphere is very welcoming and friendly. I absolutely love the experience my son is having as a student at HGP. The boys are treated like young professionals in a stron academic enivroment with the right balance of that with fun and support. Parents are always welcomed and many activities through the year makes sure that the family is included in your son's education. The academics are superior. Recommend whole heartedly that you send your son to Holy Ghost. It is no a doubt the best decision we for our son's education. Submitted by a parent Our son graduated in 2012. HGP made him work harder than I ever would have imagined (and in some cases I think even too hard) but in the end he was incredibly prepared for college. His academic achievement there earned him a full tuition scholarship for college. I have no doubt this would not have happened had he gone to the local public or parochial school. He still would have excelled but HGP forced him to be even better, If you child doesn't put in the work he won't get the benefit. Personally I wouldn't have fired that one teacher who made the news recently, but if you let that affect your decision then you're sacrificing an incredible education experience for your son to satisfy liberal peer pressure. I currently have 2 sons enrolled at Holy Ghost and could not be happier. The teachers and school environment provide support so that the boys are able to meet the challenges of college prep courses with the encouragement of their teachers. As of the spring of 2014, improvements continue in test scores, discipline issues, and overall school culture. Scott High School affords students the opportunity to take Dual Credit Courses at area colleges, a variety of language classes at the school, to participate in a variety of sports, drama programs, clubs, activities, and community service opportunities. Perhaps, also, because of the persistent prejudice against girls in math. I don't blame the school or anyone in particular. My daughter is finally in calculus and doing okay-it's been a long haul. All in all, I'd say WGHS is a good school - as good as they can be under all the circumstances. One of the biggest plusses is the small, but very active group of parents who are so involved in the extracurricular activities. With the terrible funding of public schools parents have to be involved. You especially have to stay connected to your kid - that is where the rubber meets the road. column3: Cato-Meridian is one of the top schools in the State. Great facilities, great teachers, and an outstanding environment to grow up in. I was extremely blessed to grow up in such a tight knit town. I now am very successful in my professional life and owe it all to being raised a Blue Devil!!! Excellent school, the teachers are avaiablefor one on one time with a student. the only concern that i have was the principal she tends not to keep a promise nor run the school in an orderly fashion. She rarley addresses a problem and if she does it never follows through to the student I find it interesting when I read a parent stating CM did not prepare their child for college. I graduated from CMCS over two decades ago, and even then, the district offered extensive options for learning, including AP, Independent, Equivalency, and Regents. I did not flourish in a traditional classroom, so I was placed in independent study. I successfully graduated from high school with a regents diploma and went on to obtain 6 college degrees. CMCS is a small district, but has competitive educational opportunities. If students don't take advantage of those opportunities, the school district should not be held responsible.

column1: I attended this school from the sixth grade through graduation, and I am astounded that it received such a great rating. The course options were the most basic available; if your child needs special education or gifted education, seek out a school elsewhere, as FHS cannot adequately accommodate those needs. The teachers/staff may be very nice and friendly, but the school is in such a poor location that it simply cannot offer students a wide variety of experiences (cultural, academic, field trips, etc.) or course offerings. Some parents have noted that they liked the small scope of the school, which is great if that's what you're looking for. I feel that students are rather limited in that type of setting, however; I certainly was, and in retrospect, having traveled extensively and continued my education through graduate school years later, I can fully appreciate how narrow a perspective the school affords its students. I've attended Fayetteville since Kindergarten, and I would hope my kids could go to a school like this one day. The teachers are nice, and they spend their time to make sure you can understand what you're learning, and the athletic program is great. I feel like I'm part of a big family that looks out for one another. If you're considering Fayetteville, you are on the right path. I'm a proud student of this great school. It is a good school. But there are some ups and downs to the school that needs to be fixed

column3: Not a good school, The teachers are very lazy, The students are just as lazy, This school makes you very depressed. I've been bullied for the past 3 years of my life here at FHS. The kids are bad influences and the principle does not do anything about it. We have fights almost everyday and the hallways are too crowded. They only give you 5 minutes to go to your locker, bathrooms, and get to the other side of the building. The teachers are nice and they are good to talk to, but the students are HORRIBLE! Parents Beware! If your looking for a High School for your child to learn and become a good citizen and be ready for College or the Work Force, Franklin High School isnt the place to send them. Counselors and some Teachers that dont care. They just go thru the motions as if they care, but they dont. Somebody should let them know Teaching is a Career, not a Union Job. Franklin has a spirited student council and a large number of students dedicated to the advancement of their class and their school with a disproportionately high number of Advanded Placement students. I have to rate this school as "Excellent"! My first child graduated in 2009, my son-in-law in 2007, and my youngest is now a Junior there. I beleive the school has a strong acedemic prgram and the counselors do a pretty good job in giviing direction, not always but 85% of the time. Teh TEachers are great. there were only a couple that my kids have had that I would say did not do their job. You know the Teachers are making a mark on your children when they come home and talk about them everyday. tehy hace the IB program which is only one of a couple of high schools in Michigan to have this program. Also from what I have heard from my kids, their friends, Teachers, and other paretns from Franklin and other Livonia schools, Franklin has a better focus on enforcing drug policies. I would recommend this high school over the other two in Livnoia any day!. I graduated from Franklin in 2010 and am now graduating from the University of Michigan (Ann Arbor) this May with a 3.8, a double major with high honors, and an admirable full time job lined up. Needless to say, I'm doing well. The thing about Franklin is that it is full of academically average and morally misguided kids. The advanced students that rise to the top tend to be tracked together in 4-5 subjects and are largely segregated from the non-advanced population outside of athletics and assorted elective courses (I met some colorful individuals in pleasure reading my senior year...). If you are motivated and intelligent, there is an opportunity for you to meet like minded students and brilliant teachers that will get you where you want to be for the most part. The real challenge is setting the bar high enough for yourself. I came to Michigan way behind my private-school-educated out of state cohorts. Specifically, my analytic reasoning and research design capacities were dismal compared to peers that attended rigorous prep programs. The average kid will be fine at FHS, and the will surely have a shot at state-level college admission. Exceptional kids are on their own. Franklin High School in Livonia Michigan. I support the school and their goals. My child is a freshman so I am still learning about the school. Franklin High School, Livonia, MI I never thought there could be so many sub-standard teachers. I am not surprised that the test results came in so much lower than the rest of the district after my freshman was loaded with 4 out of 6 useless teachers. Lazy, expect the students to teach themselves under the "preparing them for college" mantra. Teach the subject, give them a good foundation, and college will take care of itself. Do nothing, expect the kids to teach themselves, and smile and act nice, you get 66.67% of my child's teachers this year. Sad. Her counselor is no better. Took 6 schedules to get her into classes, and it's still wrong 2 months later. I am surprised Livonia has not gotten rid of the majority of the staff here. A;so laughable is that you have to pay as a parent to help out and participate. Who thinks of this stuff? Everything about Franklin High school has been wonderful for my son. We moved here his freshman year and he is doing great. The staff at Franklin is so amazing. Thank you for all you do Franklin and GO PATRIOTS!! I'm a graduate of Franklin. The time I spent at that school was a waste of 4 years of my life. I had an aweful experience there due to the horrible staff, with the exception of a few teachers. Many of the students will end up dropping out of this school. I blame the high amount of drop outs on the staff. The teachers are very narsistic. Many teachers picked favorites, the "good kids" that came from succecful narsictic families. The staff also picked out their targets, the "bad kids" more than likely kids of a single mother. The staff there also loves to gossip about their students there, to other staff members and students in class. Once you are viewed as a bad kid by one staff member, you were soon recognized as a bad kid by the whole faculty. When the faculty finds a target, they do everything in their power to get that student out of there school. The staff focuses on their good kids that will blend into society and grow up to be narsictic people just like themselves. The students of this school will not go far in their life after highschool. The students the school takes pride in probably will not make any significant difference in the world. Don't go to school here. Principal is biased in his deeling with parents and students with no understanding of community relations. Math teachers used to try to help and get along struggling students but my youngest says there is not enough help in class. As a parent, I have been very pleased with the education my son is receiving at FHS. The teachers and staff have been very helpful in his preparation for college. There is a great spirit among the teachers and coaches -- lots of Patriot Pride. We have 3 more children headed to Franklin and look forward to many more years of great education! I have found the staff and coaches very helpful and supportive. Franklin is a great school. I'm very impressed with this school so far. The facilities are very nice, lots of extra programs are offered. Teachers and administration have been very courteous and accommodating of our needs.

column1: Making it into National Honor Society is a subjective process, not an objective process. My daughter had great grades and participated in many organizations. She represented Padua on the state level. She wrote the winning "There Ought to be a Law Essay Contest", the year she graduated. She was a member of the All Ohio State Fair Band. We watched a lot of students who did less make it into NHS. Obviously, the teachers ignored my daughter's contributions. One teacher falsely accused my daughter of missing so much time in front of the whole class.. In fact, my daughter had perfect attendance and any time she was not there, was cleared before hand by the office. The teachers at Cleveland State got it right when they inducted my daughter into Golden Key, a national college honor society. The teachers at Padua who did not vote my daughter into NHS ripped her heart right out of her. They were not in our kitchen when our cheerful daughter cried her head off. If you want your hard working child to be appreciated, pick another school. My daughter is now a teacher. Former parent. As a recent medical school graduate, I can say that Padua is an exceptional high school that motivates, challenges, and inspires hard work, dedication, and ethical practice. Padua had tough classes and high expectations, but in the end- we are all better off for it. The faculty and staff are very supoortive and helpful and it is evident that the school values its students. Various programs, scholarships, and services are found at Padua that are unparalleled when compared to other schools. I took all of this for granted when I was a student there, but as a "grown up" that has seen and experienced what the normal is at other places, I just love and appreciate Padua that much more. Also, how many schools that you know of offer a med-track program for future health care providers? This program is fantastic and offers high school kids a chance to shadow, work, and volunteer in settings that interest them with mentors that they aspire to be. Parochial schools are historically and continue to be a cut above the publics. My son is currently attending PFHS and is thriving. Solid sports programs complement the solid academics offered here. My best choice for my son was enrolling him into Padua Franciscan High School and it made him a successful human being. They claim they send most graduates to prestigious 4 year institutions when most go to Tri-c or Cleveland State. Most of the school behaves like they are in some sort of cult where everything is just perfect and wonderful and all the students thrive, get along and are all 100% academically prepared for college. They claim no bullying occurs and they spend countless hours drawing new victims in. Its like any other high school (public or private) where teenagers will be teenagers. Bullying does occur, some students do better than others, and signaling out and cliches are present. Its an average school period. You will get a decent education and can thrive in college, but don't be fouled by the facade, Holy Name, Walsh and Trinity are just as good. They do a great job with my children. I've seen them succeed far past my expectation thanks to the instruction at Padua. Everyday our kids love going to school thanks to Padua. They keep the faith alive and makes sure everyone feels welcome. Excellent school as High School is a time that is most critical of all for a persons future outlook and path. Two children matriculated with different skills to excellent universities and graduated without a hiccough. Besides anything religious, this school offers no different education than a public school, such as Berea-Midpark. They also allow no student pick in schedules, and make them all up without giving any consideration to the students' ambition. Not worth the pay.

column3: After hearing rumors, looking at test scores, etc. I was worried about my son attending J'town. He just finished the 9th grade & during this time, here's my observation: 1) Polio appears to be a good principal, very hands on; 2) My son had advanced classes. I found most of his teachers highly competent & engaged. They seemed to be very sincere in wanting the best for him, which I appreciated. Staff is always pleasant & supportive; 3) The level of academic challenge was somewhat of a mixed bag depending on the teacher; 4) However, J'town could be a much better school but I think the prevalence of students that simply are not engaged and conducting in risky behavior is overwhelming...for the teachers, administrators and especially, the students. Staff make a good effort at trying to control what I would consider as the "riff-raff" but I'm not sure if they have the resources to really make a difference. Unfortunately, academic excellence is the exception, not the norm. I give kudos to the principal for trying to make it the other way around but unfortunately they aren't there yet. Horrible. It brought nothing but pain and my GPA is still recovering from horrible teaching and my brain is still recovering from the depression I developed.

column1: Kellogg High School is a small town school with a very big heart. the students, parents and community worked tirelessly this last summer to earn money so all of the sports could be continued in the next school year. We only have about 400 students, we may be small but we are awesome Great atmosphere for kids. College readiness is emphasized and staff truly care about the success of students.

column3: This school has to be the worse school a child can go to. They have their picks in kids in this school. If you don't have money you nothing in this school but another piece of paper. I hope when my grandson is older that they will do away with a lot of teachers in this school if not he will attend another school even if I have to pay. I have seen how they treated my daughters friends that didn't have much so I would make sure that the child had nice stuff to where she wouldn't get talked about. Now that my daughter has graduated she has much respect for the less fortunate children. She gives to kids that have much and her friend in school that didn't have much are now best friends and make sure that these kids aren't put down. John Battle High School is an amazing school. Actually the Washington Co VA School District is an amazing district. I have dealt with the county school system, the Bristol city VA schools and the Bristol TN city schools with being a mother of five children. All three systems have their good points, but John Battle High, Wallace Middle School and High Point Elementary School have impressed me throughout my children's education. John Battle's teachers and staff are happy to stay in contact with the parents and work through any issues with the child. I have been to them for many reasons whether totally educational, my child's problems with other student's (ie bullying, disagreements etc), problems at home, even help with things at home so my child had the resources at home to be more productive at school. They offer so many things other schools don't like their Community Scholarship program (which I could write so much about all the good aspects from allowing your child to participate in it) where the student does a small amount of community service each high school year, stays out of trouble and keeps decent grades and they have their start to their future right there for them. To me, that is an awesome opportunity that all schools should provide for the children, especially those that are not lucky enough to have the financial means to go straight off to a fancy college or those that work hard and want to learn but cannot pull off straight A's and get offered scholarships. They also have a wonderful selection of vocational studies. Amazing teachers that not only teach, but are willing to put extra time into the children and even money out of their own pockets to make sure the kids have what they need to be able to learn. I am an old-fashioned parent in many ways and a firm believer in teachers and schools being about the children and teaching them so they are prepared for the world ahead, and this school has been the closest I have had the pleasure of my children attending to the way things used to be when education and raising children right was a priority. I cannot give this school enough stars for the education and the guidance they have provided my children over the years. As we all know, no school will ever be perfect and there will always be one or two staff members to be the exception to the rule, but JBHS does put the effort into out kids. Absolute terrible, would never send a child of mine nor my worst enemy to this location. If you move in this area please consider, PLEASE CONSIDER sending your children elsewhere. I literally despise that entire building and every molecule it houses.

column1: This school is unbelievably horrible. The principle and vice principle are very unfair to those students who don't pay full tuition. Don't send your kids here the school is like jail. For OLSH to care about a student the parents need to have money to donate. Otherwise, you have a target. Don't send your children to this school!! Excellent school for all. OLSH is by far the best high school. It is very religiously inspired and controlled. If you want your child to have access to wonderful academic, athletic, and extra-curricular activities, then OLSH is the place go. The students, teachers, coaches, parents, and administrators truly encourage and support one another. I've been involved in education for many years and OLSH is one of the only schools that proves time and again that it is there to serve the needs of the students. I have seen my childrend grow into respectful, educated, and talented young adults -- OLSH has a whole lot to do with that. OLSH is the best school ever. Please do not read the reviews that say it is not. We have just put in a new OWL (OLSH writing and Learning center) and it is one of three in Pennsylvania in the high school level, as well as being the only one in a catholic school. The students also get to interact with the sisters, and each class has mass with them once a month. We also have all school masses on important feast days and holy days of obligation as well as once a month. The teachers are stellar. They care about their students. Students are also paired with a teacher as their advisor at the beginning of freshman year. This teacher will advise their group of students until the end of Junior year. OLSH is a family, we all care about each other. I ask you to consider OLSH as your high school! We came to Our Lady of the Sacred Heart from out of town and were greeted in a warm welcoming atmosphere. We immediately felt like a part of the OLSH family.Academics are college prep and there is a good selection of courses, including honors courses. College credit is available for certain courses. The school balances new trends in education without abandoning tried and true educational practices. They teach students about the Catholic faith and encourage them to live it and develop on a personal level, as well as through service to others.There are a wide range of extracurricular activities. This size of school allows more opportunity for students to become involved than would be possible at a larger school. Participation creates poised confident individuals. OLSH makes it easy to receive information and to communicate through creative means including; weekly newsletters, the OLSH Mobile App, emergency alerts, a quarterly Principal’s Forum, Meet the Teachers Night, and parent socials, to name a few.We highly recommend Our Lady of the Sacred Heart!-Michael and Rufie Harr If your student is academically there then they will do ok at this school (even though there is a lack of AP classes). But if your child needs a little bit more extra help they have little to offer. I'd take your money elsewhere. This school has a great curriculum and has prepared my children for college abs what to expect there. I would recommend OLSH to anyone. The teachers are very attentive to student needs, they are encouraging, challenging and fair. They work very hard to ensure that all students are prepared for college or any other career they may choose. The students are welcoming and friendly. The campus is beautiful and very safe. It is a wonderful school.

column3: The school is an amazing overall school. The teachers put forth so much effort into their students, All of them treating them like their own little kids. Which is awesome. Mr. Womack and Mr. Scott in the spotlight here, Hehe. The Football team, Marching band, And all others are very well skilled. They all put hard work, and dedication into what they do, Which should be celebrated in my opinion.Are you having doubts about westside? Don't. It's amazing as it is. The leaders and other employees at Westside are passionate about their jobs, they care about the success of their students and they respond efficiently and effectively to (my) parents concerns. My school expirence is terrible. If your schedule is wrong they take forever to fix it and they believe coming to school sick is more important than staying home and getting better. They also do not communicate certain information very well. Absolutely horrible and honestly they need to revamp all teachers to people who care for anyone, no matter there race and speak clear correct grammer If I had a option between 1-10 it will always be a 1 this school needs to change l. If I could give no stars, I would. This school is a joke and don't take threats and the safety of the students seriously. When there is a gunman on school grounds and children are running and screaming, it is school related, unlike the email that was sent out after the fact that said it wasn't. The school was told about these threats for at least a day before hand and they sent out an email to parents stating that they were just threats and not to worry. The next day, a man with an automatic rifle is at the school.My child, who is an honor roll student, was hit by some kid that was in a fight with a different kid as she was trying to get to another student who was giving her information that she missed while she was out sick. I went up to the school and all they were worried about was the fact that she was not at her next class and next to the fight. She had to defend herself against the Assistant Principle and like 4 other staff who were in this room with us.And they are more worried about students being in dress code and having their phones than they are anything else.My oldest daughter has been trying to talk to the counselor about moving her classes into the 11th grade class because the ones she is in, she has already taken. She has been trying for months. Finally, the counselor told her to come see her about it and when she did, the counselor was off and knew she would be off.My oldest is also taking college classes at Hutchins and that is the only thing that keeps her motivated at all. Both my kids are terrified to go to school and I am terrified to send them. I cannot count on this school to keep my kids safe or tell the truth when something happens. Absolute terrible school and staff!

column1: The principal is clueless! They do not prepare kids for college. They do not offier enough AP classes for students. They focus on sports more then education. Test scores low! teachers have kids watch movies instead of having to teach them. Overall this school district is one of the worst around yet we pay some high taxes just not sure for what. They over test the kids preparing them for state testing (lower levels) If the house values were there I would move to get my kids away from this school district and this high school. They cut classes and their alternative for that is block scheduling. So now you have teachers who could barely teach for 45 minutes going to be teaching for 70 to 80 minutes. Yeah that makes sense. One teacher actually was teaching the kids God is not real because that is her view. This school many many years ago used to offer so much. Now the only thing it offers is really nothing. Over paid stafff, no suport for good teachers, some lazy teachers that need to retire, no challenges. I am a former student of this school. While I attended there was an over emphasis on sports and the band and almost no focus on the actual LEARNING. The text books were outdated and the teaching staff was not invested and did not properly teach the vast majority of the students. The staff mostly focused on the children with the richest parents, hoping to get donations from them at the expense of others. The school is cold and without natural light. The special education department is atrocious and does not leave those students in any way ready for the world after school. This is a school that puts up a good front but does not deliver. Please be wary of enrolling your child if you are moving into this township. Our two children have attended Roxbury High School and we couldn't be more pleased with the experience they've had and the strong sense of community and academic achievement they've benefited from. Let me first say welcome to the Roxbury family. The schools are far superior to other districts. It's a warm and friendly community, from my experience coming from a sub par district my children grew by leaps and bounds in the Roxbury schools. My 4th child is starting full day kindergarten this year and I couldn't be more proud of this district for preparing our children of today for the adults of our future Roxbury has so many paths for all of its students to take, and they support everything! The student body is full of amazing and intelligent young scholars. no matter what group of friend you have, everyone gets along. The staff cares so much about each and everyone of the students. if a student asks any staff member for help they will be willing to stay late, come early, or give up a lunch to make sure that student succeeds. The administration staff is very involved with the student body, I'm so lucky to have the opportunity to attend Roxbury High School Roxbury is an excellent district where every student can find success. Teachers guide and challenge students to be and to do their very best. There is emphasis on respect and kindness, evident in the climate of the school, in student fundraising (go Mini-Thon!) and community involvement. There is a comprehensive curriculum including honors and advanced placement classes, up to date technology accessible to every student, and a wide variety of extracurricular clubs and activities. Roxbury High and Eisenhower Middle School serve as School of Choice for the Arts due to their outstanding visual arts and nationally recognized performing arts programs.  And the district ranks 17th in New Jersey’s Top 200 Safest School Districts! Overall, Roxbury HS is a good school. The teaching staff, in general, are dedicated professional who relate well and care about the students. What anyone coming into this district need to be concerned about is that, when the district is in contract negotiations with the teacher's union, a common tactic of the union is to use the students as political pawns to get what they want. They instruct the staff to stop helping students after school and not write recommendations for students who are looking towards college. At such a critical time in a student's life, this should be unacceptable to each and every parent. The students should not be used as pawns in this power struggle. The union leadership puts their pocketbook issues before the well-being of the students. If you are just coming into this district or at lower grade levels, you need to be concerned about this. Both of my children attend roxbury HS and they are each in different activities (one in sports and one in band). They both thrive like I have never seen and I couldn't be happier Absolutely awful. I wouldn’t recommend roxbury to anyone. Our district has dropped 200% in rankings in the time that Loretta Radulic has been our superintendent I dislike this school district Highly. Since elementary school and all the way up through High school time and time again I have dealt with incompetent support staff, a tech department that does nothing to help and just overall barely mediocre education. They should probably emulate neighbor districts such as mo7nt olive or randolph for how to do things the right way. First thing I'd like to discuss about this school is the overall structure of the school. When the school was built it was built with no windows. Many students wont see the light of day, especially if they are involved in extracurricular activities. In the winter this school refuses to put heat on for students unless absolutely needed. This follows the same trend with summer and AC. My child throughout high school has met some great teachers sure, but half of the teachers, principal, and VP are mediocre. Next with the bathrooms, they lock the bathrooms in between class time, they make you sign in and out of the bathroom and teachers love to humiliate students for how long they took to walk back. This school is famous for its lack of security and the amount of petty fights they allow to happen. Not only do they overlook petty fights, but they also overlook bullying. In fact some of the teachers and authority figures are the perpetrator themselves. The tech department and its hours happens to cause a lot of issues for students as well. Some of these students wont be able to get their chrome books fixed during these short hours which aggravates teachers. Lastly, Id like to touch on the topic of discipline and suspension. Some students don't have any real proof against them and will still get suspended, others have real proof and get to stay in school with no repercussions.
