column3: All three of my children have attended WHS. I have been very pleased with the staff. They have been very accommodating with my special education child. I am an alumni from this school. Graduated 2009, and I absolutely love this school, the students, the environment (even though there's construction -_- ), especially the teachers. I've been in college for two years now(plenty of great professors) but my fave instructor is still my Jr year English teacher at Westminster. The teachers/administrators all genuinely like the students and are all working for the students. MERITS allowed me to take all four AP science classes by the time I graduated and now I don't have to take any science classes in college. It was hard work but the teachers I had made it all worth it. If your student's middle school feeds into WHS I recommend you seriously consider this school. All of my mentors stem from my HS experience. I love this school i have been here for 2 years so far the football program is excellent and clubs are excellent. Sports overall in this school are excellent with a 6 year win in league for football. I love this school it is amazing and i have no complaints. i dont know what people mean by gun shops across the street and camera pointed in restrooms ... i havent seen that .. thats insanity hahaha their just making up stuff to give this school a bad name My kid have been in this school for two years. She is not happy at all. Students here are always bullied and jealous. One of the blond old woman in the attendant office is not very nice to the students and parents. One of the biology teacher and his wife has an inappropriate behavior with his students. The teacher makes the school look bad now. Is this how the biology teacher teach the student how to learn inappropriate manner. I am going to transfer my kid to a different school next year. I am currently attending this school going on 3 years. I love this school and its environment. I am one of the few non-Asian students that are in the AP classes and I am part of the music department. I would say that this school excels in academics, but not so much in sports. We could have a better sports program but I understand that ours sports teams do good in alternating years. The incident with the former Biology teacher should not reflect poorly on the school in any way. For those thinking of transfering students to other schools, I would like to say that 1) no other school in the district can say that they have won the OCAD 5 years in a row, 2) that student would be missing our on great academic opportunities offered at Westminster, and 3) its just ridiculous that people think because a teacher went astray that it is going to affect the students badly. I have been a student at Westminster for 3 years, and I have loved it ever since the first year! The honor's program here is extremely rigorous, but it ensures that we will be ready for college as soon as we graduate! The teachers are encouraging and always willing to help. The MERITS program is also great because it allows us to take more rigorous AP classes early on, an advantage over other schools. It has been 10 years since I graduate from this school. One word to describe it: horrible! When I hear people telling others that the honor's program here is extremely rigorous, all I can do is just shake my head. I graduated whs passing 6 AP exams with at least a score of 4; but if you think that is going to prepare you for college, you need to take a walk and breathe in some fresh air. This school is best at making kids work hard in areas that do not benefit them for college; its teachers love to assign busy works and parents are often not too smart to figure out what is going on until it is too late. If you want to prepare yourself for college, then take college classes at goldenwest college instead of taking its AP courses. 10 years ago, the math teachers there were horrible; if they are still around, start running the other way! Everything about this school is horrible to me except the friends that I made during my time here. If you are a parent and you have a choice, send your kids to Irvine. If you are a parent and you do not have a choice, then beware that some of these teachers are the most horrible people you can trust educating your kid! Don't say you hadn't been warned! I Would Like my son study english an he live a new experience, know others style live, other country, maybe play footbol whith other team A lot of reviews might criticize this school, but if read carefully, those reviews are rating this school based on that are no longer valid to Westminster High School's current condition, such as experiences a whole decade ago. This school has many resources for its students, the problem isn't with the school, but with the students who don't try or use the resources. If WHS was to have admissions requirements and entrance exams like top schools such as Oxford Academy, then this school would be one of the best, but this method is not deemed as fair here and so the school's credibility is left in the hands of its students and demographic and I can tell most of the current teachers and staff try to help all of these students. Your high school experience is greatly differentiated by the level of classes you take too. WHS has been warm friendly kind and understanding, the receptionist is doing Multitasking and has so many things going all at once, she does her job with compassion and class, the attendance secretary is very receptive and she has a keen sense of whats going on with the students she does not judge and is helpful, attendance has gone out of the way on a very busy day to make the issue i am dealing with in regards to a teenager i have been heard and understood, helped and validated by the vice principle of discipline. The school is patient with all the students, even in supervision...a much need sternness is given but i observed what I would call a great deal of love behind the disciplinary motives that came to the students who were there as i was waiting, it was very nice to see people being concerned and respectful to each other to the parents and to the students even as trouble is brewing with a student they are well trained to be an understanding sounding board.i trust WHS to care, they are very fair God be for you WHS! low test scores for 60% of the students...athletics have way too many walk-on coaches...administation has a high turnover rate...most classified were hired because they could speak Spanish or Vietnamese...school looks like a prison with gray bars around it This school administration lacks follow through and respect. The attendance office never keeps track of notes provided to them. The absences always remain as truant due to the schools neglect to detail. I get non stop recorded calls every day. I've requested for the calls to stop 6 times and I still get them. The principal never returns calls after several requests and visits. The vice principal tried to give detentions to students getting picked up by parents after school. He sent formal slips home with the students. The district office knew nothing about this, nor did the principal. This school should be closely monitored by Sacramento for their unprofessional behavior and the ongoing low test scores. 60% of the students shouldn't have low test scores. This falls on the teachers for not properly educating our children. If anyone has an option, do not send your child here. Your child will not get into college from a high school like this. The school makes an illusion to all parents worst school in all of southern California i tell this review by my own eyes i admit theirs at least 1 one good teacher for each grade and i have spoken to one of the teachers and she said that we should change my childs school that the only reason their students is because they come from a low income family and Westminster high school is the only option all students have. I put my son in this school is because we across the street i plan on moving my son to Marina highschool or ocean view highschool Just GREAT..!! My daughter has a wonderful experience with this school. She graduated with two high academic excellence achievements. She also received the certificate of commendation along with her diploma.

column1: I went to Walnut Grove for my freshman and sophomore year of high school , and it's a very good school when it comes to academics but in sports and school spirit wise, they are slacking a little bit. Great teachers, a good staff. The students Are Okay. Mostly everyone is nice to you. I enjoyed my time were before I moved to a different state. You'll have no problem with anyone or anything at this school. Go Warriors! I agree with the communication problem. The teaching staff is not available when needed. You must email them and they often never respond. I have spoken with administrative staff regarding specific teachers and issues I have had and they look at me like I am starting trouble and just brush me off. Teachers no longer teach. They just let the iPads do all the work while they check their Facebook statuses or whatever it is they do while our children are struggling to learn. My child moved to this school from a neighboring school. Has had the best experience, and is very happy to be at WGHS! Everyone works together to make this a great, safe school where kids are asked to give their best academically and as a person Excellent experience for both of my children at WGHS Great school. Teachers who care. Lots of activities . Clean and safe. During pandemic ok with zoom- online not great.

column3: Steubenville and their athletic program is the last place you would want to send your child. Why is this school even listed on the Great Schools website when clearly the school, teachers and coaches fail to educate individuals that are fit for society. Sports coaches at this school should not be working anywhere near impressionable children and adolescents. As a parent...stay clear of this school and as a mother, keep your daughters away from the football and softball team. This school's pride for their sports team or "BIG RED" culture provides young men with a very damaging sense of authority, at the expense of others without little regard. Do you really want your child to follow and accept this school's "Big Red" culture? SHS has quality teachers who go over and above making sure their students are prepared for college. They have a very high graduation rate as well. The school system rates as one of the best in the state of Ohio. I would highly recommend this high school to any student that is looking to further education at the highest degree Steubenville HIgh School has many things to offer young students at the very highest levels. First of all they are one of the highest ranking public schools for academics in the state of Ohio. They have a top notch drama program and choir. Their choir and drama club put on excellent shows every year. Their marching band is always ranked in the state and has won numerous awards. Lastly, their teachers are very caring people who help each and every student to reach their goals. I meant to press 5 stars in the last review. So sorry to have pressed 4 stars instead of 5! As a graduate of SHS, it's important to note that the school fosters a well-respected arts program, diversity amongst students, and a fantastic assortment of educators, in and out-of-classroom learning opportunities, and strong athletic programs for both young men and women. Of course every school has its bad apples, but this school's pros far outweigh its cons. It is absolutely worth a look if you are in the area, and produces many fine, upstanding, talented, respected, and intelligent man and women. Excellent academic resources available. Extra curricular possibilities abound. Modern facility with many extra not found in nearby schools. I moved to this school district in my sophomore year and I could not believe how horrible it was. Drugs were readily available. The classes were 1 to 2 years behind my previous schools teaching level. Books were falling apart. They had a fancy football field though, even if the players joked about doing drugs and fighting people. I suspect the other reviews on this site are fake. My education not only prepared me academically, but also life as a good citizen. The tradition of excellence continues with the current principal, Mr. Gorman, who shows compassion and sets the example for teachers and students. College Credit Plus courses offered free of charge, including text books, on site instead of AP courses. Students have opportunity to graduate high school with an associate degree. Excellent sports, choral and performing arts programs. In our experience the teachers children were given priority over regular kids. Still have yet to see a teach or administrator, whose child is not in enrichment. Not a lot of good things to say about academics. Sports seem to be a weirt priority for the adults who graduated 20 years ago and came back to teach and attend football games. Poor behavior control at scs. We were not fans.

We will be moving soon and the part that we are the most sad about is leaving Southeast. Go Tigers!

column3: I went to Capo in the late 80's. I was very intelligent, but was one of the students that fell through the cracks and dropped out. The school officials knew I was struggling with issues at home, but there was very little outreach to me. School should have been a sanctuary, a refuge from my crazy life, but it wasn't. As for the academic material, many of my classes were about memorizing information for tests - which I promptly forgot if I even bothered at all - there was zero critical thinking. I was the invisible and troubled child in the room that was never engaged. I ended up taking the GED the year after I should have graduated. There were quite a few students like me that you will never hear about, but we existed then and probably still do now. I went on to carry a 3.9 GPA in college and a successful career, so my story has a happy ending - but I know there are ones who aren't as lucky. I'm giving my school an above average rating because this school offers a variety of classes ranging from Marine Biology to AP Art History. This school offers alot more classes than other schools in the area, but my problem with this school is that I don't feel challenged. No one pushes you to your potential. There are so many smart kids at my school who don't know it because either they're not motivated or not being pushed hard enough. Other than that it's a pretty good school, all the teachers are nice and it's a very easy going school. Visited this school with my teenagers while on a house hunting trip. The building is showing its age, but the staff and teachers seem welcoming and very professional. They have a very nice 50 meter pool. Giving this school two stars and deciding to look elsewhere because my children are interested in engineering. The PLTW program is entered only through a districtwide lottery. So if you attend this school and don't win their lottery your kids transcript will be missing those 4 engineering classes that the other kids from capo will have. They probably should have given preference to kids from capo, and used a lottery for the rest, as this will be a significant disadvantage to those students trying to get into an engineering college. Tesoro and Aliso Viejo both have newer facilities and better test scores anyway, so I will probably try our luck with the lotto after moving to one of those schools. JSerra Catholic has a very nice Engineering Magnet, if you can afford it. I love this school! My boys have had a great High School experience and I couldn't be happier. The staff is always very helpful, our principal has an open door policy and genuinely cares for our students, and we have had great experiences with the teachers that my boys have had. The school is in need of a facelift, but it should because it's almost 40 years old! Terrible no one really cares about you, and anyone who looks forward to coming here everyday is just excited they get to hit there JUUL in the bathroom. Also if you think I am just some kid trolling that is not true, I am a 4.0 all honors/AP student. Regret that we didn't know better than choose this school Go Capo!! Could have been a lot worse This is a great school with opportunities for everyone. Like most things in life the experience here is what you make it. If you want everything handed to you easily then good luck. But, if you want to be a self starter and responsible for your own success this is a great place to launch from. There are advantages and disadvantages at every school. CVHS does an excellent job of connecting with their students as individuals. I have had only positive experience with the administration and teachers. Communication is a two-way street. Parents cannot expect more than they give. CVHS keeps the communication going until the problem is solved. I highly recommend. CAPO is a very fun and wonderful school and I think that all teachers are very nice.

column1: My son attends BMCHS. I remember when he was in 8th grade and went for a one day visit in the shadowing program, shadowing a freshman throughout the day. When I picked him up he was all smiles. He said it was awesome! Now he is a freshman and just finished his mid-term tests. He scored in the top third in a juniors ranking, as a freshman, in math, language and science. I believe this is largely in part to the teachers of Bishop. The school is not cheap but in the end, for me, it is worth the sacrifice. I m glad we choose BMCHS. i hate this school!!! the dress code is ridiculous and the administration lacks professionalism. i would highly reccomend against going here! This schools ok. There are a lot of paper you have to write and it can be very hard. The dress code is strict and shorts arent allowed. Some of the classes are fun while others are boring. great. My kids have thrived. I am so glad that we chose Bishop. An absolutely terrible school that should be avoided at all costs. I highly recommend Bishop. My oldest daughter spent four years here and is now at Carolina. I have a freshman daughter here now. The study habits they learn here are second to none. One of the most important factors to note is, there are no fights here. People we know who have transferred from public schools in both Guilford and Forsyth county tell the horror stories of the frequent fights. If you want a safe environment that focuses on both academics and athletics then Bishop should be on your radar.

column1: The teachers are extremely lazy. My astronomy teacher just shows us videos on YouTube and hands out worksheets that could be completed by a 6th grader. Many elective classes, such as computers classes and culinary, are even worse. There are were days where those teachers had absolutely no plans at all, so we'd get a free day. column1: Massabesic's new trimester structure for delivering classes seems to be making a difference. Having the same classes every day allow the students to stay focused only on those topics of study. We've seen a big difference in my daughter's grades as well as commitment to doing the work. Same as life...you get back what you are willing to put into it. The quality of any school is reflected by what you're willing to put into it. As parents we need to be there for the kids, supporting them, giving the appreciation for their efforts but also to set an expectation of striving to do well. The teachers are great at responding to any emails or calls of concern. Massabesic is working hard to do a great job. They are making significant progress with the new Principal and staff. They still have a ways to go, but are limited because most parents do not seem to care, therefore they tend to treat us all as such. The NJROTC program is excellent - keep in mind that there are kids from families who don't bother so it is a mixed group - but if a student wishes to excel, the NJROTC folks offer excellent support. They actually teach manners and respect. Teachers vary significantly in quality. They seem to be under pressure from the new administration. Some offer more support, others just dumb down the material so be careful in math and sciences - big difference in quality of teachers. The guidance department has been quite useless in getting kids toward college, but they seem to be responding to the new Principal's pressure. Keep a close eye on class schedules and make sure your child is in college bound classes if that is their goal - the guidance dept does not keep up with this and is difficult to work with. You can either be liked by many at this school. or you can get your kids educated, but you won't have both. Need to ride some of the staff to deliver. Getting better. I have just become aware of a rumor going around that there may not be a success program at our high school next year. I understand from the beginning that any student not acting appropriatly will be sent to the mainstreem program. I have yet seen this happen and for this program to be the success it really is they need to do this with students who are not willing to do what the success program was all about in the first place. I have a child who went through this program this year and I can assure you without it I doubt my child would have been a success. I am, proud of all my child had done. Please continue this beautiful program. Massabesic needs more of them. I have to give the high rating after an incident involving my daughter was handled swiftly and safely. I was called immediately because a teacher sensed trouble. Danger was averted, but this could have been a tragic event if an adult had not been paying attention!!! Thank you!!!

My son will graduate with 30 college credits and he strives to be successful. Every school has its ups and downs. I am personally satisfied and am proud of our academics and athletics and music programs. We are new to the area and the school. So far we have been very pleased with the teachers and community members welcoming us! We feel our childeren are getting a great education. This school continues to grow and change with the needs of its community and student enrollment. I am a third generation alum and currently have three children enrolled both at the secondary and elementary schools. I would highly recommend this district as a place for your student to get a competitive education and have a chance to stand out due to the small town setting and class sizes. I graduated from CI back before the teacher's strike and the old JH was torn down and replaced by this monstrosity. Back then I would have given the school and the teachers great reviews. Now as an adult with children attending both CRES and CIHS I've got to say how disappointed I am. Children with learning disabilities absolutely fall through the cracks or get labeled trouble makers. I have a straight A student who's labeled because he's apparently "rude" to the lunch lady-no other explanation given. I have a straight F student who was supposed to test at the beginning of the year to see if he needed a para-that never happened- he's a smart kid and his teachers have written him off since he was in kindergarten because he isn't as verbal as other kids. Once the teachers/administrators write off a kid there's very little hope for them in this town- and it's a shame.

column1: The school system is very good in elementary. But from JR High up is a different story. The district is nepotism at it's finest. I have one child who graduated from this school, and one who's a sophomore. I wouldn't have my kids in any other school in the area.

column3: If you do your due diligence and ask people from outside of Hopkinton you will learn about the poor character and culture inherent in the community . The community is very tight knit and clicky. In my opinion and the opinion of most I have spoken to it is not worth the aggravation of dealing with the uptight and exclusive attitudes of the people. This nature bleeds into the culture of the students and faculty of the highschool. Hopkinton High School is headed by very poor leadership governed by self interest and power plays which is fostered and allowed by the community. There are plenty of great schools in MA. Find a community which has a great school but in which you will enjoy the people. Good character is equally important to a good education. You and your kids will be way better off. Don't take my word for it - ask around. Best school in MA, hands down. Hopkinton High School was excellent in preparing my kids for college and getting them into Ivy League colleges. Great school system and community, one of the best in the state at preparing your kids for acceptance into the most selective colleges and universities.

column1: This school is a hole filled with uninspired teachers, drugs and a do nothing administration. If your child isn't a jock, they don't matter. I made the mistake of sending my oldest to school here. I will never allow another child of mine to waste their time here. I thought it was a great school to learn at.Although I personally don’t pay attention to ANY of the drama that High Schools always come with, I just stick to learning which is basically what schools are there for.If your kid is more on the introverted side of things like I was, then Santa Fe Trail is a good school to go to if you’re around Osage County.

column3: If your high school child is in sports, they will probably do well in this school. However, if not, prepare to have them swept under the rug. This school along with the other schools in Cashmere have great teachers, but ZERO communication. My kids have attended their whole lives (minus one year I choiced them out of district) and I have had nothing but problem after problem with these schools. They take no accountability for their inability to communicate with the parents of their students (unless of coarse you have an athlete child). I am relieved to be closing on a house out of the valley and getting my kids the educational experience they deserve. Amazing teachers, principals, and students. We are so lucky to have our kids at Cascade High School!

column1: I am a former student of this school and I have to say that it just sucks. There are a few amazing teachers working and I did find some good out of a few classes but overall it was too easy and did not ready me completely for college life. The small town feeling made many of the students AND staff way too comfortable with the academic environment and ultimately stunting a lot of the student's growth. Discipline is handled in an unprofessional way and it is based on how well the student and teacher like/dislike each other rather than right from wrong. This school is the worst school I've ever seen when it comes to preparing students for the real world.

column3: I graduated from Roosevelt School of the Arts and had an awesome experience. I would recommend people try and join the program because it offers so much. I know there are misconceptions about Roosevelt and it is really sad because it is a great school. Many people are going to miss out on the experience, it s not as bad as people make it seem. I felt really safe there. I was learning and having fun the entire time; HS was easy to me because of RSA. I want to thank all the teachers there for all they do, because of you I might have never been accepted into a university. Thanks for pushing me to strive to be better, the dedication and wisdom and thank you for working at Roosevelt even though you were all told how horrible it was! :-) I will always be proud to be a Rough Rider!! Roosevelt is a amazing place to be! I know there are many misconceptions about RHS but it is truly a wonderful place to be. There RSA magnet program is truly a gem of a thing. The teachers are very nice and supportive of the students. They have many performing arts programs to choose from. The Dance, Choir & Drama programs are Wonderful! The Voice teacher Mr. Woods makes the choir class fun and exciting to go. He is also very supportive and willing to help the students reach there full potiental. The regular acadmic class teachers are very helpful as well. I feel RHS is one of the best schools in the central valley! I would give this school a 5/5 Honestly, a 5/5, but they really need to pay Gabby instead of their electric bill because she lights up every room she goes in. Amazing and diverse, prepares students for college in fields like nursing, arts(music, singing, dance, stage craft),culinary arts and business. RHS has something for everyone!

column1: I love this school! Everyone is all so welcoming and nice. The students are like your family at school. Everyone is treated fairly and nobody gets left out often. There isn't really a "in crowd" which makes school so much more fun. I love this school and think it is a great school for parent's children to go if they love a welcoming community and great fun. Also NB is a very educated place depending on how much you apply yourselves. Sports are wonderful! There are many great athletes that play at NB. Also I think we have a very caring school! Like when students houses have been burned down in the past we have been one of the first people to raise money and give them needed items. New Bloomfield High School has been know as a very caring school. The teachers here are so nice, and actually care about the students. They always help you if you are struggling, and I find that they love their jobs.The leadership from the principal is very stern, but is still nice and really cares about her students. All together this is a great school and have enjoyed every minute of it! I love this school. If there is a problem with your childs grade or not doing their homework; they email you and let you know. It is very much a family based school. Excellent teachers and staff. I am glad I moved to NB and got my kids into this great school! School's just as bad as last year, do not recommend this school to anyone. They always ask for parental involvement but only if the parent does and thinks like the school wants them too. This school is horrible! I know two people who got bullied so bad they quit high school altogether to start online school. They are both doing so much better. The employees don't care about the kids.

column3: As a former student of Sentinel high school, i can honestly say i hated it. And this is coming from one of those kids who kept to himself and failed because of it. No teachers ever came to me to help me out. The teaching methods did not work for me and they don't go further than the basics. A lot of the teachers that i had only went as far as the bare minimum. I can say that they did help me out with suicide prevention, but they still treated me like i was below them and they were just doing their jobs rather than being personable. Some of the worst years of my life were harbored in this school. Educationally, it's not what it seems. If you're behind, you will stay behind if you don't help yourself because if you're not teachers favorite then you have to looking for help elsewhere. Parents need to understand reality here. And I'm not saying don't let your kids go to this school, I'm just saying you should know what to expect and understand how to handle situations. The best part about this school is the counselors. They were the only people i seemed to be able to feel somewhat comfortable with. The math teacher i had in my second year hadn't even had a real teaching degree. Could not have said it better than myself. Same exact feeling as post dated December 2010. I am a parent of a student. My son attended Sentinel High School and it was a wonderful experience. The teachers were interested, engaged in the students' welfare, and very involved in all aspects of each student's particular needs. There were extra-curricular activities available addressing a wided-spectrum of interests and, at least in our son's experience, all the different segments of the student population respected one another and supported one another. Attending Sentinel High School gave our son the education, social skills, and life skills to enter college with confidence and excitement. Kudos, Sentinel and Thank you! Amazing teachers, first rate choir and drama dept, top notch sciences! Way to go Sentinel for making this homeschooling mom of 6 happy, calm and satisfied as my kiddos have transitioned to high school! I had a very positive experience at this school other than one teacher W school we back to back state champs in most sports

column1: iI love this school ever since i got there I've felt so good about myself i am so much more confident and i feel so much more dedicated to my instrument and my art then i would have ever been at any other school. The Principal in never at school and does not care about the kids. If you want to have art as your career , I recommend it

column3: This school isn't good, it lacks DISCIPLINE, creativeness, and diverse classes. They wastes money on unnecessary things, like the grant for iPods. They should use the money to help renew outdated items. They need to replace certain teachers cause they don't care, don't enforce discipline, and lets the students run the class. This school lacks creativity, most clubs are plain. They should create clubs that diverse kids would enjoy. And this school needs new classes. Like a class for future engineers or lawyers. Yet they lack that and force kids to take tests and our scores goes down. They need to realize that this school needs change. I'm a North Rowan student, & proud of it. I agree that maybe we shouldn't have spent so much money on Ipods, because maybe then, we wouldn't have so many fundraisers. But North is a great school. And our band is amazing. I should know. I hear them play everyday. I'm a band student at NRHS myself. It's a good school, please don't hate it.<3 To the person who has an issue with the ipods and the "waste of money" that they perceive has happened... that decision was made by the school board and the current school administration, not North High School. If you want to do something positive for the school -campaign for fair attendance zones and equal access to courses. Again a great school that has been hindered by biased decision making. The school is very nice the faculty are friendly and the environment of the school is safe. My kids doing awesome. Excellent! Staff and principals are always looking for ways to help their students and the community. The best school in the district and maybe in the state. This school includes all students regardless of ability or background. Even though many students come to this school behind the leadership at this school is doing everything to make sure the high school experience is the best for each individual student by finding new ways to reach every student. Not all students are meant to go to college and NRHS addresses the future for all students not just the AP/Honors students that are highlighted by this site. North Rowan High School is a disgrace to this community. They take little to no precautions when it comes to threats, and or bullying. They will side with the one doing the bullying 99% of the time. The victim of the bullying gets treated like a criminal by the principal and the other kids. That is not a fair system to allow these bullies just walk away. In addition, this school is always having lockdowns due to kids bringing weapons to the school. Meanwhile, these kids are allowed to return immediately after the incident. The school will again take no action to prevent this from happening in the future as these issues still continuously happen. If the principal at this school says he is going to do something, chances are he is not going to get it taken care of and you are going to have to call and call or go down to the school and speak with him in order to have any chance of anything being done. This school and principal are not for the kids. If you can avoid sending your children to this school, I would highly recommend sending your kids anywhere but here. They need someone new in charge or an all-new school board. What they have going on currently is trash. I know I do not feel safe having any child go here.

column1: This is one of the greatest schools to send your kids to. It makes a difference, am telling you. Reading the reviews, I'm in shock because this is one of the worst schools I've ever dealt with. This is NOT the Western High School of back in the day. The culture/environment of the school is not conducive to learning, not by a long shot. The administration leaves a lot to be desired. Most of the teachers just do not care. When I sit in the classroom, they're disruptive, kids talking on cell phones, walking across the classroom DURING a lecture for no reason other than to chitchat with another student. There are two major groups of students at Western: those who don't care and those who are exceptional and trying for a full scholarship to Hopkins. Not many in the middle. This school needs major, major changes. This schools principal is Almost never on sight! She is so bad that the studends clap if or when they see her at there school! There is not much leadership and guidance in this school for these girls because she wants to make it a co ed school! This is my child's second year at the school and it's been the same way both years! She needs to go and they need someone who can restore the school back to its former self! These girls are told its a great place to be ! They deserve a great experience to reach there goals and potential and she's not interested in such !!! Vert disappointed a lot of females in our family are Western graduates they are sadden by the fall of there school!!! Hi, I would like to say that from reading the comment about Western High School being one the of most unsatisfactory school in Baltimore City, is true. Yes, in past years Western was the best school for young women to attend but now it is unruly. The principle is never there as well as guidance consulters. My being a junior in this situation is not helping me at all. There are teachers that barely know English are teaching me algebra. I do not understand anything they say or anything in my other classes because if the majority does not understand a topic then it doesn't matter. School is not about getting scholarships anymore. Its about passing, Which is becoming harder to do when the grading system makes no sense to the students nor the teachers. Western is a failing school to me. No air, no heat, no teachers, no principle, no cares, and no worries. Do you all not realize this is hurting those who come after me? But, I guess not, you all already have your education. That's what I'm told everyday. Hello, I am a current senior at Western High School. Seeing the review that a current junior in Western has submitted can definitely give you insight of what a student who attends this school encounters. While all of what this student states is true there are some factors that must be taken into consideration. Yes, Western does not have heating or cooling systems in each class to accommodate every student. Which is why Western encourages their girls to wear appropriate clothing during each season (Sweaters, Shorts to the knee, etc.). Also, I agree that some students are not able to learn subjects by teachers who's first language is not English. That happens. Not everyone in North America or the world for that matter speaks English; therefore you'll have to work with people such as your teachers. So get over it. Try learning and paying attention to the language of the subject and not the flaws of your teachers. Also, I would like to state that the staff there has assembled a training guide of what a Western dove should be which is great! Western will over prepare your daughter academically! Which is what she should be coming to school for in the first place! I would also like to add that Mr. Griffin one of guidance counselors is Superb. I have found the counselor that my child is assigned to, Mrs. Ward to be unavailable and aloof. The guidance secretary has little knowledge and I have found her to be generally rude and unhelpful. Mr. Griffin has always been helpful during my visits to Western. The breakdown of counselors to student is ineffective. During my time at Western, counselors were assigned by Class not by alphabet as they are now. That meant that during busy times for Seniors that the other counselors could be available. The current model does not work well for students as many times non seniors who also have important issues are not able to meet with counselors. This school has very good academics. I'm a going to Western next year, entering into the Health Science Program. You learn about human anatomy and medicine. In 12th grade you start internships in hospitals such as John Hopkins Hospital. One thing that concerns me is the space. The classroom space is very small. Other than that, I picked Western over Carver and Towson high because it will best ready me for college and getting a career. Western is not what it used to be. The students that come after the class of 2014 are ruining western with their ignorant outrageous behavior. They dont care about the academics or culture of the school and they are making western a bad place. Hello I am an up in coming senior at Western. Yes this school is deteriorating at the blink on an eye only because they lower their standards for the incoming girls. Reasons: because its an all girl school and we are going against other schools and the school needs the money for example, for every student we get an amount, plus if we had kept our composite score at 610 or higher we would not have as many girls (which mean no money), we would not have as many teachers (lost of jobs). Also some of these parents commenting on here kids might not of made it in. western is a wonderful school. I promise you if they claim western don't teach them nothing (lie) it teaches them to always be proud of your sex, never let anyone tell you a female cant do something a male can, it will inspire you to become the best of the best. You will meet great people before you graduate. Western also offer wonderful opportunities. Yes western has its flaws so does every other school, we also have some of the top kids in baltimore city they will do greatness in their life time. So please don't sleep on us. Western is a once in a life time thing. P.s don't send your kids here if they don't want to come. I would like to say this school has changed dramatically for the worst. I would not recommend any girls to attend here. The girls are more concern with fighting, being disruption in class and out right disrespectful towards teachers, adults and their peers. Clearly what once was held as a high esteem and prestigious school of scholarly classy women, has changed to a bunch of low class disrespectful girls who need a lot of home training. Also, the staff is unable to manage this girls because their definitely NOT women! Run for the hills and don't send your child to this awful place. There is no learning taken place because there's to many girls in training learning to do the wrong thing!! Western High School gets a fat F- in my opinion! Western is one of the best schools in the BCPS. My daughter completed 4 years there. She was accepted into 6 colleges, all for engineering. The school has changed from 10-20 years ago, but what school hasn t? Discipline is an issue. The staff are unable to kick-out disruptive students as in the past, but that is a school system policy. In spite of the obstacles, the staff and teachers will go out of their way to help your child achieve, IF she wants to achieve. I repeat IF she wants to achieve. The teachers are overworked and stressed because they are asked to do more with less. In spite of this they are willing to go the extra mile for your daughter if she is willing to put forth the effort. The teachers staff do not have the emotional and mental bandwidth to go get and drag your child kicking and screaming to learn something. If she wants to step up and challenge herself, they are encouraging and supportive. If she wants to get C s and not try, (homework, studying, coach class) there is no one there to pull her up and cajole, pamper, bribe, convince or force her to do so. The teachers simply do not have the bandwidth. Maybe the parents should take on that role This school is the absolute WORST one I've ever had the misfortune of attending. I am currently a student here, but I am begging my parents to transfer me after just one year of going. Many of the students did not pay attention during class, but instead they just played on their phones and blast music. I'm going to come out straight and say it, THIS SCHOOL IS GHETTO.The whole year I was there, I did not once see our principal and for the first couple of weeks they forgot to assign a teacher for our home room. DO NOT SEND YOUR CHILDREN HERE EVER WORST SCHOOL I HAVE EVER BEEN TO! In all of my years, I have been to about 5 schools. Western has got to be the worst. The students are disrespectful and rude towards one another (especially towards the teachers) and in terms of academics, the school is so much worse than anyone could've anticipated. Blasted music on phones and rude students are all you see in the halls and if you try to confront anyone about it, you'd better prepare for a fight. Definitely disappointed beyond belief. Do not come to this school. Hello all. I am currently a member of the class of 2017 at Western High School. I say that with pride, whenever anyone asks me where I attend, because I love my school! During my freshwomen year there were several issues (which you might encounter while reading previous reviews) because of the lack of leadership roles at Western. This year we have a dedicated principal who is a Western alumna and many students and teachers can already see a positive change in our envirnonment. The main problem in this school is that some students do not take their education seriously, which in turn is a poor reflection on themselves. I do not fret because those students that I just described are leaving Western rapidly. My classes challenge me and people who complain online were most likely performing poorly in those classes. If any young female wishes to succeed, Western is the school for her! This institution is allowing me to learn in a distraction free environemnt. I have and am still growing in myself while gaining a sense of female empowerment. Thank you Western. I am a Western Dove. I am only the best. I graduated from Western in 2013 during the height of all of the fluctuation with entrance criteria and our horrible principal. I chose Western because I knew that it would prepare me for not only school but for life. Honestly, this is Baltimore city and you are always going to find some kind of unruly students needing home training or some kind of lack of funding, its a system wide issue. HOWEVER, despite this, our teachers go the extra mile to prepare us. I can say that the classes I take at my university now, are of a 9th grade level at Western High, and no matter what types of courses you pursue in college and beyond, Western prepares you for hard work and dedication. No one should be deterred by unruly students in she is dedicated to her own education. I am proof of this and so many other Western Doves are, we have to be in order to even making it through middle school in the BCPSS to even GET to Western. So stop crying about loud mouth girls, they come in ratchet, but majority of you will leave with class and quiet dignity. Take it all as a learning experience. Good luck :) I am a graduate of the class of 1992 from Western High School. I am proud to be a Western Dove and the traditions of the school run deep. It is unfortunate but also not surprising that some people have had issues attending and being a parent/guardian of a student attending. It is not surprising because Western is not for everyone and it is not perfect. It wasn't perfect when I attended and it was frustrating at times for me and my family. Even with that said, I opted to transfer my daughter into the 11th grade this year. I did this because I know that without a doubt I learned to be a woman who knows that I can do anything I set my mind to, I am not a second class citizen and I am entitled to my rightful place in society. I too have had instances of frustration while trying to resolve issues relating to my child's education but what I am doing instead of just complaining or downgrading this institution is trying to figure out where I can be of service (which is another value that Western taught me). I am not to be a part of the problem or see a problem and not find out how I can assist with keeping this school intact. I understand that we all are allowed our opinions and I respect that even if I don't agree. So all I can say is, see where there is a deficiency and see if you have a plan of action, a recommendation, some time to donate to aid with continuing to build this great institution. I love Western High School and I am so PROUD to be a graduate, mother of a current student and hopefully grandmother of future graduates. I am having a wonderful time here at WSHS I graduated several years ago and am an attorney now. I enjoyed my years at Western and am very happy that I attended there.

column3: its pretty bad. the teachers make no effort to catch the students attention, they make no effort to keep the students entertained and with the want of learning. why test so much? if the student fails does that mean they're not smart? the spark kids wanting to learn is completely out. I graduated from this high school in 2018 so believe me when I say that this is a good school. One of they key factors that make this school good is they teachers. Some teachers are great instructors and some are not. Those that are, tend to care the most about the students and help them to learn. I took mostly honor and advanced classes, but for regular classes it may be a bit boring and undisciplined especially at the younger grade level. The atmosphere of the school is great in my opinion. Everyone is nice and you hardly see anyone getting bullied or being ridiculed by other students compared to other schools. Although the test scores may not be as high as other schools, this school did teach me a lot. There are a bit of negatives such as the administration. They tend to care about the security of their jobs than the students. The staff is friendly and interactive among some students. You don’t have to be a popular kid to have fun in school, just a friend and you’ll be alright.

column1: Overlea is the best school you can go to, if you are looking for a sense of community! The teachers care about the students and work overtime to help them out! I am in the enrollment process for my niece to attend Overlea High for the 2014 school year. Since she's my niece and I do not have custody, I had a few extra steps to take to enroll her, however, I executed well on all the requirements, but it seemed as though things were going too well for one individual, who at the last minute through a wrench in the progress and pulled others into her mess. She called me rude, yelled at me, then stormed out of the difficult conversation she started. Needless to say, after all the hurdles and due diligence on my part, I'm still waiting to confirm my niece's enrollment and instructions. WONDERFUL, JUST A GREAT SCHOOL!! column1: Very disappointed in the lack of communication from teachers and administration. Totally understand time constants in education; however, a number of parents are very frustrated with the lack of professionalism and responsiveness among some of the faculty and the administrative leadership at Van Buren.. This school can be great or horrible depending on where your child ends up, with what teachers, in what social group, etc. I attended this school myself and found the administration to be severely lacking but the teachers to be excellent and I succeeded in school. My first two children didn't do as well. The middle child fell into drugs bad at that school and told me of how easy it is to sneak off campus and how much the teachers just goof off and encourage the kids to in class. Also, he was a good kid making good grades and never affected by peer pressure but he said he was surrounded with the drug pressure constantly. He is in a better place now. My last child will not be going to that school. I saw for myself after repeated visits the lack of caring for the children there. They are just numbers now. As a current student at VBHS I have to say that I absolutely love my High School. They have an excellent music program. I am a former member of the band, I am going into the 11th grade I decided to get out because of the stress involved in marching band. I had the best biology teacher ever, Mrs. Gail Saifi is such an awesome teacher and she deserves the respect. I am a choir member going on my second year, Mrs. Kathy Hoover is the best ever and I love her a lot :) As far as education wise with me in marching band it was a little stressful to get my home work done and get all of my stuff done in time and work around band schedule. I had the best experience my 10th grade year. I loved band, but in my opinion grades and school work are more important than extra curricular classes :) I love I can be in chess club and in choir too :) and still have a music credit. I hope to graduate with at least a 3.8 GPA. I want to be a music major and I feel like I can achieve that at VBHS :) It is a great school, and a lot of people talking negative about because of what they see on the news about it. But the VBSD staff and facility take extra good care of us students and makes sure we are safe :) VBHS..Mu child was dropped from a class and made by the school to sign the consent agreeing to be dropped from the class. The school never contacted us to inform us. We found out the day it happened from our child. I called the school and requested he be put back in class and was told no because he may fail the class and not graduate. On September 26 they decided my child had to be put in easier English class because he may fail in May.They made this decision because he did not turn in one essay as well as other students but they were not dropped from the class yet they said my child was not singled out. When we met with the principal basically was told he will hear me out but he will make the decision as to what is best for my child's. We talked to assistant principal..He agreed with principal..They all agreed we should have been notified and they were sorry that we were not but we are not changing our decision..

column3: As a recent graduate that is now in college, I think Waukee prepared me very well for the next step in my education. I have seen kids that went to Des Moines metro and area schools that are struggling with things that I learned in 10th grade at Waukee. There is a strong emphasis on athletics here, but there are also many opportunities for band, speech, choir, theatre, and language clubs that all boast wonderful programs. I can say this because I have been in these programs along with many of my friends. The faciities are top notch, the programs are wonderful, and one would be hard-pressed to find a better high school education in the Des Moines area. Waukee High School prepares students for the next chapter in their lives. I have one in college now who is doing very well because of the Waukee High School system. I have 2 others that will graduate this year and will enter college as sophmores because of the classes available to them through the school. It's a school that only cares about the athlete's and know one else and the teaching is subpart to a school like Dowling Catholic which is what the school gets compared to. Plus their are way to many students in the school which brings up problems with class selection and being able to fit a certain number of kids in a class. Also they fit about three teachers in a room sometimes which is very weird for a school to do, and they should of started the construction of a new high school way sooner, but it winds down to a bunch of Rich kids who don't care about School

But me and my Husband Wanted to move to a close knit community like the village. column1: Turtle Lake School is full of positive students and staff. I am very proud to be a teacher in this district and a part of this community. The small size of our district allows us as teachers to keep a close eye on each one of our students. By doing this the students get the necessary help and attention they may need. Three of our four children have graduated from Turtle Lake High School. Our youngest is now a Junior. My husband and I have been happy with the overall education. Turtle Lake has done an awesome job keeping our students learning during the pandemic. The administration, teachers, support staff, etc, have a heart for the students. The small town atmosphere is a great environment for a child to learn and grow. School is well kept. Classrooms are neat. Has a better than average fitness center, pool, climbing rock wall. Very nice library. Each student has their own Chromebook available to them. My son graduated from Turtle Lake and it was a great experience for him. The high academic standards helped him do well in college and in now in physicians assistant school. Academics and extra curricular are well mixed and helped my son succeed.

column3: Mallard Creek is wonderful! My child is a freshman. The school has made sure they are welcoming. Teachers and freshman counselor is there to help guide both parents & student. Mr Crawford vice principal gets back the same day you called. Student support among the each other is impressive....Eileen Wolfe Mallard Creek HS provides your child with the level of rigor that they need to grow from where they are at academically to where they need to be, and well beyond. My children have been identified for years as being gifted and have always sought to take the toughest classes available. We thought about Lake Norman Charter for a split second but due to the small size of the school I wasn t sure that they were going to be able to provide my children with the high level courses that parents are only able to get at their local school. The number of students that attend (MCHS) provide the administration with the student population to carve out the higher level AP Chemistry, AP Environmental Science, AP Geometry, etc that parents and students want. If you were to send your child to a smaller charter school these classes would not be available to them. Many parents think that they are doing their child a favor by sending them to a private school or charter school when in fact they may be removing access to the level of rigor that they need to be competitive at the University level. Signed Parent of 2 currently @ UNC Chapel Hill, 1 @ Mallard Creek HS and 1 @ Piedmont MS. Great school and teachers, son graduated 2012... I have a child with special needs, and the school's response has been fabulous. They go out of their way to follow her IEP, and ensure all of her teachers are aware and working with her the way they are supposed to. We are having a great experience halfway through her first year there. Our son graduated last year and did very well. Good preparation for college. It's a great school. Mallard Creek High is a good school for the average student. Most teachers are great and have a lot of experience. However, if you want to be someone above average it's not the school for you. Courses aren't rigourous enough and the few AP and IBM course are full of students who don't take the course seriously. They were simply placed there by counselors that have too many students to handle. Overall it's your average highschool for the average student. My experience has went from a paradise to a nightmare since the new administration has come in. No professional skills what so ever. This school has really gone down. Directed at Principle Dean,With the addition of the new principal Jenefer Dean, the interest in sports has steadily been declining throughout administration and staff in the school, this is prevalent with all the top coaches leaving being unable to receive adequate respect among their coworkers and the administration. The Mallard creek track program has been declining quickly even with the success of former alumni even going to the olympics, this whole situation is just sad for the student athletes. Mallard Creek HS Is not for the weak. If your kid has never seen a fistfight before, get ready. There is at least one fight every day. The students at this school are rude and hostile to each other. The staff is rude also. Teachers swear often and have no problem cursing out your kid. The students indulge in various drugs and often vape in the bathrooms. The school is unclean most of the time. Do not expect your child to be treated kindly by the students, or the staff. Do not expect your kid to be challenged with the schoolwork given and feel set for college. And do not expect your kid to be the person they were when you first enrolled them.

column3: My child has attended both private and public. The accelerated classes are challenging and do a great job preparing him for college. My goal for my child is an ivy league school and the accelerated program and straight A s will get him there! I noticed many of these reviews were older, especially the negative ones, so I thought I would give an updated review. I am currently a junior at BR. The school has brought technology into the classroom in the form of online textbooks, no longer needing to lug books to school, and classroom sets of iPads and Chrome Books. Now, starting from freshmen year, you have the option to choose from over 50 courses. Unfortunately, the had to eliminate our study period from the schedule in order to do so, but study is available as an elective. BR is known around the state for having some of the best athletic teams, but we also have other after school options which includes a robotics team that competes nationally, and a very well regarded spring musical program. The school is relatively new. The teachers, like with any school, vary. (It's all a matter of personal opinion.) My class (2016) has some of the best standardized test results in the state, so obviously, we are learning and have credible academics. I know many people, and hopefully myself in a couple years, who are proud to call themselves BR graduates.

column1: A fabulous school with so much to be proud of. The teachers are helpful, committed, and interested in the success of the students. The principal has created a safe environment for this close-knit group of students to learn. The community service the students of this school do for the community is unmatched by any school in KUSD. These students are completing great projects around the city and around the country that are benefiting community members, those in need, and other students. What the students and faculty accomplish simply astounds me. Harborside Academy is a gem. The leadership is caring and compassionate and I love the philosophy of expedentiary learning. It really helps students build character and learn how to work in groups. My son blossomed at this school. It was the best thing for him. I particularly like the inclusion approach that no students sits alone. This school is outstanding. As a parent and educator myself, Harborside Academy definitely is a top notch school. The school's philosophy and mission statement aren't just words on paper, they are lived each day by the students and staff. I feel there is excellent communication to parents, the principal frequently sends out emails and phone calls as to what is happening at school. My daughter loves her teachers and loves school. I believe my student is getting the best education in town at a school that feels like family to her. I am a 2013 graduate from Harborside. Over the past for years Harborside has built me up for the real world and pushing over my limits. I would not be the person i am today without Harborside. They really care about the kids and offer insight into life after high school. The intensives were really interesting to the kids. My school is the best school I have worked at in my 25 years of teaching because it treats ALL as a part of the family. As in any family, you have your ups and downs but you always get through it together as a family! Students and their families know that everyone gives their whole hearts and souls to make everyone live up to their fullest potential. Our school has the ideal atmosphere for learning for all levels and personalities. Everyone is treated with respect - by staff, teachers, fellow students. Character is key, expected, but also shown so kids understand the importance. All kids are loved, treated like family, with high expectations, understanding, and humor. Many who feel they don't "fit in" elsewhere consider our school to be a safe-haven of sorts; they are comfortable and can learn with up-to-date pedagogy and diversified educational strategies so everyone, no matter his or her learning style, can find their way and succeed. The teachers are top-notch and are family, as well. They respect and work with each other, even though they are under more pressure than most schools with the training and continuous work it takes to plan the learning expeditions. For such a small school, there are so many wonderful extra-curricular opportunities such as in clubs and interscholastic sports. Community service is huge, and our students are at a huge advantage when it comes time to apply for college - Comm. Service is an expectation and students want to become involved. The principal should step back and trust the teachers to teach Harborside Academy is about more than just academics. It's a place where kids learn that they matter and can make a difference in the world. The Expeditionary Learning model has an extraordinary effect on how young people experience education. Kids don't just read books, memorize concepts, and take tests. They supplement book-learning with group projects relevant to them as individuals and to their community. As a result, abstract concepts become concrete and meaningful to them. Harborside fosters emotional, civic, physical, and artistic growth by encouraging student-led extracurricular opportunities such as service projects, fund raisers, interest groups, and clubs. Harborside is also a safe place for kids to develop strong character. There is a zero tolerance policy regarding bullying. At the same time, honesty, positive attitude, helpfulness, and personal responsibility are encouraged and even incorporated into grades. Finally, the teachers and administrators at Harborside are incredible. They aren't "just" academic instructors...they're my partners in raising happy, well-rounded adults that will, if we've done our job right, pay it forward someday. Harborside has been great for my child. The staff is fabulous! Additionally, they offer much more in the way of clubs, activities, and other growth opportunities. I love Harborside because they make learning easy and fun for everyone. Hands-on learning and different activities help us understand new concepts and teamwork. For the most part, everyone at Harborside gets along and work together well. Harborside Academy, Kenosha WI Great school offering a variety of options for learning and student character and educational development. The staff and students at this school have helped my child open up more and become more confident! This school is unique and he kids love it. The teachers really go out of their way to help the kids. My son is a Senior at Harborside this year. When we were looking at the different options for high school we felt Harborside would be the best match for his creative learning style, we were not let down. The hands on learning and team building not only make school fun it gives the students the opportunity to get to know each others strengths and weaknesses putting them at an advantage for post secondary learning and real world situations. I'm looking forward to watching my son grow over this next year and I'm glad to have Harborside be a part of it. I couldn't be happier with the education my daughter is receiving at Harborside. It is a fantastic school. Not only does it challenge the kids academically but Harborside challenges them to be a better person. My child's school has helped her grow in such a short time. They encourage the children to work together which leaves no one out. The projects and field work makes learning more creative and more interesting. I think the school could improve on school to parent communication. There were things I missed because my child forgot to tell me. Parking is difficult when picking up students. One big problem was snow that was never removed along the streets around the school. Parent: Harborside Academy has given my son a great start For his future. He has learned to work as a team, learned that he Can accomplish more than he thought and in his words "Harborside gave Me a work ethic that I would not have gotten anywhere else." All with small class sizes and with teachers that get to know their Students. This school has great school spirit, sense of community and a great work ethic. My daughter loves going to school. Harborside is an Expeditionary Learning school that builds character while providing an education. Students learn to work together as a crew. It is a strong supportive community. Students are connected to the community. The learning is authentic and connects students to real world experiences that prepare them for the world. Harborside also helps students understand their own strengths and weaknesses and allows students to work towards personal goals of self-improvement. It also gives clearer vision of where they want to go in life both in post high school education or careers. Harborside also provides field trips at little to no cost and ensures they are directly linked to an expedition they are studying. I am completely satisfied with the education my children receive at Harborside! Harborside Academy is a school dedicated to growing students academically and socially through experiences that challenging students to improve and do their best. The principal is one of the school greatest assets because of his passion for students, dedication to leadership, heart for students with special needs and desire to do what is right. The student population is diverse due to a true lottery system for acceptance to the school. (siblings and certain classification of students do not need to be accepted via lottery) The school could improve by screening staff thoroughly to ensure each staff member participates in expeditionary training including a multi-day outdoor "trip experience" prior to their first day of work. The union influence on hiring and the districts method of placing teachers has hindered this goal in some aspects. Perhaps this will change for the good with the changes in Wisconsin with new legislation with unions. The core requirement of CREW is the class at the school that is the best method to impact students positively. The staff in general go above and beyond expectation to assist students to reach goals academically. I'm honestly shocked by the positive reviews. I attended Harborside before transferring to my current school. The attempt to grade students character was based almost entirely off of dress code violations and turning work in on time; there's far more to character than that. Furthermore, the academics are abysmal. I made it through an entire geometry class without once using a compass once. We didn't come close to getting through the book. Likewise Algebra 2/Trigonometry-Honors was similarly a failure. Given an entire year to cover what most schools cover in one semester, they still failed to get through even half of the book. I could go on to similar stories about the other classes, but I'd like instead to move on to the discipline problem: there is virtually no discipline. Students often attend school high, violate dress code, and loudly talk about getting drunk outside of school, or having sex. Little work is done during class, the students are often too busy talking to be bothered to attempt learning. And interestingly, despite all their talk about creating a safe environment, there's a noticeable problem with bullying. Overall, attending Harborside would be a terrible mistake. I was a student at Harborside Academy and was utterly disappointed. The academics are poor, I was there for two years and can make a list of things I learned that wouldn't even fill a sheet of paper. There is no sense of discipline, that students are very disrespectful, and there are various students that should have been removed from the school based on the so-called standards that the school claims to hold itself to. Harborside's approach is both great and has room for improvement. The expeditions the teachers put together are usually very engaging and help create final products that are pretty great, but there are also some concepts that need to be taught but get brushed aside since they don't fit the learning expedition. The character grades can be a bit excessive, but they do help show where some students need to improve as an individual. The sciences at the school aren't as challenging since there is only 1 AP science course; if more were added, I'm sure many students would benefit from a better work habit. My son graduated from Harborside Academy, he just missed being in the top 10% of his class but went on to a nationally accredited Business College and Graduated with honors, making the Dean's list every semester! I have had a fantastic experience at Harborside!!! 10 outta 10!!!!
