column3: The Math program that was introduced 3 years ago across the county has been a systematical problem. 75% of the Park View students math grades have decreased significantly. Some teachers do give their time to work with the students before and after school, but more needs to be done. Teachers need to be held accountable for their teaching styles and how to help improve the student learning rather than worry about the SOL testing that only supports the teachers job status. This school is horrible. From academics to athletics. From the princicpal apoligizing for not speaking spanish to the unorganized, inconsistancy of the athletic department. My oldest child just graduated from PV and I have two younger ones attending. I would not trade to another school if I won the lottery. The teachers are committed to their students success and are available before, during and after school for extra assistance. Students are from a wide variety of cultural and socio-economic backgrounds without the tension and behavior problems seen at other schools. They respect each other. The administration is marvelous. There will be a new principal next year and I only hope he is as good as Dr. Minshew has been. Park View High School is a very good representation of America . . . a melting pot that creates good character and responsible young adults ready to take on the challenges of college or entrance into the workforce. The Principal, assistant principals, counselors, and teachers care immensely about the students. I have 3 kids that graduated and one more still to graduate. All of my kids have been positively influenced by the faculty and staff at the school. Now it was not always a smooth ride for my kids but they managed to overcome the bumps in the roads because of the faculty and teachers. Some kids at the school did not always represent the best interest of the school; however, most students I have met and interacted with are wonderful and show Park View Pride. PVHS gave my daughters something I never expected--a broader perspective. This might seem less important than perfect grades, but I know my girls are ahead of many of their peers in their readiness to enter today s work world thanks to the diverse community that is PVHS. While attending notably less diverse colleges, they felt something was missing. Post college, they ve adapted well to the now typically international work places of suburban DC. Yes, they attended and performed well in AP classes. Yes, they had teachers and administrators they liked and didn t like. Yes, like any school, PVHS is a changing environment that students and families must navigate with care. What s constant is the support found in both the staff and the community. Many parents volunteer for years after their kids graduate. Many teachers spend the majority of their careers there, enjoying deep respect from their students for their obvious dedication. The benefits of a school like PVHS can t be measured in the stats of a data set: Go there, talk to staff and parents, see a musical or a football game, and decide what s most important in your child s education. It might not be in the curriculum! Part 3 of 3: In 2013, Park View students raised $4280 for the United Way, and for a Louisa County high school that was affected by the 2011 earthquake. This was the most money any Virginia high school raised for students in Louisa County, whose schools superintendent came to personally accept our check. In 2014, students beat the previous year s figure and raised over $6,000, the second highest amount raised in the 20 years Park View has fundraised for the United Way. Half the funds went to the Veteran s Hospital. Last year, one of our hardworking first-generation American students was admitted to Harvard University. Many other first-generation American students gain admittance to Virginia s prestigious state schools. Visit Park View s website to view the many academic and multicultural clubs our students participate in. Be sure to check out the Patriot Photo and Video Galleries to glimpse our students passion for their school. Better yet, visit Park View yourself to experience its uniquely cohesive and communal environment. Talk with our students, teachers and administrators about what they most appreciate about this school. The old principal was not the best but the new principal, Mr. Dolson, is great! He is very spirited like the rest of the school and attends a lot of the school events and sports games. From the first day of school he went right to it and proved he could be awesome. The morning announcements are pretty cool too. He ends with "you have a lot of choices to make so make great ones. Have a great day patriots/park view." Great community, wonderful teachers and administrators. Athletic department and extra curricular activities are top notch! Excellent teachers! Really care about their students! Lots of AP choices. Great opportunities to be involved in extracurricular. Well prepared for college 10/10 it is the underdog of education making good changes in the past year to promote and show growth both academically and behaviorally I rate the experience at this school a 10/10. Look past the financial situations of students but judge them based on their achievements and characters. Teachers not only want you to memorize the material, but they want to help you absorb information like a sponge. This school has the most spirit out of all the schools that I’ve been to and mostly everyone is kind and supportive with each other. My experience with this school is so amazing that I wish I could repeat a grade just to attend this school for one more year. Park View High School has taught me humility, compassion, leadership, and pride. Before attending Park View, I attended schools in Arlington County (great county) and because of this transition, I truly saw how much I lacked in these characteristics. The transition from attending overly fortunate schools my whole life to a school with less opportunities, more diversity, and more struggle changed my character for the better. There is no other school I would rather have gone to.

Some of the teachers and staff were rude I would never send any of my children here and neither should any caring parent. I didn't like this school. my son is a brilliant student who suffered there !!! Attending this school was a wonderful experience. I had gone to Parkway school's my entire educational career. I was diagnosed with a learning disability when I was in second grade and received the support necessary to succeed. When I came to Parkway North I no longer required as much support in my previous years. The special education program is wonderful. They do everything they can to teach the skills that are essential to becoming a successful and independent learner. With the support of the district and my parents, I was able to graduate with exceptional grades and later graduated from Saint Louis University. Everyone is challenged and supported throughout their learning experience. The Staff was completely supportive and helpful. Every school will have their exception, but overall the staff was and still is wonderful. I have established life long relationship with many of my previous teachers. I can not emphasize enough the fantastic experience I had growing up in the Parkway District and at Parkways North. I really enjoy going to Parkway North every day! I can tell that most teachers really love their job and enjoy helping the students! There is an incredible amount of diversity and range of individuals. My favorite thing about my school is the focus on social and cultural issues. We have a Social Justice Committee that does a great job of providing speakers and events that magnify issues we see in our community, which I believe is very important! I see so many intelligent, talented, and hard working people. I believe every person plays a great role in the school, from academics to athletics, I love the Parkway North community! (: This school is so diverse that it is impossible to not find any friends. Its a very caring school in which all the students and staff work together to make it an even better place for learning, leading, and excelling overall. I would never think of sending my children to another place. This school does emphasize both academics and sports/ extracurricular activities. However it is not the school job to make sure that the student can keep up with both school and sports; that is solely the students job. So for parents who were complaining about this, your child is in high school, not in kindergarten. It's about time they learn how to manage their own time, is it not? The teachers here are top standard. Some of the teachers were college professors before deciding to teach high school because of its more relaxed setting. In response to the posting of Jan. 20 and as a supplement to my Jan 9 posting, it is the job of responsible schools to help students, particularly freshmen and sophomores, manage their time and focus on the critical academic areas. Even colleges do this by restricting freshmen student activities (ie, no pledging of frats and sororities first semester)--it's not kindergarten and the truly insightful would realize that. High school should provide a good foundation for the future, not a series of memories for those with a more provincial outlook to ask one another "where did you go the high school". Accomplished people from other areas of the country don't bother with that inquiry. Again, PNHS is a good high school but needs to re-focus on academics and provide more orientation for freshmen and new students. No complaints with the credentials of faculty though a few use a "sink or swim" approach to teaching---again, only a few. Failure or near failure is too often accepted among faculty and students. Time to shake poeple out of their comfort zone and to stop being so parochial. I am a freshman in high school at North High, and i love the school so much! I have gotten so close to some of my teachers and i love them with all my heart. The principal is one of the most caring and loving principal ever! You can just tell the staff there loves the job, the kids, and what they are doing. I can honestly say that i am proud to be a viking! teachers have god complex and forget that parents are adults and not their students. if i would treat my customers as these teachers treating parents i would be fired the same day. the forgot that taxpayers are writing them their paycheck. My daughter is excelling academically and is receiving a very well-rounded high school experience My wife and I have put 3 kids through Parkway North. They have all had wonderful experiences and have all gone on to great colleges and careers. One went to a highly selective college and now has a PhD. The second went to an Ivy. The Ivy kid is profoundly deaf and was treated with great respect and support at PNHS, enabling him to achieve to his full potential. Both kids found themselves unusually well prepared for college, academically. The third child decided not to go to college and may become the most successful of the three, in part because of the tremendous school support for his talents and interests.One fantastic part of PNHS' philosophy is their support for planning and preparing for post-high school. In addition to a dedicated college counselor, PNHS started a unique and highly effective, volunteer, college mentoring program which helps students find their "ideal" post-high school program. Their solid college counseling is the envy of many other schools (the volunteer mentoring program is spreading across St Louis), and is strongly supported by PNHS administration. Another excellent part of the PNHS philosophy is their strong support for - and constant interaction with - parents. If you're willing to work with the administration and teachers (as opposed to simply complaining), they will go to fantastic lengths to work with you and accommodate student needs. This philosophy starts with the principal and goes all the way down the chain. Everyone is on the same page.A third, tremendous aspect of the PNHS philosophy is its embrace of diversity. Whether it's racial, special needs or any other aspect of diversity, PNHS both includes and embraces it. Our kids learned a level of tolerance and inclusiveness that outstrips most other West County high schools.We have friends in most of the other West County schools and districts and wouldn't trade our kids' experiences for any other school. My wife and I send both of our children to Parkway North and have found there experience to be excellent. Both are well adjusted, socially responsible adults. We found them well prepared and as a result excelled in challenging fields at challenging top universities with advanced degrees which one child finishing doctorate work in the STEM field. North was able to provide them the foundation, faculty support, and resources to push themselves in athletics and in academics. Its friendly,challenging and offers many good electives for many interests you might have. Plus a great classes if you are smart. I feel prepared for college. My children loved this school so much. They both graduated and are now going to good colleges. Teachers are good and effective, students are nice and welcoming. The school challenged their academic abilities and helped them greatly.

column3: If you're a student considering transferring to KPHS, or you're a parent looking for a school suitable for your children, I highly recommend looking elsewhere. To be quite frank, the administration here is downright poor. Their decisions frequently put students in danger, e.g. refusing to close school the morning of a 6" snow when road conditions are awful (we only missed one school day for Nemo, and that's only because the governor instituted a road ban), not closing school during gas leaks (they happen a little too frequently for comfort), keeping school open when the ceilings schoolwide are blatantly leaking (a sign of possible roof-collapse), etc. It's actually quite comical, and the teachers will frequently note this. Their elevator is coming up on 6 months since the expiration date, and it's still used frequently. The 7-period a day schedule is a far-cry from being "college preparatory," and it ends up increasing workload while decreasing learning. I'm not some disgruntled student writing a review about how X teacher is a jerk, I'm a high school senior who's been to several high schools who can offer some insight. This school has it's plusses, but the cons far outweigh them. Very pleased with King Philip. Teachers that really care about our children, an energetic, involved principal, and plenty for all to do whether an athlete or a musician. Colleges must think highly of this school system as from my own experience and from what I hear from others, students are accepted at a wide range of colleges/universities. Many AP courses are offered as well. Like any school, it's all about making the most of it Soon many extra curricular activities, many many AP courses, top notch music program and the sports teams have been doing great with State Champions or runners up. Large number of students is the only negative and three towns need to approve the budget.....underfunded by all three towns... For the per pupil expediter, KP high is tops.! I've had 4 children go through the KP Regional system. They are thriving, independent members of society now all in their twenties. They developed life long friendships, the ability to think critically , compassion for classmates, and the drive to ever excel. The teachers here give a lot of extra time providing all students with a superior academic and extra-curricular experience...... the school sucks if you're not an athlete.

I came to MillCreek High as a new student and I have to say that the rest of the student reviews really scared me. I have moved schools a lot through out the years and I have to say that mill creek has been a wonderful experience! Every person that I have met this year is incredibly kind and welcoming! Everyone was raised right. There is no bullying or cliques in this school. Not only because it's against school rules but because the kids at this school are kind and make it that way! Great great experience! because this school is actually horrible and no one cares I disagree with the parents saying you buy your way in to the athletic program; I have not found that to be the case at all. She struggled a bit at first, but the teachers have been wonderful helping her adjust to high school. Love my Mill Creek Family, my son is a sophomore and loves it there so far! Mill Creek has really prepared him for college and challenged him scholastically. Lots of AP classes to choose from. Very happy with the whole experience.

column1: My husband is a graduate and our son will graduate in 2011. We have thoroughly appreciated the academic and co-curricular exposure that our son has received at DeMatha. The principal is outstanding. The facilities are expanding. The academic program provides options for students to excel academically and prepare for college. If your son is a sports enthusiast, DeMatha offers so much as an athelete and a 'fan'. Great school spirit. Great relationships with colleges and universities. We wouldn't change a thing. DeMatha is an academically rigorous school with a top music program and strong athletics. My bright, artsy senior has enjoyed excellent teachers and a very accepting environment where racism isn't a problem and gay students are fully accepted. The academics are tailored to your son's abilities-top students here are comparable with any in the country. Less academically gifted kids are valued but are not given such challenging work. These boys are proud of their school and smile so warmly when they win another gold medal at a music festival or WCAC championship or an Ivy league acceptance letter. Dematha is horrible. Very Very racist. They just want your money. Black kids do not get the same educational opportunities as white students. You don't see this until you have to pay full tution and try to switch your son's clases. Two sons attended the school. The one weaker academically did the best at DM, but he was good at sports and was put into classes with easier teachers. If you are not in honors clases you are bette off in public school. The oldest one still had to go to prep school because he was not academically prpeared for college. I am currently enrolled at DeMatha and love it. The all boys was the biggest drawback for me when deciding. I quickly realize how much more learning you get done here then a co ed school.Also the tution easily the best for the Catholic schools in the D.C area. It is about 13,000 wich sounds like alot until you look at the other which seem to be 20,000+ to go to. Dematha also Is the best Acadimicly Athletics Community service and religon.Don't belive me go ask someone who goes there or someone who has heard of it. It is a Catholic school so The who "gay" thing was silly considering what catholics belive. Also I have yet to see the same sex relationship here. Another thing I noticed was how well the teachers taught and helped. Before Dematha I went to A public school wich was great but was a joke compared to the acadimics to DeMmtha.Another Drawback was that it was a religon school. I also realized that long as your christan and follow simalir belifs they dont care what religon you are. The last thing that i will add is that the kids in the school are not rich spoiled kids but gentelman who will help you out anytime.Overall Dematha is Excellent and helps when you go to college/job. There are 38,000 high schools in America, but there is only One DeMatha. I'm an alumnus as well as a parent of two current students. We're not a sports family. It's great and fun to see your school's name prominently featured in national publications, but it isn't what's been important for our family. For those who are thinking about where to send their sons to high school, DeMatha's most important attribute is that it is a school for 950 individual students. Each student's needs - academic, social, psychological - are considered on an individual basis. Teachers, counselors - and the principal - often take significant amounts of time to work out the curricular and other needs of the individual student. The individual needs of our sons have often been considered and factored into their curricular opportunities, including permission to take classes normally reserved for higher grade levels and independent study courses. We homeschooled our sons through eighth grade, and the thing that we like most about DeMatha is how it retains much of the spirit of homeschooling - making the school fit the student rather than the student being made to fit the school. I have had 2 sons graduate from DeMatha. Each was as different as night and day; the oldest is not as strong academically as the youngest, yet outgoing and sociable. Neither did the Sports thing. As African Americans, we ended up paying the full tuition ourselves, knowing that if they had been athletes, we might have been offered some help. The work ethic, tradition & academic rigors are noteworthy. The culture is a bit off-putting; it feels like a lower-end Country Club that exposes itself to minority enrollment for quota purposes. All that aside, if you can afford the pricetag & ready for intense involvement, with a serious young man who wants a good start, go check it out. Shadowing is an excellent idea, but don't just send your son. Go yourself, attend the parent association meetings, walk the campus at varying times. You'll Know whether it's the right place for your guys or not. This is one place where you really need to do YOUR homework even before your son starts doing his own! Love this for my son! He chose this school for its name sake and mission of St. John DeMatha - a crusader who believed in the most Holy Trinity and power of the spirit overcoming all. We loved this school! As a white family not originally from Maryland we were told by EVERYONE that this was an african-american sports school with a catholic name. I was concerned. Smaller population of Catholics than I had anticipated, but what is wrong with that? My son and the leaders of this school take every opportunity to promote behavior suitable to God. The non-catholic population which were overly critical and negative about the mass and catholocism quickly learned from the Catholics that although they may disagree the Catholic faith is still a religion and faith deserving of respect. Academics are WONDERFUL! Great science program, excellent math, love the electives (CADD is my fave and very unique), foreign language options are unreal, campus ministry program is wonderful, the social sciences and studies do a great job. Each of these teachers has mastered the education of GENTLEMEN! I am a single parent and this is worth the cost. But the sports are all POLITICS! Very poor. We thought this would be an academically and spiritually nurturing place for our son and we were gravely mistaken. It was a very expensive learning experience.

I graduated from Beacon this June and wanted to share some of my experiences/insights. Teacher quality at Beacon is spotty for such a well respected place. Overall I have had more awful teachers here than great ones. As a freshman, there is little support and guidance, however I know there have been recent efforts to improve upon this through summer bridge and big sibs. In my experience the advisory program has been useless and a waste of time, that said other students were luckier with this. Academically, Beacon does have an innovative approach to learning. Students have the ability to select a lot of unique classes and their college program with Fordham is fantastic. However, the classics are entirely neglected (we never once read a Greek tragedy and only read one Shakespeare play) and the lack of textbooks/regents can give teachers an excuse to teach irrelevant course material. Socially, Beacon is home to a lot of hipsters and brooklyn artsy types and drugs and partying are rampant. I would not recommend Beacon for anyone who is not incredibly self-motivated. If you are not, it is just far too easy to slip through the cracks here, academically and otherwise. My daughter is a sophomore at beacon this year and she loves it but I'm not sure I do. I'm not sure I love her friends. She comes home after a late night of partying each night with the scent of cigarettes and other bad things. She learns a lot at beacon but I'm afraid her bad habits will interfere with that :( Beacon is fantastic for the right student - but this is true everywhere, no? My child went to an elite private school from pre-school through 8th grade (the private schools is one of the most difficult to get into in NYC, crammed with celebs & movers & shakers) & Beacon's teachers are, at minimum, 100% better - many 1000% better - than the teachers he had. Yes, Beacon's crowded, yes there are kids who smoke everything & do everything, get high during the day etc etc - but that's true EVERYWHERE. It's all about the teachers - the athletic teams (hello, the tennis program is insanely good - best in NYC public or private) - the theater program BDAT. The one area the school sucks in is the college office. Beacon doesn't seem to care AT ALL about getting their kids into top-ranked colleges. That's kind of refreshing in the world of college hysteria but if your child wants to go to a top 50 school you have to make that happen yourself. Beacon will not help you. You need to hire a college counselor, tutors, do research, talk to people etc. In every other way, this school is amazing. But you and your child have to get involved, be part of the community, and support the teachers! when I first came to beacon, I loved it. I met new great friends and most of the teachers are amazing and care about you. it is a little over crowded but they are moving to a new building in like a year or so. It feels like home, and I don't associate with the crazy party goers, but overall beacon is great Beacon is a really good school. The kids are highly engaged in academics and extracurriculars, and overall teacher quality is strong. That said, there are some real stars and a few duds, but by and large nearly all really appreciate and understand how to work wit the bright, creative teenagers that go to Beacon. Coursework in the humanities is quite rigorous -no need for AP English or History because they are already teaching at college level. Math and science (at least in 9th and 10th grade, and even for students in accelerated math) is not as rigorous as it could be. We are hoping for more demanding courses in the upper grades. Yes, there are plenty of kids who party, but I don't think the scene is atypical of nyc high schools that draw a substantial middle class crowd- and there are plenty of kids at Beacon who don't smoke or drink. On balance, we are very pleased with our choice and are confident that our daughter will be well-prepared for a demanding college program. prepare to feel heavily alienated if you don't live in manhattan and your family is below middle-class Our son entered Beacon recently as a freshman and is having a very favorable experience thus far. He knew no other students upon arrival but has quickly felt at home and made many new friends. The workload is heavier some evenings (3+ hours) than his fairly rigorous middle school -- but the assignments are generally interesting. Teachers are available for students to consult for extra support as needed and there is a genuine feeling that teachers, advisors and coordinators really care and want the students to succeed. Additionally there is a "big sib" program which provides "sponsorship" of each advisory group by two senior mentors. There is a wide range of extra-curricular activities for students and there are meaningful avenues for parents to get/stay engaged as well. We are so happy to have found a good fit and it is wonderful to see how comfortable our son is already and how good the academics seem to be. He is working hard but really enjoying the experience. This school was well worth every step of the application process. It is clear why it is so well-regarded. This is the second year for my son at Beacon. He is a sophomore now and he can not be happier to be part of this school. I love that the school focuses on preparing kids for University with the type of projects they receive. Teachers are great, the communication between the school and parents is fantastic. The only thing I would like the school to consider is to integrate all classes into engrade, this way is easier for us parents to keep track of our kids progress and be more supportive. Overall I am very satisfied and happy with the school experience and my son's performance so far. This encapsulates how I feel about Beacon: I have two daughters, one a Beacon senior, one currently in 9th grade. Last year, while my Younger was applying to schools, we were subtly steering her towards private school, because we find Beacon to be chaotic (tricky, because we didn't want to make Older feel bad about her school, which she likes). Not knowing if Younger would get into any of these privates, we hoped to secure a spot at Beacon, just in case. I was all over each daughter's application and I can tell you, they were the same: same school, same grades, strong portfolios, same test scores, same! I let Beacon know Younger was a sib, my Older told a few teachers as well, Younger ranked Beacon as her first choice and guess what? Rejected! Guess what else? The majority of girl applicants from her small, private K-8 were accepted, making the rejection more humiliating & baffling. How do you explain this to a 13 year old ? Older is a great student, nice kid and just got in ED to a top, top college, so it's not like she ruined it for Younger. Finally, we had been "good" parents, donating money and volunteering, There's no explaining it -- just chaos. That's Beacon. Beacon is not all it is cracked up to be. Overcrowded, overworked staff and it is hard to find any personalized attention. Leadership is focused on helping the ones that are doing very well do better and turns its head on those who are struggling. Drug and alcohol issues that the school turns a blind eye to. I have two kids who have been at Beacon, one graduated last year and is attending a top college (was accepted almost everywhere applied), and my other child is currently in 10th grade. Yes its overcrowded and not every issue is handled perfectly, but both kids were stimulated, worked hard for their teachers, and excelled at their academics. There is drug and alcohol use at every school, its not about sanitizing their environment but raising your kids to make good decisions - No school is perfect, they both came from private school to Beacon - paying money does not guarantee that the kinks get ironed out. You will never meet a group of more committed teachers than at Beacon, and Ms. Lacey is hands-on active. Couldn't be happier with our choice - feel like we won the academic lottery. Awesome school! We have been so happy with our experience at Beacon. As another parent wrote, we really feel like we hit the jackpot. This school is sought after for good reason. The students are provided with challenging/interesting work and are taught to think critically and to express themselves clearly. The advisors and administrators are very committed and the teachers are generally top notch and supportive of student success. Our son has found no shortage of really terrific classmates with whom to spend time and the friends he has made have his same good judgment and enthusiasm for learning. The music program is absolutely amazing and the wide range of sports and extra-curricular provide multiple great choices for nearly everyone. We recognize the school is crowded (but will be in a brand new and spacious location for the second half of our time there) and as with every school, is not right for everyone. It clearly is a good fit for motivated, well-rounded students who really want to learn. There are countless opportunities to lend value as a parent and the school has good communications with parents. This is a high quality high school. I transferred my son out of Beacon this summer. He was bullied and I did not feel that the administration took it seriously. The bullier had a previous record of this beaviour and they allowed him to continue at the school. His student advisor was not once of his teachers and when I told her that my son was having problems adjusting she gave us a pep talk about how great the school is. She couldn't even pronounce my son's name. I know that this school has a great reputation and it is why we put it as a first choice on the high school application but it clearly is not for everyone. Beacon is highly overrated and gets by on reputation but does very little to maintain quality. The teachers are unresponsive and the administration is beyond unhelpful. If you do not have money, do not expect to feel comfortable or welcome at the school. I am in education and have been involved in many schools both as a parent and as an educator and I can tell you that the fact that only 42% of the teachers find the principal effective is not something to be taken lightly. From the top down there is little sense of caring or warmth. My son is a junior at the school and if I could undo this decision, I would. My other child did not even put it on the list. My son is a good student and has made friends and done fine academically, but there are so many places where your child will not just get by but thrive. Keep looking! Extremely liberal school that makes traditional students afraid to speak openly, and in fact, go to great lengths to hide their opinion. Sadly, most schools today are like that. Extremely liberal school that makes traditional students afraid to speak openly, and in fact, go to great lengths to hide their opinion. Sadly, most schools today are like that. Great school! Teachers are great, students are smart As a parent of a Special Education student i would not recommend this school. One of the reasons we chose Beacon is their false claims of being supportive and providing necessary supports and resources. Unfortunately, the school has not adhered to the IEP, services or accomodations. The school has not scheduled an IEP meeting or done any assessments. Overall communication is the worst I've ever seen in a school. Phones are usually unanswered, emails not returned and parents are left in the dark completely. While there are some good teachers and quality education, administration is completely disorganized with no accountibility. The principal has never responded to any email. I would look elsewhere if you have an IEP and want your child to receive required services. Beacon does not take the regents, therefore our test scores on this website (3/10) are completely inaccurate. We reach finals for the PSAT every year, and do great on the SAT/ACT. This is not a test-taking school; we focus on writing skills and how to be a better student overall. This is a wonderful school, with smart and engaging teachers.

column1: This school has a horrible mathematics program. Students here should be encouraged to forgo taking math courses here, and take them in college instead. A few of the religious members of the students and faculty do not respect the non-Catholic or atheist students. If you want your child to grow in faith, do not send them here. The only two ways that your child's faith will be altered is in the closing of their mind, or in making them atheist or severely doubt the existence of a God (happened to me and a lot of others). We knew we made the right high school choice when our college-aged children came home and thanked us for the education they got at PCHS! They were amazed at how far ahead of their classmates they were in research and writing skills, as well as in science and mathematics! PCHS is one of the most accepting, loving and nurturing environment you will find. All students are accepted for who they are and treated the same. All students are given the same opportunities and chances to succeed. The new principal (principal for 4 years now) is great and the school is growing. With students from all faith denominations represented, PC remains a school rooted deep in Catholicism that offers all its students a stellar education. Peninsula Catholic is a college preparatory school whose students have found success beyond their high school years thanks to a strong foundation and high expectations. We are proud of our Catholic roots, but warmly welcome students from all faith traditions. We are a school dedicated to service in the local community, nation-wide, and across the globe. Last year, just over 300 students committed over 11,000 service hours and over $12,000 to those in need. Our parents choose Peninsula Catholic because they are prepared to invest in their student s future, even if it means financial sacrifice. PC has a student body that is readily accepting of others and ready to help each other in any way they can. The faculty is dedicated to their students in the classroom and through their invovement with many extra-curricular activities. Each year the administration strives to incorporate new programs and enhance the current offerings so that students have the best chance of success once they leave the halls of PC. There is no doubt that Peninsula Catholic is the finest private school on the peninsula and I am proud to be a part of this long-standing (108 year) tradition. My son has been at this school for two years now and I am happy I made the decision to send him here. The school climate is one that encourages leadership from all students. They are very accepting of individuality. The students are very supportive of each other. I have heard many students and parents as describing the school as feeling like family. Peninsula Catholic High School has been our 5 sons' 2nd 'home' since 1999. Its the school of our choice because it is academically outstanding and for its Catholic 'environment' which produces good men and women. Our family is honored to be part of Peninsula Catholic's tradition of excellence in all aspects of life!!! Both of our children attended Peninsula Catholic High School . For us, Peninsula Catholic was kind of a mixed bag. From an academic perspective, I would say that their English program was excellent; their math and science programs, however, were just okay. From a spiritual perspective, PC was disappointing. For the most part, the spiritual emphasis tended to be mostly on teaching the students about religion (rules, memorization of religious facts, etc.) and a lot of spiritual "going through the motions," rather than encouraging students to have a relationship with God and to live their faith. Both of my children were put off by the religious instruction at Peninsula Catholic and turned their backs on Catholicism before they finished at PC. To be fair, there was one religion teacher at PC who really did try to nurture his students' faith, rather than just teach them about "religion". Unfortunately, both of my children were in their last year at PC by the time they had his class, and by that time it was, as they put it, "too late." Peninsula Catholic High School is an outstanding school. My son has always struggled in school, but he is doing above average since his move to PC. The teachers make themselves available to help the students succeed. The students love the school...because they have fun! It's not free like public school, but you get what you pay for. Invest in your children's future, they are worth it. this school has been wonderful for our boys. College prep is stressed, but every student feels like they have a say in the high school journey. The school has discipline and actions, enough to give students boundaries, such as hair length, skirt length, honor codes etc.. Active athletic programs keeps kids busy after school as do many after school clubs. A bus comes from Resurrection Church in Portsmouth for help with transportation. PCHS is making great strides to take what has always been a wonderful school and improve it to the SPECTACULAR! Much needed additions to the athletic fields and the recent addition of a 9-10th grade guidance councilor are all outward signs of this tremendous growth. The teachers are warm and actually care about the education and well-being of the students and the Principal is always open and available for parents and students. Last year, my student was given a chromebook and had numerous opportunities to use it in class, opening a world of learning that would not be possible before. I am so proud to call the school home for my children! I would not recommend attending PC, the only good thing about the school is the English department and Cross Country program. Almost all the teachers are close-minded and only choose to teach their opinions. The religion in the school is less focused on spiritual and values and more focused on shoving it down your throat and condemning sinners. It makes most of the students that attend turn away from the faith. The teachers will pick favorites and make those favorites very evident. Peninsula Catholic truly prepares kids for the future emotionally, intellectually, and spiritually. The kids, teachers, and staff are top notch! Best private school in Hampton Roads and affordable too. I have many wonderful experiences with this school. I absolutely love the experience my child is having there. I would give it 5 stars however we had a situation with the guidance councilor in 9th grade that was difficult. It has been resolved but still remains an experience we had Peninsula Catholic is a wonderful school. The teachers and administration really care about the students. The teachers want each student to succeed. There are plenty of extracurricular activities. I like that my son can be involved in multiple sports and not have to train year round just to be on a team. The block schedule (4 classes a day as opposed to A/B days) really keeps things simple and allows students to really focus on subjects. Also, the technology at PC really is amazing. For example, everyone has a chrome book that they are able to use in class. The math classes have the latest computerized programs that provide extra support to students. Finally, PC uses CANVAS as their learning management system - one of the best LMS around - used by colleges and universities. Also, the religious atmosphere provides the backdrop to the whole school - with the emphasis on the shared values of kindness, honesty, integrity, etc. This is a school that any student can succeed in and it provides much more than academics. Can you tell I LOVE this school?! This school has offered quality education since 1903. It has a 100% graduation rate as well as a 100% college acceptance rate. The matriculation rate is nearly 100%. PC is a Google Apps for Education High School. The school was the first in the Hampton Roads area to implement the 1:1 Chromebook Initiative with all students. There is a full time chef on staff preparing meals from scratch daily. The curriculum is demanding but prepares the students for college. PC is the "home" I was hoping to find for my child when she started high school. After several moves and school changes, she started at PC and has found a community of great friends, dedicated teachers, and plenty of activities. For me as a parent, the community of involved families here was very welcoming. The success of the students here (over 1/3 of this year's seniors are attending either UVA, William and Mary, or Virginia Tech next fall) and the overall positive experience my child has had so far make me confident that she is in the right place. Peninsula Catholic provides a quality education for an extremely affordable cost. It boasts a 100% college acceptance rate with many students earning college credits from Dual Enrollment classes. The school is on the cutting edge of technology with their 1:1 Chromebook Initiative and the new Long Distance Learning Lab. The fields expansion from a few years ago has enabled the teams to practice and play "in house" I have only good things to say about PCHS! The academics are rigorous yet the teachers approachable and helpful; the extracurricular activities, from athletics to fine arts, are exceptional and inclusive; and, the school community, from students to staff, is friendly and accepting. There are many ways that parents can be involved, which is encouraged by the teachers and school administration. PCHS is exceptional and worth every penny spent ; which, dollar for dollar is not expensive with the multitude of scholarships and incentives available. We've had children in both public and private schools, and I rank Peninsula Catholic High School well above all the schools in the area. Peninsula Catholic is a fairly average school, although it advertises itself as much greater than it really is. It has it's fair share of problems like any other school, although this is my personal experience with it. Students are spoken to every year about bullying, but little justice is actually done. There are giant cliques within the school, and if you aren't apart of one of them, then you are an easy target. Often times there are students who don't quite fit in, and they face bullying because of it. Worst of all, these bullies manipulate staff and faculty members into thinking that they are genuine people. They will take someone's slip up, or mistakes, and use it against their victims if the victim ever tells anyone, and faculty is typically more inclined to believe in the bully, considering they are polite and respectful to the employees. This should NOT determine whether someone is deemed a bully or not. Teachers pick favorites, and that is fairly obvious, not to mention how close minded some teachers can be. IF a student does not understand course material, perhaps it is not entirely their fault, sometimes teachers need to take into account that not all students learn the same ways. Drugs and partying are also a problem, and while faculty/staff has little to no jurisdiction outside of school, they should be aware of this, and help to encourage students to make better decisions. Then there is the religious aspect of the school. PC is NOT the religious environment I would want a child of mine to be in, considering I didn't enjoy it either. Students are forced to learn about religion, and while this is a CATHOLIC school, I don't believe that forcing a religious class on students is the best way to go about deepening a students faith. Students who are not particularly religious, or Catholic at the least, tend to be disruptive in these classes, and it stops students - who actually care about Theology - from learning more about their faith. This forced religious practice also turns away potential Catholics, or people just simply looking to have *A* faith. PC is also bias against just about any sport aside from x-country, and focuses a lot of effort into "glorifying" these athletes, and leaving out other potential programs, such as the drama department. There is so much to say about PC, but point being, it has its flaws. It is not as perfect as advertised.

column3: The worst experience fir my sons in this district and both schools Jefferson and Kennedy I would rate it a 10 out of 10. My son has been challenged academically and treated fairly. He feels safe and secure while he's there and feels like the teachers and administrators have his back and are pulling for him. I can't ask for more than that. I wish private school had been a financial option. Will be elated when my child escapes this school. One son at Jefferson and one son in private school... No comparison. Jefferson is a disaster.

column1: As a student who just recently graduated from this school, I would recommend you avoid it if you wish your children to have an edge in college. I was in the top 20% of my class, yet upon getting to college I felt woefully under prepared. Most of the upper level teachers genuinely care about the success of their students, but they are burdened by having to stop and teach students stuff they were supposed to know before getting to that level. The biggest thing that worries me is the standing tradition of allowing students to walk at graduation when they technically aren't graduating. Students are allowed to walk even if they don't have the required number of credits and/or haven't passed the required classes. This should send up a major red flag that this school doesn't care about your education, but the money you bring to the school. I went to this school when I was younger and utterly hated it. Me and my sister were hispanic and constantly got picked on. Often I was physically abused by other kids my grade and even by the highschool level kids. The worst was that the staff did nothing about it or blamed it on me and tried to get me expelled. If you have any color in your skin, this school is one of the worst places you can go. West Washington is a great school to send your children. Your child will learn and grow. West Washington has a caring community of loving teachers and staff. We are excited about the future of West Washington. There is an up and coming technology program. This will allow are children cutting edge technology along with the skills that will allow them an upper hand in society. I am very comfortable sending my children to West Washington to learn. It is as safe and loving place! Campbellsburg, Indiana is home to West Washington Jr/Sr High School-home of the Senators. Like many very rural schools in Indiana and across the country, this school is more like a second family to many students and a central hub for community activities and events. The teachers and staff of WWHS work hard to make sure the school receives the high marks from state testing and accreditation boards that the school currently has to it's credit! Additionally, the adults of the building KNOW the students, the student's families and many of these connections are what help make this school so strong. The school offers dual credit opportunities as well as vocational subjects that provide training in specific areas of trade and industry. Some of these vocational programs are recognized across the state and nation as being outstanding programs and opportunities for the enrolled students. For example, the West Washington Agriculture Department/FFA Chapter is a perfect example. The students in this area develop life skills that certainly help them now, but will prove to be more beneficial later on in a career setting. Students learn about service to others while growing themselves. I am extremely happy to have my daughter in the 7th grade at West Washington. The rigor of the curriculum has increased, the students have access to technology and the teachers and staff are helpful and friendly. My daughter is excited that next year she will have her own Chromebook, and loves the number of club and athletic offerings. the staff is wonderful, supportive and caring and encourages the kids to learn and excel I am proud to say that I teach at West Washington High School. Currently I am blessed to serve in the role of Agriculture Science/Business Instructor and FFA Advisor. There are few schools that are situated in the setting that WW is, in the country with corn/soybeans growing on all sides depending on the rotational year. Obviously, the surroundings are conducive to my subject area as is the community in general with exposure to production agriculture, but one thing that really makes WW unique is the amount of pride and support that comes from the community members and parents alike. Being a rural school the impression may be that opportunities available to students to learn and grow as young people might be limited; however, that is false! WW has many amazing teachers who help make school feel like family in classes that challenge students-many classes are dual credit opportunities, program and club options that are state and nationally recognized-like our FFA chapter, and athletic teams that witness firsthand that "community pride" during the season. All this, plus the school is embracing 1:1 technology. Now, does this sound like a rural school with limitations for students? A dedicated, educational, fun, caring & loving school Corp. Once a Senator always a SENATOR. Where you are a person not a number. Ours is a warm caring school environment where we take a personal interest in the success of each of our students. We are employing the latest technology to ensure that our students are prepared for the 21st century workforce. We have outstanding Vocational training in Building Trades, Health Careers, and Technology, including a new radio and television studio. I like our school because it is out in the middle of nowhere.It is also very small compared to most school. My school is okay. The lockers are old and beat up. The desks are squeaky and usually have gum or something else stuck underneath them. Our text books have drawings on them, and the Chromebooks hardly work, because of the internet. The hand driers in the bathroom don't work at all., meaning they don't dry your hands or heat up. The gyms are nice and the school stays pretty clean. Also, the cafeteria and lobby are really nice. I think our school is very well set up. It has many challenges and things we can do for fun. There are a lot of freedoms. Then again there are also some discipline if you don't do what you told. I love this school! It is the best one yet, and I wouldn't go anywhere else if I had the chance to because this school has become home for me and it is a lot better than other schools. West Washington is a great school. We have amazing technology for learning, great teachers, and students who are ready to learn. The food at our school isn't that great. On one side of the cafeteria, we have regular, more healthy food, and on the other side, people order the "Senator Burger," Arby's fries, and other less healthy food. Every other Friday, we eat Domino's Pizza. During lunch, we are allowed to go to the gymnasium to play basketball, walk, or socialize with our friends. Our school is considered "a bully free zone," which means bullying isn't permitted. If students don't complete their assignments, they can either get lunch detention or work release. Work release is one of the best things our school has created. It forces students with incomplete assignments to go to the cafeteria until their work is finished. This helps with their grades, so they don't automatically get an "F." West Washington is a pretty great school. I feel the lunch could be much better but other than that its pretty awesome here. its great! I really like it here, it is the best school in the world My school is a great school there is so many great students and teachers they all make me fit in on my first day of being at this school I loved it. The sports are fun. The teachers work with you on more of a one on one level. My school is great. I know the teachers and staff work hard to do what's right for us. I never realized it before, until last night. My stepmom was talking about moving and I suddenly got so sad. Everyone at West Washington is close. Everyone knows everyone. Everyone is like a family. The teachers are understanding, too. They're all friendly and help you when you need it. West Washington is like a home to me and many others. It's a great school who truly cares about it's students. For the most part, I go to a great school. The faculty and staff cares for the students and all of the students are kind and loving. The only two things I would change are school spirit and teaching techniques. I wish there were more people at my school with spirit. I would love to cheer to a full student section. I don't agree with a lot of the teaching techniques. Some teachers are really great and help you understand the lesson, but others treat you like you are inferior. Nothing upsets me more than when I don't understand a problem and a teacher tells me to figure it out on my own. That's what they are here for! Thank you, Lakin Jones. Our school is like a huge family. The teachers, administration, and staff truly care about the students. We are always working hard to do what is best for them. I don't think you could find a more caring group of educators anywhere. West Washington is a great school, although the student body doesn't uphold all that the school's supposed to, such as being LGBT-friendly. There aren't many, but there are a few students that aren't friendly towards LGBT students. My only problem is that a decent amount of the student body uses terms such as "gay" and "homo" as insults, which is just plain rude as they were not insults to begin with. Other than that, West Washington Jr./Sr. High School is a wonderful educational facility with good opportunities for many.

column3: Roosevelt High School is a metropolitan high school in Chicago, Illinois. The demographics of the school are diverse. There are currently 33 languages being spoken at RHS, with a range of ESL learners needing limited support in English language to brand-new American immigrants with no English facility. This makes for an interesting and challenging learning community for all concerned. As with many schools in the United States, RHS enjoys a staff of administrators and teachers who are highly motivated and dedicated. The leadership is open and willing to accept constructive criticism, and work within the Chicago Public Schools policies and procedures to implement positive change. I would highly recommend Roosevelt High School for consideration as a recipient of your $5,000 grant. Very pleased! The number ratings on this site are very inaccurate. It should be rated much higher than it is.

column1: This school is located on a small island known for its alcohol and drug use. The kids here have no outlets other than hanging at the beach and partying. While its not the school's fault, this is not a great place for your kids. My son has gone to Port Aransas schools since 1st grade and he has excelled in everything. He is now in HS and is taking all AP and Honors courses and the teachers are great!! The High School and Elementary got a commended rating and that is the best you can get! I highly recommend this school and town to anyone. There is minimal alcohol abuse and not much drug use. The good thing is, as small as this community is if there is a problem you as a parent know about it before it happens twice! We love it here! All of our children are enjoying the schools in Port Aransas. We have lived in several different places and the schools here are the best we've seen. The intesisty of the curriculm is balanced well with the warmth of this great community. Parents, teachers and administrators work well together and the community as a whole comes together to supports families and children in an ideal way.

column3: Excellent teachers, as well good school environment.. I attend this school for 3 years and I personally love this school, my counselor took time to help me get the best classes I needed. Most of teachers took extra time to help me when I needed. And they well prepare me for college. I personally thank Mr Urquiza, Mr Downson, Mrs Rodriguez, Mrs Chaves, and Mrs Garcia for all there help and support. I am a senior at West Valley, and I have to say, the school is awesome. Many of the teachers are very helpful, there are a few bad eggs though, I will not go into specifics, but one gave me a D-(and an F on a test, which I have never once in my life received) and the other gave me an F, forcing me to re-take English, even though I was the only student in any of her classes to receive an A on all of her tests and get High advanced on the CST. Besides that, most of the counselors are willing to help, especially with a parent involved, the campus is safe and clean. The drama and arts departments are stunning! Mrs. Bailey is a tough person, but an excellent drama teacher/director. Special ed staff needs more training in my opinion. I am currently not impressed with their special ed staff and looking for another educational alternative for my child. I don't feel good with my daughter at this school so looking for different location.

column1: this school has shown so much religious discrimination to us by denying admission for my child , just b'coz we both follow a different religion. just by saying that it is clear that this school is promoting the idea of religious discrimination in the mind of innocent , young kids, which would not be nice in their future All my children have attended Harvest Prep and have had a quality education. They have gone on to college and excelled academically and spiritually. I am the new principal at HPS (started in Sep 2011). We are excited about the changes that are taking place at HPS. We are renewing our focus on superior quality academics and outstanding school culture. We are proud of our facilities and our Christian-centered environment. Our athletic teams are competitive but academic success comes first. We are a college preparatory school that believes that all students can learn. Please come and take a look to see if we can serve your children. This school has really lowered their standards. It was a great school before (years ago) however I would consider it average, if was a public school. I expected better for a private school, save your money or pick another Christian school. One daughter has been attending Harvest Prep for 4 years and my other daughter and son for two years. I am well please with the school. The school has an on-line program where I am able to monitor her progress daily. The teachers and administrators are diligent to communicate via e-mail. Whenever problems have risen, as they do in all school, they have been addresses immediately. I am a very involved parent so knowing my childs progress and well-being is very important. Also, having them in a Christian enviroment has helped me tremendously. Just the other day, my son was doing his homework for bible class. It was to write a few verses about what the bible says about him. He said that he was God's handiworK. I cannot tell you what joy it brings to my heart. And by the way, I don't think I have mentioned that all three kids are in the honor roll. I would highly recommend this school to anyone. My son has been going to this school for two years now, and from what I see it is a pretty good school. He's only in the first grade, so i don't know what might be the problem with the older students. I do however know that compared to our home school it excels. My son is learning a lot and loves this school. I think the problems I have with it are not being able to go to the classroom and having to wait in a single pickup lane for car riders. They say it's for security. I gave this school 5 stars because my daughter has been attending for the past 2 years and has had some of the greatest teachers that I'll ever know. She has learned so much being there including Spanish in Kindergarden and the phonics program they have set up is awesome. My 5 year old can read above her education level and I enjoy the extracirricular activities they have set-up for the children during the school year and after school. The Christian based atmosphere is wonderfully given through the staff through enstiling worship and faith in God and Jesus Christ. My daughter teaches me things about the Lord that I my self never knew. We are glad that we chose to send our child to HPS. Our child has attended HPS since Kindergarten and is currently in Second Grade. Along with getting an excellent education, our child is learning to be a spiritual servant of God Almighty! Our child's teachers are attentive and readily work with students and parents. We receive daily reports of our child's work and behavior. The leadership is caring and structured. HPS is involved with the community and places a strong emphasis on giving/helping others. HPS provides many extracurricular opportunities for their students - band, sports, clubs, and community outreach. Go Warriors! My son began at HPS at 3yrs old in the Pre-K program and is currently in kindergarten! We have had a great experience here and God willing he will continue here through 12th grade graduation. The staff has been exceptionally wonderful to me and my family. I have been able to have direct contact with my childs teachers, which I truly love because I am a very active parent. We love HPS, and you and your family will too! I encourage you to visit the school, tour, and most importantly pray about it and see where the Lord directs you. We are blessed to have our child in this school. Wonderful, caring teachers. Always there to help in any way the can. Excellent education. :) This school was the last option for our son which is a Junior this year. His previous school was bias towards certain cultures and the teachers showed no encouragement nor compassion for what he and us as his parents were going through!. I will not list the name of the school, but; our sons previous school made him and us miserable. Harvest Prep has given our son his confience back and he is excelling in his classes. We love this school so much that myself (mom) wish I could re-enroll in high school so I could get the academic and spiritiual experience that I myself was not influenced with when I was growing up. In our opinion if their is a child that is attending public school, and the parents are not pleased with their children's outcome then I would encourage them to seek Harvest Prep. The administration, teachers and financial aid office are caring and compassionate in your child's learning and walking in a Christian lifestyle. We love it there and I wish I would have made the move a year sooner! My oldest daughter went her when she was 3 and 4 an we moved away. She is now 13 and I have a 6 year old. This is our first year back at HPS and I love it!! My kids love going to school and the environment is wonderful for spiritual growth as well as educational growth. The year has just begun and my 8th grader as done awesome. She hand my first grader has made honor roll and I am so proud. They want to come to school and don't want to miss a day. I have gotten to know the staff and I can say I love them. My kids are involved in many school activities and I giving HPS nothing but accolades on how they work with the students as well as the family's that walk through the doors. My school is Harvest Prep. They have a great school with excellent teachers. I would agree with most of you that the past for HPS has been bad. But not as bad as everyone thinks. But a lot of things have changed in the past 3 years. And you really wouldn't know of the improvements and changes that have occurred and made HPS better unless you are inside, or willing to listen and be open minded to the truth. They graduate 95% of the students and 92% of them graduate from college. That's impressive facts. The administration there is really student friendly and have helped in the change for a better future and a school that kids want to come to. Mr. Dennis and Mr. Mills is exactly what the school needs and what the students love. I hope they never leave or get fired. The discipline has improved and the education has taken a serious turn to where they are definitely ready for college. And, it's a Christian base school. Not over doing it, but enough to allow the kids to make a decision on their faith and trust in God My daughter has been going to HPS for 4years. And she has grew spiritual as well educationally. Even thought EVERY schools has issues. I wouldn't have my daughter anywhere else in Ohio. And am very blessed to have the option to do so. I have a son and daughter enrolled in HPS for 2 years now. Last year was the beginning of success for my son, now in 6th grade. He used to despise school and his grades were below his ability. HPS exemplifies christianity while making sure students are successful academically. HPS definitely supports students being well rounded. LOVE, LOVE, LOVE the school and staff! I have 3 children that have attended HPS and it has been a great experience. My oldest son graduated in 2008, passed all the state test and attended an Ivy League College (Heidelberg University) in which he graduated. My daughter, who played on the 2010/2011 girls basketball state championship team; also graduated and attends college, she was a head of her other peers in english. Harvest Prep is a wonderful school for kids to attend and receive a christian education. The atmosphere is christian and the teachers really care about the students. The education is of great quality. I would not send my kids any where else. Hats off to Pastor Parsley for hearing the voice of the Lord and being obedient. I believe that if you want a school that is going to help your child, do yourself a favor and enroll at Harvest Preparatory. My son attends this school and I am so happy that even at the kindergarten level, he gets spanish, music, chapel, and computer lab weekly. The parent teacher communication is excellent and I would not send my child ANYWHERE else! There is nothing that my son is missing out on. They are ahead of the game!! I believe in Pastor Rod Parsley and his amazing ministry; I just don't believe he has any ideal of the lack of caliber of the many employees. I have witnessed first hand for two years teachers that have to continue to tell me they are in charge of a classroom rather than just being in charge. I have received school communication that is grammatically incorrect, listened to teachers speak using non-standard English and watched in dismay as children are labeled as "trouble" when in reality they are advanced and need more academic stimulation. I believe this school was created to fulfill a might vision and purpose; however, until each staff member lines up with that cause, the school will not fulfill what it's purpose is. This is my 3rd attempt with this school and if you have children that are behind and struggling below grade level-- then this may be a great option. If you have an advanced and highly intelligent child that needs academic stimulation; seek another option. From Pre-k through high school, HPS has not been able to provide the needed academic enrichment. I previously taught at this school and I would never send my children to Harvest Prep. The only reason I would consider sending them there would be if I lived in an awful area with an awful school. The specials are sub par. There are no library or computer classes, and the rest of the specials are lacking. The administration does not run the school well and problems are rarely handled. There are only two intervention specialists in the whole school (k-12) and the staff/school is not equipped to handle any students with any level of special education students. Also, the staff is treated poorly. School is very poor. They don't try to handle issues they just kick your child out of the school. My son was 3 and had some minor behaviors. He is very upbeat and an all around boy. They said he was not ready. For this to be ran by a pastor with the come as you are rule of thumb I was very confused! When I would go to get my child I was not allowed to just go get him. They had to have him brought to me. This made me feel like they were hiding something. They wouldn't even let me deliver lunch money! Teachers very incompetent. Would not recommend. My daughter attended harvest Prep and she is better for it. She is now a Senior at The OSU and holds fast to her biblical teaching as well as her superior academic teaching. All schools have issues; I hope that Harvest Prep is able to rise above the criticisms and resolve the conflict for the sake of the children and the church/school. This school is really not doing well this year, or the last 4 years to be more accurate. If you are looking for a school, keep looking. From my daughter and son starting here, I have witnessed many things. First, the church is too in control of the day to day of the school. Second, when a teacher is absent, NO sub is called in, so they WILL be in a class of 50 others. They may as well not have school that day. Third, specials in the elementary are non-existent (art, music, gym? Yeah right). The ONLY good thing about this school is the caring teachers. They will form a great christian relationship with you, and are willing to always help. The problems come from the leadership within the church and schools. I find it hard to believe that the overall rating for this school is so high on here. PS, my friend told me on Facebook to come and look at the 'good reviews', that is why there are a few bad reviews in a row in such a short time. How can they improve? Hire 2 principles, one for elem, one for 7-12. Next, get the church out of the school. Then, hire an assit. principle to help. They will not be there in 5 years if it continues like this. I really hope they can turn it around. I have three kids that attend H P S I don't have one bad thing to say about the school I love everything about the school from the teachers to the principles. Great School Great Choice My experience as a parent at Harvest Prep has been outstanding. I currently have two children enrolled and one of them is enrolled in the PLATO online learning class and he has been named to the honor roll. Also, the guidance counselor has taken the time to meet with every 12th grader individually and has worked with them in ensuring their post-graduation plans are established and attained. This school has taken great strides in becoming a true preparatory school and I am grateful that God opened the doors for my children to attend HPS. No school is a perfect school, but I can say that Harvest Prep does everything possible to ensure my children are provided with a safe, nurturing and educational environment. I have been impressed with the teachers and the coaches. The teachers always exceed the expectations when I email them with questions. The coaches are also amazing, because they care more about my children as individuals, than athletes. Overall, my decision to enroll my children at Harvest Prep was well worth it and I'm grateful that God provided the opportunity. I have been very pleased with HPS. I would definitely recommend the school to anyone looking for a quality school in central Ohio! This school is only fit to be private because parents are paying for their children to attend the school. Overall your child is getting an average Columbus Public School education at best. Not worth the money. poor...poor...this school is getting greedy with VOUCHERS (ED Choice) their not turning no money down. Overbooking classes and refusing to add necessary classes to students schedule. IF your child is attending k-8 no complaints (GOOD CHOICE).. 9TH-12TH find somewhere else to send your kid. No clubs for students! No organizations to join. "nothing"... don't be fooled! Public Schools are a mess, I should know, I taught in them for 2 decades. This school is a FAR better experience in every way. This is CLEARLY a Christian school. Is every child, parent, teacher, etc perfect? No! Which is why they need to be in a Christian environment to work on being "holy." I have my kids at this school and am extremely pleased in what goes on here. The overall experience here is top of the line, period. Is there flaws, yes. If you think any experience you have had here that is negative is unique to this school you probably are not being realistic. Great leadership here, great kids, great men and women of God leading the school environment to be a very friendly and conducive to learning place to be. Zero, my child will be relocating to home schooling, hopefully we can catch up to his grade level! Shame on this school, needs to be closed! Overal great experience! I would like to see more options for electives and more AP courses/teachers available! In comparison to local public schools, this is the exact environment and experience that my child needed to succeed. The individualized attention in the classroom has helped my child grow in confidence with academics. The school is not perfect, but they definitely do tremendous work.
