column1: I have had two children go through the Mineola school district in recent years. I've seen the changes with the consolidation of schools, and I believe the students ended up well-adjusted. The class sizes are decent. The teachers we have encountered are caring and competent. The district is really building the STEAM programs, always a plus to encourage students in these areas. There are numerous AP classes offered at the HS to make the kids more competitive in the college application process. The students also learn another language early on. Everyone gets an iPad in the district and much of the learning uses this tool to engage the students. They are also investing in their science research programs. The Fine Arts departments are magnificent, students are taught instruments early on and encouraged to join music clubs. There are many sport teams. The district is everything one would expect from the suburbs: small classes, caring teachers, homecoming, a sense of community. Another plus is the diversity of the student body. We wanted our children to be in a school district with different races and ethnicities, and Mineola certainly has this. I find it horrible that students who are advanced do not get opportunities to excel. This school has resources for struggling students, but none for those who are advanced. They focus on Math and ELA so much (for the tests I think), and then they cut social studies and foreign language. My children have social studies once a month on average. They have a geography worksheet in the beginning and a couple of readings on current events (from Time for Kids) and that's it. They take 4 days to teach students to write 1 paragraph by giving them templates and forms instead of explaining the thinking behind writing. They don't learn decimals until 5th grade. Its very poor. We have been in this school district for a few years now and I think it's great. One of my kids is "gifted" and they get lots of enrichment opportunities and extra work so they are not bored. One of my other kids had an IEP and we always felt supported and like his needs were being taken into consideration. Mineola High School is a modern, forward thinking, technology driven school with caring teachers, administrators and staff. Both of my children have been in the district since Kindergarten, and are now 8th grade honor students. We couldn't be more pleased with their education. The high school offers the choice of 21 advanced placement courses, as well as a cohort program with Farmingdale StateCollege and LIU Post which affords students the opportunity to earn approximately 24 college credits in computer science! There is a very strong fine arts department, athletics department and countless clubs. The student service center has many ways for students to get involved with the community. There is a focus on being a good "global citizen". The high school building has been well maintained and recent updates include new furniture, windows, air conditioning, a new auxiliary gym and strength training center, a FABLAB (which includes 3D printers) and so much more. I strongly encourage anyone considering moving to the district to arrange a tour of the school so they can see for themselves what they have to offer. When the pandemic first hit in March 2020 and schools were shut down, our district was able to start teaching students virtually almost immediately due to a 1:1 iPad program. Besides education, the school has provided a warm, engaging atmosphere for the students during this unprecedented time. They are offering intramurals for sports that are not currently allowed to be played, virtual and some in person clubs, music programs and more, which is just amazing to me. I would highly recommend the Mineola UFSD, I have 2 kids currently one in 7th middle school (entering HS in Sept) and one in 3rd grade. Through these years I have seen my boys grow academically, socially and culturally. There is one secret behind their success - it's their teachers. Under the leadership of the Superintendent Dr. Nagler who was awarded the 2019 Superintendent in NYS and there are 811 school district. They live and preach the GROWTH MINDSET...it's okay to make mistakes you learn and grow from the mistakes. They are an Apple distinguished school so yes they do use iPads but the teachers are mindful of the time spent on it. And thankful for their preparedness, they were well beyond their years when the pandemic hit and we all went into Lockdown in March '2020 Mineola Middle School and up conveniently moved to virtual the next day... followed by the Elementary grades within the same week. I have 3 kids in the district and 2 of them at the high school. They've had an exemplary experience. There are so many resources to help them excel. I am proud of my district and I would recommend it to anyone. Great school overall. Friendly and engaging teachers. Clean schools and great learning environment. Excellent teachers and administration my daughter is currently a senior and she had a great experience with rigorous AP classes great theater program plenty of sports and activities for students to excel in. Mineola HS does not get the credit for all the work they do with their students. It’s definitely a hidden gem, as an educator myself I never had to worry about my daughters education. Great experience

Within my first week of the school I could verify 5 dealers. But the drugs don't bother me as much as the bullying and separation of the students. There are many cliches that are offensive in the school, and a lot of prejudice black, and jew jokes go on. Even the moms in Mequon like to spread rumors. Some teachers are cool and have been teaching in the districts a majority of their lives! I also recommend football players going here as it has a great program! As far as faculty (Principals, etc.) they have no idea what's going on and ridicule the kids sometimes. 2/5 The students at this school are stuck up and fake. The academic part of the school is average for a 'good school district' school. The athletics are obviously what the administration focuses on. The students know nothing about how lucky they are to have rich parents who can afford to live in Mequon. Some teachers are really good, but they all favor the popular students. The parents are all overly involved in their students highschool and think their kids are saints, when really, everyone does drugs and drink because it's 'ghetto'. Homestead is a very good school. Most graduates end up surprised about how easy collage is. The teachers are very supportive and provide help at any needed time. I've emailed them at 9 at night for hw questions and 10 minutes later they reply back. Yes, there are clicks, but they mostly don't intermix, however they don't bully each other. There is a no bullying tolerance, but some still happens. We have 2 in-school cops and popular to the contrary belief, homesteads drug problem is at about the average of all public high schools. They do not drink because they think it is 'ghetto'; they do it because it's 'fun'. Besides, only the 'popular' do it. I'm very thankful to be in the MTSD school district. Homestead High School recently received a rating of "Significantly Exceeds Expectations" from the Wisconsin Dept of Public Instruction. It was the only large high school in the state to receive this honor and the only high school in the Milwaukee area. Only 68 schools in the entire state received this rating! HHS is a comprehensive high school with offerings for just about any student interest, and its district, Mequon-Thiensville, was named Best Suburban School District by Milwaukee Magazine the last two years. The principal is outstanding and has initiated programs like AVID, designed to work with students in the academic "middle." The teachers, in conjunction with a recent move to trimesters, have overhauled the curriculum to bring it in line with recently approved common core standards. The school added 3 more AP classes this year and plans to add 3 more next year, in addition to adding several classes which allow students to earn credit through Univerisity of Wisconsin schools (dual credit). Last year, HHS received an honor from the ACT organization recognizing its use of data to make better decisions about understanding student performance. Best school in the state! You couldn't ask for a better public school. They have excellent academics, sports as well as art programs. It has great teachers, courses and resources. although there are groups but you are not going to find a less stuck up high school. The orchestra and band programs are excellent and so are the acting classes/drama club. Obviously it focuses of sports so if you are looking for athletics it is a school to go to. Overall you or you child will have fantastic opportunities and preparation for college both socially and academically. Having gone to two different high schools, I can honestly tell you that Homestead isn't all that. It is a very mediocre school compared to where I went to school before. Mind you, I lived in a very affluent area previously, home to some of the best high schools in the nation. I guess I sort of had high expectations coming to Mequon. If Homestead is considered one of the best schools in Wisconsin, then Wisconsin must have a poor education system. The school itself is filled with faculty members who lie to make the school look good. People have gone off to some very prestigious colleges, but that's only because they were born smart, and probably have enough money to pay for a tutor. The school has a decent variety of classes, but the teachers don't always teach very well and are discriminatory. All the school really cares about is sports, when they could use that money to actually pay for useful things that will benefit a students education. They have mouse traps throughout the school as well as mold, which shows you that they don't take very good care of the school itself. Mequon rich? Hardly. There are places outside of Mequon that are far more nice and affluent. I've known three generations to come out of this school. Homestead may turn out a few superstars, but at what cost?Homestead is great when you look at the education ratings. But I find the education ratings to be flawed. They don’t take in to account the social structure of the school. I find this can be very misleading and even DAMAGING to your kids’ future. Aide your kids. Help them. Teach them about life. Give them hope. Raise them up. It takes next to nothing to raise a child up; it takes thousands of dollars and countless hours to ‘fix’ an adult.All three generations I talked with state the education IS great. But they lack a quality social foundation. I find that is FAR more IMPORTANT than memorizing some facts, getting a good grade on a test, or going to Yale.Please respect your child’s overall quality of life and overall well being. If you’re sending your child(ren) here because it’s the ‘best’ school or has a good rating, you may want to think long and hard about everything before taking any action.I repeat, this is your child’s life. Not just their education, please remember that!!!Thank you. This is an excellent school if you child is academically inclined in the core subject areas. There is so much there to offer for these students, and they will have great teachers. This school is limited in opportunities for students with other talents and interests.

column3: Great choice... Love it here, was apprehensive about moving but I'm glad I came xxx Inflexible Scheduling for Band Students If your student plans to take advantage of Rio s fantastic nationally recognized band program be prepared to curtail your summer vacation plans. Because of the San Juan Unified School District s current refusal to allow for a physical education exemption policy, as allowed by the California Education Code, many band students will have to take PE during the summer. This is because some band practices and PE overlap in the students packed schedules. Athlete students who are in band cannot get PE credit for after school sports. Strangely, another SJUSD high school, Mira Loma, allows an exemption process for International Baccalaureate students participating in school-sponsored interscholastic athletic programs due to their curriculum demands. Other high schools in California provide PE exemptions to students even when they participate in organized after school club sports. The SJUSD just does not seem interested in putting their students best interests first. I'm a freshman right now at rio and I am really loving it there. very friend people and everyone really does get along. really nice teachers and a really nice campus. they also offer really nice classes and a honors program which I am in called civitas which has got a California state civic engagement award and that is not their first time either. I had a choice in going to Bella vista, Folsom, and pleasant grove high school but I am very glad that I went to rio it doesn't disappoint and I definetly recommend to other people Teachers were awful and even one had serious mental issues. The principal lacks the necessary skills to perform his job. If you want proof just look at the declining test scores under Ginter. Keep in mind that this was the BEST school in the San Juan Unified School District at one time. Community support is fantastic from various parent booster groups for band, athletics and PTA parents. Many teachers are caring and supportive of students. The greatest failure is in leadership.While there is support for non-academic interests of sports, there is not a sense of purpose and direction for academic interests by the whole school. I love this school. It's hard but very good place to learn This school does NOT deserve the hype. Its way overrated honestly. But for Sacramento, I guess it's not so bad. Had a great experience with my 2 kids. Would recommend! My daughter tells me how much she loves her teachers. She feels they are well educated, intelligent, good communicators, and fun. She feels well prepared to get into a UC. the principal and few students jumped me and the nurse only offered me ice and i was knocked out cool with few broken teeth and no one called 911 untill my dad came and called 911 and all they did was try to get off the school so it wouldnt come back on them I'll state upfront that COVID and the stay-at-home order along with distance learning definitely put a damper on my child's high school experience. That said, this school lacks unity and school spirit. "Rio", as it is called, is a school where, for lack of a better word, the snobs go. The affluent who can't or won't pay for private schools along with those who are trying to keep up with the "Joneses", attend here. The jazz band program is very exclusive and is something you'd find more at a private academy or charter school. Kudos to the jazz band program for surviving COVID and continuing. It is too bad that band is the only music program at Rio. They do not have choir, marching band, dumb line, guitar, or even music appreciation. The band classes are not structured for beginners. You need to know how to play upon arrival in band class at this school. Sports are exclusive to the comp team players that make up each team. Academics are strong yet students do fall through the cracks at this school that is pushing 2,000 enrollment. The counseling department is understaffed, woefully behind, and sometimes uninterested in following-through. There are other exclusive programs at this school like Civitas, Engineering, Robotics, Medical Tech, Reader's Theater, and AP Capstone, but those do not bring together the school as whole and are very separate groups. Student leadership is not a focus at this school where unity and school spirit are typically found and led by at other high schools. Rio seems to be in the middle of change. It is hard to tell if it is for the better. Staff changes have been many in recent years including long-term staffers leaving for other SJUSD schools and positions. In the meantime, the existing students suffer from poor communication from the administration and little direction for future success. Parents, get ready to do your own research for college, scholarships, financial aid, and future career opportunities. If your child has a learning disability, is low income, or has any mental health issues DO NOT SEND THEM HERE. Rio Americano staff and some teachers provided little to no resources, denied students accommodations, and were frankly rude while doing it. The counselors (exept Mrs. Jensen) do not care about you or your child. Some of the teachers are amazing but that can’t make up for the fact that virtually all of the office staff who makes decisions for your child are not kind people. If this is the school you choose for your child be ready to provide them academic support that the school fails to provide.I would also not recommend if your kid is a person of color as there have been several recent incidents (at least one per year) of discrimination (between students).

column1: Robert E. Lee is a horrible school. Teachers and staff are unable to keeps students safe. It is a daily occurrence for fights, outbursts in classrooms, and even violence. The staff as a whole are not willing to help students, class rooms are locked to keep students from bursting in. There is little to no homework or any type of work for that matter that is given to the students. It is a great school if you want your child to get easy A's but not no a good choice if you want them to be safe. This school should be shut down. The staff should be ashamed of themselves for their lack of ability to teach, protect, and encourage students. Military dependents who live on NAS JAX are zoned for this school. Whatever you do find an alternative!!!!!! If I could give a lower rating I would. Most people generalize Lee by the general population students when they say that Lee should be shut down. They all tend to forget that there is a large population of magnet students who are some of the smartest and most gifted teenagers in Jacksonville. Both the Early College and Engineering magnets have rave reviews all over Florida. As an Early College student, I can attest to the fact that while the general teachers in Lee may not care about what happens to the students, every single one of the Eary College and they Engineering teachers take a special interest in every single one of their students. The Early College program is a very good opportunity for any student who has big dreams and plans on going places after they graduate. While there are fights and a plethora of other problems, the administration is taking special steps to keep students safe. There will always be bad apples, no matter what school you go to. GO GENERALS! EC Class of 2013! (: I love it here at lee! The administration and teachers are awesome. Yes there are unruly children here but hey thats on their parents. I am an Early College student at Lee and it is amazing here! The vast knowledge here is endlesss! We all go through the saying that everyone elses school is better than Lee but I totally disagree. I am among some of the most intelligent students and the greatest teachers! Overall, this school is one of the best I have been too! GOOO GENERALSSS (: Class of 2016 (: As the parent of a 3rd generation General I have to say the school has had it's ups and downs. The school has gone through a fire (mid 80's)with major reconstruction and has been going through a multi million dollar renivation the last couple of years. With a National Model Engineering Academy and a state of the art Early College program (which my son is in) Lee is making a comback. I have seen nothing but wonderful attitudes from all the teachers and contrary to one parents comment my son has plenty of homework. With the wonderful magnet programs and new facilities I would not hesitate to recommend Lee to anyone. As both a public school teacher and a parent I understand certain concerns that have been brought up, unfortunatly in today's society schools can be a rough place. With that said my son has not had one situation of bullying, being picked on , or any other negative experience at the school. Prestige may come from going to schools like Stanton and Paxon but your AA degree before you graduate high school (without having to take a single AP exam or pay a dime) can come from LEE!!! GO Generals!!!!! Robert e lee. This school is a joke for a high school. Feel so bad for the students going there staff needs more training and teachers more educated in what they are teaching I participate in the Early College Program at Robert E. Lee. My school isn't the best, but there is a great amount of teachers who are fully dedicated to students' success. Teachers like Mr. Benyard, Mrs. Covas, Ms. Bishop and many more invest in students who want something more in life. Yes, there are fights but there are at most schools; nevertheless the education is superb. I believe this is a place of great opportunity and wouldn't trade my experience for the world. Next year I will be a junior starting classes at FSCJ for my AA degree. I will receive this degree before I even get my diploma! It's really a heartbreak to send your kid to this place -- this is what we experienced in the one year we attended: numerous fights; bathrooms often closed; movement in the building so restricted during lunch that some kids couldn't really always get lunch; security guards made kids shake out their binders onto the floor in the hallway; an English teacher showed a highly inaccurate movie inspired by Beowulf instead of having kids read it (and the teacher oblivious that the film is way off); another teacher told kids that hurricanes in the Americas are created by the souls of enslaved people; my son would send me cell phone videos during class of multiple students just sleeping on their desks while the teacher was doing nothing. This place extinguished my son's interest in school. The name is being changed (which is great), but I hope the rest of the place can be improved for the general students. At the open house, all the principal talked about were the special tracks like early high school and the engineering program, which might not be so bad -- but what about the majority of the kids? We discovered that few of the more appealing course offerings were actually available.

This school's class sizes keep rising, despite research supporting smaller class size leads to better education. Class sizes average 28+ students per class, even in science labs. Most students continue on to achieve degrees in higher education, and I believe that's due to the competency and support of all teachers, parents, coaches and community members. I highly credit my time at ORRHS to my future education. We're taking our children out of the ORR school system as soon as financing comes through for a private school in Dartmouth &/or Plymouth. Mattapoisett is not what it's lauded to be - beware. On top of the myriad issues relating to general apathy, there's no industrial Art's program. column1: I am a student at Gabriel Richard. I am currently a senior, and I will be graduating this year. GR was the best thing that has ever happened to me. The teachers give you all the responsibility to do your own work, study, and prepare for class which prepares you for college. The grading is hard; I'm not going to lie about that. You have homework every night, but in the long run it is to benefit the student as much as possible. I am an average student at GR. I currently have a gpa of 3.16, but my ACT is a 26. 27 on math, 27 on science. These teachers prepare you for the real world. The school itself molds each student to be a respectful, mature adult. When talking with High School students in everyday conversation, you can tell the difference between a student who goes to Gabriel Richard and a student from anywhere else. Gabriel Richard is worth every single penny. Gabriel Richard is the best school in the area. It has the highest Average MEAP scores and ACT scores. It prepares students for the challenges of college and life in general. Both my children graduated from GR and have gone on to great success in college. They both attend a major nationally ranked university and have made the Dean's List every semester. GR has prepared them well. As far as the disgruntled parents that have written reviews, I am sure their children would have had problems anywhere. The fact that the one parent was upset and wondered how 2 wrong out of 5 is a D, it isn't. Actually, it is a D-. 2 wrong out of 5 is 60% which equates to a D- at just about every school in the country. Possibly, the child's problem might be his parents. They definitely have a problem with math. This school is on the way out. Enrollment has dropped and there is nothing to attract students. Faculty is too old. This principal is not for our school. He is a little boy who wants toplay with his friends. Faculty is HORRBLE. No Guidance counselor. He has let good people go, He is shameful Gabriel Richard fosters a great learning opportunity for all students. With the academic standard, community service involvement and commitment to faith they specialize in building character giving your student unlimited options for the future. 99% are admitted to 4 year colleges and universities and over 4 million in scholarships are awarded yearly. Sports teams are competitive and staff care. If you are looking for a personalized education for your child, this is the place to be. The earlier claims about 99% of grads admitted to 4 year schools is COMPLETELY FALSE! The current principal is unqualified, unprofessional, inept, and downright lazy. This school once set the bar in excellence; now the bar has been thrown on the ground. Once this was a vibrant community with qualified and dedicated staff, along with real community service. Now, disrespect, theft, and mediocrity are the norm. Sadly, this is leaving a lot of good students wondering why. Why GR? No thanks. GR does not provide a safe or Christian environment to students. Recently a Teacher used foul and inappropriate language to students and this but one example. Apparently the previous post is not by a teacher at Gabriel Richard but rather a competitor. One can look up statistics of the school to find out they have 12 AP's the highest downriver and test scores are in the 96th percentile in the state. The Average ACT is 23.7 also a fact. Teachers, students, parents and alumni are actively engaged. It is a good time to be a Pioneer ! The school is underdeveloped especially in academics and the students are clueless. I believe this school will close soon due to lack of enrollment and academic issues. Gabriel Richard is run by unqualified people and is a disgrace to Catholic Education. The students have no respect for administration or teachers. Teacher turnover is ridiculous. No counselor wants to work more than a year. This principal will be the downfall if the school Very poor treatment of staff. Principal always takes side of parents who have a grudge instead of listening to the staff. I would never send my child to a school where it is acceptable to mistreat anyone including the staff and coaches. I went to Gabriel Richard in 9th grade and they put me behind in mathematics. I took geometry at a public school in 8th grade and passed with an A. But when I went to GR, they would not allow me to take anything above Honors Algebra 1. I also encountered a bit of racism. I left for public school after I finished freshman year and I am enjoying it much more. I feel I'm getting more prepared for college at my new school and that GR was a waste of my mom's money. Gabriel Richard is the best high school in the greater downriver area and in all of SE Michigan for many reasons but the best way to gather information on a school is not by reading reviews, you must go to Gabriel Richard and see first hand what makes this school so great. Observe and talk with the students, talk with the teachers, administrators and alumni, come to a school event and see for yourself. We did exactly what I am recommending and it became very clear to us that Gabriel Richard is truly a great school. We currently have 2 of our children enrolled and Gabriel Richard has lived up to everything we expected and continue to expect from a great school. Gabriel Richard is an excellent high school. The staff is highly qualified and dedicated. The curriculum is rigorous and robust to help students prepare for college. The families help to make this awesome school community an inviting place. All of my siblings have attended GR and can attest that the school was much better off with Brother James. I currently attend GR but am disappointed as science is my favorite subject, but the science teachers are the worst I've ever had, especially in biology. Also, I am less than pleased with the counselor as she has denied me and my friends of taking honors courses due to arbitrary grades. If you have a "C" in English, you are not permitted to take an honors history class. How does that make sense? Although, if you are interested in the literature department , GR does have an excellent teaching staff. I've had many great English teachers but Mr.Lopez is by far the best. Overall, if you're looking to send your child do a private school downriver and you're considering Cabrini, pick GR. My son is a freshman and actually likes school. I love the small community that we have, and a lot of the students are children of alumni. I had gotten my son into Riverview public, but he begged me to come here. It has been well worth the money, I can't think of anything more I would like to invest in, than my children's education and happiness. I have relatives that graduated from GR and are very successful and totally recommended the school for my son. Every teacher I met at GR sincerely cares about their students and make themselves available through many means at all hours of the day. This has resulted in a very successful student body both in citizenship and academics. I have seen such a positive change in my son since attending this school. They come in as children and leave as fine young adults. The campus ministry is exceptional. I personally have been on multiple trips as a chaperon and I was so impressed. There are beautiful memories being forged out that will last their lifetimes. Academics , discipline, life experiences , friendships , faculty , dedication are the excellent attributes you will find at Gabriel Richard. Go GR ! Our son attends Gabriel Richard and I have to say, attending this school has encouraged him to "raise the bar" on himself. He is taking three honors courses and it is a challenge for him, however, he has told us he has a goal and in taking these honors courses is getting him well prepared for college. Any struggles he has had in any of his classes, they offer a learning center for kids to get the help they need. I have heard numerous parents who children are now in college consistently say on how well prepared their children are for college compared to some other kids. The school is constantly looking on ways to improve their school. I tell everyone, go to the open houses and get a tour of the school to see for yourself as I don't think you will be disappointed. As I was reading prior reviews, I am shaking my head at the comment of the teacher turn over rate. I do not find that to be true at all. I am impressed that the majority of the GR staff has been here for many years. Many could leave to earn much more money at a public school, yet they have chosen to commit themselves to Catholic education andto GR. In regard to academics, I am also impressed by GR. My daughter is a freshman and I am beyond confident that she will be more than prepared for college mainly due to the academic rigor and high expectations of this school. I am an educator who has spent 20+ years in public education at the secondary level. I would never pay to send my child here unless I was 100% confident that this is the best opportunity for her. There truly is NOT a better school downriver. I love that this school provides "big school" opportunities in a very close knit environment. Everyone at the school knows my two children by name and they genuinely care about their wellbeing. This school does not focus on the important things like education. They are focused athletics. They play favorites and are not afraid to put children down for being different. WWJD? This Catholic School is a joke. Don't waste your money Top priority of every teacher is to get off on power.

column3: No doubt Wilson Memorial is the best high school in the county - that's what scares me. The school offers a whopping 3 AP options for juniors and seniors, AP US History, AP English 12, and AP Government. Not only this, but their AP classes are overkill. I used to be in all AP and Pre-AP in middle school, and never have I had to read 37 books for English 11AA- not even AP. You'll get 2-3 hours of AP US History homework piled on top of that. All other classes (regular - only option) are more like elementary - all arts and crafts. The administration strives for us to act like adults, yet we are treated like children. We can't even walk around in the morning - we are forced to cramp ourselves into a hallway until 8:00 - giving us 13 minutes of free time (So much for using the library). People get suspended for bringing cinnamon to school, smooshing a bagel on somebody, etc. The teachers are overly nice, pushovers, but unfortunately do not care about the education we are receiving. Needless to say I'm transferring so I can take all AP again. That is what colleges are looking for anyways. This school was terrible. Personally I dealt with depression throughout high school and was consistently bullied. Whenever I looked for help from anyone, there was none to be found. They only were concerned about their academics which were subpar and certainly inadequate. Not a single positive experience. My son is constantly pulled from class and threatened to be dissenrolled over requiring proof of address EVERY 6 months! That means we have to bring in a copy of the same lease and have it notarized every six months. It is a terrible learning environment and the leadership is rude and ineffective. Bullying and drug and drug use are not being addressed in the school It wasn’t the greatest, this is majorly because of the staff. I was not a problematic student, yet was treated like I deserved no respect from the staff. Many of the office staff always seemed to have a bad day, or have an attitude when it came to needing something from them, so oftentimes students would be forced to figure it out themselves in result of fear. Do better... PLEASE. Students are at your school to learn, not tip-toe around the staff in fear of being scolded or chastised. What a wonderful high school. Caring and inclusive staff, rigorous academics. Students are held to high standards and are offered amazing opportunities. Wilson is wonderful!

column1: People use CCHS activities and programs as an excuse to say it's an excellent school. I attended Crawford County High School all four years and the teachers only hand out violations/or enforce the rules due to their mood or race. People show favoritism and I only had three good instructors out of all four years. It is a very racist and harsh place for a student to be and a lot of discrimination. I would not recommend that anyone enroll their child into this school. CCHS can get you ready for Tech school,but it does not prepare you for college at all. The counselors care nothing about your child or his/her issues. Also,if you are a senior and getting ready for college, I advise you do not seek help from the counselors. I have lost many scholarships thinking that I was getting help when I wasn't. This school will never succeed unless there is a new principal,new board members,and some new teachers. Crawford County High School is a great place. The teachers are really well. It is more of a problem with the students. They expect the best, but put forth no effort. They claim the teachers can't teach, but talk during class and never study or pay attention. I have excellent grades because I work hard and listen to the teachers. They know what they are talking about, and thy give us the tools we need to succeed. The technology department isn't the best because of the lack of support and funds. The TSA (Technology Student Association) Chapter here is doing great things, and has even made it to the National conference this year. The staff and faculty are welcoming and nice. All in all, this is a fine school! Crawford County High School is not a good school. They preach anti-bullying but don't stand by it. The students run that school. There are at least 1-2 fights a week. The kids just don't have motivation to learn there. In return these kids effect the ones that are there to learn. When I signed my daughter up they tried to give me a hard time about putting my 10th grader in AP/Honors classes. I had to jump through hoops to get her in them. Its like the kids are there to just socialize. The a disrespectful to the teachers and the teachers allow this to go on. This school needs some new people in there that can lead and take control. As you can see above the test scores and college readiness reflect these issues. This High School is what you make of it. The more time and energy you place into your education, the more the school and teachers will step up and support your goals for your education. I had an excellent four years here, and I would rather have gone nowhere else for my high school education. I would rate my experiences at this school on a 1-10 scale a 10. The teachers and the principals care a lot about education. They do not like anyone out of the classrooms during instructional times, but let you use the bathroom if it is an emergency. The school offers rewards for good behavior. The principal started a twitter challenge. He will tweet out a challenge everyweek, so far he has done a challenge over reducing skipping by 25% and no fights. You have to be able to complete this challenge over a period of 2 weeks. Once you pass the challenge you can wear joggers and warmups for the day. It is a good reward, because we have dress code. Another reward is a PBIS. If you are good for the whole month and no more than 2 unexcused absences and 3 tardies you are allowed to go. They let us sign up for different things. There is a technology place where students can hang, 2 movie stations, the gym, and games. Other PBIS have involved student grade level competitions and against the teachers. The sophomores won the kickball tournament and the freshman won the volleyball. I love CC for rewarding us good kids.

column3: I think that Ms. Marcks is a great administrator, and even though I left the school I could see the changes she was making. She knows how to treat and speak to her employees. I hope the school thrives. I used to go to Spruce Creek, doing the IB program there, and it was horrible! The students were mean, the work load was too much, and I had to take public transport to school every day because, even with all the money being pumped to that school, they don't have enough to send a bus out for the out of zone IB kids. You know, the kids who are the only reason that school is an A school. So, I transferred and came to Atlantic, and I haven't regretted it. The students are much kinder, and welcomed me with open arms. The classes are much easier to understand, and are taught by teachers who actually care and actually like their job. At Atlantic, everyone here has a passion and are proud to be a Shark. It's like a home away from home, and I will definitely be proud to graduate in my teal cap and gown come 2016. This school as a 15:1 student teacher ratio which as a former FPC high school student that is something that I greatly miss. With only about 1,000 students at Atlantic everybody knows everybody, wether you want to or not. It's really hard to make friends hear, since everybody that i know that goes to atlantic i consider to be like family to me. The teachers care a lot not only about you're grades, but also about you're wellbeing, which if your just now starting high school as freshmen going into this school. Is something that you greatly need and/or will be a huge help. With an hour long lunch, you have plenty of time to talk with friends, and/or catch up on some late homework that you forgot to do. Since almost every classroom as group tables instead of desks, it is much easier, quicker, and more efficient to get classwork done. If you go to Atlantic, or plan on coming to Atlantic, it is almost next to impossible to fail, with all the help that one receives, open arms of former students, extra-help if needed, group tables, and a campus the size of a small college. You are almost guaranteed to have some of the best four years of you're life Last year, I went to a different school, and switching to Atlantic was probably the best decision I've made academically. The campus is clean and looks great. The teachers are really helpful and funny at times. We have a gigantic library with a coffee shop in it, and it's a good place to go and work on homework during lunch, or just to hang out. I like how organized the office is and how they keep the website up to date. The school offers several academies, so there's something for everybody. All of the career academies are good, but if one had to stand out as our most prestigious it would have to be Law and Government. We have FBI agents, marines, and police come talk to us. Everyone is interested in the material and we go on TONS of field trips. We even have mock trials in a courtroom at our school, so it's definitely the right place to be if you aspire to be an attorney, senator, cop, judge, etc. One of the best things about Atlantic is how many extra curricular activities they have, especially JROTC. There are truly some impressive, patriotic people in there. I wear the uniform with so much pride. So in case you haven't guessed, I LOVE this school. Take my advice, and if you really want to study civics, get a variance. It's so worth it. I love this school and I'm grateful to be a shark. The best thing is how many opportunities it has, like talking to the FBI or all the types of sports they have here. And if you want to be an attorney, join ALAG. You won't find a better high school law program in Florida. bathrooms are terrible would not use this school 1000000/1000000. Would recommend to anybody who asked for a good high school better than Spruce Creek or main one 10/ 10 STARS. Little to no fights. Alot of really good teachers ( such as Blasko, Pio, Dalia, Cochran, Romeo, Holloway, Wallace,Howard, Haughwout, Burton, and Stewart.) . Students here are really close to teachers, and students are close to each other. The school gives everyone opportunites fofr free tutoring. Alot of the teachers will stay after school for students to get tutoring. This school also has "power hour" where all the students have a hour to eat and study. Some use it to chill with their friends , and others use it for studying. Our school is very diverse , and we get several foreign students at our school coming from Germany, London, Asia , Jamacia, Hati, and Cuba. If your student is special needs with adhd or any other special needs beware they don't care . My child has adhd and has impulse issues and is not able to take meds due to seizures. This did not stop them for disciplining my child for every little thing. Grant it my child is no angel by any means, but is not a problem child as well. The school does not see it this way though for a child with adhd they see them as a problem . The discipline lady and vice principal are a nightmare they will discipline them for every little thing they can find. The discipline lady acts like a child tattling on a class mate basically. The vice principal has no sense of humor what so ever and will judge your student even before they walk in the front door with out getting to know them first even If they have never been in the school there. They are very judgmental, pushy and act like stuck up rich snobs. There was only one teacher there that i liked and needs a shout out for being awesome and that was Ms. Viola in special ed. The sheriff on campus there was awesome as well he really does care about the kids and all of the kids safety there so shout out to him as well for being awesome, Other then that i am not impressed with this school at all. We felt they really just want to push kids thru and collect the money on these special needs kids.

column1: This is a great school helping unfortunate children become great people! It is amazing, and I love the staff. Going through the trouble to enroll your child is worth it. This is a great opportunity! Milton Hershey school is great for children who have a dream to go further than anyone that they are surrounded by. I am a MHS student and I couldn't love a place more. They teach you perseverance and responsibility.I pray that anyone who has a child who has bigger ambitions sends there child here My school is ok .... i think it could be better at times but im chillin here so yah ... also i met oliver here so ive chose to stay ... i just think they should pick better house parents My daughter is doing so good there. She has excelled in everything she has done. The first semester was a little challenging, but her second semester all A's and 1 B such a good school. The hardest part is that she is away from home. I call every other day and talk to her so its not so hard. Vacations are often enough that we get to spend time together and the weekends parents can visit the school with prior approval and take children off campus. This is a great opportunity for any child. The things they learn and what they can accomplish are so great and much better than a public school. We Love Milton Hershey School It has been a life saver for my grandchildren I is a aluma and 2 are still sudents....what a wonderful school We live in the area of very bad schools and Milton Hershey School has been a great opportunity for our children to learn in a safe environment that also allows them to participate in many different sports music activities in other extracurricular activities. We believe that the experiences that they are now experiencing at the Milton Hershey School are ones that will mold and shape them for a lifetime and help them to be very successful. Excells the expectations we had, with not only education but with the moral compass of our children, teaching them how to cope in todays society....thank you for our hope in the next generation. It is a pretty good school overall. A life changing institution where amazing opportunities are afforded to children who otherwise would have missed out.

column3: i have to children that attend this high school, they have been here for under a year n i have noticed that this school is bias against teen parents. they allow fighting and theats between kids but yet when you hear and witness thier staff verbally abuse students and you report it they do nothin about it and then go after your children with a vengance this is the worst high school in the lacey area. My son attends River Ridge High School and is having the best high school experience we could have hoped for. We are a military family, but lucky enough to be able to remain on one spot for all 4 years of his high school. He loves the diversity, the teachers, staff and coaches. We are realistic in the knowledge that kids make poor choices at times, but the options and ability for our son to rise to his potential and even exceed it made us choose RRHS vs others in the area. It's smaller, but has all the same accelerated classes as the other schools. The kids joke about how RR gets a bad wrap due to its location. But most of the students embrace the reputation and use it to prove the neigh sayers wrong. We are very please with the education our son is receiving. This is a "hang out " high school. I don't know how it got a 7 rating- when at the beginning of the 2015-16 it was a five (5). Most teachers and staff are jaded, the academic presentation is substandard, The school is not culturally competent (though they attempt to give the appearance that they are.) The sports program is good, but if you want your child ready for college-I would reconsider this school-. This school is small, unkempt, and over crowded. We are moving out the district because of Thurston County schools. If you are a parent and are concerned about you child's education then this school will be sure to disappoint. The county really needs to consider an overall school improvement plan. This is not the only school in the district that is below average; I have students that attended three others in this district and the consensus is the same about all three- below average and need for improvement. I love this school I'm a 9th grade at this school this school gives u alot of freedom witch is what kids need the staff is awesome they talk to u they are cool I just moved here to Washington state from NC I went to south viwe middle and my sisters went to south view high school the education at river ridge high is 1000 times better the svms in NC I haven't noticed any ganges in this school I have a lot of friends the kids are nice some teachers are mean like a coatch for weight lifting he's mean I can't think of his name and the other teacher in room 410 is mean to me he says I have a attetude witch some times I do but if I'm 2 min late to class he emails my parents and says I need a pass but I talked to miss in the same class they say he doesn't care if they r 5 min late so he really does not like me witch is fine with me but in this school all teachers that I have actually teach u stuff and in math room 114 he is the best he helps u with ur problems so if I had to choice to go back to NC or stay here I would deffenty stay here at this school if I could I would rate this school a 9 out of 10 so all the staff good job but I don't like that if u don't have a doctors note saying my nee has a fractur in it then they make me still run or I get a F I can't get a note yet bc my mom and dad is in the army so it took them a while to get me seen and so far I have had 3 appt I have another one soon so I have to ask for a note next time. But I don't u guys care about my nee any ways I live this school its awesome and fun I like how we get out at 2 instead of 330 so if i was u I would go to this school thanks to all the staff love this school :) Diverse pshaw. This school has been known to have the most minority students. Also they haven't improved school grounds since they opened the school. OVER-crowded class rooms. Rude bordering on disgraceful teachers who cannot handle the large classes they attend too. I would say all these positive reviews come from certain students who education was looked after by advisers. If we saw GRADES on teachers i would say we'd see a different review. School starts at 7:20 to save money. Releasing the students earlier for bus reasons. If your hoping for your child to get a good education I would look else where. I went here freshman year and I hated it It was the best year of my whole high school career We are a military family that moved to the area in summer 2016. We bought a house in what we thought would be NTHS district but the high schools were redistricted and we were assigned to RRHS. I was upset because of the Great School rating and nervous for my high performing freshman. However, RRHS did a great job educating my son this year. He had 3 advanced classes available to him that challenged him to reach farther and do better. The school has a strong positive behavior program to try and reward positive behaviors vs spending all of their time telling the kids what they're doing wrong. My son did band and jazz band. The teacher did a great job keeping the kids engaged all over our community. I have neighbors whose kids played sports at RRHS and they were equally impressed with the athletics at the school. I believe that the fairly large upper middle class area of Lacey that was redistricted into RRHS will have a direct impact on "scores" and that RRHS will start to show higher numbers on sites such as Great Schools. I don't believe the 5/10 that RRHS currently has is an accurate measurement of the quality of education kids receive especially when the kids make an effort to stay engaged academically, and socially. River Ridge really helped my daughter when she was struggling through some classes just after we moved here. They help find solutions that work best for each individual child, it’s not a one size fits all type solution. Horrible school. The athletics of this school is if your a family that is favored by the coach or a friend then your kids play. Talent dedication, hard work and doing what they say to move up, well that does not work. Parents who have emailed the coach to check in on how their kids are doing get emails back as to say well be better if they just turned in their gear , because they will not play. Kids tell us all the time how they talk down to them and school does nothing for these actions or they stand behind the coach/teacher. It honestly amazes me that the coaching staff has not been replaced because it needs to be and fast. Coach Shultz is horrible and not a decent human either with his degrading of players. Senior nights are supposed to be about the Seniors of the school not the talent levels is their night not yours so get over yourself, because your not a good coach and the kids and parents don't back you or stand you and your staff. If, I could give a 0 star and tell you anything its drive your kids to a better school with better opportunities like Yelm, North Thurston, Olympia and even Timberline. STAY AWAY. This school doesn't help student exceed, especially if you are a minority . i was a former student at north Thurston high school as a white student that really really tried to get good grades . the classes that i didn't do good in or they areas of my weakness. the staff came to me or call in the office to help me find what classes best fits me and how to help my areas of weakness to succeed so i can graduate . now i have a daughter who is non white goes to river ridge high she's is really really having trouble with her grades but instead of helping her and placing her in classes to reach her potential she's is being labeled as a problem child and they are not offering any support or assistance . sad the boundaries of high schools of mostly white schools verses minorities schools make a difference in the help or should i say lack of help in this field along with stereotyping I attended River Ridge High School from 2018-2022. I would say as a general rule, most teachers care about students and try their hardest to promote learning and equality. As for the administration team, they are absolutely horrible. I was having issues in the 2019/20 school year needing protection orders as well as support from administrators due to issues of bullying and harassment by other students. I was not taken seriously and basically told that they did not believe me if I didn’t have physical evidence (which I did and still nothing was done about it). Admin is more worried about controlling their students, saving face, and implementing tyrannical type school rules over real issues such as academic struggle affecting a majority of their students, college readiness, constant violence and physical fights, and the list goes on and on. I was lucky enough to have amazing parents as well as a support system outside of this school to help me prepare for college and figure out what my next step was after graduation. Many students who attend this school cannot say the same and administration does nothing to help. As one of the top 30 in my graduating class, not once was I ever approached or inquired about college, how they can help me in my application process, or asked if I even had a plan. On the opposite spectrum, I had many friends who needed help with those processes and could have greatly benefitted from some type of guidance. I have friends who attended other high schools in the area such as North Thurston, Timberline, Olympia, Capital, etc. All of these resources were provided to them and education and student wellbeing was a main priority. On another note, if you are someone who values athletics, this is the last school I would recommend. Year in and year out almost every single sport has majority losing seasons as well as a lack of good coaching. Surrounding schools seem to value sports much more. Lastly, there were a multitude of shooting threats and lockdowns specifically in my senior year where students would be given absolutely no information and kept in classrooms for hours at a time during lunch periods and not allowed to leave or lunch was never brought until way after the fact..? (When there was not necessarily even a threat ever) I could go on and on but to sum it up, River Ridge High School is a complete JOKE. Go somewhere else and save yourself from the worst four years of your life.

column1: I disagree, Chandler Park is a great school. Staff is strict on uniform because, its a College prepatory School which means people come to visit our school, and they always want are attire to be right. You must mintain a gpa of 2.5 to stay at the school. Also teachers may seem like they teach lower level work, but its curriculum and material thats on ACT and thats what they teach us. Our school pays every year to take us on college tours to a variety amount of colleges for FREE. Plus we have dual enrollment classes, and college classes.....so when we graduate we already would have college credit and possibly an associates degree. Its a great school, their only trying to plan us for the REAL WORLD. Chandler Park Academy High School is a very great school. My daughter is a straight A student who is involved in many activities. She was once a shy student but has come out of her shell and is opening her eyes to all the opprotunties that her teachers are giving her. She is now involved in Marching Band, Nationals Honors Society, Peer Mediation, College classes and many more. This school has many opprotunties for your child to succeed only if your child wants to!!!

column3: National Honor Society induction this year ==> The principal did not show up. The vice principal did not show up. The superintendent did not show up. Kids and parents were dressed up in their Sunday clothes. So sad. Bond just passed commits 40% of total to athletic facilities. No mention of STEM. We just lost our ranking as one of "Americas Most Challenging High Schools" Washington Post. Gee, I wonder why. A school going downhill fast. The buses from Dripping Springs now swing thru the smarter neighborhoods to pick up kids whose parents are "in the know". We moved here many years ago before my children reached school age to ensure they were in WISD. My son is dyslexic which we may not have known as early as we did, had it not been for a great kindergarten teacher. He has had the BEST support to assist him with learning to advocate for himself and to become self reliant. He is graduating with a great GPA and acceptances to several colleges but most importantly his self esteem is good and I have no concerns with his academic readiness when he leaves for college. My daughter is the consummate high achiever and her hardest critic is herself. Wimberley ISD has been as much a benefit for her. She is a well adjusted, highly competitive in academics and sports. The staff has been wonderful and even when not agreement, they have shown to have my children's beat interest at heart! Couldn't ask for more! Our school unlike others is very friendly. I'm not saying there's never bullying, but when there is it's very mild and the furthest it'll most likely go is just a bunch of name calling, because in out little town you know everyone and they all know you, so there's not much reason to fight. I think others should know that we have excellent teachers and students! I love our athletics, not because the whole world revolve around it but because not only do our coaches want us to play well, but they ALWAYS put school work first as it should be. Our athletics also has many amazing coaches who give a tips to improve and they have zero tolerance for team mates being mean to each other. What could improve my school you may ask? Well many things could, but the main issue is that we aren't able to get everything we may need. Our English teachers are working with really old books, our art teachers don't have tons of money to keep buying new supplies for us, etc. Unorganized staff. Unqualified teachers. Football is more important than academics. The technology department is the worst!! Small town, small minds. Teachers are okay.textbooks are old.the superintendent is pathetic at best.The school only cares bout football.Coaches used to be good until coach nelms left and took all the good coaches away.Now all we have is wackos trying to teach my kid on how to play a sport that the coach never played. As a parent with a dyslexic student I could not be more satisfied. My second child is a high academic achiever A well S an athlete and very happy with their working to ensure she can do all she wants and maintAin academica Wimberley High is a joke. It's all about who you know or who your daddy knows. If you weren't born and raised in Wimberley Texas, you're automatically not as good as everyone else. The coaches only care about their coaching record, they couldn't care less about helping you become a better athlete. The teachers are unqualified to say the least, i often find myself having to teach myself. The assistant principal is pathetic, the only way she solves any problem is by giving the student in school suspension or sending them to AEP. Majority of the students that attend this school are stuck-up rich kids that have been handed any and everything they want by mommy and daddy, and don't know or show any respect towards working for what you receive. And outcast the students that actually have to put in effort and work for everything they have. Welcome to Wimberley, where if you don't have X amount of dollars, you're not as good as us!! This school and local business take money from Paul Mayhew to ensure that Mayhew Children get all the local scholarships. and other perks. Very good. As a parent I feel my daughter is receiving a high education. The Career and Technical Education Department is one of the best in the State. The facilities are new and state of the art. I’m very thankful for the atmosphere my child is in here. The teachers are great and challenge the students. If you look at score and AP scores WHS is in the top 20% in the state. It’s a great place and I wouldn’t send her anywhere else. This school is not an inclusive school. If your child doesn't fit inside the box they are an outcast. They teach for test scores not for learning. You must color in the lines or there will be a target on you. Being a single parent...is not inside the lines. Not being an active member of the PTA (I work full-time)...not inside the lines. Child is an independent thinker...not inside the lines. Child advocates for the underdog...definitely not inside the lines. Child stands up for themself...not inside the lines. Child's friends that are LGBTQ are constantly picked on and harassed in the halls. Special needs kids are intimidated and laughed at. Some of the teachers don't follow the state laws as what is appropriate to talk/not talk about in class. This little town is years behind others. My child has gone here from kindergarten thru high school. So, parent beware bullying still exists in this community. Once you get past the fake friendliness of this town, you will see its true colors. Its funny, when reading reviews for anything you can tell who the winers are. I had two children go through WISD and my children couldnt have had two more completely different paths, but both would have said WISD was a great school. My son played all the sports, was on the honors society, middle of the road grades and my daughter fell into the theater crowd and was an average grades kid. The funny thing is my daughter thought she found her people in the theater kids.... only to find out mean kids are in every group. So yes, bullying is everywhere, and the school does what it can but you cant control everyone. If anyone complains about the school not helping I call Bull on that. Ive had issues and they took care of the situation. Wisd was an overall great school for both of my kids.

column1: I was SO happy when this school opened with such quality teachers, administrators, and facilities. I have two children that attend Woodgrove High School and we have all be very pleased with every aspect of the school. They are both on sports teams with quality coaches and have had fascinating projects and learning experiences as part of their academics. They have a real bond with their fellow students, teachers, and other staff at the school. I could not be happier with the educational experience that they are receiving at Woodgrove HS! This school has no leadership. The quality of the education is substandard and they just teach multiple choice and to the SOLS. There is no depth in the subject matters. There is no real diversity. The new building is nice but you have to have the talent to fill it. The students here are truely getting a low standard of education compared to Eastern Loudoun or Fairfax This school is not spending our taxes wisely. They have assemblies to figure out how to buy class rings. Some of the teachers certifications can not be found on the state teacher certification site. Some of the teachers will lose paperwork and the student pays. I handed a teacher some paperwork early and my son did not get credit, his work was lost. My son found out a teacher was giving extra classes in the evening yet when he attended the classes inexplicably moved. The sciense labs appear truly impressive yet not enough learning is happening. The Leadership has been provided with information on working programs elsewhere in the county yet nothing has been implemented in two years. You must have internet for the homework. The bus schedule gets you to school in time to run to class and takes over 60 minutes to get you home. Trying to get homework done with these constraints does not work well. The Tech Ed teachers and the coaches seem to be doing a great job! The concern for the student appears paramount! Learning and growth appears prevalent in the STEM courses. This isn't the right school.... Woodgrove is not located in Leesburg. This is the address of Tuscarora. A fantastic school - there is now tremendous energy and enthusiasm. My son really enjoys all aspects of Woodgrove! Keep up the great work! This school has gorgeous, new facilities but had a rough start in the leadership department with 3 different principals in the first two years. The administrative issues seem to be ironed out now. I am truly impressed with the quality of teachers and academic assignments that my children receive. The arts programs also seem to be well run. The reason I did not give the school five stars is because of the costs. I thought public education was free in the U.S. The fees at this school are constant: $200 for a student parking pass, $100 for each sport per student, fees for labs, uniforms, yearbooks, school photos, graduation, sports equipment, musical instruments, school supplies, PTO dues, Booster club dues, etc. Additionally, there are non-stop fundraisers. My other main complaint is that there is no bus to bring home students who stay late for sports or extra curricular activities. Taxes are high in this county, so I didn't expect to have to pay for all these things. My 3 kids always attended private school before we moved here, and all the fees were included in the tuition, so it was a shock. This is really a top notch school. I have lived in many places in this country - really all over the place - and education just doesn't come better than here in Loudoun county. It's private school quality but at a public school. Lots of opportunities for students to be challenged as much as they want. Also excellent vocational preparation. I see a parent that complained about fees at this school. Although I agree there can be a lot of fees, overall it's really not much to pay, and Loudoun county has relatively low cost per student in terms of taxes - just compare to neighboring counties! This school is outstanding! We just attended graduation and could not believe the success of the students. Many are headed to Ivy League schools and top notch schools around the country and in Virginia. The Principal is great! He is very articulate and he is everywhere and really facilitates a positive environment in the school and community. The staff seem genuinely interested in helping students achieve success. We feel so fortunate to have moved into this community and look forward to our other children becoming Woodgrove Wolverines! Both of my children graduated from Woodgrove -- great school. Academics and athletics are spectacular. The guidance department is the best in the county. We actually moved to go to Woodgrove and never regretted one day. This is a bad school lazy teachers and an absent administration. Every time I ask to speak to the principal he is not available! The most political school I have every experienced! If you are not locally born you don’t stand a chance at this school. Two students were recently arrested for armed robbery and breaking and entering into homes. This school is not building leaders they are building cheaters! We have had a wonderful year! Had a sophomore and a senior. They both have flourished and I truly think it was a blend of the administration, the counselors , and the school as a whole! Wonderful counselors and admin office. Very helpful and always with a smile. This was not what we were expecting for our teens. Very disappointed Mr. Sharp is the best teacher ever!!!!!! An exceptional school. Teachers are compassionate, counselors are supportive, and the administration, led by a phenomenal principal, are always there to support students. The academics are second to none considering both AP and DE opportunities. Students who put forth the effort will achieve success. We’ve enrolled our kids in several high schools, both public and private, and Woodgrove, without a doubt, is the best of all. We feel fortunate to be apart of this school. Poor Leadership, pull the door badge records the principal is gone by 2:00pm. Gym classes have zero structure it's nothing more then out of control recess. I would not recommend this school.

column3: Three of my children attended the "new" high school and have since graduated. I really don't have anything good to say about this school. This brand new building leaks when it rains. Air quality is a nightmare. Many teachers and staff have issues with the air quality as well as many of the students. School is run as if it's a prison. Drug issues are very prevalent in this school as well as many fights. Books and essentials to learning are horrendous, if existent at all. Considering North Haven receives grant money the school should not be in disrepair nor should the students have to do without learning essentials. If you have a choice, I would definitely NOT send my student to this school. This school is a joke. The teachers are terrible, they don't care if students pass or fail. They allow the out of town students to go around and do whatever they want, but if an intown student were to do it they will get into trouble. The drugs that go around the school are ridiculous, kids going into the bathroom to pop/snort pill. They only good part about the school was the security guard, and they got rid of him. As a former student, I can honestly say that this school is the reason why I am so successful today. NHHS fosters a safe, comfortable, and stimulating learning environment. There are plenty of opportunities to become involved and to do whatever it is that you enjoy. The faculty cares so much about the well being of the students, and as long as you put in the effort you will reap lifelong benefits from attending this school. Bad, they don't care about what's right and whats wrong. They only care about what makes them look good. Awful, a constant political push from staff via pointless assemblies that won't really change the opinions of people who think the opposite of what they push. There wouldn't be much of a problem with that at all if it wasn't all just for their positive public relations, unfortunately they feel the need to make themselves look good rather than focus on the actual well-being of their students, that could be an issue with public schools overall though. a lot of kids in this school like to hang out in the bathroom and do drug and that is not good My experience with both of my very different children at NHHS has been excellent! As a current student, I have had a stellar experience at North Haven High School. Caring, able, and great teachers and administrators. Amazing programs, and a great school!

column1: Centauri is a great high school and does more with less than any high school around. Look at the scores it receives despite having the demographics it has. Proof is in the data. Principal is awesome. Super high school and great place to be. Good leadership and good teachers produce good kids. Even though they won't get the credit they deserve, CHS is one great school. From leadership to kids, Centauri has great things going on. A or B+ rating with 68% free or reduced student population. Rated 7th in Colorado by having the greatest difference between the "expected" ACT scores and the ACT scores they get (data by Aspen Foundation/Roaring Fork Asst. Supt.). Principal was a finalist for principal of the year in 2013 and is the Colorado Principal of the Year for 2014-15. Kids are really good kids and teachers bust their tail for kids. Sports are really competitive and they have a whole bunch of activities and clubs that give kids some really neat experiences. Have another Boettcher scholar winner this year and a 98% graduation rate for the last 8 years. Centauri says goodbye to the 2014 Colorado National Principal of the Year. However, another good administrator fills the position.
