column3: If you want your child to fail send them here. Although my daughter passed her classes with A & B grades they did not issue her credits for that semester. The assistant principal failed to let us know. When trying to correct the situation I received excuse after excuse. I was expected to be psychic and know what was going to happened. Horrible school and I am very disappointed! Teachers and administrators really care about student success and do everything they can to help students. Also, great music program!

column1: I don't even know what to say besides this is literally the worst school on the face of the earth. DONT BRING YOUR KIDS HERE. Excellent, excellent, excellent. Great caring teachers, friendly stuff, amazing fine arts program. Amazing community involvement and support in the school. I've attended this school for three years, so I feel as if I have a well-rounded opinion. The school puts a lot of effort in certain areas of improvement, but the downside is that most of the teachers won't care about you unless YOU as a student show that you care. If you put in effort, that teacher will care. There is a lot of involvement in sports and other clubs, which is good. Students go wild at football and basketball games, and the stands are always full. One downside is that the school is focused on always making scored high to look good. They just want students to score well on standardized and ACT/(now SAT) tests to they look better academically. The board doesn't care about the students, but counselors do. Many interesting classes are offered starting sophomore-junior year too, and early graduation is an option. A major downside is that the school is less diverse, and that it is in the middle of cornfields. Their lunch is not stellar at all, thanks to a certain First Lady... However, they do offer some very good alternatives and snacks. They keep VERY good track of anything bad going on inside the school, and bullying isn't really an issue anymore. I am a parent where 2 students have graduated, and my 3rd student will graduate this year from Burlington Central High School.I have found several of the sports programs excellent from the standpoint that the coaches are passionate about the sport and encouraging students.If you have a student with any special needs you will not get the assistance or support that your student and family need. RUN GO TO ANOTHER DISTRICT!The administration, councelors.. including social worker, dean, psycologist, principal, any staff member that may participate in an IEP or 503, have been unprofessional, seems to have delayed support, poor communication, and essentially they do not know what to do with this new diagnosis. When your student and family learn about a new disability diagnosis, you need a supportive district, not one that adds more stress and is antagonistic towards your student and family. i have had two children in the district. One with severe learning deficit. They didnt have the resources or staff with any experience. I had to hire a advocate to help me get my daughter into a program, Mid-Valley. My second child is in the highschool, I called a meeting to ask for specific help(she has a IEP) but so far none of the teachers have gone above and beyond. I even accidentally recieved a email between two staff members who were making fun of my daughter. Overall, definitely not recommended. The different departments for the school are all bad, except maybe the english and the math department. Homework is a pain to keep track of, especially since everything is online and your calendar is spammed with classwork, which makes it difficult to find your actual homework. Tests are bad. Many of the teachers use other teachers tests, which means there are many things on there that no one in the class knows about. Overall a poor experience with the teachers and departments of this school. The students and bullying policies are ok I guess but the school does nothing to enforce the dress code policy. This school lacks respectable teachers. The students don't respect many of the teachers due the daily actions of the teachers. Techers are trying to be the students "friends" instead of authoratative figures. There aren't enough opportunities to challenge those students who excel in school. Other districts have so many more options for AT students. As far as the administrative staff, they are not willing to step out of the box to help a student in need. They would rather sweep things under the rug and keep things quiet to protect their tiny school. They are not putting the children first! If you are looking for sports don't expect many opportunities. They offer very few sports in this district. Wonderful faculty and they are striving for improvement on all fronts. It was okay. It's a high school, with a great band but not much else. The music department is far and away the best in the region, and we're given a lot of opportunity to take advanced and AP classes, but as a high school, it's pretty average. My experience at this school has not been great. I thought it would get better, but it never did. As a teacher, I did not have the support from administration that I hoped. I cannot discredit everyone at this school, because there are some teachers and faculty members that did provide support. It is great that there is a teacher's union to help us. If you do not fit the description of a straight, white male, I do NOT recommend working at Burlington Central High School. You will be discriminated against, whether you see it or not. It would be great to bring change to this school, but it will be very difficult to do. It is a shame to think that students receive education in schools that reflect this type of negativity. Terrible school for my children I regret sending them there. One of the wordt schools ever. Teachers are poor and kids are way out of line.

column1: I graduated from Prep in 1996 and will always look back on the experience as one of the best things in my life. After years in the Millard school system, the studies were challenging and while I never really felt like I fit in, the experience shaped me and prepared me for life better than I ever could have known at the time. The teachers are all in, and are working to bring out the best version of you possible, and to prepare students to be independent post HS. Regarding academics, college was a breeze after attending Prep. I wish every young person had an opportunity to attend a school like this as the world would be a much better place. Unfortunately, Prep can no longer live up to its own mission of developing “men for others”. Rampant racism, sexual harassment, and bullying, paired with an administration that cares more about optics and money than they do people, places this institution at the bottom of the private school pile in Omaha. There are many great teachers, students, and parents involved at Prep, but the culture is absolutely toxic and debilitating. Cannot recommend Prep for any adult or child.

column3: ABSOLUTELY WONDERFUL! WOULDN'T SEND MY CHILD TO ANY OTHER SCHOOL! Totally recommend it if your planning on switching your child to another high school. Too much focus on staff and administrators and not enough on students! Way too large of classes and forget individual attention. AP classes are offered but no real help once you are there. Old outdated facilities. They just used cardboard to stint a kids injury on the field. They did not even have a flat medical board to carry an injured player off the field. Unacceptable sports management teams and incompetent fields crews. Concessions came through the cardboard for support.

column1: Coleman is very community-minded and prioritizes the school. The administration has recently gone through some staff changes, but seems to have kept the focus on student success. The teaching staff overall maintains an upbeat, cheerleader-type attitude. College-bound graduates I have watched are largely prepared for the next phase of their education. Downfalls are the lack of involved parents, the 60% poverty-level, and few opportunities for advanced students to excell. The lack of special education opportunities for children who need that extra push is what gives the low score. When parents call out for extra help with their child's schooling, they are ignored. Instead of helping the chd out, by placing in a smaller classroom setting, they recommend medicating your child, if they qualify for it. When I was in school here, there was a smallwr class size for kids who needed that extra one on one teaching. Maybe 8-10 kids in the class. Now instead of this, if your child has the attention span of a bumble bee in a field of flowers, they send the child to the "resource room" with an adult who has no educational teaching background. Then they wonder why the child is not passing any of their classes. Or a phone call home to the parent to come get the kid for not paying attention. This never was the case when I was growing up. A stern talking to and moving if a desk and by gosh the parents could actually have a job. The lack of extra curiccular activities is atrocious. Took away wood shop and auto shop for agriculture. I'd rather my children learn how to fix a vehicle! You practically have to be with your child their entire school year to make sure they don't fall thru the cracks. And if your name doesn't rank high on their list of popular families...forget it. There is a large lack of opportunity in the school. It is also taking in more students with learning disabilities than it can handle for money and not helping them.

column3: Sent four kids to this school. Wish that I had an affordable alternative. Not one came out able to put together a coherent paragraph. Two of them blossomed in college, third may be so lost that he can't be redeemed, and 4th still wasting her time at the high school. All three who are out feel cheated by the experience in light of college experience. Lots of busy work, teaching from texts. Paucity of analytical thinking. Science classes without meaningful labs. Too many teachers with short timers syndrome. Feel sorry for the few teachers trying to make something happen with all the dead wood. Athletics are a disaster, essentially child care with participation awards. Parental involvement is bait and switch. . . appears extensive but mostly platitudes. Town demographics (well educated and affluent) mask student learning deficiencies. Students learn at home how to talk like the man on the 6 o'clock news. But ultimately until they leave for college they don't realize how banal their high school experience was. Emphasis on encouraging students to think and engage in the subject matter and not just score well on tests or jump through hoops by an excellent teaching staff is a major factor in making Ashland High School, a truly great school. Students, faculty, administrators and the parent community work to create a school culture where helping others and working together as a team is valued. With the support of their teachers, administrators and community, Ashland High School students are doing great things . . and go on to doing great things when they graduate. ashland high school all about politics school, they all stick together even if it is wrong doing, and do not correct the problem or concerns of all, only the problems they want to Severe bullying issues that the school sweeps under the rug and refuses to deal with - even when police are involved. DRUGS are everywhere (all kinds of drugs) and most of the teachers lack enthusiasm. We have had a terrible experience and have decided to home school (although a big factor in making the decision to move here was for the "high quality schools" - this has not been our experience). Very disappointing. My daughter started at Ashland High School in the middle of her sophomore year, and we were anticipating a difficult transition. We were delighted to find the faculty, staff, and students at Ashland High to be very warm, welcoming, and inclusive. AHS is run more like a college than most high schools; there is an open campus policy and classes have a mix of ages in them. The academics are terrific without being overly stressful. Teachers don't demand more homework than kids can handle. There are plentiful academic and elective courses to chooses from, as well as a wealth of extracurricular activities. We are very happy that we moved to Ashland, and AHS has contributed to that greatly. this school is so left wing if you're a conservative, a Christian, a republican or even a political centrist you will be bullied by students and staff. The teachers indoctrinate liberal ideals and allow for no open discussion. Any traditional minded student is ostrisised and discriminated against constantly Not nearly as good as advertised. A huge amount of energy is spent 'marketing' the school to parents, students and the community and I think it inhibits the district from admitting to problems and dealing them forthrightly. I hate it. Unfortunately, it's the best option we have. Ashland has some nice ideals, but it is also pretentious and snobbish. Big fish in a little pond. Some really bright kids can do well there, and if your teen is heavily into the Dramatic Arts, it's a great school to launch their career. When deciding to move to Ashland, I did lots of research on the schools. At that time their schools seemed good but since moving here, they have failed many students. Kids with learning disabilities or that need adjustments to curriculum, seem to not be considered much. It's a one size fits all method of teaching, and some kids are certain to fall through the cracks. It seems like a lot of the teachers and office staff can't be bothered with the needs of their students... And most of them will try to put everything on the parents. It's always the parents, and never the school's lack of effort to properly accommodate each individual student, to them it seems everyone must fit in their box.. some of the office staff are dry.. attendance lady is RUDE. Some good teachers, some not so good. The left hand doesn't know what the right hand is doing.. I wish zero was an option. We originally sent all three of our children to Ashland High School. Our son graduated in 2020 and his experience was okay. In fact back when he was a freshman or sophomore I felt proud to say he attended AHS. My husband and I have been big supporters of Ashland Schools for many years by volunteering and financial donations to both educational and sports programs.I can honestly say this high school is currently a horrible environment. We transferred both of our daughters from AHS to different schools last year. Luckily, they are thriving in their new schools. I won’t go into detail about the school but will say that the students are in charge and the focus is not on education. If you prefer your student focuses on gender, pronouns, bullying, and in general creating chaos in the classroom it may be a good fit. Keep in mind parents will not get support from AHS staff if your child doesn’t agree to it. Again, children are in charge.Sad to see this school become such a disappointment. Maybe someday it will return to some version of what it use to be. Luckily, I no longer have to worry about it. This message is meant for prospective families to read and consider before deciding Ashland High School is the right place for their kids.

column1: For many years I've had issues with this school and the district in general. It all started when I wished to transfer back to public high school after a year at private school. The teachers and administration would not help me get things in order nor would they get involved in any way. When I had problems they didn't help and I know I'm not the first these problems. Also they do not allow students to excel or graduate early and could care less about a student's future or ambitions. All it seems Mill Valley cares about is sports and looking good on paper. They do not actually care about students and their educations. Mill Valley has been a good school for my three children. It has significantly improved academically over the years and is becoming a GREAT school. There is a core group of "rock star" teachers your students definitely want to experience, ie., Mattingly, Habiger, Bogart, Keal, Dunback, Wieland, Strickland, Paredes, Chavez, DeWild, Swafford, Crosbie, H. Brown, just to name a few. These are teachers that traditionally teach honors or AP but well worth the effort!!!! The school has increased in size recently but it is not so big, where with reasonable effort, your child can succeed in sports, clubs, etc....However, be aware, many of the typical students are more interested in parties than the purpose of an education. Be proactive as a parent! Get to know your kids friends and parents before assuming they have the same values as you. Drinking among the student body is common and unfortunately, drugs are readily available, The "no tolerance" rule needs to be more consistently enforced among the teams and clubs. If you child says they are going to a party, there WILL be alcohol AND drugs. Going to these parties should be avoided. Parents, plan a supervised, safe alternative! This school is drug ridden also known as pill valley, administrations turns away from stopping the problem. This school is in need of a major over hall in how it is run. The school has many excellent offerings whether it be extracurricular or academic. The parents are involved and it has a good community feel. There is a rampant drug/alcohol problem that is semingly dismissed or ignored by either parents or staff. Unfortunately to the detriment of the students and school district it is crowed and getting more and more crowded by year. The next two middle school classes coming in are large and will make things very uncomfortable (students barely have time to eat lunch now) for the students and faculty. This could have been avoided with a recent boundary change that would have benefited both high schools in the district while keeping the academic standards high at both schools. Unfortunately athletics will be affected negatively at Mill Valley with no boundary change forcing the school to compete at the 6A level in the coming years. This has already been witnessed this year in football. We have a wonderful school district with limitless opportunities for students. Next time my hope is the BOE will make a decision based on what is best for the school district and not cave in to pressure from a select group of parents. We moved to be in the De Soto school district. They build on positive character traits and have a top down mentality rather than bottom up. MV is one of the best schools in the state. With current student population around 1,400 it is larger than it was a few years ago but the projections show slow decreases in the future. They have been expanding AP opportunities and are great at college prep. No school is perfect and I hate to hear that MV has a drug problem as I believe it is better than most, not perfect but good. Students do better with involved parents. MV has teachers and staff that connect with students, some excel and I am grateful that my kids have gone to school here. As an alumni just perusing on the internet to see how my high school ranks, I am relieved to see the overall consensus aligns with my own experience. I loved my time in high school and believe the education I received was strong and prepared me well for college. The community I was able to form with teachers and students alike during my four years at Mill Valley has supported me well and continues to do so. While there are some typical high school struggles, I believe Mill Valley High School is a great place for students to develop both in academics and in personal growth. Much of the staff has changed since my time at the Valley so my understanding of the current environment at the school may be out dated- I have ranked the below topics to the best of my own knowledge.

column3: My son attended this school for his senior year only. After years of determination and hard work at his old school for an honors diploma. He graduated with over 60+ credits, a scholarship to UK and the only recognition that he received was a low quality sticker on his diploma! I do not recommend students busting they're hump on AP classes & honors diploma when this high school doesn't even recognize their hard work! At my sons old school, they recognize EVERY scholarship and EVERY ounce of hard work! This school is so CHEAP that they'll allow the students to walk through hallways with little to no lights & charge parents outrageous book "rental" fees for text books that are falling apart! They constantly complain about being broke yet they have the funds to replace the field house flooring every 2-3 years! This like most Indiana schools are a complete disappointment! I attended this school for most of my high school years. Bullying, sexual harassment, and many other things are handled wrong. I switched to online schooling my senior year and had to drop out because my counselor was adamant that someone had done my online schooling for me.

column1: Miami Norland Senior High School appears to be a great school to attend. My peers have great pride in their school. They conduct themselves appropriately. They have great amounts of respect for their teachers and all staff members and fellow classmates. I am proud to be a Viking and walk through the halls of Miami Norland Senior High School with great pride. Because based on the struggle that we currently are enduring, the students and staff members are so highly motivated to make a change. We are currently considered a failing school based on the school grade but our students are rearing the change this. Our teachers have been going the extra mile to ensure that the students are not only provided with the needed resources to achieve but also provide students with nurturing and guidance. In short, we are giving students an outlook that will increase their productivity in the future. We are now ensuring that students are enrolled in AP and dual enrollment courses, increased summer internships and hands-on extended curriculum activities. I love the eagerness and drive of my school. I love Norland Senior High School because the staff and employees are dedicated to helping the students to achieve their maximum potential! Great faculty, excellent library media services. I live in the community and therefore I have a vested interest in the education of the students, they are my neighbors. I see them at the library, at stores, at the parks; I need to know that they are educated and contributing members in the community and to society at large. I need to see them show school spirit by saying "hi" with a smile, showing Norland like behavior, which is exemplary, and wearing school colors on their jackets and uniforms. I love my community, especially the school where I work, I wear my colors daily, I am a die hard Viking with a lot of pride! Go Vikings! Despite all the challenges you have students that are talented and optimistic about each day that passes by. They are creative and competitive. The enhance curriculum which prepares students for college and the world of work is geat for student achievement. I went to this school and it is horrible. You are better off home schooling your kids. I went to this school and it was horrible. It's is highly unorganized and rude. The school is nasty and the student are disrespectful. I highly recommend you don't go to this school. Some teacher are good but most act like the students and don't care about school. This school mostly cares about its extra curriculum activities likes sport. The sport teams are good but they only care for the "great" players. Every sport out there has favoritism and wouldn't care if a player doesn't get in the game. This school will only bring your child down. Also lunch sucks!

THEY ARE THE BEST!! THANK YOU GROVES FOR HAVING AMAZING COUNSELLORS TO LEAN ON!! I am currently at groves, however I am switching to seaholm nest year. While I have been at groves, it has not been a good experience. The teachers were nice, and the counselors were helpful, the people there aren't all that nice. I know that most people say that groves is a very inclusive place, that is not at all how I experienced it. I am counting down the days until I never have to step foot in that building again, and I am hoping that things will be better at seaholm. Exceptional! Dr. Embekka Roberson (Thompson) is a wonderful principal. She doesn’t just talk in circles about issues, she listens and solves problems. She is visible in our community. Dr. Roberson is patient, kind, and strong.

column3: Brownfield High School offers many extracurricular activities and an impressive list of Dual Credit and Career and Technology Opportunities. I am impressed at the dedication and effeorts of teachers at BHS. Go Cubs! BISD can be a great school, the administration ties the hands of the teacher. Disruption in the classroom is a common pratice and the front office lets this slide. The turn over rate for Math teachers are terriable. Most students dislike math at the High School level and homework is a must to catch them up since a lot of the students have problems with 2nd grade math. The HS admin. turns a blind eye. Wouldn't hire new math teachers, some students went without a math teacher for almost a year. Funding is spent mostly on football team. They used to have a dress code now the kids are allowed to look indecent. Some of the teachers want to be friends with the students and don't care about the students education. Spent millions renovating the football stadium instead of hiring new chemisty and math teachers. For 2 years the high school has gone without a real chemistry teacher, and for decades hasn't offered any higher math courses leaving student woefully unprepared. The statistics speak for themselves, as in all the STAAR statistics, nearly half of the school fails in all categories. A bad school in a bad town. Avoid Brownfield as if it was plague infested. They don't really care about students they just focus on sports. They spent tons of money making a new field house instead of making repairs to the middle school which is like falling apart. They act so fake when state officials come to inspect the school. They're constantly having to replace teachers. It's not really a good school to go to.

column1: Great school with high values. Kids are happy and safe. Teachers care. Parents and teachers share true concerns over their child(ren)'s future. This school is a shell of what it once was. Around 2002, the trouble started, when the talented administration was forced out, and the current one, with its obsessive focus on punitive punishments and curriculum focusing on teaching to the test was forced in. Too many teachers are inexperienced and lack the ability to manage a classroom, and one-third of seniors graduate and go on to require remedial-level courses at college. By contrast, in the 1990s, Avonworth graduates were lauded for being among the best prepared first-year college students in the state. Its middle school is good, but skill gaps become apparent in the 9th grade, demonstrating that the administration prioritizes teaching to the test over true academic mastery. All the PowerPoint classes and senior projects in the world cannot replace the comprehensive liberal arts education this district gave up when it sent good teachers away on early retirement. Send your children to North Hills or North Allegheny if you want them to enter college well prepared, because this school will not get them where they need to be. We moved to where we are 10 years ago because of the school district. Once you leave the elementary school it is straight down hill from there. Questionable practices by the now Principal is just that. Parents are informed, usually, by teachers on concerns of their childs performance in class. Getting any extra help or ideas to help your child is never offered. If your ideas aren't convenient for the teacher well tough luck for you. So after paying your thousands of dollars in school taxes be sure to have more to have a tutor on your payroll. You will have a second job searching the PA laws to know exactly what help they are required to offer & ask about it specifically or you won't be offered it. this school is Gucci, gud skool, gud adjemication. 12/10 would pet nice smol class sizez, great education. send your kids here not North Hills There are a lot of great teachers, but poor administrators. The school sweeps all of its problems under the rug. There are drugs here, cheating, bullying and nepotism. Go to Quaker Valley. There is an EXTREME lack of diversity in this district. My experience was a good dose of white privilege Other than an issue with one of the teachers, I think that they’ve done ok I have several children enrolled in the district, and I can't say enough positive things about their experiences. They have been helped with emotional issues by their teachers and counselors, given opportunities to excel from GATE instruction as well as regular classroom instruction, regularly encouraged by enthusiastic teachers and principals who expose them to different programs and new ways of instruction, while keeping learning fun and exciting with special programs and fun themed days, etc. I have worked in many of the school districts in the surrounding area, and chose the Avonworth area to live primarily because of it's school district.

column3: Amazing teachers who really want to help students succeed. I would highly recommend this school to anyone else! The principal is a dictator not a Leader. No sense into appealing student punishments. Parent - principal conferences are not worth it. I graduated from LOLHS two years ago. If I had attended any other school that would not have happened. I messed up BAD my ninth grade year and spent the next three years doing online and after school courses to catch up. All of my teachers and my guidance counselor really helped me. Sad thing is, I know quite a few of the best teachers there recently retired. There are flaws in any school but, I think it is most definitely the best public school in Pasco. I have a child in the IB Programme here now in 10th Grade and we've been very disappointed in the quality of the teachers. It seems as though the older ones have really lost their energy and just read to the kids out of textbooks. Admin doesn't want to hear it. Period. My 10th Grader has great grades, but unfortunately, especially in the case of the History classes, is mainly self-taught. There is no engaging learning and videos, notes, PowerPoints, AP practice work, or visuals of any kind have to be tracked down by the student in order to learn the material. Classes also start at 7:30am which means kids do not get enough sleep with bus time and the school literally has not one window for natural daylight. Overall a depressing experience and I'm told the kids spend solid amounts of time sleeping in class due to the boring teaching methods, lack of daylight, and early hours. I suppose it's okay for a small town like Land O' Lakes, but overall not a pleasant high school experience. My son had the worst years of his life in this school. We thought the IB program would be different than the regular classes. Neither the teachers nor the students helped. Bullying affected my child’s life even after his graduation. They turned him from an A student to barely being able to find a college to accept him. He hated the school, the teachers, and the entire LandO’Lakes area and never even wanted to pass by. We kept communicating with the school members but they were not willing to address the elephant in the room. This school is not great at all. Especially in the sports arena. My son was harassed on the football team because they didn't think a black kid should be quarterback. He was attacked in the bathrooms as well as the locker room and the administration did nothing and neither did the coach. We hate LOL and the only people who say anything positive are non POC. Avoid this school if you can We’ve had four kids go to Land O’Lakes High school and they have loved their experience there. They have found friendships, camaraderie, community on the sports teams and they’ve done great academically. They have set my kids up for academic success and prepared them for college.

column1: I love this school. Im a senior and i came to this school bak in 5th grade. Yes it was somewhat hard to fit in but now everybody gets along in the highschool. The teachers are amazing and so is our curriculum. Its a little private school but has plenty of honors and AP courses. Heavy on sports and one of the top schools in wrestling (: School board qualifications should be higher. These people only need to be a resident of 1 year and to be at least 18 years of age. That's it! They do not listen. They fate of our children is placed in their hands! Reread their qualifications.They disrespect the tax payer by dismissing your concerns in hopes that you will just go away. They are a mess!! Go to a meeting with a serious problem...you will leave ill. I am currently a student attending Saucon Valley, and like the other reviews, I find it to be cliquey and very focused on social status. Many of the girls tend to gossip about one another and judge other students who do not meet their standards. I would not recommend other students to attend this school, though I myself am still here, I will be hopefully moving soon. However, the curriculum is very well developed and many of the teachers are especially qualified, specifically in the middle school. I know this review is not on the middle school, but I would like to say that I enjoyed having many of my middle school teachers and most prominently the gifted teacher, whose name I will remain up identified for the sake of privacy. She was the best teacher I have ever had and will most possibly uphold this spot for she had the ability to teach a subject and allow a through understanding by the student. I am saddened that there is no classes in the high school aimed solely to expand on creativity such as the classes I attended in middle school during an extension period, though there are AP classes. There are also many extracurricular activities to attend such as debate club or band.

column1: I have two daughters that graduated from Interlake and it was a great experience for both of them. My youngest just graduated this week and is going on to USC. I can't believe the comment that only football was a good sport there. Both of my daughters went to state multiple times in three different sports. The cross country coach is a former Olympian (1996, best American in the 10,000 meters!). The only concern we had was that the PRISM program (for talented and gifted students) are automatically alloted the top 50 slots in class ranking so that was a negative when it came to applying to colleges since the top schools want students who have placed in the top 10% of the their class. Interlake HS.... very disappointed, my child attended all four years, and two weeks before graduation in 2012 I was notified that my child was 1 credit short to graduate...when I had been told everything would be fine. So now I have a child with no high school diploma or assistance from the school on what to do now... My child has been so disappointed by this all dreams once talked of no longer exhist now working flipping burgers. Too much emphasis on gifted program. If you are planning on attending this school, I advise you to not sign up. Especially if you or your child is not a prodigy, like over half of the students here claim to be. I have first hand experience and the teachers here are for the most part, great. The teachers help most students directly if they need help; even after school they are available. On the other hand, there are those sour apples that just read off of a poorly made PowerPoint and become enraged when a student asks too many genuine questions. The biggest and most hard hitting factor in this high school is the students, don't get me wrong here (I am not anti social or have any social problems whatsoever) but they are extremely competitive to the point where people can become quite stressed. This is mostly due to the fact that there is a program called the PRISM or GIFTED program. First of all, it's called the GIFTED program- Now come on. GIFTED? Are you trying to make us (the average person) feel incompetent? Most of these kids are pumped full of pride and ignorance because they are shoved a mirage down their throats. There are still many students in the program that are very nice so don't judge please. I am a senior at Interlake. Interlake is a good school, but has a competitive atmosphere. Students are pressured to take more AP/IB courses than they can handle, but are looked down upon if they don t. Interlake has an open enrollment policy for AP/IB courses, meaning anyone can register for an AP/IB course without any prerequisites, teacher recommendation, or counselor approval. A student who was already getting C s and D s in math and science, like my sister, should not have been allowed to take IB Physics. Now that registration is online, parents don t know what their child signs up for unless he or she involves the parent in the process. The gifted program fosters unhealthy competition. Everyone is trying to outdo each other. Many Interlake students get less than five hours of sleep which is worse if students are also involved in after school sports. Many are. IB requires more critical thinking than AP and requires a host other assessments. The other assessments are no trip either. Look on the IB website for more information. If your child is not the best student, consider a different Bellevue high school. All of them are excellent and your child won t feel dumb. If you are looking for a school with a dedicated staff, great facilities, an accepting student body and any club/sport/activity you can think of this is the one. Yes there are very competitive kids here. No they do not hate on other kids. They go about there business of working hard and do not discriminate. The arts programs at this school are well funded and highly successful. This school offers higher levels of Chinese, Spanish and French than any other public school I have ever encountered. They have extremely high level math as well as fantastic teachers who support lower level math where students might be struggling. They have a fantastic computer science program as well as other electives that are career oriented such as business and marketing. Interlake I not limited as many people here have shown it to be. It has programs that are hard to find anywhere else. Such programs like horticulture and floral design where kids get the chance to work in on campus greenhouses. The sports at this school are as limitless as the clubs and just as accepting. I would highly recommend this school to anyone. You will never feel alone or out of place. Caring and effective staff, generous and hard working students, and tremendous parents. This is one of the gems of the Bellevue School District. My son attends this school and I am a middle school teacher in the district so I have an insiders perspective on the staff and curriculum. This school has a small school feel. All the staff know the students and take the time to chat with them in the hallways. Students feel supported and there are lots of opportunities to take advanced placement or IB classes. My son will have enough college credits to enter college as a Junior when he graduates high school! Love Interlake :) Everything about Interlake High School is great, from students to teachers. Excellent environment for multicultural learning. The school runs a gifted program with worst teachers. Pre Cal is taught my a very moody and disoriented teacher. Very few teachers are willing to consider child health accommodations and in fact mentions that they will not accommodate. The school needs to review its teachers and provide a means to feedback on their approach to students. Our child is graduating from the GHSP (gifted high school program) housed at Interlake and it has been phenomenal. The teachers are engaging, challenging, thoughtful, and do an amazing job at preparing these kids for college. Our kiddo has enjoyed (almost!) all of his teachers and we could not be more pleased with the education received . They never answer the phone or call you back if you leave a message! 2/10. No way this school makes your kid ready for college. They hand out IB diplomas like nothing and they don’t care about character. Only what’s on paper so that the incompetent leaders look good. I hated my experience at this school and the way the IB program was carried out here. I liked my freshman and sophomore year, but after I started the full IB program my mental health deteriorated. I couldn't approach any teachers about my circumstances because of the tight-knit academic atmosphere. Generally, I didn't find most of my teachers genuinely interested in my health but only in my classroom participation (This is solely based on the teachers I had, and I certainly had few teachers who cared about me). My counselor has been nice to me but the tense atmosphere in this school has negatively changed my personality. I got depression in junior year and I have even though of suicide before. This is such a closed topic because most IB diploma students here have all encountered this so it is just considered a part of the IB program's stress. I feel like if I went to a different school I could have at least not lost my self-esteem and performed better emotionally and academically. My biggest regret yet is going to this school because I have lost myself, my confidence, my bright personality, and my future opportunities. *This is my own experience and does not generalize all IB students and teachers here.* Overall, I have loved my time at Interlake. The teachers are mostly good, and I haven't had any problems with them. The language programs at Interlake are excellent, with extremely good teachers, albeit tough teachers, teaching each of Chinese, Spanish, and French.I get why people say that the gifted program can be quite clique-y, but understand that it mostly comes down to the fact that many people in that program have likely been classmates for 4-5 years or more, and so they tend to hang out with who they know. To my knowledge, the clique-y nature isn't really sinister most of the time, as many of the gifted kids are less social, and I see them tend to more stick to themselves. I also can understand why some people think that the gifted kids sometimes portray themselves as more "elite", which does happen to a certain extent, but it also comes down to the gifted kids having far different interests than the kids who aren't in the program. Many of the gifted kids really enjoy and excel at debate, science olympiad, etc., so that is what they choose to do, versus being interested in theater, art, etc.The sports at Interlake could use some work. The football team is usually abysmal, basketball is usually ok, but soccer tends to be pretty good. Interlake really excels at track, cross country, badminton, and tennis. Swimming is generally good, but can never beat powerhouse schools like Newport, and baseball and softball are pretty average I guess. The sports culture at this schools is also somewhat poor, as football games aren't really a big event and the homecoming game and the game against Sammamish are the only games you can really count on a lot of people being there.In terms of the IB program, yes it is tough. It is designed that way. I had a few classmates drop out, and their mental health improved drastically because of it. Essentially, if you don't think it is right for you, don't do it. I feel like a lot of people force themselves into it, but if you push yourself and stay focused in class, it is a really good experience that prepares students extremely well for college. One of my teachers told me that he has had students come back from schools like Harvard and Stanford telling him that college is easier than high school, and I think that is a good testament to how well Interlake prepares its students for college. I went here. Only grades were important; learning wasn't valued at all. Students were overly focused on test scores and uninterested in the actual content. it sucks because too many hard classes and bad gpa as a result

column3: "A" school for 2 years since 2010. The AP program is really good, teachers are willing to help their students to pass the AP exam, also great spirit for the football team. Country football champions 2012, and has not lose by any other school in the country since 5 years. My daughter went there last year and is now homeschooled. She was intimidated by the other students, lunch was stolen every day. Administration does not return calls. Teachers are inconsistent with keeping posted grades up to date, are disorganized with and sometimes cryptic with posting assignments and instructions. Often they take awhile to respond to parents requests. Guidance at school is mediocre Mrs. Bobay, the school guidance Counselor and others do work hard to do what's best for students, but I've had trouble with getting the staff to see things through to improve my child's performance or see their plans through to completion. I constantly struggled with my child son who always complained about not liking the school. I ve applied for a n out of area transfer as advised by other parents in my neighborhood. CHS has the potential to be a great school being directly behind a college. Sr. Staff is quick to suspend students for relatively minor infractions, where detentions would have been warranted in any other school. Once a student is suspended (In School) they are supposed to be afforded the opportunity to complete all class work for that day in ISS, but teachers do not submit class work for student to work on, and often will count the student absent instead. Every class drops almost a full letter grade for this type of disconnect. Cocoa High School, my older son went to CHS and had great teachers, wonderful staff. I know that they might have a bad rep because of rumors. But CH has some of the best teachers in Florida. My younger son will now enter the 9th grade and I have now worries. The only thing I could say about CH is that the staff should so the same respect for all sports not just he ones that win all the time. If they gave the same support for say like soccer as they do foot ball maybe it would boost the kids moral. cocoa high is one of the worst in the county, my kid will transfer, reminds me of a small sub of detroit. this is by far the worst school in brevard we have moved to melbourne and love it here . my kid goes to melbourne high school and loves it! This school is filthy and constantly has headlice outbreaks. Its policy on students of age making adult videos outside of school should be revised. I love the campus, the fact that middle and high school has different buildings, the staff seems caring and I love how Dean Halbeur handles bullying. Go Tigers! I have heard many negative things about this school, but my daughter has done so well since enrolling in September. She has ADD and struggled at her school in Maryland. She is on honor roll here and has been asked to take advanced classes next year. Her guidance counselor always listens to her if she has concerns and any questions I ever had are answered quickly. I'm a foreign exchange student and i think this school is terrible. I was excited about it because i thought all the "rumors" about it being a bad school were false. Turns out they were right all along. The school has many illeterate students who will not make it to college. I've been told not to think that the American education system is bad because of this school and my experience there. Some teachers teach wring stuff and ESPECIALLY, in the metric system, the school doesn't make any effort in raising its students to its level; in fact, it actually descends to the students' level of learning. They teach stuff that are known in any other school. The school focuses more about appearance than education purposes. Students there CAN'T read, they are junior year and i'm pretty sure that it's not their problem, but the school's. In conclusion, this Cocoa High School is very bad; it's terrible, based on my experience, and if you want your kids to have a bright future, or go to college, don't register them there. 0/10 When you call the school you get no one helpful, you literally have to walk in to the school to get ANYTHING accomplished. My son went to an alternative school and I agreed to it because they said it would be wiped from his transcript like it never happened, well we moved out of state and his transcripts showed that alternative school. The new school tried contacting Cocoa HS and they got the run around, sent to dead extensions, everyone they talked to said "oh so and so can help you" no return calls EVEN WITH THE VICE PRINCIPAL WHO IS THE ONE RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL DISIPLINARY ACTIONS. This is by far the WORST SCHOOL and honestly would do best if they had a full administrative overhaul.

column1: The teacers are helpful, the students are wonderfully behaved and there are little to no vandalism/drug/bullying/sexual harassment/gang/violence issues. This is one of the best scholls in Garden Grove District the assistant principle is always very helpful he tells the students when they have any problems question or just want to talk to come to his office.... The school was below average. The campus is horrible but the school is still remodeling. The students are isolated into groups and makings friends is difficult. Athletics aren't great. Overall the school isn't anything magnificent and the teachers aren't that helpful. One teacher stood out as a jerk and barely even taught the class. The staff holds the students to a high standard. Various courses are offered for all levels of learners. Students are given every opportunity to succeed if they do their part. The students are actually what make this school great; they are, generally, hard working and well mannered. The administration does not seem to have a clue about how some of the teachers conduct their classes. There are some teachers who are just too critical and even some who don't teach well. In today's competetive atmosphere, students are already anxious to excell, and instead of making it possible for students to do so comfortably, the school is structured such that kids have no time to get the rest that the administration, ironically, keeps telling us is so important for our kids' well-being! The school even had the nerve to hold sessions for parents on how to deal with students' anxiety. It would help if the kids had more than 30 minutes for lunch, some comfortable places to sit during breaks, and less hours spent on extracurricular activities' practice hours. With all that is expected of them, in addition to a campus that has been half under construction for the last few years, the fact that the students do so well can almost entirely be attributed to their own efforts. Bad, in general. I would prefer Bolsa Grande... My son went to this school and was bated into an argument by a faculty member. Since, my son was immature and could not handle being taunted in front of his class by his teacher, he lashed out at him, and as a result, he was reprimanded by transfer to another school. Now, this fulfilled at least a couple of faculty members wishes. One counselor, who was not my son's counselor, actually said my son would get kicked out of school. A teacher told my son the counselor said that about him. One might think that people become educators for altruistic reasons. However, that is not true of everyone. Idk, why would a school counselor say that about a child that is having problems?Just an update, my son is doing VERY WELL in college. In fact, he is getting all A's and B's and working on two degrees at the same time. He is going to become a pilot and a flight manager. He is talking about getting a Master's degree. Now, I know he will be successful. Too bad that doesn't fit into some of these faculty members little scenarios. Just because someone is a teacher it does not make them a prophet that can tell who will make it and who will not. In fact, they are doing these children an injustice by staying in the teaching profession, if they don't want to help everyone. If they are sticking their noses in the air at some of these kids. My son is much better than me. He wouldn't waste his time writing these people a bad review. We'll just see who becomes successful, won't we? This school has many good teachers and many teachers that are just going through the motions. The administration is uninvolved with the students. The principal maybe knows the names of 50 student. The principal and the majority of his supporting staff are unsupportive of the teachers when they ask for help. They are uneducated on the current laws as well as students with disabilities. The environment is not warm nor conducive to collaboration with families. It is their way or go somewhere else.Teachers are not held accountable when they do not follow and IEP. The staff has had no training on accommodations. If my child was not above average I would not send them to this school. When considering this school one should look at the transfer rate and the dropout rate. Graduation rate is not correlated with the freshman registration rate. It is based on how many of the 12th graders graduate.

column1: This school is the bomb digity, You should go here! I think it's great :) Small town, small town school! Seems that your childs success is based less on their ability, and more on their popularity. They set the students up for failure by pressuring them into taking CP classes, and lead them to believe that if they don"t, they will just be "flippin burgers" in a few years when the others have their college degree. So, they are shamed into taking classes that they may not be capable of passing, and now, ashamed of their parent who is "flippin burgers" for a living. If you are notified that the school is going to take disciplinary action against your child, then it is because you have the wrong last name or your child is not running in the right circles. It really is just like something you would see on tv. It is my opinion that this school lacks in any moral values. Small town, small town school! This school is full of ignorant, close minded, and shallow students. It's almost impossible for one student to be truly happy for another student because everyone is so cut throat. It seems that popularity and where the next party is is all that matters here. I fully believe that education is at the bottom of this school's priority list, as the teachers are less than satisfactory. The teachers themselves are too concerned with what the latest gossip is. The school is extremely unfriendly, unfair, and the only thing that seems to matter is what your last name is and how much money your parents have. If you are a football player here, the world is in the palm of your hands. Also, if you know someone "important" you pretty much can get out of anything. The "good-ol-boy" comment hit right on the spot with this school! And its not just within the high school, the school board is this way as well. I fortunately only had to deal with this place they call a "school" for two years before I escaped and spent my junior and senior year elsewhere. I would not recommend this school system to anyone! Seek other options!! I have had children in each of their schools. Coming from Talawanda School District I was very disappointed in the schools here. Teachers are stuck up, gossipy and small minded. My children have been witness to blantant racism, sexism and plenty good ol boy behaviors. When we first moved here I asked a group of teenagers what they do for fun here, their answer was sex and drugs. I should have ran, but chalked it up to smart alec teens. Unless you are in with the right crowd (ie multi generation family) there isn't much else in Eaton. You can't even as a parent join in to help support the schools because you are treated like garbage. Can't wait to sell my house and move my children to a better district. THIS IS THE WORST SCHOOL IN PREBLE COUNTY IF NOT OHIO!!! The teachers are ignorant and could care less about your childs education. The discipline is awful. Fights in the halls, racism around every corner, and lets not forget about the dozens of drug users in the school. The kids are stuck up and start a boat load of drama. I feel like I am honestly on Days of Our Lives like 99% of the time. There are a ton of dirtbags who only go to school to start drama. There is this one teacher in particular who only throws notes up the board, that he got from the textbook.. much like all the teachers. And he excepts us to learn, he doesn't care if we do the assigned work or not. This is how it is at Eaton High School. THE WORST SCHOOL IN OHIO, DO NOT SEND YOUR KID HERE!!!

column1: I attended Sparta High School and am proud that I went there. The teachers and coaching staff were excellent overall. I participated in cross-country and track. Ms. Lockhart was a fabulous, patient algebra instructor. I felt a part of the school community. GO SPARTA! This school is average. There are highs and lows. Many teachers will support you if you want. If you're lazy, they will not hesitate to let you fall behind. I attend MIT now, and a few of my graduating class also attend Ivy league schools. While I wasn't accepted to MIT due to my being at Sparta high, being in college now, I value what i did learn here. My education here was very good, because my parents decided to make it so. You can go far from being a Sparta graduate, but not without outside help. All in all, Sparta is a good platform to jump off of or fall from, but it really depends on your legs to see how far you land and how well you stand. I keep reading about how Sparta students don't get into good schools, but I'm a Duke grad. Of my friends who I graduated with, we have Princeton, Yale, Dartmouth, Harvard, UVA, and Stanford represented. I'm not sure what they're talking about when they say "You'll be lucky to get into Community College." I have 2 students that are recieving an excellent education as well as an experience. As a student I feel like this school should be akin to a anvil on your back with a led pipe stuck to the heel of your shoe. The moment I got here when I moved it has pushed me to the ground, if you are sick for just a day your grades will plummet the entire semester, it bathes in pushing you in group projects you clearly have no interest in. The buses are a mess, my bus drove past me twice in the first half of the year. The teachers are either the best people ever or so bland you actually want to skip school just so you don't want to speak to them. This school also uses google classroom, so you better expect to do constant work during breaks at home. My daughter has gotten a great education at Sparta High School. She is also into music and this school has an unbelievable music program. I would recommend Sparta High School to anyone. My children have all graduated from SHS, all have gotten into their #1 choice of colleges and all are having great success in their college careers. SHS is very competitive, and colleges see that by the class rankings. I think the kids who complained in previous comments didn't put in any effort but expected to get by. I would highly recommend SHS and the Sparta community to anyone! With the exception of very few, the teachers are top notch and very willing to help every student succeed and the new principal is all about the kids. We moved here from Virginia in 2013 and quickly found out that my daughter had some catching up to do in Sparta Middle School. She adapted and then exceled in all her studies. When she got to the high school it was an even better success in both academics and outside the classroom. I cannot tell you how wonderful the teachers and staff are at the High School. They are truly committed to seeing your child succeed. We choose to live in Sparta for the schools and as my daughter nears graduation this year and has been accepted to many colleges, it has proven to be the best decision we could have made for her education. Both of my kids had a horrible experience at SHS. Very overrated. Most of the teachers & administrators are miserable. If your child is not in the chosen circle they will not flourish. The students leave a lot to be desired. A lot of shenanigans & bullying just swept under the rug. Don’t believe the hype.

column3: I would never allow my children to attend this school - I would never want to put them through what I went through. Constant ridicule went on (more then Necessary) when I attended - Teachers heard but did nothing. I did not pass the 7th grade at this school, getting F's in every class - And in the end they moved me on the 8th grade without addressing the problem. There are no art classes in this school, which was awful. Over all terrible place - I cringe when I hear the name. Much like prisons, this school has severe attendance and disciplinary problems because it favors punishment over rehabilitation. Countless Sat. school sessions will not solve anything. The community is killing its children. I greatly advise referring to a school's website to gain general technical information regarding any school. This school's 2010 annual education report, found on their website, can be accessed through this link: http://www.ironwood.k12.mi.us/index_files/fullannualedreportLLW.pdf I agree with the comment on for the handfull of teachers who care, 2 handfuls don't. Agenda to use the restroom? Lose it and pay $5 for your child to be able to use the restroom. I think the health department should be called. Ask students to live the "Wright Way" when the teachers and administration don't. Have a dress code for students when teachers don't follow it. Have a problem with a teacher or administrator and go to the school board to have the 'good ol boys club' agree with teachers and blame the kids. Have 22 of 31 children in a science class fail and blame it on the kids. They teach for the MEAP, period. The school system here is, in my opinion, very corrupt. They do not give one priority about student education. All they like to do is cram kids into a building that has been in an existence since Ironwood's more progressive days. The kids here are very, very undisciplined. Some kids are alright and cool, but the majority just aren't all up to the bat. So, if you are considering going to schools in the Gogebic Range, keep this in mind. Throughout my experiences with Luther L. Wright, I have known it to be run by a staff concerned only with the politics involved. Student/teacher relationships are almost non-existent and there is an overwhelming sense of angst among the student body. Favoritism is shown to students who participate in athletics and scholastic achievements and personal worth are thrown under the bus. If you can at all avoid it, going to LLW is not the best choice. Not by a long shot. When you ask for help the teachers ignore you. They are not helpful at all. They like to sit there and make fun of students. They definately pick favorites if you are not in sports you are pretty much nothing. I think this school needs better/helpful teachers. So many people fail there classes because the teachers just ignore you when you ask for help. This school is just a joke in general. Needs helpful teachers that are willing to give you all the help you need and make sure you know what your doing. These teachers need to get off there butts and worry about the students education and how to help them pass the class. Hurley school is the highly reccomended school to go to. They will help you as soon as you ask for help. They care about you and your grades. The teachers are there to help your child get the education they need unlike Ironwood they are there just for the paycheck at the end. I highly recommend Hurley K-12 school. Wish the city would demolish and completely restaff from top to bottom Excellent programs and communication among the teachers/staff. My children have shown great progress by attending IWD schools. I would highly recommend. LLW is a great school. The teachers and staff really care for the students and do everything they can to help them to succeed. Very pleased with our children's education at LL Wright. Feels like a family. I always feel very welcome going into the school. Schools are a busy place, but it seems like the staff will do their best to make time for you. Overall it has been a great experience. I think that parents being a part of their childs education is just as important as the teachers. So if you're involved then your child will do great wherever they go to school. Very pleased with my child's education. I have a child that has graduated and gone on to have a very successful career and another child still in school. The teachers are very supportive of the children, diversity, and discipline.

column1: I am sad to say that sports is the only exciting thing about this school. Academic learning by itself is challenging especially for those in Alternative Education, as the Administration of the school low balls students who "don't fit in". Many teachers are disrespectful towards students, which can often be a two way streak, but the amount of targeting and rude remarks done by the teachers is outrageous. In 8th grade, a teacher wrote.me up for being late to class when I was on crutches for a knee surgery. Freshman year I got jumped at school by a junior and was later threatened by the school police officer of fining me with disorder conduct for "antagonizing" the fight. The only thing the staff in this school district prioritize is their paycheck and a grade. I have been raised my whole life in these schools and would never even consider taking kid here when I'm an adult. This school doesn't prepare kids for their life, and if they do, all it shows is the negative things in this world they will encounter.

I suggest if you do choose to attend or enroll your child make sure your voice is heard from the get go or you will receive no help. I am very disappointed in this school, been nothing but a nightmare Not strong enough leadership from the top . Poor communication after leaving messages for principal.

My daughter was a transfer student and did wonderful at Glenvar Middle.

column3: I'm not longer a student but graduated just a few years ago. I felt much more prepared for college than many of my peers and thought that rchs gave me every opportunity to excel. We also had many students attend high end institutions. I was surprised the rating was so low. This is probably attributable to a wide variety of students some who didn't care about school but many of those are doing well without college. Additionally from what I've heard from my college peers it seems like there was much less violence, drugs, and teenage births at Rockbridge than many higher rated schools in more suburban areas. Positive experience especially compared to middle school experience Overall I think RCHS is a good school. We have a solid Honors and AP program, as well as a great CTE program, and a strong student government. Having taught at this high school since it opened in 1992 until my retirement 2019, I can attest to the high quality of leadership, instruction, and coaching of the staff. Administrators and counselors were fair and honorable. Teachers dedicated themselves to instruction. Coaches cultivated long lasting relationships with the athletes. Students were interested in learning and participating in extra-curricular activities. The school was well maintained and cleaned regularly. The librarians were always helpful and instructive. The bus drivers took great care to maintain consistent civil behavior. Teachers often collaborated to teach jointly. Parents offered support for both the athletic endeavors and classroom instruction. It was an honor to serve the students at Rockbridge County High School.

column1: Canfield Local Schools are ranked one of the best in the state, and by far the best school system in the Youngstown area. After going there myself, I want to make sure my children have an education as fine as mine. Don't take it for granted, not everyone has the chance to be surrounded by great teachers and wonderful school system. Awesome schools. Awesome teachers and staff!!! Everyone has been so great to my son. worst years of my life, of your not a future nfl star or a doctor good luck! Both emotionally and physically scared after attending Don't just look at the scholastic scores and think that this is a great school! Horrible experiences with bullying here and not just us personally. Many students move or do open enrollment at other schools in spite of the academic score. Ask the district for the info... Students are disrespectful, mean and petty to each other. Police have been involved in many bullying incidents, everything is covered up and the public seems to have no clue. Administration and teachers look the other way. Do your kid a favor and run the other way. Bullying is a big problem at this school beware academics isn't everything Both my children were absolutely destroyed by this school. I am originally from Austintown, but moved to Canfield when my children were very small thinking it was i better school system. I never thought i would have to apologize to my kids for bringing them here. Mainly involving its sports, the school is plagued by community politics, bullying and the worst that i wouldnt expect would be allowed, retaliation. The past AD ruined the school, and turned away from any conflict and never questioned the coaching staff. I asked him one time, along with the head principle, what there priority was in high school sports. There reply "To win" saddened me as they have long forgotten the reason for high school sports. Feel free to do a records request, all coaching yearly reviews are blank. With the recent resignation with the superintendent, i hope it gets better for future students. Problem is, there is a new Superintendent, but the old bad worms and problems still exist. I went through a 7 year lawsuit, and instead of trying to fix the issues, they are brushed under the rug as they no the the problem goes away the following year until it happens to the next person. I vented a bit, i apologize, but beware of this school system. There is a reason they have the worst reputation in the district. It's a good school. As told by other reviewers, sure, there may be a bullying problem, but that doesn't necessarily mean that the district itself is horrible. Attempts at revamping the policies of student-to-student interactions is an attempt at fixing the problems reported by parents. Bullying, however, is the cause of parental influence. Every single school has a bullying issue, though this one just seems worse because it is smaller, and drama is inflated. Trust me, I know. However, throughout my years here, I have come to realize the influence that our teachers have on students. The teaching styles are unique and passionate, and I find myself going to class every single day excited to learn something new. I know many people absolutely love learning in these classes. People that believe that their children are being left in the dust are missing out on a key component of learning-- things like that happen. Some students are not as adept at learning as others. This is merely a fact, and it is not the school's responsibility to change the way a student thinks. This is the student's choice, so blaming the school for their failure is turning a blind eye to this simple explanation. The teachers at Canfield, from my experience, are solely there to help. They are not there to inhibit your child's learning. The vast majority of teachers here are overqualified for their jobs. Every single time I've asked for help I've been helped. Furthermore, sports are not associated with the quality of the school itself. Coaches are not directed by the school, and the Athletic Director is not going to be the person to confront about your child's playing time. Times are changed. Varsity sports are not mainly for fun. They are akin to college athletics. If you are worried for your child's well-being, there is always an explanation for bullying or mistreatment. Not everything is the school's fault. The programs in place for students are phenomenal, and if you don't see the opportunities offered by Canfield schools, then you are not paying attention to the full picture. Needless complaining gets you nowhere. Simply find the roots of problems with your child if you worry about bullying and stop blaming the school for every single negative interaction between classmates. School is about learning and finding who you are. It is not about parental interference against a misunderstanding that may hurt your child's feelings. This is high school. We are almost adults. We should handle it.

column3: If you are in the local "clique" you are ok, otherwise forget it. Your kid won't succeed here. This district teaches kids 'it's who you know" not "what you do" that matters. Just look at the staff at the school and their history in the district. It's very easy to see. Don't even think of bringing your child into this school as a new student. They will be miserable and driven out of any sports/activities. Again, it's about the clique and your connections in the area. The school cares more about sports than academics. This school rates success based on a high school sports career and not much beyond that. It's funny to hear others talk about the greatness of this place. It's mostly from those who have never lived or worked outside of the area to see and learn about the real world. This is not a place where your child can be prepared to succeed beyond Davidsville. Keep looking, especially if new to the area. We are not from the area. My children, previously in a local parochial school, came to this school not knowing anyone. Immediately they were well accepted by other students & faculty. My son joined soccer & basketball & though not an experienced player at first, he certainly wasn't driven out. My daughter made lots of friends from all different 'cliques' & after 3 years, still hangs out with them all. She's not involved in any school sports. My son's preference is to have just a few close friends. I attribute their success & acceptance at school to them just being nice kids- nothing more. The school's music department and art classes are fabulous. Sports no doubt is a huge part of teen life. Though I personally think our nation is overly obsessed with sports, it gives children something to do, to strive for, and is physically healthy. Unfortunately, kids who get bullied & excluded are everywhere. But a child's feelings toward others starts at home. I think it's an excellent school and Mr. Koba is a wonderful 'hands-on' principal running a tight ship. Nearly every time I go to the school, I see him in the hallway. We are quite pleased with the school & it's academics. I went to this school as did my stepbrothers. They played sports and I did not. Their grades were excellent, though in life, they were not so successful. Your success, you see, at CTAHS was measured on if you played sports and how well. I did poorly with my grades. i was told that I read "too much" by the teachers. I even failed History though I had 100% on every quiz, homework and exam. Grades were distributed based upon popularity and popularity was based on sports participation. I graduated in the bottom 5% of my class. I often relate this to my students. I'm a university professor teaching Quantitative Economics. I speak three languages and have six degrees. I learned nothing during my time at township. My experiences there were more of a hindrance than a help. If you have a choice, send your children elsewhere. If you are looking for a school district that puts all of its focus on the students becoming athletes rather than getting good grades and being able to succeed outside of Davidsville, PA then this is the school for you.. And as far as "small town cliquey adults" I give it an A++.. It's a terrible school district and I cannot wait to relocate Conemaugh Township is an incredible school district. There is no other school like it in there area, and there’s a reason houses are a hot commodity here. The teachers are hands on and involved with the students. They are even present at outside activities just to support the kids. The school is newly renovated and changing to meet the needs of students. We moved here from another district and feel right at home. The community is very accepting and makes you feel like you grew up here. The kids are also very kind and respectful. There are no labels on what kids can and can’t do here. This is the type of school where the quarterback is also involved in the musical. If you want your child to be the best they can be, send them to Conemaugh Township.
