column3: As a former student of Shaler Area High when the high school was on Mt. Royal Blvd., I found the curriculum to be excellent. I started as a sophmore there when the school district was ordered to include all school in the Etna, Millvale, and Sharpsburgh schools. While many people thought this was a bad idea they were very wrong in my opinion. The move was the best thing for the school district. The choir and band were excellent then. I was a member of the choir and other extra curriculum activities and it was excellent. The teachers were excellent except for maybe 1 or 2, but they really cared about the students and went out of their way to help them succeed. The rest of the support staff, principal, counselors, coaching staff and everyone had the students future in their minds. They were always very available and seriously cared about everyone. This is one of the best schools in the area. Students just needed to avail themselves of the various activities, AP classes, and and technical opportunities that were available. The student/teacher ratio was one of the lowest in the entire area. Everyone should encourage their children to take advantage of everything available. Think before you move to Shaler and send your kid to Shaler School District I have never seen a school, with students that are so disrespectful in my career. The kids within the Shaler school system, get no organization, learn nothing of ethical boundaries, learn nothing of physical boundaries, there sex ed program promotes sexual intercourse. The teachers are underpaid, understaffed. They deal with bullying wrong. separation without integration or ethical approach. Nothing of the sort is seen elsewhere. This school needs an ENTIRE REBOOT. Think before you move to shaler school, your kids will not have the learning of interaction that they need. They will become bullies, or the bully. Regardless of what studies show, I have seen first hand, 9 out of 10 kids dropout or never attend college. Abysmal. Unsure of how any student who graduates from this district is prepared for higher education. If they are, it is DESPITE their high school experience, not because of it. This is the school you attend to stay AVERAGE. Nothing great happens here. NOTHING. The principals are average, the teachers are average, the coaches are average......There is much satisfaction in mediocrity. If you strive for excellence, or if you just have a choice, move just a bit more to the north....to North Hills, to North Allegheny, to Pine-Richland...all these schools are better, much better. This school is run by weak puppets that could never stand up for themselves, let alone any students. At this school you will never achieve what you have planned to. Between the lack of support from teachers and administration your student will never be able to get the help needed to get anywhere.Homework: The type of homework they give will not teach you anything. It is all just work that the teacher will take to admin to prove that they “did their job”. Teachers: The teachers here are either the best or the worst. Some put in more effort than any of us students deserve while the other 90% skid by while doing the absolute minimum. They however love Shaler as they are stuck in the past from the time they themselves went here. At this point in time the students are more dedicated at what they do than the teachers are.Leadership: There is no leadership what do ever in this school. The lack of support for students and teachers is astounding. In the end Shaler would rather have their name look good than actually teach their students.Character: “pride respect and honor” is what the Shaler motto is. However none of this is directed towards the students. They would rather have us sit there and do what they say because of “respect” than us actually speak our minds or grow creatively into adults with opinions. Learning Differences: The staff here does nothing to promote healthy learning in any way. They would rather take the effortless road of a powerpoint and a lecture than actually teach us anything. And instead of helping you learn the counselors would rather place you in a class that is supposed to “help you stay organized” than talk to you about the problem you’re having.Bullying: As far as bullying goes Shaler does not stand out. However their approach to discipline is the same for every situation. Also if you have a disabled child don’t even think about sending them here because Shalers solution to people vaping in the bathroom was to take the doors off the handicapped stalls. In conclusion it could be much worse but going here has made me realize that public funded education does not care about its students or anyone except the people who give them money.

column3: Everyone is friendly. Teachers are awesome. Loved high school. My high school experience was one of my favorite parts of my life thus far. I wish i could go back. Great teaches. Great Sports. While it's not perfect (it needs some work in the fine-arts department) most of the teachers are really good and they do a great job of preparing us students for the future. My biggest complaint would be how overly strict it got over the years I was there. ID's were required to be worn around the neck and it was enforced to an almost ridiculous degree despite being in an environment where almost all the teachers know who you are in the first year. I have had three children go through the school. All 3 have been very successful in college. Excellent, dedicated staff and administration. Great small town school with wonderful educational results. As a student at RBCHS I really do not like this school. If you don't play a sport or if you aren't super smart or your parents don't donate half their pay checks every month you are nothing. Things get stolen from locker rooms even when the lockers are locked and people smoke in the bathrooms. The student body is very good with ranking high on tests but as people they are the biggest jerks ever. Freshman year bad rumors were started and nothing was done about it. It's just kinda like a "wait it out and things will hopefully get better" attitude. There's people that either love RB or they hate it. There is no in between. I have had 3 children go through this school and with each and every one of them they were treated like they didn't exist because my family wasn't "in the click". All 3 kids were excellent athletes and played on travel teams all of their lives. My kids were even recruited by travel teams because of their high skill levels. But at RB they sat the bench all of the time because they weren't part of the click. Do not send your kids here unless you intend to donate your time, money and kiss up to the click crowd!

column3: Love, Love, Love this school!!! The staff is great; super kind and helpful. The teachers really take time to work with students that may be struggling. The school has high expectations for their students but they go the extra step and help guide students to meet and exceed those expectations. There is a reason that this school is so highly rated!!!!! This school is fantastic. My son relocated from another sate, and he loves it. Teachers and counselors are great they really care about the students. Sports however are very political. If you aren't related to the coaches or aren't from the area your child gets cut from the team regardless how talented you are. Very unfair. This school has bullies for principal and Assistant Dean. My nephew is an 18 year old Autistic senior attending this school. He moved in with me because he was being mentally and physically abused at home. about 1 and a half years ago, the school was made aware, but his mother put on great show, so they did nothing. Recently, he received a small inheritance and his mother was upset she couldn't get her hands on it. when my mother passed, there was a family heirloom that she wanted another sister to have, but my nephews mother would never give it up. so when my nephew moved in, he brought it with him to give my sister, cause he knew that is what his grandmother wanted. So his mother, goes down to the school and talks to the assistant dean. they pull my nephew out of class, and the dean proceeds to threaten my nephew. He tells him, "It's a good thing you have that money cause now you can hire a Lawyer." and then tells him " your going to Lerdo (County jail). This dean was way out of line. He is not Law Enforcement. Educators are not supposed to get involved in Civil matters, let alone threaten students. shame on him and shame on my nephews mom for embarrassing him. I called the school and the District Office, and they said they would "look into it" and contact me. nothing yet. 1 week later, and I'm still waiting. No apologies or anything to my nephew. The principal called my nephew in and told him that the dean should not have got involved and would once again, "look into it." my nephew is scared and fears retaliation. These are not educators, they are bullies. And all this, to an autistic child. Do you want your kids going to a school that turns Thier heads to an abused child? if so, this is the perfect school for you. This principal, dean , and district makes the great teachers look bad. They should be ashamed of themselves. I would rate the experience as very poor. The disrespect Administration has towards parents is very bad. It also seems that most staff do not really care about the students. There is too many examples to list them all but they all add up. My son was called "Mike" instead of his name Kevin for two years straight. Then during the graduation ceremony they announced him as "Kyle" I suppose that I should be happy his diploma was correct. This high school is one of the best in Kern County. My son has had great teachers every year and their sport programs are great.

column1: Terrible school district ... Teachers and staff do not care about the problems at Del City High School ... With all the cussing , disruptions in the class room , Dress code people wearing saggy pants ... Nice, large campus in great shape. The staff does an excellent job of making the student body feel like a family. Plenty of classes and activities to choose from. My experience at DCHS was phenomenal. The administration, faculty, staff, counselors, and teacher's were top notch! The academics were challenging and rigorous with many class choices and options. There were many clubs and organizations available (FCA). The sport programs were outstanding at all levels! I loved the school's large campus. The band room, auditorium, commons, library, weight room etc. were all remodeled and spacious! The field house is huge and impressive! We had updated lab and computer equipment along with current learning material. My experiences were active and fun, but the priority of the school was furthuring my education in preparation for college and my future. Proud Eagles!!! The leadership, and staff are dedicated to giving the students the best possible academic, music, arts and sports programs. Traditional public schools education is becoming a rare thing in Oklahoma. The student body is supportive of each other and wins many awards. The teachers go over and beyond to be inclusive of all students and parents. Del City as a city continue to put money into improving the schools, roads and library.

I know of many students who needed therapy after graduation. Now i am in college and working after i was told that i am stupid. Do not send your children there!!!! I am a former student of Toronto High School. I was pushed through. I was bullied and since I was not a "JOCK" nothing was done about it. If you don't have the right last name at that school or town. you don't have a chance. All they worry about is the Sports program. God help you if you have a coach as a teacher. All he will do is talk about the sports program with his "JOCKS" and the heck with anyone else in the classroom. When I attended this school from grades preschool through 12th grade, I felt as though my education was a joke. Now that I have completed college, and meet many people from various states and schools, I have learned that Toronto City Schools did an excellent job in preparing me for college and my career. It may not have all the classes that another school offers, or all the sports, but 90% of the teachers at this school district are amazing, and caring. When I run into them, even today, they still remember me and ask about myself and my family. It's one of the pluses of going to a small, hometown school. I am not a jock either, as others have mentioned, and I think you get from this school what you put into it. Some of my best teachers were: Ms. Popejoy, Mr. Weidger, Mr. Stone, Mr. Hlivko, Mr. Sines and Mrs. Pritts, and this is just to name a select few! I would send my children here. This school and the district is an absolute joke. Moving here my junior year, I was so excited, but that quickly came to an end. I was denied the option to take certain classes because they were “too advanced” and I didn’t have the ability. This was coming from someone who did not know me or my academic abilities. Any time I had any issues at all the school looked the other way. I was given little to no advice on what to do after high school, including information on loans and ways to get the proper information transferred to the colleges I applied to. Not only are the students extremely rude and unwelcoming, the staff are as well. Anyone who is not a star football player, cheerleader, or valedictorian is often looked down on by most people in the building. I never once felt this school was properly preparing me for my future. The issues with bullying, homophobia, and racism at this school are out of hand. There is zero place for these types of issues in this town. I am ashamed to be an alumna of this school.

column1: If you want your child to have a strong academic future south hills is NOT your school. my daughter transfered from the Crowley ISD, Were the teachers did not care about the students passing or giving tutoring. They hired these first year teachers that have no idea of how to teacher high schoolers and they were more concerned with their own personal lives during class instead of teaching and helping the kids that had difficulty learning.My daughter is now a honor roll student has all the help possible and I am greatful to SHHS. your child has to work to hard to succeed your child has to work to hard to succeed your child has to work to hard to succeed The GOOD: at the time I attended the school, they were worked hard to improve building facilities and hired many young teachers, many of whom worked earnestly to assist and motivate the students to succeed (or, at the least, to do their work.) The science and math teachers seemed especially committed to working with the students to help them understand challenging concepts (one of whom was, surprisingly, a coach.) They also offered a wide range of AP and honors courses including physics, calculus, english, and psychology. I had a great time in drama. Of course you had a few teachers who didn't seem to care or who seemed so intellectually dense you wondered how THEY ever managed to graduate, but I would say that they were not the majority. Lastly I will say that I believe your ability to receive a decent education at this school lies mainly within you (or your child's) motivation to actually learn. There were opportunities to take more challenging coursework and to receive one-on-one help from willing teachers, but it's not like a private school where the kids are miraculously shoehorned into models of success and achievement. Again, it all comes down to intrinsic motivation. Excellent - 5/5I believe any student would value from his/her educational experiences!! It is now one of the best high schools in the Fort Worth ISD

column3: North provides an excellent education, however there is tremendous pressure put on students to equal or beat the previous years performance on test scores,etc. The teachers are great, and provide excellent instruction in the classroom. The school has challenging academic programs that require many hours of study and homework. Multiple test on the same day is the norm and an average student might find it difficult to manage the rigorous schedule and after school activities. This school is perfect for the college bound student that loves a challenge. Academics at North are fairly good. Good selection of courses. However, recently the district has cut a lot of experienced teachers to save money, and both the quality of instructors and the morale of the existing teachers has declined. Culture of the school is very materialistic and the administration is largely unconcerned with students, unless the family has money and is a "booster" of sports programs. The school seems to maintain an adversarial stance toward students, and is very hostile to students/parents/families who express any concerns about the school or its policies. My daughter did excel academically and graduated with honors. One thing she never had at Edmond North and that was a true friend. The school has a lot of arrogant over privileged kids. I regret not transferring her to another high school. My daughter graduated last year from North and my son is a Sophomore. The prep for college is available and encouraged and the support from the Administration is exceptional. The principal is more than involved and is very refreshing. Our kids love this school and have developed many great relationships there. When comparing to other public schools in the area and state, Edmond North is second to none. its been good so far i really like it here i feel like i finally fit in

column1: Amazing place to be. Helpful staff, friendly students, and a great learning enviornment. I witnessed a great deal of racism and the severity of corporal punishment was determined by race factors. Even so, I never saw a single person question these decisions or complain about them.

column3: This school is fantastic academically. However if your student needs a little extra nudge then this is not the school for you. We moved to this school from another state. The experience was horrible and ended in him having to go to live with his father to save his schooling. First nobody helped him to learn the system even though I personnally talked to the VP and told him he needed direction because he is too shy to ask for help. Second my straight A student plummeted to a Straight F student in less than 3 months. He is not stupid but the teachers never bothered to catch him up to the rest of the class in what they expected and when. I never once got a phone call never once was told that there was a website that I could use to track his progress. Until the day we checked him out of school. Bottom line is. There are too many students and the ones that need a little guiding get lost in the masses. And the administration don't care enough to help them. My daughter goes to the same school and because she is out going and asks for what she needs she is doing well. Pity I miss my son but this school was not at all what he needed. great school, and great teachers. The teachers are great with working with students and teachers. The teachers at Poly go beyond their duty to assure student success. There are plenty of sports and clubs for the students to get involved. 2017-2018 VB coach Hmmmm "Wake up and use the talent on your bench" My child being self motivated and an advanced learner and has found that most of the teachers have been very academically challenging while enjoying the student/mentor relationship All around good school. Communication from staff could be better and the counselors office def needs improvement working w/ parents and students but I’d want my kids going here over any other school in the district even though they don’t really offer the same advantage like the IB program North does that my son was invited to or the engineering program King offers, considering what problems those schools have as well I find POLY a more balanced choice.

column1: The school is very good at teaching the students what they need for their future and making sure that they pass all of their classes. They punish their students properly by detention such as cleaning up the campus or a teacher's classroom. Only a very small select few of teachers are considered unbearable. Otherwise all of the other teachers are excellent. The school also has a class almost every wednesday that helps us students get ready for life beyond high school. Best public high school you will find on Oahu, hands down. Students (and teachers) are held to a higher standard than in most DOE schools. We moved to Mililani specifically because of this school's rating as the best in the state. We have been here two years and cannot wait to LEAVE! This school is horrible. The teachers couldn't care less about the quality of their instruction. Everything is "group project", in which one or two students do everything, rest do nothing, and yet they all get the same grade. The teachers are not held accountable. We have gone twice with no response either time. First time was over a teacher who taught by throwing a video in every day and telling the kids if they had any questions, to read their books. The kids were all failing and I finally raised so much grief that the counselor transferred my kid to another teacher. Second, a science teacher threw fits, called the kids "incompetent" and other names, kicked lockers in frustration and broke glass beakers on the floor because he didn't like kids wearing open toe shoes. Despite all this, kids are pushed through the grades without basic skills to get them into college. DO NOT BRING YOUR KIDS HERE!!! My daughter attends MHS and the honors and AP program is excellent. The regular classes are not challenging, but overall her experience has been good. She is also in JROTC, this is the first year that they have JROTC and she is learning A LOT in this program. I recommend this school. I just finished my freshman year at MHS, and I am overall very impressed. I moved here to Oahu from the mainland right before school started. We chose to live in Mililani because the schools looked very good. MHS is definitely a very good high school. A new principal was called this year, and he is very involved. The old principal (also very good) became the superintendent. The teachers are all very good, friendly, and qualified with only a few bad ones here and there. The Pre-AP classes are more accelerated and rigorous than regular classes and have definitely helped me to prepare for AP classes I will be taking next year. I like how this school offers a 15 minute recess break after the first two periods so that students can have a break from their work. I am not involved with athletics but MHS has a very good sports program. The students are overall very friendly and I never had a bad encounter with another student. I was very impressed with my first year at MHS and I look forward to returning next year. This school's staff and leadership are excellent. My son has been here for 1 year- for his sophomore year. The teachers he had were amazing- I wish I could name them! Mililani High is an ok school. Regular classes aren't very challenging, and some particular English teachers seem to not be able to teach at all. Any math class above Geometry becomes extremely difficult, I was able to only get a C even with coming for help constantly. Some teachers, including a substitute, are able to belittle, insult and put down students, with absolutely no consequences given. Teachers seem to just get away with everything they do here. Another history teacher would assign 100 note cards for homework, would grade unfairly, and would refuse to discuss why she how she graded the assignment. She could never be reasoned with, either. As with any school, a student's experience at a particular school is what he/she makes of it. My daughter is currently a junior and has taken Honors or AP courses since her freshman year. The teachers are hard-working and committed to student learning. She passed the AP class she took last year and is taking 2 APs this year. She also plays in the string ensemble and after-school orchestra. If your son/daughter is motivated and serious about academics he/she will do well here. 10/10 you have to consider, when reading reviews, that most people with good experiences don’t often write reviews. It’s more often that people with bad experiences write reviews. That being said, the fact that this school has so many good reviews is a testament to just how amazing it is. The teachers are wonderful and I have witnessed little to no bullying. If there is bullying it is immediately felt with and BOTH parties receive help. Im Pretty middle ground with it, my academics and grades DROPPED, teachers aren't good, and its hard to become friends with new people. Not cliquey, but hard to find a friend group My children loved Mililani High School! They had excellent teachers and a challenging curriculum. There is a robust accelerated program there. My children all got accepted into good universities and I credit the teachers and staff at this hardworking school. Excellent well-rounded school with great academics and extracurricular activities. Really like Principal Murphy and the administration.

If you are looking for an education you will find it here the teachers are great and the no tolerance policy is fully unforced mediocre, at best, with each passing year getting more racially divided and more dangerous I would rate it a 10 out of 10 I love Southaven I've went to Southaven schools my whole life and it's been fun. column1: Good school, a little too much into football. Some teachers assign "make work" homework/assignments that have little bearing on actual class content. Need to modify "common core", Common core seems to be a simplified solution to math that's made far more complicated and convoluted than the original math ever was. It is very biased when it comes to religion and school, seems if you are not Mormon or play sports then you don’t really matter at all. And teachers care more about what you wear then your education. We moved here when my son started his freshman year. He was able to make friends and be involved in different activities. The school offers many dual credit classes. My son was able to graduate with an associates degree along with his high school diploma. I have heard from several other parents that their students started college farther ahead due to the college credits they earned while at NPHS.

column3: Quincy Senior High School in my opinion is a fantastic school to learn. High School is not always a great experience for everyone but here at the administration here along with fellow students helps to make that possible. We have AMAZING school spirit along with great sports and clubs/activities. We strive to be the best that we can be. I really do love QHS. It has great class sizes, awesome teachers, healthlier lunches, and is a place where students can come and feel safe and be themselves. QHS is accepting of everyone. Academically we achieve greatly. Our school is great but every school can always use some improvement. We would benifet from even healthier lunches and snacks. I believe it students and faculty eat better they wil preform better in and outside of school. I believe we would also benefit from a more clean/fixed up school. Our school does not look the best and it would be nice if we could paint classrooms a more vibrant color to wake us up and fix up the ceilings! Quincy Senior High is a great school!! You should come check it out sometime:) Thank you. Quincy Senior High School has provided both of my children with a top-notch education. Both children have been admitted to competitive college programs. The AP courses available is large considering the size and financial status of our community. In addition to academics, the fine arts and sporting opportunities are excellent. QHS has a full concert orchestra, a marching band, superior choirs, and a theatre program that is truly outstanding. There are numerous varsity athletic opportunities, and our teams are always competitive. QHS also offers numerous Project Lead the Way classes and will be adding a biomedical element in the fall. The great thing about QHS is that there is something for everyone. My husband and I are both professionals and we have never second guessed our decision to send our children to Quincy Public Schools. This is the ONLY public High School available. The school staff, not just students is very clicky. Students should choose their teacher when choosing their classes. In getting the attention of teachers, I have had to send emails to the school board along with the teachers, or nothing gets done. The main nurse was the sick nurse during covid in 2020. She is horrible, lacking empathy and compassion. As far as safety, parents cannot get past the doors unless a specific need is addressed and a specific or area room is given. I haven't tried to go anywhere other than the counselor, nurse, front desk, and once to the commons area for class rings. They are not very friendly either.

column1: I got my daughter away from this school because she wasn't one of the chosen ones. She was bullied, harassed and ignored by students and teachers alike. When I witnessed the offenses or her dad did and we went directly to the administration or teachers directly we were basically ignored and nothing was ever done to help my child or to the ones who were bullying her because they were the athletic stars and teachers pets. I have no doubt in my mind that if I had left my daughter in this school there would have been serious mental issues to deal with later. I moved her to Southside and it's like watching a completely different person, the person I knew was there but just needed a chance to be herself without being teased and bullied.

column3: My child was extremely unhappy with this school. The bullying is horrible, and the teachers are no help. We have two children in the school system. Our eldest daughter is a student at the high school, and so far we have been extremely happy with her experiences there. She works hard, enjoys school, has a great group of friends, and she likes to participate in many of the after-school activities they offer. Barrington has many high-achieving students. As a result, the learning environment can be a bit competitive and challenging,. Ultimately, however, it benefits students because the standards are high. Overall, we're very happy with the schools here. I agree, the bullying is ignored. Not suprisingly, the link to the state bullying policy on the school website doesn't work. I transferred my chiild out after completing almost 11 years in the Barrington school system; she could no longer tolerate the bullying and was unable to thrive in class. The school was of NO help and had no methods of reducing bullying. Pros:- Excellent academics. The best public school for academics in Rhode Island and probably top 3 even with private schools in the mix. We always send around 30-40 people per grade to top 25 ranked universities and liberal arts colleges. Almost everyone graduates and goes to college, and dropouts or people who don't go to at least community college are rare enough that everyone knows about it and talks about it (part of a con too, people tend to be very nosy). - Almost all teachers I've had are amazing, strive to make class fun, and really care about the students.- Fairly good athletics. All teams are D1 and perform well enough to make some noise in the playoffs, but we don't get a whole lot of championships. Maybe 1 per season (fall, winter, spring). - Guidance office is fantastic, and will help students prepare for life after high school and applying to college as early as 10th grade. Counselors are really on top of things and will never forget to follow up with you if they promised to get something done for you, like change a course or send a transcript.- The student body tends to be nice in general. I've seen bullying but have not experienced it. From what I can see, if you're a socialite and want to associate with a lot of friends and party hard, you'll fit right in with the popular crowd. If you just want to be a normal student with a close group of friends, you'll also fit right in. Even if you're not exactly the most social person, there really aren't any traditional "bullies" here at all. Unless you act really annoying or otherwise stand out in a negative light, people will generally ignore you and not give you any trouble.- Extracurriculars here are amazing. A HUGE selection with large memberships and active communities. Cons:- Cafeteria food isn't great- There's a highly competitive atmosphere. The majority of students, even the socialites and party chasers, are on edge about college. What college you go to is a really big deal. Everyone will know and gossip about it and you’re expected to share and congratulate what colleges your friends are going to on social media. If you aren’t a fan of competition or aren’t planning to go to college, then the college-centric atmosphere will feel very cutthroat to you. Graduated from this school and continued on to college where I found that I was far more prepared then any of my peers.

column1: I am an alumni of Hopewell-Loudon, and I feel that overall the school is exemplary. I feel that the teachers are enthusiastic, helpful, approachable, and knowledgeable. During my experience as a student in this school, I found that the administration seemed unapproachable and didn't always have the best interest of all students in mind. They clearly favored some students (particularly those with familiar family names) over others. Discipline was inconsistent and sometimes unfair. They were not good at praising the great achievements of successful students, either. Certain sports teams were more appreciated than others, and students who excelled in other areas (art, band, choir, quiz bowl, etc.) were not often acknowledged. The teachers make this school a great place to learn and grow. Thankfully, the administrators didn't come out of their offices enough to ruin my great experiences. For the teachers and students, I give a 5-star A+. For the administrators, I would put them below average.

column3: I am a current graduate from the Venice High School Global Language Magnet class of 2013 and I am now a college student at California State University of Northridge. The Venice Magnet is a a great school and the community is wondeful.The counselor Ms.Roche-blair is amazing!! At VEnice you will always find help if you ask for it. You won't regret sending your child here. Me and my two sisters graduated from Venice (2012 and 2013) and know my cousin started hoing here this school year as a freshman and he loves the school already. GO GONDOS!!! The new STEM Magnet has the potential to be great, but the administration and the district could get a little more behind it. There was a LOT of scheduling confusion at the beginning of the year leading and the Magnet really needs a source of funding for all the technology needed for the electives they offer and would like to offer, but which really make the Magnet an outstanding choice in high schools on the west side. The teachers seem very enthusiastic and willing to give. It would be nice if the school could figure out how to count the engineering classes as "science" as it is very difficult to meet all the A-G requirements, PE and an elective in 9th and 10th grades with only 6 periods to schedule. my school has the best teachers you will ever find this school also has a lot of magnet students and also is a clean school This is a great school. I am enrolled in the STEMM engineering program, which is in its second year here at Venice. The teachers are great. They are engaging, teach lessons clearly and thoroughly, and will help with any problems someone may have. It is amazing what the teachers put up with working for the district. They have to deal with large classes, changing curriculum, and misbehaving kids, and somehow manage to end the day with a smile. I don't know how they do it. My child is in his second year in the engineering magnet at Venice HS, and I have only good things to say about the school. Whatever went on there in the past is clearly over. The teachers and administration are engaged, involved, and responsive. My child has learned a huge amount and is always eager to begin the next school day. I hope that they keep up the great work that they're doing. We have 2 daughters enrolled in the world languages magnet program at Venice High. We have been very pleased with the quality and dedication of all their teachers and the school administration. The magnet program offers many AP courses to choose from and attracts a diverse student group. We love Venice, the principal rocks. My daughter is doing great here. We choose Venice My daughter is a senior at Venice High School and we love it! She transferred from a westside private school and we have honestly found the level of teaching and commitment to the students as good if not better. Love the diversity of our student population and faculty, along with the breadth of AP and Honors classes available! There's something for everyone at Venice, including the opportunity to try new sports without prior travel/club experience as seems to be required in many high schools today.Our new principal, Dr. Wiedoeft, has also given the school new vision and energy that was missing under the leadership of the previous principal. Our son is enrolled in the STEMM Magnet. The principal, Dr. Wiedoeft is so amazingly dedicated. She is at every event. We get weekly emails and phone calls from her with updates. The parent community is really involved. The teachers are top notch and dedicated to student success. Our son has a 3D printer in his design and engineering class that he is able to use and he is a freshman. The basketball coach is the type of coach we would dream of-he is so great and supportive. In fact, their whole sports program is really fantastic. Please be aware that the 2016 proficiency scores are MUCH better than those from recent prior years (for the state testing). This is largely since, in prior years, most of the 11th graders taking AP courses simply signed waivers, so as to study more for their AP tests, while skipping out on the state's common core testing. Well, this changed last spring (2016) and now Venice High state testing scores are as high and higher than neighboring lausd high schools (especially for the magnet students) -- see for example the school profile published with the 2016 testing scores, in US News .com . Those past 2015 proficiency scores (on the Greatschools website) reflect only the lower-performing half of the student body; since about 52% of students at Venice take AP courses (one or more), and they were the ones opting out of the state testing, this resulted in those inaccurate proficiency graphs, prior to 2016. Do go on tour at this school and you'll learn the truth -- great AP programs (and honors classes). This school has great teachers. The administration is very helpful Our son is in the STEMM and loves it. There's a nice vibe between the kids here- it's a very accepting environment. Most of the teachers seem to be well liked too. A great school if you want your child to encouraged not only academically but with a strong sense of fairness towards others from all different backgrounds and social groups. Awful, they claim they are against bullying but they have no plans in order to stop it. It ruined my daughter’s senior year. Venice High has a lot to offer; AP classes, Sports Medicine, STEM, World Languages & Global Studies, Dual Language and so much more. Strong leadership from the Principal, along with caring teachers. This is a great community school for those that want the full high school experience; solid academics, sports, clubs, Friday night football games, homecoming, prom, etc.

column1: I am an alumni. I had some really great teachers as well as some very bad teachers here. I would expect this is fairly common in rural communities. However, what was very depressing was the lack of courses offered, the lack of commitment from the community and the poor decisions on financial investments. The community regularly voted down any votes to improve the school or build a new school to replace the almost literally crumbling HS/Elementary building. Yet somehow, new athletic structures were built and new football equipment bought (early 2000's). If you want to take a skill course or technical course you must enroll in the WMCTC and hope they have the class you are looking for. My course at the CTC was dropped half way through my 2 year program. I came out with a good education and earned a degree in engineering from a great University. I thank the teachers that helped me in this school system. But until the community gets behind them, and the board starts making better financial decisions, this school will continue to decline. Good luck Lake City. Education is more important than beating McBain...just remember that.

column3: Richland High School offers the best, most well-rounded education in the area. Maintains high academic standards while offering quality arts and athletics programs. I am the parent of two former students. The Richland school district prepared them well academically to enter college and successfully study engineering and physical therapy while helping to foster a life long interest in arts and athletics. This well run district has the facilities and budget to promote the best education in the area.

column1: Excellent staff, administration and school board. I choose this school for my kids because they consistently have turned out good kids and provide the best education in this whole area. I also like the low teacher to student ratio. I went to Sebeka my entire high school career. I now attend a public university in Minnesota and I feel Sebeka prepared me for this transition. I also completed my first year of college while I was still in Sebeka high school and I am extremely grateful for this advantage I had when entering college. From teachers to paraprofessionals to secretaries and the counselor I built relationships with everyone in the school and I am proud to be an alumni of Sebeka!

column3: A sterling school which always encourages students to go for the best.The teachers are courteous and always wish you good luck. Best school of this state of NY. As a former student i can say that for the first time in years, i was finally enjoying school and wanted to learn. the diversity is amazing and you don't hear trouble like the typical American schools. Very friendly and encouraging teachers and administrators and staffs. School very unorganized, teachers and staff really rude and disrespectful. They treat kinds like animals just because they are new immigrants which is a very sad thing. I was a student at Newcomers from 2008 to 2012. It was the best experience ever, this school is special and you will never find a place as special like this school. The staff is friendly, the classes are good and the Media and Music programs are exceptional with greatly qualified teachers. I wish I had more money to help fund this school this is truly a unique place for immigrants. I am sure this school will go into history without a doubt. It is already part of my history. I was a newcomers high school student from 2009 to 2013. I would not give it a five star since its academy is not that exceptional. There was no office hour and most teachers did not care about grammar. Sometimes there were gang fights but they are very rare.It is a safe environment overall and all you need to do is be careful whom you are with. You can leave after the official class if you want. No one would prevent you except that a certain teacher knows you have his/her class. Once you submit your works, it is your responsibility to ask questions. Teachers rarely go over homework. In a word, it is where you really learn self-management. You can be better or worse here. Interestingly, you will find out that everyone has a story behind due to different cultural backgrounds. Tips for students who want to attend this school: 1. Learn English (learn grammar on yourself) 2. Practice SAT when you are a freshman. 3. Read English books 4. Doing at least 3 practical regents exams and understand your mistakes before each exam (This will give you at least 85 or higher). 5. Take AP classes and try to pass it with 3 or higher. 6. Play as much as you can Tengo casi 2 años en la escuela, y la experiencia tanto virtual como tradicional ha sido muy interesante y entretenida. He podido aprender mucho gracias a la enseñanza que se da. Como por ejemplo, ahora tengo más fluidez en mi inglés, y he desarrollado diferentes capacidades para la universidad. Hablando de los maestros y las herramientas usadas, he podido aprender por Nearpod, Google Meet, Zoom, Lumen y Edmentum. Estas herramientas han sido eficaces para mejorar mi habilidad con el inglés. Por último la recomendaría ya que el ambiente en el que se estudia es muy pacifico y amigable, aquí todos tenemos diferencias y las respetamos por igual. This is a 4 years international high school. I have been there for 2 years, and I can say this has been a wonderful experience. I have met extraordinary people throughout the world, from almost all the continents. We have great teachers who are helping us learn as much as possible. Highly recommended, especially if English is not your first language, and you like diversity. My experience at this school was fantastic. The staff was amiable and always looking forward to help students learn in a comfortable environment. I felt that the teachers truly cared for me, and did their best to exploit my potential to the fullest. The environment is also wonderful because the student body is diverse—you will definitely learn something through friendships and shared experiences. Overall, I enjoyed my four years at Newcomers a lot, and made memories I will never forget.

column1: More opportunities for parent involvement ON campus are needed. But overall, this is a very supportive learning environment. The staff is caring and watchful. The career clusters are significant. Let's make sure the budget stays intact for THIS school in particular. Not everyone will go to college, but the ones who want to NEED to be ready!In Alaska, it is hard to raise the bar; Hutchinson should continue doing this until it beats the national averages. The English/Language Arts department is lacking in rigorous instruction. If your child is advanced, they may quickly become bored and unstimulated. I suggest that a better and more consistent librarian is in place. The presented assignments and tasks should have supplements attached for those who want to excel (paired with a teacher and parents' encouragement and awards for DOING so). Also, suggest journalism or CLUB opportunitites that are laser-focused on investigative thinking and practices. Clubs that meet the needs of those students who enjoy career clusters in the Language Arts arena could integrate with Arts AV.

column3: this needs some help. i have to say as a student that went there it not good. The teacher in the other hand are very very good. by Ab .A Don't send your child this school if you are white because they will be very uncomfortable. Craigmont High school is a very excellent school. The community thinks that it is a bad school because they only hear about the bad things that happen. There are many bad things that happen at other schools as well. Craigmont high school has a plethora of positive things going on. They have an excellent optional program and much more. If the community takes a chance to stop looking at the bad things that occur here and look at the positive things they will love it. I recommend students with positive behavior and work ethics to come and enjoy Craigmont High School. This school is terrible. Kids set the garbage cans on fire, pull the fire alarm, have riots, steal from staff, have fights every day. If your child has a little potential don't bring them there. It's horribly set up the teachers smoke with the students. And their are gangs everywhere I personally don't like Craigmont because I was used to my previous school at Hamilton,but all of the reviews that are saying that craigmont is a bad school they are lying.Craigmont supports diversity on various levels, this is my first year at Craigmont and they make sure they are on all students 100% of the time. It is a good school for a child of any color to attend

column1: Strong in liberal arts, but weak in STEM. Use of technology is weak, but looks like there is potential to improve with new leadership changes and fund allocations. Declining/Flat enrollment, and relatively small number of students per grade (@170 or so in an average year) make this a good school for student extra-curricular opportunities. SAT, AP, and 4-year college matriculation have plenty of room for improvement. AP exam costs are paid for by the district. If state school are not in consideration for your student, then seek out Wyomissing or even WIlson. The class of 2013 was competitive at the top end at SV, but wait to see class performance on the whole. For a small district they do offer Chinese language instruction, but with nowhere near the rigor of their Spanish instruction. The School Board of Directors is weak, and in many ways the Employee/Employer lines are reversed. This may be a result of the previous leadership, and perhaps the new leadership will be managed properly. What I love about SV is that it's a small school, everyone knows each other and it's easy to make friends with upperclassmen when you start. We have incredibly gifted teachers, most people don't realize that we are lucky to have the teachers we have. I love that our administration is not completely focused on test scores and data and being the best, which allows the students to be focused on things that they love. This, in turn, makes our test scores better anyway. I am currently a junior and I've loved SV since I moved here in third grade. I also enjoy our rivalry with Hamburg because everyone is in on it, even the teachers.

column3: Look, no school is perfect. No school is without crime, and bullying. No school is without cliques, and moody teachers. All schools have problems. I was born in Lee County, and raised there. I have attended all of the Lee County Schools, and my honest opinion, no matter how many times I complain, is that it's a great school system. There is a homey environment. Everyone knows everyone. Everyone watches out for their friends, and the other way around. The teachers teach you how to think, as well as the criteria. The administrators, and teachers care about your well being. There are fights, and there are unruly neighborhoods near bye, but overall Lee County is one heck of a school. For all of those people who are complaining about it, why don't you send your child to Sumter county for a year, and see how they like it. Rather than caring about social status, care about the quality of the education your child is getting. I am glad to be a Trojan!

column1: Freedom High School has poor leadership and a very poor math department. Most parents are so frustrated that they have contacted the Principal and her boss but there has been no change. Clean & new building but very poor academically. Not challenging at all. I feel that the kids are not being prepared effectively for the cut throat competitive world outside, that they have to excel in, in order to succeed. My two children are faring well in college, thanks to the academic program of Loudoun County. They are each placed in upper level courses in both English and Math, even though one child did not place as extremely high as the other in SATs, they are each holding their own and doing great! We experienced Freedom High School from its formative years, and saw the natural negative human reactions to any changes that the principal made, but if you open your minds to it, the changes are based on founded reasons, and not to be taken personally against the principal. Teachers should offer extra credit in order to engage the students into studying the subject material, but please note that extra credit is often not offered in college classes. Suggestion for the Guidance Department to filter in topics of career choices on an every day basis, so these students may be more certain of their academic paths if pursuing college vs. technical paths. New principal is really making a difference, school academics are improving dramatically as evidenced by state exams and SAT scores coming in. Great atmoshphere and school spirit. The school is becoming much better with the atmosphere the new principal is creating. My child is doing very in school This school is horrid. The staff is unbearably rude and I'm not even going to mention the math department and their lack of knowledge for the subject it seems like. My first child went to this school and I am moving before I will send my next child there. no way! We LOVE Freedom. The staff, facility and education is top quality. Our Daughter is in Honors Classes and getting A's because the staff cares about out kids. The new facility and equipment makes this school superior. Happy Kids....great grades...happy parents. Great school, I graduated recently. There are some faculty that aren't that great, but that's with most schools. However, overall, each department has at least a handful of amazing teachers (especially the history and math departments). Administrators are also wonderful and incredibly supportive of their students -- many of them made my transition from high school to college easy. By far one of the most spirited and kindest student bodies I've seen in a Loudoun county high school. I have had two kids go through Freedom. I feel that the high school adequately prepared them for college. My daughter was on the dance team and it was a great experience for her. Both the teachers and administrators were great. Good experience so far and my daughter likes all the teacher. Specially math teacher she had in 10 grade was extremely excellent and she performed very well in math last year of 2016-2017 I think if your student is neurotypical this is an excellent school. If your student has an IEP, then you need to carefully watch to make sure it is being followed. Like all schools, it is hit or miss with teachers. The admin often does not give advanced notice when staff leave which can be difficult for students with IEP's. Looking to move to give my child a chance at and a positive experience at a different school. School leadership should be replaced Best public high school in all of Northern Virginia if you’re looking for a flat out good academic program with decent sports. It’s safe and the median students are high achievers. They will get a chance to go to good colleges.If you are a parent looking to have your high achieving child to continue his/her momentum, this is the school for them. Dr Fulton has done an exceptional job turning this school around. His high expectations for staff and students has paid off. He has created an inclusive environment. Students feel welcome and heard. You will see him at every sporting and activity event showing his support to the student body. He sets an example for everyone to follow. He also changed the outside of the school with endless hours. When you drive up to the school it is warm and inviting. Kids feel safe and are able to challenge themselves. He will be missed!

column3: Half-Hollow Hills school district overall is a quality education. All 3 of my children graduated from this district within the last 3-4 years and I found they adjusted well to college and did not struggle to make the adjustment due to academic weaknesses. The environment has a decently diverse student body for Long Island if that is what you are looking for. However, I would caution that treatment of African-American students has been sub-par in my view and the district needs to do better in this area. It isn't in your face discrimination but matters are not handled transparently and evenly in my view. I believe the district should look to emphasize character and and respect for others more. The proportion of persons of color in the faculty is poor. Again, this is an area the district needs to do more. You will need to stay on top of the faculty to ensure your child is being treated with fairness.There is a lot of passive aggressive behavior and classism that we witnessed in terms of the environment even though a lot of the families are really not wealthy but they feel they are. In terms of overall education I would say it is a good if not great value for the money but far from perfect district to send your kids to.

column1: this school is sadly a disappointment. my family isnt catholic and i sensed that from the beginning that by not being catholic we cannot be friends with you. my son tried out for the JD lacrosse team and imediatly found out that the only thing they cared about doing was winning. anything less than a win would result in brutal practices the next week. another thing i found out about this school is that its rules are very strict. and non changeable. WOW... I read the first review & was very shocked. (I imagine it was a mom that wrote the review) Once you get to high school the level of excellence as well as competition in every sport is top notch or if not striving to be, with that being said my son who is involved with the baseball program is being pushed to his limits in the most positive as well as spiritual way. I coached baseball for 10 yrs @ the rec/super league level & played high school & colledge ball my self, so I know an athlete when I see one. I was very disapointed with the Minor program I thought my son was going to be a part of, untill my eyes were opened by the teachers, staff, coaches & even parents at St. Juan Diego. Every thing there is based upon merit, not your ward or if you do or dont attend mass. Give Juan Diego a chance you will not ever regret the level of academics or the quality of any team involved in sports or any other extra curricular activity!!!! GO SOARING EAGLES.... I went to this school for all four years. It was a rip-off financially and even after we'd paid almost $10k each year for tuition they still begged for money every week with various excuses. We had to spend thousands of dollars for concurrent/AP enrollment, for textbooks, and for any club, organization, or activity that was not sport-related, even though most of this should have been covered in the ridiculous tuition. The majority of students were cruel and there was little diversity in the student body--the only sector that was accounted for was rich, white, and Catholic. The sole focus of this school is on sports, and if you aren't a star athlete you will probably be miserable at Juan Diego. High school was the worst four years of my life and I just wish I'd gone to public school. The entire idea of JD as "unified" is a downright lie, and the administration is horrible. Don't do it. We moved back to Salt Lake specifically for Juan Diego. The educational, sports, music, and misc. courses are second to none in the SLC area. I would venture to guess that anyone that is "disgruntled" in the school is not a paricipant in their children's future. Parents must be involved with service hours and this keeps up with the kids' education priorities and success. The sports programs are competetive but you can't tell me they aren't at any public school like Alta, Bingham, etc. I know of students that moved to public schools after a year or two at Juan Diego and every one of them spoke about how they don't receive the scholastic attention from the staff and the accountability that they were used to receiving at JD. Juan Diego truly prepares your student for college and beyond. We moved our kids from Rowland Hall two years ago to Juan Diego looking for a school that strives to bring out the best in our children, not only academically, but also socially and spiritually. For the most part, we found it here. There are no shortage of rules here (student handbook is over 30 pages) and the staff works to see that they are followed. Unlike at RHSM, bullying is taken seriously and addressed immediately. Academics are rigorous and students are able to take honors classes in all core subjects. Learning is often rote at the elementary school and grading uneven. Classes are huge, up to 36 students. Lots of AP options, particularly in the sciences. Most students go on to 4-yr colleges, many at top schools out of stated. Our family is not Catholic- while we like the grounding in biblical education and living the Golden Rule, the education of younger students can be very dogmatic. All students are encouraged to play on sports teams, many of which have winning traditions. Football players (and cheerleaders) are the social elite of the school, which can be discouraging for those not part of either group. Overall, an excellent learning environment. Compared with public I would have rated JD higher than 2 stars. However, after spending thousands of dollars on tuition for the school (oldest son graduated, middle son went through soph year), I give it 2 stars compared with Judge, the other Catholic school option in Salt Lake. We were disappointed with academics at JD, particularly math program. Middle son is struggling to catch up with peers at Judge. Son who graduated is not where we would have thought he would be (despite earning >3.5 GPA each year). Unfortunately, we thought he was getting a great education until he started testing for colleges. I believe that the administration's first passion is sports, particularly football. My opinion is that some of the athletes seem to be 'helped' through the system to keep their eligibility to play sports. Yes, I'm a disgruntled former parent. Only posting because we are pretty disappointed that the education we feel our son received is not in line with what we thought we were signing up for 4 years ago. We have been thrilled with the education at Judge. Academically, I dont' think the schools compare. I've also been much happier with the spiritual aspect of Judge vs. JD. I saw the graduating seniors college selections and it seems this high school prepares them for SLCC and not much else. Definitely not Chicago catholic school caliber. Three of my children attend Juan Diego. Transferring from the East Coast where education is better funded and very competitive, we were very happy with the honors and AP programs at the school. My children are involved in both sports and community programs. I'm especially happy with the inclusion of faith and social responsibility with the strong academic and other extracurricular activities. It can be hectic, but I believe they are being well prepared for all facets of life. I live in Draper and am coming into the catholic faith at the parish here. I am coming out of the Mormon faith. The Mormons have nothing like this. I have observed for over a yea r the programs here for the kids. These young people can get into any university of their choice after graduating, I wouldn't send my child anywhere else. We have been part the Juan Diego community for a long time. All of our children have attended this school. Overall the academics at Juan Diego are marginal. Our children took AP and honor classes and the quality of their education was average. Our children had to do a lot of self-learning and we had to essentially "home school" for a few years. They just do not pay the teachers enough and expect them to manage class sizes of 28+. Being a 3A school our children had an opportunity to get involved in sports, debate, and the arts. The debate program is excellent thanks to the debate leader and team. However, we were very disappointed in the overall leadership of the school. There are no checks / balances with family members running the school. We thought the faculty did the best they could given the administration they had to work with. Our children had an overall positive experience, but in hindsight, we could have saved $40K per child and sent them to a public high school where the academics are the same if not better. My children have graduated and say they wished they would have gone to public school instead. Do your homework before making a serious commitment. I have attended this school since pre school. The Juan Diego environment has allowed me to have the opportunity to excel academically, spiritually, as well as athletically. The students at Juan Diego are very accepting. However, the tuition is high and I question if a driven child would be able to receive the same amount of opportunities at a public or charter school? I have been a parent and campus staff for 12 years. I'd highly recommend it for virtually any family - especially from out-of-state. Great community. Vertical teaming of K-12 teachers ensure college readiness, performing arts and debate are phenominal, and nearly every student participates in a sport or club. Racial, religious, economic diversity is important. Retreat programs like Kairos help students bridge divides and explore their interpersonal and spiritual nature. This school is significantly overpriced for the quality of education particularly compared to the public schools in the area. The choices of classes are limited and the typical educational tools like a science lab and smart boards do not exist. There seems to be a focus on making a parent and student think they are getting a superior education without any real statistics to back it up. Parents are also constantly asked to donate money. The donation requests and lack of tools seem to relate to over 50% getting financial aide. The only good thing is the religious focus and some sports (definitely not all)! After moving to Draper from across the country, We tried multiple schools and we pleased when we found JDCHS. Public school was exclusionary to our non LDS students. Charter schools were found to be dumping grounds after the elementary levels. This school is open to communication from parents and students, offer multiple opportunities to participate in activities. As a non Catholic family, we never found this to be an issue and did not find ourselves excluded or solicited. Diverse atmosphere and anytime we experienced ANY issues with our student, we simply called the school and got all the answers or assistance we needed. We had email/phone/in person contact with teachers, coaches, and administrators. Good education, traditional levels and advanced classes, safe and caring atmosphere. Less tuition cost than some other private schools in the area. We hope to see our grandchildren attend JDCHS someday. In the 5h grade, my son was struggling with the group of boys he was with at a public school. We moved him to JD and the situation was improved. The students were more focused, driven and the educational requirements were higher. I now have 2 boys there and they both love it. It is not perfect but much better than the situation we were in. They have never been bothered about their religion as we are not Catholic. I appreciate the religious influence that is there without being left out. We are included. Juan Diego is warm and welcoming environment for all students, the teachers provide exceptional teaching techniques and one on one interactions that help the students better understand the subject and what is expected of them. Juan Diego is a large campus that hosts kids grades preK-12th. The students are in small classes and that allows interaction and unique bonds between students and facituly that you will see no where else. I have seen students come from public schools or even other private schools and whole heartedly fall in love with the Juan Diego dynamic. Juan Diego Catholic High School has been the best educational decision for our family. If you are looking for a school that is committed to excellence in education, building strong community bonds, Faith, STEMS, The Arts, the success of the whole child, who takes the time to partner with parents along the way, and has a strong commitment to service in the community...this is your school! We have loved our experience at Juan Diego. We love the community feel and all of the wonderful traditions that this campus has to offer. We feel that the school offers an excellent education while also promoting extra curricular activities including the arts, athletics and social justice programs. The teachers, faculty and staff are amazing. Our children began in the daycare and we are grateful for their "cradle to college" experience on this campus. We feel so blessed to be a part of this community. Wonderful!! We've had 2 children graduate from JDCHS 2009 & 2013 and, 1 that will be a senior 2018/2019 school year. When you've graduated from JDCHS or are still attending, employers will hire JDCHS kids before surrounding school even with a better GPA because of their values! Our two sons attended Juan Diego for 9th and 10th grade until we moved to Austin, TX this summer. It was an incredibly positive experience for them, even coming in as new students to the community as high schoolers. The administration, staff, teachers, and academics, including AP classes, are top notch, and the accepting and inclusive atmosphere on campus was unparalleled. Neither boy was in sports, so we can't speak on that, but, one was in theater arts and choir (which he loved), and both felt completely included and very much a part of the community. We highly recommend visiting campus and seeing for yourself! When you have a faculty and staff committed to excellence, it’s no surprise they are a National Blue Ribbon school. What’s more important than educating the future of our country! This first thing this school's profile shares it that they are Utah's only high school winner of a National Blue Ribbon Award. There are actually 11 other high schools in Utah who have won this award. Be prepared for more twisted facts that conveniently favor this school over others.
