column3: Diverse student population and great caring teachers. Don't let the low test scores fool you. It's just the fact that students in the regular classes tend to screw around. As long as you take honors or better yet AP courses, you'll have a mature, fun experience. I can't stress the amazingly diverse population. It nearly eliminates any racial tension you'd find at another school. Counselors tend to side with the student if he/she wants advanced classes. They give you quite a bit of freedom while still recommending a path depending on what you'll major in. They don't try to steer you away from advanced courses. A matter of fact, it's difficult getting out, as to motivate students to at least survive if not strive. I've learned more this year in my AP & honors classes than I have in all my previous school years combined and it wasn't pain-painstakingly difficult. For 3 years, I've went to a different school in the FJUHSD district and as a Senior, I'm attending BPHS. At first I was really concerned about my level of education and the quality of the school. I can gladly say with confidence that I had nothing to worry about. Most of the teachers are friendly and helpful. The people in the office don't have attitude like the other school I attended. There are little to no racial conflict and students are welcoming. The school doesn't have the best academic scores (CST) overall, but if you're determined to learn and work hard, you can excel in AP classes and Honors to get your GPA to a good standing. So far, I'm enjoying my attendance here, and I look forward to a great senior year. BPHS is now offering the Middle College program. Partnered with Cypress College it will be the only school in the district for the next 6 years to have this. The Middle College classes are taught by teachers with Master degrees and the credit for these classes count as college credit. Can you imagine the money and time saved by the students who graduate in four years? What a great idea! I am really impressed with the programs that are offered at Buena Park high. My daughter is in 9 th grade. I was told to send her to the other schools in our district. This school is different from when I went here. The staff and teachers really about education and the kids benefit from that. The middle College program is saving us money and her lots of time in College. I am happy at my choice to send her to BP. I am very pleased with Buena Park High School. The teachers are responsive and helpful in providing information about their class and how your child is doing. They are available during breaks or after school if your child wants extra help. The principal is friendly and accessible. I often see him around campus and at school events greeting and talking to students and parents. Many of the faculty have their own kids at the school, which shows that they also trust the quality of the teachers and school environment. BPHS's test scores may not be as high as other schools in the district, but that does not mean that it is a bad school. There are a lot of really good, smart, hard-working and motivated kids here. There are rigorous AP and honors classes, well-qualified and experienced teachers and staff, and a supportive learning environment. Overall, great school. As a parent I was worried when we moved here from garden grove. I am so happy that we did . My son would not be where is is today if it wasnt for Buena Park High . With the early college program and his guidance councilor Ms Chow my son started college as a SOPHMORE! . . A sophmore ! He will have is AA after only one year of college . . Thank you BPHS! It is truly outstanding knowing that it has been rated in the Top 4% of high schools in the US as rated by US News and World Report 2014. Wow! This school is a surprising gem of a high school. The teachers have been very responsive and committed to the success of their students. The students are down-to-earth, no entitlement attitude, and friendly. The size of the school is just right, has that family-feel. It would be good to see more parent involvement at the school.

It s a community where you pitch in the work to be the best not only for yourself, but for CKM as a whole. It s the pride of knowing that "IT s (always!) A GOOD DAY TO BE A LION! C. K. Mcclatchy High School this school is really nice C. K. Mcclatchy High School this school is really nice C. K. Mcclatchy High School this school is really nice Excellent! column3: I would like to point out how old all the other reviews are on this site.I will preface by stating that four to five years ago the school system was in a very different place than what it is now,and that in 2008 I would have given my school system a higher review but that is no longer the case.I am a recent Stonington High School grad and I graduated in the top 10 percent in one of the highest gpa classes the school has ever seen.Through out my career in the school system it has gone to hell in a hand basket.The teachers at Deans Mill are great, but most recently the schools have laid off almost all of their part time help which is a huge deficit.All the behind the scenes and the people who keep the student to teacher ratio low have been eliminated and the students will pay for this.On top of that, the disciplinary aspect of the high school does not exists,the high school teachers do not care about their students are there is an overwhelming feeling of teachers punishing students who excel.There is an extreme amount of favoritism among the teachers, and if you have the right name you will be in good shape.I could go on but I have reached the character limit.Dont trust scores alone. Love Stonington! High school is a nice size where students get a chance to get involved in a variety of academic and extracurricular activities! I would like to point out that the positive reviews are outdated. I would agree, nine years ago when we settled here with a third grader, we were excited about our child's educational future in this district. As leadership has changed, the budget slashed and many other shortcomings, we have found that SHS caters to the AP shining stars. If your child is an average student or below, you are pegged, the guidance department will not go out of their way to help, guide or encourage them. Phone calls are rarely returned. Our child's guidance counselor actually laughed at him when he told her his post-high school plans. He is now convinced he shouldn't bother applying for scholarships or any "dream schools." Our second child opted for one of the many magnet programs in this area and we have been amazed at the other school's environment. All students are valued, if your child even starts to show signs of slipping, there's an email, a phone call, reaching out. Guidance counselors are extremely involved in each child's success - even if they are not college bound. The principal of this other school is their biggest cheerleader. She is at every event (sporting, chorus, drama, etc). The students are thriving. SHS lacks the leadership and quality environment to move forward. Changes need to be made. Our third child will not be attending SHS unless major changes occur. Excellent faculty who cares about their students' success. The awarding SHS of one star is due solely to the Football staff. The teaching staff are not only woefully disinterested, but I suspect they honestly do not even like teaching; the Superintendant's and Admission's offices are sadly, a comedy routine that you would not believe exist in reality anywhere; and the guidance department is completely asleep at the switch. All of this, is of course, a dramatic improvement over Mystic Middle School and Deans Mill Elementary.From the school nurse demanding that my children retake every innoculation shot from birth through eighth grade before being admitted to school (nurse reason given was that all shots were given by MDs outside the state of CT?!?), to no text books--instead just copied off ragged papers occasionally given out, a block schedule sytem in which you never know what class you have when, nor which to prepare for regarding tests, papers, et al., and the school's insistence that your children not attend school for weeks at a time due to their odd admissions issues (this after all paperwork has been completed and all residency proof admitted year after year). Absolutely avoid the Stonington School District at all costs! Even with 4.0 students that overachieve in many areas, this place will ruin them! One positive, however, the football program and staff have been the only positive in an otherwise intentionally destructive school system. there is a very good reason that an enormous number of parents home school in this district. BEWARE! Great School! A lot of opportunity and great community enviorment. Extremely positive. My student was very prepared academically for a very challenging college. Leadership, sports and community service opportunities were encouraged and provided for those who sought them out. The administration cares about every students and does not give up on them, no matter what their abilities. Hard work is definitely rewarded.

column1: I graduated from LHS in 2004, so there very well could be changes since then. I really enjoyed my time at LHS. The honors program and core classes were great. They didn't offer a HUGE variety of electives, but the ones they had were good- robotics, pottery, art, speech, drama, etc. They had a great music program and lots of sports. The pep rallies and school spirit were just "so so". This school and the majority of the staff are awful. I have attended this school for the last four years. The staff are very bias and stereotypical of students. the staff, who are suppose to lead by example and create a very positive learning environment do the exact opposite. They are very rude and constantly talk down to students to make themselves feel more powerful. There have been various teachers and staff that have been reported to the principle due to horrible treatment towards students. So far, the principle has made no attempts to change things for the better. I would not recommend this school to anyone. If you value your kids education, please do not register them for this school. I would give this school zeros stars if i could. If you value your children's education, do not enroll them in this awful school. You will regret it. The school does not prepare students for state test that are needed for graduation. This school constantly hires new teachers that do not know how to teach, resulting in many students failing and filing complaints. The staff are very rude and do not care about the student body. If you report an issue to the school, they will simply disregard your complaint and take the side of faculty. My son was being discriminated against by his teacher. He and his group members were completing a worksheet where every member had the same answer. Once they received their scores back, his other team members received and A, while he received an F. I have reported this issue to the school. So far, they have brushed me off and continue to make excuses for the horrible staff. This school has very diligent staff members that want you to succeed, I'm very fond of this school. =) The staff is a joke and don't expect to have your personal views accepted unless they fit the PC views of this school. I requested a meeting with a teacher that was bullying my son over his views during a Social Economics class. He made his entire school year awful. And when the teacher was looking for any way to get him kicked out, I pushed for a meeting with the teacher, principle, my self and my son. It was rescheduled by the vice principle and the teacher so many times that nothing was done and the year ended. Then when my son tried to get his license from the DMV the school wouldn't even verify that he had been a student. The DMV was shocked at the rudeness and unwillingness to answer a simple question. This has left my son scrambling to get other important documents and things done to start his life. I'm so grateful to have him out of that school and we are moving to make sure our other children will never attend this PC school. Very good school and teachers. No bullying or disrespect tolerated I am a behavior technician and I worked one on one with a student with autism. I had been with this child for his last year of middle school and followed him into high school. This child has a difficult time transitioning, Especially in a new environment. Everything seemed fine when I got there, but then all of a sudden it seemed like they didn't even need me around. They just took over. I was trying to tell them about the child and I was completely ignored. There was one staff member who knew him in 3rd grade and kept trying to reference that time of his life. The child is in 9th grade now. Kids change. Why listen to the person who has been with him consistently for a year and off an on since 2020? After we got the child off the bus, he was nervous because he was in a new environment (new school, new staff etc). I told them that it might take a while to get him to the classroom. During Summer School, it took him a couple weeks to get in the building. So what do they do? Proceed to grab him by his safety harness and attempt to force him to the building! I told them they are just going to traumatize the child. I have a picture of them surrounding him like hes an animal! I was not at all okay with how they handled the situation. Then somebody suggested to call the 911! I said absolutely not! We aren't even suggesting to call the cops on a 14 year old Black kid with autism! It was a mess, until we finally got him to the courtyard near the building, but they still decided to ignore me and just take over. Then they contact my employer and say that I had a hard time helping the kid and they want someone else. I have been with that child for a while and have never had any issues doing my job with him! I do have a minor disability that prevents me from moving quickly, but if they did not cause my kid to escalate, that would not have been an issue. I have always been able to do my job with him. So we can add ableism and discrimination to the list. And help how?! There were already 4 people on top of him, and they had me pushed out before I even started! I would not recommend Lindbergh if you have a child with special needs. I don't feel like they see the whole child. They don't care about what is best for the child, they just care about what is easiest for them. I've been working in schools for 20 years and there are always issues, but this was terrible! Violence in the hallways is a daily occurrence. Numerous times over sexual assault is swept under the rug. Staff discourage students from reporting and staff themselves fail to report.Students are discouraged from speaking out about their experiences and taking any appropriate action.

column1: I attended both Frewsburg Central and High Schools. They were the best years of my life growing up. Although I can't really compare my experience to other schools (because I never attended any other schools), others peers of mine who went else where have expressed they didn't like their schools. Southwestern is a bunch of rich/snobby kids, Jamestown is the "inner city" kids (with way to many kids in their classes to get the attention they need), Randolph is the country kids (yes, even more country than Frewsburg) and Falconer is comparable to Frewsburg. Frewsburg High School has a big pool (for swim teams and gym class), great teachers who really care, a nice, clean school, and small classes. When I graduated in 2005, my graduating class was around 80 or 85 students (including 4 Foreign Exchange Students!). great and if we had stayed in the area - would have loved for our children to have attended Frewsburg schools Educationally, the middle/high school was not good. They use block scheduling which results in students spending a lot of their day in study halls because of the lack of class availability. Block scheduling is great, but not in a school of this size. Some teachers were very professional and competent, while others were not. The elementary school was fine but I would not recommend anything beyond 6th grade. My children related stories of some students being constantly bullied, but nothing ever seemed to be done about disciplining the bullies. The previous principal at the high school was ineffective and seemed to make radical changes often. There has been a recent change in the principal, so hopefully changes will be made.

column3: This school is in a downward spiral. The staff blatantly disregards parental opinion, and the new principal is cracking down on everything from the ability to carry backpacks to the reviews people write on facebook. Yes, the school has issued a post that any negative reviews will be blocked from the school page. If at all possible, avoid dealing with this school. It was a great school many years ago, and it wasn't even too bad when my children went there; however when they lost John McDonald, they lost one of the few employees who cared about the students and the parents. With each new principal and each new board, it gets worse. Most of the faculty are spiteful, gossipy, grudge-holding individuals who pass along any negative information about the students to the next grade instructors, who then have their own predetermined opinion of the students. There is no equality at the school--it depends on who you are as to what you can say, do, or think. Unless you intend to spend 4 years fighting for your child, don't go there!! The board ignores any in put the students give them. The students are denied the right to creativity and speaking their mind. The doors for each class must be locked, no back packs, can't open windows, and security guards in and around the school. This school is one step away from becoming a prison. The teachers also no longer care about the students. As soon as the school day is over the teachers are gone and never there to tutor or help the students. This school also has the biggest ego ever for such a disappointing school. When I was in school at Hollidaysburg (many,many years ago), I would say that I had a pretty good experience; however, since my children were there (many years ago), the whole school experience for these kids has become more like a prison than a school. The saving grace for my children was a teacher/dean named John McDonald. He is the only person in the past 35 years who was a great counselor, mentor, disciplinarian, representative, and advocate of the students. It was a very sad day when the world and Hollidaysburg lost him. If there were more administrators, counselors, and teachers like him, we would have an outstanding school and community. He didn't just pick the "good" students to mentor, he picked them all. Administration and teachers work for us--they should have to answer for what they do, just like the students. Tenure is the worst thing that has ever happened to the school system. What other job can someone have where they don't do their job, are rude to their "customers", are morally and ethically wrong, and they still are able to keep their job. This school has such a giant ego. They think that they can do anything they want just because they're better than Altoona or any other school in Blair County. They don't ever change their policies, and they wonder why they're so behind. There are bans on just about everything you can think of. Backpacks, food, and drinks are all banned. Before this year, they had a strict phone policy that involved confiscating a student's phone for using it anywhere, including the cafeteria and hallways. They also treat the GACTC students unfairly, reducing their lunch time and excluding them from events. Don't ever go here unless you want to deal with 3 years of pain and suffering. 10 with the teachers 1 with administration I had a wonderful experience at Hollidaysburg. The teachers and staff at the school have made such an impact on my life. The opportunites to get involved is outstanding. The classes and work, while it may seem annoying at the time, really is just set up to prepare the students for college. When I arrived at college, I was shocked to know that most of what they were going over in all of my classes I had already learned being at Hollidaysburg. There were some students at college that didn't even know how to do simple things like APA and MLA style papes. I am still in contact with many of the teachers at the school and would not trade my high school experience for the world. It is such an amazing high school because of the wonderful faculty there.

My child was encouraged to drop out on a daily basis... She was humiliated by teachers.... and when she asked for help with her academics she was ignored. Our son is finishing his sophomore year. With the exception of only 1 or 2 teachers over the past 2 years, they genuinely seem to care about the children and want all to succeed. To be blunt, I hated this school. I felt in my years there that my education was not a priority for OPHS. They sure do care about the 'education' of their student athletes, however! I had a few amazing teachers at my time at OPHS. Most of my teachers really didn't care. My peers were absolutley rude as well. We built like 10 new building that aren't in use, but our classrooms have broken AC and or are falling apart. Classes don't have paper to print things on, but good to know we bought 2 plasma screen to replace the TVS in the cafeteria (that were in perfectly good, working condition). Students and teachers vary. If you're in an advanced or honors class, you'd be OK, but if you're in regular classes, good luck. Some students are decent people, but a majority of them are disrespectful brats that don't want to learn. They blatantly disrespect teachers and harass classmates. When administrators come in to reprimand them and the students laugh at them. They get two stars because despite the lack of discipline, most teachers show that they care about students and try (though not always successfully) to teach them. If you are white and athletic you will have a better chance of winning the lottery than gaining any further experience in your sport. The coaches are arrogant. If you think being consistently on the honor will make a difference, you are sadly mistaken, Teachers lose homework assignments, tests, and other papers then give the student a zero for the assignment the incompetent teacher lost. Doesn’t exactly encourage students to do their best. Truly a strongest survive type of school with an abundance of violence and bullying that is ALLOWED to go on. My daughter is an honors student. She is intelligent, beautiful, strong, smart, and fortunately she grew up the youngest of 5 and the only girl, so she is also very capable of defending herself. This is something you need to survive in Orange Park High School and if you don’t believe your child can defend themselves in street style fighting on a regular basis, or endure a ridiculous amount of regular and repeated at will style ridicule - more importantly do not feel that any child SHOULD have to physically defend themselves or emotionally heal from a day at school I would not recommend allowing your child to attend this school. orange Park high school does not care for the kids at that school. And the principles at the school's make kids with special need look stupid that don't care if you get in trouble that don't help you. If you have a child who needs an IEP or is an ESE student, do not send them to Orange Park High. The staff cannot do anything to help with children who have disabilities. Good luck.

column1: My daughter is a freshman at BBHS and is loving it. She felt welcome from the first day she toured the school. She had a choice of Notre Dame, Newport Central Catholic and BBHS. After visiting and shadowing at all of them she made her choice. She found the community spirit at BBHS to be friendly and inclusive. She is excelling in her academics and is fond of the teachers. We are all happy with Bishop Brossart and would recommend it to anyone seeking a Catholic High School, where your student will feel like part of the family and be challenged to achieve at their highest potential!!! Having been at Brossart for 3 years, i find some of the previous ratings hard to believe. Although there may be some bullying, as with any school, it's not tolerated by staff or the majority of students at Brossart. The motto of the school is "Charity First" and while academics is a major focal point at Brossart, the well being of its students definitely comes first. All of the teachers are willing to take the time to work with their students in class as well as outside of school. It is a great school with a strong faculty that works hard to help its students develop both academically and spiritually. "Bullying is not tolerated by the staff or the majority of students"??? Really?? That is news to me. I don't think a majority "participates" in bullying...but they definitely tolerate it...which can be just as bad.

column3: Looks like things are getting better. It went from 7 to 8. People that I know went here are doing good in life. I love the facilty and staff that are at MHS. I love the way the teachers teach you. Also the campus is safe!!1 This is a good school. Great teachers and awesome Principal. This school has 2012 API of 825 and progressive improving year over year. I love this school and it is in a great location. I think this place rocks, with the exception of a couple of teachers. Cheryl Rivera ROCKS! I don't really like anything about this school except for the technology and football program. The staff at this school needs to be replaced. For the past 2 months I've been trying to get a counselors appointment (for college applications) and ive tried at the least 20 times and have yet to succeed. The staff here do not care about the students and it's time for that to change. And as for the teachers here, it's a dice game. There's a chance you may get a caring teacher but more likely than not you'll get one who doesn't care about their subject and makes learning awful. I do not recommend this school for anyone mostly because since there's so many students there won't be much attention to your education. I recommend Coupertino High School, I had my brother go there and he absolutely loves it and is well taken care of. Excellent. My daughter went here her entire 4 years and we had a rewarding experience in all respects notes in this questionnaire. This is a poor quality school. Most of the counselors and teachers are pretty unhelpful. Some of the teachers often are biased when grading and frequently make errors when posting grades online or in the report card. Scheduling mistakes are common and due to the school being overcrowded, it is VERY hard to fix your schedule. In fact, the reason why most kids attending this school go to community college is due to scheduling mistakes such as not getting the AP class you chose. Bullying is common and low-income kids are rarely disciplined by the school. In fact, higher income students are often looked down upon by some teachers and even administrators! This school is also not disabled friendly. There is no bathroom for the disabled and these students(including injured/ill) often have to manage getting to class by themselves. This school does very little to address those with mental health issues. Coming from a student who has been in Milpitas his whole life, I think this school is superior to many in this region. There are occasional teachers who get on my nerves but almost all the staff members are outstanding when it comes to contributing to the school. Many of the students know to strive beyond the "recommended" and are willing to work hard. There have not been many serious cases of bullying with the exception of a few that happened many years ago. Extracurriculars are also very big in the school. More than 1/3 of the student population participate in a sport/ club which makes school truly feel like a community. All in all, the MHS is a great school and I would not change a thing about it except for a few bad teachers. Both of my 2 sons went their entire 4 years here. They both graduated with honors. After high school, they both went on to universities. One now is a Marketing Director for a hi-tech company and the other is a medical physician. All Teachers are different. Academic wise high school is very good.

Eden Staff need to get a little more active in the education of all students during the 2011-2012 school year. There needs to be a website for the school. My daughter attended MLK Middle and every staff was so welcoming, supportive and enjoyed their job. We loved the Middle school experience and the great involvement of the lovely MLK staff. KUDOS to MRS. SANTOS!!! The principal at the MLK was awesome and Mrs Santos was just supportive of everything on the campus. I don't see this at Mt. Eden HS. Their seems to be a I don't care mood that is unacceptable. Meeting are always unorganized, cancelled or just don't happen. This year, I will make sure that things happen because it will be reported to the HUSD school district and Alameda county Office of Education immediately..I'm tired and hate to do this, but it's my child and other''s education at jeopardy. No more, no more! Things need to really change at Mt. Eden big time. Change will happen for the 2011-2012 school year and I promise that. The CCS committee at Mt. Eden has been there for over four years, we During these four years they haven't earned anything just to spend the money they not even have bylaws. We need to have new elections, we need to have people who really wants to help the community This school is garbage. The students there will treat you like trash no matter what. Don't think they'll be nice. They can be nice at first, but they'll backstab you in the end, and that is unacceptable. I have been bullied every single day during my high school years, and because of that, this school deserves only 1 star. You all should be ashamed of yourselves. ATTEND ELSEWHERE! Mt. Eden High School may not be the best looking school there but i have been attending there for 2 years and the teachers give you major support. all thought there may be a gang problem there the only thing you can do to be safe is just not hang out with the wrong kind of people and dont start something you cant finish. As long as you treat people with respect they will treat you with respect back. The bullying is not bad at all everyone is nice and not one time hav i been bullied. There is girls there that dont like me but after all who cares im there to learn! This school may look ghetto but it's not. Mt. Eden has a lot of school pride and the people probably have the most school pride then any other school. The murals are beautiful and they make due with what they have. I have not been bullied since I've been here and everyone is actually nice. If parents are worried about their child they shouldn't. Mt. Eden is safe and it all depends on where your child stands as a person. Badmitton has been undefeated and their football/basketball programs has been stepping it up. choir and Band are #1 in Norcal and most likely in the country. There are a lot of dedicated people. The art program is really good as well. if you haven't seen the murals by ap art, you need to check it out. before you judge the school by appearence, attend one of the events! I just the district gave more money and help give Mt. Eden more potential. I wouldn't want to attend any other school and I love Mt. Eden! GO MONARCHS! I love this school so much i bleed blue and gold! Amazing school. The spirit at MEHS is strong and encouraging and the arts program is unmatched. Mrs. Marshall is unbelievable with her dance kids and transforms habits. Ms. King teaches her kids to draw with their hearts. Mr. Rawdon is a magical in guiding the award winnin choir. Mr. Kevin Cato leads the MEHS Band with pride and changes the hearts of his students. Mr. Ronnie Cato is a father, friend, teacher, and just about everything to his Orchestra and without him, nothing would be possible. Amazing school with amazing people. Don't judge a people by the practicalities of their school; Mt. Eden High School will make you eat your words. This school is not at all good. All the asians hang in one corner, all the Hispanics in the other. There are no people who will want to be your friend. The counselors there, are never actually there, they're always at "meetings" . A certain math teacher expects students to know Algebra 2, and fails 50% of students. However, one thing about this school i love is Chemistry Honors program. The teacher is great and knowledgable, and students learn skills, they could actually use in real life. (ahem algrebra 2) The choir program is great, but all the asians refuse to be friends with diverse people. Same with show choir. That is all. =) This school was not the best looking but we do our best to make ot look nice and neat I love mt Eden especially the art program its soo amazing if your an artist or love art or want to Lear I encourage you to take art.we have amazing teacher's that make teaching fun and interesting. GO MONARCHS This school use to have a bad reputation but it has completely changed for the best. I am so happy that I put my son in this school. Every school has it's flaws but Mt. Eden's priorities are there students and there education. They also have the best music program in the entire US. I love this school. I have great friends and some teachers who care. Like Mr. Klien, Ms. Shelton, Mr. Duran, and Ms. Mann. But most teachers are just their to get paid and that's it. They have no interest in the students. As a highly qualified veteran teacher I was saddened to experience such horrid conditions.The classroom had rat droppings everywhere, trash stuffed into all cabinets, rude disrespectful students, graffiti all over the desks etc, NO working heat, and outdated curriculum. ALL of which is illegal in California.Students who curse out teachers and/or destroy books are NOT given consequences. IE: less suspensions make principals look good.I did not see any social responsibility or compassion here. Students left litter all over the campus and thought nothing of stealing from each other/teachers. Mt. Eden is the best school in Hayward. Mr. Duran has really turned the school around. His passion and joy for the school has elevated the moral of students to believe that what ever they set their mind to they can do. This is the best high school in Hayward United school district. My child had always gone to private school until 9th grade. I put him in Hayward high that school has gone down the toilet. My child had a fight the first week he was there because of some bully hitting over & over. Mt. Eden the teachers and the students were wonderful. The kids cross the street In the crosswalk and we’re very respectful just like the kids that attended private school. You will always have a couple bad seeds, just like most of have in the office. My child graduated in 2020

column1: McLauin High School's staff and faculty go far and beyond the call of duty for their students. They want their students to succeed. I know of teachers spending their own money and using their own time to provide for their classes. A small school set in a rural area, Mclauin does not get the financial support from private business nor the tax money, like the city schools do. As a result, Mclaurin lacks in appearance and updated equipment. The small teacher to sudent ration is a plus for us. Less than 100 students in my daughter's class, they all know each other well. Mr. Lennington and the assistant principals run a tight ship and as a parent, I am pleased about that. As soon as you turn into the school's drive, you see male coaches, teachers and principals all out front on alert watching the parking lot and students unloading. Unlike the huge city schools, you immediately are aware of who is in control at MHS. Ms Watson is always patroling the halls and the students do not want trouble with her. If your child wants to learn and succeed, then MHS is a wonderful school. However, there is low tolerance for trouble makers and clowns. MHS - a small school with a huge heart 4 students. Both of my kids have always been great students.Unfortunately of all the schools they.have attended this has to be the worst ! I will not go into details from bullying, staff gossip about each other and students So happy my children no longer go there This school fails our children in every way possible. Staff acts more like children than caring adults- I honestly do not think they know how to encourage them or even realize their own behavior. My child has attended school elsewhere and here, the differences are astonishing. Also academically THEworse school I have ever been a part of...this school is appalling. Should be closed. ...this is all of our futures I am very proud of our school and community. McLaurin is a fantastic school and will only get better. Live Green...Love Gold...We ARE McLaurin. S. Rimes, Principal. My sons in 7th grade now I am a proud parent!Being able to send my son to a safe and educationally productive school makes me feel great for him!The teachers are wonderful, they're always there for him, and don't even get me started on how much he loves that.I remember when he went to Mendenhall he was terrible academically and sports wise he went there up until 5th grade.I always make sure to go to all of his games, because it love watching him play, and all of his friends play to and they're really good.Overall this school is one of the best schools in Rankin County its academically great, involved with sports, most importantly it's safe!After hearing about all about these school fights in places like Brandon, Puckett, and Magee I'm worried quite bit for his safety.It really scares me, I Iove him and I don't want anything to happen to him.It wasn't that violent at Mendenhall but I feel much more let at ease about my sons safety, they have great security and the teachers care so much about the students I'm not even worried!There normally are a lot of fights, but here you rarely see any!I highly recommend this school!Its a great place also a safe and happy environment. I was first enrolled at McLaurin in 2nd grade. Back then all elementary had to bus up to Florence because McLaurin was only a high school. I would soon fall in love with this small county school. Its one of those rare places that you immediately feel at home in. I am now over 40 and my children have the same love. Although it was built in 1958 and is in need of some improvements, its the only place I would have my children attend. Its the kind of stuff movies are made of that makes you fall in love with. Its one of those lost gems you are only once in a while lucky enough to stumble upon. McLaurin has heart! McLaurin is small town at its BEST! WE meet no strangers and welcome everyone. Teachers take the time to make sure you know the material. They work overtime unpaid, stay late and get there early to accommodate any student that could use extra help. Dr. Rimes, the principle, has an open door policy and is more than willing and eager to answer any question or offer help needed. You can keep up to date on all the schools happenings at http://www.mclaurinattendancecenter.my-pto.org/ this is the bes scool i have ever went o the teacher are great they ae very nice and they only seem to get better

I am originally from PA and found it a great place to raise my kids, with lots of opportunities to be involved in their education. Years ago I attended school here. At that time it was A decent school for the most part. I could go on and on about it today but I'm going to stick to the facts. Below are four different cases and four different learning levels . Two out of the four attened from fith grade on Third from first and last from kindergarten. Please note a school is to teach a child academics so they can succeed and excel in life. Whether the school is welcoming are not to me is not relevant. Insider outsider what does it matter if your child is getting the proper education. Child one should never have graduated. Did not pass yearly tests. Teachers gave child passing grades to keep the graduation rate high . Child two could pass any test with eyes closed. Was born gifted . Child missed 75% of school never turned in any work. Was given a passing grade to keep graduation rates high. I know of other children in this school who did not attend and due to absences should not have graduated but did to keep stats high. Child three has been passed along each school promising correction of a problem . Child can not read . Child is in high school and is currently comprehending at a Elementary level. Child has been privately tested. School states child is almost to grade level. Child has consistently failed all tests every year since first grade. Child will graduate illiterate. Child four is average. Passes all tests. Turns in all work. Gets whats belived average grades. Child has been marked slow in files. Needing help in areas child excels at and average in areas child does not. In conclusion your child will graduate from this school. Whether they have learned anything or not that's another question. I would never recommend this school to anyone. This has been an amazing school. We are a military family so we have seen 5 districts total and 9 schools in those districts. Poquoson is among the best of them. We are so pleased with our choice to live here. Overall my wife and I were very unhappy with Poquoson High School. They have had problems with racial issues in the past. Apparently, they still do. I would not recommend parents send their special needs students of color to this school. some of the teacher's in this school are nice while others are strict. some of the work is fun to do. many of the student's are nice but there are some bullies.

The athletic program caters to the "elite" and if you're not in the club, your child probably won't advance to their highest potential. column3: I attented Central in the 60's to be fair to the town my father was in the air force and was transfered there from California, I never knew what he did wrong to get transfered to North Dakota. What a shock, the town people did not like the base people and the base people did not like the town people, we were all just to different for each other. If I had the wisdom I have now I would have gone out of my way to make the experience more pleasant. i go to school here and i have to say most of the teachers are nice..but then there are some who won`t give you the time of day. They are strict about school work and there are some teachers who care..but some things aren`t fair. I attended Central high school from 9-12 grade, and think that it was a wonderful school to attend. Most of the teachers put a lot of effort into effectively communicating their topic to their students, and were willing to donate extra time if a student had questions .I was in the AP classes, and feel that all of the AP teachers did a more than adequate job at preparing me academically for the AP tests and the college level courses that followed. The school has wonderful music and theater programs, and also offers all of the expected athletic extracurricular activities. Since I graduated, Central upgraded their facilities and did an overhaul of the buildings structure. It can still be confusing to navigate for your first few visits, but I always found that having multiples ways to get to class was an advantage- if one hallway or stairway was too crowded there was always a less crowded alternate route that one could take. Overall Central is a lovely school and would be a great choice for any student in the Grand Forks area. They offer advanced classes, a variety of extracurricular options, and teachers dedicated to helping their students succeed academically.

column1: Milan Schools are so fortunate to have a staff that REALLY cares about children. Teachers in this school system give 110%. We have great students and supportive parents and a real sense of community. Milan is a great school! We moved to the area about 3 months ago and have found the community to be warm and welcoming. The teachers take a real interest in each student. It appears very little bullying happens in this school system and the students tend to give positive support each other.

column3: BHS is a pretty good school for your academics, but don't expect too many social skills from the students there. i'm currently a freshman there and the students are mainly all in their cliques. But, the acedemics are really good. The teachers are excellent and really do take there job seriously. The test scores are great and the school is ranked among the top 10 in Washington. Everybody is very nice and welcoming. For those who have rated this school and said that new people will not do well in the community are wrong. I moved to the area last year and have made an abundance of great friends and have met some awesome people. The high school is what you make it. Everyone is very smart and do care about there academics. There is a handful of people who are involved in drugs, but that is only a very, very small percentage. The sports are great and the extracurricular activities are awesome. Go Spartans. Bainbridge High School is extremely difficult academically, and is horrible socially. Your academic success highly depends on which teachers you get, some of which are extremely rude, and those who are nice, but don't teach anything. I worked as hard as I possibly could my freshman and sophomore year and barely scraped out of each semester with a 3.0. It is extremely hard to balance any sport with school on Bainbridge, and teachers are not forgiving when it comes to that. I was a very social student, with many friends, but I still hated the social environment at the high school. Every grade has cliques and they refuse to mesh. Drugs, alcohol, etc are not uncommon. It is so hard to be unique, and be yourself, because you WILL get made fun of it, unless you're popular. Would not recommend this high school, as it is very hard, and the teachers do not want to help you unless you suck up to them. BHS has a reputation for college prep and generating good test scores, but if you're not a traditional student/athlete, it is a horrible place to be. The school lost a lawsuit this year for not protecting a girl with a learning disability from a bullies, and also was cited for violations recently by OSPI for not providing services to another learning disabled student. It's easy to get left behind. Despite being a very quiet town, they have an officer on duty, creating an odd atmosphere. The teachers are dedicated, but BHS needs reform. I would like to give this high school zero stars. I would not send a student to any school in this district that has a learning difference that would require a 504 or IEP or any interaction with the special education "department." It is our experience that this school district does not meet the needs of unique learners. Our experiences with the district have been very, very negative. Our experience with the high school is that there are no specialized instruction/classes/co-teaching, etc. for our LD student. Be prepared to accept modified grades, an altered diploma, and low expectations instead of a specialized education. The school district has a big problem. Make contact with parents of special education kids on the island - or just avoid it completely. BHS is a great school for middle of the road kids who fit inside a certain box. For everyone else - advanced kids, kids with any kind of learning disability, kids who are not totally into sports - I would not recommend this school at all. One of my kids ended up doing running start to get away, the other begged to go to a different school. Rampant drug and alcohol abuse, serious eating disorders in girls, slut shaming posing as "health education" (using the duct tape talk) all contribute to an atmosphere that is not a positive place for learning. This was one of the worst school experiences I have ever had. If you are a new kid, no one will even give you the time of day. I was pushed and shoved in the hallways without any apology or remorse, and the staff do nothing to help. Out of all my classes, I had one teacher I felt actually cared about me. Never send your kid here. This is a wonderful school. The teachers are top-notch and passionate about what they do, and the administration really cares. The education my daughters have received there is equivalent to the best private schools in Seattle. This school is great for students who can learn and have a direction for their future. The school has high standards and expectations and provides many avenues to keep the students engaged. Particular attention is directed to making sure all students have a pathway to graduation and preparation for further education especially collage bound individuals. I have gratitude to the staff and especially the teachers who care about the success of the students. As a parent with two children on an EIP; you really need to advocate for your students. Otherwise they get lost in the system. We had several issues over the past two years including my one daughter being mismatched with a teacher who was not equipped to communicate with a student on an IEP. Even after sending several emails; we never heard back from the teacher and had to get the associate principal involved and they still prioritized the teacher over my child. I would NOT send my child to this school if they on any 504 or IEP support. I would give no stars but that is not an option. The teacher and students have zero accountability or code of conduct. There are no morals but even worse, the academics are way below what we gave previously experienced at private school. I am currently trying to get my child back in private school. We moved in 2020. The public schools here are an abomination.

column1: Lots of bullies in the school including the teachers. There is nothing Catholic in BGHS. I have my son and daughter there for the lack of Christian High schools in the area. Not worth the money. As a parent with two children at BG and as person involved in the teaching profession I can say that I am very pleased with the education my kids are receiving. The quality and care shown by the teachers at BG greatly exceeds what I have seen in the government schools. The teachers know every child's name they ask about events in their life, teachers are involved in school activities. It is more than just a job to them it is their community. Also, while no school is bully free it seems that for the most part every one has a place at BG. I spent my daughters first year there working in the lunch room, just so I could check out the atmosphere. There did not seem to be the usual "cool people's" tables ect. Also because the school is so small everyone has an opportunity to play sports. You don't have to "try out" for a team if you want to join a team you join it. Your even allowed to play two sports in a semester. I also love the fact that every class opens with a brief prayer. It only takes 10to 15 seconds but it sets the tone for the class.

column3: So disappointed. This is our 4th year at Port High and it is very difficult understand the culture at this school. I had my child's counselor tell me "I have 950+ kids to worry about, I can't worry about yours." When I contacted the principal in the fall regarding an unexcused absence, I was told to talk to the teacher that gave my child the unexcused absence. When I did, he said it was too much work to open his computer and read the email from another teacher excusing my child. And now I completely understand why my children say it is too hard and frustrating to talk to a teacher regarding their grade/missing work etc. I just received and email from a teacher that said they need to come before class or stay after school. If they didn't ride the bus to and from school I can understand how they could stay after school to discuss this with a teacher. Getting out of one class to go to another teachers class? I've also had the TAG counselor change my child's schedule without ever letting the child know! No apology, nothing from the TAG counselor. If you're a parent that doesn't want to be involved in your child's education, this is the school for you. Many exciting opportunites and the new building is going to be amazing for our kids coming up. Superintendent 's Required 100% Positive Thinking and Behavior creatives a culture of denial and avoidance among the Administrative leadership and limits teacher-parent communication that would benefit students. In The past six years of attending parent teacher conferences for my two kids, I found no teacher was willing to acknowledge any student need or challenges - just positive comments, even when my student was struggling with the subject material in their class. Administration is fully aware of increasing availability of drugs in the school building, yet refuse to acknowledge this very real danger, even when hosting speakers to discuss underage drug & alcohol use- They title these events parenting workshops. There are highly qualified teachers in each academic area, yet parents need to guide & monitor their own student's progress. Lots of favoritism & special privileges for kids of active parent booster organizations. Great school! Great planning for future whether college bound, military, trades, etc. We moved to this school district in 2018. Wow! What a difference. This school district really does a great job in academics and extracurricular activities. Our two sons are totally engaged in learning and having memorable experiences. We can tell the teachers really love their jobs. Mr. Gephart is an amazing choir director. If you want you children to be prepared for college and the future this school district is a fantastic option.

column1: Boston Arts Academy is a great school for children that want to express themselves threw art. There is no other arts school where children can do this except this great school. What I love about this school, it's not all about their art majors it is also about their academics to. People are hesitant when they hear art school but this school is very focus on the academics as well as there art major. The kids have to balance both if they want to succeed in this school. That is the great thing about this school they believe in every child no matter what they bring to the school everyone is accepted! This school gives them a chance to express themselves without getting judge and that is hard to find these days in a school great work BAA! I think it's a good school for the arts. Academically, no. Look somewhere else for that. Teachers are not supportive, never get a call back, hard to reach anyone in the school. Parking is a nighmare. I took my daughter out of a great school in the suburbs for this school which was a big mistake. I loved BAA and the community there. They supported me through my major and academics. Everyone is passionate about their majors and you learn about not only your own specific art but all of the arts. BAA helps build character and connections.

column3: Great school with an informed, aware staff! The student body is kind, and I have really enjoyed being a sub at this school several times. I could not be happier with the education my children are receiving at this school. One child is graduating and headed to a fantastic university, and the other one is a freshmen. The teachers have been phenomenal and are dedicated to helping students succeed. The building is beautiful, and the student body seems very nice. I am so proud that my children are Wolves! It has to step up its game. STRIVE, for 21.5 on the ACT? sad. No offense My family moved to the area just in time from the 2011-2012 school year from Minnesota. My daughter was attending a prestigious private school, and I can honestly say that moving to Plainfield and sending my daughter to OEHS has been more than an amazing experience! The building is gorgeous, her teachers go above and beyond. Although my daughter is in mostly Honors classes and does not need me to tell her to get her work done, I receive emails from teachers keeping me in the loop. Sure, the test scores for OE aren't ideal, but that's an average of how the kids perform-my daughter is an individual. Every school has its challenges, and OE is no dofferent. As for the social aspect, she has grown tremendously! She is involved in sports and has made great friends. Our move couldn't have gone smoother, the transition easier, and we couldn't be happier! Transferred to area...Oswego East High School is VERY WELL RUN! If a student has interest in any type of club and it's not offered, administrators will ADD IT! You can join Sports here (without having to have a personal trainer)! School offers after school tutoring with bus service for FREE with TEACHERS, not students! Student culture is AWESOME---several student groups openly discourage bullying, NO DRUG PROBLEMS, diversity with Respect for Others! Honors Class Sizes are reasonable to learn and NOT overcrowded! Teachers are mostly from Oswego or Naperville and enthusiastic about teaching and update their websites daily and communicate without attitude! Same books as other districts too! BEST HIGH SCHOOL IN AREA!!! Great school! Great facility. Everything seems clean and the kids are very happy with their classes and activities offered here. This school is pretty good and in recent times they improved a lot in all factors. Totally school out look is changing. And school is located in nice and calm area. Yes still they have to achieve a lot but i feel like they are track. My son attends OEHS. He is involved in band, marching band, and a top-notch robotics program. His teachers are friendly and I can tell that they care about his success. He has nice friends, and the school seems safe. As a parent, I feel welcome to be involved in his extra-curricular programs, and have met many nice families. Newer School so the facilities are in good condition. However, I found pictures of my daughters friends on her cell phone doing drugs at & away from the school, and the school did nothing. They basically excused the behavior of their student athletes and cited that while they have the right to test their teams under the IHSA guidelines, they elect not to. Pictures can be doctored, etc. etc. BEYOND SADDENING.... we didn t inform the school to get certain individuals in trouble, but to make them aware of what was going on in plain view at their school. While I cannot parent those students, I will surely move before my next child is of age to attend OEHS. As a former District 204 employee, I can assure you that these matters were handled differently as I witnessed firsthand. A true shame to believe that this is what my tax dollars are paying for. Oswego east high school provides lots of opportunities in sports, studies and extra curricular activities. Awesome school environment, great staff, new neighborhood. If students are interested in a new sport or arts the school is going to set it up. Very nice learning environment good for both students and parents. The students and teachers there are very friendly. Almost all of my teachers challenge me and want me to excel in school. I am a senior now and throughout my four years East, I have had more than enough elective options, AP options, and honors options. This school has allowed me to excel both socially and academically. Very Good school .Teachers really care about the students to get the best grades . Best school in the district! I moved here just for this school. And it is worth it 100%. Best school in the State in my opinion.I moved here just for that.And it worked perfect!! With 4 kids going through this school, I was really satisfied. The honors programs are great, but watch out for math. Honors Algebra II was more difficult for my kids than calculus. Cross country was great and full of good kids. The baseball program is not good which has been true for awhile. I've seen many good players quit. If you've watch the movie Moneyball where Billy Bean talks with the scouts, I picture a lot of that going on with players.

column1: My children have and are doing very well at the school. The first is in her junior year of college in a nursing program. The chemistry and anatomy classes she had at Lake Holcombe prepared her for these courses at college. If she had a question at college she e-mailed her high school teacher and got a quick answer. That's above and beyond what's required of him. If I have questions about anything I contact the staff and they help. That's the advantage this small school with a caring staff. Favoritism is the only thing this school knows. My children had no help from the guidance department and were literally kept from pursuing their interests in this school. The classes they needed for their future were always full, they were told their career choice was pointless and there were no jobs in that career path. ALL lies --- I thank God I got my children out of that school before that school and their guidance counselor destroyed them any further. I was a student at this school who earned a place in a college advancement program. There was nothing that I wasn't prepared for and I was able to return to the school to conduct my at home chemisty and physics experiments, and got help from the english teacher on my papers. The guidence counselor has been nothing but helpful and encouraging. I love this school.

No doubt that it will be the first choice to educate kids. Horrible just horrible the staff is rude and the students are mean The major changes at Terrell ISD from the district level have improved the quality of these schools. A few years ago I would not have put my child there but test scores are up and they demand excellence from the students and staff. it was a place to learn. and thats all i can say. very good! Any time they struggle they are always there to help with encouraging words and extra tutoring I’m so happy to be out of this school for the reasons stated above. Horrible, I would give it a phone. column1: My three older children graduated from Colonial Forge High School having attended from 2000 to 2008. We saw the school change dramatically over that course of time and decided to enroll our 4th child at Mountain View HS in the IB program. We couldn't be happier with the school - students, faculty and staff are wonderful and communication between the administration and the parents is exceptional. I find the incidence rates in the school are lower than they were at Colonial Forge, comparatively speaking. And while many in the school district insist the scores are higher at one school over another, I personaly don't see it. The history scores are 1% lower but their reading and writing scores are higher as of 2010. It's a perfect fit for my child - academically, athletically, and socially. Their utter lack of shop classes is a incredible disappointment. At my old school i could take welding and woodshop and all that stuff as a freshman, but here you cannot until youre a junior as it requires you to take a bus to another school. The cirriculum is terrible. I just hate this school. The teachers are fantastic, as are the classes I have to choose from. The cafeteria food is TERRIBLE, and students are not allowed to leave the building to get any other alternative food option. The security guards are very rude, demanding where you are going as if you're some hooligan about to shoot up a school instead of an innocent student walking to the bathroom. Staff can be very difficult when it comes to incidents in the home, such as a death in the family, a surgery or serious disease that has the student out for weeks, or anything else that cannot be helped. Once had the school call my parents to verify I was not forging my doctor's notes to get out of school. Just ridiculous and overly suspicious. I get that in recent times, schools need to be on guard, but stop treating every single student like they're up to something bad. Eh, it was ok, but I'm sure it could have been a lot worse elsewhere MV is a wonderful school that is academically challenging, provides a magnitude of activities and clubs, and has competitive sports! Excellent High School, from both a student and parent perspective. Excellent High School. The administration really cares about the kids. We came up from Florida for our Granddaughters graduaion ceremony last week. We didn't know what to expect. It was wonderful. It was very apparent the principal and staff were enjoying themselves as much as the students and families were. They obviously put a lot of thought and effort into the ceremonies to make them special for each student and their families. We could tell the principal and staff cared greatly for each student. Thank you for a wonderful experience, especially in these troubled times. We and our family appreciate everything you all did for our granddaughter and all of the other families. Excellent School. Strong academics, sports and activities. The principal is fantastic, well liked by parents, teachers AND students. Both of our oldest teens attended Mtn View HS and it was a great experience. Our kids seemed to have less issues with cliques or bullying or any of the other typical HS issues. The principal is fantastic, the teachers care, the counselors take time to meet with kids and parents. We've been overseas and lived in several states (being in the military) and we were VERY happy with MVHS. Our kids were involved in the culinary program, swim team, and Marine Corps JROTC. Compared to other high schools in the area, we are glad our kids went to MVHS instead of North Stafford, Stafford, or even Colonial Forge. In fact, we have one more going into MVHS and we look forward to a good experience again. All 3 of our children graduated from Mountainview. We feel truly blessed to have been in the MHS district! 2 of our children completed the International Baccalaureate (IBS) program and were early admissions to University of Virginia. Both graduated from UVA and are positive that their enrollment in the IB program was a key to their success. All 3 were in the orchestra as well as other clubs and school activities and loved their experience at Mountainview!!

column3: FHS is a great high school overall. Most of the teachers are great, and will go above and beyond to help students. The school has good facilities, including a large auditorium, and a nice gymnasium that was renovated several years ago. FHS has a terrific athletic department (this past year, many teams made it to state tournaments, including football and boys' basketball). The music department is excellent. I docked one star because FHS doesn't have as many clubs/after-school activities as some similar sized schools I know of. However, FHS is still a great school, and I'd definitely recommend it if you're considering a move to the Fairmont area. Just last year I moved away from this school after a history of sickness like pneumonia and other chronic ailments that kept me from coming to school. I am now a senior in a new school and I have found that the policies in FHS are not effective or over enforced. A good example of this is when I was having my medical problems I had signed doctors notes for every single day I was gone. However this proved to be a problem because I had to go into a credit appeal at the end of the year even though I had high grades. I almost lost all of my credits because I refused to sign a contract with the school saying I would miss no more days because of failing health. If you are bed ridden or have a family emergency they will do the same to you. If you go over their "reasonable" 8 absences per year, you will have to go into a credit appeal as well. Also there is no follow up on bullying. The worst is that them they will get detention that they can serve on their own time. Take it from an old student that has gone to a different school. This school is nothing more than a trap that does not prepare you for jobs. Everyone is white homophobic racist and transphobic I graduated recently and had a great overall experience. Rules and expectations were strict but fair. The classes were challenging but not overwhelming. Above all the teachers were kind and welcoming, if you scratched their back, they would scratch yours. Sure some students were mean, but that is not unique to this school, and there were of course teachers I will not miss, but all of that is easily forgivable because of the rest of the staff who consistently went above and beyond expectations. Teachers not only challenged me to do my best, but communicated that I was important, and that they were glad that I was in their classroom. The teachers would want you to make them laugh, but when they said jump, you said "how high?" Many people here are old fashioned, and do not put up with disrespect. Getting on a teacher's good side was easy, follow their expectations. If you were consistently late to class and the teacher called you out on it, that is not their fault, show up to class on time! It is all about prioritizing. Classes were never too big and the student to teacher ratio was higher than I would have liked, but not terrible by any means. Overall a fantastic school within a good community. The teachers and classes will not only prepare you for college, but will also teach you important life skills like respect, prioritizing, critical thinking, empathy, and more.

column1: I can't be more happy whith! 2 years here and better day after day! Nice teacher, nice everythink, my 2 kids are learning very fast and happy. They love it. great school, great people. the teachers there are one of the best. even the middle is a good school. I would recommend taking my kid here

column3: I LOVE this school. its amazing all of the students are friendly. You can go to any teacher no matter what and they will help u with anything in their powers. The sports in this school are amazing and the coaches are all great! This is a great school for well-rounded students! Aside from having talented and supportive teachers and staff it offers way more curriculum variety and after school activities that aren't available at other schools.The Art and music departments have won many awards are the best in the area! They treat the students like babies. They don't care if someone is being bullied and frankly they don't care what kids so unless it bothers them. Like you can't express yourself or anything. You are judged by everyone there. It is more like a prison environment. Students are in perpetual lock down without free movement on and off campus or during lunch. The policy appears to be based upon a false ideology of chronic danger. An armed guard at the main entrance should be sufficient in a rural area with a low violent crime rate. Drug sniffing dogs and an atmosphere of distrust permeates this school. The administration should read some educational literature on the effect of fear and distrust on learning. I personally have had a wonderful time at Wallkill. I got involved in sports and clubs and went to as many games, dances, etc. as I could. column3: I am very concerned about the cell phone policy at our school district. The current policy mandates the following: 1st offense is confiscating the phone for the remainder of the week. 2nd offense phone is confiscated for remainder of semester. 3rd offense phone is confiscated for remainder of school year. The city wastes so much money on frivolous things such as: new street signs, new downtown, new traffic lights, etc. Try and get your children into the McDowell Tech. early college program (if you are unable to move). Awful!! the best school I can say the teachers are caring the whole staff is excellent they really care about there students Just when I thought it couldn't get any worse after the "Athletic Banquet," where the Seniors did not even get a Varsity Letter after participating in a sport for four years... they left my daughter's Senior picture out of the yearbook!! This is my third review I have inputted regarding my opinion on TCHS. I am assuming someone does not want other parents to be aware of what has happened to me. My child loves the school but as a parent I couldn't be more disappointed. My child was taught by 3 substitutes for the year. How can a child learn off ditties, how can a child develop good study habits or note taking skills when an actual certified teacher is not present. Very afraid my child will not be prepared for college. I have two children attending this school and this past school year was the worst ever! In both of my kids classes there were teachers who were absent for most of the year due to their parents illness for one and the other one, I have no idea. Then you have some teachers who do not use Skyward! They do not have any accountability and use another site or none at all. When I called to complain about it, all of a sudden they would populate my child's grade and then when new semester would begin this same teacher would not use Skyward or would tell me that she had not given many grades that 9 wks. I agree with previous post that the school has gone down since Ms. Roberts left 2 yrs ago. Oh and try getting ahold of a counselor. Good luck! I hope this year will be much better. I do want to say that there are some teachers that are awesome but unfortunately they are not the norm. I do have to give kudos for Ms. P_ _ _ _ who is a guidance counselor and is exceptional!! She gets 5 stars from me!! She is quick and resolves issues quickly! Love her! BTW, my kids are both in Honor classes. I recently graduated from Treasure Coast High School as part of the class of 2013. Let us begin with the very lack of professionalism coming from the staff, they show little respect to students or parents alike, claim credit for others (teachers/students) work, and whenever a problem arises blame it on a teacher or student. Guidance Counselors are never reachable and dont do their job. During my senior year they notified roughly 60 students they did not have a specfic credit they needed to graduate 3 weeks before graduation. Mind you this being after they supposedly did credit checks at the first week of senior year. Finding a good teacher is a rarity in this school, In total i believe i had five my whole way through highschool. They fail to use the skyward system to keep up with students grades, and generally just have a lack of care for their job. This school simply represents the laziness in our education system nowadays. How can we expect students to care when the majority of staff and teachers do not. To anyone reading this review, I strongly recommend you send your child else where. This is coming from a student who played sports, was in all honor classes, and has their AA. This school is great, loved it here. The teachers are great, and so is the atmosphere. Treasure Coast High School offers great programs for students. Our son attends this school and has had mostly positive experiences. His teachers are wonderful and his guidance counselor is very attentive when needed. My son just graduated from TCHS and his entire academic team was awesome. The IEP worked very hard with him and we are very appreciative. Treasure Coast High School is a 5 out of 5 in disorganization, lack of respect and accountability, and lack of leadership. It is a failure to the school district. Two of my daughters recently joined Treasure Coast High School, and their experience has been problematic, or in better words, traumatic. Both of them are Honors students. The administration in the office defends their lack of responsibility by using excuses and blaming others. They are not respectful towards parents OR students, and have lack communication. They do not welcome parents whatsoever, and the counselors are difficult to get in contact with. While the teachers are great, the students are disrespectful, loud, obnoxious, and out of control. There have been numerous fights this year, and it is only October. The ones who are in charge of keeping the students in line only drive around in a golf cart, blowing their whistles at the kids like they are dogs, and intimidating them. And to add on to this joke, the sports facilities are unavailable (there is no football field for games), and the administration does not support extracurricular activities. This is not a school that I would recommend to any parent. I recently thought of putting my child in somerset academy but there review were going down rapidly and i wasn't very happy with what was happening there . I enrolled my daughter in treasure coast and is doing great ! There and I'm very happy with the experience she has had there . —Worst Administration, Athletic dept, teaching staff and even School Resource Officers ever experienced. Ms. Susan Seal is the only hope for this... Excellent. The ESE department really cares about the students. They go the extra mile to help students after school and whenever they need it! The administration and everyone here wants students to be successful! I’m a freshman and love this school

column3: Its a great school, where teachers focused on providing high quality education. Parents are involved in educational program and community cares of high quality education. Particularly in March where the teachers decide to exponentially amplify the difficulty of the courses. Overall I would not recommend moving to this school unless you want your child to be broken.
