They will constantly bully you into medicating your kid and if you don’t they will push them over to the Renaissance School. I have gone to warren for most of my life and so far everything is good and everyone is nice and I feel like I have been having the better path coming up career wise. All of my children attended Warren Township schools and they all did well and attended universities afterwards. They were also heavily involved in sports. All coaches (but one) were excellent leaders.They had good teachers (some were great) and student accountability.

column1: My daughter is a freshman this year at Herron. I am absolutely over joyed with the school. This has been such a wonderful experience. The teachers, staff, guidance counselors, deans etc work very hard and are hands on. They know their students, they are involved, and have high expectations. I always joke and say my child goes to a private school for free because that is how it feels. I would highly recommend Herron. I absolutely love Herron! I've met some of the coolest people there. Not only are the students welcoming with open arms, the teachers are too. The teachers can always make us laugh and it seems like there is nothing they don't know. I am overjoyed that I decided to come to Herron and I wouldn't change my decision for anything. Unlike most kids, I can truly say that I can't wait to go to school and hate being sick and not being able to show up. What a great thing to be able to say about your school. Herron is a great school! They really do prepare you for college. The class sizes are extremely smaller than a normal high school. They have an extremely wide variety of electives such as Technical Theater, Theater, Band, Drawing, etc. They also run on an A/B day schedule which is where you take classes 3 days a week rather than 5! Another benefit is that they start at 9 am Monday-Thursday. On Friday school starts at 10! The students are welcoming here and they have an amazing diversity level. This is a charter school which was recently renewed by the mayor for excellence. Looking for an Indianapolis charter high school. Look no further. Come to Herron, you will NOT regret it! This school seems to have a lot of turn over in teachers and students. There are better options for schooling in the Indianapolis area. Too many students and too strict. Students are not treated with respect as they are "talked down to" by the higher ups. My brother was In the first graduating class at Herron. I followed his foot steps because my mother loved that Herron knows everybody. I'm currently entering my senior year and when most people hate their high school, I wouldn't attend anywhere else. Every teacher will work with you, as long as you show that you care about the class, you'll at least pass. This school is awesome. They truly care about students education. Herron is a wonderful school with caring teachers and staff. As a parent, I find Herron a hidden gem. My daughter is looking forward to attending High School. Large enough to have sports but small enough not to get lost. HHS is an academically challenging school that offers a wide range of programs and activities for all students. My daughter is involved in 3 seasons of sports which we feel enhances her high school experience and broadens her colleges options. Herron High School offers and incredible education with enthusiastic and dedicated teachers. Our students receive only the best! Herron High School is one of a kind. I will never regret trusting my education with the incredible staff and faculty. Herron offers a wide range of challenging courses, focusing on Advanced Placement. Teachers and administrators are constantly focused on college prep, finding the best ways to prepare students for the university. Herron High School is the best. My daughter has been going here for 3 years, after being bullied at her local public school. She has a better attitude and more friends. I am so proud of this school. My school is the most unique, inviting, and inspiring school I have ever been to. This school is so much more than an educational facility. It is stuffed full of amazing kids, nurturing teachers, and love. It is a home and a shelter that nourishes and protects. As our school continues to grow, the school's needs continue to increase, causing teachers and students to be creative with resources. While this is a great skill for students and teachers to learn, it can be stressful when trying to work off of donations and scraps. I love my students and my school and wouldn't have it any other way though. They are home. Great school to be working at as a teacher. I have found Herron to be a place of excellence. The administration works hard to continue build on its short but strong past. I wouldn't want to work anywhere else. Herron High School is a place where students from various backgrounds can come tuition-free to receive a high quality education. Herron's passionate teachers instill values of world-class citizenry by having high expectations both academically and behaviorally. Amazing, passionate teachers who love students and sharing knowledge with them. Students learn not only from the classroom, but also from participating actively in the downtown community in which the school is located. It's a win win situation for the school, students, and the neighborhood. Herron is an amazing school. The students at this school are held to high standards of achievement and behavior. This is truly a school for scholars. If you are not aware, Herron received an A for this past year from the Department of Education. I would recommend Herron to any parent seeking to send their students to an environment of learning, welcomed diversity, and encouragement for excellence. I have two children who go to Herron. After choosing a private school through 8th grade, I was nervous that the quality of education and attention would not compare. I was wrong. I am constantly blown away that my children get the education provided at Herron for free. The teachers are passionate and many have been there from the start or near the beginning. I trust my kids will be more than prepared to excel in college and in life because of the experience they are gaining at Herron. My school is five-star school: with committed faculty, visionary administration, and supportive board members, our school is poised to do great things this year and in the future. This is a great school where you can be different and a lot of support from teachers My daughter would have been "lost" in the local high school with its huge population. In Herron, the teachers and staff know her and care about her, and she has more friends than she ever! In her second year at Herron, her self-confidence is soaring! She willingly works hard, and the extra help available for all of her courses in the form of "office hours" is wonderful. The downtown environment is actually a huge plus as well! I encourage other parents who want a safe, smaller, and caring learning situation for their children to consider Herron. We are very pleased and would not choose to go anywhere else! My younger sister went here and it really is such an awesome school. She would've struggled at other schools but the diverse and unique atmosphere of this school really helped. She graduated, is in the military and in college. I have been going here for a year and cannot wait to leave. While the school is very academically challenging and is college preparatory, they have some classes with a "one size fits all" idea. Some classes such as Math and Latin have options, but English and Social Studies don't unless you're taking AP. The students can be welcoming and friendly, but there are cliques here which they claim to not have. The teachers say they help, but if you need it its always "Come to office hours". They need to know that students have jobs, buses to catch and personal things to do and sometimes being at school at 8 am or staying until 5 is not an option! This school is also very strict. Students must be following every rule at every minute or they will be given a demerit. 3 demerits and you've got a 2 hour detention session on Friday afternoon. As stated, STUDENTS HAVE LIVES. Also next year(2014-2015) will require students to wear $40 pants with a small Herron Logo on it. Not everyone have $40 or more to throw around. Not many students even get wrote up for uniforms! Unless you have a socialite or overly academic kid, don't choose Herron! They may seem accepting but that's just a good facade. Herron is a wonderful school with top notch faculty and administration, a safe environment and a multitude of opportunities for children to grow into world class citizens within a culture of acceptance and openness. You get in trouble for everything here and it's ridiculous. I hate it here! Ugh I've been at Herron since my freshman year and I'm now currently a junior (soon-to-be senior). There are some aspects of Herron that I love and some aspects that I hate. Firstly, the majority of the teachers are all great at what they do and are very knowledgable in their subject. All of the teachers I have had strive to make us better students, as well as better people. I think that students who complain about the rules haven't experienced the "real world". I currently have a job so I understand the importance of a uniform and being on time. Herron is trying to prepare us to be above-average citizens. I do, however, think that the way the administration goes about giving demerits to students is disrespectful. The administrators strut around the school pointing out any minor flaws and then make a point to embarrass the student for it. Also when it comes to teasing or bullying, I've noticed that it's been towards religious people most of the time. I understand that everyone has different opinions, but on multiple occasions, I've seen religious people be criticized and teased for what they believe. Herron prides itself on its equality, but from what I've seen, it hasn't been so. My daughter would have been thrown away , if not for Herron high school. After being pushed into algebra as an eighth grader at her public MS/HS, she was failing in algebra before she even got to high school. Herron had her tested and we had our first case conference, all within two weeks. She went on to take four years of math, take many AP and college courses, and graduate with honors . She is beginning her Junior year at Ball State University, studying film. Herron taught her SO much more than math... They literally saved her life. Cannot thank them enough! Herron High School has offered my son and my host son from Mexico a great learning environment upheld by character development and values. The faculty are second to none. They knew my son's strengths and areas for growth. Herron has been wonderful! This is my son's first year (9th grade) at Herron and he already feels he is part of a great community of learners. The teachers at Herron really do care about each student. They challenge students appropriately, but guide them while encouraging independence. My son has become involved in many before and after school clubs and activities. They offer so many that it was difficult for him to choose. The times offered before, during, and after school to receive extra help and complete classwork really lightens students' loads at home. I'm sending all my children to Herron! I love this school, however Latin should be an elective as students should have the option to choose what language they would like to learn. Personally I would like to learn Spanish, which is not even offered, as it is needed for nearly every job you can get. Additionally the electives are very limited to the arts; theatre, painting, music. Having more electives would be great, other than that this school is awesome. The best four years of my life. Herron is a very open and accepting place. The courses are rigorous and challenging if you choose the AP/Honors route and not only was I challenged academically but I was pushed to be the best me and graduated from Herron with a 4.4 GPA, Cum Laude, National Honors Society member, Core 40 Honors and with a love to learn. Not great as they have nothing to offer except for strong academics Excellent. We shopped private and public schools, and it made little sense for us to choose a tuition school with the value at Herron. Our kid can play sports, join different clubs, and just be more involved than at many other places. In the end, you as a parent have to be comfortable with your child getting a great college prep education without shiney football fields. You have to be ok as a parent with academic rigor and no gymnasium or large theatre. You have be good with 5 core subjects (including Latin) for all eight (8) semesters and no marching band. You have to be, as a parent and student, good with attending perhaps the most diverse high school in the state without (for now) having a lineage of your family having attended there as well. Highest score possible!!! Saved my kids’ lives from the suburban, cookie-cutter-kid public schools that thought they couldn’t accomplish anything and gave them tremendous confidence and opportunity. I’m forever grateful for HERRON High School!!! Our experience with Herron has been nothing short of exceptional! The diversity and inclusive atmosphere has allowed my son to thrive. The academics are top notch. My son has access to all the AP courses and has consistently scored “4” on his AP exams! I would give Herron a high rating because they do a good job at educating the students while also building a strong bond with them as well as with the parents! Great faculty and staff!!! My daughter attended this school and it was a life-changing experience. So grateful to have found it.

column3: I am still attending maine east and it is just awesome soo many after school activities such as clubs just an amazing school. The teachers are super helpful and friendly. I love Maine East. The student body is friendly and isn't cliquey, you could talk to the person sitting next to you in class without fearing of being judged. Some teachers are horrible but there's many tutoring opportunities and make up work. It's a safe environment I use to help teachers out with home work and do other things for them I'm a former student and also had siblings that attended M.E. All I can say is that this is a great school. AP programs are great and top notch. Theater program is great. The school even has a radio station. Facilities are great. The only thing not so great is the football and basketball team. The teachers are great and care about their students. You won't see the typical peer pressure that you see in other schools. M.E. has been malign by outsiders who know nothing about the school, claiming that there is a gang problem and drug problem. In reality, there isn't a gang problem, it's suburban gang wannabes that can be found in many suburban schools. The rumors of a drug problem is just that, rumors. The test scores are not high because there's a percentage of the student population that do not come from wealthy or middle class families that have parents that are not actively involve with their child's education but you can't blame M.E. for that. A lot of these students also work almost a full time job and that takes away from their studies. If you want a great education M.E. is the place. Don't listen to the stereotypes and rumors. Bottom line is, M.E. is a great school. Maine East is a school with a many divers cultures. All of the students are different and most of the time they form groups with people who are culturally similar. I went to this school for two years and I can't say I had lots of fun there. I'm Eastern European and it was hard for me to find the right group where I could fit in since there are not so many other Eastern Europeans there. I feel that if you are from Asia it is easier to find close friends who understand you fully then if you are like me European. Not a lot of people understood me and I didn't always feel comfortable there. This is an awesome school, with a lot of 2nd generation kids. Probably the best kept secret out there (and hopefully will stay that way). Top academic programs and AP opportunities without the clickiness and social pressures that other schools have. It is diverse and that makes it unique or some like to say it "real world." The kids are extremely involved and they go on to some great colleges! The greatness of this school cannot be described in words! Maine East isn't just a "school", it is Home. It's where most students found and still find warmth and solace. Everything-- including students and staff--is phenomenal! The provided opportunities for students are amazing. Bottom line, It's difficult to find a school like Maine East! This school is pretty great, much better than all other schools in the area. go demons! I attended this school from 2009-2013. There were a lot of gangs and a lot of free time. Genuinley felt like attending was a waste of time. The first few houses nearby were actually gang houses. I can confidentaly say I did not learn anything while attending here. The school is gorgeous though.

column1: I am a graduate of Harford Tech, now in college for engineering. I enjoyed my time at Tech, mostly because it was not challenging and allowed for goofing-off. Upon arriving at a college, I realized that, despite what school officials and teachers had insisted, Tech had, in no way, prepared me for college. I graduated 6th in my class with a 4.4 GPA and was not ready for college. Tech offers none of the higher level classes found at other schools and the overall course offering is quite limited. The methods of teaching at Tech do not reflect college, either. Most teachers promote high calculator, note, and book dependence in classwork, homework and on tests. While this does, as they say, simulates the "real world", it does not simulate college, much less prepare students for college, resulting in skewed rankings and GPA's. A "smart" Tech student is not a "smart" student at other schools. This results in Tech graduates being able to get into a wide variety of colleges, only to realize they are not prepared for college. If I had to choose again, I would never had gone to Harford Tech, instead choosing to attend a real school and actually have a chance in college. This school has been wonderful for my child. Coming from a private school the adjustment was great. The teachers are very good and the students have respect. I am very grateful for this school As a graduate from Harford Tech, I would have to say that I feel as though my experience greatly prepared me for college and the real world. I was in the Nursing Assistant Program where I was exposed to a variety of clinical experiences and nursing education. When I entered into my Bachelors of Science Nursing program at college I felt as though I had a huge advantage over my classmates especially during clinical. I had already overcome the anxiety of that first clinical experience, patient care was a breeze and hospitals already felt like a second home. I excelled in the classroom as well having already been taught the basics of nursing and how to analyze those dreaded nursing test questions during my 4 years at Tech. Working my way through college the certifications I received through Harford Tech also allowed me to gain a position in an Assisted Living setting making far more money than the average college student. While they may not have state champion sports teams or a dozen AP classes, I wouldn't trade my high school experience for the world! Harford Tech is a highly academic school. we have hands on activities to help the students experience the lesson being taught. Harford Tech has a positive and culturally diversed environment. Great School.. I graduated 10 years ago and I still go back and visit my old teachers. Feels like family. I graduated 10 years ago and a lot of my teachers made an impact on my career decisions as an adult Communication is great and all teachers seem to be on point and love the athletic programs!

column3: very good school near my area, is my first year and i like it so far. make the best out of it :) This school itself is not too bad, no, decent even. However in the past three and a half years(Junior) in Granby High School- I have experienced that the learning environment is rather uncivilized and incomparable to a public zoo. If you have attended Granby for 3.5 years, as you claim, you should be a senior by now, not a junior, being as it takes only 3 years and 9months to graduate high school from start to finish. On a side note, incomparable means NOT comparable to said object, as the prefix in- means "opposite of" the word it precedes. The correct word was comparable, as your point was that Granby could be accurately compared to a public zoo (which, by the way, couldn't have been a less truthful statement, especially if you take the time to compare Granby's disciplinary records with other schools in the area). I think you should spend a little more time involving yourself in your studies and less time worrying about who fought who today, and I am sure you would find your experience at Granby, as with anything else in life, to be much more positive and successful. I have not been impressed with this school since my kids have started. My son used profanity on the base while singing a song and was reprimanded which is fine. His punishment was 5 days OSS which was ridiculous! No warning and another child did the same thing that week and received much lighter punishment. It's a shame the school administration isn't better. High School is a great time in a teens life and I think Granby leaves a lot to be desired. I was disappointed with the school. My child was only in two class due to registration and in both classes either the students were very disrespectful and cussing at the teacher or a fight broke out. While just waiting to be seen there were students being loud and wondering the halls when they were to be in class. This is the worst of the worst! Students are treated as if they are in court here and are forced to make plea bargains with suspensions. The principal shows little to no care for academics, safety, respect, or compassion. I don't understand how the doors are still open! Violence is a huge problem. When my child and groups of others are getting secondhand pepper spray from a fight being separated, doesn’t seem like an effective or safe tool. I have two children, both of whom are in the International Baccalaureate (IB) program at Granby. Their teachers are excellent and the staff and administrators have always been accessible and responsive. The principal, Mr. Smigiel, is highly capable and enthusiastic and has improved communication with parents significantly this year. My kids could not wait to get back to school after Covid restrictions were lifted. Their athletic coaches (in particular field hockey, crew and volleyball) are wonderful. To initially clarify, this review is both highly personalized and subjective; and it won't cover the full scope a typical student at Granby would face. In order to ascertain my credibility, I shall establish my ethos (credibility). I'm a current student at Granby High school - sophomore, to be specific - and in the IB program, I will become a Junior rather shortly, as it is June, I take multiple IB/AP classes, and also attend the Governor's School for the arts in tandem with Granby.Firstly; the positives. Granby has an amazing teaching staff...Somewhat. From my 2 years of experience, on average, you will get 2 absolutely amazing teachers, a bunch of decent teachers, and 1 to 2 teachers that would make you genuinely consider self-mutilation as better than taking their class. Let's focus on the good teachers, however. Practically all of the teachers are open to criticism and emails, having quite amicable personalities. Those amazing teachers that you get (Props out to Dr. Ford, absolute legend) will make your classes more than just bearable, it will be an actual sensation that, for once, you actually desire to attend. Unfortunately, this is probably where all the positives end...Now...the myriad of negatives. It would take too much time to explain them all, so I'm just going to list them. -Certain abhorrent teachers-Condescending staff (New principal Thomas Smigiel is pretty decent, though)-10s of people skipping class in the bathrooms-Some hallways smell like weed...constantly. -Fights daily (emphasize on the daily) -You are practically treated like herd animals or any other equivalent.-Our "Track" is actually non-existent (we have good tennis courts and baseball field, however)-Infrastructure standard/grade is barely legal; dismal. (this is hyperbole, but the point stands)-School food...might as well eat straight from the dumpster, provides the same nutritional benefits and has a better taste.-Real lack of emotional support, we may have more counselors than any other school, but does it matter if the school environment itself is more mentally taxing than if you were to take 2 AP exams at once with half the allotted time?In short; the academic facilities at Granby - even within the IB program, and especially the regular courses - are mediocre, borderline purgatory, at the very most. In reality, it's probably not as bad as I make it out to seem, I tend to exaggerate things - hence my introduction - But I agree with all that I said.

column1: As a student going through the schools now, I am experiencing the many changes the School is undergoing. The school is going in the right direction. There are many new ways that the school is not just encouraging the students to do well, but actually making them want to do well. With the accreditation process that is occurring, teachers are not just teaching what their told, but are making an effort to help the kids. The kids not only learn the topics, but are helped to grow as a student and a person. I am very happy with how the school is improving, and I hope they keep going on the right track. Both the town and school district are run poorly by political insiders. When the 3 school district lost 25% of their enrollment that's expected to reach 30% they doubled the classrooms at the H.S. with a $20 million triple addition plus added the less than 1/2 full Granville Village school. With this fiscal mismanagement and a School Committee that chose size over quality they have many financial problems and no money for top notch programs or equipment. They are on their 4th Vice Principle in 3 years at the H.S. and the middle school one just left after 13 years. Well liked teachers disappear without a trace, taxes have gone through the roof and there are so few students expected at the enlarged H.S. they may need inline skates to get around. Take my advice. Run, run as fast as you can away from Southwick and it's school district. Excellent. Barring an unrealistic expectation of perfection, I have no complaints with my experiences with Southwick. Terrible school system that aims for mediocrity and embraces the woke culture of encouraging students to wonder about their gender identities while they should be focusing on actual studies. I am very concerned about the future of all its students and disapprove of the Superintendent’s agendas and their teachers’ lack of motivation. Curriculum is the bare minimum of what their age should be able to handle.

column3: I had 3 graduate from here. I wanted to be out of this county by now, but my youngest is now a Hoke High Freshman. The 3 that have graduated told me to get out before the youngest starts High School. If the older siblings are telling us to get out, what does that tell you? Principal Hagen made some very important changes for the better, but was also one to placate parents and tell them what they wanted to hear and do something entirely different. Hoping for the best with the new Principal we have this year. Hoke County NEEDS another High School due to the population now but Hoke High needs more clubs and organization for the students which in turn will create more pride in their school and themselves. Some of the teachers are just horrible, but others are not only teachers, but friends to the kids, which is what they need. Too many of the teachers here have God complex and treat the pupils like children of a lesser God. Whoever leads the yearbook staff has no business being a teacher. One look at it and you'd think it was done by a 6th grader. Over the top PDA is a serious problem but the dangerous aspect has improved over the past few years. We still want out of this county. My son just graduated from this school and I could not have been happier. yes, there are problems on this school just like on every other school as well. There are good teachers and then there are not so good ones. My concern is more the age of this building, possible mold etc setting in but not confirmed. And Hoke county's concern of making sure they keep building more subdivisions but not new schools concerns me. Other than that it is not too bad. I loooooooooove this school. Hoke county is up and coming and I recommend that anyone choose to buy or rent in this area. This school has improved so much over time! Kudos to the principal, teachers, and staff! I am so happy with living here and this wonderful community! What a blessing that I live here! My kid has been in many different schools around the world because of my service to this Country. I have never seen a school this disorganized. They wait until the middle of the school year to inform you of the total school fees. Trust me, the $45 posted on their Home page is no where near the actual fee total you will spend for a Senior attending this school. In any other school, these fees would be collected at the beginning of the school year, with all medical, parental permission slips, etc... filled out prior to attending. This school waits and continually nickel and dimes a family to death! Also, the sample school work sent home by one of the teachers has poor grammar and numerous spelling errors, such as the word "was" spelled "wuz". If the teachers do not know proper grammar and spelling, then how can they grade their students? Granted, since I have not dealt personally with every teacher in this school, then maybe some are okay. The ones I have dealt with, I am far from pleased with. Now I know why our Country is falling behind worldwide in education. My advice, if you have a choice of home school or Hoke High School, would be to home school. Hoke County need to concern a new high school instead of building elementary schools and another middle school. . Hoke County school system need to make sure that sanitation regulations are followed and inspections are done more often. My daughter and her friends complainted so much about roaches abd , rat droppings, in the classrooms, bathrooms and cafeterias that i called the Sanitation Department to go out to investiage. ? . You have to have relatives working at the school or friends to get picked for most sports. Some of the coaches don't look at the talent of some students. I wish I could afford to put my child in private school. I do not think that our students show have to study black history for a month. I think if the school systems are going to require recognizing and studying one race all races should be required. Yes, there is a Native American month but how much history does the students study on Native Americans and when are there a white history month. Be fair for all races. This school needs alot of improvement. Where does the school taxes pay for? We came to Hoke County when the military brought us here. I cannot believe the conditions of Hoke County High School. Everyday I wish my child did not attend this school. It seems like no one takes the time to care from the teachers up to the administrators. This school is WAY over populated and incidents involving students is over the top. I know my child cannot get a great education there and it's frustrating to know you can't do anything about it. Most times you can't even get the school to listen to you at all let alone care! I would never, NEVER recommend this high school to any military families moving to this area. I feel sorry for the families who are from Hoke county and have no other school options for any of there children here! I feel so strong about this that I hope my child does not have to spend her senior year there, I hope we have orders. I got married and my fiance had a house in Hoke County. I was really frustrated that I had to move my kids to Hoke HS. Yes!!! there is problems in this school and some other schools also have problems, trust me my kids attended one of the "best" high schools in the other county. I dont really love the school but so far the experience is not as bad as I thought it was going to be. Both my kids are in sport now and they both are taking Honors, AP and Community college classes. I am really happy with their counselor. Sadly some student dont care for their future and they dont put the effort and ruin the class for the ones that care but that is every where. I encourage my kids everyday to look forward and move on because once they get to college they are going to encouter other problems too. I teach them that life is not perfect and no school or college is perfect but you can do the best you can with what you have. They make their own path not the school or other student. They are resposible for their future I just can give them the tools, support and the advice the rest is on them. I am a Student at HCHS, I will be a Sophomore when we go Back to school. But, Yes this school is overly populated. I agree with that . They do need to build another high school for Hoke County. It's been up forever. Parents always talking about their kids can't learn because of other people at the school, if you have taught your child to ignore people and know when to be serious about learning , there would be no Problem . And for the parent that called the Sanitation Dept., why you would you do that. Now they could close our school down and then where will we get out education at? I care about my education!! So that was wrong, your child doesn't have to eat in the cafeteria. Tell them to wait until they get home. I am currently a sophomore at Hoke County High School. Although the school is very over-populated, I feel that anyone can still get a proper education. Many people look at the negative aspects of our school, but in order to understand what really goes on, you need to experience high school in the conditions that we learn in on a day-to-day basis. Aside from that, there are many excellent extra-curricular activities for everyone to participate in. One of the most well-known activities on campus is the marching band (which I am apart of). I am a sophomore and were about to move. All I have to say is HALLELUJAH! Do not bring your child here! For starters, the guidance counselors are terrible. High schoolers HAVE drama and they have the nerve to say they don't help kids with drama, so they're pretty much useless. Do you care about your child? Well when there is drama at this school, it causes fights. When people get into fights here, they get sent to jail. So who's supposed to help the children with the drama if the guidance counselors say they dont deal with it. Then the assistant principals, I don't see how they think they are over the actual principal, who is actually one of the only decent administrators at the school. For sports, okay so some of them care about grades, but then there are some who don't seem to look at the rule saying you can't have anyone under a 2.5 GPA on the team because I have seen some people on teams with under 2.0's play. Then the saddest of all, the academics. I have never seen such lazy teachers in my whole life, instead of teaching, they'll show you a video, hand you a worksheet and class is over so you can just use your electronics for the next 45 minutes. Also, I don't see why its necessary to have only 4 classes each semester for 90 minutes, if you talk to a professional, the teenage mind cannot pay attention to one thing for 90 straight minutes. I have a whole lot of reasons this school is not good for other reasons too. Let's say we're at lunch, the fast food restaurants are across the street so for those with cars, they can just easily leave off campus. The assistant principals are in charge of not letting them leave but they obviously dont care. Lets talk about dress code, i understand the rules but it should apply to EVERYONE! If somebody with a kind of short skirt gets sent to ISS, a girl with an even shorter skirt should be sent as well. Its called being fair. Now, here's where things get gross, I have never EVER been in a school that's infested with roaches and mice. There are enough janitors, why is the school so dirty. I've seen wasp nests. When I go to practice, people get stung all the time due to all the wasps. I just really do not recommend this school for anyone who can breath air. You can try to go to Jack Britt High or even home school or online school, just don't come here. You will regret it. I am absolutely appalled at this school. My family and I moved here a year and a half ago from up north. My child had wonderful grades. It took over 4 weeks for the school to review her records and place her in appropriate classes. So, she gets her schedule and not one administrative person offers to show her where her classes are. Never mind the fact that most of the classes she had already taken previously. The teachers were rude and had no problems swearing and putting on movies instead of teaching. Now we are in her second year at this school. Teachers have blatantly refused to help her out with any of the work she doesn't understand. She has complained that many of them say to the students if you don't want to listen then I won't teach you. When she speaks up about this, she gets sent to the office! I have had many conversations with the "drop out prevention specialist" who has demeaned my child numerous times and threatened to have her sent to an alternative school. Then when I demanded a meeting with her and administration I was met with just on of her teachers instead. This school is an absolute joke. The are disorganized and refuse to make any changes with their staff. Oh, and forget parent teacher night. This is a joke as well. I have gone to every single one offered over the last year and a half. I have met only 3 of her teachers in two years. The others were not even there! I am now considering home schooling my daughter for her last year. These should be the best years of my daughters life! ABSOLUTELY AWFUL!! This high school will never change. I don't care how many times they change the staff members. The school is in a bad area as well. I would NOT recommend this school to anyone who actually wants a decent education and can walk outside of class without seeing a fight. Terrible school for violence. This review will not change anything but hopefully it will save someone from attending or letting their children attend. Honestly terrible, no one at this school cares about the well being of the students at all. CRT is being taught by the staff, I have reported them and investigation will be starting soon. Pay attention to what your kids are being taught! Please don't send your child here. We moved to this district with high hopes after having bad experiences with another NC high school. Hopes were dashed quickly. NC schools, in general, seem to not care about IEPs or 504 plans. We were told in our meeting with the counselor and only one teacher that since our child was making at least a B in every class that they did not need accommodations! My child has chronic health conditions that include widespread chronic pain and brain fog and orthostatic intolerance, etc. They sometimes need to use a cane due to joint weakness! They also have mental health conditions brought on due to their chronic health conditions. This school was a nightmare for my teenager. My teen tried to drop a class that was causing them to feel depressed and they had been having suicidal thoughts because of the stress of the entire experience (between having classes that were spread out across the entire campus that they had almost no time to rush to while using a cane and nearly passing out due to tachycardia, not being able to eat lunch because there are so many students and the line is so long that the lunch break is over before half of them get to get their food every day!, and dealing with one teacher who may as well have been a Confederate soldier who yelled at everyone and another who was putting extreme pressure on them to be his pet artist due to my kid's talent). The last straw was when we got called to pick my teen up because they were a "suicide" risk due to looking up ways to AVOID suicide on their Chromebook at school one day. They were told not to come back unless they had a note from a random mental health place that assesses for suicide risk. Even though my child already had a therapist and doctors. This place is why they dropped out of school. They are now doing amazing at the end of freshman year at WCU, after getting a high school equivalency diploma. Oh and this high school never even gave me my kid's records when asked.

column1: This educational facility is very incompetent. Only a hand of teachers are worth their weight in gold. The bullying of students is unbelievable and nothing happens for discipline. 90% of the teachers do not do their job(especially after Walker) well maybe it is time that some get fired, if their majority of their students are failing then they get fired. Pulled kids from the school. Lots of improvements have been made. Good staff and good administration. They offer a lot of advance courses and even allowed my kid to take multiple classes at MATC and they paid the bill! Big changes over the past few years with a new principal and some new staff. Would recommend to anyone looking for a smaller school with lots of options. I was very badly bullied at this school and I had told the counselor several times about it. They said it would change, but no it didn't. Some of the teachers seem incompetent and they favor certain kids. The lunch was overpriced and disgusting too. The whole school was filthy. Most of the teachers were very very nice, but there were others who were not nice at all. I would not recommend this school to anyone. The whole experience was torture in the beginning and it gets worse towards the end. If you go there now, move asap to a different school. Multiple principals within the 5 years. They can't keep good people and bullying is everywhere. Little discipline and lots of drugs. Social studies:I had the basketball coach as my teacher for multiple subjects. I was a straight A student, and although I liked him, this quizzes and tests weren’t reflective of the material learned on the PowerPoints. No one ever knew what to expect with his tests/quizzes since most of topics weren’t covered in the notes. He also has pop quizzes. The only reason I aced his class is because I would spend 2.5 hours everyday memorizing enter chapters. This left me incredibly burnt out. I spoke with the high school counselor alongside my parent and she said he can do what he wants and that pop quizzes were okay since they’re done in college. And, after attending 3 separate colleges, I can disprove that point since I’ve never had a pop quiz/surprise quiz in college.Science:I got As in all of them. They were easy and were steered in a good direction.Foreign Language:Only Spanish is offered. After receiving an A in Spanish 1 the high school counselor recommended me to take a remediated version of it instead of moving on to Spanish 2. I dropped from Spanish 2 soon after the start of the semester because it was just too easy for me. Also, colleges don’t recognize the remediated version of Spanish 1. The decision of the counselor makes no sense to me to this day and I wish I would’ve pushed hard against her decision. Rather, when I entered college, I had to pay for two semester of foreign language because of the high school counselor’s decision to not enroll me in Spanish 2.English:I really liked my English courses with the exception of the one offered in combination with MATC. In that course the high school teacher seemed to know nothing. In college I got an A in English 1 and 2, so the subject comes to me easily. But in Pardeeville course I failed my first test due to the teacher’s lack of direction. When I would ask her questions she would always admit she didn’t know the answer. And, when I asked why I got certain questions wrong on the test she admitted to not knowing why.Counselor:She’s nice… but yikes.

column3: Parents have a great deal of responsibility to help our kids stay in school. Same goes for the school staff they have to make sure our kids feel safe while in school, the way I feel is that if my child is getting decent grades. And does not seem to hate going to school everything is ok, I still ask him about his teachers and how he feels about his classes to make sure he is happy and does all his school work. In high school you are told you are completely responsible for any results you get at the end of the semester, but I think it would still be nice to hear from the teachers if your child is not doing well as he/she has done in the past this would prevent biggers problems in the future. Marina Carbajal. Principal Hides in her office. Chaos in the hallways. Great teacher leave and are replaced by new teachers that don't have a clue. The principal is rude, and only cares about images. I have recently graduated from Coconino High School. Throughout the years at this wonderful school, I have nothing but glorious memories to look back on. Freshman year to Senior year I felt that I was fully encouraged to exceed my own expectations. The staff was always there to give you that extra "push" when you needed one! I only have great things to say about Stacie Zanzucchi. Being apart of student council we met with our principal every week and discussed areas of the school we, as a student body, would like to see change in. She was always open minded to hearing new ideas about the ways we go about things at school. All in all, I am absolutely thankful for all faculty and staff members at Coconino High School for helping me succeed in life. I would highly recommend anyone to go to this school! lots of fun and unique programs to choose from. gets a bad reputation for no reason. Great place to go I wouldn't have become enthused in the high school experience. The teachers are nice and helpful while the school is large enough but not to large. Coconino is a great school, very under appreciated I feel that this school is tailored towards learning, but only if you seek if out. Those who don't try will get little out of it, but if you try, you will get the full benefits. The level of engagement between the teachers and students is excellent. No student feels left out. We're not the best but we're not the worst. Yea we have our issues but what school doesn't. Being a student here at CHS coming from another school district, we are ten times better. We have an amazing faculty and the best janitors. The teachers actually care about the students and the janitors are always making sure the school looks great. I have mad better bonds with the teachers and even the other staff, that I haven't made with my family. Coco is a pretty good school when you compare it to others. Also that person with the hateful comment can come catch these hands. This school is the best school in the entire FUSD. The principal is very nice and also very humble. She does her job to connect to the students while also providing the work hard mentality. I'm grateful for everything that this school has to offer.- Satisfied Civilian Coconino High School provides many resources for your child/student to grow and succeed. They have stellar counselors, teachers, and administration to support a well put together learning environment. If your child/student is looking into Coconino High School they will have all the support and resources they will need, provided, they look for them! I'd encourage visiting and taking a looking at our Carrier and Technical Education programs such as Digital Media, Welding, Autos etc. As a CHS alumni, I couldn't be more proud of where I went to school. I always felt welcome and all of my teachers were there for me and made sure to help me out when I was struggling. The principal is super involved and does her best to get involved with the student body and the community. It's an amazing environment for students and it's definitely underrated throughout the community. American school systems suck. This school is no exception to that but there are a few really great teachers that make it worth it by helping you in anyway they can. I wish I could take a few of them with me to college. Coconino High School is a great learning environment for all students. The school pride is high. Teachers care about the success of their students and the principal is grounded on Coconinos three core values: respect, integrity, and responsibility. This school has amazing teachers and staff. The school is fun. Coconino High School has an outstanding community! The teachers and staff establish a welcoming environment in and out of the classroom. They're always there to help their students, and help them grow. If I had to pick a school in Flagstaff, I wouldnt think of any other place than Coco. 50 years panther strong! FACE YOUR FEARS PANTHERS, RAAAWWWRRR!!! The students at coconino have a lot of pride and integrity as well! For the most part, the teaching staff care about their students' success. Coconino High School is an excellent school. As a community member whose family and friends have gone through CHS in the past and some curren, this school is always on the lookout for opportunities to grow and improve student experiences. Coconino High School is just an overall great school with highly envolved administrators who care about the students. The teachers care about their student's learning and success. I am very passionate about this school and everything that it stands for; Respect, Responsibility, and Integrity. I've been less than impressed by the counseling office at Coco. They have been completely unresponsive to inquiries I've made on different occasions. I usually need to go to the school to get trivial questions answered. I have another student attending a different school in Flag and the difference between the responsiveness of the administrations is dramatic. At CHS there are many low GPA students the bathrooms have vulgar writing in the stalls the food is decent for what students get. There are cases in which students carry drugs and E-cigarettes

column1: There is lots of bullying and a principal that doesn't do anything about it, very unfriendly office staff, and their priority is Football. There are some good teachers, but overall a place I don't want my daughter to be. This school is great. Academic, athletic, leadership and art programs are ALL strongly supported by the community and staff. With such a small school, the teachers and principal are able to make connections with students and help them out more often. The opportunities available here, if taken, can give you a head start on a challenging future. Football is a top priority at this school, and bullying is a Major problem. Academics are not pushed, teachers don't teach, homework is just expected to be turned in without explanation or learning concepts. If you're not related to someone at the school or a previous student, then communication is extremely difficult, outsiders are not welcome by faculty or students and support staff. Horrible experiences here, education is very basic. The administration and staff are very kind and approachable. My son loves that he can take forestry and wood shop in addition to the standard academics. It’s a great school and great community. Also, I’d note that when we hosted our exchange student from Spain for a school year where he attended Scio High and loved every minute of it. Sergio had spent three summer exchanges with us and when his parents asked if he could come live with us for a school year we jumped at the opportunity. He was warmly supported not only in his new school but also onto the basket ball team having only really played soccer back in Madrid. My experiences has been that this is great school and a great community of kids that are welcoming to kids from all different backgrounds and abilities, local or not.-Nicole Zedwick

column3: This is a great school. I am not sure why the ratings are showing so low. We love it. This school district doesn’t put pride in communication with parents and choose not to follow state guidelines. They set students up for failure. Avoid at all costs.

column1: I am fully in support of my children attending our neighborhood school and not cherry picking the system. We are feel so fortunate that South is our neighborhood school. The diversity, and the lack of cliques at this school is rare indeed. The culture is one of encouragement and cooperation. And the rigor of the classes cannot be denied - South High grads will be well prepared to attend any college or pursue any other endeavor that they wish. As a parent I was a little stunned at the level of demand from the students academically - but am seeing the results and realizing just how much high school students are capable of achieving. I would give it all 5 stars but I see the school getting even better under Dr. Waters leadership.. so leaving room for that process! I highly recommend South as a parent.. (oh and my student loves it as well!) Our family has recently experienced how caring the teachers and staff at South are. My daughter has had some health issues which inluded being hospitalized 2 times and missing at least 11 days of school. Each teacher made sure to check in with her when she was able to attend school and they are helping her catch up. Everyone was concerned for her wellbeing. I would like to also add that her big sister (South Alum) is a Freshman at CSU, is currently taking advanced courses & is earning 4 points in all her classes I highly recommend South High School to parents searching for a school that is culturally diverse to embrace the chance to get to know the students, teacher and staff. I have enjoyed the atmosphere every time I go to South I learn a few new words of a different language spoken. As a parent of two teenagers at South the school has broadened there horizons. They are taking honors, AP classes and succeeding my expectations. I love South. It is literally the best school I've ever attended. I transferred from Wheat Ridge my junior year, and instantly fell in love with the charm this school has to offer. I have had a few issues with some teachers, but that's expected. I've also had some incredible teachers. South is also very diverse. At least 5 kids in each of my classes are from a different country. What a way to learn about about the world! I'm graduating this spring but can't wait to come back and visit. Would definitely reccomend this school! I love this school. I came from a worse school, and this is an improvement. I love the variety of students from different places all over the world. The principal and teachers actually seem involved and seem to care about the students. The students seem interested in learning and are accepting of everyone. I recommend this for your child; and if they feel they don't fit in or afraid of being bullied, they don't have to worry about it here. My school is a great academic environment,..... it's friendly, warm and inviting to students, staff and parents! There's something special happening at South. When I walk these halls I see diversity being celebrated in the athletics, classrooms and friendships that thrive here. There is an atmosphere of respect and an honest desire to learn from our students. I feel incredibly lucky to be a part of it and cannot wait until my own 2 children walk through these doors as Rebels. South High School is full of wonderful students with different backgrounds. Every child has an opportunity to grow and learn from different perspectives. My school is one of the most extraordinary high schools on the planet. With students from all over the world, it is impossible to not expand your perspective and understanding of the world at large when you go to South. I am impressed by my colleagues and their commitments to our kids. Next year my beloved niece will start school at South--having come from a very privileged and fancy education myself, I would NEVER let my niece attend a school that I did not believe offered an EXCELLENT education. I am so proud to work here. My school is a place I look forward to going to everyday. The students, community, and staff contribute to an atmosphere of mutual respect, diversity, and continuous learning that is palpable throughout the school. I teach French and Spanish at Denver South High School. I love working at South because it is by far the best high school in Denver Public Schools. The student body is very diverse, and our principal, Dr. Kristin Waters is doing an outstanding job. It takes great leadership to run a school as diverse as South. Too bad, my youngest graduated high school last year, or else he would be attending South! I have found South HS to be very open to assisting my daughter and willing to work with me to understand her needs and learning challenges. I really appreciate the teachers being willing to contact me and inform me about what they are working on, what tasks my daughter needs to do, and how I can support her at home. This is very important to me as her parent! This is my second year at South and I have truly been pleased with my children's academic experience here. The teachers are engaged and push the students to aim high. The diversity and culture at South asked the students to interact and learn about other nationalities that you won't find in other schools. Denver South High school is a hidden gem in the DPS system! The diversity at South is a treasure that is unparalleled and creates a rich learning environment, an opportunity for the students to not only study other cultures in textbooks, but from their fellow students. The teachers at South embrace their unique opportunity, and are led by Dr. Kristin Waters, who is in no uncertain terms, a rock star, charismatic leader, and Principal who is willing to think outside the box and not afraid to implement new ideas. Excellent cultural environment. Teachers, staff & Principal are awesome. It would be fun to have a music band for all our great sports games. Denver South High School My son is a freshman at Denver South High School. We absolutely love the diversity of Denver South. Everyone is from somewhere else so there are no clicks or majority/minority. Students seem to focus more on what can bring them together than what separates them. I have been so impressed by the quality of students that I have interacted with and my son is truly happy to go to school each day! As a parent I also love the communication between the teachers and home as well as the accessibility of the school administration. I know we made a great choice in choosing Denver South! A bonus is that they have great athletics programs and many of the athletes are honors or AP students. Student athletes are held to a higher standard than at other schools we looked at and this was important to me as a parent. At South my son is treated as a young man, a student then an athlete (in that order). Our daughter is a freshman at Denver South this year. She grew up in the neighborhood and had other high schools she could have chosen to attend but wanted to go to South and has never regretted it. She takes regular, in AP and honors classes, utilizes tutoring and has a good relationship with her supportive teachers. She is involved in sports and in a leadership building elective. She, and we, enjoy the diverse student body which helps her understand different points of view and she has found friends and kindred spirits. We are so glad she is a part of Denver South and so is she! There is a culture of inclusiveness and positivity permeating the halls of Denver South. My daughter is just completing her freshman year and South has far surpassed our expectations. She is already earning college credit and could potentially earn more credit if she did well on her AP exams. We love the international students and have realized that the roughly 25-25-25-25 attendance breakdown by race/ethnicity creates a very compelling dynamic. You won't experience any of this in any other Colorado high school. South is a special place that truly must be experienced to really understand how unique it is among all other Colorado high schools. Visionary leaders and thoughtful, engaging teachers. Incredible. The principals only care about test scores and sports. All students are not of their concern. Do not go here! I must admit to having a great deal of anxiety as I performed my due diligence on High Schools for my children to attend. I even investigated private school options and expanded my search to encompass most of the Denver Metro area. I have relatives in the southern suburbs and heard a great deal from them as to why I would be crazy to enroll my kids in a DPS High School, so I even contemplated moving in order to ensure my kids benefited from the best education I could provide them. Between such strongly worded counsel and the less than glowing appraisals of South at places like this site, I was on the verge of making a huge leap. Then I remembered what brought me to the Washington Park neighborhood in the first place. Traditional neighborhoods and tree lined streets, active parks and big porches that draw economically diverse people out into the open where community can take form. Its streets are narrow and sidewalks are old but there is a sort of genius visible to those willing to see beyond its surface. So, I made the effort to look again at our neighborhood school and see if there was something deeper than raw test scores and economic struggles of many students and their families. It was there all along, I just hadn't taken note as I maintained my focus on the caution lights being flashed in my face. If you spend time speaking with the people who work there and the students they serve, it rises like smoke from a concealed flame. There is an opportunity here for the kind of education that goes well beyond IB programs, AP classes, and athletic programs. Give it some time and I think you'll see it, too. The truth is that my children have been high performers their whole lives, the beneficiaries of attentive parents with economic resources to spare. There are many good schools with caring faculty and competent administration, and my children were likely to thrive in any safe environment with opportunities to learn. This is bigger than that, though. South High School is an opportunity for them to experience life in all its diversity and attendant challenges and beauties, to understand struggles they have never known, and to see beyond societal veneers and broad labels which plague so many in the world today. I can't guarantee that South High School is for you or your children, but I challenge you to find greater opportunity than what is found here. I shadowed at this school and it was amazing very diverse the students are very nice and helpful hopefully i get in this school. I would definitely recommend your kid going there We came from a terrible middle school experience and have found that under the leadership of Dr. Waters, all of the teachers have been wonderful/caring mentors to our daughter. The sense of community is very strong and we love the international aspect of the school. Much more like a real world experience! Great new principal.....Ms. Hanson truly cares about kids My daughter has had the most wonderful experience at South High School. The ratings are not reflective of the amazing learning environment at this school. My daughter chose to leave a highly selective private school to attend South, our neighborhood school. The opportunity to get to know kids from all over the world and from all socioeconomic backgrounds has been such an enriching experience. South is a very inclusive school with teachers and administrators that truly care. Their AP classes are just as challenging as the school my daughter transferred from. My daughter was just accepted to a very selective (13%) top tier liberal arts college and South made all the difference in making this happen. South has been a great experience. It's smaller than other schools and the teachers and administrators know and care about the kids. Students also get great opportunities to participate in school life via sports and clubs. And our daughter has also gotten to know students from around the world, which has been an invaluable and unique experience. The academics have been challenging, and AP classes interesting, relevant and engaging. I strong recommend South to students and parents who are looking for a place where they're supported, engaged, and can have an interesting experience in a culturally diverse environment. Read the Newcomers by Helen Thorpe to get some of the flavor of the school As one who always felt commitment to our neighborhood schools, I am very sad to give this poor review and to share that we will be pulling our child out of this school after one year. Overall, the curriculum is extremely content poor, and many of the teachers are more interested in far-left political indoctrination. You wouldn't believe the amount of time wasted on kids being taught what to think, not how to think. These kids will graduate with lots of opinions, but very little knowledge. The language arts class is particularly bad. The teacher has jettisoned the reading of great literature, or the reading of much of anything at all, for that matter, in order to prosthelytize his activist agenda. I can assure you, I am no conservative. Recently, my student took a standardized test and pretty much bombed it, especially the language section. It is no wonder. I graduated from Denver South in May 2021 and truly I can't say enough good thing's about this place.Socially, this school is 10/10, maybe it has changed this year after all the covid craziness, but everyone just gets along, this schools staff can really become some of the best people I have known in my 19 years on this planet. The teachers care about you, but you do have to put in work in order to get those good grades you're looking for, teachers are always okay if you need an extension, just don't wait till the last second to ask. Overall, I loved Denver South, I will truly never forget the experiences or the people I met. Amazing atmosphere for a kid to go to High School. I learned so much there and got into brown university some of the best years of my life and I made so many friends there I highly recommend south to everyone

column3: The school and principal involvement is not so great. Not enough help is being provided to the students in the school with the subjects they have difficulties with. I am very disappointed with how things are handled and the personal contact with the students and teachers. The teenage girls at this school are horrible. Unless you are popular and are with the "in" crowd, your going to get treated like crap! There are several teenage girls that want to quit and move to another school due to this problem.

Although it is better than years before because gang members are keeping the violence at the fists instead of using firearms that they 100% do hav. Most students at the school are not gang bangers and are just trying to get through high school. But the 20% that are make it a dangerous environment to be in. The teachers and staff are excellent. Police officers are walking through the halls and outside the school building to prevent any violence, but the gang bangers do not care whatsoever. They literally fight in school every single day.

column1: I hate this school. I moved here a few years ago, if you are not a resident of the town of Hinckley or Big Rock your whole life you pretty mcuh get the cold shoulder. Teachers favor certain last names and they do a horrbile job. There are a few teachers that are AWESOME ! But it sucks because they work here, they can do so much better somewhere else. They either let students get away with everything or over punish . The school board does not listen to the students. This is a farming community so to me I feel like most are sexist. I would not reccomend this school for anyone, but if I did it would be for the few teachers that you actually feel like they care. I have been attending Hinckley-Big Rock High School my entire High School experience and I have to say it is wonderful. Yes the school is small but what can one expect from only 200 teenagers. The teachers are wonderful and really try to teach people not only the class they are the administrator or but also good morals and proper conduct. The English, History, Math, Science, and Spanish departments are top-notch. I, personally, am very excited to go to school next year (senior year) because the board has included two new classes: Advanced Psychology, and Speech. The only problem I see with this school is the students. A lot of them do not participate and are, dare I say, bad kids. I highly recommend Hinckley-Big Rock High School to anyone's choice in a school to have their children attend. The review below was written by a teacher - in fact, the teacher doing the two new courses listed. I flagged the review below to be reviewed by Great Schools. This School is good in some areas. the Spainish, english, history, and biology areas are very good and they teach me a lot. unlike those classes, the algebra area is downright AWFUL. the teacher doesnt care if the students fail. the teacher also has very few work days for students to actively practice content and get feedback/sufficent help.some staff members are rude, like the principle and tech staff. the food also is gross and your portions are TINY, the same ammount given to me in 1st grade. i am very displeased with this school. School district struggles to find quality educators. Administration is more concerned with high test scores versus actual quality education. Special-education department is adequate at best. Beyond great! We came from another district specifically because this district is so wonderful, we have not been disappointed, have been here 4 years with kids in elementary, middle & high schools.
