column3: Monta vista kids/families spent too much time talking about how bad other schools are.....every Monta Vista student (does not matter if they are A or a D student)have this one thing in common......send your child to a private school where your child will learn to respect people if you are not happy with your school but NOT Monta vista.... I will try to be as objective as possible in this review for potential. I'm a freshman student and I really enjoy my time at Monta Vista. It's a challenging school, there's no doubt about that, and if your child is not getting As or better in most of their subjects, Monta Vista is not the school for them. Of course, it's not really all about intelligence though. To really excel here, your child needs to be dedicated or hard-working. If you aren't prepared to put in the effort, there's absolutely no point sending your child here. The teachers are very dedicated, nearly every single one has an afterschool club or lunchtime club, dedicated to helping students understand everything; which is definitely necessary, I spend nearly 3-4 hours on homework every day, excluding the extra-curricular clubs I do. I will say this, allegations of racism and bullying is really not true. Everybody here is so open and so friendly with everyone, simply because they haven't got the time to waste on making someones life difficult. They're much more likely to be studying!' However, with around 600 students in every year, the campus is loud and noisy, and it can be difficult to get the personal touch. Monta Vista High is one of the top schools in the nation, ranked as among the top on usnews website. I wasn't so sure what to expect when i entered as a freshman, but after four years, it's amazing to see how much ive grown as an individual. ppl here are very respectful and open and willing to work with you, and the teachers are also willing to help you if you ask them for it. academically, it can get a little stressful, but when i asked former monta vista alums about it, they said that mv really helped prepare them for college. everyone here has something special about them, so it's hard to stand out but it also makes for an interesting campus. it is possible to take hard classes, have extracurriculars, and enjoy high school life - football games, dances, prom - i know a lot of ppl who do all of those things. all the departments are well-organized, so you'll be kept busy all four years, with ppl to meet wherever you look. there are a lot of clubs on campus - something i didn't realize until junior year, so you can always find friends who have the same interests as you. bullying/drugs/sex/violence/racism is NOT a problem at this school at all - never seen any of that here. I have son who is a junior a MVHS. He is doing well, but the amount of stress and lack of social life (due to kids doing only homework) concerns me. I will not be sending my younger children to school there as the kill and drill/memorization focus and the focus on "being stupid if you re white" or "Stupid if you don't have a 4.5 and 2300s on your SATs" is just old and does not foster the type of education I wish my children to receive. While some of the teachers are amazing, an equal number are unprepared, don't teach or just plan mediocre. If you want your child to get great test scores and be able to spit back facts, then MVHS is a good fit. If your child is creative, likes to think outside of the box or does not work well just memorizing facts, then look elsewhere. In addition, while my son has great friends, there is a culture of underlying racism and exclusions by some of the kids. BTW, I don't think this stems from the kids, but from their parents. Class choice is very limited given the size of the school and there is no individual attention. If your student cannot advocate for themselves, no one will do it for them. There are just too many kids here for that. Outstanding high school that outperforms virtually all open registration schools in California year in and year out. Beware of the chemistry honors department. They do not teach anything, but put unreasonable questions that were not in the textbook on the tests. In addition, your GPA at Monta Vista will depend solely on which teachers you have. Some teachers are unreasonably easy, and give automatic A's, while some make sure they give none at all. beware of the post below - he states that he takes ap classes and gets straight a's. you are not allowed to take ap classes as a freshmen at MV-no matter how brilliant you are. as a matter of fact the only ap class you can take before junior yr is comp sci which you can take as a soph. not sure which Monta Vista high this student is talking about but it is not the one in cupertino. you may want to remove the post as it is bogus. also there are a far amount of drugs at the school. bad teachers and grading. I never have fun and lost 25 freaking pounds in a week because of the stress. Luckily i'm going to dublin high in feb! There seems to be quite a bit of misinformation on this site regarding Monta Vista High School. The high marks it gets are well deserved, however if one is to look at how these are garnered, he/she would sincerely question the merits of the administrative and teaching staff. To get things out of the way, let me first state that I'm a former student, and though I excelled here (2 Engineering Degrees), I've realized that the image this institution has is really a facade to hide the incompetence that festers inside. Now, things may have certainly changed in the decade or so since I have left, and likely for the better, but my experience here wasn't particularly positive and thus this writing serves as a bit of a warning for future parents.In all honesty, I had TWO terrific teachers that ingrained an indelible mark on my childhood whilst there. This is 2 out of (7 periods x 4 years) 28. And judging from the fact these two teachers are STILL THERE, it goes to show that their efforts are beloved. Their names are April Scott and Scott Deruiter for those who are interested.Unfortunately however, the vast majority of the faculty during my time there served as little more than "Gate Keepers". They lacked motivational skill and relied purely upon parental involvement and peer to peer competition to get results. The end result was that that child who really "NEEDED" extra help was left behind and those who excelled were not necessarily great on their own accord, but were "coached up" to be brilliant. For better or worse, I was one of the latter ones. Similar to many of my colleagues, we had PhD parents who coached us daily on Math and Science. And if it was a subject our parents were weak in, private tutors would be hired to fill the void. Summers were spent in Boarding and Cram Schools to "Preview" material for our upcoming year thus making the actual year "easier". Therefore I ask, who deserves the credit here? I'd also like to bring up that many of the teachers were so insistent upon "their ways", that they left little room for creativity. Quite honestly, I'll be the first one to say that if I used "their methods", I would never finish a College Engineering exam let alone the SAT or GRE. In other words, they knew little else than to teach "from the book". -GREAT SCHOOL, but for the wrong reasons... I know my children will be ready for the real world because MV is heartless. Sincere students, pathetic teachers who hide behind the performance of students. Instead of teaching, they have an ego competition. It is a public school, incorrectly overrated. Minus the stellar students, it is filled by mostly lame teachers. My time spent at MV were the worst years of my life. I usually felt looked down upon and felt like I was worth less of a person just when I didn’t have straight As. My self esteem was lower than ever at this school and I never felt happy there. I couldn’t even go out on weekends because of the heavy workload and there were days when I pulled an all nighter to prepare for a test of get an essay done. I actually transferred to another high school because I got autonomic ataxia from all the stress. Do not send your child here if you want them to have a happy school life. The schools academics was overrated, the quality was not mediocre in some subjects but in math especially, the teachers lacked in assistance. Your skin color determines your treatment at the school. The treatment from students, faculty, teachers and parents was extremely awful, as a African American student last year I was singled out, scrutinized and bullied because of my race. As a African American student any time I has a complaint about students and teachers, it was never handled well and the responses were only "it's just culture shock", "They are just kids" "We always hold a bully prevention auditorium meeting" and "Do you have evidence". The teacher that deliberately used the N-word several time is still a teacher and was never suspended, instead they moved me from the school. The students agreed with the teachers racist stereotypes of black people and used the teachers words against me. I felt singled out because not a single student rallied behind me or supported me after the incident, instead they laughed at me and at his racist stereotypes. I would never send or recommend a student to go here. Going to multiple high schools, this high school by far gave me the worst experience and taught me nothing Monta Vista challenges its students in various ways. Besides college preparation and maintaining a resource-filled campus, which are effective in planning for the future, the school also prepares students to learn on their own. There are a few teachers that dedicate the extra time towards aiding their students. However, for the most part, students require external tutoring and training sources to supplement their education. This is not because of poor education material, but because like a college preparatory, Monta Vista's learning environment conveys a need for self-learning. This may prove useful as it was demonstrated by some students, but others have struggled due to a lack of necessary additional support. Overall, most school clubs and organizations are essential to join for a more well-rounded experience outside of academics, and one should keep in mind researching a few external resources when attending this school. Utterly horrible. The teachers have progressively gotten worse throughout the years, especially in the mathematics department. The harder the math course, the worse the teachers are. Additionally, the principal has an utter disregard towards his students' needs. The principal also fails to uphold his promises from the beginning of the year, most notably his vow to eliminate the disparity in course difficulty between different teachers. Examples for the first is the recent California fire. When the AQI was nearly 200, the principal refused to cater towards student needs by 1) closing the school entirely and 2) not opening enough classrooms during brunch or lunch for safe air. As for the latter, the most notable example would be in World Core Literature and AP Calculus BC. Certain teachers like Kaufman for World Core Literature or Conlin for AP Calculus BC will drastically make the course much much harder than it needs to be. Let me start off by saying that I am an extremely self-motivated student that managed to pull off a 4.0 at this school. Even though I have achieved so-called "academic success", my experiences at this school were anything but successful. As mentioned in other reviews, the teachers are a mixed bag, with a larger than necessary share of them being subpar. Some have little regard for student wellbeing (as seen with the monstrous amounts of hw my APUSH, Calc BC, & Pre-calc teachers assigned each night), while others are simply unqualified for the subject they are teaching (Moore for AP Chem, Mueller for Java). NOT to say they're bad people, but there definitely needs to be some quality control, since teachers absolutely shape your school experience. The high regard with which Monta Vista is held is solely due to the caliber of its students. With the school lying at the heart of Silicon Valley, the vast majority of MV students are children of hardworking, high-achieving immigrants who want their offspring to achieve the same. This pressure drives each individual to succeed, taking copious amounts of enrichment and test-prep courses. This would be fine, if the school fostered this demographic into an ambitious and mutually-uplifting community. However, many teachers' strong disdain for doling out majority 'A's' renders the courses, and ultimately the student body, into a toxic and competitive setting. Yes, I may have learned how to work hard and adapt to the difficulties, but it was at the expense of my sleep (mind you, I hate procrastinating), psychological wellbeing, social skill development, and extracurricular exploration. Monta Vista administration, if you are reading this, students can succeed without having to complete 6+ hours of HW every day and being "motivated" by the stress of being a B student amid an increasingly competitive college admissions process. There have been some efforts to improve upon the issues mentioned above, as noted with the bell-schedule change and wellness surveys, but there needs to be more hard-pushing actions to enact the changes Monta Vista so desperately needs. I simply can not recommend this school to anyone. If you're not Chinese or Indian, prepare to feel scrutinized at this school. Awful. You'd have to pay me to even look in the direction of this school once I graduate. The teachers are the kind of people to go, "We want you to be a teenager and have a life outside of school :)" and then go ahead and assign you mountains of assignments and homework. What a joke. My school has become a place that makes my life painful. Every time I show up, I am practically assaulted with homework assignments, presentations,, and exams that continue to increase the stress that is eating away at me. Students feel very pressured by their families and peers to get straight A's and teachers don't understand this pressure; they just tell students that it's okay to get Bs and Cs so that the students can't blame their stress on their teachers. Many students, including me, deal with mental problems like depression and anxiety disorder, which we don't have time to deal with because we are constantly working. In fact, I have 2 tests, 2 presentations, one in-class paragraph, and a test-prep period tomorrow. Welcome to Monta Vista. I would never want to go to this school and I wish I had not. Yes I would wish 4 years at Monta Vista on my worst enemy and their entire family. This school would be a good fit if you are extremely serious about school or don't want a fun high school experience. It's more of a training camp for students to become competitive, but also snobby for no good reason. Majority of the students at this school look down on certain colleges, especially students going to community college or even other high schools, even though they end up transferring to the exact same colleges in the end anyway. I'm a junior this year, but from my past two years and asking other people just in general, it's not an ideal high school if you're looking for the high school experience, but if you want to challenge yourself past your limits and are prepared to put school in front of friendships, go ahead. I personally don't care about being the top of my class or going to a UC (which is rare here), so I'm often made fun of because I'm not super thrilled about college or get all a's. People will jump at the opportunity to make fun of others who aren't as "smart" as them in their mind. It's quite sad what the mv environment has done to it's students, as so many of the kids who are working hard are depressed and anxious (I'm not kidding, so many of the kids go to therapy or need to go but their parents wont allow it) and it makes me so sad because all of the kids here deserve a break from the constant pressure that's being put on them, but may sadly never get a break until they're past college. Teachers here don't teach. They follow FLIP model, where they ask students to watch video posted by youtubers online (not teaching videos by MV teachers) and come to class and then the students solve problems in class while teachers are on their phones. may be 7% of teachers are here because they love teaching. yep, students teach themselves. Teachers just grade and get paid.Staff just doesn't care. today was a great display of their neglect. They made students take 75 minute long AMC test sitting on hardwood floor. this school can't even provide tables and chairs to students taking test. Teacher in charge of it just doesn't care. what a shame what a shame As an alum, I will say that Monta Vista prepared me academically for college. However, if you love your kids at all, and want them to become happy, well-adjusted adults, then don't send them here.This advice extends especially to BIPOC, female, queer, and/or neurodivergent students. You will be discriminated against. In cases of sexual harassment/assault, the school did absolutely nothing. In an incident where students were found to be making a "kill list" of Black students' names, the school did little. Any "efforts" in response are lip service - students often deride them, and teachers grumble about having to teach anti-discrimination lessons. Besides, they mask the fact that the administration does NOTHING in terms of real action responding to these issues. AP CS Principles, a class that is not "hardcore" coding, was dismissed as a class for "girls and gay guys," which contributed to its perennially low enrollment. Slurs, such as the N-word and R-word, were used frequently by students, and when reprimanded for using the R-word, students called "stupid" things/people "autistic." Students told stories about boys growing their hair long and applying (and being admitted) to college while pretending to be transgender as heroes. Assuming that because Monta Vista's population is not majority white (it's 80% Asian) that it will be friendly to students of color is the most inaccurate assumption you can make - and I say this being Asian myself. I have witnessed racism here against every race. Monta Vista (and Cupertino in general) is, by far, the most discriminatory environment I've ever gone to school in.Additionally, Monta Vista is a hypercompetitive environment, which has adverse effects on mental health. I've spoken to other alumni, and everyone seems to agree that our experiences there have sparked emotional trauma. Students were mocked for grades below an A-, taking fewer APs, going to anything less than an "elite" university, and not being "on the grind" all the time. I was once mocked for getting 8 hours of sleep (rather than < 4). Once again, the school only paid lip service to the idea of mental health, making lessons and holding workshops, but they were mocked, as you would expect at a school where visiting your counselor makes you "weak." To this day, I still struggle with overcoming this mentality.Overall, you can't call Monta Vista a good school. The SAT scores aren't the whole story. Don't send your kids here - they'll thank you for it.

column1: As a former student of this school (3 yrs), I read the previous reviews with a bit of amusement. Yes, I was harrassed publically and setup to fail in a Math class; but it often backfired on the teacher, (i.e. when he had to change his answer key.) I still 4.0'd his class. Yes, there are a few drug use problems on both the high and low end of the student spectrum; but again isn't that expected for upper middle class neighborhoods? However, my overall assessment is this is one of the best schools I'd EVER attended. If you want an education the staff here will help you achieve it, period! If you just want to coast, it's not the schools fault if you (or your child) doesn't learn anything. I am VERY Happy I graduated from this school. We like this school, but were very disappointed in the band program. They are touted to have this great band program, and it's just not true. The marching band is a joke...they don't even march! Academics are fine, and I think the environment is good. But the music department is a huge disappointment :( If you want a school where the teachers waste time in class, shove their liberal ideas into your childs head and couldn't care less about their academic success, then this is the school for you. The building is nice and the admin staff are very nice but that doesn't make up for what counts. This High School is in an excellent area and the Middle Schools that feed into it are excellent. Although the school facilities are excellent, the focus of the school is more about the advantages of being popular and having wealth than it is about self-worth and achievement. You can get on the sports teams if your parents could afford to give you private instruction. You can park close to the school if your parents can afford to pay the ludicrous parking fees. This focus on status and popularity encourages a student culture of class separation and exclusion. As far as the curriculum goes, there are some very dedicated teachers and others that give less than their best. If you don't know this beforehand, or don't know how to get your child into the right teacher, your child's education will suffer. Don't bother reporting things to the counselor's either, unless your parents....oh well, I think you get the picture. This is a great school if you want to teach your child the importance of money and status. If you wan to teach your child the importance of self reliance and self worth, find a different school. The experienced staff leads to high graduation rates among classes year after year. The student life is a bit more about popularity and status than anything else, but you'll find that at any high school in the nation. As a wealthier neighborhood, you are going to find easy access to drugs and alcohol for the students that attend. It's really on the parents to monitor that behavior and set limits on allowances for their kids, nothing the school can do about that. For those interested in sports, the teams are great due to private club teams and lessons provided by families in the area. Hundreds academic and athletic scholarships are awarded to students every year.Foreign language programs at the school are awesome, and kids can earn college credit while enrolled at WHS. Academics for the school are very good, hands down. A lot of AP and challenging course work with supportive teachers. Their ranking tells it all.However for a balanced student, athletics are a joke for girls, especially for Girls Basketball. Coach picks girls through the feeder program making decisions years in advance based on the how the parents suck up to him. Little opportunity for any girl get a different opportunity.. It's really bad when you see the dynamics. The high school needs a shake up. Coach needs to leave as does the athletic director. They don't care about the environment, never want feedback on coaches. Teachers have feedback all the time.If you provide feedback it's the typical response, "it's a competitive environment". But it's really not. I've play high school and college athletics. It's not really competitive, couple be so much better and definitely not a positive one. I'm all for competitive when positive; no one there is going to the WNBA.1. Shouldn't have a JV coach that coaches his own daughter on the team. 2. JV players should all play decent minutes else let the girls know they won't at the start of the year. Set better expectations. 3. Just watch... even in a blow out they don't put in other players. Girls still only get 1 minute even if a win is inevitable. Create a better environment for these girls! Thank god we moved schools and my daughter started played varsity in high school and was league 2nd team.At Woodinville she didn't make the team, nothing to do with skill at all. I agree with the previous comments on this feed. The school is excellent for academics, but as far as everything else it is horrible. Bullying is very common and basically ignored by the administration. The kids at this school are entitled and lack compassion for their fellow students. The girl's basketball coach has ruined so many girl's self-esteems that he should not be coaching and the soccer coach isn't any better. The athletic director should do a better job of making sure that these programs are less political and more about building the esteems of their young, female and male athletes. When you are up by 35 points in a basketball game let the other kids play! When you are up by 5 goals in a soccer game sub your starters, this is just common sense! The athletic politics at Woodinville High School are second to none!If I had to do it all over again I would not send any of my children to this school! Beware. It was the worst experience of my life. Students tore each other apart over grades and teachers were hard on struggling students. The counselors were over worked and didn't have time to talk to the students who needed it. The school focused way too much on academics instead of student wellbeing. Excellent. Friendly staff. Great principle who is very involved with the students! This is an excellent school! my kids love it ! Excellent. Great teachers, great staff, great principal. 9.5 out of 10 although it’s not the best school, the teachers are amazingly unique and students are always eager to move on onto new stuff Excellent experience, period. Top notch teachers in general - certainly the equivalent or better than many top level private prep schools across the country. Lots of AP offerings, the vast majority of which are exceptionally well taught). The French, Math, English (Lang + Lit), Music, Physics, and Chemistry departments stand out. Many excellent extracurricular programs and organizations, especially ASB, Drama and FBLA/Future Business Leaders of America). Adequately prepared students who arrive in 9th grade, who are motivated to succeed and who put in the work, will succeed far above the state average. Solid sports programs and strong facilities across the board. I’m a hard to impress parent whose child is about to graduate and I couldn’t be more pleased. Bottom line, notwithstanding the ghastly Zoom-taught year of COVID, Woodinville HS provides about as good a public school experience as one could wish for. Teachers use subjective standards to assign grades. Low moral among students because grading doesn’t seem fair. This school has been for a while now has been turning a blind eye to male teachers walking into the girls bathroom just to check if students are vaping. There has been multiple accounts of this at Woodinville and under any circumstances should that be okay unless it is a life threatening emergency, I personally have had this happen to me, Woodinville high school caused me to have severe anxiety due to how much people there was in a class, I only went there for a welding class because My main school was SAS. Due to how much stress it gave me I was alway in the bathroom with an upset stomach. Well one morning while I was in the bathroom (with an upset stomach) a couple girls came in to the bathroom while I was still over the toilet, after a bit a male teacher puts half of his body in and pulls everyone out including me, again I am still over the toilet clearly in pain. I tell him over and over that I need to go back because I am not feeling well explained that my teacher already knew where I was and what was happening because it was a bit of a routine in the morning. Im vividly upset about this and he says that I don’t need to have an attitude with him. I personally feel like it was justified for me to be upset that a male teacher decided to take that situation into his own hands instead of getting a female teacher to come in instead.

column3: Teachers are extremely nice and helpful, the staff and the students are encouraged to help another. I love studying here. column1: John Carrol Catholic HS is a wonderful environment for students and parents. I describe this school as a 'big heart with lots of smiles'. The respect and attention shown to students is exceptional. The staff go 'above and beyond' in every way. We are very thankful to be a part of JCCHS. I have attended John Carroll for four years and I can say that it has been everything I have wanted out of my high school experience. John Carroll provides a great teaching staff, twenty three clubs, multiple successful sports teams, and many other great programs. John Carroll is a great family atmosphere and has allowed me to be able to excel in my studies, and prepared me for college. Being that John Carroll is the only Catholic high school on the treasure coast, it gave me a chance to really strengthen my faith and knowledge of God. I believe Attending John Carroll was one of the best decisions I ever made...plus our lunches are so good! Great school I'm a parent of a freshman student I made the right choice enrolling my son is this school not only is good in academic they also know how to treat their students and they care about them my son enjoys going to school This is a wonderful school, Sending our Son to this school was the best choice we made. The Teachers and Staff are amazing. Excellent education, nurturing environment, concern for the individual students and work on educating the whole person through additional opportunities such as service clubs, sports and honor societies. Academically, this is a below average school. My son was in AP Calculus at John Carroll and earned an A in the class. He failed the AP Calc test as did almost everyone in the class and when he took his college's Math Placement test, he scored so low that they placed him in Pre-Calculus as a Freshman in college (which is the class BEFORE the AP calc class he took at John Carroll). The AP pass rate at John Carroll I would dare say is below the national average...make sue you check this out prior to putting your child there. They love to brag at John Carroll and make it look like their students are doing so well. Students at John Carroll have an inflated GPA scale which is different from most public schools but the knowledge behind those high GPAs is not there. Nepotism is huge at John Carroll. Most teachers are either related to someone else in the school or they are graduates at John Carroll. It's who you know that gets you a job there. It is somewhat of a cliquey school as well. At the time, I didn't realize how much JCHS prepared me for my college career. I was able to learn study habits and time management skills that have proven to be priceless. The rigorous AP classes allowed me to struggle while still having the support and close monitoring of the teacher. The athletic programs have been on the up and up with a new AD. The atmosphere in the school is small and I think the homey and family-like nature cultivates collaboration and success. JCHS has prepared me and given me the tools to do well in both college and in life. Class of 2018 As an alumnus of JCHS, I could not be happier with the direction in which the school is headed! Go Rams, Go John Carroll This an amazing Catholic High School that is focused on the whole person. The focus is on education and spritiual development for a complete person. The adacemics is very strong and the students are well prepared for College. If you want a great education for children this is the school for you. As an alumni of the school, I am proud of its focus on developing the whole child - spiritually, academically, emotionally, and socially - in the model of Jesus Christ. The small school environment allows students to truly be known and called by name. The school is always focused on continuous improvement, as seen in its root belief "we are always learning."

Education: offer college courses that transfer to Ball State, have a challenge classes for gifted students, a great special educational program with teachers who work individually with students. Ive had 5 kids go through this school, all have graduated. Teachers are wonderfull and no high turnover rate. Its just a great school. I am happy with how my tax dollars are being used here. The school has good course opportunities, but not all of teachers provide good instruction. The teachers don’t seem to care for the student, and look at them as just another kid in the grade book. column1: I attended for my last year only. Has good teachers but the work is too easy. Partly because the kids there want to be spoon fed. There is no challenge when it comes to the work except for one or two classes. Yea the gpa's may look nice on the transcript but its not even close enough preparation for college and I am lucky to have attended a challenging school before or I would be lost in college. Ive been here since 6th grade (12th grade now) This school is just a Detroit Public school disguised..... Its terrible, I'm missing certain credits and yet i'm "ahead of the game" ( they told me not to complain) WARNING SIGN. My worst fear is that I won't be quite ready for college next year. I must admit we ARE spoon-feed but I know it will hurt me in the long run. I think the most I can do is go to another school. But I really don't want to do that considering it's my 12th grade year. The students are ignorantly arrogant. Even the Basketball team is terrible now, we use to be very, very (state champions) good. ALSO we need 24 credits here to graduate (6 every high school year), MR Kirk is passing some students along with 18-20 credits.... Some of us only have 11 now... This school is one of the worst possible schools to send your child to if you want them to get a quality education. The students here are students that have been put out of other schools for their behavior, as such instead of enforcing a strict no tolerance policy, these students are found in the halls on a constant basis, or serving what the school calls an in school suspension. These students are violent, and are often seen bullying other students who are not fortunate enough to be transported to another school, but the administration gives them no real disciplinary guidance. The actual teaching staff seems to care about actually educating these sorry children, but how can you teach in a class full of trouble makers who can't read write, and do simple math. I feel sorry for those of us who actually do care that are trying to make a difference. It seems our talent, and time is being wasted. I have been attending this school since I have been in the 9th grade. And this school is a very good, intelligent, family type of school. There are many great staff and students that are the many few intelligent people in the city/state, SO FOR ALL THE FALSE ACCUSATIONS PLEASE PEOPLE GET INTO THE HALLS AND SEE HOW WE TREAT ONE ANOTHER, WE ARE LIKE ONE BIG FAMILY IN THIS SCHOOL AND THAT IS HOW THE STAFF TRY'S TO KEEP IT.... SHOUT OUT TO OUR FANTASTIC CONSULAR AND TEACHER,,, ECT....... ABT GATORS

People complaining need to go spend some time in a california school, this school is exceptional compared to any school my kids have gone through, beautiful campus, great staff, so organized and informative i was in heaven when i put my son here and very grateful. Nothing is perfect but i give this school an A for sure.

After having lived in that city 20 years we fled, and fled the State to a city with a school that is consistently rated 9-10 out of 10. Teachers at MVHS and Sunnymead MS are obnoxious, incompetent and running amok without leadership. It is STILL a family joke 8 years later when we need to describe a person with no respect for society or education that we refer to them as a Mr. Moreno. This school is known for its outstanding AVID program and creative musical talents. Thumbs up for this school. I find it funny that a parent will blame a school or other students for sending their child to jail for life, as a parent, did you not play a part in raising your child? Do you not take any accountability for your own child? You obviously had no influence on your child. I feel that is the problem with parents, it's so easy to blame 'others' rather than be a parent and take some responsibility for their own children. Show up at school once and awhile and be an active parent in your child's education!! To the person who stated they 'fled' out of Moreno Valley, dramatic much?? Moreno Valley High School is wonderful. Some of the most caring staff I have ever worked with. The majority of the MVHS staff genuinely cares for these students. As a graduate of this school in 1999, I have nothing but positive comments. Wonderful Administration, very knowledgable Counselors and teachers. Like every other high school in America, there are "bad" students that lack drive and discipline. They don't mix well with the driven students... Like at EVERY school. The class of 2013 earned over $3 million in scholarships. The MVHS AVID program is a National Demonstration program, which means other schools in America are modeled after ours. MVHS also has a top ranked Ballet Folklorico program and an up and coming Band program. This school gets many transfers within the district from students who are very strong in Academics. Overall, MVHS is a safe and education-minded high school. I recommend this school to any student who wants a great education. We often call MVHS "The best kept secret in the Inland Empire." My daughters school( Moreno Valley High School ) is rising once again. There are more students who care about our campus, teachers, and our fellow self's. The campus looks very sanitary, students appreciate more of what the teachers and staff have to offer. I'm happy to say that my daughter learned more than I ever imagined! column1: I have never been around a group of students that are as considerate, caring and genuinely thoughtful. It is a testament to the people of Garnett and especially of the type of young people the get created by a great school. I am proud of the people my children are becoming as a result of the education that they receive here. That is not to say that there are no flaws in this school. Like all schools there are places that it could improve - the lunches are barely palatable compared with other high schools i have been around - the school seems to struggle to keep up with maintenance issues - bu the education and atmosphere is top notch Most of the teachers are fantastic, however the current principal at the high school is not kind or understanding to student needs. All the students are contained to the cafeteria until the bell rings and are forced to sit. My children have been told to 'sit down' like a dog multiple times already by the principal, even though there are not enough chairs to sit all the students. column3: I am currently a student at Hopatcong High and I agree with the fact that too much is going into the extra-curricular activities more than the academics. They have been class after class away and it is not fair. There are barely any AP & Honors classes. Many students are horrible and teachers do not seem to do anything about it when they should. It reflects how others see our school, especially when kids are right outside the building smoking. HHS is a poor high school. The leadership is disingenuine and self-serving. I know the district well and the people in the high school. The teachers are stifled, Guidance has been a disaster since the departure of a truly student-centered man, and students are not being uplifted. Teachers and students can immediately pick up on administrators who are only out for themselves and it has a tremendous impact upon morale. Even some secretaries are just plain mean and should retire or leave. The principal, vice principal, guidance director, two counselors, a long time guidance secretary and one particular main office secretary should leave. They are bad for the district on multiple levels. With two kids in high school, we chose to move to Hopatcong from a very highly rated, affluent Essex County town. We haven't regretted the decision for a moment. The school may be smaller, offering less options, but the personal attention my kids receive is invaluable. My kids participate in Football and Track and LOVE their teams. The kids in Hopatcong have been taught from very young to be accepting of those with disabilities, instead of simply shipping them all off to "special schools" where they don't have to interact with them. Hopatcong is educating their kids to be good citizens, good human beings. With three kids in district I have had very good experiences with most teachers and administrators. As a high school teacher, in a different and supposedly top 50 HS according to state rankings, I am constantly comparing what my own children are learning with what my students are learning and I am very happy with the education my children are receiving. The entire school district has made significant gains it education our children in the last few years. Their STEAM program is rated no 1 in NJ if not the entire country. Had to take both of my children out of this district and enroll them in to private schools. I really wish I had looked at the school system before moving here. Parents whose children have no accountability run this district and the administration is over paid while the teachers are just mediocre. No emphasis on academics just trades and sports. Actually had a teacher tell me my child should focus more on making friends than academics. Consistently low ranking overall and a recycled BOA that is not for the best interest of the town or the kids. Attended from 2002-2006. While there were positive aspects to Hopatcong High School, it's in a district that is out of step with other, more highly rated schools that can be found in nearby towns that are socio-economically similar. Their are great teachers but on average I found the quality of instruction to be mediocre and unenthusiastic. Another issue is the relative lack of AP courses. The town of Hopatcong has enormous potential but will be forever hamstrung unless the district improves.

column1: Overbrook is truly wonderful school! I had two kids go through there and I believe it was just a terrific experience for them! The education is first class. The teachers really care about the students and work hard to make sure every student gets the same opportunities. The music, theatre and choir programs are one of the best in the state. The marching band, and jazz band are always winning first and second place at all their completions. They got third in the state this year and fifth in nationals. Also, many students in band audition and get in All South Jersey band and All State Band, we even had one student make fifth in the state in mallets. The choir program is also top rate we had 32 kids make All South Jersey choir (the most in South Jersey) this year and 15 students make All State Choir. We had a student place first, second, and seventh in the state for Tenor one. We had a student place seventh and tenth in the state in Bass one. That is just unbelievable! The sports may be lacking but with such little money coming in the school does a great job! Overall, Overbrook is one of the best schools in New Jersey! If you're considering a move to Pine Hill, West Berlin, or Clementon, think again. Ignore the previous post; the poster was obviously a disillusioned band-parent who knows nothing of the school other than the performing arts program. While Overbrook boasts an impressive arts program, talent and funding are dwindling. From an academic perspective, this school will not prepare your children for a four-year university. The majority of students attend community or local colleges. Teaching is not rigorous. APs are lacking. Administration is awful, removed, and not making the necessary changes to the curriculum. Teachers, overall, are not very interactive or demanding. The guidance department lacks knowledge of elite universities and the classrooms are run by unmotivated, misbehaving students. The demographics of the school mean that many students come from low-income households and lack a lot of parental involvement. Crime and safety are a factor. It is very below average in every aspect. Technology is outdated, save some newly added SmartBoards. Do NOT send your children here if you want them to have a chance at a decent livelihood after graduation. I think Overbrook gets a bad rep by a lot of people, but I don't think it's that bad here. Sure, I've had teachers who seemed like they could care less about how their students perform, but at the same time I've had a lot of teachers who were very nice and friendly that really inspired me to do better. The administration is pretty strict on a lot of things but they've done a lot to make the school a better place and it's nice to know that they actually care. In my experience guidance has been very helpful and the counselors are very nice. The student body is also very diverse and full of talented and bright kids. The curriculum could use a little improvement as well as the general atmosphere, but overall it's not a terrible school. I graduated from overbrook a few years ago. It wasn't a bad school, actually it was a decent school. There are some bad teachers, some average teachers and some great teachers just like any other school. It isn't just the teachers that make the school bad, it's also how the students approach their classes. Coming from a student that went there, a lot of kids would show up to class late and would argue with their teachers and for some reason the students parents will take their child's side. That's why when I read some parents reviews, I would love to see who their child is because them parents might be getting bad stories. I loved my four years at the Overabrook, I've learned a lot. I am a parent but I also am a former student. When I went to Overbrook there were a lot more problems at school such as fights and drugs. I am a believer that if you are raised well you will do well. I did well at Overbrook. I participated in many activities while going there and made life long friends. My daughter is now going to Overbrook and she is graduating this year in top 10 percent of her class. Overbrook is offering her AP classes and she has some of the most awesome teachers. I am happy with what Overbrook has given to the both of us. I was very excited because I saw this school had five star rate when coming to this school. Overall it was disappointing. The teachers don't even teach, but when they have to they pretend. The school has so many young teachers who are inexperienced or teacher who attended there previously as a kid. Most of the kids cheat in each class an I'm pretty sure the teachers aren't blind. If you ask me the biggest problem is that they don't teach but the tests are very difficult. On the other hand there are good teacher there, I've been moved a couple time. College prep is way more difficult than advanced, why is that you ask me? It's because no one is strict on teachers. Also another things is you become very independent I've seen people who need help but the teachers become deaf, the counselors are useless and to start with they don't help you get involve. Sports they only care about who knows the plays from the previous year, jv only plays 5 minutes and it's very horrible to watch. Clubs are set through the years of course freshman are scared and unaware so if you want your child to start good and gets good grades 9-12 grade I recommend you don't do the mistake of bringing him here. This school is full of teachers who seem to be in it just for the pay and full of students who have no limits and no boundaries. My child has had horrible experiences at this high school to the point where it became regular for them to have a bad day. All I want in life is to make my child happy, if you want the same, I do not advise you send them to Overbrook High School.

column1: One of the best schools in Camden actually the top school ! Especially if you are entering the medical field Brimm is the top school in Camden. No other school will prepare you for college and help you with what you really need and want like Brimm. I highly recommend you try to get your child in for 9th grade entry . Its a hard process but you can do it. I really love how Brimm is set up. Students can be amazing, and very caring, however many can also be challenging given it's urban setting. This is expected. Other districts have urban students that are less volatile. Given the many instances of student deaths and shootings in the area; nearby community; as well as the difficult rigor the school places on teachers, you would assume new teachers receive a minute amount of support. Good luck with that. Thankfully, my fellow teachers were saintly enough to help me throughout he year, while the "suits' and overall Board of directors made every attempt to sabbaths a decent teaching experience. They will observe you constantly, weekly (six at a time) at the worst of times with the expectation that all challenges of the classroom are solely rooted in your identity as an instructor. Even in this "top tier" school, you will find leadership and rigor to be far more taxing than many other "less privileged districts". The pay is worse than other districts (believe me) and support is barely existent. Instances of leadership observations will have you questioning your every move. The expectations are much higher than other schools. While classroom sizes are much smaller, many of the students can be more volatile. Far commute is not recommended and you are judged by your attendance and use of proper standards. Your time spent after school, rapport with students, your love for your teaching is not significantly factored into your "success" as a teacher. Rather how effectively you analyze and raise statistics of student data is key. You are not being molded and mentored by other educators, but by the STATE. Testing and the use of data is the primary factor to your success . Fail in this and you fail in the totality of your contribution. When compared to several other districts (who are also urbanized) I would not recommend unless you are heavily desperate for a job.

column3: Excellent teaching staff. Encourages sports participation; allows and even encourages students to play several different sports. Overall very happy with all aspects of the school. 2013 review: i am going to be a senior this fall. social life is cliques. the more money you have, the better you fit in with the popular clique. sports is amazing. we have olympic teams visit school, and alumni go to olympics. they are so common i have had classes with them often. teachers create the most amazing bond with their students. open minded teachers, working their tails off. remodeled so school looks good, but bathrooms are still horrid. the school is mix of white kids and hispanics, and they do not integrate together AT ALL. so with that said, if you are chinese or middle eastern or eastern european, then you fit in neither category, and are a misfit. personally, i have had great academic success, but because it is a family tradition, not because the school is good at academics. the math departments sucks so much, i needed my dad, (engineer) to tutor me, or not i would have failed. I have straight a's with 7 APs total, so this school offers you the road to success, you just have to take it. the extracurriculars is so much that you would think thats all kids do. this is not a bad thing. this school has kids accepted to ivy leagues each year. but hard to make friends. Our family has been at Harbor for 7 years and both my husband and myself have been very active in the school as part of the Foundation and with the various booster clubs of the sports our boys participated in. Our experience at Harbor has been outstanding and my oldest son has commented on how well Harbor prepared him for college.We found that both the administration and the teachers were accessible and definitely willing to help with issues as they came up (which fortunately were few and far between!!!) Is Harbor perfect? No. But I do think it is rather exceptional in that it has a large number of very committed and gifted teachers who are one of the reasons there are so many different clubs and activities for the students to participate in. I think the best way to insure a positive experience for both parents and students is to get involved and there are many, many opportunities for that at Harbor! I ADORE going to Newport Harbor High school! The social atmosphere is accepting of everyone. There are minimal cliques and as a girl who used to be called "weird" and was bullied some in elementary school, I now have friends all around campus of every kind. One thing I recommend if you want to succeed here is be responsible and proactive in completing your homework on time and getting makeup work after being absent. Teachers, although most want you to succeed, will not hunt you down about getting your work done. I really hope you choose this great school where you will learn, grow, and have more required of you before college. Our children attended Newport Elementary, Ensign, and Newport Harbor High School. As parents we were very involved in our children's education. We started the math club at Newport Elmentary after school. Newport Harbor High offered AP classes and Honor a Society. They graduated to attend USNA and Stanford University. Math and Science Classes are the answer to getting into great schools. I would never recommend this school full of drug addicts.

column3: Actually the complaints about the grading system were entirely correct. KGHS was on the 7 point system through the 2008/2009 academic year. They went on the 10 point scale in 2010 due to an enormous push from parents and (some) faculty due to the inequity of the 7 point scale against other schools with regard to college admissions. The school has come far in the last 6 years. I'm a teacher at the school and the former reviews are irrelevant at this point. The school building is new, the stadium is new, the kids are enthusiastic about their school, and their test grades are high. For a school of only about 1,300 these students have dominated in sports. Our academic offerings in regard to AP and dual enrollment is better than the area school. I live in King George and would be happy to have my children go to the high school. We love this school! I am very happy to send my children here. The previous reviews are irrelevant since so much has change din the past few years. I have one student attending KG high school and we are really happy with his performance. I was happy to learn that the high school's SAT scores are the highest amongst neighboring school districts. There are a fair amount of administrators that are really nice, but a lot of them aren't very effective. The students are pretty rude, and it's basically based on which social class you are in at the high school if you want to be heard. They take sports more seriously than they do with academics. This is our second year in the King George public school system and my son's first year of high school, now about 2/3 completed. I find the school teachers and administration extremely responsive and courteous, in fact surprisingly so. If I leave a message I get a call back within minutes, not hours or days. No inquiry is left unaddressed and they really seem to show genuine concern about students' well being. My son's grades are phenomenal and I have asked him several times if he thinks its because the school is easier than past schools and he always says there is actually more work and the difficulty level is about the same, which means they are doing something right judging by his good grades. They have dealt with virtual learning due to covid very well and really seem to be handling that situation about as well as could be expected given the novelty of the situation, especially since we live in an area where we and many others do not have broadband. I was a little miffed that the virtual learning schedule was 4 days per week of live classes and 1 day per week of self-study (no live classes) but as long as they are getting all the required subject matter hours and so forth I suppose its fine. The high school itself looks almost like new, great facilities etc. and seems like great school spirit. They also have a number of programs for gifted kids and my son was recommended for such a program without my having to 'push' the administration or anything like that. So far we are surprisingly pleased with King George High School. Go Foxes! My son is a 10th grader and his past nearly 2 years there have been great. He is doing really well in all his classes, he’s made friends, they have lots of AP and honors choices and the facilities there are quite good. The staff is super responsive and if I leave a message i get a call back the same day. It would be nice if they had more STEM related clubs but there is no shortage of extra curricular activities.

column1: Ottawa Hills is not for the faint of heart. I have subbd there and was shocked by the behaviors of the students. Each class had only 4-8 dedicated students while the rest of class kicked chairs down, called me names, ripped up their assignments and threw the remnants on the ground. I called security, and no one came. They were too busy. I called security again and got the answering machine. It's incredibly frustrating to come to teach and end up babysitting. I sincerely hope that Ottawa Hills will someday thrive again; but I can't realistically see myself as a part of the solution. I won't be guest teaching there again. I just feel badly for the few students that want to learn. It's too hard to think amongst all the chaos. Ottawa Hills is a school full of students who face immense challenges. Most come from families who do not emphasize the importance of education and thus are not involved. The front office staff is offensive, difficult, and frustrating to interact with. Administration is concerned only with meeting minimal criteria, and squashes any attempts made by teachers or students to achieve anything beyond that. The result is a hostile environment, because everyone is frustrated and burned out. If you are a student at Ottawa, you can be successful, but you will have to work extremely hard, and with absolutely no encouragement or support from home or school administration. The teachers at this school are very good, but unfortunately they are often handcuffed by a clueless and often absent administrative body. Call the front office, and try to have a friendly conversation, the results will astound you. You have to experience it to believe that someone can be that rude in that line of work. yes yes yes yes 10/10 yes yes What a fantastic neighborhood school! The passionate caring teachers and strong leadership throughout, encourages our kids in all ways! We are proud to be Bengals!

column1: I graduated from Andrean in the lower half of my class. However, when I got to college I was tutoring my sorority sisters who did not know how to write term papers, had not read 'the classics', & seemed to know little beyond basic Math and they all were in the National Honor Society, which I obviously was not. Yes, there were cliques then as well but for the most part, the students just ignored you and there wasn't any kind of bullying. There were endless opportunities to become involved. During my time there when students got in trouble, some were dismissed and others were handled appropriately. The Basilians ran things when I was there and they ran a tight ship. However, if we were in the area, I'd send my children there without thinking about it twice. I attended this school and while I was not in the highest part of the class, I was still better prepared than most of the people I went to college with. I was able to handle the courses without any difficulty and able to take on the task of writing research papers because Andrean prepared me for them. I believe this school set the foundation for my future. I am grateful to my parents for the sacrifices they made to send me to this high school. I am not sure where I would have ended up, had I not gone here. The smaller classes and the personal care that the teachers gave made the experience unforgettable. If I had children of my own, I would make the same sacrifice to send them to Andrean so they too would be well prepared. This is a horrible, unorganized school. The students have to purchase their own books; if you are lucky, your book total is $600. The tuition goes up every year and doesn't include new things. There is no air conditioner nor heating system in the school. The administrators are all white except one teacher and they lack sincerity amongst the minorities. Plus the uniforms suck! I've had several children graduate from Andrean and one still in. The competition in the classroom on the playing field helped form them. They are well informed about their faith. Lastly, the children who graduated were accepted to the schools of their choice where they found themselves very well prepared for college academically. The most recent and current administration is creating a generation of students that will not hold Andrean in high regard. This is going to lead to Alumni giving nothing back to the school in the future. What used to be a fabulous "family" has turned in an organizational mess. Sports will continue to be regarded in high esteem, but average students are just an afterthought.

Both my kids go there. They have the second lowest tax rate in York County, yet consistently deliver outstanding performance on just about every metric, as compared to other schools in the County (which spend much more on a $ per student basis) and the State, with plenty of opportunity to excell through honors, AP courses and College dual - enrollment. Serious students are well prepared to excell in College. They have a good variety of varsity and extracurricular activities and have acheived a substantial amount of accolades at the State level particularly for a school of this modest size. The facilities are not elaborate but are very clean and well-maintained Great school! Moved here for the schools and have not been disappointed! The staff is wonderful, even when your child has a hard time. I have three kids and one has trouble and the other does very well. Both were given the opportunity to excel. They both love it and we have been very happy with the environment the school provides. Both will be ready for college and what life experiences are next. As an alumnus of Susquehannock, I was very prepared for my future of college and beyond. With a great curriculum, strong teachers, and good balance with extracurricular activities, I was able to develop into a well rounded individual. If rating immediately after I graduated, I would have given 5 stars, but I know some of my favorite teachers have retired and cannot speak to the current staff.

column3: This school WAS one of the top schools in the prior to the 90's. They're riding on the coat tails of prior accomplishments for prior years. If your child is average or sub par, this school will cater towards them. If your child is a top academic performer, they provide sub par education & involvement compared to other schools (like Troy). They are too focused on sports as evidenced by all the millions spent on sport & activity centers as they cut OCAD, Speech & Debate, music, no United Nations Program, etc. English department is horrible with the exception of Ms. Casper. I remember reading papers from my child that were so grammatically incorrect that I would be beside myself. This was from the IB teachers. Casper is great, but you don't get her until Senior year which is too late. Many teachers are inappropriate and do things like swear in class, talk about personal issues, cross lines, or joke around too much with students. Those teachers are the ones most liked by the students. This school is filled with entitled rich kids that influence other kids, and the IB program fuels elitism. We are worried about the person our son will become after his time at this school. This school fails to keep its students on-campus. I see multiple students climbing over the fences EVERYDAY. Also, DRUGGIES EVERYWHERE I LOOK. And since the racial population here is mostly white, they all tend to throw racist insults towards the those who aren't. My friends back at Tustin were right, I should've never transferred to this school! im Jaime Garcia i attended foothill back in 2003 to 2005 then i moved to Dallas TX where i live now. I loved foothill great school great teachers i recently went back to foothill to visit for old memories. It really needs a make over :-) . Im 25 now n i ways think back to when i attended foothill great times we had miss all my old friends. thanks for a great time. If.any of my friends read this ive been looking for you all look me up Jaime Edgar Garcia from little Elm Texas I hate this school so much. I am miserable here. Most my teachers are good, but are honestly just too overworked by having classes of 40-70 to really be able to pay attention to every student. I transferred this year as a junior, last year I went to a fantastic school where I was very popular and well liked, and highly involved. It is very hard to get involved in anything, especially things outside of sports. The kids aren't very friendly and some are just flat out intimidating or rude. A surplus of your mean high school girls. I came in with a positive attitude and I will continue to smile and try everyday to make friends, but on the last day of school, I will gladly stand up in the middle of the quad and scream, " [a word that may not be appropriate] you foothill" and walk off, with a smile, to my new school I have chosen to transfer to. All three of my children went to Foothill High School and none of them were served well by the experience. I had heard such good things about this school but in retrospect, I wish I had paid for private school. The administration is uncaring and more concerned about their own upward mobility in the district than they are about the students. The school district administration is more concerned about politics than they are about education or the kids. The Board of Education members are more concerned about the their political careers and reelection than they are about doing the right thing for the students. The teachers are hit and miss. Some are okay but the math and language programs are awful. The teachers are also free to rant about their own political beliefs and are not required to keep their curriculum free of political bias. The school will not address a bullying situation unless the bully is poor. If the bully is from a wealthy family, good luck. Foothill's parent involvement is just them asking for money. Families are welcome as long as they're writing checks. We still live in the area so I am hesitant to even leave this review because it can hurt my home value but I think telling the truth to warn others is more important than money. If only those involved at Foothill High School were more concerned about doing the right thing instead of protecting their own private interests, it might be a better school.

column1: Great at art, which is its purpose, but I realized that won't look good on a college application. School should be fun, but I think their lack of rules here is bad, there is too much freedom, I find students becoming more lazy and irresponsable. There is a lot of bullying between middle and high school student and because its a school where you can be yourself tere are some dffernet people, and those who aren't different are sometimes shunned and not given the power to show their true capabilities. Overall its an okay school, jut wish academics were more challenging. I totally disagree with a previous reviewer regarding the school being not challenging. I find it mighty challenging - my daughter sometimes spends way into her bed time doing homework. Maybe the difference is that we did look into enrolling her in higher level classes (which is totally possible and encouraged by this school), for example - she is in 9th grade Pre-algebra whereas it is her 7th grade. May be it would be wise to look into something like that instead of complaining about lack of challenge - challenge your child, see how it can be done. Also I do not see how it will NOT look good on college application? Love the school, do not love new grading policy - confusing and discouraging to the students, but it was not invented by this school, was done by the District. i really like it and i love the fact that we get to have all sorts of extra classes but i sorta feel like some of the calsses at my "grade level" aren't challenging enough. although that may just be the whole district as well. VERY disappointed in this school. We had such high hopes! Kids have WAY too much freedom with no real structure. Teachers are not as connected as they should be. My son went from being a TAG student doing great in school to not caring about his assignemnts at all and not having any consequences at school for any of it, just at home. I busted the janitor driving VERY fast and wrecklessly in the parking lot & he never had any consequences for it. He's still there after 6 months. He could have hurt a kid considering there were several outside at the time. It's cool that the kids have special classes, my son loves it there because of that & because of the freedom but this school is the WORST I have dealt with so far when it comea to structure and really helping these kids thrive! ACMA has strong test scores and is academically challenging. The diversity of programs also enable students to become exceptional in their chosen pathway. We have a long waiting list. Once the school is rebuilt, we may have capacity for more students. My student has been attending for 4 years, and while she may complain about the rigorous expectations, she loves the artistic and open culture at the school. I see a lot of comments about there being "no rules" at ACMA and am compelled to comment. I'm a parent with friends whose kids attend different schools in and out of the district and hear about all kinds of over-the-top micromanaging rules. I appreciate the fact that the ACMA faculty is not there to babysit our kids. The students are there to learn, not be nit picked about what they are wearing or if they are chewing gum or, in some cases, whether they wearing earphones. They hold my kid accountable. My kid has had to learn via natural consequences that you have to have discipline and integrity to succeed academically -- and as an artist. I believe this will benefit him as he transitions to college and the real world. Needless to say there are real consequences and disciplinary actions for situations involving drugs, bullying, etc. I also appreciate that there are lots of opportunities for kids to get involved in a variety of activities and that the teachers are interacting with the kids in a variety of ways. For example, the math and lit teachers are very involved in the theatre dept. My kid will leave ACMA feeling supported, encouaged, and respected as an individual. I hope your student finds the right fit, too, whether its ACMA or elsewhere. A+ if you can get in. It is not open to all. You have to apply and if you care for your children I would highly recommend it. Our child was treated like an outcast because of their disability. The school did not support them. They let our child down. As long as you are not too disabled, and meet the style of children they are looking for, you will do just fine. I have been in this school for close to two years now and I already love it. The teachers help you if you need help with anything and they can be hilarious. They teach really well and they are nice and give you a good amount of homework. The classrooms are great and well maintained. The amount of character in this school is the most that I have ever seen. No matter who you are you will always be welcome in this school. I've never noticed any bullying, unlike other schools. This school has lots of events and they always make them as fun as they can. The leadership is great because whenever something is about to happen like an event or something that happened at school a teacher or the principal or any staff member will contact your parents. I totally recommend this school if you like any kind of art.

column3: Badger High School is not the best school for preparing students for college. The academic staff, counseling center and administration are apparently overworked due to the sheer volume of students (over 1600) at the school. Personal attention for students is basically non-existent. I would encourage parents of potential students to walk through the school on an average school day to see exactly what kind of environment really exists for their student. Badger, despite it's local reputation, is really just another large, public high school with the expected problems that go along with it. i just graduated from badger a month ago. badger as a whole is an excellent school. as a public school in extra curriculars, sports, music, cullinary, clubs, ag. etc i would say we're pretty amazing. We had students in my class that were nationally and state ranked in all of the above. acedemically there are amazing departments and others that... lack. the arts, music, band, orc, choir, and physical arts are amazing at badger. our school is more serious in music than an other school ive been to... our math dept, science dept, and music depts are best. social studies and english really lack. all of that into consideration, i am a proud graduate of bhs. go 2010 SEN10RS RULE badger highschool gets a great income of cash from the people in lake geneva. the school leaders such as the principles and district staff abuse that cash to crank the heat up to 85 degree's. the district gives us very short breaks compared to other schools. the badger highschools gives many tickets to student's to those how disabay any rules such as just simply wearing a hat. the school district is just trying to make a profit off of the town and student's it is very sad. Badger high school has many opportunities. But this school sucks. We have a tardy policy that is lame we get a detention if we are tardy to class two times. If we miss that detention we get a detention on a Friday until 5:30.If we skip Friday which is hard we get ISS the whole day on Monday. We also get an ISS for the whole day if we skip 1 class. We can also get a detention if we don't have our lunch card. There are also like 200 cameras in just one hallway. There are teachers in every corner yelling at everyone. You can get expelled for missing several days. You can get in trouble for almost anything because they think it's gang related. Like if you wear certain colors they believe you are in a gang. But almost every color is gang related. Also you get sent to the ISS room for dumb things. You can't graduate if you don't pass gym which is a credit. You also need to do community service to graduate. I am fed up with this school. I hate Badger. The school has been upgraded many times in the last decade, and the students still have athletics and music, which all lead to better grades. Badger High School is one of the best High Schools located in southeast Wisconsin. Badger has a big budget to work with and they defiantly put it to juse. They have an entire book full of classes for students to take (about 80 pages). The school is a five star school compared to Wilmot Union High. Badger High School has so many opportunities for students to get involved. The school's staff is so dedicated to the students where they stay as late as 8pm to help students in subjects where they need help. Badger High also has one of the largest DECA chapters in southeastern Wisconsin. A year ago they had a student win nationals. They are also the 2008,2009,2010 culinary teams in the entire nation. They have a completely new foreign language, math, art, and music wing. They also have switched over to healthier lunches like sweat potato fries, whole wheat buns, and many fruits. Overall this is one of the nicest schools in Southeastern Wisconsin. We love this school. Never have a problem with the teachers or the classes. When we need to contact someone at the school for information there is always someone to help. The FFA department is amazing and everyone does stuff for the community! Students have access to every resource they could wish for which ensures they will receive a quality education as long as they apply themselves. A wide variety of extra curricular activities for every student to take advantage of no matter what their interest might be. Although the "Life of An Athlete Program" which the school pushes on those who participate in athletics has proven to be a cancer that has become a joke that serves to divide the school rather than unite it. Dedicated teachers, counselors, and administrators. Badger offers so many opportunities academically, as well as sports and clubs. A great place to learn and explore your interests! The FFA department is second to none and has won many national awards. Music, foreign language, and DECA are all top performing both in the school and outside. Incredible experiences await the students of Badger High, if only you get involved!

column1: Newport Central Catholic is a great high school! My child goes there and his classes are very challenging and required a lot of hard work to achieve high grades. The staff is very caring and the whole school is like one big family. The school also recently got an addition that includes new classrooms, computer lab, art studio, and a Blackbox Theatre! The main building also got all new tile floors and new ceilings! In the future they're planning to upgrade the science labs! The school also had 3 different sports teams win state last year! This school is so amazing and prepares your child spiritually, physically, and academically for life after high school! I am blessed to have attended Newport Catholic as a student and to have my 3 children attend Newport Central Catholic. 2 of my children are now in college and achieving Dean's List recognition for their grades. Although we live in Ft Thomas we choose to pay tuition at NCC. My children could not have received a better education anywhere.
