column3: The Cumberland Schools aren't too bad but the high school is absolutely horrible if you are an average B student. Special attention is paid to honors students or fundamental students; average students get lost in the shuffle. This is a big high school with horrible administration. I hated being there everyday and I'm happy to be out of that school. There are some great teachers but the bad teachers are easier to find at this school. I would NEVER send my children or recommend anyone send their children to Cumberland High. Perhaps this review will be considered null and void since new management will be implemented soon, but here's my review of the school in the past two years that I have spent here. The expression "You'll remember high school for the rest of your life," holds true for me. Because I'll always remember the friends and staff that wade through the sheer IDIOCY and BLANDNESS of this domicile of education. Don't get me wrong; the staff is fantastic and they always put their best foot forward to help students. But the lack of school spirit and discipline makes the place feel like a racetrack, with everybody trying to finish as fast as possible. Homecoming dance has been cancelled for a whopping five years and counting because no one thought to attend. Kids herd together at lunch in social cliques because there seems to be no other way to talk to each other. And the detention policy? An hour after school to have your teacher glare at a room full of kids and then letting them go isn't punishment. It's the extended version of, "Which one of you kids threw that piece of paper?!" Staffers, if you're reading this, please note you guys are the best, so I gave the teacher rating 5/5. School, 2/5. By far the best public school my daughter has ever gone to. The teachers are some of the best, and they don't get enough praise Horrible. Middle and elementary schools here are great but do not send your child to this high school. Principals and teachers don't care about students. Only students that do well are honors and students with behavioral or developmental disabilities because they are the only ones that get any attention. Nevermind the fact that RI schools are making it almost impossible to graduate with new portfolio system where you have to take samples of your work from each high school year and present it to a board of people to graduate. Also they have made it that a 72 is now passing and if you fail any one out of three semesters you fail for the year. Please for your kids consider any other option than Cumberland high. I have no reason to dislike this school other than my own experience while my kids attended CHS. For heaven's sake, protect your children and find another school. Cumberland High School has improved dramatically over the last few years. District itself among the top growth districts based on the Department of Education's analysis. CHS offers more than 20 AP courses and has continued to add more each year. New leadership has improved the academic program as well as the school environment. Clubs and sports are plentiful. Music/art programs are rebuilding with enormous enthusiasm and energy. Principal/ assistant prinicpals are passionate and committed to ongoing improvements. Looking forward to continued improvements so my younger children can benefit. Cumberland High School is loaded with a community of faculty, staff and administrators that honestly do care about the education of our children. They are constantly striving to improve our curriculum and increase the difficulty of courses and pathways offered. CHS has earned NEASC accreditation, been recognized by Education Commissioner Deborah Gist as a school of distinction, expanded Advanced Placement Courses, increased the school s four-year graduation rate, and jumped 30 percent, from 40 percent in 2012 to 70 percent in 2013, in the number of juniors scoring proficient in writing. The school has been lauded as an Innovation School by the New England Secondary School Consortium. We are proud to have our first child graduate in 2014 and get into all 11 colleges or universities he applied to. The school offers many different types of clubs, art and music programs, and sports teams to get involved with. GO BLUE!! Clipper pride rising.... Under new leadership, Cumberland High School has soared. The teachers have high expectations for all of the students and work to help them all be successful. The teachers are very accessible any time help is needed. Every child has the opportunity to challenge themselves in honors or AP classes. School spirit is on the rise and is evident with the number of students who come out to support their sports teams, which happen to be very competitive. Recently renovated, the school is very clean and well maintained. Overall I believe CHS offers a great learning community. Something for everyone! If your child is a high achiever there are many AP options. If your child struggles, CHS has a program in place to help them attain proficiency. Teachers are professional and very supportive. Top notch sports teams with outstanding support from the CHS students. Numerous activities for students interested in art, music, debate, math, leadership, etc truly something for everyone. CHS deserves an "unsung hero" award.It contributes so much to the families in this town, yet for some reason is still widely undervalued.The teachers are dedicated to the students in and out of the classrooms.They coach teams, organize and chaperone international field trips and other events in and out of school.The culture under the new leadership structure is fantastic.It promotes citizenship and pride among staff and students alike.AP course selections are plentiful and offered to students at every grade level now.Expectations are high and the administration is slowly but surely eradicating teachers who do not rise to the challenge.I went back and forth between 4 and 5 stars only because I feel that there's always room for improvement, but that requires financial resources.The continued growth in achievement levels, the addition of new courses, the uptick in school pride have all been done, for the most part, with limited financial resources, which makes it all the more deserving of 5 stars. Im a freshman at Cumberland High school and I was hoping to have a good experience this year. I have a different style from other students at the school and that lead to me experiencing bullying from students in class and in the hallways. I have been tortured since my first day of school there. I told my mom about what was going on and I would cry once I came home from school on most days. She contacted my counselor to inform them what was going on and would usually end up not getting a call back. Cumberland high school does not care about students from my experience unless you are special needs, a honor student, or into sports. Bullying is very serious and no one seems to try to change anything. I'm a freshman and I am pretty content with this school. Of course, as a kid, it's my duty to dislike school, but this one is better than the one I'm coming up from by a long shot (a Cumberland middle school, I hated it there and will leave a review there as well). The freedom here is astounding. I don't feel like I'm being babied anymore. The ability to actually see what your grades are through letter grades is great, and I actually know how I'm doing in school. There are so many clubs, and although I don't take part in any, it's great to know about how much variety there is. Teachers listen to your concerns, and you can schedule conferences basically whenever you want. My only complaints would be about the schoolwide headphone ban (no headphones are allowed AT ALL unless you need them for a lesson. I have a minor learning disability and learn better with music to block out classroom noise, and it's kind of a pain) and the fact that you cannot go outside when switching buildings, even when your next class is across campus. There are 3 buildings and the fact that we can't go outside makes it hard to get to class in the 5 minute window we are given. Going back to the good, this school also offers a WIDE variety of electives to choose from that help prepare you for your future. They make the day more interesting because you're doing things you want to do as opposed to required classes, which can be a bit boring depending on your interests. That isn't the school's fault, though. So yeah, this school is great and if you're contemplating the decision to come here, I'd say go for it!! Im a new student there and im going to be in 9th grade starting the 2022 new school year

column1: This is a great school if you have a good student who is involved in allot of activities. They have much to offer. If you have a student that is challenged in many ways they will not be supportive to suggestions. They try to work with the parents and student but sometimes have their mind closed. Some of the facility has been there too long and they are unfeeling to a student s home situation and or learning style. The HS principal is out of touch with teens and their issues. Overall they do put in the effort, but you will need to be in constant communication with varies staff to be sure your student is given all they need, if they tend to have behavior issues or learning disabilities.

column3: I began teaching at Mount in 05-06 so I found reading these reviews interesting. It acuratly portrays the changes in the school over the last 7 years. I am pleased to share that we made AYP this year and our students scored in the same range or above students in the other high schools in our district. As a member of the faculy, I know what hard work has gone into creating the positive academic results and educational climate in the building. Our faculty has worked with our administration, students, and families to make the Mount commjunity one we are all proud to be a part of. This is the year for others to "Adjust Your Perceptions" of Mount as we celebrate making AYP and work even harder to do it again this year. I go to this school, and it's ehhh, it's not bad, but its not excellent either. I do wish it were a bit more diverse, I wish we had more electives, we don't even have cosmetology. I like the staff, they're good at handling what ever issues students may be experiencing, otherwise, no complaints. I'm currently a senior , and I've grown so much as far as education. Me attending this schooled allowed me to shine and show all that I can do. I didn't have that opportunity at my first high school in the roxborough area of Philadelphia. Staff are really helpful, and they care. There are many clubs and sports. The only complaint would be dress code. They pick and choose who to call out on dress code violations. There's so many rules for dress code for a school where you wear whatever you want..uniform might as well be in forced!! Students and families are the main focus of our school. We have dedicated the last 7 years to improving our the culture and climate of our building, while raising at the academic rigor for all students. We continue to decrease the achievement gap by addressing individual student's needs by analyzing data that drives instruction. We are not perfect, but we are good at what we do. Serving students and families is what we do best. It's a good school especially the IB program I am giving the school a five star because they took my son from another school district as a freshman and gave him the opportunity to stay as an honor student AND become an honor athlete as well! The coaches saw the talent in my son and gave him opportunities in the athletic departments that he would never have received in his old school district because of polotics. As a parent I am very appreciative for the school staff and coaching staff. I highly recommend this school. They put my kid in a headlock and said that they had to control the situation but like that never again

column1: I am a student who is currently enrolled in Hazen High School The course selection is improving, but is still somewhat limited for any students who are interested in attending competitive schools. In terms of science, it is downright debilitating, as the 9th grade science course is deemed unnecessary by many, but testing out of the class is not permitted. The AP course selection is becoming better, but it could still be improved. Teacher quality is varied. Some teachers are extremely skilled, while others are downright incompetent. Resources are, again, limited. If a student is interested in attending a prestigious college, none of the resources available will be any help at all whatsoever. Extensive research must be done on the student's own time. Curriculum and student assistance are tailored to the assumption that students are primarily interested in attended the state flagship, UW Seattle. The school, overall, does a moderate job at informing students about opportunities. The Culminating Project program is perhaps one of the school's greatest flaws. It attempts to help students learn about college, but the design is so poor that it's an annoyance, rather than an assistance. I have two current students, and two graduates from Hazen. It has been a uniformly great experience. The students get along well, the parents are friendly and helpful, and the staff is motivated to get the most out of every student. It's tough being bordered by wealthier and academically higher rated schools, but I am completely happy with the decision to have all of my kids go K-12 at Renton schools Hazen what a great school. This is the Best Senior High School The teachers are the cream of the crop. Thanks for all your concern for the students well being Hazen High School - if you're super smart or super challenged, its the school for you. If you rest in the middle there's only a few good teachers that care. The staff is not friendly nor are they helpful...on the other hand few of the teachers care. Needs a better headperson in charge who will talk to all parents, intstead of using staff to communicate for her, one who cares for all people of color and their childs needs. My son loves this school! Involved teachers and committed and friendly students. Thank you for a wonderful school! Excellent school for students that are looking to advance their education and move on to college or technical schools. Teachers care about students and are inclusive, positive experience overall. If you are searching for an education that allows your child to grow and prepare for college Hazen would be a great choice. Great teachers, excellent resources and caring staff. My daughter has really enjoyed her experience here so far. She is a junior this year. She is on track for college and excelling academically and socially. One thing she did do starting freshman year is get involved in extracurricular school activities. There are on average about 25 kids in her classes. Over the last 3 years any time I had any questions or concerns I received immediate responses from whomever I reached out to be it a teacher or their Principal. The teachers here want to help your kids be properly prepared for college or technical school and the Running Start options are great although my daughter is applying out of state so she isn’t going down that path.Parents here are involved in their kids education which is apparent from the flood of people on parent teacher nights. Regarding safety, I feel the school takes student safety seriously and addresses all concerns immediately as they should.We are very happy. Our daughter has no learning issues so I feel that is harder to rate as we have no experience with that aspect of the school. This school does a good job taking care of the whole child. There are clubs, classes, teachers, etc that support mental and emotional wellness. My daugther attended private school all her life and Hazen being her first public school has not disappointed. She has not experienced any bullying and/or drugs. There is some evidence of it in the bathroom but she has never seen it herself. She feels challenged but not overwhelmed. We are quite happy with the staff! Note that truly this School is an 8 / 10 based on academics. If your child is middle to higher, I can definitely recommend. I cannot speak for the 3/10 which refers to "equity". They could possibly work on helping struggling students, yes.

column1: NO AUDITORIUM IN THIS SCHOOL! Above average teachers and students. However, there are problems with communication on discipline across the board. Cell phones are a big issue... administration and school board didn't want to really touch the issue so teachers had to do all the work and dealt with it as best they could. Great community and supportive and caring parents who care about what their students are doing. Administration seems to care and fund sports more than the arts... but then again, is that really anything new here in Virginia? KWHS is a pretty good school. I am a rising senior, and I have rather enjoyed my past three years attending this school. The teachers are great, the sports are very successful, and the administration is very good. The students strive to learn, and everybody is nice to each other. My favorite thing about the students is that there are no "cliques" so everyone can be friends with each other. The community is very involved with school events, especially sports. I'd have to say, this is a pretty good school for how small it is, and compared to the other schools around us, we're amazing. I'm proud to say that I am a Cavalier. King William High School is an excellent school with extremely dedicated teachers. My son, a sophomore last year, is very bright but equally lazy and so he seldom ever did homework. Fortunately, he scored high on all tests, due to outstanding teaching. And, when he did fall way behind, the teachers did not falter to get him caught up. In the past, we have paid up to $40,000.00 per year to ensure him an excellent education, but do not feel the need to do so, since moving into this school district. I am part of a few minorities within this school; in result, this usually leads to bullying and seclusion which seems to rarely or effectively be taken care of.

column3: Professional, well-educated and caring staff. Thoughtful, well-mannered students. Cutting edge technology. Excellent community support and involvement. World-class education in a small setting. Numerous extra-curricular activities and elective choices. Distinguished arts program. The best overall district in Western PA. All of the negative reviews that you will find here are from bitter students who did not like the school based on elements like lack of popularity or poor grades, or from parents whose children are doing badly. This is a PHENOMENAL high school that cannot be beat by any other high school in the neighboring districts. They properly prepared me for college and the work force. I am a former student and am now a high school chemistry teacher in Eastern PA. I cannot believe the poor ratings for this exceptional school district. The school has repetitively scored high and in the top 100 (out of over 600) public schools. I graduated with honors from the University of Pittsburgh with a chem major and biology minor. I then did an alternative route program for my teacher certification in secondary education with a science specialization... Anyway, I routinely scored higher than my peers on exams throughout college. I believe PT helped me tremendously and I was given a great education. The teachers are top-notch and prepare students for the future. I wish the students and parents who gave poor reviews could experience a different school district where books and teachers are in high demand. Absolutely absurd comments. One of the comments below said PT had average state testing scores which is completely false. PT is ranked very high on PSSAs amongst other public schools (top 15%, some years top 10%). Another poor rating came from a parent who complained about the school's guidance counselors not helping their child apply for school/ financial aid/ scholarships. PTHS prepared your child to actually get into a college. Many children across the state are not even eligible to graduate high school and drop out. So I have an issue with your one star rating. One last comment on a ranker before me, an individual conplained about the lack of diversity. Yes, PT is predominately caucasian but that is not the school's fault. The school is public to all PT residents... they're just predominately white. I'm not saying PT is a perfect school district, it definitely has flaws like all schools. However, now that I have had my student teaching in an urban pittsburgh public school, it frustrates me that people have given an above average school such a low rating. I just wish the people who gave one star ratings could visit an inner city school where there are bigger problems that need resolved. Top notch! The administration really cares about the students and brings a high level of academic achievement. Faculty and staff are fantastic. Academic wise, this school is great. I have learned many valuable things here. The math department is not the greatest, but it works. If you are in band, you will hate the administration. Penn-Trafford does not at all support band. I am in Marching Band, and I get so disgusted with our administrators. We barely have a budget. All of it goes to athletics. Marching Band had just a much physical activity as any sport does. We march around on a field in the middle of summer for over 80 hours, but yet we barely have money to do anything. The athletic secretary doesn’t support us at all. Football had the highest budget in the district. Crowds yell and scream at football games while bands are performing. Away bands have complained about this as well. This has tarnished the reputation of our district for away bands when they come here and are not respected. Great way for othet schools to think about us! Our budget is probably going to be lowered even more soon! If you are in band or the arts, you will not be supported. If you’re an athlete though, you are the best! Most of the teachers do not act this way though, just the athletic and school administrators. There are some teachers though that do act this way, and it makes me ashamed to be at this school. ON A GOOD NOTE: Other than the way that the band and color guard are treated, this is a great school. You learn a lot, and you are very prepared when you leave high school. Penn-Trafford is the best, except for the way that they treat their band and color guard and other activities involving the arts.

column1: Kittatinny is a school filled with drugs and sexual people. I am ashamed I have to send my children here. There is a pregnant girl in my child's grade! I am sick of this school and my child is going to a new school next year. I attended KRHS and felt that it prepared me very well for college and the world beyond. I enjoyed the extracurricular activities and had some amazing teachers. I made wonderful friends that I am still in touch with 7 years later. Overall I had a great experience there. My experience and education here prepared me for college and life as an adult. Teachers are very helpful. Many clubs and activities for any student. Please do not send your kid here. Kids in the bathroom vaping, racist and homophobic graffeti signs everywhere especially the bathrooms and locker rooms. They make you do a unit of swimming where boys will make fun of girls and gym teachers allow it because "boys will be boys". People at this school will do anything for the sports kids. Thats where most of there funding goes, to the football team and cheerleading team. Theatre, art, music, etc, are all things they do not care about. They let go teachers all the time, and most of the teaching you get is the teacher putting on a movie and you sitting there for the entire class. The guidance counslers are not helpful at all unless you need your schedule done for the next year, but they dont help you with normal everyday problems, or help you get into a college, etc. Very racist, homophobic and sexist school that I would rather die than let my kids go here. Teachers over doing it all the time with hours and hours of homework and projects that would stress out an adult let alone a teenager. Do not go to this school ever

column3: Solid 10/10. The students are kind and there aren't cliques like other schools. I came from another school district and had no issues making friends. The teachers and staff truly care about the students and want them to succeed. My experience was very very terrible and the worst time period of my life. I came into high school happier than I went out. I did everything to try to fit in, but in the end, the social environment just decided to exclude me, and don't know why! I spent years in depression as to why I was not respected by my peers and excluded from everything and there isn't a thing I haven't tried. But don't get me wrong, I loved the teachers and the other staff, as they are the reason I even woke every morning and showed up to school. Apart from that, the students are all very shallow and superficial, and I can never say I found any form of companionship in my four years here. The teachers are very great, but from a social standpoint, I strongly discourage any student from studying here.

column1: Good overall school. The kids make the school, hope there will always be a good group at CV. Poor sportsmanship, abusive language and deportment. While attending a basketball game, I witnessed some of the most offensive behavior by your student body. Chanting rude cheers, taunting and generally acting like idots. (This incudes your cheerleaders.) CVHS is the epitome of what is wrong with the school system in the USA. There are a few teachers that care about teaching; however, the majority are in a state of constant posterior pecking in order to keep their jobs. That is especially true for classified staff. The upper levels of administration (who will remain unnamed) are grossly incompetent, over-compensated, and should retire for the common good. The athletic department supports coaches that are more wed to archaic fraternity style traditions rather than more progressive methods of athletic training. The students in Iron County tend to have much of the same cultural clicks that their parents hold. As a Cedar City resident, I wish I could honestly give CVHS a shining review, sadly the truth binds me. I would'nt recommend this school for anyone's child unless your friends of the principal,vice principal! Corrupted school many things hidden from parents and a very unprofessional staff of teachers. Another very in organized school with a vice principal that is given a little to much athority. Instead of adding gas to a fire how about using some water to defuse situations with your students and listen to what they have to say instead of your staff!! I have felt very included. The Stud Gov makes sure that everyone has a friend. My teachers care about my education and my wellbeing. Many Great teachers. CV student body is very inclusive, they are generally all friends. I saw and I just heard about the Canyon View Graduation Cap story on Channel 13 Fox 9 pm News. As I listened and watched the school leaders talking to the graduate, I wanted to cry and I was very ashamed of the leaders. What it appeared to me was that someone using their power to make someone feel bullied, belittled because the adult could!! It definitely made me fill sad, for the student, with someone at the leadership authority trying to make it a special bullying of a young graduating Native girl. This never should have happened to this girl, especially when they were given the ok from the school to do it. Shame, shame, shame on the adult leaders for letting this happen !

column3: Terrible school. doesn't know how to take care of its students. the worst school ever. nightmare. We moved to historic and expensive Lexington, MA for the famous school system. The middle schools are great. However, the high school is a major disappointment. Half of the honors/AP teachers can not or would not teach. Our AP Bio and Honor's Algebra 2 teachers are so bad that everyone complains but the department heads defend them and berate the parents and kids. LHS is great ONLY because of the great parent and student body. If you have an average kid and not the money to hire a tutor, your child may sink and nobody would notice. It's funny that most of the negative reviews are also ungrammatical. This suggests, unsurprisingly, that the parents' education level will have some bearing on their perception of this school. I am an current student at lhs. It is extremely stressful and the pressure is on. Kids easily fall into stress, anxiety, and depression. Some teachers barely know how to teach properly and effectively. However, the student body is extremely welcoming, friendly, and sometimes has the typical high school cliques. The health department and guidance department are both home to some of the best people in the school. The student needs to have to confidence and willingness to talk and reach out, not to fall down softly(or hard). It's a big school. Just need to get used to it. Though lhs is tough, there are wonderful teachers and some that aren't so great. You just have to get lucky. the Principal is mean for not allowing student visitors to see their former teachers and for making excuses. the principal needs to be fired by the Lexington School Committee Worst Honor/AP classesToo much pressure, not happy school The school is literally falling apart. There are no resources for anything. I am pleasantly surprised in regards to the academics. I find the school flexible and easy to deal with. My son is only a freshman and i'm keeping my fingers crossed. He's smart but not academically focused and thought he would struggle more but he's doing well. (As and Bs) The only exception is the sports management. They DO NOT care about the kids (not speaking about the individual coaches) or the sports itself. I feel like the coaches have no authority. All decisions made my AD (even little ones) . It's really too bad because they have talented kids. If they were fostered, they could go places. We have a high performer and for him it is a super great fit. Very strong teachers (very), challenging curriculum, and lots of clubs and activities (over 100). His friends seem "normal" and decent. It is a school with a lot of kids of first gen immigrants and so a fair share of tigers. Many kids are aiming for super selective schools. This has its own set of issues and its not clear this is a good fit for our 2nd child. But so far we are more than satisfied. No school is perfect but LHS is a solid school with a lot to offer. It´s more of a hardcore private school than a public school. While this will certainly fit a small, incredibly motivated minority, Lexington High is flooded with students whose parents expect the school to be a hands off ivy producing machine for their child. For every student that gets into Ivy this school produces, there are at least a hundred who leave feeling defeated and depressed from the cutthroat academic environment and homework load that eats their personal life. Those considering moving to the town exclusively for the school system, don´t let yourself be dazzled with test scores and seriously consider the pros and cons of the high achieving and soul crushing environment created by Lexington High School. The school is literally falling apart. It's so disappointing that a town as affluent as Lexington cannot get its' act together around a new high school. There is no room to eat in the cafeteria. Teachers are generally good, but there are still teachers who are uninspiring and just don't know how to connect with teenagers. Some teachers frankly expect college level work, particularly in regards to submission of English papers. With regards to moving to Lexington for the schools: Caveat emptor. Teacher quality is inconsistent, both academics and sports are extremely competitive (in a 2000 person school many kids don't make the cut) and there has been no movement to really expand athletic opportunities given how many kids there are. This is a really progressive town filled many who could afford to send their kids to private school but choose to send them to public school. Lexington schools should be better. The high test scores and good placement come in spite of the schools; I would estimate that at least 80% of parents have college degrees, and that at least half hold advanced professional or graduate degrees. They actively nurture their kids for success, and there is a thriving industry of kids activities in this town, and most of these, too, are mediocre. Did well enough for me...and then some. Some of the reviews are hilariously inaccurate. My advice is not to take French at this school. The Dean and teachers are not interested in your child’s success or their ability to speak French after graduating high school. The primary objective of one teacher in the department is to impart her sense of social justice and political views on the class, while another teacher wants to fail the class so they can learn that life is hard and develop persistence/ resilience. The dean refuses to acknowledge their is an issue. Thankfully they hired a native French speaking teacher in the last year that makes me hopeful that things will improve.

column1: I went to TA last year, and I thought it was a pretty exceptional school. The spiritual emphasis was amazing and being there really got me closer to God through the chapels, gospel choir, and the week of prayers. As for educational standards, its okay. Although the teachers are great and the principal really wants the students to succeed which is good, the tuition cost is too heavy. If you want your children to go to college after attending TA, you'd better have pockets overflowing with money. Takoma Academy is a great school!!!! You meet so many different people they also help you financially with the tuition Strong leader in academics, sports and music I thank God for Takoma Academy Your child WILL be ready for college and in will have the learning tools for eternal Life !!! I have heard nothing but horrible things about this school. A student who no longer attends this school is now excelling when they were doing poorly at TA. I'm surprised that as a SDA school they really don't practice what they preach. TA is not a true Christian school. The leadership at the school, namely the principal has done things that are unfair, spiteful, and hurtful. His behavior has reflected on the school as a whole. I will never send my child to this school and cannot recommend a parent sending their child to this school either. I have had the opportunity to speak with the principal of this school and many of the students. Nothing I have heard would allow me to rate this school as satisfactory. The Principal avoided many of my questions regarding the spirituality of the school and some of the questionable policies of the school. Some of the staff who asked to remain anonymous, expressed that they were extremely unhappy. The overall impression is that the atmosphere at the school is abysmal. The students were not pleased with the school and the focus of the school in general appeared to be geared towards their basketball program, not education or Christian principles. One of the student that attended last year, who I also baby sat when he was younger, now goes to another school. He is much better off at his present school I believe that the current leadership at TA is bringing the school down spiritually. I attended TA. It was one of the worst experiences in my life. I was treated unfairly in the worst way. I enjoyed the students, but the school sucks rocks! I am a former employee of Takoma Academy. Sadly to say, this school is being led in the wrong direction. The atmosphere of the school has changed for the worst. It definitely appears that the Spirt of God has left the building. I pray that things get better. If you are looking for a christian school to develop your child's spirituality, look elsewhere. In fact, you will find no benefit in sending your child here. The only program worth anything at this school is the men's basketball program. But all else is not worth the money. I am not sending my child back next year. Takoma Academy is a family oriented school in which the staff is very close because they attend the same church and this is all well and good, but there is a down fall. They don't handle their business. You have to constantly stay after the staff/teachers to get things done concerning grades, etc. and practically stand over them. If you don't, it will never get done. You have to make sure that your child is getting credit for the work they are turning in - I feel as a parent I should not have monitor the teachers and staff to make sure they are doing their job. It is very frustrating dealing with them. To sum it up it is great to have a nice friendly atmosphere but their top priority should be to make sure the business of the students is taken care. They do not handle their business at Takoma Academy. This school has had 3 principals in the last 4 years... nuff said. You have no idea ehat next year willl be like. They have no accountability and the blamegame is played all day. They flat out give Sevent-Day adventist a BAD name and it's a shame. I have removed my kids from this school and I wouldn't send my enemy their. Its sad I am currently attending Takoma Academy as a High school as a freshman. I feel like an outcast at this school. The students treat each other, their teachers and me with the utmost disrespect by complaining and insulting behind backs. Whenever I think about this school - I want to cry because it has genuinely been a waste of my time. I have learnt near to nothing academic wise. Compared to my middle school education, I have pretty much repeated 8th grade. Plus freshman are not allowed to take Advanced Placement Classes which I think is absolutely absurd. A well practiced tradition at Takoma Academy is Chapel time, where the students and teachers gather together and worship God. Well, everyday there are presentations, singing, sermons and activities of the like such that are presented on stage. The presentations are excellent, however the audience will laugh, taunt and mutter and the slightest mistake you make. Now you may find my review of this school biased. I am telling you that unless you attend the same churches, hold the same belifes, are the same ethnicity, and speak the same way they do - then be prepared to feel like a weird misfit. I've been a parent of two students who passed through TA between 2007 and 2012. My children both excelled at TA. Their SAT scores were high enough to earn them high scholarships in college. Both students took advanced classes, and are now excelling in college-- I waited to see the sufficiency of their academic preparation before posting a review. The leadership opportunities are many-- both were involved in student leadership and other various roles. The sports program is broad and varied, and allowed for some travel. Other extra curricular activities such as the performing arts program -- voice, drama, and band (and ceramics!) were opportunities you don't see in all private schools. My children took advantage of all except band... but were also involved in the worship and praise band. Some of the staff and teachers have become personal friends. The school has done some purging of teaching staff that from a parent's perspective was needed. The physical plant has also had about a million in rehauling, and the place is looking quite nice. If I had a third child, which I"m glad I don't, they would definitely be enrolled at Takoma Academy! High school is definitely what you make out it! Takoma Academy is diligent in having many events and programs each year. If you don't like something, get involved in student government and try to fix it! The cafeteria food is very tasty for being vegetarian and most of the teachers are willing to build friendships and help their students. The only thing I did not like was the small variety of classes, but that is something that couldn't really be changed due to the size of the school. I am totally inlove with this scool,my oder daughter graduated from TA four years ago and is doing extremely well at Washington Adventist University.The ephasis that is place on Christianity is awesome,the mission trip they do each year has encouraged her to choose her career in nursing.My youngest daughter is now a junior there,expensive you bet it is!! but it is a priceless investment. i would not have sent my daughters anywhere else.Takoma Academy is family. The school has really gone down over the past few years. The principal they have now is sure not making the school look any better and not making any improvements. This school only glorifies basketball and does not even acknowledge any other sport. A few teachers are good but overall the education is horrible and too much drama in the school. Would never send my child here and I wouldn't recommend anybody to send their child here either. The new principal does not seem to put an emphasis on the academics, it seems like basketball is the focus. The blame game for when things go wrong shows a lack of leadership. Most of the students are shallow, extremely rude, worldly and overprivileged. Some of the parents are even worse. Complete snobs. Yeah, no one is a perfect but it's not about perfection. It's about character. I was absolutely shocked at their behavior. The best thing about TA was the week of prayer. It brought me closer to God. Overall, I don't regret going there. That experience made me stronger. I like Takoma Academy. The offer plenty of opportunities for students to get involved and experience something new such as study abroad. The academics are good, my PSAT scores go up every year. They have many events and a really good athletics program. The teachers care and are always trying to make sure you grasp a concept. It really bugs me that some people are saying bad things about this school. It's not perfect, there are some downfalls to this school, but overall it can be amazing if you put the effort to making your experience a good one. I am very pleased with what TA has to offer. The teachers and admin care a great deal about students and desire that each child does well. The arts department is well rounded and I am pleased that students can be a part of more than one aspect. I highly recommend this school to anyone who wants their child prepared for college at the end of their high school career. TAKOMA ACADEMY IS IN THE MIDST OF AN A HUGE RENAISSANCE ON EVERY LEVEL. THE SAT SCORES ARE HIGHER THAN THE NATIONAL AVERAGE, 85% OF THE CLASS OF 2013 DID EARLY ADMISSIONS TO 200 COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES & 99% OF THAT CLASS WENT ON TO ATTEND A COLLEGE OR UNIVERSITY. THE MEN'S SOCCER TEAM WON THE 2013 MARYLAND INDEPENDENT SCHOOLS CHAMPIONSHIP TITLE, THE CHOIR WON 1ST PLACE IN THE PRESTIGIOUS I-SING CHORAL COMPETITION. THE SCHOOL'S STEM PROGRAM IS BEING ENHANCED EACH YEAR. THE SCHOOL HAS CARING AND DYNAMIC TEACHERS WHOSE PEDAGOGY IS PRODUCING OUTSTANDING ACADEMIC RESULTS. ENROLL YOUR CHILD AT TA AND YOU WILL NOT REGRET IT. I have to say that this is a great school! I am very impressed with the TA teachers and the Principal. The Principal and her staff are very informative and transparent. I am also very pleased with the teachers and teacher's support that they provide for the students. One thing about the TA teachers, the parents nor the students will never have to hunt them down to ask questions because normally they answer your questions before you asked them since they are so informative with their emails, the students work websites and what they post on the school website. TA is a school with a friendly and close family like environment that focus on academics and preparing students for college. Also, they have a very good basketball and soccer program and other sports. If you are looking for a school with a very good academic program that prepares students for college, have a friendly and family like environment, have supportive teachers and a very good Principal, then TA is the school for you. Takoma Academy is a wonderful and under-rated school that values the arts, academic excellence, and diverse athletics. Our two sons have thrived in this caring and challenging community over the past 6 years. The faculty and staff understand the importance of building character and developing well-rounded individuals who are eager to be a part of and contribute to their community and the world beyond. It really does take a village to raise caring, intelligent, responsible citizens and we have been blessed to have the Takoma Academy as a part of our village for our sons. I am a current parent at the school, and this is my second year. My child struggled last year or her first year, and the school did everything possible to see her thrive. From my experience thus far, the school is intentional about its student success, and it shows. I see her thriving and happy at the end of the school year and looking forward to a new year, and it's because of what TA and the TA family are doing every day for each child to develop their character, education, and creativity.

column3: I have had 3 students at SLHS since 2009. In those 5 years, SLHS has gone through 3 or 4 principals. The last principal was horrible & the current principal is useless. They focus on ridiculous rules ("since fights happen at the end of lunch, we will shave 5 minutes off of everyone's lunch so they won't have time to fight" - like I said, ridiculous), and football. My 3rd senior has been in gifted classes, and signed up for 4 AP classes for his last year - he only got ONE of them. AP classes and advancement in academics is not promoted. They simply want to push the students through like sheep. My son skipped 2 grades, and only lacked 2 credits for graduation this year. Instead of rewarding such academic achievement, he's in mindless electives instead. The only good thing at this school is the JROTC program. I went to 9 schools growing up - private and public. As a military family, my children (5 of my 7 kids) have gone to a total of 17 schools, and Southern Lee High School is hands down the WORST of the WORST. It's hard for me to even fathom how terrible this school is, and I've had kids there for 5 long years. Something needs to be done!!! Great school, great sports, school spirit is amazing! It's a family! Hope everyone is lucky enough to have the same feeling at their own school. Highly recommend by far the best high school in our area. The most caring and knowledgable staff in our county. they really care about the kids and them acheiving their goals.

column1: This school is seriously lacking in academics. I have hired 4 graduates to work for my company and none of them can spell, write a correct sentence, or do simple math (even on a calculator). The students obviously do not learn the skills to go out into the world. How do you write a college essay if you cannot spell and know no grammar? I went to Burling city schools my entire life. Graduating in 2008 I went to one of the top rated public colleges in the country and was sorely dissapointed at the lack of diversity and chartacter I recieved from burlington. I worked hard and played varsity sports and was highly involved in the music department (the only thing that kept me at that school). AP classes were a complete joke and a majority of kids I know who took AP tests in English, Government, and History were wofully unprepared. There are some phenomenal teachers and some teachers who would be fired were it not for tenure. There were large numbers of students who disrupted the learning environment for the kids who tried to learn. Not to mention the lack of up to date materials and work materials. And perhaps more sad was the number of students I graduated with who could not read on a 6th Grade level. Exceptionally sad and would not send my children there after spending my entire k-12 career there. What an exciting time to join the Burlington City High School community! They are hitting the ground running this 2013-14 school year. The staff, with their energetic new principal definitely were not just sunning themselves at the beach during this past summer. Many great initiatives were shared during "Back to School Night"! Flags with the school mascot and colors adorned the outside of the building to encourage students to come where Blue Devil pride would greet them every day. College pennants and banners lined the hallways to encourage students to dream big and work hard to achieve those dreams. $5000.00 would be a blessing to a school who is focused on supporting their community and student achievement! Good Luck Blue Devils! I'm a parent who's children goes to burlington city high school, that schools is a joke everyday my child has a problems, like being bullied, children fighting her in halways,children throwing food in her hair. What a chlid to do. Just because you have a title dont make you perfect teachers,principal,guildance counselors all they do is sweep things under the rug , I'm a very upset parent, I feel in this day in age teachers are not taking time out for children, so, I'm not rating the teachers nor anybody else

column1: Great school, All teachers friendly and help the studnets. Everyone equally treated. it’s a safe school but just smaller than the other high schools in Stockton and there is a dress code Collard shirt with khakis but people usually wear black jeans and it’s fine. All students very friendly and open with everyone good counselors

column3: We have one child attending BCHS and the teachers have no control in the classrooms it is like being in a zoo. So the kids that are there that want to learn can't. My child is not a custome to being in such and enviroment he went to perdido middle school before coming here and the kids where taught respect. My child takes the hardest classes this school has to offer and complains everyday about the disruption and that the teachers have no control. The county needs to spend money on getting teachers that can contro thier classrooms. As a grandparent I believe this school and schools across the nation has plenty room for improvement. I believe this school is like other schools across the nation where teachers are losing control in classrooms. I agree with the parent who posted on this website on March 29, 2010. All you have to do is turn on your local news and you will see some kind of violence or disruption happening at one of our local schools or schools across the nation. It all started when we allowed prayer, the bible, and paddling to not be allowed in schools. I have a granddaughter attending this school. As a recent graduate of this school, I have seen what really goes on at this school. The one point that I cannot stress enough is that if a student wants a good education, they can get it at BCHS if they are willing to work for it. The problem is that many students just want to take the easy road and don't seem to care or think about their future so of course the atmosphere won't be as great in the basic diploma classes, but all schools are that way. Sure, there are a few bad teachers, but there are also really good teachers who very successfully prepared me for college. Since the MacBook distribution (yes, every student gets a laptop here) the behavioral referrals have almost ceased to exist, and never in my four years did I see real bullying (unlike Perdido Middle) or cyberbullying at this school. Yes, the parent involvement could be better in some programs and more recognition should be given to non athletic programs, but no school is perfect. Bottom line, if your student wants to succeed, then they can very well do so at BCHS. (Hey, our Val and sal last year went to Wharton and Yale.) Just look at the facts. My daughter graduated May 17, 2019 with honors. She will attending Auburn University in the fall. My son is a rising 10 grader at BCHS. Both of my children have excelled in this great environment. We loved our time there. The school spirit is great and the group of kids he was friends with were an awesome group. Like I said, our son was involved in multiple things, had great coaches and teachers, and has gone on to do well in post secondary.

column1: I first entered Largo as a junior in August 2010 and I was shocked. I came from Virginia and you had to know that the environment and the people was different from what I am used to. For one, the school is not diverse, the students are unruly to teachers and some teachers, take it or laugh it off and that's not right, the lunch is a mess (miss my school lunch back in Alex, VA) , the kids meander through the halls as if they have nothing better to do, and the place is old and stale, especially the nasty rest rooms. Not what I am used to but overall, its not a bad school. To me, just students who want to be bad. The people are nice, well some and it all depends on the student. Of course, there are kids who act up and there are kids who actually do a great job and the kids who do great jobs, get a bad rep for just attending Largo but that's why we work hard to differentiate ourselves from the knuckleheads and in the end we will be rewarding. I am a Largo alum, as well as a parent of a Largo HS student. She is in the biotechnology strand and we have no issues. I do believe some of the teachers could apply more effort, but I am on top of that. Yes, some of the kids are disrespectful/unruly in the halls. But it is up to the child to take his/her education seriously (with our help) and to decide right from wrong when we aren't around. Largo has proven to be just as great for my daugher as it was for me. I had AP classes while there. If you are a REAL parent, raising your kids with morals, standards, etc, Largo should be no problem. The only thing good about this school is the Marching Band. The teachers try but the students overrule. Avoid this school unless you have a child who can ignore ignorance, get their work done in noisy classrooms and has a desire for band and music. I just know what my son tells me. And if he like it I love it. No complaints this far. I have looked at the syllabus for each class he is taking. And I find these classes he is taking will bring him into his next level of education. Go Largo! Largo High School is not for the weak hearted. I am an alumni student and my 4 years at the school were exactly what the rumors confirmed. By the grace of God I made it out of that forsaken territory. With the help of self determination, select counselors, peers, teachers, and administration who really cared; I was able to make it out on time (C/O 2013). The setting is filled with troubled youth trying any and everything to find a way to be socially accepted, minus the kids that actually want to become something in life. It was definitely a wake up call for me, as I sometimes found myself caught up in the fun and excitement of "High School", which was easy to do because of the laissez-faire attitude portrayed by the staff. Definitely not the worst school, but far from the best. Not to mention the school building is as old as sin lol. However, The bonds made inside the school are unbreakable. I actually learned more from attending than actually being "taught" Nonetheless, It was definitely an experience to remember, a very bittersweet, tart experience lol.

column3: I transferred to this school for my Sophomore Year from neighboring Los Alamos High and this is the best choice I could've done in my life so far. this school is like a family, students and staff have personal bonds and can discuss issues with them. Student Council is amazing at this school! The Student Council will be hosting the annual New Mexico Association of Student Councils State Conference in two years at the school. They will be showcasing the wonderful traits of this school that are often overlooked for the negativity. I am so fortunate and happy to have moved to this school! EVHS is good school. It does have some really good teachers and some that are not so good. I believe that because of required state testing some teachers cater to students that are really not interested in learning. This can create problems for students that excel and need to be challenged. I also feel that the dress code as written in the handbook should be enforced. That does not mean uniforms but just enforcing what is already in the handbook. Overall the school is good and I feel they are trying to get better. I heard that this school had sponsored teachers meaning they are now legal resident of this country from being a foreign national. And I heard from a realable source from the Human Resources that they are no more sponsoring. That will be the biggest mistake that this district could make because I have 2 kids and 5 nephews and nieces who all go to this high school and they all said they were all great teachers. So what if they left? I'm sure there are more teachers who needs a sponsor who are good or better than the old ones. Please continue this sponsorship because it does help the high school and the community.

column1: I moved to Maple Grove from a small farm town with my two daughters who averaged 42 children per grade there. My oldest started 10th grade in MGSH with 575 students. It was intimidating to her at first with no friends at all. Her first comments were how acedemically hard it was. She was an A student in the small school. She was in one AP in MG. By mid-year she actually said to me, "I know it is hard mom but it is really good for me for getting ready to go to college. I think I will do much better now." It was music to my ears. She is shy but made friends along the way and gained a lot of respect for herself. The foundations program is very impressive. She loved the pepfests! She said mom, everyone does. Group involvement is awesome. I can't tell you how happy I am we moved here. It was the best decision I could make for my daughters. The school deserves more than a 10 in my eyes. I am a teacher at MGSH. There is high turnover in teachers, administration, and classes. The administration is distant and unsupportive. The classes are overcrowded and extremely tracked. The pep fests get dangerously out of control, And at dances the grinding is just wrong. The kids at this school think they are running the place. It will get much worse when budget cuts come. I am a prior student that attended maple grove senior for all three years. This school is biased and unprofessional. If you weren't involved in sports or theater there was no place for you. Dispite this i dis make friends there just werent any club/ activities for us to do or join. The staff, especially admin, are ridiculous. Some were overly friendly with students and others you didn't dare talk to or go to with problems for the fear you'd be yelled at or talked down to. My sister still attends the school and says the same things are still happening and the admin is worse than ever. My suggestion is this, unless you are a jock or into music or theater, go to a different school. You will make some friends but there is no place you belong at the actual school. The only way I felt comfortable was in art. The teacher was amazing and didnt choose favorites like many others did. There are some good teachers here, but the kids are ridiculously entitled. They aspire to be like an adjacent, wealthy district (Wayzata), and they are not even close. They want what they want, and they think they should have it now. If you are able to access social media and find any of them on there, it is eye-opening. I would not send my kids to school here. Hats off to the principal for attempting to instill character in them with the "Crimson Way" (for which the school was recognized). But you can't change the student body. They are getting the wrong messages from their parents, and most kids are spoiled and act like it. The kids who have more middle-class values have a very small peer group and are hyperfocused on post-high school plans. Some of the counselors here are horribly out of line. Maple Grove has some of the nicest most down to earth people, but the administrators and faculty are a joke. I was advised not to take ANY AP classes, even though I am qualified and I believe I am ready and excited for an academic challenged. When I tried to enroll they made me take study hall because apparently I had, "too many credits" I feel like they are stealing away any possibility of a learning experience. I'm glad I've transferred, because this schools culture, student body and counselors are terrible. Average with episodes of bad taste coming from teachers, secretaries, counselors. Awful. If I had to do it all over again I would have moved somewhere else so my children would have had a decent, humanitarian school experience. My son graduated from MP senior High. He had incredible opportunities there such as an award winning robotics club with mentors from the community and support from the school. He also had a wonderful experience in his higher level classes in which the teachers were knowledgeable and accessible. The principle is highly ethical and inclusive and works very hard to keep the campus safe and with open communication. This school was also challenging and taught my son how to study and learn. My son was accepted into several universities for an engineering degree and continues to do well in his studies.

column3: You will hear that you have skipped high school and gone straight to college level here and it is true. The kids here are here to learn or excel in their Art form. It is hard to get in but get your child on track now. Montessori or self directed learning programs will NOT prepare your child for this school. Lots of homework and Lots of opportunity. The curriculum is rigorous and prepares students well for an academic life after high school. I went to JCTMS and felt so stifled by the traditional program and PRAYED I would get in Manual. I did (yay!) and I never wished I had gone anywhere else. The class work was challenging, yes, but I felt freedom to choose what to study. I was in HSU so I would have more opportunities to explore all that Manual/YPAS has to offer. I took accounting, modern dance, AP Government, fashion design, business law, theatre, etc. I was involved in extra curricular activities and I LOVED Manual! I never didn't feel like going to school because due to the block scheduling, I never felt like I had the same day twice. Now 11 years post graduation, my fellow Manual grads have made differences in the world and we are confident that it's due to our education at Manual. We were prepared for college, academically, personally, and creatively. Manual is not for everyone, only the most focused and driven students will thrive. If you are the best of the best, Manual is for you! My experience at this school was terrible I loved attending dMHS. I felt prepared to go to college and have since graduated and will be attending graduate school. I was able to take a variety of courses that suited my interests and future goals. Manual is a great school for those that are independent, disciplined, and committed to their education. The teachers are overall very knowledgeable and genuinely want their students to succeed. I graduated last year and still keep in touch with several of my old teachers. The workload is extremely heavy, especially if you take a lot of AP courses, so plan on spending a lot of your evenings doing homework for hours. On the flip side, if you do take AP courses, it can take a semester or even a year off of your college career, saving you time and money if you plan on seeking a postsecondary degree. If I had one major criticism of the school, it would be the administration. The principal and some other administrators are often nonresponsive to student concerns and complaints, and in my experience, the interests of the student body are not usually taken into consideration when making decisions that affect them. The guidance counselors are also often unhelpful and are basically there just to serve as college and career consultants rather than helping students that are struggling with mental health issues. While I don't claim to speak for all students, it's a very common opinion among the student body that the leadership does not prioritize students' mental health and is laser-focused on getting the highest test scores possible and ensuring that their graduation rate remains at or near 100%. However, no school is perfect, and overall, if you are in a position where you have access to good mental health services and are confident in your ability to manage a school-work-life balance, Manual is a great place to attend. so first off, everything about the school is very emotionally oppressive, making you think that you're not good enough if you're not the best. if i stayed at this school i would've not been able to graduate. Diversity is boasted as a benefit from attending the school, but the student race stats are similar to most other high performing schools in louisville. im not sure if this is just me as a former mst student, but its hard to get into he school spirit when you're worried about homework all the time and not having the time to go to any games or participate in clubs. I wish I joined a club like BSU instead of having to hate the school for the dim atmosphere during the actual school day. its important to have a balanced academic life as well as social life, and going here creates a system where you have a VERY loaded academic life, and may have to balance it out on your own with making your own time to have fun. However, this instead results in a duality where you become a procrastinator with a large distaste for work, or a somebody who works all day and develops many emotional issues from isolation. i was unfortunately the former, and had to switch this year after dealing with this attitude of mine and the school for freshman and sophomore year (Along with NTI!). The 2020-2021 schol year, it was especially dreadful. Any joy of school that was there before as gone. You could barely talk to anybody, and literally everyone was stressed. And, you felt it, that was the worst part. I could go on and on but the school all in all is just depressing. Really depressing. I'm glad others enjoy it more than me though. Very harsh work expectations for students and overall not amazing for students with elevated stress or anxiety.

column1: Out of all the public schools, I believe the best the Hawaiian public schools could get would be way below average. However, since this is one of the better schools in Hawaii is why it would be commended. Teachers are great, and education O.K. but I believe Kalani needs to hire teachers with enthusiasm. The teachers don't know how to take care of their students, and there is no discipline whatsoever. Teaching rates are SUPER slow, and I believe these things that they call Hawaii's 'Public Schools' need improvement big time. I can't see myself as a doctor, or even a entrepreneur, or even a 7/11 owner. My future doesn't seem bright at all, and unless education increases, there is no hope not only for Kalani, but all public schools in this miserable island. High quality education and dedicated teachers. Safe atmosphere and competitive academics. Even their football team is getting better! Kalani has been a good experience for my son, who is a mainland transfer student. Former student of Kalani and i have to somewhat agree with some things people rated. There are some great teachers, but if there is no care behind the teaching, then ultimately the student does suffers. It's not just up to the teachers to teach. Its, also up to the students to want to learn. Ultimately, it is the teachers job to teach weather or not the students want to learn, but you do have agree or disagree that when the teachers come to work to do their job, its easy for them to loose sight when all of their efforts to the majority of the students are all for not, but teachers should realize that just because there may be a majority of the students who seem to not care about learning, for some of those its just an act and for some others who want to learn, you maybe doing an injustice. In my experience, when a student had a question after class or needed help after school, some teachers didn't have the time for them. That is an example of not doing your job. Kalani High School is an average school. There are great teachers that really help out the students and some that are not. In addition, the teachers have really bad favoritism that make students not learn that well. Also, the principal doesn't treat his students well. He has favoritism over the students and is not a friendly type of guy. For sports, they have AGAIN favoritism for that too! They don't pay attention to tennis and don't even come to the games to watch and take pictures which is horrible. They didn't give us new rackets/materials to play. The coach had to use his own money to cover it. Which I think is unfair because they didn't renew his contract so he is not the coach for Kalani anymore. In addition, they didn't even pay for our uniforms too. OH AND THE BATHROOM IS DISGUSTING SO THEY SHOULD PUT LITTLE TRASHCANS IN EACH STALL. Also, they should give more discipline and punish kids harder. SO THIS COULD STOP ALL THE BULLYING. ------- SUBMITTED BY A FORMER STUDENT Kalani may score great on test scores, but that as about far as it goes. That does not come from teachers, but families with one child and tutors. There are many students there who work hard and are deserving of their success. If you are in need of help whether it is academic, personal, or other look elsewhere. Disorganization with a who do you know atmosphere. Cliques that just make you sick, unbelievable the way the females in this school behave. Almost feels like your'e living in a different country, very odd. Agree with the comment below. Don't expect much for support but overall we had alittle better experience. The choir teacher is so awesome and works her buns off. Had several other teachers we had great experiences with and others who were just short tempered and disinterested. They do put quite a bit of effort into college readiness and applying for college which is probably the thing they do best. Excellent. A+. A little harder coursework than other high schools but with matched student outcomes.
