column3: Think twice before sending your child to this school. Administration has a terrible attitude. Beware, your A student could become a C student in a semester. The good teachers are really good and the bad ones are really bad! beware Aweful school! If I could get my kids out of there I would in a second! The kids get harshly disiplined for the dumbest things. Cant wait until my kids graduate and are out of there for good. As a concerned parent of a senior at WHS I can tell you that all students are not treated the same at this school. The ethnicity of the student plays a huge role in the outcome of the problem situation;whether its academic or discplinary in nature. So thank you! Mrs.English teacher ,Mr.Dept head, Mr Principal and Mr.Administration for continuing the traditon of holding our students back. Both my children graduated from Williamstown High School and We had a great experience with the school and the teachers. This school is horrible. I am a student a WHS and I have been put through too much. It is my first year here and I have been already bullied to the point of no return. Teachers cannot stop bullying and have not yet put an effort. They say it is frowned upon but do nothing. Though some teachers do teach correctly most are very poor and lacking in teaching skills and don't get me started on other administration. They are not helpful at all and at most times they are extremely rude. If you send any of your children here I advise you to pull out fast because they will think what happens here is what is normal in a school. But it isn't. Many of my fellow students are fowl mouthed and cannot behave while the teachers are too scared to act upon it. There are too many students here which means that your child probably wont even get the help he/she will need, since the teachers are juggling 20-30 rowdy teenagers in a class. I do not recommend Williamstown High School to any parent. The reviews for our High School are varied. However, we have had only wonderful experiences with our children both academically and athletically at WHS. Good students excel in any environment with strong parental, family, and community support. Contract and budget issues are a reality in ALL school districts, and yes, bullying is still a problem that must be addressed with vigilance on a daily basis, but children are smart and strong. If our kids take accountability for their education and have support they will succeed in spite of any issues that exist. GO Braves! Although I have only been at this school for a few months, I have seen many great things so far. Students have access to laptops, smart boards and many other types of technology that other schools don't have. There are many dedicated teachers who don't just care about their paycheck (let's face it, we didn't choose to be teachers for the money)! The student population is very diverse and there are so many ways one can customize their high school experience. Is there drama? Yes. Is there bullying? Of course. As teachers and school professionals, I guarantee no one wants to see any child go through some of these things. We are here to help, to listen and to become better teachers. I've been in other schools that didn't have the technology, activities and stellar level of performance. Williamstown is among the best of South Jersey. Although I'm sure the teachers and administration aren't perfect, Williamstown is constantly trying to make things better. To me, that is the biggest indicator of what a quality school really is. Its interesting reading these comments from the parents because you guys are not in the school 180 days a school year so you would never know what was going on. Also the fact that every student has a complaint is also interesting because it shows there are immediate problems that need to be fixed. For example i know for a fact majority of these kids that go here have gone to counseling because of problems in school, many have gone to summer school, and most have had credit completion. Now if i was a parent and that was the majority i wouldn't question others home life but the school and the quality.I honestly feel for the kids that are still going to be there for the next few years. I am graduating this year and thank god to my active mom, friends, and family for being there for me because from the day i got there it was a constant battle between student and staff which is sad.I am thankful to have teachers this year that are attentive, respectful, well rounded, and liked and known by many with a great reputation but sadly they are the bare minimum at this school. I wouldn't recommend this school unless your a fighter who wont fall for anything and will stand up to what is right. WHS is a wonderful school that prepares students for their future (inside of the classroom as well as outside). While there have been many complaints about the staff in these reviews, in my opinion, the staff is great.The need to discipline is a necessity in order to stop distractions from occurring, which may hold an entire classroom behind. Detentions are forms of punishment that have been going on for years all over the country. Yes, a student may miss material if they are acting out, but were they really learning anyway? It is part of their punishment to make this material up. Why should other students be punished for good behavior by keeping these kids in the classroom? 4 min. is more than enough time to get from class to class. In the real world, there are consequences for acting out and being late. The ethnicity complaint is also a joke. WHS has such a diverse student body as well as staff and people are treated with the same respect. Again, it's all about the student's behavior. If you do what you're suppose to be doing, you will be fine. Parents need to stop taking their child's excuses and really need to experience WHS themselves from a student's perspective. My child is finishing his first year at this school. He is in all Honors classes. His course work is challenging and he is engaged. I constantly ask him if he likes the school. He enthusiastically responds with a YES! We did not come from the Middle School. I found all of his teachers to be responsive if I had a question. He was involved involved in several clubs and a spring sport and was welcomed by the students. I found to be a great school, that provides a safe environment and a quality education for those that seek it. The high school administration does very little to stop the bullying of students. We had to pull our 11th grade student from this school district because the problem was so bad. The so called "anti bullying" seems to works best in the elementary school level. Beware if your child is going into the high school. The quality of teachers in the honors and ap classes is tremendous. Interesting history teachers who have been in the Gulf war they teach about. An anatomy class with actual labs. Psychology classes, classes on death and dying and criminology. The teachers engage the children to look at different perspectives. It makes me want to go back to school!Not enough preparation for college applications early enough...should start in Sophmore year. Great school for all kinds of learners. Both of my children had good experiences there. Absolutley horrid. While the teachers are nice and very knowledgeable in their feild administration is completly failing at running what could be an amazing school. My son go to Williamstown high school, very good

column1: I personally attended Cashmere High School. As a student if you are not a "JOCK" then the teachers dont look at you the same, this is the worst High School I have ever been to. I also attended Waterville and Eastmont but Waterville takes the cake. Certain teachers that are too old to understand what kids are going through as they get older greately affects the teacher to kid relationship. How are you supposed to look up to and want to immulate someone that is way too old to comprehend what they are trying to teach. The biggest problem is not the kids, food, or security it definately is that the "Seniority" of the faculty plays too big of a role which in turn keeps teachers in the school that should have quit a long time ago. Cashmere school district is FABULOUS! I am a former student of all three schools! Now, I am a parent! Still love Cashmere schools! My oldest should have graduated 2010 but decided to make bad choices but even though he wasn't a jock persay, the school staff was still always very supportive and tried to help keep my child on track. Lots of parent involvement and close community. Yes sports are high here but academics hold high expectations too. They want to see kids succeed! Along with sports being important because kids need the disipline that sports teach! If your not a jock just get involved that is all the school wants to see! :-) I went to this school district K-12th grade. After entering the real world I felt prepared and ready for college, although I did struggle at times. The best thing I liked about Cashmere, especially at the High school level was the opportunity to make my education. I was very self determined and Cashmere allowed me to take my skills and soar. I was very involved in extra curricular activities including theater, sports, and ASB. I have daughters who will start kindergarten this year and I hope to find a school district like this one. I think with many small towns you will always have those 'cliques' which is a struggle at times, and of course there is the downside to having a little less opportunities than say a 4A school. I also felt that there were a lot more teachers (mostly older tenured) that didn't seem to care about the subjects they were teaching (again I'm thinking middle/high school level) while others went above and beyond for their students. Cashmere has been known for their athletics and I'm proud to say I was a Bulldog, but they also have a great theater and music department. It is all in all a well rounded school in a lovely community. I am a graduate from Cashmere and im hoping to move back so my kids can go to Cashmere. I have nieces and nephews that have all graduated from Cashmere. I work as an educator and have seen several schools in the state and out. Every School has flaws and people who will bash schools are because their "child was wronged" or they hated school when they were there. This is the same issue in all schools. What i do know about Cashmere Schools is yes it is an athletic school that takes pride in their programs. I wasnt a jock and I was treated just like the jocks were treated. I currently live 3 states away and would love my children to be a Cashmere Bulldog! So if you read the negative reviews take them with a grain of salt and remember ALL schools have there issues. Cashmere is amazing and I give it 5 stars!!! I graduated from this school a couple years ago and I'm glad to be out of there. This school is only made to serve one kind of student, white and athletic. If you are not involved in sports you are somewhat invisible. Sports are overly funded and leaves students in music programs to do their own fundraising... As a minority in this school I felt looked down upon by other students and faculty, even though I was very successful academically and involved in extra curricular activities. With the people here I have witnessed sexism, racism and homophobia. So if you're looking for a narrow minded, sport obsessed, right wing school this is it! If you want you're children to be independent learners and critical thinkers send them somewhere else, this is far from a progressive school. If your high school child is in sports, they will probably do well in this school. However, if not, prepare to have them swept under the rug. This school along with the other schools in Cashmere have great teachers, but ZERO communication. My kids have attended their whole lives (minus one year I choiced them out of district) and I have had nothing but problem after problem with these schools. They take no accountability for their inability to communicate with the parents of their students (unless of coarse you have an athlete child). I am relieved to be closing on a house out of the valley and getting my kids the educational experience they deserve. What a disgusting place. So many people at this school possess incredible talent in various fields, but if the field isn't green then good luck getting through these four years. The drama and music departments receive little to no money, because all funds go to sports. If you are not athletic, then you are shamed by your peers and even your teachers. Jocks receive so many more opportunities than those who do not participate in sports. It's devastating. On top of this, bullying is rampant and usually done by the sporty kids, however nothing is done to prevent it because they are popular and athletic. It's really a sad situation, because many of the teachers are truly wonderful. But most only pay attention to you if you are an athlete, regardless of how good your grades are.

Point Boro is a great school that doesn't only encourage students to be the best they can be, but they encourage you that you can do anything. column1: The midland timberwolves are a small and diminishing school district due to their lack of commitment. Starting from the superintendent and working it's way down, the school administration is weak and un-inspiring to the students, coaches are typically anyone with a pulse and small town politics run rampant beyond the normal. Sad to see a school administration that continually tolerates sub-par performance and those individuals are in their positions thanks to a community that has lost hope. Most schools have strengths that they can build upon or a vision to build towards, but this district has neither. Almost unbelievably they reward mediocrity and fail to inspire children to achieve better for themselves. My family landed in this town by accident, and as difficult as it is to share, do not encourage others to make the same mistake. We spent 15 years working to make a difference only to realize that it will never happen and we were wasting our time, money and effort. If you are 4th or 5th generation "Laconite" then it is a great place to raise your family, otherwise consider Germantown, Metamora, Dunlap or Chillicothe to raise your family. A plus - good food at Club Lacon. Great test scores. great principal. Outstanding teachers. I really like the guidance counselor and the ag instructor. I really find it laughable reading the comments by the disgruntled parents on this page. If you review the test scores it is evident that this school is competing with much larger high achieving schools. I am very happy with the education my children have achieved within this district in spite of a few disgruntled parents.

column3: It has some great staff but needs to be bigger to accommodate all the incoming students every year. renovation of the third floor would help this problem. PCHS is a truly excellent gem of a school that is frequently overlooked by Westchester standards due to it's slightly less impressive score statistics. These averages more accurately reflect the impressive diversity of the school than the lack of educational rigor. The school is one of the only schools in Westchester where students can receive both a quality education and experience a diverse student body. I graduated just a few years ago and went to a top 50 college, as did many in my class. I feel like I was prepared for the real world and the workplace in a way many of my peers at Blind Brook/Rye/Greenwich high schools will never be. I had excellent teachers and highly value the education I received. When my niece was going through a difficult time, the a mount of encouragement and support she received from the administration and the teachers was amazing. Port Chester High School is fast becoming one of the most dynamic schools in Lower Westchester. The adoption of the IB program a few years back has set a new route for these schools. The population is diverse, but each year their composite performance improves ... and now it is routine to see youngsters applying to top tier colleges. The transformation over the last decade has been stunning. A new $80 million bond will shine this school ... and the lower schools ... over the next several years. Port Chester is moving into rarified territory ... and the community has firmly embraced this academic leap and decided to provide their students with the best of the best.The faculty at OCHS is professional to the nth degree ... a seasoned crew that has credentials and expertise one does not often see in such quantity. There is a special sort of loyal commitment among the staff that is just unusual ... and rather amazing.In the next few years, PCHS will emerge as the new leader in region ... and the Village will become the "must" stop among discerning home-buyers toking to provide a rich living experience along with a value educational moment for their children.

Conard is and has continually been one of the top schools in the state and deservedly so. This is a school that positively validates why you pay taxes. Graduate of the school, prepared me for the real world for sure. Good diversity of student body. The overall experience for my daughter and nephew has been tremendous at Conard! I have seen significant intellectual and social growth in the kids. I would highly recommend this high school to residents of West Hartford! Several kids from my family are attending or have attended Conard recently and they all have very positive things to say! I also found Conard to be a wonderful school for my daughter. The curriculum is challenging and the teachers push the kids to do their best. Overall experience has been fantastic.

column3: Our sophomore transferred from Kennedy Catholic HS along with a few of his Kennedy peers and all are extremely pleased with this school. We personally know many other students who have transferred from surrounding area schools such as Niles and Cortland who are just as pleasantly surprised at what a great school WGH really is. The teachers are great, very knowledgeable and caring. There are courses offered that are not available in any other area school such as engineering. media, among others as well as the regular AP, honors and college credit. In addition, the sports are outstanding and varied most being of division 1 caliber. People who denigrate this school obviously do not know what they are talking about and have never set foot inside this awesomely beautiful school. The swim team is also division 1 and the pool is spectacular. The school is kept in immaculately pristine and looks more like a college campus. Students take pride in this school and the feeling when you come in is one of acceptance, caring, and respect. If people would really understand how great this school is they would be knocking down doors to get in. I know Lakeview and Kennedy and WGH surpasses. This is an awesome school. It is a beautiful building that was spared no expense in accommodating students needs in a modern state of the art school; providing an inviting and comfortable learning environment. It is spotless giving the feeling one is in an ivy league school and not a high school. The staff is always friendly and helpful from the principal on down to the custodians- and that attitude permeates throughout the building. Students are respectful, and take pride in the school which is bar none the most beautiful in the area. The curriculum is varied and comprehensive and the college prep courses are challenging and relevant. There's a wide range of sports, most division 1, and the facilities are outstanding. The teachers are for the most part caring but more quality, top of the line teachers must be attracted to better the instructional aspect. A better job needs to be made in instilling in some students how lucky they are to be attending a school which offers so much in such a great setting. Finally a much better job needs to be done in community awareness regarding the wonderful things that are happening at Warren G. Harding. I transferred this year and really like this school. I was hesitant at first because I was told bad things about the school and the kids here. They were all wrong. If you hang out with a good crowd, do your work, participate in sports and the many activities offered you'll do well. There are tough kids in every school and even the tough kids are not a problem if you don't mess with them. I know that there are those kinds of kids at other schools so it's no different here. There are more opportunities for classes and sports here and the school is really nice. I would recommend this school.

I can barely step in the building without having terrible anxiety. Both of my children attended LS and received a first-rate education. They learned how to be self-sufficient students, team players and good citizens. The administrators go out of their way to make a connection. Communication could be better at times and at other times they just communicate too much. 3 out of 5 of my kids went onto college, 1 entered into the trade with an apprenticeship, the 5 decided to go straight into the job market. Sultan did a fine job preparing my children for the path that they chose to take as young adults. Schools lack the capacity to teach kids with learning disabilities and to communicate with parents. This school does not take differences into account when it comes to the speed and needs of other students learning I like this school. Very nice. Teachers are very helpful.

column3: This school has a highly commendable teaching staff and some very supportive administrators/counselors/coordinators especially for those students who are serious with their studies and academic goals. A large school comes with a broad range of kids with varying abilities, hence the mediocre test scores. Overall, they have managed to maintain standards in spite of challenging budget constraints. Terrible school, don't let these LAUSD faculty & Teachers fool you when they talk the school up, it is a disaster there, Teachers are always absent, Classes are 30+ students, the system the have set up with their teachers teaching the middle schoolers & also the high schoolers seems to have them flustered and overworked. Currently looking for a charter school as a alternative or maybe a move out of the district. This school seems very educated and the teacher's sound great. I don't particularly know much about the school, but it seems like a great place to send my children This school is large and intimidating. The teachers are great. Like with any school you have some that maybe should take some time away, but over all I have had good experiences. I think that MORE parents need to be involved. Stop complaining and show you mean business if you want changes to be made!! This school is GREAT! My sister used to attend this school and had a 5.0 GPA in 11th-12th grade and a 4.0 in 8th-10th grade. She graduated and was accepted into many colleges with many scholarships. I now attend the school and am in 10th grade. I have been there since 7th grade and have had great experiences since. All the teachers are very helpful and actually care about each student equally. There are always fun events happening in the school. Since im in the Gifted MAGNET program I know that AP and Honors classes are great in academics. There are almost no bullies and everyone is welcome. Every day you learn so much from the revolving 4 classes out of 8 each day. I extremely recommend this school if you want your child to have great academic and fun experiences that will help them later on in life. I love this school! The academics, the students, the events, the clubs, the programs, the teachers, and the whole school itself is great. I took my two daughters out of Renarts because it was not academic at all, all the teachers were mean, the students were bullies, and overall it was terrible. I kept my son in Eagle Rock and he loved it so I put my daughters in there and they instantly made friends, had great grades, and enjoyed the rest of their time there. There are so many great things that the school has to offer. All I can say is terrific! Both my children recently graduated from ERHS and were accepted to colleges of their choice with excellent scholarships. They were groomed to be leaders and passed all of their 6to 8 AP courses. I love the school. They have tons of sports and clubs to join. I'm excited that my youngest will be starting ERHS in 7th next year. I'm in the 8th grade and I have made many friends in this very school I enjoy the teachers here c: I love the optional classes here But there may be bullies here and there if you dress in bands t-shirts or say bad things about people. The problem is that the only swim teacher (Mrs. Matsumura) makes me cover my clothing because she is to religious and is afraid of skulls, also has thought I was a satanist but I cleared that up other than that I'm perfectly fine with my school c: im impressed with my kids learning. they easily adjust to the curriculum and environment . they easily learn English and meet new friends. I'm hopeful that they may continue to encourage and support new students especially from different country! More Power and looking forward for more years of healthy happy and trusting relationship with parents teachers and students! What a gem of a school! Teachers and staff care and are very involved, despite the lack of funding challenges. We are so happy to have an exceptional education in a public LAUSD school. Our son is challenged and is encouraged to challenge himself in this intense IB curriculum. This review is long overdue. My kids transferred from Renaissance Arts to ERHS at just the right time - the older one was able to join the first cohort of IB Diploma Programme students. Do not be deterred by the large class sizes and cinder-block campus. As a neurotic with OCD, I have learned more than is healthy about pedagogy, testing, progressive education, K-12 education and higher ed in the US and across PISA test nations, etc. ERHS excels in everything that truly matters: devoted faculty and staff, a supportive, nurturing environment (no bullying that I know of), programming for every type of student, and frequent communication and transparency with parents. ERHS is a community school with loads of school spirit, rich in tradition. Generations of families have gone here.Go see for yourself. Talk to Mrs. Keipp, a dynamo of a principal who not only teaches a class and keeps abreast of trends and technologies while managing budget and personnel issues - but parents her own kids at school (oldest daughter now at Stanford). Check out the secret garden. Go to the Jr/Sr powderpuff football game.ERHS's track record speaks for itself. 4-yr college-bound kids don't just go on to the UCs, as great as they are. Despite being staffed by a single college counselor, ERHS regularly sends a couple of kids to Harvard and Brown and is making inroads into liberal arts colleges like Wellesley and Smith (Book Award for each) and Middlebury and Kenyon. The IB Coordinator, to whom we are indebted, goes out of his way to counsel kids for college placement, write recommendations and nominate students for scholarships such as Posse. This year alone there were 4 Posse Scholarships. RenArts is a great program, but the administration is run like a cult of personality with no thought to succession planning or professional development (as far as I can tell). And that's fine for the favored few. But ERHS truly stands by all of its students. Unlike NoHo Highly Gifted Magnet, which can afford to cherry pick the very brightest, ERHS exemplifies diversity in every dimension. And unlike LACES, you don't need to strategize magnet points from birth to get in. At ERHS, the ideals of public education are put into practice every day. ERHS is a beacon of hope and possibility within a beleaguered LAUSD. We hit the jackpot when we transferred to ERHS. Don't go here.My experience at this school is one I will always remember, and its terrible. Teachers teach nothing to students, I have about 1 effective teacher there. Some of my teachers speak too harshly about your opinions, and everyone at the school is generally mean and disrespectful if you are a different color or come from a different economical status.I come to school every day with a. fear of what bad thing will happen to me next.Don't send your kids here, I was influenced terribly by this school The school tried hard but it wasn't the right fit for my kid, who needs more guidance and individualized attention. If your kid is self-sufficient, he or she will do fine here. But if your kid needs reminders and guidance, he will not. They just have too many kids for that. I must give a shout-out to a GEM of a teacher here: Eric Jacobsen, who is the tennis coach and also teaches a class in Psychology. He is absolutely amazing - the kind of teacher they make movies about! If your kid is interested in tennis, you're lucky because Eric is the best thing about this school. He's super dedicated to the kids but he's also "cool" and they admire and respect him. He's reached the perfect balance between being understanding and kind -- but also setting high expectations. He works with each of the kids and cares deeply about them in all ways - makes sure they're keeping up with school work and not just playing tennis. I can't say enough about him; he's really a treasure. I think the teachers really want the kids to do well- they give them feedback when possible and they are made to feel they can talk to them about any issues. The Principal is in touch with the kids and is super approachable, has sent her kids to the school one of which got into Stanford, and greets kids outside the school. It feels like they are working as a team. horrible, inefficient, bully supporting, can't protect students I have not graduated yet, and I hope there is a lot of change here before I do. I love this school and some of the people here, but that does not forgive where the administration has failed. Eagle Rock is a good school with the rigorous IB DP program where students can opt in beginning in 11th grade. AP and honors courses are available to all students. Students get admitted to IVY Leagues, top notch private and public universities such as Yale, Stanford, Harvard, UCs, and Cal States, and other out-of-state colleges. The school also has the IB MYP program where students are suppose to complete the personal project their 10th grade year.The sports program is pretty good with teams and individuals winning championships and athletes drafted to play at universities throughout the country. Not bad for an underfunded LAUSD school.Eagle Rock has revamped their gyms and auditorium so it has been in continuous construction for the past 5 years. It’s beginning to look better but it needs a main building out in the front overlooking Yosemite Drive.Overall, it’s a good solid school with a team of educators who are trying to get it to an outstanding school.

column1: Both my children received an excellent education at Leland. Both went on to excellent private colleges where they excelled. My oldest, who graduated from Leland after attending K through 12th grade, was Valedictorian of her College. Leland offers caring teachers, a safe environment, small classes, technology, art, theater, sports, extracurricular activities and a first class learning environment. All schools should be this good! One daughter attend since Kindergarten (Now Graduated) and another is in 2nd grade. It is an outstanding school. At times, feels as if it is a private academy. Level of instruction and leadership is tops. Being an IBS school allows LPS to offer curriculum and opportunities for the students that are hard to find at other schools.

column3: 2 years for my younger granddaughter in this school and we pulled her out due to the horrible teachers at this school. While there are few teachers that do good, if your child gets stuck with a bad teacher for a certain course, it is quite difficult to get them with a good teacher. The counselors, or at least one that I have dealt with, seems to have little interest in the students. Most schools on the island are not so great, so we settled on online school which is a much better choice than any public school here. The teachers don't teach in a way that the students can understand and don't try to help you understand. I graduated very well-prepared for college at a selective liberal arts college on the mainland. The teachers were very supportive and dedicated. Downside - lots of slackers and druggies, and some major cliques. But once you find your groove/niche, it's easy to focus on that and stay away from that nonsense. I am very discouraged about this school. If the teachers decide that they do not like a student then they won't pass the student. Even if the student is really smart. Not a good way to go about teaching. If the teacher didn't like you, you weren't going to pass. Teachers would talk to certain students like they weren't even human or they were a complete waste of space. Teachers only wanted to deal with certain students. This school has definitely improved within the last few years. I notice some say that teachers would fail you if your were disliked, although I can’t completely disagree, the teachers would just give you a harder time but not fail. I faced very few bad experiences with teachers but based on what I heard from others, my recommendation would be to take a higher level classes to avoid these “bad” teachers. It may be intimidating but the courses material taught in honors is the same in regular, it may be taught faster and more in-depth, but you tend to get better teachers. Another thing while attending, if you participate with school activities and club, I believe you would have a better high school experience. The school has done a great job of transitioning my freshman student. Teachers gave been very responsive and caring. Very happy with the school.

column1: I can't really comment on ratings older than 5 years, but today this school is a nurturing and academically enriching environment for the students. Thanks in large part to Principal Williams, who is a strong positive role model and force for inclusion and excellence. Awesome job...keep up the good work!

column3: So far this school has provided academic support and really works with learning disabilities and support while still maintaining very high academic marks nationally . Quaint feeling and excellent clubs arts and sports . Excited to see how the last 3 years of our sons academic career turns out 10/10 to us ! Quaker Valley High School may be an excellent school for some students, but may not be for others. Most of the teachers, the academics and opportunities as well as the special education department are top notch! However, the bullying and harassment policy and protocol overall in the Quaker Valley School District as a whole, needs updated and revamped to match what is happening in today’s society amongst teens on school property and on social media. This is not just our family who feels this way. Student as well as Teacher training on how to notice, report and stop bullying in its tracks, as well as student advocacy against bullying in the high school above the freshman level is not up to par. Bullying should be dealt with in a timely manner in all school districts. Unfortunately, that is not always the case at QV. This is of the utmost importance with how a decent amount of students at the middle school and high school level mistreat their peers and can be beyond cruel to one another. All of our children have either been in private or public schools for over 18 years now. This includes 6 different school districts in 3 different states, encompassing city and non-city schools, so we have experience in very different environments and a with a wide diversity of students. Not all, but a good portion of students in the class of 2022 at QV High School are the worst class for bullying and harassment we have ever experienced in all these years. What a shame that many of the students act more like immature privileged middle schoolers only caring about themselves and not caring one bit about others or who they hurt, rather than young adults who should be respectful, responsible and compassionate human beings. Teach our Children Well in all aspects of life, not just education. They are the future.

column1: Both of my children have attended this school since kindergarten - going on 6 years now. I am extremely satisfied with the curriculum. The children learn to speak in front of their peers at daily chapel devotions that the children lead. I am very excited that this year they have expanded the curriculum to include Music, Bible and Spanish for the 5th and 6th graders - something sorely lacking. Teachers are warm and caring, front office is wonderful. I love that parents, kids and teachers all know each other and look out for each other.

column3: This school is not recommended period. They instituted a program called PLATO Recovery which allows students who should be held back a grade to proceed to the next grade and make up the work from the previous year. I found several of the teachers unhelpful and difficult to contact. The office staff is judgemental and rude. Once again signs of small town USA and not so inviting to newcomers. Very little communication between parents and teachers. Teachers and principals don't answer emails. You have to search out problems for yourself. No tutoring or extra help when needed. Teachers and principals are bulling kids more than their peers do. Counselors are the only source for communication and I do give the counselors more stars for their efforts. My yougest child attends one of the elementary schools and I'm happy with it but would like to move before he goes to high school because I'd rather he not go to this one!! My oldest daughter attended FCHS in the 2013-2014 school year. I was amazed at the lack of organization by the office staff. Almost every time I visited the school there were police at the school doing drug searches. My daughter was harassed by the male students. (told they were going to "do her" in the lunch room while pushing her on to a table) I eventually had to pull my daughter out of the school. When I went to clean out her locker I was harassed by the students also. I was shocked when the principle Dr. Grider seemed to care very little about why I was pulling my daughter out and very little about the way his students behaved. My Nephew is currently a Freshman at this school despite my warnings. His parents are already seeing a negative change in him. On top of all of this he was told by his coach that he needed to choose between sports or church. I also am close friends with one of the elementary teachers at MCS. she told me she would quit her job before she would teach or allow her kids to be at FCHS. I am all for kids experiencing the "real world" but this school is bad. After I pulled my daughter out of the school It took almost a year for my daughter to seem like herself again. Franklin County High School does a great job at helping students. They have implemented a class period for students to be able to go get help from the teachers every day. The teachers care about their students success.

column1: The best school in the county. The teachers won't leave anyone behind if they are willing to put in the time to get help. It's the best in the county. My son loves going there!

She is now only months away from graduation at Stockton and I thank Pennsville for providing her with the confidence, determination, and education she needed to succeed. My husband and I plus our children went to Pennsville school district. We all went to college and are successful in life. No good and bullying so not a great school

column1: I don't have much to say, i just know that I have progressed in my education far more than I have in any other school I have attended. The friends here are great! The extra-curricular activities are endless as well as rewarded. I just know that if I were to do it all over again I would still have picked Joliet High School. As a student, I love it here!

column3: Administrators and teachers are difficult to work with. Important issues discussed seem to be a joke between administrators, teachers, and office staff. Non professional environment. Spanish Fork is an older school competing with two newer schools that just opened and calved off of it. This has left many of their previously strong programs to practically start over as they assemble staff and students. Nevertheless, the remaining staff has been up to the challenge and we feel that our children are getting a great education with many strong scholastic opportunities (concurrent university enrollment, AP courses, science olympiad, etc.) and well-supported and enthusiastic extracurriculars (music, sports, etc.). Spanish Fork High School is awesome! Everyone is so peppy and cheerful, but not in an annoying way. All of the classes are pretty easy, and the teachers always double check and ask if anyone doesn't get the material. We have amazing sports programs and an outstanding drama department. Also we have great band and orchestra and choir and and and everything departments an opportunities. Along with concurrent enrollment opportunities and many honors and AP courses. Overall, an outstanding school. Its great, everyone is really nice. The sports are really good, the teachers are really understanding and good at listening. It's just a really good experience.

column1: There is nothing great about this school. The academics are low especially in Math. Look at the school profile to see how poorly students perform in the state wide standards test called CAPT. The trades offered at this school are not 21st century trades. There is no health care trade at all...one of the largest growing areas in employment. If you want your child to become a brick layer then send him or her to this school. If you want your child to be prepared for a successful college experience there are truly great schools in the area. Henry Abbott Tech is not one of them. Abbott Technical High School is an outstanding school and has amazing academic and shop staff that work very closely with the students. They have just opened a Health Technology program, which I am currently apart of, and the program puts you on the right track to your health care career. The program will certify you to become a CNA ( Certified Nurses Assistant ) during your junior year, and also certifies you in CPR. Overall, the new program is an amazing learning experience, and the teacher will work to make sure you fully understand and retain the information. Henry Abbott Technical High is truly the " #1 School on the Planet". The teachers here are ok, the school administration are not great. . I I would suggest checking out other local Technical schools such as Obrien, Vinal, Plat or Kaynor first. Sometimes location isn't everything. Well as students, we hardly learn anything there. I know that some shops have gone through teachers and we're stuck with subs for a good part of the year too. Administration tends to be rough on the students, especially the head principal. In my opinion the schools rating should be a one. A four is overly generous. Food is terrible wouldn't even want to feed it to my dog. Academics is bad most teachers don't care about there jobs. Administration is just as bad as well they don't care about the students opinions and punish harshly. Clubs and activities forget it there are hardly any clubs at all and most activities get cancelled due to lack in student participation. The technical side of it some teachers in there are good but others don't care at all. If you think you'd like to go to college and a good school academically do not go to this school. As a parent my son attended Danbury High School during 9th grade. He really learned very little/nothing during class time. There were many fights during and after school. There were just too many children, too many drugs. We are pleased with Abbott Tech. It is not a perfect school and need to improve their academics and shop classes. Abbott Tech is a wonderful place for students to learn a trade and begin their careers as skilled tradespeople with no debt. If students choose to pursue college, they are prepared. Some of the trades encourage college after graduation; however, the majority of the students are placed in lucrative positions upon graduation, not minimum wage jobs. Henry Abbott is a community--its small size allows all students and faculty to know each other and support each other in academics and social forums. Connecticut is in great need of skilled tradespeople, and Henry Abbott is proud to provide working adults to fill this need. A true testament to the value of the education received at Henry Abbott is the connection and dedication of alumni to the school. They are invaluable in their generosity to the students and often hire many graduates. as a parent of a current 10th grader, the teachers are very involved and work hard to keep the kids on track and put in lots of extra effort to help the kids. I also have a student at Danbury High School and do not feel the DHS has the same type of relationship with the kids. He is happy and learning a lot in his trade and has lots of opportunities to participate in after school activities, not as many as the local high school for sure but it seems the last couple of years Abbott is adding more and more after school clubs. I am very pleased that he was accepted at Abbott and feel he has more opportunities for success after high school. Abbott is like an extended family. They have been so wonderful to students and really seem to care. School was using ALEKS for their math program which was terrible but switched back to traditional teaching last year. Honors Academic courses vary in how challenging they are, science needs improvement. The VP also became the Principal which has been a great improvement. School is a small community and a good alternative to DHS, which is extremely overcrowded, for the average student . Lacks after school activities but that is primarily because students are bused from neighboring cities and if they do not have private transportation they cannot participate.

column3: I absolutely loved this school and most of the people, most of the teachers are nice and outgoing, and the school isn't massive and its easy to navigate through. The hallways are a little crowded but you get used to it. The kids there are a little stuck-up but it just depends on who you're hanging out with. Most of the kids there are nice, funny, and friendly, but some of them aren't so nice and always think about their image. I never felt adequately prepared for life after high school, either college or entering the real world in general. I had great relationships with a few teachers and my school counselor; there are some truly amazing educators that teach/have taught at this school. I rarely thought about what college or my career would look like after high school and I felt the school didn't much care whether I had a plan after graduation or not. My parents talked to me about college and a career but without the support from the school it just felt futile. I did graduate college and enter a career path I'm proud of, but it was despite going to school here and not because of it. I'm to the age now where I'm hoping my kid's school cares and motivates them to continue their education, gives them the tools necessary for a successful future, and helps prepare them for life after high school. I don't feel Lewis Central did that for me. Lewis Central set me up for the road to success both academically and personally. As a former Titan, the relationships that I was able to foster with both the students and administration I still hold dear years later. The curriculum challenges students to think outside the box while using the most advanced technologies out there.The teachers, administration, and staff go above and beyond the call of duty to help their students in any way possible to meet and achieve their needs, as well as confidently continue their success in college. The teacher to student ratio is low and overall the school is big enough to compete against other large schools; however, small enough for everyone to know each other's name. As biased as this may sound, I feel that this school is the best in the metro hands down.

column1: Fantastic school that really cares about the overall development of its students, including their spiritual well-being. Besides many strong sports programs, it has a very professional Drama department that develops extremely high quality productions of musicals and plays each year. nazareth is a fantastic school for academics. HOWEVER, the students are not very kind or open to many different people. My daughter is shy and was not excepted at nazareth and it saddened me deeply because she loved the school but the students never warmed up to her. I suggest if you do not have designer things or let your child party i suggest not letting them attend because they will not be excepted by their peers. Nazareth is one of the most accepting and open schools I've ever seen! I was really nervous to go to Naz because I didn't know many people. But thanks to the tons of sports and activities I did, my friends came right to me! The other statement about not being accepted if you don't "party" is completely wrong. I refuse to drink and party like that and I have the best friends a guy can ask for. Nazareth Academy is a phenomenal school! No matter who you are, you can always find your niche here. Speaking from personal experience, I never had to have designer things or party hard in order to be accepted! I was a band geek and a science nerd how much more of an outcast can you be? Yet I still ended up with TONS of friends and an overcrowded phonebook! In fact, Nazareth s students and faculty are akin to a very large and supportive family. Offering a myriad of extracurricular activities and sports, I promise you that, here at Naz, you will never get bored. If you re a smarty-pants like myself, it is a wonderful school academic wise, consisting of challenging courses and resourceful teachers and staff. If, like the student of the parent who posted her review on 1/1/11, you are a student and finding a hard time getting to know people or struggling with friends, classes, or any other kind of stress, Nazareth has a fabulous guidance staff at your service! I cannot tell you just how helpful these staff members are, especially when you are applying to college. You just must see for yourself! If you are at all interested in this school, I highly recommend a visit! :) As a recent former student, I would not recommend Nazareth. It was super cliquey (rich popular kids vs. poorer kids) and just a pretty bad experience all together. Unlike some of the surrounding public and private schools, most years students don't get into any Ivy League schools and mainly stick to schools in the Midwest. I really enjoyed my college experience, but I would definitely not send my children here. Agree with the comment below - not a very good school and cliquey. For a private school, the college acceptance list is pretty poor and local, with a few exceptions. Also not very diverse at all. Personally, I'm not a very big fan. There are so many better options than Naz. On the plus side, the teachers are very liberal and accepting. I have to say, my daughter and son have found Naz to be great. There are different groups of friends, but as far as "cliques" go, try finding a HS that does not have that. There are wealthy kids, middle class kids and struggling families. We are one of the struggling families and I have never found anything but kindness and respect for the school, teachers and students. My daughter and son would agree. Stellar academics, compassionate staff and a wonderful, faithful community. I made a huge mistake going here. I am currently a junior and I absolutely hate it at Naz. They are ridiculous. They are starting forced consent drug tests, and to me, naz is not nearly a good enough school to do this. I didn't agree to this when I chose to attend naz and it deeply saddens me to think about what will happen when naz realizes half the school is actually on drugs. Nazareth is very fake, the only nice parts of the school are the parts that parents will see. The administration is terrible and they treat students with no respect unless they are an honors student etc. Students get into mostly local colleges. Going to naz is not worth the money you will pay. The students here treat each other terribly and it is not the "second home" that they claim to be. column1: The teachers care about not only allowing the students to grow academically, but as good citizens in the community as well. The only way you have a negative experience at this school is if your children are disrespectful, and show no effort in the classroom. One down fall is the now constant influx of low income scum moving in due to free housing that is offered (such as the gentleman who blamed the district on his addiction, and jail time below). Overall my experience at this school was positive. There is a positive environment with many great people. Unfortunately the school gets a poor reputation from the not so obedient minority. There are some areas that could be improved upon such as the a ratio of required graduating credits. It is odd that science only requires three credits while the other core subjects require four. Science is arguably one of the largest growing fields right now so that should be a more primary focus. There are also limits to what classes are available. For a small school it can be difficult to fill a class with students if it is not required. However AP biology is not available and I do not know if it is possible to take on Bulldog Academy. As for sports, the main sports of our school thrive with highly talented athletes who break records and achieve great things. The selection of sports is smaller than larger schools such as not having volleyball or tennis. This issue is not that big of a deal though. The music department could use a little bit of help. The marching band keeps winning with the little that they have but needs more support in order to gain members. The choir can never hold a director for an extended period of time. The band director works more than anybody could ever imagine. By having two band directors, it would be easier to develop the middle school and high school band separately. Or maybe the extra director could lead an orchestra. Almost every other nearby district has an orchestra and I feel that it could broaden the horizons of students. There are many places to build leadership and teamwork skills. With the variety of clubs open at this school there is no way you can’t find something to join. Recently a computer programming club was developed by a group of students who felt that this should be implemented into the school. The administration is highly supportive of students exploring their options when it comes to hobbies or skills.

column3: i graduated from PHS in 1972. my parents chose to live in pitman because of the high quality of the schools. at the time, the teacher-student ratio was about 20-1. most of the teachers had masters degrees. advanced placement classes were plentiful. the total enrollment for the high school was about 550 students. no school buses, ever! i'm grateful that i received a very high quality public school education. the teachers knew their stuff and there was a very fair sense of discipline in the school. teachers tolerated student BS up to a point, but if someone "crossed the line," they were dealt with appropriately. i don't have children, but back then, i knew better than to get into trouble at school. i trust this information, though dated, proves helpful. I am a current student. The teachers are great! They are challenging, fair and caring. The computers are always breaking down though and the computer techs are no where to be found. Great school, but cannot afford good technology or get good people to fix computers. Other than that, I love everything about this place. This is one of the worst high schools around. Horrible teachers, administration, curriculum and students - switched mine to GCIT. Lovely small school where personalized attention makes all the difference. It's a community school where everyone knows each other. The small size allows students to get to know their teachers, administrators, and bond with classmates. Kids walk and bike to school. We are very happy to not be at a large school. Pitman schools were good in the 1970's. Lots of townies seem to think today is still 1976. The schools today are a bit run down, especially PHS. The teachers are not as talented. Students do not perform well on standardized tests. Ask yourself this. How can a homogeneous town like Pitman which is largely upper middle class with few reduced lunches do so poorly on the state tests? Who knows? It's embarrassing. PHS should be closed and our kids bused to Clearview.

column1: All of my teachers (except for one and she has been sick) are exceptional! They are caring, hard working and good people. I have worked hard and learned a lot! No problems! It's similar to many urban schools...lack of funding sometimes, but that's everywhere these days with President Obama & the Common Core gang. You naje do with what you have & RHS has done just that with thriving local business/school partnerships. A lot of that was because of the opportunities I was given there. It's only bad if you don't take advantage of those opportunities. There are great teachers and students that treat each other like family and with respect. In my four years, I've never had a problem with anybody at Joe T. column3: You can receive a great education there! My second child started Western Guilford this year. My oldest child graduated in 2009 second in her class. My oldest got in her first choice college and is graduating one semester early from college due to AP classes at WGHS. Both girls made great transitions from middle school and love all the opportunities for female sport teams and the variety of clubs and service learning. We also enjoy all the cultural diversity and family feeling of the school for students and parents, We have had three children attend Western and our youngest is now a freshman. They have all had a great experience. There is a diverse population with an atmosphere where students feel accepted and that is warm and supportive. Western students are service oriented. There is positive school spirit and parental support with a pizza dinner to welcome freshmen and their families, tailgating before football games, spirit week and events throughout the school year. Our children have each taken 10 AP classes and had strong teachers. Our freshman is taking a zero period to enable her to take AP Human Geography. They have also played varsity sports and been involved in school organizations. Our older two graduated in 2008 and 2011, have graduated from Vanderbilt and are attending UNC-Chapel Hill and were accepted to other competitive colleges. The principal is very enthusiastic and committed to the school. Our children have been happy and we have been pleased at Western Guilford High School. Our school not only surpasses the others we have toured in the academic sense; Western also far exceeds them in 'customer service', promoting a welcoming, positive environment to everyone; prospective and current students, parents, and to the staff. From the top down, everyone wants to be a part of the growth and excitement at WGHS. With the arrival of a new principal over three years ago, the entire school atmosphere is charged and the enthusiasm is contagious. Communication is key at Western. This is the school to choose if you want not only rigorous AP classes where your child is challenged and able to receive incredible scholarship dollars with top college acceptances- but also, the school where ALL students and their families are treated with respect and genuine concern for their well being, Your input and suggestions matter. Our sophomore is thriving here; academically and in sports and service. PTSO encourages involvement; from tailgates to art shows - you are welcomed here. Stop by for a visit; you'll see. The things that matter most for a well rounded student are here. We love attending our 'neighborhood school' knowing that it is the best kept secret in town. This is a great school. The Principal, Administrators, Staff and Teachers create a really rich learning environment. They combine concern for the students with high academic expectations to make this a great place for my children to attend high school. As the parent of a senior and a freshman, I cannot imagine sending my children to any other high school in this city. It is a small, close-knit community where students can shine and rise to their individual potential in a safe environment without being a number. The teachers and administration seem to know all of the students and truly care about their success. We are pleased with the high number of AP course offerings (and success rates on the AP tests) as well as the extracurriculars available to our students. For those interested in music, our band/orchestra and choral teachers are top-notch and the students love them. We feel like Western is one of the best-kept secrets in Guilford County. This is the fifth year I have had 1 to 3 students at WGHS. I have watched the school go from a school that was overlooked by the county for reasons it deserved to a school that continues to strive to build itself up and achieve at the highest levels along with many other schools in the area, yet continue to be overlooked. The teachers who were here just resting were removed and replaced with those interested in helping our children in reaching their highest potential. The Principal, the staff, the PTSO and the Families at large work hard to improve this school and find ways to assist our students with their academic, technical, athletic, musical and artistic achievements. I have two children currently attending Western High school and one who graduated last year. We have been very satisfied with the education that our children have been receiving. I have found the administration and staff very efficient and willing to listen. The teachers are very supportive and offer free tutoring after school if needed by students. My children enjoy the diversity in our school and they feel like they know everyone. I highly recommend Western Guilford to everyone! There are not enough words to describe how pleased I am with Western. This is our 4th year there. We have an incredible principal and a staff that is willing to make Western the best high school in the state. It is a very close knit community and a place that is very easy to get involved. I have two sons at Western and they love it. There are plenty of clubs and sports and other ways to get involved. We also have a great selection of classes to choose from at the AP level. Come take a tour and see for yourself that Western Guilford is a school that can't be beat. I'm a 2008 grad. Mr. Armstrong was the principal then, his 2nd year I think. He was phenomenal, really got to know the students and didn't let any BS slide with students or teachers. Hopefully he's still there or has gone up county the administration ladder. I had some great teachers who I hope are still there--Mrs. Wilson for French, Mrs. Rose for AP English 12, Mrs. Culclasure for AP English 11, Gordon for AP US History, Coach Wilson for Marketing, and every art teacher I ever had there. Alot of people in my class including myself got into top universities such as UVA, Duke, Chapel Hill, Vanderbilt, etc. There are many sports, clubs, and leadership opportunities. My one complaint is not a lot of emphasis on the arts; well, let me say, not a lot of diversity. The guidance counselors' didn't help any more than the internet did when applying to colleges. Also the class set up changed from Block (4 different 90-minute classes per semester) to traditional (6 55-minute classes all year) for my junior and senior year, which kind of messed up some of my class plans. Overall great school if you use every resource available, and there are plenty. The Math department at Western has been struggling for the past few years, which is apparent in the school's well below par math scores. Pre-calculus, calculus and statistics classes desperately need much more qualified teachers. The school has the students with interest and motivation, but the Math department has yet to find good teachers. French 4 is a joke and the students teach themselves in the back of the classroom during a lower level class. The English, Social Studies and History departments are strong. This is a school with a very diverse population, ethnically and socioeconomically, so we struggle for the resources to meet the needs of our diverse population. Western is a school on the rise with a strong administration and and active PTSO. Many teachers and coaches are dedicated to their students education and willing to go the extra mile to encourage them to succeed. The guidance department offered little help with college applications, no more than was already available on the internet, and did not send transcripts and reports to colleges when asked by the student and by the parent. We had to be informed by the college they did not receive the information and we had to request it again. Overall, a good school but guidance needs to step it up for high achieving students. Just moved to the district and have heard terrific things! Previous students spoke highly of the school and articulated their points clearly. My son is a student in the A.P. Academy at Western High. This is an outstanding program in a top-notch school. We bought our current house in order to be in the Kernodle Middle School district (it had just been named among the top 100 middle schools in the nation). Gaining the new AP Academy in our districted high school last year was just a bonus. Guilford County has many magnet programs and this one received the most applications last year. The principal at Western High is the best I've ever seen. He truly cares about each student and he advocates on their behalf. Mr. Kashubara attracts great teachers who are committed to excellence in the classroom. As a U.Va. grad, I was looking for a school with a strong track record among both in-state and out of state college admissions officers. Western High is among the top three high schools in the county in this regard. Most dysfunctional high school in Greensboro. Do yourself a favor and do not send your children here.You've been warned. My special needs sister was bullied physically and mentally by students and staff, and students purposeful targeting of her with her service dog was ignored by staff

column1: I've heard numerous comments about this school, and 99% of has been more than pleasing. One thing I'm worried about is if there is a lot of homework for the student? Too much homework isn't healthy at all! This school is very excellent in the academic level. I am a student who is attending St. Vincent Ferrer and I have to say it is quite amazing how the students interact with each other. It has a very nice atmosphere. I truly believe if you are thinking of putting your daughter in a very good academic private high school choose SVF. This school is amazing! I am attending Saint Vincent Ferrer and I love it. There are so many clubs, sports, and activities. The teachers are very nice. Your daughter would be very happy at SVF Saint Vincent Ferrer is an incredible school. Teachers are amazing-the science program has to be one of the best in the city! The Pricipal is a leader who creates a community that includes everyone. Bullying is not tolerated and respect for others is always mention by the school administration. School is safe as could be and is in a gorgeous area of Manhattan. I was impressed with the school getting involved with a sister school in Africa. The school building is spacious, with a new gym, smart boards, computers, and always being maintained and improved. Each year the girls go on trips all over the world and my daughter has come back with a much broader perspective! My daughter is a happy kid whose friends actually say hello when they see me. If you want your child to be in a friendly, SAFE school that cares about others and teaches the girls that success is through education-Saint VIncent Ferrer is the place. I'm a Senior at St. Vincent Ferrer, and i absolutley love it. This school is made for girls who want to succeed in life, not just succeeding in memorizing notes to pass a class. The work is challenging and in no way an "easy A". Homework, as mentioned in a previous comment, can sometimes be demanding, but it's not overwhelming. Another great thing concerning homework and study, is that classes are set up so that there is a rotating schedule of assigned testing days each subject has. i've never had more than two tests in a day, nor has any girl here at Ferrer. I've taken both Honors and AP classes, and i must say i've never felt like school work was the only thing on my mind 24/7, I mean, there are 5 sports teams and 27 clubs, something's always hopping at Ferrer! this school has the best science department, if you have DR. Kumar, you'll be great, he is an excellent teacher. Academically, Ferrer is wonderful. There are a couple teachers who press students a bit too hard, but a majority of the teachers are willing to work with you continually until you reach an understanding, rather than say that "grades don't matter, you understand by failing."However, the school's bulling policy is horrid. Leave it at, they do not believe in dignity for all students. My friend has been bullied a lot, and the school has done nothing about it. I miss her. She never had anxiety before what has been happening. Many girls have transferred out of my school because of how bad the bulling is. They have an extremely high admission deposit of $1,000.00 to hold a spot for your daughter in the freshman class. Make sure your daughter is going to attend this school. If you and your daughter decide that she will attend and go to another high school, this money will NOT be returned! As a freshman and part of the Class of 2018, I have waited until the second semester to write a full review. I can honestly say that this school is way better than I had imagined. I take honors classes and an advanced language course. Academically I will not say I'm being challenged to where I cannot handle it, I have always been a very good student. The load of the work, however is very heavy. You must study and do your homework to understand what you are doing in class, the teachers (at least the honor classes) will not spoon feed you the material. If you're not a studious and well balanced I do not suggest you attend this school. You have many chances to make friends, become integrated in a club, and have a social life. The only downside would be that there aren't many healthy choices for snacks or lunch, its usually fried things or very oily. There are salads and yogurts available, but no one would reach for that when you have delicious muffins and cookies available. If you rather not learn go to another school, Cathedral is nearby. If you want to be more socially active go to another school, like Notre Dame. I'm a parent to a freshman, who is apart of the class of 2018. I have another daughter who is a senior this year who will be graduating in the next month. To be completely honest I was so happy with this school when my daughter who is a senior, was first starting out. Now that my other daughter is a freshman this school has definitely degraded and the students are held on a standard if they are a freshman, sophomore, junior, senior. I would expect that from a public school not from a catholic school. Everything is a double standard and the rules for one have become more strict and a lot more ridiculous. The students are not heard and not listened to and neither are the parents. If you want to deal with the aggravation go ahead and send your daughter here. I wouldn't recommend it. My daughter who is a freshman gets at least four hours of homework and is in no honors classes. So far my daughter and I are so disappointed with the school and some of the faculty. This school came highly recommended and we were so excited that she was going there but that has changed. Let me start by stating that my daughter is no stranger to the catholic school system. She has attended since kindergarten but since coming here her views have changed a bit. She doesn't feel supported is willing to travel to a school father away with hopes of getting better support and a better phys Ed program. Also I find there is no effort from the teachers or the principal to support the freshman (I'm trying to be general in hopes that my daughter isn't being picked on). And that's only one issue. There are many more limitations unfortunately. Favoritism is rampant unfortunately. The academics are decent but teaching styles are not always great; they do offer after school help for some subjects which is good. They also don't alway have room in the honors classes for all eligible students so a student may miss out on the opportunity to be challenged which I feel is unfair. In my opinion this is not a great school. It's just an ok one. We are again, very disappointed. First, Saint Vincent Ferrer is not an easy school. You will be academically challenged, especially if you plan on taking advanced courses, but there will always be various forms of aid to guide you. Most of the teachers are extremely willing to go above and beyond to help their students. Furthermore, it offers a wide array of extracurricular activities. There are various opportunities for students to be involved in not only the school, but also the community. Thus, there will never be a secluded student in this school, and you will never find a more welcoming environment. My daughter has thrived at Saint Vincent Ferrer. It is a wonderful school with great, caring teachers. My daughter has met and befriended a lot of great girls and she loves going to school. The work is challenging but the teachers provide great support. This is a very goods school education wise. However the kids are very clique oriented and the school inclusion policy is not enforced. There was a safety issue this year concerning the lives of students and faculty. God only knows if the person who made the threat was ever found. Ok. So I am a senior at SVF. I want to warn anyone who comes to this school. First clubs, there are clubs at SVF but they hardly meet. There might as well be no clubs. I was in the science club last year and this year we wanted to have it again but because the teachers running the program didn't care it just went under. The only clubs that meet are either pushed my the teacher in charge or the students themselves meet up and talk. So don't believe it when the school says they have clubs. Next sports, I actually was on the teams in volleyball and basketball so I know a bit of how things work. The good: the girls on the team do tend to have a strong bond and they play great. The bad: no one besides the girls on the team and there friends care about sports in our school. Since I was on the team I had to go to most of the games and literally there was no one ever present at games. I felt so bad because the girls would work hard and yet no one would ever come to the games. That being said the teams did win a lot so that's good but unless you were part of the team no one cared. Sports didn't really matter at SVF. Next teachers, ok so a few teachers out there actually care about you and want you to succeed (Mr. Smithers, Mr. Peck) but most teachers you could tell just come for the paycheck. They give you homework and test and then that's it. I know the school says they have after school tutoring and all that. The problem with that is that no one ever goes. Literally the tutors (which are SVF girls) sit there and wait maybe 10 minutes and if no one comes they leave. One time I needed help in Algebra 2/ Trig I went to see if the tutor was there and nope no one was there. The grading system seems so corrupt at SVF. If you get a awesome grade your average would only go up like 3 points but if you screw up and fail something your grade goes down 20 points. No lie this has happened to me. Also your schedule...Ok so during your freshman and sophomore years you take the basic courses so you schedule doesn't really matter. When it comes to your junior and senior year however it matters. The school does not care about what classes you need to take and what classes you don't. My friend for instance didn't need to take music because she was done with her art credits and guess what they gave her. Now she tried to back out of the class but they said no. I had a fantastic experience attending Saint Vincent Ferrer. I was accepted to many great colleges and I am now starting law school. (SVF class of 2013) terrible, i have learnt nothing over the last 3 years This place is ridiculous; the girls are being tortured. Both finals and regents are required of the students. Finals or regents must be chosen by this school. As a private school, they should not give the girls regents because it is meaningless and useless, and it is essentially a public school thing. Ferrer is the only private school that takes regents from a few other schools. They don't give a damn about the girls' mental wellbeing. Girls at Ferrer should not be given regents because they are being given finals. The principal won't allow projects, so finals can only be tests. She has to improve. I'm sorry for the girls. They have to endure so much and suffer so much. Ferrer is beginning to look like a public school. I would not send my dead cat to this school. There are no zero star options.
