column3: This is an exceptional school. It offers so many dual credit college/high school AP classes. This helps many kids who otherwise would not have the confidence or money to go to college to get a headstart. It really helped me, as well as my siblings. Don't let the 'small town' status of Eureka deceive you. It has many over educated, well traveled teachers. This school is great, academically, but they're way too involved and centered around sports teams. I played for the Varstiy football team last year, in which we went 2-7. We haven't made the playoffs since 2007. With that, they bought brand new bleachers, a new track, new football uniforms, and yet, couldn't meet requirements on the Special Ed programs, which my little sister is in, cutback, force retired, fired, and/or transferred Special Ed/Alternative Ed teachers, within the last 4 years. Our textbooks are falling apart and outdated to the point, where our math teachers must duct tape books back together. They also do not pay enough attention to the low grade students, as they just put them in APEX classes and/or put them in classes that allows you to earn all the credits you need to graduate, in one school year, My friend, Alex, is earning 9 credits by this. She's a senior and is 9 credits shy of graduating as she transferred from Normal West, by getting expelled. I do not recommend parents' with lower GPA and/or credit kids to come here, to reach their potential. They'll just pass them on and not even try to work with them. Most teacher's however, are exceptional and qaulified

column1: My school is nothing I expected it to be... while all the performing arts programs are pretty good, the students are TERRIBLE. Most of them aren't even there for performing arts and don't have a major. Luckily those kids say they're transferring (fingers crossed). Academically, my school is ... challenging. Only because your facing challenges by yourself because teachers "are not allowed" to help students during independent practice, which i understand because it's "independent practice" , but a little guidance won't hurt. The teachers also show ALOT of favoritism... it can be really bad sometimes. Personally , the only thing keeping me in that school is my performing art & I've spoken to other students that say the same thing. My son graduated from this school in 2014 and is now going to Harvard university! This shows that even though it has a low grade kids are able to do there best. the fact that your child doesn't get enough or any homework at all is crazy because I've gotten so much homework going to this school,the teachers cares so much for these students and always pushes them to do better every time.

column3: My ninth grade daughter just completed first-term finals. The curriculum is challenging, and the teachers and staff are supportive. my children went to Catholic private elementary and middle schools so this was our first real experience of public school. We did an out of district transfer to John swett school district based on the high rating this school was getting. My child was very nervous in the first week but two years on, i can tell you it was the best decision i made. The teachers are dedicated and fun. Admin headed by a very motivated principal are courteous and helpful. Discipline is quite amazingly implemented.I would recommend this school to anyone who does not want to pay close to $65,000 for four years of private high school and still get a wonderful education for their kids.

column1: Great, small school where we have wonderful teachers and administrators. State scores would be higher bur with a school that is 80% Spanish, many of whom do not want to learn, or their parents do not want to learn, lowers the Americans scores. We have had to lengthen he Christmas break because when many return to Mexico for the break, they stay longer than the three weeks off. With this action comes a lose of funding by the state as schools are paid, I believe, $30 for everyday the student is present in school. Lost funding and low interest in learning the English language have hurt our school. THE WORST I WISH THE STATE COULD TAKE OVER THIS SCHOOL AND MAKE A DIFFERENCE TO OUR STUDENTS, I AS A PARENT CARE OF MY KIDS EDUCATION. WHE HAVE BEEN TRYING SO MUCH TO GET RID OF OUR SUPERINTENDENT AND NOTHING HAS WORKED WE WILL SOON LOOSE ABOUTH 15 GOOD TEACHERS DO TO THIS SITUATION.

column3: I graduated in 2010, and am now a student at UF. I came back from China in 2007, and missed my freshman year. However I still had an awesome time at Boca High, the staff was friendly, the study environment superb, and the overall experience was fantastic. I will always miss coming in on LTM days still covered in sand from spearfishing. Good times, Good memories. Dr. McKee and his leadership team are very amazing educators and know each and every student at their school. VERY IMPRESSIVE.... They actually stop by every class every day.... They are out in the courtyard and are proactive.... I still can't believe I had the pleasure to work here... i transfered from Calvary Christian Academy to come to boca high 1 month in the school year, i immidiatly felt comfortable, and the staff and principle are great! i wish i would have started at boca my freshman year instead of waiting til my junior year to make a change. I LOVE this school! I have very mixed opinions about the school. My son has some teachers who get back to me promptly and are very available, but he has others who will only get back to me after multiple requests when I have had to bump up the issue to my son's dean. I don't understand how the administration lets the poor teachers stay, and it must be disheartening for the teachers who do a good job. My son had a teacher who would tell the students that their questions were "self explanatory" and would refuse to answer them. When I reported this, everyone I spoke to was well aware that the teacher did this and no one seemed to care. I would say it is the luck of the draw, if you get good teachers, you will have a great year. If you have bad teachers you'll have a bad year and your complaints will be met with indifference. Odds are you will have a combination of good and bad teachers and you will have a mixed year. This seems to be the situation for every kid we know at Boca High regardless of grade and the types of classes taken. wonderful school - like a liberal arts college in its depth, from science to art to sports. spirit of cooperation seems to be well taught and observed, as well. plus great parental involvement very pleased parent I was impressed of the school staff and organization. My son just graduated. A great school to motivate kids to excel! Best high school imaginable! Every type of student is there and everyone gets along as if family. The teachers and staff model respect and love for the students. Students try their best and challenge themselves all the time, knowing that they'll have support if they don't succeed. The performing arts, sports, and service clubs are amazing. There is something great happening at Boca High every day and every night. Over 100 kids got into UF from Boca High last year. That is the most from any high school in the world! Boca High students get into Harvard and many other top schools every year, too. I wish I had the chance to go to a high school like this! The students are getting experiences that they will never forget, and that will help them be successful all their lives. Thank you teachers and staff members for creating a school where my children love to go! Our two sons were fortunate enough to attend Spanish River Christian School and go on to Boca Raton Community High. SRCS prepared them well for high school and BRCH prepared them extremely well for college. Both are doing great in college due to the foundation provided by these two schools. BOCA HIGH IS THE BEST! I will be a sophomore this year, and I can honestly say that by joining the STEM program; this school gives me opportunities such as taking AICE, AP, and dual enrollment courses. :)~Class of 2018 Best four years of my life. everyone at the school wants to see you succeed. Our last child just graduated. When he started, Dr. McKee was at the helm. He led the school from a very poor rating to A ratings for years. Unfortunately, he left the school and it's not the same with Dr. King. The deans are meh. The kids are never heard when there is an issue; they always take the teacher's side. Homework is not always posted. It is SO overcrowded even with the addition of a second lunch. I think I was more excited than my youngest when she graduated. There are some great teachers and there are some teachers that need a sabbatical - perhaps even a permanent one! Communication between parents and teachers is horrible. Ditto between the school and parents. As with many things in life, the hype is much more than the reality. I'm not sure what planet the other reviewers live on, nor GreatSchools.org, but this high school is tops! We moved into this area specifically for Boca High for our daughter. I have been involved with the school for four years, the last two with my daughter in attendance. The programs are stellar and they offer all the tools necessary to be successful at the next level. MOST IMPORTANT is the climate and atmosphere at the school are super safe, super friendly, and there are no "clicks" or "social groups" that get in the way of learning and friendships. Zero fights, zero bullying. Teachers: unbelievably smart and dedicated to their courses and students. To me this school is an 11 both academically and socially. How it is graded a 7 is beyond me. Great experience all around. Ms. Pam in the ESE department has been so helpful getting my son started and my other two children graduated with college credits because of the availability of lots of AP classes for them. Recommend! Great experience excellent AP and Cambridge AICE programs. Excellent school atmosphere. Counsellors are very supportive.

column1: Love this school! Teachers are great and always pushing students to do the best that they can. Bonner Springs High School is a wonderful school with great teachers. The size of the school allows students to have multiple opportunities to try sports, clubs, and activities. BSHS is in a great community with wonderful teachers. They really care about the kids. I am a graduate of BSHS and 3 of my 4 kids are currently enrolled in the district. Great schools, caring teachers & great community. I have had two children graduate from BSHS. Both earned scholarships to college and entered college with an entire year of college completed by taking college credits in high school. The dual credit program saved us thousands of dollars. The community is so invested in this school district, which is obvious over &60,000 in Local scholarships offered to BSHS graduates! We have a great student body, a dedicated staff and an involved community. The Bonner Springs-Edwardsville School District is a great place to live and work! BSHS has so many offerings to prepare our students for their next level. We have a wide variety of CTE courses, as well as college prep classes. I am proud to be a part of BSHS, and the Bonner Springs community. I am an alum, and teacher at Bonner Springs High School. I have seen how the school has transformed in the last 3 years and I am very proud. I would send my own children to Bonner Springs High School above surrounding schools. BSHS is a college prep/career ready school. Bonner Springs offers 17 CTE pathways, many leading to certification in the new B-TEC building. Bonner Springs also offers 51 dual credit hours for college. They are truly preparing students for post-high school success. Students graduate from Bonner Springs High School with many college credits or certifications in a specific career field already under their belt.Bonner Springs is a progressive learning school; the teachers are young and bringing new innovative methods from the fast changing world into the classroom. They have created such a great culture at Bonner. BSHS is a trauma informed school, bringing healing to students with trauma. This prepares them to be successful adults. Bonner Springs truly has something for each student with the number of activities, clubs, and sports that they offer.The schools are state of the art, with recent renovations/new construction throughout the district. The students have labs, and spaces to learn in progressive ways. Bonner Springs has put students first since the new administration change in 2016. They offer ACT prep courses during the school day, among numerous other preparation Seminars. The ACT composite score, and state test scores have risen significantly above state averages in the past 4 years. I am very proud to be a Brave!

column3: Two of my daughters go here one is going ot be a senior and the other is going to be a sophmore. Ever since moving to this school they have been more than excited to go to school every single day. They enjoy the help of the teachers and love the fact that the school is very safe and attentive to their needs. teachers lack in the class room, lack at commucating to students or parents no strong leadership at this school Both of my children have attended CEHS and I can say as an educator and a parent, that I am very pleased with the majority of their teachers and coursework. The support staff is amazing and so helpful as well. Both of my children exceeded the standards in all content areas on AIMS and that is a reflection of the rigorous instruction they have been exposed to at CEHS. The athletic programming is an added "feather in the cap" to an excellent institution.! Centennial offered exceptional educational and social experiences for my daughter. Drama and Band provided to be positive influences in her life and I'm sad to hear the band instructor is being replaced with someone part time. He had great camaraderie with the students genuinely enjoyed his job and was committed to the students. I was impressed with all of her teachers at Centennial. I know she got a quality education that will aid her at NAU this year. I am so dissapointed in this school. The counseling department is a huge dissapointment. It seems they only help the students that are in sports or really high acheivers. Therre is alck of leadership under this current prinipal. my husband and I are both teachers and are just so dissapointed on how the "average" students get treated. The head of the math department should be fired! My daughter and her friends over heard one of the math teachers calling her students "her little retards" She was teaching a year long math class. so inappropriate and unprofessional. I AGREE I AM REALLY DISAPPOINTED WITH THE COUNSELING DEPARTMENT. I ASKED FOR GUIDANCE IN ORDER TO GET MY DAUGHTER READY FOR HONORS CLASSES AND THE COUNSELOR ACTED LIKE SHE WAS NOT INTERESTED. IT'S REALLY DISAPPOINTING WHEN THEY'RE SUPPOSE TO HELP YOUR CHILDREN GET PREPARED FOR COLLEGE AND THE COUNSELOR OFFERS NO GUIDANCE OR ENTHUSIASM. I love Centennial! I am a freshman here and it's amazing. The school spirit is wonderful, everybody loves it here, and the teachers/faculty are great. As far as I can see, there is no bullying and most people just mind their own business. The entire school gets decorated on Fridays for Varsity football games. The games are fun, too! I've been to every freshman and varsity game and we've won all of them so far(: All of the athletics and facilities are great, and the same for academics. I'm taking all honors classes and the teachers are great. If you are looking for a school to send your child to, I would definitely recommend Centennial, whether you're looking for athletics or academics. Go Coyotes!! i have been going to this school since 9th grade, i am now a senior, this school is one of the worst i've ever been too, the teachers/staff don't care. They're rude and disrespectful and don't care about the students. they do not inforce bullying policies or any policies for that matter. i would not recomend this school I am relocating from NY to AZ in June of 2013. The house I am looking at is in this district. I have two boys that would be going to this HS. Is it as good as these rating say? Any thoughts? Also, my little one would be slotted for Peoria Elementary. Is that any good? I saw better reviews for Park Ridge. Any thought? To the parent relocating from NY to AZ - We have our teenagers on a variance attending Centennial HS. They have been @ CeHS for two years and have had a wonderful experience. While no school is perfect, we have found that this HS does have exceptional school spirit, there are teachers who are passionate about teaching and there are good and bad counselors. I would highly recommend this HS. As far as the elementary schools you questioned, I am not familiar with either. Good luck! Before the school won three state football championships, I would have told you it was one of the best schools in the state. Since that time one of the coaches has become the president of the Peoria school board. Sports have taken priority over academics. Avoid this entire district. I love my school, it's so full of spirit & everyone works so hard to teach "Coyote Pride". The football games are a blast & there are lots of clubs to choose from. :) I'm a freshman, but I've already started to love my school. The Honors & AIM Program Classes are challenging & interesting, and the teachers always help you when you need it. The only thing I would change is the huge fuss some teachers make about covering your straps. I don't think they cause any disruption, but I see girls wearing super short shorts around and they don't say anything. Other than that I love it, and I can't wait to see Homecoming Week's decorations & everything (: This school is a fantastic example of great leadership, strong direction, academic excellence, sports and arts and student engagement. Everyone involved understands the meaning of Honor the Code. On and off the field, in the classroom, the hallways and the common areas. We are proud to send our kids to the school and to support their programs. We have kids in two different schools. Both same grade. Two go to Centennial. The quality of school work is grades behind at Centennial. This school is so sports driven and only sports driven. It does not offer the same opportunities that other schools do for academics and dual enrollment. My children at the other HS will be more prepared for college then those at Centennial. Years from now we will have real data, but for now this school is last on my list. My children attended 1990 - 2005 consecutively. My grandchildren 2011 -2021 consecutively. As of 2017 my opinion is, it's a great school as long as you never need a counselor. In my 21 year experience with this school, your child is NOT a priority. Many good teachers and staff, but I have never heard of anyone having a good counselor.

The school has won the Texas UIL Lonestar Cup (which represents the school with the best overall athletic and academic program in its classification) multiple times in recent years.

It's a small school where everyone knows each other and there really haven't been many drug or discipline problems as compared to other local schools. Love LOYALSOCK!

column3: We LOVE Lincoln! Though it may not have all the bells and whistles that neighboring mega-districts have, Lincoln has what counts...staff members that care about the individual. Students are not simply numbers hoarded through the system here. Lincoln's teachers and counselors are wonderful about keeping a watchful eye on the performance of the individual student and, when needed, intervene even when it means on their own time. We feel very blessed to have our children in this district. Lincoln has always been a very progressive school, with a facility very involved with their students, not only with their academic studies, but with after school sports and many community projects. The school Board along with the school districts Administrative, are always striving to bring the best tools to the students and teachers. And help prepare their students for college and life. For a small Western Pennsylvania School, they are Big City with there education

column3: Absolutely Terrible. If you have the choice do not send your child here. He will become a failure in life. I have 2 children who graduated and have become very successful young adults. They took advantage of everything that was available, law club, DECA, ski club, jazz band, chorus, golf and soccer. They had everything they needed to compete on a national level and graduated Princeton and George Washington Univ. with honors. The opportunity to succeed is there for the taking it's a hidden secret. Colleges will only accept 1 tops 2 students from each district. My experience at Glen Cove High School couldn't have been better. After graduating from GCHS, I went on to Princeton University, and felt more prepared for rigorous courses than many of my peers from private and boarding schools. Glen Cove benefits from a small student to teacher ratio (12:1) and a small school overall (995 students) so students, whether they are at the top, middle, or bottom of the class, will never get lost. The ability to get involved and take on leadership positions is incomparable, as its extra-curricular list is extraordinary and teachers are really passionate about students excelling outside the classroom. I'm currently a private college admissions counselor and know exactly what colleges are looking for, and Glen Cove is an ideal school for students looking to go on to top colleges because its small size gives multiple students the ability to shine and stand out in their own unique ways. Glen Cove High School is like many other schools -- you get out of it what you put into it. One of the beautiful aspects of this school, its diversity, is also often times used as a negative by some people. Well, the real world is diverse with different people of different races and different religions, and I'll tell you that Glen Cove High School not only introduces you to that, but prepares you for it.My graduating class sent students to Cornell, Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, NYU, Boston College and more. Sure, many students decide to go to SUNY schools, and there's nothing wrong with that either. The teachers are real people who care, not just about what grades you get and what college you end up at, but about the real, oftentimes difficult parts of their students lives as well. That's so refreshing and reassurring, and something you can't positively measure. If you can't tell, I'm a graduate of the Glen Cove Schools, and I wouldn't have had it any other way. This school is not very good. the approach to homework is mad many teachers assign videos and quizzes to do at home and some require you to print the homework at you house even if you don't have a printer. the teachers are somewhat effective but they never notice that students are playing games or have earbuds in. The leadership in this school is not effective if there was an option lower than disagree i would put it. there is one principal and two assistant principals the only reason one of the assistant principals names is known is because his son that goes to the school has the same name, many students forget we have a principal. don't even get me started on the character of this school the students are disrespectful say many bad words and don't care about any other students often in the hallways many students show homophobic behavior and are mean to their LGBT+ classmates. this school handles bullying well if you call putting up a few anti bullying posters and not acting on them well. if you have a choice do not send your children to this school. This school is AWESOME, The teachers are the BEST, The teachers are kind and respectful to the students. And the principal is also really nice, he deals with everything that happens in this school, The food may not be the best, but who cares about that, we bring in our own lunch from home anyways. The AP Classes are a lot better than most schools in this country. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND PARENTS TO SEND YOUR KIDS AT GLEN COVE HIGH SCHOOL. IT IS AWESOME AND YOUR KIDS WILL ABSOLUTELY IT HERE! Average to good school… I went to high school here… When compared to other friends who went to more demanding schools, the high school could’ve prepared me better …Some of the teachers I encountered were excellent… Some not so…Again as somebody said… You make the best of what you have to excel… I wasn’t prepared for the rigorous university that I went to … especially in writing skills… No preparation for how to write a research paper…I enjoyed the drama program… I have no regrets…

column3: The primary focus of this school is to maximize salaries and minimize output where students are concerned. Administration's main focus is the budget, not dealing fairly with students. Administration does not want to be involved with student's problems and paints everyone with the same brush to avoid responsibility. I have to say that as far as public education goes,high schools dont come any better than this.John Glenn is a fitting pinnacle to a child's education which began with the former schools in the chain. Very often,faculty the student has had in Primary and Middle School is purposefully transferred to the High School to create an immesurable continuity for the student.The fact that the faculty is trained enough to revolve in this way also speaks well for the administration,who have personal knowledge of the students in this High School,and the ability to encourage them to seek the correct college. I have had a daugther graduate from this school and attend Geneseo and graduate with honors. She had a wonderful High School education,full of not only academic pursuits but also extra curricular drama and music during which they helped her compete to be the best on a county level,with exciting results.This school is not insular.It is involved with its community and its students are frequently seen in the surrounding neighborhoods promoting their various programs and running track in groups. Many a productive human being has graduated through these doors,and the principal is wonderful. If your child doe not fit the "mold" whether advanced or disabled, this is not the school for the child. There is a lot of talk but little action. Both the budget, and NYS law make things difficult. This is a school with no immagination or inspiration. Collaboration with the parents is one-way: the parents must collaborate. Personally, I found both the academic and support staff to be unprofessional at times, and there to be a culture of "us" versus "the parents". The Worst school in the world! I an not kidding, I setup an appointment with the councilor and I had to reschedule it because he was "busy." Not only that all the staff are very hard to talk to because the way they act towards you. My Son has problems with 3 of his teachers and they are not his fault. They other students just learned to live with it. But because we have just moved in it is very annoying. If you love your child you will do everything in your power to not sign them up in this terrible school. As a student that attends this school, I can tell you that every student who attends on a daily basis, absolutely hates the school. 90 percent of the teachers do a poor job and enjoy seeing kids struggle. They also enjoy making everyone's life more miserable. The tests that are given are usually nothing like the review or ten times harder. Days in middle school used to be the glory days. Overall the high school is a poorly run place run by people with no common sense. This school, although smaller than any district does an excellent job in making sure parents are alerted to their child progress. My children have excelled on this district and in this school.. Some people will never be happy with a school system and you have to really know your children. Glenn is rated high performing and their sports programs for a smaller school is also excellent , the volleyball team has gone to state a few times as well as football. We have had students get into Princeton and other high profile schools as well due to their academic achievements here and sports achievements as well. The parents who complain are the same ones that never attend a PTA meeting or is involved in any way with the school. The kids...well ..the ones who don't want to study or think outside the box will complain about tests not outlined for them....they need to grow up...Good Job Elwood and John Glenn!! I can not understand the negative reviews on this school that I have read. This school is listed at a 7, it should be at least a 9! The only negative that I can see could be its size. It may lack a few specialty programs that the larger school districts may have but I feel it is not worth the sacrifice that the benefits of a smaller school district gives. The administration and teachers do care about the students education and their safety. The music department is great and so are the sports programs with teams that play at a level of talent of the larger schools, for example our volleyball team and coach that's well known and second to none! Bottom line .... If education is the decisive factor in picking an area to live this should be at the top of your list!!! Great school! Teachers really care about the students. Absolutely one of the worst schools on Long Island. And I mean it. I'm a student who used to go here then got kicked out all because I was being bullied to much. And they disrespect anyone who disagrees with them, and even falsely gave me a graduate's degree and even had the audacity to block me on Google Reviews as well. Worst school district in Suffolk County. Don't send your kid here. It is a great school. My son is doing well. Good teachers and cooperative on teaching staff. My son is benefiting and getting better. This school should have known better than to give me a false certificate of graduation which this school district is the worst on LI and this school never cared about autistic students. Ever. They never did and they never will. Bruzynski should be fired along with the whole district!!!

column1: Creekside has the potential to be a great school because it has some great teachers and students. However, the leadership is going through a transition. We have a good interim prinicipal but the new principal will have a few challenges to deal with such as, very little parent involvement, not meeting AYP the last few years and just changing the school culture to one that is nurturing, motivational and positive. Creekside High School has several professional educators and some dedicated parents. The new principal has done an excellent job of assembling an administrative staff that seems engage. However, he (the principal), doesn't. His passive approach to deal with situations head on makes one question his improvement plan communicated to parents upon beginning the school year. In this critical time, the school needs true and connected leadership verses an administrator that promotes the impression of being the "cool" guy. What is the purpose of a school? The purpose is for kids to have a safe and cooperative learning environment when they can make friends and study. Except in this school, new kids are left out the very first day form activities. What ever happened to talking to the new kids on the first day of school? Or maybe being the considerate teachers who popcorn introduce their new students to the class? Has times changed so much that kids are greeted with a gym teacher just using their cellphones in class while the kids stick to corners with groups of retuning kids while the newbies are in the center staring at the wall? Teachers and staff should make a greater effort to enforce communications between all students. I like it because I have friends who really care about me there but if it wasn’t for that I would not like that school so I’ll rate it 3/10 Creekside HS has a GREAT Agriculture program, Band and AVID Program. It was just featured in the AJC about their dual enrollment program.

column3: I wasn't the best student when i attended mason. That being said I had soooo many teachers that worked really hard to help me get the grades i needed to not only pass but actually make honor roll. While i was in school I wasn't thrilled about the fact that it is a smaller school caught between country roads and an antique town, but now that i am older I really think that had I gone to nearly any other school I may have dropped out all together. My teachers were amazing and actually really care about the students. My fiance also went to mason and he loved it while he attended mason schools. I moved from another state four years ago and started eighth grade at Mason. I loved every minute of my eighth grade year. I am now a senior. I have a 3.6 GPA and I have loved each and every one of my teachers. I moved from a school where I had no friends. I was bullied constantly and because I didn't play soccer of football I was an outcast. Mason has made me feel so welcome. They care equally about sports and acedemics. The Mason community is very supportive of each other as well. Mason is a wonderful school and community to move to. I am so proud to be a part of Mason and I am very happy that my family moved here. I attended Mason High School in the 1980s and recently moved back for my son to graduate from Mason. I've been very impressed with the commitment of the teachers, the culture of the athletic programs and the cleanliness of the school and campus. Mason has been a great school for my children. I love their support of the Arts (their band director is great!). There are lots of electives to chose from to help make educated decisions on future career goals. Mason also has great community pride. Great school we are glad we moved to Mason the teachers really do care about your kids and their education. not good they were mean to me

column1: This school can't even afford air conditioning let alone good school books. This school is one of the worst schools in the area. I currently attend Penn Cambria and however many people say that the education is "less than satisfactory" and however many people say that "bullying and hazing happens frequently" i have been going to this school for 10 years and never once have i ever seen or heard of any of this happening inside the schools. The teachers are incredible people who do the best that they can with the limited resources we have been provided with because of the budget cuts and they all try to help us succeed if anyone says that their education was unsatisfactory i doubt it was the teachers fault because even when i had less intelligent individuals in my classes the teachers would help them learn at their own rate and give help to the ones that needed the help the most and let ones that didn't need it go on their way until they did. Out of all my years I've probably had one teacher i didn't especially like out of 30-40 teachers. Our school is ranking 3rd in the highest PSSA scores in math as of last year so i think it deserves at least 4 stars if not the 5 that i gave it. Penn Cambria has very few good qualities to it. The school inside is not very fun to be in for anyone mainly because the school is never heated during the winter other than during the first couple hours of the day, after that it is very cold and hard to pay attention in. The bullying is minimum which is a good thing but the amount of racist, sexist, and homophobic remarks I hear everyday are too much. The school is using very out of date materials but this is understandable, the school does not have a lot of money to go off of. The biggest problem with this school however is lack of any kind of freedom. If you compare this school to thousands of other schools it would be considered a prison. You cannot have cell phones at any time of day, including lunch. Detentions are handed out for every single thing a student does that is out of what the school calls "right." The dress code is awful, though at least it doesn't require uniforms. I do not enjoy my school life in the least and I try and get by enough to get out, and that isn't how it should be. This is my personal opinion on Penn Cambria, others may differ. Penn Cambria Middle and High school are the most terrible schools I've ever been to in my whole life!I have been to many different schools in my life time, moved school to school for years and have never met such a lousy group of administrators! Money put into school accounts sometimes just seem to go "missing", the school is never heated in the winter, and bullying is at an all time high. At my time of being in Pennn Cambria (I graduated a few years ago) I managed to only meet 6 good teachers, the rest seemed to hate where they work. Even some told us students they hated the school. The middle school was just awful, the dean of students would tell you to your face he hated you, and would lie to parents to get their children in trouble. If he thought someon had a phone he would make them shake their pockets out in front of the whole class and give them a suspension if they refused.One thing that disgusted me the most about Penn Cambria is the amount of favoritism. You bet if you were related to anyone who works at the school you could go to school in a mini skirt and a crop top and not one person would bat an eye. If you weren't related, rich or popular you were treated like utter junk. The vice principle of the high school had a habbit of disobeying IEPs, would then call the student a liar when they would point it out to their parents. People will bring cigarets in school, and if you were one of the people he liked he wouldn't do anything! A girl was caught smoking in the school bathrooms and he gave her gum!!! The middle school though is far worse than the high school. The guidance counselor would let her daughter who attended the school get away with murder! She graduated every class with an A, but failed every test she ever got. I sat next to her, she would always try to copy me. She never turned in homework, and would smack girls in the face. We are told we aren't aloud piercings, and it's in the rule book. But girls wear nose rings to school all the time, and only select girls get into trouble. They pick and choose.My advice is, do not send your kid to Penn Cambria.

I currently attend Braddock leading up to my senior year and I am in the Information Technology program and it's an excellent program. New programs such as iPrep and the Arts Academy are starting to rise and the school is initially good. There's kids of all types of groups, ethnics, etc. It's a very big and diverse school where you're constantly always learning. yo creo que el Principal debe estar mas atento al comportamiento de los profesores con los alumnos, algunos de los profesores son los que estan maltratando verbalmente a los alumnos, please ayudemos a nuestros hijos, creo que el programa de Cambridge es magnifico, pero debe evaluarse la actitud de los profesores ( algunos), que pena que no puedo poner sus nombres! es tan importante la educacion de nuestros hijos, como su salud. I love my school I skipped a grade next year going to be a senior they helped me skip a year most of the staff is the sweetest the mean ones are ravelo and soriano they want to ruin you life all the teachers I have had have wanted to help me get better and progress the programs and the people are cool I recommend it it's a bit of everything fun and curriculum ! Good luck The Cambridge program at this school is beyond compare. Keep up the excellent work that you are doing!!! Teacher are good to great, counselors are very helpful, but administration and the school policy makes life very difficult for students penalizing them for minor offenses such as excessive tardiness. While Braddock may not have been the best school in Miami-Dade County, it isn't the worst either. The students in the school are okay, minus the druggies and kids that don't want to learn. The administration isn't very strict, only toward being tardy and other minor stuff. The teachers are not the best, most just give out work and don't really teach. Only with a few exceptions. An overwhelming majority of the kids in this school are Hispanic, and a few don't even know English. The food is HORRIBLE, they really need to improve. It's not very healthy and sometimes I wonder where they get it from. The school is pretty safe, except for the occasional fight or two that would happen every month. Overall I liked this school and am glad to have graduated as Class of 2015. This school does not provide enough support for freshmen. The office staff is usually rude and unhelpful. Don't bother emailing administration with any isues; they definitely feel entitled to do the bare minimum even though they get paid nice salaries and benefits. This is my son’s most stressful year. His school year started out terribly because the registrar messed up on three of his classes which affected five of his classes overall. Students here do not receive enough guidance or support when teachers or office staff make mistakes. There are great teachers here and then there are others who overstep their role. If you report any concerns to administrators, they will do nothing. Protecting students from retaliation from their teachers for reporting concerns are not a priority in this school. Being a part of the Cambridge program I was separated from most of the bad influences like drugs and smoking. Most of the teachers I had were very versed in their subject although some went a little heavy on the homework. Being a part of the NJROTC unit also helped keep away from some of the more problematic students that had issues with authority and liked to start fights. Overall it was a pretty good experience despite the lack of help offered by counselors and some other staff. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this school, my daughter has gone through very hard times, due to ethics I cannot give details but they have been disrespectful that are not forgiven.Among other things, I have seen unpleasant videos of fights between students, many drugs and the police can not do anything because the state of Florida does not give them enough support. I am desperately looking for how to get my daughter out of this school. I'm sorry because there are very good teachers here. Great School. The Cambridge Program has allowed my son to earn his Cambridge Diploma, thus earning him the 100% Florida Bright Future Scholarship. He enjoys the activities, atmosphere and the high school experience. What a great school! Security, office staff, teachers, counselors, Assistant Principals and even the Principal are always trying to help the student and the parents too. I can't say enough about how my child has developed and how much she loves it. We had other choices but I am glad we chose Braddock. I recommend it highly! Just about the environment and safety(cause academic results have been widely doscussed in this site): My son has called me multiple times asking me to pick him up because he isn’t able to use the bathrooms for several hours due to smokers and skipping students locked inside between and during classes. I have called the school and they have told me that he could call a security guard, which he hasn’t done because of two reasons: first, he says that the school doesn’t really care since it’s an ongoing problem and everyone is aware of it but nobody takes action. Second: he feels it’s the staff responsibility to fix the situation instead of him becoming a whistle blower which will not resolve the issue and might bring retaliation from the students engaging in these behaviors. On top of that, he fears been caught among the smokers and skippers and risk been expelled from his sport’s team. It’s the school duty to secure a safe environment and guarantee such basic rights as the availability of bathrooms for their intended use for their students, which G Holmes Braddock regularly fails to do.

column1: The principal, assistant principal, and guidance counselor aren't exactly warm and welcoming. Some teachers genuinely care about the students others seem to just need the job. The guidance counselor can be rude, aggressive, and lacks many necessary qualities of the job (he doesn't know what he's doing at ALL). Students casually bring up far too many drug and alcohol references even in classes. Staff barely updates students and parents on information that both should know (i.e. important dates, funds, pictures, etc..). Some teachers don't or visibly don;t want to teach their subjects so they hand students textbooks and leave them to it themselves. I feel religion is occasionally thrust into my child's face at least once a week. Students say prejudice comments towards different groups of race or religion in a joking manner. I feel the school tries to mask imperfections instead of fix them.-Not a good environment! I went to Highlands my entire high school "career " and it used to be GREAT. I never had the current administration but I have siblings in the school. I can tell you that the principal, vp and guidance counselor are HORRIBLE. The principal is the first to believe the students are bad kids, he refuses to participate in school related activities that he doesn't HAVE to be at and he acts as though he never has time for issues he deems unworthy of his time. I will say that the students are becoming more main stream in pop culture and sometimes I feel as though some teachers are not encouraging in the appropriate ways. Also, the TEACHERS have a huge problem with TEXTING during class. I've had some kids show me pictures of the teachers texting instead of teaching. The community is the greatest asset of this school, that's about it. I have been going to Highlands School ever since I was in Kintergarden. And from my experiences in this school I can say that it has been great for me. Everyone one, including the facaulty, staff and students are so warm and welcoming. And work one on one with you. Sure we've had some unstable teachers (mainly in middle school) does NOT mean our school is bad. Honestly its not just our school that have their flaws. It's every other school. Not everything is perfect. And I'm actually speaking for a lot of other people that go here. Highlands is such a great school and we're honestly like a family here. I went to Highlands School ,I moved here from FLA. I love the small school system. The teacher and students were bonded along with students with other students.I have children in Highlands School I would not put them in any other school. I know most if not all the teachers.As for the principals anytime I have EVER had a problem they have taken action to fix it. i love this school, the teachers are helpful and supportive. its a small school, but it is good because one gets more attencion. I will miss it. I made friends that are a lifetime with you no matter hor far one is from another. I have almost been here all my life and I have to say that this is probably the best school that your kids should go to the the teachers are the most intelligent no matter the grade. They will work with you until the very end. The environment is great for kids to learn in. I graduate this year and I wouldn't be here with out them. Thank you highlands school I loved every moment that shared with the teachers and my fellow class mates and the staff too, you're great I will miss you. David tanner Stephens Awesome, I went there and hope for my kids as well. It’s a small K-12 school you are feel like family and make life long friends are well pre-paired for college. Excellent! I am thankful for middle school teachers who truly embrace the “it takes a village” approach to student success.

column3: Fantastic school with a multi-cultural setting. Academic performance has increased significantly, attendance has increased significantly, discipline issues have been greatly reduced, and the graduation rate had the largest increase of all comprehensive high schools in Guilford County Schools in 2012-13. The IB program draws top students from a designated region and has 250 students presently enrolled. High Point Central High School is one of the best schools around in my opinion. It has been around to serve generation after generation. It is the "flagship" school for High Point, NC. It has been loved and will continue to be loved by former and present students and their families. HPC is a beautiful ageless school that is protected by the historians. The faculty and staff of HPC Is a wonderful group of people who truly care about our children and want them to "Achieve with Honor"! I am a former student at HPC and it was not the best experience before attending T. Wingate Andrews. When i was enrolled at HPC i noticed to a great extent it was not about the education for students. The staff never pushed students to achieve something greater and to go into college. It often seemed like a social setting instead. I stayed in most CP classes and was never motivated to be greater than i am until i transferred to Andrews, where the the school had decided to change the environment and become more strict towards the education of students. In the end it really benefits us and shows they really care. High Point Central is one of the best high schools in the state. Principal Bob Christina has turned this school completely around in the 4 short years he has been here. As a senior, I can see the changes he has made and can honestly say that the school is a place were the faculty truly cares about the students and the teachers will do anything to see their students succeed in and out of school. For example, free tutoring is offered by all teachers before and after school. HPC will not let a student fall through the cracks of the system as they are always encouraging and urging students to do their best. Founded in 1897, this school is legendary throughout the piedmont, it was the first million dollar high school ever built in North Carolina. HPC has a long legacy and there is a pride that goes along with graduating from a school with so much history. If you are considering sending your child to High Point Central I urge you to come take a look at the school for yourself and you will see how great of a school this is, how caring the people running the school are, and how anyone is capable of excelling in this incredible, one of a kind, school. Teachers say one thing concerning a policy but then when you go to the office its something different. Everyone need to be on the same page. Too much confusion and a waste of parent time and energy when they flip flop on a so called school rule. Please, please walk around the campus including both sides of Ferndale Blvd. There are papers and trash everywhere.....especially in the yards across the street.

column1: This school is a very nice place to attend. The teachers are very kind and understand their students, most going the extra mile to ensure students leave their classroom with all the knowledge they intended to give, an amazing feat given that every other week students are not in those classes. The school itself also has a very different atmosphere than other schools in the area, teaching practical knowledge rather than things that will only apply on a standardized test and not help them beyond. There are one or two problems, though. A sizable portion of the student body can be described as prejudiced, unintelligent and rather obnoxious. Teachers cannot do much if a student is being a major problem in their classes - with bullying, copying of answers, and constant interruptions being a major problem this is not a good thing. The only solution to that is to go to the administration and hope they can help, however in most cases they only truly affect students normally well behaved and punishments to chronic offenders being a slap on the wrist. Also, their computers are all hopelessly outdated, with CRT monitors difficult and painful to read. Overall, a perfectly above-average school. Because I'm quite it not as bad as it could of been but this school need to be better and someone need to hold them accountable for everything they do I believe the school can be great it just needs some help

column3: This school needs a lot of improvement ! There is a lack of student parent communication. Like I always say once your child enters through those doors, everything is top secret. Now there are a few teachers there that are really great but that is about 10% My child was struggling with a class and I didn't know until a week before graduation. If my child didn't pass the final exam it was no diploma for her. We tried to get her help in the class but no one was interested.... I have hesitated for several months to write a review, hoping that things would improve, but unfortunately that is not the case. From the day of Open House, things have not been flowing smoothly. I do not understand how a course can continue without a Teacher who is certified in the subject at hand. I do understand that sometimes these things are out of their control, however, they did not have a Teacher lined up from the beginning and had no business going forward with this class. What kind of message do you think the students are getting out of this? They are learning that the Teacher's role is unimportant, or even intrusive. I agree with the poster who complained about the extensive wait, and minimal to no time to eat lunch. It's a parent's prerogative whether they bring home lunch or pay at school. If you choose to buy school lunch, the least thing they can do, is provide a reasonable amount of time to eat it. I have two students at CCHS, and they are very different from one another, but both agree that this is a problem. Let's face it, some of these kids are on the bus 1-1.5 hrs. each way, that makes for a very long day. These are just a couple of many concerns. this school doesn't even deserve a star. not even one. this school is suppose to be bully free. ha thats not true. there is bullying every minute of every hour in that school and absolutely nothing is done about it. i should know. i use to go there now i don't bc when you ask for help the teachers don't help you at all. my own guidance councilor told me to my face i'm not made for school and that there is no way i would get to 12th grade or graduate at all. I have had two students Graduate from CCHS and both were more than prepared as they entered 4 year universities. My children have excelled at this school, more than I could have ever imagined. To the people complaining about CCHS, please take the time to actually reach out to your teachers, your administrators, talk about the issues you might be having, come up with a resolution. Turning to facebook to bash the school accomplishes zero. Being a military family and seeing several high schools first hand this is the absolute worst. Overcrowded, kids are disrespectful and bullying is terrible. It was honestly terrible. Most teachers didn’t bother to make disruptive students be quiet so those of us who cared about learning could learn. I hated it so much I graduated a semester early just to get out of there. The majority of the teachers that I dealt with as a parent were not sticking to the curriculum that was set forth at the beginning of the year. At one point, both of my children came home and told me that for the past two weeks they had both done nothing but watch movies in class. Me thinking it was at least related to the subject asked more questions only to find out they had no educational value whatsoever. After speaking to the vice principal, principal, and even the superintendent, I was told the teacher would be observed by the principal to ensure proper curriculum was maintained. It will be if the boss is watching generally. I’m so glad my kids no longer attend this school.

column1: CCA has become a place that is only focused on its test scores. Period. Everything revolves on the image and not substance. I was asked to leave because my math scores were not high enough. I know others who have been booted out as well, some in the middle of their senior year. Admission to CCA is supposed to be based on audition, but it isn't. Your academic record can make or break your admission regardless of your audition. I think that CCA is a unnecessary school. There is not any technology classses or home economics. There is not any sports. This school does not help students choose a reasonable career. My daughter attended this year. Had to withdraw her. The gang element ever bad. An ebonics school if ever there was one. she reported fighting and bullying all the tme noting done. A total failue I absolutely love CCA. I just finished my Junior year, and yes it was hard, but it needed to be to prepare me for the future. There are, in fact, three computer labs in the school, so yes, we have technology. There aren't any sports, that's right, but most of the students don't really care. We came to this school for the arts, and those who want to play sports more just go to a regular public school. I love this school, and the people in it, and I'm so glad that I don't go anywhere else. CCA pushes their students to achieve highly in their regular coursework as well as their art. Going to this school is a privilege. To earn this privilege, you must prove yourself academically and show your gift in art. Obviously, if you are not an artist, dancer, musician, actor, singer, etc... this school is not for you. CCA offers the best of both worlds. A top notch college prep education and an opportunity to do what you love. They provide the same education a normal high school/middle school would (yes, of course, they have technology!). The extracurricular activities differ quite a bit; orchestra vs. band, musicals/plays/dance/ art shows vs. organized sports. After all, these kids are not here for organized sports. they are here to immerse themselves in the arts. I believe that CCA is a great school for an alternative student. The academic classes here are pretty up to date, however could be improved. I believe to fit in at this school and truly get the "full package" of the arts, academics and socially you have to be a different kind of student and person. The people are fairly welcoming here, the teachers are overall nice, the school building is kept clean and bullying is kept at a low. However, if you do not consider yourself an alternative person, very different from the "normal person", then I do not recommend going here. The majority of people that come into this school will experience some kind of major culture shock, which isn't a bad thing considering that is the real world. As far as punishing at CCA, I would say some serious issues are ignored(such as cheating, drugs, fighting and alcohol). I feel like this is an overall good school for your 100% artsy, alternative student. But, if you don't feel that different from your "normal" classmates, I wouldn't recommend CCA. This is my first year at CCA and I am a vocal major and so far it has been great! Obviously there is a lot more ahead for me though. There's rarely any bullying. You can be who you want to be and nobody will judge you. Although there is no sports ( which I'm happy about ) until about high school when you can take it for a semester. I think the teacher and learning is great! The language arts teachers were excellent; the math and social studies teachers were a little above average; the science was uneven with one teacher being demanding, dis-organized and unpredictable but who at least knew science and the other being someone drafted from another related field. The various art and music teachers are experts in their fields, versus having a teacher who just majored in a field in college. The principal is more a politician than an educator, so appearances are stressed over the reality. I am giving the school two stars because of the unnecessary work and stress level, the emphasis on 'common core' for political reasons, but the language art department probably deserves a five. CCA is a performing arts school and the arts classes and teachers are the best the city has to offer. With all the performances, rehearsals, and schoolwork, you will have to have discipline to keep up. As for parents who are considering sending their child here, CCA will teach them self discipline, accountability, and responsibility along with lots of fun and preparation for furthering their education. CCA is an excellent school! This is my daughter's first year and the curriculum is top notch My daughter began at CCA in the 6th grade and this year she's a senior. She has enjoyed her time and has done well. The staff has been supportive and open minded. The performances are beautiful but rehearsals can be quite demanding. Kids should plan on some long days with great outcomes. I wouldn't change a thing. This school is better than the ones I’ve been to in the Chattanooga area as a disabled person, but it doesn’t provide quite enough support. It’s more support than most, yes, but it still isn’t quite enough. There are lots and lots of stairs and it is very hard to get access to the elevator. I’ve been told off for using a disability aid by a few teachers. I was bullied very badly in seventh grade and the school did nothing about it. The arts are very underfunded and the school mainly puts money towards things only a select few people want. The teachers seem to actually care about students as people and want to help us individually, unlike other schools I’ve been to in the area. I will applaud the seventh grade math teacher, Dr Pate, for giving me hope and keeping me mentally well in an unsafe situation. Overall, this school is a very good place compared to other schools in the area, but there is still lots of room for improvement.

column3: If there was an option to give a school zero stars I would do so. There are cockroaches and mice everywhere, dead and alive. This school is the epitome of the social class system from Mean Girls: If you're new to this school, you are socially screwed. The teachers are extremely hypocritical and do not teach, with very few exceptions. The sports suck, the people suck, and the school smells like manure 80% of the time. Don't go to this school if you want to keep your soul and self-respect. This School Is One of The best that I've ever attended! There's just a great atmosphere. The administration does a great job at keeping things running well. All The teachers that i have encountered are great. There is a large FFA community within the school, but that in no way hinders the quality of the education. The students are really friendly, They really welcomed me when i first moved to this school. There are also a loooooong list of activities and clubs at Walkersville. In my opinion, we have one of the best Theater Programs in the State! The Sports Program is also very top notch! If you are a senior/junior preparing for college, the school does a great job of supporting you and helping you with the process! Overall, Walkersville is a great choice if you are looking for an excellent High School. Eh, it was okay. Fairly clean. Barely any bullying. 90% of funding went to the football team. Good AP program. Ocassional pathetic attempts at school spirit. Clubs are a joke.

column1: There is little to no communication from the school to parents, when they do communicate it is to tell you of an event at most 2 days away. They have an online grade communication site, but grades are only updated maybe twice in a 9 week period-if your child is having trouble in a class you don't know it till it is too late. Asking for teacher help to understand classwork (as a parent) you are made to feel guilty for asking and I have even been told "your child needs to know this material not you". I have no problem trying to further explain class material so my child understands, but teachers are of little help. Most "learning" is directed at the final state testing requirements and most teachers are difficult to communicate with. If your child is great at sports, then you are given more attention and assistance so the sports program can excel. My child started in kindergarten here and is in high school now, I kept hoping it would get better, but the high school teachers are the worst. Only 2 years to go and we are done here....counting the time left. I was once a student at jessieville. Considering it was the only school I've ever been to I thought it was great. That is until I moved schools. After about a week or two I realized jessieville sucked. The teachers do not teach the right material and for kids who don't care they give them passing grades just so they can graduate high school. Jessieville is small and the people have horrible personalities. If you go to jessieville you will soon regret it. I myself am very embarrassed that I ever even went to jessieville.

column3: My daughter is a freshman at Tracy High and even though I fought hard to have her there, because I was led to believe it was the best of the 3 public HS options in the city, I have been disappointed with her feedback over the school year. Everything from one teacher sittin in the back of the class eating all the time and "I'm learning nothing" to "extra credit is earned by donating school supplies" to the basketball coach using the F word during practices on a regular basis. I realize that in teachers unions, it's nearly impossible to be fired, but I think someone needs to take a good look at what is actually going on in the classrooms and talk to the kids. There's a fear of even talking about it for fear of repercussions. That should say enough. I will be looking for another option for her remaining high school days, possibly home schooling as my faith is the public school system, and what it actually provides, is rapidly fading. 3 of my children have or are currently attending Tracy High. Two of them where/are in the International Baccalaureate program and the other one has learning challenges due to ADHD. Because of this we have been involved in such opposite sides of Tracy High’s learning programs. The teachers in the IB program are fun, passionate, supportive and intelligent. They realized that the program can be stressful for the students so they push self care and are understanding and flexible with the students. They want nothing but the best for them and stress the importance of a well rounded and balanced student not just straight A’s. One of my children has many limitations and challenges in school due to a ADHD diagnosis and this child’s counselor saw a issues and worked with me to set up meetings with herself, all teachers, the schools psychologist and the school secretary. We came up with a year long plan for my child involving extra support, reminders, extra time on homework and tests. The teachers that came to the meetings supported my child from that point on and I will be forever grateful. He went from possibly not passing his Freshman year to passing and then went on to get his first 4.0 the next year!!! He worked so hard but I think his teachers and his counselor all getting together to show him love and support is what he needed to raise his confidence and for him to not be afraid of trying. Mrs Carey was all three of my children’s counselor and she has made such a positive and amazing impact on their lives forever. She is such a caring, passionate, loving and supportive mentor for my children. We will never forget her. Such a special person and a blessing to the students in her care. I highly recommend Tracy High School. One star is for the few Teachers my children had who showed concern for what was being taught. Many teachers used movies and videos instead of teaching,, called out sick often and had student aides grade homework. Dress code was not enforced. My child has his lunch stolen from his backpack during class and the thief threw it in the garbage. I was not contacted by the school and the vice principal could not have cared less. Only concern seems to be with attendance so that can get their money from the government.

column1: sorry to say I would not recomment this school to anyone a good school starts with good leadership and 2 weeks my d aughter begged my to take her out and after I three week I did and took her back to her school of 1st choice when the school year started back what they were teach was 4th grade level and she was in the 6th grade at the end of the day it is n ot just about being with your race its being where the better place is for your child my faimlly members have also taken there kids out I found this to be a good school. If you are not open to an African-centered perspective. Students still learn the from the core curriculum of the Columbus City School district, just from an Africentric perspective where students see themselves in what they are learning. They can apply what they are learning to everyday situations. The outcome is remarkable in the area of self-concept, self-esteem, and racial identity development. The students prepare for college and by the time they graduate, they can have their high school diploma and associate degree. The guiding principles of Nguzo Saba and Maat is a great base to teach from. Parents should be willing to participate in the school's activities and their child's education, if not, then that is sad. One of the worst schools in the district. The principal and assistants are all unprofessional, students are always noisy, rude and not there to study. I placed my daughter after reading the early college program, it's a joke as only 1/2 students attend columbus state so it's a early college for name. Teaches don't teach and adminstration doesn't do anything. Never send your kid or let someone else send there kid here This school is in danger of closing after years of poor performance. Africentric is labelled as an alternative school and students have the opportunity to take college credit courses at CSCC. Nonetheless, the school is ranked bottom of the CCS and less than a handful of students are enrolled to CSCC. Administration lacks leadership and staff morals are low with high turnover ratio. In 2014, CCS Board decided to make changes in administration to save the school but it is a bit too late because the damage has been done with past administraion's failure to turn the school around. They catered to the terrible kids and lack of discipline, the good kids that wanted to learn ended up leaving even going back to their home schools. The infrastructure of the building is out-dated, parents were promised to have a new building completed by 2013 but it never fell through. Previous administration had failed to recruit good students and let everyone in, so the students who got expelled from other schools ended up in Africentric and continue to disrupt the school. A good school for them and nice

column1: 3 of my children graduated or will graduate from Kentlake in the classes of '09, '10, and '11. Overall, I feel there are a few good teachers that care about student progress and one administrator that puts the students first . There is a new principal this year and it is too soon to tell if there will be any improvements. But, during the years my children were at Kentlake, there was a definite disconnect between administrators, teachers, and students. Numerous teachers made it very challenging for students to seek help from them, were apathetic when a student was struggling in class, and favoritism was prevalent at the school. Teachers were also allowed to dock a students grade for non-academic matters. I found this to be ludicrous and received no support from administrators when I attempted to address the issue. Academics are the only thing that should be reflected in a grade. I will say this, if you want to be an athlete, attend Kentlake. Sports and the athletes are favored here. I had to stop by Kentlake when the bell rang for the day to end. OOPS wrong time to be at a busy high school. I was pleasantly surprised that the students were polite and did not run me over to leave. The office staff was kind and helpful. Then it was time to leave along with 1600 students. I was again surprised at the polite way the drivers (mostly students) took turns. They drove carefully and even allowed people from a nearby housing development to merge. I was proud of the students!! Today was teacher conference; the teachers were well prepared and very nice. I met with my son's school counselor; she helped him arrange a class he needed. Wow, it was painless. I am thankful my son has the opportunity to attend KLHS! I've taught at 12 of the 13 secondary schools in the Kent District, and of those 12, Kentlake is the only one with a serious attitude problem. The kids there act like they run the school, because they do. They have more power than the adults because the school is run so weakly. Example: I was talking to a security guard who said that security there never takes phones away from students by force. He said it could injure the student and that the students must be tiptoed around. Neither the adults nor students seem to realize its supposed to be the other way around. The result is a rude, defiant, dishonest student body despite their not being that way at the feeder middle schools. Test scores are OK, although they'd be higher if students cared and did their work honestly. Easily my least favorite school in the district since I love the other Kent schools. Reading another comment, I strongly agree. Many KL teachers would make you believe if you didn't make one deadline on a project you might as well give up and fail the project or even the class. I transferred my senior year not only because teachers were unhelpful, but also because the students really were allowed to be defiant and outright rude to faculty and other students with little or no punishment. (I even witness students cuss at teachers with no repercussions) Also - SERIOUS drug problem. Students smoke and drink and get high on pills at school and almost never get caught. Dr. Potts has really turned this building around, attitude-wise. The population has decreased to under 1400 which also helps. Students at Kentlake have finally taken a sense of pride in their school; they are more empathetic and caring than 4 years ago, and are more likely to get involved beyond 2:30pm. Bringing in Dr. Potts 5 years ago has turned this school from the least pleasant high school in the district to a school that is among the best to be at. Academic rigor has been stressed, and most students have an Honors, AP, or UW level class because the staff has made it a priority to encourage students to reach farther than they're used to. The school itself even paid for the SAT and PSAT to be taken by all seniors and juniors the past two years. The only thing which has worsened is the school's athletic records and, when your school loses 400-500 kids in 4 years, that's to be expected. The teams all play with a bit of a chip on their shoulders, which is understandable when you're a 2A-size school playing in a 4A league. They're a scrappy bunch with a lot of pluck, some great teachers, a lot of good kids, and the school truly gets better year after year. Kentlake is an excellent school that has shown much improvement over the last five or six years. The new administration (with Dr. Potts) has done a great job. On average, the staff and teachers are very nice and helpful. I think the only real issue with this school is some of its students. But hey, it's a public school, you're going to have a few misbehaved students here and there. Overall great school. Both of my kids benefitted from the theater and music programs at Kentlake. Although both graduated a number of years ago and the teachers may not be the same, those programs regularly took prizes in national competition and the statewide 5th Avenue Musical Theater Awards. My daughter's class included several nationally successful recording artists (Daphne loves Derby, Tess Henley) and both of my kids went to top private schools with scholarships as did a number of their classmates. The main negative was that colleges on the East Coast look at weighted scores (WA didn't weight for AP courses) and the school year ends later than most meaning that year-end honors aren't available until long after most districts have finished. Not the fault of the school but the state which wants scholars to stay in WA even when they can get into top schools elsewhere. Kentlake is almost 50% free and reduced lunch. Students are offered a variety of courses- Core, AP, College In The Classroom. Staff is dedicated and puts student needs first. Great school, we had a great experience here! Amazing school! Teachers are incredible; environment is very encouraging and friendly. Great school, no problems with it at all.
