column3: The current principal pressures teachers to inflate grades. There is a grading system here in which a teacher gives nothing less than a 50% for an "F". The reasoning is self esteem related & encourages kids not to lose hope once they have that F. A teacher strictly following this system wouldn't give any grade less than a 50%, meaning the kid only has to do 10% of the work to pass. If you look at it from the 10% angle, it's just shameful. Kids get a false sense of accomplishment. Nobody forces you to grade this way, but if you are failing too many kids, you can expect trouble with this principal. In spring 2010 the district held a class for teachers to grade in this way called "What is Pickering Grading?" So I gather this is being pushed district-wide. We have many low performing kids at Prospect, but lowering our standards is not the way. Change isn't going to come by teachers as they are frightened by the principal. If you are a parent then look for yourself on School Loop. If you see A LOT of 50% it may mean the assignments were not done at all yet 50% of the credit was still received. Write a letter to the superintendent if concerned. if your child choosed the right people to be friends with and focus on academics while of course having fun and making use of all the opportunities this school has to offer..your child will go far! school has a wonderful staff and AMAZING principal! she is new but making so many advances! make it count panthers!! Our child finished her first year at Prospect this month and we are pleased with the academics, sports and activities. She is an above-average student and was challenged with her courses. Due to an outstanding teacher, she even found out that she really enjoys science and may consider majoring in that when she attends college! Sports are competitive, but not as intense as many other schools, so many students are given the opportunity to participate on a team. Lots of clubs and an active student government group. Very diverse population of students which prepares our children for the real world. Wish there was more parent involvement, but those that are involved are very committed and outstanding! Excellent school ! My child completed 4 years at Prospect Excellent in academics as well as sportsmanship!!! Very friendly and helpful staff!! We have a senior at Prospect busy with his college apps and he wants to minor in English because of some of the amazing English teachers he has had over the past 4 years. He wants to minor in History because he had amazing History teachers. He has chosen Sciences for his major because of his interactions with great Physics, Chemistry and Biology teachers who are passionate about their subjects and share it with their students. The Math department has very good people who know their subject but when it comes to teaching strategies, some are good teachers and some are not. (I have seen this problem across the board in other school districts too where many Math teachers do not know how to present their subject material in front of a teen- many Math concepts are very subtle). All the 4 years we have been here, we have always wondered why this school does not get the community support and high regard it deserves. We have a new principal this year who was the previous VP and she has her heart in the right place (kids come first). But what her style of administration would be is yet to be seen. Took my daughter out of this school midway through the year because it was clear that staying at the school was a waste of time. People who say this is a good school are in denial. The freshmen honors classes-English and biology-are fairly good. The teachers maintain order and the material makes you think, rather than only memorize. The English teacher is an engaging teacher who thinks of fun assignments. My biology teacher is a gruff old man with a soft heart. The Spanish department is atrocious. We do exercises in the workbooks for the whole period. The teacher does not teach. Kids who are retaking the class crack bad jokes and disrupt the class on a daily basis, without facing any consequences. If you truly want to learn Spanish, you must be self-motivates and teach yourself. The geometry teacher that I have is rude and condescending. Though we do learn in this class, he talks as though we are stupid. The atmosphere of this class could definitely be improved. The kids here, in general, seem to be hurting and act very angry. They swear constantly and revel in crass humor. There is a very low expectation for their behavior and maturity, sub-standard to other high schools in the vicinity. To sum it up, the honors teachers are worth your time, the Spanish department should be evaluated and dissolved ASAP, and the general atmosphere on campus is not pleasant. Prospect is gifted with a diverse student body, excellent teachers, a beautiful campus, and great extracurriculars. The sports teams such as track, tennis, and field hockey are consistently powerhouses, and extracurriculars like mock trial and debate seem to be doing well too. Unfortunately, the new principal seems uncomfortable in her role and is unwilling to work with many teachers, weakening the previously strong AP curricula. Any student who puts in the effort can succeed at this school, as is shown by the students accepted to Ivy Leagues, Berkeley, UCLA, and other top colleges. Prospect has been improvoing every year. Our kid is a junior. The new pricipal is a bit week and I think the VP is also new. Very strong English teachers are Mr. Manning and Mrs. Churchill. Strong Spanish teachers are Mr. Tejada and Profesora Adler. Good math teachers are Mrs. Ahmad and Mr. Igoe. The teachers care about students and help at Study Hall and after school. Our daughter has been involved in sports , music and Mock Trial. Prospect has a lot to offer the motivated students. Things are getting better every year. Prospect has excellent teachers, a very good and supportive administration, a good sports program, and good after-school clubs such as robotics, speech and debate, mock trial, among others. There are a lot of opportunities for students to excel in this school; however, not many students seem to participate in the after-school clubs (although the number has been increasing over the years) - so parent involvement may help. My student began school by joining a sport and got to know a group of kids that were focused and driven to do well. She is genuinely enjoying her High School experience. The staff appear to actually care about their success in school. We have been pleasantly surprised by the leadership & community at PHS. There are more than enough opportunities to excel and have your student thrive here. I was a student at prospect for all 4 years. Loved it. Some teachers were that great but you will get that. I had some wonderful memories , I will never forget Great overall experience. My son has learned a lot, grown in confidence, and should be university bound! Prospect is a truly amazing school we’re kids can challenge themselves at any level of course difficulty, while having great athletics or arts experiences. My son is taking 12 AP classes. At the same time the school is taking steps to bring disadvantaged kids to improve their participation in AP classes. The school has a tradition of music kids being selected for All-State bands and orchestras. If you are looking for an environment in which your kid can be challenged without loosing perspective of the world, and that no everyone comes from monetarily rich environments, look no further. Can a school be worse than this one?I despise California public education and this school is no exception. Unfortunately and against my wishes one of my children ended up in this HS. I don't like just about everything, but I will go into details- curriculum; for some subjects like math, it is non-existent; CA Common Core is the worst material I've ever seen. However, if there is some kind of curriculum in a subjects other than math, we're running into the problem of "educators"- teachers: I'm sure there are great teachers even in this school, but my child hasn't been lucky with many. Pre-calc teacher has been absent mostly this year. She had a baby. You'd think that such important subject as pre-calc would have a substitute and it did, 3 of them. Then the teacher "came back", but IMO she is still mostly on-leave. Her communication usually is "I will not be in tomorrow; Here is the list of 15 items to complete". Another teacher grades everything after final grade is due. I never know how my child is doing looking at the school portal. On May 25 the student can have A and on June 1 it can be C because the teacher placed work done over 2-3 months into the portal- cell phones and school computer: I know I'm alone here, but private schools handle phones just fine; two of my children attended two diff private schools and both had "no cell phone policy". One can bring the phone, turn it off and place it in a locker. If there is an emergency to use the phone, it can only be done in the office. School computer can't be monitored by parents. The student has access to everything 24x7 for any length of time- lame snow-flake attitude by administrators: children are required to be politically-correct, non-offensive, etc., however if someone breaks the rule and further poor behavior could be prevented, nobody cares- services: anything out of the ordinary will take a battle; many reminders, follow ups, and long wait. There surely be a reason for it. Then the service "will be provided" on paper, but in fact it would happen so occasionally that it is not possible to call it a serviceThis school is not special. The entire district is awful. There will be children who will do ok in any environment. I have one of those and I'm considering sending this child to this school only because of the location and sports; certainly NOT b/c of academics. This child will complete HS curriculum in 8th grade, but I'm considering Stanford on-line and other private options.

column1: this school is 100% amazing. everyone loves it here. hardly any drug problems, as opposed to the many at shepherd hill in nearby Dudley. nobody drinks here, hardly any smoking. none on "campus" and all around amazing. everyone is willing to help you here. it is utterly amazing. No care is shown to the kids who need the most help and they could care less. Girls in this school are discriminated against and treated like dirt. There is very little access to people who are disabled, the school's layout is extremely confusing and you can easily get lost. Freshmen and Sophomores are shown no respect while seniors are treated like gods. Just stay away from this school if you are anything other than a cis, straight, male because everyone else in the school is treated like they don't matter.

column3: Nederland middle senior high was a great place for all my children. A wonderful community school! This school is small, but the staff is great and students are given an individualized school experience. Students are given access to all necessary resources and leave feeling prepared for the lives ahead of them. I'm sad that parents aren't allowed to be involved in their child's learning and teachers can choose to not talk to parents - everything has to go through the principal. Most teachers are amazing - but the administration should be protecting students - not just the teachers. I am a current student at NMSHS, and I really couldn’t imagine a much better experience. The school has AP programs with far above average passing rates, and because of the small size of the school, teachers and students can really get to know each other through the years. This really helps students stay motivated, and when they fall behind, most teachers will do anything to help. There are also several extracurricular opportunities, including an incredible theater program, varsity boy and girls soccer, volleyball, basketball, debate, art clubs, cross country running, track, and because of the school’s close proximity to Eldora ski resort kids are able to join the Alpine(downhill) or Nordic(cross-county) ski teams, along with an all school ski-day in the spring. Once again, the coaches and teachers care incredibly much about their students, and the coaches and teachers we have are all dedicated to the school and Nederland Community. Online learning has definitely been a challenge for anyone involved in education currently, but our school and our district has handled it well, having already had several online platforms in place, showing that they are prepared for whatever has happened. As a student, I have had the chance to meet the superintendent of the district, and even shoot a few PKs(soccer) with him, the district has also always listened to our input on funding for specific programs, and even in choosing staff members. Our school is very close knit, and it is easy to make friends. I have gone to Ned schools all my life and have no plan to do otherwise.

It all depends on the student effort and dedication I think the school is very diverse and little bully. Teachers are amazing and strict. I have had four children attend this school, one of which was a valedictorian from the IB program. Three of my children have been active leaders and involved in extra-curricular activities and sports teams. There have been three or more principals during their years there. My experience with the personnel at this school has been very negative. I have two older children who attended Littlerock High and the experience there was very positive. The staff at Highland are rude to both students and parents. The good teachers are few and far between. Parent involvement is nill. There is no communication to the parents about getting involved. The new principal (Ford) seems willing to change this atmosphere. I hoping his professionalism will be reflected in his staff. Teacher training and staff development are sorely needed. My son has been going to Highland High School for the last 4yrs. He is graduating this year. I personally was very skeptical when he started but the teachers he has gotten through out his 4yrs were Super excellent. He is a 4.0 student. The teachers are great. They work with the student and expect excellence from them. They are tough but great (awesome teachers). I think that the new generation needs some tough love from both parents and teachers. If they don't receive that they tend to go in the wrong directions. The teachers care a lot about the students at Highland High School and us as parents need to give them a lot of support and credit for what they have done for our kids. This school started going down hill YEARS ago. My brother was transferred here when the school first opened, it was great then. A few years later I was there, and it was nothing like it was for him. Dirty, crowded, and hostile environment. My baby sister graduated 2 years ago and said things are even worse now. I won't let my children attend HHS. Amazing extra curricular classes and teachers that actually care about students and their success! Mrs Sell is one of the best English teachers in the AV. This school has really started turning around since 2015-2016...my older kids went there in the first 10 years it was open and it was a really great school. It really went downhill after that, though. There is now a new principal and he is very pro-active and has implemented some cutting-edge programs that have set this school apart from all others. It has turned the corner and is now a great school again...the students and teachers are wonderful and we feel completely comfortable sending our youngest set of kids there now. Also, the band program is one of the best in Southern California. Most teachers just care about their paycheck and will push kids into depression and anxiety. column1: This sound like a great school I would to get more information on it.Thank you Even though the school has a reputation for being violent, its probably because the school is poorly funded. I talked to a senior today and asked where there going for there senior trip, I was told there going to an arcade place. Also while i was there I asked how does it feel to be a senior, an I was told that it feels no different from all the other grade levels. Harlan's rep. Is bad but in reality it's really good school. They have caring teachers, and great programs such as the engineering program and academic center, I've read most bad reviews versus good ones....my son applied to harlan for the fall because they offer web and game design. It's not our neighborhood school, but I do want my son to learn something that he's interested in, while in HighSchool...do you recommend this school? Being a recent alumni of Harlan, I must say that it isn't as bad of a school as it's reputation gives it. It has definitely gotten better from when I entered in 2007 to now. There are caring teachers & faculty who try their best to push students to learn the necessary tools to continue into their college careers, but students rent very acceptive to it. The post secondary department were adamant in getting students into college by making it a requirement to apply to 5 colleges of the students choice. The AP/Honors classes does an excellent job at preparing students for college level work. I was doing work that I am doing now in college back in high school. I am very thankful of what I've gained during my 4 years at Harlan. It has developed me into who I am today and prepared me for my current college matriculation. This school is a school to didnt impact my child's High school education I personally believe that this school need a few changes and this school needs a entirely new faculty and staff because my child came home every day and didn't have and homework or even any books or nothing in her bookbag and this concerned me alot . So I went up to the school to talk to the Dean and all her teachers and as I enter the school I see young men pants below their waist and I here them yell out many foul words in front of security guards and they just stand there with no intentional remark or response and at that moment I could see that the faculty and staff members doesn't take pride in their work and the students doesn't take pride in their career and education, now don't get me wrong the school has a couple bright and intelligent kids and teachers but majority of the kids and teachers need an intervention. Now as I talk to my child's Dean she explains to me that this school isn't bad and our faculty and staff members are very important and intelligent when it comes to children and that's pretty much what her teachers said too. All I'm saying is that all schools should have the best faculty and staff members and students that take their education and job serious but Harlan doesn't it is completely different. My child is at butler college prep now and she is doing tremendously great she is a senior and is about to graduate with a 3.6 gpa and I'm not trying to brag or nothing like that I'm just sharing my story about Harlan.

column1: The school has greatly deteriorated over past 3 years. Standards have lowered. Instead of getting kicked out for smoking, etc...students are given in school suspensions. Not special enough for the money. Probably why enrollment dropping drastically over past 3 years. The leaders are pretending to be Christian but are only Christ like some of the time. I used to want to go here, but if you speak up and point out when someone doing wrong - you are labeled a troublemaker. They like to brush things under the rug and pretend they didn't happen, just like some other churches. People are tired of it, probably why we have less and less students here every year. I am so thankful to have attended BMA. My family is a huge supporter of Christian education. These past few years have been such a blessing. The staff truly care about the kids and want them to not only have a good education but also learn more about Jesus. I highly recommend BMA! My kids, both very creative and dedicated, were fed by the different staff personalities at this school. Both have moved onto college with ease and have represented their Alma mater with pride! From the school setting to the philosophy of helping students learn academically, socially, vocationally, and most importantly spiritually, they have lived up to their motto: Distinctly Academic; Decidedly Christian! This school was my life for the first 20 years (8 years in the elementary school). I don't think I could have grown up in a better place. Great academics, wonderful music, all in a nature setting on the Appalachian trail. I would rate my experience a 1/5. This is the worst school I have ever attended. I cannot believe I will spend my Junior year here. What a wasted year. I would never look back into my life and reminisce about Junior year at Blue Mountain Academy.

column3: YCHS is a school where you would want your child to be! The new school facility is amazing -- probably the best in the state! I'd invite any former graduate to return for a tour so you can see how far we have come! I enjoy going to work every day -- the administration is supportive and student-focused. We have a great group of students, too! I have 2 daughters that attended York Comprehensive, one that graduated in 2010 from the former high school and one that transferred in 10th grade to the SC Governor's School for Science and Math. As every parent wants the best for their children I am without exception. York offered a great connection and very hands on interest in both my girls allowing them to be the best possible students while encouraging and supporting their interests. The advanced courses offered are top notch and the extracurricular activities are abundance meeting a wide variety of interests. Our children have fund memories of most teachers with the exception of a math teacher that was very hard for students to understand, (which we are confident is retired by now), as well as an overloaded guidance counselor we were assigned to. The school building, technology center, and athletic fields are state of the art and represents the look and feel of a university. The district spared no expenses for their students, teachers, or faculty. Our oldest graduated college with a biology degree and our youngest is graduating from governors school this year. York Comprehensive was a great experience for our family.

column1: Awesome! The majority of the teachers are helpful and I really enjoy the curriculum. I used to attend Hartford schools and was bored and could not stay focused. In Slinger, I have a lot more fun. There are events in which everyone is involved, it is less clique-y, the rules are not too much nor too little. I am a junior and have been here since 7th grade... I've rarely been disappointed. In general a very helpful staff. Students get help whenever it's needed. Love the small town enviornment! This school consists of middle school kids who transfer to the high school. No diversity or desire to step out of their "best friend circles." The teachers are hit or miss and the counselors are horrible!!! No advice whatsoever. All good if you never need anything, I suppose. Literally e mails and calls go unanswered for weeks and to sum up: Administration does NOT do their job and trickles down! How it is rated a 9 we have no clue! Biggest mistake ever to go here! We are moving to get out of this district - that is how crummy it is!

column3: Great school!!! North Penn High School offers something for everyone. Hundreds of clubs, activities, sports a music programs. Academics are unbelievable. Course curriculum looks like a small college. Unlike private school, NPHS does not discriminate and they accept all students, regardless of their academic ability. They truly are dedicated to educating all students from varied backgrounds. Great school!!! Many of the kids (especially sophomores) need to learn how to grow up. Half of the kids are talking about drama affecting their lives and are causing the classes to become uninteresting. My son goes to Judge now and while he went to NP, he HATED it. He said that although NP is a public school (which means that everyone gets accepted), some people don't deserve to go there. He said that Judge is so much better than North Penn, and that he recommends NO ONE to go there,at least go to HH to CB. Overall, horrific, and they should split the high school into at least two schools. WAY TO BIG! I am a student at North Penn and I love it here.There is a variety of many different things to do.No student is limited but they are pushed to reach for the stars.Their sports teams are really fun.This school is big but it makes it a great opportunity to make new friends.I recommend that more students should go here.The teachers are GREAT!!!I love them!! HUGE MISTAKE MOVING HERE!!! Have a child with SPECIAL NEEDS and the district has been EXTREMELY UNSUPPORTIVE and causing us an alot of unnecessary STRESS!! THE WORST DISTRICT we've ever dealt with!! We questioned the bad reviews and didn't think it would be so bad but IT'S MUCH WORSE!! Apparently this district only "LIKES" kids who are wealthy, athleticy gifted, or academicly above their peers. They have treated us so POORLY!! I have NOTHING good to say, I'm so very disappointed for my family and my child. Horrible school district for kids with special needs.....Has caused my family great stress...I liked it before when north penn did not have a class available for my child with such extensive needs because of her level of disability..... they were forced to send my child to surroundings school districts which h were much better My child's teacher makes every possible way to try and make me feel like I'm a bad parent....When I have been told by multiple doctors if it was not for me she would not be alive....I'm disgusted especially for the fact if you ever try to make a complaint it's like they don't care....My child's teacher believes it's ok to tape confidential and embarrassing health information about my child to her wheel chair where everyone can see it.... -Disgusted parent I think the overall academics at the school is great. However, my son was denied lunch because he didn't have $0.40 in his lunch account to pay for lunch. The lunch lady put the lunch away, told him he has $0.11 in his lunch account . It broke my heart to know he did not have lunch. I could have given him money if I knew the account was low. What kind of person would send a child back to class on an empty stomach, because they didn't have $0.40 to pay for lunch. I called the nutritional office, and they were of no help. I called the superintendent's office, she told me the cafeteria manager would get back to me. No one got back to me. I had to go pick my son up at school. He didn't have lunch and was not feeling he could continue the day on empty stomach. I hope the person in the cafeteria is reading this, and know that you are a heartless human being. The school does not exist to make a profit , it's for educational purposes. Overall a really good school. Absolutely outstanding academics. A wide variety of elective classes. They even have JROTC! More clubs and sports than you know what to do with. The only problems are that the school is too big. It's easy to get lost in the crowd. If a student has a problem (academic, medical that affects their academics) they have to advocate for themselves, parents need to keep on the counselors and teachers. I moved to the district because of this school and so far I haven't been dissapointed. It is a really good school. Absolutely outstanding academics. A wide variety of elective classes and programs . They even have lot of clubs and sports than you know what to do with. . I moved to the district because of this school and so far I haven't been disappointed. Hands down the best public school anywhere for music education. My child went to Inglewood Elementary, Penndale Middle School, and of course, North Penn Highschool. The teachers at all of these schools encouraged my son's love for music, and now we are looking at possible music scholarships for college. If it were not for Ms. Jordan Fletcher, Mr. Robert Kennedy, and Mr. David DiValentino I'm not sure my son would ever have picked up a musical instrument let alone pursue a career in music. I could not be happier with encouragement and education that my son has received at this school district. Worst school possible!!!!! Only cares about its rank!!!!!! Great school would really recommend it. My child has lots of fun and is very happy with the school he goes too.

column3: Most kids go to college from this school, with a handful going into the military and trades. The school is the center of the community and it's small semi-rural/semi-suburban setting has effectively insulated it from a lot of problems seen in other area schools. There is a good demographic mix and there does not seem to be economic pressure on the kids. It is socially a great, safe place for students to learn and make friends. Most teachers are excellent - a few need to go, but this is the case in every school. They have strong athletic and arts programming, and contrary to older reviews, they a new performing arts wing. Arts programs are well funded. My only complaints are that the English writing curriculum is very weak. I've taught my son to write at home as he was earning A grades for what I considered to be C papers. The deans suspend many kids when a simple "knock it off" or detention would do. They are strong in supporting kids in special ed, but mainstreamed kids with ADHD, dyslexia or other less serious learning issues are neglected - 504s and IEPs are not implemented unless parents are on their backs 24/7 about it. They lack insight into these disorders. WHS has done more harm than good with my kids They were ill prepared for college, were not taught decent skills, study habits, etc. Special needs-HORRIBLE! say 1 thing, write another- if it's not in writing it didn't happen. 1 teacher in particular is ruthless and it's her way or move 'em out of her class Freshman year. Special Ed was poorly rated for implementation from a state service that came in to "help. Teach tolerance for that rather than ship them to sedol school. Not enough is done with drugs. Zero tolerance is a joke. Especially with football and cheer. They don't enforce zero tolerance with drugs or bullying. School and police work hand in hand, but not for what's best of the student usually. They just want to "look good on paper. The school NEEDS to cut out busy work, TEACH! IMPLEMENT an across the board bullying program, including assembly high school wide to address how severe it is, more drug sweeps, and improve S.E. services that are appropriate for the child and not just the ease of the school. Superintendent is Special Ed Lake County tho. . We liked the Grade School and Middle School, and the hard working staff. Parents are outsiders unless you conform. horrible school enough said, when your brother comes home tto tell u that his teacher said if u don't understand subject drop out wow just wow. If you have an honors student that doesn't need any help they will do fine. Everyone else better be prepared to run into conflicts with the teachers and administration. They don't like to have to do any work to help the students. I hope the state changes the union rules because half of the teachers will probably be let go. There not there to teach but just waiting for there pension and benefits. The teachers don't know how to explain their lessons. They expect you to understand what they say and if you ask to clear things out they give you attitude and get mad for asking again. If you fail a test the teachers don't care about it. They just give it to you and don't take an effort to ask what your struggling with. In the other hand there are a couple of teachers who do help. The deans and security staff are Very disrespectful assuming you are doing bad at all times. And the principal doesn't take action either. They yell at students for saying their opinions of what can help the school and say that we are "telling them how to do their job". Don't do anything about drug problems, bullying problems, and sexually active problems. There's so many things wrong with this school. They say they are a "good" school but inside the high school there is disrupt young adults who are going out in the real world and have no respect and think they are superior to others. I see no future in these kids because the high school doesn't take action in helping all of us out. Most of these reviews are old and many seem to be from people who seem to feel personally put upon or are whining about some incident. As a resident if Wauconda township, I have worked with the Future Business Leaders of America club and have found the students, faculty, and community members to be exceptional! They are the largest club at the school and 8th largest chapter in the USA. This year, after participating in rigorous regional and state competitions, they are sending 20 deserving students to the National Competition. These students QUALIFIED for this honor in competition. It is a significant achievement of national importance. Quite often in high school students do not perform well. The tendency is to blame the school when the real cause is the student or the support they get from their parents. Motivated students supported by parents, teachers, and the community are what creates successful schools. These students have brought repeated honor (the club has only been in existence for about 5-6 years and they have gone to Nationals 3 or 4 times) to the school based on their knowledge, skill, drive and determination. We live in a small town with a big heart - and that transfers to our schools. It's wonderful to be in a school system where everyone knows everyone - it takes a village. Our teachers are top notch and dedicated, our school board is extremely knowledgeable both financially and educationally, our school staff welcoming and encouraging. There are many clubs, activities and sports available for many different aspects of a child's personality, and there is even a late bus to bring your child home if they are involved in after school activities. For older kids several of our schools are within walking distance of Main Street, the heart of Wauconda. My children have thrived beyond my expectations - couldn't be happier to be living in Wauconda! Great school overall. Have had teachers and coaches reach out to us. My kids enjoy their classes and teachers and are challenged. Great AP class offerings and 12 more are being added next year. There are also a plethora of other activities besides sports to be involved in for extra curricular activities. So many great programs are offered to students both academic and extracurricular. My child has been in the school district since kindergarten and we couldn't be happier with the quality of education received. I am an "All of the Above" commenter. I attended this school, my son attended this school, and I coach the High School Academic Team at this school! I value not only the education I received here (I became a teacher myself) but the character of the students and staff here. Our children are raised to believe they are part of a "First Class School" and a "First Class Community". They truly live by this credo. Right now, we have one of the largest FBLA clubs in the country, and those kids work hand in hand closely with our local Chamber members. This town in truly invested in our students and they already know how to give back! Wauconda High School has given me a unique experience that I would not find elsewhere. I plan on studying Actuarial Science and Wauconda has fostered that growth tremendously. They have a phenomenal FBLA and Math Team. These clubs have been vital to my college preparation. The beauty of Wauconda is that this is simply my story; there are hundred more just like it. All students have a club, organization, or sport that they turn to. I am truly proud to be a student at Wauconda. I have had two boys attend Wauconda High School both one very good student and one with special needs. Both were treated exceptionally well by all staff at Wauconda high school. This is a school where the students are kind hearted, warm and where my boys have made their lifelong friends. Both boys are now attending college and much of their success there can be attributed to the wonderful support and experience they have had at Wauconda. Great teachers, extremely helpful staff , with every conference, phone call you fell fully informed about your kid . My son was a transfer after freshman year and I couldn't be more happy about Wauconda HS ! Wauconda may be a smaller school compared to others in the area, but this can be a great advantage to students. Since kindergarten I was enrolled in D118 schools. The honors track greatly prepared me for my success in college. There were many opportunities to get involved at the school and receive great guidance from teachers and staff. I am now in a doctorate program and have to offer my sincere regards to the community and district for preparing me for where I am. The review from -a student. Sounds exactly like my daughter. I even thought it was . Only it was written almost 2 years before she started. This school is the worst place you could ever send your child. Its my daughters first year and she has suffered bullying and it has taken her way down. Its excruciating to watch. Her grades are down shes asked for help but nothing. I am a current student at wauconda and I love going there the staff and students are so nice and caring. The school is big on their spirit. Our sports teams we are pretty good. Considering that our wrestling team got 2nd place in state and our dance team got 8th in state.. but hey that is pretty good. Some people are not big fans of the school because they tend to get in trouble most of the time and the staff does not like it when you disobey them or if you are rude towards them, so they will give you the consequences you deserve. All in all, I think wauconda is a great place I made awesome friends and memories there I'm sure going to miss it once I graduate. Good teachers, malicious students, major bullying, dirty school. This has got to be the worst experience my child had in his entire school experience. The bullying was horrific despite my constant calls for something to be done about it. Two teachers bullied him as well!! This is NOT a first class school and never will be. The Principal and the Assistant Principal were useless. The Assistant Principal at the time was mouthy and kept telling the kids they were going to jail. It seems that rather than have any compassion for my son's learning difficulties due to the bullying, the answer was to ship him off to a Sedol school. He missed out on classes he would have enjoyed. The guidance counselor he had was so misinformed academically and left me wondering why he was in that position in the first place. There was more damage done than should ever have happened. There is not, and most likely never will be, an extensive No Tolerance Rule for the bullying. When you have a teacher who is a bully, and who tried to enlist another to do the same, there is something sick and wrong with this school. It was reported and nothing was done about it. My biggest regret is enrolling my child in this school. Wauconda High School is a great school, some people don't like it, but they just need to make the most of their experience. No school is going to be perfect and I don't think a lot of students, or parents understand that when they give this school a one-star rating. This school has presented me with so many wonderful opportunities to get involved and travel. This school also offers a vast array of different classes to take. The staff is great too! Beyond Horrible, please contact parents with students attending this school before moving into this district or enrolling your children in this institution. I went to WHS , It was a great school that I attended. It had all i needed, such as books and materials and great teachers. i graduated 2019 , i really miss my home school . i will i went back there Both of my children thrived at WHS and are currently in College and one is in Grad School. Some great teachers and nothing but good things to say.

column1: Lovejoy High is in need to have organizational skills, to this date schedules are not completed, books and materials are still missing in action, and the students are not guided well in what courses to take. I feel students do not have equal opportunities. We need to unite as a village. There's a need for more college connections to mentor our students. LoveJoy High School. I am willing to change my address so that I will not be in this schools' district. TERRIBLE COMMUNICATION. These faciliators have DR in front of their names and it makes me wonder... WHY???? and are they above the possitions that they have.? They sure act as though they are LJHS is not a good school at all, they don't communicate with the parents or the students to let them know if they are on track for graduation and they don't care about the safety of their kids. The moral is very high. Their counselor are terrible. When you go in to speak to them about your child, they want you to stand up behind the counter to talk to them. You have one that got it bad, cause she don't like anybody to come in her office. She act if she's to pretty to talk in her office. The office clerk is rude. Only thing that is good is the IB program. It seems like they focus on sports only. I sub at this school and it was the worst experience ever. I have sub at other schools in clayton Co and had a nice experience. I subbed in other schools over metro atlanta and in other states and always looked forward to going back but I will never work at lovejoy again. The students are rude and undisciplined and disrespectful. And the staff was not helpful, the teachers looked stressed unhappy and hopeless. I wouldn't sub or teach there ever again Administration worse than the children. My children will NEVER go to this school again! I think I hate it more than they do. Really sad the way they treat the kids like criminals... this school need help! Their counselors who are supposed to guide the students into higher education don't care about the students welfare or opinions. They give no help with what schools may best fit a student nor do they encourage kids to go attend college. The only thing counselors are there for are checks and lunch this school is horrible. They dont care about the students. they have no supervision. My child is bullied here and when admin was in formed they did nothing. WORST SCHOOL EVER My child is doing good, and has good teachers. I stay In touch with all of his teachers. The staff is very unprofessional. The educators doesn't show ambition towards the students. The school and staff needs to be reassessed and go to more training to be proficient when dealing with students' education and the public community. I am a student at Lovejoy. Lovejoy High School is normally a bad school ,but everything is getting better. I have been at Lovejoy for 2 years. The school is only bad if you feed into the bad drama by hanging out with bad kids. Specially if you take regular or behind classes. We are trying to do our best at making Lovejoy great again ,because it used to be a great school. We are getting t-shirts and everything to walk around with to show off that we are trying to be better. We even made a hit song that deals with our Logo called (MLG 19) Making Lovejoy Great (Class of) 2019 This school has its up and downs it's really what u make out of it, but I would say they should do more cleaning of the school and do more in depth helping students with areas and subjects that everyone or occasionally struggles with more I am a resident of Clayton County and my daughter attended Clayton County public schools since 6th grade with straight A's & B's she is a recent graduate of Lovejoy High School with a GPA of 3.8 she qualifies her for The GA Hope Scholarship.. She was recruited by 11 Colleges and she has chose a College in Georgia so she can receive the GA Hope Scholarship, but do to the lack of Lovejoy High School involvement with doing their job no one has sent off my daughter information to financial aide and was suppose to start college in 3 weeks.. The college she chose is now saying even with the scholarship she was offered from their school, she will still need financial support so now my husband and I now have to take out multiple loans for college even after we have all tried to contact the officials all school year and summer to confirm she was receiving GA Hope and all counselors even teachers have told me her grades and GPA was qualified to get GA Hope. I am contacting you to help me find someone in Lovejoy High School to submit the (1) piece of paper to financial Aide which takes less then 5 min. and her GA hope will be approved in 24 hours, My daughter has lost out on housing opportunities on campus due to lack of financial aide.. Please Help me, get my daughter the financial services she was promised and has worked so hard for.. Thank you-- I would not recommend this school to any parent. If you come to lovejoy for sports the only sport they care about is football and track...if you play any other sport and want to come to lovejoy choose another school. I hate this school!! Clayton County School System… you need to shut this me doors on this zoo. No order, kids out of control, teachers don’t care! Nobody ever answers tge phone … this place is a complete joke. Kids smoking caps in the building, shooting bee bee guns in the classroom… where is the principal.. Mr. Jordan I’m shocked that you let this school operate in this manner. You ran Jonesboro Middle like a fine tuned machine . The superintendent can’t be aware of tge fact that Lovejoy high is a circus show. The absolute worst school I have attended. Teachers do not care, students just do whatever, and admin are barley any help. I transferred back to virtual this year because of the experience I had and my teachers rarely even logged into the classes. This school will tear you down rather than build you up. There is a bullying issue at this school. A lot of students don't respect their peers. Many kids are lonely and left out because of it. Most teachers are kind and helpful though, which is very important. I feel like less assignments could be helpful though. Extra work adds more stress and students nor teachers need that. Food could be better and the restrooms could be nicer. This school is the worst school my kids have ever attended. Teachers don't care about their students and counselors never answer emails or calls.

If students do not master , it is a reflection on them , teachers, & the district. Our legislatures need to be contacted.l As far as responsibility, that begins at home. Teachers can give lots of meaningful work, but students that aren't responsible don't do it. Do you fail them or wait? Low parent involvement is not due to the school not listening. It is due to low parent responsibility. There are many schools in Texas that enroll children. Excellent! Love the band and the science classes the most!

This school is great I feel safe when I go to school and its a real convient and by my house. All my teachers are outstanding My son has nothing but great things to say about your school. column1: This school had NO set curriculum when my kids were at this school, and admitted this when confronted by the middle school principal and curriculum director!! It's a useless school that dumb's down the grades to give the impression the kids are doing well - when they are not! Abysmal test results, poor growth, repetitive teaching over and over throughout the grades, and poor instruction by many teachers is why I give this school a TERRIBLE rating.. If there was a rating for BEYOND HOPE.. I would have given it that. Seneca is a great high school. Everyone knowss eachother and gets along. The education is good, you just have to apply yourself. College prep, honors, AP and dual accreditation college courses are offered. Extremely poor leadership at the district and principal level. The district is satisfied with mediocrity and drives away the best teachers. Does not punish students for harassment , racism or making threats.Very toxic environment for children.

column3: This school focuses on nothing but being the top school. Hah. Top school in the county? Whatever. Being on top, just because of test grades, does not make a school great. What makes a school great is how the teachers and other staff treat the children. Brighton High School is not that great of a school. This school focuses only on tests- They seem to believe that as long as their students pass the ACT, SAT, and a few writing exams that they've done their job. Also, their dress code is ridiculous. I have a 16 year old brother who makes straight A's and dresses very nicely for a boy his age. He has been 'written-up' three times in his Sophomore year for not wearing a belt. I mean, really? Is that necessary? Better hope your child does not have a problem with bullies because Brighton does NOT care!!! You can't get any help from teachers or administrators or school board to deal with the problem either. As a recent freshman and a current sophomore, I can say that this school is the place to be. The teachers are amazingly intelligent and they do a great job at what they are supposed to be doing. They don't just focus on ACT and SAT scores like recent comments have stated. BHS has a great school environment and I wouldn't want to go anywhere else. GO CARDINALS!!!! this school sucks. i have teachers callin me stupid. and they dnt teaxh anything except for act. thhere only worried about money for then. there not worried about our education!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Ive read all the reviews, but I havent read anything on the Special Education classes or if there is even a class for Special Education. Im thinking about moving to Atoka, and I kno that Brighton High School is where my kids would go. Any input on this issue or on the Special Education class would be greatly appreciated. I would love to hear from teachers,staff, students, and parents. this school is bad they dont care about students . it is full of rich kids that get what they want when they wont they are so many bullys it is not funny even teachers, my son was a straight a student untill bullys started beating him up and threating him if he told teachers even know this and dont do a thing if at all possible dont sed your child there mother of a sophmore gonna have to homescool from now on. In response to the SPECIAL EDUCATION issues I can tell you they don't help them much. Actually they make money off of them, giving them a "class" to make food (sausage and biscuits) and then selling it around the school. Then they try to stop us from telling the truth on here. By saying that they need to remove the school because the word is getting out about what they do and how they act.. IT IS SICKENING! This school does not care about the children individually. They care more about their ACT, test scores, and how the school looks on paper. The administrators, and some teachers, teach the students like animals. You don't have a name at BHS. You are referred to as "You!" I have read many reviews regarding the lack of action in bullying situations. This is because the administration is too busy worrying about whether students have their agenda books or if their capris hit their shins. I'm aware some people will just brush me off as some overdramatic student, but I actually used to enjoy learning until I hit high school. I now dread it every day and it has caused me so much stress. For parents who are thinking about sending their children here, please reconsider. Brighton High School is not a good school. My son was doing somewhat ok at the middle school and it's worse at the High School. Once he fell behind in Math, no matter how hard we tried, the teachers could care less. When the teachers don't care, neither do the students. They never called when my son acted out or gave me any indication there was a big learning problem for him. I was only contacted through email, and they mainly discussed his attitude and never his grades. I DO NOT approve of inappropriate behavior and correct this as well as I can. After the first notice of his shirt untucked , that was it, it seemed he was singled out and that's when the acting out began. I'm VERY happy to say that he is EXCELLING in alternative school. Wish I could keep him there. Turns out the math course he was in at Brighton High wasn't even the right one because the other math programs were full! Math was his main problem and they put him in ADVANCED math classes. What a joke. I'm going to try and get him in at Munford and hope for a fresh start. In response to Brighton High School is not a good school. You need to follow up with the Department of Education !!! If you don't this will continue and nothing will ever be done. The same has happened to several people, if they are forced to change their ways they will have to. Enough compolaints and they will take care of the entire staff. GET UP AND DO SOMETHING!! YOU WILL GET RESULTS!! They must have violated something.. The Department of Education can't do anything if you don't tell them. It is not an easy process and I wish I could contact you personally to help you with it but there is no way to know who is who on here. Those teachers gang up on the kids that are challeged with a subject, rather than educate them. You have to force them and when you do, don't back down. Keep pushing forward... they need someone to hold them as accountable as they hold our children. They did the same thing with my child they nit picked until he snapped and said it wasn't worth it anymore. It is really sad about the education. I bet the middle school set the path for you that is what happened in our case with our three children. Lack of leadership across the board. This school has reached a new low. However, if the student is a ball player or the child of a teacher then they are golden. Everyone else..... watch out. Education is not the primary goal here. I am truly shocked at how some of these teachers, coaches, and administrators have managed to remain employed. We moved to this area just for the schools, now we are looking to move elsewhere. For the military moving to this area, do your homework on Tipton County. If your not related to someone who works in the system or you haven't lived here for years, your children will not receive the same level of education or respect. Nepotism runs rampant here! Unsatisfactory is a complete understatement when it comes to this high school. Quite honestly, I am strongly inclined to agree with the preceding statement(s) made, and as a child in a military family that has not lived here all of his life, i can strongly assert the previous statements to be true. If you have any choice in the matter, go to Munford High School or be home-schooled. As a senior I am truly sad that my diploma has to bear the name of this deplorable institution. I am currently a sophomore at Brighton High and I am thrilled to be a Cardinal. I am inside this school every day, and I can most definitely say that this school provides a sense of security as well as family. We are now under new administration and they will not put up with some of thestuff our old principal did. I gave BHS a 5/5 because of the academics, school pride, and athletics. GO CARDINALS! The scores on tests at this school DO matter. They are very driven to making the students perform on the ACT. Maybe too driven. ACT is what gets the students into college, so it makes sense to push them in that area. They are one of the hardest schools in Tipton County, and also one of the best. Regarding bullying, my daughter was being bullied this year at this school. The school was VERY involved in ending that swiftly. They brought all the students involved to the office & talked to each one of them, then spoke with the parents and even other teachers. Then they called me over the next couple of months to check on my daughter to make sure that she was not still getting bullied. My daughter has a 4.0 GPA at this school. And she takes advanced, college prep courses and dual enrollment classes. She 'should' be on a 504 plan, but refuses. And she still made a 27 on the ACT. Granted, every school has their problems & sometimes they are just with certain teachers. This school has their share of bad teachers, just like all the others. But if you have a rowdy child that isn't interested in learning, send them somewhere else please! This school doesn't tolerate them well. :) Thank GOD! As a teacher I've had the opportunity to teach at various schools,small and large,and Brighton ,like all other schools, has its own set of problems. Not all teachers are great not all students are great. One of the largest problems BHS has is apathetic students and quite possibly these are the earlier posters and their parents that are ripping Brighton. "Favorites" may exist because of work ethic and want to learn or just trying.Teachers love effort and attentive students. The ACT is a big focus but talk to state govt about that. Life is an opportunity, make what you will of it.It's not easy at times and whining doesn't help My daughter just graduated from BHS and I totally agree with teacher's post. My daughter has attended 4 schools outside Tipton county since she was 6. I believe Brighton High School is one of the best schools in Tn, and anyone tht disagrees are students who are wanting to slack without goals set for their future. They should b thankful to have a school this interested in their success. It could b so much worse, we would know, we've been in a school tht was the complete opposite. We are so invested in the Brighton school system, that we are selling our home n buying land to build a home n farm n Brighton. We could move anywhere in Tn. , be thankful, you don't realize what you got!! I know teachers at this school that don't like it or what it is about. It is really sad, watching a good teacher turn to a very poor one is something I thought I would never witness. Going to church and speaking to a teacher that says that the school is unfair and not somewhere she would want their students to attend is absolutely ludicrous.Hearing a teacher that works at the school say that her children go to Munford because there is a better education and stronger chance that your child will just blend in is heart breaking. This school needs a major renovation starting from the top! That means with the administrators! They all act like a bunch of over grown teenagers! Very dramatic over very small matters acting as their children act a lot differently. This school get the pathetic award! As a parent of twins currently attending BHS, I would like to thank the teaching staff. There is help for the children who SEEK extra help! My children have both taken advantage of the after school tutoring program for the subjects of geometry, algebra and pre calculus. Regarding the issue of favoritism, all schools will be alike. Teachers are only human - just like parents - we all enjoy the children who seek knowledge, don't go out of their way to cause problems and are fun to spend time with. I am thankful that I am able to send my children to a safe school with teachers who do push them to do well on the ACT which is a determining factor for college admission and scholarships. Brighton High School is officially at an all time high. In the past years I have felt extremely highly of this school, but that has all changed. After a personal encounter with administration and other school leaders I am disappointed and dissatisfied with how certain situations are handled. It depends on who the child is and not the situation they are in. There is NO respect for parents and Administration is so focused on having each other's back they fail to do their jobs effectively. I would say that this school is an 8 out of 10. It is very good with advance classes, school clubs, and supporting teachers who care. My daughter loves it here. That is what makes me really happy. The school is amazing!! Great teachers and staff! Would strongly suggest students to go here! The staff was unresponsive to request for assistance on learning issues...Their phones are almost never answered and messages left are very seldom addressed...The school seems to lack any type leadership leading to a staff that just don't seem to care...

column1: This school is terrible-It may have been decent in the past but this school is absolute horrid now. The teachers aren't half bad, (except for the few that clearly show favoritism) but the coaches and sports facility gets all the special attention. They dont show the Drama or Arts programs any care. If your child is interested in the arts i would NOT go here, they have a terrible theatre department, and the arts are horrible. The administration is wretched too. If you're late more than 8 times (no matter what the situation is) they suspend you. And if you're late more than 3 times (every time after you're late) you go to ISS (which is a dumb anagram for basically saying they're going to put you in a room, and keep you from learning anything whatsoever, for the entire day) They're unjust, and won't give you any freedom of speech, and you can't do or say anything that gives you any personality. They've blocked off half of the things women can wear, it be revealing or not. I was told I can't wear my sweater because It's not long enough. That doesn't make any sense to me what so ever. (I was also wearing pants, i feel i should add) This school is terrible, do not send your child there. The vice principle Mrs. Pam Smith was more interested in pep rallies, home coming dances and reliving her own glorious high school days then education. If your child has any learning disabilities expect them to be pushed on to the next grade with no regard for the individual student needs. Fights and bullying are a constant in the hallways and bathrooms. If you have another option, take it. DECENT Because i have friends to get me through the day

There is nothing more important than "Beach Pride" and the principle facilitates this high integrity moral attitude in everything the children do. I am very thrilled that my daughter is fortunate to be attending the MYP program and look forward to her graduating from such a prestigious High School. What a rare opportunity to attend the same school for both Junior and Senior High. Go Minutemen!!!! Woo Hoo for Beach Pride!! I am a Cocoa Beach High School graduate with an MBA. My daughter, 2 nieces and nephew recently graduated from this school. Thanks to the IB program and the fact that the teachers challenged my daughter she has a patent on one of her science fair projects. Her cousin along with a couple of her friends proposed the dog park for the city of Cocoa Beach as one of their projects. After presenting their class project to the city commissioners of CB the Lori Wilson dog park is always packed with puppy's (thank you CBHS). My nephew has sportsmanship awards & fond memories of many special moments on the football field. This show receives an A+ in my grade book! I received a first class education at CBHS that prepared me extremely well for college. Best school in Brevard! Beach pride!! Great teachers. The IB Program is top rated, 35th best magnet school i the country. This school is ranked 18th best high school in Florida, 271st nationally. Terrible, I can’t imagine why anyone would rate this school 5 stars I rated this school because I had a bad experience with it. I guess like most school you have to deal with drugs, trashy bathrooms, rude people, but it was too much. I don’t think this school is a fit learning environment at ALL. I would rate this school 1 Star for GOODBYE! I don’t miss it I think there’s something seriously wrong with the people who work at this school

column1: I agree with the post from 9/22/10. My sentiments exactly!! There are a few amazing teachers here, but there are many changes that could be made in this school. Fantastic school with caring faculty. Your child will be prepared for college when they graduate. I am a student at Pensacola Catholic and I would like to say that this is by far the most amazing and helpful school I have Ever attended. As a student who attends mostly honors classes I do say that the teachers who have been here longer know what there doing and will get the student the best education. Whether or not the teachers are nice dosent matter its the education that matters and if you want to be treated better get out of our school or stop complaining about things that wont change. Sincerely, A student. While there are some very positive things about Catholic High, on the whole, I can't recommend it. I believe the the principal, while a caring and compassionate person, has been in the job too long. The majority of the administration has also been at the school for 10+ years. There is very little innovation. New ideas aren't encouraged. The cultural is "This is how we do things at CHS." I’m a senior at catholic and I can strongly say that I am glad my parents sent me here. The teachers are great and the overall enviroment at catholic is great. I wouldn’t trade the last 4 years for anything.

column3: This is the best decision i ever made for my child. she's going to keep going here until she graduates. I LOVE MCKEAN ! I cannot believe this school is rated 4 out of 5. It must be the bully students or their parents writing the reviews. My granddaughter (on her first day of high school there) have her lunch taken from her and things thrown at her in the cafeteria. She was called names and left in tears at lunch. WHERE WERE YOUR TEACHERS? WHERE WAS THE ON-DUTY POLICE OFFICER. You don't have to worry about my granddaughter we transferred her out of their - DAY 1. In speaking with others "within the feeder zone" they looked to private school rather than sending their kids here. I have 6 more grandchildren and you can bet they won't be going to McKean. You should be ashamed I had to give you a star to get this on-line - you get ZERO STARS!!! BEEN IN MANY DIFFERENT SCHOOLS IN THE LIFE BUT MCKEAN IS THE BEST SCHOOL IVE EVER BEEN TO !!!!!!!! McKean is a great school. Bullying is everywhere but in the past years McKean has really stepped up to the plate on doing there best to take care of every student. They have cleaned up their act and have built new improvements to make the children feel comfortable being there. They have more clubs and organizations than any school I've heard of. The teachers and staff made a huge difference in my high school career and if I could go around thanking every one of them I would. McKean is a grand school. This is my 13th year as a McKean Highlander. I served this community as a teacher, coach, and administrator. This school is such a special place because of the amazing staff that creates a family-like environment. Students can find their niche aas they explore our many opportunities of extracurricular activities in a very inclusive and accepting environment. From our state of the art culinary program to our student-led part-day preschool program to our Cable TV and FM Radio station; our Career and Technical Education Programs are some of the top across the state. Not only do we offer eight career pathways, but we have around 20 Advanced Placement and College Dual Enrollment course offerings. Our Distance Learning Lab, allows students to take courses not offered at McKean and taught by quality instructors across the district. Not only to we offer opportunities for students to achieve great things; but also, we provide a great deal of interventions and supports for struggling students. Through programs like Best Buddies and Special Olympics, McKean has a culture in which peers support each other and embrace our differences. Come stop by and see for yourself, the great things that McKean can offer you. Look, it's as easy as this: if you take the honors and AP classes and avoid troublesome teens, you'll have probably the best high school experience you could ask for. Simple. its okay unless you are an LGBT student no one does anything about that kind of bulling and even some teachers have used homophobic remarks I enjoyed my time there while I was there because I made plenty of friends and success was easy to find. During my senior year and during university I realized how poorly the school had prepared me for college. College bound students for any intense careers, such as medicine. The college bound students coming from McKean are not put into the best spots. AP courses are offered but not as many as should be. Overall the schools good if your just looking to get your diploma and have some fun.

column1: Washington high gets a bad vibe from the media but in fact it is a pretty nice school. The teachers care alot and almost all are friendly. They have a really great sport, band, and drama programs. Washington also has a great laptop program, that starts at the middle school. It is 8-12 grades, but 8 is seperated from the high school. They have thier own section and dont even see the high schoolers except when they leave for the day. The teachers try to help you out when you really need it and do everything they can to make sure you know everything to pass your hsa, and msa. The algebra teachers push you to learn on your own and help you when you need it. The prinicple enforces the school rules the second you walk in the door. Overall it is a really good school. The laptop program that students had was ended 3yrs ago the part that let them bring them home and all work was done on them They were only used at school then last yr they started using them less then this yr students were changed back to text books. The new superintendent said he hopes to make science & technology #1 and the use of smart devices in all students hands again but not just 6-12 but k-12. It is a good school small classroom sizes and teaches that put the students 1st androp will do anything to help the kids. The staff are friendly. They have a wide arange of sport teams and our band sounds good. There is rally any problems at the school between students and there is a dress code that requires uniforms. Also we have a county wide FREE food for ALL students program no question ask. Finally we have a great bus/transportation where as eventhough we live right across the highway our kids still get a bus. I am glad I move here Teachers are trying.The administration is awful. Need to be replaced.

I can not get my work done because the work is too overwhelming, last year I only had on homework assignment a week, my GPA was a 3.75 but i was out for three weeks due to medical reasons and it dropped to a 3.13. This year fights are occurring every day and students hang around in the hallway when they are supposed to be in class and uncalled for profanities to teachers and bullying has increased. it is the best school I have ever went to

column1: This school picks favorites. Better have money if you send kids here. Kids are bullied because parents can't afford name brand. When a kid plays sports you don't have a popular name get ready to watch them on a bench. Teachers well let's just say most of them are coaches. Only care about the ones with money or plays sports.

column3: The school is grossly deficient in terms of what they have to offer a learning disabled child. For the most part, they simply push them through the system with no regard for how well academically prepared the young student will or will not be upon graduating. I'm a former student, and I can say that WHHS is like most schools. You get out of it what you put into it. I was near the top of my class, took most offered AP courses, etc, and I was very well prepared for college. It's easily the best high school in the county. I don't mean to say WHHs is perfect mind you, like any school they could be better, perhaps by expanding offerings of advanced courses (they covered the basic social studies areas very well, but as college history major I wish there had been more social studies courses overall) and so forth. The school is also accomplished athletically, with the baseball and softball programs being especially good, though again they'd not be hurt by offering another sport or two. For their athletic prowess, emphasis on athletics is perhaps low, with only football, basketball, and cheerleading/dance getting dedicated class periods. All other sports are purely after school. The site's data is somewhat outdated, the school now serves grades 9-12, for example. My experience at this school was terrible! It’s easier for the principal to bully parents who complain then deal with the real problem. We look forward to the day we no longer have children in this district. We graduated from this school district. Our adult daughter graduated from here. Our son is about done. Over three generations of our family have experienced the good ole' boy system at work. The high school is no exception. If you want your student to have a strong high school experience, go over to Sheridan or take them to a private school in Little Rock.

column1: I would rate this as zero if I could. Where to begin? bullying. Lack of administration support. Zero assistance on special needs or accommodations for students not meeting the requirements. No support to help the kids. Even pass children who have numerous failing grades so their funding isn’t reduced.Multiple reports to OK2say with little to no action by the administration.If you do get lucky enough to have a newer teacher into the district who is amazing they will get burnt out fast or have to fall in line of the poor culture. They generally quit and leave within the year or two.The board of education is full of individuals who graduated from this district and are set on repeating the same narrative of lack of diversity inclusion and action to change the culture.Do yourself a favor and don’t choose here if you can. Far better choices close by (saint johns, Ithaca, literally anywhere else)
