column1: I'm currently a sophomore at this school. With the new additions to the high school, security has tightened and students respect the building. In 2012, the Academy section was finished, adding various programs to the school. The students are overall respectful, and the staff motivated. We have a new principal at the high school who encourages school spirit and has zero tolerance for excuses. Desoto High School has really improved since the last principal was here. challenge your child, my child had a great experience at Desoto..also he challenged himself by taking all AP classes, so he was not in a class with 41 students..His classes were small and comfortable but more challenging than what regular students attempted..you get what you put in..Teachers communicated weekly like I asked and he go a full scholarship to college, was 22 in his graduating class..4.29 gpa..I am proud he was an eagle.. I am a 2007 graduate of Desoto High School and I couldn't be more proud of that fact. Through the hard with if the president of the school board, Warren Seay, the high school has truly taken a turn for the better. The facilities are top notch, and the collegiate programs are very detailed and cover a great range of studies. I have two nephews that are on their way to three high school this year, and I know they'll be receiving a great education because we put in what we want out of it. I graduated with a full scholarship and an currently getting my Masters. DHS was pivotal to my success. DeSoto High school has changed a lot . If your child is low performance than you will have to be involved for them to succeed. You must be active . I have 4 kids so far to graduate , so this is from experience and you must fight for your child , because it will not happen . Schools are not the same its being ruled by people that are not in the class room . Teachers are under so much pressure that they cannot use their expertise like they where taught in college to teach our kids! DeSoto High School strives to educate all students and provide them with the tools they need to go to college or enter the workforce. There are many certification programs such as aviation, vet tech, medical, automotive, and culinary arts to name a few. DeSoto High School has the Collegiate Magnet Program and the Early College High School where the students have an opportunity to earn an associate degree while in high school. They also have the International Baccalaureate Program. My son is graduating with an associate degree. He also took classes in animation which will be his major in college. They only care about kids who can play sports. They do not do anything about bulling. They do not respect kids parents. If your child is special ed good luck trying to get them to follow their IEP’s. This district is worse than Dallas ISD. Overall, it was 7/10. Academic wise it was maybe a 5/10, but I was in choir and my teacher helped with whatever he could. This high school is a big ZERO. Do not send your kids there if you want them to learn anything. We moved here from Southern California and my 9th grader was an honor student at his prior school, at DeSoto high he was being assigned 5th grade work at best. The staff focuses on the delinquents, of which there are many, and everything revolves around trying to control all of the derelicts. There are fights everywhere and nobody at all does anything about it, they let everyone fight at any time.

column3: worst school I ever attended. They has you sorted out by economic class. If your family didn't have $$ you were not going anywhere. There were not many options or opportunities if you were not college bound. We couldn't get to our after lunch class in the time allotted because of the distance from the cafeteria so we got detention every day. THat put me home at 6 PM. I had to work to help at home.Consequently I could work or do my homework, not both. Couldn't drive your own car, just wasn't permitted. I will say however that Mr Blank and Mrs Blank (not identifying teachers as per the terms of use) helped a friend and I get into Marlborough Voc/Tech, Now Assabet. We learned a trade and earned a pretty good living. Marlborough treated us like adults. I remain forever grateful to those guidance couselors at NAshoba, (certainly not the school itself) and to the state of Massachusetts. I'm a graduate of Nashoba, class of 2003. Nashoba thoroughly prepared me for college and had an excellent curriculum. When I attended, there were electives which focused on business which included banking, economics, and entrepreneurship. They even had an actual bank branch in the school! Because of Nashoba I was able to get a part-time job as a bank teller (not bad for a teenage job!). I truly believe that the onus is on the student to apply himself/herself. I enjoyed the fact that the faculty did not hand-hold and coddle (but they went the extra mile to assist students seeking help). When I attended, there were various levels of difficulty (2-yr college prep, 4-yr college prep, accelerated, honors, and AP) for each core skill set (english, math, science, etc...). If any student mastered their level of difficulty they could advance to a more difficult level. As a result of this system, my transition to college was incredibly easy and I found that I was light-years ahead of other freshmen. Now, in my adult life I am a co-founder of a multi-million dollar business and I credit Nashoba for having courses which allowed me to explore my interests. My children graduated from this wonderful high school. They were more than prepared for college. They have many very challenging classes. The teacher's really care about their students. The theater, sports and other extra curricular are outstanding! The new principal has been a great asset to the high school too. The staff is generally very good but the overcrowding and the mismanagement of first the central administration and then a school committee that is trying to 'fix' the system has the school in a state of decline. I graduated from Nashoba in 2009, and the teachers and course offerings (as well as the extracurricular offerings) at that time were excellent. You can take classes at three different academic levels, and the highest-level classes are extremely rigorous, to the point that college was easy by comparison. I passed all of my AP exams for AP classes I took, as did the vast majority of my classmates. The only thing that disappoints me about the school, reflecting back on my experiences now, is that I was extremely depressed for about a year, and none of my teachers seemed to pick up on it or take action to get me some help. For several months, I was falling asleep in class daily, struggling to complete work, and doing poorly on tests. I had formerly been an A student, but no one seemed to find the drop in my grades concerning on a mental health level. Thankfully, I made it through that difficult year, and hopefully the staff has had some mental health awareness training since then. But in every other respect, you will be hard-pressed to find a better school for preparing students for college.

column1: The previous reviews were written before this year. This is the first year that Marshall is a turnaround school and they are making INCREDIBLE strides. Their attendance rate is up by nearly 25%, their hallways are clean and safe, the building has been re-habbed, the new staff is providing top notch instruction in the classrooms, and more students than ever are now involved in co-curricular activities and sports. I will not be surprised if test scores increase dramatically and if a ton more students go to college. Marshall is on its way back to its glory days of being one of the best schools in the nation because of terrific students, a committed staff, incredible alumni and parent support, and the hope that Waiting for Superman inspires. Go Marshall!

column1: Cardinal may be a small rural school but it puts students first. Each student has his or her own laptop provided by the school to help prepare them for the future. Classes are smaller to keep track of students academic and personal needs. Student's are goal oriented and can begin college classes as early as 9th Grade. We have terrific students who work hard. There are certain requirements to attain those laptops and is is typically for those schools who struggle. I have a very negative view of the school system. I do believe many have the students bet interest in mind but not sure if this balances out those who are too set in their ways and conceptualize children based on the cliques within the school and the community at large. I do not beleive that the school set students up for success in the past, at least not when I attended the school. I recall (as many people from around the nation do) being 'tracked' into non-college bound courses while sitting in a room with all students. It was degrading and based on performance, but perception of people who did not a clue.

column1: This School is where all 3 of my children graduated from. It is adequate but does not encourage kids to excel beyond the norm. All 3 of my children went off to college and have done or are doing well. I think Parent involvement is the key to a good education. If your child aspires to be manager of the local McDs when they grow up and top out, than its perfect. Otherwise expect to find your child was completely unprepared for even a 2 year college. I am currently attending my second year here and can honestly say that this school is not going to help me get anywhere within 100 miles of this place. There is really nothing offered here either as far as extra ciriculars unless you've already been doing it through madisonvile middleschool....If you had the misfortune of being relocated here there is nothing besides an average elementary school education that this school can provide. In geometry I am learning things that I have already learned in pre-algebra and everyday feel unchallenged and well retarded to be honest... The people here are rude ignorant and narrow minded with clearly no vision beyond the walls and confines of that disgusting little building. Do not attend this school.. I hopefully see myself perhaps getting some sort of job in the music industry, why? Because I am in band and that's the only scholarship I have a chance of achieving with my poor education that can hopefully get me the heck out of here.. I graduated from Sequoyah High School and I am currently enrolled at the University of Tennessee. Sequoyah offers great Dual Enrollment courses that have helped me during my college career. The faculty and staff are friendly, goal-oriented people that helped make my high school experience even more enjoyable. I was involved in sports and clubs, made great grades, and had wonderful friends that I am still close to today. This is an excellent school with positive, caring people! I was very excited about my kids attending Sequoyah High School when we moved here. I was quickly regretting it. This school is too small for the amount of students that attend. There are so many students that extra teachers have been hire but since there are not enough classrooms these teachers have to move around to an available room each class period. Now a portable building is being added next to the school for extra classrooms. With a student body that large and over packed classrooms the teachers have little control. It is not fair the teacher or the students. I am extreamly disappointed. I feel that my kids are being cheated out of an education where the class spends more time socializing and playing on cell phones than actually learning. This school needs to be divided into a Madisonville High School and a Vonore High School. On a good note, most of the teachers and faculty I have dealt with are very kind. I would not recommend a parent send their child to this School. The Students are definitely not prepared for entrance to college. When a Valedictorian of any school has trouble with college classes in Math, there are major problems with the High School they just graduated from! Horrible. This is the worst school I have ever been to. They do nothing to help their students. Drug abuse and dealing happens, students are not free to express themselves unless they agree with Christian values despite it being a public school. And they do not enforce equal treatment of students by any means. I can not describe in words how bad this school is, not only does cover up bullying but even with the highest gpa you can get here you will still be very unprepared for any college you can get into, nearly all the students here are addicted to something, there is no room on the bus's kid have to sit on each other's laps and are hanging out of the isle, why even make two highschools into one? All it did was make a overpopulated mess. You get bullied for everything you do, Do your kid I favor and don't send them here. i actually attend this school and i would like to say that it’s been fun BUT if you’re looking for somewhere to send you child, it is NOT this one. i stand by the freedom of religion and who you are as a person and i believe schools should do the same and this school does not do this at all. the teachers are horrible and i haven’t learned a thing. the ex principal we just had let kids run all over her. gays were given the freedom to do whatever they please but ordinary people are looked down on. bullying is also a huge issue. if you don’t have what is nice or in style then you’re automatically made fun of. we also have so many students vaping in the bathrooms and passing around drugs which causes a major amount of ambulances to show up. i 110% do NOT recommend this school, i’d send my kids to tellico before i ever would this place

column3: As a parent of a student who attends Cleveland's Humanities Magnet (also known as CORE), I would like to reiterate this school's wonderful qualities and address some of the concerns brought up in the previous reviews. First of all, this is indeed a rather large urban school with a population of 3200. That being said, the CORE community--made up of about 900 students--is incredibly close-knit, which makes for a nice blend of the small-town and big-city experience. Furthermore, though it is true that budget cuts have crippled many programs at Cleveland, the same can be said for most other public schools in LAUSD and across the country. In fact, thanks to the dedication of CORE teachers, parents, and students, the economic difficulties have had no detrimental effect on the education that my child and her peers receive. Finally, I would like to point out that Cleveland's CORE program was one of 28 schools all across America to win the National Magnet Schools of America Award of Excellence. Sending my child to Cleveland is the best decision I could have made for her. She is incredibly happy, which is not something most people can say about their high school experiences. The magnet program is academically strong and the teachers in the program are very good. The school administration, however, is extremely unresponsive. If and when you can get through to someone, they will be rude and dishonest. Don't believe anything they tell you about non-magnet class availability. Half the teachers don't even teach or know how to teach, they just fail the students over things they have not taught. Also the students there are all terrible and trying to fight everyone, especially the girls! No classy people at this school I can assure you. This is all coming from a straight A student so if you want your child to succeed I recon another school, much bullies here as well. Everyone even teachers are rude. People got arrested this year (2015) for bringing a gun to school. This school is not safe either. Cleveland is a great school, despite its negative points. I had problems with math in the beginning of the year but Cleveland offers tutoring during the afternoon and it's really helpful, now I have only straight As. My next year is my senior year and my counselor already set up everything and we talked about my graduation plan as well; Cleveland has a great team of teachers and staff, obviously there are a few exceptions. What bothers me a lot is the magnet program, where kids are taught they are awesome and extremely superior just for the fact of being there. Consequently, a great part of these magnet kids are arrogant, so if you are not part of any learning community this will bother your classes a lot. Other than that, Cleveland has a good infrastructure, good teachers, good programs and teams. Great School great scores!!! As a volunteer coach for Track, I can say that this school has the best team spirit in the league & students are amazing! This is an A plus school when it comes to inclusion. My daughter has special needs. Half the time she is in general education classes. My daughter loves attending Cleveland HS. Her teachers are awesome. I have two children in the humanities magnet. The experience for them has been so much better than I imagined - I knew about the emphasis on writing, but didn't know how enriched the curriculum would be. The discussions, the incorporation of experiences, the group work, all motivate the students towards writing. This program builds connections between people. The skills they build not only are a prep. for college, but for life. I am so glad my family made the choice it did!! If I had to do over, I would choose another school for my child. I like the themes and culture of the Core program, but the way it is run is not okay. Also , the autonomy given to some teachers is ridiculous. Yes, teaching styles will differ and are good but if your class is not preforming when these kids are overworked, where is the quality going to come from. The foundation is good, but the way that is run is not. Some teachers are arrogant and not willing to listen. Some comments made to my child this year were plain insensitive for a humanities magnet. My child is doing fine but at a cost of family time and rest. One extracurricular and your child will be up until midnight or later. Not healthy. My child is too far in and I have offered to move but too far in and friends keep my kid there. I see the exhaustion and anxiety in their friends eyes. I am highly disappointed. Admin step it up. I am not saying easier, I'm asking for effective without breaking a kid and a family. So in closing: Excessive useless work does not equal rigor. Admin should look into failing classes and revisit what is going on (not saying bad teachers, they get pushed around too, but some go too far). Make goal attainable for healthy students, body, mind, and family. Students are given too much homework. The amount of homework is outrageous. This is a terrible school. I would never, ever recommend it to anyone, not even my worst enemy. I regret enrolling my daughter here. I feel so terrible for the experience that she has had. Don’t send your kids here. Horrible Humanities Program. My daughter isin the Humanities Magnet Program at this school. It is disgusting how they confuse a lot of the children and have them question their identity. The Humanities Magnet (CORE) is progressive and open-minded, and I love that about it. HOWEVER, the amount of homework and stress placed on the students is outrageous and simply WRONG. I regret taking a couple of respected friends' suggestions and enrolling my child here. My child used to love extracurricular activities and being physically active. My child used to enjoy spending free time with friends. This is no longer the case. When not doing homework, sleep is the goal. Tuning out is the goal. I have suggested transferring to a few different schools, where the academic reputation is still excellent without overloading the students with homework and stress, but my child refuses to leave. My child doesn't say the words, but my child doesn't want to be seen as a quitter or someone who couldn't handle the workload, and my child doesn't want to leave friends behind. My child is getting straight "A"s, but at what cost? The cost of peace of mind, for my child, my spouse, and me. The cost of free time. The cost of extracurricular activities. The cost of family time. The cost of peace of mind. Scrolling back in reviews on this website, I see that complaints about the homework load go back years. If only I'd done my research, instead of listening to others!

column1: I am a former student of FRHS and I couldn't wait to go to school every day. This high school is filled with spirit and PRIDE. As a student, you can choose to be whoever and whatever you want when you walk through the doors of this school if you try. My teachers were amazing and taught me well. I went on and easily excelled in college. Thank you, FRHS, for some of the best years of my life!

column3: My son is getting an exceptional education at Holland High. He is an advanced student and in 8th grade is already taking Latin, advanced english, and algebra. He has been invited to attend private boarding schools but we feel he can get a better education here. I am a better person because of this school. There is a kid that comes from every background and we all work together. It’s so diverse not only in the different races and backgrounds, but also because football players can be in vocals and freshman can be in student senate.

column1: Axtell High School puts out college worthy graduates every year. The teachers are caring and their lessons are challenging. UIL academics plays an important role in developing strong minds at Axtell. Parent involvement can be seen in the full bleachers at the ball games. The Principle and Superintendant are always there to support the students, the teachers, and the community. It's a fun place that is full of school Pride. Go Longhorns! As a student I have had many problems throughout my schooling such as bullying, suicidal thoughts, and even have considered switching schools, but it would be entirely unfair to post a review and only hammer on what is wrong with this school I will say I love the teachers and most of the staff and I've been at the school my whole life never once have I left the school so I remember the old administration and I remember all of the teachers I've encountered. I loved my time here I hated to watch the suffering of others but honestly my first everything came out of this school when I look back I will smile and laugh at my memories. Here now it's my senior year and I'm leaving a lot behind. I enjoy the enthusiasm of the football players in the fields as much as the students in the classrooms. I feel it has a great balance between academics and athletics. With new things being introduced to the community such as its new mostly technology based system of operating I feel the school is taking to it well. This school will leave you with memories you'll never forget. I'm glad I went here honestly I wouldn't be the same person today without it this school built me it made me the person I am today and the man I'll be tomorrow. I think that if the school were to look into its students a bit more they may see the pain they hide. I want this to be seen because I've been helping people with suicide and people listen to me, but after his year I'm gone and can longer help those I currently have. So I want anyone who is currently an administrator or staff member at Axtell to know many of your students are struggling with suicide and they don't want to seek help they honestly want help to find them. So look for the signs and help before its too late. I've seen too many scarred arms. Anyone can stop it even students you just have to try.

column3: When I got my acceptance letter to Carver I was thrilled and glad to be part of Carver's culture. After a couple weeks I realized how much I hated that school. The primes are exceptional but the academics suck. I took two ap classes and got horrible scores due to my teachers who had no idea what was going on. I personally wouldn't recommend going to this school. This is a great school. My daughter transferred from a magnet school and she continued on in their visual arts program. They taught her very well at CCAT. She has developed her skills and is now making money while in college by selling her artwork and face painting. The teachers are very knowledgeable and they push the students to do their best. Carver Center is a great school. Its prime programs are exceptional. My son is excited to be led into the world of programming. He has learned VB, C++ and Java now, and he has determined to develop his own computer games. He has learned to build his own 3D trains and tanks that can be added into those famous simulation games. I was extremely surprised when I saw my son's train running on Microsoft's simulation railway. This is an exceptional school. Being part of the Carver culture is truley an honor. I didn't mind going to school because I was attending Carver. The teachers are understanding and want to help you so that you can be successful. Respect is something the principal and all the faculty stress since day one. The students are motivated to excel not only in their individual prime but also in all academic subjects. I suggest everyone to try to attend this school. I considerate it an honor to attend such a highly rated school in the areas of the Arts and academics. I wish everyone could attend a school like this for their high school experience. Carver is an amazing school; the teachers and staff truly care about every student and afford them the opportunities to excel. We feel so lucky that our student was able to get into and attend Carver. My experience was great the teachers where amazing and always super helpful and the prime teachers are some of the best people you’ll meet. I was at Carver and I am not impressed either by the staff or the academics. It tries to be very exclusive; however, not very special. Mostly students are comprised of teachers own children; so, they tend to exclude all other county students. Its a trade school; so, if you want your student to start working right after high school, then look for this one. It will not make your child a well rounded adult.

column1: i used to go here but my mom said it got torn down, unless that was a different academy, it was awesome there, and it was also the place i learned to climb stairs ( i didn't have any in my house ) we did cool science projects and there was a big open field, and again, i don't know if this is the right academy, and if it is i will be mad at my mom, because i was so heartbroken when she told me it got torn down. i have a book i borrowed from my classroom and didn't return, and when i smell it memories come to me. This is a good school with caring teachers and staff. If you are not satisfied with standard test results it does not necessarily mean the school is not good. The kids do learn a lot and are challenged. Teachers are doing their best. Most of the kids are polite. Parents are the power so be involved in your child's education. This school has really started to go down hill. The teachers do not respond to emails in a timely fashion. All this school cares about is getting money and focusing on growth, rather then students being able to succeed in their classes. They need to focus on small class size and get rid of the late start Tuesdays because most people go to work by 8 am and not 9 am. The high school of this school is lacking. Teachers are always quitting or getting fired. That is not good sign. Fantastic, progressive and dynamic school. Teachers are energetic and passionate about teaching. Our kids have been at the new North campus since it opened, and we love the school. The Promethium boards in each classroom are amazing - the kid's grasp of concepts is heightened by the interactive teaching. We love the technology used throughout the school - they are far ahead of where other Adams 12 schools are now. Kindergarten on up all have computers in the classroom and technology is a regular part of the classroom. All parents are required to spend at least 4 hours per month in the classroom, which helps to ensure Parent engagement and involvement. The teachers at the Academy are doing the best they can with what they are faced with. They are the bright spot of this school. That said, I agree with the other parent that has posted that the Academy has slid quite significantly in quality. They are packt like sardines in a tin can. The class sizes have ballooned to over 30 per class, and this is the new norm. Parents and the District decided to cut teacher pay to deal with the budget cuts, so they continue to lose good teachers. The State needs to increase funding drastically and it seems that Charter schools get less than public schools, so to deal with the screwed up system of funding, Charters are packing in students to compensate. I think that our legislators, Fed & State(and ignoramous Colo. voters who continually vote down increases in K-12 funding) have failed us and our kids! There needs to be a renewed emphasis on smaller class sizes, more teachers and more options like languages, PE and music offered to all kids. These TCAP tests are a joke and take up way too much resources and time. There should be testing, but not like this! We, as the people who are paying for all this chaos, need to put a stop to it! Lots of inconsistencies!! No transparency whatsoever. Lots of things have changed in the few years we've been here with no explanation. We lost a ton of great teachers and now we have a school full of new teachers that don't know the philosophy of school or the culture. The board is doing a very poor job of being transparent. Parents are not presented with the truth and decisions are made without parent involvement which contradicts the mission statement. Student's education is suffering as too many decisions are being made without proper consideration for the greater good. Not sure where the school is heading which is scary. We are definitely looking at other options for our children, which is unfortunate, especially since we waited so long to get it. I hope things can turn around! We were very excited when we were told that our child had been accepted into the Academy for Kindergarten. Little did I know at the time that the classes would be crammed with 28 students (the district max for K is 24), and our teacher was actually a substitute that they hired on at the last minute. After receiving several phone calls a week for figeting in class, talking with classmates, and not standing still in line, along with comments from other teachers that "that class definitely has some issues" and our observation of the class that was more like a seminary than a colorful kindergarten class, we decided to move him to a public school which allowed for kids to be kids. First of all I would like to say that my history with this school goes way back, as I am an alumni. I started at the Academy 4 years into its opening, it was small but it was wonderful! My daughters attend the school now and boy has it ever changed! All of the people who started this school and dreamed of better for students are gone. The new administration has no clue about how tight knit and inspiring this place used to be. The teachers are great, at least the ones that have stayed the past couple years. The budget cuts and subsequent loss of good teachers is awful! They are so concerned with raising money and passing tests, it's ridiculous. They are programming children not educating them. On top of that my elementary kids have at least 45 minutes to an hour of homework and reading, then I get emails from the teachers about logging on to take practice tests and nonsense. Eight hours a day is enough! If the work cannot be completed in 8 hours it can be finished the next day. The American education system is a joke and this school was started to give students the opportunity that isn't afforded in public schools, obviously we are just "another school" trying to pass TCAP. This school is a JOKE!! If your child has any type of a personality, I don't recommend this school. The Pre K program had my child doing things we had been doing with her since she was two. ( color sorting, lace up cards, learning the alphabet, and numbers to name a few.) They have a teacher in the classroom who's only purpose is to walk around with a clip board and write down the bad things every child does. When I asked the teacher for any positives, she had none. It's really not a very loving environment for four year olds! They ask for money in one way or another on a weekly basis ( on top of the tuition we already pay) It's a real disappointment for us, since we have had out child on the waiting list since she was 18 months, and now we have her at home where honestly she is much better off! I wish I could describe with words how much I truly dislike this school. In regards to the previous post, dated October 23, you must be talking about a different school. Second graders and third graders are not even at the same campus at The Academy...impossible for them to be in the same classes. By the way, your spelling is atrocious. Yes The Academy has faced cuts, as have all other schools. Yes, the American education system is a mess. What hasn't changed however, is the School's stance that their teachers and staff provide extras to keep every kid learning. There are literacy teachers who make sure each student is reading above grade level. The students still get two specials a day: art, music, pe, science, and computers. The character education program emphasizes respect, responsibility, etc. The math curriculum has each kid working at their own level, which also tends to be above grade level. The parents volunteer a ton to help both teachers and students. The PTO has really worked hard to create a sense of community and raise additional funds so that kids aren't off selling stuff like cookie dough. As you can see, we are content with the education our kids are getting. Alright, as a student you expect me to say that this is a horrible school. But, I'm not going to say that it's horrible. I'm just going to say it needs a lot of improvements. First of all, it is a great school if you are looking for an elementary school. Other than that don't even try. This year students/ parents have been battling the administration constantly about changes that need to be made. One of their big things at The Academy is that they are always improving, making it a college prep school, always trying to help you, promises promises promises... Yet they have about only two A.P. classes, the honors classes are just a name nothing more, and they focus more on test scores more than the individualized student. Also, class sizes are about 30ish students. I was in a classroom with 40 kids and a lot of us had to sit on the floor for about a month because they didn't have enough desks. The school is honestly not big enough to have a 3-12 grade campus. We have too many traveling teachers because there are not enough classrooms. I can list some many other things. However, I don't have space. All I'm saying is if you want to be constantly frustrated, I got the place for you. My daughter is in the afternoon pre-k program at the academy and she loves it! I have volunteered in the classroom so have seen a full day from start to finish. The teachers are kind and invested in the students but firm when need be. The expectations for behavior are high, but with the direction of the teachers, the kids do very well meeting those expectations. There is a good balance of academics, free play and outdoor play. I am impressed. I also should add that the parents of the children in the classroom are wonderful people. We are looking forward to kindergarten next year! This school needs lots of improvements. Most teachers quit there and got fired, all the high school teachers are young. Im just telling you about high school, and the stop light to the school is horrible. You'll wait at least 15 minutes when school starts. They alot of times shut down the school because of the recent conditioning problem (2-3 students passed out) and they closed down another time because of a leaking problem. There once was a flooding. They also had all the lights shut down a couple of times. Its just going down. I mean the staff are great and friendly but the school itself is horrible. there money is going low and they cant print alot of stuff. There also was 2 homeless teachers there!! They need to start fixing these problems. but otherwise a great community. Just needs improvement. This school is not all its hyped up to be. They rely on their reputation alone and do not care about the students as individuals. All classes are filled to maximum capacity (29-30 students per class, 3-5 classes per grade). It is a joke trying to attend a school event as the school is so overpopulated that parking and finding a seat to sit is impossible. Furthermore pickup at the main campus is a zoo! We withdrew our children from this school after dealing with rude teachers and a snobby principal for over a year. Not recommended! (Referring to Elementary, we have heard that it only goes down hill from there once students move to Middle & High School.) Look elsewhere, much better options available that provide students with greater attention and educational support in order to help them succeed. My child goes to the half-day Pre-K program at the Academy. We absolutely love it. My son has a fall birthday, so this is actually his 3rd year of preschool. He has gone to a different preschool each year (plus the Goddard School back when I used to work). I have to say that I have been amazed at the quality of this program compared to the other preschools that he has been to. There is plenty of time for play but also a strong focus on learning. It is obvious that a lot of thought has been put into the curriculum for each week. The kids don't do worksheets; they learn through art, activities, music, guests, games, etc. Every week the teachers change out all of the toys at each center to go along with the theme for the week. They even do tongue strengthening exercises to help with their verbal skills! The teachers also emphasize discipline and independence. The kids are taught to resolve their own disputes. I wish the rankings for the Academy were separated out by Elementary, Middle School and High School. My experience so far with the elementary school is that it is a top notch school and feel very fortunate have my son enrolled here. My child started the Pre-K program and I have been very impressed. My son has been able articulate and discuss subjects like Hellen Keller and MLK. In addition, he is only 4 and is starting to read. The other wonderful thing is "my child loves going to school and looks forward to it". It has been a great experience so far, and I recommend it. After being an Academy family for years, we are moving our youngest elsewhere. The school is overcrowded and is too focused on meeting the needs of the wealthier, more influential families at all grades. They say they have zero tolerance for bullying, but when even the parents are allowed to bully others over social media, then what sort of example are they setting? Little to no support for academic clubs. Total focus on PARCC scores at all grades and no problem or inquiry based learning (so it's all rote memorization with little application to real life situations.) Too many high dollar fundraisers (do we really need a high priced ball drop or parents-only gala in addition to a 5K?). Let's stop focusing on the wealthy parents and get back to educating ALL kids, regardless of income level! First and foremost: UNSAFE!!!! Anyone can walk in and walk out of this building almost any time in the morning and in the afternoon unchecked. THEN: huge class sizes so almost no individual attention. Horribly crowded cafeteria, terrible food. Complete lack of supervision in the hallways during junior high and high school passing periods, lunchtimes, before and after school - pushing, screaming, knocking into others, roughhousing, throwing items. Library one of noisiest ever seen - very few books, no comfortable places to read, no current magazines. Few and small bathrooms for student use. Part of recess areas totally unsupervised. I am a prospective parent who walked in one morning unchecked and got a visitor pass, spent the morning walking around and saw it all. You couldn't pay me ten thousand dollars to send my kids here. Although the school instructs the parents to allow the students to be responsible for their own success, there is little to no interaction or direction. In the end, the board would rather focus on teaching to the tests than teaching for the student. Definitely, not a fan. I was at this school from 4th grade to 7th grade. from 4th through 6th (Elementary) It was alright, quite strict but helped a lot in preparing for middle school... Or so I thoughtThe Middle school here is a disaster. Stuck right in between elementary and high school students in quite a confusing time can lead to hell. The teachers never stayed for more than a few years. And the ones who do stay are very rarely decent teachers. The school itself is clean, but almost depressing. white everything. The kids at the school either make it or get chewed up like a bone. Please don't go to this middle school. I would prefer Silver Hills, Rocky Top, or Westlake. Public school outweighs this school by a mile. I absolutely love my experience at this school. I love this school. This school has prepared me for college. And all the teachers know you. It’s like a small community Overall excellent! Loved the baseball program too; and my son really grew in both academic skills as well as social awareness. Guidelines well established for emotional development of the adolescent age group! As a family we are thrilled to be apart of The Wildcat Family. We have had 2 kids at the Academy for 3 years and are very pleased with our experience. There is communication is some areas but not in alot. The teachers are strict but nice. There is little to no punishment for bullying and things get brushed off easily. There is lot of pride in the school. There is little homework. The academy takes pride in charter devlopment. If you have a learning disabilty you are treated diffrenly, some teachers dont follow the guidlines, The counselors arent very helpful Bullies are free to tease, abuse and hurt other students with words and actions with little correction. Students who have been made a target attend school in fear with little or no support from the teachers and administration. The Academy is a fantastic school! My kids are now in middle school and have attended The Academy since kindergarten. The academics are top notch, the staff truly cares about the students, and the focus on character is refreshing in today’s day and age. For many years The Academy has had a reputation for being an excellent elementary school, but not very strong for middle or high school. I am so pleased that with new leadership the last several years, the middle and high school are now equally strong. I can’t recommend The Academy highly enough! The Academy is a FANTASTIC school! I have been here since kindergarten and I am currently in my sophomore year! This review is aimed to describe a highschool experience, so if you are interested in enrolling your kid here long-term or for high school; this review is for you! Here are some important aspects broken down;ClassesThe Classes offered at this the academy is OUTSTANDING. One type of class I would like to highlight are CE (concurrent enrollment) classes. High school students (9-12) can take CE classes, which means they can take actual college courses taught by actual college professors and get both college and highschool credits for taking just one class! Around 15 CE classes are offered at the Academy itself; but if students are willing to take a 5 minute walk to Front Range Community College, students my take any college class they want! Regular classes are also excellent, and you can not go wrong with any class that you take here (EXCEPT SPANISH; the spanish program is a disaster in full honesty). Homework at this school is very effective and typically pretty light (with the exception of college AP or CE classes). CommunityAll of the students, staff, and teachers TRUELY care for one another here (of course there will always be a few exceptions). Bullying is uncommon for the vast majority but if there is a situation, it will be taken care of by the school counselors! I personally meet up with one of the three school counselors every week to talk about my home situation; and I can not be more thankful for the support given both by my peers and my teachers! (Watch out for straight white boys though; about half of them are not that pleasant to be around. However the other half are genuinely caring!)TeachersTeachers and staff here LOVE their students! Unfortunately, the average wage here is WAY below average (but will be raised by a few thousand for every teacher in the 2022-23 school year!). This results in one positive aspect, and one negative aspect. First, the low wage means teachers are not here for pay; rather, they are here for the amazing community! (Which means they truely care about their students) However, this also results in a 50/50 split; teachers who stay for 25 years, and teachers who can only afford to stay for 2-3. Half of the high school teachers will have a lack of experience. But in my experience they still teach well and I still could not be more thankful for them! This school literally frightens people, the staff doesn't care about mental health, when the students bully other students there are few consequences. This school is by far the worst I've been to. Mostly only rich white kids that treat all their expensive stuff like trash. You will get in trouble for the littlest things. All of the lessons go by way too fast and you can't even remember them. When you ask for help the teachers will ignore you. Please don't go to this school. Most kids, 6th grade and above, are dealing with depression, self-harm, and many other conditions that don't get enough attention. This is a close community. The teachers are caring and the counselors are amazing! My knowledge is from K - 7th grade so far, and my child has obtained a quality education. It's a small-ish community of great people. Inside the classroom, the school uses 7 habits to make it a positive place that strives for growth in all academic areas. We love The Academy! I have 2 kids here and we have been a part of the Wildcat family since 2013. If you are looking to find a smaller school environment (compared to local public schools) that has a strong emphasis on both education and character development, The Academy is the school for you! My son has been at The Academy in Pre-k and Kindergarten so far. The teachers have been amazing at helping my child grow socially and academically. The school utilizes some amazing curriculum to support teachers in their daily interactions that develop student abilities. They use the Leader in Me to teach students how to be a leader and take responsibility for their own learning and growth. The Wonders and EnVision curriculums help students become problem solvers and explain their understanding of skills. There are also many other programs utilized to provide differentiation to help EVERY student achieve their best. The administrative team, CEO all the way down to each principal, focus on supporting teachers, students, and families to ensure everyone feels valued and an essential part of the education team for each individual student. Elementary students also take part in varied experiences like art, music, pe, science lab, computers, and small STEAM groups to build collaboration and problem solving skills. This school works hard to help students develop their 21st century skills and become productive citizens for our future. I can't wait to see what future grade levels can help my son achieve! We have been very happy at the Academy. We would recommend this school to other families. Excellent culture, safe buildings, engaging curriculum and staff that truly care. I have been a teacher at this school for 19 years and my daughter has been a student for 11 years (since PreK). We both love our school. It's not perfect. If you are looking for a perfect school, it doesn't exist. But I can tell you from an insider's perspective, everyone who works in our buildings gives their all and wants each student to not only achieve academically, but to be a well rounded, happy individual. I love being part of a charter school because the status quo never has to stay. Often parents and staff spearhead positive change. We don't have near as many hoops to jump through. I really like the curricula we use in elementary. We are an official Leader in Me school, which means we teach the 7 Habits of Highly Effective People to our students starting in kindergarten. We have an incredible amount of parent support and volunteering. The kids at our school are truly great kids. Again-no perfect school and there are plenty of kids here making poor choices, just like everywhere. But my daughter has had such a positive experience throughout her years with very little aggressive or mean behavior from others. Here, kids all have opportunity to participate in sports and activities, that they may not get in a 4A/5A school. The middle school and high school counselors are second to none. Our CEO and CFO are outstanding humans. Our principals are great. They hold us to a high standard for the sake of our students, but also care about us as individuals. Our high school student council is award winning, our seniors earn a tremendous amount of scholarships and grants (in the millions of dollars each year), we have an outstanding graduation rate and college acceptance rate, we encourage vocational school and military as well, we have a robust internship and work experience program, and our sports program gets bigger and better every year. So yeah, I kinda love this place you could say. Perfect? No. A great place to be everyday? Definitely. This school is an awesome community with so many opportunities and teachers/staff that truly care. My kids have loved their experiences at The Academy. This is our first year at The Academy and we have been very impressed so far. We had our daughter (now in 6th grad) at a private school the last two years and she is getting a better education from more dedicated teachers at The Academy than she was at the private school. The electives are great and the staff are committed to creating a safe place for learning. Of course, there will be bullies and jerks in every school. But, any issue we've had has been dealt with immediately AND effectively. Committed and caring teachers combined with a dedicated staff make the difference between a good school and a great school. Our son also started Kindergarten here this year and I have been completely blown away by the teachers and staff. First off, Ms. Hahs is THE MOST AMAZING Kindergarten teacher in the world. I've heard that all the teachers are great, but I don't think anyone can truly compare to her. They have 5 specials that they attend each week: Computers, Science, Art, Music, and P.E. They also use the Leader in Me curriculum to teach true life skills to the kids. It has been amazing so far and I am excited to continue our kids' education here!

column3: My son transferred into this school to take advantage of an award winning band program, but found academic teachers who seemed more interested in showing movies than actually teaching. From other parents, I have heard that the teachers of the higher level classes are great, but in average classes, my son did not get the help or instruction he needed. When he tried to get math tutoring, he was told it was not available for his class. When calling the front office, it is difficult if not impossible to speak to a human being, and my son's guidance counselor seldom returned calls, explaining when she did call back that she was "too busy". If you have an academic over achiever, this school may be great for your family, but if you have an average student - forget it. Your student will not get the help and guidance they need to graduate. This is a great school, I have two boys going there right now. My oldest is a senior and he takes honors and AP classes. He has been challenged and is well prepared for college. My other son is a sophmore and has some learning disabilities. Their RSP program is great and everyone works together to accomodate the student. This school has a great Athletics program. But that's about it. Beware of teachers like Mrs. Fait. She teaches Ceramics. Unless you are the star pupil, you'll have to fight to keep a passing grade. Trabuco is an okay school, but best serves students that are self directed and not students in the middle or who have academic challenges/struggling. We have two children that attended THHS. My daughters is a self starter that took her academics seriously and did decently at Trabuco. But her teachers were a mix; some very good/dedicated and others less so. She graduated with an okay experience and is doing well in college. But for kids who are in the middle or who struggle, but do not qualify for special education (not on an IEP), there are very few (if any) support services available. We also found administration to be lacking - not helpful or compassionate when our son was having a hard time in school (has ADHD). Despite being on academic probation his first semester, there was no support offered. High achieving kids will do fine, but I would not recommend this school for a child needing additional services. We've since enrolled our son in private school and he is doing great. After moving from north OC, I was originally sceptical about THHS, as I was familiar with Anaheim Hills, Yorba Linda, Villa Park schools. However, after my daughter attended THHS for 4 years, I must say I was delighted with what my child was able to achieve and have pleasure recommending it without reservation. My daughter achieved captain varsity basketball, scholar athlete and received a congressional nomination to the air force academy. If you work hard at this school, you will do well. Overall good, mostly because I kept to myself and was pretty smart so I was in smarter classes, where teachers are generally nicer and students care less about you. Pretty good as long as your not getting stabbed

No school is perfect but I am going to explain what I have seen in my four years here: The good: I will admit that Bayside gave me a great all round education and had me very prepared for the work in college. The bad: As a general A+ student I was recommended to take trigonometry my sophomore year and the teacher (ms. Kohler) was awful. She had no control of the class and would laugh at everything even if it wasn't funny. She made me fail my first regent and I had to get tutoring at a place out of school to take it again in the winter. A lot of times I would walk into certain places like the locker rooms and hallways and it would smell like marajuana. It wasn't too hard to get a hold of that in this school. I witnessed seeing high children pacing up and down the lunchroom with the aides not even noticing. And worst of all I had a female stalker that was banned from the school and somehow she was able to get in through the door other children were leaving from that were finished with their day. She was just able to blend in and walk in with no one noticing. Talk about terrible security. It is a very good school . The teachers are highly educated, very considerate to their students. Students are comfortable in their classes. I have no complain at all. This school should get all support from the city. S.h This school is the reason I went from being a kid who absolutely hated MS158 into a freshman at an Ivy League school. The whole atmosphere at Bayside makes you want to participate and challenge yourself. I took AP classes and graduated with 18 college credits. A wonderful 4 years and a great and funny principal. My parents could not have made a better choice for my high school. This is a very good school in queens. As long as you work hard, you will see results. the teachers are passionate about their subjects and. The only issue I have with the school was that it was very crowded and is thousands of students over its capacity. Mostly terrible. Because of this chaos there is rampant drug problems, bullying, sexual harassment, and fighting. Consider another school option. I did not enjoy this school. column1: This school is horrible. Almost all of the teachers will surf the web all day, and not teach a lesson, and the district cannot do anything about it because of the tenure they have. The bathrooms are disgusting and sometimes, during the middle of the school day, all of the restrooms will be locked. The school gives all of the money that should be even divided up between all the sports and gives it to the football and baseball teams. The class sizes are ridiculous, 35+ students in a class, and the school pretty much has a "first come, first served" philosophy for text books. I wish I could give this school a 0 star rating, but I can't. This school is not a school it is a play ground for kids to do and say what they want. The rules are not tolerated. The kids are disrespectful to other adults when the teachers are not around to hear what they say. I rate the school a ZERO and rate the Teachers a 5. It won't let me submit this review unless I rate this school. It's still a ZERO but I have to rate it anyway. I have moved out of the area due to the terrible education my children were receiving. The area is filled with students who do as they please and the staff of Rio Linda do nothing to control the situation. I have seen huge improvements in this school. I have seen it go to a caring environment that is student centered. There are a lot of different opportunities for students if they look for them. The staff genuinely care for the students. There is a good push for students to consider that they are going to be doing after the graduate from high school. This school is continually improving in every way possible. RLHS continues to lead the district and in many cases the area in academics. I Am a Student At Rio Linda High, and let me just tell you that Rio Linda is the best place to be. It might not seem like it in the beginning and I felt the same way at first but when I got there... It was just... Perfect. The teachers are so kind and generous with their time. I was really shy at first but Rio Linda focuses on participation of ALL students. They finally got me to budge which isnt that easy if you knew me. Rio has many career oppurtunities. They have an AMAZING Agricultural program, an OUTSTANDING JROTC program, and let me just say the talent here is .. Just.. Exemplary! We have the best cheerleaders including boys. We have an AVID program which is college rediness elective which helps you/your child get prepared for college , to get motivated. The Band is ... I have no words to describe it. Maybe the word, AWESOME would work? Noo thats an understatement. Rio even has advanced placements for those "over achievers". Rio linda Is the place to be! - Twin Rivers Unified School District Rio Linda High School Emily Yang I warn anyone thinking of putting your child in this school or school district. This school is horrible! Not only horrible but if you have a kid of color do not I warn you do not put him in this school! Parents if you have other choices of schools pick them not Rio Linda or Twin Rivers!

column3: I have been very pleased with Spauilding. It offers an amazing variety of opportunities, both acaademic and extra-curricular. Every year the newspaper prints stories about the top 10 graduating students at the area high sschools. Spaulding's top 10 take a back seat to no one. Recent grads have gone on to Harvard, Dartmouth, Middlebury, Bates, and Johns Hopkins, to name a few. Rochester's test ratings may not match some other more affluent disctricts, but that has a lot to do with demographics. A motivated student who takes advantage of Spaulding's Honors and Advanced Placement courses can excel and get into a great college. WE have been very pleased with Spaulding! The academics are appropriate for my honors level students. The extracurricular opportunities are plentiful and varied. My two have loved the music department - marching band, chorus, and drama! I would rate it 0 because it’s that bad Great school, amazing tech program. SHS has so much to offer kids. Great teachers, admin and staff.

column1: If you are planning to send your kids here. Don't. It is ok if you are in the in crowd. I am a graduate of Bermudian and now a teacher in the district. I loved attending the school, and have thus far had a very positive expericence as an educator here. The students, for the most part, want to learn, and I can't disagree more with the reviews that say the majority of teachers are only here for the paycheck. Sure, there are some, like any school, but across the board both as a student and teacher, my experience has been opposite. In response to parent on 3-14-10, the staff and teachers did not receive blackberries, only administrators so they could be easily reached by phone or email regardless of where they are in the area. I moved here from the western part of the state and my wife is from the eastern part of the state. We both came from much larger schools and higher taxes. All three of our children started in Bermudian from Kindergarten. We are very pleased with the school district in general, the majority of the teachers are attentive and the parents are supportive. It is a small school and everyone knows each other kids through some aspect of the school which makes it very family like community. It is my observation that the students support each other better in a smaller school than a larger school. The curriculum could be a little more challenging for the more advance students, but overall they seem to do a good job with all levels of ability. The school, parents and the community provides a very good foundation for the young men and women from our observation. This school does not adequately prepare its students for college. The administration could demonstrate a greater level of professionalism. They could also accept responsibility for their mistakes instead of finger pointing elsewhere. Greater lessons are learned once mistakes are owned. It is how you move forward from your mistake that demonstrates greater lessons beyond the classroom. The school system is cliquey. If you enrolled in kindergarten or your parents grew up as Bermudian students then you should do fine. Not impressed with the system at all. This school is great IF you intend for your child to grow up here, attend local college and come right back. Most teachers hired in the past 10 yrs are related to a current employee or attended the school as children (admin too). The school board is also of the same ilk and make decisions based on their interest, not academic excellence. There is great pride in our PSSA results however it makes sense when you realize the amount of time our staff spends teaching to the test. The curriculum is VERY LIMITED and if you have an exceptional student do not expect much of a challenge. Especially if they are female. If you decide to challenge the status quo you may also want to prepare yourself for the admistration to dismiss your concerns as being a problem parent.If you are lucky you may end up with a teacher willing to fight for your child but it will depend on the luck of the draw. To say we are not impressed with Bermudian is an understatement. There are just too many locals making decisions based on family connections and childhood affiliations to make it anything other than a basic education. It is truly unfortunate that I have placed my child in the care of Bermudian Springs School District. Sometimes you do not have a choice where you live, which is the case in this situation. This school district is full of plain old averages. Average administrators and average teachers(mostly) makes average students. If you are a football player or wrestler, you have great exposure and opportunity as a student athlete. If you are everyone else, you are most likely not destined to go to college, let alone graduate school. You will not be academically enlightened. You will not be culturally enlightened. You will not be selected for advanced study if you qualify for it. I'm fairly certain that there is not a single person of minority status educating the children. There is no diversity in that regard, which is terrifying and absurd(there is a large Hispanic population in the district). There is blatant racism from students to teachers, which is largely ignored and accepted. The Camp Hill School District has none of these problems. Maybe Bermudian school take some tips from some of their higher ranking neighboring school districts. There are some great teachers but also many that share the same harmful mentality of the administration which is to support the athletes and make fun of any kid who is different. Not good so far, hope some improvements can be made. 2/10 made some great friends but staff is a joke I have had a great experience attending this school. In Elementary school, the teachers were fun to be around and learn from. Middle school was, however, not a great experience for me outside of passions. That is because all middle schools have problems that deal with students changing. High school was a great experience. I made some great friends, and the teachers were extremely supportive of my career choice and have helped me grow as a student. I am pleased with Bermudian Springs.

column3: I moved to Valpo about a year ago and VHS is a good school but it seems like the only way you will do good there is if you are very well educated, I'm surprised that I'm able to get good grades in my honors classes. I moved from a small school of 500 that didn't have a ton of money like Valpo does so most of the stuff that is standard education up here I've never even been introduced to, so if you're from somewhere other than Northwestern Indiana you or your child may struggle. And, strangely enough,there is a very large amount of people associated with drugs that attend it, which makes me uneasy as a student. I still haven't found where I fit into this school because everyone has their own group. I can't deny that Valp is a good school though, there are multiple AMAZING oppurtunities (such as MarineLab for those interested in Marine bio), and the teachers are incredible and try to help students reach their highest potential. After many years of dealing with the Valpo schools, I won t send another child to the high school. On August 6, 2013, I was withdrawing my child from this school. I relay to you a conversation I witnessed between an administrator and incoming family. The admin asked the incoming 9th grade girl if she thought she should be placed in regular classes, or honor s classes. The girl was unsure, so the administrator said, You will be taking Algebra this year. Will you ask for help in that class once or more than once a day? The girl stated that she would ask for help, as many times as she needed it, so the administrator replied, Well then you certainly don t fit in an honor s course! The admin continued, I swear many of the kids we have come into this school are only here because it is a free education and we are just stuck dealing with them. They just aren't able to keep up with our standards and I just don t know why they don t just get a GED! How well that woman s comments summed up the over-all attitude of educators in the Valparaiso Community Schools. I relay to you a conversation I witnessed between an administrator and incoming family. The admin asked the incoming 9th grade girl if she thought she should be placed in regular classes, or honor s classes. The girl was unsure, so the administrator said, You will be taking Algebra this year. Will you ask for help in that class once or more than once a day? The girl stated that she would ask for help, as many times as she needed it, so the administrator replied, Well then you certainly don t fit in an honor s course! The admin continued, I swear many of the kids we have come into this school are only here because it is a free education and we are just stuck dealing with them. They just aren't able to keep up with our standards and I just don t know why they don t just get a GED! How well that woman s comments summed up the over-all attitude of educators in the Valparaiso Community Schools. I am a former student of VHS. I graduated with honors and distinction. That being said, it is disgusting to me how much athletics reigns supreme at this school. In my day, teachers were hired according to what sport they would be coaching. The end result was that I had a number of teachers who were laughably awful at their jobs. The speech/debate team was constantly losing funding so that the school could provide more for the football team. I also dealt with a number of closed-minded and racist teachers. The oversight of employees here is awful. The administration at the school is horribly inept, rude, and inefficient. You really are treated like a number here, unless you are a star athlete or the child of a school administrator. When I moved to Valparaiso, the school guidance counselor told me that the honors classes at the high school would be "too hard" for me and refused to allow me to be in an advanced course. Thankfully, I was able to enroll in honors courses for the rest of the four years after convincing the administration that my grades were high enough. All in all, mediocre and miserable school. The offerings at this school are great. The staff is friendly and my daughter has had a great experience so far. It's average. The staff is somewhat rude, some teachers are engaging and fun, others are boring and grade on work effort rather than their actual understanding. I also dislike the emphasis on athletics. I came from a middle school who had been to the science olympiad national tournament 25 years in a row. Here, the science o team places poorly at state, possibly because the it's the same boring coach who barley coaches at all. The football team, however, does extremely well, basically all the time. Don't get me wrong, athletics are important, but there should be some involvement in academic teams. I also requested to be in Lunch B but they said no. I guess that's really not their fault but socially in the high school I feel outcasted. All the students here are just numbers. Unhealthy relationship of teachers trying to be cool kids. Think 15 year old girl's being complemented on features not academics. Worst year of school in my education. Would be a 0 if possible. I attended here my freshman year and moved away, and I am glad I did! The lunches were disgusting, packaged food was the only decent thing to eat at school and a lot of my peers were pretty cliquey and rude. I am just glad I'm not listening to all the construction during class. Not only the students were bullying, but even teachers were insulting students for their learning pace! Only way to have friends here is to either be rich or attractive. Not only a disappointment to the students, but to the community! As a former student who attended college in another state, I can say the quality of education here is not bad. In comparison to other students I attended college with, I was definitely ahead of the curve in many ways. However, it was difficult to sometimes be in a classroom setting where favoritism played a huge role amongst some teachers who want to just "make friends" with the students or, even worse, certain groups of students. Staff should also really encourage and help students if they do chose to take honors courses. It should be looked upon as honorable if a student steps up and challenges themselves; I took a course where it seemed like they were just trying to weed me out instead of helping me excel.And like most places, politics play a huge role in sports. It may never change. If you have money to play for who the high school coaches want you to play for, or if your parents suck up to the coaches, you will get your way. I was overlooked by Valpo in my sport, but went on to get a scholarship anyways thanks to the opportunities provided to me by my club coaching. Valpo high is an average school. Some teachers are great, but quite a few are poor at their jobs. Some of the honors classes are great, but like most other things in this school, it is very circumstantial and based on which teacher you get. I am sure there are worse schools, but VHS certainly isn't one of the best. Not very good so far but still working to make my child experience better! I liked the school at first but have began to dislike it because for what the school is given, in terms of funding, it’s ridiculous the WiFi is terrible, sports overrule academics, and students don’t get into their top colleges because the teachers don’t give out A’s. It prepared me to get into every State college in Indiana.

Activities are expensive and time consuming so any student who needs to work or doesn't have money will have difficulty participating. Bullying goes unchecked or undisciplined when carried out by those not in an undeserved class and black, Hispanic, and poor students are overdisciplined.
