column3: I graduated from this school and loved it. People over exaggerate on things around here. The average home around here is 175,000-300,000..... Great area just some need an attitude change. North Crowley High School is the worse school my children have attended! When we moved here four years ago I thought after coming from Everman North Crowley would be a much better educational service to my children. Boy was I wrong! You have teachers fighting students, coaches bullying athletes and with holding mail from colleges to the athletes. More so it seems that the dress code means more than the education! The kids can sag as long as the color of their shirt is right! We have tried to tuff it out, but even though our son will be a senior next year we are moving! This school is doing a great injustice to the students of this so called educational system.This year a male teacher jumped at my senior daughter in an aggressive manner in the name of joking with her. We reported him and all that happened was the teacher was "talked to" and my daughter was moved to a different class. It saddens me that we stayed this long. We have a daughter that will be graduating in June and feel that she did not get to experience the true feel of high school. She feels more like she was in prison than school! Needless to say, we are selling our home and getting far away from this area! i liked attending this school very much the teachers were excellent and i loved the experience! As a student of NCHS, I would say that it's not that great. Some of the teachers don't care at all about teaching and as a result the students don't learn anything. However, there are one or two teachers who are absolutely amazing and know what they are doing. Cheating is also extremely prevalent in this school. This school has no orchestra or Academic UIL Programs which is disappointing. It would also be nice if we had clubs such as Whiz Quiz or TMSCA that allowed us to enter in academic competitions. North Crowley has been a blessing to Tarrant county. Students are friendly and super smart and talented. The teachers and staff are dedicated to student success. The administrators are among the friendliest and most intelligent people I have ever had the pleasure of working with and knowing. Oh . . . and Java City rules! Go Panthers! I am a graduating Senior at North Crowley High School and I have to agree with the majority of the reviews I have read so far. The majority of the teachers at this school either have no idea how to teach or don't care whether the students learn or not. I always hear people saying they wish they attended a Crowley school because the academics are good and it's in a "good area" but the area seems to be getting worse and worse. North Crowley looks nice and shiny on the outside but the inside is filled with nothing but cramped hallways, annoying Assistant Principals, and teachers who care more about dress code than they do education. I think it is very sad that during the 2012-2013 school year, North Crowley had their first pep-rally in nearly 7 years. There is absolutely no school spirit. It is safe to say that I wish I could have spent my high school years at a different school, however; I do wish the best to all the upcoming students and especially the rising seniors. I am a graduate of 2013, and my experience wasn't pleasant. I admit that the school have improved since my sophomore year, but a lot of the problems remained. the teachers I received were mostly powerless to teach us in a way that we could benefit, whether its because of the curriculum is forcing them to teach stagnant lessons or a few student's behavior. and by the end of the year those who at least tried to get something out of it give up. My son absolutely hates this school. The education is lackluster, some teachers don't teach well, behavior is out of control so learning doesn't truly happen, which leaves the teachers as well as the students who want to learn very frustrated. I'm moving just so my son can enjoy the remainder of his sophomore year and beyond. I wish that I had left a year ago, but I wanted things to remain stable for him. Yet being at this school, I now see, brings him the most instability and frustration. I sense that many students feel the same way. If you can, my advice would be to avoid this school at all costs. From the principal to the lunch staff; this school does NOT care about their students! Athletic Department is a NIGHTMARE! The Counselors are a joke! Please do whatever you can to NOT attend this school! Staff is arrogant. Principal clueless. They don't care about students, about their education, about their drive to succeed in the world. They treat them with total disregard of them as people. Letting them dress however they want, means nothing in the real world. Some teachers have no business been teachers. My kid hates the school. Need to work closely with the CTE and the programs of choice. Promote and encourage students to pursue going to the CTE. Forget the $$. Disorganized even with the buses that take /leave students at CTE and 9th Grade Campus. Some students even have to walk back to the 9th Grade Campus. LAte to another class is NOT an option, specially if they have a test. I graduated in the Spring of 2015 from North Crowley High School and, let me tell you, it was a relief. My experience at this school was mixed at best. Going into things, I was extremely optimistic but my mood soon turned sour.The 9th grade campus is a huge mess. The teachers are less than thrilled to be there and dress code, at the time I was there in 2011, was their main concern. While I was a very well behaved student, I spent many days in ISS for dresscode violations which seemed to be more important than my ability to learn. I was bullied severely on that campus and my teacher in one class did nothing about it, just watched it happen, because he was a coach and the bullies were his players. Their ability to play was more important than my well being.When I got to the main campus, I thought that surely things couldn't get any worse. I was, of course, mistaken. That year I was again dealing with teachers who couldn't control their students and one teacher who wasn't even equipped to teach the Pre-AP class he'd been assigned. One year I'd asked for a locker because I had a lot of textbooks and it took them weeks to get it to me meanwhile I'm stuck with a backpack heavy enough that I nearly fell down the stairs.One thing I enjoyed for a while was that they split things up between 'A' days and 'B' days where you'd have four periods a day, each an hour and a half long and they would alternate between each day. It gave time for teachers to go over things in depth and for students to get a head start on their work. When they took that away, everything got squished together with periods cut in half and eight periods a day instead of 4. They had a good thing going and they threw it out the window or, rather, the district did which is a shame.I loved the administration at the main campus and I had a really good relationship with them. I was always able to go to them when I had a problem and they were the ones that finally put my bullying to rest. The food was great until the switch came to 'healthier food.' The Chick filet sandwich line shutdown and turned into more disgusting cafeteria food, there was another line of cafeteria food, they had a sandwich bar for a while but that closed when the new regulations came in, and then there was a chick nugget line. I think they did all they could with the food with four lines. There was just a lot of kids. We really like this high school. The neighborhood is developing, With more academic challenges, schools also expect students to put more effort and participate in academics and sports. We understand school needs more funding, volunteers.Teachers are very helpful and supportive. We newly moved to this area about 1 yr before. We can see a major improvement in school management, student education. We can under covid have impacted many schools, but now it has much improved. We strongly recommend the school.The school has taken steps to stop bullying and community participation has improved.

When a parent calls to complain, the staff argues with the parents in an attempt to dispute and invalidate the complaint. School-wide discipline polices are found to be inconsistent since they are not enforced.

column3: Poinciana is rather pathetic. They make us skip our whole day and sit in ISS for being late. Even if we're only a few seconds late. Then the students in ISS have to clean the school and pickup trash, when that's what janitors are supposed to be for. I also got yelled at for hugging my boyfriend and was told it was not school appropriate. It's not even like we were groping, it was just a friendly hug. Maybe if they'd chill a bit and actually clean the bathrooms then the students wouldn't feel so cramped and stressed. It feels like the deans and principals are suffocating us. Maybe next year it'll be better. But so far, we're only a B because the state lowered thir standards. So quit getting your hopes so high. Part 2 of 2: Why do you thing like School like Osceola school of arts and other types of school have lots of HAPPY KIDS running around, that's because those kids attending that school are at common grounds with their Teachers/School. Parents Should also be part of your child education, NO! NOT ONLY IN ELEMENTARY.... join your Kids HS PTA, if anything this is the most important part of your kids education, Make it count! If we Create HAPPY KID, that in turn will create HAPPY TEACHERS, which in turn creates a better environment in the class, creating a better SCHOOL, SCHOOL DISTRIC, Equaling a better generation of kids! KIDS take control, and TRY YOUR BEST, that way you can never say: "If only I would of" Niulka Laboy, Photographer & Graphic Designer In Osceola for 21 Yrs! Part 1 of 2: I'm Extremely sadden to hear such negative comments, especially from students. Being an Alumni of the 4th graduating class of Poinciana HS...It really seems that all of the nice and memorable Ideal experiences from a HS are long gone and a thing of the past. Now contemplating on what HS My soon to be 9th grader should go to is a decision that worries my husband (whom I met while in PHS) and I. I'm an active parent and it's really sad to see that ALL schools.....(Ok, with an exception of a handful) have lost and forgotten the meaning and the role of a "School" the school should be the home away from home for kid. Every child K-12 should feel loved & welcomed in their school (I've seen enough to be able to say that's by far that's NOT the vibe you get). High Schools and other levels of schools have lost focus, and common cutesy. OK, I don't want to sit here and sound like an advocate for the student, yes I know that today's offspring's can be a tough bunch, However I feel that schools are more concern on "school grade and ratings" instead of students needs and wants. I am a student attending this school , there nothing bad about the school they improve the students are the ones who make poor descisions and act the way they do to not learn the teachers are perfectly wonderful and do a good job so quit bad mouthing the school you have to attend to know how it is !!!! You get what you give. You cannot expect teachers to do everything; it starts and has to be reinforced at HOME. My 2 son will be Poinciana grads and the 1st one graduate with 33 college credits. He now has a Computer Eng. degree. 2nd one is on his 4th year. The more challenging the class the better prepared for College your student will be. Parents have to get involved, support the school and encourage their child to take challenging classes and WORK HARD. Parents need to Thank Poinciana Teachers and staff. I found Poinciana to have a great Academics Program, Outstanding NJROTC, Sports Program and many other fine Programs. Poinciana High School is a Quality learning environment. The staff is inspiring, hardworking and friendly. They work with what we give them, talk to your student and school and see the get what you give at work. I Spent 4 Years at poinciana High School, and I can certainly say that those were the best four years of my life. I got Involved in sports and as many activities as possible, which enhanced my high school career. My best memories are of things I used to do in Poinciana, regardless of what many people might say, Poinciana is and will always be the best High School. - John E This school is absolutely awful. you are DOOMED if you go to this school. If could I would give it ZERO stars. As my mom once said about this school...BASURA. (Means garbage in Spanish) If you want to throw away the fun years of high school....Come to Poinciana High School!!! you can just chew gum or burp you would get an automatic suspension for 5 days. If you don't want your child to graduate then...Come to Poinciana High School. Where only 30 percent of students graduate. This years graduation was only like 5 seconds long from how few people graduated. Also most of the students there are...troublemakers. Not a good environment for any kid to learn both educational wise and manner wise. Now I know why there were an F school recently....NO FUN or LEARNING. What a waste of 4 years...no... one hour...no...one second in this pathetic excuse for a school. This is my second year in PHS and honestly the school isn't even all that bad. The staff always try their best to get students involved in school events. In my opinion, it's the students who make the school look and sound bad. They want to do whatever they want and that's not how it is. But at the same time, the teachers don't motivate us in class. All they do is yell and kick people out for the littlest things. They give up on their students too easily. The only good thing about the school is that the faculty allows us to express ourselves with piercings, the way we dye our hair, and dress. Yes, we have to wear uniforms but they let us put our own little style into it. Not something big, but they let us add something so we can feel comfortable. Now we have a new Principal coming in and honestly, I feel like he's taking away all our rights from the letter he sent in the mail. We can't wear face piercings or more than 2 on the ear. We can't wear sandals or slides. I have many piercings and I refuse to take them off. I also love wearing slides we spend 8 hours every day walking class to class and doing stuff we want to be comfortable. I understand its for safety but we're old enough. the school is a horrible school, the teachers give the kids no motivation, the new principal is leading this school back to what it was 2 years ago, the school is very old, and needs severe renovations, kids are allowed to do whatever, like the school is out of control, if you ask to use the bathroom, you get sent to the office for no reason, I literally hate this school, I like nothing about it, the only way the school could improve in my opinion is get a new principle, the one we're stuck with now is leading us to our deaths. Just letting you know, if you are thinking about bringing your child here, DO NOT, your better off with Harmony HS, Liberty HS, Gateway, or even TECO. I'm a freshman at Poinciana , and let me just say I love this school. In high school , you get a thing called "freedom". Something you never got in middle school or elementary school. We're young adults. We make the decisions in life. We don't have anybody telling us what to do anymore. Our football team is great. I love my teachers. I love Poinciana High School. I'm not just saying this because I'm a freshman & I obviously don't know anything. But, for all the people saying this school is shit , you're the ones making it shit. Point blank. The school is honestly great. It's just that one small group of kids that make it look bad and that small group is literally everywhere. The teachers get involved and try there hardest in helping their students. There has also been a lot of stricter rules to avoid fights and other problems. I can 100% guarantee that that amount of fights that happened in 2012-2014 has lowered severely. There's rarely ever a fight. But there's fights in school everywhere. 2014-2015 school year has one fight. The school went from having 4-6 fights per school year to 0-1 fight. Students are extremely nice and teachers really do care about our success. Staff does all they can to help kids out and the atmosphere is wonderful. School has greatly improved and any pre-conceived ideas should be discouraged about this school. If you love your children you would not send them to this terrible school. They are just there the test grades can attest to that. The teachers are a joke( most of them) they are just there for the check. SINCERLY PARENTS OF CHILDREN WHOM ATTENDED THIS ATROCIOUS PLACE CALLED A SCHOOL. Awesome, great NJROTC Program, Highly Educated English Teachers and Fresh Air. Excellent..the best!!! Always making the difference. Num. 1. terrible, so much things go on that require serious action and they pay little to no attention to most of it I graduated last year and I know many students who love to complain about the school all the time but I honestly love PHS (Poinciana High School). There are many career certifications available. I got certified in Adobe Premiere Pro. There are a variety of technical courses. I took accounting and students even get to work in the student bank at PHS and get paid. There are many AP courses which you can transfer when you go to college. There are multiple clubs and organizations to choose from and always something happening on the campus. Of course there are things that needs to be addressed or could be addressed but it is not the school's decision alone, the district has to approve their requests and many people don't realize it. The students have to learn to be respectful to their teachers and administrators. I had the privilege to create a sports club where no teachers knew the sport so the principal himself agreed to be the sponsor. Who would do that? If the students take the opportunity to communicate and build a healthy relationship with their teachers and administrators, they will surely help you. I can guarantee that! In my opinion "A good student will be successful no matter which school he/she goes to" it is in their hands to decide whether they want to complain and waste their time or understand the differences and learn to adapt to it. At the end of the day, not everywhere you go is going to be the perfect place for you, whether is a job or marriage life. You have to learn to adjust, adapt and understand. That is what life is all about! I know what not going to school feels like and for me going to school itself is a great privilege. Students and parents, please be grateful to the teachers and the schools. Pay attention to your/your children's education and success alone not on complaining about the learning environment. If you still think the school is "trash", well let me tell you something; I graduated with a merit and scholar designation within the two years I studied there. I transferred to PHS during the end of my sophomore year. I never attended an actual school before. So kudos to my teachers, deans, administrators! Now the choice is yours :)Thank you! A teacher failed me because she doesnt like me, lunch is terrible, 50% of people have no seats at lunch and have to get fire ants in their shoes and pants. Good luck if u have ADHD because they don’t have any help for that either. And in general the staff of the school aren’t organized. And all rules are out of control. Bullying is always, and fights happen all the time. very doo doo would not recommend very bad my son came home with milk spilled on him.

column1: The school is terrible they try so hard to make it a safe and comforting place but there is Racism going on in the hallways and bullying takin place every where. What part of that is safe and comforting to you? Im a student there and I hate it. And Yes i know you think "Every kid hates School" But I honestly Hate it there. I feel like drama and bullying will never go away.. And I dont know how long I can stand the teachers and the students at this school. I just want it to be torn down.. Maybe then I can go to sleep happy that I dont need to face my torcherers the next day. I am a former student of Raymond High and I have to say my personal experience here was great! I made a lot of great relationships with friends and teachers along the way and have gained morals, values, and even life skills that i use to this very day. Granted you will find there are always bad experiences with any school but the close bond with teachers and students here makes for a great learning experiece. I will be settling down in Raymond in the future and sending my children there for school. Raymond has been consistently rated as a school in need. Despite this, the school has sent a very high ratio of children to very competitive colleges and several to Ivy League schools in the past several years. Like any other school, the kids will get out what they put in. The teacher-student ratio is good and the teachers in my experience, have all been attentive and dedicated. I have 2 kids in this school system, and both are high honor students. There is a relatively high ratio of kids who just don't do well, but it's not necessary a reflection on the school so much as the kids themselves. There are some kids who just don't care. There are some great programs that are in place to help serious student attain college goals. I attended a very well-known semi-private school and cannot say that my experience was any better there than my children's at RHS. Their Special-Ed department does nothing to help kids with special needs. They don't help keep the parents well informed either, unless your child does something wrong. If you don’t plan on attending college or aren’t a part of their extra-curricular activities, then they don’t waste any time or energy on you and you’re lucky if you get any help. Truancy is rampant and the attendance system is useless. Teachers will mark you there when you are not or mark you absent when you are there. Teachers will lie to justify their punishments. The administration will tell you one thing then change their story afterwards. Everyone there is self-serving – not one person cares. Resident of this town sine 2004. This school system is got to be the worst in the State. all they want to do is raise taxes for new buildings while hiring self serving, usless teachers for zero money. You get what you pay for. We have had an excellent experience with the Raymond school district. Excellent high school. Not too big, not too small. Great classes to choose from. The teachers and leadership do a great job. Room for improvement though during Covid time. A lot of assigning and not a lot of teaching. Classes end early too often. Middle school same thing. :(

column3: The majority of the teachers are good. However the student body is very rude and cliques are extremely prevelent. My child before he went on to college was mocked every single day by some of the other students. I went to this school and hated every minute of it. The majority of teachers are close minded and discourage individualism. The students all have to fit into their cliques and it you dont praise jesus then you most likely wont be in the "popular" group. i wouldnt recommend going to this school unless you are a regualr white bred american. any other race and unfortunately the majority of the student body will sling racial slurs constantly. This school has a fantastic selection of educated and intelligent teachers. The sports are also a great opportunity, however, the problem with this particular High School is the student body. at least 50% of the body could care less about their education, which make people like myself a target, because we DO value this opportunity. I moved here approximately 2 months ago, and all of my time spent here has at least one individual treating me like a piece of garbage. It is unbelievable how ill-tempered and unintelligent some of the students are.

column1: There are some really nice qualities about this school, but there are also a few not so nice ones. On the positive side, the campus is beautiful, the academics are challenging, there is soo much school pride, and the football games are amazing, even for people who hate sports. However, what concerns me is that a couple of the teachers are not so lovely. I remember, while I was attending Chaminade, every year, I would get one teacher who was just plain awful. They would be consistently condescending, or unhelpful, or would have unrealistic expectations of their students. Keep in mind this is a minority of faculty members. Most faculty members were very nice, a couple were even astounding teachers who were funny and articulate and passionate about the subject they taught. It's just there are a few really awful teachers who personally dampered the Chaminade experience for me. p.s. the middle school is better I graduated almost 20 years ago and had a wonderful middle school and high school experience at Chaminade. If my family lived in the area, I would hesitate sending my children there. I am a Chaminade Alumni and have the best memories for all my years. I recently met some of the new parents in the Golf Event and realized the fear they have from the high school as it compares to Chaminade's Middle School. Somehow, they all agree that the high school needs a repair job to bring it to the level of the Middle School! So maybe this could be addressed or looked at to fix before the ratings declines. Last, Chaminade is by far the best in the area. I am an alumni of the Class of 2011. I went to Chaminade from 6th grade all the way through 12th grade. What a great experience! Not only are the teachers some of the best in their field, they are so much more than just teachers of academic subjects. They are also life role models interested in helping their students in any way possible. The academic prowess is only paralleled by the athletic pride of the campus. So much Eagle pride is just contagious. The alumni community really watch out for the students and the new graduates as well. What makes Chaminade special to me is the amount of Family Spirit that the school has; everyone becomes a member of a larger family. We as alumni still call ourselves Eagles. Like anything else, Chaminade is what you make out of it. You can take the harder classes (APs and Honors) and be challenged or take the normal college prep classes and still be challenged (but not as much, of course). So many opportunities are at Chaminade that it is astounding. Once an Eagle, always an Eagle. Send your children to Chaminade, I know I will be doing so in the future. I love my school. It has a nice space, yet cozy campus feel to it. The faculty is great and friendly. My peers are very friendly and welcoming to everyone that comes to visit and review. The class schedule is very good and a little different than maybe other schools. They truly prepare you for college and makes you feel in a great mature environment. It is a catholic school in marianist tradition so there are monthly masses. Everyone once in a while, we have school-wide pep rallies to celebrate accomplishments and good sports seasons. This school is amazing and welcoming to every student and is always willing to listen and help their students with open arms. Chaminade College Preparaty is a school where anyone can come in and automatically feel like they are apart of something greater. I believe any student here can testify that as a school community, you feel as if the whole student body has got your back. We as a school promote diversity, faith, peace, family spirit, justice, involvement in apostolic works, and quality intergral education. The relationship with the teachers and students is absolutely phenomonal. Throughout all our studies, I constantly feel like my teachers are always by my side supporting me through my work and looking to help me improve, rather than scold me for being incorrect. At Chaminade, you can come in here and feel completely free do be who you want to be, participate in what you want to participate in, and know that you are supported and praised for all that you do. What I also love about Chaminade is that there is someone for everyone to enjoy. We have so many different sports, clubs, and performing arts opportunities here, it is almost impossible to feel like you don't belong. I am proud to be apart of Chaminade because the whole experience of being here is something I will never forget & cherish forever. I am switching schools soon because I cannot take Chaminade anymore. They are so closed minded in their religion department its almost like brainwashing. I am not religious and when, on the occasion I decide to be truthful in my essays about my lack of faith, I get lower grades on them. Most people lie about their faith in religion class to get an A. During mass, students are disrespectful and do not participate. Most people there are white. There is a huge cheating problem within the smart kids because they are so afraid of getting anything lower than an A. Students are constantly pressured about college and grades its causing a lot of mental issues such as stress, anxiety, and depression. great school, great kids, great education, athletics and extra curricular activities. My kids enjoy the school and I am happy to send them there. Great school. Great athletics & academics. Fantastic community feel! Highly recommend - such a fantastic option. Number One priority for the school is their Football and Basketball programs. They are no different from a college where they recruit athletes, mainly minorities who would not qualify otherwise.The curriculum does not benefit the students, there is a huge teacher turnover, my child had 3 Spanish teachers in 2014, the teachers assign busy work for homework, such as word search puzzles, the teachers allow homework to be turned in late-(colleges NEVER accept late assignments). The administration touts how easy communicating with teachers is, but most do not return emails within a timely fashion.A high percentage of kids transfer to other schools after the first 1-2 years.Drinking and drugs are a huge problem at the school. They used to be strict, but now if you are one of the randomly tested with a positive result you get counseling, and if caught with paraphernalia you are expelled. They don't test Football or Basketball players.The best thing about the school for the parents, is that the campus is very safe during and after school hours. This review is for Chaminade High School only. The middle school is a separate campus and our experience there was fantastic and a sound investment in every sense of the word. Now for the high school. THE GOOD: It is a nice campus, and safe. My daughter had great friends and her overall experience was nice. There was a lot of school spirit and the kids generally go on to college. The deans, teachers and college counselors were great and worked very hard. THE BAD: We had 4 principals in 4 years. We lost a lot of good teachers to "Blended Learning", which I feel was thrust upon the teachers without much time to prepare and the students and parents largely hated it. Great programs like Debate are "run" by speech teachers who show up at the parent meeting and then you never see them again, while the college helper does all the work and gets none of the credit. If your child plays a sport, it needs to be football or basketball. Otherwise your child spends 4 years changing in the car or Starbucks because our child's sport didn't rate a locker room, plus sub-par coaches who are willing to work for very little money and openly argue with one another during games. Speaking of money, the push for donations is RELENTLESS. We paid full tuition for 7 years and the emails, postcards, phone calls and letters for more money were a regular occurrence. If your child wants to go to a UC, he/she will need a 4.2 or above because many of the UC openings for California kids go to the top 10% of public school graduates first, something nobody mentions to you. But, if you want your child to be accepted to a $50,000 a year private college (minus the Ivy's), this is the place to be. My older son attended this school about 10 yrs ago and I had my younger son attends few years ago. The school has completely changed since my older son attended. Chaminade used to be about academics, it's now run by the athletes and a few privileged families who make enormous donations. The teachers are now coaches, who turn on a slideshow and watch a baseball game in class. There is absolutely no instruction given. These kids cheat daily and are woefully unprepared for the college entrance exams in the 11th and 12th grade. Save your money or spend it at a "Real" private school such as Notre Dame or Louisville. This is a wonderful school for middle school and high school. The teachers really care about the students, and supporting them in becoming well rounded individuals. The block schedule prepares students for college and helps them manage their time. The sports and extra curricular activities are top notch. This will be the best investment you will make in your child's future. The school is really Safe environment. Very strong program for English literature and the staff are friendly. My son is super happy at Chaminade. We were at Buckley for from K-8th grade. He had an excellent education there but we are so happy Max is at Chaminade now because we really wanted him to play on a boy's volleyball team and to be able to learn a bit about the Bible too. Max is SOOO happy. He is 14 years old and I feel like he is soaring at Chaminade. Thank you Chaminade... It is a joy to be there. The families are very welcoming and kind. We feel very included there Teachers are awful.They do not teach.Hand out worksheets and tell kids to do it without explaining material.Kids cheat to pass class by turning on their hotspots and finding answers.Very few kids get leadership positions.Kids choose their friends for all the spots.Same kids get multiple spots.No spots left for the rest of the kids.So, those kids college applications are filled with the leadership spots. They are Ambassador,link crew, blue crew,diversity.Same kids are on all of these.Not fair.Huge drug problem with kids vaping in classroom and bathroom.School needs to put in a detector in bathrooms.Alot of kids leave the school after ninth and tenth grade Eighty five kids left last year.Spend your money at a school that teaches students. Absolutely agree with the previous review regarding leadership clubs. Dominated by many of the same students while isolating many others. Thus allowing those selective students to “seem like” they are more “involved” to beef up their college applications. While students who really want to get involved aren’t given the opportunity. Our high schooler applied to 3 leadership clubs only to be rejected by all. Really hard to hear your son/daughter say, “I’m really trying and want to get involved, but...” Oh, and then even the patronizing rejection email the Link teachers/faculty leaders sent. Their use of “awesome” and “people like you” makes one feel like they are addressing a 3rd grader. Needless to say, we all had a good laugh over the following excerpts: “Thank you for your interest in the Link Crew program. We are so glad you applied! You are awesome. Unfortunately, this is a very competitive year for our program, and we do not have a position to offer you. Of the more than 200 applications we received, we have selected 94 for interviews, which means that a lot of people are receiving this email today – a lot of completely awesome people and you are one of them. We mean it when we say THANK YOU for letting us consider you!”........ It is you (and people like you) who make our school the wonderful family we are....Yours in family spirit,”This school like any other has pros and cons. Leadership by the President and Principal are mediocre at best. Heavy recruiting for athletes and providing athletic scholarships, but not for academics. Generally, students are accepting and pretty nice albeit entitled. It’s a private school so entitled to be expected. Our high schooler has a great group of friends and feels comfortable at the school or we would have left back in middle school. As patents though, we feel cons outweigh the pros. Definitely not a true college prep education or experience. I would never recommend this school to anyone. There are a small number of outstanding teachers, but that number is dwarfed by the amount of incompetent ones. The school knows about the bad teachers but is too afraid to do anything despite an overwhelming amount of complaints. Additionally, the school rarely recognizes students who pour their energy into achieving high grades. An excellent example of this is the awards night that the school puts on once a year. You only get invited if you have straight A's This means you will get invited if you take the easiest classes on campus, but if you challenge yourself with difficult classes and get one B, you will not, even with above a 4.0 GPA. Finally, the counseling department is awful. They don't help when problems arise and they don't know how to help when it comes to college application. I'll say it again, and I can't say it enough, I would never recommend this school to anyone. Phenomenal school. Our son is so happy there. He is an athlete and scholar. This school is the best secret in the San Fernando Valley. We toured everything in the valley to pick the right school. I waited two years to write a review just to be sure I had an accurate view of the school over a long period of time. I am equally blown away by the quality of Chaminade Middle & High School.We tried LAUSD and LVUSD for our kids. The schools were the right fit, but the majority of kids were not. My kids are finally surrounded by a majority of peers that have character, pride, follow rules, want to learn, and are proud to go to school. The staff and teachers are remarkable. If your child is willing to seek help, they will provide. I never thought we would find the dream school that was the perfect fit for my kids. Both of my kids are in sports so we play other schools and I go to the “away” games and get to see firsthand how the kids interact with each other or how they dress. I leave every time, so grateful for Chaminade, the values they expect from their students, and the parents that have taken the time to enroll kind kids in this school. Even though it is expensive compared to my local public school options where I felt academics were still good, the experience my kids will graduate with at Chaminade is worth every penny. While I'd love to give a positive review of this school, I've got to say, I'm fairly disappointed as to how things have been handled there by the administration. They have a history of cancelling AP exams without letting the student know until the last minute (despite saying that they allow students to self-study for exams), and it's essentially "their way or the highway" in terms of choosing classes you'd like to take for math or other core classes. Both of my kids attended the middle and high school. While the middle school (under the direction of Mr. Valentine) is exceptional. The high school fall short of that experience. They need to focus more on quality of teachers (math especially) and focus more on the big picture, not the pettiness of detentions (that they hand out far too often). Also, counseling department needs some help too. Outstanding education and holistic experience. Will make college easier.

column3: This school is getting better and better every year. Principal is really a good leader and wants to make difference but need more support of teachers and teaching skill. Parents involvement is necessary. I believe that teachers should be tested more frequently about their knowledge of content and teaching method. If this school has bad review, it is not because of principal or teachers but it is, because some parents do not care about their children at all. I wonder if they know what grade are their children in. My siblings and I all graduated from this school. We all had college scholarships and we very active in high school activities. The number one issue at this school is lack of parental involvement. There are some very caring teachers and smart kids in Chester. Education has to start at home.

column1: Clio High School is an average school. This schools academic program is set up in the most simplistic form possible. Yet most students here will still fail class after class. So in attempt to fix the clio made Freshman Academy and with it Link Crew. Freshman Academy is supposed to help freshman, when they enter the High School from the Middle School. Link crew is a group of upper class-men who are supposed to mentor the Freshman. All Freshman Academy has done is help there self confidence. I didn't know that being able to skip an entire day of school for fun games in the gym was helpful in a academic view point. Even link crew members emit that the entire program dosnt help. In all this school has low test scores, low grades, and in all unwilling students. But there are a select few students that are actually thriving in this system. Since the system is already easy anyone who can do basic math and other subjects will ultimately pass without any real struggle. A 3 out of 10 is how I would rate my experience Its a decent school, they do some stuff to help make sure you pass I guess. I never really had a problem understanding stuff.

column3: This year, Northwest HS ranks 50th among the top 100 D.C. area high schools according to the Washington Post. I believe the school will continue to climb with the successes its students and teachers are achieving. The academics are excellent, and the average learner is supported as well as the high achieving learner in the Ulysses Program and AP classes, as are students in NW's wonderful LAD program. The school is very ethnically and socioeconomically diverse, rendering much flavor to the high school experience in Germantown. Keep up the great work, Northwest! Very happy with this HS,the teachers are committed to success,my son is feeling comfortable so far and that make me feel that way too. Northwest has proven to put the students first and prepare them we'll for the transition to college. I firmly believe in Montgomery County schools and Northwest has not at all been anything short of exceptional. The entire goal of high school is to adequately prepare teens for college. I feel Northwest has done just that and then some more with the positive emphasis on extra circular activities and honors courses. Northwest HS has excellent academic programs and an excellent Principal. The teachers are great as well. NWHS has been amazing over the past 4 years. My kids are consistently challenged to excel, and are both attending excellent colleges next fall. I am more than pleased with my experience with this school and its academic programs. Northwest is an EXCELLENT choice for public schools in the area. I've found the academic programs here to be extremely successful in preparing students for college!! this is a great school. Northwest HS has excellent academic programs and an excellent Principal. The teachers are great as well. Great experience for high achieving student! The Ulysses program challenges students and helps with college preparation. Former student. I believe Northwest HS prepared and nurtured its students positively in order to obtain future success. Additionally, the internship programs also helped to shed light into what to expect in the real world. If you are thinking of transferring your student to NWHS - think twice, would be my advice. The only thing they care about is "looking good" before the county. The principal is a condescending, know-it-all lady, who looks down on people and is ill equipped to deal with the diverse students/parents population. Most of the teachers are really good though and do care for the students - it is the administration of the school that creates problems. This school is great, its graduation rate is 95 percent. such an amazing and diverse school! and an absolute amazing fine arts and drama program! I have had 2 children attend NWHS and they have enjoyed the experience, friends sports school and glasses. They were prepared for competitive university life. Northwest is a Great school, strong leadership, positive environment Our two children (3 grades apart) attended Northwest High School. Both of our children required Individualized Educational Programs. All of children's teachers, counselors and coaches worked diligently with our 2 children. The children's I.E.P. Teams were so very caring and conscientious throughout their 4 years at NWHS. Northwest High School was a great fit for both of our children. Our children attend great colleges now thanks to Northwest High School. Amazing! Northwest has great programs for students: AP classes, sports, clubs, theater and more! It is a very welcoming and diverse school. My experiences at Northwest High School have been wonderful. The leadership, faculty, and staff are strong, knowledgeable, supportive, and professional. Such a great school. My son is lucky to be a part of it. My son has fantastic teachers and is doing well with the online learning. We love the music program and clubs. Great school!! Great school. Diverse staff and students. Outstanding Ulysses Research program. Very involved principal. Wonderful experience through and through! There are a lot of bullying in school. Great school no bullying and all around the teachers are pretty great there is too much bullying at this school it sucks

column1: I am a freshman at Garner- Hayfield and I love this school! Everyone is so kind and the teachers are great!! The sports are great! Everyone out for a sport trys their hardest and leads GHS to succus! (:

Washington High School is a great school that includes everyone from every walk of life. column1: The school administration and teachers are not passionate on what the students need as far as education. Their concerns concentrate on cell phone use between classes and places late arrivals (students) in sweep as punishment. So how is this learning???? After dealing with this school for 6 years we are so disappointed and feel the school as a whole is a failure. Parents of upcoming students should beware and do some serious research. I disagree with the posted remark posted March 21. There were big discipline issues before the new principal took over in 2008. The rules state no cell phone use on campus & when a student is tardy class is disrupted. If BCHS is to be a an excelling school students must take advantage of what is offered..quite a bit at BC. What happens at school is the result of what happens or doesn't happen at home. That is the bottom line. If parents aren't willing to take a stand with a child/adolescent & cause the child to suffer the consequences of their actions the child won't learn that in life there are always consequences. If parents don't parent everyone suffers. BC is making great strides. Boulder CReek High school is an amazing place for kids. My son has had the best experience in academics and activities. He is graduating in 2010 and will have a full ride scholarship. Thanks Boulder Creek teachers for the great learning experience! I am a student at this school and I absolutely hate it! The students that attend are disturbed and strange. Once I started school here, my friends started to change and move in with the wrong crowds which there is alot of. Though the teachers are reasonable and nice. I'm definately leaving and going to a different school. I do not recommend this school for your child. An outstanding school with opportunities for all, Boulder Creek is a wonderful place for kids. Sports, clubs, advanced classes, special programs for special ed students. Boulder Creek has it all. The Arizona Republic reported Boulder Creek received one of the the top scores in the state on AIMS science. They were recognized for one of the best music programs in the region by Phoenix Magazine. The basketball team won the state championship. The school has it all! When I attended this school, I thought it was subpar, but however after comparing it to others public high schools and some private ones, Boulder Creek is amazing. Teachers are knowledgable in the fields and push students to work hard. My college roommate was the valedictorian at an unnamed private school, but does not know what party John F. Kennedy belonged to or how to use a unit circle in trigonometry. I would recommend this school, unless you want to instil Christian values into your child, than a private school is recommended. As far as shady characters, all schools have them and Boulder Creek probably has fewer due to it being in a wealthy area. BC is amazing! I learn a ton especially in English class and Spanish. In these classes the teacher actually make us think. I am glad to be a student at BC. The honors and AP teachers are wonderful - inspiring and providing a top notch experience for students. If your child is ethnic descent not the school for your child. The students get away with racial epithets, intimidation, and continual harassment. What makes it even worse is that they make your child feel as if they are the problem. Also school is full of wanna be gangsters from a higher socio/economical class. This is really amusing! The school has drug issues due to the parents who are self-centered and are busy with their own personal anthem housewives agenda. Most students have no courtesy or discipline. So if this sounds like a place for your child be my guest. I attend boulder creek. dvusd has seriously slacked in ensuring qualified teachers over my 8 years with them. if you need extra help, do not attend this school. if you do not like opprobriously disrespectful kids, do not attend this school. if you do not like teachers who do not care for you, do not attend boulder creek (there are two teachers i have had that actually care about their students out of dozens). just a little insight from the inside. I am the grandparent of a special needs student at Boulder Creek High School. The staff and students treat him with respect. The teachers are amazing and really do care about the students. This high school has had some negative press in the past, but just come on campus and see for yourself how hard everyone works to to ensure safety and education for all students. If you think it is easy running a high school, just volunteer in one for a week and you will be amazed. I think the principal (Lauren Sheahan) and the administrative team is fabulous. I am constantly amazed by my colleagues at Boulder Creek High School. They are always working to provide the best education possible to every student. Teachers are inventive, creative and believe in the vision of the campus: Act locally, Think Globally, Collaborate Digitally, Educate Wholly. Just today a math teacher used skype to host a classroom conversation with students in Germany. The Chinese and art classes teamed up to learn about sumi-e painting. Students in the brand new science facility learned about medical conditions effecting Arizona. The government classes held a mock debate between the potential candidates for President. The student government sponsored an amazing assembly with the band, choir, cheerleaders, dance team, and athletes. The best part of the assembly was when the student with special needs was the hero of the wrestling skit and the entire school cheered for him. Tonight a student band is performing a concert with all profits going toward support for a student suffering from cancer. Tomorrow the varsity girl's soccer team the varsity boys basketball team will play in front of a packed house. What a fabulous place to teach and learn! My daughter attended Boulder Creek for one year. She was bullied throughout the year, and the Administration's attempts to resolve the situation were completely ineffective. We removed her from that school after she was physically assaulted. She is now at a charter school and is much happier, as are we, her parents. After she switched schools, I heard from other grownups that Boulder Creek had a lot of problems. My daughter took some special ed. classes, and the special ed. teachers were great, but the bullying was out of control I've been a student at Boulder Creek for two years now. I came from a small school, so Boulder Creek was a drastic change for me. By drastic, I mean horrendous and bitter. My experiences here have been good only in my academics; my peers are anything but role models. Most of the guys are wanna-be gangsters who act higher than all, and most of the girls spend their free-time cutting other girls down. I've had numerous instances of bullying and exclusion, because our school is full of cliques. The teachers are fantastic and really care about their students, but the students are inconsiderate, irresponsible, rude and inappropriate. I can't stress enough how much I dislike my peers, and feel constantly judged. Very few parents are involved in their child's education, and parent teacher conferences are often quiet and uneventful. I give administration and the teachers a great rating, for they have greatly helped me, but the environment is anything but beneficial. This school is the best school I've ever been to! The classes are very interesting and the teachers really care about their students. The variety of the classes are very large. There is something for everyone. The school area is very modern and cultivated. The infrastructure is very good and new and they have for example a very healthy cafeteria. I have always felt comfortable when I attended this school. I would recommend it to everyone! i moved here from Texas and i was excited and opened up to meeting new people, and ready to start my life. But when i started trying to meet new friends they just all blocked me off and ignored me. The boys are ridiculous and act like wanna be gangsters, everybody is into smoking and going to raves. The girls grab the boys in inappropriate places. This place isn't ideal to what i thought it would be. people don't respect other people and the place is overly crowded. I'm begging my parents to take me out. My sister is a freshman and she likes it because their still kids. But upper classmen are not role models at all, and I'm afraid that my sister might turn out like one of these airheads. Oh and freshman friday is real to immature seniors and juniors. I don't recommend this school . Academically however is wonderful, but the students are bad. I just finished my first week of school at Boulder Creek. I love it! The teachers are nice and the classes seam interesting. At lunch I got a pride ticket from the Principal because I was dressed in jaguar print colors and showing school spirit. There was music at lunch too and everyone was having fun. I think this will be a great year. My daughter attends BCHS and loves the teachers and her counselor is just amazing. Yes there are too many student's in this school however the PTA works in unity to provide a safe learning environment. The teachers have been great to my son. He has been able to stay after school and get extra help and that has build his confidence level greatly. My children attend Boulder Creek High School in Anthem and I must say I am not at all in favor of new common core changes. I feel the school system does not teach our children what they really need to learn as it is. The only thing the district as well as the State is interested in is high Aims scores and not teaching our kids the core of learning. Teacher's tell the students that the computer is there best friend and they can get there information from there so if a computer is teaching my child why do I pay tax's for a school & teacher that DO NOT perform there jobs. I feel you need to work on your teacher's first then you just may see the results form the students you are looking for before you go and change even more to our childrens education. And furthe more you say the new common core changes are going to be more confusing and the children will have more homework which is the LAST thing these kids need. They should be doing the majority of the work in the classroom with a teacher that can help them, not at home were the computer teach's them or us parents are left to help them when we have NO idea what they are doing. The school system in America is broken. This is our thrid year and I now understand how everythign is fine until you need assistance from the school. I do not mean assistance because of a bad student, I mean an Honors/AP/Dual Enrollment over 4.0 GPA student. Whatever you do make sure you follow up on Dual Enrollment, as my student was told everything was fine and he was in the class for a semester to find out somehow the test was mis-placed or not taken, and "Dual Enrollment" for college pre-req was lost and they will NOT get credit. Very disappointed!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Boulder Creek is an outstanding school for a self-starter to get that "next level" education experience they are looking for. The school is structured to mirror our society in America, where hard work is rewarded. Attitude and citizenship, as well as scholastic excellence, were encouraged in my son's classes. Academic, athletic and extracurricular studies are as good as the student cares to make them. I applaud the staff in acknowledging individuals who are there to learn and grow. Do not send your child to Boulder Creek HS. It is, at best, a below average high school. The principal has limited skills for the job and the last athletic director they had was horrible. The baseball, football and basketball program are not competitive at all and are getting worse. The head baseball coach is horrendous and has been looking to get another job for several years. Sandra Day, Pinnacle, and Cactus Shadow are all better choices. This shool is complete garbage . Lots of things happen that admins do not know nor try to figure out . This school is perfectly fine. I've had 3 years of great teachers (a decent mixture of gen/Honors/AP) and all admins and counselors have been helpful. Its unfortunate to see some negative reviews but my one tip to prevent problems would be to take Honor/AP classes. You will find the most dedicated students here and classes will go a lot smoother. The teachers here also perform a lot better because they have students that actually want to be there. Boulder Creek High school is a wonderful public school with something for everyone. The Lip Dub they did this past week is a perfect example of this. Every kid in the entire school 2600 kids, had a part in the show. There were the usual cheerleaders, student government, band, and athletes but there were also roles for the diversity club, GSA, manga, choir, theater, art, dance, pre-med, chess, interact, National Honor Society, key club, youth transition program, mathletes, visual voice, media production, engineering, FBLA, Educators rising, marketing DECA, computer science, water ski, mountain bike, hockey, creative writing, World cultures, global studies, teen library leadership, and even the ping pong club! Boulder Creek has something for everyone. I love Boulder Creek. The school is cool. Teachers are nice and care about students. I am learning a lot and preparing for college. Outstanding community and community involvement, at the top end the school is fantastic, at the bottom end it is just like any other school, some kids just don't want to learn, but the opportunities are there for all students. Leave your political brainwashing views out of the school. The young minds should not be hearing your negative political rhetoric! You are paid to educate them with well rounded information! This school has hate filled leaders who are trying to indoctrinate their students rather than teach them. The Principal and the athletic director have nothing but hate in their heart. Terrible, terrible people.

column3: I could not have asked to have gone to a better high school than RFH. Now entering my third year of college, I have been given many opportunities to reflect on what an excellent education I was given at the high school level. I can definitely say that I am ahead of the curve at my school through opportunities such as the senior project. I feel as though the school prepared me for just about everything that I needed to know when entering college. As an education major in college some of my greatest inspirations and supporters were my high school teachers and staff. This school does not have a moral center equal to which I ask of my children. It may however be reflective of the community in large part, although not entirely. The most important thing to the school is winning. This is especially apparent on the athletic field where winning is above everything including morality and fairness and even loyalty to the community. There have been coaches later reprimanded and removed from the school who are left in place until the championship game took place despite the administration being aware of the indiscretions prior to the championship game. Once the championship was secured the coach was removed from the school. It is now acceptable policy in this public school to recruit athletes from out of the district so that they replace the students there in terms lineup, position etc. I know if two teams this year that recruited out of district players who were in their freshman year and appointed to Varsity for their team and one was named Captain over students that were long-term team members and well deserving of those positions. In terms of academics again the focuses is on winning. If you have a child that is pursuing options other than college, such as service to their country in the military position, it is a very difficult conversation to have with the school. Although statistically student that take some time off after high school perform very well in college and in later life the school will not aacknowledg that as it reflects poorly on their statistics and the pressure on students to conform to the schools expectations is extreme. It is with great dismay that I say that the school does not have the students best interest at heart, what they focus most entirely on their ratings reviews academic and athletic achievements. If you're looking for a school that considers your child as an individual you need to look elsewhere. A great HS that prepares young adults for a post HS learning experience. Teachers that have long tenure and work hard to motivate students to want to learn independently.Tons of extra curricular activities for students to get involved in and a strong sense of parent involvement in supporting these programs and the school in general Beautiful campus, great facilities, quality education, and overall wonderful experience. Great selection of courses, good athletics, and all-around great educational experience

column1: I was a student at Wilson High School, and I am enraged at some of the comments I am seeing about my alma mater, especially from parents and students who cannot use proper grammar or spelling. To those parents, take an interest in your student and make the first move to call the teacher or principal. I am sure they will make the time to talk to you. As for the students, if you'd listen in your classes, you wouldn't make such terrible spelling and grammatical errors in your posts. I attended WHS from 1st grade until I graduated, and was always encouraged by my teachers. They were always looking out for the students' best interest. They were also fair in their punishment of those students who chose to disrupt their classrooms. My great grand daughter is a fourth generation Wilson student. I suppose I have nothing to compare to Wilson, but my experience over the years with the staff and the level of learning speaks for itself. Especially through my family. I am over 65. I attended Wilson and went on to become a Registered Nurse. My son was drum major and participated in band for 9 years before he graduated. He went on to become a Physical Therapy Aide My daughter graduated there and now is an employee of the school. My grandson graduated as well. Now, I have a first grader there and feel confident she will receive the best education just like her family before her. Great school and staff! We need to be objectively honest here, instead of biased and one-sided. There were good experiences/memories here, but unfortunately, there was (and is) also favoritism by most of the staff, particularly toward those who are involved in athletics, certain clubs, and/or if one was an honor roll student. Unless one was one of those, one was usually not taken seriously, and teachers had little to no time for them. There was (and probably still is) bullying that is all but ignored by the staff, especially if the troublemaker is an athlete. I love everything about being a Wilson Warrior!! My children love this school! It’s a great one! Major lack or diversity, few teachers communicate with parents when needed, lack of arts program, lack of foreign languages, only a few sports teams that don’t experience terrible season after terrible season... When you go up to the school you’ll notice the parents’ and students’ lack of motivation, dressed like they just crawled out of bed. Students are left to fend for themselves against bullies, and unless you’re an athlete or top academic student, don’t expect to feel a part of the school. Standardized test scores are mostly below state average (which is already bad) and there is a sad percentage of students who pursue college after graduation. Don’t recommend.

It is a very sad statement, but the other schools failed to protect him in this most basic requirement: Milford, NY, JC, ME, UV. column1: This school is great!! You should totally go here!! The teachers and students are so nice and the classes are great too!! I no longer feel students are safe here. One student was pinned against the lockers and had his/her life threatened by other students. When the parent came to the school demanding to see the student that had just been assaulted, they were placed in a separate room and told they couldn't see their child. An hour and a half later the parent was told everything was fine and the student would be remaining at the school for the day. The administration "swept it under the rug", as they have done with many things of late. Bullying from faculty and students has become a daily norm. When the above larent wanted to file charges with the local police, they were told they had better not, it would just make matters worse at the school. As a student, I feel like the environment is great for the most part. Because of it being such a small school in a small town, everyone knows each other. The teachers are very laid back and friendly. The school board however, needs improvement. There's not a lot of options for classes, sports, or other activities. For example, there is no football, swimming, golf, soccer, or anything like that. There is boys and girls basketball, volleyball, cross country, cheer, and we co-op with Georgetown- Ridgefarm for both softball and baseball, as well as track. Most students and staff are very friendly.

column3: We had 3 students in this school system and though the school is making marked improvements in teaching staff, and gradual improvements in curriculumn alignment, the process has been too slow to benefit most students. Four Blocks: The elementary school utilizes 4 Blocks which largely neglected teaching of phonetics, basic grammar, syntax, and spelling. EDM:The elementary school utilizes Everyday Math which neglected to teach students regular long division (where you end up with a decimal) or handle decimals without converting them to fractions. The EDM method did not teach how to divide a smaller number by a larger one, i.e. 37 divided by 99. Most EDM methods are so non-traditional that parents need the reference manual to teach themselves how to help their student. Our students did o.k. but only because we made sure the limited class choices at the high school level were supplimented with online VHS and/or VLACS classes. Limited extra-curricular activities other than basic sports and student government. There is no active band or chorus at the middle/high level. Our children went through the high school. They earned numerous scholarships and completed college degree programs. All are successful in their chosen fields in the job place. Awful. My son has disabilities and every time there was an issue they'd call us to pick him up. No effective support for children with disabilities. Their special education program is a joke. Moved after 1 year because I couldn't keep my son in this school. We moved to town 3 years ago and pulled him out of school after the first year because of bullying and their lack of education.

column1: They have a major problem with bullies and the administration refuses to deal with it. I would never send my child to a school in this district. SWH has great school spirit. column3: Great school with great teachers. I would send my child there. AP and advanced courses are offered. Highly recommended for all level of students. We have had a great experience with this school.

column1: Great school. Wonderful athletics, honors courses are extremely well taught. Above and below average students receive all the attention they could possibly need. The HPAC is the pride and joy of this school, they take wonderful care and host many great local shows. Worst school ever. The majority of the teachers/faculty all act like they are in some sort of hierarchy. Staff treats students like toddlers but expects them to be adults. In my four years of high school here 2 out of 32 teachers (4 classes per semester) actually wanted to teach and enjoyed it. All the others hated their job and hated the students. I was constantly harassed over absences in which they wanted to suspend me? Because that makes sense. Ended up dropping out my senior year and enrolling in the community college to get my High school diploma (NOT GED!). Ended up blowing through that with straight A's and received my diploma 6 months before the school year was up. Overall this school is just horrible. If they could start worrying about teaching their students and not about which administrators have the most power than they would be fine. Havelock High School has been an excellent high school for all 3 of my now graduated children. My children are young adults now; they are all successful and loved attending this high school. Two of them were awarded scholarships to the colleges of their choice, the other an honor graduate in the United States Air Force. This high school gave each an excellent education and so much direction and fun through excellent programs in band, sports, and guard, in addition to their academic classes. I could recommend more a wonderful place to raise kids and give a great start to youth than Havelock and its schools, including Havelock high school. I am a Havelock High alumni and I graduated as valedictorian of my class. HHS was a great high school; the teachers and faculty were and are supportive, inspiring, and dedicated to their students. Many of them are still mentors to me that I feel I can always count on, and I will always have a home there. The band program is excellent; most of my favorite high school memories were made there. I attended Havelock high in my senior year in 2012. I just want to bring everything from this school to my old high school. I wish I attended Havelock for all my education. I'm proud to say I graduated from Havelock, how can I bring this education process to my old high school? This is exactly what my old school needs! One of the best public high schools in eastern NC. Currently 10 AP courses are taught on campus with more available on-line. Good students excel here and some have gone on to great colleges such as UNC, Duke, and the Military Academies. Numerous athletic and Academic scholarships have been awarded to NCAA D1 universities. One of the top football programs in the state. Numerous recent conference championships in other sports including basketball, swimming, and lacrosse. Incredible Band and music program. National Honor Society, award winning student council program, and many other popular extra-curricular activities are available to all students. My son just stated attending this school. His first day he was in the guidence councilors office so he was obviously late to class in order to get his schedule. School starts at 7:30am we were told to have him at the school at 8am. Why not bring him in at 7am? His first class was Physical Education. Hee didn't have PE clothes, because he obviously didnt know he would need them. His PE teacher told him to have a seat. He asked to use the bathroom and when he came back the gym was empty, no one was there so my son sat in the locker room. Waiting for someone to show up. The bleachers were pushed in. He didn't have any where to sit in the gymnasium. The next day his teacher was accusing him of leaving. Made my son stand directly in front of him and verbally abused him in front of the entire class. My son did nothing wrong. His incompetent teacher didn't give him direction. Later that day 2 boys got into an argument and one of them threw a desk and it almost hit my son. This is not a school that any loving parent would want their child to attend. Maybe this is normal behavior from kids and teachers here in Havelock. I don't want my children to be influenced by this. It's not normal and it's not ok. I'm honestly disgusted. My children will be homeschooling. Shame on this school and the teachers! The principle Mrs. Freeble is a lousy principle which gives no care for student safety after two school safety threats and still holding school and plus found people to accuse without evidence on issues the school caused my stay here has been absolutely terrible though there are some good teachers.

column3: As a parent and teacher I would grade Heritage High School an A+ In any category related to education. The administrators, counselors and teachers are 100% behind the success of every student at Heritage. Their learning facilities are the best in Saginaw County as well as their athletic facilities. The security around the high school is as good as it gets and students are made to fail safe. The only difficulties I see involve the student-parent relationships in which parents do not provide the student with the educational facilities and supervision they need at home. I have a grandson who will attend the school in the Fall. I am particularly interested in all aspects of the school. Heritage has more to offer than other schools in Saginaw County. The International Baccalaureate classes and Advanced Placement courses provide students with a top-notch curriculum. The diverse student population is the best! And the after school opportunities (clubs, band, choir, orchestra, sports, drama, etc) can't be beat! This was a quality institution while I attended; the teachers were both friendly and performed well at their job. Your average public school with typical liberal progressive agenda, major focus on sports at the expense of academics. Easily the top High School in the area for academics and athletics. The teachers are great, the IB Program is something that no other schools around offer, and the quality of learning is above the area's other schools. This school is way too big. Children who aren't in the AP classes are left behind. It seems that Heritage wants to compete with SASA, but that isn't what they are supposed to be: They are supposed to be a public school which is concerned for all students. Decent school but doesn't set students up for the future. Skills like innovation and imagination aren't taught. Classes are filled with busywork and doesn't properly assess ones knowledge. The counselors are counseling many students at one time, which has multiple negative impacts. It seems like all teachers having different teaching methods and doesn't accommodate to each individual. I noticed a lack of motivation/drive in students when it comes to academics. The environment and community is great.

column1: My wife and myself both went to West Mesa Class of 91 and it was a great school back then over crowded bust still a lot of successful adults came out of that area. Now as a father of 3 I have had to make the choices of where to send my children to high school. My oldest now 24 went to St. Pius. great school perfect for her. For my middle child we chose Atrisco Heritage. Now a senior class of 16 she is graduating with full honors and received an academic full ride to NMSU. Now to my son a freshman at WM I let him select his school, a student athlete who was recruited By Volcano Vista, Atrisco heritage and Cibola for football and basketball. After attending a lot of high school games over 4 years prior to this year, He chose West Mesa. He loves it there 3.5 GPA , No Drama, Loves his coaches and teachers. and its in the District we live. High School is about having fun participating in your school and graduating at the highest level you can reach. Athletically APS doesn't produce many D-1 College athletes. Lets be realistic. West Mesa is a Great School that gets a bad rap there are drugs and trouble makers at every school. if your kid is bad there just Bad Kids! For the most part it’s ok. There are some wonderful teachers who have and continue to have a positive impact on my child’s learning. Mr. Andrew Vigil and Ms. LouAnn Fayter are two that make such a difference in their students lives and their learning. We left a higher rated school due to bullying, teacher inadequacies and principle unresponsiveness. I regret not moving my child earlier. My daughter has thrived since the move. We were worried due to rating sites like this one. I am very glad we did not go by what we saw/read here.
