column3: I have 3 children..boys...7th grade, 5th and kindergarten. Love the schools. My 12 year old in 7th grade loves AMD. I am very pleased. My two older boys are at the top of their class. All the teachers that we've experienced so far have been fantastic. Ossining High School's math and science program are rated top in the country! The recognition that the high school has received in math, science, the arts, athletics and the placement of our graduating seniors into top universities, merit more than a 5 rating! Recently Westchester magazine rated Ossining number two in places to live in Westchester county. They listed the schools at the top of the reasons to live in Ossining! Great schools!!! As a parent I wanted my kids to be challenged academically, to have lots of enrichment opportunities, and to be prepared for life in the global community. OHS has delivered. Students who are motivated to do science research can work with world-class scientists in the NY area in a program recognized by Intel as #1 in the U.S. they can participate in excellent music, art, theater, Junior state, and sports programs. They can arrive in college with a nice portfolio of advanced placement courses. And they get to know all kinds of people. It's a well-rounded life. Very thankful for this school. My kids are both at OHS and are thriving, and very happy. They are right at home with diversity. They both excel academically, and the school has great sports facilities . We have gone through the entire school system and we would do it again if given a choice. I have actually looked into moving, and the kids got very upset. Love where they are! I have a freshman enrolled in Ossining High School. Her first year thus far has exceeded my expectations. Each student is assigned a counselor who will remain with them for the duration of each students' high school career. The school offers many courses, including advanced, AP and SUNY courses which do indeed prepare students for college in many ways. I find it hard to believe that in this site's review that the Ossining Science Research Program has no mention! This is an amazing opportunity for our students. All students in Ossining have the opportunity to thrive in a diverse, positive and amazing atmosphere that goes unnoticed amongst districts like Yorktown and Chappaqua. If I had to do it all over again, I would choose Ossining again and again. I have three children in the district who have all thrived and continue to thrive. Thank you OSSINING HIGH SCHOOL. I am confident that my daughter will continue to have a successful high school career and continue her successful academic journey into college and this begins with the foundation OUFSD offers. Excellent. My child and her friends have had amazing opportunities in the nationally recognized science research program, the arts, and the many AP courses offered. They have been accepted at top Ivies etc. No idea where Good Schools gets its scores, but it isn’t accounting for the fact that Ossining has long had a solid cohort of high achievers whose families choose to live in a real community, not a sterile suburb. Great. I get along with everyone. Teachers are nice and understanding. Great school. Best town for diversity and equity.

column1: Blackduck high school has high academic performance and does a great job of preparing students for the future. Blackduck is a great school with a lot to offer to the students. They always do well in math compitions, speech, knowledge bowl, and athletics. Academically they are a very strong school. I would recommend the school to anyone who was considering it.

column3: One of the better schools in Siouxland, top athletics, quality teachers and staff. Well built, clean, easy to navigate. Tons of Teenagers get disorderly conduct charges every year, this goes in their record. It's dangerous to stand up for someone as there is too much drama involved. We don't trust teachers, they don't do anything, there's fights almost every day! My children have both found ways to succeed at SC East High School with supportive teachers and administration. It's a large school, but they know my kids by name and take a personal interest in their success. They have figured out ways to bring out the best in them and have been in communication with me if they noticed any concerns. My children have discovered new interests and potential career paths because of the great guidance they've received in the classroom.

column1: WSHS is on the safest HS in the county. We moved from Lake Braddock school because there were entirely too many students there 4500+. My daughter loves WSHS and the administration does a great job of keeping the parents informed, especially when something unforeseen happens. The school DOES NOT try to hide incidents that occur at or around the school to make the school look better. Student safety is WSHS #1 priority and I have the emails from the school to prove it. Anyone who thinks WSHS does not keep the parents informed must not have an email account. I have countless emails from WSHS. One could actually become annoyed from being too informed by the administration. Anytime something happens at our school or anywhere else, we receive an email from our school and the FCPS. My son graduated from West Springfield High School. It is a good high school. We moved from Michigan to Virginia. My son found the school officials friendly Whatever you do, do not have your child take French. When you start a foreign language, you are saddled with it, and as a result I am now stuck with a teacher who never teaches us anything and expects us to know what we're doing 100% of the time. Honors classes are not as scary as they sound do not be afraid to take them. They are a great alternative to AP courses. I am currently a freshman at West Springfield, I honestly can say it is awful! To start off this is the last school to be renovated in fairfax county and lets just say it not a lovely sight, most classrooms are to cheap to even have white boards and they still have old fashioned chalk blackboards! But looking past the building it is still horrible! I took three honors classes and had to switch out of all but one because it is way to much to handle on top of all my other classes! I have been taking advanced placement classes for a very long time with no issue, but here the honors program is just a lot of extra work and nothing but work! Each honors teacher at West Springfield treats you like their class is your only class and loads you with on a average at least an hour of homework for each class a night! The regular classes are not much better with I would say an average of 30 minutes or more each night! Add that all together with seven classes! THATS A LOT OF HOMEWORK! That does not even count for the many projects they assign you! Also THE TEACHERS DON'T TEACH! I just moved here from out of the area and in a 55 minute class I feel like we got more done than in their 1 hour and 30 minute long classes here! The teachers barley teach for example they will say something once and never repeat it and if you did not happen to hear it then you are screwed for your next test because that thing they mentioned ever so briefly will certainly be on there! Moving on from the horrible teachers, you would think since Springfield gets a lot of military families moving in and out frequently they would be used to getting new students set up with all of there online programs, but NO THEY ACTED LIKE THEY HAD NEVER HAD A STUDENT THAT WAS NOT FROM FCPS ATTEND THEIR SCHOOL! It took me forever to be able to log on to the school computers and I still have no idea what my school e-mail is! ON TOP OF ALL OF THIS I AM A STUDENT ATHLETE, there is no possible way to mange practice for 2 hours everyday after school and for 2 hours from 8 am to 10 am on Saturdays with all of the HOMEWORK! We just had a for day weekend and my family and I could not enjoy it because I was doing homework the whole time! Furthermore, I have also not felt welcomed at all by students or staff, this is my 7th move and I can easily say its been the WORST! In conclusion, DON"T SEND YOUR CHILD HERE! Alright, so I've been here for three years. I'm a junior and I will say that this school has it's ups and downs. We're in the middle of construction, yes. However, to address the young person that commented saying this school is terrible, the teachers work hard and their methods may not work but they care about the students as they are. I myself take my time and get to know the teachers. Honors classes are a breeze and should be taken into account that the teachers will pile on more homework because you believe you are up to the challenge since you decided on what classes you would take. AP classes are a lot of by yourself work. Do not take them lightly and be prepared to, sadly, loose sleep. Now, students may complain and say that they feel like everything is unfair, but isn't that everyone? This school is probably better than most right now. I mean, we're stuck outside in trailers half the time while freshmen are coddled inside. I will only say that no one deserves to be disrespected the way people do it online. I will not stand to have children of all things say that about teachers they barely know. I have my opinions, you have your's, but do not hate the teacher. Figure it out how you work and make your path because this school has the tools where you can do it. Fantastic school located in an involved community! Excellent teachers, principal is really on it. Under renovation but it's going to be gorgeous! It looks good from the outside but grades are highly inflated. Students pass classes without any real knowledge of the subject and then move on to the next class, only to struggle and yet keep getting passed on. There are too many opportunities to pass in late work and retake tests, and this isn't preparing students for the real world and as such they are struggling in college. There are no consequences for student issues like tardies, cheating, disrespect, and leaving campus. The principal seems concerned with pushing his agenda through and doesn't seem to want feedback from parents, students, or teachers. And there is way too much emphasis on the state tests. Excellent school! My husband and I are so glad we moved to this area when we were relocated to DC. My daughter can't say enough good things about it and feels right at home. The renovations are a nice bonus. It's gonna look incredible when finished. Two thumbs up We’ve been very pleased with the quality of the educators, the curriculum, and the overall atmosphere of the school. The newly updated facilities are also state of the art. I was a former student at this school. Teachers are not effective and a lot of them seem inexperienced. They didn't really teach, just handed out packets to do. There were some good teachers, but most of them were mediocre and subpar. Teachers also favored certain students even if they were not worthy of a good grade. Especially the English department, they did not prepare me for college writing. They rewarded basic levels of writing that was below what advanced writing should be. A lot of teachers dumbed down the material and if you were to write above their basic standards, they would give you a lower grade. Multiple teachers I had got frustrated easily and did not take the time to teach. They seemed easily overwhelmed and did not do their job. Whenever I tried to meet them after school, they would ignore me and not show up at all. If they did meet me, it was only for a couple of minutes. Multiple teachers did this throughout my four years. When asked a question they would get frustrated and would not explain. Teachers rushed through material and didn't take the time to teach the new concepts. The counseling office didn't know how to help with the college process and did not give helpful information in regards to preparing us. Overall a below average experience. My experience is based on four sons who had different personalities and talents and their needs were met and more. One in foreign languages, one in music, one in history and one in drama. It might have helped that my wife and I were actively involved in school activities also. I attended WSHS before and during its renovation, hence losing a star. The school is beautiful now, but had a lot of issues when I attended. I went to WSHS because of bullying issues at South County. The atmosphere at WSHS is very welcoming and pushes students, sometimes a bit much, to succeed. Nearly every person from my class went to and finished college. Many of us, including myself, also went to graduate schools. WSHS pushes students to succeed academically and puts a huge emphasis on AP courses. AP courses help the school, but not the students; always try for dual enrollment instead! WSHS is a fairly diverse school that celebrates differences. Being a new student, I struggled at first to make friends but joining clubs and athletic programs is the easiest way to meet people and “fit in” at WSHS. WSHS is like all high schools: there are popular kids, kids who do drugs, kids who do very well, and kids who slack off, but I found this school to have majority of its students really want to succeed. Looking back at my time as a student, I realize just how much my teachers cared and that the homework I thought was so difficult was actually fairly manageable (despite the AP courses). I enjoyed my time at WSHS and met many wonderful people there. West Springfield is a big school, and the majority of the students and teachers here are nice. As a student with a 504 plan, for the most part it has been respected and implemented properly. The school is safe, and we have regular drills and very clear procedures. I will point out a few problems: This is an achievement-oriented school and there is a lot of pressure on us to take Honors, AP, DE, and get straight A's, be in honor societies, and be on a sport's team. They are trying to support student mental health and wellness, but the time where we did that was when we can work on assignments and study for tests. The teachers care about our mental health, but the student mental health lessons aren't helpful. This led to more stress because we had less time for our assignments, and we get a lot of them and I have had up to three tests in one day. Incidents where students use offensive humor (racist, sexist, homophobic, ablest "jokes") should be taken more seriously. On multiple accounts, I have heard my peers use the r-slur, racial slurs, racist jokes or say "special ed" as a derogatory term.

column3: The school went through serious budget cuts years back and they got rid of a large number of really great teachers. The administration is often slow in dealing with problems and the special education department is a mess to be polite. Parental concerns are often swept under the rug and the driving force is to just push the child ahead to the next grade and "pass the buck," no one steps up to be responsible for ensuring your child makes effective progress as a student. Support is said to be in place for students but nine times out of ten when they try to access that support it is unavailable. I would not intentionally place my child in this school system. Graduating from this high school would probably give a student the equivalent of a middle school education. They now have an Academy system that help advance the student towards colleges, and career paths. It an amazing advance program. Only the most advance schools have programs like this. I see Northbridge part of the top ten in the state in just a few years. They have addresses issues quickly and have effectively managed poor situtions. Outstanding programs and options for good students to exceed With parental support Northbridge is great for any student to succeed.

column1: My son graduated from WBMSHS 2 years ago and he got an excellent education there. Small class sizes, very personal attention to each student, full nurse staff, music, art, sports are all well-supported by the students, parents, faculty, and community. This is a public school that gives all of the good facets of a small private school. This school is on the smaller side. Small means students and teachers are not exposed to enough variety in culture. In addition I have witnessed teachers being treated poorly, both by the school system (school "leadership") and by students. Newly built school, great atmosphere and staff with many modern features to the building 10/10 The teachers with special needs kids in integrated rooms don’t know how to meet these kids accommodations. The teachers also participate in the drama at the school like they’re still high schoolers. They also don’t take bullying seriously i remember one time a kid threatened to do something bad and they did nothing about it.

The teachers care and they also trust the students to be mature and let their parent know when somethings wrong. If their grades improve, they don't call parents. The one bad thing about BC is it is so small and there is a lot of drama and backstabbing. Senority is also a big deal. Respect the upperclassmen, that's a big deal.

column1: As a graduate of this school, I believed my children would be best served here. My children are part of the open enrollment program, they have been for over 6 years, and now we are moving back into the area to keep them there (their choice). All schools have problems with clicks and popularity; but I think it is becoming a larger and potentially uncontrolled problem for this school. My child is almost "bullied" as a Freshman because of rank. I also believe that some extra curricular activities are currently being placed before academics; this was obvious to me the other day as my child spent almost 14 hours at the school for one activity (and classes). Overall, I love this school, but I'm beginning to question the methods of its education. Truly extravagant. The best school I've ever been in. Everybody is very welcoming The reviews on this school are a joke. One is directed at a student, the other is directed at one particular sports coach. It has nothing to do with the school itself. Kingsley is an amazing school.. from elementary to high school. The small town feeling you get with the school and community is refreshing. Staff all know your children by name, know their quirks, and how to make them smile. GO STAGS As a community member I feel unwelcome to provide suggestions. The school board President, said "You can talk till you are blue in the face, if no one is listening, what good is it going to do?" A previous Superintendent said it more subtly; "We all have to think the same way, or we will get noting done!" Meaning that any suggestions from the community, me, will be nullified by this attitude, or unwritten policy. When made a member of the Curriculum Committee, my request to be on the Agenda, was nullified and made optional. I was allowed to talk only after the committee was dismissed. My request to have the school publish the actual grade levels achieved by students in each grade was nullified and effectively rejected. There is a huge discrepancy in how you are treated based on your last name in this school. Lessons seam to be taught to the kids with the right last names by throwing the book at the kids without... and when a student with the right last name does the same "crime" it is covered up and they are not punished at all. This blatant favoritism feeds the mean girl cliques as they are convinced by the school and parents that they are in fact more valuable than the other students and they treat them like it. This school made me sad... I've never seen a more shortsighted view taken when it comes to student's success. I'm a student at Kingsley High. Some teachers at the school are fair and kind but most act like they have no clue how to teach and do the bare minimum. I have had so many problems at this school, its ridiculous. The students at this school are out of hand and disrespectful towards their fellow classmates. No one respects anyone and its full of a bunch of fake rude students. If you're a parent and looking for a good school to send your child this is not it. No one accepts the new kids and its very clique. This school is really only known for its competitiveness and good sports.

column3: I graduated in 2010 and I miss every bit of high school! Those 4 years were so much fun! I enjoyed the classes, the teachers, the extracurricular activities (mainly JROTC), and the overall environment! I wish that I could do it all over again - Bissonet, Meisler, and Grace King!!! The principal at this school, Meg Griffon is horrible with the school. She tries to run the school with an iron fist, but that has only made the students hate going to school, and one teacher even stated to me that they are all too intimidated to go to the principal with any opinion other than hers for fear of being fired! She has also had no parent involvement whatsoever since she's been assigned as principal. She claims she has an open door policy, but this is simply not true! Her assistant principal has been much more helpful towards both the parents and the students than Mrs. Griffon has ever been! Perfect! Everyone is nice there, the block schedule works perfect, there's only 20-25 students in a class, a lot of teachers, a safe school, good environment, a clean campus, it's just a great school overall! If you live in this district, SEND THEM HERE! It's perfect! I'm new to this school. I came from bonnabel high. My first few weeks were ok . Then people started to mess with me. The other day a guy him me .(I'm a girl). I'm new and no one knows me and everyone knows him bc he's "popular" . So they all said he didn't hit me . I got in trouble for him hitting me . Since then I been bullied everyday and it's still going on. I got to the point were I HAVE to be taking out of this school and be online schooled bc I can't deal with bullied and me getting in trouble for what they did. Also you can barely learn everyday the teachers teach something new, they think you can learn all that stuff in 90 mins. If I were you I wouldn't send your kid here . I'm a freshman at Grace King, and this school...well, this school is alright. I have found that the educational amounting of Grace King exceeds my expectations in some points (The Geometry courses are sipmly amazing!) but also lack in others (Creative writing: No creativity whatsoever.). Being in the advanced classes, I still do not feel like I am doing my highest possible range of work, but that's what the school gives us. As for students, Grace King is a great enviroment. When I first showed up, I was really scared, because I didn't have the best experiances with school the past few years. But the student body really accepted me, and I have lots of friends all over the grades. The Seniors are very helpful! The school is lacking in a good Band Program, but is working hard to get up to highschool level. The Band room, to our dismay, is the only room that hasn't been renovated. We also lack in support for our Girls Soccer team. Altogether, Grace King is a wonderful school! There's so much to do, and if you play your cards right, you can have a lot of fun! I'm A Freshman At Grace King High School The Student Body Is Amazing The Teachers Teach You So You Can Get The Lessons My First Thought Was I'm Going To Be Bored Out Of My Mind. Now I Love Getting Out Of Bed To Go To School. The School Spirit They Have Is Outstanding. The Rules They Have Are Really Crazy But It's Teaching Us How To Be Responsible Adults ,and When 20 Years go By You'll Say I'm Glad We Had Those Rules. If I Was A Parent I'll Send My Child To Grace King Also Assistant Principal Suzan Serigny should resign as she is the single worst administrator I have ever worked under. She overly identifies with problem students who cause a lot of disciplinary problems and actively backs them up as they give staff and other students a hard time. I was a new teacher working under Serigny and it was one of the worst experiences of my life. Serigny was extremely abrasive and offensive in a way that was completely unprofessional. She is a disgrace to her profession and should go into a new line of work I'm a Senior of Grace King , Class of 2015 , Grace King taught me so many things that's I've never knew , Its a blessing to wake up every Morning to come to school . The teachers are there for you thick and thin Im very proud of my school because we work very hard to make things happen at Grace king Some of the rules may be unfair , but we know how to suck it up and move on . Any parents looking for a high school to bring there child send them to Grace King . I am I Freshman at Grace King. Class of 2018! This is a wonderful school, the teachers are great and they push you to do your best daily! At GK we have many different opportunities to help our education, like AP courses and Honors. There is also and ample amount of activities to be in. I am class vice president and it is a lot of fun .We have football, Student council, dance team, pep squad, cheerleading and even video game club along with others.GK is a B school and our principal expects nothing less. Of course we do have some rules that we think are unfair but they do them for our protection. We may have a label from the past as a "D" school and some of the kids are not civil as well.All schools have that group of people and the disciplinarians handle it very well. This whole year we have only had a small handful of fights and of course none were gun related. All in all I love Grace King and honestly it is the best school I have ever been to and I feel that I am a better person because of it! I hate this school! The new principal comes there and just changes everything. The traditions we've been doing and everything. They make us not want to attend school. When mrs.griffon was there she made the school fun but now it's like we're in prison! They discontinue classes that the kids were taking and no good subject to replace it. The lack of communication with the parents. Need more information about daily happening are not consistent. We have had a great experience at Grace King High School. It was good at first but it progressively got worse and worse. It's my senior year now and I'm constantly so stressed. NOT at all because of coursework, but because of the pure laziness and ignorance of the staff. I've had to fight them for so much that I should have to. (fun fact: my grade level was wrong and I went twice to get it fixed and I ended up having to email the principal to fix it because the counselors are so incompetent. And THEN after fighting to get it fixed, they still failed to print my ID correctly so I'm still being pegged as an 11th grader when I shouldn't be! Thus creating MORE fights I have to make for the rest of the year in order to get what I need since my ID is wrong! yaaay) Grace King is like the ultimate metaphor for modern society. Unfair treatment, lazy administration, all walks of life in the same room together, and an unclear goal.Don't come here unless all you need is the diploma to further your future goals. If you want a good education, scholarship opportunities, and/or literally anything that would improve your education, do not come here. This is the losers' brewing pot. There's a reason we aren't in the advanced academies. It seems attendance is all they care about. The education of the child is pretty much last on the priority list. Abysmal, difunctional faculty. Macon is a failed leader and his staff follows suit. Do whatever you can to avoid this institution.

column1: Pittsford schools is a great school to go to, friendly atomosphere, excellent teachers. Has a great sports program. If you need one on one help, they are willing to give you everything you need.

column3: I do not thin'k the school is very well run. The food is horrible, fruits do not even taste well they are frozen and with no taste. Teacher's are not very interested in the students. column1: My wife went to this school and now my son does. This is a good school and it seems like the staff really cares for its stupents education. I believe that this is one of the best school in Ohio and this area is great! I just moved here from southern ohio and my son now goes to this school. column3: I went to Mooreville all my life. I must say K-5th wasn't bad, but I was just a kid. When I hit 6th grade things went down hill. By my 8th grade year I hated it more than ever! There were so many teachers who decided if they liked you based on your popularity or appearance. I hated it. Mooreville was extremely judgemental and harsh.... Favoritism was also an issue. The academics were good, but when it came to socializing.. Mooreville isn't very good! Worst school ever! I went there my whole K-12 and hated it! Then my kids had to go there cause they said I couldn't pay tuition for them to go somewhere else. My kids hate it. Mooreville is all about money. If you got it then you got it made if not you don't. When I went there was teachers sleeping around with others and the coaches sleeping with students and those same ones are still there . But of course the school system doesn't want anyone to know about that. The kids that have it made can wear whatever they want and walk around with cell phones all the time. When my children would have their phones took away or sent home for something they wore. My review of the school is worst school ever!! Really wouldn't even give it one star.

column1: I agree with the above poster about being political, however having being new myself I learned if you get in there get involved CONTRIBUTE something in anyway you can be it monetary or just your time you will be more then accepted into the politics.You can't sit on your thumbs and cry about it, you participate and they invite you to join. The priority of this school district is sports over academics. I am involved in the middle school and high school. The reading capability of majority students is low at best. I have 2 children in the elementary and I am busy teaching them after school more in a couple hours than they learn in a few days and they can read better than most high schoolers. I have heard many stories from middle and high school students that teachers give away grades and find non academic ways to receive extra credit in order to pass to meet UIL requirements in order to play a sport. Just 2 days ago I was shown a picture of a coach/teacher that was taking a nap, feet propped up on his desk, while the students were just chatting. There are a few great teachers that stand out because they care about your child's education but the overwhelming amount of staff is medium quality or below. I attended this school and I can say from first hand experience that I would not recommend this school ortown to anyone. The people in this town are very click-ish and that does include school staff. If you movethere from another town, people will go out of their way to make you feel unwelcome. The kids will bullyyour children. I can say that if you are from a big town , you don't want to move here. We moved here from a big city and my son had many new friends on the first day. He is finally enjoying school and learning. Great staff and the kids are very polite. Small towns are click-ish and the people of small towns in Texas are the local native people who don't care for outsiders coming into their home towns and trying to turn things around, and the local people like how things are in their towns and don't want change, especially the business owners of small towns. With all that said, people of small towns are some of the best people you will ever meet, especially after you have made time to get to know them..........people in small towns will give you whatever they have to help you and people who they don't even know! I plan on moving back to small town Texas even though I will always be an outsider, at least, I will not have to live on top of my next door neighbor, like I currently do here in big town Texas. "Here's a saying about small town people," "If they don't know something about you, they will make something up about you, just to say, they know something about you, to the local people of the small town." "It's the way they roll, you got to love them for it!" GTR

column3: The staff and faculty are first rate. The city of Davis is very focused on education as the University (UC Davis) is the main employer in town. Small town feel with big city opportunities. Many highly educated people call Davis home. My son attends Davis Senior High School and loves it. Students need to expect lots of work and difficult courses. Highly recommend Davis Senior High School (and Davis in general). This school has lots of kids that dont care about their education all they care about is having fun not learning anything. Outstanding. I'm a parent who attended all private schools and this public high school is in the same league. Superb teachers, great facilities and equipment for things like chemistry lab, sports, etc. And other kids ha e educated parents which is a big factor in school experience and safety. Overall I would rate this school excellent. Prepared my son for UC Berkeley! Please be sure your review is 7 words or more in length Two years here and numerous incidents jeopardizing my child's health. If you have a child with special needs of any sort, this is not the school for your family. They are too busy, disorganized, and unprofessional to handle anything other than the "typical" student and there is a very apparent disconnect between administration and teachers, and then both display bare minimum communication with students and parents. Every area of this school needs proper training and some sort of team building so they actually work together.

column1: Love this school. Wouldn't want my children to go anywhere else! The teachers are excellent who know all of the students and work to make each one do their best. I love the fact that my children can graduate high school with college credits and help them get a head start. This is the worst environment I had to work in. The administration doesn't control the misbehavior of the older kids as if scared of ruffling some feathers. I couldn't believe the lack of competence and professionalism at that school. I would never allow my own or anybody else's child go there. Westville School has offered not only my Daughter's but our family the opportunity to learn, grow, and be involved. The staff and administration have served to not just teach our children, but care for them as individuals as well. Your child's success is built not just on the school, but on us as parents too. My Daughter was able to not only attend Westville her Senior year but also nearby Purdue North Central for dual credit courses and finished high school with 33 credit hours in college. Being a small school it's true they cannot offer as many extra curricular courses, however being small allows more kids the opportunity to participate. We are proud parents of Westville School. I graduated in 2007. This school is amazing and the teachers and staff are well equipped to deal with all learning functions. Im not saying this to boost ratings. Just to inform people westville is an amazing school. 2 Students attended k-12 and had a great experience! I graduated from Chesterton high school so this is what I’m comparing to Westville. I’ve also had the misfortune of having multiple kids attend this school. The school is completely disorganized. No communication between departments whatsoever. Misinformation about events and event times is routinely given to parents. It seems that there are a lot of teachers that work there that have applied to other schools but we’re turned down for whatever reason. Westville Middle/High School is a great school that offers many academic opportunities for students. It has continuously increased rigor, especially with adding more AP and dual credit classes. The staff is wonderful and work hard to ensure and promote student success! Westville MS/HS is a great place to teach. They hired a student support staff member who really helped meet the emotional needs of students on a daily basis as well as made himself available to staff. The principal is the most supportive administrator I have worked with. She goes above and beyond to personalize notes for staff because she is genuinely appreciative of the hard work and effort put in by her staff and takes the time to recognize it, which few other administrators do. Westville has a great work based learning program, is connected to AK Smith, and is a place I would send my child for MS/HS! The principal and her staff truly care about each student. They make every effort in making sure each student is given every opportunity to be successful.

column3: I had two children attend Ayala-classes of '09 & '11. The work and teachers were fine. The athletic department was a joke. When Coach Bowler was in charge of the baseball program it was horrendous as he turned that program into his personal "cash cow", if you didn't pay for the Bulldog off season program you didn't play in season. Which is against policy, the Director nor the Principal addressed our concerns nor with other parents. My two boys ended of quitting after being benched, definitely not due to skills as they both play in college. Be cautious with the athletic programs. Had a few issues with our counselor, trying to sway my son from taking classes I wanted him to take to help with college, he just wanted him to pass and graduate, and persuaded him NOT to take Chemistry. I had to go in and change that. As a current student here I feel certain areas can be improved. But overall this high school is what you make out of it. And I'm truly sorry for the bad experiences students have had. There are students and staff who genuinely care. As I said high school is what YOU make of it. This school is outrageous and chaotic. My firstborn son could not focus on his studies due to despicable teachers and rude students interrupting in his classes. I talked with the principle myself to ask if he could change my sons classes. He said no problem, but it was weeks before the principle actually REMEMBERED. Last but the very least, the elective my son chose, band. Don't get me wrong, the band is great, but the parent meetings are so important and its a shame that other parents NEVER attend these meetings. As a result, what's the point in calling it a meeting if only a few participate? My son was unhappy and was getting C's in classes when he should be getting A's. I switched my son to Chino, hearing that it also a great school. Reading reviews, I gave it one chance, and it blew my mind. My son is in Chino High, and WILL be staying in Chino High. My other sons and daughters will also be attending here. Overall, I strongly recommend to not enroll your students at this "prestigious" school and enroll elsewhere. This school is the place to be when you're into sports and extracurricular activities. I believe there is nothing wrong with Ayala, it's just very lively and active. The Band is the best in the state, Mr Stone is a great Teacher. I wish they would sign up for the tournament of Roses Parade. Great Marching Band Program Band and Colorguard is truly amazing. Provides the students with skills needed to endure change from high school to college. Mr. Stone the band director is inspiring and the students learn to become productive and responsible adults. The instructors are so involved to the success of the program and the students development as well. Amazing high school! All three of my kids went to Ayala and all three absolutely loved their high school experience. I absolutely loved the teachers and staff. They were very supportive and helpful throughout our time there. They are great for college preparation and strive to get all students into college. Overcrowded. Run down. Basketball coach is unapproachable and only communicates through email and refuses to speak to parents. Students seeking to play other sports or participate in band cannot do so without being penalized by the head coach. the school is average, there are many great teachers but many subpar ones as well the teachers dont help u learn anything and i been to 2 diffrent high school and this is the worst one i been to , its so outrages

column1: North Warren is slightly above average for a high school. The athletic programs aren't well supported by the community, and a general lack of school spirit is present. Few AP classes are offered, most troubling is the lack of AP Physics. There are a number of great teachers at the school, especially in the English, Science, and History departments. North Warren provides very little guidance on the way to college (no fee waivers, parent-student-college meetings, etc.) The campus is aging, but well planned. The students are of a high caliber in the upper level classes, and are generally amiable and friendly to all. North Warren has a great teaching staff and a fair principal leadership. Athletics seem to be improving and school spirit is up. The teachers seem to be very involved with their students. The new administration is showing great improvement. Great school with very nice teachers who want you to suceed. Same with the principal who is trying to make the school have a safe enviroment. The classes are hard, but the teachers help you and treat you like a friend. Some good teachers some not so good. My kid was an underachiever throughout HS and it wasn't until senior year that a teacher felt he wasn't getting the best and referred him to guidance. He ended up getting A's in that class and decided to pursue a major in Physics. Not enough homework is given so that they can be proficient in reading and math. Kids need to practice to be proficient - it's that simple. I agree with a lot of the posts here. If your child has ANY issues and needs services, they will FAIL your child dramatically. I have met more than one parent whose child has been basically bullied out of the school by the Vice Principal. If your child is not an over achiever or a straight A student, good luck. They will actively try and get you to send them somewhere else. They will also threaten to call CPS if you disagree with their special education plan, which is...zilch all they want is to get your child OUT of the school if he/she needs any special services). The teachers are good, the administration is HORRIBLE. Most teachers are attentive and informative. Some, teachers, would be more effective, however, if they communicate with the parents of the students. Great college readiness for seniors; guidance department was extremely responsive and helpful. Sports are improving. Great security. The school structure could use some updating; small classes a + Admin very welcoming to new students. Some staff went the extra mile to help with some exceptional circumstances. My child/student reports that the teachers seem knowledgeable and are responsive to questions. AP courses and interesting electives available. Chromebooks provided to facilitate assignments and tracking of various aspects. Great experience so far. Many of the teachers are so unprofessional. They are completely unapproachable for extra help. You have to make an appointment to use the library??? There is actually a Tik Tok video poking fun at how unapproachable and unavailable the staff is. I've never seen a school where it was acceptable for the teachers to make fun of students in front of other students and be disrespectful. It appears after their covid hiatus they don't want to teach any more. It's sad. My child is an honors students who loved school and wanted to teach. Now she dreads getting out of bed in the morning. The school is completely inbred. All the teachers, counsellors, and parents know each other. The new history teacher has taught ONE lesson this year (because his supervisor was there that day). Is there even a curriculum anymore? Is it ok to tell your class you were 12 when you "came out" and that our Founding Fathers were monsters? I wish I had another option.

I know many kids, parents love it, but ... So far, I've had 5 kids in this school. All with different needs and this school has served them well. In fact, of my older kids, one has gotten her Masters Degree with honors, another attended an Ivy League School and has an offer from Harvard to attend law school, the other will be graduating with honors from PBSC. We have 2 in high school and another going next year. Our experience is more than good, it's great! The best school I have been in my life

column1: The teachers care about the kids like no other school I am a student at Colon High School. I believe that Colon is the best school I could have ever went to. I am in the eleventh grade for the 2010-2011 school year, and the teachers are AMAZING! They love us. And we create strong bonds amongst each other. The principal is alittle iffy right now, in my opinion, due to her calling the class of 2010s graduation, "her graduation." My fellow peers are pretty much what you would find at every school, except we know everything about everyone here. Im in an advanced placement math class, College Algebra, so I would say that they are challenging academic programs :) Please dont hate on Colon. Its an amazing school. I love it here. I am a student and I LOVE it there! Amazing teachers, they care about us like we are their own children. I am a student here and I have to say that I haven't been completely happy with what I have had to go through with this school. The office faculty and leadership isn't very professional. I have had numerous problems with communication with the office workers. I also seem to have problems with my schedule every year. Some of the workers are condescending. The school work isn't very hard and I have heard a lot of people say they go to college unprepared. On the brighter side, the school has just been renovated, so the building is very nice and also, the teachers are really nice. However, I would not recommend going to this school.

column3: As a junior, I have gone to school in Yukon since kindergarten and I really enjoy it. We got a new high school this year (which is way to extravagant) and its really nice. As for the "drug" problem, there are drugs but people don't go around selling drugs to people, and not everyone does drugs, you just have to pick the right crowd to hang out with. And all schools have drugs and alcohol. Every single one of my teachers I have enjoyed, they all really care about the students and will help you succeed. I also noticed that most of the negative reviews on here come from parents who don't go to the school so they have no idea what its like, and the students seem to enjoy it. As for the policies, they go through the entire handbook at the beginning of the year so students know what's expected. At the beginning of my Freshman year I was surprised to find that Freshman really weren't bullied, you always hear horror story about kids getting picked on and you don't see it happen. I would reccomend this school to anyone and plan on sending my kids there when I get older. It really is a great school, and if you are skeptical about sending your kids there make them take Leadership with Mr. A! I have had one daughter go through and graduate from Yukon High in 2012 and love this school. I have a second daughter who is a Junior this year and is excited about graduating from Yukon. The teachers, principals and staff are wonderful. The new high school is phenominal. It looks like a junior college instead of a high school and they aren't finished yet. They still have a ball field and swimming pool to add. I feel any child would be lucky to attend Yukon High. My children started at this school this year I am not pleased with what is going on. I moved my children to this district after i thought the last one was bad i was wrong. They may have nice things but I was wrong they do not truly care for their students its what they can get to make them selves look good. To me places that are more into their look are not in it for their students they are for the money that they can get out of people. My brother and I grew up in Yukon schools and loved it. I was in the last graduating class at the old building, so I don't have an opinion on the new building. But in my case, going to YHS was amazing. Generally, the teacher quality is superb. There was a definite divide between the harsher teachers and the calmer, friendlier ones and in the end I think it was a good balance. Personalities aside, the teaching methods at Yukon have helped me so much in college, and I appreciate it even more now that I'm about to graduate from university. I had a great experience as a student there because my other classmates were great. It was very easy to "mesh" with everyone, and I have to note that it was especially prevalent with new students. We are a very welcoming charm about us. Yes, there is a party scene but it's certainly pretty easy to avoid it if you want to. All in all, I'm shocked at how great YHS is considering Yukon as a town isn't all that great. Great staff, great students. I'm really thankful to have gone here. Great school teachers and the facilities are great they work with the kids if they need help all around great place This is a great school system. There are many opportunities for the children both educational and extra curricular. My kids both perform above average on standardized tests thanks to these schools. To all those negative reviews (one stars): School are exactly what you put into them. If your kids aren't pushed at home to do well, then they won't. That's not the schools problem. Also, if you are moving your child from a small town school 'A', then chances are they will be behind. After moving my children here there was a lot of catching up to do (again, not this schools fault). Take that into consideration and give your child a chance to get used to it before complaining about the school and taking your frustrations out on the internet. It was alright. The students are the real issue, make teachers not want to do their job. Many teachers are just lazy or right out of college. My kids hate this school so much and that pains me as a parent. Talking to the school is useless. My kids are not a-typical kids, so I guess that makes them free game for bullying. I have witnessed a staff member purposefully try to emotionally hurt one of my children in my presence. I went here too and it’s sad to know it’s the same unacceptable behavior from staff, what would you expect from the students?

column1: I have 3 children that goes to North. I think its a great school.It is a big school but the teachers make your child feels like they are the only child there. And has a small town feel.I can go in and talk to any teacher at anytime if i want. Great school and would tell everyone to go there. Great school! I'm an involved parent and I'm proud of the school spirit of the newest high school in the county. My daughter has had a great experience up to this point. The leadership at this school is top notch

column1: Herriman is a great school with for the most part excellent dedicated teachers. The hallways are decently crowded but other than that is a great school with a relatively good high school environment. You don't have to be on a sports team to be accepted unlike Bingham. I would highly recommend this school to anyone this is outgoing or just looking for a good public school. I am not aware of any gangs at Herriman, so gangs are not problem here and drugs aren't an issue either if you aren't looking for them. Overall an excellent school!!! Herriman High School has been a great educational experience for my brother of which I am an acting Guardian. He was able to take college courses from SLCC while in his final year in HS The teachers were positive, encouraging and worked to create an environment for all different types of students to feel confident and comfortable while learning. My daughter attends Herriman high. She enjoys singing with the choir and she soars academically. She got a high score on a test and her teacher was really impressed with how dedicated she is. He gave her a key card. She won a free photo shoot which she used for her sweet sixteen! I love a school that acknowledges students achievements. i would give this school an overall score of 1 out of 5 stars. it’s a really big school, there’s a LOT of bullying, a lot of teachers aren’t great and the environment is just bad overall especially if you’re new. piece of garbage school with a horrible football team Herriman is a great school, they have the highest graduation rate in the district and are running a lot of concurrent enrollment and AP classes. Students are service minded and raise thousands of dollars for charity. The performing arts programs are AMAZING!

column1: i have gone to this school inmy 9th grade year before i had moved from down there. it was really crowed and the students were horrible and the teachers were just not that great either. i mean some teachers were okay but majority of them were not teacher accessible. Newton High is one of the schools to where they really don't care about anything... i have been going here for the last 3 years. and they haven't really improved on anything.... and to be honest with you this is the worst school for any parent to put your child in... and remember that im a student that's saying this. Just don't, they got a new building but the school still sucks, just don't, that's all This school is a joke!! It's so sad that our children are not being taught the things that are necessary for their future! I have tried to contact the principal many times and have not gotten a reply. And you can't communicate with people if they don't care! I regret moving to this district! Its sad! My daughter has loved attending Newton High School. The faculty and staff are very happy and enjoy working with the students. The ALANHS program has offered a very rigorous program for students who have an interest in a strong liberal arts courses. The students are happy. The teachers are working hard to get students ready for whatever they want to do after high school. Several students have been GATES Millennium Scholars. Good Job Newton High School! Just tried to register, don't want to but this is where we are zoned :(. Posted signs everywhere state that registration is between 12:30 and 2:30. Got there at 12:40 and the door was locked, two people sitting in a dark office. Without explanation was told to come back at 1:30. Very unprofessional, and a bad omen about this place if they can't even do their jobs correctly for registration. I am currently an enrolled student at Newton High School. I will be going to the Newton College and Career Acadamy for my sophomore year though. I didn't enjoy my Freshaman year at all because of the lack of support from the teachers, staff and students. Majority of the students could care less about learning, most of them are only their for their friends, girlfriends/boyfriends, sports, drama, gossip etc. Most of the kids are awfully rude and discriminative towards others. There are some good teachers there though, but I still didn't feel comfortable enough to have a conversation with them. There was only one teacher who I felt actually cared about the students. The teachers also have their favorite students, and by the end of the first semester, a few of them get lazy. The school is full of drama, and there are too many fights!! The principal takes away our right to use the restroom because the ill-mannered students keep fighting. And sometimes I feel that the teachers are only there for their paychecks. I found it very difficult to learn and grow academically because of the negative energy I was surrounded by. So, I'm taking a chance at the Career Academy. Newton high school is very organized, and have SOME great teachers but the way they handle things with fights and bullying is not great at all. For me..I take bullying serious. I will not let someone just sit there an hit me and push me around. I will fight back, which is called defense. you can tell the assistant principal so many times that someone is picking on you but they keep letting them off with a warning...so the next step is to defend yourself....but when you want to defend yourself you the one who gets wrote up, iss and oss when all you wanted to do is defend yourself. They should really work on that and listen to their students ...probably there wouldn't be as much fights..... Excellent faculty, but students feel entitled if they have even some intelligence. Unfortunately, solving problems with violence seems the norm for most of the kids and of course, phones out to record it no matter how badly someone is being hurt!

column3: A few exceptional teachers. Some not so much. I know several extremely bright kids who are leaving. So in the next few years check scores reno high's are sure to go down and if it is between manogue, sage ridge or Wooster IB And academics are important to you, iI encourage you to go to any of those over Reno High. Socially Reno High is extremely cliquey and smart kids have to act like they are not to fit in. It is also true that boys and girls are extremely promiscuous from several stories I've heard. I've seen a lot of examples of cliquey groups purposefully ignoring an individual or group. A lot of unhappy kids if they aren't in the major popular group. Apparently kids at Reno High aren't aware that this is bullying. Respect? The students have none for themselves. Honor? Honor what, the corrupt social hierarchy? Strength? There is nothing strong in academics or athletics here. I have gone to Reno High School for 3 years and I want nothing more than to transfer. It is not because I don't have friends or have bad grades. I'm an AP student who would generally be considered popular, but I hate the culture of the school. It is extremely cliquey and watching other kids be ostracized 24/7 isnt right. If you dont have money, play a popular sport, or have the right friends you are not noticed. Those who are popular are highely involved in partying aka drugs and underage drinking. Not to mention the nasty rumors that are constantly spreading and the disrespect for the school. Kids show up drunk and high all the time, girls constantly break dress code, and some teachers (not the AP ones) are consistently unprepared and don't care about the school. Do not send your child here. If they fit in they will get involved in partying and if they dont theyre going to have a horrible experience anyways. Reno Huskies are a pack and pack mentality here goes too far. Reno High is not a school I am zoned too. I was originally going to go to Hug High (really bad school) but instantly got a variance to this school. I like the challenging courses and the education we gain. Compared to other high school honor English classes, Reno Highs is the best and most challenging. Very good school which has 7 periods, giving us an extra period for more elective classes. This school is just overall perfect for me and I would NOT go to any other school. McQueen? There's so many kids there and the school is so small that everyone has to share a locker. Glen would be the second choice for me. The fact that Reno High has a high rating on Great Schools makes me question the validity of the site. RHS used to be a good school, unfortunately it is mediocre at best. The bar has been dropped very low - raising it's test scores, athletics run the school and fights/incidents are not reported much less dealt with on a regular basis if at all. This is an amazing school. The teachers and support staff do a wonderful job of being involved in the students lives. Sure, there are some issues with certain kids, just like in every school. People seem to believe that the school is where kids might pick up bad habits, but that starts in the home. At Reno High, it has always been the cool thing to be smart. There is enormous competition between the AP students to see who can do better. No one should ever feel left out, Reno High celebrates everything from Academics, Art, Theater, Band, Orchestra, Sports, ROTC, and any and all in between. It is a family, all Huskies belong to it. The high rating of this school makes me question if this site is valid or not. To begin, there is no parent involvement, the students are rude and disrespectful, and the school even allows a place where kids can go skip class and smoke if they want. Also, the "common core" program is completely detrimental to a student's education experience, with it's ridiculous standards. Furthermore, the teachers don't care about the students at all, and only want to make themselves look good for a decent pay check. Now, let's delve down into the core "values" of the school. Respect? The kids have no respect for anyone, not even themselves. Honor? Little to nonexistent. Strength? Academically and in sports, there isn't any. Don't waste your time considering this school, it's only a mediocre at best public school. It is a good school but the whole "zero tolerance" of bullying is definitely not that it is "okay you did this don't do it agian and they go off with a warning and not a punishment " and this is for all schools across the board and it's the fact that the people who get hurt emotionaly or physically get hurt again and it makes me sick to my stomach that the "zero tolerance" is really "we tolerate it till it gets serious" Terrible administration, ridiculous approach to scheduling any testing, teachers are overworked, overwhelmed, and undependable.

column1: Bluestem is a really great school, I am a Bluestem alumni and I'm so happy I was able to go Pre-K through graduation. The teachers go above and beyond and what is the best part is being such a small school there is enormous amounts of 1-on-1 time with the students. Music program is amazing considering size of school. Super safe for everyone, I never felt unsafe in my 14 years in the district. The new principal and vice principal are very involved and know each student. Most of the teachers are wonderful and truly care about the students. The school encourages students who want to continue their education to enroll in dual credit courses, the counselor works very hard to ensure students are looking towards their futures and planning accordingly. This is a small school with mostly farmers, all students are encouraged to participate in sports regardless of talent. I have been to this school since 3rd Grade and the school is good in the Elementary, but the high school and middle school suck. Awesome system and loving approach to kids! Terrible. As long as you show up and put forth a little effort, you'll coast through which will come back to bite you IF one of their graduates goes to college. Majority of graduates do not go onto higher learning and those that do have a hard time adjusting to harder coursework because the coursework at Bluestem is a joke. As an alumni, I would love to see things overhauled. Just because almost everyone at this school is low income, they are not stupid and they need to be challenged academically. As a current student at Bluestem, I would say I'm glad to have come from another school. I did my elementary and middle school education elsewhere, so I just came to finish high school and graduate. I have to say from my few years here that I'm way ahead of the other students and I've not learned anything new besides in the arts. The fine arts teachers are amazing at what they do and truly care about their jobs. As for the rest of the teachers, it's not too terrible, but it's also not top notch teaching. The only time you get "homework" is if you need to study for a test and that's about all. The student leadership is very poor, and school spirit is kind of rare.More than 50% of the students are disrespectful and rude. Teachers and staff don't punish the kids who need it. I haven't had any problems with bullying, but I know some who do. Reporting the bullying is almost pointless, and this school has the most drama I've ever experienced. People love gossip and teachers join in on it most of the time too. Kids with learning differences are often overlooked and not cared about. Students who are failing are ignored and allowed to fail.Bluestem does have it's positive aspects though. If there's a serious issue with student safety, it gets taken care of. Threats are taken seriously and dealt with quickly. The principal is great, a fun personality, and easy to talk to about any concerns. The teachers are active in the students lives and most of them are really nice people.In the end, I have to say I'd recommend Bluestem over any of the surrounding schools. They're an agriculture and business rich school, they offer a large variety of classes in the high school, and overall the teachers are easy to get along with. If you're an average student, this is the place for you and you will find your group of like minded friends quickly. If you're an advanced or gifted student, I'd recommend going to a larger school in a bigger town/city.

column3: I just graduated and I would like to say Troy High School cares about us students! The teachers and staff make you feel more connected like you're basically home. One advice I could give is always try your best and never leave work until the end! Best of luck I am an RPI student that has had experience, although limited, with Troy High as a volunteer tutor and from organizing some educational/college prep programs for students. From my limited time there it seemed apparent that the administrative staff do not believe in their students' potential. They identify, praise, and push the high performers but disparage the rest. When a classmate and I went to announce a College Application Essay Writing program to the seniors a few years ago, the students' counselor opened up with "These ladies are here to discuss a college app essay program for you all. For the few of you that are lucky enough to apply to college, you might want to listen. Don't forget, HVCC (the community college), will be here next week and offer automatic acceptance. But still, please, listen attentively." And then went to praise one of his "star" students, much to the chagrin and embarrassment of that student. I think that the parents that have the time need to get more involved and demand more from the institution. I also believe the school needs to open more pathways that take advantage of the hundreds of RPI students qualified and eager to offer academic support. I have been a student at Troy High School for the passed three years and it has been quite an experience. My teachers are always willing to help me in any way they can and made me the successful student I am now. One of the main reasons I like the school is because of it's diversity. They're are students of all kinds in attendance. I have one more year left before I graduate and I believe I will look back on high school as a wonderful 4 years of my life. Troy High is an amazing school. They have many electives and you can graduate with over 30 college credits. They have a variety of sports and after school activities.

column1: My daughter is in 7th grade at the Junior Academy. This is hands down, the best investment that my husband and I could have made. My daughter, who has always had to work hard for her grades, is developing a great deal of self confidence. The principal and staff have put so much extra time and caring into my daughter's education. They understand that she "Learns Differently" than other students. They are not so much about a test score, they truly want every student to master an understanding of the subject matter. If you are considering NDJA, there is not a better placement in Toledo for your daugther. Hands down the best. No matter your daughter's interests (arts, sports, adademics) Notre Dame has it all. They are the only all girls high school in Ohio with the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Program. For the fine arts, I have never seen a better arts department and the staff is outstanding. They excel in Speech Team, Dance Team, Choir and all the arts! You name it, NDA has it and the students make it amazing! My daughter loves it and will be well prepared for college and her future beyond school. As far as sports, they have athletes that perform great and many receive college scholarships. All around, a top notch school. Excellent teachers, involved parents, graduates admitted to top universities. IB program sets school apart from others in area. I strongly caution parents to thoroughly research this school before giving it serious consideration. It has a good reputation and a great marketing department. It is easy to be "sold" on this school when you visit. However, after spending a year there, my daughter has chosen to leave. She is an excellent student, but was unimpressed with several teachers. Some were simply under qualified, some who used favoritism overtly, and even one who was a complete bully. The leadership is arrogant and acts in ways to alienate parents; they are not interested in partnering with students/parents in the educational process. Simply stated, they don't "walk their talk". Additionally, while strong in athletics, the arts and music programs are very weak. It is very sad that I felt the need to write this review. I do so in the hope that other families will feel led to go into their school search with eyes wide open, ask many questions and perhaps be spared what we have gone through. Notre Dame Academy was the best investment my family has ever made for our daughter's education. Both of my daughters benefitted tremendously from their high school experience and have done very well. One has since graduated from college and is working and the second is in college. They have great heads on their shoulders and are confident in new situations. They are strong in their Catholic faith and look back favorably on their Notre Dame education. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a well-rounded Catholic education for their daughter. Notre Dame Academy was the greatest gift my parents could have ever given me. After graduation I came to fully realize how blessed I was to attend such a phenomenal institution. NDA is a well rounded school, excelling in academics (very high ACT/ SAT scores), athletics (several state bound teams per season), and the arts (esteemed performances and several state/ national Speech and Debate students per Speech season). My sisters and all attended NDA and loved every minute of it. They offer courses for all interests and offer honors, AP, and now IB courses to give students an extra push. Student involvement is high and parents are equally as involved. I know parents, including my own, that are still on boards and volunteer on a regular basis even though their daughters have since graduated. Teachers, faculty, and staff are all very friendly and try to establish a relationship with the students they interact with. When I come back to visit, teachers still know me by name. I would never change my decision to attend Notre Dame Academy, and hope incoming parents and students see the value this school offers. Notre Dame Academy has been an excellent investment . Our duaghter has grown in such positive ways since her began attending NDA. She has been challenged academically and she has learned to assess her priorities and balance her time. Academically and in terms of poise, respect for others and strong values and character, she definately out paces her peers in the suburban public schools. NDA is strong in athletics, excelling in pretty much every sport offered. Our daughter is happy when she comes home every day, she is excelling academically and in athletics, and she has grown iN very positive ways since starting at Notre Dame. This school has a safe and positive environment, strong teachers and leaders, wonderful young women, and opportunities that other local schools do not offer. We have no regrets and highly recommend NDA. The education is the best! But, the students are rude to each other. Also, I have noticed staff members can be rude to students for no reason. If you really want to get a good education, but not have the best social life, this school will have it for you. Best education, staff and students in town. I am challenged daily, I am excelling in advanced classes and I have the opportunity to work on a daily basis with strong, smart, and friendly students. I would choose to go to NDA all over again. This school has it's reasons for failure. For one, the academics are not as good as they make it. They don't really challenge as much as you would anticipate. Also, not on,y the academic environment, a student attending cannot go one day without being bullied by either a staff member, faulty member, or student. From my experiences, being a good 4.0 student, I have endured much stress from staff members who did not like my personality. Thus, getting in the way of my academics. Also, home life, being that my siblings also go to similar Catholic schools (St. Johns), the student turns out to be very belligerent at home. The environment seems to influence this. But it's not just my home life. Many friends and other family's have similar complaints as well. For me this year, it has greatly affected my home life with my family. Thus, I had to go. For those looking for. Good education, stick with public high schools. For they provide a student with a stimulating and positive environment as well as honors and AP classes. Thus, NDA is nothing too special, for anyone can get a similar opportunity anywhere else. Currently, we have 2 daughters attending Notre Dame Academy and have 2 daughters who attend college who graduated from NDA. I can say NDA has helped our daughters grow academically, spiritually, emotionally,... and they are well prepared for college. The faculty and staff have gone above and beyond to make sure the girls succeed in all areas. Our daughters (all above 4.0 gpa) have taken many challenging IB/AP classes and the teachers have been more than willing to go the extra mile to make sure they understand the material and understand that sometimes a students has a special situation that effects her ability to do an assignment in the given time period. Although many of the students who go to NDA are competitive, they are also willing to help each other. I thank God every day that our daughters have the privilege of attending NDA, and for the effort NDA makes to help any student who is academically qualified be able to afford NDA through financial aid. Our daughter graduated from Notre Dame and our daughter and our family had a positive experience with the school. Our daughter received a high quality education, she was challenged, she was an athlete and she was involved. She had many great friends and was challenged by the faculty. Not only did she receive a great education, she also grew as a person in so many positive ways and she made life long friends. Notre Dame teaches young women to be strong, confident, caring and supportive of others. No regrets, very pleased with our experience. 10 out of 10. Best decision we have made for our daughter. I've sent all 3 of my daughters here. It has been a great environment academically and spiritually. The girls leave NDA more than ready for college. It also does a good job at maintaining its Catholic identity.

column1: Decent administration, but many of the teachers need to just hang it up and retire. Mr. Antani is a beacon in this school. Greatest teacher and leader the school has and he's earned everyone of the 5 stars I've given to the school's teacher quality with everything I've seen him do (I hear this from my kids and a gaggle of other parents and their kids, too), but I doubt they'll be smart enough to keep him and the few others like him. School is just not what it used to be, sadly. This school is a typical high school, it has highs and lows. When I was a student here the nooks were old, the desks were older, but some of the staff was amazing. Ms. Mac was a wonderful teacher and the school should try to hire teachers similar to the passion she had for teaching. I graduated a few years ago from this school. It has some good teachers, and some bad teachers. The bad ones always seemed to stick around for way too long, and would make actually learning about the subject nearly impossible. The good ones would either leave, or would only teach certain classes. There was some blatant sexism going on in between the lines. Girls are limited to wearing clothing based on a strict regimen (because this would be somehow "distracting", which is textbook sexism), while boys are allowed to wear their pants down past their rear. Additionally, not allowing people to go to bathroom when needed? Wrong. The classes were fine, but the social aspect was annoying. Teachers who were there that obviously did not like to teach really should not have been. They made students miserable and caused extra difficulty to get decent grades. I digress, the class choices and curriculum were not bad, and most of the people were decent. I just wish they would get the rules and regulations into the 21st century where they should be. Honestly, it’s not that bad. Everybody says it is but it’s not as bad as most schools. Definetly not as bad as beckwith middle school so glad I’m out of there. Anyways it’s mediocre it’s no awesome private school but it’s one of the better public schools I’d say. There’s a wide range of sports and activities as well as academic and elective classes. Some teachers give out too much work while others give out none. The homework they give is usually pointless. Honors classes depend on teachers some are like you’re in honors you need lots of homework others are like i don’t believe in homework for honors. Most teachers will stay after to help you if you need help with something. We’re allowed to use our phones, there’s a dress code but it’s not super enforced, foods terrible but the snack shack has some good stuff like the cookies, desks are old and gross, books used to be old but now we all have our own chromebooks so most work is online, there’s lockers but nobody uses them and if you do you usually get weird looks because you’re usually a freshman. I don’t even know where my locker is tbh lol. There’s no time to use them since there’s only like 5 minutes in between classes and most of the time you’re walking all the way across the school. There’s 3 language options: spanish, portuguese, & latin. I’d say latin is the easiest. There’s lots of art and music classes. We only have to take 2 gym classes which is nice if you’re like me and don’t like gym. Theres also like carpentry, tv & radio, auto, drafting, marketing, childcare, etc. Students aren’t terrible but they aren’t great. They’re mean, they judge, and hate you for no reason just like every school. People like to act like there isn’t popularity in school but there is and it’s definitely shown. Spirit week themes this year were trash. Although the pep rally was fun. We were outside so it was freezing but that was just Covid hopefully we’ll be back inside next year. Hoco was decent, most of us thought the DJ was terrible, we were very crowded cause it was a tiny dance floor some people liked it, some didn’t.
