column3: Too pressuring, highly spoiled and enabled kids and parents. Teachers who take little interest in students. Very clique like and not a friendly place to be.Adminstration that doesn't respond to srudent/parent needs.Can't compare to LFAcademy or private schools! I am concerned about what the kids are learning with the less homework and less testing emphasis. Students who engage will be prepared. Extracurriculars are outstanding, but most kids need to find their niche to be happy. The school has tried to improve its approach to emotional wellness. Teachers are strong, though writing, in particular, does not receive enough focus and some tend to encourage the competitive strain that runs through the school. College assistance has been fine tuned, and more kids are really looking at more schools. The community is competitive, and that can help or hinder your child. Kids who have a strong skill tend to have better outcomes; the B student, with average extra curricular interest and abilities can flounder. The comment about improving feedback, apart from grades, particularly to freshmen, is one the school should consider. New principal really tries to know the student, in a way the old principals have not. Fantastic education. There is something for everyone. sports, music, new media etc. I would rate my experience at this school as a 5 out of 5. Going from the hell-hole that is DPM to LFHS was such a relief. You will not regret sending your child here. It is one of the best education systems I could experience in my lifetime. horrible, my student had a terrible experience at this so called "high school", what a joke.

column1: My experience at this school these past two years have been honestly hard to believe. While I applied, i was told that UHS was a "terrific" high school and that I would be challenged to out-perform others. Turns out, intellectual competition is saddening for a "GREAT" school and not many care about what grades they recieve. We are "the best" and yet the rest of the students do not seem to make the effort to become the best. -A current sophomore My experience at uhs was the greatest! Like honestly the teachers care about you can the principal maybe strict but at least we are controlled. Im currently in all honor class, and they are very challeging! I believe that this school is one of the best in newark! I'm going to start freshman year at UNIVERSITY HIGH SCHOOL , but I would love to get to know more about this school . I've heard it's a very good and respectable school to attend . I am an alumni from University High School class of 2013 and I absolutely loved everything about this school. The staff is dedicated to the excellence of the students futures and their well-being while still in school. You will not find another school whose staff is as nurturing and attentive as the facility at University High School. Go Phoenix!

column3: I have a son who is a senior at ROHS this year, and he has received an excellent education and will be prepared for college next year. He is currently enrolled in two dual credit classes and two advanced placement classes. The reason this site has received as many negative reviews is the fact that generally, people who are disgruntled are the ones who speak. Those who are content do not think to comment on sites such as this one. I truly believe that there are many more satisfied parents of students in Red Oak ISD than there are those who are dissatisfied. Count me as a parent who isn't pleased with this school at all. Poor teacher quality, weak academics, out of control students and incompetent leaders who consistently fail to address these problems are the main reasons this school has continued to rapidly decline. Also, bullying is definitely a major problem at ROHS. It has happened to my son and his friends and nothing is being done to address it. The fact that several other parents have mentioned bullying of students in their posts just shows you how widespread the problem is. I posted my comment here and later the same day, I was attacked in another post for exposing the bullying problems at this school. That is what you have to deal with at Red Oak High when you speak up. If it was your kid being picked on, you wouldn't be making excuses for the bullies. I am a mother of a Young Lady at ROHS and I love the school. She has attended Red Oak schools since ROJHS. Yes there are kids who pick and prod other kids but that is not the schools fault. That would be the parents not doing what they need to with their kids. My daughter has been picked on for her acne and I talk to her daily to see whatis going on now. My daughter doesn't bully people because she is. I as a parent have taught her not to be a bully. I don't put the blame on the School for bullies I put it on the parents. My daughter loves the schools and beged me to stay in Red Oak when we were looking at moving. A school is not just the Principals, teachers, and staff. It is the students and the whole community. I am glad my daughter is at Red Oak and so is she. All my support to the teachers who have to put up with disruptive kids. I am a big part of the program my daughter is in and will always like the teachers for what they have taught her. Red Oak is a great place to be. Love this school and everything about it! Keep your problem kids in other schools, please :D Has a dumbed down curriculum (research CSCOPE); teachers that are treated badly and harassed by incompetent tyrannical vice-principal; students know they don't have to work and learn because the district lets them recover credits by takin a short computer course after they fail regular courses. Teachers are beaten down and have given up, so they just go along. District is led by a superintendent who is totally focused on the money--thus they will allow anything to happen as long as kids show up every day so they collect their funding which is based on daily attendance. Weeks and weeks of instruction time are sacrificed by incessant testing and assessments, some of which are put together by central office personnel with no knowledge of subject matter--teachers are excluded from participating in any determination of instructional policy--total top-down political administration. Principal bows down to system and does not support teachers. I do not recommend. The school falls short when it comes to handling disruptive students. My son has classes where problematic students are preventing the planned lessons from taking place. Something needs to be done. Big enough to offer unique programs, and small enough to feel like an individual. My daughter attends ROHS and I love the fact that she has so many clubs, sports and programs to choose from. Urging your kids to get involved will mean a better year for them and you. Any time I've had an issue, the office staff seems eager to talk it through. Just sayin' This school is below average at best. My son is a senior and had we not made sacrifices outside of school to supplement the inadequate education at RO, he would not be college-ready at all. I feel so sorry for the parents who want a good school for their children, but are unable to afford outside tutoring and classes necessary for them to obtain a decent education that Red Oak fails to provide. I loved the education my two children received at Red Oak High School. I think a good education is the responsibility of not only the school, however, but the parents as well. This puts parents in the responsibile role of finding outside help if it is needed to supplement a child's learning, and if supplemental help is required, that is fine. Both of my children are doing great at the four-year colleges they are attending, and I give the credit to Red Oak ISD! Their AP program is outstanding!!! I do think you have to know what each child needs....and some kids just need more help than others. Teachers at RO do their best to provide for their students.... from what my family and friends have seen! Red Oak ISD is a joke and anyone who doesn't agree either doesn't have plans for their child to further their education after high school or enjoys seeing their tax dollars pay for the superintendents house along with many other non district related things. I graduated from Red Oak K-12 and now my kindergarten started this year and the only reason for that is because our house isn't finished being built yet and we live behind the elementary. The teachers are inadequate, administration all close personal friends that were brought in after Scott Nivens became the superintendent, the dress code is the only thing I can say they're strict on and well educated about. They check kids for socks! Socks! Who does that?! I've been to eat with my daughter several times and watched the lunch teachers make them throw their lunch away and not eat because the one the parents provided wasn't up to their standards (they looked just fine to me) I've then gotten up and bought (6 kids) since the first day of school lunch with the money I put on my daughters account because no kid should go hungry and then when it was brought up to the principle was told it wasn't any of my business. I CAN NOT WAIT TO GET AWAY FROM RED OAK. take your kids anywhere else and I mean anywhere and they'll be better off! I thought it was bad when I was in school and years later it's 1000x worse. Hi everyoneIf you like your child has a good disiplin and high education with very firendly atmosphere , this is the right place . I am so happy my son is going to this school and I believe , he is in right path . Thanks to mr Dylan best headteacher ROHS is awful and it is shameful to see a once decent school deteriorate into what it is now. All three of my kids have attended the school. My youngest is currently a student. The education she is receiving is noticeably worse than anything my older children experienced. Parents that value a top notch educational environment for their children should avoid Red Oak High.

column1: I am the parent of an 11th grade student at OHS. This school has been great for my daughter. They have been flexible and progressive and offer programming that far exceeds what I would have expected of a small, community HS. My daughter is an accomplished musician and the strings program and strings orchestra is excellent. They have a good drama program and vocal music program, too. My child has also been able to take advanced mathematics at the school and in partnership with the University of Maine. We have had an overall wonderful experience in a supportive small-school environment, with big-school opportunities. P.S. Excellent athletic programs, too!

column3: We have 3 children that attend this high school. It was recently rated # 314 out of 2000 is U.S. News and World Reports. It offers a multitude of activities and many AP courses. We believe that it should be an 8-10 on Greatschools website and are working toward the upgrade. Please do your research when choosing a High School. There are many sites to choose from. After you read reviews and talk to parents who have children in the school and school district you are considering to purchase in----you will have a more accurate picture. Quality of teachers has exceeded our expectations. Athletic program is getting better and more competitive every year. Extremely happy with the education, support and opportunities that Magruder HS has to offer. This school has an excellent music program and really great teachers. There is no other school like it. Our family moved from Out of state where our kids attended two of the best schools in the state We had reservations about Magruder because of the Great School Rating, but despite the rating the school has been amazing. The counselors and leadership worked with us to ensure our child was in the right classes and several of the teachers have gone above and beyond to involve our child in leadership opportunities to enhance their learning. Great experience for all of my three kids at Magruder. Upper level courses are very good and the community is wonderful. Involvement in the school beyond classes makes a huge difference. Like all schools, there are some real world issues to address like alcohol, violence and such. Staff handles all these well. There are strong academic and athletic programs at Magruder High School. I was both a member of the basketball team and took AP classes. The school felt safe as well as having diversity among the students and staff that helps prepare you for higher education. The county is known for good schools and Magruder routinely ranks high among the county schools. A diverse high school and rated one the best within Montgomery County. There are teachers, counselors and administrators who care and want the best from their students. There are AP and Honor courses which students can participate in and receive college credit. There are plenty of after school activities; athletics, clubs and organizations for students to take advantage of. I attended Magruder from 2001 to 2005, took on-level and honors courses, as well as participate in Track and Field. I can personally say, I believe what I learned from Magruder set a foundation for me to succeed in college. Diverse and well rated school with plenty of opportunities for high acheiving students. Great staff and administration Administration is apathetic and it has lead to a predominately apathetic staff and very little pride in the school by the student body. Very nice kids at the school that are being short changed in their high school education and experience. This school failed my child. It is a disgrace in a county that has always had some of the best public schools in the country. From its teachers to the counseling staff to the principal, I have seen a complete failure in the administration of their duties. If I could do it all again, I would move my child to another school. Both of my children graduated from Magruder (2020 and 2017) and are in college now. It was clear that their teachers were patient and communicated expectations very clearly. All of their teachers were very dedicated but their math and science teachers were particularly engaging. My children did not have a math or science background from home but my kids learned to love math and science at Magruder. The athletics program is first-rate. Certainly not every student is going to become a star athlete but the staff has the attitude that brings out the best in every kid who wants to participate. Also, when I have visited Magruder, I was always impressed by how the staff and students are. Students would actually run to the main door to hold it open for me.I'm not sure why there some negative reviews of Magruder, but every school has some students and parents who just can't be pleased.That's all I have. Hope it helps. My son attends Magruder HS and it has been a great experience for him. Teachers have really done their best to deliver a solid learning environment during this challenging time of virtual education and have communicated with us regularly regarding our son's progress.

column1: Quality teaching in a safe environment (even though the area isn't the best.) I attended Argo, and it was an excellent school. I feel that at Argo, you get what you put into it. I have seen students go forth and pursue Ivy League educations, as I have seen students who simply could care less. This, however, is no fault of the staff because I do feel that the teachers at Argo amongst the best. They are genuine, educated, and for the most part, warm hearted. In my time at Argo, the English and Math departments were the ones who I feel left a lasting impression on me because of their own experience and intelligence. All in all, I know Argo has a notorious reputation, but you would be a fool to write it off. It is in a bad area, but it really is a good school. Argo is a wonderful school with a great theater program. The staff and teachers are awesome Although this school tends to get a bad rap because of the surrounding neighborhood I would highly recommend this school. My daughter has been attending this school for 3 years and I am pleasantly surprised. The teachers go above and beyond to help students as well as the counselors, deans, coaches, etc. They offer free after school tutoring and have so much to offer as far as sports, clubs, etc. Don't pass this school up!! I am a resident of Willow springs and was originally upset because my daughter was not in the LT school district, however now I have no regrets. She is excelling and with the free ACT prep, tutoring, etc. she is preparing for college and her future. I have nieces who attend LT and struggle with a subject only to find out that there are not many tutoring/after school help for them. Argo is a great school!! I never feel unsafe nor does my child. Although the school isn't in the best area, I consider the school to be just as good as its counterparts Staggering H.S. and Sandburg H.S. The teachers are great with the kids and seem to be very motivated to teach. The schools facilities are top notch and their curriculum is very challenging for students including my son. He is currently in the Honors program and I see everyday how he is being challenged not only by his instructor s but by his peers. At first I was a little skeptical about the school but now I would recommend the school to any parents who may have doubts. This is great school--I would be proud to send any of my children here. The majority of staff members really care about kids, and there are excellent opportunities for students on both ends of the spectrum-- those who struggle and those who excel. There are many choices in AP classes, and the school has done a lot to build these programs for our kids. The school is very safe and well-organized. Don't let the rumors and gossip fool you-- this is a good school. Worst school I have ever had to send my kid to. He ended up getting his GED in his third year rather than finish here. My high school experience at Argo was phenomenal. If students applied themselves, they were challenged immensely academically. The honors programs and AP programs were extremely well-developed and prepared you VERY well for the AP exams. For instance, I took AP World History, which was NOT a forte of mine, and managed a 4 on the AP exam. There are good teachers here, teachers who genuinely care for their students and challenge them. The area the school is in is not the best, but the school itself is incredible. Also, there is an immense amount of extra-curricular activities that students can participate in. I alone was involved in 5-10 clubs throughout my high school experience and enjoyed every one. This school do not care about students academics, overall very unprofessional staff especially the attendance office marking students absent when they’re sitting in the classroom and send you to court for truancy tickets. Worst school ever! I don’t like the deans since the school started this year they been denying my daughter and giving me a hard time putting her in school I always have to keep emailing them a lot and they ignore me and been saying I stay with my sister in law she took me and my daughter in and don’t have no proof of address only thing I got with the proof of address is my I’D or mail and that’s it since we we’re homeless now staying with her only people that are respectful is the front desk and I am reporting this school the the bored of education since they wanna deny my daughter and not wanting her in school.

column3: I was going to write that the school is wonderful as long as the student is a regular ed student, but come to think of it even my regular ed child had a tough time here with the counselors advising him incorrectly about courses to take for college prep, wrong info about Running Start, wrong advice about PSAT/SAT test taking. My special ed childhad not been happy attending this school, he feels like a second class student with far fewer opportunities than his older sibling had. I'm pretty disappointed. Lots and lots of the kids sign up for Running Start to get out of the school sooner...how sad is that for a small rural school in a small rural town? Terrible institution with horrific leadership it is like something out of a Stephen King Novel. Quite literally the worst place my kids ever attended school. Do yourself a favor and don't you will regret every minute your child attends Lakeside High School. I love lakeside HS* very family oriented, small, 98% graduation rate & A very high rate of collage graduates. As stated in another statement* a lot of the kids choose to do running start not to get out but because they are ready! Why not graduate with a two year collage degree? Just means the schools challenged the kids & they were ready! Also if your ready for collage why not let the state pay instead of waiting two years & the kids have to pay? Smart choice to me & yes' my child did running start. LHS also has a great sports program. In one of the surveys LHS was rated 7th in the U.S. For its size as one of the highest test scores, graduation rate & collage graduate's. I did have a problem with counselers but as a parent I did my homework & figured out what was the best for my child! We've lived in Nine Mile since our oldest began Kindergarten so our entire school experience has been the Nine Mile District. We could not be happier! From Lake Spokane Elementary to Lakeside Middle School and now Lakeside High School each one has been a wonderful experience. We have been most impressed with our districts teachers and their relation to the students. They take any problem serious when brought to their attention and have been johnny on the spot to take care of issues. School pride is always high and it's refreshing to see kids enthusiastic about their schools! Wonderful school district with committed caring staff through all levels from elementary to high school. I would also add that I agree with another comment that the reason for high number of students doing Running Start is because of the financial savings, not because of their disdain for the school district. I am a former student of lakeside, graduated 2012, I don't understand how people can come on here and say there are no opportunities at this school from a parents perspective... You didn't attend this school. There are opportunities everywhere, it's just a matter of motivating yourself to spend the extra time or effort to take advantage of them as a student. Not a lot of students want to do that though. The teaching staff starts prepping kids for college as freshmen with courses available, at the school, that will get you college credit. I personally got college credit for taking accounting one and two, engineering one and two, and Photoshop. That gave me 15 college credits just doing classes I probably would have taken anyway. The students definitely know that there are classes available that do this. They just would rather take the easy route and take life sports or be a teachers assistant. I am a parent of a middle school student that has been in the district since 1st grade. I am also a high school teacher in a different school district in the area. Nine Mile School District has always had an excellent reputation in academics and extra curricula activities. The effort by the caring teachers and coaches at all grade levels is very apparent to the students and parents. This close knit community is fortunate to have high quality administrators, teachers, support staff, and athletic departments. Our family specifically chose this school district for our child based on the above average state assessment scores, school facilities and caring atmosphere of the community. Lakeside does well academically and athletically. There is something for everyone, if advantages are taken from LHS, Skil-Center, and community colleges. I have watched and been here as this school has tried to work with a less than ideal high school that is 25 or more years old. I have had two issues that I went to the administration with and it was resolved quickly and I was so happy with how they handled it. The superintendent is nothing less than passionate as many staff and teachers and other administrators are. We have a very very low turnover rate. That speaks volumes! I moved here specifically to go to this district. This is a great community that wants to keep low crime rate and well educated kids! (I would award zero stars!)As of this writing, there are 11 reviews. SIX of them were written within a few hours, and are all 5-star! I have no doubt all SIX of these are an arranged campaign!This school is so horrible, our children got their AAs from Running Start before they got their worthless LHS diplomas. This District doesn't care one bit about academics; they are far more interested in their sports and in carrying the bottom performers while ignoring top performers.In a Board meeting, a school principal warned the School Board not to listen to parents, because "they don't know what's best." This school doesn''t care what parents think, and are unaccountable when they lie straight to parents' faces. When asked, the Board stated parents should expect that their children would not require remedial math when entering college. Promise broken! Estimates are, as many as 85% attending 4-year schools in WA, needed remedial math.

column1: This school is great I would definently recommend it . Students are well taught . I would just suggest they pack their own lunch. My son went to the Middle school. In 3 words HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE, HORRIBLE. I was forced to withdraw my son because he had dispute with his friend off school grounds. There was a misunderstanding were they thought about fighting but did NOT. This was grounds for expulsion or the option they so graciously offered, withdrawal. There policies are completely unrealistic when it comes to teenagers. This misunderstanding happen through a third party trying to make them fight who also video taped the dispute. The boy that provoked/ video tapped is still a student. My son had never been in any trouble or suspended in this school or any other. My best friend daughter was bullied so horribly she had to go into therapy for thoughts of suicide. This school turnover rate as far as teachers/ principles is ridiculous. My sons grades where always up and down during his time here because in August he would have one teacher/principle and in February he would have another. Be warned and be cautious if you select the Friere Middle School for your child. I am a highly involved parent and it still wasn't enough to prevent my child from being railroaded. I am a MS parent also & I feel their discipline policy is not fully developed. Disciplinarians should have some level of child development training or at least be certified in Social Svcs. FCS specifically advises applicants that they will be working with urban youth, that being said-they should have systems in place to TREAT urban youth, not politely advise you to withdrawal your child. This is totally contrary to educating them. Their 'no tolerance' policy only removes that child from their school, this only contributes to missed educational lessons. Historically, researchers have found that suspensions DO NOT work. If the student is not a threat to themselves or others, FCS should consider in-house suspensions. I was not aware of the high turnover rate at the MS, however my child's teacher was recently abruptly 'let go'. FCMS, however, does have other systems in place to assist in student development. Unlike other schools, FCMS has an academic advisor for each grade, classroom aides, a family therapist, other non-teaching staff & pleasant staff to make this a full-service educational institution. I feel their lottery process is unfair. Don't tell them anything about your child or it may be used against you. i like this school mr steve is the best teacher ever and also alot of others and the bathrooms are ok somtimes they have poop in them and used toilet paper on the ground best school ever it might be kids who hit in the bathroom but overall best school u will ever go to they have xbox/playstation/nintendo there and a lot of big giveaways and events, if u dont go there u twekinn.

column3: My son will be graduating this year and another son will start there next year. I am an educator, and can say from my perspective, I have been extremely pleased with the quality education my son has received. The staff is extremely involved with the kids and there is a sense that they truly care. As a parent you still need to remain involved throughout your child's high school experience. Communicate regularly with your child's counselor and your child will thrive. Another aspect I love is the diversity of the student population. There is a true respect for all races and a harmony within rarely seen in many high schools. I have always said that if the world could get along like the kids at Chino Hills High School racism would be a thing of the past. It's not easy to choose a high school for your child, but I highly recommend this one for so many reasons. You should definitely visit the campus to see for yourself. I am so pleased with this school. My daughter has been involved in the theatre program and has had a fantastic experience. She has great teachers and is learning so much. She is a freshman and we look forward to 3 more years Hi My stepson is going to Chino High School, He is going to 11, next Year, however He is always complaining about the bulling at this school, He is 17yrs old this month, and highly over weight also always complaining about the excess of drugs at school, He doesnt like to be there do to this facts, my concern is about His way to see things and the way He talks about His teachers, pls keep track on this over weight INDIVIDUAL This is the 2nd year of my son in Chino Hills High. So far, I have no complaints about this school. The teachers updates me and replies to my email whenever I have questions about my son's homework or class work as well as his grades and class standing. I hope this school will improve more because I have a daughter that I'm planning to enroll here too in the next 2 years. I have nothing but great things to say about everything this school did for my son who graduated in 2012 after going all four years here. My son was so happy to go here. He worked hard in his academics with AP classes and sports. He made amazing friends and participated in yearbook, having more fun than I could've ever dreamed of. I'm very proud of the city of chino hills and this amazing school for setting him up for success. The activities director for the school is amazing, with their pep rallies and everything, these kids have so much love and pride for their school. I've heard great things about Ayala as well but this school was the best decision I've made and recommended to many other parents. The baseball program recently took an unknown turn as the new principle let a very successful head baseball coach go, Kyle Billingsly. Kyle represented all the qualities you would want in a high school baseball coach, but I'm sure the new principle will replace him with someone who has better credentials. Kyle's success over 12-years included, active players in MLB, top draft picks, D1 scholarships, and plenty of CIF wins. Looking forward to finding out what the new principle has in mind for what was considered a great baseball program. Decent school overall - homework a bit much and athletic department is a Pay-to-Play environment of prejudice toward any clubs not Legends or Dirt Dawgs. Nice to see they caught coach Billingsly and let him go. The dirt Dawg prejudice is ridiculous. So far I cant say anything good, teachers need to be more proactive as well as office staff This may have been the worst school experience I have ever had in my life, I have nightmares about going back there. Fix this school for goodness sake if that is even possible at this point. The staff at Chino Hills high are so lazy. The school nurse was never in the office when needed. Overall Chino Hills is a terrible school and I would warn any parent who thinks of sending their students here. I had to pay for additional tutoring for my daughter in order to be adequately prepared for college admissions. Counselors don't care about college prep for students and will discourage anyone with a lower GPA (my parent group has discussed this). This school is the worst and I will not be sending my younger child here. The enrollment process is begrudgingly difficult, as they requested things that no other previous schools touched upon. When contacted, they expressed an uncooperative opinion and would not explain the issue in depth. The counseling office and school administration are awful. Bad service and communication; they don't help students to solve problems.

column1: I'm an 8th grade student at the Rufus King Middle Years Campus (the proper name thank you) and I think the classes are just fine. I don't know what happens in the 7th and 6th grade classes, my classes are no where near theirs. Our teachers tell us about how their old school have been SO BAD and that we're so much better than them. And we just took our MAP testing, our teacher we had said our scores were a lot higher than her other schools. Last year our MAP testing scores were high above all the other middle schools and above National Average. The new leadership is very knowledgeable about what it takes to manage an IB program, as well as sensitive to the needs of students in the city. He has a vision for not just the two campuses that are considered to be one school but for what is possible in the IB world of MPS. The teachers are committed before, during and after school. They make themselves available to students and are accessible to parents. Many attend school sporting events and show their support financially as well as in person. The level of work is well at the college level and will provide students the lead they will need to succeed beyond high school. RUFUS KING HIGH SCHOOL is not comparable to the Middle school campus at all. There are two teachers in one class at once, so the student-to-teacher ratio is very excellent. This is my daughter's freshman year and she loves it. She lives in west allis, wisconsin and she gets transported nearby. The school offers transportation in a lot of milwaukee areas. She says that there's never been ONE FIGHT just yet. This school is just excellent, despite the neighborhood it's located in. She has a 3.500 GPA. I am very proud of rufus king and I regret not sending my other children here. The school also educates students with a lot of different ethnicities. I really love Rufus King and there has not been ONE fight as far as I seen. The teacher's teach very well when giving the lecture. Some parents don't want to send their children here because of the neighborhood it's located in. But parents DO NOT have to worry about that. This school is racially diverse (Hispanic, Asian and caucasion) and it is VERY mixed with all cultures. Nobody has had any problems with the neighborhood. Rufus King is such a good school and I hope that they continue to ONLY accept children who wants an education and with excellent behavior. This is the BEST MPS school to send your child to. 29 students at BAY VIEW high school got arrested, riverside has a lot of fights (Even though it has a good reputation), Hamilton has a lot of fights, and vincent high school has a lot of fights. But if you want to send your child to an excellent high school in the milwaukee area. I advice REAGAN and KING a choice. I wish the best for this school and that it continues to stay the way it is currently performing. I LOVE RUFUS KING AND I COULDN'T FIND ANY BETTER HIGH SCHOOL. As an ASIAN, I think that it's great that Rufus King has an ASIAN CLUB. Nobody don't have any bad reviews about the high school. But all the bad reviews are towards the middle school campus is horrible. Everyone has good reviews about the HIGH SCHOOL CAMPUS. The high school campus is filled with harvard-type students who wants to learn. I worked at the middle school campus and it was HORRIBLE. FIGHTS ALMOST EVERYDAY and over-crowded classrooms. But at RUFUS KING- HIGH SCHOOL CAMPUS IT'S WHOLE NOTHER STORY. I worked at other MPS high schools and it was NOTHING like king high school. Rufus King high school is a challenging academic focused high school and all of the students are HIGH CLASS. Many students get excellent grades in my class. They are so focused on getting prepared for college and their near future. Rufus king is a really awesome school. I advise ANYONE to apply here. My oldest sister goes rufus king high school and from what I heard it's really a good school. I wouldn't say the Middle Year Program is bad but its really difficult in the 6 grade. The teachers was really unorganized with work, tests, homework,and the students are really full of themselves, ignorant, and you know what I mean, i'm not trying to be mean but they wanted to their stuff their own way, last year they made the Art teacher cry, they were all up in drama and fights, it was really really ghetto. Though the classes are really much of a help, I took tutoring for math and science and it raised up to a B and C, I recommend taking the tutoring classes or ask the teacher for extra credit. My last GPA was 2.5 and I barely pasted music, the teacher for music was gone so they replaced a new one but he was horrible, he gave me a U and wrote review that said I didn't turned in my worksheets, it doesn't mean you have to give me a U for not turning in ONE project. any all the school is very bipolar but I might recommend going to a other school if you dont think the school is perfect for you child, its a IB school though so you may learn more, the highschool is good choice to get into a college or to get a diploma (im a 7th grader) I go to Rufus King Highschool and im not all into school spirit but I really do love my school. It is very diverse and brings challenges to students like myself, who find the curriculum in other schools too simple. Other mps students find Rufus King students "stuck up" because we work hard and take pride in our work. Just like every other school there are some idiots who act out, but that is inevitable. My daughter has attended King since 9th grade she's now a Sr. I have no issues with the staff and their leadership. Academically they push the students to strive to do above what is required of the average student. I think that is going to help the students better adapt to college life. My concern is King ranks well on paper but in my opinion they have the same issues as schools that are not up there academically. My daughter is in her junior year at King. In a sense, King is a school within a school where all students are expected to achieve but there is a clear path for those that are particularly focused. By junior year, students branch off into higher level classes, particularly in math or science. That's when the rigor really takes off and students are in a classroom of like-minded peers supported by talented teachers. Yes, it's an old, urban public school so it's no frills - no salad bar or heated pool. But the extracurriculars are extensive and there are many opportunities for competition using your brain, not just sports. King graduates are recruited by top colleges due to high ACT scores and the well-rounded approach to IB education. King kids are different, they are in an urban school and interact across broad cultural and economic experiences. Despite all of the competition, the kids support one another and are proud to boast about a colleagues "perfect" ACT score or free ride to Madison. They are in it together. One wish: Superintendent Thornton, please leave the high performing schools alone. Take the best of what they do and replicate it where possible. The high school is separate from the middle school they have two separate buildings and administrations Great Schools should designate as such. The school is pretty good . The students score high on math & reading . Can't really ask for more . Our son is a junior/class of 2019 and he has had an exceptional experience at King. The school offers a variety of extracurricular activities across disciplines - social, musical, fine arts, athletics, past times and more. The community has true diversity and the staff, students and families express a great deal of school spirit. Rufus King IB is an International Baccalaureate school. The students take IB courses NOT AP ones. The Great Schools AP/testing metric makes it appear that King offers no rigor, it is actually required. My daughter, class of 2020, loves this school. We believe she is appropriately challenged. Great Schools rating only considers AP classes and rating did not mention or consider the International Baccalaureate program. Rufus King International High is one of the most prestigious high schools in all of south eastern Wisconsin. It is commonly disrespected for it's academics due to the high concentration of African-American students who attend. King sends many of it's students off to universities other schools in the surrounding area wished their students would attend. It's time for people to wake up and realize what Rufus King is doing. No more need to be closed minded about sending your children to this school for the sole reason that it is in a bad area.

column3: Awesome school. Fantastic staff. The block schedule really prepares students for college. Their test scores are improving every year. I graduated from San Marcos High School and I have to say my experience was amazing. Great campus, teachers, and classes. San Marcos was a great medium. It didn't have the pompous feel of DP and the less than adequate curriculum of SB. The AAPLE Program is amazing. My daughter is so well prepared for university. Equally as important is that my daughter has loved the program, the school and really enjoys everything about SMHS. I went to SBHS and was a bit sad when my daughter didn't want to follow family tradition, but I feel she got everything that she needed and wanted. She loves going to school each day and loves her teachers (in particular AP Chemistry, AP History, Year Book and Tennis). Nothing is more important to a parent than this balance in education--excellent teachers, administrators, students, program/curriculum and the school grounds are looking so, so good. Way to go SMHS--go Royals. Cheers for the principal, Mr. Behrens and the AAPLE director, Mr. Nielson. Best kept secret in Santa Barbara. Great teachers and great kids. So happy we transferred districts to be here. The other high schools just don't come close to comparing. I love San Marcos High School! It is the best high school in Santa Barbara because 1. the teachers and staff are nice 2. they are competent and helpful 3. they love their subject and job 4. the kids are low-key 5. they balance their academic with sports and activities 5. the students are proud to be Royals 6. the atmosphere is happy 7. You learn a lot and well! 8. You are prepared for the university. I JUST LOVE IT! My son was beat up by 4 West side gang members after school. The administrators did nothing about it. Because he only knew one of the guys, they did not even try to find out who the others were. I feel like if my son had been a minority and the gang members white, it would have been a different story.The campus police said he didn't want to ruin his rapport with the one boy we did identify. I've never seen anything like this. I had to go above the school to the board and local legislature before anyone took it serious. They tried to make my son, the victim, feel bad, instead of the perpetrators. Kind of like blaming a rape victim for getting raped. His vice principal never would return my calls or emails unless I cc'd the principal. We are from Nashville, and I just had a lot higher expectations out here. In three days, my son will graduate from this school and it couldn't be sooner. Yes, some students do thrive here, but most fall through the cracks. There is no sense of community and the parents who run the school explain what it means to be a "Royal." What a joke of a school and our other child chose DP after witnessing the dysfunction of SMHS. Stay away!

column1: Absolute joke of a school. Teachers are disconnected from there students, especially in the math department. Communication is atrocious and not reliable. The administration sucks. Overall this school is terrible if you have even the slightest interest in a trade. We had to put our kids in private school. Kids run the school and administrators and teachers are afraid to discipline kids. There is nothing for kids to do in this town so kids just drink and get high. Plenty of kids come to school high. Teachers give everyone good grades. Students and teachers are racist and homophobic. If your kids go here, they will be severely bullied. If you're not white, this is NOT the place for you. It's a great place to visit, but keep on moving b/c these hills have eyes and it can get scary out here for the wrong people.

column3: If you are from out of town, don't put your kids through this mess. Administration is blind to the horrible problem with bullies. Girls and guys will make life misurable for you and your kids. The schools do not want parent involvement at all and are not about to address any problems. You feel like you're bothering them if you go into the school for anything. You might be ok if your child is a star athlete but if not, then the school has no use for your child. 80% of the teachers are coaches which is their main priority. We have moved around a lot and this is the worse school district yet. We were fooled by asking locals and reading positive reviews and I'd hate to see another family go through what we are. We have a couple years left and are exploring other options to this High School. I just graduated from this school and i have to say I loved it. No sport was more important than the other. I played softball and the coaches really cared about school before the sport. This school district is much better than the surrounding school districts. Decatur ISD parents are super involved in everything their children do. Nothing was ever done without parents being asked to participate. If you want a horrible school district, Bridgeport is just 15 minutes away! Decatur is the best school district I have Ever attended. All of the teachers care a lot about how well the students are learning and are available at all times if the students need more help. Also the SRO is hard hitting and will crack down on any bullying issue that is addressed. While attending decatur high school i can say from the classes u took though out my year i can only remember about half of my courses because they would slap a textbook on the table instead of teaching students or make us read things on our laptops Decatur High School has been a positive experience for my student. When he transferred into the district mid semester, the students and staff were welcoming, which eased the transition. Since attending Decatur High School, he has become more involved in extracurricular activities and all aspects of his education have improved. The teachers are committed to helping the students succeed and the community is highly supportive as well. My experience with DHS has always been positive. My child has loved his teachers and has had a very positive experience.

column1: Calhoun Academy is a great small town school. We have lived here for 16 years and as with any small town, I will always be considered from 'off' which doesn't bother me. My son graduated from there and my daughter is in high school. I have been pleased with both of their levels of education and their extra activities - one chose to play sports and the other did not. I think that some of the comments here are pretty harsh - you will probably find that most schools, private or public, are going to have 'in' crowds and other issues that all kids have to deal with at some time in their lives. I don't know if my children are classified as 'in crowd' by their peers, and I really don't care because that is not why they are in school. What I do know is that they have a good education from caring teachers, they love their school, and they have made friends which will last a lifetime. I was a student here from 2010-2016 and it was a great experience. But I think it got a lot better when I left though especially with technology.

column3: This school is not safe. Read in any paper for details. Some staff seems to have a blind eye. Our daughter went there a few short weeks before we had to put her in another school. Fights and disrespect are rampant. The Harrison students are bullied daily. Look somewhere else, in my opiinion. My son is a senior at LHS and has received a very good education at this High school. He has had the opportunity to take many AP classes that are not offered at other high schools . He has also been very involved in extracurricular activities. He marched in the St. Patrick's Day Parade in New York last year and represented the LHS Band proudly. He has never been bullied or felt unsafe at LHS. The teachers are involved and efficient at their jobs. As we prepare for college our family credits the staff and faculty of LHS for giving our son a well rounded education and an abundance of opportunities to grow and mature as a responsible young man. LHS has both a great academic record and an excellent sports program. The majority of students that attend here are very happy at this school and are offered a wide variety and range of both classes and sports venues to be involved with. The alumni are also very active and proud of being Dreadnaughst! Many of whom, are serving their community, state and country in very distinguished positions. I want to wish the class of 2014 a wonderful journey as they end their high school years and prepare for their adult life. Go Naughts!!! Excellent teachers at honors and AP level. Extremely helpful staff with children who are struggling. Compassionate teachers. Excellent counselors who are always looking out for their students. Please don't send your children here if you care for them constant bullying, discrimination from teachers who only care about their pay. The school is overall disgusting if I could rate any lower I would

column1: I had 2 children going to Carroll at one time. My youngest was excused from Carroll right before Christmas because of too many demerits! We were told to find him another school. My oldest refused to go back in her in her senior year. She was bullied, beat up, suspended, and recieved detention. She didn't start the fight, and the other person knew the principal and recieved NOTHING! In a world where we are trying to teach our children tolerance. Is it really important that a shirttail is sticking out? The reason they have such a high percentage of college scholarships is because if you don't conform, you get dismissed! Not the Catholic education I wanted for my kids! Since then, a new principal but the clicks keep on! Archbishop John Carroll High School is a Catholic school that welcomes children of all faiths. Our child, a non-Catholic, received an outstanding, academically challenging, faith-based education. We believe a CHS diploma is worth MANY times the cost of tuition. The fine guidance staff helped our child apply for and earn a full college scholarship. Carroll's wonderful student body is a direct reflection of involved parents, an erudite and dedicated faculty, and a visionary administration. I can't think of a better gift to give a child than a Carroll education. 2013 Graduate - Environment is not Catholic at all. Students regularly face bullying issues and nothing is done about them. Administration ignores most student issues especially personal. Some staff/teachers "pick" on students which downgrades the student a lot. Teachers love to throw demerits @ students like they gain satisfaction from it. Some even don't let you use the bathroom in an emergency or even ban you from a certain bathroom(you know who you are.) The academics are pretty good especially the science/biology/medical classes. Your fellow students are not going to grab you into their clique, they are not going to come up to you and ask to be your friend. Only reason I stayed @ Carroll was because my friends were there with me especially in times of needs. The freshmen/sophomore counselor was like a mom to me. Really helpful in keeping you in check. I could go on and on but one more thing, this school doesn't have air conditioning... so you will sweat your body out in the spring/summer which greatly affected my education in class negatively. I graduated in 2012 and I can honestly say going to Carroll is was a great decision. I went all four years and even though there was no air conditioning its still a great school. The teachers genuinely care about their students. Carroll prepared me so well for college it was crazy. In my first couple of weeks at college I had felt like I had already learned everything they were teaching. In regards to the negative reviews about Carroll, I never experienced bullying nor did I ever see anything that constituted bullying. Carroll is a great school and I highly recommend sending your child there. I have found Carroll High School to be the best choice for our son. Many know how far superior their academics are and how the Catholic faith is immersed into the student body through mass, numerous service projects, and daily life. The teachers are passionate about their commitment to their students. My son has found everyone to be friendly and supportive. I have seen Carroll work very hard at trying to make it a place where everyone has an opportunity to feel welcomed. Our experience has been that it is an extension of family and I'm very excited to have my daughter start there soon as well. It is worth every amount of investment and I am always inspired by the young men and women that achieve so many great things before they even graduate. I highly recommend parents and their children to visit the school and talk to many who attend so they can hear for themselves how great this place is. It truly elevates their minds and challenges them to accomplish great things in this world. You would be amazed. Carroll High School is a great choice for any parent wanting a faith based and academically challenging school. I have found the faculty and staff to be very committed to helping all students achieve. . My husband graduated from CHS and my first of four children has graduated. I can't imagine sending them anywhere else. My son is currently a sophomore in college and was well prepared in all his classes and I attribute that to his commitment to work hard in high school and the commitment of the faculty and staff at Carroll High School. They offer many activities for all students who want to be involved. They also offer many types of service projects that really help develop not only good students but great adults. I am currently in my 3rd year at Carroll high and I highly recommend this school. I take all AP and honors classes and I feel very confident in my education and teachers, most certain with my science teachers. The religion teachers are very tolerant of other beliefs which is wonderful since I do not believe in theology. My math teacher, Dr. Carter, was the best teacher I've ever had. She's quite intimidating but funny and very fair although extraordinarily strict. I have not witnessed any bullying. A new principal took over my freshman year and many positive changes have happened in our school since. Very caring, very involved, and very open to new policies and clubs. I would say that I am not one to stay home a Friday night and I do not quite follow rules, but I have only come across fairness in my punishment. I truly feel my teachers care about my education and I have never felt my grade has been personally affected by a teacher spitefully. My only complaint is the lack of air conditioning. I was a not a super star but the teachers all cared about me and pushed me to be the best I could be!

column3: Stratford cares about sports. Period. Football essentially comes before everything else. The last few campus improvements involved renovating the field house, installing a new track, and building a gym. Never mind that they don't have an auditorium for band and such. On a more positive note, the teachers are great. They are willing to work with students and are very understanding. The principal, Paul Uttley, truly cares about the students. Stratford High is in the Spring Branch School District. I have recently moved into the area. My daughter is a freshmen and she is loving it already. All of the staff that I have encountered are nice and helpful. The teachers are very encouraging and the school spirit is very enlightening.

column1: The truth about Andrews High School is the majority of the teachers care more about being your friend than they do about being your teacher. They try their best to get paid for doing nothing, and hardly any work ever gets done at this school besides watching movies and playing games. I transfered out my junior year, and it was amazing how far behind Andrews was. I spend my last 2 years playing catch-up. The education I recieved at Andrews was unacceptable, and thanks to AHS, the only preparation I had for college was the 2 years at another school. Andrew's High school is a wonderful School my three children loved going there. The teachers are caring and helpful and try to help the Students work at their level and try to help them succeed so they can graduate on time. There are always grumpy guesses at every school who will leave bad comments but this school is really wonderful.

column3: Its a Great school, in a great location, my kids are excited to be enrolled here. My daughter loves this school. She takes advantage of all of the wonderful opportunities the district offers and has been inspired to do her best by many teachers throughout the district. She understands that her success is due to family support FIRST and the wonderful teaching that is provided. It's time to realize that success begins with a positive partnership and effort between parents and schools. I do believe that the schools in this district are doing their part, but student and parent accountability must step up in order to improve test scores overall. I wish my education level was better. Test Scores. Our AP choices. I wish we weren’t FORCED to take standardized test, but it’s the only thing this school does to even help our future. Besides that, we are set up to fail and they don’t even realize. Even our top students can’t create a great resume just through the school. We don’t provide enough awards and honors, even clubs. They never even try to help us start any as well. It’s tiring. Although there are a few educators that actually try to help us, it starts with the students and in this school, THE STUDENTS aren’t motivated enough, but then again there’s no motivation or motivating happening in the schools community. The teachers are very friendly and have a genuine concern for my kids academic goals. Everyone involved with this school should be ashamed of themselves. Parents who say it’s great and kids are excited are lying. You are failing your kids, failing your community and failing yourselves. I understand one Starbucks location probably has a bigger operating budget but it is clear that no real teaching is occurring here. Support the teachers, work with the school and save these kids. Don’t throw their lives away!

column1: I love Dawson! I just moved here from Louisiana and it's amazing. Everybody's nice, from administration to the students. The teachers are great, and I've learned much more than I thought I would. And i forgot to add that my daughter (the biology major) who graduated from Pearland High, instead...she graduated with all honors: National Honor Society. I'm proud of every accomplishment (now also the National Biology major society) she has made. Looking forward to my future doctor :0) My daughter attends here and LOVE IT! I only had one issue with the Spanish teacher and it got resolved REAL quick. The administrative office was on top of it. This school is wonderful. No complaints!! Dawson is an awesome school you should attend i am a senior this year and the councilors are excellent. this school is a great. so many nice and helpful teachers. the APs are cool and friendly. i love going to this school. i couldn't be happier This school is absolutely amazing! I'm a freshman here and I have loved my first year. As a whole, the teachers are friendly with students but are serious about their teaching. The administrators are very supportive. My child LOVES this school – from the teachers and staff to the students to the challenging curriculum. Glenda Dawson High School (DHS) integrates compassion into its teaching standards, emphasizes the importance of values, and builds leaders through its classes and lessons. DHS allows for a lower student-to-teacher ratio than most schools, giving students more confidence when asking questions, engaging in group activities, and plenty of opportunities for one-on-one time with the teachers.The vast majority of DHS teachers are passionate about seeing their students succeed. They are so great about sharing moments of school pride and achievements. They know the importance of getting the parents involved should an issue arise and do it in a respectful and approachable manner.We LOVE DHS!

column3: I am a former student of DVHS. I have currently graduated in the summer of 2011 and I can honestly say this is one of THE best schools in PA. The teachers are some of the smartest people and they truly know what they are talking about. Yes, the kids are immature, but what school does not have some of them. If you want the best for your kids, this is the school to send them to. The school offers OUTSTANDING organizations such as FBLA (Future Business Leaders of America) which is the schools Largest organization with near 200 members. DVHS is also the best school in the State of PA for FBLA. This school is absolutely wonderful. I have very 6 different children--some are athletic, some are academic, some are artistic, and I can honestly say I cannot imagine a better school for my kids. There are art clubs, science clubs, reading clubs, fishing clubs, academic clubs, GSA, sports, and fabulous teachers. One of my kids started college with 27 credits, one with 6. I've been here for 15 years, less 4 years in NJ, and the school there was not comparable. You will find people complaining, but usually 1) they are from a more populated environment, and are not used to a rural environment or 2) it wouldn't matter where they lived, they would have an issue. I had three boys graduate from the school. It was excellent. But now with the construction of new bleachers, purchase of lands. Building of new buildings, in a county in a continued downward spiral of enrollment, the schools leaders and planners have become a laughing stock. I see a school with a focus on thing which are not priorities to advancing education but instead focusing on the American dream, to have more cool stuff. I am so glad my kids are finished. DVHS could of been more supportive, even though I excelled at math and now work for a large national investment bank and long career in finance after easily acquiring my B.S in Finance after high school, will never forget how my guidance counselor at the time -" she " advised my parents that I should be an automotive mechanic circa 1994-98. I guess I got the last laugh ... Anyway otherwise a great school and had great buddies I still talk to - just don't listen to the DV guidance counselor you will get much further in life and with your career!!! I'm glad I moved into this district. The High School and Shohola Elementary provide my children a stellar education. Great school. All 3 of my children had very good experiences at DV This is an amazing school. I completed my Freshman year with outstanding teachers who were always there. I hope to see only better and more challenging classes during my next three years

column1: Clinton School has absolutely astounded me. I have attended this school for two years now. On my very first day, I was greeted by staff, fellow students, and other parents. I enjoy the fact that everyone knows each other. I enjoy being at this school. I have never been bullied or offered drugs. This may seem like it wouldn't be a big deal to others, but I moved from a large school where you don't see the same people twice. I love Clinton High School and moving to this school was the best thing that ever happened to me. My Daughter has had many problems with bullying in this school (kindergarten thru high school). Cameras are not on all buses, so no proof for parents when lies are told. I have started documenting every incident now I case I need a lawyer soon. it was atrash place not good people they were rude mean they did not care about the students People here aren't very accepting of outsiders (Clinton in general). Superficially nice is an understatement. Hope your kids don't play sports, because they will be shunned for not being here since prek 3 on the same team that never changes. Bullying is a problem with kids and adults in this town. I also was not happy with the education in the least.

column3: My two kids had an excellent experience at EHS. They excelled at academics and were involved in sports and LOVED their cross country and running coaches. They loved the arts available at Eastside and participated in art classes and chorus during their four years. The student body was diversified, and that is one of the things my kids loved about their experience. While some teachers were mediocre, others were outstanding, and their courses were rigorous and inspiring. The English department was especially good. The student body pulled together and were generally warm to one another. Student leaders were typically of high moral character and were kind to others. Drama in the school was rare. Teachers were pretty responsive to parental concerns. The new principal is very involved with the student body, as are parents. The new school and sporting facility upgrades have been awesome. The grounds could use better landscaping and mature trees -- as the building's aesthetics do not evoke warmth on approach. My kids' physical education experience was abysmal. There is such an opportunity to get kids active and teach nutrition and healthy living, but in their words, "It was just a joke." I attended Eastside for one year and ended up transferring to Wade Hampton. EHS is a highly acclaimed academic program, and the atmosphere is fantastic, but there's a strong clique element in the student body. While the facilities are warm and bright, and school spirit is incredibly high, the student body is rather standoffish, especially to newcomers. Wade Hampton, while having a more institutional facility, was a much more inviting school. All 3 of my kids attended Eastside, we are lucky enough to be zoned there. Teachers were awesome, their athletic experiences were great and the atmosphere was warm and inviting. School is what you make of it and Eastside provides a lot opportunities to get involved in several different area of interest. My kids went confidently in to college after graduating. No wonder there is a wait list to get into Eastside My child is finishing the first year at EHS and all I can say is WOW. After having a "so so" middle school experience at the 'best" middle school in the county, I have been blown away with EHS. My child has soared! Moving into the honors classes for the first time my child has become extremely confident in her abilities. She has earned great grades but even more importantly, respects all of her teachers. Even my teenager can see how much her teachers want her to succeed. Bravo EHS- you have made my year by making my child's year! I have three children who have attended Eastside. Their experience has been fantastic. Their teachers and coaches have truly invested in their success and encouraged them throughout their time there. My child loves it so I'm happy My son loves Eastside. We moved back to Greenville from TN. We visited several of the area high schools and he picked Eastside to be his top choice. It was the friendliness of the students and comfortable atmosphere that sold him the most. But the size was just right too. great school love the teachers and students and great principal. I walked in too the school on my second day just to get dress coded and was told i couldn’t continue with my day until my mom brought me another pair of jeans, my mom was at work. I’m tired of all this about girls getting dress coded cause boys can’t see females legs.

I have found the school to be a wonderful high school for the area- teachers are engaging, the students are interested in what they are studying, and are able to carry on well thought-out discussions about the material during class time. column3: We moved to Abilene last school year and purposely bought a home in the Wylie school district so our son could go to high school there. He was going to be a freshman, and anyone's first year of high school can be difficult. Wylie High School made it even worse. The students were not welcoming at all, as they have all grown up together. There is no diversity amongst the student body, and basically every student there was the same. I found the Wylie community as a whole to be fairly cliquish and unwelcoming to someone who did not fit their type. This school year, we moved our son to Cooper High School in Abilene ISD for his sophomore year, and we couldn't be more happier that we did so. He is loving it. The student body is much more welcoming and diverse as a whole. He has made many new friends and really enjoys his classes as well. I wish we would've settled in Abilene ISD originally. If you are moving to Abilene, send your kids to Abilene ISD. Wylie is a great school, it is very friendly and has a welcoming community. Good athletics programs, with friendly and helpful teachers. My largest issue is that it's kinda small and I cannot find others with same interests and barely anyone with the same ethnicity, yeah it may sound like a politically biased "issue" but really what I'm trying to say is that I can't really fit my personal puzzle into groups (since it's niche) because of it's size (this should be fixed in the future since this is a fast growing development by the way), other than that; I moved here for educational opportunity and because family members live close by, the last time I have ever touched Abilene was in winter 2011 in order to visit family members which means that I never grew up/got to know anyone prior at all. Despite differences in personality and opinion, I feel very welcomed and a lot more comfortable than my last school. They have helped me catch up into this new and amazing educational system after leaving a corrupt and failed education system; yeah it's taking months, but I do really feel like I am really learning! The homework policy is very reasonable since it reviews what you need to understand (as it fits all learning types) and the people are very helpful in helping you through your troubles of understanding the material. Overall, the school is amazing but I nicked off one star since it's too adapted into people who already live here (don't worry, they don't bully "outsiders" at all) and because it's socially boring for a niche person (like myself) which pushes you to go to the internet to talk to people which isn't good in the 2010s especially with less niches online (the last resort). If you want amazing education and friendly people, then come here, it was worth the stresses of moving!

column1: No matter what a student's passion/interests, St. Henry District High School has a place for him or her. Their slogan of "Come as Many, Leave as One" is more than a catch phrase--it's something you feel in the classrooms and halls of SHDHS...a true Christianly acceptance of EVERY student. Whether they're a Governor Scholar or academically challenged, an athlete or an artist, SHDHS offers an abundance of opportunities in each of their five pillars (Faith, Scholarship, Leadership, Arts, and Athletics). Moved our children from the county school to St. Henry this year. This children have adjusted well and love their new school. We see our children growing leaps and bounds in their education. we love the family involvement and pride within the school environment. We know we are giving our children a wonderful education and a great jump into their future learning experiences. Unbelievable culture, very talented teachers and staff, rigorous academics, Art and rising in sports. A top-notch school and community in the area and state.

Plus, it's just a family-oriented place to live, and a great place to raise kids. so many great teachers middle school through high school. Strong in core subjects. Frustration of late with all the testing that the state now requires with the new guidelines. Caring, hardworking teachers and great students. I recently read in Buffalo paper that my high school wants to change the name of redskins. I am totally shocked that the school is considering doing so. I am 1961 grad. who will be sadden by this action. Society has become over the years way to sensitive that being said if the action is taken I would like to suggest that a couple of names be considered 1. King Fisher after tower lake Otsego 2. But if you talk to most of the sports players and even most of the people in the town, especially the ones that went there, they are not happy about the name change. my son we classified learning disabled. The principal literally said to me that there were more deserving kids to be enrolled in the area BOCES program. My only choices at the time were to keep him in high school to repeat ninth grade English a third time, with a teacher who called him stupid in front of the class, or have him get his GED. He had his GED in six months. My younger child doesn't attend Cooperstown Central School. Has provided a solid education for our children. Has been especially good at math and English. Overall, though, would say that athletics are valued more than academics.

column1: new student attending school in 2013 2014 year. looking forward to what the school has to offer. Hoping some of the reviews are incorrect. Graduated from this school in 2002. Brown for everything and all my favorites teachers. I missed you a lot .

Parking passes cost $75 at Badger High they cost $10. nd guess what the dumb school spent $500,000 on a football feild and they have to replace it in a couple years which cost $400,000. They don't have that kinda money. they r constantly fundraising, and wen i go to badger they don't do any fundraising, only for deca meets and fundraising for the community. im embarresed to be a studnt My school is exceptional. The opportunities they present for my kids are outstanding. We have moved around a lot and when we moved to this area, we picked Wilmot over others; we could not be happier with the choice. Other schools in the area are good, but Wilmot is GREAT! My kids and I love it. Worst education ever. Poor communication. Go to this school, get a high school diploma, with no learning invonved. They are too busy to notice the students are failing, and there should be more drug searches...pay attention to the students. Good students do well, poor students, the ones who need extra help, will be pushed under the rug, (sent to APEX or Truval), and forgotten. The Principals will be secretly hopeing the poor students quit school....Don't want to ruin the "top school" rating! Academic Decathlon team best in Wisconsin in 2014 and 2nd in the nation. Being national Runner-up in the Academic Decathlon competition is a very impressive feat. Wilmot beat every school in Wisconsin (regardless of size) then went on to take 2nd in the nation in the "medium-sized school" division. This school is definitely on the rise and has an ever-growing AP program. I am also impressed by Project Lead the Way, a national pre-engineering program which Wilmot offers classes through. Not only does Wilmot offer pre-engineering classes but they also have a Biomedical Sciences curriculum through Project Lead the Way. I was a student at Wilmot for 4 years. I loved that school. I learned so much from all of my teachers. There wasn't any violence or problems. There was a fight every once in awhile, but that was it. We took pride in our school. I want my son to go to this school when he gets older. When I graduated I had colleges that wanted to give me academic scholarships. I had a blast in this school! My son has Asperger's and might experience "bullying" in other schools, but Wilmot High School has been a very accepting climate. You expect teachers to be able to work with special needs children, but the fellow students have been very good as well.
