column3: West Bend West High School was a very good example of a very poor high school. My two daughters attended and received mediocre grades at best. We recently moved to Brookfield, WI, and now they attend Brookfield East High School. The difference in the teachers were night and day. The teachers at West Bend West High, checked out along time ago. The enthusiasm and positive attitude in the teachers of Brookfield East was a night to day difference. In my daughters' first year at Brookfield East, my daughters were A and B students. My only regret is that my sons didn't have the same great opportunity of attending Brookfield East High School. I do not recommend sending your child to West Bend West High School if you want them to be successful in their academic education. West Bend West is a great high school with numerous Honors and AP classes available. My daughters will be more than prepared for college. Communication between school and parents is excellent. My daughters are involved in band, athletics, debate, and other clubs not offered at some other area schools. Terrible administration, horrible communication and operates as more of a dictatorship than a cohesive learning environment

column1: While it may seem as though this school has much to offer, and will prepare your child for the college and subsequently, the real world, all of the claims to fame are simply just that. As a student now about to graduate college, I can say the only positive attribute of HTA for college was the aid in the application process. After 3 years in college, I have struggled with Math, Science as well as Physics. The classes were anything but challenging, and the more your parents donated, the better you were treated. The community was not "family-oriented" or morally sound, as they claim to be, as most parents and kids seem to think they are better than others. I had many friends in a rival private school, as well as a few public schools, and they have had much more success in college than my fellow classmates from HTA. For these reasons and many more, HT, if anything, prepared me for the opposite of the real world and college alike. My recommendation, save over 50,000 for for years of high school and pay for a real education in college. Sincerely, Past student. I have two sons that graduated from Holy Trinity and I appreciate everything that was done for my children. I can hardly believe how lucky we were to have been part of the HT family. I wish that all students could receive the counseling, encouragement and education that HT students have. There is a marked difference between what HT does and what the typical school does. My sons received a foundation beyond academics... they were encouraged to develop spiritually, morally, athletically, creatively. They weren't perfect and they made mistakes during and after but through it all, they had the basic foundation to draw from and see them through the bumps. The college counseling was phenomenal. I haven't spoken to anyone who has had anything like it elsewhere. People are amazed when I tell them how my kids' high school led them through the college process starting from the 9th grade, ensuring that they got Bright Futures and other scholarships. One son will be finishing up with a masters in engineering this year with a job! My other son has graduated from college and is now attending medical school. Mr. Chiarella had an extremely positive impact on both of my sons. Our child attended the lower school. She has been bullied, asked to sit at a lunch table with kids of her own ethnicity (by other kids) and ridiculed by other children. When we discussed this with other parents they had seen the same thing for multiple years with their kids. The staff tepidly acknowledged the issue and did nothing to remedy the situation. We have always sent our child to private schools and this is by far the worst experience we've had. The impression we get from the staff is that we are not customers, we are simply "lucky to be here". Academics at this school are fair at best but not worth the money being spent. The "care factor" from the staff is frustrating for parents who truly care about their child's education. The response to concerns is even more frustrating. You are not a customer her... your child is not the primary concern of the staff... don't be foolded by the hype. I have two children that have attendend Holy Trinity since Early Childhood. My older child attends the Upper School, and I feel it was a seamless transition. He was well prepared, both academically and socially. My other child currently attends the Lower School, and loves the enrichment opportunities (music, art, PE, Chinese, STEM, computer lab and library). The teachers have open-communication with the parents and the character education program is fabulous. I have been consistently impressed by the quality of teachesr and the academics offered at both the Upper and Lower school. We are a Holy Trinity family with our son currently in the Lower School. He started 8 years ago when he was three and as parents we feel it was the best decision we did for him. The school has a rigorous curriculum with a low student to faculty ratio, very successful programs of extra-curricular activities such as chess, boy/girl-scouts and many athletic activities. Most importantly though, Holy Trinity share the vision of an academic community based on the love of God, self respect & respect for each other. The kids learn to give back to their community at a very young age through the very special Character Education program and that is another quality that sets the school apart from any other school in Brevard. Unmistakably Holy Trinity is the premier private school in Brevard. Good school but favoritism of staff kids is legendary...down to a "others need not apply" rule regarding any school production/activity. Parents do complain but with futile results. I do believe they keep many students (and their parents) enrolled simply due to the economy. They are rather ineffective in dealing with socially troubled kids (once again, and their parents) in that you will see these parents at the school "shadowing" their children as often as they can. Daily lunch with Mommy and Daddy continues even into the 6th grade! I suppose I have been rather harsh in my comments but these items have caused quite an uproar among many parents. We still think it's the best school in the county, but these concerns are very troubling for many of us! Holy Trinity is an amazing school. I have two children at the Lower School. They both started in preschool. The school offers so many opportunities for educational, social, and emotional growth. I love the character education program at the school. It teaches them how to be the best they can be. It also offers many extra activities, sports, and clubs before and after school. Just recently my child began learning "Scratch". It is a computer coding program. She is also learning how to make movies on the iPad. It is amazing what they come home and teach me. My children love going to school and are always so excited to share their day when they come home. I have found all the teachers to be loving, caring, and open with communication. I love being a part of the Holy Trinity family. I went to Holy Trinity from pre-kindergarten until 9th grade when I transferred to Viera. I was also at Suntree Elementary for a short while. I can say with complete honesty that the quality of education is no different from any public school. The only difference (aside from thousands of dollars in tuition) is that Holy Trinity makes you wear a uniform and has 15 minutes of chapel each day. Some of the teachers were good but the faculty was just awful when it comes to playing favorites and singling kids out. I am not up to date on the lawfulness of recruiting athletes, but because Holy Trinity has a waiting list for prospective students (or at least they did when I went there), they tend to accept more African Americans. Going from 6th to 7th grade, my class went from having no black students to having upwards of 20, almost all of whom were on sports teams. Do your child a favor and don't waste your money. There are schools in the area with the same (if not better) quality of education that won't cost you tens of thousands of dollars in tuition. Our children have attended HT's lower school for 4 years, and we are thrilled by the growth we've seen in them during this time. The academics are advanced with a rich curriculum including Singapore math, hands on science, dynamic music and art programs, Chinese, Library, computer sciences including programming, STEM lab, PE everyday and more. All of this is offered in a Christian environment where character education is a priority. The teaching staff is warm, bright, dynamic, and simply wonderful! We have found both the teacher and administration to be caring, open, and accessible. In addition, HT has an impressive offering of extracurricular activities that has something for everyone. Our children have participated in sports that they otherwise would not have given a chance. As a result, they have developed skills, confidence, and friendships along the way. We believe that HT truly teaches the whole child: mind, body, and soul. Brevard County has some of the best schools in the state, and we toured several of them in area. The decision to send our children to HT was based on the well-rounded approach to education described above. This is absolutely the right school for us. Love this school. Was an easy transition from public grade school to upper school. We were so thrilled with the teachers and communication. Is an expensive school, but worth the comfort of communication on a daily basis. And a happy middle school child. Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy in Melbourne, FL is a wonderful school (ps-12th grade). They are known for their challenging academics, caring teachers, wide variety of extracurricular activities, and small class sizes. My daughter is in Kindergarten and has attended since preschool. It's a big investment financially but it is well worth it for our family. I honestly believe my daughter would not have the same opportunities or be treated with as much sincere love and care elsewhere. She loves going to school every day! Great school - outstanding academics with strong focus on STEM, Arts and Music. Athletic program provides opportunities for all kids to get involved and many go off to play sports in college. This school is not worth the tuition they charge. Some of their teachers are not caring and their staff are money bigots.Education is below public school standards. I would not recommend this school to my friends. Many of us are what we at HTA consider "lifers", and we are so saddened to watch the slow demise of such a great establishment. The new leadership has failed our community, in part, due to not understanding that this place is our home. We pray that this dark era will pass soon. My daughter is in junior high at the Upper School and started out in Early Childhood at the Lower School. She has flourished with all of the opportunities given to her. Her teachers are willing to put in extra time if she needs extra help. She has played two sports and been in photography club and gotten to know her teachers and coaches outside of the regular day. She also enjoys volunteering at summer camp with our younger students. This is her home away from home! Holy Trinity has in the past been an excellent school for academics and sports, providing a safe and positive learning environment. Sadly, the new administration has acted in manipulative and underhanded ways, compromising the core values on which this school was founded. Their actions are having severe negative effects on students, staff and parents. As expensive as this school is, you will not be getting your moneys worth by placing your child here. Holy Trinity is sadly a rapidly deteriorating institution What once was a top academic , Christian academy , the recent events have divided the school . Poor leadership , newly hired with no previous headmaster experience has left the school floundering . Precious resources are being funneled to a public relation firm to combat parent dislikes . This school refuses to listen to it's customers and will only continue to raise tuition and weaken their academics until the leadership wakes up and deals with the truths. Beware the slick advertising and ask around . Find parents who are enduring this demise ! HTEA is a wonderful academic establishment. The teachers are caring, the students are kind and respectful and the administration is always available for the parents. The firing of a beloved coach has caused a rift between some of the parents and the administration. Honestly, if your student isn't a part of that particular sport, his not being there doesn't effect how one feels about the school. (side note: there was no explanation for the firing, many rumors have spread, but it was a decision made by a unanimous vote by the Board of Directors, not the administration, which tells you something). Many AP courses are offered and the college counseling office is top notch. No school is perfect, but HTEA is a wonderful, academically challenging and caring environment for students. I'm amazed that a positive review gets one like and a negative review gets 7 or 11! And the start rating is a high four, (should be a 5). I'm a super happy parent and am totally behind the current administration and teaching staff. I trust them to hire the best teachers and if they let someone go, I have absolutely no doubt that the decision wasn't taken lightly, and is in the best interests of the students. The academic standards are top notch, as are the athletics, arts, science and technology. It's a true college preparatory education. Reading any review, you will believe what you want to believe; and if a less than stellar review leads you to choose a different school for your student, believe me, the loss will be yours. Beware the internet and as another reviewer suggests, tour the school, look at the results, speak to students and above all, trust your gut. Mine said this was a solid pick and I couldn't be more impressed. We have been a part of this school since my children were in preschool. We are so proud of the education they have received to date. They have a strong academic foundation, but are also involved in clubs and sports. My children are happy and safe at school. We have been blessed to be able to give them the gift of a fabulous education! Students get the whole picture at Holy Trinity -- great academics and preparation for college, but also, lots of options for sports, clubs, leadership and service. Kids can dive into science, math and tech while still participating in sports and the arts. HT is preparing kids to be well-rounded citizens of the world! We are a new family at the Lower School this year. My child has been challenged academically and is loving it. He also loves being able to play after school sports and join different clubs. We are so glad we made the choice to enroll him at Holy Trinity this year. Holy Trinity is mediocre when compared to the public schools beach side and in Viera. The academics are soft, students are not challenged. The extra enrichments are average with the exception of Art and PE. If your child is average or above average then Holy Trinity is not for you. Save your money. My daughter just graduated from this hidden gem in Melbourne, FL. Having attended Boston private schools in my own life, my bar is high for excellence in academics. HTEA has that with outstanding teachers. What it also has is a student centered, supportive environment that I am grateful for. My daughter flourished there taking AP classes, competing in state choral competitions and performing at Disney, playing (undefeated) volleyball freshman year, attending Model UN at UF, and so much more. Anything your child may be interested in is here at HT among caring teachers and with lived spiritual core values. My daughter is off to a "little ivy" small liberal arts college in the Northeast. Her future is bright and I couldn't be more grateful to Holy Trinity. Basically an average public school with chapel tacked on so they can pretend to be a Christian school. Mediocre teachers, poor / transient administration. There are much better schools in Brevard - public and private. You owe it to your kids to keep looking. I have an 11amd 5 grader. Been at the school since the older one was in kindergarten. Excellent experience. Loving teachers. Challenging curriculum. Lower school has so much to offer with hands on science experiments, dedicated STEAM class, dedicated coding class, amazing art and music every week and PE every day. Homework has been the perfect amount to verify the kid understands to concepts, but isn't busy work. Upper school has wonderful teachers and lots of AP classes. We met with our college advisor this summer and I am so impressed with their knowledge and drive to find the perfect college for our daughter. Sending our children to school at HTEA is the best parenting decision that we have ever made. We have an 11th grader and a 7th grader. Both children started when they were 3 years old. We have a girl and a boy. Our children have very different personalities. The educational development, character development, and physical development at Holy Trinity is exceptional!!! The school is a community. We are so thrilled that our 17 year old made it off of the wait list and into the classroom all of those years ago! My husband and I were split about Holy Trinity. He wanted (understatement - I have never seen him so upset) to send her to a good school of choice public school for 7th grade (Edgewood); I didn't. She was waitlisted at Edgewood, so she went to Holy Trinity with the thought that she would reapply to Edgewood. That was two years ago, and we have liked it so much we stayed. Have had no problems with other students, teachers or administration, and the academics are top notch. If you are not doing well in a particular subject, they will provide you with help/extra tutoring until you are doing well. The teachers seem genuinely interested in the students learning! Lots of opportunities to join clubs or sports. Our daughter transferred there this past year. She was doing fine at her old school, but needed help with math and was off the charts in english. So we decided to give HTEA a try. It was a great year. Her seventh grade math teacher has made her confident in math and she was also able to take accelerated english and sciences class. She is now so eager to learn and earned the straight As thru the entire year. She also got a chance to play softball on the varsity high school team and perform in two performances this year. She is not a genius. She works hard, but she knows her amazing teachers at HTEA are supportive. She knows they truly care about her. As a parent I am so excited to see her passion for learning. My husband was worried about the transition, especially in middle school. But Our daughter is happy, has made friends and is more confident about trying new things. HTEA was the Best decision we made for her. At Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy, students benefit from the continuity of an academically challenging, college preparatory curriculum that spans preschool through 12th grade. Founded and sustained in the Episcopal tradition, the school’s environment reflects the joy and peace of Christian values, with an emphasis on educating the whole child – mind, body and spirit. Students who "Start Here" build a strong foundation of skills and are prepared to "Go Anywhere" – in college, career and life. I loved ht until I got to the upper school. Academics are ok but I felt more challenged at the lower school than now. Too many intolerant classmates and admin / teachers who look the other way. There is a big problem with drugs and alcohol at ht. At prom and homecoming most students can't wait to leave the dance so they can hit the after parties. I'll be ready for college but most of my classmates don't seem ready. My two started in preschool and now my oldest is going to college next year. We know her years at Holy Trinity have prepared her for whatever major she wants. Great school! My son has been a student of HTEA since Kindergarten and is now in 9th Grade. We have had nothing but a wonderful experience in all aspects of his education & growing experience. I cannot imagine teaching anywhere else. I have the respect, kindness and support of administration, parents and students. I love being part of the HT family! Hate it. 6 more months. I can do it. Our daughter has attended multiple schools, both public and private, in different parts of the country. By far, our experience at Holy Trinity has been the best. Due to the small environment, students receive personalized attention both academically and in extra curricular activities. The teachers make themselves available to help students at all times. As a parent, when entering the campus, you feel like part of a family and community. Initially, we met other parents who were so welcoming, helpful, and shared similar values. We feel confident that our daughter will be ready for college and will have a wonderful high school experience. Our family would highly recommend Holy Trinity!! Holy Trinity educates the whole child: mind, body, and spirit. My children start the day in chapel and end the day playing HT sports. They receive a rigorous education from caring and loving teachers. They all go out of their way to make them feel safe, loved, and valued. I can't say enough positive positive things about the faculty, staff, and administration. When you walk on campus, you become family I am proud to be a part of the HT family. Our first year at Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy is going GREAT, we can’t imagine any better learning environment for our daughter. The curriculum is excellent and taught by professional Teachers who truly care about our daughter’s success. Everyone is so kind and easy to be with, all the students are forward looking with bright futures. Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy is truly an extension of my family.The teachers go above and beyond to make sure each student has an understanding of what is being taught and will even take the time to explain the subject if there is a student who isn't understanding fully. Each teacher has the passion and love to teach, they want to teach and they want to be there to make sure each student excels in their dreams and goals.The students and my daughters'' classmates are respectful and kind. Each one knows how they want to be treated and treat each classmate that way. In the event that there is an issue it gets worked out with communication and teamwork to compromise. The academics is spot on. My daughters are challenged enough where they ask questions but will get the answer after talking it out with us, teachers or even classmates. I truly love the history lessons and how one teacher will make learning like scene from a movie. He will assign each student a part in the history lesson and each student is encouraged to act the part. It makes learning a lot more fun and entertaining. Sports at each campus is fun and there is a lot to experience. My youngest daughter is not very athletic but she was able to explore different sports to see if it was something that would interest her. My oldest daughter is involved in multiple sports at the upper campus and the coaching and skills that she has developed is going to be with her into her professional life weather it be in sports or not. HTEA is a school I do not worry about my girls. When they go to school I know they are being treated fairly, learning and having a great time doing it. HTEA is my family and will be my family for years to come and even after both my girls graduate. Having 2 children attending Holy Trinity Academy, one currently in the upper school and one in the lower school, my family has been given the great opportunity to evaluate all aspects of this school. From the school's response to the Covid-19 health crisis, to the physical safety of the student, and to the education of the student’s mind, body and spirit, we have nothing but high praise. In response to the Covid-19 health crisis, Holy Trinity developed a Safety and Health Guidelines to minimize the potential risk to the children. These safety measures included a Covid tracking app for temperature recording; mask-wearing protocol, hand sanitizers throughout; high touch areas sanitized throughout the day, new webcams and microphones for the remote learners making them a part of the actual classroom, as well as many other precautions.Both the upper and lower school also offer excellent physical security, from on-site deputies to onsite nursing care, it is evident that Holy Trinity truly values the safety of each student.The curriculum at Holy Trinity offers each student strong college prep academics, many AP classes, tons of electives, a wide variety of athletic offerings with well-coached sports teams, and their chapel/character education program exemplifies how the faculty and administration cares for the whole child. Holy Trinity also offers many leadership opportunities for students. The school is small enough for students and faculty to all know one another, building lifelong friendships, and small enough to allow students to focus on the challenging curriculum that private schools are known for. This school maintains high standards and expectations which will help them to easily transition into college.Teachers at Holy Trinity engage and teach with passion and love for their subjects. The Administration and College Counseling office advisors are very helpful to the student and to the student’s family. Holy Trinity is an all-around great community that welcomes students and their families.Students attending Holy Trinity grow to appreciate their value to themselves, their community and their future. Holy Trinity has this slogan, "start here go anywhere", and they live up to that expectation completely. Our son and daughter are enrolled in the Lower School and we absolutely love this school! The teachers are caring and engaging and our kids love going to school. We recently moved from out of state and my biggest concern was my kids being able to adjust to a new school, and now, after a year and half here, my kids would not want to leave Holy Trinity. We love that the class sizes are small and the teacher/parent communication is great. Holy Trinity has been a great fit and the right academic choice for both our sons. We wanted a "bubble" that was not too small, not too big, challenging, inspiring while loving and kind ... My husband and I both grew up in the midwest. My early childhood education was within a catholic private school while my husband was in the public school system. The christian private school environment, the well rounded education including a "mind, body, spirit" comprehensive approach and the size of the student body checked all our boxes when we were looking for the perfect academic home to enroll our kids. We liked the separate campuses of a lower school (up to 6th gr) and an upper school (Jr and Sr high) and we appreciated seeing how long several teachers and faculty had been at HT as well as a handful of alumni students who returned to their alma mater to work and send their kids to HT. This had to be a happy home right? And many years later, we can say YES - HT has and continues to be a happy home for our family.Our boys began at the lower school in Kindergarten and are now at the upper school in 9th and 11th grade. When our boys were old enough to discuss their opinion about where to go to school, they always said yes to re-enrolling at HT. Which reassures us that our decision was the correct one.This past 2020 year, the pivot to remote learning has continued to meet the academic needs of our boys. They have adjusted well with the virtual platform and they have remained connected to their friends in creative and traditional ways. Both have been and continue to be very active in school activities, especially school sports. I can name several teachers and coaches that have made (and continue to make) a tremendous impact in their lives.Choosing a school took many hours of discernment - and I also found that the admissions team at HT spent the same if not more number of hours making sure the school was the right fit for each of our boys. Its obviously not one size fits all - and requires both sides to look at what is best for the child. However, in our case - HT was the right home at Kindergarten and continues to be the right home today (over 12 years later). I love this school. Our daughters were both “lifers,” and the school helped shape them into the amazing young women they are today. Mind, body, spirit is a mantra that the community lives into every day. The school is not for everyone. Students, faculty and staff need to want to be a part of a community that promotes hard work and living into potential. It’s a very safe and comfortable place for those who want to be a part of something special. A focus on the whole child is what you will find at Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy. HT helps each child build their academics, character, community service, leadership, moral compass, athletics, and prepares each child for college and for life! The teachers and staff achieve this through instruction, compassion, hands on learning, daily chapel, empathy and love. Sending our children to HT was one of the best decisions for our children we ever made! We chose not only to send them to school, but to put them into an environment that would help us create the good people we wanted our children to become. I can't say enough awesome things about Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy.. My daughter is thriving in 7th grade, the past 4 years have been wonderful. The curriculum is challenging, the teachers are proactive and helpful. The communication from the teachers and staff is amazing. We always know what is going on, in each class, in the grade level and campus wide. The classes are small, there is before and after school help, the resources and technology are on point! The teachers have done a tremendous job in this difficult time, pivoting between in class students and online students. There are so many opportunities for after school enrichment, the arts, sports, clubs and other activities. If you have ever wondered about HT, I highly recommend scheduling a tour. Enrolling at HT was the best decision we have ever made. Go Tigers! All three of our children attended and thrived at Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy. Our older son has an MBA, is happily married with their first child and wants to give the same HTEA experience and sense of community to his son. Our twins are in their final college semester. Our son has accepted an IT manager position, and our daughter is getting ready to start medical school this summer. Here’s an excerpt from her medical school journey blog, “Having gone to a small private school my entire life, I loved the more individualized attention and ability to form close professional relationships with faculty and staff.” Holy Trinity has been such a blessing to our family. Our children have loved attending school at the lower school, and are both looking forward to attending school at the upper school. The teachers, administration, guidance, and all of the staff encourage and foster a loving community for both the children and their families. Choosing Holy Trinity Episcopal Academy for Junior High for my son was one of the best decisions my husband and I have made. He has been challenged and engaged academically all year long and has met new friends. I can’t sing enough praise for the teachers and advisors’ responsiveness when we have questions or have needed help. We especially LOVE Mr. Wilson, he has been so encouraging to my son and helpful to our family. Holy Trinity is great place for kids to grown and find themselves. My son is involved in the Robotics program and has really blossomed with the encouragement of working alongside High School and other Junior High students. My son attended another private school in the area for Elementary and we never felt that he was truly challenged to his full potential. This year he has had the opportunity to take High School level math and all Advanced classes and has done well! Holy Trinity has helped enhanced his confidence and knowledge base. We are a military family who moved to Patrick SFB in December 2020. Our son enrolled mid-school-year which wasn't easy for him, but he was warmly welcomed by HT. He received a student ambassador who made sure he knew where all of his classes were located and sat with him at lunch. He's just completed his second school year at HT and has bonded with friends and staff. I cannot say enough about Dr. Cobb, Alison Bell, Emily Totre, Marc Bailey, and all of the teachers at HT who are responsive to both students and parents. There are opportunities for students to volunteer and as a parent, I have enjoyed volunteering as well as substitute teaching at the lower school down in Melbourne. I tell other inbound military families to consider enrolling their school-aged children at HT. It's free to take a tour of the campuses and see what we are all raving about! Go Tigers!! Beware of the recent sharp left turn in the curriculum with integration of Critical Race Theory in the curriculum. School chooses coursework that teaches students that riots and demonstrations against police are acceptable. This is not a true Christian school when intoxicated students are accepted to attend school functions and teachers speak in class about the back seat of a car can be used for “making out”. Multiple families were not allowed reenrollment after voicing curriculum and faculty concerns. School admits students with known juvenile criminal records if the student is a strong athlete. Safety for the female students is a concern. Save yourself $20K and go to a public school or research other private schools. Holy Trinity is not so holy. This school's main interest is economic. My experience was short but unpleasant and costly. Read carefully the contract and all documents they provide before signing and enrolling your child. Contract is full of errors and omissions that will only affect you. They talk about teaching Christian values to the children but when it comes to money, that is all forgotten. They answer by threatening with their legal team and will stop at nothing for money; money they have not earned and do not deserve. They talk about respect for one's neighbors in their core values, however they don't care to listen to you, won't answer your questions, won't admit or fix their errors, won't consider your situation or care about how your family is affected. A school that lacks empathy and respect for others, that turns a blind eye to the errors in the system, that disregards parents' voices, and were communication only exists if it benefits them, will never be a good option for your child.

column3: Business Careers is the best place in the world. I'm a freshmen and i love it! Can't wait 'till my feild trip. ;D Business careers is an outstanding school academic and social wise. Business careers offers outstanding programs that you get to choose from, they push you to the highest caliber so you can succeed. The teachers are amazing especially. Overall, i would and i do recommend this school to my friends, because this schools is outstanding. This school, while there is great programs in this school, this school in my opinion did not live up to my standards. The admin seem to be as if they care for themselves. for example, for two months the AC was down in two of my classrooms in 2016 right after summer, it is still pretty hot. The admin got multiple complaints even from parents, it wasn't until i got fed up with it for another month when i called central office. Magically the AC was fixed nearly immediately. Another thing is that they WAY overcharge for a laptop repair. I would almost be half tempted to fix the laptop myself if even knew a thing about repairing them. Sure there is a couple of good things about the school, mainly saying that you graduated from a magnet school, however i would have much rather gone to my home school O'Connor any day. This school is not following normal procedures for evaluating and providing services for students who need special education. I think it's because the students are majority Hispanic. I'm considering filing a complaint with the US Dept of Education Office of Civil Rights or with the Texas Education. They don't follow normal docomentation procedures. They are also ineffective at identifying and assisting students who are especially vulnerable to bullying. They rely on suspensions instead of problem-solving with some of the core issues causing absences or misbehavior. Academic ratings at this school would improve if they addressed these issues. Teachers here need more resources. My brother graduated from here with a 3.3 gpa. That actually put him in top 10% of his class. He can barely read, he certainly doesn't comprehend what he reads, his math skills are minimal, his knowledge of history & science are comical. He was in honors math & science!! I feel so badly for him, I don't even know how to tell him to not tell prospective employers about his rank, as I'm afraid they'll expect things of him that he'll be unable to perform. I'm thankful I graduated before we moved to Texas. How could any high school graduate someone with a 5th grade reading level, at the top of their class? How can the teachers even feel good about themselves, sending people out into the world with diplomas, yet they can't even spell it! What a disservice they did to my brother. I realize parents are also responsible, but I'm not his parent. Someone should have stepped in. Perhaps the state will. I wonder about the remaining 90% that had lower averages! That thought is actually scary... great high school my child loves it here good teachers and faculty great teachers they also speak spanish which was helpful to me they have a good aproach to bullying and overall a great school would recommend

column1: BHS is great! I'm only a freshman there, but it is wonderful. The lunches have definently improved, immensely. The teachers are absolutley the best. They all connect with their students, and go out of their way to give every student an equal oppurtunity to succeed. The student body is very diverse, but there isn't much seperations between them. 90% of the students get along well. Overall, I wouldn't want to go to any other High School! I visited Berrien HIgh School this past summer with my son. My son was having a job interview for a football position at Berrien High School. I rode with him from Atlanta just for the ride. I used the time to drive around the community and to visit a real estate office in case my son got the job. I was impressed with the community and the folks I met at the school. We live in the Atlanta area and the prospect of someday having my son at Berrien High School was very exciting for my entire family. I hope everyone in the school community has a very exciting and successful year. C. Charles Duplantis

column1: Byron schools are awful!! There are a few really good teachers, but that isn't enough to make me send my kids there. Principle leadership is really bad from the elementary to the high school. Teachers stick together and gang up on the kids. The special ed program is a joke!! out of the 3 case managers available only one does their job, good luck getting her! After 4 years of elementary I pulled my child out to home school and then pulled my high schooler out too. This school needs help. I have had 3 children attend Byron Schools from K-12 and I HATE the way the school pushes the children through even though it is clear the the child is years behind academically. When my daughter left that school she still used her fingers to multiply, she was lost when it came to all subjects. I tried to beg the teachers to stop pushing her through but their response was "she'll probably catch up soon." There is very little communication from the school as to upcoming events, progress issues, or social issues. As a parent I was not allowed to volunteer anywhere in the school once my child was in the middle school. There are not a lot of classes offered due to budget cuts, and each year it seems to get worse. Putting my children in this school district was a HUGE mistake, two of my 3 children have graduated as lost souls. I wish I knew then to look at school ratings and reviews like you are :( I agree with most of these post. The school board don't realize how smallwe are & they want tons of money for improvements to buildings. What about improvements to the teachers. The teachers dress like high school tramps yet condem our students for the same dress. They think they need to be the kids friend instead of a roll model & a teacher. If you are not into sports forget it this school has nothing for you. this school is amazing this school is so small i didnt know it was even there till i moved. the teachers are great and there is nothing wrong with it It is very true that Byron schools are small and that the class choices are poor and the classrooms are way to crowded. However the community tried to make changes that would not have increase the common home owners taxes. Personally i enjoy the school and happy i am a student. the teachers are great most of them want you to learn and take time to teach you. A vast majority of the teachers stay after to further assist students. And on top of that they are very one on one with students and consistently ask on ways to improve there teaching to benefit the students. just look at the test scores...no other review needed....the fact that we are only 21% and have declined in the last few years says it ALL! This school district is continually declining. The Superintendent needs to be replaced as soon as possible! Most of the High school teachers need to be fired!!!!! It is a very poor excuse for an educational institution!!! WHAT A JOKE!!!!! They don't pay their bills, but yet want the tax payers to pay more millage to support the school. The distirct is run by a bunch of "WANNABES"

column3: every classes are packed over 30 studends. most of studends aren't able to sign in actitivities like sport teams and some of them got no attention at all from certaint teacher, but most of teachers are excellent with experience. A communication is weak between shool and parents. Your kids would get lost in the school if they aren't strong enough. I'm currently a junior and I can definitely tell you that the teachers at Cardozo are amazing and they let you get involved with everything pertaining to the subject matter and beyond. The students are interested in fully understanding the educational matter and will work diligently to achieve high scores. The school is dominantly a law-based high school, but there are two specialized programs: da Vinci and Law. In addition to the programs offered, many AP courses provided as well. The teachers won't hesitate to get to know your child, which, I believe, is the core of educational success. The student will feel welcome because there's always a place for the child to succeed both academically and socially. There's a club and team for nearly everything. I am currently a senior at this school and I've attended this school since I was a freshman, so you can trust me when I say that this is the one of the best schools in Queens, NY. There is a wide variety of classes to choose from and at many different levels: regular, honors, Davinci (for math and science only), AP. You can always challenge yourself. Also, the teachers for the most part are good and knowledgeable! If you are having trouble in class, many of the teachers are willing to tutor you during their break. This school really tries its best to prepare its students for the regents exam. During the Spring term, students may stay after school twice a week for extra regents help. These extra regents help classes are free and taught by actual teachers. If that's not enough, students having trouble in a class may sign up get tutored by an Arista student in the library during their free period. Arista is a special program at Cardozo for the students excelling in their classes and willing to commit hours to community service. It's not a great school after all. Most teachers are dedicated, but the school administration, student support staff,etc. are not there. You are on your own , sink or float. Send your child to a smaller school with better management and support team. With only 83% graduation rate, it's not a great school. 17 out 100 students are not getting their diplomas from Cardozo. Im a current freshman and i love this school!!! the teachers are caring and first i thought cardozo was a large scary school, but no!!! Its very nice and makes us feel like a family. All the clubs and sports are amazing. Orchestra and band is good as well! Classes are all provided and LOVE AND LOVE my teachers. :) I love cardozo diverse student body! great programs! solid faculty! this school is great at preparing students for college level work. The school has a great reputation and continues to give its students a quality education. My kid is a senior at Cardozo. I would say the experience here is mixed. Academically it's good as my child is naturally curious and motivated to perform well for respect from peers and teachers alike. Extracurricular wise, the school also provides plenty of opportunities engaging students with varied talents. The high school counselor is outstanding in terms of supporting students applying for scholarships and summer programs. The issues lie in student body which is extremely diverse, not only ethnically also socioeconomically. Some groups of student cause concerns on school safety. Cardozo has a separate College Office dedicated to supporting college applications. While understanding the staff members have been chellanged by the load of paperwork for a graduating class with 948 students this year, I still find the office could do a better job communicating with a student and family, and offering more meaningful advice on college app process. On the other hand, classroom teachers are very responsible and inspiring. Most of them serve 5 stars! I hate this school so much! It's apparently known for its "good" teachers, but the reason why I don't feel like going to school in the morning is because of the fact that I have to deal with my horrible teachers again. Not only are they unreasonable, stubborn, rude, and horrible at teaching, but some of their tests don't even have anything to do with the topic! The school itself is extremely unorganized; with people in the guidance office who will yell at you for simply asking for something, rude and disrespectful students, and much, much more. The bathrooms are extremely unsanitary, especially later in the day. This school looks and feels like a prison. Because of this school, I sometimes don't feel like living anymore. My overall impression about Cardozo HS: for both students and parents, it's a tough job navigating through the system to get support. It's much easier to become lost given the complexity the student body in addition to the 24:1 student-teacher ratio. A lot of opportunities out there, but you need to work very diligently to find out, to capture it. You are pretty much on your own, so stay strong, focused, and try your best to thrive. College app process is no difference, you figure it out yourself, don't even bother the college office because people there are always busy. I'm not saying they are unsupportive, in fact, with the huge help from parent volunteers, all required forms are filled and sent out on time, but in terms of information and meaningful advice, don't rely on anyone but yourself. Others should know that this school offers a variety of classes, organizations and clubs to participate in. I like the fact that it has many clubs, organizations, sports teams that I can join. My school could improve by being a little less crowded. Our family moved to bayside from out of state in order to enroll our kid to Cardozo, which enjoyed a great reputation for being strong academically. The freshman year went well. Since his sophomore year thing have been changed drastically: many kids transferred to Cardozo from closed low-performing schools in Jamaica, which cause so many problems to this fine school and motivated students. Cardozo used to be one of the finest high schools in NYC housing so many high-achieving minority students who eventually land themselves in top colleges and universities. Is this the reason that Bloomburg decided to cut its budget for advanced courses, put unmotivated students into classrooms so the school's overall performance got downgraded? Achievements should not be punished, and the students aiming high deserve support rather than discouragement! Guidance is exceptional. I have one person who was a Godsend right from the first day of school.. As far as safety.. it's not terrible, but it's not great either.. I am in the process of getting a safety transfer for my child. I don't want my kid in this school anymore. The closing of another school in the area, has changed Cardozo's reputation. It's unfortunate, but I would prefer to keep my child safe. My son's first year was fine all the teachers he understood . Second year Mr Shin he is having a problem with along with the other classmates. The kids don't understand him also he has poor teaching skills and doesn't care abt his kids. Math AP takes his side when addressed with the problem with out hearing my son side of the story. Mr Bomer is the kindest caring person he actually cares abt the kids and help in the best way possible. It's great and fun. Most people are nice and polite to each other. It is a very safe school due to many security guards, and many teachers make it fun to learn. The teachers make learning a fun opportunity for us to enjoy. They make us want to come to class often. The tests are difficult level, and the AP classes expect a lot from you. The AP classes challenge you and your limits. People in this school are very talented and funny. There are many clubs to join, and fun activities to take part in. Cardozo is having their annual blood drive for those who need it. The security guards and school aids get along with the students very well and ensure that everyone is in their classes at the right time. They keep us safe and hallways cleared. You should come to Cardozo High School! dont let this schools past fool you, this is nothing but an average high school and nothing special. yes it may have been great but with foolish decisions made by the staff and with every class having over 30 kids, your child is better off going to their zoned high school. say what you want but their is nothing special about it, the school is nothing special and will its performance will begin to decline unless it starts to fix its act soon. too many kids attend this school and they don't think its a problem but it is. teachers don't teach as well as they used too since they don't understand every single student as well as an average sized classroom they made my relationship with my parents fall apart. My father curses at me for being "lazy". My mother doesnt pay attention to me and doesnt even cook for me. the teachers here had made my self esteem go down. :( very bad school Unfortunately its terrible the school is out of control

column1: This is the third school my child has attended in the last three years, and is by far the best of them all. I love the way the school encourages students to do their best,and at times, implements a reward system for achieving their goals. The school provides a very positive environment for the students learn in. Although it is fairly early in the school year, I have already had necessary communication between myself and school faculty. This communication puts my mind at ease that my child's education is of the utmost importance to the school. The absolute very best school that my kids have attended or myself. The staff is very friendly, teachers go out fast of their way to help the students succeed and make sure they comprehend the lessons given. One of my sons has a disability and they have exceeded my expectations of helping and accommodating him. Very impressed with Pisgah!

column3: Having moved from Fairfax County, Virginia, the bar was high when looking for a new school for my high school son. We searched the greater SE NC region before choosing to come to Topsail HS. Mr. Skipper was excellent his first year and Mr. Simmon has done well with Marcus having moved on. There are always issues with any school system but Pender County has done well and has modern programs without much of the politically correct nonsence we experienced at Lake Braddock. Class sizes and technology are very good. Our research paid off and we are quite pleased. We would prefer email/ TXT messages vs. phone recordings but they do communicate well. I must honestly say, this school is quite the bees knees! It is certainly satisfactory for the average citizen to recieve an education of an honorable level! This school is amazing! My child has special needs (he has an IEP), so we have to request special help from his teachers on a daily basis. These teachers go above and beyond our expectations. They always keep you in the loop and most of them will send home several progress reports so that you can see how your child is doing before the official report card comes out. This helps you in making sure that your child is caught up and has turned in all assignments, etc. There was a new principal last school year who put a few new practices into place. Though I'm not pleased with them, we have adapted with no problems. There is one person in the office who can be less than pleasant, but that's really the only negative I can think of. This school lacks in equity in race some students are treated better than others It is amazing, I think this should be a 10/10. It is the best school I’ve ever attended. I saw other comments talking bad about equality... lies!! This school is perfect. the most racist school i've ever been too This school is ok the cooking classes are great everything else sucks

column3: If you truly want your student to have the best education possible, run far away from this school. It's unlikely their needs will be met, and much of their potential will be wasted. The administration is a complete joke. They tend to get so wrapped up in trivial issues that more often than not the bigger problems slip through the cracks. As far as teachers go, some are good, some are really really bad, and some have just given up. Troubled and struggling students are usually completely swept under the rug or handed off to Ashley Valley Education Center so they won't be in the way anymore. While many boast the school's vast array of extracurricular activities, the sad truth remains that the art and music programs are on the verge of collapse, despite these teachers' best efforts. Nearly all of the funding goes into sports and other teams like drill and cheer, without so much as a second glance at these other programs. I am a student here at Uintah High and I absolutely love this school! Uintah high offers some college classes to students from across the street at the Uintah Basin Applied Technology College (UBATC). Teachers are great, administration is great, school spirit is amazing, and sorry I have to brag but Uintahs drill team is beyond amazing taking state for 4 years straight in 3AA and first in 4A region and state is next week! GO UINTAH #proudtobeaUte The administration is a joke. All they care about is getting paid. I am currently a student here and a week ago, i received a parking ticket for a day that I was excused from school. This whole school is a complete joke. The administration is ridiculous. They're only there to collect a paycheck and don't care about the students and also don't want fun to be in school. Would not recommend. I'm now in college and am very underprepared for the workload compared to the rest of the students in my classes. I've learned in my time here that there is no problem that this administration can solve. The school culture is awful and it seems like theres a big fight I hear about every other couple of weeks. The workload I've received in most of my classes has led me to struggle to keep a healthy work/life balance, and that's not even taking my job into account. The one thing they did right was letting students come to UBTech. I've had a couple of good teachers but the other ones have been incompetent. Learned that you cannot personally criticize this school without being pulled into the office for interrogation. This school, along with the school board, needs an overhaul and fast, or these new students coming in are in for a hellish four years.

column1: Norfork High School is fantastic. The teachers care about the students and help to keep parents informed. The principal has many years experience and is respected by the children. The parent involvement exceeded all of my expectations. Above all, this is a nice & quiet school. You dont have to worry about all the things you would have in the larger cities. Norfork elementary has its problems and is now limiting parent involvement most of the teachers are experienced and curious some think they rule even over the parent and the principle and superintendent is allowing it If you are an involved parent and want to work with the school for the good of your child look else were.

column3: This is an amazing high school. The students are very welcoming and accepting of others. The teachers are amazing and always willing to help. There are a number of different clubs and organizations to become active in. The courses are challenging but not impossible. Henry Ford II High School is a family, and the other high school in our district ( Including Chippewea and Dakota ) are our extended family. Within this past year we have lost two students within our school to tragedy, and within our district we have lost five friends. Today, May 11th, 2015, is the day we return to school after the lose of our fellow student Michael Wells, and the loss of our three friends from Stevenson High School Jon Monolios, Jack Parry, and Manny Malaj. As I walk through the halls I see broken spirits and hearts due to this tragedy but our principal Ken Cuchi has provide us with an area to grieve in our library and suport from our counsellors and professional grief counsellors from our district. If you are thinking about sending your child here know that you are send them to a family, like all families we of course have feuds but when a fellow family member is in need of a hug or support we will always be there. Being a senior here currently I am happy to be leaving this school knowing its halls will continue to be filled with endless love. Falcons Flock Together. - Sara Schoenherr

Sulligent School is like my childrens other family. My children can't wait to get up every morning and head out for the bus. Sulligent School is the best and I would recommend it for any parent or any student for that matter.

column3: After a year at this school my eyes have been opened to how different school has become since I was a high school student. I have to say this school was so much LESS than what I expected and bad thing is I believe it starts with the Principle. It is hard to run a school already but when you allow some kids to be held to different standards than others you are really asking for more trouble. I fear that the Quality of the Teachers are going to be overlooked by the Principles lack of stability. When you allow your Athletes to do what they will and allow these CHILDREN to disrespect teachers and their class rooms......YOU ARE HEADED FOR TROUBLE. This School is out of control... I am currently a student at Cedar Shoals, and I truly believe I am getting a good quality education. Many of the teachers are outstanding and have material to fill the full hour and thirty minute block, despite popular belief. The social aspect isn't the greatest, but it really does depend on who the students surround themselves with. Cliques are not an issue and our wide variety of elective courses allow students to try different things from all the departments and maybe discover a talent they didn't know they had. One of the top JROTC programs in the nation. Instructors are totally involved with the students both in academics and the extra curricular activities. National level Drill and Raider teams. I currently go to school at cedar and am glad I am leaving after this year. I mean the fine arts department is amazing with caring amazing teachers who push us to do better. But the academic teachers take advantage of the fact that students who do their work will and focas more on yelling at the ones who won't. The drug use is crazy and well known but nothing is done about it. This school is out of control. I go to Cedar Shoals and it really does depend where you hang around in this school. The fine arts building is the best and most positive place at this school. But when you step into the academic building, there are evident problems not being solved. There is a large drug and theft problem, but yet nothing is done about it. The administration is also very ineffective and takes no action with serious and important issues. Hopefully, a new administrator may turn things around next year. Also, very good teachers are leaving the school due to the forced teaching model and unsettled administration posts. A plus at the academic building is the AP courses. Many 4s and 5s are received on the exams. An emphasis is put on the top 5% and bottom 20%, but not for the students in between. Those students are left to fend for their own achievement and are not challenged due to dismal advanced curriculum courses. To get challenged here, you have to take AP courses. Both of my children graduated from Cedar Shoals High School. They were both in AP classes and are now college graduates. My eldest has a PhD. and is a college professor. The fine arts department is excellent. My youngest son had a wonderful time in drama and participated in several plays while he was there. Like any diverse environment, there can be some problems , but my children made lifetime friendships at Cedar, and learned valuable experiences there.

column1: The administration is completely unresponsive to parent concerns, and doesn't inform parents of substantial proposed changes in the curriculum. They told parents a month before school began that the middle school would combine grades 7 and 8. My son now sits in pandemonium among 75 other students, with sub-groups constantly coming and going. The idea of combining 7th and 8th graders is idiotic. My son tells me that they're not learning ANYTHING. If they hadn't sprung this on the parents at such a late date I think many parents would have found alternative schools for their kids. As it was, it was too late to find any alternative other than the public schools or home schooling. I will shout from the rooftops, for all to hear, that LMMS is a disaster and a waste of money. What's worse, it's wasting valuable years of my son's education. If I pull him out and send him to another school for 8th grade he's going to be way behind because HE'S NOT LEARNING ANYTHING AT LMMS. Outstanding education in a caring, nurturing environment! All five of our kids love their experiences at LMMS and LMH!

column3: I went to Woodstock from 1994-1998. The school was very demanding academically. I echo the sentiments of one of the previous posters who stated that classes at Woodstock were harder than any of the classes I took in college. I knocked a star off because the worship of athletics, especially the football team, was a little embarassing when I was there. Also, I felt the school was rather cliquey and many teachers perpetuated the caste system by playing favorites with athletes and other favored students. I hear my college friends, who grew up closer to the city, tell me that the athletes were kind of a joke at their schools. Well at Woodstock they were looked upon as Gods. This school is amazing. I am a former student and learned more than I thought I would both personally and educationally. It's staffed wonderfully, and I don't think I could've had a better experience. The teachers are willing to put in their time to help a student if they need it and are more than eager for all students to learn and succeed. I had a wonderful learning experience and was in mostly AP/Honors classes. I feel that I was more than prepared for college and was eager to learn due to my time at WHS. I would definitely recommend this school to anyone who wants the best for their student. Wonderful staff that help every one of children reach their potential. Very positive and excepting learning environment. Support teachers and staff are great. My experience at Woodstock was great! I liked almost every teacher I had and learned a lot. They always had fun events to keep students entertained! Wonderful experience! So proud my son is a Blue Streak and that my middle schooler will be one, one day as well! Great culture here, rigorous coursework. Many college credits offered and a great sense of pride. Very positive vibe in this building.

column1: My experience w/ the davis hi school principal and supt. was extremely upsetting. My special needs child was made to feel very unwelcome...a hostile atmosphere was fostered by these 2 individuals to the extent that i moved to sulphur and enrolled my child there rather than subject him/her to further harrassment. You know... I hate Davis to all extent and would really rather live somewhere else. There are bullies here, Teachers let football players slide past grades, and if you aren't a sports person... you aren't good enough for Davis. I would definitely not recommend this School! All the principals got their jobs because they're friends with the Superintendent! Please... if you have anywhere to pick from... don't pick Davis! It would be a waste of your time/child(s) capabilities! Football guys especially... teachers will let your grades get by even i they're bad, and College would really hit you, and your Grades hard, and all that money spent... is gone! So... don't waste your child(s) capabilities! its great if all you want your child to learn is football and graduate to work at the local bank or gas station, that's about the amount of education they will receive. Davis is a cesspool of gossip and cliques. I grew up here and I went to school here from kindergarten through 12th grade. Once you get into middle school, you start to realize that nobody cares about anything except football and the popular students. Football players can do whatever they want and never get in trouble. Cheerleaders are just the best rays of sunshine and their uniforms don't have to conform to the school dress code. If you disagree with the hive mind, be prepared for the shunning you will get. There's a lot more to life than this town. For the ones that escape it and realize that Davis is not the real world, good on you. For the ones that stay and still obsess over gossip and football...you're just ensuring that things never change in that town and at that school. There have been a few amazing teachers here and there, but most of them don't even see what's going on right in front of them. As long as you turn in your work and keep your head down, you'll survive and you might not even be noticed. To the kids that are having a hard time, just remember, it does get better. I promise. I was bullied and treated like garbage all through high school and on multiple occasions, I thought about taking my own life, but I made it out. And you can too. Hang in there. Davis is a great public school! After reading the current reviews, I noticed that only people with bad experiences are reviewing so I must also tell the good! Davis is a small tight knit community who stands behind their students which is typically shown thru sports. It’s a school full of tradition and that can be seen just driving into town. As a DHS Alumni (with family currently in school as well) looking back after college and careers, I’d say Davis did a great job of prepping for furthering my education and surviving the outside world! They went above and beyond just teaching the basics and truly care about you as a person. I have came to be friends with those who taught me in school and know they want the best for their students!

On a side note, the block scheduling seems to allow teachers to teach a subject more thoroughly and makes school days go by quickly. CCSHS is a really good place to be every day, and I do suggest sending your kids here. Good- the building facilities are very modern and up to date with many improvements architecturally and technology. Beautiful gyms and theater. music and art departments need more improvements and investment. Football team is fairly new and some sports are growing skill wise with new programs. Track is an excellent program here and a new indoor track and football field is in progress and to be completed in a years time, that’s exciting.

column1: The worst school I have ever seen. If you have a child that actually cares about success and is working hard toward DO NOT send your child here. column3: I went to this school from 04-08. Football is NOT the most important thing. This school spends more money on football equipment than it does trying to get a computer in the class room for every student. Their books are outdated and they went through 3 different principals while I was going there. A lot of the students care just don't care. Even though the school has the right to drug test students on the football team they don't because they know they would find drugs. There had been at least TWO drug dog searches while I was there. As most people in the community know, the education isn't the best, but it is a lot better than the surrounding schools *cough* *cough* Southland Academy. As long as your child is in the honors program and you have taken the time to instill the morals all children need, he/she will do fine. It offers many more options of success ( A.P. classes, sports, clubs) compared to surrounding schools. It's only real competition within 20 miles is Schley County. Schley County has a great basic class schedule (Chemistry, English I, II, III, Math I, II, III, etc), but they lack in the supposed honors/A.P. classes. As a student from these two schools I am impartial to Sumter and Schley because they both have their positives and negatives. Sumter overall has an OK basic curriculum while, in my opinion, the honors/A.P. classes are outstanding. The drug problems aren't that big, it is like every schools. If you kid doesn't do bad things before moving to this school, he will continue to be a good kid. I remember when I transferred from Schley to Sumter and heard all of the hype of how bad it was, but, in reality, it is not bad whatsoever. It all depends on the morals and ideals of your child. The school has lost of good thing like opportunities for high achieving students and extracurriculars. But there is a school board member that has put her whole family working in the school system. Lots of good teachers leave each year because they find out they cant cross any of these family members or their friends. So lots of good teachers just leave after a short time. Lots of folks are getting fed up with her and she will be voted out next time but the damage is done. Unfortunately our kids wont get the chance to go back and do school over again. My advice is look carefully at homeschool or the charter school. The public school can be ok if your child is a high performer.

column3: I transfered to Los Al this year from a high school in Georgia. I did not come to the school with incredibly high expectations but i am severely disappointed with the lack of attention paid to each individual students' needs. At my old school I was in all honors classes on my way to AP courses my junior year (current year) but when I transfered here I missed the AP deadline and I was forced to sign up for all on level classes (Los Al does not offer honors courses). No one would help me get into more challenging courses. What I have noticed from these on level classes is that it is almost impossible to learn anthing because the teachers always have to direct a good portion of their attention on misbehaving students. I feel like I am not being prepared for college but instead learning why not to become a teacher. The curriculum is also very lacking and unchallenging and I am finding that I have learned most of the content we go over... as a freshman or sophormore at my old school. I do not recommend this school if you want your child to have a challenging education (no matter what level they are on) with some of these classes... you can literally do nothing and still get an "A". I graduated from this school and honestly if you just pay attention and do your best, los alamitos will get youa straight way into college. My daughter goes there and now if you want to take the PSAT the school will pay for it! Making it way easier. Their sports program is AMAZING. Los alamitos gets noticed by many colleges making it better academically and athletically. The closest high school near LosAl is cypress high which doesnt really give you preparations for college the way LosAl does. And Cypress' sports program isnt best, wont get you noticed by colleges. If your in the OC area, Los Alamitos would be an AMAZING place to put your child in. The focus of LAHS is preparation for college entry, and it does a fantastic job at doing so. Students do quite well in a good learning environment. However, the availability of art and music programs is lacking. Athletic programs are not a priority although the opportunities are there They provide an amazing variety of curriculum choices for academics (math, science, technical, foreign language), as well as the arts (choir, music, drama, dance, visual arts) and sports. Many of the programs and activities are nationally ranked if not multiple year national champions. One of just a few schools to be recognized nationally for their AP course development.
