column3: I have had four children go through Penn. Sadly, I think that it has changed a great deal in the last ten years and what used to be one of the most progressive academic schools in the area has become one of the worst schools in the area. It used to be a place that was known as a 'community of caring learners.' Now they have placed two security towers in the front door and have hired rent-a-cops to 'improve' safety. They used to have an advisory system that helped to reduce annonymity and increased learning opportunities. Now they have large study halls of 80 to 100 in which they just 'warehouse' kids. Learning does not seem to be the focus. The curriculum is now a joke created out of a philosophical mindset stuck in the 1980's. Penn is riding on its past laurels. Don't be fooled. Send your kids elsewhere. I am a current student at penn and I don't like it here at all. Most, not all, of the teachers didnt really teach and just gave us "busywork" for an hour and a half and then yelled at us for not trying to learn. The schools focus seemed to be targeted towards its sports and music programs more than their actual education. The school is just so big that the security can't control us and that leads to fights happening every week or so. I am a part of the wrestling team and a few other clubs so im not an antisocial kid by any means. If you're looking at schools around this area do your kids a favor and don't send them here. I am an alumnus from 2002. I can't imagine having gone to a school where I would have had more opportunities. When it comes to education Penn does a good job overall at preparing students for the future. However, there are some key issues to keep in mind. Being a part of the alumni and being a multiple state champion while attending, it makes me sad to see the political hold from the boosters dictating who plays. More student athletes quit or are disheartened because of this very issue. Back in my day it was all smash mouth the best athlete will play. Now if you are a granger elite your kid will play. Your child could have all the talent in the world but if that "donation" is made the coaches will not rock the boat and the Elite's Child will play. This isn't only happening at the High School level. It has now spread to the middle-school Jr-high that feeds into Penn. When a coach tells a 5-yr near perfect starter who loves the game "Your just not big enough" (Mind you its Jr-high) there is something wrong with Penn Harris Madison Athletics as a whole. When was the last time the Football Team won State? Let the best players play based on the definition of an athlete and not how big your parents wallet is. So sad. Entering as a freshman who had just experienced cancer, I was worried that I wouldn't be accepted because of my lack of hair. To my surprise, fitting in was natural; and for a fairly keep-to-myself kind of kid, I was glad it worked out that way. The teachers are great (with a few exceptions, of course) and truly care about the students. They'll stay after school or come in early if you need help, which is an incredible thing to do. The security guards are, well, not very intimidating. Generally, their barks are bigger than their bites. And they bark a lot. But security is above average because we have actual police officers in school all day. The sports are competitive and intense and school spirit is contagious. There's really a place for everyone at Penn, whether you're a super sporty kid, an art kid, an intelligent kid, or somewhere in between. My personal experience with guidance counsellor a has been superb and they try to get to know you for an intimate feeling during appointments and scheduling. I'm a current junior and don't regret choosing Penn a bit. It can be hard, but it's worth it! Its would be hard for anyone school to handle so many kids. Penn is not doing all they could do to make the school a safe place to be. Its not a place where the teachers or staff will know who the students are or even try to.I guess if you scored a winning shot on the team you might be recognized but everyone else if left feeling cold. Great school all together. I'm a senior in this school and its been a great four years here! I recommend Penn High School. Penn High School is an exceptional school with excelling programs such as marching band, athletics, orchestra, choir, art, and many more. Penn can seem intimidating from the size and number of students, but this school isn't as scary as it seems. The school also has begun using Chromebook laptops (2014-2015 school year), and every student gets their own which is very helpful and gives every student an opportunity to have access to a computer. This school is filled with opportunities for everyone. Both my boys attended Penn. Their needs and interests are quite different but it was still a great experience for both of them. One was more outgoing and into electronics and music and various clubs. He had a ball, made many friends and had several college offers (choose Bethel). The other was very quite and athletic and also did well. (He went on to Purdue). Like any school there are teachers that mean the world to you and teachers you'd rather not have again. But we should expect that and the variety is good! I think the leadership under Mr. Hope is exceptional. I also know they work very hard at safety, it's not just a front. Very positive experience both as a student myself and as the parent of students. The school is great but can they please close down for a while to fix the bathrooms

column1: I am a senior at WGHS and proud of it! While we may be cheap, and the teachers small, I am comfortable and I love going to this school. I like Mr. Bible, because as an admin, he can handle the students. Yes, I get that the whole "religious" thing can be a bit, oh, I dunno, "unfair" but if you don't like it go somewhere else instead of complaining, but you won't find a better school anywhere else I will say that. As a very religious person it gives me pleasure when church activities are allowed. I also love our FCA. Best school in the county! There's nowhere else I'd rather be! BUFFALO PRIDE (: West Greene High School is a really terrible school. The teachers/principals put more stress on being late to class than what goes on during the school day. The so called "leadership club" members were selected with a blindfold on or something. The majority of the so called "leaders" are the people who should be in abic, or suspended. The majority of the teachers dont even teach. And the teachers try to be student's friends rather than educators This place is horrible for anyone who is not Christian. After moving here in 10th grade it didn't take long for people to find out I was an atheist and I caught quite a bit of drama about it. They regularly allow church and school to blend here. The teachers, for the most part, move extremely slow and they're going over things I learned in seventh and eighth grade. Its a poor education, and everyone here thinks they are at the best school ever. The school lunches are definitely to be avoided at all costs. A few of the students are okay, but many people here are judgmental. Everyone infringes on other peoples' rights if you don't share their beliefs. If you have the option, avoid this entire county. This school is behind in scores and doesn't properly prepare the student for the future. The teachers don't all care and the students basically run the place. In fact, one teacher for sure bullies the kids in their class. From telling students to kill themselves to threatening to cause a potentionally deadly allergic reaction in another, This teacher belittles and verbally abuses these students, and if any of them try to stand up from themselves the teacher makes threats to remove them from doing what they enjoy. Even if the student leaves, the teacher still belittles the student and says inappropriate things after the student is no longer in the class. Awesome loved it i loved my teacher's and the fun times there

column3: I went to South Milwaukee and graudated from there. I attended MPS from k4 - 8th grade and wanted to get out of that system as soon as possible being the only "acceptable" schools to attend were on the otherside of town. Im a mixed African-American female so it was a big shock going from a predominantly African American school to South Milwaukee. It is an okay school the teachers are great and very involved in the students lives, I just wish the school was a bit more diverse. Also it is hard adjusting to the atmopshere if you did not attend the SM school district all your life. Majority of the kids grew up and having being going to school with each other since kindergarten. The campus is very nice, and the block scheduling has its perks and downfalls sometiems you can only teach so much so there is a lot of down time which students use to mess around or do nothing. I enjoyed my four years but there are somethings that I would change. The school is a very clean place. I enjoyed attending there. It's not diverse and I have attend here since 9th grade and graduated. I would say there are pros and cons about this school. It's not quite challenging enough nor competitive unless it is about sports. I heard great things about this school and decided to send my child here, but to be honest.... this school isn't that great. Most of the staff are rude and don't really care about your child's success, unless your child is the "model" student. They say they don't believe in bullying, but then they do nothing about it. Actually, I've learned that the schools says a lot, but does nothing to back up what is actually said. I would not recommend this school if your child has been bullied, mental illnesses, or has ADHD/ADD. They don't have time to give equal education rights to students that are not the "model" student. Decent school, i would recommend bringing your child there. most teachers are good and the system for the most part runs smoothly good school, teachers are nice and the students are good We moved away from SM after the 2018 school year. Both of our sons attended Catholic school. We moved them into SM public schools at 6th and 8th grade because they wanted more options in music and sports. Although both of our sons were in advanced classes they were still behind in math and science when we moved to our new school system. If you want your children to attend college I truly think their are better choices. We attended most of not all the parent teacher conferences. I think the teachers care what is missing is parental involvement.

column1: I continue to be disappointed by the by how every little thing has to be run by the principal from class schedule changes to taking a class at a local college. Instead of letting the staff do their job, many things are micromanaged. That is why we have a counselor who is wonderful to work with. When school leadership is disrespectful to students and parents, people start searching for other schools. 90% of the teachers are wonderful & caring. Others there for the paycheck. The principal is a dictator & will not change his mind about anything once he's made his decision even if it goes against the handbook. The biggest problems at Wesclin are bullying, cliques & drugs. If you are new, you won't fit in unless you play football, are a cheerleader or on the dance team. A new school was built & opened this year. The focus of the school is apparent; the gym is huge; classrooms are not. The cafetorium is used as a cafeteria/auditorium & is not large enough for either. When plays or concerts are held, tall rails block the view of the stage. The "media center" (aka library) is in the middle of the school and the students are not allowed to pass through it to get to their classes, forcing them to walk all the way around and often making them late for classes. There are little extra curricular activities except for sports. It's mainly football, basketball & baseball/softball. There is a Math team and scholar bowl team. Education is good, but otherwise, am not overly happy with this school. They are far too worried about the students excelling in sports over academics. Being a military family, we have been to several schools, including Mascoutah, 5 miles away. When we came back to this area, we specifically chose Wesclin due to its smaller size (approx 100 students per class). Too much drama in bigger schools! The academics here have prepared my kids for college, and the staff and students were very welcoming. These are small towns with many families in farming, and the community is great. The new school is awesome. All the teachers have taken an interest in my kids succeeding and have shown flexibility when needed. I personally like that there are no AP classes here, they are overrated. Instead they have several dual credit classes that actually transferred 100% to my daughter's college. I highly recommend this high school.

column3: From the superintendent down to the "para professionals" and everyone in between this is one of the worst districts for children with disabilities. There was a sprinkling of decent teaching staff while my child attended but overall very degrading, disrespectful and condescending staff are the norm. Homeschooling or another district are the better. safer choices for your special child. My family's experience with this district has been rought with disappointment. This district negates any responsibility for their inability and apparent unwillingness to educate children with disabilities. Much easier to blame the child's "disability" than the district's inexcusable believe that children with disabilities can't learn. I graduated in 2012. This school was amazing. I went to kindergarten at Woodrow Wilson in Binghamton, my parents and one other parent were the only ones to show up to open house, for first grade we moved to Greene. In Greene, open house is standing room only. Now to focus on the high school; my teachers were fantastic, and I consider many of them to be friends. They opened my eyes up to the world. Yes Greene lacks diversity, but our teachers provided us with knowledge so that we weren't missing out on any cultures. There are many great sports with good coaches. I must admit it was hard to go from a team that never loses in high school to a college team that never wins. My senior year I took four college classes which got me enough ahead to skip a semester. Although the school is small, there are many clubs and activities for students. Band, chorus and footlights were definitely a highlight of both middle and high school for me. In these times many schools are cutting arts programs, Greene is fighting hard so it won't come to that. This school is truly great and I would not be the person I am today if I did not attend this school, with these rock star teachers.

column1: Our family has been SO PLEASED to get to know many of the AWESOME teachers and staff at Berea! Our 9th grader had attended private school previously, and we weren't sure what to expect. What we have found is a TREASURE. There is a bounty of caring, professional, and motivated staffers at this school. I've been amazed at the things that they accomplish and their level of participation and commitment. My student has achieved very high grades this year, and has participated in several extra curricular activities, which we've also enjoyed. Berea High School has exceeded our expectations in many areas. I have to congratulate them for earning a (USNews) bronze medal again this year, and for continuing to improve and succeed at an astounding rate. Great job, Bulldogs! Graduated from here, nothing good to say about the place. Go to Wade Hampton High instead, it's a far better school. Below the lowest rate as possible possible

column3: This school has great opportunities if you are a good student. If you really have to try to pass chances are the teachers will be lenient on you and you won't learn a thing. To learn here, you have to want to. The school is very clique-y in an non-cliched way and fights are common. The dress code is ridiculous, boys can't have facial hair, girls can't wear shorts. A punishment for showing up to school with a mustache--dry shaving in the office. If a teacher sees a cellphone it will be taken away. Body piercings and tattoos are a no-no. You will get sent home for a nose ring. On a more positive note, the guidance counselors are very dedicated to getting students information about college and helping them make sure they are prepared. The teachers are generally very nice and social. I, personally, had a very good experience at WCHS, it's not hard if you follow the rules and make some great friends.

column1: Horrible support from staff. If your child is moving into this school, and not steeped in Common Core trash, you will be considered and “outsider” we moved here from out of state for a new job. When I approached my child's teacher, over the difficulty understanding the “new math” I was told I was poorly served in putting my daughter in a higher grade level, but could do nothing about it, since the year has already started. I hate the “mini-God” attitude of the SD unified thug teacher Union as well. Crawford is an amazing school with many talented young students who are motived to learn. The staff at Crawford is great, they support the students with their needs. Our school has an awesome program for those who want to enter the medical field with many programs/clubs and great AP classes. The sports team is great having one best cross country team in San Diego and soccer team. Crawford happily supports all students who have learning differences. Crawford is a very diverse school with many students coming from all over the world. We all support each other culture and believes. As incoming Senior of the class of 2020, Crawford is a great school and I am glad to attend this school.

column3: I am a graduate of DHS in the class of '12 and have attended the school for 4 years. I've always felt that DHS allows you to be whatever you want to be. If you want to achieve excellence, there will be many teachers to support you. However, if you choose to fail, there will be no one to try to 'help you out' if you simply don't want to try. Graduated students who are accepted into Emory, UPenn, and Berkeley have all taken advantages of all the resources available. Of course, there will always be the druggies and gansters (in every school). I've always felt that DHS is "down to earth" and reflects a very accurate view of the world of education. There is a great diversity in academics, sports, and social statuses. There is not much pressure to conform(like preppy private schools) since students there are so unique from each other, and thus, students display their true personality. If a parent wants his/her child to enroll in a good school, but not a preppy school with snooty kids, I would highly recommend DHS. I think that the review posted by the student on June 7, 2013, is very aptly put. Not only that, the fact that this student is able to communicate more effectively than many adults on this website whose children go to other schools speaks volumes. Our son has gone to Duluth for two years; he's beginning his junior year. DHS has a culture where students are encouraged to get outside of their comfort zone in order to reach a little higher academically. Not only that, but many of the students here evidently come from homes where they're encouraged to be good students; to show respect for the school and the staff (and each other, to a large extent.) We have been very happy here. I have a hard time digesting fees for sports/activities then lackluster coaching in some areas and No AC in the gym!!!. Parents pay hundreds... and hundreds of dollars on top of in excess of $3k in taxes to be in this district. We should be competitive and up to date in all areas. Everyone who Pays ... Plays isn't the best Winning strategy. Additionally, we need MORE supervision at Football Games. The riff raff and fighting is appalling. This is Duluth... NOT the "hood". This school is excellent, and the school was a great help for my disabilities. I appreciate the teachers, fellow peers and the counseling department for being such nice and caring people. Love this school!!! My son is a freshman and loves it also!!! The teachers are very helpful and care about the students. Diversity is the school's strength. Very engaged faculty. Leading the kids into 21st century America There are a lot of fights and the way they discipline the students is extremely uncalled for. Excellent school with diversity being its strength My son studied hard and was well prepared for college Excellent because they put education first and sports second. We were so disappointed in the overall quality of AP instruction and the road blocks that were thrown up because we transferred in that we opted for full time dual enrollment after one year here. Kudos to district for offering this option. I noticed students here are very unhappy some teachers here are great and care about students education and some of them could care less. The work they give them is easy and basically anyone could teach the class. Bad experience .It’s a test in obedience. Listen to the teacher, remember what he/she says, then copy it down a few weeks later. High school often doesn’t allow for the time of exploration that is vital to teen development. Duluth high is an exceptional school that has some of best teacher’s available. They truly care about the students and go beyond to help them out. I was a former student back in 2008 and it was great then and even better now with the additions they have made. This school takes education serious and does not tolerate any bullying. Also, rest assured that they are top rated in safety. I’ve grown up in Duluth for 10 + years and it’s one of the best places to live in GA. Students are bullied and admins say their are to busy with the 2k plus other students they can't monitor appropriately. Can't ever reach the principal. My kids are bullied daily and the school is taking the side of the bully. We will be contacting the media soon!!! RUN AS FAR AS YOU CAN FROM THIS SCHOOL!!!!!!! Good school in my opinion :D, I'd like to recommend this school if your child is in Coleman MS since it's pretty close to Coleman too!

I have an Autistic student whom has been refused special education privelages twice, have promised on several occasions that any short falls on my childs progress would be handled with one on one mentorship from the teacher, but they cannot even make sure she has taken proper notes or takes her homework assignments home. This school is a joke, and more mismanaged than a democrat led presidential cabinet. Dont send your kids here.

I would definatly recomend this school over any other school in the valley. this school is horrible period. I've attend Mojave , which is right up the street before moving a little ways down. I must say I AM NOT A LONGHORN, I definitely miss Mojave. Here at legacy fights break out on a daily , i feel unsafe, there are so many arguments in the class room between kids i barley able to learn. Its funny because the reputation that Mojave has doesn't fit it all , ( the one about Mojave being ghetto and dangerous) When in reality legacy is the bad school. I've talked to my parents and we decided we will splurge on gas to take me up the street every day to learn at Mojave because Legacy Is A HORRIBLE school. I would NEVER send any family here to learn as long as i live. My son graduated from Legacy this past August. He always loved attending Legacy and was very involved in athletics and activities. He qualified academically and athletically to get a scholarship to compete at the college level. He has just completed his freshman year of college and he did well. The teachers and academic programs at Legacy prepared him for his college experience. Way to go Legacy! Longhorns for life! My daughter has been at Legacy for 3 years now. Teacher's here care about the students and those who are willing to learn. One of the main problems at Legacy is the OVERCROWDING of students!!! Sometimes my daughter doesn't even eat lunch either because the lines were toooo long or all the seats were taken. Class sizes are HUGE, she has both regular & honors. NOW there are little to no fights as administration has taken that into control. At least 50% of this school is african american if not more. I wouldnt recomend this school to anyone. Ive had so many issues as far as seeing my counselor to viewing my grades on a website they provide. Now I have moved school and cannot recieve my transcripts because of a " 2 week policy " they informed me about n is been a month. Now im forced to take clases i passed & cannot graduate with my class of 2015, horrible school. Worst high school ever I've went to. I'm not only guy that said this is worst school, my friends said this is worst high school too. Teachers/Staffs are lazy and never care of students. In this building are messy and stinky. Physical Education teachers are also lazy they don't force you to go play any sports, they allow you to use cell phone in there and only check if you're here and wear those PE uniform clothes to grade. Students may be friendly but I met lots of students they are disrespectful and uncool. They don't allow you to pick what classes you want to go to learn. It kinda ruined my life when I used to go there. So terrible and worst. My daughter graduated 2 years ago and my son is a senior this year. Both of my children have attended Legacy for all 4 years of High School. The teachers do not communicate with teachers. They don't put grades into the grade book in a timely manner. If you child happens to be an A student and all of a sudden finds himself/herself failing the teachers and staff don't care and don't notice anything going on. If you try and meet with administration about anything you may get an appointment or you may not. My son is a senior this year and participates in sports. For tennis senior night, which is held to recognize the seniors last game, there were NO administrators of any kind present. It was disheartening to see the lack of respect for these students hard work while playing a sport. Had it been basketball or football most or all of the administrators would have been present. This school has gone down over the past 4-6 years. Soooo Sad:( This school is filled with individuals with serious anger issues. I am embarrassed they are our futures teachers. WorstDo not let your kids go to this school there were lots of fighting over the friendship and lots of reasons, they were not enough to be mature or something negative. Legacy has an exceptional band director who cares deeply about the program and it's kids. It was life changing for my two sons.They also have an excellent theater teacher who has been very impactful to our youngest son.They also have several excellent teachers in English, Math, and Science.The principal was excellent and appeared to have excellent management of the school.The counselor was very caring and helpful for us as well. The administration in this school is just quite awful. They don’t have a clue of what’s going on, I have tried to register my son here 3 days in a row now and they still have approximately more than 50 students out of their class and still attempting to get schedules. Then to top it off I’m at the front office, then they send me to the library, and from the library they send me back to the office to wait at the back of the line. What is going on here? Did you guys forget organization skills? Legacy is a great school and my daughter has gained so many opportunities from there. The performing Arts departments are great and the Dual Credit classes from UNR is better then AP courses.

column1: The School is designed for students that want to succeed and for being in existence for such a short time they have shown results! And as a former student I will tell you DECA students work just as hard as college students and it all pays off! I can only give my perspective as a teacher who works there. DECA is unlike the schools I attended when I was in grade school and by that I mean that I went to schools where kids (for the most part) did what they were told without the need to constantly redirect them, repeat directions, or issue consequences. I want to write something fair so let me put it like this.Pros:*Teachers are nice (several young and new to the field) and willing to provide additional assistance and accommodate as much as reasonably possible to ensure success.*HR and administration are pleasant.*School functions as a team and make sure people are on the same pageCons:*Kids "typically are" fairly disrespectful towards teachers, subs, and other personnel. It's definitely the most unpleasant part of the environment and I suspect this heavily contributes to the teacher retention rate. Students definitely will not hesitate to put you to task. Many kids just don't care about getting negative consequences at all. Some are good and well behaved but these students unfortunately are Not the majority.*Technology is subpar and makes it difficult to perform the job efficiently.*Classrooms don't have doors that lock (or doors period) which is quite problematic for teachers. This is due to the way the school is set up.It IS true that at DECA.. college is heavily stressed and the curriculum can be a bit much for some students who may not necessarily be college bound material. However, if you make it through DECA you'll probably be more prepared for college than several other urban schools. Speaking of which, this is actually one of the highest, if not the highest performing urban school in this area. There's just a lot of discipline problems. Many times I feel several students are very socially handicapped when you just look at the way they carry themselves on a daily basis and just in general interactions with adults.Parents are involved and do share concern about their success of their kids but it's not as prevalent as the current staff (including myself) would like. I've definitely learned to be more patient and calm working here. Overall, it's a good experience (and I really DO mean that) but I wouldn't say it's quote, unquote: "exceptional". -ParentMy eldest son is a DECA graduate in which he started in the 7th grade. Also, I currently have children enrolled. We had nothing but great experiences at DECA, inside and outside the classroom. The staff want the very best for all students and is wlling to help your child reach their goals. There is alot of college prep work involved, which in my eldest son case has prepared him to be successful thus far in his college endeavors! If your child is prepared to work hard, and your a involved parent, this is a great school! The school is an excellent school! They prepare my child for success and prepare for college. The academics can be challenging to kids who are not determined and dedicated to achieve and aim high. The staff is wonderful and communicate effectively as well as leadership. The school has a mediation program for the children and take bullying serious, they also work with the Parents and have meetings or send out notifications when there is a overall issue or social media issues which is common amongst students. The receptionist is awesome and always have a smile the school staff worked together to make sure the kids and parents are heard and great at resolving any issues or concerns of the children. I love this school and would highly recommend if you would like your children to receive have great education,sustainable environment and friendly atmosphere and determination of the teachers and administration to help your child succeed!

column3: I am a senior at this school and love it. It has a great environment and probably some of the best teachers and counselors. This school is far too crowded and has a faculty that does not care about discipline. Drug deals & fighting happen during passing period every day. A teacher actually told my daughter in class on 4/20 that the faculty knows a large number of kids come to school high each day, but the administration won't do anything about it. So, the teachers stop caring about it. There are some good teachers who care and challenge students, but then there are teachers who can't be bothered for tutorials and questions to help kids who don't get it. They are "too busy". More like a college than a high school. This school has great teachers and a great atmosphere. My son speaks highly of his teachers and I can see in his work he is learning rapidly. Actually, this is not true. Central teachers do all they can. It starts witht he parents at home...discipline your kid therre and ithey want act out at school. Not the teachers responsibility to parent your child. I can't say enough good things about Keller Schools..just they are GREAT and Awesome! People can sit here and bash Central High School all they want but the truth is it is a great school full of teachers that helped shape my life. As far as administratively not doing their part-hello parents that's is your responsibility to make sure your child is going to school and not skipping. They are running an entire building while you cannot manage a household. You want stricter rules-but then you say try are power hungry. Be the adult and get your children in check! My son just graduated from Central. It was a good 4 years for him. His teachers were hit or miss. Can't have all excellent teachers every class every year. All in all it's a great high school. The staff have done a great job at turning the school around and making it a safe environment for my kids to learn. My youngest will be a junior this year and i know he will do just fine. Only complaint ....needs better cafeteria food. I am a mother of a student that came from Puerto Rico. The teacher's, the Director all of them helped him a lot to go through the transition, I am so blessed, my son had good grades. Never in Puerto Rico he got the grades that he obtain here in Central High. Again, I'm bessed and my son too, and of course he is very happy!!! My son will graduate this year. I have nothing but positive experiences with the district overall. It has it's share of troubled students, but I feel the staff does what is in its control to curb issues.(the rest is up to parents.. unfortunately too many parents DO NOT do their job!! -it is not a school districts job to parent YOUR child.) Now, this is in part the reason we have had a pleasant experience- we parent our kids and hold them accountable ,for all their responsibilities. Central High School in the Keller ISD is all smoke and mirrors. They are still under the delusion that Keller is still "one of the best towns in America" to live. That title left years ago! They do not prepare students for college they are just interested in the government $$$. Having transferred from the Chicago area, if I could do it again, Plano ISD would be a much better alternative. Think twice before relocating to this area! This is my second year going to this school and I can easily say this is an amazing high school. The teachers are great, and caring. The students are friendly for the most part and it has been just an overall amazing experience. Can't wait for this year to start! My daughter is a Sophomore and enjoys her time there. School seems to have a good mix of students and the most of the teachers seem very capable. The environment seems more supportive and positive with more school spirit than the high school I attended growing up on Long Island. Only negative is that this high school, like all the other high schools in Texas, are bigger than I think they should be. I absolutely love this school's administration! They have gone above and beyond to help my daughter with problems she's been having. We moved here two years ago & she is a bit different, so I was worried she would be bullied, but it's never happened. In fact she's had nothing but good interactions with the other students. Love this school!

column1: I graduated from NMHS just a few years ago, and I still hold a great deal of resentment towards the school. There are a few great teachers who helped me a great deal along the way, but the majority outweigh the few good quality teachers. I graduated in the top of my class with a GPA of 3.7, and continued on to college where I struggled to get a D in my English class. I was not prepared whatsoever for college format (I was even taught that college format of writing papers was incorrect!). However I will say I excelled in Math at NMHS (because of those few good teachers). North Marion is used to being on a low budget with good-for-nothing kids and they don't make the effort needed to turn the school into a success. They bring to bar lower and lower for students and in turn this hurts the students who are eager to learn and willing to work. This school has great potential, but it needs more discipline and structure I attended NMHS myself and graduated in 1994. Apparently, the school has gone far downhill since. I was successfully prepared for college, as I went on to receive 3 college degrees. My son attended, however, as a transfer student for the past 1.5 years. His transfer credits were not properly given to him and this has resulted in a complete mess of his scholastic career and put him behind over a year of courses. The counselors do not work with the students, they seem disinterested in the important job they are paid to perform. My son has tried repeatedly to schedule time with counselors to get his schedule correct and they fail miserably to care how long it takes for a student to complete coursework, if they need help, or if they ever graduate. They have enrolled my son in at least 3 courses multiple times and been non-apologetic and basically refused to address the mistakes they make with his schedule. He was transferred out of state to finish school with myself. NMHS counselor staff dragged their feet releasing his transcripts to the new school and my son has missed a complete week because of their incompetence. I am considering calling the county board of education because this problem is not isolated and needs to be addressed. I do not recommend this school, unless, as a parent you have good knowledge of required for graduation coursework are very diligent in going there in person and demanding proper scheduling, also you should employ a private tutor to help your student. Very disappointed in what this school has become. There are a handful of wonderful teachers that I have studied under myself, however the counselor's office had scheduling issues, even when I attended (uninformed and uncaring personnel in charge of scheduling coursework) and this problem has apparently gotten even worse over the years. I read another review from a student who states that she was not properly prepared for college English. That is very telling. Very unorganized. Very few teachers truly care about their students and their education. They don't stick to their no bully program and have had countless fights some ended in students being sent to the hospital. I will not enroll my kids in this school and id advice you do the same.

column3: All three of our children went through and graduated from the Mt. Lebanon school system. Having gone to a city school I was highly impressed with the qaulity of the education offered. My oldest went on to Princeton and told me that she was well prepared for it. My other children also recieved excellent educations with and although not top achievers turned out quite well. When one of my children was asked About how Mt. Lebanon compared to a highly regarded private school where she taught. She replied that Mt. Lebanon was much better and more progressive in more ways than you could imagine. We have been very pleased with the quality of education our two children have received in the Mt. Lebanon school district. The vast majority of the teachers and administrators have been outstanding. The few that did not quite meet the level of outstanding were at least competent. The poor spelling and writing skills of the two negative reviews lead me to question their credibility and authenticity. I graduated MTL SHS in 1998 and still look back on my time there as a key factor leading to my success in college and beyond. MTL students always seemed to be better prepared than others I met in college and later in life, which I attrubute to the diversity of classes offered and the high standards to which the school holds it's staff and students. Nice school that is getting redone! The math teachers and math substitutes here do an excellent job, very high standards! The students are very respectful and mature for High School level. My daughter use to come home and tell me how great her math sub was for the day. If their subs are that great, the rest of the school must be spectacular. Some nice teachers, some not so nice. My brother and and his boyfriend of over 10 years walked through the building to pick up my son once- they said a woman teacher called them freaks as they held hands at a certain moment. Not a very accepting school, this is 2014, they need to open up their eyes. If they can't accept people for their differences, then people are no longer going to accept Mount Lebanon as the great school it "was". I do not feel the students here are ready for the math section of testing this year. Many students are complaining that they are not getting the skills they need to complete the math expectations. As an alumni of Mt. Lebanon Senior High School and current college student. I can say that I am much more prepared for college classes than my peers. I feel MTL did an extraordinary job of preparing students for college and I am forever grateful. The relationships I formed with some of my high school teachers I will always cherish and I have only good memories from this great school. I owe my success in college to them and will be forever grateful. I'm a parent who in the near future will have had 3 children graduate from the high school. The Mt. Lebanon SHS is a large facility with something for everyone, but consistent with its larger size it can be intimidating and create disaffection for teens who don't find their identity. Maybe that's just the nature of the teen years. As in any school, there is a range in the quality of teachers, from truly outstanding educators to sub-standard performers. I would say the quality overall trends to the good+ level. It can be a rigorous and competitive environment, which is primarily influenced by the expectations of parents, community, and students themselves. Virtually everyone will emerge prepared and competent academically, but that is because the student cohort is strong & competitive enough to raise the tide for everyone. Beyond academics, the school district has a strong commitment to music, performance arts and studio arts, so the artistically inclined can find an expressive outlet. Additionally, there are numerous athletic opportunities, including a wide range of intramural sports for students who may not have "made the team." Overall, it's a very good public high school. I am going into my junior year at the high school, and I love this school. The kids are nice, there are many clubs and activities (I personally partake in the superb theatre and choir programs). I have yet to meet a teacher that was mean to me. Since transferring to Mt. Lebanon, my grades and GPA have improved and I feel more and more prepared to take my SATS by day. Mt. Lebanon High School will help me get into the college of my choice, and I couldn't be more grateful. The children of wealthy parents are favored. This entire area is extremely snobby. Unless you have connections or wealth, run! Drugs and alcohol issues abound. Children who are struggling fall short. Glad we moved. This is a close knit walking community. There are seven elementary, two middle and one high schools. The elementary is k through fifth grade, the middle is sixth through 8th and the HS is 9 thru 12.. Music is entered at a young age and required for all students beginning at 3rd grade. Languages are begun in middle school although it is believed the program is being pushed back into the elementary schools within the next few years. The English programs are one national recognition and the math and sciences are year after year at the 96 and above proficient levels. The Arts programs are also nationally recognized. The school has a strong sports program which allows all levels of student participation. 99% of students continue on into some type of education after high school whether it is trade, community college, or university. 15% a annually are accepted into the top 20 schools in the country. I am a graduate of Mt. Lebanon Senior High School and had excellent teachers and academic opportunities. I went on to earn an engineering degree from a top tier university and found that my teachers from Mt. Lebanon Senior High were even better than my college professors! The opportunity to take AP courses and to be ahead of the game in college really helped my entire path in life. The teachers explain the material so well, my AP Calculus class was much more understandable and much more clearly explained by the teacher than by my college professor in a course with similar material! I always had that foundation of knowing what I could accomplish and learn in high school, a true confidence builder as a woman in a STEM field. Also, my high school honors physics class was taught by a true professional from Germany with a PhD who dressed the part of a college professor and treated us as such, building our confidence in advanced science and bringing in real-life examples and field trips to analyze applied physics! I am truly appreciative of and value my high school teachers for instilling that confidence, knowledge, and wisdom at such a young age that stayed with me for the rest of my life. Thank you to all the great teachers at Mt. Lebanon Senior High, your effort does not go unnoticed, your commitment to education and your sincere interest in your students' success will always be remembered! As a college (STEM) professional, I have moved my fam across the country several times, so my 4 kids had (at different times) attended 6 school districts. MLSD has been the worst experience for the younger two (the older kids graduated before we had moved here). To say the entire area and thus the school are snobbish and elitist is an understatement. Both the parents and the kids (the majority of) , and by extension the teachers, treat non-wealthy kids with disdain; the preference is clearly allotted to the wealthy insiders and their off-spring. The atmosphere of bullying, looking down upon, and disrespecting the poor(er) kids abounds. By poorer I mean "don't have enough money for a used BMW and a class trip to France in the spring". My kids are both severely traumatized by the experience.

column1: I went to school at Wynnewood- It was and is still a very small, low funded school with limited opportunities for students. I was not prepared for College, and do not feel like the school did much for me in the way of teaching me anything. When I was there, a couple of really good teachers where there, but that was it- two or three at the most that really made you work for your grade. I knew when I was a teen there that I was missing out on so much but to have attended college now I am certain of it. If I ever do decide to move back in the area, my children will certainly not attend school in any of Wynnewoods schools. Likewise- I completely agree with comments below of how closed-minded the administration is- it really is pathetic. I would not recommend this school to anyone I knew either. I attended grades 1-12 at Wynnewood and my experience was fantastic. I had great caring teachers and was involved in many activities. This was a great place to grow up!

column3: Someone said something about how "cliquey" this school was. This person has never gone to another school before. I was extremely miserable and unaccepted at my old school, which was incredibly cliquey. When I moved to South, I had never been happy. Whether you're interest is in math or Japan or pie, you'll find friends here. On top of that, the education system is fantastic. I'v heard great things about the IB curriculum, and as an AP student, I can say I loved my classes. The school was active in the community and did a ton of the things to keep the students involved, even if many chose not to do so. I'm very sad I only got to spend one year here. Honestly, I had never been happier than when I went to this school. The one downside to it is the fact the area is expensive, but I think it is worth it for the experiences and education you'll receive from South. I've only been there one year, but I have three more coming up. I highly recommend South.We may not have a huge number of electives to choose from, but the classes that are taught are taught very well, especially English 9 Honors. I can't use names in this review, but trust me, if you see the Honors English teacher there, you'll know it's him. He's awesome. Not to detract from the abilities of the other teachers, who are also good, for the most part. We also have great extra-curricular activities, including a world-class petanque team (I have no idea what petanque is) and a history of a national level ultimate team. That's ultimate frisbee, which is a real sport, for those of you who've never heard of it. If you do go there, I recommend Classic South, as opposed to IHS, which can be a lot of busy work and stress. That said, by the end of the year, I did get a bit burnt out by the stress despite being in Classic. That's why I only gave this awesome school four stars out of five. The homework can be a bit much, especially if you take a lot of advanced classes like I do. And by the way, I agree with the last post. South is not a cliquey school at all. The environment is wonderful. My kids are SO BORED at South Eugene HS. The teachers do very little except talk, not even noticing that most of the kids have tuned them out. As a result, anything that my kids learn is done on their own, or with my help (or tutoring, since the math department is particularly bad). It is even worse these days because classes are now 90 minutes instead of 50, and my kids find that sitting and listening to a boring person talk at you for 90 minutes is utterly maddening. Most teachers at this school seem to have no sense of best practices, active learning, or student-centered instruction, and are just mailing it in. Their approach is: students should be seen but not heard; all learning comes out of the teacher's mouth and into the students' brains; and questions are discouraged. Leadership is uninterested in this problem, and in fact won't respond to emails (actually, I'm just assuming that the school has a principal, since my kids have never seen him/her and in fact don't know whether it is a man or a woman). The school has a good reputation but it is ENTIRELY due to the students' families and not the faculty. Don't waste your money trying to buy a house so you can send your kids to this school; the quality of the education is no different than anywhere else. Graduated from South with a pre-acceptance into a doctoral program after college. To say SEHS helped prepare me for college and post-grad would be an understatement. They excel in many areas. Lots of AP courses are offered, and I was able to easily enter college as a 'sophomore' in credits which really helped when registering for classes. The teachers here are all wonderful and intelligent, fostering unique and memorable learning environments. I only had 1 or 2 teachers that I didn't love, but that's just due to statistics over the course of 4 years. The school did not feel cliquey at all; we really were like one giant family. Lots of groups, clubs, and niches for everyone. I'd recommend SEHS tenfold.

column1: its not a good school. there's been numerous fights since 2011 started and recently a big fight happened, which ended in police being called. today the news cast was outside the school and before the school was mentioned on channel 12 news (not for good things). As you can tell by the star rating this school is terrible - I'm glad I did not let my child stay past the 2nd year. Pulled him out ASAP. would not recommend this school to any parent. I used to be a teacher here and i can only say that i am very glad i left when i did. the principal there in 2007 was a very ineffective manager (forget about being a leader). There were plenty of disciplinary issues that she was not able to assist. the students did not respect her and she did not respect her teachers. We did not get any professional development about using proactive approaches to discipline. Most parents were disinterested and we had very poor turn out at Parent-Teacher conferences. Students were generally extremely disrespectful and some (i did have some wonderful students) students came to school to ONLY socialize. Good luck trying to get them to listen. I'm still a teacher and have remained one because i left when i did. there were too many structural (and i don't mean with the building) issues in this school. Well I'm going into this school next year and my cousin is in there by the way she talks the school is the best. I'm trying to gruaduate 1 year before I'm suppose to. Wish me luck!!!! My son has been in eximius since 9 th grade and is now graduating. I could attest to their commitment to their students. They were there for me and my son every step. From a little boy to the man he has become in part credit is do to mr. Daly and he commitment to his school and students. The teachers put their students first and never gives up. I thank them from the bottom of my heart for everything they did for my son. I can't wait for my youngest to go to eximius. Terrible. My gay son is always bullied by staff and students

column3: I graduated from Spring-Ford last year, and although it is crowded, the new addition really does space things out. There are enough seats for everyone at lunch, and if there wasn't changes would certainly be made to accommodate them. The guidance department made it seem like college was more challenging to get into than it actually was for me, which was just a motivation to work harder. The majority of teachers are more than willing to do whatever it takes to help their students succeed and even the older teachers are still open to new suggestions. The honors and AP classes are though provoking and challenging. Arguable, a few of the AP classes are more challenging then some of the college classes I am currently enrolled in. The district is also very conscientious of keeping an excellent program for music & fine arts, as well as extracurricular activities, throughout budget cuts. Overall, it's a great place for kids to get an education. My son graduated from Spring-ford last year. We moved here the end of kindergarten for him and he loved school. He decided in eighth grade he thought he wanted something more challenging so he applied to a few private highschools in our area and he decided on The Hill school. Freshman year he began his year at The Hill school and found he lived the challenge of the classes but missed his friendships at Spring-ford. He cane back to Spring-ford to finish out freshman year. With the help of his counselor he was placed in the appropriate honors classes and continued to grow through out his high school career. I do believe high school is what you want to make out of it. I also believe as a parent you still need to be very involved and be your teens advocate at all times. My daughter graduated from this school in 2012, very well prepared and positioned for college. The gifted program in this district is great - differentiated course offerings continue through high school (philosophy!!). There are also a lot of AP courses, and with their effective instruction, she scored a 4 or 5 on all AP exams (so the school helped her trim almost a full year off her bachelor's degree and saved us a lot of money).

column1: This schools is terrible. Its very prejudice against newcomers. If you haven't lived there your whole life, no one will like you. Everyone is very clique-y. Absolute worst high school experience. These middle school teachers give you no respect at all. They absolutely hate you if you are from a certain family or group. They hold grudges terribly. column3: Since these last reviews were sent in things have drastically changed. We have a new principal now and the staff, parent and students absolutely love him. He is respectful and always there to lend a listening ear to anyone who has a problem. He treats everyone as they would want to be treated and people respect him back and love him as a person and an administrator. He is correcting the issues that came about while the last principal was there and things are getting back to the way we as teachers and the students come to know and love in the past. Principal Simmons has returned Hunt HS to the school of choice. The faculty and students are functioning on a high level of enthuisiasm. It is amazing what happens when the leader of anything listens to the people that work for them. Fair treatment goes along way not to mention his passion to see the students succeed Hunt High School is an exceptional school. With great leadership and support (from faculty, staff, and parents), it has provided opportunities for the students to excel to their fullest potential. Not only has the school showed the students how to succeed on their own but how to help others when life throws them curves. Long after graduating from Hunt myself, and seeing my daughter make her way through, the teachers and staff at Hunt have always made me feel safe and proud. Hunt High School is second to none. The administration, staff, students and parents work harmoniously to insure that every student receives an opportunity to succeed and work at their full potential. Like every other school there are obstacles, but we are overcomers. As a former student (Class of 1980), I seen the success of my former classmates, my sons and their contemporaries. I'm proud to be a WARRIOR! Most stuff and faculty are on a power trip...what they say goes...no fairness at all...

column1: The only reason this school doesn't have a 5 star rating is because the people who tend to visit these sites are bitter over their experience. Sure, the school isn't perfect but it by far is one of the best schools in Maine and was recently named one of the best public high schools in the country. I will be graduating in June and I will deeply miss the connections I have made with the school and it's staff. YHS has prepared me extremely well for life after high school and as my senior year comes to a close, I am confident that the YHS faculty is the reason why I am prepared and motivated for the future. The other schools in the area (Traip, Marshwood, Wells etc.) don't even come close to comparing to York. The school consists of basically two types of people, the people who are bound to succeed because of their parents and sucking up, and then you have the smart ones who don't get acknowledged as they should. The schools extracurricular activities are great, yes, but that doesn't reflect the poor quality of the teaching and the ill manner of both teacher and student. The students are not respected, which leads to a strong disliking of the teacher. The teachers only focus on your homework abilities, mostly, and if you need to be moved up, they won't even think about it if you don't hand in homework, which in term, leaves the student unhappy, bored, and miserable. This school could do so much better, and it is very unsatisfactory. Just want to congratulate the students and staff on another job well done. Once again you scored higher then the state average and many surrounding high schools on the MHA and other assessment tests given to you. This in addition to a 90+% graduation rate. Both my children went through the York school system. They were well prepared for their college courses. My oldest is graduating this May with honors. My youngest is a freshmen in college and has made the Dean's list 1st semester. Thank you goes to the teachers, staff and my kids. We truly do have a gem of a school system here in York. A note to past reviewers: A group of teenagers who are not open to having new peers join them is called a "clique," not a "click."

column3: Loveland High School is made to look like a School that it is not. The students that go to this school vary from the many trouble-makers to the few students who strive to become smart. The school condition itself is horrible; from the second you walk into the front office to each individual classroom. The appearance may make you think that the school is well maintained but that is just a cover-up. The teachers within the school do not care one bit about how the students are treated by other students and do not what so ever make an effort to help the students excell in their class. No parent should want their child to go to a Loveland City School in their lifetime. I am a student at Loveland High School currently. It is a good school and offers many courses in a block schedule. However, it is not very diverse and hasn't, to my knowledge, produced many Ivy League students. The people are nice though a bit stereotypically high school like. Both my Son and Daughter Graduated from Loveland High School after attending Loveland Elementary and Middle Schools. What a great education. They had great courses and great energetic teachers. They were both more than prepared for their College Careers. Both were and are Honor Students at Large Midwestern Universities. Highly recommend the Loveland School System. Loveland High School is a great high school. It offers many different courses and all the teachers are willing to help out the students. I have been a teacher at Loveland for nine years. Prior to becoming a Tiger, I had the good fortune to teach at other quality schools and a university. Loveland is ranked in the top 5% of public schools in Ohio and had a recent top National 6% A.P. award. Those accomplishments are great and many schools can boast about their stats. I know the best thing we have going for us is a proactive and tireless building principal; a staff with many diverse awards, grants, and forms of recognition, and a tornado of a student body. We were fortunate to be state champions this year in football and the student section gave more support each and every week to our kids, that I can say they were a catalyst for the team's success. Radio announcers raved about their intensity and love for their classmates and school. Our school commissioned a mural that says "Many Stripes, One Tiger." Our school lives by this motto right now. Enthusiasm and pride can be seen from so many different angles daily, that one would have to spend a week here to witness true Tiger Pride. My children were treated terrible at this school year after year. I want to move from this community due to this school district. Unfortunately we can not afford it at this moment and now we are stuck! Never move to lLoveland unless you are childless. I went to this school till my sophomore year. This school is amazing. They take care of the kids and help them with what they need. My counselor was rude and lazy. It seems like she would often make decisions for me not in my best interest but for her having less work. A great majority of my high school experience was ruined due to incompetent counseling. If I could give this school zero stars, I would, solely because of my counselor. I currently go to this school, it's a solid school. There are no giant red flags as well as nothing super enticing. Most of the teachers here are good I would say 8 out of every 10 are a desirable teacher. The bullying issue is not rampant at all except for some situations where students who are bullied are 99 percent of the time for the choices they make rather then who they are. Things such as doing dumb things and not shaking the reputation, liking peculiar things or being interested in interesting topics. I would say even though this school is 92 percent white racism is not a issue. Obviously there are bad apples which you will always have, but this school is overall very accepting of LGBT, POC, people who have disabilities etc. I believe you will have a good time at this school if you approach it with an open mind.

column1: Small class sizes give students the opportunity to thrive. Healthy co-curricular programs give students plenty of opportunities to feel like members of the school community. Students are getting into the best universities across the entire United States. Hull High School provides an excellent education with small class sizes, terrific teacher-student ratio, and personalized attention to each student's individual needs. Because of the small size, students can enjoy many opportunities such as playing on multiple sports teams where their participation makes an important contribution. There is a thriving AP program and "virtual high school" online offerings provide a wide range of subjects of individual interest. I have no doubt that my children would have not become as successful if they had not attended Hull High School. The Advanced Placement classes were amazing and let my children save time (and me money) in their freshman year.

column1: This school is a big disappointment........when I moved to Harper Woods I moved my children from DPS to Harper Woods HS and I wish I had kept them in DPS. The teachers there do not care about the African-American students and the school allows the students to roam the halls. My child fell behind her counterparts at DPS. I don't think anyone should ever send their child to this school. My child is going back to DPS where they really teach the children. I am currently a senior at HWHS. I've read many of what you have to say and I also see that a majority of you are parents and I'd like to ask those parents a question. At anytime during your son/daughters time at HW were you ever actually at the school during the school day and see what the going ons of the school were? Because from what I have read I'd have to say no. I see many of you if not all of you blame the teachers and administration. well I can tell you that the teachers are great and they do teach. They teach the kids that want to be taught and don't have time to deal with the kids that don't because they have better things to do and to the person who said that the teachers and administration don't care about the African-American students thats bull Harper Woods is a good school. It may not be the bast at times but we have improved as a school. We follow the I Can system with grading and it is the best grading system. Our teachers can be one on one with students but it does depend who the teacher is. When I first came there I cried because I though it was a ethnically diverse school but it wasn't. Overall the school is good. I like it so far. Just wish Hs and Ms weren't in the same building. This school is terrible!!!! It makes me want to kill myself just walking into it! Most of the teachers care about their students but others just downright don't care! It sickens me and all of my colleagues agree. The students are ill behaved and don't know when enough is enough. No home training, lack of attention skills and most of them don't want to be there. The students who do can't concentrate and can't stand the students around them. Most contemplate suicide and self harm because of it. A school is supposed to join students and teachers together, but this "facility of learning" does otherwise. This is not a school, is a prison!!!! I'm glad I pulled my child out of it This school has really declined staring from the administration down to the staff. I would never allow any more of my children to attend. Finances they have but skills they have lost,. Harperwoods is a very unorganized school, they loose most of the kids important information. Most of the activities are very poorly put together, and a lot of the teachers care nothing about if the kids succeed or not. I don't even know how this school is able to function year after year. Great school. Ready to teach, ready to learn

column1: Amazing school, our son is truly cared for in both mind and spirit. The faculty and staff work along side each student and family a true partnership. I have seen amazing growth in my son over the last three years in his academics and personal life. I hope too see my next two boys attend there. Worth every penny! My son is a senior this year. I've watched him grow from a boy into a man under the guidance of the folks at Jesuit High School. The entire staff is amazing. The education is outstanding. My son is getting offers for full rides at college because of the education he's received at Jesuit. It's a multi ethnic faith based community focusing on developing Men for Others. Even the other parents are great. My eldest son graduated from Jesuit in '02. My middle child in '05. We thought it was ok. Neither of them had a great experience. There was a whole lot of pressure for them to fit into a mold. They were not allowed to be themselves and flourish into the best version of them that they could be. Our youngest son is at Jesuit now. I will be transferring him as soon as the year is up. My gut feeling with my first two kids was right. This year alone, there were nearly two dozen kids caught with street drugs during class. The pressure this school puts kids under is absurd. Do yourselves a favor and get out! Excellent school! The best of the best! They are beyond generous, loving, kind and supportive. Jesuit WILL prepare your sons for college as well as transformation into adulthood. They are top notch and there is NO other school I would have my teenage son attend. Of course there are drugs in every school; however, it starts at home. I'm sorry but you cannot blame the school for bad parenting. You have to do your job at home and not expect ANY school to raise your child. What Jesuit offers is far beyond normal academics and delves deep into moral values, character building and love for mankind. JESUIT YOU ARE THE BEST! My son went there for 4 years and the administration was quite hypocritical. "Man for others" unless it came to moneyed interests or in their view what is wrong. Don't waste your time on this sham The school is all about your money! You have to give and give and it's not enough. The Admin team doesn't care about your sons unless you donate constantly. "Men for others" is a joke, don't believe them! If your son makes a mistake there is no forgiveness or second chances. "Men for others" have a different meaning here. If you are looking for a school where your son can be himself and do his best with people around him who respect and encourage him, this is not the right place. Very disappointed! Incredible school; fantastic, caring staff and educators. Our cup runneth over with our experience at JHS. Jesuit is not perfect and may not be a good fit for all boys but it was a very good fit for my 3 sons. It was harder than the public school route which can be a better choice for some people but JHS is a great choice if moral strength, great college academic preparation, athletic, club or drama opportunities are what your sons are looking for. The friends they make at JHS will be brothers for life. I gave JHS 3 boys and they graduated 3 young men with all the skills necessary to become successful college graduates, developed a strong faith, became responsible, learned compassion to be a "man for others", developed solid values to become great husbands and fathers - probably better than me. This was a big investment in our families time, talent and money but worth all we paid to get 3 wonderful sons all doing great in life. Everyone should consider JHS and make their own determination if the fit is right for your son. It was right for my family. There are a lot of statements about the brotherhood and the honor and values of the school. Thing is it is all a face. What really happens is privilege and favoritism at every level. From access to grades to sport. it is not an honest system. Those who donate more see their child "do" better. it is all a farce. I am a parent and my son is a senior and I can say it has been a waste of time and money. My son has not gained or done any better here than he would anywhere else. The whole school is setup for parents to "feel" they are doing something better for their child. Most parents buy into it regardless of the outcomes or comparative options. Also as a CSUS engineering faculty I can say coming from Jesuit buys you absolutely nothing. I've sat on the admin board for over 20 years and this is CSUS not an elite uni who will regard it even less. Jesuit gains your child nothing. Make your choices spend your time and money and roll the dice... In my own experience, horrible. The faculty is sub par, and so are the academics. It is better than some public high schools, but not all. Think about this information before in my opinion wasting money on something useless

column3: I am very impressed dwith what SHS is able to accomplish with the broad and diverse studentbody. It is able to handle kids who take AP and go to the Ivy League and kids who are heading to the military, trade school and the world of work. They have an award winning and very popular music program, excellent science program and lots of extracurriculars. Their main teams don't do so well, but they excel in the small sports like swimming, soccer, lacrosse, etc. The language programs are excellent, and of course the castle school building and stadium rocks. My daughter has blossomed here, she had the choice to go here, SOTA Bellarmine and she chose SHS and has never regretted it. Boosters are extremely active, and the administration is responsive. The pride and tradition at this school is amazing and the building is incredible great place for kids to learn and grow! I am happy with my sons experience here. I would send any kid here and feel good about the recomendation! I go to SHS currently, and am a sophomore. if you are a parent who's child is going to attend stadium soon you should know that our big sports teams- like football and basketball havent won in about 90 yrs. but our smaller teams- soccer, lacross, and swim do very well (the boys swim team won state in 2011-2012 school year). as for the academics: the teachers vary (since they are all in the union) they are rarely given crique about their teaching. some are good, some are very bad. the way to get things done, is take charge with the counclors (dont let them boss u around) ask students who the best teachers are. we have a drug problem, but if your kid is already good, then dont worry. so in conclusion: teachers vary, our big sports teams suck, and we have been known for our drug problems (like all highschools) How is there such a broad extreme from one teacher to another as to how they teach. It's hard to believe all the teachers at Stadium are all in the same school. Don't have a standard for all the teachers there and train their teachers so they would know how to live up to the schools teaching motto. I just recently went to talk to one of my Son's teachers about his grades. He has good grades in some classes and bad in others so I went to speak to teachers. Some teachers are respectful to parents but don't know how to handle the kids and play spiteful games with my son making it impossible for him to get answers about class assignments. Other teachers are respectful to parents and students. In other words they teach by example. His grades are better in the classes where he can feel comfterable talking with his teachers. One teacher is disrespectful to me/his father and the students. This teacher plays favorites, helps some kids more than others. My son is begging this teacher for help and can't get it. If a teacher is ready to throw in the towel from frustration, I can understand but education is also very important. I got a disrespectful e-mail from this same teacher. I'm in shock. The Stadium community has greatly improved over the last several years. A lot of new teachers and staff have been hired that make Stadium HS a better place to learn. Excellent experience for both my son and daughter. This school has many options and opportunities for the kids to challenge themselves. I have been impressed with the communication between staff/admin and parents. Not to mention the setting is beautiful. Everything is available for a successful high school experience. My daughter had a wonderful experience at Stadium. She was able to take a variety of electives which shaped her social and emotional development. She had caring and rigorous teachers to challenge her academically. There are more AP and College in the High School offerings than any other school in our area. The administration is impressive and communicates well with families.
