column1: The teaching staff at the school is largely unable to satisfactorily educate its students, the college advisors know little beyond the main college advising topics, and many school administrators act as little more than figureheads. The school also invests a majority of its time and resources into volleyball, football, and basketball, leaving little room for the other available sports or extracurriculars. On that note, the extracurriculars offered are few and are predominantly service-based, while the only organization the school hosts that targets civic participation is the National Honor Society, and it does it only remotely. Many teachers seem to apply the horns and halos effect to their classes, and frequently, those who speak out against the school or in some way do not align with the white, upper-middle class socioeconomic status of the school are grouped into the halos category. Additionally, homework is oppressive, leaving little room for students to develop curiosity and to learn outside of the classroom. SMCC is the best choice for secondary education in Monroe county. Students are developed both academically and spiritually. My daughter is a Freshman at SMCC. I am a hard person to impress with a school (home schooled my other kids for many years) but I have to say that I am very impressed with SMCC. For one, they adjusted tuition so our large but middle-income family could afford it. The advising was personal and accommodated our daughter's special needs. Despite having Asberger's, she has felt comfortable to join several extra-curricular clubs. Academic standards are top-notch and incorporation of faith is amazing. And when a bullying situation arose, the school stepped in immediately and nipped it in the bud. I never see that in the public schools I teach in. SMCC is a fabulous school! We provide excellent academics in a Christ-centered environment with plenty of extracurricular and service opportunities. Our students like to be involved in their communities and take an active role in doing so. They strive to do well and have big dreams. All SMCC students get accepted into college and 99-100% of them go on to college every year. They are prepared for college and do very well. Many students come back to visit SMCC as alumni with pride. It's a great place for students to learn, develop and grow. SMCC is an excellent school with staff that are caring and dedicated to helping students succeed. They also offer great athletic progams. SMCC is a school that adequately prepares its students for a college educatin and professional career. Although its rules can be argued as strict, it is these ruels that prepare its students for the professional world. By implementing such guidelines, students practice the behaviors they will be required to uphold later in life. The college counselors take a genuine concern in their students, going to great lengths to ensure their success. They are extremely knowledgeable in the majority of college aspects; if it is realized they do not know much information on a certain topic, they will immediately research the area more. The teachers take care to prepare their students for college careers, while understanding what is most important - faith and family. Should a dire circumstance occur, the teachers are understanding and willing to cooperate with the student to make the situation doable. At this school, a student is provided with many opportunities. These include French/Spanish Club, NHS, Respect Life Club, and Interact. The school as a whole, through its extracurriculars, promotes faith, service, education, and success. Being a student here has undoubtedly been beneficial. St. Mary Catholic Central is a unique environment that truly nourishes students in body, mind and spirit. Its faculty models the Catholic Christian morals that it teaches. Excellence is expected in all areas of growth. Interaction with parents is continuous and they are kept well informed. It has certainly been a great experience for our son and for us also. SMCC is a great school! They promote academics, sports, extracurricular activities AND morality in a day when morality and accountability is not in the curriculum or on the daily agenda. SMCC gives me confidence as a parent. It is like a second family. This is a 5 star school providing not only college prep courses but spiritual leadership, respect, and community service. I would without exception reccommend this school I cannot express the great deal of support that I have received from this school. From the teachers to the administrators to the students - I have felt as though everyone here is a part of my family. The College Counselors are AMAZING and have truly helped me with not only finding a great college and career, but they are also helping me with my scholarship applications. I am fully prepared for my next step - college! Very good school. Great counselors and teachers. Excellent school environment. Great for preparing children for college. Good faith based surroundings This school is so awesome! Academic, social and moral development rock at this school. Would recommend to all. Love everything about this school. Great Christian values continued to be taught at school as well as home. If you want your child to be enstilled with the fear of God send them here. SMCC provides outstanding preparation for college and beyond. We appreciate the school's focus on students' spiritual development. SMCC really does well educating the whole person. The teachers are always willing to go above and beyond. They do an excellent job preparing students for college as evidenced by their success with placement and college scholarships. The coursework is rigorous and the classes demanding, but the experience instills the kind of work ethic that will make a person successful later in life regardless of their chosen field of study and work. We have a current freshman who is thoroughly enjoying his experience at SMCC. We feel that sending him there is an outstanding investment in his future. My experience at SMCC was nothing like the reviews that likely came from parents. As a graduate of SMCC, I can only say that I have never experienced the level of bullying of students with differences, and just plain RACISM. Genuine, although at times veiled slightly, prejudice. Not only racism, but of course also prejudiced against LGBTQ, but they say that’s “okay” because they’re a Catholic school. I have never felt less supported at an institution than at this one. Genuinely not inclusive and oblivious to the gaslighting of special needs, POC, and LGBTQ students. If all you care about is your child being prepared for college, then sure send them here. But also weigh the consequences of a high school that will not support them on the path to college in any other way, and one that is VERY catholic. You’re forced to go to mass every month even if you practice a different religion. Just all around they need policy change and new leadership.

column3: Whenever I enter East high School it feels like I'm right back home. The teachers are so friendly. They are pretty much like parents to me. I mean I love my parents, but i love the teachers at East High School as well. I'm not sure why people say what they say about this school. If they just spent one day in the school and got to know the teachers and students they would know how much of a family we all are. All I really want to say is don't judge a book by its cover. My school is a good one, but lots of people don't think so... I have only been attending for 1 and a half semesters, but as a freshman I have been treated equally to all the other students. East has issues that are typical of any "inner city" school - kids who don't want to be there, kids without stable role models in their lives, or kids who have to work to support themselves/their families and thus have less energy to devote to school. In that sense, it's lower-ranked than some of the other area schools where you just don't have a high percentage students with those issues, and this is definitely reflected in things like test scores. However, if you can look beyond that, it's a FABULOUS school. Initially I was apprehensive about my child attending but four years later, I can see what a good experience it was. The teachers and staff members are so wonderful and truly want your children to succeed. The performing arts department is excellent. There are a wide variety of clubs, activities, and classes to choose from. It's a very caring environment and I'm really glad we decided to go ahead and be a part of the East "family." It's a definitely a hidden gem. I have two children attending this high school that are doing very well. The teachers truly do care about the students' success but you have to be involved as parents just like at any other school. Thur. Feb 20th my husband and I attended the girls basketball game GB East @ WDP.. Every team wants to win & we were fans for WDP. The score was on WDP side BUT every basket & good play GBE did their fans cheered them on. Also the WDP Dance put on a greet performance. The GBE fans clapped at the end. This is what sports in high school are all about. Congrats to the GREEN BAY EAST FANS.

I loved attended NRHS and you will to. As for the comments saying that the students, counselors, and teachers are horrible, this is NOT true! They are the nicest people you have ever met and they help you feel welcomed and you feel like you fit right in!! -Former Student class of 2009 This school needs a lot of help.. My children come home daily and tell me they don't feel like there learning anything. I believe something needs to be done. They teachers sometimes tell their personal business to the kids which I feel is inappropriate. I hope they get it together.

column1: The high school nurse is ansolutely horrid. My child has severe anxiety and panic attacks. The Elementary School Nurse was wonderful with my daughter. The high school nurse turned her away and said, "I can't do anything for you!" Whoever heard of this??? A medical professional turning a child away??? Anyone with a mental problem can walk into any hospital and they will NEVER turn them away. So I immediately withdrew my child and I am homeschooling her.

column3: My thoughts on my highschool are great. We moved into the community 2 years ago and since then have enjoyed so much that the town has to offer. One of the best things the town has to offer is a great school that provides me with great education and a one of a kind staff body!! I have made lots of friends and am thankful to live in a town that takes education serriously The principal, Dr. Boyd, is helpful and concerned with student performance. They have a handful of teachers who care and are involved in the success of students. They offer a limited selection of student engagement of activities. The only challenge is that they support a lot of Christian initiatives, which can be a little uncomfortable if you are not of a Christian faith. They do offer student tutoring, which is a fabulous program!

column1: Cummings High School was the best place for my children. This school allows children to be children. This school supports each and every child that walks through the door no matter the socioeconomic status. My children were at Graham High and prejudice there was just to high. Teacher at Cummings are willing to work with parents. Administration seem concern when a parent and a teacher has a difference of opinion. They work to try and solve the problem. Many people talk about the gang and drug at Cummings School but have you went and seen the school for yourself. I am sure it is there but no more than the other area high schools. This year alone 36 seniors were able to obtain over 2 million dollars in scholarships. Yes, I believe Cummings is second to none. I would challenge those that don't believe to go and observe the school when school is in session and watch how caring goes on this school from staff, students and volunteers. My school is Cummings High School. I have taught there for over ten years. I have my master's degree in teaching and National Board Certification. You will find treasure in the staff of this school!!!! Each and every teacher wants to be at this school and they are there to see that each student is successful!!! As many principals have come and gone, you will find that the teachers here have interviewed multiple times for their positions. You will not find a more qualified or caring staff anywhere in the state. I went to this school and I have intentionally made sure that my children will NEVER attend this school..I refuse to move anywhere near this district! I watched kids beat and bully other kids when I attended! I seen a boy have his head pounded into the concrete at the bus lot by another boy. The teacher of my math class refused to teach the class because of disruptive kids in class. He did not send them out he just failed everyone including the ones who wanted to learn! The principal did not care! This school needs to have police officers walking the halls constantly! HORRIBLE HORRIBLE SCHOOL! For your kids safety I would not send them here look anywhere but here! While the school isn't that great quality-wise, the teachers are usually not there for the money and are there to help. Also, the lack of bullying here is amazing especially since I was constantly bullied for having Autism back in Northern Guilford Middle.

column3: I feel that LCHS has some serious work to do. Academics are in serious disrepair. Though there are some great teachers, they just aren't supported by administration of ex-football coaches. It's a running joke among students that it really doesn't matter what you put on your class selection sheet. It WILL be wrong. and you will NOT be able to take the elective classes you want if you are in any honors classes at all. They brag about all the STEM classes they have; this is a complete joke. They have a drafting class that they call CAD and while they do offer calculus, it is not AP. The only AP class they offer is English 12. They brag about their STEM oriented robotics team. Well, even though it requires thousands of dollars to run effectively, they get $0 from the school and must operate with sub-par equipment bought from harbor freight 10 years ago. The same is true for all the less revered sports teams. The band also receives $0 from the school. However, LCHS does have a shop! Too bad there's no jobs in hand machining! They teach no industrial automation or computer skills at all. This school does not prepare students for college and it definitely doesn't prepare them for life. this school is horrible I wouldnt advise anyone to attend this school I went here the year 2010 worst experience ever I was told by a teacher/coach that it would be best for me to basically fail and get into the so called early graduation and that happened to me and the teacher/coach left for a head coach job and I found myself with no diploma but hey GED as they say good enough diploma is better than nothing.. I graduated in 1994. This school is a joke. Lucky me I escaped that town and state. I feel sorry for students who attend any public or private school in that town. Kids google is your friend. You will need to teach yourself how to properly speak and write. It took me years to undo what that town and school system did to me. I graduated this school in 2011. This school was wonderful. The teacher and staff were friendly and they helped students. I had a wonderful four years at this school and ninth grade academy.

column1: I agree that the administration at FDA II is very disrespectful to teachers. The principal could serve as a poster boy for what egomania looks like in practice. Grades are inflated on a regular basis and students' uniforms are of more importance than their work ethic. This school operates by looking good on the surface with virtually nothing of substance to back up their removal from the bottom of the barrel. The SQR and report card grade are highly suspect. As a current parent of FDA II my daughter is in middle school and this is her second year at FDA II. I am very happy with the teachers involvement with the parents. I find that pupil path is great the teachers reach out to me via pupil path, text, e-mail, telephone. The teachers are engaged in their students progress and my daughter has improved every year in this school. I have had my problems with middle school administration, but after contacting the principle these issues are resolved. I haven't had the terrible experience with the principle that other have had on this post. If I had to say one bad thing about the school, they need to get rid of the co-location why are 4,5 graders in a school housing middle and high school students. These children should be in an environment with younger students, not tweens and teens. I think the school would be better if they replaced the current middle school Dean, he is not on his game and he doesn't return telephone calls. That is not a good way to keep parents engaged. Other then that I am happy with the school and I would recommend it to any parent who is looking for a good school for their child. I'm scared to go to this school! The students are not serious about class AT ALL. if i were to tell you all the problems that are wrong with this school i would be here until the sun supernovaed and killed me . I've been going to this hell hole for 6 years now and i'm in the 11 grade right now . I can say with 100% certainty that if it wasn't for me and other selected student bring up the test scores , the school would have been shut down . the principal is a condensing childish man who lacks any of all respect for his teachers which has lead to several of the best teachers leaving over the years . this being the case my grades really suffered in 7th and 8 th grade . worst school ever , please don't come here if you care about our children. teacher don't even really punish the bad kids that make up 95 percent of all the students making learning very hard. in some classes 40 of the 45 minutes of instruction go to kids just talking and cracking jokes so even if you want to learn good luck trying to here the teachers.

column3: My daughter went to this school last year.I was very disappointed so much we moved only after 6 weeks of school. I was not allowed to eat lunch with my child, the school requires uniforms for students, but the teachers get to wear what they want to.The staff are all very rude and disrespectful to parents.Parents are not allowed to speak to other students while on school property even if the other students make the first gesture of a hand shake or saying "Hey".When I was withdrawing my daughter, the staff was like "WHATEVER".This school doesn't welcome outsiders. My daughter went to school ,I withdrew her from there after 6 weeks. This school is far below the schools in Georgia.My daughter was doing the same work in 12th here that she did in 10th grade in Ga.The staff and teachers are direspectful to parents.My daughter came home crying everyday because she was unhappy.I won't recommend this school to anyone. The town doesn't like outsiders either. My son is a sophomore this year and I really wanna talk about the sophomore teachers. Some of them are nice, while the others are totally the OPPOSITE!!! My son told me that the teachers had bad attitudes towards him. I am not saying which teacher, but I think that teacher knows who I'm talking about. You are not treating my kids right, maybe others too. Different attitudes towards every students, not treating them the same! ( I believe my kids are not the only one) You should be regret for being a teacher cause being a teacher is such a waste for you! A teacher shouldn't be lazy for doing his work, not responsible, bad attitudes and bad teaching skills . You can say what you want about the quality of the education at this school; but, I graduated from Lincoln with less than steller grades and went to College in Maryland. I completed a four-year degree in Aeronautics in just over two years and graduated with a 3.94 GPA. I am currently finishing up my Masters and have a 4.00 Graduate School GPA. Like most things in life, if you want a good education, you can get it. Lincoln is a small, close knit community and I love being here! They will offer it, whether or not you get it is up to you! Lincoln Elementary, Drew Middle, and Lincoln High Schools are great schools! I would recommend these schools for anyone. Lincoln is a great community. This school is a slum. The teachers are lazy and stop class to mingle flirtatiously. The teachers only want money. They don't care about the students, and on a daily basis I've personally heard them shout "I hate this place!" 80% of the classrooms have cockroaches in them. Most of the restrooms are out of order. The teachers and principals are all rude and spiteful. They have no respect for anyone. The teachers and principals have no problem targeting one kid. 99% Of the students here have no morals, they have no respect for themselves, muchless for others. There are a lot of racial aggression, disrespectful attitudes, bullying, drama, and generally unfair judgments. The only thing they care about is money, which is why they promote the football team. The teachers go easy on the football team members, and they can do anything. The teachers and students here are moral less, wanna be rich people, who lack ANY southern hospitality. If this is in the "TOP 50 SCHOOLS IN THE NATION" Then this nation has gone to hell. Please do NOT place your child here. Place them somewhere at least HALF WAY decent. I think this a great school because the teachers keep us motivated and so does the principles and they also have a lot of extra clubs, groups, and sportd that the students could join. And its not always a fight going on.

column1: Honestly, TF north is the complete opposite it's motto. No one is hardworking, the average gpa is well under 3.0. No one is caring, there is either a fight or a huge altercation everyday. No one is respectful, I witness atleast two teachers per day get cursed out and disrespected. Finally, No one is responsible, there is a list put up every year for how much money students owe for missing books or temporary student id's and I've seen some students that owe hundreds sometimes even close to a thousand dollars. With all of that being said i wouldn't recommend any aspiring 8th graders out there to come to tf north. I am a current student at T.F. North and throughout my 3 years of attending this school, I have come to realize that this not a perfect school, but then again, is there such a thing? Every school has it's own issues and T.F. North is no exception. However, it is an exceptional school with some great teachers. I've been in Honors and AP classes my whole time here and the majority of my instructors have been amazing and extremely helpful. Many of them will even stay after school if a student needs extra help. The behaviors of the other students are of no concern to me as I know why I am there, to learn. I am currently a student attending TF North High School And Overall, I would say that it's a horrible school and I would not recommend anyone to send their child there. They do not stick to their motto . Everything at the school now is so negative. The staff do not care to help the troubled students whom are struggling with a few classes. The counselors are also horrible because you cannot talk to them about the classes you are having troubles in nor can you talk to them about anything personal because they would also put you down and make you feel worse than you already may feel. The overall environment and atmosphere of the school is very negative and unhappy . I hate that I even attend this school . I wish I can leave or either finish the classes online rather than participating in a stereotypical environment. Need to add the avid class and the trio program need more after school programs love the parent pta need to help the special needs kids more with college is or other options love the freshman house good school overall This is the worst school you could possibly send your child to! My sister went here and always complain that the kid will always pick on her and qhen she told a teacher they did nothing about it. I went to this school back then in 2010 and I was bullied so hard by a lot of teachers and students are barely even passed algebra the algebra teacher failed me for the whole year I wouldn't recommend this school to nobody if you want your kids to succeed in life keep them out of TF North barely the deans even care about anybody all that they do is just encourage the rough housing and barely the police officers would do anything you've been warned keep your kids away from this school

column3: A Great School! They have fantastic teachers that really care about their students and wonderful programs. Oh, and an Awesome Academic League/Decathlon Team! Southwest high school may be though to be a "underdog" school but it is not, because its the best school. It may not have the best infrastructure or very fancy equipment yet it has some thing better: safe and tranquil environment, caring teacher and student that will provide the best high school experience. remember once a raider always a raider.

column1: QCHS is a wonderful school filled with caring and qualified professionals. My child has only been attending this school for one semester and I have seen much more improvement/self confidence. He participates in the wonderful FFA program and most of his teachers take the time to work with him after school as well. I think QCHS has a lot to offer in the perfoming arts department as well as the athletic department. I highly reccommend if you are looking for a smaller environment with an excelling staff/community. My personal experience with QCHS was wonderful. I attended all four years at this high school without complaint. I felt connected with my teachers and classmates and was able to participate in several extracurricular activities. I began collage the fall after graduation and managed to graduate with two bachelor degrees and my masters degree by age 22, this largely in part to the several dual credit classes QCHS offered at the time. My experience at Queen Creek was back when the school was 3A and had a smaller class size, which could have contributed to my positive experience. My brother, who recently graduated felt he had a positive experience as well, despite having been less engaged in academics and extracurricular activities. Best school ever been there for 3 years now the teachers and students are very helpful and are caring... Best school ever i got 3 kids going there and they seem to get better education everyday they come home. I am a teacher at Queen Creek High School and i think that the school is awesome all the teachers from my point of view are helpful and caring the kids that i have always positive and willing to work. I attended Queen Creek Middle School and then High School until my sophomore year. At this point, I could not stand the way my teachers taught (or the lack of teaching at all), the politics within the sports teams among coaches, and the lack of college preparation. I switched to Perry High School and had an amazing junior and senior year with teachers who caused me to be engaged in my learning and was enrolled in the AVID program there. I wish parents could attend QCHS for one day and see the miserable conditions and lack of administration. Nov 6 2012. Great story about the students at QCHS! Impressive kids! I hope the school board, parents & local government take notice and recognize all of those students! JSM Seattle WA I am very disappointed with this school, I would give it an overall rating of below average from the education to the athlectics through the administration. This school has provided less than what I want for my children in all areas. There is a lack of professionalism and character as well as ethics, honesty and consistancy from several of the faculty, staff and administration. I do have to say that there are some good teachers here and the overall student body is average or above but that is heavily outweighed by the negative environment and unwelcomed, biased attitude exhibited by faculty and staff. I would not reccommend this school or athletic program to any parent. Parents if your student is an athlete DO NOT SEND THEM TO QC! Politics will always be a part of High School sports, but QC is the worst I have ever experienced. I was a high school athlete in the 1970's and my two older children where also HS athletes who attended high schools and played sports in Chandler, Idaho, and Utah. The favoritism, lack of ethics and honesty is over the top at QC in multiple sports . This is not being posted by a disgruntled parent who has children that sit the bench, all of my children are and have been multi sport starters. Athletics at QC are bad, really really bad. Worst High School Ever! This school has teachers and administrators with very little integrity! Its poorly managed and I wouldn't recommend it to any one who wants their child to have a good High School experience. I had 2 children enrolled here and it was awful. My son played sports and my daughter was involved with several student programs. Find a different school You'll be glad later! Unfortunately in the last year the high school has really diminished in quality. They lost 30 plus teachers last year and the couple good administrators they had. Very sad to see it tank so badly so quickly. New leadership needs to take over at the superintendency and then the high school. Hard to do when the school board has a member related to the high school principal who is a main part of the problem. Ignorance abounds. Expect staff affiliated with this school to make incorrect assumptions based on their lack of knowledge and understanding of their students' situations. Heavy bias and discrimination found at this school. Lack of communication, and a strong persuasion to remove parental involvement during these critical, formative years. I am a parent of a Senior at QCHS, and I cannot say enough good things about the school! My daughter has attended there since she started High School, and it was the best choice that we have ever made! The teachers are very involved, the sports program is wonderful, the administration is helpful, and I am amazed by how smoothly things run over all! Like all schools, there can be hiccups with schedules at the start of the year, etc. However, the issues get addressed quickly, and resolved. The programs that they offer are amazing, and growing every year! I am very proud to have my child attend such a great High School, and I will be sending my youngest 2 there as well! GO BULLDOGS! This year has by far been the worst. My son is a Junior and has credit shortage. I have emailed three different counselors for a meeting since the school year began with no response. Quality teachers are hit or miss here. My son went during lunch to ask his teacher a quick math question and he wasn't in his class..Being desperate for help he went to his former math teacher who told him he wasn't his teacher anymore, and walked away. He's had several of these types of experiences here. I have also never seen a football team (JV) so against each other and willing to step on each other. There is no brotherhood here. The JV coaches do a great job of tearing the kids down, point fingers, and forget to build them back up. They are a huge part of why there is no bond there. Incredibly disappointing. The wrestling program is very similar. Everybody is against each other. It makes no sense. You're a team! The coach let's chaos happen. Fights, stealing, and worse. Athletics are a big part of high school for my son. Wishing we had a rewind button to choose differently back in his freshman year. I foresee nothing but disaster for this school if it continues to misplace its priorities and obsess over standardized testing performance and state rankings. Quality curriculum is being replaced by a costly pre-packaged program that enforces teaching to the test. Great teachers are forced replace their passion for their subject and for education with the limited, often ignorant ideals and values pervasive in the ultra conservative Queen Creek community. This has resulted in ever increasing turnover rates which will eventually leave only those mediocre drones, teachers that are willing to ignore their better judgment, as well as the true goal of their career, for the comfort of complacency. QCHS a a great school with an accepting environment and spirit abounding. This school exceedingly holds up its motto, "high achievement in a caring environment". We are extremely pleased with the education and experience our kids are getting at Queen Creek. The social studies department in particular has been fantastic and we greatly appreciate the weekly emails to parents Having been here for all 4 years of high school, I have tried to like it. When I went through a difficult time, my concerns and issues were brushed off from counseling and teachers alike. There is no control in classrooms and the teachers mostly have you teach yourself. They say degrading things to students and expect respect in return. A 10. I am so happy we moved to Queen Creek so my children can attend this school.

column3: I just graduated from here and I loved it there. Most of the teachers genuinely care about their students. The only thing is I am not a big fan of the principal. He is always on a power trip it seems, especially with the new building. He also tends to play favorites. However, the administrators are a big supporter of the sports and the arts. There is always an administrator at every single school event including band concerts and theater performances. It's an all-around good place to go to school. Principal is horrible. Teachers are alright. The curriculum could be better, I went to school in NC and when I moved here, I was ahead of my class because the curriculum here is not that great. In some classes I had to teach myself much of the curriculum because the teacher would not teach it well. Its an okay school socially, but for educational standards, its meager. This school is not one that I would pick if I had the choice of where I received an education. The teachers, for the most part, are okay. Many are more worried about outside school activities than in school learning. One reason for mediocre teachers is that they are here for one reason: sports. While the building is new and nice, a new structure does not mean the insides of the structure are new and nice as well. All in all this is an average school with average teachers and we are all just trying to surf by.

column1: Our son transferred here after ten years at Catholic school. He enrolled in honors english and history and other college prep courses for his sophomore year. The teachers were so attentive and motivating and really made his year positive and was a much better choice than our private high school ST. joes that we left. The administration is very involved too and I would recommend the honors program to incoming students Great little school with a big school feel. Academics and athletics are both great at this school. Students are eager to learn and staff is attentive to student needs. Rigorous course work and college prep for those seeking advanced classes.

column3: I have had two children graduate from Roosevelt although I did not grow up here myself. I think the district has offered many opportunities for the kids to grow as individuals eventhough the budget was very tight. They are able to work wonders to still offer higher level (although not as many as we would like) classes while maintaining art and music. This is a real balancing act and it is difficult in an economically challenged area. My children were prepared by some very good teachers and were accepted at a very selective school. One is an honors student at that school and seems to have been very well prepared and we have high hopes for the other as well (she is just starting). The principal was very good and involved in many activities of the students. We expect the administration to remain positive. Sports were stressed a bit too much. I’ve had an overall great experience at RHS. I do wish that more AP classes were offered, but with recent curriculum changes the addition of more challenging coursework is more possible than ever. There is a family-like environment here more than any other school I have attended. The teachers encourage students to do their best but still have fun, and I believe there is a place for everyone. Very happy with this high school so far!

column1: This school is wonderful.They take time with each student to make sure they understand the materials taught. They work fast but only as fast as the students can process. The dicipline is minimal because it is not required, most students get along well and there is minimal if any breaking of school rules

column3: First of all, may I say that the principles do not care about their students. For instance, if anyone accuses you of breaking a rule, you'll be suspended without question. It does not matter whether if you have a solid alibi that proves you could not have broken said rule. 90% of the teachers do not care about their students, and pick favorites. This really explains why test scores have continually dropped over the past few years. There is basically no parent involvement at this school. Bullying is awful, and most of the bullies are teachers or teacher's pets (which explains why those kids are never written up.)

column1: This school is TERRIBLE! i have had the worst years of my life going to coventry schools. i would not recomend it to anyone. Teachers dont care and dont have much intrest in there students learning, kids are getting into fights every week, and drug possesion is very high in this school. Most kids just walk out of the school during the day, and of course none of the teachers notice it. If you looking for failure this is the perfect school for you! I would say overall it was a 5-star experience. My child was accepted at a prestigious university with a considerable scholarship and entering as a second semester freshman with the ACT credits earned from AP course enrollment. column3: It wasn't helpful in my educational experience for college or life. I had always been a deep lucid person for intellectualism knowledge, yet most variety subjects weren't taught at the high school. Nothing about philosophy, psychology, politics, society, deeper science (emphasis for anything more than the intro to; being on human, tech, or creation), history, engineering, technology, or other languages. Not even the freedom of many different electives of your compassionate choice. Terrible lunch foods, and choice of club involvement/participation. Pretty awful. I'd say just awful, but the school had a few good things going for it. Like, 2 good things. A few teachers (as of right now) are alright but some are retiring soon, and the bullying isn't extremely rampant but its still very clearly there (although there's nothing the school can do about it).If you decide to have your kids attend this high school, just choose a different high school. column1: Im a student at cousino and i DO NOT recommend this school. The are absolutely no extracolicular activities and this is not a school which focuses on learning due to the budget cuts everything is getting thrown out; things like the school store, sports teams,and clubs as mentioned before. Cousino does not prepare students for the ACT and it is overall hoorrible. the school does not let its students know what to do to suceed. As a former student of Cousino (recent, class of 2008) I am very unimpressed. Most of the teachers are under-qualified, rude and care more about themselves and their paychecks then they do the students and the educations they are providing (however, this is common across the entire Warren Con district). I will say that like in every situation there are those teachers that really are wonderful but it is not the majority here. Several teachers, when I was there, were about 5 years PAST when they should have retired and their attitudes and technological lag showed it. Much of the staff, from admins to principals, are rude and incompetent; with as many people and teachers out of jobs right now Warren Con could certainly do a LOT better. With the, in my opinion, incredibly high salaries these teachers make we should have to best of the best and not the friend of a friend that needed a job. Please note this is not just Cousino it is the district as a whole! Come on Warren Con, Step it up!!! I am a current African American student here, this is one of the worse schools ever, and i've attended Detroit Public School System. I wouldn't recommend this school to my worse enemy. On a daily basis I deal with bullying and racism. Everyday I deal with teachers who don't teach, all they do is be on the computers and their phones. Not to mention how disrespectful they are. Almost everyday I have to come I cry because, I can't take anymore. This school makes me want to drop out period. Cousino High School lacks leadership. There are some very good teachers but the rest know that there is no standard to meet and no accountability. Counseling for post high school education is non existent. Sports programs need improvement, football program is on respirator, baseball is on low end of MAC Division(Gold), dance team lacking a good coach, as are most sports at Cousino, cheerleading focuses on on competition and not school events. The"activity" fee is also going up every year,have to pay for uniforms,one way bus to event or no buses. If your child has any talents that need nurtured and expanded this is not the place, no college connections for recruiting do your research on MHSAA. Students DO NOT come first at Cousino. Dress code selectively enforced, Principal appears weak and afarid to take charge of staff and students. Cousino cares mostly about anyone who is able to get all A's or are on a sports team. The assistant principals contradict each other, the principal is a figure head who like the AP's contradicts everything. The school treats CPC and Bucher students with the upmost respect but treats anyone in the WCSPA program terribly to the point of excluding it from any announcements or information to students in the program. It however welcomes any scholarships earned in the program as Cousino's personal accomplishments. The school treats transfer students terribly and does not help work with them at all. The counselors only help the students who hound them down because they just don't care. Though some teachers are outstanding most hand out a packet of notes go over them once and then move on until the test. The teachers that are near retirement or get cut due to budgetary problems openly talk badly over the school and its policies just showing how much they really care about the school and how much respect they actually have for anyone. As a parent, I am extremely pleased with Cousino High School. I get the feeling the last couple negative comments were submitted by the same disgruntled parent. The teachers are caring, the secretaries are attentive, and the administrators have been extremely helpful. The athletic teams are perennially at the top of conference. It is refreshing to be involved with a school focused on academics yet supportive of athletics and the arts. I feel very welcomed by the Patriot community. It is really a shame this has become a forum for the few disgruntled parents that do not accurately reflect the parent and student sentiment. I cannot say enought about Cousino High School. The administration and staff are truly a class act - engaging, dynamic, and personable. One of the better schools in the area. I only went here for one year but when I left to go to my old school I was like 'Why did I switch schools, should have stayed at Cousino.' The recent 1 star reviews are inaccurate to me, when I went there my counselor helped me bring my grades up and helped me become less shy.. he was very caring. It wasn't like he said 'Welcome to Cousino, enjoy it' and then I never heard from him again. He called me down to his office several times throughout the year to check my progress. So for the most part, the staff really cares. The only cons I can think of is it's a confusing school when you first arrive, I got lost quite a bit but then you start to know the way. The only con is it was very crowded in the halls when I was there, which makes you late to class sometimes. School is only one floor though, which I liked. So not a perfect school, but a good choice in Warren. I have reviewed many high schools for my son and I found that COUSNIO HIGH SCHOOL is the best you find some negative things but the positive override the bad we as parents have to teach /remind our children what they attended sschool for. My son who was a little shy became a social butterfly. The teachers are very concerned about the students the teachers. Parents and students can keep track of grades daily. Parents can contact the teachers through email, phone calls and other options. Teachers are available before and after school for help with students The parents group are awesome I NEVER seen parents work so hard for a school before. I love this school and love being evolved!!!! GO PATRIOTS! !!!!TOGETHER WE WILL! !!!!!!!! Absolutely not. Being an educator myself if over 20 years, I would NOT recommend this school if you can avoid it.

column3: for all the people who think these schools are bad...visit some other schools, and you will find out how good these schools actually are! My kids received an excellent education in Waxahachie! Of course it isn't perfect, no place is, but trust me, it's much better than other places! Im a former student and would like to mention that I was very poorly prepared for college. Particularly in the area of science. When I took my first chemistry class I truly realized how little I learned about science in high school. This school only cares about its scores on standardized testing and athletics. As a parent, I care about academics, but I also care about the environment in the school. I have been pleased with both. WHS offers more rigorous classes for those wanting more through the Global High School if extra curricular isn't a priority. If you are looking for a supreme band program - WHS is the place. The director is well respected by students, staff and parents and gets the kids to want to do their best. The new Superintendent has some great programs that will be implemented in 2015-2016 to add even more quality and variety to the school district. I've been impressed with all of the teachers at this school. They do care and want our kids to do well. The key is for parents to get involved. Don't expect someone else to raise your kids. Be in partnership with the school for the greatest success. My son is very happy at WHS and enjoys school every day. He finds his courses challenging and that his lessons are engaging. I appreciate all that WHS does to make this campus a great place for students!

column1: Because the school allows other students to do what they want and the school is just completed terriable I was there for a couple of months but the experience is real. The teachers don't force you to do anything, the push you and encourage you to do your best. It's follow yourself and do good no matter what else happens or fail doing nothing at all. This school over stresses their students and pile work on them. this school is horrible, bugs and rodents run through the halls and the pipes all burst too often, flooding is normal here. DO NOT SEND YOU CHILD HERE.

column3: Better communication than the jr. high. Nice cafeteria with alot of healthy options. Teachers seem genuinely concerned with the academic welfare of the students. TONS of extra-curricular activities. I have nothing but great things to say about Cypress Woods. My daughter graduated from there this year, which she was apart of the first four year class of CyWoods. I believe Mrs. Sue McGowan showed the very best leadership and spirit that I have ever witness and it shows in the result of Cy Woods having the most successful and largest graduating class in Texas history. Kudos to the staff and Mrs. McGowan. the school is way too big to function. The starff is uncaring and rude. The rules are ridiculous and they do not trust their students. thats is all. Students who play sports get special privileges that the remaining students do not get. Athletes laugh at assignments and tests, knowing that a complaint to the administration will get them free grades. The other students are demoralized by the disparity, leaving it to the staff to attempt to gloss over the incredible unfairness. I moved to Cypress from California and chose to go to Cy-woods purely based on everything I saw on the internet. It had a good Greatschools rating, many opportunities for scholarships, and was a new school. However after coming here I realized that athletics are the only thing that matter at this school. It's sad that star athletes get more recognition than star scholars! I had a few great teachers and a few not so great teachers. Many teachers who are also coaches put more time into their sport than teaching the students of their academic course! All in all, Cypress Woods is an okay school that focuses too much on sports! If you have the next NFL player in training or just think you do, then Cy Woods is the school for you! At Cy Woods you will meet other parents reliving their glory days through their kids, and don't forget those cheer moms! Do you have a student who enjoys music?Great, they have marching band for the football games.Oh, your child plays guitar?I'm sorry they don't have guitar for football.Cy woods also offers off season football such as track, and basketball.Cy woods also offers girls sports to give the girls something to do when they are not cheering for the football team!The school is about a 1/4 mile long and has close to 4000 students. This gives the football players practice with the "5 minute" drill called - beat the clock to class or get suspended. 3 tardies=1 absence. Absences= lost funding. Lost funding=no administrative bonuses.I promise your child will be late.I've been to back to school night.I know the school well, and it's going to happen.This school is too big, & the administrators don't know what they're doing.The focus is only on sports. Look at all your options, and know your kid.Don't rule out HISD.They have technology and music schools with no sports. I currently go to Cy Woods. I'm from the Class of 2013, and can honestly say I do love it. My graduating year we have had a lot of changes, yet there are a lot of good people who are entering to keep Wood s legacy going strong. We have always been one of the most competitive schools in the district, we always have a great turn out to games, and most of the time we have a lot of victories. Don't criticize the school based on your child's one experience; there is more to it than that! I just moved here, and I hate how large the student body is. The school feels impersonal and the lack of respect other students have for adults is ridiculous. This school has a big student body and it gets hard to get from class to class. I went to the A.P.s office and filled out a repirt because i was getting bullies and he said i would be in within the next 2 days. Three months later i was not called in and i went in and asked if i was ever going to be called in and the receptionist said i should write an email asking when i was going to be called in. I feel like the principle here is more concerned about the extra carricular activities than acctualy learning. Even the school lunches suck. Some of the teachers are nice and all the others are just rude. I'm sure Cy-Woods is an excellent school. I gave it Bad because of my personal experience with trying to communicate with the "Leaders" of the school. I'm still waiting for a call back from last year where I left a message on the after hours recording. I left one his morning as well. Matters that require urgent attention are not dealt with, they are brushed under the rug. I asked the school directly to please call me, her mother, when any calls need to be made regarding her. That has never happened in 2 years. No one other than myself or her father are to make or sign anything pertaining to her.On the plus side, I think the teachers have been very good with her and working hard to help her academically, as she has a learning disability and requires special teaching in some areas. The principal at this school is awful. When confronted evidence and an omission of guilt with an unethical teacher he did NOTHING! In addition to the lack of ethics and concerns with the principal's handling of issues, this is a mega school of roughly 4000 kids. The kids are processed like cattle. With so many kids at the school, don't expect any individual attention or support. I don't recommend this school, from the administration to the teachers. AWFUL all the way around! They are manipulating core classes to "Teach the Test" to score big on standardizations. No quality; just quality numbers on stats to make admin look good. Great teachers, administration, and culture of trying your hardest, and puttIngram a litter extra effort. average, nothing much. most reviews are as old as the dinosaurs so :) My son recently graduated from Cy Woods. It took us half an hour to find him because they did not allow any students to have their phones because they were scared to call in an air strike. That was the dumbest decision that has been made by the school. They say their for 2 hours just listening to names. I am a current student at Cypress Woods, and this school does not take an effective approach to making good citizens. They influence their own beliefs onto students and don't have many good rules. They don't trust their students. Some teachers here are really good, but some just shouldn't be teachers. Many of the individuals complaining about this school have clearly never been to an underprivileged, or even normal High School. It's quite an exceptional place. A culture of high achievement is encouraged but not forced, and besides the football team, most if not all extracurriculars are extremely impressive, most notably the Band, Choir, UIL Academic, and especially Computer Science groups. Quality teachers with a few quite notable exceptions. It of course, like every well off school has the obnoxious snobby popular kid group, that have been known to cause trouble, but that's a given with a school with this size and status. It has the typical upsides and downsides of a large school. The student clubs are supportive and progressive, but not obnoxiously so. The AP classes and programs are all high quality, but vary wildly in how they prepare. Some AP classes and teachers teach the actual subject extremely well, but don't prepare for the test, and vice versa. I have family all over this area, and that have been in 8 of the CFISD High Schools. By far, we seem to all agree that Cypress Woods is currently the best. I write this as a graduating Senior that has experienced all of the ups and downs, and even the craziness of the COVID rules. The biggest downside of the school is crowded hallways, and somewhat strange CFISD school issued Chromebook rules. But if that's all you can really leverage against a school... well, you can definitely do worse. The feeder schools for Cy-Woods are exemplary, especially Sampson Elementary and Spillane Middle. Overall, this school is an incentive to live in the area for sure, and is most likely one of the top public High Schools in the State. I have twins in the 10th grade here, and I couldn't be happier. The teachers and administrators have high expectations for the students to put their all into whatever they do, and it shows. The extracurriculars here, whether athletic, academic, or arts related, are highly successful. So many schools focus only on athletics, but at CWHS, just as much glory is given to the UIL and arts programs, which is one of the main reasons I sent my kids here. We moved to the area specifically to send our kids here, and I'm very glad we did. When it comes to the teachers a lot of them are nice to the students and good but some of them dont even know how to even teach. the amount of girls that get dresscoded in one day for the most unrevealing shirts is out of this world. The APs scream in your face and are always rude, and students get into trouble when they have done nothing wrong.

column1: I am a student at Elmira. I love this school, all the teachers are awesome, and though I wish there were more academic oppertunities I understand that the buget cannot afford this. I admit that I am biased because I go here but I really do like it. GO FALCONS!!!! Good school but we have lost so many electives. Our kids need a core education but they need variety to make them well rounded people in life. I appreciate the staff, they do a great job. The rest of the community needs to realize they can not keep voting down bond measures and expect things to improve. its our community, our kids and our future. We need to invest in all of that, and not just financially. The admin for our school has changed positively in the past few years, now let's support them. Stil alot of drinking and partying. The school has cracked down a little on the athletes but not enough. This could be a great school if we stay on the right track. Much improvement in the last 3 years, but still need more.

column3: Most disorganized baseball program EVER! The coaches have zero respect for parents, or their time. The website is never updated, I get my info from the opponents website. Love everything else about the school. Mountain Range High School, is a very good school. But I think the way they handle situations are not handled correctly. Over all, it is a pretty good school. Also, I think the teachers should start doing extra credit, and should let students retake test they got bad scores in. Teachers here are amazing and go above and beyond no accountability, principle treats staff terrible and should have been replaced long ago. This could be a great school ,they have some great staff but everyone is out on their own, no bringing a community together. Sad -district needs to dig into things and look closely. As a community member I have had nothing but positive interactions with Mountain Range 3 of 10. A few teachers are good. I still attend MRHS, I haven’t had any problems personally here. The school is good practice, it sets students up to be successful and to look beyond towards college. There are many choices and classes to take, teachers are intelligent and respectful (mostly). Horrible experience. I cannot begin to describe the institutionalized racism that goes on here. From students and staff alike This school is nice for academic work but is kind of crowded or some people can be rude. This is a newer and very big school. It has an amazing sports facility with more than 1 feild. Its actually a very nice facility. There are some good teachers, but I haven't seen anyone really great. There are a few counsilers that go above and beyond, but I don't think they receive much support from the principal. They also don't hold these kids responsible for their actions. There seems to be no enforcement of attendance and no structure for discipline problems. I have tried to become involed or volunteer my time or anything and haven't received a response at all. The student body seems to ditch class very often and they all hang out at the park down the street. No one does anything about it. We are moving our student to a different high school. It's a shame, it's a beautiful facility, the school of business is great. But it stops there, the sports teams aren't very good. Attendance is horrible, drugs are everywhere, and all the staff blame others, if they care at all. Maybe a new principal and some intervention from the district would help. It has such potential. We are completely disapointed and our time here was a waste. The drop out rate for this school is climbing. I'm stunned that no one sees this and intervenes. I plan to write a letter to the district, but I don't think it will matter. If you have another option then send your kids to that instead of here.

column1: Lack of help by staff. Very few staff are helpful. They tell you what you want to hear as a parent but no actions behind those words. If it wasnt so late in the year , id think about switching school districts this year. But i will say my son wont be going to marshall next year. Please do your homework before putting your child in this school district. I'm sick of schools ignoring issues until they're huge. The dress code... Wait, is there one? I'm shocked at how kids dress. Pants hanging down, shirts that show stomach. Teach them how to behave at a job, prepare them for being an adult. I learned that my teachers were my future references and to behave like I would at a job. Sad to see how terrible it's gotten and I see little hope for the future. Stop caring so much about test scores and teach them respect and integrity. I would rate my experience as negative. Especially with regards to the school's response to bullying. The administration did nothing about many awful cases of bullying that went on while I was in school, and they knew about a lot of them. It seemed like a huge problem among the younger kids after I graduated too. The guidance as far as preparing for college was weak as well. The only redeeming qualities this school had were the teachers. Most of them were quality instructors and a few really went above and beyond to help their students. One of the teachers at this school was an important mentor to me throughout my high school education and helped me more with college readiness than anybody else. Great school, best school experience my son has had. Like a private school experience in a public school. There is something here for every kid. We are so lucky here in Marshall. I was concerned to be moving my kid to another school, but I didn't need to be. Great school!

SHS is amazing. Everyone is so friendly. i had no friends before my 10th grade year, and now i can pretty much talk to anyone i pass in the halls. Seminary teachers are amazing and we have great school pride. At SHS the teachers really push us to do our best and will do anything for us. my math teacher in 10th grade stayed until about 5 o'clock every night to help us learn the new common core better. Everyone at SHS is commited to excelence. there are so many good and so little of the bad. We have great teachers and not so great teachers, but that is every school. Secondly, the school is a mix between high schoolers and middle schoolers(which in my opinion causes conflict between the two.)The activities are very limited and boring.Finally, the cafeteria food is disgusting and chaotic. It has so much potential - good kids (for the most part), decent facilities - but the leadership is more afraid of people "feeling bad" than developing and promoting actual successes by it's students (loves to promote the wonders of the administration, though). Try to find a posted listing of the Honor Roll. Or mentions of awards and recognitions kids other than the basketball team have received. Definitely a demotivating experience for both kids and parents. I'm a recent alumni from the school and I graduated top 15, had a decent experience overall. It's what you make of it. Students are different every year so you really can't judge them, the younger ones are often immature and many students come from lower socioeconomic classes. The staff is aware of this and do their best to tailor a comfortable and engaging learning environment for them. The students really need a good role model who they can look up to, trust or inspire.Unfortunately, one of the teachers many troubled students trusted was not invited to come back. This infuriated many people and I can honestly say, ruined morale. A lot of the older staff is running out of patience with the administration and this makes them less enthusiastic to teach. You can walk in and literally see how burnt out and tired all the teachers are. Food wise, the food is mediocre. Occasionally the bathrooms are really disgusting but honestly I just blame that on the students. column1: Regarding the comments made about the yearbook and mentors... The administration doesn't take bullying seriously and doesn't really enforce the rules for lateness, skipping, fighting, etc... Most of my peers have C's or lower. The students in all grades frequently make fun of me and disclude me because I am not from this area, I haven't found friends in the 4 years I have been here. At the moment I am sitting alone in lunch because the cliques here are so strong. After most teachers have you they don't act like they know you at all and my geometry teacher still doesn't even know half the students in my class even though she has had us for more than 4 months! The administration doesn't even know I exist even though I get all A's since I don't do sports and everyone favors the outgoing sports people. So it's a terrible school and I can't wait to get out! Well , i for one know that many many many phone calls have been made by myself to this school about bullying. And yet the worst has happened at this date. For lack of further embarrassment of my son i will not list it here as we are pursuing a legal standpoint. Also know that i have been in meetings,phone calls, guidance, sons physican, teachers and principal as well as others have been aware. I also have had teachers belittle my son. For you below who have had such a great experience i am happy for you. But please don't excuse it away with "whom" they should talk to. You need to know that bullying is HERE and active. My son lives it daily so please don't tell me how great Skyline is.... My son and I will be relocating from New Jersey to Front Royal, Va, he is currently in a private middle school but i will be switching him to a public school in September, will be Entering the 8th grade and i wanted to know more and honest opinions about Skyline High School. What a shame that people who have had a bad personal experience (bullying, cant make friends etc) want to blame the school --- the entire school faculty and principal for these problems! My son is getting ready to graduate from this school and went all four years here. He is in the top 5 in the entire senior class.... he loves his teachers and has a wonderful experience. He made friends and has gotten into one of the top colleges in the country. So he obviously learned a lot at Skyline. So I am sorry for those few that have had bad experiences, but you cant blame the whole school for it. Academically this is a superior school..... The teachers here don't care about their students at all. They don't care about homework rates. My daughter comes home with pages upon pages a day. It normally takes hours to complete it all. Plus, the administration doesn't care about anything. Bullying doesn't matter to them. They rarely suspended or punish anyone. Be wary putting your students in here. I like how AP classes are year long still......

column3: As a current freshman parent and BVHS alumnus, I can say the school has retained a high academic rating, however this is upheld by such a small portion of the population that it is actually irrelevant. I believe that the staff has become complacent and relies on this population to "carry" them through. An ordinary student that could become extraordinary with a little help and motivation is just pushed along. My child was absent due to illness for a week and I only recieved an email response from 2 out of 6 teachers. I have literally stood in the office for 10+ mins while office staff chatted, until I finally interrupted them. I have only seen the principal at assemblies, she didn't even show up to a local CABE, education assoc. conferance, for an award she was nominated for, she didn't win....there are drugs, sex, etc... in every high school, BVHS is no exception, but the students' sense of entitlement and total disrespect for each other and faculty is appalling, I've heard better language in an episode of Lock Up. im and 8th grader right now... and im from santee im movening up to chula vista and i will be in bonita vista high school.. district so thats where im goinggg... can anyone tell me what im expecting..? The school is top-notch, Consistently the best academics in the district. The classes are tough many teachers hold Phd in thier feild and most have more than a decade teaching experience So if your kid is not ready to work hard this is not the school for them. However if they can keep up with the work BVHS provides a great jumping off point to a successful college experience and success in life. If your child is planning on participating in the AP/IB track then this is a great school. My child is an AP Student and we were not happy with the lack of help and direction from my child's counselor. Also, Bonita Vista lacks attention to it's sports programs & fields. Kids from other schools attending sports functions at Bonita Vista have been heard commenting on how "ghetto" the school is. The principal only seems to be concerned with the high API scores for the school. Score boards, bleachers & fields are in dire need of repair. This staff here is a joke. They are a terrible school and have no idea how to run this school. The vice principles especially are idiots. Bonita High offers a good education for the high functioning student. I do believe that additional support should be offered, but budgets are low. They have come under fire recently due to the lack of credible sports programs. While their golf team is amongst the best, and the GIRLS basketball team is coached by knowledgeable mentors, the BOYS basketball program is the worst. The Freshman coach is knowledgeable as is the assistant JV coach, but the other coaches unfortunately show no credible ability to lead these talented young men. The volleyball coaching staff is knowledgeable. The football team walked out on the program due to the coaching staff. While the focus on high school should be academics, it does help young men and women when they are mentored by coaches whose knowledge and ability they respect. Football coach allows quite a bit of bullying among those that love the Sport and want to learn by the ones that are a lot more experienced. Principal and vice-principal seem to always and inly support the teachers but disregard the students. Cell phone use dyring class is out of control. Communication between divorced parents is not existant, they just pick one and disregard the other 100% of the time. I do aknowledge that teens can be very challenging and disruptive, but I don't feel that they have the counseling, safety measures, etc in practice or if you ask for help is pretty much a waste of time. Coming from the SDUSD I Really thought this school will be way better in quality, safety, care, support, etc I have now sadly discovered it is way worst. This school only. I remember Sunnyside was so much better back on 1996. Its a shame that this day and age that racial injustice is still being tolerated and accepted! How successful can a student be in this type of learning environment? I’ll be graduating this June and I can say that I’m so glad I went BVHS. It’s bar the best school in the district. I’m in the IB program so the rigor stood out to me to most. It’s a school that offers its students what they like. Whether it’s sports, or theater, choir, speech and debate, mock trial; they breed students for success. Two of my friends will be going to Harvard and MIT in the fall and it’s because of the opportunities they found here.

column1: Awful. The material is to hard for your average students. The teachers do not care if you have trouble and do not do a good job of explaining the work. The students are very rude and look down on you if you are different. They only like you if you have tons of money and wear designer clothes. All of Plainview is awful. If I was moving to the Ardmore area I would not send my child to Plainview School Distract. All they care about is the State and Fed ratings. The students are taught the test for the test. Plainview "Was" a great school the best in the Ardmore area after the latest administration took over it has become a third rate school. Plainview High school is the best there is. I am a former graduate and was very prepared to go to college. The teachers cared about me and went out of the way to help if you didn't understand something. The Algebra teacher would help me after class when I had problems in that class. And the classes are relatively small. Most of them had less than 20 students and were actively involved in the students. I would definately recommend this school to anyone living in Ardmore. As for the negative comments about it being about money, status, etc. I never noticed that in the 10 years that i attended school there. Great school and great teachers! this is a horrible school the teachers except for a few do nothing but pick favorites and torment you if you don't understand what they are teaching the students are just as bad they are mean towards you if you don't have a rich lifestyle or wear a certain outfit. my nephew started at plainview he was bullied non stop finally his mom pulled him out and took him to lone grove hes happier and he has tons of friends. If i were you i would take your children to lone grove instead of this horrible school The complete enrollment process with a new student has been excellent! They have have been extremely friendly and helpful! Plainview hs is one of the top public schools in the State of Oklahoma. Great educators who put the student in front of themselves. Engaging balance of academics and sports.A lack of diversity would be the minor drawback, but overall a top-notch institution.

The school offers a multitude of after school activities to help the students find their niche and create lasting experiences. Two out of my 3 sons have atended Mepham High School the oldest graduates Class of 2016 and the other Class of 2017 they as well as myself have had a Great High School experience thanks to the vigorous curriculum and the professionalism , dedication and support from the teaching staff and office admistration. This school will always hold a special place in my heart. Not only did both my sister and myself attend, but it was also the place where my parents fell in love. The teachers, guidance, and administration provided me with the best high school experience I could have asked for. I've made lifelong friends and discovered lifelong passions. I will be forever grateful for my time at such an amazing place. Al 3 of my children attended Mepham High School, teachers were great, easy to communicate with, the administration was very hands on. They all participated on sports teams, great coaching and support from everyone to make sure the kids had a great experience. Same can be said for the music department. All around great place.
