column3: I have a question that I hope can be answered. Right now I attend The Villages High School and next year, my 11th grade year, I was thinking about switching to LHS. However, I live in Summerfield, about 15 minutes away from Leesburg. My aunt said she didnt think I was eligable to attend since I am not zoned for LHS. Can someone tell me if LHS is a possibility for me? This is a great school! I have to say that this is the best High School I have been to! Excellent Teachers (Depending on who you get) But it's more than above average! I believe that this year is the best! We are now known as the "ON Time" Students! It's pretty cool and you really feel proud of your work in this school! No matter if its completely done wrong, you still get a valid grade! LEESBURG HIGH SCHOOL IS THE WORSE SCHOOL IVE SEEN. AT LEASE 5 FIGHTS A DAY. NO SUPERVISION AT ALL. THE KIDS DONT CARE ABOUT SCHOOL AT ALL. SO THE OTHER STUDENTS THAT WANT TO LEARN THEY MAKE IT HARD FOR THEM. THEY CANT FOCUS. THIS IS NOT A GOOD SCHOOL!!!! Teachers does the bare minimum and could care less if your child passes or fails. They play too much with Student and get frustrated when the situation is out of their control. This school need a staff makeover!!!! some of the staff members are very rude & unprofessional. & this school over all lacks organization.:( I love my school. If I could finish my final year at my school I would. Leesburg High School is a great school academically and physically. They help you get to where you need to be and help you to strive to be the better person you are to become in the near future. Lets go Jackets!! My daughter a freshman hereand. I love how her grades are awesome. I love how the attendance gives me a call when shes absent. Hopefully she'll be joining softball nxt year. Since she miss this year. Keep up the good work LHS. Hopeing to see a 5star school soon. Two and a half years ago I would've rated Leesburg High School a 7/10 for at least trying to rebuild after years of struggling. Since I haven't been a student there since 2016, they've had many shifts in leadership since then, and a lot of my favorite teachers have left, I'm not exactly sure what to rate the school anymore. But regardless, I'm forever a Yellow Jacket. One of the worst schools my children have ever been in. If you want your child to excel and not deal with nonsense and problems on a day to day basis I would suggest looking into another school. They have no control.and need to get a handle on this school and the children. Fights, drama, sex and drugs are a major part of this school. Like all school, Leesburg High has its problems. However the teachers and staff here did an excellent job preparing my child for the real world.

column1: We couldn't be happier and more impressed with DCC. We've had a kid at this school for four years of elementary. We have always felt welcome, the administrators are always quick to respond to issues and the majority teachers are top notch. The positives far outway the few negatives. To address some of the complaints: parking lots by definition are a hassle. Spend a little time in any of the other school parking lots. And really, is that your biggest concern? As for atheletics, the HS is new. They haven't had years to develop a strong atheletic program. If that's your biggest reason for sending your kids to school, maybe another school might be better for you. As for the IB issues, it's an IB school, so of course they'll be teaching to that cirriculum. My main goal for my children is for their continued academic success. I believe that can be accomplished with the IB program at DCC. My daughter attended kindergarten in this school for 6 months and it was a disappointment. The teacher and administration were unable to provide the challenge my daughter needed. In addition, there was bullying in the class. I personally had to stop a fight in the playground since the teacher did not act on it. When we decided to leave the school the teacher and administration did not even ask or care to get feedback on what was wrong. One day I picked up my child from school and her nose was swollen. She had a bloody nose at school after hitting the table and no one had the courtesy to call me. Between the lack of leadership in preventing bullying, the less than challenging curriculum I would not recommend this school. We made a decision to change schools mid year which was not a light decision but in three weeks I have a different kid who loves school and is challenged. She is being pulled out for enrichment 3 times a week, she is getting extra reading homework and her math book even covers fractions in kindergarten. I placed her in AIES and would highly recommend the school. We have restored the love for learning in our household. I was a student at DCC from sixth to eleventh grade. It was a terrible experience. Starting in my first year, I was teased horribly and all I was told to do was "walk away." No one ever took any action, despite the fact that we had "Bully Proofing Training" once a month. Most of the teachers I had in both middle school simply just didn't care. Despite the fact that I was obviously struggling, they continued to let me slip through the cracks. Then, in high school, I was faced with a whole new set of problems from not only the cruel students, but also the administration and staff. The lack of professionalism was tremendous. During my freshmen year, my English teacher made several remarks about my religion. Her and the entire class decided to gang up on me one day and harass me about my personal beliefs. I'd also heard several teachers make rude remarks about other students' appearances and intellect when they weren't around. They acted like they were the ones in high school. When I told the school, no one did anything. This school is filled with close-minded, insensitive and discriminatory people. I'm very glad that I finally left and I would never recommend it to anyone! This is THE worst school in the district. The teachers are just as catty and insensitive as the high school students. And the administration? Don't even get me started. My daughter went here for both middle school and high school. She hated it from the beginning, but to go to any other school was too inconvenient logistically. So we tried our best to work out the problems. Unfortunately, nothing was ever resolved. She was bullied and harassed by a group of students throughout the years and nothing was ever done about it. Also, because District 20 has this ridiculous hiring policy, all of the teachers are new and inexperienced. My daughter didn't learn a thing until she left! Plus, anytime she struggled with her work, no matter how hard she tried, it was always our fault. Working parents can do their best to help with homework, but ultimately, it comes down to the teachers. And these ones don't have a clue what they're doing! I was shocked at how rude and utterly disrespectful they have been to our entire family. I hate this school so much that I'd be willing to picket in front of it, telling everyone how terrible it really is. I have daughters at both DCC middle and high school and we are very happy with both. The actual school is beautiful with equipment that rivals many colleges. The teachers have all been responsive when contacted and the counselours we've dealt with regarding our special needs children were great - so much more concerned and responsive than those we dealt with in Distruct 49! Teacher monitored after school help is available every day, there are TONS of after school clubs and activities and community service hours are required for every student. There has the usual teenage drama but none of the bullying my girls saw in District 49 and the administration here is much more visible and approachable than at previous schools. The curriculum here is much more demanding than at other schools the girls have attended but students have the support system to succeed and teachers and administrators who are invested in their success. I'm really shocked at some of the reviews here, which totally contradict the experience we've had here! My children all attend DCC,1 HS, 1MS, and 2 ES. What a wonderful thing that they are all on one campus! We have been at this school for 5 years now and being a military family who has moved around, we have had experience with lots of schools, DCC is by far the best we have encountered. I was shocked to read some of the negative reviews, but realized some people just like to complain. Administrators at each level have been responsive to all of my requests, and have always been able to work something out to make sure my children get what they need. They are definitely child centered and do their best to make sure every kid is taken care of. Is it perfect, no, but what school is? Being a newer school, DCC has had to work through some changes and growing pains, but has come out better in the end. Having seen how hard the teachers work behind the scenes and the hours they spend outside the school day, I guarantee you will not find a more dedicated group of teachers, anywhere! I would not hesitate to recommend DCC to my family and friends(and have). I would choose DCC again in a heartbeat for my children! You will find a caring community, great teachers, and a fantastic facility! I love the "campus" design of this school!!! What a huge convenience, especially for someone with children in different grade levels (elementary through high school). This is a brand-new, beautiful school w/ all the best amenities. As far as academics go, there is a strong emphasis on IB curriculum - which is great for college-bound kids! The school is also in a wonderful and safe (extremely low-crime) area... You really can't go wrong if you send your kids to DCC!!! The principal is not a leader at the school. I find most teachers to be lazy and unresponsive to parents questions. Some teachers know less about what is going on in the school than parents. Some teachers don't teach and the kids have to teach themselves. Many poor quality teachers and I don't understand how they keep their jobs year after year. Overall, it is a disappointment. High school principal dresses too casual. Lead by example to the students. He lacks leadership over his teachers and counselors. The good ones are good, but they are few and far between. When you point out how unprofessional teachers react, the principal disregards. Eventually, when several of us parents tell the principal something, ignoring it is not leadership it is lazy. Find your professional attire and professional leadership. The school is going downhill under Bailey's lack of leadership. I have two children in the elementary school. One finishing 1st, the other 4th grade. In the beginning of the year, I was not very impressed. My son was put in a classroom where they had just moved a 5th grade teacher down to 1st grade and she was a huge disappointment. The young lady (only 2nd year teaching) realized this though and resigned about a month into school. They hired a super young lady, just out of college and I thought we were IN FOR IT!! Fortunately, this gal had her act together and made the very best out of a pretty bad situation. I think the administration could have helped the new gal out quite a bit more to get the class organized, so it took until around Thanksgiving before the class was truly in order and kids were on track. After all that though, it has been clear sailing! The new first grade teacher does her very best to differentiate in class and is very open to parent involvement. My daughter's 4th grade teacher has had it dialed in since the beginning. She is phenomenal when it comes to writing and language arts. DCC also has a "talented and gifted" program for kids that are above grade level, allowing kids to reach their full potential. I've gone to three high schools. Trust me, this is by far the best of the three. The social divisions among students is much less severe than the other high school I have been to and since there is very heavy military presence, it is fairly easy to make new friends. You can always find something to complain about, but it is better to look at the school as a whole. DCC is a beautiful school, which, for the most part, has excellent and caring teachers. The teachers and administration are much more relaxed compared to my others schools, which can be annoying when you add in less mature students, but if you are serious about your education, I see this as a good thing. If you really want to succeed and work hard, you will. The AP courses provided are pretty good, and I felt prepared for the tests. I just wish they would add more AP courses such as AP Physics and an official AP Chemistry course. I'm proud to have graduated from this school. Oh, and to the person who said the parking lot was like a maze... What? If you love your children, do not send them here.I was bullied all throughout middle school, but the worst time was when I was on the bus one afternoon, and I got beat up by this girl I didn't even know. I was hurt pretty badly. I came home with a broken nose, and bruises and scrapes everywhere on my body. I told my mom what happened and she reported it to the school. The school checked the bus tapes and sure enough, it was clear as day. However, they told me that there was "not enough evidence" to do anything about it. I was told that the only way they could do something about it is if I asked people I knew that had also been bullied by this girl to report it. Sure enough 10-15 people then made true reports. The following week I was told to "drop it" because apparently someone had pushed the girl and they immediately linked it to me because I seemingly had a "grudge" against her. I continued to get bullied the rest of my time at dcc but I never reported it because they simply don't care. A year later the police called the school because I had attempted suicide because of repetitive bullying. They said they had no idea it was happening, and even after that they did nothing. This is a great school. It is such a pleasure to have your kids come home from school with a smile and be excited about what they are learning and the friends they have made. The principal chews gum while making presentations, dresses too casual, he is more into football scores than academics and allows his teachers to be disrespectful to students and parents. It could be a good school, but the high school principal is not professional. I would guess he is skating until retirement. The band director's ego is too big for his skill set. He can't retain students due to his poor attitude and his program is lacking advancement for good musicians. If you are his teacher's pet then you get accolades, if not, you are overlooked and will not learn even if you are the better musician in the class. There are a few good teachers, but most are unresponsive and allowed to be unresponsive by the principal. My child is an all "A" student in honors and AP classes so doing fine in spite of the principal and teachers. Too bad the admin and teachers lack professionalism and pride in their work. Worst school EVER! Went there for 2 years just god awful.... I would not recommend this school to anyone. To much bullying, teachers that don't even teach. If I could rate this school 0 stars I would, just awful.... so glad I'm going to Air Academy now My 2 children have gone here for 2years....wonderful school! We absolutely love the teachers!! Love that the schools is all grade levels....way easier with multiple children in different levels of school. Not sure about the new principal but other than that....love love this school! This school has had 9 suicides in the last 4 years. two Suicides happened just this week. This school needs an intervention!bullying is out of hand I don't know why the bad reviews. The school is on top of bulling and suicide prevention. My children enjoyed going to school and did very well. If you have a child that needs Special Ed they are great they listen and help a lot. My oldest graduated from DCC and they prepared him for college and my two younger kids did very well and will miss DCC for we moved out of state. The teachers are amazing, they always help you to stay on top of your academics . But the truth about whats going on inside those brick walls is they cant control bullying or suicides. I was bullied and they couldnt fix it . One of my friends comminted suicides because it was to much. Its a great school but somebody needs to take control. The teachers at this school have been so great. They are engaged and excited about teaching. The special education has been wonderful as well. My kids have had good experiences for the last three years at DCC. They are excited about going to school each day. My heart goes out to the kids who have had bad experiences. I would say that there are more kids that have good experiences though. I have three kids in Elementary and one in Middle. This school has many positives, but one area that we can't seem to work around is the lack of lesson plans. As a parent (and teacher myself) I have asked all of my children's teachers for their lesson plans for the week/month, whatever they have available. However each of the teachers (minus music) has denied my request. This causes parents and students alike to be reactive instead of proactive. It does cause some concern from a teaching perspective as well. If I had no lesson plan I would not rest in the assurance my students were reaching their goals and their potential. It can become very easy to venture off task when we are on a subject that everyone loves. A lesson plan helps us reign in our goals and stay on task. It also allows parents to see exactly what we are accomplishing in the classroom, initiating home conversation and often further learning. I feel this lack of planning limits a students potential. I find it odd that the leadership does not require or review since there is a position in this IB school that is designated specifically for that purpose. Overall it is an okay school but nothing to write home about. DCC fails the top 15% of the students. Particularly in the math department. More concerned with keeping the students GPA's up rather then preparing them for success in college. For example: student takes all Honors classes as a freshman including Algebra 2 honors receives all A's and a 4.56 GPA. Gets excepted at a prestigious prep school and takes Precalc only to get a D+, as the teacher informs him that he is lacking a solid foundation of the algebra concepts. Same student takes PSAT scores quite well, all 90% or above except for a 70% on the Hearts of Algebra questions. Student went on to receive an A in the spring semester and an A in Calc fall of Junior year but he had to spend a lot of time playing catchup. Student 2 transfers after 2 years of Honors middle school classes and spends the first month of school playing catch up in his Algebra 2 class because DCC is unwilling to push these kids beyond the basics. So if you have a very intelligent student and they want to be prepared for college at a top 20% college or university you will want to find a different option. Suicides, bullying, drugs and alcohol, kids making out in the halls and the school turns a blind eye. Not a positive environment. This school is horrible! The school's culture is deplorable and responsible for the 6 suicides that have taken place the last 2 years. The school isn't inclusive. Unless you're white, Mormon, and rich you're going to be an outsider. Bullying is rampant at DCC and the admin and counselors do nothing to stop it. My student has been bullied for years and our complaints have always been ignored. The rules don't apply to students whose parents are wealthy. Most of the teachers are going through the motions and the admin is completely out of touch with reality. 6 suicides in 2 years is inexcusable. The folks that run this school should be ashamed of themselves. Apathetic administration, low academic standards, high teacher turnover, student suicides every year, bullying, self righteous parents, inferior technology, heroin addict janitors, overworked counselors, jaded teachers on power trips, rude staff, etc. DCC is awful. Admin needs to wake up. My daughter just started at DCC and we're very disappointed. This school is behind the times! None of my daughter's teachers have websites or post assignments online for parents and students. We feel like we've gone back in time at this school. At our last school the teachers communicated a lot with parents and ALWAYS updated their websites. Most of her teachers ignore my emails or reply a week after they receive them! My girl also has struggled to make friends since the school is very cliquish. I'm not that surprised since the principal has a horrible reputation in the community The IB program and most of the teachers are fantastic. However, if you have a disabled student I would recommend attending another school. Administration does not care about this demographic and will brush aside your issues at every turn. Attended DCC middle through highschool. Not a very fun enviroment if you arent rich, white, straight, and mormon. In the middle of an upperclass neighborhood, and acted like all of the students who attended could afford macbooks and ridiculously expensive equipment and fees. If you choiced in from a lower-income area and couldn't afford class materials, you were screwed and advised to drop the class.About half of the student population aren't accepting of the other students who don't fit their demographic. If i had a penny for every time a friend or I were called f*g or butch, I'd actually be able to afford living near the school. School admin and student counsel repeatedly brush over the national and international achievements of their arts programs and instead focus on their half-rate men's sports teams. Teachers and counselors were passionate though, and made the experience worth it. They offer several out of the box classes like astronomy, mythology, and sci-fi literature.All in all, an okay school with wonderful staff and terrible students. Mediocre experience. No diversity. With the exception of 2-3 teachers no one is interested in motivating students to succeed. Some of the success stories are due to helicopter parenting of some rich parents living in the school neighborhood. I am a student at DCC MS. I hate it. It has some of the biggest jerks and snobs. They don't do anything about all the suicides. One of the vice principles has favorite students. If one kid does something bad she's like so what. If the other does the same thing, she rages. DCC is also very liberal. and some what sexist. They usually discriminate boys. And I am a boy, and this offends me. Do not go to this school. Poor, leaving this school immediately. Dangerous climate, psychologically damaging, complete clown act. Good school. But they blocked the lane allowing parents of disabled kids to get to handicap spots in time. There is a pick-up line that they want us to wait in as well. But by the time that line gets up to those spots, our children that have special needs, have been waiting 20 plus minutes after the bell rings and they are the ones that need help! At that time, all the other kids have cleared out! It is so wrong. What is the point of a handicap spot if we cannot access them when needed and available?? Our children all thrived at DCC. They each had a great group of friends. They felt safe and intellectually challenged. And enjoyed going to school there. Mr. Beckman is the greatest math teacher. Wish all teachers were as passionate about teaching as he is. The engineering program is also great. There are definitely some staff members and coaches there that are subpar. But overall, it is a good school and has the potential to be great. I can see how maybe it's not the best school for every child, but for ours it was a great experience. Excellent! We’re generally very happy to have our kids here. Excellent. My oldest has attended k-7 and my daughter k-3. Love the educators they have worked with I went to school here from grades K-12. This school expects all students to be able to afford materials. If you did not have your own computer you could bring to school and you couldn't rent one for fifty dollars, you would have been screwed. They do not care about low-income families. It is also very capitalism and privilege based. I did not see one minority besides me (I'm LGBT identifying), which is of course not the school's fault; I just thought that was strange. Also, the suicide rates? seriously? It's ridiculous how little this school cares about students. Do not send your student here if you are not white, wealthy, nor religious. Also, the teachers were exceptionally disrespectful to students. Unbelievable. The school recently got a new Principal and he is Hard Ball IB. (International Baccalaureate) Before the kids had a choice not not do IB, but now they force every kid into all IB classes. They have switched the curriculum in the middle of their 4 years and took away a ton of choices for classes that they had in their 4 year plan. Many Honors classes have been removed (I am guessing over 50%), so the kids are not on par with the rest of the district with weighted classes. The other schools in the district give their students a hand up with tons of meet and greet opportunities with colleges along with tons of seminars on applying, finical help, choosing and how to get into a college. Other high schools have a really good college and careers staff. The College and Careers staff at DCC have been lacking and fall way behind what the other schools offer to the upperclassman. I know, because I have attended other high school's events. The Guidance counselors have been top notch in our experience and we have been pleased with their help over the years. The teachers, overall, are great teachers and care for the students. Stay clear of coaches who teach classes. Though not all the coaches are bad teachers, we have learned after 4 years at DCC, that a teacher can be a coach, but a coach cannot be a teacher. You have to figure out who these people are. I actually had a staff member tell me that there's nothing we can do to help, if the teacher is not actually teaching. I was looking for guidance for my child in a class where the "coach" didn't teach anything. Another point that bothers me, is that my oldest has not written an English essay in 3 years and I expect him to have serious problems in college with essay writing. I think a lot of their assignments are trying to promote out of the box thinking, but they take it too far and a student needs to write an essay. Because of the changes they made, I would not recommend this school, if you are not on board with IB. If you believe in IB, then definitely look to choose this school. Otherwise, I would suggest looking at Pine Creek, Liberty or Rampart. Note that Rampart is also an IB school, but up until this point, they have not taken away the students choices on classes. We are super happy with the school. My daughter recently attended Pine Creek and had to switch schools because we moved. I think the teachers are amazing and the assistant principal has been very helpful she even gave me her contact number outside of school. I couldn't ask for a better support team in the math category. If you have had some struggles with math don't fret, the tutors are amazing!!!

column3: Great school with considerably more course offerings than other county schools. Great principal and teachers who care about the success of my children. We just moved to Nacogdoches from California, and to be honest we were nervous to enroll our kids at Nacogdoches High School because we were coming from a suburban high school with a 9 rating, and Nac High is rated much lower. We have a senior, sophomore and a freshman, and we have been pleasantly surprised at the high level of instruction, amazing teachers, and the diversity at this school. The teachers and coaches are top notch, and our kids are making friends from all different socioeconomic backgrounds and walks of life. Our senior was just accepted to Texas A&M and our girls are college bound as well. We have no regrets and highly recommend this school for a well rounded educational experience!

column1: I do not recommend this school for any child that has a disability. My son is Autistic and they have done everything to get him out of the school instead of trying to help him. If you are not in there little group of friends you are pretty much not going to get any help with anything. There are a few teachers at this school that really do care about the students. I am really disappointed with some of the staff. It is small but growing i have gone here for 9 years now about to be a junior and they don't have all the classes that I would like but it's okay I'm a parent so I don't see or do a lot of things here, but from what I see and hear from the kids, they LOVE Holden and don't ever want to go elsewhereI rate the school a 5 Worst experience of my life. I am forever scarred by my experience at this school. Please do not send your kids here. This school for the most part is good, but is not great. First of all, I would like to say that most of the teachers are good but there are many that I've had that do not teach at all and do not belong in a certain grade or teaching in general. Second, the homework given is not that bad but can sometimes be a lot. Third, this school will talk about bullying like they care, but they really do not care, especially if you are different from the majority. The school is pretty homophobic and racist not to mention extremely Christian. If they find out that you're not Christian, you will be made out to feel excluded and like there is something wrong with you. The school is also kind of sexist, but that's at almost all schools. Fourth, The school does not provide much is you have a learning disability or a learning difference. They pretty much do nothing. Overall, the school values test scores over students and the environment. If you're looking for a school with high academics, come to Holden. All I can say is that I wouldn't send my kids here if I had them.

column3: My daughter went through the Carteret school system, and graduated High school, however the stories she had mentioned to us about the teachers not being leaders, lack of homework, and just winging it, kids misbehaving in class, shows that there is a lot of work to be done in the Carteret school system. Although we still live in the area, we decided to home school our son who is doing way better that what he would of done in the failed school system of Carteret. It’s a very typical school but for a small town it gets you places Felt parent involvements are not encouraged by consular. AP classes are good but not many students are capable. Parents are complainer for teachers gives more homework. Doesn't matter the school rank is...What matters how much parents get involved with their children homework and follow up.My son achieved BS in Biomedical Engineering, Master in Medical Science and he is Medical Doctor now. My daughter graduated with Doctrate in Pharmacy in 6 years after high school. What school can help more to teach on managing monies while they are in college.

column1: FRHS is an incredible school. I transferred there my junior year in 2006 and was astonished by the strong community and spirit of the school. Father Ryan focuses on producing well-rounded young adults and the things I learned there go far beyond the classroom. Also when I entered college I discovered we were far more prepared academically then the vast majority of our peers. I look forward to sending my children there. My son has attendended this school for a year now. This is probably the worst school you could possibly send your child to. It has little to no diversity in their students making "most" of them very similar. No one stands out in any special way. Just a bunch of preppy athletes as my son says. Some teachers single out students and make other students seem lower when everyone should be equal. Teachers dont follow policies by only applying them to some students. My son left and is now attending Hillsboro. Its not a good school and he loves it. Thats what matters. I highly recommend public school if your child isnt really having that great connection with a private school. The school? Very nice. The students? That's a different story. After moving across the country, my family decided to send me to Father Ryan. It was very unwelcoming. I tried to be friendly and talk to people everyday, but it just felt like the students ignored me. I just felt like I didn't fit in. At my old school, I had nice, caring friends. Here I didn't ever even make one. It made me just feel lonely and depressed. I don't recommend this school for people who aren't from Tennessee. It seems like nearly everyone went to Elementary school and Middle school together. Therefore, they already had there group of friends and didn't want new meet new people. Hopefully this problem can be fixed for future students, because I would hate for others to have the same experience I did. After reading some of the reviews below I feel like my child I going to a completely different school than the one mentioned! He is an advanced minority student, Father Ryan both challenges him academically and socially. He is in many clubs and has friends from many different backgrounds and cultures. We just found out he received a full ride for pre-med to the college of his choice. I feel like this is exactly what Father Ryan set him up for. Having three boys there now, I haven't had any issues with bulling or social problems. I hope we are the norm and not the exception to the rule when it comes to being treated with kindness. We did not attend Father Ryan so I can not assume it is an alumni thing as stated below. Excellent education and environment, beautiful large campus that rivals some colleges, and a great many social activities, plus amazing faith based teachers/staff. Will be sending my last child there definitely as well! Thank you Father Ryan!! I am never surprised to see the school still follows the "who you know or are related to" philosophy" in all matters. Academics are weak to say the least and many personnel are juvenile and quite uneducated themselves. They treat people who aren't the in-crowd very differently which is to say the least very non-christian. Its sub par at best. Needs major adjustments starting with stale, old administration. This school is the most caring, academically challenging, and Christian school in Nashville. I am thrilled my child attends. They are turning away current applicants because so many wish to attend. The people at this school truly care about our kids! The academics are very challenging. The school has 5 academic levels and 26 AP courses. It's the best deal in town for the money. I was so apprehensive about high school for my child. She desperately wanted to go to FRHS, but I was worried that it was too big. I could not have been more wrong! This school feels so small and individual, because every teacher genuinely cares about the student, her success, her challenges. And because the school has different academic levels in each area, you can find the perfect fit for your child. It has been a wonderful experience for us. Very negative, the students were very rude towards me, calling me bad things Fifty year alumni of Father Ryan. Molded me into the person I am today. Was well prepared for college and life. Love Father Ryan!!

column3: Most of the staff are fine on their own, but they have terrible communication with each other, and they promote a very politically biased atmosphere. The political bias and emphasis on conformity is downright shameless. The lone counseler is most concerned with college bound stats. The dismissive attitude has negatively affected many kids whose interests were in Technical Careers. Their needs and skillset are judged as inferior (by the counseler and teachers) to those bound for 4 year colleges. If you want to wrap your child in the bubble wrap of privilege and woke ideals this is the place for you!

column1: This school is absolutely absurd. The rules are ridiculous and take away the fun that should occur in high school. My son has told me many stories of the political factors that play into the administration's role. One student was told that he could either "tell on his friends" or "be expelled." Not very "Catholic" is it? I want my kids in an environment that conveys the importance of friendship, not an environment of fear. The deans and the principal need to open their eyes and realize that they are ruining high school for kids by making them fearful and deteriorating their friendships. I am very disappointed to say that I am a student at Bishop Gorman. There is absolutely nothing positive about this school outside of the athletics. I have different interests that most kids, i dont play football of soccer, so there are very little things for me to do here outside academics, there aren't many elective choices either compared to what i see on Palo Verde's student handbook. Worst choice I have ever made. A lesson to all you up and coming high schoolers don't choose to go to a school just because most of your friends are going there, go to a school that fits you. This school does not fit anyone that does not have an interest in sports. All you parents, please send your kid to another school i.e. Faith, Meadows, any public or tech school are much better choices. I went to Catholic school all my life until I left Gorman as a Junior, I couldn't put up with it anymore. This school isn't Catholic, and I was severely bullied there. The rich kids got special attention, and got away with things. Im disappointed with this school. Its made out to be a good, catholic, serious school. First, this school is not Catholic. It is the least Catholic school of all schools. Not many people at this school are nice, students do not display catholic values. Mass is only held around few holy days of obligation - I think for a catholic school, it should be held more often. In addition the students are terrible. It is very politically biased - athletes, especially football players and cheerleaders, are usually favored. It also seems like students are either over or under disciplined. Many programs are under appreciated. It feels like if you're not a "cool, athletic, party" person then you don't shine as much at this school. Another thing that bothers me about this school is the major lack of school spirit. Football and basketball games are almost always empty. When entering high school, I was excited to support my school but it almost seems as if you are looked down on for having school spirit - it's not "cool." I am running out f characters but i could go on. In conclusion, the school is not what it seems. Its a mess. The teachers are just ok, nothing special. Some are great others arent. I am a sophomore at Gorman currently. I play football and am in the highest level of classes (scholars and AP) and hold a high GPA, so I will admit that I do have a bit of preference going for me. However, I feel that the school is run very poorly in a number of ways. First off, the administration killed school spirit. Dress down days and pep rallies are a joke because of the absurd limits put on what the students can and can't do. Second, some teachers are absolutely horrible at their job. Gorman seems to give preference to alumni and veterans when hiring while sacrificing quality. The school also holds the legitimate teachers back from utilizing their full potential as an educator. If you don't teach the way the want you to (even if it is not effective for the kids) they will call you in for a talk and after a couple instances, consider them gone. I also notice the deans IN GROUPS seeking out people for minor violations like untucked shirts, gum, etc., just for the pleasure of punishment rather than actually doing something productive. The education is good, sports are obviously great but more leniency and less limitation would make it a much better school. I couldn't agree more to the recent posts on here. My daughter attended BGHS last year. In fact, we moved back to the area so she could attend a Catholic high school. My daughter attended Catholic schools her whole life (K-8). We realized what a terrible mistake we made by enrolling her at Gorman. This school is "Catholic" in name only. It's no wonder there are more independent Catholic schools popping up around the country. Gorman's main focus is on athletics, particularly football. Parents, if you want your children to receive a true Catholic education, do not send them here. Save your money! I recommend homeschooling since everyone knows what a joke the Clark County School District is. We moved our family to Las Vegas from out of state for our kids to have the academic and athletic opportunities Bishop Gorman offers. We have not been disappointed! Our oldest is an honor student who also plays on the football team. He has thrived at Gorman and will be well prepared for college. Further he has made life long friends, has teachers who know who he is and are genuinely interested in his success and we appreciate the spiritual element and emphasis on service even though we are not Catholic. While no school is perfect, we have been happy with our decision for our family to come here. I have a sophomore child going to BGHS. Based on what I've seen and what my daughter tells me, the students are polite, friendly and well behaved. I can't believe some of the negative comments about this school. If you are thinking about sending your children to Bishop Gorman I recommend that you visit the school to see for yourself. Thr best private Highschool in Las Vegas. Best teachers, very professional, great environment, great staff, location, etc. My daughter attend here at BGHS and this is the top rated private school in Las Vegas. Don't look else where if you are looking for a best high school in Las Vegas. Teachers are great, atmosphere and campus is great.I highly recommend this private High School to any parent that wants their child guided in the right direction, not only academically but also spiritually. Disappointed in what the school represents. No wonder other schools dislike Gorman. Absolutely horrible I had heard that this school is the best in town but no there are very few teachers who can actually teach, the food is bland only on the day they show the parents what the food tastes like do they make it nice, they do nothing about bullying, the school counselor could care less about you, and to sum it up they care more if you did not shave your beard than your academics and I’m not even a guy to have a beard. Hypocritical- Gorman prides itself on being a “Christian” school. However, they will only act Christian towards you if you donate large amounts of money to the school or are a student athlete. Horrible, unprofessional, and petty administration. These people should not be educators for your child. My daughter attended BGHS for 2 years and she was miserable. They are hypocritical, misogynistic, sexist and the administrative staff treats you terribly. They have a zero tolerance policy for drugs, etc. unless your parents have money, then there are no repercussions. The school grounds are not well maintained, the food is terrible and the teachers in place should not be teaching. There are roughly 1,470 students at this school so they bring in $19,698,000 per year for tuition. Where does the money go? I am so glad we are no longer association with this school. Bishop Gorman is an amazing High school. Great staff, great campus and safe environment. What more can you ask for high school? I had two kids graduated from Gorman and they ended up in ivy League colleges. So, I'm very pleased with Gorman High School.

column3: My one daughter graduated from Warren Hills Regional HS and my other is going into her senior year. I feel the school has prepared them well to succeed in college from both an academic and social aspect. The school's facilities could use some updating but overall it's better than most. Both on my children did well in this school, they are both in college and doing very well so over all they did a good job. column1: As an alumni I can recommend Stepinac. It is a college prep school so keep that in mind. If your kid is hard working then you shouldn't have any issues. If you are looking for the school to fix your kid then you need some place else. I am currently a 9th. grader at the school. I was afraid to go to high school because of bulling issues in the past but at Stepinac I felt welcomed right away. The teachers work with you and honestly care about the students. You can tell a lot about a school when you feel comfortable enough to speak with the principal regarding any issues ( no one likes to visit the principals office. The teachers want you to excell so they offer their services to tutor you during the week. Being a minority had me a little concerned at first but the color of my skin has not been an issue, I am judged on my academics and the respect that I give the staff and the students. I commend the principal and the staff for going out of their way to make sure that we become successful in life and I thank them for not giving up on us. The staff understands that we have our days at times but the encouragement, commitment and dedication that we receive deserves a big grateful thank you. Thanks again, Brandonn Baez My son in a senior in college now and Archbishop Stepinac prepared him well. Stepinac has racial, religious and economic diversity which helped my son to appreciate difference and will help him in the future. Like another reviewer, we also heard "you never hear anything bad about Stepinac." It is true because the administration takes action immediately when problems do arise. My son is a junior and has had a great experience at Stepinac. The teachers and staff truly care about the boys and their well-being and growth. It is a technology oriented school - the extensive use of technology within the curriculum has helped my son tremendously and engaged him in learning. He is being appropriately academically challenged. The sports and fine arts programs are solid. Wonderful! The faculty has compassion and is caring. They strive to providing a conservative approach to teaching. Not a good school at allIt’s all about sports and religion No communication between student and teachers at allStuff with very bad attitude

column3: My son graduated from Sandusky and we moved to another local school district. I felt the younger children were deprived of the education that Sandusky High School offered my oldest. Sandusky has the ultimate curriculum and the quality of teachers is outstanding. Parent involvement is lacking somewhat, but I believe those that are involved give it their all. You can't find a better educational institution than Sandusky High School. It has excellent staff who through my four years, took interest in my studies and helped getting me involved in things like bloodmobile, National Honors Society and Buckeye Boys state. Don't let OGT test scores fool you, If your child is a high achiever, SHS will help mold them into an even better student. I am a top ten senior from the Class of 2013 and was awarded a full tuition scholarship from the University of Mount Union. Sandusky High played a huge part in helping me get that scholarship. Switched from a neighboring school to Sandusky after many years and couldn’t have been happier. I received a way better education and always felt included and welcomed. 10/10

column1: this school is nothing special. I have been going to Kelly since kindergarten and im now a jr. Kelly has barely any room for all the students and just built on. the new high school has been there for about a year and a half and it has been leeking all year. another problems are the bugs. There are nats and roaches everywhere. I would rather go to oran school than kelly bc its just not a very good place to be everyday. I am a Kelly alumni, and I thank this school for getting me to where I am today. I believe Kelly instilled true core values in me that has helped me succeed and become a prominent lawyer. Being a new person to Kelly Schools this school year, I have found that parent involvement is significantly lacking. Academics at the school are okay but I do not see anything that helps to stimulate creativity. Home work usually consist of work sheets only. I have made several attempts to volunteer through out the school year with no success. The school does have two family fun nights during the school year but no other activities for parents to participate in with their children. No PTO, no Grandparents Day, no Christmas (Holiday) Party, and no opportunities to come to the school to help teachers such as making copies, helping with bulletin boards, reading stories to the children. If you want to be able to drop your children off and not be involved, this is the school for you but if you like to be a part of your childs education, I would recommend another school district. Also my kindergartener was being bullied by a second grader while waiting outside for me to pick him up. Three teachers were out there and did nothing. I witnessed it while I was in line to pick him up. He told a teacher twice that this boy was pushing him, she ignored him & didn't say a word. We called the school and asked if we needed to have our son teach him a lesson since the teachers don't care she said no they'll take care of it. But yet the teachers still dont care and when your child has had enough bullying and stands up for themselves they'll be the one punished. Sorriest school system I know of!! And don't expect good teacher-parent communication. Teachers don't let u know anything! I went to Kelly since kindergarten until I graduated and now my daughter goes to Kelly and will be graduating next year. Kelly is one of the best schools in Southeast Missouri in mine and my daughter's opinion and she transferred from Sikeston to Kelly in the 6th or 7th grade so she should know. Kelly must be ahead of other schools because my daughter had a tough time with Math and other subjects that Sikeston schools haven't even introduced to their students yet. With a lot of studying, hard work & dedication she was right back on track with her grades!! the teachers don't teach you anything and they are very rude towards students

column3: I completely agree and must add that I have never encountered more obnoxious stuedents and parents. I know that every school has their "issues" with bullying, but BCC seems to have much more, and when addressed to parents - - they turn the other cheek. It's no wonder their children are bullies. I am sure they are missing the attention from home as their parents are more concerned with their social status. As a parent, I need a complete balance; a school that cares for my son as an individual and dedicates themselves to helping him succeed in the future and not concerned only with their TEST SCORES, which seems to be the case in all of the Bethesda public schools. I rather move than keep our son there. I have to counter the view that B-CC High School is full of obnoxious students and bullies. I admit that when we enrolled our daughter this year, after years of private schooling, I was a little trepidatious. I even went so far as to look at private high schools before the year started. But after seeing the commitment of the parents and the excellence of the teaching staff, her very committed guidance counselor, the involvement of the 9th grade principal and the options she has for extracurricular activities and school bonding, we elected to keep her at B-CC. I am so very glad we did - she is exceptionally happy and we couldn't be more pleased. My sons have had a largely positive experience at B-CC. Nice, diverse population, great friends, and mostly excellent, caring teachers. We love the urban vibe and the fact that they can walk to downtown Bethesda for lunch. Overall, it was a good choice for us We have had a fabulous experience at BCC. My son comes home excited by his classes and motivated to learn. I've found his teachers responsive and caring. He has an outstanding group of friends and I find most of the parents intelligent, down to earth and engaged in the school. I feel he is getting a first rate education in an exciting, diverse environment. Yes, there is pressure to succeed (hello, this is Bethesda), but I don't feel it overwhelms the school. I am a parent of a current Senior and Freshman. B-CC is a wonderful option -- I have found the great majority of teachers engaged and excellent. I have also found the administration to be concerned about the kids and very engaged with them. There are a wide variety of classes available. There are many extracurricular opportunities. I am a working mother and I am ever grateful for the cadre of dedicated parents who provide a high level of support to the music, academic, and sports programs. There is no perfect school and I am highly concerned about the effects of continuing budget cuts on class size, teacher quality and the extracurricular programs, but I value BCC for its academic standards, diversity, and size which give students the space to be themselves. And the kids have a great situation going to school in a recently renovated beautiful building right in downtown Bethesda. There is pressure to succeed and do well, but I'd rather have high expectations than low ones. I hate the school so much. i went there for 10th grade and knew most of the kids from elementary school and 7th grade, so i thought i could reconnect with them. when i got there no one talked to me and a week there i got mean comments. there was one kid who didnt like me from elementary school and that kid got the rest of the school to hate me too. no one thinks for their self. they just stalk your facebook and say the meanest comments. i only had some friends in 9th grade. my whole grade didnt like me. some kids i didnt even know would say bad things about me. they are the rudest meanest fakest most obnoxious kids. they even look mean. dont listen to any other good things about this school. nothing good about the kids at all. the only good thing about the school are the teachers. the teachers were actually pretty good. i went to wj in 9th grade and the kids had more of their own mind there. do not go to bcc...(Bullying Children Clusters)=BCC B-CC's student population increases every year, and it is quite over crowded (I believe approaching 2000 students soon). Students can fall through the cracks. The crowding also makes it very competitive to get on varsity sports teams, student leadership positions, drama and music opportunities, etc. There are some great teachers, and the diversity of the student body is nice. But teachers and counselors generally have too big a load to give personal attention to the students that are not aggressive. My son simply can't learn Spanish conversation in a class of 31 students, for example. I think the size does help reduce bullying -- it is certainly easy to get "lost in the crowd" and escape unwanted attention. Great school for self motivated go-getters with strong executive functioning skills. Other kids might be a bit lost. Of course parents think the school is great because they don't even know what goes on! There's so much pressure at the school, it results in most of them getting high or drunk every weekend. I lost a lot of friends due to that, but I didn't start out with a lot of friends either because you aren't really "socially accepted" unless you are rich or have connections. A lot of bullying goes on at the school and I don't think people really realize it that much. No one says anything because they are too afraid of what the other people might think. That's how bad it is. I'm so glad I don't go there anymore. Best time of my life! Amazing inspiring teachers and supportive peers. Here I found my passion for psychology thanks to the AP courses. Proud alumni! It has an amazing music program with amazing music teachers! Poor. I could not wait to get out of there. The principal should be fired. Then all the teachers worth anything would stay .Teacher retention at this school should be investigated. So to should be the number of complaints to the union. Principal is an evil person. My second son is graduating now from BCC. I just want to say overall how pleased I have been with the school, especially academically and in the way it has prepared them for college. They both are going on to great colleges, and seem utterly comfortable, if not advanced, in their ability to tackle the work. Many of their teachers were outstanding, and engaged them intellectually and personally -- they will always remember those teachers and we are grateful to them. The social studies, history and math courses they have taken have been amazing. Both my kids did the IB program. They learned so much at BCC -- they know so much more than I did coming out college... and they are utterly engaged and knowledgable about current affairs and major topics of the day. Neither of my kids got hugely engaged in extracurriculars, aside from the wonderful debate team, but overall in terms of how it has prepared them intellectually and socially, it was excellent. My family all went to school here. This is a school which at first glance seems like a decent one. It's won awards! Kids get into good colleges! Look how many clubs they have! If those sorts of empty accolades are what's important to you, then you might be very happy here. But if your child has any learning differences (ex: dyslexia) or isn't completely White looking, then prepare yourselves for the possibility of discrimination from school staff and faculty, and neglect in terms of teaching plans and parent engagement. My siblings and I are half-middle eastern/half-white. We dress and act like everyone else, but this didn't stop 1 of my siblings from being singled out by administration and accused by another (White) student of making threats at school when they absolutely did not. But apparently we "look like terrorists." My sibling was allowed back in school after it was revealed that no threats had been made, but was never apologized to by the administration or the other student. My sibling felt ashamed and singled out for the rest of their high school career. Not only did the school fail to recognize bullying by another student, when my parents pointed this out they were quite literally, laughed at. During one meeting my parents requested because they were upset by the situation, when the administration thought my parents couldn't hear my sibling was called names, demeaned, and my parent was also made fun of. I encouraged my parents who had this on tape to report it to the media and the school board. It was only concern for making things worse for my sibling that stopped them from doing this. I am appalled at the discriminatory treatment my family received at the hands of this school. I am a physician now, and recently had the opportunity to move back to the area and choose a school system for my future children. I would NEVER choose BCC. Beyond the bullying against people of even a tiny bit of color, there is the fact that BCC is at best, a mediocre learning environment that leans heavily on the high median incomes of most parents who send their children to this school to generate their "student success". Most families in this area are wealthier, and will hire tutors, private coaches, etc to guarantee success for their children. Anyone will get into college after that money is spent, except for less-fortunate families. The moral environment of a school matters. BCC rewards the wealthy white. If you aren't both, go elsewhere. This is a wonderful school which prepares students to go onto highly selective colleges. The teachers care about students, and the engaged student will have many opportunities to have a high class quality experience. My son graduated from this school and is currently thriving at a selective university environment. He is responsible, open minded, and we owe much of that to the school systems that Bethesda had to offer.

column1: WWJH/HS is in a isolated area 120 miles for any large city. It is hard to attract quality teachers to an area like this. I have taught at this school for 8 years and have seen good and bad admin and teachers come and go. The good thing abut this bad economy is that we are able to weed out the bad teachers and even admin and now have a very decent staff. Student academic achievement and graduation rates have risen drastically. School spirit is high and the total atmosphere of the school has changed to a great place to learn and teach. Our biggest problem is lack of parent involvement in their child's education and the hours our students work at their jobs. Less than 5% of our parents show for open house. Seldom will parents come in for a parent/teacher conference. Few students will complete homework to practice their learning. Consequentially, we teachers try everything we can to encourage our students to reach beyond wht they think they can do. We have changed to block classes of 80 minutes to give additional time in class and we require students to take a study class if they are failing a core class. It's working, we graduated 55 students last year vs 32 before. West Wendover High School is a wonderful school and its staff and students are also wonderful! They have a lot of school spirit and they are fun kids1 WWHS has come a long way, most teachers do the best they can and go out of their way to help a student, For a student it is hard to live in a small town. Last year we had two students be state officers for FBLA and one for FCCLA. The kids are getting better, the school spirit is high. Things have improved. West Wendover has just been recognized as showing the most test growth of any high school in the state of Nevada. This is a huge honor and shows the dedication of teachers, parents and administration to our students. West Wendover offers an outstanding intervention program, after school tutuoring and we just received the Gear Up Grant for our 7th grade students. The school cares about my child and the other children in the school. West Wendover has the returning AA state boys basketball champions. FBLA, FCCLA and Skills compete and win at both the state and national level. The academic olympic team is very competitive at the county and state levels. This is a school we moved to 3 1/2 years ago and my child has had a wonderful experience that keeps getting better.

column3: Horrible admin! The classes are really wonderful however, the school lacks diversity and therefore, creates small minded staff. My child attends this school and has had a good experience. For the most part the teachers are great with the exception of a couple that should be evaluated based on the class performance. However, there are plenty of opportunities for kids to get involved in sports and the community. This school has a culture of its own,with a diverse group of children with different points of views and interests. Dont listen to the trolls that complain about a lack of diversity solely based on race. Diversity is more than race and only small minded people would think otherwise My child is an honor student. She has fought with the same govt teacher to get grades posted that were done well and on time. Despite her multiple emails to him and getting g the vice principal involved he still missed the final deadline e and had to have the grades books reopened by the superintendent! He refused to give her an A with an 89.5 in his class despite the VIce principals suggestion he do so. We are now experiencing the same thing all over again the last quarter of the year. We fear similar retaliation for speaking up. Def don’t feel this school is invested in the academic or emotional well-being of my child . Totally unacceptable. The main reason why I don't recommend coming to this school is because of the safety and the teaching issue. As a current freshman, my math teacher teaches too fast, and naturally that would lead to me asking questions. Just to sum it up, my math teacher is too impatient. For the safety issue, so there are classes outside the school's building right, so when the bell rings, and it's time for us to switch classes, how are they supposed to know if a shooter/murderer comes into the school dressed as a high school student too?

column1: We just moved to FL from out of state and chose a home based on the proximity to "good" schools. I'm afraid we have yet to be impressed with Park Vista. They decided to let all 3000 students share the same lunch period this year, which means there's no place for students to sit and eat, except on the ground with the ants. My calls to the school concerning this and another issue were never returned. My child is in an Honors Language Arts class where the teacher talks about assorted topics which may or may not have to do with what they are supposed to be learning. Dress code is not enforced. The athletics programs are good, which is the only positive my child talks about. Apparently the bar is set pretty low in FL for educating our children. Don't our children deserve better? I'm hoping to have a better impression of the school by the end of the year. If not, we will likely be moving our child to another school. I transferred here from the IB program in Atlantic High School and compared to Atlantic this school is HORRIBLE. this school has little options (such as classes and electives) for students like me. They also transferred me to regular classes so I went from IB to regular. This school is way way WAY too crowded for me. The students are THE most disrespectful kids I have ever met in my life. The guidance counselors offer no guidance like they are supposed to. If I can give this school 0 stars, I would. So focused on the students and their quality of education! Tries so diligently to keep students and parents informed and involved! Everyone has their cliques and groups. No idiosyncrasy is present- almost everyone dresses the same- MK bags, sky blue jeans, expensive shoes and sandals, polos, Sperrys, keds, toms, leggings, ironed thin hair, on bad days messy buns and sweat pants. And black girls need to be treated with more respect. Some to most of the students are very snobby, disrespectful to other students and teachers, ungrateful. In the end, this schools has a great education system, but the social life amongs students is just poor. Friendships are made and held with fake 2 faced kids. In the end you just have to find the crowed you fit in with and trust me you'll find it. Like mentioned earlier everyone has their groups they fit in. Amazing school!!! My son has attended 11th grade and is currently a senior there. All staff members are wonderful. I love how they keep their students engaged in education. If I have any questions and email the teachers, they respond quickly. Overall it is a great school. My son enjoyed his time at Park Vista and is looking forward graduation and attending college. - a parent The biggest issue the difficult grading is impacting the students ability to get into colleges. Even students at the top of third class with SAT in top 3 percent in the nation will NOT achieve many "A" grades and thier gpa will be lower then other area competing school. Even top ranked students with high level SAT/ACT scores are being rejected at colleges This school is a disgrace to the school district of palmbeach county. Students are constantly doing drugs off and on campus and no one seems to care. The teachers here are horrendous and don’t care about the children whatsoever, there only there for the money. There is no one on one at this school, there are 3,000 plus kids there so no one is focusing on your child. Overall the staff could careless about the children and the environment surrounding your child will be terrible so this school is a terrible option. Absolutely awful. Been there for my second half of junior year and all of my senior year, coming from an NY schooling system, real durastic downgrade in intelligence, urgency, problem solving, and many more issues one would call just having plain common sense Park vista is only a name, some wrong things, incorrect, specially in the athletic department, a lot of injustice and corruption especially in the baseball program, people in charge that do not have an idea of they are doing This school and the leadership at the district is a joke. Who stops children from going to their own prom? What a disgrace! I would give this school a 5/10 because freshman and sophomore year weren’t that bad, but junior year disgusts me to think about and senior year was a whole joke One star. The school doesn’t prepare kids for college, the teachers are bullies, no protection of students while on campus. The kids that go here only care about their designer things and the parents are entitled. So glad we’re out of there. Overall the school is very good. It's a lot better than surrounding schools in the area. Does not prepare students for college. Teachers were low quality and let students slide. There’s no incentive to do well since there’s no challenge. Great community school. I have three children attending Park Vista High School and each one participated in various sports programs on campus, clubs, and academics. This school offers large variety of programs, clubs, and academic programs. My kids feel safe and respected on campus. School is what you put into it, you have to want to learn and get involved.

column1: Consistently ignores those with gifted education needs. Uses all funds for athletic teams. Certain teachers that do not meet education standards are never fired because of the "good ole boy system." Salem Community High school is a decent school for everyone is friendly and pretty nice. Now also every school has its cons this school has its "bad seeds" this one it's kinda misguided teacher wise and student help. This school though is mainly just to relax and don't mind the bullies cause there is a lot of them here. The school could improve on money management because it's mainly worried about technology and upgrading it which they really need to worry about splitting the money between the different education departments. Finally that's all I have to say about SCHS all in all it's a good high school I have three children, two have graduated and have one still attending. My child that is attending at this time, does great in school and likes the teachers. It seems like most of the coaches, coach for the paycheck and not for the love of the students, they are either not trying or mean for no reason. I had one child that had a tough time in school and twice a year we had an IEP. We would set up a game plan even with me calling them, they would not follow it. I contacted the guidance counselor three times asking for him to talk to my child, since my child was having a hard time with a few things in his life, he never talked to my child. I was very disappointed. My last child did well in school, but needed a push in school and sports and unfortunately never happened. I am very disappointed in the administration, the feeder schools score much higher in performance compared to the state, but the high school drops the ball. The principle makes excuses, rather than finding solutions. He needs to stay working for the public sector, his excuses would get him fired, if he worked in the private sector. Effingham, Breese and O'Fallon would be better options, if you are moving. I graduated from SCHS last year and it really set me up well for college. I have so much dual credit I came into college with almost enough hours to be a junior in college. It's not like the classes are really that difficult either. The teachers teach you well. This has allowed me to be able to graduate from college with a bachelors in only three years. The town of Salem and Salem high school are very snoody, if you are not in the right clique, you will not fit in. You either have to be in the Elite crowd (or think you are) or receive Illinois Link and Medicaid. if you are middle working class, you are out of luck, nothing free or any help for your child.

column3: I love this school! Im attending it, and it has great teachers and it's kids are awesome too! My experience with Reed has been less than stellar. I have found that the teachers have grown apathetic to the individual concerns of the students or parents. The class sizes are 30 -1 or higher and the bureaucracy has been set up in such a way as to discourage teachers from trying innovative ways to teach and inspire. My son is well read and has a broad range of interests spanning science and literature and not a single teacher managed to inspire him. An illustration of the disconnection of teachers with their students was an occasion that my son had an accident that caused a severe black eye, not one teacher asked where or how he got the injury. If athletics is not your primary concern, look to charter schools. i just graduated from this school and i have to say it was an amazing experince it has the elements of the classic high school in it all of the teachers are great. yes sometimes the ratio of students can be a littel out rageous but they have students that are more than willing to help out others. also to be succesful you have to co-operate with its staff to really get help or enjoy it to the full extent. the school i feelt paid to much attention to athletes and less to other programs but it still has amazing other departments. the only reason some may not be inspired is they had the harder teachers and didnt like the teavhers for it every one there has character and i will miss not going to that school any longer This school has great resources available for parents to help their student excel. The counselors are friendly and will answer any questions you have. The parent resource center is available for all parents to use and they even offer free classes on graduation prep, college prep classes, etc. Of course, they have great sport teams if your child is an athlete. My daughter is on the basket ball team and they have excellent coaches. It may be an older school, but the learning is quality. It is what you and your child make of it. It is an awesome school academic and sports wise school . Great teachers and is always updated with information and great friendly staff and these teachers care . I have 2 daughters that go to this school and the teachers are always in touch with parents to let us know how are children is doing great excellent or just needs work .

column1: A step above an inner-city school. I attended Moniteau coming from a wealthier family within the area. THe school's school is meeting standards, not educating and going beyond the scope of precedent. Advising is THE single worst element of the high school. Upon graduation I am attending a nationally top rated university, on my own merit. The advising program gave little inclination to what classes would benefit me, how SATs & ACTs measured activity, how to prepare for AP exams and I was clueless as to what an SAT2 was upon graduation. Teachers came from the area, and taught to the area mostly with the goal of community college or tech school.. Moniteau is not the best school for students. Bullying is a major problem, many faculty members just don't care about their students. Moniteau is not the best school. I have been here 3 years and I still don't like it. I was in all honor classes when I transferred here, and now I don't even have a science, math, or a history class because they refused to give them to me. Now instead of having classes I needed, I have Music appreciation, two study halls, and a bogus cu math class(I do not consider this an actual math class). If I would of stayed at my other school I would of graduated a year earlier and now because this school I might not be able to graduate next year. Their 11th grade history class is a 9th grade class I toke at the 1st and 2nd high school I went to. The school cares little about the students education and more about their sports. Do NOT send your children to this school, they will learn nothing here!! I actually know someone who GRADUATED from Moniteau and cannot even read! I'm not kidding. I's true! The school is a full year behind other school districts in the area. My daughter started here in 7th grade, she did the exact same work she did in 6th grade in Butler school district. They even used the same books she did in 6th grade there! There are several teachers who like to bully and intimidate students. The office is no help with this. The vice principal actually likes this quality in teachers. One male teacher will call girls "dogs" and bark at them if he doesn't think they are attractive looking! I talked the vice principal about this too, and she didn't care! The office people are extremely rude and unorganized. I'm surprised they get anything done in there. It's August 18th, right now, and I've never been notified when the first day of school is! I have absolutely nothing good to say about this school. If you're a football player or a cheerleader, you can do anything you want. If you are not , then you are not important to the teachers or staff. It's really a shame. Supportive teachers, great athletics and coaches. I was very well prepared to enter one of the toughest and most highly competitive colleges in the nation upon graduating from MHS. Of course, it's not just the school; I had tremendous, active, and involved parents too. Moniteau is an amazing school that offers diverse programs that prepare students for whatever path they take post graduation. Nationally ranked athletic and academic teams from a small school in the middle of nowhere Academics are not stressed at all. There are a few of involved teachers but overall very low emphasis on any education beyond high school. My son was told mid-way through his LAST year that he should bring his grades up if he wants to go to college- WAY too late for that to happen. Moniteau was a so-so school. Nothing special but nothing to look down upon. I think the teachers try their best, but don’t have the best resources coming from a small rural area.
