column3: This was a great school. In this school you are listened to the teachers are nice. Great school to go to. At the moment the staff is going through a weird changing phase where half of them teach in outdated methods and a ready for retirement and the other half just started teaching and don't have much experience. In a fee years it will get better. The administration has also been changed two years ago so everything that comes with that needs so happen and settle down. In a few years I hope it will become a great school with good academics and staff and administration that are on the same page. Other thanight that there is tremendous school pride and support for sports and other extracircular activities. There are a lot of caring individual teachers, but they are held back by poor administrators more interested in legal CYA than helping children. When children are average and have active parents, they have decent outcomes, but if children are significantly above average or below average or have special needs, the schools do not support them well and tend to be actively resistant to parental involvement. (Speaking as a parent of 4 with children that range the full gamut). The administration at this school, Shaw and High School need a complete overhaul. A lot of administration is hired because they are friends with one another an highly unqualified. They use underhanded tactics to bully children and parents. Beware.

column1: Licking Heights has great teachers, but the administration lacks common sense. The administration is terrible at planning events, activities, assemblies, etc. The departments do not communicate well, nor are they taught how to do so. Students who are allowed to arrive late to school or dismissed early are sometimes not made aware of important activities or certain honors. I was a student who was allowed to arrive late (by the start of 2nd period) and I was not made aware of the fact that I received and Honors Diploma until the night of the ceremony, and when I tried to pay for my stole (which they would not be able to use again as they say 2012) to go with my gown, they would not accept my check because I was not made aware that all senior payments had to be in cash after a certain date. The only students made aware of having to pay in cash were those that had outstanding fees, which I did not. As stated before, the teachers are great and care about the students and want them to do well, but the administration is not as good as it could, or should be. I could not be more disappointed by the high school. We just moved here and I expected more from a school with an excellent rating. It does not appear that the teachers or the administration care AT ALL. Many of the teachers will not respond to me when inquiring about grades or status of my child. Even tho they have a system to post grades, assignments, etc, it is not used often or updated enough to keep up with my child's assignments. My child was failing 3 classes and I never heard from one teacher through the entire quarter. The foreign language teacher this year has no idea how my child is doing (all F's) despite repeated appeals to her, nor has she made ANY effort to help him repair his grades when he has asked. It also seems to be a behavioral free for all. It does not appear there is a standard of behavior or any discipline at all in the school. If you care about your child's education, don't send them here. The kids grades do not match their content knowledge. Some of their teachers have indicated that they give them points to get them to the next higher grade. This school district violates its own attendance policy by going back and excusing absences months after they have occurred. Overall, this district does not help the kids there be accountable or excel at knowledge. Grades are given but not necessarily the grade earned. Also, teachers seem to be not in the classroom with the kids quite a bit judging by video from the classrooms that I've seen posted by its students. We moved here 5 years ago and I thought the schools were good at the time. I had one child in 6th grade and one child in 3rd grade at the time. However, the schools have really gone downhill over the last 2-3 years. My daughter transferred out to a charter school 2 years ago in the middle of the 9th grade because the high school was just not challenging enough for her. They do not have anything to offer advanced students and she was very bored academically. My son transferred to an online school last year due to slipping grades, bullying, and absolutely no help from the staff at the middle school. The online grade book is not updated regularly. My son once spent two days straight in lunch detention because a teacher put demerits under his name by mistake. When my son tried to ask why he was in there, he was told to sit down and be quiet. When I called the principal to complain, he acted as though it was just a mistake and no big deal. My son was also beaten up at the bus stop once and the school said they could do nothing about it because he was not on the bus or school grounds. pick up child on time,which I see is not happening.phillip wagner say's need another high school is he joking omg enuff Why is my daughter so afraid to go to Licking Heights High School this year ? Licking Heights High School is a wonderful school compared to others and I find it quite excellent, although some parents need to spend more time with their kids to help them learn at home. I'm very happy to have my Daughter in this school Was a great choiceVery organized

One of them created their own business and are doing very well using what they learned while at PHS. The second child obtained his Masters Degree and is now teaching in Chicago Public Schools - again using all he gained from this fine school. We are very pleased with this school and moved into the area specifically so our children could attend Sanford, Sundling and PHS. Excellent teachers, staff, programs, IT and science labs. When parents are engaged, this high school provides education that is challenging and prepares student for the real world and their future. I really enjoy the fact that the teachers actually care about you inside and outside of school and are always there to help through the difficult years Great education for my children, preparing them well for college and grad school. Many extracurricular opportunities and well educated and compassionate staff. Bad teachers a lot of bad things in the bathrooms and the building is old bad school to be at bad bad

column1: Faced with enormous cuts and hard decisions, the board, teachers, parents, and community have rallied behind this junior high/high school. With a very strong support system and team work, the students are still among some of the brightest. Board members and teachers have continued strong leadership and students are still thriving in this rural community. The programs may have been scaled back, but the student love this school and are still very actively involved in making it the best. The school spirit is unsurpassed. At every event, the entire community is involved to participate. Most importantly, students continue to graduate in exceedingly high numbers. Teachers are encouraging and have remained focused on providing the best curriculum even amongst forced pay cuts and few lay offs. For a district in a poverty income level area, you would never know the disparities when feeling the pride walking into this school. Teachers have given the utmost respect and dignity by the superintendent and board members. Students even attend some board meetings to share projects or show slides. It truly is a dynamic setting. Wonderful small schools with caring, passionate teachers. Great community involvement. Our twins went to Shawnee Mission schools from kindergarten through 4th grade before we moved south and we've had a much better experience at Jayhawk-Linn. No regrets!

column3: My school is outstanding in the way that the teachers and staff try their hardest to educate the future of our society. The only problem I have is that some policies are too strict and learning isn't as rigorous as I need. I have been accepted into the IB Program this year that they have been running for a few years now and am very excited for my future in learning, hopefully it will be more challenging. Sussex Central is a diverse community of learners. Teachers truly believe all students can learn. The best and the brightest are pushed with rigorous course offerings within the IB program and more Advanced Placement courses offered than any other school within the county. Struggling learners are afforded deep support with smaller staff to student ratios and tutorial period built into schedules for previewing curriculum and content and remediation. Sussex Central also has many opportunities for students to get back on track to graduate if they have faced attendance and discipline issues preventing them from earning the maximum amount of credits towards matriculation in previous years. Sussex central also houses the largest English Language Learners program in the county to help teenage students who are new to the country work towards a high school diploma and build basic skills needed in today's workforce. The school has a firm but fair discipline policy to ensure that classrooms and school environment are conducive to learning, free from the distractions linked to student misbehavior. My experience at this school has been okay. Some of the teachers are unneccesarliy ridiculous however, enforcing the rules for some students while not enforcing the rules for other students based off of race. My experience at this school so far have been pretty decent. The teachers are great and I have loved most of them all equally. However, I had mentioned my first year to guidance how I was sexually assaulted by a student, and they were never punished for it. Someone had told me the best thing to do at this point was to post a rating that warns parents of that sometimes they will become bias with their cases, mine of which was just covered up and never talked about again. Anyone who plans on going here, please talk to your child more often and make sure they don't have the same thing done that happened to me.

column1: Marist is not a school for the meek and mild... the kids feed off the weak.. it is not as Christ centered as I was hoping. The kids are basically college minded, and act that way too. The staff encourages secularism by allowing the kids to disrespect eachother..the holy spirit has no room at dances , and all the music is bump and grind. I've known many kids to be inappropriate with eachother in person and over the phone during school time... I have taken my daughter out and I will home school her with online public school..not what I want but hey, if someone sells small class sizes, Christ centered and great academics...I'm in ! Academics is all they can sell here! We have two students at Marist. When we were moving to the area, we toured three high schools, including Marist. After our visit to Marist we knew as a family it was the right school for us. The small class sizes and rigorous curriculum were a few of the reasons for our decision, but it was the sense of community we felt when we walked the campus that was the deciding factor. Marist provides a welcoming, nurturing environment. We are so glad we decided to visit the school and see for ourselves all that Marist has to offer. The school’s multi-faceted approach, focusing on the “whole person”, prepares students for a positive and bright future in ways other schools do not. We could not be happier with our choice. The staff-to-student ratio, strong academics and size are what drew our family to Marist. Our daughter's experience has been excellent. She loves her teachers and the administrative and counseling staff and feels cared for and listened to. Marist was much better prepared than the public schools to shift to remote learning at the onset of the pandemic and we have been impressed with the support the staff are providing in these difficult circumstances. I highly recommend Marist. Having retired from Marist Catholic HS in 2019 after 19 years as the registrar, I can fully endorse Marist as a welcoming, academically challenging, and supportive community for high school students. As the registrar, I enrolled them when they applied to Marist as freshman, and then cheered them on when I organized their graduations 4 years later. The small class size and the effort that Marist makes to welcome students from all areas of Lane County create an environment where students feel connected, seen and that their success in the classroom is a top priority. Marist has been a great experience for my son. We were both concerned about the amount of homework, but it is manageable and he is learning great study and organizational skills, the small class sizes means he doesn't get "lost in the crowd" (although he confessed he would like that option... like when a teacher calls on a Sunday afternoon with concerns!), he tried a sport for the first time and loved it, he enjoys being part of another team as well, he was able to start his own club and he found the retreats to be "heartwarming"-- his own words. I have been impressed with the professionalism and skill of the teachers, even with the challenge of teaching through Zoom and their dedication to each student. He graduates next year and Marist will have prepared him well for further education and life. Highly recommend! Our experience has been exceptional. The teachers and staff at Marist are dedicated, generous, kind, and friendly. Teachers challenge the students to be their very best. Students also have many opportunities to grow academically and spiritually. We are fortunate to be a part of this fantastic community. Such a great place!  Marist Catholic is hands down the best high school in the Eugene-Springfield area. It offers an unparalleled opportunity for academic, athletic, social, and spiritual growth, along with a tight-knit, family atmosphere. I took full advantage of the Honors, AP, and College Now courses Marist offers. In addition to building critical thinking skills as a result of these classes, I was fortunate to enter college as a Sophomore based on credits! Marist's teachers are excellent, and many of them have been part of the community for multiple decades. They know their subject matter inside and out, and it shows. Attentive teachers and small class sizes ensure that each student gets what he needs to succeed. Furthermore, teachers are more than willing to provide individualized attention. I always felt comfortable approaching them for help, and they were always happy to provide it. Amongst others, I was particularly impressed by the quality of the English, History, Science, and Mathematics departments. Thanks to Marist, I felt incredibly well prepared for the rigors of a collegiate course load at a Top 100 National University. As a top-flight college preparatory institution, Marist offers more than just academic excellence. Its holistic approach to education sets it apart from the rest of the area schools. Almost every student is encouraged to participate in multiple sports, clubs, or other extracurriculars. I thoroughly enjoyed my experience as a member of the football and golf teams, in addition to the Christian Leadership Class and Retreat Team. My development as an athlete, friend, leader, and spiritual being was every bit as impactful as my classroom experience at Marist. Additionally, learning how to balance academics with extracurriculars was critical to my success in college. Last but not least, I found lifelong friends at Marist! I don't have kids yet, but if I did, I can't imagine sending them anywhere else for high school. I am truly thankful and blessed to be part of the Marist family! Love this school, was a phenomenal experience overall. My son just graduated last year. Accommodations were made for him as an ADHD kid and, though I wouldn't describe him as a scholar (yet), his teachers were invariably caring, supportive and concerned with his well-being, both academically and personally. Marist is small enough that everyone knows each other, but big enough that you can try lots of different things-- he was in golf, water polo, theatre and started his own club. I highly encourage anyone who's thinking about a really fine education for their high-schooler to consider Marist. Faith-based was a plus for us, but students who are not religious are welcomed and respected and I often hear from alums that one of the most memorable aspects of their Marist education was the retreats.

column3: All three of my children graduated from WBHS and with each one came different challenges. My oldest has a terminal lung condition and they went out of their way to help when he was hospitalized. My daughter loved many of her teachers; one was even a retired FBI agent. My youngest son has Autism, you would think that he would automatically be put in a special needs class. Oh no! You see, WBHS was the last link in a chain started years before. In his IEP every year they would keep challenging him, some of which I didn't think he was ready for...but he accomplished every one. The Chesapeake Public School System is the absolute best! I should know because me and my 5 other siblings all graduated from OFS (ages 64 - 42). In fact, my son had the same English teacher I did when I was in high school. He ended up graduating with a 2.97 GPA and that was a regular diploma having 26 credits! I also appreciated the fact that when my oldest son got into trouble, that they did NOT go easy on him. For every action there is a reaction. The staff is incredible, WBHS has the best teachers and staff! My son loves it there also. We are locating to Chesapeake in June 2015, and I am interested in any UPDATED info regarding this school? Enrolling our kids was the WORST experience ever!!!! The guidance office is the worst dept and offer absolutely no help in the process. They dont return calls or offer any help whatsoever. There are janitors that think they are administrators and harass students continuously. When brought to administrators attention, they blow it off. As for children on IEPs, they do not help with academics if they are struggling and allow them to sleep in class, just collecting the funding. TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE and we are moving just to get the kids out of the district and into a school that cares about our children!! Very sorry that this is my daughter’s school. School is too big to meet the students needs. Too many students in some classrooms. Guidance is no help. Bullying and sexual harassment runs rampad and you have to fight the administration for them to protect your child or file a police report before they will take your child’s safety seriously. My child spends many hours studying at home for the SOLs using computer websites. She has to do this just to pass because of the inferior education she has gotten. I’ve been going to this school for a year now. So far so good. Nice school and teachers are so respect The school is way too crowded. The halls are so full when the bell rings. Ask for a tour and to observe classroom changes. The cafeteria has 6 shifts due to the number of students. PE classes have to share one small corner of a gym. There are a lot of big and aggressive kids there. Multiple fights daily. The administration often cannot discipline kids due to city rules. Class sizes are huge. COVID-19! has made many things worse. The school was rated a 9 out of 10 six years ago. They have added a new wing on the school, but they have the same halls, gym, cafeteria, and auditorium. School was to max out at 1500. They have over 2100 students. Chesapeake continues to zone new apartments, condos, and housing. Wait until those massive Amazon warehouses are open. My children were late to class often because they had to squeeze in between packed hallways. Half of the students don’t want to be there, and the teachers are afraid to say anything about the massive loitering. Bullying, drug sales, all kinds of PDA, are rampant. Big, athletic, track and football players are taking advantage of shy young ladies. They have recently hired a new principal named Keith Hicks after my children graduated. He was a fantastic principal at Joliff Middle Sxhool. He may be able to overcome some of the issues that the City of Chesapeake created. Kids with struggles will not find help here. As I checked test and academic reviews before moving to the area, I was hopeful but I believe as new results come through it will be evident they have a broken program. Teachers unwilling to help guide and support students from ALL backgrounds will become more evident. Inclusion is not practiced at this school. I have two high school graduates (Class 2022) coming from this school both graduate with honors and heading to a top University. The faculty and staff are dedicated to high learning for those who are invested in their children future.

column1: My son goes to this school and has come out of his shell and has become very involved with this school. He likes it so much that he has decided to become an Ag teacher. At first I was very hesitant to send him freshmen year because he didn't know anyone and we didn't know much about the program. The teachers are wonderful and helps a student above and beyond their jobs. Because of this school my son is involved with the FFA, is President of the District and is very ambitious and excited for his future. It's great to see a teenager have such drive like he does and its all because of his school. Usually senior year not too many kids know what they want to do but he has known for a while and will be going on to further his education in the field of horticulture. I would recommend this school over any other high school. Its on a smaller scale for classes and your are not a number like the bigger schools. You have more of one on one at this school. I went to WHS from 7th - 12th grade and it definetly helped shape my character. Going in 7th grade I was a shy little person but graduating in 12th grade I was a very up beat involved person, and recieved a number of awards because of it. WHS has provided a number of extracurricular activities for people like me, such as athletics, clubs and after school programs. I made a number of friends at whs, a few of which I still keep in contact with, but I definetly keep in contact with the teachers more. Going in freshman year I wasn't sure to expect with other students coming in from outside schools, but it changed my friendship dynamics definetly. One of my closest friends was from out of school and we still keep in touch. The academic program was challanging all through out but the teachers helped us keep up with the material and the testing material was challanging enough for me to get into the wonderful college I'm in now. I went in as a shy little person and came out a strong leader amoungst groups that did not seem to really care about the program. I loved attending WHS and I hope my children will be able to attend WHS in the longtime future (like 20 years from now). Our son went here and it was the only time he ever liked school. Most graduates stay attached to the school and will jump right in to help with fundraisers and school activities as adults Excellent atmosphere for our child. The range of course offered prepares them for real life. So happy with Wamogo.

column3: I've heard great things about this school! I know someone who used to teach here and has spoken highly of the small school movement. I thought that this school would be good because it was near UC Berkeley. But it is not. The teachers here give out packets and the students do drugs. My granddaughter is a freshman . I am a retired teacher (from another school district) and really impressed with the leadership, the extensive programs offered by Berkeley High school and the amount of parent and volunteer participation. I just attended Back to school night and the quality of the curriculum and the teacher koowledge and organization of the curriculum was outstanding. BHS has many students from outside the district who are there without permission and contributing to overcrowding. They do help raise test scores, so...there you go. They are mostly in IB and AC. The school has many good, committed teachers, and are terrific examples of their profession. The principal is an excellent communicator and seems to really care about the well-being of the school community and stakeholders. BHS is diverse; racially, economically, immigrant and intern'l (children of foreign scholars, expats), whose mastery of English is developing. This nuance is not reflected in the test scores, but it is one of the things that make the school and community rich and amazing. The extensive offerings of AP, honors classes ensures that the smart kids that test well of all backgrounds will be engaged and challenged. The sports, arts, and language programs are beyond belief in the many opportunities from beginner to advanced levels. Each year, 100s of college admissions counselors from all over the US and foreign arrive to meet with and recruit BHS students. Our student has attended both private and public schools, and I can say that BHS offers a world-class private school education for free. The extra taxes that Berkeley homeowners pay ensures class size reduction, full-time librarians, field trips and more. It's very easy to get involved at the school as a volunteer, so you can see for yourself. It's a large school and at first very confusing to sort it all out, but after 2 yrs, I can say that we're thrilled with the academic and citizen of the world experience our student is receiving. Berkeley High is amazing in so many ways. Students are able to find such interesting classes: afro-hatien dance, video production, computer programming, forensic science. My kids (a junior and a sophomore in AC) have had an amazing experience overall. The principal is very engaging with the students and very communicative with parents. The staff, counselors, and volunteers are very helpful. Many of the teachers are excellent. The down sides are that it's an enormous school, so you really need to watch your kids on powerschool and communicate with them about typical high school problems (drugs, feeling lonely, trying to fit in, and so on...). If you advocate for your child, they will come out of Berkeley High being independent and worldly. I am a current student at Berkeley High and it has been really hard. Teachers could care less about my thoughts and opinions in the classroom and discussions are rare. I mostly learn from packets, textbooks, and worksheets. I'm in IB and the kids are competitive and close-minded. Everyone only cares about themselves and their own grade and don't really care about what they're learning, as long as it gets them into a prestigious school. Dominant students get A's and introverts or students with learning challenges don't get any attention. If you are looking to send your child here, I would suggest looking to a smaller school if they genuinely love to learn and appreciate community-like learning. Berkeley High is a wonderfully diverse institution that thoroughly prepares it's graduates for life. Our family had an awful experience at BH, my son attended BH, and would advice any parent to think twice before going into the "diversity" the school sells. Do your own research and don't be fooled by the few items that are positive about the school, while it is true that the school prepares your child for life, so does the jungle, so think twice. This school offers incredible options for students to explore high level academics, other career pathways and really great club/extracurricular activities and sports. Kids really need to self-advocate sometimes to get what they need but the administration has been responsive to kids if they are persistent, in our experience. This school is too focused on social issues. And it’s huge and under funded. Solid they passed me let’s goooo bro

column1: This rating is so sad for me to see. I graduated there 55 years ago when the poverty level was more like 85-90 percent, I didnt even have water in our house, YET, I graduated from Xavier University in Cincinnati BECAUSE of the great teachers I had and the discipline we had in the 60s. Its sad to see everything is AVERAGE. I suppose it oculd be worse, but we were taught not to only be AVERAGE to be ABOVE average in everything we tried to do. I am sorry to hear the little high school I attended in the 60s is only AVERAGE now. John Dossey Cincinnati Ohio (Class of 1964) I have attended ECHS for a little over a semester, in just that short amount of time I have witnessed bigotry, racism, and a general lack of putting education first. This school is ran like a prison, students are searched, there are drug dogs brought into the school and parking lots, some may believe this is a great effort into stopping drug use. I agree to an extent that teen drug use is a problem to face in schools given true probable cause though I do not believe it should be placed over education. When there is already limited funding in place, we have battered, decades old textbooks yet the school finds money to fund drug testing and buy new flat screen televisions. Not to mention the general mindset of the staff and students this school feels as though you step into a time machine and are attending school in the 1960s, I have witnessed students being brutally racist and homophobic with no repercussion. They have a “bullying program” in place that has met twice in the entire time i’ve been at this school. The public school system is in place to educate the youth and create meaningful members of society, in this environment I do believe my peers and myself fight all odds stacked against the student body to succeed this is reflected in the poor amount of college readiness once leaving this high school. Overall this small-minded school has given me the worst public education experience yet, and i’ve attended 3 high schools. If you have any option at all I would recommend you choose a more qualified school that is interested in the growth and success of their student body.

column3: We are new to this area and live in Lone Peak boundaries. After talking to many other parents and students, we chose to send our children to American Fork High. So happy with our decision. Teachers and counselors couldn't be more helpful and the student body seems very welcoming and friendly. My kids are excelling in challenging classes and thriving at tjs school. We relocated to Utah, my son is a senior this year with very good grades at his previous school. Back there, only 24 credits were required to acquire an advance High School Diploma. Here at American Fork HS, the standard diploma requires 28 credits for graduation leaving students that come from other states with no other choice but to accept a mediocre diploma with a "mark on it" basically stating they did not meet the credit requirements for graduation along with a "differentiation at the graduation ceremony" as they call it, held at the same time in front of the fellow classmates who received the 28 credit standard. To top it off, the diploma won't state a home school, rather it will say it was given from the school district. My personal experience is that students get discriminated here if they are from another state which holds other requirements however, students are still able to graduate with honors in that state. But instead of taking in consideration of these students good characteristics and hard work in the past, they demean their abilities and hard work that they had put in at other schools making them believe they are not good enough for future education. The Best School Ever, They Care about the students and that they graduate, they care about your education and what best for you, Im glad that i was able to graduate, they do need to work on the Counseling Department, some of the Counselors they seemed like they didn't want to help the student with graduating, they need to stop making students pay for their Transcripts, they used to send them to the school and give you your transcript but now you have to pay. but in all they are the best school out there I loved American Fork High school. It has a really good atmosphere and feel to it. The student body is friendly, the teachers help those who want to learn and it's just an overall fun high school to be at. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a good high school to go to. The majority of faculty seem to be sincerely concerned about my child's success and doing well in their classes. The school is very big and students education and development needs may get lost on administrators. specifically unimpressed with the administrations concern for budget needs as it relates to technology in a classroom (something was broken and needed replaced) and the administrator stating they could not help a student because if they did, they would not have the funds for the other issue. The student had a state approved development plan to adjust some resources - WHICH PLAN AND RESOURCES HAD ALSO BEEN APPROVED BY THE SCHOOL DISTRICT! I get stabbed with a fork every day by the guy who dresses as a fork and he should be the mascot. Horrible! Both my kids belittled because they didn’t belong to the Mormon church. It was a great experience for me as a parent and my children who attended. Each became fluent in another language because of the great teachers in that department. I am very grateful for the education my children received and experience my children had at American Fork High School. Thank you Alpine School District. The school is just focused on passing students rather than actually teaching them.

column1: Very Bad school! Bullying is out of hand. Principal will only defend the ones doing the bullying since they are the local kids. If the issue is pushed then 1 kids gets a slap on the hand but then 10 kids retaliate. If at all possable find a different school. Dont subject you children to this school.

column1: I just moved to the area which is zoned for Archer High for my incoming 9th grader to attend. The first person I saw and interacted with was the Receptionist/Registrar; she couldn't decide which title she was apparently, until she felt like doing the roles of those job descriptions. Ms. Turner is imcompetent and lazy and selectively hels who she feels like talking to. She is not the face of Archer that should be greeting new parents and students. Ms Thompson in Registration and the 9th grade counselor Ms. Morton definitely turned our perception to the positive with their professionalism and helpful attitudes. I believe the education is probably the same as the various schools within the district but I think there may be a little bit of racism in which I hate to throw a race card, but it is still Georgia. Some of the teachers I feel are more likely to work with certain students and the others are left to their own devices. I chose to take my student to this school as an out of zone student but I think I am having regrets :( We moved to Ga a couple of years ago and decided to send our child to Archer instead of our assigned school. Overall we have been very pleased with the school. We especially are pleased with the amount of help that the counselors give the students. My child's counselor is always available and the receptionist in the counselors office is amazing. She is always giving the students information that can help them and has a great relationship with them. Archer High School, in my opinion, has done an outstanding job. My son has attended Archer for four years (Senior...and college bound) and has enjoyed EVERY DAY. I must give the teachers a round of applause. He has been fortunate enough to have the most wonderful teachers a parent could ask for. To keep teenagers engaged in this day and age is extremely hard. I would have to say that thanks to them (the teachers and staff) that my son has exceeded/excelled and is looking forward to college. His teachers have really prepared him for the next level of his education. I can't thank them enough. As a parent this is the most amazing feeling. Yes, WE ARE ARCHER...and YES ARCHER High School Band ROCKS!!!!! So does the Band Director, Mr. Wolfe. THANK YOU! THANK YOU! THANK YOU, ARCHER!!!! From a VERY proud parent. We just love this school. Great teachers and environment. Great for sports too. Archer is in final four state high school football! Archer in the year of 2013-2014 has raised 17 Freshman AP Scholars out of the 29 AP Scholars in the state of Georgia. In order to achieve this title, students must pass three AP exams with a score of 3 or higher which receives college credit. Archer is renoun for its athletic excellence with participation in the 2014-2015 year state football championships. The volleyball and softball teams excel at Archer. The wrestling team has won the state championships three times in a row in the past three years. The teachers at Archer care for their students. Most do everything they can to help out struggling students here at Archer and truly care for their teaching subject. Archer has grown as a school in the last 5 years and will continue to grow broadening the horizons of students and providing opportunities for greater education Had some great teachers and an overall modern facility. Plenty of AP classes to choose from, a large variety of clubs and organizations, tons of great students, and an overall good atmosphere. This is one of the best schools in Gwinnett! I have no regrets about Archer High. If you are looking for a good High School this is the one. Archer has given me a second chance to fit in and focus on my education!! Love AHS, where Administration is proactive, cares and listens regarding the students. AHS has created a community where education is important, and students thrive. Great school! My son attended ninth through graduation. We/he had a great four years. He attends UGA now and was well prepared for college. Well my soon to be sophomore is not returning. That sums it all up. My daughter excelled and had a wonderful experience at Archer High School! Archer really prepared her for college! Excellent, I am very pleased with this school. Archer HS prepared my well for college who is now a Computer Science major at Georgia Tech. I highly recommend this school. Racism in this school is atrocious ...in all directions. Multiple fights occur daily which happens in all school because kids today are savage but the fights at archer are knock down drag out brawls. Two students brought guns on the same day and the students were taken in but no lockdown happened....where is the concern for our kids safety? Not to mention the recent homecoming disaster. Homecoming is open to all grades, however they only have the space and tickets to accommodate 1/3 of the students. Tickets went on sale and the website would not work because so many people were scrambling to get on and grab the few tickets that were sold. We tried for hours to no avail only for the school to respond and say sorry for the inconvenience the site crashed due to too many people being online and we are not selling any more tickets. This would have been my daughters first high school dance and we already paid for a dress, shoes, accessories and alterations ….all of which are non refundable. Most importantly she is devastated and so upset now that she cannot go due to the schools lack of planning. Im sorry but simple math tells you they sold 1000 tickets only at $25 each. That's $25,000 they made in ticket sales. You mean to tell me you cannot get a larger venue with $25K to accommodate all of your students and give them all an opportunity to purchase a ticket to homecoming? Another common sense though would be if you cant accommodate all students why open homecoming to 9th and 10th graders. Keep it to juniors and seniors if that's the case. Another option would be restrict homecoming attendance to students who keep their grades at a certain level. My child is an excellent student in gifted and AP classes with straight A's yet she has no option to attend the homecoming now.Additionally students that didn't have dates purchased multiple tickets for themselves and are attempting to sell them to other kids now for more? The PTA and school need to get it together. I will be joining the PTA because they clearly do not know what they are doing at this school and I am appalled.

column3: Never cared for the school. Had 3 kids go thru it. My son is not graduating this year all because he is one of those people who absolutely cannot get up in front of a group and talk. And this year Pinelands have a senior project which requires them to talk in front of their english class. He knew he couldn't graduate without that so he just blew off the whole year. He has always been a good student up until this year. I was forced to do speech in 10th grade at my high school and was totally humiliated every time. Still haven't figured out how that was supposed to help me in life. I'm sure my son isn't the only kid not graduating because of this. This school was terrible and the teachers were terrible, scary place to have your children attend. everything about this school was terrible. Teachers were perverts, and the food was aweful. School board was bad, way too strict. Highest pregnancy rating in all of ocean county. bottom line do not let your children attend this highschool. What a shame that so many negative comments are coming from parents of our wonderful children @ PRHS. I am proud to say my 3 children have thrived in this motivating, and caring environment. The school offers many many extracutricular activities not only including sports but community involvment, drama, academics, etc! You are so quick to to point out "how terrible PRHS is in sports"..SHAME on all of you. You are talking about my..our children. Every team has their time to shine in victory but the truth of the matter is the game/team work/trust building far exceeds the win!!!!!! The year my son was a senior the football team had a glowing record. The past year they did not win a game but let me tell you the young men who were on that team had the spirit and love for each other that was a lesson they will take with them troughout their entire lives! My 2 sons are college educated and my daughter still attends PRHS and is loving every minute of her high school experience to the fullest. She will be college bound, well prepared by the support of the school as well as loving, encouarging parents!!! Look to see what you can do for your kids, maybe this is where the problem is! GO CATS! This is a great school. I am a parent of a current senior girl. My daughter highly excels in her classes and is a student athlete. She is also a minority in this school and is loved my teachers and students. If your student is not doing well, don't always blame the teachers. It takes the want of the student themselves to succeed. My daughter had been accepted to a university in the fall with a major in Biology and was excepted to every college she applied to. Parents are also responsible for pushing their children to do well, set standards and expectations, and provide a nurturing home environment. I used to attend this school, I am now in college and let me tell you Pinelands has prepared me for college in so many ways. We may not have outstanding academic scores and our sports teams may not win as much as the other schools but I learned more life lessons from this school than anyone else in Ocean County. Pinelands is a small school and its like a family there, we look out for each other. The teachers are less like drill sargents and more like parents away from our parents. The coaches care about their athletes more then they care about the win. Learning is fun at Pinelands, high school is for making memories and all of the ones I have made are positive. You can say learning cant be fun if you are not retaining the necessary material but I have gone to all the schools in LEH and I am currently holding a 4.0 at college so they must be doing something right. If you come on here and want to rate the school bad because the athletics are terrible or because we have a lot of pregnancies, maybe try talking to your kids about safe sex and how winning isnt everything and stop blaming it on the school, you sound ridiculous. While this school and others in the district/area are getting bad reviews,our childrens experiences have been outstanding. There is a strong support system for the students and parents. Childrens learning does not stop at the end of the school day. They must have strong support at home academically as the parents and family must participate in the learning experience. The quality of the education your children recieve is a direct reflection on the continued learning they recieve at home. Remember teachers are not baby sitters. This school is so unresponsive. If your child has a learning issue or an attention problem, they do not know how to handle it. My son went from A-B's to F's. Almost all straight F's. Horrible. I am a Pinelands graduate with a doctorate degree and am very appreciative of the education I received there. The resources at the school are there if you avail yourself of them. Extremely caring staff and some great teachers. Drama Program is amazing. I think the parents that are complaining need to look at their children and themselves and not the school. The teachers cannot do it alone. if you are not motivating your children, ensuring that they are doing their work every night and helping them prepare for tests, quizzes and projects you should expect that they will fail in school and life. Making excuses for their failure and putting all of the blame on the teachers is the wrong message to send to your children. Pinelands Regional High School is a very good school, the staff are attentive to student needs and are always available to the students .My son graduated and is now attending Penn State University. Great school, good teachers and very safe!

column3: Lewisburg Area High School is simply great! The school prepares students for college and life. NOT NEARLY AS GOOD AS IT COULD BE.. Lewisburg gets excellent students and supportive parents. It resembles a suburban school district. The district encompasses the more affluent areas in the general area, and gets a special boost from the Bucknell faculty children and the children of many Geisinger doctors who choose to live in Lewisburg. There are many kids that would do well on tests if told to teach themselves. The school adds less than it should. The classes are not rigorous, and little homework is required. While AP classes are offered, most of the students in those classes are encouraged to not actually take the exam, which hurts the students who could do more if pushed. College admissions are a problem. Year after year, brilliant students that should be heading to the Ivies or equivalent schools get turned down. The school does not seem to have a strong reputation with admission offices, nor does it have counselors skilled at deciphering the process for students and parents. The administrators and many teachers seem not to have been exposed to excellent schools. They are content to be the best school in a backwater, but so much more would be possible with vision. I agree with the negative comments herein. My son is a freshman and is extremely bored with this school. He is not required to read any books for English class even though it is honors English. He has virtually no homework in the evenings and is just spinning his wheels. When he tries to sign up for courses he just gets study halls in stead. I'm not sure why anyone would choose to go to LAHS unless it is the only option. Talented kids are being held way back at this place. The only thing they seemed to be concerned about is having more police around. What a joke. On more than one occasion Lewisburg High School has run out of food to serve the students for lunch. Many students were left without lunch. Students who were able to get lunches shared and some students bought food at the vending machines. The school district is not suffering financially and can certainly afford to buy food. However, some families are suffering and for those students, that lunch might have been the only meal that student thought he or she could count on. The school pays Bucknell University $10,000 for every home football game, because they use the university's field, but somehow they don't have enough food for the students to eat. This is just one of the examples of how messed up the administration's priorities are. If you were to ask the principal about the situation, he would deny it, because the only thing he is concerned with is the school's image.

column3: I have taught at Ryan for 11 years. Despite attendance zone changes and administration changes, I have found that it is a school that has administrators and teachers that truly care about students and their success. Ryan has an extremely wide socioeconomic population of students. I find that this diversity is embraced by the students and faculty and gives it a "real world" feel. Students are challenged academically and have a wide array of academic and extracurricular offerings. Students are encouraged to be in all kinds of activities: athletics, arts, service clubs, etc. and just about every activity is highly successful. This success is due to the high level of support from the administration and the parent community. I enjoy working at Ryan and am looking forward to my own kids attending here someday. In spite of some of the negative comments posted here, I think Ryan High is an excellent high school. The students are given all the opportunities necessary to succeed. But they have to do their part and study. When I went to visit this school, the students were unbelievably inappropriate. It was quite disturbing. I am moving so that my teenager doesn't have to go to this HS. Ryan High School is only good at one thing. Sports. If you aren't a member of sports, you really don't matter to the grand scheme of life there. I have friends that go there and say the same thing. Also, the teachers don't really care and they let their students do whatever in class. My friends constantly have their phones out in the open and eating food whenever they feel like it. The district rules specifically states that cellular devices or any electronics are not prohibited for use during the school day. I had two daughter go to Ryan and did not have any issues with the education they received. They were both athletes and they continue to excel in college. I would call Ryan "a real world school" with a strong tie to the community spirit of Denton. If you want "a fantasyland school" then you might want to travel a little further south. I had a very hard time fitting in during middle school and i assumed it would be the same for high school but it was the exact opposite. Ryan is made up of people from every race, class and talent spectrum, making it very diverse. Unlike a majority of high schools, Ryan isn't your click based school, everyone knows everyone. Ryan is a family, not only in a school aspect but also in the community, offering activities and clubs for just about everything. I strongly recommend putting your child in at Ryan if they have a hard time fitting in or just need a fresh start because this school has been an incredible experience for someone who didn't know where they belonged. The small class sizes and teacher involvement gives all students the one on one attention that you won't find in a larger school. My son also plays sports and has received many opportunities on the field. It might have been a decent school for those with no mental disabilities, but for those that did, at least for my personal experience, was a total nightmare. I was expelled in ninth grade due to the staff's and faculty's "inability to properly handle the situation". Now my review is coming from around a decade ago, so things may have drastically changed since then, so please take this review with a grain of salt. This was just my experience from then, and for possibly other millenials that attended this school. You will likely get better or more accurate feedback from those who recently attended, or are currently attending (not counting the Covid-19 outbreak shutdown).Also credit is where credit is due, the principal of the school did acknowledge the inability to properly handle my situation, and had actively defended me during a hearing, not placing the blame upon me. So while there is a redeeming quality in the morality of the head staff, unless things have changed in that school since I attended, I would not recommend sending your child there. I had a much better experience within my brief time at District 1 within South Carolina at Saxe Gotha Elementary. I don't know how the higher level schools are there, but my experience at Saxe Gotha was actually quite nice and I had rather pleasant memories there. I cannot say the same for District 3's schools, at least not to the same degree. With a grant all Freshman and students in the Art/AV academy were issued free laptops. I've been attending Hillwood High School since freshman year. I'm currently a junior and my experience at Hillwood have been wonderful! The teachers, as well as the students, are very friendly and helpful. Some teachers may be strict but it is your education that they are working on. I'm looking forward to the rest of this year, especially my senior year. I have friends from other high schools that wish they could attend Hillwood, because of the negative environment exposed. You never know how good or bad a school is unless you have a personal experience, and this is mine:Hillwood High School has a very positive environment and no matter how much the students say they hate school, they admit that Hillwood is a lot more better than most other schools. -Class of 2014 My daughter is about to graduate in 2013 and has attended Hillwood all four years. Despite many negative comments and rumors we had heard prior to her enrolling as a freshman there, we chose to send her there because we felt strongly about the need to attend public schools. We were extremely pleased and surprised to discover that the school has been and is still continuing to improve it's acadamic stature among metro's finest schools under the leadership of Dr. Chauncey and many of the great teachers there. Hillwood may look like and old has-been great school in the middle of white suburbia, but it is definitley enjoying a rennaisance scholastically with a brand new state of the art library, excellent teachers who really care about the kids graduating and a comprehensive academy of five schools of focus for young adults to choose from to prepare them for college or immediate employment. Like many longtime Bellevue residents and avid supporters of Harpeth Valley and Bellevue schools, we are glad we chose Hillwood for our daughter and she is too. She has really enjoyed her four years there. I am proud to say that my daughters attend Hillwood. Since leaving Nashville School of Arfs their grades have skyrocketed!!! Thanks Hillwood!! I have been a teacher at Hillwood since 2010 and I couldn't ask for a better school to work at or a better group of students to teach. Since 2010 Hillwood has made major progress with end of course test scores, ACT scores, and has the highest graduation of any non-magnet MNPS school. Hillwood also offers three nationally recognized "Model Career Academies" and 17+ Advanced Placment courses. I would send my own kids to Hillwood! One has graduated (with honors) and another child is currently enrolled at Hillwood. It is full of excellent teachers and administration. They will go the extra mile for you. They have prepared my children for the real world. I wish more parents were involved with the PTA. It is the only thing lacking at Hillwood. Love this school! Great teachers, especially new math teachers. Love the Principal! My children are so happy here. They are being well prepared for college. Great school We are hillwood is the theme. They will and can help with anything. My son loves the school & his grades have improved greatly! He is getting more involved in activities. I am a parent of a graduate from Hillwood High School and i also have a daughter that is currently a senior . Both of my children have received a great education through HHS. The teachers are caring and well educated themselves. They are dedicated to helping your child reach their potential. My oldest graduated, and is now attending college with a baseball scholarship. My daughter has been accepted to Auburn, Clemson and Mississippi State ( just a few) and is eligible for several scholarships as well. While attending Hillwood they were given opportunities to explore the "Academies ", which helps you choose a pathway of study in Health Sciences, Art/Communications, or Business / Hospitality etc. I am really impressed with the training areas and equipment provided for these studies. ( health sciences has recreated the inside of an ambulance to help teach real world procedures). My children have joined many clubs and activities; baseball, cheerleading, concert band, National Honor society, and the Ambassador program which are just a few of the many activites available .The school does have its issues. The building is very old and in need of repair as well as the stadium and fields. column3: My son just graduated from this school. Initially after qualifying to attend the CAT program he only made it through his sophomore year (his own fault, started to coast on homework issues. They are strict). Due to zoning, his father is a Tierra Verde resident, he was able to remain in the regular part of this school. Having completed lots if honors courses he continued to take some advanced/honors as well as regular classes. We can truly say he experienced all aspects of the school. He also became a peer counselor, which means being involved without entire student body if needed. My son has many friends in and around the school neighborhood. We have always felt very comfortable in and around the school property. To have a truly in depth look and feel for the school, volunteer. This is the way to help the students and the faculty and to really obtain a true perspective. My son and I are off to his university orientation as I write this. I can honestly say this school made this possible with a child that was starting to drift. Did I mention the principle Mr Vicari..there aren't enough words to praise this man. He is truly a 'man of the people', you will admire him as we do. My son attended the CAT program. While the students who attend this school are top notch. The teachers fail to provoke success in there students. The majority of the classes are taught directly from textbooks and there is no focus on helping the kids develop critical thinking skills. In addition there English programs are extremely underfunded and I feel as though my sons education as imbalanced. The CAT program is extremely rigorous. Almost overly so. The kids receive hours of "busy work" each night. As a parent I felt like an outsider no attempts were made to allow me to volunteer at the school. There is almost no school spirit with very few events held for the students. While the safety of the school has improved drastically in the past few years. I would still say there is room for improvement particularly in drug prevention and education. Best School Everrrrrrr ! I go to the Lakewood High School and I love it here. It's Drama Free and There are barely any fights unlike Boca Ciega and Gibbs . Awesome school, great teachers. The students are given every opportunity to succeed. Which results in a A rated school and a Technology Magnet (CAT) that is rated #15 (2014) in the nation. Much is said of the Principal but Mr. Oberg is outstanding. He cares about the students and helps CAT be one of the top schools in Florida. The math teachers are tops. History and English teachers are not at the same level and are unavoidable. The band and robotics classes are top elective classes. The kids are competitive that helps motivate the kids. The school close by is often considered superior. With the exception of liberal arts, that is just not true! Ask how many matriculate into Georgia Tech or Cal-Tech, Lakewood is significantly more focused on science and engineering. It is not always easy we are able to maintain several extra curricular activities. One year in and we can say with 100% certainty that we chose the right school. The regular high school has not been a problem. The students have been friendly and the surrounding neighborhoods are clean. There will always be areas I could nit-pick, I prefer to focus on the benefits that have been offered by this program. The word is getting out and the CAT program is exploding at the seams, my expectation is that it will continue and that will only add to it's reputation as the best of the best will want into the program. terrible school and there is no progress being made at all This school is amazing. The students at Lakewood are very self-driven and hard working. The teachers and counselors always ensure the students are on a good path, mental health wise and grade wise. The school gives students opportunities like college level classes and preparation for college and the real world. If it was bad in the past, it has turned around. Lakewood high school has many students working on huge projects and making efforts to change the world. Stop bashing Lakewood and dragging it through the mud. Like any high school, things occur and some students may not be committed or motivated to do school work but the teachers and staff always go out of their way to ensure and provide safety, college/life readiness, and rules. All I have seen in my years there was people helping kids be their better selves and preparing them with real advice and love, giving all students a good environment to learn in with many experiences within those four walls as well.

column1: Hawthorne High School is a school with a lot of heart. 325 students in grades 6-12 participate in numerous activities--all at one time. Sponsors and coaches try to work around each other's schedules in order for the students to be able to take part in sports, drama, and cheerleading. Last year, the varsity boys; basketball team went to State; while they were working with the drama club to put on the spring musical. Over 100 students acted, sang, and danced in the show. Academically, the students are working harder than ever to keep their grades up. The number of students in AP English went from 6 to 25. The number in honors 9-10 went from 7 to 25. Math scores are up. Teachers are encouraging their students to plan for a college education and to take school more seriously. From all that I am seeing, the students have had a change in attitude and are working harder than ever to maintain a high GPA because they know without the GPA, they will not be allowed to participate in the activities available to them. What Hawthorne needs is more positive role models for the students to follow. Volunteers from Hawthorne are welcome to come help with the drama program. There are pros and cons to this school. Pros would be the staff are over all nice and the lunch is free. But the cons have more of over powering effect. The cons of this school are; Many to most of the student show no respect to the school leaving it a filthy and disgusting place. there has been instances that there was vomit in the halls a whole day before it got cleaned up, and multiple times of cockroaches just laying around dead. There is a little discipline within the teachers, mainly because some students are uncontrollably out of hand. One of my biggest problems of this school is the 4 block period scheduling. For me, I would rather have 6 to 7 different periods a day. It makes me feel like I have progressed more. There are not many choices for students in the classes thy take. I did not get the classes I needed this year which will cause me to struggle the next 2 years of my schooling. I was hoping to graduate early but this has caused me other wise. all in all, I do not recommend this school and I would prefer something a lot more then what the school is now Our family's experience has been a nightmare. Bullying purposefully not documented, medications never being administered or documented, and being told in a recent follow up meeting all of my student's IEP items were being continued, it is a great disappointment and loss of trust in some of the most important people in my child's life.

column1: Great school overall. I have several children in this school system and have been satisfied with most of the teachers, academic focus, sports activities offered and community involvement. There is some room for improvement within the community itself, mainly parental responsibilities and a general lack of discipline or control over their children's behavior. This has caused problems for my children and many of the other students trying to obtain their education and enjoy the high school experience. Some of these troubled students are labeled "special education" and are said to be untouchable by school leadership, thus continue to be an ongoing problem. Apparently, the state of Michigan has rules preventing "special education" labeled students from being disciplined the way a regular student beating on his classmates would be dealt with. Except for this issue, which may be a problem in many other school districts also, Summerfield schools have exactly what I like, small community feel with good quality teaching and caring leadership. Would not recommend this school to my enemies. The anonymous review from a student in 2008 is quite accurate. Our school board has good intentions but seems to let the administration persuade them. I do not feel the administration act as advocates for our kids. Summerfield is a great small school where community and knowing students are emphasized. The school is making major changes in instruction and grading our kids so that making sure they are proficient is the main focus. The biggest drawback is that this school cannot provide as many class choices as larger schools because they just can't afford to hire more teachers in this economy. I think that they make the best of what they have and really work to go the extra mile for our kids. You have to decide what's best for you and your family, small school with a community feel and the ability to play for just about any team/club, or going to a bigger school where your child is unknown and may not get to take part in as many extracurriculars because of shear numbers. As a graduate and community member. I've seen the changes over the years. The school is doing a great job despite a dwindling budget. Teachers care for their students and really get to know them personally. You're not just another face in the crowd. The school also offers numerous online classes, college courses, career and technical courses, and opportunities for dual enrollment. While there may not be as many choices "in house," Summerfield offers a well-rounded experience. Students just need to take advantage of it. 0/10 rating for school experience and learning ability.

column1: Landmark High School is one of best schools you could possibly attend... regaurdless to what any rating could say. Sure, there are a few flaws, but Landmark is an adaptable school with students and staff that are willing to create change that will benefit everyone. Being that this is an portfolio based school, we are not required to take regents (except for ELA) or standardized test. That is good because by doing portfolios you learn how to put together a proper research paper, give a visual & verbal presentation and discover things about yourself. Each of those things are highly useful in college. Best of all: the teachers/staff are 'real' and offer much knownlegde in and outside of the classroom. Im not sure if it is a good highschool. The students seem to be lazy slackers at times This is my son's senior year at Landmark. I'm so happy to know my son will be graduating from landmark. The staff has been amazing to him and myself. As a parent, I feel that my child has had a great experience at Landmark HS. The school community is welcoming, supportive, and responsive. Being a Consortium School, the model allows students to take performance based assessments (PBATs). This aspect was extremely helpful for my student, as standardized tests often produced anxiety that interfered with her success. The PBATs also provided her with many opportunities to sharpen her presentation skills, be creative with her projects, and take more ownership of her work overall. The school staff is amiable and approachable, and there is constant communication with parents! Landmark High School has a great sense of community, they prioritize support and seeking different opportunities. We also focus on presentation and essay writing so by the time we graduate we will be ready with the skills to go into a harder curriculum for when we graduate. The teachers are supportive is a reason why I enjoy coming to school every day, they ensure us a sense of belonging in our work. As a rising senior, I've had an incredible three years making new friends and preparing myself for the next four years of my life in college with the support and care of Landmark High School. I am a Junior at Landmark High school. One of my favorite things about Landmark is the teachers and staff. They give their students attention and always provide extra help when needed. Many teachers and staff i have met have became some of the best i have had. This school always does is best to create a community inside where students can feel as included as any grown up and where their opinions and needs are always listened to. There are also many electives and clubs to take part on such as Student council, volleyball , cooking , robotics , fashion and many more that helps it students stay not only academically engaged but also participate in other entertaining activities. There has been trips such as ice skating and field day. Overall my experience at Landmark has been great.

column1: I came here as a senior, and after viewing this website, expected to find a distinguished school with semi-challenging classes and a decent curriculum; however this school is far below average when it comes to academics. They seem to cater to below average students and have no amenities for advanced students. Although the course guide claims they offer A.P. classes, in reality they do not. The only advanced classes they offer are online college classes that are only accepted at a limited range of schools, and cost $350 apiece. The teachers, while all very nice people, do not seem capable of educating the students adequately. While they understand their subjects, they can not seem to pass that knowledge on to the students. One teacher would give tests on subject matter that he had not even covered, and then scream at the class when we did not understand the information. One teacher constantly forgets what she has already taught us and what assignments she has already given us. The school does have a couple good characteristics. The art program is excellent, and the school never runs short of basic supplies, like paper. If you have any other choice, I would not recommend this school. I struggled a lot with my learning disability and this school was ill-prepared for a student with my type of hearing situation. The teachers were super nice but the problem was with the vice-principal and counselor, who made my life a living hell. I transferred schools because of both of them. As public schools go, PR is above average in academics and has some of the best teachers in the area. With that said, we pulled our daughter out of this school at the end of her sophomore year because she was being bullied by the assistent principal. She's a straight A student - graduated from High school with a 4.0 - but she does have a learning disability which seemed to annoy both the assistent principal and one of her coaches. I cannot count how many times I had to go to the school to pick up a distressed child - who actually entered counseling because of the bullying she recieved from these two persons in leadership. Her teachers, on the other hand, were awesome - and she connected with them very well. (She plans on inviting several of them to her future wedding) So, while I do reccommend this school based upon the teachers and the academics, I would tell any parents putting their child in this school who has learning disabilities to watch closely for signs - such as a change in behavior in their child. Just be careful, stay involved and advocate for your child if they can't advocate for themselves. (Mine was an introvert and held the stress from the bullying in - not a good thing) Academically, by the end of her sophomore year she was ready for college classes because of the outstanding English, History , and Science teachers she had. The teachers prepared her well for college and instead of going her last two years to PR, she went to a community college where she also attained straight A's . So cudos to the PR teachers who prepped her so well for college. Shame to the persons in leadership who bullyied her to the point where we had no choice but to pull her out. If delinquent clowns were to takeover this school it would be an improvement but possibly an insult to the clowns.Poor communication, worse understanding of the rules, ultimate failure led to our child being completely left behind. Their form of apology? “Oops! These things happen!” Only at the new school we attend, they don’t. LPSD 38 and Palmer Ridge High School do a great job overall. The staff, teachers, and administrators are professional and work well with the students. -Curriculum. They offer a range of courses that satisfy the needs of students.-Post secondary preparedness. Excellent. The school helps young adults prepare for college AND they partner with Pike's Peak Community College to help students access career education while in high school. This is such an important offering because too many schools try to push every child into colleges (where they learn no skills and amass life changing debt) when they should instead be pursuing a career in the trades.-Extra-curricular activities. Top notch. The school supports their student athletes and has multiple programs that are very competitive in the state.The school board is run by competent people in the community who put the students first. This is a fine school as are all of the other schools in LPSD 38.
