column3: My son is a sophomore this year and he's had a great experience at Ballard in 9th and 10th grade. He has enjoyed almost all of his subjects and I have found his teachers to be very responsive to questions. The Maritime program and Mr. Foster are exceptional. The one time I had a question for his school counselor, she was great, too. I have seen no evidence of bullying and lots of school spirit! This school is one of the strongest in the district and state academically with many AP courses, clubs such as robotics and programs such as biotech, digital film etc recognized nationally. The Jazz band was chosen this year, along with Roosevelt High from Seattle and only one additional high school in WA state, to attend the most competitive Jazz competition in the country 2018 Essentially Ellington competition & fesitval in NY. Only 13 bands are chosen nationwide. The robotics team won the world championship last year out of 25 countries, including groups from China, Canada, Turkey, Israel etc and over 400 teams. Something no NW team has ever done. We have found many excellent teachers, including computer science, math, science & LA teachers, and the counselors are great considering the school is highly over-enrolled until the new school opens. The principal is perhaps the strongest and most effective in the district. He is focused on serving and challenging all the students in the community at the school, including students who are highly capable who could have gone elsewhere. In recent years many highly capable students have chosen Ballard their neighborhood school over Garfield and are happy and doing well. I had a pretty good experience here after transferring from another school. The building itself could really use an extra wing, though. Most of the hallways and staircases are so narrow and they get extremely packed when kids get out of class, to the point that I genuinely believe there would be causalities in the event of a fire, for example. The only open spaces where you can stop getting pushed around is 2 of the entrances and a cafeteria. Seriously, as schools get more populated, this place would give me claustrophobia if they tried to accommodate more kids. Also a LOT of the students tried to peer pressure me into buying coke lmao, what a waste of money. Mostly good teachers though.

column1: They place too much inportance on boys sports. Sports are great and they do teach the kids skills, but I will repeat what I have said before...how many kids playing sports in Edgewood EVER got a FULL scholarship to a college? What they need is to put more money into helping make the kids ready for the real world, so they can get a real job. Football is a sport, not a job skill required to make it in the big city. I love Edgewood, but the school falls short in several areas. July 7 - are you an administrator? Sounds like it. Everyone in this community knows that this district has political appointees for administrators who do the bare minimum. The bare minimum is offered in course offerings and the district does only what it must for the district - not the student. There is nothing to crow about in a district that should be exemplary...but that is not. Leadership is a joke. I am not an administrator, teacher, or employee of the district, no matter what it may "sound like". I write positives where some write negatives. EVERYONE means ALL. EVERYONE does not share this opinion. We have been in other schools with far greater issues. Not EVERYONE will be pleased & will always find a fault. I did not read anywhere that any particular school was on an exemplary TAKS list. This must be a "joke" or rumor. Maybe, this school is on the list for 2010. Way to go students & teachers for receiving an exemplary rating. Have a GREAT 2010-2011 school year. Who said you had nothing to "crow" about? Let us hear that crowing noise. SUPER JOB!!!!!! My academic rateing for Edgewood is good. My child is a sophomore with a learning disability and she has shown great progress from year to year. The school has it's problems, as does all schools, but over all the school academics are good. I only wish that t hey would put more money in classes and not into athletics. They hire to "WIN". They spend to WIN. If your child is not a who's who's child, they are set aside and not allowed to excel in athletics. Athletics is great, but an extra. Winning is great, but an extra. How much do you win when you compromise the self-esteem of a child for the WIN. So the athletics department in this school rates 1 star. I AM THE PTO REP FOR HIGH SCHOOL, AND WE ARE IN THE MIDST OF A LIBRARY REMODELING PROJECT. WE NEED EVERYTHING FROM BOOKS TO WIFI UPGRADES. ANY HELP IS APPRECIATED. OUR SMALL LITTLE CAMPUS GETS LEFT OUT OF A LOT OF BENEFITS BECAUSE THE OLDER KIDDOS ARE MORE SELF SUFFICIENT, AND PARENTS TEND TO BE LESS INVOLVED THE OLDER THEY GET. The new admininistrators at the High School are hateful and show favoritism to the wealthy kids.Support staff are treated badly.

column3: i have my second child getting ready to graduate from chs. my son has been in avid since entering chs what we thought would be a good program and thus far has but now not so much my son has meet all his math credits and does not want to take another math class but the vice principal says he has to because of avid and refuses to take him out of the math class he keeps talking in circles and says he would have to leave avid to do so now he wont be able to graduate with his avid class just to get out of a math class, I have made phone calls to the vice principal to get this done and has not answered me yet. this school is rude and dont take what students want just what makes CHS look good .my son has worked hard to get where he is AP classes and all . any sugestions ????? If I could give it zero stars I would. The staff at this school is horrible, mainly the people in the office. As a student, they made me feel very unwelcome. They were consistently rude and unhelpful. I felt very harassed as well. There was one instance where I had a problem with another student, and they did nothing to help, in fact they made the situation worse. A majority of the students are very stuck up as well. However, there are a few genuinely good teachers that seem to care about the students. But overall, I do not recommend attending this school. No matter what anyone says, I had the best four years of my life in this school. If students come into this shool willing to do their best, and instead of complain, learn to immerse themselves in the education it offers, they will have no problem. I can honestly say this school did it's best, and coming from harsh background such as mine, I was able to fully appreciate it's quality and mostly warm atmophere. I can say my only regrets are the never changing negative attitudes of most of my school mates, and how I didn't take full advantage of all the club, school activities, and athletic teams it easily offered us. I'm an IB graduate at this school, so I can tell you a few things about this school. It's a nice school but there really is nothing special or unique about it. The staff is average, principal okay, and IB program is actually subpar compared to the other IB school in the county (much better trust me). The options that this school provides to its students is also subpar. The experience is, in the end, satisfactory at the most. Though it has the name of "Celebration", bearing the "prestige" of the town, this school is as good as the others in Osceola County - which is not a compliment. If your child is choosing between this schools IB and Gateway's IB - choose Gateway. PS Our football sucks. Horrible staff, completely distracted with their own lives and do not care about the students. This school actually lost my child! If a child shows up at a school office with a suitcase, you do not offer to call him/her a taxi to the airport. You call their parents!!!! To actually make it where my child would rather run away than attend this school is insane. Only spanish is spoken here, if you or your child doesn't speak it, do not enroll them. Not a learning environment for children who already speak english. This is an Excellent school. It's hard to find a principal as caring and involved with the students as our new principal, Mr. Lisby. I have had kids enrolled in this school since 2006 and am happy to say that from the beginning they have been challenged with a multitude of AP classes, enabling them to be competitive and get into top tier universities. I have witnessed graduates getting accepted in the best schools in the country. This school offer the IB program, AVID, a Biomedical Program, Duel Enrollment as well as 5 different academies within the school. The students can even walk away from graduation with a Microsoft Certification. There are many opportunities for parents to become involved and in my experience the teachers are always appreciative. Celebration High School is a pretty good school, some teachers are AMAZING, others not so much. I feel like a teacher and a student should have a friendly connection because when you enter the classroom you don't feel like a teacher is teaching you, you feel as if someone you have known for a really long time is teaching and that's what being a teacher is all about but god damn some teachers are just plain horrible. First day of school my math teacher said " I am not your friend, i am your teacher, don't come to me with your personal life and if you're having trouble at home go to guidance don't come to me" I literally got up from my desk and left the room. Some teachers shouldn't be teachers, simple as that. Celebration high school offers great opportunities for students that gets them prepared for college.From AP courses to dual enrollment.Arts and Sports.Clubs of all kind and fun in school activities such as 101 carnival at the end of the school year.The school is very diverse and the campus is nice.We do have a lot of kids but it doesn't feel overcrowded,unlike other schools in Osceola County. terrible. most of the students are spanic, not descriminating or anything, but that school basically speaks spanish. i'm from Brazil and doing exchange in this school, and honestly, I've learned more spanish. These kids are as well disrespectful and fights almost everyday. Did not have a good experience. Terrible. The staff is the worst in Osceola County. Dean Mr. Munoz never answers the calls of the parents. Personally I was calling him for two months and never answered a single call. The school does not guarantee student safety. Words spoken by Mr. Munoz. Today there was a fight of great magnitude where you see how they hit several students. There is no security. In general it is one of the worst school, even if it is located in a rich city The majority of the teachers are nice and they try to support the students when they needed and school installations are fine. Good school, proactive (sometime too much) parents and engaged teachers. Overall my experience at this school has been pretty well. I will be graduating May 2019 and will say the academics portion of this school is strong. However, as a hardworking athlete, I must say the boys and girls tennis team is amazing. Coach Darren Holt and Coach Rachel Holt do everything in their power to make each individual athlete develop not only as a player but as a person as well. I highly recommend the experience of being able to be on a team with such knowledgeable and professional Coaches. Be sure to prepare to work hard!! Overall my experience at this school has been pretty well. Very pleased. It's a great school that my son enjoys attending & they cope with the COVID situation in a professional and flexible manner. Highly recommend. Susan Binau My son is in the IB program and it's by far the worst mistake I've made. All these teachers do is give them a ton full of homework and let them drown in it with no support. I asked for a meeting with the IB counselor in the beginning of the 2020 school year with no response. Forgot about athletics if your in this program because the coaches do not care and expect you to be at the practices Overall my experience at this school has been pretty well. This school is a joke. Can’t register your student until 8am. Sorry but parents have jobs to get to . You should have someone there at 7am. Since the school is open at that time. This school and district don’t care about your students at all. This is the worst school I have ever been to. We have school threats often, the school is filthy and we have students having sex in the bathrooms. Lots of drug use, The worst "Administration" ever not believing in victims of sexual assault or assault in general. Not doing anything about it. Short staffed. We do not feel safe in this school. Unless things change in the school we never will. School fights break out often. We fear coming to school a place where we should only be worried about learning.

column1: I am extremely disappointed in this current Saint Mary's. I had a very positive opinion but for the last 5 years, I must say it has not lived up to the standards. The discipline is out of control. There is behavior that is not conducive to a Christian conduct, and the discipline is nothing. I feel if the 'student' does not have the money they are bullied by administration, and those with the money are allowed to be disciplined with a blind eye, meaning no discipline. What happened to the strong sense of 'molding' the student and assisting the student to became 'leaders' of the future. Now the administration is more concerned with their own agenda and punitive. Wake up Saint Mary's, I have removed my financial support and have encouraged others.

column3: I am hoping that the Mesa School District hires us a good Principal that cares about students is what we will get. Mr. Luketich is retiring, and I hope we get a young up and comer in MVHS that will inspire our students to be the best that they can be. Here is hoping from a parent of 3 future MVHS students that we get somebody who cares about all students learning as if it is all that matters. This is a great school, too bad our Principal is retiring. I am hoping they recruit that Mr. Buechers, the turn around Principal from up near Superior or Miami. My sister lives up that way and this guy holds many of the same philosophies as Westwood's new Principal, and boy has that placed made a change for the better! I guess these guys worked together in the past and have created a whole system of success for schools, that really works! Mesa needs young, dynamic and courageous leaders if we want to be able to compete in the east valley! This High School has the look and feel of a small College! Very professional and great learning environment for the students. Although a good many are concerned about the "LDS" population, I do not see where this should have anything to do with how the school is rated. My family isn't LDS but shouldn't learning and how the school is run be the rating and NOT what kind of students go there? Moutain view is an outstanding school. I know many of you are concered with the LDS faith but it is not a problem at all. There isint very many "cliques". If you're a hard working student you will suceed in this school. While i am with the LDS faith i have talked to many non members who have said the LDS kids have always been great! Moutain view is a changed school. Dont take it from parents who have just over heard there kids complain. I have first hand expierence. No teenager is going to tell there parents how good it is. They just say the negative. Please consider this school. Reading the reviews I was surprised to read the teachers favored the LDS faith. Being of the faith I chuckled because I was not favored. In fact I was more picked on by the teachers. I wouldn't say because of my faith but because of my personality and lack of ties with sports. They say it's a great school but I was never academically in any of the higher classes. Resources were great and I had good teachers for the most part. There are more races now then when I went there 2005 but it's still a high school and not a bubble despite a large population of Lds people. In fact our class president was not LDS so you don't have to be of that faith to be involved with any leadership. My son was very excited to start this new high school being from another state this was an even scarier experience. Everything was going great until he started getting bullied. He was assaulted by another student ,with permanent damage. The school would not believe his side of the story and seem to side more with what the problems kids stated. My son is terrified of going to school here as t hey just slap the wrist of these kids and nothing happens. We attempted to talk to the principle and he has not returned our call. We talked to another staff member as she was told we were looking at restraining orders on these kids. We have never got a concerned call from anyone about putting restraining orders on students and it being a concern. We have since pulled him. I was never questioned as to why we were withdrawing. It seemed like an everyday normal occuarnce. The staff was more concerned as too why i didnt have his textbooks with me to return. Which i will. This school has great oppourtunites in their programs but there lack of concern of a students safety is disturbing. I graduated in 2012, this was the schools worst academic and athletic school year ever since opening in 1976. The students don't have intuition to get the work done and teachers really don't care if you pass or fail. When talking about athletics, the school has fired 3 head coaches for football since I've graduated. What is the staff there thinking? It's like they just find the best resume and assume what's wrote on paper can transfer to performance. This school will be a nobody school within 10 years. I was ashamed to go there in 2012. I feel bad for the parents and students that deal with that school now. If your son or daughter has a car try to enroll them in desert ridge or red mountain it will be a way better highschool experience. Still learning how this school works so far I've had issues with the administrative people being rude in the office to parents and students. I currently have two children attending Mountain View and couldn’t be more pleased with this school. As a parent, I have constant access to my children’s grades (and any missing assignments); which ensures no surprises pop up on my children’s report cards. The teachers, staff and administration are friendly and supportive to both my children and myself. Anytime I have reached out for guidance I have been quickly responded to and very happy with the help/advice I received. The Academic Advisement Department (specifically Carla Boyle) is awesome at Mountain View. Carla was key in helping me guide my children in planning their 4-year course selections to ensure a positive High School experience. There are so many course choices available and opportunities for students to get involved in clubs and community service. This is a great school and I am so glad my children are a part of it! I have 3 children attending Mountain View and all are receiving a quality education. However, my husband and I have been extremely disappointed in the principal and his passive attitude about the success of all students. When we expressed our unhappiness about a poor quality math teacher at Mountain View he simply shrugged off the concern. Aren't we a campus of champions? We haven't felt like he's a champion. I am a former teacher at Mt. View. I can assure all that if parents are willing to put in a bit of time to structure a schedule, learn about courses and teachers, and push for an appropriately challenging curriculum, the reward will be tremendous. In the category of large public schools, Mt. View is excellent. For parents, dig in, do your homework and the results will be excellent. Generally unimpressive. Several of the teachers here are outstanding, and because of them, this school gets two stars instead of one - you really feel bad that they have to put up with the mediocre dictatorship of the administration every day. There is a higher population of LDS people here, both the students and staff, but as a person not in the LDS church, the only time I regret it is around Christmas, when the school puts on a "Winter" Assembly, where the majority of the music is explicitly religious Christmas songs. I definitely wanted some diversity there at least, especially the year when a joke about Judaism was delivered in one of the performances. Sure, Mountain View puts up a facade of being a good school, but honestly, there are better opportunities elsewhere where the staff as a whole genuinely cares about the students as people, and not just as graduating machines who can improve the statistics and ratings of the school. WONDERFUL! TORO NATION IS A GREAT PLACE TO BE. Still go here at the moment, sophemore, i'd give it a 7/10 I had a great experience. A lot of people like to act like them not being Mormon is what made them hate high school... but I am not mormon and I had a great time and great experiences I loved this school when I attended! Mountain View is a great school with great students and teachers! There are cliques, but you get that everywhere. For the most part, the school does what it's supposed to, and everyone has fun. I don't even want to explain why it's 1 star just don't go I'm a sophomore at this school. I'm disabled. My legs barely work. I can walk, but not well. This is the most horrifically inaccessible school I've ever been too. The ramps are so steep that it's easier to take the stairs. They lock the elevators, and sometimes they don't even work. All of the wheelchair accessibility buttons on doors are broken. The doors can barely clear wheelchairs anyways. I have collapsed during class before and called the "Toro Tipline" for a wheelchair only for one to never come. On a day that I had a particularly bad flare up, my pain was at an 8. I went to the health office, told them by problem, asked for any kind of mobility aid, and they offered me ice. I couldn't WALK and they offered me ICE. The teachers here are all horrible except for a handful, the students are bigoted and judgmental, the campus is a nightmare to navigate. You're better off just not getting an education than going here. Mostly all of the teachers here put so much pressure on you to uphold mountain view's "reputation." They also expect you to respect them when they treat you like children and could absolutely care less about us. The teachers think that they are above us and they act so bigoted it is annoying. Last year and the year before, the school had this thing called workday-wednesday which was basically a day to catch up on work. For some reason almost all of the teachers got rid of it this year because they were being too "lenient" and "it didn't help the students." For me personally it realluy helped me stay caught up with all of my school work and it made things less stressful. This year it would have been especially helpful in my math class. My teacher gives us up to four assignments every day and doesn't have us take any notes. He will go through a few problems with us an that is it. None of our work is on the computer, it is all on paper, this leads to him losing some of the assignments. Some of my assignments I have turned in but then gotten F's on because he lost my homework before he graded it. Circling back to the bigoted personalities of the teachers, my orchestra will pick on the students and favor others. Instead of doing fair chair placement she will put her favorite students in the front and her least favorite in the back. Plus she is supposed to switch players between the first and second violin sections every quarter but she never does. She wil swap about 3 kids at the start of a new semester. She also constantly tells us we are doing horrible and never gives us any positive feedback. She never really teaches us anything, we will do something wrong and she has us play it over and over again until it is to her liking instead of telling us what we did wrong. Moving on, there often issues and contention between students and the teachers/staff do nothing whatsoever to fix this. Last year there was a bunch of fights, students kept pulling the fire alarm, and there were threats as well as bullying. Though they do address the problems, nothing is done to fix it except putting more security at the school. The staff and the teachers also do not take into consideration that some of the students have mental illnesses that can and do affect how they learn. I have anxiety when it comes to public speaking and yet my teachers still make me do presentations. It is clear that the staff/teachers do not care for the students as much as they should.

column1: My children attend Fisher's middle and high schools. My son is in grade 10 and my daughter is in grade 8. Today was my daughter'a first day of Leap, she was quite nervous but then told me that the teachers really helped her calm down. My daughter is a bad test taker and gets very worked up when she takes an important test. She takes all honors courses and so does my son. They like most of their teachers but, like all children, despise others. But I do think Fisher is in need of the money, every bit counts. While Fisher has it's problems, I wouldn't send my kids any where else.

column3: At first, I was going to Fontana High School and there were alot of physical fights, drug use, and the teachers were not teaching me anything. I felt like I was not going to be able to go to college. The bottom line is that that school sucks. My parents transferred me to Jurupa after hearing how good and safe of a school it was. After transferring, there were so many drastic, positive changes, i currently have straight a's as to before i could barely pass my classes. This school has been a major change for me, and you can see the difference between Fohi & Jurupa Hills. If your child will be attending Fohi, Jurupa is a much better school. Really surprised at all the people that gave it a good rating when in reality this school is a joke. Teachers at the end of the day only care about their pay check greaty little people. The IB Bio program has been a complete disaster. The grading scale is setting up students for failure... just wait when they attend college and fail. More students need to fail in order to have a well established society. If you pass all your student especially if all their doing is just showing up and getting an A in the class we are corrupting social system. We need those people to fail or else we wont have people that flip the burgers. Their is so much more I need to address put this will do I will send a strongly worded letter to the school about some more issues. This school is a complete joke. They claim to be better than the rest of the schools in the district, but in reality they are perhaps the most disorganized school ever. They keep bringing up the fact that they are a new school and they are still learning, however they keep using this "no excuses" policy on the children, when they should be using it for themselves. The staff members at Jurupa seem to only care about their paychecks and not about the student's education. They promised their students an enrichment program but have failed on all 3 years it was opened. The principle went missing for several months and the students were not informed and when he came back no questions were answered. The kids that attend this school are perhaps the most shameful of all. But it's not all their fault, the school values their sports rather than the education. Star players of the football team receive special treatment from the staff and the teachers. I wouldn't be surprised if they got away with murder in the school. There are still more issues, but the character count limits the rest. Jurupa needs to get their act together and soon before they have a riot on their hands. I used to move around a lot when I was starting out high school. And each school I was at never made me feel comfortable. But when my mom transferred me to Jurupa Hills my sophomore year second semester I knew it would be different. The teachers instantly made me feel like I had a real purpose at making my dreams a reality. I had a 3.0 grade average for the first time. I saw a great change in my work and am happy to say that I am part of the first graduating class of Jurupa. There is no doubt that this school is a great place for your child's education. You won't regret enrolling him/her in this school. This school is unfair. Don't send your children here because they will regret all four years of their high school experience. I wish I had transferred out freshmen year because this school is ridiculous. They are so unfair taking away hat privileges when a year prior, we earned them. They take away many things that a high school should include for the actually high school experience, such as senior actives. All seniors should be able to participate in them, ALL. The staff are nice, you do come across teachers that are dull and only care for their pay checks. Personally, if you had to choose this school or summit, I'd choose summit. They have way more school spirit and an overall great high school atmosphere. I love attending Jurupa Hills High, the staff is trusting, helpful, and overall, they help with anything a student needs. Those who say the school is bad talk about the old staff and principle the school used to have, now there is better guidance, and better behavior at the school. Jurupa Hills is a great high school for any student to attend. 100% If that is the scale rate.

column3: When you read so many post that a school "isn't that bad" or "isn't that violent" then yes...it is that bad or that violent. West Charlotte 2013 test scores in math (9.7 out of 100) and reading (24.4 out of 100) are abysmal at best. Crime is everywhere (CMPD Crime map). I attended this school and I can assure all, my child will not make that same mistake. Honestly, as a parent, I felt like the schools administration was highly disrespectful. They didn't care about how we as parents of the students attending this school felt on certain situations such a school fights, horrible test scores, and the amount of people skipping school on a daily basis. I feel this this school is content with it's bad tactics, and low exceptions. The principal is awesome, she really cares about her students. The Counsler Mrs Robinson helped my family thru some difficult times and because of her diligence, encouragement and holding my daughter accountable, my daughter graduated, when all the odds were against her. Its a great school The parents just need to be more envolved . The school cant do it alone. WC is s great school! The buildings could use some updates but the faculty & staff are very dedicated to the students.The IB program is like a family, small & supportive! We love it! I attended this school in all my high school years and I can honestly say this school was BAD. I would not recommend this school to anyone who genuinely cares about a good education. Most of my teachers had given up on teaching. Not knowing anything better, I stayed there, didn't learn a thing, and in retrospect, wasted precious years of my life. The teachers who TRIED to teach were constantly interrupted by students acting up, sleeping in class, fighting, talking back etc. Teachers cannot teach if they are constantly harassed and interrupted. I would not recommend this school to anyone.

column1: I LOVE DOSS HIGH SCHOOL MY SON IS IN 10 TH GRADE HE IS IN ALL HONOR'S CLASSES. AND THE TEACHERS AND STAFF ARE WONDERFUL AND NICE MY SON LOVE'S THE SCHOOL TO GO DOSS I really like this school I was a little worried about my son going to Doss but now that hes in Doss he loves it. column1: East Aurora High School offers the kind of high school experience many parents wish to give their children. The schools are a wonderful aspect of living in East Aurora, which is a town that prides itself in having a strong sense of community and positive social values. The students are educated well. A wide range of courses and extra-curricular opportunities are available. Upon graduation, more than 90% of the students attend college. I recommend the school highly. As an EAHS alumni, I feel strongly that EAHS is an acceptable school. However, when I arrived at college, I felt ill prepared and lost academically. I could not compose an essay effectively. I could not handle the demands of an academic school and I believe this contributed to my struggle during my freshman year in college. (No, I did not go to school to party or pledge a sorority. I went for an education!) EAHS is small. It is a school that is highly focused on offering all sports possible and unfortunately not performing any of them spectacularly. I do not believe the school is focused on education. Nor do I believe that it is sympathetic of seniors who wish to be challenged through graduation. Seniors are often left with such a light schedule that it is like they are in limbo between high school and college. It's too bad that the district does not wish to push seniors to be stronger academically and serve them better in the transition to college. I have three children coming up in the district. I have great reservations about sending them to the high school. It's a shame because Parkdale Elementary is wonderful and the middle school is outstanding.

column3: As far as the learning, Clay-Chalkville Highschool is a great school. But some of the people that go there make the school look bad. There's a great deal of drug usage there. And it's also a little racist. Not the teachers, but some of the students. But Clay is an overall good school. They have great teachers and you learn a lot. The football team is not half bad either! I enjoy going to Clay Chalkville High. I learned a lot and will continue to. This school is known for one of the greatest football teams ever. But as far as the envirement, people are rude to each other and to teachers, there is ALOT of drug usuge, vulgar language and/or harrassment, and having to be here 5 days a week makes it miserable. The learning envirement is okay but I've seen better. This school needs alot of improvement. I've been here for about a year now, and I just hope this school will get better. This school USED to be a great school but now its overcrowded and sucks. The staffs great they do the best they can with little help from the school board, (the school sends the to the board for stealing, bullying etc.. The board sends them back a week later). There is alot of bullying and stealing and things like that going on that nobody seems to know how to deal with so its swept under the rug and continues to happen. This has become one of those schools that you just dont want to send your child to. Again the school staff is great the education is good but its hard to learn anything in the type of situations you have to deal with there. Until the school board becomes stricter and takes these situations seriously this school will continue to go down hill. FOOTBALL IS NOT THE ONLY THING THAT SHOULD IMPORTANT TO CCHS . If you have a learning disability like dyslexia or ADHD, I would not recommend this school. Discrimination, is just one of the many issues. Also, children with hearing and physical impairments are treated as second class citizens. PS: Get ready for lockdowns, this seems to happen every month. As far as academics go, this school could care less, even though they have good teachers. The only thing that this school cares about is Football. Rather than add more capacity to the school, they made a turf field for football. If you are an amazing football athlete this school is for you. If you are looking for a good education experience go find another school. I do understand that the new turf was trying to get people involved in school activities, but you go to school for education The Jefferson county School System does not offer a program for High IQ students. Yet, I am a parent that pays taxes and have freedom of speech.....isn't this "leaving a child behind?????" The "no child left behind program" is structured to put all IQ's in one pot. Period. We left this "system" so that our student can truly soar at the speed desired. Eating my words....I said I would NEVER homeschool. It is totally awesome!!!! We will have a High School graduate at age 15. If your child needs more time, this is awesome!! I have a friend that has a student needing extra time. This has caused her child to increase scores since it is based on the pace you need. Soar at your own pace!!! Leave the "system."!! Great teacher involvement. They actually want every child to succeed!! Also the level of communication with the parents is off the chart! GO COUGARS Great School Great Teachers! However I'v been sending my children to the Chalkville school system since 1993 my last child graduate this year in 2017 and I must say the school has changed and I can't say for the best. I'm just glad it's over. I do not recommend this school. Average at best.

column1: I wouldn't send my child to this school unless you don't mind your son being bullied. The athletes (not all of them mind you), target "different" boys and harrass them. My son was expelled for fighting back after 3 years of bullying and nothing was done to the boys doing the bullying. I also had teachers make me aware of the problem but nothing was done. I would not recommend this school to anyone. Archbishop Curley is great school because it has a good curriculum and a variety activities for the young men. Also, most of the teachers will take time with the young men to make sure that get what is needed academically. Yes, all schools have some problems, but none ARE perfect! Send your sons to Curley! Excellent choice for me! My son is doing much better after he adjusted. A proud Sophomore parent! Extraordinary leadership, faculty, student tracks and culture. Teachers and staff are great. The student body is tight knit, disciplined and fun. Best decision we could have made. I can't thank this school enough for the changes in my son! When he started Curley his freshman year he was so far behind. He was coming from a Baltimore County public school that failed him miserably. He started in the Anthony program, and never looked back. He was out of the Anthony program less than halfway through his freshman year. He's had nothing less then Bs all 4 years as he's now a senior. He's played 2 sports as well every year. Not only that but he's going to a college he never would have gotten into had he not gone to Curley, his grades wouldn't have allowed it as he was mostly a Ds and Es in student in PS.Never had any issues what so ever with bullies, not seeing playtime on the field or anything like that.

column3: This school treats the students like they are in prison. There are way to many rules. They are students not prisoners. If you are not smart, a cheerleader, or play sports, you are treated as an outcast. If you can't keep up with the rest of the class they put you in a closet with the work that you dont understand, instead of taking a few minutes to explain it to you. My daughter was given 5 days suspension for having a cell phone in the class. I wonder if the kid that videoed the teacher beating another student recently on the news got 5 days suspension. This school not only breeds poor sportsmanship, they encourage it. The staff and administration are politically driven, and they ignore the rules for the right people. A subpar education with poor attitudes and morals. This school hasn't changed since the 70's. It is a very political school. I personally seen teachers who have previous teaching experience and had to fight tooth and nail to get a teaching job at this school, than there are some who are very young with no prior experience who get a position within the school because of who they know. The school is very clicky and they do not follow a school uniform policy. Some girls get away with wearing short shirts and some do not. Every student is supposed to wear a polo shirt without a logo and all polos have logos. Some students wear express, abrecrombie, and some wear kmart. Students can tell who has money and who doesn't. This leads to discrimination of students. The middle school vice principal is very demeaning to both the students and to parents who are the same age if not older than him. As I said in the beginning, this school hasn't changed since the 70's. If you live in one of the mini mansions in the area, your kids will do find in this school, as for all others your children may to attend a different school or reach out for counseling services. It's am best school around awesome education and the best sports and coaches in the area Valley View does not provide the academic quality education to prepare for college. My four children made so many good friends at this school but none were prepared to even complete Community College course work. The teachers low salary may be the reason for their lack of interest & motivation for their students. Very few graduates go onto College and even less remain in college.

column1: I am currently a student attending BCMHS. I used to go to VCHS but for financial reasons i do not attend anymore. Since attending Buckingham i have been called names to my face of which i have not heard of before. Being sheltered in such a great private and coming to a charter school I have had great difficulties. Bullying is an every day thing i deal with at Buckingham. The staff is great and i have no complaints of the academics. Everything great and set up for a high school experience. It just happens that such a school close to perfection has a flaw with the type of people there. SCORES ARE INFLATED. TEACHERS ALLOW STUDENTS TO TURN IN WORK LATE. SEVERAL TEACHERS BULLY STUDENTS AND GET AWAY WITH IT. DOESN'T PREPARE KIDS FOR THE REAL WORLD. DON'T RECOMMEND THIS SCHOOL FOR ANYONE. School isn't what people make it out to be. The principal on down don't know how to conduct themselves in a professional manner. I wouldn't recommend this institution to anyone. Teachers here are friendly and willing to accomadate the wide background of students (some kicked out of continuation schools, some homeschooled , etc). To a point this is a good school for students with behavioral issues as staff/faculty is use to nontraditional students. This school is not satisfactory for studnets who want to go to a college, unless they want to go to trade school or a communtiy college. Students here do not have the opportunity to take classes beyond the minimum required by most colleges. Classes offered are extremely limited. "Challenging" classes are "taught" online through a seperate company. Mostly just a lot of emphasis on the CA Exit Exam and Stars tests. BCMHS is one of the greatest schools in Vacaville!! I like how the teachers are very nice and they encourage you to do well!! If you decide to move to Vacaville in the near future then you should decide BUCKINGHAM!!!! I love my school so much!! Plus there is so much to do!! Buckingham? NO I don't want to go there mom! Well, thats exactly what I said when I was told I was going. I had attended Will C. Wood for two years before going to Buckingham. Let me start by saying I cannot thank my mom enough for making me go here. This school is amazing, it was like coming into a new family. Will C. Wood was the worst place I have ever been to. Seeing teachers crying because other students verbal abuse, students jumping autistic students, it was insane. When I came to this school I was that tough kid that didn't take crap from other people. Then I begin to change, making friends with other kids I never thought I'd ever be friends with even teachers became close friends! It was another family for me, a family that I will miss until the day I die. Buckingham truly is a school that becomes a home, a family and a safe place to be. Please hear me out! I went to Will C. Wood, I did the public schooling and it was horrible. I just graduated and I would do anything to go back and be part of Buckingham all over again, this time attending all four years! So please if you want a safe, and nurturing school for your child send them to this school! You won't regret it! Buckingham Charter Magnet High School, a CA Distinguished and Blue Ribbon school, is the school of choice for our son. BCMHS is a high performing (consistently over 800 API), rigorous, innovative, small, close knit high school that seeks to graduate students with 21st century technology skills and academic preparedness for post secondary learning. The magnet is visual/media arts so students take electives such as Film/Video Production, Video-Editing, Web Design, Photography, Cinema Studies, and 3D Animation along with traditional electives. The classes are engaging and challenging and students must pass with 70% or higher. With a block schedule, students are able to take classes at Solano Community College and therefore earn college and high school credits simultaneously. Also, students can challenge themselves and take Advanced Placement courses via an online program on site thus having the option to take 2 per semester within one block period. BCMHS also offers many ways for students to develop such as sports, clubs, and performing arts. My son chose BCMHS because he wanted to get away from the "drama" of his much larger middle school. He is thriving at BCMHS! We are a small school with roughly 400 people or so. Our "campus," if you can call it that, is located in an industrial park. The teachers and staff carry the jobs of three people and are some amazing people. If we win this money then we would probably spend it on our library, which is lacking in books. We are a college preparatory school so our standards are much higher then other school. For example, there are no D's at are school. You either have a C and are passing or an F and failing. We don't have a wide variety of classes, but we do the best we can. We only offer French and Spanish as languages. There are not to many electives but we have good ones. Some of the teachers are some amazing people. Both our History teachers, U.S. History and World History, are possibly the best teachers I've ever had. They really take time to get to know the students and help them out as much as possible. That is one advantage to having a small school, the personal relationships between the teachers and the students. INstead of teachers having hundreds of students, each teacher has around 150 students and the classes have about thirty people. That makes it easier to get to know each student. Buckingham is an awesome school! My daughter is doing well at the school and the teachers are great! The staff is very caring and the principal of the school takes pride of Buckingham. Buckingham strives to have succesful students as well as prepare students for college. Our son went to school here for one year. We switched out and took him to Vanden High School after 9th grade. Here is a breakdown of why. I will start with the positives:Pros:- small class sizes- caring teachers and are available to students- good kids and decent environment- community/family feel- communication is top notchNow for the cons:- total lack of AP and honors classes. All AP classes are online and not suitable for learning.- academics are not challenging and will ONLY prepare your student for Solano CC.- turnover in leadership areas - school is run out of a warehouse/parking lot with a lack of space.- Safety is a concern. Students crossing a parking lot for classes and a huge Bingo hall with strangers loitering the campus.- block scheduling doesn't allow student to learn material everyday. Students can go 4 days without class which is difficult if you are learning a language.- they allow students to turn in late work for credit which doesn't teach responsibility and accountability for your school work. - No PE or sports program. Gym is literally walking and watching movies. If PE is done, they have to run the parking lot. Sports program lacks.Overall we removed our son, sadly, from this school. They try hard and do have good people there, but bottom line is that they only will prepare your kid for community college. They will not be prepared to compete for admission to a UC in this school. Hopefully they make some improvements, get a campus, provide REAL college prep classes (like AP) and start preparing their students for life after high school. I attended this school myself and I can honestly say it's such a huge waste. First off, these "computer classes" were nothing more than the teacher who just got outta some UC just sitting back at his desk and expect everyone, including myself, to just figure out the software without any tutorial or even what exactly we were supposed to create with it. I got NOTHING out of my time there, aside from my diploma which is value-less these days. They did NOTHING to help me with college and Solano Community College is just as aimless. I left Solano County altogether and I attend college elsewhere and it has been a WORLD difference. Don't send your kids here, in fact don't send them to any school in Solano, the entire county is so incompetent. THIS IS OUR FIRST YEAR AT THIS SCHOOL. WE HAVE EXPERIENCED NO LEADERSHIP, NO FOLLOW THROUGH, LITTLE TEACHER SUPPORT, PARENTS ARE WELCOME ONLY IF THEY ARE GIVING MONEY. THEIR FOCUS IS ON THEMSELVES LOOKING GOOD. MOST THE TEACHERS ARE TOO SELF INVOLVED IN THEIR OWN SUCCESS AND NOT THE KIDS. THEY SAY A LOT BUT DO NOT SUPPORT THEIR GREAT IDEAS. IDEAS ONLY IN THEIR HEADS. THE GOOD THING IS THIS IS A SMALL SCHOOL NO OBSERVED GANG RELATED ACTIVITY. NOT SAYING THERE IS NONE, BUT FAR LESS THAN AT A SCHOOL WITH 2000 KIDS. First year here and the jury is out! It feels like they do not like to engage with the parents. I am very involved in my kids education so this is different. Confidentiality is sub par. They don’t return calls etc. The teachers swear at the kids. The staff in the office are nice. I get no feed back when I ask about my kids progress. I get looked at like I have a third eye. I am really thing about a private school. I had some people tell me their experience was not good, and they took their kids out! Such a great school. Beautiful new campus. Phenomenal theater program. Phenomenal leadership program. Friendly and engaging administrators, staff, and teachers. Block scheduling allows for so many different learning options for kids—in person on Campus, Solano Community College classes, on line classes. Also frees up time for extra curricular activities or work. I’m so happy we have this as a choice for kids who don’t need or want the big (over 2000 kids!) high school option.

When you walk into your child's school you want to feel like the staff is actually glad you are there. You get this at Shoals. Shoals students are also very talented - the school puts a lot of emphasize into the arts. Shoals is also a tight-knit community and this spills over into the school system. This is a great school! All the teachers are very understanding and nice. I would reccommend this school to anyone.

column1: this school district is ran like a "old Boys Club" The athletic director and baseball coach have harrased and bullied my top athlete son out of his senior year and then started false allagations. my son wants nothing to do with a school and coaches he has loved since 5th grade.. what kind of coaches are these? who ruins great kids., while superintendant does nothing. Good luck as a single female parent in this town. They are a disgrace to teachers who care about kids , not jealouse of them. shame on you Gladstone. Anyone else have these same problems? They watched her take tests to get insight into her testing issues, they orally tested her, they retested her. This was all without a diagnoses, no 504 or IEP in place. column3: All three of my boys have attended Augusta Sr. High School and all were VERY well prepared for college & work after graduation. The teachers are involved as instructors, coaches, mentors, and sponsors at almost every level, and the community does a great job of getting behind AHS initiatives to improve the school. We moved to Augusta from Wichita because we wanted our 3 kids to go to a better school for high school rather than Wichita public schools. We had 3 all in high school when we moved. 12, 10 and 9 grades. Most teachers and students were great. There were a couple though that seemed to almost shun our kids because they did not grow up in Augusta. They were treated different by a few teachers and the only thing they or us as parents could come up with was because they were not form that town like 99% of the other students that were born and raised there. The sports and classes all were great and all of our kids graduated but I think they should really look at how they tend to favor some students WAY more than they should. It is blatantly obvious to the students that seemed to be over looked. My kids unfortunately told me after the fact because had I known this would be happening as often as it did, I would have said something at the time but none of my kids go there now so I figured I would forewarn other parents to be on the lookout if you decide to move to Augusta.

column1: Winton Woods is not equipped to take care of students with learning disabilities. They also do not respect the opinion of the parents. If your child is not and A student do not send them to WWMS. I now home school my child because we live in WW school district. I graduated from this high school. It have me knowledge of different socioeconomic status' and how diversity plays a part in learning to your highest potential. Thanks WW. When I graduated in '01, the school had a lot of problems, but nowhere near the disorder which exists now. I do feel I received a good education, and I did well in college as a result. However, the school is beginning to fit that mold of the urban public school with problems it has tried to distance itself from. There is too much emphasis on specific athletics, and not so much the arts, in which there exists great choral, band and dramatic programs. Parents are not being listened to, and many of them are teachers in the district. I fear the future of this school, big time. I graduated from Winton Woods High School just last year (2010), and it is not taking on the mold of the typical urban community school. I attend Miami University in Oxford, OH, and I am an education major, and I'm concentrating on schools with an urban setting. For those who think WWHS is "Urban", would you please tell me your definition of "urban" so I can easily inform you of your ignorance? I graduated at the top of my class, and there is a strong emphasis in academics, extra-curriculars, and community service at WWHS. They want to cultivate a world class education by making well-rounded students. academic talents are great, yes, but WWHS tries to bring out the best in everyone, not just their book smarts, because that's what makes people stand out. Being just a bookworm isn't all that excites colleges. They want to see the GPA and the extra activities. It makes you looked like a balanced, model student, and this is what WWHS staff try to promote every single day with all of their students. Get your head out of the clouds people!! Don't try and defame the reputation of Winton Woods because the students are told to explore ALL their interests and encouraged to BE THEMSELVES! I am a student attending winton woods high school, and all I see is differences and racial boundary and conflict between student, and racial profiling against student from teachers. They try to pry money and funds out of students and parents by using madatory trips and uniforms, (which is a joke might i add) then the funding is wasted on its sports programs, instead of academic curriculum and the arts. If theres any smart decision a student or parent could make; its not going to this school. I am so glad i switched to Scarlet Oaks. Winton woods is a good school, it's just way students act. It's mostly an all black school, and some call it gehtto. Not all of them act out but a majority do. winton wood high school If your child has a learning disabilities this is not the place for your child i believe that they think that kids with disabilities are just bad kids they told me that they did;nt have the staff to help me .and if i did not like it then take him home and teach him my self- my child need help he has the right to school to he has some disabilities. Winton Woods High School has a program called Academy of Global Studies(AGS), It gives great opportunities for everybody. Please join this school. This school is the ebst. WWHS is one of the most unique schools in this country. It has a program called Academy of Global Studies, where you learn real-life skills in a diversified global environment. The connections it establishes with overseas schools are amazing. Our High School has a program that has a focus on Electronics and exploring the STEM -( Science, Technology, Engineering and Technology) concept. Our Robotics Educator - Ms. Smith is an expert in this area and a blessing to our children at Winton Woods High School I went to winton woods myself so I felt that my children would get a great learning experience here as I did! Boy was I wrong! I am actually considering filing a lawsuit against winton woods city schools. My son who is in one of the elementary schools was reprimanded by his substitute teacher for turning in his work wrong five times. The fifth time he went to turn it in the teacher put her hands in his face because she was fed up with him coming up to her desk! I have went to the superintendent on this matter and the principal and they all seem to beat around the bush on this matter. Along with the fact that none of them have a clue on anything that is going on with my sons education. I wouldn't recommend this school district to any parents with any children with learning disabilties the staff there are not trained correctly. Terrible the teachers are not focused nor the kids. Education is limited especially math and reading la I feel this school district is amazing because it gives me, as a student, to explore the world in many different ways. I had the chance to travel to China with the band and in high school I don't get a lot of chances like that. I have amazing teachers that care about every single child. And in the comments that I've seen this school doesn't get enough credit for how amazing it is. I've met people from so many different cultures and all students are accepting. If you're looking for a place to fit in there's one for you here. And we'll welcome you with open arms. I'm very proud to be a warrior and I hate seeing all the trash on here about my school, every school has crap to deal with. It's how we deal with it that matters... The school is a joke. On the outside it looks perfectly normal, especially the football field. What I know to be true on the inside is that the structure is falling apart. Even though there is a dress code for uniforms here, some rules simply don't apply. When you get the handbook about the dress code I suggest you throw it in the trash. Students are allowed to wear their pants down below their butts. The school has a bad reputation and deserves it. I learned so much from the teachers at this school. Even though I was a racial minority, and was out-casted because of it, I still made it to #4 of my class and graduated with honors. My oldest son graduated in 2012 second in his class. I would have argued with anyone who said you couldn't get a decent education at Winton Woods back in 2012 but unfortunately I can't do that today. The direction they are taking this schoo defies common sense. They started a program called AGS (Academy of Global Studies) around 2011. In a nutshell the kids are supposed to teach each other then they do a project and present it to teachers, other students, business people etc. It's called project based learning and the teachers are facilitators and the students are teachers. I find that a horrible way to learn but we had the option to stay in the traditional school side. Fast forward to 15-16 school year. They changed the traditional school to a program which they called New Tech Academy. We found this out a few days before school started. Needless to say I was upset. We are 6 months into this way of teaching and it is RIDICULOUS! It is a program called New Tech Network. Again, it is projected based learning. The kids learn it themselves then have to teach their classmates. As crazy as this seems I am not making this up. The teachers are called facilitators. They don't teach the material they are there if the kids are stuck or have an issue. What the facilitators do to help is ridiculous too. If one of the kids isnt doing anything they have to meet with the facilitator and tell them what they did to try to get the student to work after several of these meeting they get to "fire" their classmate. So since the teachers can't get these kids to work let's make the students try and if they still won't work let's make the students "fire" their classmates. This is the craziness our administration feels is the best way for our kids to learn. Why do we have to change the whole way of teaching just to accommodate the kids that aren't doing well? Because the majority of the kids aren't doing well. So if teachers can't make them learn by lecturing the material to them like every other school district lets give them a fun and exciting way of learning by not teaching them- let them teach themselves! So the kids who want to learn struggle to teach themselves and then have to teach the kids the teachers couldn't. What person in their right mind would think this is a great way of learning. Please bring common sense back to our school district!!!! WWHS has a an undeserved bad reputation. Like all high schools, there will be varied types of personalities for teachers, parents, and students. Everyone wants the best for the students above all at WWHS. They have actively sought out innovative educational programs to help students achieve their academic goals. Good school producing highly effective leaders. Awful. Put your child in any high school but Winton Woods. This school is one of the best schools the I have went to so I defentily recommend this school for anybodys kids educationCheyenne dempster

column3: Too many rules limit the human mind. This school will strip your children of their individuality, If they have any left. Teach your children to question everything they here, and that bending to conformity will deprive them of their freedom. Let them decide their own morals and tell them not to impose them on others. i just came to this school this year and it was a big change. i made friends quickly but most of them are guys because the girls here are self centered and catty. but i feel like i haven't learned anything. i got a lot of work done in my old school and every student here just doesn't shut up and pay attention to the class. all my grades are low!! and some of my teachers are strict and don't teach very well. i hate school but i do wanna learn. i only like coming to talk to my friends. I went to pick up my little sister and yes my mom forgot to put on as a contact. So it's was a issue but Marion in the front was very unhelpful cut me off when I was speaking to her didn't say excuse me and picked up the phone while I was speaking to her. I had to ask her what to do to get my sister out she did not offer any help it was like playing 21 questions with her. I finally got an answer from her what I needed to do I called my mom and my mom called the school and she was giving her a hard time?! If you absolutely have to send your child here, be aware of the problems that will ultimately arise. This is not a “safe” area either, the amount of threats that have happened within this school year (2019-2020) are astounding. If you’re child does attend this school, please make your kid participate in some out-of-school activity because they’ll have a hard time trying to find their place in this school. If you’re active duty look into another school before this one. While I have had good experiences this year, overall this school is incredibly underwhelming and really doesn’t challenge students academically. You have to sift through many teachers to find one that truly cares about their kids education. The staff at the front were very rude to us when we first came and a couple of the counselors seem like they don’t even want to be here. The student to teacher ratio is so unbalanced, so classes switch between being way too big or way too small. There have also been cases of student-teacher relationships so watch out. The students themselves seem bored, and many tend to act out because they need help that the school refuses to give. If you’re low-income, the school does try to aid you, but some staff literally don’t care about what you or your child needs. Drugs-use, alcohol-use, and sex are commonplace so watch your kids closely. My experience has been frustrating whenever I need to talk to a higher up because there is little to no time to talk to anyone about anything. Communication with any of the staff is mediocre and unhelpful most of the time. Those in charge of attendance do mess up occasionally, they have counted me with unexcused absences before (despite having a doctor’s notes).The overall cleanliness of the school is poor. Good luck during flu season, many parents don’t vaccinate their kids and the school gets on your butt about masks (not those fake decorative ones, like real n95 masks). The school also has a hard time cleaning the classrooms as many of them still have trash since the beginning of the year. The bathrooms are almost always a mess too. Oh and for the icing on the cake —despite how much the children try to be inclusive the school is a very conservative place. If your kid is lgbtq or of any race besides white there may be problems with bullying (and not just from other kids). as a current student I have been at this school for 3 years and it is not a good school most teachers will act like teachers when parents are being talked to but change as soon as they are done with the parent. most teachers do the least possible work to help even if the students go to them. I would not recommend this school to anyone if you want to have a good high school experience Please do not send your child here it is awful i have been picked on for so long here and nothing gets done about it no punishments nor discipline. Other studente will vape,smoke and can straight up disrespect the teachers and the teacher dont do anything the amount of fighting and threats here are so common and even if someone is in the right with self defense they still suspend them and send them to daep. Students make social meida to disrespect other students and post videos of kids fighting and the staff does nothing out of all the teachers here only a handfull care about the students. Please overlook this school and the ccisd district your better off sending your kids to another school

The class selection is okay, and the teachers seem to have a genuine, positive connection with the students. School spirit is high. I enjoy diversity (having lived all over the US), but there is little diversity here. However, that is changing, and my kids have friends of many different backgroungs. Lastly, the office staff can be hard to work with, and not very friendly, but not so with the attendance staff. Layton High has excellent teachers and staff. Layton is way better than Davis. If you send your kids to Davis, they will become elitist snobby brats. Whereas, if your kids go to Layton, they will be very chill, while still being driven and productive members of society. I am a new student to lhs, and to be honest, it sucks. I am a student who excels in science, and wanted new things to learn, but its all very repetitive and there is little to no effort made to make sure students learn new things. and the choir program is...weak. I'm sorry to say, but its overall pathetic. I've held an active role in choir for basically my whole school career, and its sad to say my elementary choir teacher (who didn't even study music) was far better than the teacher here. there is no discipline, or any challenges for us. as well as the entire fine arts category of classes is barely even there. I took the dance class as well, and for a person who never really enjoyed dance, Nybo made it fun and interesting. I have yet to try the theatre program, but hopefully it doesn't disappoint as much as the other classes.

column1: Was a great school then it went down hill can't send my kids here anymore. I would Strongly Recommend parents to find other schooling opportunities if possible. Horrible school. The bullying from faculty/administration is almost worse than it is from students. If you dare raise any questions or concerns, prepare for you and your child to be singled out and treated unfairly for years to come. It does not matter how well your child completes their work or follows the rules, they will always have a problem with something. I have literally been passive aggressively questioned as to why my son scored too WELL on assignments that the teachers clearly felt he was to stupid to do well on. Basically accusing him of cheating because they expected lower scores from him. They have a roundabout way of accusing you of anything they can think of to cause problems, and assume you're too stupid to pick up on what they're accusing you of. Staff is rude, confrontational, and unfriendly. I am an involved, concerned parent who does everything in my power to help my child succeed. And I have spent just as much, if not more time combating the constant confrontational attitudes and problems from the faculty as I have actually helping my son with his schooling. But good luck proving or getting any assistance with the unfair treatment, as they are very sneaky and thorough at helping to cover for each other's behavior. Even if you do encounter one of the few decent people working in this school, don't expect them to be able to help you either, as they are in too much fear of losing their job or being singled out themselves to speak up against their co workers in the code of silence that has been created in this "school" system.

This school has had so much turnover in staff in recent years. PMSD is not promoting quality education for our children to be challenged against there peers. Unless your kids in Honors courses which is excellent advance placement courses ...It seems that they promote school sports more than quality in education. It doesn't even rank close to other high schools in the area. Also this is the only school district not promoting a school uniform policy. All the other school have adopted this about 2-3 years ago. I am a senior of year 2013-2014 and I moved in the area in 10th grade. My school experience has been nothing but drama. The students here have a horrible attitude towards school. The only thing that thy have going on for the students is sports. It seems to be the only thing they care about and I am sick of it. This needs to change I graduated from West in the class of 2013 and I can honestly say that nothing better prepared me for coursework in college than this school's Advanced Placement classes. The AP teachers definitely know what they are doing and will prepare you for the future. And the college credit awarded from the exams saved me thousands of dollars in classes, take advantage of these courses! Thank you PMWHS Tom Horvath Absolutely horrible. column1: Hudson Middle School sucks. I dont see anything good about it. Only the counselor and teachers . They helped me out. But! everything else like the students...They are very mean and cruel. I dont like it. Sports is also good in hudson but i still dont like it. Students here are very uncaring about how they treat another student. Bullies...I cant stand them. I moved to this school from a bigger school district in Texas. I had to skip a grade because they didn't offer the same kind of advanced programs as my former school district. In example, I was a freshman in Algebra 2 at my former school and now all of the sudden I am a sophomore in Algebra 2 with many seniors in their "regular" math class. The teachers were, for the most part very kind, but Iooking back, I don't feel like I learned much over the course of those three years. My former peers were much more successful in college, and beyond. Great athletic program, and educational program as well. I have went to Hudson my whole life This school is the best I've been to. The teachers are mostly nice, and help you out with anything you don't understand. They make their subjects interesting, while still teaching you it properly. There are many athletic choices, although there is no football. The students here are well-behaved, and you very, very rarely ever have to worry about being bullied. If you do have a problem, you can go to the counselors, and they will actually help you. Overall, Hudson High School is pretty special. It has something I've never experienced in other schools.
