column3: My son will be attending his third year now a Junior and I am very proud of his achievements and progress with his academics as well as his maturity. He's had great teachers and support from day one. School is what you choose it to be, by making wise choices. I am very thankful for who my son is today. This school is great, awesome staff, and lots of career choices available. A definite thumbs up!!! LWHS has been very helpful and resourceful not only to the students but to the parents. I have no complaints with any of the staff members, in fact, they have gone beyond my expectations. I have to admit it was a shaky start at first, but now that I've met the staff there is a level of respect that is well deserved. Unfortunately, there is not a whole lot of parent involvement. The best part is the school is very diversified. It would be nice to see LWHS receive funding to enable students to have more opportunities that is well deserved. For the love of God, do not send your children to this school. The administration is always making false promises to it's students and constantly letting them down. They ruined my daughter's senior year, they weren't allowed to do anything. She saw three principals in her time there, clearly the school is unstable. And let's talk about college preparedness, these staff doesn't care if their students get into college, as long as the have a high graduation rate. No one is ever there to help these kis. The college coach is nonexistent. My daughter missed so many opportunities for scholarships because the people that were supposed to keep her informed did not. They are unreliable with transcripts and the guidance receptionist is beyond rude and refuses to let the kids see the guidance counselors. Let's talk about how they jipped all the students and parents by making the kids sign a contract for the uniform on the last day of school (2012) after repeatedly lying to the kids, saying that the uniform wouldn't be changed. No integrity whatsoever, save yourself the trouble. Lake Worth High functions better as a parking lot instead of a school, level the damn place. I'm gonna be very honest, at the beginning I wasn't sure about lake worth high but it's truly a great school. Some staff members are nice and caring, the programs are excellent! My child really enjoys school, her teachers are pretty good, well except for Ms Colon I got be honest she doesn't teach, she is hardly there and when she is there, they only watch movies so stay away from Spanish!! Maybe there's a better teacher. The principal has to step up his game, and maybe he will inspired, and so you know it does not really matter which school they attend! it matters what you will make of it! Everything is great as far as choice academies and some AP and AICE classes, we also have opportunities for dual enrollment. Some of the people in the main office and students services need help with people skills. So do some of the guidance counselors. You have to hunt them down every time you need them, and some are very rude. For example, my counselor is supposedly Ms.Smith, after my mother and i tried to contact her for almost 2 weeks, had the worst attitude with me,when i was respectful and polite the whole time i was talking to her.

column1: don't EVER consider putting your child into this school. Horrible teaching staff, the teachers play favorites by giving students who dont do their work A's, and students who actually do their work a lower grade. If you need bus transportation, Gateway is the wrong decision, they cancelled half of the buses. New principle took away most of the fun activities. The sports teams (such as football and basketball) dont win ANY games, the football team went the whole season without winning or scoring points at all. Mostly everyone i know is leaving or has already left due to the poor teaching/ feeling of a real high school. The uniforms cost way to much. the school lies constantly, and in bullying situations, they say the will help but NEVER DO! Most of the juniors have left even though they have been there for years because the school has gotten that bad to the point where no one can handle it anymore. Ii is small, cramped, and gloomy. WORST choice of school. Rung like a business not a school. Most teachers are not certified and are inferior to their public school counter-parts... Save your children a lot of trouble in the future educational endeavors and send them to public school... Better then people say it is, i'm proud to be a student of GCHS. Don't let ungreatful students give an opinion on our school Gateway Charter High School is in no way a real high school. Considering the building is an old business building, it doesn't actually look like a real school. The hallways are narrow and short in height. The walls are so insanely thin, you can hear a cough from two classrooms over. The lighting and lack of windows makes it seem gloomy, dark, depressing, and prison-like. Unlike other schools, 0% of our daily lunch is made by real people. It's disgusting and disturbing, and the price and length of lines are absurd. Besides that, the education is great. If you dont mind listening to teachers complain and getting insulted by your teachers daily. None of the teachers are actually qualified to teach the subject they're teaching. We've got some great curriculum this year though. I'm enrolled in a Law class, my favorite. Our football team hasn't won since 2009, probably due to our lack of a field. Our campus is ridiculously small, plus we're cramped in with 6th, 7th, and 8th graders too. If you're looking for a high school you can brag about, don't come. If you want to make lifelong friends and have amazing experiences, come on in! You won't learn, but you'll have a good time. My daughter went to this school and I found this school to be great! She graduated with honors and is now a second year pre-med student and on the dean's list at her university. You as a parent can not just send your kids to school and leave it all to the teacher. You as a parent has to play your part from day one of your child lives and You the student have to take responsibility for your learning. It's up to you to want to learn! At the beginning of each school year I would email each of my daughters teachers with my phone number letting them know to feel free to contact me. As the school year goes on I would send another email asking if my daughter was being respectful to her teachers and other students. I attended every parent teacher conference and returned every teacher phone calls and emails. I let my daughter know that she don't have to like her teachers but she Must show Respect to her teachers. And yes you are my child but that does not means that I will just take your word over your teacher. Parents get involve and Students take responsibility if not then don't come on here bashing the school and the teachers because YOU failed to do what was needed to succeed! WOW! Do not send your child to this school. Students are misbehaving until teachers will get fired! My daughter had 4 Spanish Teachers and 3 Math teachers in one year! The last one to stay has not even been a teacher but just a long- term substitute teacher. Bullying is a huge issue and no one cares. My child had to talk to 3 different teachers until someone talked at least to the other student. Administration prefers not to report any violence, drugs or bullying issues and rather get rid of teachers who try to do the right thing. My daughter attends a regular HS now and noticed how much she missed out on general knowledge at Gateway. They just practice for the FCAT and state testing. Real learning does not take place! A School, yes with a lot of sacrifice for our kids. This school is lucky I'm giving it a star. The school is absolutely absurd! Teaching- average. Everything else? Absolutely unsatisfactory. Where's the school spirit? The nice staff that smile instead of threatening you? Our current assistant principal for 2013 will threaten you for the smallest things, like hugging your friend, along with the rest of the disciplinary staff. I thought high school would be amazing. Not a complete disaster. (This school has probably fueled all the hatred I have just developed for people in general.) Heard only good things about this school from teachers and students. My daughter starts this year and she is looking forward to meeting new friends and taking sign language as her foreign language. She has been a Sixmile Charter Academy student for 8 years and has enjoyed each one. The administration at this school is awful, providing nearly no support and help when students most need it. Along with outdated technology and limited supplies (including textbooks, which don't arrive until halfway through the year), students have little access to materials that will help them succeed in a school environment. As a previous student of over 6 years, I beg parents to reconsider putting their children in another school. Ok so where do I begin? This so called "school" is the most obsord place ive ever been too. This was my first and final year and gateway charter and I couldn't be any happier the last 20 days are I'm my sight. From the way the principle and vice principle run this concentration camp. The uniforms are one thing and took me two weeks to get over. Wearing a school uniform is not all that bad, even though they might be hideous they are convenient.but every aspect of the school has flaws. It made me belive this was the first year the school had ever be open. There are 6 grades in this tiny office building, 6th grade to the grade I'm in Seniors. Walking in the hall ways is like ting to cross the street in times square, NYC. It's distgusting. They've managed to fit the MAXIMUM amount of students in it. For example, when there is a fire drill it takes everyone so long to get out of the building that if it were a real fire; we would all burn and die a miserable death. And when I woke up in hell I would still be at gateway charter. Even if you live in gateway and belive that it's most convenient because it's so close to the house. Do not go here, or send your student here, whatever you do. I have never seen another school treat their students with such blatant disrespect and not care whatsoever for their education. The teachers are extraordinarily subpar, some of them unable to function without a teachers edition of the textbook telling them what to do. There is no support for the student, as no one seems to care what they do or where they plan to go later in life. As a graduate of GCHS, I can honestly say that I have never experienced such a terrible environment. Here you will be taught by multiple people with unsavory pasts, or people who aren't certfied in what they are teaching/doing. The administration does nothing to prevent bullying, despite the fact that antibullying is one of the most "stressed" policies in the school. If you honestly care about your student, do not leave them to suffer in this school. You will come to regret it as one of the worst decisions you've made in your life. Great experience and my child thrived and succeeded This school should be used as an example to show parents why they should not send their child here. My son has had a rough high school experience in this school. His mental health has been deteriorating ever since he’s been in this school. Administration does a terrible job in making sure their students are doing well in academics, they don’t worry about a student’s well being rather they worry about their ratings from the board of education. Counselor is barely ever present. It’s tough to get through to the principal. My son has gone through 5 teachers in one year for one subject! They do not hire a teacher based on their credentials. They will hire anyone without a degree in teaching. This is why the student population for this highschool is getting lower. Teachers care about their grades looking good, but they don’t care whether their students are actually learning. Teachers change every few months, no one wants to remain here. Staff and administration treats students poorly. They also will charge you for every little thing. Uniform is expensive to begin with, now they’ll charge you just to wear jeans on Friday. If you are a person of color, good luck. I believe my experience with Gateway Charter has been a strong one. The school size is a major bonus for students wanting to focus on academics, athletics and a safe place to come and prepare for their next chapter. 10/10 Gateway Charter High, strives and achieves to support students of all backgrounds. Multiple levels of support are provided for students and parents. Teachers and staff are passionate and effective. It is duly noted how dedicated the staff is in furthering their students education and social interactions. They care for their students on all levels. The school has no communication when it comes to learning. When it comes to education they give notes and tests without actually talking about it and getting you to understand it. They care more about making themselves look good other than education. Teachers don’t know how to talk respectfully to students without a rude tone or being rude in general. They tell students to use proper language but anytime a student of color is being called a slur none of the staff seem to care.

column3: I currently attend a well-known four year university and am proud to say that I went to HHS. I learned so much from HHS thanks to quality teachers. HHS prepared me well for college. Thanks to these teachers, I have had no trouble at all adjusting to college level material. I was also lucky enough to take AP courses which allowed me to earn college credit via a national placement test. Harding is a source of pride for Marion, offering a great variety of coursework & diverse student population: it allows every student to find his or her niche. Staff are friendly and helpful. Some teachers should curb their liberalism and allow more points of view than the popular and/or "politically correct." Still, music programs are phenomenal, and academic offerings help the motivated to prepare quite well for college and career! Harding offers kids ample opportunity to learn to get along well with people of a wide variety of backgrounds--what a great preparation for life! I have had 2 children graduate from HHS. It is a good school.

I encourage every student to do their very best, to work hard, to be resilient, and to become independent, college ready and life-long learners. I encourage parents to work with our school to make it even better. - William J. Doyle 718.329.2902

column3: Boonville High School is a place where teachers always push for improvement. If was not for the staff I would have never wanted to complete high school. They treat everyone equal. I love the fact the no matter how much I wanted to give up there was always a teacher or even janitor to ask me if i was ok or to make me smile. BHS has the most respectful teachers and staff anyone could hope to be around for 4 or more years. They never give up on you. Excellent effort by both the students and the teachers. I left after one semester. Everybody here is mean and does drugs. Not a good place for kids looking to succeed in life. 1/10 I DO NOT RECCOMEND! There is a big problem when it comes to the children's right to go to the bathroom in this school. There is one teacher who only allows 9 hall passes per semester. Not grading period, semester. A semester is about 18 weeks. That means on average, students who are in that class may only use the restroom during that class 1 time every other week. And those aren't only just for the restrooms. They are also for going to the nurse or going anywhere else a student needs to go during class. There is a teacher in this building who does not allow students to regularly use the restroom. If say 2, maybe 3 if they are having a good day, go to the restroom during that class, they'll suddenly say something along the lines of "No more going to the bathroom today" to the rest of the class. The problem is that their class is right after lunch. Humans commonly need to go to the bathroom maybe an hour or so after a meal so hopefully, you can see the issue here. This teacher also straight-up lies to students to try to make them feel bad or make them feel less intelligent than they are. That is called being a completely toxic person. Whether they are doing it intentionally or not does not matter because a teacher, should do their best to not hurt the children they are supposed to teach.

column1: I don't like that this school has such a small population, some teachers aren't the greatest, we have no cafeteria, and I especially don't like that the sport selection is horrible. The only plus is that the students can be closer to the teachers and counselors and the students are more well rounded than any larger school. i went to this school for a little bit and it was great the teacher were nice and the small population was nice as well because it felt like you knew everyone. i have to say that if you dont like living in country setting then east nicolaus is not for you but if you want a real education that will get you somewhere in life then this school is great. i used to be a student there, i spent all four years there and i wouldn't change it for nothing the best years of my life were there and the staff was awesome not only were the teachers great but they were also your friend you couldn't ask for a more pleasant place East Nicolaus High School has done AMAZING things for my son. The faculty is wonderful, as they take an interest in each and every student. The student body is also unique in that they are all nice kids from nice families. I am yet to hear the typical high school horror stories of bullying and hazing. My son has never felt so at home and so accepted. I can't think of a negative thing to say. WONDERFUL high school experience. This is a great school if you have an average or below student. The school has had a high staff/teacher turn over the last couple of years. I'm not sure if that's due to the new principal, but as a parent, it's concerning. The turnover feels constant. Several teachers hired to replace previous ones also left after last year. A new English teacher this year lasted only a few days. There aren't many AP classes and students don't seem to pass the exams for the ones they do offer. While often the top rated school in Sutter county, you need to look at the numbers for Sutter county. Overall, poor public schools/scores. The top scores here are average at best elsewhere. Again, if you have an average student the academics are fine and small town environment nice; for highly academic students, there doesn't seem to be much challenge or enough academic opportunities. East Nicoluas and the staff are exceptional with the students. The new Principle has been amazing and knows each and every student. I have been pleased with the 3 years my son has attended. The small class sizes and small town feel has empowered my son through the years. Academically, East Nicolaus has proven high scores for years and shall continue. The teaching staff may have changed over the last few years but that happens in a small community that may not have a large school budget. Some teachers intend to use the smaller schools as stepping stones to their careers; there is no getting around that. Yet, There are many long timers at this school who make East Nicolaus strong, who believe in their students and all of their accomplishments. Good Job East Nicolaus!

I'm very happy to be out of there as is most of my graduating class. Good size school, good community. Lots of after school activities (musicals, sports, clubs) and lots of AP classes. I loved Arcadia! I met my now-husband there (while we were both students) My overall experience at Arcadia High School was awful, there are police dog searches at least weekly for all the drugs that circulate that school, as well as police always stationed on campus waiting for something to happen. column1: Maple Lake High School staff and administration do an excellent job of creating a positive learning environment for their students. High academic and behavioral expectations are held for all students. The teachers regularly reflect on their instructional effectiveness to ensure the best outcomes for students' learning. Maple Lake High School is a safe, friendly, educational environment where all students are welcome. We provide a well rounded education to our young people. Our goal is to prepare students to be successful adults. I had two daughters graduate from Maple Lake, and I was pleased with their opportunities. Being a small school , there are good things and bad things like all smalltown schools, but Maple Lake had lots of opportunities for them. There was a good variety of classes for them, and they both were in sports and other things (band, choir, speech). Both graduated with a semester of college classes completed during their 12th grade year by taking college Spanish, English, Speech, and Math classes at the school. They were also awarded scholarships from the community. That, from a financial standpoint, was HUGE for our family! Lots of kids have left other schools and come to Maple Lake. That, to me, says alot. There are issues with small schools and small towns, that they are very one way minded, and this school is no different. Far too many kids get picked on for being different.

column1: The administration for the Jr. High/High school is a joke. You can't talk to ANY of them all they want to do is constantly give our kids detentions and suspensions. They don't address problems, they create them. I feel so sorry for the kids and parents that are going through these problems. Jac-Cen-Del Junior/Senior High School. We had fabulous educators. I always felt that they genuinely cared. column3: I am currently a sophomore at Littleton High School and came to Littleton High School from a Jeffco School. I wanted to go to Littleton because I liked their IB program and passing rate. But when I came to Littleton High School, I wasn't prepared for the way they taught me. I tried to ask the teachers for help but they didn't want to help me or had other classmates answer my question for them. I don't feel that the staff is well-trained. Also most of the teachers are mean and some AP and IB teachers curse their students. I have personally experienced this. Take my word, these school is not worth going to. They only focus on their IB students. If you are planning to go to Littleton, either for AP or IB, just realize that this school will give you a butt load of homework. I am usually up doing homework until 2 am. Hope this helps make your decision. I couldn't disagree more with the negative review below. I'm in my junior year at LHS and have yet to have any struggles with my teachers. Of the ~22 or so I've had so far, 18 have been absolutely excellent, and the others okay. They've all been ready, willing and eager to help me. They've also all willing to listen to their student's feedback. I don't understand how the reviewer below - a sophomore - could write about IB teachers. IB starts junior year, and the IB teachers teach all IB classes (for the most part), so how they would have any experience with IB Teachers, I don't know. Maybe they had one teacher who taught an IB class as well, but it's impossible that they'd have multiple as a sophomore. And I've heard nothing but good things about my IB Teachers that I have this year. Littleton's community (including staff) are predominately nice, supporting, inclusive and wiling to help. It's a great school, and I don't, for one second, regret choosing LHS. P.S. Students who take honors, AP or IB classes do have a lot of homework. If you don't want a lot, then don't choose those classes. And if you're up until 2am, start your homework earlier and not at 11 o'clock at night. I'm a junior at this school, and i think its an amazing place to spend my four years, ive been here since my freshmen yearm and i believe that even though we are considered the "lousy" one of the 3 littleton high schools, we are extremely close as one. Every school has drug issues, and fights, and all the negative things we are an IB WORLD SCHOOL . diversity is extremely important to us at LHS we dont judge kids because there not white --- cough Arapahoe cough Heritage cough.. our school is one amazing place.. some teachers are mean, and really tough .. but most are really caring and will actually remember you years after you have them.. it is a great school to be in .. haters can hate LHS LION PRIDEEEEEEEE!!!!! I agree with the spirit of the review below, but it's totally not representative of our school. We don't have fights or drug issues, and are a pretty "sheltered" community compared to 90% of high schools. We've got a much more tight-knit community than AHS or HHS and our school is slightly more diverse, less judgmental, and more accepting... But that doesn't mean we're a complacent student body of druggies and 'gangstas' like the person below makes it sound. For the most part, we're a student body of dedicated, motivated and intellectual kids. We have a faculty of dedicated, caring and consummate professionals. Sure we have people who don't care, who don't try, and who are disadvantaged, but that's not nearly the majority. Most of us are in AP or IB, and working to get in the best colleges we can. As a senior, I'm honored to be in an environment surrounded by people so dedicated to their education. And I'm glad I choose to go to such an open, accepting school. First of all, I'm a freshman here at Littleton High School. I completely disagree with the negative post below. I feel my teachers are very able at their job, and, I feel I can ask them at any time for extra help. In fact, I get quite a bit of extra math help. Anyway, this school is extremely diverse. I feel completely okay with being who I am in this school, unlike another school I went to. This school is excellent. I love going here. I will miss it so much when I graduate. Littleton HS school provides a wonderful learning environment for all kids. This school is truly unusual because the student body is not cliquey. Students are highly involved and the faculty truly cares about the students, they are dedicated to the students success. There is an energy in that building that is indescribable. I am an LHS graduate and so thankful for the education that I received at LHS. GREAT school and amazing teachers. My daughter is a junior at LHS. We opted in to LHS after several visits and boy are we glad we did. She is not a number at this school. The teachers really know her and work hard to provide an excellent education. She is very involved with various activities through the school and she loves that the schools fosters and environment of acceptance. There are no cliques and kids are all respectful and supportive of each others interests. She has made so many wonderful friends. Dr. Oakes is a wonderful leader and very visible. They do a great job of creating community. Many levels of coursework so that all children are challenged. My husband and I enjoy going to the concerts, plays, and sporting events. I have deleted a previous5 star review until the school year is off to a smoother start. The school was under construction and this appears to have affected the mindset of the administration who needs to put emphasis back on helping the students with education, heath and well-being. Administration needs to listen to the needs of the students and parents instead of doings what is easiest for them. 5 Stars! Look no further. We did an exhaustive search for a high school for our child including every private school and public schools in 3 districts. We found Littleton to be the best of all worlds. If you are looking for a high school in the metro area that is not too big and not too small with a top notch IB program and clubs, Littleton is the right school. Kids come from over 40 middle schools around the metro area so there are not a lot of cliques. Our kids are thriving and we couldn't recommend it more highly. We enrolled our son at Littleton due to their newcomer English program. All of the ELD teachers are very supportive, engaged, and care about their kids. We are pleased with everything they have done for our son. Math is a major challenge for our son, so it has taken a lot of work at home to help him stay on top. Their math classes are mixed with Honor students so sometimes may pose challenges for kids that struggle a bit more in this area. This is a good, solid environment. It's not too big like many other high schools. I think the focus here is strong academics. If you are after a sports driven high school you should look elsewhere. This is a nice, quaint little high school. Unbelievable. We keep waiting for the other shoe to drop- thinking that the kids and administration can’t possibly be as kind as welcoming as they seem. My child attended a private school where the motto was “be kind” but they were bullied out of the school. They are thriving at LHS and love going to school and love their teachers and classmates. Kudos to Dr Oaks and team for establishing a vision and making sure that everyone executed that vision We had to leave due to climate. While the new school may have lower test scores, the diversity probably better prepares students for the 21st century.

column1: I went to this school in 2012-2013 for my first two years of high school. Despite the small class size, nice building, and intelligent teachers. I was miserable. They like to "judge a fish on its ability to climb a tree and tell it that it is stupid when it falls time and time again". I was that fish and I was not able to fit into the cookie cutter student ideals they created. They offer a program called Running start through the local community college for a student to attend college full time during their Junior and/or Senior year. I was signed up for this program and qualified for everything. Then with one week of school left we were informed that I would be taken out of the program if I didn't raise my math grade. I studied harder than I ever had and basically taught myself an entire semester's worth of info because the way the teacher taught did not fit my learning style. I got an A on the final and raised my grade but they still took me out of the program. I withdrew from the school and now attend the college on my own as a homeschool student and I am thriving. this school needs to figure out a way to allow students who are different still succeed and not be miserable.

column1: I am impressed with what I have seen over the years. Discipline is enforced yet the students still have freedom to be creative. Sports events are organized. They have a winning and growing FFA Organization that has made the town of Malone very proud. Their test scores are average or above. It is a small town so therefore it is a small town school. The teachers are friendly and cooperative. I have lived here 14 years and have heard more praise than complaint from the parents whose children are succeeding there. Most of the complaints I have heard are from parents whose children stay in trouble. A school is not there to "raise" a child.. they are there to educate them. Malone is doing its job and doing it well.

column1: I am currently a senior at Batesville High School, and I have to say that the previous comments must be disregarded. BHS offers nothing but one of the most incredible high school experiences a student could enjoy. I came into BHS 2 months into my sophomore year, and I was scared out of my socks for what people would treat me like as the new kid. But there was no need because the students and staff were all very accepting and WELCOMING, and I sure don't come from a wealthy family by any means. While much of the community is of higher social class, they treat everyone with equality and respect. When I came in I was gladly accepted into the football program, baseball, drama, show choir, and many more extracurricular activities that introduced me to many diverse students and ideas. This is not to mention the outstanding academic standards that the faculty strive to instill in each student. Batesville High School is a very strong school academically. They offer 3 foreign languages, Spanish and German, and are starting to offer Chinese. They offer a broad selection of elective, AP, and off campus learning options. Sports offered are football, basketball, volleyball, tennis, swimming(at local YMCA), track and field, cross country, cheerleading, dance team, soccer, and golf. Other activities include Academic Team, Key Club, Drama Club, Interact Club, Spanish Club, Set Crew, KSLA, and National Honor Society. The only bad thing is a few teachers that I don't personally like. BHS is a great school and I am proud to be a Bulldog. Amazingly fun and exciting for everyone there

column3: Bonnabel is a decent school. The education is acceptable and if your child seems more advanced than most others, they can easily switch to all honors classes. Switching classess is very easy and the couselors are quite generous. The teachers are experenced and good educators. There are deans patroling the school at all times so the area is secure. The school size is very big. There are plenty of students and plenty of space for them. It's almost like a mini college, thining about the size. There's a 50 minute lunch where you may wonder around outdoors and eat in- or outside. There's four periods, lunch being between second and third. The school is overall acceptable. This school is a joke. If your kids are enrolled here just know the staff is not aware where they are at any time. They roam the streets and hang out in front of the apartments across from the school smoking pot and cigarettes all day. Several calls to the police and school and no one does anything. I would be disgusted to know my child could walk off campus at any time and no one knew. Even when a community tries to make the school aware the dean does nothing! Watch your kids here because they are not in good hands. Initially, I was afraid to come to Bonnabel because Bonnabel had a poor reputation. My parents could not afford for me to go to a private school; so, I was forced to enroll in Bonnabel. Today I am proud to call myself a Bruin. Bonnabel can be called by many because the staff welcomes all identities. There is a plethora of clubs, organizations, and advanced courses. As a Senior looking back on my freshman year, I realized my fear originated from my belief in rumors instead of the facts. "Put good in, get good out." Unfortunately, individuals fail to realize that they create their experiences. My experiences was so great because I submerged myself in difficult classes and participated in various clubs. If you want your experience to be great don't be afraid to get out of your comfort zone. If a student actively associates with students prone to trouble, than what else could they expect but trouble. My advice to any incoming frehemen is to be the best student you can be because high school will past with the blink of an eye. Come here with an 8th grade education and leave here with an 8th grade education.

column1: I was a teacher in that school last year. The principal fakes grades to graduate students who did not complete their credits requirements. I provided documents showing changes of grades to the school board and to the superintendent. Nothing happened. The business as usual. The students graduate at a level well below 12th grade. I can't stand it, there's nothing being done with the racism and ignorance, the principal doesn't care about the minorities especially hispanic/latino students who are all categorized as "Mexicans," and plus ignorance is rewarded in the school, plus how is it that I as a student do all my homework, study, take notes everyday has the same grade as a student who doesn't do anything at all, like literally the grading method sucks giving lazy students an A isn't right, they should worry about setting boundaries towards all of these problems instead of the bathroom schedule.

column3: I've been attending this school for a year, going on two and am very unimpressed. Although this school itself is nice, new and clean there is a huge drug problem. Students openly talk about drugs, and when you report them to a staff member nothing gets done except for a little talk with the student. This school mainly focuses on sports, and leaves the less-athletic students behind with little to no advcanced classes, or extracurricular activities like art or chess clubs. Overall, I think you could get a better education online or at Moose Lake. Unless of course you love sports, and are particularly fond of drug usage. Test scores are also low at this school, and sometimes you get the impression that the teachers are solely reaching you something in order to ace the test, and not to really learn anything you could apply to the real world. This school district is known for having one of the best drama departments in the state. A community musical is performed every Fall. My 3 oldest children have participated and have grown tremendously because of it. Many acheivements in the State One-Act Competitions over the years. Overall the school has been working hard to improve academics, and is definately moving in the right direction--strong leadership who are committed to the students' success.

column1: One of my children began to show signs of a learning disability in the middle of the year. i was flat-out told that they do not have to accommodate a special needs child and was told to take him elsewhere. But my other child was welcomed to stay. This was a learning disability, not a physical handicap, nor was he a danger. He just had a hard time coping with the stress and was then told to leave. Disgusting. My husband & I are both Parklane graduates & recieved good educations there. We have one child in attendance there, but choose, as a result of the weak fundimentals he received during his elementary years at Parklane (phonic skills as well as important skills like telling time & counting money) to send our youngest child to St. Alphonsus here in town. Our youngest son has recieved what we believe to be a far superior education than his older brother in a much more sheltered & real Christian enviornment. i regret that while Parklane is a labeled a Christian school, it does not take advantage of that blessing in it's day-to-day curriculum. The peer preasure I have felt as a mother is extreem, as so many parents choose to excel their child's social ranking at the risk of morality & integrity. That, i find to be the most unappealing aspect.

column1: They have all way had a good rating.To this day I can say I attended this great school Where is this system's website? Says a lot about their communication abilities. Community and parents have a right to know what is going on. In the age of technology there is no excuse for having no website. Check the test scores. Consistently BELOW average in every category, year after year. I graduated from this school with highest honors, and performed dismally in math and science in college. I had a few stand-out teachers during my time at GCHS, and they did a fantastic job with their subject matter. But those were the exception and not the rule. If you have a smart, college-bound child, get the heck out of this school district! Don't let their grades and honors fool you......they will NOT be prepared for college level courses with a diploma from GCHS. column3: This is an excellent school. I have been reading these reviews and find many of the negative comments to be utterly ridiculous. A claim of mediocrity is not a small insult, and Hendersonville High School (HHS)is far from barely adequate. There is a continuous pursuit of excellence that drives both faculty and students at HHS. As a student there, I knew my teachers were sincerely interested in my success and eager to help me prevail. HHS has great extracurricular options that in fact do allow for much growth as an individual as well as a team player. HHS is a comparatively small school and as such, it is very easy to familiarize oneself with the faculty and fellow students. Students are not merely names on a sheet of paper at HHS, or merely boiled down to score grades, HHS faculty makes a diligent effort to make everyone feel welcome and to help them achieve. As I near completion of my undergraduate education, I am pleased to have been able to call HHS my home for four years. The education I gained there has been invaluable to me and something I took for granted while I was there. I am grateful for the tradition and excellence HHS presented me with, others are not as fortunate. This is an amazing school! I have loved every minute of it.

column1: I had an excellent education at RRHS and thank all of the teachers and administrators for preparing me college and life. This is a great school and school system. Our daughter went from a private school to Rocky River schools and is excelling faster than ever. Great teachers and community support make all the difference What makes a school great is the environment that surrounds it, unfortunately the environment of RRHS is subpar. I am a recent graduate from RRHS (class of 2016) and took AP classes and graduated with a 4.56 GPA, but that is all based on my dedication and hard work, not the school itself. If you are a dedicated and passionate student you will do well in any school. Rocky River is an affluent community and it is filled with cliques. If you belong in a certain category of "popular" then you will fit right in and have no problems. If you are not deemed into that category then you will be looked down upon. The school is mostly based on PTA and helicopter parents who feed into their children's egos. From what I have experienced the entire attitude of schools in Rocky River is that it is a popularity contest. Everything is about being popular and if you're not, well too bad, I guess you don't really matter.

column3: Mexico HS is located on a well-planned campus. The campus incorporates the area-wide Hart Career Center & playing fields & gyms for basketball, wrestling, football, track, baseball & softball. The campus is unmatched in the local area & for schools near the same size. Classroom spaces have wireless Internet & tech for students & staff. MHS has 5 dedicated computer labs, & 4 mobile laptop labs. All students are provided a Google email account for assignment storage and communication. Students can earn 30 dual credit college hrs at MHS through a collaborative agreement with Moberly Area Community College; these credits transfer to statewide institutions. Students can earn 2 years of tuition through the A+ program. MHS involves students in an enhanced ACT preparation program with practice tests, feedback, free online prep, & study manuals. The career center provides access to a certified welding program, project lead the way pre-engineering classes, a cosmetology certification, CNA, Diesel mechanics, vocational agriculture/FFA, computer network & programming. MHS students find many options to help them be college & career ready - many more than other schools of similar size. I attended Mexico High School for two years. The reason I give it only two stars is because there were bullying issues that were not taken care of. The staff is hard to keep and I had brand new, fresh out of college teachers both years which caused me to struggle because of the lack of classroom discipline. It is hard to find your group at such a small school. The Worst school in the state of MO

column1: This school is improving a lot, and has been going uphill slowly since we got a whole new administration last year(2014-2015 school year was their first year). The grading system has finally settled, which is nice. We also have many new teachers, many of which are young and bring new ways of teaching to the school. There are still some not so great things about the school, I've had some personal issues, but things have been pretty good the past 2 years(I am a senior, the first two weren't so great). As for preparing kids for college, I think that is definitely something the school should be and is working on, because so many students after high school feel the school doesn't prepare the students well enough for college. It is a work in progress though. The school handles bullying pretty well, but you still need to really push for them to actually do something about it.To conclude, Freshman year sucks for most people, but I think the rest of the years as long as you make an effort in your classes, seek help when you need it, and try to be involved in after school activities you will be fine in this school. There's after school activities for just about everybody! Get involved, stay out of drama, and don't do drugs.This website gives no information on the clubs here, but there are many after school activities to get involved in. Such as Student Council, Key Club, Gay Straight Alliance, Jazz Band, Art Honor Society, French Honor Society, and more. Moving to this school has been a wonderful transition. My kids love their teachers as well as all of the friends they've made. With all of the extracurricular activities that my kids love as well as duel placement with some classes for college credit this has been a great school. The music program is fantastic and my child loves jazz band! School spirit is great from what I could see, my daughter encourages my whole family to the football games, even though she clearly doesn't play, "it's all about the people, Mom." Great school. Great families, great kids. Yes, like with all schools there are those kids that are going to be trouble but the school offers plenty of opportunities for kids to keep busy and stay out of trouble. The staff is disrespectful and condescending, creating a unhealthy environment I am a student at this school and when I came out as trans, I was looked down upon by more teachers and students who don't try to understand. I also have slight disabilities but no teacher helps well enough with that. Whenever an assignment is given, the teachers are not reliable with taking care of your work and if you ask for help with one then the teacher will likely not help or forget you even asked in the first place. Very unfriendly and uncooperative. Good solid educational opportunities, a variety of co-curricular activities, nice upgraded facilities, and STEM opportunities. Very poor experience! College counselors do not care whether or not you succeed, and don't provide students with any tools to go much farther than community college. If you're bullied, it's blamed on you! Most of the teachers are very caring, but are under payed and don't have enough resources. Administration and counseling does not care about the student body at all. We're D2 or D3 in most sports, and yet a large amount of our funds are spent on the football team by an administration yearning for their glory days while our arts and STEM departments struggle.

column3: The students are what makes Yankton High School so great. Yankton High School has friendly students giving it a small town school climate within a medium-sized town. I think the teachers and administrators are pleased to teach at Yankton High School as sseen by the high teacher retention. Teachers are proud to work with Yankton High School students who give their time and support to each other. The teachers provide students with well-prepared classroom lesson plans. In addition, the teachers volunteer to coach many after school activities including speech, history, music, sports, and science. The administration goal is to keep the school a safe and well-mannered place.. Overall, the students have won trophies at the state and national level in many areas including science and history. Some national competitions that the students have done well in, and accomplished first place, include individual events Science Olympiad and National History Day. The students accept each other, and are proud of each others' accomplishments. Overall, the students make Yankton High School a great place to attend, and benefit from its strong teaching staff and supportive administration..

column1: The school has fallen on very hard times. The Superintendent is a poor leader and has no committment to setting high academic standards. The school recently eliminated most weighting for upper level academic course work and has diluted the value of class rank. Students with good grades in basic courses are ranked higher than students who challenge themselves in advanced courses and receive B's. The school has quit on competing academically with schools like Eastern and Haddon Twp, and seems to be content to be on par with Paulsboro and Glassboro. It will be a long, slow and painful ride to the bottom of the heap and it is a real shame. This school cares nothing about the well being of its students. This school does not bus its kids NONE OF THEM!!!! Currently we have snow and ice all over the city and yet the kids are expected to walk to school tomorrow 1/23/2014. If you want to send your kid to this school be prepared to be your kids chauffer for 4 years BECAUSE STERLING DOES NOT CARE. Oh and most other high schools are on 2 hour delay tomorrow. THIS HIGH SCHOOL CARES NOTHING ABOUT THE KIDS JUST A PAYCHECK!!!!!! DONT EVER SEND YOUR CHILD HERE!!!!!!! UNLESS THEIR WELL BEING AND EDUCATION DOES NOT MATTER TO YOU!!!!!! I am so frustrated with what I am seeing. I have a daughter who gets all As and Bs scoring low on the PSAT. The kids have to take biology without a book, I looked up the book online and bought it for $12. Come on!!! we can afford books for the kids with the taxes we pay. As a former Biology major in college I can tell you there is no way to really understand the subject and reference complex facts without ink and paper. My daughter is learning from Google and I don't like it. Last quarter she had a social studies class with a teacher who made it clear he didn't want to teach at the parents night. He had an administrative job and was told he had to teach a class. The kids watched videos every day, the grades were based on how he felt their notes were kept, and he didn't even post any till after the class was finished. Basically he did nothing but grade the kids based on what he thought their norm was in other classes. I do like the idea of the paths for kids to take for certain careers and the block system does get them ready for college schedules. But there no academic challenge here. Kids have no homework, no papers due and teachers are more like media organizers than teachers. I am a student at Sterling and I absolutely love this school! Not only do we have block schedules- which helps us learn more a day- but it's small! The teachers go out of their way to personally know you and get you the extra help you need. There are TONS of after-school activities and there's at least one class for every possible career you could want! I am a "Choice Kid" so I don't HAVE to attend Sterling (it is not my primary school). I am enjoying my years at Sterling and my choice to go there is one I do not regret!! I would HIGHLY recommend this school to anyone thinking of bettering their future! Kids have to walk to school. SO WHAT !!!!!Do not drive you kids; let them walk of that junk food, free breakfast and lunch.Haddonfield, Heights, Haddon Twp., and Collingswood all walk.Change your diaper and worry about the worthless block schedules and no labs for science classes, unless their honor's classes. Great experience fpr my kids. Very happy with this school. As much as high school was a rough time for me, I think that the school itself was great. The teachers are easily the most reedeeming quality. Even the lunch ladies care a lot – I told them that I was a vegetarian, so they prepared a special meal for me every day (and it was really good for cafeteria food!). Overall, the entire staff really cares about the students. While there may be shortcomings in other areas (like funding or facilities), they more than make up for it in spirit. Most teachers are cruel, and do not look out for children in need of help. I’ve had many bad experiences that I kept to myself when I shouldn’t have. Now my sister is now experiencing the same. The school as a whole needs some big changing. Despite whatever ratings you see on here, Sterling is a significantly better high school than MANY of the major area high school districts. A very safe environment with great sport and after school programs/clubs.

column3: I am an Alumni of Ellenville High school. And found that they managed the students pretty well. The environment in which the kids are raised in makes it easy for them to get into trouble. So considering that fact I believe that at Ellenville Schools they do a decent job, but could do better. I really love Ellenville High School. I'm sad that I won't be attending for my senior year. The school isn't good at all. There's no trips. Nothing special about the school. & the students are horribly disrespectful. I wish I never sent my children here I would recommend anyone considering it please turn around and fine a better school. Overall, it’s okay. My child wants to finish out here and graduate from Ellenville. Comparing this school to my high school and even others in the area... this school does NOT offer many interesting electives (only language is Spanish) and they subscribe to ‘common core’ which is annoying. One of the “path to graduation” options the kids are required to follow does NOT include a science path, but art is a path??? Odd. Science is WAY more useful than art.

column1: My son is in the 10th grade and he is involved in both marching band and clubs. He is also in the honors and AP program. The teachers are dedicated and show they care. There is constant communication and my son is enjoying his time there. Like any school, there are kids with different personalities, but my son has managed to surround himself with a great group of peers that build each other up. The marching band is competitive and they push the kids to excel. It is a big school and it's somewhat overcrowded, but that will all change next year when the new Hampton High School opens and half of the kids will go there. I came from SandyCreek highschool in Fayette county. This school is horrible. The teachers don't teach , the students are disrespectful, and everyone is failing all their classes when they have a hour and a half study hall. If you're not use to block schedule then you wont like this school either. You have 4 classes a day more than a hour. I'm thankful i'm only here for one year. Their acdemics are so far behide as well. I'm getting help from my old teacher from SCHS so I can stay on the right path. I'm tranferring out this school and I've only been here a month. I just can't take it. We're getting out of Henry county as soon as we can. I totally disagree and will continue to disagree with the previous post. Everyone is NOT failing their classes. If you want proof, please look at the number of scholarships offered Luella's students and you will understand why. It is nice to know that you are continuing to receive help from your previous high school. That is what a teacher should do. Unfortunately, I have heard negative things about the school you are talking about. I agree with many of the posts concerning parental involvement. Parents who are involved will always see a difference. I have seen first hand, teachers who remain late, sometimes until after six to tutor students. Parents such as these are on board. Luella cares. Every school has problems. However, LHS believe in putting student's first and sorting through those problems. My son is new at Luella HS this yr. He loves it. Great teavhers and staff! Its clean and the teachers are great. This school has the rudest front office personnel that I have ever experienced in my entire 41 years of living. She clearly does not know what her job is . I wouldn't recommend this school to a dog in the street. I have been far worst but my GOD this is beyond that. This school is just sad. Some teachers take the time to teach, some do not care, and the rest just wait on the dismissal bell to ring. The first thing I noticed off the bat was how poor the school lunches are. They care more about what we wear to school other than what they put down our throats. Most of the kids here live in 300–700 thousand dollar homes and act like thugs and gangbangers. Teachers say what they want to students without a filter. I want out! this feels like a prison every day. On the bright side of things, there’re some supportive adults are in this school. I can tell Luella is trying but not hard enough. I'm very disappointed in this school. For this school to be in a middle-class area, sadly, it doesn't have the proper funding. Lord, forbid I start talking about the people in the front office. Walking into another school the front office attuite should be welcoming, not at Luella. On a good day, you get a little smile other than that they mean mugging you as if you owe them money. If you or a child is going to be a car rider in the mornings, I feel bad for you. Last year before 8:30 am they used to cover car riders with a late car rider pass, well not anymore. If you or your child are a second late after 8:15 am they don't get a late car rider pass and they are just late. So, if you are in are a car rider and stuck in morning traffic your child is late if you don't make it before 8:15 am. My job that PAYS ME to be there doesn't even treat me like that when I'm late. Overall, by all means, keep yourself or your child away from this school and as for anyone else get your child out of this school as soon as possible. God bless...

Suffered severe health issues in my senior year and because of the 7-absence penalty I almost didn't graduate on time even with documents on my poor health caused by the social anxieties of the school's overcrowding issue. There are so many choices of classes and opportunities to take advanced class that earn college credit. South Kitsap is by far one of the best schools on the peninsula. South Kitsap High school seems like a very good school so far. My daughter is a sophomore. The school is just so crowded. There should really be another High school in the area. south kitsap highis very crowed. staff seems to have a good handle on running the school Great teachers, students are very polite and friendly, lots of opportunities for students academically and with after school activities. Very large but that gives students lots of opportunities to be involved. Scheduling is sometimes difficult. Sports teams are good. Some of the building could use updating. Helpful staff, caring teachers and great kids. Many, many learning opportunities for all kids. It is big and that could be overwhelming to some but my kids thrived here! Great teachers, enjoy all the opportunities available Terrible, overcrowded, teachers don't care. Horrible school. Aside from it being over-crowded, SK offers AP prep courses for anyone willing to accept the challenge as well as CTE courses to prepare for the workforce. We have been very impressed with the band and orchestra programs This school is a dropout factory. The district changes standards for graduation every other year making nearly impossible to graduate. Kids are harassed by the schools security guards who are heavy handed cornering kids in bathrooms and doing inappropriate searches even against district policy. My son was threatened by another student and the district did an investigation than damaged the police’s investigation which caused then perp to go in punished. If I had it to do over again I would have moved elsewhere.

column3: I think had I had the opportunity to make the decision all over again....I would not have chosen Carondelet for my daughter. Here's why....I think I was thinking that she could escape some of the drama of adolescence here...she has not. I thought that the quality of education and athletic opportunities would be awesome....and it is but pushing "excellence" in all things has really done some damage to my already insecure daughter. The bar is pretty high and reaching a state of "excellence" is not easy...the push for it and constant cheer leading to strive for it at first felt motivating...but now feels unrealistic and almost wrong. The girls here are very stressed out and I'm wondering how that will play out for them in the future. Going to Carondelet is probably the best thing that has ever happened to be. I feel very loved and safe every time I walk onto campus. The sisterhood is a real thing and you can feel it every where you go. The faculty and administration truly care about their students in and out of the classroom. Carondelet pushes us girls to strive for greatness in whatever area we are interested in. They provide their girls with opportunities to use their passion to create and be a part of changes going on in our world. The spiritual aspect of the school is so special and one of the my favorite parts. Carondelet respects girls of all religious affiliations and they encourage us to share our opinion. I am proud to be a cougar and a part of the sisterhood and their is nothing negative I could say about this amazing place I get to call my school everyday. Carondelet is the phoniest place I have ever seen. They claim to have a catholic message when in reality all they care about is money. They do not care about the well being of your daughter, but rather how much is in their pocketbook. I may sound bitter, but I'm just being brutally honest. This school will completely destroy your daughters mental health between the ridiculous amount of work and bullying that goes on. They also claim to prepare your daughter for the real world, but how is only communicating and interacting with the female gender preparing her for that? The administration is messy and rude, just like its students. Unless your daughter is a 4.0 student athlete, they will not be valued at Carondelet. Your daughter will do much better at a public school and be much happier. I would say that all in all the education is very good and the ethics and values are in line with Catholic teaching

column3: My child was not thrilled with Roswell High School. He transferred this school year to another school in the area and said RHS is not a very good school. The teachers don't care about you and they will not help you. All they want to do is get there day over with and not teach the class and will not help you. He said it was like walking in a prison with no windows and the cheap school that it is had no air conditioning ever. The community thinks Roswell needs to build a new school and build a better learning place for the kids because that building is an embarrassment to our very well kept community. Parents that read this should send there kids to Milton, Cambridge, or a private school because this school just will not cut it anymore. Not to mention Huff is a very good principal but needs to figure something out with this school because it's going downhill. All the kids want to go to Milton now and leave Roswell. Milton is a very good school! I highly recommend it to the parents who don't want to send there kids to Roswell. As to the last post, were any concerns ever brought to the teachers or administration's attention? I have children that graduated and currently attend RHS. Most of the teachers do a very good job. Just as in the corporate world, there are a few that could probably be better. Whenever my children have needed extra help, their teachers have always made time for them before or after school. As for the building, no it is not new or fancy in relation to the High Schools they build now. That money has come from the county school board not the city of Roswell. Don't know what temperature your child likes but mine have often brought a sweater or sweatshirt with them because some classes are chilly. As for Mr. Huff, he is doing a good job. He wants the students to do their best and present themselves as young adults. He does not put up with too much B.S., unlike Dr. Spurka who seemed to like being popular. That is not in the job description. RHS is the real deal. Diverse, both racially and economically. The students at RHS have a great sense of community. We are all different but still part of one great family of Roswell. Good luck at your new school. I will continue to be proud of mine. In response to the previous poster, most of the students who were redistricted to Milton actually chose to stay at Roswell High School rather than move to Milton. In fact, the ten day count at Roswell High School had over 250 more students than expected who chose to stay rather than move to Milton. I am sorry this person had a bad experience, but the roster numbers speak for themselves. I have five children, and four of them have attended Roswell. We have had a very positive experience with Roswell High School and the dedicated teachers and staff. An alumni's perspective: 1. Roswell is a tough school. The workload is larger than 98% of the other schools in Georgia. Students here really work for their grades. 2. Roswell is not considered special in the eyes of colleges, no matter what they tell you. 3. Honors Points earned in the more difficult, "gifted" classes at Roswell are subtracted by colleges during the admissions process. (Call a college admissions office.) 4. In the eyes of a University Admissions office, your child's hard-earned 3.4 GPA at Roswell is not as good as a 3.6 at a school where kids don't crack a book for four years. 5. There will be about 600 kids in your child's graduating class. There are not enough counselors to go around. I had two 15 minute appointments with my high school counselor in four years. In summary: After four years at Roswell High School, your kid will be ready for college. However, he will most likely not have the GPA to get into his first choices for school. (But, he/she will have the highest SAT/ACT at the State University of West Georgia.) Roswell HIgh used to be an excellent school preparing students for college with rigorous courses and challenging teachers. However, this has changed in the past couple of years academically. Their Math and Science departments lack trained and experienced teachers. Since Dr. Wynne left Roswell the Math Dept has shown no enthusiasm and has basically collapsed. My son took AP Calculus last year and his teacher was out most of the time. On-level Physics is taught by a coach..?? How are these students going to perform if their college peers (esp. at Tech.) come from STEM schools? Roswell High has an excellent English Dept; these English teachers are well-qualified and hard-working. I have a 8th grader and I am really concerned about his high school future.. Being a rising junior at Roswell High, I find it very frustrating when I cant attain important information through the school website, as it is seldom working properly and is not user friendly. I find that the school is very focused on sports, and I feel that some students are swept under the rug. The front desk isn't helpful. The staff appears overworked and short, not giving enough time to help you throughly find an answer to a question. There is no solid foundation to the schedules given to students because something is always being changed. Contacting and/or meeting your counselor is extremely hard. Student networking sites are common within classrooms, but students who don't have access to a smart phone are out of luck. However, dress code is well adhered to, and safety is very important. Though old and rundown, Roswell High does have some positives and is slowly becoming restored to good health. Students though, need quick and easy access to information regarding classes and assignments which I, as a student, have not seen yet. Needed improvements should be made. The staff tries as hard as they can but some things need to be focused on more so than others. Overall Roswell High is a well rounded school that can challenge students academically. The teachers are very supportive and have great qualifications. . I would like to see the curriculum expanded to included more AP Classes. Overall good school. Not happy with two things: 1) lack of student services input prior to Jr. year. 2) The Lit. department thinks a few rounds of F averages at the beginning of each school year is acceptable. Why do they test what they have not to taught? They even say each year on Curriculum Night that they predict a failing grade average! Our students are trying to get into college with these grades and Hope Scholarships. STOP! Good things: many great teachers and admin folks! Great high school with amazing teachers, coaches, administration and parent and community involvement. Love the proposed architectural changes to update school and grounds. AP classes are more challenging than some of my grad level courses. My daughter was accepted into both UVA and Dartmouth. Could not be any happier with our RHS experience. Both of my children attend Roswell High and have had very good experiences. Both have had several teachers who went far above their job requirements to help. Of course, not all teachers do that, and I must agree with other comments that something is amiss in the Language Arts department as far as grading and actually teaching the material graded...? Overall, however, teachers have been responsive and caring and all have stayed late or come in early to meet with my students when asked. Mr. Huff is without equal. He cares about our students and our school like no other principal I have met. I have listened to area middle school teachers talk about the interest he shows to THEIR classes. He wants our students to succeed. In my work I meet with people throughout North Fulton and parents inevitably discuss schools. All the parents I've heard discuss Roswell High are exceptionally happy with it. Mr. Huff is an involved, concerned, administrator. He is happy, and healthy within his communications and conversations with his students, the parents and faculty. It is just a pleasure to share his space. The institutions he works in all have benefited from his being there. My son is a senior this year and he has thrived at Roswell High School. I cannot speak highly enough of Mr. Huff. He cares about his students and works to make them successful. He is a leader and mentor to the kids....but make no mistake, he does not strive to be their friend. He empowers his students and the staff. As far as the staff goes, they have challenged and supported my son's education every step of the way. He worked very hard, but he had the opportunities and the support system in place to make him well prepared for college. Principal Huff is an attentive energetic professional and he inspires all around him. His staff enjoys working with him and the students at the school and you can not buy or pay for that....It comes freely. Principal Huff has been fantastic! Teachers care about their students. Great environment! Shaw kept me going throughout my days in high-school. His motivation and passion for the school and the students is something you’ve never seen before. Knowing a principal who cares enough to support the Roswell Band (or any school team) in a different state (and also not during school hours) is mind-blowing. Dr. Shaw is why I finished high-school here at RHS so strong with a passion again for academics and success. My kids have loved their experience at RHS. The AP and Honors classes are challenging, but teacher support is strong with early morning study sessions. Coaches have been fabulous and helped teach my children valuable life lessons. The student services helped support my son’s college support. I would highly recommend RHS!

column1: All 4 of my children have attended DSJ, and my older 2 kids have graduated from college and gotten good jobs. DSJ did a wonderful job educating my children academically and spiritually, and they were well-prepared for college and beyond. The extracurricular activities are numerous and I feel every child has the opportunity to excel at St. John's.

I am a current Junior in the former Doshi, now STEM Science Research Program. All I can say is that it takes every student to get used to the High School environment, especially in a school like John Bowne. Again, everybody is different, therefore one cannot generalize. I learned so much in this school and have had the most amazing experiences both educational and social. I have changed as a person in this school because of the courses that are offered and the level of education. Personally, I cannot recommend a better school to anybody. If I were to give my personal judgement for parents thinking about their children's education. I would say make sure that your kid keeps up his or her grades in order to apply to the STEM program. And make sure that your child puts the STEM program as their first choice in the list of High Schools. Bowne is located in a great neighborhood sharing a campus with Queens College, Townsend Harris, two elementary schools and the Former CUNY Law school. The teachers are great, the staff is willing to work. I hope that one day, I can send my kids here as well! This school has a fairly unfortunate background knowledge of past events that occurred in the school, that has caused bad ratings. Many students who go to Bowne High school enjoy there time there. There are many opportunities to succeed in this school. They offer online courses, night school, free tutoring on school lunch periods, after school and on the weekends to help students succeed in their classes, as well as passing and getting the necessary requirements for their regents exam. They have over 200 clubs offered. Teachers and Staff and students in Bowne are free to create their own clubs, and after school activities. There are many opportunities for Volunteer services. They are the only school in Queens that offer an Agriculture program. As well as the accommodating Academy of Arts, JROTC, STEM and zone programs for students. Students have a wide range of AP, Honors, and College Now classes available. They have many interactive programs as well. I am a fellow student in John Bowne High School. Most of, the principal, Kwait, stands to his roots on his opinion of Success. All students are required to aim for the Advance Regents Diploma to get ready for college.

column1: Kasson-Mantorville High School serves grades 9-12 in the Kasson-Mantorville School District. It is among the few public high schools in Minnesota to receive a distinguished GreatSchools Rating of 10 out of 10. KM High School is a good school with great teachers who care about their students. KM High School has great staff and consistently places high in academics and athletics. They offer several college level classes and clubs to promote the success of all students. My school consistently out-scores area schools in academics! My school has had multiple state championships in just the past two years! Pretty good could be alot better but also alot worse. column3: The principle punishes students for what they post on social media on their own time The principle punishes students for their political views As a Counselor at this school, I can say as of 3/8/21 - the data on this profile is out of date and woefully inaccurate. As the General Summative Assessment was phased out years ago - the Equity readings are not accurate. When the GSA was phased out, we replaced it with the SAT and the Pre-SAT. Every 11th grader takes the SAT in April. So I would say about 95% of our Seniors have taken a college prep test. As the AP coordinator, I can say that 10% of our students are in one or more AP classes. In the last three years, we have increased our Dual Enrollment with WVUP by tenfold or more, and now have the possibility of students graduating high school with, or just shy of, an Associates Degree. I will not speak for the students, and the very real problems that they all face in our society and in this valley - but the numbers don't add up to just a 3/10. So I am a Freshman Involved in many sports and involved in the student council and I can say that this is honestly a good school from what I can see so far. Its clean, large but not overwhelming and everyone is just so nice here.

column1: I graduated in the class of 1972. Looking back on high school I recognized the positive impact of many of my teachers. Being called a "greaser" was the least of the issues and in fact set us apart from other schools. I had a Baker football coach who used to tell us how much he hated Istrouma. Then I moved there and followed the footsteps of my dad and his sisters...IHS...thank you for the memories. Its amazing how people from awhile ago remember great things about this schools. What was is no longer the case, and this schools is not meeting the needs of the students. Administration is poor. Teachers are tenured and expect little from students. Wishful thinking will not help this school. This schools scores reflect this inadequacies. I feel this school needs to be closed. Since the school has been taken over by RSD and Mr. Webb has become the principal, the school seems to have been turned around greatly. Mr. Webb fosters an academically-focused environment among his staff and students and discipline is very well-maintained. Great school. Highly recommend it as a choice for those looking for a good public school in Baton Rouge.
