column3: We moved out of the district BECAUSE of the schools. This district has to be the most overrated I've ever seen because the quality is extremely low in every respect. Carmel High school is too big but it does reflect the size of the egos of those affiliated. Most teachers are lazy and unconcerned about delivering watered down academic material. Administration is even worse.It is a very mediocre system which offers very little student development. It's sink or swim which is fine for students who are over acheivers. But even then, they have a false sense of superiority. They may NOT be as smart as they think they are. They may be missing out on so many intangibles that are not included in a Carmel education. Carmel is very superficial and unsophisticated. Students tend to lack character, a moral compass and adequate balance. The large sports program enables this belief in their superiority coupled with poor sportsmanship. If other districts cared more for their wins, they too would stuff students in one huge building...but they won't. Carmel is VERY good at promoting themselves as much as the parents are promoting their kids. It's a political battlefield. Wow! The previous folks posting must have large axes to grind. As a parent of a Carmel High School graduate, I can say that the academic instruction my son received at CHS fully prepared him for success at his select private college. He is now a college sophomore, and has often commented on how prepared he was compared to students coming from high schools elsewhere in the country. Yes, it is a large school, however, I found the staff and administrators to be extremely helpful when approached one-on-one. It is not - nor does it claim to be - anything but a large public school. Those expecting to be treated with 'kid gloves' should move their children to private schools. That said, I can tell you of many families who paid the big bucks for private high school and had no better luck gaining acceptance to select colleges than CHS grads. I firmly believe that the large, competitive environment at CHS more adequately prepares teens for success at the university level. Challenged: yes. Pampered: no. As the parent of 5 children who have attended Carmel Clay Schools, we moved to Carmel primarily because of the school system and we have not been disappointed. Three of our kids have graduated and gone on to college and we still have 2 students in the system. While the academics are rigorous, our kids found college to be a breeze because they were so well prepared by the Carmel School system. The size of the school was intimidating to me but the kids have all found clubs, organizations and activities that they have participated in which has helped them connect and form great friendships. Our kids aren't all star athletes which has limited their ability to participate on the school athletic teams. Carmel has an incredible level of talent given the large student count. However, we 've found the Carmel Dads Club is a great way for kids to participate in sports. The teachers are highly engaged and committed to the success of their students. Ultimately there are pros and cons in every school system. If parents want their kids prepared for a higher education and a highly competitive job market in the future, you won't find a school system that will do a better job than Carmel. Carmel High School has a large variety of programs that cater to a student's interest. If a kid is willing to put work into it he can be very successful. I don't think any of the programs are overrated, kids can challenge themselves with AP courses if they wish. There is a college prep division in the administrative department which works with every single student during their junior and senior year. Their performing arts program is one of the best in the state. Many of the kids are pretentious, but that is the parent's fault and it's not something to blame on the school. They have a model principal that cares very much for the students. The discipline system is bureaucratic and careless at times, admittedly. If your child is willing to work hard this is one of the best schools in the country to send them to. I am a student at Carmel High School and it's truthfully much worse than people hype it up to be. I have a reasonable GPA, 3.3-3.5 in mostly AP classes. To start off, there are some teachers who are absolutely amazing in every aspect but they're overshadowed by the teachers who have zero talent teaching, I have both types and my grades in those classes reflect that. Carmel does have extremely difficult courses in every department, take that as you will. If your thinking of moving into the area I seriously recommend putting kids in elementary schools first. Carmel tends to get very cliquie and becomes harder to make friends the old you get. If I could, I would move schools instantly. Even thought I get good grades I don't feel like I'm learning anything and fear that I'll be unprepared for higher education. Your typical high school, except I'm unbearably large. Yes, they offer a wide variety of classes including a multitude of AP classes, but when the work offered in said classes is at a level so low they students hardly learn anything- not impressed. The only challenges my son faced was getting to class on time and without being bullied. If the average grade in the high school is high, it's because the work is so easy my three year old daughter could do it. Teach my students something. I hate this school the students are snobby and teachers are not involved in the class they never explain anything. The school has a very sink or swim mentality. This school is only good if you are rich and from carmel. Carmel High School is a Midwestern school that lacks culture, sophistication, and humility. Like many that suffer from hubris the school is unaware that they posses these characteristics. The school is preoccupied with reminding everyone how many State championships they have won and have created a school that fits nicely into their bubble that Carmel is the best place to live in the World. Similar to Washington D.C. this illusion may be beneficial for the very few connected families and the small percentage of kids that will have the opportunity to play sports. The school is so massive that the well connected rise quickly to the top and look down their nose at the rest of the school. Great place to live if you are not concerned with your kid being exposed to culture, diversity, and reality. I moved to Carmel Indiana 28 years ago so that my then 5 year old son could go to Carme school system. This is the best public school in Indiana. I wanted my children to have the most and best opportunities available to them. Carmel school does just that. I now have my 4th child attending Carmel high school as a sophomore this year. Each one of my children have had their own individual experience at school and I have both enjoyed and dredged through the years with each one of them. Even after all these years , I still wouldn't change a thing. I am still very happy AND proud to say that my children attend/ /attended Carmel high school! The math department is terrible along with inferior math teachers. If your student isn't a math genius, choose another school. Carmel High School is a wonderful school, with a great learning environment; with wonderful students, and wonderful teachers. However, the administration is god-awful and my only complaint with the school. If not for them, Carmel would be a definite five, but at the moment its a borderline four and almost a three. That's how bad the administration is, I can't stress how bad they are. I agree with the person regarding administration. There is an arrogance about them which makes it nearly impossible to address problems they refuse to acknowledge. The large population makes it very difficult for students to get involved in sports and other activities because it is too competitive. There are some fantastic teachers at Carmel as there are awful ones. Math is known to be terrible. Receiving low grades in core subjects does nothing to 'showcase' Carmel math as the best place to 'prepare' kids for college. What it does is force kids into less selective schools which may or may not be what is the best fit. Carmel administrators do not acknowledge this math calamity, in spite of the very vocal parents who have been outraged. Some of the sciences are similar in approach. Parents are spending thousands of dollars tutoring their kids and most of the tutors are Carmel teachers. Is this some kind of guarantee subsidy for teachers? Make classes so impossible you have to pay big bucks so your child can survive their class? This is a huge conflict of interest epecially in the math dept. Someone should investigate this. Such a travesty! When my daughter attended the 8th grade, Carmerrl Clay Schools decided to change their method of teaching math. It was changed from a more traditional teacher led method to an "investigative" student led method. No one warned the parents. The resulting decline in student grades prompted a meeting at the high school. Needless to say the problem was never addressed and many parents chose to drop their child down a level which sucked for the 11th graders applying to college. My daughter was taking Algebra I in 8th grade. Her math grades drop and so did her ability to get into advanced classes, which we learned when we spoke with the Carmel High Freshman Counselor. Because of the math grade the high school counselor suggested she start all over with lower level classes (even though she was doing very well in 8th grade honors English). We decided to send our daughter to the International School of Indiana were she is now an honor roll student and has earned the opportunities to built an outstanding resume. Carmel is not the place. UNLESS OF COURSE YOU ARE AN OUTSTANDING ATHLETE! As a student learning at Carmel high school, there are many challenges with the curriculum, but the challenges have taught me new things. The education that the teachers provide is unmatched and many teachers take the time to help me with any questions. Also there are so many clubs and sports offered at my school. With so many sports teams and clubs, it engages the interests of many students inside and out of the class room. I love my school and couldn't imagine going anywhere else I graduated four years ago. It was challenging I'll admit. Carmel kids are held to a higher standard for most things, during high school I thought it was challenging. Going into college I knew much more than most of my classmates. I had an advantage, and I have to say it was Carmel High Schools curriculum. They tought me a more challenging pace but in the end it helped me greatly in college. This is a college prep school. It actually does prepare you. I advise for parents to put their children in the AVID program, not everyone gets in though. Only a select few. This program helps you with filling out college applications and teaches you most, if not all, basic core curriculum for college. I had no surprises. A overall great school! Size is big, but that is why it's important to get involved! Not good, late-policy is asinine. She was in the facility before the bell and received a detention for being late on a rainy day. Excellent. Carmel prepared me for college beyond all expectations, and going there made college seem easy. Personally I hated my time here. To put this into context, Carmel Clay Schools is a public school district with schools of very large student bodies, even in elementary school. However, I struggle with crowds and making friends in general because I get too shy and anxious, so spending the first two years of high school in Carmel was very overwhelming. The kids also tend to form cliques (the proclaimed "friend groups") as early as the second grade so if you have a hard time making friends, are just a loner in general, or are ostracized for any reason at all then you will find it very hard to fit in socially. Keep in mind that I spent Kindergarten through sophomore year in this public school system and during all of those years I made only three-four close friends (all of whom I barely ended up seeing anyway). I was also dealing with the worst of some very personal issues during these two years that I'm only now starting to recover from, which made my school experience worse. I already mentioned in a couple of other categories how I felt about the homework load and the effectiveness of the teachers but what really strikes me is that for all of the classes offered at Carmel and for the set up of their schedule (two out of the only three things I really enjoyed about my time at the school) the lack of attention/focus on these classes is as great as it is. Carmel is, in essence, a very sports-centric school and even then the only sports that seem to get hyped up are football, basketball, and just recently girl's lacrosse. All of what the administrators can talk about is how many state championships the school has won in their athletics and how many of their academic departments are "one of the best" if not "the best" in the nation. It's scary in all honesty, as though the administration only sees teachers, coaches, and most importantly the students as nothing more than trophies/trophy-winners rather than as individuals with their own emotions, personal troubles, and limitations. The school, for as large of a student body it has, the makeup of the student body is not very diverse. Some students are very accepting and it's great to see the kids with disabilities get treated like any of the other kids would and be welcomed and accepted by the students. However, it's not enough to cover up the fact that most of this school and the people there live under a bubble. Very good I love to be here Carmel High School is an interesting school to say the least. It's definitely very hard to make friends unless you're not in a "clique" and even on sports teams and such all the "popular" people are together in a little friend group and you're left out if you're not like them. In terms of diversity and accepting everyone, most students, except for those annoying girls who are in younglife camp, accept people of all different races, sexuality, etc. When I was a freshman there was a whole scene because the transphobic vice principal of the freshmen center wouldn't let a trans girl use the women's restroom due to a complaint filed by two younglife girls of course. I think in my opinion teachers are a hit or miss. Some really do care about you especially the ones in the english department and want you to excel but others honestly do not care, especially the science department teachers. I do think that there is a place for everyone here if you're willing to go and look for it but they don't make those things well known. It is very rigorous academically especially with honors/AP classes but I think it will make college somewhat. And of course let's not forget that the only thing the administrators care about is how many state titles we've won. This school assumes everyone works around them and everyone including parents that are new to the school system know everything. Also it doesnt look like they try to help students that need help but more so create confusion. If a kid needs guidance he or she would be lost in this school environment. They treat kids like seniors in college, that is great to prepare them for college but they need help, guidance and hand holdings at times that you can not expect at this school. Counseling is useless and it is not clear how kids are doing until it is too late.

column1: I received a very high quality education from Chatard and had no trouble adjusting to college academics. My teachers were knowledgeable and experienced. However, I struggled to fit in with the social environment. When I attended BCHS, it was extremely focused on athletics and if you were not an athlete or part of an established family at the school, you were not on the social radar. I was bullied terribly by my classmates and did not feel comfortable telling the administrators. I felt there was a lot of favoritism and because my bullies were popular and in sports, no one would care. It got so bad I was begging my mother to switch me to a public school my senior year. I honestly feel I would have had many more friends and a much more positive experience at North Central or another public school, especially if I had taken honors or accelerated classes there, I think I would have had an equally good college prep education. I honestly do not have many positive memories of Chatard other than the good education I received. Bishop Chatard High School is an outstanding high school and one of the primary reasons that I have been successful in my life. First and foremost, Bishop Chatard provided me an outstanding education that prepared me extremely well for college. Bishop Chatard also allowed me to grow because of the focus it puts on developing the whole person. I truly believe that my experiences at Bishop Chatard have given me the foundation to understand my religion better, understand many different people, react and adjust to life experiences better, and provided me a greater sense of the importance of community and impacting it positively. Awesome, no complaints, nurturing environment , great lunch program, super students/faculty, like family. It was a pleasure to be a parent there. Bill Sahm the president is sensational. I can not in good faith recommend this school to anyone. After the departure of the last principle this school has been thrown into administrative chaos. The current administration is run by educators that hold little regard for the educational and emotional well being of students, selectively enforces rules, and actively disregards and ignores concerned parents. In the past two years a administrator, who will remain nameless, actively dismissed parents concerns and took measures to avoid interactions with said concerned parents. I feel the best way to summarize the student experience is that they are treated as the I.D. number they are assigned and nothing more. Any prestige or accolades this school celebrates are not in any way a accurate representation of this institutions current educational prowess. After four years at this school I can say with certainty that this school has seen a massive degradation in quality and your children will NOT be cared for. I am an alum of Bishop Chatard and a prospective parent. My experience as a student was great. In recent years, I have had many encounters with students and families and they have all been positive. The students are compassionate, helpful and diverse. The families and parents are down-to-earth, accepting and caring. Now that I am looking through a different lens as I prospective parent, I so look forward to sending my children to this school. I believe it offers a faith-filled and well-rounded experience for young adults. Very little quality teachers. They seem so unequipped to teach that the students have late start every Monday and early dismissal every Friday. That is 2 full weeks of education lost so the teachers can have staff meetings. The teachers, staff, administration, and students of Bishop Chatard High School are family. We've had 2 children graduate and go on to great colleges with much success. We have 2 children there now who are being cared for during a very trying time in our family's life. No other place has opportunities like BCHS because of it's size and the academic excellence provided by caring teachers, staff, and administration. The block scheduling referred to in a previous post offers an entire hour per day for each class. More time for teaching, more time for reviewing, more time for students to complete assignments and ask questions during class time. BCHS is an exceptional choice for anyone wanting a solid, top of the line education for their children with the addition of amazing Catholic teaching immersed in every aspect of their school day. Sadly the new administrators are the worst power-hungry individuals you will ever meet. They have no understanding of the mission of the Catholic church, and lack all the integrity that pass administrators have held on for so long. The students are welcoming, but you can't get too far when the blinds are leading the blinder. It is no longer about the hard work and service to the students but bullying staffs and lazy administrators who ignore the concerns of parent and student - Sad I have had 5 children graduate from Chatard high school in the last 8 years. They all had different personalities, strengths and weaknesses. It was a great academic and learning environment where their different levels of abilities were met and they have a great resource department for those needing extra help. I always felt the teachers respected my children and had the utmost concern for them. We wanted our chiIdren in an academically strong school that taught and lived the Catholic values we live at home. My children truly loved being a part of the Chatard community as well as us. It was truly It was a great decision on our part to send our children to Chatard and to become part of the Chatard community. Bishop Chatard is a great community to be involved with.My husband and I have had two kids graduate from there. As well as a Sophomore and we will be sending our First Grader there one day. We feel blessed that our kids are learning the sense of community in such a great place. It is obvious that the person who entered all the 1 star ratings is the same person. I am sorry they had a bad experience but most of what they said is not true. For example...1) Late Mon mornings and early dismissal Fri afternoon scheduling is not so teachers can have meetings but so that teachers get a longer time with children per class period and so they do not have the same group at the same time every day... it is called block scheduling. In the old scheduling world, when my child had math at 8 am every morning, they didn't always do well because they were tired. Now my child has math at various times through the week which has helped tremendously. They also get a little bit longer time in the class.2) The staff does not bully and are there to help. I had a concern about my child and all I did was email guidance and they were all over it to help. Met with my child and then if things didn't resolve, would meet with me. They are VERY caring.My children grow in faith and education. They are VERY involved in service, sports and activities. Chatard takes all kids from all learning levels and all socio-economic levels. They care about each one. My children are prepared for life after high school... Thank you Chatard! Wonderful learning environment, excellent sports programs. Great springboard to college. My daughter had an outstanding experience! Superb and caring staff, nice cozy atmosphere, students are great, stellar academics, few complaints if any. As an alum and parent of 4 current and past students, this school has been a blessing in so many ways. The administrators know my kids and personally interact with them. They are not just a number. The teachers and coaches go the extra mile to ensure that every student succeeds. Our experience at Bishop Chatard has been wonderful! We were not from Indianapolis originally and weren't too familiar with any of the high schools, so we compared all the schools in the area when our first child was going to high school. There are a lot of great schools around! While they all had some positives, we are so grateful we chose Chatard for our family. The size of the school, caring faculty, and opportunities inside and outside of the classroom have helped our children grow into young adults who are ready for life after high school. In fact, our three children who have graduated headed to college taking with them so many AP credits that they could register as sophomores during their first year. More imortantly, Chatard's mission is to weave the formation of the whole person through the entire curriculum, so the focus is on developing mind, body, and spirit. It is an authentic Catholic education! Bishop Chatard is a great place to call home.

column3: I feel the schools are great - good quality teachers and good parent interaction. My daughter has taken advantage of the academic opportunities presented to her at GCHS. These include but are not limited to the 9 AP classes she has completed successfully. The rigor has given her the opportunity to be admitted to The Ohio State University on an academic scholarship :-). Thank you SWCS, Buckeye Woods, Park Street Intermediate,Jackson Middle School and GCHS teachers for their time, effort and decication providing the educational growth opportunities to her over the years. Thanks!! All involved are energetic and dedicated towards the success and growth of the student. This is a wonderful school. Diverse offerings for students to choose from. Lots of extracurricular and the atmosphere is far more inclusive than most other high schools I hear about in the area. My grandson attends Grove City High School. He was on the football team, attended every practice, worked hard, and never was given the opportunity to play 1 minute of any game. How can any school allow such treatment of any student? How does this inspire students to work hard, or improve their self esteem, or promote team spirit? It certainly does not reward hard work, dedication, and sacrifice. What is this school's mission statement? In my opinion every athlete should be given the opportunity to play, especially their senior year. I feel sorry for any other young men hoping that hard work and dedication will be rewarded with fair and equal treatment. And for the parents, and grandparents (who traveled 150 miles) who attend every game waiting to see their athlete take the field, if only for a few minutes, this was crushing. My grandson's Grove City High School football memories will forever be a lesson in how NOT to treat anyone. I certainly hope the football coach never has the opportunity to treat another young man with such disrespect. If you're thinking of sending your student to Grove City for their athletic development, my advice is "Don't"!!! It is currently my senior year at this school, and I can thoroughly say my time here was iffy at best.Though I do say that, there were some good things, such as diverse artistic programs, a great French teacher whom I see as a second mother. The drama club was a lot of fun the two years I attended, and some of the history teachers were full of wonderful personality and taught well. For me, at least.However. I struggle at this school. I've always struggled with homework, and I'm finding out it may be undiagnosed inattentive ADHD making it hard to focus. I've struggled since I was little. The homework protocol at this school is basically "give homework, collect, check if done, give 10/10 if done." The first problem is that it's not checking how students did in the first place, it's just checking for completion, not understanding. The second problem is that there's often many classes giving out homework. Though the classes I've liked more are sparse in the work they give, the others are constantly giving it out (math especially) giving no free time to students, especially those with jobs or in clubs/music/sports. Thirdly, they never check why a student may chronically not do their homework. It's expected that students go to the teachers, or that such students are lazy, when that may not be the case. It's scary to go to people for help, or to figure things out, it really is. Especially when you were a gifted child in younger years.Pandemic aside, the hallways were normally extremely crowded. It was hard to move and students (commonly freshmen) would get rowdy.There was a case where my friend came to me and explained that other students were making fun of something I did online my freshman year. I told a teacher about it, and she went to someone else (I struggle to remember names and staff positions, forgive me), who called the main girl and I into her office. I was told that I was being called things like "autistic" for this action that I had done and that was recorded and shared around. Instead of a proper punishment, you want to know what happened? The girl was put on the spot to apologize, and I was put on the spot to accept the apology. The incident made me insecure and nervous about what I did around the school, and I didn't want to accept the apology, but I had to.The English classes through the four grades feel as though the repeat themselves. Argumentative essays, Old English, poems, etc. I'm running out of characters so that's all I can say

column1: Twin Spring HighSchool is definitely one of a kind. I've had two children go through from 8th-12th. Neither one of them wanted to/wants to graduate. They have loved the experience of being part of this "family" of 280 or so. New teachers who have worked in other school systems have also said they have never seen a school like it. There are no clicks to speak of and if a student transfers in and is friendly and wants to make friends, within days they are absorbed into the others like they have always been there. There have been several exchange students here and they become as much a part of it all as anyone else and in some cases return for special events, etc., after they graduate as well. My oldest child graduated in the top 10 and has attended Mountain Empire for 2 years, tuition free because of grades in high school, and is now attending a 4 year college with all A's and one B. They have access to online classes (Linwood Holton Governor's School) and in-school teachers who in most cases are willing to work with them on a one to one basis if needed. They have had one student accepted to Harvard, one to Notre Dame, etc. It's a great school. Basketball team is looking pretty good this year. I can't wait to see how the team does. Twin Springs is a joke! They recruit exchange students and kids from other schools to make their basketball team better. I know several kids there that have had hopes of playing only to end up sitting the bench watching the recruits play. They had some great teams with their own kids back in the 90's but in recent years its been all about exchange students and transfers. Very pathetic school to say the least. Great education available for those who take advantage of it. I am a 1974 graduate, now a university professor. The foundational education I received at Twin Springs served me well as I pursued and completed my Bachelors, Masters, and Doctoral degrees. I served a doctoral fellowship with a Fullbright scholar and I was just as prepared for the rigors of a doctoral program as she. Many/most schools can do very well with gifted students; the measure of a good school is how well they do with an average student. The faculty at Twin Springs excels in the preparation of graduates for success in life. The members of my graduating class have lead successful and productive lives and are thankful that they attended a high school where caring was the norm, not the exception. The staff, custodians and kitchen workers have always been very polite. I have visited during working hours, ball games and special events. I am impressed with Twin Springs High School.

A student getting all A's in AP classes doesn't get any advantage over a student getting all A's taking the bare minimum courses. Due to this, I ended up ranked lower in comparison to other classmates than I should have been. But this is an issue that will rarely affect something like college admissions, so it's not necessarily a huge problem. I see a lot of people here raving about EHS. I felt it would be best for me, a relatively recent graduate who attended a research university and is currently in graduate school for a PhD in a life science discipline, to share my opinion. I graduated in 2007, so a few years ago. However, I have a sibling that is a more recent graduate as well. One thing to keep in mind is that while EHS is probably better than the 2-3 alternatives that are anywhere close-ish, it is by no means an excellent school. You won't find significant drug problems, and the class sizes are typically small. However, you also won't find ANY AP classes. How a school that has no AP classes can be rated this highly is beyond me. They used to have AP Biology, but that is no longer available. There are no "honors" classes either. Instead of all these things you have the option to transport yourself ~30 mins away to a community college (in the winter this is no small feat), or as a freshman you can enroll in a math and science center (also pretty far away).Just because a school has small class sizes does not mean that it is an excellent learning environment. I would've rather gone somewhere that could've prepared me for higher Ed better. Once again, it's a small town high school which is low on crime, etc. It is not, however, a place where you're going to receive any more than the bare minimum. This school is alright. I am currently attending and can see why people praise it. However, there are a lot of flaws hiding just below the surface. The elective classes are few and far between. The classes available offer basic skills and the classes that were worth something were taken out years ago. Don't expect to learn any life skills only skills to prepare for the ACT or other standardized tests. Also, jocks run the school. It's the stereotypical school where those who aren't on the football team are looked down upon. Due to this, physical education classes can become a chore as every student takes it way too personally. The two major cliques in the school are jocks and white trash. Nearly every student you meet has done Marijuana at one point or another. Most students would rather talk about you behind your back than get to know you. School funding goes mainly towards sports and school lunches cost way too much for the portions and quality of the food. There are few teachers who care about teaching meaningful material rather than what's going to be on the ACT and the whole curriculum is based around this test. After the test it's basically a "what now?" situation as teachers assign the first thing that comes to mind. That said, you WILL make close friends attending as I have known most of my friends for 6 years or more. The school spirit during homecoming week is like none other as well. Seas of orange and blue as far as the eye can see. The school really does come together during these spirit weeks. Edwardsburg high school is better than most schools close to it but is still mediocre at best. The cons outweigh the pros. I went to Edwardsburg for three years and i have been bullied all three years by different individuals. I have gone to the vice principle with evidence that something was going on and he just pretty much blew it off! I personally do not recommend this school and they need to take bullying more seriously!! Edwardsburg school's priorities goes like this, 1. Make sure the school looks good. We have a great maintenance staff that works hard, and are very nice people. Mr. Udell is the most whole-hearted person in the school. 2. Test scores, test scores, test scores. Months before the ACT or SAT students spend class periods going over what might be seen on the test, and what things they are looking for. They really grind it in to the students head to do good on this test, very high pressured test. 3. is the football team. The football team is praised by this school, and by the teachers. I have witnessed this first hand, if youre on the team, you have special rights in the school. Teachers lack on discipline towards you and even the vice principal gives a little more if youre on the team. There is no "Justice" or "equality" at edwardsburg. There is just on the fly discipline, and the vice principal with bring up drama that goes around in the school when disciplining you. This school has a huge drug and bullying problem. There is no such thing as a challenging course in Edwardsburg all standard classes. There's not one class that can challenge students to better themselves and get them ready for the future. All the teachers are push overs, and are at the mercy of the students. On the outside its a great school, but on the inside there is a lot that needs to be fixed. A new board and superintendent is needed to bring in a different attitude to this school. The superintendent is also very overpaid for the poor work he does. There are absolutely no AP or AH classes. Grades for online or offsite AP and AH classes are not weighted. The school board only cares about sports. Academic extracurriculars are few and far between, and those that are available constantly have funding cut from them to add to the funding for sports. The teacher mostly do not care if students succeed. They teach to the ACT and SAT. There is little to no effort towards making lessons engaging. There is a lot of school spirit in this small town, but it feels more cultish than welcoming. Overall, I've had an awful experience with this school, and would recommend that all high-achieving students look elsewhere. This school is the definition of mediocrity, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone looking to get a decent education. DONT SEND YOUR KIDS HERE! save yourself the trouble and look elsewhere. The school system as a whole is terrible. The high school offers no help for struggling students. I received no emails or contact from any teachers when my child stopped turning in his homework. I had to see it myself in the app they suggest. In speaking with the guidance counselor al she offers is for him to go to alternate education instead. In doing research, schools recommend alt education so that the failure and graduation rates don't go down by a struggling student. It was told to me that the only way for him to graduate with these grades was to do alt education. After further questioning by me, she then said, " I mean the only way for him to graduate with his current class". He would graduate, but maybe a semester or year late. That's not how she worded it. They are striving for marketing their school, not striving for the current students to succeed. They offer after school credit recovery for kids that have failed classes. As I sit there waiting for my son to come out , I watch well over 75 students walk out after credit recovery dismisses. Why are so many students failing? Poor teaching and delivery of subjects? Possibly. After a semester there 6 of my sons friends didn't come back to Edwardsburg HS. One went to a different school, one went to alt education at different school system, one stayed home for online classes and one dropped out completely I believe. If this is such a great school system why are so many students leaving and failing classes? Save yourself the trouble and look elsewhere. I'm stuck with the system for now. I pay high taxes for a poor school system- shame on me for not doing better research before moving my kids here. Horrible. I would never send my kids here.Graduating Class of 2016. ok thank you very much guys. you rock! Its awesome and fun. The teachers make learning fun and the school as a whole is fun and energetic. I am defiantly having my kids go to this school. As a current Senior at Edwardsburg I can honestly say I am ecstatic about how my high school experience was, I wouldn´t change a thing. Also more AP and IB courses are being offered every year, take the courses you feel comfortable taking! EVERYONE has a place at Edwardsburg high school ! Great experience with solid, diverse education for leading to college experience. Especially like the Early College and band programs. This school is very good in my opinion. It offers many academic and athletic opportunities, pushing students to their highest potential. The teachers are amazing and are extremely nice and respectful. They always find ways to help their students and will never stop pushing them towards success. The student body is mostly nice and welcoming, but there are a few students who are disrespectful. The athletics are beyond outstanding as they have extremely talented and high achieving sports. The most notable sport would be football. But, all athletics to outstanding. Also, the arts programs are amazing. The choir is extremely vocally talented and high achieving. The band is award winning and extremely good. Also, the theatre program puts on amazing shows. The students at Edwardsburg are truly talented. But like all schools, there’s it’s flaws. The school is pretty old and needs a few updates. While the dress code has been loosened up a little bit, I think it is a little to strict. Also the diversity isn’t that good. Most people are either white or mixed. But the diversity keeps growing each year, which is good. Also, there are some toxic people and people who bring negative energy to the school, which kind of sucks because I love going to school here, but some people don’t, which is fine, but it kind of gets annoying when people constantly say they don’t like it, like, I heard you the first time. But, on the bright side, a lot of students are really nice and happy. I truly believe this school is beyond amazing and I recommend it to anyone. I know many people (as well as myself) that have transferred here throughout the years, and I can not tell you the amazing differences between this school and other schools. EHS is so much better than almost every other school around us.

column1: It's sad how this school had been degraded since I was a student here in 1980s! This was one of the best schools in Clinton. I attended this HS and thought was a terrific experience. I made lifelong friends and learned a lot. The teachers and counselors are great! They keep the kids focused and make sure they understand that college is the next step. Overall experience has been really good for my junior. Of his HS career, we've had significant issues with one teacher. Her teaching style wasn't conducive to my child's learning style. She WOULD NOT BEND. It took extra work at home to ensure his success. Staff is grossly underfunded, as well as athletics. Parents unite to ensure kids have what they need, and have been successful, but could use more help from the county. Small class size is definitely a plus Horrible!! Horrible!! Horrible!! Horrible!! Horrible!! Horrible!! Horrible!! If I could give this school a zero, that's what it would have. This was my daughters first and last year at this school. I have been trying to get in touch with the principle for pretty much the whole 3rd and 4th quarter, and she never contacted me to this day! I called the school and left her several messages and I sent her several emails and never got a response. The teachers tell the students that a D is passing. WHO DOES THAT!!! The teachers don't care nothing about these kids cause that is unacceptable. They tell the kids to use their phones to complete some of their work, and that is crazy. the students should not be on their phones at all during class. What are the teachers doing!!! If you care about your child's education, please don't send them here. It's a shame that you have to take your kids out of PG County to get a decent education. I would not recommend this school. The communication was there , but the follow through was unsuccessful. Counselors were not available when needed for making sure that students had the best schedules to suit their needs. Senior tshirts were ordered in October, but unfortunately my child's tshirt was given away so a refund was requested. Senior pictures were taken and there was no follow thru from staff to parent on who didn't take pictures. Yearbooks were ordered for $100 and the staff is not going to put the yearbook order in until the last day of school. Students should have had their yearbooks prior to graduation so they're classmates can share in on signing each other yearbooks. You can't get these moments back. I don't know if they're going to mail the yearbooks or what.

column3: Just a bad school in general, bad teachers, bad students, way to many fights! I was shocked to see this school getting an 8 out of 10 since when I checked a year ago it was a 2. To many teachers that do not have teaching degrees, a sports director that screams in his athletes faces, and a principal who doesn’t enforce rules. A few really great people there but they are to few

column1: The material covered in this school wasn't lacking, I thought it was fair when I attended 2 years of middle school. The kids were very poorly mannered and undisciplined racists, openly making fun of my clothing, hair, or other looks. The teachers did not do much to stop them. There were some fights there, perhaps three in my two attendance years, and there were no penalties. The teachers were not very willing to help me with my work, other than Mrs. Kat. I would not recommend this school for anyone. Truely one of he most prejudiced schools I've ever attended. I preferred Schley County, which I attended paying out-of-county fees. Friendlier and more motivated teachers, kinder students, and a stronger stance against bullying. I have had one to graduate from this school and 2 still there. I think the young man's remarks from Jan 2011 are totally biased and do not fairly represent the atmosphere at Southland.. While not all of my kids are or were in the "in-crowd" so to speak, they get along with their classmates very well. I have one in college and while he struggled in high school, he is doing very well in college. I attribute that to the foundation he got at Southland and so does he. I can highly recommend this school to other parents looking for a college prep curriculum. Other schools in the area do not come close. My child attended k4 thru 9th grade. Finally, we moved to another school because the enviroment is sooo toxic. We had orginally picked this school because we thought she would receive a good education and be in a Christian enviroment - but we were wrong. Very Disappointed.... I have had three children to graduate from this school and I have no regrets sending them there. While I had to make finiancal sacrifices to do this, I have been rewarded with well behaved kids that have made my life as a parent a pleasure. The morals and beliefs I hold sacred are reinforced at this school. I must say that this school is not for everyone. Children with learning or behavior difficulties will find it to hard. The mandatory drug testing helps keep the kids on the straight and narrow but it also causes us to lose one sometimes when they know they are about to be caught. Of course this has caused hard feelings but is needed to maintain a drug free campus. The kids know they can't get a way with it. Great school with great people. I send both my kids here and have been very satisfied with the education they have received. School placed a big empasis on producing a well rounded student. Very good academics and extra curricular activities in a safe Christian environment. I would highly recommend. We moved to Americus 8 years ago and found our dream, Southland. We had 2 children to graduate and move on to college, Both have excelled beyond our dreams. We loved the family atmosphere and closeness of the kids and faculty. Of course, when dealing with children, there were some bumps in the road but the faculty handled them to our satisfaction and our kids learned how to get along with others. We came to Southland from another independent school in Macon. We were shocked to see that Southland's tuition was HALF. People still gripe about tuition but Southland is the best deal in the State!! We did have to sacrifice some things along the way for our children to get the kind of education that we felt they deserved, but looking back it now, it was a no-brainer. We remain today a very Happy Southland Family. Southland Academy's mission is to provide a firm foundation on which each student can build a strong mind, body, and spirit. We believe that it is essential to challenge our students with experiences in and out of the classroom, developing their minds and hearts so that they are able to determine who they are and what they have to offer our school and community. Southland Academy is known for its motto: Committed to Excellence. We strive for excellence in all that we do including academics, athletics, fine arts, and service. We are also committed to providing a respectful, safe, and caring environment. Southland Academy is most certainly the best decision we ever made for our family! There are high expectations academically and behaviorally for all students. I truly believe that any sacrifice we have had to make financially has been far outweighed by the benefits of our children attending Southland. Both of my children have been there since 4K and while every minute has not been perfect I have always been able to speak with teachers, administrators, and coaches to work out any problems/issues. We have recently acquired a new headmaster that I feel is very concerned with keeping our school on the right track. The relationships my entire family has made here will be lifelong relationships. I feel this is something hard to find in other places! We LOVE Southland and would never consider going anywhere else! Southland is a great school with a rich and proud tradition in our communtiy. The faculty and staff have provided several generations of families with the educational foundation needed to ensure each student succeed at whatever they undertake in life. The new leadership at the school is committed to guide Southland down the path to many more years of excellence. The future is exciting and bright at the school, and Southland is clearly the best choice in college prep that our community has to offer. Subpar education. They were very restrictive about which kids they'll let take "honors" classes; you usually had to be in their "honors" classes back in 7th grade to be in their High School honors classes. They had only two AP classes when I attended. Former student at 'The Academy', and thought this school was terrible. This school is said to have a Christian environment, however, it doesn't nurture or advertise Christian ideals, especially in it's high school beyond racism and cynicism. The 'average' Southland student is a selfish, closed-minded rich kid. The education is sub-par to begin with, but when paired with the poor motivation of these students and peer pressure to be as lazy as possible, it is truly a joke. The peer pressure even extends to the good kids. The good kids are often ostracized and ridiculed for their attempts of success. Graduates or alumni are very proud of Southland because it was, and still is, a close-knit community of snobs who think low of you if you do not attend Southland. Overall, a terrible place to enroll your child, but a great place to put your child if you want to waste your money. My two kids have plugged in very well at Southland Academy. We came from a public school in a neighboring county and while we were pleased with the school system they attended, we were missing that family spirit and school pride element that is so important. We moved to Southland and have never once regretted it. The family atmosphere and small class sizes made it an easy transition for our kids.The academics are excellent, the facilities are top notch and atheletics have more to offer than many of the larger public schools in our area. As is the case with many private schools technology is very costly and there are not endless supplies of tax dollars to spend on the technology. However, Southland has committed to improving it's technology and has installed smart boards in many of the classrooms and has budgeted to purchase more each year. This along with the group of fine teachers ensures that Southland students are at the forefront of the latest technology and instruction each year. As parents we are extremely pleased in our decision to join the Southland family, however our kids are the ones who have benefitted the most!! I am an alumni with two kids attending. Southland offers Christian based college prep education in a safe diciplined atmosphere. My family is very pleased with Southland and the many opportunities it offers for a very reasonable tuition. I attended 3 years of bad luck! Im an African American student and I was picked on about my skin color. The staff members did not try to stop it! The kids are very disrespectful to their subs. The reading teacher told me that interracial relationships are a sin. This school is a waste of money... I appreciate all that Southland Academy offers not only my child but also my family. Starting our third year at Southland, I have been more than pleased with Southland Academy's academic curriculum, small classes, safety of the campus, and kind and positive attitude of the faculty and staff. I look forward to the next several years we have to spend at Southland! We have two children who graduated from Southland. While they were there they were actively involved in many of the activities offered. We felt that they were always safe and encouraged. Both had high SAT scores and were accepted by everyschool they applies to. Both graduated from the college of their choice and were offered jobs immediately upon graduation. Mission Accomplished!! We chose Southland Academy for our child because of the safe learning environment. Students are taught respect for themselves and others. The teachers are very caring and have the student's best interest at heart. We are very happy with our decision and encourage other parents to go visit and see for yourselves! Faculty and Staff are concerned about every student. For a small school, there is a lot of activities.

column3: I graduated from Soldotna High School in 1997. It really was/is an amazing school with great teachers. I loved Battle of the Books and the wonderful librarian we had. My English teacher my Senior year was exceptionally wonderful, but all my teachers were great. I took a class in Food Science and another in Interior Design - I still remember both and use what I learned today. I wish my kids could find a school like it in state we live in now, but nothing really matches the wonderful education students in Alaska get. I hope they appreciate it; I didn't at the time, but I sure do now! I graduated from Soldotna High School in 2001. This school offered a wide variety of electives, and the teachers and other staff put their heart and souls into making each class the best it could be. The schools on the Kenai Peninsula have a high standard that many other states and areas don't come close to, including offering classes for gifted and talented students. Overall, a great school!

column1: Just don't like the feeling of the place. Bad teachers, student body, and facility. Try another high school. Highland is the stereotypical rich kid school where everything is bought instead of earned. Except for the straight A student part, they earned that poor rating all on their own merit. Highland is like a private school. There are no private high schools in town so if you want that feel...great academics, superior athletics, parent involvement. Guess what...its free!! Sure people may say that it is cliquey here. There may be some privileged kids...but there is also a VERY diverse population found in the hallways. We have emos, goths, skaters, stoners,jocks, dorks, brains, Hispanic, Pacific Islanders, American Indians, beautiful mixes of every shape size and color!!! In Poky we have 3 high schools and all are exceptional as we have ISU here. I moved here from Calif because of the schools and needing to raise 5 kids somewhere decent. Our schools have about every foreign language you can imagine available whereas w public schools in Cali you get Spanish offered and MAYBE French I. Be happy and stop complaining. You are getting an education people have to pay $15,000 a year for elsewhere. Although we are somewhat new here, I have now had 1 child graduate from this school, and another child is currently in 10th grade. My children have had a successful transition from their old schools, and have quickly made new friends, feel a camaraderie with their teachers, and excel in their classes. The Principal is also in constant communication with parents, and is doing a great job.

column3: School was great, i enjoyed my time here. Teachers all have a goal, and I didn't have one teacher that I felt was incompetent in their section. Sports were great! Now working on my Bachelors degree! The district is trying to save money, so they have closed most of the schools and put as many kids as they can in as few buildings as they can. As a consequence, this school, is a middle school and high school combined and has 2,000 students. Being in the hallways between classes is overwhelming, to say the least! My son is an autistic student and is in an 8 student classroom. I require them to take him from one room to another before all of the halls are filled with TOO MANY students. The staff is in complete denial about the bullying that goes on there. Some teachers, assistant principal, flat-out said, bullying DOES NOT happen in their school! My son only has 2 more years of school, thank God. I predict this entire situation in the Greece school district will not end well!

column1: Deshler High School is a wonderful school. It is the only school that i haven't been bullied in yet. I love this school because all of the teachers are loving and caring, and do anything to help anyone. They put great effort in to their hard work, and work at a pace so fluently, you can't say they aren't trying. I am a student of four years and have always been proud to say: "I AM A DESHLER TIGER!!!" :)

I was surprised to find such high caliber teachers in a very rural community. This school has an excellent ROTC, band, and state award winning yearbook, and BETA club. This school has an involved student body that supports the athletics and a top notch tennis coach. It offers a really good wildlife biology course and many career oriented programs (nursing etc). We really loved ACHS. As a student when this school first opened , I hated every minute of it. As a 35 year old, I'm thankful my child won't have to go this school. My children have been very successful at ACHS. The teachers truly care and work hard to help out the kids. The admin really want to help kids be successful and graduate with a plan of what is next.

column1: Tonawanda is by far the worst school ive gone to the teacher always intaginize untill you flip out then you get suspended for sticking up for yourself Its Outragious our experience has been Teachers dont want to give extra help & bullies get aw y while victims are punished

column3: Top grade instructors who mentally prepare a student for the university setting! It is among the top highschools in the state. Shawnee Heights is a wonderful high school where students have the chance to participate in many activities and work with great teachers. Teachers really care about their students and work to make personal connections with them. If your student wishes to be in multiple activities or sports, this is a school where they can do that; coaches will work with one another and with the student to make the most of their experience. The A.P teachers are all highly qualified and push to see the best in their students as do educators in regular classes. I would highly recommend Shawnee Heights if you want your child to experience a well rounded high school career. I am a teacher in this school and this is my first year here. I appreciate the approach that leadership takes with both staff and students. This is a wonderful place to work and a place where students can truly learn and succeed. Very good school, with lots to offer all students. Simply the best school in Topeka and Lawrence area. Teachers and facilites are top notch. Shawnee Heights High School has provided me with a lot of opportunities. They have clubs and numerous extra curricular activities for students to feel involved. I have been able to prepare myself for college, have a great high school experience, and get involved in my community. 10/10 recommend this school to anyone looking in the Topeka area. It’s a great day to be a T-bird!! An excellent school to go to with really really good teachers and nice students to go to school with Love this school teachers are so nice and work great with students

column1: Excellent teachers include Shara and Joe Franey. Great community that remains involved and supportive of the students. Our school is made up of a community. Everyone is part of the bigger family that is MstM. Where in areas we fight like a family at times, we protect, support, and care for each other as a family. Our learning program is wonderful. I as a student applaud how hands on our staff is. They teach us as a whole but adjust for those who need it. We all understand things differently and when some grasp the subject better than others we help explain to those who don't. Our sports our wonderful as well. Tied for the national streak of games not lost we go to state for almost every sport. I personally recommend you add to our family. We welcome you with loving arms. Welcome home

column3: Great school in a wonderful little town. Every one knows you child and it's just a nice feeling. my kid is scared of the kids there and says they are bullies Moravia is a great school district to be in! The teachers and the school administration are very communicative and flexible! Moravia Central is a wonderful school district. I moved here in the 8th grade and became extremely ill with a rare disease. The students and teachers helped to raise money for me despite me not being here very long. It is in a small area and the principal and superintendent are very sociable and know every student by name.

column1: Brantley County High School is a wonderful school! My husband and I both graduated there ('72 and '74) and are parents of 4 children who are BCHS alumnni ('93, '96, '99 and '03), one of whom has recently returned to teach at BCHS. The staff there is caring and concerned about the students on every level. Although BC is not an affluent system, its resources are utilized to the best possible extent so that students will gain maximum benefit. My family and I are proud to be Heron alumni! Pitiful!! I am from Atlanta GA and my husband is from Tampa, FL. I knew the ideaology out here would be out dated, but this is beyond anything I would have ever imagined! I have been told by a science teacher that the system couldn't afford books, the Microsoft 2010 class has more students than computers, so they share and about 3/4 of them work. Bullying is rampid. new Principal every yr, my son is a 504 student, he is a Sophmore, they just realized he is in 504. What lil money is spent on them isn't on thier safety, being every time there is an out of town event, the buses break down. There is NO parent teacher communication, my son has been on 25 field trips or sporting events, not one time have they come in on time, nor have they called the parents to inform them of thier tardiness. Last yr the ROTC Captain lost a child, all us parents waited 4 hrs in the parking lot, before one of the teens texted back. When he did, he said they were told 20-25 minutes till they pulled in, another hr and a half later he texted and said they stopped to eat. There is a reason land is/was so cheap here, no one that isn't from this community would dare regress to this time warp.

column3: Teachers are great. They actually care about the students. Very high test scores, and the students care about academic excellence and athletic excellence. BHS teachers are amazing. The classes are tiered for the student's academic level, and the AP classes(Adv. Honor) are awesome for the college prep. All BPS grading system is through the website where parents and students could access from home. The only downside of the school is the building condition. The HS building is quite dated and much need of repair. Moreover, there is a pool project that is being delayed every year. Students and teachers are making the best out of the place, however, the town of Braintree should step up and make a better use of the tax money to improve this school. Im a student at BHS, I can tell you it is absolutely one of the worst school in the south shore. I’m not sure what the school does with it’s money but everything is outdated and gross. The bathroom is just plain out disgusting. They do not update anything! Just go down to the locker room and it looks like a third world country. Who’s ever in charge really needs to invest some money to the school, like get a paint job. Also the school is incredibly greedy. It cost me $15 to go to homecoming, yet there was nothing special about it. There was a DJ and a place where you can take your own picture but other than that there was really no need for that high price. The fact that you had to buy your water which cost a dollar and snacks which also cost shows how crazy it is. I’m just wondering where the money goes to, because I haven’t seen really any improvements. Another thing I want to point out is that the teachers are great, they are reallly supportive, and that’s what matters really. My last thing I want to say is that the school environment is terrible, coming from a household of 3 people who go to HS, we each have to reach the bus at 7am, that’s just ridiculous time, I mean we have a single bathroom, thus there’s little time to get ready and NO time to eat breakfast. Also there’s just no socialising, you have zero time to speak with freinds in school, you have a locker, yet the time between classes are like 5 minutes and ontop of that there’s a a lot of teachers who say that the bell doesn’t dismiss you, but teachers do, they also make up very stupid rules like you can only use the bathroom 3 times in the entire school year!! How do you expect me to get from class to locker then bathroom then go up a floor to another classroom, I mean it’s just plain out ridiculous and the school really needs to have a huge major change. I graduated from Braintree High in 2017, and I am happy to say that I had some of the best years of my life at this school. The school has prepared us so well to be successful in any field that we choose to approach, especially for the STEM field, which is what I am studying in college. The teachers are extremely supportive and are always willing to help when you are struggling with a subject. The guidance counselors were also very helpful in making the college application process so much easier than it could have been. It is alos super easy to get involved here and find the right people to hang out with, and as long as you mind your own business, all the other students here are usually pretty chill and you won't have to worry about bullying issues. My only criticism of this school would be that the physical building is kind of deteriorating (rats running amuck, hallways constantly being closed for asbestos treatment, lights sometimes don't work properly, etc.). Overall, great experience, and would definitely do it over in a heartbeat if I could. I graduated in 2011, and at the time I did not think much of the school one way or the other.. I was caught up in my little bubble of life. Looking back on the experience now, however, it was a wonderful school and I was given the opportunity to have a top notch education at a public school. AP classes were offered and allowed me to push my limits, plenty of clubs and extra-curricular activities were offered. The music program was a huge part of developing who I am today as a person. I was absolutely set up for success and surrounded by teachers that cared about their students.

column1: I think NPHS is great for the Kids. The activities are awsome. The classes and teachers are impressive especially the music teacher. I only see one problem and that is the dress of some of the boys. The pants pulled down exposing the underwear is both unacceptable and a problem should the need to run out of the school in an emergency arise. I hope this is addressed. I think North Plainfield Middle/High School is an exellent school because of the caring staff. The staff helps students with problems with their skills or any other conflicts. Another reason I think good about the school is the activities like sport, clubs, etc. that the school offers. North Plainfield High School Is a great school for kids who do not hv a place to fit in. This high school doesn't discriminate and there is a place for everyone. I love this school and the teachers make the place even better. Even though we do not have a lot we make do of what we do have. This school is just horrible. The staff are the 2 stars this school gets. I found out that the honors books were used in the Somerset 6 School around the corner from this school. This shows that the students are at a 5-6th grade level. The honors math class is alright. They teach Algebra 1 in 8th grade, but I learned that in 6th grade. This is not a great school to go to, I recommend going to Rutgers Prep or the Watchung Hills High School. The school is deteriorating because the teachers have lost hope in the students. There are many students coming from towns such as Plainfield and Newark, which is bringing the school down. Test scores are simply dismal and most students do not go to 4-year colleges anymore(most go to RVCC). Many students are taking classes such as Biology or Algebra a year or two later than they should. The only students getting an okay education are those in Honors/AP. PS More APs and better academic programs would improve it. I find the school and staff to be just ok. I do not feel the staff go above and beyond for the students and do not provide additional information for the kids to advance unless they are asked. As parents we MUST make our presence known to the teachers, guidance counselors and principals via in-person, telephone and/or email in order for our children to get ahead, that may be one of the reasons my son is an honors student. NPHS is a very underestimated high school. The teachers there help every students with their needs and obstacles. Overall NPHS is a great school. NPHS is a great school to learn and the teachers are a great help Meh. Students are possibly the worst part, as one would expect. Administration is decent. We clashed a few times due to misunderstandings, but administrators are generally understanding. If you aren't in an AP/Honors class, you're wasting your time. I'd even go as far as to say that AP classes provide the best education, never mind certain Honors classes. I went to NPHS during its hey-day in the late 80s graduating in 1990. Teachers, students, administration were all at the top of their game. The Canucks were winning championships, theater won state championships (under the direction of the late Tom Lanno), arts were flourishing. The school and frankly the town, was a force to be reckoned with. It was an amazing education and I had an amazing experience.Then in a VERY short period of time, it all evaporated. Fights were a daily occurrence. Police were stationed at the doors (and this was in the early 90s when this was very uncommon). Plainfield and Newark students were infiltrating. Demographics of the town eroded. I'm not surprised to see the overall scores & other reviews. So sad. Hopefully one day the normals who care will retake the town and school.....
