column3: It is a large school, but they wisely divide the population into 5 "Houses" so it is like five schools under one roof, allowing for more academic offerings and exploration of interests, teams and clubs, and more and better facilities. Students are eased in gently, expectations are laid out, then everyone is up and running. Guidance, leadership, and academics are excellent. Socioeconomic diversity prepares students well for the real world. Avoid this school. They don't care if your child is bullied. They will do NOTHING except collect their paycheck and ignore the children. If you love your daughter or son, avoid this school. I am rating the school 4 stars. IF your child is a self-starter and socially adept, they will find a pre-collegiate experience here. Open periods allow for study groups or goofing off, whichever is the behavior pattern of your child. Strong academics, charitable organizations, civic groups, etc... However the school counselors are very young and lethargic. Don't expect to find the help you need in navigating social or academic challenges. You are on your own. This school is a amazing place, and my daughter really enjoys it. She always get 100% quality education every day. Too many students in this school, many of whom do not respect their teachers. Bullying is out of control and the teachers and administration do nothing to stop it. The school is very good at sweeping student issues under the rug. Very disappointed and cannot wait to get my child out of the district at the end of this school year. When you have replacements or new teachers, there should be some vetting process as the quality of education from the aforementioned individuals is lacking. Good, it's definitely different than the typical American high school, in a good way. Amazing! The teachers are smart, and passionate about what they do. Exceptional. I learned more from my education at Greenwich High School than I did at four year college. The caliber of teaching was high and the lessons were relevant. Parent: first in person visit with two transferring students from California we were offered a course guide as thick as your thumb sideways. As a kid on sabbatical from schooling overseas I passed the entrance exam for The Bronx High School of Science from IS141 in Queens, big fan of public education; GHS is easily a school that could be identified as a national standard school!1. Vibrant orchestra program and new $40 million hall2 7 sports fields (literally dozens of extra curricular sports activities; a public school that has a Fencing Club)Raising the bar for already well prepared students is one thing, even then guiding a student to an inexpensive Ebola Test and the “Google Prize” should be and easy marker; here though it seems that there are no “bad results”.Anyway, on the comment about too much “societal difference education”, can say that we sent two kids through this school and the only reminders - of the world we were in - was the truck we’d see on drop off with offensive stickers, every town has them. Surprisingly homophobic on pride month, multiple kids saying deplorable things and laughing. Would not recommend attending for any diversity reasons. Minus points for friend being pushed down a flight of stairs and not giving friends the accessibility they need to learn

column1: My husband is a para educator at this school and loves his job. How refreshing to have him come home happy and not all stressed out. The kids for graduation all have to do 80 hours of community service. What this does is give these kids a great sense of success in their personal lives as well as give our community a chance to know there young folks. I hope this school wins they deserve it. Perhaps students access to technology and updating classrooms. The respect I see from teacher to students and students to teachers is tremendous. Great leadership by the principal and staff. Small class sizes and welcoming atmosphere. Moving Forward is their motto and it shows in the student's work and accomplishments. The leadership is amazing at this school. They have not only persevered through the COVID class changes, but actually excelled. We are very pleased with Lake Region Union High School.

column3: Bastrop High School is not at all a good school. The administration is utterly incompetent, most of the teachers have no real enthusiasm (There are several, that is to say <7orso really great teachers who put up with this for some reason). The counselors, or at least mine, were much worse even that the administration. The career center was very limited in it's usefulness. Students there are, for the most part, closed-minded and have little will to participate in an academic environment. The school's clubs/organizations are not top-notch at all, and they are starting to disappear as well. If you send your child to this school I highly recommend trying to reach out into extra-curriculars and outside studying because almost nothing in this school is going to put your child in their/your university of choice. There are, though, several very excellent teachers. Most are terrible though. I've been taught by some teachers here who really don't care at all. And why should the students care if the teachers don't. I think that everyone should know that Bastrop High School provides a safe learning environment for students. BHS gives students ample opportunities to participate in extra-curricular activities. The school clubs are active and strive to create an authentic student interest in the club and community. As the school has a lower student enrollment (due to an additional high school in the district recently) I believe there will be opportunities to grow in areas other than enrollment numbers. There is an opportunity to create a great high school. awesome! Our administrators, teachers and students are working hard to raise the bar on academic achievement and college preparedness. In 2013 we were named a School of Academic Distinction by state of Texas. We are determined to match or beat that rating again this year. We have college professors teaching Early College Start classes on campus who ask to return year after year because our students are engaged, polite and active in class. We invite anyone to walk onto our campus and feel the school spirit that fills our halls. I have been very pleased with Bastrop High School. I have three children that graduated from BHS. The education they received has allowed them to pursue their goals at major universities here in Texas. Two of my children have earned their Bachelors and landed wonderful jobs in cities of their choice. In a month, the third will earn an MBA. I have worked at BHS for over 20 years and have seen many changes. Currently we are an innovative, college and career driven, public high school with a very hard-working, caring staff. There are many opportunities for students to be involved and participate if they so choose. Please read this if your children will be transferring from another state. This is not the school you want your children to go to. If your child takes the regular classes, not very many teachers are dedicated to bastrop high and will not go the lengths they should. If they are an AP student, the classes are not rigorous enough. I can count on one hand the amount of good teachers I've had, and I've had about 20 teachers during my time here. Also, if you have a student much smarter than belongs in the district, the school will lack in effort to supplement your child's needs, trying to shove them in whatever class they think is best and taking weeks to get back to parents. If your child struggles in school, the teachers will not exceed anything past what they are paid for to help, your child will struggle more. For children that are leaders and are not affected by others behavior, this school will cause unnecessary stress, and if they are a follower, there are way too many behavior issues (drugs, smoking, being disrespectful, and immaturity) that will most likely bid the worst traits for your child. The school had no idea how to communicate with parents or students unless they want money. A great sum of school funding goes to sports, while other programs barely have a large enough budget for one semester. This school is notorious for its high pregnancy rate, and is a closed campus because the kids act outrageously and cannot be trusted to leave. Their academic standards for what they believe makes a good classroom is based on saying the same routine everyday that does not work and having kids without phones, when it should require so much more. Some teachers don't even pay attention to students, when you ask them questions they give you totally unrelated answers. There are shattered windows everywhere from students with anger problems. I am suprised this is a school for the average Public and not for delinquents. I hope you consider relocating to a nearby town if you are moving for a job. If you must live in bastrop, I am very sorry ahead of time how much bhs will dissapointed you. I have sadly attended Bastrop high school for 4 years now, and I am sorry if you are planning to enroll your child at this school. Walking down the halls of Bastrop High you can see the leaking roofs and broken windows throughout. Your lucky if you enter a restroom that does not have some sort of malfunction or vandalism in it. However the integrity of the school is not all that matters because the staff should be the most critical, yet Bastrop High school fails to deliver on this also. Besides the few teachers who actually enjoy to do there job and do it correct the rest of the teachers seem to rather move, or quite when dealing with the plague of stupidity that travels in the school. Teachers being fired for soliciting drugs or teachers quitting due to not enough pay is common. Another thing that is common is the good old gas leaks or drug test, which seem to be the only thing reliable at Bastrop

column1: I have 2 children, one attends Francis Elem. and the other is attending Byng Jr. High. We are very blessed that our two children get the opportunity to attend the Byng School Systems. We are pleased as parents that we can count on Francis and Byng to strive for academic leadership and still create an awesome athletic program system. Great Job Byng!

column3: Douglas County High School is no place for a teenager to grow and learn. I am a junior attending DC and quite frankly, its a pathetic excuse of a community. None of the teachers care about you, neither academically nor personally. And the administration is the worst. For the sake of your child and his/her safety and well being, do not send your kid here. There is a disgusting, growing epidemic of drug abuse, lack of respect, and absolutely no support for the students. Nobody cares. No spirit. No love. They think they're some big "family" and it's literally a big joke. This school has hit rock bottom. They just won't admit it. There are too many students, and too many teachers and administrators that don't care. They ignore the fact that they're students are dying and failing and giving up. Everybody needs someone to depend on. And we'd like to believe that many students could find that support at school. But it's not here. This school is messed up on so many levels. My parents would rather me attend DC Oaks. DCHS is a pathetic excuse of a high school. Great Schools should post parents reviews together and student reviews in a different place. As a parent of a senior attending DCHS, I could not be happier with the administration and teachers. As a former teacher myself, I can distinguish a good teach from a not-so-good teacher. My daughter has been successful in athletics, academics and music at DCHS. There is a sense of tradition that you cannot get anywhere else! She has grown at this school and is ready to attend a top ranked university. This would not have been possible without the teachers, counselors, coaches, and administration of Douglas County High School. Kuddos Mr. Kappas for running such a wonderful school! This school is by far better than CV. I have been to both. I lasted until Winter Break at CV my Freshman year before transferring to DC. I am now a Junior. CV's academics and teachers are horrible. Don't send your child to CV if you want them to succeed in life. Go Huskies!! After one year at this high school, I believe there is an extreme amount of room for improvement. The staff and and administration are very unhelpful most of the time, and the classes are exceptionally easy. This school's main focus is on it's athletics, not it's academics. The students at this school harass each other constantly. This school is going down hill quickly. Compared to various other schools, Douglas County has a massive drug issue that should really be addressed. Students will smoke in "the alley" and the staff is aware but chooses to do nothing about it. No body at this school cares about the well-being of each other, and instead try to determine ways to be even more nasty to each other. I am not saying Castle View High School is better, but parents need to look into other options for high school if their main concern is academics and and the over health of their child. My two kids went to this school and we lived by the rock. My daughter took some IB classes and received a scholarship and graduated from CSU last year. My son is in the Air Force. There is plenty of involvement for parents if they want to get involved. I was involved in DCHS Band and the After Prom Parties. This school has world class Learning, sports, and activities. The teachers are superb and the school, while not fancy and shiny new, is a nice large school with plenty of room for everything. I'm very pleased my children are there, and I'm very happy with the education they are receiving. Most of the teachers do very little in the classroom (there are a few exceptions who actually care and do their jobs). The IB program is a joke, with teachers put in classrooms they have no experience teaching and/or are outside of their educational training. Sports and extracurricular activities are overpriced and underperforming. The leadership is apathetic and unprofessional. I've had 3 children cheated out of an education and regret the decision to send them there. We won't make the same mistake with our 4th. I have been a student in this school nearly my entire high school experience and I can full heartedly say that this is the worst school I have ever attended. The teaching at this school is a joke and none of the teachers actually care about you academically or emotionally. Needless to say, I am extremely excited to be moving soon and starting at a new school my senior year. I have some history with Douglas County (DC) Schools, in fact I garudated from Douglas County HS in 1983 (yes I'm an older parent...). First, the county is very affluent and fairly entitled. If you look at the news the school administrator and Board are primarily interested in getting a voucher system and privatize schools their highest agenda. Teachers are leaving in droves and many of the ones staying just don't care. Forward to the school. Sports are not well funded and the football program is abominable. At the beginning of the season you hear the usual 'we are here for the kids and making them into young men' drivel. But as you watch them, they don't care anymore about being successful. On the freshman team, all but one hang around an BS on the sideline, barely watching the game. At the last home game, DC parents were loudly mocking the coaches and rooting for the opposing team who thrashed us. Academically? At the beginning of the semester that had far more students show up than they planned for and moved kids. My son got moved into another Spanish class without being asked and missed a test that had been given before he was even there. It shows up as an F and neither the teacher nor administration even cares. Multiple attempts at asking are ignored. DC is simply a model of business people trying to move away from public schools and while doing so have no concern about the students currently in the system. Check out the news and this information will be validated by some research. School District handbook states they have a no bullying policy. This is not accurate. Teachers ignore bullying. My son was a constant target of bullies, and when he finally reacted he was suspended for 2 days, but the bullies only had to write an apology letter. This district lacks the support to for diversity and educating the teacher's about how to handle bullying Very positive overall experience. I have students that have excelled and gone on to university with full scholarships. They could do better with the sports program—we have talent and have been sadly handicapped by a poor football coach and thus limiting great opportunities for those players. Academically, I’ve been very pleased. Socially, you’ll get all types of students there, but that is true everywhere. I believe you getboit if it what you put into it and there is opportunity to do very well here. If I had to go back and decide between DCHS and CVHS (the other high school in town) I still firmly believe my students have received a better education than they would have there. very racist and using bashful words to put people down

column1: The staff here genuinely cares about the students. I have had all three of my children go through this school system and I can't think of a better place for them to have gone to school. We are very happy with the small class sizes and the level of individual attention. The teachers really take the time to get to know students and present the curriculum in a way that will get them excited about the topic. In addition to strong academics, the school promotes a culture that is positive and kind. They have a no cut policy for their athletic and arts programs which allows any student to participate. There is a high level of student and parental involvement which translates into a very connected school community.Last year’s graduates were awarded more than $19 million in scholarships, which averages to $206,000 per student. St. Joseph’s students graduate well prepared for college and life.

column3: We have had two children who both attended CHS, one graduated with honors the other did not feel safe after the first year after being solicited and then threatened by another student. I do appreciate the responsiveness of the admin. and the full-time security officers. Since there is a very high teacher turnover at CHS (about 30% each year), our second child was not able to get the same great teachers that our first child recommended. Sadly, those teachers were simply not at CHS four years later. Because the guidance counselors were all new and unfamiliar with the teaching style of the new teachers, they could not recommend a good fit for our intelligent underachieving child. CHS is the only public High School in Charlottesville there is no other choice. We are thankful we could afford a private tutor for our oldest child. A personal connection with an experienced teacher, who feels secure in keeping their job from one year to the next, would help to create better students than a personal computer for each student and a smart-board in each classroom. CHS may be a great public high school choice for gifted self-motivated honors students. There are plenty of those students there. They are mostly white and wealthy. CHS has a larger population of culturally and economically diverse students who seem to be a challenge to serve. The principal has been there for two years. She is the leader and does not accept the role of a team player. She does not return phone calls to parents or respond to emails. Access to her is closely guarded by her personal assistant who will go to great lengths including intimidation to discourage access. If you are an all honors student and will not need access to the authorities it may be a great choice. If not, then your student will be in classes with a diverse population who handle the stresses of a chaotic environment in different ways. Teachers may be willing to make a role model out of your student and will have the support and freedom from the principal to do so. If a student or parent ends up needing the help of the principal, you will not get it. The administration has adopted her style. Some teachers are not naturals in their roles but some teachers at CHS are truly excellent. Former student at CHS,my children briefly attended CHS before we moved out of the state.I agree with the post below that CHS is a great school for the gifted,and academically inclined, who are actively advocated for by their parent's and educators.However,I think CHS has a long history of failing the average to below average student. These kids are placed in class rooms that are more crowded than the honors classes and can be chaotic as a result. CHS seems to have no ability or motivation to engage the average to below average student to strive for higher academic achievement.Staff development along these lines is lacking and has been so for sometime.These kids are essentially being housed,and are required to do the bare minimum to meet graduation requirements.The racial and economic divide that exist between the honor programs kids and the lower performing students is still quite obvious.It's sink or swim for the average to below average student at CHS. It's a public school, if they do not have outside support advocating and pushing for them to excel they likely will not,because they are certainly not getting that support from teachers and administrators. CHS sends more students to the Ivy Leagues than any school in the area. It is an outstanding school for the highly academic, college-bound and grade-driven student. Its like a prison, takes a toll on mental health.

column1: Great dual enrollment program where students can leave high school already a sophomore in college. Athletics is unmatched in the area with facilities, coaching, and participation. Every student having a Chromebook next year will set this school apart from all the rest preparing students for jobs of the future. CHS prepared me for college and my career as a teacher. I am lucky to have had some of the amazing members of the faculty who still teach at CHS. Teachers work hard to help students succeed and grow into real people who thrive in the real world. Great rapport with Teachers, Administrators and Students.Great atmosphere to work in.Tremendous support from Principals, Staff and parents. This school had a lot of favoritism and allowed the athletes to wear short shorts but wrote me up for wearing capris. My future kids will not attend this awful district. I was bullied by a girl and coach stamp did nothing about it. Good high school alway be the red davil Bullies, mainly principal. Guns at football games. Phenix City Schools are horrible. I had to take my son out. Run.

column3: as a parent of a senior. I am very disappointed at the Cap Advisor and her lack of interaction with the students. I try to contact her all the time and she never returns my calls. I think the teachers in this school should be focused more on the kids more. This school needs inprovement. The teachers work very hard at this school. If your child is motivated they will do just fine. amazing the school is great and the kids sure do love it. teachers work hard and administration is very involved! Nice staff. Actually above standard academics all things considered. Education is good but office staff needs improvement . The Office needs major improvement, they can be extremely rude to students and most of the times refuse to help them and later get upset and complain to each other when students bring their parents in to help them get the help they couldn't get on their own. Some teachers do not teach at all and it feels like a waste of an hour when you get to their class. I would say a five plus... over all.... This school is an "A-rated" school and is now ALL magnet. It is not a feeder school anymore. Your child must apply and be accepted. It has a safe learning environment in a safe neighborhood. Nice student body and great teachers. I have no complaints.

column1: This school is terrible. The academy principle is awful he assumes on what he sees and you know what happens when you assume, also he is barely at school. There is only one or two cool teachers that care about the students. The teachers care about the money not the kids. I only sent my son there for one year and would advise anyone not to send their child there. The worst $10,000 I have ever spent. As a parent responbility in sending my son to a better, more enriched catholic high school providing a excellent and qualified education. This school has an intention to be caring more about the money than the education and to the gentleman itself. The tuition is increasing annually from year to year, for example, from 2009 to 2012, there was an annual forecast increase of 4-5% (about $500 more than the previous years ahead). After paying more and more money to go St. John's. As of late 2011 they sponsor an iPad program that helps with academic purposes and storing textbooks, but it hindered the students as they played games, used social networks, and continued to use hard copy textbooks not on the iPads. My son knows the fact that iPads in St. John's is necessarily a way to intimidate or deceivingly send inappropriate information to others or go off task in specific info. I don't recommend St. John's Jesuit High School and Academy to anyone for its expense of money, loss of foundation, and undesirable care (Ex. My son bullied in house group). It is a terrible school to go unless you want to pay more money for the school or to become uneducated. This school is not a good school. Longer school hours and days than last year. It has very hard courses, teachers don't describe the concepts well, very uneducated staffers in the A+ learning center that lead to student failures. House group is awful. Student bullying and harassment even if student does not do anything wrong. Food fights in cafeteria. Hallway jams overcrowded. No ethical sportsmanship. Other bad as described. Looking forward to going St. Francis next year. I did not know that St. John's Jesuit High School and Academy was a Roman Catholic school, also not many people in school are catholic, they should not allow the non catholic students to attend churches, yet they are still letting everyone going to church. To be very honest, the instructors at the theology department are very evil, completing at least 45 hours of community service for underclassmen and getting a senior project at upperclassmen. They should waive the senior project and the service hours spent. In addition, their school ACT is below 6-7 other schools. How disappointing! I wanted to return to school but the school days are long because they started early at the beginning and ended very late for the 2013-2014 school year. They should reduce the number of school days so the students can get good scores on homework, quizzes, tests, projects, etc. Otherwise I will leave that nasty school. Thank you! The school is not recommended because it lets you give most of you money away to the SJJ community or Christian service departments. St. Johns is a wonderful school. Academically excellent. The staff in the academy is excellent and the Principle is kind and very caring. As I read some of the reviews here I wondered what school they were talking about! Academic challenge is good for your brain. Yes, it is a financial strain but remember this, there is only one thing you can give your children that cannot be stolen, cannot be broken, and that is their education. I would love to see more Catholic orthodoxy. It used to be that Catholic schools were clearly Catholic. Parents understood that if you sent your child to a Catholic school they would get a Catholic education. Non Catholic families that sent their children to Catholic schools made that choice knowing their children would be exposed the Catholic faith in books, classes, stories, church, prayer, and they had no problem with that. Now, Catholic schools water down the Catholicsim =( If I sent my child to a Jewish/Muslim/Baptist/Greek orthodox I would expect them to be exposed to those faiths. How could you not know a school was Catholic when it was named SAINT Johns =) Good school, good staff, good place to be a young man. I have two sons attending St. John's Jesuit. My opinion of this schools academics, spiritual culture, teaching staff and administration is nothing short of outstanding. I could not be more pleased with the education provided at SJJ. My son went their for 4 --after four years , knowing what I know about SJJ I wish I would of just keep him in Anthony Wayne , Awesome school caring I don't know why parents complain it's honestly been great to me and my family yes I understand the money is an issue besides that it's awesome Saint John's does teach a few good values, making it really feel like a brotherhood, and one could thrive very well here... depending on what teachers you have. Every year they hire in sub-par, brand new teachers. Most of whom, are not very good at their job. Which I'm not knocking the teachers, but a private high-school with tuition like SJJ's - You would think they would be able to find more capable employees. During my Junior year English class alone, we had four different teachers. The few who have been teaching there for awhile happen to be magnificent teachers. Even they complain about the dysfunctional administration, and overall disorganization of how the school runs. While I've met some great people here, I would recommend a public school over saint John's. Or a school who doesn't set up flat screens, and ping pong tables for the single week 8th graders happen to visit. It is not all fun and games, and this school's education is not worth the tuition. I was very happy with my experience at St. John's Jesuit. The education of the whole person is unparalleled in the Toledo area, from the academics and athletics to the fine arts and Christian service. SJJ is truly a brotherhood, where everybody is cared for and supported, no matter what your interests are. St. John's is truly focused on a Christ based education, educating the boys on what it means to be Men for Others. The graduates of St. John's will be the next leaders of our communities and businesses. My son has grown academically, spiritually and athletically by attending St. Johns Jesuit. The school promotes leadership helps develop critical thinking skills and offers some of the best college preparatory curriculum in the area. My son has truly grown and matured into A Man for Others. I sent my three sons here! Academy and high school are second to none! Compared to friends at our local high school it was much more effective for college prep., develops good study habits for college bound kids. Diversity. Core Values. Excellent! We are now looking at colleges and the help with this process is more than what I expected. SJJ is worth the money! SJJ has been great at helping my sons challenge themselves to be a leader while showing compassion towards those of lesser means. Excellent. Saint John provides an amazing environment for students to learn and serve their community. Our son loves SJJ and so do we. His grades are great and SJJ has taught him how to manage his own work load along with playing sports and doing service. We couldn't be happier that we chose Saint John's for our son.

column3: The principal at Overhills HS is racest. When a white student defends himshelf he is suspended. Why is that/ My daughter was starting her first year of High School not knowing anyone. She came home from the first day of school saying she loved this place! The principle is retired military and has a great relationship with the students. He gives them a little more freedom with cell phones and ipods than any school I've ever seen. They say it's to teach them responsibility and prepare them for the real world. They are not allowed in class and because they have this privilege, most don't abuse it. The class schedules are different than most High Schools. I feel that it's set up more like college with only 4 class periods a semester. The teachers are great and work with the students on bombed assignments or tests. I do have some concerns with drugs but I know that's going to be at any school, and don't know how it compares to the other schools. I do feel that she's in great hands when she walks through the door and that's my main priority! I am very disapointed in this school I have 2 daughters that graduated from other schools in different states and this place is thebiggest disapointed .Counselors are not on the same page, teachers do not comunicate with the parents the open house was a huge mess information was not handed to parents, people were running from room to room ,coaches and some teachers at this school do whatever they like and the principal does not even know what they are doing they are not offering try outs for kids that did not transfer in time ......the school is not at all a place that prepares the children for a future or for collage I wish I would have known this my daughter would never came to this school military children in this place are diregarded and the interstate compact is not followed unless the parents are educated about it ahead of the game The school is overpopulated has a very negative atmosphere. if any student says they love this place they are either specail one way or another or they are involved and hiding somthing. As a former and recent student id reccomend other choices first. Keep a close eye on your Student/Kids. School is over populated school seems to put a front that they care and make excuses when something happens. A lot of inappropriate kids and nothing is being done. I have 2 students in OHS and they absolutely love it !!!!! They came from another Harnett Co school and they love it here. The atmosphere is great. Students are friendly, JV went 10-0 in football and varsity made the play-offs. The education that they are receiving is great. The school has been a school of distinction for the past several years. I would not send my children anywhere else. Hands down the best in Harnett CO. Overhills High is a wonderful school. So much effort goes into helping student succeed through after school tutoring, Saturday academy for those with attendance issues, and an opportunity for any student to retake a teacher-made test to improve their grade. Those who speak negatively about the school are just plain uninformed. I love this school! I have two sons that attend Overhills and they are doing amazing! I counselors are great! Anytime I have a question I can just call or email and I get a response back that day. I feel like like they always have an open door policy for parents with any questions or concerns. We moved to this area for this high school because they have the highest test scores in the county and I am thankful we did! My son has went to Overhills High for two years and he likes it. He is in Honors science and doing well in all classes. The kids at the school seem to be accepting of all kids. The teachers email me with progress and the office staff is friendly. This school now has a very strong principal and is turning this school into a A+ rating. My personal issue in the past with this school was the communication between principals/teachers/staff to parents. There was little to none. Now, you can rest assured that this new principal is very involved with the students as well as the parents. Communication is outstanding from conferences to email and telephonic notifications as well as the Parent Assist Program where a parent can track their childs academic progress on a daily basis online. i dont like this school. its very overcrowded and theres alot of bullying, drugs, and fights that go on. i think the teachers dont care about the students, although there are a few good ones, and the prinicpal smiles in your face while knowing the problem wont be fixed. my children have gone to other harnett county schools and have had no problems. they were bullied as soon as they got here and nothing was done until my son stood up for himself and he was the one punished. this is the worst school ive ever seen The school of which I am attending can be quite horrendous at times. While I can say that it certainly does have more choices than the school I was previously going to attend, the communication between parents, staff, as well as students in question is lacking at best. Most times, I'm not even aware of days when there isn't school until the day before. Also, my parents were not made aware of when I was to pick classes for my next school year, and neither was I until the day I was scheduled to do so. The teachers are pretty nice, but some seem to be lacking in being aware of their students, and their different needs for learning and such. And as for the behaviour of my peers, it is very obvious that their behaviour leaves much to be desired, some actions even going unnoticed. Overhills Highschool is kinda hard to describe, because depending on what classes you take and what teachers you have, it makes entirely different experiences. I personally take all Honors classes, and I'm also taking French, and an elective called AVID. My experience in 3 out of 4 of my classes is generally average. My French and AVID teachers are awesome, and despite the huge amount of work, English is okay too. My overall issue with this school is: 1.) The Work- The school is very tech-oriented, so bad computer test takers scores will go down, also for homework, many of the teachers make you print off your work at home. 2.) The Students- Some of the students here are the most rowdy, annoying things ever. However if you take Honors and AP classes, you will likely avoid them. So depending on your schedule can determine your interaction with these particular students. Most(emphasize that word) of the teachers are really great at their job, and naturally I won't name names. The environment is very clean, one of the cleanest in the county, however some days the bathrooms are particularly grungy, but not too much. The principal is great, way better than the old one thats for sure. This school needs a lot of improvement in my opinion. The school being overcrowded is one thing that really annoys me. This year, being a sophomore I can definitely say that last year was much better, in terms of the amount of people. Less people in the hall meant getting to class faster, and less hassle to try and squeeze through people in the hall. The school also needs work on informing students on what's going on. Most times the only way I know of something happening is through other students. The fighting has to stop. It's a little more under control this year, but fights still happen. I also feel like other sports, besides football, should be noticed and appreciated. It seems like no one is ever alerted of any upcoming events with any other sports besides football. I do have to say though that the principal is trying his hardest. I really do believe he is trying to make this school better, but with some of these students it can make his job pretty hard. There are some very excellent teachers at this school, but then others... they just don't get it. They don't take control of their students... or really understand how to help the information stick. We are a military family and we picked Overhills over other high schools after doing some research before we moved here. I have had two children graduate from Overhills and have two that are currently attending. They all love Overhills. We have had no complaints. My children fit right in. They have liked their teachers. I will say that the principal that they have now is a much better improvement over who was here three years ago. It is a great school some teacher are great some really are not I had teachers that have been bad and did not care but that typical at any school my main conplaint is over crowding 5 min between classes I have to shove thought the halls to get to class I love ohs but with people stopping in the hall. It hard to get though the hall to got to classes But it hard for some students to get there on time with there class on the other side of the school and lunch to many people in the cafeteria slow lines the main problems are the crowed no order in halls not many staff in commons super vising. Students and need more staff controlling crowds OHS is an excellent school under Dr. Middleton's direction. He has done a great job there. this school was great for my son. I turned in his IEP during the summer and as soon as school started I get a call from his diagnostician to set up a meeting with me. Like every school there are kids who fight, has troublemakers, etc but my son knew to stay away from all that. I can honestly say that this was a wonderful school and very helpful. Great place to send your high school kids. I have 2 kids attending this school and 2 more on their way. Through social media, they see their friends from other states enjoying pep rallies, spirit week, talent shows, dances, theater productions, and many clubs/activities/events....along with getting a wonderful education from teachers that seem to really care. When my dtr asked for a recommendation letter from a teacher when she was nominated for governor's school, the teacher had her turn around and look at a table full of papers and was told that she simply didn't have time. How discouraging! The kids need to feel connected to the school. They want to have pride in their school. They want to be involved and have the opportunity to grow with their peers inside and outside of the classroom. It shouldn't only happen during football season...there should be opportunities throughout the year to make hs special. I'm not saying that students need to be entertained, but I feel like something needs to be done to promote school pride! Give the kids a voice...student council is a start! I know that I can't be the only parent that feels this way. They only get to do high school once! My son attended last year. No problems at all. Just hard to reach the front desk when needed. And be careful if you don't have insurance, and your kid plays sports, he got injured..... his bills were never taken care of by school insurance as promised. Harnett county is one of the WORST schools districts in NC ... I have 2 Children and Somehow every year after all of the progress reports say failing with 30's and 40's they manage to get 70's and 80's at the end of the year passing them along.... Also Best friends son is currently passing a class in 4th period with a 100% despite the fact he has early release for work after 3rd and has no 4th period????? Bullying runs rampant and unchecked, School board has no care in the world about anything with the schools, a bunch of old retiree age guys collecting checks for doing nothing is all they are.... STAY AWAY from this school district My son had a horrible experince at this school. School is overcrowded and they need to address the issues of bullying I just moved here fromGermany, and I must say that this is by far the best school I have ever attended! America has a truly amazing school system, and I wish I'd been given the opportunity to use it before 12th grade... My son is a Sophomore this year. His first year was good. He has always been a straight A student and nothing changed. He took advance classes his freshman year and was challenged. The only issue I had was that 2 out of 4 of his teachers were replaced half way through the year, affecting the class somewhat, but that’s out my control. When I asked him about the rumors I heard about fights and stuff, he shrugged and said that happens everywhere which is true. I thank God it didn’t affect him. I think success is based a lot on the child and what they put into their education. It’s nit all on the teachers. I do feel some of his teachers gave busy work and too much of it sometimes. All my done did was homework and football practice. It kept him busy but may be too much for others. Overall, you get out what you put in and I put in a lot of prayers as well. They, we, all need it. ;)

column1: Pike county school systems are pathetic, teachers care nothing about your education only the amount of money on their pay checks teachers and administration have no respect for students at all. Bulling is a huge issue and the school system takes no action several kids have switched to homeschooling because of this problem. Sadly still nothing was done. The only help I've ever received was from the graduation coach. I would not recommend this school to anyone. No matter what their ratings are their work ethic is poor. Pike County High School what can I say, I have had 2 sons graduate from this school both went to college and 1 graduated from GA Tech along with 6 other kids from the same class year. There were also a total of 14 kid the class years before and after that went and graduated from GA Tech. My daughter is on track to go to college also, and she has been in Pike County schools from pre K forward. So many so the parents who have complaints about this school more than likely have children who could not keep up academically, and no my children were nothing special they just worked. Our children have went to Pike county schools since they were in Kindergarten and Second Grade. They are now in the 7th and 10th grade. We have had a wonderful experience and LOVE the schools! I feel like the teachers have challenged our children to strive for excellence. We love the small town feel of Pike county and that they have made friends that they have grown up with. Unfortunately this county doesn't provide a lot of funding for education. I have lived here my entire life and have been nothing but more and more disappointed in the people that have lived here forever. I know many of them personally and the facts are facts. If you want better education you have to have things in this county that goes towards taxes(education). It's sad to see many of these students who graduate and never go to college. If they do it's a technical school etc. Pike county is misleading in the fact that people think it's a great rural place to live and we keep the bad people away. The fact of the matter is people who want to do bad things come here just so they can not be noticed. Did you ever think about that? Unfortunately we will be moving away to a more safer and educated town for our children's sake. It's not the teachers or administrators who are at fault, it's the fact that we I've in a poor uneducated county. Knowledge is power. We offer zero educational activities for kids here as well as zero options for enrichment. As a teacher myself, I have found it incredibly frustrating to watch uneducated people dumb down their citizens because they are afraid of a certain type of person moving here. Look at successful communities similar to ours who have well rounded children and adults loving their community and watching out for each other. If you encourage families and put money into a community you will end up with a great community. As long as you keep a county poor, it will attract those who are drawn to poor counties and generally do things to "get by" or whatever is easy money to them. Instead of tearing each other down with negativity and wanting something for nothing, try building up your community to attract and keep the type of people you want living here. Pike county's reputation is pushing good people out and inviting bad people in. Clean up this county. Provide better (safer) areas for children to play. Do you know why we don't have better parks etc.? TAXES pay for those things. Most of this county doesn't even have internet because AT&T boycotts it. Do your research before moving here and see what schools with slightly higher taxes offer kids both educationally and socially. Your children will thank you one day. You don't know what your missing if you've never had it to begin with. So sad. :( This school district is great for any child. Everyone cares about each other. This school needs to be more strict on racism. There are teachers and student who say the n word and slurs to my daughter. She has came home crying into my arms once because people are animals. She has had a tough time with the amount of white people here and she can’t go a day without hearing them say a slur. The teachers hear but don’t act apon it. I have asked my daughter if she wanted to move, but the only other option is Griffin high, and that’s even worse. She does have good grades, and she’s been surprisingly succeeding in all of her classes, but the racist problem in this school needs to be fixed. I do not recommend for blacks.

column3: Richwoods has changed in the past few years with the closing of Woodruff High School. Student safety issues and rapid turnover in the administration has crippled teachers' ability to teach. My daughter graduated from the IB program last year and was lucky enough to land in an Ivy League college, but she was a hard driven student motivated to pursue educational excellence with or without a great school. If you have a good kid with an average amount of motivation, the discipline issues may prove very distracting. I would highly recommend looking outside of district 150 for a better school. Though Richwoods has several wonderful teachers and is lucky enough to offer the IB Program, the past few years the educational qualities have really been in decline. The school caters to the lower half of the population and devotes too much focus on the behavioral issues of the minority. The majority of the teachers either don't care or don't know what they're talking about. You're extremely lucky if you have one of the few who actually care! In addition, class weights are ridiculous. Enriched classes are weighted the same as AP and IB classes, which is like a slap in the face considering how difficult AP and IB classes are and how watered down and basic enriched classes are. Drugs, fighting, and drinking are rampant. There needs to be more of a focus on the AP and IB kids and less of a focus on the minority of trouble makers. In fact, there needs to be more of a focus on educational quality and less on the school parking lot and the school dress code. Though it is way better than other district schools and much better than the catholic high school, I would definitely recommend looking for a different high school. Richwoods is a very good school. I had some difficulties and the teachers were very helpful My son goes to Richwoods and it's the best high school in the city. Mrs. Emken does a great job as principal.

column1: Its like a big family in there.its a very live school. outside of school students stick together like a gang. hardly ever a fight going on in school because everybody is cool with each other. be prepared to see a whole lot of roaches, and some teachers that do not care. but if you manage to stick around and do the work teachers barely teach you how to do you WILL graduate with honors.i was in class high almost every morning and managed to have a 2.8 gpa. and playing sports a the t is a BIG BIG Plus you will get alot of people on your banwagon. Og Mike C. C/o 2011 This school is the worst high school I have ever been to! & that says alot as I have been to 5 different high schools. I am very involved in this school, I've played field hockey,&i run indoor track; I am in FBLA & many other clubs. My GPA is 3.8 & I'm a junior. I don't believe the teachers can be blamed for the low test scores of the school. I have seen my principal TWICE since I've arrived at BTW & many people don't even know what he looks like. I can describe this school as EXTREMELY ghetto & unorganized. There are fights often & the curriculum is very slow. It is in extreme danger of losing it's accreditation. If you are a parent looking to enroll your child, be prepared to be stressed out, especially if you're coming from out of district! The bathrooms are disgusting ALWAYS & there are roaches & rats. DO NOT PUT YOUR CHILD IN THIS SCHOOL!! Best school in the United States. My child loves this school because it's one of a kind, and have teachers that care about you more than anything, almost like your their own. Their NJROTC is also FANTASTIC. They are better than any of the other High Schools i've seen in a while, and I wish that other schools would catch up to the level Booker T. Is on. My child is also on the Varsity Basketball Team, enjoying every minute of it. She plans on joining the military after an attempt at Professional Basketball. But overall, Booker T. Washington is a great school. Any parent would be lucky to send their child their, no matter what rumors you may have heard about the school. I love the school, because it is part of my community, however it has a very poor level of accountability. It is set up so that those parents that wish to be involved are unable to contact administration or even get return phone calls. I think it would be a great school if top administration would show some accountability and instill accountability in the staff members. school has the best NJROTC program, and the band has always been very nice .. however... everything outside of that is just about terrible. Dropout rate is still the highest, plenty of bullying going around, Fights on a weekly basis. Lunch is terrible ....well thats universal for schools lol. as far as the learning goes, they have a few advance study classes, but the non-advance classes leave a lot to be desired. Bottom line, if your chile is not in an advance class, pull them out now, only due to the fact it seems the teachers are teaching a test, and not concepts. There are some who go above the cut of the rest, but definietly not enough to balence it out. School was previously labled a dropout factory, and they currently are in danger of losing accredation. Be Wary This school is rated as the worst high school in the state. The accreditation has been pulled too many times to count over the years due to their inability to control the students. Barbed wire around the perimeter says it all!! Just look below at the post from July 10, 2011. That should tell you a lot....and he signed it Og (Original Gangster) Mike C. Speaks milestones to this schools reputation. We moved here from new York, my daughter loves the school. The principal and teachers have showed great interest in helping her. She has made honor roll also has joined the volleyball team. I don't have any concerns.

column3: The teachers at Cape coral are highly qualified, however my daughter's geometry teacher was actually a chemistry teacher.She didn't know how to teach.She would never send home the results of tests,and you could never talk with her.Trying to help my daughter was difficult as the teacher never explained anything in class.Her way of grading can't be understood,in this I mean she could show favoritism to certain individual students.But you can't compare one bad teacher to all. Cape Coral High school was ok. The students there werent really friendly it was kinda hard finding new friends. Some of the teachers were good but others didnt really liked helping the students its like they wanted to pick a fight with us. The testing is confuseing and the way they have student counseling meetings for all students were hard because they didnt tell stusents when we had to meet. Over all its an ok school but i wasnt satsisfied. As far as high schools go in Lee County, it's pretty difficult to launch a complaint at Cape Coral High School. They have a great website and are well focused on preparing students for college, vocational programs, and life. Cape high has a major theft problem but according to the staff, that is all high schools. We are just over one month into the school year and have already had 2 items stolen during class! One when my child walked up to the teacher to turn in a paper, the other taken from a book bag! Of course nobody saw anything, impossible since it was during class, but "hey it happens everywhere" is the attitude given. Somehow that is not ok with me and defiantly not something to teach our children! I am very, very disappointed with the attitude among students and staff with regard to this behavior. It is a shame and very sad that they expect so little out of our students and not the way to teach children any type of decent, law-abiding futures! This school is horrible. I think this school should have cops every where its not safe or a good school at all. My daughter will not be going there next year and my son is switching out. If you want your student to skip class, party like rock stars and graduate with flying colors this is the place for you. They called my and told me my daughter had skipped 30-40 days. I told them to fail her. They ended up graduating her with honors. WHAT?? Apparently a work ethic is not something they want to install in their students. You don't want to go? no problem we'll still "pay" you with a degree! While attending Cape Coral High School, I was in the IB program. My years at this school were possibly the best of my life. Teachers were involved and dedicated to student success. Mr. McPhee, the principal at the time, offered a motivated, integrated approach to leading the school. Students were friendly and close to each other. The Varsity soccer team, in which I started, won a state championship my senior year. I now attend the University of Florida on a full scholarship. I credit my academic success to the Cape Coral High School IB program and the wonderful teachers and students that I shared my four years with. Do the opposite of what every guidance counselor and teacher at CCHS tells you to do and you will succeed in life. My son is very happy at this school! If I could give this school zero stars that's how I would rate the experience at this school. This school USE to be one of the best. Not any more.

column1: Horseshoe Bend is a SACS accredited school, which means that it DOES, in fact, offer many programs and courses to get our students ready for college. We could not have achieved SACS accreditation without offering quality programs and showing evidence of student success. Maybe you weren't ready for college for some other reason. Horseshoe Bend School is outstanding and it gets better everyday! I love the new webpage they are working on along with the facebook and Twitter notifications. They Principal and staff truly care about our students. I get personal time with the Principal and when he says he has an open door policy, he really means it. He is never to busy for any students! Blessed to have my children in this school. The principals there are the best you can find! You'll be on their good side as long as you stay out of trouble

column1: I currently attend GHS as a junior. I chose to come here, being from a neighboring town, and I think I made the best choice! We're not the best school in the state by any means academically, but you won't find a nicer bunch of people. The teachers are great, the students are friendly, and I have never felt uncomfortable or out of place. It feels like family. There are plenty of opportunities both in academics and activities, but you will have to search for them a bit. We have a bunch of different art and tech classes in a variety of disciplines (everything from CAD to sewing to chorus), and I've found all my academic classes engaging. You can also take classes with VHS. There aren't a lot of clubs, but you are likely to find something you like if you search. The one thing I don't really like is that all the clubs meet at the same time, during school on Fridays, and so it is difficult to join more than one. The school spirit here is almost palpable, especially around homecoming and the massive spring musical. My advice to those looking at GHS: -Actually read the Program of Studies. If you don't, you will miss out on a lot. -Just give us a try! We don't bite too much, promise.

column3: I love this school because it supports students and teachers! Violent school. Fights, weapons, drugs are all common occurrences. Two very busy full-time police officers on staff. The school has bullies with parents in the Administration, so little punishment from the school for atrocious acts. Though no gangs evident, school life resembles closer to gang or prison mentality than a disciplined, civilized atmosphere aimed at fostering education and growth. Mainstream kids doing all the activities that you would expect only to see in kids on the fringe. Several of the teachers seem to care, but way too many students and too many problems to have a positive effect on the majority of kids. Our kids love going to Tascosa High School! The teachers make a strong effort to connect with the students, and my children each have clicked with a teacher mentor who have helped guide them in decisions that are important for their current and future growth and success. Par excellence is the only way to describe their orchestra and band programs, which includes a wonderful Christmas dinner concert for families and friends that is highly entertaining and memorable. As far as academics, the teachers have pushed our kids to do their very best. We have appreciated the administration and staff's flexibility and help with the kids' schedules to ensure they are able to take all the courses they require for their future studies and college applications. Also, the Tascosa Rebel football team are #1 in the state this year! It is such a diverse student body, we have seen that most students find their people and place at THS.

column1: The PSSA and Rating of this school here mean nothing. This is a great school. Great teachers and great kids here. The stats are just part of conspiracy. I was a student in 96 and I love this school. My son now wants to attend the school. The diversity was the best. Saul needs new administration. Current administration is very unprofessional does not support the students, and is taking the quality of the school down. They do not want to work with parents for the betterment of the students and schools. Great school that went down hill over the past four years. This school is a challenge Educationally but the staff needs to support the students. Especially the students that are now Seniors, the class of 2013!!!! I will be there to make sure everything is fair and runs smoothly!!! Active patient participation is KEY!!! This school desperately needs new administration. A large number of kids enter this school doing well and getting good grades, but then prejudice and favoritism by the teachers and administration takes over and ruins these kids, The kids give up because no matter how hard they try to do well, if they don't fall into the right racial group or become one of the pets, their efforts will never be rewarded. The principal and especially the vice principal need to GO! This school has created more stress, depression, and discouragement than any other school I have encountered. If you have ethnic children and desire for their well-being to remain intact, do not send them here; you will regret it!! A great and special school for students who don’t want a typical high school experience. Where else can you go and plant flowers rider a horse, milk a cow and make homemade ice cream as classwork. I have one graduate from this school and another child currently attending Saul. It has been an excellent program for both of my children academically, athletically, and socially. They have both grown infant ways during their time at Saul and have earned the strong base they need to go on to college and beyond. I would highly recommend Saul to any interested family or student. Excellent!! My oldest graduated from Saul, and I have another son, graduating from, Saul this year!! I absolutely love the hands on learning the students recieve along with what's offered, in terms of Majors. My sons absolutely love. Saul! And so do I!! Outstanding. I am so happy with Saul. My daughter transferred from Central because it was too big and too intimidating for her. At first, I was nervous about her going to Saul and wanted her to be at a really academically challenging school. However, seeing how happy she is at Saul has made all the difference. And, she is taking AP English and Honors Chemistry. She has the perfect amount of challenge at this school. If you are looking for a truly holistic experience for your child, look no further than Saul. The Agricultural program is unique to high school experiences. Being able to interact with animals, plants, and new foods has done wonders for my child's overall mental health. The school is small enough that your child can pretty much "know" everyone. Saul families and alumni are wonderful. This school was excellent for my son, giving him opportunities in Agriculture he couldn't have gotten any where else.

I attend this school from freshman, I really try my best to study and work but the teacher make so hard for me to get a good grade. The teacher also don't allow their student to go to restroom even in emergency case. The teacher are pick on bad student and didn't care about good student. For award, always bad student receive not good students. Some teacher are so mean to their student just because something happen at home and she is in a bad moon. The sport is terrible. column1: I graduated from South Greene High School in 1966, the first year of its existence. Later, I served as Assistant Principal and Principal (1978). South Greene has always been a good school with many ready graduates. Ready for higher education or ready to join the work force. In all my years of association with South Greene, I have always felt that the very best teachers and coaches work at South Greene. Many are former honor students and athletes from South Greene. Luck may have played a part in these people having the opportunity to return to the school to work, but my guess is that these people were rewarded for accomplishment by being given a choice to return. I'm an alumni ('06) of South Greene High School, and have nothing but wonderful things to say about the school. The principal and assistant principal are outstanding, and the teachers are hands down the best in Greeneville/Greene County. I was always proud of what the school accomplished - academically and athletically - considering that Greeneville High School is the perceived "premiere" school in the region. The faculty, staff, and administrators will make sure each student is well prepared for either higher education or to participate in the workforce. The way the students and staff handled the stabbing incident was wonderful,they prevented any others from possibly being injured. They handled the situation. Thank you. Best school I've ever been to. Accepting of all types, caring staff, and great a principal. I have two grandsons attending now. One is an acedemic senior. The other is a football-basketball all star junior. Next year another grandson will be a freshman and three years later a granddaughter. It's a wonderful school.

column3: Amazing principal, terrific core academics with dedication to both AP classes and ELC. Love the band/music program. Feel like both my high-achieving kids got a stellar public education. Moorpark high school not only has an excellent academic program with caring teachers, but also has a band program that is truly magnificent. The Principal and Teachers are great! Always available to help before school, lunch and after school. The teachers motivate the kids to really help them reach their learning potential. We also have so many great programs and clubs for envolvement for everyone to have great school spirit. Moorpark high school has done wonders to students and its a pleasure my son is part of this academy. Good staff, but the classes are fairly large. The education feels brusque, and it's difficult to get motivated. I'm transferring to the high school at Moorpark College instead. However, if you're into the high school social aspects, it'll probably suit you better. Otherwise, you're in for four years you'll probably hate. This school is a wonderful school for all kinds of kids, my son in particular is shy, and he comes home everyday letting me know how nice the teachers are and the kids who go there. This is only our first year in this school and I hope all continues to go well. In a couple of years my daughter will also be attending this same school, mean while we will finish up in a private all girls school that just didn't work out as well as it should.

column1: This school has amazing teachers who care for their students. I attended this school and was having issues in a few classes and had so much help from the teachers. They went above and beyond to help me understand what I was doing. It is a little school but a good one!!
