column3: I graduated from Gal a few years back... I don't regret going here at all. Made some great friends and everyone just feels like family. Teachers here are amazing as well. Our sport teams kick total BUTT! Loved getting out at 1 on Tuesdays.. Off-campus lunch and we're located right by the pier... What more could you ask for??? GHOUUUUUUUUUSE! I am a student at Galileo! This high school is super amazing! It has a well caring teachers and they will help you in whatever the student struggles, there's many clubs to be part of, and even better if the student is "newcomer" it has their own club so the newcomers can be help in what they sturggle. There's many nice people around this high school, and you will make friends by fast . There's many programs for those students who doesn't feel appreciate for their appearances or considererantions of sexuality. Lost of joyful moments! I don't regret on coming here. Because there's always someone to help you ! Even if u want to Changelle yourselves. Our son graduated 2 years ago and is now a College Student at Colby. He thrived there. We were very impressed with the school. The teachers there are incredible, from his Spanish teacher Mr. Villar, Mrs. Wagner (best Literature teacher), to Mr. Barrios (Physics), Mr. Ring (Math), Mrs. Morrison (English). OMG, this is the best kept SF secret. Through the counseling our son had access to incredible opportunities, he got a scholarship to participate in the Outward Bound leadership program and Sierra Nevada camp trip. I encourage parents to consider this school. You won’t regret it. Excellent school. Welcoming community and nice folks. Definitely not worth going to Lowell. There's a lot of controversy and peer pressure during middle school about going to Lowell, and while I regretted not applying to the school in middle school, I can say with confidence that I am very happy I got into Galileo instead of Lowell. The teachers are nice, ASB is excellent, and the people are just kind overall. Former graduate here. PARENTS, stay away from this place.Bad Things:- Some of the student learning methods forced on students are questionable. They claim that these are ways used in college, but it is actually false. It's also unnecessary and stressful for high school students.- This school does not prepare you for college. Some of the school "college prep" programs are really useless and does not prepare you for college at all. Complete waste of time. PARENTS, Don't buy into their "college prep" nonsense. If you want to prepare your children for college / job, send them to a community college through the SFUSD dual enrollment program. It's far better than any "college prep" nonsense this school advocates for. - School admins were working against teachers for some odd reasons (prob internal disagreements). They like to play "games" with each other during work time.- Some classes listed as available are actually unavailable.- No job training and some classes stated are not actually there (the pathways do not prepare for jobs because you still need a college degree to work in certain fields, but the pathways are a really interesting learning tool)- Many high school level general education classes did not prepare for college level STEM based GE courses. If you are a HS student attending this school, I highly recommend attending a community college instead of going directly to a 4 year if you are going to be a STEM major student.Good Things:- convenience if you live near by. If you do not live in this area, I recommend somewhere else and staying away- skill based pathways (computer science, digital communication, biotech). These don't necessary prepare for college coursework, but they do teach study/work ethics and teamwork skills that you will need in college.

column1: In the beginning I struggled with Scecina but my son had some major emotional challenges and they were so very supportive. He has become more concerned with his academics, and even asked to return next year!! The administrators and staff have gone out of their way to make us feel welcomed. The rules are strict, the work is hard but its well worth it for my child. My son is happy at Scecina. He enjoys his courses and teachers very much. Instrumental Ensemble with Mr. Donnie Glowinski has been a fun learning experience for Spencer. Latin II and Chemistry are challenges that enable him to THRIVE...and he plans on taking Latin 3 his junior year. Theatre with Mr. Jones has been a new & positive experience as well. Meanwhile, during mass he is a Eucharistic Minister. Although, Spencer came from Holy Name (south deanery), he has be welcomed and made new friends rather easily. Scecina offers students of all different backgrounds the opportunity to succeed. They have a dedicated faculty and staff that have helped my child overcome some academic challenges. The small class sizes helped my child get the attention that he needs to be successful. It is a great change from our previous school experiences. Both my sons graduated from Scecina. One of my sons had learning difficulties and the staff and faculty worked very hard to prepare him for graduation and college. The staff and faculty are very attentive and responsive to parent needs and concerns. I have another child that will definitely attend Scecina when she is in high school.

column3: As a current student at Hanover Area I am able to say that this school is barely meeting the standards of what a public school should be meeting. First, as for the students, students in any sports teams have a higher priority than normal students. And as well, bullying is a large problem in Hanover, and the staff does next to nothing against it. As for the admin, some of them do nothing but try to intimidate students by yelling and threats of suspension and the magistrate instead of understanding what the problem is. One in particular seems to have no care of the students at all. The teachers are a 50/50 group. While many of the teachers are of great character and do their job well, many on the other hand do not, but I suppose that is like every school. However, our guidance staff is top of the line and do the best of their ability to attend to the needs of the students. The school has numerous sports to participate in as well as many clubs and similar after-school activities. However, the largest concern with Hanover is the debt. We are currently around thirty-six million in debt, and yet the school board refuses to show records of how this money was spent. clearly this school district is passed on polictics! you must know someone of hiigher staute for your children to recieve anything from this school district! I feel our children were clearly failed because we didnt know the higher powers in this school! I am so happy we moved out of there and put our children in a school district where they will be treated equally!!!! I am a former parent of this school district and proud of it! This school is horrible. They are more focused on their little football team than education. Most of the elementary school teachers are more worried with what you are wearing than actual learning. Not only that, their football team is terrible. I hate the school so much, there is excessive bullying, and the staff are unhelpful. For example, the pin number monitor. She just sits in her chair all day, texting! Very bad school, I would not recommend it! To be honest I went here for most of my life with an exception of moving around a little, but in my opinion this school was the utter most worst one I fulfilled in going too. The teachers are one of the biggest problems, yes there are some good ones but overall they have some of the worst teachers you can get. One of the teachers just sits there the whole class period while the kids talk even though he is supposed to be teaching a class. I think Hanover area needs to get there priorities straight before making bad decisions on the school teachers that they allow there. Honestly, this school is the best you're going to get around here. WAY better than Meyers, GAR, Nanticoke, Wyoming Valley West, etc. As long as you pay attention and are respectful, there's no issues. Sure, some teachers aren't good but there are teachers like that everywhere. This school isn't that bad. People just have one bad experience here and say the school is bad. News flash: every school has problems. Hanover is better than most schools around here.

column1: Not only am I a parent of two students at Simpson, but I also teach at Simpson. It is a wonderful school - not only academically, but socially. Administrators care about each child and knows them all by name. Teachers routinely go the extra mile to help struggling students. We have lived in many places - large cities and small towns, but we are STAYING at Simpson!

column3: I have lived in Waunakee for many years and have two children that have gone through the Waunakee schools. The high school has many top notch teachers and leaders. The curriculum is appropriately challenging. Here is my one complaint. The emphasis on football and sports made it very difficult for my non-athletic child to do well at this school. If your child feels, acts or looks in any way, 'different" from the mainstream students, or has mental health issues, this might not be the right school for him or her. The school pressures students to conform, heavily favors sports over academics, test scores over learning, and sweeps problems under the rug to make sure the school looks good on paper. Phenomenal. I had two students in this high school, one with Special Needs and one without who was not an athlete. Both were extremely successful due in most part to understanding counselors, incredible teachers and caring staff and management. By far the beast high school experience of my five children as obtained at this school. Not really well always get picked on because of my skin color and also that this school treat students of different race differently and also once you get to this school you are put into a rich or not rich category. and on top of it this school has a huge vaping problem and with drugs and that they aren't really accepting of people of color. The people here categorize themselves as the "rich" or "not rich" and if your not rich they hate you, and if you are rich they love you. Also all of the girls are brats, they only care about rich people, and being mean to others. They always put themselves first, and its always about being more skinny than others or who can wear more lulu lemon than someone else, and if you dont fit in, your not welcome. Also fix your drug problem. We are a military family and we have lived here 2 and half years. Our son has been going to the high school for a few months now and I honestly have no complaints. It is a wonderful school and the teachers seem to be really great they have emailed and reached out a lot. Our kids do play sports so we met a lot of people that way and we volunteer too. My son has really enjoyed football here its his passion again which fizzles out from time to time but the freshmen's are undefeated right now. Clubs and sports have really had our kids open up here since we aren't from here. We do think that the town has complainers here but we really have really enjoyed the teachers and they do not give out too much homework and when our son actually does his homework and classwork his gets really good grades. They have also made the students feel very accepted in every way and a little too much i think they just care a lot and want to show it. The are a very proud town with tailgates and hang outs and events. Our kids don't want to leave and that makes us feel good that they have been so happy here. If there are any issues involving your kid they will call and let you know and they handle all the issues so we were happy about that as well. Overall we are really pleased with the school so get your kids involved! We never let income stop our kids from enjoying school and no one should so yes people make a lot of money from here but i think there are a lot of great people and programs here because of that. Have fun!

column1: the school is above average and exellent formychildren. Great athletic team and has a variety of interesting extracurricular activities, but I would not say this school challenges and encourages students to do well - academically, which is most important. Not impressed. Would not recommend. I was frequently in trouble for things that seeem trivial in hind sight. I was told by multiple teachers that I would never amount to anything and wouldn't be able to get into college. Turns out I did much better when I left and went to College where it was more challenging and less people judging me for my differences. I am now highly successful despite going to MCHS. Also, they worship their athletes and felt they cared very little for other regular students who go through adversity. This was late 90s. Hopefully things have improved since then since Manheim still feels like home to me.

column3: My daughter graduated from here this past June of 2012. Not once during her time at this school did she have any trouble. She got good grades, was respectful to teachers, staff and fellow students and just pretty much got along with people. That's really all it takes. If you're out to cause trouble, well then, of course, it will find you. This school is NOWHERE near as bad as it's circulated reputation. For a bigger school, yes you would think it would be more problematic, but again, that's a rumor. It's actually a pretty decent place to go to school. I'm a freshman and my experience so far is below average. This school clearly has problems to patch. For example, the school focuses too much on sports (especially on football) than extracurricular activities and classes. Speaking of classes, most of which aren't very helpful, accelerated classes aren't really teaching challenging material, and don't get me started on Spanish. Spanish classes drag at a very slow pace and most kids who finish taking it do not become a native speaker of the language. Heck, why is it the only language? What if we want to learn something else? Anyway, lunches are also terrible. Although there are plenty of food options, you don't get enough food for the rest of the school day. Last but not least, confrontations are not uncommon nor is the neglect of staff when it comes to help. The only good things about this school would be extra class options, the band (which is one of the best in the area), and the advisory periods. The administration is horrible. The guidance department is worse. There are some good teachers but that can't make up for filthy bathrooms that often have no soap dispensers, leaking ceiling tiles and a principal that has no leadership skills. The environment is not conducive to learning. Terrible experience and felt I didn't learn anything critical. Our daughters are both K-12 graduates of Amsterdam. One is a paralegal after graduating from SUNY Albany. The other graduated from Columbia University and went on to Temple Medical School in Philadelphia and just graduated as an MD/MA.As with any school you get out what you put in.

column1: My granddaughter went to Washington-Marion and I support the school. The teacher sometimes can be very difficult especially one (not mention her name) but the school has potential to be the best in town. The new principal was very understanding when it came to listening to both the teacher and the student and he did not take any size, but he made the last decision. She graduated 2010-2011 and guess what the school had a little over a million dollars in academic scholarships. What other schools in the Lake Charles area did that. I am a 1976 graduate of Washington Sr. High before combining the schools. Ghetto is this schools middle name I walked in and the 1st thing II here is cursing from kids as I left a child was hanging his head out the top floor classroom window it looks like a detention facility rather than a place of education. I always said discipline , the willing to learn and do the right thing starts at home. If you alow your child curse you out and be disrespectful to you at home.......guess what ....he or she is going to feel its ok to go off and do it elsewhere...we cannot blame the teachers and the school we choose to send our kids to for the down fall of our kids they are not there to babysit your children they are there to teach the ones that want to learn. I wish i myself could go back and do it all over but being that i cant i make sure i try my best to coach my sons on doing it the right way so they wont have the regrets i have, but all in all i think i turned out quite well for my self. #OscarGPete#

column3: This is a public school with a private school feel. I have two kids in school, an over-achiever and an under-achiever and both have gotten a lot of attention from the faculty and administration. I couldn't have asked for more. When you consider that you get to live in Mountain Lakes, and your kids get to go to great school system, what more could you want? Honestly, your money can buy a bigger house somewhere else, but then what? 1/2 hour drive to anything and everyything? Mediocre schools? Traffic? I wouldn't have left the city if not for finding Mountain Lakes. Mtn. Lakes H.S. deserves the high marks it receives in the rankings. We moved from Dallas to Mtn. Lakes when my daughter was going into her Jr. year. She is a rather shy, sensitive person who is very creative and artsy...not at all sporty. She found a great group of friends in Mtn. Lakes, and an equally great set of teachers who inspired her to learn and prepared her well for college. The school is known for its lacrosse team, but there are plenty of excellent opportunities for kids who are interested in the arts, and of course, those who desire an academic challenge. Awful. Absolutley awful. If you don't live in Mountain Lakes, don't go to Mountain Lakes High School. Students are not accepting of anyone who isn't rich and classy and "chill" about vaping like them. Teachers and coaches are family friends with students so it creates a huge bias, if you don't live there, don't bother going to that closed unfair world. The only reasons this school is praised is because it is only reviewd by the small, rich, and closed community living there. Trust me, it may have a great reputation, but if you don't live there, the people there, students and teachers with their bonds and lifestyles, won't let you succeed. Outstanding program in a unique environment, where the valedictorian is more revered than the quarter back of the football team. With these kids, the question is not "are you going to college" it's "WHERE are you going?" Excellent. My children are well prepared for their academic experience in college This school (and indeed the entire Mountain Lakes school system) has been supportive of my child with special needs and has guided her to a college where I feel confident she will succeed both in her studies and in her social and emotional life.

column1: Me and my husband both went to temple school and now my youngest son goes there my oldest is out of school now he is special needs and temple was great with him the high school especially Coach Rogers , principal and assistant principal and they are doing a good job with my youngest one . The only problem I have had is with the basketball coach other than that we love the school . My special needs son is a substitute in the cafeteria now at temple high and they r all so sweet to him couldn't ask for no better people for him to work with . So I would recommend this school Temple HS is the best kept secret in Carroll County! It is a small school with teachers who genuinely care about students. The personalized learning environment ensures student success. Great school in a very good school district! It’s small with a community feel but has access to many opportunities for students with numerous courses for a variety of career paths and many extra curricular activities. As a former graduate of Temple High School, I can speak to having an Excellent experience during my time. The administration, teachers, and student body were supportive and caring. All of my interactions were very positive. I am excited to see the many renovations that have taken place including a new turf football field and stadium, new gym, new athletic complex on campus.

column1: i some times like this school but it has a lot of bullys and violance. I have been in the Southern Boone County School system since Kindergarten. Southern Boone offers Dual Credit Courses when you are a Junior or Senior. These Dual Credits, usually are transferable to schools in-state and some out-of-state schools. If a student takes all the DC classes offered they have the ability to enter college as a Sophmore. Like every school there are 'good' and 'bad' teachers, but the 'good' teachers outweigh the'bad'. One problem with the school is some student's lack of drive, this is a problem only because it often serves as a distraction for those who want to learn. Another is that the school has drug-testing, but it's a joke of sorts since no one has been caught, and drug-use at SoBoCo is well-known. Overall it's a decent school, with many extracirricular activities and an alternative school conducted in a seperate building. I would We love that our children can attend Southern Boone schools. The class ratios are small and the administration really cares what happens to these kids. They stay on top of their homework and test scores to make sure they succeed to their fullest potential. We wouldn't move anywhere else just to stay in this school district. *Friendly and Caring Teachers / Faculty *Above Average Quality in Courses *(As far as I know) Very Little to None Bullying/Violence Issues *Dependable Teachers *Satisfactory Variety of Courses *The school in whole had a great attitude towards all goals and encouraged the reaching of each students greatest potential *Good Test Scores from the Majority of Students -Little Narcotic Influence -Rare Course System Which Some Find Problematic [10 Block Schedule]

THe state we are in now requires all graduates to take the ACT, yet students at WHHS are not even encouraged to take it. The kids here are rude for the most part and most if the teachers do not care and they WILL tell you that. do not send your kids here if possible!!!

There are some people in this school that make it seem like a bad school, but we have beaten the other schools with academics (for example, we are the only school on the eastern shore to make AVP) and some of our sports, so we can't obviously be the worst school.

column1: I am currently a sophmore at Indian River and an Army brat, and this has been one of the best schools I've attended. The classes are intriguing and the teachers really care about helping you understand the lessons. Indian River also offers a wide array of extra-curricular clubs and activities, more than any other school in the area. Everyone is very friendly and accepting of people from other areas of the country and even the world--in fact, we're actually quite fascinated by the latter. I've also noticed that some reviewers have commented on the supposed "special treatment" awarded to athletes or those involved in the theatre and JazzRock programs. Really, they're treated just the same as everyone else, they're just involved in more activities and therefore more known to the teachers. They don't get special treatment. Overall, I love this school and hope that we will stay long enough for me to graduate. I went to this school from grades 9-10. I had been in the district since 4th grade until I moved because of the military in 2014. The teachers are, for the most part, very fair and fun to be around. There were some that I wished I didn't have, but all schools have those teachers. While in this school I participated on multiple sports teams and in many clubs, which this is always a good way to make friends. I was quite sad to leave the school, but whatever new school you choose to attend, whether you enjoy your time there depends on your attitude about it. The kids at this school are very accepting towards the special needs kids. At the graduation ceremony, the graduating class applauded a young woman with a learning disability when she received her diploma. The students can be cliquey: the jocks tend to stick together and the preppies stick together. However, I've always noticed that new students fit in very easily. Overall, a nice school that can be a great experience. My children have been to quite a few schools as we are a military family. While I am pleased with the middle school and the intermediate school, I am not impressed at all with the high school. I feel like I never know what's going on and the teachers don't really seem very involved. My daughter has a learning disability and I don't feel like her needs are being met. She is struggling. She had always been a good student until she started Indian River. I'm certain she will not be going back next school year. As a prior student, attending classes from 7th to 12th grade, I really enjoyed the teachers, class room environment and everything that went with it.I knew from the 8th grade I wanted a Naval Career was fully supported by the teachers and fellow classmates. It was the best years of my life and I wish I could do it over! I'm a old timer do to the fact I graduated in 1965. It was a excellent school! I had lived in Florida for the past 15 years and my children's education was a constant battle of switching teachers and being put on waiting lists just to get into, "better schools." My children were failing to the point where I pulled them out completely and home schooled. This school so far has been amazing. After failing two grade levels in FL, IR was able to put them back into the grades they were supposed to be in and they are thriving with the exception of Earth Science. My daughters are twins and have two different Earth Science teachers. I wish one of my daughter's would have gotten Mr. Kuba because my other daughter tells me he is more hands on in the science labs, while the other focuses a lot on packets. I've also tried to email the other Earth Science teacher with the email found on the IR website and received no response. Other than this one class, I'm extremely thankful that I can trust these teachers to do their jobs and not have to constantly ask for graded work so that I can go over it with them and reteach. They enjoy the environment, made friends, and have joined several clubs. 8/10 very good, however the way they promote things aren’t the most effective.

column3: My 9th grade teenager has been bullied by the teacher in front of the class. I do not want my child or any other student at Hebron to be a victim of bullying. No teacher should ever say anything like that to kids, teachers like that shouldn't even be around kids. I am waiting for the principal to take action on this, If nothing happens, I am going to take this to the board and aware the media. I just want to aware all of the students and parents that if anything happens to their kids that they should take action immediately. My daughter is a graduating senior at Hebron. She has been there for three years. She took all pre-AP and AP classes that were available, and has been very active in the fantastic band program. If your child is willing to work hard, all the tools they need are available at Hebron. She is now an All-State clarinetist, a National Merit Scholar, and has received multiple scholarship offers. We love Hebron! Hebron's wide variety of course offerings and diverse high achieving student body are exactly what my husband and I were looking for when selecting where we would raise our children. The principal and leadership team are fair and consistent which is needed in a high school environment - we know our kids are safe here. There is incredible rigor with courses offered which you can see with the number of national merit scholars and awards given to those who graduate from this school. There is something for every child at Hebron, from areas of academic study to student activities, the environment enables students to find their place and purpose as they begin to plan for their future. There are endless resources available from books to technology, classroom tools, incredible facilities and programming....everything we have seen has been world class. Staff and coaches are caring and involved and help students achieve at their highest level if they are willing to try. It doesn't matter if your child is bound for Harvard, Technical School or an immediate career....they will be prepared if they take advantage of the offerings available here. Hebron offers excellent AP and Pre AP courses for students. Both of my children graduated on the Distinguished Academic Program path and were top scholars. They both had their choice of universities to choose from. My son was in the highly acclaimed band program as well. Great teachers and staff. Two of my children are currently attending Hebron. I am in NO way a "PTA" Mom, and I try to be objective. I have loved almost everything about Hebron. The academics and course offerings are outstanding. AP classes prepare students for success in college, and the career center offers truly phenomenal courses for non-college students, or supplementals for college-bound to jump ahead in their field. One assistant principal can be problematic, dogmatic, and short-sighted, and some applications of dress-code can be absurd and handed with minor humiliation. I do not believe this is a school problem, I think this is the style of this particular assistant principal. The block scheduling runs akin to college semesters, so missing a day of class is a BIG deal. It's like missing 2 days of class. But students come out prepared, and already used to managing time equivalency of a 12 hour college semester. The block scheduling can be a big problem if a child has to move mid-year, but I have found that the benefits outweigh the costs. Overall, I am VERY pleased with Hebron and the 9th grade center, and I honestly do not understand why it is not rated more highly on GreatSchools.org. School has a great staff. The kids love it. Lots of school spirit. Academics ate excellent. I lived in the Dallas area for more than 25 years and my daughter attended Flower Mound High School (part of LISD). She had many friends at Hebron High school (same school district) and we heard nothing but EXCELLENT reviews of Hebron from her friends and their parents. I now live in a neighborhood in Frisco that feeds into Hebron and again have heard wonderful things about this school and its' students. Hebron High School has been great for my 2 children. They offer many AP classes and utilize an accelerated block schedule similar to a college schedule (4 classes per semester). There is a career center where students can take specialized classes in areas such as animation, engineering, and health science. Students are encouraged to find an activity/group that interests them (athletics, band, theater, ac dec, etc.). Being a larger school, competition for some teams can be tough, but the school supports jv & jv2 teams in most sports so that more students can be involved.

column1: ML is not a great school. It's an average school that advertises itself as much, much more. From facilities constantly in disrepair to a teaching staff that varies from incredible to atrocious in quality, there simply is not that much to brag about. Additionally, extra curriculars are hard to come by. It's awesome that 80% of students go on to higher education, but consider that the vast majority of these students are upper-middle class white kids and that number becomes more expected and less impressive. Consider that about 25% of those students go to small Christian colleges after being repeatedly told that any other school will be a place where their all-important faith is under attack. This means that incredibly gifted students (often little of this gift is any contribution of the school) are encouraged to squander their gifts in places of little diversity or critical discussion of their prior assumptions (this also describes ML itself very well). I feel very uncomfortable in a place that doesn't allow me to express myself or criticize (or even analyze) any part of the doctrine that it forces down the throats of children daily. Avoid this school if you value discussion or logic This may be a private school, but it's not Christian. Children's behavior is unacceptable especially kids from fellow graduates . Teacher's try to be friends with students. The school is in need of repair. Principle doesn't deal with issues. Don't be a fool, save your money. I use to go to ML, when I was there it was a great school. Now that my friends daughter goes there it has went down the drain. You get the same education as you would at public school for a lot less. ML just cares about the money now and not about the education of the students. The review from below is right, the teachers try to be friends with the students, but they have to be the popular students otherwise you get ignored and looked down upon. Knowing what I know now. I would not recommend this school to anyone. This school is excellent. Although I wouldn't agree with some of the administration and their policies, I do believe it is still a school where my child belongs. The small class size is unheard of today as well as the excellent faculty. They know my sons name and they care about him and his education, that's really what matters. Is the building older, do they need some updates, are there a few select people who need to leave the school, YES! I challenge you to find a school that doesn't have those problems. This school is a private school that does cost some significant money, but they are willing to work with you and get you financial assistance. Overall this is a GREAT school. Martin Luther High School is an outstanding Christian high school! My children have received an excellent education that well prepared them for their college core classes - even testing out of Math and English requirements so they could focus more on their major. Class sizes where small with teachers who cared about their success. They were able to participate in extra-cirruculars having positive experiences from high school that will last a lifetime. I can not thank the staff at ML enough for all that they did to support the values we teach at home, as well as support my children to become the wonderful young Christian man and woman that they are. In addition, thanks to the dedicated people who are continuing to work hard making updates to the campus, including a new track! I have been to many schools, but this one was by far the worst. It is too politically involved with a local church and bases not only their staff choices but their student's classes on who they know and how high up they are in the church. For example, even though I am currently in an AP History class and my GPA is usually around a 3.5, it was recommended my freshman year for me not to take a regular sophomore history class because I "wasn't ready". As previous posts said, the teachers are too friendly with students and pick their favorites which affects the non-favorite's grades. The only thing ML is concerned with is money. For the longest time they would not accept the choice program because certain families did not like those type of people being in their "Christian Environment". Instead, they decided to bring in many foreign exchange students in to the point where you do not even hear English being spoken in the hallways. Overall, anyone who says this school is good needs to reconsider their statement or is most likely politically known in the church. The good reviews you read are just a promotion for your money. If you're thinking of sending your child to ML, please reconsider. Aside from their lack of educational opportunities, the overall environment is terrible. ML is too politically involved with a local church and bases their staff choices and student's classes on how well known they are in the church. For example, I am currently in an AP History class and my GPA is usually around a 3.5, yet as a freshman it was recommended that I didn't take a sophomore history class because I "wasn't ready", yet certain "favorites" in my grade were able to take it and get ahead. As previous posts said, the teachers are too friendly with the church's "favorite" students which believe it or not affects the non-favorites grades. The building itself is falling to pieces and all ML cares about is your money for their own personal reasons. Anyone who differs with my opinion is most likely put on a pedestal for the church and purposely advertising on websites like this so ML can get your money. I would highly recommend staying away from Martin Luther and put your money to a better private high school or college. This teachers at this school are beyond extraordinary. If you want to send your kid to a school where he will have great academic success and grow up to be a kind, respectable person, this school is for you. Martin Luther changed my life. I entered this school a lost person who was throwing their future down the drain. ML helped me to find Christ and focus on my studies. As I entered college (Marquette University) I found I was better prepared than my classmates from other schools. I cannot stress that I would not be the person that I am today without this school. Today, I am a teacher working in the inner city. I strive to give my students what Martin Luther gave to me. Thanks ML! Martin Luther High School did very little to acclimatize me to the world. Sheltered in a school dominated by cis white Christians, I did not learn how to act around people of other race, sexualities, non-binary gender identities, or religions. Instead, I was consistently taught with western, political, and religious bias. After coming out as an atheist myself, I experienced shunning and isolation here. Overall, this was not a good place for me to be at for High School. very positive and it has very good teachers. As an alumni, and now the parent of a recent graduate, I am sad to say that I cannot in good faith recommend this school to anyone. Not only is it incredibly overpriced for what they actually offer, the administration is unprofessional, arrogant, and incompetent. They do not require all teachers to have actual certification, and the communication between parents and the administration about what goes on in the school is abysmal. They claim to "teach truth," but will cover anything up that makes them look bad, which is the exact opposite of how we raise our children. We were so disappointed, that we decided to send our other child to a public school. We found the public school to be light years ahead academically, and were treated in a far more Christian manner by the public school staff than by anyone at ML. ML will only give you the time of day if you are affiliated with a certain local church, too bad they did not realize we had money to invest in them as well. Awesome school very proud to have the 2nd Grandchild attend Martin Luther High School MLHS is a wonderful high school community. Teachers, administrators and staff consider their roles in this community a mission to use their gifts to radiate God's love and to provide a holistic, caring and safe learning environment for their students. Teachers and administrators are easily accessible to parents and work well with parents as a team to promote good study habits and correct undesirable behaviors. The school principal is often outside welcoming students and greeting parents on nearly a daily basis. Course offerings during the COVID-19 pandemic included classroom, virtual, and hybrid options, and superior quality instruction was maintained in either option. Daily beginning-of-day and end-of-day prayers and one to two chapel services each week emphasize God's overarching role in the MLHS community and give students opportunity to worship and grow in their relationships with Him. The school welcomes a diverse community reflecting Milwaukee's diverse ethnic groups. The school also offers an international program that welcomes students from other countries and guides students through the F1 student visa application process. The English as a Second Language (ESL) program interactively teaches English language and American culture in a manner that helps students quickly grasp and advance their English language skills. The new dormitory building on campus for international students is modern and impressive. I would give the school zero starts if I could. I WILL NEVER recommend Martin Luther to anyone. The school’s “bullying policy” is ridiculous. The school protects those kids whose family are high up in the churches, as those kids seem to do no wrong. I’ve witnessed much bullying that the facility had never stepped in to help. I’ve been in classrooms were the teachers joined in on picking and harassing a student!!!! That is definitely not a Christian like atmosphere. It’s truly disgusting. I had attended Martin Luther all 4 years and after my experience my parents decided to send my younger sibling to public school. I was bullied for a year and with physical evidence too. When talking to the faculty about the situation nothing was done I was told to pray about it and they looked the other way. After a year of being harassed and miserable and not wanting to attend school. After receiving hurtful threats through social media during school hours I might add. The school did nothing so when I told this person to leave me alone or if they want a fight I’ll fight them. I was threatened to be suspended!!! Suspended for standing up for my self after the school wouldn’t do anything. Another classmate was bullied so badly by a group of girls whose parents had a lot of money so the school did nothing. Those girls parents actually had to get the police involved and she ended up leaving. Public schools are far more advanced academically, and have a better anti-bullying policy. The school had changed over the 4 years of me being there. Not offering the same classes, or having the option for those advanced classes. The school is to focused on its sport teams and nothing else. They don’t care if kids are actually failing there classes as long as they are able to be out on the court they can pass by with a almost D or multiple D’s just make sure they can shoot hoops. A public school is the best option you could make for you’re child. A public school offers more options and more advanced opportunities. I wish my parents would have saved the money and sent me to a public school. It would have been a much better experience, and I would have had the chance to actually be challenged academically, as well as the school not tolerating harassment.

Mead High has a very dedicated principal and staff, a creative approach to teaching, and strong performance metrics to show for it. Having moved here from CA. last year, my now 10th grade student settled in easily and nicely. All the students are nice and there are lots of clubs and sports to get involved in. Being ranked high on the list of top schools in the state and the nation doesn't hurt your resume either! Mead is a school where if you give it your best.....everyone succeeds! We love Mead. Definitely a high quality school. When looking for a new home I purposely looked in the Mead School district. The schools offer tons of activities and work hard to make sure every child graduates and goes to college. It's just a given that you'll go to college when attending here. Mead take academics seriously to prepare you for tomorrow's world, and that starts from day one. Worst school ever. Immature, childish little brats. Horrible administration. Teachers don't care about their jobs. Nobody is gonna go anywhere in life going to mead. Reconsider your choice of a school. So far so good! My kids love Mead High School. I've had only good experiences so - so far it's been great! I feel welcomed, and has both my girls. This is a wonderful school with very professional and hard-working teachers! Especially the leaders of this school are phenomenal! I am a Mead alum and loved my experience here. High school still had its battles for me, but the school itself wasn’t one. column1: I have a child that attends Coppin Academy. She doesn't hate it but she does say it could use some improvement. I feel the same way; Coppin Academy has potentials but a lot of the students there are giving the school a bad name. Many of the tenth graders are giving this school a bad reputation. Word out on the street is that Coppin Academy is the place to be if you want to fight and not get put out. The faculty has no control over these tenth grader and before long these students are going to be the very reason this school will fail to progress. I graduated from Coppin Academy in 2009 being apart of the first graduating class, established in 2005. When I started at Coppin Academy I disliked it, for stupid reasons such as it not having many kids , being on a college campus, having to wear uniform,etc. Then the longer I was there the more I begin to grow-up and realize that the school had a great system of academics and outstanding teachers. We had challenging academic programs such as taking college classes while we were only in the eleventh grade. Being at Coppin Academy we did have our share of problems, but what school does not? Having such a small amount of classmates in the school made it that much easier to love each and every one of them. With the help of the school you guys don't think too highly of, I am going into my junior year at the college of my choice.So no matter what anyone thinks I rate Coppin Academy a five star school with five star teachers, and I am sure my classmates from class 09' can back me up. & I just want to say Rest In Peace to Lacy Roberts and Ms. Martha Brown! We Love you guys and miss you!=) My child came to this school as a transfer student from Baltimore Freedom Academy right after the 1st quarter of the school year. It took a little adjusting but the teachers worked with her and brought her up to speed. Now my child is getting better grades then she ever obtained at BFA. This school challenged her, motivated her to step up. When my child received the progress report, I was impressed. My child's study habits have changed for the better. My child is more focus and mature in thinking. I am so glad that my child was accepted. I only wish I could have gotten my child in sooner This school shouldnt even be open !! They dont have an health suite,gym, hot food or anything. Teachers give more book work whether then teaching. When a child is failing they dont mention until the last minute or notify the parents. The pricipal is caring but needs to pay better attention to his students and staff. The teachers really care at the school and the material is challenging. I would say Coppin is one of the better Baltimore City schools in the city today. The principal last year didn't have the proper skills to manage the whole school, but the principle this year has given the students the strictness that is needed, and that has made this school even better. The only think should really change is replace some of the teachers that don't care (which aren't many), with teachers that actually do. The Principal of the school is very unproffesional and talks to parents as if she is in the streets. I see now why the school has gone down so much. This used to be a very good school! I would not recommend any child to this school!!! This school has the most undisciplined and dishonest students! The students here have a below than average reading and speaking level. They look and act like thugs. This institution is a disgrace to the education system. MY SON WAS STABBED IN HIS EYE WITH A PENCIL AND HAS PERMANENT DAMAGE.....THEY WANT TO SWEEP IT UNDER THE RUG....TERRIBLE.... Not a student.I am a parent and i just can't wait until my child graduates in June

column3: My son is graduatig South Plantation High School this year in their Magnet Program. Have been every satisfied with the school,it's teachers,Brace Advisor,staff. I feel he was fortunate to have an A rated education. Great security presesnce also. This school is great if you are white. The students in honors and the magnet program get to take books home. The rest of the students(regular students) do not get books to take home. They throw all the regular students into classes of 40 or more with all kinds of behavioral issues. The school has some great teachers that would love to be able to teach these students but are afraid to say anything for fear of being bullied by administration and believe me they bully worse than any student. The administration does not like teachers that try to tell the ytruth about what goes on there. The saving graces in this school are the drama program, horticulture program and the JROTC programs. These three programs are outstanding. They also have a great sports program that accepts all students. As far as academics the only students that are being educated are the magnet and honors core classes. The teachers in these programs look down their noses at the regular students and make fun of them to their students. I am writing this because I no longer am controlled by the administration, I quit, they can no longer hurt me. I just hope that someone will read this and do something. South Plantation's teachers and administrators do an excellent job preparing their students, including the special needs program at the school for the deaf/hard of hearing students. Great programs for: Drama, Sports, Horticulture, science-based Magnet program, honors programs, JROTC. Any level student who is interested in learning will benefit. I am an alumni of SPHS, and I look back at my high school experience with NOTHING but PRIDE! I loved my school, and am proud to say where I came from. I was in the Magnet Program, on the Yearbook Staff, and was an Honors/AP student. I had friends go on to Ivy League colleges, and I ended up with 8/8 college acceptances and 7 scholarship offers. My teachers were excellent, and I knew that they cared about me not only as a student, but also as a human being. I only had a textbook issue in one class, and it's because the textbook we used was no longer being printed. The issue was resolved within a few weeks, and my teacher worked very hard to solve it. I felt very comfortable there, and miss it often. I see people bashing the school on here, and I don't think it's fair: I never had a teacher during my four years at South refuse to help me, or do anything to stop me from getting the best education they could provide. My teachers always gave us the tools and chances to get good grades, and were very supportive, even to the students who were disrespectful and disruptive (as it should be). If your student puts in hard work, and stays out of trouble, South is an amazing place to be. Our school is the best of the best. You should know that in the school we have GREAT!!! atmosphere and security. The staff is very helpful and drive to make our kids strive for the best.They have tutoring FREE. After school programs, sports, band, cheerleading, baseball, football, JROTC and more.The kids will NEVER be bored if they are involved. My son is a 2015 senior and has been in the school since 9th grade. Our experience has been FANTASTIC and wouldn't change it for nothing. He has been involved in Lacrosse, JROTC and DECCA (Marketing club) for all the years his been there and I am very please with all the opportunities. My son has been able to travel to Orlando, Atlanta, Kentucky and all over the state to other schools to compete with the JROTC, DECCA and LAX, and what kid does not enjoy those trips without mom close. But the have been incredible and very helpful for him. Here in SOUTH they will learn that leadership skills and drive they need to succeed in college, life or whatever they go. Volunteer your time to the school and support the sports you will never regret it. Get moving and apply for the Magnet Program or regular school you will love it.Become a PROUD PALLADIN! Terrible staff and principal. Do not have the kids safety in interest It is our second year and we are so happy. From the staff to the coaches and students we are so impressed. Thank you Mrs. Henshel and Mrs. Cantlupe. All of the teachers have worked with my son and the coaches are amazing. A special shout out to Coach Trevor, you are such an amazing role model for Jake. So many teachers to name. Mr. Holder you are in so many places at once. Can't say enough. My daughter will be there as well. The parents who volunteer like Coach Tim give it their all after a long day, it is truly a family. The Environmental Science and Everglades Restoration Magnet Program was a great program for my son which just graduated. My daughter will be starting the program this fall.

column3: Overcrowded...poor administration...teaching to the test. Have never even had a glimpse of the principal nor have my kids. Counting down the days for my kids to be done with this school. Great opportunties for college bound students in Math and Science. Involved parent communities. Caring and involved guidance department. Have kids there and know a lot of kids there. The sports program is a little too intense and win-centric which causes stress and injuries to student athletes. There is really a good amount of terrific and engaged teachers at this school. Have had experience with just a very few unengaged or "checked out" teachers - most that we've seen are good or very good. South River is a mediocre school at best: Teachers discourage parent involvement. Too many 'specialty' programs w/ overly ambitious, overtaxed teachers who have little specialized experience to handle the problems posed to teens doing radically advanced work; teachers most effective with tiered leave or get suck[er]ed into teaching advanced curricula. We have some smart students, but face it, we're in the boondocks. Students don't need a degree in genetic engineering by grad day. Too many advanced/STEM students feel their education is the same as standard aptitude-tiered classes, but with 3 times the pressure! They comment that classes are "useless" and have "no basis in reality." No focus on *excellence* in select magnet or specialty programs, or on ensuring students master SAT material. SR grooms 2% of students, telling the other 98% to "shut up about it." Worst, every other school in the US is moving toward full use of personal tech; SR advertises a 21st-century attitude to "ready students" for the technology-based world awaiting them, but then top-down discourages use of nearly all student-owned tech in the classrooms. Really?! The school is not yet ripe. This school is garbage. Being a student, there are many intimidating people, drug addicts, and fights. There are a few teachers more than familiar with drugs, and they don't listen to the students, and do not teach, only giving us the work to get through the curriculum. The class is 80 minutes long, most days we spend the entire time on one subject, nobody is willingly or seemingly capable of learning. Many even give the teachers a hard time, just for doing there job. The teachers aren't quite bad, there is just more to be wanted from them. They don't really go into individual needs, and get frustrated with the entire class being obnoxious, and opt to punish the class in an unsatisfactory way. Also, there is too much social interaction with the work. I like to work alone, and many teachers force you to interact with other students on a subject easily learned on your own. Homework is too much. We spend 80 minutes in a class, far too much to do the same exact thing many times over once we get home. This school is not one I support, want to be in, or care about being in. In fact, I am not in the yearbook for the 2014 senior class, nor do I want to be. I went to this high school my 9th grade year. I am now a senior at Arundel High School, (South River's rival school). South River was okay, but at the same time, it could have been a lot better. This school has a lot of potential, but the students and school staff don't live up to it. A lot of the students skip school, etc. They are amazing smart kids, and I loved them, but they made bad decisions. At Arundel, the environment was better because all of the students engaged in classes and the students are challenged. The school also lacks good diversity and has mild racism. South River High has a great academic record, test scores and in my opinion does more with less. What do I mean, the average per capita income of student family is low compared to Broadneck and Severna Park, but the scores coming out of this school are consistently close to those schools. Probably one the worst experiences of my entire life in a place where I have never felt so UNwelcomed. It nearly ruined my childhood. This school has a "top" reputation that is not deserved at all. The AP participation and pass rate helps this school place high in rankings, but that's because this school buses in high-achieving students from other school clusters for their STEM magnet program, and those students have to pass AP Human Geography and Calculus. Thus, the STEM students are artificially inflating the AP stats for the rest of the school. The standardized test scores at this school (especially for students from disadvantaged backgrounds) are shameful, and this school should not be ranked as high as it is. if your child is lucky enough to get a spot in the STEM program, I suppose it's okay, but otherwise this is a mediocre school. This school is horrible at handling bullying and racism as well. My child was bullied and I met with administration three separate times regarding the matter, with the admin promising to fix the issue each time. The issue never resolved. We are pulling our child out and moving them to a private school next year. The only thing this school has going for it are many of their amazing teachers. Two boys graduated from there about four years ago. SR provided an excellent education in many areas including STEM classes and AP course in other areas such as English, literature, math. Many friends of theirs were afforded very good education. All were prepared for college level courses and did well. Mine did well in college and graduated with degrees in difficult areas such as engineering. So, for good students, SR serves them very well. South River is an excellent school regardless of whether your children are in STEM or not. The STEM program admission (and all other magnet program admissions in AACPS) are purely lottery based. No school in AACPS is pulling high achieving students from other clusters to boost their test scores. It’s not like how magnet program admissions work in Montgomery County. It’s true that STEM students are required to take two AP classes in their curriculum to graduate and that that could be influencing the high AP participation rate at SRHS, but all students at the school have access to AP courses, not just STEM students. This school has very dedicated teachers and very welcoming community. I agree that SRHS not being racially or socio-economically diverse is a huge con, and that sometimes the product of that is a school where some instances of racism are more likely to go unchecked, but most of the students are friendly and not racist at all. There were some incidents at the school two decades ago that gave the school a reputation for being “racist,” but SRHS has come a long way since then.

Half the teachers are above average and the other half don't bother to teach. The only reason why this school is considered to be a top school is because of the many AP courses it offers. Honestly this school can be the best thing to happen to you or the worst. It is very comprehensive and an overall great environment. However some teachers are not the best. Specifically the VP. Ms. Barone is straight up........Ummmmmmmmmmmmmm there are certain people you just don't want to get on the bad side of. Let's leave it at that. Great school but you don't need to struggle here when you could get into the same college by taking it easy at a different school. So good luck. Great school, staff and teachers. The AP classes prepared my son for college. He's been on the Dean's List for the past 3 years! Being an alumnus of Dr. Ronald E. McNair Academic High School is what distinguished me from the rest of my Freshman class in my Undergraduate career in college. I was comfortable with taking multiple classes at once, studying almost 12 hours at a time and having to do a large amount of homework assignments that encountered deadlines. I was always on top of my game and my priorities never changed. McNair taught me about time management and how to set mind my straight on academics being the first thing on my to-do list. When it comes to great schools that count, McNair is on top of my list. Many thanks to Mr. Slattery and Ms. Barone for running a great school. Fernando Titus Alumus McNair is portrayed to be better than what it really is. Honestly, people don't know what ot really is. It's really hyped up. Unfortunately, due to rigorous curriculum most of the students cheat in order to gain advantage. It's uncertain whether administration is aware of this dilemma. This school is hyped up to to be much better than it actually is. if you want a positive high school experience, please choose another school. the academic environment is toxic. Students are often told that they are "Mcnair Kids" and shouldn't be acting like "Dickinson Kids" or "Lincoln Kids" as if to say that these are bad or improper schools. only one of the 8 teachers that I have classes with have actually tried to help kids who are struggling. The school is in such poor shape that about 2 or 3 classrooms are out commission because of faulty pipes leaking and breaking through ceiling tiles. the only good thing about this school is that it keeps you on your toes and that I have made some incredibly kind people here.

column1: Honestly, this is one of the worst school to send your children to. The majority of the budgets seems to go to making the place look better, and giving the obese school cop a segway. quality text books, on the other hand, seem to be in short supply. Not only are they obsessed with how the school looks, most of the teachers are unable to look much past the appearance of the students, and several seem to have a personal problem with body art. Parents, If your child is the least bit 'Different,' do your self and them a favor, and do not send them to this horrid, awful institution. Having a daughter who graduated from SLHS and a son currently enrolled, I can say without hesitation that our experience with South Laurel High School has been a very positive experience. The faculty and staff are very caring and strive to help students with any issues they may have. My daughter is currently enrolled at University of the Cumberlands and thanks to the foundation given her at SLHS she was awarded multiple scholarships and is on track to graduate a semester early if she chooses to do so. Also my son loves that he is able to participate at the Center for Innovation program offered at South. Oh what an awesome school! My favorite part was when I went to the principals because I was being bullied and they kept telling me if I acted more "normal" it wouldn't have happened! Mhm! What a fun school for everyone to attend! Definitely doesn't have an issue with enabling bullies and victim blaming!

column3: While at this high school (I graduated in 99) there was a high teacher turnover rate, it's mindboggling to me that this is STILL the case. I am not shocked to read about former students feeling left behind, without adequate preparation for higher education institutes, etc. While there we were experimented on with an "integrated math" program where they would mix elements of algebra with trig, calc, etc. How could you ask me to do trig/calc before learning the basics of algebra?! Yet this is what happened and I was never able to recover from the confusion, I believe something outlandish like 70% of my class was FAILING math. I wonder why?! I hate that I was a guinea pig, I also hate that they only focused on my graduating high school and nothing beyond that. This is a diploma mill, a farm for mediocrity! If your child goes here, you'll have to pick up a lot of slack at home. I recommend a private high school, trust me, it's a wise investment in your future! Bad school all around except perhaps the choir program and AP classes. I have put a lot of effort into knowing my child's teachers and the principal, and I have been well received. Also, I have gotten a lot of support when I needed it. We have had to change classes and work with a transfer, which had some challenges. The majority of the staff genuinely care about the kids at GHS. Their expectations for students are that they will be productive and creative, caring members of society and many of the staff live and teach by that philosophy.. I've been a teacher here for 17 years and have seen the school change dramatically from being overcrowded with aging facilities and huge teacher and administration turn over rates, to now a beautiful campus with a strong administration team and teachers and students who truly care about the students, school, and each other. I feel the difference daily in my attitude and especially the students' attitudes. A true vibe of pride in ourselves, each other, and our school. Heard horror stories about Gilroy. Read the great schools reviews and noticed that the review were quite a while ago. I moved to the area and was concerned. I called school and asked to speak to the principal... I was amazed that he was available and answered all my questions. He asked me if I wanted to visit the school with my daughter. He took us for a tour! I was very surprised to see a very neat orderly and clean school. I talked to a few teachers and were very positive and enthusiastic about the school. My daughter is enrolled now and is having a great time! The campus is beautiful...impressed so far!! Looking real good. Great opportunities for students! The school has really turned around in the last few years! Many AP opportunities, many sport opportunities, safe environment and many clubs and events for the students to participate in. They have an excellent dual immersion program for spanish language and a bio technology track as well. I came in to this school to make a difference. My students were the best part of the experience. The leadership is was causes high teacher turnover every year. It is ineffective and not on the same page and does not keep students accountable. There is nepotism because the principal is so invested in wrestling that those students get special treatment and the assistant principal has a son in the wrestling program who also gets special treatment. All the other students know this and they do not feel as valued.

column1: This school is not the school to send your child to. For the price I paid it was not even worth half of it. Very unorganized staff that seems to care more about money then education. If you want your child to be ready for college then send her else where. Most of the teachers here seem to have no experience in teaching. The school makes you do mandatory fundraisers just to get more money & attend meetings that were a waste of time. With all the money they collect I never saw one improvement. The worst part is the gym has no AC and the cafeteria serves unhealthy food and from what I understand is infested with cockroaches. I'm glad I've taken her out and she's now somewhere better for half the cost of this school. I am so proud that my daughter is a graduate of Mission. She is now in her first year at college and is doing very well. The teachers at Mission are wonderful, the counselors are very helpful and the way the school communicates with us parents is more than I expected. My youngest daughter who is in middle school can't wait to attend Mission and play on the soccer team. My daughter is a sophomore at Mission. She is very challenged by the classes she is taking, as she is in three AP courses. I was very worried about the pressures of being in a lot of advanced classes, but her teachers have been working with her time management. The counselor even meets with her during lunch to offer advice. I am very happy with this school, and I would recommend it. It is value for money and the education is top notch. My daughter's experience at Mission has been very positive. She has made many good friends. Mission is very good about bring the ladies together and forming a true sisterhood. The staff and teachers are great and very welcoming :) I have a daughter who is currently attending Mission High School. She is currently in her Junior year. She is currently taking 2 Advance Placement Classes and 1 honors class. On top of that she is involved with Sports & 2 Clubs. I know that all of these things will help her get into her college of choice. Each grade has a monthly Advisment meeting to discuss what path they have to be on to acheive that goal. While she does face a hard year ahead of her she knows that this is what she needs. She is very challenged with her courses and receives the positive reinforcment at school to what we give here at home. Her counselor always shares her positive academic achievements as well as checking in with her on her personal life to make sure everything is going well. I am beyond pleased with Mission! This is my daughter's second year at Mission. I have been very pleased with both the administration and the teachers. Though my daughter has struggled she has always been able to get the much needed resources. The teachers are extremely motivated and I have always had a great response when contacting any of them. The website is wonderful, we have complete access to grades as well as school assignments. Even though I live blocks away from a prominent coed private school, I know this was the right choice for my daughter and don't mind driving 20 minutes out because of the education she is receiving. The school is pursuing authorization as an IB World School and this is definitely a plus in any high school education.. Este es el primer ano para mi hija en Mission High School, las espectativas que teniamos de esta escuela desde el comienzo del ano han sido mas de lo que esperabamos. Desde la atencion que ofrecen los maestros asta atencion que el principal ofrece. Estamos muy orgullosos de pertenecer a esta escuela. 5 estrellas bien merecidas :)

column3: Obviously the review that received one star was from a student who wants to blame everyone else for his/her lack of intelligence. I can guarantee whoever wrote this had no interest in academics and only attended because they had to. Get real, if all these problems they listed existed RCS would not be able to turn out the caliber student they do. Thank God this student was from 2003 and we do not have to deal with whoever it is anymore. In 2012 look at what our students have accomplished. Look at how many attend college. Look at the credentials of our teaching staff. Look at our Sports record and all the other activities our students are involved in. Look at our outstanding Music Dept. Sure there are those who only attend because they have to. What a wonderful world it would be if they could be eliminated from the student body so we could teach only those interested in bettering themselves. We could all rejoice. A RCS HS Teacher and proud of it. This school District is horrible, little kids being left outside hours endless, staff saying accidents happen, boys pinning girls against the wall, mean while the girls are screaming for help and not one teacher hears the girls screaming, boys choking girls. education stinks they are more concerned about sports. its so great half the kids are dropping out. this school district stinks, little skids being left outside, teachers not knowing when and how it happened. peter b coeymans made the news in 2012 because a little girl was left outside, was wondering the street becuase she couldn't get in. same thing happened in aw becker. staff saying accidents happen, thats a bad accident for kindergartners and 1st graders. kids being left on buses, they don't do much about bullying. education stinks, staff is so quick to blame the parents for things they do wrong. This school is anti-american and anti-military. The superintendent Alan R. McCartney finds the military symbols offensive. If he finds this so offensive, then how does he feel about the American flag? this school has basic education, not good but not terrible. there are not many electives to choose and most teachers do not care about the students. the clubs are very minimal, which is very unfortunate. one great thing about this school is the drama and choir programs it offers. unfortunately, the other arts programs are non existent. most people in this community care about the sports programs, football in particular. while the football team gets new uniforms every season, other sports teams like track and soccer have not gotten new uniforms in around 20 years. this community is very racist, homophobic, and sexist. this makes school days hard to bear. some people in this school do not feel safe here, which is hard to hear because this is basically their job for four years (high school) until they are sent off. Terrible because the are very rude to everyone. I have no idea who these bad reviews are coming from--the faculty, staff, and administration have been wonderful for my three children over the years. There are plenty of options for AP classes as well as electives. The music and drama productions are fantastic at the High School. RCS is still small enough that your children are known by all the faculty and they still are able to participate in three seasons worth of sports. Anyone who says otherwise must have an axe to grind. I am excited to see where my kids will go to college after their excellent experiences at RCS. I have had two children go through Becker Elementary, with amazing, caring experiences, as well as through the MS . One, has successfully graduated HS is currently performing beautifully in a 4 year private college. Graduating HS with many credits towards College was a huge plus! While the other child is currently in HS. Both have had wonderful experiences, opportunities and teachers! Being challenged in all areas and working her way through with endless opportunities. We have had chances to move to other schools, yet choose to keep them here in a smaller district with a multitude of ethnic backgrounds. Making a more aware individual ready for future experiences and appreciation of hard work. There are pluses and minuses to smaller schools, but this school is raising the bar for smaller schools. I Highly recommend Ravena Coeymans Selkirk School District, as it may have had a bad rap in the past, all schools face challenges in some part. However, this is a school going places and I'm glad my kids are and were a part of it! I am extremely disappointed in this school district. We are very pleased with the close knit community and the school system.

column1: My family is new to MSHS this year. I have missed important deadlines and activities because I did not receive any communication from the school. I think communication between parent and school is poor. You can email your child's teacher(s); some actually read emails and respond and some don't bother. The office staff is friendly, helpful, and accommodating. I have not met the principal yet, but hope I have the opportunity soon. I hope that next time you will take racial issues abd bullying of any type seriously Shocking to hear about the racism allowed within the school. One of the best public schools in this region! Great culture, awesome teachers & staff.
