column3: Whitefish Bay High School is an outstanding college preparatory school. The students are well instructed, treated as adults, and challenged in every way. The school offers a wide variety of extra-curricular activities and opportunities: music, athletics, art, drama, service, leadership... Students are encouraged to participate in and out of the classroom. The character, growth and mental well-being of all students are priorities for the administration and staff. They are well prepared for success in college and many go on to top universities around the country. So proud and fortunate that my children attend this school. Whitefish Bay High School has an extraordinary academic record and exemplary staff. For college-prep students, there probably are only a few other school systems in Wisconsin that measure up to the high bar set by WFBHS. However, after sending three children through the system, with one thankfully transferring out as a freshman, I would NEVER advise anyone to send their child to WFBHS. The social climate is cruel and toxic. There is a little outright physical bullying, but social intimidation and subordination -- rejection, hostility, and exclusion -- are really the norm. I do not fault the school system as much as the broader social environment of the community for this abhorrent condition. I fault the parents for not recognizing -- and even contributing -- to the social jungle that pervades WFBHS. The "popular" groups within the caste system make "Mean Girls" look like a nursery school. If you are not "accepted," you are outcast. To be "accepted," you must buy into the system and prey on other students. And this is true not just for the girls, although they are definitely more prone to social murder. I realize this kind of behavior exists at most schools, but I would hope it is the exception not the rule. In WFB it is institutionalized. I also realize that my criticisms could be dismissed as the whining of a mother of social misfits (which I am not). To prove my point: I have discussed this with other parents and students who fully agree with my assessment. I have done my homework to confirm this reality exists, not just for my children but for all that attend the school, on the top or bottom of the social ladder. I feel obligated to respond to the most recent posting by a parent on January 23, 2016. I could not disagree more with the advice to never send your child to WFBHS.First, and foremost, the teachers at WFBHS truly care deeply about their students and their professions. They are committed to providing the highest caliber of education to ALL students, not just a few students. The staff are incredible, caring, and compassionate as well.Second, the opportunities made available to current and alumni WFBHS students are uncommon and made more remarkable by the reality that WFBHS is a public school.Third, WFBHS is small enough for personalized attention, but large enough to provide a myriad of intellectual and social outlets for students to develop.Finally, the parents and community are committed to the school. While there is no denying that this commitment carries its own baggage too, I would prefer to send my children to a school where the teachers, parents, and community are active than one where they are not.The aforementioned is not intended to dismiss the previous parent's concerns. I would agree that the homogeneity of Whitefish Bay as a community ultimately impacts the culture at WFBHS in a negative way. Diversity is encouraged on the surface, but not always supported with any rigor or depth. Still, the description offered is more of an exception than a rule at WFBHS.I would strongly recommend WFBHS to any and all parents. Disappointing. We moved to this area for the schools. Grade school and middle school were mostly very good. The high school has been frustrating due to lack of balance, a culture that does not promote tolerance and an abject refusal to address the toxic stress experienced by students. However, there are several teachers at this school who are truly exceptional. This review is based on personal experience and it is not to say your student won't flourish here. This review is an opinion only- you may have a different experience here.To begin, the school's main focus is "academic rigor". This school is a 5/5 *if* you are academically talented/gifted, and athletic- there is no room for being average here or for being a square peg. Many B level students have been in tears from the pressure at this school. There is another high school a few miles south where the focus is diversity, arts, sports and academics. A seemingly much more balanced approach.Teachers: 8/10. Overall, quite good. There are certainly a few who leave much to be desired and yet nothing is done to help move them along despite feedback from students and families directly to counselors and administration.Counseling department: 8/10. Responsive, kind. Helpful to a degree, as this is a school of high achievers.Administration: 3/10 There seems to be a lot of box checking and chatter but not actual care for the student's well being when issues arise which is fairly transparent. The newest administrator within the last 2 years seems quite rude to students and parents. Dealing with a parent population that is fairly intense, this administrator may want to reign that in. The principal: 6/10 She receives the highest mark in this category. Recommendation: own some of the issues at the school and do not place it on the students.The students are working hard to keep their head above water in a cut throat school for academics and athletics while trying to navigate being a teenager and they do not need any additional pressure put on them from administration for school based activities/planning.College readiness: 10/10"Academic rigor". HOURS of homework. Take home:There are many schools in the area besides this one that offer an excellent education and prepare students for college. A high school student should have a balanced experience and overall enjoy their time in high school. Academic rigor, the pressure to be the best at everything, and acceptance based on fitting the mold of this school is not worth the detriment to a teenager's happiness, mental health, confidence/self esteem and well being.

column1: This school has the nicest campus on Kaua'i. This school is horrible. Some of the teachers and the principal didn't even show up for the back to school night. Bullying for NON local kids is rampant. The lack of control the teachers have over this school is unsatisfactory. The teachers are only hoping that the kids graduate, not that they succeed or get good grades. Smoking allowed right across the street by students within view of the school. I pulled my son from this school and enrolled him in ONLINE education, if you care about your child's education, I would suggest you do the same. Open house less than 10% of the parents even bothered to show up. the principal is the problem here, and as another review stated, the (district) boss is a former principal who somehow got promoted - go figure. teachers can only do so much with limited resources/support, and "more with less" only will accomplish minimal results. the teachers are rebelling one by one due to inept administration, and students suffer. WHS has fallen dramatically from its heyday in the 90's, when academics and athletics were leading the island. Violence is a major concern if you are white. Most of my son's teachers did not know him even though his attendance was great. Drugs were rampant on campus. Test scores were poor. I am glad I took my son to the mainland. I moved him half way through his freshman year. It was a great decision. Since the reviews are pretty outdated, the public needs to be aware of great strides this school has undertaken. This school has the Hawaii Principal of the Year and it is only her third year. My son is Caucasion, does not get bullied, and has access to a rigorous education. He is enrolled in advanced Math and will be able to take AP coursework as early as his Sophomore year. As a teacher at another school, I am very pleased with the offerings at this school.

column3: I love this school. It has amazing teachers and students! Pine View High School all the way! My experience at Pine View was not one I would like to relive. Some of the teachers and staff are great, while others are really not up to par. For those who were great teachers, I apologize for this rating, it is not a reflection of you. I had the chance to experience this school and one other during my high school career and this school had a lot to be desired. I was in AP English classes when I transferred to Pine View, so I decided to continue with that here as well. They were reading books I has read as a freshman (and this was a Senior class!) I did not feel challenged at all. The ceramics, choir, dance and creative writing classes were all wonderful and the staff was excellent! I just felt that in classes that were supposed to be teaching and building on necessary basics, there was little to no challenge. Great experience, great teachers, and great students! When I was going into High School my mom took me to tour each HS in town and let me choose from there. It was a night and day difference with the faculty and how they greeted me in the halls as I walked around and the positive energy that was felt at PV compared to the other schools. It was the easiest and best decision I made. I had to drive across town everyday to school but I know PV was a better fit for me rather than SC! Pine View was an awesome school to attend. The faculty truly cares about the students and there's a great sense of school spirit there. I loved it and will always have a piece of Pine View with me. My daughter graduated from PVHS this year, and honestly had a fantastic experience there. She is at BYU now, and says the AP classes really helped prepare her for the university. In addition to helping prepare students for college, Pine View has an amazing culture of acceptance with kids from all different backgrounds who all mix without a lot of cliques. That is invaluable at this age. She had wonderful teachers and loved the administrators and would not trade her experience at Pine View. Pine View has one of the most excepting and kind student bodies. They honor and respect everybody’s differences, they are kind, and include everyone. My students have enjoyed their time there immensely. Our children enjoyed their years at Pine View High School! Pine View High is awesome, a few teachers didn't always know what they were doing perfectly (or at least it felt that way), but Pine View was my home, the people were my people, and I had an amazing high school experience thanks to the teachers, counselors, clubs, and spirit of the place. This school is inclusive of everyone, especially at dances and assemblies.

column1: As a graduate from Republic I would have to say that it was a great school. The athletic programs were great. Nearly all of the teachers I had were very good and prepared me for a successful four years in college. There is no reason a student can't be successful unless they put forth no effort whatsoever. Honestly for a child to fail at Republic, they have to try to fail. The teachers have no means of forcing the kids to do anything without a parent filing a law suit and the kids who failed are the ones who just refused to do their work. The teachers do not get paid enough money to deal with all the troubled kids that interfere with class on a daily basis. I thoroughly enjoyed my experience at Republic and would hate for my children to attend elsewhere. My only complaint with Republic is with the newest superintendent. He seems to be focused a little more on his career than the students. He prides himself on school being open when it snows and students get in car accidents and are injured nearly every snow day because of it. Also, the cooperative learning program is a joke. In no way does it prepare students for a career. It just wastes the time and slows the progress of students. Republic High School is by far the worst school I have attended in all of my years of education. The administrators are absolutely clueless about the lives of students and have no idea how to make a school function properly school. They don't support local events or attend school functions unless they are obligated and have no sort of relationship with students in any way. There is also a major drug problem at this high school and offenses are never taken as seriously as they should be. My review of this high school is due to the fact that this high school pales in comparison to high schools I have attended in other states and towns. I have attended two other high schools and a total of seven different schools in all. If you are moving to this region or deciding on which school to enroll in, I advise you to look elsewhere for s quality education and choose a different school system. This is just not the best fit for any type of student with any type of background. Horrible it racist homophobic transphobic and all in out sexist

column3: If your a parent that has high aspirations for your children, then Minersville isn't the school for you. The majority of the students don't care about their coursework and just go through the motions while avoiding trouble. For the small percentage who do care and want to be prepared for college and get into a good school, the opportunity isn't provided. Minersville doesn't have the resources to provide challenging coursework. As a result, the 5 or 6 students who do want to take AP courses etc, are left without anything, which looks horrible on college applications. Besides a few exceptions, the quality of teaching is poor and the focus of the administration is mostly athletics, which Minersville is not particularly good at anyway. When you look at this school from afar, you don't see much glamour. However, it is unwise to judge a book by its cover. From experience of moving a lot and changing schools, I can tell you that Minersville by far has a great curriculum for students. Yes, the district is not wealthy nor is it the best in the country, however, this school has great potential. I have attended several "privileged" schools before and after Minersville High, and I can tell you the teachers there did not have the students best interest; they were more interested in tutoring on the side for extra money. The teachers, administration and staff of this school care about their students. And let me tell you, the school spirit in this town is amazing. I've never experienced a school in which students can be seen wearing their pride almost 24/7. Yes, there is drama which occurs everywhere! Yes, the school needs improvement, just like every other school in America. I would definitely advise anyone I know to send their child/children to this school. I would also advise that they take advantage of every opportunity in this school(academic programs, sports, arts, etc.). just like they should in any other school.

column1: Bellevue High School is #1 with teachers who care and students who excel in education . The entire school system in Bellevue is the number one reason parents live in this community. National averages show that the percentage of students that graduate from Bellevue go on to College or higher learning institutions. Great Schools = Great communities. My daughter spent her freshman year here so far. She'll be returning after summer break. She is an amazing student who makes great grades. I feel like she's getting a good education at Bellevue. She respects her teaches there as well and has great things to say about them. Bellevue is a school where you can be whatever you want and will be accepted. The students get as much out of the teachers as the student puts in. At Bellevue you make your own path and have the skills and life experiences to be successful. Would not recommend, ever. They would not open when they needed to be, and are pretty ridiculous and petty. The administration only shows respect and attention to excelling student and extra curriculars. Administration will ignore the harsh ways on how teachers treat students while taking the wrong measurements to ensure students mental health. It's over looked and always treats the students as the issue especially when it comes to bullying as that gage the habit of victim blaming. Above all else the close at nature feeling you get at this small school is nice but suffocating as anyone can know your business and shares it amongst their peers and teachers at a alarming rate. Shaming a student as well happens often and the teacher will join in just because they choose to do something differently. Is it a close feeling to everyone or do teachers/administration and students take advantage of that closeness to mistreat each other and not speak up about something when it's inappropriately stated.

column3: Small town feel with tons of great opportunities for students, no matter what their interest area from the sciences to the arts, strong athletic programs and everything in between. Our experience includes multiple teachers and staff who have gone way above and beyond for our kids, all strongly supported by the community. What a great place to raise kids! KHS has deteriorated with the change in administration several years ago. The current administration is disconnected from students and parents. Very little effort has been made to ie, learn the names of students. Communication with parents is not transparent and is limited, for example, last year a dress code policy was announced on the first day of school (after many families had gone back-to-school shopping). KHS offers no AP classes and very few classes are eligible for community college credit, which puts graduates at a distinct disadvantage to many of their peers coming from other schools. KHS focuses on sports--you rarely see an administrator at a non-sporting event, and rarely is a non-sport activity/accomplishment acknowledged on the school facebook feed. KHS went to block scheduling a year ago, and many classes did not finish their curriculum (or zoomed through it so fast at the end of the school year to the point of being non-effective). The school is clean, students are provided with laptops, the sports facilities are adequate and the auditorium is fairly new. There are many good teachers, but there are also a number who are not--for example, if you assign homework, you ought to take the time to actually grade it. Grades should be put in the online grade book in a timely manner (not all in the last week of the semester). KHS is a decent school, and it is "safe", however, opportunity is limited, class offerings are stagnant, administration is remote and unfriendly and it certainly is not the same school it was a few years ago, which is sad. Very positive. There have been lots of changes over the last several years, but all of them have been based on input from students, parents, faculty, and/or professional staff. It's disheartening to see negative remarks about the district - those of us in the community that have followed the schools over many years have seen a positive change in attitudes within the district as well as a rebounding of test scores, student involvement in the community, participation in extra curriculars (including several recent successes), and a boost in enrollment. The schools have been great partners within the community, and both are benefiting. It's a great time to be in Knoxville! Knoxville High School staff are some of the most dedicated, hard working teachers I’ve ever worked with. We strive to create a positive learning environment for all students.

column1: Though Grant HS is in a low income and crime ridden community it's administration inspires the students to be academically successful and strive for a prosperous future. There is room for improvement with the instructors and administration, the parents need to engage as well to ensure their child is getting a good education. Grant is a good high and there are good students. It should be respected for it is the 3rd oldest school in Sacramento CA. Grant High School does a great job of working with students using a holistic model. Counselors, teachers and administration are working with students through some very challenging obstacles such as homelessness, mental illness, effects of poverty etc. Test scores and other indicators don't capture the amount of love and support provided to students. As a parent of two high performing students, I am proud of what they received from Grant High School. My hope is that Grant High will receive more funding in order to provide the specialized support needed to improve test scores. My experience is not good at all im very fustraitrd and am looking into changing schools for next year. I'm a senior student currently at Grant, and unfortunately it has fallen off more so than the past three years I've spent here. This pandemic hit hard, but even then they were far less than prepared than I thought they would be to reopen in person. Every day feels like conditions get worse. Classes with more than 30 students, classes being held outside in near 100° heat, air conditioners going out in multiple classrooms without so much as a "We'll get on it soon". They are not social distancing properly, and they are having some kids wait over an hour to get a bus home. I don't fault the teachers and most staff, as a lot of them aren't in control of the funding and what it's used for, but I feel like more focus is being put on the construction rather than the actual students or teachers. I wish this was a more positive review, that I could recommend this school, but I truly can't. Please try a different place for your kid, or at least wait until you are aware if this school has gotten everything straightened out. Grant High School was a life changing experience for me. This is a school with many opportunities, if you seek them. I was college ready, and a top student. I also was an athlete and found the programs to be amazing. While Grant is lacking in funding it makes up for it in spirit. Im sad to hear alot of the staff that were there when I attended are no longer working there, but that staff made the school as amazing as it is. I feel this school would have better ratings if more people knew to post reviews on this site. When there are only negative experiences being broadcasted and the people with positive experiences are not doing reviews, it doesn't create a cumulative review thats not based on bias. This school has the greatest potential, and the greatest stories to go along with it. I blame the city and the state for not putting more into the school considering its location. Despite the adversity, those who have strong pacer pride, work hard to give the school a better name.

column3: Methuen High has been burdened with a stigma that it doesn't deserve. Sure, it's outdated and lacks full walls due to the open-concept(which is for a reason! Some people think they couldn't afford walls. Pshh.) but when it comes down to it, the school is what you make of it. They offer a multitude of rigorous, challenging courses and they even participate in the Advanced Placement (AP) program. In short, I reitterate, it's all in what you make of it. Im a senior on school, and methuen high school has been great for me, I've enjoyed a lot of groupd and activities they have. They are pretty fun yo join. It doesnt matter if it has walls or not, because the teachers are super great there, they are so nice and finally MHS has improved a lot, since it been under construction from 2012, and now the school is going to be looking great> Great school...Renovations are excellent! Student/teacher ration is solid. I couldn't be happier! We have been thrilled with the money that is going into the public school system!! I am a freshman currently attending Methuen high and without a doubt the school is very beautiful and the staff are understanding of the students. The school has many fun extra curricular activities,clubs, and sports that your son/daughter can sign up to do. On problem with the school would be control. I don't know if there is a lack of staff or what but the amount of incidents that happen at the school should and can be lowered. Fights and class skipping is expected In a highschool but it is too monotonous at mhs. Then again if you do what your supposed to do no problems will occur. Overall mhs is a good school. I am proud to be a Ranger-alum! MHS for life. I didn't appreciate it at the time, but now I do. I couldn't be more lucky to have the school experience I did. Socially, academically, extracurricularly. High school is what you make of it!!

column1: Fantastic academic and sports programs! So glad we made the switch from public to CCC. This school is what education should be about: all students expected to go to college and the development of quality character traits. I have a student who will be a senior this year. He has had a stellar education to this point. He is enrolled in the IB program, CCC is the only private school in Pinellas to have this program. He is very well rounded. He is in several sports and is on several committees and honer societies. The school has a very strong college graduation rate. I highly recommend this school. I do wish they had a stronger push towards missions. The school offers a great variety for my kids thru education and sports. I have enjoyed my time at CCC My daughter just graduated from CCC and had a wonderful experience. She loved the IB program. The teachers are very devoted to the kids. I graduated from CCC last year and it was the best four years of my life so far! The teachers are extremely involved and caring when it comes to the students; extra help was always offered when needed. I don't think I could've received a more well-rounded experience. Endless extracurricular and leadership opportunities were offered during my time that filled my college applications and helped mold me into a more polished professional. The students were very welcoming and kind so it was easy to make friends. I am very thankful for CCC! Pros: -courses are pretty good- teachers are mostly helpful- test scores are good (ACTS,SATS etc)Cons:- this is a very cliquey school. - Students are not always nice - International students from China are made fun of- staff is not up to par I am a transfer student from California in the 10th grade and came to CCCHS for a better education and a friendly environment. My experience so far has been the complete opposite. I've met the most shallow and rude people at this school and I do not feel welcomed AT ALL. My history teacher is actually a great teacher and I understand everything she says! However, my chemistry teacher in honestly incapable of teaching or controlling a class. Everybody makes mistakes of course -- but she makes an EXCESSIVE amount of mistakes and often the students in her class correct her! My English teacher lost my essay, which was also submitted on turnitin.com with a time stamp, and when she told me she never got my essay it was several weeks later so i printed it out and gave it to her. I ended up getting a 12/60 dropping my grade from an A to a 79%. I talked to the school counselor about it and she said she would talk to my teacher, it has been a week and we are taking midterms and there still has been no change in my grade. Students have been caught cheating and their parent have "made a donation" to the school and suddenly the entire incident is forgotten! The school i very corrupt because it is a private catholic school that doesn't have to follow the guidelines of the public school system. Never have I been so unhappy in school -- I used to look forward to learning new things and this school has made me lose that passion. I play a sport that I love and I have decided I will not be playing for the school next year because of the terrible 'sportsmen ship among my team and lack of coaching skills. It is sad that this school has changed me so much for the negative and I am no longer the happy, optimistic person i was before I attended to CCCHS. To sum it all up -- I am miserable at Clearwater Central Catholic High School and I have lost passion and love for the things that were most important to me. Instead of enjoying my high school experience, I find myself counting down the days that I have to spend in this horrible place. This is an excellent school! I would highly recommend this high school to all students. This school offers college preparatory classes, AP, and International Baccalaureate. There truly is a wonderful sense of community from both students and families. A top notch school with a faith filled environment and leadership and that encourages and enables each student to want to raise their own personal bar Excellent experience for my 5 children. They all received an excellent education while being able to love their faith. Overall, CCC is unsatisfactory. It earns 3 starts because it barely is better than a public school. The absolute worst thing about this school is it’s uncaring and unhelpful administration. Not only are quality teachers effectively forced out by the administration’s unwillingness to work with them, but students are also made to feel as if their opinions do not count in the slightest unless their family is a big donor at the school. Student suggestions and ideas on creating clubs and organizing events are completely negated by a stagnant administration. As a result, little opportunity to develop interests and skills can be found here. There are few clubs and outlets for creativity. Overall, you should go to Tampa Prep or Berkeley instead. Clearwater Central Catholic is an excellent school. We are so grateful to be a part of this family. The school is overrated and not what it seems to be. Their main emphasis is on sports and mainly varsity football. Most JV teams and other sports teams are very underfunded and not really cared about by the administration, faculty, and coaches. Several teachers are inexperienced and academics are not that difficult. They have major problems attracting and keeping qualified and caring teachers. Clearwater Central Catholic is a wonderful learning institution. I grew up attending Catholic schools since birth, and was excited to attend CCC for high school. For any reviews that state the curriculum is not difficult, perhaps you can enroll in the average public schools in the area, and compare. Numerous students I knew transferred from Palm Harbor University, Countryside High School, Clearwater High School, and East Lake to attend CCC. Once they enrolled at CCC, they stayed. Some reviewers here stated the classes seem too "easy." If this is the case for your student, I advise them to enroll in Honors, AP, or the IB program. These courses prepare you excellently for college. Obviously, there will be teachers who you enjoy, and others who you don't feel are the best, but that comes with any school. On a whole, this school has a wonderful learning environment, hardworking students (which encourages your student to push themselves to their fullest potential), and great teachers. This school is rooted in God; students often attend mass, chapel, and religion class at the school. I have never seen a fight break out, I have never seen a student talk back to a teacher, and have never seen a teacher treat a student poorly. These acts are not tolerated by the school, and any student unwilling to cooperate will see the principal and would get penalized for their actions, suspended, or expelled (depending on extremity of their wrongdoing). There is a 100% graduation rate, and I'd say ~90% of the students in my class (2016) went on to college and graduated from a 4 year institution (not only state schools, but Ivy League as well). *Advice to students and parents who are looking into CCC, take a tour of the school, go on their website, and see what the school has to offer, and you wont regret it! Go Marauders! I’m going to try to make this as concise as possible so as to help others. The school has mostly good teachers. It is smaller which has benefits but also means less choices with classes etc. It has the same challenges in regard to behavior and students as other private and better public magnet programs in the area. My child is in all honors/IB classes, the workload is lighter than public IB, as one parent described it “It’s IB light”— that could be helpful if your child is not up to the very heavy workload and challenge in public IB. (I’ve had an older child at Largo IB and Osceola.). My personal recommendation is try to get into Osceola!! I would consider CCC on par with other private schools in the area and less desirable than a better magnet public programs—IB or Fundamental. I was amazed at how unprofessional the admissions process is at this school. My son scored 90 on the entrance exam and had good grades. We scheduled a private tour and the admissions director told my son he "knocked it out of the park" on the entrance exam and was a shoe-in to be admitted. He even brought the principal out to meet him.Then friends of his with lower grades and lower entrance exam scores started getting letters of acceptance. My wife called and we were told this was because they took the entrance exam before my son. My wife called again a few weeks later and was told "other parents were more persistent than you" and "the squeaky wheel gets the grease."My wife reminded him of what he'd told us before and he said the admissions process wasn't necessarily based on merit. He didn't say it but I strongly suspect that rich kids are accepted first. It all worked out fine in the end because my son was admitted to Jesuit, which is a much better school anyway. Our child chose this school based on reputation, and we have been pleasantly surprised with it. Neither my husband or I are alumni, which does seem to be very important in the acceptance process. We did experience a bit of delay in our child's acceptance regardless of their top test scores and prior academic performance, but that was resolved through follow up with admissions.As with most schools, the quality of instruction varies by teacher. CCC does have some great ones, who not only know their subjects, but they are also kind and empathetic to the needs of their students. The clear priority at CCC is college acceptance. One of the surprising characteristics of the school was how welcoming it was to our child who did not attend one of the local Catholic middle schools. On their first day at school, many of the students introduced themselves and invited them to sit with them at lunch. The school does have friend groups, but they don't seem to have bullies. Sports are important at CCC. Do you need to play sports at CCC to enjoy your high school experience? No. Would it help you make friends? Sure. Are their other options to build peer relationships? Absolutely. Theater, arts, clubs, volunteering, study abroad trips and student council are also available and encouraged.Overall, we remain highly satisfied with our child's decision to attend CCC.

column3: Faculty are biased, discriminatory and incompetent. One day while on campus for my son I witnessed some old guy on a golf cart suspend a young man for running home to get a book needed for class. He was almost to the doors when the tardy bell rang, but he got suspended anyway. That same guy is always sitting outside of my neighbors house harrassing all the students that go there for lunch. I can only assume that somewhere in the past, a student from this neighborhood caused some trouble and now all the kids that live here are treated poorly because of it. Many of the rockbrook kids are suspended for trivial reasons, so much that they end up dropping out because of attendance failure. Academically, though, the school has a lot to offer. Just don't live near it. EXCELLENT AP PROGRAM PREPARING STUDENTS FOR HIGHER EDUCATION. THE CAMPUS AND FACULTY ARE TOP NOTCH....A++++ KEEP UP THE GREAT WORK My son started school here, fall 2011. We chose to go here over another local high school because of the ratings it receives in Newsweek - a rating this school is very proud of - and after talking with staff members who would work with our son. It probably is a great school if your child does not need special services, or if your child does not have IEP. Since this fall, I have had one dropped ball after another - literally over 5 situations which should never, ever have happened. Thankfully, we are moving and we will be putting our son back in a school where we used to live, but since he started here, I have met 4 other families who have taken their child out of Lincoln, or have chosen to Home School, rather than choose to send their child to Lincoln (because of their Special Ed Program)- and these are just people I have met outside of school - church and parents from one of my other children's school. If you look at Lincoln, ask LOTS of questions, and be prepared for a fight. They do not like strong parent advocates. I could expand, but it is our personal story. Hopefully, yours will be more positive. I went to 4 different high school during my time in school, and enjoyed my senior year at Lincoln very much. THe administration was very strict with their discipline, but if youre not doing anything wrong you have nothing to worry about. This school had by far the best teachers of all my high schools, as i still talk to a few and ask them for help with college assignments. It is in a bad neighborhood, which is probably why the administrator was harrassing those kids another commentor was reffering to. In my graduating class, we had several kids get substantial scholarships to major universities (UF, UNC, Harvard to name a few). This is by far the best school in Tallahassee. Though a couple administrators are very uptight, overall Lincoln has a relaxed atmosphere. All of my teachers are always available to answer questions and are willing to do whatever it takes to help a student. The AP program is pretty great and I've done really well in all the AP courses I took there. The teachers are amazing and the campus is large and well maintained (for the most part). Though Lincoln has a bad rep in town, I've never felt in danger of any violence. I have two children at this school. It is very large, but very well managed. It is chock full of fantastic teachers who really care about the progress the students are making. They strive to prepare students for the next step - whether that be college or a job. There are plenty of activities and clubs to be a part of. The administration has just updated their website, so communication if better than ever. I consider it the best choice for a well-rounded educational experience. Although there are a few dedicated teachers at this school, administrators seem unable or, worse, unwilling to address issues relevant to the course selection process at the start of the school year. Parents and students must wait an interminably long amount of time in order to make minor changes to a schedule. I went to Lincoln high school in the late 90's, and things were getting bad then I can't even imagine it in 2017....lol. But it is in a bad area. But the teacher's I had were great. If your child is going to need special education this isn't a school I would recommend. I remember the staff riding on a golf cart. So they are strict but understandably so. The neighborhood is enough in itself. I no longer live in Florida, I moved back to New York several years ago. As a parent now the special education need's is very common. As a New Yorker the education system here is like night and day to public education in the south. I was a year ahead of my grade because the North's school system is better. However I had a blast at Lincoln high school. If your child doesn't need special education this is a great school to attend. #GoTrojans :) Overall, my experience here was quite abysmal. Lazy teachers seem to be the main culprit here, as well as rampant racism and all-out disrespect students have towards each other, staff, and their environment.

column1: Adams Central provided my children with an excellent education and plenty of opportunities to explore their potential. Students for the most part care about their education and are committed to doing their best. Teachers work hard and care about their students, extremely professional. What more can you ask for? They challenge the students and provide them with the necessary opportunities to reach their goals. Students are disciplined when appropriate to do so. Office staff is extremely positive and helpful and communication with parents is what it should be. Technology continues to improve and updated. Parents work with school officials and teachers and are supportive. Thumbs up for AC! The best private, public school in America.

column3: School spirit is good. Leadership and community involvement is strongly encouraged. HHS is very strong in the arts and have a lot of talented students. Academics is average. This should be recognized and addressed. Wonderful school. Best educational system. Best guidance counselor, always willing to assist parent and student. howell high is a great school to be in. i just wish that some of the extra curricular activities would recieve some more of the credit they deserve I am a student right now here and honestly I wouldn't wish to be anywhere else. Our school spirit is great, we always support each other when a student is in need. The teachers are AMAZING, I don't know where I would be today without some of my teachers, they really guide you and help you through whatever you are going through. We have the FPAC program and that's the only flaw I could say about this school, our school favors FPAC a lot. But other then that, no drugs, bullying, or gangs are tolerated here and I know I am honestly gonna cry when I graduate here. Once a rebel always a rebel, Go Howell Rebels!!!! very good i love this school go howell rebels Excellent, prepared me for my next chapter in life

column1: I went to lincoln unfortunalty i had to move but i would give anything to go back to it. The teachers are great. Especially Mr.Nyland. Hes my favorite teacher. The food is good, and i love the school so much. Most people think its a really bad school but its not as bad as everyone thinks. Its actually good, the test scores are going up. I LOVE LINCOLN!! I am currently going to Lincoln and I've had a pretty big amount of problems. There are so many smokers that there is an actual corner where they go to smoke. The teachers range from pretty good to really bad. The kids are very loud and very morally corrupt. However, if your kid is a guy the classes are great and seem to be tailored towards guys (classes such as woodshop, JROTC, etc.) Lincoln has more AP offerings than any school in the district. They have the best welding and construction trades programs in Pierce County. Senior last year won more than $1.2 million in scholarships. Lincoln high school sucks! Just bc it's a low income neighborhood doesn't mean that education should also be dummed down.. There is not enough staff and to many unlocked doors for kids to walk off campus. I would avoid Lincoln all together! Absolutely amazing! I have heard nothing but positive and encouraging comments!! Great had a wonderful experience all 4 years Our 4 children attended Lincoln & now all are college grads & in professional careers. We now have grandchildren attending & they are receiving a great educational experience. There are many advanced placement classes to choose from along with a wide selection of extracurricular activities.

column3: If you can afford to live in the beautiful homes of Strongsville, most definitely do so! The High School is excellent with a superior 300 member band program that my son loved, he was in all honors classes which helped him to receive a wonderful ivy league college scholarship. Excellent school! Strongsville is a very upscale city with everything to offer! Beautiful homes,classy merchants and restaurants but most of all wonderful schools! We moved here from California and our $550,000 home is a mansion here compared to LA! Our daughter is in the Strongsville HS Band program which rivals ANY college! its just excellent! Her honors classes also challenge her to the fullest! We are so happy we chose Strongsville as our home! stronsgsvillehighschool is over crowded i had 90 kid in one class it was a not diversity at all or open to new ideas and the dances where terrible and it was a lot of inappropriate things going on at the school when i told my mother what was really going on there she is transferring me now and she was at the school every day for some reason like racism or people stealing my stuff and if you need some type of help learning you wont get it there and allot of kids have emotional problems This school/district is not what e veryone makes it to be. The high school is so crowded that the students are just a number. There is no help from teachers and or staff. I pulled my son out after 1 semester in the 9th grade. He was an B student at middle schI ool, then when moved to the high school the grades dropped and he fell through the cracks, I never received any callls until it was too late. I enrolled him in online public school and the grades came up and I could be more involved in his schooling. Pulling my boys out of Strongsville CIty Schools was the best decision. Can't wait to move out of this snobby city. Worst place to livel. When I was a student 7 years ago, I would totally agree with the 9/10 rating. But based on the disgusting actions of the teachers during the recent strike, I would say the place is a 0/10. I looked at Chicago last year and thought to myself, "That would never happen in Strongsville. Our community is too cohesive and our teachers care about their students." That was before these teachers started berating substitutes "who dared" to fill in for the classes they weren't teaching (you know, the same substitutes they have relied on for years to pick up their slack on sick days and vacation days), before they started to trash the classrooms of teachers "who dared" to cross the picket line and TEACH, before they acted like animals while crying, "It's for the children" (Ha!). MANY (nearly all) teachers that I had while I was a student, were all active during this pathetic display. I have lost all respect for the school (No, not the board. The board didn't make them act the way they did.) since this strike occurred. These teachers even tried to manipulate their students to use them for their sick games. No thanks SHS, you're not what you used to be. High school was okay but learning experience. I love the teacher and make like in home . The principal all kind and respectful. Please come in school

column1: meh. Its an ok school. At least it is better then Sandride. Amazing school! The teachers, principal and staff truly care. The whole city lives and supports the school. My daughter thrived!

column3: Central Kitsap High School maintains a very welcoming environment. On the first day I transferred in, I was very surprised to have the students shake my hand and welcome me to the class. I was instantly introduced, which was refreshing and inviting. Previously, I was a shy student who was very nervous about transferring to a new school after experiencing isolation from another school in the district. However, at Central Kitsap, I felt like the transition was natural and I felt truly welcomed into the community. The students at this school seem to be very open and friendly to newer students. The teachers and staff are also very helpful to students. They approach students politely and kindly. There is an abundance of higher level and AP courses to challenge students who want to be pushed academically. Regardless of the high level classes available, there is a noticeable gap in motivation of a standard requirement class and a higher level or AP class. This, however, depends on the teacher, as some teachers in the standard requirement level have higher expectations of students and give them equal standards. Overall, CK is a great school with several academic opportunities. We specifically moved into the CK school district so my children would attend CKHS. My boys both graduated from CKHS and are sailing through their second semester in college. Awesome, because the Wholesome, Edgy, Normie, and Dank Memes were with the school. I enjoyed the staff as people but as teachers, not so much. They do a poor job of preparing students for the future, as well as "picking favorites". Amazing opportunities within the magnet program. Lots of AP classes offered. They just opened this brand new facility.

column1: This school has changed for the better! I am the proud parent of a scholar who recently graduated with honors at this school. The teachers and principal motivate the students to succeed. If your child needs help in any academic the teachers make time for them. The guidance counselor helped me place my child into a great high school. The teachers reward the students with trips and prizes which gives them motivation to succeed. It also shows the students that with hard work you will be rewarded with a great job or promotion or any goal that your child is striving to achieve. I recommend this school to anyone who wants the best education in a middle school for their child. Amazing! They have a great principal and my child is happy to go to school. I would never recommend anyone put their children in this school. This school has a very poor communication system, the adults cant handle constructive criticism who a nasty attitude, they are allowed to put your children in restraints and holds without yr consent, they are their own bullies to these children, they rush through lessons not giving the children or parents the time to absorb what they are learning, the give the children no time to eat breakfast in the am uf the bus is late they have only 10m to put their things away get their food nd sit dwn and eat. Not to mention they get whats left. They lie to parents in their faces. Id rather u talk to my child how u talk tp them when im not there rather then act like your so nice when the parent is present. My child had to get in multiple fights and once b suspended for defending herself before they removed the problem from the bus. They DO NOT take accountability for their own actions!!! This school needs to shut down i have absolutely nothing positive to say about this school except that alot of them are not leaders and are guiding our children down the wrong path -1% This has not been a great experience, teachers calling about incidents saying my child was involved but denying the call when I contacted administration about it(because it wasnt true). No communication when you reach out thru email or jupiter ed. No communication when your concerned about your child's grades. I dont agree with placing "alternatives students" in the same class setting with honors students. I dont agree with the teachers not having to take the same state mandated test that teachers in the public schools have to take before being hired. I dont agree with 10 minutes to eat lunch because the teachers hold the entire class due to 1 students misbehavior. I dont agree with so much emphasis on complete uniform (and in-house suspension of they're not) when teachers are coming to work intoxicated or reeking of substances. I dont agree with 9hr school days and 4hrs of homework per night. I dont agree with NO recess or gym classes. They have a great curriculum but I dont agree with them now having to alter it so that it's made easier for the children with learning impairments. This is not a good school and if your a good parent you'll do the work to find that out! 8/10, my kids have been here 2 years and are just as successful here as they have been at any suburban schools prior to FPE and FPM. They have maintained their scholar performance at FPM Camden, NJ.

column3: At the time of this review, the administrators only care for their own personal agendas and not whats best for the community. Both sports and academics are on the decline. Passing and graduation rates are now skewed with the creation of The Big Picture to pull out kids who were in danger of dropping out or low on test scores. Majority of the teachers in district are there for the kids and are great. There are a handful that do come off as just there for the money. Just not the same school that I graduated from in 2004.

column1: This school is great in so many ways, but this is the time of year that I get so upset about their very, very long school supply list! Their list also have very specific, brand name things that are so hard to find. And when we already pay tuition? Please do one of several things: Add about $30 more to tuition and have a no school supply list- give the teachers the money and they buy in bulk online everything they want. Or- give the teachers a little i.e. $100-200 and they can go get the specific brand name things and the students have a much shorter list. Or- have club fundraisers where parents at least can have the choice of paying i.e. $35 for the 3rd grade school supply pack and save hours of store hopping headaches. It's so nice to have such and advanced Christian school in the 50th most educated state, but please, please, stop this back to school nightmare! Nampa Christian is a part of our family. With two children who have attended since they were in Pre-K and 1st grade we felt the calling to make the financial sacrifice and the rewards have been immeasurable. Our kids have been challenged academically, grown spiritually, and enjoyed the opportunity to participate in the sports they love. Nampa Christian is truly an extension of our Christian home and its unique environment has been a blessing for our family. The administration is overbearing and male top heavy. Half of the people working there don't even do their jobs. There's no guidance counselor to help high schoolers with choosing a college or helping with ACT or SAT. They care more about the dress code than they do about the kids learning in class. Since the administration is all men, they don't understand how hard it can be for a girl to dress modestly. The board fires teachers for no legitimate reasons and just says "See ya!" because they have a new teacher picked out already. The teachers get paid practically nothing no matter how long they've been working there. The grading system is screwed up so good luck. Do not send your kids to this school if you want them to not hate their lives everyday. Doesn't even deserve one star. My children have attended Nampa Christian elementary, middle and high schools. They have received an excellent education but more importantly they have learned how to be good citizens and have grown in their faith. They have been given opportunities to excel in athletics, leadership, drama, choir and art. Over the years the pendulum has swung a little bit back and forth with certain issues, dress code being the biggest issue, but when you consider all the BIG picture things, I wouldn't trade their time at NCS for anything! I have had the joy of interacting with Nampa Christian Schools as a pastor in the community for the past eight years. We have had a good number of our families connected with this school as students, parents, and staff. NCS has had a positive impact on their lives. Investing in your child to get a Christian education is exactly that-an investment. Both of my children have attended NCS since kindergarten. I am so grateful that there is a Christ centered school that teaches the same values at school as we do at home. Don't you want that for your children? There is no such thing as a perfect school but I know without a doubt that God's hand is on this school and that the staff truly care about their students. I feel very blessed that my children are able to attend this school. Our son completed his senior year in 2020. He was able to attend classes with his classmates for the last two weeks of their high school career, on campus. He will be having live, in person, traditional graduation ceremony in a few weeks. As a result of his Christian mentoring and excellent education with Nampa Christian Schools, our son will be attending a top Christian University this fall having received that Universities' highest level of academic scholarships. This is the right and best school in Canyon County Idaho, from PreK-12, if you are looking for your child to grow and be well mentored in their Christian World View, their academic prowess and their physical abilities. We look for a new Christian school for my kid, so we chose Nampa Christian school. Since we are new to the Idaho area and not involve to any church activities yet, we still are hard study at home with all the Christian knowledge esp during the pandemic time. We got the interview at that time and the administration told us they even don't have any regular art teachers for the school for their elementary school though it is a big size school around Nampa area.The school rejected our enrollment the next day because we don't go to church often. And we went to other similar school nearby which is more friendly and more better service to the parents. The stuffs in NCS are lack of education and arrogant. Bullying and not following apparent school policies by administration kids and leadership kids is frequently hidden and covered up. Massive double standards to take your money and pump out a terribly odd percentage of valedictorians that often end up dropping out of college. Would definitely not recommend this school to anyone. Try Cole Valley or Ambrose anytime first before you try this school. I do not think either of those could be any worse than the things that happen at this school if you are looking for something that says it is a Christian school. Hopefully theirs is much better and actually does what they say they will do. Policies and what they tell you when you meet with them in the interview really means nothing. It is just to get you in the door and make you think your kid will be in a good environment. Then when the rubber meets the road there is no follow through. Definitely try one of the other schools first. This school has a caring administration staff along with many caring teachers. My only frustration has been with the varsity volleyball program. The current program encourages more of a cheerleading mentality and seems to be biased against steady, consistent, thinking athletes. A coach should never elevate players who cheer louder while demoting the quieter ones simply because they're more introverted. The team motto, "Faith over Feelings", seems quite ironic in light of all of this. I was a student at this school, and I got to say this was one of the worst times of my life is because they don't prepare us for collage and the people in the school were really mean to people of color. And I saw other people make a mistake and a whole decades worth of relationship went down the drain because the people here don't really care for mental needs. It's a huge cash grab everything fun you want to do you have to pay for it. The teachers some are better than others. Nampa Christian is just a school that needs fixen. They expel people based on what they believe. There also really insecure if you go against there brand and will do stuff to you if you say stuff. And they cover up stuff they did to make them not sound like a bad school as a student these were the worst years of my life. Don't take what I said personally is just a review.

column3: This was once a great school, unfortunately the changes made by the principal who took over in 2007/08 school year, it has progressively gone downhill. The ego of the community, due to a higher income level, believe it is still a good school. The good teachers have all left. My older child graduated in 2006 when the school deserved its high rating, my youngest child who will graduate this year-2011, left for another district high school and is receiving an excellent senior year! We are grateful to be out of this ego inflated district. This place is good. No drugs, everyone helps. Good classes, nice principle, nice parents. I think it is a great place to students. This is obviously a good nice school. The facilities are and building are great, the kids are smart, the teachers seem very engaging. On the downside, language programs have been cut. For example, you can take Chinese but not French for entering freshmen. But Chinese is too difficult for most students to do well in. The sports program (for girls at least) seem to be in need of cash all the time. Finally, there is of course the appeal to snobbery. One of the "selling" points of the school is that the students generally come from privileged homes... so they have better material to work with ... something a teacher told me. This implies that we live in a pure meritocracy and that people who are poor are so because they lake certain mental gifts. I think that attitude is prevalent but misguided at CFHS. Try to get beyond the snobbery and send your child here anyway... it will be a good experience. Not the best, not the worst. This school is constantly crying poverty while its administrators spend loads on "educational trips" Most beautiful campus in Tucson, as well as a challenging and diverse education. Without saying, Foothills has the most beautiful campus in Tucson. The curriculum here is without doubt the best in Tucson as far as public education goes. You also have a wide variety of choices when it comes to picking classes (6 english courses are available per grade). The teachers are very engaging in class and are always willing to assist with anything from academics to personal issues. The administration is also very experienced and credible, and keep the school together. The only negative about the school is that most students do unfortunately act the typical Foothills stereotype. Most people are white and rich, but they are mostly friendly and very nice. Foothills also has the most expansive, credible, and highest achieving fine arts program when compared to any other high school in town. The band is the largest in Arizona, and has traveled the world; traveling to Disneyland, the Beijing Olympics, Australia, Macy's Thanksgiving Parade, Prescott, and more. The theatre program is very well known in Tucson as well. The school has excellent students and teachers, particularly in Math and English. The quality of Science teachers have declined markedly- the best ones have moved on. Some of the best teachers have been reallocated against their wishes- from subjects they taught extremely well to assignments they are unhappy about these remaining quality teachers will inevitably leave and add to this continuing decline. The Board needs to step in. The school has excellent students and teachers in Math and English. The quality of Science teachers has declined markedly- the best ones have moved on- as shown by declining test scores. The academic focus over the last year or two in particular has markedly diminished, with the departure of quality teachers. Some of the remaining excellent teachers have been reallocated apparently against their wishes- from subjects they taught extremely well to assignments they are unsuited to and are clearly unhappy about these remaining few first-rate teachers will inevitably leave and add to this continuing slide. Standards are clearly slipping and there appears to be a lack of leadership- the Board needs to step in and fix the rot. My son has just graduated this year and I will watch for positive developments in the immediate future, but am not optimistic- we may be forced to send our younger child to a different school in the future. The District Board needs to step in. We just spent the last ten years at CFHS as our three children went through the school. The teachers were top notch and the curriculum challenging and relevant. The depth and the breadth of classes, programs, and activities are unrivaled in Tucson. The entire staff and administration care about the students, and parents are very involved in supporting the school. Students are engaged in learning as well as the numerous extra-curricular activities and events. The campus and the views of the surrounding area are beautiful. Catalina Foothills is a school that claims outstanding academics but bury themselves with appearance and money. Foothills is more focused on dealing with security forces than improving academic programs. The education you get is pretty average it is just in an upscale community. Extra curricular activities and specific departments such as math are weak but the district does not care to recognize that. Everyone seems to enjoy lying to themselves and blaming the state for lack of funding. They would rather hire more security staff with a student body that is 70 percent White....Catalina Foothills gets more credit than it deserves because of the lack of education standards in the state of Arizona. Go outside of Arizona, and this school is quite average. That is why 70% of kids end up at a state college because it is essentially a free ride. Arizona state colleges are required to admit just about anyone and everyone a resident of Arizona. I see these problems transferring from a stronger school system out of state. This is the best public high school in Tucson because you don't have a lot of choices. Do not expect amazing support here. This school is descending quite quickly. This latest poster is so uninformed. Most of the students from CFHS do not go to in state schools. There is a high % of the class of 2014 going out of state to some of the most outstanding universities in the country including ivy leagues. Catalina Foothills High is more concerned about "security" and "dresscode" than they are about actually educating students. Most of the faculty and administrators are horrible and discriminate against girls, and let male students do and wear whatever they want. I wouldn't recommend sending any female, or male students, for that matter, to this school. On a side note, the principal repeatedly does not reply to parents when called, or if someone asks to scedule a meeting, she will not comply. This school has gotten progressively worse since my freshman year. The security has increased by tenfold this year even though it's completely unnecessary. A fence now surrounds the school. Former students and parents are no longer allowed to visit teachers. It is a completely closed off campus. Security is constantly patrolling and monitoring students. Everyone must have their ID with them at all times in order to enter campus. If you forget it, you have to pay $5 to get a new one for the day (no exceptions). The school uses an absurd rubric to grade homework that is complicated and confusing (4.0-A+, 3.0-B, 2.5-C etc) instead of the standard, straightforward letter grades. Most people go to an in-state school (a number of them get scholarships). Only a handful go to private colleges (a few even go to top-tier schools). The only reason that more students from this school go onto prestigious schools is because the people who live in this district are wealthy. The teachers are okay and the academics are not especially exemplary. The administration is power-hungry and it's gotten so strict under the current principal. Thankfully, I'm a senior and will be graduating this year. All things considered, Catalina Foothills is a pretty good school. Sports/extracurriculars are pretty good such as the Speech and Debate team, Science Olympiad, etc. Academics are average, however. Some departments are better than others and of course, quality of teachers vary. The math department is ok, with the Calculus BC teacher being outstanding (99.9999% of students that took the AP test have scored a 4 or higher, only one student has ever gotten a 3). Although the administration isn't the best, overall, CFHS is a pretty good school considering it is public and has no entrance requirements. Im a freshman at this school. It has been really fun and really hard. I have a learning disability and ADD... My math teacher has been really helpful and fair to me and she is the best teacher I have ever had because she doesn't just lecture you the whole entire hour. I feel as though the whole math department is similar. Im in band and the band program is impeccable, We got a superior with distinction at UofA Band day (marching band competitions) and a superior at NAU band day. We also march in the Rodeo parade on 4th Ave down town and we have won the highest music award over 20 years in a row. We also get to travel around a lot. Last year we went to China for a parade. We've gone to Russia, Hawaii, and London, and many more. Band is a major part of my life, and the pure love of music is spread all around the band and all of the kids are extremely dedicated. Band is my family really, we all are so close. Ive heard similar things about the theater program and the choir program and also student council as well. It feels awesome to be with people who are passionate about the same thing you are. Overall I really enjoy Cat Foot! Unfortunately I might have to move to San Antonio Texas A school with poor leadership can not excel. More concerned with appearances than substance. Girls are given the burden of adhering a strict dress code while boys are given the power to harass. The education is just ok. They only teach one way so if that does not work for you do not expect anyone to think creatively. Just because you put "creative thinkers" on your digital street side leader board does not make it so. The staff I have worked with have lacked this very skill. We moved from out of state and have discovered Excellent school really means excellent for Arizona. I removed my child from this school. The "Preview" Method of teaching math is absolutely the worst method I have ever encountered in education. Basically, the student is supposed to teach themselves. There is no teaching. And the "teaching" that is going on is far from exemplary. The math teacher doesn't even know how to solve some of the problems…and my child is expected to learn how to do the problem when the teacher cannot do it?? Adequate education. Math Dept. clearly needs improvement--many kids failing Math. This high school is clean and safe. There is a good selection of extra-curricular activities. This school is similar to many others in Tucson and provides a satisfactory education. As a low income student with a long commute to school, I have been treated awful. I would never send an under-privileged student here with hopes of getting ahead in education. My students each found their lane at Catalina Foothills High School. There are opportunities for all students to succeed, no matter what they are interested in. As a person of color, it's SO hard here. column1: Administrators do not respond well to parents concerns all they do is sugar coat it. Teachers are more of a joke than anything This school doesn't deserve the blue ribbon status. The teachers and administrators care more about appearences than the students. Any student problems are ignored and parent involvement is not welcome and is limited to getting funding for the school. The attitude that my son has encountered is that he 'just might not college material'. As a teacher and parent, this is unacceptable. The staff at Southern High School went above and beyond to ensure that myself and many other students graduated with an understanding of the wide variety of courses that were taught there. Friendly and firm, they guided me throughout all four years that I was there and helped me graduate with pride. Go Southern Bulldogs!!! I have been very pleased with the education that my son has gotten at Southern. My older daughter went through 12 years of pricey prep schools when we were living in another country with more problematic schools. I believe that the education at Southern has been richer than her experiences. The art and music programs are outstanding. He has had the opportunity to take a variety of AP courses, which is unheard of in some other counties. My son has a physical disability and his administrator tracks his progress and often writes to me if he feels that he is slipping in any area. I do believe if you just check the grammar in some of the parent and student responses giving negative reviews you will see that it needs a little work. Just saying ,,,,, the people who are complaining may REALLY not be college material. Southern High School is a unique to say the least. The administrators there are horrible and practically suffocate the students. Parent involvement is not welcome whatsoever. Bullying at that school is out of control and is not taken seriously. The school is filled with sex, drugs, and alcohol. Its as if the faculty and staff there are ignoring things that should be brought to attention. My child is a freshman there and once this year is over, I'm taking him to a better school. I am not happy with the atmosphere of this school. I am currently a tenth grader at Southern High. I understand what most people are saying in the comments. Southern is a joke. Most of the teachers here could care less whether you fail or pass. All they want is a paycheck. But there are like 5 or 6 teachers here that actually want to see you go above and beyond and become something better. I had a teacher that told me if I didn't like the assignment we were doing in class I could sit there and fail. I never said I didn't want to do it. I was just asking a question that he didn't like about it. But as a teacher, I feel like you're suppose to want me to succeed. But he could've cared less about what I did. I have three children who went to Southern for all four years. My oldest is a graduate of Clemson University and is a Mechanical Engineer working for Bosch. My second offspring earned an accounting degree from Virginia Tech and is a CPA at BB&T. My third has an Industrial and Systems Engineering degree also from VA Tech and is now in the naval flight school at Pensacola. I am not trying to boast but I believe Southern did a good job preparing my children for the next level. It has the advantages of a smaller school but provides ample opportunity for students to pursue a variety of interests. Amazing small town feel. Loving teachers who care about their students and their future. The school needs to be updated. The staff needs to be put in place and do their job to make the students feel heard and understood regardless the situation. The students are fending for themselves because you either walk on or get walked on. The school as a whole is not somewhere I'd send my child if I was a parent. Trying to help shape a more inclusive community This is a great school that is tied into the community. This is a great school that still has a small town feel. The community supports it and the teachers are mostly a part of the community. Supportive faculty and staff, well mannered students, academically challenging.

The academic programs were challenging, the teachers were kind and helpful, and there were extra curricular activities for all interests. Overall I found it to be an accepting and wonderful place. First, most of the teachers I have encountered have been very knowledgeable in their subject area and most have a good attitude. However, I have, so far, had a couple who, while still very knowledgeable, are not the person you would want teaching you child. This is because of their attitude. I don't think either one of them should be running a school. I have had doors slammed in my face by them and been spoken to as though they are better than sliced bread. I would not recommended this administration to any school in the country. Overall, the school has it's ups and downs and the students are great. In fact, he took away the percussion room and gave them a tiny room that barely has any room to put stuff into. The athletic director also hates the cheerleaders so they're in the same boat as the band. Most of the teachers here are amazing at what they do, but some of them don't even care or want to do.

The 8 rating is misleading because it includes lower grades. Look at the high school breakdown, and you will see a better reflection. They are very bias and when it comes to sports they play buddy ball There's something so special about a K-12 school! All the students are loved on and cared for! Eagleville School is such a great place to send your kids. ALL grades K-12 are encourage to connect through the school and the community. School is too focused on sports and not academics.
