column3: Lake Zurich is a mostly privileged area with no gangs or horrible drug problems. However there are no real resources for kids with a struggling home life, mental illness, mental disability, struggling academically, or being bullied, although it has PLENTY of money to support these issues that need attention. Things are swept under the rug, for example when someone in the school or community commits suicide or even in a much less serious situation like if the football team loses, they just don't address it and pretend it didn't happen. The staff are not people you will want to come back and visit since they are often not personally invested and often judgmental, thriving off of gossip and scolding "bad seeds" instead of investigating the real cause behind a young person's actions. The teachers are average, some are wonderful, but it's the office staff and administrators that are usually not pleasant. Teachers that can teach are few and far between. Too make up for this they assign a lot of homework. After carefully reviewing many of the local communities, we chose to move to this school district several years ago. We've been very happy with the results. The teachers are dedicated and attentive to the students and what needs to be taught. Great electives are offered both in the middle schools and high school. The community itself has a welcoming, home town atmosphere, and that carries over to the students' attitudes. Excellent programs are offered in foreign language, music, drama, art, business and engineering as well as all the honors and AP programs. Class levels are offered to address all the needs of the students, and the teachers are equally attentive to struggling students. We have experienced quite a few phenomenal teachers who really go the extra mile to make sure their students master their subjects. As a former school teacher, I expect a lot from a school district, and I have been very pleased with what we've found in Lake Zurich. The ones below this are my husbands and sons. We need to spread the word to save other families from having their children have a horrible high school experience. Excellent for my three sons. Always looking for ways to further improve. This is an excellent high school with great teachers, great programs, and a focus on college preparedness. The athletics program is high level with many athletes being accepted and winning scholarships to great universities. Excellent Facility with great teachers and programs. Performing arts center second to none. High school football field made of field turf one of the first in the state. Kids prepared for their choice of colleges.

column1: I have attended South Lamar since 9th grade and I am relieved to finally be graduating. This is a terrible school. Unless your child has attended the school since young age or has attended other schools nearby. They will be left out of everything. If you arent popular winning anything is out of the question. Sometimes winning things helps out with scholarships. but you will not find these oppurtunitys here. Nobody gets along in this school either. Everyone acts like they get along but they talk about each other like they dogs. Education and teachers are terrible also. Unless your popular or well known you might as well forget any other teachers bendin over backwards for you. they do not care. Honestly this is not a good school and i do not recommened it. I am a student at South Lamar High, I have gone to SSouth Lamar since the Kindergarten, and I just love it. Everybody gets along, most of the tme. There is some drama, but which school doesn't have drama. The teachers always find time to help you out. I would recommend this school to anybody! I am a graduate of South Lamar. First of all any education is what you choose to get out of it. If you like to party and not focus on the curriculum then yes, I say you won't learn. However, if you study and are willing to do the work and ASK questions I found that the teachers are willing to help, but there are one or two that is the exception. Every school, business, etc. has cliques. Being popular (or having "the last name") will win you pageants and homecoming and earn you playing time in sports but that's everywhere also. It's all about who you know, especially in the business world. But I received a quality education from SLS and graduated from the University of Alabama. There are many more success stories like mine from the students that did the work and tried to learn while at SLS. For those that thought school was a joke well most of them are unemployed, in jail, or on drugs. So it's what you make of it. And the gossiping and bullying are part of life. Kids need to learn to ignore what doesn't matter and stand up for themselves. SLS makes announcements every morning, often the lack of communication is from the students not relaying the info to the parents. I went to SLS starting in the 8th grade and left as soon as I got my drivers license. Some of the teachers there are ok, and the rest only care about the "last names". It is a very cliquey school and if you didn't sart there in kindergarten than you will never fit in. I moved to Vernon and my grades improved along with my self confidence. It is a much better school, much less trouble. I graduated in 2002 in the Beta Club and got 3 degrees from UofA. Now my 14 year old sister is getting bullied at SLS and is talking "ending her life because she can't take the bullying". We have talked to the teachers, the principal and the parents but nothing has changed. It is a really sad situation. I hate to say it, but it looks like something that drastic might be the only thing that will snap this school (which isn't even accredited) back into reality. We will be transferring my sister to LCHS next semester. I graduated from this school, have a mother who has taught at this school since it opened, and have also substitute taught at this school and I must say that I will send my children here gladly. It is a small school with small class sizes. It is an environment where the child can know everyone in their class and the classes around their same age. The teachers are, for the most part, fair and interested in helping your child. There are very few fights and I have never felt threatened in the school as a student or as faculty. They have recently hired a lot of new, young teachers that are very enthusiastic about their jobs and excited for their students. All in all, South Lamar is not a perfect school, but I feel it is a safe environment of adults that want to help your children learn, if your children are willing and ready to do their fair share of the work. They also have a good athletic program, especially for girls, with coaches that care more about their players than winning ball games. As far as the allegations of cliques, people are always quick to say this, however, I challenge you to find a school who has no cliques and have fun getting your child into that school.

column3: A challenging curriculum, an excellent staff and wonderful students make Mentor High School an outstanding institution. We are always striving to evolve while becoming an even better school system. I am fortunate to have been a staff member for the past 15+ years and I am looking forward to continuing in this capacity for many more years. I go to this school and I love it! I'm not a so called popular kid but that doesn't matter.This school is so different compared to other schools There are not as strong of clicks as other schools. May people mingle from different groups o friends. There is a wide course selection for students who need help to others that find school easy and need to be challenged. Students are also able to take college courses during high school for free. That means you can get college credit for free! Also, we have a large marching band, 200+, and your not "uncool" if you take it. Almost all of the football and basketball player are in the band. Clubs range from theatre, to a video game club. There is also and anime club, gay pride club, ecology club, math club, yearbook, a youtube channel making club called film Fridays, a photography club, writing club, mock trial, swimming team, science Olympiad, top 25 which is a singing group, and there are others too. But if there is a club they do not have you can make your own with help from the office. There are guidance councilors to take anytime and refused lunch programs. The teachers really care. If you have a chance come to this school. I just started going here and I would say that the school is okay. It's very good education wise but none of the students try to make new friends. All of them are majorly antisocial outside of their group of friends and it's annoying. As a current senior student here, I can honestly say the past several years at this school have been the best of my life so far. Between the friends and memories made in clubs and activities to the supportive staff and challenging curriculum, I do not have a single complaint. Mentor High is the epitome of strong AAA schools--Academics, Athletics, and Arts. Each has strong programs that are thoroughly supported by school and district administration, and recognition at state and national levels has been achieved by many school organizations from Science Olympiad, Marching Band, National Merit Finalists, and athletics. Every single staff member goes above and beyond to ensure a positive, welcoming environment. I could not have asked for a better high school experience and am extremely prepared for college and life beyond. Truly outstanding services to the students. Countless clubs, organization, extracurriculars, sports, etc. Growth and advancement for students, faculty, technology are constant. Mentor he been awarded millions of dollars in grants due to being an exceptional district and the updates that they're making are state-of-the-art, even though, admittedly, the building is old and leaves something to be desired. Academically I give MHS a good rating. Both of my students liked the vast selection of courses and extracurriculars to choose from. They enjoyed having electives in their areas of interest. When choosing where to live in Lake County, it seemed to be the best choice.

Every teacher at MHS, past and present, are truly dedicated to the care and education of their students. I have read a lot of these posts and I can believe that they are all true. These things become more stressful when of culture of apathy has been allowed to seed, root, and grow. A culture of enabling that unintentionally grew out of an effort to nuture. These things happen. Now, GCPS is worki g to correct these issues. Give MHS a try, a hope, and your prayers. Do this for all GCPS schools. They all need your hope and support. Best school ! Top 20 in GA . My son loves it here . He actually gets an education & he met over 20 friends on the first day here ! Meadowcreek High School is a really great school to learn somthing new. The meadowcreek staff are really good they respect eachother. Home of Mustang Before my freshman year I was scared to go to this school because of its "bad reputation" but when I started school its wasn't at all how i thought it was! Its not the school that is bad like the teachers but some students just don't care about their education and make it seem that way. Yes there are fights but what school doesn't have them? Im in AP classes and i dont really see the difference. There are also many good sports, like Track, which I'm in(: Meadowcreek High School is a unique place. I have 2 sons that attended so I was involved from 2003 - 2012. And I definitely saw it go through changes and growing pains. Allow me to start with ANY school is as good as the parents involved. This area is full of rental properties due to repeated redistricting of another School district. I know of at least 3 event that place mire permanent residents in that district while drawing around all the rental apartments to stay with Meadowcreek. In general the Teachers care but there is just so much they can do and still teach. There have been plenty of successful student with high SAT scores and scholarships. The sports opportunities are there but the money to be really awesome isn't. Neither of my sons wanted to go to another school so we stayed with Meadowcreek. I became involved with the PTSA, The Band Booster, The Football Team and the Baseball team. Unfortunately you seem to see the same few parents at all the events. There isn't enough parental involvement to make this school as successful as some of the other schools. I was at the school so many times, several of the staff actually thought I worked there. Administration let two children walk out of their school knowingly and did not inform their parents. By the time these parents got out of work, they were the ones who called the school asking for their children in concern. Unfortunately the faculty and staff at Meadowcreek were not as willing to help them out as they should have. Instead every single staff and faculty member played the blame game and were of no help to the parents. It's really sad when you put so much trust into an educational system and the employees and they could care less about the well being of a child. "As a Meadowcreek High School Student I can say I love this high school! I would love to stay more years a mighty and proud Meadowcreek Mustang, fortunately the rumors of this school have been proven false, since I am on the track to graduating. This school has many great opportunities, and can lead you to a post-secondary education." -Junior of the Class of 2016! IT'S A GREAT SCHOOL. PEOPLE SHOULD STOP TRASHING IT SO MUCH. ESPECIALLY THE STUDENTS THAT CAUSE THE PROBLEMS & THE PARENTS THAT DON'T CARE ENOUGH TO KEEP THEIR KIDS OUT OF TROUBLE. This is the best school. It has 5 different departments and also works with our community to make sure we have everything we need. This school challenges you , and if you need something they are always there for you. This is the best school with the best students. I did not know what to expect because it is a large school, but the staff welcomed me and my daughter with open arms. My daughter is a gifted senior and I was worried that she would not get the attention needed to graduate and get into college. She was immediately enrolled in AP classes, (which her old GCPS school did not offer) and she received an academic scholarship to college. I am happy we made the move to Meaodwcreek, you can tell they care. It is a large school so as always their are a couple bad apples in the bunch, just contact the principal and he will take care of it . I have moved two of my nephews to the Meadowcreek area because of my daughters experience. I had my concerns when my son started in the school. So far I'm very impressed with rhe quality of the teaxhers and thw school programs. We love the school within the school program so much that we are going out of I school zone and driving them to school. I'm disappointed disorganization they have every year in the beginning of the year! You think that by know they have that to a science. But besides the headache of the beginning of the school yet everything else is great! I took my GED classes here . It seemed like a good place to learn . It's a great school, very diverse. Many students from different ethnic backgrounds. Food could be better, I do have to say, the only thing they seems to feed us often is chesseburgers. It's not a horrible school as others say that it is. People that say those things don't even attend Meadowcreek at all. People will question all the good that comes from Meadowcreek High School but believe the bad without a second thought. It's honestly quite a shame. There are so many things students can become a part of at this amazing school: swim, soccer, wrestling, Tennis, hope club, key club, culinary team and so much more. Meadowcreek my high school and I will always claim it as my school with pride. I'm extremely happy I will be graduating in the spring from this amazing school. Excellent, caring, hands-on administration and faculty. Each child is known and nurtured. Wow, I recently graduated and I miss Meadowcreek so much already! I am taking a summer program at my college and the classes remind me so much of AP classes I took in high school. I know Meadowcreek has a bad reputation, but I feel like the principal is really working to change that. There are so many student leadership organizations and clubs, and my peers are all amazing as well! If you find the right club and the right people to be friends with, you will have a great time here. There also so many teachers that I love and will never forget. Yes, sometimes Meadowcreek is unorganized, but I've found the good outweighs the bad. I truly appreciate all the staff and all of my peers for making my high school experience so fun! Thank you Meadowcreek, I will always bleed carolina blue! I graduated four years ago and throughout my time there many changes where made to provide many opportunities for the students to succeed in career goals, I graduated and continued my education at GSU. Once I left my sister entered and I was able to see her engage an many ways that allowed her to explore career choices and has just now graduated and will be attending Georgia State University this fall. Educators can't do it all. I'm missing a star because the PARENTS NEED TO BE MORE INVOLVED.

column1: faculty and staff tend to look the other way on bullying issues and therefore families either leave or deal with the issue on their own. Talented and gifted students are not challenged. Athletics are not supported by administration. Standard and Honors classes are pretty much the same. Parents are involved but do now truly welcome new parents or ideas in established "committees". Students are good at helping each other out and a source of support that is lacking from school officials. An adequate alternative option to the Southwestern City School district public schools but not nearly as competitive as Hilliard city schools, Bishop Waterson, or New Albany City School schools. Bishop Ready is a phenomenal school. The teachers are completely invested in the success of every child and will academically challenge every student to bring out the best in them. There are several honors and AP courses to choose from, for many subjects. As someone with three children who went to Ready, I can say that Ready definitely prepares students for college and they do every thing possible to help every graduating student during the college choosing process. There are many great academic or extra curricular clubs to join and the athletic program is great. Above all, Ready prides itself and implements faith, tradition and the "Ready family". Ready is definitely underrated and deserves more recognition for what they do. Administration is old and antiquated. They don't understand there job is to foster growth in 21st century children.

column3: I graduated from Blackman in 2005, and I am so thankful that I received an education that prepared me for college and the real world! I went to UT, and am now a grad student at MTSU getting a Masters in Teaching foreign language, and I have realized more and more how fundamental my high school education was. The sports and programs were also fantastic! I was a cheerleader and that was a great way to connect with people and it was something I was passionate about. Not to mention, it instilled discipline. Another wonderful thing about Blackman is the cohesiveness of the different groups of people. I give this school one star cause of the teaching skills and the concern of the students education! The teachers do not care if the students fail or not, all they care about is when TCAP rolls around. I have two teenagers that attend this school and they are both failing certain subjects and not once have i received an email or call from any of the teachers with concern for my children. They are real focused on behavior, sports but not academics. If child does not have the smarts already i would not send to this school cause they will fail and their will be no concern what so ever out of any of the faculty (consulars, principle, vice principle, teachers!) most of the teachers don't teach they treat the students like they are college kids. Awful school!!! I wish i could transfer my kids but that is impossible cause they do not have cars yet. Amazing. This school gave me the best learning expirence I have ever had . . Ms.Ford, the principle, is one of the most caring, efficient, and her staff at Blackman Elementary follow suit, I am please with the level of education my daughters have experienced since we moved into this school system 4 years ago, I would recommend this school to anyone who cares if their child is receiving a quality education. This school is great. Great student body, great teachers, and great environment. This school has changed my life. I love BHS my daughter is a freshman and the faculty really works hard at helping her pick her classes, and making her feel comfortable. I am a very proud BHS mom/ Thank you BHS staff for all of your work. Love this high School. We moved here to get our son there and that was our best choice ever. When we moved to Murfreesboro two years ago, we purposely moved into this school zone. We are very glad we did and have no regrets!!!! 0/10. inconsiderate and just not right at all! My daughters all hated it! This school used to be a good school but over crowding has led to over whelmed teachers which aren't able to teach. Bullying is out of hand there! My son's experience was terrible! Upper classman males haze and sexually harass younger males and it is over looked. The school is way over crowded and bullying is also a problem! This is the worst school! Bullying is a huge problem and they don't do anything about it. They sweep it under the rug so that it doesn't get out and they can continue to be a"great" school. Principal is just awful and is not fit for the job! They also do not really care about your child's education. I highly recommend checking out other schools! Great school, Great Community, Great Communication, Great Teachers

column1: NDCL is a great college preparatory school which has given me, and all other students, amazing opportunities. I feel that NDCL has truly helped me unleash my full potential as a student, and almost all of the teachers have pushed me to be my best.

column3: Best HIGH SCHOOL in Atlanta! Teachers seem very happy as well as the faculty and students. It is a great neighborhood and state-of-the-art classes. Both of my kids struggled at Centennial after transferring from a private school. We met with our kids counselor many times and had many meetings with all the teachers. There were always suggestions but no support to help my kids be successful. The new principal doesn't even bother to respond to emails from concerned parents. My daughter's math teacher was absent over 40 days last year and the school failed to provide the class with a long term math substitute. The average EOCT grade for her class was a 67%. The school should be ashamed. When I asked the counselor to switch my daughter to another class I was told that switching isn't allowed. The icing on the cake was when the teacher came into class two weeks before school was out and announced to the students that she wasn't coming back! Although my daughter passed the class thanks to private tutoring, I'm disappointed that the school did nothing to address the concerns of parents or students. The students even signed a petition begging for help. What a terrible first impression of Centennial High School. My daughter's experience overall was ok, nothing to write home about. There was also a lot of fights for a school with such great ratings. If we don't see improvement next year we will hardship our daughter to a school that is safer and concerned with the education of all students. Do not send your children here. It used to be one of the best schools in the state, but it is probably the worst on north fulton county. Many of the best staff members, teachers and administrators, have left. There is a high turnover rate for the staff at this school. I have heard that teachers leave because there is a huge lack of professionalism by some of the staff members. My child went to Holcomb bridge middle school and the staff truly cared about my child. They were more concerned with actually doing their jobs and teaching my child rather than getting wrapped up in work place drama. I wish I could pick up the staff from Hbms and place them at chs. Recently, Centennial has been getting some bad reviews for this past 2012-2013 school year, and I can't argue with them...most of it is true. One thing that I did notice is that all these complaints seem to come from parents of on-level students at Centennial. The fact of the matter is, if your child is an on-level class they will probably not enjoy it as much. One reason being the teachers performance but the main reason is because of the behavior of most of the students in on-level classes. They are so rude and disrespectful it literally prevents the teacher from teaching and keeps other students from learning. I am not in on-level classes in am entering 10th grade in 2 APS and 3 honors classes. This past year I was in honors classes and I was challenged and I had little to no trouble learning mostly due to the fact that I am surrounded by other students who WANT to learn and do well. I honestly feel that the problems that people are complaining about are due to behavioral issues. Some problems are because of teachers but not many. Don't bash Centennial because it's not good or it's ratchet...I find it exciting compared to some preppy private school or Johns Creek, etc. Awesome staff and atmosphere. My experience so far has been most warm and welcoming. Thank you to all involved. The teachers at Centennial are fantastic. He received a great education in a real world environment My oldest son just graduated from Centennial and my younger son and step daughter are attending now. I have found the teachers to be excellent and very caring. The programs offered are outstanding and the facilities are great. I was amazed at all the Honor graduates at graduation this past May. This is a true testament to the teachers and the parent involvement. I am very please with CHS . Teachers care for the students , great programs and amazing stuff . Centennial High School is a phenomenal school which is clearly thriving under positive, student-centered leadership. Centennial was at one time a decent school with a good reputation. Unfortunately the principal has turned a blind eye to the gang activity, drugs, and violence that have become rampant in this school. Most students and parents are desperate to leave this school. Although there are still dedicated members of faculty that support the hard working members of the student body to the best of their ability, and the counseling staff is great:), it is impossible to feel safe sending your child to a school in which drug use is tolerated, gangs are operating out in the open, and violence is given a slap on the wrist. A major clean up is needed here. I have a recent graduate of Centennial who is attending a highly competitive STEM school and a sophomore. Centennial is a diverse school that exposes students to challenging academic content in a real world environment, preparing them for success in their lives after high school.Centennial High School (CHS) is ranked by The Washington Post, US News & World Report, and Atlanta Magazine as one of Americas best high schools. In 2015, CHS was recognized as one of Georgia’s top 25 schools. The school is in the process of implementing an International Baccalaureate program and is on track to become an authorized school offering an IB Diploma beginning with 2018-19 school year. This is a very rigorous curriculum and is not for everyone, but individual IB classes will be offered to students outside of the diploma program. This program will complement CHS's offering of 28 AP classes, all of which can earn students college credit.Graduation rates have risen 9% in the past two years to 88% last year. Success should be credited to the support that the school receives from the School Governance Council and the district charter system status that enables the school to implement innovative ways of teaching & learning. CHS is known in the county as a thought leader based on its success with local school flexibility requests and the implementation of a 21st Century Learning Commons (replacing the Media Center) and two Cooperative Learning Labs (one for STEM and one for the Humanities). These were existing spaces redesigned to encourage students to collaborate and leverage technology to achieve greater success. CHS is part of a select number of Phase 1 schools leading the county in technology implementation to further personalized learning. Specifically, new Microsoft Surface tablets will be rolled out to every student beginning this coming January. The counseling staff works very hard to support students and is one of the few counseling programs in Fulton County recognized as an American School Counselor Association (ASCA) National Model. CHS students continue to outperform Fulton, Georgia and National averages on the SAT and ACT and has been recognized by College Board as an AP STEM Achievement School, an AP STEM School, and an AP Merit School. Offers an excellent environment for education by offering honors and advanced placement classes in all areas of study but with a focus on Science and Math. Centennial teachers and administration are focused on improving education for all the students at this school, providing opportunities unlike any other high school in the area. For example, International Baccalaureate is coming to CHS in the next couple of years - the school is in the process of getting accredited. My son just finished his freshman year - amazing teachers who are truly dedicated to our children. My son was involved in band and sports as well. The administration and coaches are so supportive. The best part is the learning! All around academics were a win. Proud to be a Knight! Centennial is the best kept secret in North Fulton County! Opportunities for all students to thrive in education and sports. Centennial had the highest number of early admission to UGA of all North Fulton Schools for the last two years! 2016 Centennial will offer the International Baccalaureate (IB) program only one of two North Fulton schools to offer this very sought after program! Great teachers, great location! Centennial is definitely not a safe environment for learning. Fights break out often and there are lots of drug sales on the grounds. Most teachers there seem to just read from the book (if they "teach" at all) and students have to go and learn the material on their own time. I have two freshman half way through their first year at CHS and we have had a positive experience with both. The administration and faculty are engaged, responsive and regularly communicate with parents. If you have a child who values education and understands their role in development, these teachers are there for them!I love the community the school fosters as well. There are lots of dedicated parents and staff in all of CHS's activities, clubs and organizations. Sometimes the standard "scores" are misleading and I feel so much of what's great about this school is overlooked by parents who don't take the time to be involved in a school. So if you're unsure about where you want to buy your next home, talk to the community first- those who have kids in the school and those who are thriving because of it. Centennial high school is a great school I recommend it to anyone in the area people like to talk about how bad the school is but they don't know how sheltered and how safe the school and its workers make it for there employees and students they have never been to a south Gwinnett high school or ones who aren't near as decent so bad comments don't determine the truth of the school. My experience at this school has been phenomenal! The teachers care about the students and their success and the leadership in the school truly cares about the arts and extracurriculars. Bad reviews of this school may be true but only in on-level classes because of the behavior of these students. Any upper level classes are beyond extraordinary and this should be considered one of the best high schools in the area. My son has thrived in the CHS environment, both academically and in sports and volunteer opportunities. Academically, there has been enough to challenge him... and when he had difficulties in an AP course, the teacher offered many opportunities to help him understand, recover, learn and move forward. Centennial has been a fantastic experience for both of my kids. They have told me they can't imagine being in another school! They are academically challenged with great classes, and are thriving in the excellent environment offered at Centennial. So far so good, one of my daughters has bullied by other student, the school contacted me immediately and took all the necessary procedures to make sure this will never happen again. Teachers always take care for the students and there special needs. Our son has had a good experience there. He has challenging classes and the school has excellent AP and honors level teachers for demanding subjects. We will have two children at the school next year and are looking at the IB program for our second one. Going to this school is the worst decision of my life. I wish I had dropped out and gone somewhere else. I have requested if I can give my diploma back. I am embarrassed to put this school on my resume. I couldn't have asked for a better high school for both of my kids, and I have one in the Special Needs and one in all advanced classes and they each are doing great and having a great experience! Centennial has been an excellent school so far for my older kids. They have been challenged in AP classes; the teachers have been great, and they love the traditions and school culture. The cross country team has been one of the best things for my kids! Highly recommend it as a way to meet people as a freshman (since they start running practice in the summer before school starts), and instantly know kids in all grades. My kids find the students genuine and authentic; we love the diversity, and the film/AV club. I look forward to my younger children attending Centennial! I am in real estate, and have toured many local schools. North Fulton has amazing schools, and Centennial is one of them! The administration has no clue what is going on in the school. There are boys throwing trash cans over the stalls hitting anyone who is in it. When I called they all acted like they cared but they kept transferring me to another admin and this went on for about an hour. Finally 2 weeks later they called me back they told me everything they could that was calling me a liar but actually saying that. There was some racial things going on also and they had no clue when I called. The teachers will call you over the dumbest things your kids do like sharpen their pencils to much. I moved to this district just for the schools because the ratings was amazing but now I regret it and can’t sell my house.. I wish my kids never had to go to this school I absolutely hate it We are impressed by the robust learning opportunities and curriculum offered at Centennial High School Learning:It is a rarity you will find students who are motivated to learn. The pressure put on grades only stuns students' growth and numbers are always the focus. Because the grading system is based on statistics without any kind of consideration for outside pressures or circumstances. Teaching:Teachers are very much a gamble. Some are wonderful and are always willing to support students while others, I'd say a good 60%, have no consideration for students' actual education or well-being. There seems to be a tense relationship between admin and teachers as well. Social-emotional support:Posters are posted around the school of school-based resources for students but as a former student myself... no help whatsoever. There is a MASSIVE equity problem in Cen10 that is never addressed and always ignored. Ask admin or teachers about how a new policy may be discriminatory the blame is shifted to someone else.Special Education:The biggest issue with the Special Education classrooms in Centennial is the lack of integration with the rest f the school. All the classes are clumped together at the end of the school in one low lit hallway. There is no effort to socialize the students. There are no opportunities for students to help or support Special Education classrooms. Seperate from the Special Education classrooms but in the same realm, there are several students with learning disablities or mental illness that are never taken into consideration when tracking their progress in the academic setting.Safety:Fights and threats are common but usually not really an issue between students as its kinda the norm, which of course says a lot about the overall culture in the school. However, I was at Centennial when there was a stabbing in the cafeteria. The cafeteria was not dismissed, people who witnessed it noted the lack of urgency in teachers responses, the school did not go to a lockdown despite that being the school policy. Class continued as usual that day and my group were the next in the cafeteria and they acted as nothing had happened.Family Engagement:There is rarely positive communication between school and parents. If your parents heard something from the school its bad. Tying this back to the stabbing incident, statements are written and released to parents and the local news. No details are included but false reinsurance of their care is guaranteed.Cen10 has problems like every school but its unique in inaction.

column1: Green River has a professional and caring staff of teachers, administrators, and other professionals. My kids have gotten a good education and gone on to do well in life due in large part to the quality of this school. Additionally they have some fantastic after school activities. Ones I am familiar with include Speech and Debate, Cheer, Music, and Art but the sports teams are first rate as well. Green River High School has potential; however, I am consistently disappointed in the education that I received there. The accountability of students is not fair, the rigor of courses does not prepare students for prestigious institutions, the educational movement toward teaching character has yet to reach Green River, and the administrators do not support teachers and students and care more about their paycheck. I think that the lack of choice for parents renders the school a monopoly-like power; they provide the only education possible, so it does not matter the degree of effort they put into it. I am grateful for a family that instilled in me a value of education, but am severely disappointed in my public school education. On the other hand, there are a few teachers that did have profound influence because their desire to educate not merely to get paid. This school is a joke! Test scores are low. Its ran like a prison! The staff thinks they are god! The do discriminate! If you aren't some one, then your no one. They judge by appearance. Called my 15 yr old a bum!! Guess the staff was never taught they are not better then their students, they are just teachers, not high society prison wardens!! Excellent education (NOT), get facts, search it!!

column3: I attended Stagg HS and had a great experience. Stagg offers great, recently renovated facilities. I was involved in the student newspaper which is one of the best in the nation and a great resume builder for students looking to attend college.

column1: Tri-County, where would my kids be without you? They are thriving, happy and successful, and I am SO happy that we made the decision to send them there. It's the cleanest building I've ever seen, and the pride of both the students and the staff is evident. The vocational programs are varied and wonderful, and prepare the students for life after high school. The academic teachers are wonderful. They work so much with the students to help them become successful. A super place that I just can't say enough about. One of my children still goes back to visit her teachers after all these years. She was disappointed for her youngest brother that her favorite History teacher no longer works there. I love Tri-County! It is like home! Tri-County provided both our boys with the skill set and confidence they needed to succeed in anything they attempt. Whether it is Academics, Shop or Athletics the students are taught respect- respect for their facility, respect for others and mostly respect for themselves. The students are treated as members of the work force, they have responsibilities and are expected to do their job. The teachers are second to none. They go above and beyond to help any student who wants help. There are so many trades to choose from and the exploratory program gives each student a good overview of several of the different programs. Tri-County thoroughly prepares their students for what ever their futures holds. Tri-County also offers many extra-curricular activities and sports - nothing is missing to provide your child with a well rounded high school experience. Both of our sons have chosen different paths. One has worked hard in his trade and at 21 is a member of the Boston Pipefitters Union. The other son is attending college and loving it. Becoming a member of the Tri-County community was definitely the best decision we ever made. No regrets. Love this school! From classrooms to a students shop the teachers really challenge and work really hard to make sure all students succeed! This school really tries to foster academics and goes out of it's way to ensure no child is left behind. They have mandatory homework club for any student that starts to fall behind. My daughter is in the honors program and it is challenging and the teachers always push the students to do more. The only downside to this school is the girls sports coach. If your daughter plans on participating in sports this is not the school for you. The coach is a bully and many girls stop playing sports just so they don't have to play for him.

column3: I have had many issues with this school system. In the beginning, it was great, then Geye Hamby took over and implemented mandatory uniforms (aka: dress code) without an opt-out solution (like Long Beach City schools in California), which has been inconsistently implemented throughout each school (Elementary, Academy, Middle, and High). The best point has been Dr. Banks Bitterman at BHS. He's a good principle, fair-minded, and listens to the parents, no matter their ethnicity or economic background. Any issue I have had these past few years, Dr. Bitterman has handled without hesitation; his solutions, in my belief, are always presented with what is in the best interest of all parties, but most importantly for the student(s). Buford City School system is like Cuba... You can't get out of the school system unless your child drops out and goes to college early, (or) the parents hand guardianship to someone else outside the district, (or) the family moves outside the district boundaries. I wouldn't recommend BHS to any one. Lanier HS has newer facilities, good teachers, and class options. I've tried to transfer my daughter twice, but Gw. County said no - not enough space. After paying tuition for ten years my child got kicked out for not passing one semester! Never been in trouble for anything. Maybe if they were a star football player, my child would still be there. Your child's best interest is not what Buford has, if you pay tuition, Amazingly well run school! Exceptional staff and we love it! Dr. Bitterman is a great leader! BHS is one of the very best schools in GA. the teachers and staff are very helpful (both to parents/family and students). they have great school activities to join and enjoy. they promote excellent learning tools. The academics are great, teachers really work their tails off. My kids attend and I am pleased with the academics of the elementary. The high school is very political. It is all about who you are related to or know that gets you on teams, or not cut from teams. I am surprised that kids who are profiled as poor students are pulled from elective classes for extra preparation specifically to pass the EOCT. That may increase test scores for state rankings, but it kids are missing 2 days/week of classes and are supposed to be either responsible for the work or it is not supposed to count against them. Are we worried about student learning or test scores and state rankings?! As a teacher I have been told that I need to pay attention to important parents kids, and make sure I realize they all have the principals personal cell #. My kids will not attend BHS while the leadership continues down this path. The academics here is awesome. I am pleased that my kids are challenged to work hard academically. They have benefitted from the strong structure in the high school, although they complain about the uniform policy. I think the principal, Dr. B, is fair in most cases. As parents we love and support the school and always will. They have strong athletics as well, which both of my kids love very much. They do put a lot of emphasis on sports. The biggest disappointment for my kids has been the comments some kids have made when encountering others who are not like them - inferring closed mindedness. Other than that, Buford all the way!!! Biggest disappointment !!! If you are considering being a tuition paying family think long and hard. We wish she had stayed at her districted school. I expected much better teachers seeing how a large portion of the students are tuition paying. She has had some good ones but some are only there so they can coach a sport. Communication with parents and students is awful. Pretty much non- existent. A project that she had done was chosen to go on to some competition. Her teacher nor the school notified her of this. However, we did receive a letter in the mail stating that it was submitted for a competition that was to be the night the letter came to us. Really! Needless to say we weren't able to make it. Since my daughter has been there she has been on the honor roll. They have awards night for those kids but only if you are one of " the chosen " ones. Yep that's right not every honor roll kid gets to go. Dr. B said it was bk there wasn't enough room. Yeah right! Either you do it for all the honor roll kids or non. Not pick and chose who gets to go. What makes some one else's honor roll achievement better than another honor roll kids achievement . Pretty darn certain there was an easy solution to the " not enough space" issue. Dr. B has taken away the fun in highschool. I'm all for being tough but these kids can't do anything. The boys are no Longer aloud to paint up their chests for football games. I've been told that all chants that the student section wants to do has to be approved by him. There is very little extra curricular activities such as run for the cure. Etc But then again if there is we wouldn't know bk of the lack ofCommunication. Highschool should be fun too and sadly this school isn't. This is an extremely political school. If you have lots of money to sink into the school you'll be fine. If your kid will be a football great. You will be fine. Who you know and how much you throw into the school will impact greatly on making teams , class president and even homecoming court. They chose who they want not necessarily based on skill or student votes.Makes me very sad for my child as I feel a lot of the highschool experience is lost at this school and she can't redo these years. So think long and hard about this school. It certainly is NOT for everyone Wonderful. Revived my love of education. I had previously taught at other schools, and nowhere is as great as Buford. This school has allowed me the freedom to teach like I know how to do... and I am grateful for it. My coworkers are a joy to teach and collaborate with. We just moved to Buford schools last year when Covd hit pretty hard across the nation.The school gave us options to do virtual or face to face in school.I went to the meeting for concern over face to face in school setting but felt comfortable sending students in school instead of going through virtual after we moved from out of state. Looking back, I think we made a right decision to send kids to school. There was sporadic cases that flared for Covid 19 from time to time but kids and teachers were quarantined and school was very effective dealing with COVID 19 issues. In the end, there was no absence for my kids to miss school and they adapted to new environment nicely with the help of teachers.The sports activities are emphasized here in Buford system and number of AP courses are limited but can be taken through virtual classes and first course is free of charge. One of the reason that we have picked Buford compared to other competitive schools nearby is the balance between academic works and after school activities. Only disappointment I have is the absence of Orchestra in high school. The band is exceptional but it would be nice to have Orchestra especially when school spent so much money in building performance center in High School. The school focuses on white upper middle class kids. There are no supports for any kid that is different. Instruction is lectures and quizzes and tests. Kids have to do all the work themselves to get help if they struggle at all. Teachers are nice but inflexible. Standards and expectations are different for male athletes. Majority of the staff are graduates of Buford and don’t believe there is anything that could or should changed. This is a closed small town system that is not welcoming to anything that’s not white upper middle class. We started in this school system when my student was in 1st grade. Loved the community feel, the environment and the teachers. As the school got bigger, the luster of it started to fade. It became less about the student achievement and more about the athletic achievements. Grades were posted and shared with the parents 2-3 weeks after the assignment, so if your student was struggling, it seemed too late to get help to catch up. Most teachers would not even offer extra help, just put it on the student to "work harder" - when they didn't know what they needed to work on, since grades were not posted immediately. Once we got into middle school and high school, it got much worse. When you chose to no longer participate in athletics, the students were shunned by those that were in athletics and looked down on by other students and sometimes even parents (seemed they learned that at home). In High School, while the building was beautiful, the people inside it quickly became "entitled" and treated the less than average like second-class citizens. There was so much bullying to my student - not necessarily physical, but emotional, mental, verbal - and when attempts were made to address it, the reaction was, well maybe they didn't mean it like you think. Talk about blaming the victim!!! The system got way too big, way too fast and lost the love of the community, and its people. Rich, upper class are the chosen ones and if you can't pour into the financial requirements, then you are shunned and left out. We were tuition and decided to move to the school where we are districted and accepted. Such a shame that a beautiful campus can house so much hatred and disdain for others.

column1: This school is the best I have ever been too better than the other two schools I attend before. This school offers a great band program. The teachers there really care about the students. We had moved from South Pontotoc and decided to move back because South Pontotoc doesn't compare to other schools. Great school. I recommend it to anyone interested.

People should give it a chance ,and not to let them self get influenced by other people opinions about that school,because many of them have never even vist Dudley. Most of what people say are just rumors to give the school a bad reputation. My experience with the school academically has been great. I truly believe that the staff cares and encourages all students to do and be their best.

column1: Hi, i am a student who goes to this school. I know the outrage of parents who want their kids to have a safe environment. Yet, your kids are going to middle school/high school and have to learn to grow up and make their own decisions becausenoone else will make it for them. Too, i m going to 8th grade and the reputations that you here about this school might not be true unless you come and actually see it happening. Too, yes, what you call "thugs" and "gangsters" do deserve to go to a well organized school too. You guys all have your opinion but I dont think its true. Lastly, there is never any bullying because i ACTUALLY GO TOTHE SCHOOL. Riverdaly/Kingsbridge Academy (Middle/High School 141) is getting worst every year. I have my two boys in this school, since middle school and both of them bacame victims of the dangerous environment of the school. The lack of knowledge of the principal is the reason why the school is going down, she has no idea how to run the school properly. Therefore, i ask the board of education to make some changes as soon as possible. This school is horrible I am in 7th grade here. The teachers don't care about u one even slapped a kid in the face. The kids behave like animals. Don't go here. I have been a student attending this school for throughout middle school. This school is okay and if you think about enrolling your child here, think again after reading this review. I personally feel that the students are only successful if they are in honors. Otherwise, the learning isn't that good, and non-honors education in this school is lacking. The teachers and principals are very aged and out of touch with social issues and are failing to understand the problems students have. I have problems so I go to the guidance counselor who gives me very weird solutions, that i feel uncomfortable doing. I feel as if the teachers watched a quick video on the term "bullying" and don't fully understand it. This school is very out of hand with the mean people, and harassers!!!!!!!!!! This school could improve if O'Mara dropped her "oh let's be prideful with school spirit" act and noticed what kids go through in this school! Probably one of the worst school in this area. The students that are forced to attend here are placed at a serious disadvantage socially and academically. The parents who are unable to find their kid a better alternative are in for a rude awakening upon graduation. It's unfortunate that these young minds have to suffer, while nearby Horace Mann and Fieldston Academies revel in academic glory. This school is an in- direct feeder for the prison system. Not only are the teachers less than qualified but he administration constantly looks the other way. Riverdale is a great community to live in, but as far as the public middle and high schools go your sentencing your child to a lifetime of hellish inadequacy if you send them to 141. After reading this I want to share that this school was the same in the 70s-an outstanding honors & the rest floundered. The bullying then was the haves vs have nots-not racially motivated. If the kids are behaving like animals - hint they are - not the teachers fault. If you can't afford a private school - then this is where your kid goes or move to a better district. Your kid got into 3 fights here more than other schools - what does that say 2 fights in the other school? Thugs & gansters came from NYCs poorer parts & a generation ago did nothing so they are here and all over the nation. Guidance counselors have a 1 size fits all answer - deal with it. Favorites among teachers - nothing new. By the way I graduated 141 went to a NYC high school that is now closed, rec'vd a 4 year scholarship-am a married grandmother with a great well paying job. School is what you make of it. Parents stop complaining do something or shut up, teachers teach to the good and ignore the rest, principals and administration stop throwing $ at a problem with no solution-unless you want the parents to babysit their kids 24/7 & then let them complain that jr isn't learning dont expect good reviews. The teachers are great. They work hard with the students. The crossing guards watch over the students. I went to the school and I think it is still a good school to attend. My family has been very happy with the education my daughter has received. They have great communication. My daughter is now in 7th grade and has had a wonderful experience. I have a 6th grader in this school and I am impressed!!!! She is in the Double Honors program where she is challenged daily by passionate and caring teachers who love to teach. The experience for our child at the school has been wonderful. He is finishing middle school and has been in the honors program. In eighth grade, he is taking high school regents classes. The teachers are encouraging and engaging. He will continue going to RKA for high school. We are actively involved parents and this school has a lot to offer. Get involved...learn what your children are learning and become a part of the community. There is a lot to offer here...what your children and you put in it is what you and your children will get out of it. Gem of a school in our neighborhood. We have had a great experience at this school for my child. How can I describe a school that parents, community members, and locals run away from in droves. This so called "High School is a running joke among the people that live nearby It's would be funny if it weren't so tragic. They have limited arts and music programs and refuse to deal with constant bullying that occurs on a regular basis. The problems at next door PS 24 school serve as an indicator of how bad things really are. When I went to this school our teachers made it crystal clear on a regular basis how little they believed in us as students, and how much the Principal at the time was to blame for the downgrade of the school. The admin pretends that this is such a great place to attend, but academics are not a priority. Teachers who considered themselves saints for working with economically disadvantaged students. They just kept making promises of improvement that never came true. I entered an idealistic youth, and graduated with nothing but regret about my overall experience here. I went to this school and it ruined my future academic prospects, my belief in public education, and the idea that regardless of zip code every child is entitled to a quality education. As a parent I would pick ANY other school but this one. The simply don't care. I wish I had sent my son to a different school. I an very disappointed with the general education program there. I am currently attending the school and my experience has been great but I believe there is room for improvement. they students and facilty have been really helpful and supportive. but in some cases i have witnessed some bullying. what needs to be improved is that the school needs to handle bullying more effectively. also the work assigned to us need to get students more engaged in learning as when I take classes it's not about learning its about memorizing enougth information to get good marks on the next test then forgetting it all on the weekend but other then that I think the school is really good and I would recommend it to parents who are about to enroll there kids into middle school. There's a lot of bullying and fighting inside the school and out of school in the surrounding communities. Glad my daughter no longer attends.

Amazing school graduated in 2012 miss this school teachers and staffs been the mascot for 2 years! Central valley has a great staff, opportunities like sports, choir, band, art, wood shop, yearbook, student newspaper, ect. At first I was pretty impressed but as time has passed I can see the deficits the school has. It is extremely over crowded. The office staff can be extremely rude. I'm really disappointed in some of the teachers and staff behaviors. It isn't a positive experience, so much that we are considering pulling our child out of this school. I would say if you can avoid attending this school do so. i’ve experienced racism at this school. never from the students but always from teachers. no one actually cares about what you learn they just do their jobs and teach what the need to teach to get you out of this school in four years. with the recent pandemic students are more depressed then ever with no outlet, and counselors can only help so much.

column1: I am a basketball fan of the Enosburg Falls high school. I did not go to the game last night, but I saw on facebook what the Fairfax boys did at the pregame ceremonies. The respect that they gave for our team and Brandon Gleason is something that should be commended. Very well done Fairfax boys team. Overall good. PK and 1st years excellent. 1st grade terrible. Other grades such as 3rd and 5th great too. Just terrible. Plain terrible. Don’t send your child here if you went them to get a good education. I am very disappointed with the whole middle school experience here at BFA. Having previously attended a school with much stronger academics, the difference for my child in expectations, leadership, and challenge is stark. There is not even a language offered until grade 8, and then it's a "special". This school has so much potential, which is glimpsed at times. There are so many wonderful people in this town who care very much about BFA's success, and feel that "good enough" is not enough. The middle school structure and staff have offered my two students solid support and connection. My students have grown academically and socially, and I always have quick collaboration from teachers/administrators around any concerns. I believe student success hinges not on school resources alone, but on how parents/caregivers are able to build partnerships with school teams. The middle school team at BFA Fairfax has been a great partner in these hard years of pandemic learning, with teachers clearly invested in the school community. Also, the school board approaches problem solving with a practical and fiscally conservative lens, while encouraging initiatives that build on strengths and include diverse perspectives. School everywhere are trying to respond to so many demands with not enough resources, but what I can say is BFA Fairfax is doing a nice job providing an experience that models the importance of commitment to learning.

column3: I went to this school for my 4 years of high school They have plenty of AP classes and CAMs to choose from. The Track and Cross country program is very good. The coaches are the best and most compassionate I have seen. They really care about their athletes. The teachers are also very good. They truly want you to succeed. Most kids are pretty nice and I made a lot of good friend. The school also has pretty small classes which are very helpful for a lot of students and you get more teacher time. I would definitely recommend this school. I went to this school for my 4 years of high school They have plenty of AP classes and CAMs to choose from. The Track and Cross country program is very good. The coaches are the best and most compassionate I have seen. They really care about their athletes. The teachers are also very good. They truly want you to succeed. Most kids are pretty nice and I made a lot of good friend. The school also has pretty small classes which are very helpful for a lot of students and you get more teacher time. I would definitely recommend this school. My children have gone to Churchill for the last four years. Over the last few years the school has really gone down hill. New principal is more focused on social issues and less on education. The bright spot for this school are the International High School, AP classes and the computer classes, that's were the great teachers are! I highly recommend that you consider the International program. The teachers really care, the students are dedicated to learning and they will be ready for college. The Cross Country, Track and Football Programs have great coaches that really care about the kids. Sadly, that can not be said about the Boy's basketball program. If your child is lucky enought to get the right teachers, they can get a better than average education. But you as a parent will have to stay on top of it for all four years. The school offers four year International High School which is the same program at South Eugene & Sheldon HS. They work together at IHS conferences yearly. They also have newly constructed STEM(science tech engineering math building) and a WISE (women in science and engineering) program offered to female students. School offers great athletic, arts and science extracurricular activities. IHS, Rachel Carson, AVID and Project Success are available in conjunction with standard Churchill curriculum. Free College Now classes are offered through LCC (math) and IHS offers IB classes and Churchill offers AP classes. The school has a variety of religious & ethnic groups plus wide economic levels giving students a world view with international exchange students too. Both my children attended Churchill. They have a nice variety of academic pathways for students to choose from. My son and daughter both were able to start at higher level college courses, due to the AP and LCC options at Churchill. I graduated from Churchill in 2009. I was part of IHS and it was an incredible program that prepared me for college so much better than my friends who were not part of that program. I would strongly recommend it to anyone! They also offer a wide array of high quality AP classes and free college now classes. This allowed me to gain college credit for every class I took starting my junior year. I also had total say of my schedule and was able to work in an internship my senior year and my transition to college was smoother than I think it would have if I had had adults looking over my shoulder every step of the way. However, while the school worked great for me and many others, it left struggling students behind and offered no effective support, leading several intelligent but disorganized people I knew to drop out. They all felt like the adults at that school were pushing them toward dropping out, rather than finding a way to work with them. I understand the school has changed its structure, I'm assuming in an effort to better support these students, but as of 2014, I know the school was still struggling in this area. Until this school figures out how to better serve ALL its students, I can't give it a better rating.

column1: Do NOT attend this school if you are not the perfect 'cookie cutter' shape. They will ruin you. My children attend here, and their teachers are absolutely the best! I can't imagine them going anywhere else. What a fabulous community...elementary all the way to high school. Great school with small population. Students are not just a number. Staff truly cares about students and their well being. They are adding new programs to meet the needs of the students such as soccer, wrestling, chorus, etc. A well kept secret! This is the only school I have ever known. I graduated in 1973 from WCHS. My dad who is dead now, went to Wheeler County High School. Me and my brother and three sisters went to school here. All four of our daughters graduated from here. As a matter of fact, when our baby daughter graduated last year, there had been a member of our family in Wheeler County Schools for 55 years. The graduation of our daughter ended the 55 year tradition. I am now an employee with the system and I am loving it. It is my goal to retire from here. BEST SCHOOL EVER!!! Wheeler County Elementary is an amazing place. The family like atmosphere is evident in each grade level. I am so blessed that my children have been able to attend a school where the teachers that touch their lives seem to care about them as much as I do. Thank you WCES for a great experience!

column3: I'm currently a student here at Tillamook High. The teachers and extra-curricular diversity of clubs and sports are my favorite part of the school. I came to this school my Sophomore year (2016-2017) and it's honestly MUCH better than the school I went to my Freshman year. The only problems I've faced at this school are a lack of good friends and a small bias towards sports activity achievements rather than others, such as arts achievements or club achievements. For example, we would have whole assemblies, where the whole student body was pulled out of classes and the day's schedule was different than the normal day's schedule (making class time shorter), 2/3 focused on the achievements of athletic teams at competitions, while other clubs or departments, such as art show success or smaller clubs like science club, only receive congratulations over daily announcements. Overall, this school is very good. I always look forward to all of my classes and the teachers have never made me feel unwelcome. I'm moving away after my Sophomore year is over, and I'm definitely not thrilled to be leaving a great school like this; I will absolutely, without a doubt extremely miss this school and all I've been able to experience and accomplish here. (:

column1: This school is by far the worst in Houston County. The Superintendent isn't any better. They claim parents should get involved, but when we do we are ignored. Why should we put up with this? Why can't we get something done with the way we are treated. I am an alumi of Rehobeth High, Class of 2003, and I must admit that I enjoyed attending school there. The teachers are caring and are willing to go above and beyond to make sure your child receives the best education possible. Granted, some of my past teachers are no longer there and have retired, but I would send my child to Rehobeth before even considering another school in the area. I am very pleased with the education I received, the teachers, and the school board. I went to Rehobeth Kindegarden all the way up and now my 15,13,and 10 year old are doing the same ........excellent School,Excellent teachers!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Withdrew my child from the areas “best private schools “ RHS exceeds my expectations

column3: This is a great school for many reasons. The classes offered here are varied, and they offer challenging honors and AP classes. No matter which kind of class you're in, though, teachers expect a lot out of you. 80% of the the teachers here (if I remember correctly) have their masters degree, and they know their stuff. Leyden high school is one of the highest paying school districts in the state, so they expect a lot from the teachers they employ--and they do a fantastic job. Teachers here truly care about the students, but sometimes students don't take advantage of the education they are getting-- but this happens at every school, right? The school offers TONS of extracurriculars, and they also have a phenomenal ACT Prep program here (which helped raise my ACT score by 4 points). I'm proud to be a graduate of East Leyden High School. I truly learned a lot, and I was well prepared for college. This school is the best. I love it here, the teachers respect you if you respect them. Homework is substantial. And here at East, we have over 50 clubs! And over 15 sports! It may seem harsh giving this school a low rating but I currently attend here and I don't find anything real special about it. You have the kids that judge you and the teachers.. Some actually teach while some don't and for juniors and seniors they don't really give support for college. I wasn't too thrilled at all with this school. Leyden is a good school but they need to work on some things. There are all types of teachers some are better than others. Even if teachers are considered to be role models I believe they still make mistakes. It is normal to make mistakes because is our nature of being humans. I believe that they should help there student more often and more then they already. The school is good, but could be a lot better. The administration does not know how to schedule quizzes/tests/exams to allow the students to do their best. Making kids take multiple quizzes/tests/exams on one day, when it could be spread out by simple scheduling guidelines such as which subject or course type can have quizzes/tests/exams on which days of the week. We all want the kids to do better, so the school can get into compliance with the No Child Left Behind Act. I currently attend this school as a sophomore and have to say that the teachers really do care about helping the students learn and progress in their academics, which can easily be seen by the availability that teachers have to see them before school, during lunch, and after school. There are plenty of great clubs and the coaches are great for the sports, at least the ones I have had. The culture is very diverse and connected. Although there are some people who are bad apples, the majority seem pretty chill. The AP classes are challenging, as they should be, and the teachers try to help the students the best they can. I don't really know what else to say, but overall it is a pretty great school, with the opportunities we have and current technologies. Kids cannot be safe in this school especially now when a student was stabbed by another student on school property. Where the school security team was? Hmm... The service staff is very informative about current programs or future programs

column1: I believe the students of this school receive the highest quality academic instruction available. Especially when one factors in the more individual instruction one would naturally expect from smaller class sizes. I feel like the majority of the students educated at this school receive many opportunities for extra-curricular activities such sports, band, show choir, FFA, FBLA, FCCLA etc. If a student wants to participate, the opportunities are there for almost every interest. Excellent school! Administration, teachers and staff members truly care about students’ learning and well-being. They are well prepared for college or career after graduation. Great school in a great community!
