column3: Great administration, staff and amazing marching band music program Very clicky, if your child is not on a sports team or involved in band,marching band they are treated as second class citizens! They can be bullied and when brought to the administrations attention they always find a way to punish the child that is being bullied and not the ones who are the bullies as they are more than likely on one of the sports teams, these students can do anything they want and are never punished, or only get a verbal reprimand. This needs to stop! All students should be treated the same as non sports, non club affiliated student. We all have the choice to treat each other with respect no matter if you are in a school activity or just someone who just goes to school to learn! I graduated from here back in May and absolutely loved my 4 years here. There are a ton of extracurricular activities and sports' teams to get involved with. Not to mention the excellent staff and teachers. Of course there's going to be some teachers and other staff members that you don't like that much, but that's with every school. I think the best teacher by far is Mr. Maichrye. He teaches chemistry and he is excellent at what he does. You don't come across a lot of guys like him very often. He is a tremendous person to talk to and get to know better. He tells stories about his life often and likes to go off topic. The classes offered are also great. I think there are 12 AP courses and also several honors classes. The elective classes offered are second to none. If you get involved, you'll enjoy your time here. I met many great people and made tons of friends. The security here is top notch. They installed an advanced security system a couple of years ago and I always feel safe when I'm in there. They also adopted a new drill for an active threat in the building and we practiced it a couple of times and the teachers were trained in it. This school is definitely not one I would recommend to have your child go to. The staff isn't very cooperative and I personally do not agree with the rules they have there. It seems as though the more rules they make, the worse the kids get. I also agree that Brunswick just tries to look good for the state and has no intentions of actually helping the students who really need the help. They definitely favor the kids who are on sports teams or in some type of club. The teachers don't really give any effort into helping the kids who are struggling and instead just adore the "perfect" students. There rarely is ever any punishment for the kids who actually break the rules. Bullying is a huge problem and nothing is ever done about it. You'd think after everything that's happened over the last couple years, they'd take those things into consideration. All they do is punish both kids and make the victim feel even more vulnerable. Or nothing is done at all. The counselors aren't helpful either. They never see you to talk to you and when they do, they never give any advice. My experience here has been horrible and I think homeschooling is a better option. As a former student of Brunswick High School, and a future educator myself, I feel Brunswick has so much to offer to students! From the introduction of college courses, to a supportive staff, there isn't much Brunswick High School doesn't have to offer. After being out of school for 5 years, and watching my younger siblings go through their high school years here, I can only see improvements being made! This school district is much more than an education, it is a family! if you are not in an extra curricular activity you are treated poorly or they just don't care for you at all. I am a current student at brunswick high, I am not into any clubs or sports. and I am treated like dirt, the teachers certainly do not care for the students. I have poor grades and I keep asking for help but they do not comply to my needs. They cherish the smart and the sporty kids, I would recommend the MCCC they are so much better at helping students or if you do not want to go there do homeschooling its so much better. also with bullying if you are bullied they will do nothing or punish both parties which is asinine in my opinion it makes both parties feel bad. also if you are suicidal and cutting yourself well trust me they dont care. so many kids I knew and this is also including myself ran around with cuts on their arms and the teachers look at them and say "ok class lets get started" and completely ignore them. the only time they do care is when state is in the class room or something like that. they only want to look good outside of the school. and they make alot of students feel bad for not being in AP classes and they had a whole assembly to honor the AP kids. and all I heard from the kids in normal classes was "I feel so stupid compared to them" or "I am going to boycott any assemblies like that" this school is immensely horrible. this school is like neglectful parents but the only time they do care is when they see their grades then they care Excellent school! I had high achiever child that joined clubs and sports and I have child totally opposite! I don’t see any teachers being biased anywhere. My underachieving kid gets same help as any other kid would. Bullying is not tolerated either. Really nice community that always come together.

column1: If you are looking for a great school, look no further. LCA is top notch. My children have been attending since pre-k and are now in 2 and 5th grade. The teachers are very caring and the principals at both the East Campus and Tates Creek campus are wonderful. The teachers really care about the kids. The curriculum is excellent and, most important, Christian values are taught on a daily basis. Remember, no school is perfect. No teacher is perfect. LCA is constantly striving to be better than it already is. I don't foresee it ever becoming stagnant. My children love attending LCA. They love their teachers. We are VERY happy in our choice of school for our children. LCA has a challenging program that leads to great success. Last year, the 100 graduates were offered in excess of $7 million of college scholarships. 100% of the seniors graduate. The preschool program is second to none with an active program leading students toward exploration, play and learning. There are IPADS for students beginning in the preschool level! Elementary students have access as well and the school does a great job holding down costs. If you are looking for a caring environment, structured around Biblical principles and staffed by a loving staff who will hold your child accountable then check this school out. The results speak for themselves. LCA is a bargain for all that you get in return. It is safe, beautifully maintained and carries the mission to Glorify God. It does that well! This school is a blessing! We are new parents at LCA and could not be more impressed. The staff and teachers have been very involved with our son and have worked with us to make sure his transition to LCA was seamless. His teachers have been very responsive to any questions that we have had and the principal is very encouraging and keeps us posted on his progress. Our son enjoys his classes, the new academic challenges and the many school activities offered as well. This school is the total package if you are looking for a balance of scripture, academics and social opportunities. As I watch my children go through college, I reflect back on their time and education at LCA. They were academically ready, as shown by my oldest child's experience in a college English class. After the first paper was written, the professor called my child up to the desk and asked where my child attended high school. When the answer was LCA, the professor said "I can tell in your writing, it's excellent". Just a small example of the quality education LCA provides, not just high school, but from preschool - 12th grade. Chapel every week, Bible classes every day. Not just the spirit of Christ, but also the theology of the Bible. The quality you receive for the money invested is truly a blessing from God. Our daughter started LCA when she was 3. Our family thought LCA would be a sweet foundation and planned to transition our daughter to public school starting at Kindergarten. What we discovered after just a couple of years is that we could not imagine our daughter attending any other school than LCA. We fell in love with the teachers, the environment, and the curriculum. 10 years later, we stil feel the same. While at LCA, our daughter has taken advanced courses, joined the Beta Club, participated in band, drama, dance, and cheerleading, and experienced her first mission trip. It's rare to find a school that offers a child so many opportunities to explore their interests and talents. We have been blessed by talented, caring teachers, coaches, and youth leaders. We are so thankful we chose to remain with LCA all of these years. We loved the environment at LCA. The teachers and staff have been incredibly welcoming and helpful. However, we were dissapointed in the levels at which the students were learning even at the Pre-K level. LCA has the best of the best in all regards except in providing a challenging scholastic environment for your children. My child basically just did crafts all year and waited for the rest of the class to catch up. No additional work was supplied him and we continued to pay a high rate of tuition throughout the year. As parents we were willing to sacrifice to pay the tuition if the educational challenge was there, but sadly it was not. I cannot speak highly enough about the kindess shown by the staff and teachers. We were instantly comfortable and enjoyed a nice quiet, drama free year. My child has endured her first semester at LCA. Endured, barely. My child has already been bullied by a student that is on behavior probation and shouldn't even be allowed to stay in this school. Has endured teachers being just plain mean, yelling or not helping with questions on a subject, saying, "Figure it out." For this I'm paying thousands of dollars? We're seriously looking at another school for the remainder of the high school years. What the 2012 graduate posted on Dec. 15, 2012 is exactly what we've encountered this year: some great teachers, some caring administration, but definitely a Christian facade and not a "world-class education" at all. Very disappointed at this "Christian" school. It's more like a very expensive public school. Wonderful school. Wonderful Christian based atmosphere. The teachers are great and really love all their students. Although I do believe that a student can get a good education in public OR private schools as long as both the child and the parents are involved in the education, I still wouldn't want my child to go anywhere else. I am a graduate of lca and I can tell you to never send your kids there unless you want them to be bullied by other students or teachers. Also make sure you have a ton of money. And make sure you give your kids as much money as they need to fit in or else you will need to spend money on counseling. I graduated years ago and I still wake up from nightmares with what I had to deal with from other students. Overall you could not ask for a better education in central Kentucky. I am a pastor so some will say I'm biased. However, our child graduated with the class of 2014 and though we heard all the typical complaints daily about rules, admin, teachers, workload etc, the personal attention, preparation for college and the level of education were well worth the price. Did we agree with everything? No. But where would we have agreed with everything? LCA is led by human beings, My son was safe, well directed, challenged and I do believe loved. Sometimes there were unhealthy (incomplete) religious views he encountered both from students and staff-- but LCA is representative of what you find among all Christians trying to figure out their own spiritual lives. And the fact that normal teen behaviors (and misbehaviors) fill the hallowed halls should shock no one. Come on...really. These are teenagers LCA is an excellent school with a proven track record. If you're; considering a private education, it would be unwise not to consider it. Very happy with this school. It offers an outstanding Christian education. We are so glad we chose it for our children. Awful. I took my son out of the school. If you can afford to send your child here you should. This is a college prep school. Be prepared to work. We have been at LCA with our three children since 2012 beginning in preschool. We cannot say enough wonderful things about the school experience our children have had. Academically, our children have excelled and have always been met at the level of learning they needed. Spiritually, our children have a strong foundation of the Bible and have been taught to have a relationship with Christ in all they do. They have learned discipline, respect, and service which has helped them continue to develop a strong moral character. Any opportunity from sports to robotics to fine arts that we could hope for has been offered as an opportunity for our children. It's wonderful to know the leaders and staff are praying for our children and making decisions based in prayer. The friends our children have made and their parents have become like family. It is a blessing to get to watch your children grow and learn with families of all different walks of life who share the same moral values. The teachers are remarkable. Their passion for learning and helping push the children to thrive not only academically, but grow to know Christ is a true blessing. These teachers don't just teach our children, but love them with all their hearts. All in all, our children are thriving because of LCA and we are so thankful for this school. We would confidently recommend LCA to anyone considering a Christian education for their children. Great! We enrolled our kids in preschool at Lexington Christian Academy and were so happy we couldn’t imagine ever leaving. Despite our initial plans for them to attend public schools, after one year at LCA, we knew this is where we wanted them to graduate. For us, LCA goes way beyond providing a good education for our kids, it is helping instill a strong Christ-centered foundation in their lives. The love that surrounds my kids at LCA is evident at all levels. The teachers and staff get to know all of the students and go above and beyond to provide a happy and safe environment to learn. The greatest testament is probably that my kids love school and truly can’t wait to go every morning! As the parent of a first year student, we could not be happier with LCA. Our daughter has thrived in the environment created by the LCA faculty and staff who show the students the type of love every parent would want. The education is first class and I am confident our daughter will be more than prepared for her next educational steps. AMAZING and would highly recommend to any family considering sending their children. Our family loves LCA! We have two elementary aged daughters, and they LOVE going to school each day. The teachers absolutely love the children and want the best for each one. They are truly devoted to the wellbeing of our children! We could not be more pleased with the Christ centered environment and challenging academics. We have 3 children that have been at LCA their entire academic career. We have been thoroughly pleased with our experience at this private Christian school. LCA offers top notch academics! We have two high schoolers currently and are very pleased with the various levels of curriculum - standard, college preparatory, Honors, AP, and dual credit. All 3 of our children have been heavily involved in extra curricular activities as well — sports, theatre, choir, robotics, academic team, leadership opportunities and much more. LCA goes above and beyond to provide a loving, nurturing and safe environment for all students across both of their campuses. We can’t say enough great things about our overall satisfaction and happiness at LCA. We selected LCA 3 years ago before our older son began middle school. He started his journey with LCA when the new sixth-grade academy opened. His younger sibling also transitioned to the Sixth- Grade Academy most recently. We feel that middle school and high school years are critical to ensure children receive not only rigorous academic and extra-curriculum programs but also solid spiritual and social foundations. LCA’s commitment to the students and families have helped both of our children to thrive and excel academically, as well as to continue to develop strong character and lasting friendships. Our children are happy and doing well and it is clear the school environment plays a big part in their well-being. Choosing private school is a huge sacrifice for most families, but at the end of the day, it can be life-changing for the kids. We look forward to continuing to partner with LCA for the remainder of the secondary education for our children.

My daughter was able to exempt several courses during her freshman year in college and has done quite well. South Pointe is an outstanding school in all aspects - academics, arts, and athletics. South Pointe High School Teachers and Administrative Staff do not follow District Employee Guidelines are absent quite often even durning exam reveiw and exam dates. Administration Staff do not know what is going in the class rooms of the teachers nor do they know if the teachers are present or not present for the day. AP History did not even cover the material needed to be covered in order for the students to be ready to handle or pass the AP exam. This school has so many issues that need to be dealt with that our three year experience has been a total nightmare. The Rock Hill School District Office does not know nor do they care about the problems with South Pointe High School. As was stated in the last Academic Awards Ceremony as long as we keep sending great football players to the University of South Carolina that is what matters. There is at least 10 to 15 disicipline problems a week fighting in lunchroom hallways bathrooms and classrooms. This school is out of control. South Pointe High School regularly produces high-achievers in academics, the arts and sports. Honesty and respect are emphasized and students are encouraged to believe in themselves. The staff is friendly, teachers willing to provide extra help, and the buildings and grounds are excellent. In addition, class size is smaller than that of the other two Rock Hill high schools. I have two children currently at Sout Pointe and have one who graduated last year. South Pointe has amazing teachers who truly care about their students and are invested in seeing them succeed! The parent groups (SIC, Academic and Sports Boosters) are extremely active and find a supportive administration at South Pointe. Please tour our school and meet with Dr. Al Leonard -Principal. You will be impressed. South Pointe has an open door policy for parents, and never once have I worried about the safety and well being if my children while they are at school. With 2 SPHS students, I have found everything about this school to be positive except for the perception others who know very little about the school have. Being the youngest of 3 high schools in the district has proven to be a challenge to overcome. Our boys are involved in athletics but that's not the highest priority even though SPHS has many state winning athletic programs. I feel that SPHS has provided our boys with what they need to succeed. The Arts, Academics, Athletics and so much more makes SPHS a great school. If you have not visited SPHS you certainly need to do that. Talk to those who are a part of "the South Pointe family" and form your own opinion. I know you will agree that SPHS is one of the BEST schools in this area! GO STALLIONS!!! SPHS gives our kids all of the opportunities we could ask for to succeed; strong academics with some really excellent teachers, award winning arts programs, and great athletics, to name a few. All in a school that is small enough that your child does not get lost in the crowd. Thanks, Dr. Leonard! My son was an IB Student and wanted/needed to be challenged. The IB Program at SP exceeded his/our expectations. Plus the over all experience at the school was outstanding for hem and for us. I was able to have a unique experience with having 2 high school students at 2 different high schools at one time due to rezoning. We were much more pleased with the administration and teachers at SP than we were at the school across town. Our 2 children that graduated from SPHS were both prepared for college. All around they had wonderful high school experiences. Proud to be Stallions!! South Pointe High School was the perfect school for me to grow as a performer and a learner. I left prepared to college academically, and prepared to function in a place with people from all different parts of the country and world due to my experiences in the IB program. Doctor Leonard works hard to be fully invested in everything going on at school from football games to musicals. I transferred to South Pointe for its opportunities and it was the best decision I've ever made. South Pointe High School is the best, most well-rounded school in this Rock Hill area. Teachers encourage students and care for their success, both in and out of the classroom. Administration is on top of any and all problems that arise within the school and work well to keep everyone at the school staff. Students support each other, no matter who they are or what they are involved in. We had just as many people in the auditorium to watch the arts students perform as were in the stands to watch football games and other sporting events. Al Leonard is the best, most supportive principal out there. He works to make sure he meets his students and works extremely hard to ensure that they succeed in academics and curricular activities. I have nothing bad to say about my experience there. GO STALLIONS LIVE THAT SOUTH POINTE WAY! We recently arranged a transfer for our son to go to South Pointe for his senior year after attending a cross-town school. We did it for the strong journalism and dual credit programs: journalism beats all other options hands down and he wants to work in sports journalism. South Pointe has great teachers and great programs for students. There is help for students who aren't getting the best grades and programs to help those excelling to continue to make strides. SPHS offers a wide range of diversity . The staff is terrific and the teachers go out of their way to help their students. The theatre program and Art programs are amazing! My daughter feels safe and cared about at SP. It is definately a nuturing environment! We transferred in as a 9th grader because I hear such good things about this school. We can't play sports for 365 days from transferring and it is worth it to be at a school with STEM program.

column1: From what I have observed, Marshall is a great school with wonderful teachers, students and an outstanding principal. They have had problems in the past but things have definitely turned around for the better. Bad language, student conduct and parent involvement have all made a tremendous change for the better. Students now enjoy going to the school and student expectations are much higher than ever before.Last year the graduating class of 2012 at Marshall HS had the second highest dollar amount of scholarships awarded in FBISD. Marshall is on the right path to become one of the most outstanding schools in Fort Bend ISD. GREAT JOB BUFFS! Keep up the good work! I graduated from Thurgood Marshall in 2009. And it certainly did not prepare me for college. Of course I was a star athelete and had multiple scholarship offers in football, but all my hopes and dreams of letting footbal be my ticket went down the drain after having 2 knee surgeries. There is no community involvement, the moral of the school tended to be low. I am not sure how much it has changed but gangs was a real big ordeal at my time of going to Marshall '05-'09. Since I have been out of High School 80 of my fellow classmates that I know are in jail. And at least 9 have been killed since 2009 (currently 2012). It is not totaly the school or the teachers fault. The district adds fuel to the demise of Thurgood Marshall, by not paying it any attention and most definitely giving it no support what so ever. At one point the school had started to pick up and become "succesful", but the district does not want that for a prodominetly African-American school. How do I know? Because any minute piece of success or positive light that comes to the school wether it be academic or sports related, count on the district to "re-zone students" or "Reassign adminstrators/teachers". I was long term sub for two months. Really worse experience ever in my life. This school is made for those who has no aim in their life. Students are promoted to not to work and learn. Teacher support them to have free grades. Parents are concerned about their kids grades rather than their knowledge. Really they just care for their grades. Most of teacher are subbing there. Most of the classes have no permanent teacher for 6-8 months. Parents if you love your kid do not choose this school. my school strives to give the children the foundation they need for successful careers. I have been a parent fhere beginn from 2005 and must say thatthat graduate wnt on to coplete her graduate studies at Harvard University School School of Law!! is now a well sought after atorney but also a well rounded citizen who loves community service and believes in giving back!! Thanks TMHS!!!!! Lets be clear. Thurgood Marshall High School is a high school none the less. Here you will find students just like any other high school. Ones who care and ones who don't. That does not have any reflection on the teachers who are there and have been there for years now. Teachers there are good people as well as the staff. This is a place full of people finding themselves and adults steering them towards graduation. How dare you say "if you love your children do not send them here"?. If you raised your children correctly you can send them to the slums and they'll still achieve everything you sent them for. School is not where your children are raised, home is. I love you Thurgood Marshall. This school should be shut down. I was a staff member at this school last year....singlular....one YEAR, and because of what occured at TMHS, I will never step foot in a classroom again. Overall, the kids run the school, because the kids act out, cry to mommy and daddy (while lying), mom or dad cries to the principal, and the child who is causing the issues gets to return to class with no consequences for their actions.With that being said, no, all the kids aren't "bad". Actually, most of them are quite pleasant. It's the few bad apples that tear the whole school down.Parents: you may think that you're doing the right thing by "vouching" for your child, but in reality, what you're doing is setting your child up for failure. In the real world, when a person is out of order, they get the boot, especially for those of us of the melanin persuasion. So, by defending your kid in their wrongdoing, you are only teaching them the wrong principles. College professors and deans don't care about how you feel, despite the fact that you are paying for your child's education. Overall, if Marshall had parents that are actually raising thier kids, instead of showing them how to beat the system, maybe, just MAYBE, TMHS could thrive. However, the reality of that happening is slim to none, and as time goes on, there will continue to a revolving door of principals, APs, and teachers. If you are a parent who is actually doing your job by teaching your child the right principles in life, then my advice to you is to send your child to Ridge Point, Clements, or Hightower (if you are going to put your kid in one of the many academies). But the better choice all together is to send them to a Katy or Cy-Fair ISD school. Happy Schooling! Horrible experience. Principals and staff never answer the phone. Everytime I encounter them it is unorganized and unprofessional. The leadership is there and the school will prepare your kid for college. I really recommend if you want the best for your child. kids fight to much but the teachers are nice I guess it’s like most other schools

column3: I am just fed up with RCHS! School started in August! It is now November and my child has had a total of 4 Spanish teachers! There is a constant revolving door of teachers at this school! Get it together Rockdale! Aren't you tired of being the underdog? Hi my name is A and i went to this school four years was suppose to graduate 2013 and i finished at open campus because i was given a class that i failed from 9th grade that i retook and this school is highly unprofessional and the only reason anybody would want to go to this school is because of the sports that's it the overall teacher population has declined i was actually told from a teacher "i don't care i'm still going to get my pay check. Not a good environment to learn, the school cares more about they're appearance than the students learning and experience. And i finished my classes and i still yet to receive my diploma due to many excuses.I hate this school i would not recommend it to anyone and not just because of petty reasons.Go to Heritage or Salem or a private school anything but this school. This is a great school i am currently going here and both my brothers, my mom, both aunts cousins, and pretty much everyone on my moms side. This school has wonderful athletic and acadenic programs. They are willing to work with those students who fall behind and have numerous steps to ensure they graduate(if they are willing to work hard). Also they have the best athletics in the county. The negatives that i would like to see improved are more school spirit from the staff & students. Also more interaction with the students from the staff in the office and counselors(seems some are there just for the check). However this ia wonderful school and the best way to enjoy it is to get involved and join things. This is my daughters first year of high school and their registration process is horrible!! Thank you Rockdale County High for making the beginning of my childs first year a horrible experience I have nothing good to say about anybody I have had interactions with. If they hadn't have held up the registration process, she may have her schedule!! She supposed to walk around the school aimlessly? Rockdale county schools are TERRIBLE. The high school is worse. I have never seen a school that allows students to do whatever they want. The dress code is not recognized and students are very rude. This is an atrocity and something needs to be done ASAP. The class rooms are overwhelming over crowded. it sucks. this school is the worst one ive been to.

column1: I like the school very much, the only thing i see that needs to improve is have teachers after school be more supportive. Academically this school has a lot to offer, however be warned parents there is a group of truly bad students that are often involved or talking about doing unspeakable things as well as fighting. Make sure your children know how to pick friends and this school can be a blessing NOT A good choice if you have a student who excels in academics. After completing all graduation requirements in 3 years, my student could not attend a 7th period band class and attend Lake Tech full time . Lake Tech gave her some hands on experience in her field that she is pursing in College. Band and Music is a love and interest since 6th grade. Hmmmm One did not interfere with the other. The staff has been wonderful. Administration and teaching faculty are working hard for the students.

column3: I feel bullying should be handled A.S.A.P,I felt this was a good school.When something drastic happens,the school do not know how to deal with the problem.I reported bullying and never got called in for a meeting,a return call or anything.the bullies are still picking with children and maybe if we parents go to channel 4 something will be done. Strong leadership, hard-working teachers who stay current with best teaching practices, a small and tight-knit community...Cleve Hill is a place to be proud of and one of Erie County's hidden gems. Horrible experience after having my daughter attend one year she went into depression and I had to have her transferred out.

column1: My kids are in Hardin Valley elementary now. We hear only great things about the school. My 1st grader class and I enjoyed a field trip there last year 2012. What I would to know is when is the highschool going to receive a score on greatschools.org? That matters to me. We moved to Knoxville from out of state, and have two daughters at Hardin Valley Academy. They have felt comfortable there from the first day. The kids have been nice to them, and even invited them to eat lunch the first day so they were not uncomfortable. It is a large school, but my girls do not feel like they are a number. They are taking many challenging and interesting classes like Orchestra, French, AP, etc. We are very pleased with our decision to purchase a home in this school's district so that my kids can attend the Hardin Valley schools. We moved from the Farrugut school district with the hopes this school would be just as great. But it has been nothing but problems. First of all, the school is over crowded. They have to make multiple bus trips for the same route. The staff is less than stellar. They literally mocked my child because she was upset they screwed up her schedule and she has to take throw away classes that do NOT count towards her desired course of study because of crowding issues. The guidance office does not contact the parents to help work out these issues. I would talk about the attitude of the children who attend this school, but I do not want to offend other parents. Lets just say this school sucks and I regret EVER buying a home in its district. HVA is absolutely the most progressive high school in the county. Moving into the zone to send our kids there is the best move ever. The administration has defined goals and an outstanding staff; the teacher, teaching methods, Academy approach are all focused toward the student excelling in a particular area before graduating. The advanced level of certain classes, AP level courses, and outstanding extra curricular clubs and events are all top notch. The athletics programs and facilities are first rate, as are my kids coaches. All 5 stars for our family. Dear the parent that made a comment in August, You have to realize that in August, the staff are overwhelmed with many schedule conflicts due to the school year starting, it happens in every school. The staff do not mock the students, they may joke around with the kids because it relieves tension and creates a more friendly bond that makes kids comfortable with being around them and confronting them with issues, like your child did. Also, HVA has a wonderful academic program and even if your child's class doesn't go to their preferred field of study, there is room for extra classes in the schedule that don't have to be part of the focus, that's what block scheduling is for. Furthermore, every school has overcrowding. It comes with the growing human population and even if you had stayed in the Farragut district, you would have the same issues there. Even though HVA isn't the most perfect school, it's still in a lot better conditon than others, and the staff is trying to figure out the best way to run things but the school is still considered new if compared to surrounding schools, so it still has some flaws. our Academy is wonderful community of students- all shapes, sizes, & smarts- and teachers- also all shapes, sizes, smarts and empathetic- , along with an administration ( both at HVA and in the county school system) who see the bigger picture in their planning of courses, advanced opportunities and academy endorsements. And the athletics and arts opportunities are awesome too! Just six years ago, Hardin Valley Academy is Knox County's largest high school with just over 2,000 students, with its students divided into four academies- Business/Law/Public Affairs, Liberal Arts, Health Sciences, and STEM. HVA enables staff and students to collaborate on educational projects in all academic areas. The school offers multiple AP and Honors track courses plus dual enrollment opportunities at the nearby community college. Its 2014 grads were awarded $22 million in scholarships last year. The school boasts nationally recognized a first rate band, orchestra, arts, and theatre program plus TSA, FIRST Robotics team 3824, an award-winning yearbook, DECA, HOSA, and diverse extra-curricular programs. The sports department features several state champions and numerous opportunities for student participation. Challenging academics, caring staff, and amazing students foster a terrific atmosphere. Administrators know your kids and support them in so many ways. PART 1 As a student that attends Hardin Valley let me give you some advice. Firstly, all over the walls and floors of HVA there are stains from several unknown substances. In the gym I have seen what appears to be snot smeared on the walls, in the bathroom something brown around the toilets, and many other things including a variety of drink stains. There are dust bunnies everywhere covering every corner, dead bugs scattered about, and one time I found blood all over one of the water fountains. Classrooms seem to be kept reasonably nice, but bathroom and other areas of the school are not. Secondly, bullying is a huge problem at HVA. As a student I hear numerous ocassions of people being bullied, and it's not just any bullying. On a daily basis people get followed to their class, told to kill themselves, pushed, shoved, provoked, ridiculed, and shamed for their body type, skin color, and much more. Yet the teachers do nothing. Everyone who has talked to me about their cases of bullying has also gone to the office. They have had proof of bullying like text messages, they have broke down crying, and even been scared to go class. I am a student at HVA. I came from a small town with a class of 20 people. With that being said, I was terrified to leave the only place i had ever attended school to go to a school where I didn't have any friends. HVA is 10x bigger than what incas used to, when we walked in I was nervous, but the guidance office made me feel so welcome and helped me pick a academy. They were very respectful to my parents, gave me a personal tour and made sure I had someone to meet so that I was not alone at lunch. Over the past two years I have been there I have created a bond with the administration, had teachers stay and come early to help me further my studies, and went from failing grades to A's and B's. Moving to this school is the best thing that could've happened to me and I'm saddened to leave next year! The faculty here is top notch and devoted to the learning of all students. No matter who you are in this school, there is a place for you to fit in and belong. Hardin Valley Academy is an outstandng school providing support and educational opportunites for all students.i This was our first year back in the public school system after having homeschooled for 7 years. My son had a wonderful freshman year and we are very thankful for Hardin Valley Academy. Love the way the administration listens to parents, teachers and students! The kids from different backgrounds get along well. It is a safe and structured environment. There are always fun events in the works for the kids to look forward to! After school clubs adhere to all hobbies and interests of students. They are not limited to a couple groups’ interests. Students will have a variety of positive memories to look back on all their lives! My daughters have had a wonderful experience at HVA. The course work has been challenging and rewarding. The AP classes will definitely prepare them for college. The classes are completely over crowded. Unless you have a straight "A" student it is easy for kids to fall off the radar and not get the help/attention that they need to learn and get better grades. It is hard to get responses from teachers. Also the office administration in the front or answering the phone seems to be too busy/annoyed to help with any questions or concerns that you may have. I will be moving so that my younger son can go to a different school . My experience at Hardin Valley was fantastic. There are so many opportunities for students to get involved in clubs. sports, and other organizations that the only way a student would "fall off the radar" would be because they were not involved in anything outside of the bare minimum class time. My son was so excited about starting at HVA 4 years ago. Let me start to say yes the school offers great clubs or activities, but 50% of teachers along with principal not so great. When you address issues and they are partially issued, that is not good. When teachers tell students to look in your text book because you don't understand, well past time for that those teachers to retire (and they maybe teaching for 10 years?). And yes when a freshman has to go back to their 8th grade science teacher to get tutoring....well enough said there. Yes those teachers are still there. Anyway my son along with some friends have nothing positive to say. Kids will speak truth. My daughter had a great experience at HVA. The teachers in her classes were supportive and held students accountable for doing their work. As a result, she entered college well prepared for the rigor of college level work. The faculty seem to be well supported by the school leadership. There were many opportunities to volunteer and be involved in clubs and organizations- but students have to reach out, listen to announcements, check their school emails, and check the website for information.The area of the county this school is located in is the fastest growing portion of the district. The school is at capacity level to near overcrowding. I suspect that in the future, there will be redistricting. To feel informed, it is necessary for parents to keep up with communication and information by "plugging in" to the school's social media and the school's webpage for updates. The way this school handles sensitive issues is beyond inappropriate. The students appear to be drones with no active thinking for themselves. The principal is the worst, he is rude, callous, and pretentious. He feigns care and is overall haughty. I pulled my child from this school with no intention of ever returning. My oldest survived his time there, but has struggled in college. I do not believe this school is performing as it should. The teachers are heartless. I do not allow my children on social media or to have a phone and some assignments are available only on the phones so it presents a problem for the lower income or more structured parents who don't/can't provide access to those items. Student section during athletic events have a mob like mentality. Racial and personal statements being shouted out non stop! Administration does nothing about and it’s been going on and reported for years. I would not recommend this school for lack of character. Overall the education seems decent. But over the last three years, the rest has gone downhill. What used to be a nice campus is now full of litter every single day. If your child is a car rider, you will find that the parents cannot follow the very simple pick up procedure without taking up two lanes. And today my son was served moldy lunch. Apparently the good stuff is served during first lunch period, but they run out. I’m looking into moving my kid to online school for his senior year as it appears the administration no longer cares for the school and if it’s appearance is a reflection on how the kids are being treated, well it’s not good. I went to Hardin Valley a few years back and it was a great experience but it has gone downhill. With the new principal and staff my siblings have faced discrimination. Recently I went to the school and encountered a rude office staff. I wasn’t aware one couldn’t bring drinks from the outside and she gave me attitude about it, when I had told her I didn’t know. She proceeded to say “she wasn’t going to allow it” and looked down on me for not knowing. Before office staff were so nice and kind, now everything is changing.

column3: It's basically just the best school out there these days, not much else I can say. : ) If your child needs special services/ special education classes elementary and middle school are great you start high school the do not follow the transition IEP at all . I had to pull my 11th grader out in 10th & transferred to ALC . May have to do the same with my 9 th grader Its really sad that there is such awesome support up to high school then it like trying to talk to the walls to get these ppl to do their jobs and its like your voice and opinion are completely ignored I am currently a student here, and I really love it. The students and teachers here are all very nice, and the classes are challenging. Sometimes there are communication issues. There is also a wide variety of clubs and activities, and almost any student would be able to find something to join. The teachers are willing to help struggling students, and our advisory program focuses on making the school a better place for everyone. Overall, this school would be a 4 out of 5 stars for me. Terrible. This is an upper middle class school where you need to be following the latest trends or you are relentlessly picked on The inmates really are running the asylum—and that's not hyperbole. We moved to Woodbury for the public schools, really starting to regret that decision. Major drug, alcohol and vape use at the school, on school grounds in bathrooms during the day. Was so bad they had to close bathrooms during the day to monitor traffic. We talked with neighbors that have students here and their student avoided going to the bathroom at school unless he really had to go. Seems to be little done in the way to successfully curb it.Your child can change their name or gender without parental consent. Despite asking the school to disregard our child's request based on things we were dealing with at home, social media influences we noted, ongoing mental health struggles that predated any gender issues by years and on top of this just a noted desire to standout so our student chose this path the school still went ahead and granted our child's request. So much for being a partner with parents, respecting our wishes. I prefer a school that doesn't undermine a parents rights, authority or values.There seem to be some good teachers still that work with your child and work hard to educate kids. COVID has been hard on teachers and kids so this review is more about school administration and public school policy.

column1: Dont buy into all the hype trust me this school is LAME. First off everything about the school is boring it has no activities and the teachers put you to sleep. Im a sophmore at the school and its my first year here, and it will be my last! Some of these teachers barely speak english. The teachers dont even care about the students, this mite be the most uninteresting school in history. Sure it offers lots of stuff, but trust me you'll fall asleep on these teachers and you'll probably fail anyway. Whatever you do dont go to this school, you'll regret it! learning hot to appreciate and yes, utilize,My natural initiative and enthusiasm. I was one of those Students that if portrayed in a positive light would be called rambunctious, exuberant and smart. I'm a teenager after all, and our goals is to have a good time. I could turn any material into a good time, that is if teachers let me, and most did not. But these two teachers were different. They let us transform what could easily have been a very run-of-the-mill weekly vocabulary assignment in which we were to study and incorporate as many of the new words as possible into our new enhanced Attitudes. With their blessing I try to remember that as a teenager,with all the issues and concerns that any normal teenager has, what I most wanted and appreciated was learning in a light, enjoyable way. And for this I always tell myself that if im not being engaged, or dare I say, entertained in some way,most likely im probably not learning, at least not in any meaningful way. This generation is full of teenagers and they are different. I try to remember this when facing my own reality. I am not always successful but i will be if i work at it. Administrative personnel and teachers are extremely helpful and caring both with students and parents which makes any problem or concern be resolved right away. Opportunities to advance and get the best out of school are unlimited - great asset for students who really care about their future I graduated from William h Turner tech from the television production program in 2010 and I'm in college now studying Mass communication with a concentration in journalism with a minor in television production and I can most definitely say that Turner tech have prepared me for college. It may not have sports but, I did run track at Miami central. And, that payed my way through college. I'm glad I went to Turner Tech instead of Miami Central. I have nothing against central Turner Tech is a school where if a student is willing to learn they will but however if they aren't interested in learning this is not the best place to be. If one does not have an interest in education they'll automatically fail at this school and really give he or she a bad reputation on their life and it'll show in their grades in the future. To conclude this, Turner Tech is a great school as long as the child put an effort in he or she studies. Current Sophomore.. 8.6 out of 10 , it Is for those who want to learn

We were going to pull our child out of this school for safety reasons, but they reassured us that our child would not be harmed. All of my four years st BHS have been very enjoyable, besides the stress that comes with being a high school student! This school does an excellent job in preparing you for college. column1: NKHS has made great strides over the course of the past 5 years. I believe it will continue to improve as the population increases. It is worth noting that NKHS is one of the only schools in the Central VA region that has survived the financial crisis. Other counties have completely cut entire programs (advanced placement, foreign language, art, music, drama, etc) and have eliminated teaching positions in an effort to save face financially. As an outsider looking in at SBO meetings and "town hall" style meetings- the SBO has made every effort to find suitable solutions with their teachers, administration, and community so that the most important component: the students- don't suffer. They have their fare share of problems, but unlike other schools- they attempt to handle them in a way that involves community. I feel that makes a big difference. Please be sure to take into account that most of the reviews are quite dated. As an employee, I can tell you that a large majority of the faculty/staff have very good intentions and want to be an active part of student success. NKHS is not immune to the ever-increasing demands and stresses of demonstrating student achievement. However, most staff AND students care about success and are invested. Moreover, there are many opportunities for academic challenge, with increased Dual Enrollment, Advanced Placement options and the introduction of the first technical center/ STEM academy in more than 20 years. There is an eye on continuos improvement as well. NKHS is a great place to develop and learn. They did a horrible job with my education. The case manager I had didn't even try her best or the one before her. The school at the time should of had a tutor program for me to catch up and being in all regular classes instead of putting me in slow classes. They just had a messed up program at the time. Idk If Its getting better or not but I will not put my kids in New Kent schools ever! They are all terrible! All of my school years I was with them nothing got better for me. They were holding me back cause they didn't want me to do good in all regular classes. Very bad experience with them! The central office (school board) admin are absolutely terrible. They have run out several great teachers and administrators who have questioned the all powerful "oz" director of admin. There are a few lap dogs and petty admin who don't dare question the status quo and have cut off their nose to spite their face. Great kids and great teachers but just a shame that they are rotting from the top down. After having dealt with Henrico County Schools(West End), New Kent has been a breath of fresh air..They are excellent schools! Keeps parents informed through Trojan News phone calls,emails and texting. Love the use of Chromebooks. Keeps the kids relevant in today's workforce. 9/10 for expience. New Kent is Strong! Because of the illegal substance abuse, if I had any other HS option we would probably take it but unfortunately since we live in New Kent, we are stuck with no other options than NKHS.

Deans harass students constantly. (I was verbally abused for holding hands with another student, and written up pulling on a winter hat on a -15 degree day just before I left the building, for example.) Teachers have either given up, or don't care. Young, up-to-date teachers are fire over those who should've retired 20 years ago. Bathrooms are disgusting at all times, classrooms are overcrowded and small. Teachers "teach" from the textbook, word-for-word, and focus exclusively on standardized tests. Unless you are a student involved in a sport or one of the many gangs,, you will absolutely hate it here. Unless you join the academy, you will NOT receive a quality education. Advice to deans, staff, and police security officers: Stop harassing students for IDs, hats, and holding hands. Start worrying about the rampant gangs, bullying, awful teaching standards, theft, and general unsafe and unsanity environment you are forcing children to spend 8+ hours a day, 5 days a week in. They had an outstanding experience at the school, so much that I one of my children is studying to become a teacher and wants to go back to SHS to teach. They both were academically challenged, received good scores on their ACTs, both attend college and received outstanding scholarships. The school is diversely populated which gave them a sense to treat everyone as their brother or sister. Are their problems in the HS, yes, all high schools have problems, but it is the parents responsibility to be in tune with their children. I will always be proud that I attended SHS, because it is where I got my second chance to be the person I want to be today. I believe this school was a blessing to me. Go sabers! Not that great, if I could grade it I’d give Streamwood High School a C-. The disorganized operation, unanswered email, and lock downs make a higher grade impossible. From a parents perspective, I am very concern with Streamwood High school . My daughter recently transferred to this school and she is already lost all motivation she had in finishing high school. If i could go back , I would . i am disappointed in this school i thought it was better. a couple of students have been arrested for stealing from other kids and destroying school property. some of the teachers are nuts make accusations they cannot back up. you go to the school to get things resolved and they say lets just move past this. very unhappy. my child is failing major in one of her classes and cannot get anyone to call me back Before attending Hollywood Hills, I had spent 10 years in a private school. Now, I'm not entirely sure what other public schools are like, bear with me. I feel as though freshman year didn't offer as many options for me as I would've liked. I could have easily been in AP English with the seniors, but I was instead put into an honors class where the teacher appeared to view my ability as an annoyance. In my Integrated Science Honors class, I was practically teaching the other students. In Computer Engineering, we sat in a classroom that didn't have computers. We should have had them. My only saving grace was Creative Writing. The teacher was the best I've ever had, and I cannot recommend her class highly enough. She really made my year, and got me involved in all of the after-school activities Hills has to offer. Sadly,many of the students at Hills behave in an atrocious manner. They seem to know little and have no interest in learning anything. There are some decent students, however. AP classes and Creative Writing seem to contain better quality people. Because of the ACE academy, my sophomore year will contain some great classes, I can say that much. Physics, Pre-AP English, ect. This school just keeps getting worse and worse. The teacher's are unable to academically challenge their students, but I guess that doesn't really matter when none of them want to learn. In addition to the mediocre teaching and atrocious behavior of the students, Hills dropped to a "D" rated school which means that the all the attending students received a letter allowing them to transfer to a different school in the area, and that's just what most of them did... so now all the students who wanted to learn transferred to a different school. Honestly, good for them; they dont deserve to be in an academically inadequate environment. My husband graduated from HHHS and now our child is a freshman. So far the experience has been very positive - academically, athletically and in school spirit. As a graduating honor student of Hollywood Hills I can truly say I have wasted 4 years. I feel like I learned very little and the administration is quite unfair. Aside from picking favorites not only did the Principal had purchased AP books in which we could not take home to study with, when our class was filled with painting fumes and we special requested to do our work quietly in the patio. As we sat down, her along with 4 unnecessarily mean security guards came and escorted us rudely into the library (which was closed to all students except for kids who have failed the FCAT 4 years in a row) to have us (Four top of the class AP students) to work on the library floor in a corner instead of in the empty fresh-air patio. I am sick of being under appreciated and have my time wasted at such a facility. They don't even offer any variety or interesting classes. Oh and the guidance counselor had told me and many other students we will never go to college. I am currently admitted to a very high accredited Florida University. Send your kids to a nicer school. :-) Parents please listen to me when i tell you do not put your child in this school. This school gets worse and worse every year. The administrators do not care about a single thing. The school dirty and small. The kids do what they want, and its just not somewhere you want your kid to be at for thier first year of high school. Im just waiting for bcps to close it down. Horrible. Horrible. Horrible. This school is a disgrace to the bcps system. Academically, its just not somewhere to put your kids. The hallways are not presentable. The school is very very small. The administrators are there just to be there. Save your child and throw away the thought of putting your child here for the next 4 years of their life. One of the coaches put it very appropriately: "We have everything you need here, good and bad. As long as your daughter stays around good kids and wants to do well, she will get everything she needs." The horrible politicians in Tallahassee, including our criminal governor, have done little to help the school systems. Too many classes in portables; needs updating throughout the buildings; needs SEATING around their playing fields; a concrete track that should be surfaced with rubber to protect athlete's legs; has cut down on bus routes forcing many children to walk more than half a mile across major intersections to get on a bus; and needs to pay their teachers more money. A very good military academy, many honors and advance placement classes, an involved PTSA and some excellent coaches. Football, flag football and volleyball coaches and teams are top-notch. I spent last year searching for a great college for my older daughter and learned that most high school seniors have little understanding of where they should go to college. I have volunteered-officially-with the school and no one takes advantage of the great lessons I have learned. More parents need to participate. I had been a student at Hollywood hills high school for the past 4 years now,but many will give the school a bad review & to be honest I wouldn't have scored such a very high rating if it wasn't for my experience in the Magnet program, Hollywood Hills Military Academy. I have tended classes on both sides & worked with the staff on both sides. The Academy has they're own set of staff, these administrators try their out best in providing the needs to their cadets (Students in the academy are refer to cadets). There is always some one they could talk to whether it's about grades or something personal, they are always there for them. Most the teachers are very helpful, if you need help with any subject there is normally peer tutoring 4 days a week & teachers normally stay an extra 30 mins to a few hours after school to finish grading & be there for any students who need to come in talk to them. Most of teachers will stay after school and schedule tutoring times if a student need a 1 on 1 session. Most teachers in the academy also provide opportunities for grade improvement. Anything from extra credits assignment and re-doing to projects for finals. Unlike main campus teacher, I have seen many who struggle to meet individuals needs & many are gone out of the door once school ends.Hills & Academy has their own office & information are found quicker & easier in the academy office than in the front office. It takes forever to finally make an appointment , get transcripts, or have a simple question answer but the Academy help aids the student to get the information they are looking for quicker.I have read comments who they feel they wasted their 4 years but to be honest I felt like I gain a lot more than any other high school could have given me. The Academy had help me apply for colleges , understand the process, open me to scholarships opportunists, & help me create a future. It's not just to get an high school diploma for cadets but to make them college & career bound. I've learn skills that would stick with me and I am thankful for, even though the classes are all honors & AP, & could keep one very busy , the challenge is worth it & the struggles pays off after allI could write more but my space is running out, & if you want a special high school experience & life long skills , give the Military academy a try, it would be worth it in the end. My daughter is a freshmen at Hollywood Hills Military Academy Is a wonderful school but you have sergeant's like segeant Gonzales who can make things very hard for your kids. My daughter is a member of the Drill Team with a 4.2 GPA which we all know the hard work it is to keep a 4.0 GPA or higher . EVERY TIME she wants to join anything that has to do with the DRILL TEAM she is never picked so it makes me wonder if the students are beinging picked academically or favoritism. I confronted him regarding the issue and he is heck of a sarcastic person and I can be as sarcastic as him. I spoke to my daughter and told her to keep working hard and still keep her eye on the prize . I am a Hills graduate and live one mile away. The students and teachers are good and campus is safe. It is not a "wealthy school" like it was when I went there. But it is still a good quality public school. I visit campus occasionally as part of my current job duties as a teacher trainer. I'm not sure why some of the comments say it is a small school, as if this is a bad thing. Your kids will get more personalized attention here than at the big schools.

This is a great high school! St. Pius X has been an outstanding high school for my two sons. One received a full ride to Architecture School at the University of Houston Honors program and my other son received a full ride to Honors Engineering at Texas A&M as well. They both participated in sports, student council, national honor society, ambassadors, etc. They were never bullied or excluded from any activities; had many great friends who traveled with us because they were like family to us; teachers and counselors worked with us; I regularly volunteered and attended games, plays and concerts. My youngest son was a National Hispanic Scholar and AP Scholar. I went to school here after transferring from Houston Christian High school and it made all of the difference. They enforce rules but have freedoms, they let you be who you want to be, and I was definitely prepared for college. Worlds away from Houston Christian High school.

column3: Both of my kids graduated from LHS. My daughter is an honor student in Purdue's engineering program, and my son now owns his own business after graduating with honors from Purdue also. Without the preparation from LHS, neither of my children would be so successful. I always felt tremendous support from LHS and TriCreek. School is a dual effort: It starts at home, ends at home, and school can't make up for lack of parenting or leadership that parents needs to exhibit. The Administration lacks any kind of common sense and really do not care about the students just about their statistics. They offer no vocational classes such as welding, metal or wood shops, etc. The students grades mostly consist of participation instead of work performed. I would not recommend anyone to send their children to this school system I am currently a sophomore at this sad excuse for an educational facility. I have been in the Lowell school district for my entire life, and ever since I got into high school, everything became statistical, not about actually learning. No matter how often the facilitators say they care about the students and their well being, that is a huge white lie. They don't care about us. They just care about having a successful school. There are only a few teachers who actually care about us, and most of them are treated like absolute garbage by the school district; on the verge of being fired due to the fact they don't conform to the 'New-Tech' standards. I have gone to the guidance department countless times due to bullying/harassment in classes, only to have all of it blamed on myself. I attempted to take it to the principal, only to have it dismissed, yet again. Might I word it differently, this school cares more about statistics than the students safety. On December 15, there were three, legitimate threats to this school. Yes, the police were involved. The 'heads' of the school knew about this days in advance, but took no precautionary measures until the DAY OF. We were placed on lockdown the second we got into our first hour class, but the school continued to let students and other people in and out, DURING the lockdown. There is no excuse for that. They put us at risk, and lied to the media, our parents, and us, saying the threat was false, when really there were two indoor threats and one outdoor threat. If you want your children to get a quality education, I suggest you run FAR away from Lowell, and if you are a student currently entering the high school, or are a student here, my condolences. Great school! Great classes! Great athletics! Best school in area

column1: This school stinks, they never have homework, they study for major tests that are designed to give the school and teachers more moinies, but they hardly ever learn anything new. Unless you are a highly motivated, self starter on your own, this school is for babysitting only! I currently attend LHS and I canhonestly say this school has its good and bad overviews. Things come easily to me but sometimes even I have difficulty understanding a certain teacher's teaching method. Over all, this is a good school with a caring principal and lovable staff.

I have never seen a school like central, racist, discrimination.

column3: This is the greatest little high school in the upstate! We moved from a larger high school to Clinton High School this year and the teachers really work with my child to make sure she is successful. Go Devils! My child has had a wonderful experience at Clinton High School. She is a senior this year. Thank you to everyone at CHS for working with me to help my daughter. Just moved here from out of state and our family has been so impressed with Clinton High School. Beautiful school with great things going on for our kids! As always has been a great school, they also just had one the highest academic graduating classes.

column1: This school when it comes to a learning curriculum, is pretty good one of the best in Illinois. However this school has one of the worst bullying problems i have ever experienced. Six years that are supposed to be some of the best of your life, ruined by the schools inability to acknowledge and deal with the problems. I not only went to different teachers, but also the deans and principals and nothing was done. i have now moved to a much better school. but i am still haunted by the memories of Beecher High School. This school sucks. The teachers don't help you if you being bulled. They have cut alot of classes. They can't even maintain a Spanish teacher. Spanish is the only foreign language we can take. If your think of moving here think again it's a terrible school. They could make the school better by gettin more foreign language options and bring back more classes. I had to transfer out of this school after two of the worst years of my life. The teachers are inconsiderate and unhelpful. The principal is a joke and did not help me when I was continuously being harassed by other students nor when I returned after facing a family emergency. The teachers will not make time to help you and one claimed to me he was "too busy to tutor me". Do not enroll your kids in this school unless you want them to experience 4 of the most horrendous years of their lives in which they feel miserable and alone as opposed to 4 years they should be enjoying and actually learning during their time in school. The worst school in the planet, okay maybe not an planet but it is the worst school ever. Just six months in beecher and we are moving right back to Bartlett Illinois, where students do matter to teachers and help them every step of the way. If you're moving to Beecher please don't, you'll regret it just like I did

column1: I believe that Bishop Luers offers the most comprehensive highschool program in the area. When considering academic excellence, along with arts, athletics, community, diversity, and those intangibles that the Luers community simply refer to as "Luers Spirit," we believe that Bishop Luers has the best program in the Fort Wayne area for educating the WHOLE person. We looked carefully at a number of local schools, both "private" and public and gave careful consideration to academics as well as those other factors that are critical to assisting children in becoming true "renaissance" individuals. Bishop Luers offers a complete selection of Honors, AP, and Dual Credit courses to provide academic challenges for students and have an indisputable tradition of excellence in the arts and in athletics as well. Luers provides the same welcome to all students and has an environment which creates a true "home" for students with diverse backgrounds and interests. We looked very hard for a school we felt we could trust our children to and we are thrilled that we could find a school like Bishop Luers. Our son is a freshman this year and could not be happier. He feels right at home. My oldest child is a freshman at Luers this year making him the first of the third generation of Knights in our family! Bishop Luers seems to always grow and change and improve the curriculum without ever compromising the excellent tradition and values of previous generations! GREAT school, GREAT tradition, GREAT LUERS SPIRIT!! Bishop Luers has provided me with a great education. I got into my first choice college and I have Luers to thank for that. The teachers are excellent and I have learned to much from them. Luers offers so many extra curricular activities from Sports to the Arts to Academic Super Bowl. I have had a fantastic time during my time at Luers and I will never forget everything Luers has done for me. Luers is a pretty nice school to attend IF you can tolerate uniforms, and some strict rules. Mrs. Keefer is the best principal I have ever had, and the assistant principal is very involed with things as well. The tuition is steep(5000.00+) and some students can get away with things easily and the administration sometimes will not help you with it. They give friday and saturday schools frequently and although i have never got one they can be annoying when you get one for just being tardy. My freshmen year was OK at best. My two students were bullied horribly while they attended this school. The staff did little to help the situation, and transferring my children may have been one of the best parenting decisions of my life. This is my child's 2nd yr here and he has not had any problems really and when he did they were addressed and taken care of, my child really likes it there and I like it too, even though we are not Catholic they treat us all the same and we have family members that are Alumni's of Luers and still relatives that attend there, I would recommend it to anyone and very glad I sent my youngest child here where I feel he is in a safe environment and getting a good education, my child struggles in certain areas & they have bent over backwards to help him and I am very grateful for them. One of the Premier schools in Indiana, the athletics are exceptional, curriculum offered are various to suit your needs, and provides a spiritual awakening for some kids, God Bless Hands down the best decision we made for our child. We transferred from Canterbury to Bishop Luers and never looked back. Parents, kids and administration are down to earth and always supporting your educational needs. I was completely turned off by Canterbury on our exit interview. They used every trick in the book and trashed Luers in the process. Talk about class acts. Overall, Luers has educated to every level and beyond compared to Canterbury. Wish we would have made the move sooner. Go Knights!!! Bishop Luers is a great school. We sent our children there for the academics and the Christian atmosphere. They have a very strong curriculum and many extra curricular activities. My children participated in Show Choir, sports and many of the clubs. Mrs. Keefer is the best principal and cares about every student at that school. Bishop Luers is a great school. The teachers have sincere interest in their students' success. Bishop Luers is a great school. There are so many opportunities. Not only do you get a great education, but you can also be on a great sports team or be in a music program or in a play. Students can go on educational trips. Every year there are trips offered to Spain, France, Japan, Haiti or some other interesting place. Teachers really care and go out of their way to help you learn as much as possible. I am truly grateful for my four years at Bishop Luers and I am leaving for college confident that I have the background I need to succeed at the next level. Great school. My son is a junior and he is new at Luers this year. He was a straight A student at his old school but never felt challenged. He never felt like he was really learning enough. He really wants to get into a good college, so we decided to look for a college prep school for him for this year. We looked at a number of different schools but none of them seemed right until we visited Bishop Luers. Everyone was so nice and very helpful. Both the students and staff were so friendly and welcoming. When we left after our visit, my son said that he thought Luers was the place. After only the first week of school, we now know that we made the right choice. In only one week, my son says he is learning so much. Even though he felt like he is maybe behind the other kids in his classes, his teachers have been very helpful. All he has to do is ask, and the teachers just offer to stay after school to help him with whatever he needs. What a great school. So glad we made the decision. If you are looking for a great school that will help your student prepare for college, you should look at Bishop Luers. We are sure glad we did! I loved going to school at Luers.
