column3: My school is one that will help me thorough my life and career in this school(Cedar Ridge). I have come to learn that this place WILL take you places you want to reach. Cedar Ridge is a fantastic school. The education opportunities for the students include many honors courses, AP courses, IB program, and Middle College. Great extra-curricular activities through many clubs and sports. The school has slightly more than 1000 students now but the facilities were designed to handle that. There are plans to construct another building in the next few years because the feeder area for the school continues to grow. Teachers are politically motivated instead of teaching the basic items students need to be productive citizens Teachers should not be teaching their political opinions to our children, they should be teaching behavior and strategy from the schools curriculum. I am a student at Cedar Ridge and so far my experience has been great! They offer many different athletic and cultural extra curricular activities, in addition to extensive offerings in AP and IB classes. I have been able to make lots of new friends and I have found that Cedar Ridge is much more "homey" and welcoming as compared to other schools in the area. This is most likely due to the fact that Cedar Ridge is on the small side for a high school based on the number of students it currently has enrolled. Other people on this page have been discussing a particular issue with a teacher sharing their political views with their class earlier this year, however this teacher has since left the school and the administration has done a good job of making sure that other teachers are not including their personal beliefs in their lessons. Overall, this school is one of the best that I have attended. I am a student at Cedar Ridge and over the past couple of years the school has gone downhill. Overall they have nice facilities but don't let that fool you. Since they have lost the majority of their best faculty and staff, students are left with very few outstanding teachers. As a student I only recognize the principal, and other faculty are still unknown to me. This year Cedar Ridge's athletics have also suffered. The overall high school experience has diminished since we only had a JV football team. The walls are left bare due to the lack of color and personality within the school and students withhold a sense of school pride. Pep rally's have been taken away from students because of overly strict policies that don't allow students to have fun. This leads students to the decision to leave school before any "fun" activities. Lunch time is also a disaster because students are forced to schedule themselves for tutoring even if they're doing fine is classes. During lunch students aren't allowed to leave campus even though Cedar Ridge is only a few miles from downtown Hillsborough. Cedar Ridge has potential to be a great school but it is going to take time to make a change to the current situation. I'm a teacher in this school and I feel like it is a supportive teaching environment and administration turnover is a bit concerning, but all of our individual administrators does their best. The other teachers work hard. Students here are not any better or worse than other schools where I have taught, although they recognize the lack of consistency in administrators and know they can get away with a lot more before disciplinary action is taken. Our school would benefit from consistent leadership and a strong supportive leader.

column1: I am a graduate of both Cabrini Elementary and High school, and had a great experience. I felt that we had successful, well-supported athletics, and fairly high academics. I was just an average student in high school and still found myself being well-prepared in college. I found that many of my college classmates were struglling with things I already learned in high school. The faculty had high behavioral and academic expections in the elementary and high school. Went to grade and high school at Cabrini. I know of several alumni had their children and now grandchildren attend. To me that is the best reference a school could have! I went to grade and high school at Cabrini and now my child goes to a metro public school. Seeing the public education my child is getting I can't believe how poor the math, science, and language programs I received at Cabrini. Apparently the public schools cherry-pick the best teachers and Cabrini can't afford to compete with that. If a parent is searching for a good school for their children, use the MEAP scores in the 90's where you will find the great public schools. They care more about enforcing their uniform policy and giving out detentions than they do in helping the students.The religious and the staff don't walk the talk of being a Christian.The high profile sports get top priority and the other sports and activities get neglected along with the students that aren't star athletes. If your student is struggling and needs help they are pretty much on their own. Very dissapointed to say the least. Not inpressed with this school at all. This used to be a good school. it's not worth the money. My son attended Cabrini for high school. In my opinion it is worth the money to know your child is receiving a good education in an environment that is much more controlled than the public schools. The teachers and staff really helped my son and took the time to contact me and work with us whenever my son was off track. Father Joe was awesome as well as the the teachers. I would definitely recommend the school to anyone considering Cabrini. The recent investments in computers, chromebooks and improvements like the new athletic fields, roof and parking lot are amazing considering the very low tuition. There is a nice blend of young, energetic teachers and more experienced ones who have been there for many years. This school is academically demanding, and the majority of the students are actually kind and respectful to one another! Great opportunities and atmosphere, good sports and facilities; very, very good school overall. My daughter attended Cabrini for middle and high school. It is worth the money to know that my daughter was receiving a good education in an environment that is safe, she was able to really concentrate on her studies. The teachers and staff really care for the students and their families. I definitely recommend the school to anyone considering Cabrini. My time at the high school has been pretty decent. However I have noticed throughout my years there that some teachers are not effective at teaching, For example around 40% of my teachers will give you the notes from the book and homework from the book. That doesn't seem bad until you ask for help and they either don't know how to explain it properly or only regurgitate what is already said in the book. If you need your child to get help on homework, it would be best to get a tutor that knows what they're doing. My son (a recent graduate) found supportive teachers, staff and students to help and enoucourage him to succeed academically and socially. Despite challenges presented by attention deficit disorder his. He entered college at university of Michigan and has been on the deans list for the past three semesters. No school is perfect but cabrini really is a great school. While we are not church-goers, the school re-enforced the values of honesty, integrity and kindness that are so important. As an employer I have noticed in my workplace cabrini students posess greater social and interpersonal skills that many students from other high schools. I have hired two and work with many other cabrini graduates This decision, to have my child at this private school, was rhe worst parenting decision of my life. My child and I have experienced bullying, prejudice and judgement (we are not Catholic) both in the classroom and outside the ckassroom. We paid higher tuition than others because we didn't know many others "barter" or don't pay at all. I have had coaches that cheat and lie, and when called out about it they were supported by the athletic department administration and I was made out to be the villain. Regretfully, my family has multiple alumni from Cabrini, but now none of us can recommend attending this school. And Christian values, forget about it, they are not there. A mistake was made going to this school. Cabrini High School combines faith, academic excellence, service, community and leadership to help students plan and prepare to achieve their goals after high school. Caring students and dedicated staff. I’m a parent of a graduating senior. She is well prepared to tackle challenges she may encounter because of the great foundation that she was given at CHS Cabrini High School is a small, safe school that offers challenging courses (AP, Honors) as well as support for struggling learners (Guided Learning, mentors). It has sports, clubs, and theater so there's a fun activity for everybody. Teachers, staff and pastors try to promote social justice, tolerance, love, compassion and good values - inside the theology classes and church as well as outside. By the end of high school, students graduate with close friends, a strong foundation and quality academics. Cabrini High School is a great school with a very strong family and community atmosphere to it. The school has a very strong Christian atmosphere among the staff and the students. There are many extra curricular activities and sports for all students to participate. For the learners who struggle there is homework help in the library, guided learning classes, mentors and many support systems.

column3: Its aerial view is basically it's description. I graduated in 2007 with a tartan diploma but begged to leave junior year to the alc because I hated tartan. Most of the teachers were awful and rude, occasionally a teacher would be fun and make learning enjoyable. The staff was horrible the women in the office where a joke i called them Suckratarys along with everyone in the guidance office. The most enjoyable thing was leaving for pseo at century in the afternoon. I would call it more of an institution. I felt bad for special ed kids as they didn't seem to have staff or teachers care for them or learn much.not much discipline for students and the jokedale rent a cops were always on premises standing around watching everything.School is old and needs remodeling and some air conditioning. At that age we don't leave our friends at school and go be a new kid unless there is a serious problem. This school is the worst i have ever attended. i felt as though the staff didn't care about their jobs at all! The students are even more horrible. I recieved countless racial descriminations and experienced horrible torments at the hands of classmates. The best day of my life was the day i moved to Anoka and began attending school there. Honestly parents, if you want a good learning environment, send them anywhere but here. I love tartan! I can't really speak for any of the regular classes because I'm in all AP or Accelerated classes, but for the classes I am in the teachers are great and they really go out of their way to stay after or before school to make sure you understand what's going on in class. I'm also in the AVID program at Tartan and from what I've heard from some of my friends at other high schools our class is more close and supportive than other schools, we're really like a big family. (And yes we actually do tutorials and binder checks!) As a former student I can say Tartan is an overall good school. The good was most of the teachers would take time after school to help you if you were having problems learning a subject or concept as long as the students listen to when office hours were or cared enough to ask. The teaching staff were very knowledgeable in the areas they taught. The AP or advanced placement classes were excellent and having the opportunity to go to 916 at Century College for college credit my senior year really helped me get prepared for college. The theater group does an amazing job as well as the band and choir. They have been remodeling the school slowly and the football field has gotten new bleachers and turf. The bad was there were lots of fights and kids being jumped by other kids, the office did not handle these situations very well at all and in some cases the kid that got jumped and didn't throw a punch got suspended for just "being in a fight" even though they had it on the security tape showing they did nothing. The coaches for athletics teams were very biased on who they picked regardless of how tryouts go and this reflects on how the teams have performed in recent years, students who did not make Tartans teams went to other schools and excelled. The school has been overcrowded and siblings sometimes have to share lockers(happened to me for two years). Overall I would say it is a good school and with all schools there are things that they do well and some things they need to really work on. Go Titans! We have had a really great experience at Tartan High school. I have two kids that attend the school and while no school is perfect and without some issues, overall Tartan is a great school. My son with special needs is treated with care and respect. My other child is in mostly AP classes and is very happy. My youngest child will attend Tartan once he is gets to 9th grade. This is my child's first year attending this school and let me say, I do not recommend it. While attending one of his football games I witnessed about three fist fights that happened between students in the crowd and other kids who were vaping and selling vapes right in the open. This was mentioned to staff and nothing was done. I would feel uncomfortable bringing younger kids to games (which should be a family event.) My child also has witnessed kids vaping right in the school bathrooms and drug deals being made. I brought this to the schools attention yet again and nothing has been done. Since being at Tartan my child went from having a 4.0 GPA and he is now struggling to get by with Cs. He has been picked on and bullied by other students, yet when he stands up for himself I get a phone call that my kid is name calling and may be suspended. How about the staff focus on who is being the bully and getting the drug use and vaping under control. I am beyond furious and very disappointed. At this point to help my very intelligent young man get back on track, we are going to home school him until I can find a much better school/ environment for my son. I really hope things get better with this school and that the staff starts opening their eyes to the smoking and drugs that are being done right under their noses.

They have security camera all over the school and one had caught the kids cause they fought in front of a camera. If a Teacher ever does anything wrong or incorrect the teacher will most likely get in trouble. I've had a horrible teacher and I had told my counselor and she had a sight down conversation with the Teacher and the Principle. Some things could change for the better but ask yourself why does BVHS have the highest Star Testing score in SJUSD. Its because we learn what we are required to learn. I have sent 3 children to this school, and they have been well prepared for college courses. For the most part the teachers are awesome and care about the kids. I have sent 4 kids to Bella Vista and they have all been well prepared for life and college. My daughter graduated in 2011, and had a wonderful experience all four years! I always was informed and happy with what was happening with my daughters education. The Bella Vista community is amazing!! Academics at this school are okay, however the overall school experience is lacking. Clubs and sports are not supported (other than band) and the school administration doesn't seem to recognize the importance of how the combination of academics and extra-curricular activities truly contributes to the overall success of students. Northgrand like any other school is trying to get these students to graduate and go to college. But overall the amount of pushing from my teachers I've gotten was unexpected. I honestly didn't think I would want to do anything with my life. This school has really motivated me to do better. Anyways enough about me, maybe this school sucked when your kid was here before. Really this school (like any other school) you just have to deal with the other kids that don't wanna do much with their life's and your work. Simple and pretty easy for a student who is motivated. If your kid is having trouble there is help if your kid decides to seek for it. My grandson has had a positive experience at North Grand High and he wants to finish High School here.

column1: This school does have quite a few decent qualities, however, there are more negatives than positives in this school. While you may get a decent education with quite a few of the courses (mainly in the fields of math, science, and history) you are likely to find massive problems with other areas of the school. The first of these core fundamental problems is their treatment of special needs kids, especially with some examples of at least one staff member actually bullying them and treating them as lesser beings or "inconveniences". The second one is the problem with the rules and their enforcement. There is a massive amount of inconsistencies within the school as well. One of the core problems being the dress code and its enforcement. Though it specifically states in the student handbook that there are no extremely short shorts allowed or low cut tops a majority of students wear these and only a few are ever punished. This is only made worse by the fact that only certain teachers only seem to enforce it, much to the dismay of the principal's statement of how they would all do their part to enforce it. Another problem with the dress code seems to be with special events. The school regularly has things like "Dress-Up Days" where students can dress up in costumes based on the day's theme. However, it appears some teachers do not get the memo as on these days most of the staff will be fine with these costumes. However, some have been known to become very hostile if one of these costumes has a hat as a part of it. Hats have always been a part of a mock holy war within the school as the principal is very fanatical about hats not being worn inside (except for on days where you dress up, of course in which he is fine with that). While that is perfectly acceptable some teachers will become very aggressive towards you for wearing a hat in school on these dress-up days. So, in essence there needs to be consistency on that aspect of the school ruling because when it comes to a lot of these "school rules" there are too many mixed messages for a student to possibly understand what is acceptable. This can also transfer over into the class as well. As there are some teachers who love to have discussions with their students and small debates where in others your grade can actually suffer for questioning a teacher. So, in the end, do not go to this school. This school does have quite a few decent qualities, however, there are more negatives than positives in this school. column3: Very competitive school athletically. Wonderful honors classes. Tremendous variety of classes to choose from for juniors and seniors. Principal is fantastic--genuinely cares about students. Current school board seems out of touch with teachers and most of community. This school has a lot to offer its students. The CTC offerings allow for kids to explore careers in a high school setting and the business classes are outstanding. The issue I have had with this school is that the close proximity to the university makes drugs highly accessible to students. University housing surrounds the high school two building campus allowing for too much open opportunity for activity that should not be permitted. Sadly, the community is building/renovating a new school and chose to keep a two building plan - obviously those who voted (random surveys were sent to homes) have no idea what happens around the perimeter of this school. I love this school! State College is really the perfect mix of outdoors, city, and University. The other close schools- Grier, St. Joes, Grace Prep- pale in comparison and if you're considering applying, DON'T. They might look "safer" but their academics and athletics are bare; SCAHS offers classes in business, ag, auto, comp. sci, engineering, journalism, art (photo., film, ceramics, 3D, etc) other CTC, and countless honors classes for exceptional students. The teachers truly care about your academics. If they push hard it's always for education, but ever school has that old, cranky teacher. Also, being next to Penn State (#32 in the nation) is fantastic fall back for those who struggle in school. I've always dreamed of going to an Ivy league but sold myself short; with my classes I am now on track to attend UPenn (in Philly). My only concerns: the school is in poor condition but is planned for renovation, and the difficulty to start clubs. Overall, the Thespian program competes nationally, all major sports are varsity PIAA Division AAA or above (the best), students can take PSU classes, small-city setting is ideal, and students graduate more than prepared for higher learning. A+! For those interested in a critical review, salaries, and tax impact of the State College Area School District please go to statecollegewatchdog.com I have 3 kids in this district, and one at the high school. I've personally known, and have knowledge of, multiple kids who are on the high honor roll at State High--and either didn't meet the benchmark for college readiness when taking PSATs/SATs, or went onto Penn State and practically (or did) flunk out. This school focuses on the elite and everyone else is left in the dust. The "average" or "college prep" courses are easy enough to ensure kids make As--but the education at that level is worthless. My kid was making 100s in regular math, but they wouldn't move her up because the advanced classes were full of kids who still scored higher than her on the standardized tests. So she has spent years unchallenged and bored. ALSO, BE AWARE OF MAJOR GRADE INFLATION and ridiculous methods for calculating a final grade. Students can get Cs and Ds on all test and still pull out As if they do their homework. What good is an A if the kid doesn't actually learn anything. It's almost fraudulent. Parents may not complain because, to them, their kid is doing great and in on the high honor roll. Approximately 30% of the school graduates with a 4.0 or higher. If your kid is gifted, this is a great school. If your kid is average, they will get lost, given an A or B, and forgotten. There are also not enough counselors to handle the large volume of students in the school. Unfortunately, the school boasts about it's BS reputation, but fails to have the best interest of ALL students at heart. Well funded district with excellent schools. Community very involved and consulted regarding future plans for schools in district. The vast amount of programming opportunities is outstanding. The career and technical center is integrated into the school (e.g. - faculty includes a physical therapist, electrical engineer, agriculture professional, registered nurses, CISCO certified instructors, etc.). I regret moving my kids into this school district. The time change for the start of the day is something that should not have happened. Sometimes these kids have hours of homework and since the middle schools do not give out a lot the ninth graders are unprepared for this. Add in sports and job so these kids will be up even later doing homework so a half hour in the morning is nothing but ignorance of the school board and superintendent. We moved into the SCASD school district from out-of-state, and are extremely pleased with the quality of State College Area High School. The curriculum is challenging and there are many, many opportunities to be engaged including theater, music, sports and extracurricular clubs. The connection to the university provides opportunities far beyond what a typical high school offers. Overall the students have a voice and feel connected to the school and community. Also, the school building itself is extraordinary - more like a community college! State College Area School District is a joke. Teachers show extreme favoritism to the students and constantly deny other kids opportunities to thrive. They have been investigated by the Pa Department of Education for not meeting the needs of gifted children and have been found non compliant several times. If you happen to be in the inner circle with the teachers your child will have a great experience, but if you're anybody else, be prepared to be denied opportunities, communication, support or anything else your child may need. Please reconsider moving into this toxic environment.

Much better than many expensive private schools, I bet. If you are planning to stay for an after school activity and take the school bus be prepared for a long ride. Also, make sure you do not overwhelm yourself with clubs and classes you know you can't handle or you will suffer. so... as much as I lack school spirit, I have to say that it's not so bad. there are some pretty cool people here. if you work hard enough, you'll pass your classes. sure, there may be some unbearable teachers, but you'll get used to it and eventually minimize your own complaints. people are supportive + the counselors are approachable. I just wish we had windows to see the sun. I don't know why this school only gets a rating of 7 on comparison with similar schools because this school is great! My son chose to go to DMHS because of the computer programming track and it has been well worth the effort of getting up at 5:30 AM to catch the school bus to downtown. This is a small high school which is very college oriented. We are so very lucky to have a great college counselor (Ms. McGee) who is always available to help and is very knowledgeable about everything college. The teachers are very engaged with the students and know the kids on a personal level. The administration is friendly, supportive and always helpful. The kids are very accepting of each other - there is no racism or bullying that my son has seen in his four years here (he will graduate this spring). Downtown Magnets is truly a Stellar school. I would rate this school experience a 9/10 because most of the adults in this school are nice and respectful to students around and they're taking responsibility most of the time. This school has achieved outstanding academic achievement that makes it stand out in Los Angeles, but unfortunately, this has dwindled in recent years. The environment at the campus is extremely competitive amongst students, and the stressful feeling is excessively seen throughout the entire year. Due to excessive workloads, very demanding instructors, and a change of administration, students work themselves out to a point where it affects them emotionally, mentally, and health-wise. The school offers great opportunities at the cost of four excessively demanding and stressful years. Very bad experience I choose this school for my child because I thought it was the best. I was wrong

column1: Knox Central High School is truly a great school. It has something for everyone. If you want to take advanced classes, you have a wide selection. If you want to take simple classes, you have a wide selection. There are many interesting electives and clubs. I am a Junior and currently have a 28 on my ACT. I have went here almost three full years and never have felt insecure or have encountered drug problems. The staff and principle do focus on academics. Also, the whole 'only the rich in the community play sports or achieve anything' just isn't true. I feel as a student that Knox Central is improving each and every year. The school is heading in the right direction, and I wouldn't trade me years at Knox Central for anything. Kc has Its ups and downs. If a student is committed and hardworking, Central gives them a clear, challenging, rewarding path to success. It should be understood that a majority of low test scores stem from the high number of students from broken, impoverished family's, a result from the lack of development in the region; known for drugs and alcohol. It can be reasoned that these problems are less prevalent in local city schools. If a student is willing to take the advanced classes, extracurricular activities, and focus on success; the same things that apply to all schools, they will emerge well educated as well as prepared for life in the real world through college and beyond.

column3: Agoura has a lot of ups and downs. I can honestly say I don't think it deserves anything more than a 2, however, for many reasons. One reason in particular is that the teachers are very mediocre here. I came here after going to other schools and you cannot compare this school's teaching methods to my old schools'. I took a few honors and none of my teachers demonstrated a teaching style that was appropriate (ie, they just read off powerpoint notes or tried to be funny the entire time.) Some teachers stand out but very few indeed and many are uncaring about you as a student. Nonetheless I will say there were a few good friends I made here and that is why I give AHS anything more than a 1. Sadly, Agoura High has let us down. Prior to high school we had nothing but ravingly positive things to say about the LVUSD school system. Now, I say apply out. The teaching staff is jaded and angry, the principal per his own report is helpless to change anything, and the students get lost in the shuffle. As parents - forget it! No one has the time of day to deal with concerns. I strongly advise that if you care about the education of your child, want to develop a well rounded, four-year college bound student, then head somewhere else. Agoura High School is a top-tier public school that excels in its academic curriculum as well as its award-winning music, athletic, and drama programs. We are thrilled with the supportive new principal, who just took over this past year. The only thing I would improve is that a few of the underclassmen counselors could be a bit more prepared in suggesting appropriate curriculum spanning a student's four years at the campus, and some of the class schedules presented conflicts for desired AP classes. Overall, very happy with the experience. Agoura High is a phenomenal school for the arts! The theatre teacher is fantastic, and she actually teaches. Although, she is the only one of my teachers that actually teaches. We have 100 minute classes at Agoura, which should be plenty of time for teachers to actually teach, but instead there are teachers that leave the classroom for a good 20 mins unannounced, who then come back and give us 20 mins more of a break. I have a teacher who wouldn't help me, when I asked a question about how I should study for her tests until I started failing the class. That same teacher would make fun of you, and encourage the class to laugh when someone answered the question wrong, she did this even to the shiest kids. There are more teachers who are like this, or they can't even teach, because they don't know the information. So, the only reason I'd encourage students to come to Agoura is for the Arts. If it wasn't transportation, and our stubborn district I'd go to another school and come back to Agoura to take Theatre, and choir. The main thing I'd improve on is getting rid of the ten year plan, so that teachers would stay on the ball. AHS is a disappointing high school although resided in a decent area with vast donations from parents and the community. There are unbelievable numbers of teachers who have convinced us through their daily teaching that students and their leanings are not the teachers concern. Many staff in the office treats students as they were stupid kids, or even worse, criminals. Some staff takes advantage of students and their parents, selling beauty products to garner extra income. Too many unqualified counselors are in AHS collecting tax payers money. Many of my friends constantly feel that we are wasting time in AHS, but we are stocked here because we can t afford private high schools. On the other hand, some exceptional teachers are as dedicated as teachers can be to their students. I mostly admire the teacher who works very hard and cares about her students despite of herself battling cancer. My star goes to these teachers. I wish AHS deserves more of the stars. My daughter is a freshman at AHS and is having a great experience. She is in the pre-IB program and is challenged appropriately, has good relationships with her teachers, and is supported both socially and educationally. Some teachers are inconsistent with keeping grades posted and have been difficult to reach, but not excessively so, and others have gone out of their way to be helpful and welcoming. We are very happy with our choice of Agoura High School. Our principal keeps us informed and is involved with the students. I am a parent of a Junior year student at Agoura High. I have another child who graduated several years ago, so I have a fair idea what this school is like. I think it is a mix of good and bad - more good than bad. There are some awesome teachers and there are a few "teachers" who should be working in the DMV , not a high school. A lot of the teaching issues in AHS stems from the California curriculum which things that if you throw a lot of information at the students, they magically transform into mini Nobel Laureates. There is often a tendency to hire sports coaches who are also faculty members. With a few notable exceptions, these are some of the worst teachers in the school. I believe the current Principal Mr. Mercer genuinely cares about the school and is quite proactive unlike his predecessor. Great teachers, great and challenging curriculum, and prepares students very well for their college / university experience. I have been very pleased with the education of two children at this school and look forward to sending a third. I am thrilled with the breadth of offerings, with the rigor of the academics, and the social support. The music program is spectacular. My older kids went to a very well known private school, and my son is being just as well served at Agoura High School. He's in the IB program and the teachers are supportive, engaged and committed to their students success. Environment is fine if a student is performing well but can very quickly turn negative if they stop, and staff do little to help students recover from academic, social, or emotional difficulties. Nearly impossible to catch up if you fall behind. Teachers and staff don't generally seem to care much about students. Administrators transparently care more about protecting themselves in court than protecting students. A damaging experience at this school that is unconscionable. Agoura High school is like any other high school. Teachers are average but the student body is not welcoming nor polite to adults. Pep rallys and dances are fun though. As of the writing of this review, the school has a weak Principal and Assistant Principal who do not enforce guidelines put in place by the California Department of Public Health. While it is stated that masks are required indoors, not all teachers enforce this and some have openly complained IN FRONT OF STUDENTS, how much of a burden the masks are and they don't understand why mask wearing is required. I'm not joking. In addition, when students openly ignore or refuse to put on their mask, there are no consequences. Per CDPH, if students do not (or cannot) wear a mask the school is required to provide an independent study program for them. While this may be in place at Agoura, it is not enforced by the administration and, in fact, students are targeted by some teachers for speaking up about this. This may sound hyperbolic, or conspiratorial, but we have experienced this first hand. I understand the political pressure the administration is under to have the schools open, but it is meaningless (and dangerous) if there are no enforcement (key word is enforcement) of rules put out by our own Department of Public Health. It's ridiculous, and illustrates an apathy towards every student's well being. What is needed is action, not lip service. Unfortunately we mostly get the latter than the former. AHS has many wonderful opportunities for all students. Great college and career options in courses. Students are accepted into the top colleges across the country. There are a wide variety of sports, music, arts, drama and clubs for students to be involved with. Great administrators and counselors for social emotional, academic and college and career. If students want help the school has it. Great teachers who work hard to make sure students are well prepared for college. Beautiful campus. So fortunate to live in a community with great schools. I have three children who have attended Agoura High and they were very happy there. There are many options to suit the needs of different types of learners. The AP and IB programs provide incredible learning opportunities that prepare students to be successful in college. The Sports Medicine Program is very impressive and attracts students who may be interested in careers in the medical field. The campus is welcoming and the staff works hard to make the environment warm and friendly. Go Chargers! Agoura High has an amazing Jazz, winds, and choral programs. If you student is into music, they will love it here. The theater program is also fantastic. Like most high schools, the teaching is mixed, but the majority of the teachers are great and really care about the students. AHS was an absolute nightmare for my son, who is part of the LBGTQ community. He was relentlessly bullied by students on the basis of his sexual orientation and also mocked for following health guidelines in covid. When he was called a racial slur in front of witnesses, the administration only addressed it reluctantly and with zero follow up or concern shown. Of course, the bullying got worse after he reported it and he just had to endure. His friends were also bullied and all felt helpless and demoralized. His counselor, however, was very kind and supportive- she was simply wonderful, but unfortunately she was powerless over discipline or bullying issues. This is a school made up of largely white, mostly conservative parents and administrators who seem unconcerned with diversity and tolerance (or public health, as teachers let students wear their masks down even in the height of the pandemic). We withdrew from the school and will be trying to teach our son what kindness looks like at a new school.

column1: GDRHS is a very good school for its size . Child 1 graduated in last couple of years, one attends now. Block scheduling is a very good idea, enhancing focus, in a time where distractions abound.(FaceBook, e-mails texts). However the drawback to it is having 4 blocks classes each semester makes for tough scheduling. If your child wants to pursue band/chorus as part of curriculum or a second language and still track for a couple of AP classes by junior year), they need to be very careful and work with guidance and it is just not possible to fit things easily given classes are not all offered spring/fall even in math and sciences making selection tricky even for basic tracks. Guidance is wonderful but kids from outside district or parochial schools may be misaligned initially since grades seem to be suspect and placement exams not always best for getting slotted correctly into honors/regular classes and not all classes are offered in spring and fall. So- If you don't manage carefully your child might not get to track for 1-2 AP classes by spring of junior yr.(top colleges want AP grades). 5th block/split would allow music, 2nd language. Principals changed twice, Still very good HS Groton Dunstable is a very good school. The majority of teachers are excellent. The new principal is by all appearances doing a very good job. We do not have as many courses to offer as would a larger school, but we cover the basics and then some. There is a good selection of AP classes and the material in them is on a par with college course work. Our student body is a wonderful, caring community and they all seem to really get along. Our school continually strives to improve. They are currently focusing on improvements in technology, since that is a relative weakness for us. ...I feel very fortunate to live in this town. It's a very good school, with a good administration despite some recent turnover. My daughter is in mostly AP classes and doing great. The school facilities are well-maintained. My only complaint is that they need a cell repeater because there is no T-Mobile service there, which makes it hard to contact my daughter at school sometimes. My child transferred in for the second part of Sophmore year, and just graduated in 2020. Moved to Groton in large part BECAUSE of the school. One of the best decisions I’ve ever made. Loved the teachers and staff. Caring professionals.

column3: This is absolutely the best school ever! It is so easy to make friends here, teachers and students are so kind. I have learned so much at this school and I love it! My student has really blossomed at Franklin. He was a tag student at his middle school, and mostly into academics. At FHS he got a chance to run cross country, try the school paper, and get into lots of other extra-curricular activities. He also took AP classes nearly every year. FHS has a good, diverse student body and lots of chances to get involved. Couldn't be happier or more grateful to the staff and teachers at FHS. Their AP program is soaring with student participation, thanks to Susie Bartley and others. Graduation rates get better every year, due to the passion and enthusiasm the teachers pass on. Our child was involved in many, many activities, scholastic, athletic, leadership, etc and has emerged with a great scholarship at an acclaimed university. The climate at FHS fosters and encourages growth, learning and participation. PS. Even the athletics are improving. The previously mentioned Volleyball coach is gone and coaching in all sports is getting better. The cross-country running program is among the best in the conference. I would rate my experience a 4/5. The one point I'm taking away is because I got mugged once, right outside the school. Some dudes walked up to me and stole my bus money. However, during the frightening ordeal, it also built a lot of character for me and taught me a valuable lesson on how not to get mugged at Franklin.

column1: Poor in all areas. Since the dismissal of critical teachers, and administration the school has deteriorated with no regard for students or parents voices. It is also very one sided when it comes to politics a big no, no for any school district. (they do not give choices) they have expelled so many children that the school can not get funding for anything. Absolutely terrible! We heard for years about how bad the school as academically. We tried for two years with our child there and really saw some positive aspects. Unfortunately the teachers (overall--there were only a few exceptions) and the administrators could care less about student achievement and understanding. The teachers union in this district should be VERY ashamed with what they have done! I would NEVER recommend this school to anyone. Truly a gem nestled in the foothills. Relatively small student population keeps the learning personal, and creates a fairly tight knit culture. The facilities are very well kept and newly remodeled. I would recommend this school to anyone seeking to live, and provide their children with the small town experience. I am a graduate of golden sierra. And I must say it is the best School i have attended. The teachers really care about their students and really want them to succeed. Golden Sierra has one of the best athletic programs I've ever seen. Their football team went undefeated this season and almost won the championship. It is truly a great school . This school is absolutely horrible and i wish i had parents that gave me an opportunity to leave. all these people saying its great are lying, trust me. Golden Sierra graduates have no future, i mean look at me. they dont prepare you at all. This is really a great school. The teachers really care about the students and want them to succeed. Almost everyone is really friendly here and cares about this school. Everyone saying this school is terrible is probably the parent or the student who just is mad that they couldn't get by without putting in any effort to their school work. A truly great school. My daughter went to this school for a year and a half and had a wonderful experience there. The teachers truly cared about her understanding the skills. The office staff go above and beyond to help when needed. I can't say enough about the wonderful teachers and administrative staff they have. It's a small town school and it's more like a close knit family. I would highly recommend this school to other people. Sometimes you want to go where everybody knows your name... this is the Cheers of schools! Kids, parents, staff, community care for one another and support a positive learning environment. Highly recommend. This school is like all other schools. The administration, counselors, and most of the staff are stuck in their own school days in their heads and can't function as adults. Please do further research on this school and school district. Something I wish we would have done prior to moving here .

column3: I have had two kids go through this school, the first one had bad experiences with teachers who wouldn't help or answer questions and I had a poor impression, however, when the second one entered and had some of those same, tough teachers I learned that there is more than one perspective as she was able to relate and work hard to get good grades -- this first one, not so much and now three years later admits she didn't work very hard, so I know not to take anything on face value.. The staff if courteous and the campus pretty safe, don't hear much of bulling nor fighting for the most part and the students seem very tolerant of each other, no matter what their differences. The school could use some revamping and it can be quite crowded and small. They could also use some new full-time math teachers as every year my kid has had some terrible substitutes teach classes abandoned due to personal situations, however those situations were handled with re-grading and/or re-testing and the outcomes were more than satisfactory -- given all of that, I think Pacifica offers a solid education and recommend it wholeheartedly.. The school could have a better school spirit if it isn't demeaning and that it does not make students feel uncomfortable. Make sure your student gets involved with clubs, or any sport, that builds camaraderie that helps focus study habits. I would like to see what percentage of students have to REPEAT classes at Pacifica vs. the California average. I notice my son passes the science and math benchmark tests with ease - but struggles mightily with Pacifica's teacher's own tests in geometry and chemistry. Same for his friends - many of whom will have to take Chemistry twice to avoid killing their chances at college. Why is there such a difference between student's performance on benchmarks vs. in class tests? What does that tell us? I think the teachers aren't getting the more complex issues into the students heads - a substantial amount flunk tests - and the teachers don't care - just move on. Everything seems to be in a mad rush. GRADING homework would be a good change. My son's geometry class gets full homework credit - just for turning it in. But are the students doing the homework correctly? Who knows - until you FAIL a test. Ugh. Private school - I wish I invested in it. the teaching is so much better. The caring is so much higher. Just like any HS you have your teachers that care and teachers that don't. It is our job as parents to let them know that you are on top of things and to ask questions if your student doesn't get the right answers. And if you don't play baseball or softball forget it the sports programs are a joke from an old boys soccer coach who usually has talent but can't do anything with or the girls soccer coach who is a club president and coach and only uses the school to farm players and forget about football it's just not gonna happen they don't even have there own stadium. But they take the whole bullying thing very serious and have lots of parent seminars and such for a variety of different things. Relatively safe I guess..... My student is an IEP student and has difficutly keeping up with some of his classes. He has always been taught to ask for extra help before and after school. Yet, this year he has several teachers who have not been willing to meet with him, even by appointment and he is now really struggling in that class. It's very sad to see students try to obtain the help they need and have teachers unwilling to help. I understand they have lives and families, however it seems to be more and more of the teachers are showing less care for their students at this school, which is very sad to see. Not sure we will be sending child #2 to Pacifica in the next year. As a student who transferred into Pacifica this year after spending my freshman year at a different school, I've found that Pacifica offers a very different high school experience as opposed to what I had before. Pacifica is a very small school in comparison to the one I came from, and I've been happy with the clean atmosphere and generally well-kept image of the school. However, the entrance I use to get into the school has no side walk at all and forces students to walk in-between cars coming in and out of the school's lot. I find that to be really poor design, and dangerous. The teachers I have now as opposed to the ones I had before are not as good at what they do. Some have very poorly planned classes, Some are not very interactive with their class at all, and are very vague with help when asked for it.. Most are not very clear when it comes to instructions. The school spirit here is a joke- we never have any pep assemblies and most students generally accept that our sports teams are terrible. All in all I've found it to be a downgrade, and though there are things I enjoy about Pacifica, I've been pretty disappointed with my new school. I attended Pacifica from 9th grade until 2nd semester of 11th grade. In my 3 years there I had absolutely no encouragement from my AP or teachers. I actually had a teacher tell me he isn't dealing with my "bullsh**" and accused me of things I did not do. Two other teachers told me that taking my final is pointless because I will fail anyways. I transferred to Hare Continuation when I left Pacifica and got straight A's, which continued once I started ACCESS. I did better on my own than I ever did at Pacifica. In my opinion they just don't care about the students that are struggling because it makes them look bad, which they should because they did not take the time to help me rather than putting me down. I know other students that have said the same so it is not just my own personal experience. Excellent. 2 children attended. An average student and one with learning disabilities. Both treated equal. My child attended here from 9th to 12th, he transferred over when we moved from a different school district. He attended a jr high school that was not very supportive even with having an IEP. He was struggling so much I honestly felt my son would not do well at Pacifica. Finding himself in a new school and new peers, my son had a ruff start freshman year. My son has a good heart and showed he wanted to learn and become someone important. He got along well with his peers and teacher’s. A polite kid. All four years at Pacifica my son had all great teachers but one. He gave my son a hard time but my son did not let that teacher get the best of him (there is always one or more in any school). My son did great with the help of his teachers, counselors (especially Mr. Ocean) all staff, principals( Mr. Osborne will be missed, happy retirement) and peers. It takes a great village to help a child succeed in school. Class of 2022!! Pacifica Mariners all the way!! Nothing but great memories of Pacifica for my graduate! And his education continues…!

column1: Everything that has been posted here about poor academics, excessive drug use, and bad counselors is simply not true anymore. The academic program is rigorous and hands-on in many classes. Students pay for the AP textbooks because the school district does not have enough money. If a teacher hears of financial hardship caused by situations like this, they find a way to get the student what they need within their means. There is some drug use at this school, as with most schools, but as a student I find it very easy to stay out of those circles. There are no gang problems. Students who struggle can set up an appointment in the counseling office with any one of the counselors and can choose to speak with a peer support counselor (a senior who is chosen and trained in confidentiality, listening, and problem-solving). Unfortunately, there is little racial and religious diversity at this school, but both students and teachers accept all types of students. There are a number of great clubs and athletic teams to join. Out of all the schools in this school district, I would happily argue that Berthoud High School is the best in balancing opportunity with community. Great school, great staff, great counselors, great principal. Love the small town feeling here, and how everyone knows everyone. There doesn't seem to be as many of the drama issues at BHS as there are at other schools. My child attended this school all four years of high school. He liked it for various things such as teachers who connect with kids (for the most part) and the small size it offers. There are problems within the school that may seem amplified possibly because it is a small school so problems seem more prevalent. You have your athletic kids, smart kids, cowboys, party crowd, etc. Each group of kids is clearly defined! There is a sense of community but beware that outsiders are generally not included. Some of the sports excel, but most cannot compete at the levels needed to be successful. Leadership of the school is less than desired. The principal and several staff cannot lead by example in a positive way when they exhibit personal decisions such as extra-marital affairs within the community and all the students are aware of it. It is the best academic high school in this pathetic district but be warned that the environment of this school is not for everyone. Berthoud is a great school that is relatively small. Their performance is the best in the district and in the top tier of the state. The staff is responsive and there are a lot of opportunities that students can take advantage of at the school. Ask the right questions and advocate. Most of the teachers are very good and the staff continues to improve with the changes in staff that have been made over the last few years. We made the biggest mistake when we moved our grandson from Loveland high school to Berthoud High school. The clickiness of the students is horrible---definite devisions in social status. Teachers show huge favoritism to students that are long time residents of the town. MUSIC DEPARTMENT is disappointing to say the least. If a child needs help, they would just as soon they leave the school than stay. Very depressed school is the overall feeling. They say no bullying? What about the upper echelon kids that simply make fun of others? HUGE MIISTAKE ON OUR PART BHS is a very math and science oriented school. A student there can really excell if they take the initiative. No, the staff doesn't coddle the kids. They are expected to do there work and research post-secondary options for themselves. Your child will easily fall behind here if they're not motivated because there simply isn't enough staff to cater to the lazy. The academic opportunity is endless, but our sports programs are as successful. Students put forth their best effort but it isn't as big as the other schools we play and we lack diversity. Most of the staff is amazing but there are a few substandard teachers. But overall, I would highly suggest this school to anyone in the area. Our neighbors just graduated their second child from Berthoud High School. They speak of the school very highly. He has grown up to be a very fine young man. Our children will not be in High School for 4 more years. We love the small town feeling with high standards. So far I’m highly dissatisfied at the learning environment with my teen’s peers.

column3: I loved all four BHS. My high school years were the best years of my life. I can't wait to get out of college and go back to my hometown! The school seems to be controlled by autocrats who care little for the students. There is a climate of bullying which begins with the administration. Anyone who is vocal may be subject to retaliation. It is sad since there are some great teachers who have the ability to really inspire but the climate prevents it. A nightmare that will never end. Their disregard for students hopes and the example set will be with students for the rest of their lives.If you have a bright student please avoid this school. They teach to the median and have difficulties offering bright students opportunities. A fine school when compared to the state's surrounding public schools. Well funded, and many resources for a student to turn to if needed, e.g., therapy, support groups, tutoring. School counseling really depends on the student - sometimes 2 people can be very similar in grades and overall academic accolades, and be given different attitudes, demeanors, or treatment from the same counselor. If you're not assertive as a student, you will be carried by the school; however, your potential is not of concern to the school, so much that you complete the bare minimum the school requires for community service, take the mandatory classes, and receive the required credits. Beyond that, College Board is your support arch when the school isn't, it is an overused tool in my opinion but overall can do the job if the student knows how to apply themselves academically, which is not always the case. Above-average school in terms of funding and resources, and ranked higher than average for a public school. BHS offers academically rigorous classes, invested and highly qualified teachers, a variety of extra-curricula activities, a beautiful facility, and a supportive and progressive environment. I am proud to have my child attend. The new rules are ridiculous, one student out at a time is super annoying. What if there was an emergency where a female had to use the bathroom for period reasons. If student skip class then it is there fault for any work they missed, the students who don't skip are also getting effected by this rule. Also, the breakfast rules are not right, multiple people should be allowed to get breakfast at a time and we should be allowed to eat in the cafeteria which is what it is meant for, why are we getting yelled at for eating, why are teachers getting yelled at for being polite and letting multiple students to go and eat. Also, there handing out detentions and suspensions like crazy, those punishments should be hard to get.

column1: My son goes to this school, and I must say that at first it was an odd transition coming from a school where he knew everyone, to Bishop Brady where he only knew a few people. However, three years later he is thriving. We see his grades improve, his work ethic soaring, social skills thriving and he seems happier. Everyone at the school works to make the ttransition to Bishop Brady easy, most notably the admissions office. Bishop brady really does work towards it motto of faith, learning, and service.

column3: Terrific school, wonderful teachers, great curriculum. There is good school spirit and a responsive staff from the top on down. Excellent in all ways. Great principal, teachers and kids. Excellent program and the scores you report are way off.... SSHS is tops with a Regents diploma rate of 99%. Best integrated district in the country. Currently, I will be going into my sophomore year at SSHS. Lots of the teachers are very good, however you do see some teachers who aren't as good. They have a huge amount of extracurriculars, and the food is better than the middle school. Kids have more freedom, as you are allowed to wear hats, carry backpacks, chew gum, and leave campus during your off periods. They also have great choices for electives (Go computer graphics!). Overall, I love it. SOUTHSIDE High School is a wonderful institution for learning. I have 3 children in this district, one who has already graduated, one who is in her senior year and one who will begin next year. I have always felt my children received a top notch education here! Most teachers were helpful and caring. The one thing that I feel would give South Side greater recognition, would be to have more minority students involved in extra curricular activities and even allow them to start up clubs that appeal more to them. I would like them to look into a Step team club or even have a class on African-American studies. There is still a small divide when it comes to this area. I have asked some of the students why they don't do more activities and they say because they don't feel welcome and they never get chosen to be a leader. Have you seen an African-American student be a leader for Red and Blue?! I will never leave this wonderful school district until my last child has graduated. Thank you teachers and administrators for doing a wonderful job!! Great school, good curriculum and nice teachers. Various after school extracurricular activities to participate in as well. Good school, good curriculum and nice teachers. They had a large number of after school activities. Good rating overall. Wish there was more diversity in the school. Speaking as a former student, SSHS prepared me well for college and beyond and I was surprised to only see 7/10. One issue I have with this review is the AP test participation and pass rate. South Side offers and emphasizes IB courses (the international equivalent of AP) and only a limited selection of AP courses are offered. I hope this metric is not negatively effecting the overall score. I am a current 11th with straight A's, going full IB diplomapeople do as people do, especially kidsThe kids who don't care are encouraged to care but they don't care; nothing can be donekids who care have opportunities within the IB structure and electives, and the club system is phenomenalno matter what kind of kid their like, they can find kids like themselves to comfort themselves.school is not particularly sports oriented but it does have varsity sportselectives are great here, many options and solid teachersThere are some teachers you wont like, especially if you don't like the subject, but the average teacher can get their lessons across well and there are a lot of fantastic teachersA lot of really wicked smart kids go here but it doesn't feel elitist; I've heard it is more clicky than other schools, and while I don't know other schools, most people will have a group of friends that they spend most of their time with, though people don't advertise themselves by their friendsAdministration and counseling center are suboptimal but its works; most rules are easy to follow and logical and it's not very strict during off periodsIn 11th/12th, most classes have an option to take an easier v harder version of subjects; easier classes are effectively exclusively based on strong effort/motivation, while the harder classes demand an abundance of it, along with reasonable reasoning skillsOverall, great school for students who want to excel, the average student will find the harder classes challenging but rewarding, or the easier classes comfortable, and the weaker student will find themselves in easier classes. No matter what sort of kid you are, you can find similar people and the school is comfortably sized to not be too big where its intimidating, but big enough where there are enough people for you to say, 'I must be doing well because I'm not like them'. I've enjoyed the time I spent here, but unfortunately am going to hit the character limit and have to stop procrastinating my work.~TBE

column1: There is no soap in the bathrooms. Vaping out of control. One star, just add soap and it would be 4 stars.

column3: I am personally very dissappointed with the assistant Principle Anna Allen. Her lack of knowledge or even caring about what is going on out side of the school is appauling. Her lack of concern or concideration is appauling. She should be in another organization, not working with kids that may not have the ideal situation at home. She needs reeducated as well as a taste of her own mediciine. Her nose may not be so high up in the air if she took some time to concider others. Maybe she can use a lesson or two in humility, humanity or how about just empathy. How does a person get to be in a role that she is in with a lack of heart. How does she look at her self in the mirror every morning? Or does she? Beware of Lakewood Hogh School! They are busing kids from other ares and my student ended up being bullied and assulted, the school stated its not there problem even tho they were fully aware of the problem. If I could do over again we would of nerver put our children in this. This is school is going down fast with the violence and drug problems. The principal and asst principal are the worst both yelled at me when speaking with about the problem, they have no need to be involed with trivial matters. DO NOT SEND YOUR KIDS THERE This school is a unique one as it services students of all abilities from the special needs, to ESL, to AP, and has the top IB program in the state. While the test scores may not be the highest possible, you must consider the vast population of socioeconomically low students it services. This school should be a model for the nation equal access to a great education. The school is robust and has offerings in art, music, theater, sports, clubs, and a dedicated teaching staff. My student transferred to LHS their sophmore year.. I have never meet the Principal in the two years he has been there. This principal is very removed from the parents and student body except for his class interuptions over the loud speaker for annoucements or e-mails to parents asking for donations for the school. Supposedly he has earned some award for a being a top principal. The school administrative staff is very aloof. Teachers are a mixed bag. Some are good , some do not want to be bothered and feel because the student is in HS a parent should have no involvement. Special Education , IEP and 504 services are sketchy and hard to enforce as is the case in most Jeffco schools. The school has a large student population and has it share of clicks I loved my LHS experience!! I am a recent Lakewood graduate and I can honestly say that I had the best experience here. I entered in the IB program but decided to just take AP classes my junior and senior years. I felt incredibly prepared for college and like I received the best public education I could have. Not only does Lakewood have great academic programs but they also have an incredible arts department, including music and theater, and a great sense of community. Principal Castagna was a fantastic principal and he has run Lakewood with extreme success for years. I am still so proud to be a Lakewood Tiger!!! Best school in Colorado! This school is amazing. They have great classes, they help your children learn clearly. The sports are great. The tutors are amazing. The school has great support and school spirit. I would definitely reccomend this school! Pre-IB Lakewood teachers do not encourage high quality work, but they do encourage cheating, if unintentionally. Teachers generally do a cursory job grading assignments, if they grade them at all. This is likely because the volume of busy work given each day is huge (3 hrs + per night) & would be difficult to grade (unless teachers spend 3 hrs + per night grading). Instead, they just glance at the student's work to make sure the quantity is there. As a result of the volume and lack of accountability, cheating on assignments is rampant. When students don't cheat, they often do a very cursory job just to get it turned in. I see no interest on the part of administration in acknowledging the issue, much less addressing the student behavior or the teaching policies (e.g., lots of busy work rarely graded) that lead to the need to cheat and do low quality work. I am sure many parents are not aware of this situation, and are very pleased with the school. But, for a school with such a good reputation & so full of smart kids, I find the low ethical and academic standards very disappointing. The teachers don't seem to be very motivated to help struggling kids. From the inflexibility in the curriculum and assignments for those that are having a hard time, to the lack of care from the counselor office.You may try to reach out and try to get some help from the teacher or the office, but it is a lost cause. You are on your own and your child is shuffled along or made an example of. 13 years of struggling to try to help my child with learning disabilities... all down the drain. 13 years of schooling and trying to help my child work through the problems he deals with on a daily basis.. all down the drain. 13 years all culminating to one big F. My child didn't graduate because of ONE class. 13 years waiting for this day to come, and it is not going to happen. No graduation day. Cancel the party, cancel the grandparents traveling out to see this big day, cancel all celebration plans. LHS, feel free to hang my child's Cap and Gown in your office. If he doesn't get to walk, then we don't need it. The way I see it tho, you had one job. ONE JOB, and YOU are the one that failed. You didn't give my kid an F, you gave yourself an F. The anger I feel is all encompassing. It is an average-good school. Other schools in the district are catching up, whether it be with innovative programs or also having IB programs. If Lakewood wants to keep up its reputation then it really needs to stop sitting on its previous accolades and become innovative again. The administrative staff needs improving or more help to keep up with the number of students(which I believe is too many for the size of the school). They like to say they are a family, but each class is made to feel very distinct. The senior classes make it known that they rule the school. They will kick out underclassmen from the front rows at sporting events. I do choice enroll my kids there, and I am hopefull they are getting a good education, but we shall see when my daughter starts college in the fall of 2017. The school is great because of the teachers and the over all environment. I just wish that they would teach us more in class instead of giving us homework with no known knowledge and with no available guidance. it was basically a nightmare and I'm glad it's over because he's not there anymore. I’m a recent International Baccalaureate or IB graduate who graduated from Lakewood in 2018 and I think that the school was quite frankly as good as you can get. I had great teachers and the student body was very close. The only pitfall or contention that I had was in there being a definite liberal agenda being pushed seen primarily through the English department. Overall I had a great experience with this school not only for the academic aspect but also when participating in sports and extracurricular activities. as a student here they do not put any kind of learning disability until the middle of the school year

column1: Why is there no PTO (parent, teacher organization)? If such an organization were to exist, maybe more parents would take interest in their children's education and not wait until the child is failing. Although I don't have a problem with tenure in general, I do think that in order to be able to retain it, a teacher must meet certain requirements. For example, to treat students like humans and not talk to them like they are dogs, also, actually to have a calling to be teacher would be a plus. I think that all of the people who say this is a great school must work there. I have children at this school, they are picked on, ridiculed, and made fun of by staff at this school, I wish that I could afford to move back home to Florida, schools there are great. HCHS has a small attendance of students, many of which you might consider are of a disadvantage. As such, my student has had their locker broken into, clothing has been stolen, books, binders, pens, pencils... stolen! There are no lockers in the gym and the athletes have to leave their personal belongings behind in a duffel bag during pep rallies/games and personal belongings are stolen. The school needs lockers in the gym for students who are required to change from school clothes to uniforms. We now live in a time where our youth is being brought up without any parental guidance and run a muck. They have no conscience when it comes to taking something that doesn't belong to them. The school staff needs to step up and do a better job protecting their students. Perhaps if lockers are not in the budget, find an area or room with a locked door where the students can leave their personal belonging and make it mandatory all personal affects are locked up. The school staff and teachers for the most part are acceptable, however, there are a few who could benefit from a course in how to encourage your students rather than discourage a student by making disparaging remarks to them. Children/students need a daily dose of vitamin e - ENCOURAGEMENT! You won't find that at HCHS. The administrative staff fail terribly! Students are told "they will never be successful; you're stupid; you'll never amount to anything". The school has become a dumping ground for those teachers and administrators who can't get a job in a real school. The school definitely needs to be cleaned up. The school board has no interest in the school and turns a blind eye. Very sad indeed.
