column3: Thomson High School "strives to become a top-rank learning community," but does not accomplish this, they are far too concerned with dress code that they are totally oblivious to the fact that education is why we are there. The school is also an "alert school" at the moment because of previous students' grades so now current students are suffering- we can no longer have a bonfire(which took place after school anyways) and our ONE pep rally was cut in half and lasted only thirty minutes. There are some very excellent teachers at this school but some are not quality educators and the students suffer- also many teachers have expressed dislike for the school. If the miserable expressions on the students faces do not tell you this school is not a pleasurable experience then I don't know what will. Also I have to comment on the overpriced drinks which are all "diet" and many of the machines are constantly out of order. But in short Thomson High School is not a good school and I will not be sending my children here. Thomson High School is historic and treasured. They have great traditions and the teachers care so much about their students and their success. 5 atars -lots of CTAE pathways to meet needs of all learners Outstanding programs at THS! They have so many opportunities for students outside of core classes. Students can choose from so many excellent CTAE Programs!

column1: I have had 2 children graduate recently from AHS. Reading the other reviews I agree the school may overstress sports, but the students have alot of school spirit and parent are very involved! Both my children were accepted into very a very respectable university and were academically prepared to meet the challenge. They both have very fond memories of their high school years, and so do I. terrible school with a biased and lazy administration and guidance staff. Teacher tend not to give students their full effort. If you are a student at this school, you will be judged on your looks and race. The school has a diverse group of students that come from various econonmic backrounds. It is made up of good families who care for their childs education. It has active parent groups. Students are non judgmental, caring and driven without the the bias we may see in other schools. It is a comfortable environment that promotes education and well rounded students. People feel at home no matter who they are. Great school. I have two daughters currently attending Atholton. Both are very smart, taking full loads of GT and AP classes. Unfortunately, the teachers don't seem to keep up their end of the job. Oldest daughter was very excited to take (GT) biology and chemistry, but teachers who only read their slides every day and don't know how to explain things just totally ruined her on science. Her math classes haven't been much better. Some of the teachers must be better, but why would the GT and AP classes have such bad teachers? I hope my younger one has better luck. But AHS and the teachers should be ashamed at the poor quality teaching. I currently have one child who is a senior at Atholton. Most of the GT and AP classes are fast paced and they expect the students to come to class knowing most of the material and all of the basics. It's not just Atholton, but prevalent among all the schools, through all the grades, that the focus is on testing and on teaching. The kids are expected to learn at home with the parents, that is why parent participation is so emphasized. The JROTC program is one of the better programs in the county. However, in many instances, it is very disorganized. Although the seargents and colonel are exemplary people, they tend to reward the outstanding performers and leave the rest alone as long as they don't make waves. Their sports program was very disappointing. I wanted my child to to join a team to learn the sport and to feel a sense of belonging but instead, they only chose the "outstanding" player. They are worse than the professional teams. The coaches only showed interest and inclusion for those they deemed are or will be stars. I must agree with some of the others in that there are many lazy teachers, (I use the term loosely). But some are actually excellent! Easy transition, friendly kids, safe environment, plenty of opportunities to find your niche in sports and clubs. We are a military family that has moved often and atholton did not disappoint. Worth the higher housing costs! Your kids will have a good education and easily fit in with welcoming admin & parents. Diverse, articulate, kind, fun student body. It's been two years, one child entered as a freshman and the other a junior, two different personalities and interests, great choice for both. Atholton High School is such a wonderful school academically and is very diverse. The students are very friendly and actually care about their education. Many of the students were going on to 4 year schools, some being prestigious. The faculty are very qualified and skilled. As a student of color (black male) I felt very comfortable going to this school and felt like the staff actually cared about my education. I highly recommend this to all students and families. Some HCPSS schools are high achieving by virtue of uniformly affluent and homogeneous student bodies. By contrast, Atholton is high achieving while maintaining the economic and ethnic diversity reflective of Columbia and its ideals.We have a junior at AHS and have been delighted with his experience. The principal is dedicated and caring, the students and teachers are supportive and accepting, and kids at any academic level can learn and be challenged. By the end of his junior year our child will have completed 9 AP classes (nearly a full year of college!) with all 4s and 5s. AHS is also rich with activities; our child has enjoyed the robotics and math teams, cyber-security, table-tennis, and MTG clubs. Atholton is truly a Great School; we are grateful that our kids can attend. Love the diversity - a true representation of what a Howard County school should look like. Caring, communicative school principle, educators, & coaches who challenge students to perform at their highest level without the overly stressful environment reportedly present in some of the other area high schools. Inclusive, supportive environment in & out of the classroom. well Im only in 10th grade but so far it has been okay, there could be more support from the administration. Other than that there are a lot of students there for you even if you don't know it. (speaking from experience). Atholton’s “diversity” is soooo overstated. The school only has 8% of its students from low-income backgrounds and white and Asian students make up the over 60% of the student body. This school, like River Hill/Marriotts Ridge/Centennial/Glenelg, is ranked high because this school is NOT socio-economically diverse at all and most of the students are upper-middle-class or straight up rich. Atholton has lots of virtue-signaling “liberal” wealthy families who want to say they send their kids to a school that’s more diverse than River Hill or Glenelg but aren’t comfortable with sending their kids to Long Reach/Hammond/Wilde Lake/Oakland Mills and freaked out at the prospect of their kids being sent to one of these schools during the county-wide redistricting in 2019, while the folks who were redistricted to River Hill weren’t complaining at all. Atholton has wonderful teachers, academics, and programs, and your child will get a top-notch education there, but don’t send your children to this school thinking it doesn’t have the same problems that the other wealthy schools in HoCo have (helicopter parents, excessive competition, racism, snobbery, and “designer drugs”), because it absolutely does to some extent. Great school.No complainIt is one of good school in this area My son has a physical disability and extensive medical care. The nurses, guidance counselor, teacher, school staff and leadership have all been flexible in his schedule and make up work, empathic, solution oriented, and encourage the love of learning. My child is in all honors and GT classes and they help him flourish. He absolutely loves going to AH. He refuses special treatment and feels normal there. The students are also very kind and thoughtful kids.

column3: My son graduated from George Bush High School and I must say that it is definitely a diamond in the rough. It is one of Fort Bend ISD's hidden jewels that you don't hear very much about. It has excellent teachers, an award winning basketball team, diverse student body and great academic credentials. The only area that I would suggest a need for improvement in is the area of parental involvement. I go to George bush high school and i just want to say that the school gets such a bad reputation for no reason. We have the best principle in the world and she enforces all of the rules. We did have 2 fights thought the entire school year which is very low compared to other schools, but also what school does not have fights. Don't listen to anyone about the school unless they go to the school or work at the school. Extremely poor, Many PRE AP and AP classes are taught by substitutes or teachers with no GT training or 0 years of teaching experience Great school despite what most people may think or say of it. The JROTC program is the best there could be, and, if I'm not mistaken, it is the number one program in the greater Houston area. This school has an effective approach to homeworkTeachers try their best, they attempt to understand students situation, as a current student who has had many medical setbacks, teachers have helped accommodate me.Teachers at this school are effectiveTeachers (For the most part) try their very best, and some students are even somewhat friends with faculty, using them as people to go to in tough times. Teachers are extremely stretched out, due to the leadership, as one of my friends was taught algebra II for 75% of the year by a substitute with no training.Leadership at this school is effectiveAwful leadership. I have been taught at many strict Christian private schools, and I would rather deal with that than the people in leadership positions here. They just simply do not care whatsoever. They harass not only students but teachers as well, giving teachers unrealistic standards, which scares away teachers, meaning many classes, including Pre-AP and AP classes, are taught by mentally harassed and untrained teachers. It's extremely upsetting.This school develops strong character in its students, like integrity, compassion, and respectTeachers care. Leaders don't. Teachers try their best to be there for students and instill good morals in them as well. However many situations the leaders handle end in suspension, purely because they don't care and don't want to deal with it.This school effectively supports students with learning differencesThey try, but because of the way the school is run, with teachers that have no experience, they often fall short. This school effectively deals with bullyingAgain, many of these situations end in not only the bully being suspended, but the school will find a way to suspend the victim as well. For example, if a student were to jump me and beat me up, I would probably be suspended for trying to defend myself. It's ridiculous.

column1: The student body is very clique-ish and I feel that allegations of bullying are not investigated or handled properly. I cannot recommend this school. The staff is outstanding, helping me with all my kids paperwork. Unlike other schools, very little fights. This school is amazing! The science, law and art programs are designed to meet individual student needs and go beyond the standard curriculum. The camaraderie among students is terrific with very little fighting or bullying. The teachers are so willing to help a student succeed that they provide time at lunch, after school or at Saturday School. The administration and office staff is also top notch. They go out of their way to be friendly and helpful. I can't imagine a better school for my son to go to. There is a reason why it is ranked #7 best school in Kansas by U.S. News. We love NEM!

column3: Typical public school - not stellar and not many great teachers. Principal cares mostly about her looks, not the 5 time/day arson on her campus or the educational accountability of her teachers. It works if you have low expectations of a the school in all regards. I'm thoroughly impressed with the compassionate, competent, thoughtful teachers, administrators and counselors at Sehome. After coming from a private school experience and having children with both gifted and learning needs, I am overwhelmed by the quality and thoughtful education my children are receiving at Sehome. I'm so grateful for my children to have the opportunity to attend this school under the guidance of Mrs. Kuss-Cybula. Don't be fooled. Sehome HS is a sub-standard high school. The teachers are mediocre at best, there is minimal/no school spirit and the teachers have no control over students regardless of their outrageous behavior in class. If you have a poor or average student, Sehome won't help their academics because they will be surrounded by the same. If you have a good student, do them a favor and send them to Squalicum HS or Bellingham HS where they are more likely to get on the college path. The 5 star review below sounds suspiciously like it was written by a Sehome school administrator or teacher. Be wary. Disappointing. Send your kids somewhere else...anywhere else! I am echoing several of the negative reviews here. We started attending this school pre-pandemic in 2018. The student orientation left my student with little to no information to orient my two students. I had to return to the school and get the missing basic needs info like passwords so that my student could log onto the system and the schedule that was handed to him. (there were only 3 people there new to the school) had errors. Both my students on two different occasions told me the orientation was lead by a student who basically found a friend in a classroom and hung out with them. This happened 2 years in a row as one of my students started a year later. Even after I brought it to the attention of the staff the first year. Parent and student access to grades are a hit or miss. They often use a zero grade of F as a placeholder until a grade is put into the system. My kids have gotten lots of lectures from me for going from A students to F. To find out later the teachers were doing this. We have had several teachers not even give grading feedback to the students bringing up that the teacher knows how the kids are doing, or know they need to work on a concept before it snowballs? One teacher only posted grades, still not graded assignment feedback until the school required the grades. This was for an AP class. Another AP class was a split class where the teacher has both a study hall in the library and a class down the hall. I am not sure that was legal. Today I just received April a note from a teacher that he/she forgot to give the students a syllabus. Which that teacher is not the only one. When you get the syllabus it is more about civic behavior, morals, values rather than laying out the academic year and grading expectations for the semester. My student came to the school excelled. Was strongly discouraged from using the program that sends kids to the community college. Then my student was told to take a full load even though he only needed 2 classes his senior year since the state we came from allowed students to start high school classes in 8th grade. I have seen a significate drop in my student's performance from being very engaged in school to "what is the point". There are times I question assignments that are filler assignments and do not follow curriculum standards and objectives. There are times a student gets graded for how well they colored when it is not an art class but a math class, etc. The rare find, an excellent teacher. Sehome High School cares only for it's outward appearance. The current principal (Sonia Cole) Has put no long lasting actions in place after 3 separate threats where put onto the school within the course of a week and a half. And when trying to "follow procedures", has caused more panic in students then calming everyone down. One of the threats put the school into a full blown lockdown and not one single person knew what was going on, nobody knew if somebody was in the school with a weapon, if somebody was outside with weapon, ETC. The whole year we've had one lockout drill and no lockdown drills. And while I understand when multiple threats are put onto your school it can be stressful and hard to go about it best but it doesn't excuse the how everything was done. Besides all of that, the school preaches about inclusivity but the teachers and staff do absolutely nothing when students use gay as an insult or when they use abelist slurs in the classroom but when someone says a simple curse word you get shouted at to not say it?? The only positive thing about Sehome is it's generally nice students; I'm in my freshman year and I've been generally well by my peers which has helped me through the year but that HASN'T helped me through the year is the assignment and grading system; in some of my classes I excel because the teachers know how to work with students and keep them engaged but in other classes when a student isn't doing well or turning in assignments the teachers do almost nothing to help or actually figure out what's wrong and though not doing isn't entirely the teachers fault it doesn't mean when they do turn in something and get one thing wrong you give them a zero and tell them to do it all over again. This school is an absolute mess and its beautiful outward appearance does not make up for all of it's inward mistakes.

column1: This school was horrible, ,my classmates were overly judgemental, some teachers were biased,they would not grade fairly, and would not cater to any select student's needs, now there were a select few teachers who I will miss and were really passionate about their job, but overall the school was horrid. I have recently transferred schools and could not be happier. It is a huge school . The teachers are good, and there is a lot of students.

I don't regret anything I did/ACCOMPLISHED at waggener high school !! If a student wants to suceed , then they will !; You're given an education at waggener ; what you do with it is up to them ! They Make Us " COLLEGE & CAREER READY ONE WILDCAT AT A TIME , LETS MAKE IT A GREAT DAY WAGGENER !! #WaggenerProud I like this school! We have gone through major changes in the past 2-3 years! Its been great! I feel I have succeeded in my ap/advanced classes also in many leadership programs through my awesome councilors. The people are great too; when you figure out how to fit in with them...but overall Its been a great couple of years! This school has some very caring teachers. Small size for a public school. Would not want my children anywhere else. Probably the WORST school in JCPS! The leadership SUCKED when my child was there! Thankfully, she came to me and begged to transfer to another school where she excelled. This school should be shut down! By far the most caring school in JCPS. I have never seen a faculty as supportive and caring as they have at Waggener. The new leadership has really turned the school around! Good students come from great parenting. Judgment of how well a school preforms should not be directed only toward the teacher and staff but the :PARENTS and STUDENTS. I believe that Waggener offers a lot if you have the will to learn. I have a freshman attending Waggener that has her future already planed and is volunteering at Baptist Health. The medical program at Waggener is a hand up for the students. They can graduate with a CNA certification if the student has the will to make a difference in their life. Every student needs a great parent, Parents Please don't give up on your child, let them know that they can make a change for the better. Perfect, The Only real issue is lunch food. Im Enjoying my Experience & The teacher make the learning enviroment much more easier.

column1: Our family feels incredibly fortunate to have our children at Chief Sealth. Our children have had an outstanding experience academicaly, socially, musically. The students are friendly, the staff and principal are outstanding, and our kids are challenged and engaged. I feel very fortunate to have chosen Chief Sealth International High school, where I am soon to be a senior (c/o 2011). The teachers and staff are extremely helpful and quick to accommodate special needs. Other students are friendly. In regards to the "reputation" it has received from students enrolled in other schools and middle school students looking at high schools is almost completely unfounded and undeserved. This school is extremely diverse and safe, no matter what people continue to say. The IB (international baccalaureate) program is challenging and yet informative. Another bonus is the two academies offered by the school, Academy of Hospitality and Tourism, as well as the Academy of Finance. Other notable programs include Proyecto Saber, Global Leadership/Global Visionaries exchange program, and the school now houses the Confucius Institute of the State of Washington Education Center. I love Chief Sealth International High School. This probably one of the worst high schools in Seattle. There's has been many bullying cases. Students do not feel safe. It is a crime to be smart, to want to thrive. Students will get beaten for being a 'nerd'. The teachers, frankly, have given up on all students because the students don't care anymore. This school gives students a reason for depression and I won't even say what depression leads up to. Do not send your child to this school. It may have been good in the past but as of 2011 and beyond, stay clear. This school has the worst principal in the district. She is new to the school this year. Has a top down only management style and has no respect for some great long term teachers and support staff. She talks to no one. Staff moral is at an all time low. Teachers and support staff are leaving and going elsewhere. I have observed this school over the past 20 years. This is it's worst time ever. Since the new principal at Sealth started just this year, everything has been going downhill. Not only are students looked down upon but the teachers are as well. The administration now has no respect for their students and don't take the opinions of the students and staff into consideration whatsoever. Although the administration is sub par, the teachers are wonderful and extremely great at what they do. With that said, I still believe the authority of the administration outweigh the good of the teachers. I find it sad to see Chief Sealth's great teachers under the horrid rein of the new administration who seem to only care about what they think is right. I haven't once seen the principal interact with any of her students, other than telling girls their outfits are inappropriate or boys to pull their pants up. I look forward to if/when this principal begins to understand her duty as a principal is one who doesn't just scold kids for the bad, but to encourage them for the good. I'm so sorry if you ever have to go to this school in the future -- it will not be a pleasant experience. My children attend Sealth and overall we are happy. The teachers and staff are great with my kids, unfortunately the Principal is the worst Principal in the district and needs to move on or retire. She does not respect the teachers, staff or students. 5 stars for teachers and staff, 1 star for Principal. Unfortunately my experience has been really bad. Chief Sealth could be so good. They have amazing programs, a beautiful campus and a community rich in diversity. The principal does nothing to bring out the best of people. Most of her staff is just waiting for her to "retire or leave so she can take care of her family" I refuse to be part of a community that is only waiting for its leader to go away. No IB program, dual immersion pathway, mariachi band, academy of finance is enough for my family to stay. We are leaving but my heart breaks for families that do not have any other choice for their kids to prepare for college or any other opportunities in life.

column3: I have nothing good to say about this school. When my son went to this school years ago, he hated it. Please note that this happened a few years ago and I don't know if it has change since then. Discrimination among students was one big issue. Students skip school all the time and teachers don't care if you go to school or not. Academically, they are slow. Coming from a european U.S. Military base, my son was disappointed that they are still taking lessons that he already took 6 months prior. He was hoping that they were somewhat advance. Therefore, he wasn't challenged and he couldn't wait to move to another school which we eventually did. It takes a village? Please. It takes parents taking control of their responsibility (children). This is our first year at Hampton. We are there only because the program my child is in is only provided there. Discipline is poor but you can lay that at the feet of parents and also the school board. The board is more concerned with a law suit than anything else. Social engineering seems to be the primary educational goal. If you can afford to, move out of the city entirely, home school or go private. Our experience with the teachers has been very good overall however. With one exceptithison they do their jobs and actually care. In the case of this school, nothing will change until they expelled about 25% of the students there and let them begin their careers elsewhere. DO NOT ATTEND THIS SCHOOL. We have had numerous bomb threats and fights. My shirt was ruined by applesauce that was thrown on me during the most recent fight at lunch. If you don't wear Diamond Supply, Jordans, Coogi, or Eckno Untd., you automatically don't fit in. Hampton High school has a great faculty and staff. They truly care about the students and want them to succeed. The students have a wide variety of classes, clubs and activities to choose from. While Hampton High might be well known for it's sports that is definitely not all it has to offer. It truly is a great school! My son transferred to this school if that is what you want to call it in January from California. The day we arrived to enroll him we saw a son, his father, and the vice principal involved in a physical altercation in the hall. We also watched many children hanging out in the hall well after the bell for class rang. Security guards laughing and inappropriately joking with the children hanging out in the hallways. And as if that wasn't enough teachers not caring. Making statements like "I am going to get paid no matter if you learn it or not." No high priority on education at all. The school was more of a day camp then a educational facility. If you can send your child somewhere else than do so. This school needs to fired everybody in there and start over. The need to have several police officers on duty at all times. This school was something I seen in a movie before Joe Clark cleaned it up. I never knew such a horrible school could exist let alone in VA. This state is surrounded by higher education and to have a facility such as this. You are better home schooling your child than sending them to Hampton High School. My school is amazing, during the first week the teachers are amazing and so sweet. They help you get from point A to B and they don't hassle you. They work with you to shift you from a middle school mindset to a high schooler/ young adult mindset and it's been a pleasure so far. Hampton is continually receiving a bad rap from the community and others outside of the school for things that happened years ago or isolated incidents that happen at every school I've even taught for, including the Catholic ones.First, we're a family. That's why 96% of our seniors graduate on time. We don't let our students fail. Second, we deal with what we've got, and that's a mixture of high and low, wealthy and poor, and a good deal of institutionalized poverty. We address that head-on. Third, we try to educate and grow.I've never said I have the best students, but I always have the ones who are willing to fight against stereotypes in an effort to change them. Our student was in the IB program. Clearly, a fantastic curriculum based on critical thinking and advanced writing expectations. THE way to go if your child is undecided when looking at all the Academy options. Fat shamers, homophobic, isn't even legal, they'll discriminate If you send your kid there make sure they don't talk to the principal at all... they'll get suspended

column1: If you have the choice don't come here. this place is void of any quality My experience at this school, for the first month at least, has been a roller coaster of sentiments, mostly hatred, melancholy, and a little bit of whatever pleasure or joy you can get from a low grade, low effort in giving a feeling of security, school. Every school in this vicinity provides a sense that everyone is there to compete against each other to be better, having a hierarchy system for intelligence which, for the most part, has been rigged to where sports kids are allowed to be in higher classes due to their athletic ability and are treated better because of it. At my junior high graduation ceremony, everyone would cheer for the athletes rather than the people who will actually get somewhere, myself included. Some students are allowed to bully others, and when they get called out for it they are victimized and threatened, those who are bullied will use their past to get them in trouble, and teachers do not see the line between bullying and joking (What little joking there is). Not complaining about students as it is not the absolute worst thing, the teachings are also laid back to the point where you have no time to finish projects and end up with them missing, and some teachers ignore your questions or concerns and restate previous things they mention. Very few teachers actually made me feel secure and rather they prove to me they just relatively teach for money, as I never had a week where all the teachers I had were there and the substitute did nothing but let us do whatever we please. River Valley High School also includes little to no internet connections for most projects, insects everywhere (Dead crickets scattered through halls, walkways, etc), inadequate hygiene, and broken air conditioning, which for Arizona, when school starts during Late July - Early August, is absolutely inhumane. I currently attend because there isn't any other around where we live, going into it I already had a feeling the school would only care about sports, which I stand correct, they do it because they want money as they are excessively cheap and sketchy, to the point where I bring my own lunch instead. That being said, do NOT go to this school, if you do I am sorry for those who attend if you have to or not.

column3: This school is deplorable, my daughter transferred here from a Kentucky high school, if we could go back we would. Springstead behavioral discipline is non-existent. Students publically curse, fondle, kiss, yell and are unruly and disrespectful to peers and teachers. The faculty turns a blind eye to it all. However, their enforcement of tardy-absence borders on ridiculous. My daughter continually gets marked absent for attending approved senior school functions and the teacher gives her 30 minute lectures about how it's NOT HER JOB to correct the absence. If you have a choice, don't send your children here. It's a small town, but this high school is straight out of inner city Detroit (where I went to school, and it sucked). I want to comment on the athletic part of the school. The athletic director is just their for a pay check. He is not active on creating what every other school has. Its 2011 C'mon man update your school web site. Keep parents and students informed. Post pictures of game highlights and news. I look at other schools we compete with and I am embarrased. The site has not been updated since 2008. Get a new young athletic director who is passionate about the sports and school not just a pay check. This guy now has the personality of a rock. Also start making changes at head coach of the football team. His game plan has not changed in 10 years. Time for someone who knows how to mix it up and run a program. I moved to Spring Hill in 2003, at that time I enrolled my son into Springstead HS. When my son was in HS there were over sometimes 40 kids or more in his class, the staff was overwhelmed, and disorganized. Some of the teachers tried but with no support from the district office they started to give up. Now it is my daughters turn to be enrolled in Springstead. After the bad experience I had with my son, was expecting the worst for my daughter. But, I was pleasantly surprised, the class sizes are much smaller, the teachers are willing to help. And the staff is just wonderful exspecially my daughters consulor. She was accepted into the wevb design program and she absolutely loves it. The only complaint I have is that the school does not offer enough variety of of electives. I am very happy with this school and I am proud that my daughter is a student at Springstead HS> I think most of the staff bring down the students self esteem. I am not at all happy with the school. Also their enforcement of tardy-absence borders on ridiculous. Yelling at these kids in hallways, and if they are tardy by a few minutes/seconds and the bell just rang and they are in class with door closing behind them, they get sent to the tardy table which makes them even later and missing start of class and disturbing class. A more positive attitude should be shown to these kids in highschool to particapate more in activities, PE, etc. I have seen this school go steadily downhill in recent years. There appears to be a great lack of control at this school as the students deal with overcrowding; they are subjected to a continuous lack of respect, inappropriate language and behavior, harassment and fighting by their peers; with a seemingly tremendous lack of concern by administrators, counselors and other staff. The main priority appears to be test scores not the students. This makes for a very unpleasant atmosphere for students to 'learn' in. F W Springstead HS is no place for ESE students due to the lack of knowledge, compassion, understanding and training to accommodate students. I have seen questionable practices as administrators/staff appear to have their own set of rules and the freedom to do as they please. Parental involvement is not welcome, other than gathering volunteer hours in extracurricular activities. The only bright side this school seems to have is the theater and music programs, along with some of their sports. This school and its administrators/councelors/teachers are ALL a joke. The lack of concern for these children is simply appalling. There main priority only appears to be test scores NOT the students. This school turned there back on my son when his GPA was low and encouraged him to drop out and get a GED. To make a long story short I signed my son out of this school immediately only to enroll him in another High school and he graduated High School with his diploma,and now is enrolled in Full Sail University. So to assistant principal Ms. Michalicka and the counclers who never thought my son would NEVER make it..THANK YOU FOR BEING THE MOTIVATION BEHIND MY SONS SUCCESS. I am very pleased with the school & staff @ springstead high school. My grandson is doing very well academically,he also plays baseball for the EAGLES. I am happy that he attends springstead. Honestly, as a sophomore, my freshman experience was mediocre and not memorable, academically. If I walk into the door 5 seconds past the bell, I am sent to the tardy table, where I waste even more time and missing even more class activity. I was prepared for the IB program, but many teachers tended to be insensitive to the workload and didn't care if you were failing or not. That being said, there are the few gems that aimed to connect to the student and teach and help and guide. I have three years to go, and I'm still unsure whether or not Springstead will positively or negatively impact my high school experience. My daughter attended this school for the 10th grade and we moved to weeki wachee school district and I have done everything I could to keep her in Springstead for the ROTC program that she has participated in for two years going on three. The staff has done nothing to help, given me no helpful information and has been utterly rude to me and my daughter. There is a new principal at the school this year, but it may be too late for my daughter. If they would have given me the proper information I could have applied for special circumstances months ag,o but no one would help. I would prefer my daughter in weeki wachee but unfortunately they don't offer ROTC and this could drastically change the direction of my daughters future and no one seems to care. But if I walked in and said I was homeless and needed my daughter in school, they would be happy to sign her up without documentation....that just doesn't make sense! Now last second waiting to hear where my daughter will be going on Monday morning. The staff at this school really needs to be re evaluated and given some proper manner courses to deal with people!!! So frustrated!!! In 2014-2015, as a new principle and new administration comes in Springstead. I have seen the changes as bad ones. They think they know everything and they don't even realize how hard it could be with all the new changes including the testing. Now there will be tests called yellow testing. Which still including the 6 EOC of all of the classes, the SAT, and the PAT. It would be a great school if they stop making kids worried about getting the best scores. I have even heard students talking about Christmas treeing all of the new testes. But don't get me wrong. Most teachers think this is ridiculous. But they can't say anything because they'll get fired or the administration won't listen because the adminstration think they know everything. Dress code very strict. If your shirt shows any shoulder you're in trouble. Even if you're wearing a jacket over it. Some teachers don't even really teach! They give you a textbook and tell you to figure it out. The football team stinks. Most of the Spanish teachers stink. Kids are thrown into AP classes just so the school can get more money. You practically pay fees for most of your classes. The current way school lunch is set up leaves little time for students to eat- the fact the school is overpopulated does not help at all. The time to travel between classes is way too small and teachers constantly say you should have gone to the bathroom between classes but you never get the chance. There is so much homework you'd be lucky if you have any time to do anything else after school unless you're willing to stay up to midnight. IB students get special treatment. The school reeks, the bathrooms are disgusting and half the sinks don't even work, there's cockroaches everywhere. The coffee is gross, most of the food is. Teachers are invasive. The only good parts are band and Latin. My daughter has been to 3 High Schools based upon our military requirements and let me tell you Springstead is BY FAR the best. Dont get me wrong, there are issues, overcrowding, faculty disconnect, and the usual bullying issues. However, Springstead has the best run administration Ive seen. They hold the students accountable for their actions and attempt to treat all students the same. Dress code is strictly enforced (a good thing). Lunch is 30 minutes long allowing the students enough time to eat and go to class. Again, Springstead has its issues, but overall its a great school! So far its only been 2 weeks and I am just disappointed in the school overall. They don't seem to ask parents what they think about anything with some of their policies. The kids have to dress for winter in the freezing cold classrooms and then they say 2.3 miles is a "reasonable" walking distance home in the 95 degree heat. Then leggings are a big no-no which I really don't understand. Tight shirts are ok but leggings are scandalous? So not only ISS for dress code violation but my daughter has to walk over 2 miles home with jeans on. Not a good start so far. Just teach already! The school is okay. A wall was built to protect us from active shooter situations, but we only have one door to get in and out of the building when school is in session, so we're basically fish in a barrel. Additionally, I've seen ants and cockroaches everywhere, and it seems like nothing is being done about it.

column1: I am a mother of an incoming senior and we have been very pleased with the education my son has received at Henry Ford Academy at Greenfield Village. Coming from a private school for K-8th my expectations high and the school has lived up to them. Henry Ford Academy has been ranked #1 for Charter High Schools in the Detroit area. That with the campus in the #1 History attraction in the nation makes for a great experience. I have twin daughters who are graduating from HFA this Monday, June 13th. They attended school here their junior and senior years. The only thing I would change is for them to have attended freshman and sophomore years too. We love the school and staff. The teachers are great, they truly care about the kids and want them to excel. They go above and beyond to help them. Their grades improved and they met so many great friends here. We attended a baccalaureate service the other night with some of their classmates from their old high school, I was surprised after when they said they didn't miss their other school at all. They said it was just how they remembered, lots of clicks. I have recommended this school to many people. We even brought two of their friends from their old high school with us junior year. We have had nothing but positive experiences here and will miss the school and staff very much. I am a freshmen at HFA and I just want to say that I was in the position where I didnt know which highschool to go to( it was between HFA and riverview community high school) and about a month before the school year i finally decided henry ford academy and so far its the best descion i have made. the best school ever in mi to me.just because it in a museum.we have the best teacher that help use out and care about us. This school has many fights without teachers being aware. Students fight mainly in the bathroom. Students drove my son around campus just so he can fight him in the museum bathroom. HFA is the ideal environment if you prefer your child to be educated in a small personalized environment. HFA's class size allows the teachers to become personally familiar with each student. The academic requirements are stringent with a AP program for students that qualify. HFA also provides a program that includes students with special needs. It is important that students receive their education in an environment that exposes them to the real world. My son is a 10 th grader and enjoys his time at HFA. I would highly recommend this school I am a freshman at HFA. I love this school so much. The school is small and you can talk to your teachers. At many schools parents can't even talk to the faculty, but at hfa you can email the teachers and get a quick response. The teachers are excellent and very kind. The students are also very kind and welcoming. This school is also very amazing because the 9th grade canpus is in the henry ford museum and the upperclassmen campus is in greenfield village. This is a remarkable experience. Not many people have this oppurtunity. I recommend this school to any student or staff. Class of 2017!! HFA is a great school with a ton of history. HFA does a great job preparing students for college. It's a good school and it will prepare you for high school. One of the best schools in Detroit. HFA is a good school and a good fit for my daughter! The unique environment of the school gives the kids a one of a kind experience, but more importantly I like that it is not too big and the teachers my daughter has taught to her level. The accelerated (ACE) program is good, I just wished it allowed for more interaction between the ACE kids and their grade level peers. My daughter is a senior and she loves it! It's given her great opportunities, that I don't think she would have gotten in a lot of other schools. I would recommend it, especially for students that are academic focused. HFA is an amazing experience for students. Students at HFA go to school in a world class museum and are more than just a number they are treated with respect.

column3: I am an 80 year old Grandparent whose Grandson is on the golf team. At his golf match yesterday, carts for the able bodied were not allowed. Bob Sullivan, Golf Coach, recognized that 80 year olds are not designed to walk 18 holes. He arranged for a cart which was greatly appreciated. I believe his kindness and caring typifies most teachers at BFHS. I should add that Mrs.Kaufmann, Administrator, is a graduate of BFHS and the best addition ever to the Administration Staff. All 3 of my sons attended BFHS. The last one would have graduated in 2003. Each of them has gone on to become a leader in his chosen career. During their years at Big Foot, teachers worked with the boys to help each find his individual goal. What I like particularly about Big Foot is, it is not steeped in Psychiatric babble as are so many public schools (Since the APA took over the U.S. school system in 1963) and my sons easily opted out of psychiatric experimentation in the classroom. The school is still small enough for parents to have a say. Staff is outstanding, as well as the administration. Wish they had put in a swimming pool when they renovated, though! Hardly needed I guess, with lakes all around. The building is spacious and clean, the kids are cool! I should know - I was a school bus driver for some years and still live right behind the school. With parental interest, your kids are sure to receive a good education at Big Foot. BFHS is rated by US News and World Report as a great school.

column1: Dealing with administrators that live in a bubble and refuse to see that they have issues they are neglecting. Overall the worst education experience my children have had. Incidents that hopefully do not scar for life.

column3: Prairie ridge offers a large amount of classes and I urge you to take a look at them they do offer honor and ap classes but they are hard to come by unless you have been set up with honors classes your entire life. I am not happy, no one cares about the student who wants more challenging classes and they make it extremely hard and frustrating to get into those classes it is not a good school for getting into America's best rated colleges and gives students a very limited educational experience. Prairie ridge is a good school I'll give it that, but academically it does not excel in. If your student wants a higher education you will not find it here, but the football team is good. I am a former student of P.R.H.S. & I can say without a doubt that this is one of the best schools in the area. I graduated from P.R.H.S. in 2004 and went on to graduate from Illinois State University with a teaching degree. The academics, atmosphere, athletics, students here gave me some of the greatest experiences of my life and I will always be grateful for that. If the child has 100% attendance and never questions why, there will be no problems here. However, not all the instructors are capable of dealing with a challenging child. The PE dept is quite draconian in it's grading system as well. One of my children caught a cold because she was playing a softball game for PR on a wet cold day. She missed 2 days of school, which were excused. She received two zero's in PE because policy dictates a zero is issued for non participation regardless of reason. Those zeros dropped her from an A- to a B+ and have affected her overall GPA. Utterly ridiculous. This school is great if your child is doing well and are on a clear college-bound track, lots of positivity and support., however, If your child runs into trouble or has issues you are on your own. If you ask for intervention do not expect any help. I have experienced both with kids in this school. I definitely feel that it was a mistake sending my kids to this school, especially that we are surrounded by outstanding school districts just 20 miles from Crystal Lake I see these other reviews and scratch my head. I have two students attending PR and they really like the school. Both are athletes as well as taking liberal arts courses, business, computer and the general education cirriculum.Honestly there is so much available that at times it is almost overwhelming. College prep, SAT prep. Student having trouble? There's help. Want to be in the play - sign up. Like sports? PR has them. PR and D155 does a great job communicating as well. Just read your emails!In short, tis is an excellent school. I believe you make of the experience what you wish to. Embrace the programs, embrace the activities, be the leader you are capable of being. Opportunities are around every corner. Do you walk away or grab ahold? We can all blame others for things or we can take ownership and make an incredible life. Such is life. Have one graduate and a current freshman. Wonderful school climate, enthusiastic teachers. Focus is on being well rounded students with academics and activities. Happy to be a part of it. Excellent staff and administrators. The cool is pushing for educational equity, and encourages parental and family involvement. Both of my children graduated from Prairie Ridge High School. Both of my children had amazing experiences at PR. They both were ready for college and have done very well. Prairie Ridge has been wonderful so far for my son. The extracurricular activities are well-organized and it seems as if there is definitely something for everyone. Teachers have been great at facilitating learning and have been understanding and accommodating. I am glad we moved in this neighborhood- we have 2 other children who will be joining Prairie Ridge highschool in the future and I feel confident that they will graduate with the skills and knowledge needed to succeed. Such an amazing school with some really great teachers.

column1: I don't belive in this school they don't care about the children nor do they do anything to stop bulling. someone needs to step in and take control and remember school is about education not sports and rich kids. Our School has been one of the highest performing schools in the region for a couple of years running. Our band is a yearly contender for the State Title, with a state championship in our recent past. Students who participate in our science club have been to national competitions in Envirothon and SeaPerch. Our 2014 team placed 3rd overall in Hattiesburg Miss! My kids really enjoy working with the staff. This school has nothing but a good future.

column3: Henley is the best high school in the area. Test scores are above all other schools in Klamath and one of the highest in the state. Staff care about students personally and take an interest in their success. Athletics are second to none. it is a good place to learn, but i mean it is a high school, there is going to be some inappropriate behavior all in all it is a great learning environment and this schools athletics are second to none. I now have my second child attending Henley HS. I was very pleased with the education my oldest child got here. She was well prepared for college when she graduated. My second child has many different interests and we find she has more than enough opportunities to participate in a wide range of activities. The teachers are caring and have good leadership from a newer administration. I find the front end of the school is running much more smoothly. My children have always felt safe and valued at this school. Parents are given many chances to volunteer in just about any area they would like. I will be pleased to send my third child to school at Henley HS. The counselors have a hard time with students who are taking advanced college classes that count towards HS credits. Followup to parents was almost nonexistent. Causing issues with needed credits. The high school also gets their “100%” graduation rate by moving failing kids to Falcon Heights academy. All in all not the worst school in town but also not the best. My daughter went through all 3 Henley schools. She took all honors classes while in high school and learned a lot as her teachers really cared about the education she received while there.. Many of her teachers had her challenged in her classes to help encourage her to do research on her own. She graduated in 2021 with a 4.0 top of her class with honors diploma and just shy of a 2 year college degree. As a parent I was and continue to be involved with my childern's education. I found that her teacher were always available to discuss concerns I may have had. I never had a issue with the administration as if there where any issues They were always very willing to help address them.Great school. yet it is high school..

column1: The teachers and administrators seem to really care about the students. Student attendance is a real problem and a major reason why students perform below average on standardized scales. The kids who come to school and try are well prepared for college or a career.

column3: Sanderson is truly the best kept secret in Raleigh. Excellent teachers, rigorous academics, strong administration, and a real sense of community. Sanderson has very high test scores and success in the university system. We've had two children attend Sanderson and we would not choose any other high school. Our third will go next year. Excellent school!! I have had one student graduate from Sanderson...doing great in college. He was definitely prepared for the rigors of college classes. Have another son that is currently a junior. Wouldn't want to be anywhere else. Great coaches, teachers and administration. Trying to get back into the Sanderson school district because I love the Special Education services that my now junior has been receiving. I totally agree that Sanderson is Raleigh's best kept secret. I would not want my child to be enrolled anyplace else. Sanderson is a well kept secret. It s not inside the beltline so it doesn t get the recognition that Broughton does. It is a great school and it has a family feeling. It s has an inclusive attitude for all the students who are there to learn. There are several programs designed to help students. They have a fantastic AFJROTC program with instructors who are dedicated to helping students get prepared for life after high school, whether it s community college, college, trade school etc. If you have the opportunity to go to Sanderson I recommend it and you should check out AFJROTC!!!!! I LD child who attend Sanderson. He has done very very well there. Everyone from the Administration to his IEP team to his classroom teachers have always helped him to succeed. He is a proud AFROTC cadet. This Program is excellant. It has won the distinguished unit award every year for the past 8 years. I definitely would NOT send my son to any other school. Sanderson is also ranked nationally as one of the best high schools in the nation!!! Go check it out and you will understand why This school has gone downhill fast. This year (2013-2014), the scheduling and student services staff have done an AWFUL job in preparing for a switch to a new system. NONE of the other area high schools had problems. Students received their schedules weeks before school started. Sanderson had the students pick up their schedules on a "walk around" day a few days prior to school starting. The schedules were ALL messed up. Holes in schedules, random classes, no upperclassman priority on getting in a class to graduate. It's been absolutely terrible and the principal and staff should be ashamed. Worst communication ever. DO NOT COME TO THIS SCHOOL. Find another option. It's abysmal and getting worse by the year. As far as the teachers, there are a few good ones, but MOST of them are just mediocre. Even in some of the honors classes you have some people just phoning it in. The Math curriculum is dreadful and getting worse with Common Core. They haven't spent the time to train the teachers so the classes aren't as available esp. for Honors students. It's a real shame. There is so much potential but it is being completely obliterated by some really incompetent people. This school works against you every step of the way. Before I graduated, I married an United States Sailor and changed my last name. The office women put me down and paraded my marriage certificate around, asking for people's opinions on me marrying so young and always asking me when I was due. I was never pregnant. I graduated in the top 15% and also from the North Carolina School of Science and Math Online. Sanderson refused to let me wear my metal from the School of Science and Math without giving me a real reason. We couldn't throw our caps at graduation or anything traditional. DO NOT make your children go here, it will be the worst mistake you will ever make. Sanderson has been wonderful for my son. It's a very nurturing environment. The administration and staff are fantastic! Sanderson has very caring and dedicated teachers. The level of support available to students is huge. They focus on student success and are constantly looking for opportunities to get better. Scheduling was much better this year. Great school! I have 2 kids at Sanderson and they have enjoyed their high school experience and I have been very impressed with the majority of the teachers. Looking back, Sanderson was the perfect high school for my kid. The size kept things manageable without them being lost in a sea of faces. Teachers reached out at critical times.,My kid was not a genius nor high enough to be a junior Marshall BUT the preparation in the honors and AP courses prepared them so well they got accepted into all universities applied to and is performing at the highest rank possible as freshman in top tier school! The Academy of Finance is a hidden treasure in terms of preparing the child for real life exposure to computer programs, budgeting and business courses in college. Now they are a full year ahead of people in the business school already with a great resume. Sanderson was small enough to accommodate a lot of kids who might not have played at larger schools in the athletics arena. Special needs kids were treated to a wonderful club students volunteered in to make them feel special. The rankings do not take into account the high number of disadvantaged students who go to Sanderson but who make it a great place to learn about different populations in the real world. College was a seamless transition for my kid because they were at a school where the focus was not on rich kids driving up in fancy cars. The “relaxed” casual vibe meant kids were dressed fairly simply and They could bust it in the APhonors courses or find niches in ROTC or drama etc. Just ask admissions counselors how well they have taken to Sanderson students ;) I feel strongly that “education“ should include developing interpersonal skills with different types of people. The environment at Sanderson cultivates this because it is so eclectic and I appreciated growth opportunities that exposure to immigrants, etc. provided us. The parents involved in the school deeply cared and made significant contributions. It is a public school and cannot be expected to have unlimited resources nor enough counselors for the need but while my kid was there and Dr. Decker was the principal for the most part kids were manageable and had whatever opportunities they chose to take advantage of right before them.I’m always shocked that SandersonHS is not ranked higher given the success rate I have seen. Sad. One more thing... Every school has its cliques but at S it didn’t seem to be the driving part of the culture. Walk the halls and you’ll see wide diversity is accepted as normal.

column1: My son goes to the Wheaton Engineering Magnet and he could not be happier. The teachers are great at the school. They are energetic and engaging with the kids. We live in Olney but because my son went to Lee Middle in the DCC he was able to apply to the Magnet. I moved to Olney for the schools and now I drive my son to and from Wheaton every day. It's worth it for the academics and school over all. Looking forward to the new school, opening this winter. Wheaton High School makes learning and education a fun experience with 4 excellent academies and 2 excellent magnet programs! I love coming to school everyday because the teachers allow me to enjoy learning and working! They really are great teachers. The teachers are so enthusiastic and respectful! The school's diversity is beautiful and makes the school very unique. If you want to make a mistake in life, go to Wheaton. The people there have lots of different bad intentions for you to choose from. Amazing. The administration is very much on the ball. Our test scores are outstanding ; the information here is incorrect. Wheaton high school is a great school to be honest it is really hard no to succeed all you got to do is work and you get a good grade Ever since the opening of its new building, WHS has become a great school. Students have wide ranges of opportunities in multi-level courses and academies, school spirit is increasing every year, teachers are attentive and challenge their kids. There are a lot of slackers at Wheaton who don’t put in effort at all and fail classes, but most of the students care about their grades. I’m sure Wheaton will be seen as even better once they finish our football field. The biggest problem I have is that WHS is becoming more and more white, since the magnet programs are growing and the new building makes the school attractive. The school definitely has way less gang affiliation, but fights are still a weekly occurence and we have had issues with vandalism in the past. Overall, WHS is a great school to go to despite its bad reputation, and I wouldn’t want to spend 4 years at any other school. I love this school. My child has been here all 4 years and I feel like we have won the lottery with Wheaton. My child feels welcomes, supported and challenged. The school works hard to help children succeed, which isn't easy given the population served. Many have English as a second language and parents are struggling. I would say that the school overall is good, and the teachers are good, but classes are a tad big. It’s about 20 a class. I currently have an 18 year old (graduating senior) and a 16 year old (sophomore) at WHS. LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this school! The teachers are extremely helpful and the faculty is very supportive. My kids receive the help and guidance they need and my 18yr old senior was able to get into the CDI program (Collegiate Directions - a truly amazing program that offers students step by step guidance and aid throughout the college application process. The counselors stay in touch with the students through their years in University).Wheaton Knights are focused and engaged.- Judy (WHS parent)

column3: The chances of finding a good person who doesn't smoke or drink on a regular basis as a friend are slim. That's my main reason for not liking this school. Some teachers are great, but others are not. The size fools you, it does seem smaller once you're inside. 'Nuff said I attend the school now and I believe the school is great and you truly have a great experience while there. This school is good and mostly because I have never experienced bullying but then again maybe that's because I'm a quiet girl who doesn't talk as much. Teachers are helpful......but there are a couple that are bossy. So yea that about sums it and this my senior year so yea. The school is a place to learn about the real world. At first it seems huge, but once you get used to the size it's not that bad. The school has many interesting classes from cooking to car engineering. They also have a tv studio that is used to give information to students. Although it may seem that the amount of people in this high school is insane, it ends up being ok once you are attending it. Bullying happens everywhere, and this school is not perfect, but since there are so many people, it was very rare when I was going there. Another great benefit is there are clubs for, literally, EVERYTHING, and if there isn't one you want, you make one. It is pretty great. Our principal was great, although he retired, the new principal is awesome too. The only problem you might have is being stuck in a traffic jam in the hallways and be a few minutes late to class, but teachers, for the most part understand, because they get stuck too :P arlington high school offers very very many AP classes. most AP class teachers are top level teachers. Music program is one of the best in the nation. 4 full size orchestra in the school and they won grand national championship 2 years ago! Science research class won several different national science research competition . My son is struggling and not getting the help that he needs despite the fact that he is classified and has an IEP. When I called the guidance counselor to ask what else could be done, she asked me "what do you want me to do? The school has no money." Disgusting. I would not recommend this district unless your child is self motivated and very smart. The music program at this school is national level caliber. With 4 orchestras, 2 choral groups, 5 bands and a plethora of small groups from Jazz Bands to String groups, plus the Marching Band, the music teachers are top notch. The vast diversity of clubs and groups at this school means that you will find your niche. With a population topping out at 3,500 almost 10 years ago now, the idea of an overwhelming populace can be daunting, but you quickly get used to it and find yourself learning how to navigate the congested halls like a pro. Bullying is a problem at every school no matter where you go unfortunately, but with Arlington's sheer size and population you rarely see and/or experience it. One of the best school districts that you'll come across given size, population, budget, location, teachers and student activites spend too much money on school bus purchasing; qualtiy of education is not as good as that of 10 years ago. John Jay HS has better academic programs especially AP math, stat and other science subjects. Going to this school made my life a living hell. It was okay. But that’s only because I was on the basketball team and kinda popular. But for most I doubt it was a very comfortable environment Arlington is a great school offering many courses that are not available at other schools. Arlington offers many AP and honors classes as well as classes that are outside of the "norm" you would see at other high schools in the area. Some of these courses include, Contemporary Issues in Biomedical Sciences, Philosophy, Criminal and Civil Law, Forensics, Psychology, Science Research, etc. After Arlington I went to a private college with many high achieving students from "high achieving" high schools. None of them took classes that even came close to the ones I was offered. My professors were also impressed at the long list of classes. As far as teachers go, many of them are amazing and willing to do anything to help their students. Many of the teachers are very involved within the Arlington Community and have degrees from some of the best schools in the country (Ivy League, Seven Sisters, etc.). I left Arlington truly prepared for college. And Arlington sports are some of the best in the area. There are many teams to choose from and many of them win the league and some are even state champions. I also believe that we are the only school in section 1 that has two turf fields for athletic teams to use. I did not have much experience with the music program at Arlington but I have been told that it is very strong and nationally recognized. Same for the marching band. They are usually state champions. Even though Arlington is a big school, there really is a place for everyone to fit in.

column1: I think this school would be okay if the students knew how to behave other than that this school is good [; I feel this way because I think you can get yourself a better life and make you feel satfied My daughter is in the IB program at this school, and is in the top of her class. The curriculum is challenging and the teachers care.
