column3: We chose to live in Hanover for the schools and it was the best decision we could have made. Our kids ('10, '12) never had a social problem, have received wonderful educations in and out of the classroom. The only complaint would be the enormous amount of homework, more work than the oldest is getting at a top-10 national college. I am unfortunate enough to be a student at this school and I hate it. Its cliquey and cold. The teachers are good but the culture in this school is such that kids are overworked and stressed. Kids never get a break. I cant wait get out of here. Don't send your kids here! I graduated from HHS several years ago. My experience may be a bit dated but I do recognize several teachers and faculty on the current directory. My experience is that HHS is an outstanding public high school for high achieving students. Where it falls short is dealing with the average (B and C type grades) or special needs students. As a little bit of a late bloomer academically, and thus just an average high school student, I was written off by several teachers. One very highly regarded teacher even told my parents she did not want to "waste" her time with me because I was a "lost cause". Well I graduated college with honors, have a masters degree, make well into six figures annually, and am trusted with the lives of hundred of people daily, so her professional judgement was way off base. Like I said, it is a great public school for high academically achieving students, several classmates attended the Ivy League schools and other highly prestigious universities. But average and special needs students can expect to become surprisingly lost for such a small school. Academically, you're not going to get a better place for a public school. I'm a senior and can say that while I love Hanover's drive for academic success, it can become incredibly stressful at times. The pressure for us as students to perform at a high level is intense; I have a 3.77 GPA and I'm ranked fairly low among my peers, who hold 3.8 like a golden standard as to whether or not you're a great student. Besides the academic pressure, I've also experienced my share of social pressure. Because Hanover is a fairly wealthy community, it produces high schoolers with very nice and expensive materials. It seems like everyone has a Macbook and an iPhone or other variety of smartphone. I don't have one and get along just fine, but it does deplete your social status just a bit. Finally, the part that makes me give Hanover a four star rating is the teachers. I have had incredible teachers my four years at Hanover that have all wanted to see me succeed. Whether you come into the school with a 4.0 or a 3.0, there is always going to be someone willing to stand in your corner to make sure you perform to your best. So, great academic school but a lousy one socially. That's all there is to it. Yes, the education is adequate. I have definitely seen better and seen worse. This school is very clique-y. Money talks, if you are not athletic or rich you are pretty much outta luck. Good education, bad high school experience. Beware. This school has a wide variety of options for students, both academically and sports-wise. There is a lot of freedom, something critical for a School, especially a High School. I was a student at Hanover High. This school has a very good education and lots of freedom. And also, Hanover High is known for having good athletics. But my experience at Hanover High wasn't what I wanted. It is very clique and it's hard to make friends. You would have to dress well, be good at sports, and be pretty to fit in. That wasn't my scene. Don't know how I survived but I am glad to be out of that school. Academically, not the best school. Very stressful- but it's only busywork, nothing important or difficult academically. The music program is quite good. They have some talented musicians, nothing special but very good for teenagers (I went to their concert). Their sports are very good. It's a very cliquey school and sort of typical. I would have rather gone to a different public school or even a private school. We moved to this area of New Hampshire because of the amazing reputation of this school - as well as the high SAT scores and test scores overall. We haven't been disappointed! It would be difficult to find a better public school. The academics, teachers, and extra-curricular activites are 2nd to none. We are so pleased with this school! We couldn't rate or recommend it more! I do not have any comment to make about this high school in Hanover New Hampshire As a graduate, I'm giving HHS 5 stars—though that should not imply I think it is perfect. I can agree with the gist of the comments here: 1) HHS has excellent academics and teachers2) HHS teachers (especially in honors classes) expect quite a bit out of their students 3) There is a good deal of peer pressure from other students to succeed 4) The athletics are overall solid and important to the sense of community5) Groups of friends tend to be fairly tight-knit.I do not agree that Hanover is "cliquey" in the sense that one needs to be x or y to fit in. Every school has students who are more well-known or otherwise "popular" than others. If you look at the different friend groups they aren't really based on anything in particular. It isn't like a movie where you have the jocks and the nerds—at all. HHS is a place where intelligence, athleticism, ambition, and social ability are all respected and seem to be entered into the popularity calculation.My favorite aspect of HHS was easily the students, whom I found insightful, and the classroom environment, which I found intellectually engaging. I went on to attend an Ivy, and while I found the faculty excellent, I missed my HHS peers. I'd traded in the free-thinking intellectualism of Hanover for the worker-bee-lets-make-money Ivy mentality. Hanover is a special place not for everyone. Visit and decide if it's right for you or your child. There is a culture of bullying, hazing, sexual harassment, threats and cyberbullying at HHS. The administration has done nothing to stop or address this other than to victim blame. Victim blaming not only perpetuates the situation, but reinforces the culture and re victimizes the person who has been bullied. HHS is not a safe environment for all. Don't expect any help if you report. Expect the opposite. If you are considering a move to Hanover and it's for the schools, beware. Very disappointed. We chose this school because of its reputation, but it’s really not lived up to a minimum standard for leadership and safety. I’ve had two children with very different personalities and aptitudes graduate from HHS. They both came out very prepared and, in fact, graduated from college after four years of hard work and success. As with any school, some HHS teachers were stronger than others. If I had any concerns as a parent, the school was receptive to meeting with me to hear about and address them.

column3: Very bad school. Bad teachers, bad principals, and the buildings need a little TLC after 70 years but I guess in Doniphan buildings are suppose to be chipping away..and really unfair discipline. The teachers just really don't care about anything else but that salary. I should know. I've had 3 teachers say the same thing that they don't care if I flunk. They are still being payed and they are always complaining about the pay. Teacher I had sat at her desk taught us nothing.she just handed us busy work and never graded anything.just gave us a grade for showing up.also this school has a lots of fights..some of the glass doors have cracks.some teachers let there students have there phones out in class Playing music while others try and work.how can a person concentrate when another student is barring music.. I graduated a few years ago and nothing has changed. When I was there Several teachers said to the class "I do not care if you pass or fail, I get paid the same". These are high school students not college students, you have to get them interested in school. The building is old and run down. If you want your kids to have a good life and have them go to college and get a good job, not have to worry about the next payday. This is not the school to be in. Nearly a third of the class dropped out in high school. Okay so what, some kids just dont make the cut. Not even a dozen people out of a class of over a hundred have completed a four year degree. So If you want them to graduate from doniphan, Don't worry they will stay close to home because they will work at mcdonalds, Briggs, Vitronic, or will sell drugs to make there money. I have had more positive interactions at the school than negative ones. It definitely has its faults as does any school. There is a lot that needs repaired and fixed both in the staff and the buildings but when the community refuses to pass any new tax raises then I'm not sure how they expect the school to improve things. If the community and parents would step up and start supporting the school, the administration, and the staff then we would see an improvement in the school. In the most kind and general description of my experience: Teachers have long stopped caring. Students talk over class. Sexual harassment is rampant. Corporal punishment is still a part of discipline. This school did nothing but prepare me to meet the minimum test scores for state requirements. Going to college was a wake-up call for how unprepared and out of touch DHS left me... And I was EXTREMELY lucky. Tax payers, I beg you invest in this poor city's education. It will make the world of difference for your children, grandchildren, and the future of Doniphan as a whole.

column1: My student loves this school. She feel challenged and enjoys that the rules and regulations are strictly followed. She sought this school herself when she found her old high school was not meeting the challenge she wanted. The staff is caring and lets you know what is expected. They encourage the student to flourish and branch out. I like the family school environment, but I do get frustrated because I don't know how my child is doing until it is almost to late to reverse the low grades. The school feels that each student is responsible for their own grade, but I believe some children need to be kept on track by their parents. To graduate or not graduate is not an option, students are challenged in all classes and this school requires more credit hours than most high schools so that the students can compete when it comes to getting into the right college. This school trys to take your money in almost every single way and does not repay when have to and they fail to live up to their promises of a "working education". And if a student fails to live up to their very high standards, their kicked out without a explanation Cristo Rey High School, is the school that other schools should model. Students, required to work weekly to gain the necessary skills and experience to be self-sufficient, is a curricula model to replicate. While the expectations of the school administrators are high for their students, in the corporate world as it relates to employment, an employer's expectations are higher as well as any college, university or post-secondary learning institute. Overall, the curriculum design prepares students, our community and nations future leaders to be self-sufficient. Keep up the good work staff members. Parents, be patient with the staff and get INVOLVED and stay fully ENGAGED without wavering. Together, your teen, teachers, administrative staff, other community adults and you, will have a student, who will be more focused on purposely pursuing their future career to be self-sufficient.

I graduated from there. Went to the army. Went to college. Worked for san bdno county schools. And now my son attends. I am a parent who goes to games. Talks to teachers security and coaches. When I entered college, students who attended other high schools complained about how difficult it was. For me it was easy because the coursework in the SBHS honors program was equal to or more difficult than the coursework assigned by my college professors. Because someone cares about my child enough to make a call home when she was falling behind in her studies SBHS is the very best! The school provides hands-on learning such as the e-Bussiness class that runs and operates The Nest student store and the coffee shop in which they are trained and certified by Starbucks. As well as the Publish Safety class that provides students with knowledge and experiences in careers that involve public safety and are certified by CPR; FEMA certifications including Incident command system, Emergency Planning, Active Shooter What You Can Do, An Introduction to Hazardous Materials, and Fundamentals of Emergency Management. Cardinal City also will include a 21st-century Makerspace for engineering that will work on 3D printers and animatronics from Garner Holt the world's largest Manufacturer of Animatronics & Animatronic Figures and designer of Disneyland robots. This school has unique features such as the Cardinal City Museum that showcases the history of the school and the community do their rich history that data back to 1883 as being the first high school in San Bernardino County. The museum brings history to life with the use of animatronics, videos, and palpable items. These are some of the many things SBHS has to offer.

column1: I am very pleased with my child's education at Gibbons. Despite a few less-than-great teachers, my daughter is thriving. The school is small enough so that the kids get lots of personal attention but large enough to offer many AP and honors classes. Even though she's not a star athlete, my daughter has had the opportunity to participate on sports teams. The school makes a big effort to get the kids involved and to make high school fun. I have also been very impressed with the guidance department -- the counselors are very helpful and knowledgeable. Negatives? Like all schools it has some warts: school-parent communication is inconsistent, the front office could be more helpful, it's a crazy parking lot with kids slumming in their luxury cars, and a definitely 1-star lunch program. But on the whole, Gibbons is time and money well spent. love this school for my children! excellent experience! this school knows what to do! give the kids a top education, and tons of activities and fun! well done!! A+++++++++++++ I will send my grandchildren here! No problem!! Worth every penny! no regrets here.. I am a parent finishing my fourth year with CGHS. Cardinal Gibbons is a clean and safe enviroment, with nice facilities. Unfortunately it is less than perfect. The Principal, resides at a competeing St Thomas Aquanas and manages or leads both schools. This is a conflict of interest. This has allowed an aging leadership at Gibbons to live on their past reputation. Cheating is rampant. Athletics is run by apathetic leadership focused on select teams in which they have a personal interest. The totality of athletic programs are mediocre at best. I make this statement after the end of year banquet where I endured a consistant beratement by the parents of the program. Like many other schools, most months have a 4 day work week with too many frivolous days off. The plus of this school, it is small enough that most staff know the names of most of the students and are helpful in providing extra attention. The one thing I was most impressed with, was the quality of the students. For this I give credit to the parents. The kids are extremely well manered and come from a high class enviroment. Everyone at the school is very nice and available, but until there is a change in leadership, sorry. We moved from up north and were excited to send our son to CGHS. It wasn't long and we were regretting our decision. The open house was full of promises we just never saw played out. We did not see that teachers were interested in student learning as much as they were about every kid following all the ridiculous rules- notebooks arranged a certain way, no flexibility helping kids transition to high school, poor communication. I thought a private school would be preparing students for the 21st century but what we found was very out of date teaching methods. Most assignments were read the book and answer the questions. poor principal leadership. According to the Florida Certification site he is not a certified administrator, he has no experience outside of CGHS and it shows, his way to solve problems is if you don't like it at CG then find another school--and that was before ever offering to meet with us. There are lots of parents who drink the CG kool-aid because they went to school there and I understand in its day CG was a good school but now it is riding on the past success and not making changes to keep up with today. I would recommend finding another school. Parents, think twice about this school. Rarely have any national merit scholars, I have never known them to have any Silver Knight winners and only one or two nominees in the 20 years or more that I've been following it. The administration and administration cronies need to move over. The principal has been there way too long and thinks he's still in high school in the 60's, when he went there. He's never left and never moved the school forward. Considering the location and uppity student body, they should be excelling in academic and social areas. Oh, and their sports teams are, for the most part, failing too. Do your kids a favor and send them to St. Thomas or anywhere else if you want a decent education. I can honestly say that if you aren't already in this school go to another one...the teachers are not very qualified and the school is small so they don't have all the after curricular activities a high school should have. I am dissapointed. And think I could have had a better education and future should I have gone to another high school. I have enjoyed my tenure at this institution There is nothing extraordinary about Gibbons, the administration is sub par. They don’t seemed to want to be bothered by any one who may have a concern with their child. Forget co-laboring together with your guidance, admin or teacher. It wont happen. I feel we as parents and educators should work together to help our children achieve their goals. Well good luck, it wont happen here. They have virtually no STEM program. They don’t mention DE. Most likely due to the fact they haven’t taught your child enough to pass a college level course. They do have AP but they don’t push that either. It’s a very archaic system. The school needs a total overhaul. If your child needs extra help, well you wont find a teacher staying after to help, they cant leave quick enough when that last bell rings. But rest assured they will give your child a couple minutes at 7 am before school starts, so get up early. I have received numerous unprofessional emails from staff and teachers alike. It’s basically got a “don’t bother me” vibe.It is a one track ticket to Tallahassee Community College and FSU if you are a Seminole fan. I barely saw kids wearing cords at graduation which goes to show somethings not working right. I could go on and on but if you do have a choice to pay for your child to attend a private high school I would not choose Cardinal Gibbons. Horrible! I wish I would’ve never looked into the school. I regret having put my child here! I went to this school for freshman and sophomore year. The education is good no complaints. If you’re not rich you will be excluded. This school produces snobs who look down on those whose parents have less. They make you sell raffle tickets once a year if you sell enough you get to wear what you want on Friday if not you have to wear your uniform. You know who the poor kids were on Friday. If you did not sell enough tickets, they told us we would have to come to school on days off. If your rich you can play sports and make friends. My parents were poor and could not give me money. I worked after school so I could have money. All of my friends did not go to the school. Once again you know who the poor kids were. They had great field trips to colleges that I did not go on. One again you know who the poor kids were. I would here these children complain about a life that I am still saving for. In front of the school my mother’s Honda was hit by a student driving a BMW. The mother of the BMW driver yelled at my mom this is a BMW, you had to be driving pretty fast to damage my daughter’s car this bad. WHAT A SNOB. I had to walk home in the rain 3 week later because my mother had to work. The same girl who hit us drove by laughing at me. You know who the poor kids are.I went to the church St Johns by the school last week to try and have my son baptized there because that's where I was baptized, they could care less, told me to come back later, did not even ask me my name. I work construction so since I did not come in a suit they must have known I was poor. The snobbery even extends up to the church. My main concern with Cardinal Gibbons is that it doesn't provide as high a standard for the next level – college. Most students are perfectly content with getting an average SAT score and attending average colleges. I found my friends and competitor schools, such as St. Thomas, would have higher standards for themselves than my friends at Gibbons. It's a shame because I would occasionally see top students fall in the average students because they thought it was cool and would end up at average schools. Furthermore, the guidance counselors are decent at getting students into typical colleges, but are awful at helping students reach for the best. 1 star is too many. This school has a habit of denying students admission due to them having medical issues (without saying so) The principal is rude as is the admissions director. This school is nothing more than a place for middle class white people to send their kids to so they can pretend they are rich. Also to keep their kids sheltered from the diversity that the public schools have to offer. If you aren’t afraid of diversity, choose a public school. Academics are leaps and bounds above what Gibbons has to offer. I can not tell you how much I hate this school. Teachers are mediocre, at best. Several are highly incompetent. They're either way too young or don't know what they're doing. The staff is rude and threatening. The principal with his chin strap facial hair looks around 30. The people in the front office are the worst. Rude is an understatement. They make threats and are snotty. Nothing will change though. Time to move out of the area. This whole place is a great disappointment. Cardinal Gibbons has been a great school for my son. I am very pleased with the quality and moral standards of the staff. There are many teachers who really strive to be the best they can and they care if students are not doing their best effort. the buildings re all in excellent condition and most classrooms have advanced technological aids. I highly recommend this school to any parent or student who wishes to receive a well rounded catholic education with principles and good moral requirements

I give this school a 5 star rating. I think the low test scores at this school are a reflection of the high percentage of students who are English langauge learners. The ESOL program and department, which is very large, is amazing and consists of a team of very hardworking, dedicated professional teachers who give their all every day to help almost 500 English language learners to succeed in school. The other students in the school are also given a variety of activities and programs to help them get a great start in life. Nothwood High School is a great school! Northwood has been an amazing school for my son. His experience in the GTLD program has made him love school and helped him be an extremely successful student. The staff has been wonderful and great at communication. I haven't encountered anything that matches the negative picture these statistic paint. I think if someone is considering the school they should go and visit, learn about what it is available, and meet the amazing staff. Judging by these numbers alone is a skewed picture and does a disservice to the school and staff and the wonderful job they are doing. Northwood is an excellent school, despite some people's ideas of it. The teachers and students are very welcoming; I remember my first day of school as a new student I felt accepted. The classes are challenging, but you are able to stay on top of your schoolwork if you pay attention and turn in your work on time. One thing to note is the difference between AP and honors classes vs. standard classes, as the difference is somewhat significant. If you want to challenge yourself, taking harder classes will be a good opportunity for you, and if you take standard classes you may not be challenged. I know that another thing to be aware of is the misconception that AP (and honors) classes are not diverse... However, with experience, I can oppose that and say that they are diverse. You should want to consider joining whichever classes you think you will be most comfortable in regardless of what anyone says about Northwood's equity... This website displays a misconception that has been given to this school about its diversity. (That there are mostly Latino students who take standard classes while most of the students who participate in AP classes are white... not true). They also offer multiple programs like sports and activities, and the teachers and staff there are especially involved with helping the students with their interests.

There are a few teachers that don't teacher or choses to give there students class work and not even go over the material. I feel like there's only 2 teachers that are actually good teachers that actually teach. The school lunch is especially disappointing. I'm literally scared to even eat now because I have no idea how old the food I am eating is. I've been attending Cascade for 13 years and every year it gets worse. I wouldn't send my children to Cascade if it was the last school on Earth. I have gone to Cascade for 13 years now and the school has not changed one bit. The building is very old and is falling apart. We are very overcrowded. It is hard to walk in the halls to get to class on time. There are about 14 total classes outside in portables. There is no room here, and not one thing has been done to fix it. Also, the teachers are not good at teaching. I feel like I learn nothing. They never seem like they want to help us which makes you not even want to learn. column3: This is a great school with great teachers. Your child will get a solid education if he really wants it. Try hard enough and you will succeed. Every school has its problems but there are none significant enough to mention. 92% of the students graduate and many go one to 4 year colleges. My child graduated 4th in her class and went on to a university that was almost impossible to get into from out of state. This school caters to the high performers - both academic and athletic. If your kid is already in the top 10% of his or her peers, this school will focus lots of effort and resources to maximize your kids success. The remaining 90% of the student body are neglected in every way. An awful cadre of teachers serves the majority of the student body, extracuricular sponsors ignore the students not competitive for college scholarship, ect. The vast majority of the student body would progress farther if the government simply issued out the text books, sent the kids home, and bulldozed the school. Pro: high achieving children are well supported, decent course offerings, decent extracurricular variety. Small size seems to make inclusion easier for military kids. Large population of high achieving kids due to high achieving parents stationed at/employed by West Point. Con: as in most high schools, foul language, inappropriate attire during the school day and lewd behavior at dances. I think parent chaperones would solve some of this at dances.(not allowed) Dress code is randomly enforced. Uniforms might be helpful. (Also minimizes difference between 'haves' and 'have nots') O'Neill doesn't excessively build up nor tear down. Experiences your child get's LITERALLY results from what they have inside, or you ALL make of it; little comes from the school itself. If you're an introvert, or struggle with "school," life will be a challenge. Force them to help you! School starts early; buses arrive by 630. It's very clique-like because of what they offer and focus on. If you're not a sportsaholic, academic junkie or "attractive-college-transcript focused," little is left. EVERYTHING is centered around academics and sports!!! Arts are offered as courses but there aren't activities after school or clubs that support that type of interest. This set up forces kids into groups, or cliques, rather than them choosing their passion. Well-roundedness is verbally encouraged but not fostered by activities. The counselors are responsive to me when I call for help and strive for your child to look attractive to colleges. In general, the school has a decent atmosphere. What I would like to see is more clubs offered for the artsy-fartsy or engineer-minded kid. Generally, the area is very competitive. Students follow suit. There isn't an much of an outlet from that mindset. This school caters to their own kind, upscale or high income families. I don't understand how, if this area has median households. O'Neill High School offers more academic and extracurricular programs than any school it's size in the region. This is in part to its proximity to West Point and location in the Hudson Valley. The exceptional programs are supported by a guidance team that provides support to those that need it. The facilities (cafeteria, gym, track, and more) also provide a great high school experience. I had three students at JIO. When one of my children was having difficulties with a teacher, I reached out to the principal, who couldn't even be bothered to respond to me after repeated requests. Thumbs down for leadership. JIO has the highest average SAT scores in Orange County. The curriculum is excellent with extensive AP course opportunities. The extracurricular offerings are expansive and given the relatively small size every student has the ability to participate in many activities. Many students attend top tier universities. Our child attended JIO and attended an Ivy League university. This is an excellent school for it's size. It caters to 3 different communities who all blend seamlessly. I had 3 children attend and graduate from JIO. All were leader's in their class, accepted to multiple colleges, and all graduated college with jobs lined up. Every school has it's issues but most of the bad reviews are from disgruntled parents who don't hold their child accountable and don't encourage their child to do well. I would wholeheartedly recommend JIO.

column3: I'm both a Bob Jones teacher and a parent of two current students and a BJHS graduate. This is, hands down, the absolute best school I've ever seen. The students are well behaved and conscientious, the academics are top notch, and the teachers truly care about student well being and the quality of instruction that they bring to the table. We ask a lot of our students and they deliver. Bob Jones High School is just great. I have a brother who got a half-time scholarship from track just after one year and he is now a senior in a college in KY. I was at Bob Jones for my freshman year then transferred to another school in Harvest (will not state) and Bob Jones had twice the amount of AP and advanced classes then the other school. I had transferred late at the school in Harvest and the teachers did not help at all when I asked for help. I did unexceptionally horrible there. So I think I had made the best choice of my teen years and went back to Bob Jones. I'm not just saying this because it seems like everyone does and as if I wanna quack like a duck too but I HIGHLY recommend this school to ANYONE! My high school was Bob Jones High School, and I absolutely loved it! The principal is an amazing guy, you would never hear a negative word about him. I am proud to be a Bob Jones Patriot! The teachers are very good and experienced. My only comment is based on some students' input about the new principal...there seemed to have a perception of lack of authenticity and cheesiness on the methods used or applied this school year that is not on par with the level of intelligence of the students. These are high performing kids who were a perfect fit with the previous principal. If the previous ways work, pls don't fix it. No more insulting elementary- level tricks. Overall, teachers and counselors are superb. Great thank you to these educators. To the new principal, pls talk to these kids like high performing intelligent conscientious students who really just want to excel and appreciate the high standards. Bob Jones is one of a kind! I went to this school all four years, and it was the best four years of my life. The teachers go above and beyond for their students along with all faculty members. The student body is very welcoming and makes sure everyone has a voice! Sports are excellent all around the board. Most if not all of my former teachers not only taught the required curriculum, but went above the standards and taught us college readiness and life skills to prepare us for the future. Madison City School Systems is where you want your kids to grow up in! Awesome school!! Both my kids graduated from Bob Jones and I couldn't have been happier with their experience. This school is great - if you’re of a certain demographic and social class. If you aren’t, you might as well be homeschooled. Aside from the obvious - that this is the kind of school that cares MORE about sports - Bob Jones only really caters to prospective engineering students. Much like the surrounding community, the school HEAVILY lacks diversity in teachers, staff and students; and speaking of the students, how many times can I mention the words “stuck up, snobby and snooty”? Cliques run deep in their halls and it’s saddening. Blindly put, if you don’t look a certain way, you’re arrogantly ignored during your time there. And something else that’s arrogantly ignored? Accuracies in history. Everything Bob Jones has taught me in history class was extremely one-sided, watered down and ignorantly wrong. THIS SCHOOL PUMPS WRONG AND HURTFUL HISTORY ALLUSIONS UNTIL THEIR STUDENTS. I could go on and on.... bottom line, this school is awful, inside and out.

column3: The building is physically falling down, but the parents and community are currently fighting for a new building. The teachers vary from highly superior to way below average. The students can find anything they want at SPHS. If they are academically driven the school is AP course driven, if they are looking for sex, drugs and rock n roll that unfortunately is available in abundance also. Students who excel in sports can try out for football, lax, track, swimming, field hockey and more . The drama department offers multiple opportunities, with one act plays, improv comedy and singing and dancing in the Rock n Roll revival show. Students who excel in band are encouraged to join, if you simply enjoy band; don't bother as you will be pushed to always be the best. Second is NOT acceptable. This is a highly competitive school and if your child is not in the top 25% or the bottom 10%, expect a bumpy ride. There is a work hard/play hard mentality. Opportunities are available for parents to get involved, both in the school and outside of the school. Severna Park High has been a wonderful school for all 3 of my children. Our principle shows a lot of respect to the children, and in turn I see the respect that they show him. If you want a great public school move to Bethesda. This schools test scores based on the demographics are disappointing. Construction on the new school will start this summer, with anticipated completion in 2017. the 53 year old building has seen better days, and yet the students excel. Whether you are an adult or a student, if you are one who enjoys climbing the social ladder by meekly following King and Queen Bees, you will probably like Severna Park. If you march to the beat of a your own drum and think independently, you will probably be unhappy here. And be forewarned, the players can be viciously competitive. The person who wrote something about Bethesda schools is obviously an angry student or parent from Bethesda's Walt Whitman High School. I used to go to Walt Whitman High School, and I wrote a review telling the truth about how horrible it is, and recommended this school (which is where i go to school now, my parents go to Severna Park). Severna Park is NOT a snobby school. Most of the rich kids in Severna Park go to private schools, so enough with calling us snobby. We are just a public school. Severna Park is a great school, and has a very friendly staff and student body. I felt so welcomed here. Coming from a real snobby high school, I think I can assure you Severna Park is just fine and not snobby at all. Its the perfect school, and I'm GLAD I go here instead of Walt Whitman. And at Severna Park, we don't just pass our students to make the numbers look good like Whitman does, we actually work hard to get those numbers. This is a good school for a student interested in academics. The test score results are remarkable. Before sending your child to this school, you may want to google aahealth consumption survey regarding drug, drinking, and smoking. Don't judge this book by its cover. There are two ways to assess SPHS. If your goal is to indoctrinate your children into the world of high stress, high academic achievement, and progressive political thinking models – SPHS is for you. If your goal is to raise independent thinkers who have high ethical and morals standards – SPHS is not for you. Teachers will tell your students that any career that equals a high salary is admirable but any career that involves altruism or serving others with a median salary is “stupid”. The basic philosophy is to get superior grades, go to a top college, then earn a lot of money to buy a big house, car, and boat because that equals happiness in life. This is really indicative of the entire culture of Severna Park, the most common question you will be asked is “What is your Job/Title” and “Where did you go to school” then a “Parky” will decided whether you meet their “Status Meter” and they wish to converse with you or not. I’ve actually been “shunned” by a mother at a social engagement because I didn’t live in a particular subdivision. If you have lived anywhere else outside of Maryland, Severna Park will come off as snobbish, rich, and pretentious but residence/students see this as the norm and will tell you “we are not snobbish.” Most students have an entitlement mentality (Mommy and Daddy buy we anything I want) versus a strong work ethic. Students are some of the most self-centered, conceited youth we’ve ever encountered yet again, they don’t see this in themselves because this is the cultural norm. Overall, this is an outstanding school for academics, sports, and preparing your kids for college but also understand the other understanding principals and morals your kids will be inculcated into. This was a wonderful school! The teachers expected greatness and most of us provided that. I will say that only mature teens that can self-monitor should go to public schools. If your children strive for excellence, have confidence, and they respect teachers (know how to please different types of authority figures)- they will succeed here. SPHS is not made for adolescents that often compare themselves to others, question themselves, or lack drive. Sadly, SPHS has a high rate of self-injury (fatal and non-fatal). It is a complicated problem and I think one major aspect is that some teens do not know how to dismiss the negative appraisal of their peers. I loved this school and it prepared me to graduate in four years from UMCP. Only 40% of people graduate from a four year university in four years, so that says a lot of SPHS preparation. Please send your child to St. Mary's, Severn, or Spalding if they need their hand held during high school as you must be a resilient person to attend public school. I will miss the old school but the new one looks amazing! Signed, Class Clown I went to this school as well as my children. As with any public school it serves the public. All different levels. No matter what level there is support and help if you seek it. there are o many tools available to help and challenge a student no matter what their goals are. It is available but you need to use it. Outstanding high school w great teachers and awesome curriculum. Definitely prepares students for college and success beyond! My child is a freshman and is loving it. The teachers are great, and the curriculum provides so many options. I moved to this area for the schools and I've never regretted our choice. SPHS has many pros - a great Engineering Program and Business Program, and fantastic Physics, Math, Engineering, English, Government departments. The only weak links that we have experienced is the Chemistry Dept and the over-the-top focus on athletics. The data contained here is incorrect with reference to test scores and AP participation. SPHS switched to PARCC testing three years ago and the scores represented are for the bottom 25% of students. PARCC resulted from the No Child Left Behind initiative to ensure that educational standards for low achieving students are being met. In the last year, 15 participating states have dropped the test because the scores are not representative of the entire student body. Also the AP participation at Severna Park is 70% for both math and science. I have seen with my own eyes the participation sheet that gets sent along to the university your child is applying to. Prospective parents beware that you are not seeing accurate information on this website. 10 out of 10...the property is incredible!!! This school has a lot of good teachers and students , but the administration here is just horrible. If you mess up once or do these slightest thing wrong, you will be harrassed by the principals and school police officer. Constantly following you around and questioning you. And if you don’t have s snobby attitude, you won’t fit in. There’s also still a significantly large “wrong crowd” here that starts fights , does and sells drugs, steal, and doesn’t care about academics in the slightest. You have been warned. I am a student at this school and when I got bullied they told me I was provoking the bully I have a son that is about to graduate from SPHS. I am confident my younger children will receive the same quality education. I have mixed feelings about SP I have one child that graduated from SP and one who tested out and went directly to college at 16 mostly because at police officer told me at my dining room table in front of my child that it was not safe for him to walk to school. Luckily we had just moved from Fairfax and he was about a year maybe two ahead academically from his classmates and had no problem testing out of high school. My daughter stayed. We did have at one time an incident where another SP student broke into our house and drew swastikas' on her bed room walls. It terrified her. That thankfully was contained. I have to say I was not impressed with the adminstration of SP though the teaching staff is stellar. Both my children overcame their experiences at SPHS and we attend SP events. The new HS is ugly to be sure an example of someone's bad judgement in architecture that we will have with us for years to come. As a parent I made the best decision at the time for my kids I would opt for a smaller class size option with a focus on community and kindness and not on a self entitlement. I have gone myself and had my kids in private and public schools and this one is meh as best and for some kids soul dangerous. If your child is self aware and independent you may be safe enough I would not want a vulnerable child to go here. Growing up in Western Howard County and attending one of the state’s best high schools, I understand the importance of a high-quality education. Thus, I bought into the hype of the Severna Park schools. After having two children go through this school, I have to agree with the other reviewer that SPHS’ reputation is far overstated relative to the actual quality of the school. It is a good school that prepares students for the rigors of college, and the school has top-notch teachers, but it is not significantly different from many other AACo schools. In my experience, the “Severna Park schools” hype stems from community members and local real estate agents who feel that the school is “better” because it is in a “wealthy” area. These are largely folks living in strictly middle-class housing with snob attitudes greater than what you’ll encounter in some of the state’s most exclusive enclaves within Bethesda/Potomac and Howard County. I feel sorry for the people who believe they are “rich” and have clearly never left Severna Park to see true wealth before. They are not as different from their neighboring towns as they’d like to believe. The principal of SPHS has extremely poor leadership. Whenever a major incident occurs at the school involving a fight, bullying, or racism, he always tosses the issue under a rug or only briefly addresses it. The issues continue to linger because the leaders at this school are far more concerned about protecting SPHS’ reputation than they are about caring for ALL students. If I could do it over, I would have bought in the Crofton/Gambrills area instead or avoid AACo altogether and move back to HoCo. There are so many parents who claim to be concerned about mental health, but they do little when their children are the ones being the bullies at school, and the culture in this school and community is completely abysmal for ethnic minorities. Majority of the members in the community around this school love the homogeneity and fight to keep it that way, and lots of people here view diverse areas and schools as being “inferior.” Long story short, this school is very good, but the school leaders don’t demonstrate leadership, there is a lot of close-mindedness among parents, and there’s plenty of other good and even better schools that you can send your kids to that won’t inflict trauma in your children if they’re non-white. I moved to Severna Park from Hanover (Meade High feeder) for the schools, and my youngest just graduated from Severna Park High this year. My oldest did 9th and 10th at Meade High School and 11th and 12th grade at Severna Park High School. Really, the biggest difference between Meade and Severna Park were the buildings and the demographics. I did not feel that my children’s teachers at their Severna Park schools were better than their teachers at their Meade schools, I did not feel that the curriculum at SP schools was any different than the curriculum at Meade schools, and my children did great at schools in both feeder systems. People I’ve talked to who moved to SP from other “bad” schools often say the same thing. I miss my larger, newer, and beautiful home in Hanover that I traded for my older and smaller home in Severna Park. I miss the diversity we had in Hanover as well. Severna Park is a nice area with nice schools, but don’t feel like you HAVE to move to Severna Park “for the schools,” because I can 100% promise you that your child will receive the same exact education at any AACPS school and it’s all about how you parent your children. The school ranks high in student achievement and college preparedness. Students on average have fewer discipline problems and are more driven to achieve academic success. My children have formed many lasting friendships. The sports programs are competitive and well managed. The band/arts/drama programs are outstanding. As a person of color I feel accepted at this school. There isn't much diversity but the academics and teachers are great. I feel like I am getting a proper education. I am very impressed with this school so far and recommend it.

column3: I am a current SHS student. The academics here are fairly good, however, the math department needs a complete makeover. Students care more about making grades, instead of actually learning, due to the fact that teachers don't spend enough time teaching the subject and give excessive amounts of homework and tests. Most other subjects are well. The world language department is great along with English and History. The science teachers are great, however, make sure your student is responsible when it comes to homework for those classes. The arts program at Sanger High is a little small, however, it is growing. The drama department has received a lot of new members lately, and with the help of the new community theater program, it is expected to grow even more. There are many visual art classes at SHS. For the 2015-2016 school year, they are adding a dance PE class which is also expected to help build the art program. For athletics, Sanger high has a lot of spirit that carries all the way down to the middle school. Sanger is a football town, so basically the whole town shows up to Friday night football games (including away games). The band department is huge, and I guarantee you will be impressed with them. The cheer program is becoming more of a presence as well. They won their division in CIF for the 2014-2015 season (it was their first year competing). Water polo, Volley Ball, and Track are all large and great sports teams as well. For ASB, the program has a lot of members, and they do a lot of great things for the school, however, it could use a bit of a makeover as well. They need to broaden their ideas more and be less demanding and power hungry. Watch out watch out watch out! This school has reopened during Covid but is not following guidelines! Behind closed doors staff is not consistently wearing masks, people are catching Covid.Be careful about sending your kids back!

column1: Poorly managed. Administration and Faculty divided. Parental input not encouraged. New (2010) Administration openly shows arrogance toward previous Principals and teachers by downgrading and claiming all successes as their own. Three Administrations in four years, and this one is the worst. New principal is tough on the kids. That is what I want. Real life is tough. Fully support the administration in their effort to move forward to another level of education This is a violent school. Lock downs are the norm. My daughters grades have plummeted drastically since she has been here. There are too few school choices in the area. This makes it very difficult to change schools especially now that her grades have suffered. I WOULD NOT recommend this school if you can avoid it. This is one of the poorest ran schools in Oklahoma City. The teachers seem to be intimidated by the students, and refuse to try to find out the true nature of problems with them. Students are constantly roaming the halls and staff is not to be found until there is an altercation. Where are the preventative measures to stop matters before they occur? When you check back you find nothing has been done about the problem. The only time the staff seems to take action is when there is a fight of some kind. As I stated before, there are no preventative measures just reaction to problems. I view this school as a housing facility, not a place fit for learning. This linear structure set by whomever will never work. When you are not allowed to think and use reason to fix matters, and press this nature upon the students then they are destined to fail in the real world. The community is great The school year has just started and we are looking forward to a great year at Wesson! column1: Chelsea high school is very good and has improved drastically in the past two years. It others courses that students can excel in and has teachers that are fun, cool, good, and teach. Chelsea offers a brilliant band program with some all state musicians, state wide recognized artists, brilliant theatre program, and the football team does fairly well for now being in the region with Spain park and oak mountain. Expect highly of this school. Lots of new teachers, and good principal My kids attended Chelsea Elementary, Mt. Laurel Elementary, Chelsea Intermediate, Chelsea Middle and are currently in Chelsea High School. These are all great schools. I am so proud of our schools in the Chelsea area and the dedication of the teachers. I did not dedicate time, but did donate money because I knew how it would be spent! Chelsea High students are eligible for the School of Technology and offers the only Cisco Networking program in the entire State of Alabama. Thank you for educating our kids with the low tax base we pay in Chelsea, AL! Some teachers are nice and seem to care but the rest have no respect for the students and make the time at school miserable. Zero stars if possible and I don't think parents should comment on these school because they don't go to school there and they only see the fake smiles. They don't really know anything about this school. the test scores look good, but the school isnt so good. the teahcers are rude and dont communicate and barely can really help you. they just go with the flow of what the governemnt says. theres better educ. out there. the students are disrespectful to everyone including teachers. and the hallways are full of transgression. its terrible. plus, the discipline has gone down hill so that may be why its gotten bad.the lack of courses makes it hard to be challenged and to go after more because i dont feel challenged at all. the sports is all about football and maybe guys basketball so sorry girls and baseball and soccer. its so clickish and ten times worse than the normal cuz ive been to two schools in the last 4 years and chelsea has been the worst. ive never been so ready to move again. This is our first year attending Shelby County schools and the experience has been good. The teachers communicate well via edmodo and email. The transition from one school system to Shelby County was a little tough at first but with the help of the Counselors, Teachers and Coaches my child adjusted very well. Inflated test scores only due to location and sample of the populace, covers up what is really a failing school, at least, one that is failing its students. Alternatively draconian in policy, conservative in allowances, sparse in electives. Does little to prepare students for the rigors of college, operates more as teenage daycare than any sort of enrichment. I am a student at Chelsea and I think this school is just average. Out of my 8 teachers I only like 2 of them. I am in mostly honors and ap classes and the teachers don't know how to teach. Whenever someone asks my ap history teacher a question, she doesn't know the answer and has to look it up. One of my other teachers is never there and showed up late on the day of our semester exams without even making the test. Even after this the teacher wasn't fired. Even when he is here he "doesn't feels like doing anything" so we just sit there. The pe coaches just sit on their phones, and make us walk around the gym everyday. The teachers also pick favorites and the same students get the same 5 awards every year. Bullying isn't really a big issue, but some of the upperclassmen that I have classes with make crude and inappropriate comments about teachers and other students. There are definitely cliques and pretty much half the school is on drugs. Football is the most popular sport and unless you're a cheerleader, no one pays attention to girls sports. They also don't have enough room, half of the classes are in trailers. This is inconvenient and not safe because the doors lock but you can just yank them open. Overall, this school doesn't do a good job encouraging students to learn or challenge themselves, and lacks the appropriate funding. Excellent school with teachers who truly care about education as well as shaping the young men and women who attend. They take an interest in who they are inside and outside of the classroom. I am astounded when I go to piano recitals, sporting events, and Scout awards nights and see teachers there, on their off days, supporting these kids. I hear about the teachers who open their classrooms to students before and after school and during their free periods. What a great example of being not just a teacher but a mentor!Great choice of AP classes, out of the ordinary electives, many clubs, and sports available. There truly is something for every interest. Dual enrollment is also offered with the local community college. Technical school is an encouraged choice as well.COVID rules have been instituted as needed. They did a GREAT job of limiting COVID exposure even at the height of the spread while still allowing families to choose between in person or remote schooling.I've been so impressed with nearly everything at Chelsea. So many more opportunities than other schools I hear about through other parents. A free computer for every kid is unheard of elsewhere. Learning trips to DC, Florida, Spain, etc, while not attainable for all financially, are available. Additional fundraising for these never being offered would be my only complaint. It would be great if all the students who want to go and are willing to work hard could earn at least some of the funds through fundraising assisted by the school/county/faculty. With that said, a scholars bowl group from Chelsea won their local and state competition and were headed to the national competition. They were allowed to send letters requesting financial support from community members. One of the faculty sponsored the kids to travel to Kentucky for a week to compete. The school is in a great community that supports them! My son says the school does not have a bad problem with cliques or bullying. I haven't heard of any issues with those at least as long as he has been at t ht e school.

column3: I think that Eagan is a very mediocre school with bad standards. Their productions are ok, and after school activities are mediocre as well. The offer very less honors classes, making it hard for a student to keep an honors ranking, when compared with students taking 5-6 honors classes every year. In my opinion, between Eagan, Apple Valley, Rosemount, and Eastview, any other school would be better... Eagan High School is a high school with both stellar students and underachievers. Therefore, it is my belief that it is hard to determine the school as either a great school or otherwise. However, I will confidently state that the school was very draining when it came to the way that the curriculum was structured (the short lunch period doesn't help either.) It is possible to become very successful after attending Eagan High, but I found that success to be at the cost of constant sleepless nights and amounting stress. The school wants it's students to do as much as possible to succeed, and, consequently, I noticed my peers either seemed to give up or overwork themselves. In retrospect, I was never truely happy while attending; it just wasnt right for me. Eagan High School has been led by the same administration since it opened 20+ years ago. Time for a new perspective and fresh attitudes. If you're not a superstar athlete, academic, or actor, you're out of luck. The school does not know what to do with average kids. Lots of needless pressure with teachers who don't even recognize that your child is in their class! Too big, too much stress, with outdated ideas about how to manage it all!!! Look elsewhere!!! If you are thinking of sending your child there as "the new kid" please don't. This school is designed for either very academically high students or for star athletes. Not meant for the average joe. The students that attend this school are very cliquey. They do not want anything to do with outsiders. You will have to try very hard to make friends in this school. The principal is nice yet he makes students feel less of themselves, which is not very motivational. The school is far too big and you can easily get lost, with no one to help you. There are many extracurricular opportunities for students. The workload plus after school activities can get very stressful. If you go here prepare to have a lot of work on your hands. Eagan High School is rated fairly high according the new test scores but it is just a factory with way too many students plus includes the Middle School in the same facility. If you can afford it send your child to a private school with fewer students. If you do send your child to EHS make sure you let the teachers know you care about your child and meet with them as much as possible. Home Schooling kids score better in MN and you can have your child "do" High School via computer with certified teachers free too without sending them off to this giant brick box which just is a processing plant for thousands. Frankly, they just don't care-too many kids being pumped through.(Except for the surface politeness BS for the parents.) I'm a former student at EHS and about to graduate from the U. I've grown up, been able to comprehend my high school experience and compare it to other places I've lived. I feel like I got an above average education. EHS caters to those who really do well in school. After school programs are solid. There is plenty support for both sports and music. Here s the problem. It's an EXTREMELY hostile environment for students of color. Not so much from the teachers (although there are teachers who seem to keep an eye out for certain students) but the school itself is very segregated. The black kids hang out with the black kids, Hmong with Hmong, etc. Obviously that is not the case for all but students aren't very receptive for those who stray from those lines, probably because there s little diversity in the school to begin with so minorities are already the outsiders. I'm a mixed student of color so I noticed it a lot more than others since I was treated like an outsider. There seemed to be negative connotations associated with the different racial groups. Those feeling transcended across the student body and racial slurs were used quite frequently. As a parent of two kids that are attending Eagan High School, one of which is a stellar student, the other and average student, I will report that Eagan has been a very good high school for both of them. Eagan offers a wide-array of classes, including a lot of AP and honors and does well to offer classes for kids that are not high academic achievers. There are a lot of opportunities with sports and other extra-curricular activities. The teachers that I have met, and that numbers in the dozens are very solid. Every year Eagan gets ranked in the top 3 public high schools in Minnesota and they deserve it. Eagan faculty work hard to allow the kids to achieve to the best of their abilities. I have 2 kids in this school now and we've been impressed at the options open to them if they are willing to engage. There is a fit for everyone, but you might have to reach out and find it. The band program is amazing and yet not all-encompassing that you can't do other extracurriculars too. There are lots of sport options and if you're not into sports, there are literally hundreds of clubs that you could find a niche. The majority of teachers have been excellent. The Athletic Director and Band director are top notch and go above and beyond. You would be hard-pressed to find better anywhere. This school puts on a good “show.” The teachers largely don’t care and the princpal is not helpful. If you reach out to try and figure out how to help your child especially if they have a learning disability and a 504 Plan, they will never put anything in writing and talk down to parents. Subpar education at best. We moved here from out of state and most of tue science and civics curriculum my child learned in middle school. I expected more from such a “highly ranked school.” My child will not be going back next school year. I kind of hate the people here.PS. Thanks for the depression lmao

column1: Dr.Newcome and Dr.Haller are unfair and won't answer any questions asked. So please watch yourself around them! They really upset my son and that makes me angry! Research test result scores. Research test result scores. Research test result scores. Research test result scores. Enough said! I have never truly considered dropping out until I started going to this school. The only kids who get to go on field trips are the kids in the agriculture department. The art kids were supposed to go to New York for a day but our trip, once again, was given to the agriculture kids. We havent had a field trip in a long time, yet the agriculture department goes on a trip practically every month. Living in the district for 30+ years and raising 3 kids attending there I have had my own experiences some good some bad. I rate it low due to my experiences with faculty, administration and board members. It is a school in a farming community that spends money like the community (home owners) have it to give. It tries to keep up with the other Chester County districts which WERE farming and now all commercialized and HAVE the deep pockets to pick for funding. This district is worse due to it's low scores, all are below the state average!! Our property tax has increased 400% in less than 15 years due to building schools and buying property because they hired an outside firm to "GUESS" how many students would be coming into the area due to development. Guess what, nobody came. According to many in the area that attended school there in the 80's the amount of students has not increased nearly to what was estimated. One of the worst districts my children attended. We have been in three Love this school! Teachers care, Kids feel successful every day, gourmet chef prepares the menu for healthy and tasty food.

column3: I was a student teacher at Fairborn High School this past year and I have also subbed there and at the elementary schools. I enjoyed my time at Fairborn High School very much. The teacher I worked with was great and the rest of the teaching staff that I encountered were very friendly and helpful. I loved the principals and the office staff. Admittedly, I was nervous about teaching there because of past reviews from a few years back, but I couldn't have been placed in a better district. From my point of view the teachers seem to really care about the students. I didn't notice any excessive behavior or discipline issues beyond typical things like being tardy. The principals were very supportive. Anytime I spoke to them or asked for assistance they were more than willing to oblige. My son transferred to the district after the leaving Beavercreek, which clearly has issues with embracing diversity. The school has a strong community pride. Many of the families are military and move in and out of the district, which accounts for the fluctuation in enrollment and funding. I am a teacher in another district and I am very involved with my children's education. I have no complaints about the education my son receives. Currently, the school is rated an Excellent STEM public school by the Ohio Department of Education. Three generations of my family have graduated or are now attending Fairborn schools. Every graduate went on to receive advanced education and degrees. My grandchild is autistic and the special needs program in the district is fantastic. I can't say enough about it. I have had two daughters go through their entire school experience in Fairborn. There were a handfuls of mishaps but I have found out quickly that there are AMAZING people in this district. The teachers we have encountered have been very supportive. The support staff has been great. Our youngest will graduate this year and I'm thankful for the experiences both of my girls have had. The new Superintendent seems to be willing to do whatever it takes to make this district stronger than ever and as a Fairborn resident I'm excited to watch our schools flourish. GO HAWKS! The teachers are not concerned with the struggling students, they are seemingly focused entirely on putting blame on anyone but themselves. Sadly the administration apparently supports this behavior as nothing is done to correct the issues. Overall, my experience at Fairborn High School and in the years since is nothing but stellar. The teachers still contact me to check in and see how I am doing, and they are continuously investing in new things! I just saw that the high school is now offering a sign language course in addition to reading interventions and more. The theater program has been revitalized and things seem to be really looking up here! not too great. services for students hard to access. ranked low nationally and within the state. with a larger number of students some get overlooked. My son went to this school and it was great. The teachers were very helpful and his grades increased. He is now in college with a 4.0 gpa.

column1: I graduated from Central about 10 years. Central did a great job preparing me for both undergrad and professional schools. While Central may not have as many course options as some of the large public schools, I didn't miss a beat in college and had a good chunk of college credit through AP classes. There is also something to say about knowing all your classmates rather than never knowing some people you go to school with. I still talk to my central friends on a regular basis even though we are all living in different cities across the country. I would send my kids there in a second, no matter which school district I live in.

column3: Academically, this school offers much to Austin students. For those who want a challenging environment to prepare for college, this is a good school. However, administration is significantly lacking. Administration starting with the principal are very beauracratic, poor listners and take the path that is easiest for them, not the students. I have first hand knowledge of the principal lying - manipulating situations to suite her needs often for the sake of expediancy. The teachers are great - just don't hope you need anything from the adminstration.. A GREAT school. I don't agree. Student lunches that are at 12:16 or 1:54 (or both, alternating days), double blocking football, band, and dance. The principal caters to the booster clubs, so the money continues to flow. (Principal's husband is HR director at AISD, so the teachers really have to be careful) My sons' educational experiences vary. Pre-AP/ AP classes are good; regular classes, fair. This school caters to the top 10% and the lower 10% and the 80% in the middle, its a coin toss. Some do well, others get lost. Not too sure of the role of the vice principals; know the one assigned to 504 actually said that the school is not responsible for " getting the best out of the students". (We transferred that son to a private school, where he excelled). The counseling staff is improving. We have another son starting here in the Fall and we'll see if his needs are met; otherwise we'll find the "best fit" for him. I'd love to see an administration change during our time at the school. I have two kids at Anderson. Both are in pre-AP, AP or IB classes. For them I think the academics are good. I feel they will be prepared for college. (I've heard that the regular academic classes are disappointing.) There are certainly many outstanding teachers but also some that have been sub-par. As a whole pretty good. For the brighter kids there is a lot of pressure to excel. It's a big school but I think there is a place for everyone. You need to seek out social opportunities through the various clubs and activities. Lots of people have commented that the school has cliques. All schools do. If you have your heart set on fitting in with the Belles or being the star football player you will probably be unhappy at Anderson. If you are just looking for a nice social group to fit in, not necessarily the most popular, you can find it here. I know many kids who came to Anderson from private schools and are thriving. It's what you make of it. Lots of opportunity for parents and kids to get involved and volunteer. A really nice community of parent volunteers. Considering that this is supposed to be one of the best schools in AISD, it indeed does have great teachers, and a very laid back environment compared to other more suburban schools. There are plenty of clubs to join, however if your child wants to be involved in athletics, the programs are generally weak. The biggest problem has to do with the administration, and how social life can be towards your student. It is very hard to make friends at this school, and most kids as well as parents have an oddly stuck up demeanor. If you are looking for a good high school, I would suggest you pass on this one. There are many excellent choices such as Westwood or even McNeil which have good academics as well as a nicer facility, which to some matters. To most students, this school has a sink or swim policy; your student will either thrive, or hate it. Personally I suggest that you avoid this school, and either send your kids to private school, or move to a better school district such as Leander ISD or Round Rock ISD. As a professional collaborating with faculty and staff at Anderson High School, I am repeatedly shocked by the level of disorganization and poor building security. Meetings are poorly planned, staff are unprepared, and follow through is lacking in the special education/504 areas and with discipline issues. Students are free to roam the building and grounds during classes and visitors can freely walk through the halls without identifying themselves or checking in. Staff have difficulty locating students when needed. I feel it is an unsafe and disorganized environment. Test scores are only one aspect of a school's success. Real mixed bag of ratings here. Unfortunately most people that post things are those with an axe to grind. Anderson is one of the best schools in town. Are there better? For some kids, absolutely. For some parents, absolutely. It's as diverse as the neighborhoods that feed it, like any other school. The teachers, like parents, are people with strengths and weaknesses, good days and bad days and personality conflicts. They're not going to like everyone and not everyone is going to like you or your kid. Welcome to the real world. But there is real dedication all over the campus in the staff, the kids, the teachers and the parents and that's part of what makes Anderson a great place. It is what you as a student and a parent make of it. I'd also put it up against any verticals in town - it's hands down part of the best. People buy into the neighborhoods that feed Anderson and Murchison for very legitimate reasons. I have a freshman and this year has been horrendous. My student has gotten involved with drugs, has been skipping class on a daily basis, has been bullied, and tells me that a grand majority of students do drugs. The sad part is that I had been in communication with the counselor for months and had described his behavior, falling grades, excessive tiredness, lack of motivation, and in no moment he suggested that these symptoms may be associated with drug use. I had no idea that drug use on campus is so high. Apparently the school has services for children at risk, however these services were never offered to us. I am looking at alternatives for my student for next school year. If I had to do it all over again, I wouldn't ever picked this school. As a parent, do your research with the 70% of children that get left behind here. It would serve you best to speak/find those in the bottom 10% so that you see what suffering they have and will continue to go through. Coming to this school from one of the top schools in Dallas I thought I would be fine, because my research said that this was a top performing school in Austin. Little did I know that the school doesn't assign homework, which is fine (except in math), yet kids always complained. The school rarely assigned reading assignments, yet kids always complained. The workload was less than what I had in sixth grade and I was being taught basic grammar and vocab in an AP class. I was underwhelmed with the education and ended up leaving my sophomore year. We’ve had a great experience at Anderson. It is a big school with lots of opportunities. It’s a great mix of kids and mirrors “real world” demographics, which I appreciate. I love that my STEM child felt both challenged and encouraged. Our child is now a senior.
