column3: Atherton high school provides a great experience in any area of learning. they teachers and staff are friendly and the students are above average. I am currently a senior at atherton, and having spent almost four years there, I can safely say this is the best school I have ever been to. Atherton is the most unique school in JCPS. We offer a wide variety of courses and academic levels. Atherton has both AP and IB programs. IB (International Baccalaueate) is an academic program taught in over 140 countries. It is cosidered the world standard in education. The teachers at Atherton are excellent. They are highly skilled, and really care about the students. They are devoted to providing the best education possible. I have become very close to a lot of the teachers. There are also 5 foreign languages at Atherton, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, and Japanese. Atherton also has a diverse student body. We have a large number of exchange students and ESl students. Our school comunity is very close, and there is no descrimination of any kind. There are all types of people at Atherton, we have large percentage of gay, lesbian, and bisexual students. Students love Atherton so much, they often come to visit after they have graduated. I really love Atherton, and will miss this school when I graduate. I hope you can enjoy Atherton too. It is a wonderful school that really cares about it's students. Children and students who are "unique" really excel here. At this school there are really no cliques or real high school drama. Our principal Dr. Aberli really cares about our school, and is actually loved by students. Its a fun place to go to school, and even though our football team is lacking every high school event is filled with students. I would recommend anyone who wants to go to a school that will care about you and your academics should come visit Atherton and see why we're great. My daughter loves it at Atherton. She is currently a senior and will graduate well prepared for college. She left the traditional program to attend Atherton. While it was the scariest decision we had ever made for her academically, it turned out to be the very best decision we could have made. She has wonderful teachers and a great principal and staff. Plans are for the next child to attend as well. I thrived at Atherton loved it in every way possible, was involved with soccer and learned things that I would not have learned anywhere else. I would recommend Atherton to any parent but only if their child has a strong moral compass because I found it hard to find a group of kids at Atherton that I could relate to that didn't do drugs. There are alot of drugs going on there. Atherton is a hidden gem in the Highlands. It has a very accepting culture and we have found almost every teacher to be engaged and focused, not just on education but on knowing their students as well. Coming from catholic school K-8, we were thrilled at our decision to send our daughter to Atherton. I'm am the class of 2020, in my 4 years at Atherton I've seen many things that stand out from other high schools. An overall feeling of unity among students, a school spirit that is crazy contagious, and a committed student body. But also in my 4 years at Atherton Dr. Aberli (the principal) wasn't present for my underclassmen years (9th&10th), and those years seemed to run much more smoothly than when he came back. We had a complete overhaul of the administration in 1 year. With one of the new assistant principals coming from my former middle school where she taught english. 3 new counselors with one of them only being at the school for one year. This overhaul was due to the fact of Dr. Aberli's return back to Atherton. In the two years that he has been "my principal" he rarely develops relationships with students, compared to the principal during my underclassmen years. Dr. Aberli as well has decided to invest over 1.5 million dollars into the academies which will benefit a small amount of student body. That 1.5 million will be used for 3 classrooms, which will destroy the history of our building. Atherton is a school that has received more and more interest as its name has grown and grown and this has made Atherton incredibly overcapacity. With not enough bathrooms for students, not adequate technological resources available for students and faculty, increasing issues with facilities, and an outright obvious additude toward the issues throughout the school by the administration. This school used to be THE school to go to, but more and more it's going down the drain because they've gone away from their roots. I hope that the time that you and/or your student spends at Atherton is beneficial as it has been for me, but I pray that the administration gets their head on straight.

In spite of the budget cuts, they are holding up the quality though the teachers do seem to be overworked. I hope we pass our new bond to help out this year. My child is very comfortable at school. The Lewis-Palmer High School is a great place to send your kids. They make the children feel comfortable to be themselves and my son cant stop talking about how great the food is. He fit right in and is making so many new friends. This school has been great for my kids. There seems to be a place for everyone to get involved and have fun. column1: If you want your child to receive a good education from a small caring staff. Athens is the place to go. We school of choiced our children to Athens in 2011-2012 school year due to their consistant positive MEAP scores and we have not been disapointed. We have been well excepted by the community and my children have been involved in sports, band and extra caricular activities. The choices for electives is small as you find in almost any small school but the core classes more than prepair my children for college. The affiliation with the Battle Creek Math and Science Center is also a huge plus as well as the helpfulness of the school system to get the assistance to advance to college level classes that my daughter wanted to take at KCC as part of her senior year. We also have taken on a foriegn exchange student this year and found the program which runs through multiple schools all around the southern Michigan area to be very supportive and has been a wonderful support system for the families and students in the area. Overall this community and it's administration have been a wonderful experience for my family after some very poor experiences in other schools in the area. AWSOME, I have 3 children in this school system, I could not ask for a better group of TEACHERS, they TRULY care about the students!!! There is not a better group from the Kindergarten to graduation!!! and BTW we have also had 4 EXCHANGE STUDENTS, all by our choice in our clean house and every single one of them has had a wonderful and fulfilling experience at ATHENS SCHOOL and would put in writing!!! The worse school district in the area- children with differences are told to find a different district and teachers become the bullies. Nothing is available at this school to help those who are different succeed- no remedial, no AP, no honors, and nothing to suit students with different interests. Test scores at this school are one of the highest in the county, they are nationally and state rank in education, no they don't have a swimming pool, no they don't have a soccer team, but what is it we send our kids to school for? Some may complain that they don't offer AP classes like most small schools they simply can't because of the numbers, but they do offer College courses through KCC and are part of the Battle Creek Area Math and Science Center, so if your kid does show higher apptitude in those areas there are courses available to them. Why parents don't look at the statistics before sending their kid to a big shiny new school is beyond me, looking at the educational facts provided by the MEAP and Mstep give no argument as to why you would choose a different School in the area.

column1: Excellent school, very demanding academically. Our son in addition to being accepted to Saint Joseph's Prep was accepted to Lasalle College High School,Central High School and got a scholarship to Roman Catholic High school, however he decided he wanted to go to the prep and it was the best choice we made. Every night he spends three to four hours studying but he doesn't mind it because he loves going to the prep. As an alumnus of St. Joe's Prep, I cannot recommend it. The school strictly enforces minor dress code issues, while tolerating bullying by athletes. Many teachers are fundamentally dishonest, or make false claims against students to assist with fundraising. Although there are many good teachers, it is a case of a few really rotten apples spoiling the bunch. I had two sons and 2 nephews who graduated from the Prep. I have another son going there this year. Both of my sons and nephews who graduated got into top tier colleges and are on track to get top tier jobs. The son who I have at the Prep right now is very shy, and did not want to go to the prep and have to leave his old friends. After a day of being there he immediately fell in love with everything from teachers to to food. The atmosphere is great and the motto of "man for others" could not be anything more than what I ask for. The academics while demanding and challenging, are a nice way to challenge my son into becoming the best student possible. The teachers are also engaging, and willing to help at all times, while the religious aspect is also perfect. I could not be more impressed with Saint Joe's prep and feel that it is the best high school in the country. The Prep is truly a place where you can find yourself. If your son is looking to grow academically, socially, and morally, this is the place to be. While the Prep may not be for everyone, there is something for everyone at the Prep. If your son is an athletic type, this school offers top-tier sports teams with top-tier coaches. Even if your son doesn't make the team, there are tons of different sports and activities to try. If your son is intelligent and is looking to be further challenged, The Prep offers many honors course options and a variety of AP classes. The teachers are terrific and are always available for extra help and tutoring if your son needs/wants it. If your son is the adventurous type, he will find the many service opportunities and school trips that the Prep offers in addition to the added independence and freedom of being located in the city. All in all, the Prep stresses the goal of making their students "Men for Others". Your son will undoubtedly, finish his high school experience with a sense of responsibility to care and conquer the world before him. Go Prep! 5 Stars Every day, I become a little more grateful that I attended Saint Joseph's Prep. This is a school that took me in and instilled in me a voice and a confidence I thought I'd never have. When I arrived at college, at one of the most prestigious and oldest of all schools in the US, I started to really realize the power of the Prep. My college classmates initially bragged about how easy high school was for them, and how they "didn't need to open a book". The transition for most of them was incredibly rough. On the other hand, I could not have been better prepared. It stunned me how even some of the prep's introductory classes were on par with the AP level classes at some other schools. You may doubt your place at this all-boys school initially, but I promise you, if you graduate from this school, you will be better off. The tuition is currently $21,550. This is a tremendous sacrifice for any parent; it certainly was for mine. However, it is called a sacrifice for a reason: you give up something in exchange for something even greater. I don't think I will ever be able to repay my parents for the sacrifices they went through in order to send me to this school. I cannot thank the amazing faculty at the prep enough. Extremely high and I learned tons that I'll use in life

column3: I attended the school from 1971 to 1975. It was and is a great school. I almost graduated in 1975, needed 1/2 credit! I am currently a sophomore at Round Lake High School, and I am enrolled in both honors and AP classes. I honestly don't think that RLHS gets enough credit, because it had been looked down upon by other school districts for years; the regular classes may not be as productive but I feel that the accelerated courses are challenging and rigorous enough, and our scores of SAT and ACTs in math are pretty high, even above the national average. The math team is ranked 24th/50 schools in IL. True, we have a long way to go, especially in the English and history departments, but academically, we're doing quite well. However, in terms of the social environment of the school, there is a lot of bullying and physical violence that goes on that need to be resolved. Teen pregnancy is another major problem. My other complaint would be that the Fine Arts at this school doesn't get enough recognition, and that we lack funds to do greater things with our band and choir programs. Athletic-wise, our Varsity soccer team is ranked 10th in the state, which is not too shabby and our football team is making a great comeback this season. We may lack the prestige and the money, but this is a pretty good school. Excellent school with great honors programs and support for multilingual students. School offers many different programs for all students. THIS SCHOOL IS GOD AWFUL . I advise everybody not to come to this school if you have a choice .. this is coming from a current junior in the process of transferring schools . Do not attend RLHS . People who rate this school as awful are most likely coming at it from an outsider's perspective. I went to RLAS from K-12, graduated, and now attend one of the top private schools in the country. Some of my classmates are at institutions like Yale, Dartmouth, Harvard, Smith, Amherst, etc. Some of the highest ranking schools in the country. This school is what you make of it. This school is brought down not by the people who work here but the stigma it's been given by outside communities. We are expected to not do as well because we're from a poor neighborhood, but honestly, putting in some effort on the students' and parents' side of things is what's missing. I have a child who attends RLHS. I agree with the last persons review, school is what you make it. The Staff cares and is actively involved in the well being of the students. My child with his effort and help from the staff(direction every year what needs to be done to obtain his goals) has graduated a semester early. Yes the school is old and it has gangs. Alot of schools do now a days. Cant get away from it really. But if youre actively involved in your childs life then it doesnt matter how old the school is. They are even talking about adding on to this school. And school is what the student makes it. I am sorry but I experienced RLHS first hand and I can assure you that "You make what you want of high school", is not an accurate description of that "awesome" institution. No, most schools do not have gangs. In fact most schools remove those type of toxic people to better the students that do care about their education. I was only subjected to this school for one year (Junior year) and I can definitely say that anyone that wants to have a good foundation for College should NOT attend RLHS. To start off I was given 4 study halls because of lack of funding for a full 8 period day. If that is not enough for you continue reading. The classes that I did have I was in Honors classes (they did not allow me to take AP classes as a Junior for some absurd reason). Lack of extracurricular activities means people just clock in and out during the school day. No one stays after for enrichment and/or extra help. The ratings as of May 2017 need to go up. Round Lake HS ranked in the top 10 percent in the nation and top 12 percent in the state. The village voted to renovate a huge part of the school and trust me, Round Lake has definitely gotten an upgrade both physically, but also academically. Any of these comments older than a year are outdated, Round Lake is thriving and advancing, and it's definitely noticeable. Great school. No gnags anymore. Some Teachers a bit questionsble tho(racist remarks have been said).

column1: A challenging, encouraging environment for students grades 8-12. Students benefit from small classes that afford them personal attention and easy access to teacher office hours. Classes span a wide range of levels and subjects. Upper classman have the opportunity to take honors and advanced placement classes, which are great preparation for college level classes. Additionally, advanced classes present the opportunity for students to place our of first year college requirements. Wonderful teachers that are frequently involved in extra-curriculars, as well. Extremely robust athletics and extra-curricular program that helps keep students involved, focused, and in touch with their community. This is the first school in the nation to receive the government's Malcolm Baldridge award for excellence and it is apparent why to anyone who knows the school. Students are highly motivated; the environment is highly competitive. Most teachers go above and beyond what one might expect so that the students receive the best education possible. For example, my daughter was out sick for a week and we recived a call from one of her teachers. He was worried about her grades and offered to stay after school or come to the house in the evenings to provide her with the lessons she missed. He was worried while her test scores averaged 98.5%. If he's that concerned about a good student, I can't imagine the effort that he puts into helping the student who is struggling. Parents are very involved and teachers are very approachable and interested in addressing concerns. The school prepares the students quite well for college. Both of my children went on to highly rated private universities, one to the number one rated medical school in the country, where they graduated near the top of their class. They both owe much of their success to the education received at Pearl River High School. The school is very narrow-minded. The school treats all it's students, except the sport oriented students, as insubordinate to the teachers. I can honestly say, as a student, that only very few of the teachers actually care. In fact I can actually say that I was even bullied by a teacher -Posted by a disgruntled and unhappy student. Cares more about the funding of the sports teams then the funding of classroom resources such as textbooks. Great experience and strong college prep programs. I made great friends who I keep in touch with years after graduation. Diverse and tight knit community of professionals and working class parents who are involved in their children's learning. My children have had the opportunity to take advanced placement and honors classes. Teachers are kind and competent. There are plenty of sports and after school programs. PTA is involved and plans nice activities. There is something for everyone.

column3: The HS is a great school and i would tell anyone to go there Scotia Rocks The Teachers work really hard on the students education I am a current student at Scoti-Glenville high school. The teachers here are amazing. They try very hard with each and every student and still have time for a good laugh... I love you SGHS! This is o e of the worst schools in Schenectady county I regret ever getting a house out here children are not the schools Number one priority ! DO NOT MOVE HERE YOU WILL Regret it Everyone knows everyone, it's an amazing school. The teachers make it amazing with what little they have to work with. Who ever says this school isn't great doesn't know what they're talking about. It's like a family, the classes are small, so the friendships and relationships built throughout our four years here are stronger than ever. I want my kids to attend this school, it's that great. Scotia-Glenville is a good example of a community centric school district. It's size and history provides an ongoing civics experience. The school provides academic excellence, a safe environment and opportunities to participate in a wide variety of interests. Local organizations and residents have consistently supported the schools. Students have responded with high graduation rates, outstanding musicals, award winning artwork and winning sports teams. ( Scotia-Glenville's undefeated Boys basketball was 2014 NYS champions & are on track to repeat in 2015) This school allows bullying to go on. When administration is alerted they never get back to the parents. The school is building a reputation of being a "rough school " The same way of teaching and activities are done year after year and they never seem to reach outside the box to challenge the students. Looking for another school to send my children. Recommend not to send your children to this school!!!!!!!!!!!!! The parent who stated that the school allows bullying to go on is 100% correct. I have reported several incidents to admin and absolutely nothing was done until I contacted the superintendent directly. Do not send your child here! As a student who will graduate in June 2020, I'm proud to say that I attend Scotia-Glenville Senior High School. EXCELLENT! Met the needs of all three of my children with very diverse needs and personalities.

column1: Hmm well this school is okay , but i love the fact they help you if your behind on your credits , like PLATO I currently attend this school and it's amazing!!!!! The teachers are the best that I have ever had the priveldge to be teaches by .they care about their students and main goal is to see the student body succeed!! The student body might not be the best but we accomplish things ..I couldn't Be more proud to be called a south Houston Trojan !!! GOtrojans!!!:) our community pride and joy I couldnt be any more proud of being a trojan & a Jannette dancer, C/O 11'. The school itself may need some repair, but the teachers are pretty good. Of course, not all of my teachers have been the best. But if I ever have a problem in learning something, I find a way out of it; look for a great teacher to go to during tutoring, there's many at this school. I've succeded academically so much. I love South Houston HS & I'm going to miss it very much after I graduate. As a 1981 Graduate of SOHO, I would like to say that living in the area, I have seen many changes in the area which can't help be relected in the schools. There was a time when parents parented their children and were involved in what was going on at school. But the area has changed and the culture has changed and now the majority of the students at SHHS were not taught the smallest amount of respect for each other but worst of all no self respect. The staff of the high school has a limited time with the KIDS and thats what they are they are children whom will soon be released into the world. If parents would do their job then perhaps the dedicated staff of SHHS could also do theirs instead of having to deal with BS from the fringe few whom have no respect for Education I attended this school over a decade ago and it was fairly decent. The education was up to par. Older siblings attended over two decades ago and it was even better then. Now the new generation of family is attending and I have to say that the level of education has hit rock bottom. Not only is there no more diversity among students but the grammar of these kids is horrible. I have met with some of the teachers and they are either (a) fresh out of college or (b) just don't care. If the teachers are not organized how do they expect the students to be. It seems that this school has declined tremendously over time. I am highly dissatisfied with the school and its curriculum/teachers. Lame, the principals are rude,some teachers don't want to stay after school and help the student, in class when asking for help the get upset and say we were not "paying attention" when they really suck at teaching sometimes. If they do try to help your even more confused than you were before. This school's a.p. staff are terrible. If they do not like a student on a personal level, yes they brig personal feelings into play. They will almost stalk your child around the school just so they can catch them doing something they do not approve of. Like what? Having a hat on or a backpack. You can not carry a backpack in high school? It's not like the students don't have school work and books to carry. That is outrageous I think high school is when a backpack is needed most. Idiocy.

column1: I've found that throughout my years at Spencerville, the entire atmosphere is just great. The teachers are very caring and the students are over-all well behaved. Being a small school, it's great to have a staff who will reach out to each individual. I've really noticed how much of a family our school has become since we got our new school. The academics are growing as well as the athletics and school spirit. The high school rating, 5 out of possible 10 doesn't begin to cast light on the degree of mediocrity present here. Bullying against new students or those with any form of learning disability is rampant. Several have withdrawn in favor of online schools rather than be subjected to the further insult of being disciplined for defending themselves. If you're satisfied with a school district that still schedules its opening to allow time for the county fair, then perhaps this is good enough. The district like to cite the fact that they are awarded a state honor for achievement each year, but truth is - you get that just for having toilet paper in the rest rooms. Overall, if you're happy with a school where your child will be an outcast and ostracized just for being new or different, this is the place for you. If the idea that a public meeting over renewing the football coach's contract draws more attendance than any other school board business, your priorities will be met here. To The Only Parent Writing A Review As of This Time: Sadly, I agree with you, & I support you & I'm so sorry for what you & your child/ren have to endure. This site is such a disappointment {although not surprising} that one writing a review is being held in a choke-hold of censorship, "conditions", etc. No thanks....I'm choosing to express myself where our right to "FREEDOM OF SPEECH" is freely granted.....Facebook. {P.S.My version of "the star rating" is...Our School "gets" 4 stars because the great majority of our teachers' MAIN priorities are their STUDENTS...& they treat them fairly & equally, & they could care less what their last names are/aren't, who their parents are/aren't, etc. Teacher Quality: The same reasons previously stated, plus they CARE. Principal Leadership: 4, Because he's more of a problemSOLVER, than problemMAKER. *I'm treating "Parent Involvement" as meaning how involved my sons' teachers are/have been re: keeping ME updated re: anything having to do w/their lives @ school.} Donna D. Burnett

column3: Many new additions, as said below. one does not have to be above average o succeed, they only need to try, math department goes up to Calculus 2, and AP Calculus 1; a math class is completed every half year (semester, students can take either 1 or 2 math classes a year (or not at all, if math requirements are meet), as a freshman you can only take one. A very large amount of classes are offered alongside the standard academics, there are currently 6 general use computer labs, over 4 carts of about 25 laptops (class sizes vary), a cart of laptops in the shop, and a cart of the districts best laptops (better than the techies) for the engineering programs. great school with lots to offer for all kinds of students; science, engineering, math, athletic, dance, arts, music, photography, 3 languages (Spanish, French, Latin). This school has some good teachers, but has a very poor record in teaching students with disabilities (4th year of academic warning status with the state for its large achievement gap). No encouragement to take the PSAT or early career planning for gifted sophomores. Administrative leadership is non-existent. If you are relocating here look at Naperville or St. Charles High schools. I have found BHS to be a great school. The continue improvement in their teaching and curriculum offerings have made it one of the top rated high schools in Kane County. This school is the worst school in the world! Bullies try to get good kids in trouble, even though those kids didn't do anything at all! Even though there is no proof that the kid did anything that kid got suspended. Batavia High School is the gem of the Fox Valley. Most Western suburbanites seek out the Naperville school districts when looking for a new community, but this top rated school, just a notch under Dist# 204 is a terrific option (with less congestion and traffic when you learn to avoid Randall Road). Although there is a huge focus on sports, the music program is second to none and the staff support a college readiness agenda. The band/orchestra program is very impressive. Students are on a block schedule and are expected to immerse themselves in coursework, think and work independently, be responsible for their own future. Both the brightest who will be well prepared for college, and those who prefer a non-college path have challenging course options. I have one son who is still attending BHS. I wish we would have moved here sooner for my older sons to get the benefit of all four years in this great learning environment. As a mother, home-owner and a Realtor I recommend this community for the school district. Well worth the taxes. Unfortunately, the students never see their counselors so it is very difficult to get college help. Very rude office staff. They should be welcoming to students and parents! Teachers and administrators show favoritism towards athletes, especially football players, while students in the arts or who aren't in extra-curriculars fall to the wayside. They don't try to work with people who have behavioral issues, they stick them in an isolated room all day and basically ignore them. All they care about is test scores, they're not too concerned about if the students are actually retaining the information or if they're actually learning things that are substantial and may help them in the future. I'm currently a student at BHS and I feel that the curriculum itself is ok. The main thing I have problems with are the the school bathrooms. The bathrooms in the school are in total disrepair, but the janitors don't seem to try to even fix it. The only thing they try to fix is people writing on the bathroom walls and people peeing and pooping on the floor. Oh yeah. I forgot to mention that people do that in our school. The school just dumped a bunch of money towards improving the hallways of the school, but not trying to fix the bathrooms when they're needed to be fixed. Batavia has the very best high school! As a high school teacher (from another district) I feel the administration and teachers at Batavia go above and beyond to make each student's experience the very best it can be. I LOVE the block scheduling. It allows students to actually learn and it allows students to really focus on four classes at a time. Our daughter is flourishing here. I am so glad we picked Batavia 10 years ago! This school cares more about stats, test scores, and impressions. Control that, and you can discredit anyone's criticism and accuse them of being a grumbler or complainer who jumps to conclusions. They do not prepare most students for college like they claim. Only those students already at the top of their game and already possess college level skills will say differently, and so will their parents, because they get all the attention and advantages in both the classrooms and the school. There are a huge number of students with great potential at this high school that aren't learning or scoring quite as high as they are capable of if they had more devoted attention, but because they are performing average or good enough, they fall through the cracks. They are not taught the required college skills at all. Their grades only reflect that they haven't mastered self-learning and self-direction, not what they are capable of learning. In addition, there is no way to have complaints resolved. Anyone you have to report to a superior is above reproach. When you go to the very top, you are told that you have to deal directly with the one you are having a problem with even thought you tell them you already have. There is nothing else you can do because parents are always treated like hostiles, no matter what the disagreement is. Staff will quickly try to cover up what they did wrong, and amass support from other staff to discredit what a student reports or the parent. This kind of oversight prevents this high school from actually becoming what they purport they are because it keeps bad employees in place where they shouldn't be. Horrible. So many students threaten others. Teachers are rude, and have friends to support them. And kids bully each other. They are rude and disrespectful. I don't know how anyone likes this schools. Don't let the high SAT scores fool you. Avoid this place.

column1: I was a student at West Campus coming from Sutter Middle School. I believe that WC's reputation is greatly exaggerated. At one time it might have been accurate but when I attended it seemed as though they attracted high achieving and motivated students and put them in classes with below average teachers and counted on their already high test scores. In fact the school seems obsessed with preparation for standardized tests. Most of the ever changing administration and staff seems uncaring for thier students. And because it is a small school there is very little choice in classes. If you are looking for a small, safe, average, meat and potatoes school then go for it! But dont have higher expectations. If it has gotten better in the last two years it will be a pleasant surprise. West Campus is the best of the best! If you come here, you can tell for yourself.This is a school that's everything but your average!We got the highest API of all the other highs schools and honestly I can say we don't even consider ourselves decent.We still strive for excellence every day.There's just so much school spirit here you simply can't ignore it.I had the chance to go to Hiram Johnson, McKlatchy,Health Proffesions,Sac high,and a arts & science school which I forgot the name of.My Cst scores are advanced and even though I moved to Elk Grove I had the option & choice to transfer.I know girls that go there which are now in prohibation.Events,Rallies,and everything you can think of is magnificent! Even though we don't have the amount of school funding and money we want we still make the best of it. ALL ABOUT SCORES AND TESTS. The administration lacks the ability to know each "high achieving" student on any kind of personal level. They a public school snobs. Education is a collaboration between students parents, and schools. At West Campus Parents and students have very little say. west campus is sadly all about scores and results. they dont care about the students they just care about keeping their reputation We will be moving to Sacramento this summer and I am trying to determine which high school we would like our daughter to go to. We also will decide what part of the city to live in based on this decision. Thank you for all your help. I hated this school it was one of the worst schools in Sacramento. The people at this school are mean and rude.The years that I spent at this school were horrible. The school is outdated and old. Overall I hated this school coming from Caleb Greenwood. They needed to be more welcome and forgiving and have a better introduction to people who came to smaller schools. I HATED MY EXPERIENCE AT WEST CAMPUS !! :( Its an excellent school with awesome teachers. Teachers willing to put efforts and spend extra time into helping the students. You might have an A or B in other school and turn out you have a B or C in this school. But for future, grades are not really the thing that should be worry if you work hard. Working hard always helps to lock great longlasting knowledge: ) And Knowledge will always go along with you. i have been attending West for over a year now and I must say if you want something better for yourself, this school will help acheive your dreams. At frist it was very overwhelming but during the second semester it became at ease. It might feel like this school pushes you off the edge, but in reality it is actually shaping your life...even if you oblivious from the effect. I hope this school is right for, if you want to succeed in life. :D What impresses me is the students want to learn and this school's "culture", despite the old facilities, promotes that. The students care. In my daughter's group project groups everyone is involved. Her older siblings were at a couple different local high schools and over the years there always were students who didn't care and hampered the groups. We have been very happy with our son's experience at West Campus. He is doing very well academically, taking AP courses and participating in the marching band and the winter drum line. He came from a very small private school, and had no problem fitting in from the beginning. The size of the school is a plus, as it is smaller than most of the other high schools. To those who say they are only concerned about test scores, that is the nature of public education these days, and to the degree that West is guilty, I would say all good public schools have the same concern. I believe our son is getting a good education in spite of that. Even though there were times i dreaded at West Campus, I could not possibly see myself anywhere else. I love this school and I feel honored to be graduating from there. I graduated a few years back and i must tell you- it is a very difficult school (academically) but as I made friends the next few years in college, I slowly but surely realized that ( it may sound wrong) I am a lot more in tune intellectually than all my other friends. I soon showed most of my friends my technique of taking notes taught by West Campus' own Mr. Hotell and my friends have been getting nothing but A's and B's in the college classes. West Campus was a great experience, it definitely gave me stepping stones. West campus curriculum is harder than college. It is all doable because you have such amazing assistance and the teachers are more than happy to help. They really improved my critical and analytical skills during my four years there and really prepared me for a four year in a university environment. If your child is a transferring upperclassman in search of AP classes prepare to be disappointed. My transferring junior was shutout of three AP classes for which she applied and I bored to death in general classes that provide zero challenge. To add insult to injury the school sends us a letter recommending she be enrolled the very three classes in which they denied her at the outset! The reason stated is the smaller enrollment size and the demand for AP classes. Result: a lot of time being wasted re-hashing curricula she learned in middle school. My transferring senior fared somewhat better. However; since he didn't take geography in CA, and there's no way to test out of the class, he wastes that period hanging out with freshmen not doing anything constructive. It took the school half a semster to decide music was an art after telling him it wasn't, therefore requiring him to take an art class in which he had no interest but had to as a requirement. When he attempted to switch over to band because he's been playing an instrument since the third grade, they denied that request citing no reason. Still waiting to see the benefit of enrolling my kids here. The West Campus teachers and administration only care about test scores and their reputation. It is a perfect school for students who can teach themselves and never have any questions. There is no tutoring offered and teachers do not extend themselves beyond their regular class hours. The office staff is unfriendly and condescending to both students and parents. This school looks great on paper but is a totally different reality. My daughter enjoys the school. The Principal is very personable and friendly, going out of his way making sure we are comfortable. All classes are college prep. The students are nice to each and especially to new students. The teachers are knowledgeable on their subject matter and willing to give extra help. We like this school. If you child struggles with school at all, this is not the school for you. This school can only handle the best of the best. My three sons have attended West Campus and as my eldest prepares for graduation, I must say, West Campus has the BEST school community/ environment that I have seen a school have in all my years in education. I sent my sons to West Campus for the education but what they received was more than I thought they would get. The student lead school spirit is wonderful. It is beautiful to see the student body come together and support their school teams and their peers. I have attended school rally's and school sporting events along with student lead fundraisers and let me tell you, every time I feel welcomed as a parent. The small school environment allows the students, teachers and staff an opportunity to really get to know one another. I couldn't have asked for a better school. Give your son or daughter the opportunity to enjoy high school and get a great education at the same time, enroll them at West Campus. "WEST CAMPUS IS THE BEST HIGH SCHOOL EVER!" I am going to debunk this lie. What seems to be education here is really massive regurgitation of pointless facts and ideas, because that is what West Campus is all about. West campus only cares about your test scores, mainly so that they can keep the school's reputation high. At west campus, the majority of students only care about grades. Here, it's not about learning. In class, you will usually hear students ask, "What questions will the upcoming test contain?" Other than that, you will rarely hear students ask questions in class about the subject in particular. Contrary to popular belief, students also cheat in this school, because many students only care about their grades, not whether the learned anything or not. Like other students from other schools, West Campus students detest learning, and only study what is being spoon fed to them at the moment. Pros: > West Campus is known as a college prep. school, which helps prepare students for college and university. > Students who attend this school are generally respectful to others, meaning there are no fights, no bullying, etc. >Rallies are one of the most exciting and enthusiastic I have seen. >A good school for people who want to major in Liberal Arts and History, especially for English Majors. Cons: >Large class sizes >Mathematics and Science are not taught well in this school (many teachers are simply those who majored in Science and Mathematics only to teach math or science) >Lack of Hands-on experimentation (science labs in science classes are rarely used, and science is a hands-on subject, not only out of the book) >Science class is a JOKE (really? liver and H202?) Simple science equipment. >Bad school for those who want to become Scientists, Engineers, and Doctors, Computer Gurus. Lack of funding for better science labs and equipment, no engineering classes, and useless Science Fairs (who wants to see simple science experiments such as Color Changing Carnations again?) My two cents on West Campus. A great school with a great staff, students, parents and most of all academics. A awesome place to learn and become a great person. I would say it has helped me mature, well more specifically in the case of the past few years where my class had to go through a lot. I think it has definitely taught me how to be a more critical thinker as well as adaptable in the real world. I definitely felt both annoyance and appreciation towards the school during the past 4 years. There's highs and lows to this school. You can't really generalize it and put it into a category of whether it's good or bad because it's definitely more complex than that. If you are planning to apply to West Campus, go for it! You will definitely change during these four years, although I can't guarantee you if it's for the best or the worst. I love this school so much. It is the best.

Though I cannot attest for standard classes, I know the teachers I had were excellent and they helped me tremendously. I also love the school spirit here, especially when it comes to our rival. I miss it, and I would not have wanted to go anywhere else. Bleed black and gold.

column1: The teachers are not fun and don't care about anything i cant even listen to music at lunch out loud and the food is terrible it either tastes like cardboard or plastic. i mean there is good teachers like Mr.O he is amazing. some teaches purposely fail you because they hate you and just don't care and that is being a but influences on the kids. and all the money that the money it goes to stuff and like teachers that don't even need it and they gave the students chrome books and blocked everything so the kids can go on anything at all. I think every school has it's ups and it's downs. As a student in her second year of high school. I think that I can inform the public what Montello Jr/Sr high school is really all about. Over the years our school is really trying to change for the better. We have great teachers even, if some just use our school as a stepping stone for something better. Then there are the teachers that has been here forever. Mr. Huan a math teacher, has been here for 32 years. He is a super committed to what he does and most of the teachers here are the same. Mr. Broud is my advisory teacher, he always starts my day great. Mr. Broud is always cheerful and ready for every day. I think our main problem in our school is the "higher powers" something my old history teacher Mr. Lloyd said a lot. I think some of them just need to leave which, would help our school A LOT. But not our principal Mr. Harsh. He is a hard working guy and enjoys his job. Mr. Harsh believes that every student is good kid, just some of them choose the wrong path. There are also good factors about the school like Chrome Books that every student gets. Which helps with classes that we need to write papers or when do our every day assignments . Plus this year the staff had worked hard to make our schools motto time to climb since we are hill-toppers it makes sense. If a student has one missing assignment they go to the climb room during lunch and keep going until they don't have missing assignments. Which will help the students learning to become better. I'd say the best improvement this year is lunch. We had gotten a new foods director and she is doing great!! I love my lunches now the other day we had mac and cheese and it was delicious. They also have a salad bar and a sub hub where we can built our own subs. All this is a major improvement. Montello Jr/Sr high school is moving forward and becoming a place I actually like.

column3: I wanted to like this school and sent my son there with hesitation. It has not been a good year. The security is the hardest working faction of the school. The Principal is rarely available, the teachers do not return calls or emails. The online grade program is only as good as the teachers who keep it updated, and most of them do not seem to so I never really have an idea of the grades for my son. The Digital Arts Academy is a complete joke and most kids have dropped out of the program. The tutoring program no longer exists because I'm told the teachers would not do it. If you have a bright and motivated child, of course your child will do well here and anywhere else. If your child needs guidance, assistance, and may be easily led, this is not the school for your child. The Board of Education is weak, and they still cannot figure out why they are more than half a million underspent. The sports program uses up taxpayer money and does not produce results. The athletes are targets for discipline because they are the only students that may be motivated by discipline. Despite the town's troubles with race and culture challenges, there does not seem to be an effort to teach. Amazing. I loved going here. I just graduated last year and miss it a lot. Teachers are wonderful and available when needed I wish I had never enrolled my kid here...it did such damage to her self esteem and self worth. Would give it 0 stars if possible. Most of the staff does not reply to emails and some staff members (ex. the principal) are never available in their office when you need to have an important meeting with them. Some staff members treat the students with blatant disrespect when the students ask important questions or have certain concerns that need to be addressed. The head of the science department does absolutely nothing to help the students when it comes to resolving grades with teachers who sometimes give unfair and biased grades to students. The staff is entirely focused on sports and gives little to no care about the academics which are weak (we barely have any AP classes). Our school at one point of time did not have enough money to fix the printers and buy printer paper but then used money to buy useless TVs that they placed in the school lobby. The staff is more concerned about creating stricter rules to infringe on our freedom rather than actually preparing us for college. Very poor. Administrators are rarely available to meet with, even by appointment. Education quality is sub par and issues like bullying are swept under the rug. rgZFzf s f z f b v b g

column1: People say that high school is supposed to be the best time of your life. Personally, my time at Delta High School was a complete waste of time. I have attended DHS for 3 years, but have recently decided to finish my senior year somewhere else, so I could have a REAL high school experience. This school is a huge disappointment. As much as people say the teachers really care about the student, they don't. There's no diversity. I feel that the Latino population at DHS isn't given the same help/opportunities as other students. About 90% of this school isn't interested in things like Prom, Homecoming, ect. (Plus the price to attend these events are way to expensive) So because so many people don't care, the event is canceled, and it ruins the High School experience for everyone else. The school's agenda revolves around the FFA program. It seems like if you aren't in FFA, you are looked down upon. FFA kids get away with lots of things that other student wouldn't, because they are favored by certain teachers. I hate this school, I wish I never attended, I wouldnt recomend it to anyone. http://www.greatschools.org/california/clarksburg/4661-Delta-High-School/?tab=programs-culture As a parent at Delta High school, there was a big change recently. I read the review from a student who said the prom and homecoming was canceled. This is not true last year and the year before. Also, they support hispanic students with classes, counselors, scholarships, and college nights. I am sorry that student had those experiences but honestly I do not think that is what is happening anymore. They have FFA classes and some great art, music, and Spanish classes. I like that the teachers all know my son and care about how he does. This would not happen at a big school. Go Saints! There are certainly draw backs of going to such a small school but the benefits are numerous. Being in such a small community, students receive a ton of support. Also, there aren't very many other schools at which so many students can be involved in so many activities and excel at them all. The school is basically void of problems most big schools face. There is MAYBE one physical fight a year, the school has little to no gang violence, there is no circulation of hard drugs, and bullying is not an issue because of the everyone knows everyone factor. Class selection can be limited, but there is plenty of flexibility in changing your schedule after the school year has started. All in all, pretty good school. Overall, its an esthetically pleasing atmosphere. The classrooms are clean, the grounds are very nice, and the number of students enrolled is nice. We like a small town feel. However, the Staff is extremely disengaged. They don't interact with parents unless the parents reach out to them. They also don't utilize their counselor. There are several kids I know of who clearly would benefit from counseling and as a Counselor, I personally would be on the lookout for red flags or warning signs. It seems that the counselors only job is on an "As Needed" basis. The principal is pleasant to deal with but she should also be working with the counselor for students struggling academically to ensure they get the best shot. My Daughter graduated at CMS last school year. and has gone over to Delta High. she is special education. and doing fabulous! Mrs. Spralding is the best. she refused to see my daughter fall behind she kept pushing and encouraging and she did it. My son just started at CMS and he loves everyone. Mrs Hiromoto office manager is an angel handles everything just as smooth as can be, never seems bothered and as kind as they make them. Mrs Uslan Principal and Mrs. Walker vice Principal are very strong Leaders and make the schools run as best as they do. we are very grateful our children attend this wonderful smaller community! The overall experience at Delta is infuriating and leaves children completely unprepared to enter college or the workforce (excluding agricultural related jobs). Delta does nothing to help children learn, the admins are biased and unprofessional. The school does not help the children who are succeeding and only focuses on helping the students who are failing because they clearly just don't want to be in high school anymore. This school is headed in a dark direction. No one learns anything at this school. Students will be left completely unprepared for college if they even graduate or get into college. Lots of teachers have jumped ship and most high school students will tell you to go somewhere else. Everyone there is depressed and miserable and most of the teachers are just complacent because they are burnt out or just content with their job. Our daughter went to Delta High for her senior year. The school counselor and his support staff got her transferred the week before school started. She was shown kindness and they worked very hard on her behalf! The new principal is a huge blessing to this school. The teachers did their very best for our daughter. This was Delta High's first year dealing with virtual education. The entire staff and faculty were amazing and successful at making a quick transition.Our daughter has wonderful memories of her year there. May the Lord bless them in the years to come.

We need to build a new school.... FHS is overcrowded and tired of people shipping in people from the city because they can. Franklin is no where near what it used to be! FIX IT! Some of the students will have s3x with principal to get other students expelled. Avoid at all cost! If you love your kids do not send them here! Hey

column3: Hayfield is a nice, big school. The staff is very professional and the schedule is amazing. I've had a great experience at Hayfield Secondary and hope to create new memories with my friends and teachers! -Class of 2015 :) I am one of the original alumni from Hayfield...class of '73. So sad to hear what happened to this school over the years since I left. I have such great memories of my time there. I was in awe of the place. When it opened in '69 it was a wonder to behold for sure. The biggest high school on the east coast for a while. The planetarium was amazing and the gym was HUGE. Great sports coaches and teams, and outstanding school spirit. I think I still have my Harvester yearbook. The teachers were great and really cared. I haven't even seen what the school looks like now but hopefully one day soon I will drive by and go down memory lane. Very large school, 7th through 12 in same building. For the most part, middle schoolers are separate from the high schoolers. I don't like the block scheduling- seems that most of my son's teachers have a difficult time trading for a full 90 minutes and keep the students engaged. Also, when a teacher is absent, the sub gives a "time waster" assignment and they lose valuable teaching time. My daughter recently graduated from Hayfield, and we couldn't have been happier with her experiences there. The school is large but accommodating especially for students with special needs. She transitioned from almost complete isolation to actively enjoying and participating in many of the social events there at the school until her graduation including the dual enrollment option at NVCC in the 10th grade. Our experience has been that you get what you put into as far as involvement. The neighborhood is nice, clean, and safe compared to others in the area and there are so many ways for kids with varying interests to get and stay involved. Sure, there are some teachers who aren't on the same level as the superstars, but our experience has been overall very positive. Any issues my son has had, which have been few, have been addressed by his teachers and counselors quickly. They have plenty of opportunities during and after school for kids. Our son has had amazing teachers at Hayfield, especially for his AP classes! His councelor and the administration were very helpful when needed making the college application process much easier. We love Hayfield! So were do I begin.... First: the entire school is way understaffed. Too many kids fall through the cracks because of this. Second: there is ZERO and I mean ZERO to bare minimum accountability for everything in this building. No consistency in initiatives, discipline, school rules, EVERYTHING. Third: Discipline- what a joke; no consequences for delinquent and disruptive behavior whatsoever. Fourth: If you're a parent of a child with and IEP my advice to you is to ASK QUESTIONS to your child's case manger, administrator, SPED department chair, and especially the SPED administrator. I'm also sorry to say that the majority of the administration has really fallen hard as there is no true leadership and teamwork to make the school a better place. In addition, the majority of the teachers at this school are uncaring and highly unprofessional. And the counselors.... forget about it. Parents: please support your child in everything in this school. The place is so big they cannot keep up every kid! My son is in 7th grade and so far the first year experience has been amazing. He is the Avid program and it has really helped with his overall curriculum. I love the school so far :) The most underrated school and staff in Fairfax County! We were initially apprehensive about buying a house in this district due to the overall greatschools.org rating, but could not be more pleased! I would absolutely rate it a 9/10. Amazing, amazing, amazing faculty who care and invest in the students (they even come to support my kids at their extra-curricular activites), and tremendous academic and athletic opportunities for whatever you desire. The population is diverse, which is a significant strength, as it has helped our kids develop genuine life skills in learning how to bond, communicate, and appreciate differences in our society and has helped them become much better prepared for life in the real world. 100% recommend Hayfield! Hayfield is an underrated school. The best parts about Hayfield are its diverse student body and strong school spirit. The academics are strong at the most advanced levels and there are many nationally-recognized clubs and sports at Hayfield. Hayfield has great teachers and most importantly a diverse student body- which is the reason I love it so much. Leaders who don’t listen will eventually be surrounded by people who have nothing to say. There definitely needs to be more training for the administration on how to effectively address bullying. I’d say about 75% of my student’s teachers have been great. I thought everything was great until I had an issue that needed to be handled by an administrator. However, the administration is a mess. More training and/or some change ups are needed or it’s going to get worse. Very poor. New leadership may help. I think most teachers want a better situation. Can I give it zero stars? It seems great and is great until you have a problem. Then you’re out of luck! I got a DECENT education with honors and AP classes. Some teachers are great. Some are not so much. I’d say 75% prepared for college. As one who experienced bullying first hand, it was rough. Tone deaf administration made it worse. I was born the way I am. Telling me not to be so “out there” about it instead of punishing the bully was bad. Teachers were pretty good and used correct pronouns, but regular parent volunteers were allowed to purposely not use correct pronouns and complaints about it led no where. When kids see parents do it, they feel they can do it which leads to more bullying. A vicious cycle. A change in leadership may help. COVID helped bc I got a break from the bullying for a year. Can’t wait to graduate. How many times must I ask for an IEP meeting before I get one? I’m in the double digits now! AVOID THIS SCHOOL IF YOUR CHILD HAS AN IEP OR A 504!Don’t get me started on the bullying! The only solution offered is to remove MY kid (away from their only friends) instead of the bully. Shouldn’t the offender be punished and not the victim?Teachers are hit and miss. Many do not follow FCPS guidelines for minimum grades and weights. One of my kids classes only had 7 grades and it’s the second quarter. Rules are arbitrarily enforced. My kid sends me videos (cell phones aren’t allowed, but some teachers allow it anyway). It’s crazy to see kids playing inappropriate music and dancing around during SOAR, kids fighting or kids looking up inappropriate things on their school computers. My kid never has homework and some teachers refuse to follow my child’s IEP. My requests for meeting are ignored. Can’t wait to PCS! Some love to brag about the diversity, but they turn a blind eye to the inequity with test scores and minority students. They like to blame ESL kids, but that’s a small portion. They pat themselves on the back for donating to the Hawk Pantry instead of addressing the inequity issues. “Diversity” isn’t something embraced here. It’s just a badge to display. Counselor is never available, even if you leave a note. Some teachers are great. Others are awful. Administration is TERRIBLE. Problems are ignored. If you bring an issue to the admin, they paint a target on your kid’s back. All of the sudden rules that are never enforced (dress code, bathroom pass, random bag search, etc) are suddenly enforced for YOUR kid only. My kid knows the school is not fair and to keep their nose clean so admin can never find a violation, but boy do they try!!! Bullying, drugs, fights and mental health are serious issues that are ignored. That’s what admin should focus on instead. This school looks good from the outside and that's all there is. It's a travesty. Bullying goes on and on and on. Drugs, fights and nothing but talk from the administrators. Certain kids get away with anything but if one kid is a certain type, nothing will ever come their way. Not to speak of the corrupt sports teams where the same kind of kids make it. Rejection after rejection and again the administrators and so called coaches have excuses. You ask something, they are fake hurt and vehemently defend their nepotistic way. It's a chaotic school that screams Hawk pride while feeding on their young. Worst school by far. Blatant disregard of any kind of fairness while they claim to be so inclusive. An honor student goes to C- yet they advertise their academic programs that fail to address even the most basics in education. An outgoing kid is beaten into submission and anxiety with teachers standing by high fiving the perpetrators. An always athletic kid can't make any of the teams. The disconnect between their always empty words and slogans and propaganda and the reality of projecting fear, disregard, disrespect and exclusion is deafening and scary. My kid goes to Hayfield and so far I have no complaints. They have student from different backgrounds and perhaps because it is so large, the teachers or the administrative staff do not create a bond with the students and parents, which should improve. As for the rest, in my opinion, it is a very good school. It’s also very competitive in sports. Hayfield secondary is a great diverse school for kids. Not only are they learning from Great teachers, but there learning with kids that look like them. There is multiple afterschool groups that support's each and every one of our kids unique interest. Yes there is fight's and problems that occur with students, but that is expected. I would recommend this school to any parent that is looking for a place for there children to learn.

column1: This school has really impressed me. It truly is like a family that not only understands the importance of academic excellence but the urgency of nurturing, guiding, and protecting our children. My child has had a wonderful first year of high school and the moment he needed support, the Sacred Heart administrative team comprised of Father Maurice, principal Dececco, and their guidance counselors responded immediately in a fair and respectable manner. The teachers go above and beyond on a daily basis and are the main reason why my child feels comfortable and engaged at this school. As a parent, my child's academics are a priority, but their safety and emotional happiness are a NON NEGOTIABLE and for this reason we give this school 5 stars. I am so grateful for this school and all they do! Teachers don't teach. Only a few of them will even care about the grades a student gets. Faculty is terrible and doesn't care about the wellbeing of students as much as the teachers do. Office faculty is incompetent and loses important papers all the time. Important information never reaches the students properly. Principal is consistently absent. Dress code is way too strict. Tuition money seemingly goes nowhere that benefits the students. Speaking of students, most of them are racist, mysoginistic brats that don't ever get in trouble no matter what they do because they're a "valued" member of a sports team. No music opportunities at all. Art program is funded mostly by the teacher herself and the club part is dying. The only good thing i have to say about this school is the drama club, it's amazingly organized and a welcoming environment; probably because it's entirely funded by fundraisers and the school actually has no part in it at all. Just don't waste your money sending your kid here, I spent my entire school career here (kindergarten included) and trust me when I say you will destroy your kid's opportunities if they go here. Horrible. Zero out of 5 stars. 1 out of 10. Stay away HORRIBLE PLEASE TAKE YOUR MONEY ELSEWHERE DO NOT WASTE IT ON THIS VILE PLACE

column3: Richland High is amazing, it offers a good education, and the sports are amazing. We pretty much dominate Hanford. We take pride in our school, and pretty much everyone gets along. WASL test scores for hanford and rhs go hand in hand every year. Here it goes. I am a former RHS student and want to say that it is a really good school. I can's say it's the best (even though that's how I feel) because I have not attended any other schools in the area (even though I am enrolled at Southridge, I do full-time college and Tri-Tech). When I came to USA in 9th grade, I had met great support from all the teachers, and had been helped a lot. I would not agree that the grading is too easy, it probably depends what class level you are taking. The teachers are great and are very supportive, make learning fun and interesting. They have prepared me well for college. I also love the school grounds, along with Hanford High they are the most beautiful of the Tri-Cities high schools. About which school is better... It is hard to be objective here, but it is thought to be one of the best, along with Hanford High and Kamiakin High, maybe Southridge HIgh too. Overall, the days at RHS have been the best, and I miss them Being a bomber is prideful! Mostly everyone gets along and isn't rude to people they usually wouldn't hangout with! The teachers and other staff are great!! And we usually dominate in sports!! GO GREEN AND GOLD!!! :) I had four children attend Richland high school and receive a great education and all four of them went on to get a collage degree. I was a new student to Richland high school last school year (2014) and I'd have to say the school was not welcoming at all. I don't feel at home here and the teachers don't even try to connect with the students. actual learning wise I was getting much better grades at my school back east. this school makes me cry daily because it makes me miss my old school. 2004/2005 (my freshman year) the school was pretty good. From 2006 on, the school became a prison, which almost all students hated. More technology is needed to suit the needs on people who learn differently. I very much disliked school for the last 3 years. I am guilty over sending my children to this camp of horrors Overall I am very happy with my experience at RHS. If you are a parent or a future student, I would highly recommend that you participate in after school sports. Sports like cross country, swimming, and track do not require try outs and anyone can join. I have many fond memories from those sports and I built many great friendships. I would also encourage students to take some advanced math or AP courses. There is a wide range of students at RHS and I think your classroom experience will be better if the majority of students in your class are engaged learners. Failed to Graduate 2 of our students I am sure they will blame the students blame the parents and take no accountability for the failures

column1: Our children have all attended public school until they attended BK as freshmen. My children have thrived at BK. There are numerous activities for the students and parents to become involved. The school has a strong strategic plan and is striving to work towards their goals. My children have also participated in the school work study program which has provided them with valuable job skills. I recommend BK to any parent looking for a school that exudes pride, academics, spirituality, community service and personal growth for their student. Bishop Kelly provides a high quality faith based education. They constantly seek to improve on an already excellent education system. Bishop Kelly High School is the best high school in the Treasure Valley and one of the best in the Northwest. Our child loves school, her friends, and the faculty and staff. If you want your teen to feel like part of a real community with great values and opportunities, send them to Bishop Kelly. Great academics, wonderful, caring teachers and administrators, and fantastic parents. Worth every penny (and then some) of your investment of time and money. This is a place where your child will build relationships that will benefit them for life. Bishop Kelly is a learning environment where the whole child can be embraced. Teachers, staff, and administrators are able to meet the needs of students academically, socially, emotionally, and most import...spiritually. Collaboration between home and school is strong which creates a community where everyone works together to meet the needs of the children. Both my children currently attend Bishop Kelly, but before that they had been in public schools their entire lives. This is a GREAT school. The school emphasizes academics, sports, and community service, and is a faith-based school that educates the entire student--body, mind, and spirit. The kids are nice here. The parents are involved. There are high expectations at Bishop Kelly, from parents, teachers and faculty, and though my kids occasionally complain about the dress code and closed campus, they have both thrived at this school, both academically and socially. Great college prep school, great builder of character. My child started as a freshman this year. Overall loves the teachers. Socially it is a different story . My child has never struggled with friendships. However bk is cliquey with a lot of entitled kids . The kids from the Catholic feeder schools are not open and welcoming of new people. Sports have not helped. Unless you are paying the head coach outside of school to be a part of their club team, don't expect your kid to get any attention. My child has spend most days being ignored by peers. This school appears to be more about networking and money then about character development and faith. It's a lot of money to pay for this experience. Awful! 1 star.......I’d give it 0 stars, but it’s probably good that my child spent a year there only to learn how deal with difficult people...a good life lesson that not all schools and/ or organizations are equal. Learning that people can be actually be so ridiculously unreasonable, unfriendly, and cultish is a good eye opener. If you’re thinking that BK is a good school, think again!! Save your money and go to a public school......the schools in Boise are great.......we’ve since transferred to a public high school and couldn’t be happier with our experience and decision to leave BK!!!! My daughter is a St. Mark's alumnus. She chose not to attend Bishop Kelly and attends a different high school. However, she enjoys going to BK games to support the school and spend time with her old friends. Tonight she called me in tears, during the third quarter, to come and pick her up from the game. She was sitting with her St. Mark's friends in the student section and apparently, when a certain BK student found out that Lexie did not go to school there, she started screaming at my daughter to "GET OUT!!!". She kept on screaming at Lexie to the point that half of the student section was all SCREAMING at my daughter to leave. This girl did not know who my daughter was, only that she is not a student of BK. When my daughter became so mortified that she began to walk out of the student section, most of the students there began to APPLAUD that she was leaving. So much for a CHRISTIAN environment. So much for the "SAFE and CARING" place you pretend to provide. I urge you to UPGRADE your teaching instruction on ethics, morality, Christianity and how to possess a basic moral compass! Office staff is rude. A few of the teachers are okay, 2 stars. The leadership (or lack thereof) at this school needs improvement. Phone calls and emails go unanswered. It seems they do not value their "customers" (paying parents) or appreciate parental involvement which I would think a faith-based school would actually encourage! terrible. that’s all i can say about this school. would give 0 stars if i could

column3: Teachers seem to be helpful and supportive. The student body is cliquish and unwelcoming. Discipline against violent acts is not enforced well. Administative staff can be rude and abrupt when issues are confronted. excellent school for helping children with learning needs. The teaching staff is good, but the student body is one of the least mature I have ever seen. They can be very intolerant, probably mostly cause it is a small town and they are not as exposed to differences as some schools. I got along with most teachers, and they were generally found to be very helpful. All in all, its a good school with a poor student body I was assaulted and accosted at this school many times and absolutely nothing was done about it. They didn't even notify my parents. I have a permanent injury disability because of the administration's negligence. I'm not the only one. There are several of us from my peer group who experienced similar situations. Great teachers! But if you are a teacher’s daughter or son, be expected to be treated differently. If you are in sports, expect to be treated based on who you know, not how good you are at the specific said sport. If you aren’t a hill billy trumpy, expect to be treated differently.

column1: Hector High School is more involved and proud of the sports. Athletes are treated specially and the others, such as those in the music programs and art programs are not. Funding goes more to the sports and technology that isn't even used by most of those who don't even need them. We have maybe two teachers in grades 9-12 who requires use of technology for their classes. People get away with having prayer circles and some get away with drug activity. We don't focus more on learning what we need to get a decent score on the ACT, and some of the teachers don't even teach. Teachers pick favorites and they basically let everyone know it. Some of the teachers though, are in understanding of their job. They are there to teach, not be our friends. There is bullying that goes on at the school. I am a victim of it. I have been since I begun in Hector Elementary and no one did anything to stop it even though there is a no bullying policy. I feel that the higher ups need to do their jobs. There aren't very many clubs. They got rid of the chess team and clubs like that. There is Drama club, FBLA, FCCLA, and that is about it. There are no other clubs. How can a student grow without them? They can't. Furthermore, this school sucks and I am glad to be leaving for another high school for my senior year. I love this school I have been here for 9 years going on 10 and I went to pottsville but they failed me because I would not talk and I also went to dover and I learned most of the things that I learned there at hector so I strongly recommend comeing to this school it is great and our sports teams are great
