column1: Both of my children went here, one went on to graduate and get a full scholarship to his first choice school and chosen field. The things they do right: Diversity- From every demographic of life, race, culture, sexual orientation, etc. they celebrate it there. Not only is the student body very diverse, but the staff are as well, and I think that speaks volumes to the kind of school this is. They have fun after school groups that both support the minority group featured, and educate and include the students that are interested, not of that minority. Bullying- They do not tolerate it, period. The staff are very watchful of any behaviors and address it immediately. I only saw one instance in all 6 years I was there, a cyber situation between students, and it was solved swiftly. Every kid I have met there, was happy and felt included. My children were bullied horribly before coming here, to the point that I was truly scared for them, and they blossomed under the support of the staff and the warm inclusivity of the students. Curriculum- They always say, "We don't simply teach art, we use art to teach". This is a very important concept. While they do teach many aspects of art, you will find that art is integrated into almost every lesson, every subject, so the kids not only enjoy it more, they absorb the information better. Also, they have a strong curriculum, but they work very hard to make sure students have all the tools for success, including before and after school tutoring opportunities with each teacher, for one on one assistance. The Staff- I have never seen a group of teachers more involved with their student body. They work very hard to make sure the kids feel seen and heard. School activities- From random fun school-wide events to summer programs designed to help a student toward a career goal, they make sure kids have a good time. My personal favorites are the color wars where the staff join the kids with music, food, games, and powdered pigments flying, or self care night where several rooms in the school become relaxing sanctuaries or lessons in self care. The spa room and animal therapy room are very popular. I could go on for days, but the point is this is a place for kids to grow with grace.

column1: I currently moved into the Massapequa area, but my school district is the Amityville district. In order to give the school a fair chance, I decided to ask for a walkthrough of the high school. My experience was horrible. A great school starts with great leadership and this school has NO LEADERSHIP. The Assistant Principal showed a great deal of disrespect to new parents. I was not only shocked but appalled at his comments. The staff was very friendly, but I was amazed to see the number of students walking in the hallways in comparison to the number students in the classrooms. There are no enforced dress code and conduct policies. It is very upsetting to see students in a beautifully kept environment with no type of formal education being provided. I was informed about the great Catholic Schools in the area from neighboring homes. This school is the greatest school on earth. The teachers work hard and many of them spend afterschool hours helping students. The student body is close knit, and bullying isn't a huge issue. I loved going to this school because of its uniqueness in comparison to other schools on long island. It is predominately a black school, however almost every culture is represented. There are so many wonderful school events and activities. I was president of the class of 2013 and this school undoubtedly had the best impact on my life now as a college student. I loved it here I wish I could go back! Wonderful school. There is a very high number of students who are immigrants and just starting to learn English, hence the low test scores. The teachers are great, and the student body is very close-knit. Wonderful school! Close-knit community, Hardworking teachers who care. A well-organized administration. Respectful student body. My children did excellent here. I have no idea how this school is only a 3, I think greatschools accidentally switched Massapequa HS and Amityville HS scores. Amityville is definitely better. I've had experience with both. Since the new Superintendent has taken over the district 3 years ago, Amityville has the same outstanding curriculum used at some of the top districts on Long Island. We have passed a substantial and historical bond for the first time in memory. The changes in the district are polorizing and everything these kids deserve. I personally moved to Amityville. And I know what it is like to go to top schools and with my current experience in Amityville, it has not been bad at all. I do not believe that the ratings that the school has currently do the school and the students justice. The school is clean, new buildings have been made with new technology and new rooms. The students are nice, and the teachers are also kind. I don't know what the school was like before I moved, but from what I see, Amityville Memorial High School is a functional school that has all of the traits of a 4+ rated school. i go to this school its nice it teaches u alot the teachers are so nice like Periott. and its a very safe place This is a very mediocre high school

column1: Concordia Lutheran High School cares about each student individually. The small class size helps kids get more one on one time with the teacher. The number of activities for the school's size is incredible. Young people can participate in sports ranging from the typical football and basketball to the more unique like lacrosse. They also have an incredible marching band which has been to State six years running taking second place last year. Above all of this, Concordia is a place where faith in Jesus Christ is lived out and taught. Is it a perfect place? No, Does it have its share of issues? Yes, but I love it and would not send my children anywhere else. (btw- I have two there right now) Concordia exceeds my expectations for what I thought I was getting in a high school. Communication with the teachers has been awesome. I never knew how much high school teachers would communicate home to parents. I figured my son would work and I would be left clueless. Not the case here. This is a Christ centered school from its academics to sports. It is great to know others are helping me raise my son with the same morals I am teaching at home. My son is thriving in this environment! Thanks Concordia!!!! Think long and hard before entering your student into this school. While there are some teachers who are absolutely fantastic, there are others who are sub par and that's generous. This school has beliefs on the extremely conservative side. Students with different opinions are put down by faculty and other students. It is almost no different then a public school would be except they lack academically in some areas. It's not fair to be extremely critical because they do have some great teachers and the principal is caring and understanding. iPads are a necessity at the school but are rarely used. There can be a very positive attitude and good feel in the school but other times they are squashed totally by the extreme political views and almost non accepting attitude. It's an okay school with somewhat of a hefty price tag especially when you take into account the lack of some teaching. I received papers from a teacher with a date of 1999. This is a demonstration of how out of date and lack of any effort is out in to the day in and day out education. It could be a great school and recent hires are good teachers. It's the ones who've been there forever who need to be asked to move on. I can only speak to my own experience---didn't have contact with every teacher or subject area. But overall, it's a great school. There are lots of options for honor students, and the typical range of extracurricular activities. I know of some Concordia students who got to college and thought their college classes were easier than their high school classes. If you take college prep type classes, you're going to be well prepared for college. It's definitely not a "name-only" Christian school---faith is an integral part of everything.

Turpin is a excellent school, I would like to say the best in the city and even in the state of Ohio. As a student here you get a great education and the staff is very friendly and helpful, and they will ALWAYS go out of your way to help you with work. Free tutoring after school is always great, plus the many clubs and sports that are diverse/ something for everyone. It is a very challenging school though and offers a variety of classes such as AP and Honors or CP. Turpin is also a Blue Ribbon School which only about 400 schools in the United States have been awarded. Also Turpin is rated Excellent with Distinction 11 years and running by the state of Ohio, and also appears on Best Schools In America Issue every year! I have one 2008 graduate, one graduating in May of '13, and a third child that will be a freshman in '13. Throughout the years, and the vastly different personalities and learning styles of my kids, Turpin has consistently been an excellent school that went above and beyond in meeting their needs. There are all kinds of academic and extra-curricular opportunities. My older kids have been involved in band, tennis team, chess club, drama, the choral groups, and in student leadership capacities. Your student can find their niche at Turpin. The sports programs are top notch, the academics are rigorous, there are clubs and opportunities galore, and not least is the environment of interested and involved administration, teachers, and students, all headed up by the principal, Mrs. Johnson. Parents are welcomed within the community, and there are plenty of ways to get involved. Perfect? No. Outstanding? Yes! Despite it's large size, Turpin was small enough to provide the attention that my son needed. The teachers and adiministration know and care about the kids. They are very focused on the students. I think that's the most important thing. This school is always looking for ways to improve the whole experience. This includes clubs, curriculum, building safety, and positive thinking.

column3: The top students in the school are very solid. The bottom 15% very weak. A very big school which allows for many electives to be offered. Hempfield High School is a great school! I just read a lot of the reviews and I will be honest, I do agree with both the positive and negative comments. The teachers are truely amazing. They honestly do everything they can to prepare us for college. I can't tell you how many times my teachers stand there and telll us about things they did in college and give us assignments that prepare us for what they went through. There are a wide variety of activities and clubs. There is something for everyone. If you can't find something, then you haven't tried or looked hard enough. Yes, we do have some bad kids in our school but you really can't blame the school for that. Last time I checked, it wasn't the school raising the kids and doing all of their decision making. Our faculty and peers do they best they can to try and keep us from making bad life decisions and do as much as they can to help us. We have drug awareness assemblys more than twice a year and there are teen issue seminars offered to help any student who is going through some hard times. I don't know anything in great detail, but I do know our school is doing what they can to make our high school experience the best it can be. Hempfield Area Senior Highschool is the worst school. I was bullied there by football players and they never got in trouble. They ruined my highschool for me and I was held back for no reason. They teachers are awful. Do not go to this school! Horrible because the teachers are ineffective at teaching and the students in the school are toxic and obnoxious. Overall, this school district does a good job academically for students that have the initiative to want to do well and be prepared for life after high school. Those students that do not have the gumption...will fall by the wayside academically. Good academics are one good thing about this school and they do keep bullying under control. However, the district is wrought with politics, nepotism, favoritism, etc.....in other words, the circle is very small. This is most readily apparent with the athletic programs and other extra-curricular activities at the school. Most of the teachers, administrators, coaches, etc. at the school are Hempfield Alum and they help their own fellow colleagues, old school friends kids, siblings of kids they like, etc. get ahead (whether they deserve it or not) over those that are more deserving. Yes, this happens to a certain degree at all schools, but as one Hempfield Administrator I know who has also been at several other schools put it...."yes it is bad everywhere, but it is really bad at Hempfield". If you are looking for a school with good academic opportunities, that is safe and falls more to the "right" and your kid is a go-getter in these areas then Hempfield can be a good school. But if you also want your kid(s) to have a fair opportunity at extra-curricular like drama, student government, athletics, etc.....go somewhere else. Much better options locally and regionally.

column3: Franklin Central is the best High School that I have ever attended. They are very fair and understanding and get to know you as a person. Choose FC as your school choice!!! All 3 of my children have attended Franklin Central Schools. All 3 of them have done well academically. My youngest child has been in the top 10 since first attending the high school. The AP classes have completely prepared her for college, SAT and ACT testing. They keep the parents and students well informed. FC does have challenges just like every school in America created by mixed cultures and negative influences in today's society. I think FC has done an excellent job handling all different types of situations to the best of their abilities. Keep up the great work, parents and students love you. My son is in his first year at Franklin Central; it is simply a fantastic school. I cannot say enough good things about Franklin Township as a whole. My son isn't an athletic type but the school has a great choir and arts program for kids more inclined to like music, arts, band and theater. He also thrives academically and I've never had a problem with any of his teachers. In fact, his gym teacher took the time to call me just to say he had improved a lot since the first of the year. How many teachers bother to call to say something positive? I was recently offered a job out of state but had to decline because I can't be sure we could find a school we like as much in Nashville, TN. I'm here until he's off to college! Most of my life I have spent my school years in the west. I had moved from WA. State after my sophomore year. If you are a parent or student who have just moved from the west to here it's very different. The teachers are amazing, they really know how to help you understand the criteria and help you get through class. The AP classes are wonderful too and really do invite a challenge. This school has the best teachers I've ever met. However on the social aspect it's very difficult. I'm a pretty outgoing person but they way people in the Midwest interact is completely different from the west. I had a hard time adjusting to the people and making friends. This school is also very competitive and you have to be really good at something to get into sports or theater. It's a huge school as well, all my life I've been to smaller schools so it is a big adjustment and it gets scary at times. If anyone is wondering they have a closed campus so you cannot ever leave school unless you are excused and are forced to eat in the cafeteria. Something I didn't like. If you're a person from the west who is used to more open minded, smaller, uncompetitive schools, this is going to be hard. column3: GPHS is a fantastic school with a lot of tradition. The teachers go above and beyond to make sure the students are successful. column1: This school is a hidden gem. It has the best education and one of the highest achievement rates in all of the greater metro. The policies are clear, the curriculum challenging, and the overall attitude positive and safe. They have absolutely no concept of multiple children in one family. They schedule different events, all at the same time. I have missed countless events, trying to get three kids to three different events all scheduled on top of each other. They are going through growing pains, so even schedules change last minute. They need to get some people in here from larger districts to help with growth. They need better communication between all the campuses to avoid scheduling conflicts. The staff needs to be organized, before the teachers can teach in an organized manner. They need to work harder to retain the outstanding teachers. This school has fallen apart - teachers don’t care for students anymore - most have stopped teaching; just turning on videos and ignoring the kids.Super disappointed I live in this district. The school district, as a whole, rates higher than any other in the Austin metro area except for one other, which is much larger. My older children have been more than well-prepared for college. My son is at Texas A&M, and my daughter is at Texas Tech. They have repeatedly said that college is "easier" than high school.My other two children will be in high school this year. I have every confidence that they will be prepared for college as well. Has gone downhill significantly with the overwhelming growth over the past few years. There is a drug problem that seems to be getting worse and school officials do not have it under control. Teachers don’t care about individual students or their grades. If your child requires any help or 1:1 attention, forget it. Excellent school. One of the best in Austin, TX. Teachers are great and helpful to their students. Great extracurricular activities. Two of our daughters have now graduated from Liberty Hill High School. We moved to Liberty Hill when my oldest daughter completed one year of middle school in Austin. Our local elementary school, Casis, was excellent, being a neighborhood school. But in middle school, AISD began bussing children from other neighborhoods and our zoned middle school became a jail more than a school, with knives and guns, fist fights in the cafeteria, violence from students to their teachers, drugs and children having sex on the school bus in the sixth grade, which our daughter demonstrated to us with videos from her phone. She also slipped and fell on a condom and had a concussion. When we complained, no one took our complaints (or those of our neighbors) seriously. Our neighbors sent their children to private school. Since we have seven children, we could not afford to do that and pay for college, so we moved.My daughter gained nothing during her time at O’ Henry, except for fear.My children have attended LIberty Hill Elementary School, Middle School, Junior High and High Schools. My oldest daughter was so grateful to finally feel “safe.” She is now a Senior at U.T. with a 3.9 and says it is “easier” than Liberty Hill H.S. Our next child is a sophomore at Texas Tech and has a 4.0. They both say that they had more rigorous assignments in high school than they do now. Our five other children are still students here.We have noted that people online complain of our “lack of diversity,” and that our lower income students (17%) have not progressed at the state level.That is too bad, but from where we are standing, our children have been, and are being well educated.

column3: Terrible. No one should be subjected to the kind of rampant bullying my son had to experience here. We have switched schools, as Marquette is no place for a child to go. Anyone who truly cares not only about their childs mental health, but overall safety, should not even consider Marquette. I agree with the teacher below when she says Whitefish Bay is truly the best Milwaukee/Wisconsin school. My older daughter attended here, and she has gone on to prosper at Stanford University. As an Alum of MUHS, I can say without question that it was the best thing that has ever happened to me. I know many students and graduates from other schools that had experiences with peer conflicts that never occured at MUHS. I was frequently bullied in grade school and middle school, and MUHS instantly felt like home to me. The brotherhood that is shared between Alum is unlike anything that anyone else can understand, and the faculty and staff do an excellent job of educating the person athletically, artistically, spiritually, and academically. Without MUHS, I am quite sure that my teenage years would have been different for the worse, and I would not be on the path to success that I am on now. As a student, Marquette High has been the best experience of my life. The school not only develops one's intellectual skills, but develops the student as a person who will be serving the community for his life after high school. Through the retreats students are able to bond with their fellow classmates. I was very skeptical to attend an all boys high school, but coming from a co-ed primary school, I feel that I am able to concentrate on my school work and i am able to participate in class without being ostracized for being the "smart one." I fully recommend MUHS for any prospective students and parents. - Member of the Class of 2014 I am of the Class of 2014 and so far, MUHS has been the best fit. Everyone is so welcoming - there is a certain brotherhood here that is just so great I can't explain it. The religious life is amazing but even if you're not Catholic or Christian, you are not discriminated against at all. The academics and extra-curriculars are exemplary. If you're looking for good academics, a strong sports school, and a great service-oriented place, MUHS is the place for you. I know that I will be prepared for the challenges of college in the next 2 years. I am an alumni of this high school and overall as I look back, the school was very good. Just like any other high school, MUHS had its cliques and politics in sports but I think everything was noticed up a couple notches unlike other high schools. Many of the kids care only about their money and do not feel bad to bully nor leave out others intentionally. Many of them speak highly of themselves and solely focus on how the look in daddy's new BMW and their name-brand Lacoste clothing and tan sperry's. As for the academics, you cannot even compare. MUHS prepares students (incl. myself) so well that yes, college IS ACTUALLY EASIER. The teachers put a lot of work and deadlines on the students but it teaches them time management and discipline! Two traits an average college freshman rarely have. MUHS has a ton of opportunities to get involved too. Clubs from chorus, jazz band, scuba diving, spanish and everything in between. The retreats were my favorite part. The teachers do such a great job with them and they teach you to open your eyes, respect and have faith in one another. I'd say MUHS is definitely a great school but isn't as good as some people hype it up to be. My son is a Freshman and he loves it. I know he is in the best place possible. The teachers are as good as any college professors I had. He is growing academically, spiritually, athletically, and socially. They really do help "good boys to become great men!" Marquette High School is unlike any other school in the sense that we focus on being a COMMUNITY. Marquette helps all the kids that enter it by making them feel comfortable in this new environment through retreats and other programs. The sports teams are good, and there is a non-cut sport for every season, so you can always be active. There are a lot of clubs ( a lot more than listed on this website), so no matter what your son is into or what type of person he is, there is definitely a club that suits him. The academics are probably the main highlight at this school. The teachers prepare their students unbelievably well through challenging course work. Overall, Marquette continues to be a great school in every aspect. My son is a freshman this year (class of 2020) and is enjoying his 1st year, he seems to be maturing into a fine young man, and I think MUHS is part of that process. Homework is not excessive, and the clubs (robotics and after school weightlifting) that he has joined are very good. The Tuition is a bit of a struggle, but I think its worth it. This school has been helpful in many aspects. It sets you up for a real working environment and never fails to educate you. I'm an alumni from the early 90's. They had an amazing approach to developing the future leaders of the area. The mentoring received from the teachers carried me for the rest of my life. A Half Century After Enrollment, Family Still Deriving Value from an MUHS Education. I need to belatedly thank Marquette High for the incalculable support the school has given our family, particularly this past Summer. Back in 1970, as our Dad struggled to find a way to pay for our older brother to attend MUHS, we all knew it would be worth it. But, we had no clue just how much. This past Summer, we lost that brother, John '74. Through his life, he encountered more than his share of challenges, and failed to keep up with his MUHS friendships. Very fortunately, Fr. Doug Leonhardt, SJ '56 – who had been Principal John’s senior year - heroically tracked John down. In John’s final days, Father Leonhardt ministered to him and then arranged for a funeral Mass to be celebrated at the Jesuit community chapel at St. Camillus. We were further buoyed that many Hilltoppers from John’s era joined us on that dreary day. Almost two dozen came from all over the country. Some of my favorites were those who'd never been close to John, but were nonetheless intent on paying respects to a wonderful guy who had carried a heavy cross. This experience of Hilltoppers helping us endure that day was transformative. It was a bulwark of brotherly support and brought about needed peace for our family. We are ever indebted to Marquette High.

column1: This school is by far one of the best in the area. While they cannot offer a giant variety of programs, they are dedicated to the quality of what they do offer. The teachers are excellent and really do care about the students. The average class size is right around 26, though many I have taken are much smaller. Most of the students who go here have gone to school with each other for most of their lives and those who haven't have no trouble making friends. Mrs. Anderson and Mr. Charbonneau (Math & Science respectively) are exceptional teachers who make this school a great place to be. This school offers a multitude of activities for all students--from athletics, to hands on robotics, engineering and wood/metalworking activites, to FBLA, ASB, drama, music, and others! It offers many different courses and college credit can be earned in high school upper division science, social studies, music, math and English courses. The current principal is highly supportive, as is district administration. For a smaller school, Zillah High School has a reputation of offering a lot to its students in a quality manner. It is also the home of the National Teacher of the Year for 2013! The best part about this school is its committment to building relationships with every kid. There are programs for all kinds - and the staff seem like they are always willing to work with the kids. Check out the graduation rate - above 95% for several years in a row. They are doing good things for kids! I love that this school has so much to offer students academically and socially. I have children with varying interests, and they are all able to find many activities to be involved in. I also love how well the teachers are willing to work with parents and students to achieve the students goals.

column1: I attended Mt. Carmel from 2001-2005 and I loved every minute of it. Was it challenging? Yes. Was I stressed out sometimes? Yes. Did I always get along with every girl there? No. However, those are all normal parts of high school. Students are suppose to be challenged! It helps them learn how to work hard and achieve goals. When I attended MCA there were approximately 1200 girls in school there. You aren't going to get along with every. That is just a part of life. I think that is an important lesson to learn early on. That being said, I made some of the best friends I'll ever have during my time at MCA. I found the teachers to be extremely interested in our progress and in our well-being. However, they do not baby you. If you are struggling they expect you to seek them out for help. There is ample time throughout the school day and after school to do this. I never had any problems with getting help from a teacher when I needed it. I am now a teacher can appreciate how much work goes into creating an environment like the one at Mt. Carmel. Sr. Camile Ann is an amazing woman and role model and I wish I could work for a principal like her! She believes in her students and staff! The girls are fake and there is a lot of superficial and materialistic people in that school. To belong, you have to have what it takes to be like the rest of the girls there. If you don't, you're not going to feel welcomed. This academy is the best private school in Louisiana for girls. Taught in the Catholic tradition with academic excellence as the aspiration while still providing multiple opportunities for all. The school values and protects its rich tradition and diverse opportunities for all. The leadership at Mount Carmel is stellar. Mount Carmel, is led by Sr. Camille Anne Campbell, whose guidance has made MCA the academically superior choice. I highly recommend it if values and education are both important characteristics sought in the education of your child. I am a graduate of MCA, and I really can't say one truly negative thing about my school. I'm from an average, middle class household, and i never experienced any of of snobbery or bullying that is being suggested in the comments. The school has so much to offer, and the faculty and staff are truly dedicated to helping each girl be the best she can be in every aspect of her life. Of course, things aren't perfect. There may be an occasional bad teacher or mean girl, but I don't know of a school without these things. The curriculum can be difficult at times, but that is a part of high school, and I've found that working this hard in high school has prepared me for college, as well. MCA is also very focused on spirituality. I wouldn't be the Catholic woman I am today had i not gone there. I am incredibly proud to tell people where I graduated from, and I hope that if/when I have girls, they will choose to go to MCA as well. I attend Mt. Carmel and I absolutely love it! I met so many new friends here. At first, I was really scared to go to an all girl school because I thought that there would be so much drama, but there actually isn't really any drama here at MCA. Also at MCA there's so many fun events such as spirit day, but at the same time we learn a lot. The school can definetly be challenging at times, but it's manageable. If I could pick another high school to attend, I would still pick MCA! When I first heard about Mount Carmel, I thought I am definitely going there. Then I had my spend a day. My tour guide kept leaving me behind and I couldn't catch up to her. The hallways were not really filled with laughter and joy but either way I still went here. Honestly I think it was the worst mistake of my life. People bully others and girls do things that they shouldn't. My cousin even suffered terribly there. I honestly don't think it's the school for me anymore. Worst place I have ever experienced. Awful environment for young women terrible girls were mean, super easy had no challenge sports coaches were rude I attended this high school for 3 years, going on my 4th, and then decided I had to leave. This is the worst environment I have ever been placed in. This place made me believe bullying, eating disorders, disrespect, and the use of religion as excuses for unacceptable actions was something normal in society. This place tries to brainwash their students and is completely unprepares kids for the realities of the world. After my own experiences and plenty of money spend following on counseling and mental health medication due to this place, I suggest going to a public school such as Ben Franklin or Haynes. Both of these places are academically superior to Mount Carmel and will not have such a damaging effect on your child. Please, please, please consider this advice, I am only trying to warn future students from the trauma this school results in. I am not only speaking for myself, as I also know of at least 7 other girls in my grade who experienced such trauma from this school they were placed in in-patient mental health institutions, so if you don't believe me at least look at the numbers and give it some type of reflection.

column3: Teachers care enough but the administration cares only about appearance. If you require any extra help as a result of ADHD, anxiety, ect. the admin won't even make an attempt to hide their agenda; running you out of the school. What an amazing community! We could not be happier that we chose this neighborhood and school. It's now our second year at Saguaro, and we're off to a great start. My daughter has everything she needs on her schedule (after a little bit of reworking) and has her honor classes. She enjoys dance company , which is great... and will be going on a trip to New York with her dance company. It's never easy for our kids to navigate through high school, but I know she has the support to be a success. It is exactly what each student makes of it, up to the student to keep up with their assignments and become the student they need to be.So glad she loves her school. I want to start out by saying that I attended Saguaro in high school and I loved it so much that I wanted my now highschool aged daughters to attend. I now feel responsible for the bad experience that my daughter and I have been through with the Administration. After researching previous post, I am informed that exactly what I thought is true, if your child has any type of need or "issue", saguaro will do whetever they can to get your child out of their way!! Saguaro is known for their sports, mostly football and they do go above and beyond for the football players, which is great if your child plays football, but in the case that they don't play, don't expect any help from the admin in any way. My daughter had an encounter with the principal along with a few other students, one of which did the same thing as my daughter, however my daughter got kicked out of Saguaro and put in the SOL program, online learning through Scottsale schools. I wont go into too many details, but what we have been put I feel that Saguaro High and especially its math and science program is a hidden gem. All of my daughters teachers are excellent. Some of them even go above and beyond by attending various school and community events (out side of school) that their students are involved in. The math and science program is strong and hopefully with time it will contiune to grown stronger and become better recognized. I feel that Saguaro deserves a better rating/ ranking than this site is giving it. I would rate it as one of the better schools in the Phoenix metro area and I am a picky parent. Honestly hands down best school around. The staff actually care about their students unlike Chaparal! The student body is friendly and amazing to new students. The staff are amazing with helping your child integrate into the school. A++++ Since covid hit this school has declined a significant amount. I am a current student here (class of 2022). It was never this bad. I don't know how anyone could take pride in being associated with this place. It's disgusting how people treat each other here. The teachers are for the most part good, but the security is has been understaffed lately (understandable). So that excuses the literal moshing in the lunch line. I am reminded every day in the lunch line, that my voice does not matter to the EIGHT people I've talked to about being assaulted in the lunch line. That's understandable though cause you're understaffed, right? Dear staff, I apologize for bothering you in the first place.

My grade had students going around school making written death threats, and when a physical paper with death threat was brought forward, the main girl involved saw no punishment, yet when I stood up to this girl and called her a name OUTSIDE OF SCHOOL HOURS, OUT OF SCHOOL GROUNDS, I was SUSPENDED for “bullying”, and lost almost a week of school right before finals week. The teachers are rude, and contribute to the bullying half of the time. When there was a mixup with my sisters IEP transferring her file from the middle school to highschool, they refused to help us, and my sister lost all of her resources she had.I would not let my kids near this school with a ten foot pole. They are a narrow minded school, who ostracizes any student who doesn’t fit their idea of a “perfect” student, because all they care about are test scores to make them look good.

column3: This is a great school. My son will be graduating this year and his counselors have been VERY helpful with college scholarships and filling out applications. It is because of his great education in the Cedar Falls School District (which has earned him good grades and a great ACT score) that he will be going to college and will not have to take out any loans. The school calls me if I forget to call when he is going to miss school. I can check online at any time and see what his grades are and if he is handing in assignments. I can not say enough good things about the schools in Cedar Falls! We moved here from Texas and had no idea where to enroll my son in 11th grade-so happy we ended up in this school district-he loves this school!!! We moved here from a small town full service high school. Peers groups are better, teacher quality is roughly the same and administration and support are rigid, unfriendly, uncoordinated and difficult. Overall, it was an always safe environment, with a passionate staff of educators. Infrastructure wise, it shows its age.

column1: I am graduating senior of Thomas Edison (Class of 2018) and all I have to say is: if you are truly interested in one of the CTE programs that Edison has to offer, you will most likely enjoy your experience here. However, if you are a very high-achieving, ambitious student (probably someone who is interested in attending a top-tier university like the Ivy League later on) then I would highly suggest not attending this school, for Edison does not provide enough resources for "the best and brightest" students to truly shine and excel academically. I am currently a senior at this school. This school is not as good as it used to be from when my brother went to this school. The school is dirty, roaches and mice in classrooms and locker rooms. The girl's locker room, before the school, allowed girls in the '70s was a storage room. This is not ideal because there are always a lot of girls in the gym class. Some classes are unnecessary, especially regents courses even after you have already received your five regents credits. This school also does not ready you for college. So if you are passionate about your shop class, then you would be fine in the future but if you're not, then this school will most likely not be for you. Edison is inconsistent and unorganized. And the school board is sometimes not on top of things. My shop class was changed over 3 times for some odd reason which really made me lose disinterest in the shop class. So choose your shop class WISELY. Terrible. Issue after issue kept piling up. I did have VERY few teachers that got back my well-deserved credit and got me transferred out. It's all love for the staff there. Change your rubric, have security at the park consistently afterschool. Students who attend PM school should not have their grades be determined via quizzes and exams. They have already been there from 8-3, now students are there for an extra 2 hours. Burnt out. Give em classwork. Determine their grades via determination. I mean, what else can I say? It's not gonna do anything. Each class will continue to have different rubrics, and time will go on, I guess. Just know, those failures have a mental effect on students. Adios amigos.Yours trulyThe king of New York Terrible, the school is great academically for those who influence themselves. Yet most students here aren't encouraged to do their work. Rather they take the easy way out. Unless the principal takes better action in connecting with the student then I can see Edison evolve. For now it is declining, you should visit to and verify. love it, school so pretty school offers really cool stuff

column3: Would love to send my kids to WTHS. I am very unhappy with the local school that they are in now. LArge school with a lot to offer kids. Great teachers and a great Ap program. Teachers care about the kids and the school system in Washington Township gets parents involved. Kids are encouraged to become involved in the community. My Daughter loves the High School and has done well in and out of the classroom. With a tough workload and plenty of activity after school she is kept busy, too busy to find herself bored. She has scored well on all placement tests. Like anything, if the parents are invovled and the students are responsible thay can excel! School sports are run by politics. If you are not well connected your child will not play sports here no matter how talented he is. Sad. My child is an honor roll student and excels at baseball, but we are transferring him to GCIT so he can have the opportunity to play sports. Great school as long as your kid doesnt need any special attention academically. If they are an honors student they should have no problems. If they need anything extra by way of support academically they wont get it here. The politics within the sports program is the most disgusting thing ive ever seen. So blatant that they favor much less talented kids whos parents are affiliated with the school. Shameful TWP!!!! The Principal, Joseph Bollendorf is actively involved and interacts on a personal level with the student body gaining their respect and loyalty. During his tenure he has exponentially increased the student scholarships through his solicitation of local businesses, clubs and scholarship funds. He instills a sense of pride within the student body to the point that they refer to their school simply as "Township". TWP, "Together With Pride". The academic resources, activities, clubs, sports and music program are all there for the taking. The only prerequisite is that the students choose to engage and get involved themselves to take advantage and make the most of their time to really benefit from being a TWP alumnus. This is where you the parent and your child must take responsibilty yourselves to proactively make most of the time spent here to ensure a bright future. Largest athletic program in SJersey and head football coach won't go the extra yard to help a player get to the next level. Needs to take a page from Timber Creek and Woodbury. Title of Head football coach comes with personal responsibility, but Instead this coach turns his back and feels he owes his kids nothing which is exactly what he gives them. Parents of talented young football players better explore all options before intrusting your son to this program! Where are your NCAA DI players? On the sidelines or flunking out and being ignored. I am currently a student at twp class of 2013. Being that I am about to graduate having being at this school is bitter sweet. Academically the school is 4 stars IF you have a child that catches on fast. Alot of the teachers dont go out of their way to help your child learn. When they are ready to move on their going to move on wether the children tknow the lesson or not.. Not saying all the teachers are bad because I did have great teachers that I instantly connected with and learned alot from. As for sports twp takes that super serious especially for the sports they feel are most important such as cheerleading, football , and basketball. I know for a fact that they do grimey things with in the sports department too.. And they also favor other sports over others. As for students the kids are just plain mean if your kid is not strong minded, and asertive, or at least gives off the appearance of being that sort your child will be eaten alive. Some of the stuudents there even get to the point where they harrass people that are different.. the only thing about this school that is five stars is the school spirit. Twp pride is the best. No school has as much pride as twp in my opinion. As I read some of the negative reviews I can't help but think mabey they just can't be pleased. Let me touch on a few of the negative comments; don't kid yourself if you think drugs aren't readily available and used at all schools. If your child needs academic support there are more than enough counselors and teachers that will go out of their way to make sure he or she succeeds. Is your son or daughter an athlete? Be prepared to sit or get cut to make room for a more talented player. In other words the best athletes play, no politics involved. Even as a senior, don't get comfortable with your spot you have to earn it every week. Alumnus here, parents need to realize and relate to their children that their high school experience will be molded by what they do in middle school. In order to really get ahead academically you need to push your kid to get them into the advanced classes (starting in 7th grade). Do this and the AP program will offer them the opportunity to get into top colleges. Every year this school sends the students who focused on academics to some of the top colleges in the country. What the kids do there is up to them... If your kid wants to play a sport they need to work on that sport starting early in middle school in order to have a shot at playing at WTHS. I remember a few students who did not make the transition from WT middle schools to WTHS because they understood the depth charts/ how large the school is and understood that if the most important thing to them was having their kid start their freshman year WTHS is probably not for them. While at WTHS i can say I only had one bad teacher the whole time. I had an administration, athletic, and guidance department that helped me get into a great school. High school like life is what you make of it, teach your kids to make it out. Both my kids graduated from college thanks in large part to the great teachers at Washington TWP. HS. WTHS is an exceptional school with high academic standards. They offer various extracurricular activities that cater to a variety of students. They have excellent sports teams with dedicated coaches. In my four years at the school, it was an overall incredible experience that greatly prepared me for the future. Some teachers are god awful and don't know how to teach. Students stay in their own groups, and don't expand their horizons. Many students have no academic integrity, and find answers to online quizzes and share homework answers. Students will also help students in later classes with quiz answers. I’m a 2018 graduate and WTHS is the best school I’ve ever been to. Most of the teachers go above and beyond to help students. The administration is involved and personable. The rules are very fair, and the administration actually takes the students opinions into consideration. There is a great variety of classes that are offered. I always said if this school offered a degree program I’d stay for college in a second. The school pride bonds everyone together. If you take advantage of all the school has to offer you will be pleased Excellent. I would not change it for the world. This is a great school! Great students, and staff!

column1: This school need to expand because overpopulation of students and these students need to stop being so racist to one another, they need security outside after school to crack down the trouble teens plus this school need more activities and more sports to do after school. My daughter graduated from here, June 2013. She had a good time here. The school is for average students. A few honors and A.P classes are offered. Not too many sports or clubs. There aren't any fighting allowed nor gangs so the school is pretty safe. CHSAS is very diverse and small, only 500 students cap. My daughter is now a freshman at Western Illinois University and she is doing really well. Overall, the school fit her academic needs. If youhave a above average/gifted child, this isn't the school for them but if your child is average learner and you are looking fora diverse and safe school, then consider Ag Sciences. I am currently a senior at CHSAS. The school in these past 4 years has been good. Before getting accepted to CHSAS, I had either the option of going to lane tech or bogan. I was waiting to see if I had another other accepting high schools, and that's when CHSAS had accepted me. There is a variety of sports now. I have participated in soccer, football, and volleyball. The sports are going up in competition, especially the volleyball teams. Academic wise, the classes are well. They leave homework almost every night, but not to the point where you are very stressed out. I am ready to graduate from CHSAS and start a new chapter in my life. Graduated in 2009 and CHSAS gave me scholarships and pushed me to apply and then later receive scholarships for college. Fortunately, I continued my higher education with agriculture at Illinois State University. I would say CHSAS is for the MOTIVATED "average student" and for the ABOVE average student. Every year CHSAS has more and more seniors getting accepted to Ivy League schools with scholarships....overall the school is safe, challenging , and EXTREMELY hands on. i can't understand why this school does not provide books especially in critical areas, like math. can some explain to me why these kids are working from work sheets instead of a book. becuase of this, i can not rate this school high. the school is great in every other way. Fighting is up, wish the school can expel the problem kids (a handful, but the handful disrupt the whole). last a week a senior jumped on a freshman (something that started on the bus, according to my daughter). the senior was wrong and should be made an example of, there is no reason, none for jumping on a freshman, zilch. Inner city school brought to a nice neighborhood. Lot of fights, zero discipline and an apathetic principal who can't be truthful. No books for many classes, teachers out for weeks at a time and mist can't control the kids they are teaching. Pay the money and send kids to private schools. Learning about commas and quotation marks in high school? School out of control. All this business about good opportunities...garbage. My other child has many more opportunities at private school...which is exactly where my child is going this year. They will get into U of I with a low ACT though....Just go in through school of agriculture...Anyone can do it....not just ag kids...BIG SECRET.My niece did! Teachers are unbelievably uncaring and do not care. Kids out of control...no one cares. Free trips....well that is why CPS is broke...maybe they should use some of that money and invest it in education. Drive by the school at dismissal and you will see the crowds. Fist fights in halls all the time. No one stops them. Security guard stands and watches it. This school is a mockery of the education system. Shame on them. The kids are smoking hookah walking down the hall changing classes. No needs to do homework...or study for tests....the teachers don't care one bit. The difference in the private school this year is shocking. There is actual teaching and so many things to be a part of. You can actually join sports and the coaches show up to practice. There is Christianity. What a sad reflection of the times this school is. The Ag is creating an environment that shows kids that you just can skate by and not be accountable...no need to do what is required. You can do the bare minimum and be top of the class. Truly...pay the tuition for a private school or move to the suburbs if you want a quality education and a dignified school that your child can be at a place where they are shown respect and expected to perform and reach their highest expectation. I truly worry for the kids stuck here. Such a pity. Parents...do your research....this school is a mockery. I have been in the education field for 20+ years...I know how it is supposed to be...this is not it. I am currently a freshman at CHSAS and I would like to say the information reported in the reviews is exceptionally false. For starters, students do not smoke on school premises. I know ths for a fact considering there has been a time whereas a student attempted to have a cigarette outside of the school, and was later suspended because of this. Another issue I would like to address is the Spirit Week problem. There were no eggs or vegetable oil and whoever is claiming that there was is untruthful. Prior to Spirit Week, rumors circulated about what were to happen. Friday of Spirit Week, the only thing that was done was glitter and silly string being thrown at all students, not just freshmen. Of course there was the traditional "Go Home, Freshmen" chant, but that happens in every school (I attended Marist's Spirit Week last year for shadow day). As far as the "Teachers and staff do't care about students" claim, that is also false. If your grades have declined or are declining, you will be advised to speak with he academic counselor. Tutoring is offered afterschool and teachers are willing to stay afterschool to help if need be. So far, however, there has been one physical altercation which was soon handled by security and the principal. If the student population is too large, compare it to Marist whereas there are over 1,000 students. The principal also teaches a class to upperclassmen in need of help. Chsas even offers a mentally disadvantaged department for students and other students are very friendly and welcoming to them. At lunch, you'll see students chatting and laughing with them as well. In conclusion, the choice for your child to attend Chsas is up to you, however, don't base it off of false information from those who have never even attended/ been to the school.

column1: Excellence, opportunity and community! Our teachers have provided our children with top notch academics paired with winning sports teams! Former student here..........the school is not to bad....great students.....great teachers......the environment is good. However, it's not for everyone. They give alot of homework and focus too much on academics. Definitely great for those who wish to pursue academic careers such as medicine and law, but it is definetely not for those who want to pursue non-academic careers such as arts, music, or sports. The bullying program in place is not very effective. Perhaps they should consider revising it. I go to this school. I have classes all over the building, so I know what are the classes around me are like. The teachers are really great. They teach well, and I think about 99.9% of the students will succeed, there will always be those several few who just hate everything in life. The only thing I don't like is the amount of homework given, it's too much. This however is good for the students, it's practice for quizzes and tests. The exam passing rate is quite high, higher than the surrounding schools. I really like this school, it's great academically, musically, and with sports. It's an awesome school with awesome people, and if you are considering someone to go here, it's a good choice. My school(new berlin eisenhower) is an OK school. Administration definitely plays favorites with the students. Some teachers are amazing while another's treat you like your nothing and give you no respect. I definitely wish their was more authority in school because their are several high schoolers and middle schoolers that are doing drugs openly but our school resource officer does not know. Academically the school is very hard and strong. You need to make sure you are doing homework. Which will definitely help with bringing your grades up The least understanding and helpful school you can imagine. Anyone who does not fit in to the exact mold of a perfect student is persecuted. The biggest bullies in the school are the administration, and the ACT scores are all that matter. I'm a former student of this school who graduated a few years ago (2013). While Eisenhower has talented teachers who truly care about the students, administration is enforcing stupid policies and rules that inhibit students from learning. Teachers are required to attend pointless meetings that cut into the amount of time teachers would normally spend helping students, causing the most talented and compassionate teachers to leave the school. Administration only cares about the school's image and not about individual students. If you're a student who makes them look good to the public, they love you. Being what you might call a "high achieving student," I saw first hand that when I did something recognizable, administration was all over it. As soon as it died down, it was like I didn't even exist. The school needs more classes and resources to prepare students for the real world, especially since most students in this district have no idea what it's like to take care of themselves. College is going to knock most of these kids to the ground. Overall, poor policies and attitudes result in discouraged teachers, negative students, and an overall worsening experience. This rating is regards to the new Standards Based grading system. Several classrooms were used as pilots for this new system that will be fully implemented next year. Our experience to date has been horrible. While in theory this system may sound good, but the inconsistency in how teachers interpret the 1-4 grading system is all over the place. It is almost impossible to achieve an A now. All grades are subjective to a teacher's opinion. Expect GPA's to fall and for students and parents to become very angry, upset and discouraged. The school is using the students as test subjects for a poor system that will take away our kids ability to qualify and obtain scholarships, as well as be able to choose colleges that they would like to attend. This system needs to be adjusted to better fit a High School atmosphere. This is not grade school. Why can't New Berlin understand our concerns and take responsibility for the stress they are causing and how they are destroying opportunities for students? Until other school districts are on board and this system and standards based grading is recognized, this is a disaster! Scholarships and colleges base their decisions on a student's GPA. That's the bottom line. This whole thing makes me sick to my stomach and I wish I would have never moved into the district. Anyone else experiencing this or have concerns? Amazing, this school is great at helping The school is definitely good and they make sure to give all students a challenge and things but the administration just needs to care more and really applaud every student no matter if they have a low GPA or what. Each student needs to be recognized- this could have stopped so many things to happen, including the terrible and tradgic incident that happened in late November/ early December of 2017. Come on Lions, we can do better than this. The School is above average at education and It shows on the test scores #3 currently in the state. The school inside is very boring and could use some updating. The sport teams are good too! Overall this school is good if you want your child to be successful. :) I am a parent of 2 children who attend Ike and are polar opposites of each other (1 senior and 1 freshman). They are each doing great in their classes and we have been luck to have had teachers every year that really take the time to make sure that they are learning the material. The majority of the teachers will go above and beyond to help the students and take extra time out of their day to tutor. This school does a great job of celebrating academic achievements NOT just sports like many neighboring districts. The overall atmosphere of the school is positive but in reality we are dealing with teenagers so it will never be perfect. We specifically bought in New Berlin so that we could enroll our kids into Eisenhower and we don't regret it for a second.

column1: Best high school in houston!! Academics,Extracurriculars, and Athletics are the best in the distict. I am proud to call this my school. Travis is a wonderful sschool. Teachers aren't taking responsibility for their mistakes and are just blaming kids on it. The only thing this school is proud of is their diversity, not how good the education is. This school is fine as long as you find your place. I do wish they placed more emphasis on college, prior to the senior year. It's too late then. I have two students at Travis and they are both being challenged academically and are involved in several extracurricular programs. We love Julie Diaz! I would rate my experience at this school very high and would recommend anyone to Travis high school myself I am a student there with learning differences and Travis makes me feel so welcome and love like I'm not different I would really say any parents child would feel safe loved and cared for and truly not like you are different It's a great school. A place for everyone -- a club for everyone. Most diverse in the area and students get a long so well. The school in a way is what you make of it. The friends you keep and the classes you chose to take but the culture of the school, such as the clout chasers or the student athletes make the school mentally draining with also takes a toll on physical health. I have meet some amazing people here, both students and teachers but i wish that they would care a little bit more about mental health. Make an effort to actually include all students and incorporate the diversity within the school. Teach us more about college before we reach senior year, before its too late to do anything. I also wish that the mentoring system that they have in place AKA 'AMBUSH' did more then just 'habitudes' that barely anybody watches and especially on the most irrelevant things. I wish that the system was more geared towards helping the freshman invest their time in something that will help them further in life. The clubs that we have on campus i wish that they weren't a 'paid membership' and that there was more to them then how much money you could put back into the school. there are so many things that i wished that the school could have done for me but unfortunately fell short of greatness. This school has so much potential to create powerhouse students if only they invested the amount of money that they put into sports into getting new textbooks or other activities that the students could participate in. column3: I have two kids in West High School. My son is in chess club and my daughter is in cross-country. Neither of them could enjoy school more. There are over 2000 kids currently enrolled in this high school, so there are enough kids of each personality type that most everyone can find friends. For example, my son, who is on the autism spectrum, has never had a problem being bullied and is very happy with the level of social acceptance he finds. The teachers represent the whole range from good to bad, as well. The level of parent involvement - as well as the overall culture of this part of Madison - is great. Full disclosure: West also has one of the highest achievement gaps in the country. It's also probably the most liberal: largest Freedom from Religion club, Marxist Club through to Young Progressives but no Young Republicans Club. Required reading in Eng Lit = book on the expriences of 6 African-American women (2 of whom are lesbians). There's a place for everyone but the vocal diversity is significanly skewed left. Just so you know. My kids are attending. There are a lot of professors' kids at West, and that makes it academically challenging, which is good. It is an extremely liberal school, which can make it tough on a kid from a moderate home. There is a strong bias among the faculty for liberal causes, which permeates the curriculum. US History for example is the history of the civil rights movement, heavy with scorn for traditional figures and the US government in general - Howard Zinn is revered and his works are required reading. Similarly, US literature is the literature of minority writers espousing favored political causes at the expense of commonly accepted literature. It's something to consider if you are not far left. This school is overloaded with kids. The school has kids from Verona, Middleton, etc. in one small ish building. The building is very old and dirty with a lack of resources. There are smart students and a lot of students get very good test scores and earn high grades but this is because most of these children come from backgrounds of academic success, ex. professors or doctors as parents. There is a large achievement gap because the students who are underprivileged do not get the resources that they need at this school and do not learn at home as much as the wealthier students. Most students skip a lot of classes and there is a heavy amount of drug usage and drug dealing on school property with little done about it. The math and science departments are very weak and it is easy for students to fall behind. The school is overall too small to accommodate so many students and pulls statistics from its smartest to make it appear as though this were a very good school when it is in fact quite average. I moved to Madison last year, and my son who's a sophomore currently attends this school. So far, I have been pleased with this school and its curriculum. As the other reviews have stated, it is an ultra-liberal school, which is VERY TYPICAL for Madison and not a personal issue for me. I want my child to be exposed to different world reviews and to have a heightened cultural awareness in a society where other ethnic backgrounds are frowned upon. Extremely terrible. I would gave given the school a 0 if that was an option. If you have children with special needs and you are a minority, stay away from this school!

column1: Our son is going to be a sophomore in the 2011/12 school year. His freshman year went great. We've been happy with how he's doing academically, and the teachers have been communicative and supportive. As an involved parent and one who does her best to be supportive of my child's education, I can tell you that this school's administration is crummy! The AP classes are given the poorest teachers. I'm sure the thought is that these students will be fine, and they generally are. They are used to being responsible for their own education. The admin. has its own agenda and it does not involve supporting the education of students or the education goals of the teachers. Most of the admin. and staff do not support extracurricular activities if they are not sports and are often rude to students looking for support. Many of the teachers try to do well by their students but they are overworked and receive very little support from the admin., other than the activities director, who is also incredibly overworked! Parent support is not the challenge here. It's going to take a complete overhaul of the administration and a willingness to dismiss dysfunctional staff to change what is wrong with this school! Sure, my kid will go to a great college, however, she is a strong student. I'd hate to be a student who is not good at managing his or her own education and be at this school! This is a great high school which great facilities. They have a great football program and a recently upgraded stadium. They also offer a great band program. worst school in the bay go to los gatos. leigh needs money, so they can make the school better!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Wonderful high school. Excellent instructors and highly esteemed sports teams. Teachers are very supportive and highly educated. 1 counselor per 900 students, administration is non-responsive regarding individual students issues. Was a great school 10 years ago. Wouldn't recommend Leigh for 2014. Needs new management and new Honors level teachers. I hope that these parents that post negative comments about Leigh High school are going directly to the Principal, Administration Offices and the District Superintendent to register their complaints. In addition, If all parents participated/supported the school and communicated with the above contacts this would help the school to improve in the right direction. Parent participation is not high at this school in comparison to other High API scoring schools nearby. Are you participating and contributing to making this a better school? A grandparent of a student at Leigh High. Out of the 3 high schools I've been to, Leigh is by far the best one! The teachers I am fortunate enough to have are caring & for the most part good at what they do, with a few exceptions. Unlike a lot of the schools in the Bay Area, Leigh trusts their students enough to provide them with lockers which I believe says a lot. Because of the nice facilities, outstanding teachers, and tremendous amount of school spirit, every student at Leigh is privileged to go to such a fantastic school. Even though this is a large high school, it has a small school feel. The teachers are great and have a geniune sense of community and care for our students. Leigh High School is currently going through administrative changes. This is good as the past four years have been less than stellar for the staff and the students. Despite any glowing reviews posted, Leigh is not a good environment for students that are unable to be self-taught or independent learners. Departments are constantly changing their rules and processes. The Math department is horrible. There are only two teachers truly qualified to teach. The rest could care less about being there or take any interest in their students. Consistency does not exist. I would highly recommend reconsidering sending your children to Leigh. Attend both school and District meetings to get a better understanding. Ask recent grads and parents before you send your children to this school. The reviews describing Leigh High school's management are spot on. My son attended Leigh 08-12. The staff do their best and many are very good. But the poor leadership has created an evironment that keeps quality education mediocre at best. My son was accepted some very good universities but still struggled as a freshman. He is a junior now and is thriving now and on track to graduate on time thanks to his own hard work. The folks who give this school 5 stars are not seeing the whole picture. The administrative change occurring at Leigh is validation of this review and other sub-standard reviews. Leigh has been a very good school in years past and I believe it will be again one day. I believe the school staff tries but they are short staffed and seemed to be overwhelmed. I have a son with a moderate learning disability. Unfortunately, he has fallen through the cracks and not received the instruction needed. Each teacher uses school loop differently, if they use it all, which makes it extremely difficult for a parent to help their child stay on top of tasks. We are very happy now with new principal, Kara. I rate it an 11! Leigh High is now ranked in top 100 schools in California in the US New rankings of US schools. CUHSD needs to now remodel and upgrade the school. HVAC and bathrooms are broken. Tax payers passed a bond measure in 2016. Have not seen any upgrades to Leigh High. FIX IT BEFORE IT BREAKS DOWN. US News ranked top 10% High School -- for AP/honors/college prep it should rate far higher -- dig into the scores -- Leigh is the among the best available large HS in the California Public School system, similar to Saratoga or Los Gatos. BASIS kids go here to do AP Calc and finish High School. Excellent teachers, variety of course selections, well maintained facilities, and great learning environment. Leigh is a very average school I would say. I'm not impressed by how utterly gross the bathrooms are. Graffiti, dirt, pee on the ground, truly unsanitary. Also, the school is obviously in need of money. When SJ & LG had horrible air quality, most school districts shut down for about a day, although, Leigh did not shut down, and we all had to go to school wearing masks in the horrible air quality. Not impressed :/ Great school, great principle, lots of improvements. Top school in the bay area. Good facility. Nice teachers. Great curriculum. Students are motivated to learn.

column3: My daughter graduated last year with all kinds of honors. The facilities are not new and state of the art, but a good education is there for those who want to go after it. The teachers and admin. tend to take a special interest in those that do and really try to help. Per an article in the Hawaii Tribune Herald, dated July 2, 2013, "Pahoa High and Intermediate School leads Big Island schools in the number of cases of serious misconduct committed by students over the last five years. Between July 1, 2007, and June 30, 2012, Pahoa students tallied a total of 1,663 Class A and Class B offenses of the state s administrative rules Chapter 19, which governs student misconduct and discipline." - Doesn't sound too good. The Principle, Darlene Bee has broken the trust of parents and students by not following the Chapter 19 of DOE of St. of Hawaii Large class sizes, poor security, little or no homework, little input allowed from parents or teachers, low morale... teachers and students... Needed: More funds, progressive leadership, more meaningful involvement from students, teachers and parents... Since the new principal, Darlene Bee was appointed, the school has been a downhill slope. Disrespect for her isn't just present in the students, but in the teachers also. With security that plays favorites, an overall uncoordinated staff, terrible food portions, and students who genuinely believe they're stupid and refuse to learn, the school turns off kids who actually want a good education. Its low funding and lack of teachers who aren't jaded and/or likable doesn't help either. It's like the government have given up on us. Bad. The administrators are beyond unfair and choose favorites.

column1: My children transferred to this school from Hyndman last year, and what a differnce a great school makes. There are no apparent bullies, my girls are soooooooo happy here with the teachers and classmates. I am really glad we chose to change. The principals and staff genuinely take an interest in giving a great education and they care about the students futures. My chidren transferred to the Bedford Area schools from Hyndman. The best decision ever! Staff is wonderful, doesn't matter who your related to or what your last name is here! Unlike in Hyndman! Great education opportunities!

column3: LCHS has educated all three of my children. The teachers here are of high quality,and do a wonderful job. I totally support thier JROTC program,with what they teach in these young adults. And the ones I have met are fine young men &women. A fine school to educate your children. My sons are current students, one will be graduating in May 2012 and he has been Principles Scholar for a lot of terms. My issue is that with good grades - he is having a difficult time being accepted at colleges outside of MS because the school curriculum has different requirements than required by other states- so he is being punished for that as if he has a shortcoming. He cannot meet the requirements to attend college- because of the school curriculum? After putting one child thru the torture of this high school I hope I never have to again. My child is a straight A student, no thanks to the teachers or staff at this schoold. In a consolidated high school, if you are not from Monticello, then your child doesn't have a chance in sports, scholarships, awards or anything else. The teachers only care about the locals with the exception of the Advanced Math teacher, she appreciates children who are prepared for her classes regardless of where they come from. This small town is in complete control of the school, the sports events, and anything else. It is so unfair for kids who are not local to have to drive ten to twenty miles to school and parents must provide their own transportation if the kids are involved in sports and required to stay after school. In hindsight, I would have paid for private school had I known how unjust this school system is.

column1: Great faculty, arts and sports! Great school...caring faculty... committed to a quality education and an emphasis on service to others...we are one big family! I have been a part of this wonderful school for more than 25 years as both a teacher and a parent of two graduates that are now successful adults. TSA is A+++ (academics, arts, and atheletics)!!!!!!!!1 I love Tattnall because not only is it a wonderful Christian school, it is a wonderful academic school as well. The people who work there are GREAT! tattnall is a wonderful place to learn. the teachers are amazing and really care for the students If you send your child to this school, listen & TRUST your child if she/he tells you they are being bullied. Bullying is something this school does NOTHING to discourage or stop! I love Tattnall! I am acctually a student here, and I couldn't think of on ething I would do to change this school. It is amazing and I love going! WWe have been so pleased with tattnall square academy! Not only is it a wonderful school with a christian environment, but a second family environment! My children love it and are learning so much! Teachers listen to the parents and do everything possible to accomidate every type of child! To a parent that complained of bullying on this site......bullying is everywhere in every school...but, i know that the staff at tattnall does take care of complaints such as that! Tattnall is a great school that provides a wonderful education and is lower priced than other private schools in macon....we LOVE TSA! Don't waste your money, your child will not get a better education here than any other school! My brother and I are both graduates from Tattnall. I attended Tattnall for six years and my brother attended for eight years. It was a great experience. Tattnall offers the perfect blend of a faith based college prep education as well as fantastic extra-curricular activities. Tattnall definitely prepared me for college and I received early acceptance to UGA. I couldn t have been more prepared for the future.
