column3: My daughter came from Franklin Special School District and has a disability. I was always asked from FSSD schools 'what does your daughter need from us to be successful'. Since we've been at CHS, I've been battling to get the services my daughter does need to be successful. I love this school!!! All the gossip that has been going around about Centennial High is complete nonsense!! They are rumors which rude parents from other schools begin. Centennial has wonderful academics, and teachers that truly do care about students' education. The students all have a love for each other that you honestly couldn't find at any other school. If you would like your child to grow accustomed to diverse cultures and ways of life, Centennial is the best place to be. Centennial is an awesome awesome school!! I hate how the rumors that other parents of different Williamson County Schools have ruined the reputation of this wonderful school!! The teachers are great, and the students are even greater!! There's such a wonderful, loving atmosphere when you walk in the building. (They also have an awesome media team) Lastly, the new principals really have their heads on straight!! It's just a wonderful place to be! We have two kids at Centennial. It's a great school. Faculty and administration are truly engaged with the student population and the families. AP and Honors classes are challenging and doing a great job to prepare our children for college. We have two more children and look forward to both of them attending Centennial in the future. Top ranked is a way to describe Centennial High School. A web-exclusive extended list of America s Top High Schools in 2010. CHS ranked first for Tennessee comprehensive public high schools. The current graduation rate of CHS is 99.4%, the highest among Williamson County Schools and 98% of the most recent graduating class went on to attend a four-year university. Twenty-two Advanced Placement classes are offered at Centennial and they are very popular among 10th, 11th, and 12th graders. In 2009, 89% of the students received a 3 or better on the AP test. Testing is an important aspect of Centenial High School. The ACT is required to graduate. The average score in 2009 was 25.4, 24.8 in 2007, and 24.4 in 2008. Although not required, many students take the SAT. The combined score in 2006 was 1267 and the score in 2007 was 1306. The school produced six National Merit Semi-Finalists in 2007, nine in 2008, and 13 in 2009. By far the best school in the county in preparing students well for the real world. Centennial students go out into the and succeeed. Other high schools prepare their students to go out into the world, get intimidated, and come back home to their protective bubble. We have been completely amazed at how great Centennial is for our children. We moved in from out of state & was expecting TN schools to come up short of our previous schools. We went around to the various schools before purchasing & found CHS to be the most down to earth school in a relatively upper class district. From day one we have had multiple people in the front office, counseling & teachers help us get transitioned to the academic courses & school procedures. As parents we have seen our children love everything from the computer aided design courses to the year round running program to being able to get a quick frap in the school's coffee shop. Our children have been successful within their abilities while getting to know a great group of students. If you are moving to the area, I would encourage you to go to the schools & meet the people who your child will be spending most of their teen years. While the test scores are very respectable for a school of diversity they do not predict my child's success..the people working with them influence the life long learning process along side of parents who truly care. Hope to meet you at one of Centennial's many great functions! My oldest daughter graduated in the Class of 2011. Any parent would want a similarly compelling high school experience for their child. Academics, Art, Choir, Drafting, Student Council, Sports, Spirit, Theater and real relationships with friends and teachers for four years. CHS helped her be accepted at nationally recognized Undergraduate Architecture programs at top universities, with scholarships. The professional educators and administrators at CHS want your child to be successful. They want parents involved (a lot happens between open house and graduation). They will partner with your student to help them discover their interests, strengths, and weaknesses (this is a two way relationship). They will work to create the best possible educational experience for your child within the constraints of the larger Williamson County System. The Parent Teacher Student Organization (PTSO) is a great place to get plugged in. At CHS your families investment will pay a lifetime of dividends. God bless. Centennial is a really special place. With the energy that Dr. Brown brings to the school and his philosophy of loving, challenging, and supporting all students, great things are happening at Centennial. The school spirit is amazing, the students are respectful and well mannered, and the teachers are wonderful. We could not be happier. We are one of the families that was rezoned from Ravenwood, which is a good school, but Centennial is pushing our student harder and farther than Ravenwood ever did. Our student does not deal with the clique issues that are rampant at Ravenwood because they just don't seem to exist at Centennial. Join the Centennial family and you will love it too. My son is a freshman at Centennial and I have to say I'm stunned at how little homework he gets. Other than studying for tests he's had actual homework a total of 6 times during this year. Some of his classes are so easy he really does no studying - History and English being two of them. If you want your child to be prepared for college he/she MUST take honors level classes, anything at a lower level is a waste of their time. The college prep classes have been dumbed down so badly that the students really aren't learning anything. Not sure why the school feels it necessary to segregate the freshman so they have little to no contact with older students. This freshman year has just been an extension of middle school. It's crucial for social and academic development for freshman to have contact with older, experienced students in order to learn how to prepare for college. They need to see what older students are doing to get ready and to learn from older peers the appropriate way to conduct themselves. Having all of the student body interacting throughout the day would really help the freshman grow up. Right now it's not happening. Having been a teacher at CHS prior to moving to MNPS, I can tell you CHS kicks tail. The faculty are committed to excellence and growth. Bottom line, I saw kids develop, and that is what Centennial continues to do. Residing in Centennials Zone, I get to see my former students all the time! They pop in to tell me how life is going and how much their times at CHS have impacted their lives. Continue the legacy. CHS will always be my true home as an educator! To the person that posted on April 11 about too little home work, low rigor, and "segregation" of freshman, are you serious? Centennial has the highest expectations in the county. My child came from Ravenwood to Centennial and the difference is HUGE. Centennial's challenge to students is far ahead. The freshman have their own lunch period and directed studies period that enhances the Freshman Academy. Other schools in the county do something very similar, and this is one of the reasons your child has less homework at home. They are doing it during study hall, and if they need help, they get it through the Freshman Academy and don't leave it to chance. Freshmen are interacting with upper classmen all day long, but you make it sound like they are sequestered away from everyone else. Nothing is further from the truth. Centennial is amazing and by far the best school in the county for genuine learning and a real world, normal school experience. Our family has now had a year at Centennial after having the previous year at Ravenwood. Centennial is absolutely wonderful and there is no way we would ever want them to go back to Ravenwood. Our student was pushed exceptionally hard but given the support and resources they needed to meet the high expectations. No offense to Ravenwood, but the teachers only told kids what they needed to learn, but never actually taught. The teachers at Centennial TEACH. The administration is very strong and responsive. The atmosphere is wonderful and i have never seen better school spririt and pride. Fabulous school. The academics are highly challenging and the school spirit is incredible. Many of the poor teachers are now gone and the school has an entirely new attitude and atmosphere. Go Cougars! Centennial is a great school that has come a long way in a very short time. The leadership that guided the school to such a high level is now gone. He did indeed bring CHS from a 6 to a 9 in this site. Hopefully we won't fall back to where we were. The students are great and there are some good teachers. The school spirit is very good. Everyone knows what shame it was to treat the previous principal they way they did. The superintendent should be ashamed of himself. He owes the entire school community and most especially the principal an apology. His bungled handling of what should have been a private matter at the most set the school back hugely. We had come so far with such great leadership. Then the interim principal proved to be useless and harmful. And then they hire an inexperienced kid to run the most difficult high school in the county. Centennial will fall back off the cliff and undo all the hard work that has done by a great principal. Because of poor leadership from the home office and hiring of weak leadership at the school, I cannot rate Centennial highly at all. There are some fantastic teachers here that inspire students to learn and grow. Fortunately, we've experienced most of them. Unfortunately, they are the exception. This school is plagued with petty, power tripping tyrants that harass students over minor dress code issues, give less than achieved grades when parents dare to question what or why they are teaching a certain way, etc. I was hopeful the new principal would be a catalyst for change, treating our students like young adults getting ready to face the reality of life outside of HS. Sadly, this is not the case. The dress code (stricter than the Williamson County dress code) perpetuates the illusion of gangs being prevalent in this school. Furthermore, it treats the young adults of this school differently than their peers in neighboring schools. There was a survey given to the parents but as far as I know the actual content of the survey was not made public - only the results. The educators would be wise to spend more time inspiring our children and less time nitpicking and making examples of them. Communication with the parents and being accountable for what and how you are teaching seems obvious, but not welcome All of the great strides Centennial made under Dr. B are lost. We have a new principal that speaks with the passion and knowledge of an anemic, monotone, pseudo-intellectual. Most of the students never see her. We went from a 6 to a 9 on this Great Schools rating site under Dr. B. We will be back to a 6 all too soon under this administration. We need a new director too. He hinders the progress of most schools while looking for the next photo op or chance to self promote. He is also the reason we went from a great principal to someone just taking up space in an office. It was the worst handling of a situation that had nothing to do with schools possible. So excited about the direction this school is going! This is the strongest administration this school has had in the last several years we have been involved there. The teachers are not only strong academically but have a compassion for this school and the students they teach. Both my children graduated with high honors and scholarships for college. great school, nice & clean environment, we are happy with all teachers and edu level There are some fantastic teachers here that inspire students to learn and grow. Fortunately, we've experienced some of them. Unfortunately, they are the exception. This school is plagued with petty, power tripping tyrants that harass students over minor issues, give less than achieved grades when parents dare to question what or why they are teaching a certain way, fail to communicate with parents, and the politics and favoritism within the athletics department is awful, etc. Kids with amazing potential get lost in the maze, harassed by administration, and lose all confidence and momentum to succeed. My child is a Freshman at CHS, I can count more times she has come home crying than I can good days and no one at the school cares, and I am told more often than not that it is "her fault". I moved into the district so that she could go to this school based on the things I was told and am moving out of the district and to a different school based on the ACTUAL experience. My daughter is a Freshman at Centennial and I couldn't be more pleased with here experience so far. Not only is the environment strong with regard to trying to get all students to excel academically and to challenge them to learn at a high level, the school also offers tons of extra-curricular activities and the school spirit is out of this world. Whatever negative rep this school has gotten in the past in undeserved in the present. Much of the credit goes to the Principal Leigh Webb. She is super and only promises to bring this school to higher levels in the future.Go Cougars! Awesome teachers and administration. The principal, Leigh Webb, is doing a great job and is highly respected by all. This school has No accountability for the students. They give do overs on every assignment until they make their desired score. The teachers spend most of their time pressing their political views on students instead of preparing them for college. The athletic departments are a mess. Coaches allow the kids to say what they are & aren’t going to do instead of coaching them up to their full potential. Teacher quit anytime of the school year & leave the kids hanging with rotating subs for the rest of the school year. The communication is very lacking in every department. The students all look like zombies on their cell phones every time we’ve been to the school. I wouldn’t recommend this high school based on personal experience. Do your research, do your homework, find the best fit for your child. No longer recommend any school in Williamson County due to the way the district is handling Covid. No mitigation strategies that are useful. No option for remote learning anymore. When they have to shut down they just use a snow day.

column1: I cannot say enough good things about Calvert Hall College HS. My son is a Sophomore this year, and I wanted to write this review because I don't think we are what most people consider a "typical" Calvert Hall family. We are not Catholic, and my son is not athletic. I'll admit I had reservations when we first applied, but they were quickly put aside when I saw what a great school this is. The boys are required to take religion courses and attend Mass occasionally, but he never feels marginalized or like anyone is proselytizing. There is an ever-present culture of kindness at this school. Obviously, sports are a huge part of Calvert Hall, but there are so many other activities available that my son's lack of interest in sports is no big deal. I've seen so much growth on his part since he started attending this school. He is learning to advocate for himself; a direct result of the staff being dedicated and responsive to the students. He is being challenged academically, enjoys all of his classes, and likes his teachers. He talks with me about what he's learning all the time, definitely a good sign! Opting to send my son to CHC was one of the best decisions I've ever made. If you child is taking Honors and AP courses, it is worth paying the tuition for this school. If not, don't spend your money. There are teachers that genuinely care about the students and take time to work with them. The administration is filled with homo-phobes. If your son is gay, do NOT send him to this school as he will be treated disrespectfully by the administration. Even though this is 2015, they are one place that is NOT tolerant of anyone that doesn't "fit their mold". Academically the honors program and AP classes are top notch. The school prepares individuals for college level courses by having weekly lecture halls, an upper level curriculum, and personalized day-to-day schedules. I am an alumnus of Calvert Hall who graduated in 1978. CHC taught me most of the life skills (above & beyond a normal High School would) to be successful in both my professional and personal life. The Brothers and lay teachers were always attentive to any questions or concerns that students would bring up and go out of their way to help explain & give guidance. The college preparatory scheduling really helped me with budgeting my time for academics, extra circular activities and recreation. I found this helpful later for both my undergraduate B.S. degree and M.B.A. And priority was given from day one to respect both other students and the CHC staff. I highly recommend a tour of CHC and meeting with the academic advisors for any prospective student.

column3: I grew up in the great city of Somerville and graduated from SHS in 1985..If any parent out there that is looking for a school that has school spirit and that teachers that care about there students and that is SHS.I can not think of any other high school in this state that has the best teachers around than SHS .We had a saying at SHS that once your child walks through those front doors they will have memories about SHS that will last a life time and that is the gods truth.I had so many awsome memories about SHS i have about 100 of them.There is not one high school on this planet that would give your child the best education than SHS.Somerville leads the way and always will Somerville High School has undergone a sea change in the past 5 or so years, all for the better. The new headmaster has made intelligent changes to the school; he's active and solicits parent & student input. Grade 9 has a cluster system so kids take major subjects w/ the same students, & the teachers share an office to consult re their students. There are 11 AP classes, & other classes are Honors, Standard, or Skill level; there's a great voc-tech program & biotech. Kids can take classes in any strand if they qualify (so, standard in one class, Honors in another, voc-tech & AP, etc.). Morale among students & faculty is terrific, which is great b/c this is a highly diverse school (racially, ethnically, socio-econ.): kids whose parents are professionals or artists, whose parents grew up here or just came to the US, all get along & share school spirit. A great mediation prgm helps too. Teachers are enthusiastic about their subjects & about teaching/mentoring/coaching kids. The result is kids love to learn & try new things, without being stressed out. College attendance rates are climbing (close to 80%), & PSAT is free to every student. Sports and clubs are free, too. Great art pgm Somerville High is the Lab School of the 21st Century. It has the most diverse student body - in cultures, languages (50), nationalities, and aspirations (with one of three integrated vocational programs in the state) - and the richest range of in and out of school activities in Greater Boston. More than any other school, students teach each other and their teachers - key skills across class, culture and career, critical media and communication, pride and collaboration - while teachers help students use that teaching most effectively in creating futures. The weakness of the school is parental involvement - both outreach to bring parents in, and engagement to make more careers more palpable to more members of the community. Just as the school has stabilized its teacher population, increasing skills with technology to match interpersonal sensitivity to race and class and aspirations, it is slowly and carefully engaging parents, community resources, and others in broadening the overall experience of each student. And students are documenting that increasing breadth in online, multimedia portfolios that show increasing awareness of how their multicultural skills are critical. I can not think of a Better High School for any Student than Somerville High School.I grew up in Somerville born and raised and i can tell yea this School is the best hands down .If you are thinking of Moving to Somerville Mass i can assure you that the Somerville School system is the best..One great thing about SHS is when your daughter or son first walks through the door from the first day of school it is the memories that will last a life time .I graduated from the High School 28 years ago and i can tell yea i still thing about the great times i had and the friends i made.The other best thing about SHS is the teachers who care about there students everyday and it is also a very safe to send your child to SHS .I can not think of any other high school in Mass that would top SHS .The school song says it all Somerville leads the way and always will.I can assure you and trust me SHS is the best always had and always will be .The student body is also Terrific and they all get along Fantastic. Great Teachers. Great Athletics Program. Great Diversity. Great Music and Arts Program. Constantly Improving Good responsive school, they called me back when I asked to chat.

column1: Great school no bullying just fantastic benign a freshman is awesosome. The only thing is the sophomores are not mature yet Appo is a very excellent school and as a freshman i enjoyed my first year, all of my teachers were excellent and I did an amazing job at this school! i had great scored on the state testing. The sports organizations are great and so are the clubs. Our sports fields are AMAZING and I always look forward to going onto the fields! This school is just as good as a top rated private school. APPO JAGS RULE!!!!! Appo is a wonderful school. My granddaughter just graduated this month. all thru high school she had wonderful teachers that were there to help whenever she needed it, all she had to do was email them and they got back to her right away. She was always coming home with a story that happened in class that made learning fun. Appoquinimink High School *conditionally* is one of the best schools you can find. I say conditionally because it really depends on what kind of student someone is; those that work harder and strive for more typically turn out better than those that do not do their work, and that comes to no surprise to anyone, but it's a common sense thing that MUST be stated. If you're not going to do work at this school, then it's just like any other school. Otherwise, while issues that happen in most schools like sexting and drugs do happen in here, and there is a group of kids that I urge everyone to stay away from, it's a great school and can only lead to opportunities. Students are relatively nice, counselors are cooperative and will work with you on anything and nearly everything you need, and teachers are typically good at teaching (with few exceptions, most of which leave after one year). As someone who gets higher grades than most, it's not hard to get them, but in some pathways and classes, you definitely have to work harder than others. There's no bullying in this school as others have said, and the environment is just fantastic. If anyone going into Appo is reading this, and assuming that the teachers I'm about to list are still in the school, I would strongly advise you to try to have Mr. Lunsford (PLTW Engineering - POE, DE, EDD), Mr. Hoffses (IM III and Calculus AB), Mr. Milchovich (World Studies Honors, occasionally AP Psychology, and AP Human Geography), and Mrs. McCloskey (Spanish II and Spanish IV). Personally, Mr. Lunsford was my favorite teacher because of how he approached teaching, and not only gave us an education, but life advice. I'd have to say that the last three teachers are all tied, but I'll give some insight on them. Mr. Milchovich is a hilarious teacher, his World Studies Honors class was one of my most fun classes, and I actually learned a lot in it. Mrs. McCloskey was my favorite language teacher because she tried to keep the playing field as even as possible, and in doing so still shared bits about her personal life (which I found interesting). column3: I am a graduate from the class of '98. Among my classmates, we have professionals in fields as diverse as law enforcement, education, business, and theatre; several post-graduate students studying in excellent schools; married folks managing their homes and children; and one cloistered nun...and that's from my class alone. The combination of the fine education centered on the virtuous, sacramental life, and athletic teams and clubs of all sorts formed us so that we could mature into happy adults, well-equipped to engage culture and society. Seton has built a school which gives a strong Catholic formation to its students. It's teachers are dedicated individuals who will do anything they can to help your child. The principal is a real-life saint. Seton does away with the negatives of modern education and focusses on the canon of Western cilivization giving students strong skills in math, English and religion. However, at times and in certain circumstances, the culture of Seton can be smug -- somewhat condescending to students or individuals at schools with lesser academic or moral standards. This can get in the way of teaching our Catholic children to meet the culture in a genuinely loving and friendly way while still standing strong in their faither. For some students who struggle emotionally or academically, this can and has been crippling. Conservative Catholic families enroll regardless of cost or other difficulties because it is fully faithful to Church teachings, takes the sacramental life of its students seriously, and has remained independent of educational fads and innovations that have proven ruinous at other schools. There is a community of faithful families that is inspiring and sometimes awe-inspiring. Nobody locks their lockers. Parents can feel confident their children are safe from violence and that most classmates are protected from and not immersed in popular culture at home. Academically, the emphasis is on writing. "Lost" subjects like Grammar and Geography are taught. History taught by the principal is excellent as are American Government, Biology and Chemistry. Math and foreign language varies from excellent to disastrous depending on the teacher. There is a revolving door of new grads from Christendom who teach for 1 year and move on. No band or music. No PE -- learn sports on your own time. Computer technology is last century. The physical plant is decrepit and lacks climate control. The important things are done well, and the rest somehow falls into place - that is all part of its charm. The school is small so everyone knows everyone which is cool and the teachers are the best

column1: This is school is awesome I couldn't of graduated if I didn't go.the teachers arnt strict and treat you like a adult they also do care about you and will take the time out of there day to help you. Unlike bigger schools where the teacher might be pretty close with 1 or 2 kids but beyond that it’s just not the case because of how many kids they see in a day of teaching. They are also more hands on in teaching and can focus on every kids needs because of the small class size (anywhere from 6-20 kids). Along with the teachers being great, don’t even get me started on the counselor, Maria, she is the sweetest, most fun and caring lady you will EVER meet. She makes sure to have a very very good relationship with every one of her “kids” (she calls us her kids). She cares so much that she will make sure she knows your story and why you are where you are. She makes sure she always has snacks and water for every kid who comes in to say hi to her, and there’s a lot because of how much she is loved. She gives you her number (if you, and ur parent are okay with it of course), so that you can text her to come up to her office if your having a bad day, she’ll text you in the morning reminding you of the schedule that day (as it changes), along with checking on you and making sure your okay after missing a day. The principal Dean, is the coolest dude as well, he makes sure to give you a fist bump everyday and treat you like an adult. I could go on and on, but all in all. This is one of the best environments ive ever been in. The one and only downside i would say is, is the lack of a social life. As i said, it’s a very small school, so there’s only a handful of friends that you hang out with, also there’s no football games or anything like that.

The teachers and faculty believe children over adults, even if you have proof. Its he said she said, pure chaos!! The Teachers and staff are like dealing with children. My child has a better chance educating himself. Also as far as safety is concerned put your kid in self defense! BUT BEWARE if your child finally defends their self THEY WILL GET THE REFFERAL. They allow the females at this school to punch, hit, slap boys with barely any consequences. They belittle the kids infront of student, so they think its okay.

column1: Don't really like it anymore. The removed and fired all of the good profound teachers that made learning fun, and replaced them with terrible teachers who can't control the class and criticize the children. academics here are lacking. what's the point of an audition when they're admitting students who have mediocre talent? There is quite a bit of outdated information here. To begin with, under the new principal, addition AP courses, several new sports options, and a wide array of clubs not mentioned here. I'd encourage students and parents to come see the school for themselves. You'll be blown away by the talent of the students and teachers, as well as the academic rigor. My daughter was accepted to High School of the Arts as a dance major midway through this year (2016/2017), and we've been thrilled with the school from day one. Even as the new kid, she found a warm, welcoming environment from both students and teachers, even as she hustled to get up to speed.The dance program is great. She's being challenged and pushed in all the right ways, and between the visiting choreographers and the class trips, her access to the wider artistic community has grown considerably. She comes home tired and happy every day from school.The academics are plenty rigorous too. She's in several AP courses, and we've both been impressed with the level of passion and dedication from every one of her teachers. They work her hard and expect the best from her. We couldn't be happier.Also it's worth noting that even as an "out" teenager, she's been accepted into the community with open arms. This is a tremendous school for arts and academics. A safe environment for diverse learners! Everyday at this school, I feel motivated to reach the high expectations of my dedicated teachers. With an abundance of challenging advanced placement courses and a focus on performing arts, Brooklyn High School of the Arts manages to give students the perfect balance of academic acceleration and artistic encouragement. I am currently a student in Brooklyn High School of the Art. As a student, I feel that this school give a lot of activities for their students to have fun. If any students have any ideas or suggestions, they want to make, the principal, assistant principals and Dean's will always welcome everyone with a open hands. The Arts in this school is amazing. Not only the Arts, the education the teachers give is, too. The teachers help students with works, and expand their knowledge to their full potential. For the past three years I’ve been coming here, you learn that in order to succeed you don’t let anything get in your way, that may include peers, teachers etc. You do what you have to do in order to graduate and move on. The school provides a great place to experience AP courses and even as a quiet person bullying is rare and for the most part nonexistent. Teachers that believe in your potential believe in you fully but the ones that don't can often make discouraging comments to both the student and the parent. The arts themselves are great to learn here. Its a pretty ok school since you get to focus on your major but you also get academic classes. I currently have AP classes which are challenging, like really and also I'm a bit ahead for someone in my grade and things can really get stressed out. I have to sleep a bit late because I really want to learn the material but my brain can't cooperate as I want it to; yet teachers offer after school so I looked forward to that and it was pretty helpful. Honestly, don't procrastinate cause teachers seem to be getting together to load you with homework on the same day. There are too many safety concerns at this school This school does a great job. You can tell from the comments from students below they have a lot of pride. Amazing school. The students are talented and bright. The teachers really care. You can tell as soon as you walk through the door that this is a safe creative space where students can grow. Amazing diversity! i’m a sophomore at this school and the environment is overall very supportive and uplifting. the teachers, especially the arts department are patient and clearly want the best for all of their students. the only downside is the bathrooms. Brooklyn High School of the arts has amazing opportunities for the art’s department, and the teachers actually care about you here. The only thing that I would change are the bathroom rules. I have had a great learning experience at BHSA. I am a senior and I have made a lot of new friends at school. The teachers, class counselors, and administration are always very supportive. There is a lot of talent at the school and all the studios have amazing shows to showcase this. The school offers many different opportunities to see professional shows and exhibits and they also have tons of different after-school clubs to pick from. I highly recommend this school to anyone interested in the arts. I am currently at junior at Brooklyn high school of the arts and I will ensure you that BHSA is the best fit .You can pursue your major (talent ) and you can learn your academics at the same time .BHSA is a peer like environment everyone helps each other and the teachers care about your education.We also have many different after school clubs and programs that’s fun such as the music club or a bit more academic such as tutoring . As a senior in high school I can truly say that although my high school experience hasn't been perfect I've gotten a really good education with teachers and administrators always at your corner. Teachers at this school want to see you do your best. This school is simply full of kind creative and very talented people. BHSA is a community that I have been happy to be apart of. I have nothing but wonderful things to say about Brooklyn High School of the Arts. This is not only due to the fact that I have been a student at BHSA for the past 3 years, but as a junior, I have been around long enough to hear other students sing (literally) their praises! One of the attributes that attracted me to this high school is not only do they specialize in enhancing students’ gifts in the various arts, but the staff at Brooklyn High School of the Arts equally focuses on providing the highest standards of academic excellence. Generally, incoming high students may feel disoriented and experience unwarranted pressures, but the teachers and administrators of BHSA have a way of quickly making you feel you are part of their family who is always ready to support you. When I graduate in 2024, I will certainly be proud to say I am an alumnus of Brooklyn High School of the Arts! Brooklyn High School of the Arts gave me an extremely warm and welcoming community for me to express my identity and artistic passions all the while giving me a rigorous academic experience. The school provides a multitude of opportunities for students to explore the arts through partnerships, providing private lessons, and trips to some of the best arts hubs in NYC. AP courses are also offered allowing students to gain a head start in their college experience. As a clarinetist and saxophonist who participated in the school's instrumental program, I can say that I have been given loads of tools that prepares me for any career in music education or music performance. I have enjoyed learning at Brooklyn High School of the Arts. I made many friends and all the teachers are very supportive. We have many great showcases every year. If you love to sing, dance, act, or knows how to play an instrument, you should join this amazing family and make it better! This school really enjoys their arts! My love for somany subjects grew because of the amazingeducators there!! I appreciate it. This school has provided me with a good sum of experience and knowledge I've deemed valuable so far. Considering I'm a Sophmore at the moment, I've still got a way to go until I can create a fully versed and concise opinion on the school, though I will say my experience with the school has been generally positive overall. The teachers are professional and respectful both inside and outside a current lesson, allowing for an environment where I can learn efficiently, while also being able to enjoy my time at school without unnecessary work pressure added onto my shoulders. The teachers act as actual mentors rather than something less than standard.Fights are broken up relatively quickly, and it's never difficult to reach out to administration or teachers in the event of an issue. The clubs are alright, but certain ones demand a heavy amount of time, taking away a bit of accessibility I wish I had otherwise.

column3: Best school with the Drill team. Also if you stay smart and excel in all subjects then you will love this school because i know i do. this is my high school and I love airport, we need better servers fot the computers Airport High School is really what you make of it. Make sure your student stays in the highest level of classes possible and they will be good. There are not major differences between the coursework, but there is a huge difference in the quality of the classroom. The lower level classes are filled with students that don't care about being there, being quiet or behaving, making it impossible for the students that do care to learn anything. The higher level courses, the students are well behaved and carry on insightful class conversations and make it a wonderful learning environment. I've found that majority of the teachers like the school and care about their students. Safety is not a major issue in this school- never felt threatened or saw any physical violence between students. There is a high emphasis on sports at the school and between the two high schools in Lexington II, Airport Football usually performs much better than Brookland-Cayce, and draws more attention.

column1: I had 2 children attend this school and I can tell you that if you do not have the right last name you do not belong, if you do not play sports you do not belong, and if you are not from there you do not belong! The education comes second to the sports and that is unexceptable! My child had to take all general educations classes in college before he could start the classes he needed to obtain a degree. This community is low income, to near poverty and it shows. I am very thankful to have moved my other children to a better school district, but the problem has been that they are so far behind that I am afraid they will not pass. The program the new school follows is at least one year ahead of Shakamak, and that is if Shakamak teaches the same program. It has been three years since moving and my children have excelled since leaving Shakamak! The other concern I have with Shakamak is that they mainly hire staff that are alumni of Shakamak, I feel that this is done to help perserve their main interest which is not educating our children but teaching them sports. It's sad when you receive a letter saying that the kids can attend another school if one was offered in the district. I was a former student of Shakamak and ashamed to say that I attended school there. I am also ashamed that my child ever went there! Unless you have a certain last name,money, certain clothes or are into sports, you are nothing. I tried for several years to get my daughter tested for learning disabilities so she could have an IEP # & get the help she deserved. I was told there was nothing wrong with her. We now live in Ohio and she got the help Shakamak wouldn't give her and she's excelling in school! Shame on you SHS! The bullying that goes on at that school is horrible and the principal did absolutely nothing about it! I wouldn't not recommend ANY PARENT TO SEND THEIR CHILD TO THIS SCHOOL!1 I am ashamed to say I currently go to shakamak. They could not care less about 85% of the student body, and only care about you if you play sports or have a certain last name. There are very few good teachers, such as Mrs. Morin, Mrs. Meyer, Mrs. Estey, Mr Gambill, and Mrs Miller. Discipline is terrible because in school detention causes you to miss all teaching. I'm ready to get out of here as fast as possible.

column3: Taft embodies the warmth and charm of a small town community. Friendly; from administration to teachers to students. My daughter is in her first year of high school. Freshman orientation was great! It offered the right amount of hand holding yet with enough learning opportunities for both me, as a parent, and my daughter, as the student to navigate on our own to become familiar with the new high school environment. When we had questions, anyone, everyone was there to answer them for us. A solid good school. The personal and the whole system are first class, this is a place every future profes sional should be. This school is way over crowded! Fortunately, my kid attends ComArts, which is next door, but my kid has to go to Taft for electives and lunch. The one elective is band....so disorganized! My kid had to wait 5 hours to get fitted for a uniform and another 3 hours to get shoes and locker. Also, the practice schedule is too intense and interferes with their academics. My concern fell on deaf ears, when I contacted the band teacher. He doesn't care and puts winning competitions above the needs of the students. My kid loved band until moving to this school. So, be aware if your kid wants to be in the band. They don't follow the online schedule and add practices to an already full schedule. I'm a student attending Taft high school, I also am a member of the band. Yes, the practices are long and intense but this isnt middle school, we have more competitions and we could possibly even go to state this year, Mr. Solis told everyone that year was going to be different. Band isn't mandatory if you're not able to handle the homework and practices (we dont have both morning and afternoon practice so there's plenty of time) your child can always get out of it if he dislikes it so much. 300 other band students handle both academics and band so I don't think there's a problem. I was only there for my freshman year. Taft can be a really a great school or can be a really bad school..it all depends on the crowd you hang out with. Sadly, the crowd I was in ,had a strong spark in my life. I felt Tafts drama was intense but nothing I couldn't handle. And I strongly believe that in highschool, you find out who you are, what your capable of, and it's all just an experience. Experiences are lessons, lessons are a part of life. Taft has lots of diversity n will give your child or you an opportunity to be aware of peoples beliefs and culture. Building memories. Building expensive. Over crowded this year and I was told by administration the enrollment next year will increase! The parking lot is already very congested and dangerous! I'm horrified for my kid to drive to Taft/comm Arts! The next two years will be difficult for teachers and students being overcrowded until the new high school opens. Great school, and happy my child attended this school. This is an overall horrible school they have no good homework assignments for us to do. I would never send my kids here. Driving by the school in daily commutes, appear to be very well maintain and effectively managing space. Many opportunities for extracurricular activities, teachers support and assist the students that ask for help, many vocational type of training opportunities. It was a great experience for me as a military child. I felt right at home at school.

column1: It is actually horrible. If you care for your children, DO NOT TAKE THEM HERE. Bullying is supported by teachers, they participate in it. If you care for your children go somewhere else. This isn't where you wanna be. I agree 100% with the other reviewer that mentioned how bad bullying is at this school. If you are not part of the popular, rich crowd and stand out in ANY WAY, teachers will not support you when you are bullied. My son was physically assaulted in the lunchroom and in the halls several times a day. I eventually had to get him transferred to Andover Central High School (which is a process in itself). He did so much better emotionally and mentally at ACHS. I am grateful my child has left this school behind, I just only wish I had known earlier what went on here before I enrolled them. I know it is typical for schools to advocate for a zero tolerance for bullying and not mean it, but this really takes the cake. I thought I had lived through and endured a time full of hate so my child would not have to experience the horrors I did growing up. But I am sad to say I have been let down and I was deeply disturbed by the behavior students exhibited towards my child and students like him. There was an incident my child overheard a student saluting Hilter in the hallway and the teacher instead of reacting to this abhorrent behavior decided to chide a student who had reacted to the salute. I wish I did not have to hear about things like this and hope no one's children ever go through what mine went through. I wish I had transferred my child to Andover Central sooner. We moved into the district from a small private school and have really enjoyed it. Lots of opportunities for students to engage and explore their interest. Great facilities. At first our kids were overwhelmed by the size and variety of students in the school, not everyone was a one size fits all overachiever, but they have gained so much from the range of student body. Even with that, Andover doesn't have nearly the inner city (violence, lack of support) problems I experienced in my years growing up in an inner city school. Its a very middle to upper class suburban school. No large school environment is going to be able to completely address bullying the way people want. Parents have the hard job of providing support, and t working to strengthen their own children to become resilient in ALL environments. These are life skills that will be critical when adult life presents challenges. As far as academics and creating opportunities, Andover has that in the bag.

column3: I graduated from KHS and loved it. Teachers were great, got a good education and went on to graduate college with Honors. Found a job in Appleton, live in Kaukauna and make a decent living. As far as the bullying that some have reported...that happens in every school at every level. Nothing specific to KHS. I'm glad I just graduated from that place. It is a complete dump! They never clean classrooms or bathrooms. It's disgusting. The food there is overpriced and low quality. The only good thing about that school are the teachers. Administration sucks. Felt like we were being controlled. Kaukauna takes sports way too seriously. They even encourage EVERY STUDENT to participate in a sport, which is completely rude. Not everyone is athletic or gives two craps about sports. I dont know how people like going here. This could go on, but I have better things to do with my time. Once again, glad I'm outta there. Dont send your kids there! All in all some excellent teachers. Unfortunately, budget cuts resulted in adding more administration and cutting the new, savvy, passionate teachers. I saw administration as a couple of suave guys with nice hair cuts who failed to connect (but maybe that's typical in high school?). Graduated a few years ago. Thought I was a big shot upon entering a large state university because I took most of the offered AP classes (a total of 4 offered). Found out in college that for a high school of 1200 students to only offer 4 AP courses is a complete joke/embarrassment. Not sure if these courses are offered now, but I wish they were offered when I was there. -AP Chem -AP Bio -AP Computer Science AP computer science NEEDS to be offered. Go on any jobs/careers website to find that the majority of all careers available are software engineers/programmers. the school absolutely is terrible for the student body. Teachers treat students horribly. Bullying, racism, and sexism rose to the breaking point. AND NO ONE IS DOING ANYTHING ABOUT IT! It's a terrible school you don`t feel welcomed its like a prison and they only care about you if you play sports or are rich theirs always kids doing bad stuff in the bathroom and they really haven't done anything about it. Kaukauna is a terrible school district don`t send your kids here for yours and their sake

column1: Oakhaven High School in my opinion is one of the great schools that Memphis has to offer. This past school year Oakhaven High met all the EOC set scores for all of the EOC tested subjects.

column3: Cedar Crest provides a very high quality education, with challenging acedmeics that can be suited to any learning style. The sports and music programs are excellent. It is a fantastic school! Cedar Crest provided me with the best education I could get. They did a fantastic job of preparing me for college and the academics there. I always felt that the school had excellent leadership, and academic resources. The school has all the amenities a student could ever wish for. I was involved in music and sport clubs and the are simply top notch. Cedar Crest provides the very best that a student needs. Also the facilities and campus is beautiful. This school provides an above average curriculum with many students moving on to Ivy League Universities. The student population is diverse and there are many academic and sports activities to satisfy all interests. The teachers union is very strong which is good in some ways because it allows for high standards, but can be negative when it comes to salary/benefit negotiations at school board meetings. The teachers come across as entitled and take credit for high test scores when, in fact, there is strong parental and community involvement. I am unfamiliar with special needs offerings but it would be unfair to rate the school poorly based only on this criteria considering it is a very small portion of the student population. Overall, the school district is the best in the immediate area. This school couldn't have done a better job to prepare me for college. I felt that the time I spent here was both useful, and gave me a great intellectual edge. I know many of my former classmates who are currently in Ivy League Universities, which only confirms the high sense of accomplishment and prestige in this school. This school is most definitely accommodating to all disablitys and all teachers and staff the best class is typing and study hall and pottery and art one and 2 and viscom and phise ed is the most fun cause you get to swim in the indoor swimming pool but it al statts from higher up on down the same as for as far as home to school it all starts from parents on down to their kids/students one thing you do not want to do though is whem you are on the afternoon bus goin home is throw anything out of the window cause for one that is dangerous for the oncoming traffic and the bus and and you do not wanna get embarrassed by the principal cause you possibly will be facing some disapline and or a school meeting int the audatorium me again this place still sux i have 10 kids and they all hate this place the foods nasty and the walls ooze green slime My daughter graduated from Cedar crest and had an excellent experience. My son is a student there now and enjoys it very much for the most part. I personally know several teachers there and they are top-notch individuals. Sports? that's another thing entirely, unless your child runs track and field or cross country. Those coaches are some of the best I've seen. Overall I would highly recommend the school. Outstanding school, administration, staff, and students appear to strive for excellence. Tiny school, which has no redeeming qualities. I regret my time here and wish I'd never attended. Students were mostly drugged out, the teachers inexperienced and/or overwhelmed, and there was no counseling or support for disabilities. Does not prep for college at all. Avoid this school! My experience at this school was very negative. Most of the teachers did not care about the experience that they were giving their students. Obviously there were the exceptions. The counselors are also very self centered. They don’t care about students wishes but rather the easy way out.

column1: Great school. An advantage- its so new..everyone is open to new ideas. Our first senior class is paving the way for new traditions and fun things to come. As mentioned by others, the block schedule is amazing, and helpful for people to get ahead, as well as help others catch up. The only drawback of this school is that the people are horribly vain and everyone is 'too cool' for each other. My life has been miserable socially. I think due to the small size of the student body, it is more difficult to find a good group of friends. I'm looking forward to tranferring to FHS next year. This school is great, I have a daughter that is been ranked among top 3 in her class. She loves the school, academics, teachers, campus, etc. I like the level of parent involvement. The issue is that socially she is absolutely miserable.I have never seen her this unhappy. What happens with the teens here? Are they really too cool to have fun? She is transferring to FSH next year. This is sad because the school is great , the principal's team, teachers, administrative personnel and resources in time of budget cuts are simply awesome. My son is a freshman at Vista this year and is having such a great year. This school is night and day from Folsom Middle (I'll save that for my review on them). My son is very smart but not very motivated. Vista has brought a complete change in him. He excelled in regular classes and was quickly promoted to honors and is still excelling with the challenge. The block schedule offers so much more opportunity to learn things of interest (great for artists, btw) and moving more quickly through subjects that are less interesting helps keep him motivated to push through and do his best. Vista del Lago High School has an excellent principal, classes, and coaches. Students can be prepared to qualify for any university, including elite universities. The athletics are great. The students receive challenges and encouragement. Wonderful school! The school is excellent when it comes to acaemics, however, the students and teachres here are not very friendly as a whole. They think because they are wealthy and high achieving, they are better than everyone else.... I LOVE VISTA! I've never "loved" school until now! I'm involved in so many programs and have never been happier! The only thing is the dress code while I applaud the modesty policy is extremely sexist! for the most part... Teachers and staff are fantastic I'm a senior in Vista Del Lago and have been a student here for the entire four years. It was a competitive, fast-paced school for me, built with high academic success and many options for a challenging course. I found that the best things are my school were the teachers, the block schedule (providing for a true ability to obtain lots of credits and take many honors and AP courses), and our clubs. I've been president of two clubs here, SNAP Medical (founder) and Drama club and we have made a great improvement over utilizing innovation and ideas from our students. Folsom High seemed to be the supplement to the few things that Vista was lacking in. Folsom High is known for its performing arts in choir and theater and an extremely successful football team. If you are a parent making the choice, I'd base it off of what your student is most passionate about. If they love sports and arts I would recommend Folsom High, if they wish for strong academic success and rigor on a Bully-Free zone, then Vista is the place for them! I've worked at several high schools and I can confidentially say that this is the best. The environment is intimate and nurturing. "Nerd culture" is pretty popular and students are allowed to be themselves--I love how safe it is for them. Plys, we have high standards in the classroom and have been very successful in adapting to the challenges of Common Core. Students are better prepared for college with the rigor we offer as well as the schedule. Time and time again, graduates tell me they experience success in college because of the foundation they got at Vista. Finally, we offer some awesome classes. Martini's guitar program and CME are excellent examples of this, or our sports medicine program, or our Mass Communications, or our Careers in Education program. I love everything about Vista, and I know our kids are benefiting from all we have to offer. This past summer, I had an interview to teach at Vista del Lago. The panel was very organized and the school entryway was impressive. I enjoyed the opportunity to possibly teach there, but at least this year that was not the case. This school has no respect for students, diversity, or the law. Administrators at this school regularly make their own rules in complete disregard for students' due process rights, and treat students in a harassing, threatening, and discriminating manner. Academically, this school is sub-par too. Overall it's been well. Some teachers have put on more left-leaning socialist views but they were respectful. Beautiful campus with many different programs including the Guitar Programs and Academics. There is a growing problem with tensions from the LGBT group against other students and also racism is rare here, it's often that racism is directed towards mostly White and Middle Eastern students here. Overall, it is a great school but we should direct more attention to academics and athletics instead of extracurricular activities. I have attended this school for the past years and I have been severely bullied. Many of the times these occurrences were in front of teachers and they did nothing nor did any of my classmates. I either asked for help later from the teachers as well as from the VP's and they said it was up to me to figure out to handle this or they forced me to confront my tormentors making me feel utterly defenseless and have lead to me having severe mental health problems. I have a 504 in place which is government document allowing accommodations for disabilites (mine is for ADHD) and for almost a year they refused these accommodations and I had to file a report to the office of civil rights and only until after this government agency came in they listened. I know hundreds of people who have been bullied at this school and I know dozens who continue to be bullied for their body weight, ethnicity, religion, and disability (whether or not it is clearly visible). Students are afraid of telling adults about being bullied because their is a culture of unwillingness to help and they know if they tell administration, administration will force them to confront their tormentors. Our school is known as the mean school, where if you send your kid here, they will be bullied. Please think of this before sending your child here. I was a student at this high school all four years, and I had a great high school experience. I had great teachers that were actively involved and truly wanted each student to succeed. I felt prepared for college, and enjoyed the variety of classes there were to choose from, like Drawing & Painting to Engineering Design. I enjoyed being a part of a school sports team, and felt that there was a wide variety of students there. Overall, I felt prepared for college courses and often look back on my experiences at Vista. The teacher that buillyng the kid at this school

column3: This school is poorly run and disorganized. It takes many trips to the school to get anything done. The best way you get response to anything is to send an email or make an appointment. My daughter spent one semester there and loathed it. She indicated there were fights at the school on a regular basis. There are some good teachers and counselors but overall the academic quality at the school is very poor. Her AP classes were a joke. They were not taught at that level. This school is a joke. none of the teachers never return phone calls(even after I left msgs), I called the school after no returned phone calls (a week and 2 days) and I was put on hold for 20 mins with out no one coming back on and tell me if any one helped me or not. I did get one phone in Spanish but who ever left me the msg didnt leave a name or where to call back they only left the name of the school and said call back. Now that is a SMART TEACHER.... yea right. I even spoke to the principal she tells me I will find out and call you back. She took my name but no phone number.. I am still wondering how this principal will call me back. This school needs help big time.... My child has done excellent in the AP Courses. The teachers are very helpful, return my calls, go the extra mile in assuring that students get the help they need to understand the course and pass. Their VPA Dance Program is the best, they put on a great show and the director and teacher are wonderful. Parent involvement and support is very important and it works hand in hand, I get involved as much as possible. This school has come a long way, I applaud them and hats off to the principal. Bad school. Dont waste you time. The school board want even follow up on the complaints. Dont even take you dogs there :( Help.................................. to the parent that wrote in on Feb 16, 2011...try grammar classes prior to bashing the teachers and school Reading all the comments below I am afraid of my daughter attending this school for the first time. I tried to get a transfer but unfortunately the school I want is full. I will pray that all turns out well for my child at this school and get a transfer as soon as I can. The staff members are incredibly rude and offer absolutely no help. If you're a student or parent who needs to stay in contact with staff members because of certain issues or situations, forget about this place. The school's not worth dealing with. I love this school the students are really nice and the teachers care about you and your grades. I feel like it's a safe environment and that everything the school has to offer me will benefit me in the future. This school is excellent. It is student centered. Very good school. They help children to graduate

column1: I love this school and I am a student. The teachers are the best and yes we get homework but who cares! The school has a great athletic program and a great principal. I would never want to go to any other school. I love the excellent teachers as well. I am a former student who came on from public school and felt obligated to leave after my second year. I came in eager to meet new people but was shocked by how many close minded people there were who stuck with their middle school friends. As for sports teams, unless you're a killer athlete or had a sibling who was on the team, it is basically impossible to be seriously involved. The administration and many of the teachers DO know many of the students by name... That is the students who are part of a legacy, have a parent who works there, or are a captain of a sports team. And unfortunately for me I had two different classes where the teachers' bias for certain students affected my grade negatively. Furthermore, the few AP classes I did take neither prepared me for the AP exams nor for the classes in college, for the teachers were more interested in seeing all their students pass with a "3" than actually learn the material. Very few students from Pius go to outstanding schools and truly it's only the ones who entered the school unbelievably intelligent. The majority go to lower level state schools. Do not waste your money on this poor education and experience. I came from a public school, and my dad works here, so I knew most of the faculty. I didn't expect how loving they are, and how the students are open to new members. At my public school, I was the odd guy out with no friends; now, I've got at least fifty. The teachers I have are amazing, squeezing in fun activities at every opportunity. Yeah, if you aren't Catholic,it's kind of confusing, but whatever! The teacher you're bound to get is so loving and can really explain Catholicism for you. It is really easy to communicate with your teachers via email. St. Pius X Catholic High School, keep it up! I am a rising junior at St. Pius and absolutely love it. It's a difficult school academically but I believe that is a great thing because we are leaving prepared for college. The principal Mr. Spellman is one of the kindest and greatest people I have ever met. Recently I lost my phone at school and went to him to ask if any teacher had turned it in. He stopped what he was doing and helped me to look all over the school! He even let me look thorough the faculty lost and found. He is just an all around great guy. At Pius there is a balance of good and bad teachers, just like any other school. But what truly makes Pius amazing (better than Marist) is the people. Everyone is so friendly. Also the sports are incredible. As a former student, I did not have an pleasant experience at this school. Although education and sports were actually really impressive for a Caholic High School, the social scene was pretty horrid. Diversity is rare at this school and since I was of a different ethnic background, I was often bullied or treated as an outcast. The only way to make "friends" at this school was if you were either white, rich, athletic, thin, or just happened to attend the same former middle school with some kids. However, teachers are very friendly but there are some (but not many) that play favorites and if your not on that list, then expect an uncomfortable class environment. Overall, this is a good but not great school for academics and sports...student body is just frightening. The past 4 years have been absolutely wonderful at St. Pius X! We are sad to see it come to an end, however we plan to apply there for our youngest son because we want him to have the opportunity his sister received. This school is very diverse in it's student body and was very welcoming to my daughter who is not only ethnic but came from a public school. Our entire family is very involved in the school and we are welcomed and encouraged on all levels. The education is excellent and competitive with other private schools. Pius has an excellent reputation of preparing their students for college. My daughter often says, some of the nicest and most supportive people she has ever met are at Pius and she often brags about the fact that there is NO bullying issues at the school. I believe the people who say they "had" to leave, is because they can't manage the rigor of the course work and the expectations for exemplary behavior. IT IS GREAT TO BE A GOLDEN LION!! I attended 4 years of high school at SPX. Loved it. Great teachers, faculty and staff. The best Math and Science teachers. Language, Drama, Art, and Music classes were wonderful. Many friends attended SPX who were not Catholic. Religion classes included history of Catholicism, and the comparative study of other religions. Community service was a class requirement. There were extra guidance classes to help choose a college that fit your future goals and move through the college application process. All told, I enjoyed it, and SPX prepared me for Georgia Tech. I am a student at Saint Pius and I had a terrible experience. I came from a public school and all the others came from a private feeder school, so they already had their friends. Nobody wanted to branch out to make new friends and just stayed in their little groups and then the most popular kids from each school become friends. Popularity is based on Money and Attractiveness. I am considering leaving to go back to Public School I am a freshman who came from public school and my experience has been amazing. The teachers are caring and determined to help you. Classes are challenging but worth it. The students here are more than welcoming and very friendly. The president and principal make you feel like family. There is no other school I could see myself at or want to be at. Outstanding. Pius is about family. Its not about how much money you have, what car you drive, or where you went on vacation. Its about caring for each other in a Christian environment. Very concerned with their academics. They have too many teachers that are new and are not teaching the students. Our experience has been not so great and are spending a lot of extra money on tutors for just about all subjects that happen to be taught by new teachers. I am a former student of this school. Academically, this school is rigorous and truly a college preparatory academy. I attended a well known public university as part of their honors program and did not have an issue with coursework or testing in college. That said, the other reviews that speak of the lack of diversity in this school are VERY true and a real concern. While St. Pius X may do a decent job (i.e., better than the other private schools in Atlanta) at balancing low income and high income students, the student diversity during my attendance was atrocious. In addition, there were two incidents in which a student made racially charged comments at me, and neither of those incidents were dealt accordingly. The administration absolutely refused to step in and almost drove me to leave the school. In any other school, the principal of vice-principal would have stepped in to intervene, especially when the school has a supposed zero-tolerance when it comes to racism. But neither I nor my parents met with anyone above the Dean of Students. While I look back fondly at some of my teachers during my tenure at St. Pius X, I cannot ever recommend this school to anyone who is not cis, white and privileged. The parents, faculty, and staff are the absolute best. We have one daughter currently enrolled and another recent graduate, who was one of a record 73 in her class (of 270 +/-) admitted to UGA, which I have to think stands up against any school in the state, public or private. We didn't have SPX on our list initially, but our older daughter wanted to look at it, and here we are. We are not Catholic, but have felt welcomed into the larger family since Day One. There is a palpable sense of humility about this place and its people. There is no "keeping up with the Joneses" here, unlike most private schools. They take their mission very seriously in that regard, to the point that their facilities are...ehhh...not all that impressive, shall we say. But they seem to manage okay, anyway. ;-) I am a graduate of this school and although I only attended one year, my senior year, I can honestly tell you all that it was a frightening experience. For one thing, having moved to Atlanta from a different state and attending a school where I did not know a soul, when I arrived at the school for the tour I was to be in uniform, even though no one was helpful enough as to tell me what the uniform required, or even where to obtain said uniform. Nonetheless, I came dressed in a uniform for the tour, where I was stopped by multiple angry and incredulous teachers questioning why my attire was not up to code. Although I tried to explain that I was a prospective student on a tour, they did not believe me. Finally, after asking a hall monitor where the office was, the office secretary who had spoken to me on the phone that morning to confirm the tour, advised me that there was in fact no tour scheduled. Instead of sorting this out, she went into the cafeteria to grab some kid who would spend about 10 minutes with me walking me down two hallways before the lunch bell rang, I was again stopped by a teacher who was wishing to give me a demerit for holding my wallet and phone in my hand. Again, I attempted to explain my predicament, she assured me that I was playing a prank on her. When the school year finally started, I was virtual for the first two months, and no teacher reached out to me as to welcome me to the school or to the other students. Instead, I was met by unanswered emails when I would ask about certain online databases that were necessary to pass the courses. When I started in person, not a single teacher seemed to notice a new student in their classroom, so I decided to respectfully announce this. About half of the teachers did not understand what "new" meant, and the other half, again, thought that I was playing a prank on them. Let me give a word of advice to those teachers that did not care that I was new: It is a miracle that a kid at the age of 18 is able to join a brand-new school in a brand-new state, when she hasn't even unpacked all of the boxes in their home, let alone take the time to mingle with the incredibly snobby and up righteous children at this school. Throughout the year, this is what I encountered: teachers putting extra work on me and standing over me to make sure I did not make a single mistake, to the students not helping out when I would ask where the bathrooms are. That is when I became virtual for the remainder of the year.

column3: Having nice teachers and offering extra curricular activities does not matter when up against POOR education. The bottom line is the entire school system suffers and it is in black and white with well below acceptable test scores. It is all in who you know and who your parents are at this school with very little focus on being all you can. Go private before going to MHS. The high school may have shortfalls in test scores but has not been labeled a failing school. The staff seems friendly and offer lots of extra curricular actives and clubs. column1: Urban prep is a very disorganized school. They need to work on professionalism and organization. Urban Prep does not provide students with books, and the handouts are not logically organized. It's 2013! If they cannot afford books, the materials should be available online. This school is all hype! sadly, there is nothing that we can do about the terrible things that urban prep has to offer. We need better schools. Especially ones for Black men. Because this school is very low in stats and performance. Urban Prep Charter Academy-Englewood Campus (UPCA) is an excellent school for African-American Males. I have witnessed great improvement in my nephew grades, confidence, leadership ability, he knows is not his environment and will prevail. The staff promote is available to assist our young men to succeed, in as much as parents and young men also have to do their part. If you want your child to engage in a sucessful future, UPCA is a good start. How about weeding out those young men and their parents that are not in acceptance of the discipline and accountability that it takes to have a rewarding future. We believe this environment is a good match for our young man. SUGGESTION: I like to see my nephew receive books for each subject, considering the multiple ways of learning. Offer rental books, or give the parents the book information ISBN number, etc. in case they want to purchase the book elsewhere. I suggest this option be made available for parents/students that are interested during orientation, registration, etc.. This will assist with the multiple forms of learning. It takes a village relative Auntie..., I'm apart of that village! I have a son who is graduating this year from Urban Prep Academy, Englewood campus. Having had reservations, I see now the method to their madness. My son is a mature young man with a solid idea about what he wants to do with his life. He will be leaving for college this fall and I will have no concerns about his being ready for the world. He has learned so much there and I am so proud of him. I am grateful to Urban Prep and recommend this school to all young men who are serious about getting a quality education and a huge lead in life. Urban Prep Englewood campus is all the persona. The school focuses too much on making sure they look good and their rules than the actual academics of the students. Hoping in the future the school will start to focus more on academic as well as maintaining structure within the school. This school is more than a number. You have to experience it to know what great teachers and opportunities this school will provide your son. I love urban prep my son is going into his sophomore year and I must say they are doing an awesome job keeping him focused and on point I change any thing about this school . also I love the creed they have to say after event , just awsome This 1 star rating is for the Bronzeville campus. After only one semester, I am desperately trying to transfer my son out of this school. To refer to it as a school, or Academy for that matter is a huge over statement. It's more like a Juvenile detention center. There are fights everyday, there is more gang activity that I've been exposed to. Dean Tony Stone threatened my son and bullied him and this was allowed by both the Assistant Principal and Principal. The teachers are not qualified. The curriculum is awful. There are very few extra curricular activities. They have no books. Do not believe the hype. The "100%" that they boast on is just acceptance rate most of which are to very small colleges in places no one want to live for 4 years. Most students that graduate from Urban Prep are gravely under prepared for college and because there aren't very many extra curricular activities they aren't afforded many scholarship opportunities either. Do not send your son here. Poor.. incompetent leadership, throwing around of unearned power. They remind me of Chicago cops who know there’s a fellow officer out of line but will not speak up.

If you are good with people and have money, WAY TO GO! South is for you. The people in south can be harsh, but if you find the right group this is the best school ever.
