column3: I am a parent and reading all the high school reviews has led me to this school. I have searched the web but would like feedback from actual students. My son is a freshman and has great grades. Tell me something about the classes and teachers.. How do they add up? I am reading some bad reviews but do know that you can succeed once you put your mind to it. I am an involved parent and DO NOT tolerate bullying, or bad teachers. I graduated from Escambia some time ago. It definitely is not the best school out there. There were constant fights, a high dropout rate, and some pretty bad teachers that didn't do their job. The school was too poor to afford cameras so it was easy to skip class. However, it is possible to obtain a good education there. In my experience, all of the honors, AP, and dual enrollment teachers were the best teachers in the school and were caring about my performance in class. Regular-level courses should be avoided as they tend to be led by poor teachers. If you have no other place to send your child to school and you are reluctant, I believe it is possible to make it work out. My parents were skeptical about sending me here at first, but were glad I stuck around and I ended up graduating here with honors. Escambia High School is a terrible school. The administration is a joke. I would NOT recommend sending your child here. I will not be allowing my younger children to attend Escambia High School. This is the school we are zoned to go to. I wish we could afford Private school, this school is a joke and so is their Sports department. My son tried out for Basketball and they told kids that a list would be put up the next day. Well guess what his name was not on there but Kids that did not try out were, How is that fair to anyone? Teachers are just there to get a paycheck. Escambia High school is the worse school my children has ever been at. Teachers don't follow IEP either does the SRO. The SRO are rude and think because the have a badge they know everything. I would think twice before letting any child go to this school. My child went over a month with out a math book and she reserves a E in the class because once she got a book she didn't know the work. Run fast away from this school. The engineering program at EHS is top flight. My child has completed all 4 yrs and was accepted at 5 major engineering universities and will attend Auburn next year with a full ride. She was not even the top student in the program! As with all schools there are problems with the duds but these are mostly hard working, caring and smart teachers. The ROTC program is the best in the country and the music program is hands down the best in the area. The honors science and math programs are of the highest quality. In short this is a good school in an old building with a diverse student population. This school is horrible. I tried to address many issues this past year and administration never corrected the issues at hand. My daughter was bullied though out the year by her teachers not students. I tried to meet with the principal and he would only email me. My daughter put in several request to speak with the principal and her never allowed her speak to him regarding her issues. Being a student at Escambia High School made me realize that the experience your parents guaranteed would be the four years that you would enjoy is difficult. You can not just go to school and expect to have the best time of your life. You have to get involved, put some effort into your work. Now the school may not have the best facilities but personally I love Escambia. The teachers who have given me guidance in my times of need, the friends that have built me up whenever one of my AP assignments were due, and the fact that I was so involved made me gain so much respect for the administration and staff. No high school is perfect and Escambia is far from it. The respect that some parents and students need to give is ridiculous, seeing that the majority of our staff waits on our parents and students hand and foot. The improvements that have been made, made the school better. Overall my experience at Escambia has been life-changing in many ways. Escambia High School was typical of the schools I attended. Not even EHS, like all the schools I attended, were unable to provide an education a student with traumatic brain injury. As a consequence of my years of education, the diploma was worthless preparing me for college. In college, while not designed to help a student who was poorly educated, college is where I got the educational help I should have received in government schools. I DO NOT attribute my academic success to public schools. I am thankful for the help I received in College.I earned three college degrees, no thanks to the public schools, including EHS. I am still cognizant of some of my academic weaknesses to this day. I was an adjunct instructor at the college level for thirty-five years. EHS played no role in my success. I am still working even though I could retire because I am providing my son inspiration to teach himself rather to depend on any teacher. -High student to teacher ration-Teachers are just there for a check-Lack of safety resources for students The staff of this school is absolutely awful. They have incredibly low standards of teaching, which do not prepare you for the real world. DO NOT send your children here, from Lock downs once a week to being targeted by School staff this school is not a good place. It is highly unsanitary and not sure how it is still open, the bathrooms back up and sewage comes up through the floors and floods the halls not to mention it comes through the water fountains along with rust. I lived in North East and saw small number of students in class but Escambia high is full of students and the job school management is doing is Fabolus.I will rate escambia high no 1 in the country because of 2 reasons .They have more children and more challenges and they are handling it well and still going to make our children successful.Good Job Mr principal and team Keep it up! School was more dangerous than most neighborhoods in Pensacola, which are very dangerous. If you don't want your kid to grow up to be in a gang and sell drugs, don't send them here. My daughter is being moved to a different school My daughter attended Escambia and had a wonderful experience. She was involved in sports, band, and advanced academic classes. The teachers were interested and engaged, the students were encouraged to participate in extracurricular activities, and the administration is/was second to none. No school is perfect, but I couldn't be happier about her experience and her academic achievements while she was there. She would wholeheartedly agree with me. We considered private schools but diversity is very important to us as a family and she was excited to attend. There are students of every economic and academic levels and we wholeheartedly believe that you get back what you put into it. column3: I absolutly love this school! What first attracted me to this school was the friendly atmosphere, and I can honestly say that my first expectation has been lived up to. I am so glad that I came to SDA! LOVE the quarter system and clubs. Teachers in the San Dieguito Union High School District, which includes San Dieguito Academy, are the highest paid in San Diego County. The district says they pay the best because they hire the best. While there are many absolutely incredible, dedicated teachers at SDA, there are also many who are just there to collect a paycheck. Many teachers are not available before or after school to meet with students. The minute the last bell rings, they bolt. Also, teachers are permitted to do whatever they want during their prep periods, which includes surfing, exercising, etc. Then the teachers grade papers during classes when they should be teaching students. District is overrated in my opinion. Constant revolving door of principals and vice principals. Some good/dedicated teachers, but a large amount of tenured unmotivated teachers. Very good selection/variety of classes. Ask parents of older students for the teachers to avoid - some of them are very well known. Strongly recommend private school if you can manage it. The 4x4 schedule allows for students to take only four courses a semester - giving them time to focus on those courses like college rather than juggling 6-7. If your child is going to take AP courses, this is an advantage because they are not taking them all at once (!) but can take 1-2 per semester instead. Also, it allows for a lot of electives and a student can take multiple languages. My son benefited from having 4 classes every day rather than the block schedule of 6-7 randomly throughout the week. Juggling the course load was much more manageable. Teachers love being there and it shows. 19 CIF teams. The SDA environment has the feel of a college campus rather than typical rah rah high school. Very happy. The learning experience was excellent! All three of my children chose SDA, and all we’re happy that they did. The school is relatively 'new' for school years (began in the '80s) so maybe one day they'll figure it all out. Excellent school with great academics and Christ centered education. honestly i do not like it, the school claims to be college prepatory, and the label their baseline classes as CP (or college prep) and then come senior year i get into calc and the teacher claims that its a college level class just slowed down. For refrence i have never taken an honors, dual enrollment or AP level class so i was not ready for calculus being a college level class; even though parkview claiming to be a college prepatory school. overall they failed at trying to prepare me for college, whereas some subjects i feel like Im learning a great deal, in others it just feels pointless. save yourself while you can. This school was the reason for my trauma. The school only cares for kids who put money into the school. They threatened to suspend and send my friend to a conversion camp because of RUMORS ONLY. Do not go here, no matter what. pbs sucks at sports academics and just in general -pbs member

column3: I am a student at la serna high school. Soon to be sophomore. And I honestly love la serna. They're so many amazing teachers and staff, I met a lot of great people. My teachers are very helpful and resourceful. I love la serna's clubs and activities. If I could go back to my freshman year and start all over, I totally would. Walnut High School is much better! Go Walnut! Go to Walnut High School, a Grammy Award-Winning school in Arts and Sciences! Great School!My Husband and two daughters attended La serna High School. Wonderful staff, specially the teachers and counselors. Amazing school, great place for learning and students go above expectations. Counselor that is assigned to my daughter absolutely worthless (Kelly Strong) never returns emails and always seems to be on vacation. Thankfully the school has Marco Ramirez who is great at responding but unfortunately has to carry the load for lazy counselors like her. So far my daughter has had a few great teachers and a few not so great (I was extremely disappointed with the Art teacher there, but her English teacher is amazing). She's a freshman so let's see how the year goes. When I went to La Serna we had a fantastic A+++ art department. You worked on a portfolio to show in art school or college level art courses. And you had competitions to compete with other students for art scholarships. We use to practice our language skills when we went on field trips to places that spoke German, French or Japanese.

column1: Worst experience I had in my teenage years . I was emotionally deprived of self-esteem. Teachers were tolerant and well educated,but did not push you to excel. A C was a "good grade". Mr. Owens was best Spanish teacher and band director was awesome.go Elizabeth! Lack of Social interaction, Lack of girlfriends and too lonely leaving a brother lost like he's in a maze questioning his identity.

column3: I graduated from this school almost 10 years ago. I moved from a much larger town half way through my junior year and was shocked at how friendly and accomodating everyone was. They made it a seamless transition. The teachers and staff were amazing and the resources were up to date and useful. I had a great experience here! My son is currently in this school and I feel as if the administration, teachers, and coaches all go the extra mile for the student. They challenge and encourage their students to set high goals and to reach them. My son absolutely loves this school and has grown so independent and confident since attending. I can't rave about our experience enough. This a great school although small it offers a variety of classes that allow students to really pursue their passions. This school system is not friendly towards parents and children with special needs or who are not a part of the status quo. It was a battle to get my son the accommodations he needed and my daughter was pushed through instead of engaged. They did not address her reading comprehension problems until her last year. The misogyny towards her and other female students by male students was also very shocking to me. I would not recommend this school if your child needs services.

column1: I chose to send my son to SCPA and chose to pay out of district tuition for 6 years because of my belief in allowing students to be able to express their thoughts in a creative way. Schools are consumed in just passing tests for state funding. This school is for the creative and artistic child and very accepting to a diverse group of students from all backgrounds. It is a public school but has a small intimate feeling. You see students smile the majority of the time. This is a special school for the children who do not fit into the normal public school because of their creative minds. They have majors in the different arts and the students are well trained in their art programs. Many students graduate with scholorships. This is now a K-12 art school. Students who apply must audition and have good grades to get in at the 4th grade level. They can audition and the school staff looks for creative possibilities in all the arts. The only downside would be the students ability to be able to focus on the academics. The student puts alot of hours into the arts. I love this school and the arts. I'm proud my child is a student here. There are many wonderful teachers, staff and students at SCPA. Unfortunately, there are also adults and children who display unbridled, poor behavior that negatively impacts others. In reality, the overwhelming desire to portray "perfection" does not benefit this school or any other school. The public is keenly aware there are problems everywhere. Our school will truly excel when honest efforts are made to prevent, address and resolve problems. This is the best all-around school in the area. The teachers and staff go above and beyond for the students. The academics are on par with Walnut Hills. They expose the children to many opportunities children usually don't have. My only complaint is that sometimes it takes them too long to weed out the riff raff. This school is outstanding in the quality of artistic preparation and also academic preparation of the students. It is full of life and positive energy. It really gives the students what I like to call a well rounded preparation. My daughter says this school is like her second family for her. This school is amazing. I was there from 4th grade to graduation. The music programs are excellent. I graduated in 2013 so I’m not sure if the same teachers are there, but most of the teachers were great. I would recommend for my child. This school used to be a great school. The current administration and staff are running it to the ground. The main focus is money. Performances for money, constant soliciting of random items to make money and duplicated charges of broken item fees. There are some good teachers here, there are also some burned out and uninterested teachers here. It's like a lottery when it comes to what type of educator your child will get. The bully culture is prevalent at this institution against students and teachers. It is a hit or miss on the performance art part as well. You better hope your child is one of the chosen ones when it comes to selection and promotion. Schoolwork structure is lacking. With all of the technology and sites available, teachers have become lazy and leave these systems to teach kids. The very minimum is offered. Several leadership, self esteem and positivity programs have launched but they are not sustained. It seems like a 'bullet point' so the school can claim they are offering that program or leading that initiative.

column3: As a student at Lawrence I feel there is a big bullying issue. i feel that faculty needs to hunker down on the bullying. many of our students are being bullied and there is nothing being done. All they get is a slap on the wrist and then they are suspended for 10 days and then get to come back and do it again. as far as the teachers, I think they are great. They take alot of time time to teach the students the best they can and push the student to achieve their goals. i think this school is a great school but bullying needs to stop. i think the school needs to work on how it uses its money. everytime football season starts thats where all the money goes. and when its other seasons money goes there. the money should go to the teaching not the extra things. in my opinion the school is going to be closed in the next few years at the rate their going. the faculty keeps alot of things "under the rug" when things happen. They push their kids to finish high school and completely rip them off of their education. Being a Senior at LHS in a few weeks, I strongly feel that there is a bullying problem, some of the teachers do not care, and if I had to say anything good, it would be that the food is WAY BETTER than the food served at Benton Elementary School. After several attempts to view the curriculum from K-12 communicating directly to the staff, administration, school board and the Department of Education Office in Augusta, one year later a curriculum was provided by the Superintendent for our review. The curriculum provided was incomplete and out dated. After becoming a School Board member 2014 both School Board Policies and Curriculum are now available online. There are 13 School Board members that make up the School Board yet three School Board members and the Superintendent meet each week and discuss business without involving the other members of the School Board and meet without public notice or agenda. The School Board has not followed Policy ADA which requires them to set annual goals in cooperation with the staff, administration and citizens of the community. Setting annual goals per policy ADA have not been complied with for many years. The School Board as a body has publicly stated they are not required to hear public comments or concerns. When suggesting to have goals established and a schedule set to meet those goals and review progress, the School Board refused to adopt this basic practice of success. Its a decent school to those who are willing to do as asked.

column1: This school has a multitude of options to cater to each and every students personal interests there are many slc's to choose from and even more clubs and activities to participate in. I would rate my experience at this school good because it offers a variety of programs. Some benefits may include tutoring classes, global kids after school programs, and fusion club. Best school on south queens. It prepares you for college. As a soon to be former student this this school is terrible, I applied for early gradation and upon that I was given a lot of work to complete by a certain time. The new work and the regular school work caused me to have many sleepless nights and break downs, but I completed my work with the promise I'll be done with school by January 25th, 2021. Without the school informing me I had to find out I'm not graduating until the 26th on top of that I'm going to have tot stay in school until January 29th, 2021. With all that said that's enough to sue the school for mental trauma.

column3: I spent my freshman year at Nelson County High School, but recently decided to homeschool instead. I have to say, the other kids are extremely nice and there is no bullying whatsoever, but academics leave a lot to be desired. As a gifted student, I didn't feel challenged at all. Most of the other kids didn't have a lot of ambition and complained about the (small) amount of schoolwork we had to do. However, because I was willing to work hard I always had time to finish all my homework in class (I literally NEVER brought work home), I usually found myself with over 45 minutes of class where I was sitting at my desk doing absolutely nothing. I don't know why the other reviews are so great for people who've transferred here, perhaps the entire national standard for education is low? But all I have to say is that I don't know how the current students are going to get through college when the pace they will have been used to in high school is so slow. column1: I attended Holly Pond School for 13 years and loved it! The teachers were very supportive and involved in our lives. I also loved the fact that it is a smaller school and that you recieved more one on one attention that way. My mother attended Holly Pond, I attended Holly Pond, and my children will attend Holly Pond. It is a great school! I graduated HPHS in 2004. I had a great experience at Holly Pond. Most of the teachers really care about you and try to break through to the students who don't care about their own education or maybe have a rough home life.

column3: Overall the quality of education available is excellent. The school has some outstanding teachers who prepare kids for the next level. As parents we have a duty to prepare our children to be good citizens and promote the importance of academics. Work ethic starts at home. Whether you like it or not our children act in public and at school based on the expectations we set at home. If you make excuses and play the role of the victim, you have done them no justice later in life. This is a Great School system and like many there are tweaks we would like to see. If that's the case get involved and go to your school board meetings and hold the elected officials responsible for the changes you would like to see.

column1: The number one problem with this school is: no matter how many times a student demonstrates bad behavior, they are never disciplined according to the very discipline plan this school (district) has written and claims to uphold. In short, the school is not only run by the students, it is run by the students with long histories of discipline problems. The principal and vice principal habitually take the student's or parent's side against the teachers - destroying teacher morale and causing a great amount of teacher turnover (some teachers even break their contracts to get away). Like so many of my fellow teachers, I quit rather than endure another year under an administration that doesn't hold students accountable for clear violations of their on written student code of conduct--classroom disruptions, sexual misconduct, boys walking around school with boxers fully exposed and pants down to knees. An administration that blames the teacher for everything and provides no support to our teachers. The principal is a joke--parrots the phrase "on our way to world class" while presiding over horrible state assessment scores. COHS isn't even ranked in the BOTTOM 25th percentile of all Texas schools. It's that bad! This principal is and self-absorbed, far more focused on using COHS as a springboard to get his next job. Turnover at this school is a scandal: 6 principals and 3 superintendents in 7 years; teacher/staff turns over at an alarming rate. No continuity for students, poor pay for teachers, terrible classroom furniture--looks like a 3rd world country. NO parent should send their child to COHS if they care about educating that child.

column3: Great school! The faculty and curriculum helped prepare me for college and made me the well-rounded person I am today. I had no bad experiences with any of the faculty and would recommend this school to anyone. I am a sophomore at West Hills and the staff there really do care about their students. I have had teachers ask me if i'm ok and inquire why other students seem unhappy and the majority of the teachers are pretty awesome :) sure there's the occasional crazy but hey it just makes the day better :) the campus is fantastic although not built for rain and the people here are generally very accepting of new students :) Boy do I relate to the counseling staff they have 2 that try to cover for the rest that do absolutely nothing. It takes weeks for them to see a student. This is a real problem when you have a Senior. The district office doesn't even want you to know where they are. The have you leave voice messages but no one ever calls back. I just finished my sophomore year at West Hills and it was amazing. The staff (especially those in the science department) is remarkable and genuinely care about their students' lives. On multiple occasions teachers took the time to talk to a student if they seem upset in anyway. They are supportive and truly want to see all the kids to succeed. I was once a student at West Hills for one month back in 1999 before I moved out of state, and I found this school to be decent. The best positive I have seen with this school is the student body activities that are performed before and during the school year (spirit activities, etc.). Also, both males and females are treated equally if they wanted to perform. A major downfall of this school is the lack of quality. I took French as a subject (Spanish was filled up), and I was shocked to find out that when I left the state that I learned baby French and not actual French. As a result, I had to relearn French in a short period of time. Also, in English, learning 1200 words per semester seemed to be a drudgery, and does not fall in line with national standards. Those that did not perform well with reading comprenhension would be setup for failure because of this requirement. Teachers seemed to care, but were not as good as my next high school that I attended. The counselors were fine with me, but seemed to be a little rude at times. Overall, West Hills is decent, and could use some improvement. The school never had my son's 504 plant so they did not help him in any way. When they learned that he had one they did not do anything to remedy the situation. My son failed the last two years of high school and they would not hold him back or offer any other solutions to the problem. They have been accused of having racist staff members and I thoughj that it wasnt true until I would look around at teachers and epecially administration and be shuned because of my skin color. It is a 95% White school so people of other skin color are looked down upon. There are reviews on other websites confirming what I am saying here. I have had first hand experience with the horrible administartion, they suspended me last year over a petty violation, throwing a piece of paper. Now they have expelled me over horseplay with a fellow classmate even though we are friends and playing around. That matters little to the horrid staff members that work in the Administration building at West Hills. Good riddens, WHHS, sad to see 3 years of my high school education wasted in such a place. It is an okay school. Some teachers act as if they dislike being there which causes our day to drag on. There is a lot of bullying and everyone is rude if you get to know them. I would not recommend this school for anyone I am in the process of switching schools because of the lack of caring on the campus West Hills is a modern school that has consistently outperformed other schools in the area in all aspects (academic, athletic, and extracurricular). During my time 80% of my teachers have gone above and beyond to ensure that I get the highest quality education available to me. There are course offerings for everyone including remedial, college prep, honors, and AP. I have found the staff to be kind and encouraging, and even the teachers that I haven't been fond of have still produced better test scores than teachers from other schools in the same district. There is little violence and bullying, and in time of grief the school has come together as one to get through it. The one complaint I have is lack of foreign languages. While the German and Spanish programs are very strong and are generally successful, I would like to see another two or three languages added in the near future (French, Chinese, Arabic, etc.). I would highly recommend this school to any prospective students looking to obtain the highest quality education available to them. This is a school that shows complete unfairness to any race that isn't white. Being at this school will leave you feeling very frustrated with the staff as well as the students. If your child is a senior in marching band, expect to be treated unfairly and forgotten during senior night. Two years in a row they pull this stunt with excuses....”we didn’t get the list from so and so”. They point fingers and never take responsibilities. Just an empty apology. These kids are seniors! There’s no do overs!! Honors classes so far seem incredible the rest has a very long road up. disappointed in the 'top counselor' who dismissed my daughter's academic needs to be placed in higher level classes with transcripts that had been received including our class preferences months prior. Terrible time here, at least it made my son resilient and determined to succeed against the odds Poorly. While I appreciated the support I had from a few key teachers, overall the cultural issues have not seemed to change over the years. This a very good school and a safe area for teens to walk to school. The Sheriff department always had a squad car at the entrance of the school. Great school! My children have had wonderful experiences with teachers, staff and coaches. We have been so pleased with everything West Hills has to offer. The wide variety of classes (Honors, AP, College Prep) provide challenging, but realistic expectations to students who vary academically in different subjects. The many extracurricular sports and activities offer students with varying interests a place to fit in and thrive during the high school years. Both of my daughters have been active in clubs and theatre and love it! The theatre and arts programs are amazing and comparable to those you would find at an arts-focused school. The school is well-run and friendly and the campus is beautiful.

column1: Parents are discouraged from participating in school functions unless they are in the 'elite' parent groups. Phone calls to administration take sometimes weeks to get returned. Athletics take priority over academics. The attendance at this school is awesome (56 in perfect attendance for 2010-2011 school year)! They must be doing something right!

They were made to feel welcome from day 1 by the Principal Mr. Newell who is amazing at remembering details of all of his students. The academics are challenging and the extra curricular activities are plenty with good coaching and access. An Excellent school for all round development of students.

column1: my son graduated from BE in 09..It was expensive and I had to work an extra job to pay for it but well worth it. The staff is wonderful, service is important and students have to do community service. My son graduated with honors and is now studying engineering in an honors program at college. Great writing skills ! Terrible school. The staff is lack-luster many of the teachers don't even have degrees. Not to mention the school is filthy with a leaking roof . I pulled my child out of this school and now she is very happy at her PUBLIC high school. I do not recommend wasting your money on this school. The kids do not even attend good colleges This is an excellent college preparatory school with a wonderful spirit of community. The one disgruntled former parent clearly has some personal axe to grind. I'm a faculty member and, believe me, there is NO ONE on the faculty who does not have an impressive degree (or several degrees!) - I'm honored to be among them! What a sweet spirit, too, at Eustace. The supportive community helps the students to excel and to grow as people, too. As a student attending Bishop Eustace, I can say that this school has had the best influence on my life, both inside and outside of the classroom. The academics are very challenging, yet success is attainable with hard work. Service has helped me attain a better perspective on how I can contribute to the world. As a community, the students are tightly knit and have very high academic standards and good work ethics. The teachers are amazing and have a passion for what they do. I can honestly say that I have learned more in one semester of Bishop Eustace than I have in all of my years of middle school. I write as a alumni and now a parent of a student attending Bishop Eustace. It was such a great school that I couldn't imagine my children attending any where else. Not only did Eustace shape me in to the well rounded person I am today,but they are now doing the same for my children. They well prepared me for college and taught me how important it is to give back to others through community service. My children love it at Eustace and have expressed how much they would like it if someday their children woulde attend. Eustace is well worth the financial sacrifice made. It is an investment in their future!! This school is with out a doubt a superb institution of learning combining a high standard of religious ethics and academic discipline. My son attended St. Augustine Prep. School, (Richland, NJ) for 2 years and like MANY other parents & students I've talked to, hated it! He transferred to Bishop Eustace his Junior year and is so happy there. Academically, socially, and staff-wise, Eustace is exceptionally superior to SA. My husband and I wish we had sent him there from the start. Like other parents, we got caught up in the "Brotherhood" facade promoted by SA. The "Brotherhood" portrayal is a scam. Talk to any student outside of the shore area ... for the most part, students are very clickish, and to say the least, are not accepting to others who come from outside the shore area. My son wasn't bullied, but I know of those who have been and have also left. In what appears to be an effort to keep enrollment up, teachers tend to coddle the students unlike BE which is academically more challenging, Thus, students are much better prepared for a college envrionment. Also, in addition to surpassing SA in every aspect, BE exceeds other prep schools as well. It has a great reputation with the colleges we've visited. My brother class of 1989 started the tradition of attending Bishop Eustace Prep and we are so glad he set the bar. Our sons class of 1994 and 1998 soon followed. Now our niece class of 2016 attends and her brother class of 2019 starts in the fall. When you see "Tradition is that of a winner" on a banner in the gymnasium you can be assured your child will be receiving the best education available in a Christian environment with dedicated teachers and staff. All of our family graduates went on to Master level degrees and higher and are fully functioning adults contributing greatly in a world that needs the strong role models that they have all become. It was worth every sacrifice our family made to make this educational experience possible for or children. Bishop Eustace helped to foster the potential within each student through rigorous coursework, informal/formal faith experiences, and mandatory community outreach programs. At the time of being a student, I did not appreciate all which the school had to offer. But looking back, I can honestly say that my time there helped to better prepare me not only for college, but for life. Eustace instilled its morals and ethics within me to become the best version of myself. This is hands down the best school in the area! It best prepares teens to succeed in college. The teachers are first rate, as is the administration. It is worth every penny. The atmosphere at Bishop Eustace mimics a college campus, both in the classroom and on the grounds of the school. My family has been coming to this school for generations. Wanting to be different, I allowed myself to look for the negativity in this school during my freshman year hoping I would transfer. Not only did I fail to find anything I didn't like, I fell in love. The students at BE are so genuinely nice people and the school fosters goodness in all of its pupils. The teacher are BEYOND qualified for their positions, the review that says that they are not obviously does not know that most of my teachers have a degree In their areas AND have been teaching forever. Many of my teachers also have doctorates. Not only that, my dad attended college with a scholarship as well as my uncle, both now top lawyers in the country. My cousins all graduated here and went to amazing schools and now have top of the line jobs while being amazing people as well. My sister was the class of 2015 and now going to St. Joe's (honors college) with lots of money. EUSTACE has shaped me into someone I barely recognize before freshman year. I have become a leader, a friend, a student, and part of the most amazing family I could have wanted. Not only am I on my way to performing on Broadway at just 16, my gpA and ECs allow me to attend any college I want thanks to eustace. the academics are stellar and the moral and religious values that are instilled in each student is remarkable. I have become an altar server, club leader, school-wide organizer, student council senator, and more. Eustace provides its students with immense opportunities and sets high standards because they know we can achieve them. If you don't want to work, don't come here. Those that don't like it here most likely wefe unwilling to put in the work. Try and find negativity like I did, but you will be unable to. I will be a junior this fall and could not be more sure how bright my future is thanks to BE and its faculty. The teachers are my best friends and mentors and my parents away from home. If you send your children here, they will be indebted to you for a lifetime as I already am to my own. Parents. We are a tradition of winners and achievers. I love my school and am proud to say it I have mixed feelings about this school. The students are almost all very well mannered. The campus is beautiful. The problems lie with the admistration. The school policies are ridiculous the claim to prepare students for a college environment yet give students no freedom. You can only go to your locker at certain times. All students including seniors must be there 8-2:30 regardless of if they have class or not. Teachers are almost all over 60 and mostly out of touch. I have never even heard of a school with such an elderly staff. There are so many rules and policies with everything at this school. Coursework is very rigirious but very dry. Not an lot of creativity in the classroom. There is no art classes or programs what so ever. Not worth the money at all. On top of tuition money this school thinks nothing of asking parents to shell out hundreds more for textbooks, uniforms, supplies, Bishop Eustace did a great job preparing me for college, as well as my future career. While there are challenges that come along with any high school experience, I believe Eustace was as good of a prep school as you are going to find anywhere. Excellent, it is a demanding school and great education. If you are willing to spend a great amount of your time studying, this school is right for you. A once proud school is on the verge of being overtaken in terms of quality of education and overall student opportunities by the neighboring Catholic High Schools. Is this a blip or a sign of a longer term declining trend?

column3: I am currently a junior and have been pretty happy with Stone Bridge. Some of my teachers could do a lot better, I have friends with similar gpa in the same classes with a different teacher who are doing much better than me. It sucks to get an iffy teacher because the guidance dept makes switching classes very hard. Unfortunately, I have had to get a tutor just to keep up in two of my classes. I have only had this problem with math/science and language, the history and English teachers are top notch, especially history. I have loved history class all three years. I have thoroughly enjoyed the majority of my teachers, so don't get the wrong idea, it's just really difficult to have inadequate teacher junior year and I'm frustrated because I know I can do better. I am heavily involved in theater and consider the auditorium area my second home. Getting involved with something really helped me fit in, so if you're having trouble with the "clique" system it's a good idea. Stone Bridge has excellent extracurriculars all around, not just sports. We have award winning music and art depts, several great service clubs like Key Club, and all kinds of honor societies. My child attended SBHS for 2 years. She excelled academically, she had a nice group of friends, and actively participated in clubs, sports and music. I was pleased with the administration and teaching staff. She never had a problem with registration or getting into any if the classes she needed or wanted to take. The parent involvement was obvious. Sometimes I would see the same parents doing a lot of volunteering, but there seemed to be many willing to volunteer. Curriculum or Back to School night was really well attended, which makes me believe there are many parents at SBHS invested in their child's academic success. Love this school. I saw my teen grow into a responsible and determined youth here thanks to the teachers and staff. Excellent school. I have had a great experience with Stone Bridge so far. They have really good leadership and caring about students needs is their best priority. They also are really good with students that have disibilites. In addition, they had something called Unified Track and Field that was an activity after school for the students with disibilities. Next year I am planning on trying out for the cheerleading team as a sophmore. Some of the teachers are not the best or only have one student that they enjoy, but even those teachers aren't that bad. Overall, a very good school in Loudoun County that I would definitely recommend. Very competitive academically; tons of activities; prepares students for college Pretty solid. I think it speaks to our generation as a whole that the adults are lackluster, so the teens step in to fill in the gaps. I know we have been called snowflakes, etc., but I think it's unfair. Many of us just want stable, middle-class lives without a crisis. I think many of us feel like the "chosen ones" that have to deal with racism, global warming, etc.Anyway, it's a solid school. Top 5% in the world, I'd say. But it's surrounded by better ones. Riverside and Broad Run are way better. Briar Woods is comparable. The Principal at this school is amazing! He genuinely cares about his students and staff. The School Resource officer and School Security officer are on top of things. All four Assistant Principal's stayed involved in the school and try to make connections with students. My kids have gone here for the past 6 years. I would not pick any other high school in the area over Stone Bridge. "Go Bulldogs!"

column1: What sets this school apart are its teachers. All have been truly inspirational figures in my goal of becoming a school teacher myself. I cannot stress enough how wonderful the teachers are at Black River. If you're having a difficult time understanding something that was covered in class, the teachers will never shrug you off, they are very caring and you could clearly tell that the vast majority love their job, which is fundemental to the learning process. There is definitely a lack of funds, which is why some students are not being challenged enough. The extracurriculars are average at best, but academically, Black River does the best with what it has. I honestly would not recommend Black River local schools to anyone. Black River is a failure to its students and community. The administration and teachers do not have students as there top priority. The school spends more time fundraising for the football program then working on getting High School busing back. Black River places a greater emphasis on sports (primarily football) then academics or essentials for the school and students. As I have said before, I would never recommend this school to anyone.

column3: Worst school ever. Academically, is it fine, but if your child is not white then watch out. This school has a huge racism problem, and the administration is extremely rude. Chantilly is a great school. I moved to Virginia before my sophmore year, the teachers were great with helping me catch up on all of the things I would need to know. Also, the large majority of Chantilly High School is accepting of diversity. It is a great school academically, athletically, and socially. I am a former Chantilly student and am now the parent of a Chantilly freshman. My years at Chantilly were good ones. I had wonderful teachers, a few are still there! Some of my former classmates are now teaching here. I received a great education that helped me when I continued on to college. I don't felt like I was ever ignored by teachers and I was an average student (graduated with a 3.0 GPA). I had many good friends who I am still close with to this day. I hope my daughter enjoys Chantilly as much as I did. So far, so good. :) I used to work at this school and I have to say that if you are a person who embraces, promotes, lives, and celebrates multiculturalism and ethnic diversity then this is NOT your school. The majority of the teachers at this school are rude, unprofessional, and hate each other for stupid reasons. There is even a strong animosity the teachers have towards the students and the administration. Unless you're rich, suburban, stuck up, and cliquey do yourself a favor and stay away from this school. My kids feel safe and respected at Chantilly. My senior has scored very well on the SAT and is feeling confident in his ability to succeed at university next year. I give 10/10 ,because it has strong and amazing enviorment with outstanding staff and teachers The Kids are rude and disrespectful and they use drugs in plain sight This school does an amazing job preparing students for college and academic success. Fantastic preparation for college. This school consistently prepared all my children for success. Could not ask for more! It was the best public education I could have asked for. It has served me well. I moved to this school zone just so I could have my son attend Chantilly HS . I did my homework beforehand. There are some very good teachers at this school who show genuine concern for the students. I don't have to point out how well the school prepares the students for college. The statistics speak for themselves. US News & World Report ranks (as of 2021) Chantilly HS as #7 in Virginia. This school continually gets better and better every year. Their average SAT score is 1240 or 1300 depending on the site you look at. Either way, your son or daughter will be ready for college. If there is a no star option, I would give it. This School has served me well, I have been enjoying it a lot, I would want that more kids come here, I made many good friends. This school gets one star in my opinion

column1: I am a former student of this school, and now just the name makes me sad inside. This school ruined four years of my life. If, as a parent, you are more concerned about sending your child to an insular institution wherein a "Christian" education is more important than diverse academics, then perhaps this high school is for you. I am disappointed to say that, while a student, I was never taught to engage positions that fall outside of Lutheran doctrine beyond ad hominem attacks and simple dismisal with rescourse to the bible. Students who do not practice Lutheran doctrine or conservative values are directly and indirectly scolded by students and faculty alike. Further, there are no AP courses available, no true science lab, and the only foreign language offered is Spanish. While a student there, there were certainly a handful of exceptional teachers who made it very clear they cared about my success. However, most teachers are overburdened with extra-curricular activities; my geometry teacher regularly cited football (of which he was the coach) as a reason for why we didn't have homework or he wasn't in class. While a Christ-centered education may be important, it is also important to ask at what cost. The student review below from Feb 2013 is exactly right. This school has been a disappointment both academically and as a welcoming community. Directly contrary to what we were told before we moved our child to this school, If your family is not from the Lutheran Grade School/LCMS system then you are not welcome. The ultra-conservative Lutheran doctrines overtake all other aspects of the education. Teachers are generally good but the academic standards appear to be no better than the public school system with less diversity. For the $8K annual tuition/fees we are not impressed and will be moving our child back to public school. My child and I both tried to become involved in school activities and were pointedly ignored. I was able to send all three of my children to this school. I found the faculty to be approachable. The general atmosphere of the school was one of great concern for each student. Those wanting to be involved with activities were given numerous choices with over 90% of the student body being involved with something extracurricular. My children left the school prepared for post high school academics and all thrived in the college environment. Those students who prefer to not get involved with outside activities will not like this school. Well worth every penny I spent on tuition. Christian based private school focused on high standards of education and growing responsible young adults! Excellent students with fabulous instructors! The school provides a high quality environment for students and their families.

column3: Updated school, very nice, great teachers, but the students are somewhat clique and raciest. All the teachers are related or know someone. Horrible football coaching. They have new coach and haven't won a game in almost 2 years. Good players that need a good coach. They don't play the best players. They play who they like. It's sad! Do not go to this school if your child is in sports. Horrible football coaches. They do not know how to coach, don't play the better players, play who they like and have only won one game in two years. Good players, but such poor coaching. Watertown-Mayer has been a great fit- not too big; not too small. LOTS of opportunities for students to be involved in athletics AND clubs/ organizations. Great for kids to be able to try new ways hints and discover their passions!

column1: Ben Lippen is a school with a long history for making life wonderful for missionary children. My tuition was the best investment my grandparents made for us five children. I enjoyed so much the strict study of English grammar and literature. One of my classmates is even an editor for a famous internet company. Another is a great treasurer for a leading distributor for musical instruments. Sports were fun enjoyed so much, although not at the time running their cross country course and working out in the gym as well as in polar bear soccer and varsity tennis. Scholar ships handed out to some children from Kenya during my time gave added to the already diverse student body. I would love if my children could also go there, however we are now residing in another town. Really glad to know SC is a school choice state allowing parents more latitude in their choices for a hope based education. I took a five-year-old child to Ben Lippen to apply for their kindergarten program. I told them that he had been rejected by another "Christian" school because they did not consider him prepared enough to entire five-year kindergarten. I was told that Ben Lippen would never do that. In effect, I was told that admission was fairly open. Later I was told that they would not accept him because his parents are not actively involved in a local church. We have had him enrolled at Seven Oaks Presbyterian Church pre-school and Hebron Day School for four years. At those schools, he was accepted unconditionally and received wonderful Christian nurturing as well as a great beginning for his educational journey. We had assumed that Ben Lippen would be a great next step and had always thought that Ben Lippen and Columbia International University are both interested in evangelism. And we assumed that such a school would cherish the opportunity to help to mold a child who needs their kind of training so much. Imagine our surprise when we learned otherwise. I suppose we still live in a world where a child can be rejected because of his parents. My children were able to attend Ben Lippen while my husband was an employee for 6 years. Ben Lippen balances strong academics while never losing sight of the importance of learning from a biblical worldview. All students that graduate here are well prepared for college & often go on to be leaders at their universities and jobs. I was a student there, and have since transferred. With limited characters, I cannot describe to you the horrors of this school. You have to, essentially, be Southern royalty to excel here. Plus, for a "Christian" school, the people are rather judgemental and heartless. Ben Lippen is a Christ-centered school with high academics. Our family is very pleased with the education. In addition to the challenging curriculum, we love how the faculty and staff pour biblical truth into our children. They pray for, and pray with the students on a daily basis. They also have a strong athletics program and fine arts program. With 99% college acceptance rate, 2016 SAT scores averaging 1390 (in the top quartile) and 20% of the 2016 seniors receiving the Palmetto Fellow, they ARE preparing the students. Last year a National Merit Finalist who is now attending Dartmouth attended Ben Lippen from kindergarten to 12th grade. I highly recommend Ben Lippen! Ben Lippen is a wonderful Christian school. I love Ben Lippen and feel blessed that I have the opportunity attend. The teachers are engaging and disciple us daily. I feel like they truly care for me. If I ever need help they are willing to take the extra step and work with me before or after school. It's a safe, and loving community for my whole family! Ben Lippen is a wonderful school! I know my children are being taught by amazing teachers. They are receiving a top-notch education and learning valuable skills like critical thinking, even in the elementary school! I have no doubt that my children are getting the best education in the Midlands! Our third child is now in the high school at Ben Lippen. We have been a part of the school community for 14 years . We count it as one of the greatest blessings of our lives. I would say that one of the unique benefits of this truly Christian school is that the teachers approach their work as a ministry. They pour into their students in a way that makes the students feel loved, encouraged and challenged. My two older children were wonderfully successful in college and still hold dear their memories of the years at BL. You simply cannot underestimate the value of the scripture memorization starting in 4K. We are very grateful for BenLippen and the privilege of being a part of this special community! Enrolling our children in Ben Lippen School has proven to be one of the single best decisions we have made as their parents. The "family-like" community coupled with strong administration and teachers, who love on our children, along with strong educational instruction inside the classroom has brought more value to our children and our family than we could have ever envisioned. Ben Lippen is a community, a family, an education, a school unlike any other! We are in our fifth year at Ben Lippen and can say with full confidence that we wouldn't choose any other school in Columbia for our girls. We absolutely love the teachers and staff. We love the fellowship and community we have with other like minded parents. But most importantly, we love that the Word of God is woven throughout every aspect of their education. It has been such a blessing to have our children at Ben Lippen for the last ten years. Not only have they received a wonderful education, but they also have had the opportunity to grow up in a Christian community where they are loved and discipled. We love the family-centered environment and are thankful for the role Ben Lippen plays in our children's lives. Two years ago, I would have never thought I would be exploring options for our children's education. We were very comfortable and happy with our former school. Some changes made me realize that there were more opportunities outside of "my bubble." While I was very hesitant and disliked the circumstances that brought about the need for change, I now realize my children have had opportunities and will continue to have opportunities that did not exist in our former school. Ben Lippen is preparing our children to excel academically all the while promoting Christian values and morals that will help mold them into great leaders of tomorrow. We could not have found a more perfect match for our family! This school has been such a blessing to our family. We are Christians and wanted a school environment that was both academically challenging and supportive of our faith values. We found both in Ben Lippen. Our daughter has now graduated and is attending Clemson University. Our son is currently in 10th grade. We have had a, overall, great experience with the teachers. We weren't even sure we could afford the school at first, but after much prayer, applying for financial aid, and making some personal decisions, we have been able to see both of our children covered financially. Our kids started attending in K-5. We have never regretted choosing Ben Lippen. Ben Lippen School has been an excellent experience for our family academically, athletically, and spiritually. We are immensely thankful for this opportunity. Our experience has been a huge blessing! Ben Lippen is one big family that loves on and cares for my kids. I always feel like my kids are in a safe environment when I drop them off every morning. I know that when or if I have any problem they will bend over backwards to help solve any issue! Our family has been involved with Ben Lippen for over 14 years. My oldest two are now out of college with successful careers and my youngest is a junior in the high school. What a blessing!! The school is solid, the teaching excellent, the extra curricular activities plentiful, and the community outstanding. I honestly can't imagine going through the teen years without the ministry of BL to support the family and Christian values we teach at home. The dedication of the teachers and staff to serve the Lord by faithfully caring for and loving our children is evident. The community and teaching at BL helped prepare my children for the challenges of college life that can derail so many. As my oldest son said after a grueling initiation week into his military college, "Now I know why it was so important to memorize scripture all those years at Ben Lippen..I needed them this week!" My husband and I will be forever grateful for the Lord's marvelous and gracious provision for our family at Ben Lippen School. My son's first year at Ben Lippen School has been amazing! From our initial visit, the presence of God was evident, with the students and faculty. Our son is receiving a Christ-centered education from a faculty that exhibits daily how much they care about his development: academically, spiritually, and socially. If we chose one word to describe Ben Lippen, it would be family. Observing how students, parents, and the staff interact, genuine care and love is evident. The peace we feel knowing our son is at Ben Lippen is immeasurable. He is being prepared for success, while living a Godly life. Sending your child(ren) to Ben Lippen will be the best decision you make; it has been for us! Ben Lippen School has been such a blessing to our family. The teachers and staff are so caring and supportive. My children love going to school every day. I know that my girls are being prayed for and that their teachers are sharing the word of God with them in all that they are learning. You cannot put a price tag on this! Along with superior academics they have access to an extensive list of extra curricular activities. My children are such a gift and therefore CHRISTIAN education is not an option. We are so thankful for all that Ben Lippen School has to offer and are confident that this is the best decision we have made for our girls. I could go on all day about Ben Lippen and how much we love our school. God is there-all day, everyday and every night, in every person, classroom, hall, gym, office, and on the fields. And we are growing in leaps and bounds thanks to Gods glory. We started school here a month into 3rd grade and my son is now in 9th grade. The best educational decision we've ever made!! Ben Lippen is a wonderful school! BL has been a great place for my kids to grow learn and be challenged. They have grown in their faith and have had many wonderful opportunities in sports, theater, and leadership. We are so thankful to have a Christian school for our kids to attend. Having a school that believes and teaches what we do at home is a huge blessing! BL strives to be better and better every year. Super conservative. Doesn't teach students to think for themselves. Such a great school for our child! We have seen him develop in so many areas. Would highly recommend Ben Lippen to any family! Best of the best! Ben Lippen truly sets the bar for Christian education. Simply stated: We love Ben Lippen! Because of their high academic standards, our children were behind in some areas when they first attended the school, but the teachers took the time necessary to work with each of them to ensure they caught up… Personal one-on-one attention is something that not many schools provide. Their love for and commitment to their students is unprecedented. Our children not only received the attention they needed to grow academically, but they are now thriving in their classrooms… Ben Lippen believes that every student is important. They are more than a name on a roster. They are part of their family. We are so grateful God led us to Ben Lippen. Our son has flourished spiritually, academically, and athletically since coming this year. He has great teachers, mentors, coaches, and friends. We are satisfied and certain that we made the right decision. We absolutely have been blown away by Ben Lippen. All the reasons I thought we were coming to Ben Lippen are there, however these have been multiplied by so many more! I've found at Ben Lippen, we are NOT here to "keep our kids from being exposed to certain things"...we are here to EXPOSE them to the many things at Ben Lippen. They have been given so much freedom at Ben Lippen to be all that the Lord has in store for them....which is so much more than I could ever plan out for them. Ben Lippen has been a fantastic place for our sophomore and senior in high school to began attending school after years of home-schooling. They have been welcomed, cared for, and challenged academically and spiritually by staff and faculty. The atmosphere is positive, encouraging and points them in the right direction. They have already made some wonderful memories and new friends in their first year at Ben Lippen while they are being well-prepared for their future endeavors. Our family is thrilled for our kids to attend Ben Lippen. Our children are thriving there. Ben Lippen is extended family to us. They provide a safe learning environment for their students and teach from a Biblical worldview that aligns with what our family values. One thing that strikes us is the importance that the teachers and faculty place on being relational with the students. As parents to a teenager, this is something that matters to us greatly. We knew Grace would flourish within the school and we loved knowing that our kids’ teachers would know and care about them personally. Our children aren’t just another number; they are souls that matter deeply to the heart of God and will matter to their teachers. Our family has become known by the faculty, staff and other students. We feel the family environment, care and love that Ben Lippen has to offer. We feel the Holy Spirit’s presence in this school. It is a place we trust will come alongside our family in raising our children to know Jesus and learn what it means to walk with Him daily and honor Him in all we do. We know an eternal impact is being made in the lives of our children by choosing Ben Lippen for our family! I have had elementary age children at Ben Lippen for 6 years now and I am a very happy parent. My children are challenged academically and spiritually. The school has a high standard for behavior and character. The teachers and staff couple the high standards with love, so, the children know that the teachers expect a lot from them but it is also a safe place for them. Ben Lippen has grown so much in the past three years and they have grown very successfully. Their staff hiring choices continue to impress me. They really find great people who are very qualified and are walking with God daily. I can’t wait for my children to enjoy all the wonderful opportunities that await them in the upper school. There are so many ways afforded to students to grow in Christian character and to know and love God. We love this school. Ben Lippen School (BLS) has been a God sent for our girls. We home schooled our oldest daughter for middle school which we were blessed we could keep her home for a difficult time for children. As we were finalizing plans to do the same for our youngest daughter, God had other plans. He showed me private schools that we have thought over twice before. We started mulling over the idea of reconsidering private school for our oldest daughter’s high school years. Then we decided we would also send the youngest as well if they were accepted. This way there would not be any missed experiences shared from the oldest and no room for competition in the home. It was the best decision we could have made for our family. We don’t have the same worries as we did when our daughters attended public school. Our daughters also have a new perspective on being more Christ-like, school, and their overall educational goals. They absolutely love BLS!! They can’t wait to get to school in the mornings and we have to pull them away from school in the afternoons.BLS is a place that we feel our girls are safe, well educated, and most importantly are learning to put God first in everything they do. They are comfortable talking about God with their peers without feeling they will be shamed. That is all we can ask for for our family. BLS has become a family away from home for us. We fellowship through camps, mission trips, football games, home coming, coffee mingle, and other school events. Be open to a Christian education it has been a wonderful experience for our family. The investment is well worth iWhat I have learned is when God speaks, be open to listen and explore even when you think a situation is impossible. Because with God, any and everything is possible you just have to have faith the size of a mustard seed. Moving our children to Ben Lippen was one of the very best decisions we've made. The quality of education is unmatched! And the support by all faculty and administration is personal and valuable - they really do care about the overall wellbeing of each and every student! There's an intentional effort to develop each student in every way, academically, socially, spiritually, etc. The administration is focused on what's best for the students, and continues to make decisions that prove that. We love our BL family!

column3: Seems relatively organized so far. Concerned that there may not be enough books for students. New to the area new to the school district. Driving farther than the nearest high school due to some recent redistricting. The staff has been very welcoming and I have been pleasantly surprised by the manners of the student body. For such a large school the staff does a remarkably good job of personalizing their interaction with students and parent. So far very pleased! There is a bullying problem at this school. Bullying distracts from learning. While the official stance is that bullying is not tolerated, the reality is that bullies are not dealt with, and the children who are bullied are scolded for allowing it to get to them. There are a huge number of students who are Baker Acted from this school, while students who are really in need of help go without it. I'm a student at this school and I don't like it. I just came here as a new student from Virginia and I'm a rising senior. The student population to me I think, is just rude and unfriendly, it seems like you have to go out of your way just to get someone to become your friend. The school only cares about their ROTC program and nothing else, like Acting, Art, Band, Chorus, etc...the administration and teachers need to start encouraging students to do well...have regular meetings with the students to encourage them and make sure everybody is doing well...they need to step up their game! Education in the state of Florida is much different and easier than it is up north...this is why florida is low in test scores, etc. This school is the worst school by far my child has attended. The only good thing is the ROTC program. If your child has special needs especially Asperger's, ADHD, Sensory, ETC. Then look some where else. They don't care nor follow the students IEP. They escalate the student rather than find a solution. They don't advocate for the child. They don't find solutions. The assistant principal for your child is never on campus nor the ESE dept. I have had to call the school board, CARD (center for Autism and related disorders), I have consulted a lawyer and have called, emailed and shown up at the school. this is so sad because the person who loses in all of this is my child. I find that most situations could be avoided, teachers are not educated about special needs therefore they make matters worse. They tell your child they can do something then write them up for that same thing. Again, if you have a child with special needs!!!!! I urge you NOT TO ATTEND THIS SCHOOL. All you will find here is frustration, stress, sadness, and a teenager depressed with low confidence about their capabilities that were not there before they arrived at this school!!!!!! The absolute worst high school imaginable. Being a student there actually feels like being in "Mean Girls" or some other comedy movie that portrays typical high school students with all of their worst traits accentuated. Students there suck and so does the staff. Neither of them seem to care. The deputy that works here is awful. He's constantly having kids Baker Acted and they're sent to mental health facilities for no reason at all and he gets CPS involved as well. He thinks he has the right to tell you how to parent your child. Kids are not allowed to be kids anymore. If they're even a little "different" than other kids then counselors get involved because they think the child has a "problem." I hope members of the administration, the deputy, as well as the board itself are one day served with a lawsuit and everyone loses their jobs. Children go to school to get an education, NOT to be psychologically evaluated by "experts" who don't know how to mind their own business.

column1: This school is one of the best schools in the state considering average grades and test scores. Parents and students have a choice to choose either local or online classes for their children, while keeping themselves up to date on the JMC grade website. They have many extra-curricular activities and clubs to keep your child involved while world class teachers are helping as much as they can. Triton is one of a few schools that have Senior Seminar which helps seniors get ready for their life beyond school, creating a project, writing an oral paper and then showing what they did to a board of adults; including teachers and public officials. I would recommend this school to anyone who wants a full 4 year high school experience that really involves in everything the student needs to help them achieve their goals. I believe the school is still small enough to really get to know the students and big enough to offer great opportunities for learning.
