column3: Very happy my daughter made the commitment to leave her neighborhood school and dare to walk her own path in life. She has made some very good connections and friends that she would have never made if she stuck to the same old thing that was fed to her through APS. The classes are smaller, the teachers and counselors are always available, and there is no reason for any student not to pass their classes. After school and Saturday help is also available. Parents and Students need to start thinking outside the box. The world is a much different place than where we grew up in., and so are schools and education. As a graduate of this school, I have mixed emotions about this school. While my parents would recommend this school to anybody simply because I graduated; I on the other hand, do not recommend this school. The grading system in the Math courses is rediculous to the other systems. It does not challenge the student and makes it quite difficult for the student to recover from a bad quarter. Also, since the math is nothing like any college math problems, you have difficulties with going into college level math. The English program kind of helps, but it does not help you grow in your writing style until the last year and one year does not help with growing your writing style. However, the teachers will help you when you need to....but it feels more like a "crash course" more than actually learning the material. I do not recommend this school unless you want your child to have a decent learning experience with somewhat little learning. Amy Biehl is strictly for those who are planning on going to college, it is not a school to get credits you are missing or to attend just for you diploma. Because it is labeled a charter school does not mean it is easy. Amy Biehl has a structure set up from sophomore year to senior year that helps understand and learn concepts of writing, reading, and developing work habits to prepare you for college. The teachers are wonderful they will help you of you ask at an appropriate time and encourage you seek help because the work can be difficult and overwhelming. I've heard people say that some class structures are harder than those at moderate colleges and I've yet to find out because I haven't graduated, but my experience with my college class was much easier than any class junior or senior year. The only teacher that doesn't offer frequent help and encouragement is Jax Sanchez, she often gets upset when you ask for help or a better explanation and thinks that when she explains something the first time we will get it and be okay which does not work. Another issue with the school would be the athletic programs, the athletics are unlike APS so it makes it difficult for athletes who are competitive at any sport to try and excel to the next level. Overall Amy Biehl is good school for those who want to go to college, if you are an athlete than I would recommend going to a public school because it'll be easier balancing work and sports and you will have a greater opportunity as an athlete. The experience that I have had at Amy Biehl High School has been overall very mediocre. The relationships that I created to staff during my time at this school are one's that I value greatly. Many of the teachers that I forged great bonds with have left and have been with sub-par teachers with little experience. I don't blame the teachers though, I blame the hiring process and the low skill set of efficient teachers in Albuquerque. Amy Beihl's Curriculum is very progressive/liberal, almost to the point that I would not recommend any children who may have conservative views to attend this school. This was most prominently modeled for me in sophomore year.This school is very difficult and should not be taken lightly upon entry. This is a school that will consume about 75% of your waking time if you want to do well. I wouldn't have gone anywhere else for high school, and I appreciate all of the opportunities I have been given through Amy Biehl. However, this is a school for someone who is diligent about their work and willing to learn. The workload is intense but is often worth while. The main issue I have had with my time here is that if you want to go ahead of the class or start on something else it's not necessarily allowed and the class can become boring. I've really only had this issue with senior year. I do recommend Amy Biehl because I believe it is the best Albuquerque public school, but it really depends on the person attending as to whether or not they'll be a good fit. This school has given me so much support through out the years. It is amazing, I mean you really have to stay on top of everything but if you do that, communicate with your teachers, the community and bond with them is amazing. Its a relationship that you will take with you. Choosing to attend this school has really changed my life and changed it for the better. It has put me on track to the life that I want as a college-bound student. The school is very community-based and has lots of support. The curriculum supports the community, and before, in middle school and elementary school, I found it hard to fit in and found myself picked on a lot. Coming to Amy Biehl, that disappeared, and i found myself many friends. There are about 150 freshmen that enter the school, and only about 50 seniors that leave the school. These are the students that are college bound. Many students leave the school, and those who stay are ready. ABHS has a rabid Social Justice Warrior curriculum that focuses on white guilt and revisionist history at the expense of the three R's, but it's still an alternative to APS. Best for kids who wouldn't fit in at a big-box school. Good teachers for the most part, but they tend to lose their best to other schools after a couple of years. Some don't belong in the teaching profession at all. There is a substantial volunteer-hour requirement that would be better spent, you know, learning real academic subjects. Still, AT LEAST IT ISN'T APS. Better than most high schools, we are given a lot of freedom, which makes us feel trusted. Going year round really helps when it comes to remembering things from the previous year.

column1: Burlington High School has some good attributes; mainly a number of awesome teachers who are excellent educators who go above and beyond the call of duty, stand outs I know of are in history, language, and the music program is excellent. Unfortunately this is countered by *way* too many teachers who have made it their mission to pass their personal political viewpoints onto their students. So, if you want your kids to embrace socialism, be taught that race and ethnicity define who people are, learn why America and the west--and law enforcement-- is intrinsically racist and bad, & why the world would be a better place without white males, then this is the school for your kids...I haven't been particularly impressed with the science program either, which is surprising considering we are in MIT-land. Although, to be fair, my kids are underclassmen so that could change. Also, maybe as in most high schools these days, who knows, there seems to be a fair amount illegal drug use. Vaping is certainly widespread, and such a problem that they often shut most of the bathrooms down to try and stifle that issue, but with only 3 minutes in between classes and an expansive building having 2 bathrooms open can be pretty miserable for students. I feel a little bad writing this are there are some really caring, decent people who do a great job at Burlington High. However, there are just too many negatives to say it's a good school. I honestly can't wait to get my kids out of there.

column1: I love this school. I barely went here my junior year and I am happy that I am going to graduate from here. This school deserves more credit! I understand that it has its problems..like every school. But this school is something else. My peers are family, I love them. The people are easy to get along with and welcome everyone for the most part, There exists no cliques....everyone comes together. The teachers are great, though there are some that are a bit rough. The counselors..lead us in the right path. This school is really great. I hear from other schools and how they have conflicts and I'm just baffled since I've never seen that here. Yeah, we have problems with test scores, but we're on our way up again. Teachers care about the students and the staff just want us all to succeed. One of my teachers once told me, "We're here to support these students, sometimes we're the only ones there to help them succeed." There is a magnificent peer leadership program and a huge number of clubs. We have the AVID program and tutoring almost every afternoon. I am the fifth out of my sisters to come here and I am the fifth who is on her way to college. I have had two students attend and graduate from San G. Both graduated with high honors. The AVID program was very helpful in guiding both students with college preparation. San G. also offers a parent clinic which informs parents about the college application process and financial aid. The key to success is to be an active parent and allow your student to participate in school activities. Both of my students were very active in sports and school activities.

column3: -It is flat out a bad school. Now that i have kids of my own i would never put they through what i went through there educational standards are too low Get some new teachers and administrators . Students need to have gone examples to follow so they can expand their knowledge and experience. Great school with great teachers, parents and student. The school is a safe place for everyone that comes in. I absolutely love this school. The teachers truly care about their students. The people at PHS are amazing, students and teachers alike. The administration at this school takes the time to make the students feel like they are important. The teachers really care about their students. You can find programs at the school for any student: everything from rigorous academic programs for those kinds of students and excellent fine arts, to career and technical programs like auto and agriculture. There is a lot of diversity in courses (sport psychology, film history, American wars, etc.). The culture of the school feels like a family. Attentive administration and staff. Very helpful and dedicated to the students! The students are amazing! They provide an excellent environment to learn together. Faculty care about the students and go out of their way to help the succeed. Students and community have a great attitude. I am here to say that Payson High School is NOT Trash. Often we are viewed as a trashy school, this is a stereotype that we are trying to break free of because not everyone does drugs, not everyone gets pregnant, and not everyone has failing grades. This is a good student body and a good school. No it's not perfect but it's not as trashy as everyone makes it sound. And yes our football team has not had a great past, but this year we have made progress, a lot of progress. A football team, a few failing grades, a few bad choices do not define a school or the students in it. Payson High has pride to be proud of, because WE ARE A NEW PAYSON! Amazing! I love how much this school cares for each individual student! I am grateful for this schools influence on the kids and how they treat them all as individuals and not just numbers. Everyone I have spoken to or have had to speak with has been fantastic! Just an amazing school! Alright Besties buckle up for the best review. I am literally in love with my Payson. We have the funnest people, teachers and students. The BEST student section and I love my high experience. Clubs are fun, classes are cool! I love my school so much!!!

column3: I graduated in 2005 and there were more than 180 buckets catching water upstairs. They actually had to stop using 3 of the classrooms upstairs because they were full of buckets. Most days they only turned on about 1 of every 10 lights to save on utility bills. I managed to get a decent high school education thanks to a couple incredible teachers but they usually don't last long due to ingroup-outgroup dynamics and the ridiculous administrative turnover. The school is terrible, all the money for the school goes to sports mainly wrestling. none of the textbooks are up to date. us as students dont get the education we need that is why this school is poorly and sadly misfortunite. I am an ex-employee of Perry, OK School District. I found the Superintendent, Timothy Smith, to be a smug, self-satisfied autocrat who has converted his office into a virtual throne room. His less-than-stellar administration has resulted in Perry High School's poor performance vis-a-vis neighboring high schools. I am genuinely sorry for the students, faculty and ancillary employees squashed under this tyrant's thumb. As an update in 2013, the high school has been completely renovated now. There is a brand new elementary school, and the middle school has has some updating also. There is a new superintendent who is a Perry native and alumni, and has been a teacher at the high school. Things have greatly improved in Perry schools! Also, you will rarely find a community that supports it's schools so strongly. I graduated from these schools in the 90s, and my children attend them today. My children briefly attended another Oklahome school of roughly the same size (slightly larger), and it was a great disappointment after the Perry schools. Perry was more advanced, cooperative and caring by far. I moved my kids back to Perry schools!

column1: My experiences are in the elementary school. Our teachers are the true heroes in this school. They are working with limited parental as well as administrative support and resources. However, after volunteering weekly in my children's classrooms, the focus is way off base within the administration. This place is not preparing my students for the competitive educational world they will soon enter. The school board is focused on daily district finances and no one is talking about creative educational ideas to get parents involved and students inspired. This place is technologically antiquated with computers freezing so frequently, that our students cannot complete their daily reading tests. No extra activities of any kind, no science fairs, or art classes, let alone art fairs. The district administration and school board are extremely slow to react and focusing on one foot in front of the other and no real future vision for our students. The PTO is plagued with the same virus, is disorganized and virtually non-exsistant within the school. Communication is awful. Very disappointing experience and I plan to put my children in a private school nearby. Teachers to student ratio is excellent . Lots of new teachers bringing new ideas each year I have seen . A big change since our last student attended ,it was 6 year age difference. Farmington just won an award from the Japanese American society, the award was started to honor an Illinois nobel prize winner. This award is usually earned by wealthy schools like Naperville, new trier and private academies. But Farmington won the award in 2015 and is up for the 2017 award.Farmington is a rural school yet has amazing teachers and opportunities. For the recent paarc testing the teachers put together a hip hop parody. There are talented children iffarmers, several children of physicians, university professors and caterpillar workers all working together.For a small school we offer wrestling, golf, football, girls volleyball, basketball, bass fishing club, and we are working towards a soccer co op.We partner with our newly constructed town library to offer summer programs to prevent reading loss that school kids experience.All located close to Bradley university, one of the best mid sized privaye universities in the U.S.We have out share of whiners, but when there is a field trip of 27 kids, you will find 9 parents attending. This was the case when our 3rd graders earned a grant for building a replica of the titanic out of milk cartons, which was on display at the Peoria museum during the travelling titanic exhibit.

column1: While I believe BJA to be a good place for any child whose parents are looking for a Christ centered education for their children, this is not an easy school to transfer to as a high school student coming from a public school They comb through your transcripts and look for any thing that stands out, both good and bad. They decided against accepting my child because of a couple of grades were not up to par for them and they would have wanted them to retake classes that they successfully received credit for at their school from another state, even though this high school is nationally ranked. They are a private school so they have the option to be picky and they are. The reason for the two stars is because I feel their approach is judging and not helping. . . . which is not the proper mind set for a Christian school. The structure and curriculum is wildly effective with our kids. We had them at two other private schools before finally getting into BJA. We were interviewed by the school administrators before they accepted our application. it's a long process to get in and many parents apply while they are pregnant. My wife and I are a mixed race couple and that has no effect on how we are treated and were surprised to see so many other mixed race couples with their kids at BJA. Not at all what we had been told. They also email us during the school day if there is an issue (behavior or we forgot something) and that is very comforting to know how attentive they are to the parents being involved. Highly recommend. Good security as well, and the car line is awesome, they get your kids out of the car and escort them into the building. and have gone out of their way if we forgot something to get it to the children in the classrooms. the teachers are great! polite and professional at all times. both kids are learning so fast its wonderful to see the results.

column3: Great school if your kid is gifted. Otherwise, only so-so. School is big, so they can afford to lose a bunch of kids and still have good overall ratings. The principal said 90% of the kids at the school are successful (meaning they graduate). That leaves out 150 of the current students. That's a lot for an area as successful as Westport The School design assists students with A select atmosphere to study, the students have room to grow and have advantages of the most proper equipment in all areas of study and fitness. Excellent school system, teachers, administrators, facilities, teamwork. Demanding academically, rich music and art program, excellent sports teams for both boys and girls. Staples High School when it comes to the facts is easily one of the top public schools in the Nation and even competes with highly regarded private schools. However when it comes to the true nature of the school, I find it not to be as perfect as its status. This school is the equivalent of Harvard in education and Alabama in football compared to other schools.: but its a public school. Believe it or not, that actually is one of Staples greatest faults. This school is built for students of the absolute utmost excelance on the sports field and in the classroom. If you are anything average, you don't really realize how special this school is because you dont get to play on the brand new turf field or take part in the incedible honors program. Here if you are a genius, an athlete or both you have everything but if not, Staples ranking in the nation isn't so easy to comprehend. I'm a 3.6 student who plays for a poorly respected Ice Hockey Team, but I love it. I just thought I'd offer the other side to a school which is almost always seen as being the best. Not academically rigorous, does not compare with private schools and boarding schools in CT. I was at private school all my life but I went to staples for high school, because it was supposed to be good and private school was getting expensive. I went to staples for a two years- I took a lot of AP classes and a lot of the teachers barely followed the strict "AP" curriculum, and did not prepare us at all for the AP tests. I did so well at staples in AP and honors classes simply because they were TOO EASY; and other kids do well for the same reason. It is a rich town so it does not face the troubles that other public schools in CT do (i.e. bridgeport central); so it rates high as one of the best/high funded schools in the state but it isn't necessarily the most rigorous. I went back to my old school , and I learned a much more there, from much better teachers who cared about their students, than I ever did at staples. The kids at staples were racist, homophobic, and just generally arrogant and mean. My peers from my private school were much more mature and humble, even though they came from the same wealthy backgrounds, and some wealthier, than staples kids. My 2 kids went through Staples and both landed in top universities, secured internships and went immediately into careers with complete financial independence. Both children were well balanced between academics, athletics and artistic pursuits. They are well rounded adults with a huge network of friends from their time at Staples. They are truly moving and shaking in the real world. Enough said! Both my kids love this school. Great support from teachers in what they are interested in. So many teachers go the extra mile to make sure kids understand the material. When one of my kids bombed a test, the teacher sought her out and explained why. Since then she got straight A's. Extra curricular activities are excellent. It's a safe school and the children are respectful of each other. Great attitude of school staff. The adminstration listens to parents and adjusts proactively (happened twice in last year alone). We moved from California Bay area, and compared even to the private schools there, Staples is a notch higher. Recommend! Our son is truly thriving at school. Teachers actually care about their students. Strong curriculum with depth and students are well prepared for college. Their top students last year headed to Harvard, Yale and other top institutions We intended to move to Westport "just for the schools" but after much thought decided to keep our kids in the Norwalk school district. We came to the conclusion that compared to Brien McMahon and Norwalk high schools, Staples high is in actuality equally rated and not all that. More modern classrooms though. Brien McMahon high in Norwalk offers an international baccalaureate degree, which is demanding to get. And a global studies program. Norwalk high has early college courses, students can graduate with a highschool diploma AND an associates degree Can wholeheartedly confirm that the Norwalk school district is without question a leader in educational innovation, new initiatives and preparing students for a competive world. Plenty of Norwalk students get into Ivy Leagues on their own merit.

column1: Seymour High School does a great job of providing a high quality education for all students. My kids have been able to pursue their dreams and have enjoyed all that high school has to offer! They expect to go to college and have great careers! The teachers are TREMENDOUS! I attended this school from 2010-2014. I would strongly advise sending your child somewhere else for high school. While there are a few great teachers here, most of them are a joke. They don't take teaching seriously, therefore leaving students with a serious lack of education. I attended during 2006 to 2010. During my time, there were a few questionable teachers and situations, but things seemed alright. However, there was very little emphasis placed on STEM courses while wood working, shop and other 'trade' classes were given emphasis and variety. At the time, there were no programming or computer science based courses outside of web design and a basic networking course. Upon graduating, going to college and visiting the community, it became clear that a lot of things changed. Also, there were situations that became extremely public because of social media and because of teachers, substitute teachers and other faculty openly discussing these situations. One situation involved a remedial teacher being impregnated by a senior. The senior involved had been very open on social media as had teachers and faculty - however, no charges were pressed and the teacher was allowed a silent exit, taking a job at another school in Green Bay. Also, there was a gym teacher, who I had, and was known for his extreme temper and for altercations that had arisen between him and parents during sporting classes. He, also, was given a silent dismissal and able to take up another teaching position in a nearby district. Don't Like it Mean Teachers And Office Staff. Allows kids at our school to get away with blatant racism. A female individual brought up a sign that said, and I quote: “If I was black I’d be picking cotton, but I’m not so I’m picking you 4 homecoming?” The boy said yes to her invite to the dance. I notified staff and was told that the situation would be taken care of. What happened next was nothing. They were given a talk to which the staff said “it’s a funny joke but it isn’t appropriate for school.” This was an inappropriate approach to the situation at hand. The couple went to the dance and to school as usual. They had gotten away with it. And because the school hadn’t punished them the students took it upon themselves to harm the female individual. If the staff would’ve done something it could’ve all been prevented. Take your kids somewhere else. my childs teacher would bully my child every day

column3: Strom Thurmond High School is a terrible school and I would not recommend it to anyone. When I am older, I will make sure that my children do not attend such a school! The lack of discipline is awful; the majority of the student population is impudent, not willing to learn, and are lacking a proper education. The advanced classes that are offered at STHS can be a little challenging at times, but let me tell you, the majority of students in them are nothing to be proud of. In STHS it seems as if the clubs and sports are more important than getting an education. The school itself is rather unsanitary; they've got cockroaches and mice running around in the place! The teachers are not entirely thorough in what they teach. One thing I especially hate is the forced participation: Several of the teachers will force you to get in front of the class and force you to work out/answer problems while at the disposal of the class, not even realizing how stressful/nerve-wracking that can be for some of the students. It should be an option to get up in front of the class and make a fool of yourself. I mean presentations are one thing, but working out problems for the whole class? No! Strom Thurmond High School would be the best high school to send your child to if you live in Edgefield County School. The school has so much to offer academically, numerous award winning extracurricular activities, and a family friendly enviroment that helps with the students learning experience and education. The school has its own magnet school, Thurmond Statesmen Institute, and has a career center that offers a diverse number of career furthuring classes. The career center is right behind the school and also has a terrific teaching staff like the high school itself. Thee school is a great school but also recognizes it has problems but what school doesnt. Except at Strom Thurmond administration dont overlook the problems but strive to fix them so the students can continue recieving the best education they can get. I am a current student of the school and I am proud to be student at Strom Thurmond High School. If I had to do it again I wouldn't change a thing. Great school. I was class of 2012 and really enjoyed my 4 years as a Rebel! Great teachers (for the most part) who really care about the students and love the subjects they teach. I would highly recommend Strom Thurmond to anyone.

column1: A hidden jewel, Brenwood High is great! My child was very prepared for college and received many scholarships. We are so glad we chose a home in the Brentwood School District. Brentwood school district offers private school quality at a public school price. While I wish there were more funds available for updating the facilities of Brentwood High, which has been serving the community for decades, we have been very pleased with the teachers, staff, and level of education our kids have received.

column1: I love St. Laurence School because we are family there. They go out of their way to help families who are struggling to keep their boys in school. They help as best they can. That is why they really can use the $20,000 because they are always trying to help our families. It feels like home! The staff, teachers, parents and students are good people, who really care about the well being of each and every student! Leaders are born here and heart of gold are found here! Life is Good! Saint Laurence always makes you feel welcome. A diverse group of students along with a great ciriculum. Numerous clubs for you to join to keep you involved even if you aren't in a particular sport. The school has something for everyone and is reasonably priced. Quality and personable teachers make for a great experience. My son just graduated from St Laurence. He worked hard and was in the top 10% of his class. If your son wants a HS experience where he gets to be in individual and not just a number, then you should send him here. Teachers were very interactive with him. You can call and speak directly to the principal or any other administrator. St L costs less than other private HS in the area and they arent always twisting your arm to make donations. Sure there is fund raising but ST L doesnt pressure or make mandatory donation requests..Whatever activity my son wanted to try he, he was given an opportunity to succeed. My wife is a teacher and felt that the staff at ST L was excellent. No school is perfect, but ST L was perfect for my son. ST L isnt an ultra-competitive school in sports or academics, but both students and staff try really hard and care about each other. If I had more boys, Id definitely make them Vikings. My older son graduated from Marist and wasnt happy he went there becuz Marist got too big. I tried to talk to the principal about an issue my son had at Marist and he never responded even after several contact attempts. What a great school for boys. My son was welcomed on his first day as a Freshman and this experience was just the beginning. This is a tight, highly involved environment that brings out the best in each individual. Now a senior, he has become very involved with the schools activites. Kudos to Mr. Muting. He really knows what he is doing. I'm so glad we sent our son here. St.Laurence is an over all great school. The teachers did a great job with handling my disability and giving me the accommodations I needed to succeed. If you want to make friends at St.Laurence join sports or clubs, there are many to chose from. The sports programs are doing very successful, I wouldn't be surprised if they win championships in the up coming years ;notably football, baseball, and soccer. The only down fall is the dean of students, he is over strict and not many people like him. St.Laurence is a great school if your deciding high schools, choose St.Laurence

column3: I am Parent of student who is aspirant of getting addmission in this wonderful school. Tucker is a good place to be. We learn about real world situations and learn from our differences. There is 'unity in diversity' and we have to work on it continuously. Tucker is amazing! The diversity just makes the school so much more fun! And the fries are love! JR Tucker High School is extremely diverse. We all are from across the world. Though there are many different nations and languages at the school, we all are united by our passion for being apart of the Tiger Nation. this school is the best. i love it because there is no bullies and there is not alot of fights. our officers does every thing to keep it safe. it has some nice teacher. and i really feel safe in it. Best four years of my life! Tucker being a high school with three specialty centers (Advance College Academy, IB, and World Languages/Immersion), the people in and out of all classes are usually very accepting and fun to be with! Teachers work to their best abilities to make sure all students understand their courses and they are very passionate in what they teach. Even though the school "looks" rundown and old, it's actually more beautiful than what meets the eye. I LOVE the art walls and the campus life-style. Words cannot describe my fondness for this school. I graduated with many memories and life skills. Love everything and everyone at this school! Everyone is excepted Very satisfied. The school has complied when I’ve requested meetings. The administrators will take & return calls. The school provides many extracurricular activities and volunteer opportunities for students to become engaged in and expand the student learning experience. This is a great school. The leadership is supportive and positive and the kids are so caring towards each other. A hidden gem! Finding a teacher who genuinely cares about their job and the kids (and isn't burned out) is rare anymore. At least in the Henrico County school district. If there are any of these teachers at Tucker, I haven't come across one yet in the 3 years my child has been there. The amount of bullying, fights, illegal substances and lack of learning that happens at Tucker is ridiculous. A new building isn't going to help. going here is truely a experience! When you go to tucker you’ll definitely find your group of people . There are a lot teachers that genuinely care for you. One of my personal favorites is Mrs.Jhonson , she’s a great science teacher. The learning and education is good and helped prepare me for high school, but the community is a toxic wasteland with borderline racists. Teachers tend to coddle white kids and ignore whatever things they do that could get other POC in trouble. They also showed more polite gestures towards other white kids and ignore others in the morning before school starts.During middle school, I had a heavily stressful time and even cried a few times because I got in trouble for a trivial thing that never even happened. A teacher I had would usually give me weird stares whenever I talk to my friends during class. I had a stressful time in their class because I was not naturally good at that subject as some other kids were and highly cared about my grades. One day, I was walking to school and they called me because I was accused of saying something I didn't say, started to yell at me, and thought I was lying even though they had no evidence of such incident other than some other kid who twisted a conversation I had with my other friends. They ordered that I had to go to the principal's office after school and I thought I was at huge risk of getting suspended over something so dumb with no evidence. Luckily, nothing happened and I was cleared of the charge, but it was still so stupid. Since that day, I was more quiet and kept to myself during classes and funnily enough was glad the pandemic hit so that I can take care of my own mental health.I also have other friends who had their own struggles and issues because of things such as ADHD or dyslexia and teachers did barely anything that could help them. There is another comment that explains more about the toxicity, so I would recommend to read that too. The reason why I gave it two starts is because their education helped me personally and that I met good friends there. If your child has any learning disorders or a POC, I would think twice before sending your child there.

column1: This school district cares about kids above all else - test scores are one tiny part of an entire educational experience. Staff from custodians and kitchen, all the way up to the superintendent show care and concern for students.

column3: I am a former student of North Shore Senior High. I graduated in the top 3 percent of my class, class of 2007. I rarely did any work, honestly, if you just behave correctly teachers will pass you. I had some friends who seriously couldn't read and they still graduated. They spend way too much on their athletic programs, hence, I had to use a 20 year old calculus book they was nearly torn to pieces. Though, the orderly structure of the school is good. They do not care about education all that much. I am currently a senior at Texas A&M University @ College Station, and would like to express that if you have a choice, do not send your child to North Shore High School, unless just being satisfactory is what you want. i freaking love this school is the best in every aspect there is literally the most awful and i mean most awful school, I am currently a junior attending. I just moved here from another city and i just started 3 weeks into the school here. My expectations were high but came out disappointed at the end. The teachers are terrible, they dont care about the students, they're not helpful whatsever. The staff and teachers are so rude in my opinion. The teachers just dont care and they move too quickly. I dont know. This school is just terrible. The teachers need a reality check. Cant wait to move back to my old school next year! As a teacher, im terribly disappointed in what this school has the potential to accomplish. It has a high rate of teacher turnaround. Every year masses leave and more get hired since they do not know how to keep their teachers. They teach to a test and have the one size fits all mentality. Its also very micromanaged and thrives on favoritism. On a scale from 1-10 I'd say a 6 Excellent!! The teaching staff is very interactive, knowledgeable, and interested in helping students to achieve individual and district goals.

column1: It is a privilege to have my three children attend Edgewood. They are tackling a rigorous academic schedule, but they are learning how to function independently, challenge themselves, and lead others. They will all be well-prepared for their futures, which include a 4 year college degree. They have many opportunities to participate in sports and other extracurricular activities and have many lots of friends who have similar goals for their futures. I am so grateful to have a school like this available to my children. Edgewood is an accelerated academic college prep school. The curriculum is challenging. Recently the school was recognized as a National Blue Ribbon School and it was also recognized as a National Senior Project Certified School. Outstanding administrative leadership, teaching staff and community. Edgewood was not a very fun experience. I went there for middle school and there was no way i was going to stay there another 4 years. You are so sheltered and there is no time to socialize or have any fun. They hardly have any sports and the what they do have arent very good. I have to admit though that the drama department is pretty amazing and a lot of fun. Other than that, school is boring. No school spirit and no homecoming events (other than the dance). I am now a Junior at Merritt Island High and the decision to change schools was the best one i have ever made. At MIHS, the variety of classes are huge and the teachers are a lot nicer and dont stress you out so much. The school is a lot of fun and i absolutly LOVE going to school. If you want your child sheltered from the real world and looked at as a "Nerd" by the rest of the community, then Edgewood is the perfect place. But dont be fooled, its not as great of a school as others make it out to be. I am proud to say that i will be a MIHS graduate instead of a EJSHS one. Hope this was helpful and GO MUSTANGS!! My daughter is a senior and has attended Edgewood for the last 6 years. This is a school for kids that what to be challenged in a enviorment where other kids are there to learn. It's nice to have her at a school where the other kids and parents have the same values and beliefs. My daughter has attended Edgewood since the 7th grade and she is getting ready to graduate this year from high school with her AA degree which was fully paid for by the county. She is fully prepared to attend college and Edgewood was instrumental in that preperation. It is NOT for kids that want to have "fun" in highschool and are overly interested in their social life. It is absolutely the school of "nerds" and they revel in it. The most popular children are the best actors in the drama department and the best students, not the cheerleaders or athletes. All of the classes offered at Edgewood are Honors or AP, there are no easy classes. They do not tolerate bad behavior and they do not hesitate to kick out students that can't maintain at least a C average. It is the perfect school for kids that are high achieving, goal oriented, self-motivated, determined and those who aspire to great educational heights. If they want to be the next footbal phenom, this is not the place for them. I am so grateful to the principle (who was my high school literature teacher at MIHS) for developing this school into what it is today, a school that not only wants nerds for students but caters to them. I loved Edgewood, and I've been there since 7th grade. I am now about to graduate from college and was accepted to Isenberg School of Management at UMass, and I can honestly say that going to Edgewood was an advantage. I currently hold a 3.7 gpa and I owe it all to the extensive preparation and determination of the staff. I breezed though the first two years of college thanks to the coursework we were prepared for. Seriously, if the students and parents would stop complaining about the course load, then take your kid elsewhere because Edgewood prepares you for the REAL WORLD. And when is anything ever easy in the real world? Edgewood "edged out" Westshore as the best high school in the Brevard County according to US News for 2014 (6th vs 9th in Florida). You can't go wrong with either of them but I'm really glad our daughter will be attending Edgewood in the fall instead of the one she's zoned for as middle school could be quite tough as she's very shy. I'm glad she's an ideal fit for Edgewood. I am a former student. I remember when I would meet other kids from other schools... They would ask me what school I went to. When my response was "Edgewood," I would always expect a chuckle out of them. People all around Brevard County called Egdewood "the nerd school." Now, as a former Edgewood student/current college student, I laugh at the people who laughed at me. Sure, we are kind of nerdy, but because we are smart? I'm not quite sure how that is something to laugh or poke fun at. Weren't #1 in sports, but we were were the ones who got Merritt Island on the list of the top 50 schools in the nation. The NATION. Some students left Edgewood complaining that the teachers assigned "too much hard work," but right now, as a college student, I could not be more grateful for all of the college prep Edgewood provided me. Too much work? Too hard? Welcome to the real world, which, might I add, is not easy! I'm so glad I didn't go to a school that just let me breeze by my classes. I am proud to say that I went to a "nerd school" because compared to the other student bodies that I graduated with, MY class is excelling in colleges all around the nation. Edgewood is a fantastic school! I have one child who has just graduated from Edgewood and two who are still attending. I have been delighted with the education that all my children have (and are still) benefiting from. The teachers are committed to excellence and really seem to care about their students. The number of kids that are getting into Ivy League (or equivalent) schools is impressive. If you are interested in sending your child to a school that focuses on academics and has high standards - this is it! Keep up the good work Edgewood! I am really impressed with Edgewood. I have 2 children there. They are turning out into fine human beings. Their grades are amazing as well. The quality of the teachers is excellent . The principal is fantastic. I am sure my children are getting better education than they would in private school! (2/2) (Please make sure to read the comment before this one first.) This only applies to specific people, as I would like to say again. They are overall great people. After that, I would like to talk about something more positive. The leadership at this school is incredible. We have a great principal who does so much for us. This review is to help you, so when I say that your child may have learning disabilities, please don't go to Edgewood. I support everyone with equal respect, whether of their sexuality, race or disability. However, Edgewood won't stop for a student, rather kick them out. I hope no one will have to ever go through this, however it happens pretty often. Other students don't help if you are gay, biesexual or lesbian. I know this because this is the biggest problem at Edgewood. We have a decently large population of students who are these sexuallitys, and they will get killed over it. I myself would like to share this. I hang out with a bunch of people who are of these sexuallitys. I love each of them with all my heart and being a male, hanging out in this group, I have been called gay, a lot. And I mean a lot. The truth is, I only support these sexuallitys. I choose to mainly write this review because of this. If you go to Edgewood, you know me. I could be referred to as popular, although I don't love this title. There has been a lot of peer pressure on me to join the pop kids, not "gay", which is how they refer to them. No way, do I ever want anyone to feel this. Another this is moral. Edgewood has very very low school spirit. If you like sports, go to any school you want. Just make sure that the school name isn't Edgewood. They are very bad mostly and there is no football, baseball, wrestling or softball. But Edgewood is a great school for those who love learning, are mentally advanced, want a challenge, and can get work done. Edgewood is way better than Westshore, for everyone wanting to choose between the two. I love this school, and me personally am doing very well with it. Please read this with an open mind. This is the complete truth from a current student and someone on the inside. If you are a parent, be careful with your decision if your child is given a spot at Edgewood. If you are a kid like me, I see you, and know what's best for your future. Edgewood is going downhill fast. Most of the teachers I have right now are pretty bad. The physics teachers class average is about a 70, with those people working hard. Other teachers just use other teachers work from other schools and hand it out mindlessly. Guidance is no help for students trying to survive these classes. Guidance brushes off students and parents often. If I could go back and time and never go to edgewood, I definitely would! I am a well rounded student: mostly A’s with one B, sports, clubs, etc. Trying my hardest, I am barely getting through. Me, as well as most other students I know at edgewood are totally burnt out, and have bad mental health due to extreme stress. The school brushes this off and just tells us to time manage better or to find a tutor, as if we have the time. The student body is a mess overall. Half the students are too socially awkward to have a conversation, unlike other schools where you can make lots of friends and find your own friend group. I have had to go online to FLVS for multiple classes due to terrible teaching, which is not uncommon at edgewood! Going to school every day is a dread and struggle, I speak for lots of my peers as well.I’m a junior and considering switching schools for my senior year, to at least have one year of comfort before college.

It doesnt have the best academics, but there are much worse out there. the teachers are great and most truly care about how well you do in school and will help you out. Sports program is very good and at times can seem like sports matter more than academics in the school. Principal is not great at all, he has some rediculous ideas and lacks leadership. But he's also at the mercy of the town officials and the tribal leaders/parents.

column1: I have one child in 8th and one in 6th at Ariton. I absolutely love this small school. The teachers work so hard for our students they truly love what they do. Our administration staff is very organized and so professional providing an excellent environment for our school. We are so blessed to have a principal who cares about our school, he is always working to improve our school he helps out with PTO functions always available for parent conferences very open door policy one time I had to go to school on a Saturday to pick up some chairs, he and his whole family were all by themselves cleaning up our campus after a Friday night football game, ( that is LOVE). He makes each student feel special I LOVE AHS!!!!

column3: I'm being really nice about the 4 stars, because this school really deserves 3.5 at the moment. I've attended this school since sophomore year and I will graduate in the spring. Overall, I love LE, because the school really works for me. I'm taking mainly AP classes and I have had some really excellent teachers that made me work hard. I feel like this school is improving, but the new administration (their second year) should try not to make the kids to feel so trapped sometimes. They honest want to improve the school and I am glad for that. The transition to STARR has been difficult for my younger sibling. I did great on TAKS. I think project based learning is a joke, but I don't have to worry about that in AP. Drugs are an issue like any other high school. Also, they have one of the best Color guard/ winter guard programs in the state (a little known fact). The band is truly amazing. Football changes with the seasons, but I really think they're building up the program. The people here are diverse, down to earth, and I think there's somewhere for everyone to feel accepted. The school doesn't have a great reputation but I believe that may change! Little elm high school is terrible. They're trying to act like others schools which is not working. The more reinforcements they keep putting in this school, students are not going to do anything. Someone spilled milk on the stairs one day during lunch and now for on and til' the school year ends no one is allowed to pass the stairs, which I think is really stupid just one little incident. Teachers don't care. With intervention it's pointless thinking oh this is going to help our students well it isn't working. During an assembly their were talking about our STAAR scores saying we had the worst scores. We probably wouldn't have the worst scores if you would stop reinforcing these rules and more stricter on these students maybe we will, or if you actually took the time but no little elm doesn't take the time. Now they're going to need a new high school the freshman this year grew and it's going to keep growing as it goes soon enough they won't be able to fit them in classrooms cause its over crowded. Little elm needs to step it up and work out their problems instead of focusing on kids education 24/7 for once. Little Elm Schools have turned the corner! The new Admin is making it place where learning is taking place. Where more is expected, more is acheived. Hats off to the higher standards and increasingly better results. You know it's working when the students are saying it and the scores are steadily moving moving up. A big thanks to the focus on technology and advanced teaching methods. This is my third year in this school and this year has been the WORST!! theres one principle that blows his whistle every 5 seconds in students ears and scream at us to keep walking . especially that principle tends to make fun of us and screams it out loud so everyone can stare at you. He even told me to GET A LIFE like really to me that is very disrespectful . Just because he was from the military doesn't mean he has to treat most of us like that. i do agree that they are very rude and they keep us moving like if we were cattle or something Some of us can wait to leave that school we feel so trapped in there I moved to Little Elm last year from Plano with my husband and son who is now in his junior year. What a drastic downgrade! I wish I had paid more attention to the realtor when he warned me about the school system here before we moved. 100% financing on a home is not worth my child's future. The college preparedness is absolutely horrible at Little Elm High. It was brought to light this year that out of 27 school districts in 2 counties(Denton & Collin) their SAT scores rank last at 1352. However, I did not need to see test scores to know just how bad this school is. Before this school can get better at college prep, it first needs to be able to have students who are prepared for high school. My son tells me that that he is so far ahead of his friends, and that this school is run like a prison camp with teachers blowing whistles and acting like maniacs. This school could improve drastically if the principal and his staff would show more interest and respect for their students. Even the mature respectable students are being treated like criminals and their morale is being destroyed. Thankfully my son will be graduating next year because I want to stay in Little Elm. This has to be one of the worst schools ever! Before I moved I read some reviews but didn't believed what everyone was saying was true. But now I actually see everyone's true colors. I'm so happy that I moved far away from this school. DO NOT LET YOUR KIDS GO HERE! The students are RUDE and very DISRESPECTFUL. Despite some things about it that need serious change. As a former student here I loved it according to my perspective.The hospitality was 100 times better than the other school I later on had to attend since I moved. The friends I made were more like family and some of the teachers have done so much in their power to help and guide me. To be honest I truly miss that place because of so much memories. Now though I do believe that their does need to be some improvements to the way things work their. Test scores are pretty low and from what I feel, students need a fairer chance to pass or find a better solution than standardized tests. I could go on but I still see more good then bad from my point of view. If they can find a solution apart from T.A.K.S testing then maybe their might be a great improvement to a higher raise of test scores. Ok... we've been thru a lot. Over the course of the last 8 years, we've seen 2 superintendents, 5 principals and countless assistant principals walk in and out the doors at LE. Today, rest assured, things are looking up for Little Elm High School. When I began working at LE in 2007, LE high school was the high school everyone would want to work at and every student would want to attend and every parent would want to send their children to. We're on the path to being that way again. Kids enjoy (as much as kids can) going to school again. Teachers enjoy coming to work again and administration seems to finally care about the people in the building as much as the curriculum and test scores. Changes took place over the summer of 2014 and life is good at LE. I won't deny, things had been real bad..as bad as I've ever seen it in 25 years of teaching. I'm also proud to say things are real good now. 4 stars because we're not perfect yet but we're on the right track. We're 1 school in 1 town. We're not a cookie cutter school. We're unique. We are LE! I am a high school senior and have been attending Little Elm ISD since I was in 2nd grade. I realized what a terrible school Little Elm High School is, consequently, it all started going down hill after my freshman year. The administration changed, the students loved our new principals and assistant principals, however. But of course, they didn't last long. My favorite and BEST teachers from my early high school career that had been there for the majority of the time the school has been open, all left because they felt the same way as the students did. The frequent changes and unprofessionalism of the school drove them all away; I wouldn't have stayed neither. It was always a whole new teaching staff EVERY YEAR. In addition to that, they were new teachers with minimal teaching experience. I have been in AP/Dual Credit and advanced classes since I was in 8th grade, yet, I feel so unprepared for college and have no idea what to expect. Although I have proved my maturity with good grades and behavior, the administration still treats us like children and criminals. The disciplinary punishments are WAY too harsh and they are unfair with the punishments they give each student. If students are disrespectful at school ...............that would be a parent issue. Parents........do YOUR job at home teaching proper respect to your children so they know how to behave properly in a school environment. I'm currently a Junior at LEHS and I'm completely UNSATISFIED with the school system. multiple staff members such as principles, teachers constantly go in and out of LEHS. The majority of the staff members here INCLUDING teachers are extremely disrespectful to their peers and students. I can honestly recommend NOT to enroll/register your child to this school. I had an incident today with a teacher who had the nerve to pull my backpack because I couldn't hear them since I had my headphones in, minding my own business. to get the story straight, I've been entering these side doors to get to my class in time ever since the school year has begun. a group of teachers started raising their voice at me for attending to go into school through those doors. regardless of the age and what position these staff members are working in this school, should NOT disrespect the students. especially if you've never even seen them before. like I said, I do NOT recommend any parent to enroll their child to this school. if you want what's best for your child, ANY school besides LEHS would be best for your child. coming from a student whose been enrolled to LEHS 3 out of 4 years. People outside of the Little Elm School District do not know and understand that Little Elm may not be as outstanding as neighboring districts, but we are not terrible. I, as a student of Little Elm High school, have been going to school in Little Elm since kindergarten, from former Zellars, to Oak Point, to Colin Powell Intermediate, to Lakeside Middle school, and finally Little Elm High school, I do not regret any of my past learning experiences in Little Elm District, whatsoever. We are constantly improving and districts around us is 3 to 5 years behind, according to statistics, and are believing in the reputation we've had up to 5 years ago. We have improved greatly and will continue to do so. It is a very diverse place though in a "close-knit" community, and this gives many schools within great pride. Our teachers do not lack the teaching skills other districts have, they are just as talented, if not more. Our students are ready to learn at the right instructions and do not hesitate to ask for help. I believe Little Elm is a great environment for every individual and I myself will continue to live here and raise my future children and the many generations to come. Little Elm is overall, an average school. In my opinion that is. We have good education and academics for a small school. Yes, we're kinda overcrowded but, thats only because people keep moving into our small town. I like Little Elm HS because there isn't a lot of drama like other schools. The most we have is gossip about who is dating who. Nothing major. Also, in my experience in the schools (Pre-K - HS) I am yet to witness any major bullying. Unlike others, our school system doesn't have much of a bullying problem. When teachers find out that a student is being bullied they work hard to stop it. Trust me, I know, I've been bullied before and have helped others who were bullied. Since we're a small yet growing town, we don't have many elective classes to choose from. But, our student council along with the administrators are trying their best to add more classes. I honestly think that our school district is doing the best that they possibly can. Teachers are engaged and supportive of students. My kids are encouraged to do their best in academics and their chosen activities and electives. LEHS is a great high school. The teachers and staff create an atmosphere that values respect and fosters creativity and learning. The students are well rounded and respectful. LEHS has a spectacular Fine Arts department! The kids really become a family. The leadership is top notch! When we initially moved to the Dallas area 3 years ago we were very attracted to the soon to built K-8 STEM Academy. Since enrolling 2 of our children in this school we have gotten to know the administration led by Dr. Lowell Strike and Cynthia Mika, both of who are committed to project based learning throughout the LEISD. Our son is a junior at LEHS and has been attending LEISD since 5th grade. We love the learning atmosphere created by a smaller school district -- it allows students to stand out and succeed. We've been very happy with the administration and level of education our son is receiving. He is challenged and gaining the skills he'll need to be successful in college, but he isn't overwhelmed with ridiculous amounts of homework. Most of his classes offer a good variety of projects and application-based assignments, which engage him and help him learn far better than just reading and testing. We have had a very positive experience at Little Elm High School. This high school Seems to change administration each year. Not a very consistent and organized school. LE high school has high academic standards. it has great teachers and fabulous sports and extra curricular activities. The High school is the center of the community. Excellent schools! Proud mother of two Little Elm ISD students. Both our children earned Dual Credit for college and were able to start at the university with a year of college credit. Thank you Little Elm teachers for doing a great job! Community feel and high expectations for teachers and students. The district has undergone a major transformation the last two school years and it has had a significant impact on the high school. Little Elm High has caring teachers, high academic standards, and still feels like a small town school. Best of all they offer tons of extra curricular activities and advanced academic programs. Their technology for every child is outstanding. Lots of opportunities for parent involvement. Jusy beginning our High school journey. We have had a good beginning! Passionate teachers in their subjects.... helpful staff & most of admin. (Still some old ways of thinking in there that needs to go...in my opinion) but it is getting better! CTE choices are increasing and teaching space is in the process.of being built (completion Aug 2017 - new band hall, culinary arts area, collegiate style cafeteria and more secure entry) CTEs are a state requirement... local isd's chose what they offer.Very proud to be part of this great changing district. I feel as though my son has had a great experience thus far. This is his first year and his teachers have been extremely helpful and responsive when he shows signs of struggling. Our experience has been very good in this school and we are unbelievably happy with our son's experience at this school I graduated from here in 2016. If it weren't for me being falsely accused of doing drugs and being sent to DAEP, I would've dropped out. I took a drug test that came back CLEAN, yet was still sentenced to 30 days of DAEP. From there I found the GOALS program and it saved my academic future. Little Elm High School is terrible and so is the administration staff. Avoid LEHS at all costs and go to Lonestar High School or literally anywhere else. Really good so far, execept for they act obilivios to bullying. Amazing! Have been very happy with how my student has done and accomplished with the support and leadership of the school! Excellent school with wonderful installations and programs. So the school and the community are great on the surface.. HOWEVER School academics are well below state average and even AP courses are a joke for our son and hes not challenged at all. That alone would be enough but the consent issues with gangs/violence/ and major issues with bullying is enough to pull our son out.. unfortunately we have no other choice living in Little Elm. I like everything about my HS. Great trackers and staff as well as good friends. I have had nothing but positive experiences! Wonderful staff and course selections help prepare students for many different paths in life Overall excellent school and getting better all the time Our experience with LEHS has been AMAZING!!! Excellent! My dyslexic daughter has thrived in Little Elm. Great sense of family environment in the schools. I have had 2 children graduate from LEHS and a 3rd who will be a freshman. I have seen good and bad over the years. The District and the school are definitely headed in the right direction. Look at how old many of the negative ratings are before judging. One of the best things about LE High School is the college program. Kids can get credit for college classes starting in 9th grade. Also, the extra curricular activities are exceptional. As LE has grown it has improved tremendously. Very pleased. Stellar educational experience for gifted and talented students, with personalized collegiate support, advanced placement offering and 1:1 advanced secondary languages. Coming from an IBD program this school is top notch! Wonderful teachers, although many teachers do not last long, and the turnover rate is a known phenomenon among teachers. However, teachers do demonstrate and interest in students and are passionate and honest with students.Administration does not care about what students have to say and favor aggressive approaches to students rather than de-escalating situations, a choice unfair considering a significant portion of Little Elm students are considered low-income. It is well known that Little Elm cares much more about its athletics than its academics, and most of the budget is spent on football rather than more teachers, expansion, better career programs, etc. Even other sports and athletics, i.e. the school’s drill team and color guard, are completely ignored and don’t have the budgets that other sports do. The art program is severely lacking.

column1: I as a concerned Grandparent we go to all of our Grandchildern's concerts and it is very disheartening to go to see their performances and have to watch the person playing the piano!!!!!! We came to see our children and grandchildren perform MOVE THE DARN PIANO!!!!!!! These children work very hard all year long and for WHAT TO STAND BEHIND a piano??????? Last night was the 3rd concert this year that we COULD NOT see our grandchild!!!!! THIS STINKS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!I am NOT the only one complaining about this! It was a very good concert but it would have been an OUTSTANDING ONE if we would have been able to see our Grandchildern!!!!!!!!!!!!!!and I had three performing last night!

column3: NOT impressed. As a parent of two Centennial graduates, the school is VERY overrated. The students are snobs with an 'entitlement attitude'. Test scores aren't everything. Being a student there, I can prove that the elitist attitude is there. That isn't the biggest problem, though; the worst, by far, are the number of people with mental disorders of various kinds that stem from the academic pressure. A lot of the times, the students put much more pressure on themselves than anyone else, and this ranges into a variety of mental disorders. The numbers of children with eating disorders is frightening, and people who self-harm or have attempted even suicide are even more alarming. The teachers, though, are pretty good generally, and present challenging yet balanced coursework. All in all, it's the atmosphere that is causing the most issues. There are a more percentage of white students than asian students attending centennial high school. I have moved around a lot and all the schools in the other counties in MD are just different compared to Howard County. Centennial is the most diverse high school in Ho. Co., which I'm pretty sure is the most diverse county in MD. Anyways, CHS was the only school where i did NOT experience racism and bullying (I am a minority.) CHS also has the highest AP class enrollment and is very academically competitive. I have friends who are taking seven AP credits per year. I had to actually drop out of AP math because I could not keep up with the curriculum, since I had Cross Country, Track and NAHS. Compared to other schools in Ho Co. and other county schools, there WILL be more school work involved, but from all my college friends I've heard from, they're having a relaxed time because it's so much more "chill" in college than it was at CHS. (The one thing I can't get over is that a 2390 is considered an "average" score.) You can view it as a good or bad thing, but CHS really will prepare you for college and get more out of you than other MD schools, you just have to know your limits. :) Centennial students are achievement-oriented, and their families place a high value on education. The average student there would be a top student in many other schools. The teachers push the students to be their best, but not in a high-pressure way. I consistently hear from former graduates that college was a breeze because of the preparation they received at Centennial. Both my kids love the school. This is an amazingly competitive and diverse school. The curricula is rigorous and challenging. Also, the people are very competitive. But what I noticed immediately, is that there is no teasing, no bullying, no hatred, no violence. It was all such a shock to me when I first moved here as an African American from the South. No more racial or homophobic slurs thrown at me everyday. No more teasing because of what I love. The amount of acceptance and caring can bring me to tears any day. Very difficulty to relax at my school. The pressure to be perfect, the pressure to have the best clothes, and be involved in sports, academics, AP classes is unbearable. I know theyre trying to prepare us for school, but I hated waking up every day in High School when I went here. The teachers don't hesitate to put you on the spot and make you feel stupid, if you don't know the answer. They hide this when the review people watch them teach. I cant say enough about how horrible my high school was. I don't know if I'll go to college right away. I may travel this summer and get a job and see. I want to get far away from my pushy parents. All I want is to be happy. It does not have ad-quite staff diversity and awareness. The lack of training and understanding of cultural differences is not there. The lack of diversity in students and teacher radio is outrageous. For an area that is so close to Columbia and Baltimore. Students are bullied not only by other students also how teachers and staff administration views incidences when they are disciplining students with other cultural backgrounds. The consequences and views are looked upon differently based on race and culture. The teachers should be held accountable for their behavior and what percentage of students are passing their class and how the information is transmitted to students of better understanding. The Administration excepts teachers excuses. Yet, students are stress out because of the school goals. Centennial is pretty overrated. It isn't the powerhouse school it used to be, and now with some of it's math and physics teachers retiring, this school is going to have a significant drop off. Lastly, the front office administration is pretty horrible. Don't spend all the extra money for real estate in order to go to centennial because right now, it simply is not worth it. A lot of the past reviews say good things about Centennial, and I agree with most of those reviews. However, Centennial has been going on a downward slump for years now, and Riverhill, Marriots Ridge, and Atholton are probably better alternatives right now. I graduated from Centennial in 2009 and I would NEVER send my children here. People get so caught up on the good test scores that they ignore all the other horrible things. Teachers are elitist and snobby. Enormous bullying and clique issue. If you're not filthy rich don't expect to be treated well. Parents and teachers put so much pressure on getting perfect scores, getting into the perfect college, getting perfect grades that none of the students were happy, In fact everyone was stressed constantly. 0 school spirit or morale our senior pep rally fell silent multiple times because nobody liked eachother or the school. Our principal continually added new and ridiculous restrictions on the school for no apparent reason. AVOID at all costs. I'd much rather have gone to high school with lower testing scores and grades and a more welcome community. Academically, the school is fine -- but because of the students, not the teachers. The neighborhood is affluent and parents are educated and set high expectations for their children. With only a few exceptions, the teachers put in their time and teach to the tests. Overall, the school administration is incompetent. The best administrators in the county go to the more difficult schools and Centennial gets the second and third string. There are actually more cliques among the parents than there are among the kids and there are MANY helicopter parents who are always advocating for their children over others. That leads to a lot of favoritism and bias. For example, this year the JV football coach favors one player whose parent works for Under Armor and provides swag for the coaches and dumps on all of the other players. Consequently, there is no team spirit. Administration knows and does nothing. I wish my kids went to a school with fewer pampered parents and kids and actually learned how to deal with real world problems. it's okay. teachers aren't very good. it's mostly friends motivating each other. don't expect to fit in new people! Centennial High School has excellent teachers, involved parents and academically competitive students with tremendous school pride. I would say my experience was filled with some good memories, but there some awful ones too. My experience is really bad, there was lead in the water fountains, and they are very pressuring, and they only care about test scores and academics. I also find it very hard to make friends there. Overall, Centennial is a strongly overrated school. People talk about the magnificent test scores, which are notable (I am amongst the people who strongly value academic success and can be considered a top student here). However, this is entirely due to educated, affluent parents and students. The staff is good, but not particularly amazing while the administration isn't very useful at all. The social experience is terrible, with strongly defined cliques and friend groups. Too stressful and totally overcrowded. Frequent redistricting. Very professional staff. I would recommend this school without hesitation. I am very happy with this school. Teachers are very helpful and considerate. No doubt academic pressure is there but it’s good for the students. Those who don’t want to study please don’t join this school and keep complaining about academic pressure. As a parent I would recommend this school. Absolutely horrible, I can't wait to graduate. Very few teachers teach well, and I've had several experiences with an inconsiderate staff member. The school itself is a very toxic environment, and many students suffer from lack of sleep, stress, and depression. The only thing holding up this school's rating are the students and the few teachers that actually put in the effort to teach their students instead of expecting them to learn everything on their own. School spirit and fun are zero, so don't have high expectations. Student government is convoluted. This school has incredible and caring staff who really support the students. Best school ever for kids and adults

column1: KML is more than just a high school. It feels like a family. Of course, there are the typical cliques and "friend groups" that form within the first year or so, but everybody finds their place and sticks with it during the four years there. No matter what, people are going to care for you at KML, and that's especially shown in the classroom and during sporting events. Students are brought up and instructed according to Christian standards, to be lifelong learners and role models for everybody around them. The rigorous coursework and the sheer number of possibilities of classes allow each student to get their own, individual outcome in the end. No matter what, KML equips its students well for college and beyond.
