column3: Great quality educators, parent involvement, curriculum and school layout. Great team spirit~ They want your child to be a success as long as your child strives for it as well. Fantastic! Mitchell is an excellent school. Two of my children have graduated from JWMHS and two more are soon to follow. My two oldest daughters are in college and have received honors scholarships from Florida State as well as Bright Futures and a few other miscellaneous scholarships. I believe this is directly due to the excellent education they have received at Mitchell. The Trinity area is a wonderful place to live and the public schools are unrivaled. I have read some bad reviews dating back seven years or more which I find hard to believe. I could not have chosen a better community to raise and educate my children. My children have all flourished in this environment. They love their school and are involved in sports and social activities. I truly believe that Mitchell is the best preparation for a successful college education and beyond. GO MUSTANGS! The school is horiabbly over crowded and keep getting more crowded from all the new houses being built. There's as much as 35 students in a class and makes it hard for the student to get 1 on 1 help from the teacher. The school has outdated technology. Also the school was not designed to have a lot of students so traffic and hallways are hard yo get through. The only reason I continue to teach at this school is because of my love for the students. We try so hard to provide the students with the proper resources to learn yet when we ask administration for teaching tools we get hardly anything. The books my students use are so old and decrepit, yet the sports teams get all that they need. There are to many inappropriate relations between administration, staff and school board members. Those personal connections create an unfair advantage for many and should have been dealt with a long time ago but the schools Superintendent protects those at the expense of the students. Im a student at jw mitchell and i liek the school and teachers. But one problem i always notice is the lack of supervision by the admin. Whenever im going to lunch or walking to class theres no one supervising which is a problem. Cause if a fight breaks out how will it be stopped? Students also can easily skip class and leave the campus in their vehicle. I believe the school needs to crack down on the class skipping because it seems to be a big issue at this school. I attended J.W. Mitchell for my senior year. The school is viewed by outsiders as the best public high school in the area, which is very concerning. The school has very poor academics, lots of drug use, a lack of professionalism among the teachers, constant use of cell phones and social media during class, very disrespectful students. Students take inappropriate photos and videos during class, without reprimand from staff, teachers can even be seen encouraging this behavior. There is no supervision, making it easy for students to walk out of class and drive off campus. If your child is serious about their education, do not send them to this school. The desire to further your education is not promoted. I was scoffed at and dismissed whenever I expressed an interest in college or sought assistance in making that desire possible. I wholly regret my time at this school, and feel as though my senior year education was thrown away. The academics are average and the school is overcrowded but the Principal is horrible! She (Shultz) tries to run the school like a dictator. She is way overboard and doesn't want the kids to have any fun and is negative and condescending. The teachers for the most part are pretty good but we moved here from another State and are very disappointed with Mitchell (even though it is supposed to be the best school in the district - ouch, would hate to see the others...) This is the best school ever. Communication is impressive from administration to students and teachers. There is a voicemail every single Sunday that the principal sends to all staff members and parents.The difference is the positive school culture and the fact that the individuals who work here do their job and do it extremely well. Excellent school! I have been to many other schools and this one has been the best and my favorite so far. The amount of clubs and sports they have is amazing. They also offer many different types of classes and AP courses. One of my favorite parts of the school is they're a magnet school for special ed kids and they do an AMAZING job with them. I am a wrangler for them, basically means I help the teacher, and I can see how much the kids adore the teachers and how much improvement they make on the daily. This school has more good qualities then bad for sure. My daughter has had a wonderful experience in her four years with JW. She is an honor student, active in the band and color guard. I couldn't have asked for more from the teachers and staff working within this school. Yes the school is currently overcrowded but that is not the schools fault. There has been an explosion of population in the Trinity area and JW is one of, if not the best schools in Pasco county. They have the highest college preparedness rating in the county and one of the most successful after school programs for nearly every interest. Their football team is undefeated two years in a row, and their band is one of the largest and most successful in the state. GO MUSTANGS! We moved to Trinity so that my son could attend a good school. He struggles in some academics and needs some extra help. There have been some teachers that have been accommodating and will do their best to help, but for the most part, it’s an inconvenience and they do not try to help. The kids deserve more! The school overall is great, but some of the teachers clearly play favoritism (chorus). The same people are recognized and celebrated while those a little more quiet go unnoticed. My daughter had a birthday and was excited to be sung to in chorus because most kids were, but the teacher did not even acknowledge her. Solos are offered to her favorites without even auditioning. Why bother trying when 75% of the class feels like they are second best? Everyone should be treated the same, and have the same opportunity to try out. I know only the best will be selected, but the same 25% of students get the offer without even trying out. Puts a damper on the whole school when some teachers are clearly biased.

column1: this school could be a lot better the school lacks alot of things its going down hill i hate that my kids go here also teachers are rude so is the staff towards me they need to work on this to better there selves Staff does not seem to care about the kids or the town itself. SOME of the staff appear to care more about themselves and how they can make things easier for them. It seems they do little for the student body and as little as possible to get through the day

column3: My youngest son is currently a Senior at SVHS. For 3 out of his 4 years he has had the honor and privilege of taking Video Production + Broadcasting classes with Peter Hansen. Mr. Hansen procures financial donations to help fund his Video Production + Broadcasting courses at SVHS. The yearly Sonoma International Film Festival is one of the regular donors. These classes and Mr. Hansen's support has enabled our son obtain employment filming events for the high school, local TV station and other schools in the valley. Our son has had some additional tremendous teachers, Mick O'Mera (who moved to Tamalpais HS in Mill Valley this year), David Donnelley and Robert Midgley. His counselor, Betzy Chavez, is always available and responds to every inquiry. Our family is very grateful to SVHS. Sonoma Valley High School has been a great school for my now 16 year old. There are over 40 extra curricular activities available including sports, music, drama, forensics (speech and debate), cheerleading, dance, newspaper, etc. Like all schools, and all workplaces, there are amazing teachers and those who should probably have chosen a different career. But I maintain that the outstanding, amazing and motivating teachers are changing student lives for the better...the others, well, it's a good lesson in life to the students that not everyone in your world can be fantastic. With our superintendent, new principal, and absolutely amazing college counseling center, I give this school high marks, and am very happy that my child is able to learn and participate. Sonoma High is the heartbeat to much of the community here in Sonoma. To have a public high school that has continued to offer numerous electives including woodshop, metal shop, photography, culinary, engineering, and agriculture helps students create a successful career path outside of the typical core classes taught at all high schools. SVHS supports students that are high achieving by giving them the tools they need to be successful Lower than it should be. 50% of graduates are not prepared for work or college. Was does the school board do during the pandemeic? Votes to spend $14,000,000 on a second football stadium 5 blocks from the existing stadium. Completley ineffective. The community was good but some of the teachers were very bad. There was an AP Biology teacher that wanted to be a friend over getting us ready for the exams. But overall, not a horrible expirience.

column1: 90% of the parents of this school's students are non-English speaking. It is amazing that these parents have taken the time to attempt to rate this fine school. My children attend East Early College and are on track to receive an associate degree in science before they graduate from high school. This school has a very dedicated faculty and staff and they are promoting a college bound culture for everyone who is part of this growing community.

column3: Sun Valley marching band rules. Parents, staff and community are all supportive. Booster are always welcome. Sun Valley High School seems to be a happy experience for my daughter who is in 11th grade now. She is in honors courses and has been getting good grades A's and B's. The teachers seem very involved and intelligent. The school adminstrators are very knowledgeable and helpful with the course selections. I have not heard anything about the kids being bullies, starting fights or taking drugs. The kids that attend Sun Valley High seem to be very nice friendly students concerned about their future success. That is what makes it a happy day to be there. This school is doing a great job given all the budget cuts they've endured these past few years. Hats off to the leadership and teachers of this school for finding ways to make up the some of the loss of funding. While there are some good educators here, my daughter's two years so far has been completely hit and miss. This year, she enrolled in Spanish, but is switching classes because the school can't fill the position (they have a French teacher filling the spot). Her history teacher last year had students build a castle--I remember doing that same project in 5th grade. She always complains about out-of-control classrooms and teachers who can't (or won't) do anything about it. I have a student who loves to learn and loves school, but I can see that drive and spark diminishing every day she comes home. This isn't just SVHS's fault. North Carolina is killing curiosity and love of learning in our schools all the way from K-12. Should you stay away from SVHS? Maybe. But the best advice is to leave NC. Great educators, it is also parents responsibility to be present at school to make the changes they believe is necessary. My niece has been doing really well at Sun Valley. Teachers are very dedicated and supportive!! My daughter went here briefly, but loved it. She was in advanced classes and felt she was challenged. Kids were nice, too. Our daughter was redistricted to Sun Valley this school year. Initially, we were reluctant as we were happy with the school she had been attending. Much to our surprise, the transition was not only smooth, it has been very positive. Our daughter is thriving both academically and socially. From administration to teachers, she has been welcomed. Her classes have been challenging and she has thrived. We could not be more thrilled. I encourage all prospective students / parents to talk with current students / parents. You will be astonished at the overwhelming sense of community and pride - which is just a bonus on top of the quality education in your child's future at Sun Valley. Welcome to Sun Valley Spartans!! Supportive staff and great students. Each student is accepted no matter what their background is or social status. Each department works as a team to encourage support for each student as they strive to achieve a successful school experience. Excellent staff, excellent kids! This school has a great learning environment matched with plenty of great kids. My kids instantly liked it here. My student told me that some classrooms are out of control and noisey when she was trying to learn. The teachers didn't do anything but say to tune it out which I think is very unfair. There is bullying and not much done about it. The school is very dirty and old. Hopefully there will be a new one built very soon. My student didn't want to use the bathroom at school. There is smoking in the bathroom. There was some good experiences but a lot of bad as well. My daughter attends this school and was diagnosed with a learning disability. The counselor and VP were very proactive in modifying her curriculum and offering help with a 504 plan. She's adapted well and has a great support team.

column1: The dress code is getting out of hand. I understand no spaghetti straps ect., I also understand the two finger strap rule. Now it's no sleeveless tops. They must be at least cap sleeves. Even in the sixies, it was considered appropriate to wear short sleeve shirts. At 80 or 90 degrees the only thing on those kids minds is how hot they are.. While after much effort, the latest policy of having to have sweater type coverings over your prom and winterfest dresses was changed just in time. . Modesty certainly is appreciated but antiquated dress codes are just plain silly . On the other hand the school in general is pretty good. Good school spirit. A lot of the teachers are fantastic. Others have a problem s with communication. The many events offered at school helps with the camaraderie between the teachers, kids and parents. . column3: School is blessed by good demographics in South Bryan County. On average, wealthier and better educated parents than most areas of Georgia. This allows the school to coast and not put any extra effort into education. The district is more of a good ol' boy style of governance. That is why the faculty and administration at the school is all white despite a more diverse population. Also, they value athletics over education. They recently hired two coaches with no education training to teach classes. I've been graduated from the school for almost 3 years. The staff can be a bit strict, but there were always some teachers that stood out among the rest. They placed more importance on education than discipline. The school prepares you well for college. Where many other college students struggled, I succeeded because my high school prepared me enough for the future. The football team was mostly terrible, but all the other sports teams were pretty great. I didn't like the school very much while I attended, but ultimately I am glad I stuck with it. Preparing your children for future education is extremely important, and I'm glad my parents had me attend this school system. Absolutely without a doubt one of the best, if not the best high school's in Georgia. I am the parent of a an 11th grader currently,senior next fall, he has struggled all through school, he is learning disabled.I have met or talked with many teachers,counselors,coaches,principal and assistant principals the last two years.I never left the school thinking anything less than impressed,amazed at how they do it and thankful my child is enrolled in one terrific school.Student enrollment for the 2012/2013 year is/was 1901 teenagers.The teachers,staff and coaches respect these kids ( for the most part) and from eveything I've seen, the students(for the most part) return that respect back.Most, if not all teachers take a personal interest in each students success, and how they do that with 1900 kids, I don't have a clue.Never hear of drug issue,gang issue,nothing really.Most kids are involved in a sport or band or ROTC, something, and all these activities are taught or coached or managed by some of the most dedicated,hardworking caring people I've come across in quite some time.I truly believe that kids see this dedication,see the sweat,hear the compliments and feed off that. I LOVE RHHS I graduated recently (class of 2013), and I can confidently say that this high school is loaded with opportunity. They added 5+ AP courses just last year. There are tons of clubs and did I mention the AP classes!?!? The new principal is looking to further improve this school, so look out! By the way, this school is disciplinary superior to the Savannah schools. Everyone is well-behaved. I've been in the Bryan County school system my whole life and I honestly hate it. This school fails to bring to light the racial issues that plague our hallways daily and it is absolutely ridiculous. This school is very unorganized and changes teachers and classes much too often. Our athletics are okay, but they are biased to just the football team. This school places too much emphasis on sports and dress code more than they do to academics, bullying and actual problems. Basically, if you do not play a sport, you do not matter. If you or your child is a minority like myself, I strongly advise you to not make them go to a school where there is daily unnecessary prejudice. I hate this school and I know exactly why people kill themselves from being in an environment similar to this. This is not as great a school as I had hoped. Let me first start off with saying the teachers for the most part are GREAT. My son struggles and has a LD though and the school is on a block schedule. They go at a VERY fast pace and it is hard for my child to keep up bc of this. Very long class periods as well. Counselors are only minimally helpful. Class sizes are also very large at 30 kids per teacher. School doesn't have the technology you would expect either. Can't wait to move and get back to a standard schedule of 6 classes. There is some bullying and kids are disrespectful, but it isn't an issue for my child. If you have a child that struggles to focus in school or has a LD I would consider a different school. Once your child is in the block schedule you are basically stuck to finish off he year since online schools,etc don't follow that type of schedule. It would also be a HUGE problem if you have to move in the middle of the year. I am very disappointed in this school. We moved to Richmond Hill because it was suppose to be the better school in the area. We were let down! Most of the teachers are great and seem to care about the students but the administration and counselors are a different story. They are never available. I have been trying all semester to reach my child's counselor but he has never returned any of my phone calls or emails. My child has not even met with him and he is never available to talk. When I addressed this issue with the assistant principal her response was, " I'm not sure what school you came from but he has over 600 students to look after." That is unacceptable! That is his job! I was told by other frustrated parents that if you are not from this area or military your child can easily slip through the cracks because they do not care. They figure you will be gone soon anyway. Funny thing, they get government funds for every military child enrolled. If you send your child to this school you need to advocate for your child so they do not get left behind. My daughter is soaring with this school and the teachers are extremely helpful. I can't say enough nice things about this school. I'm very happy with my choice. We are a military family and moved here when my son was starting his Junior year, hard move! He THRIVED in this school and when he graduated he said his only regret was that he didn't get to do all 4 years here. He started off playing football that summer before school started and his senior year decided he wanted to spread his wings and do drama club and young republicans. HE LOVED IT! There are MANY clubs for the kids to join which is nice if they don't want to play sports. This is an amazing community. Probably the best place we have ever lived and the best little town to raise children. I didn't realize towns like this existed! We LOVE RH! If you have an issue or concern you need not bring it to the heads of the school as it will do no good. They will listen to your concern & then sweep it under the rug but tell you they have dealt with it. My mother regrets not homeschooling me because of the poor education I received here. It is awful that these kids have to take exams AND state tests. That is TOO much and unnecessary. Since the EOC is a make or break and counts against your grade, it should be counted as an exam. Also frustrating that the kids aren't able to wear basic athletic shorts. They are anything but inappropriate and it's what the kids have been wearing for years. It seems like a really silly battle! I give this school a one star because they don't care enough about the students. The front office staff are not very respectful. Neither good, nor bad....just average. Nothing made it stand out to me. Her school in Florida was an example of what I feel a school should embody As a military family, we have been to several schools. Both of my children were fortunate to attend RHMS and RHHS. They did wonderful here! I never had any issue that was not easily resolved, whether it be with a teacher, or any other issue. Staff was very responsive. I am very pleased with this school. Was not great old building that’s run down but over most teachers are good other than the select few. Terrible. Councilor and Administrators do not solve problems or work with parents to solve issues. My kid had been bullied and they did not even consider our request to change classes. Over crowded high turnover for staff and teachers. Very unhelpful. Our daughter has been in RHHS for the past four years and has enjoyed every day! Her guidance counselor, Ms. Bunyan, has been a pure Godsend that has directed her in the correct path all four years. The overall majority of the teachers care for the students and have provided an exceptional education for my upcoming UGA student. RHHS offers a large selection of AP and Honors classes that have allowed for higher levels of academic achievement. We could not be more thankful for the entire staff at RHHS and the Bryan County Board of Education that has set a spectacular example of how to carry on throughout a pandemic. Great schools in a great community with loads of opportunities for all from academics to extracurricular!

column1: My daughter is junior at Davis. If you are looking for a smaller high school for your child, with very good teachers, this it. I am however concerned about the lack of extra-curricular activities. The administration is good, and the students for the most part are well behaved.

The teachers are very carrying and well prepared to teach the required subjects to prepare students for college. My favorite teacher was let go from the school, not because she was a bad teacher, but because the school board did not like her. Seriously. Really. I know better. All the other students do to. Also, a lot of times students will have to wait outside in the halls after class bell because a teacher isn't there to let them in. Online school through Edgewater is extra difficult because some teachers simply will not show up. Even in physical school, sometimes the teachers will not show up, and students will have to wait in class doing nothing. I would not recommend this school.

The school is neglected, the students are not ready for college or anything else. All we do is raise taxes. column1: I somewhat enjoyed my experience there. There were some teachers who didn't provide me with a quality education, but there were others who went above and beyond. As I became an outsider looking in and gained more knowledge from better, more thriving districts, I was able to see the flaws that seem to be getting worse. A few pluses that have developed over the years are the UIL program and the band program. There have been several students perform well at state competitions in multiple UIL events. The band program is the reigning state champion for marching and concert competitions. 1/100 and I would like my 4 years back Overall, it was a pretty average school. It was nothing special. I don't feel prepared for college, and as ready as I am to graduate, I don't feel confident going out into the real world. The majority of teachers were really good and helpful, other teachers acted like they didn't want to be there and didn't take their jobs seriously. I would love to see this high school prepare students more for college and the real world. If I had children, I would send them to a school that focused a little more on college readiness.

column1: Lanier High School is a clean environment for the students and faculty Lanier Co High has made progress in the last year and has really become a school that parents want to send their kids to due to the hard work or the new administration and team effort! Kudos! Keep up the hard work! This school rates a zero. My oldest son went to Lanier County High for his freshman year in 2006. Luckily, we were able to move out of the area for the rest of his high school time. Three problems I had with this school: 1. The counselor gave the parents and students a visual demonstration on freshman orientation night describing why the children didn't need to go to college. She described statistics that showed that 70% of them would get jobs that didn't require college degree, and then that of the 30% that attended college, only 10% would ever graduate. 2. The tech prep diploma is not accepted at any college except Valdosta Tech or GA Military College. The diploma isn't worth the paper it's printed on. 3. Expectations for the children are low, and therefore no effort is made to improve the school curriculum. This school has gotten a little better over the years, however there are many kids that bully. The teachers nor the administrators ever do anything about it and it should change. Bullying causes a lot of things including depression so being bullied everyday could lead to someone committing suicide. This is a REAL problem that NEEDS to be addressed. The 9th grade teachers at LCHS are amazing. As a parent, I stay involved with my kid's academics. The teachers are really concerned and focused on helping their students achieve and attain their goals necessary for graduating. They are always kind and courteous. Along with them, the staff creates a wonderful learning environment. When you walk through the doors, you get a warm welcoming feeling, that I know is comforting to me, as well as my kids. Thank you LCHS! Small town which makes it very difficult for kids to fit in if they were not born in the town. Bullying is a big issue in the school system and some administrators/teachers are quick to look the other way. Bad lunches an overall bad school. Kids here only know how to get pregnant. An how to bully other kids for what they dont know. Excellent small school in a rural district

There isn't a real punishment if you don't get your homework/class work done. Half of the kids on my bus you'd see smoking before they get on. You can skip classes or leave classes like its nothing. It's just bad what's happening to Mapletown wish it'd get better soon:(.

column3: I have love this school the moment I stepped into it myself, now my children are attending the school. The teachers are top notch and caring! I hated most of my time at this school. The unequal opportunities that most people turn a blind eye to, the students that are allowed to get away with practically anything, and the faculty and families that allow it to happen appall me. Unless your parents have a foot in the door, this school isn't worth wasting your time on. I go to GCHS and it is terrible, bullying goes unnoticed, which is something all schools should be concerned about. Greensburg high school is not somewhere i would put my kids.

column1: Awful. If you happen to live here and can afford to, send your kid to private school. I have to agree with the previous parent review. With one principal and two assistant principals you think that they would make an effort to know each student in the building (not just the ones constantly in trouble or good athletes )after all these students will be in the building for four years. -100/10 this school sucks if you’re a POC please don’t have your child go to this school. I’m telling you, they will literally have the worst experience of there life here. I looked forward to going to school every day. The teachers are very supportive in even way possible! They want to help you be the best and succeed at your school work. Teachers are not big on homework but it is something that helps our grades when we do it. Teachers treat everyone equally no matter race or income and look at each student as an individual. The Administration is very good at handling issues that come up.

column3: This school is so great! It helps student learn to become smart and responsible adults! I was a student at this high school, 2010 graduate. I was cyber bullied my whole senior year by another student and even though the school pretends to care about how their students are being treated- I was told to deal with it and the most they could do was watch my car during school hours. Besides for the few amazing teachers I encountered, your child may not have a good experience if they are not an athlete. Drugs? There were a few major drug busts in my year and about 6 major fights. All in all, the teachers care - management does not. i don't understand all these negative comments, especially from parents! they didnt even go here!! i'm currently going into the 10th grade, and Dakota High School is a great school, if i do say so myself. Just like any other school, it has their druggies, nerds, bullies, populars. The ones who fail chose to, and the ones who succeed actually put effort. I honestly do not think athletes get better treatment, considering i am one of the very few good, girl tennis players there. They're fine arts program is phenomenal, as i am in the band. They have tons of AP classes, and the teachers do care if you ask for help. They are not going to spoon feed your children, learn to grow up. My mother went to Chippewa High School, so it has been here a while and she excelled even though she was bullied. Overall, i would go here if i had a choice. But if you have negative things about this school, then don't go here and waste our time listening to you complain. These comments speak for themselves - all of the positive comments come from the kids/parents who are, or have athletes in this school. I attended every Parent Teacher conference for four years. I had a kid who was honor roll when she started there. She had some issues socially at this school with harassement and she withdrew and declined academically. I met with the staff and the situation just got worse. These ignorant comments about Parents not getting involved simply do not apply to everyone universally. I also get a kick out of a tenth grader telling parents how to be behave. Imagine that, an athlete at the school thinking that athletes don't get special treatment. Anyway, for those of you have kids that are self motivated and do not require extra attention at times, I am happy for you. You should consider yourselves fortunate. However, not every teenager falls in to that category, and to say that others are un motivated slackers is over simplifying an incredibly complex equation. Long story short, school should meet the needs of the entire student body, this school is great for the low maintenance students and athletes. I am a parent of a daughter that recently graduated from Dakota and another one that will be graduating soon. I have nothing but great things to say about this community of administrators, teachers, security, etc. As a parent, I have had the opportunity to be very involved from elementary school all the way through high school giving me first hand experience at what goes on. Resources are available to all....just ask! There is an excellent Fine Arts program graduating some of the top students at DHS. The athletic department offers a variety of sports, many going on to win championships! Encouraging your child to become involved in something is my best advice. There are so many after school clubs available to meet people and to be able to be a part of something. My college student recently told me that she loved everything about Dakota. She felt it totally prepared her for college. The climate of the school is amazing, as are the many varied programs offered. From the Fine Arts to the Athletics, the programs offer the student population a chance to succeed within and out of the walls of the physical plant. Tour the building, meet the staff, talk to the students...they are all approachable, and caring individuals. Kudos to Dakota for taking what can seem like a sea of craziness and turn it in to something amazing for each and every student. Great variety of classes offered. Great area. There is a culture of disrespect at this school, from the administrators to the teachers to the parents and kids. The school and classes are crowded. Many tout the athletics at this school, but unless your child is an exceptional athlete and willing to stick to one sport year round, he/she will not play. You are better off at neighboring Utica Community Schools, where there is more emphasis on college prep and smaller classes. Pretty Good !I would recommend it . Coming from middle school did well but first semester was rough . The AP and Honors classes are excellent! Great teachers , strong administrators who keep the school safe-not an easy job with such a huge student body. Overall, the school has great staff, great athletics but just too many students to be excellent . Covid caused online learning which was a tough transition .

column1: Pretty great school. Graduated from there in 2011. Sports teams are pretty up and down. Football team was not great while I was there. However, the Naval Junior Reserves Officer Training Corps is one of the best in the entire nation. Consistently competing in all areas in national competitions. Also, academic are pretty good. Constantly getting pushed to achieve more and take AP classes. As a parent I have a few issues with this school, granted it has been years since I have been to high school, but when does it become acceptable to lock bathroom doors or suggest to a child that if he/she does not use a pass to the bathroom, locker, etc there lowest grade can be dropped. According to history using the restroom to relieve bodily functions is natural and normal and should not be discouraged. Also, what is going on with online classes? My child was homeschooled for 3 years, I made the decision to matriculate her into a public school to interact with TEACHERS and students, not online classes with no assistance. How was it possible for the school to have French last year with a teacher and this year no french teacher?? If a child wants to take 4 years of this language should it be acceptable that the child has to do online for 3 years. My child was referred for Honors French, surely that implied with a teacher, she is not in Honors French though. I don't even want to talk about the PE class, I can't mention how many times I was told, oh we didn't do anything today. And my child receives little assistance from counselor. As a parent I have been quite please with the Union Grove High School. I have two girls who have attended the school and one is there in her second year. I find the fact that parents want the school to teach there children how to behave a cop out. The school has performed beyond our expectations. If parents understand that they need to support their children then this will always have a lasting positive effect on the children learning experience. The girls love the school and they have had high grades. Our graduated daughter has been afforded the opportunity to attend one of the finest school in the country. This does not happen by luck. Parents need to stand in the gap and support their children it is not up to the public school system to cast the future of our children. Parents take up your parental duties and work with the school to ensure the success of our kids. This you will not regret. Your children see you are involved and care, now be there for them and be part of the solution. I think this school is very overrated. It's superficial. I came from a disadvantaged school towards the end of the year knowing the good status and high standards expected of me and was ready to be pushed to better my GPA. However, when I arrived nobody gave me any information. I never met any of the staff, never got a rule book or agenda, and was constantly scolded for things I knew nothing about. It was a complete shock and nobody made me feel welcome. The students looked down on me, or just blatantly ignored me. My grades plummeted and thanks to no help from the teacher, even when sought out. I was made to feel stupid and inferior to everyone. Disgusting and disrespectful. Awesome teachers and staff! Always going above & beyond for their students! UGHS is a great school! I graduated from UGHS in '05. I have moved on to earn a B.S. I didn't receive much attention at this school. I taught myself nearly everything. I don't know if the teachers that I had are still working at this school, but the ones I had really didn't show any attention nor did they try to help. I received more help from professors at the University I attended. I really hope that it has changed. Hidden and blatant racism is more than evident at this school. I was saddened when my daughter came home and said children choose to segregate themselves at lunch (and the principles not addressing this) and racist remarks as well as disparaging treatment from teachers often occur. The fact that this school is 15min from the heart of our diverse city of Atlanta is simply appalling. just a couple of normal day to day things: - keeps bathrooms locked all day, only unlocked in between classes. WE CANT CONTROL NORMAL BODILY FUNCTIONS??? - use of many trailers which contain roughly 30 students, 30 desks, 30 chairs, all in space that could comfortably fit about 15 people with no equipment. - sexist in terms of dress code BY FAR (females always getting the short end of the stick) - unhappy office staff, especially principals. they never seem positive and it makes you feel like school should be exactly like their facial expressions - teachers are under MUCH stress in terms of what they need to teach us, and the stress easily transfers to us. - councilors don't even try to view anything from a student's point of view. they'll say whatever benefits the school. - If you're not an athlete, do you even go here? - students only care about how rich they're parents are. if you don't have the nicest car or the most expensive clothes, then why even go here?? - DIRTY. chewing tobacco between bleachers... need i say more? we're actually having to move because of how bad the schools are. All henry county schools are pretty much the same anyway. Union Grove is a fairly good school. I would say I've had a satisfactory experience with the teachers. There are bound to be bad teachers at every school, but the good teachers definitely outnumber the bad at UGHS. The teachers and administration definitely push you to reach your potential. That being said, I do agree with the other reviews about the counselors not being able to see things from the students' perspectives. They're very nice and pleasant to talk to, but sometimes they try to send you down paths that would overload you and give you a chaotic year. Otherwise, the counselors are great. Some of the principals could be a bit more...cheerful. Otherwise, the administration is wonderful. The school equipment is pretty pitiful. Many of the textbooks are over 10 years old, and some have been around for longer than the school has. The biology, world history, health, and other textbooks are frequently missing pages, covers, or whole chapters because the books are literally falling apart. Having classes in the trailers is fine, except that they are overcrowded. The microwaves in the cafeteria hardly ever work, and it's frustrating when you have to wait in line for 15 minutes waiting to heat up your food because there are two working microwaves for a ton of kids. (Side note: the lunch periods are way too short! 25 minutes is hardly enough time to eat lunch when you spend over half of it just trying to heat up your leftovers.) The sports teams fluctuate. The football team this year isn't too marvelous. However, our softball team and NJROTC program have done wonderfully. It just depends on the year, I suppose. I also noticed some of the other reviews complained about the bathroom policy, but I believe they have tried to remedy that recently. Now you can go to the bathroom as long as it's not in the first or last 15 minutes of class. Overall, UGHS is a pretty decent school. Could be better, could be much worse. Overall, I've been pretty happy with it. After such a wonderful few years at the middle school. I've been very disappointed by my daughters freshman year experience at UGHS. Some teachers act as if they could care less about the students or their success. The principal is aloof and the counselors, as others have mentioned only seem to carte about the honors numbers so they push that to keep the school highly rated. It's very disappointing and I now know that I habe to stay on top of them about everything. UGHS is not a place you would want to take your High School student. If you are thinking of enrolling here, don't. As a student at Union Grove, I can say that my overall experience at the school is below par. This is not an extensive list of everything that’s going on at this school, just a list of things that occurred. To give a little background information, me and my family moved to this school because it had a high rating. We were not expecting to encounter so many unprofessional staff members at school. Assistant principals and even the principal don’t respond to emails when they’re busy. The teachers aren’t better at that. I was trying to figure out the situation with one of my grades, my parents wanted to schedule a meeting. No meeting was scheduled and I went to the counseling office to try and figure out the situation. When I came to the office, the staff called in the assistant principal. She began yelling at me, I was trying to explain the situation, and she began talking over me. I then called my guardian so the assistant principal could go talk to her and she started yelling, talking over her, and saying “mom we’re not gonna go back and forth”. In my view, she was trying to explain the situation to her but she wasn’t willing to listen. She also told her that she will always be on the side of teachers. This is not everything that transpired in the five minutes she entered the office to communicate with us, and we didn’t get the situation solved. When you’re absent for some time, some teachers don’t want to help. My technology teacher wouldn’t let me fix a mistake she got a student to help me because she was busy. She didn’t grade from the rubric and took points off for things she didn’t like. It appears to me that UG just wants their students to pass. This is not only our opinion but what several other students and parents have told us. I had several situations where I needed something resolved and the staff wasn’t willing to help, this is one example. Being a parent at UGHS, the school administration and some teachers don’t complete their duties at all. The director doesn’t know the facts at all about what is going on at the school and twists the information. When you show him the facts, he doesn’t even bother to respond back. Be ready to be yelled at by the assistant principal: you and your kids. They tell you they have other things going on that are more important. When you tell them the facts, they completely turn their back on you and ignore you. They think it’s normal to yell at kids and parents. We had an instance where my daughter’s father died, so we went to email them with no response, asking them to be more understanding. Only to be yelled at more. And these are the “top people”. This is not only unprofessional but just bad etiquette in general. We wrote an email about this with no response, no apologies, no anything. We had a lady tell us about her instance of having a kid with autism and the teachers didn’t want to help. They had to transfer them to a different school. The principal always takes the side of the teachers and administrators and covers them up. They think the teachers are always right. All in all, this is the worst experience I had with a school in my life. We moved here because it was supposed to be a good school.

column3: I was concerned when we first moved here. I had been involved in our district in Colorado. My child struggles to make friend and fit in. Our 9th grade year was concerning in that she had one person she visited with by the spring of her 9th grade. She liked her teachers and enough so that we did not have to push her in completing assignments. Now she is 11th grade, she participates a some after school activities and has a small group of friends. She continues to do well in school (her choice). From how my child is doing my experience has been Excellent.. Honestly, pretty decent. I went to Sherwood Marksmen before Harrisonville, and compared to Sherwood, it is way better. Far more opportunity, whether it be for a class or just something to do from the school. Plenty of sports and activities, too.Though, be warned that a lot of the students here are at least slightly toxic, thus bringing it down to 4 stars.

column1: We are so thankful to send our children to this school! It is large enough to have all the classes and programs you would expect a modern school to provide, and yet small enough to give each student a sense of place. Mazomanie and Black Earth are communities that care about their school. The voters continue to approve referendums year after year to enhance the quality of instruction and infrastructure of the school district. Need we mention the school's performance on test scores -- they are among the best in the State of Wisconsin. The teachers are excellent in Math, English, and many other programs. The principal has the confidence of the teachers and most of the parents in the district. We moved here from out of state (husband commutes to Madison), and we count our blessings every day that we found this quiet community with an outstanding school district. I'm currently a senior here and I'm really glad this is the school that I attend. Academically, this school is amazing, the teachers can be tough at times, but they really push you to do your best. There is a wide range of classes to take in all subjects and levels. The arts program is really great, although I'm not an artistic person I like to take art classes and see the musical every year. The sports here are really good as well. Overall just a fabulous school that is making me feel very prepared for college. Quality is strong on all fronts, including music, art, sports and other extracurricular activities. Parent involvement is high. We are proud of our top performing and safe school. Great school overall! A whole lot of focus is on academics. Excellent career counselors for higher education planning. An active PTA. Wisconsin Heights has relatively high number of students who attend higher education (especially UW) after graduation. Amazing! Teachers are dedicated, children are hardworking students. College is very important to children and staff! Love, love this school, kids and the Village of Mazomanie. Just cant say enough good about this school! This school is amazing, I just graduated and I feel as though I am completely prepared for college and life in general. The only thing that isn't great about that school is that there is very little diversity. Other than that, this school has so far given me the best four years of my life. I'm impressed. I wish the school was more diverse and growing faster so it was more exposed to our diverse American culture. The community support is some of the best I have ever science. Whatever the concert, game, and even more for school concerns and planning. The school truly is the focal point of the community. My son has been in 4 districts and this is the best for his needs. For a small school they really work to provide experiences for students and participation in sports and organizations is very impressive. Many students in multiple opportunities. Being so close to Madison is a great benefit, yet experiences a district that can focus on the individual is terrific for my student.

column3: This school offers excellent public school education as well as great athletics. I graduated in 2012 and am now attending Northeastern University on scholarship from the Army for ROTC. I took 4 AP classes, was President of the school's band for two years, and received varsity letters in three sports (cross country, winter track, and tennis). I had great success at JCHS. My only regret about my time at JCHS was that I didn't play football. The school's football program is outstanding and really seemed to develop individuals on and off the field. The community rallies around the football team too, and it would have been great to be a part of that. I am a Senior graduating this year, and I must say that James Caldwell provides a solid education from top to bottom. Certainly comparable to any private school in the area in terms of academics. Sure there are some not so great teachers, but they are in the clear minority. And I would go as far as to say that all of the teachers look out for the kids- I have never had a "disinterested" teacher. The administration effectively runs most aspects of the school, although enforcement of things like the dress code, etc could be better. Like I said- teachers are always looking to help you- they aren't out to get the students. The guidance department has been shaken up over the four years I have been here, and there is room for improvement, but I have never had any real issue- all of my college stuff was taken care of in a timely manner. And although sports (mainly football) are considered "important," the athletics program is not overwhelming, and to be honest, even the teachers who double as coaches get pretty pissed when students either miss class or claim that sports got in the way of school work. The first year at this school - a great start to high school! Wonderful ESL classes! I love my school!!! I watched my nephew's and niece go through JCHS and they all did well with no complaints. They have all went onto (or will be attending) college and continued to have a good work ethic. We have attended all different sorts of events from School plays, Holiday concerts, Football and Baseball and have always been impressed. the only reason i give this school any stars is because of the teachers and the friendships. as a current student with ADHD and anxiety, this school heavily leaves behind disabled kids. that happens everywhere unfortunately, but it’s really bad here, and just because it happens in other places doesn’t mean it’s okay. other schools have it more figured out. there’s no excuses. the upper ranks such as principals and the guidance office (and even one of the social workers!) don’t really attempt at all to see things from disabled children’s sides and resort to punishment and consequences (such as tanking your grades or more serious things like detentions, removal or ineligibility from sports, or even ISS and suspensions) instead of offering any real help. the way they throw around the word “accommodations”, if i am being completely honest, disgusts me sometimes. it is often treated as almost an “if we give you ALL these ACCOMMODATIONS and you STILL can’t perform well then that’s on you” type situation and just makes disabled students feel like nuisances. for a lot of disabled students with 504s and IEPs, their accommodations are not enough. they aren’t working. and i don’t appreciate that they make you feel that you should be nothing but grateful for the bare minimum fair treatment they give you (which, based on the things said earlier, is not really all that fair anyway). i am also a low income student and can say that there’s also huge issues with the way these situations are handled. i grew up in a very complex situation. i wasn’t homeless, but we didn’t have a home of our own, and i had zero private space. this along with the traumas of living there at all AND having ADHD made it incredibly hard for me to complete work, and while teachers and the bridge counselor showed support and in some cases understanding, i still fell behind when what i needed was help. it only got worse during the COVID-19 pandemic when i wasn’t in school. again, the upper ranks offered little to no understanding of my situation, and one of the principals at the time (no longer there) continuously called my special permission to keep my camera off in my traumatic and quite honestly humiliating space a “privilege” that could be taken away if a teacher marked me as a skip because i was having trouble connecting. tl;dr, the teachers are mostly amazing and the bridge counselor is fantastic (albeit VERY busy), but the higher ups don’t care if the students are disabled or poor.

column1: My daughter graduated GAMP this year (2011). GAMP was the best experience she had. Their standards are very high and the support for students is impressive. She is now a freshman atTemple University and sees how her training at GAMP prepared her for college academic challenges. We shall miss the school and its wondeful students, teachers, support staff and administration. I Do agree with an earlier comment that the school has its hands into the pockets of parents entirely too frequently. I am just starting to get to know GAMP because as have applied for 5th grade. The feedback I hear from other parents is almost uniformly positive. We love the "feel" of the place. GAMP is leaps and bounds better than most Philadelphia public schools, but that's not saying much. The school leaves a lot to be desired in terms of nurturing the children. Like most schools the classrooms are overcrowded so the teachers do not get know each child individually. In my opinion, the 5th graders are thrown to the wolves and the teachers show little interest in getting to know the children unless they have exceptional musical talent. I have been made to feel like a nuisance when I have requested one on one feedback regarding my child's progress. It's a good school comparatively, but it lacks what it takes to be a great school. GAMP has been a second family to me and my children for the past several years. The teachers and staff dedicate countless hours, week after week, to ensure that their pupils are receiving a valuable education and a respect for society. This is a school that CARES about the future generation(s) of our city! Graduating classes are always sad to go, but they are well prepared and have years of strength, knowledge, and confidence to fulfill their dreams. I can honestly say, there's no other school in the city of Phila, that can do what GAMP does! To sum it all up, the school is AWESOME; Ms. Domb is TERRIBLE. Nuff said. What a gem in South Philadelphia! Carol Domb is a leader with integrity and vision. She is passionate about education AND the music that is an integral part of the GAMP experience. Yes, this is one of the competitive Special Admissions Schools, but if your child passes the rigorous academic criteria and has an apptitude for music, consider GAMP. Fabulous music program, top notch academics, and amazing teachers - what more could a parent ask for? The school has a very welcoming atmosphere, good academics (top 3 in Philadelphia), and the shows (talent show, musical, concerts) are fabulous

column3: Looking back as a college student, I am so glad I went to Grand Haven! I'm thankful for the safe learning environment it provided, and for all the passion and wonderful teachers I had during my four years there! They helped me become a more confident person with my professors here at MSU, and I feel prepared with all my assignments. In fact, I find I'm ahead of many other freshman here, in terms of work ethic and the quality of work because of the level I was held to at Grand Haven! Go Bucs, and Go Green! -A former alum, class of 2010 When considering school districts, check to see how many tutoring centers ( ie. Sylvan, Kumon, etc) are located within the city/district. We recently moved from an equally high test-score district that does not compare. Here the teachers do the teaching. In our previous district, parents supplemented their child's education. Some districts are fine with mediocre teaching, because they know the parents will do whatever it takes for their child. A very highly supported high school and educational system by the community and parents etc and the various school rating venues notice and reflect it. GHHS is a very fine top ranking school of learning and adult development academically for college and/or the student's adult life. Also has been awarded nearly every year for being the best in "sportsmanship" in the state in their athletic programs and that also says something. The team's in the entire school district are coached as being "a Family" and that's just how the teams act from grade school thru high school. GHHS is a quite large public high school with an enrollment of between 1800 and 2000 yearly for grades 9 thru 12 on it's more than 100 acre huge campus. Yet has a very good teacher/student ratio as that's important. GHHS has a very rich history of state and national championships and honors in both academics and sports programs now and over it's close to 150 year existence. I'm also extremely proud to be a graduate of Grand Haven High School many many years ago. What a great foundation was learned there which set the tone for a very happy and productive adult life! Winning in life starts early! I have had three children graduate from Grand Haven High School. All of them loved their school and their teachers. As a parent, I am thankful for the wonderful education that all three of them received. Our youngest has just finished her Master's degree. She has always loved to learn and that is because she has had wonderful teachers. Ineffective administration, excessive punishments for students outside the parameters of being straight, white, or cisgender. Teachers may frequently go out of their way to single out and publicly humiliate students and face absolutely no consequences. While other teachers may be kind, inclusive, and caring, this is not the norm. As a 2018 graduate of ghhs, I would not recommend enrolling your child here if you are looking for a healthy and comfortable learning environment. There are a vast majority of teachers who are truly amazing and care about the well being and quality of learning students receive, and they deserve that credit. But administration is and will always be a hindrance to the quality of learning and comfortably of the students. In my 4 years I spent at gh there were so many examples of sexism, racism, homophobia, transphobia, classism, and overall unjust punishments brought upon innocent students.Grand Haven has the absolute potential to be a wonderful place to learn and thrive but it will never grow until T Willy (principal) and any of the others in administration who agree with her ethics get off their high horse and take that stick out of their collective ass.Tldr You’re only going to truly thrive at Grand Haven High School if you were born into money, white, straight, and cisgender. (Extra points if you’re male) 10 out of 10. I Graduated from GHHS, our children graduated from GHHS, had 5 grand Children graduated from GHHS, and have one more grandchild still at GHHS and all had very high opinions of GHHS, as to their time at GHHS, how excellent and fair, excellent, and effective and supportive the teachers were, and really had prepared them well for college and adult life. All gave GHHS a 10 out of 10 ratings (Strongly Agree) except for one out of the nine asked who is 33 years old now and had given a 9 out of 10 rating or dealing effectively with bullying.

column1: Our 5 children attended the elementary/preschool before we relocated to another state. The educational standards was high so my children had no problems adapting to a new school system but more importantly the real Christian training and values influenced them so they were a light even at the church where we currently attend in Tucson, AZ. Want a great Christian school, this is the best of the best. The academics are top notch, their sports teams kick butt, drama and band are awesome, and the teachers rock! Wide variations in teacher abilities.....I love the quantity of male teachers in concept but have seen extremely competent women let go when obvious examples of lower teacher performance are kept. Great support for sports programs .....performing arts does well with great instructors who struggle with lip service support and no financing from the school. The teachers are loyal and work hard.....actually they have too much expected of them I believe. Teachers loyal to the school but are compromised in some ways by superhuman expectations from their admin who appear to lack empathy and loyalty to their own employed educators to save a buck. Some of the teachers are excellent, and some terrible. The lack of passion for subject matter and the inability to inspire has made us look elsewhere. The recess area is tiny. The lack of technology and an abundance of busy work, worksheets, deskwork makes me feel like it's a classroom from the 60's. We have tried to make up for this at home, but then wonder what we are paying for. "Money Grubbing" and going after distressed families is shameful! Manipulating issues for monetary gain is disgraceful. My Grandson attended another Christian School but all extra help required paying additional money to receive it. As a primary grade child, Cedar Park is committed to each child not being left behind. Teachers are willing to stay after school to help a struggling child. It may not be as fancy as some private schools but was is most important is a child is taught to love to learn reading, writing, math and science. The school is top notch where it counts! My daughter played this school in soccer and the girls were rude three girls body slammed her her back was sprained in three places and her ankle was severely sprained. While many are nice there are students in that school who are extremely bad influences and are rude and can be violent Just to be clear, this is a Christian school, I know the parent who posted on Posted -November 12, 2014-. There are discussions on world views, but once again it IS a Christian school, if your not looking for a Bible based education this might not be the school for you. FYI, the staff and teachers meet every morning for devotions, which include praying for your child. Cedar Park is a wonderful school! We have 4 children attending and I would not want them anywhere else. The teachers are amazing and do a great job of loving students and teaching them well. I have taught in a public school setting and significantly less students are behind at Cedar Park. Many teachers give of their own time to help students get caught up. The education standards are high, from what I have seen, a year or so above public schools. In addition, the schools top priority is on helping children learn to love God and His word and live out their faith. They do a great job of encouraging students gifts and talents and providing great programs to develop those skills. There is no room in this world for teachers and schools that kick children out or make them feel like they are worth nothing, forcing them to decide on the spot if they are gay, lesbian, transgender or heterosexual and ask them to repent for sins they dont even understand. Absolutely disgusting. They are leading by example of teaching bigotry to judge other paths. These individuals in leadership roles need to go. Being a true Christian is not judging others and treating children with such disgust. Teaching of compassion, tolerance, acceptance, is the Christian Way. We have removed our children from this school based on what we've seen happen to other kids here. Its disgraceful. #LGBT #Gayrights #HRC #glaad #huffpostgay I feel so blessed to have my 3 kids at this AWESOME school! They are learning Christian values and have acedemics that I truly wish I could have had! I graduated from this school in 1997. Now my 4 children attend CPCS. I am so grateful for the time the teachers put into each of my children. CPCS puts Christ first and they aren't ashamed to say so. It is very hard in this generation to find a Christian school putting Christ first, above all the latest trends. My children are all happy to be going to CPCS and love their teachers. We went to another Christian school for a year when we moved, but decided to move back to Bothell area to put our kids back in CPCS. Cedar Park Christian cares about children individually and there is a lot of community here. If you want Christ to be first in your child's life and you want them to have teachers who care about them holistically then you would definitely want to choose Cedar Park CHRISTIAN schools! They also have great sports programs, LEGO club, Robotics clubs, drama, and many other specialized extra curricular activities. They have a great turf field for sports and are building up a large playground for the kids. The cherry on top is that I can drive to one place for all my children, since I have elementary - high school. Ask a school that preaches Christian values such as honesty and virtue why they hired Bellevue High's coach after all of the scandals he was embroiled in.Clearly winning football championships is far more important than hiring coaches with any integrity or moral compass. Our child attended Cedar Park Christian School in Bothell for several years. The experience was negative for many reasons: inexperienced/unprepared teachers, little to no curriculum/books, unethical and dishonest leadership. The principal of the high school, Mr. Smith, was very unprofessional in how he dealt with us, as parents, and how he handled our child. In retrospect, we wish we would have sent our child to Kings or Bellevue Christian. This may be one of the worst Christian schools for your child to attend. The education is text driven, very average teachers, and probably the worst part is the lack of supervision. Expect your child to be compromised on security, leadership, and access to quality facilities. I withdrew my child after the first few weeks. My husband and I come from a very strong Christian and conservative background and with strong education/careers. I really regret ever sending my child here. He recovered going to one of the best schools and receives great Christian teaching and leadership at church. He is an A student and has scored highly on WA standards. This is a very poorly run school with limitations. Expect the staff to take multiple roles for lack of funding. Expect your child to haul around his books in a heavy backpack and limited locker space. It was a huge and costly mistake to send my child here for 2 weeks. I wish I could erase it from his memory and mine. I am a parent of two kids (just completed 6th grade and 3rd grade) at Cedar Park and I am also a teacher at Cedar Park. I did all of my student teaching in the Northshore School District and then taught for a year at a Northshore School District School. I had a good experience there, however, when I moved to teach at Cedar Park Christian School I knew I had found the place that I wanted to teach forever, and also the place that I wanted my children to attend. I have just completed my 9th year of teaching at Cedar Park and have loved every minute! The staff at Cedar Park is tremendously committed to the growth and success of every individual child in all areas, including spiritually, emotionally, academically, ALL areas! My two children have THRIVED here. They are both challenged academically and supported where needed. They feel loved and cared for by their teachers, who work tirelessly to help my children succeed. I absolutely love my job at Cedar Park because I get to teach in an atmosphere of academic excellence, while at the same time helping my students to see the world through the truth of God's Word. I am proud to be both a teacher AND parent at Cedar Park and I know there is no other place I'd rather work, and no better place to send my kids to school. I went to Cedar Park from 5th through 12th grade. My experience was a positive one. The postivity came out of the relationships I had with my teachers and the relationships I observed them maintain with each other. A school operates in some ways like a family, and backbiting and lack of support can undo the infrastructure. Seeing my teachers model integrity, compassion and respect toward each other and toward their students made my learning experience a healthy one. Yes, I still fought normal anxieties that come to every teenager, but I did not have additional anxiety about being embarrassed by my teachers or other class mates. I do not believe ANY utopian school exists, but the consistency of the teachers I had at Cedar Park still affects me today. Today, I am grateful to say that I teach at Cedar Park and hope to continue the legacy I experienced as a student. It is the place I would want my children to go. I want them to learn about who the Lord is and what His character is like and how that forever impacts they way we operate and care for people we encounter. I believe Cedar Park endeavors to do this work with humility and integrity. We enrolled our five children here at Cedar Park five years ago. We are so grateful how our kids found their place in this Christ centered community. Our children are constantly being challenged to pursue Christ in all their classes, activities and athletics. We are grateful for the accountability to follow rules, model Christ and be responsible for their academics. There are times our children are grumbly about school because sometimes they would rather be home on the couch watching TV eating donuts with soda (choosing the self-centered path of less resistance), but CPC staff partner with us parents to develop capable, competent and confident children by going above and beyond what any school traditionally offers. I started at Cedar Park in seventh grade and very quickly found myself cared for in many aspects of life: spiritually, academically, socially, and athletically. This place was like home away from home, and I genuinely felt a sense of belonging uncommon just about anywhere else in life. The foundations of knowledge and integrity built from the school have led me to success in college all the way through grad school and into my early career, and many of the friends I made there are still good friends today. At Cedar Park, you get as much out as you put in. I went in with a good attitude and humility, and I came out with lifelong skills and lessons. I am a parent of two children, both started in preschool at CPCS and my son graduated 2 years ago and my daughter is going into 10th grade. We have been so happy with the education that our children have received at CPCS. My son, who now attends WSU constantly is saying how well he was prepared for college by CPCS. His friends have struggled with the adjustment of going from HS to college and my son feels like it is just another day at school with how well the teachers have prepared him for college. The teachers at the school do more than just teach the students, they care about each and every one of them. I wouldn't have my kids anywhere else! Overall experience is luke warm. There are a few teachers that my kids adore. Regrettably they appear to be the exception to the norm. This school does a brilliant job of marketing how much of a superior environment and education they offer compared to orher private or ounlic schools. The reality is much different. After many years we pulled our kids out of the school and actually went public. Quite candidly we have been pleased with the environment, curriculum and attention from the teachers and administration. CPC is not all it is cracked up to be actually lead me to dissolutionment from the church I know it may seem pretty mixed, however, there are very few teachers and leaders that I would say need to be let go. The office staff is not kind or genuine and needs some training on how to manage people and do customer service. However, overall, the school is exceptional and my daughter is excelling. The teachers are what matter. My daughter is in 2nd grade and reads at a 4th grade reading level and continues to rise! So blessed to have my kids at CPCS. Great school teaches people how to live a Christian life and also teaches basic school stuff I have two kids that started their 4th and 5th grade years at Cedar Park. They had previously been in the LWSD. I cannot tell you how happy we are that we enrolled the kids at CPCS. The teachers are too notch, the kids are kind (too many entitled bullies at their last school) and the education is amazing. They have learned more in 4 months than they did in 2 years at their last school. It’s night and day. The school also feels like it’s the parents choice not the governments to make health decisions for their kids. They aren’t forced to wear masks while running in a soccer or basketball game, it’s up to the parents. However, they do follow state mandates (no matter how ridiculous) so that they are compliant during covid. All and all, this school is absolutely amazing. Mediocre school academically with some very dated curriculum. They seem unwilling to change and just defend their method. Dress code is restrictive especially for female students. Be wary of sending your student here.

Some teachers were a little less than helpful, but other teachers made up for that. The school offers a wide variety of courses that really prepare students for college. I would love to someday send my children to Durand Shcools.

column1: This school will be a good fit for your child only if he/she is a phenomenal athlete, has money, and is from a conservative family. Racism and homophobia are rampant; the popular kids regularly bully others and nothing is done because of who the kids are. VERY small-minded thinking. The kids from this school are known for their poor behavior when at other schools for athletic events. Several athletes vandalized the bathroom and locker room of a neighboring school this year. My son has a diagnosis of autism and attended Unity High School. He had an excellent experience with very supportive staff that encouraged him to achieve his goals. After graduating from Unity he attended the University of Illinois and graduated with honors and now works in the Psychology field. Without the positive and empathetic feedback and encouragement he received from the Unity staff this would not have been possible.
