column3: I have a son at East he is a honor roll student. East has drug bust and fights on regular basis which is reported through emails from principle. This school is already over crowded and they let kids out of district transfer in a school that is busting at the seems. If you didn't attend the feeder middle schools then you want have the same chances in playing sports. East is very political in sports! At this point I'm not very pleased with the school myself. My daughter is a freshman and has started being bullied already. I've already been in the vice principal's office with her once and she's been in the guidance office again on her own. At this point she already doesn't want to get up and go to school and her year had started off so well up until now. She's in the drama club and in an upcoming play and very excited about that but the bullying is overriding any of that excitement. At this time they're only talking to her and not any of the kids that are doing the actual bullying, which I personally think is wrong. If something isn't done very soon I will be back in there again myself probably threatening legal action!!! There's supposed to be a NO tolerance for bullying at all schools now so I don't understand why they're not speaking with anyone else involved. I have a daughter that Graduated from East High,and a Son that is now a Freshmen at East Forsyth High. For the most part I have been very disappointed with WSFCS including East Forsyth. Kernersville Elementary was probably the only School my kids enjoyed. Theysay their is no tolerance for bullying,not true!! East Forsyth is loaded with drugs! The parents are always wrong,and if you upset them and step on their toes you may have ss at your door. They have caused a lot of turmoil in my Sons life. WSFCS needs a makeover! I disagree with all the negative reviews of this school. My kids love it! The teachers are great. My son, a freshman, even wrote a paper for his english class about how much he loved it. The principal is second to none on her involvement. The teachers don't teach. Some will just give you worksheets and expect you to know the answers without given any notes or instruction, while some will not assign any work at all and not care if you pass the final exam or not. Some teachers don't know anything about the topic they are teaching. I've went through 2 months in theatre arts class and everyday it was a free period. We just stared at each other. It was really boring, I felt like this school was punishment. I don't know why everyone else is giving a good review saying how good the teachers are, even though they suck. Very little teachers here properly give us notes and worksheets. I care about my future , and will never go to this school again. I hope you make the same decision After moving from San Diego to Kernersville we were surprised how well we like this school I absolutely loved my 4 years at East! My son goes to school there and for the most part it's a good school all except for the lady who works in the office. She's always in the worst mood and her attitude shows it.

column1: i graduated from HHS a few years ago. I found that the school expects you to live by their specific religous standards. I am not religous at all and found this completely ridiculous. However there are some REALLY great teachers there whom I learned alot from. A decent school if you put forth the effort. However, I found the lack of diversity at this school (racial and religious) a distraction many times. Again, it is what you make of it and it has decent academics. I just felt very different at this school, more so than before I moved here. I love this school. It is a wonderful environment that supports students progression in any of their desired fields. Students are taught to behave respectfully and to be responsible. The Arts teachers and AP or CE teachers are superb; especially the fantastic drama teacher who has built up student's confidence and dedication time and time again. The principle doesn't get the credit he deserves from many of these reviews. He does care about the success of the students and does a wonderful job. The councilors are friendly and always desirous to help. It is a school that is backed 100% by the community! Go Tigers! I really enjoyed going to school here. It is a small school with a lot of pride and spirit. The community is very tight knit and although the city council might not be the best the school is wonderful. The teachers are great, but you do have to be willing to put effort in, because as much as they would like teachers are unable to carry all of their students. MY DAUGHTER IS A GRADUATE FROM THIS SCHOOL SOON TO HAVE MY OTHER TWO FALLOW, THE OVER ALL SCHOOL IS GREAT THE TOWN SUPPORTS EVERY THING THEY DO.. over ALL I WOULD GIVE THIS SCHOOL A 5 IT IS SO MUCH BETTER THAN CALIFORNIA SCHOOLS AND THE DRAMA TEACHER IS GREAT ..HE REALLY LOVES THE KIDS AND WORKS RIGHT ALONG WITH THEM HAND AND HAND ..IM PROUD TO BE A TIGER SUPPORTER I was a Student at Hurricane High School for My Sophomore year and I LOVED It! By Far the best school that I have ever attended in my life. I am so sad to leave Hurricane High School. I have so many great memories there. The Teachers are amazing and I Loved every minute of my time there. The Drama Teacher (Hill) is Awesome! He works Hand in hand with each student and makes sure that you succeed. There are NO cliques! I Loved that there were No Cliques, The Students at Hurricane were so friendly and welcoming to new students. All around I would say that Hurricane High School is an amazing school and I wouldn't hesitate at all to send your child there. Amazing Teachers, Friendly Students, Great Test scores, and all over just a really fun school to attend. The teachers like to get a good kick out of teasing ya but its just for fun and only jokes they would never say anything to offend the students. I Would not think twice about sending your high schooler here. GO TIGERS!

In today's environment where you can pretty much send your kid to any district you want, I am very happy to say, I am doing just that. Excellent! My education prepared me for further education (three degrees), and inspired me to be the best that I could be!

column1: Brookville is really great in terms of acceptance and peer interaction. Students are really nice to all others, even those in different cliques. The problem lies in the academics and arts program though. The teachers are decent, but the offering of higher level courses leaves much to desire. It's the typical set the standard to the dumbest kid in the room type setting. Sports are pretty good here though. The drama department, though loving, fun, and developing still needs much to work on, and the band, though full of talent, also is only okay. The choir program is in really good shape though. Overall Brookville is a decent school. It was an awesome experience many years ago. And continues to be that way for current students. Very good communications between teachers and students. Very devoted faculty & staff. Excellent extracurricular activities, lots of students involved in a variety of things. Students are very supportive of each other.

column3: I had gone to Santaluces Community High School for the past 4 years. Honestly I can say that this school has prepared me more than just academically. The experiences you get from my school are just incredible. As a Jamaican and Chinese male I can say it is more than easy mixing cultures with other students and teachers of all races and backgrounds, which is important in coming of age. Students from all races do more than just get along, they are best of friends! The visual arts academy is the BEST at this school than anywhere else! Come to this school for this program! The art teachers are so dedicated and really do want students to succeed! The teachers at Santaluces are outstanding! Few teachers have their bad moments but you learn to get through it with them. They teach you the material you need to know to make sure you can understand, and if you are not sure ask them and they will be more than happy to go over it. They are there to teach you but you also laugh, cry, and share amazing times with these people. Everyone at this school will be your family and love you for whom you are! High School is a important step in life and I am glad I had the chance to grow up at Santaluces! My son is in his senior year at this school and it just seems to me that this school only seems to get better. The academies are top notch and the school does a great job of keeping parents informed. I love the diverse population and the camaraderie that the kids all seem to have with one another. I am a student at this school. The teachers are mostly terrible. Some don't even teach. They give u a worksheet and hope you learn it. Some are basically just supervisors. They watch you work. The students here are awful. They're rude and have no respect for people. They spit in the halls and push people. Many are entitled, loud, and flat out arrogant. The staff treats the school like a jail, yelling at the kids as they walk by, and give out lunch detentions for the pettiest of things. If you miss a day of school, you're simply accused of skipping. The school itself is gross and dirty. The walls and floors are nasty, and there are dead bugs everywhere. The school can barely afford decent desks. I've witnessed some break as people sat in them. The buses, especially mine, are packed nearly two times the legal limit. Do not go to this school if you have the choice. The worst school. Stay away from it while you can. Take your kid to a better place and save a headache to yourself. Amazing they helped me raise my grades Stay away from this school with the sanctuary status students do whatever they feel like it. Teachers and guidance are leaving the school because it is a joke. Teaching is no existing here. Do yourself a favor and take your kid to a much better school than this one. Bullies are free to do whatever they feel because they can get away! The principal is rude and lacks of intelligence. The worse experience ever! After two years here I am so glad that I will never return. All schools have their share of problems. Santaluces provides every opportunity for students to succeed. If your child embraces their programs, guidance assistance with higher education, and clubs your child will be successful. I am a parent who has been involved for the past 8 years and counting. Yes, there are awful teachers and phenomenal teachers. As long as you communicate, Santaluces Administration will work with you. You can go to any other high school and see the same problems, but Santaluces has so much to offer.

column1: Horrible!! There is no standard of learning. Children are taught to be seen but not heard. They allow students to be assaulted. I have never known a school to have such a high turnover rate in teachers and staff. attended the school from pre-k to 9th grade. the school gradually got worse and worse. very bad bullying issues. very poor education system, especially is sciences.

column3: I graduated from Irondequoit HightSchool, as did both my children. I moved back to Rochester/Irondequoit from Northern California because I wanted my kids to grow up in an awesome family oriented environment with great schools and lots of recreational opportunities. My son graduated from Brockport and is now the Owner of several businesses and my daughter is a sophomore at SUNY Cortland. IHS prepared them well for their futures. Beautiful School. Clean, great staff, lots of sports and opprotunities. The teachers are fantastic and it's a pleasure coming to school everyday Both of my children graduated from IHS after attending Listwood, Iroquois and Dake. They were all excellent schools with parent involvement and very good teachers. Wonderful community. IHS prepared my children well for college, both at Ivy Leagues. Great teachers, great classes, and a great community. I am an alumni of IHS and now raising my kids going to the same school district. I have had nothing but great experiences!

column1: A great school starts at the top, and Waterville has smart, professional, friendly, caring and innovative administrators. Those same qualities are evident in the excellent teaching staff, who pass along strong community values of warmth, kindness, generosity and a sense of humor and fun to the students. There's a lot of hometown spirit and pride here. Great marching band, interesting variety of electives, and a stubborn tradition of being the only school to remain open when all other schools call a snow day gives extra days off when the weather turns nice.

column3: Woodbridge has been a very good High School for my Daughter, and she has attended two other highly rated High Schools listed in Great Schools. Due to my prior Military career (now retired), my Daughter had to transfer twice. With Woodbridge being her last School, she was still able to maintain her high grades and have a diverse group of friends that she likes. The Teachers,Staff and curriculum have all been great! Woodbridge Senior High School has disappointed me. We were impressed with what it had to offer when we moved here but have found the school only looks good on paper. I highly advise you to avoid this school if your child will transfer in from another high school out of state/country. We came from a DoDEA school in Germany. The school guidance/ administration is not educated in this type of transfer. Mostly the SOL requirements have confused them. It's been tough. My children registered for JROTC and were extremely active. We have become more and more disappointed in this program. The leadership doesn't follow school guidelines for field trips and basic safety. They also lack in any type of mentoring. Comments about administration not caring or listening to parents are spot on. Have had two graduate from WSHS with more following. Won't send the others there. They won't even follow county policies. WSHS does not want parents involved. On a positive, if you child is a star football player you'll be treated like royalty. I graduated from WSHS last year and have to say there are no "pods" yes the school is over populated but it has yet to cause any sort of problem. The guidance councelors are not great. They seem to lack motivation and did not help me in any way when it came to picking classes, writing college essays, essays to receive scholarships, or anything SAT/ACT related. Most of the teachers on the other hand are so incredibly helpful, it is rare to find a teacher that won't let you retake tests/quizzes or stay after for tutoring. Over all a great school, change the guidance counselors and it would be the best in Prince William County. Guidance counselors are foolish, unintelligent, and unhelpful. They are lazy, careless, and lack motivation to help students with the college process. I have had few memorable teachers and overall they have been nothing special. There is a lack of attention towards students who are not star athletes. There is a high demand for money here, and students are required to pay fees for required classes, transcripts, and everything in between. Huckestein is the poorest excuse for a principle in the entire county and cares only about how well his sons are treated in the school. The only positive thing to say about this school are the memories I've made, my friends, and close relationships with a select few teachers. Otherwise, avoid if possible. Made many memories here. Unfortunately some not so great, but some will change my life. For the most part, very supporting and helpful of the LGBTQ+ community. Unless you seek help by yourself for college, you won't recieve any. Football games are very spirited, a lot of school pride. And I agree with the others, it is money hungry and overpopulated. Because they plan to move the CFPA program it likely will change. Teachers typically go against county rules, the homework rule in specific. You are only supposed to have 30 minutes of homework per class, including AP, and I often find myself spending up to 2 hours on certain subjects. I can't imagine how rough it is on student athletes. Certain faculty show care towards you, but favoritism is evident. On a more positive note, they do their best to make school a fun experience. Many extracurriculars and sports, as well as events and fundraisers that are enjoyable. Very clique-y at times. Each group of friends is very divided and rarely blend. Again, if you play sports you'll be worshipped, it's evident that if you spend your time as a scholar you are under appreciated. I have one year left at the school, and educationally it's extraordinary. I promise it's an amazing learning space. Socially is where issues arise. I will return to update is anything changes. This school is community oriented and has wonderful traditions from a 50 year history. The new principal is Ms. Heather Abney, she was just what was need here. The guidance department has also had a change of leadership. The school continues to have amazing teachers. They are the heart of the school as well as all the students. The engineering program, Project Lead the Way is outstanding. There are numerous clubs, but the Robotics club is definitely a stand out with their winning history. The Marching Band and the Vikettes Dance Team have always had award winning seasons, each receiving top honors. All the sports are well represented. the football games are well attended and enjoyed by the students with incredible school spirit demonstrated at the Friday night home games. Most sports make it to the conference tournaments and some conference championships. A hidden gem, is the ice hockey team at this school, they lost in the state championship last year. In general, a very well rounded school. Do NOT Go HERE! No one cares. My son has had an amazing first year. The school spirit is the best in the county and we love all of the performances put on by the drama department. WSHS is a great school!!! There are a lot of structural things that need to be done, but there is a group of parents that are working very hard to get these issues fixed, by going to school board meetings. I do know the past years at WSHS has been poorly manged by past administrations (Huckstein was the poorest principal and did nothing to better the school, but somehow our children along with some fabulous teachers got through those years). We now have Ms. Abney and she has made the most positive changes and has the school back on track to achieve goals. It is on its way to being one of the best schools in Va. if you have the chance to visit and meet Ms. Abney you will know that this is the school for your children. WSHS is an excellent school! We really like the diversity, community, and welcoming feel of this school. When you walk into the school it feels warm, accepting, and a sense of belongingness. My son really enjoys it and we do as well. WSHS is an older school but continues to have the legacy that makes it stand out. There are updates to the school that are beginning to happen such as a new stadium starting in January. The principal, Mrs. Abney is absolutely amazing and encourages the students everyday to be their best. Her leadership and committment to the school environment has increased the morale of the school tremendously. In addition, WSHS just received the School of Excellence award! We are so proud of WSHS students, leadership, and staff for this huge accomplishment! I can’t say enough great things about this wonderful school! Woodbridge Senior High School has been an absolutely positive experience for our family. The teachers and administation are phenomenal. They have met the very difficult year of covid with transparency, and adaptation and commitment. The school offers a wide range of clubs and teams for all interests. Ranging from Football to one of the largest (and best) Robotics teams in the state. Being a large school, they are able to offer a full selection of AP classes as well as programs such as Aviation Maintenance, Project Lead the Way (Engineering), and Cosmetology. I would definitely recommend WSHS! Avoid at all costs. The teachers routinely bring politics into the classroom in an extremely biased fashion. The Principal and administration are useless and refuse to address the outright indoctrination occurring in many classes. On top of that, many of the teachers are poor at best; their ability to impart knowledge and motivate students is dismal. All three of my children have attended this school and even they can plainly see the issues. Our experiences at WSHS has been great! The teachers, administration, and staff truly care about the students. WSHS is a community based school which is warm and welcoming. The respect for diversity is also shown throughout the school. WSHS did an excellent job with handling COVID and virtual learning. Woodbridge High school's rating should be higher to truly reflect how wonderful the school is. We have been pleased with WSHS and our children have been happy here as well. This school is great. My child graduated with AP college credits and now, she goes to GEORGETOWN UNIVERSITY! I totally believe that your children can do the same and the teachers are supportive most of the time. This is one of the best schools in Prince William County! This school encourages parent participation and welcomes volunteers.It’s a big school with lots of kids and some very good teachers

column1: Hamlin High School is a great place to work. We are moving forward with integrating technology in the classroom. Hamlin Collegiate, new name new attitude and standards. The current administration has taken steps to ensure all students have the opportunity to graduate with college readiness. Things are changing and improving at this school. We came for the Montessori program, and my children thrived at ages 3, 4, and 5 with the freedom to move around, choose works they found interesting, and had strong relationships with their teachers.

column3: I love what this school did for my child. The teachers my child had really cared about students. The principal sits with his students during lunchtime and gets to know them. That is unheard of in other schools. I believe and have observed that both the administration and teachers really want to help our children become successful. And they LIKE their students. This school certainly turned my child's life around. There are still issues of bullying, serious enough that there should be police action taken for harassment and yet things go untouched as teachers are held in the bind of morally standing up for the right thing and risking loss of their jobs over taking a stand and having some bully's parent get angry and defensive. There is a wide divide between the 'haves' and the 'have nots'. There are a few teachers that show active favoritism toward the students that are from better parts of town, better families. While this could be because those teachers are simply uncomfortable interacting with the other students from less wealthy families, this should be something that they should get over. The school itself academically is still struggling to break out of the cookie cutter mold and catch up with today's job situation. The idea is still to gear us/students for college, but the focus should be on what career/job and THEN college. There is so little preparation in this area that is sets everyone back. There are so few classes geared toward Accounting, Technology/Programming, and medical areas -all key work fields now- that it is a hindrance. One of the best in the area! We loved RAHS. My daughter did so well there, her teachers were terrific and they DO offer a great deal of programs geared toward future college goals. Not sure why anyone would say otherwise, as now that we have moved we no longer have the options Reedsburg offered. They do offer Accounting 1 & 2, Intro into Health Occupations, as well as a lot more. We are not wealthy and my daughter was never made to feel any differently than anyone else. She has a very good attitude and great personality, so maybe it is all perspective? I would love for her to finish out her last two years at Reedsburg, but with moving this is no longer an option. We will really miss it and can only hope she gets the same level of education and support that she did there. Good job RAHS, you ROCK :)

column1: Should have moved to a bigger school that offered more opportunities. This school lacks diversity in always including thought. As a parent of two Sparta elementary students I could not be more proud to say my children attend Sparta! I love the teachers and staff ! My children do as well! However as a parent of two Sparta high school students I could not be more dissapointed with how they seem to make sure they cover their faults instead of making right by them! One specific teacher lied and put blame on a student for something that my child witnessed her do! I think the superintendent has covered things up to make things "go away" and people in this community are talking. Just ask around before enrolling your children!!! Low test scores and a lack of supervision in the high school. The administration covers its self before worrying about the kids.. Low test scores and an administration that lacks control. The high school is lacking in diversity. As a parent of a Sparta elementary students I could not be more proud to say my children attend Sparta! I Yet the high school is at the bottom of schools in the area. I believe that there are favorites and that drug testing should be for all student athletes not just the same ones who pass. Poor test scores that point larger problems. If you dig into these scores you can see a pattern of decline. Our Sparta school system wastes taxpayer money and it is in a very steep decline. Great school!!! Great community! The class sizes are great. This is truly a great place to send your kids!!!

There is only one word to say about this school and it its just wow. This school is just terrible, with these new rules they have for 2022 my daughter and my son have been struggling to make sure they are not late to class or even in the morning. In the morning my kids ride the bus but whats the point if they have to wait outside for 45 minutes. Bowsher needs to get everything fixed or I'm taking my kids to Maumee.

column1: This school has been rated in the top 100 high schools in the nation by US News and World Report, Newsweek and the Washington Post. The class sizes are small the staff is excellent. The students are high performing even when it is not expected.

column3: Great school system! My kids do not attend school there now but will soon. My kids go to school in Seminole. It will make you realize how good Andrews schools are. Horrible school. I personally don't like it an I talk to the students an I could say that atleast 65% agree with me on this. Many teachers are very polite an respectful, but majority of the people in "charge" are ignorant idiotic people. Still don't take my word on it. See it for yourself. I went to school here grades K-12. I have two kids of my own now and cannot fathom them going anywhere else. The schools here are one of the best things about Andrews. I am so blessed to be able to raise my family here. We moved to Andrews for my husbands job. My daughter is 14 years old and it in 8th grade. From the first day she was being bulling and another student. She had people tell her they don't like new kids. In class there are things said to her in front of the teachers and still nothing is being done. Things are being said about her that are untrue and mean. I would never wish any-other child be put in this situation. I beg you as a parent PLEASE do not let your child go to any Andrews ISD school!!!!! Andrews High School is a joke. The school has no control over their students, the teachers do not want to teach and are fed up, let's not for get the staff they don't want to be bothered. The environment at this school is disgusting. The students run the school and their is a major safety issue. This school is not a school to send your child if you want them to get an education. What a terrible place. I was warned about avoiding Andrews due to a bad mix of parents, but the homes were cheaper. They were right, we messed up and sent a kid here. The students are mainly backwoods or “think they’re rich” and the kids act accordingly. The school talks more about its football team than both the other sports and especially education. The majority of the football team also smokes and drinks and frankly, I worry that some of those parents actually provide it for them! The kids are about the rudest we have encountered anywhere. Since most of the kids don’t accelerate in grades, the parents mostly focus on sports and that’s just a bad combination. When my child started AHS. They were picked on daily. I went and talked with one of the assistant principals, and for the most part, it was fixed for a moment. The bullying lasted from freshman through sophomore year.. My child's last year there, my child, got seriously depressed, that they no longer wanted to go to school. We went up there and talked with the counselors. They made my child feel worse then before. We then talked with the principal, and boy! He cannot be reasoned with. He feels like he runs a perfect school. That his school has no bullies, only kids that are not being nice. The principal and one of the counselors both made us feel like our child was the villain, and not the victim. Overall, we thought that the teachers were pretty good. The principal at this school is completely incompetent of maintaining order and following through with discipline. His management of the discipline code is poor at best. Inconsistencies and lack of consequences has allowed the students to run the show. Mr. Clark, you should be ashamed that you allow bullies to participate in the athletic programs!!! Disgraceful! Personally I don't think that Andrews High is that great. I have gone to Andrews schools all my school life. I've always disliked it due to favoritism, homophobic remarks, bullying, cliques, and just the overall feeling I get being there. I don't feel safe there. No amount of safety precautions will because my issue of bullying. Start from the inside out, to be truly safe, Andrews ISD. Never have my kids and nibblings have gone to a school where the administration has been disrespectful on multiple accounts. Never have I heard about a school where the teachers do not teach yet blame students for not understanding. Never have heard about a school where teachers have laughed in faces of students and parents/guardians. the staff at AHS is incredibly disrespectful and takes no account/responsibility for anything. My kids and niece are all honors/AP students with good grades, I've never ever had problems with any school they've gone to ever gone to except for this school. At this school, it's hard to be different. Most people at this school are Caucasian, athletic, and Christian. Students of a different sexual orientation, other than heterosexual, have a hard time fitting in at this school. Most of the teachers are wonderful, caring people who truly care and go out of their way for the students. They try hard to instill great values in their students regardless of their background, and are effective leaders. The level of preparation for college could be improved a bit.

column1: I am a former student of Eureka Jr./Sr. High School. I dropped out because of severe bullying and the complete disinterest of the school board to take action. I went on to receive my GED and went straight to college at age 16. This was due to my own interest in furthering my education and not because of any support from teachers or school board. The state of student life should be a cause of concern to say the least. Bullying is a terrible problem. The staff shows favoritism to students who are more active in sports and the 7th through 12th grade set-up under the same roof is a major problem resulting in (among other things) thirteen year-olds dating eighteen year-olds. This school is a disgrace and is in major need reorganization and getting priorities straight. I went to school in Eureka from sixth grade all the way up to my senior year. The reviews I have read on here do not fit my experiences I had at Eureka Jr./Sr. High School. As a student there, I found myself in a small and loving community, where the teachers genuinely care about not only your performance in school, but about you as an individual as well. At Eureka Jr./Sr. High, you are surrounded by teachers and coaches who want to see you achieve even your wildest dreams. From 5-Star faculty to a great building with very new technology, Eureka is a great school for everyone. Growing up in Eureka, I had a great education. The teachers prepared me for a successful college career and I always felt that there was someone I could talk to. Going to school in Eureka, even though there was drama, I knew that everyone would deb there to support me (especially the teaching staff). They still keep in touch and ask how I'm doing fairly regularly. Eureka is an excellent school to attend because the staff members are of a very high caliber and really prepare students well for college and life experiences. Additionally, aside from the professionalism exhibited by the staff members, they also are there to help whenever students need something that may not even pertain to school and go above and beyond their job descriptions on a daily basis. On the service Eureka looks like any other school, but if you work there or been around long enough to see the secrets then you know this isn't true. Idk maybe all schools are like that. I know the staff will lie to get the courts involved when parents, or students don't go along with what they want. I have never seen a teacher tell a Doctor he didn't know what he was talking about when describing an illness & how the school can accommodate like they supposed to, except in eureka. It’s a wonderful school! My daughter has loved this school since her first day. And we moved at winter break. So it was already enough for her. But everyone has been so accommodating and great with communication on what my daughter needs more of to be successful.

column3: My daughter was viciously bullied at McMichael. She was in the special needs classes and I believe that made her a target. My daughter "learned" in middle school that no adults were to be trusted and they blew off her reports of being bullied. She took a regular class and the teacher of this class berated her. She stood up for herself, reported it to the principal, and she got a week's worth of detention. Overall well. I have loved this school and now that I am currently at a university with no student debt, I can confidently say that this school has prepared me for college. Students are polite and respectful and staff is great to work with

column1: This is my son's first year at the school and so far, the feedback has been great. He is highly motivated by his teachers. My daughter is so excited to learn. Although she has to get up at 6am to make it to school on time, she does it with a smile and a whistle. She usually is so hard to wake in the morning. On top of that she has 3 honors classes in the 9th grade and has to work hard, but she loves the community feel she gets at this school. BJS is a tough review. The teachers are dedicated and the administration strict. Sadly, like any typical Catholic school, some kids get away with being disruptive because parents throw money at the school. As parents, my spouse and I didn't make much money and worked very hard to enroll our sons at Snyder. Our older son did not like it. He loved his teachers, but never felt like he fit in with his peers and came home crying very often. Still, he pushed through and I'm proud that he excelled in college, while many of his classmates barely got anywhere, despite a college prep education. This does not undermine the quality of the school's curriculum. Teachers always challenged the students, many whom were very spoiled and arrogant and brought it upon themselves. Our second son went later after the school had grown more and he loved it. Between both, I earned the trust of some teachers who vented with me their initial frustrations. More recently they have told me things have gotten much enter at BJS: the new incoming classes are more respectful and teacher morale has improved. We have been at this schoolFor 7 years and It has been throw a lot of changes and I’m not sure that it’s a good thing. Just the past 3 years we have started having problems. It’s a special place. Academic rigor with a laser like focus on faith. Kids are polite, leadership makes an effort to be present and know families, and the kids are pushed to aggressively to prepare for college. If your student isn’t one to thrive with structure, this may not be the school for them. A lot is expected of the kids. Kids can play sports and enjoy sports and activities.

column3: Our son graduated from this high school and our two daughters now attend FIHS. The academics are decent and the teachers competent, but all three of our kids were made miserable by an influential minority of pampered suburbans white kids who model their behavior after inner-city thugs. They use urban slang, deface property with grafitti, and get into fights. The moral and spiritual impact on our kids has been devastating. Wish we had never put them in that environment. If you love your kids and can afford it, you will be much better off putting them in a private school. I purposely purchased my home in Fleming Island for my daughter to attend Fleming Island High School. The lack of interest from the guidance office is truly a sad affair! I have never been treated so unprofessionally and was embarrassed that my daughter was witness to it. To be pointed at without at word and directed into the male guidance counselors office with not even a handshake or introduction with again another finger point infuriated me. I was dressed in business attire and expected to be treated with respect as a mother and a professional business person. My daughter and I were reaching out for help during a difficult time and were treated so poorly. I can only hope that this is not a typical event for other parents. I did speak with the Principle and he did offer kindness however unable to offer any help with the original issue. That being, my daughter asking to be transfered to another class where she would be able to study and learn, from as class where the teacher was unable to do so due a discipline problem with several other students. We were refused this request . I definitely would not rate this school a 10! My 2 sons went to FIHS and performed fairly well academically. It seemed as though the students in the honor's and AP classes received a lot more attention from the teachers, for developing the students for college. My daughter started there and I saw a whole different side on this school. The front office receptionist make everyone feel as if they were bothering her and unimportant. Lack of leadership. The principal was aloof to the students. Teachers that stood out, Ms. Weldon, Mr. Taylor and Mr. Neidrich. My daughter ended up transferring out of this school 2 months before her senior year, because of the tremendous amount of peer pressure and cattiness from the girls at that school. She was threatened and bullied many times and asked to change schools 2 years before we made the change. Once we transferred, I realized how rude and disrespectful the staff was at FIHS. The staff and administration at OPHS were so helpful and courteous. Even the principal introduced herself to my daughter. So, glad we made the change. My daughter is flourishing now in her senior year! Wish I had sent all my kids to a different school. I came to post a review and came across many similar reviews of what I was going to address...This school needs to run an anti-bully campaign, and enforce more parental involvement on this matter. Many kids with "I am gangster" attitude", bullying kids with better moral values.These bullies start their verbal attacks in school hallways and inside the school buss, bringing the worst on the buss stops. It is a shame that children look forward to the High School years and withing the first month of class they rude awakening. Many parents moved these neighborhood due to the "great" school system. This school is no longer what it used to be when it gain its great reputation. Great families have moved in the near neighborhoods, but also families with poor family values and children with lack of parental guidance, with that "wanna' be gangster" attitude. Bringing down the happy, safe, and family oriented stigma these neighborhoods have.These are the same people who have ruined the quality of the high school experience for our children. I agree 100% with the FCAT comments bellow. Not to mention the awful attitude of many of these teachers and staff members. I have 2 children that attend this school. 1 is a senior the other a sophomore. We have been very pleased! My kids are average students, some honors classes. They have been on a few sports teams but not every year. They have not participated in any groups or clubs. Just some background info. We moved to Fleming Island in 1997 because of the school. The kids have attended school in this area from pre-k to current. If we have had issues to address they have be met with full attention an concern. We have always felt that the kids best interest was attended to. All staff, ads, teachers an administrator have been available and willing to assist us when ever needed. The kids safety is always first. I only have good things to say about the entire school! We are very fortunate to have this school! I definitely agree with the other reviews regarding the front office woman that you have to deal with. She is so unfriendly and seems annoyed every time I come there. Hoping the new principal will rectify this. Both my kids are honors. One graduated last year and we are both thankful he is done. Academically he did well but as for the teachers being competent and caring, not so much. He admits that he didn't learn much. I have another child going into 10th this year and I pray that it will be better than last year. He had a few good teachers and a few terrible teachers. I am a very involved parent when it comes to education and trying to jump through the hoops to have conferences with teachers who don't seem to care about their students and have poor, unprofessional attitudes was so frustrating to me. I think this school is going downhill fast. So many great teachers are leaving and being replaced with people who don't enjoy teaching or like kids for that matter. The electives and programs like AICE, Business Finance, & TV Production are a joke. They sound good on paper but few benefit from them. Depending on the day, counselors can be helpful or not. Good luck. "The front office receptionist make everyone feel as if they were bothering her and unimportant. Lack of leadership." Agree 100%. This also includes other staff members, and teachers who lack skills to deal with children (and seem they are just teaching to have some kind of authoritative position in their lives, not because they like to teach) , like others reviews mention. Every time I have to walk in to this school I have to take a deep breath and prepare myself for the regular and inevitable unconformable experience, I can't imagine how many children feel this way every day they have to come to this school. I hope to see changes this year as well. The guidance department is handled unprofessionally, and definitely does not address the best for each student. Beware!! First of this school is horrible the teachers seem to have no regard for the students well being or even care too the fact that they are even teaching us instead they act as if everyday was one day closer too being away from the students, please if your going too try to send your kids here yeah the multi million dollar school looks awesome on the outside, but Clay high is like 10 miles up the road and Orange Park not that far either, if your planning to come to Fleming Island for the school, find a nice house in green cove and never let your children get zoned for this school, i wish thats what i did. I am only writing this review because of how ridiculous these other reviews are. I am a former student of FIHS. The academics of the school are above par. But the curriculum that the child is to get is solely based on their academic prowess. The AICE program is as good as it gets (No I wasn't in AICE), while the standard classes are decent. I was in mostly honors and AP classes but I had numerous standard classes as well and they are taught by good teachers. Teachers who show regard for students well being and care for the kids WHO ACTUALLY CARE. The kids who act like idiots in class don't get the same POSITIVE attention. I wonder why... then the parents go on rants about how the teachers don't care about the kids, yet their kids are the ones acting out... Now this is a HIGH SCHOOL remember, so there is going to be bullying no matter what. It is going to happen, some no bullying campaign won't help, trust me. Kids will be mean, it happens, so deal with it or home school them or put them in a private school and stop complaining. The kids don't fight, they're too prissy for it. In 4 years there I remember like, 10 fights max, mostly girl fights. It's a good school. My Daughter graduated from FIHS in 2007 and my Son is a student now. FIHS is an excellent school. The teachers and staff are outstanding! My Daughter had an issue with another student bullying her and all it took was one phone call to the principal before it was resolved. All of the programs are very well organized and the guidance counselors have been there every step of the way for us. One thing to keep in mind when reading these reviews is that most people only post a review when they're having issues but I can assure you that there are 1,000's of families that would recommend FIHS. He has found the AICE program to be challenging and has already gotten involved in student Government and other freshman class activities. The majority of his teachers go out of their way to email agendas and other information to parents. The AICE guidance counselor has also been great at answering any questions we may have whether they applied to the program or not. The principal is very approachable and makes a point of attending even the smaller school functions. We moved to Clay County for the schools and been very happy so far. I have a 10th grader at FIHS. She attended private school from K-8 and walked into this school not knowing anyone. Thanks to the broad programs offered at this school, she has made wonderful friendships via multiple programs. The teachers are tough and set the bar very high, which is what we need more of. Our family is thankful to have moved here specifically for better education. The principal definetly shows that he cares - this is via my daughter telling me (of course). And lastly, the kids CHOOSE to wear FIHS clothing - which is NOT something we did back when I was in school and says SO much about how the kids feel about FIHS. Great school! I am a parent of 4 children who have now graduated from Fleming. I have never had a problem here at this school and all 4 of my kids have enjoyed going being apart of the Eagles. Great school, Great Teachers and a wonderful staff. We moved here for this school and have not regretted it one bit! We moved from St Johns county where the schools are rated very well but going downhill. The teachers here are caring and involved. I get regular emails on my daughter's progress and have found the counselors to be busy but helpful. This is my daughters second year and we have not run into the bully issue or such things. In St Augustine, it was a daily problem for students. We love this school. The only downside is that they do not have a program for special needs students. My other daughter attends Clay High, which I find to also be outstanding. It has been quite an experience, as the teachers are often amazing, the students are rather lacking in kindness and competition is at its peak. I was a student at this school and the experience I had here was so incredibly awful. The school is obviously predominately white which believe it or not has caused various racial issues. Racial slurs have been written in the bathroom, on desks, and in numerous other places around the school. Let's not forget the infamous craigslist post titled "Slaves for Sale", which was possibly the most disrespectful thing I have ever seen at Fleming Island High, possibly at any school in Clay County. The kids who made that post didn't get a good enough consequence, which brings me to the administration. From my experience, the administration at this school plays favorites. Unless you're an athlete or "relevant" enough for them to even slightly care, don't even bother going. Along with the rude and nasty kids there, the administration is just as bad and childish as these rich spoiled brats. The teachers can't even teach properly but when you get a bad grade or answer a question wrong, they get highly offended and this and that and just blame it on you. You could have a whole notebook of notes and study days on end, but that doesn't matter. They'll teach a whole lesson in an hour and a half and announce there's a test the next day. My experience here was also horrible with the students. They're rude, constantly looking for ways to talk about somebody and think they're better than everyone since they're of course, at Fleming Island. Nobody respects anybody and oh let's not forget, a student committed suicide because a few of the students here. This school all together is a horrible excuse for a school. The administration is horrible and cares about how they look and their status of the school, students believe the same, especially athlete. Nobody cares about a true education here. After the school year was finally over, I quickly went back to Orange Park High School because I have never witnessed such a sad excuse for people, education, and a school. If you are a parent looking into sending your kid(s) here, I suggest you look somewhere else unless you want them dealing with bullying, competition, and snobby rich brats. If you want them happier, I suggest these 3 schools in Clay County which I have great experiences with and who care about their students, Ridgeview High School, Orange Park High School, or Oakleaf. Horrible. Lady in the front office is very rude. If you call to ask for help she has an attitude and acts inconvenienced. When you need to interact with the school to contact teachers, coaches, school counselors, etc., the person in the front office is often the first point of contact. Tells a lot about the administration. I am sure this is a good school for the advance placement kids. However, truant students are not given any consequences and the grades earned by truant students bear no relationship whatsoever to actual school attendance. Indeed, the school fails to follow its own rules regarding tardies or unexcused absences for truant kids. This is unfair to all the kids who actually put in the effort. Both the state and federal departments of education should investigate this situation at FIHS as school graduation rates impact the amount of state and federal funds a school gets. The school also has been nicknamed "the pharmacy" by the community at large. The school does not care what happens in their bathrooms. Private schools, in my opinion, would serve kids better.

column3: There is very little supplement for the academically advanced. Everyone needs to equal in Granby, but there is no focus on students after they hit a certain level. Great school system for students who are struggling but think twice before sending your kid there for an advanced education. Had fantastic teachers and was phenomenally accommodating for kids with disabilities. Bullying was practically nonexistent. This school is a terrible school. Most of the reviews that you see here are written by a teacher, that is why they have for some odd reason the best word choice. Teachers focus solely on the work rather than the feelings of the students. Workload is often overwhelming. Obviously no coordination between separate departments on anything. Don't let the Nine fool you unless test scores are everything and environment nothing. I have tried to stay objective, but many students are mean and entitled, if your child is a popular sports kid then your in luck but if not buckle up for a few years of dragging your child to a battle ground every day. The techers try so hard but the culture has formed around students and their parents. The complete lack of diversity does not help, and this was highlighted by racial slurs popping up as graffiti on the school sign. Want to know that the culture is like, just watch the movie "mean girls". If you are looking at a culture of students that embraces differences, is kind and accepting look elsewhere for your child! We moved our teen from a highly rated private school because we’d heard terrific things about GMHS. Small classes, great teachers, coordinated multidisciplinary curriculum sports and extracurricular activities, AP and honors classes available in nearly every subject. The school is run well by a committed staff, and is quite large for a small suburb. Two gyms, separate practice and instructional rooms for band and chorus, large updated cafeteria that’s being expanded and upgraded, beautiful large library, many sports fields, great running track, set back with large surrounding fields and woods. School is a bit large to navigate class to class but our teen figured it out quickly. It’s also nice that the school offers digital design, robotics classes (and club), as well as a full complement of arts classes. Disability services are excellent and well-coordinated. A structured study hall is offered and pleasantly small, offering one-to-one customized coaching. Our kids are enjoying the community and taking advantage of the many opportunities. We can’t speak much about college counseling except for the programs that start freshman year. We’re very pleased thus far. The collective school community has been much more than we could have ever expected. One of our teens receives support for several learning disabilities, and in a short time, has progressed with the support they received. We’ve been able to dial down parts of their support and coaching while still keeping services available as needed. During COVID, our teen needed more support transitioning back to in-person learning, and the school quickly stepped up. Our teen is now taking multiple AP courses, as well as honors classes, and is independently, proactively managing their challenging course load with a small bit of support in organizational skills through disability services (checking in weekly, assessing their progress, following up with teachers, and coordinating other support services). GMHS sees each student in a holistic way, and it’s been apparent since our first shadow day there. Great school!We can’t say enough

column1: This school is great!!!! Under the guidance of wonderful teachers and a very involved guidance department - my daughter has blossomed from a B/C student to a student with almost all straight A's. We love this school!!!! I found Holy Cross High very disappointing in regards to the way the administration handles any concerns or problems. The archaic policies and way of thinking, I feel will never change until the current administration changes. Students and parents seldom find any satisfaction to situations that may occur because of the lack of any authority overseeing Holy Cross. You are often left with a " Too Bad " attitude. If I had to do it all over again I would find another High School to spend my hard working money on! Holy Cross is in desperate need of some policy changes! For example, the Valedictorian and Salutatorian of the school may not actually be the 1st and 2nd ranked in the class. This is solely due to the fact that they follow a policy they have been using that is at least, 43 years old! While other High Schools perform the simple calculation appropriately at the end of the school year to determine rank, HCHS does their calculation back in December, ignoring half of senior year. This method can result in the wrong student receiving an award. The worst part is that when this problem was brought to their attention, they really could not be bothered to address it. Imagine if your child worked hard all four years to achieve the rank of 1st or 2nd in the class to not even get acknowledged in the slightest bit for their accomplishment. Beware! This is just one of the backward policies that are in use at Holy Cross High School! My third child knew in 7th grade that he wanted to go to Holy Cross, I'm not sure why but I'm sure glad that he did. After my two older children attended Pomparaug HS I see the comparison in the two schools as night and day. You can argue over which school has better teachers, programs, courses and athletics but the greatest difference I have seen is in my child. He goes to school with a purpose. He gets good grades, sure. He is involved in sports and to my surprise the school play and musical, sure but when your kid tells you after asking him how was school and his response is that he heard the best sermon that he has ever heard in his life, wow! When your kid says he favorite class is Christian Morality. i now understand why my second child said to me I wish I went to Holy Cross. I asked him why and his response was that every kid he's every met from Holy Cross where nice people. Then he said, even my friends aren't nice people. I am new to the school as a parent. I attended public school in Waterbury and wish I went to Holy Cross High School. This school is so supportive so school spirited that I have only ever seen in movies. I watch kids in and out all hours of the day. Supporting the athletics their friends the community. They are all so helpful always a smiling, The school initiates help and guidance with grades with being a ear or a advocate. I am so proud to be a Holy Cross Parent and will support whatever the school needs. GO CRUSADERS!!

column1: A review has not been done in quite sometime, so let me take this opportunity and say...This is my 6th year having my children attend TVCS and this will be the only school my children go to. Great right? :.......well unfortunately our friends in old people Disney USA dont follow any of those rules, they ONLY and I repeat ONLY allow students to attend their "school" if their parents worl in the community known as the villages, like working in a small store in a giant mall. THey spend more money per student here than anywhere in the state (beautiful grounds) The complaints I have read are based on the school's rigorous disciplinary, dress, and conduct code, which are absent in other schools in the area. THEY HAVE HIGH STANDARDS so if you aren't into having a child that is goal-oriented and more proficient that required by the state, don't have them attend here. PERIOD. Parents MUST be involved and be employed directly by "The Villages" so check into that before you seek employment. Also, you must volunteer 20hrs per year for each student - check the website. Excellent culinary program and the dance program is award-winning (google it) Since we moved here in 2008, they have built a new Preschool which opened 2012, a new structure for the 4-5th graders opened 2013, and a new wing for the 1st graders opened 2013 also. All to accommodate the growth of the student body. Staff is superior.... all set the "golden standard" - Definitely exceeds the state standard on all levels. Not in any way lacking. They proudly claim that reading is their number 1 priority (hence the reason they rarely teach the other subjects). However, for my son to be on grade level in reading I have has to teach him at home, every night since kindergarten. It's sad how many people can be fooled by pretty things and a smile. It is an amazing school with an amazing staff and student body. The teachers stay by yourside and do everything they can to help you succeed. The students (all though we are teenagers ) are on their best behavior and show respect that you wouldn't normally see in a high school. There are rarely any fights on school ground. Cops are rarely called. If you are interested in bringing your kid here I strongly recommend it. Though there is a lot of requirements I believe it is a small sacrifice in return of giving your child a great school experience and to have a successful outcome :) it really is a great school and that's coming from the student who has to wear the uniforms everyday and be with the staff everyday. He us a senior this year and he has half day at school and asked if I could take him to The Villages High School so that he can visit his friends. We went today and were welcomed with opened arms. The staff has been looking for opportunities for me in the job market there so that he can be re enrolled for his senior year. I've seen some reviews about this school from a few that are upset with the way this school goes through the eligibility process. Everyone knows from the beginning about the requirements so why those people are putting the school down...Not a clue. Terrific school by far. I’m the grandmother, but I know my granddaughter has blossomed transferring to the charter school her 9th grade year. She’s a straight A student in advanced classes, and she’s a varsity Golden Girl. She seems to have lots of friends, and she likes all of her teachers. I feel blessed and happy my daughter and family moved to Harbor Hills. I’m in The Villages. Thank you Charter School. I have had two daughters go to the Charter school and a son in law. Other than the politics played in sports by Athletic Director, this school has high marks in my experience. Both girls did great in sports and school. There is always politics in sports, football, softball and tennis.

column3: My child attended the academy. School is very large so children can easily get off track, few of the teachers will intervene to help. Guidance is overwhelmed and mostly impossible to get help, or anything that will assist the student. Some teachers care but most are just putting in their shift. The academy coordinator is the least helpful of anyone I have ever met in the VB school system. Worst part is that the students don't like her and avoid dealing with her. Wasted position as kids do need support in such a big school. Can't recommend this except for a very mature, self motivated student but of course most 15 year old aren't there yet. The focus is very much on after school activites, which may be difficult for out of zone academy students. High turnover in administration areas My boys have had an excellent experience at Landstown, the teachers always offered to stay late & help them or let them make up missed work. They care about the students! Security is excellent! The teachers & staff are excellent! So much that every year for Christmas & the end of the year, I'd buy a bunch of gift cards to different restaurants & give them to staff! My youngest is a senior this year, honor roll all 4 years!! He couldn't have done that without teachers going above & beyond! Great school! Beautiful building, great teachers and principal. Lots of different types of kids in the student body. Many AP offerings, its a Govenor's STEM school, and they have the Techonology Academy there. School is very good, second child going here. One went during football years and she did well. Second just came over from different academy and feels better education at home school and more welcome. Not seperated by academy or place and teachers are good. You have college course's and get that out of the way now-great! School has order to it and is safe and students are nice and welcoming at events. Feel nice coming to events people talk to you here. Nice school and teachers are good and classes are in order. This school is the best in the city. My first year was Awesome thanks to a guidance counselor and a great teacher. I will have the best 4 years at Landstown High! Thanks Landstown for being the best! Go eagles! Upcoming 10th grader! Great teachers and staff. new building, my daughters test scores are off the chart. Active parent involvement in the sports community. My son went to a different high school in Virginia Beach that is ranked high but I am so pleased with Landstown for my daughter. I feel she is better prepared for college having attended Landstown High. Best High school In Virginia Beach , Way better than green run. People always say landstown is for snotty rich kids but twin canal kids go to landstown as well. they have no racial problems unlike green run and my little cousin goes to green run now and gets bullied for being the only white kid in his math class. i wish he could experience the joy of school i did. Over it is bad because when I started here in 10th grade we had good administrators and they worked with the students when teachers caused issues. However those administrators are no longer here and we have assistant principals who were security guards just last year so they really don’t know what they are doing and they don’t care. So my experience started off good and has only gone down from there. To the point we are considering home school for the remainder of my senior year. There is so much room for improvement. This school as many schools these days are so focused on passing the state tests that actual teaching of information that is needed in the real world is excluded. The required classes in order to graduate are pretty standard. How about a required Financial Planning class so students understand how to balance a bank account, how credit cards can get you in trouble and how a student loan works. We need a better staff in the administration, teaching and coaching. ALL students need to feel encouraged and supported. Not just the gifted few. I’ve had 2 daughters graduate from Landstown. Both were challenge academically by their teachers and pushed to become more than just a name or number on a sheet of paper. They both had teachers that had profound impacts in their lives which they still talk about today. Both of my girls are studying medicine in college and the foundation of how to become a great student started at Landstown High School. The worst school ever in VA Beach... They do the least amount possible, completed assignments go missing to where you have to send physical pictures to show proof of completed assignments, communication with many are non-exsistent, and a multitude of other factors. I would steer away from this school completely. Go to Salem High.

column1: Wonderful staff and students alike. Both try their hardest to get successful students. Some teachers have a hard time getting to all their students within their class period though. Teachers have schedules posted on their doors so that the kids can come ask questions when they cannot during Enrichment (study hall). Tuesdays are specially for reading in Enrichment to help the kids' reading/English ability grow. Principal S is the best I've had. Very accepting and hard working school all around. Just 3 years ago we were in Watch and now we're a B rated school! I hope to see more from the future generations of students as I have seen much from just my point of view. And I am a Class of 2014 Junior. This school is a really good school but the teachers and the rest of the staff are a joke. They wanna believe the lies that come out of the students mouth and have it put in the paper instead of calling the parents or grandparents and getting both sides if the story. I use to love this school and the teachers and staff now I don't care for them. I know i'm not the only one who feel this one about the school. Sorry but whitehall yearling high school is not that great. my school that I went to is WYHS and i like all the staff of whitehall and if you dont understand the home work from the teachers miss Foster and Mrs Wright are good english teachers I also liked the principle of white hall Mr S I am a class of 2013 class of wyhs Miss Wilcox is also a good teacher she was my tutoring teacher and she helps you with the home work all the staff of Wyhs are nice staff also Mr. White the tennis coach is the best tennis coach and we are good at tennis I think fisher catholic is not a good school I won doubles against Fisher Catholic and also Mrs Hoggarth is the best Biology teacher

column3: We've had 1 son graduate with honors and win the state championship in football in his graduating year. He loved his time at Thunderbird as well as his teachers.We currently have another son going into his junior year, following in his brothers footsteps, playing football and taking AP classes. He is doing well also and loves it there. Probably one of the worst admin teams out there! Assume every student is guilty. Hands down discipline without input from parents. Will not consider parent feelings in decisions! 1. This school seems to be filled with uneducated staff members. Something was recently brought to my attention and I feel that this school should be shut down because of it's lack of (knowledge on history) . It was the best four years of my life great teachers Garbage is a pretty good way to describe it. The past 3 years have been great. I would recommend this school. As the parent of two graduates in the last five years, I would rate this school 5 stars. I graduated from here in 1981, it was average, but I see why it now consistently churns out national merit scholars and Speech and Debate among the best in the state. Ignore the 1* Star ratings...most likely from students and parents that don’t have “the right stuff” to be good students ready to contribute positively to this great COMMUNITY. Child is a recent graduate and had great teachers all 4 years. my only complaint with the school is that their "career center" is very mediocre and does little to help kids research post high school things. Very hard for kids to get one on one help, encouragement, advise on continuing their education. Our son is an honors student at Thunderbird currently. He has a 504 Plan, which his counselor does a good job helping communicate and coordinate with his teachers. In our experience, the district strives to give equal opportunities to all students. Arizona demands a lot of its educators, yet pays notoriously low wages. As a result, higher paying states annually lure the best away. TBird, however, manages to keep its teachers longer, which lends to a stable learning culture. High School is challenging no matter what school your student attends. We love that Thunderbird High School has a leadership culture where Juniors and Seniors are strongly encouraged to welcome and support the underclass students. In programs like Band and the NJROTC our experience is that Juniors and Seniors actively work to include, mentor, and train the Freshmen and Sophomores. Our experience with teachers and administrators has been excellent. Yes, there have been challenges with assignments and grades, and we have been able to work through each of those challenges with our teachers. The school has many activity options and students are strongly encouraged to participate in extracurricular activities to get the full High School experience. In our experience, Thunderbird has strong family and community support with many social media booster and parent association accounts plus a Thunderbird Parent Association.com website. We feel welcome at sport games and at student performances. We love Thunderbird High School. Go Titans!

column1: I graduated from this school in 2009. I had attended a high school in chino until 2007 then moved and attend roosevelt. It was a major difference! The programs, teachers, classes, clubs, etc. were all of much much much higher standard. I was able to be challenged and supported at the same time. I will gladly be moving back to eastvale upon my graduation from college and hope for my future children to attend their wonderful schools. This school loses several excellent teachers every year due to poor leadership and support by the principal. I am a student going onto sophmore year. I have to admit, freshman year went fast. But anyways! This school is great. But it has its flaws that need to be fixed! Drugs: if they let a drug dog loose there... The dog would be running to just about every class room. Its a huge issue and teachers completely ignore it! Teachers: they just dont care... Food: discusting! If this website let me post pictures , id post my rock solid black "healthy" french fries and my half frozen burrito. Along with my mold infested strawberries in my yogurt ERHS is a great school. All schools have their problems. It's how they handle them that can really make a difference. My teenager feels secure and supported by the staff. And that is a great feeling for a parent to see in their teenager. Eleanor Roosevelt is a great school for being only 5 years old. It has state of the art classrooms, olympic pool, tennis courts, advanced music and band program, facilities to enrich student activities and a steadily rising academic tract. With the retiring Superintendent coming from highly rated Walnut School District handing the reigns over to a capable Michael Lin, things are vastly improving for CNUSD and Eastvale schools. School ratings change constantly with student demographics from 1 year to the next and I can say the students now coming up from Middle and Elementary schools are academic achievers. I feel student success is mainly driven by the student and parents not just teachers responsibility alone. High parent participation from my own observation from school parent activities along with engaged teachers are driving high test scores. Eventually Eastvale, as the student demographics is changing will be very very academically strong like other blue ribbon districts. Looking at the elementary school achievements these children will be driving the middle and High school scores up as they are promoted. I went to this ERHS and I loved this school, the staff is friendly and very involved and students work together as one big family. Everyone is always working toward striving to get the highest in everything whether it's AP scores or the football team everything is a competition but in the best way possible. Teachers are very supportive and want to make sure you're always doing your best. Best high school experience a school can provide :) class of 2014 I am very happy with the teachers and administrators. The teachers genuinely care about their students. I hope the school continues in the same path. I can’t attest to all metrics in your Great Schools review, but I can attest to the commitment of Eastvale Leadership to the protection, wellness, and success of most their most prized possession - Eastvale students, true Defenders of children. For the first time today, I met Roosevelt’s “Defenders of Children” - Dr. Jeremy and Dr. Michael - in addition, to other Roosevelt/District Leadership. Although not your typical “Make-a-Wish” wish, (no Grammy or Heisman Trophy winner involved). Witnessing child milestones - rolling over, crawling, walking, a first word, then preschool, kindergarten, middle school and junior high, cumulating in high school graduation - is EVERYTHING to a parent, and high school graduation, I would argue, is the most meaningful of all milestones for a parent - a sense of accomplishment felt by both parent and child as no parent sits through their child’s high school graduation ceremony without reliving every childhood milestone, in a state of disbelief, “how did this happen...just yesterday...” Thank you, thank you, thank you, Dr. Jeremy, Dr. Michael, and other Roosevelt team members for creating the ultimate make a “Make-A-Wish” for my dear friend, a nursing colleague, an amazing Roosevelt parent, and Defender of cancer patients, last minute, on your day off, and Holiday. Drs. Jeremy and Michael you “Talk the Talk” and “Walk the Walk.” Again, thank you for creating happiness and beautiful memories and in the midst of deep sorrow and lastly for formally recognizing that there’s no job more important than that of a parent. School was not clean. There were lots of bugs in the classroom.
