column1: This is the fifth year at EMHS for our family. I already see our youngest being challenged as he has never been before. You hear so much about what a huge adjustment college is for many high school students, but our UNM freshman says it's business as usual. EMHS did such a great job of preparing him. I think there's a unique opportunity for each student to shine. I have been impressed with willingness of the staff at EMHS to go the extra mile for the kids. I would wholeheartedly recommend EMHS to anyone. This is a review of East Mountain High School (EMHS) in Sandia Park, New Mexico. This is simply the best college prep school in New Mexico hands-down. EMHS is a (tuition free) charter school with heavy emphasis on academics, offering several dual-credit (college/high school credit) right on campus. EMHS's science program has taken students to the Czech Republic to teach robotics to high schoolers and was recently awarded a $19,000 grant for robotics. The Speech and Debate Team is nationally ranked and has competed at Harvard and will go to Berkeley in 2014. EMHS promotes diversity in all of its classes and extra-curricular activities. Students are motivated to succeed and given the tools to do so through excellent teaching and exceptional resources. The staff and teachers are extremely high quality and the parents are heavily involved in all aspects of the school. The school has been a wonderfull help to our daughter. We love it. The small student body and student/staff ratio is a huge positive for us. We love having our daughter attend East Mountain High School because of the college focus and all the opportunities for dual-credit. We are a small community working together for the benefit of our students. This school is great because it focuses on the whole curriculum and is very concerned about each child and what they will do after high school. EMHS has lived up to its fantastic reputation with our Freshman so far this year. The teachers are very supportive and the curriculum is advanced and thorough. I have no doubts my child will enjoy the next 4 years and be completely prepared for college. 2 hours of homework almost every night, but she feels challenged for the first time in a long time. great school. best teachers ever they really know their stuff and the campus is really nice and it is a great in the community. Great charter high school that is focused on preparing students for college. Rated one of the best schools in NM due to demonstrated student outcomes, community involvement and family commitment. Recent visits from NM PED to learn more about how this school has beat the odds by delivering a high quality education to students while receiving less money per student than APS schools. The school puts its money where its goals are and spends money on the things that matter most. Very basic buildings, nothing fancy or frills- simply focus on education and the extra cirricular activities that drive results. I have two kids (senior and a junior) that attend this school- they love it and would not change if asked to do so. We are in the college search process with our senior and feel he is very well prepared to master college. I am very pleased to have my child attend East Mountain School. I love the fact that it is a small school. The teachers are all very caring and proactive with any concerns that may arise. I also like the fact that there is plenty of opportunity for tutoring. There is also a high expectation for every child to succeed. I homeschooled my students before we found this high school. Academics is promoted here and there are a lot of activities. I especially like the golf team that gets to practice at Paako! I also like the speech and debate team because they have a great team. I'm happy with almost every part of this high school. I wouldn't sent my kids to Manzano. EMHS is a college prep school with 4 classes per semester. The students have an Advocacy period every day where they can ask their Advocate questions about anything. The Advocacy time is also constructively being used this year to study for the PSAT and ACT. I love that they're doing that! Students are constantly being given information about colleges that are presenting information sessions in the region. "College" is in the air at EMHS, which is why I send my student there! This is the answer to high school woes. The school has so many activities, interesting classes, and great teachers that our student has been very happy there. The school guidance counselors really care about the kids' emotional and physical safety. Every student is assigned an advocate their freshman year who stays with the student throughout the rest of high school. The students can ask this advocate ANYTHING and she will answer. During "Advocacy" every day, the students meet with their advocate. Prior to the PSAT and ACT, the time was used to study for the tests. Loved that! Also, we love the 4 class block system that most colleges use. Since this is a college prep high school, all college information is given out constantly. From FAFSA to visiting colleges every angle is covered. I also like that the school embraces diversity. Gay and lesbian students can feel at home here. Also, students of all races and religions are accepted. NO bullying is tolerated; as soon as a student reports something amiss it is taken care of. This is very important to our family. We want our children to be NICE people, even in high school! My daughter is a freshman this year and she truly enjoys going to school at East Mountain High! I love the fact that there are smaller classes, the teachers are active in what the kids do, and the small community feel overall of the area is fantastic! We are very pleased with E.Mountain HS and are so thankful that our daughter made the lottery and was able to attend the school! My daughter entered this school in her senior year, and is having a very good experience. Her teachers are kind and dedicated, the assistant Principal, Ms. Millea is a wonder ... We recommend this school. Excellent academically. There are wonderful connections between the teachers and the students, and every staff member makes us feel at home. I love this school because we are very open-minded, we give back to the community, and we are a family. I couldn't be more impressed with the high level of rigor provided at EMHS, and the positive environment provided by the volleyball coaching staff. I am so happy we made the choice to send our daughter to EMHS. She is so happy here. We have two very different children. This school is smaller, but there are more electives then they can all take. They are also able to participate in HS athletics, but not have it dominate their lives. Education and self reliance is stressed at this school. When things come up, they are easy to work with and certainly put the student first! This school did not prepare me at all for my future and many of the teachers and well as the principle were very unprofessional.

column3: We have two kids attending Mountain Pointe and are so happy with EVERY aspect of the school. Our son has been part of three sports programs. Each sport had wonderful, challenging coaches, who were tough enough and uplifting enought to make our son's experiences just what parents would hope for from high school sports. Our daughter has been in one sport and continues to be thrilled w/the coaches and program. Lots of parent support and very little drama in both kids' sport programs. The coaches just don't allow it. Their teachers amaze us -- each and every one has good experience in and out of the classroom share w/the students. We feel like school is fair and love seeing rules being enforced, (even when our kids have been swept, dress coded, and phones taken away). We so appreciate the "no tolerance" policy. Mountain Pointe is a fabulous, well-rounded school! This is an AMAZING school! For all the parents out there tell your child or children to get involved. It makes things a whole lot easier and you meet a lot of new and fabulous people. Never be afraid, it only makes it worse! But other than that Mountain Pointe is the school to be at! As a Mountain Pointe Alumni of 2009, I can honestly say that the school itself is a joke. While many lifelong memories were made here that I will cherish for forever, these memories have not helped or prepared me for the real world. The teachers are generally funny, fun, and engaging, however they do not live to their title of "teachers" as many do not actually teach. Rather the Mountain Pointe philosophy of teaching is to sit at your desk while you students watch a video that barely pertains to the subject matter at hand. There are many success stories of students out of this school going to prestigious and great universities, however the sad truth is that for the most part the administration turns a blind eye to all students who are not part of the principal's son and daughter's friend groups. Furthermore most teachers do not care about the students and would turn a blind eye to them in their time of need. This school is an over crowded mess, and needs help. only send your child here if you do not care about their future We love Mountain Pointe! We actually live in Desert Vista's district, but have chosen to send our kids to MP. It is more diversified, the teachers and staff are wonderful, the courses they offer are exceptional. Principal Kipper has truly turned this into an A+ school! My observations of Mountain Pointe High School (daughter graduated May 2011) are that MPHS is a very special place where the faculty/staff are really working towards the success of each student in school and their future. Mountain Pointe's dedicated teachers, helpful staff, involved Principal = GREAT school! The "Pride's Peak" program for the gifted students is excellent --- and is enhanced further (personal recommendation) by student participation in MPHS Academic Decathlon resulting in complete academics-social/student-faculty involvement (with accompanying family (Booster Club) support). The Foreign Language, and Science departments at Mountain Pointe High School are especially outstanding! Very motivated and involved faculty members who have a deep interest and knowledge of their field. Wonderful Visual Arts program. What has impressed me the most about MPHS is how the faculty and staff truly care and are looking to help each student succeed. Mountain Pointe High School seems to be a place that an individual can find a group of friends and a mentor(s) with whom they can relate to help them grow and flourish in school and life. My daughter attends MPHS. She is now a senior & developed SO MUCH P R I D E! I really respect Mr. Kipper's communication w/ parents. We are ALWAYS in the loop. The ongoing communication is excellent and I am VERY thankful of the safety. Each school has an occassional bad apple that brings drugs or alcohol to school, BUT MP does NOT take this lightly and responds VERY quickly to each situation. My daughter is very safe at MP. She s involved in many clubs (100 s MP offers) which has increased her self esteem and confidence. I cannot say enough about MP. We tried to visit Desert Vista when deciding a school for her, but had a terrible time communicating with staff or anyone returning our phone calls. They gave us a TA for the tour, but communication with an adult was impossible. My son is starting this year as a freshman and working with the freshman football team. They have been EXCELLENT with him and we are confident he will have the awesome journey my daughter experienced. THERE S A REASON MOUNTAIN POINTE S RATINGS ARE SO HIGH. Thank you MPHS and keep up the EXCELLENT work! My son just began his freshman year here at MPHS. From the beginning the staff and upperclassmen have been awesome! Their two day Freshman boot camp was a huge plus in my son's early success in transitioning to this level. Wish we had that back when I was starting high school! Mr. Kipper is great at communicating school needs, events and expectations and I was thoroughly impressed with his prompt reply to emails. Two thumbs up!!! The school has seriously gone down hill. I dont know what it is my oldest graduated this year and i have another daughter that is a freshman and ill i hear about are fights and disruptive students in class. Its sad because this used to be a nice school. I am a graduate of Mountain Pointe, and I have nothing but good things to say about it. I moved from Northeast Ohio as a sophomore, and was immediately embraced by my fellow students. My experience was extremely positive, and l have nothing but fond memories. As far as I am concerned, I will always be a member of the pride!! I didn't have the a great high school experience. It's mostly my own doing. I was shy and lacked self confidence. I was intimated by the rich popular kids. The nerds didn't like me either. I didn't fit in. I was a loner. The education was good. I learned things. I went to a good private university in the east. Learned how to be social. Got a doctorate. I think the environment has a lot to do with how successful a person can be. If I am uncomfortable in a class because I had no friends in it. Why wasn't I allowed to switch into a different class? If the few friends I have are in a different lunch period, why can't I switch lunch periods? But would things have mattered at the end? I still became a doctor despite the lack of a social life in high school. I missed out on the memories. Regarding 2014-2015 AZ Merit test scores published here, MP was one of the only schools statewide to give the new pilot test electronically and the school did not have the network infrastructure to support the # of students taking the test at the same time. Many of the students tests timed out, computers crashed, etc. The district and the state dept of education indicated it was a pilot year and scores would not be published so not to worry about it. Obviously that was not the case - as the scores are published here. Mountain pointe is not your cookie cutter school. The diversity of the students and the diversity of the classes offered there create an environment that will prepare kids for real life. People choose to send their kids there not because we have to but because they want to. great school i love it everyone is so kind and all the student are so kind to one another This is likely one of the most ethnically and racially diverse schools in the nation. The campus is nice and the teachers are phenomenal. Aside from that, it is vital for your child (or your own self; if you are a student, of course) to get involved with as many clubs, organizations, sports and student unions as possible. As a recently graduated senior, a lot of my peers regret not getting involved enough through the years. High School is the last life you get before the real world, so make the most of it! lol olo l ol o lol l o l o l ol o l o My children attended this school and had I been aware of what my children were being taught and about how badly they were being treated by the teachers and other students I would have them pulled immediately.

column3: Okay here's the deal. I am a Junior at Whitmer, and I have enjoyed every year I've had in attendance (all three). I've gone to both Maumee and Washington Junior Highs (Washington local) and I've found that here, in this district, the socially diversity is so much more extensive than any other district I've been to. There is literally a place for every one to fit in and not be left out. Teachers treat you like young adults (as long as you act like one) and I've personally found that even in classes I'm uninterested in, I've become good friend's with the teachers, they enjoy what they do. In my freshman year, I found myself just going through the motions of high school without much involvement rather than education (don't do sports or extracurriculars) that is until joining welding sophomore year where I found my family that I had wanted all along. Saying that Whitmer is focused on athletics is absurd. We are so much more. We don't only rise in the fall, we are welders, automotive and computer technicians, we are culinary scholars and economically aware, college prepared, spirit proud, maize & blue sporting students, friends, family, club members and industrialists. We are Whitmer. Lots of different classes, many extracurricular activities and many ways to earn college credit through high school courses. I look forward to my children attending Whitmer as I did when I was a high school student. I spent my entire academic career in Washington Local and not only felt prepared academically for my future, I continue to feel a sense of community years later. Whitmer provided the depth and diversity to help make me successful today. Loved my high school experience at whitmer! The best piece of advice I can give, is get involved because it is well worth it! Drained all joy out of my life and left me depressed with no hope for the future. I love Whitmer! I am very proud to be a family of Panthers! I don't even know where to start. The problem is the district, the superintendent, and the board primarily. There is so much disorganization administratively. They are dishonest and do a lot of hiding and making excuses. The special education department is incredibly poor. Their primary goal appears to be paying students through whether they are ready or not. Instead of taking the time to teach a child with behavior issues to write, they just have an aid do the writing for them, for instance. When my son failed a class, they did not require him to do any sort of summer school. He graduated, and feels completely incapable of any success.How they handled the pandemic has been beyond disappointment. My child contacted the virus at school. When I contacted them, they didn't even answer my numerous emails for 2 weeks. After that, they completely failed to contact any of the people my child was in contact with. Though I love many of the teachers, the administration and the corrupt board over shadow any of the positive things the teachers bring. Perhaps it is a Toledo thing. As, the entire city is a terrible mess of a place to live. Move to a suburb and go to a better district. I would do a lot of things to avoid coming here ever again. Made my anxiety and depression worse. Other students will harass you. The bathrooms could be cleaner. Some of these teachers don't do enough teaching and just whip piles and piles of work onto you. At lunch they make you pay for the good stuff when some schools give out the same type of stuff for free. Other than that though the food can be really good sometimes, though they are stingy with the portions of food you get. Some teachers only give you a certain amount of passes for you to leave and go to the restroom each quarter, that's weird and a little bit too controlling. Some teachers put grades as a zero BEFORE its due. The gym teacher makes us walk around the gym as sports are going on around us at the same time, which causes people to get smacked with a ball, sometimes he will let us walk in the hallway instead but mostly we walk in the gym. People will try to steal from you like stealing pins off of backpacks, or the time someone snatched the pencil out of my backpack pocket. This school has caused me and a whole lot of others too cry inside and outside of this school time and time again. The teachers (most of them) are really annoying and don't try hard enough to make learning fun or entertaining. Some people here are really really dirty (i know certain peoples situations aren't the best I get that sorry if you have something going on at home) but its really bad sometimes. One time a random dog broke into the school running around the halls and onto other floors (I loved the dog though they were so cute and friendly) like i usually only have fun in this school when something not caused by the school happens. Gum is everywhere outside. We stare at a screen all day for everything, i am now near sighted because of technology (my phone didn't help but school making us look at smart boards or computers all day didn't help either) and will have to go to the doctor to ask about whats wrong with my eyes and if i need glasses some time this year. If you are already mentally ill this school will most likely make your mental health worse like it did to mine and many others I know. Overall its a below okay school but its probably better than the other schools in the area, but that's not saying much. Anime club is fun at least. And if you are antisocial and considered weird like me then you can probably find some good friends (a lot of people here toxic though so be careful) First of all I want to say “WLS4kids” is very misleading and a flat out lie. They are NOT for the kids. I cannot speak for the teachers. I will say that my son really enjoyed his short 5 weeks at Whitmer. He was 5 weeks into his Freshman year when the school unenrolled him without verbally speaking to me or reaching out to me at the very least to see if there was a reasonable explanation to why they were told that we do not live at the address when they came out to do a residence check. They had my phone number, why not call me, the mother to see if there was an error and instead of going to 3517 the went to 3511 because the 7 looked like a 1. So they handled the situation like all others. Unenroll the student right away. As soon as they were told there is nobody by that name that lives here they went back to the administration building started the paperwork But did not send home one letter with my son indicating there was a question about our residence and asking me to correct it. They cannot possibly care about the kids after seeing how they handled our situation. And to top it off the school has open enrollment and below average state testing scores so why would anyone need or even want to give a wrong address so their child can attend this school? If I didn’t live in district I woulda have just registered him and filled out the open enrollment form . I am so disappointed with the way they handled our situation when it was all just a typo mistake. Then the process to re enroll him required a ridiculous amount of extra documentation to prove our residence. Do they think they are the Harvard of Toledo? It’s obvious they have a very high opinion of themselves. I don’t know how with the recent results of State Testing.

column1: St. Anthony's is a wonderful school. Their academics and sports are great. The best part is the discipline. Although I felt it was too harsh as a student there, I know now it was the best for us. It kept us in line and concentrating on what was important. Only now I appreciate it even more being that I work in a public school in Brooklyn! The tuition is high but well worth it. Saint Anthony's high school is overrated. The academic programs available are not nearly as diverse as most of the public high schools on long island. As an alumni of St. Anthony's, I saw the schools reputation diminish to an extent while tuition continued to rise. Overall a great school where the students can get involved in many extracurricular activities. Most teachers take a personal interest in the students and programs. Saint Anthony s has a very good reputation with colleges and will open doors to quality Universities. I used to go to this school. I liked it sometimes and hated it at other times. Although public school can be a drag sometimes, the academics are far more better in all aspects. You're being surrounded with real world situations by attending public school. St. Anthony's isn't reality. Definitely reconsider placing your child here if you actually want them to succeed academically. $8,000 a year is way too much for a school that really doesn't challenge you when it comes to schoolwork. After 4 years, you would've spent $32,000 on high school when you easily can just send your child to public school, SAVE $32,000 and put that towards a much better college that'll probably accept you quicker than if you went to St. Anthony's because your grades would've been 10x better. My 2nd child just graduated from St Anthony's after spending his freshman year in public school and then transferring. It was the best decision he ever made according to him. He was definitely challenged academically taking 6 AP courses in his senior year and getting some of those credits transferred upon his acceptance to Notre Dame. I don't believe he would have been accepted to Notre Dame had he remained in public school....but that's just my opinion! I also believe the money spent was well worth it. I have 4 children - 2 of whom attended public school and 2 attended St Anthony's. If I could do it again, all of them would have been at St Anthony's. You can't put a price and the things learned there such as respect and discipline. I also liked the aspect of added religion in the program. The only downside with St Anthony's is the overcrowding. There are just too many students in the building but Brother Gary runs an awesome building nonetheless. Everythign they do is very organized. I would definitely recommend the school to anyone moving to the area or presently here and not happy with their public school system. My son has completed his first year at St. Anthony's high school and we are thrilled. The academic program is challenging and top notch. The teachers and administrators are supportive, helpful and always willing to go the extra mile for their students. The character of the student is vital. Athletic program is one of the best in the state! I would highly recommend st. Anthony's to any parent who truly values a solid academic and spiritual education. I graduated St. Anthony's in 2012 and I absolutely loved the school. Had a great time, I actively participated in many clubs and activities, and I got into many top notch colleges. I highly recommend this school, and everyone I know loved their 4 years there. Truly a fantastic education! It's an amazing school. There's really nothing else to say. The love you feel as soon as you walk in the door is something you will never feel at any other school. The brothers are phenomenal; especially Brother Gary. He is one of the most loving, accepting, and understanding men I have ever had the privilege to meet. Everyone is so thrilled with this school. Im in my 2nd year of going to st anthonys high school, and some of the teachers, dont even teach. I came to this school thinking it will be an amazing opportunity to learn, but the teachers, and the students there are just not the kind of school i want to go to. They always talk about how they have the greatest security, but kids go around smoking, doing drugs and doing other things that shouldnt be allowed in public, especially in a private school. Im seriously thinking about changing schools next year. Here at St. Anthony's our children's minds were nurtured spiritually .... As well as encouraging service and commitment to our beliefs as Catholics . St Anthony's high school has prepared my three daughters for their college education academically by teaching them to be an independent learner, to crave knowledge , be accountable for their education and most of all to share their knowledge with others . The best review is when your child is a freshman in college and they call to tell you "thank you Mom and Dad for encouraging me go to St. Anthony's I am so prepared for college !!" Bad school teachers are crazy not certified any person can go an teach there! Also kids behavior is crazy the school doesn't teach them respect for other is just about money ... You better give brother Principal a big chunk of money otherwise you are not their favorite Not as good as I hoped. Anything that affects a student's grade should be put in writing, but that was not the case, and administration did nothing to help. The parents who recommended this school to me had children who were extremely bright, and would've succeeded anywhere. When my kids need extra help, I must drive them early in the morning, as none is available during or after school. My kids rarely get math tests returned, presumably because the school re-uses the same tests. We don't know if the grades are accurate, or what to improve on. We also find that while their school grades are excellent, their standardized tests scores are not. I'm only keeping my kids there because they've made a lot of friends, not because I'm thrilled with the school.

column3: I was a student at Santa Teresa High School. I graduated in 2007 and I do not believe that STHS prepared most of its students for a college education or for the workforce. I am currently a college student. I was a top ten percent student. I took pre-calculus, received an "A" in the course and when I joined the university I am currently attending I placed into pre-calculus. I should have placed into calculus since I had already taken pre-calculus. Why did I receive an "A" in the high school but wasn't able to pass the test at the university? Take into mind too that this was an honors class. The regular math classes were a lot worse. Many of the friends that I had that were taking Algebra two said that some of the teachers made the tests real easy and that the the teacher didn't put effort into teaching them. The band program was real good when I was there, but I don't know about now since they have a new band teacher. There were some teachers that really cared about students like some of the science teachers I had. My pre calulus teacher seemed like he cared too, but a lot of the kids were not prepared for the material. STHS needs a lot more college preparation for kids. I go to this school the level of academics is the best in the district our current report card delivered after state testing was a b the faculty thought this was great but not good enough they laucned a campaign every teacher in school has badges tht say Be the chAnge meaning change from a B to an A. The teachers are all amazing thy do not let any one do the bare minumum. I can't even begin to tell you how disappointed I am in our school district. Where to begin... we moved here thinking our children would be in a district that was rated higher than average. Well not so much. The teachers barely speak English, the principal said... Your kids will know they are different here.... REALLY?? Extracurricular activites well needless to say... They do not exist here. This has been the worst experience in a school I could have imagined. To top it off the school is so poor, that they are now charging the kids a dollar to see the nurse. You have to be kidding me?? This school district is absurd. We have tried to speak with the superintendent. Well he has been too busy to call us back the 4 times we have called. If I was you, I would never think of sending your kids to school here. Move away... That is what we are doing. Selling the house and moving to a district that has some motivation for children. Besides horrible leadership and horrible teachers; this school should be shut down!!!! This will not let you give less than one star. Sad I know, not even one star worthy. This scool is awwsum! I learned so much from this scool! The akademmics are top-knotch! I wennt to this scool and I learned soo much, especcally in englich and gramar. Am so todally sending my children to this scool! Am proud to bee a Santa Teresa gratuade! Blakk, Wite, Loyal forrever! As a student of Santa Teresa High School I find this school to be improving each and every year: having and seeing older siblings graduate from here. The teachers here do an exceptional job and forging bonds with their students. Through this bond you do receive individualized help from your teachers. The teachers don't just view you as another student like some schools do. One of my teachers explained it to us the best, "We are an investment in their future" that is why they care that we receive the best quality and education out there. Fights and bullying at a minimum. SAT and ACT scores improve each year, as well does our state test performance. The fallacies on the nurses charging a dollar and our own teachers being illiterate in English, bemuses me because there is no merit to these statements. STHS is a terrific school striving towards higher standards yearly.

Phoenix has had to endure many staff and curriculum cuts. With out the wonderful community surrounding this school, there would be further unwanted cuts to school activities.

column3: I had three children go to this school from 9th to 12th. Two have graduated so far. I feel that for the most part it has been a good experience. I agree with most that has been said good on here, but also agree with the one negative. That is favoritism, especially in band-choir-and sports. All three of my children have talents that they pursued, but students with a certain name do tend to land in parts regardless of talent. One student could not block for nothing (well known family), but never got pulled from the game---ever. One in Madrigals (my son was in this too) who absolutely could not sing or dance. This is pretty typical but sad. Other than that...great school. Concerning the band program, I have seen no instances of favoritism in my four years of marching band and Wind Ensemble. For example, my friend didn't make marching band her freshman year and remained in concert band the entire year, but by her junior year she was sitting first chair in Wind Ensemble, the best band in the school. DeVault, the band director, provides equal opportunities that every band student is able to utilize. Further, the marching band audition process is necessary to the well-being of the band. The marching band is comprised of 170 students, and through a rigorous rehearsal schedule we are able to produce a quality half-time show every year. In fact, in the 2013 season we received straight Superior ratings at the K-State festival and we were named Grand Champions of the Neewollah Marching Festival in Independence. The band program has taught me a lot about myself, given me the opportunity to make new friends, and it has by far been the best experience I have had at this school since my freshman year. Please do not get discouraged by some of the accusations in these reviews; I definitely would recommend joining the band to anyone. From the time I enrolled my child in the Derby school district in 6th grade, neither him and I were never accepted. Once those teachers put a “label” on a child, it sticks with him/her throughout the rest of their years in the Derby school district. some of the teachers do an excellent job and really care, others, so so. administration is terrible, they will not work with parents or students. if you are a football fan, then this will work for you, that is where all the attention ( and money) goes. school is too large, but as another viewer wrote, this will never change because that could/would affect the strength of the football team. there is a lot of bullying, with little to no repercussions, except for the victim. for the size of the school and the kind of community ( derby is a great town to live in), the high school only has a 90% graduation rate, this is very alarming and the school nor the school board seem to care any or do anything about those numbers

column1: Great school in a nice community. Pre-K through 12th grade are on the same campus along with great sports and recreation areas. It's nice to have everything in the same place and such a connected community. Administration stands idly by while watching certain students get bullied, while others are favorited.

column1: I am a student at King High school, and I must say it is not full of violence, but of course it's gonna have a fight or two. I had a choice to leave King but I said no I want to go back, I been there since I was in the 9th grade and I will be a Junior this September I couldn't leave the school that I know and I grew to love. No it's not the best school, and so what ! People think they know my school because they heard this they heard that , yeah king was a mess along time ago, but I think it's fine and that it is safe. King is a beautiful school, it makes me feels like home when I walk down the halls looking at the beautiful morals. King Has Loving, Caring teachers who wants to educate us. Some of my favorite teachers got laid off and I am not happy about that but I know I will meet new teachers in September that I will grow to love . I just wanted to let people know that my school isn't bad it's a good normal school that need a little push and support! column3: Timber Creek High School is excellent, my son study in this school and I happy .This is beautiful. This school is great! My younger son is currently studying here as a Sophomore and the classes are great! The electives are great, the AP classes are excellent, and the many extra-curricular activities are incredible! My only concern is the Band on how they treat the students there. My oldest son used to be in the Band and let me just say that he was a bit exhausted at how hard he worked to earn the highest band last year. They kept him in the lowest band for 4 years straight. This got him a bit depressed in which it led to his confidence and self-esteem to drop. I guess it was a bit of a waste to pay for the uniforms for those four straight years. I don't know what they do to manage the bands there but I don't suggest it as an arts elective. In fact, I am happy to join my daughter to this school with high capabilities, as well as my daughter a happy existence in this school and to the good handle thanks to Timber Creek School As a former student of TCHS! I will say that it was an awesome experience for me. The campus is clean! The teachers are very involved in the student's academic progress. I left TCHS forming wonderful friendships with my teachers and guidance counselor. I still often visit that school, just to say hello to some of my former teachers. I can't say how thankful and privileged I am to have attended TCHS! Even though it has been a few years since I graduated! I still reflect very fondly on thy school for such wonderful memories. I would recommend this school to anyone who just moved and is new to the area. If you want your kids to get a wonderful education, TCHS, is your school! I go to this school, and let me tell you it's amazing the teachers get really involve with the students to get the best of them. you have plenty of classes and extra-curriculum activities. this is also a 'A' school again this year so if you are thinking about moving near this school, don't think it twice and register. I am currently a Parent at Timber Creek High School. The hallways at the high school can get crowded because of the enormous amounts of students in the school. However, I believe that all departments in the school are excellent. My Son is in AP classes and have been since freshmen year and I am very confident and satisfied with the teachers i have had. My daughter Sara graduated from TCHS in 2011. I consider our TCHS a magnificent high school with terrific teachers, support staff and an administration to match. TCHS provides students with outstanding academic programs and successfully maintains a strong sense of pride and school spirit. I love the students, the parents and I am so proud of the community involvement. TCHS rocks! We relocated from CT in the summer of 2013 and I have two children at this school. I was very concerned about what I had heard about schools in FL vs CT. I am happy to say that both my children are being challenged in honors and AP classes and doing well. The teachers are extremely involved with the kids and the whole experience has been positive. TCHS was a great choice and my kids are benefitting from a great staff and facility. I am in freshman year. I started brand new to this school and I am so thankful to have come here. Everyone welcomed me so well. I tryed out for all the sports teams and made it in the cheer team. My cheer coach is so sweet and kind and knows what she's doing. All my teachers (I'm advanced) all help me to graduate well and encourage me to learn more. If I weren't in this school I wouldn't be so happy. Everyone is so friendly welcoming and respectful. There's never fights or bullying. Recommend this school to anyone. Although we have lots of students the administration team works hard to please everyone and also I forgot to mention everything is brand new bathrooms,desks,computers,boards etc. if this could be college, I'd stay here forever! Also I love the scholarship opportunities. I am qualified for a $50,000 scholarship just by doing well in school. My successfullife ahead of me is on progress. So thankful for this school definetly recommend every aspect of it!!!! TCH is an amazing school! The technology, career planning, and classroom settings are extremely advanced. It can be as broad or as specific to your child's future career choice. We are impressed by the level of teaching, the amazing teachers and administrative team, the large number of clubs available, and overall opportunities offered. Take a moment to watch the school video. We feel blessed that our children are and will be attending this school. Some may view the enormous size of the school as being threatening; however, we view it as a great preparation for their future university years. We feel blessed that our children attend this amazing school. The teachers and administrators are very involved and attentive. The large number of career opportunities offered is incredible: Vet Assistant, Pre Law, Business, Advanced Computer and Graphics, Pre Med, Advanced Theater, etc. I agree with the reviewer who stated one should watch the TCHS video to see all of the opportunities that are offered to the children. The extra curricular activities are also very organized and extensive. The Honors, AP, and Dual Enrollment classes prepare the students for college and sets them on the right career path. We could not ask for a better school! This school has allowed my daughter to be horribly bullied and not only have they not done anything about it they actually revictimized my daughter. It is a very misguided school in how they handled students interactions. Counselors should be able to see through bullies but instead they side with them. If you have a child who is not accustomed to a bullying environment better not to allow them to be subjected to a school like this. Competition should be with the self but in schools like this there is inappropriate misguided ambition to the point of running over the person inside. It's very sad but best to avoid this school if you have a child who has not been exposed to these kind of children or administrators. Great staff and teachers, however more balance is needed when teaching anything political. Most of the teachers are clearly on the left and the opinions they give is slanted. Teachers and staff should not be biased or give thier own political opinions. Students should make his or her own decision on what party they affiliate with. Let's be fair... There are plenty of conservatives that go to the school as well and don't need negative or biased opinions when in class. Very happy we send our kids to such a great school. My kids are given every tool they need to succeed the rest is up to them The worst ever of all Orange county schools. There are skilled teachers and teachers lacking skills. Engaging teachers and boring teachers. TCHS works to hire teachers in a timely way when needed but it doesn't always happen. OCPS is a big district and there is lots of red tape to work around so nothing happens fast. We enjoyed clubs and sports and academics at TCHS. The athletics at this school are not run with the kids in mind. There are daddy coaches and some how their entire 9th grade travel ball team made the baseball team!! They even beat out 10th graders!! The kids even know that this isn’t fair but nothing is done about it! It is not fair and every kid should be treated fairly no matter who they are! Shame on Timber Creek for allowing this.

column1: Just transferred here and this is my impression; Do not.go here. Way too hard and difficult. Everyone that goes here has a very unflattiering appearance too. So if your a student looking for love, turn the other way. Great school. The classes are easy yet challenging, the teachers (most of them) work with you, all the coaches keep their players in line and transform them into this great being. Definitley attend and join the panther family. I'm sad I have to leave here and I have on =e more year but definitley go. Teachers are so kind & helping with any problem. Offers 1 on 1 help whenever needed. I think it was a good school, got a scholarship to UT so yeah it's good Great school I loved it here during my four years. It's such a small school and that makes it feel more like a community in contrast to Kingwood High. The classes are rigorous and the students are competitive in terms of class rank. You'll see this in the AP classes especially but this school will prepare you for college if you don't fail.

column3: Very satisfied with the education at MRHS. Excellent, caring staff members, nice school community - numerous activities & sports teams. I'd recommend this school to anyone. Great School! Students are nice kids. Staff seems caring and friendly. Wish the school started a little later in the morning as 7:15 is too early to get teenagers to school, but I guess you can't have everything. I sub in the school on occasion and this district is a nice place to work. Most of the children are very nice. It would be nice if they had a golf teem since non teem sorts are great for children with Autism. The sports and programs they do have all seem to be good. This school seems to be under rated since I have read higher test scores and college readiness higher in reports in the Asbury Park Press.

column1: I agree with the parent on 3/7/12. My daughter knew of the fight. It make me made these girls did not get suspended. My daughter is threatened with a detention for wearing a non uniform,Cor Jesu sweatshirt in her chilly room. She is a high honors student, ACT Score 35, varsity athletic, member of clubs & has many friends. We sent her there so she would be in a academically challenged environment. Alumni kids are catered to, girls are admitted without any consideration to the kind of heart they have or morals, 50% of the girls are socially awkward creating a frustating experences for the more rounded kids, administraion does nothing to teachers that are failing to teach, too many classroom assignments are to be done in a group and usually one person has to carry the weight of the group (very unfair since my daughter cares about her grades). They worry too much about school uniforms instead of having the girls confortable to learn. The plus side: Love the office staff, the tradition, the all girl environment, love that it teaches organization skills, love the school building, love the juke box in the cafe,. I wish the school did better screening of students and teachers. To the parent who wrote on 3/7. I went to CJA and I absolutely loved it. I was a multi-sport varsity athlete and honors student. I wasn't an "alumni kid" and I felt like I was treated the exact same as the girls who were. I don't see anything wrong with group work. In fact when she gets into college she is going to have a lot of group work, and even in the professional world you have to learn how to delegate work and how to get a long with others. I don't see how 50% of the girls being socially awkward has any affect on your daughter's experience. No matter what school you go to, there are going to be girls that are different than your daughter, that's part of life. I graduated 10 years ago and looking back those "socially awkward girls" are some of the most fun, interesting, successful people. As far as the uniform-All private schools have uniform rules. I was one of those students always pushing the envelope with what sweatshirt or undershirt I wore (sure I got detentions), but really that is why they give you choices of sweaters you CAN wear. It is just a foundation for rules. Their rules are a lot more lax now than 10 yrs ago too. LOVE CJ AND WOULDN'T CHANGE IT! You will not find a school better than Cor Jesu Academy. As a graduated student, I wouldn't trade my four years there for anything. So many of my best memories happened in the halls of CJ. Not only did I make friendships that I know will last a lifetime, but I also established great relationships with teachers who I still keep in touch with. Cor Jesu is more than just a school. It really is a family. I feel so lucky to say that I loved everything about my high school experience. I woke up every morning looking forward to going to school. I don't think many people can say that. I was undoubtedly challenged to grow both academically and spiritually, and I am proud of who I am today because of it. Amazing school. Many people can give out bad review to this school for the extremely competitive acedemics and stress load, but honestly, it isnt bad. Cor jesu is known for its difficult acedemics and its not something the school hides. I love this place so much. The food, the staff, the enviroment and education is amazing.

column3: I am a River Road alumni and that school is literally the worst in the area. Most of the teachers are coaches who don't care about any kids unless their on their sports team. And if you want to be in any other extra cirricular activities, they expect you to pay for every little thing because all the schools money goes to their sports teams. The people in the area are either rich farm kids or kids living below the poverty line. The teachers choose favorites and will easily ignore students that are not excelling in National Honor Society, which by the way, they are so desperate for members they let anyone in. Also, the school allows racism to happen. Because a lot of kids are white in the region, they don't care if the kids yell racial slurs or even taunt others kids about their races. Another thing, their academic programs are so bad that students in River Road's National Honor Society don't qualify for Amarillo High School or really any other honor society because the programs are so ill constructed. Any student graduating from this high school is being cheated a real education. Please, if you love your child, do not send them to this school. River Road High School and River Road ISD is the best in the Area. The teacher and administrators care deeply about every student and work very hard to ensure they receive the best education possible. It is east to cast stones when you have parents who expect the schools to raise their children but despite what the teachers, principals and staff have to deal with, they do a fantastic job. I would not have my kids in any other district. We have been very pleased with our childrens education and will recommend River Road to anyone looking for a quality education for their kids. Thank you River Road! Worst school I have ever been to and I have been to lots of schools...The teachers rarely teach and when they do they do it very poorly! Do not send your kids to this school worsr school ever!!!! I graduated from River Road ISD & was involved with many extra-curricular activities. I had several friends, although I wasn t classified as popular. I enjoyed my classes & several teachers went the extra mile helping when we didn t understand. I wanted my children to have the same experience with caring teachers & admin, hence why we moved back to RRISD. My son went from an A-B student to a D-F student. I m highly disappointed with the service (or lack therefore) for my child. I'm a very involved parent & was told to back off- let the school handle it . We were hopeful, when we enrolled him, due to small classes & the small town feel; promised an individualized curriculum & caring environment. Our son has special needs & we feel defeated where education is involved, instead of well informed. Meeting after meeting has been rescheduled, most teachers don t have tutorials, & papers can t be corrected. Teachers have favorites & the other students tend to be ignored. This is not a district that wants every child to be successful; this is a district that mainly cares about looking good on paper. Bottom line, the quality of this school has deteriorated since I attended. With the introduction of the new principle, Mr Chevy, the school has gone downhill fast. When a student who had a child requested, and had previously been approved for, a 2 hour class day to go home to her baby, he told her that she would have to be a full time student until 5 weeks so he could get the money for the school with her as a full time student. The staff is horrible. The only things this school cares about is money and looking good on paper.

column1: Not enough text books to take home to study, three class in the 12th grade. i am currently a student at ELHS, i'm glad i'm a somebody since i play sports. that is not true, we would be more than happy to have other people join our sports teams, it's the same few people who play every sport. maybe your child is just to lazy to play anything.. you don't come to tryouts.. you don't know how they do there. you do not have to pay $600 dollars to play football.

I'm sorry but standards should be higher for people that have to educate our youth. Understanding, patience and BRAINS are a must. But as I said it's only the beggining of the year and I havent even met the teachers yet. Hopefully the person my son actually has to deal with has some manners. If you want your kids to do anything other than the aforementioned two, send them to Cypress, Kennedy, Western, hope he can get admitted to Oxford, pay for Servite or Rosary, or homeschool. I mean outside those schools, the rest of the district is complete garbage. its a good school people who wanna learn.....learn. people who dont well thats their own fault Teachers, staff members and students do not tolerate bully. People speck up for the silence and clubs are formed for students who have a hard time making friends. They have free after school tutoring. great school but struggling on finances on most basic materials. seems neglected by district leaders. Loara is amazing. I am currently a student and have had incredible support. My sister went through Loara and just finishing her undergrad at Chapman University and My brother went to UCI and is now a pharmacist. I plan to go to UC Santa Cruz with a double major in Fine Art and Business. Loara prepared all of us and gave us a lifetime of memories. You will find good and bad teachers at every school. My cousin went to Oxford and was stressed all the years he was there. Went to UCI with my brother and my brother is more successful. You get out of high school what you put into it. Love it I was a student 2 years ago and it’s was amazing Aldo the top comment I agree with because it’s not getting as much students as it used to.but anything other it’s great because i recently passed by and I saw that they repainted the sign and it’s getting better. My son is a sophomore at Loara. He is in sports, clubs and does well in his classes. He have three cousins that recently graduated from Loara and all did well and are currently at different UC colleges that they got into because of the schools relationships with those colleges. Loara has been amazing for my son and our family.

column3: My daughter left a private school in the Springs deficient in math. The individual attention she gained allowed her to excel. She struggled through challenging honors classes to be brave enough to take on the extensive AP courses. She graduated 2012 and is pulling a 3.7 GPA at the University of Colorado. She insists it was the teachers specifically in Math, English Composition, Biology, Chemistry, Anatomy, Government, Psychology... and their dedication to her success were in sync with her determination to succeed. Pair that with top notch extra curricular activities and you have a great school. In a year when it comes time for our son to attend high school we are certain Doherty is the best choice. We've found our school This school is one of the best things that's ever happened to me. One thing that really meant a lot to me was making the volleyball team at Doherty my freshman year even though I didn't make it all three years in middle school. Our athletic program is absolutely amazing if you ask me. The kids at Doherty are super friendly, as well as the staff! I'm super thankful and blessed to be part of such a great school with a lot of team spirit and support! I would recommend Doherty to any kid. I had a great experience at Doherty (I was an AP/honors student juggling homework and 3 different bands as well as cheer and graduated with a 3.99 in 2014. It can be done as long as you focus), but I can't say the same thing for my brother. He was bullied so bad for wanting to do cheer that he ended up transferring schools. The admin did everything they could to stop it, but nothing worked. Doherty is a good place for academics and sports, but when it comes to the way kids treat each other, its one of the worst places ive ever seen. The teachers try to help, but kids will always lie about what happens. They also have a drug issue, but if you don't know people who do drugs, you'll never know about it. Unfortunately Doherty is not as good as many people may tell you. I attended Doherty my starting in 2013 and I transferred halfway through my Junior year (2015). Doherty is a place of competition in every aspect weather it be in sports or personal status, i.e. Who is the most popular, who is in student council, or who throws the "craziest" party. Sports is one thing but once you cross the line into person status and ego that's where everything gets twisted and unethical. Without getting into detail, it can be hard enough to keep yours grades up and then add that the feeling of having to keep up with all the "cool" kids is ridiculous because if you don't, good luck ever finding your niche. I left because I lost sence of who I really was and the pressure of trying to keep up was not worth it anymore. Because in reality High School I just a stepping stone in our lives. All in all I would not recommend at all going to Doherty, but in the end it's your call. It was an awesome experience. All schools in the U.S. have some sort of problems with one or two teachers or students. Overall my experience was really good. The teachers really care about there students. I had the opportunity to join pretty much any club or sport possible. My teachers took me for a week long fieldtrip to learn about water, geology, astronomy, ancient cultures, etc... It was one of the most amazing experiences of my life. I would highly recommend any student to at least try out Doherty. I love this school and it’s people. There are no AP math classes that I am aware of, so idk why there’s a statistic on it. I love the staff, teachers and students. I like it that my kids are at a school that is racially and socio-economically diverse. It teaches the students compassion, kindness and to accept those that are different then them. If you care for your child find a different school. Bullying goes unchecked by the administration. Kids in the bathrooms drugging and drinking and this is well know by security and the administrations- as long as they get on the bus to home they are not the schools issue. Reaching out to teachers or office staff generally takes persistence. Do not bother calling attendance as they do no mark correctly and you still get calls and have to call again to clear up the mess. Teachers overload students to the point of tears without help. Constant bullying goes unchecked by the teachers and staff. Counselors are not available and takes WEEKS for them to respond. Honestly? I've been at this school at the beginning of the 2021-2022 school year. I have noticed quite a few things, if you aren't outgoing or conventionally attractive at the beginning of either semester, good luck making friends. I didn't. Even then, many of the people here are the sort of people who would talk badly about you behind your back for an ego rush. The teachers are either there just for the lackluster pay, or in just ONE of my classes, actually care about the students and how they are doing. Personally, I wouldn't recommend this public high school for kids that tend to be more reserved and antisocial, there's a decent chance you will not make friends. I have been ridiculed right next to me by people who I don't know, been made fun of behind my back by classmates, and much more isolating behavior from other students. Don't come here unless you're social, attractive and want to join a club, this school will destroy you. Unfortunately, the classes suck most of the time. bad bad bad bad bad bad bad I’ve been a parent at Doherty for five years. The teachers and staff are always responsive and send frequent communications about their courses. I attend PT conferences and have had meetings individually other times of the year. When an issue has come up, it was handled quickly. Both of my children participated in athletics and my oldest has finished her freshman year of college with a 3.987 GPA so I feel my children are being well taught and prepared for college. We have one more child currently in middle school that will attend Doherty as well. Understaffed, underfunded and overcrowded. Unaddressed bullying, rampant racism, drugs and sex in bathrooms. There are some great teachers lost in this mess but more who are coasting to retirement and do not care. Our daughter’s now in an alternate school for no other reason than a smaller learning environment. Doherty’s M/O is to push students through no matter what. Preparing students for the future? Yeah, a future at McDonald’s. I want to support our local public school, but Doherty is a lost cause short of a complete overhaul of how they do (or don’t do) things. Doherty High School has amazing teachers that care about each student!! The staff bend over backwards to assist students on their educational journey!!All four of my students had great pride in DHS and had received strong education!! Doherty’s moto “We Before Me” has been a great life lesson for them too!!

column3: Uneven teaching, but the only high school in the area in which you'd want your kids. If you go to parent/teacher conferences and check your student's homework and grades (online!) you can get a good feel for the quality of this school. The music and theater programs are great. Chemistry and history are standouts. Every other dept. has both excellent & disastrous teachers. 2011 state f'ball champs, lots of Nat'l Merit Scholars, counselors are helpful if you are persistent & involved. Very crowded but getting a facelift. Fayetteville High School is an amazing school with plenty of opportunities to excel academically and in the community and a school where you'll get to meet amazing people along the way. Socially, FHS is one of those places that accepts everyone and people are able to float around group to group; there are no boundaries with finding students from all walks of life socializing with everyone. Academically, the teachers are well suited in teaching students the fundamentals of a curriculum, but also going above and beyond by adding their own twists from their experience to make learning accessible and fun. The language teachers and AP teachers are the best (in my opinion). ;) I love this school. I am planning on moving down t here over the summer i have three kids two with disability can someone tell me how the special classes are please. This is a great school if you are talented in sports or extremely smart. Keep in mind, the only reason this school did not split into two high schools was athletics. The high school is being renovated for $100 million and has numerous issues such as traffic congestion, no time to eat lunch, and no additional parking. They could have moved but chose to stay in the same land locked location. However, if you want to pay local property owners $500+ a semester they will let you park in their driveway. If you an A/B student, this is not your school. You are just a number and teachers are hit and miss. Some are excellent. Some are bad and just waiting to retire. With so many students, they do not have time to invest themselves in the students and the counselors are overworked. I would look at the high schools in Springdale, Rogers, or Farmington before enrolling in Fayetteville. Too overcrowded. Kids get lost in the numbers. Way too competitive. Athletes must specialize in a specific sport due to over-crowding. Even if they make a team they may not play/travel. Many scholar recipients are children of UA professor types--excellent students do not stand out.Teachers are advancing careers for pay raise; too busy w/administration requirements (trying to keep their school numbers falsely impressive). Good normal students are overlooked. Parents must be aggressive & proactive yet risk offending someone who isn't doing their job--teaching. Impressive facilities on the outside yet overworked tired staff on the inside. Parking/traffic issue is a nightmare. DAILY Spent 1 HOUR driving middle/elementary schools on opposite ends of town with HS in the middle despite alternate start times. Parents find out 1 day before school they were moved to a different school due to over crowding. Some schools do not have same calendars; if you have more than 1 child they may attend differently: don't plan vacation. Long-standing community families are elitists who shove their weight around &administration/coaches cave. Exodus to smaller rural schools is the trend. Do not go here. We stuck it out just to try to teach our child to never give up. However do not consider this high school. Fayetteville lower levels are great and junior high is too but run from this high school. There are a few coaches that are good but for the most part all of the good ones are gone. Winning titles is the only interest they have. Preparing children for their futures or helping Someone in need no way. They will crush your child's spirit with this exclusivity. They manipulate the system for their favorites. It is really crazy. I am a believer in Christ and many of them say they are but it is a farce. There was a female coach and who actually prayed for every senior but purposefully excluded mine. If there were room I could tell you story after story. Don't go here if you like sports and never expect The principal or Counsleor we to help. Our ADHD student taking advanced level classes has had nothing but accommodating, supportive teachers and has a very nice school vice principal assigned. Our exchange student took general level classes and said they were surprised how much Fayetteville High School teachers seems to care, compared with teachers in their home country. Cannot speak to sports culture or the how school treats students with more serious problems. I can say that, due to our child's disability, we have had to interact more with the school and its teachers than most parents, and we have been impressed with the level of caring and responsiveness of the teachers. Academically, FHS seems to have a lot more homework compared with other Fayetteville high schools, if a student is taking the most difficult classes. It seems quite rigorous compared with other nearby city and town schools, as well. One teacher said moving from a nearby town to FHS is like night and day in terms of how much his son has to work. With the university and kids from those parents nearby, there's a lot of preternaturally brilliant kids who value academics, and perhaps they set the pace for the more advanced classes. I am very confident that while my student won't be an academic big fish in this big pond, they will be well-prepared for college as a result. We are frankly surprised how much teachers seem to care and how intelligent, responsive and professional they are. We really expected less from such a large school, where kids and mediocre teachers might easily get overlooked. I certainly wouldn't cast doubt on others' less positive experiences. It IS a large school, and we of course have not met all the teachers, staff, coaches, etc. But in our narrow window of experiences (our own student for a couple of years now and the exchange student), we are quite pleasantly surprised. Our only complaint in terms of our own student is that the classes are too large, and we feel that a community like Fayetteville has the resources to cut classes down to an evidence-based size. The district should not have 30+ students in a room. It would serve students and teachers alike to reduce class sizes. The AP program is great. Very good teachers on the whole, both in AP and outside, but especially in AP. Very good votech with Mr. Laney and others. He actually puts his own cash in the program and has gotten many kids jobs. Other parts of the school are more mixed. It is very big and bureaucratic, so some kids get lost in the shuffle. Kids are now taking 8 courses, which is just too many, I think to get them through the building fast so it won't be too crowded. The leadership has not handled covid well, starting with the fake temperature checks to start the day as kids enter. It doesn't work and is all for show. Again too many kids are just getting lost and not showing up to anything since covid; many classes have 25% attendance combining online and in person. All that said, the school's teachers are generally solid, a few losers but not many. The kids are nice. Good facility. It is a school where if you want to get a good education, stick mainly with AP classes and you will learn a lot, as least when covid is not happening. Some of the activities are also very good, including drama, litmag, quiz bowl, music, and there is a college level athletic program. Oh, and just having filled things out, there is a very laid back attitude toward cheating, too much so. Some teachers and assistant principals would like to change that, but they get no support. There was a lot of disruption when they went from a school discipline scheme that mostly worked to one where they took away most any punishment. Kids are not stupid and could immediately tell. I think they are rethinking that, and luckily, since the kids are mostly nice, things never went too out of control. Kids feel safe at the school.

column1: dear parent who wrote that mean thing below: i may be a student, but you need to grow up please and thank you. To some shs may be a good school.But the school has flaws,such as,It's so little that they dont offer great education.Instead they focus on sports.Plus if you ever wanted to get involved in a sport,you had to be popular or a teacher's son or daughter.Otherwise,you're stuck with nothing. over rated . My daughters struggled through the first year of college and had to do plenty of tutoring sessions to catch up.

column3: Very poor school. Caters to Athletics and Gifted students. My children only had 2 teachers that cared about their progress in the 8 years they attended there. Liberty schools are MUCH better, send your kids there. IMO, this is such a dissappointing school ... Academics and getting kids ready for college and real life just doesn't seem to be a priority, and the decision making within this district baffles me. All schools have good and bad aspects but for an overall quality education, access to a multitude of extra-curricular activities, and teachers and staff that care, you can't top Kearney. My children are not star athletes nor the star students but these teachers have gone out of their way to help each of my children recognize their potential. And the support of this community is amazing! Maybe I shouldn't write this...it may give away the secret of this fabulous district and people will flock here. Scratch everything I just said! Kearney High School is a great school. The kids are smart, the teachers are great. The way that they get the kids ready for college is fantastic. All three of my kids graduated and went off to college, where they also graduated. No complaints! Very disappointed in this school district. Transferred my family from a bigger school district to Kearney, despite being warned by a friend about a bullying issue. This year was going okay because the “mean girls” all seem to have last names L-Z and thanks to the hybrid schedule my youngest daughter didn’t have to interact with them. When it was announced that they would be returning 5 days a week, I was told that I couldn’t switch my daughter to online only despite transportation concerns. In the past, numerous time children have had to sit on the floor of the bus. I was told that this “might not” be an issue this year because parents are really answering the call for transporting to/from school. That isn’t an option for me. And these other parents? It’s easy to get your kid to/from school 2 days a week but 5? Not likely a solution for many! It’s a COVID outbreak waiting to happen. So many things to hate about this district. Only had experience with two other districts, one which isn’t as highly rated as Kearney, but my daughter says she’d choose it over Kearney any day. Would not recommend this school at all. I'm moving out of this school district because it is so bad. There is no diversity whatsoever, there is bullying and a lot of white supremacist people. DO NOT go here if LGBTQIA+ at all. You would not be able to come out without being harassed daily for it. A friend of mine gets called slurs on the daily for being out. This school has me scared to be myself.

column1: ECHS is a good school for parents that want their students to feel a good connection with everyone around them. It is a sports driven school, and most of the teachers that are there also coach something or are involved in the sports in some way. The leadership for the school is a little lacking. The high school principal is rather lenient on anything that isn't threatening. The only thing that I have bad to say is they force the students to take a speech class, and say it's required for graduating by the state, when it isn't. East Canton High School is a great school with a variety of options located in an admirable facility built only four years ago. From the basic classes to both on site and off site college level courses, this school has the academics covered. And in disagreement with a previous review by another user, the teachers are not hired based on their coaching ability. In fact, the current boys basketball coach is not a teacher at East Canton at all, and many of the teachers are not and never have been coaches themselves. The school, like the town, is very small. While this tends to limit the variety of sports, there are still many options available to students. The one disadvantage of this school is its lack of funding. Currently, there is a $200 pay-to-play fee on all extra-curriculars that require transportation, no field-trips for students, and only busing for students who live outside of a 1 mile radius of the school. This problem though could easily be remedied by the township by a contribution from the citizen.

column3: Overall, this has been a great school for my kids. Although, they have strange discipline rules. Such as, looking through my daughters phone before they can return it. Which didn't get passed me. But the learning and overall ojectives were great. MCHS is Family. Teachers are passionate and engage their students. I especially like Freshman Academy. The freshman class never have to leave they're own 'school'. This promotes them to focus on their studies instead of upperclassmen and other distracting issues that high school can bring. Horrible, beyond all measures. I'd rather be in prison than enter the gates of MCHS again. My biggest regret in life is that I didn't leave this school. The teachers are incapable of doing their job, the administrators are useless but act as if they're improving the school, the community isn't that bad but most of the students are god-awful. If you value your child's high school career, I strongly suggest, no I BEG you to pick another school. I can’t imagine my children attending any other school. I have been thoroughly impressed with the school, the teachers, and the other students. My kid started to go to this middle school in her 7 the grade and immediately was a target of bullying. She’s been minority in every school in the south so we were again disappointed. We responded quickly to the problem this time to solve it with the school but the school didn’t get the bullies parents involved. Instead, they offer counseling to my kid and some “talk” to those bullies. Of course it didn’t go away but kept going under the water. They started to call my kid “snitch”. We reported several times after that and had meeting with vice principal and school counselors but all they assure us was that they will talk to them and they will meet consequences if it didn’t stop. The entire thing made my kid isolated from peers and the bullying group became bigger.The end of the 8th grade year, those bullies were chosen to be awarded students (award was something about good behavior). My kid had won region writing contest but the school didn’t even mention it.

column1: Some of the faculty is really good. The athletic department is the strongest. Discipline seems to be the major emphasis of the administrators (most of whom has a PE background). This place is a revolving door for teachers. My child had 3 different teachers in one year in history. That department appears to be the most problematic in terms of teacher retention. Foreign language is also very weak. Morris Knolls is an amazing school to develop into a young adult. The course load can be quite rigorous, but well worth the effort. The teachers that my son had the opportunity learn from are in my opinion "superior." He always felt that there was a good support system. He was involved in all aspects of the school including the athletics and chorale. Again "superior." While my son succeed at his pace, my daughter is now suceeding in her own way! The school supports all students and their endeavers! I will miss Morris Knolls when my daughter graduates! This is a phenomenal high school! I have 2 kids there now: 1 is a senior, the other is a freshmen. The teachers are great, caring, and involved with the students. If you want to assess the health of the school, do like I have done, and drive by nearly any time of the day and you will see students and teachers there. Am not talking about kids hanging out looking for trouble. Am talking about kids who are in sports, clubs, plays, marching band, chorus, and other clubs that keep them at school by choice. There is diversity and a range of socioeconomic factors at play in case you thought otherwise. The respect each other and get along. I love this school! My son just graduated . He struggled academically both Freshman and Sophomore years..but I was impressed with the teachers and guidance support and diligence. He felt supported ...got the hang of it. Honors all Junior year...High Honors and AP courses his Senior. Attending college and doing great. We all look back fondly at the Knolls experience Morris Knolls is a great school with lots of academic options and there is a huge amount of school spirit.
