column3: My family had an awful experience at this school. Our student is smart (tests show it) but lazy in class (almost straight Fs). We would stay on top of things from home, but at school, nobody would help. They wouldn't even keep us updated about his progress (or lack thereof). After 2 years of failing every class, we suggested holding him back. The counselor said that we would be 'ruining the forward momentum of his academic track'. The school made it clear that you can do nothing, literally, and still get passed on all the way until 12th grade, when you become someone else's problem. Its easy to be a good teacher to someone who wants it, but a remarkable teacher will find a way to engage even the most disinterested studens (as opposed to just writing them off). Thankfully, he is doing really well at another high school. I have two students at Burroughs. Edline makes it very easy to contact teachers, get emails on absences, progress reports, and grades. The teachers are good about emailing me back when I have questions or concerns. One son has been accepted to a variety of universities, and I'm confident he has the skills to succeed in college. Burroughs has prepared him well. The other student is not Honors/AP but needs help to do well. I basically have run the gamut of programs at Burroughs....and BOTH serve students' needs. I've also found the counselors to be incredibly helpful when I've had concerns. Burroughs is definitely lacking compared to other schools. Having moved from Indiana, my son was in the middle of his junior year where he was in the college prep curriculum. At Burroughs, he was relearning things he had learned at the junior high level. After 2 months, I pulled him out and transferred him to Opportunities for Learning, which is basically a charter/home school atmosphere. Needless to say, he started college courses prior to graduating high school through Opportunities for Learning. I was very disappointed in this high school, but in the long run and looking back, I am glad we took the road we did as my son was able to start his college career early and was much happier than being "the new kid" at the public school. He also was able to still compete on the swim team while at Opportunities for Learning through Immanuel Christian school (private) and lettered. If I had another child, I would not send to Burroughs, but would pursue private schooling as the education level is much higher. Burroughs has done really well for my students. One just started college and Burroughs has prepped him well. The Honors AP courses prepare students well for what is expected of them in college. The other non-private place in town is called Opportunities for Learning; it is just a credit mill that has kids do a few worksheets for lots of credit. It's a shame that the public allows places like that to exist. If a student is going to an accredited college, then real prep work is done at Burroughs in the CP/ Honors/AP classes. My daughter transferred into BHS her sophomore year. She was welcomed by so many of the staff, who bent over backwards to help her adjust. She has been treated better here than at the local private school she had been attending since she was 4yrs. I love the teachers and admin, they are involved with the students and want to help them. I would highly recommend this school. It has prepared my daughter academically for collage and I am very thankful for the opportunities it has provided her with. They charge you $150 per student for the worst bussing I have ever seen, the student is guilty until proven otherwise, they are more worried about busting your student than teaching them, they have a money fine for late library books, they infringe on the student's rights, and they use Comancore.

column3: Excellent school. The Principal, the parent coordinator, the Assistant Principals and teachers are the best in the city and thus in the country and furthermore in the world. I am so happy that my daughter has achieved to be there and further achieved to be at the top 2-3% of her class. We heard warnings from other parents whose kids had terrible experiences at Stuy, but we didn't listen and thought our son would do just fine. Sadly, he had a terrible four years and I wish we'd listened more carefully to what those other parents told us. Stuy is a brutal factory school. If your child is a superstar with a thick skin and tons of self-confidence, she'll probably be fine and go to Harvard. If your child has moments of insecurity or is not prepared to study 12 hours per day, you may well have problems coming your way. And don't expect the administration to listen when you wonder why your child is extremely stressed and depressed. They think that's normal for teenagers because that's how the majority of their students are. I know I sound bitter, but you can't truly believe it until it happens to you. No wonder stress and depression are constant topics for the PTA. If you have the opportunity, make another choice. Your child will thank you What I've learned from my experience is that Stuyvesant isn't for everyone. On paper, it sounds amazing, but the experience can really make or break you. Some kids are tough, are great at studying until 4:00am every day. For some, it's a great school. It's got a lot to offer and and is amazing academically. I feel that students don't get to have a good high school experience going here. If cramming is your thing, than Stuy is the place for you, it will not let you rest or get a minute of free time. You'll get into a great college and learn tons. Personally, I think that Bronx High School of Science is a better all around option, astounding academics, sports, opportunities, community and will lead to a better high school experience. Stuyvesant is a great, great high school, but if you don't know what to expect, you'll be surprised. Stuyvesnt High School is a well-rounded and competitive public school that prepares students for their next journey to higher education. As a parent of a Senior student, I find the lack of commitment from the teachers at Stuy extremely disappointing. The teachers had the audacity to deny a student a teachers recommendation. I am hoping and praying my child gets into a college of her choice ,as she was already denied the ED opportunity, thanks to the inability to get a 2 nd teachers rec.And to make matters worse, when I reached out to the parent teacher coordinator for help, it made matters even worse.Now my child is upset that I reached out to her school for help and fears retaliation.A word of advice to other HS Students parents- Do your own preparation to get your child into college. Don't expect a miracle from the staff and or Administration.They have 3 guidance counselors for 843 students. What can you expect from these so called guidance counselors when they are themselves sinking?I so want this school year to be over and see my child back to the land of norm and decency and courtesy, back to being a regular teenager, not looking like the world is weighing her down. When I was in 8th grade last year, my heart was completely set on Stuy, and my mother told me, if you're not willing to do well in school, there's no point. And there really isn't: this school is meant only for people who have the proper work ethic and are actually willing to put their heart and soul into their work. But I guess that's a good thing, because then you're surrounded by all these people who are so hard working and they've got their mind set on such a fixed goal, you've gotta admire their determination. That kind of perseverance is so amazing and at Stuy, even if you don't want to, you're forced to try your best. This school is simply amazing! Stuyvesant has been one of the best high schools in the country for many decades. More Nobel Prize winners have graduated from here than from all but a few colleges. After graduating I went to Cornell and Columbia; Stuyvesant was more intellectually challenging than either university. Every student here would likely have been at or near the top of the class at their local high school; here most will be average or below. If you view these facts as an opportunity to grow with the best and test your tue limits, welcome. If this doesn't appeal to you, that's fine; you may also reach your potential elsewhere. You just may have to do it more on your own, with less support from your school community. This is a wonderful school, my daughter really liked it, I went to the schools many times, the president was very nice to meet the parent if he is not busy, lots of out of school activities from all areas. it is hard to get in, lots of kids travel from different zones. What I think others should know: There is a reason for this prestige. Kids aren't necessarily "geniuses" but they are hardworking. There's around 1 or 2 hours of homework everyday, but with computer science, it's more (coding takes time). On top of that is studying. What do I like: You can learn anything here. Everything is offered. Everyone in Stuy is really nice and has good morals. You learn what hard work is and determination is. It pushes you to your ultimate self. Improvement: Some downsides are that to achieve a 90 at Stuy requires you to study until 12am (for the most part). It's not an easy school. Everyone remains depressed and sleep deprived due to pressure to study. Some homeworks do not help since only tests are counted towards your grades. It would make you feel stressed out, 85% of the time. AP's aren't weighted either. Overall: Stuy has changed me as a person. Even if it doesn't get you into Harvard (due to low grades administered), it gives you knowledge and ability to carry on through hardship. It's 4 years of pain, dull mental and physical soreness. But it's a pain that also can leave a beautiful scar. quite excellent!... since 1904... pls see www.ourstrongband.org. Neal H. Hurwitz, Executive Director. Publishers of The Centennial Book: Stuyvesant High School: The Fiorst 100 Years, 1904-2004. ILM of Frank McCourt, Sterling Jensen, Murl Thrush, James Cagney, et al. Thank you!!! Stuy has many brilliant brilliant kids. It is not competitive because the kids are mean - they aren't. It is competitive because the top colleges will only make a few offers and so everyone works hard to get to the top. This has led to a wide-spread culture of cheating. Also, it is too bad that many of the teachers aren't as smart as the kids. Some are great, but many are terrible teachers. The admin knows but can't get rid of them. My son had some horrible teachers for important science courses. Also, the school is so large, it is very hard to get issues addressed by the admin. If your kid never needs extra help, then it is all good. But if you need to work with the admin on anything - forget about it. My school MCJHS is the best school. It is very small but but staffs are very dedicated. Most teachers are very much involved in state test preparation. Some of the teachers are extremely good, they encourage student to do excellent in their study. i don not go to this school but my friedns ae going there. Im in 8th grade and willl be taking the shsat exam next sunday!!! in any caseit is a hard school. Think of it as the Harvard of high schools. Many cant take it but its worth it at theend. the amount or ed. you get at the end is unbelieveable Stuy is a place where ambitious, spirited kids of different personalities, interests, socioeconomic statuses, and ethnic backgrounds commute from all over the city to work, learn, and grow as people. As cheesy as this sounds, no matter who you are, you will, for the most part, find an accepting environment that values your individuality. The curriculums of the plethora of courses offered at the school have been well designed to challenge even the brightest students, and even the standard-level required courses are taught at levels far above those of most schools. On the other hand, I agree with the previous review of Stuyvesant calling it a "brutal factory school". Our averages are almost solely based off of difficult tests that are often multiple choice. Even on the tests that are not multiple choice, no free points are given. If you don't know or understand the material very well, you WILL fail. Despite being a specialized high school, the school does focus on city standards and has strict rules and requirements based on this. You will risk some of your well-being if you go to Stuy, but almost everyone says it is worth it. Stuyvesant is a meritocratic system that rewards intelligence, grit, and ambition - providing a level playing field for students from all socioeconomic backgrounds. It affords an unparalleled opportunity to explore both the arts and sciences through its endless selection of classes and extracurricular activities. Students are challenged and motivated by their faculty, but more so by their peers. While the environment is undoubtedly competitive, the culture is no less collaborative. Lifelong friendships are forged here as this uniquely spectacular experience binds us together. I look back on my high school years fondly and proudly. Stuyvesant is a special school which provides great opportunities for bright students from all socioeconomic backgrounds. If your kids have learning disabilities, do not send them to Stuyvesant. The school has no supports and cannot make accommodations. Most of the teachers do not understand learning disabilities. I wish I had known this before I sent my daughter there. Stuy is ideal for children who want to learn and who are willing to put in as much time as necessary to achieve a good result for him/herself. Extremely competitive atmosphere, but equally cooperative atmosphere. Everyone wants to get into Harvard, Yale or Princeton, but nobody hides books in the library. Mutually supportive. Success at Stuy makes college a comfortable journey. Stuy in not for kids/parents who stress strong excurricular activities to the detriment of studies/homework/class projects. In short, Stuy is the educational experience of a lifetime, unparalleled elsewhere. The worst school ever, highly over rated. Stuyvesant saved my life, it was my life. Excellent. Teachers are extremely smart and yet very patient with the students. Assignments are thorough. Prepares you not only for college, but prepares you for the rest of your life! Stuy is not miracle factory that will transform the average middle school graduate into a Ivy League - level student in four years. Stuyvesant is a school that takes already top performing students and pushes them to their limits. For reference, about 850 students make it in to Stuyvesant every year, while about 30,000 apply. That's about a 3 percent acceptance rate. It's a lower rate of acceptance than Harvard, Yale, Princeton, or even Stanford. The school itself is not a free ticket to college, as many parents might be expecting. It's a pretty brutal grind in an environment where everybody is scrambling to outdo themselves. The pressure to do well is immense. I cracked in the first semester of freshman year, and spent the rest of the next four years struggling to recover my GPA. I did get into my college of choice in the end, but it was a tough four years. I knew a few kids who broke down or gave up entirely in the junior and senior years. At the same time though, there were kids who were ridiculously on top of things. Some students pretty much never got less than a solid A in a class, while also balancing clubs and events. And even then, those students were constantly struggling to do better. The teachers at Stuyvesant are, overwhelmingly, highly competent and extremely knowledgeable. That said, every year your kid will have at least one teacher that they hate, and it could be for one of a few reasons. The most common of these is that the teacher isn't effective at conveying ideas, but expects students to understand concepts regardless. This is the case for a few STEM teachers at the school. The next possibility is that the teacher is mean. Note that in my experience, the "mean" teachers at Stuyvesant tended to be very knowledgeable and effective teachers. The least likely scenario is that the teacher has no business teaching, and sadly, this is the case for a select few teachers at Stuyvesant. I myself took two courses that were taught by teachers who spouted nonsense, pushed political agendas in class, and were totally unwilling to accommodate students' situations. And I got A's in those classes basically by sucking up to those teachers. In conclusion, Stuyvesant is an extremely high-stress institution where success requires both dedication and ingenuity. Don’t procrastinate or else you will end up getting 3 hours of sleep. Bullying doesn’t seem to exist in this school. Everyone including the upperclassmen are nice. Even though they don’t look nice, the seniors have muscles larger than me. I’ll be back in 4 years if I survive them.

column1: Although the school is full of amazing teachers, it lacks greatly in other areas. If you are moving to this district from somewhere else you can forget making friends. The kids are cruel and i get teased for "being born above the mason-dixon line." They are not at all accepting of diversity. The dress code is way too strict. They need to focus on making their classes actually challenging, not spend all their time measuring the hemline of my skirt with a 3x5 notecard. I am rather conservative person, but no where sells skirts that are three inches above the knee unless i get it from the old lady section. Principal and staff are pretty good. It is easy to make friends here, and the academic and sports here are overachieving. Probably not the best school out therem but certainly not the worst. -Graduating class of 14 My son is a Senior this year and I am so thrilled with the outstanding education he has acquired while at Creekview. The principal is excellent and the students think so as well. Academics are challenging and I feel my son is definitely ready for college. Thank you Creekview :) I don't know if she is still there, but Mrs. Brown is probably the greatest teacher I have ever had. I had her for econ my senior year and if you pay attention and retain it all college econ will be incredibly easy. She definitely knows her stuff. I haven't had to study for any of my test. So shes either the best teacher on earth or I'm some kind of savant. But seriously this school is pretty swell, definitely prepares you for college, except for math. The only worthy math teacher is Mrs. Norris. We never dreamed that we would find teachers like my son has at his school! My son gets denied lunch on a regular basis because it would put him "over", even though they don't want to give him his balance if he asks.They are supposed to have online system (Aspen) for tracking grades and assignments but not one teacher in two years has kept it up to date, so by the time the grade is listed as missing in the system they say it is too late to hand it in. The art teacher makes ongoing snarky comments about how some kids (she looks at my son) can't draw or won't graduate from high school. Now he doesn't want to take any more art classes because of the teacher.Very assembly line in many ways.My son was rated 'exceeds' on all his tests before he started at this HS and now he is just barely in the minimum levels. Not much to brag about. And in addition, school now gives him anxiety and insomnia. We may move just to get away from this school. Horrible ratio is really 30:1 they need a lot more teachers They are doing an amazing job here This school is really unsafe for children with disabilities. Don’t send your kids here or to its middle school please. It all starts with the overcrowding. The zoning expands to the entire northeast section of the county so it’s severly overcrowded with kids that live 30 mins away. Plus they keep building more houses, which doesn’t help. Because the overcrowding is so bad, only seniors and some juniors can park. And because the middle and highschool are right across from eachother and get out at the same time, about a million kids are car rider. The busses are also severly overcrowded. I only had a locker my freshman year because we didn’t, and still don’t, have enough. The only reason the test scores are so high is because they push AP and honors classes down kids throats. In this school your kid is literally a slave to the system. You would think, since they are getting rich off these kids, that theyd be able to afford better materials. Nope. We still have dell laptops from 2009 and classes that hardly get cleaned. Their lack of effort reflects on the students too, it makes them uninspired kids that only get good grades because of the hope that they can get out of there and to college. The hallways are barren and it looks like hospital, honestly. There’s no art or anything that says “hey we’re actually embracing the youth of tomorrow”. Just white walls. The only thing I can commend about this school is its English department. Anyway I transferred to a nearby school and experianced a total culture shock, I can’t tell you how badly I wished I had transferred sooner. Oh and the school knows they have a problem, because so many kids transfer out of it. At my new school I’ve met 6 people already—that I know of—who were in my grade at Creekview. I’ve talked to them and their experience reflects mine. I didn't "graduate" the traditional way, since I dropped out and got my GED at 18, but that's besides the point.I was in this school from 9th grade to 10th grade, and dropped out the beginning of 11th grade.Homework: This entirely depends on the teachers and classes you take. If you take a regular class instead of an honors or AP class, expect less homework. The teachers hand out homework differently, too, but to be honest as long as you pay attention in class and do a little studying you will be okay.Teachers: I really liked the teachers I had. They knew what they were doing, and taught well. The people in my classes who complained about teachers were the ones who didn't pay attention in class. I had to be given a 504 plan for my mental health, and the teachers accommodated to all of my needs. For example, I had severe anxiety when presenting in front of a class, so the teachers agreed to let me present alone to them. They are great people!Leadership: Not sure what to put here, but there are many clubs to choose from at this school. Also the end of the school spirit at football games is crazy. I was in the band and the student section always went wild at football games.Character: There isn't much compassion as a whole. It depends from person to person, but everybody is fending for themselves. If you aren't already in a clique or group of people, they could care less about you.Learning Differences: This school apparently has a great program for disabled kids according to my mom. My brother has autism and graduated from there. Most of the students who aren't disabled are incredibly nice to the disabled students. They say hi to them in the halls, high five them, etc. There will always be some bad apples, but for the most part they are nice to the disabled students.Bullying: I wouldn't say there's straight up "bullying", just no compassion. Also leaving people out. This goes back to the clique thing I mentioned earlier. The school doesn't care.Overall I recommend this school. I wasn't there to make friends, I just wanted to graduate but my mental health interfered with that. I hope this review helps someone. This school is not the best, my sister has a learning disability -has ADHD- and her teachers know that. They don't help her, she gets distracted really easily, and gets off track. She can't help that, she has been taking medicine, but it doesn't really help her. The medicine makes her feel upset and she cries because of it. The school has had a meeting with her, and they had asked her if she need a helper there to help her or help her understand, and my sister said yes, because she needs it. That was over 1/2 months ago. They hadn't provided her with a helper, that can focus on my sister and only her. This school is not the best with people who have learning disabilities. Overall, this school needs to do better.

column3: I loved going to Andover Central High School. This school has so many opportunities to do great things. Someone said that high school is what you make it and I agree with that. If you take the time to be involved and get to know people than you will enjoy it. Their teachers are good and the place feels much more polished than usual public schools. The food from the cafeteria is good and some days I miss their enchiladas. The principal has changed since I went there so I cannot really comment on that. The extracurricular programs are great and a lot of money is spent on new technology each year. They really try to keep things up to date and well maintained. I am not sure where to begin with Andover Central... To list off the FEW positives they have a nice building and technology. As far as that NOTHING else is good ! The teachers don't care about actually getting the children educated, and the administration may be the worst I've EVER seen. They cannot resolve any problems in a correct manner. Math is horrible at Andover Central and in math assist little to no help was offered the teachers allowed their students to use iPads to work on a program that related nothing with math so the teacher did nothing . I transfered my children to a private school in Wichita after an AWFUL year at Andover Central where they had a D in a math and at the private school they had As... this school as has major bullying problems and the adminstration does nothing . If you want your kids to grow up as rude disrespectful adults send them to Andover Central.. if not spend the money on a private school. Trust me Wichita has superior private schools.( Kapaun Mt. Carmel, The Independent School, Wichita Collegiate School, Trinity Academy, Sunrise act.) Excellent school, excellent teachers. Administration that cares. Firm but fair disciplinary structure. Kids are allowed leeway but faculty clearly in charge of their classrooms. Achievements are a matter of public record....students perform extremely well on standardized tests. Numerous extra-curricular activities. Safe, supportive environment. Things like dress code and student section antics are reasonably monitored and well controlled. Facilities are very good. ACHS is a place for good kids and good parents. Kids that want to disrupt the learning environment should consider other options; they just don't tolerate that in Andover schools. Progressive discipline system, again, is firm but fair. All they care about is test scores and Stepford children. They'd sooner get rid of your kid then help your kid. Heaven forbid test scores get lowered! Biggest mistake ever moving here! Great School, faculty and staff care and do a great job for their students. Honestly, my experience with this school was horrible. They try taking away privileges from everyone, when only a few people messed up. They try to control every aspect of every little thing, and when one person violates one small thing, the whole school has to suffer with them. Instead of taking care of that one person, they punish EVERYONE. Even some of the teachers acknowledge this is not the way to do things. Using negative reinforcements on kids makes them want to act out even more... maybe if they used their heads more.

column1: This is a great school to grow up at. Teachers are great and they interact with the students really well. Small school benefits -- small class room size, good community support, great teachers. Overall, moving in a positive direction. Lacking with educational opportunities for students. I would not define as progressive. However, family involvement is high. Those families that give more monetarily seem to receive more. The early elementary reading program is outstanding. The kids have progressed with reading and writing quite well so far. We've been very impressed with the small school feel, and the communication to parents has been great.

column3: My daughter is a freshman and is in the honors program - all honors classes (except one which is AP). As of now, she is hoping to major in engineering in college. The Wildstang robotics program is an excellent resource for students to see how an engineering team works together. The extra curricular activities offer a broad spectrum for varied interests of the students. The teachers are helpful and caring. For the area, the school is considered "small" and I think that is a plus. I also like the block scheduling. District 214 is fantastic and RM is great. The school sometimes gets a bad rap from those who would rather have a all-white school like Prospect or Hersey, where the aggregate test scores are skewed higher with low latino populations. I am quite certain that if your child is smart they will excel at RM. The staff at RM is excellent with few bad teachers, and athletics are very competitive with ability for your son or daughter to make the team without having to get lost in a sea of rich travel kids Freshman year. The vibe and school spirit are on the rise at the school. I grew up in Rolling Meadows. When my husband and I found out we were expecting twins, we decided to return to RM from the city. I am an alumna of Rolling Meadows High School. I loved my four years set RMHS. I keep in touch with a few of my teachers. I believe that a student will receive the support they need from the wonderful staff. School staff support is just one part of the education equation. A supportive family and an intrinsically motivated student are the other important factors. I look forward to returning to RMHS when it's my children's turn to walk the hallways. As a parent of 3 RMHS graduates I highly recommend this school. The children were involved in the many activities and clubs the school offers and were also involved in dance and sports. They were in honors and AP classes and were well prepared for college. All 3 attended great universities, including an ivy league school, graduated and are working good jobs. Rolling Meadows High School has an excellent teaching staff and a stellar college counseling department. You can't go wrong with District 214, and Rolling Meadows High School is one of the bet in the district. As a parent of one graduate, current student, and spouse is RM alumni- we couldn’t be happier. Our daughter was accepted to every one of her reach universities, awarded scholarships and is now on Deans List at a major university. Our youngest has a 4.25 GPA, is involved in sports, activities, AP and accelerated classes. She is challenged, constantly helped by teachers and loves her school. My husband got an engineering degree from Purdue after graduating from RM. What you put into your education is what you get out. This staff and school loves their students and works hard.

column1: Columbine High School. Seriously? The worst High School in the United States. Even inner city schools address their problems and do better than this. Given the quality and intelligence level of the students, this school performs so poorly that it cannot even be rated. It is a negative influence on everything it touches, including your children. Horrible Principal. Worest school I have been too. Staff doesn't care for students. Not recommended for any students. This school has a great staff, lots of extra curricular activities, and many AP classes. The school fosters a sense of community where students care about each other and the school. Great school and a wonderful community! The "family" feeling at Columbine is like no where else. greatest school i have ever been to. it is better than chatty or dakota is every way. During the toughest 2 years with Covid, the leadership at Columbine prevailed for our students!! Mr. Christy (Principal) is one of the BEST Principals in Colorado. He truly cares about the students. Great sports programs, Honors and AP classes. The teachers are amazing support for our children! It's truly a family atmosphere!! Highly recommend!

column3: My school is the best school in the world and I love the teachers (most of them). I'm so glad I go to this school. It'd be cool if we had a swim team though.. and a pool, or something like that. I'm very impressed with the faculty and student support for each other and the community.

column1: My two eldest children attended this school and graduated in 2008 and 2010. In 2011 we moved out of state and my youngest child attends school in the Illinois Public School System. The main complaints I noticed from my children and parents who I associated with outside of school activities who had children attending, as well as my own observances was the amount of time spent on frivolous subject matter instead of the core subjects and curricula other districts (i.e. Oakland County) teaches. The school has state of the art athletic facilities on the outside, but lackluster classrooms and learning materials on the inside. Many of the teachers I noticed were still trying to live high school over again. Both my children attend(ed) public universities the fall after graduating and both complained how they were ill prepared for college. The administration is stern and efficient but many of the younger staff especially in the social studies and english fields and elective staff was to absorbed with their own needs and the desire to relive high school. Trickery on multiple choice is not learning. Many students of Carlson are typical products of their Downriver environment. For the past 7 years I have been a science teacher at Carlson High School teaching Chemistry, Biology, Physics, Forensic Science and Math. I have also been the Science Tutor for the high school's "Study Table Program" for any student needing help understanding their science homework. After having taught at other schools in the area, I can honestly say that Carlson High School does a wonderful job providing students with great academic, extracurricular, and sports opportunities. In my own science classes I always emphasize the importance of learning science concepts in order to be able to succeed in scientific and medical fields in college. As a former Medical Technologist, I often point out various concepts that they learn in class and how it relates to my former career and to the careers of my husband, two daughters, and son-in-law. (Chemist, Doctorate of Pharmacy, Nurse Practitioner, and Mechanical Engineer). I emphasize "College and Career Readiness" in all of my classes. Carlson High School's administration emphasizes self-discipline and good behavior in all students so that students can learn effectively. The school puts more weight in sports rather then a education! An eye sore of a multi million dollar football stadium that out does one a ferris state university.( they cant even up keep) it seems like they are trying to be another grosse ile....without the $$$! I withdrew my son from school on a friday and enrolled him back in florida..... The school in florida sent 4 faxes and 3 voice messages with no reply after 3 days i had to call the school to put a fire under the office to fax info to Florida. I found out after speeking administrators i found out that the HS decided not to replace a counseling Secretary but to keep one in the athletic office I guess the athlectic director is more important then the students!!! If you are looking to move here for the schools..... Look elsewhere!! Grosse ile or Trenton would be my suggestion!!! Fewer options and opportunities. They keep asking parents for more money and delivering less service. We have a lot of really great students here at Carlson. Students are nice, and we have a great school climate and atmosphere. At CHS, we have a program called PBIS, for Positive Behavior Intervention Systems, that promotes positive behavior and comradery among students. The program has many parts, but for one part we have our "Marauder Captains," who are some of our best juniors and seniors, and they mentor the incoming freshman and incoming students. Since we have started the program, I have seen a positive difference in the school atmosphere and student behavior. I really enjoy teaching here and being a part of the school community. My daughter is a student at Carlson and is bullied. The school is not doing enough to handle the situation. The girl was suspended, but continues to intimidate my daughter. I would not recommend sending your children here. I feel that enrollment numbers are too high and the children suffer, the taxes here are high as well and the district is not doing well financially. Excellent. We wouldn't send our children anywhere else. my friends and i get bullied and called slurs constantly, and the school does nothing about it. my health teacher also said autism is caused by vaccines. do better, carlson.

column3: I am currently a junior on the Dean's List at Penn State, and I graduated PTHS in 2008. My success in getting to college and succeeding there is in no way a reflection of my education at Pemberton. To put it simply, Pemberton is a failing school. The teachers are qualified, but the administration only caters to disciplinary issues. There are no incentive programs for high-performing teachers, office staff/counseling/scheduling services are substandard, and students are not adequately prepared to succeed at a 4-year university. Violence has become a widespread problem, due to laughable security staff and unstructured free time in and out of the classroom. Extracurricular activities are mediocre at best. If I was planning on my child going to college, I would NOT send them to Pemberton. As a graduate of Pemberton Township High School, I get irritated when I hear people bash this school. I received an excellent education there from some very outstanding teachers. Also, the ethnic and socioeconomic diversity of the school ensured that I was able to relate to and work with people from all walks of life. Education is a team sport...you have to get out on the field and get involved if you want to succeed. I find that the people who do the most complaining about the school are those that sit on the sideline (or in the penalty box) and expect the education to be handed to them. Those of us who applied ourselves, got involved with clubs and sports, and took advantage of eveything this school had to offer, went on to great colleges and careers. When we moved to McGuire we were told we had a choice of 2 high schools. I chose Pemberton because they were the school that had a JROTC program. After a few months I realized that what they didn t tell us was they also have a gang problem. I tried to get my child moved to the other school when I learned she was being bullied by some of these gang members. I was told the 2 schools and the base had an agreement that once a child had started in one school they could not switch to the other. She should not have to be afraid to go to school every day. What kind of education is she really receiving? There are fights of a weekly basis. I would not recommend any other military families putting their children in this school. Okay let's be serious for a moment. Why would anyone want their child going to this school when Northern Burlington is right around the corner. We moved to Ft Dix a year ago and the first this we were told was "it would be wise to not send your kids to PTHS." This was told to me by many high ranking military members and military spouses. Even though I was thankful for the advice I still rather of seen for myself. I visited both schools and I couldn't find one thing that PTHS was better then NB at. I did find it very odd that at PTHS that the kids seemed to never be in the classrooms. There were many occourances where I saw students running down the hallways yelling and screaming while class was in session and the main response I got from the faculty was "Oh that just one of the Special Ed kids. Continued I have 3 teenagers and all of them have played for Sumter HS in SC. They had some of the best sports teams in the state and one of the best football teams in the country. We went to watch 1 PTHS football game and my sons and husband all agreed that their was no way that they were going to play on that team. They now play for NB and they couldn't be more happier but we do find it weird that half the team is from Brownsmills and most of these kids are not affiliated with the military in any way. The one good thing that PTHS did have over NB was that the class sizes were not as big. NB is becoming more and more overcrowded by the day. Now like I said my kids go to NB so I can't pass full judgement on this school but you have to think that there is something to why the military tells its members to go to NB over PTHS, the sports teams and clubs are filled with students that are from the Pemberton district but have no military affiliation and why the teachers and staff at NB tell the students that if you get kicked out your going to PTHS. Pemberton Twp. High School offers a multicultural and diverse learning environment. Students can participate in any sport you can think of and the high school keeps students involved with extra curricular activities and clubs. PTHS has dedicated teachers who help students achieve both academic and social success. There are honor courses and AP courses offered as well as up to date technological devices used within the classrooms. Transportation is provided for all after school activities and sports and we do not pay to play sports in our township. I am a graduate of PTHS and my daughters have graduated recently with much success. I was an okay student (3.0 gpa) but was always well mannered and shy. However, I was pushed and ran into in the halls every year. I was harassed and tormented by certain students asking for money. I was so alone and felt unsafe. Teachers witnessed students run through the halls and swearing but never said a word. These students were untouchable. I am almost 30 now and have 2 bachelors degrees and several professional licenses - no thanks to my education or experiences from PTHS! PLEASE READ!!! We are now stationed at Dover AFB and let me be the first to tell you. Military does not send there kids to this school anymore they send them to Northern. Heck those that are not military that live in the district that have a fully functional brain don't send their kids to this school. My daughter said all she did in class was listen to music on her IPhone and as long as she was quiet they gave her an A. The only kids that go to this school are those that just got out of jail or got kicked out of everywhere else. Awful school, god-awful area. You can t help but feel sorry for the teachers that work here. My daughter came home complaining that she is unable to hear the teacher teach because the other students in class are loud, disruptive and basically act like complete animals. I contacted the teacher and the response she gave me was I do apologize but all I can do is write the students up but past that there is nothing we can do You have got to be kidding me! So basically I was told the students can do whatever they want and there are no consequences? Yep that's what their showing the students and telling the parents. Who and how are they running this mad house. Out of all the bases I ve been to this has to the most ridiculous anything thing goes schools I have dealt with. I am proud to say I am now in the process of sending my child to Northern. Do yourself a favor instead of sending your child here, just send them to you local zoo. At least at a zoo they ll learn something. Although if you are into the gang scene, pregnant teenagers and fist fights you ll love this place. How is it possible a school could fall so far? This school is now known as the place you go to if you screw up everywhere else because they take anybody and kick out nobody. I am a Pemberton grad and I really wanted my children to follow in my footsteps but at the same time I have to do what's best for my children. My advice to all parents is if you know someone that lives in the Northern Burlington district ask them if you can use their address. It's as easy as that. I really have no idea how Pemberton is still open. I live in Browns mills and everyone that lives in my area attends NB. Put it this way when the military openly speaks bad about this school in their base paper and online you know this school is in bad shape. I do advise those that are from Browns mills that decide to pull their children from or not attend PTHS for NB do know that the community is starting to create a somewhat resistance because of the overcrowding. Now also know NB is a choice school, so even if you already attend PTHS you can still transfer. The process is not that hard. My son plays on the baseball team and all but 3 of his teammates are from Browns Mills and they all utilized choice. I had three kids graduate from this school. They loved this school and visit old teachers when they have a chance since their sister attends the school now. I am a teacher in another district and I can tell you that this school is much better than most I have seen throughout the state. Improvement is needed in regards to guidance of the students to post secondary education. I would also like to see improvement when it comes to indoor graduation exercises. Graduated from Pemberton and I did well in collage both undergraduate and graduate. Yes that is right I have my Masters degree in education and I graduated from Pemberton. Your education is what you make of it! Go hornets!!! My school is a diamond in the rough. The schools gets a bad reputation, but PTHS offers everything you need to prepare for college or a career. When we first moved to Browns Mills in 2006, we heard that PTHS was a school. By the time my eldest son got to 9th grade, I was PLEASANTLY SURPRISED!! We attended the freshman orientation and learned about all the efforts to turn the school around from its bad reputation. The school has so many opportunities for children to learn and succeed! Unfortunately, after my son's freshman year, the military moved us to Little Rock AFB, AR. Let me tell you... there isn't a day that goes by that I painfully regret asking for a transfer! The schools down here make my son look like a genius! My son was in all honors and the A-STEM (Aeronautics - Science Technology Engineering & Mathematics) program and finished his only year at PTHS as #1 in his class with a 5.44 GPA. PTHS is a phenomenal school and we are seriously considering having my wife bring the kids back to NJ for school while I finish my last few years in the Air Force in Arkansas. <cue banjos> Pemberton High School has been my second home since 1979. Speaking specifically about my area, Choral Music, .I am proud to say that our Choral music program is on par if not superior to a great many school districts in the state. Our students perform a wide variety of quality repertoire, participate in curricular and extra curricular select vocal ensembles, as well as regional and All State Chorus. They are taught music literacy , musicianship, vocal technique and critical thinking skills, to name a few...a wide variety of teaching techniques are used . Not only does our district offer a wide variety of extra curricular activities for our students to choose from but they provide late afternoon transportation home twice each day for clubs first and then sports. I have had more students than I can count receive advanced degrees.Our school climate is diverse. The bulk of the reviews here are written by people that did not send their children to our school. Our faculty members and staff are dedicated, long term professionals who work tirelessly to educate their students. This is a school that is under appreciated and has so much to offer. The Cross Country program is a joke..the students lacked the discipline to follow the coach's direction, while training and during meets, plus they still got to participate in the events. This school has a few staff members that genuinely care about their students and giving a quality education however, it's in dire need of new leadership as things have been too bad for too long. If you ask any decent student or staff member they'll tell you just how exhausting it is to be getting the short end of the stick from the administration AND by rowdy, unmotivated students. It would usually be fine if you got into AP however, in recent years they'll throw anyone in there so now it's just as bad as being in a standard class, with all the constant disruptions and outbursts. I really tried to make the most out of my time here, truly I did but now that graduation is on the horizon all I can say is that I'm happy to just leave. This being said to any potential parents reading this, if you can do better DO IT it's worth it, and to any other students, all I can say is stick in there. Our Son graduated top of His Class at Pemberton Twp High School. He graduated one year early and went on to Rowan University and Finished with a Masters Degree in Science at the age of 20. He currently works for Lockheed Martin. If it wasn't for the Education that He received at Pemberton Township High School he wouldn't be where He is today. He study in the STEM program that prepared HIm for His future. We can not say enough good about our experience with PTHS.

column1: Mr. Edmonds was great and the new President/Principal seems prepared to take Pallotti to the next level in every area. I have always loved the family I found at Pallotti and knew that my children were getting a great education, now I believe others will see our school in the same light. I have found that Pallotti is a great place for a teenager to grow into a responsible adult. Pallotti is a great school and investment! The use of technology is very helpful and would definitely recommend it to any interested family!!!! Great school, but not so great choices in Leaders. It's unfortunate the school can not find a decent principal to run the school. Great faculty and campus ministry program! Pallotti is a really good school. Teachers are very nice, so are students. It creates a lot of opportunities for students. I STRONGLY recommend parents to send their kids to this school Poor leadership and communication strategies on all levels. Their school fees border on the ridiculous. Great disappointment in classroom behavior - it is a huge sore thumb that a vast majority of students disrespect the teachers constantly and the teachers do little to stop this behavior. Inconsistent rules and regs, no consequences for those constantly breaking the rules. Physically, most of the school is falling apart-although the newer part is such as the gym. lunch room and main entrance offices are "newer"--the rest of the school is poorly maintained-bathroom sinks are from the 50s. Poor emphasis on academics it appears that only sports is king here. Colloquial student body and staff does not make a good learning environment for all students. They embrace all cultures and religions which is good thing, but rarely do you see students embrace each other's differences--very cliquey groups. My son recently graduated from this school and my feelings are somewhat mixed. He attended another denominational private school from kindergarten to middle school and had an excellent sojourn. I wanted him to have a different experience and more exposure so when he picked Pallotti I was happy. His first year was a nightmare. After two months he begged me to take him back to the prior private school system. I didn’t, because I realized that the issue was with the kids attending Pallotti and discipline, not the teachers or the contents of the curricula. I spoke to the student director and was able to convince him to stay. In my child’s case, he wasn’t around certain behaviors and I believed that he needed to know how to navigate difficult situations now rather than later. I also believed that the teachers at Pallotti are Good teachers and do their best. Covid came and changed everything, however, Pallotti and it’s administration and faculty handled teaching through the pandemic like champs. I was impressed. On returning to school, the atmosphere was different. I think the school has made conscious decisions to up their admittance procedure so that the quality of students now attending and behaviors have improved. Per my son, there are less behavioral issues and I can see the difference. I personally think my son’s batch was the worse. Overall, I believe Pallotti is a great school and if discipline is made a serious objective the school will see students do wonders. I would definitely recommend this school.

column3: the school is so competitive the teachers expect you to learn everything on your own we might as well have robots being our teachers because all they do is watch you learn. I personally was a good student in the middle school mostly straight a's and i was on honor roll every marking period now i have c's in the two honors classes because those are the worst teacher in the hardest class.i think the teachers should all be evaluated by the students so the administrators can realize who are the good teachers and who should be let go, because there are some very talented and truly good teachers who deserve to be recognized. We moved to Bridgewater in 1992 so our children could go to a top rated school system where my husband went to school. It was the biggest mistake we could have made. We have an LD child. There is no understanding of no child left behind. They left my son behind. I had 2 children go through this school experience. It is too big, too unsupportive to children and staff. The guidance staff is great, but overwhelmed because the admin doesn't support them. It is not about the students and some of the deans border on being bullies themselves. The transition for a student coming from another high school is extremely difficult. The expectation is that the student be "independent." The school is full of cliques and it is difficult to be accepted. The services for students lagging behind in anything means there is something "wrong" with the student and services are limited. It caters only to the the top students. There is nothing innovative going on for the average student, only things that look good on paper. This school is about public image, not creation of a hardy, healthy school environment that fosters creativity, healthy peer relationships and bringing out the best in students. If your child is "average" or too creative, forget about this school. Your children will be miserable. Many of the teachers are knowledgeable about their content subject but have no backbone in representing the student. Many fear the administration. I currently attend this school, and I like it, I don't love it nor do I hate it. I feel that this school is too overpopulated and thus everything is super competitive. There is a wide variety of classes for students to take, but some teachers aren't working to their potential. Overall, it's an OKAY school. My school is next door and a great school. I have no children in school but I enjoy seeing and hearing the students practicing for sports activities or band or jogging or running by. The students here seem happy and involved. Although my husband and I have no school age kids we will be Panther supporters going to the first football game this Thursday. Go Panthers! i hate this school too many people teachers do not teach well AT ALL so much work i dont understand dont even get me started on the layout when it rains, you better have a rain jacket hate my highschool experiance so far only good thing i can say is they have many clubs and activities for everyone BRHS kinda sucks because of how its a huge open campus. When its really cold and/or raining you better have a jacket or your screwed. Some teachers are mean but most of them are really nice. There are a lot of kids here so it should be easy to have at least have one friend. There are also a lot of clubs and sports but its sort of hard to get into some sports because of how many kids there are. But even though this school isn't always that great, I love this school. After getting used to the flow of things, it got easier. There are a lot of nice people here but it is sometimes hard to find them. But when you do find that group of people that you become friends with, everything will get much better. I am pretty happy to spend 2 more years here. One of the better schools you can find. Just remember that this schools is for students that are willing to put efforts for their future. Teachers will always help you if you ask, they are willing to stay after school for help. The teachers will not spoon feed you. There are tons of extracurricular activity, you will find something that suits you.At BRHS they take security really seriously they have security checking people for IDs. Great school. Good programs including AP courses. Good teachers. Large selection of after-school activities and sports. Mostly good kids. However some disobedient kids need to be disciplined. Smoking on school campus is unacceptable. This punk kid Jerry Vogel was seen smoking cigarettes next to the cafeteria building everyday. The school needs to take strict actions on this kind of behavior. I currently go to BRHS, let me just say that it’s a very competitive school both in athletics and academics. I am an athlete. I play soccer but sadly the coach has his favorites due to the type of soccer clubs you play for. There are so many talented athletes on the team that NEVER see the field. It can be pretty harsh at times as well. Going into academics, in my opinion sometimes the teachers give “busy” work just to put assignments in the grade book. It bothers me alot because why am i wasting my time on busy work when i can be doing other assignments. There is a great program for upperclassmen called “Teachers Aide”. At first I didn’t get in only because my GPA was just below the minimum. My dad called and asked why GPA’s are required and they said to him, “its about responsibility” a GPA is not about responsibility. I juggle a job, school work, soccer and my own personal life and they have the audacity to say that im irresponsible. That is not okay to assume that. Now to the teachers, some teachers are GREAT! You’ll actually learn stuff but a large handful of other teachers will pile work on top of work for you to do. Socially, the amount of fights are ridiculous, vaping is out of control and there are many incidents just all around. All in all, people have good experiences other people have awful experiences at bridgewater. You just better hope to get the right teachers then you’ll be okay. The campus is terribly designed for New Jersey. It's a very wide open campus, with outdoor walking required for every class. When it rains, you're pretty much out of luck when walking to a specific building. The guidance department at this school has also got to be one of the worst ones in the state. In the 2019-2020 academic school year, the schedules were sent out much later than normal to prevent mistakes. What ended up happening was that many students ended up having to set up appointments with their guidance counselors to fix the schedules. Some students emailed their counselors since the start of summer to set up teaching aide positions or work positions for their schedules, and are now finding out that they can't change their schedule until the start of the year, making their prospects grim. I strongly suggest going to another school if you can. Graduated last year and overall I had a pretty positive experience. There’s a large variety of clubs, sports, and electives available to students and all my teachers were amazing. Administration made sure we weren’t given too much homework, but at the same time, there was still a competitive atmosphere. The school lunch was also very good. Enjoyed pasta with at least one side (roasted potatoes, seasoned string beans, broccoli, etc) on the daily. However the school is definitely on the large side, so some might not like that.

column1: I am a student here at Y-C, and i love it here. I moved here in 6th grade and since then i have met my best friends that i wouldnot trade for the world YCHS is a joke. I skipped school every single day and they still gave me my diploma a year early. The staff doesn't know how and doesn't discipline you for anything. Not to mention staff picks favorites so if you're on a teachers good side nothing will happen to you. Our textbooks are atleast 10 years old or more and our curriculum is the same. The administration is the worst. The principal is a cool guy but then we have the absolutely unhelpful in any way counselors who actually make things worse and the vice-principal and dean of students who could care less about any of the people who go there. If you send your child here you can guarantee that they will go nowhere in life. All of the graduates from this high school may seem promising for a small school until they hit the real world. No one will do anything to change the world and will fade out and die just like the hopes and dreams of everyone who lives in the area. This school is a mess! I just recently graduated from here and I'm so glad I have this giant catastrophe of inefficiency behind me. It takes forever to do anything and the administration and counselors (the counselors are the absolute worst) do nothing to help you. Toward the end of senior year everyone I know was getting called down to their office and coming back angry. The teachers are ridiculous, there are a few good ones here and there but mainly its a bunch of ridiculous, unprofessional nut-jobs or barely licensed amateurs who have no idea how to teach.They also pick favorites which is really aggravating if you aren't on their good side. The school is also falling apart! It looks nice when you drive by the front , but head inside or around the back and you'll see a school that hasn't been remodeled or maintained for decades - the heating system doesn't even work half the time and I don't think there even IS a cooling system. If you send your child here you are setting them up for failure because the counselors and teachers do absolutely nothing to help you get into college, they are pretty much on their own, earning a mediocre education at a school that isn't even worth it. YCHS is an absolute joke. Don't send your children here unless you want them to be woefully unprepared throughout life. Pay a little out of pocket, and send them to Mac or to Gaston. It will be worth it in the long run for your child's education. Teachers take FOREVER in addressing kids concerns or helping them....forever, as in, months. Teachers are highly unapproachable. The discrimination that is allowed between students is appalling.

column3: i was a student at this school and personally it was one of the best schools that i ever went to!!! I love the studenst, teachers, and staff. everyone is nice and as long as you stay out of it you dont have drama personaly i had barrly any drama. yes, there is inappopriate language but every highschool will have it no crimes! I went to a lot of different schools, but this one was the best one I ever went to. The teachers were always helpful, the students were usually nice, and the extra requirements from teachers and principals for the students always made me push myself harder and exceed my own expectations. The counselors helped me through so many hard times. The entire faculty is just so strong at that school. I am so proud to say that I graduated from Truman High School in 2011. I graduated from Truman in 2013, and it is an excellent school. I attended three different high schools in the Metro area, Park Hill South being one of them, and they are no where close to Truman as a whole. The teachers are caring and supportive, and contrary to what others have said you don't have to act up to get attention. I loved everything about this school and I am so proud to be a Patriot alumni! Disgraceful management. In a world where there is a lot of horrible things happening they are adding to it instead of properly dealing with it Good school. Excellent staff. Highly recommend Truman! the schools and the district as a whole is completely racist. the environment is disgusting, there are a lot of bugs as well. Hate this school, my cousin gets bullied and no one does anything about it she had to transfer schools and go virtual for Van Horn From the halls of Truman, you'll hear children crying from their bodies being contorted and their bones being crushed. Nobody can move throughout the hallways without slow walkers, yelling people, and a stupidly congested T. The school used to be a middle school. It's not meant for all of these people. The curriculum is terribly average, and there is at least one fight every day. For me, the choir team has been the only positive experience, community and whole.

column1: I'm a student at this school. I love it! The teachers are very nice and helpful. If you're struggling on homework or what you might be learning in that class, they'll take off their lunch time for you. Or there is also a club where they help you on homework or if you're struggling in math. They have amazing clubs for you to join. This is a really good school! I highly recommend it. I love this school. It is a diamond in the rough with wonderfully caring teachers - who actually call to check on your son/daughter if they are sick. The staff - especially Ms Hershfang - is caring, supportive and LISTENS. My son has enjoyed his 4 years at LVHS and I'd recommend this school in a heartbeat. Go for the AP classes if possible. The school has been trying to improve its reputation ever since the new principal has taken the lead. BUT the student body itself HAS NOT been improved which might surprise others. Want proof? Well, when I graduated, we had a surprise guest: the CEO of CPS, Forrest Claypool who visited only our high school out of all CPS because apparently Lake View had the highest graduation year. That might sound like a good thing, right? Not if you knew that student who didn't meet the graduation requirements STILL graduated.Another example, recently a kid with autism was physically bullied by another student... more specifically FLIPPED sending the kid with autism to the hospital. Yup. Lake View High School DOES NOT address the issue of bullying. Oh... Forgot to tell you! A classmate of mine had brought a taser to school and was playing around with it in class. I approached the deans with the issue and it was never addressed.Yes, they might have a great STEM program and other great opportunities like College Possible, etc but trust me, IT IS NOT WORTH putting your child through what he/she sees at Lake View. 0/10... transferring. Your child will not get accepted into a good college if they attend this high school, I have a child at LVHS who graduated in 2021 and another child who will graduate in 2022. My kids' experience at LVHS has been excellent. They have been provided with challenging academic classes including many AP and Honors choices. The teachers at LVHS have been outstanding. They truly care about their students and provide feedback to parents on a regular basis, which is not the norm in high school. LVHS fosters an environment and culture that embraces diversity, respect and individuality. Both of my children have been provided with opportunity to play Varsity sports and get involved with a number of other extracurricular activities. The smaller size of LVHS provides more opportunity for students to stand out and chart their own path. For students who want to pursue a 4-year college degree, LVHS will prepare them to do so! My son graduated in 2021 and was accepted into multiple universities including University of Illinois, University of Michigan, University of Wisconsin and University of Miami. LVHS is a neighborhood high school that offers a great learning environment, supportive culture and many opportunities for its students. We never imagined high school teachers being so connected to the kids throughout all 4 years. At first we were nervous not to have "tracks" for kids before they go there, like many Selective Enrollments or IB schools do. But we are so grateful it is purposefully not this way right up front. Our 2 students at LVHS are creating their own tracks with their teachers as they go, and building on things they discover they love. We're seeing this with 2 students with 2 different interests. The kids learn study skills and leadership skills that are setting them up for college success. The parent community is welcoming, with options to jump in and do one thing, just meet and not commit. It's been amazing to meet people with the same values and mindset from all over the city. So grateful to have found a fabulous music/arts and stem program in our neighborhood!
