column3: The school is very crowded; the hall traffic is problematic. Office staff is very irritated all the time. They pretty much forget you exist after about a second. Drug are very prevalent. Smoking is an issue. The people are often not very nice. Violence is high, particularly in the freshman class. Dropouts and class cutting are rampant. I hear about expulsion a lot. Heavy favoritism is played. I've never met a student who wasn't dissatisfied. Most of my teachers are good people and understand an have passion for their subject but are quite lousy at reiterating it to students. Overall, Edison high is unpleasant but not unbearable. High school sucks in general but I have to admit that Edison High School was the worst four years of my life. I was terribly depressed throughout my entire high school career because of it. First of all, it is way too overcrowded, there were too many fights, and the staff picked favorites. You basically feel like nobody cares about you. In all my four years, no one staff member was ever friendly or polite to me, they spent all their time focusing on the bad kids and the kiss ups. I felt like you couldn't even look at someone in the wrong way or you'd get attacked/ accused of something. I'm glad it's over but I have to admit it was an experience. If anything, it was a struggle at best. My high school has a very excellent educational program for our students. They has the up to date technology for student to learn. Edison High School from the teacher right up to the principal are very bad communicators. All they care about is their Pay Checks. The teachers give very liitle extra help to their student that very much need the help. This school and the teacher need pick it up in every Category you can think of as educators. Not the best high school out there, but it is definitely improving. It has a good learning environment and immense diversity of students. The teachers are understanding and cooperative, but other staff are often rude. The school provides a huge amount of facilities and is technologically advanced. Overall, a decent high school to study in. very successful school in a perfect neighborhood in the prestigious north edison school district. builds great caracter in students and offers great education in a competitive environment. I think EHS is typical of a NJ high school. My daughter graduated from EHS in 2008 with honors. On the other hand, I sent my son to St. Joe's because I felt that he would fall through the cracks at EHS. My children are 2 very different personalities...my daughter would be a professional student if that were possible and my son would not bother to go to class if that were possible.The point is that all kids have different needs, and with the overcrowding and diversity, I don't believe that the teachers have the ability to meet those needs. Edison school is a horrible horrible school for special needs and education. MLK in particular is the worst. They place higher functioning students who are verbal and talk in sentences with completely non verbal students have way to include them. My friends whose kids have special needs of all kinds have either left the school district in disgust, or home-schooled or filed a case against them or left the town. Christopher Conklin only cares about school and money and not about the special kids. The whole child study team is a fake. There is a support group in NJ that hates this school and is dissuading parents from joining this school. Please improve your moral ethnics and dont play with the life of children. Disgusting school district !! The worst school I've ever attended in my life. As a student in this school, I tried a lot of things in this school. They have a good education and also they have kind teachers. I don't know why would you say this school is bad. Edison High School's principal is kind and he is also energized. While I am learning here, there is no bully here ( what a surprise ). I know my words are kind of the same with bots ( because I am an ESL student ) but I am learning in this school and I promised you this school is good. ;) This school is very usual, and ordinary in every way. However as a student the teachers, although nice, some of them don't care if you pass or fail. A friend of mine stated that his teachers said he hated his job. For anyone coming in, work hard, because some of the teacher's won't care if you pass the class or straight up fail. I am an alumni of Edison High School, teachers and leadership really care about their students. High school isn't going to be easy, students succeed with determination and dedication. I'm proud to have graduated from EHS.

column1: Bad experiences! Unimpressed all around... teachers, students, academics, and school spirit/pride alike. The clubs as well are extremely hard to be accepted into. Kids are very "cliquey". The parents and students that attend the sports events are a rude, disrespectful bunch. It just show the classlessness of the people that attend Fossil Ridge. I even had a Fossil parent come to me after a basketball game and apologize for the rude parents and students that night. The reputation Fossil has gained isn't a good one. If you care about the important things in life such as sportsmanship, respect, integrity and character there are better high schools in Fort Collins to look at. Oustanding! I am a freshman here at Fossil ridge and i am really looking forward to the next four years. There are many things at fossil that really impressed me. For one, many athletic programs had a no cut policy which means that everyone makes it and we were undefeated all season. The academic programs such as the advanced placement programs and STEM Academy are amazing and really prepare you for higher levels of education. The advisory program is also a gift because it helps you in life and school. Anyone which says that fossil isnt a great school, I dont know what they are thinking I have to admit, I was wary when my daughter started here in her Junior year. She was coming from a small school, so I was worried she would get lost in the shuffle or fall in with the "wrong crowd." No school is perfect. Trouble can be found anywhere. The good thing is--there is less trouble to be found, so the odds are in your child's favor. She has excelled and has nothing but good to say about her teachers. When she first started, she had no intention of going to college. Her former school had burned her out. Here, she has thrived and, with great influences, will be starting college in the fall. Fossil has strong academics--probably the best in Fort Collins--plus great sports and music/band programs. Thank you, FRHS, for making the transition a positive one! I am currently a freshman at Fossil Ridge High School, and I can safely say that this is one of the best school's in the country. I have been moving schools my entire life, and have had many experiences at different schools. When I first came to this school, I was pleasantly surprised to find what a great school it was. The school had outstanding academics, some of the best sports teams in the state, and great school spirit. The highly qualified teachers are loved by the students and are ready to help every student. The environment is good also; there are almost no cliques, everyone is welcome, and no student is left out in anything. I have never felt more at home at a high school. We've been happy with Fossil, but are very disappointed with a change in policies with the new administration for the 2013-14 school year. We've made choices for our children over the years based upon what was best for them as well as representations that were made by administrators at the schools we were choosing. As recently as last year, we were assured that school of choice would not be a problem for siblings of current students. We have verified every year on this and always been assured that our younger child would have no problem being accepted at the school her sibling attends and where her fellow students from middle school will be going (Fossil). Now, we've been told by the new principal that NO new choice students will be accepted for the next few years and that our family, and others, will need to have students at multiple high schools since they will not take our incoming students next year. I am a freshman at Fossil Ridge High School and I am always feeling accepted within any group. With any school comes bullying and drug use but I think Fossil Ridge High school was the right choice for me and for any incoming student. Fossil does a very good job limiting the bullying and drugs. All around a very good school. This is my senior year of high school at Fossil Ridge High School and I have spent all four years here. I absolutely love being a part of this school- its a great environment! I have so many friends that have transferred from other schools around here to Fossil and I have heard nothing but great things about their decision to transfer to our school. One of my friends, (who transferred from another school to Fossil last year) told me just yesterday that, "People at Fossil actually pay attention in class and are nice." Of course no school will be perfect, but I am very impressed with this school. I feel safe and have learned a lot! Awful experience, unprofessional staff and all administrators abuse their authority in order to make it easy for themselves. They will not help you if you beg for it. The procedures are exagerated and irrational. 0 out of 5 stars This school disgusts me. Most of the teachers are rude and the students are only prideful in their parents wealth. Disrespect is shown from every body of the school (admin, teachers, students) Coming from Kinard we expected the same guidelines and help from the staff. We didn't receive any at all my son is struggling so hard wih grades and communication with his teachers. I send emails to his teachers that get no replies or very few words if any. This school lax and discipline when it comes to skipping class. And they do not watch over the freshman students leaving the school. This school is highly populated and has too many kids for as few staff members to watch over. I am a student Fossil Ridge that will be graduating soon. And having been at Fossil for the last 4 years, I can easily say that this is a good school, compaired to some of the other schools in the Poudre School District. I have known MANY students who have transferred to Fossil from Fort Collins High School and they have all told me that it is such a better school & are glad they transferred. That being said, even though its a "good" school, it is not & never will be a "perfect" school. No school can be. I find it lacks the support & involvement of the administration team & Principle...but at the end of the day, thats not what I go home and think about. I think about all the amazing friends I've made here at Fossil (and trust me, not everyone here is a stuck up rich kid!), along with finding my passion & future career path. Im glad I stayed with Fossil for all these years, because its halls are filled with the kindest & most caring students AND staff, which not many schools can say for themselves. I love you Fossil & will miss you <3 -Grad of 2014 Fossil Ridge High School was a disappointing experience for our family. Our experience over the past four years has included a disproportionate share of inexperienced, bored teachers who assign a lot of busywork to make up for a lack of real teaching,, a band teacher with a giant ego interested who is only in winning competitions and not in teaching, and a principal who wants to be friends with his staff and has trouble holding them accountable. Our children received a substandard education. Wish we had enrolled them at Rocky Mountain High School. I have had two children attend FRHS, and my third will be going elsewhere. Both of my children have had mediocre experiences at best. Other than a couple of great teachers, the staff is unmotivated and uninspiring. Lots of movies are watched in class. Very little interest in encouraging individual students to find their passion and develop their strengths. There are a few amazing teachers (I can count them on one hand), but most are ho-hum. A few students receive the majority of the attention. Availability of staff to students and parents is poor. Several teachers find it necessary to prove they are smarter than the students by testing them over material that was not covered. They then think it is funny when the class average is a D. The philosophy of most of the math department is that the students should teach themselves. New administration leaves much to be desired. Lots of head nodding and smiling, but no real action. FRHS should be an awesome school, but it is not at this time. First off, I'd like to say you should read the student reviews of this school. I see that a lot of parents complain about this school but the kids love it. I went to Fossil all four years and absolutely loved it. I would do it all over again because I grew so much there and was so prepared for college. The school is completely student-focused. I could contact any of my teachers anytime and they would meet my needs. The teachers were also great at teaching the kids to have a great work ethic as well as good character. The school not only teaches the required courses that all high school students must take, but they also teach many classes that allow the students to learn many life skills. These include: cooking, sewing, writing cover letters in applications, and also finance, communication, and research skills. The school is absolutely the best high school in Fort Collins. Now that I'm in college, I can see how the other high schools in Fort Collins did not prepare their students for college nearly as well as Fossil Ridge High School. I am proud and humbled to say that I was part of Fossil Ridge High School. Just left FRHS and I can honestly say the education declined year after year while I was there. To begin with, it was a much better school with better staff overall but as time went on things only got worse. Teachers definitely got lazier and most now follow a "student should learn on their own" approach whenever possible, and many in the school can't be communicated with and many are often very bad in terms of providing help. A few good staff members here and there but for the most part, bad teachers. Can't speak to the new principal because I only saw the result for one year and considering it had already declined in past years, it wasn't a surprise. The administration overall however wasn't very helpful nor nice throughout my years, and definitely encourages self learning. Student body is definitely wealth oriented and there is no doubt the school and ridiculous fees no other school would charge revolve around it. Test scores are high, but after my experience I have to wonder if that's just the result of smart and rich kids, or a mediocre staff. Overall, I can't say it's "worse" than other schools, but there is much to be improved. I was concerned to read the negative reviews, but I have seen, so far, that the students are able to learn, and learn well, if they are motivated. This is no longer K-8, nor should it be, but rather a bridge between K-8 and college. My child has had excellent teachers and encouragement to learn. It is similar to most aspects of life--you get out what you invest, plus more. I have seen hardworking, caring teachers who teach the classes, offer assistance as needed and evaluate student performance in a timely manner. I have seen teachers that care about their students' success. Finally, we have witnessed great education for our child, which will, if it continues, will prepare her for an excellent future. Thank you, Fossil teachers and staff! Fossil Ridge is great. They offer a lot of after school and before school programs. They also have plenty of electives that can suit any person. I am happy with all most all of the teachers. We have a very good Marching Band, Science Olympiad, Knowledge Bowl, and good sports teams. I think that this is a great high school. Overall, this school is ok. The administration and counseling departments are mediocre-acting on a "take initiative for yourself and we are not going to help you" approach; especially the counseling department who I think get so overwhelmed that they don't want to help. However in the past few years, I have always felt helped by the counseling department, just not this year. A lot of the staff is also extremely horrible at teaching, which most of the administration fails to notice. I've had a lot of great teachers that had to be let go, and a lot of permanent teachers that are horrible. I think the administration should take into consideration what the students think about the teachers, vs what they think they know about them. To give fossil credit, I have had a lot of great teachers and a lot of the clubs and sports are really good, I just think that fossil has been going downhill since I arrived a couple years ago. The issue with FRHS is really an issue of leadership. Prior leadership understood the needs of a top grade high school in Colorado. Current leadership doesn't understand the demands, needs or trends. You can't speak directly to an administrator. In fact, they sent an email with the protocol that outlined their desires to not be bothered with concerns from their community. The principal is never visible. One of the Deans is gone all the time -- at Disney World. The AP's just don't seem to care. There seem to be a lot of excuses -- "PSD says we must..." There is very little communication home -- no newsletters, weekly updates and the website is not updated. On the other side: The teachers are incredible -- some of the best in the state. The students are great -- very caring. The curriculum is excellent. A change of leadership and the school would again would be a 10. I am surprised to read negative comments about the leadership at FRHS. As a parent, I have been impressed with the principal, who has increased communication and brought about a sense of school family that was lacking. He greets students each day at the front door - by name. The career center staff bent over backwards to help my senior with college transcripts upon discovering they had her entered twice in the system, once as a senior and again as a sophomore. Both of my daughters are involved in activities, work hard in class and their teachers are truly outstanding. Fossil Ridge is a 5 star high school! Fossil Ridge is a lousy HS. It does not give enough homework in classes that will be used in subsequent HS and college classes. The teachers grade so easily that the student thin they are doing great, but when they take the practice SAT tests the students lack of knowledge will be abundantly clear. This is a fantastic school with great opportunities. I sent three kids through Fossil Rige and one more still attending. There are those that don't take full advantage of the opportunities provided, for them I am sorry. However, those that choose to take part in all that Fossil Ridge has to offer find this school to be among the best. If you can think of a club they have it. The teachers take pride in their school and it shows with the amount of attention and time they are willing to spend on their students. I highly recommend this school for those that want the most out of their children's education. My experience with Fossil has been wonderful. As a senior, I have been able to experience much of what Fossil has to offer. There is an abundance of opportunities for every student and the counseling office is fantastic. Of course some classes/ teachers are stronger and harder than others, but overall the classes are engaged and beneficial. It is up to the student to participate in the many extracurricular activities available and to take a rigorous schedule. Every student decides his/her own high school experience. Very poor academics. Very poor leadership. Extremely liberal teaching and viewpoints pushed by many of the teachers. Teachers are not doing their best and are not held accountable for their ineffectiveness/poor teaching. Also, my kids have seen first hand lots drugs being used within the school. As a former student, I had an awful experience, and I was considered a "normal" student. I was in clubs, performed well academically, and was in sports. I was involved, I did everything right, but I was brown, so was excessively bullied with no help from the administration. I had to watch others like myself, "different," suffer for 4 years at FRHS. Both of my children attended FRHS for four years each. They both absolutely thrived at this school. Academically, they took every opportunity presented with AP courses, special interest areas such as journalism, computer programming, art, robotics, and foreign language. The teachers, with maybe one or two exceptions, were outstanding. They were accessible to my kids. FRHS supports the kids to self advocate for themselves. We found the counselor staff equally excellent and went out of there way to help our kids thrive. The principal, Julie Chaplan is wonderful and involved. I was shocked to see some of the harsh reviews on here. I’ve found FRHS kids to be respectful, polite, and motivated students. As a volunteer, I was always impressed with the caliber of young people I was working with. I’ve watched our robotics team work as a family, truly caring about each other and the color of their skin was never an issue. They were friends and teammates…nothing else mattered. Fossil Ridge HS is a great place to go to school! This school was a terrible experience for me. While I attended this school I was horrendously bullied. I could not walk down a hall without being harassed because of the way that I looked. The forms of harassment I faced were horrible. Every day I was called transphobic slurs, people would threaten to hurt me, people would take photos of me without my consent, and I was constantly laughed at and yelled at. When I attempted to report them to the deans, the only punishment they would face was a small talking to. Because of the way the deans handled it, many students found it fun to harass and bully me. It was so bad that I was forced to leave the school after my first quarter there. I could not attend any after-school event because of how concerned I was for my safety. The teachers would do nothing to help me, and most ignored me when I asked for help. I couldn't sit at the door by any of my classes because people would stand by it and take pictures of me. When it came to the point where I couldn't go a class period without having to make a report of being harassed, my family and I decided to withdraw from the school. Only when I left the school did the school decide to have an assembly about bullying. I would not recommend this school to anyone who is looking for an inclusive environment for their children.

column3: There are some good teachers, but there is a bully problem and a drug problem. Also the cafeteria food is not very good. The bathrooms often are out of soap and paper towels and the floors are not clean. I liked the four-class schedule. Also the track and cross-country program and coaches are very good.

column1: To start off If I I could give the school a zero I would. Although Oakton high seems to be the top rank school in Fairfax county it is way over rated. Oakton gets the high marks due to high AP testing results that have nothing or very little to do with teachers. My experience with teachers has been a average experience there are some good ones that I really liked and some ok ones and some horrible ones that I dont think should have jobs there. I ran across 3 horrible ones in 3 years. The reason for the high AP scores are from tutors that parents higher. I Knew people that had tutoring multiple days a week. I can only imagine that there were some people that had it 5 days or more. Oakton seems to be controlled by money in almost all areas. The people with money can pay for tutoring multiple days a week while the people with little money are left to fending for themselves. Some teachers stay after school regularly and that helps but generally there are multiple students there as well. Some teachers you will have to stay on them for just a little help. It is really hit or miss. I also ran across several cheaters at the school. The students are rich and dont care for anyone but them. Great school. My son is a rising senior and my daughter will enter the school in a year. My son has nothing but great things to say about his teachers, peers and coaches. He gets good grades and the teachers challenge him and he has a lot of homework and exams/quizzes but that's why it's a great school...because the teachers care. Yes, there are a lot of rich families and the school have clicks and as a parent, I don't care for that either. However, there are average families with good kids as well. You just have to look. I've had 4 kids go through Oakton and have been a parent of a student since 2000. Really great school. A few complaints - we hit bad teachers only in math, but consistently one of the kids had a bad math teacher from 2000 - 2011. They dropped Honors classes around 2008 forcing all kids into AP everything or gen ed. Gen ed was ridiculously easy and AP was ridiculously hard so there was no happy medium for the kids. Also lots of emphasis and support of the sports teams but little support for any other student activity. Otherwise, this is a school to be proud of. I'm constantly amazed at how poorly run this school is. Oakton has a reputation for graduating students for some of the finest colleges and universities. However my daughter's teacher scheduled a field trip to NYC that conflicts with SAT testing. Hello, anybody home there?? Apparently no one is responsible for approving this, or they are just incompetent and not checking for conflicts like this. Guess the parents must be amazing to offset incompetence like this. its a poor school now. Parents obviously don't understand anything that is really going on. most teachers are terrible few are tolerable. in each of my years, I have had one teacher I have actually looked forward to seeing and learning. Most teachers just give you filler packets and then slightly alter them and give them to you as homework and then give tests on completely different material Attending from 2008-2012, there was little support for clubs and extra curricular activities, with the majority of which being self funded by students. While money was tight due to the economy. The teachers are okay, there was a good number of engaging faculty members that challenged and worked with the students, however there seemed to always be at least one or two teachers per department who were, in a way, under-performing in their duties as educators. As far as the principal leadership goes, it seems like the principal and his staff members were at a disconnect with the other faculty and the students. The severe lack of personal involvement by the administrators was evident in that they were only present for the handing out of disciplinary action and then putting students on their way instead of trying to seek a reform. The school social structure is divided in two segments. There are two types of students a person can be, with little overlap. AP students hardly mingle with general education students, leading to a system where general students wouldn't seek to challenge themselves, for the fear of entering what would seem like a whole new school. Oakton is an excellent school, but needs work to stay on top against competition from other excellent schools in FCPS. Let's get the bad out of the way first. 1. The principal is totally MIA. I have NEVER seen him at a school event, and my kid has only ever seen him once, at a football game. Being used to other FCPS schools this shocked me, and is a red flag. The principal is like the standard bearer of an army: if they are missing, something is not right. 2. The facility is decrepit. For example, mice in the science labs and mold in the bathrooms (which was only resolved when the students kicked up a stink about it and went public) Now for the good: 3. The teachers are very good. Core subjects taught very well and electives strong too. Too many good ones to name but Sharkoffmadrid was a standout in Art History and Jones was a Latin rock star. I'm told Jones was pushed out and ended up at Flint Hill, which if true would be another strike against the administration: she was Teacher of the Year material. Not bad. Most things at this school are relatively good. The teachers are good, the classes are quite good, and the community and diversity is alright. I have three big complaints though:1. The school facility is tiny and cramped and old. It is up for renovation in a few years, but still, the hallway often fills up with students, slowing down movement in the hallways.2. It seems very clique-y. Although there is a diverse background of students, people don't seem to really talk much outside of their friend group, and this is made worse because most teachers allow groups to be picked during group projects instead of assigning groups.3. This is not as important as the other two, but the cafeteria food is, to put it politely, lacking. The lunches are small and often bland and flavorless, and the textures are kind of weird and squishy a lot of the time. I'd recommend bringing your own lunch. We have found the curriculum to be challenging but they also have good supports in place for those with unique learning needs. Great in some areas, horrible in others. Unfortunately, the horrible will likely affect my child's future success. Oakton is a top notch school all around. The academics, in-school activities, and extracurricular activities are all outstanding. Like every school, it’s not perfect, but its strengths far outweigh its weaknesses, which are still relatively slight when compared to even other top schools in the area. Oakton has long had a policy of molding students into future leaders and productive members of society rather than catering to the whims of parents and kids who want hand holding. Both kids had a great academic and social experiences at OHS. Very involved with sports. Both went on to top VA schools: JMU and VT. Very happy with OHS overall. so nice, I love it, great teachers The Teachers and Staff are very kind and understanding. They offer a large selection class (There's something for everyone). They also offer lots clubs and sports programs. Also the school is newly renovated with lots court yards and a nice cafeteria.

column1: Lake Side High School is a complete joke. I attended school there from K-12. By Lake Side, being the only school in Lake Village it does not leave any choices for anyone to send their children elsewhere. The teachers at Lake Side, are not there to help the students succeed in life or prepare them for the future for after high school. I can count on my hand how many good teachers I have ever seen at Lake Side and that is very few. Half of the teachers where coaches teaching subjects they had no clue about and just passed us alone. The teachers that are placed now are teachers of America, who are just there for pay or get experience behind their belt. Teachers at Lake Side High, will rather see a student in an alternative school or suspended rather than work with the parent on how they could work together to help the child. Lake Side just have employees there for the pay not to help the children get a good education. As parents you all need to have a voice, get involved more, stay at the school as much as possible. Something must be done! its very below average because the kids fight,curse,and bully each other! Some kids have no friends because of those things! Kids like Ya'ryah Rone who do all those things have all the friends but no kids have any friends. And the teachers are horrible! They swat their kids with no note of the parent and the dont do anything to stop the bulling and the cursing! I think they should improve the teachers because they are being to nice! column1: Terrible experience with Brian Murphy, Dean of Student affairs. Bullies students, ask inappropriate questions of students. It's a matter of time before parents figure him out. Glad my son graduated. Thank God but no thanks to him. Once he targets your son, Murphy uses other students to bully the kid. The principle a nice guy but apparently helpless to interceed. You get the feeling this guy want to hurry and retire leaving the hanging job to Murphy. Mount Saint Joseph is an excellent High School for any young man. The Principle is outstanding. He is very involved in all aspects of the school. He sets a high standard for learning and discipline. Our son has thrived at MSJ. As parents we highly recommend this school. As a student, I am disappointed in Mount Saint Joseph. They focus entirely on athletics and not the academics that really matter. The school administration uses all of their funding for things like building new athletic facilities and scholarships for students who are good on the court, and terrible in the classroom. The school should use their money for the technology we so desperately need in this day and age, and for renovating our aging classrooms and labs. I will not be "continuing the legacy" because I will not send my future son here, that is for sure. In my 3 years, this school has been wonderful. It does form the person spiritually, intellectually, and physically. Like any other school, its up to the student to decide whether or not he takes heed of anything and does something with what he's been given. For the most part, of all the recent grads I've talked to who have utilized what they've learned, great things have come to them. I love this school. I believe that this school presented a tremendous oppurtunity that students can take advantage of if they are mature enough to recognize it . Teachers change ovr he years but with mentorship, guidance and motivation one can graduate with far more tools with which to face life, college or career.

column3: Your kids are in danger at this horrible school. At this very moment, Bonita High School is being investigated by the California Department of Education for refusing to let parents participate in meetings regarding their children. The CDE is currently investigating violations of ELEVEN different federal and state laws. The special education teachers and school psychologists are incompetent - so are their general education teachers. At a meeting held at Bonita High School a month ago, it was discovered the their teachers are completely unaware of the No Child Left Behind Act. Run, don't walk from Bonita High School if you want your child to receive an education. They've harmed my child - don't let them to the same to yours. At Bonita High School, your child will be left behind. We have been very pleased with the Education 2 out of our 3 children have recieved at Bonita, the third will enter BHS in 2013. We are proud to say our oldest is graduating in 4 years at Berkeley with an Engineering degree. Her success in college stemmed from the support and the academic rigor during her years at Bonita. Thank you teachers, staff and Administrators. If you have an over achiever child they will be treated much differently than if you have a child who struggles and/or has learning difficulties. Those with very high grades and good test scores are treated well, those who struggle are treated with distain and are sometimes humiliated by the teachers. Great behind the wheel students. Most of Bonita High School students are very defensive. They look out for others. Bonita High School is a superb school, with nearly all aspects of school-life flourishing. Arts, sports, and most-importantly academics are all taken seriously there. It is currently a California distinguished school. The campus is a great size, not too large and classes are easy to find. If you are struggling in a subject, there are so many options of classes to fit your needs. Bonita has a fantastic Freshman CORE program, and an abundance of athletic options for every season with friendly coaches. The arts program is also one of the best I've ever heard of, with complex theatre arts classes and clubs, a fantastic array of bands, an abundance of art classes ( such as jewelry making, and one of the best choir programs in the nation. Bands have performed at the LA County Fair, and in many competitions (always winning awards). In short, this school absolutely covers the triple A (arts, acedemics, and athletics) and should definitely be a consideration for people looking for a successful high school life. Students here are really nice. Bonita has a lot of resources. Some of my teachers are kinda mean..... but most of teachers are nice. My shopmore daughter love BHS great teachers and great environment. Small school. La Verne, CA is a small city perfect to raise your kids. This school is just ok. I've called the principle 3 separate times to get a voicemail, and no returned calls all 3 times. The school is concerned mainly about money. The band program struggles horribly. The kids are very cliquish, which is so annoying. The students don't communicate with others outside their little groups! La Verne is a nice city, but Bonita High is overrated! Students are very clickish!... No sense of community! My daughter loves music, but the band program is so bad. The band instructor is rude, and seems burned out on his job! Teachers are good, but the principals are also rude and egotistical! If I could start over, I'd consider, Glendora, San Dimas, or Claremont! =/ Bullying is not addressed properly at Bonita High. It's preventative measures that work with bullying, "Preventative Measures People". Also, many of the students and parents are very snooty. It's a smaller school, so the pool of friends can be very narrow, and the kids are very clicky. Getting the president of the U.S. on the phone is easier than getting in touch with the principal. This is a small school so there is no margin for error with the kids or staff. Bonita is overrated! Very poorly! The music director is very rude and so are all the coaches. No matter how talented your student is, the staff is very bad; and everyone should just consider a different school where the programs have a better sense of community and the leadership & appreciation is better displayed to the students that want to succeed! Bonita is the worst when your child needs extras. They are very money oriented. Teachers are rude and never disciplined for their actions. They are there to support their students and instead criticize and demean them. A parent told me about these horrible reviews about the band program, so I had to chime in. The band director is horrible, mean person. My junior son absolutely hates him, and I have to constantly talk him out of quitting band. If you are coming to Bonita High for the band program, think twice, and don't say I didn't warn you!!! Bonita High addresses bullying "after" the incident takes place! The Band instructor needs to go! He is very rude and unappreciative of the help he gets from volunteers! He's the worst part of Bonita High! Most students cant stand him! Bonita is a horrible school. I'm so sad because I expected so much! The band instructor is hated by most of my friends in band. Our middle school band instructor was better than this guy! He is more interested in launching his own band than he is with his students, but he'll never make it because he sings horribly! Sadly, I will not return to band next year! Bonita High School was great to me as a student. If your overall experience throughout four years of schooling was diminished by the band instructor, you were focused on the wrong thing. Also, parents, if your student struggled with the senior project (an 8-page paper), further education will NOT be for your child; 8+ pages should be light for introductory college-level work. Get out ya feelings. The school is one of the best in the area. This school has given me the opportunity to take several classes that I wouldn't be able to take at other schools (such as jewelry and history of rock and roll) and as an AP student, the learning atmosphere is great in the right places. However, there were some classes (some departments in general, really) that were not as promising as others. The teachers bully the students a lot especially the ones who have a hard time learning and they get away with it, and students are just as terrible if I could go back id send my child to a different school. Top tier high school with outstanding choral and band programs. My son loves Bonita! This is his senior year and he has had a great experience! Bonita is a very clique school. Too many “LaVerne” people (Bonita K-12, then went to ULV now teaching at Bonita) infest the staff making them elitist bullies and the kids are bullies as well. The school did a horrible job with the academic program during the pandemic. The principal is a poor communicator. $ will help you get what you want. If your kid is an average athlete give money and volunteer your time and it will pay off. Bad school. Send your kid to another place. Parent to a current Bonita high sophomore. I can’t say much about sports or clubs because my daughter started her freshman year during the pandemic so there wasn’t much going on in those departments. As far as teachers, courses offered, and coursework, I’ve loved everything about it. My daughter has always excelled at school and I really like that Bonita offers rigorous courses, plenty of AP classes and from what she tells me all of her teachers have been awesome. So far we’ve had a very enjoyable experience and are excited to continue at Bonita. Bonita has been a wonderful experience for my son so far. The staff is wonderful and are quick to offer help when my son was struggling. There is great communication to parents. The school, at least for my son, has a very inclusive and friendly atmosphere. My only complaint is that the campus is pretty spread out but hey, I guess that is part of the cardio training. My son hated school until he got to Bonita now he gets up early, excited to get to school on time for 0 period (jazz). The music program is phenomenal and the AP teachers are fantastic. All of the kids in the performing arts and advanced placement classes are overwhelmingly friendly and supportive of one another. My daughter also enjoyed her time at Bonita, though perhaps on a more normal enthusiasm level. She enjoyed participating in swim and water polo and, as a slightly above average student, was able to get into UC Davis :)A nice perk is that it is right next door to a police station and the principal appears to be in constant communication with them. When attempting to transfer you child here beware that they operate like a private school. If your child doesn't "meet their standards" they will deny your transfer over and over again. When I first called to enroll my child the lady in the office said "your child isn't special needs is she" i was in shock. Never in my life have I dealt with a school like this. When it was all over I realized why would I even want my child to attend a school like this. I gladly enrolled my child into a school that doesn't discriminate. The faculty at this school is completely oblivious to what the students are doing. While many of them are getting high, others are encouraging their fellow students to take part in this behavior. This is a terrible place for your child to be at, and it should have been shut down long ago. I am very disappointed in the teachers and staff here. My daughter has attended this school for 3 years. The staff and teachers are lazy and do not take time to help my child. They completely treat her unfairly due to her skin color, but the “white” kids are free to do whatever. The classrooms have these phone caddies but the teachers do not make all of the students put their phones up only daughter and 5 other students out of 20+ kids! UNBELIEVABLE.

column1: This school is amazing, but the truth is that this is a school for kids who really love the performing arts. This school will give your child the tools needed to have a successful career in the performing arts. The new principal (Doreen Winn) at PAPA is taking the school to new heights and soon PAPA will be a premier school in New Mexico. The Public academy for Perfoaming Arts or PAPA, is an amazing school. If your child is interested in the performing arts or is allready in the performing arts PAPA is the perfect school for him/her. After getting our new princible (Doreen Whin) our school has been more organized and has done things our school is very proud to say we have done. We have made feature length movies with our film department and every year we have a spring dance show at the national Hispanic Coltural Center showing our amazing dancers talents. Our students have done things in the perfroming arts that only kids at PAPA have the oppertunity to do. If you want your child to succeed academically and in the performing arts PAPA is the perfect place for them. PAPA is a great school that provides a rigorous academic curriculum while maintaining the love of the arts in each of its courses. The students that attend are very talented and often do not realize they have such talents until they attend this school. There is a small student to teacher ratio and a variety of college-prep courses that other schools do not offer. The staff communicates well with parents and do their best to help your child succeed. The school may be lacking a "building" (it is currently stuck in portables), but they are able to utilize their facilities in effective ways that do not take away from the student's learning. This is a great school and it is on a lottery system to attend. The only way this school can improve is by having a better facility for teaching the students. Awesome. On the waiting list. Hope to hear the great news soon Good luck at all applicants Where else can you see a 6' guy twirling & leaping across a tiny quad or hear an intricate run on a classical guitar during lunch? PAPA's is the best school for creative kids to be nurtured & taught their talent. The school caters to those who would be ostracized in a public school because of their unique set of skills. Where else can a kid take six years of musical theater, drama, fine art & three dance classes a day ranging from jazz, ballet, hip hop to flamenco? Students can sign up for piano, guitar, strings, or join a variety of choirs. All this happen on a shoe string budget & works because of the dedication of staff, parents and children. In this small school kids don't get lost in the shuffle and everyone knows your name. PAPA puts most Special Ed kids in regular classes with everyone else. There are a few sessions of class of math & English classes if needed. My daughter came here for her senior year for drama. "I feel like I've come home," she said. "I belong here and they accept me." *With a new principle and staff, the school has improved a great deal since 2007 when my kids started. The older reviews reflect problems that have been solved, so ignore them. PAPA is a nice school because of its students. My child attends PAPA but leaves complaining every day. Now that they invoked a new parking procedure to the already existing one I was met with rudeness from the staff (daphne benavidas) and confusion from the lack of school to parent communication . (I Do not recommend this school) I am a student at this school and even though the staff can come of as rude they really do want to help you. You have to put up the effort and not expect them to do everything. over al I think this school is absolutely wonderful and I would recommended this school to anyone wanting to go in to the 6 grade to the 12 grade This school is amazing. My daughter spent her elementary years miserable, it was a fight everyday to get her to go. She's now in her second year at PAPA and loves to go everyday. Even though it's about art school, standard curriculum is taught and my child is held to a high standard but she wants to do well and cares about learning now. She loves her visual art class, has improved so much in dance, and even loves her piano class even after years of private lessons. If your child loves the performing arts or has had trouble "fitting in" somewhere else, this school is perfect for kids like this. It's not for kids who don't want to perform. It's also not for kids who rather spend their days belittling others, I love the small school atmosphere. The principal and teachers know my student - his strengths and challenges. My son's friends at his school share the same interests in music and dancing. It is a small school experience with a very engaging arts program that keeps students motivated.

There is an excuse for everything including absenteeism, test scores, complaints, etc. Pay is below average and student satisfaction needs improvement. Teachers need additional support. The food offered to students is not to state standards and is not balanced. The policies for the schools are standard but yet not followed nor does administration know about existing policy. The district has a lot of racial issues and doesn’t treat people fairly. What are the positives? There are some amazing teachers within the district.

column1: They are not preparing these young adults to enter highter level colleges. At best, they are preparing them to enter the local community college that is not much better than the school as far as the education received. The administration itself has admitted that they are behind in math, so their solution is to charge over $100 each for "dual credit" trig, calculus, and stats classes with the class only counting as a college credit IF you get a high enough score on the ACT in math. These are classes that should be offered without paying that type of cost for it to MAYBE count as a college credit. Even after taking them taught at the high school, they are not prepared if they need to take them in college.As one parent stated, sports are more important than anything. Also, what your name is is just as important, so you can be publically fawned over, yet things that are important are ignored if the child doesn't have the right last name, so their confidence and abilities are not built on.

column3: BEWARE parents of students with disabilities!!! Alta's administration deserves "0" stars. I have a special needs child who is mainstreamed, and we had to CONSTANTLY educate the support staff there about her disabilities, which they were in denial of, regardless of the fact that my child has had an IEP since elementary school. Some "new" and also some "old," and jaded teachers were horrible, while some of the veteran teachers and the counseling staff were excellent. We had serious problems with the principal. Instead of recognizing the serious mistakes made on the part of inexperienced staff and offering training and support, the administration (VERY inexperienced themselves) accused my child of misconduct, effectively "blaming the victim" and denying any wrongdoing on their part. This was despite the fact that my child had an above average grade point average, even qualifying for college courses, and a good rapport with teachers before attending this school. For the first time ever, we had to involve legal counsel. If your disabled child is mainstreamed in the general ed classroom, look elsewhere. We did, and our student earned a 4.0 the final quarter of the year. Alta High School is a very innovative school with excellent teachers who go the extra mile to ensure student success. Lots of extracurriculars and very involved parents. Alta is definitely a great school. Our children attend here and they love it. The teachers and admin have proven to us over and over again how much they care about their students and for that we are thankful. Go Hawks! I’ve had all 4 of my children for to Alta High School even though I work as an educator in another local high school. ALTA has been stellar preparing them for college and they have all done very well after high school, owing much of their confidence and success to the teachers at ALTA. The teachers were very encouraging, and Interested in what came next for my kiddos. They gave a solid education along with opportunities like “Step to the U” which aren’t available at other local schools. They have a great offering of AP classes and well as the amazing location. Overall, Alta has been a great school that I am beyond grateful for.

column1: To be honest, this school isn't what it used to be. Broad Run was one of the very first schools in the county, so back then it had some pretty high rankings. Now these newer schools are far better. The school was built in 1969, seeing mice has become a norm around here. Academics could be better. Our sport teams suck now. A lot. Except for maybe volleyball. Some teachers are excellent and others are just AWFUL. I wonder how some of them even got the job when they could care less about their students success. Here are some pros about Broad Run: Although academics aren't great, they're not horrible. Many classes do require a good amount of effort to pass. You will learn, regardless. School spirit is big around here, especially at football games. People are approachable. There are cliques and bullies but hey that's at every high school. There are great ways to get help for your classes, teachers can help before school, after school, during lunch or study hall. NHS tutors are available for every subject. Overall, Broad run is an ok school. Needs major improvement. There are much better schools in the area. But being a Spartan isn't too horrible after a while. I have a senior and a freshman at BRHS, and we have had great experiences at this school. Academically, there are many very strong students at this school, and a wide variety of AP courses are offered. The staff is motivated and dedicated. Broad Run boasts many strong sports teams including last years 5A State championship boys soccer team, conference titles for both boys and girls basketball teams, and a strong football program that is currently ranked in the WaPosts top 10. BRHS is one of the oldest hs is the county, and we are looking forward to the many improvements and upgrades that are underway and will continue over the next two years. Our family has been very pleased overall with our experience at BRHS. Broad Run is an amazing learning environment for a very diverse community. We have awesome teachers and very involved parents. Although 45 years old, it's getting ready to go through a much needed expansion and renovations. I have a freshman at Broad Run and I couldn't be happier with the teachers and administration. He is receiving a fabulous education from a staff of knowledgeable, caring teachers. We have a wonderful, energetic, new principal this year, and the school has just begun renovations. I have a Freshman girl at Broad Run HS and since she is an avid reader she loves the Library, the Debate and Creative Writing Club. Academics are challenging and interesting, teachers are engage with subjects. There is always something going on for every one! We have a child who has been in the school district for 3 years and at BRHS for 1 year. We have been exceptionally pleased by the caliber of teachers, the sports program and the Debate Club. Teachers arrive early, depart late and have ensured success for our child. They have been caring and concerned and reply to email. Only once have I felt the need to write to the principal recently about an issue and within 45 minutes of hitting send, the issue had been discussed and resolved without any excuses. Pretty amazing and supportive of parents. Administrative staff and most teacher care about the students and their success. Any school will have a few teacher that are just able to qualified to inspire and understand our modern day children. It’s a difficult time to connect with these them in today technology filled world. I’ve found that what does make Broad Run a step above the rest and that we don’t have all new and top of the line, best of the best but what we do have and compassion, caring, average folks (both staff and student) which to me makes the equality of our school 10! this is my first year and I love it

column3: This school has been wonderful. My son is a sophomore this year and we couldn't be happier. The teachers have been great, engaging, interested in my child's long-term success in life in general, as well as the here and now in h.s.. BEAUTIFUL facilities and technology. The cafeteria is excellent here, I should add, as that was my complaint with the JHS. :) There is great community spirit here and it shows. I was on your campus for a track meet for a relative from another city. I have NEVER been so impressed with your campus. Your stadium was very clean. Easy to move around. Enough area for the handicap. I was in a wheelchair and needed the ladies room. My partner being a male could not enter ladies room, but 2 young ladies from Your school stayed and helped me until I could get back to my partner. I was overwhelmed. I know all have their moments. But April 14, 2022, they showed off exceptionally well. Thank You.

column1: A very supportive school with great outreach programs for students. Other students are friendly and the teachers really seem like they care. The neighborhood is also great and I felt safe being here. Overall a good school that gave me a good foundation and job readiness as well as college readiness.

column3: I attended here 10 years ago. Great school with good teachers and staff many of which I know are still there. Sports have had their issues with being competitive, some sports we tend to have teams that do really well where as other sports have a hard time winning. Music program has always been great, as is the drama program. They renovated the campus after I graduated but the improvements look great. The school is beautiful and the teachers are ware well equipped and caring but the culture of the students is caustic! We came here from rated 10 school and was impressed with counselor and tools the school has for kids to succeed. The social environment only benefits kids who want to party. People should think twice to moving there child to this School. My daughter is still going to school there in fact has been going to school in tahoe since kindergarten she has been a straight A student since she started she's never been bullied teachers go above and beyond for there students.i have three grown children who tried to attend school in LA county school districts and all 3 I pulled out due to gang violence and bullying. All 3 had to go on independent study.in Tahoe I never had to worry I would thousand time over. Recommend tahoe hight all there schools are awesome. This school can’t handle students who are struggling academically/emotionally. It is easier for them to send students to tallac (continuation school) than make an effort at helping their students by persistently offering different forms of help. Counselors don’t pay attention to their students and don’t make an effort to reach out to them when they are missing class/ not turning in assignments, instead they are immediately labeled as bad kids. The principal doesn’t seem to understand it may hard for children to reach out for help so he gives up on his students if they decline the help he offered after offering it one time only.

column1: it' christian based and a all girls school so they are not distracted by boys. great curriculum. I'm an alumna of Josephinum High School and I feel it was a blessing to walk through those doors for four years. I had a safe, one of a kind education that prepared me for the rest of my life. I was a parent and a non academic employee at Josephinum ,I loved the education and the personal on hands teaching that my daughter received .Josephinum is the perfect place to become a intelligent and independent women . Most fulfilling - giving you all of the learning tools for the future (both acedemic and life time skills). Its the best - I know I went for four years and came out a well rounded person in all areas. Josephinum was a haven from my insane family life. The teachers were genuinely caring in guiding me toward my full potential. I graduated with a strong sense of integrity that has been challenged throughout my life. I know I wouldn't be the person I am today without the development of a STRONG foundation created at the Jo! great teachers and enthusiastic P.T.A. allowed me to become a strong and independent person. Caring environment, personal attention, challenging academics, exceptional teachers, awesome students, committed parents. I don't even know where to begin with Josephinum Academy! For it being my freshmen year, I am in love with The Jo! For me, the best part are the young teachers. Because of the fact that they're a bit younger than the "average-aged teacher," they relate to us a lot, which has been very helpful. The teachers make classes so much fun, they actually CARE about our future, and you can have a personal relationship with each of them, without feeling weird about it. The classes and curriculum is also another positive key factor of what Josephinum has to offer. They offer advances courses, like AP Biology and AP Calculus. I love that they arrange us based on how much we know, and what we need more help on. Currently, I'm in advanced survey literature, which has been great for me because I am being challenged, so it makes my learning education that much more rewarding. The school also understands that not all students work on the same level, so they make sure we are placed in the right classes. Josephinum is the place to go if you want to become an intelligent, positive, insightful, and independent woman. Josephinum Academy is a special place for young women. The academics, attention and love shown to the girls is not found in the majority of high schools, especially in Chicago. My daughter is a freshman and I find that she has begun to blossom, finding her voice and expressing leadership. She was extremely introverted, lacking friends and now she is enjoying developing close friendships. I feel great watching her grow into a more self-assured young woman. Like I began, "The Jo" is a very special place! Josephinum Academy is an extraordinary school that offers excellent academics, a staff who always go the extra mile and teachers who care about the students in a manner seldom seen. The overall performance of everyone at Josephinum has impressed me beyond my hopes and expectations. I work with several children to ensure their educational success and I endorse Josephinum as a school that encourages, supports, guides, teaches and cares about its students. I am impressed and grateful for all everyone has done. The students exhibit enthusiasm and a joy in learning. Josephinum Academy is outstanding. Josephinum is a school unlike any other. It s a place where a girl can come to learn without holding back because of male distractions. The teachers really care about how we learn and where we are. Though unsure of the school at first, I came to love it and can t imagine being anywhere else.

column3: This school and in fact the entire district is highly overrated. The administration and the staff are not doing anything more or better than any average school. They barely do the minimal. They are not interested in listening to parents or involve parents in any decisions or processes. The high test scores and student achievements that earned the high rankings for the school are in no way a reflection on the teacher's quality or effort. It's the wealthy and education mindful parents that send their kids to all sorts of tutoring schools and expensive camps all over the country that explains. Just look at the student ethnic profiles. Yet the school just stands to reap the benefits with no shame (just google the school teacher salary database to find out their ridiculously high pay). Don't be mislead by the rankings. Mr. Prisinzano is an effective, concerned principal who works constantly to enhance the educational goals and opportunities for the students at Jericho High School. He and his staff provide a safe, encouraging environment to foster students' success. I graduated from JHS in the early 90s. Jericho was ranked #1 in the state and in the top 20 nationally. I excelled as an athlete but was a solid B student. I did go to college with 18 college credits and felt very prepared when going to class. I earned my B average and worked at it. Jericho teachers helped in every possible way. School just life is what you make of it. If you put in effort, you get rewarded. The diverse courses are great and the teachers do care and are engaged. They never went "through the motions." Yes there was always a bad teacher, but that makes you appreciate the better ones. Drivers Ed, dissecting cats, etc. this was a top notch education. I earn a 7 figure income and owe a lot of the life lessons to JHS. It's a great place and the taxes are well worth it. Every school has clicks. Significant wealth exists here and it spills into the school and students. Being wealthy isn't a bad thing (unless you are Bernie Sanders)-let's be real folks-you want your children around successful people. Raise your children with good values and they can see through the materialistic BS. Amazing district and anyone would be lucky to go here. The new principal Rosenberg is a real b****. She has no interest in helping students or parents, no integrity, no skills, rude and arrogant. She managed to have the previous principal kicked out and got his job. In case you wonder how she did it? Her mother was on the district's education board. So go figure. It's only a matter of time that this high school will go down the drain under her leadership, sadly. I received a fantastic education, made lifelong friendships, and learned from fantastic, caring teachers. I loved JHS and its culture of taking education seriously while supporting students at all phases of their lives. There's so much bad to say about Jericho High School. I attended this school over a decade ago because, like 99% of the other students there, I grew up in a life of privilege. I attended a great university and I work as a software engineer and I love my job. That being said, I attribute almost none of it to JHS other than the fact that it got me into college. Grade inflation is a huge problem at this school. If you don't do well enough in your classes, they send you to the "learning center" which was basically just teachers sitting with you while you took exams so they could help you with the answers. Parents routinely came into the school to yell at teachers, who were more afraid of the students and their parents than not sufficiently educating children and so pushy parents would guarantee their children received straight As. Just a joke in so many ways. That said, if you want your child to succeed in life then honestly going to this school is probably not a terrible thing. They'll have a good chance of going to a great university and doing great things in their lives. They just won't learn anything of value while they're in HS. I've had three children attend this school with one graduating just last year. Each of them got out of the school what they put into it. My oldest excelled and left with more than 30 college credits and a great group of long time friends. My middle child took the Engineering tract and entered an engineering program very much ahead of his peers. My youngest did not enjoy school as a freshman (not because of the school, it would have been any school) but the educators and staff were somehow able to ignite a spark in him as a sophmore that continues to this day in his college career. My family moved to this town because of the reputation of this school and we have never regretted that decision. I can't say enough about the education my children received here. Choosing this school district for my 2 sons is one of the best decisions I’ve ever made. My kids are happy, successful and is surrounded by a group of kids who share similar goals. This school’s reputation for being one of the “best” schools in the nation is a bit of smoke and mirrors. The majority of the students go to outside tutoring institutions after school and in the summer, learning curriculums before they are taught at the school. Test scores are not necessarily representative of teachers. As a parent you will be expected to pay for tutors if you child can’t keep up. There is very little support for students that are not high level. The school is a very intense competitive environment. Not a very nurturing environment. If all you care about is academic achievements for your child then this is a great school for you. If you are looking to have a well rounded kid skip!

column1: A student - I graduated from NWCS only a short time ago and the only thing I can say is don't understand the 5/10 rating. North Warren was a school I had transferred to from a large school, and even though the school is small the experience I had there changed my life. Still to this day I have close relationships with some of the best teachers I've ever had. I learned so much about myself through going there, and overall the student body was made up of great students. I know that all of the teachers I had in high school were deidicated, caring, and loved teaching their students. All the other faculty was so kind to me and I'll forever be thankful for all that the staff at North Warren had done for me. I made great friends, learned so much, and had an experience that I'll forever remember as some of the best times in my life. If you're a parent wondering if you should move to this school district and enroll your child into this school I'd tell you to do it 10x over. I live in this community, and my boys go to this school. Some of the teachers there are overly aggressive to special needs kids. Some are outdated and need training to keep with the times. The principal is a bias man. The superintendent is a fair woman. The school has had numerous covid alerts. In short the principal picks and chooses what rules and policies he wants to enforce or not abide by on any particular occasion. I would not recommend this school, especially for anyone who has special needs. My children were constantly picked on by the previous bus drive. My son is constantly being bullied by the music teach, who also violates my son's first and 4th amendment rights. He has told my son he can't say certain words, and has gone as far as taking my son's phone without cause, reason or consent.
