column3: Keene High School.. Not the best.. New Itime scheduale is wack... causing kids to stay in school longer which many students have sports affterwards.. I graduated a few years ago and I have to say that Keene High School fully prepared me for the rigors of college and provided me with important skills that have helped me at work. Even the teachers I was not fond of, or the classes that at the time I felt were useless have actually been very important in helping me through school and work. Although the administration can be a headache sometimes, the teachers, the diversity of courses and the community are wonderful! I graduated a few years ago and loved my experience at KHS. The staff really helped me love learning, and went out of their way to help me when I needed it. They nurtured my interests, pushed me to succeed, and challenged me to be a better person. I almost went to private school instead of going to the Keene public school system, but I am glad that I attended and got the experience and education KHS has to offer. My son is a freshman this year at Keene High and the bullying and violence is out of control. Yesterday the ambulance was there again to recover a student who was beaten by another student. We will not be returning next year since the same people responsible for this unsafe environment were just reelected to do more of the same. It's so disheartening. The teachers are dedicated and know their subjects. Parents turn out for theatre and music. Yet the staff are undermined by policies (homework does not count toward grade), "study" hall is noisy cafeteria, and a teacher who was punched 2022 needed surgery.

column1: Our daughter is a Freshman at POB in the Engineering Academy. We have been VERY pleased with the quality of teachers and instruction and teaching by the teachers. The Engineering Academy is excellent. Our daughter passed her Intro. to Engineering class and will receive college credit for the class....that's awesome. And we contribute her success to her teacher, Mr. Mariano, who was voted "Teacher of the Year" last year. He's an awesome teacher! The principa, Mr. Carroll provides superior leadership to the teachers & staff as well as being accessible to students and parents. We are extremely pleased with Phillip O. Berry Acaedmy of Technology. ALL families with children interested in Engineering, Computer Technology or the Medical field should consider POB as top notch public high school in Charlotte, NC. I'm a freshman here at Phillip O. Berry. So far, I've seen absolutely NO change whatsoever in the quality and challenge of the academics and even curriculum, comparing to middle school. This school is publicized with such a good rating, with propaganda that proposes that the students here are all high-level and advanced, and that the curriculum is more rigorous than that of normal schools. True, the ratings are high and the success and graduation rates are also high. But what is ALSO high is the level of IMMATURITY that is displayed in the classrooms. There is absolutely no display of discipline that I'm aware of, and I'm in classes with freshmen, sophomores, and juniors. The level of intelligence is also lower than I expected from this school. But I will say that there are, in fact, students that are very smart and mature, but the average classroom is not very high-level, considering that about half the students almost all of my classes are failing. Well, I suppose this school is better than my home school, Rocky River, so I guess I'll give them that. Overall, the teachers are decent, the students, not so much. And the rigor...I can't seem to find it. Phillip O Berry is a great school to go to. Initially, very hesitant to attend the school. Once get to know teachers and the staff, I fall in love with school. POB is t started offering STEM curriculum very recently. Bio-tech program is awesome. In less than 2 years POB came 3rd place in state HOSA competition. Medical intervention lab and teacher is amazing. She has lot of passion for the subject and has vested interest in student welfare. Bio teacher is an exemplary, his focus is on ensuring students are well prepared for college and goes above and beyond. He adopted research based papers and book to educate students. English teacher is amazing, right from the beginning of the school year, she wanted her students start thinking about college and AP. DBQS, assignment, and quizzes are college level. She understand the student abilities and challenges them, but ensures they are motivated. Overall, Phillip O Berry is an excellent school. If you are attending a school for academics, you have chosen an excellent school. My son is a sophomore with a 4.62 GPA currently. He plays football, which isn't the best, but his teachers are great. I can email any one of them at any time and can expect a response within the hour. I appreciate teachers that are engaging and genuinely care about the student versus the check. My son has been at POB since his Freshman year. As he prepares for graduation in a week I feel it is finally time to give a review. To speak on the academic program I will list the colleges he has been accepted to.....Harvard, Vanderbilt, Citadel, Naval Academy, Morehouse. All have offered some form of scholarship. He was accepted to the Citadel the summer before his senior year. Now has he gotten into a physical altercation.... yes twice. Both times he was agressed and defended himself. The principal acted swiftly and fairly. I love this school. At the end of the day the numbers speak for themselves. His senior class is less then 350 children and 90% have over a 3.0 . Curtis Carroll is visible all the time he supports his students. They concentrate on academics..not athletics. My son was on the biomedical program and looks foward to the next chapter of his education. There are so many problems with this school. Phillip O Berry has changed so much now that there is a new principal on the horizon; Ms. Kennedy. The previous principal, Dr. Carroll, was trying to build and educational environment but that all was destructed with Ms. Kennedy. Phillip O Berry has the potential to be a top school, but lacks the support and fundamental foundation that many schools such as Ardrey Kell and Mallard Creek possess. I DO NOT recommend this school for Your teen, or yourself. The teachers and the administrators are separate which on the most basic level, means that if a student has a problem in a class, they won't be heard because the administration will blindly trust the teachers. My call for help was ignored, and "if I was lucky" I would get told that the teacher is the teacher and will stay that way. The teachers here are pathetically lazy. They rarely are engaged in the teaching and we always have tons of random paperwork to do each class period. If You don't have access to a computer then you're already behind, because the teachers here are too lazy to actually engage You in the class so they put You in front of a computer. Great experience with staff and guidance counselors... They have great programs for students.. Great communication

It's a shame for those students to are blacks cannot see their own teach! SHAME OF YOU CONNETQUOT! Excellent excellent excellent. Connetquot is above the rest! So happy to live in this amazing community. My Two Children went to This school District from Elementary Through High School! My Son & Daughter both had Positive Experiences. They both have become Very successful Adults. Just Remember Your child will only get out what they put in, no matter how Good the School District is Amazing talented athletes especially girls varsity soccer. Very good school, my grades are higher then ever before and I’ve noticed my skills getting higher, they are even putting me into higher level classes since I’m doing so good. Teachers care about our progress, bullying has strict protocols, none of the quiet kids get picked on much, any fights are broken up within minutes most fist ones which I’ve only seen 1 or 2. Only problem is some vaping but it isn’t too severe. Most my classmates care about their grades and compete. This school is perfect. I am a current student at this school (2022.) The teachers are really great but there are somethings the school needs to fix. The food they started giving out free snack with your lunch. No wonder why SOME OF IT WAS EXPIRED. Also, after school breaks, they give out bad milk. Also at this school there is at least one school threat a year.

column1: It's real easy for a teacher to get on here and blame the incompance of teachers on the lack of parental support. The truth, however, is this is one of the worst schools I have ever regretfully had my children attend and I am ecstatic about pulling them out and sending them to a much better district. There is no structure, incompetent and untrained as well as unskilled teaching staff, contribution to bad behavior from students do to lack of moral, professional behavior from staff, poor communication skills, limited teaching materials, and the list goes on. I have met few teachers in this district who honestly care about the education of their students. Instead of making improvement though, they would prefer to come to this sight and point blame at parents like a child playing the blame game. If you live in this district you would probably get farther with your child's education of you homeschooled them. The most unprofessional staff I have ever had to deal with. What a nasty little school and school district. From the school board all the way down to first grade. Do not expect your children to get an education. You MUST stay on top of it. From the principal to the teacher they do not want to see parents (they are professionals) who know what they are doing and frankly will tell you it is none of your business. Avoid at all cost. Why are people giving biased reviews? If people are being biased, then so shall I. I moved my child from a nearby large public school to Venus and I absolutely don't regret my decision. My older children graduated from the larger district so I have personal knowledge of both school environments. Venus is by far the superior school district. I always know what is going on with my child's education. If I have a question it doesn't take 5 days for somebody to call back like in the big district. The academics are very comparable to the larger school district so I know my child is getting a good education and will be college ready. No school district is perfect but I think Venus ISD has worked very hard to improve in all areas and are making great strides to make it a good choice for parents. The only downfall is the lack of class choices for high school but that's only because they are a small district. The benefits of the smaller district far outweigh this one downfall. I have no regrets moving my child to Venus ISD. I always thought that high school years were supposed to be the best years of my life. Sadly for me I attended Venus High school and got the exact opposite. Half of the coaches are teachers, their misbehaved athletes are given special treatment compared to other students. A lot of students got away with things simply because they were favored students. In such a small school, being the victim of bullying was very common. There were few teachers where I felt like I actually had to try to learn something. Most teachers had such low expectations and I was surprised that failing was even possible. Many teachers and staff knew the problems that were occurring in the school and looked the other way. The clubs at the school were very selective and did not include all students that wanted to be a part of them. Many teachers were fired, some quit or retired out of nowhere, and we were left with whatever teacher or substitute that they could get their hands on. The only reason I'm giving this a one star, other than the fact that it's the lowest I can go, is that the lunch ladies were very kind and some teachers and staff actually did care for the well being of the students. Avoid at all costs. Cronyism and nepotism are rampant in this district, and there is far too much emphasis placed on a failing sports program and little to none on education. Taxpayer money is continously spent on frivolous things and creating fake jobs for friends and family of the administration and the school board instead of sorely needed repairs to unsafe and hazardous buildings. If your thinking of moving here just do yourself a favor and don't. It's only a matter of time before the state comes in and shuts the place down and hands it over to a nearby town.

This is the best school ever! I used to go to this school (back when I didn't graduate yet) and I loveed it so much!!!! Usually as a child not everyone is excited to wake up early and go to school.. I couldn't wait till morning to go to school. Every morning I was excited to wake up and go to school. The teachers there are friendly and students are too. Everyone accepts you for who you are. Now I have 2 children of my own and expecting a 3rd and when they will be going to high school, This is the school I'd want them to go to because I know this is a GREAT, EXCELLENT school! The principal and administration are not up to standard. On 3 occasions when they had to provide information they were either late or provided incomplete information that was very crucial. Major overhall ugently required. Teacher comment :- One math. teacher is seriously subpar. There only for pay not for teaching. It is obvious the two negative ratings this school has are by parents of kids who had problems staying out of trouble. Low drop out rate and very clean safe school. This school is horrible. Some teachers won't grade papers at all. They just mark down if they turned it in, which does nothing for the learning process. My daughter tells me that her teachers regularly break down crying in class, scream at the students, curse at the students, and watch while students bully each other. It sounds like a complete free for all. We recently took in my husband's brother who moved here from out of state. The school has been amazing in terms of getting him acclimated and up to speed. We met with the counselors and administrators. We had a tour of the school and were given access to all kinds of online programs to make sure we keep up with his homework, lunch money and all the other things you have to worry about. Century is a great school, considering that they meet the academic needs of the students very well. The schools avid program helps kids who may be the first in their families to go to college, and provides them with additional guidance. For advanced students, there over 14 AP and honors classes. The principle is excellent, and takes an interest in the students learning. Teachers are passionate about what they teach and work towards the success of their students. Overall, Century is extremely safe, well lead, has a student council that has ranked at a gold level for 5+ years, over 30 extracurriculars, and courses that meet the needs of their students. I love Century! I transferred here from Forest Grove, and I love it! My teachers are awesome and I have made a lot more friends here than at Forest Grove! I already have the phone number for one of them! I feel like I fit in here better than at Forest Grove. I believe I will be very successful when I move on to community college, because I am getting a great education here! Go Jaguars! Century is a good school aside from its principal, Ms Guise. I will say that is the only reason I won't recommend Century. Regardless of Century being a good school, I can't, in good conscience, recommend it with Martha Guise being a part of the administration.

column1: I love the school district. But the teacher no longer care about what happens there and couldn't care less. The principal and vice principals both do not enforce any of the rules. Especially dress code, girls walk down the hall wearing short shorts and boo one does anything unless they are bigger and then they make you change. The school was decent at one point but the kids are becoming disrespectful. The isd was good about 4 yrs ago. Now that the community is older and being inundated with new residents, the teachers are not equipped to handle the influx and lost their passion to teach due to babysitting. I love Hutto. Its a great school and has an amazing football program. i like Hutto high school a lot This school is trash, they do not care about the students. They are more focused on dress code and phone use than anything else. The teachers are rude, and they like to make students take the fault for their own mistakes. Also don't look for help from the counselors because they will side with the teachers.

column3: principals and administrators are absolutely horrible. My son got threatened with expulsion for playing "hackysack" with a few of his friends after they got out of vocational. The principal (Mr. Goetz) even told the boys before, "you can play hackysack outside, just not inside the building." The next time principal saw them playing outside, he brought them inside and told them they could not go home, and were forced to sit in the cafeteria after they were out of school for the day. There were other occasions where unnecessary punishment was used over really ridiculous things. They're supposed to be there to help the students. How is this helping them? It's just making them want to rebel against authoritative figures like Mr. Goats and Kevin Zeck. I have had three children go through the duneland schools. One is now in college and one is in High School and CHS. Due to my child having a medical condition they have an IEP. I wasnt sure if CHS would be a help or not. I can tell you that they have wonderful teachers who really care, and once they understand what they are faced with they really do try and help. My child is on the honor roll and with the help of Ms. Corso she is excelling. I am Currently a senior at Chesterton and I have been in private school and also in the Portage school system. Chesterton is by far the best you can get in NWI. All of my teachers were on the top of everything at all times. Also I wish people would quit complaining about how the "jocks" get away with more than the "normal" students. Life's not fair, it never was and never will be. Our school could be improved in many ways. The Athletes are favored by the teachers and have rules that don't seem to apply to them. The Choir director loves the show choirs and treats the other choirs like second class citizens. There are some good teachers, but most seem uninterested and are reluctant to help students. Fighting has gotten out of hand lately, making it an unsafe environment.

column3: My twins attend this school and I am very happy with the advanced courses that are offered. They got into every class that they wanted this year except Algebra II and driver's education class which can be taken for free online from Florida Virtual School. The academic adviser is helpful and the staff are very friendly. Some of the teachers even send email reminders for tests and assignments that are due soon. There aren't large expenses like for field trips for our four children that we encountered in the lower grades. The free bus service is great and my children have been safe riding to and from school. I think this school should have gotten at least an 8 out of 10 score. With sufficient effort, I think most students can excel at this school and be prepared for college. Initially, I was very pleased with this school. But over time, I could see that several of the teachers that my child had were unqualified - one seemed to have a mental disturbance, one had a head injury from playing college football, and others just didn't care. Yes, there were some AWESOME teachers there, but pifitully few. My other child had some learning issues, but instead of helping him, he was given "bonus points" so that he wouldn't fail the class (the teacher told me this herself, "Some of the kids are slower than the others and I don't want them to feel bad, so I give 'bonus points' so that they don't fail and feel bad about themselves."). As a result, my child stopped trying, as she knew that she would pass no matter what she did, thanks to the extra points, and sure enough, rather than the "F" she deserved, she ended up with a "B". I assume the teacher did this to get her Merit Increase...? My biggest complaint about this school is the quality of teachers. So many don't care. Several only teach so that they can coach (and it shows). I initially would have highly recommended this school, but over the years, I can see its true colors and would not recommend it. This school is both good and bad, and here's why it got 2 stars in my book. To start off, the teachers at Astronaut can be hit or miss. Some really do care about the students and their academic progress, however, some don't at all. I know teachers that use lots of curse words, every class. I could see maybe slipping up, but intentionally knowing that you're cussing in front of your students shouldn't be permitted. Don't get me wrong, I have had a few great teachers. Secondly, the administration at this school only supports the sports teams. Wonder why all the reviews are raving about sports? Because that's all they care about! With a wonderful choir program that I got to take part in, which gets straight superiors, performs at Disney, and more, administrators and many teachers don't fund the program, or even come to the concerts. I find this to be such a shame. Also, only Spanish and German are offered here, which I think is another disgrace. "Popular" kids get to dress and act however they want, while other kids get dress coded constantly. Overall, I think this school is a small town school, and it is extremely unfair, and needs to rethink it's priorities. Far below a minimum standard! I couldn’t be involved in after school activities based on bad grades mainly because of over expectations of homework.. who knows I could have been a great athlete and now we will never know.. academics is not the only form of advancement in life and should not be a prerequisite to more athletic forms of careers.. I should have been able to seek all available options for a career instead of just academics! I was 145 lbs and benched 210 I had natural ability’s that were untapped and left unenriched! My son is doing fantastic at AHS. He is enrolling in dual enrollment and doing great in his classes. He likes his teachers and is involved in after school activities. The principal is fantastic, I receive a weekly phone call AND email to let me know what is going on at the school too. I am pleased with AHS. I've recently removed my child from Astronaut. The principal is the #1 problem at this school. Hopefully all the complaints about her blatant favoritism and disgusting racial bias will get her removed soon. If and when that happens I'll gladly send my child back.

column1: I took my son out of this school. It was so awful I took him out of the Little Rock School District. This school was on the news for lots of problems and I received a letter stating that the teachers would have to get recertified and they were given another chance. They wasted a year of my son's education. I am currently a student at Hall High and to be honest the school is an OK choice. There is great diversity in the students, staff, and teachers. MOST teachers put up a great effort to teach and relate to students. From my one year at the school I have encountered a nice amount of school spirit, effort put forth by administration, and students trying to create a more united and peaceful environment. I would recommend this school if you have a student who can deal with a challenge every now and then, not only academically, but, also socially. But if you have a student who is very focused and can do with more of academic challenge. I am an honors student and I am very pleased with the effort put forth by the staff to give me the chance to remain at the level I am and help to push me to strive for academic sucess. Hall High is a disaster and LRSD should be ashamed of themselves for even sending kids there. Nothing but bullying by students and staff and an extremely inattentive administration. Hall High is a waste of what little taxpayer money is being used to fund this very sad excuse of a high school. Great School, my son had a great time at this school one of the best in the nation. I have watched Hall High School grow over the last 2 years. They now have a large number of students that holds a high standard of academics. High GPA's and very involved with the schools activities. Gabrielle Gillespie a junior is an excellent role model for Hall. I'm seeing more and more scholarships each year for College. Hall high school is a horrible school! They have students that fear for their life after severe bullying and the staff does nothing!!! I have so many students I know that go there and I have to talk to them so they can at least have a little dignity because of that place! I hope it gets shut down. This school has changed sooooo much! Great new staff and curriculum programs. My daughter loved the biomedical science classes. Great changes!!!! Don't let that "1" score scare you away. This school has changed so much over the past year. New magnet status, new high academic classes, new staff and the new AP teachers are awesome!!! Go visit the school and see the changes. My kiddos LOVE It there. My son is helping start the archery sport there. Great new opportunities!!!! This school has been reconstituted into a STEAM magnet school. It is now the high school extension of the highly successful Forest Heights STEM Academy (K-8) just up the street. My child started at Hall in the 2021-22 school year, and our experience has been very positive. We live in the neighborhood and can attest to the changes.

column3: My kids have gone thought the middle, junior, and senior high. The schools are great. Teachers and administration are attentive to student needs and abilities. Every kid can participate in sports or extracurricular activities. If there is any negative it is the school spirit is lacking in many students. It would be great to see more kids participating. There are activities for everyone from sports to music to drama to academic groups. There is no reason to not have every kid involved with some sort of activity. Love the opportunities here at Athens. My kids definitively took advantage of what was available and had a great experience. This school is focused on numbers and not the students. They push the students through instead of actually educating them. Their sole purpose is for sports, not education. If they spent more on the education factor and reducing the class sizes this might actually be a good school. Please don't get me wrong, there are some great teachers here, but they can not do the work they need to because they are overwhelmed with students that they can not give each student the amount of time they need to excel. The people in charge are the worse. they spend more time on trying to raise taxes to spend on sports then on the education of these kids. It's a disgrace! These schools are the worst in the state of PA. They do not care about the students unless they are from wealthy families. They push the lower income students out and do not take the time to help them. They rush to make judgments on the students instead of getting to know them and their families. Robust curriculum that allows for multiple pathways for student success. This school has the most electives and opportunities for students than any other school in Bradford County. Focus on all students and college and career readiness. Intense focus on the whole student and their social/emotional/ and mental health. Many supports are available for students from all backgrounds.

column1: I am a student at homestead senior and it's not really a bad school what people say it is. The only thing that is bad is that there is teachers who really don't want to teach us. They don't even try. Yes there is teachers who do try and they do a good jop at it. But other than that homestead senior high is really a great school. I love HSHS , because of the atmosphere. Everyone think's that HSHS is such a terrible school, when it really is not. You get a great education, and also it feels like home when you first arrive to the school. HSHS should be acknowledge for the hard work that the staff & students, are doing to change everybody's perspective on Homestead Senior High. Sadly, I am a student who is currently enrolled at HSHS. The teachers are highly unprofessional, and the students are practically illiterate! Coming here all the way from upstate New York, I'll have to say that there is a tremendous decline in education here compared to where I'm from. Ever since I've moved down here, I haven't met ONE single kid who can read cursive! There's kids in my school who've never even read chapter books! Almost everyone here as repeated a grade or two, and have very poor hygiene. I've heard nothing but negative remarks regarding Florida's educational system, and I'll have to agree. The administrators focus way too much on discipline and not enough on education. The curriculum here is very poor. While I'm here learning about nouns and verbs, my friends in New York are taking advanced calculus! The school's teachers and administrators will only prepare you for upcoming state tests, and never for anything important like, say, college?! When people ask me what school I attend, I am HIGHLY ashamed to say that I attend HSHS. IF YOU REALLY LOVE YOUR CHILDREN, DON'T SEND THEM HERE!!! My son is a junior at HSHS and he is in honor classes and dual enrollment classes. He is doing great and the teachers I have come across have been excellent. They are concerned for the kids education, they call you and schedule parent/student/teacher conferences if they feel they need to, to make sure your child stays on track. My son has been there since he was a freshman and I absolutely love the school. No school is perfect, but the principal, staff and the teachers have done a great job in turning this school around. I am proud to say my son is a Bronco. He loves his school, his teachers, and his friends. Just an extra little note: This school does prepare you for college despite what others have commented on here. My son has attended college fairs with the school, and his teachers have more than emphasized how important it is to prepare for college. They don't teach just for the kids to pass state exams, they teach for the kids to learn.

Our School thrives on finding your own personal pathway and making sure you are succeeding in life.

column1: I'm a freshman at Richmond High School and have been going here since 5th grade. Anyone in a half mile radius of the school has to walk, which includes me. With the horrible winters that we've been having, there's of course ice and snow. Well, Richmond High School does not salt their parking lot or sidewalks, so you are eventually going to fall. Walking to school is a short walk, but not good at all during the winter. The school parking lot is small and there are always cars racing around the parking lot, almost hitting people with no cops near the school. The teachers are okay but I can say that the average classes at this school would be advanced at any other school. All the school cares about is sports and we have pep assemblies every two or three weeks. The school also has a lot of discrimination and bullying from my point of view. It's okay, but if I had the choice I would send them to a different school. My family has lived in Richmond for multiple generations and we all went to Richmond schools. The families who have lived in this town for many years tend to favor certain families over others. Outsiders are not really welcome in general. But if you are exceptionally talented or wealthy you can find a place in their circle. Bullying has been passed down from generation to generation. Teachers and staff turn a blind eye to bullying and refuse to believe their favorite students are bullies even when they see it happening. Infact, sometimes the teachers and parents are the bullies. They have no time for kids they don't see as special, talented, and athletic. The reason Richmond has a lack of funding - The older people ( the highest percentage of those who take the time to vote) say they will not vote for funding because their children are grown and they don't want to spend money on kids they don't care about. I am the parent of two kids in Richmond school district the school is clean, the teachers are wonderful and the superintendent is very involved in the community. The teachers and administrators are the best.

column3: There are a lot of distractions with physical alteration and classroom disruptions. The main goal for the teacher is to have their students pass the yearly state test, pretty much just meet the minimum. There was not enough support or help for those students who wanted to go to college and were first in their family to do it. Apparently these people that are posting negative comments have disruptive kids that have no sense of intelligence. If you have a child that wants to learn, they are willing to help you all the way. We even had a teacher offer to come to our house and help her if she needed it. They were more than willing to offer up their cell numbers to help students and go the extra mile. I really commend the teachers and faculty for being so involved with the parents and students. If you want to be involved, they will be there. You have to make the first step. You can't just sit back and fail and wonder why no one helped you. I'm a former student who graduated in 2009. I currently go to Texas A&M University, but I know high school did not prepare me for college. I never felt challenged there. Graduated top 10%, NHS, yet now that I am attending college I have realized everything I've learned has not been because of EHS. I understand children will not attempt to do the work if they are challenged more, but maybe that will encourage tutoring or more one-on-one teacher time. Well where to begin. Very low expectations of students. Text books are very rarely taken home. Very little parent involvement for the kids who need it the most. High School if anything was young adult day care with a lot of busy work. Way to much focus on athletics and TAKS now EOC exams. In regards to EOC exams because instructors jobs are on the line its obvious why they teach little else than to the test. Administrative staff is very friendly. Very low end student body though. Not a place I would want my children to attend. Very clear divide between low and high end students which is primarily because of generational poverty in Ennis, TX but that is a different bag of worms all together. They have made great improvements technologically but have disregarded prevalent issues that need to be fixed in the classroom in regards to unqualified instructors (teachers who see teaching as a job not a passion and pursued such as a fall back career). The bar has certainly been lowered in Ennis, TX where failing is literally passing. A score of a 65 is enough to graduate. I would like to think taxpayers deserve better for their children than a second rate education. I think Ennis High School is a great school. My daughter absolutely loves going to school. The school has so many different options of what a student can do, getting ready for college, dual credit courses, various clubs to get involved in, many clubs are active with community service, great teachers, and great administrative team. The staff is extremely passionate about their students! Great administrative team! Lots of school spirit! Beautiful building! Love this school! I have three students in the high school and one at the early childhood center. Their experience at the high school has been great. They were hesitant about moving in the middle of the year last year but all were made to feel welcomed. The teachers communicate with me through out the year and have been very professional. I love the multiple options/electives the high school offers and the quality of teachers. The administration has been very helpful as well. Ennis ISD has great schools all around. Ennis High School is a school in which teachers care about their students. Teachers take time out to make sure students will be successful in not only their school career, but after school as well. The school has a very diversified student population which enables students to take on different roles in the many organizations that are offered. Ennis High School is one of the Nicest High Schools in the Nation. If you are ever on the campus you will be met by kids that are well behaved and well mannered. The halls are wide. The cafeteria is nicer than those of most colleges. The auditorium is state of the art. Their career and technology department has lots to offer. But the best thing about Ennis High School is that the kids take pride in the classroom and in winning. Their band program is one of the most successful the state has ever had. The kids are successful in all Sports and are always contenders in the State Playoffs. In UIL the kids advance to Regionals and State every year. Winning is a state of mind at Ennis High School. The school administration looks to hire teachers who care about kids and who are the best in their field. You cannot ask for a better all around high school. Very awesome school with caring considerate teachers and staff!! I have full faith that my child will receive an excellent education. Great school. They have good interaction between teachers and parents. The teachers are very passionate. The staff is very friendly. We have two students in high school and we all love this school. Parent -Academically, Ennis is overall very average. Ennis has 1 kindergarten center, 4 elementary schools, 2 intermediate schools (4th-6th), 1 Jr. High, and 1 High School. The kindergarten center thru intermediate schools are outstanding. The faculty is intelligent, caring, and very capable. School ratings might be lower than other similar sized schools; however, the socioeconomical divide in Ennis is more to blame than curriculum. There is a large sector of Ennis that sees the school as an 8-4 daycare center rather than an educational system - unfortunate but true.The Jr. High & High School are below average. Once the kids get to these schools it becomes more about getting in AP, and avoiding the general curriculum. By this time the lifelong Ennisites are jocking for position to get the "best" teachers. The unsuspecting new students, and students lacking parental support are left with the rest.. This does two things; it segregates the student body, and it defines a teacher as good/bad when the next class moves up - so the cycle continues year after year. The entire faculty is excellent. The teachers work hard, and inject enthusiasm as they teach the curriculum. The so-called "best" teachers are determined by the locals, but they're all good. Opportunity is lacking in high school. Football is what makes this school go. If your student is heavily involved in Friday nights then he/she will have an amazing HS experience. The football team is a perennial contender. The band is top notch military, and the cheer team is a big hit. All other UIL activities (basketball, baseball, softball, UIL comps, theater, etc) are second hand thus limiting any personal growth or opportunity for your son/daughter. This perspective also carries over to the community at large.Be informed.. I graduated several years ago from Ennis. There are the small handful of excellent teachers who truly care about the students academics and progress, but unfortunately the majority couldn't care less. They let the students control the classroom and the assignments are a joke. Fights breakout on a regular basis and bullying is an issue. The principal is great as well as many staff members. However there are only two student counselors/ advisors and only one does her job. I waited for 30min for the advisor to get off a personal call about what type of wine she wanted to bring to a party later that week (during school hours). It's awful. The school is obviously huge in football, but if your child is not in athletics then I would say find another school where they will actually learn. I'm moving out of town so my kids won't have to go to Ennis hs.

column3: There are many issues to deal with at the high school level and BFA has the tools but is lacking the ability to get the students on boardl. Having seen many students go through this school, I can say the most pertinant issue to manage is student/teacher relationships. The students are allowed to wak in (or not), text, talk, disrupt calss and many teachers are so overwhelmed by these constant bad behaviors that they do not stop the class to correct, they just teach over the disruptions. Some students are unable to concentrate, though they want to, others just give up. Very few are gifted and have groups of like minded students in their classes who all strive to succeed. I will say that the guidance office and the administration are willing to work with parents, but the classroom support in many classes is just not there. I've heard so many complaints about BFA that I often wonder if it's truly the school or the student. My son thrives at BFA. He's "gifted" and his former school never challenged him. He flew through middle school pulling straight A's without ever studying. BFA challenged him for the first time in his life. This has good and bad points. Because he was used to flying through and not having to study, studying skills have been an issue. He's used to doing work last minute and rushing through it, only now he's learning that doesn't always work if you want to maintain A's, There are a few duds when it comes to teachers. They seem to have no interest in relating to their students. Most, however, are outstanding and kids generally get along with them. My son and his friends rave over many teachers they've had and go out of their way to stop and chat if they have any free time. For BFA to work for a child, it has to be a two-way street. If a student chooses to be disruptive or never do the work, they're not going to get much from their education there. For the rest, BFA does an amazing job of treating students like equals and not students. Well ... the new administration is certainly into enforcing the rules. The teachers remain good, some, especially in AP and accelerated classes are excellent. Hopefully the school board won't yield to pressures to abolish these classes.

column1: Not the best school to go to for students who want to be challenged in class. There are no honors classes, and AP is only offered for juniors and seniors. This is an excellent school, and I think that it's one of the best schools in Illinois. Bleh i lowkey cant wait ti graduate I absolutely love Andrew high school. Both of my sons have learned so much, The staff is dedicated and amazing! All 3 of my kids attended Andrew High School and all were extremely prepared for College. Great teachers and overall very good experience.Wonderful community to raise a family. Great School; Great community; Great Administration! All of D230 schools are great however, my kids attend Andrew and I could not be happier! SO many offerings of a large school but being a tad smaller, my kids never felt left out or lost. When they needed help or guidance, there was never a shortage of support and or direction. My kids have received a strong education and I am very proud of how this school, as a whole, has helped them with the foundation blocks they needed to grow. This high school is great. It was a 10 out of 10 just recently. I would recommend joining as many clubs or sports you like. That is how to make many great friends. I have 2 kids there and they absolutely love it , so do I, great staff in Andrew high school

column1: Without a doubt one of the worst school districts on the face of the planet. If you're related to the small group that runs things, your child is set. Otherwise, your child will be treated as a second class citizen, and stuck in a class taught by one of the many lousy teachers they have who should have retired eons ago. Pay no attention to the test scores. This school is 90% little rich white kids who are going to do well on standardized tests regardless of what school they attend, and Wall students actually perform worse on those tests than students at similar schools. My son had a great teacher(s) the past 2 years. This year has been terrible! They don't help him like they're supposed to. They stick a rediculous label on him and then when he tells them he can't read (reason he's there) they tell him just do his best & then walk off!! He hates school now & it's breaking my heart because he really wants to read. Also his teachers were telling the whole class today about my best friend going to school there several years ago supposedly having (sex) ect....He's so mad and is going to call the school because most of the things she said were untrue & also inappropriate!

column3: John I Leonard has been really great! We switched from a private school here and it has been a fantastic experience. I was worried about the switch, but the Academy Coordinator and Guidance Councelor have been so helpful, patient and attentive the transition was easy. Teachers and Guidance respond quickly to e-mail questions and seem always welcome to help. There are so many opportunities to succeed here with the Academies, the on-campus DE, the Saturday Success Academy, community service, sports and clubs. The Academy Awards for the kids and parents was great! Appreciated all the decorations, and little touches that went into it! Made me proud as a parent to see my child get rewarded for their effort and accomplishments! Made some friends there myself this year! Been a great year! John I. Leonard offers an average high school education, but does employ a few educators who excel at their craft. The facilities are a bit outdated, and could use an overhaul. GREAT SCHOOL! "A" SCHOOL! I am so happy that the school achieved the "A" I, as a parent, always thought they deserved! That grading formula only accounted for 10th Grade FCAT scores. Now it encompasses the entire high school experience. It now includes the high achieving juniors and seniors who are taking AP and DE! Our son had a great experience at John I Leonard. The arts programs like jazz and marching bands. As well as the sports programs. You will always get out of it what you put into it. Go Lancers ! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! ! My child attends John I Leonard, she was in private schools all her life till 10th grade. She enjoys the school, the majority of the teachers care very much about the students. I was surprised to have a chemistry teacher call me just to let me know who well my child is doing in her chemistry class. My child is a cheerleader since the age of 5. She joined the cheer squad at JOHN I LEONARD however the coaching needs to be better organized, better communication with the squads and most of all they need to be consistent with applying rules the same for all cheerleaders not just the ones they prefer! The competition squad was a joke, 5 of the girls picked couldn't even do a simple stunt. It was great at the time i believe they tried there best to give us a great school but i do thank it's to overcrowded.

column1: Two of my children have graduated from this school and two more are currently attending and they are all straight A students. This school works with children to help them excel in both academics and athletics. The teachers are caring and go out of their way to help children excel. The school features small classroom sizes that allow children personalized education. Any student would be fortunate to attend this outstanding school.

Tell the kids when their are texts such as a important SAT test coming up. Small school and all related to each other so if you speak your mind then you are hated. School has teachers whom pick and choose who theyll treat good . some of the non favorite kids get left in the dust. school has extreme problems .then the kids who have teachers as parents who are teachers get special treatment (Mrs.jager brand) I previously attended Gilboa Conesville Central School but my little sister currently is attending and she came home crying to me saying the teacher have been Harrising her and she had trouble at school with another girl where the girl constantly bossing the her around so my sister asked her to stop an went to the teacher and teachers did nothing about it repeatedly, she began getting really upset due to a group of teachers surrounding her asking her about what they saw and not what the real problem was where it had ended up the principle(Katie Allen) grabbed my little sister an pinned her to the table and holdig her arms behind her back were she could not move, this upsets me because there was no need for this she did nothing wrong but ask for help to avoid a situation, a number of students had witnessed this accur. column3: I attend at this school and I really like it.. I came from York Suburban and that thing was like a nightmare. Teachers In York High are very pleasant, and lots of help to offer. Once you get to know all the school, everyone in there and earn the teachers love, you'll be FINE. The staff here really care about their students. We put in extra hours and really try to make a difference. I myself run a free club for students after school, and have used as many best practices to help student engagement and learning. While working here I have seen the entire furlough process happen and in that time we have lost a lot of good teachers and principals. Those of us that are still in the building also have seen first hand what those cuts have done to not only the education but the environment of the building. We need to bring back programs we used to have, baseball, swimming, more art classes, home economics and maybe even some shop classes to get students excited and involved in their great Bearcat school! Honestly, just save your time and choose another school district. Once your child goes to this school or school district, he or she is enrolled into HELL. I would say for seniors this is a good school. I graduated in 2019. They really helped me figure out what to do next in life. So thank you guys And the school lunch wasn’t bad. But is your child is in 9th or 10th grade look out because they’ll be fighting and in nothing but drama.

column1: Cares about all students and has strengthened their academic standing in recent years. Supportive staff & community, CTE programs for students who arent looking to go to a university. Supportive, great programs and opportunities for the students. Great! The staff is very welcoming and positive. Teachers were given an option to teach while children were in quarantine. They just sent the assignments and expected them to know the information. Teachers don't input grades until after report card date so looks like all students are failing when there not. Teacher gave medical advice to my daughter telling her not to take prescribed medications. Teachers gossip and slandered parents and students. I would not send your child here.

column3: I graduated from HF in 98, and though I had a wonderful experience, I didn't realize just how great a school it really is until hearing others highschool stories. I thought it was normal to have a top notch theater program, tons of amenities, cultural diversity, fantastic music program, fabulous teachers, and a super supportive community that cares. I am so glad I did not grow up in a generic, sprawling, all white suburb. Though I do not live here anymore, I have friends that have moved back to raise their families. It truly is a gem. HF is a very good school FOR ITS AREA only ... it is top notch for South Suburban communities. HF is currently on AWS through the state due to failing test scores which does not make the HS as desirable. This school was one of the top in the nation at one time, I was proud to get an education here. After going through 4 years of education I was terribly disappointed, half of my teachers did care and control the classroom, the other half couldn't care less. Students talking all the time constantly distracting, just not a good learning environment. Even more interesting is that H-F is known as the drug store among students in the south suburbs. Sure the school has security it does not prevent fights, or drug dealing... HF was once a tremendous high school- one of the best in the state- but that was a long, long time ago. I am shocked at how bad the test scores are now (they are well UNDER the state average!!). What is going on? Really shameful. HF has dropped like a rock. This is one of the top schools in the state. It was just listed by The Washington Post as one of the top academically challenging school in the nation. This IS a great place to learn and grow. My daughter is currently a student at HF. Some of the students appear to be a little rough around the edges, but I don't mind because college will have individuals from all walks of life as well. I rather her get the exposure now while I can monitor it. Overall, I am happy with the education my daughter is receiving at HF. I am in constant communication with her teachers to see how she is progressing in class. She is currently taking all honors classes including Mandarin, key club and in the band. She has always been a straight A student her entire life, she's very focused on getting into a great college. I do feel that sometimes she has a bit too much homework, as many nights she doesn't get done until almost midnight. But that's life and its preparing her for what lays ahead. I'm a firm believer that you practice like you play and play like you practice. So this is just a short term sacrifice for a long term gain. Best school in the world love this school We moved from central Illinois to Flossmoor a few years ago. When looking for a high school for our two teens to attend, we decided it was better to live in the suburbs and send them to H-F to avoid rolling the dice regarding them both getting into a select school in Chicago, or enrolling them in a charter school. This school was also highly recommended by friends. We are happy with our choice. H-F has great facilities, amenities, true school spirit, and I feel my kids are being prepared to succeed in college. A parent cannot ask for much more. Was a great school, but that was many years ago. A dangerous place for a kid to go to school. Would NOT recommend it. I have three children at HF and one has special needs. The HF system far exceeds my expectations. There are drug problems in the neighboring communities that are never discussed. We left Linconway (exceptional academics but no one mentions the herion epidemic) to come to this environment. The student body is more diverse and yes I am pretty sure we have some out of district kids...but I think in comparison to the other schools in the area the kids perform really well. We have awesome academics, awesome athletics and a campus similar to a small college. What is not to love? Overall the school is great. They have a zero tolerance policy in place for bullying. They have plenty of activities and clubs for kids to be a part of. Best High School in the South Suburbs. My two kids recently graduated from HF. Both were accepted to all colleges that they applied to and received financial support from the college of their choice. The school offers strong academics (IB, AP, Project Lead the Way) and recently launched a Fine Arts Academy. They have a newly renovated fieldhouse to support their sports teams and clubs. There are lots of clubs and extracurriculars, making it easy for all students to find their tribe. Teachers and staff are great overall and many live within the community. Also parental support is strong. The high school coordinates their curriculum with the feeder districts and gives students opportunities to earn high school credit in middle school. We are a Caucasian family but it was important for us to live in a diverse neighborhood with a high school that is committed to seeing all of its students succeed. I think my kids are better equipped to compete anywhere in the world because they have flourished in a high school environment where not everyone looked and thought the same. HF is a place to be, a place for kids to learn and grow. Wonderful experience with my kids so far. Great high school! Amazing programming and teachers The "H-F Experience" did not live up to what I had hoped for my kids, after putting them through Flossmoor schools for almost 10 years. There is plenty of blame to go around, Parker Jr High was ridiculously unacceptable when it came to High School Readiness and at PJHS there was absolutely no consequences for your actions. I thought that if my kids could tough it out there HF would be different, sadly it wasn't and I realized I forced my kids to go to a dangerous environment for years. And being a black person in Homewood Flossmoor community I can assure you the community is divided too. The entire town including the high-school prides themselves on "diversity" however diversity is not an 70% black high school. All the white people think they're saints for living in this "diverse community" but there are very few other races there besides the huge percentage of black people and small percentage of white people. The parents all fight against each other on social media about local issues and somehow it always ends up black against white no matter what the issue is. Thanks to a divided community, an increase of crime and violence in the area, failing feeder schools, and poor leadership at HF, the high-school is failing. Of course people will always disagree but there's proof. According to US News they're ranked an astonishingly low ranking of 6,912 of 18,000 which is far too low considering that we were paying over 30k in taxes each year and the general community is middle to upper middle class. It gets worse however when you scroll down on US News ranking to see that only 29% of students met or exceeded mathematics expectations. And only 39% of students met or exceeded reading expectations. What used to be one of the best high schools in the state fails to get even a third of their students to meet general expectations. The school runs off a push pull philosophy claiming that if students push hard enough, the school will pull them forward. This only works for gifted students that are able to push forward, leaving the other students ignored and left behind. They recently approved another multi million dollar project for fine arts. They throw huge amounts of money towards stuff like a renovation of a perfectly fine swimming pool and now a fine arts center, but yet they can't seem to raise the amount of students meeting expectations. H-F is a wonderful school. Great teachers that prepare you for college and great students. They have an amazing Fine Arts & STEM program and 100s of clubs and extracurricular activities. My daughter was new at the school and so was my son my daughter didn’t no any one there until she met her friend which she was new to the school also. So it’s these senior kids that didn’t no my child or her friend and they insist on letting the kids get away with bullying them and as much as I went up there they would always do something to only my daughter and her friend but don’t actually punish the ones that was doing the bullying they don’t handle the issues at hand they only hide everything to keep their rep as a school so at the end of it all they removed my daughter from the school lying saying it was be cause of her attendance and the crazy part the other friend is the one with the attendance problem and they still removed my daughter so now I am taking legal action against the school cause I even heard what the deans was saying once they got off the phone with me and I recorded it so I bet for now on hf staff will take it serious cause I do horrible school as far as letting bullying fly but for the most part academic they are great Nice environment and great leadership. Provides opportunities for students to thrive in and outside of school. HF is an extremely welcoming school with plenty of space for innovation and creativity. They have strong academic programming such as IB, Project Lead the Way, and a Media, Visual and Performing Arts Academy. The students are very successful, we recently had two students named National Merit Commended Students. In addition to academics, the school has a boatload of extracurricular activities, which help to further students commitment to each other and the Homewood-Flossmoor community. I Highly recommend this school, it is one of the best in the Chicago area.

column1: This is a great rural school. There are pros and cons to a small school. There are a limited number of teachers and often limited opportunities. At Custer County you have the problem of limited teachers. If your student doesn't like the Spanish teacher there isn't another to chose from, as in a city school. The BIG pro is that the teachers are, for the most part, excellent. They are caring and work to give students the best possible education. WHat I have loved about it as my kids have gone through ( both began in kindergarten) is that there are abundant opportunities. Unlike a city school kids are not pigeon holed into one activity. At Custer County kids are encouraged to try everything and be involved. Kids can be a "band nerd" and a football player....or a "drama geek" and in FFA. There are not the traditional boundaries or cliques. What I think is amazing is the way this district has kept the arts, ag education, building trades and Advance Placement classes in this time of huge budget cuts and declining enrollment. This is a great school. I am glad my children graduated from here and I wish my grandkids had a school as good in the city they live in.

column3: I was a student at Rubidoux for only a year, sadly. This is a great school for those on their way to college. The RECHS (pronounced 'reaches') program allows students 16 years or older to take college courses concurrently with their normal high school classes. This allowed me to get a full year of college done... for free! The staff really cares about the students, and as someone who wrote a review earlier, those only students that are failing are doing so because of their own lack of initiative to ask the teachers about their grades and how they can achieve better. The only thing that isn't great about this school is its reputation, which is totally wrong anyway. Someone needs to check the last names of our top 10 students, including our salutatorian and our valedictorian. Latino. In eighteen years of being in education, our principal is one of the finest I've had the pleasure to work for. Our administrative team cares, truly cares, about the welfare of every one of our students. Yesterday, I saw seniors earn their graduation, seniors whom everyone gave up on except the staff at Rubidoux. I've seen the teachers pour blood, sweat, and tears into the lives of other people's children. We care more for the students than some of their parents do. Rubidoux is often the only stable, loving, and encouraging environment that some of these kids have. Anyone who disparages this school has an axe to grind, probably brought on by bitterness with something else at its source than Rubidoux. All I can say is, congratulations class of 2011. You made all of us proud. Go, Falcons! RECHS is such an incredibly amazing program. The staff is great! The reputation is misleading. We're coming back, watch out for these Falcons soaring with P.R.I.D.E. I have friends who constantly talk about how great of a school Rubidoux is. Great teachers and great students. You make life long buds at this school :)

column1: When I went to school, my school was great, all of my teachers would help us if we had problems with our work. By the way they helped me was that they made me think about how to go about and find the answer that I needed for the question I was having trouble with. That's how I learned to get things done. I am a student here, sophomore. Recently, we can't keep teachers, and the teachers we do keep have no idea what they're doing, with the exception of a few. The students are rude to others, not accepting (generally) and all think they are top of the social class because they're 'country' and drive big trucks. I guess it's worse for me since I've been here since first grade, but I don't recomend Palmyra-Eagle. We are statistically one of the lowest paying schools in Wisconsin, which is the cause of not so great teachers, who disrespect the students and get mad when they get disrespect back. It's all backwards, in my opinion. I school choiced my child out of Eagle Elementary to a neighboring School District, when I started to question the education they were receiving at Eagle. Much to my surprise I learned that my child was over 2 years behind in reading and almost a year and half behind in math. Eagle claimed they were fine and at grade level. After learning this, I school choiced our other child out the next year. I would NEVER recommend this district. Palmrya/Eagle School District makes claims that they are doing great and children are thriving, but when my story is the norm of parents choicing out I question their numbers. As with all school districts there will be some that love it and some that will hate everything about it. I believe it all depends on the student and their family and how they interact with the district. Sometimes the parents are worse than their children for spreading information. Sure, there are things I would change within the district and there are things I would not change. I for one, dispise school choice and everything that goes with it. You want out ... then move! Otherwise you should be thinking "what can I do to make it better for my child". And to those who diss on any school, all I have to say is that EVERYTHING starts with the HOME environment!Also as in every school district, there is politics involved which makes everything more complicated. My point is, the schools are what you and your family make of them. And to me, Palmyra-Eagle has been good, but I got involved early and have not regretted it. Small family atmosphere with terrific teachers and programs are what this school has to offer. My oldest son is currently attending school at Palmyra-Eagle High School and has had a fantastic experience thus far. There are a variety of courses to choose from including 8 AP classes. The school offers Spanish or French electives beginning in middle school. My child has been able to participate in multiple sports, and being that it is a small school, there are no tryouts, which makes it very inclusive. Recently, the school adopted a new bullying prevention program which has been well received by parents and students. Students meet regularly with the school counselor to develop post-secondary goals. This early planning results in graduates being accepted into many different colleges and universities, including Ivy League schools. The graduates also receive huge amounts of scholarships from local businesses, with nearly 50% of the students being awarded at least one. Palmyra-Eagle also has a very caring and supportive staff who truly know and care about the students and families. I would encourage anyone to check this school out! A great local, community school to be a part of. There are plenty of electives and extra-curricular opportunities for students to be involved in. Our family appreciates the ability to be a part of a small school district. Horrible experience. Very "toxic" administration. Parents bully the weak administration to control what goes on in the high school. It is way past time for new and effective leadership. Terrible. Created a bunch of internal and mental/emotional problems that are still struggling to be dealt with, and the education quality isn’t even that great. Our family has had very positive experiences with the PEASD. But its like anything else, you get out of the experience what you put in. Expecting to be involved in many levels and activities, bringing a positive attitude and willingness to participate, yields positive rewarding learning experiences. Overwhelming positive experience not only for my son, but also for me, a 1986 graduate of the school. I have never seen support like this from teachers and staff in ANY school setting the way I have seen it here in regards to my son. I have nothing bad to say. this school is horrible i have been getting bullied since middle school and have even got sent death threats bc i had a small pride flag in my backpack i got diagnosed with severe anxiety and social anxiety at the age of 13 and have been struggling mentally from the toxic environment

column3: The teachers to me, seem more dedicated than in some of the other districts. As a single parent of two teenagers, I have no complaints. Anaconda High School only cares about its sports programs. They have dropped drama, speech and debate, and other related classes to support the sports teams that can't win a game to save their life. The school board is a joke and they just voted to put grades 7-12 together. The other reason this is a terrible school is the faculty only cares about your last name. This town and school system are extremely clicky and with the right last name a student can get away with anything. The vice principal starts his yearly speech to freshman with most of you aren't going to graduate so you should drop out now. They'd rather see students drop out then give them the support they need. My children have had teachers in AHS that have pushed them to become strong, empathic, and hard-working members of society. Most, if not all, of the teachers are willing to reach out to help students in need in all areas of life. There are many students that come from a difficult place, and the teachers and Anaconda High have done an excellent job in helping them find their "spark" in the world. column3: I really like GHS. The sports are fun, and include everybody. Not to mention the Boys Cross Country team has been to state 4 years in a row. This school has excellent teachers, and a good educational program. Grinnell schools are great if you are an average to intelligent kid, or great at a sport or an extracurricular. Not a lot of thought is given to anything outside the box, but that seems to be an Iowan trait. It's important to conform here and fit in. If you don't, good luck. There's a divide between town and gown kids, and it shows in the way the administration treats students. I think if you're good at being good, you'll do fine here. It's not an exceptional education but with nothing else available in the area it's your only choice. Our school recently adopted a one-to-one program, which gives every student in 7-12 a MacBook Pro & the ability to learn in a "global atmosphere" in which students can connect with others. However, in my time at the HS l I have seen students on Twitter, Facebook, Minecraft, Netflix, Pinterest and every which thing which allows students to totally disconnect from the learning experience and the subpar teachers, which I will discuss later. Not to mention it is not even a useful tool. Our fairly new Superintendent found it imperative to adopt such a program with no empirical evidence that it would be successful in our district. Not only has it been unimpressive, it has actually brought the school's GPA, which has total causation. Folks, this is just the beginning. I am being told to end this however, so I would like to tell you, that the school is full of teachers who aren't prepping students for life, and I want to congratulate the only heroes in a high school full of those in need of a heroic classroom revamping: Michael Hunter, Bill Rudolph, Todd Crites, Dan Covino, and Elizabeth Hansen. Thank you for standing out and doing all you can to prep us for the future.

Unless there is a last minute bailout by the state, Juniata will hve no kindergarten, no agricultural ed., no business ed., no band, no sports teams at all in the 2011-20012 school year. Per pupil expenditures are #500 of the 501 school districts. The County has not been reassessed in 30 years!

column3: This school is the best they can have. I still go here so I know I know the teachers are very nice. W-P is a school district that is stretched to the very limits of its financial means, but still puts the kids first. The teachers and other staff genuinely care about the students and go to great lengths to see that everyone gets the attention they need. It's unfortunate that the school's curriculum and extracurricular activities are both so limited. It bothered me when I was a student there in the 1980s, and bothers me even more now that my own kids attend W-P. This isn't the fault of the school district (I always assumed it was a matter of funding), but it's still the kids who lose out by not having a debate club, or a journalism class, or a swim team (these are only a few examples). As hard as the staff works to get these kids a decent education and prepare them for life after graduation, there's only so much that even the most devoted educator can do without proper funding. I recently graduated from this school last year, in 2013. The school isn't necessarily a bad school. But, it definitely isn't the greatest school. It all comes down to funding. With such little money, it's hard to have things to keep people interested in sending their kids to the school. I mean, for instance, the school had to get rid of band. I was in band up until 10th grade, then they cancelled it because I guess they couldn't afford to keep it around anymore. I mean, we only had 11 people in the band when I was in 10th grade. So, it was obvious that band wasn't that important to many students. Although I believe that schools need some kind of musical program for the students, it is what it is. Basically, despite the school's poor funding, and lack of certain classes, it's a great school. Every teacher I had, except one, was super friendly. They all want their students to succeed in class so they can graduate and move on with their lives. The teachers, for the most part, are strict when it comes to such things as homework assignments, but since it's a small town basically everyone knows each other, so it's rather easy to get along with teachers. I give it a rating of 5/5.

column1: I am a parent of three students that went from K to 12 in the North Cedar school system. They had teachers of varying quality and dedication in all levels of their education. The educational opportunities were not nearly as broad as in a big city school, but the overall level and attitude of the students was higher. My children were all driven to make the most of their education. They all graduated near the top of their class, but had plenty of challenging teachers along the way. If a student has the desire to learn at a high level, North Cedar has the teachers and staff to fulfill that need. I am quite happy with the education my children received. All three obtained near full ride scholastic scholarships to very good colleges as a result of their education. Reviewing what has been written previous years, I am sorry to say that the original intent when the 4 districts combined in '94 is no longer the current administration intention. Be forewarned. It will soon be reduced to a Clarence Lowden district again. They are slowly removing high school activites to the Clarence building and are attempting to close the Stanwood site altogether. What will remain for the Mechanicsville site? it isn't looking good. I am so glad my kids are moving their families outside the school district. Great! Very supportive and innovative in their programs.

column1: Mayer Junior/Senior High School is a sad example of Arizona's lack of focus on education. It is an inadequate school serving mostly at risk students, and not doing it well. There are some great teachers here, but they get no support from the board or administration. They are paid nearly nothing, less than almost every other school district in the state. The board hires administrators out of retirement whose sole focus is to reduce costs and cut student programs. There is no library, no overhead projectors, few books, no school nurse. There is no formal discipline policy, and favortism is shown to school athletes and children of employees. I could go on, but you get the picture. Enough said. I think that this school has a terrrific staff, principal, superintendent and board. Recent changes have all been improvements and very effective. Some teachers can be good about pushing students to sucess but most push them down and lead them to failure the School also did not offer extra curricular activities such as art drama technicians or any interesting subject The turnover in teachers is something to be concerned about. For the 2017/2018 year, there are 2 new out of a total of 2 math teachers. 2 new out of a total of 2 English teachers, 1 new out of 1 Science teaching position and 1 new physical education out of 1. Out of 5 core subjects being taught (Math, English, Science, History, P.E.), there are 6 out of 7 new teachers. Why can't MUSD hold on to their teachers??? There has been issues with the superintendent, but the teachers and coaches step up and empower the students. They work hard on getting the students to find their potential and push to better themselves. Over the past few years, they went from a failing, or near failing grade to a B.
