column1: This is going to be my 3rd year at Fort Hayes, and I still love it. A lot of people complain that the workload is too much or that the teachers aren't good, but honestly they don't realize how lucky they are. For being a public school, the arts are good (especially the acting and dance programs), the teachers in generally try their hardest, and the principal tries to bring as much diversity and opportunity to all of us as he can. If you or your child is interested in the arts as well as a good education I would highly recommend scheduling a tour or looking into the Fort. I am a graduate from Fort Hayes. I graduated in 2011. The attention I got from the teachers and staff there definitely changed my course in life to a much more positive path by opening my mind to new ideas by using the arts. I was always involved in some sort of club or activity that kept me focused and motivated to have a successful high school career leading into a successful college career. I am now at on of the top private art colleges in the U.S. If it wasn't for Fort Hayes and the amazing teachers who sheltered me and cared I wouldn't have found my calling for the arts. this school has no sports it is just a school with all talk no work gets done.Do not send your kids here! Fort Hayes High School is the ultimate contradiction. They preach a self satisfying message of creation, hard work, and college readiness, but then continuously take measures to work against this. The teachers are a sole bright spot in this otherwise piss poor institution. The problem is Fort Hayes forces them to set the bar extremely low. I currently take two AP classes, both of which have been forced to slow the curriculum down to a crawl in order to appease the majority of students who can not for the life of them grasp the material. In my AP Government class such questions like "What is the electoral college?" and "What is a Democrat?" are frequently asked and my teacher is forced to slow down the class to cover basic material rather than preparing us for the AP exam. There is a reason why 48% of kids take the exam at Fort Hayes and only 17% pass, they let anyone into the classes without any type of requisite. There is absolutely no standard of excellence being set at this school so far as I can tell. The administrators are self serious, condescending, pretentious, and are not taken seriously by the faculty, in most cases they are mocked by the teachers in class. DONT GO! Great School. It's a lot of work but it is High School so you know. The teachers are very helpful. Heck, it's only been 8 weeks and I've learned quite a lot. Very easy to get lost but teachers or staff are very helpful.

My dad and two aunts graduated from here, and like them, I love it and can't wait to be a proud graduate in 2015. Am so happy that my son was in this school...all his teachers were amazing and the principal and counselors have done so much to support him. It has been a truly fantastic four years here. I'm presently a parent of a sophomore and even though she complains about the rigorous academic challenge I know that this school is great for her future. The academic choices are fantastic for both my overly intellectual child and my sports enthusiast. The leadership, teachers, parents and community work together with passion and enthusiasm for the kids' best interest. FANTASTIC High School! SEVERELY OVERCROWDED!!!!! column3: I am a current student at Tupelo High School, moved here 3 years ago, and am absolutely not recognized for anything here. Unless you are rich, play soccer, are Baptist/Christian, and have known everyone since elementary school, then you are not considered someone worth recognizing. Teachers of the arts (Art, Theatre, Chorus, etc.) constantly complain about poor funding and half of your school year is filled with ridiculous amounts of fundraisers! I mean, does the school not have funding? Also, the administration is like an old bridge: unstable and unpredictable- you never know when you're going to be thrown off, either. We've had so many teachers quit/be replaced in the past two years, and the replacement of our new principle who only wants to boost his reputation is a recent situation conveying the educational failures of the TPSD. The teachers are horrible, not caring whether you pass or fail, and will absolutely not come up to you and ask if you personally need help with anything if they even recognize that your grades are falling in the first place. One last thing: fights. The security is tight but float in the background, not bothering with some fights. I wish I could relax. There is a trend in theses reviews that people should note. Outsiders have a difficult time coming to Tupelo, school or otherwise. If the student is not very outgoing or involved in extracurricular activities, they will struggle. I believe the tough review written on Dec. 8 2011 brings up some real concerns. I'm a current student at THS, and the only reason I stay here is for the band program and my friends. I don't enjoy Tupelo, my parents don't like it, and I don't think that It's a good school for my younger sister. You won't be accepted with most students unless you're rich, play sports, party hard, or don't care. I don't feel accepted with the majority of my classmates. Also, the amount of classwork given by some of my teachers is ridiculous. I am in band with takes up so much time, and I also have a job. All that along with homework leaves me up late every night trying to finish just so I can pass. And most of the teachers aren't lenient on homework and projects, even if you're in my situation. Which is a downer. I wouldn't attend Tupelo if I wasn't already sucked in to it. I'm a junior at THS. Let me just say that I love my school. The teachers are great, and the vast majority of them are very passionate about what they do. If I had to complain about anything, it's that there are some uppity snobs; but I'd like you to point out a place that doesn't have a single one of those. And before you get the notion that this only applies to so-called outsiders, I was born and raised here with most of those people. In fact, during my time at THS, I've seen more people that have moved here in the past few years get along better than I have. As for ruffians, it's Mississippi. Anywhere you go, there will be fights and idiots. It happens. Tupelo is one of the most cultured schools in Mississippi when it comes to the arts. We've got one of only a handful of Thespian troupes in the state. I hope this helps. In response to the earlier post concerning "outsiders" having a hard time here, THAT IS THE PROBLEM! This school has a problem with inclusion and diversity and bullying especially among female students. My experience tells me that the girl bullies are most likely the product of their mothers being an earlier generation's bullies, or being victims and telling their girls to bully before they get bullied. To make maters worse, we even had an experience with a teacher being verbally abusive and bullying students. She was a coaches wife, so the administration fought parents tooth and nail defending her. Send your kids elsewhere, this school has a terrible environment. Furthermore, this school and town have a serious problem with rampant teenage pregnancy and the dropout rate is higher than average. The last I heard, the school was on academic probation as well. Tupelo has a general problem accepting those transferring in from out of state. They have a small town attitude and at same time believe they are more metro.

column1: It's really just an average school. As someone else has mentioned I do really wish they spent less attention on the school's athletics and more on the academics, as some teachers really should not be teaching (but of course we have some of the best teams in the state) There are a few teachers that genuinely care about the students but as a whole the staff is somewhat mediocre. I admit this was a decent school. There were some pretty good programs, such as honors, AP, and Dual Credit courses--if it wasn't for my success in this school, I wouldn't be in the Naval Nuclear Power program right now--but there really is a lack of focus on pushing students to succeed. Frankly, I was never really challenged in this school. The school focuses way too much on athletics and really should put more funding into academic and humanitarian courses as well as equipment and books. Many of my classes throughout the course of my attendance lacked even books that were up-to-date. Nevertheless, there are some passionate teachers that do very well at their job; however, this school could really use more motivation I had two students graduate from PFHS, one in 2018 and one in 2020. Both students took advantage of honors classes throughout the 4 years as well and dual enrollment through University of Idaho (U of I) and North Idaho College (NIC). One student graduated PFHS with just one class remaining for her Associate's degree. They also had a department dedicated to assisting students with college admissions, campus tours, scholarships, grants, and even in-person FAFSA workshops where they helped for every question every step of the way. For students not on the university path, they're partnered with KTEC where students do morning general ed classes at PFHS and afternoon workforce/industry-business grade training at KTEC. They really strive to help each student succeed based on their individual path. As with all schools, parent involvement in their student's progress is key, and PFHS teachers and counselors worked with my students and myself to meet my students' goals.

column1: Was educated by Carmichaels Area schools including the H.S. graduated in 1969. I think we received what we as students put into it far as a good education. Even though I no longer live in this school district, I cyberschool my kids because of the very poor education I received at Carmichaels. Not all the teachers were bad, though I have heard it has become much worse. But one example of the inferior education they provide: I made pretty much all As in high school, including math. Got to college, struggled to pass basic math. What Carmichaels views as A work is D level work in college. That is the fault of the education system. I had no idea my skills were so inferior. As a college freshmen, it is embarrassing. The previous reviewer who graduted in 1969 must not live in reality. This school has gone even further downhill since my own graduation a little over a decade ago, with more abusive teachers, more drug issues, and I wonder have they replaced the old textbooks from the 70s I used or have they continued to slip that to fund more important things like sports uniforms or renovations? As the administration are also very well known for verbally abusing and harrassing any family who chooses to homeschool. I feel very bad for all of this schools students. They deserve better. Then again most come from broken, abusive, drug ravaged families who simply don't care. The whole community is dying. The downward spiral at the school is i suppose merely a reflection of that harsh reality.

It's not based on talent, as if the coaches voted on students to join in, there would not be enough to have a team. The people below me, obviously have not experienced life as a STUDENT in Malcolm. We are not racist, as other schools are exactly like ours, just bigger. Horrific. The small town views date MPS in the worst ways. Rampant bullying while educators turn a blind eye

column1: Great students, great staff. Great place to work. Our test scores show that we are equal to or out-performing Montana's private schools. The test scores though are just a small portion of what's great at CHS. this is not a good school for you children to graduate at do to the unfairness of the teachers I love it here! it's always a great place to be! Its filled with happy people and great staff :) This school was a 2012 U.S. Department of Education National Blue Ribbon School of Excellence. Way to go Cougars! Majority of the staff is great, but when it comes to a specific teacher and principal it's a nightmare. I have not met a single parent or student that have not had a problem with this teacher, and why is he still teaching I ask? The school in general is great, but If you want your kid to graduate, make sure they play sports and is in the 'right' cliche or your in for a ride.

column3: I graduated in 1997! Back then it was an incredible school, there was no high technology or even Air Conditioning! Think the kids today are way to spoiled! Best part of HHS was the band!!! It was my life for 4 years! Now the standards set by our band is shot! HHS is now a laughing stock at competitions! But the education I received was A+ HHS is concerned about the who community in Hutchinson, not just the wealthy north side. Despite the segregation, HHS maintains high quality programs that are accessible to all. During my time as a student, there was an ample amount of courses that could be taken whether it was electives or higher education. The teachers were easy to get along with and always pushed you to your potential and even above it.

column1: I just found out about this website today. There is a reason we have a 3. This school is terrible. Our fairly new building is being destroyed every day by students such as gang tagging and destruction of furniture, doors, etc. There are no consequences for students' actions, and the students know it. They show up late, are truant, and some are very defiant. The administration does very little about this. This school needs a lot of help. The students, who do want to learn, are very frustrated or want to leave as do the teachers who care about their students' education. There is way too much incompetency and apathy at that campus with no guidance or support. Will we have to wait until something else bad happens before action is taken? I can understand the frustration of the parent that just wrote a review before me. For a school in only its second year, there are many flaws with the building design that simply will not change and the physical and degradation, though mostly cosmetic, would make many justifiably concerned about the the presence of gangs. I think it's important to remember that public schools don't intend for the growth and prosperity of gangs. Just the opposite it true. I agree that consequences for poor academic performance, poor attendance, and behavioral misconduct are not what everyone would like. Maybe too many issues seem to be glaringly ignored. I do not think this is willful on the part of the administration. They are only using the tools they have been limited by the laws and regulations. Give back public schools the right to deny admittance, like private , magnet, and charter schools. HBHS took the best teachers from the local schools and developed great programs. This school won 1st place in the Engineering games this year for the entire city of LA. Over 90% of its graduating seniors are college-bound. A handful of students are all-city top athletes. The school is a model for project based learning, and teachers and administrators from schools all around come to observe what's being done right. Several teachers and students have achieved national recognition for the work they are doing here, and are continuing to do. What more do you want from a school? Stem is the only good SLC, as I witnessed, AME and BTLR students are just smokers, drinkers, and teens in gangs. DONT send your child to this school unless you get them in stem. Please take my advice and spare your child!! In regards to the teacher who seems to imply that school is fine. Well receiving first place in the Engineering games may be something to be proud of, but you have to consider the rest of the school. The overall appearance and performance, STEM may have shown progress, but please account for the other SLCs. I am a student from the school and there are a lot of things I can personally say that are improper. A lot having to do with students who just don't care about their futures, etc. As stated from the parent who had left and earlier review "There are no consequences for students' actions, and the students know it. They show up late, are truant, and some are very defiant. The administration does very little about this. This school needs a lot of help. The students, who do want to learn, are very frustrated or want" the teachers are good but the principal is not ...i could say not into the job or something or does not have much experience running a school Look i am a student in AME academy i have nothing to complain about this school because well this school is great as i have witnessed the only bad academy is APEX academy thats the worse!!!! It is full of trouble theres many fights there and lots of students affiliated with gangs there its the worse academy there is in the bernstein complex. Since i am a student in ame academy i love it the teachers always are commited to helping there students they stay after school to tutor the students, on their on time, they help you in case ur in danger of failing, there are the best teachers in my opinion they think of the students first always and how they can help them improve. This year i have seen my academy get closer much closer i am very proud to be in ame. Well as former Helen Bernstein Hs student i really dont think hbhs is a good school because the school is full of bad influence people that do drugs and drink. I just think that the staff that work there should be more alert about what the students are doing. I also think when there is a class of 45 students at once it is hard to learn i think the average class should have aleast 28 not more or not less. I was at a class that wasfull it is not a good thing. Now i attend Glendale High it is a way better school beccause i thing the school has a better environment for the students and the staff and the rating of the school says it all GHS test socers r above average that means GHS has better students and students that want to suceed. HBHS has good students but the students in general r not that good. I am a former student of Helen Bernstein High School, and I would have to say that this school is not worth sending your child to. When I entered college, I was behind from all my peers in my courses because their high schools had much more competitive academics than this school ever had for me. Your child will be put in a classroom environment that does not challenge them and not benefit them for college. However, I would say that the STEM academy is probably the best choice if you have to send your kids to this school because they are doing well and are still progressing. The teachers in STEM work with the students and challenges them based on their past achievements and improvements. During my time in this school, I have seen drug deals, prostitution, gang crime, and many more both during school hours and non school hours but still on campus. Be very careful when sending your child to this school. It may have improved since the few years I left that place, but I highly doubt in little time. I have been a teacher at Helen Bernstein High School since it first opened. The school has come a long way since its first year, and I'm proud to be a part of such a dynamic team. My fellow teachers are hard-working professionals who really care about challenging the students, and preparing them to succeed in college. I continue to be impressed with the character and abilities of our students. I have always found that young people are willing and eager to work hard when the teachers engage their interest and respect and acknowledge each student's unique gifts. I have taught at other schools, both public and private, but I have found such a warm and positive community at HBHS that I am here to stay. Ah yes, Helen Bernstein High School. I was a Student there and thank heavens I left after 2 years spent into that school, and I like to share that. First off, the Principal there is not a Principal; its a person put in charge at the last second because no one wanted to be Principal of that School, plus the last principal there left, knowing that it isn't worth caring for this school. Additionally, I've seen the Principal, on rare occasions, mistreat their students even though they haven't did something wrong. The Staff there, nothing much to say, but they are much hardworking than the Principal to be honest. The teachers there are teachers, however, I felt some of them just want to work at another school, mainly due to the amount of students they've seen slack off or something. As for students, this is one of the key factors on why this school is terrible. Students in this school are just people who just want to hang out with friends or don't want to do anything there, and the teachers/principal isn't doing any encouragement or something helpful towards them, causing a harsh tardy rate to rise, even truancy. Lastly, the school setting itself. The bathrooms are the dirtiest sight I've ever seen, same for the lunch room, and even the stairwell, it seems the Janitors aren't doing their job or they simply slack off. As for the classrooms, they look like a clean sight. Overall, this isn't the school for people who want to take their education seriously, this isn't a school at all, its more like a former shadow of all the other professional schools around the neighborhood. So parents, please do not send your kids to this school. That is all i have to share about this sorry excuse for a "Professional" High school, please make the correct choice and choose the high school that'll benefit you in your education. My review for HBHS was not an accurate representation of HBHS. I attend STEM Academy of Hollywood, which is VERY different from HBHS. STEM is a separate Pilot school that operates in the same campus, but it seems that GreatSchools doesn't know that. HBHS seems unsafe and not as effective as STEM, and I wouldn't recommend it, especially because there is some gang activity. At STEM students participate in PBL Projects based on their pathways (Medical or Engineering), have opportunities to take AP, Honors and other advanced courses, as well as college classes. My experience at STEM so far has been great, the teachers and administration are very supportive and effective. The school keeps getting better both academically and in the community.

column3: It is safe for me to say the my education at WHS prepared me more for life than most State Colleges do within many regions outside of the Northeast area. It is the very lessons I learned from some of the greatest teachers I've known (even compared to many of my college professors) that I still go back to when making difficult decisions. I truly believe that WHS prepared me not only academically, but also socially and culturally to fully be prepared to engage in today's complex world and not only survive, but thrive in my career and all other areas. I am proud to be a Wizard, and as one of my favorite history teachers says: "It is not just what is being taught in the classroom, but what YOU the student put into your education. If you're looking for the challenge in high school, you'll find it. The problem is that (smart) students avoid these classes and then apply to top name schools for bragging rights. If you're an honors kid, you'll definately get a more well rounded education whereas the "regular" students are cramped in classes of 30+ where the teacher assigns a 10 minute assignment for an 80 min class period. What's surprising is that a good majority of students DO go off to nearby community college... strange for a more affluent public high school. Everyone tends to know each other and there's a nice hometown feel. The problem is diversity is LACKING!!! Students are deprived of learning about other cultures and belief systems. Yes, there are other people who DO exist in this world who ARE NOT white Christians and they don't always cater to deragatory stereotypes. Even 95% of the spanish department is white. There is a lot of underlying racism present. The suburban feeling is a little erie. when you get to school, you tend to pass by a lot of houses that look the same and the school is soo CLIQUEY!! But at least academics are good, top notch if you allow it to be but you wont be pressured. SS Washingtonville HS and particularly the principals office did not prepare me for college. Fortunately I had parents that aggressively prodded me to excel, I did graduate with a 99 average, even with all AP courses. There were a few teachers that rose above the others, unfortunately they were the minority. The school administration reinforces mediocrity, simply put, teachers tongues don't speak success. Athletics are the anticipated way to college for many WHS students. If I lived in the area, my kids would attend private school. I used to go to this school and it was amazing the school had its problems but over all its a really good school. The school needs work, most teachers do the minimum and seem to only care about the kids that do well and are easy to manage. Give them a child that needs extra help or support and its hit or miss. Sports seems to dominate in the way to college for a lot of kids. The school is to easy. My daughter said it didn’t really prepare her for college. She made deans list every semester in college but leaving WSHS she said they didn't give her enough. My son is now graduating and since the city kids parents bought the new homes they have brought their city fake thug attitudes. My son can handle his own but now he fights kids every week after having three years of pure happiness and the principle is powerless to stop the kids from going at him every week. If he says something back he gets ISS and the other 5 kids get nothing. If my child was a weaker kid he would be getting bullied and provably found in a gym mat. Send your kid to Cornwall if you can

column1: If you want to your student to go to a state university or a college with selective admission rates (35% or higher), St. Francis will serve them well. Provided your student gets As and Bs, St. Francis' college prep curriculum will prepare him/her for the ACT and SAT. However, if you want your student to attend a top 20 school, he/she would be better served at school with stronger AP classes and more extracurricular activities beside sports. I am lucky enough to attend a university ranked in the nation's top 15. However out of my class of 179, only 1 made it into a top 10 school and only 9 made it into schools ranked in the top 20. Four of those 9 attended Notre Dame and were, in addition to being good students, legacy. Only 2 students who were admitted to top 20 universities chose to attend other schools. The problem is St. Francis only offers 9 or 10 AP classes (AP music is offered every other year) and only half of those classes prepare students to get score 4s or 5s. I speak from experience. I got 4s or 5s on all my APs except for one exam, but many of my peers didn't even manage to pass. Bottom line, I don't believe the academics are worth the yearly $10,000 tuition. Given the quality of the public schools in the area, I frankly don't see why you would spend $10k/yr to send your child to St Francis. The academics at St Francis are good, but the public schools have much more to offer in terms of breadth and depth of curriculum, and more opportunities for extracurricular involvement. If you're looking for a true Catholic education for your child, look elsewhere. St Francis provides the same insipid religious ed that you can find in most parish CCD programs for free. Though they have pictures and quotes from St Francis on the walls, the atmosphere and the expectations placed on the students are little different than what you'd find in the surrounding public schools. I regret sending our child to St. Francis. She could have received the same or better education at the public High School, and we would have saved a ton of money. I'm blown away at how well St. Francis welcomes both students and parents to the family and recognizes and appreciates their unique values and talents. My children are thriving here. At St. Francis students are challenged academically as well as extracurricular. The culture is inclusive and encourages students to get involved. If I were to sum up the culture, I would borrow the phrase: "All for one and one for all". IT's consistent with who they are and is line with the Catholic religion. At a time when a lot of Catholic institutions struggle with their Catholic identity, St. Francis H. S. excels. I believe that sets the school aside and above others Saint Francis is a college prep high School, the academic program and curriculum is fully committed to that mission. They strive to make good students; great students in a caring and academic environment that is truly a Christian community. The Saint Francis community; including all staff, administration and parent volunteer organization collectively strive to include, to understand, to support and to nurture the students. This was one of our best decisions as parents. St. Francis High School in Wheaton is the best college prep high school in the area. Bar none. High achieving students achieve as high as any other school and ALL students are college bound. My daughter is a freshman in the class of 2017 here and everything this school is doing is top notch. I have had 4 children graduate from St Francis and have another one starting there next year. I am very happy with virtually all aspects of the school. My kids were well-prepared for the rigors of the college application process, as well as for college itself. The school is large enough to provide a broad set of courses, yet still retain a family-style environment where pretty much everybody knows everybody else. St Francis does an excellent job at providing the Catholic element to these young adults. Extracurricular activities, both sports and non-sports, are great. I would strongly recommend St Francis to anyone who is seeking an excellent college prep school, with strong Christian values and a culture of community that lasts long after the diploma is on the wall. I have two daughters that are at St. Francis and we have had a great experience! They do a great job of transitioning the kids to High School and there is a true family feel that provides them a comfort and confidense to excell. They also do a good job of spending time with the kids and truly preparing them for college. We have loved our relationship with St. Francis and highly recommend it! SFHS is a fabulous academic institution that offers a complete educational experience for all students. What is a complete educational experience? I am talking about an experience that fosters challenges for young adults to realize their potential in academics, sports, music/arts, diversified extra curriculars and most importantly in growing through human interaction with faculty and peers supported by the presence of Christian values. Our honors and AP classes are of collegiate standards. The world needs the talent of our students to be emotionally, spiritually, and physiologically prepared to embrace the future with a humble confidence that is anchored in the solid virtue of helping others reach their potential, hence a "we" versus "me" attitude resonates strongly in the confines of SFHS and the SFHS community. There are few investments that will realize the potential yield that a family gains when investing in the SFHS experience. Hard work is expected, accountability is high but respect and support are everywhere. We are not for eveyone, but our doors are open to all. I urge everyone to consider SFHS. It is a blessing that keeps on giving. Peace and wellness to all. My son loves the school and so do I. St. Francis is a school where everyone cares about each other. The environment is safe and the teachers cars about the students. St Francis is a great college preparatory school! High achieving students are challenged with a curriculum that includes many honors and AP classes. Average students are encouraged and challenged to be their best! Awesome fine art, athletic and campus ministry programs. With the academics and the many extracurricular opportunities, this school truly offers an wonderful high school opportunity for all students.....and their parents! SFHS is the best. I graduated in 2003, and I walked away with plenty of life skills that I continue to use to this day. There is a family atmosphere created at SFHS that I have not seen in my post-high school life. i still regularly see my 15 'best friends' from high school, and i love that. Everything about St. Francis HS makes me feel fortunate to have such a place to send my kids to high school. The atmosphere is warm and friendly with the highest level of achievement as the everyday goal. The administration and teachers alike are enthusiastic and caring and pay close attention to the progress of their students. There are many ways for students to be involved in the St. Francis community with a wide array of great programs including academic clubs, sports, theater, a variety of musical groups and more. I have two children at St. Francis...one about to graduate and the other with two years to go and I am very pleased with the quality of the education they are receiving and the atmosphere in which they are learning! We have had 3 children attend SF. It has been the perfect school for each of them. We are so blessed to have been able to give the gift of a St Francis education to our kids. My daughter has thrived at SFHS. This is a well run school with lots of parent involvement and a strong community feel. St. Francis High School has been a wonderful experience for our entire family. We have a 2011 graduate and two still there. From the teachers to coaches to administrators, everyone at St. Francis feels like family. My wife and I went all thru Catholic schools and wanted the same for our children. We have had two already graduate from Francis, they both had great experiences. Both were admitted to every college they applied to and ended up at their first choice. Our youngest is having the same great experience. From the staff, to the teachers, coaches and AD, we can't be more proud to say we are a Francis Family! When my children were in 8th grade I encouraged them to shadow at all of the high schools in our area. All three of my children chose St. Francis primarily because they felt at home when they visited. The St. Francis community pushed all of my children to be their best academically, athletically and spiritually. They left St. Francis as a more well-rounded person than when they arrived with lifelong friends and mentors. We absolutely love St Francis High School. It offers the complete education for a student. Academics, exceptional teachers, great leadership and direction, and too many extracurricular opportunities to count, I am pretty sure that almost every student is involved in an activity. My children who have graduated from St Francis have done very well in college. True, we have great public schools in Wheaton, but I wouldn't trade the St Francis experience for anything. We have had three children attend St Francis high school. We are thrilled with the impact the school has had on each one of our children. They have all been challenged academically. They have grown in their faith. The best way we can sum up their teachers is that as a group, they care. We couldnt be happpier with the overall experience the school provided. We have had a fantastic experience at St. Francis School! My son transferred from the Wheaton Public Schools and was warmly welcomed by students, teachers, coaches and staff here at St. Francis. The environment is immensely supportive and there is a place for everyone. Extra curricular activities are many and varied with outstanding coaches and club sponsors. There is an emphasis on providing for the needy and community service is a part of the curriculum. Faith and kindness are ever present at St. Francis. Prayer is a part of every day and students attend monthly Mass with student vocalists, musicians, liturgical and eucharistic ministers. Parents are invited to attend and many do so. St. Francis Masses are quite inspirational. Parental support and volunteerism is encouraged and one of the many attributes that makes St. Francis so uniquely special. We feel privileged to be a part of this positive, welcoming St. Francis community! My daughter is just about to finish her first year at St. Francis. She loves the school and her friends. We are all very happy to be sending her there. It would be very easy and much cheaper to send her to the local public high school down the road, but SF is the right choice for her and our family. Kudos to the wonderful Fine Arts program at SF! Very disappointing behavior from the school that is not living up to its charter. Cancelling a football game with another school because it is a "bad neighborhood" is unchristian and unprofessional and unnecessary. Perhaps if more expensive school kids met poor school kids the world would be a better place. So disappointed. They spent hundreds of thousands of dollars to build a football stadium that constantly floods, for a football team that isn't that great. But they can't find money to get air conditioning for the school, something that every student would benefit from installing. Or they could use the money to build a bridge to get students and their families safely across Roosevelt. My daughter has thrived at St. Francis. The academics are challenging, and her teachers are accessible and encouraging if she has any questions or problems with a course. Her confidence has risen. There are numerous extra curricular activities for students to become involved with, and she is taking the opportunity to explore different clubs and interests. She is getting a good foundation academically and spiritually for life after high school.

column3: They have some good teachers and academic programs, but if you aren't an athlete you are considered to be 2nd class in the category of importance there. There were students there when the Avon Lake Shoremen were contending for a championship that got suspended long enough to get off suspension in time to play in the next football game. The administration is very inconsistent with rules and school policy and there are different consequences for one students actions than that of another student depending on their social status. I left Avon Lake High School early and switched to ECOT after begging my parents for months and having to prove that the treatment there was unfair. Try to avoid this school system if you can. They care about academics but if you aren't planning on attending a high quality college the counselors think less of you. After contemplating a Catholic - Private School education for my two sons - we decided on ALHS. A terrific choice - great teachers, programs, mentors and experience. A very rare combination of small community spirit, where the high school anchors the town. Perhaps that's why their mascot is the Shoremen...... plus the community supports when needed - by passing the majority of levies. A true find !! Having had two kids graduate from ALHS, we have many positive memories and experiences to cherish as we all move on to bigger and better things. Everything was great, except the marching band. Yes, the kids work extremely hard, but the halftime shows are always incredibly boring. Everyone has noticed the opposing band getting a more enthusiastic response from our crowd, and the reason is because we have all been to more entertaining funerals than the shows that we have been forced to watch for several years. It would be nice if the administration would look back and re-examine the purpose of the halftime show: to entertain the crowd. Back in the seventies and parts of the eighties the band was well known as a huge, loud and entertaining band. Not anymore. It is too bad that we don't have a quality band to go along with the quality football team. (By the way, I was a season ticket holder until a couple of years ago, and the same comments that I have written were spoken every Friday night by many people in my section who are very well known and influential in the community.) Besides the lousy halftime entertainment, Avon Lake High School is great! Most of the teachers are horrible, they don't teach, teachers take a really long time to grade tests and HW. MANY OF THE TEACHERS SHOULD BE FIRED, if tons of kids are doing poorly in your class it has to be you the teacher, lack of ability to teach. No one in that school cares if your child is bullied, as a parent u will have to fight for your kid and take aggressive action, the school will not support you. If you are having a hard time with any class you will get very little help from your teacher. You will mostly get an attitude that your annoying. if your teacher is really awful, you are stuck with him or her they will not let you change teachers! if your failing and can not learn from the teacher you still have to stay in that class. nurse is never there so if your sick your on your own. I would like to know as a parent, every test that is given, how many got A's, how many got B's, how many got C's and D's and F's for that given test. They need to be totally transparent on test scores. This holds the teacher accountable for poor passing students. The teacher is absolutely accountable to see that every student succeeds in there class. I would rate my experience at this school very well because it is an overall great school. It's not the worst, but it has declined drastically over the last decade. Need new administration.

column1: Don't bother wasting your time going here. If you want your kid to be boxed in a small environment, then I'd recommend this school. In a school of roughly 200 students, the number of cliques are countless. We sit on the floor for lunch. No one has school spirit, and 80% of the girls attending this school are miserable here. Some teachers just hand you packets and don't even teach. Take it from a student that goes here. I wish I went somewhere else. This school is too small, I wish I had a real high school experience. I don't recommend an all girl school at all they might say it's less drama but trust me there is more. The school has nothing to offer, there is no school spirit at all I wish there was more students and a way bigger campus. The main math teacher is worthless and rude. They have no darn cheerleading team which I always wanted to be on. This school has nothing to offer. Next year is my last year here so I hope there is a big transformation because most of the students here deserve it. Oh plus it's too strict, I just wish I was gone from here. This school made me realize how useless school is and a student isn't suppose to think that. This school is suppose to teach religious ways but the teachers are so mean that they don't set an example. I just wasted 3 years of my life being here, hopeful next year changes my opinion. Honestly, who would want to go to an all girls catholic high school without a gym and with a population of 200 students? When I was an 8th grader, "ALL GIRLS" was not even an option for my high school criteria. HFHS will not offer you that "normal" high school experience, but let's not forget that at every high school, there are others that feel the same way you are feeling. This is the bond I created when I came as a freshman. As messed up as it sounds, the friendships that were made started with how much we didn't want to go there in the first place. We couldn't wait to get out. As the years have gone by, I have personally been humbled by how much we lacked as school. We don't have much to offer like bigger private catholic/public schools, but the administration tries their best to make something out of nothing; whether it comes to sports, music, or academics. It's definitely easy to shine in this school if you get involved and make close bonds with the teachers. This school is definitely not a contender as a first choice, but if you do choose to come here, you make it work and take advantage of the resources you DO have to succeed. Oh and I forgot to mention, tuition is cheap. Absolutely horrible. Too strict, small campus, etc... I REALLY don't recommend sending your daughter here. I am reading these reviews and it strikes me as odd that parents are complaining that the school is small and strict. Isn't that why we are sending our daughters here? If you want a big over crowded school with no rules than send your daughter to a public school!! What a silly complaint to make! The staff and administration are wonderful! I don't really know about these negative reviews. This is an excellent school. The principal, teachers, admission director, etc. are great people. My daughter graduated here and got accepted to one of the prestigious University in California. Remember that in order for kids to do great in school that parents should also be involved in educating their kids. In addition, the students that gave poor scores must be doing badly in school, because they are not studying. Parents should take accountability instead of blaming the school. My daughter love this school. I am very satisfied with the quality of education. I went here for summer school. Nice people chill place. They have a dog for a mascot who walks around like he owns the place. I went here for summer school. Nice people chill campus. Needs More cafe food. The mascot is a dog who walks around like he owns the place. The school was nice and the tour guides were cool, but I told them, "Honestly, we probably could not afford this school."They said, "Don't worry honey, we'll take care of the money.""I know I'm smart and I'll work hard." came from my lips, I heard, "Great, you'll qualify for academic scholarships!"I said, "I live too far from this place", they said, "Don't worry we provide transportation so get the worried look off your face."I asked if I am guaranteed to get all honors classes, he said, "You'll get everything you want" as he wiped his eye glasses.The school was okay until I uncovered the lies. I got taken out of class and I just cried!I was taken out of class because we could not pay the tuition.I believe I told them that during the tour, but I guess they did not listen!I said, "I have all A's what happened to my scholarship. They looked away knowing one did not exist.I said, "What happened to my sweet ride to school?" Their snarky expression implied, "We never said that, you stupid fool!"I asked, "What about the guarantee to get my desired classes?" They shrugged and whispered, "We have more seats to fill with tight little assets."Lie, after lie, after lie.But still they deny, they deny, they deny.Looking back, the entire experience was quite odd. The word that describes it, is the word FRAUD.Not So Holy Family. Thank goodness I graduated from this school. It was definitely a humbling experience. The transition from high school to college is taking an absolute toll on me. I'm not prepared for college. Everyone around talks about how rigorous their high school and how the workload definitely prepared them, but honestly you can cruise through Holy Family with a 3.5 EASY... but don't be fooled because once you take that AP Test, don't expect to pass LOL. Once you take the SAT, expect an average of 1600, maybe even lower as a class culminative average SAT score. College Prep? Absolutely not. This is honestly a great school that does not get enough credit. It might not have such an excellent name compared to other schools out there but that is because it is different from those. It does not focus on "being known for sports, theatre, arts, etc." rather it focuses on the individual students. The small school gives a family type of sisterhood where we strive to only support and better one another. Holy Family may not be as rich, popular or large as other schools but it is a school where women make history. It's pretty cool going to high school that doesn't have too many students and has a small campus compared to other high schools. A lot of the students her are very nice and the teachers are very supportive. Incredibly positive. Holy Family has been receiving a lot of positive attention in the last year and I can see why. This is an incredibly good small school for girls. I have been around the community for years and have seen first hand the positive changes and growth the school has made in a short time. It's one of the best girls schools in the area, for sure. I have enjoyed my time here. It's been one of the best schools I've worked at. Very welcoming. I have been working with the school for years and have seen a major evolution in its facilities, staff and programs. They are deeply committed to girls and their success. My daughter has just started her freshman year and is absolutely thrilled even if she’s attending remotely. She feels very welcomed and loves the campus and faculty. Ms. Peters is an incredible individual who makes us feel right at home. Our overall experience at this school has been very positive and we are very happy with our decision to enroll our daughter here. Holy Family has been a perfect fit for our daughter. The small size and the caring staff and faculty has allowed our daughter to flourish in high school. She is involved in campus ministry, ASB, ambassadors, and multiple clubs. Her teachers are all really caring and are passionate about their jobs. One policy that my daughter loves is their sports no cut policy. This will allow her to play sports all year long and participate in sports that she would not be able to play at other schools. Our daughter has been able to take a computer programming class at Glendale Community College, which is the JC close to Holy Family, and will take more classes this spring at GCC. If you are looking for a small and friendly school where your daughter can thrive, I believe that Holy Family of Glendale would be a perfect fit! Holy Family has been a tremendous blessing for my sister. I wanted her to go to my school, another all girls catholic school in the area, but she decided that Holy Family was a better fit. I believe that my sister made the right choice. She currently has all 4.0 and is involved in many after school activities. My sister was extremely shy in elementary school and seems to be coming out of her shell in high school, growing more confident every day. Recently, I had a chance to go to one of her volleyball practices. I was very jealous. I knew their coach was good because I have played against him for the past three years, but I did not know how good. He might be the best coach I have ever seen, besides Coach Angel. My sister is so lucky to have him as a coach. Volleyball is not her best sport and she probably would not have played at most schools. The no cut policy gave her the opportunity to be a part of the volleyball team. Now she is receiving great coaching and will improve her skills as a volleyball player. If you want a small school and caring environment I believe that Holy Family High School is the right place for you. My experience at Holy family has been a blessing. Prior to coming to Holy Family I attended a coed school. It was difficult to attend a school with both boys and girls. Anytime I raised my hand to answer questions people would make fun of me. This is not the case with holy family. The students are friendly and the teachers encourage student participation. All the teachers are extremely nice and only want the best for you. All the teachers also take an hour out of their day for office hours to help you with any questions you might have. Holy family is also a very small school which means that you are not just a number, all the teachers know you by name and are able to tell when you may need extra help. My favorite part of Holy Family is that all clubs, extracurricular activities, and sports are all included in tuition! For our sports teams there is a no cut policy which means you can join a team even if you've never played that sport before, and if you're not interested in sports you can be a manager for a sport. This has allowed me to feel comfortable joining volleyball, asb, campus ministry, and ambassadors club. I also plan on joining basketball and softball during winter and spring. My daughter is a freshman at Holy Family High school and we could not be happier for having selected this school for her. At first, we were a little concerned of the small size, but now we see the benefits. Not only do the teachers know all the girls but so does the staff. They know each girl by name, making it difficult for a student to fall through the cracks. We are delighted that our daughter has made the transition to high school seamlessly. She is involved in sports, student council, and campus ministry. Holy Family has truly inspired my daughter to recognize her gifts, discover her voice and find her purpose. Holy Family is an excellent school for girls. The students there are very friendly and the teacher are very helpful with preparing girls for college. Since there are only a few students per class, every student is given utmost guidance towards holistic excellence. Additionally, they give importance to the safety of the students and choose to push through online classes instead of face-to-face sessions while there is a pandemic. I'm excited for my child to do more activities, meet friends, and be immersed in the school as soon as the situation allows. Holy Family Catholic College Preparatory High School that is located in Glendale, California is a true hidden gem if you are interested in an all-girls exceptional school. It is a school that has very encouraging faculty, compassionate staff, amazing students, involved administration and caring parents. The class sizes are small enough for each instructor to get to know every student and support them when needed, inspires them to strive to do their best, and holds values of giving back to the community. The students are encouraged, guided, and prepared to attend higher levels of education upon graduating. Since there the school is a small school the students there have an advantage because they get much attention from teachers for there academics. It a wonderful school and would recommend. Holy Family High School is a small catholic school that parents needs to consider for their daughters. We had our eldest daughter study here and with the development we saw in her, we decided to have our 2 other daughters study here too. The school is small but the academics are very good; our daughters were able to join clubs of their interests; the sports program have been improving; and the facilities are very clean. We wish though that they have better facilities for volleyball practices. The teachers and faculty have always been very nice and very supportive. The school's focus on the character, faith, and education is really commendable. Holy Family High School is a great school for discovering who you are. There are so many different choices for clubs and extra-curricular, and because of this students can learn what they like and dislike. As a player for the volleyball and track and field teams, the teachers and coaches are very understanding about the struggles of balancing sports with school work. They are all also very encouraging of the athletes, letting us feel more motivated both in sports and academics. Great school for anyone’s daughter!! This school is small and perfect for individualized learning. I am a student here and I love it!! This school was welcoming from the very beginning, and there are lots of events and activities to look forward to here. Holy Family is a great school to express your leadership skills. Being a student at HF, I love how the student body has a voice in planning events or leading the school with things such as ASB or simply participating in extra curricular activities. I love how small it is as well because the student: teacher ratio is great because you truly do get attention from the teacher in any time you need help with anything. I attended HFHS and it was such an amazing experience. The friends I had in High School are still my good friends after 26 years. We still get together and remember the good times we had in school. I love the fact that I went to a small school because you knew everyone and all the teachers made such an impact my life. Honored to be a fellow Gaels. Currently both my Goddaughter's are attending Holy Family and I see how much they have grown. They have become more confident and want to make a difference not just for themselves but for everyone. HFHS is really helping the girls become strong independent woman. I would not be surprise if in the future we hear the President or Vice President graduated from Holy Family. As a student who is currently a junior, I am very happy to say that I am true GAEL because it has helped me recognize my gifts. This school gave me wonderful experiences each year with many opportunities to discover myself. The community is overall wonderful and it truly feels like a family. Life is funny, one day you have a new baby girl, and the next you find yourself choosing a high school for her.What most called my attention to HFHS is their emphasis on getting students ready for college, you can find that on their website. And after that on their parents' meetings.All is important academics, faculty, facilities, ...however most important now, is who has my daughter become. I feel her happiness when she talks about her classmates, teachers, and her interactions with girls that are at different grades. Give me great sense of community, and supportI feel we made a good choice, and I hope you can too. My daughter’s freshman year has been a great one so far. I’m glad I chose Holy Family High. It’s a small campus with small class sizes. My daughter is doing excellent in all her classes. The teachers are wonderful and doing a terrific job due to Covid and Zoom learning. The school year is almost coming to an end. I’m thankful for everyone at Holy Family High. For keeping a positive attitude during these uncertain times. My daughter is now a sophomore at this school-I can’t be prouder of how excited my daughter is to go to college- Holy is doing a perfect job in preparing her to realize her passion and dreams . Cant wait to see her sore- thank you Holy Family High School! Holy Family is committed to providing relevant programs and services to form a school community to be God-loving, evangelizing and responsible members of society. My niece graduated from Holy Family HS four years ago and loved the school’s atmosphere. I believe the school prepared her well and instilled great learning and social habits that she has and will use as she now graduates from college. As a student of Holy Family I believe that the teachers strive to help to improve and make sure the students are getting the best possible education. I'm sure I made the right decision when I picked up Holy Family High School, I feel I'm in home. The staff is very welcoming and friendly. During this pandemic, the learning process has been very helpful and understanding. My sibling attends this school and she appreciates how the teachers thoroughly dissect the material being taught. My god daughter is a freshman in high school, and she has learned so much. The smaller class is beneficial when it comes to learning. My god daughter feels confident enough to participate and ask questions when she is confused. The teachers are amazing and assign a reasonable amount of work. Holy Family has been a blessing to our daughter, even though this year has been very hard for everyone, especially for a freshman who was looking forward to her first year in High school, never the less my daughter has very much enjoyed the classes on line. Teacher work very hard to help make the high school experience on line a great one. She had the opportunity to interact with other students virtually as well. Ever since she experienced shadow she new it was the best school for her, super friendly & inviting students, very safe environment. They have lots of elective classes to choose from. Teachers & staff continue to work hard to help my daughter grow in faith as well as encourage her daily. Holy Family High School is a great school for an all girls environment. The campus is clean and provides a good learning experience for all the students. Overall it is an above-average school with an amazing staff of teachers and i would greatly recommend this school to anyone that prefers an all girls school!!! Holy Family High School is a great school for girls. The teachers are very approachable and the students are very friendly. It’s very easy to make friends here and there are also many different sport teams. Holy Family High School is one of the best schools in academics, leadership, and extracurricular activities. The school has extraordinary teachers who focus on the wellbeing of its students. The faculty is amazing and always a step ahead, ready to assist parents and students. This school has definitely helped my niece continue her success in academics. Having smaller classes gives more attention to students. It also has great events giving the students opportunities to grow socially. It has been a continued success throughout her time here and the family is so happy that she attends this great school. “My daughter has enjoyed her freshman year at holy family even with the trials of dealing with the pandemic. The school has been very supportive and organized academically. They recently started playing sports again, it has been a fun start to the summer”. Holy Family has provided me with courses that focus on my individual talents and gives me direction into what I would like to do in the future. From teachers to the students, it’s a happy environment where you can pick up social skills and get a sense of college. My daughter is senior at holy family high schools. She feels well prepared for college and has enjoy playing sports and being involved in school clubs .we like the school and the staff very much. I highly recommend Holy Family High School for there daughters education. They offer quality education and spiritual practice. My niece loves Holy Family High School because of its warm abs friendly atmosphere. The quality teachers the school has is excellent because I see how academically prepared my niece is becoming. The school offers a lot of activities which help the girls become active and envolved. I highly recommend this school. Holy Family has been great for my daughter. She enjoys going there every single day. Holy Family has very good education and sports. They are very strong in faith. We chose Holy Family High School initially for its catholic faith-based environment. We were looking for a campus that demonstrated goodness, stability, respect, and recognition of the value of being human. We did not need to compromise on academics, sports, creativity or college as a goal. The instructors do not coddle, they challenge. The academics are solid. It is a small, serene, comfortable school. My granddaughters have changed in this school. They are more confident. They have dear friends. They find the administration and faculty approachable, supportive, and kind. They are able to be themselves. An unexpected pleasure was the sports program. Learning to be part of a team. Striving to become better through sports. Finding out how to accept defeat and victory with grace.This year the business entrepreneurial class has filled them with excitement and joy for the future.We have needed this after the rough Covid period.It is a place designed for growth. They have the time and the peace to think. The big world is waiting. And they will be prepared. As a parent of a current Holy Family student, I'm happy to say that I love a lot of things about this school. This school created a new journey for my daughter and helped discover her talents Our daughter has been at Holy Family for 2 years now and we are extremely pleased with our overall experience. The staff and teachers show great dedication and passion for the students and parents. We look forward to our daughter’s academic journey alongside the great support of Holy Family HS. She plays in both the volleyball and soccer team and has improved in her social skills and physically as well. I am so happy we ended up being part of the Holy Family team. My daughters look forward to participating in the school events and activities. This school has much to offer and values each of the students. The teachers and staff are kind and always willing to reach out for any concerns or updates. They help students discover their gifts and how to utilize it. I'm a proud parent of a senior at Holy Family. My daughter is an excellent student and I owe this to the wonderful faculty and staff at HF. I'm so grateful to be able to send my daughter to such a safe and loving community. I'm a current senior at Holy Family. I transferred here my sophomore year and absolutely fell in love with my school. I have the absolute sweetest classmates and the most experienced teachers who make challenge me academically while also making learning so much fun! My daughter Francyne started her freshmen year at Holy Family during this pandemic and she is now a Sophomore. She loves her classes and teacher’s at Holy Family. I have never seen her this motivated or this excited to learn. The daily schedule she follows helps her organize her school work and helps her keep up with her homework. She is more focused and motivated to learn. She speaks highly of her teachers and tells me how much she has learned so far.I love the family atmosphere and the values that Holy Family embodies. I am so excited to see my daughter grow and reach her full potential in this school! I have no regrets sending her here! Great school! Great staff! I’ve known about this all girls Catholic High School from acquaintances I’ve had since my high school days in the late 1980s.Because of the great experiences and education my friends had, my wife and I decided to enroll our 9th grade daughter to this school. We were not disappointed. The staff are the best the facilities are outstanding and modern. The student to teacher class ratio is another positive fact about the school.Public high schools are all over crowded and students do not get the best focus in learning. Especially for the girls, there are no boys to distract their studies.Not only that our daughter had found her two best friends while attending this school, she finally felt the sense of belonging as Holy Family is now a part of her heart and her life.Although private schools usually are not cheap to attend, this school offers ways to apply for discounted rates for those that are a little tight on budget.Because we like what we see and happy on how our daughter had become in her first year 2021-2022, we just re-enrolled her again for the upcoming school year 2022-2023 to continue her education at Holy Family High School.It’s a great school to prepare our child for college. holy family is a great school and it has taught my daughter a great work ethic and responsibility. the clubs and sports are amazing. the teachers are very attentive to the students needs and grades. great school! Holy Family is a fantastic high school with aprincipal who genuinely cares about the successof all students. Teachers are generally caring andsupportive of their students, the resources areexcellent, and the students are a tight groupwho care about and support one another.Academics are rigorous, school spirit is strong,students feel safe, and a positive attitude is constantly fostered. I love being a student at Holy Family! Going to school here has impacted my life in so many ways and has made me the person I am today. Teachers are so nice and understanding and you can tell they really care about your success! I'm so glad I made the decision to enroll my daughter to Holy Family! I recommend every other parent to send their daughter to Holy Family! Holy Family High School is a great school for students. Teachers support the students and motivate them to achieve higher. My daughter has frown in her leadership skills and is confident of her skills and talents and ready for college. I highly recommend the school. Holy Family High School inspires its students to become women of faith. I’ve seen my niece grow in service to others and to the community and in leadership. The school provides the students with an excellent academics program and four-year college preparatory education. Students will be challenged and will grow, learn, and thrive. They will be able to run for Student Council, participate in the many clubs at school and in athletics. Holy Family High School is a campus where students develop a profound appreciation for independent, critical judgment and creative expression and will be prepared to make lifelong decisions. My daughter is in the junior year of her high school journey. I have seen her grow as a scholar and a young lady at HF. She heads two clubs and serves in the study body. HF has helped her develop academically, while teaching her how to balance her studies and extra curricular activities. Our daughter has been at Holy Family for 3 years now and we are extremely pleased with our overall experience. The staff and teachers show great dedication and passion for the students and parents. We look forward to our daughter's academic journey alongside the great support of Holy Family HS. Additionally their sports program has been immensely helpful to our daughter's social skills, leadership, and participation. She also always has sources that provide help when she has struggled with classes and material. Thank you Holy Family for being an amazing encouragement and help to our daughter's goals.

column3: Now upon graduation 2013, I can say that Gloucester High School was an incredible school for my son. The NJROTC program was far surpassing in excellence. The courses open to students to pursue careers right out of high school were varied and backed up with thorough instruction on campus or off. Those pursuing college were given constant options of dual credit earned while in high school. My summation would be - that if a student was serious about getting as much out of their education as possible ~ there were staff available to help them make their goals. The NJROTC program is excellent in guiding a student in structure, discipline and a great peer group of cadets helping other cadets even in academics when subjects might prove a difficult challenge. I thank Dr. Beverage for the great four years my student had as I'm sure as principal much was attributable to his steering the course of this academic ship. Thank you... There are too many students for the size of the building. It is the only high school in Gloucester County. The building desperately needs renovation. Teachers telling students to look up videos to learn instead of teaching,not many good programs, TV production is a great class for students but really need a lot of help on acting and audio, need new coaches because Gloucester high has been losing for many of years. Just like for my kids to get a good education and be proud of where they graduated from. The varied Career and Technical programs available for the students are such a positive aspect of GHS. There is something for everyone. School is going downhill fast! It’s time to rethink staffing. I graduated from this school and now have children who attend. I left Gloucester due to the military and came back because of the strong community. There was never any other choice for where I’d settle down. Pleased to have my own children graduate from here and call it home. Administration, teachers, and other faculty members care about the children in this county. It’s a wonderful place to live and grow up. I love this school.just had 1 graduate this year .now another in 9th grade .I feel if the parents or family members stay connected.be involved and follow up with your kids ,this ultimately will project a positive influence .not just on your kids but the staff .teachers.princiole as well...totally loving all the teachers and commitment to their students current student here, this school is so depressing

column1: 2 of my children completed all 3 years at Desert Hills high school. My son is a quadriplegic he uses a power wheel chair. Every student and teacher took the time to be friend him and make his high school experience the best time of his life! My daughter also was surrounded by St. George's finest teachers and students!! My school is what i would tell other people that it is the best school in our district, because the people here are amazing they all get along, and people talk to get other they don't just stick in there clicks they migrate, are social. I like it a lot, because it isn't like any other school in the district they help their students when they need it and make sure they are on track to graduate and the staff is wonderful. My child's school is the greatest! The people are wonderful here.The staff is wonderful they help their students get on track and when I need something they get it done. I am currently a senior at Desert Hills, and I absolutely love my school experience here. There are plenty of AP, honors, and CE options available for students who wish to enroll. As well as classes that move at a slower pace for those who need that. The staff and administration are wonderful and I can definitely see the deep love they have for the students in the way they are so dedicated to their work. The only problem with Desert Hills is the many cliques. When I moved here, it seemed that everyone already had their designated "group" to which they remained. Nobody really branches out from their groups. This was rather intimidating when moving to a new school. The student council holds a welcoming party for new students, and that makes things a bit easier. But I do wish that there wasn't such a big division among the student body in the form of cliques. I transferred to this school, and the thunder family treats new kids great! The boundaries include areas with lots of growth, so there are new students every month! As soon as I walked through the doors I was able to make friends and surround myself with awesome friends and teachers!

column3: We've had three kids come through FHS, all very different from eachother, but all found ways to connect and feel good about their high school experience. They have been well prepared for college and each has scored a 28 or above on the ACT. We can't say enough good things about Frenship. Frenship is an awesome school; from caring teachers to outstanding fine arts programs, the school has so much to offer each student. Frenship High School is an amazing school!!! Everyone at the school was amazing when my son went to school there. They have a zero tolerance bullying policy and they stick to it 100%!!!! They were all so kind and caring when my dad passed away unexpectedly from leukemia in September 2020, the beginning of my son's senior year. Thankfully my dad didn't have COVID, but it was still a complete nightmare for all of us!!!! Everyone from the principal, to the teachers and nurses were concerned about my son and check on him on a regular basis after he returned to school. Frenship High School is a VERY safe school!!!! They have their own police department that patrols the schools on a regular basis. All doors are kept locked except for one of the front doors and you can only go into the office. You can't access the rest of the school or the students at all. They are extremely protective of their students and they do everything possible to keep them all safe under any and all circumstances!!! Frenship High School built a 9th grade center for just the 9th graders to attend before moving to the high school, which was wonderful!!! When my son was in the 9th grade center, a student at the high school made a stupid comment, which they took VERY seriously!!!!! They locked down all of the schools in Wolfforth and they had the Wolfforth police, the Frenship ISD police and the Lubbock police and swat team out there. They did EVERYTHING to assure there was no threat to the students and that they were safe. Thankfully they were all safe. During that time, I texted my son a lot. I knew that the teachers would understand us calling or texting our kids excessively to make sure they were safe. Lots of parents went there even though we were told not to.
