The extracurriculars go above and beyond any other school in the area. The classrooms and campus are new and well-maintained. Wolfpack spirit is so extraordinary that theyve even won an award for being the most spirited school in the nation. You can beat the friendly enviornment, challenging courses, dedicated staff, and wolfpack spirit! My child has not had one bad thing to say about this school. Being a military family, we've been to many schools. She began as a freshman and is now in the middle of her sophmore year. She is in the AFJROTC program and enjoys it. She does really well, and the teachers provide online tools for students. This provides the children to be self reliant. She is in AP english and AP world History. This is her first year taking advance placement classes and I have never had to contact her teachers. I've rated teacher, principal and parent involvement at 4 stars mainly because I haven't had too much interaction with them except on back to school night. That night, many parents were present considering it is high school. There are many sports programs, plenty of clubs, and fun activites for the children. School spirit is awesome. My school is one of it's kind. It is the school most coveted in the Riverside County area. This schoolyear of 2013-2014 there were 1000+ freshmen enrollments due to its reputation as a great academic school. The students, the faculty, the parents, the whole community is what makes the school so excellent - the spirit is alive in this learning institute we call Great Oak, it stands high mighty and proud with all its branches and leaves that make up the Great Oak. We, the people, are its leaves and branches. That's why I am so proud to be a Wolfpack, I'm so proud to be a part of this Great Oak. My daughter is a Senior this year and my son has just started as a Freshman. My children have attended private schools in the past and the education they are receiving at Great Oak can only be compared to Centennial in San Diego. Both are enrolled in the IB program and my daughter has also completed several AP classes. Excellent school, the IB program is great if you have a high performing student, it really pushes them to do their best. My child graduated from this school IB program and was admitted to MIT, many others in his generation were admitted to Harvard, Stanford, Berkeley, etc. Sports are good, cross country is among best in the state, ranked nationally. The only drawback is that is a very large school, so you loose the individual recognition. NewSenior This Year My student came to Great Oak as a new senior. The counselors made it a smooth transition. They also have a few "meet n greets" for new Seniors. The staff and leadership has so many things in place to ensure new kids get acclimated and can smoothly integrate. My kids transferred from a small pricey private school is the immediate area. They do not hold a candle to GOHS. The QUALITY and PROFESSIONALISM of administrators, teachers, etc. is the BEST you will find. GOHS offers as challenging of an academic program as you or your high school student desire. Many wonderful sport programs to choose from and there is a club for everyone. Kids are the best at this school! It is large in size, but we feel it will better equip our kids for the transition to college. My Child Is Now A Junior At GOHS And Has Excelled In So Many Ways, I Can't Say Enough About The Staff And Teachers Here Are Helpful In So Many Ways, And Hold This School To Such Standards. This School Is All About Education. There Anti Bullying Is One To Be Proud Of . You Constantly Are Hearing Other (TV) Schools Talk Badly About GO, I Have Even Heard Moms Speak Ill And They Wounder Why There School Is Hurting. My Child Was A "C" Average Now A "B+" Student And Owe It To This Amazing School. As A Parent This School Gets My Seal Of Approval!! Not To Mention They Have A Incredible Athletic Department WitH Sports Ranging From Mountain Biking & Horse Riding...... This school is AMAZING.Very spirited and positive. Very easy to make friends. Also in an awesome area. The teachers really want to help you.They actually know what they are talking about. I literally have nothing bad to say about GOHS. I went there freshman ear and had the best high school year of my life. Sadly, I moved out of state and started a new school. Very hard to leave such a good school. If you are moving or trying to decide what school to go to, choose here. There wouldn't be over 3500 students there if it was a bad school. Great Oak has amazaing teachers and staff. I could not have asked to attend a better school. School is awesome! Teachers and staff go above and beyond to make every student and parent feel welcome :) Horrible school! If u want a good future for your kids go to tvhs instead They have a BIG problem here with staffing qualified teachers in classes where teachers are on leave. Many teacers are "Missing" on leave of absences for various reasons and the students that have the misfortune of being in these classes are completely disadvantaged!!! These students are TOTALLY unprepared for AP exams. Nobody that heads these departments or is in the administration seems to Care about these students . Why are you putting long-term subs in so many AP classes ? These are students that have chosen to work hard and try to excel in their high school experience and you are completely setting them up for failure. I have talked to many parents whose kids had long-term subs in their AP classes and as a result they were not prepared at all to pass the exams. There are some amazing teachers there but there are also too many that have tenure that are lazy and do not seem to care or have any passion for teaching. They are there for a paycheck. You are not inspiring students to learn with that kind of an attitude. But again when your class there for a paycheck you're not too interested in inspiring people. Best public High School you can find!! Compares or is better then some local Private High schools. Great teachers and excellent athletics programs. Best High School in Riverside County. Awful experience at this school. Administration is horrible, counselors are worse, and teachers are hit and miss. God forbid your child is different from the norm. If they are, then Great Oak has no idea how to handle them. They have a LONG way to go to improve in this area!! We are so happy our kids are in this school! Excellent mix of education and activities! We had 2 students graduate from here. IB and AP classes are helpful for higher education. The sports programs were a great addition for the kids to learn spirit and teamwork. The faculty and staff are amazing. Always willing to help students and parents, and create an incredible learning environment as well as fun social environment for all students. Great communication to parents about events and issues. The culture of college readiness is of the charts! I don't like this school, especially students there. My kids dislike the school for being too strict and force students to do more than they can. My opinion at best this school is a 7/10.

column1: My daughter has attended PK for the past two years. She got in a week before her 4th grade year. PK was certainly the best possible choice we could have made for her. The teachers are awesome and WANT to be there. You can tell they love their jobs and the students. My daughter is very bright and her teachera are constantly working to make sure she's appropriately challenged. I have attended PKY since the fourth grade and I admit that it is a very unique school. The only problem is that there are barely any clubs and whatnot to choose from, which is why BHS tends to look more appealing. Yes, it does have a family "feel" to it, but it can also make you feel as if you aren't able to grow up and explore yourself because the people you see everyday have known you for a long time so a fresh start is almost impossible. There are some cliques but no one really cares about them because they aren't worth the time. This a good school for people who want a stable environment for their children. For people who like adventure, this is NOT the school for you. My daughter started at PK in the 6th grade and has been there 4 years. I could have enrolled her in a magnet program for high achieving students but prefer a more integrated classroom, with little distinction between "regular ed" and "gifted" students. There is a "family feel" to PK and it really seems that the students are known by teachers and administrators. My daughter also reports that the campus is safer than at other schools because they have rarely gone into "lock-down", with no bomb threats, and student infractions are handled quickly. It's true there are relatively few after-school clubs other than band, performing arts and sports.

I am a recent graduate of Cape Central and have been very pleased with the school in general. Although it does not have the best reputation, I received a very positive experience here. Aside from a very wide course selection, they have a multitude of different sports and extra curricular activities available to students. The school is very diverse, and is very accepting of all walks of life. It is an accredited institution that boasts a very new and modern facility. Cape Girardeau is very fortunate to have a public school like this--keep up the good work!!! I am graduating next month, and I am very pleased with the education I received here for 4 years. Lots of these reviews don't reflect what Central really is; we have fantastic teachers who care about the students, lots of opportunities for every kind of student, tons of student diversity, diverse sports to choose from, great facilities, and a WONDERFUL arts program (it could use a little more funding, but even still what we have is great!). The leadership itself isn't the best, which is to be expected, as of right now there is lots of transitioning going on. I have had a great experience here. I would rate this Cape central high school a 1000 stars because this is the best high school in Cape Girardeau Mo

But if they have any behavorial difficulties or learning styles that do not go along with the cookie cutter program this may not be the school for your child. And...considering every child will not attend college, offer at least 1 or 2 vocations in the school. Maybe, that's too much to ask with all the budget cuts. There's gotta be a solution to help our children. O AND LET ME NOT FORGET HE PULLED OUT SOME TEETH GUARDS OUT OF HIS POCKETS AND TOLD MY FRIEND HE'LL BEAT HIS A_ _! REAL LOUD OUTSIDE OF THE SCHOOL O YES HE FOLLOWED US, ALL THIS BECAUSE I WANTED TO WITHDRAWL MY SON SMH SAD. i hate this school they need to get shut down because of poor behavior and loud running up and doen the steps its so nasty spit on the walls bugs every were I am an an alumnus of AHS class of 1965. Our school was one of the best academic High Schools in Washington. We had National Merit winners, Westington House Scholars, service academy appointees, many college scholarship winners. I was in the honors track and received a scholarship for my BA and MA. I also have a doctorate. Many of my classmates are professionals and have achieved much in life. I am so saddened by the decline and failure of my beloved alma mater. I am the Senior Fellow for Ethics and Public Policy for the National Clergy Council, Washingtom, D. C. I enrolled my child in this school and its a Month later and I will be enrolling het OUT!First I would like to say that thr school has been fixed up nice. It actually looked nice and clean in there. The Teachers do try to teach my child have nothing but good things to say about herTeachers. The students totally disrespect the teachers. Kids bring in Mace and gods know what's else. Its always a fight or police (a lot) after school. I reallly wanted to like the school and have my child attend but I fear for her safety in this school and coming out of this school. We had our trepidations about attending Anacostia, but no more. He enjoys going to school everyday. He has nothing but good things to say about Dr Roberts, Mr Comfero, Ms Quick, many other staff members and students. We see big things going on at The Academies at Anacostia. I am also a 2012 Anacostia graduate (shoutout to us!) and recently completed my bachelors of arts in economics (yes, I graduated in three years). Yes the school gets a bit rowdy and learning can't always happen in that environment. The main problem is that students are not understanding the value of education. Once we return to instilling this value in our children.... we'll see the great things Anacostia SHS can do! Our ancestors literally DIED trying to learn to read because they knew how critical it was. Students have to work together to create and maintain a feasible learning community.

column3: I go to Atlee currently. I'm a sophomore there. I'm in IB prep classes, and it's rigorous, but it's prepared me well for all that's coming at me. The teachers really care. If you need help, they're understanding, and they're willing to help you as much as you need. Things are pretty flexible if you're in a rut, and it's great to know that. The food is pretty fantastic, the classes are difficult, but not impossible to succeed in, You're challenged, but not overworked. As far as extracurriculars go, our Arts departments are amazing. Whether you're into band, strings, showchoir, theatre, or physically making artwork, we're well equipped. Theatre is especially awesome at Atlee. I do it all the time, it's a major part of my life. The kids there are like my family, Mr. Wax is an amazing director and mentor, and we're very loving and accepting towards newcomers. Otherwise, our sports teams are pretty great, and there are a lot of opportunities to participate and play. Atlee is just overall awesome. I think we're the best high school in Hanover. We've got a lot of school spirit! Go Raiders! Great school for standard education, one of the best in the country, however, they are not very well equipped to deal with special needs students. I have a graduate and one still in school. I have been very pleased with the commitment of the teachers and their personal investment in the students lives, whether it be staying after school to help with tutoring or showing up at an extracurriculuar event to show their support. My son got into his first choice college and I don't think it would have been possible without teacher and counselor support. I also like that they offer both IB and AP curriculums which gives students more flexibility in their course selections. I love the school spirit that the students show. They are very proud to be a part of the Raider Nation. this school is terrible th eteachers arent good nor is anything.This school is unwelcoming to new students take it from me a current student. Most teachers are extremely helpful and go outside their job description to make sure you understand the material. It's not an old school but some aspects are definitely dated. The class selection is pretty good, it offers classes I'm interested in and a wide range of others. One thing I do not like is the counselors, they try to be helpful but in the end have not helped and I would go as far to say they harmed me and my friends. One example is that they persuade you so much into taking standard classes which even one year of standard can ruin your class rank and overall GPA. Grade inflation is rampant at this school. All the parent has to do is ask a teacher to help raise the student's grade to an "A" and it's done. We moved from the far west end. The curriculum here is so much easier. Shockingly easier. The homework load was half of what my child was doing in previous school. Her grades sure have improved though. But she doesn't have to work hard at all anymore. Also many students won't take the AP exam after taking the AP course because they are afraid it will ruin their GPA - they'd rather take the teacher test hoping that it will be easier. Overall very disappointed in the choice we made to move. Questionable character with some of the teachers. Favoritism for certain families and their children. Overall, I would like to suggest stop covering up issues at Atlee. It is not good for the success of the children. Some teachers are too friendly with the male and female students. Do a survey monkey Very positive. Teachers invest in their students and it shows. My son excelled. Excellent!! My children have received an excellent education that prepared them for college and beyond! However not all students will attend college, and those who don’t have multiple opportunities for training in a trade at the high school level. And those who choose to serve in the military get special recognition at graduation! Excellent overall. From academics, to sports, to arts - I think Atlee was a great experience for kids/young adults. Definitely not perfect, but mixing it all together, it is very well done and the teachers and administration are overall superior. I wish every person/parent could feel this way, and we've been blessed with great kids and circumstances. That's not always the case, but IMO the school itself does very well based on my kids and their friends. We feel blessed and fortunate.

column1: In the past four years, this school has really taken a nosedive academically. test scores are down, teacher respect is nonexistent, and behavior problems (i.e. drug usage, fights, and bullying) are on the rise. Football players are given immunity, and chaos often ensues because of it. I know several of my favorite teachers left (two of them even took a pay cut to go somewhere else) because they were fed up with the administration and plummeting standards. I've compared my education with those that I went to college with, and the differences have been astounding. I had to do so much extra work just to get on their level my freshman year. I would tell anyone living in the area to drive a few extra miles and go to a neighboring town's school. Wonderful school. Even though the facilities are not great, the staff at Gilmer High School are! My kids thrived in at this school and had much success, thanks to the teachers and administrators over the past couple of years. I highly recommend Gilmer High School to anyone. I have a student at this school currently and I have had students in this school over the past ten years. I have been consistently been pleased with the education my children have received. State test scores at this school have been great over a long period of time. Anyone that would say differently is just uniformed. While extra-curricular activities are important, this school has always stressed academics as well. You can look back at this school's academic performance over a long period of time and see for yourself. Try looking at reliable sources of information such as the Texas Education Agency's website. column3: I graduated from Brainerd in 2009 and I now attend Concordia College. I miss the Brainerd Area and the Brainerd High school. The students and staff were great, I learned alot but it was still such a laid back atmosphere. I am going into Biology Secondary Education and I hope I can find a School as great as Brainerd to teach at. Every child is allowed to fail without teachers or administration intervention. It seems as if no one cares about poor grades except the parents. When failing grades are addressed, they are quick to make you feel like a nuisance. A child spends most of their waking hours in a school building. once a child leaves school, a parent has very little control over how to pick up the pieces of a failing system. I don't think this school does a very good job at preparing children for the real world. The real world holds you accountable at your job. If you don't do your job in the real world, there are immediate consequences. If you don't do your job in school there are no consequences except for a bad grade that is very difficult to make up. There are very few inspiring teachers in the entire school. it seems everyone pays attention to the very good students... The easy ones... And leave the quiet confused ones in the dark... It seems to be easier that way for all of them. There are so many good kids that are doing below average....and apparently.... that is acceptable. Brainerd High School is not a great school.

column1: As a student at Gridley High School, I feel as if Gridley High School holds me back from from the full potential of success that I desire as a student. The school in general does not give me the resources desired, such as educational and extra curricular options. Furthermore, coming from a student, I can attest that the school is an abomination to the level of schooling that we as tax payers deserve in "The Golden State". I believe that the school is wonderful. It allows students to express themselves with art, band, and ect. I believe that without Gridley High School i wouldnt be able to get the proper education that i crave. All the schools in the gridley distict are phenomal i love living in Gridley and i love the school in it's self. It's teachers and staff have taught me so much and i am honored to attend Gridley High School and all other schools of gridley before it. The students think the principal is an evil vindictive power-hungry monster who must win win win at all costs... regardless of right and wrong. She cares nothing about teachers, students, or parents. My daughter is an AP student, and her and her classmates can't believe what is being done daily. The kids love their teachers, however, and actually feel bad that the teachers have to work here under this type of so-called leadership. Many amazing teachers who could teach anywhere, and why they picked Gridley who knows! Three of my children have gone to this school, The teachers that I know dont worry about how there students are doing I've had to work harder then them to get my children to pass they classes because the teachers dont show the students how to do the work. They are lazy and dont care if there students are failing. The rate that students go to college from the high school is 50% so that should tell you what kind of job the teachers are doing. If I had to do it again I would have moved to Biggs Ca. And put them in school there Biggs rate of students going to college is 80% I am very impressed with Gridley High School. I have a sophomore and freshman student. My children both have different learning styles and the school has proven to adapt. The counceling department is quick to make adjustments and suggestions to ttheir students. The Ag. department has hired 2 new teachers and the students are having a great year.. I would absolutely recommend Gridley High. I wouldnt change schools. I am athlete and I struggle at times in school. My teachers and coaches take the time and help me to understand all my classes... I feel that each year the school is improving..The school is very small but safe!! My child is a freshman and so far we are having a great year. The community is trying to pass a bond that would make the school much more modern with current the necessities that will enable our children to be completely prepared for the real world... My daughter had a blast this year building floats, and being involved with the band. As a teacher at the school, I can attest to the dedication of the faculty to doing what they feel is in the students' best interest even though students and parents and even administration don't always agree. Are there some great teachers? Of course. Are there some not-so-great? Of course. Is the principal an evil, vindictive monster as some reviewers have suggested? Nope. Before she came to GHS, state test scores and graduation rates were considerably lower than they are now and we sent even LESS students on to higher education. I have seen a tremendous turn around in the school since she came on board with regard to the academics and attention to core subjects. GHS is now one of the highest rated schools in the state when compared to similarly sized schools and for a school with a high language learner population and huge percentage of socioeconomically disadvantaged students (60 percent!), we beat the pants off of other schools in the area when it comes to graduation and high school exist exam rates. We are definitely doing something right - it's a shame that so many cannot see the progress that has been made since 2005.

If you're one of those parents who think teachers should be the only educators in your child's academic career, or you do not firmly stand with the teacher, please don't move here. Auburn Enlarged City School district is right up the road for you. Many teachers and administrators at this school do care and are trying to make changes. They seem to hire teachers who are young but passionate about what they are teaching, and skilled at doing so. If your child is a "go getter" they will do great here. Academics for us were great.

column1: I graduated from this school in 2003. I went there from 2nd grade on. I sure missed Mr. Crews when he left but it is an excellent school. Mrs. hart is the best teacher in the entire world! Mrs. Landry is so sweet and fun and helped me so much. The only problem I know of with the school is last I was aware of they did not offer Spanish classes anymore. I mean the students dont need to know French, they need Spanish especially considering the local population of different languages. I am a SHHS student , and I wouldn't go to any other high school besides Scotts Hill High School. The classes are great , and we have AMAZING teachers!! The school is very safe and secure. Mr. Norton and Ms. Ivy are very nice and will help you if you need it. "Once a Lion always a Lion" Class of 2014 As far as I am concerned this is by far the best school to send your child to if you want them fully prepared for college. My daughter who is in the Class of 2011 graduated early and is now attending college 6 months ahead of her classmates. While at SHHS she was always treated with respect and kindness. Mr. Norton and Ms. Ivey are excellent leaders and the teachers are always there to help your child. A special thanks to Ms. Belinda and Ms. Sandy in the Ayers Foundation office for all of their hard work, the amount of scholarships and grants that they helped my daughter find and apply for got her into college early and at very little expense to me. ONE A LION ALWAYS A LION, Thank you SHHS!!

column3: I have one child at heritage and one child attending the middle school. I have experienced city schools and in my opinion they do not hold a candle to RV. The teachers work hard to give you weekly progress reports and they keep the lines of communication open. There are many activities offered like summer sports (tee-ball, baseball etc..) and a running club for the elementary school students to encourage fitness. Character education is taught and they have a great bully policy. If you look at the district progress report it beats MCS hands down and has for years! The staff is great and I will never go back to mediocre city schools. Excellent schools just like their rating!

column1: I moved my small family from Caswell County, NC to the Tunstall High School district because of Tunstall's reputation of being the best school in the area and this is what we found: a principle who never smiles or has a kind word to say except to a very select few of her buddies, you can never get through to anyone on the phone, the couple of very nasty teachers who feel it is more important to be popular than do their job make the school day a very long and sad one for many of the students, virtually no communication from the school to the parents, no uplifting events promoting honor students, very few extra curricular activities (other than sports), very low student moral, last minute notice of parent teacher meetings, I have been disappointed in the staff on many levels and if this is the best the school system has to offer I feel very sorry for the children of the State of Virginia. However, there are a handful of very good teachers at Tunstall who do their job well and professionally with kindness: Ms. Dallas, Mr. Sleeper, Ms. White, & Mr. Myers, that is all, for now. Students all said "Ma'am" and "Sir"; quiet hallways, polite teachers, friendly office staff--one of the principals was a bit, less than enthusiastic but I suppose I would be too if i were a principal. God bless THS! Great school, with a great parent support system.

column3: As I read through these comments, I was literly shocked by some of the comments on here. I have had my son in a couple different schools, and he now goes to GHS, and is excelling beetter there than with any previous school. It is a safe school, the teachers truley care for their students from what I have seen, and to hear other parents bash this school truley amazes me. Maybe if your kid wasn't lazy, and didn't try to succeed, maybe they would have done better. GHS is a great school, try sending your kid to Two Rivers, and see how that one goes over!. I think it's interesting to read these comments, however, I wonder how many truly haven't experienced GHS firsthand and are just writing out of spite. Regarding the post on December 13, stating that GHS is lacking in teaching and preparation for college, I have a rebuttal. I have 3 graduates from GHS. My first struggled with Math skills but was offered tutoring after school by the late Sherry Freeland. With her help, my child improved greatly and graduated to go on to become a business professional. My second and third were active in many leadership roles while scoring mid 30's on ACTs. They both were awarded many scholarships, and went on to do well in college. My last has maintained a Summa cum Laude rank throughout college years. This is only from the base starting point of teachers that showed how to succeed and the desire to learn which GHS teachers instill. As far as sports favoritsm, everyone likes a "hero". But I do not ever "run into" any teacher that my children have had in the past (many years later) that those teachers do not ask about them or their current lives. That is the difference of a teacher and someone that cares. GHS has both. I work with a very professional group of educators. The atmosphere is very upbeat and condusive to the students learning and safety. As with any school, the student will get out of it equal to what they put into it. The student that is there to learn and have a positive experience will do so. The student that is there to cause problems will do so and bring problems on himself. Attitude is everything. I moved from Davidson county in 1990 just so my kids could attend their neighborhood schools. Both my sons attended Watauga, Greenbrier Middle & Greenbrier HS. They graduated with kids they went to kindergarden with. Can you say that about other areas? That alone means alot but all through their time at these schools, they had wonderful teachers except for maybe 1 or 2 here & there but you get that at any school. My youngest graduated in 2009 and we are very proud of all the schools and strongly recommend them to anyone. Education wise it was a good school but the leadership at the school is terrible .You have to be in the family circle and Greenbrier to be treated fairly if not you get put to the bottom of the list . My children came from Williamson Co schools where education matters. When I saw how Greenbrier students were allowed cell phone use (I check my child's cell phone usage in class and was appalled at them being able to text more than 50 times a day at school. Needless to say they are no longer allowed to bring their phones to school. Shouldn't the teachers be aware this is going on? Apparently not. SAD to say the least. I'm moving to another county in other for my children to get a better education to prepare for college. I would give this school a 2 out of 5 stars. Surely there are worse schools out there who deserve the 1 star rating, but we chose this community to move into because of the high ratings of this school. The ratings are wrong. The school itself is average at best, and the kids are positively hateful. Intelligent children should be celebrated, because in this community they are as rare as diamonds. But they are not celebrated. They are teased and mocked and belittled for their intelligence. The leadership did nothing. Some of the teachers try to be supportive and positive, and the vice-principals have tried to be supportive and understanding, even if they are completely ineffective at stopping the bullying. This school has very hateful small-minded community of kids who are not welcoming to outsiders. If you are an outsider with intelligent kids, do not move here. If you do move here, homeschool your kids. To get straight to the point my child will not be coming here anymore, all I know is that he was working while going to school here and ended up stealing money. The school must have had a bad influence on him with the wrong crowd. I am appalled.

column1: The academics in the school are below par. The teachers seem to act like the students and would prefer to fit in with the kids as oppose to be the adult teaching in the classroom. The district is small as well as the school budget so basically, the teachers aren't the cream of crop. If I had the money I would send my kids to private school, but unfortunately, I'm not able to. The school also lacks in the athletics department offering only a handful of sports. DHS is not a recommended school at all. The school teachers are know as being horrible in a discriminatory or sexist way. Small school with plenty of resources to help students excel. My kids came from a “blue ribbon” school. It I have to say I made the right choice to move back and send my kids to the schools. The teachers are wonderful! My eldest was having issues with Math or at least at the “blue ribbon” school. She is excelling, her confidence is nothing like I’ve seen before! The kids at the school are friendly, the teachers want the kids to grasp the lessons- they teach with heart. Yes it’s small but the teachers are able give more time for one-on-one, if necessary. We now have a new superintendent that is fine to bring this school district to a higher academic level, prepare students for their future.

column3: We moved into the school district without knowing anything about the school we came from an excellent rated school which look good on the State's Education score, but not as it pertained to the students. We have now lived in Delaware three years. We have found Hayes High School to have exceeded excellence in individual care of each student, including our son. Our son has bloomed since he has been at Hayes. There is a lot of nonsense gossip about Hayes that is just not true. The teachers are top notch. I received immediate responses to my emails for updates. The sports program is growing with the new football coach (Loparo). Great things are happening and YES, with a small town atmosphere. Couldn't be any better! My experience with Hayes High School has been outstanding. Hayes High School is an exceptional high school with diversity, rigor, and community.Review the test scores compared to other schools in the State of Ohio. Hayes High School out performs so many and will continue to do so because the teachers, school leaders, and community are invested in the success of their students and children. I cannot imagine a reason why someone wouldn't want their children to attend this high school. My daughter's experience in Delaware City Schools has been positive (5th grade to senior year). In fact, it's the primary reason I've stayed in the area and ultimately, it's the reason I'm opting to purchase a home in the area. I feel she has been supported in her extracurricular pursuits and has had plenty of options for dual enrollment at the high school. There are a couple of FANTASTIC guidance counselors going above and beyond at the high school. Unfortunately, there are couple of very lackluster, lazy teachers and I don't always feel administration does enough to address parent complaints about them (then again, having worked as a high school teacher, I know that admins' options can be constrained by union regulations and change can be slow in that regard).

column1: This school is located in a great community, but the school itself is not that great. The teachers are lazy and because the school is crowded the classrooms are packed and hectic. This not only causes students not to pay attention, but the students themselves don't get individual attention. It's a really a shame. I can not get what all the excitement about this school is. Although, my children haven't attended, from what I am hearing...IT'S NOT THAT GREAT! If you want great schools, go to the Princeton, West Windsor area. It's unbelievable that realtors will list a house stating "in the Steinert district". And that people will actually move to another house within Hamilton, just so their kids can attend. How about giving the other two schools in the district a look???? We moved here because this was the school to go to in hamilton. After talking with parents and finding out : How bad the drug problems are there. How hard the children clicks were How bad the teacher\principle support How they keep flunking State tests Better and more opportunities exist in other schools Sorry we moved there. The last man standing in hamilton, and won't be for long. Anyone who would move to Hamilton for the schools is a fool. They might as well send their children to Trenton, it will be cheaper with the same results. I am a student here and am appalled by the reviews on the site, which could not be further from the truth. Steinert is a strong school academically, offering 9 AP courses, and has produced a Supreme Court justice, as well as several politcians. Emphasis on academics is strong, but there is plenty of balance. The soccer and baseball teams are historically among the best in the state, and the football and wrestling are beginning to compete for state championships. Dahntay Jones was a high-school All-American at Steinert. The music and arts department is also very strong, usually cleaning out the district and county competitions. The staff is relatable and approachable. Robbinsville High School- top in the county NOT West Windsor... Love it here. Went to Steinert in 1986 it wasn't good then is worse now the bullying is horrendous in Hamilton altogether and ignored. You all are very wrong steinert high school is a very great school with high academic standards , excellent peer leadership, and on top of all of that in a great area so you can take whatever crappy school you or your child goes to and go on about your buisness. You all are just jealous of steinert because they have some of the best test scores in new jersey and opportunities to meet kids from Reynolds, Crockett, and Grice so stfu haters and thank you to the people that actually know about steinert unlike these other dense people god bless you all Steinert is a great school. I graduated from Steinert. I had wonderful teachers and was challenged academically everyday, my guidance counselor was fantastic. I have heard even when I was in school, that Steinert has stuck up snobs as students. I went there not knowing anyone, and made great friends from the start. I truly believe that most of the people who don't like the school, are really jealous. I know no school is perfect, but I can honestly say I'm excited for my child to be attending Steinert in the future. I attend steinert as of now & am currently in 11th grade. This school has gotten increasing worse from the time I first walked in the doors. I try to enjoy every day I habe to spend there, but the administration has made it hard to even have school spirit anymore. They expect us to give them the respect they think they deserve, yet they don't guve us any at all. Some of the teachers I've meet really and truly care about their students future & I have become friends with many. Some aren't even qualified to tech the subject they are assigned to teach. Which is appalling considering they want us to learn what the teachers don't even know. The students do have a habit of being bitter & outspoken, and not to forget rude. Some of them are just stuck up rich kids whose parents buy them everything. On the other hand, I've meet some of the most amazing, talented, funny & beautiful people in my years here so far. They've really changed my life. Even though I only have a year left here, I seriously hope I keep meeting more amazing people & the school at least trys to pick itself up. I am currently here as a 10th grader. we have some really good teachers who will throughly go over lessons especially if they feel as though it's a hard lesson but don't get me wrong I have had or heard of a few teachers that just give you worksheets and do not explain anything so how would they expect you to do well on test. I would also like to address our "drug problem" I read on the reviews about. We do not have one and I guarantee you that every school has kids that do drugs and alcohol so it's really Unfair so rate us on that. Also I'd like to address the bullying review. Every school has bullies and mr. Smith out vice principal really does take it seriously. Now our principal I'm not sure I would say has a really good understanding on the topic because they all think it'll just blow over which is terrible considering they are the only ones that can doing anything. But seriously in general we are an average school filled with a variety of people and yes we do have a lot of white people but some of them are genuinely the nicest people you will ever meet. I am not going to lie there are some wonderful teachers in this school who go above and beyond for you. There are more teachers that like to see you blood boil. Which is why I have had a bad experience. My advice to you is to just fly under the radar. If you ever think to move to this area because of the school, don’t . It might be perfect for people that grew up in the area but if you are not local your kid will be descriminated , and really it’s not even worth for a school that doesn’t prepare the majority of the kids for anything more then MCCC. Even their Honor Cociety is one big joke with incompetent people. There is not much class or integrity to find at Steinert. Big mistake, we made the wrong choice to move to this area. The school is making a joke out of our children education. My son went to school for the first time last week, he said nobody is even paying attention to the students, majority of the teachers are not present and they dont care at all as is with the remote, they assign stuff for the children to do, and then they go their own way. What I am expiriencing this year with the education is a horror. No leadership, teachers can care less about anything they do. WE have friends who attend Bordentown HS and Northern Burlington HS, and compering how they have their classes which is log in on time, teachers doing their work, children learning with cameras on so they pay attention and have interaction with their teachers.Here in Steinert we are far away from it, teachers do nothing, no interaction whatsoever, no teaching, just assigning stuff so the kids can do it themself or go back to sleep or play games instead. Is this how teaching should look like??? What are they doing with our kids??? Best High School besides Princeton, teachers care and are educated , anyone who says different has a bad attitude and just wants to make trouble. I went to this school many years ago and it was one of the worst experiences of my life.I was a very hard working straight A student and was bored out of my mind at this school. There were a handful of good teachers. and that is where it ended. The counselor was useless. Luckily I managed to do well and still ended up in a good college with a scholarship. I do not credit my success to this school though.

column3: This school was the greatest. I was in the class of 08' and almost wish I was back there. I attended school there all four of my highschool years. The schoolwork was terribly and mindnumbingly easy. Once I got to college I found that my highschool had not prepared me for any of the work, I wouldn't reccomend sending your child there. As a student of North Hardin i will say that it is a good schools to attend the JROTC program is great and we have one of the best band s in the nation. The teachers care about the students and help them succeed. Over all North Hardin is in my opinion one of the best school around. Class of '09 here. I enjoyed my time at NHHS, but it could have been a lot better. It's not the school's fault, but more so the district--we didn't get enough money or attention because we weren't JHHS. When I went to college, I found myself woefully under-qualified, or at least under-informed. I feel like I didn't learn very much at NHHS; again, not the teachers' fault, but the school for not allowing us to have better classes. 4 history classes total, and maybe twice as many AP? Seriously? It's pathetic in regards to fostering intelligent growth. We couldn't have a valedictorian, but could have athletic 'heroes' all day. Perhaps that's where the problem lies: focus less on sports, focus more on what schools are actually meant to do, which is teach. I am currently a student at NHHS and I feel like the education I'm getting could be considerably better than it is. The overall education given could use improvement, and so could the general focus of the school. Based on my experience, I feel as if athleticism is too much of a concern versus the value of a good education. I'm highly disappointed with this school and do not recommend it. I would give this school no stars if it would let me. One of the worst High Schools I have ever sent my child to. Loss and theft of personal items is high. Principal and Superintendent do not care about students, only the money that they bring to the school. Staff does not care about the students, more interested in pep rallies and extracurricular than actually teaching students. You are taking a risk sending your child to this school. Being class of '18 which I am a freshman I couldn't be happier with North Hardin. The diversity in this school is unbelievable leaving no one left out. We have one of the top bands, sports, and we are rising higher and higher each year in academics! My most favorite thing is probably the amount of school spirit at our school! Every sports team gets recognized and cheered on by our humongous student section. All of my teachers are very involved and make sure that your getting the education needed, North Hardin might have a bad reputation but coming from a student this is the best school I've been to and I can't imagine not being a Trojan! I could go on & on about how much I love it here and I'm defiantly proud to go to North Hardin. I would recommend this school to anyone & everyone. " We believe " This school has made such a major turnaround in the past few years! The leadership change to a new principal was the key...he changed the climate, encouraged teachers to challenge themselves, and helped students see just what they could do if they stuck to it. The school has been a distinguished school for two years straight, which had never happened before. I bet they're on the way to a third award! It's a wonderful place to learn and grow. I was worried moving here with the low rating but both of my children attend or attended North Hardin and have been supported and encouraged by teachers and counselors. The course options are abundant including dual credit and honors courses My teens have gone here since freshman year and are now seniors. The staff are caring and professional. They are more than willing to help the kids when needed, and resolve issues professionally and efficiently.

column1: Average high school filled with tons of diversity, great advanced placement program, a plethora of clubs and after school activities. Along with copiague middle school the building is very nice & convenient location the school is very helpful and reliable for students and it is a grat choice to go to and student will really enjoy an opportunity to attent the school! Excellent! The inside of the school is immaculate and well-kept. The teachers are top-notch. The arts in this school are very well-funded, so they put on great productions. The course offering includes Advanced Placement classes that ensure students are prepared for college. Overall, Copiague High School, as it is usually called, is a great school. The school is your average diverse High school similar to Brentwood high school only a lot smaller. The guidance department is always full and the college and career room is useless unless you are constantly on top of them to get your things done, other than that I'm pretty sure everyone can handle college work on their own with out their help. The Internet is always failing, even right in the middle of filling out applications for college related things. The teachers are good and nice and they help out alot, also copiague is rated one of the top schools with the most socially interactive student body which is a good thing once your out in the world. The school has its perks and it's downsides but overall a good enough school to get things done and get a career if you really give it your all. There are alot of after school activities and sports. I feel that music and art are undermined and should be funded more

column3: As a student I have really enjoyed my time here at Robert E Lee. The name betrays the school, however. It is an incredibly diverse and loving environment in which students of all types are given many opportunities from specialized magnet schools, vocational education programs, and many opportunities for those with learning disabilities. The teachers are outstanding in both their ability to teach and their love for the students; I truly feel as though I matter and am part of a beautiful community. Lee gets a bad reputation for seemingly no reason, and, as a primary source, I can assure you it is school filled with wonderful students, teachers, and administrators. Twilight Zone meets Hee-Haw. What a shame. I was a student at this school. It is now called Staunton High and it has been completely remodeled. The school had a lot of issues in the past and continues to have lots of issues but it has gotten better in the last couple of years. It has a problem with losing teachers but continues to hire every year.

column1: DHS is an excellent school. The facilities are great. The faculty is great and cares a lot about the students. There is a lot of parent involvement. Our son has been at DHS for six months now and is doing great. The AFJROTC is his favorite but he is also in band and soccer. The soccer program is above average and the coaches are willing to work with players of all skill levels. Overall the school is very nice and our son is really enjoying it. Highly recomended! Yet another terrible GA school, check the scorecard on their website. SAT, CRCT and graduation rates are pitiful. If you want your kids to have a decent education in Georgia you better pay for private school. Sending my children to Dutchtown High School is the worst mistake I have ever made. This school really needs to get rid of ineffective teachers. I placed one star by parent involvement, because I do not believe the school wants parents to know the level of incompetence that is going on there. If parents start sharing information, the administrators and teachers would be held accountable. Bring in new, innovative, and competent teachers. This is a great community of parents, but this school has been going in the wrong direction the last few years. We also need to hold our administrators accountable for where they have been lacking in leadership and as role models. I cannot help but note that there is one administrator there who is angry all the time. Her interpersonal skills are horrible! She hollers at the children, she is even loud with parents. When I hear her I think, "My God, no one should be that angry so early in the morning." I feel as if some of those poor children are paying for whatever is going wrong or went wrong in her life. Parents, wake up! Pray for a massive change in accountability for Dutchtown, and most of all, pray for our children. DHS Swept the Henry County Science Fair This Year!! ALL of the students sent to International and most of the ones who went to State came from DHS. It was such a win that they asked the science teachers to stand up and take a bow from DHS. (and the football team is not bad as well!) As a freshman, Dutchtown has a great education system. I think what needs to be looked at more is the administration and the math department. I am currently in Adv. math 1 and i have never seen such ridiculous teaching before. This new math thign they have going on is really absurd and I,personally, hope it goes back to subjects such as Algebra, trigonometry etc.We are learning unessacary information. Please study how other countries do their education and see how they are excelling. But as a school, it could be something i look forward to everyday. It is very boring as a whole. I'm in the band program but all I can tell you is to tutor yourself in math. The english department is good,however. I loved Dutchtown High School. My son attended and he is now in the Air Force and doing well and both my neice and daughter attended and they graduated in May and are both headed to great Universities. Ms. Noble does a great job with adding diversity to the school and I feel that this community should be grateful for having such a great administrator and caring teachers in place. Kudos to the teachers and to the staff. Dutchtown High School of Henry county at times has teachers who don't have their heart in what they do. Sometimes you may sit in a class and learn absolutely nothing because the teacher finds if necessary to talk on the phone with her best friend. You often times find yourself teaching yourself. The AP teachers never assist you in a time of need. The student body as a whole is great. Although the teachers may not be so great your fellow peers will always be there when you need them and that is what I love about this school. You can call on your classmate to assist you when your teacher doesn't find the need to. Love this school. They motivate both of my daughters academically at the middle and highschool. I have always told them that THEY make the school, the school does not make them! Most of the teachers try their best to help you succeed. They will help you when you need it. I never learned physics because they fired my teacher two months into the school year and replaced him with someone that didn't even bother to teach us anything unless she found out she was going to be evaluated on the day of, and even then it was an old lesson plan that we'd already learned. I also didn't do anything in my AP English class for a larger part of the school year because my teacher's husband died but the principle didn't bother to hire anyone else, including a regular substitute teacher. Sometimes we'd head into class and no one ever showed up because the principle "forgot" despite the fact that there was communication of a qualified substitute being required prior to our teacher's husband's passing. column3: I am 2011 alumni. For the first year and a half of high school I attended Newman Smith High School down the street from Turner. I had a horrible experience with Newman Smith as a whole. The teachers, principals, and counselors have absolutely no sympathy for their students. Their philosophy seems to be guilty until proven innocent and they certainly enforce this. Because of this and other issues with them, my mother and I agreed to transfer over to R. L. Turner where she and my older brother had graduated from. We were very pleased with the change because immediately I was accepted with my peers and with the administration. Turner allows their students to make the right decisions on their own and because of this it builds great character in their students. I recommend this school for students who want to have a great relationship with their peers and teachers who are also wonderful. I loved Turner in '95, and my son loves it now in 2012. As far as the tardy rule we have never a problem. He only has gotten one tardy and it was dismissed. If your child shows up on time, has desire to suceed and works at it, this school will allow them the freedom and comfortable enviroment needed. I get emails from his teachers and coach, and from the 9th grade counslers even calls from the assistant principal with progress reports. My son has requested when we move we gotta move to Turner territory. I have two kids who live in the CFBISD area.Parents know your hand book, policies and TEA information. Janie Stark Elementary school is AMAZING!Its the Middle school and high school they get lost and the faculty are desensitized. I have had two students go from K-12th in CFBISD. Turner has been a great school, awesome school spirit and staff. The new small learning communities are a big benefit to students that start as freshmen and attend all 4 years. Our youngest will graduate in May, and she is extremely well prepared for college, as was our oldest. No matter where you go to school, volunteering and parent involvement is still important. I like Turner for my Child. He has made very good grades and has met lifetime good kids in the METSA Program which prepares a student for college like courses. A parent heps make a good student. If you are black and from another country, don't take your children to RL Turner. In other words if you are from Africa don't take your kids to this school. Kids from Africa are discriminated against and no one says a thing. Teachers, counsellors pretend nothing is happening. Racism is serious at this school. WARNING! this school will not accept credits from Africa! I was really shocked when one of my kids was placed in 9th grade despite being in 12th grade in Africa. When I complained, no one cared. I had to remove my children in a hurry coz they were severely depressed. My child's grades were later accepted in another school district and she has since graduated. And to make matters worse they don't have too many high schools in this school district so you don't have too many options. Do some research before moving to this area. We moved from Dallas to Addison thinking Addison fell under Richardson School District little did we know it was in CFBISD. Other black parents with kids who came from other countries are removing their kids too. By the way most African kids in America do better in school I don't see reason why credits from Africa can't be accepted. Turner is not only a school, but a home. It has provided me with the greatest education a gal like me can ask for. Not only were the teachers so loving and generous, but the student body was inspiring. They would roar in the stands at football games, and win or lose they would bleed blue. Being a lion was not something you are given, but something you earn. I genuinely miss walking down the hall ways and feeling the spirit of Turner in every corner. "... hail to Turner High!" the entire schools chants at pep-rallies where we would cheer on our school and all of our outstanding, award winning programs and sports. It was a blessing being a lion and being able to say I bled blue. I highly recommend Turner. It's gr8 yo. The teachers refuse bathroom breaks to the students. There is very little time between classes and often they walk from 1 end of the school to the other. If a girl needs a eat room break to attend to a need of nature so to speak she is expected to announce it to her teacher so the entire class hears it. This however does not mean the teacher will let them go to the restroom. One teacher told my daughter she thought it was funny when these spoiled high school girls suffer embarrassment. So many pregnant girls here because they send all of the girls that are pregnant from Newman smith here. One teacher teaches chemistry from YouTube. She is a history teacher but they have her teaching chemistry. She has told her students that she dosnt understand chemistry. last year all students 11th grade and below failed her class. The teachers are rude and a lot of the assignments are rediculious.

column1: I attended Smithsburg as a student in my freshman and sophomore year. All in all, it wasn't bad. There's no doubt smithsburg is a big agricultural, predominately white school, and as an african american I have felt overwhelmed at times (zero diversity here, I know my graduating class had about..4 or 5 black men, I can't even recall any other races). I had no trouble fitting in socially though, and at the end of the day school is what you make of it. The teachers were very nice, and I feel like Smithsburg definitely prepared me for college, even in the beginning 2 years i attended. To anyone who didn't attend the middle schools: I attended Smithsburg after moving from the midwest. It took a little adjusting, but I did find a nice group of friends from joining sports. To anyone new to Washington County schools (especially Smithsburg), EVERYONE has grown up with each other. Worth noting. Small side note: I know there has been a new principal/VP since I've left smithsburg, but I have NEVER seen the principal before. I didn't even know what he looked like. Don't know if that's good or bad, but definitely worth noting. The Vice Principal was always there, and he was very approachable. I attended Smithsburg as a student from 2007-2011 and I i hate it, i only get bully and school do not stop it. They treat me like child. I had a disable with reading and writing and they do not help me out. I'm currently attending Smithsburg as a sophomore and I can say it is a great school. The teachers are very helpful and mostly everyone is nice. Smithsburg is a primarily white school which is difficult when you're Hispanic in honors classes and you're the only person of color in the room. In the first month or two you will probably know 90% of the students even if you don't join a sport. Sports are very important to SHS (mainly football) and the student section is absolutely insane(in a good school spirit way). Even for someone who doesn't partake in sports, I really enjoy the pep-rallies and going to events. They also offer more extracurricular activities (Drama Club, Art Club, FFA, etc). There's something for everyone. This is the best school that I ever went. They are so supportive and all of the teachers that I have are really respectful. This is a big plus because I used to go to a horrible school and then moved here. Also this school will help you pass big tests and you more likely to get in to a very good college or university. In conclusion I suggest anyone to come to this school. Do not go to the school in PA because I went there before and most of the teachers that I had very disrespectful and not supportive at all. Very good school. This school is WAY better than old school that I used to go which was in PA. My old school in PA was horrible and had extremely bad teachers.

column1: small classroom size; doesn't matter because the conduct in some of them is horrendous Some of the Teachers leave before the busses are out of the parking lot! Maynard Jackson, you are getting the best principal. Mrs. Johnson is so good at her job. Your parents, teachers, and students will love her!!! If you want to be the best, you chose the right principal. The graduation coaches are encouraging and give excellent suggestions as to how a student can improve on their academics to be prepared for college. The new principal is very involved and as a parent I enjoy working with her. There could be more parent participation in PTA meetings and activities. The teachers and principal are much concerned about the students and the level they are on . We hope to get the coaches and atheletic director on board to have the students working as brothers on the field as well as in their studies. I am actually a student who attend Jackson and my school is an awesome school we have newly renovated school. Teachers are more concern than before. My mother can come and talk to the principal with no problem and the principal gives her great responses. The curricular there is phenomenal during and after school. Our ballet department is great, the chorus is wonderful and the band is magnificent. This school is horrible they do not respect parents what so ever DO NOT listen to these other reviews because they are all lies that are written by the principal. The renovations are great and they are on the rise. I wasn't expecting such courtesy and professionalism but I was honestly blown away. I'm hoping this going to be a great school year! This school has improved by leaps and bounds over the last 4 years, and I am thrilled with the hard work that Principal Johnson has put in. I am also grateful for all of the parents that have worked so hard to make these things happen. I have not contributed as I would like to, but many parents have. I have a Class of 2016 senior and a Class of 2020 rising freshman for the 2016-2017 school year. I just attended a meeting for the rising freshman and can only say "what a difference! " So much more organized and positive. While I can't say every thing is exactly perfect, I don't think I will find a school where it is. However, my child has taken rigorous classes, participated in a fabulous dance program, and been a member of the academic decathlon team in it's first 2 years in existence. I am proud to say that team beat Grady and North Atlanta high schools this year and went to state. At state, they came in 8th out of 22. Last year they came in 16th out of about 24. This is excellent considering the other schools have had AD teams for years and knew what to expect. The school now has 26 boys and girls sports and over 40 clubs. If a student is interested in starting a club, the school supports it. There is also a garden at the school and the kids are working hard to get certified to use the food in the school cafeteria and provide it to the community. They have learned so much in this process, about food, nutrition, gardening, and how to work the bureaucracy to make things happen! The principal has been very friendly and welcoming every time I have visited the school. Some people at this school are friendly, just got to find the right people. The teachers there are very good, and actually help with the work. They really want you to pass and if you don't then they're other sources you can use/do to pass. Some of the clubs are fun too, and the groups as well. The uniform isn't hard to match with either, I actually like the colors of the school. The test are easy if you understand the work same for the classes too, I would suggest that you take AP or honors classes because they can be really beneficial. Also doing college course classes really helps to ,as well as helping around the school or doing any helpful tasks.

column3: I attended Hueytown in the sixties and seventies. The community embraces this school and the students seem to know and appreciate it. Joe Pilkinton, the student resource officer has helped many a stray spirit find their way. This is my first time experiencing this high school and I am not satisfied at all. My husband and I was thinking moving to Hueytown that our children will have a better education but to our surprise, the high school system is very poor. They are not fair at all when it comes to certain students of color. It is awfully funny that only the black students fail at AHSGE when the majority of the school is white (how odd). Our child and children will be attending a different high school I do not care how far we have to drive to get them there. My daughter graduated from Hueytown in 2009 and at the time we we mostly happy with her education there. She was always an A-B student and active in many extra-curricular activities. She took what AP courses she could but was disappointed in the offerings and that the administration really did not seem to support addition of more. We generally felt that the teachers were good but the administration was abysmal at best. However we always felt that she was getting a good, solid education. She will soon be a Junior at Alabama where, through extra hard work she is still an A-B student. Now, looking back we see that our judgment of the school was clouded by our lack of comparison. We now know that Hueytown did not adequately prepare her to for college at the same level of other schools, even those in the Jefferson County System. I have withdrawn my son (another A-B student), moved and he is now a Junior at Vestavia trying to catch up from two years of sub-standard education at Hueytown. Maybe is will improve with the new building, but with the prevailing administration I have my doubts. My niece graduated from Oak Grove last year and seems far better prepared. The administrators, teachers, and councilors have given my daughter new insight to studying and pursuing a college for a career. They are very helpful and nice and encouraging to her. The goal of the school is to be safe, study and have fun at doing this. They are very nice and have helped her through many trials. Thank you Hueytown. Safety first. I am so impressed with the turn around of Hueytown High School this year. The administration, teachers, students, parents and community members have created a great environment for our children. As a graduate of Hueytown High School, I would not recommend for anyone to send their children to this school. It makes me feel disgusted when I think of all of the excellent teachers I had throughout high school that were fired or pressured to leave by the administration. The administration is known to harass and target only certain students when it comes to discipline to "make an example of them" for the rest of the school. The administration is notorious for cracking down on athletes and students who are more involved and letting delinquent kids with a record of disciplinary infractions get away with more and receiving a lighter punishment. The school is far more concerned with discipline as opposed to academics and I believe that is why academics are failing on a grander scale. For a student to receive the best possible education and most preparation for college, or the real world in general, honors and AP classes are a MUST. Without these, a student from Hueytown would not be fully prepared for college. All in all, HHS is a huge disappointment. It is sad to see the school's decline in the past 10-15 years. I see no improvement for the school in sight. I am not sure what level of academics are offered at this school. One conversation with one of the school's counselors and being ignored by not one , but 3 ladies at the front desk/reception area upon my arrival was enough for me to enroll my child in a private highschool in Homewood. I felt very unwelcome there and knew that it was not the place for our family. This school was not what I anticipated it to be, it is on the falling school list for 2022.

column3: The main way to describe Smith is "up and coming". We've seen a lot of improvements in the last year that shouldn't be forgotten. However, there's still some lingering problems. The school is broken up into Common Population, Honors, AP, and IB students. The main problem is the CP students. The students who don't take the initiative to take higher level classes are the ones who have a larger amount of behavioral problems. These behavioral problems mean less trust from the administration which leads to less fun opportunities for the whole student body (dances, fieldtrips, etc.) It's exciting to see what's offered to motivated students. We have first rate college advisers, and counselors meet with each grade level regularly to make sure everyone is on track for graduation. She's a true asset to the school, the community & the parents.She makes you feel like your child is the only child @ the school.She works hard to make sure that their needs are met.Kids like my 2nd often get lost in the system,get "labeled" & for some who don't have the care &concern of someone like the Assoc. Principal,quit school or "just make it" to graduation by teachers moving them thru the system.You get 1 chance to get it right w/your kids.I'd put them here again.Safe envir.Caring staff.Broad Class choices.Very positive exp With so many schools forced to provide remedial programs for struggling schools (which Mt. View does), sometimes it means cuts to programs that help top students...not at Mt. View! There are so many Advanced Placement classes-in nearly every offering. The teachers are skilled at not just teaching to the AP tests, but really immersing the students in the subject(s). My kids will be so prepared for college (both in knowledge, rigor and credits). My children attended Mt. View High School. They received a very good education. Challenging courses are available as is running start (tuition-free college) for qualifying students. Neither of my children needed remedial education upon entering college, and both successfully completed their college program with a high-level of success. To reach this goal, a value for education and reasonable encouragement is necessary from the parent, student, teachers, and principal. Outstanding. The Thunder Family is real and strong. I love this school and community! We’ve had two kids attend here, and two that will follow in the next few years. I am grateful for the many wonderful teachers, athletic programs and opportunities available to our kids here at Mountain View ! smh worst school ive gone to so far, the only nice teachers r the front desk ladys. also my orange was moldy once :(

column1: D0 NOT GO HERE!! You have been warned. They are rude. They are discriminative and will not understand. Pretty Good excepts needs to be more challenging. Needs get that California Distinguished School to have a higher rating. Also probably needs that IB program, so don't send your kids if you want them to be challenged. Only good if you want them to have a good class rank and want colleges to see your kid or child stand out. Half of the kids in the classes don't study and too many class distractions, but overall nice. Too many students don't do well. Not sure what happened to my original review but I don't mind posting another. I was very surprised just how many of my former classmates amounted to nothing after graduating from here. But perhaps for starters, instead of requiring community service from your students in an effort to prepare them for when they're inevitably arrested and on parole/probation, you could instead offer a coding course. It's almost 2022, it's about time to teach the students how to code, granted most of them won't care about it, but it's at least giving some of your students a fighting chance in the real world to try to help them work tech roles.
