column3: Average academic school. Some great teachers, but most are just fair. The school lacks leadership where it's principal is concerned. Dr Lisa Stueve is between fair and in competent at best. Several good teachers have left the school because of her inability to lead. Will not be sending our next child to this school next year unless there is a change in leadership at this school. Leadership is a problem here. I feel like teachers and parents should work together to make a successful student...and while they SAY that's what they are all about, they're not. I know from personal experience. I've tried to contact at least two different teachers and actually had one write a very insulting email about me intended for the principle, but she accidentally sent it to me instead. I know EXACTLY what they think of parents who are trying to be involved...and Lisa Stueve did nothing. I didn't even get an apology. Needless to say, I pulled my daughter out of there. Her grades have improved and she said she is much happier at her new school as she complained about how the teachers/staff and students interact with each other. No respect. No leadership. My child had great potential and was selected to attend the Magnet program. Unfortunately the Magnet program is a ruse, where achieving students are used to improve the grade level of a school with very low performing general students. This program is there only so that the school can get better government funding. Unfortunately for my child, he was pulled down by the general population at the school and did not end up performing very well. The teachers and staff don't have much interest in the students, and we found it very hard to get ANY information from anyone. We found the school very apathetic.. Don't send your child here! DO NOT AND I REPEAT DO NOT ...enroll your student at this school, UNLESS.....you want to pay (HIGH) fees to a school that is portraying itself as a "CHARTER" school!! Do the research, they lost this a long time ago due their LOW scores! Also if you want your children influenced by ALL the other "BAD" students there! Oh lets not leave out the caring Administration, that will NEVER solve any issue that may arise with your student, The wonderful Principal that NEVER returns phones calls, until SHE feels ready, the other staff that once your child have an issue (they label them as the problem) instead of getting to the root of the issue! This school is a "JOKE" academically and sports wise.....this school could possibly recover if: they clean house by replacing administration and allowing ONLY district children to attend the school......."if" you are considering this school...RECONSIDER...READ THE OTHER REVIEWS AND IF YOU NOTICE MOST OF THE PARENTS ALL HAVE THE SAME ISSUES THIS SCHOOL IS JUST . . HMMM NOT AS GREAT AS THEY SAY IT IS . The school is dirty and filled with roaches crawling all up the walls , locker rooms, and bathrooms . There is never tissue in the bathrooms and the toilets are GROOOSSS ! Janitorial staff is slacking on the cleaniness. The teachers aren't as bad, except how they don't communicate very clearly and dont follow up with you. I feel as a student uncomfortable going here, It's unclean and just a bunch of lies that were in the magnet contract . I feel as if this school is a waste , the counselors won't change your schedule so you can have the classes that you need to graduate and complete for your college pathway. This needs alot improvement and I clearly see there is no Charter . You lost that along time away , because you wouldn't be suffereing for funding things at the school . I enjoy going to North Springs, it's just not as amazing as I thought it would be. They widely promote the magnet program, but when you get to school no one even knows about it. None of the teachers have a clue about next year's academies, which I have been very confused about. I am in two on-level classes, math and spanish, and the kids are HORRIBLE. The teachers are not even trying to make these kids learn. A lot of my friends agree that the on-level classes are awful and you can't learn anything. The honors classes, on the other hand, are wonderful! The teachers are great and they engage the students so everyone doesn't just learn, but actually has fun in the class. Even if you aren't an honors student normally, take an honors class because the teachers will really help you learn the stuff. All in all, North Springs averages out to be an okay school, it could be better! It is a fantastic school that is very diverse and has a place for everyone. The teachers are great and really help each student reach their full potential and spend one on one time with their students that struggle. I would recommend it for any student. The school has a horrible administration and all the great teachers have either left or are leaving. What is wrong with the Fulton County School Board and Leadership at the county level that would allow the administration to run off the best and brightest of teachers? It is really a horrible place for students and teachers. Do not send your child currently to North Springs Charter High School. This school is an absolutely the worst place for a student to attend! The teacher's & staff NEVER return phone calls & e-mails.My honor's & gifted student who skipped two graded attended for one semester & became very depressed and ill from being there. I had to take her out so that her stellar academic record will not suffer even more. Her grades started to drop because of the lack of organization & disrespect from a teacher. Not to mention when her teacher's ever decided to show up. Dr. Stueve is the most ineffective & hands off principal that I have ever met. Some teacher will find the need NOT to put grades in for several weeks & blame your kid,to cover up their inability to keep a grade sheet, grades mysteriously changed. It took me months & several calls to the Fulton superintendent to get any type resolution & a call back from staff. It took me 2 months to get a report card and 4 months for transcripts. My child's current school had to fix their mistakes although she was ahead 1 year prior to attending NSHS. We hated this place so much we moved back to our home state & my child is SAFE & is excelling. The Latin teacher is the best ! Poor leadership,poor teacher's ='s NSHS! It's funny how most of the parents are saying bad things about North Springs, but they're not a student so they know absolutely nothing about it. Just because you're child or you (if you were a student) had a horrible experience, doesn't make it a horrible school and it doesn't make it the same experience for everyone else. I absolutely LOVE North Springs! This is my junior year and I've enjoyed every moment of North Springs. The faculty, staff and students are so diverse. We LITERALLY have students from everywhere. I'm Nigerian and there are Nigerian kids that I can communicate with, along with students who are from Hawaii, Taiwan, Russia, South Africa, South Korea, Brazil, Cuba, and other foreign countries. I'm blessed to say that I went to North Springs. I'm not going to say that North Springs is perfect because we most definitely do have major problems, but no school is perfect, and all schools have major problems, some more severe than ours. The Magnet Program and the Academic Program push the students harder to get the diploma that the want like the Academic, Advanced, or Magnet Diploma if they work really hard. All I'm saying is don't knock it 'til you try it. I can't wait for senior year for my student to come and go next year! This has been the most unorganized school I have ever been involved with and I have 2 older students that went to different high schools so I have experience there. Maybe if you are in honors or AP classes it is better, but if you are in on level or have an IEP you are on your own. No one follows up in a timely manner and it is obvious no one in administration will do anything about incompetent teachers. Make copies of all your work because it is likely to be lost repeatedly. I regret not having transferred my student somewhere else in mid 10th grade. There are a few good teachers there that care, but I honestly don't know how they stay there and deal with all the disfunction and disorganization at the school. My child would say the same as me and also can't wait to be out of a school where many ,but not all, of her teachers have been incompetent. Very unprofessional, unwelcoming and standoffish Front office staff and counseling staff. If you so happen to have this school as your child home school, expect the worse and hope for better. North Springs is an okay school .Some teachers may give off bad vibes or have heavy accents but you cant expect every teachers to treat you nicely or with respect.They are rude some of the administrators and janitorial team are also rude and incompetent .The education and experience are great if you apply yourself .There isn't really bullying .Sex and drugs would be the same at any other high school.Dr.Ruiz is really cool and interacts with the student to find problems and try to help them.He even taught a class because of a long term absence of a teacher.Very diverse no major racism (you can find racism anywhere).Ive had one problem and thats being singled out for a cheating scandal that i didn't partake in.NS just needs to work on discipline while keeping the actual interests of the students in mind. The visual and performing a arts program is really good, but teachers outside those programs do not give a crap about anything. The way the student interact is horrible. My son loves going to north springs & the new principle is making north springs even better . I don't understand why some parents talk bad about north springs when they don't even know nothing about the school My daughter attended North Springs and it was by far one of the most unorganized schools she's attended. We couldn't wait for the year to end. On a side note I found the staff and administration to be extremely unprofessional. My daughter received a schedule change and was plucked from a solid, effective teacher's class only to end up with the most awful teacher we have ever encountered. I use the term "teacher" loosely, here. This individual was a sponsor for an extracurricular activity at the school, and it was clear that this club was her priority. Teaching the AP class clearly was not. My daughter's class received few reading and writing assignments, unlike the other AP classes. Instead, the teacher gave one writing assignment (yes, one) and gave lots of vocabulary tests. She told my daughter's class that, if they made a B in the class, that they should be glad because a B was "gold." She frequently told the students she was very busy, thus, she did not have time to respond to parents' emails. Being in this individual's class cost our daughter a year in which she could have been prepared for college. To top it off, an administrator told parents that this teacher was one of the school's "very best teachers." To be fair, we have encountered a few good teachers at North Springs. We have had our share of average to poor ones at the school, but this individual took the cake. The school year could not end fast enough. Other issues include messing up students' schedules. We have set up our daughter's schedule at year's end only to have the schedule messed up with our daughter being taken out of honors classes and placed in on level classes. It is never the other way around. Is it that students are systematically being taken out of honors/AP classes to make room for preferred students? I have no idea, but North Springs has been a disappointment for this family. Consider sending your children elsewhere. The staff are completely clueless and unorganize . I was getting my daughter register in this school.Everything that was needed to be done for her registration Ive tooken care of it. As I came to the school to give The lady all of my documentation . she tells me I'm missing something ,so I said ok I'll have what you need from me tomorrow .I came back up to the school the next day to see the lady again and she tells me great this is what I needed now I need something from you . This paperwork u gave me isn't right . From their It begins to be a problem because you'll assign me to a certain task but then wait till the next day to mention something else wrong .Instead of telling me all the errors in my documentation while I'm their. she made it so hard for me to register my child in.At the end of the day she should do everything it take to make my daughter get in school and get her education . Instead of slowing the process ..The staff is horrible. I would ask for a certain person to speak with they always say this person hasn't made it in yet. I'll ask well when we'll they'll be here , they mention they don't know . School opens at 7:00 am everybody that works in this school should be here all at the same time .Mostly everything I ask from this staff has been i don't know or I'm not sure . Unlike the previous review, I found the registration process easy as long as the proper documents were brought to the school. I was impressed and found it comforting that the school was very strict as to the documents that were accepted for enrollment - the school runs a tight ship. Appointment process was easy. Great school with a hands on principal. A lot of these parents are bad-mouthing North Springs and the majority of yall haven't really paid attention to what's going on in the school. We do have our problems. The administration could do a lot better because they are not organized. Just because they are the first people you greet when you walk into the building does not mean that the respect the school is like that. Since it is a high school with 1749 students in it and it was built in the 1960's you can only keep it so clean. Our sports teams are great. Our track team is second in the US. Our basketball team has been undefeated. Our test scores are not the entire picture. for example, I may fail geometry, but I could be a genius at calculus. Our test scores are not accurately represented for the students. North Springs has problems, but we have improved. North Springs is NOT the "horrible" place a bunch of people say it is. Truth be told, North Springs is what you make it. You can be anti-social and say it is a bad place, or you can put on a smile and make the best of it and see it for what it truly is. Half of these people saying bad stuff about Spartan Pride haven't had any type of experience with it, so that means that you don't really know what's happening in the school or you just think you do. Look up your facts before you judge what you THINK is going on. My kids graduated from North Springs last year. My daughter just finished her first year at Tulane and my son his first year at Georgia Tech. I was co-president of the PTO for two years and involved in the Dance Booster Club. During those two years, I worked with most of the faculty and a lot of the parents at North Springs. As a parent, I loved North Springs and everything it offered my children, academically and socially. The faculty encourages parent involvement and appreciates it. The teachers at North Springs are dedicated and passionate about their jobs and care deeply for their students. North Springs offers several academic paths, on level. honors and Ap's. My kids were well prepared academically for college and socially for the real world and I attribute that to their years at North Springs. We have two children who graduated from North Springs. One is a student at Ga. Tech and the other at South Carolina. North Springs gave both children a chance to grow in their fields of interest. We felt the diversity of friends was a POSITIVE impact of the school ! They had a chance to be involved in community service, school clubs and sports. Parents have every opportunity to participate in school activities and make a difference in our community. Our children are making a difference at their respective schools and will be assets to the communities they join after graduation. First and foremost, the quality of the education my recent graduates received was superb. As demonstrated by the affection they received at graduation, the teachers went above and beyond and were committed to my children's success. We saw lots of school spirit at sporting events, school plays and other after school events. I am a parent of 3 North Springs High School students (2 recent graduates and one rising junior) and am more than pleased with my kids' experiences, as well as my own experience. When my oldest daughter first started at NS, I chose to get involved by volunteering for PTO activities, school store, the foundation, etc. In doing so I was able to create personal relationships with administrators, teachers, parents and students. This enabled me to form a better picture of the environment in which my kids were spending their days. I found that I was very welcomed into the school community. All 3 of my children have found mentors and cheerleaders who have helped them through their struggles and celebrated their success with them, even after graduation. When students seek personal connections to teachers as mentors, everything changes for them. An overwhelming majority of teachers were committed to helping my children succeed, probably because my children showed an interest in succeeding and were willing to work for it. Their academic achievements helped the older 2 receive admittance to colleges of their choice, as well as scholarship opportunities to help us with the tuition. In addition to the academic growth, my children also grew tremendously as individuals and as citizens of our community. They developed an amazing strength of character, learning to push through adversity and work towards goals, work well with others who have similar interests as well as others who may have not share a common interest or motivation. They were well prepared for their next steps after high school North Springs is a very diverse and accepting school. I have never seen a school with so few cliques. Students of various interests and talents can find their niche here. The course offerings are many and very varied. Athletes can find an opportunity to participate in most sports here. Administration works hard to accommodate students various needs and most teachers are very talented and dedicated. I have a rising Junior at North Springs high school. We transferred from a private school that my son attended through eight grade. Our experience with North Springs has been positive. I am most impressed with the amazing relationships between this diverse group. This is such an important life lesson for our children. The magnet programs are outstanding and offer so many options for your student to build on their strengths and interests. North Springs has been a fantastic high school for my son, a rising junior. He has been able to choose from so many different classes-from acting to AP classes. I feel the teachers have been supportive and encourage to reach his true potential. I am happy to see thriving parent involvement there. The diversity allows for the kids to realize that the world is this way- full of many different kinds of people from varied backgrounds. I feel he will be very prepared for college after graduation from North Springs. i currently have a rising Jr, and have been blown away by what is offered at this school! There is so much going on, there truly is something for everyone! The teachers have been fantastic, approachable, communicative. My child came from Sandy Springs Middle School and was more than prepared for his honor/AP classes and i feel he is on his way to be more than prepared for whatever college he goes after. Thank you North Springs! I have had one student graduate and one student is a rising senior. Diversity is a plus and my children have had opportunities that have helped them achieve their goals. Is the school perfect? No. Is every teacher great? No. However, the majority of the faculty that I have interacted with over the years have been tremendously helpful and have cared about my kids. The parental involvement is good, although we would always like to see more, the ones that do get involved, really do care. North Springs provides exceptional academics and extracurricular activities in a fun, supportive, and diverse environment. The Dual Magnet program provides students with exceptional opportunities in many different interest areas. I heard horror stories about the organization of the Administrators, but to experience was another. They are NEVER on the same page with regard to your child. My daughter was bullied for SIX MONTHS and the staff did NOTHING! They had SEVEN pages of discilplinary action against the other student not include, the evidence I provided of the student and her gang MEETING my daughter outside her classroom, they did nothing! My daughter went from being a straight A/B student to a failing student. I was never even notified until my child MISSED almost a month and a half of school that she was even failing! Never received a call, e-mail, or letter in the mail for tardiness. I updated the school of me moving a YEAR and several times and each time I found that they STILL had not updated my info. My daughter began to hide in various places of the school to try and not run into the gang!! Everytime I went to the school one administrator did not know about this issue from the other!! I now have to PAY to get my MAGNET student back on track to graduate! This school failed MISERABLY on communication with me as a parent. So, if your child attended this school, I suggest you create your own excel spreadsheet of when assignments are turned in, make sure that teachers are logging grades(they take months to do that), and keep record of ALL calls and documents!! They will have your minor child signing off on docs and not even provide the parent with them! I just say, STAY ON THEM!! Hopefully the new principle will bring order to the school. My daughter graduated in 2016. She was in a highly rated private school and switched because she wanted "bigger" and said the classes were harder at North Springs. They have so many more AP classes than most schools and several levels of a diploma for the magnet program that every child can be as challenged as their gifts allow. She played on multiple teams and got to know the administration and coaches and was very grateful for her experience. She's now in college on a scholarship and felt very prepared. This magnet school is underappreciated! North Springs is a school with a diverse population. That being said, there are kids that function on level or below, there are kids who go to Ivy League schools after graduation. The point is, North Springs offers support for everyone who seeks it.. Just as private school is not for everybody, public school isn't either. Ive had two children graduate with 30 hours of college credit from AP classes. You have to pass a national exam to get that credit. I currently have a third child enrolled. Is it a challenge dealing with the public school red tape? yes. Does having students with a wide range of abilities sometimes affect overall test scores? yes. Our school has increased it's graduation rate exponentially over the past five years which speaks to the dedication of the teachers and administrators. Go visit! School is more than academics and test scores. It's learning to navigate in the real world. Terrible I hate racism and bullying. It’s not a safe place for people of color. My daughter currently goes to this school. I moved to Sandy Springs so my daughter could go to a "great" school. I looked forward to the diversity and wanted to get my daughter out of a rough neighborhood. Well, not much has changed EXCEPT for the scenery. The school is full of bullying. Just last Friday, a boy and a girl brutally jumped a girl after school on campus. All fights happen on campus after school. Where the administrative staff is when this happens, I have no idea. The video has been circulating and it is horrible. The boy was at the school the following Monday walking around on campus. My daughter has been bullied with no assistance from the administrative staff. I am appalled and do not wish anyone to send their child to this school at all. I am looking to switch schools for my child as soon as possible. We have had 3 students at North Springs. One recent graduate and one now in her Madter program. One student current enrolled. Their needs, and there were many, have always been met with good results. They have had amazing teachers, learning opportunities, great sports experiences as well as developing into well rounded young adults prepared for college and the work force. The school diversity made for a better understanding of all people. The students are comfortable mixing with all students and can find a place where they “fit in” and are accepted. This is our first year at North Springs and we have been so impressed. All the metrics are strong for our family: great teachers (super responsive and really care about their students), excellent principal (great communication), lots of extracurriculars, excellent facility, we feel safe and a part of something. The 9th grade teachers have been fantastic for my son and we can't wait for next year. We are thrilled! I wish the building was newer, but I can trade top academics success until the new building is done

column1: Taylor schools have gone down-hill. It has started a new way of "learning" called New Tech. That means that everything is more technology and project based. First of all, the technology is not reliable. In fact, just today, my computer would connect to the Internet, so I tried to shut it down, but it wouldn't even do that. New Tech is also project based, and that is the real problem. Nothing is learning by doing a project. Students spend about 3 weeks (it varies) on a single project, usually more. Hardly any material is covered. Group projects are also a terrible idea. Good students end up with people who don't care, so the good student ends up carrying the other people. If he or she doesn't he/she gets a bad grade even if he/she did the part the group agreed on at the start. It's too much work for one person.I have shed a lot of tears and lost sleep because of the stress. DON'T send your kids to Taylor. There is one good thing, the teachers. They are put in a bad situation without a solution, but they try their hardest. They are all very nice and personable and truly care about the students. Don't put the blame on teachers. They all deserved to be thanked for their efforts. I graduated from Taylor and went there K-12 along with both of my brothers. I am now approaching my last year of nursing school and preparing my self to apply for Medical School. My older brother is in his last year of Pharmacy School at Purdue. My little brother is PreMed to be a psychiatrist. All 3 of us graduated from Taylor and went there K-12. I believe this is all because we learned how to properly apply ourselves when we went to Taylor. I will always love this school. This school and district have displayed a focus on safety and learning. The system they use is Professional Learning Communities. My son as truly is successful at Indiana University as a senior due to his experience at Taylor High School.

column3: I attended Pasco High School for 3 years and then I moved. In my opinion, Pasco High School was a greatest school. i love all the teachers and students. I felt very comfortable in school. It has a very nice invironment to study. Horrible!!!! My child hated every minute that they attended this school!!! Poor admin. all the way down to other staff. I think the test scores speak for themselves. The students at Pasco HS can't possibly compete with college bound students that are graduating from top performing schools. I would guess that the top performers at Pasco HS, if transferred, would struggle at high schools with a more rigorous and academically challenging curriculum. Would be interesting to see SAT scores from this school, but based on the state test scores, probably predictable. Only took one semester to figure out that this wasn't the place for my kids. Picked up and moved to a better district. I attended and graduated from this school a few years back. The school is great. You can get all the support you need from the teachers and the class offerings are great. I took 8 AP level courses in my 4 years there, and there were many, many more to choose from. There are many low level classes too for students who have fallen behind. Countless students end up at Ivy League schools (even have a graduate going to Harvard this fall). It's eye opening to see how many things this website has wrong about this school. 91% white? The school is 70% hispanic! The hardest part of going to this school is the stigma some of the community has about it. There school has a wide range of students and the students at the bottom receive the most attention. People need to go to the school and see for themselves how great it is. They also have many extra curricular activities. They have more music trophies than any other school in the area (including 2 grammies). Their sports have taken a recent hit but they have hallways full of trophies, with State Championships in soccer, football, basketball, and dance. There are better schools but there are worse schools too. I really enjoyed going to this school, but I grew up around a lot of friends from around the area. It's different if you move there and try to fit it. But still enjoyed it, and learned a lot, ended up attending WSU after. Graduated 2019 and I don’t understand the low reviews? When I attended it was great, many students take AP courses and take college level courses as well. I got many college credits from here that I was able to transfer to UW. Pasco High needs to be given more credit. Although I am rating this school as a 3, I still believe this is a good school. When a school is as diverse as Pasco is even the best teachers are needing to differentiate their lessons to accommodate their population. The school probably deserves a 4, but the district is holding it back!

column1: This school is amazing. The teachers are wonderful and do a very good job at teaching. For the 2008-2010 school year Godinez got the highest API score in the Santa Ana District. They beat Segerstrom High School. They are doing great progress for them being a new school. At Godinez Fundamental, the teachers do everything possible to help there students achieve academic success. Students are presented with all the necessary tools to become great people in and out of the classroom. Students are encouraged to strive for their goals and reach their full potential. It is truly an amazing school with wonderful and dedicated staff. Campus is in need of repair, i'ma freshaman, rather go to Segerstrom. HOWEVER SOME teachers seam preatty good at their jobs and students are preatty nice. Counseling, AVID, and French Departments in serious need of help though. As a former student, I can attest to the phenomenal staff and support provided by all who work at Godinez. Godinez prepared me for college since day one. I used to find it really annoying that we would have countless assemblies each year addressing the same issues (Financial aid, A-G requirements, SAT/ACT scores/exams, the different branches of public/private schools, etc), but, in retrospect, I now see that they were ensuring students were prepared for the arduous, and sometimes confusing, college application process. As opposed to my peers in other campuses, when senior year finally came, I had very few questions in terms of college.As far as my high school experience, I was involved in six clubs during my four years there, ASB, nine AP classes, a myriad of honors classes, and was an avid supporter of the fantastic shows the VAPA department put on. The school also runs a great, inclusive athletic program that only gets better every year. Currently, I am in my final year of college and have returned to Godinez as a staff member. In the three years since I graduated, the school has added four additional AP courses, more instructional support (including tutoring opportunities), and, to all students' delight, a more relaxed dress code. Back in the day, the boys had to have their shirts tucked in, students could not be expressive with their hair if it did not look "natural," and girls could not show their shoulders (now, to my knowledge, their straps can be 1-2").Overall, this is an outstanding school that just concluded it's tenth year of operation. They have a waitlist spanning hundreds of students for each grade level, so if your child makes it past the lottery, consider yourself lucky as I know a few students who broke down into tears when they realized they did not make it. On another side note, I wanted to mention that in my four years there, I saw Godinez Grizzlies head off to Harvard, Stanford, Columbia, Cornell, Princeton, Georgetown, Tufts, Amherst, Middlebury, MIT, Olin College, and the University of Pennsylvania, to name a few. Like any school, your experience here will be what you make of it. All the resources are readily available to you, take advantage! :-)P.S. To the "community member" below, your post does not indicate that you attended this school or are a parent of an alumnus of this school. What purpose did your comment serve? This school has gone through major positive changes since it open in 2007. There are now more opportunities such as an expansion of AP classes and new after school programs. Godinez continues to exceed my expectations by further developing each day. Way to go Grizzlies !

column3: i dont go here YET !!!!!. but i cant wait omggggggggggggg. i feel like its going to be really fun. The reviews that are saying that this is a great school were written as a JOKE by my peers. None of the recent graduates from Sunset are attending Ivy League schools. I graduated from this school this year (2013). I can honestly say that Sunset did absolutely nothing for me as a student. The faculty is a joke. Whenever I needed advice or help, nobody knew or cared to help. I was in all honors and AP classes, which were taught by the "best" teachers, but even many of them refused to answer simple questions or explain something to me that I didn't understand. The regular-level teachers do nothing but hand out worksheets. I can honestly only say I had 3 teachers that genuinely cared about me and my education. By the time you are a senior there is nobody to ask questions to about college or scholarships. I am headed to a very good university, full ride, but if it wasn't for me going out of my way and finding info about schools, scholarships, etc, I would have nothing, like many intelligent classmates I knew. Do your BEST to steer clear of this school. Almost ANY high school in Kendall is better than this. The only good thing I can say is that I felt safe on campus. When I was there, it was a decent school. I had maybe three teachers who invested their time to help me be a better student and musician. I graduated in 2011 and there are some things about it that I do miss. Happy to have both of my children attending Sunset Senior High. We are happy with the school curriculum and the attentiveness of all the subject teachers. the school has a good volleyball team and baseball players are hot. also has great academics.. the girls are attractive I'm so happy with my son's school, all of his teachers and couselors are great! Transition from middle school to high school has been very easy for him. He's learning alot and he's very happy with his school and freinds. I am a graduate from Miami Sunset Senior High and I can tell you that this is an amazing school! I have had nothing but great memories here! Teachers and staff are great, the school atmosphere in general makes you feel very comfortable. It has prepared me for college academically wise. If I can go back to my senior year I definitely would. The conditions are disgusting and unsanitary! There is mold in the food, it's infested with cockroaches, the school drinking water supply is undrinkable, brown and yellow. No one is allowed to check books out of the library for fear of messing them up. They aren't even allowed to take the books off the shelves! There are no toilets in many bathrooms, and much of the school is filthy. This school should have charges pressed against it! This school let's mold grow in its halls and in the milk containers, they let cockroaches just wander at will. The drinking water is dirtier than the Ganges river. They don't allow the students to take books off the shelves, all around this is the worst place to receive an education, due to the disgusting conditions these students are subjected to. I was walking out of school and there was a giant roach in the hallway. I had to act like I wasn't freaking out on the inside because there were people around. But this school is truly disgusting. I switched in the middle of my freshman year from Broward not even knowing that this school existed, to be honest. But when I first saw it I thought it looked like a prison. My first thought was "How can students enjoy when there isn't even any windows or anything? It looks like a prison." I would give ANYTHING to go back to my old school. I'm a junior now so it's a little too late but I miss is so much. Sunset doesn't even have an actual football field or track. It's ridiculously poor because Dr. Lucia Cox is putting all the money into god knows what. The adult Ed didn't have almost anyone working there to help out. One of the classes didn't even have a teacher, and everything was disorganized and crazy there. Everybody tells you something different. At one point they put a young kid (probably 18 or 20) to sit as the instructor and he didn't even know how to help the students on their computer software. He explained he worked with the lower level student on another software and was not familiar with theirs. Where was the actual teacher?!? The esol adult ed. students don't learn the basics of English, not even the alphabet. As it is, they seem to have dismissed 3 teachers for the computer class. Then they wanted to teach us without any Spanish. It becomes very confusing and I leave the school having to basically teach myself on my own. This school was helpful but not very good. You get what you pay for. It was a decent stepping stone but don't expect to learn too much English here. As a parent who has seen this school grow over the past few years as my children have all graduated in the past 5 years, the difference of this school is nothing less than impressive. With a brand new administration and custodial staff, the school spirt as well as the overall image of Miami Sunset Senior high has chanced dramatically. It was an honor to be a parent of 3 graduates of Miami Sunset as the teachers and staff made my children's high school experience exactly what it should be. The teachers are hard workers who strive in the effort to fully allow students to reach their maximum potentials. My graduates of Miami Sunset have now all been accepted into local colleges and universities and are constantly making the deans list with high honors. I thank MSSH for guiding them into the right path. MSSH may have a negative reputation but I am proud to say, from a parent point of view, that the recent changes this school has made will only get better in the next years to come. My message for parents who are hesitant in enrolling your child into Miami Sunset is the following: The academics are incredible, from medical magnet programs to engineering to sports medicine. Your child will strive in this school with the help of the amazing teachers and staff. Highly recommend joining the MSSH Knight Family. There are a variety of Magnet programs, highly qualified instructors, and unified administration.

Honestly I couldn't have asked for a better school. And if you think they don't take care of things, I was bullied there and they took care of it amazingly, it didn't happen again.
